Great seafood platter. Gumbo was awesome. Worth the visit. Crispy Kale with the swordfish was unique and tasty. Fish very fresh. Bit pricey but great for a special meal

Pretty nice restaurant.Shrimp and Grits were awesome choice.The best thing they had on the menu.I also had a chance to taste their kids fried shrimp and that was good as well. Over all it was a good restaurant.

After eating here on Saturday night, I can't wait to go back. The atmosphere is amazing! The staff seemed to be having a great time and really enjoyed their job, especially Rich. He made the experience fantastic! He helped us with food recommendations and all were wonderful! The crispy brussel sprouts were better than any I've ever had. The squash blossoms with goat cheese were amazing, as was the crawfish  etouffee and steamed chocolate with salted caramel ice cream! We sat at a great table where we were able to see the food being made, which I loved! All in all, it was great experience and I can't wait to go back!

When I first found out that I was spending a week working in the Warehouse District I was disappointed that I wouldn't have time to get to my favorite NOLA spots. Turns out it is just an opportunity to find some NEW FAVORITES! Lüke is definitely that. This was an awesome meal in a wonderful setting with top flight service. Shout out to our server Kenneth! 

Here's the long story. When I took the included photo my dining partner knocked his Martini to the floor shattering the glass and causing a minor scene. The waitstaff handled it perfectly. Then I said to Dan... here is the test... is this a good restaurant or a great one? Kennth had replaced the Martini within 3 minutes! That is a great restaurant. As he placed it on the table he said, "Usually when this happens the second one comes in a sip cup!" That's FUNNY!!  The oysters were perfect both raw and stuffed. My etoufee was spot on and i loved it served over pasta. This was a great night at a GREAT restaurant.
Service was slow. Thank goodness the food was great to make up for it. The gumbo has oysters in it and the burger was actually really really good.

My colleague and I ate here after attending a nurse practitioner conference. We had heard amazing reviews about this restaurant and were excited to experience a taste of New Orleans. We arrived at the restaurant and were informed it would be a two hour wait to be seated, though there were plenty of open tables. We gave them the benefit of the doubt, and assumed they were reserved. We took a seat at the bar, where we were helped by an amazing bartender who also seemed confused that we weren't able to get a seat. After speaking with some coworkers, the hostess was able to get us seated in the mostly empty restaurant. Our waitress was rude and blamed us for moving a water flask we never touched. Food was decent. But overall a bad and strange experience.

Positives:  We had the gumbo and fresh gulf fish--excellent.  The veggies were perfectly cooked (my wife still can't stop talking about the brussel sprouts).

Negatives: The waitress was in a bad mood and my seat was right under the A/C vent.  I got so cold, I sat on the bench seat by my wife and another diner.

Food:  5 stars
Service: 1 star

Luke's Happy Hour 4-6pm M-F. 75 cent oysters as well as half priced cocktails, wine, and beer. Nice lively atmosphere with a good mix of locals and tourist alike. Come early as the bar fills up quickly. Oysters were fresh and plump and the house gumbo has to be one of the best in town.  Come on by and enjoy a dozen or two.

Visited this restaurant  because of the great reviews seen on yelp, it totally lived up to every word. 

We came in at 1030am for brunch. I ordered the shrimp and grits which was DIVINE! My friend ordered the Southern  breakfast with a side of mimi's pancakes.  This was also delicious and the bacon was cooked to perfection, crispy and smoky..

We had Mimosas to top it off and quench our thirst. Overall, the atmosphere  was cozy and our waiter Thomas was attentive enough but not intrusive. We will definitely  come again and would recommend it to anyone visiting  NOLA.

After a few excellent experiences at Luke in San Antonio, we decided to give them a chance to redeem themselves in New Orleans. So. Glad. We. Did. The cocktails and oysters impressed once again, and the service had improved beyond belief. As I mentioned before, the oysters are better than Felix or Acme, and if you come for happy hour, they are only fifty cents a piece!!! We had a dozen oysters, an order of fries, 2 import beers and one French 75 cocktail : $24.42   Not bad for a bistro run by one of the most well-respected chefs in town. Get yourself to Luke around 4:00 and reap the benefits!

In a city full of great eating destinations, Luke may take the cake.

As others have mentioned, Luke offers the best HH in NO! 50 cent (at time of writing) oysters and half price drinks are a great way to kick off your NO weekend. The place gets busy quickly so to ensure your spot in the HH fracas, do arrive early.

Bonus tip: the pate is awesome.
Best meal so far in New Orleans. Undiscovered treasure, the ceviche. Order it, it's not on the menu as a single item.

Not happy with the changes to the menu. I miss the Choucroute Garnie and the escargots. I also loved having the option of ordering just the rillettes, but now you can only get the whole charcuterie plate.

Was looking forward to trying a John Besh restaurant but wound up being so disappointed. Waited 15 minutes for a table, very reasonable since we had no reservations. Upon sitting greeted by one waiter, different one brought drinks, back to first waiter who took appetizer order, back to second waiter who took main meal order, 1st one brought condiments, second one meal. Never knowing who our waiter was resulted in poor service, bread was never brought until we noticed other tables had it and we requested ours. Now down to the food, sooooo underwhelming. We started with the Flamencuche, which they were praised for based on the framed news article when you entered the restaurant. It was compared in the news article to a good pizza, it was terrible, thin flat bread was overwhelmed with an insane amount of onions, its all I could taste. For our meal ordered the burgers, because all the reviews praised Luke's for this. Once again so much carmalized onions and bacon, it made it hard to taste the meat. This place simply was overpriced and under-delivered. Even on their sodas, 3.25 for a small glass bottle soda, ridiculous. So disappointed, didn't even care to see the dessert menu. Mr Besh, I was not impressed would never return.

Found this gem on yelp. The service was top notch. Came in for happy hour. My wife loved the oysters. Were were educated on the various kinds and locations they came from. Great place. We visited twice during our stay in the city. We will go back.

This place was recommended so we decided to stop by. It wasn't busy so we got a table right away. 

We got the seafood gumbo and the shrimp with grits.  Overall good dishes. The gumbo was not the best I've had but it was pretty good.  The shrimp with grits was really good. My mother told me she had to force herself not to lick the bowl.

Friendly wait-staff and overall good dining experience.

I do not know where these other reviewers ate. It was not here. When we first walked in, it was only 50 degrees with no heat on. Only one person was working. Their soda machine did not work and out of half of their menu drink selections. It took way too long for our food which I did not understand because we were the only two customers in the place. My tortas were good but greasy. Her chimichunga had unchewable beef and a hair. Did I mention the employee wore no hat or hairnet. She just couldn't eat it. We couldn't complain because the employee did not speak a lick of english. He did not know how to use the credit card machine and when he finally ran the card, he asked us for a pen to sign (in sign not english). Don't bother going here. Ever!

Ok came back for another meal and it was just as amazing as our first a year ago!Our waitress Deseree  was perfection, as was every dish! Had the French 75 cocktail and it was incredible. So happy to get back to NOLA & have another exceptional dining experience at Luke! May come back for Brunch on Sunday!!
In a city full of great restaurants, Luke is a classic stand out. Try the daily lunch specials with an entree and soup - both will be great.

I was only in New Orleans for 3 days so I wanted to eat at the best New Orleans places they had to offer. Well Luke's helped make that happen. This was my first breakfast encounter in New Orleans. I was greeted by this super attractive hostess. I wanted her for breakfast, but miss beautiful wasn't on the menu and wouldn't dare ask the waiter what the market price for her was. So I settled for an equally sexy option The Eggs in a Jar. This fun sized mason jar came out filled with creamy grits, two poached eggs smothered & moistened with hollandaise sauce, and 3 soft shell crabs battered & fried perfectly protruding out of the  chubby lil jar. Talk about fun presentation. The creamy grits were the best grits I've have had the pleasure of devouring. The entire combination was perfect. Eating breakfast out a mason jar really gave this modern southern feel that I doubt many other places could have nailed like LUKES did. This place was pricey but only in the monetary sense. All in all one of my fave breakfast encounters ever.

My friends and I were visiting Nola for the first time and decided to yelp a restaurant close by to our hotel. This place had pretty good ratings so we decided to give it a try. We were on a laid back vacation, we were all dressed quite casual. This may or may not have been the reasoning behind our effortless service. We could tell we were being judged as a group of young kids pretending to be grown ups. Where was the southern hospitality? Not found here, at our table at least. 

I ordered the shrimp and grits, which was said to be a favorite, and I was extremely disappointed. It was SO salty, I was only able to take a few bites and had to stop eating. I really regret not sending it back but the service made me feel uncomfortable. So I basically paid $26 for a couple bites of sodium enhanced grits. Taste aside, the portion was also saddening. You get a little scoop of grits covered in too much sauce. While taking our orders, the waiter asked us if we wanted soup or salad. Where I'm from, this signifies that it comes with the order. But not here. So each of us ordered a side and got charged $5 for it without even meaning to. 

Almost everyone else at my table had ordered a burger, which they seemed to enjoy very much. It came with fries which also seemed to have endured a heavy hand on the salt. Their large burgers with fries were much cheaper than my tiny plate of shrimp and grits. 

So to round it all up, my personal experience consisted of bad service and unsatisfying food. The atmosphere was nice though. I'm sure the other costumers who dressed a little nicer and knew what to order had a better time than I did.

Where do I start? This restaurant is amazing the staff, their service and the food and drinks they serve are top notch! After 6 days in New Orleans this was hands down my favorite place we ate in. We went back because it was so wonderful. 

The staff.... A friendly group that truly show southern hospitality. On our first visit we sat at the bar where our bartender Brandi, made some fabulous cocktails and even gave us tea to go since it was so hot and she knew we had walked.  The oyster snickers Jamaal and Derick were so fun to visit with the told us places to go get their favorite po' boys. The found us huge delicious plump oysters while shucking and getting us laughing. What a wonderful experience.

Now for the food.....OH MY GOSH, absolutely fabulous. We wanted to lick our plates. I will start with one of my friends dish, it was a simple ham eggs and grits plate. My friend said she didn't like grits but Jamaal said she would like these, he was right she loved the creamy grits and the eggs were cooked to perfection. Another friend had the eggs in a jar, grits with a poached egg and shrimp wonderful presentation and even better flavors deep in the mason jar. My other friend had their matzo ball soup (best we have ever had even in a Jewish Deli) and the frogs legs, crispy and delicious. Even our picky eating friend loved the frog legs. Now for my dish..... I am still dreaming of those flavors. I had the shrimp and grits. Roasted jalapeño cheese grits topped with andouille sausage grave packed with sausage then topped with jumbo shrimp. I wanted to lick the plate clean it was the most wonderful dish eaten in New Orleans.

We wen back again for happy hour, don't miss it! The oysters were amazing we had them raw and fried. Again the cocktails were wonderful, best mint julep in New Orleans. I felt like I was sitting on the porch of Tara

If you are in New Orleans do not miss the opportunity to try this amazing place! I personally can't wait for my next visit to go back!

Great place for good food and amazing service! I'll be back. I came for happy hour (on a Sunday!!) and the oysters were freshly shucked. The service was bar none. The atmosphere is fun!! Thank you Calvin and Phil for being the best part of my night!

A solid four star restaurant. The small seafood platter is pretty good and enough portion for two. The seafood jumbo soup is a must. Rice soaking in salty seafood and creamy soup is so good! Yum! Besides the service is really good. The waiters are attentive and friendly. 

But the fresh gulf fish is not impressive. I understand it's "fresh" so it had little sauce and salt in it, making it kinda bland. Besides it is a bit greasy for a fish dish. 

Would definitely come back if revisiting NOLA but would pass the fish dish as well.
Great happy hr deal. The oysters were very fresh. The atmosphere was classy yet down to earth. Drinks were great as well. A definite must do when you're in NILA.

I love this place!  Great service, fantastic food, awesome cocktails and wine... You can't go wrong. Order the bread pudding...no other dessert... It is a religious experience! Best bread pudding I have ever had!!!
This was my second time visiting this place and while the food was good, I thought it wasn't good enough to warrant coming back here yet again, especially since this is quite a pricey place.

As I sit here at the bar desperately trying to get my waitress attention  I can't help but think back to a time when Luke had really great service. I love this restaurant. The food never disappoints . I have been here countless times.  But the service is to be desired. Ive had cocky waitress's, who love to talk over you when asking a question to next to little attention at times at the bar. And no not during happy hour either. Mr. Besh you need to spend some time there.
Great service, great food and great bar. I found the French 75 to be a great brunch drink similar to that of a Bloody Mary or mamosa, although totally different.

Bread that they serve before the meal is warm and excellent. I ordered the Court-Bouillon that came with a soup so I chose gumbo because it was my first time trying it. I was disappointed by the portion because it was a tiny cup that was priced at $7.50 normally. The Court-Bouillon was good and J was able to try some local staples all in one dish including the region's popcorn rice and some fresh seafood. I also ordered the Lüke burger medium well which was cooked perfectly good but not outstanding in any way but did come with some pretty well seasoned fries. Lastly, I ordered the fried quail that had a really good balance of sweet and savory because it had a honey sauce but had a gaminess to it with the quail. The peppers were also a good garnish because they were also in the honey sauce but the whole dish was well balanced and of course the quail was cooked well and crispy. Waiters were friendly and I was pretty satisfied with my experience but the portion sizes were a bit smaller for the price which is on the upper side of $$(yelp price point).

Upscale bar/restaurant with an adjoining elegant dining area. The establishment is large, has a full bar equipped with TV's and fresh oysters clearly on display for you to witness the art of shucking.

Daily Chef Specials are available Monday-Friday. I visited on a Monday and therefore went with the Honey Tabasco Chicken special. However, I started with a cup of Crawfish Bisque soup; a delicious choice to get my palate fired up for the main course. The Honey Tabasco Chicken was the perfect combination of sweet & spicy atop a succulent lightly battered chicken breast, accompanied by red beans and rice, putting a southern twist on a classic dish. I enjoyed it immensely but could only eat a small portion. My eyes are always bigger than my tummy. Jackson, my server, was a real gent & wrapped the remains for me. 

Lüke is a perfect NOLA spot for date night, business meetings and hour happy.

~Christy

One of my favorite places to eat in the city! Especially during happy hour (1/2 off drinks and 50cent oysters??  Are you kidding me??!)  Sitting at the bar and chatting with the bartenders and oyster shuckers is a great way to come down from a long work day.

The entrees never fail to impress me.  I could pick off of the menu at random and always leave happy (even the burger was impressively good).  Try the beet salad if you're craving a few bites of something healthy (roasted beets, pistachios and crumbly cheese on fresh baby greens) but, if you're craving something a little less healthy, check out the fresh sausages for sure! 

Oh and get the french fries (yes, the french fries).  They taste fresh, look hand cut and, rumor has it, they are fried in duck fat.  All other french fries pale in comparison.

While my husband dined on four dozen happy hour oysters (yes, 48!), I enjoyed a glass of wine. Amazing happy hour prices, no vegan food options. I had two glasses, he had 2-3 cocktails, and like I said , 48 oysters- bill total under $80!

I Love Cosi food and what they promote far as healthy eating and alternatives while still being tasty. I can help but be disgusted that the workers at this location don't wear hear nets!!!!!!!!!!! this is the food industry have to be clean and use all precautions when handling food. They need to enforce hair nets same way you have to wear gloves when handling food

My mom said they have the best beets salad  she's ever tasted. I love the bartender he checked on us regularly and new the menu and special items really well. Great ambiance, seems more business casual but I dress how I want, no one made a fuss. The Friday special, Court Bouillon, was very good and my mother loved her chicken and veggies.

helpful staff, never had a bad wait time;
normally i go in the evenings after work

My husband and I went to Luke for our anniversary dinner and we were so pleased with our meals! Both our cocktails were creative and delicious. I had the Silver Saint which I would describe as a refreshing margarita ish cocktail but with less sweetness and more flavor. My husband had the Bufula Negra (I think) which was very tasty, I don't care for Whiskey and even I liked it. (he later tried the Slow and Low at the waiters suggestions, and was very pleased with that as well). 

Both our waiters were very attentive and had great attitudes. They were sweet and just chatty enough without over doing it. My favorite level of attention at a restaurant.  

Our meals, were, sublime. I ordered the Grilled Rib-eye with lump crab meat. The whole dish was buttery and the flavors were interesting and delicious. Often times I get bored with a steak part of the way through... not with this one! My husband had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en Cocotte" (fancy Shrimp & Grits) and it was so full of flavor and the shrimp were cooked perfectly. He said the grits were like clouds. 

We had read on yelp that the Bread Pudding was the best, and while I am not normally a fan, we ordered that and Bourbon Vanilla Bean Crème Brûlée. The Bread Pudding totally stole the show. It was decadent, buttery, fabulous. The Crème Brûlée was good as well, but do not miss the Bread Pudding. 

Over all a wonderful experience. I'll be back and plan to bring my friends!

Hands down the best sushi around! The rolls are creative and fun, the fish is fresh, and there are so many different options. There are many other menu options, but I can't stray from the delicious sushi!
Great happy hour.  Burger was delicious.  I have also had shrimp and grits which were outstanding.  Highly recommend.

Lüke's happy hour is phenomenal. It is everyday from 3pm-6pm; don't miss it. Their raw oysters are 75¢ and fried ones are $1.25. All drinks are half off during happy hour, also. What a deal! To make matters better, the service, which at times seemed like multiple folks taking and providing our orders, is exceptional and very friendly. This was our first time eating raw oysters, and Lüke didn't disappoint. Make sure to make a reservation. We will be back.

I'm still thinking about the bread pudding.   I've been craving bread pudding since eating the one here.  What I liked the most is that they didn't put raisins in it.    The roasted chicken was friggin delicious also !   We also ate at August but I think I prefer Luke.   Not that one was better than the other, I just like the casual atmosphere of Luke because we didn't have any formal clothes and we were dining with kids.   Oh yeah, the french fries were really good also.  I also like the location of being in the CBD and away from all the chaos in the French Quarter.

Happy hour review only. I had a sazarac at pretty much every bar I went to in NOLA, and this one, while very good, doesn't rank anywhere close to the top. However, the price was absolutely unbeatable...I didn't think it was possible to get a sazarac for under $5!  We also split a dozen of the happy hour oysters, and really, all I can say is that they were worth the $.50 each. I've had better oysters in DC, and way better oysters in New Orleans. I'm guessing the non-happy hour ones were higher quality, and I think next time I'd pay a bit more money to get better ones. Ultimately, everything we had was pretty good, but with so many excellent restaurants nearby, I'm not sure I'd make it back.

We had a great anniversary dinner at Luke.  The atmosphere is very welcoming and the staff were all very nice and informative.  The food was delicious and excellently prepared!  Robert and Vusi took great care to make sure that everything was perfect.  It was the best dining experience we had during our visit to New Orleans.

Service was slow and absent and the heat was high. Summer in the Big Easy. However, 50 cent raw oysters and happy hour bar prices made up for it.

The home brews here are tasty and well thought out and the smoked pork shank w/ sauerkraut plate would have made any German and Cajun mother rejoice with thanksgiving.

I'd like to go back and try more, but so far so good.

Delicious food!  The service was great , the maitre d' and our waitress were very friendly.  The bread is to die for, actually the bread all over New Orleans is to die for.  I ordered the roasted chicken and it melted in my mouth along with the mash potatoes.  Only complaint was that the air conditioning was on and it was freezing, but apparently it is a consistent problem that restaurant has with the hotel it is located in. Ohhh, almost forgot, the dessert. I can't remember the name but it was this chocolate, chicory, mousse type dessert, WOW! So good!

Hands down the best restaurant in New Orleans!

Crispy brussel sprouts appetizer was good, very saucy, not bitter.

Lump crab appetizer was pretty good. 

Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" (roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausage) is my absolute favorite meal in New Orleans. Also their jalapeno cheesy grits is the best in town. No one makes it like them.

We have ordered food to pick up twice and both times it has been great.  It is fresh, well seasoned and plentiful. Additionally, the food is prepared very quickly. Both my husband and I agree that it is the best Chinese we have ever had.  I was pleased to find out that the honey chicken is actually fried and smothered with honey sauce versus being more like sweet and sour chicken where you dip it.  It was so so so yummy. We have also had fried wontons, fried dumplings and cashew chicken.  Definitely a winner!!

4.5 Stars

We came in on a Monday night around 4PM for the oyster happy hour and were surprised that the wait to be seated was a little less than two hours. I guess we should have done a little more research and made reservations, but it was a spontaneous decision, so it was what it was. Once, we were seated, we ordered:

Baked Oysters: A must must get. They were phenomenal. I don't even know how to describe the flavor. It was just really tasty.

Raw Oysters: Fresh and good. And they're really big in size here compared to all the other places I've been to for raw oysters outside of NOLA. And at $0.75 per oyster? Couldn't get any better.

Gumbo: I'm not usually a fan of gumbo and I wouldn't order it ever, but had to try it here after hearing the next table over raving about it with the waitress. I wasn't disappointed. Not too salty and the overall taste is clean and flavorful.

3-6pm happy hour 50c/oyster. Awesome! I sat at the bar. They also had half off for beer and wine. I haven't tried their beer but if I remember correctly, they brew them. When you order oyster ask for mignonette. It's red wine vinegar with charlottes and pepper. It's good when you pour it on top of the raw oyster, I personally like this better than lemon. They will also give you horseradish and shrimp cocktail sauce.

Such a yummy restaurant with a fun environment. The Jumbo Shrimp on Jalapeño Grits was delicious and cooked perfectly (we even added crab on top). Definitely recommend the Crab and Shrimp "Etouffee." It is amazing and served on top of roasted rice to add a bit of crunch. The service was great thanks to Jessie and Chi who were both very knowledgeable and very helpful!

I have mixed feelings about this place. The sandwiches are delicious but way way overpriced for a chain drive through. I got a 1/2 sandwich in the Pick Two yesterday and it was TINY. Like four bites. I paid over $12 for half sandwich and half salad. I can get an awesome meal at a local restaurant for that or less. It also took forever to get through the drive through. Unfortunately, I probably won't go back since Boise has so many better options.
Very good. Happy hour $.50 oysters are where it's at. Great cocktails. Delicious desserts. Always a fav place to stop while in New Orleans.

Thank you yelp! We came in on for Sunday brunch and requested something we've seen on YELP! They were more than happy to replicate the dish. We also ordered raw oysters and crab benedict. The main star dish was the Roasted jalapeno cheese grits with yard egg topped with a crispy fried soft shell crab. Yes, it was very rich in favor. The egg yolk oozing with perfection & you can taste the jalapeno like you just bit into a fresh one.

Luke's was one of our favorite meals in New Orleans. Our only problem was I made reservations on Open Table, we get there and after about a 15 minute wait at the bar, we were seated at a table for two in the back by where the waiters come in and out. My husband was not happy and after asking a couple of times we were moved to another table for two (there were several) more to the center of the restaurant.

The Louisiana Rabbit and Chicken Liver Pate was wonderful and we loved all the sides that went along with it. The manager has since sent me the recipe that is used at that restaurant and also his Provence restaurant. Can't wait to try it.

I have also recreated the Salad Luke. I loved the presentation of this salad. I made my own pickled yellow beets and added beets to the different layers instead of just on the bottom of the salad. 

The black drum with the meunier sauce was also wonderful as was the lemon cheesecake with lemon sorbet for dessert.

We could have stopped eating after the pate but we surged on. They brought more crostini and it was just hard to quit eating the stuff.

We recently moved in the area and tried sushi at various  places. None of them around here were up to our satisfaction until one day we decided to try Haichi. The ambiance is great, the staff is very nice and the food is great!! I took my daughter just the other day and the same great food. I would recommend this place to all sushi lovers. 

Kate

Excellent food, excellent service! What an amazing staff. We came in during Mardi gras at happy on the parade route. The resturant was sooooo busy, they had every excuse to drop the ball but instead Amili (sp) and Jamie made us feel so special. They treated us like kings and queens. They made my 80 year old, old man feel special for his 1st Mardi Gras. Hats of the ownership and leadership of this super AWESOME resturant, your commitment to quality and service excellence is refreshing. Shout out to the most amazing bar staff in all of NOLA, you guys are awesome. Definitely, the highlight of the trip. We'll be back.

The food was great, and the service was awesome.  We were a table of 12, and had a great time there.   I had the filet, which was grilled to perfection.  The potatoes on the side were great, but the dish is lacking some sort of sauce to go with the potatoes, other thank ketchup.

Came here for lunch. The service was good but the food was underwhelming, especially for the price.

Ordered the...
1/2 dozen stuffed PJ oyster ($19)
Croque Madame with fries ($15)

The oysters were stuffed and broiled over a shrimp and crab mix. They were very salty and had very little flavor.

The Croque Madame is two pieces of bread with ham covered in cheese with an egg on top. This dish was also very salty with little flavor. The Croque Madame along with the fries was cold.
Cute and friendly! :) came here with my family for a quick meal and ended up staying and eating more!

Stopped by on a stormy day to find it nearly vacant at lunch time; I quickly found out it was because they had lost power and were not expecting their kitchen to begin producing hot food for another 30 minutes. Thankfully, I only wanted some oysters! The staff was super attentive, and I was quickly enjoying 6 of the largest oysters I've ever seen. They kept apologizing for the inconvenience, and the bartender gave me a free bowl of the gumbo base (sausage and okra). Then the oyster shucker handed me 2 more oysters on the house; all of the oysters were very fresh and mild. 

I can't speak to anything other than the oysters, really, or what their service is like during busy times, but what I experienced was fantastic!

Quite honestly, the worst dining experience I've ever had, not just in Nola. 

We got there early for our reservation, and they sat us early. Good start. They brought out good bread. Ok, not so bad so far. First issue: we specifically asked for a game to be on their TVs when we made the reservation, and they assured us that the bar would be playing that game. They did not play that game. Oh well, not really a big deal.

Hey, that reminds me. Didn't we put in for drinks and oysters half an hour ago? Where are they? After another 15 minutes, a separate waiter comes and gets our drinks, finally. After another 15 minutes, no oysters, so we decide to put in our orders. Maybe the oysters have escaped.

Our oysters finally come after an hour of waiting for them, and they're ok. My matza ball soup is pretty much tasteless. The broth has a slight chicken flavor but other than that, nothing. The gumbo my friends got was tiny. Our waiter has now not talked to us or checked on us in well over an hour. He is busy talking to the bachelorette party and some random guy at the bar. Our other waiter is busy with his own tables, but makes more of an effort to check in on us probably 3 times over the course of a 2.5 hour marathon restaurant experience.

Now I get my entree, the fried oyster salad. The only redeeming quality of this salad is the bacon. Everything else was pretty much worthless. They oysters tasted slightly of salt, but that's it. 

The bread pudding was only good for the topping and ice cream. Once you run out of sauce, it became literally a semi-thick, unsweet dough. 

0/5 terrible experience.

I have heard several people talk about Luke... now that I finally made it here... i can't believe I have deprived myself of this place for so long.  Very very excellent food.  Shrimp and grits w/crab meat was a one of a kind dish!  Crawfish bisque was no slouch at all either! Already planning an encore visit.
Great brunch. I highly recommend getting the crawfish omelet! So good and flavorful and that's how to eat crawfish in my opinion! Already peeled :) very tasty!

My wife and I came here to celebrate my mom for Mother's Day. We had the Drum Fish and the Shrimp & Grits! Both selections were fantastic! Their shrimp and grits is as good as it gets. The Drum was nicely cooked and perfectly complimented with the sides to create a delightful dinning experience. Great atmosphere!

Luke's restaurant was amazing! My husband and I came for our anniversary and the service was excellent!! Shawn and Uusi were so friendly and recommended the best dishes for us to try. We had the crab fritter's which was crispy on the outside and perfectly cooked and seasoned on the inside. We also had the shrimp and grit which were God sent!! The shrimp and grit were the best meal I had in New Orelans!! They were perfectly seasoned the grits were light fluffy and cheesy, and they just the right amount of shrimp and sausage. I will recommend Luke to all my family and friend. Great food, amazing service and a cool bistro atmosphere!! We love Luke!!

Wow...I went here three times in New Orleans even though we had said we wouldn't go any place more than once but it was just so good. 
Two times we were there for happy hour...$.50 oysters and half off all drinks meant I slurped oysters and drank French 75s twice in New Orleans and the oysters were the best I've had. The pate & charcuterie plate was absolutely amazing with the fennel jam and the pickled watermelon rinds as perfect accompaniments to the pates (the rabbit & duck liver was especially delighful), the pancetta and the delicious head cheese. The boudin noir was just as good as the boudin noir at DBGB in NYC but was made even better by the potato, apple and onion hash it was served with. The flamenkuche (a flatbread with bacon, onions and cheese) was also delicious. We meant to have entrees the first time but ended up full after all that so we had dessert which was bread pudding ala mode with pecans and bourbon sauce and gateau basque which was a vanilla cake that was a cross between a pound cake and angel food cake that had creme fraiche and blueberry sauce on top. It was like a dream it was so good.
On the 2nd visit...more oysters and the heirloom tomato salad with fresh mozzarella. The basil and balsamic reductions made for very intense flavors with the tomatoes and mozzarella and the mozzarella practically melted in your mouth. Eric and I shared the shrimp and grits which were also wonderful...just spicy enough and  the grits were perfectly creamy but heavy enough to really complement the andouille and shrimp.
And our third visit was just for dessert and drinks...I got the gateau basque again and it was just as amazing the 2nd time :)
And I would totally come back again a few times when we are back in New Orleans.

I'm a foodie from the Carolina's, so I have a high standard for certain foods, shrimp and grits in this case. I was wowed, shrimp and grits did not disappoint. Simply amazing. Sat at the bar and chatted with their professional oyster schuker while enjoying a fantastic meal.

Staff was pretty friendly. 

The food area was a bit of a mess. 

The pinto bean looked like bean paste. Not refried bean. But bean paste. Very unappetizing. 

The portions were once again very small. 

Ordered a burrito and it ultimately looked like a frozen burrito you would get from a truck stop. 

Hopefully after 2/8/2016 something will be done to get portions consistent as well as do something with the bean paste. 

Certainly not my favorite chipotle. 

I miss the days when going to chipotle was satisfying.

The coffee and bentons bacon was good, but I wouldn't order the frittata again, under cooked so runny in the middle, too much caramelized onion and the dressing on the arugula was pouring off the plate. Made for a soggy mess.

Great deal for happy hour -- fifty cent raw oysters, one dollar fried oysters, 50% off drinks.

Unfortunately, other than the oysters and drinks we were a little disappointed. The Etoufee was moderately tasty but very small for the prince, the complementary bread was frankly inexcusably stale and un-appetizing and the foie gras terrine was on the edge of frozen when it came out.

Come for the happy hour drinks and oysters but skip the rest.

Chef Josh Besh's shrimp and grits was pretty amazing. This is just one of the many places he operates in New Orleans and a must if you are in town for some signature dishes.  Their lunch menu was fantastic. The person next to me got some kind of a grilled cheese with corn beef and a fried egg on the top, calling chef Besh creative is an understatement.

Luke was my first meal in NOLA and the start of an entire week of eating.  WOW.  Everything was amazing.  I had the seafood gumbo (which I had to ask around the table if they also agreed that it was good) and it was best gumbo I had the entire week. Also had the shrimp etoufee and housemade sausages which were also yummy.

Saw all the reviews here so wanted to try them out.   Not to mention they were downstairs from my hotel. 

Everything was good. Food had slot of flavor, servers were fast and easy going. 

Price is good for the environment.

This place is a bit expensive for "fast food" and the portions aren't too generous, but if you're in a hurry and you're walking home from a night class, this may be your best bet (it's open most weeknights until 11 P.M.)  Lunch items aren't served until 11 A.M. - if you go any earlier you're stuck with bagels (I believe they're called "squagels" by virtue of the fact that they're squarish and not circular) and other items I don't really consider to be "real" food.  I tried the jalapeno and cheddar squagel on two occasions - I ordered cream cheese with it and it was fairly tasty to my sleep-deprived, 7 A.M., slightly off-game taste buds.

The Asian chicken salad was acceptable and the piece of bread it came with was fairly good and added value to the meal.  The chain also offers a 1/2-salad, 1/2-sandwich combo which is a convenient (though obvious) idea. I usually get the Tuscan pesto chicken since it's the least offensive and least messy of the sandwiches I've ordered here (the chicken tinga sandwich is a bit messier - the guacamole and stringy chicken bits tend to spill out of the sandwich when you bite into it) and I order a salad with it.  I've never gotten a soup here.  

The coffee is acceptable if not memorable.  The brownies and cookies don't exactly taste homemade, but if the mood strikes you, they're available.    Going back to the sandwiches - order them raw (not toasted) since the toasted bread is crunchy and hard.  Also, the Tuscan pesto chicken tastes better without melted cheese.  The latter ruins an otherwise quasi-healthy meal.  I've never gotten the carrots with a sandwich, but I've opted for the pepper-flavored kettle chips.  Raw carrots don't particularly appeal to me.  For beverages, I do recommend their lemonades (mojito lemonade or raspberry lemonade) albeit they're full of empty calories.  

Service: B-
Taste: B-

Best chicken and waffles I've ever had. Don't be afraid of the pepper jelly. It's made in house and makes the dish!
*I forgot to take a pic so I asked my neighbor lol. He already started but at least you have an idea...

We liked the food but we're completely ignored at the ordering counter by FOUR employees.  They would make eye contact with us and continue to not help us.  It was extremely rude and unprofessional.  I will not ever go back here.  Then when one employee finally decided to acknowledge us, I asked if they were still open at 8pm because of how poorly we were treated.  Then a second employee decided to help the first employee- put a glove on to start handling food items, and jokingly slapped the first employee in the back of his head/ neck with the food glove!  Then started working with the food!!! I thought I was being pranked! This place is a total joke!

We wanted to like the Flamenkuchen, but just didn't.  Those big pieces of ham/bacon with all that fat was just too much.  And we encountered the most arrogant server, Kenneth, that we have ever had.  After the first course, we decided to cut our loss and not stay for anything else.  We expected so much more from a Besh restaurant.

Top shelf experience, for food especially but also atmosphere. Raw oysters,  crab meat au gratin, and rabbit & liver pate (all with  exquisite crostini) made superb appetizers. At our table were served delicious and perfectly cooked mussels, a magnificent medium rare ribeye (and was glad to have taken the waiter's suggestion to choose only the pat of butter for the topping; this was an excellent cut and well cooked), and well received shrimp and grits. The cocktails, sides, and wine were up to the task as well.

It's worse than I thought
Their "chicken" is processed stuff
Fake chewy "meat" -- Yech!

Yelp you've done it again! It was my birthday and we were attempting to eat at Acme but the wait was ridiculously long so we grabbed a table across the street...mistake. After ordering drinks we asked for the bill due to really poor service (think: server eating chips at the register next to our table). I searched on Yelp and discovered Luke so we took the short walk over.
Upon arrival, we were pleasantly surprised. We were quickly seated and served water and bread. The servers were informative, patient (we may have had a bit to drink), and friendly, but more importantly, the food was delicious! 
As others have said, happy hour is well worth it, we ordered fried, stuffed and half shell oysters along with a bowl of seafood gumbo for the table to share. BOMB.com! 
I wish I had pictures to share, but the food was so good I forgot. I do have one though...

I've eaten at Luke before with good results. The Hamburger seems to be the best deal on the menu in terms of portion size and quality. The service seems to be suffering on my last couple of visits. They had three hostesses and a host rotating around the restaurant but somehow it took the waitress 40 minutes to take our order and bring out our food. When the shrimp and grits arrived the shrimp were room temperature at best. The grits were warm, likely secondary to the hot iron skillet. The portions are undersized. I don't want to go to apple-bees and get 10 pounds of food, but I would like my entree priced at $20 plus to be larger than an appetizer. 

Also, do they really have to serve diet coke in an 8 oz bottle. Can they just give a large glass which will be refilled like every other restaurant? I feel like the drink seems to be a way to generate revenue. It was ha hassle.

I also would have ordered dessert but the service was so slow that I didn't know how long it would be until we got out of there. 

In short good food, undersized portions with mediocre service.

Maybe, they should transition one of the five host/hostesses to wait staff to minimize this problem.

Won't be eating here until this is fixed.

Went for the Happy hour after friends had highly recommended Luke. We were in town for a cruise so we flew in a couple days early. From the airport after flying for 14 hours we checked into our hotel and then bee lined it to Luke before happy hour finished. The bar was packed, but luckily a table for 2 opened up and we were seated with 45 min left. We started with 1 doz baked, 2 doz raw oysters, and a couple glasses of champagne. Baked arrived first and my wife was in heaven (she doesn't care for the raw ones) next the raw, these are plump  med. size gulf oysters, fresh as can be, simply wonderful !! We were going to order a bottle of the same champagne at the same time as I was ordering another 2 doz raw, but our waiter informed us that it was cheaper to order by the glass during happy hour. With 15 min left I got a call from my 82 y/o mother who had also just arrived in town with her 3 friends. I asked if she wanted some oysters and of course she said yes. Our waiter was great, after informing him that we needed  another 4 doz  raw for my mom and her friends he cleared a table next to us even though happy hour was almost over. All of us had a great time, the service, food, drinks, and atmosphere was as advertised and then some. The next day my wife and I decided to go back and we were seated at the same table. The manager recognized us and came over to chat, commenting that he had just seen us at the same table 23 hrs ago. NOLA has a lot of great restaurants and happy hours  to choose from and we think Luke  should definitely be high on your list to experience.
I've been twice for lunch and disappointed each time. The food is fine but in this city fine does not cut it. The service was down right bad the 2nd visit.

Really awesome, oysters were super fresh, well shucked, good size and variety. 
Wine was excellent, good selection but nothing too extensive or bamboozling, just a careful choice of old and new world - they have been chosen well! 
The pate was incredible, I spent an hour just grazing.....seriously yum. 

I would have given this place 5 stars but tv with football screening makes me give it 4. Yes, harsh I know, but personal preference! 

They had been really busy over the holidays so I think the staff were a little beat but they were still great, friendly and nice, only tip would be if they had more knowledge of the seafood especially, they couldn't tell me the different oysters but whatever, still a great experience.

Dr. Reddy has taken care of my cat Abbey for 5 years. They are wonderful. Always willing to get us in when we need to be seen. They take the time to answer all our questions! The best vet we've ever had!
Everything from atmosphere to food and service were impeccable. Oysters were amazing, shrimp and grits to die for, delicious steak. Bread pudding to finish off this feast was insane!!!!

Amazing meal great service. It's not cheap but so far it's one of our best meals in Nola. The crawfish etouffee is good but not worth ordering given how much better all the other meals are.

The brussel sprouts are amazing!

I went to Luke with a friend for the happy hour and we had really good experience.  The decoration and the service both met my expectation. We tried raw oysters, fried oyster and red bean and rice on their daily special menu. All of them are good. I am surprised that their fried oysters are not too greasy. Overall it was a great experience and I will definitely visit again.
Happy Hour from 3-6pm. If you love oysters this is the place for that at 50 cents a piece with half off on selected alcoholic beverages.

Absolutely love this place! The crab bisque soup was amazing. The service was spectacular. The manager even sent over champagne and shots and bread pudding for my birthday. Couldn't have asked for a better experience. Wish I could give this place 10 stars!

First of all let me say that John Besh is my favorite and so I think all his restaurants are marvelous and perfect. (I'm talking to you Domenica, my precious, tender angel.)

I prefer Luke for those cold/rainy days when you want some warm, heavy, and hearty food. The interior is also very warm and cozy and comforting. It has a golden kind of glow that is quite pleasant (and no, it was not just the wine, I promise!)

I found to be one of those places where everything on the menu is amazing. (Except the escargot. He may even have the best escargot in the world. But no amount of talent or whimsy can make snails look/taste/smell/feel delicious to me).

I love the pate. For an entree, my favorite has to the schnitzel.

Wonderful Sunday brunch. Make a reservation for sure. Gulf oysters - the best. Yummy French 75, sausages and unique bread pudding - from a bread pudding snob. Will go back for the charcuterie platter.

Great place for happy hour oysters. The gumbo was delicious and they kept the drinks flowing. Service was impeccable and the servers are very polite and friendly. I wish they would expand to other states.

Quiet elegance, excellent cuisine (even by NOLA standards), prompt and attentive service.
This was the only restaurant we visited twice during our time here.
Their Omelete of Local Crab is absolutely phenomenal! This will be my official go to breakfast place in new orleans!
This place was very nice and intimate, a great place for a date or a mid afternoon desert for two.  It was definitely a little pricey, but in the end the food and service was worth it.
$0.75 happy hour oysters, great deal. There can be a wait (HH 3-6 pm) so try to get a reservation or call ahead. Ask for the mignonette sauce with the oysters.

We read about the great happy hour at this place, and so we decided to try it on my first trip to New Orleans.  First, let me say that we were sitting at the bar, and Jamie was the bartender that evening.  She was so friendly and helpful, I have to credit her for a great start to our vacation.  The Oysters were some of the best we have ever had - but even better than that was the fact that they not only make their own cocktail sauce, but they even make their own horseradish!  It definitely makes a HUGE difference!  She whipped up some amazing drinks - and even let us sample some of their delicious brandy-soaked cherries she was using for one of the most popular drinks.

I am just sorry we didn't have more time in New Orleans, and couldn't get back to Luke's again and again.  

You MUST go for their great happy hour - and have dinner there as well.  We'll definitely be back if we get to New Orleans again!!!!

Cannot say enough great things about this place!!  The food is AMAZING - great oysters, great sushi, great pad thai, great desserts....I haven't had anything that was not outstanding.  The servers are always pleasant and wanting you to have a good experience.  It's a small restaurant in a strip shopping center but the interior is very cool.  It's a BYO but the liquor store is two doors down.  If you love sushi, you will love Hachi!

I thought I had found the world's best chicken and waffles until I went here. What a great place in dt Nola! My friend took me to brunch and she had the omelet and I had a tough time choosing, but ultimately took the waitress's advice and I couldn't have been more pleased. The pepper jelly is so fresh, the chicken is so moist, the waffles are so fluffy, and whatever cinnamon-butter with which  they top the waffles is divine. We also had a dozen oysters on the half shell, so fresh and clean! I couldn't recommend this place more for a really nice brunch experience.

By far the best sushi we've ever had and we've dined at Michelin starred restaurants such as Sushi Ran in Sausilito when we lived there. The place is a hole in the wall in an anemic strip mall in Chalfont. Do not let this minor detail discourage you. The inside is sleek and beautiful.  The staff is friendly and attentive. It's a BYOB and two doors up, there is a wine store. We had oysyers, sashimi and 4 rolls. All amazing.  The himachi was an inch thick and about 3 oz. which is unheard of at shushi restaurants.  The Manhattan Monkey and Snow Mountain were our favorite rolls by far. The sushi chefs take their craft very seriously. We are going to try the sushi boat next time. It came with an ice sculpture! Wtf? What an excellent meal.

I eat here every time I find myself in New Orleans. It has consistently been a favorite dining experience. Ambiance is comfortable with a slightly masculine feel. It's good for a date night or dinner with friends, but also perfect for a business occasion as well. My favorites: Mint Julep, Crab & Corn Bisque, Croque Madam w/ fries. Another notable is the sausage plate....but it is a comically large amount of meat...shareable.

Fantastic.

Great service. Great food. My sister and I had out last meal in New Orleans at Luke. We had planned to have dinner and then head over to the French Quarter, but we ate so well at Luke that we took out happily stuffed selves back to the hotel to relax.

My sister had the Croque Madame which she loved and I had the Luke burger. The homemade fries are delicious! Our drinks from the bar were well made and the meal was topped off with a box of chocolates brought with the check.

If Luke were in my city, I think it'd be on my regular rotation.

Went in without a reservation for brunch and were told it would be a 20 minute wait. Had a glass of wine at the bar and a few minutes later we were seated.  First off, service is fantastic. Had the Louisiana jumbo shrimp and jalapeño cheese grits...best shrimp 'n' grits ever. Grits were very creamy and the shrimp was perfectly cooked. Also tried the Fried chicken biscuit...Chicken was crispy, juicy, and well seasoned. Biscuit was light and fluffy and had notes of honey. Finished it off with bread pudding topped with vanilla bean ice cream. Pudding was warm, yummy caramel sauce made with rum and the pecans tied it all together. Great meal in NOLA John Besh restaurants never disappoint.
75 cent oysters and half off cocktails and beers 3-6pm errrdayy! I can definitely get behind that errdayy! Much love for lüke and NOLA :)
The absolute best part of my trip to New Orleans. I'm honestly still dreaming of the Luke burger. The staff was really lovely and the atmosphere charming. All around amazing place

Ordered the crab & corn bisque to start. I should've ordered the bowl not the cup. For dinner I had the Fresh Gulf Drum (pan fried white fish) topped with crab meat. Great dish!! Service was great, waiters were friendly.

Went to Luke's for happy hour oysters and half prices wine. Had 1/2 dozen oysters with  a glass of sauvignon branc.  Not bad very fresh accompanied with horseradish and cocktail sauce. My first time trying oysters on the half shell.  Good experience. Then ordered stuffed oysters which was very good. All this for 26.00.

Oh my gosh!!! I had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte". It was the best meal I have ever had in my life!!! The ambience was very nice and I was seated very quickly with my reservation. My server was adorable as well as the friendly hostesses. I would surely say that my visit here made my trip to New Orleans that much more memorable!!! Thank you!!!
Best oysters in NOLA! Happy hour prices are amazing and the service is friendly. Sit at the bar, order a drink and a dozen and relax!

I like how you can see the cook , it's looks nice and clean, cute seating area.  The people working was great. The food was good and tasty plus  fresh . Just wish they devein the shrimps. Next time I will get the beef. I will be back

Great happy hour and awesome cocktails!  French 75 is made with cognac (as it should be) and the raw oysters were huge, the fried oysters delicious, crawfish bisque out if this world, and the lemongrass shrimp meatballs w/ spaghetti was equally awesome.  Also,love that they have an absinthe cocktail and a variety of pastis.

This is a great spot for sushi. It is always fresh and prepared nicely. I've never had a complaint here. The restaurant itself is clean and has a calm atmosphere. Although it is not very big. I usually order takeout because it's more convenient for me. I look forward to ordering sushi from here when I'm at work.
Food was amazing.  Came for breakfast, had the shrimp and grits and the southern breakfast.  Shrimp and grits were delicious.  The coffee is amazing!!!!  Service was excellent.

I gotta give it three. First I have a sneaking suspicion that the same Asian family owns this and the restaurant next door....I could be wrong, but I doubt it. That place serves average american chinese. This place serves average Asian fusion...from a variety of off the shelf cook books.
There is nothing original here, not even the Stephen Starr inspired music. Its like they went to POD and tried to copy it...poorly.
You walk in to a chalk board in the vestibule. Take a picture of it because it is nowhere to be found inside. Look at the sushi counter. To the left is a few bits of shellfish on ice. I don't know if this is for show. The other two are filled with grocery store sushi makings. Why show off the kani? Is yours different? Homemade? Its krab stick from a box. 
We ordered the left side of the menu. I told the waiter that I hate cilantro. Over 50% of the dishes have cilantro in the description. Almost every dish came covered in cilantro microgreens. It is still cilantro! Btw this is a steal from Bluefin in East Norriton. 
They throw the food at you. Out of order and several at the same time. No sequence. No break. We got king crab croquettes, average with no noticable crab and wasabi crackers with spicy tuna. A hot app and a cold app at the same time. Before that was finished I got my soup put in front of me, a clam miso soup, with sandy inedibleclams. The broth was fabulous though.
Japanese cuisine does not rely upon cilantro. Chinese and vietnamese do. So we aren't japanese. Do what you do best.
Oh back to the menu. Its huge. Too huge. Cut it by 2/3. 
The sushi was very sweet. Too much mayo. Nothing really popped.
The tuna pizza sucked. Sweet. Too sweet. Unweildy to eat. 
What are you trying to be?! Habachi?! No habachi tables. Korean...there's galbi and gochujjang, but no real spice to anything. Japanese..nope.
I wouldn't go again.

3.5 stars. First the good news: the food here is amazing. Succulent pork, flavorful bisque, to-die-for jalapeño grits. John Besh knows his flavor profiles. But really, everything else about the restaurant was downhill from there. The oysters were tasty, but inadequately shucked. We had TWO servers, but still felt like we weren't paid adequate attention to. Getting our drinks, placing our order, and trying to pay took longer than we liked. The ambiance is confusing.  Are you fine dining? Or a bar? Or an Applebee's? Why are there newspapers hanging down as dividers between the tables? Some couples were dressed up for dinner - jackets, dresses, and heels. Others had shorts and flip flops. And then there were the fellas at the bar with Tshirts and hunting camo baseball caps on. Maybe it's b/c the restaurant is attached to a hotel? The hostess at the door had this really loud, piercing laugh that she unleashed more than once during our meal.

Food this good shouldn't be taken as carry out - unfortunately, that is the only way we can see ourselves eating it again.

WORST SERVICE EVER. and i mean ever. 

After someone took my food by accident, I asked them to make another one for me (and I waited ANOTHER 5 minutes). They misunderstood and didn't add chicken to the pizza I ordered. So the employee rolled his eyes at me and gave me this look. 
So after 15 minutes of waiting...I got my food.

I have never been treated this way at ANY fast food place even. No one apologized. 

Now I go out of my way NOT to go to Cosi. They don't care about their customers. They just make the money. But hey...students need food...so they go to Cosi.

Is it too much to ask for employees to be respectful?

Came for drinks and an appetizer and was not disappointed at all. The best roasted Brussel sprouts ever. Sat next to a local and had a great conversation.  We will be back in the future to have dinner next time.
Besh has done it again. A beautiful blend of fancy foods and a French menu with a casual feel and very affordable prices. The shrimp and grits are to die for.
Lunch was awesome. You've got to try the soft shell crab BLT. Geeeeezzzzeeee! Had to be sent from heaven.

Ahhhhmazzing. 
We had some mishaps with our drinks not coming and soup being a little on the cold side, but they remedied the mistakes immediately and sent us desserts at the conclusion of our meal. 
Raw oysters were divine. 
I had a special of grits with pork belly. Only compliant was that it wasn't served to me in the comfort of my bed. I would loved to have curled up with that cast iron dish and dreamt sweet dreams next to it. 
This place is a must. Fairly priced, too.

Luke is just one of those places hat I have to visit each time in visiting NOLA.  It's a great restaurant attached to the Hilton Hotel that doesn't feel like a hotel restaurant.  Service is fantastic...usually. (I will get to that in a little while...)

Was in town with a coworker who is Vegan, and he raved about the concoction that the kitchen whipped up for him. It ended being his favorite NOLA meal EVER.  Unfortunately, it set up all the other meals during our trip to be failures because he enjoyed it that much and was impressed by our waiter's knowledge of the vegan diet and how he worked with the kitchen to make my coworker happy. Thumbs up guy with the ponytail! (Sorry, didn't get your name.)

We were so enablers by the service, that we hung out, ordered more drinks and dessert...forgetting our our urgency to make it to Bourbon Street for a fun night. Oops.

Fast forward to Sunday Brunch.  Waiter seemed hungover and slow. Kept reaching over the table to serve drinks and fill our glasses.  Now, I've never been a server, but I am pretty sure that is incorrect etiquette.  And as much as I have been to Luke's, all other wait staff made this guy look like a chump.  Anyway, we kept trying to warm him up by being super polite and friendly, but it was more out of annoyance than anything...

Food is always consistent here.  Although, I will say that the bacon bits in my salad seemed more fresh on Sunday morning than they did on Friday night.  I also love to get the shrimp and grits when I am feeling like something more hearty. Luke does it the best. 

Get the bread pudding.  It is a MUST.  You can hit the gym the next day.  No regrets.

We dined at Luke for Christmas dinner 2016.  This is a busy, hectic restaurant and does not bode well for a relaxing atmosphere.  In addition, the layout is a long galley so the servers are carefully navigating the space to not bump into each other or customers.  The lighting was bright, not what we were expecting.  We spoke with the manager that night, a woman named Tea who was really great and you could tell that she was the glue keeping the operation together.  Food was good, but I wasn't blown away.  It's tough to stand out in a city with so many great options.
Nice space, great vibe and some good dishes.  Especially fond of the pork rillettes appetizer!

If you lonely and need someone to talk to go here!! You will find people old and young to talk to who are down to earth, live in the neighborhood and are friendly. This place has pole tables,good kitchen bar food, and borderline decent staff. When you first walk in it takes a second for you to find a seat since the seating arrangements are disorganized a little. People are loud at talking and normally screaming at the sports on t.v. When a bartender finally approaches you , they are on a grand hustle. They speak real fast, get to the point, take your order and charge u up !!!! At the end coming out of there I would always be cautious seems kind of shady and maybe some cops hiding in the cut ........This is a place I would visit a few times out of the year!!

John Besh delivers in a big way here. The $.75 raw oysters are amazing and the fried ones are soft, not greasy or chewy and just friggin delicious. Drinks are half price during happy hour and I'd suggest the French 75 or the bourbon smash with peaches and mint. I was looking forward to this as was my wife and let's just say, there was not a single drop of disappointment in this place. Just fantastic.

The presentation of every dishes was so artistic! And loved the modern tasteful interior! Toro & King salmon sashimi were so fresh and delicious. Duck Confit came with a small side salad in house made plum dressing, toasted pine nuts, grapefruit & pomegranate was so fragrant, tender and juicy. Spicy seafood soup w bok choy was perfect for that snowy day. Most of all, never forget to try their dessert! Especially Thai Mango, passion fruit and Yuju sorbets were soooo good!!! Caramel cashew ice ream, Yuju ginger creme brûlée, and fresh Yuju whipped cream in fried wonton with berries in top - they all pleased our eyes and taste buds at the same time!! Chef Ben is simply a genius! One of the finest dining experience.

Worst service! Told the hostess we wanted to sit in the bar area and she insists on sitting us in the back of the restaurant which is empty. Sat there for over 10mins with tons of staff walking by & just staring at us but no service, not even water. We finally got fed up and walked out. Horrible!

Went on a trip NOLA in May with family and friends. We tried out Luke since it was right across the street from the hotel. We ended up eating here 5 more times during the trip! Each time it was great.
The service was amazing and the food even better. I tried a bunch of stuff I've never had before, loved all of it. One night my father in-law got a steak, it was perfectly cooked to the temp he ordered. If we ever go back to the area, we will definitely stop in again!

Enjoyed myself very much at this establishment,  I was in town on business and we had dinner here the steak was perfect.  I would tell you that the level of service was awesome from our servers. ...my wine glass never was empty. ...by the way corn and crab bisque was very good. .....

The service was excellent. The barista was attentive, friendly, and the latte was unique as well as delicious. It's also a charming location with a lovely front patio. I am looking into moving into this neighbourhood, and Elm Cafe may have clinched it!
The owner John and his manager have always been very nice to me.  Food is great and our server Cheyenne was hilarious and very good at her job.

Luke is right next to the Hilton - part of it connects through to a lobby hall where the restrooms are located. There is a front dining area and a back room which winds along.

Great cold seafood, and we were impressed with our jagersnitzel. The Saturday night rabbit and pasta dish were good too. The sauerkraut was not worth ordering and or ciabatta bread at the table was rock hard. 

Great happy hour values - some half priced drinks and half price appetizers.

Okay, so my girl friend really hated the burger, and thought the spatzle was even worse ... but I loved the pork special, the value, and the fact that they brew their own German beer!  

Food: Ordered an onion tart bacon pizza concoction to start things off.  The Emmenthaler cheese is SWEET.  And I think that's what makes the flamenküche (yeah, try pronouncing it) work, the combination of sweet and savory made my tummy happy but at $13, it was only a slightly overpriced tease compared to the amazing pork special I dived into next.  That dish is big, succulent and at $15, probably the best value of any one entree I had all week in New Orleans.  The pork is resting on top of crab and  crawfish stuffed cornbread that layers the bottom of the plate so it almost resembles a casserole, or a Thanksgiving stuffing.  In between the pork and the stuffed cornbread is a generous heaping of greens (kale? spinach?  whatever it was, it tasted great mixed with the sauce from the pork).  

The burger on the other hand ... one of the more expensive items on the menu at $16, we both were expecting more, especially after reading the newspaper clippings lining the inside of the restaurant that all raved about this one item in particular.  Sure, it was big and pretty, but the meat really lacked any distinct flavor.  It was kind of bland, and the spatzle my girl friend opted for on the side was even worse.  Our waiter was kind enough to throw in a complimentary order of pommes frites ("because they really are so good") that were also under-seasoned but which I happily devoured anyway.  Basically, you don't go to a John Besh restaurant and order a burger anyway, right?  SO don't follow our strategy either.

Service: Our waiter was very conversational and a fellow foodie lover.  We even got to talking about great places to eat in Manhattan.  I just wish we spent more time talking about that damn spatzle because the way he described it to my girl friend was totally off.  We had never had the German staple before, so we were surprised to see what looked like macaroni salad on our table instead of the gnocchi he promised us in the totally inaccurate description.  

Atmosphere: A real classy joint that is connected to the Hilton on the border between the French Quarter and the business district.  Every plate is served on top of a wooden carving board, which kind of blends the whole upscale American and hearty German atmosphere as well. There is a full bar also, and happy hour is a must (25 cent oysters and half off drinks and beers).  It feels like a place where business people go to enjoy themselves after a long day of work, checking their briefcases at the revolving door.  I guess you could compare it to the Wall Street crowd in Manhattan, although it's STILL New Orleans we're talking about, so don't worry about it being too stuffy in there.

Value: As I mentioned earlier, I really do believe for the quality and quantity of food, Luke is a great value if you stick to the specials.  Happy Hour is one of those great specials, even if you don't like oysters (down a Sazerac or two) and for dinner, they offer 3-course specials at $23 a pop.  Not bad at all, and I heard super things about their chicken and matzah ball soup (one of the 3-course options to start).  Just don't order that burger everyone keeps talking about!
First time trying Raw Oysters and they were very fresh and tasty. They have great drinks and a cool Happy Hour daily!

The best tasting foods in town. The Étouffée was AMAZING. The Croque-Monsieur or Croque-Madame are to dine for. I definitely recommend giving Lüke a try if you haven't been there. You won't be disappointed.

When I started planning my wedding in New Orleans, finding the reception space was one of the easiest parts.  The fiance and I had been served one of the best meals of our lives at Luke's San Antonio location, so when I asked him what he thought about booking Luke New Orleans for our reception, it was an easy sell.

For your party or reception, Luke is extremely affordable, especially considering the other options in town.  They have two rooms available for rental--one is a private room that can be closed off, suitable for smaller groups, and a semiprivate wine room that's for larger parties.  Our reception will be in the wine room, and we were coincidentally seated nearby, so we could sneak a peek at what it was going to look like.  What did it take to secure our date?  Only a contract saying we would commit to a $1000 minimum, no deposit needed.  Sign me up!

When we signed the contract, I inquired about gluten-free options since the fiance is gluten-intolerant and was told the chef would accommodate all food allergies. Anyone who has an allergy as all-encompassing as gluten will give that statement some major side-eye.  But I'm skeptical no longer.  When we were seated, we asked our server about gluten-free options and he went back into the kitchen to talk to the chef.  "I'm sorry we don't have an actual gluten free menu," he told us when he came back, but he went through EVERY. SINGLE. ENTREE. on the dinner menu and told us if it was safe or how they could make it safe (grilling a fish fillet instead of dredging it in flour, for example).  For gluten-free folks and the people who love them, this is the equivalent of a unicorn sighting.  You are told more often than not you can just have a burger without the bun, or something equally deflating.  In fact, our server was so knowledgeable about gluten, he even joked about bring us a bread basket.

With the menu opened up to him, my fiance chose a dish of house-made bratwurst, pork shank, pork belly and sauerkraut, and I ordered the shrimp and grits.  His entree was a true mountain of meat, each component of it outstanding.  I don't even LIKE sauerkraut and I found myself stealing nibbles here and there.  And the shrimp and grits--ye gods.  I'd had it in San Antonio, so I knew it was good, but it was a pretty excellent reminder.  With bits of Andouille sausage sprinkled into the mix, the fiance and I agreed this one is DEFINITELY going on the wedding day menu. He remarked that usually due to cross-contamination he feels at least a little crummy after he eats at a restaurant, but that his meal at Luke left him without any--er, shall we say, inner turmoil.

Service was wonderful--the word that I keep coming up to describe it is "easy".  Not because it's simple, but because it felt so natural.  We truly felt taken care of during our meal, which is not an easy feat on a busy Friday night.

Speaking of which, if you're going on the weekend (and maybe even not) I would highly recommend reservations.  Running late after my bridal portraits and still needing to dress for dinner, I called Luke and asked if my 6:30 reservation could be moved to 7.  No can do, I was told.  I basically disrobed in a flurry, dressed, and we just short of ran to get there on time.  In fact, en route a passerby yelled at me "Slow down, little lady, you're in New Orleans!"  SORRY BUDDY CAN'T SLOW DOWN MUST GET SHRIMP AND GRITS.

With our stellar experience at Luke New Orleans, I'm looking forward to our reception even MORE now--if that's possible--and I'll update after our wedding day.

I enjoyed a nice lunch at Luke's during a recent visit to Louisiana. I ordered jumbo lump crab ravigote with toasted ciabatta  bread. The crab was excellent the only thing is it comes with a horse radish dressing mixed into the crab and it was very strong. If I went again I would not order it with the dressing although I'm not certain it can be extracted. The corn and crab fritters are a delightful taste of seafood, but crunchy enough to pass for a stand alone afternoon snack. The crispy brussels sprouts were fresh and in season and had great  texture to the meal.

If you have never been to a John Besh restaurant, there is no easier way to be introduced than to spend an early evening at Luke's rightfully acclaimed happy hour. I have eaten my share of oysters (and part of yours) in my day, and a significant percentage of them have been consumed in Louisiana, which is only notable because I've never lived there. If you like your oysters plump, briny, ice cold, well-cleaned and grit free, this is the place to go. It's even better during Happy Hour because they are only $.75 each! I have eaten my way around NO twice last year, and these are my unchallenged winners for best oysters on both visits, even though I ate at several traditional oyster houses each time. If that were not enough, they also offer fried oysters for $1 each during HH, and they are the best I have ever eaten, any time, anywhere. We eventually tried most of the items on the HH menu, and they all exceeded expectations. The specialty cocktails are outstanding, even at full price, but they are a cocktail connoisseur's best value in a city known for impeccable cocktails.

If you are like me you want great service to make it a truly great dining experience. Nicholas was our waiter, and he gave that perfect blend of friendly service and attention to detail that makes a meal into a perfect evening. He's worth asking for.
Fourth time at Luke. Wonderful oysters on half shell! I had shrimp and grits and it was sensational....well seasoned. Great noisy atmosphere. Wonderful wait staff.

Oh my lord. This is food of the heavens. First they start off with warm baguette and butter. You shouldn't fill up on this because there's so much amazing food here but seriously who can turn away fresh bread? I think I ate like 3 baguettes. 

My sister and I split the shrimp and grits for lunch (which is a really good idea, they give you two separate skillets which are ample portions for no extra charge). My waitress described the shrimp and grits as a food "that goes straight to the soul". And boy was she right. I have eaten shrimp and grits many a times, but this dish was a spiritual experience. The grits was equally cheesy and creamy- a consistency I didn't know was possible. Every time I would bring my fork to my mouth a fat string of cheese would follow. This is the life people. The tomato sauce was so flavorful and spicy. This is probably the best thing I've eaten in the world, and I've eaten a lot of things.

Happy hour from 3-6pm is the bomb! Oysters, fried oysters, and beer. What more could I ask for? How about great service from Richie Rich and the staff? If you can ask for his service area, do so. He makes the meal so entertaining. This restaurant is just outside of the French Quarter, but the 10 minute walk is so worth it.

Great food, but slow service. 

We walked in and seated right away, ordered drinks and food immediately. But then waited just about an hour for our main food to come out. 

Such a shame becuase the food is so great! We would come more often over lunch if it didn't take so long.

I give this restaurant 3 out of 5 stars. The service was great. Had some locals that worked there tell us what was good on the menu. I got the shrimp and grits which was delicious but it wasn't enough. The fresh baked bread was good too! We also got gumbo for an appetizer and I bit into something very hard which made me stop eating because I didn't want to lose a tooth. The bread pudding was not good but I was able to return it for the cake with blueberry sauce which was very good. My boyfriend got the stuffed shrimp and peach cobbler. The shrimp  was good but the peach cobbler was not the best I ever had. Overall this was a nice place with great service unwound go again to try something else on the menu.
Loved this restaurant. Probably the best grilled cheese sandwich I've ever had. Also enjoyed some delicious oysters. Very friendly service which made the experience even more enjoyable.
Excellent service and etoufee was awesome . Also the crawfish soup was good as well. Riggidy Row is coming !

Amazing. Fried Oyster salad, crawfish bisque. I'll be dreaming about that salad!! Great service. We walked in with a 9 month old and 4 year old. Were nervous but were seated in the back. Kids behaved, dinner was amazing... wish we would have ordered more off the menu!
Great food, great staff and their happy hour prices cannot be beat.  I recommend the fried oysters and Brussel sprouts ... !
Very tasty dinner and great drinks and service. Recommend the grits, fish, and bread pudding!

Luke is a great place no matter the time  of day. Food is excellent and happy hour is the best in NOLA. Staff is friendly, kind and very helpful with any questions you may have.
Shay the bartender is the best. And you have to sit at the bar down by the oyster shucking. Shucker Sean is awesome. He likes to be called Kenny Stills.
Thanks guys see you soon.
