Since I'm allergic to shellfish, the menu was a bit limited for me--I'd estimate that over half the dishes contain crab, shrimp, or mussels.  However, I was not at all disappointed with my choice.  I ordered the croque madame with frites and my husband had the pressed sandwich of cochon au lait with frites and an excellent hefeweizen.  It's pretty hard to screw up what is essentially a ham and cheese sandwich with an egg on top--but this was absolutely incredible.  The egg was perfectly cooked and I broke the yolk so the whole sandwich had the wonderful flavor of it.  The ham was perfectly sweet and salty, and I'm not sure what they do with the bread to this sandwich but it was melt in your mouth delicious.  The frites were perfectly cooked, and the service was impeccable.

I will dream about this sandwich from afar, and if I'm ever in New Orleans again this will be the first place I visit.
Excellent oysters!  Sit at the bar and view the shucking.  Great beers on tap.
Have dined here twice on my NOLA business trip. Both dishes were exceptional. Service and atmosphere are first class.

tomato basil soup, omg delicious.

bbq chicken flatbread is good when I'm eating it but then I feel sick afterwards.

My bf loves the curry chicken but I'm not a big fan of any of Cosi's sandwiches.

Came here for Brunch on a rainy Saturday while visiting New Orleans. The menu was somewhat meat-heavy, so I ordered "eggs in a jar" - poached eggs over grits with fried shrimp. The presentation of this dish was very cool. Poached eggs were perfect, but the dish was pretty heavy overall. My friend had eggs with ham with a biscuit, and she loved her dish. I took a bite of her biscuit and immediately had to order my own, as the biscuit was incredible, especially with their homemade jam... If I ever find myself at Luke again during brunch, I'd probably just order a biscuit and poached eggs, as I would be really happy eating that again.

Lüke is the "Hotel" restaurant for the Hilton, and what a cool and classy place it is. It has a grand old European feel, with nice hospitality, deep woods, and staff in jackets.

I was here for breakfast recently and received an extra bonus when an old work friend (who I hadn't seen in years) happened to wander in just after me. It was a great time and atmosphere to catch up and contrast my healthy choice with his full on Southern Breakfast.  I'd love to come back and give this place a workout for Lunch or Dinner.

Great oyster half shells.  
Went there for lunch had the Thursday special lunch. 
Jambalaya was ok just a bit too much of pork for my taste
Ordered a dozen oyster half shells and waited for awhile 
It turned out my server forgot to order and left. 
The server who had us after my first server left was quite nice. 
We had to order a half dozen cause we had to head out to the airport. 
Food were nice and the oysters were great.  
Wanted to try more but couldn't. 
By far the worst service i have experienced in New Orleans.  I was disappointed
But i will give it a try again next time i come.  
Hopefully, i will have better experience

The food was amazing and the staff was equally amazing!!! We had the roasted chicken, raw oysters, and shrimp and grits. We also ordered to go for a friend that has several allergies and they made the food to order and didn't give us any trouble! Richie was our waiter and he was very personable!

We would absolutely come here again and highly recommend this place if you are in New Orleans!

I agree with both the good and bad reviews on here.  I think the trick is in ordering.  There are a few standouts and also a few things that should be left alone but if you stick with the tried and true favorites, you'll do just fine.  That would be oysters on the half shell (especially during 50 cent happy hour) and French 75s.  Perfect way to end a long day!  The pork rillette is also phenomenal, I realize I might as well just spread it directly on my love handles rather than eat it but sometimes you just have to indulge, right?  Make sure you let it sit for a few minutes to come to room temp and that's when it gets really good.

Boudin noir, not so great, cochon sandwich, fine but not worth repeating and the Choucroute Maison kind of made me feel like Fred Flinstone.  I have had really indifferent (bartenders) and even downright rude (hostesses) but mostly I just find the servers there either preoccupied, unknowledgeable or overly busy. But I don't go for service, just those perfectly mixed cocktails and briny, cool oysters!

Yumm! My husband and I are huge fans of Besh. We have been to every one of his restaurants and have always left happy. It's not cheap, but worth it. My husband had the chicken and I had the grits. Every bite was delicious.

Ate here tonight.  Took over 30 minutes to get a personal pan pizza and a tuna hoagie.  Waitress did not write down order so I question if she forgot to put it in.  In fact, after about 30 minutes, I asked if it was almost ready.  She said the pizza takes over 30 minutes to cook!  Couldn't wait to see the pizza after it cooked 30 minutes but I can say the pizza was excellent.  Tuna hoagie was ok.  I also ordered fries which she obviously forgot to put in and brought them out when I was almost finished my meal.  They were undercooked.  She never came back so I could ask for ketchup.  I would recommend that if you are NOT going to write down an order, get it right.
The eggs in a cup-- with either shrimp or soft shell crab is exceptional-- eggs Benedict with a twist! Chef john besh rocks!

5 stars for the service ! Wonderful southern hospitality...
Now let's talk about the food. 
The gnocchi was delicious with a really nice creole tomato sauce. The veggie risotto was flavorful. 
They do make vegetarian pasta/ rice dish which is not on the menu for the vegetarians. 
The bread pudding was ok not that great, a little too sweet for my liking.
Simply the best Cajun/Creole food I've had. The freshest oysters and the best shrimp and grits you will ever have. Husband and I had to go back TWICE, it was that good!

Really good. My husband and Is a real foodie and since we were on vacation in New Orleans we looked up good local restaurants on Yelp. He had the shrimp escaroff. He loved it. We got take out since the kiddo only wanted pizza ( what else !!!). Only drawback is that they are busy so it took 45 minutes to get our order ( they warned us in advance ) still it was long time to wait 
We will be back tmrw to get the shrimp grits

Gotta say this last time as a bust.. We come to NOLA once a year and have eaten here each visit. This time though nothing worked. The food was cold, the wait staff was not attentive and the overall experience poor.

Of course, another fantastic dinner of shrimp & grits, followed by a mousse-like dense steamed chocolate dessert. Great service provided by Melanie (& Chi)!  If Richie Rich is your waiter, ask to move tables.
Food was great. A little bit pricey for what they offer, but the service was phenomenal. The environment and location were great too.

Luke's was by far one of the best restaurants we visited hands down in our stay in New Orleans! Food was superb, there is not one thing on that menu that won't blow your socks off and taste buds away! Every bite of everything is just bursting with flavor! A little on the pricey side especially compared to most places but Luke's will not disappoint and is more than worth your money! Customer service here was a real taste of souther hospitality, oh and by the way they also had amazing drinks! This is a must go!

I looked forward to Monday lunch my whole trip because I was so excited to get the Tabasco honey chicken here at Luke. What a disappointment! Let's start at the beginning: the hostess was very friendly and promptly seated us. The waiter came over quickly enough and we had water in a timely fashion. However that is where it ended. My boyfriend ordered a beer and it was at least 10 min before he got it, that was after the waiter came back and we had to ask where it was... the waiter did not come back much after that. I ordered the crab bisque which was actually the best part of the whole meal. I recommend it if you decide to go! Then comes the lunch I have been looking forward too. It looks delicious and is presented in a cute little cast iron pan. I took a piece of the chicken out and put it on a plate to cut it, it was like trying to cut rubber. It was so dry and had no flavor  the only saving grace of the dish was the rice and beans. They were tolerable. Maybe I caught the cooks on an off day? I could not believe when I looked up must do's and eats, that this is what came up! Save your money and go elsewhere...

An amazing concept that delivers! 

I had wanted to try Luke for awhile now, but we couldn't get down to NO until this month.. Luke made it worth the wait.. 

My wife and I love France and the food, while Luke is a mix of classic French and German flair the French side is definitely the shining star here.. 

The decor is a bit simplistic, but in a good way. Light colored hardwoods and shared bench seating are both warm, comfortable and inviting.

The menu is is a bit German, a good amount of French and a splash of Creole added. 

We started out with the gumbo which was perfectly balanced and seasoned well. I'm not a seafood lover and I have to say this was the best gumbo I have ever tasted, my wife agreed. 

Oh before I forget.. The French bread and butter were done so well it would have made Lionel Poilane smile..

For mains my wife had the crab ravioli and I had the ribeye, both were excellent.

The pasta looked and tasted handmade and the sauce was creamy yet delicate, while the crab was fresh and large.

The ribeye I had was great, I want to address the comment below about  the ribeye being mostly fat.. Ribeyes are just that, a well marbled cut of meat which lends itself well to being slow roasted (Prime rib, Standing rib roast) when grilled the fat will be more prominent especially at lower temps.. Maybe he got a bad cut, but knowing your proteins is half the battle.. Back to the steak, I enjoyed my ribeye and the presentation on a wooden cutting board is a nice touch, however I did not care for the béarnaise sauce.. The fries were a bit salty for me, but I'm a hypersensitive to course salts so some might like them.. After brushing the salt off the taste was spot on and tasted like they were fried in a good oil not just plain ole veg.

For dessert we split the bread pudding and were pleasantly surprised at the souffle style presentation.. The taste was good, however the ice cream could use some work and I would try another dessert next time.. Even with the ice cream, it's still a very, very good dessert, I'm just more of a chocolate lover.. 

Drinks at Luke are AMAZING! It's not the typical NO drinks, these are high end fine cocktails.. The French 75 is well worth the price of admission and the brandied cherries that are put in random drinks are out of this world good.. Also, any time someone goes to the trouble to put a super high end Italian steam pump espresso machine in his restaurant I'm impressed.. The latte my wife had was better than I can make at home using peaberry Jamaican blue mountain.. 

For the value, concept and variety this is one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans..

Five Stars

I've been going to Cosi for lunch every now and then, and I think that the decor and "fast food" feel psycologically tricks people into rating this place lower than it deserves. The flatbread is hot, soft, and fresh. I think the place is good because of the flatbread. The greek salad is not bad and the tomato basil soup is tasty! Check it out.
Shawn is the BEST!!! Ate shrimp and grits, shrimp and cavatelli, and bread pudding dessert for dinner. All were beyond amazing!!!

We were greeted by a ho-hum hostess and a waiter in a dirty jacket who stuck his elbow in my wife's face as he poured my coffee.  Don't get the eggs in a jar as they have goopy texture problem. Dry tough sausage and watery chocolate for the beignets provided the finishing touches to a perfect breakfast!  Couldn't get out of there fast enough.

WOW I am never coming back nor taking my friends and family foodies here.

I tried this place today for the first time and I love trying new places and coming back if it was both a great food and service experience. Our waiter was not very talkative, he just took the order and brought the food. That is totally fine with me. But when we put our napkins down, and sat for him to come over and ask us if we were finished or wanted dessert... He didn't... He walked over and picked up one plate, and I told him we are ready for the check. He didn't clear the table like he should have, he picked up one plate, ignored and didn't acknowledge me and walked off. My friend said to me, I don't think he heard you. Well obviously he did because he brought the check and put it on the table and walked off!!! He NEVER said a word. Never said THANK YOU. Nothing. From the very beginning I just felt like he hated his job or was having a bad day, so my friends and I were being considerate and just tried to look past his grumpy miserable face. So we asked to split the check and he came back asking about tip to make sure we tip on the card since we split it etc... So basically he was assuming that we might forget or not tip or something. Then he came back to drop off the cards and we still gave him a 20% tip because we are just too nice and know what it's like to be in this industry. We no longer are in the service restaurant industry but used to be in the past for 10 years! So when he dropped the cards off, I asked him "are you having a bad day?" He smiled and said no im not having a bad day. Then walks off. It was the most uncomfortable smile... Because he never smiled until then. Honestly I felt like he was making assumptions from the start when we sat down. He did give us a look when we said we were going to share everything because as foodies, you want to try more than one plate to yourself but not over order and be disgusting full... And be able to go onto the next food stop later. But seriously I'm probably under describing the whole situation. He was so rude. You can be rude without talking and making the rude actions and not acknowledging. Just terrible, we should not have to feel like we didn't belong, not welcomed or didn't want to be waited on or if waiting on us was just a miserable hassle. No one should have to feel like that!

We went to Restaurant R'evolution and Commander's Palace the previous two days and the food was amazing and the service was more than perfect. Maybe you should send your staff and pay for them to eat there to see how it is to be a nice friendly waiter....
I'm just speechless at today's experience and restaurants like this need to be aware that there are countless other restaurants offering both amazing wonderful food WITH good service. 

On to the next amazing restaurant on my list. 
Don't care to ever come back.

Best grab and go breakfast for sure! Sandwiches are delectable and unique combinations which are different every day! Fairly priced and will cure any hangover or just start your day off perfect! Friendly staff and funky atmosphere.
Honestly I don't go here for the food, I go to this Cosi to study. I think it's great for studying. The food is just an added benefit!

Very great decorations and service. The place looks awesome. 

We first ordered the half dozed jumbo gulf shrimp. I'm not from the gulf but I didn't think that they were that jumbo. They were also a nightmare to peel and eat but the cocktail sauce was really good. Kind of pricey for the size and quality of the shrimp. One was mangled and awkward looking.

I ordered the gumbo just to have a Nola dish with my meal. Unfortunately the gumbo itself was room temperature, but the rice that they put on top was refrigerator cold. As soon as i stirred it, it was completely cold. Kind of sad since I was paying $6 for 4 bites of gumbo. Small portions here too.

We then ordered the pate and the green salad. The pate was good, and was a huge portion. The pickled sides were probably the best part. I had never tried pate so I can't be the best judge but I liked it. It had a mild flavor to it. The salad was $17 and was 5 leafs of butter lettuce drenched in a basic sauce. 

Overall this place isn't bad, it just seems like one of those places where you pay for the ambiance and not the food.

We got there for a Friday brunch. The service is great and the food was pretty tasty as well. I ordered the fried oyster salad and find the bacon to be the highlight of the dish. My pork schnitzel was lightly battered and deep fried. It comes with a mushroom Sauce. Personally I like it prepared without any sauce but the sauce actually is not bad at all. My hubby ordered a seafood bullion with creole flavor and he loved it.

I tried to call this place to make sure they were open.  All I got was a generic mechanized recording to leave a message.  I did not get a call back.  This is at 6:20 pm on a Wednesday.  I guess they went out of business.

I've been eating here for 10 years or something like that and I've had various luck.  I've always enjoyed coming here and I have to insist that the original menu and it's variations for the first few years were much better than it is now.  They're going through some changes and it's painful.  

I had come here in December and had a terrible meal and the GM invited us back to try them again.  I was kinda thinking that before he wrote me that it had been my last visit.  We ate here last night and had a very good experience.  Of course, we received some special attention (the service last time wasn't good) last night was terrific.  We liked everything but the duck dish.  Even the oysters, still not nearly the best in NOLA, were decent.  

I liked the burrata salad a lot, it's really well balanced and was perfectly dressed.  Miriam's Luke salad similarly so but over salted.  Still edible but over salted.  

I liked her shrimp and grits a lot.  Too shrimpy for me, not my thing, but I appreciated it anyway.  She loved it.  I liked the grits and sausage.  The duck dish is too much.  Too sweet, too rich, too much rice, too salty.  It's cloying in the end.  The duck was prepared perfectly and it was delicious.  I loved the texture and preparation of the rice too.  I doubt anyone finishes this dish.  1/3rd of the rice, a little more confit and maybe a small pile of those great Brussels sprouts on the side would be perfect.  

We love their French press so we finished with some coffee and some of the best creme brûlée in NOLA.  The biscotti is a complete miss.  Heavy and made by someone who doesn't have a clue.  These are easy to make, by the way.  

Here's a big problem though.  It's a corporate restaurant.  Upper management here is ruining this place.  They're still serving the worst bread in NOLA, they know it, and are still serving it.  When you have people making decisions for your restaurant who don't work there and don't know anything about food you're in trouble.  It's just about the money.  It makes it impossible to create and execute a clear vision about the food your serving and why you're serving it.  How can you serve a product you know is bad and do it anyway?  Can't be 4 stars until they decide that their staff can make decisions about the food and they focus their vision about what the heck this place is supposed to be about.  Says a lot about the Besh group.... sadly.

I've been a few times when they first opened. Food was good not great but good enough for me to return. The wait is ridiculous and that's why I stopped going for like a year.. Went today and ordered cheesesteak rolls and beef egg foo young. They changed the cheesesteak rolls. It was mushy inside and it was some type of pasty sauce and onions. Not a piece of steak at all. I cut open my 2nd roll because I wanted to examine it and again no steak. The it had a chicken bouillon flavor. So weird didn't want to finish it. The beef is the egg foo young was tough and flavorless.. The egg part was also mushy.  I normally eat at the Chinese store across from overbrook hs but they are a cash o my establishment. I didn't have any cash on me. Their food may not be halal but their food is 10x's better. Not going back to Chan halals again... waste of my time and money. Now I'm sitting here hungry.

Place is consistently good, fresh and delicious. Kani Salad and Sticky Ribs are still my go to favorites. Philly Roll is one of my favorite rolls if I want something plain and simple. Their food is not only tasteful but also very artful. It's a very cool place with good service and flavorful dishes.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in the city.  I've been over and over with nothing but excellent service and food.  
Their burger and fries are amazing.  Also, the braised lamb with gnocchi and vegetables was unbelievable.  I kept grabbing pieces of bread to soak up the sauce.  The paneed veal cutlet is delicious, as are the croque madame and corn and crawfish bisque.  I definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone in the CBD or surrounding areas.
Don't forget to try the Saint Charles Streetcar or  Champagne au Peche.
And when you finish, not matter how full you are, please get the bread pudding.  I have tried it all over the city including Mr. B's and Commander's.  This bread pudding is to die for!
You get what you pay for... the shrimp and Gritts are second to none. The chargrilled oysters are also some of the best in town.

I am honestly still stunned by my experience last night, this place is not what it used to be.  My husband and I went there for his 3rd annual birthday dinner at Hachi.  Both of our previous experiences were stellar so we have high expectations.  The night started off poorly when our waiter did not seem to know what he was talking about, and basically had to go to the kitchen multiple times to speak to the chef on my persistence after he made up answers and then admitted that he didn't really know.  There was also waiter confusion, another waiter came by to take our order and then they both kept coming by.  The sushi rolls came out soggy and falling apart.  The entrees did not meet the descriptions listed in the menu, tasted terrible, and looked like take out from a Chinese restaurant.  We sent them back and left in search of another place to celebrate my husband's birthday.  RIP Hachi.

This place was sooooo great.  The servers were so nice, and I ordered 
jumbo Louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" (shrimp and grits)...Amazing

And for dessert...wait for it....Brennan's Bread Pudding with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce.  After the rest of the table that didn't order any dessert saw me take 2 bites 2 of the 3 dug in, and finished it off, the 3rd person stayed away only because they had allergies to nuts.

I will be back FOR SURE!!
The Brussel sprouts were so crispy, with the honey and Serrano peppers that I had to ask for the recipe to try to make it myself at home.
Great food and service. You must try when in NOLA. Our server Price was excellent. The bread pudding is excellent!

Had the tabasco honey fried chicken with beans and rice. Wow! Delicious and so filling...not really spicy at all. I couldn't even finish half of it even though the portion size is medium at best. Somewhat loud restaurant but overall, would eat there again. German with a louisiana twist is how it was described.

When this place opened I thought it was too good to be true, to have a decent sushi place so close to my house I could walk there.  Well I was wrong.  This place has unbelievable sushi!  It's seriously so good and up there with some of the best I've had in Philly.  They have a great menu with tons of creative options and some really unique sushi rolls ("The Boston Monster" is a personal favorite) Once you walk into this place you would never think you are in a Shopping Center in Chalfont.  Really great place to grab sushi, so grab your friends and a few beers from the Blue Dog and have yourself a good time at Hachi!

Food was good. Ambience was nice and lively. This place is 5 stars compared to half the places I ate, just because I'm pretty sure it was clean. -3 stars for the service, but at every place I ate at the staff had terrible attitudes. +1 for the rabbit pate. I wish the grits didn't have jalapeños in them, but the shrimp and grits were good. +1 for cleanliness.

One more checkmark on the list of Besh restaurants!  This cute little brasserie makes me think of a bustling foreign area (I've never been to France but that's the definitely the vibe they're going for).  The seafood is on ice front and center at the bar, the small tables are quite close together, and people were coming in from the rain and shaking off, it kind of felt like a movie :)  We had a party of 4, and our two waiters were busy busy busy that night.  One of them was named Kenny, but I'm not sure of the other one.  They were helpful, but not the most attentive.  We started off with 2 dozen oysters, char-broiled, and an order of the Brussels sprouts (GET THEM THEY ARE SO GOOD).  Drinks were had by all, mostly wine, but I think someone had a scotch or whiskey maybe.  For meals, two of our party had the steak, I had the roast chicken, and the other person had an oyster salad.  Everyone else's meals were very good, mine was good but overly salty and the menu said it came with vegetables but there were no vegetables to be seen, just potatoes and chicken.  I was bummed that we were going to an event and couldn't take extra food home in a doggie-bag, because the chicken was great.   For dessert one couple shared the apple pie, and we shared the creme brulee.  So good!  
 Glad I got to experience this little Besh restaurant, overall happy with the service, food, and atmosphere.

We went here for the happy hr specials. Raw oysters were 75 cents each and 1.25 for fried ones. They were big n juicy. Had a three doors cocktail n hubby had a white wine for half off. The cocktail was ok only, nothing spectacular.  Server was nice and professional.

Luke is okay. The food was too fishy for my liking. We ordered the blue crab salad (returned it) gumbo, and jambalaya. 
The customer service was really good although we did not know who our sole server was, we had at least 4 people come to our table. 

The bread pudding was the bomb!

The food was amazing, the ambiance was charming,  the service was impeccable and the prices were very reasonable!  I had an amazing shrimp and grits and my husband's oysters were sublime.  This place is a gem.  Enjoy!

Service was fine but the food was a great disappointment. Ordered the shrimp etoufee but it was really pasta etoufe. 5 small shrimp and a lot of pasta. I'd expect this in New Mexico but not New Orleans. Manager said that's the order but didn't charge me. I didn't want no charge, I just wanted a good meal

Second time in 2 days.  Dinner was outstanding - rabbit pate, shrimp and grits, and oven roasted chicken were excellent.  Brunch menu selection excellent.  Quality of ribeye excellent but under seasoned.  Medium rare steak came out overcooked to medium.  The oyster salad was excellent but gritty.  Mussels outstanding.  Service provided by Sarah and Andrew was excellent.

This is a very nice brasserie.  I happened upon this place purely by accident when I arrived in town on Friday.  I had to stop at the local tailor and had an hour to kill.  I didn't realize at the time that it was a john besh restaurant.  I entered about 2pm on a Friday and was the only person there.  The service was excellent. I sat at the bar, it was a pretty open layout with a lot of dark wood.  I had some raw oysters that were briny and fresh and tried a glass of reasonably priced champagne.   I tried their foie gras terrine after that which was served nicely with some crackers.  It was a very good light lunch on a hot summer day.  I will go again.

While the food was excellent the service and prices left something to be desired for me.  I was seated underneath a particularly cold air conditioning vent and when I asked them to turn down the air I was told "that's just the way it is".  The food was a little on the expensive side for what it was, but i'd still recommend this spot if you're in the area.
The PJ oysters are very fresh and tasty. We also ordered a shrimp entree which is good but not excellent. Recommend the raw bar.

I've been to the one is San Antonio and I thought I would give this one in New Orleans a try.  Needless to say, in both places they ruined my order.  I'm never going to another Luke's!

Food was ok.
Service sucks!

With the vibe of a brasserie and a kitchen cranking out southern classics, it's hard to go wrong. The service was slow, but they quickly appeased these customers by bringing out complementary bread pudding (perfectly crisp with hints of caramel- seriously delicious).

We ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" and the Étouffée. The Étouffée was slightly dry and could use a more complex flavor profile. The shrimp was the clear winner as it was served on a bed of roasted jalapeño cheese grits and Andouille & green onion sausage. No further explanation required!

I wouldn't make a point of visiting this restaurant again with so many stones left unturned in NOLA, but I thoroughly enjoyed trying it once.

I went to breakfast at Luke by the suggestion of the hotel I was staying at.  WOW!  The very best coffee I have ever had...no really!  They have some kind of bacon that is from another world altogether...twice smoked and yummy!  The servers were so friendly and helpful.  One of them made great suggestions for local sites and sounds to catch while I was in town.  I think this place is a perfect example of how New Orleans dining scene is world class.  I can't wait to go back to New Orleans and eat dinner here.

While hotel restaurants aren't generally my favorite places to imbibe, I'm a fan of Luke, which was conveniently attached to the St. Charles Hilton. 

We stopped in here several times for cocktails before embarking on adventures, and found extremely friendly service and tasty concoctions both times. The first time, I went with a house cocktail, which was sweet and unique. Can't recall the name ... 

The second time, we caught happy hour, and the bartender let us indulge in several mimosas at happy hour prices. Score!

Their menu, although meat-heavy, looked like it offered some interesting selections, worth trying,

Excellent, excellent food. Great service. Only issueh the place gets a little too noisy sometimes.

I would highly recommend:
Assiette de charcuteri (OMG!!)  Very unusual presentation,. The selection, the taste... Not enough words to  describe it...  
Fried oysters and avocado salad - I would call it Luke's version of Caesar salad. )

With the exception of Shrimp and Grits (had much better in NOLA). this restaurant is solid 5 stars.

-Great Atmosphere 
-Great Service 
- Terrific Food
- Loved!
I seriously don't know where to begin.  This wonderful John Besh creation is purely delightful.  

The location is only a few blocks from Canal Street but seems like miles from the tourist feel of the Quarter tourist restaurants.  

Upon entering we were greeted promptly and warmly.  We had reservations and in just a few minutes she walked us back to our table almost in back (which was really great)

The tables are fairly close together so chances are very good you will hear your neighbors' conversation so be warned.  The overall feel reminds me of something from time past; the restaurant is in a beautiful old building with many unique details on the walls and I love, love, love the bar in the middle of the room.  The whole feel was very lively and energetic yet in our little table from afar still relaxed.

Onto the food.... I had built Chef Besh up so high in my mind I honestly thought he couldn't live up to it. Too unrealistic.  He did live up to my expectations and surpassed my dreams for a perfect dinner.

Appetizer - Baked Oysters - sublime

Appetizer 2 - Crab bisque - made many other crab bisque I have had pale in comparison (more soupy than bisque-y by the way)

Appetizer 3 - (hey we were sharing!) Cold Shrimp- these were very good quality.  Only odd thing was I had to ask for horseradish / only served with ketchup.  A note on the horseradish.  If you like horseradish - order some on the side here just to try.  I don't know why or how but it is the best horseradish you will ever try and the most potent.  I wish I could get my hands on it to keep at my house. 

Entrée 1 - Hamburger.  Just so wow you can't imagine how good until you taste it.  The meat is probably the tastiest hamburger meat I have ever had and I have had some pretty great burgers.

Entree 2 - Blue Crab Cavatelli - pasta with red sauce with blue crab.  Just perfect.

Dessert - are you kidding?  After 3 appetizers and tasting a little of 2 Entrees dessert wasn't even a consideration.

Bottom line: Go, go, go, go, go, go!  (but make a reservation)

Such a nice location! Both the Interior and exterior were very inviting. I bought grilled cheese and tomato soup, perfect for a rainy day. It was delicious! The cashier was very friendly and offered many different options. I like this location and will definately come back if in the area again.
Good food.  Slightly better prices than Qdoba. Not worth getting the peppers and onions on the burrito though.  Ruins the fresh taste of the white rice with lime.

My soulmate and I are planning to begin our first thru hike in New Zealand this November. We have been doing a lot of research and wanted some help choosing footwear for me and packs for the both of us. We began in the shoe department and were assisted by a friendly employee named Eric. Eric cleared up a lot of my questions and made me feel more confident in what style and size of shoe I should go with. I thought about it over the weekend, and it is because of his advice that I have made my decision and will be purchasing from REI. After we finished in shoe department, we went to try on a couple of packs. 

We were both thinking about going with an ultra lightweight pack to try and save on weight for our 1,800-mile journey. When we arrived at the backpack department, we were kindly greeted by another phenomenal employee, Jake. Jake was so knowledgeable about packs from his own, personal experiences and relieved us of a lot of the anxiety we had about which packs were right for us. Jake sized me for my pack and made specific recommendations for my body type. He also reminded us of the importance of comfort and talked us into considering a heavier pack. Jake not only made us feel better about what direction to go with our packs, he also brightened our day and reminded us of the how beautiful human connection can be. 

We definitely were not expecting to meet such wonderful people when we entered REI this weekend, but we will be shopping here as we gear up for our future adventures to support this sort of customer sevice. Thank you for employing such amazing people!

Food is good, waiter not!.  Their wines by the glass are overpriced! So I ordered a Sauvignon blanc for $12... Bill arrives and was charged $14. I asked the waiter if he would double check for me. He brings me a menu with the $12 printed as I had seen and proceeded to tell me that it was a misprint and that the wine was indeed $14!
Wow, that took some nerve, really? So, I deducted two bucks from his tip.

So this review is for the happy hour only - as my group did not eat dinner, but just enjoyed the happy hour specials - ie 25c Oysters!!! that's right a dozen for 3 bucks in an old bistro type setting.  

This deal is every day between 3-6, drinks are half off  (wow looks like according to another review they've upped their prices due to the Oil Spill, I was there just as the spill happened).  

Definitely give the house made beer a try it won't disappoint.  Overall its hard to get a better happy hour deal than this from a pretty classy spot.

Loved our brunch here. Food and service were great and while it was one of the pricier meals of the trip (mostly due to the drinks, not the reasonably priced entrees), it was certainly worth it.

I was craving a burger but was hesitant to get something that I can get anywhere. Our waiter promised that it would be different than your average bar burger, though, and he was definitely right. In addition to being absolutely massive, the ingredients were so fresh and the fries were also prepared perfectly. 

As much as I enjoyed my burger, part of me wishes I had ordered some of the other dishes I sampled. My friend's fried chicken and tabasco honey biscuit was to die for and, to my pleasant surprise, not too spicy. If I ever come back, that's what I'm getting. 

I'd come back but I'm not a huge fan of this part of the downtown/CBD area, which is a little soulless compared to the rest of the city. That probably sounds a little douchey but as a visitor with a finite amount of time in town, I'm not looking to spend my time surrounded by 9-5 office buildings.

Ambience perfect
Staff needs improvement 
Location perfect
Cocktails delicious
German starter surprisingly good 
Food ... well this is the kind of place you pay 25 dls for a salad and when you specify no bacon because you have an allergic reaction to it an they bring bacon on it because kitchen forgot or waiter forgot who knows but makes  you think is it worth paying 25 dls for the salad and after you request for a fresh salad because you think they will do a fresh salad with no bacon and they only remove the bacon and you find a piece of bacon  again !! ... is it worth paying 25 dls for this salad?  No!! 
I loved the place but imagine they missed this huge detail and I will end up in a the hospital not worth it !!

The Silo Eatery-Coffee-and Bakery is a great place to stop and have breakfast or lunch. As a retired employee of the school district I was well aware of the quality of the food as I used to work at the downtown main office which housed the first Core Cafe. The eatery as it was referred to by my friend that I met there for lunch, actually works at the site and assists clients with having events at the building as well as several divisions of the School District to conduct training and other culinary demonstrations. I was able to take a tour of the facility with my friend and took several pics of the well appointed decor that surrounds the training area and where the events are held. For Lunch we got the Margherita flatbread and the Haystack sandwich which is offered half or whole with several choices of sides. Everything is made to order on premises and is fresh. Also they have a wonderful choice of salads daily and several fresh baked pastries with an in-house pastry chef. Today they had several cookies with seasonal fun decorations on them. They also have fresh cupcakes and fresh Jeffrey's brand coffees available. This cafe is tucked away in the Silo bend office complex and can be accessed by anyone. Hidden Gem would best describe this place. The Menu changes weekly and there is a digital board for you to view or check the website.  They also can cater for your office as well. Check them out if you are in the area for your next quick bite.  They offer indoor and outdoor seating. The cafe was very clean and all the employees were very helpful. The cost for two for lunch was about with one drink and a water was only $14!

well sure enough my church went back to nola another year, and i just had to come to lukes again!

this time i went for dinner with a group of 10.  They took my last minute reservation and seated us promptly.

since it was dinner, and i already had  my softshell crab for the week, i decided to go with the traditional roast chicken and potatoes.  it was delicious!  a very tender half chicken, with whipped potatos inside, on top a bed of green beans, bacon, and some au jus.  the "only" negative i have about this is there seemed to be a little excessive oil in the dish.  im not sure if this was from the bacon or au jus, but still the dish was fantastic!

among other things i saw, the jagerschnitzel only lookd medicore, but my friends generally liked it.  the croque monsiuer looked pretty good, and the pork hotpot(pork belly, rib, knuckle, and potatos) tasted pretty good as well.

lukes has earned a permanent spot in my book!

We both enjoyed our meals, although I wish the portions were a little bigger. We were sat next to gentleman that had less then stellar service. He said he was sitting, waiting for his server for almost 30 minutes. We didn't have any problem with service. 

We did have some oysters and they small, but good. I would have no problem going back here for oysters. 

For an entree, I had a lobster and it was cooked perfectly...only issue was that it was a small lobster so I was't full after eating it. 

She got the fish and enjoyed it. She did ask for brussel sprouts to be grilled instead made crispy and they happily complied. She did enjoy her meal.

We will go back...very nice atmosphere and experience for us.

If I were smart, I'd lie and say this place stinks and should be avoided (so that it won't be impossible to book in the future), but I will be honest and give Luke the five stars it deserves.  

The food is fantastic and the service attentive, but the best deal by far is the happy hour when you can stuff yourself with raw oysters or scrumptious fried oysters for almost free.  The wines by the glass are half price, but I found them disappointing.  The cocktails are also half price.  the ambiance is posh but the service is not snooty.  The one weird thing is that I asked for fresh grated pepper and was told they did not have one that was operable. WTH?  Small quibble though.  

The brunch is also outstanding even if it's a bit pricey.

Pizza isn't all that great. Burgers are decent, but what makes Jerzees great is the beer and the service. Wonderful people work there and the selection of beer there is pretty amazing for a smaller place. So pizza gets 2 stars but service and beer saves the day.

Very disappointing. The waiter seemed rushed. He didn't answer my questions about what i ordered correctly, so i ended up not getting what i was expecting. Our lattes were luke warm. No pun intended. As well as the food. It came out very quickly and my friends croque monseiur was not even melted in the middle. I got baked or fried kale when i was expecting wilted. The server asked my friend (as she was putting food in her mouth) if she was all done eating and did she need a box?!?!?!?? Not what i expected from JB. Think ill steer clear of celebrity chefs from now on...

The food was very authentic to the chef. Their fries were hand made and were very good. The pasta noodles were also handmade. Got their croquette madame and the shrimp pasta. I would def recommend getting the croquette madame because the flavors of everything together was so good. Although, it is a heavy meal. The pasta was very good and worth it because the shrimps in the pasta were big and fat with lots of meat!

I must say this is the BEST ..BY FAR in BUCKS COUNTY and you can tell
This chef has been professionally trained by the best. Soooo Impressed. Who knew in Chalfont, PA you would find Nobu and Morimoto...

My meal at Lüke was by far, hands down, my favorite meal while in New Orleans. I was in town for a bachelorette party, and we decided to come here for a nice dinner together. When we walked in, we were greeted enthusiastically and seated right away. Since the staff recognized that we were here on a special occasion, the manager personally brought out a round of champagne on the house, congratulating the bride on her upcoming wedding. Amazing hospitality right from the start!

The way our reservation time worked out, we got to enjoy the last fifteen minutes of happy hour: fifty cent oysters and half price drinks. Many of the ladies ordered multiple drinks at once to last through the rest of the evening, which the waiter had no problem with. The oysters were ice-cold and fresh, served with cocktail sauce, horseradish, and lemon wedges. The texture was velvety soft, with a wonderfully tangy taste with little to no brine. I usually dislike seafood because of that salty sea taste, but these were cleaned very well. The other ladies were also very happy with their drinks, notable ones included the Riverbend and St. Charles Streetcar. 

For my entree, I ordered the shrimp and grits after seeing all of the stellar reviews. It definitely lives up to the hype. The plump shrimp was paired well with the sauce made from Andouille and green onion sausages, and the jalapeño cheese grits were amazing. The cheese makes the grits more savory, and you get that flavorful kick from the jalapeños. A bite of that with a piece of juicy shrimp on top is divine. The dish is quite rich and a little on the salty side, so make sure you have a full glass of water ready. While the plate may look small when you get it, it is quite filling. 

We finished off with dessert, and this was what made this meal one of the best I've had. Usually one of three courses of a meal end up being subpar, but the bread pudding was the best bread pudding I've ever had. Coming from the south, I've had a fair share too. Brendan's Bread Pudding is exceptional. The bread is fluffy and soft, giving it an airy texture that doesn't just taste like a sweetened, compacted piece of dense bread. Instead, it's more like a cake in airiness and soaked in the delicious hot buttered pecan sauce. This creates the great flavor of this dessert, with caramelized nutty notes, as well as what tastes like toffee. The vanilla ice cream on top keeps things from getting too sweet and mellows out the pecan topping from being too overpowering. 

When we were ready for our bill, we asked the waiter if we could split the bride's check evenly amongst our own split checks. After waiting for twenty minutes, the waiter came by to tell us that the computer was having issues and wasn't splitting the bride's check the way we wanted it to. So in order to apologize for our wait, he comped the bride's meal entirely so that the computer would be able to split our checks and pay separately. This was a sweet gesture that they insisted upon, and we really appreciated their effort to make things right. 

Lüke is fabulous, and I would definitely come here again and recommend it to everyone I know in the area! Quality food, quality service!

Great breakfast spot..food was top notch, did not give 5 stars, other than the hostess claimed it would be 20 min wait when 10 + tables were open the entire time. We ate at the bar and service was great..

This review is for the pizza and service only.  A friend on Yelp recommended coming here for the pizza.  We are glad we did.  Pizza was good, half pepperoni/ half sausage.  The crust was thin and perfect.  The rest of the pizza was very good, but I've had better.  It was a little greasy, wish we had tried the plain.
The waitresses were both super attentive and friendly.  It seems like a nice local place to go.  We went on a Friday night and the crowd seemed to be a twenty to fifty something crowd...there was even a young family getting pizza.  Wish this place was a little closer, we would come more often.

4.5 review for happy hour.  The 75 cent raw oysters are surprisingly very good for the price.  Been to tons of oyster happy hours all over the US and this was probably the best one.  The fried oysters were hot and delicious.   Pate was a good balance of flavors. Cocktails were on point.  Brussel sprouts were okay but hey you cant please everyone with everything.

We went here for brunch on Sunday before the final Saints game.  We made reservations for  a party of 6 -- and we all had different items from the Brunch menu.  I had the Southern Breakfast and was able to substitute their hash browns from the grits -- fabulous option!  My daughter also had this and she was able to get a fruit cup instead of potatoes -- and the cup was filled with berries (blue, straw and black) and melons (cantaloupe and honeydew) which was a wonderful choice for her.  We had a burger at the table as well as the eggs in a jar -- it was exactly as others have described.  I would recommend this restaurant for anyone who is visiting the city of New Orleans.  A bit pricy -- but for Sunday Brunch -- well worth it!

I really want to like this place more than I do. The host staff could be nicer but I get the impression that they're so busy they don't really care if they're welcoming or not. I've had better experiences during lunch in general then happy hour or dinner. The bar area is not separated by much from the dining area and so if you're seated at the bar you tend to get jostled a lot from behind when it's full. That's a real turn off for me. Food's tasty, staff a little cold in general. Oysters are a good happy hour deal by local standards and excellent when compared to Florida and other cities. The bisque is one of the best I've ever had. The beer is definitely worth a try, if you're interested.

I had the pleasure of visiting Luke on my mini-vacation (more like food-cation) to New Orleans. The restaurant is inside the Hilton and I will tell you, the only reason we stopped here was because I WANTED MY SHRIMP AND GRITS DAMMIT! 
(pause) And boy did I get them!!
The hostess promptly sat us and we were acknowledged and served in a timely manner. Our server was great. Just awesome. The restaurant itself is very nice. At first glance, you don't really appreciate how nice it is, but as I sat and looked around, I realized how nice it was. Very cozy and intimate. I wasn't here with a man but if I was, I would definitely go back to Luke. The shrimp and grits was the 2nd best thing I ate in New Orleans. OMG it was so good, as soon as I got back home I went and bought some grits! You will gain at least 10 lbs foolin around in New Orleans! 
The only reason I took off one star is because it was so expensive! $22 for some shrimp n grits???? Haysoos Christo!!! 
Other than that, great restaurant, great service. Will definitely return the next time I visit.

Had two very well behaved kids with us and they said they wouldn't have a seat for 1 hr when it was evident there was plenty of seating available. They could have just told us kids aren't welcome. Hostess even fumbled around with the lie
This used to be my regular lunch spot until I got fed up with the turkey and brie sandwiches. The honey mustard is carelessly distributed on the flatbread so the sandwich is very dry and tasteless.

We went there last May upon recommendation of our daughter and son-I law.  It was awesome- great menu, excellent food  and service.  It's a small place but definitely worth going to.  Will definitely be back.

For the past few weeks, I've been craving the crab omelet.  Went in once but there weren't any seats at the bar and no open tables with a 30 minute wait.  Went back a few weeks later and was able to get a table.  Unfortunately, I was really disappointed that the menu changed and the crab omelet wasn't even on the menu.  I double checked to see if they could make it but they couldn't.  :(  I wish I could get an email reminder when they add it back to the menu. lol  

I ended up getting the crab bisque and fries.  The bisque was was flavorful.  The fries were good as always.  (I knew the bisque wouldn't be enough alone but didn't see anything else that really stuck out to me...probably because I really wanted that omelet.)

Nice waitstaff.  Pretty fast and acknowledged us.  I'll be back again though because I really like this place.  Hopefully my favorite dish will be on the menu again. :)

I liked this place a lot.  Thought for the price, they could of put a little more jambalaya in my bowl.   But, the beer was cold, the food outstanding, oysters were fresh and shucked so you didn't have to fight to get them out they slid perfectly.  

I went with the local oysters as recommended by staff.   Was NOT disappointed. They were large and tasty.    

Lots of great items on the menu that are encouraging me to return for a second visit before I depart for home.  

Again. My only disappointment was portion with the jambalaya but other than that. People were awesome and the food was great!!!
Great culinary experience!!! Outstanding service!!! Just really awesome experience! All the food and even the dessert were great!! One of the highlights of our food road trip. Thanks!

Luke was hit or miss for us. 
First, dress well even though the food is really casual, because we felt really out of place in jeans and casual tops because this is that kind of restaurant/style of food in Chicago, but apparently everyone just dresses well in the south...

Food is fine here. Just execution wasn't up to my expectations of a restaurant of this price point/ambiance/reputation... Like, shells and grit in 4 of our 12 oysters?!, unevenly cooked vegetable in our salad (which they split for us because we were splitting everything; that was a nice touch), really really salty and overcooked shriveled mussels we had to send back because for $30 I hoped to get really great mussels and broth... They kindly made some sauce for my fries to dip into, but it came back underseasoned! 

Our favorite was the pan fried fresh gulf fish, which was cooked really well and had nice simple clean flavors and accompaniments that went well overall. 

Our server was a nice guy, but a bit absent and awkward? Had trouble answering our questions and did not deal with the mussels with the hospitality I hoped. I kept reading about great service here, but we ended up having to ask a floater who kept filling in for things (additional orders, our utensils replaced, our check). It was a bit of a bummer, because good service could have really saved our night despite food not being up to our expectations.

A little disappointed by how many things could be done better if they're charging this much for food. Glad we came, but would not recommend to friends who are visiting. August looked really good when we walked by though! Maybe next time we're in town...

I really enjoyed dinner here. I was traveling alone so I walked in and sat at the bar. I started with a cup of the crab bisque - I should have ordered a bowl. For the main course I enjoyed the shrimp & grits.  The meal was excellent and the service was solid. I would definitely go back!
Ehhh... At least for lunch. Étouffée was ok if you live in Wyoming. Value and cost are not commensurate... Not even close. Go to a diff John  Besh (like Borgne near the Hyatt Regency)...

Had the crawfish bisque: a little grainy, but good. The burger: really good, but the default prep is with bacon so if that's not your thing you gotta tell them. The bread pudding: nice, but a little TOO sweet. Also had their house-brewed lager which was very good, but a little "fizzy" for my taste. 

As others have noted, service was a little slow on a Thursday at 7:30pm. Flipside to that: waitstaff won't bug you too much.

Price was just right too. If I get a chance while here in town, I'll make a return trip.

Some things should never change and always stay around. Garavelli's is on of them. A style of restaurant, cafeteria if you will, that has all but disappeared. Don't confuse this place with the all you can eat buffet style joints. 
The food here is excellent. The beef tips and gravy were as good as any I have had lately. The baked ham, as a sandwich or plate, tasted just right. Mild, juicy and no fat. Just as it is supposed to be. There is a choice of fountain soft drinks and bottled soda pops.
If you find yourself in St. Louis, this place is a must.

WOW! This place was pretty amazing in every way! We had a short wait, but got two seats at the bar . This was our first trip to New Orleans and had SOOOO MANY RESTAURANTS to choose from, but we picked right !
The bartender made me a perfect French 75 cocktail . We sat by the Ouster shucker and that Was a  highlight. What a nice guy!
I am not an oyster person but these were so sweet and fresh that I had about 1/2 dozen. Amazing variety.
The boiled gulf shrimp were also delicious. 
My bourdin stuffed pork chop was perfectly cooked and accompanied.
Definitely have the beet salad after you have the gumbo.
This is a great place to try all things NOLA. 
This dinner was unforgettable. 
Try to sit at the bar if you can and order a little bit of everything to share .

I tell you the truth... Very poor service. Also there are little flies in the restaurant. Disgusting. Then I saw every big fly. Totally disgusting. I won't go there again.  I gave it 2 stars because the food was not too bad.

absolutely unprofessional.  I contacted them last Tuesday indicating that my HVAC unit in the basement was leaking fluid and would like to schedule a diagnostic. I spoke with Matt who indicated that they could have someone out the next day at 4pm.  I left the office early to ensure that I was home in time; they never showed.  At 8:15pm, I received a call from Bob(?) stating that they hadn't forgotten about me but that they were down a truck.  I replied, "you were supposed to be here over 4hrs ago."  Why would he wait 4hrs to tell me he was down a truck?  Wasn't that known at 3:30pm?  No apologies, no attempt to waive the diagnostic fee, nothing...he quipped, "when can we come out?"  Ummm, it's July 4th weekend!!!! They threw a wrench in my plans to have my unit serviced, at the very least diagnosed, before the holiday.  He hurriedly scheduled me for the next business day.  Honestly, when people don't respect my time, I can't give them my money.  It seems that I avoided a headache & misfortune after reading these reviews.
Great food. Shrimp and grits, Luke salad and Brussel sprouts were our favorites. Kid friendly. Good service unlike some of the reviews said.

Let's start with the good.

The food was really good. Here's what we had:

Blue crab and corn fritters- The tarragon aioli was delicious and paired well with the fritters. The crab flavor was strong and the corn had a good bite to it.

Gumbo- M liked it more than me. He remembers liking it more last year. Not a big fan of all the okra.

Shrimp & Grits- Yum! I liked the heartiness of the grits and the sauce was tasty. Good amount of shrimp.

P&J oysters- I didn't have any but M like these a lot.

Now onto the bad. Our waiter was never really around. After having the fritters, we were served the oysters but our table didn't get cleared of the empty basket of fritters. After the our entrees came, the basket of fritters,the oysters, and dirty appetizer plates were still sitting empty on our table. We had not received the gumbo we ordered so someone else (still haven't seen our waiter) brought it out. 

When Matt was 80% done with his main entree, our waiter finally came to check on us and asked if we needed anything from him. Uhh... Yea! How about clearing the table? Or checking to see how our food was because maybe then he would have known we were served our last appetizer after we were already served our entree. 

Food was great, but the subpar service tainted the experience. We did let a manager know on the way out. If our server was around we could have told him too.

Everything here was amazing.  We got there before 6 and found out there were 75 cent oysters and half priced glasses of wine. And it kept getting better.  Amazing tuna nicoise tartine and rabbit/duck pate.  Incredible Brussels sprouts and cheese burger.  Great service too.

Can I leave negative stars? We're actually in the process of filing a complaint with the BBB for being swindled by Fahrenheit. Trust me it was as awful as others say. They installed a blower for the heater in our rental house, ended up wiring and mounting the blower incorrectly, and than never came back to fix the faulty repair. We scheduled 4 different appointment times to have them come back and they failed to show up all 4 times. We've tried to call multiple times to obtain some sort of refund and the company is basically ignoring our calls. We ended up having another company come out to fix their mess and still no calls from Farenheit. 

I cannot emphasize this enough- DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE!!!!

If the option is polar vortex and no heat or working with Fahrenheit- choose polar vortex.. Once again- GO ELSEWHERE!!


Update: I responded to the owner's comment below and also asked for a refund if all receipts are provided. Lets see what happens...
We just came for dessert but what a treat we received!  The Creme brûlée with fresh fruit accents was incredible!  Can't wait to return to try out their dinner menu!

Great place for breakfast.  (only breakfast review)
Crab omelette: Great crab, a little greasy but the crab made up for it.
Coffee: Good
Biscuit sandwich: Made vegetarian, very good.  Comes with a nice fruit salad.
Beignets:  GREAT WITH THE JAM
Pancakes:  Great (except last bite had onion--weird)
There are tons of newspaper to read.  Service was great.

Best happy hour ever!! 50 cents a piece for delicious raw oysters to start followed by amazing etoufee and swordfish dishes!! The house beers are also not to be missed items.  I'd be a regular here if I lived in town.

Was happy to hear that New Orleans has a number of restaurants open during the Christmas holiday. My fiancé and I came here for Christmas dinner and really enjoyed ourselves. We ordered 1 appetizer, 2 entrees and 1 cocktail. 
Appetizer was Gnocchi which though decent, the sauce it was dressed in tasted like pizza rolls from my childhood. Definitely pass on those next time. 
I ordered shrimp and grits - very flavorful and well seasoned. My fiancé ordered the rib eye which came with fries. We were happy when the food came out because the portions were appropriate. Cocktail was great and definitely strong so worth the cost. 
Overall really nice time and good ambiance.
The best shrimp and grits I have had ever. Homefries were absolutely delicious as well. This is a must dine experience.

mit umlaut und...delicious burgers. I heard good things about this place but wasn't convinced until I made an appearance. The bacon was other worldly...I need to know where to order that from...amazingly delicious supplement for a burger.

The waitress was brilliant. She knew what was in the food and could accommodate or substitute accordingly. She even knew where the products originate, speak about loving food & your job.

Customer service was above and beyond and the delicious food also made a difference. I will definitely put Luke's on the short list of places to re-visit especially because I was too full to indulge in dessert.

Even though we were seated in what was basically the restaurant lobby, this was still a great experience! We came for lunch and this was our favorite fancy meal of our trip. Great service and cocktails, too. 

We shared the baked P&J oysters and the Pate de Campagne to start. I think those oysters were my favorite bite of the trip. We were all really sad that they only sent us 11 instead of a full dozen (believe me, we counted), but fortunately the pate was also great.
 
I tried to order a salad, because I had a mental lapse. John Besh knows better though, and basically sent me a plate of perfectly fried oysters and bacon with a wedge of lettuce in the middle. BEST SALAD EVER.  Other highlights for me were the etoufee, the shrimp and grits and the Tuesday special of Maultaschen. The Le Viet sandwich was good, but way too rich for me after all the butter and fat we had just ingested. This was the only place where we genuinely could not eat a single bite of dessert (we love dessert, so that's serious). We love John Besh!

If I could give this place a 3.5 stars, I would. We visited this place on a whim for brunch and were not disappointed. The food is good and this seems like it would be a pretty classy place for dinner or happy hour. My only complaint is how pricey it is and maybe I just don't fit the lifestyle this place is catering for. I really enjoyed the food and while we sat at the bar, the bartender was very attentive.

Our first day in Louisiana and after only small bites all day we picked to have dinner at Luke. 

We got there at 7pm as a walk in and was offered a  table with a leak from the roof or wait until 8; we went with the leaking table.

Right when we sat down our server comes and we order wine and stuffed oysters. He comes back with the wine and we add on the cold seafood platter. I'm not sure how long we waited but the server comes back and says the appetizers are taking a little long and asked if we wanted something else in the meantime. We order the Brussels sprout and shrimp and grits. 

Our seafood platter comes out. We finish and we wait. We flag down our server to check in on the first appetizer and he goes he knows what happened, mix up with neighbors food. He said it should be coming out right now. As we wait our neighbors put in their orders. 

Finally our stuffed oysters come out and we down those as our neighbor receives all of their food. We anticipate our meals should be coming as we ordered way before them and happy we got some food to hold us over. We wait and wait. It's 8:30, an hour and half since we got there. Our neighbors are practically done. The Server hasn't come to check in on us. My husband wants to cancel the food, but I was so hungry as we hadn't eaten all day so I said let's wait a little longer. 8:45 still no food or server in sight. I flag down another server. I tell him to please cancel our food as it has not come out hoping to catch food at another place. Even he thinks we are on our dessert and I say no, our entrees never came out. He apologizes, notifies our server. 

Our server comes back with the bill and says as if he did us a favor, I took the food off your bill. (Of course you did, I NEVER got it.) As he was about to put down the bill he second guesses and says I'll take some more off. Comes back and says he took off a glass of wine and asks us to give them another try. Said he was embarrassed and did put in our order and kitchen was backed up. (Reminder, our neighbor ordered after us and got their food. They actually ordered everything we ordered!)

As we sat and debated about tipping for a good 15 minutes (My husband still wanted to but I didn't feel there was any customer service to warrant a tip)  Our server comes back with a new receipt with 2 wine and 1 appetizer taken off our tab with no word. I figured decent enough gesture I paid/tipped. I'm in the restaurant industry so always try to be compassionate, but after 2 hours and leaving hungry, I was upset and surprised it was the first time I did not want to tip.

Suggestions: 
1. Offer to rush the food! Get it out!
2. A manager should have been notified and stopped by the table.
3. Offer a voucher or gift card (even just a for a drink or $5) to ask customer to come back, not just on your word or items comped. 

Food:
Seafood platter like any other cold platter. Ceviche was just ok and don't expect the shrimp to be peeled. Cocktail sauce had a nice kick to it.
Stuffed oysters were perfect. Just enough mayo mixed in with crab to top the oyster. Texture and taste was on point. Even then it could not make up the disappointment in the overall experience.

I came here just wanting to try 2 things, the Crawfish Bisque and the Shrimp and Grits.

I got there on Saturday during the brunch hour, and they didn't have the Crawfish bisque, so I went with the Crab & pumpkin bisque instead.

The bisque was very creamy and thick, and the portion was just enough for you to enjoy it before getting tired of the creaminess. I wish the bisque had more crab flavors, and more crabs in it though.

Moving on to the shrimp and grits, it was pretty good. Good sized shrimp. Decent amount of sausages. Cheese grits were creamy. Poached eggs w perfect runny yolk. A little salty though. But when i poked the egg yolk to have it with the grits, the flavor was perfect. 

I was pretty full after this "brunch," and the price came out to be $40 before tips, so it was quite pricey as well. The male server was super nice though, waving me off when I was leaving the restaurant.

The cocktails were fantastic. I'd have drank many more French 75's if only I could have. The food was good, but it didn't knock my socks off. I'd come again for lunch, but it probably wouldn't be my first choice. I would come again for drinks any time.

First place we walked into upon arriving to the city...right outside our hotel. Greeting ladies seemed flustered that we did not have reservations at 3:30 on a Thursday???

Anyway, although there seemed to be plenty of available tables...they told us it would be a 1hr 45 min wait?!? Didn't make sense...got the vibe if we would have dressed a little nicer we would have been treated differently, just my impression. 

We were told we could go to the Bar...which was over crowded...seems the thing here is to send everyone to the bar while the tables sit empty??! Weird

Don't even want to give them a second chance, too many other warm and friendly place close by!

Best grilled oysters I have ever had.  John Besh's restaurant, which he calls a Diner on their menu, is a very casual comfortable place to dine without any pretense.  We ate upstairs, a lot quieter than the room below and were actually able to hear ourselves talk.  The staff, though a bit slow, were very friendly and we were in no rush.The jumbo shrimp en cocotte were very good but not as hot as my DH would have liked.  The shrimp and grits were to die for.  I wonder if they will give me the recipe for that and also for the marvelous oysters?

Came here while waiting for my hotel room was getting ready. The food is amazing, especially the crawfish bisque with the head stuffed with jalapeño corn bread. Stayed a lot longer than I meant too. Wow!  I cannot recommend this place highly enough!

Can you say incredible?  My favorite place in NOLA. Everything is fantastic, the fried Brussels, are worth a direct flight just to get, staff is great, and all the seafood is 100% NOLA worthy. Go to Luke, it's worth it for sure!

This place has a fantastic employee named Juanita. She is ON her customer service.

I only pulled in here because I was driving past, needed an oil change in my mom's car, saw one of the two bays was empty and saw a sign that said "we honor competitors coupons". Around the block I went and pulled in. Before I could put the car in park, Juanita was at the window. She got us into the system and escorted us into the small waiting room and offered coffee. She was then off to help another client. 

A few moments later, she came in and sat next to me. She had a filthy air filter. She inquired if I wanted to replace it and advised of the cost. We discussed it and I authorized her to have it changed. 

Within 15 minutes -  maximum - of pulling into the drive, we were checking out. They honored the competition coupon. 

I did notice their base oil change is $41.99, which seems very pricy when so many other places offer $19.99. That being said, I normally wait at least an hour for my oil change when I go to the $19.99 place. I'm normally changed a shop fee and other misc fees like a disposal fee and my bill is almost $30.00 (right, for a $19. 99 coupon). If this place is $41.99 out the door with no extra fees it would be more worth it for me to come here, rather than have to deal with my kid in a waiting room for an hour when she's bored to death.

We didn't even have time here to read our story book!
very unusual for a chipotle - all but one server/ attendant was unmindful! They kept talking among themselves instead of serving the folks in line

Went here for brunch and thought the food was just okay.  Had the shrimp and grits - $24 for five shrimp and an appetizer-sized portion of grits.  Food was a bit over-seasoned as well.  Left hungry and disappointed.  Maybe dinner is better?

Service was subpar for the type of place this is - it wasn't particularly busy but waited about 5 minutes after finishing our food before the waiter came by to even  check if we wanted a coffee refill.  So much for southern hospitality...

Rabbit and chicken liver pate is really amazing. It'd be the reason I'd come back. Nice environment and good selection on the menu. You start off with a warm bread that is crunchy on the hot side and soft on the inside - real delicious. Shrimp and grits a little too much flavor.

Awesome steak, burgers, shrimp and grits and the fresh oysters. 

Take note that come for happy hour weekdays (3-6) for 75 cent fresh oysters

My wife and I had a great experience here while on a work trip/vacation.  First, the service was fantastic.  We started with a half-dozen big, fresh oysters matched with great cocktails.  I had the Choucroute Garnie Maison, which is a massive pork shank, a bratwurst, all on a bed of awesome sauerkraut.  B had the Moules et Frites, which she loved.  And the Bread Pudding for dessert was so good that we must've been making a scene - after finishing our dessert, the couple next to us was like, "You two really liked that dessert!"  Hell yeah, we did!

This is purely based on the bread pudding because thats all I had while here.

It was my last stop before my ride to the airport, so in essence the absolute last bite of food I put in my mouth before departing the great mecca of culinary deliciousness known simply as "NOLA".

I sat at the bar and honestly, after eating like a complete ANIMAL for 8 days and just having a decadent meal at Willie Mae's and a few beignets at Cafe du Monde my belly was ready to tap out. However, it was on my list of things I HAD to try before leaving. After reading the reviews of the bread pudding and seeing the pictures I was still psyched even though I was so utterly and probably more so disgustingly full.

But yes, I soldiered on. And what a masterpiece it was. Arriving it its own cast iron staub pot, piping hot and served in a pool of a whiskey caramel rum sauce. A heaping scoop of vanilla ice cream melting on top (EAT THIS ONE FAST!), and some huge Louisiana pecans dispersed throughout for sure. No joke, I got through half of this in about 20 seconds flat before reminding myself to slow down and enjoy it. I could see the rest of the people in the bar staring at me with envy. They were surely reading my facial expression to see how much I was enjoying it.

What a fantastic dessert, Or maybe even a breakfast. Or maybe you can have three and call it breakfast, lunch, and dinner. In a trip that included lots of bread pudding, this one was among the best... and best I've ever had. 

Great way to end a great trip of gluttonous, delicious feasting!!!!!

I've always wanted to come here, especially since I always bypass this on my way home from the gym. Though we had to get this lunch to go since we ran out of time waiting for it (it was a bad idea coming here on a Friday, the first one of Lent), the bread was really good and the waitress was really great despite her having to bus a lot more tables than probably the norm. Had the Friday special - redfish 'court-bouillon' with crab, shrimp, oysters, and rice - they gave me two huge, fresh oysters and the crab and shrimp were really fresh too. I wish I ate it when it was hot, but it was still good!

Overall had a good experience.  Being a top chef fanatic it was nice to hit a "celebrity chef" restaurant
We walked in without a reservation on a Saturday night.  Initially told there were no tables for 1-2 hours. Then while discussing where else we were going to go... poof!  They magically found a table.  That was nice

I had had a big lunch so didn't order an appetizer (rare for me!)
For my entree i had the fish of the day meuniere style. with roasted veggies and spaetzle.  It was satisfying.  Felt like i could get something similar at a million NY restaurants though.  Nothing particularly N'awlins about it.

My mother had the roast chicken with veggies and french fries.  The juices from the chicken were soo tasty i kept dipping fries in it.  I guess i liked her dish better than mine!

A solid meal...

In all my years of coming to New Orleans this was the first John Besh restaurant at which I've dined. Since I don't have anything to compare it to I'm not sure if his recent resignation had anything to do with our evening, but I've got to say there was a relaxed and exuberant attitude pervasive throughout the restaurant. 
We started with a special request cocktail that slightly confounded the waiter and bartender. At first I thought, "Uh, oh" were in for a long and troubled night. But instead of making it a problem they made it a great learning experience and reveled in discovery something new. I think the fact that we were adventurous got our waiter Rich to really have some fun with us. We ordered small plates and large plates and everything we ordered was beyond perfection. The P & J raw oysters are some of the best in the city. Clean, briny, fresh. (The day before we were stuck in a late meeting and my companion wanted to get a plate of oysters afterwards. A friend had suggested the oyster bar at Luke but my friend wanted to go to Acme [thumbs down on that one]. After tasting the P & J's at Luke last night I'm kicking myself for missing out on another opportunity to experience these.) One of our party had ordered the oysters on the shell but they delivered the stuffed oysters instead. They didn't hesitate to fix the mistake and the waiter shucked the 1/2 dozen (+1!) himself. Oh, and the stuffed oysters were left for us to enjoy with the restaurant's compliments. Shrimp & Grits - spectacular. Perfectly cooked shrimp with perfect grits seasoned with roasted jalapeno & cheese. Other highlights were the Fried Oyster salad, Crab & Corn Bisque, and Seafood Creole Gumbo. We didn't order it, but saw the Luke Burger with duck fat fries being delivered to several other tables. If you order it, you better have an appetite. It looks like a pound or more of beef. Our friends have had it before and say it's amazing. After gorging ourselves we were unsure about dessert. Rich described them beautifully and as we hemmed and hawed he finally just offered to bring us two on him. Thank you, thank you, thank you. It was far too much but we might never have known the joy of a S'mores Torte or Brendan's Bread Pudding.
Service was relaxed, attentive, and spot-on. The management was always on their toes and came by several times to insure our evening was great. Looking forward to my next visit.

Stopped in here for breakfast on a Saturday morning - the server was very friendly and paid close attention to our table. All the food was exceptional. Special recognition to the grits - they were fluffy and almost mashed potato like. The best I have ever had. The mixed berry marmalade was exceptional as well and was fabulous on top of the hearty multigrain toast.

Wish we had found this place for breakfast earlier in our trip! Highly recommended!!

This was perhaps the best meal we had during our time in New Orleans.  We decided to give Luke a try for a change of pace and because we wanted to see whether a John Besh restaurant actually lives up to the hype.  In a couple words: hell yes!

Our meals consisted of the following:

* "Le Plateau" of jumbo Louisiana Shrimp (1/2 dozen): Humangous shrimp that were juicy and oh so fresh.  It saddens me how Chicago's seafood can not even begin to compare to what the folks down in New Orleans get to eat.
