* Pate of Louisiana rabbit and duck livers: I developed a newfound appreciation for/obsession with pate from my trip to Paris last year.  Luke's pate was absolutely phenomenal.  The pate is served in a little jar and comes with an assortment of garnishes as well as some "country bread croutons".  After we went through the first batch of croutons, we got a second helping and proceeded to polish that off too.  That's how good the pate was.  

* Moules et Frites: A French bistro staple, Luke's version of it did not disappoint.  First off, the portions are absolutely massive and the mussels themselves are ridiculously plump and fresh.  Our server taught us a little trick on how to use the mussel shells as pinchers for removing the meat -- so clever and effective!  The mussel broth made for a perfect dipping sauce for the frites.  Terrific dish and yet another reminder of how New Orleans seafood kicks major ass.

I also got a cocktail called the French 75, which was basically cognac, lemon juice and champagne.  Very refreshing on a hot muggy day!

Service was terrific -- friendly and polite, what one would expect dining in the South.  Prices were very reasonable and the ambiance is relaxing and inviting, which I much preferred over the rowdiness that one might find while dining at a restaurant on Bourbon St.  All in all, it was a fantastic meal.  Consider me a believer of John Besh!

I've stopped by several times on the weekend, each time for a drive thru visit.  I was ordering for several people and the order came out correctly and quickly each time.  It can kinda stink getting out of the parking lot when traffic at the light backs up.  Turn left out of the lot and you can go around rather than wait.

Great food and service. 
1. Super friendly server who is very attentive and knowledgeable. 
2. Pate of rabbit and chicken livers, w/  watermelon pickles and current jelly
3. Crawfish Bisque was rich and yummy 
4. Rabbit stew with pasta was great.
5. Great wine selection.
We will go back
Great food and amazing service! They have a cool private room that we were lucky to get for dinner. To top it off, we had the best waiter ever!  Pretty awesome!

Luke was the best dinner I had on my recent trip to NOLA, and was a great counterpoint to the previous night's experience at Cochon.

This won't be a comparative review, but the two evenings were a study in contrasts. I was equally excited for each dinner, but all the anticipation I had for Cochon led to a bit of a letdown, whereas Luke delivered with excellence.

We were seated immediately after arrival (8:30pm Saturday reservation), and my friends all ordered the highly-recommended mint julep. They were well made and universally praised.

Soup course was 3 for gumbo, and 1 for corn and crab chowder. Everyone was happy, and the gumbo was probably the best we had in the city.

Dinner topped the soup course well. The hamburger was as large as advertised, and had a fantastic rich, char-grilled flavor. The fries were a treat as well. I had the duck breast and absolutely loved it. Cooked well, with great combinations of sweet and salty flavors. The nightly special of rabbit was also very tasty, and shrimp and grits were wonderful too. I'd love to gush about the food, but hopefully you've stopped reading this review and have already ordered your food at Luke.

As for dessert - we all got it, and we all liked it. Bread pudding was a touch too sweet, which made it unfinishable, although it was very good. My friend enjoyed the crepes, but I didn't sample them. The pot de creme was among the best I've ever had (better than my homemade!). Creme brulee was equally good, and notable was that it was served only slightly-chilled, letting the vanilla flavor really sing. 

Just go. Enjoy it. Order well, and savor!
Excellent food, closest thing to being in Japan!! We will definitely be dining here more often
Richie rich is the bees knees. He showed us such a good time, suggested great food and hooked us up!!! Definitely a great place to eat

Another visit, this time seated at the bar, and I need to admit that aside from the snit that their "etoufee" put me in, this place is really damn good. More of the best shrimp and grits I've ever had, the best raw bar experience I have ever had AND one of the greatest burgers ever as well - not just greatest in New Orleans, either.

Amazing seafood, service, and authentic Cajun cuisine. A bit pricey but worth it for the fresh quality of the food. Right next to the hilton French quarter and they have an amazing happy hour most afternoons from 4-6pm .

Wow! I mean wow! their Étouffée blue crab & shrimp is a MUST try, although its a small portion it sure hit the spot!  Dessert: chocolate moose yumminess ;p French 75 is also a well known drink here...Yumminess =)

It's okay.  Kind of cold and not very welcoming.
Loud!  no soft surfaces to absorb noise.
The burger that everyone loves was really nothing special.
Hey, I'm allergic to onions (yeah, that stinks) so they bring me a burger without the grilled onions BUT IT WAS ON AN ONION ROLL!!!
Maybe they were trying to kill me....
anyway, I wouldn't go out of my way to eat at Luke.
no matter how they spell it.

The wait for a larger group on Sunday night was ~a half hour. Service was super meh. The waitress interrupted our conversation so many times for unnecessary reasons and it felt so intrusive. We were also rushed so much to finish quickly (even though the entire wait for a table was because two tables had paid already and weren't being rushed to leave...). Even though I asked for the remainder of my food to be boxed, it ended up being thrown away, which I found to be a strange miscommunication...

However, the food was not bad. I didn't like the Brussels sprouts (14$) -- too salty and overcooked, and they were billed as crispy, which they weren't really. I did like my entree, the fried oyster salad (17$) a lot. The oysters were crispy and tasty, and the greens were quite good.

We came here looking for breakfast, but we found out they serve breakfast only on weekends. Our server was kind enough to recommend a great breakfast restaurant nearby, but since we were already seated and it was almost lunch time anyway, we decided to stay. I ordered the Lüke Burger and my friend ordered the Cochon De Lait Jambalaya. Both were good, though not great.

Our server was quite friendly. He asked if we were visitors to the Big Easy and suggested we visit the Le Bon Temp Roule to listen to the Soul Rebels brass band. Great recommendation. Authentic NOLA bar with great entertainment and diverse crowd. Lüke gets an additional star just because of our server - too bad I don't remember his name, but thanks anyway.

Overall food is 4 stars and service is 5.

P & j oysters were awesome. Must have.

Luke burger was fine but nothing great. 

Waiters are all very friendly and attentive.

This place is great for oysters. We came here mainly for their oyster happy hour and they were some of the freshest we've ever had. Not fishy at all. We also had their cocktails which were all amazing. Very complex. The only other thing on the menu that we tried was the brussels sprouts. Mind blowing. So, so good. I wish we had gotten to try the rest of their menu but we already had dinner reservations at another restaurant later that evening. Will definitely be coming back  on our next trip to New Orleans.

The service was brusque and by far the least friendly of the places we ate at, but the happy hour was still pretty good - the fried oysters were our favorite, hot out of the fryer and crispy and the oysters pretty plump at $1.25 per. The raw were also good, and at only 75 cents, a bargoon. The cocktails were strong and also good - the blackberry smash was my favorite, a bourbon based drink, and the ponchat cooler. 

Pretty popular place for HH so I think people fill it up near 3, and then there's a lull by 4:30 or so as the first wave stumbles back (to the office?).

Best French 75 of my life - almost creamy but in the best way. The shrimp & crab "etouffee" was spectacular as well - perfect amount of spice in a delicious sauce. I would definitely make reservations - the space isn't that big and they had a huge wait.

I got the shrimp n grits and although it was very good, I could only eat one shrimp because of the gumbo and beignets I had an hour prior. I assumed since I had only eaten one bite and explained to the waiter it was delicious but I had eaten right before, he would box it up. As I sat there for long enough I realized he wasn't going to bring it. The waiter apologized and said he'd make me another full order for the inconvenience. Unfortunately when I came home, I found that he had not given me a full order but only 3 shrimp (out of a total of 5 that come with a full meal). Very disappointing.

Soooo, not sure if I'm seeing a trend here or not. However, my self and my 2 friends (Asian) went to Luke for happy hour. After getting some low looks from the host, we got seated. While waiting for my food I noticed that we had a small hair in our butter - I used my knife to pick it up and alerted the server. When he came over I let him know that I found a hair - he grabbed my knife from my hand and came back a few minutes later with a clean knife, all the while not speaking a word to us. When I asked him if he could bring us a clean butter he grabbed it off the table and slammed and I mean slammed a new one on the table, still not a word to myself and my friends. I saw a review from a previous Asian diner and feel that something is going on at Luke. I've visited before my my American husband and have had great service before this trip.

The raw oysters were great! The creole gumbo was okay, my Bloody Mary was blah. It was a long ways away from the Bloody Mary I had this morning at Ruby Slipper.... which was amazing. Although Luke is conveniently located in my hotel, I think I may need to venture out for the remainder of my trip.

There is only one reason for the 4 vs the 5.  We will get to that. 

I took my angel here for our top of the line dinner during our most recent trip to this magnificent town.  She was the focus of my attention as she was wearing "that dress" and she looked magnificent.  I was proud she wanted me on her arm!  In any case we had a reservation for 8:00 and got there a touch early so spent time at the bar.  Our bartender knew his craft and was fantastic.  When you can ask a bartender to do something different than the norm with gin and he comes up wth corpse reviver number 2(?!) thats a pro.  Unfortunately we got forgotten at the bar for over 45 minutes and then got attitude from the hostess as we asked for our table (wtf?)  

We got a great table once we did get seated and proceeded to love love love this place.  We were seated right on the glass showcase kitchen and I was able to geek out on technique and process and the like.  This was pure theatre for me!  

My angel got the chicken dish which was sublime.  I know chicken right?  Its been brined for 3 days, crispy to the outside with tremendous flavor and juicy to the inside.  WOW.  I got the shrimp and grits and was not at all disappointed.  Finished with the Bread Pudding.  Holy cow!  

We had a great time, wonderful food and amazing company.  How can you lose?

Got the flamenküche, herb roasted chicken, and the shrimp & grits. The chicken was great- very flavorful and juicy. Ask for extra veggies instead of potatoes and you'll get lots of interesting squash in great sauce. Shrimp & grits was amazing. I usually don't like grits, but these were coarsely cut, cheesy, and soaking in a delicious sauce. Shrimp were well seasoned and perfectly cooked. The flamenküche was a great start with a razor thin crust and tons of caramelized onions. The bacon chunks were a bit large for my taste but I understand that people in New Orleans love their pork! Service was great- ask for Kevin C.

My fiancé and I booked our reservation at Lüke for a Saturday night to celebrate my birthday. My fiancé, having grown up in Alaska, is definitely the seafood connoisseur of us. We both agreed it was probably the best seafood we had in New Orleans during our week there.

We started with the frog legs and 1/2 dozen gulf oysters - would highly recommend both. The frog legs were tender and oh so tasty. Gulf oysters were our server's recommendation and he did not steer us wrong.

Fiancé ordered the shrimp & grits, and I had the gulf fish with almonds and lump crab. CRAB WAS DELICIOUS, brown butter sauté was AMAZING, and the veggies (though not the star of the dish) were also surprisingly yummy.

Ended with steamed chocolate (also YUM). We ate it all and no regrets were had. Would eat again!!

Go here for the raw bar and only if you have the patience of a saint. The food here is mediocre. Over salted and over done. The bread pudding tastes like citrus, the rabbit sausage pasta has too much going on, everything is fatty and salty instead of flavorful. Service is awful. I once had a waiter spill soup all over me and they didnt even offer to reimburse me for my dry cleaning. John Besh needs to get his act together. Less time trying to be a celebrity and more time making sure his restaurants up to par.
Awesome coffee, great sandwiches, friendly staff.  Always enjoy a visit to Elm.  The patio is an extra benefit in the summer.  Just don't expect to find much room for indoor seating.

Fabulous experience and meal.  Second experience at Lüke. Brought friends for a special anniversary dinner. Wait staff was attentive but not intrusive.  Food was presented well and was one of my favorite meals of all time!

Came to Lüke for dinner after getting in late. Good thing they are open late. First off the ambiance is great. Love the music and feel for the place. Now to the good part, the food. It was delicious. I had the steak and my boyfriend had the fish of the day which happened to be a black drum. Steak was perfectly cook. Textbook ribeye. It came with a side of shoestring fries which I really didn't care for. The black drum was delicious. Lightly breaded and served with a decadent sauce. Would definitely recommend this place to any tourist.

Holy Smokes! The Duck/Rabbit Pate was amazing!!!  I'm still thinking about it right now.  Went to happy hour and had platters of oysters.  $0.50/per oysters during happy hour, can't beat that.   Beer was good as well.  Will definitely have to go back to try out the rest of the menu.

Heard about the happy hour oysters. So I thought, we can't miss that!

The hostess and pretty much everyone but one of the staff (a young man who cleans our table) seemed to have something hooked their noses up, or have some restraint air to them.  Hm.. is it because we were wearing our hoodies when we walked in (it was really windy and really cold that evening!) and we were wearing casual wear?  But looking around, this is not a dress up kinda place. People came in jeans, Tshirts, casual, yeah some in their working shirts. But still, this is a tourists place. You gotta be ready to serve with a smile. 

Whatever.  We came for the happy hour. And thank goodness for that. Or else I probably won't come here at all (or anymore for that matter).

Oysters are fresh but tiny.  The trumpeted home fries are, well, regular french fries. You can get much better one from In-n-Out.   Crab and corn soup is good but nothing screams special.  Wine is good, but come in a short glass typically use to serve your table water (??? WTF ???)  I almost thought it was a mistake!  I didn't say anything.  I think it was a poor presentation.  

Luke's is good, but not great.  A typical joint, expensive and positioned themselves as an exclusive restaurant, but take out the fancy price it would be a=just another seafood and bar.

Jumbo shrimp and grits dish was amazing! Nice and spicy. The Gumbo was too bland for me even after adding loads of Tabasco to try and spice it up. The P&J oysters were creamy and delicious. I give it a 3 star because the service was subpar. Server literally came zero times after delivering our food to the table and it wasn't even busy at all.

1st time....4 stars
2nd time....3 stars
Last time....1 star!!!

I wouldn't go back except for the happy hour oysters.  In fact, the oysters are the only consistently good thing on the menu....and you don't even have to cook them.

It has been really salty the last two trips and it's not worth the cost.  While not as expensive as New Orleans can get, overall not worth the trip.

I don't really have ANYTHING nice to say, so I'm tempted to say nothing at all... But in the spirit of helping others I will say that our service and food was poor... in fact my partner was served a salad with rotten lettuce pieces and a brown avocado. Upon sending it back because who'd eat that (especially for what they are charging...) The waiter snatched the plate off the table and didn't say a word. I realize he didn't make the salad and technically he's not responsible for it but his reaction was a little unreal... My $21 crab app was meh... so we didn't even bother to order mains and left. I'm so confused by all of the reviews raving about this place. In a word? OVERRATED.

A couple of us wanted a fancy-ish place on the last day of our conference and landed at Luke's. They seated us inside, far away from the A/C, beside the kitchen area. Thumbs up for the fact they asked us instead of freezing us to death!
We ordered a bottle of wine, the Malbec. Our server was very nice. I ordered the petite seafood platter. Now I have ordered seafood platters a lot of times. The mussels and clams, especially, came spicier and more flavorful than I get at other places. The perfect, subtle kick to these otherwise strong-smelling sea animals. The oysters were fresh and tasted nice. The shrimp was great too. The way they serves food is quite cool. My friends said their steak and burgers were amazing. 
I also ordered the bread pudding because that was my last night at Nola. Nicely done, came with a dollop of ice cream and toasted pecans. We had a wonderful night for a reasonable price. Definitely going back.

Great late night place ,you get lost in it. 
Food service this quality just expect a little bit more .

We reserved a table for New Year's Eve.  Had a lovely time, the bar is beautiful inside is nicely done, though crowded.  Had the champagne cognac with lemon juice --can you say YUM. The roasted Brussels sprouts were out of this world. Had the fish and husband had the   ÉTOUFFÉE. We both cleared our plates and I saved room for dessert. We would definitely go back just for the cocktails and Brussels sprouts . The table next to us had a burger and fries and that is my next order. Love me a good burger

Had a good lunch here today.  Everything was solid, fresh & well prepared.  The service is sort of upscale diner so don't go in with high expectations, but prices are reasonable and there are definitely some good choices on menu.

This place is just yummy. The atmosphere and décor is upscale and trendy too. I had a cup of shrimp gumbo (sans sausage) and it was perfect for a rainy day! Also had the bread pudding which was basically heaven on earth. Definitely recommend going here when you are in Nawlins! Enjoy!

A first timer to NOLA and a fan of Besh, I cannot imagine a better spot to bring my friends. The bar at Luke has a fantastic happy hour that cannot be beat. P and J oysters for .75 and wine/cocktails/drafts half off. Kris, our bartender, had great suggestions while Phil and Tim shucked our oysters- the shells were clean and easy to eat. They're so fresh you don't need the amazing sauces. Ryan the manager even stopped by to say hello and was kind and friendly face. I can't recommend this stop enough and can't wait to be back.
Great service, food was delicious - especially impressed with the Matza Ball soup. One of my favorite shrimp and grits in the whole city! Oh and did I mention the cocktails? spot on!!

I went here three times in five days. It was overkill, but I'd do it again in a heartbeat.

If you aim for their happy hour, the oysters and drinks are reasonably priced. This restaurant has the best raw oysters for the price. When I went in early January, the regular gulf oysters weren't too large, tasted great, and had minimal grit. I also stopped by Acme during this trip, and Luke's raw oysters were much better by far. The ones at Acme were too large and gritty.

Oysters aside, my absolute favorite item on the menu is the rabbit and chicken liver pate. My friends and I talked about it for days. The pate was rich and creamy without the usual metallic, slightly game-y taste. It's definitely a dish you'd want to share, because the portion is large.

If you attempt to catch their happy hour during a special event (we went New Year's Eve), you might have to "shark" it to get a spot at the bar if you don't have reservations.

After visiting almost all of the Besh venues, this location sits in the Hilton in the CBD just across the street from One Shell Square. Very easy to get to and accessible parking all around. Going in, I expected the food to be the typical fresh local flavor that you get at all the Besh restaurants but the lunch I had exceeded my expectations. I will tell you that if you only ordered the Brussel sprouts, you will leave happy. Very rich with great flavor and kick that will surprise even the Brussel sprout hater. The drum or snapper almandine is fantastic! I ordered mine blackened but both are fantastic. I had Mauthes cheesecake which is right in line with the local selection of mushrooms that Besh serves up. The cheesecake, topped with a blackberry sauce should not be missed. The service on my two visits was only adequate and should be kicked up just a notch but the food continues to speak volumes and I will definitely be visiting again!

Also, one of my go to places for raw oysters. Enjoy them at the bar with a cold beer.

An exceptional and authentic hole-in-the-wall.  It's carnitas that does it for me here.  Huge portions and meat of exceptional quality.  Helpful and friendly service -- very happy to explain and accommodate.   I went there years ago when it was Gillin's cafetreia, and I'm so glad I went back after it became the Mexican In.  .

I was so-o-o bummed to come back to the St. Louis area and NOT be able to get my pancake on a stick!! Why did you take this off the menu!? It was the one thing I looked forward to when I came out here!? Overall everything else is good! They don't have too many of these out in Illinois but I definitely won't be going too far out of my way now! ;-(
Love this place! Great local bar/restaurant. The seafood is fresh and the matzoball soup is delicious! Staff is very friendly.

I came back to Yelp to make sure I reviewed this place. I have a confession - I visit every time we come to New Orleans, and I get the shrimp en cocotte (fancy words for shrimp and grits) every single time. No shame. We also usually get some form of fresh seafood from the raw bar and every time it has been amazing. My favorite is the small seafood platter - the tuna tartare and shrimp chips, omg. Huge shrimp, delicious mussels and clams, and giant P&J oysters. Luke is my happy place.

This breakfast was OUTSTANDING. We ordered the shrimp and grits and the chicken and waffles. Both were so different and flavorful. The shrimp and grits were decadent with the rich savory jalapeño cheese grits. When you add in the eggs and the andouille sausage...it's just wow. The chicken and waffles is HUGE! The jam topping was a great sweet and spicy accompaniment. I'm in a food coma now.

After standing at the register waiting for what seemed like an eternity for someone to help me I finally placed my not-real-difficullt order for a medium latte with ONE pump of syrup.  Oh...I forgot to mention that when I was waiting (for what seemed like an eternity) there were TWO people standing statuesque-ly behind the registers.  I kid you not.  It was almost like time stopped and we were all frozen for a few minutes.  Awkward.

Anyway, same girl who took my order goes to make my drink and gets into an argument with another barista about re-steaming the milk.  Surprise, surprise, my lazy girl wanted to just reheat the stuff that had been sitting around (which would've been okay with me had she at least made a bit of an attempt to top off with a gulp of fresh milk...as it were, there was about an extra 1 1/2 inches of NOTHING at the top of my cup).  

So, she goes to squirt the syrup and squirts three times and then tries to argue with me that one shot is actually 3 pumps.  Which is fine but I specifically said one PUMP.  She admitted that that's what I said but then proceeded to say (again) that three pumps equaled one pump....now thinking about math problems makes my palms sweat and I'm NOT that great at it but I do know that 1 does NOT equal 3.  Moron.

I forgive.  I forget.  But this is maybe the 5th time that something like this has happened at this location.  I won't be back.

We ate dinner here on Wednesday night.  We started with the crabmeat au gratin and Brussel sprouts - both of which were very good.  To be honest, I am not a fan of Brussel sprouts but our friend was and I tried her's.  They were so good I would order them on my own next time.  My spouse and I each got the Luke burger and fries.  Our friend got the chicken.  They were ok, not good not bad just ok.  For desert we shared the bread pudding and cheesecake.  The bread pudding was outstanding and the cheesecake was good.  The restaurant got more and more throughout the evening.  By the end it was so hard to hear each other we just stopped talking.  The food was pretty good but the noise level was so high it was hard to really enjoy yourself.

译文
This is my favorite Japanese restaurants in the city. All of the food is amazing. Exquisite decorative plate with delicious food really is perfect
When you walk in they ask you if you have reservations but it's not necessary to make them they will still sit you. Customer service is good and the food is delicious. I would go again.
This place is perfection! The atmosphere is so " New York"... The food is outrageous! Complimentary dessert was a real treat!

It is really unfortunate to leave this review as it is not indicative to the food at Luke. I was in town on vacation a couple of weeks back and stopped in for a bite. The burger was great and the service was fantastic! 

However, during my visit I accidentally left a really nice pair of sunglasses. The next day I went in to see if they were there - the great waitress that served me previously said she stashed them in case I came back. Which was really awesome - it goes to show there are great people everywhere in this world.

Unfortunately, this is where the reason for the poor review comes in. In between the time I had left and she had stashed the glasses for my return - someone who worked at the restaurant stole them. It sucks to know I won't be coming back because this place is great in terms of food and service. I can't support a place where workers will steal their customers stuff.

- disclaimer: I never leave reviews for places (good or bad) but this incident compelled me to

This place is amazing! Great ambiance and service. Food was delicious! Best oysters my husband has ever had. I had the lobster and crab bisque soup and we were very happy with our meal! This was our first time in New Orleans and we will definitely be returning to Luke on our next visit!

Had Sunday brunch here while on vacation and the food was great. Upon arriving, the hostess was a bit pretentious with a few comments she made, but overall it was a good experience. The waitress was kind but could have been more attentive to water glasses and checking in on us. (She asked how everything was near the very end of our meal.)
Loved it! Great atmosphere and food, and reasonably priced for the quality. Try their Luke brand craft beers and make a reservation because it does get busy.

Came here before a friend's dessert and cocktail party to have a light bite. We had three appetizers, the crab maison, the flamenkuche, and the frogs' legs.


The crab maison was fabulous, just a light hint of horseradish that really kept the creamy sauce from being too rich or heavy. The flamenkuche was delicious, the abundance of caramelized onions made this thin-crusted tart have plenty of body, and the frogs' legs, despite being fried, were light and airy, with a nice acidic compliment from the sauces on the plate.

Overall the food was amazing, we were so glad we came here. The atmosphere is cute, with  very classic decor. It is next to/shares bathrooms with the Hilton Hotel's lobby, but it doesn't feel like a hotel restaurant and it is extremely clean. 

Our waiter, "Richie Rich" was awesome. Funny and quirky, but by no means one of those waiters that is constantly present/tries to take center state each time they visit your table side. 

Overall, I wish I would have been in town longer to come back and try out their entrées.

Lüüüüüüüüke, I am your father! 

Returned here for a very nice Sunday brunch with our group of six. I hesitated a bit on the five stars because our food took forever to come out, but we all had a great time and the meal was beyond amazing. 

We were still smashed from the night before and were taking it a bit easy rather than order a shit-ton of seafood and go family style, as we had been doing. Everyone had individual seafood plates off the brunch menu, and it was all top notch - but boy did we want to go for the seafood tower.

When you hear from your friends best _____ I've ever had, in this case the Crab Bisque and pâté in particular, then that's as good as it gets, right?

Peach Champagne was delightful.

I am a HUGE fan of John Besh and was excited to try Luke with my husband. I will say that the food was good but oversalted. :( We split the flamenkuche for an appetizer. It was very delicious but I was surprised it was not hot at all and room temp which meant to me that it was made ahead of time? Still, it was very tasty. I had the shrimp and grits which was very tasy but again, OVERSALTED. My husband had the Jagerschnitzel which was tasty but again OVERSALTED. He raved about the mushroom sauce. Our drinks were *fine* and water was refilled by the ancillary server/bus person. I thought the service was REALLY bad. I am in the hospitality business and I forgive a LOT of bad service but this server was clearly having a bad day. She had 3 tables and she was so short. When I asked about the fish of the day, it was a short - "it's a white fish". Ok... The two gentlemen next to us waited over 25 minutes for oysters and had to flag down the ancillary server again to find out where they were. Everyone has a bad day but her short and almost rude service ruined the experience for me. We didn't get dessert because we were disgusted by the service. I certainly expected a lot and was not disappointed in the food but food is only part of the experience and the bad service really soured this experience for me. I never even saw a manager to complain. Hopefully if we get another opportunity to try another John Besh restaurant we will have a better experience.

What an introduction to New Orleans. Be forewarned, this is not a typical hotel restaurant. Rather it's John Besh's hidden gem, attached to the lobby of the Hilton.  After eating New Orleans for 4 days non-stop I can easily say that Luke easily stands out for the freshness of the ingredients and overall quality of the food...

The decor is old school brasserie. Lots of copper, darks woods and a nice old school bar where ppl linger. Its also not that busy, probably cuz ppl see it as being part of a hotel and assume it's nothing special. Little did they know...

The highlights!
1) One day we ordered 6 dozen oysters...they have happy hours every day until 6PM...50 cent oysters and half off all beers and cocktails. What a deal. The oysters were some of the best we had in New Orleans. Nice and sweet, paired simply with lemon, vinegar mignonettes or freshly made horseradish that lit a fire in your nose

2) A variety of wurst sausages and an awesome bacon onion potato hash that was just out of this world. 

3) Freshly ground grits that were heavenly and you could see why having it hand cut vs machine cut really made a difference

4) Half off all the drinks including a steady stream of Bloody Mary's and Pimms cups! 

****

Great Brunch, I was here during Mardi Gras weekend and ordered the Jambalaya.  I asked for it extra spicy (how the locals like it) and it did not disappoint.  The Sausage was extremely flavorful and the pork belly was succulent.  My fiance ordered the Croque Monsieur which was doused in a layer of baked emmentaler cheese and served on a wooden cutting board.  The portion was enormous so she only ate half.  Very enjoyable meal and our waiter was extremely friendly.

Limited menu which changes. Be sure to check in advance if you want a specific dish. 
Great escargot 
Limited pours on drinks

Bottom-line it's Hard to find a Bad place when it comes to food in New Orleans but there are some places that go beyond the mark of Excellence and that would be added to the list Luke Lunch and Dinner, a little weak with their breakfast! All the places I visited I grade on the TASTE/FLAVOR not always the portions!!!!

I'm a big John Besh fan.  But I have to say that I was a bit disappointed with this restaurant.  Our seats were in a very busy spot with lots of passing traffic. If we had known we would have asked for the back room. The table was too small to hold all of our food.  Drinks took too long to come.  We had the brussel sprouts. ...they were very interesting and tasty.  Other than that, the food was okay.  I guess I had my expectations too high.

Great food and excellent happy hour. 
Need to make a reservation but worth trying this restaurant for their seafood and Cajun food. 
I thought they had the best gumbo and jalapeño grits. 
The size was a perfect portion. I'm going back for their burger which looked great and almost everyone ordered it. 

Customer service was good . Couldn't really  tell who my server was but it seemed like everybody helped each other out in the restaurant so flagging down a random server didn't really matter they were happy to assist you.

The place has an impressive menu but I was not impressed by the atmosphere. I felt like I was in a church hall at a pancake dinner. Not much ambiance. The rabbit pasta was OK. I probably just ordered the wrong thing because everyone else loved it.
Wow...just unexpected.  Try the smoked pork shank.  I haven't gotten it off my mind.  AMAZING

I wouldn't really recommend eating here per se-- your money is always undoubtedly spent better elsewhere --however, Cosi is really not a bad spot to meet someone for coffee at (not to say the coffee is good, but it's alright). Plenty of seats and reasonable decor make it half-decent.

Best local coffee shop in town!..they made everything from their own catering company, altho the place (for indoor seating) pretty limited, they have outdoor tables which is suppper nice when its sunny n warmer!
Their sandwiches are delicioso!!!
Luke was a very good place to eat.....not quite around the French quarter but, it was good....I had the Swordfish and it was cooked to perfection!

Came here with my marine vet and best high school friend in New Orleans 11/1/14. We were in good spirits and wanted to give this place a chance.
Nestled on St. Charles in the business district surely gave the experience a different a twist than what I'm used to-very metropolitan. Once inside, the ambiance had a degree of warmth yet the seating was cluttered and uncomfortable. I did like the tin copper ceilings and wall decor. Everything flowed and nicely put together.
We ordered the crab bisque and flamenkechu as appetizers. My friend ordered the burger and I had shrimp and grits, as a suggestion taken from our waiter. 

Everything we ordered was good, almost borderline great but not quite there.

Why? PORTIONS. 

The crab bisque tasted really good but it was served in ounces  in what resembled a shot glass. 
Same thing with my $24 shrimp and grits. 
My friend jokingly asked me "you got the shrimp, but when are they going to bring you your grits?". (the flavor was great but definitely not unmatched anywhere in a 2 miles radius- the Wank and Chalmette included)
My buddy is a marine and I'm 6'2/230lbs and the waiter brings us ONE roll for both of us prior to the appetizers.
My buddy was extremely pleased with his burger and we shared the flamenkechu which really was a home run.
The service was good but not great. I accompanied my meal with water since I don't booze and the waiter didn't offer me any options for non boozers. I literally ate my entire entrée with an empty glass the whole time. And I had to request a roll because that shrimp and grits was beyond skimpy and an insult to the "paying hungry". In all seriousness, those grits were ridiculously overpriced and should be an appetizer if they insist in serving sample portions to the "paying hungry".
I understand that the location is probably very expensive and in my conclusions it is clear that this restaurant is over hyped. Thank you Travel Channel.

Would I come again? Sure. (as long as someone else pays) Not worth the cents off a food lovers hard earned cash- there are others places in New Orleans worthy of charging like they do here. Lükes definitely hit the right notes in flavor but have yet to provide the experience as some established and legendary restaurants  do in this city.
 
If you read this and you're already sitting down at Luke's; get the burger and the flamenkechu. 

One thing to note. I'm a true local and have in New Orleans since the 1980's. The people sitting inside around me... All tourists and transplants.

Great ambiance, good food and amazing service. I wish I could remember our waitress's name since she was such a doll and deserves a shoutout (she was blond and super sassy if that helps :) We tried the tabasco honey fried chicken with dirty rice, the crawfish bisque, and the shrimp encocotte. Our favorite dishes were the crawfish bisque and the dirty rice. The other dishes were good...just not great. However, I'm still giving this place 4 stars because of the overall experience due to our wonderful server.

Went here for brunch a while ago. Very nice atmosphere, staff was very attentive and all brunch items were very good. My friends go here all the time, it's consistently good quality food. There have been places I liked better in New Orleans but I would return here.
Nick V was absolutely amazing, charming, and the service was outstanding. Food was amazing... He even hooked us up with free desert

We went for breakfast. The food was great and the service attentive.

It is away from the crowded parts of town so nice for a quiet brunch.

They have a happy hour where oysters are special price.  I went with high expectations but it was just okay.  My food wasn't seasoned enough and lot of it tasted bland.  The fish was not crispy.  Too bad because it could've been really good.  Wish they salted the water more when the potatoes were boiled because no matter how much salt I put on them, they didn't stick and it just wasn't the same.  It was super busy as usual and I waited a long time to get my water refilled.  It was my last meal in NOLA and I almost wished I had gone to Cuchon Butcher :(
Went for the  happy hour oysters. SO GOOD! Will go back for all my future NOLA visits

Have never been to Elm but I attended an event that was catered by Elm and it was fabulous! The food arrived a few minutes before lunch break and there were various boxes organized by sandwich types.

First, there was an awesome selection of drinks.  They had various bottles of soda and San Pellegrino drinks to choose from.  There were 4 assorted sandwiches cut in half but I found they were generous  Having 2 portions left me full although I couldn't resist the dessert.  It was a rice krispie square with marshmallow flamed on top.  Lots of gooey, sweet goodness that almost put some of us in a food coma though.  I had half a huge square and couldn't finish the rest.  Wow! 

Sandwiches were delish and very creative dessert.  Definitely more creative and good than the typical boring catered lunches.  Great choice for catering company!

Excellent food, service and atmosphere! We all had several items and everything was cooked to perfection. The desserts were scrumptious, especially the bread pudding. The appetizers are a must, especially the Brussels sprouts. And the entrees were all amazing. A must in NOLA.

75 not 50 cent oysters at happy hour. It was still my favorite food experience during my short visit to NO. The ambience is cool bar but not dark.  Would definitely come here after work for drinks. Had half off wine glass and draft beers. And happy hour is 3 hours!!! Also had the amaze balls deep fried brussel sprouts with apples and cheese - so friggin delicious. Tried the rabbit and chicken liver pate which was pretty good. Almost tasted like bleu cheese and had so many nice relishes and mustards and chutneys. Had a dozen raw oysters all to myself. Best with just lemon juice and bit of fresh horseradish. yummy!!! Wish we had a place like this back home.

My first ever review ever. Just never been blown away by such good food before! This place is incredible! Do note that I am a vegetarian, and finding veggie places in NOLA is no joke. So I just walked in here, hoping to get lucky. The initial menu selection was disappointing. Apart from a couple of salads, pretty much nothing for me. So I started with a French 75, and oh my! Deliciousness! Then I decide to try the Brussel Sprout salad, and am speechless at the moment. Can't believe how good this is... Must Must have. 

So excited to try more of NOLA cuisine.

This restaurant is amazing! Perfect lunch spot in the CBD. The decor and staff are very welcoming. I tried the croque Monsieur as suggested by the waiter, and it was delicious! It was perfectly cooked and perfectly cheesed as to be expected with that kind of sandwich! Would definitely recommend to someone looking for a nice lunch.

Beautiful restaurant. Small. It was cold OUTSIDE & they kept the a/c on INSIDE? I asked three times to turn off a/c & they said they could not b/c it's from the hotel???Whatever....
The prices are high 
Quality is good
Gumbo was the best I've had so far in NoLa with mussels, Okra & shrimp ....
The shrimp & grits for $24 had 6 shrimp hmmmmm??? It was good but not really better then the S&G I had for 1/2 the price. I was here as 3pm hit and the oysters dropped from $16 dozen down to $6. They were local but not as consistent as ice had elsewhere. Price was AWESOME but I'd rather pay literally a few dollars more for more consistent oysters. 
I really wanted to like the place, but....
The cold bothered us
The waiter never refilled my water even after asking
And he didn't clean my table of Galen food until asked...
Poor service (Alex)
:-((

We went here for lunch right after getting off the plane from DC and checking into the JW Marriott. I had the crab sandwich which I did not know would be a whole soft shell crabed in there. I thought it was going to be like crab meat BLT sandwich so that was a little surpriseing. We both got the gumbo which we loved. Hubby got the lunch plate with the 3 sausages and he ranted and raved about them the whole trip. I thought the little diet coke in the glass bottle was too cute! We are used to seeing little glass classic coke, but not diet coke.

Come for happy hour $0.75 oysters and half off cocktails! I would definitely recommend making a reservation if you can. We walked in and was told the wait for a table was going to take almost an hour and a half. Regardless, we put our name down and prayed for some bar seating to open up as those were first come first serve. We ended up finding some standing room at the end of the bar where we ended up ordering some drinks while we waited. I tried a sazerac and the french 75. The French 75 I particularly enjoyed and would definitely recommend to anyone. The girlfriend's mint julep was also quite refreshing and delicious.

Their drinks are quite strong as I was pretty tipsy by the time we got seated at a table (probably 45 minutes after we put our names down, which was well before their estimated time). We had heard good things about the burger so we ordered one to share (which came served with fries) along with 2 dozen oysters. The burger was phenomenal! My opinion may be a bit biased due to my partially inebriated state :P but this was probably one of the most well-cooked burgers I've had in my life. The meat was moist, tender, flavorful, and the best part, it was huge! The fries were addicting, I think we ended up ordering another batch. Oysters were delicious and fresh, I enjoyed them more here than at Acme. Definitely a place I would recommend for anyone visiting to check out.

Amazing service, ambiance and food. A party in my mouth. Great for dining with friends, a date or alone in a corner with the paper. 

Crispy oysters with warm bacon, avocado and a light caesar-like dressing. Generous oysters twice what you'd get in NYC, LA or Boston. Followed by swordfish atop crispy kale with a garlic lemon butter sauce. 

Only one complaint: kale swordfish sauce is way too creamy and buttery. Other than that it's a wonderful experience all around!

I believe a Besh restaurant is to NOLA what Starbucks is to Seattle (and just about everywhere else) - there seems to be one every corner!

Okay, not really, but you've got August, Borgne, Domenica, Besh Steak, Soda Shop and La Provence.  How is a girl to choose?!

Well...time, geography, and funds would up being the deciding factor.  Luke seemed to be a place that would give me a great 'Besh' experience, without draining my bank account.

We came for lunch and this place was PACKED!  Another place I would recommend taking advantage of Open Table.  We were seated in the back room, adjacent to the open prep kitchen.  The decor was very bistro and seemed fitting for the fare.

I ordered the special of the day - the most amazing seafood salad sandwich.  It came on fresh baked and grilled bread.  The salad consisted of shrimp, lobster and crab. All fresh and ALL delicious.  The portions are incredibly generous! 

Hubby ordered the croque monsieur.  The perfect layering of bechemel and the most savory ham.  Very yummy!

Service was outstanding - is everyone this friendly in NOLA!?  

If you're having a hard time narrowing down your choice of Besh eateries, you can't go wrong with Luke.

Luke was a good experience. I went on a weekend for brunch and really enjoyed the food. Everything was reasonably portioned but it was a little on the expensive side. I don't mind paying for food in any capacity but I spent $70 for two on brunch and that turned me off a little it. But even with the price being that high for brunch, the food was still great.
Obsessed with this place. Great fresh seafood and incredible hors d'oeuvres and the service is impeccable. 5 stars for another besh favorite. ASK FOR RICHIE RICH

This was one of my favorite meals when visiting NOLa.  Do yourself a favor and get the Shrimp & Grits. It is by far one of the best things, if not the best thing I ate when visiting the city.  They also had a German meat plate that one of my friends had that looked like it was enough food for three people (very tasty as well).  For apps I recommend the oysters and one of the local soups... they are all good.  Bread pudding for dessert as well.  I will definitely be back when I am in town.

Came to Luke solely for the 3:00 - 6:00 pm happy hour special (half off drinks and 75 cent oysters). Made reservations for 3:30 pm but that wasn't necessary as the restaurant was pretty open (we went mid-July)

We got exactly what we were looking for. Oysters were great and provided to us quickly. Much bigger than what we were used too in Toronto. Staff was extremely friendly as well.

Not impressed with this restaurant compared to Emeril's for the prices and John Besh was here himself, on Saturday night. But instead of walking around and making sure things were/should have been going well with his diners, he was having diner himself with three other people. Casual setting. My husband said it wasn't the best shrimp and grits as others have said. The crab appetizer was really good and my steak was great. The stuffed oysters were okay but didn't compare to Drago's. Rosemary potatoes were nice and crispy but too much Rosemary in them in my opinion.

I love this place.  Best sandwiches in town.  A sandwich is $8 and it's worth it.  The menu changes frequently offering 4 lunch sandwiches and 2 breakfast sandwiches usually, and a type of soup.  It's cramped quarters with about 4 stools inside and 4 tables outside.  It's a little gem tucked in the bottom of an apartment building.  The lack of seating is annoying but once you have the first bight from the menu, Wow!

We are big fans of John Besh and had eaten at his American Sector restaurant and were sitting at the bar in Drago's and the bartender brought up Luke, saying it was his best.   My wife had gotten a Lonely Planet guide book prior to the trip (and they usually steer us the right way) but it had NO mention of Luke.   

So on our last night in town we decided to give it a try.   I made a reservation online and when we arrived the restaurant was very busy, but they seated us right away.   We were taken through the dining room, through a set of doors and up into another dining area that overlooked the kitchen, providing a cool view of the chefs at work.   

We started with two glasses of champagne, which immediately led the nice waitress to inquire if this was a special occasion but we were just celebrating our last meal in town with a glass of bubbly.    We were continually tag teamed by her and another young lady all night, both taking great care of us.   

We had gotten the charbroiled oysters at Drago's and loved them so we decided to try the P&J Oysters as an appetizer.    Hmm.....how to describe other than so so good and wished we had 3 orders of them.   I could have picked the shell up and cleaned every drop with my teeth if given the chance :-)   

Another nice thing is that for wine drinkers you have not only a variety of wine to choose from, but you can get bottles, carafes, 3/4 carafes, 1/2 carafes, or glasses.   

For entrees, my wife got the shrimp and grits and I got étouffée.   I must say that hers blew mine away, first of all the grits.....soooo creamy from the mascarpone cheese that they put in it, I decided I am ONLY going to make my grits that way from now on.   And the shrimp, were so perfectly cooked, it is hard to describe.  Not spongy or gummy like some places who use frozen shrimp or overcook them, these were cooked perfect.   As for the étouffée, sorry John but mine is better :-)   

If you're in New Orleans, give it a try, you won't be disappointed.

Amazing food! Rabbit and chicken liver pate with a variety of mustards, preserves and pickles. So very yummy. Possibly the best pate I have ever eaten, and I am a fan of pate! Brussels sprout appetizer was amazingly flavorful. Rib eye steak came with a creamy rich bernaise sauce, burgers were mile high and loaded with bacon, shrimp etouffe was spicy and served over pasta instead of rice for something a little different. Try the French 75 cocktail - champagne and cognac with a cherry... They even wrote the name of the restaurant with cherry juice in the foam! Wish I could be hungry again right now and order another pate appetizer...

One of the best brunches in New Orleans! The pancakes are the BEST I've ever had...they are served with a cinnamon butter topping. The chicken biscuit is awesome with the Tabasco honey sauce...the jalapeño cheese grits are a must have!!! The burger was good but nothing special...This place is now a must do when I'm in Nola!

Wow. What to say - honestly one of the most disappointing meals I've ever had in New Orleans. Two stars only for the service and amazing brussel sprouts the table next to me shared with me!

I ordered the P&J oysters and steak frites per the server's recommendations. The oysters were huge, but the smaller ones were actually the more flavorful and tasty. The big ones tasted like ... nothing. They were also very gritty - I kept having to slyly take shell out of my mouth :(

The steak. I was SO LOOKING FORWARD TO A GOOD STEAK. It was chewy and fatty. I had to spit out so many pieces and left a good amount left. The fries were overcooked and burned. My server asked if everything was okay, I said no not really, and they said okay and took it away and gave me the check.

The only saving grace was the service and the people next to me. OH and the fabulous Russian River pinot. SO SO SO disappointed and cannot in good conscious recommend this place. Maybe it was an off day, Sunday? Either way, sad face.

If you like dragon rolls this is the place to go. They are huge. I love this place. Miso soup is great. 

never had a bad experience and the fish is filled with flavor

This place is awesome! Luke's has a very lively atmosphere and the food is superb! I ordered the fish of the day. I can't remember what type of fish it was, but it was a local gulf catch and was as fresh as it gets. It was also a very large portion, which I was not expecting.  It was prepared lightly-pan fried and served on a bed of perfectly yummy vegetables. I also order a side of creamy potatoes, which are small red potatoes. Very good!  For dessert, I had a steamed chocolate dish with salty caramel ice-cream that was to die for. I really  enjoyed my experience and would recommend to check it out.
Perfect Dinner, very family friendly. Coming from Germany and having traveled a week. This was the best food. And: thanks to Nick and Nick. The service was perfect too!

Fantastic lunch! I met a friend for lunch and we sat at the bar. Brandy was our bartender. She was funny, helpful, and we had a great time chatting w/ her. The seafood tower was amazing. We got the small one and couldn't finish it. I also had a cup of the crawfish bisque and it was lovely. What a great restaurant!

Hands down the best restaurant for a anniversary! Our severs Chi & Shane made sure our night was perfect. Right when we sat down, we received complementary glass of champagne---amazing. We started with the crab bisque to split. It was overflowing with lump crab meat. Couldn't get enough of it! For dinner, I got the mussels and they were dynamite. They came in a buttery thyme sauce and I couldn't stop dipping bread and fries into it haha. My boyfriend got the infamous Lüke burger. It was so juicy and good. The fries were hand downs awesome. Love that they are shoe string style. You get enough in one order to split! For dessert we decided to get the creme brûlée to split. That was to die for. It came with fruit on top. We got the bill and noticed the restaurant comped our dessert! We will definitely be back and will ask for Chi and Shane!

I want to give this restaurant an higher rating, because it probably deserves one by most accounts. Yet, my star ratings are based on an overall feeling I had about the place, and my overall feeling about Luke was "It was ok, but not memorable." In a city of great restaurants, there was nothing that would compel me to return. At the same time, there was nothing that would keep me from it. 

Our group very much enjoyed the caramelized onion and cheese flat bread appetizer, and the patte platter that hearkens to the German influence here. I chose the burger because of its high rating on Food Network. With the large onion bun and the fresh meat, it was incredibly large and excellent. The fries were a nice complement. Other friends enjoyed the very rich but excellent shrimp and grits. 

We all left satisfied, and our server was very attentive and sweet. But would I tromp back over to the Warehouse District for it again? Not sure, but I'd be happy if someone paid. :)

Like many others I'm still confused as to why there is an umlaut in Lüke. I almost laughed out loud when the couple next to me thought that there would be German food served. Silly nolans. 

I came here due to the fact this place was walking distance to my hotel - well at least my original hotel reservation at Intercontinental. 

It was "We Live to Eat" week in NOLA which was an equivalent of restaurant week. So I made reservations to try their prefix menu.

I started off with the oysters (not part of the prefix menu). They were really good and fresh. I was disappointed I missed out on the happy hour special as I would totally come back for the oysters. 

For the prefix menu I had: 

Lobster and ricotta stuffed squash blossoms
This had an interesting lime-y taste - yet savory. The thing I can compare it to is the lime, salt, pepper sauce you dip french cube beef in. The squash blossoms were good and the lobster was a bit negligible. 

Slow cooked swordfish with heirloom tomato, olive, caper, garganelli
If I learned anything on this trip, it is that I don't care much for green olives. I don't know what I was expecting with this dish -  and I think this is my fault for perhaps not reading  the menu carefully or asking questions. I suppose this is a good dish if you like swordfish, tomato sauce and green olives - however because I don't like those things that much I really shouldn't have gotten dish dish. 

Fig tart, brown butter ice cream
This is really good if you like fig newtons. It was basically a giant fig tart with ice cream. It was pretty good - but I don't care for figs that much. The ice cream was delicious though. 

In all I couldn't really understand the flavors that were presented at Lüke for restaurant week. I think the ambiance is great for an after work kinda deal as it's very french brasserie. The happy hour specials I understand for the oysters are also very good. I would come back for happy hour if I lived in the area.

A part of me doesn't want to review this place, I would rather keep it a secret gem, but hey it's always good to share.

This maybe one of the best happy hours in New Orleans!  Happy hour is from 3 to 6 and it is not limited to bar seating.  It is a white tablecloth restaurant but most people where casually dressed and it seems pretty laid back.

Now on to the happy hour specials.  Raw oysters were 50 cents and I think the fried oysters were a dollar, but we kept with the raw.  These oysters were the best oysters we had during our twelve days in New Orleans and we had quite a few oysters.  No grit what so ever and they were good size oysters.

Specialty drinks, draft beer, and wine are half price.  We started with a couple of rounds of mojitos, the mojitos were not on the drink menu but they were included in the happy hour pricing.  They were a little on the sweet side but we asked our waiter if he could bring us some fresh lime wedges, which he did and that  solved that problem.

Decided on one more round of drinks but we changed it up an ordered a Silver Saint and a Sazerac.

The Silver Saint (tequila, fresh lime juice, cucumber syrup, Serrano pepper, and soda water) was a great drink, loved the kick from the Serrano pepper.  

The Sazerac (Rye, sugar, peychauds bitters and herbsaint) BF enjoyed this drink.

Definitely check out this happy hour, you will not be disappointed.  Wish we had learned about it sooner, I'm sure we would have gone a couple of more times.

Smash #1 hit.

Couple cocktails before / with dinner...  of course..  

Of course they were tasty.

The oysters were delicious.

I consider myself an oyster snob; and the one's here were terrific.

I had the fish o' the day (I think it was grouper) and it was extremely fresh tasting.

The place is booshie.

There are many very good restaurants in New Orleans, and "dis be" another one..

Oh, and I forgot to mention the service start to finish, head to toe was spot on.

You're a bad boy!
The bread pudding and shrimp and grits were amazing!! The male waiters look like models nice,.professional atmosphere.

Although I am still trying to figure out how to pronounce "Lüke" because an umlaut is not normally used in the English language, I would say that this restaurant deserves my applause.

We actually came in TWICE in one night. First, we figured out that they have an amazing Oyster Bar happy hour, whereas an oyster -- cold, shucked, accompanied with horseradish and cocktail sauce -- is provided to diners for the wholly unbelievable total of $.50. Yes folks, that's FIFTY CENTS.

(SIDE NOTE: A table of 6 gentlemen in the dining room were simultaneously enjoying delicious shucked oysters, and they ordered 15 dozen. FIFTEEN DOZEN. 180 OYSTERS. Still amazed by that, as were the sarcastically happy oyster shuckers who kept getting tickets for more oysters by the 3 dozen.)

We left, changed into some dress shirts and closed toed shoes, and returned for dinner a mere hour later. Immediately, we were treated with some amazingness in the form of meat:

Onion Tart appetizer: Amazingly tasty smoked bacon, emmenthaler swiss, and carmelized onions, baked on top of a thin crispy bread. It was a flavorful combination of cooked items, cheesy and smoky at the same time. Only bad thing was it was overly herbed, as there were lingering flavors of herbness that drowned out the rest. 7 out of 10.

Ribeye Steak: 10 ounces of prime beef, perfectly grilled, topped with an herb butter, sided with bernaise and frites. It gets an 8 out of 10, simply because a ribeye should be no smaller that 16 ounces.

Pork Shank: RIDICULOUSSAUCE. Must've been cooked for a day before. There is no way the chef gets an order for this fall-off-the-bone amazingness and is able to take it from raw to amazing in 15 minutes. Slow roasted, TENDER, with an amazing sauerkraut underlining and a hidden sausage just under the shank. 10 out of 10.

We left in the worst food coma that I may have ever experienced. I actually had to spread out my body, stand up, and stretch in order to BREATHE. I have never been quite so full as I was when I left Lüke, but it is not the food's fault. 

I. Just. Couldn't. Stop. Eating.

I was caught off guard by the casual/formal atmosphere of Luke. The food was absolutely top drawer, but it felt as though John Besh couldn't decide what type of restaurant he wants Luke to be. The waiters wear white jackets, the tables have white linens covered with butcher paper....the music is loud 70's and 80's pop. Can you say Adam Ant? The waitstaff was almost overly friendly, singing along with some of the songs!  The food was amazing.... delicious from the crab/corn bisque to the final bite of bread pudding.  It just felt a little like the old movie Sybil.....how many personalities can you have?

Had an early lunch here. They were kind enough to serve what I wanted of if the lunch menu even though it was still early. 

I had the BLTAAU open faced sandwich on a very slim toasted bread. The tomatoes were thick and delicious. The Allan Bacon was thick and crisp. The sandwich was so good. 

Everything here was good!

Luke is one of my top 3 go to New Orleans restaurants.
This is a great place for happy hour!  1/2 price drinks from 3-6, maybe until 7.  The bar munchies are delish, too!
Amazing lunch- options for vegetarians, vegans and omnivores alike. Make a reservation if you can.
wonderful food. first time to nola will eat here again if we return to nola. great customer service.

I just can't say enough good things about this hidden eatery that is the best in Edmonton in my opinion. The staff are all fun, happy, eager to please, polite, encouraging and understanding when I can't make up my mind! Their soup is the best ever!!!!! Their salads are amazing with different flavours in every bite, and the sandwiches . . . dripping goodness in every bite. They now have $1.00 coffee at lunch time and they have won me over from Tim's as their coffee has is a whole bodied flavor but not to strong either. The breakfast sandwiches are surprisingly good as I was really impressed with their grilled vegetarian cauliflower breakfast. Amazing that I haven't repeated any of the items I have ordered yet but still want too! I have been eating at Elm Cafe for over a year now and it is my number one go to place for breakfast and lunch!

Came for happy hour with my son.  We ended up starting with two dozen 50 cent oysters and fries.  The fries were fantastic.  Not crispy and frite-like as I expected but slightly sweet, creamy interior and well seasoned.  Oysters were great, oddly the first couple of dozen didn't have much liquor, but they were clean and not a hit of a bad one.  We ordered another dozen which were swimming in their own juices, briny and even more delicious.  But were were pretty much stuffed to order more.
The staff was fantastic.  Very attentive, the waitress couldn't tell me much about the Luke Alt so afterwards came back and asked me about it's hoppiness vs. malt.  (pretty balanced actually).  Got a Mardesous next cold and perfect.

All in all, simply couldn't ask for more even though it was just happy hour.  The price was definitely right, the staff was righteous and I will be back.
Great food and super friendly staff. We had flummenkuchen, salads, steak & etouffe and would have them again.
The oysters were really good and fresh!  The drinks are tasty and I especially loved the shrimp & grits dish.  Definitely do the s'mores dessert.

Just stopped in for a quick bite before a wedding...not a franchise sports bar...had the blt club on rye and was pleasantly surprised...I think they cooked the bacon on the spot rather than have a bunch of precook bacon reheated...quite tasty and enjoyed it a lot...

I was pleasantly surprised with my dinner at Luke. Several people in my party have specific diets gluten and vegetarian to be exact. The staff was very accommodating and made the visit even more enjoyable. Our waiter Alessandro and the manager Robert were very attentive and helpful in helping us pick dishes. They were able to make changes to the dishes  and the end result was perfection. I grew up in Germany and the spaetzle could rival my grandmothers. The flamenkuche was a slice of yum and the garlic mashed potatoes were amazing. Just when you think the meal couldn't get any better we ordered dessert. The baked chocolate mousse was like having a piece of heaven in your mouth. If this is what a John Besh experience consists of sign me up every time.

Awesome! Best dining experience in New Orleans over a 6-day stay. A fresh-faced server with a northeastern accent was exceedingly friendly and helpful.

The burger is in the top 3 I have ever had. Fries were good too!
The gumbo was tasty and nuanced.
Nice conservative, comfortable, clean atmosphere.

Go here, Please.

We really enjoyed our happy hour here at Luke. We were from oot and came for oyester happy hour and honestly don't have a lot of money. The place was very nice. I wish I remember  the names of the staff. They were really so gracious and helpful. They didn't not seem annoyed that we were there for happy hour. They were so professional helpful and kind. We ordered fried oysters, raw oysters and drinks. We had a super lovely time and they food was wonderful. Really I suppose we don't really like raw oysters but had never had them. These seemed like good quality tho. Thank you so much Luke! If you are in the area I would recommend Luke.

The best Brussels Sprouts I have had!!!! The Luke salad is probably on my top 3 favorite salads so far. Just those 2 reasons right there are enough for me to come back here next time I'm in NOLA!

It was raining cats and dogs when we arrived. Not sure if that's the reason we were able to be seated right away during their brunch time without a reservation. The restaurant has 2 separate seating sections I believe. The decoration is very French colonial type, classy and beautiful. 

For starters, we got the Brussels Sprouts and Luke salad. They are must try here! The Brussels Sprouts have so many flavors going on, but not in an overwhelming way. Everything compliments each other so well. They are cooked perfectly too, nice crispy texture outside, a lil soft inside, not too greasy. The salad was super fresh and pair so well with their delicious dressing!

For the main entrees, I got myself the chicken cordon blu sandwich. It was huge and super hot with each bite, the hot lava cheese would almost burn my mouth if I eat them too fast. Definitely have to eat with a fork and knife. My SO got the shrimps and grit which I think I enjoyed more than my sandwich lol.

We ended the meal with the hazelnut Paris Brest which comes with pate a choux (not sure what that is lol), passion fruit, coconut. The ice cream and passion fruit were really good. The pastry (maybe that's wat pate a choux is?) that's supposed to bind everything together was too dry for me and didn't have much taste. 

Overall it wasn't a bad experience, except the super slow service at the end of our meal, it took our waitress a good 15-20mins to give us our check and another 10mins or so to complete everything. We would definitely come back here again for their salad, Brussel sprouts, and maybe try other entrees on their menu next time.

Scoped this place out and made a res prior to arriving in NOLA. Definitely recommend a reservation as it was happening even on a Tuesday night! The baked oysters were delicious as was the shrimp and grits dish. These are probably their most well known dishes and I am glad to say they lived up to the hype. Skipped dessert but the waiter tried to sell us on a smores thing that sounded yum, so will have to try that if I make it back. 

TBH the table service left something to be desired.. it was friendly but nothing above and beyond. Two guys were working in a team and one was more attentive than the other. Although, I will say the manager brought us a complimentary soup due to a minor delay on our app. That was totally unnecessary but very much appreciated, and it was delicious. So that was redeeming. 

Overall food was delish, so would come again!

Came here to celebrate my 60th birthday on the recommendation of my client in Toronto. We were seated @ the bar area right in front where the staff was shucking fresh oysters & ordered the large assorted seafood platter, brussel sprout, bread pudding, all were fresh & delicious. Service was excellent & will return for another rememberable meal, when in NOLA.

J and I are suckers for celebrity chefs so on our trip to NoLa, we had to eat at Lüke. We came for lunch and ordered:

The Southern Breakfast ($15): sunny-side up egg, Allan Bentons bacon, hash browns and a buttery flaky biscuit with fresh chunky blackberry jam. The hash browns were amazing - pan fried potatos mixed with chunks of cubed bacon. 

The Lousiana Shrimp&Grits ($22):  The dish came in a small 6inch cast iron griddle. A bit pricey (considering we paid half the price for shrimp&grits at Surreys) but very delicious.  The jalapeno-cheese grits were the perfect consistency (very creamy from all the butter) topped with sausage and jumbo shrimp swimming in a some cajun sauce. The dish was small but very heavy and filling.

We came back the next day after hearing about the happy hour 50 cent oysters on a half shell and $1 fried oysters. We got 2 dozen raw which was a bad idea considering each oyster was the size of my palm ANDI felt they didn't taste fresh - as if shucked hours too soon in preparation for happy hour. Stick to ACME or Felix's for the raw stuff.

The best hamburger I've ever had! And the fries -- to die for! Everything from the decor and ambiance to the drinks and food were perfect. And at reasonable prices for New Orleans.

If you can't afford Chef Besh's more expensive restaurants, then this is the next best thing.

Happy hour!!!

We are a group of friends who get together once a month for dinner club. Every month a different person selects a restaurant and we hit it up. Today was our two year anniversary and we decided to start reviewing.

Draft beers
1 luke fru - nothing special. Rating close to a natty light or any regular light beer.
2 Luke alt - much better deft beer. Good flavor, but light for an amber. Great summer beer.

Mixed specialty drinks
Champagne au peche, sazarac, streetcar, French 75, old fashioned, absinthe frappe - all really good! Can't go wrong in this area!

Oysters - $0.50/oyster during happy hour . You just can't go wrong there.

Pomme frites - great fries. A must for happy hour 

You really can't go wrong at like happy hour. Super classy joint, great food, great location, great drinks, great atmosphere.

The only reason we give Luke's a 4/5 is because the group couldn't decide on the full 5 I wanted to give.

We really really liked this place. Found it by dumb luck even tho we wanted to eat at a few of John Besh's places. Had brunch and while it was quite pricey, it was also very good. Loved the crab bisque and the chicken biscuit. The shrimp and grits wasn't the best I've ever had but it was a little different and I still liked it a lot. Our waitress was friendly and it's been one of the best breakfast/brunches we've had in Nola. It's also amazing to see how swiftly the manager replies to all the negative reviews! I did joke with my husband that I could lie to get a free meal but I'm not that underhanded! I'm not so sure some of these other bad reviewers aren't doing that tho ;) We had a great experience and would happily come back!

This was average food.  Had a reservation for 7 people.   Restaurant confirmed it in the morning.  When we arrived it was obvious there was some confusion. Sat us at a table right in front which is kind of an after thought area.  Asked if there was a table more toward the back but there was not. Cool air comes in every time door is opened.  People waiting to be seated right on top of us.  Our waiter Vusi was very good.  Brightest spot of the place really. Manager came over to see if everything was ok after seating us with "5 minutes notice and doing the best they could ". So this was the issue our table was given to walk ins.  When we told her it was not ok and we had made a reservation over a week ago she realized their error.  So she offered dessert to the table as a consultation. Some dishes very good , shrimp and grits for example. Others just ok.  If back in the area would not make it a point to return

They have a few of my favorite things: NFL Sunday ticket! 7 flat screens on the wall. Victory HopDevil on Tap. Fellow Fantasy Footballers hanging watching 5 games simultaneously. A nice wait staff. 
Their menu is the stereotypical sports bar menu. They have it all. I've only had the wings, of course the first thing I try. They are good, but not Union Jack's good.
They do still have smoking in the bar area. Which means they make most their money from alcohol sales. A brew and a game go great with some wings. That's all I need for a local sports pub.
Good food but great service! Seated in the back upstairs corner table, managers checked in often. By Linh was the best server on the planet!!

Highly recommended. Great Japanese food with high quality fish. The owner is willing to spend money on getting the best while  remain reasonable price. Check this place if you are professional for Japanese food.

I've been to Luke many times and always enjoyed the food. This past time the service was beyond outstanding. My boyfriend and I were lucky enough to to have the Rich Whatley/Rusty Russell team serving us. Rich recommended outstanding menu items based on what we were interested in. We always get a couple dozen oysters, gumbo, and shrimp and grits (all of which are excellent). It was refreshing to have such accurate recommendations and wine pairings! Both gentlemen were friendly, professional, and attentive throughout the course of the meal. Just another reason to go back again and again!

Ordered $100 combo. The quality was slightly better than what you would get from chinese buffet places. What made the experience even worse was that the servers were extremely unpleasant and constantly hovering around the table making me feel rushed. I enjoy going to japanese restaurants because I expect excellent ambience and services. I wasn't receiving neither.  Needless to say,  this will be the first and the last time I will be going to this place.

I tried gumbo for the first time here. It was OK, there shrimp was too squishy, something else in it tasted funny. The base of the gumbo was OK tho, maybe it was old idk but never had i had shrimp just squish in my mouth.

The service was terrible, the guy never came. I had to flag him down for a refill (which took 10 mins).

Food came out fast but i wouldn't recommend

All I've had here was shrimp and grits and wow was I impressed.  Loved the service and atmosphere too, look forward to a return visit next time I'm in the World's Best Food City :)  Somehow I didn't know about this restaurant, a Besh restaurant no less, it just happened to be across from my hotel.  Man am I glad we stopped in.

Last night in NOLA and we had stayed away from luke since it is in a hotel. But it is definitely not a typical hotel restaurant. Made reservations thru opentable like 2 hours before we wanted to eat with no problem. Got there, table ready, and started on our food exploration. Menu has some items in French so don't be afraid to ask about items. They have a 23$ special where you get a soup, entree of the day and dessert. We ordered as appetizer the seafood bisque and matzo ball soup and a pork pate that was really good. For entree, the unanimous choice for best of the table was the Luke burger. Everything else was great (coq au vin, roasted chicken, ham and cheese sandwich) but the burger got reviews such as best burger ever. Desserts were ok. Definitely worth the visit.
Great staff, fine kitchen, nice beverage choices and open all day! A better than home away from home!

Arrived late into New Orleans Sunday night and nothing seems to be open later than 10 pm. What??  I supposed I should be sympathetic being in the industry but my wife and I were starving so....  

Luke was open till 11pm. Yes!!!!!  Walked a few blocks to it and was not disappointed at all. A mint julep and an old fashion later, we were in a good mood. 

A little gumbo was full of shrimp and andouille sausage rice and green onions. We have arrived. 

Shrimp sausage and grit was amazing. My wife's. Mahe mahe was perfect as well. Crispy fried kale to go with purée of cauliflower was fantastic. 

Our dessert was a bread pudding that was absolutely the best. Broiled till crispy and topped with candied pecans butter bourbon caramel.  I couldn't be hungry anymore at this point but we flying through the bowl like there was no tomorrow. 

I can't wait to eat my way through my trip to NOLA. Visiting gracious bakery tomorrow. Awesome trip to come.

A French brasserie with a very solid happy hour with 75cent oysters and half off wines and cocktails.

Service is professional and friendly but unfortunately the kitchen is soooooo slowww....but I guess that gives us time to consume more wine!  

On a side note, I've never been a fan of oysters in New Orleans. They lack flavor and crispness and brininess whatsoever. But that's just what you get here.. At least they were fresh.
Pretty good brunch. Wonderful venue, friendly & competent staff, and delicious food. I'd certainly recommend the mixed vegetables, tuna tartare, and the fries (but with the house aioli).
Delish grits,  wonderful french bread, would like yo go back for din!
