ate here for my birthday  with my family which included my 3 year old niece and 5 year old nephew. we wanted some place affordable but nice. the place was affordable yes nice not really. for a place that has an expensive frutti di mare on the menu. i would have expected it to look more upscale like his other restaurants.

 i had the famous burger my sis had the shrimp and grits and my niece and nephew chicken tenders. my burger was good but not the best ive had. my sis shrimp was good but the grits were too dense for my taste.

i may be back perhaps for brunch.

This was a good but not great brunch place in New Orleans. The server was friendly and on top of what I needed. The menu just didn't have as much variety as I expected. The food itself did taste great though and you will find something you like for sure. I'm just not sure it's a place I would go back to without trying out some other choices first.

Another great Yelp tip. It was really cold the weekend I was in NOLA and I wanted
to have breakfast somewhere other than Mothers (which I really like) but it had to be close to my hotel. Read the reviews and went for breakfast. Had traditional breakfast of scrambled eggs and bacon (no grits and no biscuits cause of diet) but they
happily substituted a terrific fruit cup instead. Bacon was really good. My wife had the crab meat omelet and devoured it. Service was very good and I was very happy with the choice. Thanks again Yelp reviewers.

Excellent decor and vibe, very Parisian bistro feeling. We had brunch, the Bloody Mary was great; we sat at the bar & all of the cocktails looked yummy and thoughtfully prepared. Eggs in a jar crowned with big beautiful fried shrimp was worth the the
hype. A crabmeat starter was generous and tasty but could have used some more greens, the accompanying croutons were crunchy and tasty.  Since Luke is the only restaurant affiliated with the Hilton, they're open early till late 7 days a week. Ill be back next trip to try more, everything on the menu sounded awesome.

First stop on our trip to New Orleans and it was delicious! My girlfriend was set on going to a great restaurant in town and picked this one and I'm very glad she did. We both had delicious appetizers and meals and, though a little pricier than what we're used to, it was worth it. She had the gumbo and I had the crab bisque for apps, then enjoyed shrimp and grits and the ribeye and fries for meals, all which were great. Our desserts were ok, not as memorable, though. Would certainly return and recommend!

Great after work meeting place in downtown NOLA. Raw bar is awesome.  Typically sit at the bar and order as required.   Staff friendly. There is a full menu but it's hard for me to venture out past seafood.

Dude, happy hour at Luke was excellent. Half price on excellent cocktails - I tried the Cypress and the Riverbend - and  cheap oysters. We also got the shrimp and grits and the flamenkuche, which was a crisp bread covered in creamy cheese and onions. Our Swiss-German coworker said it wasn't as good as her mom's, but what ever is? Definitely a good place for a nosh.
Try happy hour fresh oysters.  Delicious! Bufala Negra cocktail was amazing.  Staffs were very kind.
I just wasn't impressed. With so many wonderful places to eat in NOLA, I expected something really fantastic and just was completely under-whelmed.
A very good meal at a decent price.  We got the daily special which also came with Soup and Dessert for 24 dollars.  Well worth it.  I would go back.

I had an amazing time at Luke, not only the food is great.  Oyster happy hour is only $.75 each and super big!  Servers always make sure your needs are met at the first time. They really deserve 5 star and yet they only charge you so low.. 
Compared with the Felix... I can only say Luke is like heaven while Felix is a nightmare...

I knew I wanted to eat at one of John Besh's restaurants (I think he has around 9) when I went to NOLA a few weeks ago. I just wasn't sure which one. Judging from all the yelp reviews, we chose Luke. 

It was around a 10-15 minute walk from Bourbon St., and we definitely worked up an appetite getting there. The restaurant is fairly small and once you walk in, you see all of John Besh's cookbooks lined up on a table for purchase. We came at around 2pm and the lunch rush was dying down. 

We ordered:

Stuffed P&J oysters: They were good and the oysters were large, but the toppings took away from the oyster. I prefer Acme's grilled oysters.

Crispy brussel sprouts: So yummy! I love the slivers of green apples they added.

Crispy crawfish etouffee: I wasn't sure what to expect, since I've never had etouffee. This dish surprised me with the texture. The waitress told us they deep fry the rice before making the dish. So it was kind of like eating a savory version of rice crispies. If you love crawfish (there were like at least 3 crawfish in every bite) and love texture, definitely order this!

Shrimp and grits: I've never had grits either! The first few bites were rich and creamy, but I don't think I can eat more than 5 bites. 

Jambalaya: I hardly remember it. It was a part of their daily express lunch menu. Too bad we didn't come on a Monday, I wanted to try the tabasco fried chicken.

Soft shell crab BLT: The housemade bacon made this dish!

Bread pudding: It was alright. A little too sweet for my taste. 

Service was great and our waitress did an amazing job educating us about all the dishes. She was training another waiter and they make trainees take a quiz about all the food after training. Nice to know they take such great pride in their service and food. 

Even if you're starving, share your food with someone else. The portions are large!

Located inside the Riverfront Market, Tokyo Sushi probably has the best sushi lunch specials in all of downtown Wilmington because while the pricing is similar amongst other establishments, there rolls are far bigger.

You can get any number of items that are pre packed in the refrigerated cases or order freshly made rolls from the menu. The ingredients, especially the tuna, is super fresh.

Happy Hour Oysters!! 75 cents!

Came for oyster happy hour with a friend while in New Orleans. Saw the great reviews figured I'd give it a shot while in the central business district. 

Nice space, friendly servers and quick service. 

The oysters were probably slightly above average. They seemed fresh however they were really quite sandy, which was disappointing. The sand kept us from ordering more than our original 2 dozen. 

The oyster are gulf oysters which are huge compared to Washington or east coast oyster, so be prepared to order less than you expect. Since they were so large we filled up quite quickly on just 2 dozen for a happy hour snack.

Service was exceptional and food was amazing. Nice cocktails, wine and beer for happy hour half off. Oysters .75 cents and seriously great quality. I think happy hour ended at 7. One of my favorite dining experiences of the many times I've been to New Orleans

After I posted my review of Luke, I was contacted by their general manager who apologized profusely and let me know specifically how they were making changes to the hot room, services as well as the food.  He also invited me to come back to set things right.  Very impressive and I look forward to giving Luke another try.  Well done!

Food was good.  Hostess was extremely rude though. Hostess' behavior seemed to be racially motivated as we were the only Asians in the restaurant.  I don't know if the food quality is worth the rude behavior by the staff.  I will avoid this restaurant in the future.

i was surprisingly unimpressed by lüke. after all the raves i would have expected better. the skate fin entree was so heavily breaded that more of the crust was left on the plate than there was actual skate fin. the root vegetable were alright, only because i'm a big fan of turnips and such. 

i ordered a side of potatoes (and i can't remember exactly how they're titled on the menu but it's EXTREMELY misleading).  basically, was came to our table was three whole boiled red potatoes - no seasoning, olive oil, nothing.  i mean, john besh - really?!?!?!  i thought this was a fucking total lack of effort on the restaurant's part.  to boot, i didn't touch them because i was pretty pissed about it and the waitress didn't show any concern for my disdain for the dish.  having worked at pretty much every position in a restaurant, i would have done my best to take it off the bill because i would recognized how displeased the customer was with this dish.  i'm all about naked cuisine, but this is just bullshit.  $5 for three boiled potatoes.  HUGE turnoff all together.

my brother's dish was not very impressive either.  i would have to say i'm not really into giving lüke another try because this effort was pretty damn weak.  there's SO many more staples that i frequent that just make this meal look so lackluster and junior varsity.

Yelp wasn't kidding about the Oysters. I can sit at LUKE and eat them all day like seeds, they are fresh and delicious. 

The shrimp and grits was also the best I've had! Atmosphere inside was nice and sophisticated, definitely more of a business district type of establishment vs. One in the French Quarter. 

I highly recommend Luke!

Love me some Chipotle!  This is my favorite quick meal place. I won't call it fast food even though they are super speedy and cheap. Everything is always fresh and in stock. I'd say I've visited this location 10+ times and they are never out of any ingredient on their menu. 
They always greet you as soon as you walk in then proceed to ask a bunch of questions right in a row so I do recommend knowing what you want before going in otherwise you will feel rushed.  I kind of like it because it keeps the line moving. Oh yeah, there's usually a line during lunch and dinner hours. But that should just be proof of how yummy it is.  You can easily throw together a healthier option here as opposed to other chain restaurants. 
My usual is a bowl with brown rice, chicken, black beans, mild salsa, cheese and guac.  Its a very filling portion for me and I can usually make it into two meals ( I have no issue with leftovers but I know some people do).  Their tortilla chips are also the bomb!
My partner was so turned on by the foie gras he stopped breathing for a few minutes. The first words out of his mouth after his near-death experience: "so buttery..."

We had pre dinner snack and drinks as we were staying across the street but had Rez elsewhere. Sat at the bar which provided entertainment in the form of a delightful bartender making beautiful cocktails. We had the gumbo soup and crawfish soup. Both were perfect and accompanied by a warm and flaky baguette. Didn't have enough nights to try for full dinner but definitely will on next visit.

Fifty cent oysters during happy hour!!!
Prices and food are really good
Service was mostly good, a little absent sometimes.

We had fresh P&J oysters, the bisque, the tuna tartine, the roasted chicken entree, and the king salmon entree. All were sublime. The puzzling part of the meal was the cold, rock hard, factory produced (little nubs on the bottom) baguette. In a restaurant dedicated to the place and in a city where every restaurant serves hot, fresh, light baguettes, this just seemed like such an obvious miss and such an unnecessary misstep.

I stayed in New Orleans and found this gem of a restaurant on Yelp.  Wow, the food was amazing and service was superb.  I had the shrimp and grits and they were the best ever. Even my friend, who is from LA said they were the best ever.

This is my third time at Luke and the first time leaving my review. I've been here twice for brunch and once for happy hour (can't beat $0.50 oysters!). This past time I came here with family and we shared the Flamenkuche, Eggs in a Jar, and the Crab Omelet. The Flamenkuche was amazing and eggs in a jar were as good as I remember, I would get both again (but not before I try the sausage platter and BBQ shrimp which people at the next table got and it looked fantastic). The omelet was very good (better than most omelets) but was perhaps overshadowed by the other two to the point where it just didn't stand out next to them. 

Service was great, everyone was friendly and helpful. 

Luke, along with Besh's Restaurant August and Domenica are some of my favorite spots in New Orleans.

I went here the other day for lunch with the family. I wasn't sure what to expect at first, it being a Besh restaurant and all I was initially worried that the price would be exorbitant, but I was pleasantly surprised at how relatively affordable it was considering the name and the area.

The menu is very diverse, you have everything from Oysters on the half shell, to eggs and bacon, to rabbit sausage and burgers. I wavered back and forth for a while trying to decide what to order, finally settling on my favorite food of all time the burger (yea I know who goes to a John Besh restaurant and orders a freaking burger?).

Well I wasn't disappointed, the onions were perfectly caramelized, the burger was cooked exactly to my taste, and whatever type of bacon they used was outstanding. The wait staff naturally seemed attentive and knowledgeable about the menu, and even though they were sort of busy they didn't mind special requests.

I will definitely plan on coming back here to have a nice dinner with the Mrs. one day, but for a great place to grab lunch downtown on a Saturday afternoon (and even though they were busy we just walked in off the street and got a table with no wait) I'd recommend this spot in a heartbeat.
Definitely order the brussel sprouts!!! The crab dip was also amazing! Did not love the Flammenkuchen, it was ok. Great service.

I have been here twice, and I've only been in New Orleans for 2.5 months.

My first time was during Restaurant Week. I dined alone on Saturday, September 17th. My meal consisted of:
- Rillettes of Mangalitsa pork with savory marmalades and grilled country bread. OH. MY. GOD. This was so good. It makes me want to try making rillettes myself. The marmalades went so well with the rillettes. I think this is probably what Besh is best at: finding flavors that go together so well but that you don't necessarily think of as accompanying one another.
- Shrimp Farci over corn and field pea succotash and Hollandaise. Delicious.
- L'opera for dessert. This huge cake went home with me because I couldn't finish it. And I'm a plate cleaner, especially when it comes to dessert.

Well, and that's another thing about Luke. The portions are huge, which I like, because I love having delicious leftovers. From this visit I took home leftovers from each course. I was a happy child the next day.

My second visit was some time in early October. It was another Saturday night and I was on a date. It was kind of an unexpected visit so we had to wait about half an hour, but we got drinks at the bar. I had a Champagne au Peche, which was refreshing.

Once we got seated, I resisted very hard to order the Rillettes again. Because it's that good. But I did a good job of resisting and tried the Flamenküche. This reminded me of my short time in Strasbourg. Everywhere we walked, we saw these flat pizzas with caramelized onions and bacon. Needless to say, it was delicious.

I ordered the Choucroute Garnie, because I was feeling like a carnivore, and my date got the Jagerschnitzel. It was funny when they brought out our main dishes, because the server thought the Choucroute was for him. I was like, uhm, that's me. Too funny. I guess it is a pretty masculine dish. A bunch of meat and potatoes, you know. I really enjoyed my pork shank, pork belly, and bratwurst, and took a lot of it home. The mustard they served with this dish was to die for, and our server gave me a little container of it to take home with the leftovers.

I don't think we got dessert, which is very unlike me, but the date was pressed for time and I was full anyway.

Another great time and I can't wait to go back.

Best raw oysters in NOLA! 

If you've seen any of my other NOLA reviews, I've been all over the city looking for the best oysters, and Luke's definitely tops all the others. I've been there 3 times in 16 days. They have the fantastic happy hour special, during which they have .50 cent oysters and half off beer. Can't get a better deal. And their oysters are the fattest, juiciest oysters in the city! They actually have a minneret sauce and the sharpest horseradish sauce that just goes straight to your senses and cleans your airways. Love it!

I also had the shrimp & grits once, and I had never had them before, but the dish was wonderfully balanced and delicious, unlike some of the other New Orleans restaurants that only heap on the salt and butter. Their bread pdding is a wonderful dessert as well. Again, very balanced with an even texture, with handmade ice cream piled on top.

The only reason why this place has 4 stars instead of 5, though, is that the service is not great here. Wonderful, wonderful food, but they have some of the slowest service I have had here. They have all of these staffers and hostesses and waiters walking around the restaurant, which isn't too big, but they take a long time with everything!

Went here when in NOLA on a business trip... we were lucky to get reservations for brunch and ran over! I didn't take a look at the menu since were just excited to get a John Besh restaurant spot. So i didn't realize this (and pretty much any place in NOLA) is not so vegetarian friendly! I ordered the pancakes which were delicious! My friends ordered all sorts of meat heavy things-- a burger, shrimp and grits (he said it was one of the best meals of his life, and he's a foodie), and oysters. Everyone loved their food. 
Service was solid, and we stayed and chatted for quite some time with no pressure to leave from the staff (i'm from NYC so that was huge). 
If I were a meat eater, I'd be running back to this place. As a vegetarian, not so much.

Lüke's food is outstanding!! My mom and I came here after a long night out on Bourbon to try and come back to life. The Lüke Burger, Local Crab Omelette and Bread Pudding did it for us!! Our server and the hostess were super friendly and joined in the humor of how hungover we were. It's a little pricey but you're on vacation!! Worth the splurge.

Generally love this place. Today they were a bit off. Seriously cold fries which they replaced immediately. Service a little slow.  Could be due to shift change. But on the plus side the French 75s are to die for.  Hubby loves the gumbo. Will certainly be back soon.

I'm on the fence with Luke based on very poor service yet very good food.  

We were greeted by a not so warm hostess and told we would be seated on time based on our reservation. Unfortunately, shortly after a group of 7 came in and were ushered ahead of us because they knew someone working at the restaurant.  Perfectly fine under most circumstances, but not when that ends up with us being seated a half hour after we were told.  Once seated, I was further disappointed that our server didn't know much about the food she was serving. 

Oh well... Once the food came all was forgotten and I was a happy camper once again.   We had a lot to eat, but the roasted beets salad 
and cochon de lait sandwich were standout favorites.

Went here one evening when La Parada was too crowded.  I was the only one in the place for most of my meal.  I opted for the burrito dinner (I believe they were out of a couple other dishes that I was more interested in).  Beans were anaemic and watery.  Rice was mushy and bland.  The burrito was just a straight up gristly mistake.  The menu looked interesting enough that I might have overlooked something worthwhile, but without a sure-bet going in, I don't see myself returning anytime soon.

We have visited Jerzzies a number of times. Mostly because it is local.

The real reason we come back is the food is great and the killer beer selection.

1. The sweet chilli wings are amazing. 

2. Cheese steaks are excellent.

3. Service is very good.

4. Nice tvs with all the games on.

5. The beer selection is fantastic.

4 STARS
Great drinks and brunch. Crawfish beignets were amazing. Shrimp and grits were perfectly cooked as well.

Best shrimp and grits ever!!  The French 75 drink is amazing.  I've eaten a lot of shrimp and grits around the world and this place is the tits!!  Even if you don't like grits you should still order it

Had one of my most memorable meals here on my first trip to Nola! I highly recommend this place and was very pleased with the food and service. Dined here for dinner and made a reservation through open table. We ordered the fried Brussel sprouts as our appetizer which was delicious and it had this unique sweet and sour taste. For my entree I ordered the roasted chicken with rosemary potatoes with a side of roasted jalapeño grits. Both dishes were fabulous! The chicken was very moist, tender, and tasty. Topped off the dinner with their bourbon breed pudding with vanilla bean ice cream. Definitely revisiting Luke!

I would have given this place a better rating but the custom service is lackluster.  The food is pretty good but the servers are rude. On the brighter side, at least the hostess was nice. Do not visit this establishment unless you are not particularly interested in good service.

The food is excellent.  I've been twice and both times it was really off the charts.  Had the same thing both times, oysters on the half shell and shrimp and grits.  My only beef is with the service.  The first visit the service was ok.  However, the second time I ate at the bar and it was pretty abysmal.  They didn't clean my area of the bar from the previous patron and, for all intents and purposes, refused to do so.  The bartender just put a napkin down and served me my food.  I'll still come back though, the food is just too good.

Invited back to Luke after being contacted by management regarding my previous review I was privileged to a dinner out of this world. It began with huge raw oysters that were succulent and salty needing no additional condiments. My party then had the baked oysters which were again excellent, oysters on the half shell baked with fresh shrimp and crabmeat. Then we were treated to a chef's special called Flammenkuchen. The Flammenkuchen was a German style pizza with pork belly, caramelized onions and Emmenthaler cheese, that was unbelievable. The next course was a cup of gumbo which is always a staple for me anytime I come to Luke, a dark rich roux filled with seafood and sausage. The main course was their number 1 seller the famed shrimp and grits which was the best shrimp and grits I have ever had. The sauce was rich and full of flavor probably also made with a roux with huge shrimp, soft creamy grits and cheese. For dessert we settled on the bread pudding that was served in a soufflé dish served with a great pecan reduction sauce. Ask for Tristan if your going for dinner, he provided great service all evening long. This was from start to finish the best dinner I have ever had.
Very nice atmosphere... Staff very friendly... I ordered bread pudding and my husband ordered baked oysters... Everything was awesome... Taste great!!! A must !!!

This is my first review on yelp so... I will start by saying the manager at this location did a good job when it came to the customer experience and that is where my positive review stops. I'm never going to a jiffy lube in Tucson again. I've been to 2 of them this one on 22nd and the one on kolb and tanque verde. Both times I had to get service done on my car the next day. The first time I had to get a new battery and the manager at tanque verde was rude and overly pushy with sales. This time I haven't been able to take my car in yet but my check engine light came on, so it is fair to say that it might not be connected but my air filter was also put in backwards, so that doesn't add to my confidence in their ability. Lastly one of the employees at the 22nd location has sticky fingers and took some money I had in the side door. So make sure if you go there which I won't be in the future you have everything glued down.
The shrimp and grits with andouille and poached eggs is the best breakfast I've had in ages. Pair that with the vintage brasserie decor and you've got a big winner. I will definitely go back.

So they have fresh oysters, but you can get fresh oysters and a more welcoming attitude in so many other places in New Orleans. Why allow some bartender make you feel uncomfortable when you're the spending money and trying to have a good time.

We came here for happy hour and ordered 2 dozen of the raw P&J it was so flavorful! Best raw oysters in town! Also the happy drinks were amazing!!! For a really good glass of cab is was only $5! Can't beat that! Also I believe their happy oysters were only 75 cents!!! We came back for more the next day because it was that good! This wasn't on happy hour but we ordered a dozen of their Louisiana shrimp! Yummy!!

Headline: GOOD, NOT GREAT - DECENT VALUE

OVERALL IMPRESSION
Nice atmosphere, pretty good service, and good food (but not as good as expected), and some significant red flags in food preparation.

I had high hopes after discovering that this is John Besh's restaurant and reading the reviews on Yelp.  The food was good, but not quite up-to-par with what I expected after reading the reviews.  Considering that it is in New Orleans on Super Bowl weekend, the overall value was decent.

COCKTAILS
After a long weekend of indulging in local beer, we tried their Old Fashioned.  It was well executed and smooth.  I'm a big bourbon fan, and I appreciate the balance in this cocktail.

APPETIZERS
I had the Rillette of Local Pork with savory marmalades and grilled country bread.  This was a rather large portion that may be better for sharing.  It's like a pork paté in a short, wide jar.  The pork was flavorful and served as a good base for the accompaniments, however if you don't like paté, you probably won't like this dish.  The savory marmalades were not quite what I thought they would be.  There were four items: 1) grainy mustard (which I loved), 2) a sort of pepper relish that was a a little sweet and savory (a good complement to the pork), 3) a kind of pickled diced peach (a bit too crunchy and sour for my liking), and 4) some brined/lightly pickled half slices of pickling cucumbers (I didn't care for this even though I love pickles).  The grilled bread had a nice crunch without being too crispy or dry.  I think this appetizer would go well with a malty, lightly hopped beer-perhaps the local Abita Amber.

My friend had the Seafood Gumbo and enjoyed it quite a bit.  He commented that there were nice chunks of seafood and sausage (presumably andouille).

ENTREES
I had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en cocotte" (aka Shrimp & Grits).  Our waiter said that this was the dish that they are known for and I'm a sucker for shrimp & grits, so I had to have it.  Also, other Yelp reviewers had hyped this dish quite a bit.  Although it was very good, I don't think it's the best I've ever had as some other reviewers have stated.  The shrimp were large, plump and well cooked - perhaps ever so slightly overcooked.  This may be due to the shrimp sitting in the hot grits and continuing to cook a bit.  The grits were excellent, but I thought they could be a touch smoother.  These comments may be nitpicks, but they were what made the difference in me really enjoying it vs. swooning over it.  Overall this dish was very satisfying.  The flavors were layered well and the savory, creamy combination worked well.

My friend had the Poulet Grand-Mere.  From the pictures on Yelp, this looked like a great, homey, comfort-food dish.  Perfect after a long, cool, rainy day.  It's a half herb roasted local chicken served with bacon, veggies, and whipped potatoes.  Everything looked delicious and the crispy roasted chicken skin looked great.  However the problem was with the chicken.  It seems like they may have pre-roasted the chicken and reheated it for service!  When my friend pulled the drumstick off, he noticed that the meat inside close to the bone was actually cool to the touch.  When he pointed that out to our server, the dish was whisked back to the kitchen and a new dish was prepared.  The young lady who later returned with a fresh serving apologized nicely and expressed that this is not their standard.  However, the second time around was no better than the first! THE CHICKEN WAS COOL INSIDE AGAIN!  I could not believe it and my friend decided to go ahead and eat it anyway since it was getting late, he was hungry, and I was already halfway through my dinner.  After alerting our server of the second mishap, they rightfully took this dish off our bill and did not charge us for dessert.  This was an appropriate response on their part, however it was not sufficient to give me faith that the execution of this dish will be better in the future.  I was shocked that a John Besh restaurant would have such an issue.

DESSERT
I had the Apple Gallette with ice cream.  The apples were tasty, well-cooked, and well-seasoned.  The ice cream (pecan, I think?) was very good and paired well with the Gallette.  The pastry itself was a bit disappointing.  Parts of it were the flaky pastry it ought to be, but the outer parts were chewy and tough.  Overall it did not taste that fresh and I suspect that some corners were cut with this dish.  I would not order this again or recommend it to anyone else.

My friend had the bread pudding and enjoyed it.  It came smothered with sauce and ice cream, so I don't think I would have enjoyed it (I'm a bit of a bread pudding purist).

SUMMARY
Don't order the chicken!  The cocktails we tried were great and the service was pretty good, but a little more formal than I expected for a bistro.  The portions are generous.  Good, not great, food.  I'd go back, but have to deduct a star for the chicken.

I stopped here and had the Southern Breakfast. It was simple, yet delicious. Eggs perfectly cooked. I had the sausage and biscuit options which were great. But the star of the dish was the jalapeño grits. Not spicy, just delicately flavored and added complexity. Service was slow and the bar smelled a bit fishy with fresh oysters being shucked.

I recently spent several days in NOLA and just stopped in to Luke for a quick lunch on my first day.  I kept going back, because it was so good. 

Oysters on the half shell...some of the best I've ever had. Ended up getting a second dozen. 

Gumbo...very good.  Roux could be a bit darker, but still top shelf!

Croque Madam...excellent.  High quality ham.  Toasted just right.  Delicious.  

Fries...very, very good.

Charcuterie board...excellent variety and very, very traditional, with pate', blood sausage and several other delicacies.  Probably one of the best I have ever had.

All meals served with great, crusty French bread and butter.  

I ate at the bar each time, and service was always top notch.
Ate here with coworkers way back. Great food and great staff. Hope to eat there again soon.

I've been to Luke for both happy hour and dinner. Unfortunately, they've raised the price on the oysters! At $0.75 a piece for P&J oysters, they're still a good deal, but not quite as good of a deal. Generally speaking, they're pretty big and fresh. Other happy hour specials include 50% off cocktails, wines by the glass and draft beers. Service has always been spotty here; some of the waiters are really nice, but some of them will actually roll their eyes at you when you ask questions. It's nice that you can even make reservations during happy hour times. I've also had the fried oysters and the burger, both of which are good, but nothing amazing. As with the other John Besh restaurants, it's a pleasant atmosphere. For the times I've been here, it's been a mix tourists and locals that skews more toward tourists. I recommend trying out Luke at least once, but I wouldn't classify it as one of my go-to, staple restaurants.
You have not lived until you have tried their "etouffee". It's a delicious twist on the classic dish that is out of this world. Very rich but worth every bite.

Went here for dinner and had a pretty nice meal. Started with the Brussels sprouts and gumbo, both were pretty good, the sprouts had quite a kick to them. 

For dinner I had the risotto (which the chef added the night before) and it was amazing! Would definitely recommend it! Overall a good meal, but not a must do.

First, the staff was okay. Interesting decor inside too.

We ordered some food to go since they were about to close. I got my mom a cup of gumbo, which she enjoyed. I chose their Steamed Chocolate dessert (good!) 

My sister ordered the Gateau Basque. Upon returning to our hotel, we discovered she only got the cake!! No creme fraiche or berries!! They were closed so we couldn't do anything about it. Not cool.

Edit: Thank you John for reaching out. Unfortunately, there wasn't time to go back to the restaurant. Thank you, very much appreciated!

I came here the night before I left NOLA...
Wish I knew about it earlier.
Creamy, buttery oysters, Nice staff, although they were busy and I waited a few at the bar.. no prob...
The chef / oyster shucker  ( i think he was filling in shucking) was easy on the eyes. Grew up in Sausalito..I love bay connections.
I was originally going to order the veal pate, but the bartender recommended the Pate sampler. Amazing...
head cheese, scary to most, but I love that gnarly shit...
a whipped something with a truffled fat...fois gras, rillette of something..
I cant even remember what they all were, because I was hungry and forgot after a bottle of Gruner.. Either way...
I ate most of the whole sampler ( 2 friends came and sampled it) and killed a dozen oysters.
Will be a go-to restaurant when in New Orleans,
Cheers!!
Food was good, atmosphere nice.  Easy walk from our hotel.  $$ means entree is over $20!

Wow. If you like oysters as I do, the Luke happy hour is the place to go. Great fresh oysters and half price drinks. Did I mention that the oysters are .75 ea. Doesn't get any better. Didn't have a full meal, but loved the grilled Brussel sprouts as well.

went to Lukes three times during this recent visit to New Orleans.  Happened to stay at the Hilton right there (which is very average and passable).  But I am still thinking about the Luke burger and wish they would deliver to NYC.  The burger comes with bacon, cheese, lettuce,tomato and this bbq sauce.  I had mine medium rare and I still am thinking about it a week later.  I also really enjoyed the the jumbo Louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" which I had the next day.   The oysters were served with three different sauces - and I enjoyed the horseradish one the best.   

I give Lukes five stars for the burger, the shrimp and the oysters.  My friend had the ravioli which she did not say much about.

What can I say?  Happy hour at Luke's is THE BEST!!!! Oysters at $0.75 each and 50% off selected wines and beers.  The oysters came out ice cold, plump, and sweet.  
We were in NOLA for 4 days and my wife booked Luke's for happy hour starting at 3pm to 6pm.  It's best to make reservations as this place will quickly fill and the only other option is the few seats along the bar.
We started with a half dozen raw and half dozen fried.  The raw oysters fall outweighed the sweetness and taste over the fried ones.  We then proceeded to go through another dozen, then another dozen.  
Service was attentive and Kevin came around continuously to make sure we were okay and had enough drinks and food.
Although the check arrived with the first dozen (6 raw/6 fried) at the non-happy hour price, I brought this to Kevin's attention and he quickly took care of honoring the happy hour prices.
All in all, this was the best place for getting your fix of oysters at rock bottom prices.
The bar itself is very modern and upscale, although it didn't feel stuffy or uncomfortable for someone in jeans.
I highly recommend you checking out this place.
Never had an issue. We always order online and food is fast and tasty ! Everyone is friendly that delivers to us. We love the pizza tracker. Great location all around !!!

Party of ten, seated within 10 min on a Tuesday evening. EVERYONE was happy. From my Rosemary Bourbon to my squash 'ravioli' it was sublime. My tablemates who got the traditional NO food were tickled as well.  BROCCOLI APP WAS OUT OF THIS WORLD...who says that? All 10 of us.  Go. Enjoy.
Nice and clean but oysters are ok... the fried oysters are better. Happy hour was ok... not worth for me imho

It's almost impossible to eat good food in this town without hitting at least one of John Besh's restaurants.

For our final meal of the trip, on New Year's Eve, I wanted something a little more classy but also delicious, so we decided on Luke, which was I think the second or third Besh restaurant in our four day trip.

After our meal here, it was obvious why he has so many successful restaurants in this town. This was an incredibly satisfying and enjoyable experience.

We started the excellent meal with one more shot at the Turtle Soup. As I said in previous reviews, it was decent enough, but I'll be OK if I never eat the stuff again for the rest of my life. We also got the Rillette of Local Pork ($9). They give you a very very generous amount, paired with a lot of crispy bread to smear it on. There was so much we couldn't even finish it all.

For the entrees, we got the Luke Burger ($16.50), which was awesome. Such a good burger, covered in onions, bacon and swiss cheese, it was one of the better burgers I've had recently. The house-made fries it comes with were also insanely good - nice and salty and piping hot and crispy. We also got the Poultry Gran-mere ($19), which was also delicious. The chicken was so soft and tender it was all pretty much fallen off the bone and delicious in the stew of vegetables and mashed potatoes it was sitting in.

To end the meal, even though we were stuffed, we went for two desserts to sustain us until midnight for the New Year's Eve countdown. We got the Apple Gallete ($8) and Brendan's Bread Pudding ($8). Both were delicious, but I really loved the bread pudding. This was one of my favorite versions of the many I had during the trip (probably second only to the Chocolate version at Red Fish Grill).

The service is also perfect. The waitstaff is very attentive and friendly, and you get the full white glove treatment. This is an excellent option for a satisfying meal from the Besh empire of restaurants. There is not much else on the menu that I feel the need to return for, though it definitely made me want to go and try the rest of his places the next time I am in town.

Recommended to us by the hotel staff where we were staying.
The oyster bar was a popular choice and my friend said he oysters were fresh and tasty. I'll take his word for it since I'm not a fan.
I had the roasted chicken, it was quite tasty and a very substantial serving.
The crispy Brussel sprouts were very very tasty according to everyone at he table.

The fried Brussel sprouts were delicious and a masterpiece of art. Seafood and sausage gumbo was good. Waffles werevso soft and tasty and the chicken was so juicy in the chicken and waffle entree. Great service by Matt. Great recommendation from Eddie at the Courtyard Marriott.

I don't really leave reviews on yelp ever but I had to do it for this restaurant. 
We had a party of 14 people and got a really cozy room. Food was prepared right and every dish were delicious! 
I was just visiting NOLA for a conference but I really wish to be able to visit this restaurant again. 
Great food, great service, and great ambiance. Nothing more I can ask! :)

Stopped by this cool place to check out the happy hour from 3-6pm.   Including Half price cocktails and wine by the glass.     The interior was really cool with high ceilings and pulley style ceiling fans. The oysters on the half shell were .75 each fried oysters 1.25 each.  Half shell were good but the fried oysters were so delicate and tasty cooked perfectly and tender with the perfect crunch.  Might have been the best fried oyster ever.   They served with a sauce that I didn't eat because frankly the oysters needed nothing at all.  The cocktails were different and tasty as well.  The service was absolutely outstanding and seamless.  They appeared to be working in teams everyone working to make sure your experience there was perfect.  I saw a neighbor table of 4 ordered the burgers and omg the looked delicious and they were huge!  Will definitely go back to this place on my next venture to Nola.

It is inside the Hilton on St Charles but has Valet parking or an easy uber. Lunch and brunch are all I have done and both are wonderful. The burgers are probably the best in town according to my companions, but I stick to lighter fare which they do have to choose. Seafood bar is excellent if you want oysters etc. Atmosphere is fun and service excellent. I like the front dining room.

Typical New Orleans fare. Delicious. Great service and laid back atmosphere. It is located right next to the Hilton which makes it easy for out of towners to try.  

I went here the night before a bachelorette party officially started with the bride and MOH and honestly it was the best meal of the trip. We started out with the oysters (picked by the waiter) which were fresh, clean and crisp. We tried several different types (west vs. east vs. local) and they were all delish. To accompany that we got the french fries - crispy on the outside and skinny - my favorite. To continue below these were the items we chose and the order we went with. 

Wine - Rose 
Shared EVERYTHING
First Course: Oysters & French Fries
Second Course: Crispy Brussels Sprouts & Heirloom Tomato Salad (can't go wrong with fresh tomato's and burrata)
Entree: Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en Cocotte" (creamy and fresh  typical NOLA)
Dessert: Steamed Chocolate (very heavy - MOH loved - I felt like i could take one bite) & Bourbon Vanilla Bean Crème Brûlée (not usually a fan but the top was torched to perfection) 

Thursday night. 3 girls. Shared everything. Set the trip off on the right foot. Thanks John Besh.

I usually don't write reviews and especially negative ones FYI. That said food and drinks prices are a little but on the ridiculous side. We know chef had been on TV but that shouldn't mean you gouge your guests. Crab entrees were nothing special and shrimp and grits w poached was very good so I can recommend but still tough to justify price. Especially with all the amazing shrimp and grits choices within blocks of there. 

Server was very good, hostess was wiping her runny nose on her sleeve which was not appetizing. 

If have to have a meal at one of J Besh restaurants go to August for 3 course meal at lunch instead. Enjoy and happy dining in Nola! Oh also skip acme and go to Felix's right across the street.

Luke was very delicious. I do not remember the "official" menu names but I had the grilled ham and cheese with an egg on top and the fried brussel sprouts. Soooooooooooo yummy! The atmosphere was great and Nicole was super helpful and attentive. She was also very pleasant to talk to. If not for the food, have yourself a drink and visit Nicole.
Best chargrilled oysters I tried and I tried 3 dif. Places. Not Acme. You have to ask for them. Good atmosphere.
Hot and a lot of food. Quick service too. Ask for their homemade hot mustard for no additional charge.
Amazing! The food is wonderful and the service is on par! Fiancé and I ordered Brussels sprouts, shrimp and grits and the frittata and all were noteworthy. If get them all again and again!

Love this place! John Besh needs to come to NYC! Conveniently located across from our hotel, Intercontinental, so we went there twice in 3 days. The duck po'boy dribbled delightfully between my fingers as the egg yolk mixed with the duck juice, and then I licked it all off! Then at the 2nd visit, the happy-hour oysters and the shrimp and grits really made it one of the most memorable part of our entire trip; it's up there with the Segway tour and Preservation Hall, I'd say.  You may hear different things about various shrimp and grits while in New Orleans, but we've tried it in 3 different places and Luke's was our favorite.

We always stay at the Hilton St Charles, so Luke is a must.  We actually love the bar here and it is tough to get a seat, but so worth it.  We had breakfast here before the football game, and wow!!! The grits were off the chart delicious.  Cheesey jalapeño grits cooked to absolute perfection. The bacon and sausage were pretty darn good too!

Keep your afternoons free for Luke! Happy hour here is truly a deal you do not want to miss if you are in the area. In the words of the man who prepares the oysters, "50 cents, super fresh and de-lish!" Plus, all the beers, wines, and liquors are half off. For cocktails, I would recommend the St. Charles Streetcar. 

If you like fresh oysters and cheap, but delicious, drinks, you will most likely want to go back again and again to take advantage of this deal. (Plus, you'll get to see your nice, friendly waiter again like we did!)

On the advice of a very kind gentleman we found this little cozy place.  Went for lunch and it was excellent.  Kinda tucked out of the way but worth the find.  It's a John Besh restaurant and worthy of his name for sure.

I had this awesome southern breakfast with eggs, bacon and hash browns. It was all delicious but the hash browns stole the show with little bits of bacon in there (never enough bacon!). My boyfriend got the pancakes which were good too. It's a cute spot in a hotel. I'm glad we tried it but it's not the kind of spot I'd be dying to go again.

Great eats! The food here was fantastic. Service was a bit slow but the waiters more than made up for it. They comped us a second round of drinks and even our dessert (and frankly it wasn't that slow compared to restaurants I've eaten at elsewhere and none of whom have offered much apart from apologies). After profusely apologizing for the delay even though we didn't say anything (honestly didn't even notice it was that long) we enjoyed the shrimp and grits which was great and fish. The best part of the meal was the bourbon bread pudding, incredibly delicious! Unlike other reviewers everyone we encountered was extremely friendly and accommodating, we were immediately seated even though we were 15 minutes late for our reservation, so maybe there has been some recent staff changes? Either way I will definitely be recommending this restaurant to friends!

Recommended by the concierge and appreciated by me!  My go to question is "if you were to go eat right now, where would you go? "  I got there about 2 in the afternoon and I was asked if I had a reservation,  a strong indicator that they stay busy all the time.   There was bar space, so I sat there and enjoyed a nice glass of chardonnay.  I asked the server for their recommendation and was thrilled to get it,  shrimp and grits!  Delicious!  I also had 1 oyster which was a giant.  The grits were larger than I've ever seen and three was a sweetness to them that was unexpected.  Loved it all.
Incredible breakfast and so much food! Try the crab omelette and get a side of the cheese grits. You won't be disappointed.

I tried crawfish etouffee. It was amazing. The sauce is good, the rice is crispy and there were a lot of crawfish.  The environment and service is better than most of the restaurants in New Orleans. I will have a second visit if I could.

The staff was very friendly and knowledgeable. I had the Shrimp and Grits...these were by far the greatest Shrimp and Grits I have ever eaten. I would highly recommend everyone try this place, you will not be disappointed. This was my favorite meal in NOLA, and we had some good ones, until this greatness.
One word:  divine!  Had the baked oysters ~ flavorful. Not at all slimy. Also the pate was orgasmic.  But my fav was the frisée salad ~ amazing!!

This place is so cute ! We came here for brunch and could not wait to eat here. I got the shrimp and grits while the girls got a little bit of everything. Coffee was served is white teacups/saucer :) so cute! 
The shrimp and grits came in an iron skillet the grits were buttery and delicious. The shrimp were huge and seasoned well. What really made the dish was the sauce/gravy they smother the whole shrimp and grits with. So damn good!! I wish we had enough time to come back and do the lunch/dinner menu :) Next time I'm in NOLA I'm def. Stopping by here !

We actually came here twice during our weekend in NOLA. The oyster happy hour can't be beat. The raw and fried were both delicious and we loved all the cocktails we tried. We also tried french fries and brussel sprouts.. would definitely recommend both. Brussel sprouts had a spicy sweet thing going on and the fries were house cut thin and fried to perfection. The bar was packed both days we came, but the small tables were available through the hostess.

You couldn't really tell it was happy hour as it wasn't advertised anywhere on the menu, and the place was definitely not filled with crowds and it was more of a fancier place than anything else near the french quarter.  And the hostesses were absolutely not wanting to be there that day.

But we knew why we were there.  Half off beer and 50 cent oysters.

3 girls, 4 dozen oysters, $24.
Excellent seafood jamabalya and crawfish bisque as well.
Ready ... Set ... Feast!!

This location continues to consistently amaze me! The fastest delivery I have ever experienced - and I'm on the opposite end of town! Ordered today - submission to pizza in hand: 19 minutes. That type of service, with consistent and excellent quality, is why I am a regular and happy customer. Keep up the great work!

I normally love Luke's. but I came here w a group of first timers for happy hour. We ordered 100 oysters and they were dirty++, w broken shells, poorly shucked to the point where some oysters were just decimated. We had to send back 20 bc a few of us were sick of getting broken shells in our mouths. Service was good otherwise. Maybe the day we went we got the shucker on an off day. I was disappointed and my guests were too.

This is one of the best bar/restaurants in New Orleans. The food and drinks are amazing. The stuffed P&J oysters are a must-have appetizer. These baked oysters are huge and stuffed with shrimp and blue crab. For dinner, I had the roasted chicken with crispy potatoes. The chicken was moist and the entree was the perfect size. Yes, I said "moist". My girlfriend had the shrimp and grits. As a grits connoisseur, she says these are some of the best grits in the states. I have to agree. Drinks are really good too. We had the St. Charles sour. It's a slightly spicy take on the whiskey sour. I just wish the drink was bigger. We loved Lüke so much we came back for brunch. Get the chicken and waffles!!!

Tasty food for decent value.

We arrived a bit early with a reservation, but it took the staff at least 10 minutes to figure out a place to seat us early despite there being plenty of available seats; overall, the service was much less helpful than other places we ate at during our stay in New Orleans. However, the food was quite good--we split the seafood platter to start, which included very tasty oysters and other fresh seafood jars, while we split the ricotta gnocchi with butternut squash as an appetizer, which had very nice flavor from the squash and the change in texture from the chickory crumble. My slow braised lamb and chestnut pasta entree was also tasty, while the duck duck rice my friend had quite a bit of an Asian tilt to it and was just okay. The food was overall tasty and is a good place to grab a meal.

I was really torn between 3 and 4 stars, but my boyfriend votes for 4.

I give the menu 5 stars, everything on it sounds divine.  I give the food somewhere between 3 and 4 because it was well executed, but nothing really stood out as magnificent to me (and it was a little over-heavy or oddly seasoned).  Nothing was bad either.  Solid, French/German fare witha creole flare.

And the service was at least 4 stars.  Attentive without being intrusive, lovely warm bread and good cocktails, good wine list.  All those little things that make a bistro more than your average american diner.  Those were done with panache.  

I would come back, I would eat the redfish again (if there are any left after $#@#$@$@$# BP).  Maybe not the tart.  But the pate was very nice indeed.

We ordered the Sunday special Pork Grillades with gumbo and jalapeno cheese grits, and the Roast Chicken. Both were tasty, but the pork was very fatty (more than 50%) fat and the chicken was overcooked and needed to be cut off the bone and the butter knife wasn't cutting it. Maybe it was just an off night for the great reviews. 

It was also a little pricey for a $$ rating on yelp.

I came here recently with my mom to relax before a big interview, and we had a great time! 

We started with the marinated crab claws form the bar. They were good! I really liked the sauce they came in, but I wasn't expecting them to be cold. Still good! I ordered the Shrimp and grits dish, because of course. The grits were some type of jalapeño cheese grits and very good. I liked the dish a lot overall. I just wish they took the tails off of the shrimp for you. It just makes things messy and harder to eat when you have to remove the tails. 

The service was a little lacking. I felt like the waiter always had somewhere else to be. He seemed very removed from our conversations. If they could fix this, they would be a 5 star place hands down.

It's surprisingly a good Japanese cuisine restaurant. If I had to rate it on a scale between too casual and too formal (-5 to +5) I would give it +2.5

Things I liked about this place 
1. Comfortable seats.
2. Decent interior.
3. Food is great.
4. Hygiene conscious staff and the place is pretty clean too.
5. They go an extra mile with the presentation of food.
6. Prices are moderate.
7. Smart use of space. Despite being a small place there is enough room to walk around.
8. Good music.

Things they can improve on
1.  Uniform lighting in all corners. It was pretty dim in some of the places.
2. Somewhat noisy.

We went for happy hour & thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. How could you not, with half price oysters? Both raw and roasted are available at a discount, as well as half price on most drinks. I had a perfect Bloody Mary, and my husband enjoyed a wine from their extensive list. Friendly, casual yet well appointed atmosphere.
Amazing! I can't stress enough how good this food was.. I had the Monday special (fried chicken with red beans and rice) and lobster corn chowder. By far the best I've had

More of a 3.75.
Seating is mad crowded. Happy hour prices especially for oysters and drinks are really good.
It was bout $.65 per oyster. Without happy hour still not bad at $1.25ish. Definitely anything cheaper you can find in NY or Cali lol.

I didnt get to try anything else. The fried oysters were just ok.

Get there for happy hour on time. Even if ur seated, if u dont put in the order before happy hour ends you dont get the happy hour price....and im talkin even a seconds/minute off...the waitress tried to put it in and it was too late so had to pay full price.

Outstanding dinner for Creole brasserie cuisine.  Luke is a testament to John Besh's culinary magic in NOLA. It's next to the Hilton (across the street from the Intercontinental Hotel).  If you're in the CBD for a business conference or a visitor seeking an elegantly casual dining experience, this place is well worth a visit.  Why, you might ask? 

First, the appetizers are simply delightful. You can't go wrong with a cup of seafood gumbo or the crispy brussel sprouts (which go nicely with Abita Amber beer). I was impressed the waiter brought a card with the recipe for the crispy brussel sprouts.  Second, for main dishes, I would concur with other positive reviews for shrimp and grits (Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en cocotte"). Third, the service was attentive and professional. If you are fortunate to sit in the back dining room (hidden from the main reception desk), you can watch the kitchen staff briskly performing their culinary magic. Fourth, the brasserie-like atmosphere gives a casual, elegant vibe. I also liked that several John Besh cookbooks were on display in the reception area (which is a bit cramped given the proximity of the doors). 

Although I came twice for dinner at 7pm, Luke Brasserie is open for lunch and brunch as well.    Given the layout and configuration of tables in the restaurant, smaller groups (2 to 4 people) may have an easier time with reservations during peak times. The entree prices may be higher than in the French Quarter, but well worth it for the high quality of food, cleanliness, and professional service.  Luke is a superb introduction to Creole cuisine!

Delectable food and fun vibe. A variety of fresh oysters, king crab legs and mussels greet you at the bar to visually stimulate your taste buds in preparation of the culinary delight about to be consumed. The waiter was a bit slow but our threesome was entertained by the chef and his crew who were non stop preparing attractive plates geauxing out! The bisque did not disappoint and the crawfish étouffée with popcorn rice was exquisite. I will bring Wanda K here next time!!!!

Meh. I've been to other Besh restaurants and have enjoyed the experience way way more. BOTH times that I've been to this place, I expected so much more than I got. I insisted on taking my fiance here after his NOFD Academy graduation, and to say I was embarrassed for not choosing a better spot is really an understatement. Not only was the menu minimal, it wasn't nearly what I was hoping for to celebrate such an occasion. If you're in the area and spot this place, I would honestly only go in for fries and cocktails.
They have a wonderful happy hour. Delicious  sweet oysters 75 cents each. Great atmosphere.

Walked here from the Marriott and had a fantastic dinner with my sons. If you go here ask to sit in the back and if you are lucky enough to sit back there you will be treated to a show. The kitchen is surrounded by glass and we watched the chefs prepare monumental amounts of food. It was like watching dancers maneuvering around each other creating one tasty dish after another. The Brussel sprouts could be the best I ever had and if you ask they have recipe already printed out so you can attempt to make them at home.  Steak was top shelf, chicken was moist and the pasta was cooked perfectly. 'Look over there the chef is using a torch to toast something on that desert' was a frequent comment as we chowed down. We ended the meal with some bread pudding that I would consider world case. This is a great place to eat.

Love this place! I usually stay at the Hilton attack when I am in town for work and it's super convenient and the food is pretty good. The menu is constantly changing so I never know what to expect.. other than deliciousness of course!

Oh-- and if you are in the mood to be mad-- definitely try one of their desserts! (Banana Bread Pudding, Creme Brûlée, etc)

The short list first: 
Order the Shrimp & Grits, Cochon de Lait sandwich, & or the Stuffed Shrimp. Thank you to our Yelp research Mom, hubby, and I ordered these 3 dishes to share. I'm pretty convinced these are their top dishes, so if you stray from these I can't make any promises. Oh yea, & the burger at the neighboring tables looked awesome too, but we had had too many burgers that week already. 

We went here after missing service at Green Goddess. It was late afternoon at that time where many restaurants close for dinner prep, so keep this place in mind if you get caught in the situation where you can't find good grub during the 2:30-5 hours. 

The happy hour is super. I love it b/c it's so easy to remember. All drinks are 1/2 off. How simple is that? They also offer raw oysters at a good price during that time. 

I'd go back for sure. 

Oh! Almost forgot. Our waiter was a jerk. Really. He had an awful chip on his shoulder. He should get out of the service industry. All others form Luke were very courteous and welcoming. Needless to say, we got the bad egg that day. I wouldn't let this deter a try.

My group of 5 was extremely excited to try one of John Besh's restaurants, and we'd saved it for our last night in New Orleans to close out a fun girls' weekend. Unfortunately this experience was VERY disappointing. There were so many missteps, it was almost a joke. We basically had 5 different people dealing with us throughout the night, but even five people weren't able to deliver decent service. The sommelier was apparently new and was not knowledgeable about the wine list so someone else was sent over to try to help. When we asked him to describe a certain Cabernet and a Merlot, the man said he didn't like either, as he only drank Zinfandel and Shiraz. I don't care what your personal preferences are or how long you've been at a restaurant - if you claim to be a sommelier or have knowledge of the wine list, you should be able to describe the wines on the list! One redeeming factor that came out of this was that our first bottle of wine was pretty awful, so the sommelier offered to let us a) try another one to see if we liked that and b) then offered to give it to us for the price of the first bottle (which was about $8 less). 

Our waiter was simply incompetent and totally inattentive. First of all, when he brought out bread, he only brought out 3 plates, and then sort of looked confused before going to get two more. When we went to order food (which took some time because he disappeared for a while), we had a couple questions about food preparations, and he was very terse in his responses and made himself sound very unknowledgeable about the menu. For example, I asked what shrimp "en cocotte" was and his response was "Grilled". That's it. Well I was somewhat curious, so after googling this, I discovered that "en cocotte" means cooked in one pot. This was completely different from the response I got unless the shrimp were grilled and then returned to the pot with the other ingredients, but I have no idea since I received no real answer to my question. Similarly, my friend was trying to decide between the two patés on the menu, and the waiter recommended one over the other because "it came with more things". Well this isn't really the point in ordering and being able to enjoy food so she was a bit frustrated by that. After we ordered, that was pretty much the last we saw of our waiter who was supposedly completely overwhelmed dealing with a large group in another room. The restaurant didn't seem overly busy, given that it was a Sunday night, so if he wasn't able to handle more than one table, someone else should have been assigned to ours. Our first course plates hadn't been cleared when our main courses were brought out, and the new person who brought us our mains didn't take the time to clear these plates so we sort of had to move them out of the way ourselves while he set down our new plates, and only after he had done this did he proceed to clear the first course plates. Additionally, no one ever came over to re-fill our wine glasses - not saying that we're snobby and need to have our wine poured by a waiter, but empty wine glasses would be noticed if anyone ever stopped by our table, and it's usually safe to say that this service can be expected at a restaurant of this caliber. The woman who came over to clear our entrée plates was thankfully quite friendly and offered to bring us dessert menus pretty quickly. One of my friends had ordered the "Express Menu" which came with dessert (bread pudding), and when she asked if she could choose a different dessert (since they were all the same price), the woman said that wouldn't be a problem and that we should just let our server know...and then she looked around and decided she would just take our order since our water "was a little pre-occupied" (I'm glad someone finally acknowledged this). 

Our waiter re-appeared (shocker!) to ask if there was anything else he could get us before bringing us the check, but he almost seemed annoyed by having to stop by our table. Now our group was not very demanding and we are all typically pretty easy-going so we weren't sure what his problem was, especially since he'd been by our table a total of maybe 4 times during the evening, and we received no apology from him for being absent the whole night (not that we expected anything from him at that point). I will say that the food was pretty good, but it was all unfortunately completely overshadowed by the AWFUL service we received.

My experience was disappointing, but that could very well be because I ordered the wrong dish. My friend and I both ordered the Tabasco and honey fried chicken with red beans and rice, the dish was very bland. We didn't even eat half of our food. We also ordered the crab bisque and seafood gumbo, both were delicious. 
The menu is pricey.

Such a lovely night. Loud bar environment but I really liked it. The BEST bread pudding I've ever had. My chicken was great. Actually devoured my vegetables. I don't know what Luke did to them, but they were great. I'll be back.

Hail Chipotle the savior of all fast food restaurants! Hard to believe it's still classified as fast food coz it's really healthy and since v are regulars, we practically know everyone at this joint! Ask for extras, these folks are genuinely Awesome!

My tip: Go just before they shut down for the night! They give u more food...and more is always good! :)

Great place to have lunch; the food and service is great here. I've had the Bento Box and Hibachi Lunch Specials. These options come with a lot considering the price of $12-$15 for each. I personally prefer the Hibachi Lunch over the Bento Box. Overall this place is amazing!
Shrimp and grits was delicious!  Wonderful selection of local beers.  Good times and great eats!

I'm going to start by saying the food was amazing, we started with a sazerac and bufala negra and got the ribeye and crawfish etouffee with bread pudding for dessert. Everything was fantastic.

The subpar rating is for the service. We had a late reservation on Valentine's Day but the front dining room was about half full around 9 pm. Our server came by for drink orders and about 15 minutes later we finally got our drinks, this was frustrating because I was facing the bar and could see the bartenders doing side work instead of making drinks for guests. The drinks and food came, both times they gave the items to the wrong person. I was under the impression that this was a fine dining establishment where the servers would be able to input which guest ordered what item so there was no confusion at the table. After some very minimal attention from the servers, one of them came over with the check while we were still eating dessert and said 'let's wrap this up' . 

The food was amazing but along with the large price tag I was expecting great service and instead it was just very underwhelming. I'm glad that we got to eat at a John Besh restaurant but we won't be back.

Awesome sushi/Japanese/fusion place in the suburbs! It reminds me a lot of Sampan in the city in terms of atmosphere, it's really nice and great spot for a date or family dinner. I like that their menu had a big variety and a lot of a la carte items for the hibachi portion, as well as a nice lunch special selection. Although they don't do hibachi at the table as a show, the food is just as good. I loved my scallops and veggies! The fried snap peas were amazing! I also enjoyed the brussel sprouts and everything else. The pad thai was a bit dry but still delicious. Overall, we had great service, atmosphere, food and prices. Would definitely come back again!

I shop this store whenever in Boise.  "Most" sales associates give personal assistance without rushing me along.  Great variety of goods!  It's hard for me to leave store without purchasing something!

My friend went here for the oysters. They used to be $0.50 during happy hour, but I guess that was awhile back. Now it's $0.75. They weren't really big either. But then again, if you're coming during happy hour, they won't serve the better choices since it would be gone fast. We were here mainly for oysters, but my friend did order a side of fries. They were pretty good. Nothing too too special. They were thin and warm when it came out to us. There was also the complimentary bread that came out. I am unsure why there was no plate provided with it as it just sat causally on the tabletop. Lol. 

The service was attentive. The restaurant's atmosphere was one of a dimly lit bar scene. I guess this place is good for drinks and oysters during happy hour.

Decided to try this place out for dinner on a Thursday night. We didn't have reservations and were a party of two. Only had to wait about 20 minutes before we were seated. The hostess who sat us was sweet and had a lot of energy. The food was very tasty, we ordered the shrimp and grits along with the rib eye. Definitely recommend ordering the shrimp and grits! The service overall was excellent, attentive and quick.

It's one of those places that can make a trip memorable. Came in at 1:45 and had such a great time with great food and excellent cocktails that we didn't leave till 4:30. Greg was a knowledgeable and gracious server who facilitated our party to the fullest extent. John the manager brought us a round of traditional "southern" shots and a trio of delectable desserts rounded out a truly fabulous experience. Will definitely be back!! Go here for a great time you won't regret it.

Stopped by for happy hour and met Shawn!  It's great to meet someone who enjoys their job and puts customers at ease.  The oysters were grrrrrrrreat at happy hour prices!  Now, One of my favorites in NOLA!  Thanks Andre for the referral!

Friday, 6:00 PM.

Quickie:
+ Food quality
++ Service
- Hygiene
+ Product knowledge
+ Menu variety

And then...?
Friendly staff offering good recommendations. Shrimp n' grits gets a thumbs up! 

**********
Constructive comments:
*Source ingredients
*Compost
Was the first group out on Saturday. The staff and course are perfect and keep up with the required maintenance.

We ducked into this place as the rain started to pelt down Friday night... what a happy accident!  It was the best gumbo we had in NoLa.

I had the redfish meuniere, which was delicious and not overwhelmingly fishy.  The burger was also fantastic, but the hit of the night was the jumbo shrimp "en cocette".  Heaven.

Ask to sit in Nate's section - he is almost freakishly knowledgable.  I think he must have an eidactic memory of every menu in town.  He recommended drinks, dishes and even other restaurants for the next night.

Chef John Besh keeps knocking it out of the park.  Since arriving in New Orleans 6 months ago, I've eaten at four of his restaurants and have been amazed at each one.  So, when it came time to choose a restaurant to celebrate my birthday, I chose another one of his establishments, Lüke.  Service was excellent and helpful.  Wait staff was very knowledgable of the menu.  Although I have always hated brussels sprouts, he convinced me to try the appetizer of crispy brussels sprouts with honey, toasted almonds, progress milk and barn cheese. I hate them no longer.  They were amazing.  For an entreé, I had the roast duck with crispy rice, duck confit and grilled figs. Be warned that the duck is served very rare, which I like but some may not.  My wife had pan seared drum with roasted vegetables, almonds, brown butter and lump crabmeat.  They also serve it blackened (which should be outlawed) or grilled, but the traditional pan-seared is the best.  I remain a huge fan and can't wait to try his other restaurants.

One of the best restaurants in New Orleans considering you get way more bang for your buck. The service is on point always attentive but never overly smothering. Our waiter was great his recommendations were helpful and greatly appreciated because we went with the mussels which he suggested and they were excellent. Another excellent plate was the oysters pj which were huge and very scrumptious. The bib salad with golden beets was a delight and I did not want it to end. The dessert we had was the steamed chocolate which was simple and sweet nothing over the top but very tasty and satisfying.  In conclusion the restaurant is well worth a trip to try their food and you can be the judge wether or not to go back but I will definitely be making a return on my next stay in the crescent city.

Went here alone for happy hour and ended up being at the bar with a bunch of other women who all had the same idea as me. The bartender took good care of us, highly recommended. (Didn't have full dinner here)

for starters, i was annoyed by our 10pm RSVP.  it was my fault; it was a friday night during jazz fest, and i called that day.  when we got there, i was even more annoyed by the hostess who asked me my name about 3-4 times and rarely made eye contact.

once seated, things got better. the vibe is pretty cool.  i liked the lay-out and style of the restaurant.  we were seated in the back part of the restaurant, which had an amazing view of the kitchen; they were working hard back there!

we started the evening with the roasted beets salad; it was good.  i especially appreciated the pistachios.  my wife ordered the "express menu" for friday, which included the soup (crawfish bisque), entree (the redfish "court-bouillon" with crab, shrimp, oysters, and rice), and dessert (bread pudding).  she loved it, but i thought the entree was a tad too smoky for my taste.  i had read in other reviews that the burger was good, so i tried it.  it basically melts in your mouth, and the fries are incredible; however, the bacon was a bit much.  i kind of liked how they served the burger on a wooden cutting board, but i did not like how the fries came with mini-bottles of ketchup, mayo, and mustard.  it seemed kind of wasteful.  dessert was good, but i wish they offered a variety of choices.

when we return to NOLA, we will definitely go to LUKE again to try other items on the menu!

Awesome happy hour - 50 cent oysters (that are huge!) and half off beer and cocktails! We also tried the chicken and rabbit pâté and the bread pudding, both of which were delicious! This was our first meal in NOLA and were so happy it was!
Fantastic food - a great place for a date and for friends!  Best seafood I've had in awhile.
Amazing raw oysters, and the fried oysters were delicious. Fresh oysters are on the menu at Luke, and the house drinks are also very delicious.

Today's lunch was the reason I started yelping! I went on Thursday because I like veal and a yelper said that would be the special. My lunch cost $20.00, including tax and ice tea. The bread was hot and fresh and they must put something in the butter because it was real good. The crawfish bisque came highly recommended and it was a good idea. A little seafoody, if you know what I mean, but since it was seafood I guess that was right. The veal was unbelievable! It fell apart and was just fatty enough to make it perfect. It came on a bed of home made pasta that was great and with roasted green beans and small carrots. The lunch special (entree and soup) was $15 and I think the dinner special was $21 for entree, soup, and desert. Check their website (link in another yelp review) for daily specials. Such a great meal that I'm planning on bringing my wife to NOLA in the near future for a few days and this meal made me decide to do it soon. Setting was great, atmosphere was superb, service was exceptional, food was five star - without a doubt. I've given a few 5 stars for atmosphere and unique food - but this is a REAL five star restaurant with a three star price. From Canal, it's one block from Bourbon and about two blocks off Canal. Lunch portion was huge - I can't even imagine the dinner portions. I'm coming back every time I come to NOLA!

Love this place!  Its a little small but I like take out better anyways.  The food is updated often and its helpful on twitter to know when your favorite dishes are available.  I will definitely be back!

Food was OK but very bad experience (the waitress dropped the source on me and my food). They did apologize but did nothing about my food. I tried to be nice though coz something like that happens. However, even I said nothing, what they responded was disappointing. Won't come back:-(

An interesting experience to say the least.  What rating do you give when the food is fabulous and the service is horrible?  

We had a reservation, and yet they couldn't sit the six of us.  We were left standing in the middle of the restaurant amongst many empty tables.  There was nothing the manager could do, he said.  When we asked to put three small tables together (along the wall), we were told it was "against the rules"!  They expected us to split up with two at one table and four at another!  How absolutely ridiculous.  Finally, a lovely woman (Deedee?) found us a table and we sat TOGETHER.

Four of us ordered cocktails, and two of us ordered wine.  The cocktails came fairly promptly, but we waited and waited for the wine.  Finally, I asked the waiter if they were out stomping the grapes, and he replied that they had run out of wine glasses!  Huh?

The duck duck rice was wonderful as was the shrimp dish, but only three of us stayed to eat.  The noise was UNBELIEVABLE, and the rest of our party ate somewhere else.

Much as I loved the food, I won't be coming back to Luke.  The noise, the ridiculous rules, the loss of our reservation, and the terrible service will keep me away.  Such a shame.

I'm giving it four stars as an average.  The boudin noir and fried chicken were 5 star worthy, but the waffles were a solid 2. 

Our group stopped here for a mid-day snack after having stuffed ourselves at Brennan's late that morning.  We wanted to check out some offerings from the brunch menu as well as the house-brewed beer, and we were not disappointed.

We started with the boudin noir.  While the boudin was tasty and tender in its own right, the apple/potato/onion saute was the star.  We kept going back to it while we sampled other offerings.

My husband claims the french fries are some of the best he's ever had.  I am not a fan of fresh-cut fries (never crispy enough for my taste), but they were certainly good.

For the entree, we split the fried chicken and waffles.  The waffles were my main disappointment.  I prefer a darker, crisper waffle, and these were light and chewy.  On the other hand, the fried chicken had a delightfully crisp yet light coating that helped me ignore the waffle.  Delicious!

The house amber beer had great flavor as well - nice coffeelike finish.

We came on a Friday night without a reservation, but we were still promptly seated. Our waitress was sweet and super helpful. 

Their raw oysters are very good and are just $0.75 during happy hour-- we caught the tail end of it because we arrived at 5:45p. All three dozen were clean, fresh, and super tasty. We also tried their other raw oysters and all were perfect. Unlike what you'd see at other raw oyster places (i.e. across the street at Trenasse), the oysters were actually CLEAN on the outside and NOT covered with mud and grime on the shell.
