The rabbit and chicken liver pate was served with crispy croutons and was actually really delightful. 

The crispy brussels sprouts were wonderful. Not quite as good as the brussels sprouts from Uchiko in Austin, but still my second favorite preparation ever. 

The one negative was the mojito my wife ordered which was 90% sugar. 

Would love to go here again. I only wish they had fried oysters as well.

After a few meals in NOLA, I was honestly over the rich cuisine.  My gf did a sh*tload of planning and Luke was our final dinner before we left.  A few of us (including myself) was craving Asian food HARD so we actually considered canceling our reservation.  Well. I'm so glad we didn't because it was my favorite dining experience on the entire trip.  

Our waitress, Savannah, was nothing short of amazing!  She def heightened the entire dining experience. She accommodated us when we told her that we disliked our vodka cocktails, she brought over a dish that we considered ordering and didn't, and ironically, it trumped the actual dish we ordered, and she made the sharing plates easier within our larger group by already halving our plates for the purposes of sharing. 

Highlights of our meal: 
-the charcuterie plate that had the pate 
-French 75 drink
-desserts
-Savannah, Savannah, Savannah....

This is our 2nd time in new Orleans but our 1st time at Lukes. My wife and I are celebrating our honeymoon! We got a referral to go to Lukes, so we checked them out. Our 1st waiter Kevin was not present after his 1st greeting! We almost left because we didnt initially see what we came there for. After he passed by us more then a few times we were greeted by JULIAN! He made sure to get what we were looking for. He is our new favorite waiter! He showed up and made things happen, with a great personality! My wife wanted her favorite a croque monsieur sandwhich. It turned out to be a lunch item and we showed up at dinner time but Julian made it happen. This turned out to be the BEST we ever had! We also had corn fitters for our appetizer, and I had the shrimp and grits, which were very tasty and flavorful.  He also gave us complimentary champagne and a complimentary bread pudding dessert for us dinning here for our honeymoon. We were very impressed with Julian and this restaurant! 5 stars!!!!

The food was, by and large, rock, solid, but there were a couple of issues, which is why I'm only giving two stars. 

Our server was pretty slow on getting out to us on the drink orders. This would normally not be the end of the world, but given the "turn them and burn them" way of getting people in and out of this place, please let me at least try one of your specialty cocktails. 

Once we got them, the drinks were good, though the Riverbend lacked promised notes of basil. My strawberry something-or-other was tasty. The app was some kind of tart with onions and pork, and it was nice, with a lot of smoke in the pork. Several chunks were pure fat, they got left on the plate. Need a little meat with that fat and smoke.

Entreewise, the shrimp and grits was amazing. The two stars comes in right here: I had a special, which was drum, delicious, part of the dish was a fried squash blossom stuffed with crawfish. Nothing wrong with it except the fry oil was clearly too cold and the thing was greasy as all get-out. When our server checked with us (his assistant tossed our entrees at us so fast that there was NO CHANCE of getting a drink to have with dinner, despite empty glasses) I told him about the squash blossom issue, pointing to the offending item on my bread plate. He was somewhat apologetic, but offered no remedy. He followed up with us on our meal, saying, "except for the squash blossom, how was everything else?" Seriously? Strike two!

I know the server can't be blamed for the mistakes of the kitchen, but he can make it right, once the wrong is corrected. 

Besides pointing out the greasy squash blossom, could I have done anything differently? All I wanted was a refire of the greasy component. I really expected more from one of the properties of one of the country's top chefs.

EDITED TO ADD: 
Brian Katz, the manager, got back to me immediately and has been very proactive in making this right.
I was excited that a sushi place was coming to the neighborhood. The food is really good although a bit pricey. If you are looking to do takeout I suggest calling ahead because they are very slow.

$0.75 oysters during happy hour + delicious cocktails, what more could you want? Oysters are so fresh, big, juicy&plump. Service was great and atmosphere of restaurant is nice/upscale, but laid back. Would definitely come back!

Walking into this spot in a strip mall, I was not expecting the very trendy decor, and more importantly I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the sushi and sashimi here. I felt this place was much better than the sushi places in center city and rivals some of the high end sushi I've had in nyc but at a fraction of the price. We will definitely be coming back

Luke was wonderful. I absolutely enjoyed my dinner. I couldn't decide between getting the Foie Gras and Boudin noir. So I got both and glad I did. I could never pass on the foie, very creamy and the saltiness was just perfect. As for the boudin noir it was cooked perfectly along with the side of sautéed apples and onions. Yum!
For main course I chose the rib eye, again just perfect. I finished my dinner with the steamed chocolate and salted caramel ice cream. It was great. I would definitely go back because I can't get the meal out of my head.

This restaurant is awesome!  We weren't really sure where to go and found this place via Yelp!  We had the best dinner, and service, we went back on our second night in town.   Kevin and Camella were our servers and they really were the icing on the cake as far as our experience.   The food was great.  We had a bunch of appetizers, including the 50 cent oyster for happy hour and the rest of our choices were amazing!   When back in NO we will be sure to go back to this place!

Make reservations! We stopped by when half of the restaurant was being remodeled and could not just walk-in.  We made reservations for the next day and came back. The waiters were very friendly and attentive. They had two servers  for each table. One waiter recommended the crab bisque. I didn't think it was that flavorful, so he took care of that for me. The shrimp and grits was delicious. Creamy and seasoned very well (slightly spicy). The bread pudding was amazing! Lots of caramel, ice cream and bread was soft and delicious. I would highly recommend.

Came here for a quick lunch while spending a weekend in New Orleans. It was Thursday afternoon and quite busy but we were able to get seated quickly and the service was great. We ordered the etouffee & shrimp "en cocotte". Both were outstanding. Will be coming back for brunch or dinner next time I visit.

This place was just a nice place to eat.  Went on a Sunday, but pretty early, 6 pm.  Had the matzo ball soup, and it was the best I have ever had.  If you plan to have another dish, just get the cup.  After that, I went for the burger. (I am allergic to shellfish.)  The bacon was wonderfully smoked, the grilled onions were awesome.  Great place for seafood lovers who also need to satisfy someone who can't go there.

I gotta say... I LOVED LOVED LOVED LUKE!!!!! 

We were in New Orleans for my 30th birthday in early July and decided to dine at Luke on the Friday of our arrival. Everything from top to bottom was great. Besides the good food and excellent service, what I really liked about the place is it's casual, pub-like feel.

Our waiter, Chris, was fantastic!!! If you ever make your way into Luke, I recommend that you call ahead and ask to be seated in his section. We specifically told him that we were hesitant to order our entrees together with our appetizers because we were in no particular hurry. He promised us that he would take the order but not put it in until we gave him the go ahead, and that's exactly what he did.  He was very attentive but very laid back at the same time, which suited us well that evening.

I definitely recommend that you try the fried oyster salad and the rabbit and duck pate - both were savory and delicious!!

Get the pizza special on Friday night.  Ask for it well done and pick up a fancy 6 pack.  You don't like fancy, they have plenty of "normal" beer too.  If you stay Jager is always cold and the Superfries are great.  This is a regular Joes bar with a nice food menu and some great beers.  You can do a shot and a beer too and no one will bat any eye.  Great stop.

I went to New Orleans with my sister looking to enjoy some authentic southern cooking.  I found it at Luke. We ordered all the recommended dishes.  The wait staff was incredibly friendly and helpful.  

We started with the STUFFED P&J OYSTERS. I don't normally enjoy oysters, but these were delicious. Crispy and buttery goodness.  I had the gumbo next. My experience thus far had been that the gumbo in various other locations were generally over-seasoned and salty. But the SEAFOOD GUMBO Á LA CREOLE at Luke was perfectly balanced. Before I knew it I was scraping the bottom of the bowl with a hunk of the warm, crispy French baguette they had served alongside. 

For our entree we had the SHRIMP AND GRITS. The shrimp were enormous and perfectly cooked, cradled in the smoothest, cheesiest grits I've ever had. Just the right balance of spices and herbs, each mouthful was heaven. Even though we were completely full after the gumbo, there was not of speck of the shrimp and grits left at the end of the meal.

I'm a live and die Los Angeles girl, and it's rare that I crave anything in another city this intensely. But as I'm describing my epic meal, I'm wishing I was back in New Orleans.
the jumbo Louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" does not disappoint. it's hearty and delicious with lots of flavor. everyone should order this! don't forget to add a lump of crab meat on top.
Excellent! I was blown away by the Brussels sprouts appetizer. I was even able to get the recipe!!! So good!!

Dined at Luke on a busy Saturday evening and was so very impressed with the service (ask for Anthony) and cuisine.  My ribeye was cooked perfectly, the fois gras stunningly delicious, and the overall ambiance way cool.  Loved it!

The service and hospitality at Luke is amazing! Our server Kenny was friendly and knowledgeable about the food and drinks. He went above and beyond to make our experience at Luke a pleasant dinner. I had the shrimp and crab étouffée it was delicious. We went back for happy hour the next day and the service was the same. Service, food and drinks are consistent all around! If you visit New Orleans stop at Luke and if you live in NOLA make sure to stop at Luke.

This is a bit of a hidden gem in Chalfont. It's a Japanese place one would find in a city, but seemingly transplanted in suburbia next to a Giant, a Cheeburger Cheeburger, and a pet store. Fine by me.

Very modern and beautiful interiors. Nice elements throughout. BYOB!! And liquor store nearby.

Dishes at points were over-engineered with too many sauces, often over-competing with the flavors of the nice ingredients. It's like the chef wanted to maximize techniques and sauces and ingredients and...kabam!!! That's how a dish is born. 

Enjoyed several dishes including the tuna sampler, duck rolls, warm mushroom salad, scallop ceviche, hibachi and sushi rolls.

I was impressed by all of the dishes, but especially enjoyed the raw tuna sampler, the mushrooms and the hibachi. The sushi was also very nice.

The raw tuna sampler was presented beautifully and was a joy to experience. If you were ever curious of the differences between fatty to extra fatty tuna cuts, try this.

The mushrooms are all less common types; enoki and trumpet for example and were fun to devour.

The hibachi was very impressive. I'm not sure how, but the rice, was excellent. Very flavourful, and this is coming from someone who steers clear of rice heavy dishes. The steak on top was garlicky so beware if that's not your thing, like it isn't mine.

Sushi rice was good. We ordered one of the fancy rolls with several types of fish and tobiko on top. I would even consider this roll again.

The service was close to being very poor from our waitress as she seemed more concerned with conversation with closed out tables, but the host was able to catch the drift, intervene and save our experience.

For all those who watch Food Network, we all know that John Besh should have been the next Iron Chef...

Thank you John Besh!  If not for Luke, I would have left New Orleans extremely disappointed.  Luke (sorry, no umlaut hot key) was simply great.  We ate there twice and left both times wowed by the food.  The boudin noir was awesome, pommes frites perfectly prepared, and the Luke Burger magnificent.  I could go on, but I will not bore you with the details of just how good our meals were.

However...

For all you yelpers that like an awesome hamburger, then you must try Luke's.  I was amazed and know for a fact that you will be as well.  Besh has hit the right combination with his use of Emmenthaler, bacon, and caramelized onions.  This hamburger is so good that the use of mustard, ketchup, or mayonnaise seems sacrilegious.  Funny, but the best thing you can eat in New Orleans is not gumbo, etc., but the burger at Luke's...

THE. BEST. SUHI. PLACE. EVER. 

Their rolls are so flavorful, so unique, so enormous, and so... perfect. We've been going to HACHI for the last 4 years and no other place compares. No matter which roll I've ordered, they've never been even slightly disappointing. They really put so much effort into their presentation, too. 

Some of my favorites are their oysters with jalapeños, the sticky ribs (omg), but a true must-have is their Kani Salad. I can't talk about it without craving it instantly. It's a very large portion, with a big helping of crab, and the perfect amount of crunch and heat! 

My kids are the pickiest eaters but they'll easily down their chicken wasabi fried rice in two seconds bc it's THAT good. Another staple is their chicken pad tai. They nailed it, of course!

Alright, I have to go order some HACHI. I'm drooling. I'll be right back...

This place is awesome. They accommodated two of our friends who came in late. There fried ouster salad is a must try. The oysters we're crunchy and there were huge pieces of bacon in it. Yum yum yum! They recommended jumbo shrimp and grits which was served in a cast iron skillet. I shared both orders with my husband and they split the orders in separate plates. We totally devoured both items. Highly recommended

4 stars for the food:  Loved the: raw oysters and escargot,  shrimp étouffée, grits shrimp, and gumbo.
2 stars for the ambience: Felt like a meat locker in there.  Waiter tells me it's the hotel.  I literally had to get up and leave because it was so cold.

My family and I ate at this historic New Orleans venue this weekend.  To say it was fantastic was an understatement.  We started with a dozen P&J's and a bottle of Chablis which were both excellent.  We then had the brussel sprouts that had a hidden hot sauce mixed throughout that was like something I have never had.  They were also delicious. Our party had the Shrimp and Grits, the Ahi Tuna with lump crabmeat, the duck, the lamb, and a steak. Basically, we tried everything on the me menu and it was all spectacular.  The only thing that was not up to our liking was the lobster bisque. It was much to thick and had heavy tones of cinnamon and nutmeg.  It tasted more like a pureed pumpkin pie to me.  Be that as it may, I still give this place a 5 star review and will definitely recommend it for friends.

Love love love this place! It's definitely the best sushi in the area, hands down. They have great service and wonderful menu choices. Prices are about average for the area, not overpriced. They seem to take pride in the quality of their food, which is very nice to see. This is my go to place when I want good quality sushi or Japanese food in general.

Have been here twice recently due to traveling in the area. This place is a must hit. Favorite so far was the Monday special, Tabasco Fried Chicken with Red Beans/Rice. It is the best. Have also tried the Grilled Dorado and it's damn good. Wifey had the Ribeye and I have to admit, one of the best I ever tried. This place is worth the trip and would recommend.

Really 3.66 stars but ok 4ish.  50 cent oysters were the bomb, paid $4 in SF for ones almost as good.  Shrimp with grits was slightly better than the cochon au lait both great if not a bit too salty. Overall good place!

Great Food very rich and tasty - good athmoaphere
Had the clam soup which was delicious but a bit pricey 
Oysters perfect

The food here was awesome. There was no wait to be seated and everything smelled delicious.  It had a nice vibe going on here.

The menu was a little confusing at first because we had no idea what was what, but the waiter was very patient with us and everything we ordered turned out so good!  I got one of the dishes with chicken and it had so much flavor.  I also recommend getting a flatbread appetizer, it was amazing!
We've never eaten dinner here...only lunch, but it has always been great. Perfect oysters (for $.25/each sometimes) and the blue crab BLT are not to be missed.

Good happy hour with half price drinks. the creamy orange sauce for the fried oysters was really good. The French 75 (cognac, fresh lemon juice & champagne) was probably my favorite drink while in New Orleans. nice place with friendly staff. if I lived here I would be here all the time.

The Hors d'oeuvres are on the larger side, and phenomenally delicious!! I had the Flammenkuchen and my husband had the Brussels sprouts, and we were quite full; But not too full to avoid dessert, that was just as fabulous!  Great service, Melanie was a delight. Highly recommend this place!!

I wanted to like this place more. It may have been a problem of my expectations. I thought that Luke was Cajun but a lot of the dishes were French.

I enjoyed the beet salad a lot more than my shrimp and grits. They were ok. The shrimp and grits at Dante's Kitchen are way better. My friend did not like her fish dish. After reading the rave reviews, I was disappointed.

The service was a little off. It seemed like our waiter was trying to upsell us and the prices were steep for what you actually got.

The food was great! The ambiance isn't as warm as other places that we'd tried in New Orleans, and the staff weren't what I would refer to as exuberant with the spirit of New Orleans.

We tried the fried chicken on a biscuit and the crawfish omelet. They were tasty. The chef understands how to mix the tapestry of taste into a memorable sonata. 

The ingredients were all fresh ; the music not to die for and the staff and the ambiance need to speak a bit more in what is the spirit of New Orleans.

Veronica was Fabulously Helpful!!!! my Barbacoa Beef with Black Beans & Fajita Greeen Bell Peppers & Red Onion with a little rice was To DIE For!!! the Guacamole FRESH & my beer COLD !!!!! the OutDoor seating a little windy but with some shake your just massaged  hips Music, we had the best time, we were all Full & took some home

The food is great!!!!  Only reason for the 4 stars!  Deal with the room service through the hotel and its a joke.  It's terrible to give a bad review of the food so I can't do that!  It was great, but when we called back down for a few things missing the girl on the phone was extremely rude.  I'm sorry we did not ask for silverware or bread with our dinner.  The place is great just wish I could rate the room service a zero!

Despite the reviews, I was still skeptical of Luke since it's inside the Hilton.  I spend 1/2 my life in Hilton hotels and rarely find a good restaurant.  Luke is certainly the exception!

Surely I may have been biased since my boyfriend proposed right before dinner, so clearly I could have been served canned cat food and would have thought it was the most amazing thing ever.  I kid.

I started with the escargots - very good!  Cheesy and rich and delicious, not even slightly chewy.  Perfect.

For my entree I had the etouffee, which was unlike any etouffee I've ever had.  Served over pasta (which I don't normally eat), a small portion - nothing crazy huge like you'd get at an Americanized Italian restaurant - and so, so flavorful.

The new fiance had the ribeye and it was perfectly cooked and also delicious.

Our server was fantastic and when she noticed that I spent 89% of the evening staring at my new ring she congratulated us and brought us each a glass of champagne.  Perfect finish to a wonderful meal!

Thanks, Luke, for making our special day even more special with delicious food and wonderful service.

Great food, great service, great drinks.  
Will return next time I am in town. 

The Crab Maison salad is to die for!

Shrimp and Grits.  Patè, Court Bouillon and Mussels.

Pesce and vegetarian friendly

That is All. Great Service. Good daily specials. Great happy hour. Seems like a good staff to go with it.

Easy 5 star, but I was only there for happy hour. These oysters are divine, both raw and fried (that malt vinegar aioli!!). They're fat, juicy, but not too briney. Amazing value for HH, comfortable upscale casual atmosphere, and the service was attentive. I hope I can make it back before I leave town!
Best matzo ball and chicken soup then amazing local fish meunière. Why don't I live here? I'd be in every week.

Oh. My. Word. We loved this restaurant! Service was fabulous and they rushed our order since we were going to see U2. I got the shrimp n grits and just wished I'd been able to eat every bite. Soooo good! Bf got a dozen oysters-super fresh!  A friend got the burger and it looked amazing, and he said it was great. Would definitely come back here!!
Shrimp and grits are awesome.  Desserts are excellent.  Fun,  casual place.  Will definitely go back for happy hour.

Fantastic Hawaiian pizza and wings...umm..wait a minute. That's what I ended up eating at Gio's Pizza in Maple Glen.

I could not get noticed/served at Hachi.

Had a 7:30 sushi bar reservation. Got there 5 minutes early. Was seated right in front of the head chef.

Laid out my martini shaker, glass, sake bottle. And, then...waited.

After sitting for 15 minutes (timed), I was able to hail the hostess. She was confused but ultimately brought me ice and and bucket.

The whole while, wait staff was buzzing around me, serving the couple next to me 3 separate times.

At the 35 minute mark, the head chef finally had words with a waiter, and the waiter then asked me if I cared to order anything or if someone/anyone had taken my order.

I calmly said I had been ignored for 35 (timed) minutes, why pay attention to me now?

The head chef made a feeble attempt at explaining the situation by pointing at the numerous orders he had completed...for others.

Realizing his bad form, he quickly became quite.

I left saddened at not trying the fare. Que lastima.

Typically not one for brunch, I decided to go for it while in New Orleans and was glad I did. For this one, I did it New Orleans style....beginning with a cup of seafood gumbo, which had a deep, dark, thick roux that had just the right amount of kick. It was full of fresh tasting seafood including two plump oysters, shrimp, and a chunk of fish. What a perfect beginning for my Southern Breakfast to come....two eggs over easy, with Allan Benton bacon cooked crispy, two links of sausage, a biscuit, and creamy grits with specks of jalapeño peppers. I topped it off with deep, dark-roasted coffee. Outstanding! Service was good, but maybe could be a little more attentive. Would highly recommend - if I were in town for another day or two I would definitely go back for another meal!

This place doesn't even deserve a star. We called ahead of time to try to give a heads up that we had a large party of 17. Instead of listening to me, they gave us a number to call to speak to a caterer. I called the number, no answer, the person stated she was on limited hours on her voicemail...ok. So we show up for lunch and immediately are received by a severely ungracious hostess who looked angry we bothered to come by. It was 1 pm on a Thursday and the place was almost empty, however they acted like they couldn't accommodate us--we didn't even ask to all sit together. The hostess grabbed I guess who was supposedly the manager and he proceeded to act like we never should've showed up. Finally once they realized we weren't going anywhere they sat us. The waiter came over and had zero personality. He treated us like we were a burden. My friend ordered a dirty martini which came back literally just vodka, no olives, no vermouth. The drink was $15 and when my friend asked for olives she was ignored. Then the waiter told us he couldn't split our checks. I've never heard of that. The way he said it made it feel like he was chastising us for having a larger group who ordered separately. At this point we hadn't ordered food, so we decided to just leave--they wanted us to anyway! I've never felt so unwelcome before in a restaurant. They clearly didn't want our business. I'm not sure why this place is in business as they have zero hospitality. I would not eat here! Take your business to some place that will appreciate it. We walked down the street to the acme oyster house and had a blast!

I don't want to sound like a broken record, but damn, you can not MISS EATING HERE if you are in New Orleans. We went back for dinner 2 days after our first time there. First time 4 of us, second time we took the rest of the family...so there were 8 of us!! We couldn't get enough!!  We had Tristan & Elliott as our awesome servers! We have made Tristan family!! Food choices are amazing & never a disappointment!!  (also, all the staff is wonderful..So pleasant & helpful & it is Genuine!! Thanks also to Hostess Belin!)

I visit New Orleans often and had been trying to get into Lükes a few different times but they were always so busy. This time I lucked up and was seated right away. I was glad I came back the third time.

The food is phenomenal, the atmosphere has an air of sophistication without being stuffy and the service is top notch. My waiter even made sure the kitchen charbroiled my oysters despite it not being on the menu. I was quite literally never told no. I can't wait to make this a stable of my trip every time I come.
Plump and juicy $.50 oysters during 3-6PM happy hour!! Parking was also across the street as well, reason for 4 stars because service wasn't very great.

We've eaten there many times, and have never had a bad dining experience. From small intimate dinners to large groups, they have accommodated us. Happy hour is awesome with drink and raw oyster specials.

First night in NO and ways looking forward to a Besh restaurant...upon arrival the host/manager had trouble finding our reservation and searched for some time with no explanation or eye contact as to what seemed like a 10 minute wait, while talking to the hostess?  Once they figured it out and seated us, we placed our drink order and appetizer of a dozen oysters...they were just ok, very small oysters, nothing like Acme.  We had to ask for bread and butter...once the bread arrived, it was fantastic! 

We then placed our entree order of black drum with crab meat and shrimp and grits.  We also ordered the gumbo to share for an appetizer, unfortunately they brought it at the same time as entrees (they apologized and removed from the bill) My drum was fried/sautéed and was very soggy, crab was sparse for a $13 dollar addon, taste was just ok and I was disappointed.  My wife swears that although her shrimp and grits were drenched in butter, it was the best she had ever had! She would go back just for that dish.

As we were celebrating my birthday they brought us a comp steamed chocolate with salted caramel ice cream...it was great!!

Service was very good, not sure I would return...we may give it another try next visit.
I'd like to give this place 2 1/2 stars. The food is decent (I like the TBM), but it's usually crowded and it's TOO expensive. I feel fooled whenever I end up there. Unfortunately, that's a lot.

Brunch was very nice. Our server was attentive. But the meal started off rocky when we waited forever for our soup & and it ended up coming out with the meal. The portion size of my shrimp and grits was a bit smaller than I expected for the price, but it did not lack in taste. I was very excited to try the bread pudding because of yelp reviews & pictures, but it was a tad underwhelming. It was very dense. The crawfish bisque was yummy and mimosas were on the house! It was an experience I can check off my list, but I can't say I would return.

Not my best New Orleans dinner experience.  Service was slow on a Tuesday night when they were no where near full.

The bread they bring to each table is meh.  Opening corn and crab chowder was very good.  I ordered the Tuesday special, a trio of pork.  I expected the pork belly to be fatty, it always is, but the slices of pork were mostly fat, and the fried pork neck was bland.  Overall, the dish had about 7-8 bites of pork meat. I was still hungry.

The fries were good.

PS. I forgot when I first wrote this. My dinner came with bread pudding for desert. Best. Ever.  Crusty on top with lots pecans, soft and delicious in the center.

i won't be beating down the door to go back.

Luke was overall pretty good. I would say 3.5 stars. The crawfish bisque was good, it had a good flavor, lots of crawfish, and smooth consistency, but I've had better. The blue crab and shrimp étouffée was very good, but very small, like really small, portion for an entree. The shrimp and grits was also very good, but small. There could have been more grits and it would have been more satisfying. The bread pudding was the best I've had at a restaurant. The sauce was great and it came with vanilla bean ice cream on top! Best part of the meal! If the portions were bigger, I would def give Luke 4-4.5 stars!

If your looking for some good Cajun food, look no further. We started with the stuffed Oysters and crispy brussel sprouts for our appetisers. (so good) For my entree, I ordered the jumbo shrimp on jalapeno cheddar grits and it was absolutely to die for. We finished with a cream brulee and the bread pudding. Both were excellent.

I went to Hachi with a friend because I had a Groupon. The atmosphere was really nice inside, even though it's a little small. The food was amazing. I had the Rainbow roll which I love. The presentation was really good too. I hope to go back to Hachi soon.

The silver lining here was the accessibility and extremely quick service...I always like to start with something positive.

My girlfriend ordered the soft shell crab BLT...except its apparently not a sandwich. Only one piece of toast on the bottom. It was exceptionally difficult to eat. The soft shell crab was supposed to be fried...I don't usually like a lot of breading but this had hardly any. The bacon marmalade was tasty but very salty. Served with a bland dish of seemingly boiled veggies.

I had the crawfish etouffee on "crispy rice." The "crispy rice" was odd, the best thought I could come up with as to why "crispy rice" was to liven up an otherwise very basic and almost bland dish. I was starving but couldn't muster the interest to keep eating. I took it to go because I thought that maybe I could get a homeless person to take a liking to it...the one I found seemed to have a similar reaction as me and didn't seem to eat more than a few bites.

All that being said, it wasn't the worst cajun I've ever had, but with all the hype I was highly disappointed. This was more like a cajun meal I'd expect to eat if I had ordered it in Minnesota or something, not NoLa.

Went to lunch here last week. The French onion soup was awesome. The kale salad was awesome. My smoothie was awesome and the cheese Danish I got was also (you guessed it) awesome. I was very pleased with this place. My mom and I both were totally full and happy for less than 30 dollars. The staff was really nice and helpful. I will definitely be returning!

Babyyyyyyyyyy! Their shrimp and grits is EVERYTHING. I don't eat pork so they were able to accommodate my dietary needs. Unfortunately the first plate that was present s to me had sausage. I pointed it out to the server and he apologized. My next batch was great! The grits were well seasoned and I had plenty of shrimp. This restaurant is owned by Chef John Nesh so I expected nothing less than the best. Also try the Bloody Mary's! My BFF had the crab omelet with a side of grits! Heaven!!! I swear I heard angels singing as I took a bit of hers. And when the vinaigrette touched the perfectly made omelet, they made a beautiful melody that made my heart smile.

Very nice ambiance. This is another John Besh creation as well. This restaurant is located inside the Hilton on St. Charles across from the Intercontinental. My favorite hotel to stay at in NOLA BTW. The Honey Tobasco fried chicken dish is simply delicious! The only downside is that I believe it is only served on Monday's. Nonetheless, there are several great selections on the menu for signature drinks and awesome food. Don't cheat yourself; treat yourself when in NOLA!

Pros: The etouffee was great but the grits were amazing
           Seafood is fresh- try the oysters during happy hour.
           casual comfortable atmosphere
           Friendly servers


Cons: Crowded during peak hours
            Servers disappear for long stretches

Somehow we were able to get a late night reservation here at 9:45 pm.  We came earlier in hopes to sit at the bar, but there was no room so we went across the street to another bar.  Later, we find out there is another bar in the back!  Oh well - next time. 

But anyway, great oysters!  The gumbo and burgers were good but not anything to crave about.  

Great wine selection too.  I'd recommend the Russian River Pinot Noir!  

I did deduct a star for the service though.  It took a good hour for our food to arrive...

Food was fine but when someone says there is a dairy allergy and specifically asks multiple times... I would hope a restaurant would take it seriously and not assume adding it in any way would be acceptable (and on top of this, not mention that it was added). 

In the beginning we enjoyed a nice meal (I had the baked oysters and he had the roasted chicken and potatoes because we were assured it could be made with no dairy). After the meal we asked how the chicken was prepared simply hoping to come away with a new cooking tip and found out it was prepared with CHEESE. At which point we got fairly upset explaining that dairy is cheese to which the server said "I knew, but the chef assured me it would be minimal since it was cooked down." We notified the manager of the issue and he jokingly asked if we wanted the cheesecake and did nothing more regarding the situation other than saying he would be sure to speak with those involved. 

I am APPALLED at how poorly the situation was handled, especially after making very clear one of us had a severe dairy allergy.

We had our Thanksgiving dinner here.  I had the short ribs and my wife had a shrimp pasta.  

The short rib was satisfactory and would have been better if there had been less fat on the bone.  It came with a shrimp dressing which was delicious.

My wife's shrimp pasta was wonderful.

Luke serves a bread which could be better.  It is an easy problem to solve by simply having lunch at Galatoire's and determining where their bread comes from.  Their butter too.

We always enjoy Luke.

Can't say enough about this place: the ambience is great, the food is great, the service is phenomenal!  New Orleans on a whole is always an amazing culinary experience but Luke's took it to another level!  The stuffed oysters were amazing, the crispy Brussels sprouts were phenomenal (I'm raving about brussel sprouts people!) and people here were just awesome. Kudos to Didi the manager and our server Jesse!

The service was excellent but the food so-so. My mussels were big, juicy, fresh. But the sauce was bland, a sort of creamy thing with no real notes of garlic, butter, pepper or wine. Bleh. But I ate because I like mussels. The pork shank was huge and filling but not terribly smokey. The crème brûlée was awful. The sugar was fired well ahead of time and the crème itself was very blah--a tasteless custard that was not set correctly. The place is loud on weekends so not for a cozy dinner. On the up side, the service was great and the oysters superb. I'd give it another go just to see.
Decent burrito for lunch and chips with it. Had chicken and queso on it. Very quick service
Stopped in for happy hour. Drinks are unique and delicious! One piece of advice. Order the bread pudding. You will thank me.
Very good restaurant. We got there at 830 and had no wait. The waiter was very nice and informative. We got the chicken and shrimp and grits.

One of the few 'fancier' places you can eat on a Sunday night, between 6 of us, we had pretty much everything on the menu and were delighted, the most outstanding was the pate, go for it...amazing and a great portion. They also offer reasonably priced wines by the bottle, so don't order by the $12 glass. Be sure to save room for dessert because the bread pudding is magnificent! For a full meal, with apps, wine and dessert we got out of there on $45 pp!!

Located in the business district of New Orleans, just right outside the French Quarter, I would definitely recommend trying Luke. You can't beat 50 cent oysters and $1 fried oysters during happy hour everyday from 3-6 PM. Super fresh and yummy! The shrimp and grits were also a favorite here. Although, i wouldn't be able to eat this alone for a meal because it is so rich. So I would suggest sharing this entree. The bread pudding was to die for! It is served with hot buttered pecan sauce and vanilla bean ice cream. Perfect!

The only reason I give this place 4-stars is because of the hostess. When I originally tried to put my name in with the hostess for a table, I was told there was no more availability for happy hour seating. I asked her some other questions and I was given such attitude! So I walked out, looked at open table and found a 3:00 reservation, which was in 20 minutes. I was secretly laughing at the lady when i strolled in 20 minutes later with a reservation. The hostess was probably not happy about this, but she had to acknowledge this open table reservation. Despite the reservation, I still had to wait another 30 minutes while she seated all the other parties that came after us. 

Overall, I was pleased with this dining experience minus one grumpy hostess.

This place has great food and great service. The only downside is how small it is inside but in the summer there is a small area to sit outside so this is definitely somewhere you need to check out. I had the taco chicken sandwich, which was amazing, but you have to ask for hot sauce if you get it!!!

I met some friends in New Orleans and we decided to try John Besh's Luke. We went during Happy Hour on a Friday and it was busy but not overcrowded. We had reservations and were seated right away. We started with some raw and fried oysters. For the price(75 cents) it was alright, I enjoyed the fried more than I did the raw. I also ordered a cup of gumbo which was fantastic. I had the French 75 which had cognac, champagne and Lemon juice. This was very good and the mixologist did a terrific job. My friends ordered the Crab blt, and shrimp and grits which they both said they liked. I had the Salmon which was phenomenal. The bed of corn that it laid upon was perfect. Food and drink wise this place was 5 stars but I had to give it 3 because of the service. Our main waiter(we had 4 people visit out table) was rather rude. Anytime I had a question he would answer in a rather "annoyed" way like it was a pain for him to have to take the time and answer it. Also, we had the check split 3 ways, yet as we went to leave and my friends had already left and I stayed to ask if he had added the tip to the bill (as it seemed more than it should have been), he said he did to theirs but not to mine( I had ordered an extra beer so mine should have been a tad more than theirs) That was a little weird to me...but I took him at his word and gave him a cash tip. Why would you not just do it for all 3 guests? I was confused but just wanted to get on with my night.

I would have given this place 5 stars BUT it was a incredibly slow service.  It didn't help that our party was flying out of New Orleans that day and we were in a time crunch.

Sunday for happy hour.  1 dollar oysters.  Juicy and Plump.  Oysters were great.  Had about a dozen, I assume this was why it was slow because our hot food came before the oysters.  The gumbo was awesome.  The best I've ever had and the crunchy rice on top was awesome.

My girlfriend and I shared the burger which was really good.  But the rest of the food at our table was awesome.  Fried chicken and the pressed sandwich were amazing.  Just really really good.  No other way to describe it.

The food and service and atmosphere here blew us away. We had Matzo balls in Chicken Soup, Buttermilk fried Quail and Seafood Gumbo for our appetisers all of which were cooked and balanced to perfection. Our mains were the Lüke burger, Covey rise farm Duck breast & Prince Edward Island Mussels, again great portions and delicious.  Tim our waiter was prompt, courteous and very helpful and  the music as a good mix if blues, jazz and modern songs. Could not fault anything, highly recommend!!

"Luke, I am your fodder."

The weekend getaway to NOLA began here, at the Hilton on St. Charles and it's delectable brasserie, Luke.  Anyone who knows food, knows of John Besh and his place among Southern culinary royalty and Luke appears to be a signature Besh establishment.  

Anyone who knows me, knows that I like beer.

Luke is perfectly adorned in unassuming charm.  The simple caramel, tan and mahogany overtones mixed beautifully with the elegant white linens of the servers and tablecloths belie the strength and sophistication of the bar and menu creations.  This is the place to come if you wish to experience gastronomy without the stuffiness of a dress code.

Like a true Texan with my ever present ten gallon halo, I moseyed up to the bar and sucked up whatever class remained lingering in the room with one deep breath.  I cordially acknowledged the diminutive septuagenarian casually enjoying her Croque Monsieur and pint of beer directly beside me, spread my wide frame across the expanse of my sturdy wooden bar stool, and began my descent into madness.

The wall of liquid shame displayed at Luke is breathtaking,  an eclectic selection of high end liquors, aperitifs and wines, mixed in with a small but comfortable selection of drafts, including 3 house brands, and ample bottled beers.  I ordered the local Abita amber and watched with pure delight as the ladies who accompanied me tried more adventurous concoctions, such as an egg white and absinthe creation that required the sexy bartendress to get in her daily shake weight routine with a rigorous cocktail shaker emulsification process which seemed to last a minimum of five minutes.  I'm sure she hated me for recommending someone try it.

The culinary delights abounded from the kitchen to the table sides in waves of trays swept through the dining room by deftly capable servers to the exhilaration of some and the dismay of others who expected that is was their time to dine.  Jumbo seared shrimp over creamy grits, tangy moules et frites, duck and white bean cassoulet, shimmering pork belly and clams in tagliatelle, and a bone in shank or chop of some sort jutting from the plate in a stunning, Flintstonesque presentation. 

 My jaw dropped at the sight of this meaty delight and I could see from the smirk on my wife's face that she was contemplating the Seinfeld dare of 50 bucks to ask for a taste.  After a few minutes of deliberation she turned to me with the proposition only to find that I was no longer there and to her dismay, as she whirled herself around on her stool, saw that I was already taking a knife and fork to the aforementioned meat shank still resting on the oval tray, much to the horrified stares of the diners and servers alike.  I casually winked to the salivating diner whose dinner I had sampled and simply stated, "A most perceptive choice madame."

Ain't war hell!

Stopped here around 8:45pm because I'd just flown into town and heard this was a great spot.  I'm a vegetarian so I started with the sprouts which where simply perfect.  Roasted in a cast iron pan and then drizzled with honey and topped with a nice salty cheese and apple splices, they were delicious to the last bite.  

Service was a bit slow, had to watch an empty glass at the bar for quite some time before I was offered another but I digress.  

I heard from another patron that the happy hour is amazing so I might be back soon.

Wanted to give this five stars but the food wasn't consistently great. Service was good but when they got busy it seemed like there weren't enough servers so the hostess/manager had to jump in. But they did jump in, so can't complain. And everyone was friendly and knowledgeable about the food. Appetizers were great! Such interesting flavors. The best Brussels sprouts I've ever had and the salads were phenomenal. The entrees were solid, but only the burger was outstanding. Desserts were delicious. S'mores torte was outstanding!

Update: Dinner at Luke, 9/20/07

Went to Luke for dinner with my dinner group and the meal was excellent! First we started off with Malpeque and some other non-Louisiana raw oysters. Delcious! Then I had the fried oyster and avocaldo salad. Again, delicious! Then I had the gourmet Luke burger and pommes frites which I shared with a fellow group member for half of her croque monsieur. The burger was much better than I thought it would be and the croque monsieur was fabulous. I also sampled the onion tart/pie/pizza looking item - it was very, very tasty. Might have been the best tasting item on the table!!!

-----

Update: Breakfast at Luke, 8/12/07

Construction is finally finished so you no longer have to go through the hotel lobby to get to restaurant. I love how the day's oyster selection 'greets' you on the bar as you walk in. Front dining room is very nice for a bistro-style place. I had the two poached eggs on crispy crab cakes with ham and the blood orange screwdriver. The crab cakes were simply perfect! Great crunch, very well seasoned, went perfectly with the poached eggs, ham and hollandaise sauce. Yummy!

-----

A recent addition to the scene, Luke is John Besh's new bistro style restaurant. 

The place is open for breakfast, lunch and dinner, but I've only been there for lunch a couple of times so far. If you like oysters, they have Louisiana oysters, but also Belon and Malpeque (selection varies) on the half shell as well. 

I don't think the word is out yet on this spot as it has been nearly empty every time I have dined there, but I have had some good cochon de lait and croque monsieur there on a recent decadent lunch there with a foodie friend. In fact, we had some much food there for lunch, we had to 'watch' dinner on TV that night!

One of my favorite new places, definitely worth a visit!

Tried this place out due to the great reviews and Yelp did it again!! This reminded my husband and I of Chinese food we had up north. The food was delicious, and you get more for your buck!! Definitely worth the 20 minute drive.

Our waiter was great. He was knowledgeable and attentive. Service was lightning fast. Their burger was one of the best I've ever had. I can't speak to anything else, but I definitely recommend trying the burger if you come here.
If you're looking for a place that will have absolutely best food and original taste of New Orleans please go to this restaurant

No idea how to pronounce the umlaut here. But the food is unquestionably awesome. Would come back here and bring guests, since service was expedient and the restaurant was nice and clean.

We came for brunch. The raw oysters were fresh and well sized, although I've had more delicious ones with more sea flavor and sweetness to the meat. They went down real smooth.

Drinks wise, the champagne-cognac-lemon juice drink is the best hands down. Yummy with a good size, none of that tiny champagne flute nonsense.

I had the shrimp and jalapeno cheese grits. Best I ever had, perfectly creamy without an overwhelming cheese flavor. The shrimp gravy was like, POW I am flavor invading your mouth and ravishing your tastebuds. That good.

The boyfriend had the burger and fries. Perfectly medium rare patty, that's one well cooked burger. Other than that the flavorings were nothing unusual, so I did find myself wishing they would change it up. But they only offer one burger on the menu and it's known as top ten in the U.S., so why fiddle with success? Fries were thin style with grated cheese, very good. None of that feeling of, oh, these just came out of a freezer and were sitting under a heat lamp.
 
Excellent service. Waitress was intelligent and understanding when half our group on the reservation didn't show. Great place!
I am lucky enough to have Elm right across the street from where I live. The coffee is wonderful, food is unique and inspired, and the staff are friendly. Great place!

My favorite Chinese restaurant in Lutz. The owner is very nice. The crispy beef is our favorite followed by the steamed dumplings. Ask for any other dish with "little oil" for better flavor (Chinese restaurants always seem to over-oil all of their dishes, this one is not exempt).

Food here was amazing.  I had the ribeye which was delicious.  Others in my group got the hamburger (I tried a bite and probably the best hamburger I've ever had) and lamb shank which was also great.  The food is reasonably price at roughly 20-30 dollars a plate.  

I would highly recommend if in New Orleans!

Attempted to go here for dinner - checked open table to make sure there were open reservations. There were plenty (we weren't sure how many would be in our party so I was reluctant to make a reservation before I had confirmed everyone). When we got there I was told a table for two was 2 hours. I checked open table again when we exited - I still could have made a reservation for virtually any time in the evening, there were plenty of empty tables as well. Not sure what the thought was here...

Ended up choosing Luke after a few trips to New Orleans.  Nice space with nice decor.  

Ordered:
Crawfish beignets
Raw Oysters 
Shrimp and grits 
Burgers 


The oysters were huge!!!!!     Crawfish beignets were average at best.   The sauce was delicious.  Friends enjoyed the burgers and the presentation was nice.  The shrimp and grits were tasty but could have had some more heat.  All in all not a bad choice.

The store was very clean and the service was very friendly.  We were looking for the toe shoes and they were out.  But, the guy working the shoe department informed about why they were out (apparently they are very popular) and then told us how we could order them online and get them shipped directly to our house with free shipping.
We went for happy hour and their prices for oysters and drinks were amazing! So good, that we're going back for brunch! Also, their service was fantastic and the bartenders made a great drink!

Hachi is a breath of fresh air in an area (Chalfont) with plenty of "just okay" restaurants. Each time I come here the sushi is excellent, there is a commitment to presentation of all dishes and the decor is a nice modern contemporary.

I took a stab at some non-sushi items and was not disappointed. The fried brussels sprouts were excellent; if you like them crispy like I do then you will love them. I also tried the seafood udon bowl which was absolutely beautiful. It was filling and tasty, the noodles were al dente and the seafood was plentiful. The broth could have been a bit more flavorful but all in all I couldn't complain much.

Nice to have a place nearby that is dedicated to quality ingredients and presentation; it makes a difference! I just hope that it gets recognized for the gem it is and sticks around.
Cochon du lait, 50 cent oysters at happy hour & crawfish: All good

I was not previously a fan of Cosi in general, but ever since the weather has gotten colder, I've stopped by to give it another chance.  The Taste Two (I think that's what it's called) is not a bad deal - get half a sandwich + soup (it's a little confusing, because sometimes they give me different size soup).  

The chai latte here is also not too great.  It tastes more like sugar water with some spices in it.

Good service, solid food.  I didn't like my cocktail very much.  It was one of their specialty ones (sorry, can't remember the name) and it was just too sweet for me, like drinking cough syrup.  The bread that they give you in the beginning of the meal was incredible - warm, crunchy crust and soft on the inside.  I wanted something simple that night, so I got a burger, which I was told was renowned.  I didn't think it was great, mostly because it was kind of dry.  They serve the burger to you sliced in half.  I admit that eating a burger in halves is easier and I usually end up doing just that when I get it.  But the problem with the kitchen cutting it is that the juices run out of the meat while it's sitting and waiting to be served.  And then by the time the customer gets it, it's kind of dry.  It seemed to also be cooked more than the medium that I ordered, but that's fine.  So yeah, points off for the burger.
However, I did try my friend's shrimp and grits and it was delicious.  The bread pudding dessert was also very good.  I probably just got something from the menu that was a miss.
They took such good care of my little man, Merlin during the last few days of his life. The staff and Dr. Reddy are very friendly and professional.

Hachi has become our go to restaurant for sushi!  We've been here several times and the sushi is always fresh and delicious.  The service is attentive; everyone is very friendly.  My wife does not eat sushi; she loves the Pad Thai here (best in the area).

You can usually get a reservation on Friday and Saturday night with short notice (although that may change as this place gets more popular).  And it's BYOB - what more can you ask for!

Amazing ribeye here; the star of the show.

Crab & corn chowder: 5 stars all the way. So light, not too cheesy or heavy. Good amount of crab meat.

Crab and shrimp etouffee: 4 stars. Sauce was decent. Instead of rice, pasta was the base starch. It was a thick rolled pasta so the interior was sauce-free and with every bite, a plain pasta noodle would be tasted. I think I would have preferred a open macaroni or rice (so the sauce could coat more surfaces).

Spiced apple glacee with rum ice cream: I loved the ice cream a lot. The spiced apple was really wonderful. The pastry holding the filling was good, but I suppose I wanted a wetter dessert so I didn't enjoy it as much as I wanted to. 4 stars.

I tried the bread pudding and it was nice. I only got a small spoonful but I'll give it 5 stars.

I tried many bites of my friend's ribeye: I want to give it 6 stars out of 5! It's the reason that even though I have hangups about the etouffee and my apple dessert, I have to give Luke 5 stars. The steak was perfefctly cooked, wonderful buttery texture. But the flavor, the flavor was out of this world. It was like the steak was infused with a nice beef broth (think a fine pho soup). I didn't know beef could have such strong beefy flavor - I've never experienced that before. I would come here to eat that ribeye every day if I could.

Great french fries.

The only BAD: During the meal, there was a incredibly loud drunk man who came in and started conversing with a drunk spanish speaking family(?)/friends. The 'family' group sat at the table next to ours (each person had their own Bourbon St. fishbowl) and proceeded to yell loudly over other diners to their guy at the bar. That I didn't mind as much as other diners. HOWEVER, the man's laugh was shockingly disruptive to all conversation at our table. So loud and piercing. I've *never* before had my thoughts interrupted by the laugh of someone across the room in a crowded restaurant. He laughed at a rate about once a minute. The staff did tell the family they couldn't yell to their friend anymore after 10 minutes or so. They did nothing about the laughing man, much to my dismay. The flavor of the steak was actually good enough for me not to knock my rating of Luke down because of the atmosphere I experienced. But there is still a part of me disappointed in the restaurant as a whole due to that man.

this place is so great! I'm holding myself back to go a third time in 2 days! best burger in town, maybe in the state! best burger I've ever had! drinks were delicious! last night we had a terrible server but everything else was so good and I had had a few drinks, so I could care less. Since the bar was right behind us we just got up every time we wanted a drink, so we didn't have to "burden" our waiter. worked out just fine. 

the only reason why i didn't give five stars it because of that one crappy waiter who seemed to have his panties in a twist. poor guy, maybe he was just having a bad night, i hope that was just it. no worries he still got his tip, of course. as a server i understand, we all have our moments. 
love this place, love love this place. 

first time we went for breakfast, and i loooooove grits. so i ordered them with a couple poached eggs, biscuit and some bacon. the grits were luke-warm, so i sent them back, and oh boy I was glad I did, the server came back with a fresh batch and MAN they were awesome. 

the pork sandwhich with cherry dijon mustard was FANTASTIC too. 

can't wait to get back to the big easy so I can stop by one more time and try something else!

Went on girls night out here this past Tuesday and there isn't much to say about this place but just mediocre.  Its a fairly narrow restaurant with a pub like feeling.  There were four of us and they seated us at a fairly small table with hardly any wiggle room.  The servers wear white lab coats which remind me of medical students instead of wait staff.  It would be nicer if they used real linen napkins instead of raggedy kitchen rags.  Besides that the food was ah.. I've had better.  We started off with the assiette De charcuterie which is an assortment of the pate.  It was very good and out of all of the 4 pates my favorite was the rabbit and the condiments were also delicious.  For entrees we had the moules-frites (mussels with french fries basically) which was a large serving for dinner, entrecÔte grillÉe et frites (grilled rib eye steak with fries), jÄgerschnitZel (panned veal ) and the ÉtouffÉe of blue crab & brown shrimp.  The food was nothing spectacular but truthfully I think Besh's restaurants are overrated since I've never had a memorable dinner at any of them. So will I be back, probably not.

I won't be back. 

My first time here back in February was phenomenal. Five stars. 
Second visit with work friends was "good" but lacking attention to details. 
Third visit will unfortunately be my last. Please don't misunderstand, the oysters and raw bar are spot-on, but attention to details and being service oriented are no longer present in my last two visits. 
I couldn't even get my server (I sat at the bar) to pay any attention to me, even though I kept saying I couldn't decide on anything other than oysters. I felt like I was keeping her from tending to more important matters. 

The manager, or a person who looked as such-big guy- kept walking by but never stopped and asked how things were. I think I may have been visibly upset because the "oyster guy" interrupted his TWENTY MINUTE flirtation with the customer sitting beside me (he was peeling her shrimp for her as she ate it, piece by piece) to ask "are you doing ok?".  

On the comments line on my receipt, I wrote "I felt like I wasn't important".  They probably didn't notice.

Went for the oyster happy hour. The oysters were excellent and the service acceptable. 

They make a pretty good Old Fashioned and I liked the overall ambiance. The host/manager allowing us to sit at a table in the back (facing the open kitchen) during happy hour was appreciated. I'll be back.

Poor. Breakfast was terrible. Staff was not helpful and seemed inconvenienced by the business. I heard good things about this place but I was verry disappointed.  Yogurt and granola had an odor to it. Toast was burnt. Eggs were cold. Poor poor poor.

The best shrimp and grits I have ever had. Period. The wait was long but they have full service at the bar. The bartender was extremely polite and recommended I try the shrimp. Definitely coming back for more.

I think our server was a little new, because she seemed a little flustered at times.  The service was not all that attentive either, and she actually forgot to give us bread.  The place is pretty cool inside though, and with some better food and staff, could see this being a fun place, even if it is pretty much a hotel restaurant.

Oysters - we ordered a dozen Gulf oysters, and while the flavor was fine, they were extremely sandy and gritty.  Luckily though, we mentioned this to our server and she ended up taking them off our bill. She even mentioned it was a little late in the season, so she wasn't sure why they were still serving them (which would have been good to know before we ordered as we would have gone with the other oysters.  Also, they should have more than 2 types of oysters. Just sayin'). Luckily, we ordered a Bloody Mary to go with the oysters, and it was pretty damn good.  

Cochon Pressed Sandwich - Given, I'm not a huge ham fan, but I usually like pulled pork, especially if it's got a kickin' BBQ sauce.  But this was way too sweet, and just not my style.  My girlfriend kind of liked it though, so maybe it's just me.

Mussels with Fries- My girlfriend ordered this, and her main complaint with it was that it wasn't served with nearly enough broth, leaving some of the mussels at the top a little dried out.  Other than that, the flavor was decent, and the fries are pretty good.  

I'll be skipping this place next time I'm in town.  Nothing we had was all that good, and I don't think you should keep oysters on your menu if they aren't in season.  And if you're known for oysters, have more than a couple types to choose from (4-5 from different locales would be a good start).

Food is excellent, service is great, and we had the nicest and most fun waiter, Richie Rich! 
My fiance and I are both foodies with high standards when it comes to seafood. After being disappointed at ACME and the Court of Two Sisters (seriously, worst service ever), we tried Luke without much anticipation. But it turns out to be the most pleasant surprise. We were pretty hungry so we ordered a lot. They came at the same time by three waiters, and it feels like carnival. Everything was great, but I gave their "Plates to Share" section highest recommendation. 
Richie Rich is just the perfect waiter when you want a true taste of southern hospitality, but the guy is from Chicago and hilarious. We had a great time chatting about the Chicago Cubs, and he gave us a little surprise to take home. 
Thanks to Luke and Richie Rich for making us love New Orleans much more than we would have!
Our party of 7 were seated in our own private dining room. Exceptional service and our most enjoyable meal in New Orleans!

Another great Besh restaurant. Happy hour has nice oyster specials. The rest of happy hour is just ok to be honest, nothing really special. The swordfish rillietts were really good. I'd come back for the tasso wrapped swordfish...or just a few beers when I'm downtown.

This was our favorite restaurant in NOLA. The barren tender, Brandy, was simply amazing and made wonderful recommendations while being so friendly and outgoing. Food was top knotch-the Brussels sprouts and crawfish bisque was amazing. Highly, highly recommended.

Ok so mixed review. Really good food but the service...not so sure! My friends and I ordered the special that day - fried chicken & Tabasco honey. Apparently the chef that owns this restaurant is known for this chicken. Twenty minutes go by after our order and our waiter comes by to let us know they are out of the chicken. Really? You couldn't have let us know sooner? We then make a comment about seeing a picture online of the etouffee pasta and the waiter tells us he will check if the chef can make it even though it is not currently on the menu (nice of him). He checks and the chef says yes. We then order fries while we wait. Our food comes and the waiter never brought our fries. He never refilled my water or really checked in. Maybe he was just having an off day. Ok so the etouffee pasta was DELICIOUS! It felt lighter than any of the other ones I had in New Orleans. One of my friends got the shrimp and grits and really enjoyed her dish. I would come again but was turned off by the lack of attentiveness from our waiter.

Upon discovering that Luke had $.50 oysters during happy hour, I just had to go there. The oysters were fair in size although the flavor was a bit lacking. You can't blame that on the restaurant completely though. We ordered the crab bisque which was delicious, as well as the chicken and rabbit Pate. That came with some mustard, pickled watermelon rinds, bread and butter pickles, and a marmalade (I think). Very tasty. 

My bf ordered one of the drink menus but didn't seem too happy with it. It seemed like our bartender was easily distracted because we told her we wanted a dozen oysters, and instead of letting us finish our order she went straight to the POS to input the oysters. I had to call her back to finish our order, which was a bit odd. My water cup was empty for the longest time, and after eating so much horseradish I really wanted some water to wash it down. We also didn't get any crackers to eat with them, which was disappointing. 

It was quiet during the happy hour, but you could tell everyone who came there knew about the oysters. I'd definitely go there again for that deal, as well as to try one of the daily specials.

I'm not sure if we went on an off night but our experience was memorable in a bad way. 

The waitstaff wasn't coordinated, drinks took forever, and our food was LÜKEwarm. 

Out of the four of us, only one enjoyed the meal -- the ribeye. The other dishes were either bland or overflavored. 

Additionally, we witnessed one of the waitstaff eating fries off one of our entrees, which left a horrible impression. 

We walked out of the restaurant irritated because Lüke was the first restaurant we chose to try as soon as we got to NOLA.

Went in for happy hour and it was great! 50 cent oysters (huge by the way) and half off glasses of wine were a great way to spend an afternoon. We also had the fried oysters and they were crispy with a slight spice. The cocktails were also inventive and tasty. We sat at the bar and the staff was great and very helpful. If I lived in NO I would be here a lot.
Not too good, not too bad. Service was slow but food was okay. Probably not worth the money though

First stop after landing was our hotel, the Hilton on St. Charles, and down here for lunch. Very, very impressed.  I had the Luke salad, which far exceeded any and all expectations I had, and the special of Chappapeela Pork Ragout. Wow! such wonderful flavor, would definitely recommend!

Thanks Yelp'ers for pointing to us to a fabulous Gem!  I've been to so many great places in strip malls and this is certainly one of them.  We stopped in at 8:30 and first time for both of us.  My partner in crime is local but she hadn't tried it yet.  We both love the BYOB and being next to a PLCB store doesn't hurt.

So cut to the chase... 48 hour Pork Belly, Alligator Roll, Hawaiian Poke and Uni.  Where do we start?  The pork belly is absolutely tender and unctuous.  Add the slightly smokey finish and I would put this stuff on my breakfast cereal any day that ends in "Y".  The Poke was unique with the use of sliced almonds and yellow/green squash.  Amazing texture and tender Ahi will make you want to face plant into the bowl and pretend you're in a pie eating contest.  The uni was great.  My favorite thing in the world and theirs was fresh, sweet and had a nice savory finish.

As Arnold says, I'll be back!
Luke has the most delicious happy hour... Yummy oysters crab soup specialty cocktails three till six... I love all of Beshs places

This must be one of the best places for oysters in New Orleans.  I went with a group during their happy hour and we tried fresh and fried oysters and both were exquisite.  They even made some of the fried ones gluten free for us.  The cocktails were delicious, simple traditional flavors that are half price at happy hour.  Highly recommended!
Was there for breakfast.  I had the healthy breakfast- yogurt with granola and berries.  It was ok.  Service was decent.  Not a place I'd go back, but I am glad I tried it once.

Great for a fast, good (not great) burrito (yes, it is a chain).  The ingredients are fresh, well prepared and it tastes like a burrito, can't ask for much more.  

Still I would go to Pollo Alegre for real Mexican food if I had the time.

Still getting used to paying $6.49 for a burrito (without guacamole or chips) , why is food so expensive in Indy??!!

worst meal I've had in a while.  No doubt the food trucks in the area are totally superior.  Brazilian steak bowl....a joke.  Undercooked, flavorless, tough, and thoughtless.  The help, basically a don't care don't communicate attitude.  No pride here.

Was here on New Years Day in the afternoon and swear I spotted a couple of actresses, though I am hard pressed to find their names. The coffee was delicious, good Bloody Mary's and the service was on point. Get the P&J oysters, you won't be disappointed. I followed it up with the burger. It was good, not outstanding. I could not finish it. My date got the Eggs in Purgatory and those were rich and decadent. She had the jalapeño grits and they were absolutely amazing. We couldn't stop eating them. Forgo the French fries for the grits, you can thank me later.

The pain perdu is really good, especially with the bacon stuffed inside. Huge portion size, enough for sharing. Our waitress was very nice and service was prompt. I'll definitely remember this spot for brunch and breakfast next time.

Really 4.5 stars.

Two of my friends took me here for my birthday, and it was quite a treat.

They serve .75 raw oysters, 1.25 fried oysters, and half-price drinks (drafts, wines, cocktails) during happy hour. My friends got the oysters, which they said were great. I ordered a Buffala Negra, which was a whiskey-ginger with balsamic vinegar and basil. Sounds kinda odd, and was a bit like a salad dressing with alcohol, but was very very good. We also ordered the flamenkuchen, a German onion, emmenthaler, and pork tart. It was good, but quite large and so rich that even between three of us it was a bit much to finish.

For dinner we ordered three entrees and shared family style: crawfish and pork pasta; swordfish with cauliflower and kale; and grilled shrimp over cheesy grits with andouille. All were good, the shrimp was definitely the best.

I was very excited when I found a John mesh restaurant in my hotel. Than extremely disappointed with breakfast. The meal started with a miscommunication with our server and continued downhill from there. I ordered the egg white frittata which came out over cooked and tasting like it was fried in bacon grease. The side of potatoes were fried in bacon grease and contained bacon. As a vegetarian I was pretty dismayed the menu failed to mention this. 

My husbands plate was lackng the accompania to advertised. The grits were dry and the requested butter to put on them took 15 minutes to arrive. 

I would try this restaurant again but would choose lunch or dinner.

Great cozy restaurant with an amazing wait staff!

Food was reasonably priced for the area and definitely did not lack anything in taste. 

Everything we ordered came out quickly and tasted delicious. Oysters were great, steak was great, shrimp and grits were great, even the creme brulee was good!

Only thing we wished for was if we were around for happy hour!
Great wine selection. Shrimp and grits rocked. Weird waiter outfits

Sometimes you get a dish that is so good, you have no choice but to give a place five stars...  This is one of those times.

Went here for brunch and was absolutely blown away.  First had a really good Bloody Mary, subtle spice, good flavor and a nice way to start brunch...  

For appetizer, I ordered the bacon and cheese tart (minus the caramelized onions) and loved every bite.  The bacon was soooo thick, not an overwhelming amount of cheese, bust just enough and thin crust which is perfect to really taste the bacon and the cheese. 

Finally, for my meal I got the shrimp and grits, with eggs and crab meat.  It ended up being something like $25, but, it was PHENOMENAL.  One of the best breakfast/brunch dishes I have ever had.  Soooo many flavors, the sausage, the warm gooey grits, the perfectly cooked shrimp, the crab meat, did I mention the sausage!?  I mean honestly it was incredible....  

YOU MUST TRY THIS DISH.

Excellent meal.  Went on a Saturday night 5:30 dinner, four adults, two kids and an infant. We were sat promptly, near the front - not a problem.  
Kids and wife  had matzah ball soup, was excellent.  This from a New York Jew.  Seafood gumbo was very good as well, though milder than I expected.  Kids loved their mac and cheese and the grilled geese was perfectly cooked. 

The adults had the chicken liver and rabbit liver pate, swordfish, the Luke salad, and the roasted chicken.  All were excellent. The pate is a huge, gout inducing portion. It was amazing.  Chicken was  perfectly moist, seasoned, with crispy skin. Potatoes underneath were some of the best home fries I've had in a while - salty, crisp, and a complement. Luke salad was the only so so pet of the meal, it was bland and overdressed.  

Wine was the 52 dollar Bordeaux on the menu - excellent at its price range. 
We spilt the steamed chocolate pudding for dessert.  The chicory gave it a wonderful mocha flavor. It was fantastic and a great end to the meal. 

The meal delivered, all for 200.   We will defiantly come back.

Terrific Salmon Teriyaki Bento Box! Thought this would give me a good idea of a different variety of what they offered and everything was delicious. For the tempura they had acorn squash, which I've never had but was delicious and very creative! This is definitely going to be my new lunch spot!

Perfect way to ease into New Orleans from out of town with a Sazerac followed by the soft shell crab BLT.  The creole and heirloom tomatoes really added to this dish but the perfectly done crab was the star.  Excellent unpretentious service.

The shrimp and grits and Luke burger are both fantastic.  I love the shoe string fries that come with the burger.  Being gluten free, I get mine without the bun, but the fact that it comes with bacon more than makes up for it.  They also make one of the best French 75 cocktails in the city.

I took off one star because most of the time I end up at Luke as Plan B because my first choice was full or I couldn't get a reservation.  That said, this is a damn good Plan B.
Happy hour from 3-6- so good. Best oysters. We had fried and raw. Sat at the bar. The bartender bragged that he made a better sazerac than the sazerac bar & I agree.

3.5 would be my true rating. 

Walked in on a Sunday morning, about quarter to 10. We were immediately seated at the back. The shrimp and grits was the best breakfast I've had here thus far. Coming from SF with only having Brenda's Shrimp and grits, my palate was totally blown away. And this is where my pros for this resto ends. 

Southern breakfast was average. Bacon was hypertension-inducing salty. Mimi's pancakes were dense and just lacking in flavor. The batter was likely over-beaten. Their OJ tasted as if it was poured out of a store brand bottle you could pick up from Safeway and the coffee was unremarkable. I'll be honest, I don't know anything about famous chefs, but my palate knows no lie. 

Ambiance and service just didn't fit, which seems to be the theme here in NOLA. For such a huge tourist attraction, I'm scratching my head thinking "why?!"

Good food. Lovely staff. I had the crab omelet which was good but slightly over cooked egg. The accompanying waffle fries were delicious. This restaurant just wasn't as fabulous as Restaurant August and Domenica, so perhaps my expectations were too high.

Quality Natural Food With A Local Flair

We had two meals here, dinner and breakfast. For dinner we had roasted chicken, a Luke burger, and Étouffée. All took close to an hour from ordering to delivery. All were excellent. 

For breakfast we had the home made granola yogurt dish, southern breakfast and OJ. Be advised that the bacon is not traditional bacon, but instead is very thick sliced and salty. 

This is really a nice restaurant.

Visiting New Orleans and made reservations at Luke for my boyfriend's 30th birthday.  Good food isn't always hard to find, but paired with incredible thoughtful service? I was blown away and really touched by the effort the service staff made and how special our dinner was. They brought champagne to our table when we were seated and the hostesses helped me surprise my boyfriend with ordering a birthday dessert.

Luke is a restaurant I'd come back to over and over again. And then I'd come back again, cause omg I looooove it. It is just the right amount of fancy (a brasserie) with an amazing happy hour... 75 cent oysters ( that are HUGE) and half price cocktails and wine 3-6 daily. The oysters are some of the best I have ever had... Huge and briney.... And the cocktails are among the best in the city. I had a French 75... And now I am ordering a mint julep to go, cause I gotta say I don't know when I'm gonna find another amazing mint julep... And I am making my way through the best of the best of the city!! Run here for their happy hour... Ahhhh... Even if it is not happy hour... You will be thrilled. Word. Oh and a big shout out to Terrione... What a sweetie!!

Worst service of my life. Sat down at the bar and the bartender didn't even wipe down the bar! We each had a drink and changed our dinner plans because we decided we didn't want to sit with our elbows in crushed saltines and old basil. Wish I could comment  on the food, but like I said the bad service made us change out dinner plans.

It was as advertised. I ordered the burger and wife ordered shrimp and grits. We were seated quickly, food came out quickly, tasted great. Service was good but not as attentive as a 5/5. If I could I would give it a 4.75.
Great lunch on Independence Day. Had the place to ourselves. Wife had the chicken chili salad, I had the tortalinni.

The food was amazing! The prices are a little higher than expected but it was money well spent! The place is nicely decorated and comfortable. The service was pleasant and fast. You must try the shrimp and jalapeño grits-they are life changing!
