The shrimp was so tasty and cooked perfectly- pairing that with the spicy, cheesy goodness of the grits and sausage you will be transported to tastebuds heaven!

You won't find Lorelai Gilmore here, but you will find... 75 cent raw oysters! 5 stars for happy hour.

Half off drink specials as well, but we came for the oysters. Ended up coming here all 3 days we were in NOLA, that's how good it was. The oysters are way cleaner than what you get at Acme, and just as fresh and delicious.

We also tried the shrimp and grits ($21) and pancakes ($9) at breakfast. We added crab meat on the shrimp and grits, per our server's suggestion, which cost an extra $13. Both dishes were good, though the shrimp and grits were way too salty. I needed to follow each bite with a bite of syrup-doused pancakes to rid my mouth of the saltiness.

The other item we tried, which I liked a lot, was the pâté of Louisiana rabbit and chicken liver. It was beautifully presented with crostini and 6 different condiments-- I thought the mustards went really well with it. We couldn't finish it and asked for it to go, and they kindly packed each of the remaining condiments along with the pâté and crostini, which I really appreciated.

Service was excellent every time. 

Definitely come here for happy hour if you're in town!

We got there barely in time for the happy hour oysters. $.75. Quite a deal. They were huge! Also got the happy hour drinks good deal.
Had the crawfish etoufoille. It tasted a little squid like for me. But that is probably how the dish was supposed to be.
My wife got The softshell crab BLT. It was the biggest softshell crab I had ever seen. She ate it all even thiugh she had a huge lunch. It was great.

To put what I think of Luke simply - the food is great, the service sucks. 

Luke's located in the Hilton on St Charles, across the street from the Intercontinental and a block or two from Poydras. And as usual in the New Orleans CBD - parking is a bitch, or expensive. but nevermind that -

Luke is one of John Besh's restaurants - he seems to be taking over the restaurant scene nowdays - think a casual French bistro complete with newspaper racks, wood tables, knives and forks wrapped in kitchen linen - the windows also bring in a good amount of sunlight so coming in to eat lunch here it becomes a bright spot. However the way the restaurant is with the front and there's a back open entrance to the lobby/kitchen/whatever if you sit in the back tables you can catch a nasty draft. 

I'm a big fan of the wild boar and also the rabbit pate - they come in these jars and crostinis - however once in a while I'll get one that feels like it has been in a refrigerator on the highest cold setting and it gets kind of a real hard consistency - but for the most part - creaminess. They also have a charcuterie plate, soups such as gumbo, a matzo ball soup (which is pretty much vegetable stock and a dumpling). 

For lunch they also offer specials - I think it's a cup of soup and an entree for about 20 bucks - they serve up different choices each day.

I got the Luke burger - which is just a great burger. I feel kind of dumb getting it a lot but sometimes nothing beats a well cooked burger for lunch. My friend got the mussels which come in this huge cast iron pot (cheap - 17 bucks i think?) - I also tried the shrimp and grits, which is kind of a smothered in this rosemary sauce - extremely rich. There's also the shrimp farci which I think is one of their best dishes - shrimp stuffed with crabmeat over this extremely rich blood orange hollandaise. They also have a pretty big raw bar - with crab legs, fresh oysters, etc.

So food is on point.

Service however - every time I came in here the servers seemed kind of aloof - one in particular I had on my recent trip - she had extremely bad breath (I think every server should be carrying a pack of mints if they're working all day) and neglected to tell my friend that they charge for every refill on soda - my friends drank about 3 diet cokes each - so they were charged 18 bucks for refills. Now in New Orleans, people love their Coca colas so it's kind of odd to see a restaurant such as Luke to not have free refills - however I feel like the server should have said something about that. Service is on point with the time and food - but the apathetic moods kind of turns me off a little. At least fake a smile. 

I frequent this spot for lunch - Luke is open early for breakfast and is open late (I think 11 pm?) However with better options for dinner I'll just keep Luke as a lunch spot.

This place is awesome, great signature drinks and great atmosphere.

Food is delicious and wonderfully put together the dishes are designed to enjoy all the best of Cajun/ American food.

The proportions run smaller than a regular place but the taste is worth it.

We enjoyed the Gulf fish and shrimp jambalaya, champagne au poire and all was perfect!!

We were so happy to find a place that served the very rare Kumamoto oysters and made our way there. Although they had a Happy Hour going on featuring .75 cent oysters, we opted for the $45/dozen Kumamotos from Washington. The oysters were divine. They are buttery and about a 1/4 of the size of a gulf oyster, but wow! Worth every penny. We should have stayed to eat entrees there (as we love John Besh), but we were there for the rare oysters. Next time, we will def order other entrees.

We love Lüke, but shocked they took the veal Jäger schnitzel, spaetzle and other items off their menu, so they are not really considered "German" anymore.  It's a real shame too, since Lüke was the last restaurant in New Orleans that served it now that "Jäger Haus" (only other German Restaurant in the city) has closed.

This was one of my favorite places in New Orleans. We had to make reservations because it's a small cozy homey place that gets packed! I had the rib eye steak it came with fries. I got the steak medium well and it was so juicy and probably the best steak I've tried yet! We also got baked oysters they had a pesto sauce and tasted incredible! My coworker had the shrimp and grits which was a recommendation from a friend and it did not disappoint. The bottle of wine added amazing to the rib eye steak I had. Yum!
A truly great restuarant.  baring some minor service errors they would have gotten a 5 star rating. I most definitely will return.

OMG, i knew this was going to be due to all the revies on yelp but i was a bit afraid i might be let down, bt NO IT DIDNT.  OMG $6 bucks for 1 dozen oysters (happy hr), u cant lose with this and it was great!!  The drinks were strong and good, i got the luke hamburger, it was def one of the best hamburger ever, well worth the 16 bucks for a burger :)
Had dinner here on my trip to NOLA. Food was tasty just a tad on the salty side for my taste.

Definitely recommend the pate. Very rich - way more than enough to share among two people. 
If you're not an Oyster connoisseur and just want some fresh oysters, go for the P&Js (local oysters) and skip the expensive stuff. 

Not a huge fan at all of the grilled stuffed oysters. The "stuffing" isn't enough crab and mostly cheese for the price. The oyster itself was also incredibly chewy. 

Overall the experience was pretty good!

We had a large party and were lucky enough to get a private room in the back. We were lucky enough to have Rich Whatley as our server.  He was absolutely amazing and made our experience even better.  Besides for the food being amazing he was very attentive and helpful with a party of 8 rowdy fools. One of our guests was a little tipsy and asking some really stupid questions.  He was still helpful and even busted his chops which made us enjoy our time even more!  I will 100% go back any time I'm in Nola and recommend anyone and everyone go there and ask for Rich because you will not be disappointed!
Oysters were just ok. Crawfish bisque was amazing. Best dish. Brussels sprouts appetizer was delicious. Good atmosphere.

One of our best dining experiences. Try to get in before 6pm for 75 cent happy hour oysters (with insanely good horseradish) then continue with the Luke burger, Brussels sprouts, shrimp and grits. We had a table of ten and had excellent service.
Great, fast, and friendly service. Went in for an oil change and the staff was incredibly friendly and knowledgeable.
Great place. We had the mussels, the foie gras and oysters. Breadpudding for dessert -- everything was spectacular.

I've only been here once. We went for happy hour which is a great deal. The deal is only for the local oysters which we ordered. I know it's a cheap time, but the oysters came out so dirty it was difficult to eat. One of our oysters also had a small shellfish (maybe a mussel) attached to it which felt weird. I assumed it would be okay since they shucked it and served it to us... I'm not sure if that was the cause, but I got food poisoning the next day. 

We didn't order any of the other menu items. 

The drink specials for happy hour are amazing. That is mainly the reason for the extra star instead of 2 stars. They have interesting and tasty cocktail concoctions and are included in the happy hour menu!

Other than that... the place is super cute and the service is great. They treat you like you are having an expensive meal, and the bill comes out to so little compared to the ambience. The table bread is just whatevers.

Fine dining prices with terrible service does not make a great meal. Our waiter took forever to greet us and seemed completely disinterested once he finally did. He got both of my parent's orders wrong and they had thoroughly discussed their food allergies and sensitivities with him while ordering. The pacing of the meal was totally off; entrees were brought as appetizers and appetizers as entrees. Once it was set right, the food was all very good but the service left us all with a bad taste. I don't think I'll be returning.

This review is for Luke's happy hour. You DO NOT want to miss this happy hour. It's extremely popular and I've read reviews that you often have to wait and get it. My husband and I were lucky enough to nab a stool at the bar and we got to watch them shuck oysters. First of all, the service at the bar was incredible. Extremely attentive. Drinks came quickly and I greatly enjoyed my GINtilly. The drinks look smaller but you are paying half price for them so that didn't bother me. We ordered a half dozen fresh and fried oysters and omg. Now I'm from Cape Cod, MA so I know oysters. I'm spoiled with fresh Wellfleet oysters on the regular. But I can see why NOLA is known for their oysters! These were massive and fresh. And the fried oysters were out of this world, I've never tasted anything like them! .75 cents per raw oyster, 1.75 each fried oyster, but you have to order them in half dozens or by the dozen. Completely worth it, do not pass it up!!

Really have to update this after a few years.  The staff and the ordering process (yes, even special orders!) have gotten markedly better over the years and I now have nothing negative to say at all about Jerzee's. 5 stars for sure.

I've been ordering consistently here for 5+ years. The pizza is the best around. The takeout beer selection is excellent, and you can't beat a place that's open 365 days a year. Love this place!

We went to Luke's for a Monday morning breakfast around 8:00 am.  The restaurant didn't appear dramatically busy but we weren't in a huge hurry since our flight wasn't until later that morning. My boyfriend ordered the eggs in a jar  which was described being served with fried shrimp, cheddar grits, jalapeños, and a poached egg. He was turned off by the word "fried" since he didn't want a heavy breaded fried shrimp but reluctantly ordered it. I ordered the crab omelet with asparagus with a side order of Mimi's pancakes. I was happy I asked about getting a side order of pancakes since it saved $4 off the bill and you get 3 pancaked instead of 5, which is plenty. 

The wait seemed like a long time considering the restaurant was not busy at all but you almost have to expect this for a nicer restaurant. After all, you are the for the experience along with the food, right? It would have been nice though to have the waiter ask if we wanted another drink or to give us an update on our order. But, 20 minutes later the food arrived. We got the shrimp and grits along with the pancakes. My boyfriend LOVED his. Perfect balance of cheese and grits, not too spicy at all, and the shrimp seemed more sautéed than actually fried. Delightful surprise. Shrimp we're perfectly cooked and with such good flavor. I was regretting not ordering it myself but was looking forward to the omelet. Oh yeah, where was it? I only got the pancakes so far. I ate one pancake and it was okay. I mean you can't really screw up a pancake, right? The pecan butter on top was a nice change to the standard version we get in western New York though so I wasn't unhappy. 

Since they seated us at a small table and there was not a lot of room, I decided to have the waiter take away the pancake plate to make room for the omelet and I didn't want to overeat. After that, the waiter must have realized I didn't get my omelet yet so he quickly hurried off to the kitchen to check on it after he blamed someone else for the mistake. He brought it back finally and when I tried it, I was unhappy to taste a sweet flavor, which I later found out was mascarpone cheese. It was also barely warm. Not good overall. Plus they serve it with a side salad which, frankly, I think is bizarre. I mean, no toast? I saw they had multigrain toast on the menu though so I though I would get a quick order in so I flagged down the waiter to get some. I had maybe 2 bites of the omelet and just couldn't eat anymore so my human garbage disposal BF ate it. Thankful to not entirely waste $16, I eagerly awaited the toast. And waited. And waited. And waited. The waiter finally returned, sans the toast, and asked if the was anything else he could get us and I tried to politely remind him about the toast. Well, he apologized after he again tried to blame someone else, than ran off to the kitchen to get some. Well, the toast was burned on one side and untasted on the other. How the heck can you screw up toast? It wasn't warm and the jam it was served with was a blueberry and strawberry blend. No butter? At this point, I was pissed and we had to hurry up to check out of the hotel and catch a cab to the airport. It would have been nice if the waiter asked how our meal was. At least he didn't charge me for the toast. 

I would try Luke again but not for breakfast. After $75 and it being my last meal in New Orleans, I was not a happy girl. I would also not want Charles for a waiter again. I honestly expected better from a Besh restaurant. The shrimp dish deserves 5 stars though!!!

The reviews did not lie. The bread pudding by itself deserved 5 stars. Completely awesome. You can taste the rum in the pecan sauce. OMG!!!! The shrimp n grits had soooo much flavor, the shrimp were not over cooked, soo good. You would not be disappointed with this selection. Go for it.
Make a reservation, it gets packed.

We went to Luke for the 75 cent oyster happy hour. When we first walked in the restaurant looked packed and I was worried there were no tables, but the restaurant extends farther back than the first front room and we didn't have a problem being seated at a cozy banquette table in the back room. In addition to a dozen raw oysters, we also ordered a bowl of seafood gumbo and the rabbit and chicken liver pate, all to share. I absolutely loved the pate. It had a rich and creamy flavor and also came with several great accompaniments. My only "complaint" is that there was so much pate that we could have used more croutons. On the other hand I was pretty disappointed with the gumbo. While there was a lot of seafood in the bowl, the gumbo itself was bland and lacked any kind of kick. It was the most expensive and my least favorite of the four different gumbos I tried in New Orleans. All in all I'm glad we tried Luke's and coming from Orlando the 75 cent oysters were a steal. In general though we were underwhelmed by both John Besh restaurants we visited.

We had a fantastic time at Luke. All of the staff was extremely friendly and made perfect recommendations. We started with the Brussels sprouts, a cup of gumbo and the tomato salad. For the entree I had the mushroom risotto. Everything was absolutely delicious. I would highly recommend this place.

I have to say upfront that I was a pain in the ass during my visit to Luke... I would have been annoyed with myself if I had to deal with me. Wait... oh ok, that made sense.

So this was a birthday dinner for the wife during our trip to NOLA. We showed up an hour late from what we booked online. The host wasn't fazed at all... he said that we'd be punished later and led us to a table in the back. This restaurant was PACKED so I was appreciative of him finding us a spot and a little humor goes a long way with me.

Let's talk about the food... If you like oysters, MAKE SURE you order the Fried Oyster Salad. You get several huge fried oysters on a bed of romaine, bacon & avocado. Fried...bacon...how could you not want this? It was delicious and a lot of food for a salad.

We shared a crab meat bisque and it was good but spicy! We got a bowl brought to us with a crawfish head floating in it... I immediately grabbed it (yes with my fingers) and sucked all the crawfish goodness out of it. I was met with a mouth and throat on fire from the heat! After downing the glass of water, wiping away the tears and waiting for my wife to stop laughing...I got the strength to whisper "hey that's got a little kick"

Yeah... I'm a joy to eat with

As we continued... I got the moules et frites after some talking to the server...poor woman got asked a ton of questions and didn't seem to mind a bit. The bride & I don't do french OK, stop judging us!

The wife dug her shrimp dish, I can't recall what it was called, but the shrimp were huge. I think she was more impressed by her wine selection but the meal as a whole got a great review from her. Way to make me look good!

All & all, the joint is a little pricey but very good. It's a great selection of regional dishes executed especially well. Epicureans looking for something fancy won't be disappointed.
Great place with fat juicy fresh oyster. The service is attentive and efficient! Should go try!
Oysters, oysters, oysters.  Happy hour=amazing. We got our oyster fix at this place.  The lunch specials are good. Service is good.

The interior is crowded and dim, but not in a cozy way.  We were seated at a table so close to the next patrons that we heard their entire conversation as if they were sitting with us. 

The menu is limited and the service was so so (with the exception of the greeter who was genuinely friendly and attentive). 

Regarding the food, the biscuits were bland; the fries were cold and the corn bisque was watery.

I ordered a Bloody Mary - although it was tasty, it was almost non-alcoholic.

For those it matters to, I think we were the only locals in the place.

Luke is one of the benefits of living in NOLA CBD. It is good both for lunch (best crawfish bisque you can find) and for dinner. This is the exact NOLA food we like - Cajun cuisine with European accents. Subtle, flavored, but letting you savor freshness and original taste of the food in every bite. Love the atmosphere and staff.

OMG went at 3 pm for a late lunch
Fantastic 
Brussels sprouts 10
The crawfish Bisque 10
Oysters HUGGGE $9 for dozen  10
Happy Hour
Wednesday special Pasta Sausage dish 10
Yelp rating scale sometimes is just to low
If your within an hour 
This is a must eat at

This review is mainly for the service. I felt discriminated by the color of my skin at this restaurant. 

We came in at 3 pm on a Friday when there were a lot of empty seats. Our first server introduced herself right after doing so at two neighboring tables, but we waited about fifteen minutes before anyone asking if we needed anything or introducing today's specials, while the table next to ours had already got their first dish. (We came during happy hours, but I found out only through her friendly conversation with the girls next to us after we were done eating.) 

I thought she had forgotten us so I told her with a smile that we were ready to order. She turned around and sent a trainee-looking guy to us and never spoke to us again. (You could tell because they don't take orders, dress slightly differently, and mainly clean up dirty plates from tables.)

I don't mind being served by a trainee, but our glasses were empty the whole time and no one bothered to add water. It was very hard to get the second guy's attention because we sat where most customers were served by the first server.

I noticed our second guy served all Asian customers who sat in various areas. I hoped this was a coincident.

I'm usually very polite to my servers. I understand how stressful their jobs are and I respect them a lot. I don't need everyone to put on a smile while serving but at least I shouldn't feel neglected with no water and no plate for bread, or being treated as a less valuable customer while people next to us were getting a five-star treatment. I really hope this doesn't happen to others because this experience was very unpleasant. I'm never coming back here again.

The food is great, I recommend the sofritas. They have good vegetarian options. The staff was okay, I felt like they wanted to gossip more than help the customers. Also, shouldn't be discussing the matters of the staff out in the open.
Stuffed oysters, shrimp etouffee, chicken thighs, cabernet.. all excellent!

Outstanding food! Service was a little slow but the food made up for it.
It was slam packed when I went there. I had the shrimp and grits which were exquisite and the bread pudding for dessert. Both were recommended by the waiter and they did not disappoint!

I will definitely hit this place I my next visit to NOLA!

This place is coasting on a name. Our first impression was that the service was terrible. Food was mediocre and service continued to be terrible. Actually writing this review while waiting ten minutes with dirty plates in front of us, waiting to be cleared. Asked for the check as soon as we finally found someone to clear the table. Can't wait to get out of here. So many better places to eat in NOLA!

Besh, Besh, Besh-- everybody tells you to go to some part of the John Besh empire, and who am I to say no?  Looking for something open on Sunday night, but less expensive than August, we ended up here.  We were nearly turned away at the door-- "no walk-ins for at least the next hour," we were told.  But we found a small corner of the bar and ultimately convinced the waitstaff to let us squat there.

The name of the game is shrimp.  Shrimp cocktail for an appetizer: these things are substantive, meaty, and flavorful-- nothing like the bloated, frozen stuff I buy at the grocery store.  Shrimp and grits for an entree-- a tasty, rich, sauce, for more delicious shrimp and grits like nothing I've ever had up North.

I liked my sazerac too.  In a town like New Orleans, I am told you can eat much better, but let me tell you, you can also eat much, much, worse.

Update:  Downgraded to three stars after my experience at Cochon-- which rendered this but a pale memory.

Thanks to the large, bald-headed man that looked like the manager... Lüke, you make me want to PUKE!! Service was so horrible, it left a bad taste in my mouth from our trip to New Orleans. They did not make any effort to accommodate our bachelorette party group without a reservation!

This is an overpriced bistro with decent food. The restaurant lacks the kind of ambiance to justify their prices for food that is just OK. After reading rave reviews of Luke in our guide book and double checking on Yelp! we were excited to try it. Luke probably serves the most inspired German food in New Orleans, but it is still German food.

Used to go here often for their pizza special. Was great for a year or two. The last few times, the pizzas were burnt, and I mean black on the bottom. I complained to the manager, and was given a credit for two free replacement pizzas, and these came out burnt as well. The idiot that brought them out to me said that this is normal since you have to melt the cheese on top. REALLY? I will never waste my time or money on this place again.

Came here for brunch on Christmas Eve. Food is great, served in a big portion as well. I suppose the cuisine is creole. The menu is in French. We ordered three dishes to the table, for any of which I couldn't pronounce the name. But the food tasted very fresh and flavorful. Each dish had a hint of kick in it but not too spicy. The andouille sausages, the grits, the biscuit, the bacon and the cheese all were very satisfying. Definitely a place I like to go back to. Not a five star simply because there are so many great eats in New Orleans.

I chose Luke for my last meal in New Orleans for my birthday weekend at the recommendation of one of the bell hops (Kevin) at our hotel (Le Meridian). Thanks Kev! When I first viewed the menu on Yelp, I was honestly nervous. But I went anyway since I had a flight to catch and was pressed for time. I didn't want anything fancy...just breakfast food. So I ordered the Luke Breakfast. I had a French 75 for my last drink while I waited. First of all, that drink is probably one of the best drinks I've ever had with cognac in it. I couldn't stop talking about it. I was highly disappointed when the bar at the airport said they didn't make it. And you call yourself a bar. Whatever. I'll make it myself. Now to the food. The food. !!! It was so good!!! Best Grits I've ever had in my life!!!! The biscuit was....immaculate. Tender. Even the jam was good. There are other parts to the breakfast that were also great but I won't comment on them. I'd rather leave you in suspense so you can be pleasantly surprised. Enjoy!!

This was, by far, my favorite restaurant experience in New Orleans.  I came for dinner and man oh man did I feast!  I'm so glad I looked at Yelp's pictures for this spot prior to my visit, otherwise I would've totally overlooked the flammenkuchen appetizer.  It's BACON PIZZA.  Get it, eat it...ALLLLLLL.  Best thing on the menu.  The fried brussels sprouts are pretty bomb too, and as for the pate, it can easily feed four people and it's so buttery and delicious, it'll be gone in a flash!

Now, no trip to New Orleans is complete without having some good ol' shrimp n' grits, and they were good indeed!  What was really nice is that I was splitting this dish with someone, and the kitchen served us two plates!  Great gesture!

You need to get the steamed chocolate dessert.  It's kind of like a mousse, but thicker and a bit more cake-y, and for someone who isn't the biggest fan of ice cream...SALTED CARAMEL FOR THE WIN!

I love the location of this restaurant, it was right next to the hotel we were staying at (Le Pavillon)

The food was delicious! you definitely have to get the grits and the baked oysters! The restaurants ambiance was nice and fancy, service was good too.

Happy hour is from 3-6, and it gets booked fast so make a reservations!

This place is great from the moment you walk in the door. Huge selection of beers excellent food menu and the staff has the beer knowledge and are very welcoming. We will be back soon. #chickenparmpizza

We were excited for dinner on my wife's first trip to NOLA and decided to try this place based on reviews and the menu we saw online. We ordered the pate "scented with truffles" there was certainly no truffle flavor but the pate was very good. I had the Etouffee which was good and she had the entrecote with fries which was perfectly cooked but served with a massive portion of butter. Overall the food was good but the service was slow and almost uninterested even though they were two waiters assigned to our table.

Their happy hour menu has only oysters on it...but that is all you need, my friend.  

The oysters are the freshest of all the places we tried in Nola - comes with cocktail sauce, whipped horseradish and lemon.  75cents a piece!  

The fried oysters are light and crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside.  Some of the best fried oysters I've ever tried - these were a little over a buck a piece.

All their cocktails and draft beer were half off.  If you join them outside of happy hour times, their other food looks amazing as well.  Prices are a bit expensive - they're a nice restaurant though - which I didn't expect at first.  Great for date night but also good for groups - they have a whole upstairs area.

This place is simply amazing. The first night in NOLA my group and I went to Luke's for dinner. Our server Kenny made us feel welcomed. Kenny is one of the best servers I've had in a while. He made our experience unforgettable. The food and drinks were also amazing. If you are in NOLA you need to visit this place!

Had brunch here. Great ambiance. Very intimate. Visiting from Philadelphia it was nice to be in a establishment that put emphasis on southern traditions. Seafood was super fresh and affordable. Waiters we'e complete gentlemen. Enjoyed their accents. Lol. Drinks took longer than expected. Definitely will visit again when in NO

We stopped at Luke lunch and dinner on our last visit to NOLA.  Service is professional and attentive, not overly intrusive.  The fried oyster salad is excellent.  My wife had the Jambalaya at lunch and there was so much meat that it could easily feed two people.  The quality of the ingredients and preparation are first rate.  I think Luke is a very underrated restaurant in NOLA and deserves more recognition.  I will be in NOLA again and will be sure to stop for another meal.
Awesome!  We enjoyed a huge platter of fresh seafood ~ crab, king crab, mussels, clams, shrimp & oysters. Happy hour is a must $0.50 oysters on the half shell & BOGO tap beer :) Enjoy!!

From the start to the end, the dinner was a great experience. We arrived at our reservation 20 mins early and was able to get a table no problem.

I thought the restaurant was a good looking restaurant that felt nicer but not too stuffy. The wood floors are gorgeous but could probably use a nice polish.

We had two servers who were both friendly and very easy going. We had a little help ordering a nice bottle of pinot gris to go with the seafood that we planned to ordered. 

Appetizers: The petite seafood platters was the perfect for us 3 ladies to split. The seafood was so incredibly fresh! We also ordered the fried oyster salad which was very good. Bacon and fried food is always a good combo.

Entrees: We ordered the mahi mahi with the crispy kale. The mahi was cooked perfect  and the citrus topping was a great touch. The kale was a bit over salted for me but the texture was great! We also ordered the Shrimp Cavatelli. This was definitely my favorite out of the two dishes. The pasta was perfect and the sauce was amazing. 

Dessert: Brandy Milk Punch to close off dinner and an amazing Steamed Chocolate cake which was rich and fudgy and warm and a perfect contracted to the coffee ice cream. 

Definitely one of my favorite meals in NO.

Simply amazing! The Étouffée with blue crab & brown shrimp is hands down my favorite dish EVER! It's THAT good. The chargrilled oysters are also amazing. The bf ordered the grilled ribeye and was super satisfied with it. The buttery sauce added to the juicy flavors of the ribeye & the grits complimented the dish well. And you get fries on top of that! Holy moly! Needless to say, we were stuffed with all the deliciousness in front of us.
Happy hour oysters were outstanding.  The little neck clams were a totally new preparation.  And the charcuterie plate?  BAZINGA!  Go here!
Great hh oysters.   Definitely some of the best in town.  We went at 3pm and service was quick and friendly.  We will be back for more
Loved the atmosphere you can have a drink and get lost for a while. Just had the oysters and a beer but will be back!

Two stars seems generous. First, they don't have control over their A/C and heat because they're connected to a hotel, and it was FREEZING. Literally everyone in the place had their jackets on, and the food became lukewarm almost instantly. Second, the service was poor and uninformed--everyone there seemed peeved, and clueless about wine. Third, I had the bizarre mozzarella-topped ham and cheese sandwich, and my homegirl had jãgerschnitzel, both of which are kind of hard to mess up--we both could only bring ourselves to eat half of our portions with great willfulness. The ambiance is nice, but kind of chain-y, which could also be said of the food. It was a huge bummer to spend so much money on such sub-par food.
Amazing food.  Had the etouffee and it was beyond amazing.  The charcoutere platter was great as well.  Best place I ate in my entire stay in NOLA.

Luke did not exceed my expectations, but was delicious. I feel like if I am going to pay a lot for food, I should be blown out the water, and I was not. Still gets 4 stars because I enjoyed everything, staff was great, and I really do not have any complaints. I would recommend this restaurant to a friend.

A bit disappointing for brunch. They were understaffed and service was slow. Brunch menu is a bit limited. Had the fried chicken and biscuit which was solid. The egg on top was superfluous and forgettable. Shrimp and grits were just ok for the high price point. 

Update: went back again for oysters at happy hour. Service was still pretty bad. The quality of the shucking was awful. There were gooey globs of dirt on the shells and on the oysters and most of the brine was gone.

While I can't speak for the notoriously popular happy hour oysters here, dinner here seriously hit the spot.  Luke worked out to be the very first stop on my recent NOLA trip and the chefs here executed Cajun Creole cuisine darn well.

To begin, my crispy brussies was arguably the best I've eaten yet as its incorporation of honey, marcona almonds and cheese gave it much textural contrast and a very pleasant sweetness to round out the savory tones.

Thereafter, my crawfish etouffee was just downright fantastic - brimming with crawfish and bursting with bold spicy flavor from the roux.  Even the pasta itself was hefty with texture almost like that of gnocchi.  All together, it gave me one glorious food coma for hours.

My one gripe was that the maitre'd was astonishingly cold, in fact the waitstaff in general was pretty much devoid of any warmth.

The food is great but the service is terrible.   Wife had shrimp grits (awesome but a little salty)  I had the rib eye and it was cooked to perfection. But I am still waiting for the dessert menu an I think I will be here until infinity.

the shrimp n grits and grilled oysters were yummy. great service in the middle of mardibgras weekend .the burger looked ridic and most couples were sharing one with eeach having their own truffle fries. check it out!
Amazing food! I recommend the shrimp and grits- just delicious and fitting for this beautiful city. The service was also very welcoming and the ambience very impressive.

Menu was small and we didn't love the rabbit and liver pate. I started with the stuff we didn't like because we loved everything else. The food was excellent, service was top notch and the location was convenient. If you are in NOLA and want something good outside the French Quarter go to Luke!!

pros:
free wifi - no login, they let you use it forever, no hassle.  yay, thank you!
large upstairs space uncrowded on a Thursday evening.
friendly woman at checkout.
clean.

cons:
i really like unobtrusive, alternative rock Shins-style music in cafes, not kinda-loud 90s soft rock-style.
really loud environment, even with earplugs.
staff was unfamiliar with special orders, was patient with me, but it seemed like an effort.

I came to Lüke after my mom raved about it for months, and as far as the food goes I was not disappointed. The oysters were great (although they were out if two varieties by 6pm), and the creole tomato salad tasted as fresh as a Whole Foods smells. The peach & blueberry pavlova was a great and light was to finish the meal off. My friends got the bread pudding which smelled fantastic. 

We sat in the bar area so we were tagged teamed by two waiters - one of which was amazing. The other took out drink order then didn't return for twenty minutes, and we had to ask the other guy to check on the wine. For the atmosphere, the service just didn't match. 5 stars for food, 3-3.5 for service.

I love the food at Cosi and there's adequate seating. But my complain is it is very confusing to place an order. It is all over the place. Sandwiches in one corner, pay in another and pick up beverages in yet another. The cashier keeps asking what you got, but doesn't hear half the things because there are always too many people. When it's crowded, customer service goes out the window. The cooks are yelling, cashiers are confused and as a customer you are afraid of making a mistake while ordering. Phew! Quite stressful. A cafe should be a welcoming place.
Had dinner and a breakfast here. Excellent food and service. I'm pretty picky and I couldn't find a thing I didn't like!

People are pretty harsh on this establishment, here, but I think it does what it does well. I've gone in there when the line is to the door, but I'm always through in 5-10 minutes. The signature salad is always good, full of fresh greens, grapes, pistachios, blue cheese and dried cranberries. 

Today, I tried a duo, so I had a half signature salad, that was definitely not quite a full half, and a tuna sandwich on the standard cosi bread, along with cracked pepper chips. It was all filling and delicious. At $7.77 with tax, this rings up to be one of the pricier on campus establishments for a quick bite. But it's definitely my favorite salad. Also, they have outdoor seating, every day of the year. It was unseasonably warm today, and I sat out with coworkers and enjoyed the blue sky.

3.5 stars
Not the fanciest place for dining in. But their great for cheap eats. Basic menu you would typically find at a food truck spot. Business hours they stay open pretty late. To go orders you can drive up to the curb and one of the ladies will approach your car for orders. And the food will be brought out to your car. 
They have the cantaloupe drink here that comes in a extra large cup for $3. Definitely a favorite that has us coming here just for the drinks.

Great service, friendly staff, & an immaculately clean office. I called at 3:00 PM on a Friday afternoon, & was able to get a 5:00 PM appointment. Dr. Lisa Clifford was an exceptionally knowledgeable doctor & she performed a thorough exam with the help of a friendly vet technician. My little guy was not at all traumatized by the blood work, so I know they had to be gentle. I purchased a pet wellness program. A little high pressure sales but in this world, you get what you pay for, nothing in life is free and if it's too good to be true, it's not! Dr. Reddy is building a state of the art veterinary hospital on S.R. 56 right near his current practice that is seconds from my home. Let's be real, if you really love your pet, you are going to take care of them so be prepared. Their prices are in line with all the other veterinary practices in the area, you are paying for skilled professionals and there are three great doctors on staff to pool their knowledge to provide your pet with the best treatment plan. The wellness plan does contain some very technical legal terminology so read it carefully if you are going to pay monthly, my advice is to pay it in full if you possibly can & you get a 5% discount. 

I was sent home with a real "Doggy Bag" of medications for my little one, including ophthalmic antibiotic drops & oral liquid drops. One good tip, get written prescriptions & go to Walgreens because the ophthalmic solution "Tobramycin" was $37.00 from the Vet & $19.99 from Walgreens & Publix & CVS also offer pet medications now. I am sure the Clavamox was also at least $15.00 cheaper too. All the take home medications were clearly marked with precise instructions & the technician went over each one explaining step by step how to administer before I left. All & All, I was very satisfied with the professionalism of the office staff & the way we were welcomed in on the same day after a long week. I was even more impressed that Dr. Clifford called me on Saturday to go over my little guys blood work results. I am glad I chose Seven Oaks Pet Hospital and I owe it to my fellow Yelp users who took the time like I did to write an honest & truthful review of the business. Thanks for your honesty and thanks to Seven Oaks Animal Hospital for an outstanding experience. I just hope that when you move to your brand new larger facility & grow your client base, you won't lose that comfortable feeling that makes your office so warm and cozy. 

BTW, when you visit Seven Oaks Animal Hospital, be sure to look for Dunkin, the "Lion Kitty" that rules the office. He can be found allowing the staff to share his chair, or just taking a nap on the front counter next to the computer monitor or anyplace else he desires. He is the friendliest office mascot you will ever want to meet.

Lovely place very good food
Service very slow as everywhere in New Orleans

Pricier than the 2$would let argue
Absolutely amazing! Good portions and very tasty, savory food. Must haves: shrimp and grits, pâté, bisque and gumbo. Phenomenal! Great service too.

This is one of the best restaurants I had ever been to. Good service. The brussels sprouts were amazing, everyone should order them! Good drink selection, good main meal. Liked it so much we went back for breakfast on our week long trip another day. Must eat here if you are visiting New Orleans!
OMG!!! Happy hr is the BEST!!! Half off on Cocktail menu and $6 for a dozen of OYSTERS!!! YUMMMM! I wish LUKE will come to Los Angeles! You must go! HH is week day btw 330-6pm. Don't miss out!
Great atmosphere, food, and location.  The P&J oysters are an unbelievable deal at $16/dozen.   Really enjoyed the draft Luke Alt bier.

The best meal I had while in NOLA was the crab and shrimp étouffée. We also had the shrimp and jalepeno grits. The seafood was all cooked to perfection. Tasty cocktails, too. We ordered the steamed chocolate dessert which was a confusing dish... it was neither steaming nor hot... 

The service was great. Plus, we got a few little chocolates for dessert. The people that were seated around us? Couples who couldn't stop making out over their oysters.... I was kinda grossed out but hey, good for them ;) .

My wife and I ate there late Friday night after watching part of the Saints preseason game in the dome. We had the P&J Oysters and Crab Maison for appetizers -- both were excellent. For entrees, my wife had the fried oyster and bacon salad and I had the shrimp and grits. The fried oysters were incredible and the bacon was outstanding. The shrimp and grits were on the rich side but incredibly tasty. For dessert we had the bread pudding and the creme brulee. The bread pudding was phenomenal. The creme brulee was very good as well but nothing special about it.

Amazing! My husband said the shrimp & grits were the best he'd ever had, and I loved the Lemonfish. We also had the brussel sprout (salad), and the stuffed squash blossoms, which were both bursting with flavor and well presented. We also had the best server in the house, and in Louisiana as far as I could tell. "Richie Rich" was funny, and on top of the evening. We never sat for too long with out food, or drink on our table. And he was worried about our experience because of a "loud(-ish)" table in the back. But his attention and the quality of the food, made our experience the best one we had in New Orleans.

As you would expect just amazing attention to detail in this Besh signature. I had the sazarec to start and wife enjoyed the Mexican Hefeweizen. Opened with the Baked Oysters (delicious!) and then enjoy the chicken for her and I had the shrimp and grits with crabmeat on top.  Amazing! The strawberry dessert with a cappuccino perfect after a great first day in NOLA!  Recommended!
Happy Hour Oyster! You must have it!!!! And for entree, try the Mussel !!!!! Awesome!!!!!

Food was amazing. We ordered a ton of food and had to take some home!
Service slow and they were not interested. They could have made more money if they asked for drinks or came back to table. We would have ordered more appetizers.

I give 5 stars-food
I give 2.5 stars-service

I would recommend going! 
Loved the gumbo! Set the bar high and the whole vacation-"gumbo was good but not as good a LUKE!" I would go just for gumbo!

I ordered this-Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en Cocotte" (DELICIOUS!! Had to take home ordered to much food)
Kids had Oysters which were inhaled and served with fries (which were awesome)

Go during happy hour but make a reservation it gets busy! 
Happy hour raw and fried oysters were great!

Minus service this place is Excellent! Go you will not be disappointed!

Came in to Lüke for breakfast on a Friday morning and enjoyed it so much that we came back for Friday supper. 

The breakfast items seemed basic, but were cooked with so much flavor and diversity. The crab omelette was a lot of food because it came with a mixed greens salad and a side of fries. The omelette itself was creamy and packed with crab, and the fries were crispy and salty. 

My favorite breakfast dish ordered was the shrimp and grits--it was served in a skillet, with andouille sausage and a brown sauce. The shrimps were huge and cooked tenderly, and the farm fresh eggs on top added extra creamy texture to the grits. The description said 'jalapeño grits' but I couldn't taste any heat. This dish would be even more amazing if it came with a biscuit on the side to scoop up the brown sauce and grits. 

The Pain Perdu was like a French toast with mascarpone spread and born slices separating the bread. Perfect balance of sweet and savory. 

We returned to Lüke for dinner, mostly for some small bites. Saw photos on Yelp of the charcuterie board and that appetizer is a must try!! There were 5 different types of cured meats on the board, including a duck sausage, terrine of pork shoulder, rabbit pate, and more. It was served with crusty bread, and able to be paired with whole grain mustard, horseradish mustard, bread and butter pickles, and pickled watermelon rind. AMAZING if you love trying cured meats. There was a balance of creamy textures in terrine and pate, and also a balance of fattiness and meat in the other meats. 

Also ordered a small seafood platter, which had raw oysters, crawfish ceviche, and steamed clams, mussels, and shrimp. This platter was a hit or miss. The oysters were sweet and not briny or sandy, the crawfish was sour and had a little kick from the serrano chilis, but there was nothing special about the steamed options--the shrimps were slightly over cooked and hard to peel and the clams and mussels were only slightly flavored. For the amount of food served on the platter, it was worth $29 (something in California of that price, quantity and quality would have probably been about double the price). 

Also ordered a side of Brussels sprouts, crispy and full of flavor in the chili oil, and extra crunchy in texture because it was topped with apples and almonds. 

Lastly we had a bread pudding with pecan sauce and a scoop of ice cream. Excellent way to end a Southern meal! The top of the pudding was crispy, inside was moist, and the hot buttered pecan sauce wasn't overly sweet. I probably could have used double the amount that was plated. I am definitely glad I stopped in twice. 

Thank you John Besh for getting both lunch and dinner spot on!! Everything was so enjoyable that we tried another one of his restaurants, Domenica, which is located only a few blocks away from Lüke!

This place exceeded my expectations, I was just looking for a place to have lunch, and ran into this place, nice, cozy, traditional, but amazing fusion of flavors.  My wife got Brussels sprouts and I had a hamburger w/o bread.  This place has a great location between CBD and the French Quarter!! I strongly recommend it.
Jumbo shrimp does not have any flavor but being salty. Happy hour has cheap and good oysters.
Good food. Bistro atmosphere. Brussels sprouts were a favorite.  Staff was busy not overly friendly.  Good drinks. Would go back for the food.

People crack me up when they rip places like this apart.  IT IS A CAFETERIA STYLE RESTAURANT!  Let's just make that clear. 

 If you like cafeteria style food, then you'll probably like this one.  They use a surprising amount of salt considering their target customer base (the retirement center across the street should give you a hint).  So, their food actually tastes better than other cafeterias around town. 

The drive thru is what I like most about it.  I can run thru the drive thru on my way home from work and get fast food that actually has vegetables involved instead of grabbing a burger and fries.  

If you live in S. City, its a good location, if you don't, it's not.

For a cafeteria, they actually stay pretty busy too.

*Didi B's review is right on.*
I had the crawfish bisque. It was delicious! We had a party of 8. They accommodated us and put us in a private room. Great service

Our first experience was a good one. The restaurant itself is conveniently located a few doors down from a liquor store. Convenient because it is BYOB so pick up a nice pairing of wine to go with your meal. The inside is clean with a modern chic décor and nicely laid out with a sushi bar and small dining area and single bathrooms. Service was great and attentive, the prices were reasonable. The food looks like a work of art when it comes out to your table but the reviews on it was a mixed bag for me. 

Spicy taco trio= Average with no real spice to it. Bit too creamy for my liking
Miso soup= Good flavor and better than what I have had at any other places
Grilled seafood salad= Nice presentation and good portion however it was a bit on the salty side
Sushi- I thought it was really good quality and flavor, but my son (who is used to your standard way of how a shrimp tempura roll is made and tastes) thought differently
48 Hour Pork Belly- I thought it was a really good combo, but would have expected the pork belly to be a bit moist and delicate.

I think I would go back again (minus the kiddos) just to be able to try some of the other interesting dishes on the menu and sample more of their sushi offerings. Instead of hiking out to Doylestown for a an adults night out or date night type spot, consider trying this place out.

happy hour features $0.75 fresh oysters and $1.25 fried oysters, you can't beat that!  The oysters can be ordered by dozen or half dozen, and safe with fried, and only one type of oyster is offered.  The breading on the fried oysters falls right off when you fork it up so it's a bit harder to eat, but delicious anyway !  We were lucky to get in on a weekday afternoon as well as the afternoon on a Friday - it can certainly get crowded by the weekend, and you're welcome to wait by the bar (which can get overcrowded as well) for a table, so remember to book ahead if you can!

i knew that this would be a good place to come after a tiring flight from LA.
they're open later than most of the other restaurants in NOLA, which was the initial appeal.
this spot is casual but nice, which was friendly to my super casual attire. friendly service and busy late on a Friday night, but not obnoxiously busy.
they do specials for every day of the week, and i highly recommend going with the specials.
for Friday, it was redfish court bouillon, which came with a choice of soup and also dessert. my first gumbo in the city and it remained the best that i eventually tried throughout my weekend visit. the crawfish bisque was also really good.
the oysters on the half-shell were probably the best that i had in town as well, despite recent issues and questions about the NOLA seafood. tried both the kumamano and the local "P & J" oysters, and the local ones were much better.
the entree was amazing, and i managed to eat most of it even though i was already stuffing myself with the delicious appetizers and bread. the fish was cooked PERFECTLY.
at the end of the meal, we had their bread pudding which was covered in bananas foster sauce, and it was so good. props.

I cannot express how grateful I am for the staff that work at Luke! We came in based on yelp reviews and recommendations from our hotel staff and were blown away with how kind everyone is and the incredible food.  As soon as our waiter saw we had a bachelorette we were served free shots and champagne from the manager along with free dessert!  The busy wait staff congratulated the bride while running food and offered to take pictures for us.  We walked in on a Friday night around 7 and waited 10 minutes which we were not expecting at all. We were all amazed at the food and hospitality thank you for an amazing experience!

I would qualify it as one of the best restaurants in town. It is a mist.
We got to sit in front of the kitchen and you get the real experience there. Food was incredible!
Also the service was amazing. When we finnished dinner started to rain and blow very heavy wind. Thanks to the hostess we didn't got wet!! We really appreciate it! She saved us from getting soaking wet!!

Delicious from my ginger salad to the espresso mochi dessert. We ordered the 12 piece sushi combo for three people which was the the perfect amount for 3. And our 4th person ordered the teriyaki chicken which looked good and came with fresh veggies. And being byob is a big bonus especially cause the wine store is two doors down.

This is a popular restaurant, so I won't try to add on anything that hasn't been covered already. The reason I am writing this review, though, is to throw some wind into their sails since their service on Christmas Day was outstanding.

Place was packed, kitchen got a little behind, and servers were scrambling. Food finally came out, was delicious, and at the conclusion management came by and personally apologized for the wait. I love to see this level of concern for the guest experience, and would happily return to experience it again.

Ahhh a week later and i still remember our wonderful server Shane and all the fine recommendations he made, from drinks to eats.  I think by far this was my all time favorite place to go when I visited New Orleans.  I kept begging my husband to take me there but alas time run out and we were so booked with other dinner engagements.  You can't help but love this place, it's of course trendy, clean, professional, and just plain yummy things come out of the kitchen.  The menu is interesting, the drinks intriguing.  We sat in the back dining area and I had a beautiful view of all the fun going on in the kitchen.  People just seemed happy to be working there.  All and all a super great place to go, not just because of who it belongs to but it does give it a lot of credibility that it will be a wonderful dining experience.  

I can't wait to go back...!!
Perfect experience. Oysters were delicious! Shrimp and grits were some of the best I've ever had. Solid 5 stars!

Went here for our first dinner in the Crescent City. Soooo glad we avoided the tourist traps of the Quarter!!! A W E S O M E food!!! We had the oysters and drinks for happy hour and the rib with crab meat and shrimp w grits for our meal. Both were fantabulous!!! I repeat, stay out of the quarter for food!!!

We really enjoyed our dinner here. Drum meunière was excellent, and roasted chicken was probably laced with crack.

Didn't make it for happy hour - definitely will next time we're in New Orleans.

Full disclosure - planning to steal their Brussels sprouts appetizer recipe for our next dinner party

We ate at several restaurants during our recent trip to New Orleans and Luke stands out as one of the best.

There was a 30 minute wait for lunch on a Friday around 1:00 but the wait was definitely well worth it.  Every aspect of the dining experience was wonderful including the atmosphere, selections, presentation, and wonderful wait staff.

I normally despise bread pudding but this experience taught me that bread pudding can not only be good but desirable.  I never thought I would be writing a review including how wonderful bread pudding can be.  This taught me one should never say they "despise" a dish until they find out how it's prepared.  Unless you have food allergies.  Then you should probably despise or at least stay away from whatever you're allergic.

I will definitely make sure I stop by Luke every time I return to New Orleans as it is well worth the trip.
It was excellent. Enjoyed the decor and ambiance.  Well mixed Sazerac.  Service was good.  We had a good time.

This place is great for happy hour! Their raw oysters are $0.75 each and their fried oysters are $1.25 each. My boyfriend and I shared a dozen of the raw oysters and a dozen of the fried ones. The raw ones are so incredibly fresh and they were huge! I've never seen oyster this big before. You definitely get the bang for your buck. The fried oysters are really good too- crispy and super flavorful. They come with a spicy, creamy dipping sauce. 

The restaurant also offered half off of selected drinks including wine by the glass, draft beers, and cocktails. I got the Gintilly Lace cocktail. I wasn't a big fan of this cocktail because it was super strong for my taste. I could only finish half- but if you're into strong cocktails, this one is for you. 

Overall, I'd highly recommend this restaurant for happy hour drinks and oysters! Such a great deal.
One of the only places open for Christmas Day brunch... Absolutely amazing! You have to try the crispy brussel sprouts and shrimp and grits.

Food was fantastic and the place itself is comfortable and cool. Would have been five stars except our service was super slow. Watched as couples next to us ordered, got food, ate and paid all before we got our entree. Oh we'll. I had the duck for my entree and absolutely loved it. Would go again in a heartbeat.

Glad they are friendly and having fun at work, but these kids play too much. Should have been in and out much quicker, but at least have the staff were just joking around (while what seemed like the new girl was left fending for herself on the line.)

We came for brunch and had the best shrimp n grits ever in my entire life!!!! And the other duck dish we had was also really good. Our server was really attentive and welcoming. The price is a bit on the higher side but since it's a hotel restaurant and has good vibes I wouldn't mind paying more.
With a great happy hour, a delicious burger, a blt with a literal fried crab on it, and killer margaritas, I would say this is one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans!

Kept me waiting for over an hour 
Always trying for the up sell and had to run out to the parts store for a filter

Cajun food with German flare!

We came here for breakfast on a Tuesday & there was no wait.

Friendly customer service, very attentive, & good food!

Southern Breakfast:  2 eggs, bacon, Andouille sausage, buttermilk biscuit, grits.  A hearty breakfast!  Very filling & delicious.
Yogurt Parfait:  A light yet filling meal to start off your day!

Best fried oysters ever. And best brussel sprouts ever. Hands down. No question. We wanted to get more food but weren't starving so we decided on fried oyster salad which came with a generous amount of oysters and were perfectly fried and with a perfect texture! The shrimp and grits was also just perfect and the brussel sprouts....I need that recipes- some magical honey balsamic vinaigrette w almonds and cheese on top.

I was at a conference in NOLA for a week, and Lüke was one of the restaurants I planned to visit. I waited about 20-25 mins for a table, but it was worth the wait. 

I did my typical thing by ordering an entrée, a cocktail, and a dessert. 

Entree: Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" (shrimp and grits)
Cocktail: French 75
Dessert: Bourbon Vanilla Bean Crème Brûlée (Soooo good!)
My friend's dessert: Steamed Chocolate (She really liked it.)

It was all delicious. I will totally go back the next time I'm in NOLA!

If your in New Orleans and looking for a great breakfast try Luke. One of Chef John Besh's great restaurants. We went in the morning and tried their "Shrimp & Grits". It was a blend of smooth, creamy grits mixed with a variety of cheeses, spices, andouille sausage, and shrimp covered by two perfectly cooked eggs. Fantastic! The coffee is some of the best ever for a restaurant: brewed individually using a French press. The restaurant is a few blocks from the French Quarter on the St. Charles St. trolley route in the Hilton Hotel. It was a little more expensive that I'd prefer. You honestly can't go wrong with anything on the menu - it's so hard to choose! Portions were large and filling. I highly recommend this restaurant for both expert, professional service and for the food. It didn't disappoint!
My favourite coffee shop in town.  Great coffee and super-friendly staff that will know you by name within a few trips.  Small location though, so don't come with the expectation of staying long.

The staff are wonderful. I went for a leisurely Friday lunch and loved the roast chicken. There is a reason this place's reputation is stellar. You won't go wrong. The space is quite charming, too. I've ordered oysters here in the past and haven't been let down. If it was possible to give more than five stars, I would.

I have been going to Elm Cafe since it opened. During this time, I've noticed the steady deterioration of quality and value of their offerings. I'm not sure if it correlates with the burgeoning Elm Cafe enterprise, but I suspect Elm Cafe has been a casualty of the business phenomenon of 'growing too fast' at the expense of other Nate Box businesses.  Simply put, Elm Cafe has lost what made it special in the first place and ceded that position to the likes of Farrow Sandwiches.

The final straw was being charged $9 for a lackluster parmesan chicken sandwich the other day. The green in the sandwich was limp and the chicken was dry and stringy, and overall lacking in flavor. I suspect the $7 pricing of sandwiches during 12 and 1PM is meant to offset the poor intrinsic value of Elm Cafe sandwiches. 

Once upon a time, Elm Cafe used to put out quality sandwiches for better pricing. Now they put out mediocre sandwiches for premium pricing. As a result, I will not be going back.
Rich!!! Fabulous dipping sauce for the beignets. Delicious, savory breakfast grits. They serve heavy cream for your coffee! Would definitely return!

This place is a joke.  The staff is rude, the tables are sticky, the room is nasty and dirty, and they claim to have free wireless internet but they lie.  Their wireless internet does not work. 

Never come to this place.  Waste of your time, energy, money and health.

Mint julep was strong!  The shrimp and grits was a bit salty but quite interesting and good.  The bread pudding was amazing.  Service was good but a bit slow.  Maybe hire more waiters?  Overall, very comfy experience.

We went to Luke for my birthday during our 8th annual  trip to New Orleans. We were disappointed that our dining experience was not as good as our first time at Luke's (both service and food). We walked into the place around 6 on a weekday, and the hostess told us we would be seated in a couple minutes, GREAT. We watched and waited. There were a good amount of tables available and we waited quite some time while we watched the other hostess chat with a fellow worker. Waited some more. 15+ minutes later when she was done talking, she came over to seat us. I believe it was the manager, who came over to apologize for the wait which was nice, since we were getting irritated. 

My wine glass came with wine spilled all around the top and bottom base of the glass and dripped on me when I picked it up. The handle of the glass was also all sticky. I had to wipe it clean with my napkin. At a higher end place like Luke you would expect it to be not dripping on you but it wasn't a big enough deal to mention to the waiter. 

Service was lacking this time around. To the 2 waiters' defense, they probably had 6 to 7 tables PLUS a big party in the party room so I know it was busy. But when you go to a place like Luke, you expect service to be a little more responsive. They probably should have had an additional designated waiter for the big party. We had empty water glasses 70% of the night and was never asked if we wanted more wine/drinks. And the 2 waiters were so busy they didn't have time to communicate with each other, so when we were helped, we were asked the same things twice in a row multiple times.

The food was just okay this time. The swordfish was dry, and the 2 burgers that our table got said they were average bar burgers. Okay but nothing special. 
The drum fish with meunière sauce didn't have the sauce on it, and when I asked the waiter about the sauce I was told there was, but he would get more. I grew up eating a massive amount of seafood and I can say there wasn't even a tiny hint of lemon or butter taste to the fish. Bread pudding was okay. Chocolate dessert was the only dish that was very good. 

I was not a happy camper for my birthday and I think the waiter sensed it so he didn't charge us for the bread pudding and also gave us the extra chocolate dessert. It would have been great if he could have came over to say that but I understand he was very busy with all the tables. 

After our second time here, Luke was okay, but for the money and just being okay I'm not sure if it's a place we would make a point to visit in New Orleans now. I was very happy with the gesture for the dessert so because of that, if someone wanted to go back to Luke I would. Maybe next time for us it would be better to order other things like oysters.
It hurts me to say this, because it makes me feel like I am betraying my seafood-centric hometown, but Luke has the best shrimp and grits I have ever had.

Friendly service and a brief but thoughtful menu. My dinner buddy enjoyed her etouffe, and I liked my stuffed pork chop, though I wouldn't have said no to a few more peaches mixed in with the veggies. They were so delicious with the sauce. Our desserts came faster than the cappuccinos, the appetizer never arrived, and the drink orders were a struggle - I'm not sure if that was on the kitchen or what, since the servers were friendly and bustling about the place. It wouldn't be a spot for quick meal but it would be a good one!

My wife and I went to Luke for an early lunch. The environment is relaxed and the service was top notch. Our waiter was very friendly and helpful, but not annoying. I ordered the brisket and my wife had a sandwich with ham, egg and cheese. The brisket was better than any I have ever had. It was served in a cast iron dish with potatoes and carrots: so simple, but done just right, tender and delicious. My wife loved hers and the few bite I had were very good. The prices were very reasonable and we will be back on our next trip to NOLA.

The place neighbors the Hilton hotel on St. Charles in the Business district. Nice location, clean. We went for breakfast around 0900 on a Sunday and there were plenty of tables. We were initially greeted not-so-enthusiastically, no smile and a monotones "I'll be with you shortly" then seated quickly. Wait staff was good, friendly and attentive. I'm a bit picky with appearances and was put off by the waiter's stained, dingy white coat. I feel that if you are going to serve food you should look spotless or at least wear dark clothing (to hide the inevitable food stains that can occur.) The shrimp and grits with eggs sunny side up were good and just what I had hoped for. My husband had the chicken and waffles and unfortunately wasn't happy. The chicken tasted like it had been prepped earlier and reheated. Parts of it were cold! The waffles were descent as we loved the pepper jelly that added to the sweet and savory appeal. The chicken just broke the whole meal. I don't think I'd be back but if I HAD to, I'd stick to the shrimp and grits and try out the breakfast sandwiches which looked like they were made to order. There are just too many better choices that are less pricey in the area.
Should be able to use real butter instead of hydrogenated oil in their dishes boo !!!!!
This is not a 2 $ place. Portion size was small and prices were large. Liked the food but would have liked more of it. Service was a little forgetful but friendly. Would not go back.

Outstanding food and just OK service.  Not my first time here and glad to see that the food is still as good as I remember.  I would have rated hie but the waiter was quite slow and desert too forever- Manager apologized but did not offer anything to compensate the 30 min wait for bread pudding.

Amazing service, amazing happy hour, amazing cocktails! Can't wait to go back to New Orleans and/or they open up a restaurant in San Francisco. 

When you go, definitely get a French 75 (made with cognac-yum!) and the oysters are superb -and a great happy hour price! 

Can't remember our servers names but both gentlemen were friendly and attentive. 

Go now!
We had lunch here while on vacation. All I need to say is that our food was amazing. The service was quick and courteous! I would absolutely eat here again!

Literally the best dining experience from start to finish! 
We came in dripping wet no reservations and thank god the amazing beautiful brunette hostess took pity on me. We got sat with Elliot and Richie Rich and I can't even describe the duo it was like a beautiful dance that we were a part of and add in Dede the manager who like everyone else is so kind, funny and helpful. They made my night. 
This was my first time ever in New Orleans and all I can say is this place is the epitome of southern hospitality. 
I had the best time with the best food I have ever tasted. I'm so happy we got lost and found this place in the rain. Thank y'all so much I'm never ever forget my first time in the south!
Damn good, Fresh seafood! Very reasonably priced too!!
Avocado and eggs over easy top this delish open-faced BLT with smoked bacon and toasted sourdough.  Brown butter waffles were light, fluffy, & crunchy on the outside.  Heavenly!

This restaurant is the lobby of the Hilton where we were staying.  We tried three times to get in for a before dinner snack and twice for dessert each time the hostesses were less than friendly and told us that the wait would be over 30 minutes as we were staring at multiple empty tables.  The hotel staff advised us to order room service and that we wouldn't be refused. So we decided to do that while we sat in the lobby and people watched.  The hotel staff had been wonderful the hostesses at Luke not so much. They are so rude.

[ Visited in October, 2010 ]

Lüke's is really a great place to have dinner with that special person, or with 7 other friends. The waitstaff is very attentive, food is EXCELLENT, and the environment is just romantic enough to impress that special person....should you need to (don't worry, they'll be impressed more with your excellent choice of cuisine). Check out the shrimp and grits because you cannot imagine how fantastic it is until that first fork of greatness enters your mouth.

Walk over to the Central Business District and go to Lüke's...it's worth it.

The service was kind of lack luster and the food was pretty good.

I would definitely recommend the baked PJ/ herbsaint oysters, they were delicious, they had a light breeding on then which consisted of herbs, bread and cheese. They were then lightly baked but not too long... They were still slightly raw. I thought it was delicious, and so didn't the other 3 that were with me.

We also had the hot boudin Louisiana 2which was actually really good too.

The étouffée was good, not amazing.

We also had raw oysters which were very good and lastly, the shrimp and grits... Which was probably the best entree.

Service was good. But the food was incredibly salty. Beyond anything I've ever eaten. We ate at quite a few other Cajun/Creole places during our time in New Orleans. This was by far the worst due to the amount of salt used.
Went there for a late desert. Cheese cake ... did not care for the after taste. Crumble... it was ok. Felt like my homemade was better. Seemed like a cool vibe great service just fell short on flavor

The food at this place was good but not great. The service was good but not great. The waiter was nice but forgot to ask what we wanted to drink, so we basically didn't get drinks. They didn't have many drink options so we didn't care too much. I had the pork chops, which seemed like the best thing on the menu. My girlfriend had the shrimp and grits, it was good. This place wasn't great because the menu didn't have a lot of options and they also had a lack of drink option. I don't understand any restaurant in the south that doesn't have sweet tea or a good lemonade.
Only 2 stars because everyone was nice other than that food was too salty and uncooked. I'm the type to not bother so I did not say anything, but, never again.
Food very good  - waitress had a bit of an attitude and rather spoiled the experience - Shawn just acted like she wasn't trying.

Poor breakfast spot. We asked for an americano and latte and they brought drip coffee and drip coffee with milk. I'd prefer some honesty that they don't have an espresso machine. Also no fresh orange juice.

Everything from the lady that sat us to the men that served us to the food and drink was excellent. Our reservation was for six but we were 15 min early. They sat us early and our waiter came over and got us oysters and happy hour drinks before it was over. It's always a great experience with the people that live in Nola. Tonight didn't disappoint. Thank you for the wonderful time Jon Besh. I have been wanting to try this place out. Glad we did! We will defiantly be back next time!

Very cool restaurant with old look, been there for lunch, got good portion of food, Luke burger actually was really good, mussels taste delicious as well. Little bit overprice for ragout and shrimps. But the rest so far so good.

This place is more casual than I initially expected, but it still has a nice ambience. My friend had the shrimp and grits (which was everyone's favorite) because it was packed with flavor. I had the chicken and it was a little dry for me. We also shared a bottle of wine. The prices were reasonable.

I had dinner last night with a group of people at Luke and it only reaffirmed my preference for this place. Started off the evening with a mint julep, my new favorite drink in the world, that was stupendously stiff. And then we received our raw oyster sampler - Louisiana, malpeque, beausoleil, and kumamoto. Talk about a vision of heaven! And they even had a mignonette sauce prepared (who wants crappy cocktail sauce)! I dove into the oysters with passion and they proved to be very salty, sweet, and savory. Spectacularly fresh were the oysters. 

I was going to order the cochon du lait sandwich, but our server said the 'special' version of this dish was cochon du lait with greens served over sausage cornbread dressing. Hmmm, okay, I'll bite on that. And did I ever bite on it! At first I thought the dish might have been a little overcooked (it was very hot), but that cochon du lait was so well seasoned and tender that I couldn't stop eating it. It actually was served as a cube shaped piece of meat with an outer 'skin' which was very tasty. 20 minutes later, my belly was full and plate nearly empty. Kudos for the presentation as well - the dish came out in a personal sized cast iron dish.

I thought the service was above average, but the timing seemed to be off as we waited really, really long time for dessert (bread pudding, yummy!). Place really got crowded later in the evening though, surprisingly crowded for a tuesday night. 

Still one of my favorite places in NOLA...

I basically have a crush on all John Besh restaurants and I LOVE that this place is open later than most!!

The beet salad is great!  I love the mix of blue cheese and pistachios.  It's a perfect appetizer to go with the bread they bring out.  I went for the bacon cheeseburger, fancy I know.  This thing was huge and so good.  The fries that come with it are small and thin so if you're into that you'll be all over it.  

I've been for brunch before a Saints game but since it was so crazy busy that day I can't judge the service too bad.  Everyone is distracted on football Sunday!  The waffle was delicious no matter how long it look.

I decided to come here 4 nights in a row to test out the various menu items. Happy hour is excellent w/ half-off oysters and bar drinks. That was a 5 star experience. 

The entrees each night were great. Definitely not the best I've ever had but very solid, dependable and great combinations of flavors. The salad of avocado, deep fried oysters, and thick cut smokehouse bacon was intense. The Wednesday lamb shank was terrific. 

Service was friendly although a little cliquish. Behind the Bar, Jessie was great - very client oriented. Thomas - arrogant, in-attentiive and rude, always acting like he's doing a favor by waiting on you. He should be fired.  

The bar side is definitely more fun than the sterile dining room side.    Sit at the bar near the waiter service window and you'll really here what's happening in NOLA.

Best shrimp and grits I have EVER had. And I usually don't care for grits. 
The portion is huge so I ordered half of it to be packed up to go.

You'll find water ice and custard at this Rita's, as well as a wait in line and few parking options (usually). There's nothing special here, just your standard offerings. There's no seating, but they do have pretzels.

Yum.

The food was delicious and the staff friendly and courteous. Hollywood Oysters raw bar and Shrimp & grits are the best that I have had to date!

Was in New Orleans on Business and pulled up Luke on Yelp. Decided to try it and it was great. Sat at the bar and ended up talking to the Oyster/ Sea Food specialist Phil for a while.
Hostness Shemoan (She-Moan) was very pleasant as well. 

I will be back.

Had the crawfish bisque and JUMBO LOUISIANA SHRIMP 
"EN COCOTTE".  Both were amazing!!  Definitely recommend this to locals and visitors of New Orleans.
Restaurant week menu had smaller portions, but overall very good.

My absolute favourite place to get a latte in Edmonton! Love their creative, thoughtful breakfast sandwiches and convenient location. wish they had more of a seating space so I could frequent it more often since I'm usually at a cafe to work on projects
Don't know what other reviewers are talking about. Food is fantastic. Like arguably the best Cajun/creole I have had in NOLA.

Amazing food. Had the Shrimp and Grits. Best I've had in New Orleans! I think it was our servers first day, or they were just short staffed that they had to pull someone from the back, but the service was just mediocre. I'll give 4 stars based off the food.

Another great recommendations by my buddy Mark! I went for brunch and I was blown away by the soft shell crab in a jar! An explotion of flavor from the first bite to the last. You have to try it!
