I was feeling a little adventurous and I I was rewarded handsomely. I saved a little room for the oysters and a cold glass of a local IPA and thank goodness I did. It was an overall great experience and I will be recommending this place to all my friends.

I have always selected from their refrigerator of always fresh pre-made boxes.   They have a good selection of rolls, piece sushi, and combo boxes to choose from.   A good variety standard sides as well Gyoza,  seaweed salad, edamame and the like.  If you arrive later in the lunch time the selection may be somewhat picked over.   Just grab and go when you are watching the time.   They also have counter service if you prefer to dine at a more leisurely pace on made to order offerings.   The price is very reasonable in comparison to other sushi joints.

We had a mixed experience here.  One dish was good enough to warrant our return.  One of them was good and the other tasty but missed the mark. There are two areas - the bar and a separate, quieter dining area.  The bar was crazy busy and deafening.  Luckily we'd made OpenTable reservations so we were able to get seated.  Unfortunately, it was in the bar area.  When I asked the hostess about eating in the quieter area, she said there was a wait (didn't say how long) and pretty much indicated that our table would be in the bar.  At first she sat us at a dirty table.  We were immediately moved to a ready table after I complained.  Minutes later we saw the couple that came in after us seated in the dining area.  WTF?!
The Food: we ordered the Flamenkuche - an Alsatian onion tart, for a starter.  This is one of the best things we've had anywhere.  Piled high with caramelized onions, rich cheese, crispy pork, and a beautiful crunchy crust.  It was too rich to finish - definitely too much for two people.  We ordered the shrimp and grits (jumbo shrimp "en cocotte") and a shrimp/blue crab ettoufee .    The shrimp/grits had a great flavor, but the kitchen was heavy-handed with the salt.  I like salty, but this was almost excessive.  The dish could've used 30% more grits and 30% less salt and it would've been great.
The shrimp/blue crab ettoufee was served over pasta, along with what seemed like melted butter, not much of a real sauce - we didn't taste the fennel.  The seafood in it was excellent, but there wasn't any balance to the dish - nothing to offset the richness.
We ordered a fig tart and got a cold apple one instead (almost seemed stale).  Not a good tart at all.  When we asked the waiter about it - he said they didn't have the fig tart.  He comped  a couple of our drinks to make up for the dessert - worked out well, but why don't they take the fig tart off of the menu?
This should be a four-star review, except for the screw up with the dessert, the lackluster hostess skills, and the mediocre ettoufee.

Truly a sad experience that left me wanting....
After being in a conference all day myself and 10 others went to Luke's to unwind and have dinner. Sadly one lady at our table received a cocktail with a baby fly who decided to do the back stroke in her drink (Why didn't the waiter look at her drink before serving it? Who knows?), our table waited two hours and thirty minutes, yes 2 and 1/2 hours to receive our meal and when the meal was presented three people received a cold platter of shrimp and grits and my burger was well done, not medium rare liked I requested. Overall, the service was so bad that the manager gave all 11 of us complimentary entries. I felt really sorry for our waitress because she had an opportunity to really make a great tip; nevertheless, it is what it is. I am sure Luke's is a great place to dine. Unfortunately, my first experience left me disappointed and desiring a better dining experience.

This was a very impressive establishment from the decor to the service. attentive  and helpful along with smiles & conversation. the food was tasty well prepared. finally tried shrimp & grits. 2 salutes

Top notch service and food every time! You can't go wrong with House of China. It's easy to call ahead or ever find something to do like Winn Dixie while you wait ten minutes. You can eat it there too I just always get it togo.

I love this bar! Great happy hour and awesome bar atmosphere. From oyster shuckers to the bar staff everyone is awesome!!! 

The shrimp and grits is the best in the city, hands down!
Excellent place for drinks after work. Everything I have ever had to eat here is amazing as well. Great atmosphere. Super attractive bar tender.

This place was amazing in every area.  The food was amazing: I recommend the  crawfish bisque and etoufee. Even better was the service. Nicest waitress ever and even the manager came by and greeted us. A+.
Wow, spent 200 bucks on food that had  NO FLAVOR. From crab legs to soup, boring and tasteless.  Hostess totally forgot about us. Not worth the $$$ or time

Loved this little find. Had a great dinner late night. Some really good gumbo, decent coq-au-vin, amazing crab raviolis. Really good drinks (mint julep, yum!) and good creme brulee, though I prefer mine warm... Theirs was cool.
Really nice atmosphere. I'd definitely go back and recommend to those traveling through NOLA looking for a decent meal at a not-so-steep price.

This restaurant is one of the BEST! I was disappointed that the 4 days I was in NOLA, that I didn't run into this gem until the night before I would leave. I came here with family but sampled everything, the crab and corn soup is amazing. My mother had amandine fish Was good but she was jealous with my order which was the swordfish. BEST fish I've had. Packed with flavor and will not disappoint. 

The next day was brunch here at Luke's since Dinner was so yummy. We ordered the chicken waffles, crab omelet, shrimp and grits and got a kids burger. Tried everything was impressed and glad I got to try everything because I would be stuck choosing. The kids burger was out of this world and has this smoky flavor . Highly would recommend!! Service is great. Get the tables in the back with the view of the chefs cooking the food.
We only had oysters and beers but I love this place. Friendly staff, the oysters were big and delicious, and the guys behind the bar even snuck us some extra. I'd go back!
Brunch! The bar knows how to make a drink. The menu is chalked full of fun treats to boost your sundayfunday.
I recently went to Luke for happy hour. Oysters are $0.50 a pop and HUGE! I ate a dozen and was beyond stuffed.  The cocktails are half off for happy hour and nice and strong  :-)  Highly recommend!

Nice new addition to Chalfont.  Walked down from the office today for lunch.  I am pretty sure the owner was our server.  Ordered a plate full of Sushi, had some Gyoza, and tried my colleagues Chicken Pad Thai.  Everything was fresh and delicious.

The atmosphere is minimal, but upscale.  I thought I was in a Sushi bar in the city, or NY.

BYOB will be nice for that early dinner after work.  Come soon and often.  We need this place to succeed.

No. 7 Volcano Roll was just the right amount of spicy.  The rest of the Sushi was fresh, and well prepared.

This is one of my favorite spots for Happy Hour.  We stopped by yesterday after watching the Southern Decadence parade.  The hostess was lovely and offered us a table but my partner and I choose the nearly empty bar.  In no time at all, we had two dozen raw oysters at 50 cents each with half price drinks.  The new River Bend cocktail is delicious and there's always good beers on draft.  It's a great location, and a terrific happy hour (3-6 pm daily) spot.
I got the turkey with brie sandwich today. It had buffalo chicken in it. Otherwise it was delicious. I also had the lentil soup which I must say is some of the best I've had in a long time!

Excellent restaurant and exceptional staff. My husband and I are in new Orleans to celebrate his bday and our anniversary. I knew about Luke's because  it is located next to our hotel. We almost didn't eat here because I figured we probably wouldn't need a reservation on a Sunday night. Well I was wrong, when we saw the hostess she made us aware the wait time for a party of 2 was an hour. I called another restaurant and it was the same. I decided we would go somewhere and get a  drink in the meantime and exactly an hour later our table was ready. 
I am so happy we were finally able to get in because the food was delicious. I ordered the duck and my husband the seafood etouffee, both dishes were extremely flavorful. The fried rice that comes with the duck will amaze your taste buds and your senses, I wish I could learn to make it at home. I asked my waiter if they could bring dessert with a candle for my husband and they not only did that but they also brought us two glasses of champagne for our anniversary. I didn't get their names but thank you for making that night a little more special.
Elizabeth and Tristan were amazing!! And the thanksgiving dinner was excellent. Terrific service, delicious meal. Try the Sazerac cocktail to start and the Kumanmoto oysters if they have em.

Went to Luke for breakfast after finding rude people at one place and an hour and half wait at another. This popped up on yelp as being close, good, and a John Besh place. We were able to get a table right away (around 10:30 am on a Sunday). Husband went for the shrimp and grits - very good. The grits were buttery and cheesy. Shrimp were spicy. Add the egg - good call. I went for the cajun breakfast or something that was eggs, bacon, potatoes, and a biscuit. The best part was the awesome blueberry compote that came with the biscuit (and i don't love fresh blueberries). SO good (even if it did make my teeth blue-ish). And, the breakfast potatoes were great! 
Service started off good then our waiter vanished (coffee refills were challenging). But, a mgr did come by and was helpful and apologetic. 
Big props to Luke (and Besh) for doing a tent (on veterans day) providing free food and drinks to Marines - very cool. 
Overall - breakfast at Luke was quite good and i would go back to try more.

Third time here. I ordered over the phone and was told 30 min wait, no problem...50 min later no food and informed I need to wait an additional 25 min. Unacceptable. I try to make my point that the delay should have been fully explained and to allow me to make the decision to wait or move on. Now I have no lunch and wasted an hour of my day and to insult to injury, I was treated poorly and the Muslim sister was rude and ignorant. Poor communication and a bad attitude, just lost my business for good.

A concierge highly recommended this restaurant.  It was solid-good.  I would not say out-of-this world great. I found the gumbo to be fair at best. My shrimp and grits entree was very good. The wine list was good with nice selections by he glass. Service was very good.  No reason not to eat here, but frankly nothing that would make me want to go back either.
My friend was having lunch there and I went to meet her.  I only tried the desert. It was a very good bread pudding. I will be back to try the whole meal next time I'm in New Orleans.

I totally disagree with some of the comments below. I have always been treated with respect on the phone and by the drivers when they arrive at my home. My pizza is usually here within 20-25 minutes, hot and fresh. Highly recommend!

So we at Luke which was across the street from our hotel. We have eaten here on other trips but decided to review it this time around. We sat the bar and was helped with drink choices by our very great bar tender. She recommended the drinks all of which were nicely made and interesting. We started with the brussel sprouts which have to be the best we ever had anywhere. They print the receipt as many ask for it. Seems to be laced with pepper jam, bacon and sliced apples. Really ensure you have some when you try Luke. Also ate the redfish which was good, just a little wet from too much butter. Then we had the mussels which are always very good. Bread pudding was good but not special. We will eat here again and at John B's other restaurants in NO.

This place is so good I had to go twice in 3 days. Even my 3 year old was going nuts over their mac n cheese (from the children's menu) which was amazing. The people who served us were as awesome as the food. Even the chef (Blake) stopped by our table and said "hi." He was complimented by two thumbs up from our little one. We had a Luke burger, crawfish etouffee, roasted jalapeno grits, bread pudding, beignets, fried chicken biscuit. All were awesome but the etouffee was the best!
Fabulous! The service was great! Super friendly staff. The bread pudding and molten chocolate cake are delicious. Gumbo was seasoned to perfection. We will definitely be back again!
Fantastic food at Luke. Strong, custom cocktails too. Spaetzel, beet salad, shrimp and grits.

The Happy Hour is an absolute must for oysters lovers! HH is Mon - Fri 3 pm to 6 pm. $0.75 per fresh oyster is hard to beat. The oysters are of a very good size and are fresh. All the drinks are half off!!! The drinks are really good! The bar is small though and gets crowded very fast. Please note that HH is at the bar area only. Service was alright, but they were crazy busy.

How do you go to a Hotel restaurant and they remember you... remember your name and your favorite drink... even though they see sooooooo many people DAILY...  they always take really good care of us here... I've had just about everything on the menu... the Steak is amazing... shrimp and grits off the chain... all the drinks are crazy... oysters for Happy Hour... the Brussell sprouts are awesome... and the service is AMAZING... Huge shout out to my man Richie Rich who always takes really good care of us each time we come! My favorite restaurant in NOLA thanks to the incredible staff and amazing food! Looooooove Luke!

This was our first meal in NOLA and quite possibly the best. We went to happy hour and were seated right away. You can call ahead. We had my 13 year old son with us. Not many kids there and definitely not a lot of options for picky eaters, but my son had an AMAZING burger and fries that he was happy with. Hubby started with dozen raw oysters and loved them so much he ended up eating 3 doz and decided to forgo ordering a meal. They didn't judge, just kept them coming. Big, plump fresh delicious oysters with cocktail sauce and fresh grated horseradish. He was in heaven. Yum!
I had the shrimp and grits. I don't have adequate words for how much I enjoyed this dish. I've had shrimp and grits in many places and these were special. The shrimp were big and so fresh and perfectly cooked. The grits were creamy and cheesy and absolutely delicious. Savory and decadent. It was perfection! 
We finished with the bread pudding at our servers recommendation. It was phenomenal. It was hot and sweet and gooey and delicious. I would have liked a bit more ice cream but nonetheless delicious. My picky son even enjoyed it and was digging in the corners of the bowl for every last bite.
Luke was a phenomenal experience for us and at this price point was comparable to some of the other touristy type seafood places that can not even compare to the food quality and the creativity and execution of the meal that Luke offers through their menu. I withheld the 5th star bc we had 3 different servers throughout the meal. Not sure why that was but we did have to wait quite a bit for drinks and refills at one point while our first server was talking and laughing and promptly getting drinks for the table next to us.

I wish I had read these before I got involved with this company. My heating unit broke on a Sunday 2/7/15-and I could not get a call back from my regular company so I googled and found this company.  They came out right away and I thought it was a good fit since they were local.  It was freezing so I didn't have time to search prices. I purchased a unit and their package came to 8400.00... they removed the old unit and installed a Williamson-the unit shot water out in my basement within an hour of the technician installing and leaving, he came back 2 hours later and said it was fixed, the next day there was another problem/ they sent a different technician.  It worked ok for 5 days, I went away for the weekend, when I returned on Sunday (2 days later) the house was freezing, the unit off.  They sent a different technician-the next day. He got it working but 3 radiators are cold. He couldn't figure out why. Today is Tuesday-the service manager said someone would call or be here first thing. It is now almost 11 AM-I've been waiting since 7-I finally called them at 9-their technicians are busy with other calls. The company manager said he was more annoyed than me because he was losing money! I guess I wasn't a priority since they already have my money, which was several thousand over what seems to be the going rate. (The staff has been nice and I haven't found them unprofessional, although the owner Joe did give me a bit of a lecture about light switches and the receptionist was a bit rude to me the first time I called.)  They finally fixed it!

Every time we come to New Orleans, Luke is a MUST. We requested Rich as we always do and once again we had the best service and food! We tried the CRISPY BRUSSELS SPROUTS and they were some of the best I have ever had. I have always looked forward to the beet salad in the past but since they changed up their menu I tried the BURRATA & HEIRLOOM TOMATO SALAD which was just as delicious if not better! Luke will never disappoint and we will continue to go every time we visit New Orleans. Thanks again to Rich for making my husband's birthday dinner so much fun!
Nice atmosphere, pleasant people, excellent friendly service and great cocktails at reasonable prices. BUT... be warned, the food here is mediocre at best

This place was awful. Freezing cold, almost idiotic staff and really bad food. I mean BAD. My meat was tough, the spaetzle was dry and flavorless, the wine was no good, and my dining partners sandwich seemed as if it was a joke. It was huge, covered in cheese and almost inedible in size and flavor. I cannot begin to even fathom where these good reviews are coming from, or how they can justify these prices. I really would have rather eaten fast food than this crap.

Walked in on a Saturday night and sat at the bar. Fantastic service all around! Our bartender was friendly and she had us try the bread pudding which was delicious. 

-Tasty fried oyster salad (with bacon!)
-bead pudding was warm and moist
I've had the oysters there in the past and they are great.
Best raw oysters I have ever eaten. The horseradish mixed with the cocktail sauce was superb. This is a definite must at happy hour for .75 cent oysters and half price drinks.

WAAAAH. I wish I lived downtown so I could be closer to this gem of a sandwich shop. Barely larger than a closet, this cafe boasts some of the best sandwiches in the city -- and if the duck confit sandwich I had the other day was any indication, then they certainly have lived up to the acclaim. SO GOOD IT DESERVES ALL CAPS.

One of my biggest pet peeves with sandwiches are the bread-to-filling ratio (often overwhelmingly bread, barely any insides), and Elm somehow got it right. Great, crusty bread, too! I also got their last "Turtle" muffin -- apparently, sourced from Duchess (as we all know is one of my faves) but baked and put together in-house. FANtastic.

They only lose one star due to the size constraints, which is partially made up by their patio outside... just wish there was a wee more elbow room and sitting space because I would love to bring clients and such for meetings here.

45 min wait for a table, for a Saturday lunch after Christmas, so we sat at the bar. The burger was built around a generous and juicy charbroiled patty. The fried oyster salad featured large chunks of fatty artisinal bacon and was equally tasty, though the dressing was uninspiring.

I went here this past weekend with a girl friend of mine. I had a great experience that was due to the food and company!

I reserved my table on OpenTable for 7:15 pm and arrived there for 7:05. I was seated right away all the way to the back of the restaurant. I arrived a little earlier than my friend and was waited on right away! The service is excellent! We had 2 waiters that waited on us throughout the night, so we were never waiting for our drink refill or any requests to be fulfilled. When my friend dropped her silverware on the floor, without even asking, the waiter brought her a new one within a couple of minutes! Talk about prompt service!! We hadn't even had the chance to ask for a new one. I guess he saw it and brought it right away! That's never happened at a restaurant before (well, not so quickly at least).

We started off with drinks. I ordered the Champagne au Peche and she ordered the St. Charles Streetcar, which was divine! I ordered two more of those streetcars that night! 

What we ordered:
-P&J oysters. A must try!!!! I don't care for Drago's oysters much. My favorite oysters were from Borgne (another Besh restaurant), which are similar to these. However, now these are my favorite! The oysters aren't over cooked while the topping is perfectly cooked and crisp! SO GOOD!!!!!!!!! And trust me, I know my oysters. I can eat 2 dozen raw anyday (minimum). 
-Terrine of slow cooked foie gras with brioche and sea salt. This is a slice of foie gras and probably my favorite spread of the night. The brioche was great! Crispy yet soft. The perfect combination with the foie.
-Assiette de Charcuterie. This was the charcuterie board that had the most variety. Along with the rabbit pate (which was divine), hogs head cheese, and something else that I had forgotten by now (I don't know if it's due to the wine or old age, haha), it also came with stone-ground mustard, house-made pickles,  and pickled watermelon (different and delicious!)

I had a great experience here. Atmosphere was sometimes loud then sometimes a little quieter, but remained a constant energized and happy ambiance. There were tables of families, dates, friends, groups; variety of people. Would definitely come here again. I want to try the escargot!

I have dined here three times and find the food and service to be flawless. Outstanding seafood selections and perfect steaks.   Round out the meal with a beautifully prepared cocktail and you will get the full treatment.
Excellent service and best duck breast I ever enjoyed!!! Dined there during Mardi Gras and was still packed with locals.

There is no other place to get take out in Lutz, FL except here. Living here for 20+ years, we have seen multiple renditions of take out places around the area and the great food coming out of this joint cannot be beat. 

We haven't had one order that had issues or lacked taste (maybe it's luck but I think it's quality service). 

I've done both eating in, and take out. However most of the locals choose take out as this is always a go-to option with consistently great food. One thing that I always enjoy is at the end of the ear, or beginning of the new year, they always offer complementary calendars to their customers. It's something I look forward to every year and just gives a sense of gratitude to customers. 

When focusing on the menu, everything is great.... My favorites are the veggie egg rolls, honey chicken, and wonton soup. Soooo yummy and always consistent. 

One change to report is that they seem to be changing their shop hours to close on Sunday.

Amazing service! The crawfish bisque is a MUST. We had the fried chicken with rice and beans it was delicious. The beans have brisket and a Cajun flavor. The portion is large enough to share - we also had the praline bread pudding dessert. No complaints would definitely recommend this to anyone visiting NOLA!

Happy hour has 75 cent oysters and half off drinks! Can't go wrong with that!
fantastic food, very efficient and friendly wait staff I would definitely eat here again

Decided to try out Lüke's since it was next door to the hotel I was staying at.
The hostess seemed surprised that I didn't want to sit at the bar because I was alone. Three parties were seated before me, but I was finally seated after waiting 10-minutes.
The server took a while to get to me and only showed up sporadically to check on me, but was very friendly when he did show up.
Started off with the Blue Crab Bisque - nice flavor and nice helping of crab.
For an entrée I had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte". Wow!!! The shrimp was very flavorful... The grits were absolutely wonderful!!!

I come here often and have never been disappointed. Staff are friendly, food is always hot and fresh and they always get my order correct. The location isn't the best but it's worth the hassle getting in and out for such yummy food and smoothies.

Best German food I have ever had.  Period !!!!!!!

The service was top notch and beer selection was on spot.  

Thanks
Great decor and service at this trendy spot.  I had the gumbo and the shrimp and grits.  All was excellent flavor and well prepared.  I don't even like grits and I cleared the plate!

The food at this place is excellent. All the food we ordered tasted great and had nice flavor. We ordered the roasted chicken with potatoes, pork chop, and cheese burger and chicken tenders for the kids.  They have a good kids menu and the portion was pretty good. The staff was attentive and friendly. This place is a bit pricey and it's best to make a reservation before you go there.

For a Sunday night, this place was sort of happening.  There weren't any festivals going on nor were there a lot of people walking around so we couldn't really find a restaurant that was open at 10pm at night.  This place was not only open, but also somewhat full.  It was lively with a nice atmosphere.  The food was pretty decent.  We weren't that hungry so we had soup and brussel sprouts.  I had a bowl of seafood gumbo; the portion size looked small, but it was just enough for a late night bite.  My friend had the matzo ball roasted chicken soup and enjoyed it.  We order the brussel sprouts with cheese and marcona almonds.  They were delicious- a bit oily, but nice and crispy and browned.  We asked for the brussels without the honey vinegarette and the staff was able to accommodate our request.  The bread served wasn't really warm and it seem a bit undercooked; it wasn't nice and brown on top and wasn't worth the carbs!  

The dessert selection looked delightful, but we didn't partake.  :(  Other tables around us ordered oysters and other dishes which looked really good so I think this place is worth going to late at night on an off night if you want a light meal or a big meal.

The restaurant is located right outside the French Quarter in the CBD. We haven't been disappointed with any of the food we've eaten in New Orleans and Luke is one of the best meals I've had... ever. 

The food came out ridiculously fast.... literally 5-7 minutes after we ordered, which is amazing since the restaurant was pretty much full. The service was impeccable and very on point and was a joint effort during our entire meal. Everyone seemed to be more than willing to help and we didn't feel like we had to specifically look for our server. I love places like that. 

We ordered some raw oysters which were of course very fresh. The gumbo was also an excellent choice. After reviewing the pictures and reviews, we had to order the Brussels sprouts and we're so glad we did. Definitely the best Brussels sprout dish ever! I was tempted to order another serving to take home.  The shrimp and grits was also very tasty although the extra $12 for the truffle mushrooms wasn't really worth the price since we didn't really taste it. Otherwise, the shrimp and the grits themselves was absolutely delicious. 

Overall a very pleasant dining experience that I would definitely recommend to everyone. I'd say it's a must-eat if you're visiting NOLA.

So glad I decided to check out the .75 cent happy hour Oysters!  Happy hour from 3-6 half price drinks too. 
Got there at 5:00.  Was seated immediately.  They did ask if we had reservations which we didn't.  
Ok, you guessed it, started out with 1 dozen fresh oysters.  So good.  Plump and juicy.  Chilled to perfection!  We had to do it and go for another dozen.  Just as good as the first patch.
Our waiter had a weird way about him.  Was attentive, but never made eye contact.  I felt like he wasn't listening to me or that he might not get the order right but he did! Just wish he looked at me when I ordered my drinks or meal.  Funny thing is he was singing and dancing by the bar waiting for the order, but then a standoffish attitude by the table?? A weird way about him like he didn't want to be waiting tables, but was good at it? I Saw this with other tables.  His assistant, was excellent.  True charm, & professionalism.  With that being said, the manager made her way over to make sure all was fine, and that our needs were met. 
For our entree we both ordered the Ribeye.  Cooked to perfection!  Came with your choice of sides, and we both went with seasonal vegetables.  They were grilled fresh, served in cast iron.  Incredible!  That steak was incredible! The meal was incredible!  So impressed with the food. 
I usually don't give out 4 stars unless I'm that impressed!  I was impressed by the food.  Lost points  for the noise level, and for our waiter.  A shame.  this place was so close to making my first 5 star review!  Close, but no cigar!

My boyfriend and I went here last week just to try out for dinner. I don't know because we came in a little late but the servers didnt give us the service like an upscale restaurant suppose to be. They put us in a corner all the way at the end where it was so dark that we had to ask for better seats, and they wasn't busy at all. Then we had to ask for our plates because the guy forgot to give us when they served the bread and butter. On top of that, all the servers was messing around, talking, laughing really loud to each others. They even started to punch each others, chasing around right infront of our table. The food was ok that why I have two stars. Don't know if we should come back

Came here on a Friday night with a bachelorette party. We originally had a reservation for 8pm, but called around 6 to request a later time, and they accommodated 7 of us at 9:15 easily. 

Upon arrival, we were greeted by the manager, and immediately served complimentary champagne. We sat towards the back of the restaurant, and it was very private. 

Our server, "Richie Rich" was amazing. He made friendly conversation, suggested entrees and drinks, and brought warm bread with the waters.  I ordered the Poulet- Grande-mere, which was herb roasted chicken, summer veggies, and whipped potatoes. It was delicious and filling. I ordered the Streetcar drink, which was also very good. 

I was impressed with their service and attentiveness, as well as the ambiance and clean restrooms. I paid for the bachelorettes' and myselfs' dinner, and it was less than $100. I would recommend eating here when in NOLA.
Neve had an issue with delivery or food here.  Great place for delivery and food.  Food is always hot and timely.
Will be coming back to Luke on my next trip to NOLA. Pâté plate & the shrimp & grits was superb. Service was great.

Had the Southern Breakfast.  The creamy grits were outstanding, the eggs were poached perfectly, the sausage (sage, cane sugar or maple syrup--don't remember) was outstanding; just a touch of sweetness.  Pots of French Press coffee delivered to your table...a bit weak for my taste, by excellent blend.  Would love to go there for lunch and/or dinner next trip.

This was our first meal in NOLA. I wanted to try out a Besh restaurant, and this one was the closest. The overall experience was great. I had the crawfish bisque that was absolutely delicious. There were even bits of seafood in it, which you don't usually find. I had the Amberjack special, which was a nice chunk of thick fish covered in a crawfish sauce. Needless to say it was delish. We had two waiters so we never had an empty glass of anything. Definitely a must try.

Food was authentic. Oysters local and the strawberry ale was the best!!!! Tried the gumbo, it was ok. Tried the rabbit and duck liver pate and it's good if that's your thing. But inexpensive so it's worth trying. Great service friendly atmosphere.

Service is always great. Which is why it gets three stars.


The food and menu have taken a dive though.  I've eaten here at least 6-8 times over the years
 
It used to be really great.

The steak was Just salty, Pork Schnitzel had no flavor, gumbo also just eh.... Not worthy.

The menu has been chopped down to what seems like bar food.

Not sure what happened here!? 
Everything used to be excellent.

You can do a lot better for your money in this town

If you want  to try a John Besh restaurant but are looking for a more laid back experience, I think Luke is the restaurant for you.  I like that the menu still tries to incorporate some southern dishes (ie:Gumbo) but if you've been in NOLA for a few days I'm sure you're looking for a little change of pace.  

For starters they serve fresh baked french bread.  I have to admit this bread was better than anything I've had all weekend.  If only all Po Boy's could be made with fresh baked bread....  I recommend adding one of the soups as well.  I made an effort to try as many Gumbos in NOLA and Luke's did not disappoint.  

If you are a meat lover, you will love the Choucroute Garnie Maison (smoked pork shank, Mangalitsa belly & bratwurst, house-made sauerkraut).  This dish can easily serve 3.  I'm just a big fan of Mangalitsa anything so this was a no brainer for me.  The smoked pork shank was tender and the meat was falling off the bone.  Very rarely will I ever leave any food on the plate but it was too much...I could not finish this dish.

My gf ordered the Etoufee of Blue Crab & Brown Shrimp (fennel, garlic, saffron fumet, handmade garganelli).  It's not your typical Saucy Etoufee with rice, intstead it's a light pasta dish but you have to love the fresh garganelli.      

Whatever you do, make sure to leave room for Brendan's Bread Pudding.  It's pretty good.

I would have given Luke a 5 star review had it not been a rowdy table that ruined the 1st half of our meal.  Instead of throwing the drunk diners out, they just moved everyone from the back dining room to the front.  A small apology was given but nothing material to make up for the unpleasant experience.  I just expected more from a John Besh restaurant.
Food was tasty and portions were large sizes. I went during lunch so they have lunch special which I recommend!! Ambiance is a bit fancy and most of the customers dress nicely to go eat here.

We had two very different experiences here. A 3 star with mediocre service and not so great oysters and a 5 star with the best service and huge, juicy oysters - hence the 4.  They have a great happy hour special with half off cocktails and 50 cent oysters, which was great.  A local told us about the deal. Go from 3-6 pm every day.

160/365

Came here for happy hour after the game. The person seating the customers looked completely overwhelmed. She sat people who were behind us first. Then lied to make excuses for not being able to keep track of everyone.  Would've like to try this place out, but the management has no idea how to seat customers :o
Occasionally the employees aren't the nicest, but the food  and coffee are solid at all times of day.

If you are looking for a real New Orleans food experience without pretentious of fancy pants items on the menu this would be a great choice. At first glance it looks like a bar but the mouth-watering display of oysters, crab legs and shrimp front-and-center when you walk in will tip you off to its real purpose. 

Lüke is buzzy, fun and the food, delicious. Diners at our table had everything from the etouffee to then fried oyster salad and all of it was delicious. They had an excellent selection of local beers, too.

Casual, lively, great service and all at a reasonable price. When next in NO, we'll be back.

I was in the mood for a fancy burger and the one at Lüke was pretty damn tasty and seemingly the size of a VW hubcap.

Good fries, skinny and crispy.

I was also half buzzed, so I started my meal off with the boudin noir.  It was decent, but easily overshadowed by the diced apples and bacon it was served with.  If I could just eat a skillet of those, I'd be a happy camper.

My only gripe is the accompanying condiments...really?  Teeny room service bottles of Heinze mayo, ketchup, and mustard?  I know you share a space with the Hilton, but how about some house made shit?
Excellent sushi,  very well made, fresh and tasty. Inside is clean, well decorated and the staff is very friendly. The only downside was the music was a bit too loud.

When we walked in, this place reeked of beer, you can tell it's been there forever. It was a great place to watch some Sunday football games, but the waitress complained to us that they wouldn't let her put up any games but the Eagles on the main TVs at the front of the bar. It was ok, we watched on the TVs towards the back and sat at a high top. It is a comfortable bar, and the appetizer sampler we got was really pretty good. The chicken wrap we got was completely inedible. It was soaked in honey mustard and chicken was dripping in oil. Gross! The turkey club we had was super dry but was ok. I think it probably would've been safer to stick to typical bar food. The service was great, but I probably would just go to drink and watch a game rather than eat!

Amazing. Started out with happy hour oysters (raw and fried) and drinks. Great draft beer selection and mixed drinks options. Ordered burger and frammenkuchen. Both were amazing. Never thought I'd order a burger for dinner at a NOLA restaurant but this was worth every bite. Spent $100 and left extremely full and satisfied. I've been here for brunch and it was just as great. Can't wait to return. Great food, great atmosphere.

One of the best Restaurants we tried during our recent vacation. I had the Thursday special and OMG it was AWESOME. Mu daughter had the shrimps and grits and it was great too. When in New Orleans this is a must try.

We came here for brunch with a large bachelorette party. I couldn't quite corral all 13 attendees at our reservation time but I called and they were able to accommodate my request of pushing the reservation back 30 minutes. Our waitress (name started with a K, maybe Kayla) was very nice and attentive. Our food came out quickly and was extremely good!!

Great food, great ambiance. Service was great. The gumbo and matzo ball soups were awesome, as were the fries. The breakfast plates were delicious and more than enough food to make you super full :) We will certainly be going back on our next trip to New Orleans!

I feel like I should have come here for dinner! We stopped by for breakfast. The shrimp and grits were amazing (high calorie).  According to the waiter it's also his favorite dish and that it's even better with crawfish during the season for it! I like dark roast coffee. I think the roast used in their press is lighter. My husband had the Southern breakfast and the biscuit was too mushy. I would replace it with toast. Hope this helps breakfast hunting!

I love Chipotle. Fresh ingredients, tasty recipes. I usually get the burrito bowl with steak. It's really good and you won't be hungry for a long time. If you aren't concerned with calories, get a burrito b/c the tortillas are perfect. 

I can't give this place 5 stars b/c it is a chain. But, as far as chains go, this one is awesome.

What can I say, it's cheap, easy, fast and simple while still being relatively healthy.  It's not really Mexican despite being based on Mexican cuisine.  It's more of a Gringo restaurant.  At least I know I can go into one in Manhattan or Indy and get the same thing.  The only difference being one has a longer line.

I went to Luke solo for lunch on Monday.  I was in town for a conference that had all day sessions and really no time built in for lunch.  But I really wanted to try this place so I headed there at noon.  I had no trouble being seated even though I had no reservation (I doubt this would work as well for dinner).  The place was busy but not crowded.  My server was fantastic.  When I asked for a Pilsner he suggested their home brew which was excellent.  I had the sausage platter (Plat Lyonnaise).  So much food!  The sausages were great and the potato lyonnaise even better.  And I was done in time to make it back for the 1:15 PM sessions.  The restaurant is in the business district and I noticed the lunch crowd seemed mostly business, not tourist.  And it did clear out by 1 so they must be used to serving a business crowd there on their lunch hour.  I would definitely go back, hopefully for dinner next time.

What a great find. Located in CBD we were overall exhausted with The French Quarter restaurants, Luke offers a daily happy hour from 3-6. I love that they only serve local beers. Try their own brew, very tasty. I also had the whiskey cocktail with basil and balsamic vinegar. Excellent combination that will definitely get you where you need to be!  We had several dozen raw oysters and the fried oysters were to perfection  Waitstaff very friendly and helpful.  Restaurant Is a mix between New Orleans and New York.  Great find!

For a time, I came to Cosi every single day and ordered the Signature Salad with chicken. It really never gets old. It's hard to find healthy options around campus, but Cosi is right near the library and was always reliably quick and yummy. I particularly enjoyed eating the bread samples while waiting in line. I've also tried the TBM melt and the BBQ chicken pizza. Also delicious! The bread is baked fresh daily (you can see it from where you order), and I like to treat myself on occasion to the specialty drinks (mojito lemonade, raspberry iced tea). Similar to Panera, but it has its own charm.

First meal we had in NOLA did not disappoint. For lunch, we started off with crab bisque and the rabbit liver pate. Both delicious! The serving of pate was more than enough for the two of us. My friend had the boulettes d'agneau which is the daily special. I took on the louisiana shrimp and grits, delicious and flavorful. The last bites tasted heavy with salt. We enjoyed the casual and nostalgic ambience.

The baked P&J oysters were great. The crust was just right and the seasoning was spot on. I'm not even a fan of oysters, and I thought this was great. For my main course, I had the duck. To be honest, I thought the breast was slightly underdone, but the duck leg was cooked just right. My party split the creme brulee and bread pudding for dessert. Both were tasty, though the bread pudding stood out more for me.

In terms of the experience-to-price ratio, Luke's breakfast asymptotically approached zero.

Our initial cup of coffee was, not ironically, lukewarm. It was eventually replaced, but only sporadically filled. (It bears mentioning that our server was managing exactly two tables.) The toast also was no better than room temperature - incidentally about 65 degrees - and it was replaced as well. The yogurt and granola featured no more than three tablespoons of insubstantial, powdery granola and perhaps half a cup of berries for $12. This stood in stark contrast to the previous evening's uniformly outstanding experience at Emeril's, at which no detail was overlooked.

The server predictably made no accommodation on our bill for either transgression, and so it was that we left $34 poorer, literally and metaphorically.

Nothing wrong with their pizzas. They overcook 'em like the chain has been doing for years. I have a problem with this particular location's management. They have never once honored a coupon that we receive in our neighborhood circulars because they are for other Domino's stores, but they don't send us any of their coupons, and they are the only store in our delivery area. So instead when you say you have a coupon for such and such deal, they start hmming and hawing about, "Well, I don't see that we have that available." They then proceed to offer you a deal that is twice as expensive. Eventually they would offer something similar that they were running and maybe we would accept. Their pizzas arrived hot and burnt as usual, and since I was a regular customer, they knew where in my development my house was so they no longer needed directions. I always paid by check. 

Now they flat out refuse to honor any deals, only offer menu price when I call and refuse to accept my checks. I have never ever written a bad check, or even floated one for that matter. I asked for an explanation and they said that their manager was tired of making special arrangements for folks. 

Well, I'm sorry Mr. Manager, but I've worked for a place that has a restaurant. Special orders and arrangements is how we make money. If we refuse the special arrangements, then we are refusing business. The customer will take his business elsewhere and then write a scathing review on Yelp, which will take away more business. Now ask yourself, was the refusal to bend worth going broke?

Easy pick--shrimp and grits. It's a southern staple and it is done really well here. You won't hear this often...the butter is outrageously good. That's right, the butter that comes with the mini baguette is actually memorable. 

One knock...the gumbo. Specifically, the shrimp IN the gumbo. I suppose since it is made in huge vats and sits, the shrimp gets mealy, otherwise I would actually suspect that it's *gasp* frozen. Great flavor, but the texture of the shrimp is a big turn off.

Amazing, all the gals enjoyed their dishes, but the crowd pleaser for the evening were their burger and the cheese grits with shrimp. I still think of those grits and wish I was back in New Orleans! Service was excellent and I had the best bachelorette week during Mardi Gras!

Disclosure: this review was written for their happy hour $1 oysters.  

The ambiance was a kind of French-bistro feel, reminding me of the likes of Thomas Keller's Bouchon, which gave me high hopes.  Unfortunately both service and food quality were lacking.  We ordered a dozen oysters during their happy hour, and I was quite surprised to find how flavorless and large these oysters were.  They were almost gross they were so big. Needless to say we tried a couple and sent the rest back.  When we expressed our displeasure with the oysters there was no apology and no effort on the part of the waitress to right the situation.  Very, very unfortunate to encounter that level of attitude, especially in such a friendly city like New Orleans!

Perhaps it was the choice of entree - the burger a customer had ordered next to us looked quite good.  And admittedly the pizza we got was very tasty - but we still were hungry after sending back the oysters.  And the cocktails (while half price during happy hour) weren't roll-over impressive either. Needless to say we moved on to greener dinner pastures.

I didn't love Luke and I was completely planning on it! The drinks were good (albeit pricey), oysters were fresh, service was prompt, crab and corn bisque was fabulous, but my entree was disappointing. Our server confused days on the daily specials and I thought that I had ordered the slow cooked veal and crispy pasta in a creole tomato sauce. I was bummed when I received breaded pork chop over red beans and rice. I took a bite of the red beans and rice and got a mouthful of pork and was confused. Unfortunately I maintain a pork-free diet...so that was kind of a bummer. Our waitress came to the table and apologized and suggested a dish that would be quick for the kitchen to cook - shrimp and grits (minus the andouille). I don't have all that refined of a palate and I found the entree to be overly salted. The textures were enjoyable as was the spice, but the flavors were overpowered by the salt. Bummer.

My first five star review. This place is the perfect combination of price and quality. Reasonable prices for excellent food. The mussels were great, even my 8 year old daughter loved them. The herb roasted chicken my wife had was equally impressive. Decent French wine selection with very good restaurant prices. Service was also very good. I will hit Lüke again when I come back to this foodie town.

A couple of things come to mind when I think of Garavellis... 

1) Cheap, home-style food w/a drive through. 
2) Memories of the school cafeteria. 
3) A geriatric social event. 

You're not going to meet your future spouse here (unless you're an Ana Marie copycat), but you will find a huge array of home-style food and the option to choose each part of the meal (meat, sides, salads, dessert). This is an old fashioned cafeteria, with solid home-style food at affordable prices. Very clean and updated (for a cafeteria). 

Garavellis serves the usual overcooked veggies and a large supply of starchy sides and heavy gravies, but their meats are solid. The baked white fish is pretty tasty and they have a decent collection of roasted and fried meats (turkey, roast beef, pork chops, ribs, chicken fried steak, etc.). They always recommend the white gravy, but I advise... no. All flower, no flavor. They know how to cook meat. So, try it without the sauces and gravies, pretty tasty. 

They offer daily meal deals for around $5 (be sure to ask) and the fact that they have a drive through ROCKS. I am not usually a fan of this style of food, but every once in awhile, I gotta have it. 

I am giving Garavellis 5 stars. Even though I am not a big fan of cafeterias, it is the best in the area.

This place would no doubt get 5 stars from me if the service had been just a little bit faster. The food was amazing. We got the Flammen...uh the onion tarte thing, and the Etoufee with crab. So good I could cry. The servers recommendations were awesome. (But we often sat with empty drinks for too long.)

Very very good muffins and sandwiches! I'm a little undecided on some of the beans, they have different varieties on a regular basis but generally just 2 at a time. Still trying to figure out my preference on the coffees and cappuccino. The butter caramels for a buck are great too.
Really loved the service and the food was really really GOOD!!! I would get the stuffed oyster shells.  Beware the soft shell blt is a beast so huge yet delish!!

Went in for dinner on Sunday night.  Fries were as good as everyone says they are.  My "chocroute?" skillet of sausages and pork pieces had a quarter inch of liquid fat in it, which was a little much for me and my wife, and I'll try almost anything.  There are definitely better things on the menu.  Waiter was terrible, but the observant hostess was on her game, jumped in and saved the day.  Fortunately, they also sport a fantastic dessert menu - espresso profiterols & more, all excellent.  That pastry chef has got skills.

The food was excellent but unfortunately the service made the night less than memorable. We ordered an appetizer plus a seafood platter with crab legs and a bottle of wine. We had to refill our wine twice (which isn't easy while cracking claws) and my utensils (claw cracker, little fork, shell plate) were taken before I was finished. The service was overall aloof and rushed. Had it not been for the unwelcoming service we would have stayed for dessert and cocktails (i.e. more business for the restaurant). There were only a few tables that night. It is unfortunate that we will not recommend this restaurant to friends, despite the quality of the food.

Lovely atmosphere and great food steps from the French Quarter. Price per person is on the top end of yelp's $$  range. Our table enjoyed the seasonal champagne cocktails, the fried oyster salad, the shrimp & jalapeño grits with added crab, a pasta dish, and the crab bisque. Was able to cater to a Celiac / Gluten-Free diner with ease.

We really enjoy coming to Luke when in town.  My favorite dish is actually the mussles & fries.  Great spot for a late night dinner!  While most customers tend to be dressed more casual, you won't be overdressed in business casual.  They also have nice rooms for larger parties and after-work dinners.

5 stars for food, 1 star for service ! This was our first dinner in New Orleans... We live in Chicago, and like to think of our selves as foodies, and I have to say this place was delicious-- best Brussels sprouts we've ever eaten and the pasta was delicious!!!

Our complaint lies with the service. Our waitress was not attentive, rude at times and just seemed preoccupied with chatting to co workers and annoyed to have to serve customers. It was so strange and not expected at a nice restaurant  . We were looking forward to the "southern hospitality" and ended up being more appreciative of the Midwestern charm of Chicago. John besh-- you may want to check in on your staff, your foods great but management is slipping if your staff can't thrown on a smile and pretend to care

I came here on reservations with a party of 26 and we had the opportunity to try a 3 course meal for parties around our size. 

To me, their interior design was reminiscent of a vintage hotel. It is recommended to have a reservation due to its high volume of customers (at least when I went). The service was top quality, despite our huge party.

The bread that was given prior to the 1st dish had an outer crust that was firm, yet crisp. The inside of the bread was soft and carried a light flakiness.

The 1st dish was a blue crab bisque. The bisque had a medium consistency and packed a bold flavor. Each spoonful was filled with the crab's distinct taste, but left my pallet with a light spice. Personally, I felt like the bisque lacked in a balance of flavor that I was expecting and was a bit too salty. Perhaps that crab and saltiness could have been tapered down a bit.

For the 2nd dish, I had shrimp and andouille over creamy white grits. The dish gave off a wondrous aroma. The shrimp was not as "jumbo" as I expected them to be, but each packed a flavorful punch. The shrimps carried that bold, Cajun flavor but was not overwhelming. The grits balanced out the the shrimp by providing that neutral flavor to refresh the pallet.

For dessert, I had bread pudding with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce. Flavor explosion can be used to describe this dessert. The pecan sauce was very rich, but was balanced out with the vanilla bean ice cream, and both matched well with the bread pudding canvas. I would have liked more ice cream.

Overall, I was satisfied with my meals and overall experience, and I definitely would love to come by again next time I'm in New Orleans.

Super let down. So to be fair nothing was horrible or anything like that but at this price point I think it's ok to expect a little more. 5 minutes after we got our appetizers were delivered they showed up with the entrées and you either have to send your food back to sit under heat lamps or inhale your apps- they whole experience was like that - extremely rushed and not really what one would expect. Pâté was probably the only real standout - all the other items you've had before and likely better and with better service.

We came here for oyster happy hour and it did not disappoint. The shuckers are fun to watch and so fast and kept the oysters coming and we got to try a few varieties, and all were delicious! Had a lot of fun and met some characters. Definitely will come back if we are in town again!

I joined YELP so I could write a review of this restaurant.  On day 3 of our trip June 15, I convinced my fiancé to go here because it's a John Besh restaurant, and it was terrible.  We left feeling like we were just robbed.  Not one of the three hostesses greeted us.  The service was slow, took fifteen minutes for our wine decanter to arrive, although our waitress was something close to nice.  The food arrived fast, but it was AWFUL.  I almost cried.  The Friday special, the court bouillon, had a synthetic taste to it.  My fiancé's roasted chicken was bland, but the mashed potatoes and crawfish bisque stood out in a sea of terrible.  The atmosphere is so lackluster - and on a FRIDAY NIGHT.  Never again.

This place was a good happy hour experience because the cocktails were half off and the oysters were discounted. I had the French 75, which they make with cognac instead of gin; vastly preferable. I'm not sure I would eat here without the discount. Still, good place.

Enjoyed the happy hour today. The oysters were great, and the cocktails were just as incredible. The door#3 was so refreshing. Husband had the burger... Which was HUGE! Only complaint was lack of dark beer selection on draft.
Second time I've gotten coffee and it was cold. This time, every single canister(?) of self serve coffee was empty. They didn't seem to mind of course. Stay away.

Was here for  breakfast and the ambience is old New Orleans  with tile and wood and the food although easily considered standard breakfast fare was fine excellently. The biscuit was delicious as were the eggs and the smoked sausage was large and robust.
Better than some sit-down Mexican places! The employees are always in a good mood.

We only enjoyed a couple of cocktails and the pâté of Louisiana rabbit & chicken livers but must say that the entire experience was great! I also paid close attention to the atmosphere and how others seemed to be enjoying their experience and it was a really nice sight. I saw attentive servers, smiling patrons, and I enjoyed all the great smells as dishes past by us at the bar. Oysters is one of the only food I do not eat but I can say that this definitely seems to be the place to come for those fresh ocean beauties! I'm glad my friend recommended this place.

Quick service. The 75 cent oysters during happy hour were delicious!! Very fresh. The fried ones were just okay for me, the bf loved them (i think it was 1.25$ each). We also got the shrimp & grits and rabbit & chicken pate board. The pate i would probably not get again, the chicken taste was overpowering. It came on a board with all of these pickled jams that were interesting, but not good enough for me to ever go out of my way to eat. The shrimp and grits was awesome though. Comes served on an iron skillet (so very hot ); great balance of flavor and textures, especially with the creamy grits and large chunks of sausage/shrimp. The bread roll at the beginning was also pretty good--soft on the inside and crusty on the outside.

Mint julep- Very very very strong. I guess they give you your moneys worth but I felt like I was just drinking a big cup of bourbon. I did not taste much else besides that

Gumbo- Flavorful and chunky goodness. Prob the best gumbo I had in New Orleans.

Jumbo Lousiana Shrimp En Cocotte- Loved every bite of this. Shrimp was fresh and cooked just right. Grits was creamy and perfect. This was my first time having grits and I was impressed.

Brendan's Bread Pudding was ok but the Gateau  Basque Vanilla cake was gross. It was excessively sweet also very dry. Disappointing.

I try to visit New Orleans at least once a year, and I always make sure to eat at Luke. It's one of my favorite places in the entire city. The menu is exciting, the food/wine list/bar is of a great quality, service is good, and the atmosphere is a fun one with the perfect mix of casual elegance.

The menu is a Franco-German fusion, which sounds weird, but it totally works. Everything is great, but their pate appetizer that comes in a jar is out of this world - it's smooth as silk, meaty and laced with truffles - a sexy, sexy dish. Their seafood is great. I was there in August and my boyfriend and I had the best oysters on the half shell we have ever eaten. Ever. Yes, they were that good.

Another great element is the price - if I remember correctly, entrees are under $30 for the most part - you can have a really fabulous meal for a much better price than you will end up paying in some of the more "traditional" New Orleans restaurants. 

To eat here is to know that you are in capable hands - John Besh knows what he is doing. To give an example, we noticed a small detail - egg crate foam fitted to the underside of the tables in order to absorb noise - that shows this restaurant is all about delivering a great customer experience, even to the smallest detail. 

I will keep visiting Luke's every time I make it down to the Big Easy!

Food was top notch - we had crab legs, beet salad and crespelle - all were spectacular. Unfortunately, the service was sub par. The courses were served on top of one another (half way into the salad, they delivered the main course) and shortly after, they were asking about dessert. We were clearly being rushed out. Expected much better from this type of establishment. Borderline offensive.

I don't know what I can say about this place that hasn't been said before, however I am still compelled to add my 2 cents. It's really difficult to get beyond the awesomeness of 50 cent oysters during a 3-hr happy hour with the delightful mild horse radish sauce and amazing drink specials to boot (try one of the 2 house brews!) but we ordered the charcuterie plate which featured 4 housemade pates that were unique, rich and very substantial for an appetizer. Fresh bread got to us halfway through our pate tasting, but better late than never (especially with the delicious meat spread awaiting it!). The pickled watermelon rind was a fun refreshing surprise. We wanted to sit at the bar, but waiting for the back to open up was fine since we got a view of the kitchen. Our servers were friendly and very knowledgable. Great experience and we didn't even order a meal. Can't wait to go back for one (or two or three or more)!
Food was very good and according to my French friend the Pate was very authentic. Considering the quality I must say it is reasonably priced.
Food was delicious! Service great! Loved the ambiance! Especially loved the coffee. Short walk from hotel.

I recently moved to Glenside and stopped in here on a Sunday night during the NBA Finals for a quick bite and a beer. The regular pub food is delicious. I had a chicken cheesesteak, fries and a few beers. Local bar with a sports bar feel to it. They have plenty of tv's and the bartender/waitress was very nice. A good spot to stop into to watch a game, grab a bite to eat and have a few beers. They also had a good variety of beers on tap.
Found this restaurant using yelp last Saturday. The food and service was amazing. Had the Jägerschnitzel for dinner and the Mussels for an appetizer.

I just wanted to let you know I thoroughly enjoyed my lunch. I know people are quick to complain but I prefer to be quick to compliment. I had the river Bend drink-excellent. I had the gumbo for app and shrimp and grits for entree. Both were awesome! Great taste! I also wanted to compliment Johnny as a waiter. He knew his foods and how to explain them to a tourist as me and made sure everything was to my satisfaction.  I never had to ask for anything as he was quick to make sure all was filled (drink) and food prompt. Thanks for a great experience!

Went w friends for dinner. 

Food: It was just okay. Swordfish dish was a no. Flavorless and dry. Ribeye steak...average. Lack flavor and nice char. Some got the butter on top and some didn't.  Limited menu.

Place across the street was awesome and meat seemed like a better grade. 

Location/site: Clean and cute. Smaller place. Making a reservation would be a good idea.

Service: good dinner service.

We had a wonderful time and the service was amazing. Ordered the turtle soup, brussels sprouts, french fries, shrimp and grits (minus the sausage) and finally the rib-eye. For dessert we had the steamed chocolate and salted caramel ice cream. 

Apps - 
Fries were skinny and delicious. If you enjoy skinny fries, you will enjoy these too. 

Brussels sprouts were amazing! Get them, you will love it. 

Turtle soup, tastes like regular chili with ground beef. Didn't taste any special being that it was turtle. Take it or leave it, I wasn't impressed. 

Dinner - 
Shrimp and grits - my wife loves shrimp and I'm not a fan (I hate the crunch of the shrimp every time I chew.) This dish was creamy and very tasty. Loved the shrimp and no, the shrimp didn't crunch. In fact, the shrimp was perfectly delicate, meaty, and soft with the perfect amount of resistance. I loved this dish and would love to come back and have it again. They are known for this dish and it is available on their breakfast, lunch, and dinner menus. We ordered without sausage and devoured it. 

Our friends ordered the fish and sent it back for the rib-eye (medium.) It came out medium rare but he devoured it. Very fatty piece and it wasn't trimmed but he enjoyed it very much. It comes with fries so don't order any as a side if you order the steak. 

Desert-
You can't go wrong. If you like chocolate, caramel, sweet, salty, and a hint of coffee, order now. 

The service was with a smile, ambiance was fantastic (we were seated right next to the chicks window and we're lucky enough to enjoy the cooks put everything together.)

Loved the restaurant and would love to go back again soon.
Breakfast was fantastic. Light and very fresh. Awesome service that's very hard to beat. Another success of John Besh's restaurant. Their BLTAE entree was phenomenal.

Staff have always been kind and helpful (every other word in the menu was not in my vocabulary) 

This time, I had the shrimp and grits.  It was good but, like the other reviews have said, it's a bit too salty--overpowering the actual seasoning.  In the end, I felt like it wasn't worth what I paid.  

Friend had the Luke burger, which she said was delicious (and more than worth what you pay).

Last time, I had the Foie gras, veal w/pasta, and bread pudding for dessert. The bread pudding is one of the best I've ever had!

This place rocks! The burgers/sandwiches/steak/french fries, everything is yummy. I know New Orleans has so much to offer in terms of dining, but Luke always seems to pop up in the itinerary when I go..

Definitely my favorite place to grab a dozen oysters after work.  I recommend their Happy Hour 75 cent oysters are a go to for anyone in CBD or the surrounding area.  Sure you can get oysters from 20+ others places in New Orleans but this is where I recommend going.  

I'll have to sit down and try the actual menu one day but you can surely find me sitting at the bar at least one day a week with a plate of a dozen raw oysters and a beer in front of me.

It was our first time, and we had NO IDEA that it was a "betta have a reservation" place! But, Deirdre, who we found out later was the manager, found us a table for FOUR! She, Kevin, & ALL the servers were FANTABULOUS!! We had SOO much fun pickin appetizers & drinks & the place was just buzzin with HAPPY! The food was AWESOME, even tho we'd never had many things on the menu, like Crispy Brussel Sprouts, Yellow Beet salad, & Pate'! The stuff we were used to like raw/fried/baked oysters, & crisped french baguette sliced was PERFECT! Oyster ACTUALLY tasted like OYSTERS...even the FRIED ones (they & the raw ones are part of Happy Hour fare, along with half priced cocktails & wine)! I kno this is LONG but it's worth EVERY WORD! I'd recommend this place to EVERYONE, from locals to tourists! THANK U guys for makin us feel SOO at home!

Well.. thier service was really good. They customised our drinks and food as per our needs. Food presentation was really good and the sever was the best ever. She suggested some very good local places to eat

Reviewing in January 2018. I am not sure what happened to this place. I have been here twice in the last two weeks. Both times the staff seemed either overworked or just apathetic. My salad had most of the toppings wrong - it seemed like they were putting whatever they felt like in it. On top of all this the whole staff seem very grumpy. Overall the place appears disorganized- running out of utensils at lunchtime, etc. I will not be coming here again.
Great happy hour! We got 1/2 dozen of fried oysters and also 2 dozen raw oysters. Great deal. Would come back!

My favorite place on my New Orleans trip. Ordered the raw oysters which are 75 cents per oyster during happy hour,charred oysters, Brussels sprouts and the shrimp with jalepeno grits. Everything was flavorful and fresh. Wanted to try more, but my stomach was too full. Highly recommend in the New Orleans area
We had shrimps and grits, omelet with local crab. Both of them were sooooo good!!!!! Especially the shrimps and grits, tastes like heaven!

Dear John (Besh):

The last time I was in NOLA, I fell in love with you at Luke.  So why, John, why do you forsake me now?

Don't get me wrong: your $0.75 oysters during happy hour, up $0.25/each from the last time I was here, were cheap enough and the size of your head.  But it took so long to get them at 4:30 on a Saturday that your guy gave me half a dozen extra and a sheepish apology about being in the weeds.  Okay, well, these things happen.  

But tonight, my dear John, tonight was another story altogether.  I went with two friends of mine for dinner.  We had reservations at 8 and were promptly seated.  Our waiter was very nice, and tried real hard to remember your bourbon selection, but could only come up with Maker's Mark and Jim Beam.  We placed our drink and dinner orders, and waited.

The appetizers came out very quickly.  I was pleased because the service was so speedy.  But as we watched the kitchen activities from the table in the  back corner of the room, it became apparent that the speed with which we received our appetizers was not to be replicated with the entrees.

We waited. And we waited.  And we waited.  Our waiter never came back.   Not once!  He seemed to be ignoring us. Then a waitress came by. She said, "I've just been to check on your order, and it's not ready yet. What did you order again?" Does that make sense to you, John? It doesn't make sense to me. And we kept waiting. We could see our waitress in the kitchen. She was clearly trying to get something for us.  Finally, after five or seven minutes, out she comes with someone who must have been the manager, who is carrying a purse (something we all found to be very odd) and they were carrying two salads and soup.  The manager said that there had been a misunderstanding or a mix up or something, and dinner would not be for a little while, and for that reason they were offering us two different salads and a lobster bisque. She said, "I don't know if you are hungry for these, but I hope that they will tide you over while you were waiting."  But all we really wanted was our dinner, John.  Was that too much to ask?

When our dinner had finally come out, it had been close to 45 minutes after we finished our appetizers. Yes, the food was delicious, but there is no reason why we should've set onto it like ravenous vultures. There's no reason why it should've taken that long to get the food in the first place.

After dinner, the waitress asked if we would like some dessert. We ordered one dessert for the table with three spoons and some coffee. It took a full 15 minutes to get the desert and the coffee on the table. In the process of eating the ice cream on top of my dessert, I found a small ice cube embedded in the ice cream.  How do ice cubes get into ice cream? The answer is beyond me.

In any case, John, the food at your restaurant was very tasty, but the service leaves a lot to be desired.  Do you think that it should take two hours and 15 minutes for three people to have a few appetizers, three entrées, and a shared dessert?  I don't.  

Dearest John: you need to do something about the service in your restaurant. Giving your customers extra food because your kitchen or bar can't keep up with the orders is just shooting yourself in the foot.  Giving your customers extra food because your servers forget to place, fire, or hand off an order is also just shooting yourself in the foot.  Instead, you should probably just get the order right the first time. It seems pretty straightforward to me.

I want to love you, John. I really do. Do you think you can improve on these things for the next time I'm in town?  If not, I may have to dump you for Donald Link.  

Love, 
A foodie from DC
Nice corn bisque and crusty baguette, really good red beans and rice, although the pork cutlette that came with it didn't thrill me.  The bread pudding was outstanding!  I'd definitely go again.

I generally go to Lüke for their happy hour and, like all John Besh restaurants, the specials are incredible. 50 cent raw oysters, dollar fried oysters, and half price beers on tap. The oysters are great, but remember only to go when they are in season (months that contain an "r"). The beer selection, however, is wanting. The in-house brewed beers are just bad. Like, really, really bad. Bad in the sense that the first time I made my own beer, it was light years ahead of their in-house brews. The burger, on the other hand, is one of the best in town and the paté plate is incredible.
It was on the pricier side for us (~$30 per person), but food was delicious along with great service

Had dinner here with my wife. We had the seafood gumbo and the bisque. For the mains I had the mussels in white wine sauce which came with steak frites style fries. Both were wonderful. My wife had the jumbo shrimp with grits which was also fantastic. Topped off the meal with a nice bottle of pinot noir. We would eat here again when we come back to town.

Got the Luke Burger / it was fantastic / it was huge / loved the Shoe String French Fries.

The Service was Great / taking the order, then finally getting the product.

Gary H

Just so so, only is that location good, near to conference center and CBD, the food is definitely not $$, very little food for each entree, taste ok. Service, as we experienced today is not that good, wait a really long time for dishes. And no waitor add water.

Great little diner restaurant with a classier ambiance than most diners you'll find.  Food was delicious.  I ordered the moules et frites and the BF ordered the jumbo louisiana shrimp "en cocotte".  There were a couple of dead mussels amongst the batch which is to be expected, the white wine sauce in the mussels had a nice flavor.  I had to ask for some bread which is definitely the best way to "taste" the sauce. 
The star of the restaurant however seems to lie with the shrimp and grits.  Seriously the best shrimp and grits I have ever tasted! The grits were so creamy and dressed in such wonderful flavor with the andouille sausage and jalapeno topped with the juicy sweet shrimp and a gravy like concoction that blended all the flavors so perfectly together!
This place is a must go for the shrimp and grits alone!

Steamed chocolate. Make sure you save room for dessert and make sure it's the steamed chocolate (or bread pudding) absolutely delicious. 

We ended up here because this was one of the few nicer restaurants in the area that could accommodate a large group of 12 at one table and man did they take care of us. 

Most of us started off with one of the fruits de mer (seafood platter). I had half a dozen jumbo shrimp and each one was nearly as big as my hand. Our table also got mussels and clams. The shrimp were amazing, probably the best I've ever had. Several guys started with the bisque soups and oyster salad which they all said were fantastic. Most of us followed that up with burgers. The burgers while very good, weren't necessarily anything special (which was a little disappointing) although a really special burger is hard to find. Dessert though, other than the seafood, is where Lüke really showed off as I said before, the steamed chocolate and the bread pudding were amazing. 

I will definitely go back next time I'm in the area, but I think I'll order something other than a burger. The chicken dish and the fish looked amazing-oh well, live and learn.
The gumbo and the oysters were top-notch! Our waiter was very friendly and informative.

We stopped by here for happy hour. They had $0.75 raw oysters served by the half dozen. I also tried the fried oyster salad with avocado--that was definitely my favorite. I've never had fried oysters with so much flavor before. Their fry batter is the best! We also tried a cup of the seafood gumbo, which was equally flavorful and delicious. The atmosphere here was fun and lively, not too stuffy. I'd definitely recommend stopping in here for a snack before a late dinner!

I came here with a few girlfriends for dinner and the service was a joke. Our server was rude for no reason... I mean, he set our water carafe on my breadplate. Wtf!? Weird. The only bad service we've experienced in New Orleans. This city is awesome.

Luke is a more laid back restaurant from John Besh.  This is Besh's homage to the brasseries that once dominated New Orleans.  I would consider Luke an entry level restaurant to fine dining accessible to most people in a casual atmosphere.

The Crab and Corn Bisque has a rich and velvety texture and a nice briny, clean and sweet flavor.  For a bisque it is somewhat light and doesn't coat your palate with heavy cream.

Mimi's Buttermilk Pancakes are light and fluffy.  Topped with a honey-pecan butter, this transforms it into true Southern comfort food.  The fruit cane syrup is a little too sweet for my taste, but eaten with moderation makes this a winning dish.

The Louisiana Shrimp and Grits is a revelation.  The shrimp are perfectly cooked, and the grits are nice and creamy.  The sauce is made with shrimp stock and Andouille sausage.  For a traditionally heavy dish, the shrimp stock base seemed to lighten the dish up.

The Bread Pudding tastes like a combination of French toast and crème brulee, but without the usual bourbon sauce.  Although good, a little kick of booze would have put it over the top.

See blog for pics.

More of 3.5, and I'm rounding down. This was our big splurge meal of the weekend.  Another group of 7 ppl, and the food was only ok.  I split the seafood tower without the  lobster ($65) with a bunch of people, and everything was fresh, but I feel like there should have been more seafood for the price.  Ambience was good, up-scale without being stuffy.  I split the smoked pork shank with my girlfriend who's on the Paleo diet (urgh, don't ask), and it was a bit dry, in my opinion.  The sauerkraut underneath was delish though.  The bread pudding dessert was rich and satisfying.  Coffee: sooo good.  I only got decaf and it was full-bodied, and had no burnt, acidic aftertaste that is so signature of that place called Starbucks.  Everyone else seemed to be enjoying the food, and the service was quite friendly and attentive.

SO happy I have a friend from Dallas who knows her food. She took us here for brunch and we all stared at the menu for a while until someone broke the ooh and ahh-ing with the suggestion to order numerous plates for the table. 

The Chapagne Au Peche is SO DELICIOUS. 

We went on to order the Luke Burger, Croque Madame and then a dish involving shrimp. The burger was delicious and very filling. Even though I just had a fourth, I got what I needed. But I also had the intensive flavor of the shrimp dish (which I'm sorry I can't remember the name of or point out on the menu). It was delicious - but some could say the flavor is overwhelming. It's not for the 'oh yeah seafood is pretty good, i'll eat it if it's around' person. You need to commit to that shrimp.
