The croque madame was made to perfection and I was basically licking my fingertips to get the last tastings of those fries. 

You will be well fed here. The waiter will NOT steer you in the wrong direction. We wanted to order something, but our waiter advised against it saying it was typically a great item, but just wasn't coming out strong the day we went. We also somehow got extra fries out of him. It was a great way to kick off the day in New Orleans after quite the night.

My sis loved her duck, cooked 2 ways. I had the Sunday roast pork special which seems like a small portion initially but is is rich and filling! The special came with desert, so save room. I chose the bread pudding which has a whiskey flavored sauce that is traditional NOLA style. The Étouffée is perfect also. The étouffée and the pork special came with Jalapeño grits. 

It was a last minute decision to eat here but a very good call. The place is bigger than it appears. The front is narrow but the space is deep like 2 building joined together. 

As the Bacchus parade rolled along outside we dined. There are only so many floats and beads you can collect in a day before tiring.

Good seafood. The crab bisque was wonderful. I also had raw oysters (the local ones) which were nicely cleaned and a good size. I give it 4 stars because while it's good, it's nothing special compared to other Nola seafood places. It's a solid place to go though. Great service too!

Went here for lunch with my wife during our NOLA trip. Nice location, can't even tell it's connected to the Hilton (which is a good thing).

I had the crawfish bisque as a starter and my wife had one of their salads. My bisque is one of the best seafood soups I've ever had, delicate but full of flavor big crawfish tails all over, in a word great. 

My gumbo was a great entree but my wife's schnitzel was lacking a little flavor. Crispy and tender as a schnitzel should be but very little seasoning so it came a bit bland.

Overall a great experience, will definitely go back.

Amazing. Best meal we have had all year. And we ate at Commanders Palace 2 days ago. Luke's was in another league. Had the Luke Salad, the Crispy Brussel Sprouts, the Shrimp and Grits and the Shrimp Étouffée. Wow. So good. Thank you Nick and Kyle for the awesome service and recommendations. Luke's is the #1 reason we will be visiting New Orleans again!

Be careful at this place.  My daughter just had her purse taken by an employee.  This after an acquaintance had something similar happen to her last month. Take your business elsewhere. And hold on to your stuff...

Luke did not disappoint; went for the raw oysters and they were lovely.... fresh, plump,  and luscious. The service was attentive, efficient, and fun. The ambience was perfect, and the entire experience relaxed.

Came here for dinner with my wife having high expectations for a John Besh restaurant and we were overall pretty pleased with our experience. We called to make a last minute reservation and they were able to accommodate us immediately. There is not very much parking besides street parking right outside of the restaurant, some meter parking or free street parking around the corner.

We started with a couple appetizers: The Pate of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken livers which was amazing!! We also enjoyed the crawfish Sharon, although it was nothing to write home about. My wife tried to order the crispy soft shell crab for an entree, however we were told they had run out and the server recommended she try the shrimp and grits as an alternative (it was very tasty and I actually enjoyed the grits which I'm usually not a big fan of), but still left us wondering if the soft shell crab would have been even better?

I originally ordered the Washington parish roasted chicken... Not only did it come out cold but I found there to be a tremendous lack in flavor and I expressed my discontent with the dish to our server after a couple of bites (something I rarely do). I had it sent back and decided to go the safe route and ordered the Luke Burger because I had heard good things about it. The burger turned out to be delicious and very large in size (almost hard to take a bite out of) and amount of fries was very generous.

For dessert we had the steamed chocolate with salted caramel ice cream which was heavenly (highly recommend you try it)! The staff was very attentive and friendly. We always had our water glasses filled to the top, and one of the servers assistants came by to change our white table top cloth (which was a little dirty from our appetizers and entrees) while we were waiting for our dessert. We told him that it was ok and that we were just going share a quick dessert and didn't want to dirty another table cloth, but he insisted that it would be his pleasure to change it for us. We were so impressed that we left him a tip for doing that.
We will be back in the future, perhaps for happy hour oysters next time!

Visiting New Orleans for a few days and we came across this restaurant for lunch. OMG!!! I can barely think of the words to explain this food. I also sat near the kitchen so I got to see a glimpse of the action. Nicole M was our server and recommend the swash blossoms. Amazing. The stuffed oysters. Amazing. I had a small cup of gumbo. Amazing. My wife had the soft shell crab BLT, it's served open faced and looks so appealing your mouth waters as you take pictures of it to tease your friends, then you dig in. Amazing. I had there fried chicken and red beans/rice. It's was good. Celebrity chef restaurants normally live up to the hype but this one was beyond just a good experience. I currently work in celebrity chef Tom Colicio restaurant Beachcraft in Miami so I know what to expect. I'd definitely recommend this place to anyone that has a mouth and taste buds. Again Nicole M was great she really made our experience 10 times better

This restaurant is highly recommended on yelp and we were in the area during happy hour. When we arrived, the hostess was totally rude & we were shocked! After she told us that we could wait hours for an empty table or sit at the bar, we told her we were happy to sit at the bar and said thank you. She literally ignored us & looked away. We were so mad by the time we pulled out our seats at the bar that when the first, then the second, then the third bartender greeted us, we nearly dropped our jaws! We sat there quietly shocked instead while all three bartenders continually checked on us, offered us more drinks, & made recommendations on the menu. It was probably the best service I've ever had at a bar (and by the way, the BEST oysters I've ever had). I couldn't help but wonder why that hostess what trying to ruin what these people are trying to do so we let one of the bartenders know. She sounded like she'd heard this story before and asked if we would speak with the Manager. We agreed & the manager came over (which was really nice though she seemed too busy to really care). Moral of the story? Act like you give a shit & you'll get a big tip! Oh & you'll keep your stars too.

AMAZING food and even though we got seated very promptly, it took a bit longer than usual to get our food and our tab :( Still, i would go back and enjoy this food again when I'm in town, the food is worth the wait for sure!

Service was disinterested, but the food was good:

- Oysters were delicious
- Gumbo was only OK. Disappointed given the raves
- Shrimp and grits were really good. Really liked the touch of jalapeno.

We saw a bunch of people order the burger which looked really tasty. If I'm ever back in town, will try that!

Had shrimp & grits, delicious huge shrimp!  The lobster bisque good. We tried ordering oysters but the table before us had ordered over 120, every last one the restaurant had...will go back when we are back in town and order oysters!
Went here during their Happy Hours (3-6pm) for the Oysters and drinks. Please make reservation. Fresh oysters and good wine.

Can't beat 75 cent oysters that are actually nice and meaty, half off cocktails and draft beer between 3-6pm. We also got the stuffed oysters, which we could have done without - itty bitty oyster hidden under a small mound of mayo and crab meat. Service was great!

This was my overall favorite dinner in New Orleans. The menu reminded me of Thomas Keller's Bouchon (which is a good thing). Lots of hearty bistro dishes with a Louisiana spin. The redfish amandine and the lamb shoulder ravioli were fantastic. I would return in a heartbeat.

We had Sunday Brunch at Luke and enjoyed it so much that we went back for dinner the same day.  So good!  The shrimp and grits were delicious, perfectly done.  We sat by the kitchen and enjoyed watching the chefs do their thing.

For dinner we ordered the seafood platter ("le grand plateau de fruits de mer") and mussels ("moules et frites") to share between the four of us.  The oysters and mussels were my favorite, but everything was amazing.  The platter also included shrimp, ceviche, and crab legs.  Service was great, even though we came in 30 minutes before close!

We will definitely be back when we are in New Orleans!

Everything was good... especially the brussels sprouts... so good we ordered another serving ;-)

Good cocktails... the somm was very helpful on the wine choices and steered me in the right direction... :-)

Definitely a recommend...
Excellent service, but the food was really really overrated. Was expecting much more. Everything was really fried and not overly refined. Service was very good though!

We arrived at 7:30pm on a Saturday without reservations but we were seated right away.  Service was great, and the food was even better.  I had the Luke burger and my boyfriend had the ham sandwich.  I would definitely recommend this restaurant.  My only complant is that its very very noisy.
We had great oysters and crab legs! Our waiter, Elliot was attentive, humorous and every suggestion was spot on! You can't go wrong here!

Came here specifically for the Oysters during happy-hour and thought they were "okay."

My group of girlfriends were so excited, we ended up ordering 2-dozen Oysters along with appetizers such as: crispy brussels sprouts, shrimp & grits, and house-made fries. The oysters weren't shucked correctly and we had a few unfortunate surprises during our meal =( 

Overall, it's a good place to get your oyster fix while in NoLa but it definitely is not the best.

Came here for brunch...their have a variety of brunch dishes and great appetizer dishes.. a definitely must try if u looking for a more classy comfortable great service restaurant at NOLA..

It blocks from French Quarter, so walkable if u staying around central area of French Quarter.
Can be busy..if u have large group, best to make rsvp.

This is one of the best bars in the area. All of the food is good but the pizza and wings are the best. Drinks are pretty cheap and they have lots of specials. What makes this bar stand out is the outstanding service from the bartenders

The Tahoe was complaining that it needed an oil change. Jiffy Lube has always been a good place to go. Patrick took us right in and started working on the beast. When he came in to give me a run down of what needed to be done, I was surprised because I thought the air filter would need to be changed, but he showed it to me and said not this time. He didn't try to over sell anything and agreed to what I wanted done, like using a synthetic oil blend rather than straight synthetic oil.

This kind of service is why I continually take my Tahoe to this Jiffy Lube. They do a great job quickly and honestly.
Went in while being remodeled, and still had great food. Two thumbs up. Can't wait to go back to NO and have some more! Hostess were very welcomed and made great recommendations.

75 cents oysters during happy hour. I was in town to eat raw oysters and this place is it. I've tried 50 cent one down the street and came back here the next day. Luke's oysters just tasted fresher and 25 cents difference isn't a huge deal breaker. 

The waiter that served us for Wednesday happy hour was on point. Super nice at explaining the food and cocktails.

Lüke was the final lunch of our vacation to NOLA in February 2015, on the drive back to the airport. Parking was very difficult to find during lunch hour, but the hostess was very understanding while we tried to sort out a street spot.

Their must-have dish is the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en Cocotte" (which rings in at $24) which was probably my favorite meal the whole trip. I added the poached eggs because we were still in brunch mode, and it just sounded too amazing.

We started with their 1/2 dozen Stuffed P&j Oysters (gulf shrimp and blue crab) ($17) which were unreal tasty. Highly recommended as a starter.

Great service as well, our server was attentive and very considerate of time constraints. This meal made it to so hard to leave! We will be coming back next time.

The best time we've had out in a long time. The guys were funny and we just connected with them and had a blast. Oysters were great and the gumbo was the best but had to order two bowls cause they were a little on the small side. Will definitely be back, Semper Fi Besh!

Ate here last week as I really wanted to eat at a John Besh restaurant in New Orleans, and had the Luke burger. The burger was great and cooked exactly to my medium request and the fries were great. I ate at the bar and everyone's food around me looked equally amazing.
Loved this place!!! Great staff!! Food was the best we had in New Orleans!! Brussel sprouts were fantastic.l!!!

The food that wasn't overly salted was very good. 

We started with the fried oyster salad, which would have been great if the bacon's saltiness didn't take away from its taste. Like most people, I love bacon, but not when its salty taste stays in my mouth hours after the meal ended.  However, the bacon might not have been the only culprit. The crab omelet was also extremely over-seasoned.  On a positive note, the salad had the proper amount of dressing and the fried oysters were delicious (it didn't have any of the ooey gooeyness that I dislike about oysters). 

We also ordered a croque madame.  I had high expectations since this is a town known for its French food. Unfortunately, I've had much better ones in San Francisco (Bay Area folks - check out Tartine's croque madames).  The bread was soggy and the cheese was lacking.

Overall, the food was fine, but it didn't live up to the hype that some other Yelpers gave it.

It's a John Besh joint, so I expected a lot, and it delivered. More casual than some of his other spots, total French Bistro vibe. The service was exceptional, and the food predictably good, especially the fresh oysters. On the loud side, for those who are concerned about such things...

Despite perfectly good food, the surly demeanor of the help from front to back can't overcome the bad taste left in my mouth after eating at Luke. I took my son and his lady for Brunch recently and was thoroughly disappointed, especially after the stellar food, service and atmosphere at Borgne - where everyone seems genuinely happy to see you! Not sure why two places owned by the same group offer such wildly divergent experiences, but Luke is off my list for dining in the Big Easy.

Ordered fillet mignon on a hot stone, got a few carpaccio sliced pieces of non fillet mignon cut meat. That i had to cook myself. Ordered uni sashimi ( huge mistake) the low quality made it taste like eating poop i mean that literally. Then the steamed buns with chicken teriyaki  came out. Chicken taste like they freeze diced up chicken and throw it on the grill frozen for a minute and the buns that are suppose to be soft and delicate were plastic hard!  Over priced spot that can decorate a platter nice which will taste terrible.

Hands down, this was the BEST dining experience I had in New Orleans. The wait staff was extremely friendly, personable and quick. We told them it was our last night in the city and they truly made it a memorable experience. We ordered the Gumbo and the Fried Oyster salad as a starter- I am not usually a fan of oysters but both dishes were amazing. The main course- the shrimp and grits and the cavatelli pasta. They were to die for! I definitely recommend both of these. It was heaven on a plate. The dessert: bread pudding and the peach and blackberry cobbler. Both were AMAZING! I can't say anything bad about this place. Throughout the meal the chef complimented us with extra dishes to try which helped us on our mission to eat our way through the city. Again, the staff was amazing and the chef was fantastic.

Overall if you're looking for a good place to eat in the city, I definitely recommend Luke. I will be back next time I am in town. It was a great dining experience.

We had so much fun at Luke during happy hour. Amazing P&J oysters raw and fried. We came back several times during our short stay in New Orleans. Shucker Shawn made the experience unforgettable. Thanks for your hospitality!

After seeing positive reviews decided to try Luke's for dinner. Walking in the place was busy and we were told the wait would be over two and a half hours for a table; luckily, there were spots at the bar. I decided to go with the shrimp and grits (termed 'en cocotte') and enjoyed watching them shuck oysters while I waited. I didn't have to wait long, though, and was pleasantly surprised at how quickly my entree came. The shrimp were nice and plump and the grits had jalapeños mixed in which made for a delicious combination. 

I was going to be satisfied leaving until someone asked for a dessert menu--and then I saw the bread pudding. Oh my gosh: this stuff is so good. Not only is it bread pudding: it's topped with a pecan sauce and then ice cream that perfectly melts as you scoop your spoon into it. 

Overall, a nice dinner and absolutely delicious dessert. And by sitting at the bar, some shucking entertainment.
Love the happy hour oysters and I really think its the best French 75 I've had
Best ahi and bread pudding I have ever had.  Period.  This is not to be missed. If you have one meal in NO this is the place.
Great place for all sorts of oysters. The raw dozens are massive.
Breakfast selections all pretty good. Yummy shrimp and grits breakfast- super rich and creamy. Great coffee. cozy and friendly. Great last meal in nola.

Son mis tacos favoritos en esta taqueria, bueno lo eran ahora ya no, la carne tiene mucha grasa y la carne tiene mucho tiempo recocida eso hace que pierda el buen sabor, la salsa es muy sobraza y el servicio de las meseras me párese muy bueno ..!! Admiro sus ganas de trabajar a pesar de los diferentes climas .!
Have dined here twice on my NOLA business trip. Both dishes were exceptional. Service and atmosphere are first class.

This is a great place to stop with work buddies.......conviently located close to 364 at 270......have a cocktail......and back on your way home in time for dinner. Or pick something up from Balducci's down stairs.....great food.

REI is a great company and the Boise store has a knowledgeable crew always willing to answer questions and give friendly advice.

I purchased a hybrid bike a couple of years ago from them and were happy with their assistance in finding the right size and making adjustments for the proper fit. I've also taken it in for routine maintenance and have been happy with their service. 

It doesn't appear that Larry Craig comes in anymore. At least I haven't seen him wandering the aisles.

Fantastic fresh seafood, incredible (and unique) drinks and great service ! We went here on our last day in New Orleans in October 2016 and it was the favourite meal of our 5-day stay in NOLA for all 6 of us.
You won't go wrong here.  Creative shellfish.  Fresh.  Its John Besh.  Location away from hustle and bustle

Luke is always a great place to eat especially to bring out of town people. Drinks are on point! Freshness of the oyster is one of the best. Entries portion are shareable. Will definitely recommend to everyone!
Food was FANTASTIC. Lunch service was a bit slow.

Do it. The food was very good however the oysters took 30min to show up. When they arrived they were great. Stay away from the blackened boudin. Not to tasty. The crab ravioli was good and spicy  as well and the shrimp and grits were great. The stuffed shrimp was very good but small. Only three. Bread pudding is good but hard to share. Will return.

They have the best tacos from any taco truck in the area! However they are ridiculously priced! I bet they make a killer profit! I got only 4 mini tacos, and they charged me $9!!! I think price per taco is normally $1.25 but they have steep prices to add cheese and avocado (on 2 tacos). Back home, for $7 i got 4 tacos, charro beans AND a baked potato. I mean they're good. But not THAT good. I'll definitely be taking my business elsewhere.

I wanted to like Luke more, but my two visits here have led me to only 3 very generous stars.   First visit here a year or so ago we were seated towards the back by a bust stand and stared at dirty dishes all night long.  This was so distracting I can't even remember if what I ate tasted any good.  It must have been decent since I didn't just leave mid meal.  I complained to the manager who had the dishes removed but within a minute there were dishes piled up on the stand again. 

Second visit we had the seafood tower for two and it was a huge disappointment.  I'm tempted to try Luke again because of all the great reviews but not sure if I will.

My husband and I stayed at the Hilton for my birthday 7/28/18 and decided to have dinner downstairs at the Luke. It was AMAZING! The food was our best experience while visiting NOLA. We had two different waitresses and they were super nice! We even were offered a free glass of champagne!
Great Brunch!  I had the Crab Bisque, Pork Grillades and Grits.   Great service too.  Check it out.

Luke was 4 for 4 last night. We ordered a cup of matzo ball soup, a cup of gumbo, the crispy brussel sprouts, and a mixed drink with gin, prosecco, lemon, and lavender. The brussel sprouts were quite possibly the best sprouts I've ever tasted. I will be telling my friends that come to New Orleans to stop at Luke, if for no other reason than to taste this dish. They had small apple slices, really really thin slivers of jalapeno, honey, cheese....every bite had a different amazing flavor explosion across the spicy, sweet, crunchy, savory spectrum. 

I also can't say enough great things about the soups, as they had the exact right amount of spices. I wish I hadn't had such a heavy lunch so I could have tried more of the menu. While the menu is a tad closer to $$$ than $$, the flavors in the food more than justify the prices. You can't go wrong!

Update: THESE BRUSSEL SPROUTS THOUGH! These aren't your mothers sprouts (sorry Mom!) Come here and have your veggies!
We love this place! We typically just get sashimi and they have the freshest around, better than most of sushi places in center city. This place is a hidden gem.

Well, it's 6 years later and Tokyo Sushi is still here and seems to be larger than I remember it.  I picked up a 3 roll combo from the pre-made case at $12 which have 4 pieces each of tuna (fine), salmon (fine) and Yellowtail (surprisingly very good) with scallions - all in brown rice and rather large pieces.

I am pleased and Shall return now that I am back in this area again.

Seems more like a "real" sushi place now and less like "supermarket" sushi.

Next time I will order some nigiri to order.

My only complaint?  $7 - $9.5 for a sinlge handroll (They call theirs a demaki vs. temaki)???
Way too high.  

All in all very pleased and will return - and soon!

Went for the first time a few weeks ago. I usually go to Wild Ginger. This might be my new spot! there were some really interesting rolls and it was tasty. The booths are comfy and the atmosphere is really modern and cool. The waitress asked if we wanted anything else like dessert and we said no thank you. Then she came out with a dessert and said it was on the house!

I'm adding to this 5 months later after my initial post. I recommended to someone on a Facebook page to come here. they went on Father's Day and they gave the man a gift card! I came here on my birthday with friends (my friend made me wear a birthday tiara) and they gave us free dessert and gave me a 10$ gift card. I just went today to use it. they are delicious I love them so much.

Although we had a 9:30 reservation we weren't seated until at least an hour later. They truly tried to be gracious about this. However when we were seated this is where the graciousness abruptly ended. The waiter was horrible.....rude and very unprofessional. Never checked on us after our meals were received....and removed dishes prior to being finished. Even after I made a comment! 
The food was absolutely divine and i will be back for this reason....however if we are seated with the waiter we experienced this weekend.....we will wait for someone else.
Lots of great places in NOLA and some people won't put up with rude wait staff but will go somewhere else.

This place is off the chart! Awesome food all around. We had 4 in our party and we all had a great dining experience. Service was perfect and the food was delicious. The ribeye was the best flavor ever!

Well I have to admit that John has ruined what was my favorite Besh restaurant. I ventured to my favorite spot for oysters though early in the season for a friends birthday party. I was interested in the oyster special happy hour which is 75 cents not 50 cents as it used to be and that was a sign of worse to come. We ordered bowls of gumbo that is excellent but has gone from $8 to $10 per bowl since I have last been here. They used to have daily specials where you order get an entree and a cup of soup for about $20 and that is gone. The menu has been reduced a bunch of high priced items that you would have expected from August or any of his other places that you didn't get here. Luke was like a neighborhood kitchen that served really good food at a good price but now he has gone for the tourists instead of the locals and it shows in more ways than one. They have added more tables and crammed the small interior, the tables are now so small you really can't fit the oyster trays on them comfortably when seating a table of 3 or 4. The oysters themselves were the worst I have ever had from them with about 3 that were not opened that I had to open at the table. Gumbos normally come with hot french bread and they only brought one for a table of three where they are supposed to be given to each person not per table. The oysters have really turned into a lost leader to get you in the door and spend a check that you really were not anticipating. They have baked oyster not char broiled at a whopping $17.50 per half dozen. My friend though it was for a dozen and ordered the half not knowing the $17.50 was for the half dozen which made the situation even worse. To top it all off we were there for a birthday and notified the hostess and the waiter and there was no recognition with a dessert or not even a happy birthday from the waiter. From start to finish this was a miserable experience and one that I was not expecting from a John Besh restaurant and is not qualified as a TOURIST TRAP. In fact this place has changed so much they really should start over with their reviews because many on here were for the previous chef and menu.

This is by far the best Japanese restaurant I have ever been to. Every dish is prepared and presented like a work of art. And it's not just beautiful, it's fantastic as well!  It opened too long ago for us to not have tried it before now. I blame the location even though it is only 5 minutes from our house, but sits right between our favorite Chinese restaurant and one of our favorite bars! Now that we've experienced it, we will surely become regulars! Friendly service all around and excellent food! Go. Just go!

Ate at Lukes 4 times.  The first time it was great...the next three times it was barely edible.  Twice got one of the specials and was sadly disappointed.  The last time, I opted for the same dish I first enjoyed and it was not at all the same.  Hope his other restaurants are better.

Amazing food and service! We came here after a Pelicans game late at night, ordered the Brussel Sprouts and Shrimp grits to share between the two.

To our surprise, they split the grits in two so that "we would get more shrimp each"! 

The shrimps werent piping hot(even though they were in skillets) so we asked if we could reheat it. The waiter (Gary) was so nice about it and they were reheated super quickly.

The brussel sprouts were amazing, paired with the grits. And also... WARM bread for the table!! For dessert we had the choco torte with peanut butter icecream, also really good.

We simply just loved eating here and the waiters are super accomodating and nice. 15 mins before closing at 11pm they still seated two old ladies!

DESSERT

bread pudding - always a winner...solid new orleans bread pudding
steamed chocolate - deep dark chocolate was decadent and rich.  chocolate to ice cream ratio was perfect

The shrimp en cocotte is literally one of the best things I have ever put into my mouth in my life. Jalapeno cheddar cheese grits, sinfully savory shrimp stock/broth, perfectly cooked shrimp, tasty but not too spicy andouille... it's quite possibly the perfect dish. The etouffee was delightful, oysters were fresh and huge (and cheap during happy hour! 50% off!), the mojitos were super boozy, the desserts were pretty ok (I honestly should have ordered another en cocotte for dessert) and the wait staff was wonderful. Overall I was super pleased with our visit and would be happy to return.

Happy it's a halal restaurant Masha'allah but I waited almost an hour for one small chicken and broccoli, I watched them cooked the food and noticed everything went into the deep fryer before the saucepan #notgood when I got home everything taste fried I really wasn't impressed and I won't be going back. May Allah preserve them all for there good efforts Ameen

Great place for breakfast! Usually get the Steak & Egg wrap or a yogurt parfait. I wish they had more variety, such as egg omelettes. Beware that the egg omelette sandwich does not actually have an omelette inside. Just scrambled eggs with toppings.

This was my go to place for meals and drinks. Felt comfortable at the bar as a single woman and the food was beyond excellent, especially the shrimp and grits, Brussels sprouts, crab bisque, bread pudding AND the French 75!

When you have to work on a weekend it's nice to stop off for lunch at a spot that screams panache. Luke (or Louuuuke) is a great place that (as it appears) tons of Yelpers flock to. Being brought here is a delicious technicality.

For me, N'Orleans fare goes a really long way; not that I don't love it; but I love it more when I have it less. My colleague ordered everything in oysters, and I mean everything. While he slurped away, I fell in love with my bisque. How can something so decadent and buttery, still taste light and sweet? 

Our drinks did not arrive during this wonderful appetizer round, though. That they had a crowd was putting it mildly. It's at these moments you can take in the decor: that being warm and relaxed, which I also loved. Our table was located very close to 3 other diners: I could have grabbed a handful of pickles from each of them. 

When our main meal arrived we were not disappointed. The cracked crab was amazing; amazing enough for all to worship at it's altar; it was coupled with a light slaw that was not knee deep in mayo; but spicy and tangy and on my plate it was gone! It came with a grilled stuffed tomato that was loaded with a crab and cheese mixture with a definite kick! Awesome.

My colleague ordered what many seemed to be ordering: the crab bit; in addition to fried green tomatoes. He seemed to have no complaints because he leveled his plate.

Our drinks came at the end of the meal, and it's a good thing too because by then our pH levels had altered dramatically. Though attentive in certain areas, the service was not "up there". But the food at Luke was wonderful.

They say everyone has a "double". Well, I have a friend at home who looks just like John Besh. Though Chef Besh didn't appear for me to compliment him on the meal: I can do that when I get home. :-)

I went to this restaurant with friends from New Orleans, and the company for dinner was fantastic.  I had a great time.  Unfortunately, the restaurant had nothing to do with my great dining experience. The food was just average. The service was inattentive, and the restaurant is set up in a way that every table is in a pathway with people walking right on top of you.

For my appetizer we shared the charcuterie plate, and it was good. Then I have a couple of the crab bisque which was very tasty, but didn't have any crab in it. For my entrée, I had the Viener schnitzel oh, and the pork was like breaded paper the meet was paperthin dry and tasteless the breading was nice and crispy but extremely salty. For dessert, I had the bread pudding which was touted by the waitress as the best dessert on the menu, but it was tasteless and dry.

Went to dinner based on several strong recommendations from a friend who has been multiple times and always enjoys her experience. This place did not disappoint! Gorgeous serene interior, lovely staff and an extensive and creative menu. They offer a lovely specials section and the ceviche just melted in our mouths! We had the Alligator roll and the Rainbow Roll of which piece  was topped with the most amazingly seasoned shrimp. Cannot wait to go back and try more of the rolls. Everything was divinely presented and amazingly delicious!

I guess the reviewer, ACE B., dissing this place doesen't know how lucky he was to NOT find chineese-being from San Fran, take it from me, the Chineese food in St Louis is horrible.  Garavelli's is a survivor, still serving comfort food.  Ms Sherry's, Ms Hullins and the place that used to be downtown are all gone now.  The place is clean, inviting and the dining room has enough ambience to make it feel just like home.   Cafeteria style sure beats many of the other eating places, where you have to order one of the 20 things on a list on the big boards all the while an impatient teenager order taker yells "NEXT, NEXT!", "WHAT'S IT GONNA BE!" only to have your order wrong.   At Garavelli's It's kinda entertaining having one guy with an accent, maybe Italian, and nice middle aged women serving behind the counter, and just to look, there is  so much variety of appealing, of good quality and fresh food.   There are several salads and appetizers. They even have watermelon for Mom.  Although they use steam tables, the vegetables are al dente and my niece, a vegetarian, approved.  The main dishes cover anything you could want, from carved beef to fried fish or chicken and they even have steamed fish.  Although they have a variety of deserts, St. Louis' guilty pleasure, Drewes', is a tempting two blocks away.

Oysters + beer = happy is probably all you need to know...! 

Really standout and delicious oysters. Same goes for the beer, although I'm not sure that had anything to do with Luke (although they kept it cold and poured it nicely). Overall, it was really fun to sit at the bar, watch the game, and down some great food. The oysters were probably some of the best I've ever had, and it was a great intro for the husband.

We'll be back, and I can't wait to try some more items off the menu.

This was the first restaurant I went to in New Orleans and the best one I've been to. I had the Oysters and the Gumbo and they were exceptional. The staff is very welcoming and attentive and the experience is truly filled with Southern Charm. A must go to when in NOLA!

I love John Besh's show. I was underwhelmed. After coming off of a cold watching the bartender slam paperless straws with her bare hands wasn't fun. She also wiped at her nose a few times which made me no longer want to drink. The food was ok. Lauren, the other bartender was very professional and the cleanest looking employee there. I did buy one of the cookbooks

Boyfriend and I took a mini vacation to New Orleans and wanted to try a local restaurant near our hotel. Based on reviews, we went to Luke to try it out.

***Experience. It was A-OK. 
We made a reservation and when we arrived, they said we can sit in the bar... Normally when I make a reservation, I expect at least a formal seating arrangement to have been ready or at least close to being ready. The service was decent. Nothing amazing but people just doing their jobs and serving you normally.

***Ambiance: I expected it to be a little bit more on the fancy/intimate side but it's not. The lighting didn't make any romantic vibe but that's okay.

*** Food:
I ordered the steak/fries and my bf ordered a seafood pasta or something. They were both good savory meals.

I found weeks Luke's by checking out a gluten free restaurant option google search for New Orleans.  I'm so happy I decided to make reservations!  The food was incredible!
The staff listened to my food restriction requests and delivered with tasty food.  Not just leaving off ingredients but making adjustments to the dish which enhances the flavors.  It was our favorite meal of the trip

Enjoyable atmosphere - we had a great view of the kitchen from our table and really enjoyed watching everyone in there do their thing while we dined.

The tables were a little on the small side. Our party of 4 was a bit cramped, and there weren't even any larger tables to switch to. Food was brought out in a slightly haphazard fashion - our drinks, gumbo and salads were all brought out simultaneously (after we waited for a good ten minutes). Our server was obviously bothered by this and removed our salads (delivering them later, at a more appropriate time). 

The menu was inventive - gumbo and spaetzle on the same page! The gumbo was really, really excellent. The entrees were good. Not terrific, but good. My family enjoyed some braised lamb that was pleasant, some mussels which would have been better if there were more sauce in the "bucket" they came in, and a sausage platter that was tasty and a little mysterious (never could quite pinpoint what meats were used, without asking). The bread pudding was heavenly. Really, really, really worthwhile.

For the first time yesterday I made it to this Chipolte. I was feeling a need for Mexican food. However I did not find it appetizing that every employee behind the food counter was wearing some sort of mouth piercing. Big turnoff if one is hungry.

Holy crap this place was delicious. I had visited New Orleans for a Bachelorette Party weekend, and this place was walking distance from our hotel, and also from the French Quarter. I had the "Crab in a Jar", which is soft shell crab over jalapeno cheesy grits and a poached egg. The soft shell crab was perfectly crispy, and the grits were really fattenfully (if that's even a word) good.  Eating the crispy crab, with the runny poached egg was delicious - I'm going to have to bring that into my kitchen. Though, I had a friend's shrimp n' grits, and those definitely won if the two grits battled. The waiter was really helpful - definitely knew the menu and had great recommendations. I was there with 8 girls, and everyone thoroughly enjoyed their meals.

If I went back - I'd definitely get the Crab In a Jar again!

*(0 stars for the hostesses at the front, as I was met with rude stares and unfriendly demeanor upon looking for my party)

Group of about 12 of us, we came for some bites and HH oysters. We ordered a few dozen of these, some crab and corn chowder, and shrimp and grits. Everything was exquisite.... The oysters were FAT and the chowder was thick, the shrimp and grits were also to die for........ The food was nothing short of food-coma inducing. 

The service, however, was super...... s l o w. Some orders came out late or perhaps even forgotten altogether. This combined with the surly hostesses at the front made the experience kind of meh. Food = 5/5 though.

Can you really beat 50c oysters and half price drinks at happy hour? After devouring 3 dozen amazing oysters we were super happy campers. Everything else we ordered was delicious as well. It gets super busy so make sure you have a reservation or be prepared for a long wait.
The best crawfish bisque I have ever taste! If you are visiting the big easy u should dine her, I promise you won't regret it !
It was so good we went back the next day.  50 cent oysters and great service   Just the right amount of attention. One of the best burgers ever!  Get the Luke burger

Oh my!  From appetizer to entree a delightful experience featuring an open airy dining room with a huge bar. Lump crab in a horseradish sauce, duck breast with a crispy dark rice, gnocchi with sautéed kale and to finish bread pudding with vanilla ice cream and praline sauce. The menu features some classic John Besh recipes. Service was solid.

So this is where my wife and I went to finish our blitz around New Orleans. We had recommendations from friends that this is a place to eat at, and definitely happy that we were able to make it here.

We get there for brunch, no reservation, and with no wait went to a table near the back. After reading through the menu and having an incredibly hard time making a decision.

We ended up with Brussels sprouts to start. They almost had a sweet chili sauce flavor that surrounded them. It was a huge pile but didn't last all that long as the wife and I went to town on them.

I had some breakfast with eggs, grits, sausage and Allan Benton bacon. Sounds pretty standard, it really hit the spot.

Wife went with the biscuit and fried chicken sandwich. It used the chicken thighs because its better that way.

As I write my reviews of Nola food I wish I was still there.
Best oysters (raw) I have had in a very long time. Fresh, cold, meaty and tasty! Also has the shrimp, grits and sausage, which was excellent as well.

overpriced.  Had the swordfish and it was dry, possibly over cooked.  It was also about 6 ounces.  $28 for a 6 oz swordfish that wasn't very good.  Disappointing.  Overall it's a nice restaurant but it is overrated.

I was here this past weekend for a bachelorette party.  As the maid of honor, I was in charge of organizing the weekend.  I found this restaurant from reading reviews on Yelp and Open Table.  All the reviews looked great and the prices looked good as well.  Well it turned out to be a smash hit with all the girls.  We ordered from the charcuterie menu for our appetizer.  Everyone loved it.  For entrees, 3 of the girls ordered the seafood etoufee, which was outstanding.  I chose the mussels and frites, which were delicious, but the serving size was huge.  I could have definetly shared with one of the other girls who ordered the same dish.  One of the girls ordered the skate wing, which ended up coming just a few minutes later after everyone elses.  So the manager came over and offered to pay for her entree!  All the girls were very impressed with the service, the food and the great time at Luke.

The best thing to get here is the flatbread. I've had the vegetarian melt - ~$7 for a big flatbread sandwich with melted cheese and pickled veggies. I wish the veggies didn't taste so sweet as they did (the Indian in me wanted to douse the sandwich in hot sauce) but the bread was the redeeming part of the meal and I would come back just to try another sandwich with the same flatbread! Not a bad deal for a huge meal.
Amazing raw oysters at great prices (65 cents during happy hour!). I loved the gumbo. The friendly, accommodating service pushes this place to 5 stars.

We spent xmas eve 2012 dinner here and were all pleasantly surprised!

My first John Besh experience and boy was I made a fan! The oyster shuckers and bar attendants were very attentive while we waited for our table. The gulf oysters were phenomenal and nothing like any that we've ever had in the northeast.

Once seated, we started with the P&J baked oysters, the escargots, and the bacon/oyster salad. The baked oysters were just so-so and the other items were pretty solid.

I had the grilled ribeye and frites for my main course and it was quite possibly the best meal that I had during our 4,700 mile cross country journey!

I'm already planning our next trip to NOLA as we speak and Luke's is at the top of the list of must visits!

I went here for lunch with two friends based on yelps recommendation, and the fact that this was a John Besh restaurant.  It is a little walk from the French Quarter, but very doable.  When we arrived it was farely empty(we came around 1-2pm on a weekend), and as expected service was good.

I ordered the mussels and fries.  It was not only delicious but a very generous portion.  The mussels were cooked in a heavy pot in what looked to be a butter, garlic, wine and herb sauce.  The fries were thin and crisp.  My friends ordered the pressed pork sandwich and veal spatzle.  Both looked and tasted delicious.  I

 didn't realize this until after I had left, but the "buster crab" in their "BLT" is actually slang for soft shell crab.  I was quite disappointed to find this out as I am a HUGE soft shell crab fan.  

Their menu is not very large which is the only reason I gave it 4 instead of a 5.  If you're in the area and would like a change of pace from the traditional french quarter food/decor, I would highly recommend making a trek to Luke's!

Oh my goodness. Eggs in a jar. 

Based on my sentence above, you may be wondering what the heck I'm talking about. Well, Luke has an incredible breakfast dish called Eggs in a jar. Now, I'm not one for grits....they're too....."gritty" (heh). I actually demolished these cheesy, jalapeno-y goodness. The eggs themselves were very straightforward and poached, but once you pop the yolk and that lovely golden center runs over the already cheesy grits...all I can say is, "heaven". Now, throw in several batter-fried shrimp to rim the jar, and you have a meal that will keep you full far past lunch time. 

For an added treat, get the beignets with the chocolate sauce and preserves. While they aren't as good as Cafe du Monde's, they are still quite delicious with a cup of coffee.

Oyster happy hour is amazing. It was even more amazing when the oysters were only 50 cents, but even at 75 cents, the P&J oysters are a great deal. Get a couple dozen raw oysters and a couple appetizers like the crawfish bisque (that comes with a seafood stuffed crawfish head) and the crispy brussle sprouts (flash fried with a slightly sweet and spicy vinegar sauce) and you've got a very tasty, very filling meal for two at a great price.

I wish Yelp had half a star, because this should be 3.5 stars. I might be punishing this place just for not living up to my expectations, but I was underwhelmed. The brussel sprouts were the stand-out (so much so that we requested the recipe). But an appetizer should never be the most memorable part of a meal in my opinion. Honestly the brussel sprouts almost earned that 4th star from me, but I just can't seem to make myself do it. Why not? Well, we had a seafood tower (the medium sized) and the crab was over cooked (really???). A few of the mussels seemed over cooked to me as well but I might be nit-picking. They should get those things right every time. In any event, maybe try the brussel sprouts and a salad.

I've come here for lunch once but dinner was just terrible. We ended up ordering the steak and the shrimp and grits. Also ordered a few drinks which were actually delightful, so that's the saving grace for the 2 stars. 
Steak was well over cooked and ended up being way too SALTY, and so were the grits. Our food was barley touched and ended up being a total let down. It was surprising to see a restaurant of that caliber have issues with seasoning. 
We were extremely disappointed but you win some you lose some, they did end up giving us a free dessert which was the "Salted Caramel". Not sure if that was unintended or clever joke. But needless to say we won't be going back here again. Plenty of other places to try, so it's hard to give a place a second chance.

very accommodating after our party grew spontaneously. The food is ridiculously good. Priced about right for my taste, but i'm used to LA prices. The grits were money and the service was prompt and attentive.

Gawd... so good!  Especially for the price!  

We went for happy hour oysters and ended up having dinner there.  Food was a tad salty for my taste but totally delicious... one of the highlights of my NO visit.

THERE IS DELICIOUS FOOD to be found here, thank you Chef Josh Besh! My coworker and I made last minute reservations for a late lunch, and they were busy, but still able to accommodate our party of 2 around 12:45pm on a Wednesday. We sat in the back room next to the kitchen, and tried:

-Seafood Gumbo a La Creole ($7/Cup, https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=fn_2V849nbN3jss-BNXvSg&userid=76vIFZcC7owykCBjMfGVXg): So delicious. We loved how chunky and flavorful this gumbo was (there are tons of oysters and Andouille sausage), and it put the version at Mother's and Commander's Palace to shame. A must order for any gumbo lover!
-P&J Oysters (Half Dozen/$9, https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=wLx1wqK8mdFK83yB9u_HXA&userid=76vIFZcC7owykCBjMfGVXg): Super fresh oysters, and worth trying if you haven't had them before. They aren't very briny and not super flavorful on their own, but great with the cocktail sauce and/or horseradish.
-Luke Burger (Bacon, Caramelized Onions, Tomatoes, Emmenthaler Cheese, Served w/Housemade Fries, $16.50, https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=RfrlmL8yqHnD4YbFyfQ7TQ&userid=76vIFZcC7owykCBjMfGVXg): Yum- this was cooked a perfect medium, and I loved how all the flavors worked together. The fries were also amazing, and had the consistency of the McDonald's fries back in the day- crispy but soft inside. This isn't the most authentic New Awlin's dish you can here, but it's still an excellent burger and fries- recommended!
-Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" (Roasted Jalapeno Cheese Grits, Green Onion Sausage, $24, https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=chiuw3JVSTiu4XUZrN5hTg&userid=76vIFZcC7owykCBjMfGVXg): SO DELICIOUS- a must order! The shrimp were cooked perfectly, and the roasted jalapeno cheese grits were amazing. I'm salivating a bit just thinking about this dish again.
-Bread Pudding ($9, https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=oXSFnooeonlP0IIfykEuYw&userid=76vIFZcC7owykCBjMfGVXg): Yum, what a great way to end a great meal! This bread pudding comes with a giant scoop of ice cream and additional pecan praline caramel- a must order for any bread pudding lover!

Service was the only part of our meal that wasn't amazing- our server was ok, but forgot about us a couple of times so it took forever to order our food. However, all was forgiven once we started eating since everything was so delicious. Portions are on par for the prices, and we would definitely come back if back in New Orleans. Parking in this area looked really tough since there didn't seem to be much street parking.

I wish I could give this place zero stars. The food is barely edible; my margherita pizza had the hardest crust I've ever eaten and a bit overpriced for it's quality in my opinion. The ordering process was extremely confusing. There were no signs to indicate where the ordering line was. I approached the cashier to try to order my meal and was rudely asked to return in line and proceed to the food bar line where the ordering actually took place. I ordered two sandwiches for my family, and was immediately given one sandwich, but not being told which one it was. Since there were many other people ordering as well, I waited off to the side for my second sandwich. After a few minutes, I was skeptical as to whether or not they heard my order correctly, so I asked the gentlemen if my sandwich was made. I clarified my order, and was shouted at by him, as well as another crew member, both of them saying my sandwich had been called five times in an extremely condescending manner. Though I did not hear him call the sandwich earlier, I felt violated since he treated me with such impatience. It was my mistake for now knowing which sandwich I received, but even more so that I was stupid enough to let them get away with such poor customer service. I hope this review acts as a warning to those who may want to eat here. BEWARE OF UNCULTURED AND RUDE WORKERS.

I will definitely come back whenever I'm in NOLA only for their happy hour specials which includes the PLUMP, tasty 50cents oysters and alcoholic beverages. 

I ordered 2 dozen just 'cause I lOoooOve me some oysters! I'm glad I did because they ran out pretty quickly so I do suggest you get there early into the happy hour. 

I also got a plate of etouffee of blue crab and brown shrimp. Shrimp was great and was drenched in brown butter sauce. Sadly, there were only about 3 pieces of blue crab. For $26 a plate I expected a little more than 1 piece of shrimp, 3 pieces of blue crab and a less than handful of garganelli pasta. Don't get me wrong, it was delicious but not filling at all!

Overall, my party and I had a great experience (except for those who came late and missed out on the amazing oysters).
Everything was amazing. Being a visitor and new to the cuisine, I was surprised at how great each dish was. The staff was great too.
Amazing food in a great unpretentious atmosphere with an incredible server (Kenny)! Made a normal business trip a true culinary experience. Thanks for a great night!!

The waitstaff was overly attendant but very slow moving.  I thought it was just a southern quality but it was a bit over the top.  We were there for over 2 hours with a large group and a pretty empty restaurant.  If you want to take a slow leisurely brunch, then this is your spot!  But if not, I'd skip it because the food wasn't extraordinary either.  Their jalapeno grits are enjoyable.

Jalapeño grits are AH-mazing!   Great beer on tap. Oysters are delish!  The ambience is nice - there are two rooms - one that's near the bar and another that's a little fancier (you'd want to sit with your parents  in the fancy area unless you drink with them in which case the bar area seating is fantastic). 

Service and food is great here - enough that I'm coming back for the second time in two days (thank you grits and gumbo!).  Our server last night was personable and knowledgable.   I'll definitely be coming back the next time I'm in NOLA and will be looking out for my next Besh experience!

Thank you YELP for the Happy Hour information.

Hands down the best oysters I have had in New Orleans!! (And the cheapest!) 

We stopped by at 4pm and ended up having 3 dozen P&J oysters for $9.00. The smoked venison sausage was also good for $2. I wish we came here for dinner instead of Cochon.

Having read the rave reviews for Luke, we couldn't NOT try it out for ourselves. The food and service were good but we were disappointed that they were out of all draft beers and, a bigger sin, out of foie gras. The dish that was recommended instead (rabbit liver pate) was okay but much too rich to finish even half of it. The moules frites were excellent and the portion generous. Front of house was a touch indifferent and lacking in Southern hospitality. All in all, would still strongly recommend but perhaps check ahead of time for availability of dishes you absolutely want to enjoy.

amazing happy hour .50 cent oysters-- super fresh and huge! the fries were a bit cold and but the servers were very accommodating and brought us another order. the champaign cocktail was perfect as well.
OUTSTANDING customer service and DELICIOUS food. Brussels sprouts, crab and pumpkin bisque, shrimp étouffée and bread pudding were all out of this world. Have to fit this into your vacation!

Awesome place... great food & even better service 
The food was fabulous... Try the shrimp!

Luke was recommended by our hotel staff and it was a good suggestion and close by.  Smart looking but casual spot, with sort of a French bistro menu.  The chicken paillard was excellent; the fries were very good and I am told they have one of the best burgers in New Orleans.

I can't say enough good about this wonderful pet hospital, and if I did it would be a book... This was the second part of our longest day ... our cat, Honey, had not eaten in way too long... upon entering entering Seven Oaks Pet Hospital (It is the only hospital for animals in the area that has an on-site ultrasound.) The reasonable price took me aback as everyone else who said "come back next week, when our specialist can be in our office to help you," was going to charge even more than they did. Seven oaks pet hospital called me back and said can you come right now... We would love to help you... That was a complete miracle from God! The veterinary doctor was very kind as he shared the bad news. They bent over backwards to help us in our time of need. The facility was very clean and inviting. The staff at the desk was especially loving and efficient. I was very impressed and will definitely recommend them.

We came here for brunch and everything we had was spectacular. The escargot was especially good as it comes in a soup
bowl with a broth strangely like French onion soup.  I loved it. The shrimp and grits were also something to write home about!  It was a great variation on this dish. I would love to come back here sometime. Thanks for reading.

Went to Luke for Happy hour, thinking I would be getting the most delicious 50 cent oysters and excited. When I breezed through the door with my companion, the woman at the desk informed us that unfortunately there were no reservations available. Looking around the restaurant, this was hard to believe, as 85% of the tables were empty. Yes. 85%. So we went to eh bar, and to our dismay there were no seats either. So we returned, oysterless, to the woman the desk and asked again, "are there any seats, just for half an hour, so we may consume our oysters?"

"No" she replied,"All of our tables are absolutely booked. We are just swamped."

"but..... it shows me I can make a reservation on open table,." my intelligent companion interjected, with her iphone in hand, the light glowing on her face and over my heart.

And in my head, the trumpets sounded, while a dark gloom came over her face. Slightly puzzled, and slightly annoyed, she said that she could lead us to a table, bcuz she "trusted" our ability to make the reservation.

WAHT?!?!?!?!?!!?!?! And then she promptly seated us, in the back.

The oysters were fine. They were fine. P & J 50 cent oysters They didn't have minuet sauce. Sad face. Only cocktail and sauerkraut. Disappointed Sad face.

The onion tarte is awesome! The burgers were some of the best I've ever had....service was awesome! Even on a busy Mardi Gras weekend.....did think it was weird that food runner looked throughout burgers with bare hands checking burger temps? Maybe those little picks with temp on it (rare,medium etc)...

My fiance and I were visiting New Orleans and stumbled across the Luke restaurant. I must say, this dining experience was phenomenal. The appetizer we shared was the flammenkuchen. The onions were caramelized to that sweet goodness, bacon smoked to perfection and the cheese was delicious. For an entree I HIGHLY recommend the shrimp and grits. It's a cuisine unique to New Orleans and it was exceptional. I was told by a few people this place has the absolute best shrimp and grits in the city and it lived up to that expectation. My fiance ordered the gumbo which paralleled the shrimp and grits in quality and taste. We both chose to decline dessert because our entrees could not be topped. I will recommend Luke to anyone traveling to New Orleans.

This place is good, really good. Happy hour runs from 3 - 6, half price cocktails and 50 cent oysters...you can't buy oysters at the market for 50 cents. Half price drinks, I recommend the Sazarac, the official drink of New Orleans, the best deal in the city at $4.50. Andre, one of the oyster shuckers, is one of the most personable people I have ever met. He is extremely passionate about what he does and is very good at it. We are in New Orleans for a week and thank God Luke is only a block from our hotel, we have been there 4 times during our stay and will be going back tomorrow. The rabbit and duck liver pate is one of the best pate's I have ever had, served with country bread, sweet and sour pickles, pepper jam, pickled watermelon rind and country mustard, all house made of course.

I bookmarked this place from my last visit to Nola. I was super excited to try this place! Upon arriving  the atmosphere was better than I expected (upscale). 
Me and my husband ordered the chicken biscuit which is a larger plate so we decided to share. The presentation was excellent the chicken was tender, juicy, & flavorful. I also order a mimosa it wasn't the best I've had I asked to have it returned and order another drink. 
Upon eating half way through my meal my chicken wasn't done all the way. Instead of sending it back and getting my ordered comped I paid for everything. 

Honestly I don't know if I'll try them again

This is a great little place it's just between being fancy and casual. The food is excellent, especially the shrimp and grits. Be sure to show up between four and six for happy hour since your going to pay half-price on a lot of the drinks as well as special pricing on the oysters. Make sure to get reservations since it's rather hard to get into without them. Highly recommended.

Overall experience not so great but due to no fault of the staff. The staff was very patient and friendly and different people constantly check up on you to see if your food came out ok, if you need a refill, if you have any other issues. 

We went on the Saturday night before Mardi Gras and although there restaurant was on the parade route we easily scored a reservation; every point of interaction was nothing short of friendly. Great knowledge of menu and good recommendations; best shrimp and grits (their point of pride) and really delicious, buttermilk fried quail (think fried chicken but better - great price for the portion - two birds split into four pieces). The gumbo was underwhelming, lukewarm and strangely viscous, but otherwise it was a good dining experience.

The firealarm went off halfway through our meal and lots of patrons cleared out; they are obviously unable to turn off that alarm once it's on, so they gave us complimentary beer to-go to continue our mardi gras festivities, which was nice. However it's a damn shame that I did not get to sample their bread pudding due to the premature kitchen closure :( will try and return the next I'm in town.

This place is phoenominal. Walking in I will admit it didn't look like much.  I misjudged on appearance. I was quickly proven wrong after I tasted one of the best drinks ever had, the Jalapenoma cocktail while we waited for our table. For appetizers we had the Brussels sprouts... So so good. My entree was the shrimp and grits with a side of corn and crab bisque. Both were so delicious and were perfect representation of the area. My husband ordered the ribeye. While good, it wasn't the best we've had, but steak isn't the known specialty in NOLA. Overall wonderful experience.

I attended last night's Sunday Supper at Luke's.  It was really rather fun sitting with a bunch of strangers and sharing food and conversation.  I enjoyed the overall experience.  Three of the four courses were great but the coq au vin was one tough, dry bird-even with the yummy sauce.  It was authentically made with rooster, but I thought if you slow cook something long enough it would eventually become tender.  That didin't happen.  On the other hand, the oysters, baked and raw, the king crab legs thermador, the butternut squash with shrimp bisque, and the baba au rhum were all great, even if the shrimp in the bisque were a bit salty.  If only they'd been able to pull off the main course, this would have been a five star review.

Every time I'm in New Orleans, I try to swing by for the oyster happy hour here because it is such a great deal! 

I came with a group of 10ish, right at 3pm on a Monday, just in time for happy hour. If I recall correctly, it's $0.75 on the half shell, $1.25 for fried oysters, and half off select wines/beers/cocktails. We made a reservation ahead of time and we were seated almost immediately. The staff was very friendly, patient, and accommodating. The oysters were plump and fresh. Drinks were fantastic. The decor and atmosphere are on the upscale side, but not pretentious. My group had a great time and will definitely be coming back the next time we're in the area!

Food was delicious.  I enjoyed the shrimp and grits and crawfish bisque.  Savory and salty, with just enough heat to liven up the dishes.  I especially appreciated the attention to detail in including the stuffed crawfish head in allusion to the practice of sucking the heads of boiled crawfish, after all the flavor is all in the head.  The oysters were wonderful.  My only complaint is the service.   Could have been faster and more attentive.

Great. Dinner and brunch at fairly cheap (~30-40 for two people) meals. 

P&J baked oysters: 5/5 Must get. It's fantastic.
Gumbo: 4/5
Shrimp and Grits: 5/5 Excellent, excellent, excellent dish that was creamy and savory .

Brunch was not as great. Crab omelette was the standout (4/5) and other breakfast items were very, very sub-par. That said, it was great place to eat a relatively cheap,  exactly whatI expected, sort of meal.

The food here was great, but honestly the experience was not worth 16 dollars for a chicken and waffles dish. The menu is very pricey, we had a dirty utensil, and the complimentary bread comes out uncut and the waiter seemed annoyed when we asked for it to be cut, at least they could have given us a proper knife to cut the bread so the table could share. Just found that strange but the food was ol, the fried chicken in the chicken and waffles was great, the waffles butter I could have done without, I would have liked my own syrup on the side as there was only a very small amount of syrup on the waffles so I was not impressed. I have had a better chicken and waffles at Cheesecake Factory. The gumbo and crab bisque were phenomenal and they had great fries and burger. It is an ok place but not somewhere I would make a point to go back to.

We went to Josh Besh's restaurant for an early round of appetizers and drinks. The decor inside of the restaurant was perfect and the atmosphere had great ambiance. The Oysters on the half shell were amazing. They were very large with great taste. The baked P&J Oysters were really good. They had a great garlicky flavor. The Pate of Rabbit and Chicken Livers was to die for! It was easily my favorite item that we tried. We also got crab bisque which was pretty good. Drinks were amazing and the staff was very friendly! I will go back to Luke next time I am in New Orleans
Can't say enough good things about this place. Great drinks, affordable oysters, fantastic atmosphere. Classy atmosphere without pretension.

I have been there three times.  Once for happy hour, with half price drinks and half price oysters.  Once for lunch, where I had one of the best burgers I have had in town; and the third time for dinner where I had a pork shank with sausage and sauerkraut that was incredible.

The half price oysters ($0.50 each) where of excellent quality and extremely fresh.

I will continue exploring their menu, because everything I have had so far has been excellent.
Beautiful ambiance. Great brunch menu. Highly recommend the burger, which was cooked perfectly. Tender and juicy burger.

We had dinner here and brunch here.

Dinner, we had great P&J baked oysters, gumbo, the shrimp and grits (which they kindly split into two separate griddles, as we had indicated that we'd be sharing), and the peach fritters for dessert. Everything was good; the grits were especially tasty, and the peach fritters were a little bit of a letdown - pretty oily, but I guess that's what we signed up for when we ordered them. Creme fraiche was good. Our mint julep was very bourbon-heavy, and less minty than we'd hoped for.

Brunch was a letdown. We had very standard fare, eggs and bacon and whatnot. The crab omelette was decent, but not spectacular. 

Dinner is great, brunch is not worth it.

All the food was excellent and prepared well.  Pricey to be sure (5 crawfish beignets with 1 tiny crawfish each for $15?), but very tasty.

The service was lousy with our disinterested waiter really putting a damper on the meal. The meal was saved when another waiter noticed, swooped in, and started taking care of us.  His name was Steve or Rich... great guy from Chicago.

At any easy $100 before tip for 2 people with 2 drinks, appetizers and entrees, I am not sure I can give a glowing recommendation.   It feels a little greedy for a small bistro with a very limited menu, but it was a very tasty meal.

Must stop every time I'm in NOLA between 3 and 6pm for 75 cent oysters!  I was with a group of 11 girls for a bachelorette party and I called to see if they can seat us.  Unfortunately it was game day so the restaurant was pretty packed so they couldnt :(.  We took our chances anyway and stood by the bar.  The staff was so accommodating and ended up opening up a private room for us (so long as we were out the door by a certain time since they were reserving it for another group).  It was such an awesome experience - shout out to our server Rich who kept us entertained and put up with our crazy bachelorette party shenanigans.  We were so happy with them that even though we were only in NOLA 2 nights, we made sure to stop by one more time before our flight home.  Can't wait to go back.

I completely spaced taking photos. This place was unique and delicious...lots of great choices and was very torn. I ended up getting the burger because its been feature in Travel and Leisure magazine. It was so so good. The bread was soft and light...was told its baked fresh daily. The caramelized onions and then the fresh tomatoes and lettuce made the burger. It had thick sliced bacon too. Yummy!!! I got the Luke said and it had delicious beets both red and yellow. The dressing made this salad. Also, had the shrimp etouffee, which is served over pasta made the dish unique; was delicious. 

I was so full, so I skipped the bread pudding which pains me. I regret not trying it because I bet it is spectacular. This is a must visit if you are in town.

Slightly mixed review, but overall a very nice experience. Service was a little spotty, but when you got their attention, it was excellent. When we mentioned that we didn't particularly like our first course (flammenkuchen), the waiter offered to remove it from our bill. My steak was perfectly cooked, and the red velvet doberge was divine.

While I am just not big into sandwiches in general. I really like the atmosphere here. Good coffee, great location and good sandwiches too ( when I am in the mood for one). I like the interior design of this place.

This is my first time reviewing a place and felt the need to just because the front of the house service was so, so awful. Long story short, my two friends and I arrived around 5:30 for happy hour and the hosts -- all four or five of them inexplicably gathered around the podium -- were so inattentive, unorganized and rude that we ended up giving up and leaving. We're all very polite, undemanding people but the staff literally ignored us and demonstrated zero interest in having us as customers. I was really bummed because I wanted those oysters so bad!!! But the service was so terrible that it would take a lot of persuading for me to consider trying again. My tip for them would be to have one or two front of house persons who know what they're doing/remotely want to be there, instead of whatever it is they're doing now.

Outstanding practice! All of the vet assistants were super friendly and knowledgeable. Took my 7 year old Shiba Inu in for some routine vet "stuff" (rabies vaccine, heartworm test), and she was having some itching near her rear end that seemed to be bothering her. Before EACH procedure/test was completed, the assistants ran an estimate so I knew what to expect at the end of my vet visit. They offer a great "wellness plan" that covers most of your vaccines for a year. We chose not to get it this visit, but probably will the next time we go in. 

Dr. Clifford was super friendly and got right down on the ground with Laina. She made us both feel comfortable. They suggested a lot of different things for her - not only for this visit but for future visits - but I didn't feel like I was receiving a high pressure sales pitch.

It is hard to navigate a French cuisine menu with celiac disease but the staff made it very easy and the food was fantastic. I really appreciate their patience and knowledge. Everything was very good.
Ate Xmas Lunch here. Downside: they ran out of shrimp. Upside: great crab omelette. Reasonably priced and lots of locals.
Get here if you can. Delicious food, pretty good service, in a loud atmosphere. Dessert is a must!!
Love everything about it! Best happy hour oysters bar ever. Fried oysters are amazing, best French 75 also.
Amazing food!!! Love love love! The duck was phenomenal. Can't wait to come back some day! Our server was also the greatest person of all time! Thanks Kevin!

The oysters were good. Service was a little slow but none the less very friendly. I had the salad with buttermilk dressing. If every salad I ever had was this good it would definitely be the only thing I'd eat every day. The sugar beets were yummy! Best salad I've ever had :)

Stopped in for happy hour before the Pels game, half price drinks and $.75 oysters. Grabbed half a dozen and a whiskey-a-go-go. Massive cockles in an upscale atmosphere, yet the bill only comes to $11. Sign me up anytime.
ordered an Americano & maple butter muffin. Both were delicious! I wished I got the chance to try their sandwiches but was only able to drop in for a few minutes to check out the place~

Best. Grits. Ever. I don't know what was in them, probably cream and cheese of some kind, but I about died when I had a bite (in a good way, of course). Sadly, I only had a small bit as another member of my party got the grits and I was wondering why she got grits at dinner. I wonder no more. I intend to use the gift certificate my wonderful brother got me to go here again for Christmas Eve Breakfast with Mom. Grits will be had.

Okay, I had the fried oyster, bacon, and avocado salad, which was good. Those were certainly some of the best fried oysters I've had and I loved the little, juicy bits of bacon.

I liked the ambiance, including the juice glasses for the wine. This is not dressy, "city" French nor rural French but something in between. I'll call it suburban French.
Great food and drinks. Happy hour is awesome with buy 1 get one free drinks and raw oysters are 75¢ a piece.

Have been to Elms just three times but I love the coffee they serve on drip here.  It's the 49th parallel roaster's coffee which is pretty unique and flavorful.  A great change from say, a Transcend go-er since they get beans from various parts of the world - Guatemala, Columbia and parts of Africa as well.  It's a really small cafe with place for 4-6 people to sit, but with great functionality.

They have fresh baked muffins on a daily basis and often times different from the previous day.  I've also had an awesome breakfast sandwich here once.  Don't remember the ingredients but it was really tasty.  The breakfast sandwiches and muffins change on a regular basis so it's always a welcoming and courageous experience to blindly pick up their sandwich and a cup of their coffee on the go!

Locally sourced ingredients, adding to the charm of local produce that's getting ever more ubiquitous among new cafes on the north-side of Edmonton.  Please, if you live in this part of time, treat yourself with a great cup of coffee en route to work.

Saw chef John Besh being interviewed on network TV, so I decided to come to Luke to find out what the hype was.  

Beautiful restaurant in an old school look.  Excellent service.  I had the shrimp cavatelli etouffee with extra fried shrimp on top.  The cavatelli with cheese was ok, didn't need the extra shrimp which didn't add anything to the dish.  The bread pudding was excellent.  

Should have ordered the gumbo.

Nice place. I sat at the bar for a late lunch and the service was really good and friendly. The butternut/ricotta gnocchi was very good and the prices seemed on par with the other area spots in NOLA.
The oysters looked great. Fresh etc. I also had a very nice French 75. Really a nice lunch.

Lüke is one of many restaurants that I wanted to try during my visit to the Cresent City.  One restaurant that I really wanted to try was closed on Monday so I gave this one a shot.  I ordered a Rosemary Bourbon to drink and a Crawfish Etoufee with pasta.  The pasta was similar to mac & cheese pasta instead of the noodle type but was good and filling despite the portion being a bit small.  I also received a complimentary bread pudding with ice cream on top since I was there around my birthday.  The servers were attentive and did a great job making sure I had an excellent experience. Lüke is located on St Charles right next to the iconic St Charles line Streetcar.  There is parking on the street and around the corner.  This restaurant is very pleasing inside and out.  A great place to take a date or to have a fancy meal while being surrounded by the overall unique character of The Big Easy.

We had a delicious breakfast here:

* Eggs in a Jar: Fried Shrimp, Poached Eggs, and Jalapeño Cheese Grits 
* Fried Chicken Biscuit with Spicy Mayhaw Glaze

My friend said there is $0.50 oysters during happy hour.  I have not been to Luke for happy hour, but definitely will keep that in mind for the future!  How likely can I convince the restaurant to serve breakfast items during happy hour, too? :)

Since my cousin was in need of someone to talk to, he called me and suggested meeting for dinner at Luke.  I balked much because I had alot to do for school but the guilt in me wouldnt let me turn this invitation down.

To listen to my cousin complain about work and to eat great food.

The restaurant is attached to the Hilton and so really there is no seperate parking lot.  As it is located in the Central Business District, parking off-street and paying by meter is one option or you can park at many of the pay by the hour parking lots in the area and walk over.

The place reminds me a bit about the Palace Cafe.  The no-fuss design of the bar, the tables and chairs.  It was all very country French bistro.

At any rate, I got there first and was told to wait by the bar for the other person, so I went and sat in front of the guy adjacent to the bar---the oyster shucker guy.

He had his own thing going own.  I asked him what it was that he had going on down below the bar.  I leaned across the bar to look and saw 6 compartments he was keeping fresh ice around.

Lobster tails, spiny lobster crab legs, squid, mussels, clams and lemons.
