We were immediately (and nicely) accommodated when we asked to be moved.  There WERE families in there, which is fine, but that noise level is inexcusable.  Luke has a menu that combines German, Alsation, and local fare in a brasserie setting.  Great wine and beer list to accompany said menu.  We had very good service.  The place was busy, but not insane, and had thinned out by the time we left.  Wines are available by bottle, by the glass, or in 1/2 or 1/4 carafes, a nice touch.  Excellent assorted breads come to the table first.  We started with glasses of Gruner Veltliner and 1 dozen delicious fresh oysters. (these are not the happy hour price, they were $14 doz)  I am used to Puget Sound oysters and these were far superior.  I opted for regional fare, and had the famous shrimp and grits. Spouse had the Etouffe of Blue Crab & Brown Shrimp with fennel, garlic, saffron fumet garganelli pasta.  Both of us practically licked our plates.  With this we consumed a Dryer Sonoma Chardonnay (unoaked in the Chablis style).  We shouldn't have, but we had dessert:  Basque cake for him and bread pudding for me.  It was all simply wonderful - we would go back in a heartbeat and highly recommend Luke.  Our total bill was $154
Popular downtown spot with good food and service. I wouldn't call it special, but it was a convenient place to eat before an NBA game.

Service: Outstanding 
Food: even better
Wait: had reservations but made them an hour before I went. This was also on a Sunday night so others may not have the same luck.
Would I recommend? I recommend this is your destination.

This is an amazing place to do a happy hour after work if you work in the CBD!  I can't speak with any knowledge of the whole menu, but the oysters were absolutely fabulous.  Our waiter was fantastic, and when I asked if there was a cheese plate available for munching before oysters arrived (there wasn't, which I would have known if I glanced at the menu), he made it happen even in the middle of very busy service.  Wonderful service, good food.  Wine pours were a little short, but hey-- for half off, I can't really complain!

We had breakfast at this restaurant today. I have to say that I found it to be a pretentious and unwelcoming. I got the southern breakfast. This included two eggs, three sausage links, biscuit, and grits for $15. The grits had a firm, congealed consistency. The links were good. The eggs were forgettable. The biscuit was cool and hard around the edges. My wife had the spicy frittata. This was pretty spicy but it was tasty. Overall, I found this place expensive and forgettable. The server, refilled our coffee once and never refilled our glasses of water. Once the food came out, she lost interest in our table. I doubt that we will return.

I took my kids for some smores. End up ordering snacks. lol. Half Turkey and Brie sandwich with clam chowder. Both were really good. My son ordered the tuscan sandwich, that was also good. My daughter had the itailian sausage pizza and that was so so for me. The apple pie and smores were the cake. Fun and good. For drinks we had ice coffee, frozen hot chocolate and raspberry ice tea. All drinks were really good. To top that off we had top notch service from Daniel. Who does it all. Made the sandwich, made the drinks, cashier and waitress. I would definately come here again just to have great service from Daniel. Cosi is a great late night snack place that is kid friendly.

How does a chef ruin chicken and waffles? I went for sunday brunch and the food was horrible...soggy waffles and greasy chicken. The waiter was nice and offered me another entree but I had already lost confidence.  I would not recommend it!

First of all, my experience at Luke was just perfect. In my opinion, Luke is the best of Besh. It was my last night there while on a business trip so, I sat at the bar. The real benefit of sitting at the bar of a wonderful restaurant like Luke is informative conversations with the bartender is possible. They work there and have had everything on the menu several times. I stuck with the hors d'oeuvres (p&j oysters, crawfish boudin, gumbo, salad and a few raw oysters), Every dish was just delightful and forever memorable. Luke is a mandatory go-back for me.

Happy hour is now $0.75 per oyster! (Not $0.50) Still one of the best deals in town. Oysters taste so fresh that you don't need to put any sauce on it. Seafood gumbo has huge chunks of oysters in it. Yum!

Saturday
The food was great even the coffee. Had grits and a cup of crab bisque. Loved all the flavors. It was like a party in my mouth. The only thing I would suggest is that they add to their staff not enough help for the amount of people being served. But other then that everything was great

Great restaurant with a good range of excellent entrees.  Everything is good and consistent here - food, service, atmosphere.  This is a solid choice for lunch and dinner.  It is a John Besh restaurant so that is what you expect and what he delivers.

Everything was delicious. Amazing service - Rich was our server for the night- very friendly and entertaining guy. For appetizers we got the Brussels sprouts and the flammenkuchen. The Brussel sprouts were incredibly flavorful - highly recommend. For main, the shrimp and grits was amazing. Rich brought us a free sundae dessert after which was delicious too. Best dinner in Nola!

Overall Great food with a few minor hiccups. Its a little cluttered in the restaurant, it does get Busy so make reservations ahead of time(a must). My meal which will probably be my next one also is by far the LUKE BURGER WITH FRIES....amazing. I'd definitely go back and the hiccups I wrote don't bother me that much but if I'm being anylitycal than Yes. GREAT RESTAURANT

I had a short love affair with John Besh's Luke.  Ironically, I went here the day after I ate at another of Chef Besh's restaurants - Domenica.  

It started slow... the bar staff was inviting and I was there on business.  I stumbled right into happy hour, where the local oysters are 50 cents each and the drink specials are nice.  The oysters were amazing; I had a dozen all by myself.

That first night, I moved on to the crab bisque and the champagne au peche -- so good.  I'd consulted a really sweet bartender who told me the bisque was a better choice than the seafood gumbo.  I liked him... he seemed honest.  It was velvety smooth and had such a wonderful sweetness from the crab.   O-M-G.  From there, I had the shrimp and grits.  Super big, so flavorful, and just the right portion.  I decided to switch drinks to the St. Germaine.  Not as good as the champagne au peche, but nice and crisp from the pear flavor.  Not like I could take any back to my hotel room.  Since I'm not a dessert person, I just finished with coffee.  

Everything was so good that I had to come back for another round the very next night.  I sat in the very same seat the bar, where the same bartender and oyster shucking specialist greeted me.  I think the guy shucking oysters had a little bit of a crush, but I was more interested in those oysters.  Crazy good.  This time, I had to try the cochon.  A girl next to me had it the night before and it just looked so good.  A pork lover's dream.  Fresh bratwurst, pork shank, pork belly, and fresh sauerkraut.  Rich and salty, savory, the hint of vinegar.  I can't even explain how good it was.  You just have to try it.  I ate every last bite.

I'm so in love with this restaurant, and the very next chance I get to visit New Orleans, this is where you'll find me.

If you only try one creole place this would be a good one. Its on the upscale side with amazing service, but you'll fit in just fine wearing jeans.

The menu has a great range of options, from the awesome burger to the duck. I've been twice and all of the dishes have been winners. Don't forget to order dessert, they have the best bread pudding I've had in town.

Highly recommended:
The Luke burger
The shrimp and grits
The shrimp etouffee
Dessert

I work in the medical field and the white lab/doctor coats the waitstaff wears, just throws me off. Also the kitchen rags they use as dinner napkins. I get it, they trying to pull something different off, right? The food was okay, not great as I heard it would be. Worth skipping and eating some place else.

Best drink: French 75
Best food: shrimp and grits with crab
Best dessert: bread pudding 

The atmosphere is welcoming, fun, comfortable, and the waiters were very accommodating and helpful with selections! The French 75  is awesome, they make it with cognac and an egg white, which definitely mellows out the lemon and champaign. GREAT DRINK, FOOD AND SERVICE.!

This company just installed and unit for 7000$ and it never worked. I am already in claims court over their thieft. They will give you run around and won't do anything. Don't use them . They are thieves

Got some free WiFi
Tiny buns can't hold my meat
Thank you for smoking

This place has more flat screens than Best Buy! Mix in Sunday Ticket, free WiFi , good bar food and beer selection and you have yourself a prime out of house Fantasy Football command center my friends.

If you don't smoke than this probably isn't your place. It is the most spacious neighborhood bar I've been in yet, but seemingly everyone was burning cancer sticks and you will want to fabreeze when you leave.

I was about to flip a coin on whether to get a burger or wings and the decision was made for me when I read you can choose fries or Tatter-Tots with the burgers...I love me some tots! The burger was good, nothing special really except the nice sized patty was served on a bun the size of a biscuit! lol, I was most impressed that it held up throughout. I did see many plates of wings and they looked top notch. Oh, and the Tot's were a heaping mound a mini-fried potato goodness.

Lastly I'll say that I thought everyone was great, staff and regulars alike. The regulars were outgoing and friendly. The guys and girls working were outgoing and attentive.

As the Governor of California once said, I'll be back

Good food. But service is inconsistent and chaotic. Most recently I went in on Wednesday, placed a large order to be picked up on Thursday.  When I came for the pickup they had not even started preparing my order. I sat at a table for 45 minutes and waited with my family sitting in the car and my guests parked in front of my house waiting for me to get to my own party . What's worse is that while I waited they were preparing other pick up orders for people who weren't there yet before they started mine.  Can't say I will never again call in a small lunch order for myself but I won't sit down for dinner in Hachi again and won't be using them for party platters or catering.

Wow! Rabbit pate was Delish. Crawfish bisque was Delish. The king crab was awesome and oh so sweet and we had three different kinds of oysters in our dozen. We didn't get the 50 cent oysters but the ones we got were well worth it!!! However... Parking was OBNOXIOUS!!! The Hilton hotel valets are ASSES!!! The valets threatened us with tickets and towing when we parked in free local parking out front. What a joke! We offered a tip as yeah they're trying to work (I get it) but they tore it up and threw it in the passengers side of the car when we left. Unprofessional to say the least!!! The local sheriff watched the whole scenario and said the valets always give people a hard time and gave us the managers name and number. Thank you sheriff! Luke is a fine restaurant but the Hilton has to work on their courtesy!

I couldn't rave enough about how amazing the service was here. Shout out to our waiter, Kevin, who was working on his birthday! We got here and there was no wait at all. The staff from the hostess, to our waiter, to our busser were all very friendly. We were in NOLA to celebrate our friends bday and they overheard and without asking, provided us with a happy bday bread pudding which was delicious! 

The oyster were huge! They even put hearts in our French75. :-)

This place was huge disappointment. It's pricey and the food is mediocre with capital 'm'. I had a tasty crab bisque which had a heavy taste of old bay. It was serviceable salty and spicy. Not terrible. My friend had the shrimp and grits. Shrimp really over cooked as if it had been sitting around for a while. An expensive cocktail that was very sweet. I had salad with fried oysters, avocado, and bacon. Oysters were fine, hardly any avocado, and totally generic salad. This would all be fine but the food is truly expensive. A thousand better values in New Orleans than this place.

I didn't get too crazy here because I was alone with my kids, and they won't share anything cool with me. However, the service and food were great. I loved the look of the bar and the floor. Very classic and tasteful. I had the monsuer (or something). Its a fancy ham and cheese. Their fries are DELISH. Also, bottled Coke?! Whaaaaat! Loved it.

In terms of food, Luke is really a 3.5, but I'm rounding up because the atmosphere and service were really great. The Croque Madame and pomme frites were delicious, and, though it's probably a seasonal thing, if you spot their pickled watermelon rind on the menu--GET IT!

My food took too long. I think I waited about 45 minutes to an hour. I ordered 3 different orders. 2 general tso chicken and a sesame chicken. Let's just say it wasn't appetizing. It doesn't taste like typical chinese food. There was no air condition inside. The guy who I think owns it or runs it was nice, and offered a cold drink free of charge.
Great service and food taste fresh! The lunch special offers a large amount of food for a great price! Got the salmon and chicken hibachi and a chicken katsu bowl.

The baked oysters are a must they are unbelievably wonderful.  It was one of my favorite dishes of our stay in Nola.  For our entrees I got the shrimp and grits and my husband had the hamburger.  Both we good and would order again.

for starters, the oyster happy hour cannot be missed. $0.50 per oyster and 1/2 price bar from 3pm to 6pm daily. these are local oysters (the kumamotos etc are regular price).  

waitstaff is efficient and friendly. great gumbo. delicious cochon de lait. excellent bratwurst. heaping portions for an affordable price without sacrificing quality. casual easygoing atmosphere. 

my only complaint are the tables can be a bit small for a party of 4... especially if you are ordering apps in addition to an entree. also bathrooms are outside of the restaurant in the adjacent lobby.

Might be the best burger in town.  Juicy, tender, well seasoned, tender bun, and awesome flavor.  We really enjoyed the happy hour specials as well. Wonderful selection of local and craft beers. The oysters were fresh and briney. 

Only reason they didn't get 5 stars was service.  I'm  not sure if she was in the weeds or just not feeling her rhythm, but we along with the tables next to us were felling neglected.  It seemed like she was distressed. 

Overall wonderful experience and look forward to our next visit
Coffee was quite good. The French country decor was cool. however,  limited menu, sausage a little sweet, service a tad slow even when the place was not that busy.

Happy hr: Raw oysters 75 cents each..ordered 1.5 dozen.
Fried oyster $1.25 each 6 each
Drinks 50% off: Silver Saints and Bufala Negra 
Door #3 super good
The Chelsea with rose and strong!

The food was pretty good, not quite as fantastic as I'd expected, but the portion size was definitely worth it. The boudin Benedict was a little dry and bland. Service was great, we happened to go on a Sunday for breakfast before a Saints game so everything running smoothly and quickly was a blessing. It got a little busier after we'd received our food, so I'd recommend going earlier than later. Would probably order something different next time, but would definitely recommend overall

I was really looking forward to eating here after all the suggestions.  The mint julep and old fashioned were not horrible but definitely not great.  The hamburger looked amazing but lots of bread.  Bread pudding was sadly my least favorite I've had in NOLA.

Side note baked oysters amazing and nice staff.

Great happy hour with oysters and strong drinks! 
Beside that though the menu was limited when we were there for happy hour. 

We didn't make reservation for happy hour but next time will try the brunch.

After reading about how great the happy hour was, we decided we needed to try Luke.  We were a group of 8, headed in at 3pm for happy hour.  The food and drinks were fine, but the service was the worse.  From snooty hostess to the chippy servers, we felt unwelcome.  These are snobby people working here, they seemed annoyed they had to serve us.  Never again.

Wow this place was such a let down. I had heard a lot about it. Heard it equated to Nolas, so friends and I came on in. We endured  more than 45 minutes of wait, so much so that at least two other groups of old ladies got into fights with the staff. "Where's my table!? I expect Service. There WILL be a complimentary bottle of wine at our table. No make that two!" Amusing for me, over a round of drinks. But once we did sit, we were treated only with very average food.

By this time I was sick of fried food so I ordered red-fish expected a nice grill. Instead it was the same old fried fish, except it was even soggy! Meaning, it was probably sitting around for some time. Served with some potatoes and limp green beens. Whoopdedoo... Certainly not worth (19). The gumbo was a highlight though (4.5). It was extremely seafoody with a well balanced fishy taste. I should have had that as my entree. 

In all, everyone's food was pricey and overratted. Wasn't horrible, but really for that kind of money we expected at least a little more.
Food was good service was excellent. Sat at the bar and had stuffed oysters, gumbo and 1/2 doz raw oyster. Oysters were great, gumbo was good

Talk about not judging a book by its cover. A friend recommended Luke so I thought it would be a great place to have our first Nola meal upon arriving to the city. When we walked in, I was a little disappointed with the atmosphere-- it was very bright inside and seemed a little bland, decor wise; however, the menu definitely piqued our interests. Wow, so much amazing dishes to choose from, and the food, excellent. We ordered the escargots au gratin as an appetizer and I went with the shrimp and grits for my entree. It was the perfect amount and so very delicious. I will definitely be back!

I typically get a Filet when in the mood for steak, but the menu only offered a Ribeye. I was skeptical but I my goodness.  Best restaurant Ribeye ever.  The flavor was good and steak melted in my mouth.  Friend had the $18 dollar burger and it was worth it.    I will return for the steak next trip.

This is truly one of St. Louis' best little hidden gems. It would be a perfect spot to woo an out-of-towner looking to get a real sense of our culture. Or a great place to bring a day-time date for a cozy, intimate setting and a shared cup of pure love. 

The tea is done right! I don't know of any other place in town that does teas like this. The ginger turmeric tea, is straight up just ginger and turmeric. It feels like a kick in the chest,  that your body really needed. Seriously, if you are not used to strong teas it might take you aback. But I guarantee you will be craving the stuff soon enough. You will have dreams where you are floating in a cup of Hippy Hot Chocolate with that ginger just infusing every pore of your body. I promise.  

The place is tiny, hence the name Smalls. It's basically a wide hallway with benches and tables along the side. It doesn't seat many people. But what it lacks in space it makes up for in sheer adorableness. At the back of the space, you will find Lisa. I am still not sure if it's the tea or her warm welcoming smile, but I always feel better after a trip to Smalls.

From the reviews I read before coming here I fully expected a not-so-great experience, but I was really craving spinach artichoke dip so was willing to give it a chance.

My first impression was the smell of burnt bread, which after a while I got used to, but is really pungent at first. I already expected the meal not to be great but there was no turning back now.

I ordered my dip and they said it would take a few minutes, which really didnt bother me. Then after 5 minutes they said it was going to take a little longer so while I waited they offered me a free drink or soup. It's funny bc I wasn't even waiting for a long time, but they are obviously trying to keep their customers happy and I have no problem with that. In fact, I appreciate the fact that they acknowledged how long the food was taking. If this situation happened in NY, they'd be probably give you a dirty look and some fake apology. I had no complaints about the dip and the soup was good as well (reminded me of spaghettios sauce, my favorite as a kid). Overall not bad. Way better than I expected it to be.

Love, Love Loved the pressed cochon sandwich here. Ate here twice for the sandwich and ordered 3 more to take home on the plane so that my family could experience how great the sandwich was!!! Wasn't as good after 6 hours of travel but I will definitely be back when I'm in NOLA. The staff is super friendly and the atmosphere is really nice.!!

Our entire experience at Lüke was stellar from start to finish. We started out at the bar and met one of the nicest bartenders of all time. Wish I had gotten her name - she was blonde and fun. Our server Nicholas made fantastic recommendations for our meal. The Brussels Sprouts were the best I've ever had. Gumbo was great. Heirloom Tomato salad was fresh and perfect, and the ham was a nice touch. I am not a shrimp and grits person but Nicholas insisted I get them with crab meat. It was the best dish I've had in New Orleans. I recommend sitting in the back room, it's a little more rowdy and seeing the open kitchen was fun. Love Lüke!

I just ordered a salad from them and returned to my office, I sure wish I remembered to request dressing on the side.  This salad is gross, it is literally drenched in so much dressing that I don't even know what I am eating besides the dressing, it ruined what would have been a good salad and it's too late for me to return it because I don't have time to go back there.  I don't understand how anyone would think a salad needs to be soggy with that much dressing, the amount they put should NOT be the norm.

They didn't shade me for ordering my steak well done. And when it came out, it was not burnt at all, but juicy, perfect, and wonderful! Not many people can do that!

Drinks were yumtastic and the atmosphere was chic! I'll definitely go here again!

Luke has a fun, energetic atmosphere. My husband and I came here twice during our four-day trip to New Orleans. The drinks were wonderful and the food was amazing. Great service also. We will absolutely return next time we're in NOLA!

We stopped by here on a whim following what was close on yelp, and it was a great place for a lunch. It was clear people came for the oysters, and I had never eaten them before so opted for the fried oyster salad. It was a delicious babystep! My boyfriend was also happy with the gumbo- he said it was the best he had tried.

We have devolved completely into madness.

So we're all like "Screw it, we are (Wo)Men of the World. We are living for today, in this glorious NOW with nothing to hold us back from doing all the things we want to do and We Will Do These Things with flaming torches and galloping horses and clear voices echoing in to the night YES, WE WILL HAVE THE CHARCUTERIE EVEN THOUGH WE HAVE TOTALLY HAD CHARCUTERIE FOR LIKE 3 DAYS IN A ROW! BUT SCREW IT AND ONE MORE MINT JULIP, PLEASE!!"

Maybe we should abandon our Best Burger search and refine this shit a bit.  It's starting to look like we should be doing Best damn Charcuterie search.  Because that's what we are doing. We just haven't named it.

The best part of the charcuterie?  Relishes. 100% hardcore relish party.  Pickled watermelon rind and pepper relish and house made mustard brought this meats platter from Regular Awesome to Awesome Awesome.  

We all ate off each others plates and we all agreed that everyone's meal was totally fantastic.  But, I mean - of course it is.  John Besh has his shit tight.  (also:  dude was THERE that night and came over to say hi to our table and he was really smiley and nice and we were drunk and kinda starry eyed about the whole thing)

When we got home later that night Chris said "that butter had no idea how good it was".  I don't know if that butter will ever know how good it was.

Had an early dinner at Luke's and it was awesome!  Restaurant was busy but we made a reservation and got seated in no time.  We skipped the appetizers and went straight for the happy hour oysters (50 cents each from 3-6pm!).  Oysters were fresh, went down smooth, and were very nicely sized too.  We ordered two dozen, and then ended up getting 2 dozen more because it was that good and so inexpensive.  My husband also ordered the grilled rib eye - cooked medium well - and it was perfectly seasoned and grilled.  I'm not a huge meat eater and I thought it was delicious.  The fries also hit the spot - perfectly seasoned and piping hot.  Would definitely return to Luke's on my next visit to New Orleans!

Easily the best sushi in Bucks County. Where do I begin? Kani salad - amazing. Tuna pizza - ridiculous!!! The Sunrise appetizer is "off the chain". Sushi is super fresh. The closest thing to Manhattan sushi you can find around here.

Best damn raw and fried oyster I ever had. The 3 to 6pm happy hour is an incredible deal. My daughter and I ate our weight in them. The fried oysters were so perfect that I crave them daily. The spicy ranch dipping sauce was drinkable. We sat at the bar and were just in heaven. JUST GO!

Lüke is a magical place that manages something few restaurants in New Orleans have come close to: taking me away. 

When I walk through those revolving doors, I'm whisked back to my beloved Philadelphia. The European influence is evident on this menu, and I feel like Chef Besh captured the essence of what a cuisine does as it mutates over the years. He just skipped the 50 years it would take for his menu to evolve by being chef-smart and pulling it together. 

Others have complained about the beer and wine in odd glassware, but it somehow suits the restaurant. I feel like I should bring my grandfather here for lunch. Retired lawyers and doctors and high-powered business people would spend their morning here, reading papers and sipping a beer and chatting. Lüke feels like the Galatoire's for a different class of people. 

I've eaten at Lüke a couple ways: straight dinner, just apps, and a mixed meal. The very best decision I made was P&J oysters (a dozen for $13!), the poached yard-egg salad sans bacon (oddly filling), and a slice of Black Forest inspired cake (rich, creamy, heavy with Chantilly cream). The oysters here are always delish, and the price of the local oysters (P&J, for those not in the know) is really competitive for a restaurant in the CBD. 

If Lüke is my magical fantasyland of a restaurant, why only three stars?
Le sigh. 
Say it with me: the service.  

The first time my lady and I came, our server looked like she was on speed or something. She was spacy and wired and jumpy without ever making eye contact. Of course we had a chat with the manager. I honestly thought it was a fluke because there were three other servers working the back room (where we sat) that were amazingly attentive and charming. 

Then I jump on Yelp and see that everyone else hates the service. But...but...but I love Lüke! I don't want to hate Lüke! This is my little oasis in all of New Orleans! Am I deluded? 

So I visit again. Similar experience. 

And the third visit is really what sealed my review. 
I came on a Sunday night after work. I sat at the bar with my Kindle. There were two bartenders, hopping around Doing Important Things™. Between making drinks, gossiping with waiters, avoiding the managers, and running back to the kitchen, I sat for 20 minutes before anyone greeted me. Then the really surly bartender threw my menu at me as she walked past. That was surprising. The rest of my meal unfolded in similar, odd fashion with long periods of being ignored followed by rushed service. Having to defend my plate of oysters kept me amused which was good because I probably would have lost it and snapped at someone after the 4th attempt to remove them before I was finished AS I WAS SLURPING. It was like a game, only I would always be the loser. The food runners who brought my salad and my dessert didn't speak to me when they set the food down, but I don't think I can fault them on that. I was obviously reading. It was clear that I was busy so I think they were trying to respect that. 

That dinner took two hours; to say it borders on excessive for one person, seated at the bar, with no cooked food is an understatement. 

I think I'll keep coming to Lüke, but my expectations have shifted. (I'm getting so much better at managing my disappointment.) Lüke, if you ever shape up, I'll call you like that proverbial ex-boyfriend who promises to join the Army and get things together. 

Accessibility notes: Revolving door at entrance is not automatic. Restaurant gets very loud at peak hours. Back half of restaurant is up several steps. No braille menu or signage.
Great oyster happy hour. Some entrees are "German" inspired...  more like New Orleans food wearing a lederhosen.. Great apps though, hence the three stars.

Well I am in love. I came for a solo dinner and the food and atmosphere took me right back to my year in Paris. 

I opted to maximize tasting potential and ordered two smaller dishes instead of an entree. Well, for one person they're not really small! The pate was incredible. With the different mustards and jellies and pickled foods it felt like a playground for big kids. I had the heirloom tomato salad next, which was a big bowl of tomatoes and mesclun and cheese. It was a solid compliment to the rich, savory taste of the pate. I was sad to leave both dishes uncleaned but I could not fit any more food in to my belly! :) 

To drink I had a door#three (I think it's called?) which was very pretty but not mind-blowingly good tasting. I do however hail from DC aka land of the $15 cocktail so I have some heavy standards! I still enjoyed it.

Service was lovely and very minimal. My water stayed mostly full (they got a little busy towards the end of the meal) but once they realized it, they checked up on me more than average. Bravo.
Went here twice on a five day trip. The food and drinks were incredibly tasty and the service was amazing as well. Big thanks to Gary, making both nights very enjoyable.

Last night we had party of 4 went to this restaurant for dinner at 8pm.

We had ordered a whole lobster and a seafood platter with oysters, clams and shrimps.
First, we found that they did not have mussels, so the chef gave us more shrimps. But why don't they be honest and told us earlier!

Also, the most horrific part is, we ate the claws of the lobster. Then we opened up the body of the lobster. Then we found a LOT OF green, blue stuff inside the body. We had never seen a lobster with that many green stuff in it, I think it was tomalley. It was DISGUSTING. Then I googled it and found these warnings from FDA.

http://www.fda.gov/NewsEvents/Newsroom/PressAnnouncements/2008/ucm116927.htm

http://www.webmd.com/food-recipes/food-poisoning/20080728/fda-dont-eat-maine-lobster-tomalley

The chef came to our table, trying to say the lobster is fresh and fine and actually people will eat the tomalley. The chefs said the lobster is from Maine. And this is a rare They kept on defending themselves and the manager, was rude to us. But we are cancer scientists and we know all they were trying to defend was invalid. The overloaded green stuff was full of toxins. According to the FDA report, if we ate that lobster I won't be typing this review right now, I would be suffering from Paralytic Shellfish Poisoning (PSP), being intoxicated and we may die if we consumed too much. 

The manager told me that we should not eat the green stuff, in a rude way. Then I said why a big, upscale restaurant like this is serving toxic lobster to the guests on the table? If they are professional, they should inspect the lobster before serving us! They should not serve anything that may harm the guests!!!

Very bad experience. Extremely furious for what we had been treated. The health authority should come and investigate this and get the answer professionally. One lobster can kill not only the restaurant reputation, also can potentially kill someone.

Update: I have lodged the complaint to the health authority.

Matzo ball and roast chicken soup ($9 for a bowl) - 3 stars
We asked them for less salt in whatever dishes they could put less salt in and this was one of them! It was a delicious light broth to offset all the rich food we'd been having.

Stuffed P&J oysters 1/2 dz ($19) - 4 stars
A nice change from raw oysters but you probably can't eat more than 2.

Crispy Brussels sprouts ($14) - 5 stars
Probably my favourite dish and the best part is hat they give you a recipe for the dish at the end of the meal! Definitely gonna try to make this dish at home.

Jumbo Louisiana shrimp "En Cocotte" ($25) - 5 stars
Their star dish as they will tell you. The cheese and jalapeños made it taste like a Mexican dish, which was delicious.

The ambience and service cement the 5 stars. My favourite place in New Orleans so far!
Oyster happy hour is great, food is awesome! But service needs to be improved...takes forever for someone to pour water, takes forever to get the check...low standard for a tourism city.

An ok-experience, nothing to be missed.. We ordered-
Chicken n waffles- meh, the meat was ok, waffles were soggy and extremely sweet. not worth the price at all.
Shrimp n grits dish - pretty good
Coffee - meh
Best part was they accommodated couple of vegetarians in our party.. The server was very attentive and checked with the kitchen for options.. N everybody ended up with a decent breakfast.. Portions are small though.. You need a reservation .. service is pretty slow, even the coffee refills took forever.

This sushi place is a nice little gem located within the Wilmington Riverfront market. You can either grab freshly made sushi from their refrigerator area or you can sit down at the bar style table and order. The service is fast, and the portions are very generous. I had the seaweed salad, tuna roll, and salmon skin roll and all three were very delicious and very filling. I also drank a jasmine green tea beverage that was very refreshing. The only drawback is this place is closed on Sundays since it is located within the riverfront market.

This was very good experience.  We started off with the pate of rabbit and chicken livers which was very good.  It came with several different accompaniments.  I liked the stone ground mustard and pickles.  We also ordered a dozen oysters on the half shell ($.50 each for happy hour!!!) which were very good and plump, with a nice briny flavor.
I had the etoufee of blue crab and brown shrimp as a main course.  It lacked much crab, but the shrimp were perfectly cooked, as was the pasta (garganelli).  The sauce was rich and  delightful.  My wife had the nightly special, a spicy lamb meatball and pasta.  The meatballs were rich and delicious, and the pasta was cooked perfectly.  
The location in a hotel was odd at first, but the space is nicely appointed and good for any type of diner, from shorts and t-shirts to evening wear (we saw a little of both).
The only hiccup was the service, which was pretty slow.  Our server was friendly, but she seemed a bit overwhelmed and had several other tables (I counted five) which seemed a bit excessive.  Perhaps since it was early (5pm) they had an early rush and reinforcements had yet to arrive.  Both of my experiences at a John Besh restaurant have left a lot to be desired in the way of service.  Maybe it's bad luck, but in any event it's frustrating.
Despite the service, the food is reason enough to look forward to returning on our next trip to New Orleans.

The food was great. Me and my 5 year old went on a Thursday night about 7:30. Staff was more than pleasing. They adjusted tables so we could sit side by side. Our waiter was great and did everything he could to make it seamless for us. 

Will be back for sure!

Please go here!  We chose dinner here because of the rave reviews on Yelp and it didn't disappoint.  Nice relaxed gastro pub atmosphere.  Our waiter, Will, was so knowledgeable and patient with our questions.  I chose their most popular dish, the shrimp and grits.  Wow, I never knew grits could taste so good.  It was one of the best entrees I've had in years.  They have an extensive beer menu, also.  I'm still trying to find out where in Chicago they sell the beer I drank there.

Did someone say .50 cent oysters from 3-6pm EVERYDAY??!!
this has got to be the best deal in town??
unless you know of some other nice rest establishment in Nola with a better deal. holla at me!! 

After all the superhigh prices and average tasting gumbo, jambalaya and Poboys! i was glad to have found Luke's and their oysters!! 
I'm no oyster connoisseur but you can't beat .50 cent!! 
the oyster not the rapper! =P 
It's right on St Charles on the parade route and right beneath Hilton St Charles!! 
oh yea, half price beers and cocktails as well from their menu!! 
def HAPPY TIMES!
Delicious lunch at this very fine restaurant. An excellent vibe with top notch service and food.

Yeeha! More amazing Nawlins' eatin'.  Yelp pointed me to Luke, so thanks to all those hard workin'  "yelpas" (as they like to say in Boston). 

Luke provided a fantastic lunch. Cocktails were a must, so we set ourselves up with a French '75 and Sazerac. There was a Herloom Tomatos salad on the specials menu - 2nd best edible of our entire trip (beaten only by Delachaise's Apricot Riesling Creme Brulee). Really amazing flavors. 

Wifey got the crab meat omlette, which illicited a "yay" response. I got the Cochon au lait pressed sandwich, which fullfilled all my shredded river of pork dreams. 

In regards to the whole look of luke - it has the french Bistro tiled thing going on. But in addition to that, all the waiters look like 1950's lab technicians (or pharmasists), with white coats, notebooks in breast pocket, and black rimmed glasses. There are a ton of interesting decor choices -  newspaper racks, a still behind the bar, animal head above the bar. All good stuff. 

Luke is a "must visit"  to anyone visiting New Orleans.

Went to brunch here on a Sunday. Was pretty obvious I had a rough case of the booze flu, so our server was quick to suggest and deliver a bloody mary. It was a bit horseradish-y for my liking, but after asking for less on the next one, I couldn't have asked for much better. We split a soft shell crab sandwich, and literally had more than enough food for two people to take home leftovers. The service was attentive, and personable. And the food was STELLAR. I've always heard that it was a bit pricey, yet I found it pretty affordable for the quality. Highly suggest this place.

My girlfriend and I came to New Orleans for the weekend. We ordered oysters and they were so fresh, huge, and delicious. . We also ordered one order of shrimp and grits which was plenty to share for both of us. 

Would highly recommend!
Food is great, service needs a lot of help, 2 waitresses in the entire restaurant on a Friday night and a packed parking lot. Took 1 hour to get the check...hire more staff please.

Rabbit + Chicken Liver Pate. OMG. To die for. I mean, to die for. Like, mmmmmmmmm. I could have ordered two more and just eaten pate all night. Also good, the lamb, the chicken, the wine, the cocktails... If you're looking for a casual yet classy dinner in NOLA, go here.

Came here on a whim for a late lunch/ early dinner. They have happy hour on Sunday- discount oysters and half price cocktails. We split the corn and crab chowder and gumbo. Both were delicious! I preferred the chowder. We also split the shrimp en cocotte. That was so good. Huge shrimp and sausage on a bed of jalapeño grits. Yum! We also had an order of fries. Service was good. Definitely a favorite meal while visiting NOLA.

First meal in New Orleans!! It was delicious! Service was great, a little blooper in one of the entrees ordered but they corrected it immediately.  Great customer service, plus it's happy hour!:-) (I got the Mahi with vegetable medley)

This place is not clean. When we went there were flies flying around.  My son was so bothered by it that he refused to eat. Since then we have never went back.  We love sushi.  We went back to our favorite place on Bustleton pike.

I had no idea that this place was owned by a celebrity chef. I came here on a whim after eating dinner and headed home. Passing by, we decided to check it out. Unfortunately for us, the place was booked solid. The hostess apologized that she didn't have any availability tonight and wanted to see if we wanted to wait for an opening.

Almost immediately, a lady in glasses and grayish hair smiled and came over and see if maybe we would be interested in dining at the bar, even though it was completely filled.  When we couldn't find anywhere to sit at the bar, the lady re-approached us, and offered a series of other wonderful recommendations in the area that we could try since we couldn't get seated at a table or a bar. She gave us a brief introduction as to why they were such a busy location and that the company has a few other fairly similar restaurants. She told us how she absolutely loved working there and enjoying the great food at the other restaurants as well as that one we were at.

Before we had another minute to think about it, she asked to see if we were interested in dining at the end of the bar. We advised her that we already ate and was looking for dessert only. She immediate gave us some fabulous suggestions on popular desserts and offered us to get the Gateau Basque, because she's been eating it for years!

The waitress at the bar greeted us and was incredibly nice. We had a small discussion about oysters and where they were from. We ended up getting a dozen oysters. Although the PJ Oysters weren't anything too special for me, it was still very fresh and delicious. I think I'm biased because I'm a big fan of Kumamoto (which they have) and Shigoku. As mentioned above, we ordered the Gateau Basque, which was basically a vanilla sponge cake with creme fraiche and Louisiana berry marmalade poured on top. It was incredible.

As far as desserts go, that was the highlight of all the desserts we ordered in a week's timespan in New Orleans. Before we finished, the lady in glasses came to check up on us again. She was very nice and asked to make sure that we enjoyed the food. She told us that she'll check on us again before we leave. But we didn't get to say goodbye! She was probably busy making sure the rest of the patrons were having a good time.

The staff here is worth recommending on coming here to New Orleans. The food is great, and the service is incredible. We had a stunning of a time, thanks for the Southern hospitality of Luke.

I am so lucky to have Elm as my friendly neighbourhood coffee shop!  Great food, drinks and service.

The food:  OMG NOMS!  The sandwiches are delicious and HUGE!  There are two choices (warm and cold) for sandwiches at both breakfast and lunch.  Nate (the owner) tweets the sandwiches everyday so you can check if you're into them before heading over.  

Elm also makes fresh muffins every morning that are drool worthy.  I often get there just as the muffins are coming out of the oven and Nate makes sure to warn me not to eat them while driving because I'll burn myself - MacDonald's take note: this is how you avoid crazy lawsuits!

Drinks:  I actually didn't like lattes all that much until I started going to Elm.  While Elm doesn't offer a lot of different flavours, they make up for it by making their own  vanilla syrup (I think).  They also have great sodas and make their own hot chocolate!

Prices are equivalent to Starbucks but quality is much better!  Service is friendly and fast.  Great atmosphere - makes me wish there was more seating available!

They really need to think about employing more people, or better qualified people. Today is the second time I had a bad experience due to under staffing. First time was an elderly man by himself working the bar and tables, both were busy so it took him a while to get to us. Then today I placed an order for pick up. A cheesesteak & fries. When I got there, there was only one guy working again. I asked about my order, then he spent 10 minutes serving alcohol before checking on my order. He comes back and tells me there's only one cook and that my food would be AT LEAST 20 minutes (meaning they hadn't even started cooking it yet). I've eaten here before and the food isn't bad, that's if you have time to wait.

So as I always am when I'm reviewing restaurants I was traveling for work. This restaurant happened to be located in my hotel. Score for me since I didn't have to just walk downstairs! 

I ate two meals here. I ate my breakfast on the second day and had dinner my first day. Breakfast wasn't anything special. The dinner was very good. They have a happy hour and offer 1/2 priced drinks and 50 cent oysters. Which is a great deal if your interested in drinks and oysters. I had the shrimp and grits. Shrimp and grits happens to be one of my favorite meals. There's was very good! They serve it in a small black cast iron pan and the grits were cheesy, and the gravy/sauce was VERY tasty. So much I used my bread to mop it up. If you are in the area try it out. The menu isn't huge but they seem to do a good job with what they offer.

What a wonderful find!  We stopped in here for a drink and to get change for the streetcar - ended up staying for dinner in this fabulous french restaurant.  The raws were delicious, the beet salad was yummy, but the shrimp and grits were a work of art.  The white cake with apples and creme fraiche was decadent.  I tried their absinthe frappe - and though it has a strong licorice flavor, it was fun to sip all evening.  We missed the happy hour which was over at 6pm, but during oyster season they offer raws for .25 a piece.  They were a buck apiece regular which was the going rate as far as I saw.  Will definitely go back here and also look for other restaurants by this owner.  Excellent!

Great ambiance, while also being a close walking distance break from the hustle and bustle and price gouging that the quarter does so well. 

The bar staff was amazing and super nice.

Crawfish Bisque was amazing and the happy hour was killer for drinks and oysters. In the words of terminator, "I'll be back"...

Had a great time at Luke.  Upscale but not stuffy, with a staff that was friendly, acommodating, and attentive but didn't hover and read our table very well.  We enjoyed a really nice dinner with drinks and wine, and were not rushed in any way even though we lingered laughing and talking for quite a long time.  The food was all good, but I especially enjoyed the escargot and my friend's pork shank.  Beyond that, being there with good friends, feeling the bright, comfortable, classic American broiler ambience, vibe and energy made it an excellent experience.
Great atmosphere, great shrimp and grits, and great cold seafood.  Sometimes the service can be a little off if they're slammed, but it's not much of an issue.

Stumbled in. And basically never came out. We were here for three days and kept returning because the food was exquisite and the service (sybille?) made you feel special! She seemed busy but somehow managed to acknowledge everyone and even make jokes to entertain while you waited. Happy hour had .75 oysters and great prices on drinks! When she found out we're were honeymooning she made sure to congratulate us and offer us a drink! Which in turn made us stay longer and order more  great place to come over and over!

Great shrimp and grits, cool place and overall good service.

Oh yeah the rabbit pate, you must try the rabbit pate.

Holy crap this place is gotten so many good reviews since the last time I was here. You can come here for really cheap oysters and the most savory food ever for happy hour. I think I went back three times during Mardi Gras, because all the other restaurants just weren't hitting the same spot! I will return next time in NOLA
Food was good.  Tiny portions.  Service was severely lacking.  They are not quick.  Our food showed up roughly about an hour or more from time of order.

HANDS DOWN BEST MEAL I HAVE HAD IN NEW ORLEANS DURING MY TRIP!!

Came here on a Friday afternoon, and even contemplated whether if we should eat here since it is slightly out of our budget (this place is more like a 2.5$ rather than a 2-$$ sign restaurant). Nonetheless, we figured we're here anyway, looked at the pictures, and decided that we didn't want to miss out. We were so glad we made that decision. 

We sat down, and wasn't sure what we wanted to order. our waiter gave us some recommendations and we ended up order the Friday daily special (Court-Boullion) with their seafood gumbo (which counts as a soup!), and their Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte".

The seafood gumbo arrived first, and was stuffed with literally all types of seafood! They had shrimp, crawfish, and even two whole oysters!! The taste of the gumbo was fantastic, I don't know how else to describe it. 

The daily special (Court-Boullion) and the shrimp and grits (shrimp "en cocotte") arrived after we finished our gumbo. They both looked beyond heavenly. My boyfriend was so happy with the shrimp and grits that he said "All shrimp and grits should be served like that"!! The presentation of both of the dishes were fantastic, and both dish was totally worth what we paid for! Plenty of seafood, big, fresh, deveined shrimp. The food was not oily nor too salty, yet powerfully flavorful. The cheese on top of the grits, beneath the shrimp, soaked up all the flavor. Every bite was blended with all different kinds of flavor. 

I don't know how else to describe this place, but if you want to spoil yourself with good creole food before leaving NOLA, this is the place to be!! This is as good as it gets!
I thought this would be one of those over-hyped, celebrity chef affairs, but it was quite good.

rice and fish had no flavors
especially the rice was not prepared properly for sushi rice
tasted like whole food sushi
I'd rather go to nyc to have some real sushi from Azabu or Sushi Nakazawa

Service was mediocre.
Soup was great.
Oyster salad was not good. It showed up cold and small for an entree salad. Not worth it.
French 75 was great though.
Great food. Wonderful atmosphere. Great service.  Had the Luke Burger.  It was massive and very tasty.

Came here for brunch during vacation. After reading the reviews I expected it to be absolutely fabulous but it was definitely a bit of a disappointment. The decor and service were impeccable I have nothing to say about that but the brunch selection was ehh. I was hoping for an amazing french toast or poached egg but other than some scambled eggs everything was pretty much a lunch option. The woman next to me must have been a little disappointed too because she asked the waiter to see if they could make her French toast but he said they could not make it for her. Seemed a little crazy since they just made it 20 minutes before for breakfast.  We started with the Brussel sprouts, crab bisque, and gumbo. The Brussel sprouts were delicious. The crab bisque and gumbo could have been much better. The gumbo tasted more like red beans and rice than anything. Then we shared the chicken and bisquit which was the biggest disappointment. The chicken was no better than anywhere else and the bisquit at popeyes is better than the one we had there. Maybe if we came for breakfast or lunch we would of had a better experience

Great food, great price, if you like oysters and are available 3 pm to 6 pm daily. Environment is good, restaurant is probably owned by Hilton, service is ok depends on which waiter or waitress you got. Forgot to mention, some beers are 50% off between happy hours as listed above.

My husband and I make it a point to go to Lüke every time we're in New Orleans because they never fail to please. The food is ALWAYS exquisite and is priced well for the quantity + quality. This past weekend I was in New Orleans on a girl's trip & we happened to visit Lüke during happy hour. OMG! What a deal (/steal)!! First of all their drinks & food are already amazing and most things were 1/2 price! Our server Rich kept us laughing (rolling!) the whole time, was very professional & did a Wonderful job taking care of us! We ordered P&J oysters, brussel sprouts (so ridiculous!), dessert and a variety of beverages. I'd never had raw oysters before & was not eager to try them bc of the texture, but once I did, I was sold! Our experience was so great that we came back the next day. Sadly, Rich wasn't on the schedule but we still enjoyed ourselves and everything else. Lüke is a definite must if you're in the area!

Located in downtown, right next door to the Hilton Hotel.

My husband and I decided to come here for their 3 pm happy hour (Happy Hour 3-6 pm daily: $0.75 raw oysters, $1.25 fried oysters, half off featured cocktails, beer and wine by the glass). 

After we walked in a little before 3 pm, we were greeted by the hostess. I asked her if we had to sit at the bar because we are interested in the happy hour deal. She told me that we can sit at a table if we would like (we were seated at a table). 

We ended up getting:

Door#Three, $10 prior to tax- There are 6 featured cocktails to choose from off of the happy hour menu and I am glad I went with this drink. I liked the pomegranate, lemon juice and mint flavors together. I wished my mint leave wasn't limp though that was served with the drink (sometimes presentation is part of the dining experience too). 

Riesling Wine By The Glass, $6 prior to tax- I didn't have any, but my husband did enjoy his white wine.

1.5 dozen raw oysters, $0.75 each (prior to tax)- The price was right for these little jewels and the wait time to get these out to our table was quick. But the majority of these oysters were gritty and still had some sand in them. I think they needed to be soaked/ washed off a bit more because tasting part of the salty gritty sand is definitely not good eats. 

1/2 dozen fried oysters, $1.25 each (prior to tax)- I have never had fried oysters and so I thought it would be worth trying. These oysters were pretty good with the 2 different textures (crunchy and hot with the cool and creamy inside). I would order fried oysters again. 

Complementary bread- Just a small baguette bread per person, pretty standard but good. Liked that each piece of bread was brought out warm. 
-----------------------
(Total= $36 After Tax)

Service was pretty friendly and attentive by both of our servers. We initially had a female sever and then halfway through, a male server took over. 

I think I would just come here for their strong drinks and fried oysters but pass on the raw oysters during happy hour (we had oysters over at St. Roch Market at the Elysian Seafood food vendor and their also have $0.75 oysters during happy hour. Their oysters were not gritty. We loved their fresh tasting oysters so much that we went twice during our NOLA vacation).
great food, opened late. service is a bit slow, but the food makes up for it. best place for tortas!

Absolutely fantastic!! They spoiled us, it was great food and great service. Elizabeth was our waitress and was so kind and accommodating, she brought us free appetizers and desserts!! Highly recommend!

This restaurant is on the higher end of $$, but has the service and food to justify the price. I was surprised to see Matzoh Ball soup on their menu along the crab bisque and lobster bisque that I expected to find. I had a bowl of the crab bisque for lunch, which came with a piece of french baguette and butter. It was a lovely lunch, and I would do it again.

A local guy recommended this place to us, said if we were looking for good gumbo, to come here. It was near our hotel, so we walked. But it's just as easy to Uber it there. When we arrived, we were impressed with the cleanliness, the kitschy local decor, and the calm of the entire place. We were greeted by two women, both smiling, and happy to seat us right away. 

We sat down and it felt like we had two servers. Both were getting drinks and asking us if we needed more of this or that. The menu, though small, has so many great options for localized cuisine. And the server had his favorites, and shared them with us!

I came for the gumbo, so that was first on my list. I also order oysters everywhere, and Luke has crab stuffed oysters, and of course I ordered them. The local guy and the server both recommended the shrimp & grits, so that was my main course. 

The food came out quickly. First the gumbo. I had shrimp or andouille sausage or oyster in every single bite! It was amazing! My only regret: I should have ordered the bowl. 

The stuffed oysters came out next. They were creamy and delicious! It was like the best crab stuffed anything you've ever eaten. It was rich, so the six they give you is perfect! 

Then the shrimp and grits!!! The grits were so cheesy!!! The shrimp was cooked perfectly, and there were more than I expected! The andouille sausage was diced added this smoky flavor. The whole dish was to die for! 

If I ever come back to NOLA, I'm coming here first!

This place is a huge sleeper in the Glenside area. With great service, amazing food, and very exciting drink specials, Jerzees is the place to be if you are looking for when going out with friends to start or end your night out. The environment is plenty of fun and the menu offers a huge variety. Definitely a place you should consider for any occasion!

i've heard that the food here is "Natural", sustainably produced meats & organic veggies
i went with a friend of mine to Foot Finesse & dropped in here afterwards, since it was just down the road, we could see it from there
Ethan & Brenda were friendly & helpful since i was a first time caller, the atmosphere is open & modern  yet simple,
i got the Spicy Beef with pinto beans Salad, the only dressing is the Chipotle dressing, which i got on the side because most chipotle items i've not been that fond of, but i've found something new that i'll go back for, Delicious (after a few bites i put all of the dressing in my salad)
i will try the Chicken next time, they have different meats & beans to choose from
OMG the Guacamole was To Die For with the Lime Chips (best $2. i've Ever spent)
i didn't have any but they do have Mexican beers there
http://www.chipotle.com/html/food.aspx
Excellent breakfast. My husband has the eggs in a jar and I had the southern breakfast. So tasty farm to table food.
Must! Must! Must stop! Especially if military, and definitely if Marine Corps. This is one of  our own who made it big, but did it right. Food is phenomenal! Staff is extraordinary!

Classic cajun restaurant with great crawfish bisque (opt for the bowl not the cup).  They had delicious (and very generous) chicken & rabbit pate. The fried quail wings were flavorful and great. The fried chicken & biscuits were more on the sweeter side with honey.

I ate at Lüke and now brunch will never be the same. 

Dwarfed by the huge Charles st. Hilton hotel right next door, one could easily walk right past this John Besh restaurant, but after the experience I just had there, it's safe to say that I'll sing praises of Lüke every time I'm asked about where to eat in New Orleans. 

The ambiance is professional and clean, casual and refined. Diners are greeted by quick-witted, smiling hostess and the servers here are incredible.  As a matter of fact, it's safe to say that this place has some of the best service I've ever received in a restaurant. And when you taste the food, you realize why the workers take such pride in their operation. 

The food at Lüke is magnificent. Southern cooking meets French influence here, and the food (and wine) options are all very tempting. 

Our server Nicholas recommended the crispy brussel sprouts. They were outstanding. Fried to perfection and cut into perfect bites, they were mixed with almond slivers, micro greens, and a fresh cheese, then dressed with honey. Get the brussel sprouts. They're insanely simple and delicious. 

We followed this appetizer with a crawfish bisque, which was also quite good. While I would have liked more crawfish tails included in the soup, the addition of a bread crumb stuffed crawfish head staring right back at you made the bisque a real treat!

The main dishes we shared were the Shrimp and Grits, and the Fried chicken on a biscuit. Both were mind blowing. The first involved Piping hot jalepeño cheesy grits which paired perfectly with shrimp, sausage, and a subtle but spicy red sauce, and the portion was larger than expected. The
Fried chicken was...well...fried chicken. But the fluffy, honey soaked biscuit upon which it rested and the over-easy organic egg it supported, came together and made for a damn good entree. 

Want great service and excellent food at a reasonable price? Eat at Lüke on Charles street. You will be glad you stopped by.
We ordered the raw oysters--they were huge, but very bland--and forgettable.  We heard great things about the chef, but can't attest to anything but the oysters.  Pass.

I came in at 9:30pm right before they closed (I work in a restaurant so I know that sucks, I'm sorry!) but the employees were happy to serve me with a smile. The food was delicious too. The nailed it all across the board. The only gripe I have, and I know it's not the employee's fault, is their new queso. It's just not good. Sorry but I'll stick to my yummy guacamole!
Great place in New Orleans to eat seafood. The oysters are incredibly fresh.  Highly recommended In New Orleans.

I love this place, named for John Besh's son, absolutely great for the 3 to 6 pm happy hour with actual NOLA people, friendly and fun, also, very good food, and the , as far, as I'm concerned, the best oyster shucker in town.

I came here a few nights ago and had one of the best meals. I had the barbecue shrimp which was to die for. The oysters were very fresh as well. Service was really great and I can't wait to return back to luke!

Great courtbouillion, seafood gumbo. Service (i.e, pacing between courses) was a bit uneven.

The very best bloody mary I've ever had, anywhere, anytime. 
I'd love to check out happy hour sometime, also looks amazing. 

Improve the service a bit and it's a "5".

We decided to have lunch here spur of the moment.  I am so glad we did.  The service is friendly and congenial, but not overbearing.  I ordered the BLT made with soft shell crab.  OMG, I wish I could have eaten more.  My memory stops there because all I can think about is that sandwich.  I do know my boyfriend loved his sandwich as well, but I thnk he liked mine better.  Either way, you can't go wrong. The crab was fried in a corn meal batter and was light, airy and meaty all at once.  The bread is also amazing.  A must go when in NOLA.

Went here for my birthday while in New Orleans on vacation.  Had the Shrimp and Grits and gumbo for starter.  Wanted to go to at least one John Besh restaurant while we were there and it didn't disappoint. Was very busy and noisy but that was to be excepted - there was a Saints game that night

AWESOME.  This place was great, literally everything we ate was well cooked from the oysters, shrimp to our hot dishes.  They have great happy hour specials as well and the service is extraordinary.  Our waitress was a local student and she was very helpful and was accommodated all of our needs.

CHECK THIS PLACE OUT!!

The service is slow (in a good, southern kinda way y'all) and the concierge had a bit of an attitude. That being said, our last day there a server named Kevin listened to our need to be done and out of the door by 5 to be at a wedding in the French Quarter. He accommodated all 6 of us amazingly and made every dish arrive and had us ready to go in less than 45 minutes. Amazing. Then he made sure we wouldn't forget him by gifting us a complimentary dessert (whoa...that brownie had us fighting to lick the plate) 

Great recovery by a wonderful server. The food is always excellent, you just might want to be really clear with your service expectations.

We were wowed. Lunch served until 4 with Happy Hour from 3 to 6pm. Staff was attentive without hovering. Food was good but the Happy Hour is incredible!  Raw oysters were .75 each, fried oysters 1.25 each with half price drinks. What's not to love? Good food with great prices. Wanna go back for more!

Went for dinner on our last night in New Orleans.  Pretty expensive but good food.  Highly recommend the Gumbo -- my wife had the crab bisque which was also very good.

My wife and I shared some of the shellfish and the brussel sprouts which were really good.  Nice spice to them.

One of the best bread puddings for dessert.

Simply awesome food - shared a plate of oysters with friends. Ordered the Luke burger, which exceeded my expectations. I've been overwhelmed with uniquely NOLA cuisine during my trip and it was nice to John Besh's take on the cheeseburger. Also, the fries are a thing of beauty, served in a decorative metal cup. Tasty too. My highest recommendation.

Happy hour for the win!! 

It really can't get any better than 50 cents an oyster.  The oysters were fresh, large and delicious.  They come pre-shucked so you don't have to do any dirty work.  Simply season them to your liking and slurp it down.  it was notable that none of the 60 oysters that we ordered had any sand in them.  Lüke -- you've really impressed me!

The servers were friendly and checked on us frequently.  Unlike most restaurants, happy hour applies to the whole establishment so you don't have to scout out a seat at the bar.  

Half price on wine, beer and specialty cocktails.  Now if only I can find an oyster spot like this back home....

This was one of my fav's in Naw'Leans!  John Besh, you've made a fan outta me!
Delicious oysters and great service. Fair prices for Happy Hour. Will return next time I am in NOLA!

I have soo many places to review for NOLA...but I chose Luke's to be the first place I wrote down...because...

FIFTY. CENT. OYSTERS.

yes. 50 cents. Happy hour. 3-6pm. weeknight. half off drinks. and...oh my gawd.... 50 cent oysters!!

My friends and I feasted. The bartender told us we ate half the ocean. 

The goods:
-The bartender was soo sweet!! Very friendly...even gave us a free drink :) 
-The oysters were soo fresh, juicy, and huge! (They were at least 3 times bigger than Acme's..fosho..) 
-Their Blue Crab Bisque was soooo delicious. creamy, with a little bit of a spicy kick, and pieces of chewy crab. 
-I suggest you sit at the bar. chitchat with the bartender and the locals. watch them shuck the oysters. Get another drink. 
-The place is very classy and pretty. wooden walls and decor. pretty lighting. 

Had a great time! If i had another day, I would have gone back!

Unfortunately I developed a TBM sandwich addiction a few years ago. Food poisoning from the aforementioned sammich nipped that one in the bud. Overpriced, rancid mozzarella and stoned or otherwise distracted staff.... yeahnotsomuch.

HAPPY HOUR OYSTERS!

Great deal for raw oysters. $.50 each or $6 for a dozen. 

They were very fat and plump oysters.

Another John Besh restaurant, but more casual. When we came for breakfast the oyster bar wasn't open yet. They still accommodated us and got the guy to shuck us some fresh raw oysters. Ordered a dozen and it was so good we wanted another half a dozen, but they gave us 10 and didn't charge us for the extra. That is super good service!!! Who eats raw oysters that early in the morning? I do!!!!! It's NOLA!

We also got the local crab omelet and shrimp and grits. when those dishes came out it did not look good at it. It was actually very delicious. Ingredients were fresh and everything was very flavorful. Don't judge a book by it's cover....thumbs up!

Great expectations but didn't live up to it. I asked the waiter "How do the soft-shell crabs look today?" "Excellent!" was his reply. Well, that was the skinniest softshell crab I have ever seen, and it was undercooked to boot. The dish, softshell crab with poached eggs over grits topped with a hollandaise sauce sounded too decadent. And it was. The softshell should have made this dish over the top. Instead, the itsy bitsy, skinny, undercooked crab ruined it. How disappointing that I was led astray by the waiter. In all fairness, the kitchen was slammed, although they were aware of the crowd size as all had reservations. Others at my table got the crabmeat and asparagus omlet and was very pleased. Shrimp and grits tasty but small portion. Overall interesting place but will be a long time before I return, if ever.

An amazing experience!  Our waiter Carl recommended we try the pork shank and the shrimp and grits.  They were amazing and we are so glad we listened.  The pork shank was tender and the grits were the fluffiest i have ever had.  

He was very knowledgable about all of the food and really made our dining experience enjoyable.

The food is not only wonderful, but the service is on point. Ask for Gary or Kevin, they are both great waiters and made our experience at Luke's the best. Come here, get some grits and bread pudding!

Everything was excellent. I had the shrimp etoufee, which had pasta in it similar to gnocchi. I ate every bite. So delicious. My husband had the Luke Burger, and oh my gosh that was good. If I ever come back, I would get that burger. This was probably my favorite restaurant of our trip.

The food here was delicious! Best meal we've had in New Orleans so far! Happy hour fresh and fried oysters were great and good size! 

Shrimp and grits was delicious as all the reviews had recommended! 

Duck duck rice was also excellent. I loved the crunchiness of the rice and contrast with the sweet fig. 

Brussels sprouts were the best! We even got the recipe to take home though I doubt we can replicate them as good! Haha

Last but not least the bread pudding was perfect for dessert. 

My boyfriend also had a couple drinks with the happy your price. I tried a sip of his Ruston smash and it was good! I don't even drink ;$
Great food and service.  I had the shrimp and grits  and added crab and shaved back truffles.  Legit!

Our captain, Rich, was the best server in this city. I love him and he gave us one of the best dining experiences I have ever had. Thank you so much Rich! The oyster salad was awesome and the Luke burger were so bomb. The Brussels sprouts are also bomb! Love you Luke!!

Solid food. The gumbo was the best I tried in New Orleans (and I tasted many: most come in a tiny cup for about $8, but the bowl here is reasonably large for the same amount). The burger was pretty tasty and the salads were also good. Everything here was pleasing and on-point. The condiments (like Heinz ketchup) come in adorable personal sizes. 

The service was very pleasant. Make a reservation though, the wait can get pretty crazy (2 hours on a Saturday night). 

The best thing about Lüke (aside from the random umlaut in the name), is the happy hour. 50 cent oysters and 1/2 price fancy cocktails? So amazing. 5+ stars for the happy hour. Do yourself a favor and go to happy hour here ASAP.

Overpriced considering the portion size. Sandwiches are greasy and have more of a Quizno's reheated style of preparation. Staff isn't particularly welcoming either. I walk past here almost every day but I'm really not interested in going back.

It's too bad that Penn's campus has this instead of a Panera.

When my already large family group gained 4 more members while walking around the French quarter, we made the wise choice of visiting Lükes for brunch on a Saturday afternoon. Since there were 12 of us, they rushed to provide a private room with a clean and dressed table. 
Immediately our drink orders were taken. I went with one of the specialty cocktails with pomegranate juice and vodka. Wonderfully sweet and tart. 
When not even five minutes later we started receiving gorgeous complimentary appetizers and bread, I was so thankful we visited. The chicken pate is creamy with great flavor, and the Brussels sprouts are freaking amazing. I don't usually enjoy raw seafood, but I could not resist trying some of the shellfish tray. Everything was so fresh! 
For my entree, I ordered a bowl of the seafood gumbo. My other family members chose items like matzo ball soup, oysters, ginormous burgers, and the kids were even able to share a giant grilled cheese sandwich served with a side of fries. 
The waiter poured my gumbo in the bowl when it was served to me, and that small touch really made a difference. The actual meal was decently delicious too, and the bread served as the perfect dipping vessel. 
Derrick (I think he's in charge of the place) was an excellent host, and even joked around with us when he was able to stop by. 
I'd visit again for a nice brunch or even try stopped me by for dinner.

You get what you pay for. This is the easiest ordering model for fast food. I get a Bowl, with brown rice, a little amount of black beans, protein, very little cheese and as many salsas as they'll let me have. Under $7, I'd say worth it.

My friend and I came here for lunch while vacationing. WOW, the portion sizes are HUGE.  The restaurant itself had a great atmosphere. The place was a lot bigger than it looks from the outside.  When we first arrived (without reservations) we were told the wait would be about 40 minutes.  We ended up only waiting about 5 minutes and we got a table.  We ordered an appetizer, which was very tasty.  I decided to get a burger and fries.  I think the burger was bigger than my head.  They served all our food on wooden cutting boards which I thought was unique and fun.  The wait staff were all tremendous and so very nice. The food was excellent. I would definitely come here again.

Tonight a Monday night, I placed an order at 7:02 P.M.
It is now 8:30 P.M. and still no food has been delivered.
I've called an all they can say is the food out..I just hope 
it tasted good and it's hot. To be continued....

I want to give this place 4 stars, but there have been some quality issues lately that I have to point out. Luke has a potential to be a solid casual brunch/dinner restaurant to visit for years to come, but they have to keep consistent with their food prep. Months back, I enjoyed the rabbit pate. Just the right amount of liver taste, not too salty. However, each time I've ordered its been different in texture and taste. Less livery, more buttery..too salty at times. I've noticed the same for the crawfish soup...too creamy one day...too bland or too salty another. Some servings with chunks of crawfish, some without any. Not to sound too picky, but its the small things that really make a difference in the dining experience. 

I've also noticed that when ordering through Doordash, they often forget an item. If Luke can keep consistent, I would continue to visit. But they really need to work on this.
Oysters are outstanding, and at their happy hour they are 75¢ each. Classy place, good drinks, great oysters.

I always hit the restaurant when I am in town. The Luke burger is unbelievable. I am also a big fan of their southern breakfast, never had better grits. I like that they serve your coffee in a french press.

I've always enjoyed the oyster happy hour at Luke. Everything I've had is delicious and the cocktails are on point. The brussels sprouts and fried oyster salad are some of my faves. Giving it 4.5 out of 5 just because the pricing on some menu items is a little over the top. Otherwise, I love this place!

We were very excited to check-out John Besh's restaurant and were extremely disappointed. Ambiance was not romantic or friendly at all. Lights were too bright, very loud as all tables are located right next to the bar that had tv screens. It gave a feel of sports bar, but definitely not a fine dining restaurant. 
Food was ok, but it was not anything special to recommend or return for. We ordered charcuterie platter and rigatoni Bolognese. One of the pate's had really bad taste. Wondering if anyone in the kitchen tried it before serving it to the guests. Pasta was al dente, but nothing special. 
Service was absolutely unacceptable! First of all stuff was not friendly. They acted like they really did not want to be there. Their uniform was dirty and not ironed. Made me question quality of the food and cleanliness of the kitchen right away. They never smiled or asked us if we like the food or offered 2nd round of drinks. When we told server that our sauté vegetables were steamed and looked unappetizing, he just took the plate from the table and woke away without apologizing or offering anything else. We were given check before we asked for it or had a chance to order desert. Shockingly disappointing service! I will make sure to write a review everywhere I can. Maybe John Besh will pay his restaurant a visit and take off his name before it's too late!

if its possible john besh made me fall in love with shrimp and grits more so than i already was the night we ate here. 


we wanted to do one night where we kind of splurged...and this was supposed to be that night but we didn't wind up paying that much money for some really delicious food (and LOTS of it)! shrimp and grits! i dont even remember what else we had but i remember walking away food drunk and so happy to be in NOLA that the freezing temps didn't even bother me!!!

They have the best selection of Hiking/Camping backpacks in the Treasure Valley.  I was able to find the perfect pack for my son AND it was half-off.  I would have given five stars if they had better selection on other items we needed.  This has got to be the smallest REI location. The employees didn't ask me if I needed help but I would have turned it down anyway.  There was one employee helping out a girl also getting a pack and he seemed very doting.

I went to Lüke for my birthday lunch with a co-worker of mine and it was WONDERFUL. Nicole made me feel so special and went out of her way to provide a great luncheon for my friend and I. It was truly a great birthday and I thank Lüke (and Nicole) for making my day shine.
In NOLA for a conference, and on my own for dinner one night, I sat at the bar at Lüke and had their blackened drum fillet. Quite possibly the best piece of fish I've ever eaten!

The prices make Besh's food more accessable.  The service is ok and the food, well it was good.  Normally I would expect more but given the price it is a good value.  Next time I'm going for happy hour and the raw bar instead of lunch.

Lüke gets 5 stars, because:

1. The shrimp and grits is just... Amazing. You should try it and see what I mean! 

2. Any place that make Brussels sprouts taste the way Lüke does should get at least 5 stars (it's an appetizer you won't regret.

3. We were seated right away.

4. Service was good.

5. Clean, nice, simple atmosphere.
