Fantastic service. Better Food. The burger was delicious but the baked oysters, shrimp, and crab are worth the money inexpensive. Hospitality is out if this world.

BEST RAW OYSTERS. This is Chef John Besh's most famous restaurant. Yes, you must come here for raw oysters during their happy hour. It was $0.75/ raw oysters. We had 2 dozens of raw oysters and a dozen of also the best fried oysters I've had. The raw oysters were the star though. They were so meaty, creamy and tasty. We also had the best service here. Our waiter, Willie Will ( I think that's his name hahaha) was so attentive and funny. He was awesome and we told the manager how great he was. They also gave us some delicious chocolate cake. 

A lot of restaurant in NOLA has great raw oysters but this is the best.

Ordered Shrimp and Grits.  Tasty, but the amount is about a small bowlful....for $22.  Salad was separate and uninspirational.    Gumbo shrimp and oyster was not fresh.
Very disappointing for a John Besh restaurant.
The Choucroute Garnie Maison (smoked pork shank) was delicious. And leave room for the bread pudding!

Quick service! And the food was a delight! I got the fried oyster salad and it was over the top good! The fried oysters were the best I've ever had. My husband got the croque madame and it was also great! Our only complaint was that there were some bugs, perhaps fruit flies, flying around, but it is the south right? 

Our waiter Kristoff was very helpful :)

You can probably go to New Orleans for a meal everyday for the rest of your life and not have the same thing twice. Well not being biased but every experience I've had at a John Besh restaurant has been magnificent! I've been to Lüke twice now and have ordered the same thing twice. Lol! The rabbit and liver pâté is the best pâté I've had in a restaurant. From the toasted thinly sliced bread to their creole mustard seed spread to the pâté itself. You'll finish the whole thing. I also had the Louisiana shrimp and jalapeño cheese grits. Talk about carb loading. You definitely don't leave hungry. My boyfriend had the burger and even he questioned getting a $16 burger for brunch but what the hell, we did and it was a wonderful decision. The burger had a nice grilled taste, fresh flavorful beef, and bacon. Bacon....the fries were pretty basic thin cut fries bordering shoe string styled fries which weren't salted and maybe taken out a bit early bc it wasn't quite crisp but nothing ketchup doesn't fix. Overall, we'd come again and again for the páté, the other food would just be a bonus.

There are so many restaurants serving creole/Cajun cuisine in New Orleans that it can be hard to choose one.  My wife and I had an all-around excellent experience during our lunch at Luke.  

We had the seafood gumbo which was outstanding as well as the crawfish bisque --which was even better.  I had an enormous croque-monsieur with very tasty fries.  

But the real highlight of the meal was the Friday lunch special court-bouillon which is a seafood stew.  The shrimp, crab, and fish were super fresh and the dish had the right amount of spice.  

Our server was knowledgeable and the bloody Mary's were fantastic.  Our only regret was that it was our last meal in New Orleans so we could not go back again!

After living pretty much next door to this place for a year, I have certainly had my fair share of experiences eating here. Unfortunately I probably shouldn't have eaten here quite so often.

This place is pretty much a second-rate Panera: they have some interesting sandwich combinations (like putting brie on sandwiches mmmmmm) but there is nothing particularly special about this place.

The pizza is pretty okay but definitely overpriced.

There really is no reason to come to this place when there are tons of other sandwich/hoagie spots/carts scattered throughout West Philly with higher quality food.

Second time there. Food still excellent, but it took some time to get my Sushi order to the table. Everyone else was finished eating by the time it came. Not a difficult order, 2 rolls and 6 prices of sushi.  It was tasty though. 

We did throw the server a loop with the bill. 3 credit cards and the balance in cash confused them, then the register crashed.  Oops.  I will be back, just need to keep in mind the lead time for the sushi.

Unfriendly people, a strange line system and high prices - that pretty much sums up my impression of Cosi. However, I do like their food which has never failed to be delicious somehow.

I don't know why this place needs a separate line for salads when more often than not you have to wait for your order anyways. It also doesn't help that there are a bunch of people around you who don't know where to go, where to pay and whether the person randomly standing in front of them is in line or waiting for their food. This could all be avoided if the place was better organized - or had people actually helping their customers out.

Food-wise I am quite fond of Cosi. Most of their pizzas and sandwiches almost live up to the price. If only it was a bit cheaper, I'd come here much more often.

Had a great experience at Luke. Was actually seated a little before my reservation time.  Service was impeccable.  The French 75 really is good and worth a try if you've never had it.  Had some of the best oysters I had eaten in New Orleans her at Luke.  The raw P&J were delicious, but the stuffed P&J was probably one of the best food items I ate the whole time I was in New Orleans.  Also had the fried oyster salad. Oysters were cooked perfectly but breading was a little too salty.  Will definitely go back to Luke.
My family and I really enjoyed our meal. The atmosphere was pleasant and the waitstaff very friendly and accommodating. I will definitely be back.

REI is great, easily the best outdoors store out there from casual campers who want quality gear to pros who need the best.  An REI membership is more than worth it, and pays for itself with the dividend.  However, this Boise location is not that great compared to the three locations I've been to in Oregon.  Its tiny and just doesn't have the same REI feel.  The customer service is just okay depending on who is there here in Boise.  I also am a bit spoiled not having sales tax in Oregon, which cuts deeply into my dividend, and keeps me from purchasing at this location.
Hands down best shrimp and grits I've ever had. Prompt service and excellent presentation.

Good food in a classier environment. If you want to eat at a place that the terms "Chef De Cuisine" "Celebrity Chef" apply to,  and has a team of wait staff tag teaming you throughout the meal, this is the place to go. The fish was excellent in both dishes. I had the local catch of the day and my wife had swordfish. The food overall was slightly edged out by the other classier, celebrity endorsed restaurant we went to, but it was still REALLY good. John Besh is like the poster child of New Orleans.
This fairly newcomer is my all time favorite restaurant in New Orleans and I've been to most of them!

Went for lunch our first day in NOLA. Everything was wonderful: the service, the wine selection and the food. Had life changing crispy brussel sprouts with jalapeños and honey! Also tuna crudo was beautiful and delicious. I will go again for sure.

One of my favorite lunch spots. Food and drinks are on spot and very delicious. Luke burger is a great lunch option. Roasted Jalapeño grits and Crawfish bisque is also highly recommended. Finish the meal with bananas foster, can't go wrong with that. Highly recommended

Probably the worst chipotle there is. The staff is very slow and unfriendly. They spilled an entire burrito bowl in the cheese and was about to scoop the mess back into the bowl and hand it to the customer. Not a pretty sight to see. I would rather go 5 minutes out of my way to go to another chipotle store from here on out

AMAZING SERVICE!! I wish I would've caught our server's name but he was both witty and attentive.  He gave us an extra dessert on him because I was so skeptical about the bread pudding.  Our experience there was wonderful and everything is delicious! You won't be disappointed.

Great local sushi place. Omakase set is a must. There are various kinds of fish and quite fresh for each kind.
And the lunch set is a great deal

3.5 - maybe even 4 stars.

This is the Tokyo Sushi stand in the Riverfront Market.
Today I had a roll combo - 4 pieces each of Salmon, Tuna and Yellowtail - for $9.95.  

I also have an order of microwave-heated gyoza for $3.50.  (Your standard frozen gyoza - tasty but in no way mindblowing).

Fish was fresh and tasty, but cut unevenly (the nigiri were a MESS!).  Reminds me of supermarket sushi - but a hair better because the fish is, indeed, fresh.

Just amateurishly presented.

But hey - It's Wilmington, DE in a market.  For that you might give it 5 stars!!!

Must! Must! Must stop! Especially if military, and definitely if Marine Corps. This is one of  our own who made it big, but did it right. Food is phenomenal! Staff is extraordinary! Great times, great place AGAIN!!! My fourth time

I thought I had died and gone to food heaven, but no I was just in New Orleans, kind of the same thing. One of my favorite dishes is Shrimp and Grits so I asked my friend who was born and raised in New Orleans for a recommendation on where I could find this. Without hesitation she mentioned Luke. 

I snatched one of the last Open Table lunch reservations and was on a mission to try, arguably the best shrimp and grits in the city. I took a seat at the bar and got fantastic service. Both bartenders were extremely attentive and helpful. I started with their fresh bread and also a cup of the seafood gumbo. Then, I had one of the best main courses I've had in a while!! WOW! Shrimp and grits may never be the same again. The grits were jalapeno cheese so already the plate was off to a tasty and slightly spicy start, then it was topped with huge, fresh shrimp and sausage. The sauce was plentiful and just spicy enough. I highly recommend this dish and don't know if I could order anything else here.

Luke is located in the Hilton hotel on St. Charles Avenue. The service and food is worth the cost, which is reasonable considering that Luke is a hotel restaurant. If you are heading to New Orleans try to get a reservation at Luke on Open Table!!

Kris and Tristan helped make our night amazing! We came to celebrate our anniversary and they exceeded our expectations! We were seated with champagne! We came early for the happy hour on wine and oysters and everything was delicious! In addition to oysters, we got the Luke burger and it was amazing! It had so much flavor! To end an amazing evening we got a complementary anniversary dessert! We will definitely be coming back!

A dining establishment that's located in the CBD and away from the din of the French Quarter.  We had two waiters (presumably because one was a newbie).  The waiters were fairly attentive for the most part, but they didn't keep my water glass filled, which is a minor pet peeve.  Overall the food was pretty good: sort of Cajun/Creole with a Modern American twist.  I liked that the restaurant had two in house brews on tap; I had the alt amber, which was tasty.  Overall, I'd recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a casual dining experience with reasonably priced food, away from the noise and crowds of the Quarter.

While you may find white table cloths on the table, this is anything but a standard white tablecloth establishment. Luke describes itself as a model of the Franco-German brasseries of old New Orleans. Here you will find used newspapers available for patrons to read, french fries wrapped in paper, oysters shucked openly at the bar and a laid-back, casual atmosphere.

Tips: If you like being near the action, ask for a table in the back where you get a nice view of the chefs at work behind a glass room.

I've never eaten there for breakfast or brunch, but I have enjoyed many a lunch, dinner and happy hour there.

Their lunch specials change daily, but they include some really good eats, if you can catch them on the right day.
As appetizers go, you can't beat the deliciously cheesy, buttery, oniony, bacony lamenküche. Delicious!

If you haven't guess it yet, I'm a cheeseburger girl. And Luke has one superb Cheeseburger; however, they have many other delectable selections to offer too.

Luke's Shrimp and Grits rival some of the best in the city. 

If you'd rather fish, you won't be disappointed with the fish meunière... go ahead and splurge on the added jumbo lump crabmeat. It will definitely be worth it.

A little warning, if you order the ravioli of local crabmeat you will absolutely love it.... for about 5 minutes when you realize that there are not nearly enough ravioli to satisfy you. The portion of this dish seems very small to me.

Don't skip dessert! If you still have room left, go for the profiteroles. And make sure to get some coffee. Luke has some of the best restaurant coffee I have ever tasted.

Another tip: Be mindful of the cheap oysters, appetizer and drink specials during Happy Hours throughout the week.

Most importantly, it's not just the food that make this restaurant 5 star worthy... It's the cocktails. One cocktail in particular, actually. The French 75.

I'm sure that their other cocktails are also good, but you will have to check that out for yourself. .

You see...
Luke is where I fell in love with the French 75. And Luke's French 75 is the French 75 by which all French 75s will be judged through my lifetime.

If you're a gal eating alone and DARE to make a reservation and get a table, be prepared to be ignored. I had to flag a hostess down to even order a drink. Food is good and worth a wait, but I am not sure it is worth being treated Luke a second class citizen. Hello, John Besh, are you listening?? How about you, Hilton hotels??

Great happy hour (half priced drinks and $1 raw oysters).  Delicious shrimp n grits (although I think they were called something else on the menu) and my colleague had the étouffé.  I would've given them 5 stars but our waiter disappeared mid meal and never returned - there was never an explanation.  We ultimately had to flag down a random waiter for our check.  NOT cool.

I have been eating at this location since it was called house of Q some 30 years ago while it is not as good as I think it once was it's still very good Chinese food wherever you should note that spicy items to me never seam as spicy as they should be like beef Szechuan and curry chicken I had to add hot sauce to both. The curry chicken had an unusual melted plastic taste to it to start which was really strange and offputting. This was an exception to the normally good food so I'm not holding it against them. Portion sizes or generous and the prices are reasonable and the staff is always friendly and service is quick. some of our regular fav meals are Szechuan beef orange chicken General Taos chicken and we never forget to get egg rolls which are always excellent.

So many glowing reviews and the fact that this is John Besh's latest restaurant made us want to dine here. I was meeting a dear friend I have not seen in 10 years, I wanted the experience to be memorable. Looking at the reviews and considering my previous experience at Mr. Besh's other restaurants, I made reservations for four at Lüke. 

The experience from start to finish was mediocre at best and rude at worst. Our friends arrived before us and they were having drinks at the bar. I greet them at the bar and walk over to the hostess stand to notify of our reservation. I couldn't get to speak the hostess for a good 10 minutes even though I was standing right in front of her because she was busy taking calls. She never acknowledged anyone standing in front of her, nor did she ask us to wait for a while. There were at least three parties that stood by the hostess desk waiting for her to get off the phone. Finally, after she got off the phone taking calls, she asks if I have a reservation. I gave her my name and said it is for 7:30pm but we are early and she says she cannot find the reservation. A moment of panic set in because I made the reservation two months ago and I was worried it may have been lost since then. After putting me on hold again to take a call, she resumes the search and says - with an eye roll - "you made the reservation for 7 not 7:30". Oh, ok. How dare I not remember the time?! And then she walks away...no words said. Baffled by this bizarre reception, I go back to the bar and order a drink with my friends. My husband offered to take over the "wait at the hostess stand" duty while I get a drink. The River Bend cocktail made with vodka, lemon juice, basil syrup, blueberries, and ginger ale is excellent. The ginger and basil make the drink exciting. 

After another effort at the hostess stand we are finally seated. 

We peruse the menu while catching up on the past 10 years and decide to order. Our server - Ben - was aloof from the start. Never once asked if we have any questions regarding the menu, didn't offer any drinks, and disappeared for extended periods of time. Halfway through the meal and noticing that every table around us has a bread plate, my husband asks for bread. Ben brings us some bread nonchalantly. After trying to get his attention a few times, and finally getting him to come to our table, i request a glass of wine with my meal, which arrived as I was about to finish my main course. A glass of wine should not take 20 minutes to arrive at the table...not in a restaurant of this caliber. All through the meal we had to flag other waiters to get water and wine because Ben was MIA.

This would have been a one star review if not for the food. The pate of Louisiana rabbit and chicken livers was a great start to my meal. Simply delicious! For my main dish I ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" - a different take on the traditional shrimp and grits. It was excellent with the green onion sausage bits being my favorite. My dining companions all enjoyed their dishes. 

We did not get dessert because we were asked or offered any. In fact, after being ignored for another extended period of time, we were offered the check, not dessert. I would have loved to try the chocolate bourbon pecan tart, but alas!

While the food at Lüke is stellar, the service from start to finish is abysmal. Somebody at this establishment needs to train their staff well. The silver lining of this entire experience is that I got to see my friend after a long gap of 10 years.

One of the best brunches I have ever had. First time For me to have Crawfish with no shell. Together with the creamy tasty sauce, it was very creative brunch dish! My bf had the chicken waffle and also agreed it's the best waffle he has ever had. The Brussels sprouts was served first, and we liked it a lot. But compared to the main dishes, no words left for it. The portions for all of them are huge, so we couldn't finish them, neither did the guests at the two tables next to us. So if you don't want to waste food, no need to get any appetizer to share.
But weirdly, not many ppl come to this place during a busy Sunday brunch time. I definitely recommend this place over other popular and long line brunch places. Try it urself and like my post.

I noticed that my A/c was starting to fail the previous season. So in April I  scheduled an appointmnet to have it checked.System was 15 yrs old and needed replacement. I didn't want to patch it and waste money so they sent the service manager Joe out, quoted a reasonable price of$10000.00 .I was able to negotiate it to a more suitable number I liked , allowing them their profit . The install of a complete system was completed and the service technician was very pleasant .I then call the service manager about my return system, he was kind enough to set up an appointment to come out. After they cancelled 2 times on the day of the appointments and wanted me to rearrange my schedule for the third try is when I decided I'll look elsewhere for my services.
Great spot for lunch or dinner.  Food and service are amazing.  Fried oyster salad is awesome!

Had the gumbo; pretty average. Seafood in it was soggy and sort of mealy.

Small but decent bar.

Dined solo at Luke one night while in town for a work conference.  Ate hear after the 2013 New Orleans Oyster festival and had high hopes after reading the glowing reviews.

I was not disappointed.. Not only were their cooked oysters better than anything at the festival, the rest of the entire meal was superb- my first stop on the next visit to New Orleans.

Had the French toast (challah bread) with bacon and mascarpone.  The picture really doesn't do it justice. It's a small menu. Larger brunch on weekends. The staff is friendly. It's cold!! Really rally chilly.

I did not realize it was part of the hotel but that didn't matter.  The atmosphere, at least in the front of the restaurant, was very authentic with tin ceiling, white tablecloths and comfortable chairs.  The oysters were fresh and wonderful - not briny, buttery,and large.  The brussel sprouts were to die for with a spicy vinaigrette, almonds and apple and as a bonus, they provided the recipe.  Crab and corn bisque was rich and very tasty. On the downside, our server was totally indifferent. Rushed us and when we could not decide on our main, she abruptly left us with the feeling we were not using her time wisely and then gave us cursory attention.  If you don't mind that service, the food is worth it.  I would not return however.
My mom and I went here for lunch today. Service was great, food was amazing. We will definitely be returning!
The happy hour here is fantastic! Great drinks and oysters!!!

i wasn't gonna come to new orleans and not go to a john besh restaurant.. thankfully this was located nearby my hotel.. so it was just a short walk to this amazing restaurant.. 

service was perfect.. the waitress even gave me some cough drops since i've been hacking away with a post-nasal drip for a couple weeks., as for the food.. it's absolutely phenomonal.. 

i had the  poached yard egg salad with fried pig ears, bacon and chicory.. the crispy smoky pig ears and bacon are absolutely a sinful delight.. the poached egg was perfectly cooked.. i love a runny yolk 

i then had the seafood gumbo.. although i wasn't in new orleans for very long.. this is the best seafood gumbo i've ever had.. it was spicy and deeply flavored.. the seafood flavored was infused into the gumbo. 

as for my lunch entree.. i had the crab BLT.. holy crap it was a good.. a soft shell crab served in a BLT on a cutting board.. absolutely genius.. the french fries were also magnificent.. perfect browning and 
crunch.. 

this was the second best meal i had in new orleans..  the first is at august (another john besh restaurant)..

Dear Panera....

We dine with you at least 1-2xs a week...

Never fails... something IS.... ALWAYS missing. 

I've even called after multiple times of going through the drive-thru and getting home to find key things missing from my order. 

(When I called- I did speak with a manager- and he was very helpful and even took my information and sent me a free meal postcard) - I totally appreciate this. 

Tonight- yet again- missing items... like the Egg in my Green Goddess COBB salad. 

Never. Fails. 

Usually it's the croutons to the tomato soup.. or the pumpkin shaped cookie. Today it was the egg. 

I've never been to a Panera that gets sooo many things wrong. 

Please... please... change up your consistency. Get better.
Biggest raw oysters I've ever seen for only .75 each at happy hour (3-6).

Came here for lunch while on business in NOLA. It wasn't very crowded so I was seated quickly (the bar was full). Even though its a white table cloth establishment the atmosphere is relaxed. The staff was very friend and attentive. I had the LÜKE burger with fries. The burger was great: very juicy and cooked the way I requested. The cocktail and beer list are very nice as well. I would def come back here next time I'm in NOLA.

A little trek off the french quarter area, but definitely worth the visit.  This restaurant was the end of my trip dinner, and it was surprisingly good.  Their menu has classic southern cooking with a gargantuan seafood platter of oysters, mussels, clams, and crabs.  I would definitely check this out next time I come across NOLA.

We had the gumbo and shared a shrimp platter.  Everything was delicious with the service friendly and accommodating.  We did not have high expectations, so it surprisingly gave a southern flare towards the end of our trip.

I would highly recommend this place if you are staying the south side of canal street and want a nice dinner without the packed in a can of sardines feel.  I would love to check out their huge seafood platter next time!  Good job, Lukes!

My husband and I were visiting New Orleans from Denver and made a reservation for Sunday night. I had been to New Orleans before and had been to several of John Besh's restaurants but had not tried Luke. 

We came a bit early and were told that it was a slow night and we could be seated anytime. We decided to sit up at the bar and have a few drinks (always sit at the bar when visiting places, you'll always get the best stories). The bartender Amelie was a delight and made us several perfectly balanced cocktails. Before we sat down to dinner, Amelie had shared several cocktail recipes with us that we promptly saved in our phones.  

When we were ready for dinner they sat us up near the kitchen, which you can look into while the chefs are working. We ordered the chicken liver pate as an app and I ordered the plum duck breast and my husband ordered the shrimp and grits. Both were outstanding. We didn't even ask our servers (Camille and Cheyenne) for dessert but could see that we were going all out on this meal and brought us two desserts. Two words. Salted caramel. Wow. 

The general manager, Robert so pleasant and accommodating. Top knotch food and service. 

It was really the staff, who went above and beyond to make sure we had a fab meal, that put this over the top for us. I'd go back again and again if I could keep eating like that and not be a huge fatty. The only thing that would've made this meal any better was it Chef Besh himself was in the house.  

By far, this was the "Besh" meal I've had in recent memory. You will not be disappointed.

Shrimp & grits was overpriced at $25. It tasted good, but the portion was small. The grits were cheesy.

The oysters on the half shell were a decent price. Half dozen for $9. They shuck fresh ones in front of you if you sit at the bar.

I am pretty sure that John Besh is my soul mate.

Luke is a more casual and affordable jewel in Besh's empire.

There was not a dish on our table that was less than stellar and our table near the kitchen afforded us a view of the talented staff through the glassed in prep area.

The folks in my party had the crawfish bisque, beet salad and mussels. All were spectacular. 

I had the burger, which, may be the best burger I have ever had. No fancy condiments here. Just a personal sized version of the Heintz and Hellman's we know and love. The pomme frites were not the best I have had but I wasn't shy about clearing my plate (or chopping board, as it is served.)

The table next to us spent their time gulping down oysters and sparkling wine and they looked to die for.

You definitely can't go wrong with Luke.

I was out in search of a new café. I browsed around on Yelp and found this place called elm café. It looked worth a try indeed. I pulled up in the tree-shaded street and found parking quite close. (finding parking might be an issue sometimes) I walked up to the door and there were people out on the patio enjoying drinks in the sunshine of the morning. I opened the door and was greeted right away by a friendly young lady. I asked what they had for iced drink options. She showed me, and I chose an iced latté. It was ready quickly and I took it out to the patio. The café itself is quite small. Just one small counter with three bar stools to sit on if you want to stay inside. The latté was delicious and I hope to be back sometime soon.
Disappointing meal with slow service, average salad and dry fish.

LOVE this place! The P&J oysters are awesome and the staff are pleasant! Too many great things to name I think there 4 Stars speak for themself, go place to try if your spending a few days in Nola and a MUST if your staying at the Hilton on St. Charles because it's right there!

loved the oysters!! the service was MMMEEHH!! most of the time I wondered if the server forgot about us...this happens alot there! I liked their crispy brussel sprouts! all in all GOOD FOOD! come back just for that!

BOMB

Had the shrimp and duck 
It was sooo bomb

They prob put a shit ton of butter but it was delicious

Also had the vanilla crepe bulee very yummy but that duck rice was legittttttt
Highly rec

Came back to Lüke today expecting the pecan pancakes, but alas, they have changed the menu. I was disappointed but ordered the Croque Monsieur. The presentation of the sandwich was beautiful. It looked delicious. Maybe I didn't like the cheese or the texture, but I wasn't a fan. The French fries were good. The service was awesome, but I don't like the new brunch menu!
Two words - Bread Pudding! The menu is good especially for brunch food but you'd be missing out on a staple if you don't try the Bread Pudding at Luke's. So don't leave without a heapful of dessert

I loved the look of this place and was hoping for that at home feeling of a small hole in the wall, neighborhood bar. Unfortunately what I got was WAY overpriced beer and rude service.
My girlfriend and I waited at a table for service from the waitress but she never came. Without giving it much thought after about 10 minutes, I went to the bar to get a drink. The waitress of course popped up at that exact moment and have my gf a hard time about me going to the bar. Super weird. Then, She vanished again.
We later saw the same waitress playing darts, messing aroundon her phone, and smoking behind the bar instead of actually waiting tables. Maybe if she waited on people and served them with a friendly face people wouldn't go to the bar. 
We won't be going back.

I was pretty disappointed with this place, I had high hopes. 

I'll start with the good...Now the food was amazing - we got a few appetizers and cocktails. The Gnocchi was amazing! Like melt in your mouth amazing! We also had the Brussels Sprouts they were fabulous. The Tuna Tartar was also super good, menu describes as "with shrimp chips" it was just one fluffy crunchy on top of the dish. Wish it had more, but it was really tasty. Cocktails were amazing as well - best French 75 ever.

Now the bad, I was super disappointed with the service. They were nice but seemed out of it, we had two servers too, so for them to mess up was like really? There are two of y'all. The waiter forgot to put in an order of mine, so I was  

I'd for sure give it another shot, I hear they have a great HH. Service I'm sure is prob always stellar, they prob had an "off night" I'd still give it a chance again.

Cosi is another salad/sandwich/soup place similar to Panera. They have two lines, the one on the left is for salads and the one on the right is for sandwiches. They have many great healthy options that it was hard to decide, but the line behind me was starting to grow. I quickly decided on the tandoori chicken salad, which came with a slice of flat bread.

Since I'm a clutz, I dropped my flatbread on the ground but the cashier was really nice and gave me another slice. Unfortunately their flatbreads are pretty difficult to chew since they are hard, so I would recommend eating it with soup or hummus. 

However, the tandoori chicken salad is AMAZING! The ingredients were really fresh and they did a pretty good job of imitating the tandoori flavors with their sliced grilled chicken. It came with onions as well, so I may have had stinky breath afterwards but it was well worth it.

If I lived around the area, this would be an ideal lunch place to have a quick dine in or order healthy food to go.

[61 of 100]

Amazing breakfast!  They don't have a lot of selections but we really enjoyed the shrimp and grits and Mimi's pancakes.  Best pancakes I've had so far, and I love how there are no extra fruit flavors like typical pancakes.

Awesome Burger & Fries! you will see some of the reviews are bad from a hippie looking for a veggie burger, an idiot that wants Cajun and thinks the menu is French?? If you're in the Big Easy and want a break from the typical NOLA eats after 5 days of business/pleasure it can get a little old, Go to Luke and grab a burger  you won't regret it!

Darn, I really wanted to give this place a good review. We loved the fireplace in the cold weather, and the people seemed friendly. 

So, why can't they honor what they say are their specials on their own website? We went in expecting happy hour on Monday, all day and all night. Exactly as their website shows. The bartender was nice, but just blew us off and couldn't explain why she couldn't do it. Honestly, it wasn't so much the ten dollars, it was just that crappy feeling knowing we picked the place. 

Oh well. Decent place, just don't look at specials or expect them to do the right thing...
I had the shrimp and grits like so many other folks here.  It did not disappoint.  It delivers on good old fashion southern classics.  The service was excellent as well.

Good service = good food = happy customers ! We shared the stuffed P&J oysters and the Brussels sprouts and both were fantastic! I had the duck fried rice entree and there was a lot of rice but the duck was tender and flavorful. My dinner mates had the shrimp and grits and étouffée and I didn't hear any complaints ! I only wish I would've had time to stop in for the happy hour during my visit. Ah well next time ...

So good. Every. Damn. Time.
I am obsessed with the Flamenkuchen. The pate is divine. I recommend the crawfish bisque to everyone.
With all the great reviews I'm not going to spend a lot of time on this one. Just know this place is awesome!

If you want a break from the rowdier restaurants in the French Quarter for a more classy dinner, this is a solid option. It's not too loud. The service was impeccable. Not only were our waters always filled, but several of waitstaff came up to us to apologize when our sides of fries took longer to come out than expected.

As for food, we ordered a half dozen of P&J oysters, matzo ball and chicken soup, shrimp and grits, mussels and frites, the Luke burger, and steamed chocolate for dessert. If you're ordering oysters, I think there are definitely better options elsewhere in the city. These oysters were fine but probably only worth it if you're getting them for the happy hour price. I generally find it hard to mess up dishes with shrimp and mussels, and these versions did not disappoint. While all the food was good, the truly memorable dishes of the night were the fries and the burger! 

Not sure there's anything unique enough on the menu that makes it worth rushing back to eat for a second time, but my family and I thoroughly enjoyed the meal and would recommend this for a classier night out!
Huge oysters for happy hour. Would've liked to have tried the other menu items but passing thru. Love this as an alternative to the quarter mayhem.
I really enjoyed my fish. I had never tasted drum fish before. The staff were super friendly. Elliot was doing tricks. Classy place. Everyone in my party enjoyed their food. Prices were not bad.
I went there for the breakfast bar, but was blown away by the individual breakfast item choices on the menu. The food is incredible and the service is excellent.

I was soaking wet from a torrential downpour when I popped into Luke's to wait out the rest of the storm. I was able to grab a seat at the bar and take advantage of their incredible happy hour offerings. Half priced beer and wine, and .75c oysters that were better than most I've ever had back home in Boston. I finished off my stay with a Luke burger, and I highly recommend it. Easily one of the most delicious gourmet burgers I've had--and the fries were great, too. The staff behind the bar was wonderful, and I hope to stop back in for another meal before the end of my stay here in New Orleans.

Luke's is one of my favorite happy hours in NoLA - they have awesome specials on fresh oysters, and discounted drinks as well. It's only at the bar, so be sure to get here early to get a seat. I actually preferred the bar seating at Luke's because you got to see the oysters being shucked in real time, and learned new things about the food from the shuckers. Definitely a place I stop by every time I'm in NoLA.

This place was an incredible value!  The interior is beautiful, minimalist Asian aesthetic, so upscale and chic, it is hard to believe you are in a strip mall.
Four of us ate for $100.00 and we tried items from every page of the menu.  We started with several small plates, including the wasabi lobster roll, tako ping pong, and tuna bites. The presentation was outstanding, each white plate showcased the food in a clean artistic manner. We had raw scallops sliced thin and served in a citrus glaze set upon a bowl of ice. It could have served as a centerpiece. We also ordered a steak that came out on a sizzling hot stone, it was cooked perfectly and simply seasoned. 
My husband, who is more of a meat-and-potatoes guy, had the hibachi. It was a generous portion and he loved that you could "build your own." The desserts did not fail to impress either. The same careful presentation went into the warm  chocolate cake and the fried banana bites, and both were served with tiny dishes of ice cream. 
I will definitely be back, I need to try the sea urchin.

Talk about great service. I hate getting the oil changed because as a woman there's always this feeling like your getting "played". Yes, I don't know much about getting my oil changed but I don't think people should take advantage of it. Well this wasn't the case at this location. They didn't try to over sell me things but they did offer additional services if I wanted it of course. They were very knowledgeable and courteous. I wish I would of stopped at this location last week When I services our other vehicle. I would have to say that I found a location were I will be servicing our cars and no where else. They did a great job.

We walked into Luke after having the wind driven rain turn our umbrella inside-out.  Not exactly happy coming in.  Wow, very welcoming.  Nice welcoming raw/oyster/crab display as you come in.  Got warm, got hungry, ordered crawfish bisque to warm up more.  Fantastic.  Then ordered the Pate of Rabbit and Chicken Livers.  That is a wonderful thing to have if you're a little pissed off about the rain (or anything else).  Between the Pate and all of the sides, you will get happy.   Sigh, wanna go back.

I didn't know what to expect with this restaurant as I'm not a fan of French or German food, but this place was excellent!  My mom and I came here for brunch, and not only was the food amazing, but the service was top-notch!   Our waitress was very attentive and knowledgeable about the menu.  The location is only a few blocks from Canal St./French Quarter, and it wasn't super crazy busy (as brunches typically can be).  My mom had the Croque Monsieur, which she loved, and I had the cheeseburger, which was so big I could only eat half.  The winner, though, was the brussel sprouts!  What??  I kept reading about how good they were and decided to give them a try... they were SOOO good!  I wanted to go back the next day just for the brussel sprouts!  My mom, who doesn't even eat sprouts loved them.  Tip - ask the girl at the front for the recipe, they have them printed on a card.  :P

This Cosi is located on the University of Pennsylvania's campus.  If you have been to a Cosi before, then you know what to expect.  If you have not been to a Cosi, then you should know that it is a decent place to go for something quick and a step up from fast food.  The flat-breads or the salads are usually both good choices.  Although if want something sweet and have a little more time, the S'mores is a great option.  You actually get a small burner of your own so you get to toast your marshmallows.  The one really nice thing about this particular Cosi is that it has a lot of seating, including upstairs and tables outside.

Fabulous experience! We went for lunch. I ordered from the express menu which included choice of soup or salad, I went with the gumbo. The main dishes was shrimp etouffe . Both dishes were fantastic. The gumbo wasn't spicy and had a lot of flavor.

Worst Cosi ever. I remember when they came to town in '94 at 15th and locust. They were great then, not anymore. Won't go back due to the way upper management has no oversight of their units. See re: recent health inspection from City. Disgusting!! 

Cosi
130 S 36th St.
25 violations, 10 serious
An insect was crawling in the pistachios; dead roaches observed in/or on the exterior of the ice machine, gaskets of the reach-in freezer and walk-in cooler, on floors inside the walk-in cooler, on wall near the elevator, and above the cold-holding unit where marinara sauce is stored, and on floors in the food preparation area; Live roaches were crawling along walk-in cooler gasket, on the ceiling in the food storage area, stuck to duct tape in the hallway and crawling under negate display case; mice feces was found on the wall ledge at the front counter, base of dough mixer, on floors in the food preparation area, under Coca-cola refrigerator, and under the beverage display case; a fly was found on bagels in the warewashing area; a fruit fly was on the cutting board; a moldy pear found in the walk-in cooler; chicken and carrots were not held at proper temperatures; the food safety certified person was not initially present; food employees were donning single use gloves without a prior hand wash; a tray of bagels was uncovered in the warewashing area; there was black residue and pink slime on the interior of the ice making machine; there was no water at the handwash sink at the front counter; hot water was not available at the hand sink near the large dough mixer.
Due to imminent health hazards observed during this inspection, the establishment was issued a Cease Operations Order and must discontinue food operations immediately. The establishment could not operate for a minimum of 48 hours. Inspected August 6.

Being a first timer in New Orleans, this place was high on the list of things to try. Unfortunately, it did not meet expectations. 

Our waitress was rude and acted like we were dumb each time we asked a question about the menu. We also had trouble getting her to take our order in the first place. The bread was hard and tasteless. You could get better day old bread from Jimmy Johns. 

We ordered the oysters. They had a funny taste to them, yet being hungry, we ate it anyway. Later on that night I had a bad reaction from them (I am not allergic, something was just off about them). 

Do not recommend.

great causal chic atmosphere and awesome service.

but the food was underwhelming and overpriced, small portions, and it seemed you could get better at the millions of other restaurants in the city.

The food here, is great!  I've been here twice! First time, the service was fine but the second time, was pretty bad. I wanted to make sure my friends loved New Orleans food and wanted them to be happy before sending them back home! I'm completely embarrass about the service here, after raving about one of John Besh restaurants to them! 

This is my first bad review on yelp! 
I'm more than just a little upset, our waiter Ruben, was incredibly disappointing. He probably hates us for sharing an appetizer and 2 entrees as a table of 3 for lunch. And splitting the bill in three. As we made sure he got cash tip! We ate here on Monday and my card was ran twice in two different amounts after I had ask him to run a certain amount that are the same on two different cards. He could've just told me, he ran my card for a different amount. It's was pending for 3 days and it's the wrong amount. The 2nd amount that was ran, disappear after two days. We left him a good percent of tip even though he didn't deserve it. Was just hoping he would cheer up a bit but he didn't. Whatever it is, it shouldn't be taken to work, he's representing an amazing restaurant with one of the best chefs in town with great food. There's so much more but really what's the point. This yelp has so many complaints on service and yet, nothings changed. But asking all of us to email the manager.

So after writing that review, I went back 4 more times during my week in New Orleans. (I'm a bit obsessed) This is my absolute favorite restaurant of all time! Try the heirloom tomato and crab salad appetizer, the crawfish Sharon, Brussel sprouts, pan perdue, the breakfast fried chicken and biscuit thing, and basically anything else. My friends and I never ate a bad dish. Everything was AMAZING! Please eat here for me, I don't know when I'll be able to return.

Like other people have said, it's like another Panera but I do enjoy Panera more. Cosi is conveniently located near UPenn campus and could be a good study spot. They have an upstairs, which is more isolated and quiet so you could get more studying done up there. 

I've gotten food twice here and occasionally drop in to just buy a drink. I'm not too big a fan of their flat bread sandwiches. The last time I had it, the bread was really hard and just hard to bite into. I've recently gone there as a quick stop for breakfast and ordered a squagel (square bagel), and I really enjoyed that! I ordered the club squagel, which consisted of eggs, cheddar, bacon, and tomato. I chose to get the basil parmesan squagel out of many other choices you have. It was a solid quick breakfast at a very reasonable price! The other thing I really like about Cosi is their selection of drinks that they offer in the afternoons. I've gotten the grapefruit apple, raspberry mojito, and some other form of their mojitos. It's light, refreshing, and delicious.

Inexplicably poor food and service.  I ordered the Luke Breakfast.  The coffee was weak. The grits were salty and lukewarm. The biscuit tasted like a pillsbury pop-out-of-the-can type. My poached egg had clear egg whites and was cold. Worst meal I've had in New Orleans. My wAitress, while sweet, was clueless about the menu and returned twice to correct herself. When I asked for cane syrup sausage brought me bacon, explaining that they only have andouille sausage, which is incorrect.

In addition, when I sent the dreck back no one inquired about what was the matter nor how to fix it. The rest of our party choked down their food. Love Willa Jean but this place was a miss.

ETA-- I spoke to management on the way out and the best they could offer was that they hoped we would try them again.  Zero stars.

Outstanding brunch menu!!! A great mix of local flare and breakfast staples. The Brussels sprouts, jalapeño grits, and the fried chicken brisket were phenomenal. Cool ambience, great service, and yummy coffee!

Ate here while working a convention. Really great place. John Besh really knows what he is doing. Of course, I had to try the local stuff even though I also travel to Lafayette. The Gumbo was really good with a nice dark, nutty roux with generous helpings of meat. The main dish was a very pork centered one with cracklin on top. Very filling and tasty. Also found out that Chef Besh is opening a restaurant in the Houston area, which has all of us there jumping for joy.

Don't judge this place on their lousy breakfast. Dinner is amazing! 
The pro's- they make a great French 75, bartender adds some brandies cherries and swirls the cherry juice. The ribeye with lump crab meat was worth every penny! Great flavor and served on a cutting board. Wasn't impressed with the fries but that's my fault. I should have read the menu closer and subbed in mashed taters. 
The con's- breakfast was lousy. Eggs were sent back. Toast was burnt and very hard to chew. I gave up before they brought over butter. Who wants cool hard toast? Menu said hash browns but they're new potatoes quartered and burnt. This one was free as I'm staying at the hotel. This meal was also worth every penny. Lol 
Side note. Hotel voucher doesn't include a drink or breakfast meat. $9 for a small diet coke and a side of bacon. The bacon was very good. Could've bought a pound for $9 but eh.

A must visit spot during every New Orleans visit! The atmosphere is awesome, a lot of relics to admire. The shrimp en cocotte / aka shrimp and grits is to die for! I order the same thing every time I come and am never disappointed!

Food was great.  Des and Savannah were fantastic!

Our large party would absolutely dine here again.

They have a large raw bar display in the middle of the restaurant. It is not a large place and it did get a bit noisy although you could still hear table conversation. 
The table next to us got the raw bar sampler which came out in a 3-tiered plate and looked quite impressive. They seemed to enjoy it. 
I had the shrimp and grits which was excellent and the Flammenkuchen, which was like an onion pizza - it was actually quite good, but a bit much for one person. The bread they serve is freshly made. The service was quite attentive and the waiter made excellent suggestions for dinner. 
The bread pudding was also excellent for dessert.
Wonderful incredible food and cool Cafe ambiance. Apps incredible - Crab bisque, crabmeat maison, and flamenkuche(best little pizza you will ever have)

Great food, good portions, great service. But we don't know top with slightly crab meat cost $13 after we got check. That's expensive for a entree already $26. But general is good, will come back again.
Their oyster happy hour is the best!  Good drinks, but it's always full so make reservations or go during off times.
I've eaten at some amazing places in New Orleans. This was not one of them. The staff seemed flustered, it was loud, and the food was too salty to eat. Not a fan.

My husband and I stayed at the hotel across the street from Luke and we were so lucky to have been able enjoy Luke for happy hour many times during our stay. They have an amazing happy hour for drinks. The French 75 was the best. I still order the French 75 at places in Los Angeles and it doesn't hold a candle to the French 75 at Luke. They have a great deal on oysters too during happy hour. Their shrimp and grits are delicious too.

Excellent service and delicious food! We had the shrimp cocktail, Shrimp n Grits, Porkchops, Creme Brûlée, everything was amazing! The service was on point-our server was funny, attentive, and friendly. Would definitely recommend Luke's!
This restaurant is GOOD if you are in New Orleans go to this restaurant.  The service was great and the food was excellent.
Great sushi! Rolls are bigger than usual. Try the eel and egg rolls!! Much better sushi than Mikimotos.

A-MAZING FOOD. Came in on a Sunday at ~4pm on memorial weekend and the wait was thankfully not too bad at 20 minutes. We decided to wait by  hanging out at the oyster bar to drink some chardonnay and eat 75cent oysters for happy hour. The oysters tasted great for the price, and the shucker working behind the counter was extremely friendly! For the main course we ordered shrimp and grits, gumbo, and seafood étouffée...All of the dishes were the best I had in NOLA. Would love to come back again if the occasion arises.
Best place for oysters in New Orleans! During happy hours, you can have 12 oysters for 6 dollars! And a mint julep for 4,5 dollars! Nice atmosphere too!!

The entire place is disgusting. The last time I was there, I got up to grab some napkins and came back to find baby roaches all over my table. The time before that, water was dripping from the ceiling onto a countertop where food was cooked.

Had a rough previous night, so I needed a little hair of the dog. We stopped in here to order some to go Bloody Mary's. The bartender was really cool and that we looked like hell, so he helped us out with an extra shot of vodka on top. It was a delicious Bloody Mary and definitely helped the rest of my day.

Good food. Slow service though. Hard to get any waiters attention for service. Water refills? You literally have to walk to a waiter for service. Waiters, when you can see them, only focus on their tables. They need to scan the room more.

Credit due to Pierre for another great find in a Hilton.  This was one of the few places left with last minute Christmas Eve reservations so we took it without knowing much.  Pierre said it was a John Besh joint and wouldn't disappoint.  Who dat?  I would soon find out.

Continuing with my oyster extravaganza, we ordered 1/2 kumamoto and 1/2 local.  Entrees: I had the jumbo Louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" with white corn grits and Poche's andouille.  The friend ordered my first choice, the shrimp farci.  It came with a fried ball of crabmeat and shrimp with a blood orange hollandaise sauce.  I also got to try the Luke burger, and the bread pudding for dessert.

Local was better than kumamoto. Gasp!!  I was totally expecting kumamoto to be better, but am glad I enjoyed good local oysters.

My overall impression was: strong and well balanced flavors.  The shrimp was huge, tender, and flavorful.  The grits were a complete surprise.  I really don't like grits, but keep ordering them in hopes that I'll find something I can tolerate.  It figures, I have to go to the South for awesome grits.  It was so creamy and umami filled that I just kept eating it till it ran out.  

The blood orange hollandaise was complete and utter magic in my mouth.  Everything else on the plate was a distraction from the goodness of Mr. Besh's magical concoction.  

Burger was also great.  Meat had little fat content, hence it falling apart when you bit into it, but it was really flavorful and I didn't mind the meat falling apart, it only reminded me that it IS actually grounded up beef rather than a hockey puck.  Bacon was really smoky and stood out.  Bread was of the artisan variety, yum.  

For dessert we shared a bread pudding with a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top.  I'm not a caramel fan so it was a little too sweet, but otherwise solid.  

Service was excellent.  We got great tips for things to do on Christmas day, a little bit of back story on our server's family, and extra blood orange hollandaise!! Man, Southern hospitality is something we need to bring to Cali.

Only regret, missing $.50 oysters for happy hour :( Unheard of!!

Excellent drinks!  The mint julep and Bloody Mary were favorites.  Also, the food is second to none.  Oysters are a major draw here but even if you're not a fan, you can't go wrong with anything on the menu.  Standouts for us included the crawfish bisque and the croque madam.  We will be back!

Stopped in for a late lunch! We had the raw and fried oysters and would come again for them. We also had daily entree special split with gumbo... think it's called something Bouillon... also really yummy and would have again...oysters shrimp crab all included! The service was prompt and helpful.... definitely would come again!
First time.  Had the swordfish, perfect!  Oysters .75 for happy hour 3-6, try the fried.  Nice for lunch, pricey but worth it. Great service, nice place.

Service was nice, we walked in without a reservation but they still sat us

Had the P&J oysters, and chicken with mash potatoes and vegetables, MASH POTATOES were amazing!! 

Boyfriend had the shrimp étouffée which was good as well! But the portion was smaller than mine,

We ordered cocktails and had the champagne with peach and boyfriend had the cognac with champagne - both were refreshing and tasty! 

Our server was Ben I think and he knew the menu very well and he was very sweet! 

The waiters were very attentive and polite!
Definitely a lovely place! Would come back!!

The grits and french toast are to die for. Service is quick, but who cares...  try the grits and french toast! Ate here twice during my weekend stay in NOLA. Will go  back next trip for grits and French toast!
Don't overlook this restaurant.  Located right next to the Hilton New Orleans / St Charles. Good wine selection and service.  The food was delicious.  Try the rabbit/chicken Pate as an appetizer.
Amazing food and great service! Was the true highlight of our trip to New Orleans!
I have never written a review and I'll tell you right now this is the best restaurant I've been to in longer than I can remember.  Visit this place if you can.
I highly recommend going during their happy hour times because it is 0.75 each for raw oysters.

We went to Luke's on accident really. We ended up loving it. Rich is an awesome waiter! They have the best oysters. Rich got them to chargrill them and they are better than every other place we went to. They have great cheeseburgers also. It's our new favorite restaurant.

Food was good but the service was off. Bread wasn't served until after we finished with our salads, although the beet salad was very good. And for dessert we watched our tasty ice cream melt on our bread pudding while waiting for utensils to eat with.

If they worked out the service issues it would be a four star. Also the place is noisy so not easy to carry on a conversation.

Jerzees is one of my favorite places in town! Its a place where I've gone with the boys to drink beer and watch sports but have also gone here with my Mom when she was visiting. It is suitable place to go any time of any day!

For food I typically get chicken, either hot wings or the buffalo chicken tenders (because they come with fries), but have also gotten pizza and their stromboli (even their small stromboli is massive!) Their menu is massive and has options for every person and every craving. Safe to say I've never gotten food from here that I did not enjoy!

They have beer specials, live music, trivia nights, and much more throughout the week. Seating and parking can sometimes be limited, but I've never had to wait too long or walk to far to find either. 

What is very convenient is they offer carry out and beer delivery during buisness hours. I have never personally ordered beer for delivery, but being able to get a 12 pack after the beer distributer is closed has come in clutch many times!

Jerzees is my favorite spot in Glenside. I've been here countless times and have never had a bad experience!

I have truly never had a meal as good as what I had at Luke last week. The oysters and squash blossoms were so delicious! I had a bisque and salad for my meal, both of which were perfect. Then the desserts....the bourbon sauce on the bread pudding was to die for! I would buy that and have it shipped home to michigan if I could! 

The only reason I took a star off was that our server wasn't easy to find.

My two friends and I ate here while in town on vacation. To be fair, one of my friends really enjoyed his food and it did look good. But my other friend and I ordered the crab BLT (something we would not have done if we'd overheard the server tell the table next to us to order something else - we'd already put our order in when this occurred). It was so incredibly salty that it was inedible. Neither of us could eat our meals. In hindsight, I should have sent them back although I hate making a fuss at a restaurant. But for $30-something, not being able to eat my dinner really stunk. Service other than that was great so it's a shame the food didn't live up to our expectations.

Went there for lunch about 6 months ago.
Delicious. 
Was in New Orleans again recently, I was upset that we did not have time to return again. 
Very memorable meal. I would recommend if you are not afraid of trying new things.

Amazing! First off, our lovely animated waitress was THE bomb. I wish I could remember her name, but she was funny, attentive, and her nails had me gagging at how gorgeous they were. The place was clean, the food was delicious. Honestly, everything on the menu looked great. We ordered grilled oysters (as you do) which were great. My favorite part of the meal was the Shrimp and Grits, these honestly were the best grits I've ever had.  We were only visiting for a few days, but when we come back to New Orleans we plan to eat here again.

What a delicious surprise! 

Went here twice while I was in New Orleans. Just really yummy.

Came here for their oyster happy hour, which is a great deal if you're looking to stock up on oysters. The raw oysters were good, and wasn't a huge fan of the fried ones. But didn't compare well to the delicious wood fire oven ones I had the day prior at Cochon (I know, it's not a fair comparison), so I walked away feeling a bit disappointed. Wouldn't make a special trip here unless I was craving a ton of raw oysters.
Quaint and delicious! Excellent food and service! Tried 5 different rolls, all fresh and very tasty! Hibachi grill also highly recommended.

So attempted to go into Luke's to try the famous bread pudding. However, I say we have a table of 8. Without even looking at the host board, I was told that they didn't have a table for 8.  I look around and there are a good amount of open tables. Then the other hostess says well we can find something. I then say I will pass. It was like they just didn't want to help.  A man comes in ask for a table of 1. They acted as if they just didn't want to help.  They ten take him to the bar even though he clearly states he wanted a table. The manager just said she was surprised to hear that.  It was like she didn't believe.  I am sure the food is probably good here. However, with the lack of service at the hostess stand. I imagine the restaurant could be as inconsistent. The decor was nice in the restaurant.

Meh. Was expecting so much more. Most of the reviews rave about the fab oyster deal (not the full menu). Like others have said, service was mediocre. Might want to work on the layout (e.g. large bags of trash carried through main dining room???).
Very good food, well presented. Cut the prices and we'd be sold. Came for breakfast but paid like it was dinner
One of my favorite sushi places in the area. Will definitely be going back again. Reasonable prices and friendly staff.

I've been to this place a couple of times after hearing a lot of good things about this place and also that it is somewhat close to where I live.  The inside of this place is really modern, chic, and a really nice place for a date.  Parking is plentiful as it is situated in a shopping center and you can easily find the place as there are flags of the restaurant in the lot right directly in front of the entrance.  Place is wheelchair accessible as well :)

The sushi is the real gem of this place.  Everything that I've had here looks fantastic and are delicious.  You can definitely tell that the chefs here take great care in preparing every roll.  Being a fan of scallops, I had to try their Spicy Scallop Roll and it exceeded my expectations.  You can definitely tell that the fish and other ingredients were really fresh.  The presentation of every plate was amazing and bordered on being too nice to eat.  The desserts are also great and the Creme Brûlée that I had was one of the tastiest desserts that I've had in a while.  The food is on the pricey side; however, given how good all the food is, it is justifiable in my opinion.

I will definitely be returning to this place.  I can easily say it is one of the best sushi places in the area.
A great place to take friends for a taste of Europe in New Orleans.  You can even enjoy half-priced drinks and oysters.  Thanks for another food gem in N.O. Mr. Besh!
Appetizers were very good but my entree was mediocre and everything was a bit over-priced. Will not go back unless for happy hour and appetizers only.

The oysters, mussels, and champagne were all amazing. We had the pavlova for dessert which was decadent and delicious. The waitstaff was delightful, knowledgeable, and fun. 10/10 would eat here again.

Cosi is like a Panera without the good quality sandwiches. The convenience of this place being in the center of Penn's campus makes it a great option to grab a quick meal to-go. I've gotten their flatbreads here a few times and it has always been a hit or miss with their sandwiches. Sometimes my flatbread would be so scarce  with ingredients or the bread would be too hard to bite into to. So I always go with the safer option of choosing their salads. You can also get just a single flatbread for $1 if you're in the mood to just nibble on some bread. 

Sometimes the service is a hit or miss as well. I would come here more often if it weren't for the expensive prices for the below than average quality food and unfriendly service.

We had the lunch:
- 3 roll meal: California Roll, Spicy Tuna, & Shrimp Tempura
- Mango Bento Box - Good but sweet
- seaweed Salad - very good
- I like the oranges at the end

The knife skills of the sushi chefs are good.
Great selection of German, French, Cajun cuisine. Excellent experience with hostess Alex. She was very welcoming, charming, and sweet! What a nice, young lady! Awesome experience and amazing food!

I'll keep this simple and straight to the point, since I'm on my iPhone. 

Best fried oysters I've ever had. 
Best shrimp and grits I've ever had. 

Fried oysters... The crispy batter on the outside is surprisingly good, and then you have oysters just pop in your mouth from freshness. Delicious.

Shrimp and grits... The shrimp was good, but those grits... Those grits!!! The hint of jalapeño is the perfect touch to this perfection. 

Although I have only 20+ reviews I eat out all the time. Take my word, and thank me later. 

Enjoy the pics! :)
Great service, good food esp since they serve food until 1am (everyday), awesome beer selections, and Comfy atmosphere!
Solid food and expensive but the service here sucked ass.  They had 3 people on the hostess stand and 2 waiters with a half empty restaurant.  Not a great use of staff.

Oh my, the food!  We are now big John Besh fans. We were lured here for the 50 cent happy hour oysters. I think the local beers during HH were $4. We also tried the food other than the oysters and it didn't disappoint. So far we've had the rabbit and chicken pate, Tabasco fried chicken smothered with red beans and rice, crab bisque. The flavor of the red beans and rice was so good and smoky. If you like red beans and rice, this is something you have to order. We've only arrived 3 days ago and have been here twice and plan to eat here more times.
Tip: make ressies for happy hour- I've seen the hostess make people without reservations wait a while and it gets busier as the evening progresses. Order your oyster in batches. That's right, go for it and put in your order for 3-4 dozen at the beginning. It's a busy place and the waitstaff may not get to you right away. Service is ok for a busy place. The waitstaff do try. There was this one guy who was our main waiter- he was a sweetie. Forgot his name but he was tall and lanky with long braids. Give that guy a raise!

Delicious! I had soup to start and roasted chicken as my entree. Everything was simply amazing. The waiter was extremely attentive, food didn't take too long, drink selection was impressive. My friends tried seafood options and both were very happy. Great place to try out I you're looking for a flavorful meal with great service.

I want to like Luke. I want to LOVE Luke. But, every time I dine here, I am beyond disappointed. My first experience, way back when, was for happy hour, and the oysters were pretty good. 

Now that I often stay in the area when I'm in town, Luke is one of the few restaurants within walking distance with my hopes and dreams for a decent experience still dangling on a string. I'm so determined to make it work that whenever I'm in town, I usually eat here at least once hopping that it's me, but alas, it's most definitely them...

On my most recent trip, I actually stayed at the Hilton St. Charles, and on my last night in town I was looking to not have to change into real people clothes, and instead get some food to go so I could eat in my room. I got a menu at the bar, and asked a bunch of questions. The waitress didn't know a lot of the answers, but she graciously said she'd check with the kitchen. Awesome.

I wound up ordered an appetizer with shrimp and then a side of rosemary potatoes. For some reason I was really in the mood for potatoes... 

A little while after I paid, someone from the kitchen came up to the bar and said that they could not make the shrimp dish I ordered gluten free (even though the waitress said that the kitchen staff said they could). I was instead given the option to switch to a crab dish. Without a menu in front of me, the kitchen worker explained what the dish was. I agreed. Shrimp. Crab. I love both.

The kitchen guy went back, and then the waitress told me it would be a slight up charge. Ok... I wasn't all that happy with this, but I understood. I handed over my credit card, and she redid the order. 

I waited a while for the order to come out (ordered to go), and just when I was about to leave, someone from the kitchen came out and said, "You forgot your fries." I didn't order fries. Apparently, they all forgot to mention that the crab dish came with fries. While this is not a terrible thing, it is pretty obnoxious that they clearly saw that I ordered potatoes, and didn't think to mention that the dish came with fries. Couldn't they have said something so I could then cancel the potato order? Or maybe they could have eliminated the fries and not up-charged me for the changed dish? The whole thing left a bad taste in my mouth, and that was before I even tried the food! I had way too many starchy dishes (one of which was thrown away...)

The food:
-The fries were over salted and wilted, not crisp
-The potatoes were ok
-The crab was tasteless. There was no seasoning whatsoever. It's like they just through the thing in the fryer. 

They get points for convenience, a nice location downtown, and pretty interior.

Love this place! Perfect seasoning.  Delicate flavors. Nice service.  Delicious drinks.  Beautiful ambiance.  got fresh and fried oysters.  Both fresh. Friday's lunch special is outstanding!  It is seafood tomato cream based stew. Incredibly delicious!  
I take a star for being on the pricey side.

Probably one of my favorite places to get oysters in the city! It's usually fresh and fast! Getting a table can sometimes be difficult but just sneak in and find a seat at the bar you'll get served right away. Get their crab bisque, it's solid!
You are still the best!  Sure hate to see you go.  The staff is great!  Best wishes to all!  You will be missed!
So disappointed.   French fries were cold.   Our waitress ignores us.    I would not come back.   It is highly overrated
Loved it.  Happy hour offers delicious 75 cent oysters.   Service was great.  Beer half price.

I wish I could be dishonest, but I can't.  The service here is so atrocious that I'm perplexed beyond my wits. (the staff were arguing and cursing in front of me)  Does John Besh really own this place?   The food is good, eclectic pub food. The wait staff is hung-over, unkempt, and uninspired.  I'm sorry, but after 3 fair tries, I've made my final judgement.    The Burger was very good. Oysters were average. Shrimp and Grits was fine.  Review is mostly for the terrible service.

One of my favorite restaurant in downtown NOLA. We went there at 10pm and there still full of people. Their menu is small and simple covers almost every category. The cocktails were top notch. The peach flavored one (forgot the name) was my favorite. From appetizer to dessert, everything I had was satisfying. The burger was huge, but every tasty. Can be shared by two, save more room for the other good stuff. This is a place you can really be advantageous without much concern, because they are just that good. Even if you don't agree with some taste, simply tell your server and they will take care of you just like they did with my friend. She nicely shared her opinion about a salad dish and the manager just simply add a dessert for her. This is how a good restaurant should be. We will definitely recommend it to anyone loves food.
Love John Besh, great Croc Monseur. Definitely a fan of our lunch here.
Always an excellent meal!  One of my favorite places for sushi!  A great selection and all fresh!
Great food, service, ambiance.  Had the croque monsieur and a cup of gumbo - and a few mimosas, too!

Love finding new hidden gems locally- this place is great. Been here a few times eating in and for take out. Hibachi dishes are a bit on the small size ( we were hungry) but food was all tasty. We had a mixture of rolls and hot food including using teriyaki salmon, beef, chicken, tofu and other appetizers. Baby Bok Choy was a little salty for my liking but I don't usually like a lot of salt in my food. We had 3 orders of Gyoza- it was a big hit with all the family, big and small! 

Decor is new and modern. Nice atmosphere.! Look forward to trying more items on their menu.

Everything we ate here was delicious.  My favorites were the escargots au gratin and shrimp and grits; so flavorful.  The moules-frites came with fries that you could use to dip in the sauce and they gave so much mussels.

Eggs in a Jar. 
That's all I'm saying. Order it now.

I stumbled upon this place because of Open Table. I wanted to eat away from the W Hotel for breakfast and this place was a block away from my conference hotel.

UM, I arrived a few minutes before the place opened and there were two other foodies waiting for the place to open. The other foodie told me that I had to get the beignets in a basket. I told him I was going for the eggs in a jar.

The place reminds me of a French bistro. 

The service was great. When the eggs in a jar arrived I couldn't believe how amazing it was. Fried shrimp, poached eggs over jalepeno grits. AMAZING. I know it sounds crazy and so heavy for breakfast but it is so good.

I decided to go somewhere else the next day for breakfast and regret it but will definitely come back to LUKE.

I really love what Nate has done with this tiny space. I've enjoyed every soup and sandwich I've tried and admire the fact that despite the daily changes in options, the quality is always high. Elm serves 49th Parallel coffee and they do an excellent job pulling Epic espresso.
The agnolotti was incredible. My husband said "I would fight someone for this" - that sums it up. Drinks, brussel sprouts, and shrimp and grits all worth a return!

A colleague recommended this restaurant and I'm glad I tried it. I came in for breakfast on a Monday morning. The breakfast menu is limited, but this allows them to focus on the quality of the dishes and it shows. I was seated quickly. Coffee took a few minutes to arrive because I ordered decaf and they brewed a fresh pot for me. I really appreciate when a restaurant does this since many places brew a pot of decaf and it sits for hours.

I ordered the local crab omelet and substituted fresh fruit for the potatoes.

The food came in a reasonable time and the presentation was very nice. The omelet was accompanied by a generous fresh greens salad with a light dressing. The omelet had a very generous portion of crab chunks in it and the flavor really came through. The eggs were light and fluffy and the amount of cheese was just right. The fruit was top quality and very fresh and flavorful.

Service was unobtrusive but I never lacked for anything. The staff were pleasant and professional.

I will definitely return to this restaurant.

Came here on a busy night and waited approximately 20 min after our reservation time, after showing up 20 min early.

Service 3
Food 4
Ambiance 3

Overall: 3.5 Stars

Had the foie gras which was good, but came with really hard garlic breadsticks, which did not go well with it. Also had some of their shrimp and shimp/grits dish.

Overall just did not feel welcome, or well taken care of compared to the other restaurants we visited on our trip.

This is our first meal in New Orleans and boy was it good we had the gumbo soup and shrimp and grits. This was the first time we had ever had shrimp and grits and they were amazing. The atmosphere the food and service were all great.

Okay so we are suckers for ambiance and great service. Thats what makes us regulars at any place. We do not mind paying extra for great dining experience and showing appreciation for it.
So...
We went to luke for breakfast last saturday and had an amazing experience. Because of which we decided that breakfast at Luke every Saturday would be our thing as a family.

Unfortunately , this Saturday it totally bombed. We have a toddler and a baby so to us the booth seat perticularly in the back out of the way and away from all other diners but close to the waiter station suites us the best.  That way we are able to better manage the kid and still enjoy dining while watching hustle and bustle of the restaurant.

I called Friday and made reservations for that particular table and stressed that we absolutely need that table or we wouldnt be able to enjoy dining. Saturday mornings usually arnt that busy for them so i was assured the availability .

We get there and the table was given away. It looked like it was given away maybe 20-30 minutes before we arrived..as the people had just got their food.

Considering the kids, We had to pick a table in a spot that was very easily neglected. From there it was down the hill. We didnt  get water for atleast 15 minutes we were there. I had asked for buscuits so the kids could eat sonething while we wait for food and get busy.  They came 15-20 minutes after we asked for them.   The table never got cleared as needed. After we got the food..the waiter wasnt able to check with us if we needed anything..which we did.. and had to flag him down.  "
We were definitely very annoyed since our kids were starting to get wild. 
My husband has been on sugar free diet and made sure the waiter was informed. His food came with salad topped with "sugarcane vinaigrette". 
The whole table was never cleared till the end so we had a mountain of dishes with a 1.5 year wanting to go wild with it. 

Ok so bad day right?..it happens...it wouldnt have deterred us from coming back.

My biggest dissappointment was when the manager did not want to admit that they gave the table away by mistake and instead defended and defended with a defensive tone. We would have to pay an upcharge to book a table in a half empty reataurant? Really? Then why didnt you guys ask for my credit card when i made the reservation??

Just admit..mistakea happen...the hostess made a mistake and didnt check on reservations and notes and mistakenly gave the table away. 
 
Mr. Manager, we have trained in hospitality management,  worked in the restaurant industry for a long time in the past. We know restaurants and service standards. The excuses given were B.S. 
Its such a turnoff when you talk to your customers like they dont know better. 

The restaurant wasnt full...there were plenty of tables available to be given away. So No you did not try "your best" to get us the table we needed. Your hostess made a mistake. You didnt want to admit it. 

For a restaurant of this caliber, we expect better customer service 

Food is good not great..we mainly came here for the experience.
