I visited Luke with 4 of my colleagues on Monday 01/30/17 upon the recommendation of another friend who resides in New Orleans.  I was able to make a reservation.  Diamond was very helpful with the reservation.  When we arrived, we were seated very promptly. Tristan and Vocy were awesome.  They meet our every need with great professionalism.  Vocy recommended the Shrimp & Grits and they did not disappoint.  It was an awesome dish. I also had a cup of gumbo which was perfect.  3 of my party had steaks and were very complimentary.  Another had the drum which he said was delicious.  The bread pudding was devilishly good.   Service was excellent.  I will return.  Thank you for the enjoyable evening.
The bar itself is actually pretty cool but the scumbags that frequent the place really kill the atmosphere.  Most of them are knuckle dragging mouth breathing blue collar wiggers

My family and I ate here on our last evening in New Orleans.  Food and service were excellent.  We had the raw oysters, ribeye, entouffe, and slow-braised pork.  Best overall restaurant during our four-day stay in this city.  Thank you.

Wife and I had reservations for first night in NOLA. Upon entering the restaurant I got a big whiff of seafood. Hostess sat us near the kitchen where we could see all of the action. Waitress was mediocre at best. I tend to shy away from getting recommendations from restaurants for obvious reasons but this time I could not resist. I order the pork plate which was described as having a lot of meat. Let me tell you I was not disappointed. Dessert was delicious. Opting to go with a NOLA classic, bread pudding, with a John Besh twist. Wife and I left fully satisfied with the meal but not the service.
Oh. My. Lord. Fried oyster salad and much wine. Creme brûlée is on the way! Rich has aggressive customer service. He knew our needs before we did!
Brussels sprouts were amazing but the part I couldn't resist was the kale chips that came with the sword fish!  So amazing I would order them instead of fries with any meal!

My first visit was purely by accident and this last visit last week I found you with laserlike precision after a day of eating lucky dogs and drinking colored drinks.  My friends be dammed I had to have a really good meal before I left your fair city and I knew of only one spot that had a good bar where I could show up and feel comfortable in jeans.  I went here last Thursday and found a nice spot at the bar.  This is a great authentic brasserie and I wish we had a restaurant like this in Pittsburgh, but sadly while our dining scene is improving we are still in the stone age in some respects to other food cities.  The tin ceilings are great, the huge fans, the oyster bar and the wall decorations are all great and seem authentic and reflecting back to a time when spots like this may have existed all over NOLA.  The service was impeccable the bartender and oyster guy were friendly and I made many new friends with the other patrons at the bar.   I love the cold appetizers here and had a wide array as again I knew it would be a while before I could try this type of food again.  I had the wild boar pate' with pickles and mustard, which was delicious and rich. I also tried the flamenkuche, which was so delicious.  It is alsacian onion tartare with bacon, caraway seed and some type of rich cheese.  You can think of it as a pizza type concoction that is both rich, savory and sweet.  I also had the foie gras terreine again, which is delicious and rich and ended with some briny fresh plump oysters which were light and a nice way to end a really savory, fatty, calorie laden experience.  Along the way I had a glass of crisp pinot and a shot of patron' with my oysters.  The prices were reasonable I felt for the quality of everything I had and a nice way to end my most recent visity to this fine city.

Oh hell yes! Hands down one of the best places I have eaten on my trip. It is located on St. Charles Avenue in the central business district. We were greeted and sat immediately. 
Service at this place is superb and so is the food. We started off with their Crispy Brussel Sprouts that were the best Brussel sprouts I have eaten at any restaurant. Just imagine the crispiness along with toasted almonds, honey and cheese. Mouth watering already. 
My favorite part was dinner. I had ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte"...let me give you a visual...jumbo shrimp, jalapeño cheese grits, andouille and green onion sausage...is your mouth watering yet because mine is!!   
It was a party in your mouth. So damn good. Seriously. I ate it very slowly because I didn't want to make it disappear. Ha ha!  Dessert was their Louisian Peach Meringue. Delish! I highly recommend this place to anyone coming into town. This is another place on my "must go" list when I come back.

Before leaving NOLA, I had to try one of John Besh's restaurants... especially while we were on company dime.  Being the last day with a few hours left, I convinced our group to go check out Luke, and I was not disappointed.  

Great service entering in, and lots of space (we got in around 11:30 AM on a Friday).  We ordered up a dozen oysters to eat amongst three of us at the table and while they were great quality oysters, we definitely have had better in the past few days here at other restaurants... though if we were here for the $1 per oyster happy hour, it would be hard to beat...

I had myself a Luke burger which was absolutely delicious and fantastic... crisped bacon, great caramelized onions, melting cheese.  Yeah, I know, why order a burger at a restaurant like Luke?  Well, it was recommended by our waiter, so I went for it, even though there were many other great looking options on the menu.

Verdict:  Price ain't cheap, but the food is good.  Worth checking out if in you're in the area, particularly for their $1 per oyster happy hour (assuming that the happy hour oysters are equivalently sized).  I'd come back, but only after I check out all the other restaurants in NOLA on my ridiculously long list...
Stopped by for breakfast was recommended the shrimp and grits and boy was I impressed. Definitely a must have when in town.

Our large group was seated in a private room (good choice on Luke's part, we tend to laugh out loud a lot).  I had the crab bisque as a starter, and the cochon de lait, both were delicious.  The bread pudding for dessert was good, but not great.  I sampled some of my friends' dishes as well, all were good.

The bummer here was the service.  The waitress seemed flustered and not very knowledgeable (perhaps she was new?).   I ordered a bottle of champagne and after waiting 20 minutes (the rest of our 15 person party had already been served their drinks), she informed me that they were checking at the bar to see if they had a cold bottle.  Okay, no worries.  Another 10-15 minutes later, she comes back to tell me they weren't sure they had it at all, and asked if I had a second choice.  Well, after another wait, it turned they didn't have my second choice either.  By then I was getting frustrated (by this time, some of our party was on their second round of drinks, and we all had our first courses on the table), so when she came back to ask me for a third choice, I asked her if we could just cut to the chase and could she just tell me what they DID have!  She brought me two tasting size glasses to try, I took a little sip out of each and picked one of the two.

THEN SHE TOOK THEM BOTH AWAY.  Thanks lady, I already have to wait one more time for my bottle of champagne, and now you're going to leave me drinkless again?  I can understand if you take away the one I don't want, but sheesh, leave me the two sips left in the glass of the one I ordered.  I'd hate to imagine what the service would have been like if I had just ordered one glass and not a full bottle - not that it should make any difference in the service, but I was once a waitress myself, and we all know that a bigger check usually equals a bigger tip.  The more you can get on that check, the better.

If the bottle service had been more prompt, a second one would have likely been ordered.  But by the time we got the first bottle and finished it, everyone else in our group was pretty much done eating and drinking.  The food is easily 4 star as expected from a John Besh joint, but the drink experience left such a bad taste in my mouth, I'd hesitate to go back.  If I did, I think I'd stick with water. :(

I tried this place for the first time today. I thought I saw online there were chicken and waffles, but then I didn't see it on the menu (could be for breakfast). However, it allowed me to try their croque madame, and it was very tasty! I liked the atmosphere, and the service was great. I would come back to this location.

Love this place. Didn't think I would find good sushi in Chalfont and this place has outstanding sushi, lunch specials and food. Highly recommend and it's a really cute place inside. Nice staff is always a plus.

Simple food elevated to new levels and perfection. Also loved the sense of community at the bar between team and guests. They clearly love where they work and support one another. Will crave the fried oyster salad and burger until I return.

The food here is fine, particularly the oysters. It is a bit of a cliche though, modeled on a French brasserie, and from the looks of it, focus grouped and researched heavily to hit just the right demographic in the John Besh empire. But as a result, the restaurant has no soul. Food is executed well but without imagination, and the decor is generic. The faux-French posters and other decorations look like they came straight from Pier 1 Imports. There is something overly corporate about the whole experience.

This was our biggest disappointment over Christmas in New Orleans. I loved the idea of Alsatian-inspired, but this was overrated. 

We visited on a Saturday afternoon. I'd heard the fries were great, so I got those early. They were great. Next, I ordered the waiter-recommended shrimp farci. I was mostly happy with what I ordered. My fiance ordered the jagerschnitzel mit spätzle which is served only on Saturdays, is the most Alsatian of all the options and was downright a huge disappointment. Bland and completely overcooked. 

My mother got the poulet grand mere, also on suggestion from the waiter -- hers was the best of all.

I loved the atmosphere -- very Parisian and the service was okay. (Which, actually, is probably bad for New Orleans' standards.) I think the waiter was put out we didn't order champagne at noon but it's not like we stuck with the Mississippi River NOLA bonafide tap water!

There are too many other fantastic restaurants in NOLA to waste time here. Go to Cochon instead!

Smoky?  check!  A little dirty?  Check!  Hole in the wall inside a strip mall?  Check!  Pretty run down bathrooms?  Check!  Patrons with "their" bar stool every night of the week?  Check!

Yep, everything a good dive bar should be.

Plus, as an added bonus you can order Balducci's pizza from downstairs and they'll bring it up to you!  Yum!!

My first time to Luke.  I was very impressed.  Staff was friendly and prompt.  The waitress we had was amazing. I had the burder which was incredible. Perfectly cooked, great flavor and delicious ingredients rounded out the taste.  I had the asparagus as well.  The people dining with me had the fries and the sautee'd veggies- All of which were delicious.  

If you want a nice atmosphere, great service and well seasoned food, this is a great stop just a few blocks off canal street attached to the Hilton.  

Bravo Luke!

TERRIBLE SERVICE FROM FRONT DOOR STAFF.  Walked in on a Friday night, was told by manager that it would be a 45 min wait.  I put my name in and went to Blue Dog for a drink.  They called me and told me they had sushi bar tables available.  I responded that I prefer a table and to call back when a table is available.  Waited 30 min and they never called back.  Walked over there and there were 2 empty tables that could accommodate my party.  Apparently Hachi's management does not value new customers.  Heard the food was good but never got the chance to enjoy it due to the unorganized, ignorant host/managers!!

The eggs in a jar are excellent and unique. I don't like poached eggs or grits, but I liked this dish, which is remarkable. The crab omelette is full of crab. The steak frites were very good. My daughter loved the beignets. I tried one and they were quite good. Also enjoyed the pate very much despite the fact that I generally don't like pate. It is only the second place I've eaten where I have enjoyed the pate, with other being a French restaurant in Toronto. 

Service was fantastic. My daughter had their hearts set on breakfast, and despite having already turned the menu to lunch, the staff accommodated their hearts' desires. I definitely recommend this place.

My husband and I made reservations for 6pm but happened to get there early so they let us have a table.  Good thing too because we decided to try the 50 cent happy hour raw oysters.  I'm not a raw oyster eater but when we tried them they were so good we ordered another dozen! I would definitely go back again for their happy hour raw oysters. Had the beet salad which was good. The boudin appetizer was good but you can get good boudin many places for half the price so i wouldn't order that again.  My husband got the rabbit sausage which he said was good.  I got the smoked pork shank which was too much food for me to eat.  Next time I'd like to try their veal.
Delicious pate and jambalaya, best shrimp and grits in town. Great service. Make a reservation or sit at the bar as it is first come first serve and full service.

Went here on Thanksgiving, when I was not able to get a reservation at August.  

I enjoyed my experience, but was not thrilled.  I liked the concept, German/French brasserie.  The food was comforting, and comfortably good, but not inspiring.  

I ordered the shrimp farci, which disappointingly, was flash friend.  My companion had the shrimp and grits, which he enjoyed, and I'm told is one of their signature dishes.

Yay for happy hour 3-6PM daily - 75 cents oysters and half off beer! Would've been a 5 star if not for the little mishap in getting our table. 

We arrived at 3PM on Sunday with no reservations. The hostess informed us that we could either wait for bar seating which is first come first serve or we could put our name down for a table. Since our hotel was nearby and we weren't too hungry, we didn't mind the one hour wait and left our name and number with the hostess. An hour passed by, we made our back to Luke, and the hostess seemed surprise that we came back. The restaurant was not even half filled, and many tables were open. It didn't make sense to us why they didn't bother to call/text when our table was ready. 

Anyways, the happy hour is as good as it sounds! We got two dozen raw oysters for only $18! What a steal! And the oysters were all meaty and juicy. It was a nice mid day snack, and next time I would consider trying their other food as well. 

Try to make reservation and double check with the hostess to avoid what happened to us.

This stop is number two of our happy hour tour which is based on our hotel, AC hotel, location. Luke's is a fancy-ish place. Way busier than our last place. Better then our last place. The bartenders are good, even though they are slammed. The happy hour drink specials is half off cocktails!!! Hello french 75; this F75 stands out from others because it is made with cognac, lemon, champagne, and granished with a marchenio cherrie. It was so lovely that I got one to go!!!! 
We had 6 oysters which were on ice and they were bet tasty. I didn't need hot sauce or anything on them. Oysters are $.75 each during happy hour. They were medium to large and since they are gulf oysters they are not briny.

Looked over the menu and asked the waitress for suggestions. I was torn between a couple of options which is always good. I thought I should behave and leave room for later so I found an absolutely amazing healthy option!! Had the fritata with onions and peppers and it also has duck sausage with arugula and vinegrette with chuncks of feta cheese and pesto, tomatoes, and avocado. Comes with wheat toasts. It was pretty big so I was able to finish about 3/4 of it. I would have taken the rest home if I lived nearby. Overall good service and food came out pretty quickly. Went early in the morning to get a seat. Staff wear white coats so you know its fancy. From the pictures, they serve a lot of oysters here but I did not get any whiff of fish smell which pleases me.

This review is based on service. Horrible service for our large party with reservation. It took over an hour to get our entrees and they messed up many orders. Jumbo shrimp dish was a joke. I do not recommend.

Oh my gosh, this was the best meal I've had in months. One of the few places I wish I could take back with me to NYC, and that's really saying something. 

Great atmosphere, we had the perfect waiter who was helpful, friendly, and provided us great recommendations of where to go after the meal as well. I had the pork shank and it was delicious and perfectly cooked. Not a bad meal on our entire table of 7 people, and even the dessert (think we got the pound cake or something like it) was amazing. 

Would definitely recommend if you are looking for a nice dinner but somewhere that's not extremely stuffy and moderately priced for a very nice meal.
Ribeye Steak was awesome! Shrimp & grits yummy & so was dessert. Service could be better, but still ok, I have patience
Very tasteful. Breakfast shrimp and grits (w/ egg) were really good. However, they could add mire shrimp for the price. Opens at 7AM is also a good thing.

When I found out that a Jon Besh Restaurant had a $15 Express Lunch special, i knew i had to come here. 

Good service, good food, weird location

The restaurant is located in the Hilton Hotel on St Charles Ave, on the stretch of the street where it's surrounded by boring state/city offices. Completely uninteresting. The inside of the restaurant is done up like a french bistro. 

Food:
$15 Express Lunch Special: A different entree for lunch everyday of the week (Wednesday was Veal Raviolo, which is what i had) + Soup of Choice on the menu

- Seafood Gumbo: Pretty yummy, esp with the warm crusty roll of bread that was provided

- Veal Raviolo: Tasty veal filling. The only thing that i really didn't like about the dish was the massive amount of Shaved Almond topping. What's up with that? Not only did it blitz out the dish, the crunch was an odd balance to the meal and did not add any tastiness to it. The dish would have been tons better without Any almond at all. It just didn't go with the dish. Otherwise, a tasty dish. Lose the almonds, please!

I don't know about the rest of the food here... the oysters are A++++++++++++++.

Happy hour, 50c oysters, HOW CAN IT GET BETTER THAN THAT? Especially coming from LA where fresh (and even not so fresh) oysters run $2.5-4 EACH. My family and I literally came here every day we were in New Orleans during happy hour for their oysters, freshly shucked, incredibly creamy and light, so refreshing after being out in the New Orleans summer heat.

Just how much do we love it? 6 dozen for 2 people. Can't wait to go back and do it again. It's the first place I'm hitting up next time I'm in New Orleans.

Came here so the Yibbie could get her oyster fix even if they were out of season by a bit     The Happy Hour special was a bargain and was shocked in a good way when the check came considering how many oysters she had and how many beers I drank

I really wanted to like this place...from all the write ups, I was definitely expecting to.

But I wonder if everyone was at a different restaurant?

Our service was slow, slow, slow. I realize that there is a slower pace here in the South, and that's fantastic, but this was unacceptable. And our server made it known several times over that he wasn't from here. It took about 20 minutes for us to get an order in -- any order. The server was nice enough to stop by and tell us he'd be right back, but that only goes so far when he would only take food orders and not drink orders. So he takes the food order (in a really weird order, and couldn't be interrupted or asked any questions) , does not allow us to order drinks...puts the food order in then comes back about 15 minutes later to get drink orders. 

This was the service all evening. The server was nice, sure, but it took FOREVER. It wasn't even crowded...perhaps it was an off night, or others had called in sick, but based on my experience, I wouldn't recommend this to anyone.

My burger was ok, though kind of cold; none of my other dinner companions raved about their dishes...unfortunate, really. In a food mecca like NOLA, I would have rather spent my money elsewhere.

Just checking into to say this place is STILL awesome!  Great food, big portions with loaded ingredients!!  Call in for take out a few times and they know your voice (and if you generally get the same items, your order) on the phone.  I try all of the new places I can, but I have to say this is still our most reliable and favorite regular!

MAKE THIS A STOP!!!!!!!

I felt that was necessary to put in the first line of this review.  This was recommended restaurant while in the Big Easy and I am so glad we listened.  We visited this location on a Sunday around 2:30pm and it was pretty busy.  It was Halloween weekend and a home game for the Saints.  For just two of us was a wait of 45 minutes.  We lucked up and got a seat at the bar right in front of the shucking station.  

While sitting at the bar we were able to see alot of food being delivered to everyone's tables and I must say EVERYTHING LOOKED GOOD.  My friend got the Shrimp and Grits which is suppose to be one their best dishes along with their oysters.  I didn't want to get the same thing and I decided upon the Crab omelette and the seafood gumbo as an appetizer.

The gumbo was delicious!  Some of the best I had while in the French Quarters.  And trust me I had alot of good gumbo during my 5 days here.  It wasn't runny and cling to the rice as GUMBO SHOULD.  It had sausage, shrimp and mussels ;)  Talk about perfect.  The gumbo was so good I literally came back about 5 hours later to get some more to go.  I am not exaggerating !  

My crab omelette arrived shortly after and the presentation along had me sold.  The eggs were perfect and so light and fluffy.  Inside the omelette their was cheese, crab, tomatoes, and mushrooms.  The crab meat was so sweet and perfectly seasoned. They really set the bar for a good omelette.  The dressing on the salad was so light and full of flavor.

The employees that work at the restaurant is what really sealed the deal for me.   The staff really works together to make sure their customers enjoy their experience.  I could really tell everyone really enjoy their jobs.  

Thank you Luke for the amazing experience!  I will be a return customer EVERY TIME I come back to Nawlins :)

I wish I had read Yelp before we called this company. My advice is simply go to another firm and do not consider using Fahrenheit. Basically, I was charged $99 for a call out to be advised that the motherboard (control unit) on my 7 year old system needed to be replaced. Also the thermostat. I was told it was the wrong system anyway and given a lecture about it. I was told it would cost $2300 to repair and when I asked about new systems,  $5100. My wife called ECI who came quickly to actually examined the system, went to buy a new pump from Home Depot and installed it for $300. The AC now runs fine. How many people does Fahrenheit swindle like this? Yes, negative stars needed as they don't deserve 1 star.

The food varied from excellent (baked oysters) to inedible (profiteroles) with our entrees somewhere in between as just average. The service was off - not exactly slow, but just weird. The food, atmosphere, and service were all underwhelming for the price. If you want to try a Besh restaurant I would highly recommend Domenica instead.

SO disappointed after seeing all the good reviews! Came here for breakfast while visiting NOLA and was very let down.  The biscuits were really dry and heavy, and even the eggs tasted off.  Wouldn't recommend to anyone, at least not for breakfast.
Crab omelette, jalapeño Grits, and Crispy Brussel sprouts are out of this world! I highly recommend this spot!

The setting and the servers are really nice. We really enjoyed our soups as starters although they were tiny. But the beet salad I had was soggy with dressing and they put the cheese on the bottom of the bowl on purpose (because it was so strange I asked). I didn't realize that when we paid $13 for crab meat it was going to be lathered in cream. My boyfriend found a long dark hair in his food halfway through his burger. The manager came over and apologized, still left the burger on the table as if he was still going to eat it. She proceeded to bring out a free dessert that we neither asked for, nor really wanted. When the bill came they had very graciously taken off the $7 coffee cup sized, little bowl of soup. Would never go back. It was ludicrously overpriced.
The best French 75 in the world bar none.  And the food absolutely delicious. One if the places I never miss when going to New Orleans.  Good vibe in the place as we'll, quite lively.

Is it me or does it seem like every Besh restaurant in NOLA has really gone downhill? Service, not food. 

When Luke first opened, I had some really wonderful experiences here. In the past 6 months, not so much. Service is lazy, rude, and incompetent. The waitstaff doesn't seem to care about the diner's experience. It really just seems that the staff is not well trained or managed. However, I saw this most recently at the American Sector only 2 weeks ago as well. It seems to a Besh "empire" issue. As I've heard this from folks who've also gone to August and Domenica recently. Perhaps it's time for a new management partner...

The food that comes out of the kitchen is still delicious and well done. However, if they could only match that level with the service. 

The burger is delish as well as their moule frites. Great homemade sausages and excellent raw bar. 50 cent oysters from 3-6. 

The bottom line: There is amazing food at the other 1200+ restaurants in NOLA; get great service AND great food.
Prime atmosphere, phenomenonal food, and top notch service! Will definitely be back for more shrimp and grits.

Solid 4.5 star
We had the Monday special - Tabasco honey fried chicken with red beans and rice. Highly recommend it! The jumbo shrimp and cheese grits was great too.
For dessert, we had the bread pudding, it was a bit too sweet with the candied pecans.

Got the matzo ball soup. The broth was absolutely mind blowing and the matzo balls were fresh and delicious. I would definitely recommend this dish and restaurant again.
My friend got the roast chicken and thought it was awesome.
The customer service was excellent as well.

Came here for a quick oyster fix during happy hour. On a Tuesday afternoon around 3:30pm, there was no wait, and the servers were very friendly and attentive. My partner and I ordered a dozen raw oysters and a dozen fried oysters. The batter for the fried oysters was very light and nicely fried to perfection. The raw oysters were some of the best and freshest that I've had. I love raw oysters, and Luke satisfied my craving in NOLA. 

I would definitely come back to try the other items on the menu.

Dearest Lüke...

I miss you and am in withdrawal. Do you deliver to Dallas?

Yours Truly,

MZ

I had a terrible experience here on thanksgiving day. I was anticipating a fine dining experience but it was the worst. The service was poor and the food horrible. The people next to me sent their food back also. I ordered a lame version of turducken which was completely dry. The stuffing on the side was watery and soggy. The greens were so salty I had to spit it out. The waiters came to our table only twice in the evening. When they saw my untouched plate, the waiter just looked at it and took it away with out asking how everything was. They gave us some hard bread about 30 minutes after we got there. Poor poor poor.

Went to the place on Friday night. Crowd of happy people. Do yourself a huge favor and try it. I am telling you, this place is amazing. Presentation and creation are fabulous. Yes, they are better than most Japanese restaurants in NY City because they serve real Japanese food. Happy to finks this place in Chalfont.

This place is outstanding.  I went with group of 12 for a work dinner, and they did a great job serving our group.  

We started with the "Le Grande Plateau de Fruits de Mer" - it was a great seafood mix appetizer.  We also got the "Le Plateau" of Prince Edward Island mussels, which were great.

Luke had a pretty comprehensive French wine menu.  We started with the Chateau des Tuquets, which is a Bordeaux, as well as a white that I cannot remember.  The Chateau des Tuquets was the only part of the meal that was just okay; everything else was top notch.  I had a great Belgian beer there - Grimbergen Blonde Ale - definitely worth trying.

About half our table got the corn and crab bisque, which was incredible.  For my entree, I got the jumbo Louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" (shrimp & grits).  It was by far the best shrimp & grits I have ever had in my life and one of the top meals I had in 2009.

I will definitely return to Luke next time I make it to New Orleans.
Luke is great for happy hour and dessert. For dinner there are other restaurants in the quarter that are better that have a similar cuisine and price.

We went here for dinner on Christmas Day - what an excellent experience - a carnivore's dream!  The food is inventive without being off-putting and the atmosphere is classy and friendly. Plan to ask for extra toast points if you get the foie gras.
The gumbo, people - it is to die for!  We also tried the crab omelette - delicious.  They also have a cadillac of a coffee maker - so good.

This place is awesome! I had this place bookmarked while planning my trip to NOLA. Be sure to make reservations. The decor makes you feel like you're experiencing a time warp. I could have dressed up a little, but there were all kinds of people from dressy to very casual. My husband had the Jewish penicillin aka matzo ball soup and I started with the crawfish bisque. My only regret with my soup was I wish I would have ordered a whole bowl of it- delicious!!!! I had the bib salad and ate ever ounce. We shared a shrimp dish that was in a skillet- I forget the name, but that was so flavorful! Can't go wrong with this place!

Wow!  Is THIS what it took to get me out of my Yelp coma?!  Seeing as Luke has been the only antidote for my horribly shameful MIA status, I should have ventured over to New Orleans sooner!  Should I ever return to that crazy, pothole infested city, you can bet that I will fall all over myself to eat at Luke again!  

First, I must say that our server, Al from NY, was like the BEST server I have ever had EVER!  Major props.  He was extremely attentive, but not stuck up our butts the whole time, you know?  His recommendations were precisely what I hoped for, and he knew to steer us clear of the things we weren't hoping for (ie: the brontosaurus leg sized pork dish that looked delicious on the menu, but when another guy at our table ordered it, I was very grateful that Al took the liberty of suggesting it was probably not a dish fit for a hamster...and he was right).  Anyway, we were all very impressed by the awesome service.  Later, the GM came by to check on us and make sure everything was to our liking.  Affirmative.

I had to try the Schneider beer, because well, it's practically my maiden name.  I am happy to report that I taste pretty delicious!  Everyone else's beer that I sampled tasted great too.  It's hard to ever go wrong with beer...especially when it has your name on it!

For the entree, I ended up getting the amazingly juicy duck confit with white bean something or other deliciousness with crispy pork belly treasures and the most flavorful sausage I've ever put in my mouth.  Freakin' good!  It had whole pieces of garlic!!!  They sure know how to win my heart!  One thing I noticed is that this place really knows how to cook meat to perfection: fall of the bone, melt in your mouth, juicy and tasty.  I tasted some of my friend's red fish, and it was also a real winner, but in the end I'm glad I committed to the duck confit.  

75 dollars later (2 entrees and 2 beers + tax & tip), I left Luke feeling the giddiest I've felt in months.  Completely satisfied, slightly buzzed, a relaxed time with friends and great service makes for a perfect evening.  Life is good.  The only thing I regret is not saving room for dessert.  After stuffing myself silly with their fresh, baguette style bread and butter, entree and sampling friend's dishes, I was more than full...let's not go overboard and then spoil the moment by having to scout out the nearest drugstore for some Tums.

Next time...there's always next time!

If you aren't prepared to pay for an upscale meal, don't go.  This is a restaurant about a certain style of food using some of the best local ingredients available.  Breakfast is okay to good, Brunch sensational, Lunch very good, and Dinner outstanding to sensational.  The wine list is good to very good. (the sancerre is the weakest, the pinot gris my favorite)  All of the express menu specials are meals to remember but the Court Bouillon is my favorite, with the veal a close second.  Don't look for boring, standard, or 'comfortable'.  Northern France meets New Orleans is not something to be bashful about.  Order something new and exciting and don't think about the bill.

Loved the 75-cent oysters for happy hour! We sat at the bar and Sean gave us the VIP treatment. Quality was great and service was outstanding. Definitely our best dining experience while we were in New Orleans
Service wasn't great. The food was pretty good, but not nearly as good as August!

Our lovely front desk person from our hotel recommended Lüke.  While the valet was trying to send us to Daisy Dukes.  Someone should really have a talk with that guy....

The hostess staff here was completely incompetent.  And when we finally got a table, we got stuck in the back near the open kitchen.  But our server was great.  BJ got a  Lüke burger with Allan Benton's bacon and caramelized onions.  He loved it and his 
house-made fries hamburger.  I got the ÉTouffÉe, loved the pasta and the huge shrimp.  The portions were good sized and very sad for me, we had no room for dessert.  This place is so good, we will be sure to visit on our next trip to NOLA.

My wife and I spent our honeymoon in New Orleans over Christmas and ate Christmas dinner at Luke. 

It was by far our best meal in New Orleans. The staff was incredibly friendly and generous, and the food was unbelievable. I kept thinking I was too full to go on, but each bite was better than the next - from the oysters and shrimp through the brussel sprouts (a must) through the bread pudding. Eat here!

This a thoughtful, delicious place to enjoy and have a great conversation. I was fortunate to stop by during happy hour. First the drinks were 50% off and oysters were 75cents fro raw and 1.25 for fried. At point I decided to try the fried oysters with a minimum 6 orders. This was my best decision. Crunchy, flavorful and not over fried but most important is you can taste the freshness of the oysters. I wanted to eat dinner like food so debating between the gumbo and ettoufee, I went with the crayfish ettoufee. It was creamy, yet the crunchy rice made it its own. I really love the twist and it was delicious. Totally new spin to a traditional dish.
Wonderful experience. Johnny and the oyster shuckers where great. Gave us the 411. Our bartender was great. The drinks where great

So, we were told there was a two hour wait, stepped outside, made an Open Table reservation and where then immediately seated. Had fun waltzing back in to the same woman, looking her in the eye and saying. "We have a reservation". 

The highlights were happy hour 75 cent oysters and half price wine along with great service from Maddie and Kenny. The pate was great and generous. 

Lowlights. Crab and tuna appetizers were great, but tiny portions for $15. Did not order any entrees because I'm not a tourist and won't pay $28 for a soft shell crab sandwich or boiled shrimp. Spent nearly $100 and left hungry.

Enjoyed lunch here with co-workers. We started with oysters then gumbo and finally main meal. The gumbo was the winner for sure. It was just the right kind of spice. I ate the red beans and rice, which I enjoyed. Service was good. Overall a good experience.

The food here was absolutely fantastic. Im a big sauce person.  The sauce can make or break a dish, and let me tell you,  this restaurant didnot disappoint. The crab bisque was PHENOMENAL. For my meal, I had the jumbo louisiana shrimp en cocotte. This was also extremely delicious. From the first taste,  I knew that I had chosen correctly. The grits with cheese toasted on top,  and the sauce that drowned the dish, typed with shrimp,  made this dish a flavor explosion. I loved eveything about it. I'll be sure to visit again the next time I'm in New Orleans and try another great dish.

Was here for happy hour oysters.  I had a couple of drinks and some seafood.  Everything was ok. I'm not sure how other food taste cuz I was too full after eating  the cold seafood. Can't beat the 75 cent oysters. Lol

Hands down my favorite Restaraunt in New Orleans and I've tried a lot of them.  John Besh knows how to curate a menu of the highest level. The Baked Oysters are top of the line and the Seafood Tower is impeccable. We shared the Baked Oysters, Brussel Sprouts & a Seafood Tower between 3 of us.  We all left stuffed.  Best meal we had on our 10 day food tour/business trip from Texas to Louisiana.  Don't miss out on this one!
Neat atmosphere, good price on raw oysters for happy hour, limited seating, touristy close to bourbon, I wouldn't seek out again

"Folks have a certain way o' doin' things down here".  Luke's is no different.  Great example of all the cultures in NoLa coming together on a table.   Duck Duck was very good but note the rice is crisped in olive oil so it carries that flavor throughout the meal but the crispy rice was a great texture/flavor addition to the duck. Their Étouffée comes on cavetelli which added a great twist to a big easy tradition. Cost was in-line, no Jacket required, reservations needed, would go again.  Bon Temps!

Pros: Seafood Gumbo, Shrimp w/Grits, Brussel Sprouts, Bread Pudding
Cons: Onion Tart appetizer had ANISE (didn't specify that on the menu), service was spotty

John Besh is one of my favorite chefs and just all around a pretty awesome guy that has been true to his roots so I had pretty high expectations for months leading up to a trip to New Orleans.  I chose Luke this go around over his other restaurants in the area because I had heard about Oyster happy hour.  Our entire experience did not disappoint!  We started with some extremely fresh raw and fried oysters during happy hour so we got them at the happy hour price.  The friend oysters took a little extra time so they actually ended up taking them off the bill with no complaints from us just because they felt it was the right thing to do.  My boyfriend and I shared the shrimp and grits with the crab.  Don't question it...ADD THE CRAB!  It would have been delicious without but it took it to a whole new level.  My boyfriend is NOT a fan of grits but these jalapeno cheddar grits completely converted him. We also shared some frites which were quite delicious but I had wished I had not added those so I could have had room for dessert.  Lastly I have to say the cocktail list was pretty unusual and the happy hour pricing certainly made it easy to try several!  My new favorite is the French 75!  I have tried with little success to have it made for me back home.  The cocktail alone is worth a trip to Luke in my opinion!  Came home with an autographed copy of My New Orleans so we can't wait to cook our way through New Orleans at home and relive our meal at Luke!

I would certainly return for the fantastically seasoned shrimp and grits dish, however, our tableside service was somewhat unpolished. 

Two of our sides were never submitted to the kitchen and arrived only after I mentioned it to our server, which was as we were finishing up our meal.  The dishes were removed from our bill and while appreciated and not prompted by myself, I did very much enjoy Luke and its food offerings, we'll be returning for dinner.

If I could give this place seven stars, I would. I think I've given a few places five stars, I might have to lower their stars to express how good this place is. Food and service is as good as it gets. 

My wife and I were originally trying to go to Bon Ton Cafe but for some idiotic reason they don't open on the weekend. Fortunately, we already had our eye on Luke. 

When we sat down and ordered our drinks, I decided to get the Baked P&J Oysters for an appetizer. When I took a bite of the oysters, it was like they woke up my taste buds and took them for a night on the town. 

For our main courses my wife ordered the "Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp 'En Cocotte'" and I ordered the "Choucroute Garnie Maison". 

When our dishes arrived my wife looked a little disappointed at the portion size but then she took a bite. She says it was like the flavors were dancing in her mouth and the after taste beckoned her to eat more. 

As far as my dinner goes, I don't think I've ever been bombarded with such high levels and quantity and quality at the same time. I was drowning in delight and almost didn't come back up for air. When I decided to stop eating (which was about half way through the meat) I felt like I was going to burst at the sides. 

In the end we decided we couldn't pass up on the dessert and ordered the "Gateau Basque". It was a perfect way to end such an uplifting culinary experience.

Great food and great drinks.  My husband and I were in New Orleans for the first time right after Mardi Gras 2008.  This place was great.  We liked it so much that we went back again our last night just for drinks and dessert.  I highly recommend this restaurant!

This neo-Franco/German spot is the bomb - tick, tick, BOOM!!! I wish it was located in Atlanta! I ate the crawfish bisque and the "pressed sandwich of whole roasted cochon de lait" with cherry mustard, carmelized onions, and pommes frites. AMAZING! This was true, even if the mustard and onions were a bit tangy for my likes. The waiter was quick and attentive. But, beware: There is a nasty bartendress. She was absolutely unpleasant and even pushed us off onto another bartender. That bartender, Tom I think, was marvelous. That man knows how to treat customers and to make drinks worth the money. Long story short: We stuffed ourselves silly and sleepy. Seriously, I didn't want to leave because everything else looked great. But they forced my lovely to roll me out the front door. Get there without delay. MiLO

Started with fried oysters and they were tasty, plump, and cooked perfectly. Had the burger and fries for my entrée and it was outstanding; cooked to order, a little messy, but really good. Would definitely return

We had a great brunch at Luke's. My wife ordered a Bloody Mary that was perfect. It was spicy but not overwhelming. We ordered the Brussel Sprouts and they are to die for. The omelette was very good. And as you would expect the waiter was professional.

Great location. Creative food. Solid service. 

Ate here twice this week. They describe some of the food as life changing.  Well, not for me, but it was great and fun. 

The soft shell BLT is delicious, inventive and really good. The shrimp and grits are wonderful also. 

For me, the place needs some music to bring it to
life. And that cost them the one star. Looking forward to LUKE in San Antonio.

Great drinks, food and great service.  Right next to the Hilton, and one of the best places I went to all week.  Real wheat beer in a real-wheat-beer glass, Wiskey flights, some crab legs and a kick-ass burger.  Yep, I too had my fill of Turtle Soup, Gumbo and shit and had an amazing burger.
The burger was phenomenal. Crazy happy hour deal for oysters and beer. Good looking restaurant.

Not happy, the wait to get served was about 15mins to just order a drink, then they took another 10mins to come take our order, then the waiter comes back to tell me it would be an hour for them to get me six oysters because of happy hour. not for nothing the customer who is paying full price should be the priority versus the happy hour customer.

One of the best happy hours in NOLA. ALL wines by the glass, all beers and well drinks half price- and they have a terrific selection of craft beers and belgian ales, as well as some excellent French wines and champagnes. Also, their most popular oysters are only 50 cents apiece. Super fresh and served with a wide selection of accompaniments, even my favorite, red wine vinegar. Service is friendly and professional. Can't wait to try it for dinner.

Every bit as good as August 
The rillete is the best I have ever had.

We loved this place. Went for brunch and enjoyed everything we got. Raw oysters on the half shell, baked oysters, eggs in a jar and I think another rabbit dish. Service was great. And everything tasted delicious. I liked that you can see the kitchen as well. Clean and professional.

The best meal I had in New Orleans!  We had a reservation and were seated immediately. Our waiter was extremely polite. He brought our food to us rapidly. The food was excellent. I had the shrimp étouffée. For dessert I had a flour less chocolate cake. Everything tasted as if it was made from scratch. I would recommend this place to anyone for a nice dinner out!
Hachi has great quality sushi and a great selection of Asian cuisine. Sushi is highly recommended. Cozy little spot

Great deal on oysters ($1) during happy hour. The fresh horseradish is more like wasabi and you can feel it on the top of your hair. We ordered a mint julep and a sazerac, both were loaded with booze but completely unbalanced and just a waste. I went back to martinis. Our waiter was a flirty, unkept, odd ball. I watched as he sat down with two female patrons and schmoozed after raking his fingers through his mane a few times for affect. I think he learned it from fonzie or wade kinsella. Anyway, it's only hot on tv when this person is not bringing you your real food. We ordered a beet salad and a roasted chicken. The beet salad was perfect and light. The roast chicken was beyond sloppy. It was soggy, stewey and fatty... No love. I would go back for oysters. But, again, let's hope the hygiene issue doesn't translate to seafood handling. Lastly, they dropped a few glasses at our feet and gave us some cocktails to go for free, for our trouble.

Had the turdunken from the thanksgiving day menu, was very good, coiuld have been heated a bit more thorough as I had cold spots in all of my food. The flavor made up for it. The jambalaya soup and crab and corn soup where both very good. It was a bit expensive coming in at just over $130 for a party of 3.

I am a fan of August. Luke is good but to me it's more of a burger, oyster or  breakfast place. It is not a destination restaurant in my opinion. There are places I would rather go, but if you are staying in the hotel, or live in the CBD,  it would be convenient.

We spent a boatload on brunch but received an incredible meal. The squash blossoms were crunchy and creamy, savory and sweet. I was mesmerized by the creativity and complexity in the menu without feeling exhausted by it. The shrimp and grits had a truly special sauce that had a really dimensional flavor. The soft shell crab and grits could have used some more heat but were good. Delicious.

I was disappointed with my dinner at Luke.  I was eating solo on a Sunday night, so I sat at the bar.  The vibe was great, but most of the food was poor.  I enjoyed the Salad Luke, but the market (Drumfish) fish meuniere was awful.  It was basically an oily, fried piece of fish that lacked flavor except for the heavy dose of salt - that also permeated the accompanying vegetables.  And it seemed as though the Crispy Brussels Sprouts were prepared in the same manner.  Yes, I expected them to be fried, but these were drenched in oil and doused with salt.  I was really not happy and left more than half of each dish.  I chose not to waste time with dessert.  The service was very good.
Loved it.  Had dinner on 12/24/2012.  Food was fantastic.  Service good as well.  We will go back.

This is the only place I go to for Chinese in the area. The portions are generous enough to last me for several days and the food is slightly above average in my opinion. The customer service is always friendly as well. Also very reasonably priced, I usually pay less here for more and better food than most Chinese places.

Luke is one of the places I try to go every weekend that I'm in New Orleans. The food has never disappointed. It looks like the brunch menu was changed a little. I didn't find the selection to be quite as good as it used to be, but my Croque Monsieur with a fried egg was delicious. The $9 mimosa is equivalent of a $3 mimosa somewhere else. I'd like to see them using freshly squeezed oranges for that price. Overall good experience.

Finally a sushi place in our back yard !!!

Amazing sushi and beautifully crafted dishes. Been here a few times and have left very happy with an empty wallet ;). Place can become quickly pricey as everything looks and tastes good. Definitely the best sushi I've had in this part of town.
If you are a fan of sushi, you definitely need to check them out.
Get your iPhone ready to snap some pics, they are like Picasso with their dishes.




Why 4 stars?
- they have their mesmerizing pseudo Japanese Indian trance music turned up way too loud. i feel like i nee dot start texting my wife for fear she will not hear me across the room. Had t take a Tylenol on few occasions for pre-op....

- place is always cold, they definitely need to turn the heat up a bit, its not that cozy easting sushi with chopsticks while wearing a hoodie over my head.

- their hibachi menu is ala carte, meaning if your order steak hibachi, you will get just that, any grilled veggies or rice or anything else is extra, meh. I would have maybe added a few more bucks to the entree and thrown in the veggies, who has hibachi without the yummy goodness of those grilled shrooms, onions, peppers and so forth.
Great restaurant.  Crayfish bisque was awesome. Even the chicken was good in this seafood restaurant.  Shrimp & grits - order it.  Waiter was slow to bring our dinner drinks :(

Even better than the last time I was there! Our server, Richie Rich (really!!), was funny and personable, and didn't even blink when I ordered eggnog and oysters. Yes, it's a disgusting combination, I know. Mostly the eggnog came before the oysters. But I digress...

The house made eggnog was simply delicious. As I write this, I want to go back and have another. But I like eggnog.

My friend and I split a dozen local oysters, which were amazing. They were sweet and briny and super fresh. So good. I think I ate most of them. 

We then had a few other dishes. The crab and corn bisque is very rich and creamy, but with a nicely balanced flavor and enough crab to make you know you're eating it.

The burrata is a giant sized salad wig a great big hunk of creamy cheese, and was fabulous as well. Not to be outdone, the ricotta gnocchi were pillowy little morsels of deliciousness.

Can I go back yet?

Went to the Luke Happy Hour for oysters.  It starts at 3pm.  What a joy!  .75 oysters and half price drinks.  Thanks fellow Yelpers for letting me know about the Happy Hour.  When you walk into Luke you just have to love the look of the place.  Of course this is a John Besh restaurant so you expect nothing less. 
They serve large PJ oysters on the happy hour.  I have  gone to other happy hour  oyster restaurants and they serve the smallest oysters they would not serve during regular hours.  Not here, they are large and succulent for .75 cents! You can also get 6 fried for $7.50.  There are also six specialty coctails that are half price and draft beer is half price as well.
several appetizers are half price.  The rabbit and chicken liver pate was just outstanding.  My wife ordered the crawfish bisque and the depth of flavor was heavenly.  (Bisque is not on happy hour).
Luke is just simply an outstanding restaurant with quality food and service. I have been for dinner and truely enjoyed the food as well.  The Happy Hour is just another reason to come and enjoy and save a little out of pocket as well.
Gumbo and shrimp and grits are well worth it. Door number three cocktail is quite tasty--not too sweet but refreshing.
Really nice atmosphere. Staff were so nice and helpful. We loved our food and drinks. Don't forget to order yourself their nice Bloody Mary . Located in the French Quarter and so easy to park.

LOVE this Place!  Arrived before a Saints Game, had a Large Party, no reservations... the staff was Great.  They seated us, no problems and the food was amazing!  We started with coffee and a wonderful "Southern Style" Brunch and of course some Adult Beverages.... The Staff and Fare is Not to be missed.  This place is a MUST for locals and I highly recommend it to visitors who wish to experience True New Orleans Cooking  and Southern Hospitality.

Came here based on other reviews, and we were not disappointed (although we didn't take the advice on booking a reservation. Should have!) Oysters were phenomenal...2 dozen between 3 of us and they all went down fast. I then had one of the best salads, yes salads, that I've ever had - Salad Luke. The beets were sweet and perfectly bitter. It was a little hard to eat, but worth the mess. My hubby and I split the King Crab and had a wonderful time cracking and dipping. So good. Finally, my 20 month old loved the grilled cheese with veggies (btw my husband may come back just for these veggies). I don't recommend coming with a kiddo, but if you have to, they still treat you right. We will be back!

I found this restaurant on Yelp when I was looking for some oyster places in New Orleans. And wow - I'm so glad that I decided to check this place out!!

[Service]
My friends and I made a reservation for 4:45pm. We had to walk from French Market, so we were twenty minutes late to our reservation. But we still had our reserved table ready. The hostess was also very polite and welcoming when we arrived. 

[Ambience]
Very clean and classy! It is quite upscale so I recommend you to dress up a little when you visit this restaurant. 

[Food]
Luke has a happy hour for 75 cents per P&J oyster at 3-6pm everyday! This was the main reason why I chose this restaurant for oysters. My boyfriend and I ordered 30 oysters in total. They came with horse radish, cocktail sauce, and lemons. Beware - the horse radish was a bit too strong. Oysters were really fresh and tasty! 

[Drinks]
Luke also offers half price on cocktails and beers during happy hour. I got the door#3 cocktail which had vodka, pomegranate, mint, and lime. I enjoyed how refreshing the cocktail was!

All in all, I was impressed by this restaurant. Food, drinks, atmosphere, and service... they were all great, and I have nothing to complain!

I came here with the expectation of "the best burger ever" maybe not the best ever but at the moment I could not think of anything better. My boyfriend and I were here for happy hour, we ordered the fried oysters and we were not disappointed. Then we decided to split the Luke burger as we were not super hungry. We were brought out a sliced burger and fries for each of us. The burger was delicious and were happy it was already split between us. Would definitely recommend it to others.
2 words Happy Hour!  Calvin will shuck you some mighty tasty fresh off the boat oysters and a smile for $.50. Can't beat that anywhere! 3-6

I was lukewarm to Lüke, which is a shame as it was the New Orleans meal I was looking forward to most.

My dinner had potential, but it feel apart largely in the execution, starting with the cut of beef. I ordered the entrecôte grillée au frites, which featured a sizable ribeye with a side of fries. Unfortunately, a third of the ribeye was fat, it was full of tendon and was cooked well below my requested temperature of medium. 

Nova seemed to enjoy her shrimp and grits more than I enjoyed my entree, but she did comment that the dish almost had too much going on. Bold flavors generally don't bother her, but she felt a few subtractions would've greatly benefited the overall taste. 

Our server was pleasantly friendly, but ineffective when it mattered. When she inquired about my meal, I mentioned the issues I had. She seemed genuinely disappointed that I didn't enjoy it, but she really didn't do anything about it either. 

So if you're visiting New Orleans and thinking about trying out a Besh place, I'd recommend going to another of his spots. Friends of ours have liked their meals at both Restaurant August and The American Sector. 

Sadly, however, Besh is the second Next Iron Chef contestant who's let me down with their food. I guess there's a reason why they didn't win, huh?

Hooray for 0.75 cent oysters during happy hour!!!!  Their HH drinks specials are amazing and the cocktail selection makes me want to have a couple at a time and be very very bad.  We all loved the Silver Saint and French 75.  Keeping it classy!

Came for happy hour at the recommendation of friends. (Happy hour is not just at the bar, by the way!)
The 75 cent raw oysters and half off drinks are an awesome deal. The oysters were huge and delicious, freshly shucked right in front of us at the bar. The Rosemary gin drink I got has a nice flavor. We also had the crispy brussel sprouts-- definitely recommend. The service  was spot on. 
Overall, we loved everything and felt like we got a great value and a memorable meal.

This place is SO GOOD. I had a burger of some sort, but also tried a jambalaya type dish which my mom and sister ordered and some quail wings my dad ordered. 

Food: everything was absolutely delicious. The best food I had in NOLA, I think.

Ambience/waitstaff: the place is comfortable and not noisy, and the waitstaff is very chill and laid back, but also efficient.

Overall excellent place, the type of restaurant yelp reviews were made for.
Very disappointed... waited extremely long to order drinks... ordered appetizers and one plate came out with hair and waiter acted like no big deal... finished and left!!!

Excellent service. Delicious dishes and large one


We had the pork ragout. It is great, very tasteful and there is lots of it

We had the oyster salad. Wonderful, fresh greens and six large crisp fried oysters

The people at the next table ordered hamburgers. They are enormous

We will go back

I really ought to visit this little cafe more often a they have such delicious sandwiches (a personal favorite is when they have chicken and waffles options available!). I rather like how they tweet out what their features are each day when it comes to food.

I don't drink coffee so I have no idea how that tastes but I do know that a number of my friends really love this place for their beverages too.

So pricey. I do not know why sandwiches need to cost $6.90. They are good, though.

Also the coffee is downright BAD and too expensive.

Horrible. We were staying at the hilton and stopped here because we were starving at 9 pm. I used to serve tables and rarely complain about service but...

Our waitress forgot to put our order in the computer ( I know because 45 minutes the first time she came back, asked for our order again and proceeded back to punch into the computer). When food finally arrived an hour and a half after walking in, it was tasteless. How do you make Cajun food tasteless in New Orleans. Thanks to Luke, I now know that every restaurant in NOLA isn't amazing. I was starting to wonder since all of my other dining experiences have been amazing here.

I am torn on this review as the food is awesome both at this location as well as the San Antonio, TX location and i think Besh is great.  

The issue I have is that the server was a complete asshat.  I am a very positive person and will rarely call someone out on the Internet (in person where they have a chance to defend their self is more my style). this was rude to my mother and cut her off mid order then proceeded to act like a prick to my sister-in-law.

I will most likely visit other locations or other Besh restaurants instead of  this one in the future.

I actually really like this Cosi! The Law School is right around the corner so I've turned to this trusty Cosi many-a times with minimal disappointments. The tomato soup is always a winner and most of their salads are good (except the Asian salad is a bit wimpy, which is a big no-no in my book). The pizza is really tasty too. 

I mean, if you come to Cosi, you shouldn't be expecting anything gourmet. Just something quick, easy, and tasty. I guess it isn't super cheap relative to the competing lunch options, but its not that expensive either. Don't come here everyday though with the plethora of eats around Penn. 

I don't know about anyone else but when the cold strikes and I crave soup, Cosi's tomato soup generally hits the spot.  3.5 stars! (Yelp needs to have half stars)

I like Lüke, their dishes were interesting and well presented and tastes great. The only comment I have is that maybe they should be light handed with the salt. We loved the stuffed oysters and rabbit and chicken liver pate as starters. Word of caution, the pate is pretty big and like organ dishes, it is very rich. So if you order the pate, then maybe order a lighter entree. I had the etoufee and my husband had the soft shell crab. We love them both except for the saltiness of both. Other than that, the cocktails are great and in general the food are delicious!

Lüke is a chef John Besh restaurant located in the Central Business district below the Hilton Hotel. It's very close to Canal Street. 

I visited Lüke with a group of 5 for happy hour. The happy hour special included: half off cocktails, wine, beer and OYSTERS daily from 3 to 6 p.m. 

We ordered 3 dozen raw oysters, a dozen fried oysters, jalapeno grits, pâté of rabbit & chicken livers, and crispy brussel sprouts. Everything was delicious and so flavorful. It was one of the best restaurants we dined at during our visit to New Orleans.
BEST HAPPY HOUR!!!  $0.50 oysters and half priced drinks across from our hotel...  What else does a girl need?

Very disappointed in the service as well as the food.  Our first night in New Orleans Luke was recommended by the hotel . Lamb was rubbery and tasteless.  Pork was over done. Adding salt didn't even help the taste . 
Will not get a second chance .

The lines here during lunch time are always chaotic, and really inefficiently organized. Service is pretty lacking too, just come during a time that is less crazy. Love the Cosi flatbread and squagels. They have a thing called "taste-two" where you can get half of a flatbread sandwich, and a soup or salad for around $9. It's not bad at all... just really do not come here around 11-12pm.

Really special Japanese restaurant. The quality level of the food is outstanding. The presentation is beautiful. They offer far more than what has become generic Japanese food in my area-be sure to explore some of the Chef's unique dishes, like the yellowtail or Kobe beef that you sear at your table on a hot rock-absolute amazing! It is not inexpensive but it is byob and sooooo worth the money. I almost forgot to talk about the super hip decor. You can't believe you are in a shopping center restaurant. It looks like it belongs in downtown Manhattan.

Found this place close to our hotel. Read the menu, read the reviews and decided to give it a shot. Glad we did. This was the best meal we have had in New Orleans. They started us with some really fresh bread. Good fresh bread is usually a mark of a good restaurant. I ordered a cup of gumbo. It was a little cup, but it is was loaded with shrimp and oysters. Very good! 

For our entree, I got to the shrimp and grits. Like another reviewer, I'm usually not a fan of shrimp and grits. But I was mopping this stuff up. I couldn't get enough. My wife ordered the shrimp cavatelli and she loved it as well. The kids got chicken tenders and the biggest grilled cheese I've ever seen. We were a little out of place with kids, but whatcha gonna do. 

I capped it off with the bread pudding which is also a must have. 

Other details. It's s pretty tight squeeze in here and it was loud. And it was pricey. But none of that should take away from the fact that it was an amazing meal.  People have knocked the service, but our waiter, Kyle, did a great job. 

You need to eat here.
Best experience I've had since I've been to Luke. Request for Cybill bartender! She gives you a warm feeling.

South belle oyster were ok. The Alabama one last we're on point. Not the p&j stuffed oysters with crab were delicious. As far of the service by Tristan top notch. I recommend it for a fancy little date. The gumbo was delicious had to order more bread so I can clean the plate. As far as the main dish. Shrimp étouffée that was amazing. Their sauce, seasoning of everything that was cooked here was just strictly amazingly delicious. This is what food should taste like. Luke is killing the game! Parking was not too bad and their big sign show where they are located. Is definitely for people with money as the prices are high. Now to close it off I had some creme brûlée which put the cherry on top for a good 4 course meal. I shared with adding all the oysters and stuff and came out to an even meal for 2. Unless you are planning to be stuffed or just overindulge then I suggest sharing. As it will help with cost and still get to enjoy many plates.

Enjoy your come. You are about to have a party of flavors in your mouth.
Went for happy hour, 50 cent oysters and hugh ones at that. very helpful staff. Give it a try.
Good burgers nice comfortable atmosphere people that work there are very nice I would keep comming back
Food used to be really good. Delivery is horrible. Last 2 pies I got looked like a rally car driver delivered it. People inside are nice but do yourself a favor and Go elsewhere

So great! We had the oysters, mussels, clams & shrimp platter. All great and salty! The Brussel sprouts were delicious. Crab bisque is always delicious. Then we tried the Bread Pudding for the first time..... AMAZING!!!
Had the croque Madame. Unbelievable. Throw some tabasco on it and it is WINNING!!

Food is not good. We ordered Fois Gras and the toasted bread along with it came cold and old. Roasted chicken dish was oily and not tasty at all. 
One good thing about the place is service, but I won't come back for that.

One of the best restaurants I've ever been to. Didn't partake in the 50 cent oysters but their breakfast was amazing. I ordered the eggs in a jar, which may possibly be the greatest breakfast ever. The staff was super friendly and our server gave us free champagne. Great place, definitely going back next time I'm in town!

The atmosphere was pleasant during lunch hour. The waitress was delightful! She was very sweet and consistently kept up with our table in addition to the others. My friend ordered an old fashion, and it was the best I've ever tasted. We ordered the pâté as an appetizer and it hit the spot. I wish I would have ordered just two pâté platters. Anyway, my friend ordered the swordfish and I grabbed the local fish grilled. Will go again. Kinda pricey but you get what you pay for

I usually go during happy hour to enjoy 0.75/ per fresh and clean oyster.
This time, because my parents' in town visiting. We decided to have dinner after oyster. 

We had jumbo Louisiana Shrimp and crawfish étouffée with a French fries.

We feel those two entree were a bit to salty.
This was probably one of the best meals I have ever had in my entire life. Seriously. Omg AMAZING!

Horrible Customer Service .. Placed an online order and after we placed the order,we called an was told 20 min.. Oh and no soup because the cook had not come yet ( it was 1pm) when we got there was told oh it will be 45 min to an HOUR because there were several other orders that he did not know about. He said he canceled our orders but still charged our card!
Went here for happy hour and got fried oysters & desserts. We were very pleased with the pricing , service and atmosphere . Would def go again. Thanks staff :)

So it is Saturday night.  I arrived in NoLa Wednesday and am leaving Sunday.  I have eaten my way through most of the city and this is to be my last stop on the gluttony train.  

My wife is a big John Besh fan so this was a very exciting finale for her.  

The outside of this restaurant is nothing special.  You could walk right by and not even notice it.  As soon as you walk though the door, however, things change.  

It is lively!  Great music, warm wood finishes, cool old school tile floor and a kick ass 
raw bar!  It was piled high with mountains of ice, covered by shellfish.  You could belly right up and start your seafood adventure.  We were a party of four so sadly we opted for a table.  I do NEED to sit at that bar next time.  

We at least sat NEXT to the raw bar.  I immediately ordered a mint julep (after the ladies ordered obviously).  It was served very traditionally and it was delicious.  Everyone at the table ordered different drinks off of the cocktail menu and they were all good.  

For starts I went with the liver Pate'.  It was extraordinary.  I am not using that word lightly.  I love pate' and order it almost every time it is offered.  This one was velvet, like Coming To America velvet.  I was in love.  (Insert second mint julep.)

For dinner...oh for dinner I had Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte."  This was a culinary masterpiece.  The best shrimp and grits I have ever had.  Creamy, spicy, perfectly cooked grits. The shrimp were huge, again perfectly seasoned and cooked. (Insert third mint julep.)

Now you might say why the four stars?  Two things.  First:  The chairs in this place are crazy uncomfortable.  I am not kidding.  Who picked these torture chairs?  They have a raised lip around the edge of the seat that digs into the back of your legs. Check it out I swear.  Second:  When we arrived I told the waited we were going to be on a slow roll.  Please give us some time to eat and enjoy.  Five minutes after the first course came out the entrées showed up.  We obviously had to send them back which I hate doing.  Now the manager came out and apologized and they fired us new meals which was nice but that kind of stuff makes me nuts.    

Besides these two points you must go here.  The food is amazing.
An old school feel restaurant with great food.  It is a little loud inside and is quite busy.  Blue crab bisque and shrimp and grits were great!

Very classy find more toward the downtown area of the French Quarters.

The staff were absolutely perfect. Our waitress was very kind to talk to and made sure we had everything our stomachs desired. The manager even took her time to check-in and converse with us, and that was really appreciated.

I had the opportunity to enjoy the croquet Madame which allotted me delicious bite after delicious bite. My friend had the frittata which was beautifully light and fluffy. 

The decor was very nice as well and we got to sit in front of the glass kitchen window where we watched the chefs work their magic on the stove. Think of magicians with the grace of a fairy godmother but still the ferocity of Harry Potter.

Definitely recommend this to anybody in the area

I ordered the Étouffee of blue crab & brown shrimp, my friend ordered shrimp and grits. We came when drinks were have off (SCORE!) so ordered a sazerac and riverbend...sazerac was super strong! I thought the food was really solid. The etouffee had so much flavor and the crab was fantastic..really fresh tasting and freshly made pasta. Shrimp and grits was really tasty and had a nice spice to it. I'm taking off a few points for the service which was really bad. By the time we got seated it took 15 minutes for someone to take our drink order or even acknowledge us even though the servers past us by at least 10 times.

Loved it! Ate here our first night in town and headed back tonight. Friend and I can't decide if we like it here or at Cochon more, but it's not apples to apples so please eat at both!

She had the drum fish and veggies while I had the mussels and frites. Both were good but we both wanted to fill our water bottles with the broth from the mussels, wow, so good! We shared the Louisiana shrimp appetizer; they were great too. As it was happy hour, we each had a cocktail. I had the mint julep and she had something pink and yummy that for the life of me I cannot name, sorry. The important part was they were good and half price. Yay!

Between Horrible Boss stories, Ryan confessed that he'd once split 7 dozen oysters with a friend here.  I can see why.

Being a left-coaster, I'm used to oysters having a strong umami flavor with a hint of sweetness under the brine. Not so here.

Gulf oysters are so mild and creamy that pairing them with beer would be a waste of both. Ryan ordered a French 75, and tho I was tempted to order champagne, we all had a couple of 75s.

Fifty-cents each at happy hour (4-6pm) is a steal. I've been addicted to shellfish since my uncle in Mexico ripped open a bushel sack of raw clams and taught me to eat them with lemon and chili sauce. I was maybe 5 and ate raw clams till I could roll myself to the car. This platter comes with excellent and pungent fresh horseradish, a good cocktail sauce, lemon wedges and saltines, should you want to pollute the little swimmers. I eat mine bare.

Lüke's shuckers are shucking precise. No grit, sand or broken shells.  Just good, clean slurping.

PS The Gulf accounts for 70ish% of the US oyster production, according to Fish & Wildlife stats. Izat why the Pacific Northwest varieties are so damn expensive? 

http://www.oysterguide.com/new-discoveries/why-gulf-oysters-are-never-named-by-their-home-bays/

Been to Luke twice and so far so good. The restaurant set up is nice and super clean unlike some other restaurants in NOLA. CMON! anyone in NOLA understands what I mean. Shoes stickin to the floors and what not...

Anyhow...I ordered the crawfish omelette the first time and it was ok. Plating was pretty and it tasted good but probably not the best thing to get when you're hung over. 

Second time I got the shrimp and grits. The grits were made with jalapeños and cheddar topped with a sauce made with sausage, green onions and decent sized shrimp. Every bite was...OH MY GAH! Toe curling goodness.

Nice improvements. I had a craving for a flatbread pizza and decided to brave the madness again. The bosses must've been reading these reviews because there was more organization to the place. They've set up some makeshift aisles for placing an order, with much more clearly defined and clearly labeled purposes. Unfortunately the waiting area is still an open pit where people look as though they aren't done ordering or confused about what to do with themselves. 

I still didn't see a "pay here" station. I think it would be better if the food preparers direct you over to pay for your order instead of allowing you to stand idly waiting for cashiers to start screaming at you. Not fully there yet Cosi, but nice moves in a better direction. Much appreciated!

Buritto, need I say more. They taste do damn good. Chipotle, a fastfood chain that I actually  come back to. 
In full disclosure, I thought this was such a great food and concept I bought the stock in 2007, it's been a total winner!

I had the duck confit and white bean cassoulet. I also had the chocolate cake, bread pudding, and profiteroles for dessert.

The duck confit was outstanding. A quarter of duck was cooked with a nice crisp on the outside, yet tender and delicious inside. The cassoulet was yummy with a nice flavor of bacon, although a little dry. The garlic sausage was great. The dish came with three big chunks of fried pork belly for a nice alternative. This is a VERY meaty dish. 

I tried the Monday special - daube of slow cooked lamb and it was excellent. Little patties of tender lamb, flavored perfectly. 

For dessert, don't waste your time with anything but the bread pudding. The chocolate cake was dry and profiteroles just okay. The bread pudding was warm, boozy, and with the right consistency. A big hit for me.

Went here the first night we were in town.  
Was not expecting the casual atmosphere, but very much appreciated it as we were so beat from traveling.

We had made a reservation, but it was Monday night and New Orleans seems to be sleeping in the beginning of the week and wakes up as you advance in days.

We loved the Flamenkuche, which was like a flatbread with onions and bacon.  Very tasty.

Very much liked the croque madame, cooked crispy and the fries were salty and plentiful.

But in my opinion if you know what a Jewish matzo ball soup tastes like, then you will want to skip onto some other choice on the menu.

I'd go back, but it might take awhile to go through all the other restaurants in town.

What a wonderful meal! Everything was outstanding and the shrimp and grits were heaven sent! And the service by Elliot was so so exquisite! He did such a fabulous job taking care of our private party. He took such great care with the food and it was clear the joy he had in providing impeccable service just was icing on the cake. I will definitely be doing this to list!

If I could sum up our evening at Luke in two words, it would be "absolutely terrible."

We arrived early for our reservation on a Saturday night in March to find a half-empty restaurant. Despite the ample amount of empty tables (that remained empty the entire evening), we were told to wait by the hostesses for about 15 minutes until they decided to seat us. They brought us to a back dining room near the kitchen that was practically empty, and sat us at a tiny table in the corner.

Another ten minutes elapsed before our waiter came to introduce himself. We had the misfortune of being served by Kyle, who is hands down the most inept waiter we have ever encountered. He didn't know the menu whatsoever nor did he have any idea what the specials for the night were. When I asked for more information on the specialty beers, he couldn't answer - rather he turned the question back on to me, like I was supposed to provide the knowledge myself.

We started with the Baked P&J Oysters, which was the highlight (and only highlight) of the meal. They came piping hot, and were absolutely delicious.

My girlfriend ordered the Etoufee. Despite repeatedly asking Kyle if the entree was spicy (he assured us it wasn't), the dish arrived far too spicy for her to even eat. She was only able to manage a few bites before spending the next 15 minutes drinking water to cool her mouth down.
