I ordered the Steak and Frites. While the steak was cooked perfectly, it wasn't brought out hot. It came to the table lukewarm. Same deal with the fries. Lukewarm. Maybe now I see where the "Luke" in the name of the place comes from?

We were so disappointed with our experience that, after receiving the check, we asked to speak to a manager. Jennifer came over and we explained the situation. To her credit, she seemed genuinely concerned and asked what she could do to make things right. She offered to take care of something on the bill, or try to get us to come back another time to give us a better experience. We refused both, because A. we ate the food and B. we didn't want to waste another meal at Lüke. 

It seems like most people's experiences at Luke have differed from mine - which makes me wonder if I came on an off-night? Perhaps Kyle was new on the job? Perhaps the kitchen staff was slacking? I don't know. All I can say is that our experience was awful, and we'll never go back.

I picked Luke solely because it was one of the few restaurants open on Christmas for dinner. It is a hotel restaurant with a generic NOLA menu, raw seafood to steak. The cuisine tilts toward French what with rabbit pate, crab en ravigote, etc. Some dishes are served en cocotte, small cast iron deep pans, and the portions are fairly large, perfect to split. After ordering the mixed seafood platter and waiting a while we received without explanation a slightly altered variation. When we inquired we were told the kitchen had run out of one of the items, so they had upped the oysters. Had to send it back, because one of us can't eat oysters and miffed that the plate was plopped on the table without any explanation. One of the two servers who took care of our table was an absolutely clueless airhead. Luckily, we had the better one wait on us the rest of the meal.
As a second alternative,  we had the boiled gulf shrimp, not deveined and unpeeled. Somewhat messy to eat and the veins soiled the whole experience by making the texture somewhat gritty. The server brought us soaking wet napkins to wipe our hands. LOL. 
We split the grilled drum and ended with a simple salad, both fairly good. 
The kitchen is not where the restaurant is and I think the temperature of the dishes suffer for the distance, the room temp.  fish and accompanying veggies, as well as the butter emulsion, almost solidified. 
The space is large with a handsome main dining room, a pressed tin ceiling and a dark wood bar, newspapers hanging on dowels. I'd avoid the rear room/the Siberia.

I was kinda skeptical of this place at first since all the locals I had talked to recommended other places. But I decided to go on a gutsy feeling and checked it out and I'm glad I did...the food was amazing, our waiter was friendly, the other wait staff were attentive to drinks and such.

To start out we ordered the qual. I was extremely excited for this one at first, it came out with a beautiful crust on it (fried), smelled delicious, it was cooked to perfection.

As a soup, I went with the gumbo. I'm a gumbo snob, I make it...I make it pretty good. This gumbo was top notch, normally I always have something to say but I honestly couldn't really think of anything to say, it was perfectly balanced...not too salty or anything, I had to add some pepper but I like a little kick. Would recommend the gumbo to everyone!

For my entree I went with the Shrimp and Grits which was suggested by the waiter. This...was the damn highlight. If I could eat something everyday...I'd eat the Shrimp and Grits, everything was amazing....the Grits were cheesy and just freakin awesome. The Shrimp was perfect. The sauce along with it was on point. Everything was on point.

I wish I had room for dessert because I'm sure it would've been just as great as everything else. If you're in the area, Lüke is definitely worth a stop for!
The pancakes were on point. The pecan butter in them excellent. A little pricey though for breakfast

Based on my research and my experience here last week, this has to be a top 5 happy hour spot in New Orleans!  3-6pm. 75 cent raw oysters. $1.25 fried oysters. Half price beers, cocktails, and some wines I believe. Cocktails are tremendous. Nice beer list. Oysters were delicious. I ate my very first raw oysters here, so it'll always have a place in my heart. Got some coaching from the friendly bartender. Fried oysters were amazing. They come with a spicy ranch sauce, but if you ask, you may be able to get some remoulade, which the oyster guys told us we needed to try. 

I know there's plenty of reviews about the happy hour here, but it can't be recommended enough. Beautiful restaurant that offers a cozy spot to spend the mid afternoon sipping quality drinks and enjoying top notch oysters. This is a must try.

3 - okay service 4 - food 3 - New Orleans opportunity cost when there is K-Paul's and others that are very New Orleans

Great food fun but too many places that are better. American Sector is a better value and also a Besh restaurant.

Luke's is fabulous! It was on our 'must visit again' list of restaurants from our last trip.  Our server, "Richie Rich", made the evening an experience!!  Amazing service, excellent suggestions , tasty food, wine pairings, etc.  (Can you tell we loved it?!) 

Visiting four months later we were thrilled and charmed to be at the same table and Rich is our server. All the food is amazing; you won't be disappointed-and ask to be seated with Rich and his team!

We came here for breakfast upon a friend's recommendation.   The shrimp and grits were excellent.  I added a biscuit which was steep for $3.00.  The shrimp were large and cooked perfectly.

The bloody Mary was the best ever.  I tried the bourbon milkshake which is a local special.  It was not sweet at all, and good with breakfast. 

The Luke breakfast has delicious bacon and sausage.  I would highly recommend.   The biscuit was ok.

I just recently moved to the area and was craving sushi. I stumbled across this little gem while exploring what was around. There's a wide variety of different rolls offered and it was good. Coming from a family that owned a sushi place I was happy with the quality at Hachi. The dining area is modern and elegant. I will be returning.

Best raw bar happy hour I have ever been to. Happy hour is from 3 to 6 so I was a little concerned when I got there after 5. I was pleasantly surprised that happy hour applies to tables (in my home town it almost always only applies to the bar area). Nothing beats .75 cent oysters and half price cocktails.

They refused to seat us despite having a reservation.

We stopped by Luke at 5 pm today for happy hour. Upon entering, we were told that they were booked up for the evening as a result of the St. Patrick's Day parade. So, we stepped over to the bar to look for a seat and also went onto Open Table to see if there were reservations available. We were in luck! There was a reservation at 5:15, which we promptly booked. When we returned to the hostess stand, they told us that they weren't honoring Open Table reservations. Why be on Open Table then? 

This is not the first time they have pretended to be fully booked when trying to walk in. Last time at least they honored the reservation.
Saturday and Sunday Brunch Menu . . . Did not include Etouffee.  Did include gumbo.  Mission Yum accomplished!  Note, no Lunch Menu was available during this time.

Fried Oysters (a happy hour special...don't get me started on the dipping sauce!) Crispy Brussel Sprouts with green apples, marcona almonds, espilette honey & fresh farmers cheese. Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp & Grits (and I'm talking melt in your mouth roasted Grismill jalapeño cheddar grits) with andouille and green onion sausages. We ended with Brendan's Bread Pudding with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce. AMAZING!!!!

Normally, I like this Cosi, but today, when I ordered a Turkey, Bacon, and Cheddar Melt (very good, by the way), they failed to even START making my sandwich until after I had paid and waited for my sandwich for at least five minutes. Needless to say, I was not very well pleased, but I was even more surprised that the cook offered a really weak apology.

I like the food here, and I think the half and half option (e.g. half a salad, half a soup) is a good deal, but I'm never really confident in the quality of the service here. It's often crowded, and things don't seem to be very well organized here.

First... after indulging in what I will say is the most explosive flavorful shrimp and grits, chicken and waffles, oysters and mimosas... ever... we wondered how it was possible someone could rate this place less than 5 stars. I could not believe someone rated this place 1 star after saying their shrimp were not cooked correctly... like there is a single way a shrimp is supposed to be prepared! And then requested the same thing 3 times... please...

The service was great! Not only was the staff friendly and informative for this Alaskans random questions about Cajun food and the South in general, 3 staff even came over to help with our plans for the day as we were tasked with sourcing exotic plants for the arch at a wedding!

If u are trying to treat yourself for your first time in New Orleans in the 20-50 per person. range, this is the spot!

Thanks Luke!
Great happy hour spot for oysters and cocktails. Tried the sausage plate and was very impressed. Steak was also well seasoned. Will come back for the hamburgers that we kept seeing being ordered.

What a great place! If we had a place like this in DC I would be a regular. The food is the best we have had so far in NOLA. We didn't even make it to the entrees as we filled up on the appetizers. Oysters were great as was the charcuterie plate and the onion tart with pork belly. Service was a little slow but to be expected with the Mardi Gras parade passing by out front. Plan to go back to try the entrees.

I love going here for happy hour (3-6 pm), which includes 75-cent oysters, half-price beers, cocktails, and wines by the glass. Probably my favorite thing on the menu is the rabbit and chicken pate. I already swore to myself that I'd one day request a day off of work, order the pate togo, and binge watch the sh!t out of The Office on Netflix. 

Oysters - Decent-sized. Make sure you go easy on the horseradish. Don't try to prove how brave you are. It's not a competition.
Rabbit and chicken pate - Insert fire emoji here
Fries - Good
Crispy brussel sprouts - Okay, not missing much if you pass up on this

Bloody Mary - was bloody terrible
Door#three - Good!

I've never had trouble parking around it, which is always a bonus. Just keep in mind that parking downtown is $6/2hrs. You might want to make a reservation if you're planning on going during happy hour on weekends.

We just came here for desert and coffee. 
They had great strong coffee and their bread pudding was very tasty and rich.
happy hour oysters, half off drinks- can't wait to go back.

It's been over a month now....and every once in a while I just think "hmmmmmm, wish I had another soft shell crab blt with that really good pecan beer".....I just cannot get it out of my head! SO DAMN TASTY.

I have to say...I have never been disappointed in a Besh place (unlike Emeril - steer clear)....always great food and excellent service....keep doing what you're doing 'cause I am lovin' it.

Not a huge fan of this place.  I've been all over New Orleans, but didn't think the restaurant was worth the price.  
1.  We got the fried oyster, avocado salad.  It was incredibly overdressed, to the point of soggy leaves at the end.  But good flavor.
2.  I got the gumbo, yummy but not dissimilar to more affordable places
3.  burger, good but not amazing.  Fries were a bit cold and had to ask for a new side.  They weren't crispy either, a little soggy.
What was the strangest thing was that it was really difficult to get a reservation, but when we went--the restaurant wasn't full!

In town alone for a recent business trip, I was on the hunt for good food in a place that I could eat by myself and not feel like a total loser.  Luke not only fit that bill, but was so darn good that I ended up eating there twice during my four day stay.

The foie gras appetizer was delicious, as was the gumbo.  But the real draw for me was the 25 cent oysters during happy hour.  TWENTY FIVE CENTS!  And they were huge and fresh and delicious.

The atmosphere is modern and casual.  The servers were attentive and friendly.

All in all, I have absolutely nothing bad to say about this place.  And on a return trip to NOLA, it would be high on my list of places to eat again.

Ah restaurant Luke, I had an very good experience the first time I went, but after the last two I honestly cannot really recommend it anymore with so many other options in town.  

During my first visit I was seated promptly and ordered the burger and a soup.  The burger is probably the best I had in the city so far.  It 's served with tomatoes, bacon, some caramelized onions, and cheese.  The quality of the meat is amazing.  The fries are also some of the best I've had.

My 2nd experience at Luke was not good.  I arrived and asked to be seated at a table and was told the wait would be 20 minutes but I could sit at the bar.   I proceeded to the bar which happens to have a giant post blocking one side of it.  The bartender saw me asked if I wanted a drink, I said no, just a menu.  I looked it over real quick and proceeded to wait...and wait and I notice that a table has opened so I ask the hostess if I can get seated there since I'm not getting any service.   I get seated at the table and they say the server will be right with me.  I specifically asked her if they were understaffed that night and she said no they weren't.   So I start waiting again and don't even get a I'll be right with you or anything.  Maybe I'm exaggerating the length of time, but at that point I was done so I just walked out.

During my next rotation in the city, I decided to give them another shot.  I tried the pork shank, belly, and bratwurst.  Honestly, it was pretty bland and that's coming from someone who cooks without using a lot of salt.  

As others have mentioned, their service seems inconsistent and understaffed.  I might go there again for the burger, but there are still so many other restaurants that I would like to try that I don't think I'll go back to Luke's again.

Great experience...enormous burgers.  Had lunch and some appetizers.  The service is awesome and the menu offers a nice variety.  The food is delicious and filling.  Your lunch meal maybe end up being the only meal of the day since the sandwiches are huge.

I came here on the recommendation of a friend, even though some of the reviews said it wasn't that great. I don't know what they were talking about...it was amazing!! I ordered the Louisiana Jumbo Shrimp "en Cocoette" with roasted jalapeño cheese grits & andouille & green onion sausages. Omg...so delicious. I also ordered the brussel sprouts as a side. They were a little sweet as some others mentioned, but they also had a little spice. I liked the flavor combination, and they were roasted a perfect brown. For dessert I had the steamed chocolate with salted caramel ice cream. Divine. Seriously. So good. Service was good as well. I had multiple people checking on me throughout the meal. Yum!

Best gym ever. The help is great. The equipment and facility is extremely well-maintained. The protein smoothie bar is clutch. I'm a sucker for my protein shake after my workout. It honestly brightens my workout and my day. I honestly cannot even begin to say about how wonderful the employees there are. I love going to this gym. For $20 a month, it's all you'll need.

After visiting the Dermatologist's office on the floor above, I decided to give this place a try. 

I can't quite remember the exact name of the sandwich I ordered, but it was comprised of roast beef, egg, super melty cheese, mushrooms, and arugula. The roast beef was surprisingly tender and juicy, and the cheese was gooey goodness. I'm not much of an egg fan, but it was cooked well and it complimented the sandwich nicely. 

The only complaints that I have is that service was somewhat distant, and the limited space. Otherwise, it was a great experience, and I will be back!
Great sushi!!! Was nearby at a paintball tournament and stoped in. The hachikaze roll is amazing!!!!
I had breakfast here every morning I was in town.  The food was amazing and the coffee was perfect.  Great service rounded out the experience.  I would highly suggest the crab omelette.

O-M-G, so delicious and with pro wait staff. They took us without reservations and sat us immediately.  I was so glad to hear they had kids menus given the sophistication of the offerings. Chicken tenders and mac and cheese, check! Our waitress was very personable, engaging with the kids and knowledgeable about the menu. From several potential selections, she steered me toward one which was especially good in season (right now). 
The crawfish omelet was amazing, full of buttery deliciousness, baby asparagus and little pieces of mushrooms, I think chanterelle, alongside a mixed greens salad. The omelet and the kids meals came with tasty frites. Hubs had a quinoa bowl with farmers cheese, poached egg and avocado, declaring it delectable. 
In addition to the awesome food they had cool decor, with contrasting parquet floors, stuffed board heads (also intriguing the kids) and oyster shell-framed mirrors. Wish we lived here to visit Luke weekly. My kids keep asking to go back, too.
This place exceeded all of my expectations!!! Great food, reasonable prices. Amazing presentation. Great service. Cool atmosphere. Couldn't have asked for a better date night.

Very good experience overall! We started the meal with drinks.  The house mixed drinks we selected were sophisticated and well made.  The wait staff was a younger and authentically New Orleans which personally added to our experience.  The menu contained a good variety that fused local Cajun and German styles to please any palate.  Conclusion, the food and wait staff was very good and I would definitely recommend this restaurant.
Had the chicken for dinner and Creme brûlée for desert. Both were fantastic! Best meal I've had on this business trip.

Was in for breakfast today. The front and back of house should be a training ground for any restaurant that believes they are doing it right ( you probably are not )

I started off starting brunch three hours to early. The waitress and cooks said fuck it he wants pate let him eat pate. He doesn't like the crostini and bam they made me a lightly toasted crostini. The shrimp and grits all perfectly presented and delicious. My water always full and attention to experience well beyond expectations. If you don't stop in you made a bad choices with your time and money.
Good food, and experience especially if you consider yourself a foodie, or enjoy a hip dining experience.

Luke was a great find in the Hilton hotel. We tried brunch and were very happy with the results. We ordered the Boudin Benedict and crispy chicken biscuit. The boudin Benedict was a huge portion and very tasty-the best part is you get to choose how much hollandaise sauce you want to pour. The crispy chicken biscuit was very tasty with a Tabasco honey and delicious grits.
Although it seemed like they knew what they were doing, all of their prices were outrageous.  He wanted to charge me several hundred dollars for a $30 thermostat.

Came here for happy hour for half off cocktails (delicious), $1.25 fried oysters (best I've ever had) and less than a dollar for raw oysters! You get the local P and J oysters for the happy hour oysters, which are quite unflavorful and full of oyster shell pieces from shucking. Can't really complain though because for less than a buck a shuck it's still a steal! 

I would have given perfect star review had it not been for the strand of hair embedded/cooked into our crawfish.... kind of ruined the moment of a superb meal. We couldn't even just pick it off because it was so cooked into the crawfish! Also, no one even came by to ask how our meal was or if we needed anything else, so we never got to show them the hair-wrapped crawfish.

First the Bad (what very little of it there was): The rice in the gumbo tasted like instant rice. Incredible gumbo with cheap rice. I would just assume not put rice in the gumbo. Also, my Sazerac was on the slightly tiny side.

Now, the good: I didn't order any foods I hadn't ever had before. I've had my fair share of head chees and Cochon de lait; I've had more links of smoked sausage in 25 years than one should in a lifetime; I've had cracklins a few times; and I've had enough Gumbo to float an aircraft carrier in.

I've never experienced the taste's I did that evening at luke. The familar items gave me tastes I've never had before in my life. It was dream like. Also, the house brew beer was more than noteworthy.

We tried this place for the first time. Raw oysters. Great. Stuffed oysters.  Great. Roasted chicken. Delicious.
The flammenkuchen  (alsacian specialty) was different from what we had in Alsace Lorraine,  but also delicious with Tennessee bacon! A southern twist to a specialty of France!] We enjoyed every bite and will return for more! Cocktails were also delicious... GINtilly lace.

We have dined at the San Antonio location several times previously and enjoyed the occasion. 

Walked in around 1.30pm on a Saturday - where the host desk ignored us before saying it was a 30 min wait. I don't mind waiting but it is concerning when the place is only 60% full. While we were a waiting 2 other couples walked in without reservations and we're seated promptly - the difference? We were casually dressed while the people they seated were more formal. A complaint to the Manager before we left - she couldn't care less - pretty much ignored us again - only saying "I understand". 

We left for Dragos on the Riverfront - where we were warmly welcomed and had a host and waitresses that understand the concept of customer service and not profiling beforehand. I am sure that the Staff at Dragos appreciated the large tip on a $90 lunch check. The Host desk at Luke feel that looking down on People is more important than their paycheck and those that fund it.

UPDATE - 11/23/2014 - 2 weeks later - neither this review - nor an email to the John Besh Restaurant Group has got any response. I know reading this review sounds like an embittered customer - that is what I would think, but I am more than willing to praise places that do a good job and care about their customers - just bear my experience when making your dining choice.

Raw oysters: Happy hour oysters are from 3-6pm. You MUST get their oysters. For 75 cents each, they were fresh, clean, tender, juicy, everything you can ask for in raw oysters. In a course of 2 days, my gf and I ordered 3 dozen of them. And that's on top of all the food we ate at other places. I really love the ambiance of the restaurant too. It's super classy and clean. 

Shrimp and grits: salty! The waitress recommended putting crab meat on it which was a nice touch. (It's $13 extra btw). I really enjoyed mine but my gf thought it was too salty. It would've been nice to complement the saltiness with some bread or something. Overall the flavor profile was there.

Pancakes: Decent pancakes. Not the best but wasn't terrible. Kinda pricey. ($9ish for like a stack of 5-6)

Louisiana rabbit and chicken liver pate: came with an array of dipping sauce. The sour/saltiness of the pickled dipping sauce went well with the pate. 

Mint julep: Got it for happy hour (1/2 off). Too much bourbon. Ratio was off. Too much ice. Wasn't a fan.

Tl;dr: Go for the happy hour oysters. 75 cents. So good.
One of our very best dining experiences ever!! Enjoyed the turducken and rib eye for thanksgiving dinner. Best bread pudding ever and the drinks were delicious! Go there now!!

Had crawfish bisque,  gumbo, chicken and biscuit,  and shrimp and grits. 

Ive never been a fan of bisque but theirs was very good. Their gumbo was just as delicious but a little too much okra. But thats where it ends. Chicken and biscuit with honey sauce was overly sweet and greasy. Shrimp and grits were salty. Looked great but failed on taste.

Really delicious seafoods. The first meal we took when we got here. Highly recommended. However, I am not really satisfied with the server. We waited for a lot time until he finally appeared. And the server was not around the table ALL THE TIME. Foods are super good.

Ate Xmas dinner at Luke with my wife. We were made to sit at the bar though a good amount of tables were empty the whole time we were there. Horrible service at the bar. Both of our meals came out undercooked (burger and mussels).  

I've had a decent lunch there in the past, but won't be going back.

On New Year's morning, in NOLA's business district not too far away...
I enjoyed the very best breakfast of my life at Luke! 
 
Luke (named after Chef John Besh's son, although I kept thinking of Star Wars!) is an unpretentious brasserie with nostalgic décor such as copper ceilings, pulley and belt ceiling fans, newspaper racks, and rich woods. Although Julius and I had reservations, we decided to sit at the bar - right in front on the Saints game on TV (Who Dat?!) Julius ordered one of Luke's own beers, while I tried the mint julep.  I told our bartender that my goal was to have every drink invented in New Orleans, and he joked around with me, like, how could this tiny woman handle all that bourbon and gin?  Size matters not...judge me by my size, do you? ;)
 
I already knew what I was going to have for breakfast after I saw Luke's menu three months ago...Eggs in a Jar. It was LUSCIOUS - and I've never used that word to describe anything here on Yelp!  Lightly fried softshell crab, creamy, buttery grits, perfectly poached eggs, and this heavenly hollandaise sauce is what I'm talking about!!! My prior faves (red velvet pancakes in Vegas, and tocino & eggs in the Philippines) don't even come close.  Julius, who tries not to have pork, took a trip to the dark side and had the BLT.  Luke's version included a buster crab, along with a thick cut of bacon between two behemoth pieces of brioche - how Julius was able to get it all in his piehole is beyond me!
 
When we finished our amazing meals, we were ready to blow this thing and go home!  BUT, our bartender topped it all off by giving me a complimentary drink (I totally forgot what he called it, I was already tipsy from the mint julep :P) Awesome service AND out-of-this-world food?  May the force be with you, Luke!

Once you get past the dollar beers and crispy tots you find the true treasure at Jerzee's- the megatouch gaming system by the bar. Not only do they have great puzzles and quiz games they have a thrilling adult section. Wooooo weee me oh my what a selection they have going there. Jerzees come for the great food and atmosphere, stay for the countless hours of photohunks
The croque madame was amazing.  Great restaurant!
Wow, wow, wow. Accommodated me with a Foies Gras entree and everything everyone else ordered was delicious and perfect! Delicious place to dine!!!

I've tried Luke's on several different occasions and have been impressed each time. They keep a steady flow of traffic and the staff is very knowledgeable of the menu so I've tried a variety of different drinks and happy hour items and have been impressed each time. Only think I would say that would make this place even better would be to have more seats at the bar but that can be easily fixed by showing up early. Always found a seat pretty easily in the main area; never had to wait to long for my food to come out; the fried oysters are cooked to perfection and for only $1.25 each during happy hour that's a steal.

Outdoor seating is wonderful...don't sit by the slamming gate though unless u are hard of hearing or love the clang of metal.

Service with a smile per usual! I love my tatooed Chipotle Peeps! They are good Peeps!
Very good. Delicious shrimp and grits, nice cocktail menu. Everything we had was excellent. But I don't understand all the newspapers draped from the seat backs. Art, I suppose?

We had the shrimp and grits which were very good. The crab soup was delicious but it was the French toast dish as dessert that was over the top. You will not go wrong with the French toast dish!!!!!!!

Richie Rich took care of the eight of us like royalty. The food was superlative. You have to try Bufala Negra. OMG. Btw you can't go wrong with the Brussel sprouts, oysters fresh or fried, shrimp & grits and bread pudding. Love this place.

This was a really nice restaurant.  My daughter took me on May 9th for Mother's Day.
Our waitress was so nice.
The atmosphere was so classy.
The dishes were artfully created.  
I didn't realize it was a BYOB which is a plus !
It is in a strip shopping center so plenty of parking.
The sushi was excellent and artfully presented.
The fried ice cream was delicious!
I had the cooked Maki with 
 shrimp tempura / California / eel-avocado -
came with ginger salad and miso soup $25
The shrimp tempura was the BEST !

I liked this place very much.
Oysters - very fresh.
Shimp boiled in a little spicy water - very good.
Rabbit and chicken liver mousse - excellent, sweet (from the rabbit livers) slightly undersalted.
Flamenkuche - very good
Chou croutte. The saurkraut was too sweet and the sausage was just ok but the smoked and braised shank was unreal.
Shrimp etouffe - really whrimp and crab in cream sauce with garganelli.  Good.
Strawberry galette - strawberries were great butt he galette was under cooked a bit and doughy.  Needed a sugar sprikling on the outside.

Amazing service and a good wine list.

we came here 3 times in less than 20 hours. once for dessert, then breakfast, and finally happy hour/late lunch.

happy hour = 50 cent gulf oysters!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! =D

breakfast = HAVE TO GET THE EGGS IN A JAR!! the pain perdu was meh......i wish i got something else.

dessert = everything. yum. get it. we shared: Brendan's bread pudding, gâteau basque, steamed chocolate, and dark chocolate bavarois


WE LOVED THE SERVERS!! they're all super friendly and nice.

My goodness what an absolutely terrible experience! 

We came to New Orleans for New Years with a bunch of my well-traveled, well-brunched friends. We picked Luke because of the great reviews for brunch. We got a reservation at 10:45AM for 8 people.

We were seated in the back room by the kitchen, kind of in a long booth n the corner. Our server was not warm or welcoming. She took our initial drink order - one bloody Mary and a bottle of champagne for the table with a glass of orange juice (as they did not have any specials for mimosas, apparently). 25 minutes later... only the bloody Mary had arrived. 35 minutes into our visit, a man shows up to the table with one glass of champagne. Ugh.

We eventually got the champagne debacle sorted out and began enjoying our brunch drinks 45 minutes after we arrived. We ordered food - the lobster bisque is fantastic. I ordered the croquet madame. The presentation is awe-inspiring, but the taste and overall "eatablity" of the dish is not great. The cheese on top is overwhelming and makes the whole sandwich very soggy. i wish I had ordered something else.

The brussel sprouts were very good.

By the end of the meal, we had only seen our waitress maybe one additional time to order a second bottle of champagne. We even tried asking other servers and a manager for assistance or to find out where she was. 

The waitress struggled for an additional 30 minutes after we wanted to check out to split the check into 4 couples. Our checks were all incorrect. As a group, we decided to just pay and then settle up later due to the amount of time it was taking to get through this meal. After putting our credit cards in the payment slots, it was still another 10 minutes for her to pick them up, and an additional 10 to get her to run them. The whole meal took about 2.5 hours - was kind of expensive, and we had absolutely terrible service. I won't be suggesting this place to anyone traveling to Nola!

This place is a must when in nola! Our server, kristeffer, was on point! Had great timing & tempo with our food, made great recommendations, & was very friendly. The small fruit de mers was enough for 4 people but oh so addicting. Shrimp was spicy but we love spicy. Brussel sprouts with Marcona almonds was delish as well. Hands down, best entree, shrimp & grits! You won't regret it!

Having a yen for some German style food, we stopped here last Saturday for lunch,and I'm sure glad we did.  The Gumbo and Crab Bisque were top notch, but the Fried Oyster Bacon and Avocado Salad was truly blessed, and the "Jagerschnitzel mit Spatzle" (the Saturday special) was out of class; that wonderful local bacon in both of the latter dishes, and the best Spatzle I've ever had; helped me forget that Berghoff's in Chicago has closed.  If this is any example of John Besh's work, I've got to get to Restaurant August next time I'm in town.  

Aside from being open on Sunday, this place has extended hours for lunch, which, for us, was very helpful.

NOLA has more local boosters than any city I've ever been to; we were seated next to two of them enjoying the Burger and the Pressed Sandwhich,  and advising us about the local products, including bacon, utilized by Chef Besh.   Good company and good service too.

Lüke made my honeymoon amazing!
We both love the food sooooo much!
The service is much more than excellent! 
They offered us champagne and dessert for free. And their bread pudding is amazing! Must try it!
We went for their happy hour oysters, they are good for its price.
Overall, we love lÜke! It's service is unlike those "French Quarter" service, which means servers are busy and they got no time to even check on you. Lüke's servers provide really personal service!
Love love it! Will be back for sure!

I swear every time that I've come
here my palette has always left extremely happy and tummy full. the mister and I have been having some trouble amidst our paradise so a nice stroll downtown in the CBD to a late brunch was extremely needed. 

the lovely hostess was very accommodating allowing us to sit in the corner away from a more crowded area, I don't like sitting that close to people ... esp when I'm that hungry.
the service was great as well. 
in lieu of happy hour we got the half cocktails. I ordered the French 75 which was a nice frothy cocktail and the mister the champagne cocktail with the rosemary and peach vodka I think? we both agreed the French 75 was the better choice all thanks to server's suggestion. 

for starters we ordered a dozen raw oysters bc it was happy hour, .75 cents an oyster, fried oysters 1.75 for one to start off with. the fried oysters? phenomenal. raw oysters were a nice size too. 

for entrees I had the assortment de charcuterie which came with an assortment of hog's head cheese, rabbit and chicken liver pâté, pickled melon pieces and more! it was all too delicious! I think the board became a massacre almost bc we did a killing on it. 

the mister ordered the grilled ribeye. which was cooked to perfection! had customers breaking their necks like "oh.. my.. God. Becky, look... at.. her.. steak" and I'm
just like "yeeea.. I know -cuts off piece and plops in mouth-. 
we just couldn't finish all of charcuterie and the ribeye though so we "doggy-bagged" it. LOL

I'll say though ... I've never once left this place unhappy. from the service to the food....  well executed. I prefer Sundays to come here... no parking meters, no school or work to rush off to afterwards,.... and if Mother Nature allows it the good weather when you stroll through the CBD to get to and fro here. it was def the best Sunday brunch I've had in a good while.

5 stars for service.  The servers were friendly, attentive and knowledgeable regarding the menu.  4 stars for the food.  We started with a dozen oysters, which were some of the best we had!  The gumbo was fantastic! My husband and I shared the beet salad.  He enjoyed it but I found it a little too sweet.  I wanted to try a boudin, which is a sausage mixed with rice.  I don't know if it's typical of a boudin, but it was very soft and mushy - almost pasty. The pickled cabbage was also too sweet.  My husband tasted it and agreed.  My husband had the schnitzel and spaetzle and thought it was very tasty.  Overall though, it was a great experience.  The food was generally very good and the prices were reasonable.  I love the casual atmosphere and great service!

I went to Lüke for twice in my trip to New Orleans. The food was good and the restaurant was comfortable. I had a seafood platter with crab for dinner. The crab and oysters were great. The clams and mussels were fine but just too small. I went back to the restaurant to enjoy happy hours for oysters. I though they would give us smaller oysters as they charged much less but it surprised me that they gave us the same oysters! It's such good deal that each oyster was less than $1. Our server was great. I was glad that she was serving us also the next day.

The only reason that I took one star out was because the receptionists. When I asked for a table the first night, the lady did not say Hi and not even looking at me. I thought she was busy so I waited but actually she heard me. I was pretty pissed and thought the service of the restaurant would be very bad (which turned out not the case). When we returned the next day, there was one more lady (got a faint smile at least) but they kept us waiting for no reason. There were plenty of table available and set but we were asked to wait for 10-15 minutes. We waited as we thought they needed to allocate the tables even so we got to wait for those being tidied up. At the end, we were led to a table that was ready since we were there. It's not about the 10 minutes but the attitude. I didn't think they cared if I walked out of the restaurant. 

Anyways, don't walk out of the restaurant because the receptionist is bad. It's a good restaurant at very reasonable price.
Awesome, awesome, awesome! Fantastic consistent food with a pleasant atmosphere and incredibly gracious staff. If you like hamburgers try their's. I will be back and continue to recommend Luke's.

Delicious bewilderment.  That's the best way to describe this experience.  I didn't know food could taste this could or make me so giddy.  My friends and I would like to give a special shout-out to Cochon Restaurant for being closed on Sundays-- we never would have discovered Luke otherwise.  

The 5 of us ordered up a total feast.  And everything was not only delicious, but otherworldly.  The meal hands down blew anything I've ever eaten out of the water, and I've been to some 3 star michelin restaurants.  

APPETIZERS: We started out with a dozen gulf shrimp and a dozen clams on the half shell.  I was a bit confused why the restaurant refused to serve the clams raw, but cooking, then chilling certainly worked (though personally, I still prefer raw).  The shrimp were AMAZING.  Huge prawns, seasoned like crawfish, firm meat (very fresh).  The platter came with cocktail sauce and remoulade.  The remoulade was superb.  Never had better.  Next, we had Louisiana rabbit and duck liver pate with a variety of sauces (honey mustard, fennel relish, pickled watermelon rinds, sweet peppers).  Creamy, rich, and yet still light.  The portion was a lot larger than I expected.  They could definitely have served half as much at 3/4 the price, and I would actually have been happier.  We also got seafood gumbo and shrimp bisque.  The shrimp bisque was perfect, but for me the seafood gumbo was the only miss of the meal.  There was nothing bad about it, but it was very forgettable in an otherwise unforgettable meal.  Finally, we had flamenkuche (basically, caramelized onions, bacon, and cheese on a flatbread).  Together, the ingredients don't sound all that extraordinary, but the way Chef Besh marries the flavor... total delight.  We were ooing and ahhing through that whole dish.  Either Besh sources grrrrreat bacon, or he has the world's best smoker.  We were literally sucking on the bacon.  

ENTREES: We had fried mangalitsa pork, cochon de lait sandwich, crab omelet, and the Luke burger.  Outside of the mangalitsa pork fried crispier than I thought possible; inside, the pork was juicy and tender.  The cochon de lait was the best I've ever had (and it was paired magnificently with a cured ham).  Initially, I was worried about the ham overpowering the cochon, but Besh calmed all fears.  This sauce came with the sandwich and it was also mouthwatering.  The crab omelet was perhaps the most delicate item we ordered.  You could taste the technique in the preparation.  The Luke burger was about as good a burger as you can get.  The bun just CRACKLED every time you bit into it... yet maintained a nice clean texture... not an abrasive one that super-toasted bread can have.  

I am in utter shock at how good this restaurant is.  AMAZED.  Chef Besh, please open a restaurant in the Northeast.  PLEASE.

+ food was delicious (when we finally got it!) and good drinks and beer. Prices are great during happy hour. 

- however, the service was pretty bad. orders were forgotten and took more than an hour to get an order of fries (which I had to send back b/c they weren't fried enough!). Good thing they gave us our drinks before they forgot so at least we had something to keep ourselves occupied.

They gave me food poisoning two days ago. I went there June 30th, 2016 for lunch. This woman ahead of me ordered up all remaining chicken. Apparently the cook didn't care to make sure the chicken was fully cooked so orders  could be completed. I ate less than a third of my burrito. Barely made it back to the public bathroom at work before it all came back up. I was sick for the next two days. But I don't have a job that I can just call of for. WHAT KIND OF IDIOTS DO THEY HAVE COOKING THE CHICKEN??!!!  You can't sell raw chicken to consumers just because you have run out! After that I picked through my burrito, I saw the chicken wasn't fully cooked!!!

Came here for a Sunday brunch.  Food was really good, but a little on the pricey side.

We ordered the eggs in a jar which was really good, but very creamy and a bit heavy.  The dish was served with jalapeño grits which were awesome!

We also ordered a sandwich "madnam" maybe?  Can't remember the exact spelling, but it was served with an egg on top and was also good.

Last entree was the shrimp and grits which was very good as well.

Kids ordered the hamburger and chicken strips.  Hamburger seemed to get the thumbs up, chicken strips were just ok.

Dessert- we had steamed chocolate which the chocolate by itself didn't do a whole lot for me, but the ice cream combined was fantastic!

Wife ordered the gateau basque which she said was also really good.

The flamenkuche which was our appetizer and had incredible tasting bacon.

Gave this place 4 stars due to our lunch bill adding up to $159.00 (before tip).  Which we did have a couple of bloody marry's, but still a bit much for a lunch.

Got to eat at Luke twice recently, once late (10pm-ish) and once for lunch.  I'd give them a star just for the daring of running an Alsatian (i.e., not Parisian) bistro in New Orleans, which has, I think, nothing else like this.  Alsatian food is great, but badly underappreciated in the US.  John Besh, I salute you.

Like Lilette, you get a real bistro feel here.  The decor is perfect.  We came in late one night for what amounted to a second dinner and liked it so much, we came back for lunch 2 days later.

The dishes:

Salad of chicory, lardons of Allen Benton's bacon croutons and soft poached yard egg with creole mustard and tarragon.  Delicious - not too heavy, but the bacon gives it a great nuance. 

Fries - these need a separate mention.  They're absolutely perfect - crunchy with a strong potato flavor.  Superb!

Moules et frites - the Belgians should be worried about their dominance with this dish, as Luke's is terrific.  Nice traditional broth with chives and just a little bit of cream.  Slurpable!

Shrimp farci with blood orange hollandaise, crabmeat and shrimp - I wasn't sure what this was (should've asked about the meaning of 'farci'), but took a small gamble.  They chop up the shrimp and crabmeat, then bread it and fry it.  That hollandaise really makes this dish - it's lovely.

I thought about giving Luke 4 stars, but that would be ungenerous - it's great.

We're from New York. Not to sound like snobs but we know great food. This restaurant is on point! From the warm bread and sweet butter upon being seated at your table to the friendly staff, Luke has an awesome thing going here. We had the shared plate of brussel sprouts that is to die for! The sauce is sweet and spicy along with the sliced apples to cut the heat. This shared plate is like a meal! It is truly for 2. We also had the croque monsieur with a fried egg on top. The bread was fluffy in the middle and crispy on the outside. The fries were definitely hand cut and super crispy. We also had the jumbo Louisiana shrimp en cocotte with  grits which was to die for! It's super rich but totally worth the food coma after. Word to the wise don't order both the soft boiled eggs and crawfish on top of the cocotte unless 3 of you are sharing it haha. 
We were so happy we chose this restaurant for our first New Orleans experience.
We just had a delicious lunch here! Great prices, and very good food. It is right across the street from our hotel. I love that it's quiet, and the experience is fabulous!

Visited at Happy Hour on my quest to run into John Besh. They do 50 cent oysters from 5-7. They were amazing. Rest of the menu looks pretty southern. Service was attentive and the atmosphere was nice. I'd go back for dinner.

I've worked at different sushi restaurants in the area so I am a bit picky when it comes to my sushi. I always see Hachi when I come to my local wine and spirits and the interior looked beautiful but I never really wanted to give it a try. 
Finally, I give it a shot last week for lunch. 
Whenever I go to eat sushi for lunch I almost always order a chirashi, which is simply chefs choice of sashimi on top of the chefs version of sushi rice. 
When I first saw the bowl, it was beautiful. And oh boy was it good. The one missing star is for the mackeral (I think it was mackerel ?) I am not sure. I never asked. I assume by the taste it must be mackeral. Mackerel  usually has a very fishy taste, but this one seemed a bit over the edge.  Nevertheless I destroyed all of it, except mackerel and my girlfriend ordered the salmon spicy bowl, which is essentially like the spicy salmon inside a maki on top of a bed of rice. 
She liked it a lot. I enjoyed the maki too. Yeah I eat alot.

Had a great meal here. The warm bittersweet plantation goat cheese salad was amazing. The crabmeat ravioli with galic, cream, lemon, and herbs was delicious. We ordered a few desserts to share and while the flavor was good, they were all too sweet for me. However, this does not deter me from recommending this place because everything else was excellent. Would love to dine at other John Besh restaurants.

Good food.  Ordered the veggie Lo Mein, Szechwan beef and General Taos chicken. Tasty. Not oily at all.  Fresh and not overly seasoned.  

I will go back.   Nice to see good Chinese food in Lutz.
I personally liked this restaurant in Nola. The steak was SO good. But don't get the crab - it's not worth the price, the just put a thin layer on it.
The place sells nothing but quality stuff and the customer service is the best you can get in the retail industry.  Store in neat and clean and always has great sales.  Great winter clothing store.
Quick friendly staff, floors, tables, and trash receptacles quite dirty. Store would be great if it was kept cleaner.

I have added a star to the review for the restaurant reaching out to ask about my experience.  Any restaurant that is looking to improve its customer experience deserves a second look - the next time I am in New Orleans I will do so.

Loved this place. We found it on Yelp. The food and service was excellent. I felt like I was a local not a tourist.  We ordered Washington Parish Roasted Chicken and I didn't want to share the Luke burger for my younger daughter ( she didn't want to share either) The next time we are in New Orleans we will be back to Brunch and Lunch and maybe even happy hour.
I'm too cheap to eat here normally, but their happy hour rocks my world! 1/2 price oysters and drinks every day from 3-6pm. I go in for a dozen raw and a fresh lemonade. Yummmmmm.

I ordered the ribeye and it wasn't anything too exciting. Don't get me wrong, it was good but definitely something I could've cooked at home minus the $34. My waitress was also very pushy and seemed to be in such a rush to get my mom and I out of the restaurant. One time stop only
Delicious food, nice atmosphere! BYOB. We thoroughly enjoyed our night out. They sat us right away at a table, but had a sushi bar there too where people could sit. The service was great too

Breakfast. The breakfast sandwich is actually a breakfast burger. The shrimp and grits is creamy, well seasoned and delicious. Come hungry if you choose to spend some dough on your first meal of the day.

Great food and amazing service. 

We made a quick reservation a few hours before the Bacchus parade and they lived up to their reputation even during the mass chaos of Mardi Gras. 

Once we got there Elliott was top notch with his flair, pride, and panache in his service. Wine, lobster, and their shrimp and grits were all amazing. 

Sadly we had to leave in a rush once we realize the Bacchus parade was only four blocks south of us and we needed to get on the other side of the street prior to its arrival. Elliot and his team member packaged everything up and made sure we were out the door before the parade could travel another block. 

I look forward to coming back on my next trip to New Orleans.

My boyfriend and I stayed at the Hilton Homewood Suites which is pretty much right down the street from this restaurant. We went there for breakfast and it was delicious! I had the egg white frittata which was mouthwatering. Topped with pesto, arugula, tomatoes and avocado. My boyfriend has the Pain Perdu which was to die for! Challah break smothered with mascarpone and topped with smokey bacon. We went back the next morning to get more!

Had lunch here on December 13 with my very picky parents!  Everyone loved it!  Outstanding baked oysters with herbsaint, lobster bisque, and caramelized onion and pork belly flatbread.  Shrimp and grits, one of the best in the city, pork sandwich and croque Monsieur were yummy.  Great wine by the glass and dining in front of the kitchen was delightful.  We love Luke!  Living in the quarter makes it tough when it comes to dining in other neighborhoods.  We love to walk to the numerous great eats around us but Luke is worth the "effort" to grab a cab and go across town.

Happy hour OYSTERS are amazing here. The quality of oysters is superb, juicy and plump. Unlike most other places, you do not have to order a drink to get the .75 cent oysters. But they don't have chargrilled oysters. Go to LUKE's and skip the lines at the French Quarter spots. 

I tried the gnocchi appetizer and it was delicious. It was topped with sautéed greens, browned pork and a delightful crumble. I also recommend the bread pudding dessert! I don't usually order bread pudding but I really enjoyed this one at Luke's. 
Although the raw oysters were perfect, the fried oysters were not that big. So just come here for the raw oysters during happy hour, and try out their menu! Everything on the menu looked great but we came for the oysters (2 nights in a row)!  

Located in the central business district and less than 10 minute walk from Bourbon St, this is fine dining without the fuss. The service is attentive and friendly. They have bar seating and even large tables to accommodate 10+ people. The atmosphere is pretty relaxed. 

You don't have to dress up to go here, and we only had to wait 15 min ish for dinner on Friday night. The restaurant is next to the Hilton hotel if you can't find the place.

The staff was able to accommodate us as we arrived into Nola pretty early. We came around noon and was able to be seated right away. 
Our waiter was attentive, kind, and educated us on the menu.
We started with the Brussel sprouts. Delicious!!! 
I had the fried oyster salad. A great balance of freshness and not to over powering with the oysters. Fried to perfection. Crispy!
Husband had the Luke Burger and he enjoyed it.  We will definitely be returning!

Very limited menu here at Luke restaurant. The portion size is huge, the service is so so, the drink selection is below average the ambiance was average but the food is pretty good. Definitely not the best place but certainly not the worst either. We had the chicken, duck and schnitzel.

Happy Hour is a must here! The bar scene is lively and the oysters are 50 cents from 3-6 Mon-Friday. The one downside was that all the cocktails with syrup were laden with it, so much so that they had a cough syrup dreariness, especially the riverbend. Other than the that, the other cocktails were great and the oysters were delicious. Make a reservation for the tables in the area is you're getting there around 5ish.
Shrimp & grits is highly recommended! The atmosphere and service are really good. My boyfriend and I had a nice time here
I have to agree the chicken and rabbit pate was outstanding!   Though the pickled watermelon tasted like a jolly rancher!

Elm Cafe is really close to where I live and my wife and I have been anxiously anticipating the opening. The owner and operator Nathan Box ( @nathanbox on Twitter ) is a friendly guy and always seems up for a chat with customers.

Beans are from 49th Parallel @49thparallel in Vancouver - according to my wife, the espresso is fantastic. I usually go for the brewed coffee and the two I've tried - the BURUNDI KIBINGO and the COLOMBIA FINCA LAS BRISAS are both very tasty. Staff are being trained by Sammy Piccolo  (@SammyPiccolo), one of the top baristas in Canada.

The fresh muffins every morning are from Duchess Bakery on 124th. We also recently tried one of the breakfast sandwiches and it definitely did not disappoint. 

Local, high quality ingredients and great service. It's going to cost you a bit more than McDonald's or Timmie's but the quality is definitely worth it.

We enjoyed our meal at Luke.  Best Brussel sprouts I have ever had!  I would go back just for these.  The shrimp and grits were good,  but I would recommend trying something different because they were very traditional.
Came here during happy hour! Definitely got a great deal on the oysters! Left very pleased!

I came here for happy hour with my husband and friends. Our friends ordered several dozen oysters (delicious) but I had my eye on the "Shrimp & Crawfish étouffée on top cavatelli". LIFE CHANGING. The entire table could not stop eating it. 

Also ordered: the fried oysters- delicious but pretty chewy, and the Brussels- YUM.

Do yourself a favor and order the étouffée w/ a nice glass of pinot noir.

Ok I've been meaning to write a review for this place for ages and just haven't gotten to it. Ate there again last night and boy it never disappoints. I love the food and the vibe! Our waiter was great and my friend and I had a fabulous night. Thanks again Luke for a wonderful evening!!

I'm currently sitting in a blazing hot dining room experiencing my second bad experience at a Besh Restaurant Group this week and we haven't even ordered.  I've been told "no" to very simple requests since I walked in that would accommodate my family better.  Not "we can try" just flat out "no."  We should have gone to Cochon. - Continuation after the meal...this really was a disappointment!  Lüke has been a favorite of ours for years, but the extreme lack of quality in attention to detail in the dining room and plating, the reduction in the Franco-Alsatian menu items, the so-so products used, and much more marks a new low for my former favorite brassiere.  We won't be back and to be perfectly honest we most likely won't dine at another John Besh restaurant.  Maybe this celebrity chef is spread too thin to check-in on his restaurants.  A sad day for this fan and frequent diner.

Stopped at Luke for brunch last Saturday. The restaurant is very well run, service was excellent, decor was great and the food was fantastic. Most of us went for the shrimp and grits which we all agreed it was the best dish of the week. The little gem salad was excellent as well. Highly recommended when you're hungry for some great southern food.

Excellent from the beginning to finish, every bite. 
We were there at 4:30 and the timing could not be better. They oysters are at happy hour pricing ($0.75 per) and you can eat to your hearts content. Crab bisque is super buttery and the depth of flavor is incredible. We also got blackened jumbo shrimp, yummmmm it makes me drool just thinking about it. Shrimp creole was our main dish, and we also got bread pudding for dessert. Everything, including the warm fluffy bread, was excellent by foodie standards. Highly recommended.

This is a go-to spot for my boyfriend and I.  You really can't go wrong with 50 cent oyster happy hour, and the oysters are huge!  We go to happy hour for oysters and drinks at least once a month, and the service is always excellent.  Drinks are strong (and half off during happy hour) and delicious.  We ate appetizers once - I believe we ordered the bacon avocado salad and the crab bisque - both were amazing, and we'll be sure to go back for dinner sometime soon.  We've gotten lucky with walking in on Friday nights, but calling for reservations would be the smartest thing to do as this place gets crowded for happy hour.

Went to eat from the bar but service was non existent. There was a tender and oyster chucker guy but after getting a glass of wine they were not to be found.  I hung on another 20 min without service and went elsewhere.  They really need better service.

But ... Since im staying at the hilton and its a hundred degrees out I came back a few days later.  Had some coffee and vanilla cake.  Cake was five stars.  But "fresh" blueberries were still thawing out.  Service at the bar was a bit better but still slow.

The happy hour 25 cent oysters, were full price today due to the oil spill. Nonetheless, they were fat, milky and delicious. Definately worth full price. Rabbit and duck pate was served with pickled watermelon rind-- weird and licorice-y, but it grew on me. I didn't need much to compliment the pate anyway-- just a buttery crostini. This was my third time here. The oyster shucker was quite friendly and helpful, but the bartender was not as attentive and quick as he could be especially with only eight people at his bar. Maybe its because he had to make drinks for the servers as well. It's a  kink that could be easily worked out. Despite the slow service, the quality of the ingredients definitely picks up the slack. Hopefully the 25 cent oysters will be back in full effect soon. God willing.

Came here for lunch during the weekday and it took about 15 minutes to get seated, but not a big deal cause we weren't in any rush. Ordered the fried oyster and bacon salad and it was absolutely delicious! Oysters fried to perfection and seriously the best bacon I have ever tasted; so flavorful and juicy! They were also kind enough to split the salad without me even asking since I was sharing with someone else. Also had the burger and it was also pretty good, big portions so I had leftovers for later. Would definitely come back to try breakfast or dinner though and probably make a reservation too so next time we don't have to wait. Overall pretty good!

Came here for the TG day buffett whic was great.  i alsotried the shrip and grits which was good.  The Marine Corps stuff on the walls was neat to see.  A bit overpriced though copared to comparable food elsewhere in the quarter.
We enjoyed this place! They have a great happy hour. The fried oysters were the best we had in NOLA.

I place a lot of value on written reviews. I read some very good comments on the Alligator role. It didn't live up to those comments. It was good but not four or five stars. The same my wife and I found true of a couple of dishes. Maybe an off night.

Luke's is my favorite hangout spot in New Orleans. The bartenders - Brandi and Brian - are two of my favorites in New Orleans. Manager Steve Beasley is my favorite. 

I highly recommend Luke's for Breakfast, Lunch and, most especially, happy hour.
Good service local ingredients some must try items fried chicken and waffles and the crab meat and asparagus omelet.

Two words - Crawfish Bisque.

My friends and I were in town this weekend for Wrestlmania XXX and couldn't wait to enjoy the authentic cuisine. One of my friends said we had to try this place as he'd eaten there before we landed. Once we ate here, it was a wrap. We kept thinking about the soup even after we left! We went here twice.

Cheyenne was great! She was friendly and attentive. The manager thanked us for returning by providing a delicious complimentary appetizer. There wasn't one thing on the menu that didn't look delicious. The next time I'm in New Orleans, I definitely plan on returning.

Fantastic! We were lucky to get a table at 7:30 without a reservation and had a fabulous time. Our waiter Kevin was great and made several suggestions that were absolutely spot-on: Brussels sprout appetizer (never liked them before but now I'm a huge fan!), crawfish etoufee, shrimp & grits, and the Luke burger. All 4 of us loved our food -- everybody was raving about how good it was.
I highly recommend this restaurant if you're looking for some memorable New Orleans cuisine! One note: I think $$$ is more accurate than the $$ price rating it has, but worth every penny!!!

The best dinner we had in New Orleans, and we ate at quite a few places. The food is amazing. Attentive service too. The only knock was a not so good wine recommendation, but other than that, awesome!

The crawfish étouffée was pretty good, even though the rice was crispy, which was different but good! The shrimp and grits were good. Nothing I just HAVE to come back for. The stuffed oysters were amazing but crazy expensive. Overall the food was just okay and way overpriced. The food itself only gets three stars... but Kayla, and her excellent customer service, got them a four.

I was really looking forward to trying Hachi last night and was un-impressed.

The night did not start off well, we had reservations for 730, when we entered and told the hostess she looked confused then asked if we would mind sitting at the sushi bar!!  To preface this, my wife and I have two small kids and maybe go out ourselves every 2-3 months, sushi bar was not ok, and it's not like they lost our reservation, i could see our names on the list.

They got that all figured out and we sat for dinner.  For appetizer we had the sakuro steak, great presentation, but steak was too tough to eat with chop sticks, shoudl be cut smaller or use different cut of meat thats more tender.  Long hot on top was good.  We also had the sashimi salad, just ok and fish was not great.

For main course we split a bunch of sushi, overall was just ok, we have other places in the area that is much better.  Had no 7 volcano, good spice but again fish was not great, also has big island which was overspiced and fatty salmon sushi - which was tough and not ok flavor.

I hate giving bad reviews, especially for local places, but we had high expectations and they were not met.  the ambiance was nice and place has potential, but they need to step up their game.  unfortunately we don't go out much and probably will not give them another try.

One of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans is this little gem by one of New Orleans own Chef Luke. This upscale restaurant is nice enough to be classified as fine dining without being stuffy. When you walk in you're greeted by a long lit bar with feeding on the side for drinks and appetizers. In the back area the room opens up with seating all around the open Kitchen in the center. The place itself is gorgeous. 

The menu has so many different options from Chef Luke that it was truly hard to pick. The wait staff was extremely helpful and attentive. They started off good old classic Sazerac. The drinks are Madewell here, strong drinks at a decent price point, comparable to New York or any City restaurant. Also started with the oyster platter, one of their specialties, and they were served on ice. Delicious and fresh who's excited for our main course. I ordered the steak with fries and my husband got the Luke Burger. Wanting to try everything we split our dishes and we're happy with both. The steak was tender and well seasoned and the fries came out in a little cone and were crisped to perfection with just the right amount of salt. The Luke Burger, also tender and juicy, was amazing. We thoroughly enjoyed everything here. I would come back in an instant if I could.

Not worth the hype. The prices are higher than other places and the food is ok had better. Nice ambiance however the service was poor. The servers seem to have a bit of an attitude and not fully understand the meaning of good customer service.

We were here for Luke's happy hour for oysters and beer, but also to check out one of Chef John Besh's many New Orleans Restaurants, who we were told we just missed by minutes! No worries, I had the pleasure of meeting a few years ago at a seafood festival, but it would have been nice! We sat at the oyster shucking station, and was totally entertained by 'shuckin Shawn' who had a vibrant friendly and happy personality, along with Johnny in the same area, and Savannah, our server, always smiling. The oysters were wonderful, and served beautifully, on white napkins, on ice, and in addition to cocktail sauce and the sinus clearing horseradish, a red wine vinegar concoction that was terrific. We also got a taste of the 'Bama Beauty' oysters, which were smaller, but nice and briny. Luke's label beer on draft was great. You will not be disappointed!

Shrimp and grits was spectacular! I couldn't stop eating. Oyster happy hour was definitely worth it as well! Boyfriend and I killed 2 dozen easily! We would've ate more but had to make room for the many other delicious cuisines in NOLA! Their cocktails were also awesome! Mint juleps = just the right touch

My wife and I went there for brunch. The Service was very good. French press coffee was great and just what we needed. I had the chicken and waffles which were phenomenal. My wife had the crabmeat mozzarella omelet which she said was good as well. I had a side of andouille sausage which was the best I've ever had but didn't need it as my dish was a generous portion.

I was at the bar!!! The service was great & the drinks were creative & feisty... The oysters were yummie!!! It was located in the hotel I stayed in & that was perfect... I got the bread pudding to go....

It was the BOMB ;-)

During happy hour, this place gets 4 stars.  With $0.50 oysters there really is nothing to complain about.  I have also eaten here twice during non happy hour (once for lunch and once for dinner).  I got the burger one time and the croque madame the other time.  The burger was pretty tasty.  The croque madame was good as well, but both seem overpriced for what they were. The meals come with small condiments which were a nice touch.

Yes, I know there are plenty of mom-and-pop pizza shops in Brownsburg and yes, I know their pizza is much better than Domino's, but when it's a weeknight and I just want something quick and cheap and there's an email with a 50% off coupon tempting me from my inbox (Whaaat? A large 3-topping for $8?!)... Well, sometimes I'm weak. 

I like Domino's better than any of the other big pizza chains, and their recipe retooling a few years back certainly paid off. I don't expect it to be gourmet, I just expect it to be pizza. 

I'm never there long enough to interact much with the staff but they've always been quick and polite.
Fantastic gumbo and fresh gulf oysters.  Oh and the Sazerac's were really great too!  I will definitely go back!
Definitely worth every star! You should try: crab/corn chowder, duck 2-ways, and the bread pudding. If you want more the French fries were pretty tasty too!

Stopped by for lunch. The ambiance is nice and the staff is very friendly. Prices are mid to mi-hugh, but hehe food was delicious. We had a burger and the friends chicken lunch special which came with crab bisque, which was creamy with big chunks of crab. The menu is not too huge so picking great lunch or dinner for old is not complicated.

The back section of Lüke is devoid of the charm that makes the front of the restauant such a delight to eat in. The air conditioning was uncomfortably cold because the neighboring hotel had the controls. (I wish I had brought a sweater.) The single serving coffee press might be cute, but the waiter couldn't keep enough full coffee carafes on our table. Also, because the air conditioning was so cold, the coffee cups were equally cold and as soon as the coffee was poured into them the coffee went from hot to lukewarm. (It is only with the greatest restraint that I kept myself from using a wonderfully awful pun by adding an umlaut to lukewarm.) The hostess, the waiter and I had some kind of miscommunication which ended up messing up one order. That's a laundry list of complaints right? You'd think that's deserve a two or maybe three star review. Well that's not the case for Lüke, because they still make the best Shrimp and Grits I've had in my life, and I've had a lot of shrimp and grits.

2.5 stars
This place is clearly over rated.

First, you wait. Tables are empty but you need to wait to be seated. so you wait 10 minutes and then you are sent in a remote location (last table of the most remote room). ok. Why not? ...as long as the food is good.

So I went to Luke for happy hours and oyster specials yes BUT.. Oysters had definitely been frozen (and No. I do know about oysters: I am from Normandy, France, and lived 5 years in Arcachon as well, the homeland of oysters, so trust me, I know when an oyster has been frozen. You can try this at home: simply put lemon on the oyster: if it moves (it retracts naturally with the lemon acidity)  it means it's alive, if it doesn't move well...good luck.)
So, oyster were dry on top, previously frozen. 75 cents/per oyster: you get what you pay for.

beer? very nice at 3.5$ during happy hours (7$ otherwise).
5$ fries? why not. but don't expect anything special.
Honey brussel sprout: interesting, but so much honey that I couldn't eat them. I don't eat sweet. Honey seasoning should be more subtle and less sweet (maybe a vinegar reduction with a bit of honey?). You can perfume a dish with honey not literally dip your Brussels sprout in it!

Place itself is classy, clean, nice service.

Might update my review if I try more of their menu. 2.5 stars for happy hours deal.

Best meal in NOLA! !
First the service was spectacular starting with the hostess when we called to get the only remaining reservation on 12/26. 
The Happy Hour Specials are the best in the City. 
We started with fresh oysters, fried oysters and build shrimp with several rounds of drinks 

The seafood was soooooo fresh! 

Back to the service two words:
KYLE & KENNY!  
They were so cute and friendly,  they gave us just enough attention and made fantastic recommendations.

Tip: get a table in the back to watch the kitchen!  

On the rest of the meal... we has the crab bisque which was fantastic.  The bread was fresh with a really great butter.

The shrimp and grits were out of this world!  
The Roasted Veggies Were Amazing#
The wild boar ragout was the the best pasta dish I have ever tasted.

Luke is my new favorite restaurant of all time. 
 Tip: make a reservation and go now!!!

After all my rave reviews of LUKE I finally had a subpar meal. On a previous Sunday I was here with a friend who ordered the house special veal dish. He was raving about how good it was so I decided to order it myself. I really was disappointed this time as the veal was overcooked and stringy. The gravy did not have the flavor that my friend had previously either. I was very disappointed by this dish.

We also had the happy hour oysters and cocktails which were great. I guess no place can be great everyday.

John Besh, I love you. Your rabbit and chicken liver pate is heaven on earth. The gumbo is one of the best I've had in NOLA, and mussels are pretty good too. I wish that I didn't have to wait 30 minutes for my table, even though I had a reservation.  It's casual and worth the price of the menu food items. It's a great way to sample Besh's cooking without the heavy price tag of August. Luke, I'll be back!

Luke was my first visit to a John Besh restaurant (though I have had the opportunity to partake in Alsatian food in Alsace).  As a guest of the Hilton, I was excited to have an attached restaurant that raised expectations beyond the traditional hotel faire.  Ultimately, my expectations were not met.

The layout of the restaurant is poorly conceived - the dining area is bisected by a hotel hallway.  This is not a showstopper in terms of layout, however the positioning of the host stand at the front leaves guests that enter from the hotel side standing mid-dining room with no pointers to the host location.  Once the host stand was identified (through a query to a passing waiter), I was seated promptly the the hostess polite and courteous.

Within a very short time, my drink order was taken and I was offered bread that was relatively fresh.  My order was taken quickly, and my starter, the matzah ball soup, was delivered quickly.

The soup was well proportioned, not skimping on either the chicken or the matzah, and not falling into the over-salting trap that so many matzah ball soups fall into.  The vegetables included were fresh and appropriately cooked - neither mushy nor crisp - overall a good start.

Unfortunately, the positives (on the food) ended there.  I ordered the ENTRECÔTE GRILLÉE ET FRITES, better known as a ribeye and fries.  There were several choices of topping, but I went with the basic MAÎTRE D'HÔTEL BUTTER - a good ribeye should stand on its own.  The waitress asked if I would like them to bring ketchup for my fries - I appreciated the polite reference to fries to avoid embarrassing individuals who request it for their steak itself (I politely declined the ketchup).

The steak is where things went south.  The initial appearance was appealing, with the traditional crosshatch flame pattern on top and bottom, and I was looking forward to it until I cut into it.  The steak itself was one of the worst cooked steaks I have ever eaten - it was oversalted (which is difficult to do with steak), and had clearly been sitting out - the butter failed to melt even over the course of my dining.  More importantly, the steak looks like a sandwich from the profile view - two large white bands of well-done meat with a center that was barely rare (purple-red and cool).  I guess that they average out to Medium Rare when taken together.  With a ribeye that is barely 3/4" in thickness, this is almost difficult to do (the only way I could see being able to make this happen would be to pre-cook the steaks to Rare, then sear them quickly after they have become cold).  The chefs would have benefited from a Thermapen.  Additionally, the meat was largely flavorless.  Ribeyes are intended to have a fairly robust and dense mouthfeel, with a hearty flavor.  This steak had a limp mouthfeel with no flavor save "salt".  

Unfortunately, the salting problem did not end with the steak.  The fries were shoestring-cut (atypical for a higher-end steak), and had way too much sea salt added.  At least the professional and attentive wait staff were kind enough to keep my drink refilled.  

Especially for the price point, I expected much higher quality.  I do not know if this is representative of all Besh restaurants, but if the kitchen staff cannot get the basics correct, I would be hesitant to order anything more complex.  I definitely recommend a pass on this one.

I came here for a weekday lunch, and the place was packed with people. Everyone was dressed very nicely, so you could tell that it was a very business crowd. However, this place is huge, so seating was not a problem.

I really enjoyed their special that day, the jambalaya. It seemed that everybody was getting it, and the portions were huge. I ate my meal, but it barely looks like I touched it. Their lunch specials come with soup or salad and bread, so definitely fills you up.

I also saw a lot of people getting the burger, so must've been good! The service was also phenomenal, and the place looks very upscale for the price. Definitely would come back!
Two words: Happy Hour. The oysters are amazing. If you love fresh oysters, this is the place to get it. And the bread is fresh as well. Definitely recommend this place.

Without question, one of the best dining experiences ever. First off, we sauntered in about 10pm on a Saturday night (sans reso), and they entertained the idea of seating us anyway. We had to wait a bit, but the bar was perfect for grabbing a coupla of pints prior to dinner. I rarely eat oysters, but the man next to us at the bar had the most humongous and delicious-looking plate of oysters I have ever seen. I'm talking mutant-ninja looking oysters. Incredible. Eventually we were sat at our table and quickly made our way through the unique drink list. The drinks were strong, and really good. The crawfish bisque was delectable, as was the pressed sandwich of "cochon de lait."  I ate and drank myself stupid in this restaurant, and I can't wait to go back and do it again.

This was an excellent experience!!! First time ever eating sushi and I loved it! 

Great service. 
Amazing food. 
Excellent atmosphere.
Delightful happy hour experience. I recommend the raw oysters, gumbo, LA rabbit and Chicken pate, and St Charles Sour cocktail (not the French 75).

So good -- we ate it all before I remembered to snap a pic!  All small plates and cocktails at happy hour for us.  The GINtilly Dragon and the Pate plate were some of the best, but everything was wonderful. Service was ON POINTE! Everyone was attentive to our table, not just "our" server, and incredibly friendly.

I absolutely LOVE LOVE LOVE their happy hour! You can bring your own wine and appetizers are discounted! Regardless of how you feel about oysters, definitely try their P&J Oysters - absolutely fresh and delicious! Every bad thing you've heard about the taste of oysters - none of it can be found here! The hoghead cheese and boudin noir are absolutely mouth-watering, & both come with great pairings! The Luke burger is pretty good but definitely try out their sausage dish or something else if you like to be adventurous....you can't go wrong. As for dessert, skip the apple galette (unless you love apples) and Creme brulee (I've had better) and go straight for the bread pudding and baked mousse - two of their best!!!

Great dinner experience! Enjoyed the food we ordered. Waiters were cool asked for recommending what's good. 
Crabmeat au gratin
