Crawfish bisque 
"En Cocotte" Jumbo Louisiana shrimp highly recommend their version of grits and bbq shrimp.

Order a basic pizza and it'll be amazing. Ask for anything on the side or "without onions" and you might as well be speaking in a foreign language. They will just not get your order right. Tonight is just the 15th example for me, and finally caused me to right a review.

I'm a regular, who lives a few minutes away and I order from here often. The food is amazing, but if they ever say "let me make a note" during your order, then they're going to get it wrong.  Place special orders at your own risk.

We put in our order 50 minutes ago. We ordered the burrata salad, shrimp and grits, crispy Brussels sprouts, and flammenkuchen. We asked our waiter to bring the plates as they were ready. 50 minutes and nothing has come out. AND ITS MY BIRTHDAY. To top it off the staff just seemed annoyed that we mentioned we were hungry. They brought over two more rolls.  I don't want to get full on bread. 

Our waiter did give us two glasses of champagne after he saw my hangry face.

My husband and I sat at the bar for lunch last weekend.  The bartender was super friendly.  We sat right next to the oyster shucker area which was a fun site.  I started with a bloody mary which was really good and helped with my hangover from the night before!  My husband and I shared a bowl of the seafood gumbo which was good but kind of different from what I'm used to.  The mussels were by far my favorite EVER....and they came with fries which was a hit.  This place is a little too pricey, I would go back for a nice dinner but not a place to go for lunch.

Review is for brunch.  My first besh experience and I was not disappointed. So much southern flavor. My fried chicken biscuit was awesome and of the 4 people I ate with--- 3 loved and 1 liked. Strong place.

How good is Elm Cafe? The Second Cup around the corner has since shut down.

What can I say? People love local, fresh food, amazing coffee, and wonderful, friendly service. What's for breakfast/lunch? Check out @elmcafe's latest tweet. Then head on down to see Nate and grab a muffin, sandwich, and a coffee.

I've had their Americanos, 49th Parallel coffee, and delicious tea and haven't had a bad experience yet. 

And the man behind elm cafe, Nathan, is a treat in himself! He's always got something interesting on the go, and he knows some real characters. Stop by for a chat, drink, and a sandwich - and give him kudos for waking up so early to provide us with a great local cafe in downtown Edmonton.

Oh, and just a tip? The tuna/curry sandwich is the best sandwich you'll ever have. Seriously. Try it, and when your tastebuds thank you - don't forget to give me props.

Luke is smaller restaurant located in the Hilton (the Hilton is a cool hotel that used to be a Masonic Lodge, go check it out).

I always head to Luke to check out their oyster bar teeming with ice and to enjoy a cocktail...they make the best French 75 in the city (with Cognac and cherry).  Wow!  

The food is American with a french twist.  I have had the Croque (fantastic), the oysters (fantastic), and the burger (fantastic).  This is a more formal french style restaurant...not over the top pretentious, but it is a classy place, with folks in jackets and dresses...so dress accordingly.

The service is excellent with the staff and others (managers, etc.) always stopping by to ask how things are.  They know how to take care of you at Luke!

Luke is a good value for the money, great food, and outstanding cocktails (try that French 75!).  You can eat at the bar, but it is a small bar with folks standing around waiting on their table.

One piece of advice:  GET A RESERVATION as this is a smaller restaurant and you probably will not get in as a walk in.

Luke nails it.

Got drinks here, Sazeracs to be exact, during their happy hour. Fantastic prices and solid drinks. Good bartenders here..On the con side, their oysters or whatever the hell they cook here makes the lobby of the hotel next door stank like bootay

In town for a conference, looking for a nice place, not too pricey, where we had seafood and non-seafood options.  

Luke fit the bill nicely.  We walked in at 7 on a Saturday night, had a drink and some fantastic duck pate at the bar while we waited for our table (20 min wait) and then were seated.

The food was fantastic, the burger was amazing, the fries were wonderful.

The absinthe frappe and the mint julep were great.  

If I had more time (and money) to spend in new oreleans I would go back and try more of cocktails, and appetizers!

4.8 stars.

We had 2 meals (dinner and breakfast) at Luke's.  On the Open Table reservation I had commented that dinner would be my first meal at NOLA in almost 20 yrs, my daughter's 1st meal at NOLA and I wanted it memorable.  They did not let me down!!!  Gave us a table next to the kitchen window where you can watch the chefs preparing the meals.  To celebrate the return, the restaurant gave us an Alsatian onion tart with this incredible bacon.  I will never call the thin, papery pork slices  "bacon" anymore. Husband had the Louisiana oysters for an appetizer--large, juicy heavenly bivalve heaven.  His shrimp and grits were very good but could not hold a candle to the oysters.  My daughter insists that the burger is the best one she has ever eaten (better than Father's Office, Eugene City Brewery) with perfection fries.  Had the dinner special with chicken soup and matzo ball--somewhat bland; cochon au lait--tender and full of flavor, maybe a little too much salt.  Was too full to eat dessert because...I also ordered the cheese grits!!!  So this is what grits are suppose to be like--not the weird bland clumpy cream-of-wheat stuff they serve in Los Angeles--this is what is going to bring me back.

And it did.  Came back for breakfast 2 days later.  A waiter (not the one that served us dinner) remembered what I had written and asked my daughter how much she enjoyed her 1st meal.  How cool and personal is that!!  Got the grits YUM!!  Daughter got pancakes with fruit infused cane syrup YUM!!  Husband got muesli with yogurt YUM!!

Mr. Besh--please open a restaurant where I live.  We have great local produce for you!!!!!

i had my annual christmas dinner with friends a few days ago, and one of them suggested luke for this year's repast.  we met early to take advantage of the happy hour (1/2 off well drinks from 3-6 pm).  while i'm not one to order a ~special~ libation from a menu, i was disappointed in their selections.  the beverages were very spring/summer-y (think: heavy citrus and other light concoctions like frappes.)  the bartender was nice and prepared some very delicious winter standards for us.

i ordered from the express menu which is comprised of soup, entree, and dessert for 23 usd.  since i'm gluten free, my soup was limited to the chicken soup minus matzo balls.  the broth was very flavorful and would be a fine selection if you wanted to start with something light.  

the tuesday entree special was cochon du lait with sauteed greens (chef 86'ed the cornbread dressing due to my dietary restriction).  i'm a huge fan of anything that comes from a pig.  the cochon was perfectly cooked - roasted skin and all. the greens were a little salty but had a nice smokiness.  

the restaurant would have received 5 stars had it not been for the dessert snafu. i was waiting and waiting (...and waiting) for my dessert so when the bill came, i asked for my dessert because i thought they had forgotten it.  turns out, the choice was bread pudding which is obviously a no-no but instead of asking what i could eat, they were going to send me out without dessert.  at a finer dining establishment, such as luke, i was very surprised...i mean, some communication would have been nice instead of just handing me my bill.  i told the server that i could, in fact, eat ice cream if there was any in the back.  he apologized and said that he would send some out.  i selected the caramel apple but could have chosen from chocolate, coffee, or some other flavor.  the ice cream came out with a cookie placed on it so we had to send the ice cream back with instructions to not put any cookies or other flour-laden goodies as garnish. a different server brought back a newly prepared cookie-less dessert and gave me a little attitude (he said something along the lines of "does this suit you now?" it's not that i'm trying to be a problem.  if i could eat gluten, i would. my diet would be a lot more varied, and my grocery bill wouldn't be so steep.)  regardless, the ice cream was fantastic! it was well-balanced, creamy and not too sweet.  a very delicious ending to a filling meal.

all-in-all, though, i would return to luke because they have a fabulous menu.  i like the dining space and the location.

nota bene: gets busy around 7 pm so either come around 5.30 or 9 pm to avoid having to wait for a table.

Had a fabulous Sunday birthday brunch! Complete with mimosas and delicious shrimp and grits. I have to say it does annoy me when tails are on shrimp when a sauce it used. But the sauce was delicious, so I didn't mind too much getting in there to remove the tails, then lick my fingers . Finale was bread pudding a la mode!

Second time here and it was just as wonderful at the first time!  Got there just before 6 on a Saturday and got half price appetizer and drinks! Got the local gulf oysters on a half shell and they were yummy.... flavorful and creamy.  Had the pate of Louisiana rabbit and OMG it was soooo good so if you are a pate lover this is a must!  Also ordered at our table were the mussels, the pork shank (both huge) and the Grilled ribeye with bernaise. Also worth mentioning were the fries... Think they are the best I have had in a long time, thin, flavourful with just the right amount of salt.  Everyone thoroughly enjoyed their dinner and we were too full to order dessert! 

My only negative comment would be the atmosphere. It was good in the main room but unfortunatetly we got seated way in the back and it was freezing and we were pretty much alone in this room most of the time. Would have preferred a table in the main room with the bar so if you make resevations and like this atmosphere, make sure you request a table in this room.

TIP1: Be Prepared for all kinds of recommendations from the 'safety check.'  
  WHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE:  "I don't want anything extra done unless I specifically approve it!"

Okay they GOT me. I had a Groupon today for a Synthetic Blend oil change.  I know my truck is rated for 7qts, but I rarely put over 6 back when changing.  So I knew they would most likely charge me the extra 2qts, because 'most' oil changes are for 5qts.  Extra $16 for possibly 2 qts. They did tell me the groupon was only for the credit of about $72 and would be extra.

So the CSA Matthew was very nice, it was not busy and I went right in.  He started the standard, 'We'll check it and get back to you.'  Later, again pleasant, he came back with multiple 'recommendations.'  Radiator Fluid flush- Me: Just changed the radiator and fluid. We can top Radiator off- Me: I got some at home (It was at the minimum line).  Fuel Filter- Me: I just replaced the whole fuel pump and filter last year.  Transmission- Me: I had it done last year with the fuel pump.  So really nothing had to be done. 

He did note the differential would be checked, which I was not sure when or if it had been checked.  Also he mentioned vacuuming the truck, the cracked windshield and I did hear something about 'window treatment,' but I just assumed he was rattling off standard Service. Ended up being a 3.99 charge plus tax for RainX on the windshield which sucked because my next stop was the car wash.

My differential came back with small shavings on the magnetic plug.  I went ahead with a differential service $100, plus $24 for fluid.  UGH!  I asked the price before and got $100, but not the fluid costs. 

So my Synthetic Blend Oil Change Groupon cost me an extra $20, plus another $130 for RainX Windshield treatment and a differential oil change (and vacuum).  NOW, I am not sure whether they should have made a referral to have the differential looked at.  The shavings were pretty big, not sand, but actual shavings at least 2 were over an inch.  I have no current issues, so I'm still researching.

Anyway, this was about what I was expecting and I should have done it myself for about an hour labor and $60 in parts. So I figure it was barely worth it in the end.  But I wish they had said more about the differential issue.

Final TIP:  Military discount is only for those with a military ID, veterans do not receive any discount.
The tomato basil soup is delicious! Love the Cobb Salad as well, although it is a bit overpriced. Overall a little pricey, but cute place to study and eat!

Beautiful facility with spotless dining room and clean bathrooms.  I stopped by to try a selection of oysters.  The raw were sweet and creamy with a very nice home made cocktail sauce, but the char grilled oysters were fabulous.  It paired perfectly with the Bavarian style hefeweizen beer on tap.  The service was the absolute best I found during my week in NOLA. My only two regrets are I can not remember my servers' name and I couldn't get back to Luke's to sample more of their fare.
Semper Fi Devil Dawg

I have to say the experience was far superior to the food.  And the food was DAMN GOOD.  We showed up for Happy Hour and it was EVERYTHING.  The raw oysters were plump, fresh and sweet.  The fried oysters were fried perfectly.  The Brussel Sprouts??  OMG, they were DIVINE!!!  My mom had the Luke Burger....it was HUGE and cooked perfectly.  The only disappointment was the boiled shrimp.  I think we were expecting shrimp cocktail, so having to peel and eat shrimp was like UGH.  But the remolaude sauce is also DIVINE!! Plus our server Rich was the bomb!!  We will be back...

Luke is a let down compared to Besh's other restaurants. The food is german diner style with seafood? I am confused. The happy hour on raw oysters is pretty good, but how hard is it to serve food you literally don't cook...
The shrimp and grits are incredible. The seasoning and spice were perfect for a breakfast dish.

A Sunday brunch...featuring fried oyster salad, an excellent crab bisque, shrimp and grits, and pancakes. All were executed very well. Service was amateurish. The restaurant has a split design, with half of the tables upfront and half across a hallway with glass walls looking in on the kitchen. Two very different experiences.

I love this place!  The chicken was amazing, and the server was very kind and accommodating.  I would totally come back here again, and might do tomorrow for lunch.  *So* awesome.  I even told the front hostess about our server and how awesome he was, which is a rare occurrence for me.

I didn't even realize it was John Besh's restaurant until I stepped inside. My group of 4 came here for breakfast before heading to meet a group for lunch so we wanted to try a few things but the intention was not to fill up.

We ordered the gumbo -- it was something I wanted to try at every single restaurant I went to -- and it was pretty good. A tad salty, but I'd rather that than bland.

The local crab omelette was decent, the egg part was fluffy and it was stuffed with plump morsels of crab. I was really happy to see that there was no skimping on ingredients here.

The piece de resistance was indeed the shrimp and grits. The shrimp are fried -- there are 6 of them -- and hangs off the lip of a mason jar filled with jalapeno grits and topped with soft poached eggs and a very light Hollandaise sauce. It was absolutely incredible!! The shrimp were perfect crispy on the outside with a great snap while the grits is just a smooth, luxurious, velvety, unctuous, gooey blob of deliciousness.

Really happy that we stopped in here!

I had no trouble getting a table at Luke for lunch on a Wednesday. The waiter was extremely attentive, the shrimp and grits were delicious and the portion sufficient that I got to eat the leftovers for dinner, and I would eagerly eat here again.

Prior to visiting new orleans, I asked around for some rest recommendations. Luke was one. We had to make reservations 3 days in advanced for a Sunday 5pm table. 

It is a nicer place, we wore like jeans and whatev and kinda felt out of place.

I was pleasantly surprised to find that they offer happy hour even when you are dining (not just at the bar). Half price wine and cocktails. I believe $1 oysters. 

We ordered 4 orders of brussels sprouts lol. They're really good, just get them. I also ordered the crab bisque which was awesome. 

Service was soooo weird. Servers were dressed very professionally but their personality said otherwise. Maybe this is a southern thing? Also like I would barely put my fork down after my last bite and he would already be taking my plate.

The service wasn't great, but the food was DELICIOUS! Between the 4 members of my family we tried a little bit of everything. It was was yummy, but the shrimp and crab étouffée was the best thing on the menu!
Company Luncheon here. Good to the last morsal. All our guests impressed and full.
Excellent shrimp and grits.  The best crab omelet I've ever had!!!  Awesome service...can't wait to go back there again!

Wow. So disappointed as it was the first John Besh restaurant I tried and it didn't meet any of my expectations at all.

None of the food was memorable, in fact, some of it was simply bad. The frites came out cold and instead of replacing them they tried to re-fry them into brown sticks of starch - ugh.

The bartender didn't know how to serve pastis - in a French Brasserie?

Food was cold or delayed. The server forgot drinks. And, nothing tasted great. 

Sadly, there are too many other good restaurants in NOLA I would try again before here. Damn, I really like John Besh, too.

My fiancé and I were visiting New Orleans from Philadelphia last weekend and could only manage to squeeze this place in for happy hour- but I'm so glad that we did. The service was so welcoming and timely- and in the one instance when a cocktail that we ordered took a little long, our server took it off the check. Since we were eating light we went with happy hour oysters and the fried oyster salad, which they split into two separate bowls without us having to ask. Both were delicious and the thick-cut bacon in the salad alone was something to marvel at. 

We finished with the warm bread pudding and I can honestly say that in October 2016, when we return for our wedding, I'll make sure to stop by in the midst of all the craziness to have it again- it may have been the best dessert I have EVER had.

Only giving 4 becuz I'm going back tomorrow to try sumn different! LISTEN UP!!!! This. Here. Is. The. Business!!!! 

Ok...ex had ribeye steak with crab meat (oh lawd I just melted) and I had shrimp and grits (scraps skillet with spoon). Flaw.Less.com/itwastheboooomb.com.net/org/lemme.edu.cate.u.on.good.eating/damn.slapyomama.com 

#imdone
Food was fantastic, very comfortable surroundings and we were seated right next to the kithcen where we had quite a show while watching the kitchen staff make their tasty morsels.

Went to Luke for dinner with several friends Halloween evening and it was incredibly good. Our server was exceptionally on top of things, offered great suggestions and was very personable. All of our cocktails were delicious. I had a chicken dish that was amazing and my fiancee's steak was good too. The portions were very French. It was a great setting for a wonderful beginning to our evening. Definitely will go again next time I am in New Orleans.
Disinterested service. Slow food preparation. Food was good but not great. Looks like besh set this place up and has never come back.

I came here with my girl for brunch. I brunch every weekend in NYC and this was the single best brunch I've ever had. I got the crawfish omelette and have never had anything near this good. If you don't get this I feel bad for you. 

This omelette is overflowing with buttered craw. There's a salad with it with a vinegar base to cut it. They through some fries my way for free but I didn't waste my time. I wouldn't let anything mar the perfect flavor of this plate. I recommend you do the same. 

Finish with the coffee they give you with real cream ( not milk and absolutely no cheesy little packets). 

I left feeling satisfied and classy. Odds are this place can't be beat. There can only be one best and I think Luke claims it. 

Andrew served and is a great host.

What a nice place but SO pricy. This is the first restaurant I tried in New Orleans, Louisiana. Nice ambiance. Loud and busy. Service is fine and little bit slow.

Food: 

Gumbo soup - delicious flavors. It has a perfect spicy kick. Definitely recommended 

Crab bisque soup - one of the best crab bisque a I ever had. Very rich and creamy.

Jumbo shrimp and grits - ahhh this is a must to try. It is like a party of great spices in your mouth. Best one I ever had !

Powerful drinks, great happy hour specials!

Get there early, though, if you are going for the happy hour because it will get packed fast!
Great staff and great food. Took care of my dietary needs with expertise and great taste. Thanks

Luke has recently done a rebranding.  The got rid of the umlaut and made the menu a bit more NOLA style.  We had a reservation and were seated immediately.  The restaurant is much larger than it appears.  The front looks very much like a trendy bistro whereas the back is a bit more American looking.  We sat in the back and they have the clear walled kitchen, which I liked.  Being a Besh restaurant, I expected to be blown away and wasn't but thought it was very good.  Our server was very good.  She was prompt and friendly and knowledgeable.  

There were four of us and we shared several dishes.  My least favorite was probably the flammenkuchen.  It was a standard flatbread.  Nothing really wowed me.  The crust wasn't that great or crispy.  The pate was quite a surprise.  I sometimes do not care for rabbit but this was really tasty.  The flavor was really wonderful as well as the accompaniments.  We had to get some jalapeno grits, which were good but not great.  I would have liked some more spice but the texture was good.  The 'etouffee' was very tasty, albeit not a traditional etouffee.  However the pasta that came with it was actually extremely good.  Overall, I expected a bit more but struggled with only giving 3 stars cause the food, ambiance and service were all above average.

Four of us went to Luke not once but twice in the same day. We went to breakfast and had the eggs in a jar, a couple of southern breakfasts, and the shrimp and grits. Everything was delicious! In the morning, the service was fine but didn't stand out.

After a bit of gambling, we decided we were craving seafood and decided to go back for dinner. We got one of the very large seafood plates and were beyond impressed by both the size of it as well as the freshness. TRY. THE. HORSERADISH. So painful but so good. :) So fresh! Also, one person had the burger and it was fantastic! Everything on our plates were 5 star quality.

What really made this a 5 star experience was the dinner service. We arrived at 10:30 with an 11pm closing time. We apologized repeatedly for being the last customers but we were treated like we were the best guests in the house. The beers were good, the drinks were good, and the food was amazing! The service was out of this world and we appreciate that they would joke with us and put up with us, even after a long day.

For anyone going to New Orleans, this is an absolute must.

When you're having cocktails at a venerable NOLA institution and the bartender there recommends another bar, you go. Thus it was that we left Antoine's for Luke on our way to a late dinner. 

Sitting at the bar, we asked about the oysters on hand and ordered half a dozen Blue Points, plus a dozen steamed, chilled mussels. There was suddenly a rush of activity and the bartender was delayed about twenty minutes; although we assured him we weren't in a hurry, he apologized profusely and then threw in extras of both. Great guy!

The shellfish arrived on a round tray on a thick bed of crushed ice, accompanied by plenty of lemon, cocktail sauce and horseradish (asking for more lemon is a pet peeve at raw bars, so I appreciated this.) They were superb. The mussels were perfectly tender and flavored with herbs, with a subtle spicy kick; the oysters were plump, briny and sweet, as oysters should be. 

I'm forgetting drinks: I had a wonderful Belgian witbier, redolent of banana, and my husband ordered a Death in the Afternoon. The bartender didn't know how to make it but gamely followed his tutorial, asked a couple of questions and then just charged us for house champagne. I cannot say enough good things about the service!

After an hour in the sublime hubbub of the bar, we were reluctant to go on to dinner --  but enjoyed our experience there just as much (see Borgne review for more details!)

Luke's was our first stop here in NOLA.  I was excited to have me some shrimp n grits!  Unfortunately, it didn't wow me like I thought it would.  I am not a pro of any sort on southern comfort food, so I guess it just doesn't suit my tastes.  *shrug.  I found the shrimp and grits to be greasy.  (Is it supposed to be like this?) When the order arrives, it looks like a pretty dinky order for $22 or so, but I wasn't able to finish the whole thing because it was so heavy.  Flavor wise, it was wonderful.  The shrimp was not crunchy at all though- was a bit mushy in the dead way.  Boyfriend got Saturday brunch special - jagerschnitzel over spaetzle and a cup of gumbo.  The gumbo was my favorite part of the meal (warning: I steal food).  However, for a "seafood" gumbo, there wasn't really much seafood.  One baby oyster.  Mostly andouille sausage.  The schnitzel was fried nicely; it was crispy without being too heavy.  The spaetzle was OK...inside was kind of dry instead of chewy.  Service wise, our waiter was great!

Ok, I know this is another review of Jeerzie. But when it came down to choice between Jeerzies and Dagwoods (another favor), Jeerzies won for 1 reason and 1 reason only.

The SWEET CHILLI PEPPER WINGS!.

Plus the service stepped up big time tonight. There was a birthday party happening, but the 2 girls handled the sellout crowd like it was nothing new. No order pads. The took the orders and delivered without 1 mistake. That rocks!

Plus the mini tacos were surpringly good. The pitchers of Yuengling Lager are ice cold along with the frosted glasses just make National Beer Day great!

So good we made a reservation for the following night, while we were eating  there on the first night!

The raw oysters were super fresh, the crawfish bisque was as good as a lobster bisque, and the shrimp & grits was also a hit! (Slightly over done shrimps, but delicious!) We stumbled on their happy hour (before 6pm) when the wine and other libations were half priced! Can't sniff at that! 

A mention to the wait staff too, who were attentive and friendly.

Overall, a great experience. Can't wait for tomorrow night, when I'll be trying their rabbit and chicken liver pate, and the sausage and seafood gumbo!

The food was good but not great.  A bit overpriced for the food and the lack of atmosphere.  Also, when we were there on a rather busy night, it felt very chain-like.  Still, I'd give it another shot and go between 3-6 for the oysters.

There's something about food in New Orleans that just makes wonders. I just think that every place (small or big, fancy or humble) in New Orleans put so much effort in food.  

Luke is one of those places.  

First of all, you must take advantage of the happy hour. Not only for the booze but for the amazing oyster at .50 cents..., opened as you ordered them.  

They have an amazing burger.  The seafood gumbo is equally great.  Service is good and location, too.

Love the atmosphere! The wait staff are very attentive. I always go for the oysters, but you do have to be careful and possibly count your oysters. One time I was missing a dozen oysters.

I absolutely love the duck pate! for $11, that's a steal!
My girlfriend went for happy hour the other day and Tristan and Vusi could not be more attentive and in tune with or needs. #flawlessserver #iwantedfornothing

Extremely pleased with Fahrenheit service. They diagnosed an issue I was having with an air conditioner that led me to replace the air conditioner and the heater. They were out at 9 at night and at 9 in the morning the next day my new unit was being installed the crew did an exceptional job. Very professional very nice people good rate on the new AC heating unit. Highly recommend you will never find a more professional nicer group of people than those at Fahrenheit!
Good customer service, awesome shrimp and grits. Perfect place to get a relaxing lunch before you take off to go back home

The oysters were great and the service good.
However the schnitzel and side dishes were small. 
We talked to the water but he charged us for another side dish.
The red cabbage was not very tasty, not enough gravy and the spatzle
Were at a premium .
Overall it was just ok.
Go for the oysters.

My husband is an avid hunter and says the quail was the best he'd ever had. The drum was pretty good. The vegetables were over salted for my taste.  The fresh oysters were delicious as our appetizer.  Nice location near le pavilion.

I am a huge supporter of our good local cafes in Edmonton, and this is one of them! 

Now that I don't work downtown anymore, the only time I get to stop in is when I am in the city for training or the odd day off.  

The food is fantastic!  The muffins are always innovative flavour combinations and they always seem to have something with rhubarb when I stop in!  

I am a touch claustrophobic so I can never stay in to enjoy my coffee.  The place is a little too small for my liking.  However, outside seating is available when the weather is good.  

There isn't a more cheerful way to start your day than when your Barista is so thoughtful and kind enough to give you some beautiful art in the foam of your latte!  The espresso shots are never bitter which just makes the lattes that much better!

This was great!  Just went last night, got the beet salad for appetizer/starter and the sausage for entree.  I definitely did not take advantage of all the menu has to offer but what I had was excellent(apparently sausage is house-made), I made a reservation and got seated right away, the service was great, and all in all, it was a really great meal in Nola!

Had this place as my first meal in New Orleans, I was very pleased with the meal, we got the crab au gratin, the shrimp and grits, and the bread pudding. All were outstanding dishes. The bread pudding was so good we went back for seconds the next day, but since it was about to close they made it to go, even though they let us eat it at the bar. It was missing the delicious candied pecans and wasn't as pretty but still yummy. I would love to come back and try the burger among other things!

So order   exactly the following: A sazerac, Duck and Rabbit pates with watermelon pickles and mustard and grilled bread, the crawfish boil po boy with fries and ice cold abita, then a bread pudding a la mode. It's some of the best food in town even if it's a little hidden off the lobby of a Hilton hotel. This is one I run to everytime I get to visit NOLA!
Explore the menu & try new things.  Regardless of what you order it will be fantastic and memorable.  This is one of my top 10 places to dine in NOLA

I had come to New Orleans with few ambitions.  However, one of them was to eat at a Besh owned restaurant.  

A group from the conference I attended wanted to have something other than jambalaya.  We settled on Luke because the menu had lots of homey options like steak frittes and roasted chicken.  
I started off with a cup of the crab and corn bisque.  It was tasty had had a sharp kick that I enjoyed.  

I also ordered the duck.  The huge entree consisted of half a duck and lots of hash brown-like potatoes.  The duck was completely rendered of fat and not at all gamey (which is sad for me because I actually like the pungency of duck).  I did steal a couple of frittes from my colleague's plate and they were okay.  

I ended the evening with the gateau.  Delicious.  It was probably my favorite thing I ate all week in Nola.  The cake was dense, rich and wonderful.  The brown butter sauce with sauteed quince was perfect.  I could have done without the tangy whipped marscapone but I understood that it cut nicely into the richness of the dish.  

Why only three stars then, you ask?  There were more than a couple of misteps in the service.   While our server could not have been nicer she seemed to mix things up like setting down juice glasses instead of wine glasses and serving freezing cold frittes.

Great breakfast.
One of the people who had breakfast there day before recommended it. His description was great so we tried it.  Seafood omlet was great. Jucy and deletious.
French frise was crispy and little salty just like I like.
Cofee was not your regular cheap type of coffee it was good quality. Server was professional I don't know why but he looked like some kind of law school student. 

Overall great place.

My friend and I came here during happy hour, and though we were not dressed fancily, we weren't treated any differently! We were seated (no reservation) reasonably fast.

The oysters were great as it often is in New Orleans, and the savory crab beignets were decent. Not enough flavor but the garlic sauce that came with was interesting to make up for the blandness though. The shrimp and grits though. OMG. so cheesy, so heavy, but so good.

The interior is decorated really well, too. Lots of space, and really helpful and friendly but professional service all around. Someone to my right ate 75% of his burger and complained to the waiter at the end that it was an awful burger, but the waiters dealt with it super calmly and reasonably! props

Lukes was probably the most acceptable place we ate at during our trip to New Orleans this past March, and that's not saying much.  The prices were bordering on absurd but the entertainment offered by our "hosts" sort of made up for it.  We ordered raw oysters, fried oysters and chilled shrimp.  The shrimp was served to us un-peeled, which was very reminiscent of a Las Vegas buffet. I've never dined at an upscale restaurant where you had to peel your own shrimp.  The staff wasn't very knowledgable about the oysters, admitting that they don't eat "those thangs" lol.  But they DO eat turtle soup and alligator, they said. Nevertheless, the oysters were relatively fresh, as were the shrimp.  The raw ones were on ice for quite a while and tasted like tap water, and the fried oysters were seasoned (unlike the ones we got at Deanies, which were horrible) but some were much more seasoned than others. We could literally see the salt on a few of them.  Anyway, Sean and Jamal kept us laughing and smiling (Miami Dolphins!), which we appreciated, but we both found Lukes to be highly overrated. Perhaps we've been spoiled by the seafood readily available here in California at reasonable prices. For instance, at Fisherman's Wharf you can get a whole dungeness or local crab plucked right from the ocean and steamed up for you for a mere $8 bucks. And having said that, I'm now wondering if I'd fallen for a tourist trap by going to Lukes. Hmm...

The happy hour oysters were the size of my hand for 50 cents each!! This is not a drill. We pretty much split 50 oysters among the three of us because they were so tasty & affordable. Luke has plump raw oysters (more meaty if that's your preference) and fried oysters (but they were much smaller) and a variety of other styles that we didn't try. The bread pudding is definitely a must - it was the perfect ending to our meal! So delicious!

Happy hour! They have .75 cent oysters with half off drinks from 3-6pm. It is next to the Hilton hotel and the place was barely full. They have some of the best P&J oysters I have ever had. The are usually priced at $2-4 and I don't think there is a better deal in the area.

This place is nasty and many of its employees seem to be encouraged to treat customers like the garbage that often covers the tables.  Like Jen D. says, this restaurant only stays open because of its proximity to Penn.

This places lives up to the Besh-hype. Arrived right at 5pm on a Monday hoping to enjoy an hour of their happy hour (half price drinks and draft beer as well as $.50 oysters. We were sat immediately despite not having a reservation.  We ordered a French 75, dozen oysters, and  shrimp en cocotte (basically the best shrimp and grits ever) and loved every bit of it. Besh knows what he is doing so do yourself a solid and RUN to Luke!

I've seen this place on Instagram a lot so I'm here. At first we were very excited to try until our orders were taken. My order was taken at 10:22 pm and currently it is 10:59pm and still no food yet. (Currently waiting in the store) it's not as busy as I would have assumed. As I sit and wait I can over here the ladies in back saying that my order is messed up and I only order beef and broccoli a shrimp roll...  Regardless on if the food was worth it or not I would never give a place my money with POOR CUSTOMERS SERVICE. 100% totally horrible... the food is overrated very small portions for an high price... the employees in the front just sit and watch and gossip when your waiting an hour for a lunch size dinner for 15 bucks ... Business rule number #1 great customer service  #2 treat all customers equally... it was all of me and my friends first and last time... and we drove 1 hour for this experience..
Great happy hour price. Raw oysters are not so clean. Whould pay more for better oyster shuck

Great restaurant and yummy food. Definitely a little more upscale than what the group and I thought it was going to be. Oysters from Cape Cod were $31. Worth it! A couple of people got the Luke Burger and I had a bite of it...it is so good. The MOULES ET FRITES were delicious as well. A plate full of PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND MUSSELS STEAMED WITH GARLIC & THYME WITH HOUSE-MADE FRIES..yes...delicious..wow. JUMBO LOUISIANA SHRIMP EN COCOTTEI was another dish that a couple of the group members ordered. Same comment, consistently great. They both enjoyed it so much. I had the Fruge Farms Crawfish Etouffee and it was definitely something that I enjoyed eating, but the presentation of it was not so great. Let's just say that the noodles don't look so appetizing. Overall, great restaurant...very beautiful on the inside and great service. We left the restaurant highly satisfied. What more can you ask for?

Came here for brunch on a Monday and this was probably my favorite meal of my visit in New Orleans. The place has an old school vibe from the dapper looking wait staff to sections of the day's newspaper hanging up for patrons to read. The brunch menu is not nearly as extensive as what you typically see at a diner these days, but the selections are high quality. My girlfriend and I ordered the egg white frittata and fried chicken biscuit to share. The frittata was conveniently served for us in two small portions. It was perfectly seasoned and so full of flavor that I didn't even miss the egg yolks. The fried chicken biscuit was also excellent. Chicken was crispy on the outside, moist on the inside and the biscuit was warm and fresh. The chicken biscuit also came with a seasonal jam that added a little sweet/tart dimension to the plate. From top to bottom, the ambiance, service, and most importantly the food were all very good. I definitely recommend brunch at Lüke!

Went into Lukes on Mardi Gras.  Incredible is all I can say.  We were seated right away, .50 oysters and 1/2 price beer is incredible.  Definitely try the pressed pork sandwich and the bread pudding is a must have!!  Loved my experience!!

#Yelp365 6/365

swine and veal pate + blt sanwich + sunday special = holy smokes! 

this place has some cajun influences but it's a straight up gastropub... a badass gastropub

the buster crab sangwich was fantasmic... texas toast, ripe tomatos and bentons bacon.  nom nom nom

pate de champagne was off the richter scales, i think i soiled my pants eating this app....

went with your mom... we had a nice brunch together

There is only one downside to the Elm cafe - they make a handful of custom creations every day, and if it's not to your liking you don't really have another option. However, they quite reliably have multiple, suitably diverse choices these days, so that really cuts the risk factor down.

As an added bonus (althought this really should become the status quo someday soon if you ask me) the Elm Cafe team are mavens of social media, so you are one Twitter search away from knowing exactly whats going to be on today. You may not want to follow them on Twitter, as doing so will compel you to eat here often. The food doesn't just taste fantastic, it reads like it's going to taste fantastic, and 140 characters is not few enough to prevent hypnosis. 

I dare you. Go read up over at https://twitter.com/elmcafe . It's ok, I'll wait here.

See what I mean!? I'll meet you there for breakfast.

(as a note I usually find the breakfasts better than the lunches, because they are so creative and there is basically nobody doing interesting breakfast sandwiches in Edmonton, so they are a very special treat. Lunch is still top shelf stuff, the breakfasts just have a extra twist of magic)

The barista services are similarly outstanding, but its the food that brings me back every time. 

Elm Cafe is TINY (I guess that makes two downsides...), so I will only visit in sunshiney weather when I can use the patio, or when I need to take it to go. Remember that eating while driving is against the law now, because let me tell you that your takeout order will taunt you from the passenger seat.

In planning my NOLA trip, making reservations, in advance, for dinner was the first thing I wanted to get out of way. When I was doing research on Yelp, Luke came up when I filtered for "Most Reviewed" and it was a no-brainer that I should plan a dinner here for my girls and I. I was able to make reservations for 4 at 8 PM on a Sunday with no problems on OpenTable. We had no problems walking here from our hotel which was a block over from Bourbon St. 

We arrived and the place was packed, both the front room and towards the back in the separate room which is where they sat us. We were lucky enough to be seated right next to the kitchen, where they had clear, glass windows and we could see all the chefs working hard preparing all the meals.

Everything on the menu looked good, but I ended up ordering the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en Cocotte" ($24) which was comprised of Roasted Jalapeno Cheese Grits and Andouille & Green Onion Sausages. Seeing that the grits had Jalapeno cheese, I was worried because my spice tolerance is very low, but when I asked the waiter, he confirmed that the dish wasn't spicy and that the Jalapeno cheese just gave the grits flavor. I'm glad I listened to him and went ahead with ordering that. 

The food took a little while to come out but we understood because the place was really busy and you could see them working non-stop in the kitchen. The Shrimp & Grits were sooooo good. The Jalapeno cheese added another level to the dish and it complemented the hearty, flavorful sauce that the Shrimp were swimming in. I'd never had grits because and I kept forgetting they were actually grits because the sauce was all over them. Thickness-wise, in my opinion, they were probably similar to mashed potatoes but definitely grainier but I didn't mind them and I'm glad that my first experience to Southern grits was in this beautiful dish. I forget what my friends ordered but all I remember is everyone loving their dish.  They all seemed to enjoy mine as well. Also for all of you Gluten-free folks, the waiters will tell you what could be made GF so you don't need to rule this restaurant out if you'll be eating with someone with Celiac disease. Even though we were stuffed, there's always room for dessert so at the recommendation of our waiter's we ordered the Steamed Chocolate to share and it was heavenly! 

I'd definitely recommend Luke if you want a nice dinner!
Lükes had a nice environment. The food was superb. The servers tended to our large party quickly. The gumbo was phenomenal.

Arrived on a Friday evening in time for  Happy Hour with half priced drinks and 50 cent oysters.  Pleasant atmosphere, varied menu and exceptional service.  I had shrimp  ettouffee (?) and my wife had Jaegerschnitzel and bread pudding for dessert.  Most enjoyable.

we ate lunch at luke's during jazz fest a few weeks ago.  it came recommended by a friend for quality food.  they may have been understaffed but it was hard to get our waitress' attention.  we definitely did not see her between her taking our order, dropping off our food and then the check.  we even had to wait 10 mins for someone to pick up our check so we can pay for our meal!

the decor is very trendy with a gastro pub feel.  it's a lot of open space and very clean looking decorations and furniture.  they have an interesting drink menu and i tried "the riverbend", which had blueberries, vodka, lemon juice, basil and ginger ale.  it was too sweet for my liking and i did not finish it (which says a lot b/c if you know me, i never leave a glass empty!).  my fiance got a bloody mary, which was made with their own home made mix.  it had a bit of a sour/tangy taste and not the spicy/horseradish-y taste that we generally prefer.  on a side note - one of the best things about nola is that every restaurant provides you with plastic cups so you can take your drinks to-go!

on to the food... unfortunately, it was not for me.  we ordered the crawfish bisque and seafood gumbo to start, followed by a dozen specialty oysters and peel and eat shrimp.  i also ordered the fried oysters, bacon, roman and avocado salad.  first off, everything came out at the same time.  it did not come out in shifts and we went from nothing to everything all at once.  the gumbo was just okay - we had better gumbo at 4am the night before at a hole in the wall place we stumbled into.  the crawfish bisque was good!  the specialty oysters they had that day were blue points and another kind that was harvested on the east coast, but raised in washington state.  both were pretty tasty.  the peel and eat shrimps were huge and probably the best part of the entire meal.  finally, i did not enjoy my fried oyster salad.  the oysters were too large and the batter had no flavor.  the bacon and avocado were delicious though.

on a final note, keep in mind that this is a german restaurant.  it's not the place to get home cook nola specialties.  given that, i still would not return as there are much better restaurants in that area (financial district).

i am giving LUKE 5 stars soley based on the LUKE BURGER. i do not need to eat anything else here. perfection! and it's as big as my head. perfect to split.  i recomend a good cabernet to go with it  and you've got a pretty tasty date night!
Can't beat 75 cent oysters and half price drinks during happy hour! Not the warmest of bartenders but I'll take it at the price!

Poor quality Sunday breakfast/brunch service for a messily party of 3. Would have liked to try the food, but we couldn't even get served water within 20 minutes so we left. Won't be returning for sure. Went to Palace Cafe instead (which I highly recommend for Sunday brunch).

Extremely delicious breakfast.  The menu is not extensive but this is a good thing. They put effort and heart into each dish.  Our server was awesome in dealing with a big party needing separate checks. The biscuit sandwich with sausage was fantastic. The grits are perfectly seasoned. The pancakes were divine! We will be back!!

Time for the oil change and this is where my wife and I have been brining our vehicle for a while.  Joey and Matt do a terrific job of receiving the vehicle and doing the job.  They let you know of other recommended items to take care of, but are not pushy about getting them or not.  They are very knowledgeable and polite.  Great service.  We will continue to bring our vehicle here for service.

We went for Oyster Happy Hour!
OVER THE TOP EXCELLENT!!! Huge fresh J&P Louisiana Oysters! Great service and food! We ordered 2 dozen oysters and 1/2 dozen fried oysters! Excellent! Just get there early 3-6pm we arrived at 3:45 pm and it was pretty packed. We got lucky and were seated in 15 min.

This is an excellent brunch place in New Orleans. While it has the regular greasy good typical brunch options, it also has a decent amount of vegetarian breakfast options which are actually excellent like the Benedict. Reasonably priced and excellent service.

I popped by Luke for the simple reason of hitting them for their HAPPY HOUR SPECIAL - $0.75 oyster, $1.25 fried oysters and half off drinks 3-6pm Everyday.

I just wanted a couple of the fried oysters, but was told that they come by the half dozen.  Okay, that's fine.

They arrived in a cute fry basket, and down they went way too easily.

Stopped by Luke's for our last lunch before we leave New Orleans.  The place was pretty busy for a Friday afternoon when we were there. My bf had their special of the day (forgot what the name was) and it was awesome.  I had their roasted chicken, and we both said it's the best roasted chicken we can remember eating for a LONG time.  And then we realized why, it's cooked with pancetta, which means it's probably cooked in chicken and bacon grease.  Um... what's not to like?!  Super buttery/creamy mashed potatoes and yummy squashes veggies on the side.  I might get a heart attack on my way to the airport, but I would've died happy.  

Also kinda funny people watching, some looks like high brow business people, some look are tourists, some young adults getting together with friends. Lucky for us, the "couple" next table kept us guessing/occupied...  Older guy with younger girlfriend?  Mistress?  Dating service?  Mystery unsolved but entertained none the less.   

Service is ok, not awesome, not terrible.  Can't say they're super attentive but not neglected to a point where I was annoyed.

Came here  for their HH,  which is everyday! You get 75 cents oyster,  and half off on drinks.. Need I say more? I made reservations, but it wasn't really busy. The restaurant is fairly large with a large space in the back for seating. 

I also got the bread pudding with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. It was pretty sweet, but the best part were the nuts!! Overall, a great spot for good oysters at an amazing price!!

Luke was on my bucket list for 2015 and it didn't disappoint. I went for the .75 oyster happy hour. The oysters were quite good but not any better than Acme. Had they not had the price right I would have passed on this one.
Clean, fast, filling, but tacos and burritos are about the extent of it.  NOT nearly as healthy as you think.  Hit up West Coast Tacos when they are at 86th and Michigan, otherwise hit Chipoopie.

This pertains to breakfast only:  The one time I've had breakfast here, it wasn't anything special.  I would have been happier with Waffle House.  I'm not saying it was bad.  Given some level of expectation, it should have been somewhat better than an average breakfast offering.

Saturday late morning brunch. Everything satisfied me, dining atmosphere, friendly waitress, delicious food, classy interior, even good value!!! Must try when you're in town. Shrimp & grits totally recommended!!! The best fit cajun to my taste!

Holy ****

Let me preface this by saying that I was really really not wanting to like this place because our waiter initially seemed too rushed/ and not focused on my table. 

I have eaten at 5 star/ Michelin Star restaurants around the world. Food is my passion. This place is incredible. 

It might be the perfect French 75 that I had to start my meal, but hot damn this would be my last meal on death row. 

The oysters: incredible. 

The "éttoufee" is the actual best thing I've ever eaten in my entire life. When I die, I will haunt this establishment and eat this dish for my eternal being. 

Don't go anywhere else. There's no point. 



I'm dead. I've gone to heaven. The end.

This restaurant was very unexpected. We were walking by and were hungry so we got seated right away even without a reservation. The food was amazing. The best was the Brussel sprouts! Omg! I just can't even begin to tell you how good they were. For my main course I had the fish and it was delicious as well. I would rate the service and quality of food 10 stars if I could! Food is semi pricey but worth the money.
Good raw and fresh oysters. .. bar staff was great... Happy hour prices that you can't beat ....looking foward to future visit to try tower

We were visiting NOLA and came here for my sister's birthday dinner. From the hostess to the waiters, the customer service was superb. But more importantly, the food was delish. Highly recommend the oyster and avocado as an appetizer and the shrimp and grits as an entree. Of course you can't leave without trying the bread pudding. So good!

Great local dive bar! Stopped in while I was working in the area. Folks are friendly. Easy to jump in a conversation. Bartenders are top notch. Very attentive. Never had to wait for a beer. Plenty of tvs for sports. Overall great place. Stop in if you get a chance.

The 50 cents oysters are such a great deal, and the location is convienient. 
I like the mussels and frites also.

Update: This restaurant was truly amazing in remedying an unfortunate situation. I was contacted almost immediately and management was very kind and attentive. They took my issue seriously and that meant a lot to me. My partner and I returned for dinner last night and were truly blown away. The service was excellent, shout out to Shawn and Vusi y'all were amazing.The food and drinks were also amazing. Highly recommend the stuffed oysters, shrimp and roasted jalapeño grits, and steamed chocolate. 


Dining here would be cool maybe if it didn't come with a side of waiters talking about how they would fuck me. Y'all are around a corner, my boyfriend and  I can still hear you assholes.

They now have an excellent happy hour from 4 to 6 where oysters are a quarter and most drinks are half-price. This brings the drinks down to what I would consider a normal price, i.e., I had a glass of beer that was normally $6.50 for $3.25. So if you're in the neighborhood you could definitely pop in just for beer and oysters. Or if you were with someone you could split the 3-course express menu ($23), which is good and more than enough to feed two people.

On the downside they had the air conditioning cranked and I was literally shivering -- make sure you wear a few layers.

Why don't they have any Cosis in LA? For all you sandwich/flatbread lovers, Cosi redefines lunchtime.

What I Ordered: The Cosi Duo. For around $10 you get a half portion of any sandwich on their menu and a small cup of soup. I try to keep it simple when ordering there. Plus, I fell in love with their TBM (Tomato Basil Mozzarella) sandwich. Couple that with a cup of their tomato basil soup, and you have yourself a lunch!

Verdict: There's nothing really to write but praise. It's relatively cheap and tastes phenomenal. What more could you ask? From time to time they feature some special sandwiches, but for starters, try their TBM. Absolutely cannot go wrong with that. Money back guaranteed. Well, not really. But you catch my drift, right?
The service was very good. The food was yummy, but a bit salty. I enjoyed this restaurant and would go again but was no my favorite in New Orleans where there are so many good restaurants!

Breakfast was tasty, but it didn't blow me away. Service was great and atmosphere was attractive, upscale and clean. They lost 2 stars due to price. I felt they were priced for convenience of the hotels rather than trying to be competitive with other restaurants. 

I heard they have a decent happy hour, but after breakfast being so pricey, we didn't go back.

First restaurant that my hubby and I tried in New Orleans on our trip and it was AWESOME.  We arrived without reservation and was told that they don't have any availability for another 1.5-2 hr, but the bar is open seating and we were GLAD that we did.  Walked right up and there was two seats available in front of the oyster shuckers.  Order some oysters and also the Chappapeela Pork Schnitzel. Oysters were fresh and sooooo good, the pork schnitzel with wild mushroom sauce was great. Excellent service, had a great time talking to the oyster shuckers :) Definitely would visit again and would recommend sitting at the bar area !

Horrible experience.  Will never go back.  I've never experienced such a rude waiter in my entire life.  Was visiting New Orleans with my boyfriend and made a reservation at Luke based on a friend who is a local.  She suggested I we go to Luke for his birthday dinner.  Upon being seated, the waiter came by and rudely asked what we wanted to drink.  At first I wasn't sure if I was being sensitive but no, he acted like we were inconveniencing him.  I watched him as he went from table to table and he continued to show this attitude.  I couldn't believe it.  We ordered appetizers and again with the lackadaisical "what do you want" attitude.  I was pissed.  My boyfriend, on his birthday ended up going to talk to the manager because I would have laid into them. What makes it worse is that everyone knew it was his birthday. I called specifically to let them know. Well needless to say, after the appetizers, I was too upset to stay.  We left and I'll never go back there again. That guy should not be working there. Complete disappointment!!

Best sushi in the area hands down. Very fresh fish, great service, and the decor is perfect! The miso soup is awesome (best broth ever), beef carpaccio is out of this world with that sauce, and the sushi/sashimi is always prepared beautifully every single time. I make it a priority to go here at least once a week, completely worth the 30 minute drive.

Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp En Cocotte. It's roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille and green onion sausages, and HUGE shrimp in an iron skillet.

In Los Angeles, you go to Animal, and get the pork belly sliders. In San Francisco, you track and find the Señor Sisig burrito truck. In San Diego, you have brunch at Hash House.

And in New Orleans, you damned well better go to Lüke and have the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp En Cocotte. And make your friends order it too, and steal a few of their shrimp. And then get one to go.

Seriously the best seafood dish in the city. State. Country. World?

Outstanding Oktoberfest menu. Great value for money as well as splendid beers to compliment the four course dinner. My wife ordered half dozen oysters on the half shell; they were fresh and delicious.

Highly recommended.

Had breakfast.  Average french press coffee, wife got yogurt and granola which was overpriced for $12. I got the egg white fritata which was excellent.  Overall I would want to come back but restaurant was average on this visit.

Our party ate here twice.  We went to happy hour with half prices drinks and 50 cent oysters.  Best oysters and cocktails I got the whole trip.  Sazeracs were made well, with good rye and my friend got some extra, a pretty large one.  We did also get the chicken with vegetables and they split it into two portions, each in its own iron container pan.  Classy.  You also get bread with your meal and won't go hungry. Good staff too. Some of them are funny and from the North.  It is also cool to sit towards the kitchen and watch them prepare food in the big windows.

I took two girlfriends, visiting from California, here last night based on the high percentage of good reviews. 

First of all, even though a dinner reservation had been made, we were banished to the very VERY back room, passed the first back room, to the absolute most desolate corner table in the restaurant. In said desolate- corner-table-restaurant-abyss, there was no music, no boisterous laughing, and no clinking of glasses and silverware as one would expect from a popular restaurant. Instead, it was just us three and the awkward table of three men seated next to us. 

I realize this is not really grounds for a one star review. So let me tell you about the service and the food. Our waiter (who took at least 10 minutes to get us a glass of water) forgot our beer order three times. He asked us twice what we had ordered, then brought the wrong beer on his third trip to our table. He did have a small green order pad in his hand, that he apparently forgot about as well. Writing down the drink order could have saved us all a lot of time. 

I ordered the daily gulf fish special, which was nothing special at all. Just fried fish atop three brussel sprouts and a few small potatoes. One friend ordered the duck confit and white bean cassoulet. I did not try it, but it was basically an entire sausage and duck leg atop very dry and very salty white beans and bread crumbs. She only ate about three bites (which went unnoticed by our waiter). Friend #2 ordered the steak and frites which was the one somewhat redeeming part of the meal. It was cooked rare (to her liking) so at least the dinner wasn't a total bust. 

Perhaps my expectations were too high. 

Bottom line: Go to COCHON skip Luke.

Since coming to Boise, this is pretty much the place we shop mostly with anything outdoors! From camping, hiking, biking, snow/ski etc! They carry high end, great quality stuff that's why it's a bit pricey! It's great to have a membership though coz you get some special discount every now & then plus they have seasonal garage sales!

On our last day in New Orleans, we wanted to treat Russell's mom to an awesome brunch. There were tons of options, but we settled on Lüke and were quite happy that we did.

On a Sunday afternoon, we were surprised that there was not a long wait to eat here, and there was in fact quite a bit of seating available. We were greeted by a very pleasant waiter, who took our drink order. Coffee was great, as was the Champagne au Peche (which was very light and refreshing).

I ordered the Eggs in a Jar, Rusty got the Omelet of Local Crab and his mom got the Shrimp & Grits. We also started the meal with some delicious fresh oysters. Everything was quite good. My Eggs in Jar was probably the cutest meal ever, served with soft eggs, grits, and about a half dozen shrimp sitting on the rim of the jar. I was so full after eating about half of this that Rusty had to finish it for me. His omelet was full of big lumps of crab meat, it was very tasty. The Shrimp & Grits, which had a much more "cajun" taste than my meal was also very good. I'd recommend any of these, but the shrimp dishes were definitely my favorite. 

The oysters were so good, that we ended up ordering another round. We also tried the the bread pudding which was so so good. Don't forget to dip it in the caramel sauce served on the plate. My next mission in life is to make bread pudding that is this good!

A great meal, a little bit on the pricier side, but definitely worth it.

Took a gamble on trying a new place, especially since my grandma's lived here for over 40 years and doesn't like sushi. (I'm the sushi lover).

Let me tell you...you will NOT be disappointed! The service was exceptional from the moment we walked in. Everyone was friendly. It looks unimpressive from the outside but the place is quaint and trendy inside. We were seated right at our reservation time. 

I ordered the Szechuan chili seafood miso soup, a Philadelphia roll and a spicy crispy tuna roll. The Szechuan chili seafood miso soup was EXCELLENT. It's VERY spicy, but can be made mild if asked. Both sushi rolls were fresh and had the perfect amount of ginger and wasabi on the side. My dad got the mild version of the soup and loved it. He also ordered chicken udon noodle (soup) which came with a side of vegetable tempura. He said his meal was also excellent. My grandma is a tough crowd pleaser. She's the first to tell you when something needs to improve. She got the ginger dressing salad and Yaki mushroom noodle and had ZERO complaints. 

Our server personalized our experience by coming to check on us and asking if I liked my Philadelphia roll. Another server came by and asked my dad if his soup was too spicy or mild enough instead of the "how is everything?" After dinner they serve a complimentary bowl of fruit with oranges and pineapple wedges. 

Our server was awesome. I didn't catch her name but she wore glasses. She was very attentive to all of us. Again, my grandma was even impressed! My dad and I were already talking about coming back here on our way home want to come this Sunday!

I had never heard of Luke before until a couple weekends ago my fiance proposed, then surprised me again right after with a weekend trip to New Orleans to celebrate, and had made reservations at Luke's to end the weekend with a bang! 
I am so glad my fiance found this place. It was wonderful. We are both originally from the East Coast, now in the Midwest, so we have never really experienced cajun food before done right. After our dinner here, we are now huge fans! So many flavors and too many choices to leave hungry. I think between my fiance and I we ordered plenty, but every dish that came out and went to a different table we were wide eyed and asking "Whats thatttt", drool and all. 
Hopefully we will be back here soon and can try the rest of the menu. The service is also extremely friendly and they make sure to take their time with explaining the dishes and making you feel comfortable.

Everything about this place is great! Upon the waitress' suggestion, we all ordered the Shrimp and Grits and had the pleasant surprise of crab on top. It was the bomb. Like seriously, best first meal in New Orleans. Service was great, ambiance was great, food was great. Highly recommend this place!

Fine dining with its hair down--superb, though I could do with two fewer dots over the u. The service is fun and rowdy and attentive and knowledgeable, the food is delicate (rabbit pate with pickled watermelon) or unrefined (crab ravioli), the decor's bar-ish, a little rough around the edges and overlit, but it's bustling and delicious and pleasant. I'd come back over and over if I could. Spend a lot or a little: $11 for a croque monsieur or $85 for a fruits de mer platter.

If you're not from New Orleans watch out for the oysters, they're weirdly saltless, I always avoid them.

This is one of those situations where it's probably best that I didn't pop in here with a dining companion...one who no doubt would have had to listen to a semi-tragic rendering of ill-advised Star Wars verses. It's a cool restaurant, though. 

I wandered in during the first half of the first pre-season game the Saints have played since winning the Super Bowl last year, and that must have had some impact on the crowd, as the room was busy but not overly so: the bartenders chatted casually with one another behind the counter as I bellied up, ordered a Schneider Weiss and Steak Frites and settled in. 

My food hit the spot in front of me in a reasonable period of time, and as I'd been too busy to eat well that day, just in time. The service wasn't the friendliest I encountered in the city, but the food was spot on. When you're craving some French Food, you could definitely do worse than here.

The sushi was excellently prepared, they have perfected the spice so the flavors come through of the meal and the flavor isn't overwhelmed by spice! The rolls we had were #7 volcano, Crazy Tuna and angry dragon! We also had the Spicy Tuna which was delicious! The quantity and flavor were amazing! The kids got the sesame chicken bento boxes and they go so much food!! They ate everything! I can't wait to come back! The staff made the kids feel so special they catered to them and brought them Lollipops and special ice cream
Bowls!
Would say the sushi is only average. Prices are a bit high for  some rolls. The sushi "chef" that was working when I ordered hardly spoke & came off as rude. I won't be back.

Came here for happy hour with a group of 9. Were sat within about half hour. I had the fried oysters that were great! I also tried the raw oysters and the burger and fries. Everything I tried was fabulous. I would definitely go back.

Amazing food at Lüke! This was one of the best restaurants that we ate at in New Orleans. I know, even better than Commander's Palace. I made a reservation via Opentable and were seated instantly. We sat in the back of the restaurant with a view of the kitchen. It was very cool to see the chefs in action. 

The food was awesome! We used the warm bread to soak up extra sauces from our entrees . I ordered the Aile de Raie ($22) which was a parmesan crusted skate wing, Meyer lemon caper buerre blanc, and roasted veggies. WOW! The crust was perfect and the fish was not salty. The sauce was so beautiful with the fish. Loved the variety of roasted veggies - brussels sprouts, baby carrots, and turnips

My husband had the Etouffe of Blue Crab & Brown Shrimp with fennel, garlic, saffron fumet garganelli pasta ($26). Oh goodness. This was the star entrée of the night! The sauce was so delicious with the creaminess from the blue crab and spiciness. Yum! The homemade pasta was also a real treat. The blue crab was fresh, and the four shrimps were juicy. This was a small pasta dish, but had hearty, rich flavors.

One thing that the restaurant should improve on is the service. Our waiter didn't stop by our table too much. He hung around near the kitchen area chatting with the other waiters as they were waiting for the prepared food.

I highly recommend this place!

Clean bland puffy food
It's all right when it's late night
and you have no choice

I was seriously disappointed with the quality of food and service at this location. The waiter didn't tell us about the happy hour specials and we had to wait 20-30 minutes for them to pack our left over food and get a check. 

My gf tried shrimp with grits which was good but not worth $24. Crab bisque was the main highlight. My burger was alright, nothing to separate it from a Chillis burger and fires were stale. 

Overall, this is a very pricy place ($$$) with a very mediocre quality food and service. They do have happy hour but they won't tell u about it. I'm not sure why are there so many positive reviews, I think u can do lot better at other places.

The service is horrible here.  This was the second restaurant that my friends and I went to in NOLA, so we weren't sure if that was just how the service was in NOLA, but after being to a few other places later on, we found out that the servers here were just plain rude.  

I admit we had a big group, but it took us literally half an hour before we could order and another hour before we got our food.  Whenever we asked the servers for anything, we'd have to ask them multiple times, before we finally got it.  This wouldn't have been a bad thing if what we were asking for was salt and pepper or tabasco, but we needed utensils  or it wouldn't have been so bad if they didn't come around once every 30 minutes.  Worse, one of the servers spilled a drink on my friend and didn't even come back with any towels or anything.  He just came back with another drink 15 minutes later.  These are really the type of places that annoy me, when they put an automatic gratuity for tables larger than 6.  If the server only checks on you 2 times during the course of your meal, you shouldn't be forced to pay over a $100 tip.

Anyway, I will also admit the food was pretty good.  I'm not sure if it was because we were all at the point of starvation at the time, but it was good.

If you plan to go, try going with a smaller group, I don't know if that will help at all, but I figure it couldn't hurt.

Cosi makes yummy salads with quality mixed greens and flavorful dressings that are to die for.  Unfortunately, that's pretty much where the positives end.  This location is notorious for 2 kinds of servers:  totally inattentive and witheringly nasty.  Maybe it's something in the water; maybe this property sits on top of an ancient burial ground & the spirits haunt the Cosi workers, who then take out their anger on the public.  I've been coming to this place since it was a Xando & nothing's changed.

Something that has changed is serving sizes at Cosi.  It seems like the portions of meat you get on sandwiches are exponentially decreasing.  We all know that Cosi's price point is a little higher than Wendy's.  When we walk in the door, we accept that a sandwich will cost $8.  However, when you pay $8 for a sandwich, it better have some meat on it.  

Adding insult to injury is the fact that the staff's ability to manage high customer volume is a total crap shoot.  On some days the system works.  On other days you end up waiting in agony for 1 of the workers milling about to decide to come stand at the register and ring up your stuff.

We were in New Orleans over the weekend of April 20-22 and ate at Luke that Friday, hoping to get a great introduction to New Orleans French cooking from a master chef and New Orleans institution, John Besh. Unfortunately, this place failed to live up to the expectations I had in terms of food and service. 

Our waiter was clearly uninterested in our table of 2 and saw us twice, once to take our food and drink order and once to drop off our check. All other interactions with staff went through runners or bus boys who dropped off drinks/food. We also went to NOLA while we were in town and John could learn a thing or two from Emeril in terms of good customer service and wait staff expectations.

On to the food, we were just unimpressed. They oysters were just ok, we had far better at multiple spots in the city. While they were large, they were also muddy tasting and not firm, juicy, and plump. They gumbo was boring. The shrimp and grits were just ok.

With so many great places to eat in New Orleans, we definitely won't be back.

Best restaurant I ate at in NOLA-  and great service! A great staff that worked as a team to ensure I had a great experience. Shawn was an excellent server who gave great suggestions on the food. Had an amazing steak and the oysters were as big as my hand! Great selection of craft cocktails as well. Call for reservations because it gets busy.
招牌沙拉就是生菜叶拌咸味沙拉酱，星期四特供的炒饭就是剩饭炒饭，绿洋葱香肠的味道实在不敢恭维，法式面包夹火腿奶酪腻到塞牙，整体也冷冰冰的，薯条和家里做的味道差不多。唯一觉得还可以的就是马芬，虽然上面漂了两片猪油糟，略微诡异。

Best shrimp and grits I've ever had.  On our first visit we did to-go and brought the food back to the hotel room (the Hilton connected).  Eating Luke's food in bed in front of the TV after a long day on the road was one of the highlights of our trip.

The only reason this is not a 5 star review is because on our second trip they didn't cook my wife's burger correctly.  She ordered medium.  The center was perfect but the edges were raw in the middle.  We sent it back and the 2nd burger was exactly the same.  Honestly, I'm curious how they cook the burgers to get the center more cooked than the edges.

I have nothing but praise for the flavor of the food.  It's just pure deliciousness.
Came here for brunch. The food was rich and very tasty. They have a great cocktail menu and our waiter was really pleasant. He gave excellent recommendations. Will go back for dinner soon.

Now that we've had our reception, I can wholeheartedly recommend Luke for your private dining needs.  The staff, from the back of house to the hostess, treated us like royalty from the moment we walked in.  We had just enough time between courses for our meal to feel leisurely, neither rushed nor slow.  At the end of the meal my husband and I were served champagne, compliments of the kitchen, and it just about brought a tear to my eye.

I was offered the option to have the credit card on file run for the meal, so I didn't have to deal with payment on the day of.  On Monday I received an email from the catering director saying they weren't able to run my card on Saturday but didn't want to bother me during my reception.  She asked me to call her at my convenience with the correct number.  I called right away, horrified that it hadn't been charged yet, because I don't like to feel like even a little bit of a deadbeat, but Luke's staff was very laid-back about the whole affair.  It turns out she'd misread one of the numbers, and they ran the correct number without any fuss.  I really appreciated the discretion and calm approach.

All of our guests were raving about the food and my dad was telling everyone "Danielle really went over her budget for this"...I'll just let it be my secret that in the end I was actually under budget and very happy when I finally checked my credit card statement.  Luke gave us an incredible wedding day experience, in no small part to their fantastic staff, and I look forward to many more visits in our future to bring back those happy memories.

Went there for lunch during our 'Sugar Bowl' trip to New Orleans.  I have the PEI mussels and fries.  Mussels were small but they gave me so many I got over that.  Husband had the burger (gigantic - have an appetite).  A great last-minute decision.

This place lives up to it's name. We had friends that had been to New Orleans a few months before us and and told us to go to this place. It was already on my list though being a hard core foodie person, I had already pretty much researched where I was going to go in town. 

Luke was something else. It was packed when we got there but we were lucky to get a place at the bar. It was Happy Hour. Bf had the crayfish boil, I had the crab Maison with the breads and some of the Matzo ball soup. Loved the guys at the Oyster bar, they were too much. We made a couple of friends I hope to see again in on the next visit. 

This was ultimately one of my favorite stops and we were lucky to be able to get in. I was almost scared we wouldn't be able to with the days coming to a close on our visit. 

It is definitely worth the stop and  the food is outstanding. I wanted to go again, just didn't have the time. Next time. On the way out BF talked to the managers or owners? Who were also completely hospitable. This restaurant is what this town is about.. It's a feel good at the end of the day kind of place. I can see why people flock to it!  The ambiance, the food everything is New Orleans style!!

Great neighborhood hole-in-the wall cafe. Coffee sourced from Vancouver's Forty Ninth Parallel Coffee Roasters. Daily selections of crafty sammies for breakfast and lunch. Tastes thoughtful, ingredients are fresh, really delightful. Nice people watching if you can grab a spot on the patio or at the teeny bar inside. What a great addition to the area. Really brightens up a particularly drab section of Jasper.

Fried Oysters are the bomb! I've never enjoyed oysters to be honest! :/ 

Brussels sprouts were pretty good too, the drinks for happy hour are to die for absolutely delicious. Got hammered here. We also tries fried goat cheese stuffed blossoms, it was bursting deliciousness in my mouth!!

Stayed at Hilton and stopped in. Not your regular attached restaurant. Place is legit. 

We had the crab au gratin, salad w chicken, and the shrimp and grits.
