Best oysters we'd ever had, and for 50cents...our minds were blown. Creamy, non fishy, perfect, smooth oysters. What made Luke even better for us was our lovely waitress, and our very friendly oyster shucker, Calvin. An incredibly kind guy, really fun to talk to, attentive, and he even brought us a delicious bread pudding with b-day candle and sung me happy birthday after we mentioned we were in New Orleans for my b day. I would recommend Luke to anyone 100 times over, and I'd visit Luke  100 times over again. Thanks Luke, and Calvin for making our last few hours in Nola memorable and awesome.

Came here with my family & were told it would be an hour wait, but honestly we only waited like 30 minutes. We were starving so we really appreciated the fast service. We ordered the small seafood tower, stuffed P&J oysters, the rabbit/chicken pate, the crawfish bisque, motzo ball soup, crawfish etouffee, moules et Frites & shrimp and grits.

The seafood tower was great, everything was fresh and my whole family enjoyed it. The stuffed P&J oysters were also delicious, nothing like the charbroiled oysters elsewhere, but definitely still so good. The crawfish bisque was creamy and hot, very satisfying. I would probably pass on the motzo ball soup though. The crawfish etouffee was full of flavor and had a great crunch texture to it. My personal favorite were the mussels. It was served piping hot in a spicy broth. After the mussels have been eaten my family used the bread given to dip it in the soup and eat it all up. I've had pate, but never rabbit pate, I was a little hesitant to try, but it was great paired with all the sauces.  I loved everything at this restaurant and the service was amazing. I recommend anyone to try this place!

As we were visiting NOLA for the first time we wanted to have a great dining experience. Luke's was sadly lacking. The menu was not interesting or innovative.
The dinner arrived cold and the server was too busy to check in with us. If you plan on The best part of our meal was the outstanding Oysters, which were Kumoto and from the west coast. We should have saved our money for dining in San Francisco.

Do not recommend this place for a great dining experience.

I'm going to say upfront that I usually like Cosi's food (depending on what I order), and that my main problem with this particular Cosi is the service. Today, for example, the oven they use to toast the sandwiches and pizzas on stopped working, so they had to switch to another one, which took some time to heat up. I've worked in food service, I understand these things happen. What I was not happy about was that even after the manager assured us we'd have our food shortly, and me waiting 25 minutes from when I walked in the shop, I find out that my sandwich was never even made. How, I'm not sure, as the employee that took my order filled out an order slip. Perhaps someone else grabbed it, but whatever the case is, I was on my lunch break, and I ended up spending 35 minutes just getting food to-go. Their employees on the whole tend to be unfriendly and sometimes rude. I've seen some stick their hands in the food bar and eat in front of customers, and then continue making food with the same pair of gloves. I really wish that they could get their service together, because it's in a convenient location and is relatively affordable on a college student's budget.

This place is excellent across the board! The food was 5 star and the portions very generous. We had the Lüke Breakfast. Best grits, eggs and bacon I have ever tasted. The bisque and gumbo are excellent too. The wine selection was excellent. Melanie our waitress was 5 Star. She demonstrated the art of customer service. She was professional, warm and gracious. Before we even had to ask for refills or accommodations she was tending to our table. The restaurant is classy and clean. I will definitely return every time I am in NOLA.
Ugh!   When one server asks you if you want to wait for fresh fajita veggies & another server slaps the tiny bit that's left in the container in your bowl.  Super rude & disappointing.

Hat's in the air for ole Luke's!!!

Classy, Cool, and just plain undeniably good.

Let's just get this out the way now... to date, the best French 75 I've had... such a perfect balance and now I'm going to be thinking of it til my next fix. Another drink that has a 20yr balsamic vinaigrette in yet was great as well, matter of fact.. Props to the bartender who did a fantastic job... she killed it.

The complimentary bread seemed just too plain, no score there but let's get on with the dish... the Roasted chicken entree... tender as hell and the potatoes were a perfect compliment.
Although there were much chicken dishes, that's really the staple in Louisiana but this is a easy go back to and your stomach will appreciate you after.

Easily seeking a return bout!
Excellent happy hour prices...oysters for .50 each!!!  Dinner prices a little pricey I had the shrimp & jalapeño grits....delicious!!! Would return!!!

Best restaurant experience we had in New Orleans. We went for happy hour and had an amazing meal. Definitely try the 75 cent oysters, shrimp and grits, and brussel sprouts. The best thing was honestly the service. Gary was an exceptional server. My girlfriend and I have been in the hospitality industry for 15 years and have never received better service at a restaurant. A++!!!

Visiting from California and Miami I can say this was one amazing restaurant!!!!  Food coma.  I was so pleasantly surprised!  Party of 8 came in and expected to eat at bar but luckily a table was closing out.  We ordered a few plates of oysters and the horseradish was so hot I couldn't stop smearing it on everything.  The homemade bread and dipped in steamer wine sauce that was out of this world.  Our first bottle of wine we ordered wasn't good and without hesitation Robert (the best waiter from Chicago) went and got a second bottle of the a different wine.  French fries were amazing.  We got a lot of everything to share and I was full by the end.  
Our waiter was so animated and made the 50th birthday dinner a fun fete!  Bravo !!!!! I usually shy away from celebrity chefs restaurants, but this was exceptionally delicious.  I would highly recommend
Really enjoyed our evening, the service was fabulous-the right amount of friendly and attention without being overbearing. Everything we ate was a treat, particularly the pate.

Went here on a recommendation and the food did not disappoint.  Shrimp with grits were excellent and the swordfish was wonderful.  P&J oysters were good but thought three per order is too small for the price.   The place is a little loud, the atmosphere promises to be high end but really comes off as more cheap. The bench seat was dirty. The waiter didn't smile or have any sense of humor. He was nice but learn to smile and act like you enjoy being a server.  I think this place is past its prime without some cleaning up of the staffs attitude and a little more polish.   Think of red lobster with coat and tie.  Food is good but the atmosphere lacks and that is half the experience.   

We may go back for the food since it was good but don't expect huge wait staff miracles.   Also go a little earlier like 6 pm and you can pick just about any seat in the  house.  Bon apetite
Best oysters and seafood dishes in my life ! If you are a seafood fan come to the happy hpur for $.50 oysters special.  Love that fresh gulf oysters and shrimp.

I look for every excuse I can to get a cuppa from Elm Cafe - it's actually worth the $3.50 for a large cup of brewed coffee and I like how you can sweeten it with simple syrup. The sandwiches are always an adventure as well - lots of unique flavours and always changing.

Had lunch with a friend.  The Shrimp & Grits very good.  The Cochon de lait sandwich was Delicious!  Stuffed shrimp & veggies, good.  It was a great lunch.

Only one thing disenchanted me.  The waiter was good but not very friendly.  He handed me my straw with his hands on the straw where you put your mouth,  :(

Perhaps the best coffee in Edmonton.  I go out of my way on weekends to get my caffeine here.

The menu includes 2 options for breakfast, 2 sandwiches for lunch plus soup and muffins.  I've tried a few of the sandwiches and a muffin, and now get Elm-sandwich cravings.

Parking is limited, but on weekends you can take your chances in the private lot adjacent to the building.  Worth it.


Seating is also limited to a few spots on the window bar, and a couple tables outside.  Eat in your car, hang on the patio in the sun or take it home if there isn't a spot for you, the food is terrific.

This is one of my favourite places.

We went there around 9 pm on Saturday without reservation. We stopped at this restaurant on the way back to our hotel. I ordered seafood gumbo, which was tasty, maybe a bit salty, and it didn't have any seafood in it except some shrimp. The service was awful. Once we were seated, nobody came to our table except taking our order and delivering out food. Other tables were getting all the attentions. I don't know whether we didn't order expensive food, or we arrived late, or we dressed casually. But we were complete ignored. I can see that their food is good, but I don't think I want to come back to this place again.

I HIIIIIGHLY recommend this place. I had the best experience and the YUMMMIEST food! OMG, the FOOD! Before I go on talking about what food I ordered, I would love to point out that the service here AMAAAZING! They are very accommodating and sweet. 

Our waiter was MATT! He is freakin AWESOME and probably the best waiter we have ever gotten! Definitely my top 3! I hope you get seated in his section! We had trouble ordering from the menu because everything looked so yummy! He helped out a lot with our food selection, especially the BREAD PUDDING! Best decision we've ever made! I would definitely come back to this restaurant!

We ordered:

A dozen P & J Oysters (which are also on their happy hour menu!) - VERY YUMMY

Croque Madam - Very Toasty bread and runny yolk that complimented the entire meal. Eat it while it's still warm! Don't take too long taking pictures of your food ;) haha just playin.. And the fries! Ohh my looooord, I finished mine and had more of my friend's! Haha 

Bloody Marys - They were nicely spiced! We had a few of these c(: And I looove how their pickles are string beans! Or so that's what they looked like

BREAD PUDDING & VANILLA BEAN ICE CREAM! - I don't usually like bread pudding and have given it a try quite a few times just incase it was actually good. I'm glad I gave it a try again this time since Louisiana is known for their bread pudding. And let me tell you.. if you are to ever have bread pudding, go to LUKES! LUKE's has the BEST BREAD PUDDING IN THE WORLD!!! In the WOOOOORLD!!  You will not regret it. You will actually fall in loooove :D The pudding was nice and candied on the top. The pecans are perfectly toasted and drizzled generously on top. Get this bread pudding with Vanilla bean ice cream. PERFECT COMBO! I ate as much as i can. I might not be able to have another bomb ass bread pudding like this one again. 

BREAD PUDDING & MATT ALL DAY!! :D

It's our first night in New Orleans, the flight was average, American Airlines sucks. But that won't dampen our spirits, were going to partake in a food orgy over the next several days. I've been researching restaurants over the last few weeks and will begin our journey at Luke. So we start our order for dinner with a few appetizers. 

Absinthe Frappe - Obsello and Peychaud's bitters over ice, wow that's a strong drink. It's got a licorice taste to it. I gonna stick with vodka from now on. On to the appetizers 

1.) Raw oysters (P&J, Komomotos, and locals) delicious and fresh served on a tray of crushed ice. These morsels are sweet and meaty. And with a spicy cocktail sauce delicious. 
2.) Mussels steamed were good but on the small size, not as meaty as I would of liked. 
3.) Clams steamed in a nice sauce, but again on the small size, barely got the clam taste after one bite and done. 
4.) Gumbo that had a rich and flavorful rue, oh that was GOOD... 
5.) Assiette de charcuterie, for the less sophisticated a plate of pate, sliced sausage, and other delicious meats. A country bread crispy toasted, and sliced thin like a cracker. Wonderful flavors and textures to the pates. The hogs head cheese was spectacular. And the grainy mustard's and pickles, together on the bread just exploded in your mouth. 
6.) Flamenkuche you ask? No this isn't a foul word its a pork belly pizza with sauteed onions and some damn delicious sauce. And it's served on a flat crispy pizza cracker. Oh my god this kicks ASS. 
Moving on to the salads we start to feel a bit full, but that won't stop us yet. 

Salad Luke was concocted of bibb lettuce, cucumbers, beets, and a buttermilk dressing. Very tasty and fresh. 
Roasted beet salad was just that delicious beets with toasted pistachios. I really enjoyed the crunch with the beets, nice offset. 

Everything we ordered turned out great, and the service was excellent. They times our orders so that we had plenty of room on the table. Very nice and professional. Can't wait to go back and try there entrees.

The chefs are fantastic.   The staff was very friendly and attentive.  The decor was interesting.  Check out the oysters and artwork.   The prices were reasonable.   I have gone with girlfriends during lunch and happy hour.   Great food.    You should try one of everything to see what you love.

Mixed review here. We ate with a group of 10. Service was awesome. Most of the food was incredible. The shrimp etouffee had enough salt to turn the Great Lakes into oceans. The grits and Flammkuchen was to-die-for good. Creamy grits. Giant burgers. Oysters fine.

We came here for dinner since it was close to our hotel. When we got there we just missed the tail end of HH which is 3-6pm .75 oysters! So sad we missed it. So we ordered three things off the menu ans everything was delicious! Flammenkuchen which is sort of like a flat bred pizza with lots of cheese and fatty pieces of bacon! And the ribeye with fries which was so flavorful and delicious! We finished off the meal with their famous bread pudding which did not disappoint.. Definitely a place to go if you are arouns the business area of NOLA @missericayvette

Ended up here on a whim after our first choice proved to be in a sketchy part of town (it was an attempt to eat where the locals eat). We were not disappointed in our choice. We started with the gumbo and it was amazing. You can really taste the fresh ingredients. Next we had the oyster avocado salad and the shrimp and grits as our entree. Again can't say enough about the fresh ingredients and the shrimp tasted as if it just came off the boat. We didn't try the desert but our table mates next to us did and they enjoyed the bread putting. Definitely would go back no eat there again.  Make reservations if you can, we didn't but you should.

We stopped in last night and were seated at a table that backed up to the bar. If you were sitting in the chairs with your back to the bar you constantly had people bustling by you & got whacked a time or two. It felt more like a busy diner sitting where we were. We ordered the eggplant sticks as an app. I liked the breading but didn't have much flavor to it. Marinara sauce was like water and no flavor. I wouldn't order this again. Portion was definitely shareable. It was just blah overall. I had the tuna rare and it was delicious!! I would definitely order that again. My husband had the lamb and the pasta that is served with it is delicious. He said it was good but nothing to write home about and my tuna was definitely better. Our waitress, didn't even know her name and was underwhelmed by her. I felt we were more of an inconvenience than her wanting to help. My husband asked her about a drink on the menu and she was like um and shrugged her shoulder and said I don't really like it. Never recommended anything so he didn't get a drink. We live here and there are so many good restaurants we truly enjoy. So, it wasn't a bad experience but wouldn't rush back here.

Was there as part of a bachelor party this past weekend. At first glance, the private room they put us in seemed pretty great, even though there was no house music on. 

Now, granted we were a group of 12. I probably wouldn't be suited for the job. Unfortunately, I don't think our waiter was either. The menu was a little all over the place and it took us all about 20 minutes just to collect our thoughts and figure out what to order. Waiter came in and was a little unfriendly at first, then pretty much seemed to have no concern for explaining too much. He said we saw the special listed outside, which we had not, but went with it anyway. We also ordered drinks, a few plates of pate and the seafood tower for the table. 

Drinks took forever. I'm talking 20+ minutes, maybe more. Not good. Then, the apps came, but no seafood tower. Finally it arrived, close to an hour after we got there. The quality was very good, I must say. Pretty much first-rate. What was the absolute best was the pate. We had the charcuterie sampler and the Louisiana rabbit pate. Both were astounding and a culinary highlight of our trip. Also, the escargots were good.

I ordered the shrimp and grits and it was pretty good. By the end of the night, our waiter had loosened up a little bit but I think the dining experience fell a little short of our expectations.

Randomly came here with a friend one night because there was no other place to go to for dinner, and Luke closes quite late. Will be judging this restaurant a little more critically based on its standards and because it's a John Besh restaurant. 

Good service, the waiter was super nice and attentive so that's a plus. However, I do not know if he was just being honest about his opinions or he was trying to rack up the bill so he'll get a higher tip, but everything our waiter recommended was at the top of the list in terms of pricing, and after we were done, like done done, he kept on pushing us to get some more food and drinks. 

We had the fresh gulf drum and the Washington Parish roasted chicken for entrees. The fresh gulf drum was pan fried I believed, but it was topped off with sweet and well-seasoned veggies. Despite the veggies, the dish itself was quite bland. The roasted chicken was even more bland. Quite dry, and the veggies were less flavorful than the ones on the gulf drum. 

The only reason why I am giving this place a 4 instead of a 3 star rating is because, before this review, I came here and tried the grilled pork chop and soft shell crab dish, and the food were superb. That night I could have easily given this place a 5 star. Would definitely come back here, just because I think this night was a rare phenomenon, or that I could just have ordered the wrong dishes.

We went to Felix, oceana grill, acme, royal house, and basically all the 4 star and above seafood places on yelp, but nothing compared to the oysters at Luke.

Also if the other "specials of the day" are as good as the Monday fried chicken special, then GO FOR IT. We were amazed by how moist the chicken was and how it still managed to pack so much flavor. Portions are big and although it's a tad pricier than some other NOLA brunch places, it's well worth it!

Pretty good burgers, sometimes a little overdone. Good fries.

My husband loves the gumbo.

Everything else is ok.

Bc it is in the CBD, it can be a pain to park at.

And it's pretty expensive. Burger and fries will run about $16.

What a tiny little cafe! Seriously this place looks like it's from NYC because that's how small it is! You have to be careful when driving by or you might miss it! I opted for a lovely tea latte on a rainy day and it was delicious and warmed me right up! They have such a lovely variety of fresh food I wish I would have been hungry when I stopped by because I've only heard good things in regards to their sandwiches! 

I only wish Elm were bigger so that more people could enjoy such a marvellous thing. We ended up sitting outside but the rain came back so we had to take our coffee to go. They also seem to have local/fair trade coffee beans for sale which is always a bonus! I definitely cannot wait to come back and enjoy more of this place!

Awful.
I ordered a bowl of muscles. More than half were undercooked. including the ones that were open. They also weren't properly cleaned and the entire bowl was grainy. Only reason it deserves a star is because of the fries.

Everyone who visits New Orleans comes away with a story... well here is ours.

After a couple of really hot days and with only one dinner left before traveling back home to Memphis, my wife and I decided to try Luke being fans of the chef and it coming highly recommended from friends and others who had visited the area. Upon being seated towards the front of the dining space on a two top next to two other couples we began trying to navigate the menu and how to narrow down all of the delicious offerings. As wise shopper should, we looked to our left and right to see what everyone had ordered and see if we should do the same.

We noticed one couple next to us had decided to share the ribeye/steak. Unfortunately they were upset about how medium rare, their medium steak turned out and called for the waiter to complain. To our immediate dismay the gentleman decided to let the waiter have it even though the wait staff immediately apologized and quickly removed the steak to make it right. After the gentleman asked for the manager my wife looked at me and quietly said, "Do you think they are trying to get a free meal?" I dismissed it, but was wrong as the man immediately told his date that he felt the reason the steak was undercooked and not to his liking was because... (ready for this)... he was gay. His date replied, "Do they even know you're gay?" My thoughts exactly. 

Once the manager approached the gentleman asked to speak to him away from the table and let him have it explaining how his steak was undercooked and how somehow his sexual preference must be involved. I'll be honest, it made me sick to watch it all unfold. 

The manager of course helped calm the situation and replaced his waiter with another team (by the way, it turns our his original waiter was gay too) but this man didn't care and felt the restaurant owed him something. Luke bent over backwards to help this man enjoy his dinner and in the end comp'ed his meal - entire meal, wine, steaks, etc. 

My review here is to compliment the manager Derrick and the servers Gary and Tristian on how professionally they managed a challenging situation. I hated to see it all unfold especially with such circumstances, but had to tell the tale that we took home with us.

If you're looking to be treated well and enjoy a delightful meal, Luke is a excellent option. My wife and I share the burger and loved the bisque, oyster salads and special cocktails. Dessert was delightful and thanks to the amazing front house team we will return and tell others our tale while encouraging others to put Luke on your New Orleans must visit list. From all of the reviews here, I think my next visit will be during happy hour!

I needed to get my oil changed and found out it was going to be over an hour wait at the dealership.  So I stopped by this particular jiffy lube and Frankie took care of my oil change in less than 15 minutes.  

I thought she was just calling me up to the service desk to pay, but she handed me my keys and said, "you're all finished!"

I almost didn't want to write this because I feel like this location is Tucson's best kept secret for a fast oil change, but Frankie and her team deserve the credit!  Amazing work, keep it up!

So f'in good, I dined here three days in a row.
(1 dinner, 1 lunch, 1 breakfast)

The food and the caliber of talent in the kitchen speaks for itself. 
Great bar
Great staff

Honestly, I didn't think it was going to be any good.
#1. It's a hotel restaurant. Uh-oh, I thought. 
#2 It's a celebrity chef restaurant. Usually spells trouble, but they haven't screwed it up yet. They've started cloning it all over the place though. 

The flammenkuche was a favorite. The other items were all specials. Here today- fleeting memories. 

Dessert? Yes. Save room. 

The room is a little hard and a little cold, but not deafening. The second dining room is a little more intimate.

A friend of mine recommended Luke to me and boy am I glad he did!! I was planning my mother's 70th birthday party and Luke had the perfect private dining room for the small gathering. Since I don't live in NOLA I was able to do all the planning with Melissa (their private events contact) through email. Melissa was very responsive and accommodating to all of our party's requests. On the actual night of the dinner, I was super impressed with the quality of the service, the food and the atmosphere. Our server, Kevin, was amazing and he did a wonderful job making our event very memorable. Everything I tried was delicious. The shrimp and grits, the gulf drum, the gumbo...everything was very flavorful!! Cannot wait to go back next time I go to NOLA!!!

I enjoyed this place quite a bit.  We came after a long, hot, tiring day at the zoo, and I felt a little bit gross walking in and not realizing it was a nicer restaurant.  I wish I could have showered first, but that doesn't take away from the fact that I thouroughly enjoyed the experience of the place.  

Our server was really really nice and helpful.  We were all slightly delirious from exhaustion so it was pretty difficult for us to concentrate and think.  The drinks were fantastic.  I went for the St. Charles Streetcar and I wish I would have felt up for another two or three.  I wasn't really feeling up for any kind of heavy food either, and since I didn't feel too much like shrimp, the server got me some crab claws which weren't on the menu.  

The claws were quite delicious!  As well as the home-made pickles. One of group ordered the roullettes and said they were phenomenal.  Another in our group ordered the flamenkuche, per my recommendation.  I lived for a bit in Alsace so I am pretty familiar with tarte flambee.  This thing was delicious but NOTHING like a real tarte flambee.  Being that tarte flambee is one of the only things I liked about my experience in France, I'm really glad I hadn't ordered it.  For anyone not looking for the real thing, it was really really tasty and bacony though.

Small bar perfect for a small super laid back group. We threw my boyfriend's 30th birthday here. Had about 30 or so people and it was great. A little cramped for that many people. But the staff was great. The beer was cold and the atmosphere was inviting. We will be back.

When you eat at Luke, you wonder why Besh didn't win Iron Chef.

The raw bar has a great selection, and Besh's take on French fair is very very tasty.

I recommend the duck confit with white bean cassoule. 

The bread pudding was also great, topped off with a light carmel suace.

All in all, a great tasting meal that hits the spot.

I don't eat seafood and not much French food lol but I had an awesome glass of cabernet half off before 6pm! The matzo chicken soup which was very good and French fries which were of course amazing. Everyone in my party loved their food mussels, clams, oysters and crab bisque.
The atmosphere at Luke is great. The breakfast is amazing and the staff took their time to explain the menu. The shrimp and grits is
I had the stuffed oysters which were the best I've ever tasted.  Great food, ambience and service.  Highly recommended and will come back often.

My wife and I just stopped here to try to get dessert. They had a bunch of tables open as well as seats at the bar. Somehow they wouldn't be able to seat us, but had tables open for reservation when we checked online after leaving. All we wanted was bread pudding :(

Okay at best....far better choices in NOLA!   Shrimp & grits was good but tiny!!!  I have had this dish in many places and this was by far the smallest.  The girl who waited on us had a huge attitude...Shawn.  Pretty much gave us the impression that she did not care at all about if we were satisfied or not.

Edit: They called me and resolved the issue to my satisfaction.  Although I had to pry a resolution out of them, I'm pleased with the outcome and will continue to shop there.  

I can't say I'll be shopping at rei anytime soon again. I had to order a new garmin after the one the sold me was defective. The first ordered replacement sent in an HR+ BOX, but the actual watch was the inferior HR. Not cool. Ordered again. Sent me a USED watch. This is it. Literally covered in white shit. I yet again had to return it. That's not only two weeks (and three trips) of my time wasted, but also just plain bullshit. The refund was nice, but they can't compensate me for my time, energy, and emotions. I'm sure anyone with a fitness watch can agree, it's hard to go without. Ridiculous.

5 stars coming from a generally skeptical, sometimes thrifty , and ALWAYS critical Yelper. 

We came to Luke seeking inexpensive oysters and any type of happy hour drink special. What we got was an amazing happy hour AND dinner experience, after we couldn't bring ourselves to leave. I wish I was still there now.

First off, FIFTY CENT oysters. My table of New Yorkers (accustomed to $3 oysters) almost died from both sticker shock, and then the amount of seafood consumed. The oysters were HUGE and unlike anything I've ever experienced. Oysters and horseradish sauce? Never would have thought. Now, a combo I cannot forget. 

On to the most amazing appetizer of all time : Pate of rabbit and chicken livers. Absolutely, to die for. Along with the crispy bread for the pate, the app comes with delicious mustard and PICKLED WATERMELON bits. Together, a perfect marriage of flavors. This best $10 ever spent is what sold us on staying for dinner.

Dinner: I got the jagerschnitzel. This consisted of a gigantic amount of veal covering a layer of home made pasta in bacon mushroom sauce. Everyone tried it. Everyone LOVED it. I am not typically into gigantic portions but brought home easily another huge meals worth. 

Lastly, and certainly not least: for the duration of most of our meal, drinks were at happy hour pricing. This equates to $4 juleps, the best I ever could have imagined, and $4.50 sazeracs. Service was consistently attentive and knowledgeable throughout the evening. The whole experience was a great value.

Just came in for the .50 oyster happy hour, will be back for dinner tomorrow.  FYI, despite some previous tips or reviews the oysters are fresh shucked and fantastic.  I watched them go from stack of oysters in the sink to my plate. Fresh.  Staff is great.

We had an awesome time at Luke thanks to or amazing server, Richie Rich!  He was kind, generous, and extremely hospitable.  We had giant oysters, delicious brussels sprouts, and fantastic cocktails.  We'll be back and definitely hope to see him there again soon.

Food is very fresh and delicious, and service was quite poor, which lowered our rating. Fruits de mer was good and a very nice selection with excellent jumbo Gulf shrimp. Brussels sprouts tasty but over priced, chowder exquisite.  Bread pudding light and rich. Hard to find service people on a Thursday night.

The main question I had going into this restaurant was the pronunciation of "Lüke". How does the 2 dots above the U affect the pronunciation? I asked the hostesses, and they seemed to be unsure. They said the ü is maybe pronounced longer like Luuuuuke, but it remains unclear. It is my personal opinion that the ü brands them as a fancier restaurant to charge higher prices.  Nevertheless, I really enjoyed my meal. 

We had reservations just to be safe, but there is plenty of seating in a separate section of the back. This place has an old school but classy feel to it. Plenty of nice artwork on the wall and decorated appropriately. 

I ordered the crab and shrimp étouffée. I know, it sounds fancy. It had tomatoes, garlic, and crispy rice in it. The crispy rice had a nice texture to it and complimented the rest of the ingredients well. Very flavorful and didn't find it to be too spicy. Plenty of food and the crab and shrimp were delicious. Service seemed to be good. Received food in a timely manner and my water was refilled consistently. If I am in New Orleans again, this is definitely a restaurant I would come back to.
Perhaps a bit pricy, and definitely a bit noisy; the food was very good and the service was more than adequate.
Delicious food and great service! It's on the pricey side so be prepared to spend some money!

Before I get deep into this review, I want to say that sometimes the Yelp star rating throws me off a bit.  I tend to judge an establishment more on whether or not I could see myself coming back again in the future.  To me, that's really the deciding factor.  That being said, yes, I would come back here again!  While Luke Restaurant may not be a pioneer in the culinary world, the kitchen does deliver sound dishes that cannot be ignored.

Luke Restaurant is located on St. Charles Ave. in the CBD, directly across the street from One Shell Square.  It shares the adjacent space with the Hilton Hotel, which, if anyone remembers pre-Katrina, used to be the boutique Hotel Monaco.  Luke Restaurant used to be The Cobalt, a hip and modern lounge/restaurant owned by Susan Spicer, where great cocktails, as well as amazing eats could be found.  While the restaurant has changed owner, chef and style, the quality of the dishes has not diminished in the slightest.  Luke Restaurant advertises itself as a fine dining Bistro and I would say this description is accurate.  I've been frequenting this restaurant off and on since it's opening in 2007 and I've never been given a subpar product.

I would like to draw special attention to the detail of the interior design inside Luke Restaurant.  It reminds me of a social steakhouse ripped straight out of New York City in the 1920s.  Heavy and very ornately carved wood cabinets, doors and bar surround the dining area.  The floor near the bar is completely tiled in black & white while the dining area is situated upon what resembles vintage wood flooring.  To the front and left side of the restaurant, there is a large wooden board containing various newspapers for businessmen to peruse.  Above dining guests are slow-moving ceiling fans which are operated via a pulley; a system no longer common these days.  The restaurant sports a very vintage feel and I believe this works in Luke's favor.  The only other steakhouse resembling Luke Restaurant in terms of interior design and dish offering that comes to mind would be Anthony Bourdain's home base, Brasserie Les Halles, located on Park Ave. in New York.

The last two occasions that I dined in Luke Restaurant were over lunch with colleagues.  I am somewhat a slave to routine so I placed my order for the Luke Burger, a monster of a burger that attempts to contain tomatoes, Allen Benton's bacon, caramelized onions and Emmenthaler cheese within the confines of the bun.  It also comes with housemade fries.  Now, believe me when I say that while this burger is steeply priced at $17, I dare you to eat it all in one sitting.  I typically cut the burger in half and take the rest home, as it easily can feed a single person twice!  It is delivered to the customer on a cutting board and you are given pocket sized bottles of Ketchup, Mustard and Mayonnaise.  This is one heck of a huge burger but it's worth every penny!

Before diving into the burger, I also placed a starter of the gumbo that, when paired with the fresh rolls, is out-of-this-world!  The rest of my table ordered various dishes and starters but all who had selected the gumbo also stated it was terrific!

My burger later arrived and it looked amazing.  The flavor was breathtaking.  The large cuts of bacon, the delishus swirl of caramelized onions and cheese created a sweet aroma so thick, one might say you could swim in it!  The meat was perfectly seasoned and cooked and the flavors came together in a manner that literally created an orgiastic feast of the senses.  In the nature of a true wine connoisseur who takes most pleasure from a vintage's distinct scent, I thoroughly enjoy breathing in the fresh smells from a dish produced by a kitchen.  At such times, one could wish for the olfactory powers of the canine.  It's often occurred to me that pulling a dog away from a scent is akin to seizing a scholar at the museum by the scruff of his neck and dragging him away from his studies.

As I've said before, Luke Restaurant may not be groundbreaking but what it does deliver is exceptional quality and great service.  This is a wonderful place to pop in by yourself or with a small group for lunch or dinner.  If you find yourself hungry and within proximity, do yourself a favor and visit Luke.  Your tummy will thank you!
Great margaritas, amazing BLT which has a fried crab right on it, awesome oyster happy hour, great burger & fries!

Was at NOLA this past week. Tried lots of restaurant, only few worth my time writing an review for them,  because I want people to try THEM.

Felix's
Luke
Willie Mae's

Went there for the happy hour!! well we were attracted to Luke because of their 50 cents oysters (vs $1.5+ per at the other places), no limit, from 3pm-6pm. 

we ordered 2 dozens of oysters, sizes are great (some are huge), very fresh. If we weren't flying out that same night, i think we would have ordered more!!

Also, their Crawfish Bisque is great too, very rich in flavor and creamy.

MAKE SURE YOU MAKE APPOINTMENT!! NOLA's streets might be empty, but not LUKE @ happy hour!!!

I had never heard of this restaurant when I and a party of eight arrived here this evening. It was packed, but they took good care of us and the food was absolutely fantastic. A great steak, great drinks, great appetizers. Definitely worth your time. I would feel good about bringing friends here to eat. I will be back.

HAPPY HOUR. Just come for the happy hour.  I came here almost everyday. Make reservations. Order the seventy five cent oysters and everything on their drink menu. Might as well since everything is half off.  Their drinks were meh-okay.  I suggest Arnaud's but its just so inexpensive that it doesn't matter.

Bright, open space with a bistro feel. Traditional tin ceilings. Large and ornate wood trim on the bar with matching wood half-walls to break up the narrow space. Luke is inside the Hilton Hotel on St. Charles. Side note: take a look at the hotel hallway to the bathroom and nearby elevator area for its gorgeous marbled walls and flooring.

We came on a Thursday afternoon at 4:30 for happy hour. It's a great deal - all the wines by the glass, beer, specialty cocktails and well drinks are 1/2 off, and .75 raw P&J brand gulf oysters. Our oysters were large and fresh, brought with red cocktail sauce and separate horseradish. These were comparable to those found at Crescent City Brewery and other NOLA favorites. The Jalepaloma tequila cocktail was refreshing, though a bit too sweet and not enough "picante" (heat) for my taste.

We had been wanting to come to Luke's after we had tasted their yummy shrimp and grits at an outdoor music festival on the river. But, the shrimp and grits ("En Cocotte") disappointed. The shrimp almost seemed to come from frozen. They were a bit too soft. The sauce was uninspired but the grits were good with a soft texture, a bit cheesy and not dry. We prefer the shrimp dishes at Mr. B's Bistro, to be honest. On the upside, the Luke salad had big chunks of heirloom tomatoes, yellow and red beets, and shaved carrots with a light vinaigrette. Couldn't really taste the horseradish. It was fresh and delicious.

One of the unfortunate trends in today's cooking is the overuse of sweetness on vegetable dishes (and cocktails, too.) Being on a low carb lifestyle, I asked the waitress if the Brussel sprouts were overly sweet with honey. I hoped that the honey would be an accent, not the main flavor. If you're cutting down on sugar (and, yes, honey and fruits are sugars), don't order these. They're as sweet as dessert. Even my husband didn't care for them mostly because they didn't compare with the crisp, tasty sprouts at our local Brown Butter restaurant. The wait staff, though, was very accommodating and took the charge off the bill. I would add an extra star for service, but the food really was disappointing overall for a restaurant of this reputation.

Not sure if we'll be back unless visitors would like to try the good deals at happy hour and see the beautiful space.

Love Luke's. Came back to New Orleans just so we can go to Luke for my bday after finding it in 2016 for my bday and we wanted to come back again on my bday this year. They did change up their seafood tower abit, but it was still amazing. Hoping to make this an annual thing for us as long as we can

Oh Panera...why can't this location pull it together? I just went through the drive-through. I ordered the ancient grain, arugula, & CHICKEN salad. I got home and started eating my salad. Guess what? No CHICKEN!! I'm ready to give up. There's a Zupas around the corner. I'll go there as I can watch them make my salad.

Our server was really great and the food was pretty tasty as well. The reason why I'm giving it three stars out of five is because the ambiance was very loud. They have a cabinet next to the hostess stand which holds all of their silverware and about every five minutes you'd hear ridiculously loud noises of forks,spoons,etc. being dropped on the floor or being thrown into a drawer in the cabinet. I know it might sound petty but it's really annoying when you're trying to hold a conversation with someone.

Went for Monday happy hour.  Oysters were great, shrimp spicy, wine 1/2 price. Service was very good.  Not wild about the layout and sound level.  Would go back for lunch or happy hour but not the ambiance I'd pick for dinner

Food in this place is excellent . Gosh so good. Service is a little slow but very nice, appropriate to the place. But Woooow food is amazing. We order the chicken and honey biscuit and was amazing. Also the shrimp and grits was to die for. Delicious . Highly recommend.

Chipotle's menu is dead-simple, the food is generally tasty, and the restaurant itself is always nice and clean.  They've added a few new menu choices in previous years, but the main draw is the burritos - they're hilariously large.  It's like a giant food pillow wrapped in foil.  The individual ingredients may be healthy (brown rice is a welcome addition), but they're served in such huge quantities that you're pretty much getting a day's worth of caloric intake from one burrito.  Share with a friend, unless you plan on skipping a meal or two that day.  Considering what you get, the prices are A-OK.  They've got beer, too, but the only thing worth drinking is the Negra Modelo.

Very good breakfast: the french toast was perfectly cinnamon-y, and the french fries were delicious--they didn't even need ketchup, they were that good.  Service was OK, although our server kept bumping into tables and chairs because they were so crowded together.  Quality breakfast.

Fantastic Food!!  Why did I not know about this place!?  Love the hot sour soup and the fried rice was above and beyond any I've ever had.  Wonderful Mom and Pop place.  The egg rolls are nothing to write home about and hot tea would be a great addition, but other than that, wow!  I asked one of the girls at the counter what was in hot sour soup.  They called the chef in from the kitchen (aka Mom) and she explained the ingredients happily and in detail.  Great folks great food.  Not a sit down and be served restaurant.   The other local mom and pop Chinese food place T.G.I. has just been replaced!

Best place we ate in NO in my opinion.  Super friendly, reasonably priced considering the food quality and atmosphere.  Supposedly the dude won something on Top Chef.  I smashed some duck livers and pork shank.  The place was killer!

"Sometimes we create our own heartbreaks through expectation." My friends and I were in New Orleans for vacation and of course the food was a major selling point. And every place we had been to had delivered... until Luke's. We had ordered the Giant Seafood Tower which consists of clams, mussels, tuna tartar, oysters, and the main piece of the puzzle: lobster. Presentation was great, but we were in for quite the surprise when we made our way to the lobster. Upon cracking it open, a gooey, guacamole looking green substance oozed out of the lobster. To say my friends and I were shook would be an understatement. After a quick google search (we thought this was lobster excrement) we found out that this was "tomalley"- the lobster body cavity that serves as the pancreas and liver of the lobster. And what we learned is .... don't eat it because it contains many toxins. Trust me, no one was planning on eating it, it was an immediate turnoff. Being that the lobster was the crown jewel of this $150 meal (yes, not a typo) we mentioned something to the manager who tried telling us that it was a "delicacy".... we told him we saw articles of the FDA saying not to eat this. This debacle was a big turnoff for us, especially considering that our waiter had checked on us only twice the entire time we were there (not that crowded). The manager, sensing we were not happy, offered to give us a round of drinks for free. This wasn't going to win us over but we weren't going to say no to free booze. But we should have considering we had to wait another 15 minutes for 6 beers. Food overall gets 3 stars, service gets 1.5 stars (the manager rubbed us the wrong way due to his condescending attitude) and that combines for a pretty disappointing end result. Too bad!

First time there and we were impressed! Great brewed coffee and a creamy latte satisfied our needs for caffeine very well. We each had the Early #1 breakfast sandwich and that's the real reason for the 5 stars. Best breakfast sandwich either of us have had anywhere.  Fresh artisan style bun filled with apple cheese egg bacon and some roasted garlic,  and  perfectly toasted. They've earned their place as Edmonton's #1 take out food spot. We'll be back often I'm sure!

Got a little wild with the girlfriends at Luke during their Sunday happy hour. Between the four of us, we started with two dozen oysters (50 cents each). Thirty minutes later, we ordered another two dozen oysters. So fresh and delicious! Meanwhile, we treated ourselves to a multitude of cocktails including the silver saint and mint julep. Our server was awesome and kept the drinks coming - which were all half price during the happy hour (3pm to 6pm every day). It was pouring rain that afternoon, so we ended up staying for more than two hours. Way after 6pm (end of happy hour), the staff continued to let us have the happy hour prices. We ended with the bread pudding which was perfect! Definitely a great experience at Luke, which was recommended to us by multiple friends.

Dinner @ Lukes was a total disappointment.

Bad Yelp -  you lead me astray!

Even though we had a reservation, we were stuck at a small corner table near 2 large corporate dinners so it was very loud. The atmosphere was average.   The menu did not have all that many options so I settled on the shrimp and grits which was too spicy, a small portion and not all that great.  I forget what my husband had but he was equally disappointed.  Service was inattentive and slow.  

NOT Recommended
Went on Christmas Eve for the first time and I can say that I will come again.  All the food was amazing!

The food and service here was pretty darn good.  

I made reservations at 8:30 PM and arrived at 8:10 PM -- got seated right away. I was flip flopping between all of their yummy options on their menu & I was trying to avoid the shrimp & grits since that's what I've been eating all weekend, but ell into peer pressure when the the waiter recommended it.  He insisted that it was one of the most popular things on the menu, so I couldn't resist.  And I didn't regret it!  The customer service was great, very attentive and kind people!

If I could do half stars it would be a 2.5 but I'll give them the benefit. Disclosure: we came at 10:15p and they close at 11p so it probably affected service but it is a John Besh restaurant and therefore I expect a bit better.
Our 2 waiters clearly did not communicate with each other in regard to our service, one was professional and the other was not. Neither explained any sort of special and mainly showed up to take our order rather than guide us through the meal.
We ordered a tuna tartare for an appetizer and it took roughly 15 minutes and was average at best.
Our main course was a ribeye that was cooked perfectly but lacked the substance of a good slice, my wife's Blue Crab Cavatelli was good but nothing special. We ordered a side of sautéed seasonal vegetables and were met with brussels sprouts, with sparse amounts of green beans and yellow squash, which took a side of bearnaise sauce to get through.
Dessert was a bread pudding that was above average but not the best we have had in this city.
All in all this meal was sadly forgettable, I will definitely give another Besh restaurant a try but this was definitely not the impression a restaurant of this caliber hopes to makes.

So there we were the week of Mardi Gras on a Saturday evening and We were early for our reservation so the super cool hostess who I think may have been the manager told us about Happy Hour on a Saturday? During Mardi Gras? Up to the bar we went and had a great bartender I think his name was Jonas  2 for 1 drinks and I asked him what appetizer he would recommend He recommended the Pate Plate assiette de charcuterie.Now I am in no ways a pate kinda guy but this stuff was amazing! all different kinds with some head cheese that turned me into a fan!

Later for dinner I had the HOUSE Special Jaugersnitzel and it was so good except I'm not a veal fan so I didn't enjoy it and couldn't eat  but it tasted real good but that's what Happy hour can do to a guy

The hype is real! 

Did not have reservations, but was seated within 40 mins on a Thursday night after reminding the hostess I was still waiting. 

Servers are very friendly, and accommodating. 

The oysters are so fresh!! hot bread rolls per table .. yum! 

The crawfish "etouffee" is amazing - instead of pasta they make a homemade pasta made of ricotta! So delicious and definitely worth it!!

ordered through grubhub first time (6.99 delivery fee) i dont recommend it. They forgot to give soup and cheesesteak . I found out they didnt have soup so they remove it from my order without telling me and still charged. I decided to give a 2nd chamce through yelp, After being charged and waiting 1 hr, I called and they said they never got the order and just said deal with yelp.

Great, never again,

Came yet again for a work lunch.  I had the softshell crab BLT, which comes on a toasted brioche bun and with fries.  Ho-Ly Cow!  It was delicious.  The crab was huge and the breading was crispy and flavorful.  The bacon was of high quality (very little fat) and was cooked to a prefect crispiness as well.  It was served as an open faced sandwich to be eaten with a fork and knife; and this is the only way to eat this monster dish because there's no way you could fit that huge sandwich in your mouth for a bite, let alone with the addition of another bread layer.  This dish is a home run for Luke.

I stopped going here earlier this year because the service had reached new lows in abominable. Not to mention the oysters we had were shucked so poorly and shredded beyond belief. The BF swore them off for good. But I love their French 75 and bargain oysters so I wasn't ready to write them off forever.

It's taken me a while to get back on my own and I am so glad that I did! They have a shucker named Anthony who is AWESOME! I told him about our previous experience and he said, very seriously, "That's terrible. Oysters are too precious to mess up."  My oysters (from Plaquemines Parish) were big and salty and perfect. And shucked the right way. 

IMPORTANT NOTE: Bring cash to tip the shucker. I usually spend more on oysters than I do on booze and I don't think it's fair that the shucker doesn't get a little something. Otherwise all my credit card tip goes to the bar.

Oh this is wonderful.  Classic bistro vibe and fantastic food.  Raw bar is amazing.

Service was slightly awkward, like a trainee, but very friendly.  The neighborhood feels a little corporate office-ish.  Not the super cool NOLA vibe you want.  Those are the only markdowns.

Absolutely with a visit for the food.

Popped in for a late lunch on a Friday with my daughter. We were in time for their happy hour oyster special. 6 P&J raw oysters for .75 each? Um, yes please. We also had a really tasty crawfish bisque and flammenkuchen (basically a thin flatbread topped with onions, cheese, and thick cut bacon). The flammenkuchen was pretty good but we both thought the bacon was a bit too thick for our tastes. Service was spot on. I'd definitely come back for dinner.

Luke has been my favorite restaurant for a couple of years now.  I have tried EVERYTHING on the menu at least twice so I think I have a pretty good basis for comparison.  

This restaurant is not for everyone.  If you are new in town and looking for classic New Orleans creole or soul food cuisine.  Look elsewhere.  If you don't like Alsacian food (or don't know what it is) you might want to pass.  But if you are game you will find Luke serves earthy food with a light touch.  

Literally everything is good, but there are standouts.  The Luke Burger is made of fine beef and served with fries that I believe are cooked in duck fat.  It is the tastiest combo in town.  Although it's great, I don't often get the burger because it weighs about 5 pounds.  You will need a doggy bag.

I do get the matzo ball soup and Luke salad often.  The soup is a rarity in NOLA and I'll admit that I don't get the connection of this Jewish staple to the French/German border.  Who cares?  It tastes a little like chicken gumbo, which means it's delicious.  

The redfish is probably the best all-around dish.  It's lightly sauteed and covered in lump crab meat .  However, my personal favorite is the Flamenkuche aka German pizza or bacon, Emmenthaler and caraway cheese and onions on a tarte.  This dish is savory and so good that I sometimes dream about it.  

At the risk of belaboring the point, there are plenty of other standouts.  The redfish court-bouillion.  The white bean and duck cassoulet.  The cochon de lait.  Did I mention they put on a fine breakfast?  Grits and grillades.  Buttermilk pancakes.  Etc. Etc.

The service is friendly and attentive.  The decor is cool and very detailed.  Note the old fashion belt fans in the front room (I didn't notice them until my 10th visit.)

Just check the restaurant out.  It's got plenty to offer.  I hope you will agree.

A tiny, tiny cafe that outputs an enormous energy and killer product and service! I have recently dropped coffee from my diet. It's killing me but my body thanks me. So what the heck am I reveiwing a cafe for? It's creativity and stellar attention to quality food and local sourcing!

This past weekend I was lucky enough to be involved in the TEDX Edmonton event. It was a long and inspiring day. Lunch time approached and we were all amazed at what awaited us at the top of the stairs in the Citadel up from the Rice Theatre! 49 hand-crafted wooden boxes arranged to spell "Awesome food goes in. Awesome Ideas come out." We were encouraged to forms groups of 6, grab a box, and park ourselves for a picnic.

What was inside these boxes? Each box contained 6 sandwiches, dessert, salad and drinks. These were not regular lunch items. The salad was a veggie qunioa salad, the sandwiches ranged from BLT, Turkey, Cubano, roeast beef and veggie. 

I'm a veggie so I opted for this sandwich. It was amazing! The main star was pan fried apples! 

Also included in this box was a package of seeds. The bottom of the box on the inside was stamped with a message about the importance of eaty healthy, local, and creative yummy food!

Imagine making all this glorious food AND 49 wooden boxes! What a treat!

We had some left overs after the event. I scored some sandwiches for my dad and husband. My husband is a meat eater and ate and fell in love with the veggie sandwiches!

Beautiful local concept. Love affair with artisan food and a great big warm heart and socially conscious mind!

Ate lunch here.  Had a dozen gulf shrimp that were delicious.  Wife fad the croq-madame, also delicious; and her colleague had the cochon de lait, which he raved about.  Great service, atmosphere, and location.

I came in for an oil change and the service was the best I have had in a very long time.  Because I am a woman many places take advantage of that by trying to convince me that I should have more than what I ask for.  But today I did have other things done I was given a great discount on my work and I will definitely be back to have other things done with my truck. Robert and Patrick was the best today and highly recommended others to come to them for service on your vehicles. Thank you for your honesty and great service today. My vehicle is my job and I need to get my vehicle ready for my customers to be comfortable and safe so I just want to say that I really am glad I stopped in.

I found everything at this restaurant to be wonderful. When my girlfriend and I went we were a little overdressed. No problem though. We did not feel awkward at all. 

We ended up sitting in the back dining room which was just as fun as the front. Our server was really fun and he made great recommendations. 

We ended up having the beet salad and pork rillette to start. Afterwards, my girlfriend had the Luke Burger. It was really tasty but I would recommend getting it at a maximum of medium well. Anything over this takes away a lot of flavor and the smokiness takes over from the bacon. I had the duck and it was incredibly succulent and tasty. 

For desert we had the black forest pudding and also the vanilla ice cream. 

Great side note.... They don't have a corkage fee if you bring your own wine. I brought a wonderful bottle of 1998 Perrier Jouet and was surprised at this.

Great place. Daily specials are excellent. Don't let the price fool you the portions are huge. Great drink list and cocktails as well. One absolute must get is the BLT. YUM or as they say in Hawaii. Ono.
One of my favorite restaurants for Happy Hour.  Order a French 75.

Love it!  Staff is very friendly and helpful.  Treats everyone like a friend of the owner.  Food is amazing and creative.  If you're tired of the same old sushi dishes hachi is your answer.  Desserts are huge!

This is my 2nd restaurant for We Live To Eat Restaurant Week and my fourth Besh Restaurant (I still haven't tried Besh Steakhouse).  Besh has another winner of a restaurant.  I just loveee how all of his restaurants are so completely different from one another!  Off the set menu, I got the crab and corn bisque as a starter, which was tasty.  I just wish there was more crab in it.  My entree was the Veal cutlet.  I could not finish it since the portion was too big.  I liked it, but I didn't love it.  I really wished their infamous shrimp and grits were on the set menu for me to try!  My boyfriend had the Luke Burger which was HUGE and so tender.  I highly recommend the burger!  He also got the Abita Turbodog which he said was "really good."  Those words rarely come out of his mouth, because he's already tried a big variety of food and drinks so he's usually very nonchalant about anything he intakes, so that beer must be something!  He's a big fan of dark beers if anyone wants to know his taste.  For dessert, we got the Bread Pudding. OMG!  AMAZINGGGGGG!!!  It had to be one of the best Bread Puddings I've had!  it came with a rum praline sauce and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.  I would come back just for this dessert!

I definitely plan on coming back, since I want to try so many things on the menu including the pate and the shrimp and grits.  I'm also going to try to come during happy hour for those quarter oysters!
I had the Drum fish meunière with veggies and The house Fru beer haven't had a meal in a while that just made me smile it was so good...this one did! Delicious meal, great atmosphere.

They have fifty cent oysters from 3-6! And one of the best burgers and fries my boyfriend and I have ever had. Simple ingredients elevated to something sublime. Get some oysters and split the burger and fries and you've just eaten at one of the best restaurants in New Orleans on the cheap. The service was friendly and impeccable.

Dear Luke, what amazing happy hours you have!! 50 cents oysters and 1/2 off bar..you heard right! 50 CENTS OYSTERS AND 1/2 OFF BAR ::sigh::

We took full advantage of the happy hour of course. Never ate so many raw oysters in one sitting in my life, and that's only 1/2 of what my boyfriend ate. What's even better is this restaurant is literally right across from our hotel so we went here twice on our trip lol. 

Tip: don't sit at the bar, horrible service. We sat at a table the second time and service was much better, we actually existed! yay.

Since this Cosi is located in University City with a significant customer base of students, I wonder whether it is coincidence or intentional design that the store has two levels, the top one especially good for studying in the morning hours . I am not sure if this applies to the afternoon and evening hours, as I have not been there at those times. In terms of the food, I really enjoy the Turkey Light sandwich for lunch and the sesame bagels (Cosi calls them squagels) for breakfast. Just recently, Cosi upped its coffee game with more diversified offerings. For example, I tasted an Ethiopian blend this morning. It was excellent. Service speed can slow up at times with big morning and lunch rushes, but having been here on and off for many years, the service and food have been 3-star consistent. A pretty high traffic Cosi, the place is not the cleanest at times, an area that I hope that they are aware of and are working on.

I think the description "good chain restaurant" is an oxymoron.  So what a nice surprise it was to enjoy my first ever visit to a Panera Bread.  The choice was based on the real estate adage "location, location, location" for a quick breakfast with a lovely Yelp friend who was in town and suggested we meet up.  Since neither of us had ever been to Panera and this fit the bill for being able to eat and visit for an hour before her morning appointment, in we went.   At 8:00 'ish' on a weekday morning this spacious, sparkling clean, fast-casual food restaurant was virtually empty.  So there's a note if you're looking to avoid crowds.
 
SWEETS & OTHER BREAKFAST EATS:  The pastries in the bakery case looked pretty darned good, with a sticky bun calling my name.  Alas, no sweets for me until Lent is over so it will give me a reason to go back to respond to the call.  There were healthy breakfast choices too, including steel cut oatmeal with fresh strawberries and pecans.  Also bagels of several kinds with cream cheese of several flavors.  Breakfast sandwiches too.

THE DRILL:  Order at the counter or by kiosk at the front of the store but that's way too high tech, low touch for me so we did it the old fashioned way by talking to the helpful woman behind the counter.  They'll give you an electronic "id disk" with a number on it.  Take it with you to the table or booth and when your order is ready, they deliver.  Bus your own when done, but if you fail to do that they do clean up after folks.  Food is served on real plates.  Hooray.  Coffee, the dark roast is pretty darned good, is serve yourself in ceramic mugs or big paper "hot cups".  

PRICES:  Very reasonable, we thought, for the quality of the food and format.  Light breakfast for three was under $12.

THIS N THAT:

1) PARKING:  Private lot which seemed to have ample spaces.

2) ACCESSIBILITY:  Accessible parking in lot.  Level in the door and all on one level inside.  Lots of standard height table seating.  Booths along wall are standard height too.
Nice atmosphere and place to go with a group. Étouffée was yummy and light, served over bed of homemade pasta, burgers were huge and ham/cheese with egg was great.

Hum this to the tune of Lady Gaga's "Bad Romance"

Oh-oh-oh-oh-oh-oh-oh-oh-oh-oh-oh-oh! I'm going to split my pants!

That's what I was singing after I tried to eat a complete Luke burger.  Oh my Gaga, that thing was a monster!   Did I eat the whole thing?  You'll have to read on to find out.

Was staying at the Hilton and several people recommended eating at Luke and we're glad we did.   We each had a great tap beer...b/f had the jaeger schnitzel, bffc had the flamenküche which is like a pizza with Alsacien onion, bacon, 
caraway and Emmenthaler cheese.  That was off the charts delicious.   

I had the burger which was just so delicious but it was huge!  As Richard Gere said in "Officer and a Gentleman"...No, sir. You can kick me outta here, but I ain't quitting.  That's what I said when the giant burger was set before me (ironically, there was no MAYO-nnaise on it).  Anyway, I couldn't finish it.  I had to quit.  Guess I was more like David Keith's character than Richard Gere's!  (Read the synopsis on IMDB to see what happened to him if you haven't seen the film)

Our server was delightful...she had great suggestions, a lot of enthusiasm and clearly loved her job.  This Besh guy, the celebrity chef of Luke, really knows what he's doing.  I'm a fan.

This food lifted me up where I belong.

If you are looking for a great place to get cafeteria style...well...cafeteria food, look no further.  That is exactly what this place is: rows upon rows of jello, green beans and corn in small bowls, fried chicken and ham hanging out on plates under heating lamps and of course, the rows of pie hanging out at the end.  

This is the standard cafeteria, in South City that I am sure you have been dying to find.  I am only assuming you don't know about it because, well, you aren't 85 years old if you are on Yelp looking at reviews.  Well, perhaps I shouldn't assume.  I have been to this place many times in my life as it was a favorite of my grandparents.  The food is edible, and it's certainly cheap, and there is an array of choices so everyone can at least sort of get what they want.  If you are looking for a great place to take your grandma , well, this is certainly worth checking out.

Their Happy Hour is simply amazing. I mean we came back here 3 times during our 3 day trip just so we can partake of their happy hour. Where else can you get fresh raw oysters for $.75 each?? 

Each time we stopped by there was little to no wait. The second time we were smart and made reservations in advance. 

We were seated pretty promptly and of course we immediately knew what to order- this time we each got our own dozen of oysters, which come with a small loaf of fresh bread and butter, as well as spicy horseradish and cocktail sauce. Absolutely the best oyster happy hour I have ever had.

If I ever go back to New Orleans, I will definitely be back to this gem!

Stopped in for lunch on Monday, the service was friendly and the food was good.  Had pj oysters and the Monday special.  Now the Monday special with rice and beans was good, the chicken was fantastic.  The mino cocktail was pretty good too.

Tried for a second time to eat this place. Both times I never received my food. the first time was 60 minutes of waiting for my order which I never received. The second time was 90 minutes. This time they simply forgot to make it. Organization at this place is not existent. attitude is equally as bad. On a side note...avoid the Hilton Hotel it is attached to as well. 

I've ate here last and it was adequate. Staff was rude but the food was okay. Staff is still rude. Food? Avoid this joint at all cost.

Happy hour from 3-6 everyday with 75 cent oysters on the half shell. The oysters were plumpy and fresh and the horseradish was delish. 

The crab corn soup was like liquid gold in a bowl--this might be one of the best soups I've had in my life! It was rich with crab chunks and buttery. I never wanted it to end. 

I had the Luke burger cooked to medium. The patty was huge and the onions complemented the flavors of the meat so well. The first thing I noticed was the bun which looked like a fancy artisanal bread. It was light and doughy. 

Thank you Kevin for awesome service! Kevin our server was very polite and personable. It was an unforgettable experience and I will be sure to come back next time!

I went to Luke last month for lunch and really enjoyed my meal.  Even better my boss was picking up the bill; not that Luke is super expensive though.  I thought my blood orange hollandaise sauce (on shrimp farsi) was good enough to drink.  And I enjoyed a specialty cocktail but I can't remember the name, but it was light and perfect (and I was with my boss who doesn't drink, scandal!)  She had the crabmeat omelet and couldn't stop raving.  My only problem with the restaurant was that it was so loud.  It was difficult to have a conversation across a table and I'm generally considered...a high volume person.  Definitely looking forward to going back.

I'm very glad that my first true #shrimpandgrits experience was had at John Besh's New Orleans restaurant  #Lüke. The jumbo Louisiana shrimp "En Cocotte was atop roasted jalepeno cheese grits and loaded with andouille sausage. I always envisioned grits to be flavorless but salty. Boy was I wrong! The cheese and jalepeno proved me wrong! The crawfish beignets was the choice for my first sampling of a savory #beignet and to be fair, they weren't out of this world, just okay, but the green garlic aoili saved the day! The accompanying sauce had so much flavor yet had a subtle and pleasant endnote that made me enjoy every bite. Now, why would you order a burger here when there's #cajunfood to be tried? Well, you always take the recommendation of the few people you ask and try it. Very very glad that advice was taken. The Lüke burger was a definite hit! Seemed massive and heavy, but once you bit in to it you tasted the lightness abd fresness of the protein. The amazing caramelized onions, bacon, and Enmenthaler cheese all paired well together to create the perfect bite. I highly recommend this be added to anyone's list of places to eat in  #nola

really good,fresh oyster,the fried ones are much better than other restaurant we visited , the raw is as good as some other restaurants. The Luke burger is huge and very tasty. The soft crab BLT is very good as well .

Breakfast:

Pain Perdu.
Eggs in a Jar.
Omelet of Local Crab.

OMG!!! Food Heaven!!

**Note to self: Next time I MUST order a Biscuit Sandwich!!

I came here for the happy hour oysters and they are AMAZING.  i ended up coming back here a second time because I had to have it.  they are just so fresh and i probably ended up eating 100 oysters my entire trip.  i couldn't get enough!  there was never much of a wait and their happy hour is daily which i love it when restaurants have a daily happy hour!  they had some drink specials too and i fell in love with the French 75.  It's so far made it to the top of my favorite cocktails and I haven't had a favorite cocktail in over 10 years which is saying a lot.  I did have it at another restaurant but it was definitely not as good as how they made it here. I can't stop dreaming about the oysters here.
Service is great, even is rush hour. I love the food there, entouffee. French 75 is great.
This is the type of brunch you want when in New Orleans. The crawfish and asparagus omelet was delightful. The pancakes melted in your mouth, especially with the pecan butter on top. Yum yum yum!

Came here waiting on the parade. Sat at the bar and met several people. Food was fantastic and drinks kept coming. They sell a place to watch the parade from and was worth every penny. Come during happy hour to enjoy the wait!!

So I thought that Lüke was straight up German food. I was totally expecting brats and beers. Better yet, it's actually an Alsace-Lorraine themed restaurant which is completely awesome. There are touches of German influence, touches of French, touches of Cajun, touches of Creole, but all in all this place is touches of awesome. 

Okay, so it's not exactly the most affordable of restaurants, but it's definitely worth visiting once, maybe twice.

The onion tart with pancetta or pork belly or whatever it was, well the onion tart was all kinds of amazing. My friends had seafood, I had the shrimp and grits. It all looked amazing, but I was real pleased with the shrimp and grits as my choice. 

Give it a go already.
We came here for a light lunch during happy hour to satisfy my oyster craving for 50 cents a pop. It did not disappoint. I'd love to come back for dinner!
Great sushi fast service and a lovely dining room.  We were pleasantly surprised at how nice it was.  Would definitely go back!

The oysters were fresh and delicious, service was good. Surprisingly my favorite dish was the Brussels sprouts, it's a must order! 

I ordered the rabbit pate which I would also high recommend, I do think it's on the saltier side.

Absolutely LOVED this place! We stopped by for happy hour and enjoyed $1 raw oysters, $1.50 fried oysters and half price cocktails. The fried oysters were the BEST! We also enjoyed several entrees and an additional appetizer. All top notch dishes. The wait staff was excellent...fast paced and on top of the situation. A must happy hour stop if you're visiting New Orleans.

Of all of the restaurants that we visited during a long weekend in New Orleans (and there were many) we thought Lukes had the best food across the board. This Franco-German John Besh restaurant left us craving for more and seeking out more of his restaurants during our stay. 

We came in for lunch on Friday and this appeared to be a popular "power lunch" spot as many people were dressed in business attire. It took us about 30 minutes to get a table for 4 without a reservation.  It was well worth the wait!

Rarely, have I gone into a restaurant with several other people each ordering different things and each person leaving extremely impressed, full, and enjoying each dish we shared. For the rest of our trip, we kept visiting other restaurants and while individual plates may have been just as good, nothing compared across the board to what we had at Luke's.

I highly recommend the Lamb Ragout (listed as boar on menu online, but changed to lamb). While we could not determine our overall favorite dish, someone at our table who claimed they "do not like lamb" could not stop talking about how good this dish was. The croque-monsieur  (grilled ham and cheese) was also very good and the fries that came with it where crispy and very well-seasoned. We shared (devoured) an order of oysters and shrimp and thought these were among the best we have had in the city. The Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp was a delicious mix of jalapenos, sausage, and shrimp and was perfectly seasoned and spiced. Everything was delicious here and we look forward to our next visit.
Doesn't state anywhere that reservations are highly recommended! Arrived at 5 & was told next available seating was 8pm?! Unbelievable! Ready to spend $100s!

Always a must stop when in New Orleans. One of my favorite restaurants in a city filled with great places.  Ate here over the Christmas holidays twice, once for breakfast and once for lunch.  At lunch, had the assorted chacuterie.  It was simply amazing.  Also had the beet salad and the crab salad.  Again, just wonderful.
  
The service is attentive and professional. And the atmosphere is great.

Located in the Hilton on St. Charles, so it is open everyday, even major holidays for all meals.

I called this company last year when my ac wasn't working.  They came out same day.  They told me they could do a fix but that the unit was old and may not last too long.  I said I'd rather just replace instead of a short term fix.  So imagine my shock that 1 year later the ac is not working.  I called them to come out and they said they didn't replace cooling unit only the blower.  He said they obviously did what they were supposed to because we had ac for the rest of May, June, July and August.  They never replaced the outside unit.  They completely misrepresented themselves.  I would never recommend this company to anyone.  I will be reporting to the BBB as well.

Amazing from start to finish. Try the étouffée and the Brussels sprouts. The oysters are so fresh and sweet and the service is amazing, drinks are amazing, and the food is so so amazing. The waiter also printed us a recipe for the Brussel sprouts to make at home. Thoroughly impressed.
Came here twice on my trip because we loved it so much the gumbo was amazing we also had 24 oysters at .75 cents each and the bread pudding is to die for

Came here for lunch from a recommendation from a local bartender. We order the fried oyster salad and a Croque-Monsieur which came with fries. Everything was delicious. I am not a fan of ham but the ham was delicious!

We reserved a table in the back for a party of 12 or so. Had a great time, great service and as a group we pretty much sampled the whole menu.  Everything from the oysters to to steak fritters was wonderful and the service kept the food and drinks coming!  I highly recommend for groups and romantic dinners.
The food was amazing.  We were sat without reservation because I wasn't very busy at the moment. By the time I was done with lunch it was packed. The fried Oisters are heavenly.

Very affordable brasserie from John Besh of the Next Iron Chef fame.  Had the fish of the day prepared with lemon and brad crumbs.  Great choice.  It is very affordable for a restaurant by a nationally known chef.  Got to say the bread pudding has a caramel on it that you would expect on a cuban flan, just a depth of flavor you don't get with a regular bread pudding.

When looking at various John Besh restaurants, I thought Luke would be a good try but I wasn't thoroughly impressed. The atmosphere is great if you sit in the back where you can see the kitchen staff hard at work through a clear glass. Otherwise, be forewarned that the front of the house is accompanied by their uncooked seafood (hello, wafts of ocean...).

The food is more so where the 2 stars come in. While the service and set-up was great, I really think you're paying for the chef name and recipes. After trying the vegetarian dish once (veggies and pasta), I asked our server to woo the chef into making me an original dish- most places take on this challenge with absolutely no compliant. What came out was- wait for it- pasta and veggies. Same dish, different noodles. My parents tried two different carnivorous meals and both said they were "meh," especially after our previous meals that weekend. 

Overall, worth a shot if you're looking for a fun night and some new food. Irony is, after seeing the two things on the menu that we thought "Who would get those at a place like this?", we realized those should have been our orders. Their hamburgers and the ham and cheese sandwich looked good enough for a vegetarian to try! Mind you, I'd sub the ham for tomatoes, but they were exquisite!
