And their french fries are totally worth it.

How do I begin. The.75 cent oysters during happy hour; the out of this world seafood gumbo; the best red beans and rice; the fried boneless Chicken. Everything was first rate delicious food. My first time at a John Besh restaurant and worth  all the accolades.

Had the shrimp and grits. Excellent choice and recommended by the server. Perfectly seasoned with a healthy portion of shrimp. My only issue is the price. Will service was great this place seemed unreasonably pricey compared to some of its competitors. 

But overall it was a good experience.

Luke, Luke, Luke. I want to love you, but there are just too many things wrong. I love Besh's other restaurants. They rank at the very top of my favorite restaurants list, but Luke is just disappointing.

Happy hour? Great happy hour, especially since I work next door. (3-6pm daily, half price for most drinks, 50c oysters). I love their French 75, and the rest of their cocktails are pretty decent too. However, the oysters at happy hour are usually small and they recently raised the price to 50cents per oysters.

Lunch? Oh my goodness. If you have two hours for lunch, feel free to stop by, but if you're like any normal person, you probably don't have that kind of time. Service is incredibly slow at lunch, almost to the point of being inexcusable.

Food? Eh. I've never had anything bad, that's for sure. The burger, BLT (it's made with softshell crab!), mussels are all very good dishes, but nothing has ever come close to being amazing.

Overall, I would say Luke is a mediocre restaurant that has decent food. I will continue to go for happy hour drinks, but that's the only draw for me.

Luke was great! We got off the airplane and this was our first pit stop for dinner.

We tried:
Large Platter for Raw Bar
Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte"(aka Shrimp&Grits)
Shrimp & Crab "Etouffée" (aka Seafood w/ Cavatelli)

Service was so great, Rosalynn and Elliott were very attentive and answered all our questions. Food came out quickly.

The Raw Bar Platter came with oysters, tuna tartare, crab ravigote. I loved the homemade shrimp chips and remoulade. The tuna tartare tasted a little bit like spicy mayo tuna in sushi rolls, tbh. But they were nice enough to give us some complimentary  oysters! ANY SHRIMP HERE IS DELICIOUS. Everything is so fresh. However, I felt like the portion size for the tuna and the crab were a little small.

The entrees were delicious. I am usually not a fan of tomato based sauces, but the pasta was very good. Again, the shrimp is SOOO fresh. The crab meat was in the sauce, rather than chunks on top, so I couldn't taste it as much.

I only tried a bit of grits, but it was very good. The gravy-like sauce on top was delicious though.

Would come back again for ambiance, food, and service.
Old school building vibe, sort of feels 1920s to me which is fun. Cool staff. Dining room is open and not best for intimate setting but good for casual business dinners with good food.
The food is simply fresh and delicious! The mussels, Lüke salad, and bread pudding were amazing!

Excellent!!! We had 3 hungry young kids in tow and there was a long wait, but we stuck it out because we really wanted to try it! And we are so glad we did!! Even the not-hungry-anymore kids were happy. They even wanted to go back the next day! We had the shrimp and also the Brussels sprouts as appetizers - delicious! Even our 5-year-old was chowing these down! Two of the kids split an adult cheeseburger and fries, and loved it! The oldest had the mac-and-cheese off the kids menu and was pleased with her choice. My husband got the Tabasco Honey Fried Chicken and a cup of the Crawfish Bisque - both excellent!! I got the Matzo Ball and Roast Chicken Soup. It was perfect for the dreary, rainy afternoon! The elegant feel of the restaurant is top notch. Our waiter was friendly and gave wonderful recommendations of things to do in New Orleans (we took 3 or 4 of his suggestions, and he was spot on!). We got to sit in the back dining area where we could see the kitchen in action, and the kids thought that was pretty neat! We recommend this place, for sure!

Get the oysters! Best raw oysters I've ever had, they actually converted me to the oyster obsessed person I am now. We had the Cape Cod ones that were on the menu that night and they were huge, fresh and delicious. We also had the stuffed oysters, which were incredible, the crab fritters, which were fairly average (Acme's are better), the shrimp and grits (delish, even for me who doesn't love shrimp) and the bread pudding - AMAZING. Way better than Commader's Palace. As you can probably tell, we did quite the food tour of NOLA and this was by far my favorite meal. Great, courteous service, tasty drinks (we tried the mint julep and a spicy tequila-based one) and we were seated very promptly with a reservation. A tad pricey compared to other restaurants in the area, but not at all unreasonable (although I am from NYC, so take that as you will). Not sure when I'll be back to New Orleans, but I do know this will be my first stop when I am.

I have nothing bad to say about Luke, it is my absolute favorite restaurant in New Orleans.  You must go for Happy Hour and stay for dinner.  The atmosphere is lively and the service is attentive.  Trust me, this place will make your nipples perk and your mouth salivate.

Stick to the bread and soups folks. Ordered a hot chocolate and a cinnamon roll: hot chocolate was a tepid glass of sugar. Wasn't drinkable at all. Even my 2 year old said it was "yucky". Cinnamon roll....let's just say I've never seen a cinnamon roll that didn't have a center until today. You can get fresher ones (and better tasting) from any local gas station. We got a couple of cookies for the kids also....MAYBE worth about $0.50, definitely not the $2.69. Once again, stick to gas station treats. Your wallet and palate will be better off.

Went to happy hour on Thursday. Only had oysters and cocktails. Oysters are very fresh. They give you a giant glass of french 75 too, which was very tasty. My only complaint is that we didn't seem to have a specific waiter. We waited 15 minutes and no one came to serve us, we had to wave someone down to get our orders in. And then the orders never came, we had to wave someone else down. I gave a very small tip, considering we barely got any service. But REALLY GOOD OYSTERS.

Our server was wonderful and took good care of us.  The Étouffée was AMAZING... however the gumbo was very salty and was warm.  

Menu is limited and its a gourmet restaurant... so not really kid friendly (they do have a fancy hamburger)

After meeting long wait times at various brunch spots around town, we checked online to see if we could get a reservation at Lüke. Lucky for us, there was a spot available 30 minutes in the future, so we made our way over and arrived to a relatively empty restaurant: bonus. 

Apparently I shouldn't have mentioned our reservation, as we were forced to sit at the bar and wait for "our" table despite there being more than several available at the time. Not a huge deal, but really obnoxious at the same time. Luckily service got better from there. 

Our server's name was Gene and he was an absolute dream. Precious, charming, and totally on top of everything, he really enhanced the whole experience. I chose the shrimp and grits and decided to add two poached eggs to it, just to go a little over the top. And over the top it was. Absolutely delectable, although not *quite* as memorable as the same dish I had in Charleston and a heck of a lot more expensive. 

I'd recommend Lüke whether you're a tourist or a local, and I'd recommend you ask for Gene. He makes this place 4 stars.

Extra great service from arrival to departure. Love a waiter that has a favorite dish and is willing to give an honest review of the dishes rather than "everything is good."
The heirloom tomato salad was not for us, but the brussel sprouts are a definite- yes!!!  Really nicely roasted with excellent full flavor. 
I had the shrimp n grits with crab on top- OMG, the grits are just absolutely amazing. As in slap yourself amazing- 
My friend had the burger (minus the bun) and said it was delicious. 
We ended with the carrot cake- there are few words to explain how truly sublime the brownie like carrot cake was- my gluten free friend couldn't help herself but have some it was that good. Just WOW!

The Sunday morning started out a little rough since Saturday night ended at 5:30 am.  Got to Lūke around 11:25 am for a quick bite to eat before my flight out. I was a little worried it might take awhile since it was fairly busy.  I sat at the bar and the bartenders were super friendly. They made several suggestions, and I settled on the chicken cordon bleu sandwich with fries. It came out ultra fast and steaming hot. It was outstanding. I even liked the little cutting board it come on. Unfortunately they said this item is going away the following week-long but if it pops back up on the menu, consider it. 

I will definelybe back next time I'm in the city. Although the amazing sandwich is gone, I'm sure everything else is delicious based off of what I experienced so far.

Staff and food were all tremendous.

We made a reservation through open table for a large party of 7 for dinner, which is obviously a benefit as not all places allow a res through open table, let alone a large party. Our table was ready, and our appetizer orders were taken right away. However after that service was a little shaky. It took quite a while to get refills on drinks, and we ran out of water on the table quickly. When the entrees came, my entree was incorrect and I had to wait. I encouraged the rest of the table to go ahead as their food was getting cold as we sat, but as this was a dinner among colleagues it was a bit awkward. They did then bring my food but by then everyone was half done and I burned my mouth trying to catch up. The wait staff never really apologized. The food itself was good, but not outstanding in my opinion.

Come here for the happy hour. $0.50 an oyster. The food is good also, but expensive. The shrimp and grit was $24. Another $12 to add some crab meat. It was very good, but not quite a good deal.
I'll definitely come back for happy hour.

Delicious! ! Took the waiter's recommendation and had the fried oysters and the shrimp and grits. By far the best I've had.
Service was excellent and quick. Price was a bit above average at $40 for my dinner, but well worth it. Definately want to go back again.

Visited twice now in last few months, last time for Thanksgiving Day lunch. They had Turducken and five kinds of stuffing. I chose oyster.

Son ordered the steak and wife had fish. Food was grand, ambience perfect and after meal cappuccino spot on. 

Fresh oysters at the bar. Bistro style casualness with an energetic vibe. 

Too full for dessert but will try next trip in.

Recommend and will return.

I came here a few years ago for the first time after my fiancé read an article that they had one of the best hamburgers in the whole country. 

I remember that first visit, we were in the french quarter enjoying lots of drinking and listening to jazz music and we were in the mood for that burger so we got here really late and they were still really busy. We decided to order the burger to share and an order of Shrimp and Grits. 

The article was right (the hamburger was so good) and the shrimp and grits were also amazing.

I came back last week because of that burger. We shared it again and it was still awesome. They didn't have the shrimp and grits on the menu anymore but they had plenty of variety. 

The burger and the staff at the bar were so good that we came back again the next day to enjoy happy hour where we ate a ton of oysters (and another burger).

Best place we are at while in Nola! Firstly shrimp and crab etouffee was heavenly! The service was excellent - Richie Rich took such good care of us. They have a great happy hour deal on appetizers and drinks. Definitely a spot to check out!

Stopped in this Cost location for a quick breakfast this morning and I was really disappointed. Something that is always super important to me, ESPECIALLY at chain restaurants, is service. As a former employee of a large chain restaurant, I know that management is everything. 

This morning I was disappointed in the service I received from all members of staff. The guy who took my order rudely corrected me when I ordered a "steak and cheese" instead of the "steak and egg" as it says on the menu. It was just unnecessary and I apologized for the mix-up and moved along with my day, despite being frustrated. Again, the staff member at the cash register basically barked at myself and the other two people in line with short answers and statements like "for here?", "receipt?", and "you want milk?"

The food and the iced coffee were fine, but I will most definitely walk out of my way to go somewhere else for breakfast and lunch when I am around campus because of the really poor service.

This place is my favorite!! Stopped by on a busy night and was luckily able to sit at the bar. They were doing a half price oyster special which made us order a dozen. Only to 14+ oysters on the house. Delicious and highly recommend.

This review is for the HAPPY HOUR only.

Lum had a chance to leave early from work so we decided to take advantage of the opportunity and actually make it in time for a happy hour special.  Hard to pass up on $0.50 oysters and half-off drinks, amirite? Fun new fact, at least for me: P&J oysters (the ones offered for Luke's happy hour) are from a local oyster shucking company in New Orleans. I still have so much to learn about this city.

FOOD: Oyster heaven (at least in quantity).

Over the course of our stay, the two of us ordered six-dozen oysters. The majority of them were on the smaller side, but thats probably more a result of the oil spill ramifications than anything else. However, what Luke can control is the amount of water still left in the shells. To an extent, all oysters will have some water residue as a result of cleaning, but these were literally soaked in water to the point where slurping the oysters down wasn't really an option since you'd get a mouthful of liquid to go with them. On the plus side, they were very clean. I was also hoping for another sauce besides the basic cocktail and horseradish, but it wasn't as big of a deal as the water issue.

Lum's mint julep was definitely on the strong side so depending on your drinking preferences this can be a positive or negative. Luke has a couple in-house brews available as well, and the Luke Fru (blonde) I tried was actually pretty decent as far as blondes go: "wheat-ie" taste, smooth finish.

SERVICE: Professional but absent-minded and over-extended.

Our server was nice, engaging, quick with jokes, and seemed like he knew what he was doing. The problem was that it looked like he was the only server for the entire front room so it took awhile to get anything from him. Even when he seemed like he had a spare moment it was almost impossible to get his attention. Case in point, I was more than willing to order at least another drink or two and another two dozen oysters from him, but with all the long waits in-between service (drink sitting empty 15 minutes, finished oysters on table 10 minutes) happy hour was unfortunately over and we had other engagements. From my viewpoint, it looks like they need more staff.

While the staffing issue is pretty much uncontrollable by the staff on the floor, short-changing customers on oysters is not. Good thing I counted our oyster orders because we were short four on the first order of two dozen. That's pretty unacceptable, but kudos to our server for taking care of it and adding the missing ones to our next order.

ATMOSPHERE: Like stepping back in time.

I like it. Newspapers hanging from wood poles at different sections of the restaurant, cherry wood everywhere, hunting trophy head over the bar, sweet bar stools. With the music playing overhead it felt like a scene from Boardwalk Empire. It's one of those restaurants where someone could have a nice relaxing meal but it wouldn't seem out of place to see higher-society types getting a little boisterous. Noise suits Luke.

RELATIVITY: How does it compare to expectations and other restaurants in its class?

Slightly not as good as expected, especially when considering the class of restaurant that Luke is embracing.  One glance at their regular dinner menu and it's clear what type of clientele they are catering to and what style of dining they're wanting to provide. The quality didn't match up with the expectations, I guess.

OVERALL: Three stars overall, no bonus for relativity.

This is probably one of the best happy hour deals you're going to see in the city value-wise, but if a place wants to convince me to come back for a dinner experience then even the nitty-gritty parts of happy hour should be up to snuff. I guess based on Luke's pedigree, I expected better-prepared oysters and a bit better service than what we received.

I always make it a point to go to Luke when I'm in New Orleans, the food is SOOOOOO amazing.

My favorite thing to get, and I recommend that YOU try, is the flammenkuchen! Besides being fun to say (LOL!) it.is.DELICIOUS!!!! OMG!!!!! The sweet carmalized onions with salty bacon + cheese, OMGGGGG!! Just try it! Party in your mouth!

I also got the Luke Burger, more of those carmalized onions, so good. We went for dinner and the place was packed, so you may have a wait. However, the waiter(s) were pretty awesome, and attentive.

Again, don't forget, if you are here, get the FLAMMENKUCHEN!!!!!

Savannah took great care of us with the help of Patrick.
Order whatever she suggests. Savannah is a pro.
We suggest the shellfish platter, crab appetizer, étouffée, soft shell crab sandwich, shrimp and grits, steamed chocolate and the seasonal pumpkin cake! The three of us had a lovely meal that I know I'll go back for when in NoLa. My only neutral thought is the gumbo wasn't exciting.
Vusi! Luke's has a great Server that is very informative and accommodating!  Great service and great food! Oysters great! Mussels great!  Gulf shrimp (huge ! ) great !

I have been here for lunch and dinner. Very casual.

Small winelist, but lots of good stuff. Try the daily specials. The redfish and brisket specials are fantastic. Located in the Hilton which requires they are open 365.

Also try the crab salad and stuffed shrimp with orange hollandaise. Amazing sandwiches at lunch. My wife had a softshell crab blt that was enormous.

This place is slipping. Service has gotten slow.
Best cheese burger around and gorgeous place. The service was on point. Not a thing wrong with this gem.

I came with a group of six on a Friday around 3pm, purely for the means of wanting to get their happy hour oysters. The hostess told us that there were no tables available because of reservations. After debating, we told her that we were willing to split up into small groups for tables and she directed us to a table of 6 chairs.. then proceeded to ask if we would be done by 6pm. I don't know if I've ever had a meal at a restaurant that lasted 3 hours. I think I understand where she was coming from but it was still a little off-putting that she wasn't going to offer us an empty table for a reservation 3 hours away.

That aside, this place is pretty nice and our server was friendly and on-top of his game. We ordered 6 dozen gulf oysters (one for each of us) and I got a cup of the seafood gumbo. The rest of the table also ordered drinks. The gumbo was alright. I think I would prefer a small mom&pop's gumbo. On to the main attraction of the meal.. the oysters. They took a while to come out (understandable, busy happy hour) so my group was able to drink a couple drinks each. The oysters, when they finally came out? Totally worth it. They were some of the best oysters I've ever had, fresh and good sized.

If you're looking for good happy hour oysters, this place should be on your list.

50 cent oysters?! Too good to be true, but it is for REALz!!! 

What a steal.  I had two dozen and could have gone for more.  I just feel bad for the workers cause they barely get any tip on such cheap items.

They were really chill though and did not judge us for ordering so much.

This deal is a secret.  Without Yelp, I would not have known.  It's not listed anywhere and they don't volunteer this deal out unless you ask.  

That's all I ate here.  My friend ordered some bills to make it more worthwhile for the waiter to continue serving us.

Good location but not great food for breakfast
I went to Luke based on great reviews of it for dinner. I didn't experience great food for breakfast, however. I ordered a standard breakfast of scrambled eggs, bacon, and a biscuit. The food was very bland, and the biscuit didn't come with jam or butter until I asked for it. Otherwise the service was rapid, and the waiter was nice. If you're looking for a good breakfast, try elsewhere.

Clean, simple atmosphere. Let's the architecture speak for itself. The military plaques hung behind the bar are crooked and misaligned as if haphazardly placed in a rush before an uncle came to visit, expecting to see his honors displayed. Other than that, it's pretty to look at. 

Crab bisque is AMAZING! Our appetizer took an insane amount of time, so they threw in a few free cups of bisque. It was the only thing we didn't actually order, and it was by by far best thing we tasted. 

Bartender was great- warm, nice, helpful. We'd definitely go back if it wasn't so unbelievable crowded all the time.

Great place, the service was amazing!! Were our first time in the city and the hosts gave us a famous drink of New Orleans called French 75 ( DELICIOUS!!).
For dinner we ordered the GULF SHRIMP (great great great!!), definitely the best one, with creole tomatoes, garlic and homemade pasta! And after the Moules and frites! If you are mussels fan is great, the sauce is awesome!
Good food the wait staff was phenomenal. Nice selection of cocktails would recommend for dinner.

I was here last week for breakfast. The food was good. My mother loved the pancakes with berry cane syrup. I had the southern breakfast, with the cane syrup sausage, which were delicious. 

        However, the service was terrible. Our sever was very nice, but he seemed to be the only server for the entire dining room. It took almost half an hour just to get a coffee refill. There were several people in server outfits just standing around. We asked one of them to bring water for the table, but it never came. I would give this place another try based on the food, but there are too many good restaurants in New Orleans to waste time and money on bad service.

Did you know Elm Cafe does catering! I've actually never been to Elm, but I've been to Burrow and know they make good sandwiches. So when I was searching for a lunch caterer for a business meeting, I was delighted to see that Elm Cafe not only catered, but they had fantastic prices. The menu consisted of gourmet sandwiches, side salad, and cookie, and was about $13-$14 per person. 

The food arrived well on time, and was so easy to set up. The sandwiches were really delicious, and amazing fresh bread!! The meat on the sandwiches was all local... Pine Haven beef and smoked ham, and Valhalla smoked turkey breast. And the cookies were humongous and delicious!

Honestly, I was super impressed. I've ordered a lot of lunch catering and this is by far the best value and amazing quality. 

And the best part... there were left overs. I've got enough Quinoa salad to last me the rest of the week :)  I guess that's because there were a lot of men at this meeting, and there's something about men not enjoying quinoa.

Yes, I know I said I'd never go back. I said that after my pervious two- and one-star reviews. But I can not be held 100% responsible for the things that I do when I am NOT under the influence of caffeine...

So, third review is the charm....I'm pretty sure this location is under new management and for sure they've hired some new (super nice! competent! friendly!) staff. 

I still only go in for drinks (and usually early a.m. when there aren't many people in there) but they make them perfect (1-pump and extra-shot) every time. Served with a smile & engaging conversation. Side story: one night when I was waiting for the trolley one of the baristas was also at the station and asked me if I had ever been there (to Cosi) & how my experience was!

Way to go Cosi!  Tell your morning coffee bar staff how fabulous they are!

I had a great experience here. We came in for happy hour on a Friday. It was busy but we were quickly seated. 1/2 off specialty drinks and $.50 oysters...they were great! We split a ribeye that was cooked to perfection and topped with lightly seasoned crab meat. Excellent!

Wow...what can I say about a John Besh restaurant that hasn't already been said.  His food is one of a kind.  Its a great take on local ingredients and flavors.  I loved my experience eating here.  The shrimp and grits is phenomenal.  Next time im here, ill be back.

I ordered the LÜKE BREAKFAST:  TWO EGGS COOKED ANY STYLE, BACON, HOUSE-MADE ANDOUILLE SAUSAGE, BUTTERMILK BISCUIT GRITS.

It was so rich that I was sick for two days. The bacon looked like it was deep fried which I have never seen before. The sausage did not taste like andouille. I didn't eat it. 

I would not recommend.

The places was amazing!   Got lucky due to we didn't have a reservation. The food so delicious!  I ordered the tuna it's was on point, definitely recommend ordering it rare.  My friend got the duck it's was amazing, I don't even like rice but theirs is crispy which I liked a lot.  Dede the manager just made our last night in New Orleans amazing!  Loved her personality and awesome customer service!  She honestly went over and beyond to take care of us!!! This place is definitely a must if you are in New Orleans.  Great atmosphere, amazing food, super fresh seafood, and great staff.  Stop in and say hi to Dede for me!

This place is a MUST if you're in the area. The BEST crab dip and crawfish soup. We stayed at the Hilton property and decided we might as well try it since we were starving. It was so good that even on our second trip we went out of our way to eat here. The best French 75 in all of New Orleans and for all of us who aren't familiar with boudin...try it here!!

Stopped in for lunch. Crab bisque was wonderful! House salad was very good too, but seemed to take longer than expected for a salad to be made/served. Staff was very friendly and attentive at the bar.

We ordered the court-bouillon from the express menu and jumbo Louisiana shrimp. The gumbo soup came with my order of court-bouillon was the best I had in New Orleans and the combination of shrimp, oyster, crab, red fish with rice was amazing! The other order was the jumbo shrimp and together with cheese tasted perfectly rich and fresh. Our waiter was very knowledgeable even though he recommended a draft that was just ok. They also offered breakfast and brunch and we overheard the customers next table visited 3rd time in two days. Definitely a place to spend a night in French Quarter.
Good food, well styled restaurant. Better suited for the sushi connoisseur however. As a new restaurant they are still feeling their way to being consistent routinely.

Come here and park your a** here from 3-6 for their happy hour, half off drinks (beer and cocktail) and 50 cents oyster and they are good!

My only caution is don't order shots of Jack Daniel like I did, it like like $9 a shot, stick with beer and their cocktail.

As my first John Besh restaurant, Lüke left me a bit underwhelmed. I went with my co workers who had always said great things about the restaurant. I went with the red fish, which was good, but not something better than a fish dish you might get at a chain like Cheesecake Factory. My colleague got the roasted chicken which actually looked amazing, and will be my choice should we return.

Ambiance was simple but nice. Service was attentive, but nothing spectacular. Bottom line, Lüke is a good restaurant, but with so many other great restaurants in the area, it doesn't seem to stand out to me.

It was never a good experience the first time. But I tried it a second time for something small like coffee. First and foremost the service was extremely slow. I had gone there with family and ordered 2 lattés. It took them almost like half an hour to make the drinks. This was the time when the restaurant was empty and not much crowd. I can only imagine what happens at rush hour.  When the lattés finally came they tasted so dull. It was like they did not add any espresso shots or maybe just added half a shot. I don't know. The taste was not at all good and very sub-par if you compare it to a Starbucks or any other coffee shop for the matter.  This coffee was the worst. This experience left me and my family feeling disappointed and we vowed never to go there again. Avoid if you can.

LOVE Oysters and drinks at this place.  We had the chargrilled oysters at ACME.  It's good.  But, Luke's fresh and fried oysters are the BOMB!!  We had a dozen of raw and half dozen of fried to start.  We ordered another dozen raw and dozen fried in the second round.  They are definitely fresh and big fat juicy oysters!!!  I had Door#3 cocktail to start.  I think it's a little too sweet for my taste.  If you are going to get one drink only, you should get French 75.  So good!!!!!  Hubby had a bowl of gumbo which he likes a lot.  All in all, it's the best meal for me thus far at NOLA.
Great food and staff was very attentive. The raw oysters and gumbo were excellent. I think I had the Luke breakfast, which was good but my friends' meals by far exceeded my expectations.

Nice place with good food! We had dinner here on our first night in NOLA and it was delicious. I ordered the fish (grilled instead of sautéed) with some crabmeat on top while my wife had the shrimp and grits with crabmeat on top. We both we're extremely satisfied with our choices! Taste was very rich and the food was well cooked. If there's anything to point out it's the price, but you get what you pay for right?! Recommended while in NOLA if you're staying in a nearby hotel.

Probably the best oysters I've ever had. Wife had a Riverbend cocktail: delicious. The German style alt beer was great. The Belgian-style fries were disappointing--a paper cone filled with tiny pieces of what were once french fries (kinda like the very bottom of a McDonalds french fry bag). Service at the bar was ok. The entrees looked great, but we were full from the two dozen oysters.

Great atmosphere and the happy hour some of the best value for money.
Personally I am a small oyster fan...(Hate complaining that most oysters were way bigger than my taste) but then again - it was still fantastic.!!

During my 5 days in New Orleans, I came to Luke twice! The happy hour oysters are amazing. Not only are they cheap, but also huge, sweet, and not sandy! I've been craving them ever since and am slightly upset that they have ruined all other oysters for me, especially the puny ones served in NYC. 

I also got the Pate of Rabbit and Chicken, and it was so so delicious. The flavors were strong, but not overwhelming, and I savored every last bit almost as much as I savored the oysters. Luke is definitely a must-go-to in New Orleans!

My friends and I were drawn to Luke based on the incredible photos and reviews -- upon arrival we were thrilled to find everything even better than we imagined! From the food to the service the entire experience was incredible. Our server Nicholas V made us feel right at home and did an amazing job of answering our many questions and providing delicious menu recommendations. Luke will definitely be my first stop on my next trip to NOLA!
Came here during the daily happy hour -- half price off wines and a dozen oysters for $6. Great high class atmosphere, but at a bargain price.

08/12/2011 - 11:25 am

On my way back to pack around 10:45 am I saw Lüke and checked out the Lunch Menu.  Inquired the Hostess of Lunch hours and she told me it's ready when I am.  Same was said when I was at P&G which was weird as if New Orleans early-open restaurants have Breakfast/Lunch hours intertwined.  I'll dropped by after when my Breakfast dissipates.

Back soon after to have the same welcoming Hostess show me the way to my table.  Btw, I was in my city-sporty-casual gear lugging a carry-on and they welcomed me just the same.  Brasserie setting reminds me of Manhattan, NY but the big windows allow for plenty of natural light to flow.  The Vintage Pulley-and-Belt driven Ceiling Fan weren't rotating but cool to see nonetheless.

The initial attraction I saw in the Morning was their Daily Lunch Special($15.00) and as it was Friday, Seafood was the deal.  Mint Julep($8.50) was strong on Bourbon weak on Mint/Cane Syrup.  Rookie mistake, I should've let the ice melt to mellow the alcohol down.  Oh well, better for the Flight home.

Seafood Gumbo a la Creole(Cup) - Soup Starter

One sip of the Hot served soup and my mind went haywire.  This was the New Orleans I flew 1,300 Miles to find and I didn't even dig into the Seafood ingredients yet.  My photos might be a bit blurred because my instincts wanted to take a photo while my mind just said WTF you waiting for?  Looks to be Andouille Sausage, Okra, plump Gulf Oysters and Rice added to the mix.  I even found a tiny Pearl in an Oyster, Jackpot!  Too bad this wasn't Harrahs.

Redfish "Court-Bouillon" with Crab, Shrimp, Oysters and Rice - Main

Served on cast-iron plate, it served the same plump Gulf Oysters, Shrimp, Blue Crab Claws in a thick consistency Bouillon while the Redfish was hidden underneath the Rice still cooking(slash overcooking) but flaky.  Not as exciting as Gumbo but healthy Meal portion, good value considering all Seafood served.

I left happily and it helped that my Waiter was playful with conversation for the extent of my Meal, checked on me plenty looking like a person satisfied with his customer service position at Lüke's.

New Orleans Saints season opener.  Go Saints!

This guy John Besh has his act together. I would describe this place as a bistro with a german twist? it was packed to the rafters when we went for lunch...we just made it in before all the people that work in the area started coming in for their lunch breaks. I had a charcuterie platter that re-inforced my love of offal and meat by-products. Seriously, the hallmark of a great chef is one that can turn organ meat that most people wrinkle their nose at into something wonderously delicious...and John Besh and his talented do that here, and at his restaurant August. I also had oysters that were CLEAN (read my review of Acme) and pig's feet made into a croquette and fried. The fact that I had pig head and pig feet in one meal was rather impressive I think.

Had ribeye, Brussels sprouts, onion tart & bread pudding. Ribeye was delicious after we added salt. Brussels sprouts were excellent. Bread pud was great --a little too sweet for our taste but we suffered through. Worse thing: ketchup in little Heinz bottles. Very tacky for a white tablecloth restaurant. Best thing: Elliot our waiter.  He was knowledgeable, atttentive and very very nice.

This review is for Happy Hour Only. 

A trusted fellow food lover suggested Luke as my go-to spot for oysters while in New Orleans.  Not only are the oysters 50 cents a piece at happy hour, but drinks (except top shelf) are half off.  We went twice during our 5 day trip.  Oysters were fresh and delicious; drinks were well made.  Even more impressive was the bartender, Tomas, who was very informed about the various beverages and was able to suggest good beers based on our interests as well as whipped up some tasty NOLA staples (Sazerac was delish!). Next time I pay a visit to the town, I will make sure to return for Happy Hour!

Ate at the bar as I was dining solo and late night.   Loved it.  Their pate dish is probably the best I've ever had.  I also really liked the shrimp and grits, although I would probably prefer to turn the cheese level down from an 11 to an 8.   Great cocktails but a mediocre beer list.  That being said, this a great spot for a late night bite at a bar.

Once again, I wish we could give half stars, because I'd prefer to give this place 3.5 stars.  The infamous shrimp and grits were tasty, but I failed to see what was so "life-changing" about them, especially when I compared the grits here to the grits at Restaurant August (both John Besh places).  However, the oysters here were possibly better (fresher and cleaner tasting) than the ones we had at Acme Oyster House the night before.  The hamburger was also really good, too (it's won awards because they grind up steak meat for the patty), and my mom really enjoyed her first ever mint julep =)  We really liked our server, who was dynamic and fun, and we kept him updated on the score of the Saints-Falcons game.  Dinner was a success, and it was a relaxing and casual night.  To top it all off, the Saints won that night, so the walk back to our hotel was entertaining as we passed several Saints fans celebrating in true NOLA style =)
This place gives new meaning to Shrimp and Grits....AMAZING!  energetic vibe. A bit loud but great place to gather with friends. I'll be back on my next visit!

Stopped here for a quick drink and couple dozen oysters. The service was quick and the oysters tasted very fresh. The oysters were huge! We definitely ordered a few too many and has leftovers. Would definitely come back for dinner as I've heard great things about the restaurant.

I would not recommend this company. After a series of mistakes and spending the month of July without AC, the folks at Fahrenheit finally scheduled our install for today (Aug 13) between 9-11am. When they DID NOT show up, we called only to be told they were not coming and it would be 2 MORE WEEKS at the earliest. We are very disappointed with their disregard for customers, complete lack of communication, and poor follow through.

Luke is a busy and happening restaurant with a bar in the French Quarter. I was walking around looking for a nice restaurant for dinner and definitely glad to discover this place. It's quite popular so it was packed when I walked in around peak dinner time. I waited around for like 15-20 minutes for a spot at the bar.

The Luke Burger sounded pretty good - Allen Benton's bacon, caramelized onions, Emmentaler cheese (apparently from Switzerland) with housemade fries, for $16.5. Definitely a good choice and I'd recommend it. 

I'm a sucker for pate, so I got the rabbit and chicken pate, which sounded interesting; it turner out to be quite delicious. The caramelized brussels sprouts was also very good.

I'd highly recommend this restaurant, which I'd imagine would make a fun dinner date place.
Luke is great. Its john besh...you cant really go wrong there. The burger is great, oyster happy hour is a must and the French 75 is a fantastic drink.
Fantastic lunch options! I had Brussel sprouts, bisque, oysters, shrimp & grits, and Chappapeela Pork Ragout -- all amazing! Fantastic service, lovely atmosphere; recommend!

Between the two John Besh, Lüke and August, August wins hands down. Granted we went to Lüke for lunch and August for dinner. The food at Lüke was ordinary and the lunch menu extremely small. 

Go to August.
Wow, do not miss the Grilled Oysters with crabmeat and shrimp. The Jalapeño Grits with shrimp is a must. The 17.00 burger was good but stick to the seafood. I will definitely  be back ...

Oh my goodness, what a phenomenal experience. The ambiance is great, we went on a busy Thursday but were seated in minutes, maybe call for reservation if you don't like to wait at all, I can imagine it's busy on the weekends. The service was EXCELLENT.  We had two servers, a male (I think his name was Rich, Richy Rich? Lol) and a female. Both awesome. He showed me a trick in eating the muscles I ordered that he said his wife uses, using the shell to extract the meat. He treated our table like we were friends, and it was so welcoming. The shell trick worked like a charm. He was charming, had a great sense of humor and was helpful. Service can make or break a meal, and this was no exception the food was great and the service was even better. This was probably some of the best service I've received in a restaurant. I'd highly recommend Luke.
This place has amazing Brussel sprouts.  Absolutely fantastic, best dish I've ever tried. If your going definitely order as side.

Chipotle is a cult. I belong. When it is time to commit mass suicide, I will do it laying in a pile of pico and guac. 

Seriously though, Chipotle wins my heart, mind, and stomach on multiple levels. First of all, they boldly rely on REAL flavor. Unlike places like qdoba or taco bell, they don't smother their food in queso to win your taste buds. No, they rely on high quality, often local and hormone free ingredients. They are generous with your made-to-order requests (always always always ask for extra cilantro). It is, and is priced like, fast food. However, It can also be a very healthy option.

My regular dish made to my specifications is a light 420 calories. This is incredible for how filling and tasty it is... especially considering its fast-food classification.

Treat yourself. Join the cult. Never step foot in Qdoba again.

We came here nearly everyday of our 5 day vacation just for the $.50 oysters and the cheap happy hour drinks. Service was so much better sitting at the bar. The drinks were stronger, service was a lot friendlier as well as efficient, and the bartenders were attractive, pleasant and worked hard.
 I wished i had sat at the bar the first 4 visits, that way I wouldn't have had to endure the same short haired, standoffish waitress and the mousey, wavy brown haired waiter. Both were very unwelcoming and weren't very apologetic when they would repeatedly forget parts of our order. The white coats that they wore were constantly dirty with very apparent stains. I noticed they never changed coats because I would be staring at the same stains the next day. The hostesses up front could use a bit of work as well. Gee, you are greeting paying customers, would it kill you to smile?

With all this aside, the oysters were cheap and fresh, drinks were cheap, and our last visit sitting at the bar makes my review 4 stars

* the restaurant was about a 2 min walk from the Le Pavillon Hotel

Came here for my last stop until I went back to Cali and it wasn't a bad choice. I've been reading that this place is to go for happy hour raw oysters. So come and check it out during those hours if you can. Other than that the food was good. We had the shrimp and grits and the Croque Madame with an egg. These were really good. Also you can have Sunday brunch without a Mimosa. Also try the Crab Bisque, very good as well. The only problem we had wit that was not ordering a bowl of it.

I recently went on a trip with my girlfriends to New Orleans for my birthday and let me tell you this restaurant did not disappoint. The chicken and potatoes was so good, but not only that but the service was amazing to say the least. They were very generous and kind people. They gave us champagne and desserts on the house because it was my birthday. I don't think I lifted a finger because their staff was always on top of everything. If I'm ever in New Orleans again I'm coming here without a doubt.

I was in New Orleans for a major conference, and Luke had reservations out the yin yang so we dined at the bar. I was super excited to try some of John Besh's food having seen him on Top Chef masters. 

I gave into fellow yelpers and my natural inclinations by ordering a cup of gumbo and shrimp & grits. The gumbo was fantastic with a really deep, rounded (did I really just say that?!) flavor that I couldn't get enough of! The shrimp and grits deliciousness was only made better by the addition of andouille sausage that gave it salty intense kick. The grits were the fluffiest I'd ever had, and I have had some fluffy freakin' grits before. It was like a corn-cloud drifting across my tongue. 

The bar service was very good and attentive. I will definitely be back next time I'm in town.

possibly the best shrimp and grits ive ever had. shrimp was gigantic and grits taste like they were hand ground. who knows. not overly spicy if thats a concern, even with the jalapenos

it had huge chunks of sausage and the service was superb. 

table bread was some par baked generic baguette

i would go back in a heart beat. 

JEANS: OK by far
ORDER: wait staff
"Pearl" in the 19$ dollar oysters. Sounds like a good deal! If you are a high fan of "pearls", please come here and try their oysters! 4 out of 6 times you will find a "pearl"! Good luck have fun!

Good things:
1) As with many of the John Besh restaurants, this place has a great happy hour
2) Good oysters

We go here for happy hour pretty often, as they have 1/2 beer, wine, and specialty cocktails, along with 50 cent oysters. And they are the good, briney, yummy oysters! I would recommend the happy hour to anyone and everyone. 

Since its near where I work, Ive also been there for a few "fancy" lunches for celebrations. The food is pretty good, its just not my favorite in the area for the category of "fancy lunch".

I had a really excellent brunch here. The mimosas were a bit weak but my shrimp & grits made up for the lack of taste in the drinks. The ambience was great for a casual Sunday and I can see coming here for a dinner date or business dinner.

I had a bite of a friend's French toast, I don't like food stuffed with creams so it wasn't for me. If stuffed food is your thing the French toast will be a winner.

Went here for brunch while on vacation, and it was so delicious. I had the crab omelet. It was light and fluffy and came with a salad that had a sweet dressing on it. My boyfriend had the yogurt, which he enjoyed. His also came with toast and housemade preserves, which I couldn't stop eating. I would definitely go back.

**Happy Hours are a Broke Nursing Student's Best Friend:  The 1st of a 3-Part Series**

Luke serves the largest, freshest, most divine oysters I have ever enjoyed...and they are only 50 cents each from 3-6pm on weekdays!  Their baked oysters (not on special, unfortunately) are a food-gasm on the half shell.  Better than Drago's, better than everyone in town.  Speaking of which, where you at Oyster Fest last weekend, eh?  I expected Luke to be showing off down there at Woldenberg Park, stealing everyone's thunder.

Happy hour specials also include half-off cocktails (the French 75 is my personal favorite) and half-off glasses of wine.  

Luke's happy hour has earned a place on my reigning Top 3 deals in town and is destination of choice for my comrades and I post-exams!

I usually don't give a negative review without trying a location twice which I did at Luke. First night I went at 9 on a Monday and they were apparently cleaning up for the night and had little regard for the patrons. As a rather surly and obscene blond walked into the restaurant cursing I was disappointed to find out that was one of the bartenders. I sat at the bar and ordered "THE" burger and their house amber. OOOPS they were out of their own stock brew.  As I mentioned the place was near empty and yet it took a full 20 plus minute for my burger and fries to arrive.  And when it did I still had to ask for silverware and salt and pepper.  Actually I reached over the bar and got it myself because if I was going to wait for the bartender it would have been a long wait. Fries while supposed to be spectacular fell flat as they were as cold and old as a gutter cigarette butt.  The burger was served on a cutting board and I agree with another reviewer, this is gross. The burger that is so highly touted comes on an untoasted slightly chilled old roll. Sad. The meat was cooked medium on half of the burger and rare to raw on the other. While the meat was gently prepared and tender it was not particularly flavorful. The bartender said smugly "How's that burger?" I replied "I've had better" She looked at me like I had three heads instead of asking how she could improve my experience. After she splashed me with bar water a few times during her sloppy nightly cleanup ritual I paid and left. 
I found myself 3 blocks away with friends the next night and they were looking for a final meal. I felt I owed it t John Besh to give Luke a second try. MISTAKE. We sat in the back and I have to say our server was excellent in every way. I am sorry I don't recall her name. Sadly the food missed the mark again. I ordered the pressed couchon sandwich which was warmish in the outside with cold guts. My mates had the rib-eye which was not appropriately charred which led to a big pile of mushy fat left on his plate. A Luke burger and the couchon special rounded out the foursome. Yawn.  The fries were improved the second night. You just cant fake fresh fries, why try. Too many other places to go to waste any time or money here.

Excellent food, service and experience!  I came in solo during their happy hour. The space is beautiful and has a vibrant energy. I tried the gumbo and shrimp and grits. Both were out of this world delicious!  I had the French 75 for my drink (1/2 price during happy hour!).  It was refreshing and had a great, not too sweet taste to it. When in NOLA, be sure to go to Luke's!

This review is for breakfast. I would bet that Luke is the best breakfast place in a 10 or 15 block radius. We had a terrific hearty breakfast there with fresh eggs, thick bacon, nice big biscuits, and the true standout, the grits. Normally grits are just sort of meh, but at Luke they are light and fluffy with a bit of white cheese, and totally delicious. The prices here are reasonable, at most a dollar or two more than the street cafes. That is a bargain for fresh food and superior service. Our order was taken quickly and our water and coffee cups were swiftly refilled. Most of all we appreciated being able to make a reservation for breakfast instead of standing in line outside on the curb for an hour with grumbling stomachs at the other places.

I was in New Orleans for four days and this was by far the best meal I had while I was in town.  The Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp 'en cocotte' was out of this world.  It's a bit heavy for a lunch dish, so skip breakfast if you want this.  

Service was perfectly non-existent except when taking orders and bringing food, which is exactly what you want during a business meeting.  Food came out very quickly as well, so they're used to accommodating business lunches.

I don't have much more to add that the 1,200 reviews haven't already covered, so go give it a shot!

Can I just say the soft shell crab BLT with bacon jam is the greatest BLT I have had in my entire life. I also highly recommend the shrimp and grits. Great food and great service are pretty much a constant here.

Lüke has been on "our list" for a while now. So happy that we finally visited. Everything was perfect. The layout of the restaurant, the friendliness of the staff, the ambiance. I wish that I could have sampled everything on the menu. The Salad Lüke was exceptional as was the Crispy Goat Cheese Stuffed Squash Blossoms. You could tell immediately that the pasta was house made. The roasted jalapeño grits were so good that I would go back just for them.  I highly recommend the "Gâteau Basque" and the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Crème Brûlée. Both, "to die for" desserts. They also have a great drink menu and they brew their own beer. Try the River Bend. You will not regret it. I can not wait to visit again. The brunch menu looks mouthwatering.

First Chicken and waffles I have ever had. They were delicious. The pecan butter and the Tabasco raspberry jam...mmmmm. The staff were friendly and attentive. We had a bit of a wait due to lunch rush and a few larger groups, but were seated promptly. Excellent experience.

Happy hour oysters .75 a piece from 3-6. Half price cocktails and well drinks. Oysters are what you would expect from the price and enjoyable for a dozen, but they lack mineral flavor, are large, and are shucked quickly so lose salt water and add pieces of shell. Overall good experience for the price though with nice staff and good atmosphere.

Positives: 

Clean, tasty and you can actually see the food being prepared and not behind glass. Plenty of vegan and vegetarian choices .  Gravy is thick and spicy . Original drinks 

Need work: time for food to get prepared, in dinning area is small and congested
Great service, good clean raw bar food. Great lunch spot!

As I came to New Orleans to visit for the weekend, I decided to visit Luke for some oysters.
This place has happy hour for $.75 oysters everyday 3-6pm! Asked where the oysters came from, and our waiter told us they were from the east coast. 

Location: located inside the same building as the Hilton New Orleans/St. Charles Avenue.

Service: couldn't complain, friendly staff and attentive.

Ambience: more upscale than abnormal restaurant. Just don't show up in a tank and basketball shorts with flip flops.

Food quality: Only ordered the oysters. Ordered 18 of them and absolutely devoured them. Definitely fresh and were very tasty along with the cocktail sauce, horse radish and lemons they provide.

Good place to chow down on fresh oysters especially if you're looking to go easy on your wallet, as oysters can be expensive. Go ahead and call ahead to set reservations as they do so.

Fantastic food.  I ate 50 cent oysters during happy hour and they were delicious.  Alcoholic beverages were also half off, so I imbibed a few.  My husband got the grilled cheese sandwich and it was mouth watering.  He also got the vanilla cake and it was awesome.  Who knew something that sounded so bland would be so good?  When I visit New Orleans again I'm going to eat here again.

Great little gem on Nolensville, meats are grilled outdoors on wood fire, had carne asada and pastor tacos with rice and beans....very tasty....friendly service, delivered food to car after I ordered at window

This was the first dinner I had during my most recent trip to New Orleans.  It set the bar high.  Service was top notch.  We had the pork rillettes as an appetizer.  It was excellent. I ordered the roasted chicken with vegetables.  The chicken was cooked to perfection.  very moist and flavorful.

The food is good. The service is great. Our waiter was very attentive. We had the rabbit pate, Brussel sprouts and crawfish beignet for apps - delicious! We had the shrimp & grits and seafood gumbo for dinner. The shrimp & grits were very flavorful but a bit too salty; the seafood gumbo was tasty but the texture was a bit thinner than I prefer but again, tasty. The bread pudding dessert was also very good. 
I had a bug in the pate and the waiter quickly switched out. I was running low on the crostini for my pate and I didn't even have to ask - the waiter brought me another order. Unfortunately at the end of the shrimp & grits we found a hair - at that point we were already done - bummed us out a bit though - we didn't make a thing of it.... but based on the service thus far at that point, I'm sure the wait staff would have done right by it. 
All in all a great dining experience.

I do have to say, for an inexpensive, quick pizza... It's pretty good. I have ordered here a couple times and I have never had a bad experience. The food is always good and the staff is always pleasant. The only thing that slightly disturbs me is that every time I order at this restaurant, I watch the employees assemble my pizza before they bake it with no gloves on. The cleanliness of this store could be a bit better.

Wanted to try a John Besh restaurant while in New Orleans, so decided on Luke since the menu had a nice balance of seafood and non-seafood items. Made reservations for 7:45 and were seated immediately. I absolutely loved the ambiance and decor here- modern and rustic but open raw bar gave a great nautical feel.

Appetizers: We ordered half a dozen oysters on the half shell and the brussels sprouts to start. The oysters were large, juicy and extremely fresh- would return just for the raw bar alone. The roasted brussels sprouts were literally the best I've ever had. The combination of heat from the jalepenos and sweet from sliced green apples gave a unique but balanced flavor- definitely going to try replicating this recipe at home. 

Dinner: I ordered the shrimp and crab etouffee which was served over fresh homemade cavetelli. It was spicy and light and just an overall outstanding dish! My boyfriend ordered the Luke burger which was served on a fluffy golden brown biscuit with carmelized onions, bacon and cheese. It was cooked perfectly! 

Highly recommend to anyone looking for a great restaurant near the French Quarter but far enough away from the craziness!

Went for a lunch meeting and, despite not feeling well, enjoyed the meal stupendously.  I had a cup of Matzo Ball and Roasted Chicken Soup.  It was hot, comforting, and delicious.  For my entree I had the Fried Oyster, Bacon, Avocado, and Romaine Salad.  After 6 weeks in Africa, this fresh dish was absolutely perfect.  Though I think it would've been just as good had it been any other day.

I personally love Luke and will always recommend it.

If I could've given a higher rating for service and food, I would have. From the moment that we came to the restaurant (an hour before our OpenTable reservation because we saw the Happy Hour at the last minute), we were welcomed in, made to feel like we were cared for and taken care of, and given amazing service, and that doesn't even include the outstanding (!!!!!) food. 

Casey (the hostess) and Greg (our waiter) were true standouts. They went out of their way to accommodate our 2 separate reservations and combined them into 1 so that we could all sit together. We were treated with respect and concierge customer service, which I didn't expect on a busy Saturday night where many convention goers were finally let loose. We all loved this placed and waddled away happy, even though many of us had eaten here twice in 5 days!

The Happy Hr oysters ($. 50/ea from 3-6p) were amazing, but the Shrimp and Grits "En Cocotte" and the Etoufee of Blue Crab and Brown Shrimp were true standouts!  I could have eaten several servings of the En Cocotte.  The other memorable option from Luke was the Sazerac, which will spoil me for all others in the future.  My only disappointment was in myself for not having been able to eat more.  Apparently, the elastic in my waistband was not prepared for the demands placed upon it.  I may never be able to sit up again.  

Given the amazing food available in New Orleans, this was the BEST meal we had while here!

This place was great. We had Christmas Day brunch, the food and the service were spectacular. The rear dinning area (where we sat) has a great view into the kitchen which was fun to watch. We wish we could have gotten back in for dinner...

Went for Happy Hour!! Great prices, but couldn't enjoy after spending the last 3 nights in New Orleans. Oysters were huge and we both had the shrimp and grits. It was really heavy, but tasty!! I would definitely try something else next time.

Modern twist on the NOLA cuisine. The chicken and reboot liver pate was really good. The sides and sauces that come with it add to the flavors. The Brussels were okay and drenched in sauce that masked the nicely cooked sprouts. The shrimps and grits were amazing! Huge gulf shrimp and creamy grits with flavors that kept going! Recommended to someone who wants a flair on the common Nola menu.

I rarely give more than 4 stars but this place made it. Polite server (Deseree) and awesome food. The taste, dressing, and service for the price deserve 5 star. We ordered 3 types of food (mushroom omelette, crispy chicken, and egg sandwich) all were great!

The good...Calvin, and Dave were excellent servers!
The Shrimp and Grits....extremely salty, but I was hungry so choked them down with two very good draft IPA's. My friend had the fried oysters,  but had to be sent back since they were overcooked, chewy and dry.
They brought her out some more, which were somewhat better. Dessert, the Hummingbird cake was bland and dry, very disappointing. Sent it back in exchange for the bread pudding, which was very good.
Excellent staff, friendly, great service. Will not be dining here again though. I will go to the tried and true, Mr. B's for their BBQ shrimp, or any other establishments that do not over salt their food.
The food here is good but compare to Nola standard I think this place mediocre, a 3 star and not 4. There are many other restaurant in this area that offer better items on their menu

We had a wonderful time on a busy weekend. They did great accommodating our large party and got everyone's order and ticket spot on! I ordered the LE PETIT PLATEAU DE FRUITS DE MER... Amazing presentation and everything done to perfection.

Arrived for happy hour yesterday - their happy hour deal is excellent! We each had a glass of Tempranillo and shared raw and fried oysters. Everything was fresh and tasty. The bar was packed the whole time we were there and I can see why!

How far this restaurant has fallen- Came 4 years ago and had a wonderful culinary experience. This time came for breakfast- Our Waiter, when asked how he was said " I'm here" then was not seen again until it was time for the check. Took 15 minutes to have our cocktail brought us and when the food arrived it was cold! Not sure how, in New Orleans, French fries are literally cold at 10 in the morning unless they were taken out the fridge from the night before. I noticed the elderly man at the next table get up and grab some cream for his coffee from a table where the diners recently left. I had to walk across the restaurant to find a half empty carafe of water after realizing that was the only way to get a refill- again never had any wait staff stop by my table but to drop off food/drink. My guest commented at end of meal that he had never had OJ delivered- though it was on the bill. I do not usually post reviews but felt the need to warn unsuspecting travelers.

Didn't even get to sit. The place was half empty when we came with a party of 8 (bachelor's party). We were in sports gear for our bike tour after brunch.  Hostess proceeded to inform us they can't take a party of 8. When I asked if she can split us into parties of 4, she had a peculiar look and proceeded to let us know, politely, that she's "actually" all booked through Mardi Gras and can't take walk ins.  -.-"  

Not sure if it's the dress code or our ethnicity, but I'll give the benefit of the doubt and assume the former. 

If there was a strict dress code, they should've been upfront with it. 

It goes without saying that we were a group of polite professionals with two officers with us

I went on a gumbo binge during one weekend; traveling all over town trying as much gumbo as I can. This is the best of what I've tried so far. The only place better was at a friends house. 

My friend ordered the duck which was super tasty. I had the mussels because on a previous trip, I envied the mussels that she had, and they were just as good as I remember them. The only unfortunate thing was that half of them had some sand in it. *sad face*. But the staff was really nice and made sure that we were stocked on bread so I could dip it in the butter sauce from the mussels.

This is a MINT JULEP review, we didn't have food.

We got our Mint Juleps to go. 

In short, this is most likely the strongest drink you'll have in the French quarter. Every sip, felt weirdly good in the sense that you know you'll lost fine motor skills in your body but you can't NOT finish a Mint Julep. 

Come here when you're ready to be fancy drunk, as this is a fancy place.

Pro Tip: get your Mint Julep To Go! We went there on a Saturday afternoon and the place was PACKED! No sitting or standing room, simply go to the bar, get your drinks, enjoy a clean hotel bathroom and bounce!

Came for happy hour specials, Oysters were small and Fried oysters my daughter had were even smaller and noting special. 
Place was nice and service was good. I gave them it a three because ultimately. I come for the food.

The food was good but overall the experience was average.  I ordered the shrimp and grits with lump crab and it was good. It had a nice flavor cajun that wasn't too spicy,  cooked in lots of butter but honestly the grits were my favorite part?!  The boyfriend ordered the fried chicken and waffles.  On their own the chicken and waffles were okay but overall I was not a fan.  The syrup had a weird sweet, licorice flavor to it and was really unpleasant but my boyfriend loved it so, who knows?!
I ate here twice in the span of a week. The choucroute and moules et frites were great (very very good fries). I would definitely recommend to others.

Trust the reviews! Every bit as delicious as promised.

We're only visiting for the weekend so we're not all that familiar with the area, Luke's was close to our hotel so we gave it a shot. I had the grilled ham, cheese and egg which was excellent. Others had the seafood gumbo which they enjoyed also. 

I definitely recommend this place for reasonable prices and very tasty food.
Like a lot of the other reviewers, we went for Happy Hour, twice during our 3-day trip. The have the BEST gumbo in the business!

I came here for dinner about 8 years ago and then went back for a brunch earlier this year.  Both times were enjoyable, but the food was a little rich for my tummy.  Food was a little on the pricey side for what you get. I did find it a tad loud, so it was a challenge to hear the other people at my table talking.  All in all, I would come back to give it another try, and hope for a better experience.

We went to luke purely for happy hour oysters and drinks. This was a perfect place for those items. Drinks were delicious and oysters were an amazing deal. I would recommend this place to anyone, whether local or tourist.

A friend of mine has constantly raved about how great Luke is. Well, I finally had the opportunity to taste it for myself today at lunch. Every weekday they have an express lunch which is $17 and includes a side salad or soup of the day and a daily entree. I opted for that she opted for the bowl of gumbo, another friend had the Luke burger which was huge and we split the stuffed oysters. 
During lunch, the stuffed oysters come as an order of 4 served on a bed of sea salt. 
The lunch menu offered a really nice variety of Southern delicacies, German dishes and a raw seafood bar, and all dishes are prices between $11-$25. 
I opted for the Express lunch and Monday's special is red beans and rice with honey fried chicken. The chicken was 2 huge pieces of filet breasts. Soo good, and just a touch of honey.  
Overall everyone enjoyed their meal, and I can't wait to come back to try everything on the menu for both lunch and dinner because everything looks delicious! 
Since it's on St Charles, there is no street parking or valet service. There are a few hotel parking garages nearby that is open to the public and accessible on the streetcar line.
This is me and my wife's top 5 restaurants. Service is always great. Food is really good. Atmosphere is tight and cramped toward the end of the week.. And I kind of like it that way.

Terrific dining experience. We decided to go to Luke because of its proximity to our hotel , Yelp reviews and ability to make a reservation. We were seated in the back; great to see the cooks at work they the glass wall. My dinner mate and I were pleased to receive the comped roasted Brussels sprout appetizer which was melt In your mouth delicious. We then shared the puppy drum entree and oyster salad which was plated for 2. The Puppy Drum is a light white fish served with an almond sauce and was excellent. The salad was very good and was a nice balance with the fish. Portions were good. My only wish is that I had saved room for dessert. Luke is next door to the Hilton on the other side of Canal Street from the crowds and worth the  2-3 block walk on the other side of Canal St. Service was very attentive without being at all overbearing.

The reviews were all very correct. Good little location with great service. We arrived before 6pm and there was a raw oyster special, so there was a delay in getting them. The manager brought out the fried oysters and they were great. I would recommend the fried oysters and arriving after 6pm unless you want the happy hour drinks and don't mind waiting for raw oysters. It was rather loud but enjoyable for two to talk during dinner without he next table listening in.

I've actually never written a review on Yelp before, but I feel compelled to for this place. I've eaten at countless sushi restaurants in my life - I've even traveled to Japan just to eat sushi. And this place is top quality. The quality of their rice and fish is amazing. The raw fish tastes very fresh. The portion size is generous. The service is great and the chefs give a good energy. This is how sushi is suppose to taste. And this is also on a MONDAY night - it's no wonder the restaurant was super busy on a Monday. If this quality is sustained, then my visits will be too :-)

I highly recommend any salmon dishes or the spicy scallops roll. But you can't go wrong with anything because it's all prepared fantastically.
Hands down the best sushi I have had in a long time!! Absolutely outstanding and so fresh! Love that it's BYOB too
Their brussel sprouts are addictiveand they have some of the best raw oysters in the city (their house horseradish is amazing, but super powerful).

Menu is ho-hum, especially for the price. I made the mistake of ordering this onion tart that reminded me of a bbq chicken pizza from CPK. Should've picked up that the waiter wasn't as enthused when I ordered but didn't dissuade me (too subtle for me at the time, but understandable behavior from him).

So glad I had so many recommendations before coming to NOLA. Luke was one of the recommendations and it was right in our hotel. I went with the shrimp & grits which were delicious! What stole the show though was the Brussels sprouts. They were probably the best I have had in my entire life! What ever sauce/seasoning they use is fantastic!

We ended the meal with the delicious caramel bread pudding. I'll also add they have a happy hour from 3 to 6 with 75 cent raw oysters. Usually I'm weary about hotel restaurants, but this one was great.

We were excited to dine here and were not disappointed!  The Crispy Brussel Sprouts were perfection. They had just the right amount of crisp, sweet, tang, nuttiness, and heat. The Pork Schnitzel was deliciousness . Don't ignore the lemons on top...the juice squeezed into the schnitzel enhances the flavor of the wild mushroom ragout...which is brought out on the side so that your schnitzel doesn't get soggy before you're ready to eat it. 
The atmosphere is nice and overall it was a pleasant dining experience.

Caveat: This review is only for their happy hour. I have not been for lunch or dinner but I will update the review when I do.

Luke's happy hour absolutely kicks ass. 50 cent oysters in a setting as nice as Luke's would be enough on it's own, but they also made the best Mint Julep ($5) that I have ever had. Bourbon, mint, sugar (simple syrup), ice...sounds easy enough but they are often made incorrectly and, in my opinion, if the ice isn't crushed, it's not suitable for sipping on even the least sophisticated of verandas. 

Luke's serves theirs in a cylindrical glass with a nice sized snow cone of crushed ice protruding from the top. Sweet enough to take the edge off the bourbon and muddled to release the flavor of the mint without shredding the leaves beyond all recognition, the result is a refreshing cocktail so cold a thick layer of frozen water vapor encrusts the glass once stirred. Perfect.

My colleagues and I come to Hachi for lunch and more often now for dinner.  The food is excellent and we love the atmosphere!  I always order the sushi and I get the combo dish!  The service is great and they are very nice.  It is a BYOB (liquor store next door).  The rolls are tasty and the presentation is beautiful - look at my dish the last time I was there!

Ok I know I was just here but my lord! If it couldn't get any better! Had friends in town from jazz feat and took them here! Our waiter, Kyle, was the nicest guy! Super cute and again so informative! Told us where to go to get the best live music and such! And our new dessert some sort of strawberry thing was soooo delicious!



This was my previous review on  4/17
Your Previous Reviews
4/17/2014 Edit "
The staff is incredible! Our waitress, Cheyenne, was so nice and informing on not only what to eat but helped us out for fun things todo in the city. The bartender made some of the best cocktails! And I feel as tho I should mention the men who work here are quite attractive (a blond man I'm not sure what his name was and a man with the prettiest brown hair I have ever seen).

The food not to mention is rediculousy delish our and their happy hour is just too much fun! I would recommend this place to everyone! Families, singles, dates etc
Great service...the water was never empty. The food was amazing too. Great bread pudding to finish things off helped.

Not sure where to start but starting at the beginning seems fitting.  First sit at the bar and be served by the team (Garrett, Calvin Johnny) their service is impeccable.  They work together and are verily observant of your needs. They respond immediately even before you ask. Next, the drinks. Garrett makes a great "Belle of the Bayou" and I'm pretty sure he can do any drink well because of his commitment to  customer service. Then there's the food.... we ordered the P&J oysters (local) to start however they allowed us to sample two other types and shrimp just to get a feel for their flavor. P&J won hands down.   Followed up with the Louisiana Shrimp En Cocotte...Amazing. Check them out when in NOLA can't go wrong!
Man their shrimp and grits GOES! That was delicious, the waitress was effin great and the gumbo as well. Want to go back to New Orleans just to go back.

This place is awesome and I think I have a chef crush on John Besh! We came in here NYE and ate the most glorious foie gras terrine ever (I still dream about it). We also ordered the heavenly tower of seafood goodness (if you like seafood - it's a must have). Simply but perfectly cooked crab, lobster, clams, oysters, shrimp - you name it. It was delicious, but a bit messy. I couldn't get enough of the oysters and stone crab - the portion was perfect for 2 ppl. And the best part - good value for the money. I definitely think for the money we paid we got great food. I am coming here for sure next time I'm in the Big Easy.

A John Besh Bistro. Very high quality ingredients, expertly executed at reasonable prices.

I'd recommend the boudin noir, country pate, rabbit and duck liver pate, Luke salad, beet salad, and, of course, P&J oysters. I didn't care for the hard croutons the rabbit pate was served with though.

One of the best values in New Orleans is Happy Hour at Luke from 4 to 6. It's hard to beat $5 martinis and $3 a dozen for gulf oysters.

Although we were seated without a reservation on Christmas night, generally for dinner I'd recommend a reservation if you want to be seated at a table. The bar is first come, first served. Service is pleasant enough.

This place is the f'in bomb. Went here with my friends while traveling in New Orleans. $0.50/oyster for happy hours 3pm-6pm. 50 cents to New Orleans locals sucks since they are used to 25 or 10 cents, but someone from NY/PHL/DC? 50 cents is awesome! And they were juicy and plump. Service was amazing. All servers are in white-jackets, akin to the Palm restaurant style - very classy. Very relaxing atmosphere. If I ever go back to New Orleans, I am going back to Luke.

I left my dogs at Seven Oaks Pet Hospital over Thanksgiving. When we picked up my dogs, I knew my 8 month old mini dachshund wasn't right. I took him to our vet (NOT Seven Oaks Pet Hospital) and they said he was dehydrated and needed to be put on IVs. When I called Seven Oaks Pet Hospital to inform them of the health of my dog, they went back thru their logs and even have it written down that he would eat and drink sporadically daily. When I asked them if this behavior would be of any concern for a small 10lb puppy they said that they thought it was normal for a new boarding puppy which I can understand, however, we left them at a vet for a reason, and a quick feel of his gums would have let them know he was dehydrated. Very disappointed in the care that they provided to my baby . I will be telling anyone I know to NOT use Seven Oaks Pet Hospital.

My favorite restaurant for my first trip to NOLA! Happy hour 3-6 pm! Raw oysters are $0.75 and fried are a dollar something. My fiancé and I had both and they were superb! The fried oysters were not overly fried and still nice and juicy on the inside but crispy on the outside. The raw oysters were not grainy and very fresh! We also had the chicken and rabbit pate and it was great with the bread. They give you a variety of small accompaniments to cut the taste of the pate. I enjoyed it but it's a pretty large portion so we couldn't finish it. We had the gumbo and it was average. Service was great! Nick & Nick were awesome! :)

Gezellig sfeervol restaurant met aardige bediening. Flamenkuche was koud bij het opdienen. De openkeuken liet ons zien dat hij opnieuw de oven inging en hierna droog was. Ander hoofgerecht bleek iets anders te zijn dan besteld. Voor ons dus een tegenvaller. Als "compensatie" werd hoofdgerecht en drankjes niet in rekening gebracht

THE FORCE IS STRONG IN THIS ONE

Great atmosphere. Doesn't feel like a tourist trap.

My go-to for lunch when I visit NOLA.  Has been great for many years.  A dozen P&J oysters, followed by jumbo shrimp and grits. Get the crab meat w the shrimp and grits. Bar service is great. Highly recommend.

Delightful brunch experience. The food was 5-star as expected. I don't like when a place touts 5-star but isn't. 

Highly recommend their homemade / house goodies. These are unique experiences to Luke's, and we enjoyed their interpretations.

Great shrimp and grits! Tried the rabbit and chicken pate, which was good, but didn't stand out like the shrimp and grits. Would have liked to try the quail with picked peppers and Tabasco honey. Sounds really good! Atmosphere was nice but loud. Looking forward to coming back.

Tremendous experience here at Luke! We popped in for Happy Hour before our dinner at Arnaud's and were greeted by the lovely Ms. Elizabeth- a true warm and inviting welcome! We let her know we were just here for HH ( a rec from a NOLA native) and sat at the bar right in front of the buzzy oyster bar! The bartender was just precious, acknowledged us immediately and served us the most elegant French 75! These were to die for and went down a little too easy! The oysters and chilled shrimp were some of the best I have every had! I am drooling thinking about them! We loved the interaction between the bartenders and the shuckers- a pro of sitting at the bar!
