The entire team recognized it was our ten year anniversary and gifted us a glass of bubbles and a heart-donned French 75 to mark the occasion. Little touches like that, exceptional service and wonderful seafood have made us Luke fans for life! Thank you!!
Best shrimp and grits I've had in NOLA.  Brussel sprouts are also excellent.   A must stop every time I visit the city.

To be honest, I've only eaten dessert at this place (bread pudding) and it is phenomenal! It's served hot with ice cream and lots of caramel. Not mention the service was great! Next time I'm in New Orleans, I'll go there for dinner.

The food was exciting, multi-dimensional and vibrant- not unlike the service! Everyone enjoyed their meal, and we even caught a glimpse of a celebrity chef enjoying a dinner here! Per the waiters recommendation, I had the shrimp n' grits and it was unbelievably good- I will dream about it for years to come. Warm, diverse, convincingly authentic- though my friends felt the same way about their meals!

Came here for happy hour. 75 cents oysters, can't beat that. Fried oysters were $1.25 which isn't bad either. Got here around 430, no wait got seated right away but by 5, it was starting to get busy. You also don't need to sit by the bar to get the HH oysters which is a plus too.

Disappointing.  We went for brunch on a Saturday after reading some good reviews here.  The food was ok but overpriced for what it was, especially a dozen TINY West Coast oysters for $45. But the real issue here was the service or the lack there of.  We had to chase the waiter down several times to refill water glasses and to find out why 1 appetizer came out right away but we waited 10 minutes for the oysters and Bloody Mary's.  Burgers were ordered rare and medium but came out well with cold fries. We assume the problem was the burgers were cooked before the appetizers were even delivered to the table.  Overall, can't recommend when there are so many better options in New Orleans!

Derr. 

The food tasted good, but it was REDICULOUSLY packed, and the fillins' were skimpy.  

So not worth my 10 dollars. 

Go to the one on Walnut for a more substantial sammich, a smile, and relatively no crowds! (except maybe during the lunch hour, which is, expected).

Go here to eat.  Now.  We were going to to Ruby Slipper - 90 min wait - no thank you - walked right into Luke and into heaven.   Gumbo rich and dark - full of shrimp and oysters, the Etoufee with the handmade cavatelli was in a sauce that was silk - pasta soaking it up.  Attentive service.

3.75

came here foe thanksgiving. had turducken, blue crab mac and cheese, and oyster stuffing. everything was tasty but it was sent out cold. hate sending things back but had to. they were embarrassed and took care of it. handled it like pros. 

it was hh when we were there too. $0.50 oysters and 1/2 off drinks. hard to beat. 

nothing we ate blew me away. everything was good. had higher hopes for turducken in general. it was my first time trying. 

i'd go back and try their normal menu.

What can I say about Luke other than omg thank you for being you! We ended up coming here twice during our stay in New Orleans and both times were fantastic. The first was on a Friday right before lunch to celebrate my wife's birthday! Our server was fantastic! I wish I would have written this review sooner as I would have remembered his name, for that I'm awful!! Anyways he recommended some amazing house drinks  1 with vodka and the other with bourbon. So so good!! I ordered the chicken and waffles with peppered jam and honey butter. The chicken was crisp, flavorful and cooked to perfection. My wife had the shrimp n grits with a sunny side egg. Equally as good, so much flavor and spice, but comparing both I leaned towards the chicken n waffle. Which funny enough we both ordered on our second trip back here Sunday morning! Luke was by far breakfast and lunch spot during our lovely New Orleans weekend!! Thank you again Luke for being you!! #neworleans

Luke is a "German" restaurant in New Orleans.  I didn't get the German part but I did get an excellent meal. The setting is fine, it's actually in a hotel.  I didn't think it was intimate or romantic, but I wasn't looking for that.  It was a full and busy room.  The food is by John Besh and it is good.  Three of us loved pretty much everything we had.  Highlights for me were the crawfish bisque and a Fried Quail.  The bisque is like butter and cream meet sweet crawfish.  The flavors were exquisite.  Quail had a seasoned batter that exemplifies New Orleans flavor.  We had oysters that were super fresh and super tasty.  You have to traipse out of the French Quarter for Luke; but it is well worth it.
Enjoyed a very nice meal here and liked it so much, returned for a second dinner the next day.  Will likely come here again.  Service could be just a little but sharper, otherwise a 5 star.
Food and service was great. Happy hour $0.75 oysters were really good. Drinks were fantastic. All around a very nice restaurant. I would eat here again

Excellent food, service and atmosphere. One of our favorite restaurants in New Orleans. 

As an appetizer, the blood sausage with potatoes and onions is wonderful.  Served on an iron skillet, the potatoes and onions were still sizzling. Blood sausage is the type of dish that can be very, very good; or very, very not good. Lüke's blood sausage was superb, leading to my dining mates requesting a taste of it for themselves. 

For the main course, I chose the burger and fries, which was said by a friend to be one of the finest in the city. The burger did not disappoint, with a high quality, melt-in-your-mouth patty and thick bacon. The french fries were long and crisp with a slightly spicy batter. Paired with a pale ale from the fine beer selection, the meal was a fantastic lunch during a very long and busy day.

Lüke is located a few blocks away from the convention center and the French Quarter. This provided a welcome respite from the crowds with a very relaxed atmosphere inside of the restaurant. The bar in Lüke is very well stocked, and staggeringly high. The drink of choice for our group was the French 75, which includes champagne, cognac and lemon juice(!) It was amazing, and hands down the best drink we had while in New Orleans. 

When visiting the Big Easy, do not hesitate to add Lüke a stop on your trip.

I went for one reason and one reason only - for the oysters.  Sunday night, happy hour, 50 cents a piece - they were the biggest and best oysters I had all week while in New Orleans.  I ate oysters daily - every place I went - raw, charbroiled, steamed, etc.  I was so excited when I sat at the bar and ordered them up and planned on eating about 3 dozen.  I was so stuffed after 1 dozen that I had to stop.

The staff is very attentive.  The Flamenkutchen and Heirloom Tomato Salad are marvelous.  The Heirloom Tomato Salad has all the flavors of summer.   A relaxed French bistro atmosphere makes for a relaxing place to dine
75 cents per oyster in the happy hour time!!! We come for lunch and cannot help to order one dozen and another dozen after that!!! Highly recommend this place. Everything is delicious.

I dropped in for breakfast and ordered the shrimp and grits. Tasty but the Anson Mill Grits were clearly the star. I enjoyed the meal but I have to point out it is the same size and twice the price of the Herbsaint shrimp & grits. This a bit pricey but the atmosphere was nice. Service however left a lot to be desired. I finished my meal and had to stare at my dirty plate for 20 minutes. Even when they brought the check no one took the plate. Even Fridays clears away your plate when you finished.If I wanted to stare at a dirty plate that long I could sit at my house. There were only 3 other occupied tables and I think someone could have managed to clear me out. I think if you want me to pay that price and be happy the service needs to match the food.
A good stop for unique cuisine in New Orleans.

The Roasted Beet salad was great. I got the entrecote grille au frites . They served the wrong sauce with the steak, although good not what I asked for, cooked perfect though. The fries were cold within minutes of service. The beer selection was unique, I got Belgium ale that was great. 
I would give it another try the next time I'm in New Orleans.

The food is great, and it's a nice welcoming atmosphere. But, they keep running out of things, like yogurt and not at the end of the day, but early. It's ridiculous, clearly you need to order more or make more or get a bigger fridge. Someone needs to sort it out because being sold out of a breakfast item before 9am on a weekday and before 10am on a weekend is annoying.

We made a reservation for dinner on January 2nd and had a great experience!  The dining experience couldn't be any better.  Our waiter and waitress were very attentive and were fantastic; they were very professional and knowledgeable.  We sat towards the back of the restaurant near the kitchen so we could see as the guys were plating the meals which was a really unique and cool experience.  I had the farm raised raw oysters as my appetizer; they were massive and delicious! My friend had the crispy brussel sprouts which I highly recommend; it was fantastic!  I had the mussels and frites as my meal; the sauce was a little bit more butter than I preferred but nonetheless, it was still very delicious and well cooked!  I would definitely go back and eat there again the next time we're in New Orleans.  The food and service was on of the best experiences.

I like grabbing sandwiches here. Their food are made from fresh ingredients and delicious. They serve good coffee too (49 parallel coffee from Vancouver). The place is tiny (there are a few counter sears).It is located in a hidden place, but people come here for good quick food and coffee.

I visited Luke last Oct. for a friend's birthday.  We had a lovely private room. Although my day long hangover killed my appetite (and my drink order), the service and the dish I ate was wonderful. The waiter was very sweet, even offered me bitters to help with that good ol' NOLA hangover. Go there BEFORE the night you decide to drink 4-6 Hurricanes, among other NOLA libations.

The Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" is delicious. I had mine without the sausage as I don't eat pork. This this was very filing and had me dancing in my seat. We also enjoyed two desserts, the bread pudding without the pecans due to my nut allergy, and the chocolate cake item with ice cream. The service was great and this place is highly recommended. The only downside was that it was a little chilly inside the restaurant.

I discovered this bar just this year through some of my friends. It's for sure a college bar. They have great deals, so much better than Keswick Tavern! The vibe is better to, you can actually walk around and talk to people compared to Keswick where you are confined to the bar area. The bartenders are also super nice! The food is pretty good, your average bar food.
They also have a separate area where you can buy beer. Mostly just 6-packs, not the place to get a case from.
We loved it, a bit pricey but most places in NOLA are.  Gumbo was the best in NOLA.  Hubby had Shrimp and grits.  I had pasta with boar meat.  Flavors were incredible and we had a great time.

Seriously this is the freshest Chinese food I every had!  

The first time I went I had chicken & broccoli and the the sauce was light and let the taste of the chicken come through.  The chicken was soft and tasty.

The second time I had General Tso's Chicken, fried rice and 2 egg rolls -- again all tasty and fresh.   These egg rolls actually taste healthy!

If there's only one thing you can order from here, order the crawfish bisque. And if you can, go to their happy hour also. You won't be disappointed. 

During my short trip to Nola, we stopped by John Besh's Lüke twice - once for lunch and the other time for happy hour. Both times, we ordered the crawfish bisque because it was that good. I don't usually like creamy foods, but I fell in love with the crawfish bisque and it's perfect creaminess and smooth texture. Combined with a generous amount of peeled crawfish, the bisque was nothing short of amazing. In addition to the bisque, we also ordered two entrees off their lunch menu. I got the jumbo Louisiana shrimp en cocotte aka shrimp and grits. It is a rich dish and very flavorful. While it was good, it got overwhelming very quickly. My boyfriend ordered their special of the day which was a pork dish that came with some very tender pieces of pork. 

For happy hour, we ordered a dozen oysters ($0.75 each) and half a dozen of their fried oysters. Both were really good and extremely reasonably priced in my opinion given the quality and size of the oysters. 

I highly recommend this place to anyone visiting New Orleans. At the very least, swing by for a quick happy hour and order their crawfish bisque. Can't stress that enough!

Happy hour review only. Great oysters and great price. The PB&J oysters were rich but so yummy. You have to try them. The gnocchi was tasty. Didn't think it was amazing. I'd come again for oysters but there's plenty of other amazing places.

Only have been here for Happy Hour 50 cent oysters. The place is packed. Oysters are plump and fresh and disappear quickly into my stomach. Drinks are strong and cheap. Can't wait to go back to New Orleans to try other things on the menu. Great thing about this place, Happy hour is not restricted to the bar area. You can make reservations to get a seat at the restaurant and then get the happy hour deals. The Sazerac was my favorite!
While the service was good, the shrimp and grits were just ok. This is an upscale restaraunt, if you want good shrimp in grits, I would suggest you go elsewhere

Caveat: we went to Luke during Mardi Gras. 

Luke was my first John Besh experience. We were excited to enjoy a late dinner after the parades and were hoping to enjoy some oysters. Enjoy some oysters, we did. Unfortunately, our service left a lot to be desired. 

Our waiter was inattentive and did not seem to know much about the menu, which was disappointing as we found it a bit daunting. We worked out what we were going to order and from there on out, things were not awesome. 

Our food and drinks came in a baffling order. We received our oysters first, then our drinks, then a burger, then salad and gumbo. This would have been fine if there was a minute break between each part of the meal, but unfortunately it was more like 10 minutes.

The worst part of the meal was the bibb lettuce salad I ordered. When I received the salad, it was made of brown romaine. I was so baffled that I asked the waiter if it was the right salad. He had no idea, so I just requested a cup of gumbo to match the 3 other cups of gumbo at our table. The waiter returned 5 minutes later without gumbo. They had run out...what? 

We eventually had a bus boy track down our waiter to get the check, which included the salad. Our waiter took the salad off but never seemed to acknowledge that anything out of the ordinary had happened during our meal. 

On the way out, we overheard two waiters talking about how desperate they were for Mardi Gras to be over. As someone who has experience Mardi Gras more than once, I can understand how it would be a nightmare for a service employee. For this, I give Luke a bit of a pass for the awful service. Overall, with the exception of the salad, the food was quite good. If you have the money, I would pick August over Luke, but Luke still provides a nice place to eat.
Without a doubt, THE BEST sushi restaurant in the BUXMONT area.

The seafood gumbo and Luke salad were amazing. To finish it off I had the bread pudding. Definitely add Luke to your list when visiting New Orleans. Ask for Richie Rich and his team to make your experience.

Not as good as I had anticipated considering how many stars it got.

Food: Some onion tarte thing with bacon & cheese, ravioli with crabmeat, rib eye, bread pudding

Taste:
- Onion tarte: GREASE! It seemed like after they had cooked it with the bacon & cheese, they deep fried it in oil and brought it out to us without letting the oil drip off. It was kind of tasty though...
- Ravioli: Garlic butter oil sauce? I thought it was going to be creamy, but it was more oily & the portion was kind of small. The crabmeat was good.
- Rib eye: I was expecting it to be a little more soft considering it's one of the more fattier steaks. I wasn't impressed.
- Bread pudding: Never thought I'd be a fan, and I was right. It was too sweet for me, but the ice cream was good. My husband enjoyed it though.

Value: Not really worth the price.

Parking: Walked, but I think it's only valet (&10).
Great service. The gumbo is amazing. Same with the salads- both big so good to share with the fam. The Brussels sprouts might be the best I've ever had- sooo good. Everyone enjoyed what they ordered
Fine dining and service type of place, food was seasoned perfectly and cooked the way I asked, the rib eye was soft and every bite was consistent, this is a place I will be back to eat.

I can't remember if I wrote a review for this gem back in fall 2010, and I'm too lazy to go look. In either case, both reviews - then and now - would and will share the same result: wonderful.

In 2010, the week of Thanksgiving, I had the best-ever restaurant dining experience in my life. I was treating myself to a full dinner, and dining solo, I was a bit worried that service would be "meh" as it often is at finer places. Rather, my waiter was fantastic. When I told him I hadn't really had raw oysters before, but was curious, he fetched me two on the house to try out (resulting in something yummy!). And, when I had a little green organic visitor in my salad - showing that everything was extremely fresh - they took care of me. I didn't care much, as it wasn't something that signaled a lack of cleanliness. But, they swooped on in without a word, took my plate, and dashed off. The manager swung by, and apologized profusely, swearing that everything was 'taken care of'. And, he wouldn't let me argue (I seriously didn't mind paying!).

Everything I had - a full five courses - was delectable. Not to mention, they made a darned good Old Fashioned.

Since then, I've craved a return visit here. And, two weeks ago, I was in town and had just killed off the better part of Saturday walking around the Garden District... exhausted and in dire need of a light bite and a beer before the wedding I was set to attend that evening, I made a special hike over to Luke. 

I got there in the middle of their happy hour which is everyday (weekends too!) from 3-6pm and includes $.50 oysters and half-priced drinks (I think there are some that aren't, but many/most are). I sat at the bar, ordered a full dozen and a house beer, and found myself remiss to leave in time to hoof it way back to my room to shower and change for the wedding.

Now, the oysters weren't as good as the ones I had two days before at Felix's, but... for $.50/ea. and decent conversation with the bartenders, it was a welcome stop at the end of a long, hot, tiring day.

I will return again on my next trip. And, for someone who is always looking for a new place to eat, to find one to repeat visits to, that's saying a lot.
While the food was ok, I am not accustomed to begging for a coffee refill. I do not like being treated as if I am invisible.

I have never ever experienced better service! We had to evacuate FL due to Irma and the manager- Ron- and our server- Richie Rich- did everything in their power to take our mind off of our worries!!!!! Our evening started with a round of drinks (which they took care of), next we got our appetizers- fried shrimp, a dozen oysters, crab bisque (all taken care of by the manager), our server also brought our children out some French fries (so they had an "appetizer" too) SO THOUGHTFUL! Next we're the entrees and they were beyond delicious! I had the roasted chicken (I think that's what it's called) and my husband had the Luke burger. He said it was the best burger he's ever had! Then dessert which they also took care of for us! Considering our day- they made us feel at "home" at a time when we had a lot our minds! For one dinner we could just relax for a moment! Thank you Ron and Richie Rich- we will never forget your kindness!
Friends recommended this place, the food was decent, a bit too greasy, but the service was not what I expected, I am not saying was bad but they can do a better job.

What an amazing place! Lovely happy hour..must go in New Orleans for oysters (large and great quality)! Great atmosphere, wonderful food, but most of all, INCREDIBLE SERVICE! Richy Rich was fun, attentive and majestically entertaining! All without knowing it was for a friend's 40th birthday. Thank you Luke! Would recommend to anyone visiting NOLA!

Lüke was the very first restaurant I visited my first night in New Orleans, after hearing so many good reviews, I thought I would try it. Luckily, they did not disappoint! I came right in time for Happy Hour which was incredible, the French 75 was delicious. Oysters were super cheap, either raw or fried, both were great. The service was probably the best part of the experience, the servers were incredibly funny and were very quick to get anything we needed, even while being busy. I would definitely recommend this place!

I love to eat healthy so I was excited to hear about the standards of Panera. However, I think they are over priced for what you get. I got the chicken Thai salad  and was shocked at how little chicken there was on it.  I appreciate their level of quality but I still think it could be obtained with a lower price tag

Food and service was good. Highly recommend the happy hour or else it is too pricey. They had 75cent raw oyster and $1.25 fried...both good just slightly expansive even for happy hour. High recommended experience.

This restaurant single-handedly made my business trip delightful.  I went last spring with a team in town for a tradeshow.  Found this gem on Yelp and enjoyed it so much that we went back twice.

Located in an art deco-era office building, it doesn't look like much from the outside, but venture in and you'll discover an excellent cocktail menu and a country terrine that I still miss to this day.  The raw bar selection is outstanding, and they accomodated our large group with ease. I look forward to returning on my next trip to New Orleans, even if it is for a tradeshow.

Despite the shaky service I still find this restaurants to be amazing.  Shrimp and grits were amazing. The balance of flavors was perfect esp since I hate spicy and it made with jalapeño peppers. Dont be afraid of the dish its not spicy at all! Cocktail just put me to bed. Will go back soon. Yes.

I love this place. It was first place I ate at when I was in New Orleans. The food and service were incredible. I had the  grits and shrimp which were each flavored deliciously. I also had the rosemary  and champagne  drink.

There is not too much more to say but what an outstanding  place. Happy to give 5 stars.

I love this place!  I try to go every time I visit NOLA. The shrimp and grits are close to the best in the city!  The drinks are always unique and top notch! 
The raw oysters are also fantastic.

Great drinks at a decent price for happy hour in a nicer restaurant. Specialty drinks were not your run of the mill usual, get the St Charles. Our server Rich, kept things light and relaxed. He was happy to direct indecisive pallets. The soft shell crab and shrimp and grits were hits.

This is one of my favorite places to take visitors to New Orleans.  The food is wonderful and the atmosphere is fun.  I recommend the mussels -- delish! John Besch is a wonderful chef and has been taking the city by storm.  You must visit one of his restaurants while in the city.
Food...excellent.  Service, extremely subpar for such a highly-rated establishment.  Service in need of repair.

I didn't have strong feelings about Luke either way. Would I go again if invited? Sure. But to be honest, there wasn't all that much that was memorable about it for me.
   We went on a Sunday around brunch time and sat at the bar to avoid the wait. The cocktail list was a nice blend of current trends and the classics. The bartender came off a bit snobbish and would disappear for long spans of time, but when we were able to get drinks, they were well-crafted. 
  The oysters are a must. The quality was  better than what you would get at Acme or Felix's, but you will pay for the quality and lose out on the atmosphere of the oyster joints. I had the crab cakes with eggs, which were good, just not outstanding. 
The atmosphere was fun because it was game day and 90% of the place was donning Saints jerseys. Luke may not have been especially memorable, but Saints fans always are.

I had brunch here last Sunday.  The gulf oysters were some of the best that I had ever had.  I also had some excellent gumbo.    I would definitely come here again.  My friend had the eggs, grits, and soft shell crab...he said it was excellent.  We ate at the bar and the bartender was knowlegeable.

THE CHICKEN AND WAFFLES ARE TO DIE FOR. Home fries were perfect. The boudin Benedict was delicious as well. Mimosas have the option of pineapple juice, orange juice or grapefruit juice .. we got the orange juice ones and they came out super light in color. The waitress (who was so sweet) confirmed it was OJ & said they just use the juice for a splash of color (fine by me!). 

The food portions are HUGE. We could've split the chicken and waffles and left full. 


The bathrooms didn't seem like they were cleaned recently (10am on a Sunday), but they had the tissue that covers the seat at least. 

We went in on Sunday feb 24th at 930 and were seated right away. Highly recommend !

Service was top notch. Can't ask for a better service. Two servers for two of us kept it very personal and attentive. Baked stuffed oysters were fresh. I actually enjoyed eating oysters and crab meats separately because crab meat overwhelmed the flavor of fresh oysters. Pork chops was delicious. Pork chop was stuffed with shredded pork. It came with corns, beans, and broccoli puree. Highly recommend it give a try.
Great service and happy hour. 75 cent oysters between 3 p.m. and 6 p.m. Half off drinks. Really good deal!

You can't go wrong with John Besh.  Came here for lunch on a Friday.  Our server was helpful and friendly, and gave a lot of great recommendations.  We ended up having the beet salad, which was so flavorful.  The roasted pistachios added just the right spice and flavor to the mix.  I had the cochon de lait pressed sandwich.  Was enough for 2 people and came with a huge container of skinny french fries.  My boyfriend had the special of the day and loved it as well.  Great lunch spot!

Visiting from out of town and my concierge recommended Luke for a close restaurant to my hotel that would give me a foodie taste of New Orleans. 

Mint julip = 2/10 - almost all bourbon. No flavor. 
Crispy brussel sprout - 11/10 - Devine!
Shrimp and grits - 7/10
Bread pudding - 10/10
Service 8/10. 

Overall 38/50. May have been worthy of all five stars if not for the horrid mint  julip.

Excited to try this up and coming star's restaurant. A little concerned about the "hotel restaurant" stigma, but it looked okay and thought we'd try it. 
Unfortunately terrible service. We sat at the bar waiting for our table and had great baked oysters with lousy beers and lackluster service. 
When we went to our table we hoped for improvement, but it got much much worse. Our server didn't get to our table at all for about 10 minutes, so we ordered dinner immediately in fear we may never see him again. The table next to us had a yummy looking bananas foster which they couldn't enjoy without utensils, so we gave them ours after waiting an additional 10 minutes for anyone to come back. Our server did not return once over the next 45 minutes. We asked a couple other employees to check on our food and/ or server without any response. Figuring the kitchen was overwhelmed, and new orleans can be slow, we waited. After sitting for nearly an hour, I went to the kitchen to check on it and was told it was under the heat lamp waiting for " a while". The manager brought it out immediately to our table, it looked okay but who knows, we left.

I am a fan of Cosi. Their flatbread is DELICIOUS! (though sometimes on the salty side). Even though it's a chain store, I find that the quality of the ingredients acceptable. 

I've only been twice--once for the signature salad and once for the fire roasted vegetable sandwich. In terms of flavor, I really like both. 

The lunch hour is crazy! It is a bit hard to figure out where to stand..but there are plenty of employees hollering directions (adding to the madness), but it works out in the end. 

There is plenty of seating upstairs and the employees take the time to clean the tables.

AND, I appreciate the calorie information. All chain restaurants should definitely be moving in this direction. Please add sodium and fat content!

We did not have reservation but they accommodated and sat us in the back room near the kitchen, which is actually cool because you get to watch all the chefs in action through the glass. 
The place is modern new American, Southern cooking.  It's upscale but casual friendly.  They have a daily lunch that is reasonable.  The food was so deliciously rich, especially the shrimp grit, I could eat this everyday, but definitely would come back when I'm in the area.

Love it!!! Our favorite Chinese takeout!  The family that runs it is so nice.  I feel like I have watched the children grow up over the years.  Large portions - enough that we have several days worth of food.  Some of the favorite items to consider are the Beef with Garlic sauce, lo mein with any choice of meat,  the fried rice, and egg rolls. We always have the fried dumplings and beef sticks.  Crab rangoons are popular, too.  Truthfully, we have never had anything but a great meal with plenty left over even with teenagers in the house! Call ahead and the order is ready for pick up in about 15 minutes.  You can eat in as well.  There are booths and tables.  Definitely try it out!!!

While I have no complaints about the food or drinks, because they were incredible, I am giving this place 2 stars due to service.  Both the hostess and our waiter seemed like they were completely "over it".  Hostess looked annoyed that we didn't have a reservation, we were staying at the Q & C and were told Luke was nearby and that their happy hour was about to begin, so that's why we just showed up.  Our server's attitude was pretty much the same as the hostess'.  When placing our drink orders he seems like he'd rather be somewhere else and when he'd leave we couldn't find him anywhere.  My husband finally asked him nicely, "having a bad day, huh?"  to which he replies, "nah.  I just started my shift."  THAT was awkward. 

Awkward service the rest of the meal.  Again, the food was delicious as we expected, we frequent Luke here in San Antonio so we know what to expect.  Won't bother paying a visit next time we are in NOLA.  We'll just stick to eating at Luke here at home.

tried to place an order with doordash and this restaurant a day before last. they restaurant called me and asked if they could swap out an item with another since they didn't have any on stock. after an hour of placing an order and the phone call, they decided to abruptly cancel my order without explanation. i then refresh my doordash app and see that this place was now "closed". Fortunately, i was refunded but the lack of professionalism makes me not want to even consider this place again or recommend it i anyone else. 

why couldn't they just tell me they were closing rather than say they were going to fix my order?

This is the worst Chinese food ever. I ordered shrimp egg foo young...the shrimps were hard and the eggs were burnt, I also had general tso chicken and 6 wings with shrimp fried rice, the wings were burnt never ate the fried rice and the general tso chicken was for my son so can't comment but overall place was clean but the food is disgusting never again will I eat here ever. Oh and the portion sizes suck for the price!!!! I am being forced to give one star or I can't comment. PLEASE DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY!!!!

Brunch at Luke left me with mixed feelings. We were greeted by a hostess who looked at us as though we had just killed her cat, and our waiter seemed like he had a thousand things he'd rather be doing than waiting tables. They weren't particularly busy, but our waiter seemed occupied with doing anything but his job. I don't always like my job either, but after the third time I'd asked for a water refill and was absolutely parched, I had to wonder what he was up to when he kept vanishing. 
Despite the terrible service, my food was delicious. The Bloody Marys had just enough kick. I ordered the fried oyster, bacon and avocado salad to start, and the oysters were perfection (although the dressing was a bit heavy). My entree was the Croque Madame, and the crispy edges were heavenly. The middle got a bit soggy with all the cheese and a little much mustard, but overall I was happy. One of my dining companions had the Crawfish Bisque, which was one of the worst things I've ever eaten. Imagine a cup of heavy cream mixed with pepper. No crawfish flavor, terrible seasoning and entirely too heavy. Nothing like what my grandmother used to make. The same dining companion had a particularly unfortunate meal, as she ordered the crab omelet. All I can say here is that cucumber, crab and eggs do not belong on the same fork. 
The third diner in our party had some better luck with the seafood gumbo (good, not amazing), a nice crab salad and some sort of onion bacon tart thing that was divine in small portions, but a bit heavy overall. Fries were served cold. Not lukewarm, cold. 
I thought it might be an off day and was ready to forgive the bad service until a bartender popped open a bottle of champagne and the cork grazed my head (I was sitting about 20 feet from the bartender in question), and no one seemed to care. 
Our waiter resurfaced at the end of the meal to ask how things were, we told him we were finished, and no less than 20 minutes later he returned to again ask how we were doing. Check please? He wandered off not to be seen again for 10 minutes, and we entertained ourselves watching the hostess wander from her post then sprint back across the restaurant every time the phone rang. Professional. Really. Add some bizarre, disjointed decor and the overall atmosphere almost ruined my food. I've eaten at a few other Besh restaurants and have never been disappointed until now. I want to believe that this was a bad day, but as the best service we received all day was from the valet at the Hilton next door, I don't see myself returning.

Last night, I ordered Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" at Luke. After the first bite, I could tell the shrimp was mushy. But I didn't believe that a highly rated restaurant and a $25 dish would serve shrimps that were not fresh. I still finished my dinner. One hour later, I got rashes on my whole body and it was very itchy. It happens when I eat bad shrimps and I need to take an allergy pill to relieve it. I feel deeply disappointed with this restaurant. Will never go back again.

Food amazing, service eehh.  

So this place is small & very busy, reservations highly recommended..... Drinks pretty good & service as the bar was fast.  Once we were seated we had two different servers that were serving us & they both took forever to do anything, they were nice I will give them that.  We ordered beet salad OMG SO GOOD, shrimp & grits (delish) & shrimp en contte (also delish, better than the shrimp & grits & that is saying a lot).  Again, they were busy & it took forever but worth the wait.  Ahhh dessert bread pudding the absolute BEST I have ever had & I am actually not ever really a fan of bread pudding until now, I mean this stuff was to die for a MUST TRY.
Lively atmosphere and very friendly bartender. $0.50 cent oysters during happy hour.
Had a great meal there.  A bit pricey but its ok. Tried the meat platter and loved it. The food portions here was plentiful and the drinks were right on the $$$Money$$$
Great restaurant but it's more expensive than noted on Yelp. Great shrimp and grits, great oysters, amazing soups and chowder too. But should be rated $$$.

Dropped in here for dinner upon arrival at our hotel since it was very closeby.

Rabbit liver pate - I guess my palette wasn't ready for this but I didn't like it much and the fiancee totally hated it. It was a different taste than the regular liver pate I'm used to.

Seafood etouffe - Great flavor along with a different presentation - served over fresh made pasta.

Shrimp & grits - Everyone on Yelp raved about this so I gave it a try. The shrimp was bursting with flavor and the grits were perfectly cooked and creamy. Shrimp was perfectly cooked as well. It was, however, a bit salty - was probably the combo of the roux, sausage, and spices in the sauce. I had a glass or 2 of water before finishing the plate (while normally I don't drink at all until I finish my meal).

A bit overpriced for what we received but at a restaurant of John Besh caliber, this is expected.

Went to Luke for dinner. I have been to this restaurant once already and it was great. This time. I decided to go again (a year later) to see if the magic was still there.  I walked in without a reservation and had to wait a little bit.

For an appetizer we had the dozen shrimp  cocktail. They were just delicious. The shrimp tasted as if they were just plucked from the Gulf only moments earlier. I couldn't help but to channel my inner Bubba Gump and ponder the many uses of the shrimp. Next for a first course we both had the crawfish bisque. It was like drinking liquid crawfish. Seasoned just right. I had the ribeye topped with crabmeat. My lady friend had the redfish stew of some sort (one of the daily specials...Friday). Equally as good. 

Lastly, the bread pudding. It was good. I have had better...but not many. 

Definitely a place you should put on your lists of restaurants to visit when you go to New Orleans.
I have gone through the drive through on multiple occasions and three times my order has been completely wrong... frustrating.

If you want quick and fast service during lunch this is a good place to try. Do not go here on the weekends it is jampacked with bunch of drunks and it's VERY SMOKEY. The bar is way too small to hold lot of people. 

The staff is friendly and service is quick.  Food is your typical bar food but it's not bad by any means. Drinks are strong and the prices are reasonable.

The bathrooms are dirty and this place is "rundown", a hole in the wall. If I were ever to go back it would be during lunch time only. I made a mistake one time and walked in on a weekend with some friends, and we walked right out because of the smoke. It's almost seemed like foggy because of all the smoke.

Got off work early enough to make it here! I've been wanting to try this cafe forever but, while it's right by where I live, their hrs are so minimal that I'm usually at work or elsewhere. 

Anyways, the atmosphere is okay. About as hipster as one would expect. I like how bright and white it is but it's TINY. Very little outdoor seating (which isn't ideal on a cool day)... but I took my sandwich home so it didn't really matter.

Cookie was a solid 'meh'. The texture was nice; soft and chewy how I like without it being particularly crumbly. But the flavour wasn't great. It actually had a sort of bitterness to it, as if there was too much baking soda or something. Anyways. Not a cookie to write home about (and a good chocolate chip cookie is my favourite dessert in the world). 

I got a sandwich (roast beef, gruyere, tomato jam, pickles, some sort of lettuce/spinich) since I've heard so many great things about their sandwiches but it was also pretty average... maybe even below average. Maybe my expectations were off, but all the pictures people have posted are of delicious leafy looking sandwiches on amazing looking buns, but it wasn't the case. It was squished flat into a panini (the menu didn't even mention that it was a warm sandwich...) and the flavours were pretty disappointing. After taking a couple bites to try, I opted to deconstruct it and create something better. After removing the sad, soggy pickles and adding some crisp pepperocini from my own fridge it was actually pretty good... but I'm not going to rate something great that I had to re-create in order to make it good. 

I'll probably be back at some point to try a breakfast sandwich (they look so good!) but won't be back for lunch.

This restaurant disappointed - given it has 4 stars on Yelp and $$. It should really be 3 stars and $$$. Really too expensive for what you get. I was glad they were open on xmas, but that meant a more expensive menu with even less choice. The shrimp and grits was pretty tasty, as were the mussels, but other things disappointed. The worst offender was the Bibb lettuce salad (not sure how they messed up a salad, but they did) and the overly salty french fries. And the matzoh ball soup was just awful - but then again, why did I order that at a french brasserie? Probably because it was 30 degrees underneath the A/C (which they claimed they couldn't turn down because it's controlled by the hotel they are in).

I've been a member for about two years. 

PROS: First, this is a very good gym. The child care is terrific - with a nice, spacious room with a DVD for the kids. So...no guilt while Mommy works out. The equipment is plentiful and the bathrooms are good. Most of the personal trainers are very good and will work with you to help you achieve your goals within your individual abilities. The circuit training area is awesome. They have mini TV's on just about every treadmill/elliptical machine. Plus, it's cheap $20/month, or $30 if you want unlimited childcare during their child care hours. 

CONS: The classes are crowded. A number of the TV's on the treadmills don't work. The movie room should either be improved or eliminated so the classes have more space. The movie room has about 10 elliptical, bike and treadmills in it and, I swear, it's about a 12 x 12 room. If you go in here, the sweat from the five people chugging along in there is pungent. It's kind of gross and smells - pretty much all the time. There appears to be inadequate ventilation in that space, which is a shame, because some days you just want to go in, watch a movie, do a half hour on an elliptical and leave. 

So...there you have it.
Amazing service, nice staff and delicious food!! So glad we got to try it, def recommend if you are visiting in NOLA.
I order the burger every time. It can get busy, but it is charming to weave in and out of the patrons.

Fantastic oysters, fried and raw, with happy hour specials - price is right. oh hand the juleps - uh yeah, good. Raw oyster for $0.50/ea for happy hour and half off drinks. Oysters as big as a baby hand.

Might be the BEST omelette ever (crab) - very light, fluffy and tasty!! The shrimp and grits was AMAZING! Great service! Highly recommend for breakfast. Can't wait to try dinner!

So we came back for happy hour and light dinner. Good oysters, especially at .75 per.! The duck and chicken liver patte was excellent! This is definitely a favorite restaurant.

You can't go to New Orleans without getting some seafood, I've always said (I haven't always said that,) so after a glowing recommendation from my coworker, my boyfriend and I tried out the happy hour at Luke. Happy hour prices, cute ambiance, and one of the nicest servers ever = 5 star experience.

So basically, happy hour runs like 4 to 6pm and its dirt cheap. Oysters are $.75/each (YEAH), fried oysters are $1.25/each, and drinks are half off. Are you kidding? We had 2 dozen oysters, a half dozen fried oysters, the ricotta gnocchi, and I had 2 french 75s. The oysters were MASSIVE, the fried oysters were crispy and delicious, and the gnocchi was soft and hot. I couldn't even try to complain about the French 75 - they even drew a little syrup-y heart on top of the foam. Not a single complaint from us, the food blew us away.

The inside of the place feels very lavish 90s hotel, but I'm not saying that's a bad thing. It was fancy, without the pretense. When we got there around 5:30pm, we had to wait for about 5 minutes to give the servers time to sit the groups they had just sat, but it wasn't a big deal. Our server (his name escapes) was a young man and was super duper sweet, knowledgeable, and just one of those individuals who loved talking to people. On top of that, our food and drinks all came out super quickly, despite the restaurant being pretty packed. The crowd drew all sorts: business men/women, young people getting after-work drinks, tourists (like ourselves) trying out some seafood.

For the amount of food and drink we had, the happy hour prices are unbeatable. Affordable, relaxed, and excellent service. I'd love to come back and try some other dishes on the menu... but I'd still need the oysters again.

Found Dr. Reddy by reading an article in one of the locals papers. The editor had lost a pet to cancer and was complimenting the vet on his compassion and knowledge. We previously had been taking our dog to a group of vets off of bruce b downs blvd that were overpriced and all they wanted to do was run a plethora of test once they discovered our beloved dog had cancer. Taking all matters into consideration we decided to try our hand at Dr. Reddy's facility. The article in the newspaper was correct in everything they had written. Dr. Reddy and his vet tech Nancy did everything they could to make our baby comfortable for the remainder of his life without pushing every test none to man down our throats. They only made recommendations that would benefit our friend. Unfortunately, our baby lost his heroic battle to cancer recently. Dr. Reddy helped provide the quality of life that he so deserved. If you are looking for a vet that is knowledgeable and compassionate -- you have come to the right place.
Pretty good! The jalepeno grits are yummy, and pulled pork sandwich is fantastic (though heavy on the mayo)

A highly rated and much reviewed restaurant always catches my eye on Yelp...I arrived with great expectations!  I was greeted with a very full restaurant, a nice hostess and vibrant energy.
I was seated in a little corner and a nice table where I can watch the restaurant. I was brought water by one gentleman, who I'm not sure was my actual server (but immediately asked if I wanted something other than water to drink) and then it was followed up by a visit from who I assume was my waitress to take my order.  I liked her kind, attentive attitude to start.
Simple meal: $17.50 Burger (wrapped in lettuce).  Fries came out skinny, COLD, and too salty.  Asked the male server for a replacement and 3 minutes later, with burger half finished, fries replaced.  Burger was average at best.  Not flavorful, not special.

Dessert: pavlova.  A wonderful Australian fave I hadn't ever seen on a menu.  I was excited, until I took my first bite... The already sweet pavlova was drenched in a very sweet fruit compote. Totally ruining the concept.  Pavlova needs tart fruits, not over-sweetened sweet ones.
Coffee:  ordered with the Pavlova, came when the pavlova was half done.  

I never saw the female waitress again until she picked up the check with my form of payment that the had been dropped off.  Maybe my table of one disappointed them?

I would give this place a try again, but nothing about it was outstanding... Perhaps the 2000+ reviews are from tourists who are used to eating from fast food chains and other mediocre places.
Happy hour .75 cent raw oysters and half price wine, beer , and cocktails. This place is the best in New Orleans. Not on the happy hour, but a must try are the jalapeno cheese grits!

Was staying at the Hilton on the recommendation of a local friend I didnt realize how lucky I was that the Luke was downstairs. Good drinks and the food was nice but the oyster bar put it over the top. The oysters were delicious and plentiful for a good price. Most important though was the great info shared by the folks working the bar. They gave spot on suggestions and got us pointed in the direction of a Second Line parade which is a great time. In summation, food and drinks here are good but the staff makes this place top-notch.
They were super accommodating for our large group of 13 just before there dinner started they arranged a table for us and opened early. Even with all that the food the food the food!!!!

$1 oysters 
1/2 beers and cocktails

What more can a girl ask for?!?!

This review is long over due, but I'll make it quick and let you judge for yourself.  
I've been to New Orleans twice now.  Both trips, I've made it a point to go to Luke.  On the second trip, we went twice over the 5 day stay.  Yes, it really is that great.

You may have noticed that I went to Domenica and Restaurant August as well.  They're just as good, but Lukes has a special place in my heart.  The happy hour is just wonderful!!  Half price French 75s, $1 oysters, and pates are decadent pleasures one can never encounter for a bargain, especially not with the same quality.  And man-oh-man, the oysters at Luke are plump, juicy, and sweet, reminiscent of the Tomales Bay variety!  

Have not had much off the menu, but I'm sure it's top notch.  The appetizers alone are winners in my book. 

Can't wait until my next rendezvous at Luke, and hopefully to catch a glimpse of the talented Mr. Besh!
Breakfast this morning -- mediocre.  Restaurant was dark and smelly.  Eggs were cold.  Coffee lukewarm at best.  The morning at Luke has cast a pall over the day.

Had the onion flatbread as an appetizer and was impressed.  Jalapeno shrimp & grits was exceptional as well as the BLT with fried soft shell crab.
After eating - luckily after eating - watched bartender open large jar of olives and pick out with bare hands to skewer as condiment for martini's.  Three olives per skewer - she must have done 100 of them with her bare hands while handling cash, credit cards and register and then back to touching the olives.

If you want to escape the heat and the crowds for a great lunch then pop into Lüke. 

This place has a wonderful old worldly gentleman club feel about it. With old school belt driven fans hanging from the pressed metal ceiling panels. Great swivel top wooden bar stools and a lovely glass display case with the catch of the day sitting on ice. 

Food is good and the waiting staff are friendly and know their job. Top marks to the gentleman who looked after me. 

Price is like most good places I'm finding in the States a bit on the high side. I had a cocktail, 2x appetisers, bread pudding and a coffee $56.53 + tips so $65 for lunch for one. But hay it's not the Golden Arches... 

Enjoy.
Delicious Cajun cuisine in an elegant old fashioned venue. Reasonable prices, good service. Be sure to make reservations during popular hours.

By far, this is the best Chinese food I have had in the area.  The food is full of flavor, and they are very quick!

Worth the drive if you don't live in Lutz.

These guys don't skimp like the others do.

I love Panera food. However, this was the SECOND time in a row that this store missed putting something in the bag of my to go order. Last time it was a cookie - no big deal, I didn't really need it anyway, and I allow for an oops every once in awhile. This time, they forgot the cream cheese ($1.30 extra charge, btw) for my bagel. Um, that's kinda important to me. Get it together, Panera. The Meridian and Nampa stores seem to have it more together. This store needs to focus on getting the orders down on the first try.
Amazing service.  They have their own micro brewery which is cool.  Oysters fresh and great!  Overall food was good with good presentation.
Went there for the happy hour and ate 2 dozen oysters. One of the highlights of my trip.

One of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans. I had the fried oyster salad tonight and OMG that was amazing. AND it's a John Besh restaurant which means the culinary fan girl comes out. 
Highly recommend for good southern NOLA cuisine.

Two stars for the lomein and the spring roll was pretty good but the sesame chicken tasted like it's been out for three weeks tasted very old and hard to chew. Couldn't even finish eating it and had to throw out because I was going to throw up. The shrimp over rice tasted like dirty water. This place is not very hygienic. Won't be coming back again! We came very far away to try a halal Chinese and this is what we get a crusty chicken.

This was the shrimp and grits I have ever had.  The shirmp were cooked perfectly.  You don't find that often, they are almost always overcooked.  They have a local beer, Luke Alt, that was good.  Tried the Fru, but that wasn't my favorite.
One bad piece of news, the waiter was really bad and the back room was quite loud.
My friend had the bratwurst and it was pretty good too.  The bed of potatoes that the brat sat on was way yummy too.
So...food great, staff bad!!!!
Listen, I am now a Besh fan for life. We went for happy hour and 75¢ oysters and ended up staying and having some of the best food all trip. Fantastic place, lots of fun!

We walked in like clowns, so of course the hostess and servers were more playful than I would normally expect.  We got the last table in the back corner.  Oh well, it was National Oyster Day, where Luke offered $0.75 oysters.  They were shucked very well and arranged as normal on a bed of ice.  No issues.  The martinis were dirty as requested along with my requested 3 blue cheese stuffed olives.  It was strange though that my  friend said she didn't care on the number of olives and got only one olive.  I would expect at least two.  Later we saw the hostess snacking on the olives and realized that there was probably only those 4 left.  Anyways, great time, the volume of a full restaurant wasn't so overpowering.  The service was excellent.  I will definitely come back for a regular meal.  Boom!

Ok.  Just ok. I had high hopes but fell flat.  Service was excellent, setting is nice and location is convenient if you are staying in a hotel downtown.  The menu was small as I expect for a better restaurant.  However, the fried oyster salad and hamburger just didn't hit the spot.  

Oyster salad had six fried oysters that were cooked ok but the batter didn't have much flavor.  The hamburger had large smoked bacon that was mostly fat and chewy.  Had an ok taste but for $17 I expected more flavor.  The fries were excellent!! 

I would give it try if I was ever in the area but can't say I would make a special trip to visit  again or go out of my way to avoid if I was in a group that wanted to visit Luke's.

I told them I had to be out of there by 1145 so I could pick my son up. They told me no worries even though I got there at 1115. They had me out with my oil change right on time. Very courteous and very respectful crew. A very big thank you to Patrick M., Thomas F., Robert H., and Jacorie!

Great ambience and superb service. We enjoyed the gumbo, corn and crab bisque & fresh oysters. Wonderful wine list and lovely cocktails. The gentleman next to us ordered the tallest, most decadent burger I have seen in a long while - he said it was delish. We were just too stuffed from eating through NOLA all day, to order more! I will be back!

Really great happy hour. 3-6. Half off cocktails. $0.75 oysters. Attentive service. 

Pate, corn and crab bisque, and grits are all great. 

WHISKEY A GO GO is a must try cocktail. Trust me.
Love REI! Such good customer service and good quality! And the sales are amazing if you hit them at the right time! Became a member and I can't wait to shop there again!

Server was above & beyond... Craig?  I showed him a pic of the Chicken & Biscuits & he said 'it's no longer on the menu, but we have chicken & biscuits, so I'll ask the Chef & am sure it won't be a problem.'  Says it all.  Excellent service!  

The Chicken & Waffles, even the omelette, everything we saw coming from the kitchen looked mouthwatering & huge shareable portions.  Truly one of my new NOLA favs!  I cannot wait to come back!

It was my first time ever in NOLA; late flight in, the restaurant was scheduled to close in 20 minutes. The manager seated us, we had 2 waiters waiting on us, the food was out of this world, the Reisling was my favorite one. I was literally in Heaven. The Shrimp Etouffe yum, yum. Excellent service, delicious food, drinks. You can't go wrong. Cheers to Luke restaurant

Our first night in town, our hotel concierge (Greg at the International House) recommended them for dinner and he was right!  "Richie Rich" helped us with recommendations and split our entrees so we could both try the dishes. My husband's favorite was the ettouffe with crispy rice (great touch with the rice!) and I loved their cheesy shrimp and grits. BEST grits I've personally ever had!!  We had a fabulous experience on the first night of our honeymoon, and we plan on going back before we leave for home. Excellent!!

We visited Luke for a late dinner on a Sunday night and, based on other reviews, it seemed like an off night.  We ordered the blood sausage for an appetizer and, though our server told us how wonderful it is when served with mustard, failed to bring the mustard to our table.  We were hard-pressed to even get a refill of our water.  The blood sausage was pretty average and probably would have been much better had it been complete with the mustard.  We split the shrimp and grits which were quite good.  The grits were creamy but still had a nice texture.  We decided to skip dessert because the service was poor and our waiter was often no where to be found, despite the fact that the restaurant wasn't that busy.  Once again, we probably caught them on an off night with a sub-par server but our visit left something to be desired.

Staying at a friend's house I was looking for a breakfast place in the area.  There was nothing closer than the Elm Cafe.  Situated a block north of Jasper Ave it's in a great location among a mixed residential & commercial street.

It's odd because I'm still not 100% sold on my thoughts.  As I write this review part of me says it was a great food experience.  The other part of me says it's not worth the price of admission.

I was going to get food to go and I'm glad I was because this place is TINY.  Mainly a catering company it seems like they decided to have this storefront as an afterthought.  There is a nice patio but no umbrellas that I could see.  I guess the shade from the Elm trees is good enough?

The selection was tiny as they were only serving two breakfast sandwiches, muffins and a couple other baked goods.  I tried one of the sandwiches $8+ and I was quite impressed with the taste.  The Americano they made me was also fantastic.  I'd really truly give it a 3.5 stars if I could but I'll have give them the benefit of the doubt and round it up.

I'd go back if I was in the area again but I wouldn't go out of my way.

This was very disappointing to us. We really wanted to have a nice quiet evening so we could talk and enjoy each others company. However what we got was a very noisy restaurant with people yelling and screaming (most likely drunks) and the restaurant was extremely crowded. We felt like we were sitting on top of the tables next to us and could hear EVERYTHING they were talking about. We were greeted at our table but  2 (two) servers who said they would both be taking care of us. it took them twice as long to take our drink orders, serve our drinks and to finally serve our food. The food was the best part, we really enjoyed our dishes as they were cooked perfectly. We really wanted to like this place but the overall atmosphere really killed it for us.

We made reservations here during happy hour. They have 50 cent oysters and half priced drinks! We ordered 2 dozen to start and was very happy with what we got. Huge, meaty, and mild oysters! yummy. We were so excited we ordered a total of 6 dozens :) It's happy hour.... I figure why not?!?!? So, 6 dozen oyzters and two drinks later, we paid the check and walked away happily. 

It is a MUST GO place! I absolutely loved it!

We stopped in for a late breakfast early lunch. The space is beautiful and the food is wonderful. A few of us got the southern breakfast which they agreed was exactly what they needed after a long night of going out. I ordered the eggs in a jar which were fantastic and the shrimp that came with it were just so good. We also ordered the crabmeat maison which is a perfect light meal for someone who doesn't want anything too heavy which tends to happen when you are eating in NOLA. Another in our group got the shrimp and grits and again loved every bite. This restaurant is in the John Besh group and I am not really sure how you can go wrong with it. I would like to come back for dinner at some point and to really attack the raw bar but I have to say that this place is awesome for a quick and easy breakfast/lunch.
50 cent raw oysters during happy hour. Can't beat that!!

There's not a thing bad to say about this place. The price may seem a bit alarming at first but it's definitely worth the price. They offer a buffet, but unless you are just looking to be stuffed, adventure to the menu and sample one of Jon Besh's French/German dishes with a Louisiana twang. Sat down and enjoyed Nicaraguan French pressed coffee that was chocolatey and silky that sort of cut into its strength. I enjoyed the shrimp and grits that had a delicious New Orleans kick. Julia had Crab stuffed Eggs Benedict that topped caramelized onions with bacon crumbles.. LALICIOUS (it's beyond delicious)

So while the food was filling and inspired a slower moving day, the coffee got us ready for or next New Orleans adventure. DEFINITELY STOP HERE!

THIS REVIEW IS ABOUT RICH WHATLEY! THE MOST PHENOMENAL SERVER WE HAVE EVER HAD IN OUR LIFE!

Luke is incredible... every single John Besh restaurant is. But this review is dedicated to Rich.. what a server! He was incredible to our table and truly made our graduation evening special. I could not say enough good things about this guy - he was entertaining, he was helpful, he went above and beyond. 

Thank you to Luke, but more importantly, thank you Rich! We will come back from NY just to visit you!!!! You were amazing!!

While visiting New Orleans I decided to eat at Luke's for my birthday dinner with my friends. We had the P&J stuffed oysters, the shrimp etouffée and the entrecôte grillée et frites was beyond delicious. I will definitely come back on my next visit to New Orleans.

Lüke, what can I say that hasn't already been said.
Yes, it has the cache and expectation level of a John Besh restaurant.
And in my opinion, it meets and exceeds them on every level.
The P&J Oysters are of course, a sublime treat.
When I went there with my bride on our Honeymoon, they were 25cents now I hear they are 50 cents..
But still not to be missed.
Look, you know Besh will never steer you wrong and you will not leave there disappointed.
Give it a try, and let me know what you think..
Big Easy Daddy..
Brussels sprouts to die for!!! We stumbled across this little jewel and it was beyond worth the wait!!! Yummy!!

The 75 cent raw oyster special at LUKE made it to my Happy Hour hop around NOLA.  

At the point of arrival, around 4pm and stop #3/4, my crew and I had already discovered the sexy chargrilled cousin to raw oysters.  The appeal of taking them raw and stripped down didn't seem as appealing especially since none of us had the acquired taste for it...  until we had them here. 

Something between them being sift of sand, sin of slime, and less than a buck made for a very enjoyable time.  Only downsides on our brief experience here were very sweet cocktails and a very salty waiter who couldn't wait FIVE minutes for us decide on drinks and food.  I would still strongly recommend coming here for oysters or a full 3 course dinner.  See Juliana T.'s review for the more complete meal I missed out on...

Luke provided us with a great meal and awesome service during our last night in NOLA. The oysters were fresh and tasty. Crab fritters were large and we enjoyed it with a fried oyster salad that we split for us on two plates. Our server was a professional and tended to our dining needs with flair. The evening ended with coffee and a bread pudding pairing that knocked my socks off. There was so much charm provided in the food and service. Please check this restaurant out for your signature New Orleans meal.

Beautiful restaurant with a great atmosphere,  a extremely friendly wait staff and friendly chiefs.   The sushi at hachi is superior then any of the local competition.  They take  great care and pride in the preparation and presentation of their food.  They also have wonderful new creations that I've never seen before and they make for a very enjoyable and memorable dining experience.  This quickly has become my favorite restaurant.  The chefs do a great job of explaining the dishes and highlight the level of quality  and freshness of the ingredients.  Highly recommended A+++

After a crazy night in NOLA we needed food. Good food. 

Hopped on yelp, saw the reviews/the rating and walked out the hotel door. 

I noticed the menu changes seasonally or daily or I don't even know. But a lot of the pictures I saw were not what was happening when we came in today but nonetheless such a good array of food options for brunch. 

We got the crispy Brussels 10/10. So damn good 

Seafood gumbo was good. I personally like my gumbo a little spicier but there were plenty of oysters and shrimp and sausage in mine so I was a happy girl. 

Fried chicken and biscuit- If you've been to Texas and have hada whataburger honey butter chicken biscuit this is that... but upgraded. I was so full at this point but I ate a good portion of it still. What made this absolutely delicious was the Tabasco honey. good lord. 

I tried my friend's shrimp and jalapeño cheese grits. Delicious. 
The burger looked good as well but my tummy was telling me noooo 




Preston our waiter and Rob the manager took SUCH good care of us. Can't wait to be back in New Orleans

What's not to like about Luke?!?!? Good location, many great food options, clean, and classy restaurant. The boudin balls are amazing! Gumbo is good. I came with a group and we went with the raw seafood tower. Everything was great! Highly recommended!

We made reservations on Open Table and were seated at the time of our reservation. Saw some complaints on Yelp in the reviews regarding the service but ended up being pleasantly surprised.

Wow is all i can say! Started with the rabbit Pâté which was accompanied with three toppings of which the watermelon rind was out of this world. 

Had the concotte(sp) which was the grits which was infused with cream and butter and a wonderful sauce that surrounded the grits topped off with 5 healthy grilled shrimp. AMAZING DINNER for the price. Gonna be in New Orleans all week. Will be returning. 

Contrary to the negative review on service: Gene was our waiter and he could work in any 4 star restaurant. Had great suggestions and was attentive. 5 minutes did not go by and he was checking on us. So my recommendations to any of the nay Sayers c/o of the service is try Luke's again!

P.S. dessert was delicious but after being overwhelmed with the litany of taste blowing favors from our meal; we ordered light and tasted a small tart crammed with fresh strawberries and topped with creamy ice cream. Nice topper for a great meal.

Came here for their Happy Hour. 

Oysters on the half shell- half of them were clean, half still had pieces of shell and sand
Fried Oysters- smaller than we expected, but better than the raw oysters
Pate- very rich and mousse like

As I exited the tunnel from the Septa trolley I immediately looked for a rest room before checking out the Penn Relays on Friday,  April 23rd.  Just by coincidence I overheard a Georgetown Univ student comment about the bathroom in the upstairs dining area, so considering my options were limited and having to go REALLY BAD, I headed there myself. 

After returning downstairs and checking my watch I figured out I had plenty of time to get a bite to eat before heading to Franklin Field.  That's when I noticed the menu.  

Ordered the Spinach Florentine which I thought was really good.  I've never had anything like it and specifically the artichoke spread.  I went back on Saturday and had the Tuscan Pesto Chicken.  Also really good. 

One note though, this place is a bit pricey so don't be surprised.

Dined here on a Friday night at 5:00.  Not busy but our waitress was extremely inattentive.  My husband's Cabernet was served in a juice glass filled to the brim, but about 2" wide.  Definitely set the tone for what continued to be a disappointing meal.  My skate wing could have been good if it were not greasy and soaked in sauce.  Husband gives a "2"
Stumbled on this and what a happy hour find. Been there several times. On our "always list" along with GW Fins. Raw oysters by the dozen, yum!!

"Richy Rich" was our waiter and he was so wonderful! I can probably say the best in town hands down. He was humorous without being an ass (like some can) and STILL get everything done right and super tentative. 

Happy hour is half off cocktails and many beer & wine + 50 cents oysters! 
We also ordered the crab soup- do yourself a favor and get the bowl... if not two!
There's so much meat in it and just pure quality. 

Richard was so sweet, we mentioned that it was a birthday trip and he treated us to the most amazing chocolate caramel dessert. Def. made our day.

We are so grateful that strangers we met told us about this place. We will come back as soon as we come back in town!!

If you're going to Luke you're probably going because you've either read good things, heard good things, or know it's a John Besh restaurant. Your reasoning doesn't matter. If you're looking for a good meal with a little nicer ambiance at a reasonable price Luke should be on your itinerary. On this trip to New Orleans they had hands down the best service out of the 11+ places I ate at. Water was always full. The hostess and manager were able to seat our large party all at one table even though we had originally had two separate groups. And the wait staff was friendly, knowledgeable, and attentive. 

What should you order at Luke? If there's one thing you should eat there and possibly get seconds of it's the Brussel sprouts! That is not a typo. Get the Brussel sprouts! Besides the alligator sausage at Parkway Tavern this is the one dish on this trip that really stood out. I want this recipe! Mr. Besh if you're reading this please message me your Brussel sprouts recipe! I also tasted the shrimp and grits and the pork schnitzel with some kind of amazing mushroom sauce. 

The shrimp and grits was really good. Would I order it again? Probably not. But that's because I already make a damn good shrimp and grits. The pork schnitzel on the hand is worth ordering multiples of. First of all there's enough pig on this plate to serve two hungry guys. While the pork is cooked perfectly and it fried to a golden brown, it's the sauce that's the star of the show. You could put this sauce on top of balut (fertilized duck egg) and I'd eat a dozen of them. I sampled a few other dishes here as well and everything was great. If possible sit in the back by the kitchen and watch the chefs work their magic or take a look at the framed menus from the past Luke has hanging around the walls. There really isn't one bad thing I can say about Luke. Thanks for a great last dinner In New Orleans.

I don't even know how to begin documenting my experience here. We came here on a Wednesday night, 8pm reservation for 7 people.
Our server brought us water and we ordered drinks. Let me tell you, their special drinks menu is classic..haha. As I looked at their cocktail menu, every drink had a bourbon, cognac, or some other "acquired taste" type of liquer. I guess we know who their target market is. Some guys (late 20s) in the group ordered the Mint Julep, they hated it. I had the French 75, that actually came in a cognac glass. I didn't mind it and sipped it throughout our meal.

For food, we all started out with oysters. Those were GOOD! Horseradish was a little strong though. I then started with the crawfish bisque, salty but delicious. Entree for me was the crabmeat ravioli. It started out tasting a little funny, but as I ate more I started to really enjoy it. What bothered me about that dish is the fact that the raviolis were all stuck together (the skin) but broken apart in the middle and all the stuffing was everywhere. My boyfriend had the ribeye with crabmeat on top (served on a cutting board). I think the ribeye would have been pretty average if it weren't for the delicious crab meat. For sides, I had the sauteed local vegetable, too oily but tasted good. My boyfriend had the fries that were really good but salty. I tried our friend's asparagus and it was good. 

The service was SLOW and unattentive. The funny part of the night was when a married and drunken Brazilian woman in her late 30s who started hitting on this dude in our group despite her husband being right there. She told our friend that she's never had a black guy before and she heard that once you go black you don't go back...wtf..haha...she was at our table whispering to him for like 15 minutes before we had to get the server to tell her to leave. She was friends with all the servers and busboys in the restaurant so maybe she work(s)(ed) there(???) Definitely not classy..though entertaining.

SO, OVERALL, as you can see by my rambling, everything is followed by a "but." The food was delicious but you just dont go away feeling like everything is top-notch. Always a little something missing.

So good, I went there twice while in New Orleans.

The duck/rabbit pate is to die for, and the oysters are spectacular.

I also had the mussels which came in a great cast iron pot along with ample amounts of broth, and more than enough flavor.  I swear there were about 30 mussels in that pot!


Best of all, it's not some pretentious, up scale place.  It's solid food at a great price.

I had the Cuban and the chicken tortellini soup today. The soup was really good. The Cuban was just ok. If I had to point out one thing that I didn't like about the sandwich it would probably be the bread.Also the meats weren't the greatest. I was really looking forward to trying the Cuban because I haven't been able to find a place yet that makes it on point. Guess I'll have to keep searching for the perfect Cuban sandwich elsewhere. I've had other sandwiches here in the past that I really liked but the Cuban isn't one of them.

Had dinner with a business associate on Monday Evening at Luke.  We were both staying at the Hilton, making Luke an easy option.

Loved the atmosphere, our waiter was awesome.  However, the food clearly had some challenges.  We wanted to get the 75 cent Happy Hour oysters (regularly $2.00 each); however, the special ended at 6PM and it was now 604 PM.  Ugh.  So I asked the waiter which oysters were the very best.  He suggested the ones at $3.25 each.  So I ordered a dozen for $39.00 expecting nirvana.  What we got were mediocre oysters, a small amount of overly hot cocktail sauce and horseradish.  Bad oysters in New Orleans is something I don't understand? 

The waiter suggested a Brando Cocktail, stating that it is similar yet better than a Sazerac.  It looked good but was too sweet for my taste.  There was way too much Amaretto within.

Then had a fried oyster salad.  It was a 3 star salad, nothing very special.  The french fries on the other hand were wonderful, glad we ordered lots of them.

By the time I had these few items I was done with this place.  Next time I am at the Hilton I won't be lazy, will make an effort to find better local fare.
Very delicious! The seafood gumbo was amazing as well as the crab meat oysters. Waiter staff was fun.

Restaurant was amazing.  Good atmosphere and great service.  There's something illegal in that etouffee - it's been past 24 hours and I'm still salivating for it - wanting more.  Sister ordered the moules et frites (mussels and fries) and it had an amazing flavor to it.  We tried the same in Paris, but this dish in New Orleans by far trumps the original found in France.  Oysters were baked with breading on it.  Can probably find better ones in the city, but still tasty.

Only reason this doesn't get a 5 is because the beer wasn't as cold as I'd liked it to be.  Still, the restaurant is great and keeps the status of Besh restaurants as one of the best line of amazing dining in town.

l will say it right up front, I didn't eat a single thing from the menu at Luke, so this review does not speak to the food.  (My 1 star rating is only reflective of the service). The problem was that I couldn't even get that far, because the service was rude to the point where I felt the need to leave before I could even have a drink at the bar.  

We tried to call ahead to make a reservation (it was a Saturday so we anticipated that it would be busy), and were told the the computer was jammed so they could not take reservations.  Apparently these folks are averse to pen and paper.  However, the person on the phone assured us that if we were coming in around 8pm for 2 people we would not have to wait long to be seated, no more than 10 minutes she said.  Took their word for it--my mistake.  When we got there at 8:30pm the hostess informed us that they were on a 45-60 minute wait.  Admittedly annoyed, but determined to stay, we headed for the bar.  

Once we sidled up we waited a good 5 minutes to be greeted, and when we did get someone to talk to us, she merely asked, "you guys good?" and then walked away.  We had to waive her back to actually order, and when we both ordered different varieties of the house Luke beer, we were informed curtly that they were out of both types--out of their own beer, on a Saturday night.  At this point we decided to dash, having had 2 negative interactions within the first 5 minutes of being there.  

Maybe it was a bad night at Luke, maybe not, but our experience was not good, and I would think twice about going back.

What an adorable little tea shop! The ginger and turmeric tea was amazing- unlike any tea I've had before. It felt healthy and energizing and was full of delicious-ness. I also scarfed down a melt-in-your-mouth salted caramel cupcake the owner imported from a nearby bakery. I totally recommend!

Everything at Luke is fantastic. We came with 7 guys with a reservation and they seated us right away. It was a Wednesday at 4pm and the place was pretty busy. We started with raw P&J Oysters and the Stuffed P&J Oysters. The raw oysters were great, but the Stuffed Oysters are NEXT LEVEL. They only come with 4, so we had to order more. A few of us said the Crawfish Bisque and said it was phenomenal. 

Definitely worth checking out, especially during happy hour!
