Doesn't look like much from the outside but the people inside are what makes it great.  You can actually get a beer at this bar and it is one of the most friendly bars I have been to.

The live music every Friday is a must.

And yes smokers can actually do it inside here.

a great disappointment. Have been to Besh's August many times, as a couple, foursome and large groups. Never less than xlnt.
At Luke we were seated promptly. Wine service: had to practically beg for the white which was tables away. Was still on appetizer when server tried to place the main dish on the table. Couldn't be dissuaded so all on table at same time. My fish dish xlnt, partner's (same dish) mealy and inedible, ?old, refrozen?? Gumbo highly recommended by waitress had enuf seafood, but was bland, not New Orleans style. Hope this was an off night Did not complain as we did not want to offend the other couple.

Food was great! I got the shrimp & jalapeño grits! I definitely recommend. It was a short walk from our hotel downtown. Unfortunately service was very slow. Once a bus boy cleared our plates after a few minutes, we still waited 10+ minutes before I asked a random server for our check because our waiter never came back.

We had Luke's for dinner and i must say i was not impressed with a lot of factors. 

The items we tried were: 
Baked pesto oysters: People said this was amazing, but i thought this was alright. I'd rather have the char-boiled oysters or fresh oysters. 
Gumbo: This was alright as well. Nothing stood out about it to me. 
Ribeye steak: Pretty good flavor to the steak, however, not as tender as the other places. 

Overall, I thought this place was pretty mediocre. They forgot our dinner and other tables who came in later got their dinner first, so we had to remind them. They also forgot my bread that came with the steak. It just seemed like an off day for them. Customer service was good, but not fantastic.

Every time I visit New Orleans I make it a number one priority to stop by Luke. Bottom line they have the best breakfast there is. The Croque Madam if I am spelling that correctly is simply Perfect! As I heard one of the waiters call it a ham and cheese sandwich on steroids. The cheese and ham blend together in the best way possible and the fries they serve with the dish could be better than the sandwich itself and I swear are fried in duck fat and or lard in addition to just regular vegetable oil. "I never said anything about being healthy." Also Luke has a wide variety of oysters 5-7 types on hand from all over the south! I would recommend Luke to anyone every time!

I finally got the opportunity to eat at this wonderful restaurant and it was GREAT! The staff was extremely kind and attentive but not overbearing. The food was amazing as well. I had the steak topped with crab meat and it was cooked to perfection with the juices running all over the wooden board, so nice! My dining partner had the roasted chicken and the crab bisque which was divine as well, also the oysters which were so fresh! I cannot say enough good things about this restaurant. Go eat here and you will understand my admiration!
Yah, definitely stick to the oyster for happy hour only. The other stuff is not a good deal.

If you like dive bars where everyone knows your name, check out the Brewhouse.  While living in west county for a couple years, this bar was a staple in my weekly routine.  In fact, it's where my boyfriend and I met three years ago.

Since the Brewhouse, located next to Balducci's and 7-11, is surrounded by apartment complexes, it tends to draw in a crowd that's sick of going to dance clubs or driving downtown.  If you live within walking distance, you'll probably run into a neighbor or two.  

Age varies at the Brew.  Customers range from old drunky who never leaves the bar stool, to young college girls singing all the words to Journey.  During the week you'll see the same faces every day.  If you're friendly, you'll meet all the regulars and the bartenders in no time.

Even though Brewhouse is small, there's a jukebox, pool table, dart board, silver strike, mini golf, and golden tee.  If you like playing pool against other bar patrons, this is a great place.  They also have karaoke, a video DJ, and poker night.

The prices are a little on the high side for a dive bar, but they get away with it since it's a short walk away from many apartments and it's cheaper than a DUI!

Oh, and check out the walls in the ladies' room for a good laugh.

The night was fun and the menu was clear.  The waiter approached with confidence and cheer. My last second decision left me curious as I decidedly asked said: your Lüke burger please. The waiter smiled and jotted it down, he looked at me and asked "how would you like this cooked?"

"Medium well please."  I replied. 

He mentioned with a sly wink that they tend to lean on the rarer side and I nodded in response, with a cheeky smile. 

With friends aplenty and drinks on the table, the rum and coke was quite satisfying. Just about 10 to 15 minutes later we found our table tight as food was incoming with no end in sight. 

Our party dined with glee and dined with joy as our waiter checked in often to ensure everything was satisfactory. 

Yes, oh yes it was. 

I forgot to mention that the waiter claimed that this burger was the best burger in all of New Orleans.  That's a huge claim, but I can say yes, so far, it is true. 

If you have the chance to dine at Lüke-do it. They don't live on the cheap side when making drinks and their food is to die for. 

Oh and they had no problem serving a cake we had baked at a bakery for dessert, we went on the occasion of a birthday. 

So yes, 5 stars.  Go eat there. You will not regret it.

John Besh place, so you know it's legit.  Fortunately, we stayed at the connecting hotel.  The wife and I got in many fights because I wanted to come here everyday.  I usually got my way by just saying "let's just stop in for a few oysters."  Then of course, you have to order at least a dozen because they are SO good, plump, and relatively cheap.

We only got oysters and fries during the happy hour, but I've heard great things about the other foods here.  Definitely check it out if you're in the area!

Lobster with home made Penne pasta!!  Yummy!!

Hearty beef stew Delicious!!

They tout themselves as upscale but that was not entirely true. The price was extreme but we found in this case that it was worth it.  

The wait staff was attentive and friendly but not to knowledgeable.

Went here and sat at the bar to dine alone. Food was good, wine pour was way short and service was terrible. The bartender was extremely rude from the moment I sat down. I am in the hospitality industry so I try to be extra nice to those in the service business. Well, this girl didn't want to have anything to do with me. She seemed annoyed that I even sat there to begin with. I had to ask twice for my wine and where I sat (only seat available at bar) was sticky so I asked for it to be wiped down. She never smiled and couldn't get rid of me fast enough. There are many other restaurants that have great food so I will not come back here or recommend to anyone else.
Great place to visit. The food was excellent. We didn't have reservations but got a table within 5 mins.

Great service! We got their live uni because they didn't have any.... dead? Uni left but it was good. The only problem was that the red fish eggs on the side tasted like wet rag, therefor we could not take another bite from it. Otherwise the pad Thai was delicious and their specialty rolls were good, nothing extraordinary.

This place is meaty! Not much for a vegetarian. The staff was super friendly and helpful. 
The express menu seems like a great deal. A soup, entree and desert for around $22, I believe. 

It's loud but comfortable with a fun atmosphere.
By far my favorite happy hour in New Orleans. Such a friendly staff, and the oysters are always delicious!

Great place for oysters and beer.  Had the New Orleans ipa.  Was great!  Damn near knocked me on my butt after three.  Also had the raw oysters and fried oysters.  Bother were fantastic.  Service was fast, just a bit of a wait for larger parties but plenty of room for small parties.

Borgne was my favorite John Besh restaurant until I came here. Luke was absolutely outstanding. The service was impeccable and the food was some of the best in New Orleans. So many tough decisions on what to order. I went with the Oysters and the pork chop. Both were superb and cooked to perfection.

We went here for breakfast one day since it was close to our hotel and we loved it. My husband is still talking about the grits we had here. I got the croque madam and it was huge- I ate a 1/2 of it and was stuffed.  They serve the coffee with heavy cream and it is so delicious. We went around 10 in the morning and there were a few parties seated, it was very quiet and a nice way to ease into the day. Wish we had more time in NOLA, would've definitely returned to try dinner here.

The BEST food and service you will find! We had the Mozzarella salad, Brussels sprouts, and shrimp & grits. Two of us shared all three entrees and are completely satisfied. These Brussels sprouts will change your life! Highly recommend!

Must Go! After so much consideration and so many choices we came across Luke on yelp. I was hesitant going back and forth because we had kids joining us for dinner and it didn't seem like they had a kids menu but we went ahead and made reservations. We arrived early because it was raining and the kids were cold and they didn't have anything earlier so we came back. We had Chi as our waitress and she was amazing! Ok now the food part they DID have a kids menu so it is very kids friendly! We ordered a dozen of oysters should have made it two dozens they were amazing . We also did shrimp and grits and Brussels sprouts they were all amazing as well. Make sure you make reservations and if you are debating on another restaurant just stop here!

I had much higher hopes for a Besh restaurant. I went for lunch on a weekday. It was pretty crowded and very noisy. The best part of my meal was my cocktail. The experience only went downhill from there. The waiter was slow and not very attentive. Tables that ordered ten min. after got their food five minuets before me. My sandwich was poorly cooked. Too hard on the outside and too soft on the inside. My boyfriend disliked his meal too. I think the restaurant tries to to mix too many food types. German and Cajun and French and Southern.... just not good enough for a Besh

I must admit, I looked forward to coming to this place. I mean, John Besh has his name all over this restaurant. I actually remembered John Besh as I watched Food Network over the years. I remembered the time on Iron Chef when he beat Mario Batali. I also remembered how he almost won The Next Iron Chef, getting beat by Symon in the finals.

Of course, I had no idea what type of influence John Besh had at Lüke besides planting his name all over it. I'm sure he didn't come into the kitchen to prepare our meals (perhaps he did, who knows?). Well, at least everything on the menu looked appetizing.

I ordered the pork belly and clam pasta. I thought it had too much oil and tasted too salty.  Also, my portion seemed small compared to my friends' dishes. Granted, they did introduce the pork belly and clam pasta dish not too long ago; maybe they needed more time to perfect it.  I should've tried their original dishes like the shrimp and grits which looked good. 

I did taste a few other dishes that my friends' ordered. Some of them did taste quite good. So perhaps, I got unlucky with my menu choice. 

Oh well. At least the server took care of us well. That guy was quite knowledgeable of the menu and had a great sense of humor. He and the rest of the staff treated us well.

I would like to come back again to try the other stuff on the menu.  But for now, I'll give the food 3 stars and +.5 star for the service, rounding up to 4 stars.

Went for Happy hour Oysters,  which were phenomenal,   especially for 50c a piece. Ended up having Venison & Wild Boar pistachio Foie Gras. and Oh ...My...God.... very reasonable price for dimensional Cuisine. Our waiter, Kaiser,  was a doll, and I would love to be seated in  his section again when we go back...and we will. A lot.

From the second I walked in here, I could already tell im going to have some quality food. I was a little disappointed they didnt have oysters for my gf, but they made up for it. We had the little neck clam soup to start things off  and it was very good. Rainbow salad was a very good starter but I feel like its for 4 people. Its large and very filling.  I forget the names of the special sushi rolls we ordered but they were all very good and were mostly combos of spicy tuna and spicy salmon.   We also had a sashimi platter and it was very fresh.  I posted some pictures. Ming our server who I believe is also the owner was awesome and very welcoming.... He made some recommendations and was very friendly.  The place is a byob which was nice to enjoy a bottle of wine of our choice.  Cant wait to come back and hopefully have some oysters!

4 stars for happy hour.  3.5 stars for the regular fare.

we came with a party of 8 for happy hour.  easy to make reservations online, which i suggest you do, because it was really packed when we got there and that was at 5pm.  raw oysters are 75 cents each and fried oysters are $1.25 each.  specialty cocktails, beer and wine are half off.  good deals all around.

we got some brussel sprout and fries for appetizers.  good, but not great.  and for entrees, the shrimp cavatelli and the wild boar ragout.  again, good, but not great.  

our waiter was super nice and accommodating... even separated our checks for us.  that's a nice touch.

overall, come for oysters during happy hour :)

I went here today for lunch with some vendors.  The service was exceptional and everything came out on time and perfectly.  We started with the crab and corn fritters.  They were full of crabmeat and the green aioli on the side with a little kick was amazing.  I got the black drum which was one of the best fish dishes I ever had.  Underneath was veggies and 3 side red potatoes.  The other person got the burger.  It was huge and delicious.  the other person got the croquet madam sandwich and was not a fan.  The ham and cheese on the inside were cold and not melted.  The cheese on top was, so she didn't like it at all.  The other person had the shrimp and grits.  Great large portions and very good just a little heavy and rich.  Spice was perfect. Will be back!

I've been treated to a few fabulous meals here and can't wait to go back. The raw oysters and crab ravioli are unbelievable - in fact I've ordered them both on two different visits. The side of asparagus is huge, so tender and even comes with the ends shaved...perfect. This is where I learned that you shouldn't by the tiny spears of asparagus - you need to buy the fat stalks because they have better flavor, and just shave the ends to keep them tender. Yes, I bought an asparagus trimmer because of this. I've also sampled the cochon po' boy and cochon du lait...their infamous dish and rightly so. Yes it's salty. It's pork! Sometimes you need to live a little. While it's fun to sit up front at the raw bar, I prefer sitting in the very back room and watching the chefs in the glass-windowed kitchen. Delicious martinis and a few standouts on the wine list. Wonderful, relaxed but classy vibe with reasonable prices.

One of the best restaurants in New Orleans. After our second visit, I can say overall it is top notch. The waitstaff is attentive, prompt and friendly. On this most recent visit, our waiter, Rich, was fantastic. 

The food is fresh and delicious. I had fresh oysters, which are 75 cents each during happy hour. My girl had the king crab and while I didn't eat it, it looked great and she said it was phenomenal. The drinks, also on happy hour, were generous in booze and tasty. For dessert, we had the bourbon peaches and cream cake, which I highly recommend. 

We'll definitely return on our next visit to the city.
Salad, soup, and oysters were a perfect hit for lunch. Just down the street from all the huddle and bustle. If you want to escape it a little. We enjoyed our meal.
More than a 2 hour wait for our meal. Mediocre and overpriced, but good service.

Service was very slow, over 3 hours for dinner. I had the ribeye, cooked med rare, asked for med. steak was this and grizzly with no seasoning. Potatoes were cold,crawfish bisque was a way to salty. The menus didn't have a selection that looked exciting food to me. They seem to put an ingredient on everything to make it different, just not appetizing to me

Are here for lunch and had the combo fresh seafood platter of six each - clams, mussels, oysters on half shell, and shrimp with a bit of fresh ceviche. Can't say enough about how fresh and well prepared this plate was. Want to come back for dinner to taste more of menu. Great service.

I will not mention about the taste due to  we never try but I give them 2 star bcoz when we walked in with my 2 little boys (8 months & 3 yr old) with 32 degrees but they take only reservations so it means they dont have table for us so i would never ever give them a try any more. Bye!!

Luke's happy hour is a must when visiting New Orleans! They offer half off drinks, 75 cent raw oysters, and 1.25 fried oysters. Their oysters are big and juicy! The biggest I've ever had! Their other menu items are also really good if you have room for them.

Don't walk in to this place without a reservation. 7:18 on a Monday night, open tables, open barstools - asked about dinner for two.  Was told no way until at least 9. Not offered seat at bar - just "no". Good luck. Looked decent, guess we'll never know.  Nope, not giving them a second chance.
A good neighborhood Ritas stand, no indoor seating, more of a grab and go place. Staff is friendly and willing to concoct any combo can you can think up.

I've had takeout from this location a couple of times after hearing rave reviews from some of the fellow locals.  I guess since I've been back more than once it speaks to quality and taste of the food at this place.  It's a small mom and pop type place, but from the takeout traffic I knew I didn't go wrong the first time I ordered from here.  I've managed to try the Hot and Sour Soup, Black Pepper Chicken, Mongolian Chicken, and Schezuan Chicken on my visits and all of those items were prepared with quality ingredients and some of the most authentic Chinese cuisine I have dined on.

Luke's treated us great for the first meal on our NOLA Girls Trip. We both had the half price cocktails (French & St Charles Summer) which were excellent. The brussels sprouts appetizer was outstanding. Savannah & Dez provided superb service too. We'll be back the next time we're in town.
Amazing!!! Happy hour $.50 oysters were huge and delicious. Also the jumbo shrimp and grits is the best meal in New Orleans.

Casual elegance, good service, great food, well worth it if you are in the area, although a bit pricy.

While our waitress was a little uninteresting, the rest of the wait staff was great and polite with the classic hospitality I would expect from any well mannered individual.

We had the local oysters and they were great! Support local food and forget that imported or flown in stuff. We shared a Flammekuche was a definite new food for me and it was fantastic. We also had a burger and ravioli and both were great. I didn't find the burger overcooked for my medium and it tasted great, not amazingly wonderful but it was a good burger.

The bread pudding in its own little cast iron pot was crispy top with fantastic vanilla ice cream. I used to hate bread pudding but I thought I would give it a shot and I love it!

I will definitely come back the next time I am in NOLA and have a good time.

Stopped in for a quick, late-night bite while staying at the hotel. Some ups and downs made for a subpar finish. 

First, the bartenders and servers were outwardly miserable - it was a Tuesday night around 10p and two different employees told us that they were overworked and understaffed. One was very vocal about it - not being allowed time to eat or even go to the bathroom. 

Second, my fiancé got the chocolate bourbon pecan tart ($8) and said it's one of the best desserts he's ever had. 

Third, my cup of gumbo ($10) was decent - thick, rich, seafood-filled. Enjoyable, until I hit the oyster shell shards at the bottom. My bartender didn't really care when I told her, and didn't even mention it to a manager (that I could tell or was made aware of) to make sure the problem was fixed. 

Overall, not a place I would return to. Overpriced and underserved for the experience.

This is the only place I get my oil changed and for good reason. I've never had to wait, and even though I always get my tires rotated and maybe a fluid flush, it's never been longer than 40 minutes start to finish. They give you as many good deals as they can and are always as polite and professional as possible. Despite being a woman and knowing how to change the oil in my truck, I'll always go to Jerry and the JL team at this location. Go see them! You won't be sorry!

I don't understand the big deal.  Told 45 minute wait on a weekday at 4. My friend made a reservation thru Yelp after we walked in and that got us seated in 20 minutes. None of us liked the half price specialty drinks. The Brussels sprouts were tasty as were the fried oysters, but honestly we had better at cheaper restaurants.

In the era of "ethical eating", where "food is politics", I feel like I should announce my love of Luke while hiding my identity.  For those unaware, Luke is one of the restaurants in the John Besh empire and this empire was reported, in a 2017 article in the Times-Picayune, to "foster a culture of sexual harassment".

I assume that the problems reported have been addressed by now, 2019, and don't wish to perpetually punish the restaurant, its workers, or the general public by simply pretending that Luke doesn't exist.  

Luke exists and has an amazingly satisfying happy hour.

Served in a sparkly atmosphere with a buzzy vibe, Luke was my favorite happy hour experience in NOLA.  One dozen fried oysters ($15), 3 dozen raw oysters ($27: 75 cents apiece), Jalapeño Grits ($5), Crispy Potatoes ($5), Crawfish Bisque (bowl $10), and Bread Pudding ($9), there was nothing not to adore here.  Did it help that the Champagne was half off during happy hour as well?  At $4.50 per glass, you can bet that added to the joy.  

Luke's happy hour (4-6 daily) is popular.  Arriving a bit past 4 p.m. I waited for a seat until 5 p.m., when more tables were opened up.  The wait is worth it:  75 cent Gulf Oysters and 1/2 price alcohol are worth waiting for.

I love a happening atmosphere in a busy, buzzy place with decor that makes me feel special.  Luke has all that and good deals to match.
We had the lamb dish and the shrimp and grits which were both served piping hot. Our server was pleasnt but very busy!
This place is a must for anyone visiting New Orleans. They  have the best Cheesy Shrimp and Grits in New Orleans!

I like this place because of the service and the shrimp and grits. I have never had it before and it was delicious. I'm from California so grits was surprisingly like mash potatoes. Not your boxed grits. What drove me here was the well made drink French 73 which I was unimpressed with. The salad with beets was just that. Beautiful old school NOLA building. The maître d' didn't keep me waiting more than 7 mins. Have patience  and enjoy!
Good place for group meal or family gathering!! Fresh seafood!!

Great bar with good food and excellent service. Stopped by during New year's time because we were staying in the area. Bar was packed and bartender was working with a smile and great attitude! A guy got drunk and caused a scene and tried to loud talk the bartender. He shut that down quickly and then poured the rest of us shots for our inconvenience of listening to the drunk! Great staff and excellent customer service! We will definitely be back next time we are in town!

Came here for brunch on a Sunday right before a flight out of New Orleans, and it was a great choice for last meal on our trip. We got the Lüke breakfast and the chicken and waffles, and everything was delicious. Service was great, and the atmosphere is awesome. For a place so packed, it didn't feel claustrophobic at all. Easily one of the best dining experiences we had this weekend, especially since a few other oft-suggested favorites disappointed. I don't know when I'll be back to nola, but I'm definitely putting Lüke on the itinerary when I do.
they have an oyster happy hour and its so good and so cheap! nice place and very nice staff!

Excellent restaurant convenient for downtown hotel dwellers. My wife and I stayed in the hotel across the street and were largely room-bound at night due to our infant son. We ordered food from Luke to-go and were very impressed: fresh, creative, and (important for take-out) timely and hot. One of the best meals we had in NOLA this trip!
Great restaurant. I went during a business trip. Staff was friendly, service was fast, and food was fantastic.

3-6PM Happy Hour with .75 oysters and half price drinks/wine is a great deal. AND they take reservations for Happy Hour - we didn't know, but our nice hostess found a table for us. Very nice. (they do have mignonette sauce - but have to ask , and it's just ok)

Went for Sunday brunch.  Couldn't decide on what to eat so we ordered a little of everything to share.  Fried chicken and waffles were amazing.  Could 't get enough. Waitress was terrific.  Seated right away.  Pricy but worth it.

Drove up from Allentown for my first ever sushi experience. I ordered the Romantic Roll and absolutely loved it. Very clean, fresh and flavorful. My partner (established sushi lover) ordered the D&B Roll and was pleasantly surprised.
My new go to take out place.  Food is great, prices are reasonable.  And you can grab a $2 All Day Everyday High Life at the bar while you're waiting.  How can you beat that?

What a warm embrace of a send off on our last day in NoLa! I had brunch for a couple of relaxing hours here before our flight out and it was quite pleasant! All dishes from cheesy sandwich goodness and hearty NOla stews to the delectable bread dessert filled my insides with warm and comfy feelings of a grandma's love! I do advise to get dessert even if you are full to the brim and add poached eggs to the shrimp and grits dish! The servers were friendly and the interior decor was unique with a touch of modern simplicity. If you come during a popular time, do make reservations in advance!
The bartenders are all fantastic! We visited several other bars in the area but, always ended up back in this pleasant pub with a neighborhood feel.
Excellent Shrimp and Grits!  Nice, relaxed, clean atmosphere and good, quick service.  Will definitely try again next time I'm on NOLA.  Saw many people eating burgers that also looked amazing!

Only have been once as its impossible to get in for the oyster happy hour. Like seriously, don't  expect to get in.

Great French brasserie menu and an amazing burger. Attentive staff.

The service was terrible. The waiter brought our food and never came back to check in us. The oysters were terrible. They were not shucked to order. We told the waiter and he said that happens when it's busy. We told the manager who apologized and took them off our bill. I will never eat there again!

This place was amazing! We had it on Thursday night and we were seated rather quickly which was great! We took a recommendation from here about the shrimp and grits and it was THE BEST! My husband and I both had it and we loved every bite! Price is pretty high for the amount of food you get but MAN it was worth it! I also recommend their delicious bread pudding! Perfect dinner for our first night in new
Delicious oysters, excellent shrimp gumbo, good service.  Overall great dining experience!  Will be back again!

Luke is a no-lose kind of restaurant.  The menu has a variety of options so that your vegetarian, seafoodie, and meatlover friends can all enjoy a great meal. The atmosphere is nice but casual.  You can play it up to be a nice date, or dress it down to a jeans and blouse brunch.  

No Budweisers or Miller Lites here, the beers are brewed at the restaurant, which I think is a nice distinction from other NOLA restaurants.  Our waiter was very accommodating and brought us sampler glasses of beers for us to choose from.

I love this wine list, mostly because there are 2 Gamay options (a beuajolais, lighter and tarter than a pinot noir).  The list is extensive and the prices range from affordable to business-expense only.  The many options reflect the diverse menu.

I have eaten at Luke a few times and have never been disappointed.  I appreciate that all John Besh restaurants use local purveyors, so you know your food is fresh and helping Louisiana farmers and fisherman.  The poulet was the most perfectly cooked chicken I have ever had.  The crab bisque was not too heavy to enjoy the rest of my meal.  Oysters served on the half-shell are always a safe bet.  The shrimp and grits was good, but I would have liked a bigger portion with more of the stew.  The pork sandwich was probably the only mediocre dish I had.

My only wish is that, like other NOLA restaurants, the weekday lunch menu would be offered during brunch. Otherwise, Luke is consistently a palette and appetite pleaser that won't break the bank.
Excellent Louisiana cooking presented in an upscale way.  I have the smoked pork shank and it was melt in your mouth great.  A little loud inside but still a very nice place for dinner

I'm always pleased with the quality of work from Cook's. They have completed several projects for me, never disappointed. I recently had a piece of glass cut down for a frame. As always, it was perfect.  Typically, they can turn around a project in about a week.

I found them when I lived on the Westside (Avon), but now that I live in Greenwood, I still make the drive.

They also have a cat in the office. What's not to love about that? 

Show small businesses some love. Give them a try!

I went with three others for a business dinner. It is a small place so reservations are recommended -- walk-ups are acceptable but don't count on it and the bar does not have that many seats. The food is pretty good. My colleagues ordered the Lukeburger, the special pork loin (lots of food) and the breaded lamb. I had the shrimp & grits -- the house favorite. It is not overly filling which allows you to have a cup of soup or dinner salad and a dessert (I had the bread pudding and it was great). The tables are small (good for two, not for four). The service was a bit slow -- took us a while to get our bread and desserts. Bottom-line, a good place to dine.

My husband and I were super excited to try this place out as we've heard amazing things about the company, and had high hopes that this tiny little shop would become a new regular for us. Given that it is a extremely small shop, and they are very busy (especially on a beautiful sunny saturday morning), and that they can only make one or two drinks at a time, we were still slightly disappointed. We waited nearly 15 minutes for our cappuccinos and a scone, one of the coffees came out barely warm while the other was decently hot. Needless to say, I was super disappointed with my cold coffee, but didn't want to complain because of how busy it was. We will have to give this place another try and hopefully it will change my opinion of it. We have yet to go to district, but have heard nothing but good things so I think I was expecting a little more. Loved the little patio out front if you're lucky enough to get a table! Ham & cheese scone was huge and yummy!

This is my favorite go-to sushi place in the Wilmington area. Good , delicious , clean sushi... They don't have a wide variety. Then again they are a small little place so it is to be expected. Have been buying here for years . Always good customer service . If you want fair priced good sushi , take a quick stop. You'll be in and out.

A quick trip to NOLA means going to a John Besh restaurant, right?  Yessireee!  

Went between lunch and dinner on a Friday so we got really great, personal service and didn't feel rushed.  Started with oysters (mmmhmmm) then gumbo (sweet elixer) then moules et frites for me and shrimp and grits for FB.  I totally ended up with entree envy.  The moules were great, but poorly chosen, you can get good mussels anywhere.  The shrimp and crab and grits and sauce were heavenly and quite possibly the highlight of the entire trip.

Nice, classy casual atmosphere, as the site describes.  The perfect way to spend a hot afternoon in NOLA.

On my last day in New Orleans I decided to try this place. It is more of a upscale joint with a lot of business people come for lunch. I want to start out by saying the bartender, I forgot her name, was the beat service I have ever received. She knew all the ingredients of the dishes, what paired well, was very attentive, and all around great. I cannot stress that enough. We had a couple drinks to start out with. The cognac drink was very smooth and I'm not even a cognac drinker. 

We started off with a couple appetizers including the fries quail and the rabbit liver dish. The fries quail was cooked perfectly with a light crispy breeding which wasn't over seasoned or over prepared. It came with a couple sliced peppers I believe which added just the right zest. The rabbit liver dish was very busy. The liver spread was served in a small mason jar. The dish had various spreads such as marmalade, gritty mustard, apple spread. It was served with thin pieces of bread which could be used to put all the spreads on. If you are not fond of liver you probably won't like it. 

For an entree I had the sausage and shrimp dish with grits and Cajun spice. I forgot the exact name of the dish but they split it between me and my gf  on two separate cast iron skillets. 

The food was phenomenal and the service was even better. If I'm back in the area, I will be stopping in.

Just checked in at Luke's, apparently they can't combine two 2 seater  tables for a Grp of three because the restaurant closes at 11 and last call for food is 10:30....

Food is important and so, is the customer and when it's almost restaurant closing time, you can always do a lil more coz the crowd flowing in is less...

Nice atmosphere here.  Better lit and with a nicer indoor environment than Mr. B's Bistro around the corner.  The raw oysters here were huge and delicious.  I had the rotisserie chicken plate and was given a massive portion of tasty, juicy chicken.  They brine their chicken to give it more flavor and you can tell in the final product.  It was served with mashed potatoes and some kind of green vegetable, both of which were tasty.  

The food here isn't exactly "traditional" New Orleans, but they make some nice stuff and their spin on classic dishes tends to be good.  A friend ordered the gumbo and said it was one of the best he'd had on this trip.  Check it out for something delicious and out of the ordinary for NOLA.

75-cent oyster happy hour special 3-6pm! Couldn't find any places in the French Quarter to get a good deal on oysters so made the trek across Canal St to come here. It was totally worth it.  Upscale but casual spot. It super packed for happy hour but we were seated pretty quickly even with a party of 5. Also, great service.

We ordered a ton of oysters, the crawfish bisque, fries and a side of truffle butter (I didn't even know that was something you could actually order but now I want it always). I'd recommend them all.
Highly recommend their fried oyster salad! The shrimp and sausage was satisfying too!

We had reservations for New Years Eve. Dinner and service were amazing. Shrimp and grits are amazing, the grits are the best I've ever had, they cant be beat. My favorite was also the baked oysters. Delicious! I've also gone for happy hour which is such a deal. They shucked our oysters right in front of us and were so nice and welcoming. This is definitely my favorite restaurant in NOLA.

We found the place only because of Yelp and even walked right past it -- it's not exactly obvious. But well worth the hunt! The entrecôte grillé & frites was fabulous.  The wait staff was very friendly and they didn't blink when we split the steak (14oz!!). They even pre-split the meal for us (always major points for us meal-splitters). We highly recommend Lüke.

are you kidding me luke's knocks it out of the park best food ever drop  mic ! this is where yelp makes me type more words in order to post a review so how about this ......... greatnesssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssss

Had lunch with my grown daughters, couldn't have been happier! We were a bit rushed, a flight looming, and the waiter made sure we were served quickly, and was attentive throughout, even brought our bill quickly without our having to ask. We shared appetizers, the crawfish hush puppies, Brussels sprouts, fried quail and a beet salad. All were delicious, but we also managed to pack down a shared bread pudding, excellent!
Ingredients in everything were fresh, sauces were nuanced and textures perfect throughout. This place stands out in a food city, highly recommend!

I believe that the other reviews are very outdated.  First off, you can't smoke in there anymore.  We just moved to Glenside, and we love ordering pizza from there.  Best that we've found so far, and the price is great....2 large pizzas for $14.  Waiter service is always nice and efficient.  I've been there for hockey games, etc., and there are plenty of tvs.  I like the bartenders, and one of them even bought me a drink on my birthday!  My cousins frequent Jerzee's quite a bit, so that's how we got turned on to it, and I'm glad we did!  I'm "friends" with them on facebook now, and they seem to have really good specials every day.  We'll have to go check out some of their weekday specials, especially since my house is too freakin hot to cook in!

I wanted to explore one of New Orleans' upscale restaurants for a snack and a drink to mark the end of my time in town. I love trying out places that may not be in my regular budget by going during happy hour. After doing some research, I chose Luke on the recommendation of my good friend and local host.

Part of the John Besh (now BRG) culinary empire, Luke is an old-school brasserie in the CBD. It's classic interior with white tile, loads of dark wood, and servers in white, buttoned jackets reminds you of historic New Orleans. I wandered in a little before 5 pm and sat at the crowded bar. With $.75 raw oysters and drink specials, Luke's happy hour is popular with folks in town and tourists. 

Knowing I'd be having dinner later, I limited myself to a half dozen of fresh bivalves and a Stigel Radler. The oysters were large and very fresh. Luke serves them with lemon, cocktail sauce, and crackers. I'd have preferred mignonette, but no one's getting picky over sauces at this price point. The bar staff was prompt and courteous, but the large TVs showing football recaps did detract from my overall experience. They seemed out of place in this restaurant. If you love oysters and want to ry out one of NOLA's celebrated restaurants, check out Luke and it's fantastic happy hour.

Their food is usually prepared well. The restaurant is usually clean. But too often i come in and they are out of stuff. I like to use the kiosk when I come in and tonight after I placed my order, I was told they were out of the bread I had ordered for my sandwich. No big deal I just had them keep the bread it came on. Then when they brought my order, they were out of the side item I requested, so they gave me half of a baguette (literally) and, without asking, they upgraded my cup of soup to a bowl. I appreciate the gesture. However, bringing me a ridiculously large bowl of soup and half a loaf of bread is overkill. I would have preferred my soup remained a cup and given a choice of the other side options available. I will not and did not eat even 1/3 of the soup and didn't touch the bread because I don't particularly care for it.
Ate here twice while n NOLA...loved it both timesi

My husband and I had a great dining experience here. The place is wonderful, the service is excellent, and the food is fantastic. Every single item that we ordered was really good and flavorful. This was the first restaurant in New Orleans that my husband and I checked out on our vacation. I would say, if you are visiting New Orleans for the first time, this should be your last stop on your trip as this is such a great place for a last meal. Since this was our first meal in New Orleans, it definitely raised the bar super high, other restaurants were great but this one has to be our favorite.

Orders:
Crawfish Bique
Pate of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken Livers
Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cotte"

Food is amazing but I mostly come here for their French 75 drink that I adore. Seating is comfortable but tight quarters. Reservations probably best. Accidentally found this place because staying at hotel nearby. A nice atmosphere as compared to the rough and tumble of Bourbon St.

First we sat at the bar and enjoyed terrific cocktails- including an excellent Sazerac and old fashioned with a rich selection of bourbons. The bartenderers were knowledgeable and welcoming......Then we enjoyed dinner.  I had the salad with fried oysters, and the caesar dressing was perfect! My husband had the boudin noir sausage, and it was extremely flavorful. Then I had a plate of gulf oysters.  My husband had the croque madame with nice bread and excellent ham.  The food used very high quality ingredients, and I loved the atmosphere.

The desserts were good, and the service was nice, though a bit slow.
Great ambiance and awesome food... What more do you want!!!??? Every bite of this restaurants food is something to savor.

Went here on a friend's suggestion for happy hour. Went for the happy hour oysters. The oysters were 75 cents each. They just tasted okay. I wouldn't come back again because I'd rather pay more for better tasting oysters. Also got the brussel sprouts. Those were really good but after a while the sauce they have on them started to taste too sweet.  Didn't get to try any of the other food.

Nice restaurant, very affable waiters and staff always attentive to our needs. Tried the duck and chicken paté which was very good and for main entrée had the sword fish which was fresh and well prepared. I was offered a pea puree instead of the eggplant puree, which was a very good recommendation. I'm taking one star because the desserts were less than spectacular. Tried the bred pudding with vanilla ice and was tasteless in our view, which we mentioned to the manager. He was very receptive of our comments. Would strongly recommend visiting while in NOLA.

I have been to Luke many times for breakfast and thought it was so great.  Took my sisters out tonight for dinner and it was an embarrassment!

Service was not good.  No review of the menu, no offering of specials.
My ribeye was 80% fat and cold, as were my potatoes.  Im not happy and wont return.  

If you eat there, go for breakfast.  Dinner was terrible.

Extensive menu.   Lovely service.   My dining companion and I were very impressed up until we were asked to leave shortly after finishing our meal because they "needed" the table on Tuesday night...my review would have been higher if our evening hadn't been cut short.

Okay I am just going to go ahead and say it...  

I wasn't very impressed.

My boyfriends burger was dry and I mean DRY.  Besides that though everything was quite good, but really nothing so out of this world.  I had the mussels which were delicious.  My cocktail was tasty.  I would go back but I have other nice restaurants I would want to try before that.
We went here yesterday for Happy Hour 3-6 and had the fried and raw oysters. They were both very delicious. The drinks, Frenchman 75 in particular was fabulous.

We  have been getting takeout from here for so many years, the owner recognizes our voices on the phone.  We have tried many Chinese places in Tampa and this is most like what I grew up with up North. The food is always reliable, tasty, and they have great spare ribs!! On occasion, the food is a bit too greasy but worth the calories. A staple for us!!!
Great food, awesome service and nice atmosphere. One of our best experiences in New Orleans and the best food hands down!

Ambience and decor is wonderful. Service was excellent. Gary- our server was so nice and served well, and Ronald- the manager valued my feedback. his suggestions for things to do turned out to be great. 
The food was terrific! Oysters were fresh and really good. The pate is not to be missed. It had the perfect consistency, was served at the right temperature and the relishes served alongside were so creative and complimented the pate.
Our drinks were very nice as well- the French 75 and door#3.

So begins our New Orleans vacation and boy did we come out of the gates swinging.  We landed around 6:30 am, checked in at the hotel and went straight for food. 

What should I eat at 7:45 am?  You guys have a burger? I'll take it!  Man was this a burger. Brought out on a cutting board alongside a cup of crispy seasoned fries, this burger blew me away. 

The patty practically melted away and barely stuck together. Inside it was topped with a fat slice of cheese, huge and juicy tomato, semi-crispy bacon (just the way I like) and deliciously sweet grilled onions. 

Without expecting it, I think I found a rival to the Father's Office burger. 

The girl went for a more traditional breakfast item and ordered the Grillades and Grits. Yeah, they were pretty good, but I couldn't waste more than a bite because I had that huge burger to work on.

On our trip to NOLA, my husband & I used Yelp to help us pick places for dinner. (John Besh is apparently some sort of restaurant god in NOLA.) We were seated in the rear of the first floor of the restaurant (another seating room up a few stairs in the back). The restaurant appears to share restrooms w/ the lobby of the Hilton Hotel--from the previous reviews, I had no idea that it was connected to a hotel.

Oddly, the hostess sat us at a two top right next to another two top instead of at a 3rd two top farthest away from the other seated couple. It became even odder when we realized that the couple was involved in the most private & devastating conversation that they will probably ever have. When we arrived, they were at the point where the wife was asking the husband where he had been meeting the woman w/ whom he was having an affair--at their home, a hotel or somewhere else. She then asked whether the other woman was going to get a divorce & if that was her husband's plan as well. Why he hadn't left her & their 3 kids last year & when he had become such a good liar. Smartly, the husband kept his answers polite & vague. He didn't have a plan, he didn't know why he hadn't broken up w/ his wife, he wasn't sure how long it would take them to figure out if they were getting a divorce or not.  

Needless to say, my husband & I were shocked when we realized what was going on two feet from us. To our further horror, the waiter kept reminding them that there was no rush! I wanted to yell, "Do you know WTF they are talking about?  Don't you want them to leave?" I guess all the experts say you should have this kind of conversation in a public place because it encourages some restraint from yelling & getting violent, but don't tell that to my husband & I when we're just trying to have a good meal on vacation. They eventually left & were replaced by a gay couple who ended up asking to switch seats because it was too cold at that table. Cold is right. Cold from the cheating vibes lingering.  

We managed to order drinks (beer & nice, but small, Chardonnay) & put in for appetizers. I thoroughly enjoyed the Luke Salad despite the odd platting--the whole leaves of Bibb lettuce were lightly dressed w/ the Buttermilk dressing, but the cubes of cucumber tossed in dill w/ carrot slivers & pieces of pickled beets were served underneath the lettuce. I could see the beets peering out, but I almost forgot about the other accoutrements. I know that Bibb lettuce is fragile, but I would have preferred the salad tossed or topped w/ the other bits or if the plate was larger so everything could be visible. In any case, it was a tasty salad. My husband had a cup of the crab bisque, which was too crabby for me. He enjoyed it, though to be a bisque, it should have been a touch thicker or creamier.  

For entrees, my husband had the crab ravioli which he liked. I had the "cassoulet" w/ duck confit & pork sausage. Since it's cassoulet, I imagined the pork would be stewed in w/ the white beans & vegetables & there might be small piece of duck confit. Well, boy was I wrong. It came out in a 9"cast iron dish mouth-searing hot. The duck was not small, but a WHOLE LEG; the sausage was not stewed in, but a whole German-style long BRAT laying on the side of the dish. To finish it off, there was PORK BELLY about 1"2 on top. It smelled delicious & I smartly enjoyed the aroma while it cooled down. When I stuck my fork in, I found a scarcity of white beans & mostly breadcrumbs cooked, get this, in small pieces of PORK FAT. To recap:"cassoulet"=2 large pieces of fatty meat+1 small piece of fatty meat+bread crumbs+a few white beans+more meat fat. My husband found this kind of amusing since I am an advocate of eating meat fat since it's super tasty (Bourdain=proud of me), but this has got to have been the most decadent, over the top, ridiculous cassoulet ever served (Bourdain would not have approved).  

I tasted a bit of each component before I called it quits. The server, to his credit, asked me twice if it was not to my liking to which I honestly responded, it's just "so rich." I'm just not the type to send things back & make a fuss, but the dish should have been a 1/5 of the size & an appetizer NOT called "cassoulet." It's not that the description on the menu was completely inaccurate, I guess...personally, I think the server should have warned me. It's too bad my husband wasn't feeling well & that we don't love oysters (since they have a raw bar) because I think we would have tried to salvage my meal w/ dessert or seafood or cheese/spread plate.   

The menu at Luke is not all over the top like this though we heard the server explain that there is an off the menu vegetarian plate because literally there were NO veggie entrees on the menu which is to be expected at a French/German restaurant, but still. Somehow I think a place that bills itself to be pretty nice could do a more authentic cassoulet & have a French/German/NOLA inspired veggie dish.

A dinner with friends--special people is always an event.  We arrived ready for the P&J oyster specials.  The raw oysters, and grilled versions were wonderful.  The right mixture of lemon, horseradish, and cocktail sauce is my standard.  The restaurant has a beautiful, New World atmosphere.  I had a light early dinner that included the seafood gumbo.  It is hard to find bad gumbo in New Orleans, but this was particularly outstanding.  I have to find a way back to the Big Easy to try some other dishes at this popular New Orleans restaurant!  I miss New Orleans already!
Great food, fun atmosphere. Def recommended!

Wow, finally a great meal in NOLA!  We've suffered through a few lackluster meals in New Orleans, but this certainly wasn't one of them.  We had the Small Seafood Platter, Shrimp and Grits, and a bowl of Gumbo and everything was spot on.  We liked it so much we are headed back for Happy Hour tomorrow.  Our wait staff was excellent and very attentive and the ambiance was good as well.  No complaints from the couple who "lives to travel and travels to eat."

We have a rental house and on the 24th of December we got a text from our tenants that the heat was out. We scrambled to get our usual plumbers who first serviced this boiler.... were out on vacation... then went to anyone we could find for a quick visit. A serviceman arrived from Fahrenheit within the hour. We just needed to know what was going on, as this older unit had already been fully serviced and a new aquastat installed just 2 weeks earlier. We asked our tenants to text my husband when he arrived, which they did, and Doug (my husband) was there in 10 minutes. When he arrived he entered the house and chatted for a moment with our tenant, then saw the service guy pop up from the basement... had already given it a good look over.  He went down with the Fahrenheit guy and he tells Doug the boiler needs to be replaced, that the aquastat installed was not working properly with the rest of the controls. And there seemed to be a danger of carbon monoxide leaking from the system.  First quote he gave was for $8500, I was on the phone and we both thought that was quite too much. He offered a coupon and a reduced rate for $7300 to install a new unit. We declined the offer. We have recently installed a new boiler in our townhouse and last month a new furnace in another rental property and never paid even close to that amount. My husband paid the service call fee, and we looked up someone else. Got several space heaters to help out our renters through Christmas. We got another service guy from the company we used to install the furnace at the other property. He came the 26, on time, looked over the boiler and adjusted one small part in the aquastat. Then he noticed something funny, some wire leads to another controller were mixed up, which he switched back into the correct order. Voila! all powered up fine, back to running again, no problem. But this second guy was puzzled, said with all those mixed up wires, it should not have been able to run at all, had someone else checked this out? Yes, my husband said, just two days earlier. Was Doug with him the whole time? The Fahrenheit technician got to our rental first and was alone in the basement for awhile. Hmmmm.... The second service guy did not see any issues warranting immediate replacement, said it had a few years left on it. Said nothing about CO leaks or issues. The moral of the story is, If someone presses you to replace your boiler, get a second opinion.
so good. hidden in a shopping strip but that means there's usually a table open. byo is convenient because there's a liquor store in the same center.

WoW!

Luke is simply one of the best dinning experiences one can have. It's staff is friendly, attentive, knowledgeable and laid back. The food is fresh, new and amazingly good. This place is one for the real foodies who know good food.
Best Shrimp & Grits in the city!  'nuff said. Learned of this restaurant by someone on my flight to NOLA.  The Shrimp & grits is as good as it gets!
I come here on a weekly basis. The food is fresh, delicious and creative.  The staff is friendly; they know me and my family well. I've never had a bad meal! You won't be disappointed.

My food was good, loved the texture and flavor. The Lüke Salad was a bit too salty. My partner's food was a bit on the blend side, the bratwurst was huge but not very flavorful. The Service was great, the atmosphere was awesome also.

I came in here for lunch with my fiancé on 6/11/12, and ordered a melt sandwich. The person preparing the order forgot to take the paper off of the cheese, and when I presented the mistake to them they replaced my sandwich, gave me a refill on my drink, and threw in a cookie to boot. Normally I wouldn't give any chain restaurant anything above three stars, but they went out of their way to rectify their mistake. Additionally, the upstairs seating was a nice little lunch nook for me and my fiancee.

The interior feels like it's part of an old, classic, and fancy hotel. It's small but cozy. The service is nice. There are revolving doors at the entrance but they don't work.

This restaurant focuses solely on food although breakfast is in the category. They don't have anything else beyond coffee and tea, which was fine. 

I ordered the fried chicken biscuit. It was the most expensive $14 biscuit I ever bought. The fried chicken was entirely tasteless. Maybe that's what the honey was for. However, the meal came with a pile of grits that had a subtle salty taste and grainy texture I enjoyed. The biscuits were baked well. Everything but the chicken was great.

Seriously THE BEST happy hour I've ever been to! Service was amazing (shoutout to Desmond and Chi they're awesome!), food was delicious, and drinks were strong. Wasn't too crowded when my boyfriend and I came at 5pm on a weekday evening, but it filled up pretty quickly soon after! You can make a reservation online through their website.

Here's all you need to know about HH. It runs from 3-6pm. PJ raw oysters are 75 cents a piece... comes with cocktail sauce, horseradish, and saltines. The oysters are HUGE and so yummy (we got 3 dozen haha)!! You really get the bang for your buck.

Fried oysters are $1.25 each -- they cost a bit more but it is definitely worth it, trust me! Eat them right away so they don't get cold and soggy!

There's a small menu with 6 cocktails listed -- these options are half off during HH... so that's $5.50 or less per drink. They are well crafted with pretty high liquor content I'd say. The bartender really hooked it up that night!

door#three - A vodka cocktail with pomegranate, mint, and lime. This and the Amor de Fresa were the sweeter options on the menu. They're like mojitos with vodka instead of rum.

Silver Saint - Tequila with cucumber, lime, serrano pepper, and soda. Very dry, but I'd highly recommend this for tequila lovers. This was probably the strongest cocktail of the night.

French 75 - Cognac with lemon and champagne. This was a very interesting drink, and apparently the best one around town is at Luke!! Flavors meshed very well together, very smooth.

Rosemary's Bourbon - Old Forester with rosemary and lemon. The rosemary flavor really stuck out surprisingly, I really liked this one! I guess it was muddled pretty well because flavors like this don't usually stand out when paired with darker liquors in my experience.

We were visiting from out of town, but will definitely be back to Luke next time we're in NOLA! Seriously the quickest, best service I've had anywhere, and the freshest raw oysters I've ever had. Probably my favorite HH spot as well :)

Had breakfast here- not only was the service wonderful (ordered the large breakfast with eggs, grits, biscuit and sausage and they split it for us on two plates) but they also have beignets and a side of warm chocolate for dipping sauce as well as a fruit dipping sauce. Amazing.
Delicious restaurant of the John Besh chain! The food did not dissapoint! The bread pudding is a must!

I cannot say enough good things about Chipotle.  I'm not a huge fan of chains in general (I tend to think they are ugly, unhealthy, and generally bad for the soul), but Chipotle is a huge exception.  It's tasty, healthy, fresh, clean, and eco-friendly.

The menu is very simple, basically you make three decisions:
1. Chicken, beef, or vegetarian
2. Bowl or taco
3. Toppings -  salsas, cheese, sour cream, guac, and lettuce

You can also get a side of chips and guac, and a drink.

We each had a burrito bowl - rice, black beans, chopped tomatoes, guacamole, and lots of lettuce.  About $6 each.  Simple, and very satisfying.  I could literally eat here every day.

I have to give extra props for the service.  Not only was everyone friendly but the guy behind the counter, seeing that my wrist was bandaged up, offered to carry my lunch to my table for me.

This is my third time at Luke. Not a great experience this time due to careless service. He didn't write down my orders. We had to ask for services from other random servers. 

Crawfish bisque 
Matzo Ball & Roast Chicken Soup (not my fav)
Blue Crab 
1/2 Dozen of Louisiana Shrimp cocktail
Fried oyster salad (not my fav)
Chicken tender and French Fried
Apple juice( didn't make it for this table)
Pâté of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken Livers (didn't make to the table)

Awesome food and service. By myself visiting for business, sat at the bar. The bartenders made me feel so welcome. Wine by the glass selection was fabulous. Went back the next morning for breakfast. Best shrimp and grits I've ever had.

This restaurant was recommended by a local, so I had high hopes. It did not disappoint! our servers were excellent, and great at making suggestions on what to try. All of the recommendations turned out to be on point. The crab dip was very good! The wine was reasonably priced and our w tress were excellent. The shrimp and grits, were the best I've ever had anywhere and living in the South that's saying a lot!

The oysters and alligator dishes are amazing, the service was really good, compared to other places in town a little more pricey and usual but still worth it, the 75 drink is really good and the desserts are absolutely amazing.

Went here with a few friends (4 of us) the week before Mardi Gras. It was a Wednesday night around 6:30 I think. We didn't have a reservation, and they said it might take 45 minutes-but they called me to say the table was ready in less than 30. 
We all ordered different cocktails, and were all pleased with how yummy, complex, and balanced they were. For food we shared the Louisiana rabbit and chicken liver pate--which was rich and smooth and came with a platter of different pickles and sauces to pair with on crostini. I was afraid it might not come with much pate, but there was almost too much for the four of us to finish! When we asked for more crostini they brought out a full plate of it. More than we needed, but I'd prefer that over too little. 
For my entree I got the shrimp and grits. The grits were creamy and smothered with cheese, the shrimp was cooked perfectly with a soft flaky texture (I think it may have been some of the best prepared shrimp I've ever had actually), and came with sausage and a sauce with creole/Cajun spices that had a rich warm flavor without being too spicy or overwhelming the other components to the dish. I was very, very impressed. It was definitely worth the $24 price tag for the entree. 
Our server was nice, although didn't refill my water as often as I would have liked (I drink a lot of water). But I have no complaints. A manager also stopped by our table to see how our meals were, which I appreciate seeing in restaurants. 
I'd return to Lüke for sure next time I'm in New Orleans! But next time I would probably make a reservation.

Soft Shell Crab BLT. Amazing tastes and flavor combinations and incredibly beautiful presentation. This restaurant never disappoints and is consistently amazing. Waitstaff are attentive but not suffocating. Perfection.

We were so excited to eat here that we made a reservation over a month in advance for Christmas day so that we could take part in the special Revillion menu. What a dissappoint. The food was bland/ under seasoned and cold. Over $300 for cold food? You must be joking. We sent it back and when it returned it was better, but still not hot. Hey "chef" maybe if you weren't reheating day old prep... Just a thought from someone with a clue. Wine parings showed up after the food and were dropped at the table by dissappearing waiters with no explanation of varietal, region or vintage (yeah we asked to back track and find out what we were drinking, but should we have to?) We told the manager how terribly dissappointed we were with our entire experience, and oh hey SURPRISE she didn't care. Do not eat here. Seriously, anywhere else is better then this garbage on a plate.
Hands down the best meal I've had in New Orleans. Our waiter was hilarious, the service was impeccable, and the food was to die for. We'll definitely be back.

Excellent food & phenomenal service! Special S/O to Rich Whatley "Richie Rich" who kept us entertained with his humor; He had the BEST dining room awareness EVER! We are definitely coming back to Luke's whenever we are back in NOLA. Five star rating, hands down!

Found one of my new favorite lunch places near work that's healthy. On top of it found my new favorite sandwich! The Chipotle chicken avacado melt is amazing, it's spicy and crunch and warm and the avacado and melted cheese give it a gooey feel good element. Pair that with their french onion soup and you have yourself a lunch that almost feels like mom made it for you while you are staying home sick from school. Awesome comfort food at a reasonable price.  Not to mention their goodies like cookies and brownies for desert. Cant loose

I wanted to try out a John Besh restaurant but didn't want to blow the budget on August, so this was a great compromise.

Casual vibe in the Hilton hotel and hubby and I got a great laugh since the waiters all look like little med students running around in their short white coats with pens in their pockets!

Service here is excellent and attentive.  Prices are very reasonable.  We missed happy hour unfortunately but had an early dinner.  Their quick pre-selected 3-course dinners are an amazing value at about $23 each.  Loved my crawfish soup to start!  My main was the redfish bouillon that was OK but not memorable now that I'm back home.  Enjoyed the creme brulee.

Hubby had a salad and burger a la carte - very good.  Fries are thin and fresh.

It's in the central business district so it's a bit quieter than other parts of the city.  Overall great value and excellent service.

Went here last night with my husband for the first time because we just wanted something simple for dinner. Starting off when you walk in you notice it is very clean with a nice slightly modern aesthetic. You have the option to either order at the counter or they have touch screens where you can order and grab a pager and they will bring it to your table. We went with the touch screen kiosks and it was pretty easy to order from. We figured it would just be easier because we didn't know what we wanted and weren't to familiar with Panera's options. I ordered the you pick two with a Ham and Swiss sandwich and a side of mac and cheese, my husband also did the pick two but he got a Chicken Panini  and mac and cheese.  Honestly the food is good, and everything looked really fresh on the sandwich. It almost looked like something you would get at a higher end deli or cafe. On top of getting your sandwich and mac and cheese you also get a piece of bread, kind of similar to a baquette. Panera is a good place if you are looking for a healthier option for fast food, they offer sandwiches, soups, and pretty nice looking salads too. The only real reason I gave it 4 instead of 5 stars was that they are more expensive. For two you pick two's and 2 regular drinks, plus tax it was a little over $27. They are also a little selective on free add on's for the sandwiches and a decent amount of add on's cost extra. Over all I would recommend but do plan on paying a little more than you would at other sandwich places.

I can't get over how much I love this place! The staff is always making sure to greet everyone and they have actually started catching on to what I order (which is the same thing pretty much each time)! I always enjoy coming to this specific location just because I know how friendly they are and also they give out good portions!
Great food great environment， highly recommend！！！Seafood is so fresh and well seasoned. Better than most of the well-known restaurants that tourists will go to in French Quarter.

In this traditionally Catholic town, one problem confronting the out-of-town visitor can be where to eat on a Sunday night, when many restaurants are closed.  Fortunately Lüke is OPEN!

As most people already know, this is a part of John Besh Empire -- uh, sorry, John Besh Restaurant Group -- this, said to be Alsatian influenced.  As with every dining experience I've ever had at one of his restaurants, the meal was SUPERB!

For appetizers, I started out with the pâté of Louisiana rabbit and duck livers, scented with truffle and served with Dijon mustard, caramelized sweet onions, pickled watermelon and housemade croutons -- a surprisingly large portion, and positively wonderful.  Meanwhile, Lynn had the Badischer presskopf (hog's head cheese) -- about twice the amount she expected appeared on the plate, and it just may have been twice as good, too!

We each opted for the salad of chicory, lardons of Allen Benton's bacon, croutons and a soft poached yard egg, with creole mustard and tarragon -- excellent -- while Amy selected the fried oyster, bacon, romaine and avocado salad (her Tennessee roots blending with her time in California:  fried food and avocado: what could be better?) that was as good as it gets.

For our mains, I chose the moules et frites (Prince Edward Island mussels steamed with garlic and thyme with housemade fries) for $18.  I mention the price, because -- can I just ask:  who serves FIVE DOZEN MUSSELS???  After ploughing my way through 36 of these excellent and tasty little morsels, I waved the white flag of surrender, and apologized for the poor 24 that were sacrificed needlessly . . . .

Lynn had the Louisiana redfish with a sauce meunière -- and instead of one fillet, she received two . . . perfectly delicious, yet she, too, failed to finish the second one.

Amy, feeling smug that she skipped the appetizer course ("What were y'all thinking?"), chose the Lüke burger -- served with tomatoes, Allen Benton's bacon, caramelized onions, and Emmenthaler cheese with housemade fries -- yet she, too, could only make it halfway through . . . .

So the lesson at Lüke is to only order ONE thing!  Well, maybe not, but you gotta save room for the bread pudding -- the best I've had in NOLA since 1970!  Honest . . . .

We came here on a Friday 08/10/2018.
  It's a small place so you are lucky if you are seated within 30 minutes, then you are lucky. 
  Good food, courteous servers with positive attitude.
  Especially liked dessert.
  Thank you Kevin for serving us. 
   Must go place when you head here 
 Just a question from an observer: "is there a symbolic representation for the wall blocks being all at 3 o'clock the whole time.

This was the restaurant across the street from my hotel and I walked by every night to see if I could get a seat at the bar for dinner.  Alas, it was packed every time!  The day of my flight out though, I manage to sneak in for lunch and wasn't disappointed!

I got the lunch special, which comes with the entree for the day and a cup of soup.  I also got a sazerac since I had to get at least one in before leaving town.

The sazerac was great, but note that I'm not a connoisseur of whiskey drinks in general.  For the soup I chose the crab and corn bisque and I'M SO GLAD I DID.  So creamy, flavorful, delicious and... well, crab-y.  I'm sure their gumbo would have been delicious too, but I'd already had my fair share on this trip.

Sadly the entree was just ok for me.  It was the spicy lamb meatball and pasta for that day, and it was a bit bland overall.  The meatballs were tasty and juicy, but I didn't get much heat.

I'd come back though definitely!  Hoping to try more of their cocktails and beer next time around!

You can literally find oyster bars anywhere in NOLA. And Luke stands out for a reason. A friend of mine recommended this place to me. And I came here on my last day at NOLA, just to check out how good the its oysters could be. 

In addition to the local P&J oysters, Luke also had several other options to choose from. I ordered half dozen of P&J, as well as half dozen of Beausoliel, with recommendation from the oyster shucker. If you come by yourself, I would highly recommend you sitting at the bar. It was such a piece of art to look at. 

The P&J and Beausoliel were so different in their sizes. P&J was giant and looked fatty, just liked the ones I had tried at other oyster bars at NOLA, only fresher and tasted better. 

As for the Beausoliel... oh my they were truly amazing! Upon first look, they may seemed shriveled, especially when putting right next to P&J.  But when I slurped down the whole thing chewed it, I instantly got to understand why it was highly praised by the shucker. It was so refined and light, giving me a nearly sweet and crisp flavor... just everything I could ask for. 

Oh and did I mention they had happy hours from 3-6? Definitely go and take advantage of the 75 cents oysters!

Came here just for the happy hour oysters and drinks! Our waitress was Savannah. As soon as she walked over to our table I already knew we were going to get along quite well. The girl was decked out in Batman themed hair clips and tie! She was super nice and attentive - great employee. The oysters were $0.75 each and so fresh! We got two dozen ($18). Fried oysters were half off too ($7.50). Good amount to share between two people. For drinks I would recommend the Buffalo Negra. Don't let the vinegar sway you away!

I recently went back for the lunch special it was $6.25 for chicken and broccoli with fried rice and a can soda. Food was good. I still waited a bit longer than expected but take into consideration I was on my lunch break.

This is the best Chinese food I have ever had. We ate on the inside and the place is clean and comfortable. The wait was about 10 mins from the time we ordered. We came around 2pm on a Thursday. My husband and I ordered the lunch special General Tso Chicken, Chicken Lo Mein, and one pizza roll and one cheesesteak roll. Both the pizza roll and the cheesesteak roll didn't have any meat in it, which disappointed us. Probably wouldn't ordered it again. The General Tso Chicken and Chicken Lo Mein were phenomenal. I didn't expect the Chicken Lo Mein to have fried Rice in it too which was a plus. I don't like spicy foods too much, but I tried my husbands General Tso Chicken and it was not too spicy. I would order it another time I go, because I know I will be back again and again! The food just tasted so clean, not all extra greasy and suspect like regular Chinese food. Probably because this place is halal and I love that. There was a black girl working there whose attitude was a lily toe stank. It didn't affect our experience. I'm just saying because Chinese lady that was taking orders as well was very nice. Overall, I don't live close by, but anytime I want Chinese food I'm making the trip here. It is so worth it. Everything was flavorful and delicious. Just writing this review makes me wanna go get some right now!

Luke is a great joint. The food is all delicious, a fusion of French, German, and New Orleans specialties. Drinks are expensive, but happy hour is a great deal with half off their own draft brews, wine, and cocktails. The oysters at happy hour are only 50 cents, and sure, you say, you know of a 25 cent oyster joint somewhere. I guarantee those oysters aren't as big and fresh as those at Luke. Just the best raw oysters I've had anywhere.

I love their lunch, especially the two course daily lunch special. And the burger, dear me, you might not thing of this as a burger place, but it's got one of my favorites in town. The only reason I don't get it more often is because it's hard to get anything done after eating that mid-day.

They serve Cokes in the individual small bottles, so they aren't bottomless. But you aren't coming to a place like this for bottomless Cokes, anyway.

The biggest drawback to the place is the loudness, especially in the back room. New Orleans restaurants really need to cut this crap out. Having a loud place doesn't make you seem more popular. Also, I have no idea how to pronounce a u with an umlaut, so that's annoying.

This place was a big disappointment to us. The vegetarian burrito was overwhelmingly salty. My partner ordered guac, which costs $2 extra, and there was a tiny amount shoved into the bottom of the burrito. For almost $30 for two people to have dinner, I expected better food.
Seafood was fresh. Pork was really good, fish was fresh, chicken was juicy, pasta was a bit spicy but good. Wish they have more tea options for desert. Service was good too.

Okay Bumped Jiffy Lube up a star.  They did respond to my Yelp! review and offered to discuss my issues.  I didn't have time, but then Tosha from the Jiffy Lube store called a few days later and explained the issues. 

On the Groupon, it is supposed to be for the oil change (up to 5 qts) and a RainX treatment, SO I was NOT charged for the RainX but that it was listed as part of the services that I received on the Groupon credit ($71).  Tosha also noted that the Groupons are not valid until 24 hours from purchase, but that they accepted my same day purchase -So thanks for that.

On the Differential Service, She admitted I was over charged for the differential fluid because it was included as part of the service (up to 7 qts) and that she would send a request to corporate office to refund the aprox $26 that I was charged above the cost of the service.

Tosha also explained and reiterated her commitment to the military, including veterans, and that any veteran government ID was valid for a discount.  She stated that Jiffy Lube policy was not to stack discounts, so that my military discount was denied, and should have been explained, because only the Groupon OR the military discount could be applied.  She also noted they also made Free oil change coupon donations to the Military. -So thanks for that too.

I can't go to 4 stars because I'm not a 'fan.'  But If an opportunity arises to give a second chance then I would be willing to give it a second shot.  To be clear, my prior Two Stars was "Meh, I've Experienced Better" and Three Stars is "A-OK" so at this point they are worth giving a shot as they have several Five Star ratings and they did make extra efforts to resolve my issues, that I was going to let go as a learning lesson.  Now I would return if a similar incentive presented itself.  Thanks to Matthew and Tosha for always being pleasant and professional.

The corn and shrimp bisque bowl was a filling and slightly spicy entree for a light eater. A little dismayed by being handed a menu with a squashed bug on it which probably led to my light appetite. Although the menu was replaced, the original should never have been used.

Located at a hotel, it can't hold a lot of people. Had the seafood gumbo soup which was pretty good. Had the Shrimp as the main course which was done right and seemed to be fresh. The server was nice and explained most of the food to us. A group of 4 would be just right, anything larger would probably require a reservation. Just 5 minutes from Bourbon Street and not that far from the antique shops.

Pleasantly surprised to stumble upon this little gem in the suburbs. Service was fast and friendly and the food was as delectable as it looked. We started with soups and edamame and also chose a seafood special and a volcano roll. Definitely plan on returning!

My boyfriend and I arrived a couple of minutes before our reservation - was sat quickly and far from the noisy bar (thank you!)

Our server was so sweet but I forgot her name ...( she was pregnant) we got our drinks and appetizers super fast but our entrees a little slower than we expected.
