I recommend the LÜke burger and the roasted chicken... Soooooo yummy!!!


It was a great restaurant to dine at for my first dine in New Orleans :)

A part of me doesn't want to review this place, I would rather keep it a secret gem, but hey it's always good to share.

This maybe one of the best happy hours in New Orleans!  Happy hour is from 3 to 6 and it is not limited to bar seating.  It is a white tablecloth restaurant but most people where casually dressed and it seems pretty laid back.

Now on to the happy hour specials.  Raw oysters were 50 cents and I think the fried oysters were a dollar, but we kept with the raw.  These oysters were the best oysters we had during our twelve days in New Orleans and we had quite a few oysters.  No grit what so ever and they were good size oysters.

Specialty drinks, draft beer, and wine are half price.  We started with a couple of rounds of mojitos, the mojitos were not on the drink menu but they were included in the happy hour pricing.  They were a little on the sweet side but we asked our waiter if he could bring us some fresh lime wedges, which he did and that  solved that problem.

Decided on one more round of drinks but we changed it up an ordered a Silver Saint and a Sazerac.

The Silver Saint (tequila, fresh lime juice, cucumber syrup, Serrano pepper, and soda water) was a great drink, loved the kick from the Serrano pepper.  

The Sazerac (Rye, sugar, peychauds bitters and herbsaint) BF enjoyed this drink.

Definitely check out this happy hour, you will not be disappointed.  Wish we had learned about it sooner, I'm sure we would have gone a couple of more times.

We came late on a Saturday and was promptly served, even though the restaurant was busy. We started with the flamenkuche, mostly because I make it myself often and wanted to compare against a professional chef's version. They put it on a very thin crust and load it with cheese, deliciously sweet caramelized onions and huge chunks of bacon. I wasn't a fan of how the bacon was cut- I prefer my bacon diced smaller and spread out more. But I did love the onions. I had the etoufee and it was delicious- love the tasty sauce and the shrimp was cooked just right. I cleaned the bowl, sapping up every bit of that sauce with bread. I think I would prefer it on rice vs penne, but it was fine. My husband got the cheesiest croque madame I've ever seen, with a runny egg and lots of ham. Not a fan of the oily thin fries though. All in all, good solid meal at a decent price.
Good food, nice place! Only oysters I had on my NOLA trip this time, and they were excellent!

This was my first introduction to the New Orleans cuisine.  Very convenient location since I stayed at the New Orleans Hilton right next door.  Very much enjoyed my shrimp farci with new potatoes and blood orange hollandaise sauce.  Yum!   Some of the other meals (including the BLT with crab sandwich) sounded excellent. Might be a little pricier than other restaurants but other than that, no complains here.

The happy hour here is one of the greatest in the city.  A French 75 is a must have drink, and for half price 3-6pm, seven days a week.  They have $.050 oysters as well!  Cozy atmosphere just outside of the French Quarter for a little get away from the craziness of Bourbon.
Best happy hour in NOLA.  Food and drinks are spectacular.  Service even more magnificent...ask for Linda.  She is the best server in the world!!!
We came here for happy hour. The raw oyster is smaller than ACME. There is no non alcoholic menu and the coke is 3.75 and NO REFILLABLE. Very disappointed and will not recommended to anyone.

Ok I've heard it over and over. Luke Luke Luke. Y'all their happy hour is off the hook! We had specialty cocktails that are stout on the alcohol but not overpowering the original design of the drink. The food! P&J Oysters raw .75 and a half dozen perfectly seasoned and fried in a light tasty batter for $7.50.  You can also order off the menu and we did. Hot Buttered Crawfish Bread. It's absolutely perfect. Big thick slices of French bread with a healthy slab of Burrata and then covered with a savory buttery crawfish laden sauce. The Smoked Redfish Rillette was another gorgeous surprise a creamy light smoky fish dip that has a briny vinegar based chow chow on top. It's paired with thin slices of French baguettes. 

The service is impeccable. Tristan and Savannah were our servers. Tristan was knowledgeable and not afraid to be an ambassador for the restaurant and its offerings. Savannah was prompt and completely attentive. 

If you haven't been for their 7 day a week Happy Hour with half price specialty cocktails and oyster specials you're missing the out. It was a perfect way to have dinner and drinks!!

We went for the $.50 oysters, of course! We ordered 4 dozen oysters, frites, and veal pasta. The oysters are large and good but not as good as Acme. Then again, you are getting it for half the price of Acme. The oysters aren't briny like Acme either. You do get hard sharp shell bits in your oysters which makes me think if the shulker has experience. I know I shouldn't complain for the price but it took away from the experience when you have to pick out shell bits from your oyster or your mouth. They are good though. 

Customer services is Amazing. They are so friendly and accommodating.  I didn't like that even though the restaurant only had two other customers there they put us in a tiny tiny minature two person table because we ordered alot of food and there was no room on the table.  They had to use a rack to stack our food on top of each other.  We couldn't even see each other to talk.  If the restaurant is empty, they should put us in a bigger table for comfort sake. 

I would highly recommend this place as a must for the value.

I only come here for their happy hour for the oysters and drinks.  Sometimes if I feel like eating something else, I'll order some gumbo and sides. Happy starts at 3pm I believe and ends at 6pm. Everyday including Saturdays!

So many restaurants in New Orleans - so many! Why did we subject ourselves to the poor service at Lüke? 

Food is better than average. Short menu and everything was well prepared and tasty. Though if you're gonna serve big whole pieces of bibb lettuce best to use a larger plate eh?

And the local trend for serving bread seems to be in a napkin - for me this get's old and cliché real quick....

Again, everything tastes good on the food menu - though the prices do seem odd/high, especially the starters - 

I could tell you about dessert but none was offered....

Now I can go in detail about the awful service - or you can just trust me that this place a. Needs to train staff from the top down. B. Needs a new personnel manager.

I saw a "manager" clear a table by putting her fingers in used glasses and carry them away -- tacky and unsanitary; the hostess was overwhelmed to say the least and had the personality of cardboard (and not new box cardboard - like used three times for moving box under your bed that you prolly should have thrown away card board), the bartender gave looks of "why are you trying to order more drinks look and every time she made my drink (three times) it tasted different - same drink three different tastes - yea....  And the busboys/expediters were so ballsy/pushy you better hold on to the table when they landed with your order.

Oh our server you ask? I have no idea because he was barely around unless you ask another server to find ours - 

So yea, maybe three stars is generous, but the food was good.

@TravelNTings #TravelNTings we always stop at Luke when we come to NOLA! Their oysters are a must try along with the shrimp and grits.  Tried the Shrimp "Étouffée" this time around and of course we were not disappointed. There's so many great things on this menu :-)

I love Cosi - it's fast, convenient, and delicious! While I agree that the concept and feel of the restaurant is very similar to Panera, I would say that the variety of food at Cosi is very different. I REALLY enjoy Cosi flatbread, which is definitely their signature product. There's something really special about their flatbread, and for some reason I just can't put my finger on why I think it's so flavorful. They give a piece of flatbread with every salad, and it's a fantastic, crunchy, and fulfilling finish to a meal. Other yelpers say that it would be great with some sort of spread or dip, but I think it tastes amazing alone as well. 

In terms of the other food, I've only ordered the salads and have found the staff to be very helpful and willing to accommodate for any dietary restrictions or preferences. They very easily switch out chicken for salmon in my salad, so that's definitely a wonderful option for me since I adore eating fish. Plus, it's difficult to find dishes with fish in University City without paying a fortune. The workers are quick and efficient (which others may interpret as cold), but I really appreciate the speediness of Cosi, especially when rushing between classes throughout a busy day.

I guess the only negative aspect of Cosi that I see is that many of the other items on the menu are pretty pricey (many are around $8-10) for the food that you get (mainly sandwiches...), so I haven't been too adventurous with trying out different options since I know I can get the best bang out of my buck with the salad that I consistently order.

Oh, before I forget - COSI SERVES S'MORES. It's great. For around $8, they provide graham crackers, marshmallows, chocolate and skewers for two with a cute, mini-burner, making such a wonderfully unique and interactive end to a meal with that special someone. You definitely can't find this experience for this price anywhere else in the area. Recommend you try the s'mores, for sure!

We were staying at the Intercontinental Hotel and right across the street was Luke's. Walked by it several times going here and there . On our last day were we in between lunch and dinner and decided to stop in to have a drink and grab some bar food. Left two hours later and couldn't tell you how great a time we had . First off we sat at the bar and the guys behind the bar were just fabulous. We arrived at happy hour which they have every day as this was a Saturday. All signature  cocktails half price and .75 cent oysters. So we started  with a dozen and wished we had order more but be careful of the horse radish it is great but super strong just as I like it . Had a bowl of gumbo half price again and several more items that I can't even remember . All in all we had a great time the Service was spot on and food great. Ended up with bread pudding with ice cream a great way to finish. Will never make dinner but we ate at more restaurants then I can remember  during our stay but Luke's for a semi casual but up scale eatery was for me as good as most and if you hit happy hour it's pound for pound better then the rest

Amazing happy hour!!! 75 cent oysters that are local and delicious. Cocktail happy hour will blow you mind !! French 75 is amazing and beer is only $4. Highly recommend!!! Service is not as great as it should be but still worth going for happy hour 4-6. Cheesy grits are also the best I have ever had!!!

I came during Essence Fest and ordered the Southern Breakfast due to its generous offerings, but sadly I only enjoyed the bacon. After noticing that I only ate a small portion of my food, the server insisted that I order something else since it was apparent that I didn't enjoy my food. I declined the offer, and shortly after, the manager came by my table to see if there was anything that he could do. In short, the manager only charged me for the bacon that I ate, which was an extremely generous offer. Although I didn't get to enjoy my meal, I think it speaks volumes of the staff to see how invested they were in making my experience a good one. It's a beautiful restaurant and I'm sure they have other delicious options. I applaud the manager and his team.

The food was great. I had a light meal here (the place had caught my eye on the way "home"):

-- 1/2 dozen P&J oysters were fresh and ICE COLD
-- Fried oyster salad (?) ... Recommended by the server, who insisted that it wouldn't be oyster overkill. The salad was a little overdressed with salty dressing, but holy shit, the chopped up pieces of thick sliced bacon and fried oysters hit the spot

Service was okay. Not extremely attentive, but not bad either.

Atmosphere:
-- Decor was spot on for a hotel restaurant
-- Eavesdropped: "She thinks she's so cool for going to school in Alabama..." (AWESOME)

BEWARE!!! This business is a scam! After cancelling my appointment 3 times, they finally sent a Service Technician to my house to service my A/C for the season, and the nightmare began! They said that I needed to replace my unit. My unit is only 5 years old and worked perfect. They put my girlfriend on the phone with some scumbag salesman, Joe, and he tried to coach her into a new system. He was very pushy and unprofessional. She said that she could hear him cursing at the Tech after she declined. All I wanted was the A/C serviced. We got a second opinion and everything was fine. Be careful, all they want to do is sell new equipment. They do not want to fix or service anything!

Fantastic shrimp and grits. I always look forward to stopping in for breakfast or lunch at Luke when I visit town. Great little spot that I always recommend to friends and family that are heading to New Orleans.

We were fortunate, or so i thought, to book a room at he Hilton St Charles's 
Luke's, the best restaurant in NO is connected. 
However, currently the Hilton, and Luke's is a construction "WAR ZONE". Who knew the intercontinental would be upgrading the front area
Well HILTON did. Could they let guest know. NO!!!!
Anyway, getting back to Luke's. The best food in the entire world. We were fortunate to have THE BEST PERSON SERVE IS, Lilly. She is one of a kind    Perfect!
She made our visit to the Hilton NO perfect. She really needs to be recognized as an employee that turned a bad day into a great day

We only went there for he half price oyster happy hour 3-6 but OMG!!!! Sooo sooo good...we always were able to sit at the bar (which our favorite). We spent 3 or 4 days in a week from 3-6pm back in November. My husband and I ate more than anyone that works there has ever seen 8 dozen!!!! 

Btw, we went to Acme just to see.... Thumbs way down

Luke was a pleasant enough place, but not nearly as nice as it believes itself to be.

We visited for lunch on a Saturday, and the food was fine. My steak was a perfect medium, which was odd because I ordered it medium rare. The music was so loud that the waiter misheard us several times. A restaurant pretentious enough to have half of its menu in French should probably have more  discernment than to blast 80s pop at a volume that barely allows for conversation.

The tables were small and crowded, the food overpriced, and the wait staff unskilled. In a city filled with excellent food choices, I definitely will be looking elsewhere for a pleasant meal.
Awesome sushi. So delicious. Wish I lived closer, but we make the drive out anytime we want sushi. Very reasonably priced, too.

This was a really lovely meal. The atmosphere is beautiful in the ground floor of the Hilton on St. Charles which a cornerstone says used to be a Masonic Temple back in the 1920s.

The inlaid wood floor is beautiful and it wasn't too loud (partly the wood floor I'm sure), The service was attentive and helpful (I joked to my New Orleans native dad that the waiter might've been putting on his sugary accent... :-)

Anyway on to the food. I started with gulf oysters which were delicious and briny and on the half shell. MMMMM. Fresh and large and reasonably priced ($8 for half dozen).

I then had one of the best pieces of steak (billed as Entrecote or ribeye) I've had in a long time. Perfectly cooked and absolutely tender. It was really something. Served with thin shoestring fries (my favorite) and bernaise sauce. Fantastic. 

My mother had the veal and my father had a seafood pasta dish and both were quite nice. The little batons of bread were also delicious. My only minor complaint was that they came out late (someone had clearly forgotten them).

All in all a wonderful meal and not expensive especially for what you're getting.

Our best dining experience during our trip to New Orleans.  The service was fantastic (Thanks, Chris!) and the food was as good as we expected.  John Besh does not disappoint.

The standout was the Pate.  I am still thinking about it.  Probably some of the best I have ever had.  Oysters were delish as well.

I even finished off the meal with a Sazerac.  Certainly a different cocktail than what I am used to but I recommend everybody try at least one when they are in the Big Easy.

With rock star status,  New Orleans Chef John Besh serves up amatuer garage band grub at Luke.  Is he peddling some sort of  Alsatian - Creole - Black Forest - Bistro grub?  Who knows; I don't get it.  On a recent visit to Luke, my red fish was served coated with a soggy batter and covered with a tasteless dollop of lump crab meat.  The desert of bread pudding was swimming in an overwhelming praline sauce, making this New Orleans staple virtually unrecognizable.  The waitstaff look silly in white tunics.  Is this place REALLY a John Besh restaurant?

Having previously dined at August (another Besh venture), I find Luke to be terribly disappointing ... completely incongruent with Besh's reputation.  NOLA has much better to offer within easy walking distance (away) from Luke.

wow, very unexpected but oh so awesome.  I had the rabbit and chicken liver pate (perfection) and a croque madame.  Hubby had the crab bisque and a gigantic plate of pork shank, sauerkraut and sausage.  Perfect for a cool Dec evening, wonderful comfort food.  Service was fantastic, despite a couple big tables that were throwing things off, there were other folks filling the gaps for our server, making it seamless for us.  For sure we'll be back, thinking will try for breakfast.
Excellent meal recommended by Audubon Cottages, fun atmosphere and great flavor! I am a huge John Besh fan and it did not disappoint, head there for a great experience!

What a lovely place! With $0.75 happy hour oysters... YESSS! Loved it!

Happy hour drinks were also a deal!  Tried the French 75, which was highly recommended.  I liked how the number 75 was written on top.  Taste wise was decent.

Beyond happy hour, I tried the shrimp and grits for dinner! It was a delightful dish served in a hot cast iron dish - the grits were very nice and creamy with jalapenos (nice spin), with a decent amount of shrimp.  I might prefer a little less cream, and more zest.  It wasn't the best shrimp and grits I ever had and certainly not the largest of portion, but it definitely was good.

Service was nice and attentive.  I would recommend Luke!

happy hour
$0.75 per raw oyster, $1.25 per fried oyster, half off all drinks between 3-6pm
Crab bisque was awesome - $10
Mussels with fries - huge amount of mussels and the sauce is absolutely to die for. I think our group ate at least 4-5 servings of bread. 

Great service, great happy hour, great food!
Overall, great place!!

This place I found  one weekend while we were looking for a place for brunch. A Great find!

I ordered the Luke burger, and my wife had a bowl of the crawfish bisque, chicken liver and rabbit pate, and a prawns & grits I believe (Sorry, I'm writing this review late and I just can't remember the name).  The Luke burger was amazing!  The bun is so soft and the burger itself was cooked just, not too juicy or dry. The right size wasn't some ridiculous amount to make it sloppy or too small to be called a slider.  I would come back every time for the burger and their fries were just as good. I'm a huge fry guy, and the ones here are very good.  Get a side order if you don't have them with your meal.  :D  My wife liked her crawfish bisque and her pate.  While she didn't rave on and on about it, she was very pleased with those two particular selections.  I'm game for trying something new...but pate is NOT MY CUP of tea!  :(  However, for those that do like pate, my wife say this was top-notched! Now as for the prawns & grits, I believe they would have been great if they weren't over salted.  But I think this might have been a mishap from the kitchen.  Because the prawns themselves were huge and grilled to perfection, just a bummer it was over seasoned.  :(

This place has amazing value for the quality in food you get!  Yes, I think I paid like over $15 for the burger, but it was worth every darn penny and I would gladly, greedily pay it again!  :D

The atmosphere was good, they had a nice dining/bar area.  Even for it being a busy Sunday, it wasn't overly stuffy, crowded, or noisy!  The decor has both dark and light features throughout, so it makes it for a nice stop if you want to go somewhere special.  

The service was great.  We had a wonderful server that knew the menu inside and out with great recommendations.  

Not sure about the parking there, since it was located on a high traffic area on St Charles Ave.  We actually walked from our hotel, which was maybe 10 mins.  But like all things in that area, there is a parking lot or structure located somewhere near.  

Overall, I liked this place a lot.  When I come here again, I will definitely have to venture out and try something more original than a burger.  But IF YOU HAVE TO GET A BURGER, this one isn't that bad to get!  :D

Fabulous happy hour.  We arrived 30 minutes before our reserved time.  (It is highly recommended to make reservations for happy hour also because it gets busy. )  The host said there were couple empty seats so we could be seated.  

The two ladies that were bartending that night were fabulous, lovely and answered all of our drink questions.  We ordered the French 75 and the Sazerac, enjoyed both of them thoroughly.  We also tried the Saint and that was my favorite drink of the three.  The oysters ($0.75 each during happy hour) were good.  For someone that eats oysters often during business trips, my husband said they weren't the freshest but still good.  (This could be because we ordered oysters in June and not during 'r' months.) Who knows... I liked the dozen oysters and three cocktails for happy hour special.  I highly recommend going to Luke for drinks and some food.  (We had dinner plans otherwise I would've ordered off the menu as well.)   Can't wait to go back when we're in the city again...

Absolutely the best sushi ever . Tuna Bites ? Omg ! Out of control roll ? The name speaks for itself. Servers are amazing. Chefs are fantastic. I would eat here everyday if I could . I searched high and low for my favorite spot for sushi and this is the winner by far ..

Super delicious shrimp and grits. Very satiating and savory. Will come back for the shrimp and grits. Took a bite of the chicken biscuit and it was all right. Our waiter was very attentive and helpful.

The best new secret in town is no longer a secret to Ivette and I. Located in the New Britain Village Square (think Blued Dog Family Tavern and Genuardi's) Hachi offers a great variety rolls, sushi and sashimi selections. The menu also includes noodles, rice and tempura.

The décor is simply beautiful... as in beautifully simple. The restaurant has been open for 2.5 months and already has a bunch of fans. The couple next to us said that they've been there "a bunch of times already" and everything they've had has been very good.

Make reservations before you go. You are bound to wait if you don't. We went on a whim and found ourselves walking over to the Blue Dog Tavern to wait for a table. BTW the Blue Dog has the 2014 Anchor Steam seasonal. Make sure to give it a try.

I am glad we waited rather than changing our dinner plans. 

Appetizers:
* Wakame Seaweed Salad
* Yellowtail Serrano
They were both delicious. The salad portion was big enough for Ivette and I to share. But the Yellowtail Serrano stole the opening act.  I don't recall the last time I had yellowtail that fresh. The Serrano portion of the name is what made me order. I was curious about what I thought was a fish and ham combination but... no ham in this plate. The presentation is what makes you look twice to make sure it is indeed yellowtail for it looked like a beautifully arranged pieces of thinly sliced serrano ham garnished with jalapeño and olive oil. Ivette avoids jalapeños like the plague but this time she was eating everything. This is a must-have item.

Main Dishes:
* Rainbow Roll
* Roasted Beet Avocado Roll
* Pad Thai with Fried Tofu (chicken and shrimp were other options).
The rolls were among the best we've had. All the ingredients tasted very fresh. You will definitely taste everything, specially the roasted beet... unless you make the mistake of overdoing it with the soy sauce.

Pad Tai? I was almost scraping the plate! I love rice noodles and this will be one item in their menu that will be hard for me not to order over and over.

Dessert:
* Wild Berry Toban
Mango, blueberries, blackberries, strawberries, kiwi and a crunchy pie crust top served in a boiling hot covered pan. Ivette and I carved out our portions and finished it all.

Constructive comments:
Our server did a superb job serving the table. She paid a lot of attention to placement. A little more attention to keeping the table clean would have been awesome. Nothing to worry about though. I would have been nice touch.

The entrance to the kitchen is a nice-looking curtain that doesn't always close. I don't particularly care for having a view to the kitchen.

One of the owners came to our table a few times to make sure everything was to our liking. We could tell that he is genuinely interested in creating the best dining experience to his customers. As far as I am concerned he is doing that very well.

Congratulations to the Hachi folks. We look forward to our next visit.

Food was super greasy. I can appreciate rich food, as a New Orleanian, but found Luke to be deplorable. Excess grease aside, the food suffered from a lack of cohesion within the plates. I began with the crawfish bisque, which came out as a cracked roux with large grease slicks throughout. Curiously there was a stuffed crawfish shell in the soup, but no seafood fork or finger bowl was provided as means to make possible the consumption of that morsel. As my main course I ate the jumbo Gulf shrimp and grits, and while I found the grits very enjoyable, the only flavors on the plate were spice, spice and more spice, which totally obliterated any chance that the Gulf shrimp's subtle flavors might shine. Fortunately for me, the dessert that followed was certainly a high point in my week. I ordered the Banana Cream Profiteroles, and was truly impressed by the rich flavor of the banana cream, contrasted with the concentrated flavor of the Foster's sauce, it was all very lovely. The service was mediocre, but the waitress was dingy but attentive. The concept is absolutely silly: they use dish towels for napkins, paper table cloths, random kitchen tools as plate stand-ins, and unappetizing methods and procedures for consumption of certain morsels of shelled stuffing.  Do not go there under any circumstances.

So good I came here twice in my short stint in NOLA! The first time I came in the evening by myself, sat at the bar and really enjoyed chatting up the staff while devouring their shrimp and grits with seasonal vegetables on the side. The veggies here are not overlooked--the carrots were turned beautifully, and the variety of veg on the plate was such a pleasant surprise. Dessert, as is apparently becoming my fancy, was bread pudding. Luke's was as good as it gets.

The sauce with the shrimp and grits was dark, thick, layered and delicious. It wasn't just heavy, which would've been too much in concert with the cheese grits. It was a perfect compliment.

Next time I'm in NOLA, I will go out of my way to come back.

Doubt I can say anything new. You don't get this many great reviews unless you're nailing it.
Gumbo was perfect. Oysters were great, though they are a little pricey here. Probably the best brussel sprouts I've even had, and the bread pudding was so good.
The staff was very busy, but friendly once you got them to slow down for a second.

My hubby and I ate here on Christmas Day when it seemed almost impossible to get a table at a hip restaurant in NOLA. We lucked out with our early 5:00 dinner reservations it was still happy hour where the wonderful plump oysters were on .75 cents each.  We ordered one dozen and promptly ordered another.  We could not get enough so we went back the next day during happy hour where we wanted to sit at the bar but the bar seemed to be the most popular spot with all full chairs and three people deep standing behind them.  I would definitely go back as the menu was limited because of Revilion but we thoroughly enjoyed our fresh fish and shrimp and grits.  Lastly if you get lucky enough to sit adjacent to the kitchen you won't be disappointed viewing the food being prepared.  The place is also much larger than it appears.

We went there at Christmas but no seat available. It is a very hot place. 

We made a reservations the day after Christmas. The environment is elegant. The raw oyster is awesome and we can't help order another half dozen after finish one. Gumbo and bisque are also good. I like this place!

Lüke's Restaurant 

A great dining experience after a disappointing trip to two restaurants prior not working out. 

My fiancée and I shared and thoroughly enjoyed the Brussels sprouts (4.5/5) keeping in mind I've never liked Brussels sprouts in the past, they had an Asian like taste that reminded me of teriyaki. The stuffed oysters (4.8/5) which had such a great umami to them, truly delicious. Then for a main we had the Black Drum fish (3.5/5) where the highlight was actually the vegetables, simply done by way of sauté with garlic but so delicious.

But the best part of our meal had to be the waiter, Nick. He was great, good advice and very chatty (but not that over chatty, trying to get a big tip chatty)

Went for happy hours. Got 10 raw
PJ oysters and 6 fried oysters. The oysters were really fresh and delicious. They don't skimp on it despite the happy hour. Got some wine(rosè) and cocktail (French 75). Friend got beer and Chardonnay and was delicious as well. I am
Really impressed by the servers there and the quality of food for happy hours. I will come back for sure and it doesn't matter if you are visiting NO or local, it's worth a trip.

Just came from lunch at Luke. Ordered the cheese grits and shrimp and it was great. Nice atmosphere and courteous  service but I think the $$ rating should changed to $$$ or $$$$. Regardless of the cost I would recommend lunch or dinner here.

It was my first time visiting Nola!! This place came highly recommend for my local friends. So of course we had to find out for our selfs. It was a 5 min walk from the hotel which was nice. The atmosphere was very nice and welcoming we ordered the p and j oysters. We didn't pay close to the what the menu said and how they were prepared. But when they arrived they were green and delicious!! We both ordered sandwiches that were very tasty and filling. i recommend if you ever get a chance you should give it a shot!!

Came here for lunch after my brothers graduation from Tulane to celebrate.  I made reservations on Opentable and even though we were ten minutes late they had saved our table (but the hostess mentioned she was just about to give it away).  I'm happy they were patient.

We ordered the cold foie gras appetizer, which was good though the bread it came with was way to greasy.  The foie gras was much better on the regular small baguette bread they provided to the table.  The waiter had mentioned this when we ordered and we agreed.

For our entrees, I ordered the Friday red fish special.  I really enjoyed it, perfect portion and nice mix with some shrimp, crab meat and oysters.  And the craw fish bisque soup was great too.

Others ordered the jumbo Louisiana shrimp, grilled ribeye, and shrimp farci.  All were good but we didn't realize the shrimp farci was a fried dish. Since three members of the party ordered it and each was surprised and disappointed, that's minus one star.

Also minus one-star for service, it was a bit slow.  The server was nice and pleasant, but we had to grab out own ketchup and waited a bit too long for drink refills and finally to pay the bill.

I'd come back, just order the right menu item and have some patience.

This is my second visit to LUKE and I will be back a third time when I am in NOLA. Chef Besh does it right from the reasonably priced drinks to the food. Well worth the money. 
Growing up in NYC I was intrigued when I saw the Matzo Ball Soup on the menu. What Matzo Ball Soup in NOLA????Rabbi Feldman would die at such a menu item outside of NYC. Surprise, surprise...it was delicious and as good, if not better than, matzo ball soup from Katz's restaurant on Houston Street in NYC. The poulet grand-mère (herb roasted local chicken) with Allan Benton's bacon, farmers' market
vegetables & whipped potatoes was superb. I was stuffed with no room for desert but the waiter brought this little box with two chocolates in it. Nice Chef Besh...I coming back and next time just try to tempt me with Yonah Schimmell's knishes!!!!!! I dare you:)
Lovely people. Smoking bar.  Good conversation.  Not sure if they have food. Not sure what else to say. Drinks are very typical
50 cent oysters during happy hour? Need I say more? Get yo ass down to Luke's between 3pm - 6pm!

Jerzees Sports Bar is the perfect place to grab something to eat and drink watching the game. 

Food: The selection at Jerzees includes normal bar food. My personal favorite is the Jerzees App Sampler; you can choose 4 different appetizers all on one plate. Also, 2$ plain slices are a nice touch. If you're looking for a new favorite beer, Jerzees can help you with that too. They have a huge variety of both beer and liquor. The specials at Jerzees are great too. They have different discounts each night of the week on drinks and food. 

4/5

Service: This bar is packed with plenty of skilled bartenders and other help. Most of the bartenders are friendly and welcoming, my friends and I like Jackie the best. Its nice to see familiar faces when going into a neighborhood bar like Jerzees.

4/5

Location: Jerzees is a noticeable building with bar esc decor outside. Parking is selective but most nights you can get a spot. If parking is full its tough to get a table inside. When you walk in the front door, sit anywhere and relax. There are bar games, flat screen televisions, and beer advertisements everywhere. Jerzees is easily accessible and perfect for a night of food and drinks.

5/5

Total: 13/15

Luke was definitely a pleasant find for a nice relaxing breakfast. The atmosphere was warm and the staff made it very personal. If Lee is there, he'll keep you entertained with his NOLA charm throughout your meal. I love my coffee and theirs was as rich and warming as it gets. I didn't get too adventurous with my breakfast, but the grits were to die for and the sausage and bacon had me drooling even before I took my first bite. I have to imagine lunch and dinner there would be just as good. Very reasonably priced with good sized portions. I love the classic dark wood decor!

We'll definitely go back next time we're in town. Hopefully Lee will be serving again!

When I am out of town during the week I make it a goal of mine to find the best place in town for happy hour and boy did I find it.  From the hours of 4 to 6 you can come to this wonderful location and enjoy $.75 raw oysters or 1.25 fried (sold by half dozen) and they accept reservations!!

Upon arrival this place was not nearly as crowded as I had expected it to be which is why I had originally made a reservation which was not needed.  We were seated by the Kinde staff and immediately told about the happy hour specials and drink specials (half off cocktails). The staff was very patient with us when we were trying to decide what we wanted to eat and we received our food within 10 minutes of ordering.

I cannot remember the name of my drink but it was some type of jalapeño drink that was way harder than I was prepared for it to be LOL but it was still tasty. The Oyster's both raw and fried were made to perfection and they provided you with plenty of different sauces and seasonings to flavor your oysters. Overall we got 4 raw oysters, two bowls of gumbo, a half dozen fried oysters, and two drinks all for about $42. Would definitely co
Highly recommend for a savory, delicious, filling meal in New Orleans! Be sure to start off with the oysters and the Brussels sprout appetizer. The staff was very friendly and I will be back soon!

I went here Sunday instead of going to the oyster festival since it was so hot outside and I'm glad I did. Luke has happy hour on Sunday's from 3-6PM. I went for happy hour and it was such a treat. The happy hour menu is pretty good. I settled for some P&J raw oysters which were priced at 75 cents. They were huge just the way I like them. Cocktails were half off so I got 2 French 75's. The drink was so good and it was served in a big glass with 75 written in it. I think they may use egg white in the French 75, which gave it a nice texture. I also had the blue crab gratin, which I recommend. The boudin balls came with a tangy sauce that paired well with the balls, since they were a little dry. The service was excellent and the ambiance was relaxing. I definitely will go here again for happy hour.

I came here for happy hour and seated myself at the bar with my mom, since the next seating available for 2 was in 2 hours.
The oysters here are HUGE and super super super fresh.

I got a dozen P&J oysters and I also got the stuffed P&J oysters.
I felt like the price in itself was a complete steal.
We ended up paying $24.24 for around 18 oysters.

I loved it here and highly recommend this joint!
I LOVE MEAT BUTTER!!!!!!! And the oysters were devine!!! If im ever in NO again i will defintly go again
Best meal ever!!!  We had shrimp appetizers- fresh crisp shrimp.  Fried quail legs - with honey and sliced peppers sauce!!!! And shrimp remoulade on cheesy grits.
One and done! Rushed and spotty service in a cramped space with pedestrian room temperature food! Not sure who has been giving the good reviews

Being in a hotel property I was skeptical. Thursday night, torrential downpour outside, there were plenty of locals willing to wait for a table. 

Best shrimp and grits I have ever had. A guy next to me had Luke's Burger. Biggest hamburger patty I've ever seen with bacon and cheddar wrapping the outer edges, cooked medium rare to perfection. 

Definitely worthy of a repeat visit!!!

Okay, by far the best French 75 I've had here in New Orleans. Crispy Brussels Sprouts were delicious - with just the right amount of sweetness and they melted in our mouths. Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" were indeed jumbo. Whoever decided to mix jalapeño with cheese grits should be knighted. The staff was helpful and fun. My colleagues and I had a great night after a long day. Perfecto.
Awesome! Great place and excellent service. Sat at the bar during Happy Hour and had .50 oysters and half price beers. Will come back!

The staff deserve a five star because they were still open on Christmas Eve. We walked in 20 minutes before closing and were welcomed in instead of turned away and they were still nice and polite, never rushed us the whole time. The food is great, char-grilled oysters were delicious and gumbo was tasty.

Need free weights? Need exercise machines? Need cardio equipment? Well this gym has all that, which I consider are the basic necessities, plus some. If your goal is to build muscle, maintain, or lose fat, you can definitely get the job done here for $19.99/month. If you want to mindlessly work out and be instructed on what to do, then take a group class. This Retro offers a variety of classes. So you want a pool, basketball courts, sauna, a steam room, and an expensive gym membership? Then you should take your boujee self on over to LifeTime Fitness. 


Reason for the 3 stars... well I've run into situations where the leg extension machine was down or out of commission for a week to MONTHS (happened last year). Instead of the typical temporary fix of having a service tech repair the piece of equipment this past time, the machine was finally replaced in its entirety. IMO there should be 2 leg extension machines. And the instructor running the kickboxing class has to deal with some run down freestanding heavy bags that leaks water from the base for the duration of the class. He shouldn't have to be frequently wiping the puddles on the floor during class to ensure none of his class participants slip and fall. Those bags should be replaced. Or fill the base with sand perhaps?

Great place to celebrate Thanksgiving in New Orleans.

We were there on vacation and wanted a casual place and good food.

Luke's was perfect.

We had no reservation and got there about noon and the place was packed.   Great hostess staff and we had a fabulous server.  The receipt says Timothy.

For Thanksgiving we ordered the Turducken with sweet potatoes and cajun stuffing.   All excellent, we also had an order of the Brussels Sprouts salad (my Thanksgiving choice).  Absolutely delicious.    The bill included one beer and totaled $52.05.   Way better than cooking at home!

Thanksgiving buffet:  arrived at 3pm and the turducken was picked over, hardly any gravey in a hugh bowl and the pig nothing but a head and fatty nibs...to be kind maybe they don't have any idea of how to run a buffet but the one rule is that you do not let the table look savaged...I paid the same as the first person at the start...was really disappointed...even bought the cookbook before and really expected more from the BESH organization...wondered going in why people had very little on their dessert plates and then tasted the offerings:  not very good.

My son did fix me a great salad...the beets were wonderful!  The gumbo was good but the rest of the dressings and side dishs just OK...coffee was extra...price was very reasonable and there were plenty of staff but they seemed kinda lame and seemed to pass a lotta time chatting with each other.

Would hit many other places before returning to another BESH establishment and never for a holiday buffet.

Ummm how does this place not have 5stars. I mean almost 4000 reviews and they do have 4, pretty good average, but seriously!

Gumbo-my husband eats gumbo every single place it's served. This is the first time he said, "its perfect". 
Beet salad-perfect as well. Roasted to perfection, blue cheese that was unbelievably creamy, candied pecans and the greens were crisp. Oh yeah the dressing was the perfect balance to round out the fork full. 
Oysters-raw, fresh, succulent
Bread pudding-also did not disappoint! 

Mussels- The guys next to us all had a large bowl each and they said they were phenomenal. 

Tip-make a reservation-especially for dinner. 

Well done! Every time we come to NOLA this will always be our MUST HAVE!

You really cannot dine at any John Besh restaurant and be disappointed so no surprise here, this review is a 5 star review! John Besh does french very well!

I was so excited to dine here. Not only is it led by a renowned chef, but it is also very conveniently located. It was walking distance for us, but if you get on the trolley, you can get here easily as it is right on St. Charles. 

With almost 2000 reviews, I cannot add much except to say that they do accommodate vegetarians. Our server said that the chef cooks up a vegetarian platter every night. Mine was full of flavorful veggies, pasta, and a lovely sauce. Our wine pairing was spot on, and everything was absolutely delectable. With a table of 4, we got two desserts: Gâteau Basque and the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Crème Brûlée and split them. 

If you want a fine dining experience in NOLA, rush to Luke. You cannot go wrong!

2nd visit after being away from New Orleans 43 years. This ambiance is reminiscent  of a bistro in Paris of Belgium. The menu was very New Orleans and European French, Alsace, Brussels, Savoy. I had a lifetime favorite Moules Frites. which is a standby favorite from travel through Brussels. Great Souvenir. The wine I chose was the Sancerre. The Croque Monsieur , Was there for Brunch before the Football game. Outstanding experience.

We came here for a 3 days trip and we been to Luke twice, one for valentine dinner and one before we backed to NY. This is the best restaurant in New Orleans, the most delicious oyster we had, Kumamoto oyster is $5.25 each, so worth it!! We had dozen of them, fried oysters are good as well. We also love the chicken/rabbit liver, and Brussels sprouts! Highly recommend, you won't regret it!!

This place was so good I went here twice when I was in New Orleans last summer.   Once for their surprisingly reasonable Happy Hour ($.50 oysters!) and once for a high end, celebratory dinner.   As someone mentioned, the portions are mostly large enough to share and so tasty you will want to have some of ever

This place was great! Atmosphere was wonderful too. I give it four stars simply because the oysters were not the greatest. Small and bland. Otherwise, their Luke burger was delicious and they had a wonderful Strawberry "shortcake" that was out of this world. It even had freeze dried berries and other wonderful toppings.
I was not disappointed. My cocktail was good and my meal was good. Ordered the soft shell crab. Delicious!!! Will come back.

Excellent food and experience. However, a non main server, had a snarky comment after my friend used a knife to eat something, he said "knives are for cutting bro". Didn't need to be said and was rude.

Great drinks too!

Greet food but the service is terrible. .we cant eat pork and we ordered the shrimp and grits after the waiter assured to us that they can do it without. Guess what..other waiter brought the order and said without pork but it has. We returned it and after few minutes they brought us one as ordered. Normal restaurants send a manger to apologize or get the order off the check or at least provide something complimentary. ..this place did nothing of that...

We came here for happy hour (every day 3-6 pm) because they have 50 cent oysters. We had a group of 6 and the two guys LOVE oysters, so they ordered 2 dozen off the bat and added another dozen right before 6 pm. The oysters took a while, but they seemed fresh and they devoured them. During happy hour, the rail drinks, beers, wine and cocktails were also half off. We each ordered a cocktail as they had some pretty interesting drinks. 

The girls ordered a half dozen oysters and we all shared 4 orders of fries. I REALLY enjoyed the fries; sadly I could not stop eating them. They are thinner cut fries that are golden and crispy. And the amount of saltiness was also perfect. We ordered 2 at first but after everyone kept chowing down, we had to order 2 more. This is definitely a great place to go for happy hour!

We stopped by for dinner, but filled up on appetizers. The service was excellent. We had the seafood platter and the rabbit and chicken liver pate. The oyster, peel off shrimp, and tuna were delicious. I am not a mayonnaise fan, so the lump crab was just OK. The pate with the in-house made marmalades and mustards was excellent. Finally the French 75 was the best I have ever had.

My first Yelp review and I think this place is worthy to be my first! Haha :) 

First of all, we came during HH and they had 75 cent oysters and half off on fried oysters. Also half off on wine, beer, cocktails - great deals! We tried the raw and fried oysters; usually I'm not a fan of fried oysters but they were good!

Our waitress was attentive and helpful, service was wonderful. I wish I had remembered her name, she was sweet! I've never been interested in trying grits, I even asked our waitress what grits were and she had me interested enough to split an entree with my friend. And those shrimp and grits were amazing!

We're from Texas so we would definitely recommend this place~

Luke never disappoints. I go crazy over their Brussels sprouts and get them literally every time I go there. I've always enjoyed my meals, service is consistently good and their deserts are amazing. I do like sitting in the upper area better, it's more quaint and not as noisy.

We got to Luke about 8:30pm on a weeknight. It was about 1/2 full-quite impressive- considering a movie production had been filming above the restaurant all day and still took up all the  street parking with their trucks. We started with the fried oyster, bacon, romaine and avocado salad. The dressing was a peppery and creamy. The bacon is from their own hand raised pork and I am salivating at the remembrance of it now. The oysters were perfectly cooked. Then on to a 10oz. hamburger (they split the plate for me and my husband), perfectly cooked, oozing with cheese, that amazing bacon and carmelized onions. The kitchen also gave each of us a tin of thin fries-delicious!  I was extremely impressed with the service. Not overbearing but right on the spot for keeping our drinks full and the food timed. New Orleans is not known for very good service but we got it at Luke.
We dined here for the 2nd time last night and were seated right away!  The waitress and host staff were super friendly and the sushi was fresh and delicious!
This restaurant was fabulous for breakfast! Everything was delicious.  Although pricey, the shrimp and grits was amazing. A bit on the salty side, this dish was amazing comfort food.

Whenever I am in New Orleans this is one of my go to spots for Happy Hour.  $.75 cent oysters, (was .50 cents 4 years ago).  Beer is half off as well, $3 bucks.  Very nice interior and the staff is always friendly and helpful.  I will keep going back.

Wanted to try the happy hour on the recommendation of friends/locals. The service was somewhat cold and unfriendly. The Happy Hour oysters are a great price but they quite large - not everyone's favorite. Jumbo shrimp were really rubbery and hard to get out of the shell. Sour cocktail, excellent; fries, good; vegetable sides, okay. We didn't particularly like the atmosphere or the service, so we'll be investigating other oyster happy hours.

Philippe was initially a little perplexed by the umlaut,the odd maitre d'/manager interaction about urination at the hostess stand and not getting seated right away in a mostly empty restaurant at 1030pm. But the shrimp and grits made his knees weak with pleasure.

Food was delicious!  Don't miss the jalapeño grits!  I had the Cochon de Lait Pressed Sandwich it was big enough that I took half home with me.  My husband ordered from the express menu and really enjoyed the Jambalaya and bisque.  


We went during the week around 2:00 and were sat immediately at a table.  There were several other open tables available.

Upon finding out that we were celebrating a recent return from a military deployment the staff and chef went above and beyond to ensure that we had one of the most memorable nights of our lives! After sampling a majority of the menu, we can honestly say that there is nothing bad that you can pick out. Each appetizer, entree and dessert picked out was better than the last and our waiter was able to pair our wine with our selected entrees perfectly. We can't thank the staff and chef enough and we appreciate everything they did for us. Anyone looking for a restaurant in New Orleans should put this at the top of their list!

Very nice.  I ordered a hamburger with no tomato and when it came with the tomato on it, the maître d' was there in a heart beat and offered free wine for the error.  Came back later to apologize again.  Absolutely superior service.  BTW,  food'a really great too!

They had the best menu during our trip to New Orleans. The shrimp and grits was absolutely amazing! The staff were light hearted and so welcoming. They made great suggestions and everything was perfect. The crab and cheese appetize was absolutely delicious. I wish I had more time while I was here to stop there again.

This is our go to restaurant after Mardi Gras.  We started with the peach bourbon smash during the 3-6 happy hour.  Tasty!  Next was the jumbo lump crab ravigote which has a kick of horseradish.  The soft shell crab BLT is devine because it marries bacon with a perfectly fried soft shell crab.  The fries a perfect because they are fried in duck fat.  We closed out with fried oysters and the brussel sprouts.  All of which were delicious!  U can't beat the prices either...total tab was

The happy hour special of 50 cent oysters, which is daily, 3-6PM, is awesome, and that is the best thing about this place.  Oysters were fresh, great flavor, and you can't beat the price.  

However, the other food we tried there was only OK.  The fries had good flavor, but were super soft which is not my preference for fries.  The Salad Luke was overly dressed so the dressing overpowered any other flavors in the salad.  We also tried the gumbo, which was good, but not fantastic.  

I would totally go back for the happy hour and so I will likely try other items on their menu, but I think their oysters is really the only reason to come to this restaurant.

We were blown away by Luke. We came here just for the happy hour since it looked like a cool place, and ended up staying for dinner and coming back the next night. The happy hour is one of the best in town, both for the food/drinks and the price. Definitely get the oysters.

The dinner menu was also great, although the tarte flambe wasn't quite authentic. Other than that, everything was great and very reasonably priced. Service was also great, and I especially loved the interior and atmosphere. 

They take reservations and I would highly suggest it since it can get busy pretty fast. I will be coming back for sure!

I needed to catch a quick lunch before a flight home, and I stumbled upon this cute place. The waiter recommended that I get the chicken biscuit meal and I was not disappointed!

It was a huge, soft and buttery biscuit with fried chicken and honey all over it. It was wonderful in every way!

Service was quick and attentive! I highly recommend this restaurant for your perusal.
Awesome place.  Tradition New Orleans food  the best oysters in the world  fast friendly service

Lüke is an incredible deal for happy hour, and the best damned oysters I have ever had.

Mrs. R. did the research for our trip to New Orleans, and she spotted that Lüke has a great happy hour special -- $0.75 oysters on the half shell, $1.25 fried oysters, and half-price cocktails.  She's not one for oysters or most seafood, but she thought she would take one for the team.  

First bit of advice -- get a reservation.  Mrs. R. called around 2.30 and she was still able to get a reservation for us at 3.00 (I do not recommend calling this late, it just worked out for us).  When we got to Lüke at 3.00, a table was ready for us, but folks who were walking in off the street just then to get a table were being told that they were booked up until at least 4.30; and, while the bar is open seating, it was absolutely packed.

Second bit of advice -- get the raw and the fried oysters.  The raw are absolutely gonzo, they were glistening and fresh and were gigantic.  Coupled with the traditional accoutrements of horseradish and ketchup for you to mix into your own personal blend of cocktail sauce, they are a fantastic treat; and for $9 / 12 they're a steal.  

While I might be a big fan of raw oysters, I'm somewhat cool to fried oysters.  It's always seemed to me that battering and frying oysters robs them of their character and they're transformed into a mere vehicle for oil-crisped batter and dipping sauces.  These fried oysters were not those flavorless husks.  Probably because they started as the gigantic monsters that are shucked for the half-shell, each of the fried oysters is a well-balanced product of fried crispness and soft, buttery oyster.  As I mentioned, Mrs. R. set up this excursion so that I could get some fresh oysters, but she absolutely fell in love with the fried oysters.  Whether fried or raw, all of the oysters were so good that we ordered a dozen of each as a second round. 

In addition to the special on oysters, the cocktail menu also features half-price drinks during happy hour.  Mrs. R. had a delicious Sazerac that had a lovely balance of liquor and bitters.  I had a mint julep, and though it did not come in the traditional cup, it did have a generous punch of bourbon, and a whole handful of fresh mint to accompany the crushed ice and simple syrup.  Delicious.

We liked the happy hour at Lüke so much that while we were eating it, we were already devising plans on how we could make it back over multiple afternoons during our stay to enjoy more oysters and drinks.

I had Cosi before, but not recently and not.at this location. My lunch experience was ok, and nothing to rave about. 

We ordered a basil chicken sandwich, which was very tasty, but the portion is small. They were very stingy with the chicken and spread in between the flat bread. The whole sandwich cost like $9.

We also ordered an Adoba lime chicken salad for $10. It was tasty and large. No complaints except they gave me all lettuce in my salad; wished it could have been  mixed greens.
What a great meal.   The waitstaff was on par.   Had an absolute blast and lovely meal.  Thank you!

Was in town for a bit, and made it my mission to stuff myself as often as possible with as much food as was in sight.

Great location near downtown, and the French Quarter. Trendy vibe. 

There were 4 of us, Kim was our server. She was great. Her prancing around the restaurant makes me chuckle to think back. She talked highly of the head chef Besh. 

Our food selection was a bourgeois for my tastes so I will give it a 4. But many things: delightful and attentive service, kitchen with large windows so I could ensure my cooks weren't intentionally doing malice after I screwed our order up, and great prices.

Apps: Some pizza with bacon on it- delicious. We got the Pate, and I've never enjoyed pate, and believe it to be acquired taste. We hardly touched it.

Wine: Pouilly fuisse- FANTASTIC with all of our dishes. A second bottle made it to our table, and we all looked at each other like 'who ordered this'? But did we complain? Hell No. I wish I had a glass of this in my face right now, and at $52- great.

Entrees: We got the Shrimp & grits. I've never had grits before, but from what I've envisioned- they don't normally taste like this. WOW.  Market Fish was Mahi-Mahi. Holy toledo. Do this, now. 

Dessert- something mousse. Mehh

THEY SPLIT ALL OF OUR ENTREES. Good luck finding an establishment this preppy to do that for 4 people.

I am a huge John Besh Fan and this was very close to our hotel so we had to dine in. I went with a few friends who arent as big of a foodie as I am so I was the one that was the most excited. I started off with a cup of the gumbo and when it came out and I tried it I realized I messed up by not getting a bowl instead. For my entree I had to try the Shrimp and grits so I went for it.. It came in a cast iron bowl, shrimp was cooked to perfection, the grits had jalapeno's in it, I believe and the sauce on top was simply amazing.. For Dessert I had the bourbon creme brulee, it came with cookies baked in house and fresh strawberries on top... The whole meal was simply perfect and if I ever visit new orleans again, this is a must stop!!

On my recent trip to New Orleans I found myself wandering near the French Quarter looking for a nice meal. The wait times at every stop were over an hour, even for a single diner.  When I popped into Luke, initially the answer was the same. But I could see the place was packed and the food looked delicious so I asked if I could wait for a seat at the bar. 
I often find eating at the bar a doorway to an excellent meal, as the bartender, wait staff and patron usually are spot on in their recommendations. Luke was no exception. The bartender steered me towards the Gulf Puppy Drum but recommended I order it "poor and dirty" - blackened. The patron next to me said the jalapeno cheese grits were to die for...so I did both.  The grits came in their own little cast iron skillet and were surrounded in a crispy coating on the bottom and luscious cheese on top. A meal in and of itself. Not to be outdone, the drum fish was perfectly blackened and served over a bed of roasted root veggies. Holy cow was this dish an explosion of flavor.  I was so overjoyed that I let anyone within earshot hear my satisfaction, over and over again. The menu suggests lump crab on top of the drum, but frankly I think it would have overpowered the taste of this impeccably prepared gulf fish. I was too stuffed for the bread pudding, which looked scrumptious!
I know where I will be dining on my next trip to New Orleans...Luke.

When a place is that good, (well, and that close to the hotel *literally across the street*), you gotta go more than once amirite? 

Originally planned to just stop by Luke's during their infamous HH (3pm-6pm) and thennnn head to the dinner ressie. Welp, that didn't happen. The crazy fun bar side vibes had us sticking around for the long haul. 

We sat bar side on a Thursday afternoon around 5pm, to a pretty busy crowd. Lucked out on grabbing the last two seats. Proceeded to order 3 dozen raw oysters (obviously), half a dozen fried oysters, and a couple of drinks to round it out. I started with the door#three, which frankly, I wasn't crazy about. Flashbacks of my early 20s drinking cheap mixed drinks is what it tasted like IMO.

When we finally decided to cancel the dinner res, and stick around, the second round included the "ohhh snappp, gingerrrr"...and yes, you have to say it just like that. The bartender gave me a Z formation snap to go with it. I'm not saying that's what made the second drink better, but maybe I am. Haha 

In the end, the food and drinks were delish. I definitely came back a second time before leaving for the airport. Cheap, delish HH can't be missed! The waitstaff and bartenders are everything sassy and sweet. At times, a smidge overboard on the sass, that my dad didn't pick up on all the time. There were a handful of awkward "huh?" moments, and some plain just awkward moments in general. And for all of that, 4 stars. Would I come back though? Hell yeah.

My husband and I stumbled (literally?) upon this place when last in new orleans and were so impressed. We like to share and split a entree - we each got a full plate served to us. I'm also pretty sure they put something illegal in the pate, it was too good. The service was some of the best I've had and I'm picky about this....Can you open one in Baltimore please?!

Best combo - oysters - fish special (drum)
- then to top it all off the bread pudding with vanilla ice cream on top. Great small place to enjoy dinner at. Great service our waiter was nice and friendly and always checking up on us. I recommend getting reservation early so that there not much of a wait.
We stopped by for lunch and had a great meal as was expected. Good friendly service. Really enjoyed the burger- cooked right- fresh ground- flavorful bacon.  On my list to try breakfast there.

Luke serves my favorite oyster happy hour by far. Half-off cocktails and 75 cent oysters EVERY..DAY 3-5pm. I'm sold. I've always passed by this place and have always seen lines, but there is plenty of seating and I've never had to week. The happy hour oysters are farm raised but they are always clean fresh. The happy hour oysters go either raw or fried, with the fried being a little more money. Can't go wrong either way. By the way, I suppose December and January are the oyster seasons.

I've also had the fried quail appetizer which was solid and like chicken tenders, but I would definitely try others options next time. The schnitzel they serve looks amazing but I have yet to try that. As for cocktails, I have tried the French 75 and door#3 which seem to be the customer favorites. Their cocktails don't have too much ice and have the right balance for flavor and alcohol content.  Everything at Luke is consistent since I have been here 3 times.  Excellent, attentive service and impeccable menu. Luke is definitely a must-try in New Orleans. It's classic.

So thrilled with this restaurant!! Being here with 8 other wily women from Texas, and I know we ain't the easiest on a server. But my 87 year old grandmother has horrible back problems and was visibly in pain, and our sweet server brought her a pillow!!! The thoughtfulness of that gesture and the absolutely DELICIOUS food (Brussels sprouts omgggggg) will be the reason I tell all my friends Lüke's is the place to go when visiting New Orleans!!

Amazing! Possibly the best place to eat in New Orleans! I have been here several times and everything I've ordered doesn't disappoint! Today I had to Luke Burger, the photo I attached doesn't even begin to do it justice. ENJOY!

I got   the choucroute garnie maison, which was a mix of ham leg, pork belly, and bratwurst. I started with the crawfish bisque. All was fantastic, until I got an allergic reaction to the bisque a couple of hours after dinner. I am not allergic to crawfish but I am allergic to crab. So warning, other seafood makes its way into the crawfish bisque. My friend got shrimp and grits and reported that it was great.

Service was great- food came out fast and staff was super friendly. I had the shrimp etouffee which is usually with rice but they do it here with pasta (cavatelli). I substituted the shrimp for chicken cause im not a big shrimp person. I asked for the chicken well done -im super picky with my chicken and it was not well done at all. To be fair, i did change the plate and the sauce was awesome and my boyfriend said the chicken was fine so i guess it just comes down to taste. French fries were amazing- super crispy!! As an appetizer, boyfriend had the p&j oysters which were delicious - i dont even like oysters and i thought they were so good. For dinner he had the jumbo Louisiana shrimp which he loved. Its a smaller portion so order accordingly. We both had dirty martinis which were ok- def had way better but not terrible. For dessert we had creme brule and bread pudding - sooo good. Overall great place but very limited menu.
The roasted beet salad is superb; the crab and corn bisque was great. Everyone in our party loved their dishes.

It was what I expected and more. Had shrimp and grits, Bloody Mary and a dozen Kumamoto oysters for breakfast. Service was excellent! I suck at reviews so just take my word and most everyone else's. Must stop for any foodie!

I can't think of any restaurant that is so good that I can serve breakfast lunch and dinner and be spot on.
I could attempt to sing about specific dishes which were good.
That would be impossible just everything was five star excellent

I've always enjoyed REI, even though I find them a bit over priced.
I've been in this Boise location quite a few times and I get really annoyed. I get the vibe that because I'm young and probably look like I have no money, no one wants to help me. In the Spokane store (where I live), the employees are much more helpful. Sometimes I feel the need to beat them off with a stick. Not in Boise though, I practically had to beg to be helped. I hate that. 
Other than that, its a nice store.
Ordered the half Greek salad. A lot of the lettuce was so soggy & almost algae like. I picked out a lot of it but it was not appetizing.

Meh will do in a pinch but that's about it.  Their bagels are really dense and often times too hard although reasonably priced at 99 cents or $8.99 for a dozen. I haven't tried anything else. 

Staff is for the most part nice. The space is nice as well.

Oyster happy hour for the WIN! 75 cent raw oysters, $1.25 fried oysters, and half off cocktails! Our table definitely did HH right, with 2 dozen oysters and two drinks each. 
The service was great - they really made sure we enjoyed the drinks and dishes (read: oysters) we ordered.  If I lived in the area, I'd come for oyster happy hour on the regular - highly recommend.

Of all the restaurants I visited while in New Orleans, Luke was probably my favorite. I made a reservation for dinner here at 5pm for a party of 10. They sat us in a private room which was a nice plus and as usual we ordered a variety of dishes to share: 

*Crispy Brussel Sprouts - served with toasted almonds, honey, and milk barn cheese. This was a table favorite, really crispy and flavorful. 

*Pate of Louisiana Rabbit and Chicken Livers - served with country bread croutons. I loooved this dish, the pate was so delicious and served with two types of jam and dijon mustard. 

Boudin Stuffed Pork Chop - served with bourbon peach glaze, grilled peaches over tomato and summer squash. Delicious glaze and the porkchop was cooked to perfection. 

*Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" served over roasted jalapeno cheese grits, andouille and green onion sausage. The grits were AMAZING, arguably the best grits I had on this trip.  

Luke Burger - served with Allan benton's bacon (idk who or what that is), caramelized onions, tomato and cheese. Good burger (home of the good burger can I take your order?). 

*Shrimp Etouffee - cavatelli pasta served with shrimp etouffee, heirloom tomatoes and garlic sauce. The pasta was the perfect texture and the shrimp etouffee was creamy and delicious. 

Tasso Rubbed Grilled Swordfish - served over a bed of fresh corn, fire roasted peppers and topped with a cilantro lime buerre blanc. I didn't get a good bite of this to leave a proper review, but most people seemed to like it. 

Raw Oysters - surprisingly I think I like raw oysters on the west coast are better. For New Orleans I would go with the fried oysters or specialty oysters. 

*Fried Oysters - this was one of the big highlights of the table as well. The oysters are fried to perfection and served with an aioli... we ordered 5 of these. 

Not only did we get a private room, the service was top notch and the food was so delicious. Luke staff went above and beyond and comped us 4 bottles of champagne! I have to say, this was by far my favorite experience in New Orleans and I would love to come back to eat those amazing fried oysters again. Until next time Luke!

OMG, everything I had was amazing! Service was good, a little on the slow side but server was entertaining!! I had the court-bouillon and it was OMG good!! I also had the special selection oysters and they were amazing!!! They had blue points which is one of my favs!!!! The hubby got the burger and he said it was in his top 3 BEST burgers!! And the man LOVES his burgers!!!!! Oh and the crawfish bisque is pretty freakin' good as well!! I'm still high from happiness so excuse my exclamation marks!

Everything here was pretty great! The service was pretty good - a little slow, but seemed almost like they were letting us enjoy our meal. They use those stupid tiny water glasses that have to be refilled every two sips - felt bad for the servers.

We shared a seafood platter - 5 stars, I had seafood gumbo - 5 stars, my mom had the beet salad - surprisingly 5 stars as well. My dad has a burger and it was not that great.. the fries were kind of limp and soggy. We also tried to split a Flammenkuchen and it was weird and tasted like burnt things. Would not get that again.

Finished off with some bread pudding - pretty tasty!

Overall, good - just stick to the seafood - you're in New Orleans after all!

Perfect place. Great 7 day happy hour with oysters, liquor, beer and wine and great food. Nice establishment, staff, menu, quality, prices etc. 

5 stars fo sho

Fast, easy, a little pricy for an entire meal with sides and a drink but it's close and comfy food. I had the pesto chicken melt and it was amazing! My husband had the veggie sandwich and he loved it! Great place for a quick and delicious brunch or lunch!

I snuck into Luke's just before the end of breakfast service. Ends at 11am. Look at the nice crawfish omelette with greens! It tasted wonderful. I feel like the greens with a delicate dressing was almost a European touch. Had just regular black coffee. Very strong but not bitter!! Great service, tasty breakfast!

Having been told that going to a John Besh restaurant was standard procedure for visiting NOLA, I made plans to get over here during their oyster happy hour (3 - 6pm, every day). I definitely appreciate that they keep their happy hour going on weekends. However, the service during happy hour was pretty slow. 

We sat down and ordered drinks and a dozen oysters, and the oysters took nearly 20 minutes. When my oyster buddy ordered another drink (after waiting awhile to make eye contact and flag someone down), he had to wait 15+ minutes before it came out (and he had to ask about it to follow up, since it was taking so long). It definitely seemed like staff was around, but we were largely ignored, perhaps because it was happy hour and we ordered so little? 

However, the reason this review isn't less than 3 stars (because seriously, waiting nearly 20 minutes for a mint julep is obscene) is because when the bill came... it was $16. TOTAL. $16 for two nice, strong drinks and a dozen delicious oysters. The service was crappy, but at $8 a piece, I might be able to live with that. I just think I'd check out the other oyster happy hours about town and see how they compare before coming back.

Is Luke's showing their age?  Came here a couple years ago and had their brussels sprouts side dish. It was so good; we ordered seconds. But I guess since then Brussel sprouts inspired dishes have been popping up at many restaurants.   

So ordering it tonight was nothing greater than what you find at other restaurants that have a little creativity.


Brussel sprouts: very good
Drum fish:  okay, small portion Not that much flavor
Bread pudding: good; probably best part of meal.

If you're looking for incredible oysters without dealing with the lines or the general debauchery of the French Quarter, this is the place to be. Oysters here are huge and a good value for the price. Luke is well lit and has a very old school, upper crust feel to it. Sharp contrast from what you find just across Canal. Staff is friendly and engaging at the bar. Highly recommend the hot buttered crawfish bread, which comes slathered in burrata. Quite the treat. Highly recommended next time you are in New Orleans.

Food is amazing. Only service was very slow when we stop for breakfast. But during happy hour, oyster for 0.50 cents .... you cant beat that. Next time I'm in New Orleans, i will be eating there again.

I generally love Panera and go as often as once per week, picking up through the drive-thru. This morning I went earlier than normal, 11am and ordered the pick-two avocado BLT and cheese broccoli soup. The soup was cold and the tomatoes on my sandwich were the ends. Just gross. Flush that $10 order down the drain...

Time to start my NOLA review barrage!

We wanted to check out a John Besh joint while in New Orleans, and Luke and its happy hour had a decent value. Thus it was our first stop immediately upon arrival.

Unfortunately, none of us ate raw oyster ($0.50 each from 3-6 pm), so that novelty was lost on us. However, it's half-price drinks, whether at the bar or at a table. Very nice!

Luke itself seems like a place that's confused as to whether it's a restaurant or a bar. It ends up coming across a place that looks like a fancy eatery in an amusement park. I think it could fit right in at EPCOT. The service, uniformly, was pretty bad. The hostess had a bit of a pointed attitude when we were picking between table or bar. The bartender completely ignored us when we first sat at the bar. And the waitress, overall, was just average with nary a smile.

The food itself is quite delicious. We just missed the lunch menu, but the dinner prices aren't wholly ridiculous when you're just sampling. We started with a dozen jumbo shrimp from the "raw bar," which were huge, well-seasoned, and quite possibly the best seafood we had in New Orleans. That was complemented by a side of frites, well crisped and salted.

That was followed by a hearty bowl of gumbo, because, well, we had just made it into New Orleans. And in NOLA, you gotta try the gumbo. The stock was quite tasty, but a bit light on the additionals. We ended with a bockwurst, a truly large portion of wurst that completely stuffed the table and is great value at just $10.

On the drink side, the girlfriend went with a streetcar, well made, and I tried the custom-brewed amber. Yup, custom-brewed beers make a nice touch.

While the service was unimpressive and the decor was not to my liking, I'm a fan of the food. A 3:00 pm happy hour seems like your best bet (dinner menu starts at 4:00), but if you can't make it, they have a decently priced lunch and brunch menu. I'd skip a normal dinner here and make the reservation at August instead.

Great service, great food, great daily happy hour (pleasant surprise when we arrived!), and it is farm to table. Had the Luke burger, half dozen oysters, and salad Luke and split it all.  Will definitely return when visiting New Orleans!

Located within Hilton Hotel, I made a reservation via opentable app. They were busy and people were having a great time. They were a bit too loud after too few many drinks.

I asked for a quite table I saw in the back but they didn't want one person to sit there.

Server was friendly and fairly prompt.

I tried gumbo and oysters for a small dinner. Gumbo wasn't what I remembered as a traditional gumbo. I am not a gumbo expert but it wasn't what I remembered from 10 years ago.

I arrived after a happy hour but I heard they have a good happy hour menu here.

I suspect this company collects money for diagnostic fees without having the man power to actually conduct the work. It's been 72hrs after their visit and no contact or quote has been  provided.  I've made 3 phone calls and keep getting told they'll call back. I was told verbally that a gas valve needs to be replaced and would cost $1000. Gimme a break.

Tried this for breakfast and it will be my go to.  Don't understand why people are waiting in line at mediocre tourist traps for breakfast when they can enjoy a fantastic meal in a beautiful setting with excellent professional service. Had the crispy chicken biscuit served with fluffy grits and homemade bread and butter pickles.  It was excellent.  Service was outstanding from the moment we walked in and were greeted by two friendly hostesses.  And they take reservations for breakfast.  Try this place out if you are looking to start the day with southern comfort food.

Nothing special , average classic American concept food . It is not a restaurant gives you good after delish memorable   taste . You can experience this restaurant for one time and nothing special about it

I went to Luke with fairly high expectations.  The food was actually very good, but, the atmosphere was far from what I was expecting.  I had heard Luke had a nice Charcuterie dish and it was fantastic.  However, the atmosphere made my wife and I feel like we were eating at a diner .
