There were plenty of people at the restaurant, and again, the food was outstanding, it was just all in the presentation of the feel of the restaurant.  I would give the food a 5 star, but, the restaurant only a 3 overall due to the atmosphere of the place.  If you are looking for high end food with a very casual atmosphere, this is the place!

Raw oysters are very good and a great deal during happy hour.  The fried oyster salad was a lil heavy on the dressing and the fried oyster maybe a bit too salty for some folks.  The texture, however, was perfect - not to bready and just the right amount of crisp and delicacy.  One of them came with a bonus, a small pearl!!!  Now where are the crap tables at!?!  I have to come back and try the bread pudding.

The food, atmosphere and service are all excellent. If you're cost-conscious, you need to pay close attention to the menu and/or ask the waiter. I didn't expect a glass of beer would cost $6.25 or that when the waiter talked us into trying West Coast oysters, they would cost nearly twice as much as Louisiana oysters. Even so, worth checking out.

Th food is really excellent, but the service is damn bad. We literally waited an hour and even not got our appetizer, and there are still several vacant seats (not in a full situation). They also treated ppl differently! (Unbelievable) They only gave complementary mochi dessert to the Caucasian customers......really unbelievable

I too would love to leave negative stars. Do not use Fahrenheit, ever. They're fraudulent, dishonest, and do not perform anything close to acceptable work.

Their most recent fraudulent business practice was sending me an "invoice" for $200. We didn't use them nor did we owe them anything; when I called I was told it was the amount we "would owe" if we chose to purchase an annual service plan. No where on the "invoice" did it say that this was optional or that it was for a renewal--it was purely an attempt to trick customers into paying for something they have no intention of paying for.

We got burned by Fahrenheit last year when they charged us $900 to fix a perfectly fine furnace. Our heat was out and Fahrenheit told us that it needed new parts and service, and they assured us that it was 100% the problem with the furnace parts. I asked him specifically to check the gas pressure coming into the house and he assured me the pressure was fine. We accepted, but when the heat didn't go back on (surprise!) they told us to contact our gas company. The original parts were perfectly fine and Fahrenheit refused to issue a refund. PGW came that night and fixed the low pressure gas line which was actually the issue.

Stay FAR AWAY from this terrible company. They have poor morals, poor business practices, and they take advantage of consumers. Be aware of any positive reviews online here or elsewhere, they've been known to post fake reviews.

STAY AWAY.

Great brunch! The shrimp and grits are excellent although I have had better in Savannah. The grits in their own were quite tasty. The chicken and biscuits with tabasco syrup was ridiculously good.  The fried chicken was light and soft with lots of flavour. Service was also great.

Disclaimer: This review is solely based upon a few cocktails, oysters on the half shell, and pomme frites.

  I enjoyed Luke's happy hour. As my dining companion put it, "Luke is the John Besh restaurant for the working class." Nestled nicely in the dining dearth of the CBD, seer sucker clad businessmen and women are of great attendance here. Oysters are 50 cents, cocktails (originally priced under 10) are half off between the hours of 3-6 pm.
  The champagne au peche, St. Charles Streetcar cocktails were tasty, but not as stiff as I would have preferred. The oysters were fresh but lacked anything to accompany them (such as crackers). We asked for bread and solved this problem. The pomme frites rank third on my pomme frites Nola list.

  Overall, very enjoyable.

Luke was a great restaurant to visit. Definitely a higher end restaurant and the food there was likewise matched to my expectation! The waiters were very kind and well presented. The food did take a bit longer to come out, but I think it's safe to say they take a lot of time to make sure the food is well prepared.

A platter of oysters was what my friends and I started out with and it was reallly good. Very fresh and their cocktail sauce was exceptional too.

The Brussels sprouts were cooked well. I'd highly recommend getting this dish. It's a dish mixed with honey and cheese which was balanced well. No other flavor overpowered the other and I thought it was a very well rounded dish.

The mussels and fries were very flavorful. The garlic butter sauce was fantastic with the fries that complemented this dish so well.

The shrimp and grits were out of this world. This is another must get dish from this restaurant. It's just a dish you can't do justice with words.

This place is very well known for their banana bread pudding and definitely lives up to its reputation. This is a must get dessert!

Overall, I really enjoyed dining at Luke, I think it's best if you can go with a group to try out different dishes!

Go here for the happy hour and say hi to Jelly and Uncle Phil. 

Rabbit and chicken liver pate was bomb with the baguette

Upon arrival we were greeted by an extremely friendly and professional staff (Daisha). The main lobby is connected through the pet supply store. The lobby was very clean and large which can accommodate several customers and their pets.  The initial paperwork was easy and comprehensive (one page!). Our wait time was about 15 minutes and we were really impressed with Christie and Dr. Reddy. They took their time to complete a thorough examination and answer all of our questions. They walked us through each step and demonstrated a well of knowledge. We are really happy with our choice of a veterinary service.

Wow! So much seafood and i want it all! The sampler platter is out of this world.

While staying at the Intercontinental for a week, I craved this place daily. Stopping in for fresh oysters, sometimes dressed and fried. I felt bad for the restaurant in the hotel that offered oyster deals as i walked across the street to Luke.

Everything I ate here was fantastic! The waitstaff, bartender, and oyster shuckers all had great attitudes and I swear I saw the owner treating some deserving man to the meal of his life on the house. Must have brought out 5 different dishes for him while we sat beside in awe. 

Happy hour deals really make it worth the while. I wish Luke was in my neighborhood.

Luke..P&J Oysters, Shrimp, Duck with Crispy Rice  and Etouffee!!

Luke is one of those restaurants that you fall in love with by bookmarking on Yelp after seeing pictures. Then you see more pictures..and more. It gets to the point that every month or so you go back to the bookmark and drool over the pictures. Then you finally make it and the pictures you fell in love with are not even served on the menu anymore. So what do you do?? You order the PJ Oysters, Duck with Crispy Rice and ooh the Etouffee!!!

~The shrimp was amazing. Southern California never 
  would have shrimp as good as Louisiana. The Etouffe 
  was well crafted and prepared.  

~Oysters.. definately the pearl of the restaurant! Baked, 
   Fried and Raw..they are all 5 Stars!

~Tables were tiny and made it difficult to eat with so  
  many dishes on the table. Service was meh.

Overall, I am a fan!

The sandwiches are nice, the coffee was delicious. The sandwiches can only have limited modification. The crowed is local and the service is nice.

the lady behind the counter, helped me find a washroom and was very patient when taking my order. 

this place gets busy on a Sunday morning so, go early and expect to wait in line.

AMAZING!!!

I ordered the fried oysters. It was so good! I never had fried oysters before but the taste of it was delicious. The batter was so crispy and tasty. I ordered half a dozen and wished I ordered more but I ordered shrimp and grits for my entree and didn't want to get so full from it. The shrimp and grits were heavy to eat but I ate the whole thing! It was so flavorful and rich. It was the best shrimp and grits I've ever eaten. I found myself dancing while eating. A habit I have grown accustomed to when eating delicious food. One of my favorite brunches of all time! It is definitely a spot to check when you're visiting New Orleans.

Happy hour review:
OpenTable made reservations a breeze. Happy hour began at 3p, our reservation was for 3:30p. I recommend this as a midday meal, as the food and drink is top-notch, my husband's and my favorite meal of our trip. 
The cocktail menu is strong, featuring perfectly executed classic cocktails. I recommend the French 75 and the Old Fashioned.
The oysters lived up to the hype - $0.75 oysters are delicious, large, fresh. Accoutrement are not lacking - lemon wedges, ketchup, horseradish, saltines. No shame in ordering dozen after dozen. In addition to the fresh oysters, we also tried a half dozen fried oysters. These were the most perfectly seasoned, perfectly fried oysters we'd ever had (and we've had oysters). They're served with a spicy buttermilk aioli - scrumptious! In addition, we shared a crispy brussels salad; as others have shared, this is how brussels sprouts should be done! Delicious!
After our oyster feast, we weren't too hungry. We shared the daily special, a fried chicken served over red beans and rice. I did not have high hopes for this dish, as I perceived the oysters as the main event. Boy was I wrong! The shared dish was served separately plated, each in its own mini cast iron skillet.  Each bite of chicken was spectacular, succulent and flavorful. The beans and rice were perfectly upscaled peasant food and were the best thing we ate all day, perhaps all trip.
Service was excellent. Our servers kept our place settings tidy and our drinks replenished. I recommend dining here during happy hour in a tapas-type mentality, ordering dishes as you decide on them. Dishes were all prepared fairly quickly, and cocktails were there in between "courses." All in all, it allowed us to have a long, luxurious meal at a very smart price.

This is absolutely one of the best restaurants we have been to. Their food and service are amazing. In addition, Rich (our server) was funny and took great care of us. This was our first trip to the city of New Orleans and this restaurant made a great first impression for us and WE ARE DEFINITELY COMING BACK! 

I repeat, the service here is absolutely amazing. Initially, we ordered raw oysters, BBQ pork shank and herb roasted local chicken. Our server Rich made a recommendation for us to try their baked P&J oysters, we were a bit indecisive but Rich said if we did not like them, it would be on him, so we went with his suggestion. When the order came, we tried them and found the baked oysters to be a little bit too salty. Rich not only took them back, he offered to give us both the P&J and raw oysters for free! A man true to his words! We were very thankful. 

A few mins later, he came back, apologized again and made us even a bigger offer. He said since we didn't like the oysters, he would triple what we ordered. We each would get an order of their pork shank and roasted chicken (we are a party of three and that's six entrees)! We didn't know what to say! They definitely put the costumers first and care about the QUALITY of their food. The BBQ pork shank was delicious, the meat was cooked just right, it was tender and juicy. The roasted chicken was very special, and the meat literally melted in my mouth. 

Again, this was one of the best places I have tried. Their quality of food matches with their service and I would recommend to ANYBODY who comes to the city of New Orleans! Rich is awesome! If you get a chance, ask him to be your server, YOU WON'T BE DISAPPOINTED!

All the guys that worked here today were great, they did an oil change for me recommended products that would've helped the engine of my car. They had fast service and were very knowledgeable.  Especially Patrick!  (:
Tasty food and great service. Loved the gumbo! Lauren was the perfect server!! We will be back!

Called in a delivery order at 7pm, it's 8:30pm and I haven't received my food yet. I called the store about 7:45pm they said they were waiting for the delivery driver to return . I only ordered from here because it is Halal but any establishment that goes over an hour to deliver food needs to reevaluate its system. I surely pray my food is worth the wait.

We bought a 2004 Volvo from this dealership, they claimed it had no issues and 
had been in no accidents and it was a completely fine car. We spent 10,000 
dollars after buying it from the dealership for various problems that occurred 
in a few days after buying it. Essentially, they sold us a lemon - and 
according to some reviews we didn't see before, they do this all the time. They 
wouldn't even attempt to assist us after buying the car from them - even if it 
was a few days after buying it. 

For some reason, my review disappeared after they responded.
They say that we bought it for 2,999. Incorrect. They charged us almost 5,000 according to the paperwork we have. We DID contact them after the car was deemed a lemon. They would not accept the return, or assist us. It's "as is." 

They are the fraud. Please do not buy from them. We have contacted several agencies to make sure they get the fines that they deserve.
And seeing how they unprofessionally responded to my post, they know they are in the wrong.

Do not buy from here. At. All.

Visited Hachi on a Sunday evening for dinner. I made a reservation ahead of time so our party of 5 was seated right away. The seating inside the restaurant is a bit small, so I would recommend making a reservation if you're a slightly larger group. We had the vegetable gyoza for our appetizer, which was perfectly crispy on the outside, but nice and soft inside. I had the Tokyo Pearl roll for my entree, which was a perfect combination of flavors and the presentation was nice. There was a large variety of different sushi options, including a lot of vegetarian options! Hachi was definitely one of the best sushi places I've been to, I would highly recommend to anyone in the area

We were seated immediately with a reservation. The food was good, but there are lots of places for good seafood in New Orleans. Despite having two servers I felt like there were long periods of waiting to order, waiting for our drinks, waiting for the plates to be cleared. For the price, I just wanted more.

We went here for m birthday last night in a group of  9 people. Their food and service was by far the best we've ever experienced! And for foodies, that's saying a lot. Every entree was love in our mouths. Our server Timmy Glitter was the sweetest and most accommodating! Thank you Luke for a memorable birthday dinner

Best happy hour! A luxurious and very NoLa experience with perfect oysters and delicious cocktails. FYI- happy hour is offered at the tables in addition to the bar. Good to get there earlier and possibly request a reservation for a time during happy hour.

I love Sonic. All of the local ones around here have closed and I am so glad this one is still open. The servers are all really friendly. They know how to mix their drinks well here too, which can't be said for all Sonics.

Great happy hour oyster deal and drink specials! 75 cent oysters and half off all drinks! You really can't go wrong with either of those. Their happy hour is everyday from 3-6 pm.

The oysters were very fresh and I loved the sauces it came with. One was like a cocktail sauce and the other had a wasabi flavor. Well kept and elegant restaurant with playful waiters!

I went here with my parents for their anniversary and we were so amazed by how delicious the food was! Their deep fried oysters were so cheap during Happy Hour and we kept getting one order after another of it. Their burger is one of the best burgers I've ever had and their pasta is amazing too -- all of their food was impressive. I'd definitely recommend it!

Too bad I wasn't super hungry when it was time to visit Luke, but after stuffing my face at other spots, I didn't have a large appetite. It was definitely one of the best restaurants we visited during our trip, and after sampling some of my partner's food, I could tell everyone was having a great experience.

AMBIANCE is classic style and beauty. Fellas- definitely take the time to wear a nice button down shirt. To give a depiction of their unannounced dress code, the waiters wear tuxedos.

ORDERED stuffed P&J oysters. My partner ordered the pre fixe menu, which included crispy Brussels spouts, shrimp "étouffée", and I believe vanilla bean crème brûlée.

FOOD was solid. The oysters were a little saltier than desired, but still tasty. The Brussels sprouts were INCREDIBLE. Definitely the best I've ever had. Moist and well seasoned with a delicious dressing. The shrimp "étouffée" and dessert were lovely options. 

OVERALL a fantastic four stars. Luke will be on the top of my list the next time I return to New Orleans.

Overpriced touristy fare served up on crisp white table cloth. The waiters are either imbeciles or criminally indifferent; they have the competence and sophistication of C minus middle-school students suffering from chronic ADD. I guess that's what they mean by living in NOLA: working at Luke is the Big Easy. Leave Luke to the wide-eyed travelers from East Cleveland and go to Mother's across the street. Order yourself the Charlie Stevens Bloody Mary. After a visit to Luke, you'll need it.
Awesome experience! The food is great and Mandy, our waitress was amazing. Will definitely come back and recommend it to all our friends

This is an above average restaurant but slightly below excellent. The menu offers different fare than typical New Orleans menus. The Shrimp and Grits seems to be the consistent favorite based upon other Yelp reviews and I can agree the item is good. My guest had the Boudain stuffed lamb chop. The Boudain was good but the lamb chop was overcooked (dry) even after specifically requesting it not be. The crawfish bisque was good but a bit expensive in comparison to others. I don't think you will be disapointed at Luke's but it is not likely you are going to be "wowed" by the dinner menu.

Ohhhh my!! The shrimp n grits were to die for!! I could eat this every day! Tried multiple restaurants and this is the best!! Just a tad but too much cheese, but I pushed that to the side and dug into this baby! You got to go to this place if you're ever in New Orleans.

Luke, you had me at 50 cent oysters. 

Not only are they 50 cents, they are big, beautiful, fresh, and delicious. The happy hour (3pm-6pm) is enough to bring me back.

We arrived 5 minutes early for a 6pm reservation and were seated right away.  The server was awesome and immediately came over to inform us that we could still get in on happy hour if we ordered drinks/oysters right then.

After oysters, we had the assortment of charcuterie which included pate, hog's head cheese, savory marmalade, mustard, and assorted pickles.  All of it was amazing. (Seriously, when did I become someone who likes pate?)

For entrees we had the pork shank and the roasted duck. The pork shank was fantastic although serving it with a bratwurst was a little over the top.  My only criticism about the duck is the salt from the confit seemed a little overpowering, but overall the flavor was really good.

If you are looking for an excellent meal with impeccable service in a very casual environment,  Luke is your place.

Notes:  
-There are very few options for non-carnivorous peeps, so keep that in mind.
-This is going to be a "splurge" meal....I wouldn't count calories.
-Due to its location (attached to the Hilton), expect tourists.

We came here on Sunday 12/14 around 7:30 to celebrate an anniversary. As soon as we sat down, the servers came over to wish us a Happy Anniversary and made us feel welcome. They also served us a champagne toast (we were so grateful!) and not only did they give us well wishes upon arrival, the servers kept checking in, gave recommendations prior to ordering, and when we left, were consistently friendly and smiling. We ordered the following appetizers: baked P&J oysters (6 in an order- they were good but I think we normally prefer them raw - we just wanted to try them since we're from out-of-town); the gumbo (tasty, so much flavor, not overly salty); the small raw seafood platter (Le Petit Plateau de Fruits de Mer) which came with raw clams, raw oysters, a squid/calamari ceviche/antipasto tasting, cooked mussels, and shrimp (if I recall correctly), and we added a half order of the jumbo king crab legs. The seafood platter was good (a good amount for 2 people if you want to try other appetizers). For the main course, I had the grilled louisiana mahi which came with kale chips at the time. The fish was fine (not overly fishy) but perhaps a bit overcooked, and the kale was too salty (felt like you were sticking your tongue in sea salt). My boyfriend ordered the Luke Burger medium rare but it came out medium well-- we didn't want to bother the servers since they were so great but the gumbo was probably the best dish that night. You can't be the service here, I would come back again!

Had one of the absolute best experiences I've ever had getting in oil change ask for Tasha the manager here at this Jiffy Lube they treat military right!!

I highly recommend this specific location!

We were in New Orleans for a girls weekend and happened upon this place for brunch one morning.  The menu looked great so we sat down.   Our server was very attentive and all of the food was great!  I had the fried chicken biscuit.  The jalapeño cheese grits were to die for!  I didn't have one but my friends raved about the bloody Mary's.  Great spot for a nice brunch in NOLA!

We had seen the place on many visits to New Orleans because we always stay right across the street. We decided on our last visit to give it a try for happy hour and we are so glad we did! 

First of all, it's a nice place but approachable, not shorts dining but not suit and tie. Second do yourself a favor and ask if Richie Rich is working, what a guy, he won't let you go wrong and is an absolutely awesome server!

We had the Brussels sprouts, which I can say were hands down some of the best I have ever tasted in my life. Rich and flavorful while maintaining the integrity of a Brussels sprout. We also had the crab dip on Keto friendly shrimp chips thanks to our waiter. We also had a couple glasses of wine before we had to relocate for dinner.

I can tell you we loved our short time here and next time we're in the Big Easy, we will be dining here! It's amazing highly recommend!

Walking into Lüke's is like walking into the past - some decade in the early half of 20th century America - and gives me the urge to take off my fedora and trench coat, even when I'm not wearing one.  Being one who enjoys that era in history, I would come here just to admire the decor, food be damned.  

But luckily, the food is plentiful and quite good.  I had the mussels and could not finish it, they gave me so much.  There's a full bar.  

I have to go back sometime soon because I hear there are 50 cent oysters during happy hour!  

The only downside to this restaurant is parking, since it's located in an area where there's not a lot of street parking.  It's walking distance from the French Quarter though, so if you're ever there on vacation or for business, Lüke is definitely worth checking out.

The servers are just terrible at what they do... You are seen by them in which they don't ask if you've been helped or not yet. Having to ask for your order to be taken after 20-30 minutes of sitting down is ridiculous! The next morning my family & I had an upset stomach with diarrhea in which it was food poisoning smh. Never are we coming back especially with the service given & food quality.

Great food and excellent prices for a higher end restaurant.   The give you a lot of food on appetizers we got.:  onion tart.  Brussels sprouts and beet salad.   We were pretty full before entrees came    Soft shell crab blt excellent and came with great fries.   Gumbo and etoufe also tasty.   Service a little spotty but it was a crazy busy night

I came here for two things: OYSTERS and HAPPY HOUR.    

The oysters were fantastic and amazingly priced at $6/dz.  They were quickly shucked at the bar and served up promptly.  I had wine by the glass, which was 1/2 off.   

I agree with Jessica- the wine served in a juice glass and the napkins that look like bar towels did throw me off a bit- but again, I was really just here for oysters, so that towel went to good use.  

I have heard good things about some of the other menu options, so I will definitely be coming back to check those out as well.  

Thanks Luke- I shall return soon!

Oh How I wish, I wish I had a Lüke where in Denver.  First I been wanting to go here for a while now and follow Chef John Besh . I guess I could fly to the Luke's in San Antonio, it's closer. lol
Well we got up early to get here for breakfast on the day we were flying out Monday August 3rd, 2015.  It was about maybe 8am when we got there and looked like we were the only customers so far.  It looks like a really fancy place, but they are very nice and the prices are not expensive at all and the portions are great, but the quality and taste is OUT OF THIS WORLD GOOD!!!!!   So our waitress "Nicole" was helpful and nice, but i also knew exactly what I was getting and also some stuff to try before getting there. She was a Local girl who's from Maui. So her and I chatted and my pidgin accent started to come out.  So this is the low down on what we got:

Fresh black coffee was delicious & fresh and I don't usually drink coffee nor do I like it black.

Virgin Bloody Mary was just what I needed from Drinking too much the night Be4 and it was tasty.

Chicken Tobasco honey sandwich that came with Grits - Very yummy, but the Grits were the STAR and talk about it here in a few.

Famous Shrimp & Grits w/Lump Crab topped off w/over easy eggs.- This was what I came here for initially and it was delicious, but there was just a lot going on in flavors, next time I won't mess with perfection and keep it simple with just "shrimp w the grits"  

Egg White Fritata my friend been craving eggs whites - It was good, healthy wise, but we should've ate this first because after tasting the grits and other dishes, this tasted somewhat bland. It by no means was bland, but you can't mix healthy when your eating gluttonous rich tasting dishes.  It did taste delicious several hours later. We ended up taking this to go.

Fries - Now these were actually horrible and burnt like. I like crunchy fries, but only if the inside is also soft and fluffy. We ate a few pieces and they were so bad we didn't even bother taking it to go and wasted the whole thing and just left it there. It basically looked untouched. The only Bad thing and so not worth getting. 

Now the grits.  OH MY FREAKEN GOSH!!!  This was just a shocker! So I didn't  know that my sandwich came with grits and I decided to just taste it with a spoon.  As soon as it hit my mouth, all my taste buds EXPLODED in Ecstasy!!  I was soo blown away and couldn't believe it so I took another spoonful and closed my eyes & was in Food Heaven!! My friend was like "no way is it that good", then tried it and was experiencing what I just had!  Ecstasy!  It was just basic no frills grits!!!  It was sooo dang good!! We ordered 2 more on the side.  they had a jalapeno one, so we got on of each.  Now mind you the jalapeno grits were delicious and not too spicy, but When it comes to PERFECTION, the plain grits is THE BEST EVER!!!!  Oh my gosh, how can a small side dish steal the show?!! It was crazy! We had delicious entree's, but yet all we could rave, crave and talk about is the Grits!I   I am going back to NOLA, just because of the food here.  Luke's, Green Fork  and SEED are 3 reasons I am going back just for a weekend trip so that I can eat heavenly.

The Grits are the MAIN reasons why Everyone needs eat here!!!!  I can still taste that nice creamy, not watery at all and just the perfect amount of butter to it. I didn't even have to add salt or anything. If I could only have one dish before die, not meal, but "dish."  This would be it!!!!
Nice place and good service. Disappointed they would not grill oysters...Blue crab dip is a must!!!! Hamburger was delicious as well.

It's been an entire year since I ate at this restaurant and I am still as rhapsodic over the food as I was the first time. We stayed at the Hilton and while famished decided to wander down here for breakfast. That proved to change the game for the entire trip. The first day I can't even remember what I had but it was delicious. Came back later that afternoon and had the Baked Oysters... ordered them again later that night... and then the next day... and on the last day I had what could possibly be the best dish I've ever had... Eggs in a Jar.....OH. MY. GAWD.... I still gaze at the picture I took of it fondly ever saw often. Then to top it off everytime we went the servers were amazing... especially the last time where we had this young gentleman server who's name I cannot remember but he looked like a young Leonardo DiCaprio (ie hot) and had the most amazing cajun accent (which made him even hotter)... i want to get on a plane right now just to come back here again....

I love a lot of things about Chipotle, they know how to make chicken, the rice is awesome, and the atmosphere is always great!  The only problem is u have to like onions to eat there!  I HATE onions, so as happy as I am eating there, at the end I'm always disappointed....  The guacamole has onions the pico has onions, why can't they just have tomatoes!

My business partner and I had lunch at Luke yesterday and it was terrible. We ordered the tuna and Brussels Sprouts appetizers to start off with. The Brussel Sprouts were hard and under cooked and the tuna was nothing special. My friend ordered the soft shell crab sandwich for his meal and I had the burger. His soft shell crabs were greasy and so were the fries that came with it. My burger was over cooked, the cheese was burnt and it was barely edible. We were in a hurry so sending everything back and complaining to get new food wasn't an option. All I know is this will be the last time I go here for any meal.

Wonderful first impression! So I read the reviews and saw good and bad ones but figured I'd try this place since it's not far from me.
The food was really good. Everything was fresh and we'll seasoned. The chicken doesn't taste weird; I stopped eating Chinese chicken because it didn't taste like real chicken, but this one yes. The food is great, it got here on time, the driver was friendly and my food was still hot. Will def order again.
Amazing food, phenomenal service, going to miss this place when I'm back in California. One of the best experiences I've had while in New Orleans

This is our go to restaurant after Mardi Gras.  We started with the peach bourbon smash during the 3-6 happy hour.  Tasty!  Next was the jumbo lump crab ravigote which has a kick of horseradish.  The soft shell crab BLT is devine because it marries bacon with a perfectly fried soft shell crab.  The fries a perfect because they are fried in duck fat.  We closed out with fried oysters and the brussel sprouts.  All of which were delicious!  U can't beat the prices either...total tab was $90!

My wife and I had heard good things so when we arrived from LA for a few days to NOLA we decided to try Lukes our fisrt night there. We decided to sit at the bar and eat dinner....great choice for us! We always prefer that, a bit more casual and more intimate getting to really know the bartender and staff. The food was very good, and typical New Orleans style in that it was waaay too much for us to eat. The onion tart was awesome. Very good place for very good food!

I'm really impressed. Being on the Keto diet it's tough to find restaurants that cater to my lifestyle. Sure, you can get meat and veggies anywhere, but when there is an actual menu item labeled "Keto" - I feel special :). 
The very nice lady at the front desk explained that many employees in the building practice keto. Therefore they have a couple options each day for those folks. The traditional menu looks pretty great as well, but I stuck to my diet for today. 
Steak, Peppers/Onions, Brussels sprouts and I added fresh Avocado all for about $7. The meat was a little chewy and the sprouts mushy, but it was a great treat. 
To start I had an Americano since they didn't offer any SF syrups for lattes. That would be my recommendation as an easy addition that can make a huge difference- especially us keto-ers. 
They even had freshly baked cookies made with swerve and grab n go chicken and tuna salad.

I love REI for the top quality products, and for the 100% satisfaction guarantee. I loathe returning/exchanging purchases, but today I had to make an exchange because of a bad fit. The customer service associates were kind, helpful, and the whole process was completely hassle free. Kudos for an excellent store and customer service experience!

The bartenders here are my favorite in New Orleans.  I'm lucky enough to stay near here pretty often and I often stop for a nightcap after a long day of work.  
If you are unlike me and are able to get out of work pre 7 PM, it's always half-off oysters which are usually pretty decent-sized and fresh.  Their menu is pretty heavy, but everything I have tried has been absolutely delicious.  Burger and fries were ab-so-lutely heavenly!

We tried Luke's on a last minute dinner decision due to the location to our hotel. We were not disappointed at all. We went during during happy hour by accident. I would not recommend going during this time if you are not a drinker (which we are not) or you don't like a loud restaurant. 

The food- was delicious. I ordered the "shrimp and grits" which was honestly some of the best I've ever had and the oysters, which were delicious. *we also live on the gulf, so we frequently have fresh oysters! 

Limited menu, so read over it before you go! 

Great option if your in the city!

Was really close to 5 stars, but in New Orleans, every little detail counts. 

The drum was amazing. Wouldn't change a thing. The roasted beet salad was too big -- it would have made a fine entree salad. It was delicious though. 

I had a glass of Pinot Grigio and it wasn't as cold as it could have been. The service was really slow, but really friendly. It was also NYE. Great place.

Visiting New Orleans for the first time and I made to make a reservation at Luke for our first dinner.

I had stuffed P&J oysters for appetizers which was so delicious!

I had shrimp etouffee for my main, it was just as great!

Ambiance was nice.

I took a star off because our server passed us on to another server, and they weren't really very friendly to us.
Love this place don't let it scare you that's in a shopping center. I drive 40 mi. Just to eat their sushi! Delicious fresh and awesome service!!
Oysters here were so good, as was the bread pudding. Atmosphere is relaxed and inviting.
Happy hour oysters + Brussel sprouts + bread pudding were memorable... highly recommend

This place was great! Good service and even better food. We got the pork chop and shrimp and grits and they were both really delicious! The pâté is insane! The place is a little pricey, but worth it. We have come here both times we have been to New Orleans and will keep coming back

We had a 30th birthday celebration at Luke's and they devinatley delivered! The food was great, the atmospher was great, and the waitress we had (Christin) was amazing!! Next time I'm in NOLA, I will make sure to go back! 
If you're looking for a nice place to eat, but also have fun - PLEASE go to Luke and ask for Christin to be your waitress!

Really good sushi in the suburbs.  This place is so close we can walk there but we'd drive because the food is so good!  Love the variety on the menu and everything we've tried has been amazing.  Don't let the location fool you, this is legit sushi!

The flatbread here is really what is truly exceptional. The rest of the food kind of just falls to the "average" plane. It's basically a Panera bread, but slightly worse.

I've tried the hummus and veggies sandwich, the tomato and mozzarella sandwich, the Shanghai Chicken Salad, and the Lime Chicken Salad. I have a slight preference for the salads over the sandwiches, though both aren't superb. The prices are average-- not too pricey but not cheap either. The portion sizes are pretty averagae as well. 

Service is usually quick, so that's a plus. Don't expect great tasting food here, but it certainly is not bad!

One of the best happy hours in town for sure. However, you have to get there at the top of happy hour because it gets crowded really fast. Fantastic .50 oysters, best fried oysters I've ever, and of course they make the best French 75 in my opinion. It's definitely the place I take friends and family when they visit me.

I have been here twice.  I hate to be REALLY negative, however...  Have you ever walked into a room that looks like a dark hole and smells like mildew? I have, it was here.  I let it go because I thought that I was being overly critical.  But the place is dirty.  The food is OK.  It's actually decent, but I was served on a dirty bar with dirty chairs and a mildewed floor.   

The staff, well.....YOU ARE IN THE SERVICE INDUSTRY--How about some SERVICE (enough said).

What a gem. The bar area was lively and they have a dining room in the back for a quieter experience. The food was great. I was in time for happy hour and had oysters for 75 cents each and 1/2 price cocktails. The staff was friendly and respectful, providing high end service and grest food and drink recommendations. I had the soft shell crab BLT, it was wonderful.

It's been just over a year and I'm finally getting around to my review of Luke.  Can't believe I forgot to post.

On the night I went, there was some food magic about to happen.  Yes, it was MOBBED, and things were very slow...even with reservations.  But I'm not going to slam a place with my review on that.  For me, it's about the food.

My buddy and I started off with the Charcuterie plate.  Man, we could stop there and the review would still be 5 stars.  Truly, the BEST appetizer plate possibly I've ever had.  The salumi, the mustards, all the goodies to choose from.  It was absolute bliss.

I got the shrimp and grits, and my buddy got the duck.  Neither of us really spoke at all during our meal.  It was that good.  I've had shrimp and grits out several times, and have made it at home.  Luke's Shrimp n Grits took the prize handily.

I noted there were many people hanging out at the bar getting tray after tray of oysters.  They looked pretty happy there also.

Looking forward to returning here, and any other John Besh restaurant.

one of best meals I've had in a long time.   Crispy fried Brussels sprouts with toasted almonds, sliced apples, jalapeños, progress milk barn cheese and espelette honey in cast iron skillet - defiantly had some heat but very very good and jumbo Louisiana "en cocotte" - jumbo Shrimp, roasted jalapeño cheeses grits, andouille & green onion sausage topped with lump crab meat.  Friendly staff and made the recommendations!!

After reading some of the reviews, I decided to go to Luke for breakfast. I wanted to try the Shrimp and Grits at an establishment that received good reviews for this dish. I ordered the Shrimp and Grits and their beignets with apple sauce filling and a side of plum sauce. The Shrimp and Grits was superb! It was the perfect size serving. So much robust flavor yet it wasn't overwhelming. I was more than satisfied. The beignets fell short but not on taste. I've never had beignets here and the hardness of it was consistent with a scone.  I prefer it to be softer. The apple filling was perfection and so was the plum sauce had they made it more donut than scone I would've enjoyed it. The waitress was attentive therefore 5 stars on service.

The breakfast was delicious. I ordered Mimi's pancakes with a side of cane syrup sausage and homefries.  The pancakes were soft and buttery, the homefries were made with what appeared to be thick cut bacon and onions.  The atmosphere gave a relaxed old timey New Orleans feel.  The waiter Jackson was always nearby and very quick to check in.  The food was out in 15 minutes and was excellent.

Happy hour is the time to go! We had reservations for a party of 15, split in two different tables, different areas..understandable. 5:45 and 6:00 seating times, but we were there a little early and they seated us early. We were able to take advantage of the HH .75 raw oysters & 1.25 fried. Order by the doz...Fried can be ordered by half doz.  

Crispy Brussel sprouts are really tasty! We had a few different dishes at our table, shrimp with grits, matzo ball soup, shrimp pasta, rosemary potatoes. 

Our waiter could've been a little more attentive, the bus boys had more personality. 

Great meal with colleagues.

EDIT  11/26/17:   I came across my review again over two years later, and I noticed for the first time that the owner had responded.  Nothing in his response addressed the merits of my complaint - that his technician wanted to charge $850 for repair of a valve that was in perfect working order, whereas the actual problem was an easily-diagnosed issue with the thermocoupler.  So, the technician was either trying to defraud (as seems the case, given all the other reviews here), or was completely incompetent.  Second, there definitely WAS a charge for the diagnostic visit (I believe around $75).  Perhaps the policy changed, but I distinctly recall being told that there would be a diagnostic visit charge regardless of whether I proceeded with a repair, although it could later be applied to the (absurd and made-up) repair cost, and I'm certain I paid one.

Scene
I always enjoy the lively scene at this creole inspired brassiere. The front dining room is pretty cozy but there is additional seating in the back dining room so don't be alarmed when you check in with the hostess. There is a wait sometimes even with reservations so prepare to stand for a bit because there really isn't a lot of space in the waiting area. The raw oyster bar is definitely the highlight of the front dining room which offers two, four and six top tables. 

Service
The service is full of Nola charm and ever so knowledgeable servers...always pleasant, always southern and always extremely comfortable with telling what's good on the menu. 

Food
The food never fails here. I've dined in for breakfast, lunch and dinner and it really is my kind of wonderful. Some of my favorites are the shrimp and grits, crispy brussels, croque madame, drum puppy top with crab meat, stuffed p&j oysters and the crispy chicken biscuit. Oh and did I mention one of my favorite French 75 with cognac is made here #winning

Cost
$$

Tip
Check out the 75 cent oyster happy hour from 3pm-6pm. Get there early.

Tiny little place that packs a punch! I've only ever had their coffee but I make it a point to walk here on the weekends because it's so good. The staff is amazing and the main cashier person (I say this because he's always running the till when we're there) is such a wonderful human - I'd genuinely like to be his friend! He exudes such a positive energy that keeps me coming back. Definitely check this place out if you're in the neighbourhood.
I ordered the crispy fried chicken on a biscuit with the honey sauce- it was perfect and to the point.
Very good food and atmosphere. The crab bisque and shrimp grits were excellent. The staff are friendly and attentive. I will definitely be back when in NOLA.
A staple in the Lutz area.  I have been eating here since the 1990's and the food has always been very good.

Jerzees is perfect for a quick beer and some snacks to watch the game and hang out with friends.  It is a super laid back bar with no formal dress code and you can tell it's a place for regulars.  The wait staff is always very friendly, and they get to know you the more times you frequent.  

There are draft beer deals every day of the week, including $2 rolling rock and $3 bud lights.  The Miller high life bottles are always $2 and on Monday nights from 6-12 are only $1!  Thursday nights are discounted appetizers so the sampler platter with four different app choices is only $7.50.  The wings are solid, the onion rings and mozz sticks are very good, and the pizza is probably the best I've had in Glenside.  The super fries are always a win and are only $5 during football games.  

Besides the great deals on food and drinks in the restaurant area, they also have a separate section that sells cases of beer.  You can pick it up or get it delivered to your house, along with any food order!  It's the perfect place to come during the week because it isn't too crowded and there's a great environment for hanging out.

There's was a dearth of servers here on a Saturday during Homecoming at the local university. Not sure how that happened, but they were a bit slower than normal because of it, but at least they noticed us.

Food here isn't anything remarkable, but the TBM and wasabi roast beef sandwiches are usually acceptable. Chai Tea Latte is decent, although the House Coffee has no refills.

The front of the line/ barista is probably my favourite person in the world when it comes to coffee, or any sort of drink beverage. When you make a drink for someone, you are to an extent, making a connection with someone. You trust that person to the degree that they aren't poisoning you, and are providing you with a sustenance that will save you from fatigue. (I'm a university student and I also work crazy hours. I need my coffee). 

The barista made my drink, made sure that I didn't have any allergies, and then proceeded to talk to me like a human being. I appreciated this a lot because a lot of baristas in large chain corporations are far removed from their work, have a negative attitude, which portrays they are extremely unhappy to serve you and are not excited about your order, and see you as just another customer. 

Vincent (my barista) was upbeat, extremely friendly and funny, and made me feel completely welcome the moment I stepped into the door. He welcomed me in like it was his home, and I was his guest. 



I'm super impressed. The food quality is fresh and the drink quality is also top notch. Will be coming back in the future!

Every time I visit NOLA, I stay at the Hilton upstairs and eat at Luke's. It takes a while to get seated but the food here is worth it. The burgers are awesome and so is the bread pudding! I cannot get enough of that bread pudding.

The servers are nice and friendly but then again who isn't. We are in the south and everyone is so nice here!
Super fresh and delicious! The service was great from stsrt to finish. I will be coming back there when I visit again.

Delicious shrimp and grits. A bit pricey and can be loud after work hours especially since they have happy hour and a lot of people take advantage of it after work. We came here twice and enjoyed both times. The price is the only difficult thing to swallow (pun intended).

Came on Ash Wednesday and I'm thinking this may have had something to do with the slow service and  subpar food. Ordered a cocktail for my friend and a sprite for me. Sprite bottle came in a 237 ml glass bottle. We ordered Brussels sprouts for an app which was really good and probably the best out of everything ordered. My friend ordered gumbo and shrimp cocktail, and requested it come out at the same time. This request was not met and as we were ready to get the check her shrimp came (at this point not wanting it). Appropriate to note here the shrimp cocktail comes with full shell and legs. I ordered puppy drum amandine and was totally disappointed when the fish came out as it looked and tasted like fried catfish. Servers were super friendly however the service was really really slow. I changed my review from three stars to four when the server noticed that I hadn't eaten much of the fish, he politely took it off the bill and advised to try it grilled next time. I didn't know that was an option but apparently it can be served pan fried, grilled, or blackened. Thanks for the tip Gary!

This is a happy hour review only. We came here a couple times with focus. No nonsense focus. We came for oysters. Fresh, giant, tender, succulent, $.75 oysters. And half price drinks. But you can get those a lot of places. But the oysters? They are spectacular. We didn't try them at Acme or Felix's. Saw no reason to do that! These are the kind you want to eat for hours on end. We ate till we were full. 

We started with a dozen each and then added more, as needed. Add a few drinks and you can leave here with a full belly and a huge smile. And that we did. 

The place is small and is off the lobby of the Roosevelt Hotel but with a separate street entrance. There can be a wait during happy hour, which is from 3-6, so get here early. Service was ok, not great when we sat at a table. It was better when we were able to get a seat at the bar.  If I lived here, I'd have my own seat at the bar like Norm on Cheers. I'm talking everyday kind of regular. Amazing.

Really exceptional!  I had a delicious brunch here with my husband and badly wanted to return to try more of the yummy menu while in NO for 3 day stay. Too many restaurants to choose from!! This place won't disappoint..great food, menu, ambiance and service.

When in New Orleans, do not miss the opportunity to have a meal at Lüke.

The ambiance is chic without pretention. Service is top-notch. Drinks are strong and made well. Food is out of this world!

My party was seated promptly, and taken care of by a very friendly waiter (I think his name was Kevin). He was attentive and helpful with his advice on what to order. I started my meal with a Sazerac ($10); the perfect apéritif. For my entrée, I had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp en Cocotte, aka shrimp and grits ($24); hands down, the BEST thing I ate during my stay in New Orleans. It had the perfect amount of flavor and spice, and the shrimp was cooked perfectly. For dessert, Brendan's Bread Pudding ($8) was recommended, which was so decadent and also phenomenal.

The bill for our party of 7 (6 drinks, 4 appetizers, 7 entrees, 1 side dish, and 4 desserts) was just under $400 before tip; not bad for the quality of food and service!

This place is great. It has nice breakfast and nice dinner. Yes, I had two meals in this restaurant. I ordered crab omelet and British black tea for breakfast. The omelet has crab and mushroom in it. The best omelet I've ever had in my life!

I ordered steamed oyster with additional jumbo crab meat for dinner. Not too many seasoning, but the flavor is right. The dinner seats were all reserved so I ordered food to go.

Happy hour has half priced specialty cocktails, wine, and 75 cent oysters. Drinks are strong. The staff was very friendly. I had the cappuccino and bread pudding. This bread pudding was heavenly. Hot with cool vanilla ice cream on top. Perfect combo with my coffee. Absolutely would go back!

If I ever find myself on death row, the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" will be what I'll be fantasizing about for my last meal. Really, everything is delicious and I know it's been said to death but do stop by and take advantage of their happy hour oyster special. So delicious, and the oysters are absolutely massive.
Healthy and really tasty alternative take on classic sandwiches, salads and food bowls. Price seems reasonable, seeing that they use fair trade ingredients for all their products.

Food is mediocre. The workers mumble alot and it is extremely hard to hear them speak. Manager needs to train them to speak clearly and be friendly. I asked a worker about a recommendation, and she gave me a 'wtf' look. The worker is the black female making the food here april 12th at 530pm. Manager please train her.

When the oysters came they were small, but wow were they sweet and full of favor, good choice. The head cheese was excellent as was the seafood gumbo, then came the mussel. When they pick up the lid off the dish, there must have been 50 in there, or it seemed so. I could hardly finish the dish and what tastes. It was reasonable for what we got, but what a steal as far as flavor. A must do when in NO

Literally so delicious. I got the blue crab au gratin to split as an appetizer with my boyfriend and it was absolutely to die for. Richie was helping us out most of the night and he has the best input for us. He was so incredibly helpful and we were happy to have him! The rest of the staff was extremely friendly as well, but we forgot to catch their names. The ambience was nice, you could show up dressed up fancy, but we also saw people dressed in jeans! Definitely recommend, delicious food, good vibes, and a friendly staff!

Had an excellent dinner!  So much flavor.  We started with crispy Brussels sprouts and buttermilk fried quail.  They were both excellent.  For our main course we had Luke burger and the grilled swordfish.  Both were delicious.  But my favorite of the night was the extra side we ordered of jalapeño grits.  Wow very delicious!  I was not a fan of grits until last night! John Besh you converted me to a grits lover!  My favorite meal so far in NOLA!  We had an extra special surprise our table was located up against a large window looking in on the kitchen!  Such a treat!

Fish was overcooked. Service was pretty bad too. I told them of a food allergy, but the food came out with said ingredient on the plate. They agreed to remake the food. By the time my food actually came out, everyone had to leave to get back to a work event (and we were there for 1.5 hours, so it's not like they didn't have enough time!). The servers and managers came over and apologized profusely, but they did not offer any compensation: e.g. dessert, drinks, a free meal. Talk is cheap. Luke is not cheap... and not cheap enough to warrant this kind of service and food.

I would have to give Luke's a 4 star only because they have the best oysters at Happy Hour for 50 cent an oyster!!! They were so fresh and succulent they serve them with fresh horseradish and cocktail sauce that made them even better. The dinner was not bad but also not my favorite but you must go for the Oysters!!!

Hmmm. Went here during happy hour with my fiancée. We made reservations (I highly recommend this or you'll be standing forever hoping by some miracle you'll get a coveted spot at the bar). So all was well. We were seated, ordered drinks and a dozen oysters (75 cents, baby!) And half-priced beer and wine? Awesome! We then ordered the flammenkuchen. My god, so good. So much bacon. Do this! But then!!! Things took a dramatic nosedive when we ordered another round of drinks and oysters. Boom, the 5-star service/experience disappeared. Our waiter basically abandoned us, and we waited no less than 45 minutes before we finally got our second round. They did apologize, but come on. Not sure what happened, but know this place can be, very quickly, hit and miss. Still, those oysters were amaaaaazing.

I think I caught these guys on a bad night, maybe they were breaking in a new cook.  I sat at the bar which was comfortable, a bit small but still OK.  Took a bit to get served, but got past that. The guy next to me was eating a burger that looked great, just a bit rare.  I ordered the burger, and I usually order med-rare, but based what I saw, I went Medium.  Right after I ordered, the guy next to me called the bartender because upon further review his burger was in fact raw.  I still went with it.  After a long wait, I had to ask to check on my order (actually it was the couple next to me who asked, but we ordered at the same time).  The couple next to me said they were surprised about the delay and it was uncommon.
So I gave this a three because I think I just caught them on a bad night.  My burger turned out rare, but I ate it,  I also had the gumbo (came at the same time as the burger), which was good.
The bartenders were nice and bought me a sympathy beer.

Shut your mouth, this breakfast was stupid delicious!!!!

I walked into Luke around 10:30 and you can tell they were setting up for Lunch. I was seated not the best service however I'm sure that was due to it being in between breakfast and Lunch.

I ordered a Latte however no soy or almond milk so I settled on reg coffee which was nice, strong and balanced.  I would knock a star down for this but the food was that mind blowing.

I ordered the Eggs in a jar!!!
OMG OMG OMG ORGASMIC!!!!

It has creamy chedder jalapeño grits at the bottom of the Jar with 2 poached eggs on top and huge fried prawns hanging on the edge of the jar.

It was by far one of the best meals of my life and I highly recommend the dish. 

John Besh your the SHIT!!!!!

What a lovely spot! Bright and quiet-a great place for a business lunch. The croque monsieur was so good - covered with a thick crusted cream and made on bread that was a little sweet and super thick slices. The Brussels sprouts are the best I think I've ever had -not greasy or overloaded, and cooked to perfection.

Excellent restaurant. Stuffed oysters were to die for. I had something that I believe was crawfish carbonara. I have posted 2 pictures during my time on Yelp and generally dislike doing so, but I was so moved by this dish that I will indeed post a picture. Here it is. Please enjoy!

Our go-to sushi spot in the Warrington/Chalfont area. The sushi is really fresh, fairly sized and quality. The angry dragon roll is incredible. I also think for how quality the sushi is they probably could charge a bit more. Totally fine if they don't do that though

This place deserves no stars. The place is filthy. There's only one lady here that actually does nails and toes the right way. They have this young girl working that can't do nails or toes to save her life. Ain't no way she should be working here.

The Fruit De Mer platter here is really good.  And when they have it on the menu, the best Choucroute Garnie you'll have stateside.  I particular enjoy the oyster selection as they carry not only Louisiana Oysters but Oysters from the Pacific Northwest.  Who doesn't love local oysters, but they're really one trick ponies in comparison to the variety and flavor of the infinite selections that thrive in the NW.  

The one thing I'll say about this place is the manager was really weird with us and made me think "How is this person in charge?"   We dropped in to take my MIL to lunch who works in the building across the street.  We were initially to go to the Pavillon but discovered they don't do lunch there anymore, so we said we'd give Luke a try.  We've been before, MIL hasn't.  So we drop in to see if we can get a table, but they were booked up.  That's fine, I've worked in the business many years as well, we knew this was the lunch rush and we were taking a chance, no big whoop.  But this manager kept almost like scolding us that we didn't have a reservation and kept repeating that we should have made a reservation.  Like, we heard it at least 10 times while we stood there because I was talking to a lifelong friend of mine who is a serve who I just hadn't seen in a moment.  And the manager was like "aw, you know him, yeah, I could've sat you in his section had you requested that when you MADE A RESERVATION, but you didn't make a reservation".  

We'll be back, because the place is still great if not for that one weird thing with the manager.

I had one of the best things I've ever eaten in my life here - shrimp and grits. Now,  I don't know if their shrimp and grits are just that exceptional or if ALL shrimp and grits are the best thing in the world... now,  for all the non-Americans and non-Southerners, grits are corn, something like polenta, only coarser.

Shrimp and grits are grits, sausage, shrimp, cheese, probably a ton of butter, sauce.... OH MY! It was incredible.

I also had the baked oysters and a cup of gumbo. Way too much food, but I wanted to eat everything (and I did). I liked both the oysters and the gumbo, but neither blew me away like the shrimp and grits here.

It was delicious!!! Shrimp and Grits = YUMMY!! Super ass delicious potatoes with roasted chicken. And the happy ending? Warm Bread pudding topped with vanilla ice cream with caramelized pecans. OMG. I can't wait to come back!! When you are in the business district make sure to stop by, to eat or for a happy hour!

Horrible service, mis diagnosed my pet, charged almost $700 for my visit, prescribed medicines the pet did not need. Tried to upsell on everything, and as a result of the misdiagnosis had to put my pet down

Last night, based on high yelp reviews, we had a wonderful happy hour experience at Luke.  Calvin Cooley the head oyster shucker kept us entertained while shucking a couple dozen of the most wonderful oysters I have had the pleasure to feast upon.  Cannot say enough good things about this place.  Tonight we are headed back for another happy hour (3:00 - 6:00) and hopefully try out a late dinner with them.  Will update after dinner.

TL;DR this place may be good for happy hour oysters but don't expect anything extraordinary otherwise. Service is good. 

Okay, if you look at most of my other reviews from this week, you'll see why this was such a disappointment. Expectations were high and ultimately we felt like everything we had here ranged from mediocre to just okay.

To start, my wife asked for a recommendation on a dry wine but got a fairly sweet wine with a slightly dry finish (I tasted it and agreed even though I barely know wine). She felt bad about asking for a different glass but the waiter gladly replaced it... with the most watery, flavorless wine either of us have tasted. At least it wasn't sweet?

We started with the oysters, a half-dozen each of the Miyagi and Southern Belle. My wife liked the more briny Miyagis and I liked the more balanced Belles but neither of us felt like they were special in any way.

We then put in the rest of our order, asking how much food we should order. We asked for the Blue Crab Gratin, the famed Crispy Brussels Sprouts, and the Softshell Crab BLT. These were all recommended by the waiter and he didn't think it would be too much food.

The Brussels should be called Soggy rather than Crispy since they have so much balsamic glaze on them. I found them way too sweet and the cheese wasn't helping. I did have one nice bite with a fresh jalapeño but there weren't enough of those to save the dish. The Gratin was fine, nothing special.

Even with these starters half-eaten, we were full and probably should have canceled the Crab BLT but also figured it was already being made and would feel guilty canceling this late. It soon arrived, split for the two of us and it would have been more than enough food by itself for an entire meal (even before the oysters). 

Looking at the generous cup of fries that each of us got and the fairly large sandwich on each of our plates, we couldn't figure out how the waiter would have let us order all this food.

We did our best but the fries were mediocre and the sandwich was fine. We agreed that the oysters were probably the best part of the meal but nothing to write home about. Compared to most of the meals we've had here, the food lacked creativity and savory, unique flavors.

All I can say is YUMMY!!!!!  where to start.....the cocktails amazing! the happy hour oysters on the half...delicious! the brussel sprouts could be a meal in themselves!!! for dessert??? OMG the smores torte with the home made butterscotch ice cream??? you definitely cannot pass this up! I also highly recommend the yummy shrimp and cheese jalapeno grits....all of these flavors just rush in your mouth begging for more!!  We found this restaurant upon staying at the st. charles hilton a couple years back and we just keep on coming for more!!! I would say 4 1/2 stars EASY!!!!!

I loved this restaurant! The menu is the perfect size so you don't feel over whelmed by so many choices, yet don't want anything because it so small! I got the tuna tar tar and the my husband got the Shrimp and grits/ed touffee. We shared the Brussel spouts and those were amazing!! If you like spice eat the single crUnchy pieces, if you don't want to burn your hiney up eat the halves! Will defiantly come bsck when we come to New Orleans.

We were visiting from out of town. As our first meal I wanted to try some local type cuisine, and this seemed perfect! The atmosphere was great! Clean and simple. We had 2 wait staff helping us, that was different and both were very nice and helpful. My friend ordered a appetizer and didn't realize how it came and they were very nice and let us pick another since she didn't want to try the first. We ordered a second appetizer the BBQ shrimp and it has a lovely smoky flavor. I had a cup of the matzo ball chicken soup, and wish I ordered a bowl! I also ordered the apple salad with ham and still think how yummy it was! They have a large drink variety, but I wish they had a few more items on the menu. Definitely would recommend though.

Drooling just rethinking about the food here. Got the petite platter with oysters, clams, mussels and shrimp. Everything was CLEAN (which is hard to find around here) and the oysters were huge. Although the wait time is long you can see the servers and oyster shuckers working super hard, so just be patient because it's worth it.

Really great food, really great service. I came with a semi-large party and had a very pleasant experience. I'd highly recommend Luke - their prices are reasonable for their portions and the restaurant has a really nice feel. An interesting change of pace from many other downtown restaurants, but a welcome one!

We were headed to the Ruby Slipper for shrimp and grits but with an hour wait we opted to go hunting a new haunt. Luke's fit the bill. Really we picked it because I'm a Gilmore Girl fan and any chance to eat at Luke's I'm gonna take. While there was no grumpy good looking flannel
Clad owner behind the bar, our server Adam was wonderful and whit filled  with excellent and honest selection recommendations. Shrimp and grits to die for with house made andouille sausage and an open faced blta topped with poached eggs. Go here!!! Oh and no wait!

Came here for Sunday brunch, and it was just okay. A french restaurant that reminded me a lot of Bouchon in Las Vegas. Even their logo was in the light green color like Bouchon.

We started off with oysters, and they were fresh and tasty. Oysters in New Orleans are so large! Love it!

Also had a belini which was a great way to start off the meal. The bread they serve in a napkin, so warm, fresh, and pure perfection. By far, the best part of the meal. We also ordered foie gras, which was good, but I'm not the biggest fan, so I didn't appreciate it as much. went well with the croutons they provide, or with the bread as well.

I was craving breakfast food, so I went with the Southern Breakfast. Grits, bacon, egg whites, and I substituted the biscuit with french fries as I was craving me some fries as well. A pretty carbalicious brunch. 3 others got the croque madame with the fried egg on top, one got the shrimp and grits, and the other got the pulled pork and ham sandwich.

When my food came out, it looked a bit unappealing as all you see is white mush with 2 small strips of bacon. The grits were okay, a bit bland, and the eggs and bacon were normal. My friend really enjoyed her shrimp and grits, and the sandwiches came out on this fabulous cutting board. Very nice touch. Had a bite of the croque madame, and it was tasty. Fries were good as well, can't go wrong with french fries! My friend said her pulled pork sandwich tasted even better later in the day, which is always a good sign! 

Our server was great, tended to all our needs. I wish I could rate this place higher, but my breakfast was just so-so unfortunately.

Would like to come back though for a happy hour or try out their dinner entrees.

I was hoping for more. We walked in at 9:00 on a Tuesday night, and they were out of the cochon de lait special. I had the schnitzel with spaetzle instead. The meat was dry and the breading was salty; the spaetzle was a bit dry too. The apps were good, and maybe I should have had the oyster salad...I may never find out since there are many other places to eat in the area.

While the place was not full, the maitresse still made us wait five minutes while the servers set up exactly the right table for us(?) Our server was fine.

Nice atmosphere, but not the experience I was expecting from a "top chef" restaurant. I think you need to pick the right dishes to get the best experience, or get there early to score the daily special--never the winning trait of a good restaurant in a big city.

I am not really a fast food fan but sometimes you need a quick meal that's good and that's why I come here.  This location is convenient for me and I appreciate that they actually cook the food here and not take it out of a plastic bag or freezer.

The people are always friendly and the service is fast.  The food is fresh and good, I have never had any problem with anything served at this location.  

I also like that they give you options between white and brown rice, pinto and black beans.  They include their toppings at no additional charge except the guacamole.

Good place for a quick bite!

We went here for their famous Happy hour and it did not disappoint us at all. Most of their signature cocktail drinks were half off and raw Oysters were only $0.75 per piece. We tried couple of their  drinks and our favorite was Honey, It's Hot out there. It had a perfect amount of Bourbon and honey. The Oysters were also fresh. I went there with someone who never had Oyster Shots before and he was able to devour them in hot seconds!  It is located below Hilton and close to French Quarter. If you are in the area, definitely stop by for their HH.

We came here around 5:30 pm on a Saturday and were seated right away. Luckily we made it during happy hour which ends at 6pm. The happy hour was awesome and includes half of most drinks and cocktails, and $0.75 oysters! So we shared oysters and each had a French 75 a great pairing for sure. We then ordered entrees, I ordered the fried oyster salad and my husband got the shrimp and grits. I got my salad first, the fried oysters were really good. They smoke their own bacon which was nice and salty and cut into hardy pieces. The only reason I gave 4 stars is because our server brought us 2 separate shrimp and grits entrees when we only ordered 1. For some reason he thought I'd ordered one too, even though we had a lengthy conversation about how I was ordering salad and would try a few bites of my husbands entree. At $25 a plate that's an expensive error, he was quick to walk away and after waiting a few minutes to inform him of the error he didn't return so I went ahead and ate it. We both loved the shrimp and grits, the grits were thicker than traditional but weren't a grit cake (which I dislike). I wish the tails were taken off the shrimp so it was easier to eat, but other than that the food was fantastic!

Luke's is definitely a solid place to eat. The atmosphere is great. The place was not too overwhelming. Somewhat upscale, but pretty laid back. 7 of us dined in for brunch, we were seated in the back of the dining area. Our server, was extremely accommodating and made sure we were happy throughout our meal (I forgot his name). We all know it's not easy taking care of a large party, but happily enough we all left stuffed and satisfied. 

The Brussels sprouts are a must. They're crispy, semi sweet, and topped off with feta cheese (so delicious). I had the burger, which is ginormous. (shareable). The burger and fries were ON POINT! 

Overall I would definitely recommend this place. Whenever I return to NOLA, I am for sure checking out their Happy Hour specials. Those oysters are calling my name!!

Make reservations to Luke's, a must stop if you're in NOLA. We started with a cocktails, and their complimentary bread and butter. I had the shrimp and grits and the hubby had the croque Madame. The grits were cheesy, creamy and flavorful, the shrimp and sausage were saucy and garlicky. We've had the croque in Paris and hubby said Luke's was right up there with the ones we had in France. I had a nibble and it was buttery, cheesy, and the right crisp. We shared the bread pudding, which was delectable. The service was friendly, helpful, and prompt. I am tempted to return for breakfast on our last day in New Orleans.
We went here because the reviews were all excellent. While the service was good the food was just ok.

First time here and we WILL be back. Had the crabmeat rivgote and corn crab bisque as app. Both were excellent!! Split the shrimp and grits as an entree. It was phenomenal!! Great brunch spot. Great NOLA cuisine.

This place was awesome.Happy hours make me so happy..75cent per oyster was fantastic with half price glass of wine.
$1.25/fried oyster also good!
No need to talk just go and get them.

Ordered a vanilla custard with oreos for my topping and a mango gelati with vanilla custard.

A little stingy on the oreo topping and the custard on the gelati, but still tasty. The presentation of the gelati custard was not given any love either, which was disappointing.

No sitting area, but plenty of parking.

Service is average.

Everything about this place was amazing. The decor reminded me of a French restaurant with much better service. The local oysters are great value, but the real reason to go would be both the French 75 cocktail and the jumbo shrimp en cocotte. Neither are a particularly original choice as they are considered favorites of the restaurant but they are favorites for a reason. Would definitely recommend for a good overall dinner experience.
So disappointed in the customer service. I ordered a bake good and asked if they would heat it up for me and the girl rudely told me to use the microwave. Never coming to this location again.

Okay, so I came here late last night with some coworkers so try the world renowned chefs cuisine that was ever so talked about from other coworkers. Overall I am extremely pleased with the experience. There was a hostess that was a little delayed in answering questions and helping, maybe she was new. And our first server was an odd duck. He really wasn't the most organized and forgot one of my coworkers gumbo. He also had runners bringing food to the wrong tables. 

But once we asked them to cancel the gumbo, a more experienced person came and happily helped us. He is great and mentioned he is coming to Houston to help with another restaurant opening. I appreciated his help and the bread pudding he brought us as an apology for food mixup so. 

I love the atmosphere here. Like an upscale hotel restaurant that welcomes all types of clothing. I got the snapper with crab on top that came with some great sautéed veggies. We also had the raw oysters which I never had before. Then I tried the pate for my first time and all the relishes that you could pair with it were so delicious. There was a creole mustard and pickles and a fig type jam. And my favorite part was the AMAZING bread pudding with candied pecans.

So yummy!

This is our favorite bar in town! All of the bartenders are awesome and super friendly. The best part about Jerzee's is that they serve food until 1AM. It's great for being able to go after a night of work to have a few drinks and to get something to eat. Their food is always good. We get the pizza a lot, and even have it delivered sometimes with a 6-pack. Their draft and bottle selection is out of this world. You can literally find anything you're looking for. Great for trying new beers. Also the new updated interior is really nice. Service is wonderful, staff is friendly, and it's an all around great and convenient place.

Traveling by myself , sat at the bar the bartender was very friendly and helpful. Hands down the best cup of gumbo I have ever had and the bread pudding could very well been the best I've ever had too.

We eat at Luke each time we visit New Orleans. It is directly across the street from the Intercontinental Hotel. We went for lunch and started with the watermelon and grilled shrimp
Salad which was both flavorful and refreshing. Our entree was the gulf puppy drum which is a very mild fish with a meuniere sauce on a mound of rice surrounded by a moat  of lightly sautéed tomatoes and fresh vertically sliced okra. All was delicious. We splurged and enjoyed the decadent dark chocolate torte. So wonderful! Service was excellent.

This is a must if you're going to be in New Orleans. Cute atmosphere, trendy but not too crowded, and absolutely delicious. I suggest making a reservation here.  I ordered buttery crawfish with shrimp burratta tartine, eggs, and sweet peas. It was combined in a messy dish that somewhat fit on the pieces of toast but it was fine that it was messy. I suggest getting runny eggs so the sauces and flavors mix together better. I will definitely come back here.

It was National Cabbage Day so I dropped by Così to get a Korean BBQ Pork Bowl for dinner. The Asian cabbage slaw on top was actually really good, sweet and tangy. The cabbage and various vegetables were quite crunchy and refreshing. The BBQ pork was actually really flavourful as well, not overwhelming, but sweet and comforting. The pork was tender enough although it was slightly hard to pull apart and was by no means melt-in-your-mouth. The grains were a little greasy, though, but they should not be since it is just grains and rice.
The Country Lentil Soup was decent and had a strong tomato and vegetable taste. It was thick enough but not too much that it was no longer a soup. The lentils added texture and the ingredients were fresh and hearty.

The Cheesecake Brownie had a slight pungent cheese smell. It was more like a thin layer of cheese-flavoured dense cake on top of a fudge brownie. The heart shapes were cute, I though. The entire dessert was dense and chewy, the way I like my brownies to be.

Così can have a really long wait time. The staff at this particular one seem very inefficient. There are so many of them yet food comes out so slow. It takes forever every time I am there. Also, I spotted a cockroach on the wall behind the counter and that was not very comforting. Let's hope they do not get near the actual food itself.
Not impressed. If your normal is macaroni grill you will like it. If you are a foodie you will be disappointed
Great fresh sushi.  Wonderful presentation.  It's a byo and quite small so make reservations.  Best in the Doylestown and surrounding area.

Start with a cup of the Seafood Gumbo a la Creole--the perfect blend of seafood, sausage, rice, and seasonings. The Salad Luke is a refreshing pause between appetizer and plats principaux. For local fare, try the Étouffée of Blue Crab & Brown Shrimp. Wow! The Maredsous ale is a perfect pairing to their seafood selections. Note, they have a back room that might be quieter (might be).
Great local cuisine. I had the shrimp and grits which were amazing. The decor is cosy. Good for groups and have really good wines. The bread pudding is amazing
