Came here with a big group so we all ordered cocktails from happy hour. All great, except the well drinks.... but you get what you pay for. The cocktails were great though! Food was delicious and you can't really go wrong. We basically ordered one of everything. Service was nice and attentive. Atmosphere was modern but welcoming. Overall a very classy place that stood out during our whirlwind trip.

Excelent.  This is hands down a great restaurant. 

I wnt to Luke for lunch and sat at the bar with the regular mid-week lunch crowd.  lI enjoyed three courses: salad, soup, and entre.  This was coupled with three local beers.

The salad was a Slow poached egg with
Chicory, Bacon, Crispy fried pigs ear, with a Mustard dressing. This was a unique and tasty poached egg salad.  The bacon was especially good, with a rich, smokey flavor.  The fried pigs ears were tender and suculent.  

The soup was a signature crawfish bisque.  This was by far the best crawfish dish I've experienced, aside from a straight boil.  The bisque was so full of crawfish flavor, but not heavy or weighed down by butter or cream.  The bisque was acompanyed by a crawfish head filled with a delicate stuffing that, when drenched in bisque, melted in the mouth.  I was told that this was seasonal based on the availability of quality crawfish.  A must-try if available.

Finally, the entre. Being lunch and as an out of towner, I kept the crawfish theme going with a Luisianna "crawfish boil" po-boy.   The sanwich came on a thick French roll, layered with slices of green tomatoes and hard boiled eggs, a signature slaw, and creol seasoned boiled crawfish tails.  While the bread was a tad thick, the flavor of the slaw, tomatoes, and crawfish was perfect.  The sandwich was acompanyed by a healthy portion of frites. 

Overall this was an excellent meal and great experience.  The wait staff was attentive and friendly.  I will be back.

Came in post Covid end of May 2020 for my daughter's 16 birthday. Read great reviews and wanted to support our local businesses. Every single entree was to die for! My favorite was the chicken and red beans and the pate! The staff did a phenomenal job with making us comfortable and always check on us. Will be back soon!!

I'm glad that our visiting Portlanders wanted to go to Happy Hour here and partake of those 50cent oysters. It helped erase the memory of my last meal here (see previous review). We were seated in the overflow back room which was lovely...and much quieter than the main space. (Seriously, Luke, consider some sound reinforcement; your main dining room is beyond "lively" and into painfully loud when it's busy.)  I enjoyed my 1/2 price old fashioneds and as I'm not so big on the raw oysters, I ordered a delicious beet salad. And shared fries with the group.

Our server was lovely and handled a capacity crowd on Ash Wednesday with ease and grace. Our orders came out in a timely fashion and if there was a delay (with our 2nd batch of oysters), we were given more information. And of course, the company, Merilou, Melvin, Lindsay & Vicky was outstanding.

First of all, I, like every other person on the planet, have a huge crush on John Besh. That perfectly coiffed hair, that stellar smile, that knowing twinkle in his eyes, Swooonnnn. Is it getting hot in here? Aside from his good looks, I think he's also an admirable man. His dedication to locally grown, raised or caught ingredients is one I have the utmost respect for and he's a nice family oriented guy.  Now that we have established he can do no wrong, let me get on with my review.

I have wanted to try Luke for some time and I finally got a chance not too long ago. This was my first Besh restaurant experience, so needless to say I was positively giddy with anticipation.  We arrived and were seated immediately. If I have one complaint about the restaurant itself it's that tables are very close together and it's extremely loud in there, so a private conversation is almost impossible. Service was impeccable and prompt. I ordered the Saumon Demicuit...grilled wild salmon, blue crab and corn. It was delicious! I was also able to sample my friends fries and I must say they were the best French fries I've ever had. Yummy!

I really enjoyed Luke and can not wait to try more John Besh restaurants!

Not my Favorite Besh restaurant. I went with a group of 4. We all ordered something different so we could share.  We were here on a Thursday and had the express meal, the Jambalaya and the best part was the sausage, the rice was bland and  had a similar appeal as Uncle Bens Rice Mix. The cornbread was savory not sweet.
The Burger was pretty good, we all concluded though we have had better but the fries were above average. 
The Shrimp and Grits, the highlight was the grits, we left majority of the shrimp as the flavor was not that appetizing . 
Gulf Fish Amandine..just as expected and as described by Besh himself at the RCA convention
Crispy Brussels Sprout hands down the best thing we tried. The flavors were great combination of sweet and Spicy that hits you athe end
Matzo Ball & Roast Chicken Soup Pretty sure had pork in it. Just okay

Service. Slow to refill our drinks and slow to bring the check and slow to run the credit card!

Atmosphere: Didnt seem to fit the theme of the food.

Overall, it was okay but Besh Has other restaurants in the area that outshine this one
Richie Rich may be the best waiter my wife and I have ever had the pleasure of being served by. He made our experience very special by catering to our every need. One of a kind dining experience!

Wow!! I found myself talking about this place all day it's that good!

Stopped in for breakfast.  We received excellent service, coffee was refilled frequently, our order was taken promptly and the food was brought out in a timely manner.

The food was amazing!

Order:

Southern breakfast $15 - 2 eggs, Allan Benton's bacon, housemade andouille sausage, buttermilk biscuit, grits

Side of fruit & berries $6

French press $3.5 (Santa Lucia coffee), free refills.

The coffee tasted great.  

The fruit was fresh and cut into nice size pieces.  It included watermelon; blueberries, honeydew, strawberries, and cantaloupe

The meal was so amazing.  The bacon and the sausage smelled so wonderful, and had a Smokey taste that was out of this world.  The bacon was perfectly crispy, and the sausage was cooked perfectly as well.  It had a bit of spicy to it but was excellent.  The eggs were scrambled and fluffy.  The grits were made with mascarpone and were oh so wonderful. The biscuit was tasty and served with a side of whipped butter and strawberry preserves.

The meal was perfect, service was excellent, and we really enjoyed our visit.

I highly recommend eating here often :)

** high chairs = yes
** kids menu = no

Amazing and wonderful location, top notch staff and my new favorite place in New Orleans. Found myself there every day for happy hour which includes five dollar specialty cocktails as well as $.75 cent oysters on the half shell. Fried oysters are $1.25 each and they are so good so good so good so good. 
I became addicted to the French 75 cocktail and tried them all over the city and this was the very best one. I cannot tell you how much I miss going to happy hour at Luke's , I swear my eyes are tearing up as I wrote this. 
We also had brunch there I had the shrimp and grits and it was some of the best I've ever eaten. I feel like the quality here is amazing and the pricing is very good for New Orleans. 
I cannot wait to return!
The food was good, but the serving sizes were small.  The restaurant was clean and the staff were not overly friendly.

We had reservation at 3 PM and of course we arrived 15 minutes early, Great! We can grab a drink at the bar. There were many empty tables so the host said there will be a little bit of a wait since they're waiting for the table that they were planning to seat is at to close their tab.  Of course I didn't mind since we are early. We sat at the bar and ordered many rounds of drink until I notice that it's 3:30ish, wow our reservation time had pass and the seating are being all filled up. So I walked up to the host she said it shouldn't be anymore longer until we get seated.... Ok we had reservation and didn't even get seated until 45 mins later! Which I told myself I wouldn't let that ruin my meal.

We bumped into Happy Hour.. Yay! $.75 Raw Oysters and $1.50 Fried Oysters. The raw oysters were so fresh but it wasn't clean, I was biting into little particles of shells crumbs in my oysters and some looked dirty. The fried oysters tasted delicious and even the dip that came with it taste just right. I even ordered the Brussels Sprouts skillet, that was top notch. The seafood gumbo was okay... There was a few oysters, a few shrimp and some sausage. It was kind of bland to me. But at all it's worth the experience!!!
Gus and the guys in the bike dept. we're friendly helpful and knowledgeable. They offer good outdoor products and reasonable prices.

My second trip to New Orleans in less than a year started strong with a lovely dinner at Lüke.  My boyfriend and I had a 7:30 reservation, and were surprised to see a good number of children in the restaurant.  This was by no means a bad thing, though, and reflected on the casual, welcoming atmosphere of the place.  The decor was simple and relaxed, with lots of brown wood and an open kitchen.  We sat right outside of this kitchen and had a great view of the chefs preparing our food.

The service was so fabulous it deserves its own paragraph.  Our waitress was a wonderful friendly woman who made conversation without being intrusive and answered our questions with a smile on her face.  She was very attentive, checking in on us regularly throughout our dinner to make sure we were topped off with water and wine.  She also gave us great suggestions on what to order.

The food ranged from good to stellar.  The bread was a great start.  It came wrapped in a little towel like a delicious newborn baby, and it was warm and crusty and served with good butter.  We were starving, but still happy to wait for our orders with the help of this bread and a nice bottle of wine, which our waitress helped us select.

For our appetizers we got the assiette de charcuterie and the fried oyster, bacon, romaine, and avocado salad.  The charcuterie was really great, a substantial selection of meats served with stone-ground mustard, house-made pickles, and some tasty grilled country bread.  Almost everything on the plate was good.  The a pate of Louisiana rabbit and duck livers that was nice and creamy, with a forward livery flavor that I found rather welcome.  The pate en croute of local veal and pork came was pleasantly meaty and it came with some fantastic watermelon pickles.  My favorite was the rillete of Berkshire pork, which was rich, soft, and salty.  It came with an irresistible savory pear and ginger marmalade.  The one item I did not like was the Badischer presskopf, or hog's head cheese.  I don't think this was Lüke's fault at all.  This was my first experience with head cheese, and I think it may be one of the few things I've tasted to which I have a categorical aversion.  I found the gelatin weird and the idea unappetizing.  The fried oyster salad was very tasty.  It was a filling salad, with a creamy dressing and chopped bacon on top.  The oysters were the star of the show, beautifully fried so that the breading added a nice crunch without disturbing the luscious oysterness within.

For our entrees I got the shrimp and grits and my boyfriend got the Lüke burger.  The shrimp and grits - or, the jumbo Louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" with McEwen and Sons cream white corn grits and Poche's andouille - was out of control.  The shrimp was perfectly cooked, and each piece was firm and juicy.  The sauce on top reminded me of the sauce in barbecue shrimp, very butter and dark with some deep heat.  The grits were creamy like a great risotto, with little savory bits of sausage infusing it with flavor.  I don't think shrimp and grits gets any better.  I took a few bites of the Lüke burger, and it was pretty decent, if not deserving of national acclaim.  This came topped with tomatoes, Allan Benton's bacon, caramelized onions, and Emmenthaler cheese.  The meat was good, as were all the individual components, but the burger didn't make my mouth water.  Neither did the side of housemade fries, which was disappointing.  They looked so good in their tall cone, but they were sadly limp.

For dessert we ordered Brendan's bread pudding, with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce, and the "gateau basque," which was a vanilla cake with strawberries, simple syrup, and creole shrubb.  The bread pudding was good, but not the best in town.  I'd say the souffle at Commander's Palace and the bread pudding with whiskey sauce at Mr. B's were both better.  I liked the pecan sauce, but thought it would've been better with more pecan.  The "gateau basque" was the better dessert, very simple but with great flavor.  It had a really good crumb, too, like a cross between that of cake and cornbread, and the syrup moistened it up to great effect.

Our dinner at Lüke was a delightful experience, with warm service and some lip-smacking food - our waitress got a good tip and those shrimp and grits will be my standard for years to come.  If this restaurant were in my neighborhood I'd use it as a default for a nice but casual weekend dinner.  I also liked that the food was very New Orleans at heart, and I would recommend Lüke to locals and tourists alike.

Walked in to pick up rapid pick up order.  The gentleman who came to provide assistance said they did not show my order...perhaps I was too early.  He quickly offer to make my order no questions asked.  I showed him my order on panera app and he went to make it.  What great customer service skills this gentleman had! Thank you!!! I wish more employees had that attitude.  The world is a happier place thanks to excellent employees like this man.  Restaurant was super clean.  Everything looked fresh at counter from entrance.  Door says mask required but I forgot mine, I stayed by door and was not turned away.
This is probably a little on the pricey side for the value but the food and drinks were good, especially the Shrimp and Grits and the Pain Perdu.

In a world class restaurant city, Luke shines above all the others.  I wish I could have tasted all the menu but I can recommend the crispy brussel sprouts, the beet salad, shrimp in cheesy grits and the ribeye steak.  Can't remember the wine we ordered but the pricing on the wines list was very fair.  The two of us shared the four dishes and it was more than enough food.  Hope to be back when we visit next year.

Chef John Besh is a master at his craft and his team is nothing short of amazing.  Eating here was probably in my top 5 restaurant experiences in my life.

I am a major John Besh fan and for good reason, you actually can taste the love of food and pride in his heritage in each bite.

We dined here on Friday night for my bachelorette party and even though we were a larger (and probably slightly loud) group of girls, we felt as if the staff treated us like VIPs. We were treated to a glass of champagne and the manager stopped by to congratulate us.

Being a huge fan of Chef Besh, I simply asked the waiter to suggest to me whatever the Chef's favorite meals are and he suggested the P&J oysters to start and the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte." 

The oysters were amazing. Talk about a burst of flavor in your mouth. The En Cocotte was epic. It was so tasty that we were actively trying to figure out when we will next come to the restaurant and if we can find ways to fly down just for the food.

The only snag was that one meal did not make it out with the others.  The manager came over to apologize in person and as an apology treated us to another round of champagne.

We all cleared our plates and were too stuffed for dessert but the team brought out little Besh Box truffle samplers which hit the spot.  These truffles could easily compete against some major French pastry and chocolate shops in Paris.

The only thing that could have made the experience better was if I could meet Chef Besh and personally thank him for the amazing meals and for being an inspiration to those of us who share the same philosophy about food and cooking, buy local and cook with love. Maybe one day I'll have the honor and maybe I could even get him to take a pic with me or sign a copy of his book...a foodie girl can dream.

I stopped here for dinner before leaving for Tennessee a few weeks ago only because it was my third visit to NOLA and I had yet to go to a celebrity chef restaurant.  Who doesn't love John Besh and his infallible hair too? I sat at the bar to watch the Saints game and only ended up having some stuff from the raw bar but it was delicious and my shucking friend was very nice and friendly. Actually all the staff was extremely nice and let me store my luggage off to the side in a safe spot. Worth checking out for the happy hour I'm sure. I'm bummed I missed the special pricing! I would've stuffed myself with oysters!

Not my favorite Besh experience. My gulf fish was fine, but my boyfriend's burger was bizarre. I'm not sure if it is intended to be eaten open face, but that is how it was served. It seemed like an odd way to serve such a large burger. Service was a little slow, but given how busy the restaurant was, not unexpected or unusual. The waitress was a bit...off. She openly flirted with my boyfriend, which made for an awkward dining experience considering my parents were present (maybe she thought we were siblings, but event then, still very odd behavior). Overall, my food was fine, and service was average; though, I'll stick to Besh's other restaurants.

I placed my order using Yelp. I received an email confirmation at 6:01. I figured I would give about 15 minutes for the food to be finished. I called at 6:14 to see if he food was done, he told me 15 minutes. So I waited so 30 minutes total. 
Inside The space is open and you can see your food being fixed. I loved that.There are tables and a television if you want to sit.(Not sure if it was to eat in or if they know u will be waiting. Lol)
When I picked my food up the guy at the front also gave me a ten dollar coupon to use uber eats since I am not close enough for delivery. I thought that was nice.
The kids loved it, it was really fresh. We ordered chicken and broccoli,shrimp and broccoli. The Shrimp were a great size ! Shrimp, pizza and cheesesteak rolls. The kids loved the cheesesteak rolls the best. I see why people go  the food has a great taste to it. I love good food, but I hate waiting . Would give 3 1/2 if I could.

Luke has a wonderful ambience--I love the early 20th-century French bistro feel about it. I have been here several times with many different people, and across the board, people are impressed with the food. I have to confess that I have a go to meal here, so my actual experiences are somewhat limited.  Their version of the classic French sandwich the Croque Madame is one of the best I have ever tasted, and that alone makes Luke a regular stop for me.
Turkey avocado sandwich = best thing ever! Always crowded but great food and fast friendly service

Happy hour 3  to 6pm is good. Half price for the drink and p&j raw oysters 9 dollars for a dozen (reg 27 for a dozen). Some are big and some are small, all of them is super fresh. Last call for happy hour oyster takes a while which makes sense.

Really wanted to give a five-star but the service was...hmmm kinda slow

What we ordered: 

i) SOUPES ET SALADES
Crab Bisque
Matzo Ball & Roast Chicken Soup

ii) BAR À HUÎTRES
"le Plateau" Of Gulf Oysters

iii) PLATS PRINCIPAUX
Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en Cocotte" (roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausages)
Poulet Grand-mère (herb roasted local chicken, allan benton's bacon, farmers' market vegetables & whipped potatoes)
Étouffée (brown shrimp, garganelli pasta)

iv) DESSERTS
Brendan's Bread Pudding (vanilla bean ice cream & hot buttered pecan sauce)
Chocolate Bourbon Pecan Tart (bittersweet chocolate, coconut sorbet)
Bourbon Vanilla Bean Crème Brûlée (madeleines de commercy)
Gateau Basque (vanilla cake with creme fraiche & louisiana berry marmalade)

Really solid restaurant if your in the mood for fries, steak or burger. 
- Customer service is ++
- Drinks are good 
- Nice set up

After an unsatisfying dinner at a nearby spot, we came here for dessert and a few drinks at the bar. We shared the bread pudding, which was ridiculously good; even my boyfriend thought it was great and he's not a dessert person. The bread pudding was of a generous portion, warm throughout the bowl, and topped with pecans and ice cream. It wasn't too sweet either - just perfect. Along with our desserts, our drinks were pretty strong which started off our night well.

Looking around, we wished we went here for dinner instead. Not only did we see great plates being served to our dining neighbors, we saw this very large and tall tower of seafood for a couple which looked like was a first date. Kudos to the gentleman (or lady) for going big with that impressive and seemingly delicious variety of seafood.

The restaurant was nice as well as the staff, who were friendly to speak with. When we are back in town, we will definitely check out this place for dinner.

Love the healthy choices here. Cant really go wrong with ordering anything they make its all pretty delicious. Would get a 5 star, but price is a little high. Maybe thats because of the quality of food, but Im nitpicking
They have frozen agave lemonades my wife loves and some great kids meal options. Get the Panera card and get a free pastry upon sign up!
Great matzo ball soup!  Nice place for a drink too.

The food/drinks/service here were awesome! I would recommend the crawfish bisque especially. Our meal was late because they were busy and we were hidden at the bar so they gave us almost everything for free!

The customer service at this location was great!! I came in 10 minutes before closing & they still welcomed me. They walked me through the services my car needed & answered any questions I had. They applied ~$40 in coupons that I didn't even know about bringing my total down. Service was fast & efficient. Definitely going back in 3,000 miles.

Recommended by our hotel, due to well known local chef John Besh. Sorry John, never heard of ya up in Minnesota. Sunday night in July, busy but easy to get in without a Rez. Charming decor and extremely friendly host and wait staff. Brought us complimentary champagne after hearing me complain about getting my car towed at the French Market -total scam, BTW.  Besides the impeccable service, everything was fabulous. Limited menu choices, but all interesting.  Especially loved the Brussels sprouts appetizer (Crispy sprouts, MARCONA ALMONDS, ESPELETTE HONEY, PROGRESS MILK BARN CHEESE). Also loved the goat cheese stuffed squash blossoms. Entre was equally as good - JUMBO LOUISIANA SHRIMP "EN COCOTTE" -
ROASTED JALAPEÑO CHEESE GRITS, ANDOUILLE & GREEN ONION SAUSAGES, though couldn't finish all the grits after our 2 apps. Loved this restaurant and would highly recommend it for a business dinner or romantic evening.

I had a great meal. Really great. REALLY great. 

Life affirming great. 

Called ahead 

Wish I could eat more because it was really good. Got a call in the middle of my lunch from a former NYAG, and had to take it. When I went back, not as hungry. If anyone hears of a dead former NYAG, it was me.

Friendly people, good atmosphere, nice decor. Hard to say "Fabulous Food" in NOLA, with so many great choices, but this place has Fabulous Food.

Eat here. It's good.

Very pleasant staff work hard ensuring your order is accurate. Smiles and thank you'd from everyone. 
It was very nice to be able to sit outside and eat my everything bagel under a clean, umbrelled table on this Indian summer day. Cosi has a nice variety of health eats and their iced tea made with black tea is very good.

I went here 2 weeks after i came back from Japan so it was touch NOT to compare this place to cheap places i have been in tokyo.  

Anyway!!! If you have dined at any sushi places in center city Philly  (fat salmon, zama, etc..) you'll find this place similar to them. Services were awesome and staffs were super friendly.  Their ingredients were fresh!! 

I went on a sunday, so i'm not sure if it is a weekend thing or not but they have more than your typical salmon, tuna, white tuna, red snapper, etc..  I ordered 

Fatty Tuna
King salmon
king yellowtail
uni
filet mignon carpaccio
hawaiian poke
snow mountain roll

What a hidden spot, must be great for local consumers. This place brews it's own coffee and makes your meal homemade. The menu is a bit small but I guess it's for the best since the place itself is small. Feels like an organic but what do I know... One staff member working doing multi tasking which must be hard. It does get busy at times but not as much as Tim Horton's. They do cater sandwiches so check out their website for more info. www.elmcafe.ca. Ordered myself a hot chocolate which was very unique to the usual hot chocolate stuff I get made for me. The taste has hardly sugar which most things over power but this still tasted as hot chocolate just not sweet and not purely hot water. So that's a plus for starting a healthy diet. Parking here is cramped, you have to find somewhere on the street or around the building is a pay parkade. To be honest if your there for a quick meal just park on the street if you can. 
Recommended for anyone looking to try or taste a standard meal in a homemade sense.

I have eaten at the Luke in San Antonio, which was top notch. So when a friend wanted to go during our recent trip to NOLA, I didn't hesitate. I wish I did.

Every single one of our dishes were extremely salty. One of us had the burger and the other had the shrimp and grits. We couldn't finish our food after a few bites because it was so salty. And sadly, we both got sick for a few hours after leaving Luke's. 

I was hoping for the same performance I received at the San Antonio location but was greatly disappointed. I will never visit the NOLA location when I visit the city again. The NOLA location could learn a lot from the Texas location.

Luke's used to be one of my go-to places when people would come in from out of town, but since it opened it has gone down hill. 

The management is terrible. I think that this is the main reason their food, but especially their service, has gone down hill. It is not uncommon to wait 20-30 minutes after being seated to get your drinks or after your food is taken away and your waiting for the bill. Sometimes the food is brought out cold or in the wrong order or just plain forgotten.

However, I still like to eat there because they have my favorite thing on the entire earth which is a croque madame. Also their pates and foie gras are very very very good. And I love their happy hour oysters, SUCH a good deal during the week day (the service is also usually much better mid-day). 

So do go! But expect the service to suck and don't be afraid to assert yourself.

Yes it is pricey but the service and food here is IMMACULATE. On every visit to NOLA I have to have Lüke's Louisiana shrimp and grits. Very small portion (seems to get smaller each year) but they do not skimp on the flavor. This dish is seriously made with love: cheese grits made to perfection, large, juicy perfectly flavored shrimp, roumalade is out of this world. I do not eat red meats, so I remove the andouille from the dish. Pricey but so VERY worth it. Champagne au peche is a must have as well. It gets pretty busy around lunch time so go for breakfast if you can. From the hostess to the server to management, you will be treated like royalty. Easily 5 stars.

had the red beans and rice. amazing. like seriously i loved it so much, especially the fried chicken - it was so much better than the pork which itself was already very delicious. however it was a biiiiiig portion and towards the end i just felt like i was gonna die eating it lol.

This Central Business District located restaurant will not disappoint in my opinion.I can't say much about this restaurant but I will say they have the best Happy Hour for beers  and Oysters! From 3:00pm -6:00pm they have $0.75 cent raw oysters,  $1.25 for the fried oysters and Half Priced Select Beers, Cocktails, and Wine by the Glass. I don't know what you know but this is the best deal I've heard of in a long time. 

Get there on-time, the bar and dining room area fill up pretty quick!

From what I viewed they have a traditional menu that has a French/German/Creole themed selection by the renowned chef/restaurateur John Besh.

Oysters are fresh and only $0.75 each during happy hour, but shell chips left on oysters and ruin the texture. Grill oysters are good at taste but too oily. Fried oysters are over cooked and too salty. One star for the price and fresh oyster, another star for the service and environment.
Unpleasant place. Unpleasant, inattentive bartenders. Foul-mouthed clientele.Food not bad but wouldn't come back.

Found this place on Yelp as I just travel here for business for a few days. 
Nice decoration in the restaurant to begin with.
Decent food with great portion. Friendly staff and definitely help to modify the fish to your liking. Good selection of rolls and we will probably try Sashimi next time. :p
I would say ~$35 will get you very full. And my favorite picks are in the pictures. :)
Food was delicious! Staff was friendly and accommodating, and very knowledgeable with the menu.

Hands down one of my favorite restaurants. I have eaten here several times and it's always consistently great, no matter what I order. My go-to dishes are that amazing Luke burger with caramelized onions, Allen Benton bacon, and Emmenthaler cheese; the salad Luke; the flamenkuche; and the croque monsieur. And the French 75, of course!
We have been here 3 times and I am so obsessed with this place. Check out their happy hour. You will not be disappointed!

This place is awesome! The happy hour they have is unmatched. $0.75 oysters and half off on all cocktails from 3- 6pm at the bar! I recommend getting the French 75! I think it's the best French 75 I ever had at a bar/restaurant. 

The service is top notch also! They staff are so friendly and helpful. They even gave us some free oysters after we already finished our order of oysters.

I've eaten dinner at the Luke's in San Antonio and the food is definitely delicious . I'm sure the food at this location  is just as good or better! The oysters definitely are delicious. We will definitely be back for happy hour. The oysters here are better than anything we've had in the French Quarter.

We visited for happy hour drinks and oysters but ended up ordering a few extra things. Oysters were delicious and fresh and the bisque was the best I've ever had - I ordered a second bowl. The service and atmosphere was welcoming and very friendly.

Just had to try John Besh's place in NOLA.  I am so glad I did as it was well worth the experience.  We started out with a dozen of oysters on the half shell and they were so fresh and delightful.  We then had the fried oyster and avocado salad which was very tasty.  It had big chunks of bacon in addition to a very tasty dressing.  
   For the main course I had the ribeye with Bearnaise sauce which was good to perfection.  The Bearnaise sauce was amazing.  The wife had the Cajun pasta with Gulf shrimp which I tried and it was very good.  We made a reservation which was a good idea as they were very busy. 
   the service was perfect - attentive but not to overbearing.  They serve coke in little bottles which was a neat thing since we were in the South.  A nice way to finish our 4 day trip to NOLA.

We came in just after they opened for some breakfast. We almost had the place to ourselves at 7 am. New Orleans parties hard and sleeps in!

We got the Southern breakfast: bacon, sausage, grits, biscuit, and eggs. We also ordered coffee and a side of fruit. 

The bacon and sausage both had a nice smoky flavor. The grits were unlike any I've had before. The waitress said they mix in mascarpone cheese which gives them their unique flavor and texture. They were so tasty, and our toddler wolfed down a good portion of them!

The coffee was delicious, and it's free refills on regular coffee. 

The restaurant is a neat place and I suppose the only downside may be if you need to park somewhere. I did not see much public parking around. However it is right near the St. Charles streetcar stop at Poydras, so at least there is another way to get there. We just walked across the street from our hotel!

After a bit of Yelp research into really great breakfast places in the area, we headed over to Luke. It was a Sunday morning so I made a reservation so we could avoid a wait if there was one. We arrived and were shown to our table right away. Our waiter was not really friendly but efficient and pretty attentive. We ordered the Croque Madame and the Fried Chicken and Waffles. He had the gumbo to start. 
The place started to get busier as it approached noon - diners were crowding into the entry to await a table. Our food came quickly. The presentation was impressive. My Croque Madame was good, not the best I've had but food quality and piled high with lean ham. It was not hot, a little more like warm. It would have been better hot. My guy loved his meal and enjoyed the pepper jelly served with the chicken.  
We agreed that it was good enough to warrant a trip back in the future for lunch or dinner. Great location off the beaten path and away from the touristy part of the  Quarter.  Satisfied and pleased with our find, we started our day with a smile and full bellies.

Bartenders are really friendly and nice. Had the Saison named Desire, Salad Luke, and half dozen Gulf shrimp. The salad Luke is a great salad for salad lovers -- chock full of a variety of vegetables including tomatoes, beets, and I believe it was orange segments. I was really glad I ordered it! My friend got the oysters which are a good deal during happy hour. She said they weren't chewy at all (unlike most oysters she's had).

Right by my office so i eat here a lot,  but this is consistently one of the worst chipotles I've ever been to. Service is slow, they don't seem to be particularly interested/concerned with customers' time, and they always seem to be low/out of peppers, which is one of my favorite things. Also, they are EXTREMELY skimpy on the ingredient amounts, especially when i order online

A misstep for breakfast.

Came in based on positive reviews. The hostess was nowhere to be seen. The bartender - or whoever she was that was cleaning the bar area - and a waiter was chatting. They saw us and neither greeted us, nor did they look for the hostess. We stood there awkwardly for 5 minutes before a CUSTOMER got up and asked us if we were waiting to be seated. When we said yes, the customer went around the other side of the bar to tell the hostess. Turns out she was enjoying her coffee and checking her phone at one end of the bar, her back to the host station.

The waiter was courteous. We had the shrimp and grits and the fried chicken with tabasco honey. The shrimp and grits were very good, but the fried chicken was a miss for me - sounds good in theory but tasted, for lack of a better word, confused in its execution. Completely subjective though.

The rest of the service was all right. Attentive waiter and we were able to get our check and leave in time to make an morning appointment elsewhere. No one thanked us or said good-bye as we left. For a classy place like Luke, there is usually more attentive service. Maybe we just experienced an off-morning, but given the price point and overall presentation of the restaurant, the service left something to be desired. Had originally planned to return to try the oysters, but opted not to based on morning experience.
Great food, great service! Very classy place and clean. Highly recommend this place. Group of 6 people. Sat us quick. You might want to call before hand to reserve a table.

I LOVE their steakhouse gorgonzola sandwich with a side of buffalo sauce.  It's my recent obsession.  Prices are reasonable for the good quality food.  Service can be a bit slow.  Overall I'm a huge fan!

Happy hour here was off the hook. 50 cent oysters the size of my hand?! Crazy. We basically ate all we could stand for the price of a dozen back home in California. Nice but small beer selection with half price bottles during happy hour (if you're from out of town and are a beer snob, you have to try the pecan beer from the Lazy Magnolia Brewery in Kiln, Mississippi - home of Brett Favre! At least the town produced something good.). 

Also, the Luke burger (no special happy hour pricing, but worth it anyway) was amazing. We ordered it and were later informed that it was ranked by someone who knows such things (we forget which magazine) as a "Top 10" in the country - well deserved. 

The only bad thing is that with so many amazing restaurants in New Orleans, we weren't able to make it in for a regular meal this trip. We'll put that on the agenda for our next visit.

A friend recommended Luke for the food, and he wasn't wrong. During a recent class, my fellow students and I, after a bad experience elsewhere, ended up eating here most days. We each had the special offered which took us through amazing ettoufe, gumbo and jambalaya. We ordered salads and fries and coffee. The service was fantastic. The beet salad and their regular salad were delicious. The fries were crispy. And the crispy brussels were beyond amazing!

The **only** thing (4 instead of 5 stars) was the jambalaya, which was overy salty. And not just a little, a LOT! We were in a huge hurry each day with less than an hour to eat and walk back to class so we couldn't send anything back, plus the specials (as we understood it) were made in advance (maybe that morning) so we would have had to ask for something different and wait, which we didn't have the time to do.

Regardless, I loved Luke and so did all my fellow students.
Just went for a late dinner. Our appetizer was never put in and when we inquired about it, it showed up with our meal. Disappointed in the dinner visit. Interested in trying out breakfast/brunch.

Nice enough restaurant. Excellent service and ambience, but I wasn't floored by the food. I went in with the expectation for real Cajun, New Orleans food so that might of been what messed me up. If your after authenticity, try something else. But if you just want a nice meal in a nice place, give it try.

Luke's was good especially the Happiest Hour! I think the happy hour starts at 3p. They have some drink specials and specials on the raw and fried oysters! However my bill by myself still ended up over $50! Oh maybe because of this awesome Cognac/champagne drink they make. But I enjoyed the happy hour and food and drinks and will
Be back! Btw TD Jakes came to dine while I was there and I was able to shake his hand. It was a honor to meet him and he was very pleasant to meet!
I had my first breakfast here in New Orleans. Try the southern breakfast, their ham is delicious!!!

Did the Happy hour specials. Cant beat .50 oysters and 1/2 price drinks. Large, salty oysters! We sat at the bar and service wasn't super fast and had to ask for another beer- twice. Wish we would have returned for dinner instead of cabbing it to Cochon later that night.

This is one of my favorite stops. I've done both lunch and dinner here and have been very satisfied with every meal. During Christmas they had a eggnog cocktail which was super tasty. They also had lamb which was perfectly cooked. Try sitting by the kitchen, a nice view and show to watch the team cook up your meal.

Okay so this is just an update, still 5 stars but just want to leave some feedback. I ordered some king salmon sushi pieces and was really disappointed when the fish was very cold and the rice was very warm. That should be a foundation. Also got the "Aromatic Duck Roll" which was good, nice flavours but I would just tell someone reading this to order something else, like the waitress said it's nothing special. I only ordered it because I thought it was the same duck dish that I had gotten before. I still highly recommend Hachi and will be coming back many of times.

Great service, great vibe. Food was delicious but a little non-traditional which is not my preference. MAKE SURE you order the s'mores torte for dessert. Top 3 dessert in the United States in my opinion.

Best Chinese food in Lutz, and perhaps the whole bay area. I've lived in Lutz my entire life and am sad to say I'd never been here before. After reading so many great reviews I tried and was not let down. Clean! Friendly! Delicious! And pipping hot food! Why have I never discovered this earlier - I'm so mad I've been eating bad Chinese food for so long. Give it a try. I loved it.

Forget the food for a second. It's always sweltering hot in New Orleans. Wherever you go, you sweat. Every part of your body is moist - and not in the "I just ate a deliciously moist cupcake" kind of way. You're walking all over town. You're hungry, but you're not thinking about food. You're thinking about cooling off. You could go to the casino, or perhaps stop into a hotel lobby for a quick respite from the heat and humidity. But if you really want to cool off - if you really want to turn your body's moistness into a chilly frost and bring your temperature down to almost absolute zero - stop into Lüke.

Lüke restaurant is, without a doubt, the coldest restaurant on Earth, and perhaps beyond. If you sit directly beneath the cooling vent like my wife and I did - both times we visited, no less - you could probably die.  Or, if you're like me, you'll absolutely love it. I'm a polar bear and find myself in my natural habitat when I am here. Thank you, thank you, John Besh. Thank you, Lüke. Thank you for being a freezing cold oasis in an otherwise deathly urban desert.

Now onto the food...

As I mentioned before, my wife and I came here twice. That is, two times, during a 4-day vacation. In a place like New Orleans where there is SO MUCH good food everywhere you look, it is almost sacrilege to eat in the same place twice in one trip. (Good thing it was so hot out.)

The first time we came in for breakfast, and it was awesome. I had the classic southern staple: a fried chicken biscuit with a spicy mayhaw glaze. I have no idea what the hell mayhaw is, but it was so yummy and decadent, I felt like I needed to be spanked afterward. My wife had the egg white frittata, complete with burrata cheese and Covey Rise vegetables. (Whatever that means.) For a healthy dish, it looked absolutely delicious. She loved it. 

Of course, breakfast in New Orleans would not be complete without the obligatory basket of powdered beignets.  You can get them with chocolate dipping sauce or a fresh berry jam. We opted for the blueberry jam. Absolutely amazing. 

Lüke also makes a mean Bloody Mary - almost a little too mean for my taste. It's not that I mind the spiciness.  In fact, I love that. But the Lüke Bloody Mary is just so crimson red and flavorfully intense, with an eerie viscosity that reminds me a little too much of actual blood. Still, try one. Just one gave me a buzz that lasted all morning long.

The second time we came for brunch. No chicken biscuit on this menu, but lots of other options. I was so hungover during this meal that as I am drafting this review on a plane with no Internet, I can't even remember off the top of my head what the hell me or my wife ordered, but I do remember it being really good. (For more on my hangover, see my review for the Clover Café.)

UPDATE: Having cheated and looked back at the menu, I can now recall our bizarre order: the heirloom tomato salad, Mimi's buttermilk pancakes with the honey-pecan butter, and an order of the house fries. We just shared it all, and no evidence remained once we were done. Yeah, everything is that good.

All in all I would give Lüke a solid 4.5 stars. But since Yelp doesn't allow half-star ratings, I'm more than happy to give Lüke a 5.  Service was very friendly both times, though they do get busy and it may be a little difficult to get your check. But at least they don't try to rush you out and turn your table. I really hate that. (For more on how much I hate that, see my review for Emeril's.)

Bottom line: Don't skip Lüke if you come to New Orleans.

It was mouse poop in my food!!!! Smh want to give them a 0! I talk to the owner And he didn't signs surprised at all offered for my food to be free NEXT time lol like as if I would eat from there ever again!

I have worked in the back of the house for six years now and have an understanding of how things should be run in restaurant. This restaurant lacks quality of service and attention to detail which seperates the good places from the great. The concept is good but execution does not follow. The front of the house was extremely disorganized and had obvious problems with management. Sanitation is a basic category that all food service establishments should be competent in. I witnessed, through the windows of the open kitchen, eating and drinking on the line, the exec chef  constantly running his hands through his sweaty hair then proceed to plate food. Not one person sanitized stations or put on the pair of gloves to plate ready to eat foods. Beyond the procedural pitfalls the food was very mediocre, over seasoned and over cooked. One of my appitzers came with a "suprise" slice of salami stuck under a ramikcan. Another issue I had was that the napkins that customers used were the same towels the kitchen used, and the vessel for the bread.  This place came highly recommend and I left very dissapointed. I was looking forward to trying a john besh restaurant but I would have to say "SKIP IT." go to Provence or Besh Steak or Domenica.

We are in town for my friend's 21st birthday and we chose the right place for a celebratory birthday dinner!

We had a party of 4 and we came around 5:30 PM and we're seated right away! Everyone was so incredibly friendly. We were greeted with smiles and upon seating, the hostess knew our name. 

The restaurant itself is very big, with multiple areas for seating, the front section has a bar, and the back area is more quiet. We were seated in the back right next to the open kitchen, where through a glass window, we saw the chefs prepare the food. We were greeted by two waiters, Jesse and Zain (I hope I spelled that right) and they were so friendly and professional. I loved the way they filled the water for the ladies first, then the gentlemen. Most people don't see those details but I caught it and was very pleasantly surprised. We were instructed through the menu and given recommendations and we loved everything they recommended!

HAPPY HOUR is from 3PM-6PM which includes a deal of: $0.75 Raw Oysters and $1.25 Fried Oysters! The drinks are all half off as well, I believe. It is such a steal for such a great place. We ordered 3 dozen raw oysters, half a dozen fried. We also ordered two cocktails! We told our waiters that it was my friend's birthday, and when they presented the drinks for us, they had "21" written on the foam in his! It was so cute! Then, we were given our first round of food. As we were eating, they presented us with a dish and said it was on the house. I was so surprised to be treated so well! For dessert, we got a free order of bread pudding for my friend's birthday as well. They came out and sang for him, and embarrassed him just the right amount LOL

The raw oysters were served on ice and were so fresh. I wasn't expecting the fried oysters to be as good but they were amazing as well! The presentation is great for pictures as well. The brussel sprout dish was so delicious. Even if you are not a vegetable (or brussel sprout) loving person, the sauce was so good I'm positive you'll fall in love as well! The bread pudding was topped with candied pecans and a scoop or vanilla bean ice cream! It was just the right balance of creamy, crunchy, hot, and cold. I would come here just for the birthday dessert, if I could. 

The service was out of this world. I have been to a variety of places on my trip here but this restaurant has got to have the best service to date. The amount of intricacy they put into serving and how friendly they are is amazing! The servers are very professional, polite, and helpful! If you ever go, ask for Jesse and Zain! They were so awesome. 

Our tab came out to be under $45 for 3 dozen oysters, half a dozen fried oysters, and a cocktail, which is great. I would absolutely recommend coming here if you are looking for a great experience with delicious food for an unbeatable price. It's the perfect place for birthday celebrations! I will definitely be returning when I come to visit NOLA again. Till next time!!

Lots of beer . The pizza here is amazing and big. Wings are crispy and delicious. 
sometimes they have bands and it makes it way to crowded, but on the average night  it's great.

Came here for a Saturday night dinner at 7pm for a party of four with a reservation. The taste and quality of the food exceeded my expectations. Highly recommend checking this place out if  you're looking for a nice, sit-down restaurant in New Orleans.

We got the crispy brussel sprouts which were the best brussel sprouts I've ever remembered having. They were in this sweet, rich sauce and honestly it's a must-try. We got it to share and it went so quickly. The cheesy jalapeno grits were also a hit, though paled in comparison to the brussel sprouts.

I ordered the seafood gumbo for my entree and I loved it. The seafood in it was so fresh - especially the oyster in it, which was cooked to perfection. Granted, I don't have much experience with gumbo but this one tasted exceptional to me.

For my drink, I got the apparently famous french 75. It was aesthetically appealing to see how frothy it was, but I didn't really care for the flavor. I think all of the egg whites in the drink kind of added an unpleasant aftertaste to the cocktail. Wish I had ordered something else.

We got the smores tarte to share and that was very good. As a bread pudding lover I wish I had tried that for dessert, but the smores was good for sharing and also tasty.

A go to that I take all my visitors to when they come to New Orleans. Great raw bar selections, the tuna tartare and crab ravigote are my go to appetizers. The salads are enormous and so fresh. The steak was cooked perfectly. Shrimp and grits and the French 75 are the best in the city!

Very friendly & fast service. Large selection with many new & interesting choices. Very nice interior. My wife and I want to go back again soon. Miso soup with Shitake mushrooms was good. Avenger roll & Holiday roll were both very good as was the Asian pear salad.

Luke was recommended by a local to us. We trekked to this spot from a local Irish dive bar. I cannot emphasize how AMAZING this place is! Check it out- great impeccable service, delicious food, stellar cocktails and we did the happy hour which of course made our meal that much more fantastic! Oh and get the Brussels sprouts!
Wow! Chicken and Waffles, Shrimp and Grits as well as the traditional!!! All were simply delicious. Service was plus 5 stars... shall return

Our bellman, Jonathan, at the Courtyard Marriott At St Charles, recommended this place after a long trip from Beaumont, Texas, and a $10 tip.   

The place is world class!  We went in with appetizers in mind at 8:30 and left after the Bayou Rum Cake in a strawberry sauce.  If you like crawfish, get the appetizer on sourdough covered in crawfish and a white cheese was a hit.

I rarely post 5 stars!!

I felt like I wasted my time to come here I am not interested in raw oysters. I was under the impression they had other oysters they sold in singles by themselves. Quite a walk from French Quarter to come here. The selection of the cocktails is very very very minimal I was confused why that is.  This is more of a place to go if you're staying at a hotel nearby and don't want to go out of your way. The entrées looked good but they're very small and pricey I came for happy hour I was disappointed they didn't have a bigger selection.

Showed up 45 minutes before they closed with a group of 6 and we still got amazing service! Tristan was our server and did an amazing job! Food was amazing, and I feel we spoiled ourselves for the rest of our trip, as this was the first place we tried!

To top it off, we were in NOLA celebrating my brother's 21st birthday and they surprised us with some amazing bread pudding!
A Great Place for lunch for those of us who work downtown. Order a burger and ask them to cut in half so you dont have to do it at the table.  Generous Portion

This is genuinely one of our favorite places in the city. We've been for dinner several times and yesterday had our first brunch and it was EGGS-ceptional. (My sincere apologies. I couldn't help myself.) 

The brunch is ON POINT. The menu is small and excellently curated with a billion ways to mix and match large and small plates. We opened with a French 75 and a Bloody and an order of Berliners. The French 75 was topped with a foam of what we guessed were champagne kissed egg whites and there was a cherry in there. Not the French 75 that I'm accustomed to, but delicious. The Bloody Mary was spicy and smooth and outstanding. Our waiter asked for vodka choice and we chose Titos- not that you can tell once it's added to a Bloody Mary but it was spicy and velvety. A Berliner is a German donut with no hole and usually filled and fits into the German-Franco vibe here beautifully. The basket was big and we ate three before we asked them to be packed up. There was a tangy apple butter in them, if I recall...

For the big show, my husband got the Flammenkuchen and I got the Fried Chicken Biscuit. His only critique was that some of the lardons were cut really thickly and hadn't really rendered so he has some pieces of fat that he gathered to the side. Don't mistake, he ate the whole thing. When they set down my plate the people at the next table said "OHMYGOD." I offered them a seat if they wanted to come help but they stayed put. More for me!!!! And Jesus, was this thing every bit of joy. Two pieces of chicken on a biscuit drizzled with Tabasco Honey and topped with a yard egg, it took me a minute to plan my attack. (Pro tip: cut the biscuit in half, top each side with a piece of the chicken, and half the egg too. You've got two little chicken Benedicts and don't have to break out the climbing equipment to get to the top of that thing. Seriously, it's like 10" tall on arrival.) 

We got a side of the Rosemary Potatoes which is what I imagine they serve at the cafeteria in heaven and the Joe Fekete vegetables. I ate most of those with my hands. They were just amazing. 

We took a small break in the middle but both cleaned our plates. Our waiter Elliot was so tickled for us that he offered complimentary coffee. It was a Nicaraguan blend and put the pep back in our step. It came with a little pewter creamer of what we suspect was not half and half but, rather, heavy cream. And maybe everyone gets the free coffee but if you're offered it, say yes. Trust me. 

We were both full but not sick and even didn't really need dinner that night. But we did eat the rest of those Berliners. ;)

Since they opened they have gone through some good and bad times. 
I will say that not every meal I have had here is enjoyable and the service can vary from poor to wonderful. There was a period where I believe the management was horrible: the food was poorly timed, was not checked properly before it went to the table, friendliness sketchy at best. But I believe they have recovered. 

I love this place for two reasons: happy hour oysters (which of the 15 times I have had them here have only been less than wonderful once) and the croque Madame. 
The froi is amazing (A+) the skate wonderful, shrimp and grits good, egg in a jar yum, bloody Mary GREAT!
This place is kinda awesome. Go hungry.

If you are looking for 5-Star dining, or the BEST of any particular dish, you are in the wrong spot. But, if you are looking for really good food, a fun and knowledgeable wait and bartender staff (not to mention the best looking in NOLA) you have found your spot. I have eaten everywhere in NOLA, French Quarter, Warehouse District, every freakin' hotel and this place is right at the top for a satisfying, loud, get your buzz on, sexy, delicious bit of forget the day's business with a bowl of mussels and fries and more aperitifs than you can remember or shake a stick at, not too mention their own brews, a ruckus happy hour with crab and oysters and did I mention the best looking wait staff & bartendrixes in NOLA. You won't mind spending the little extra ...

I visited Luke on my first time to New Orleans. I had read a couple blogs that had mentioned the restaurant and being a big Top Chef fan, and knowing who John Besh is, I had to try it. I really enjoyed the atmosphere however, there isn't anywhere to stand inside while you wait for your table. They do take reservations, so I definitely recommend doing that.

For starters we got a couple of bottles of red wine for the table. They were moderately priced, not too expensive. Then we got the Assiette de Charcuterie for an appetizer. I thought this contained cheese, but it didn't, so that was my fault for not being too excited when I saw a tray of unrecognizable meats. However, I will say all the ones I tried were good.

For my meal I had the Louisiana Blue Crab Cavatelli. It was really great but the portion was pretty small in my opinion. Since we were gearing up for a night out on Bourbon Street, I was hoping a pasta dish would provide me the perfect base. I did get the chance to try some of my friends left over Entrécote Grillee et Frites which was my favorite of everything we ordered so I wished I had spent the extra $8 for it.

Overall, a good restaurant, but I think for the amount of money spent, I might have found a more filling entree.

I am disappointed with my experience at Luke. Reviews tallying 4 stars suggested a good experience, but i must not have ordered the right thing- the organic quinoa bowl. The bowl is cold- quinoa and roasted vegetables. The poached egg was warm and perfect, but the salad came smothered in a horseradish dressing. It may not have been that bad, but horseradish was never mentioned in the menu, so it was a surprise and WAY too overwhelming. The cheese was tasteless and the many many cherry tomatoes were mostly over- ripe and squishy.  I won't return since there are so many great restaurants in NOLA.

I am not doing back flips, but I will be back to try the bread pudding.  
I had the crab stuffed shrimp. Three huge shrimp stuffed with crab served along side potatoes and cauliflower- the shrimp tasted like crab cakes. It was filling even though the plate was small.  My friend had muscles and a beet salad that she swears by, and it did look good.   
I liked the decor but I was upset by the fact that the hostess tried to sit us in the back room when the front was empty.

So we went back for dinner the day after New Years with friends and it was just as good if not better. Best bite this time was the stone ground grits that came with the shrimp n grits. Wow! We also got lucky again and had Richie as our server - you won't find a better waiter!

I'm gluten intolerant so this was on my list of restaurants in Nola that provide a gluten free menu. Most of the regular dinner menu with a few tweaks here and there I was able to have. I chose the fresh oysters to start which were very good although a couple hard pretty big chunks of grit in them. My partner got them baked which smelled divide topped with their garlicky cheesy goodness. The beet salad was good too although the beets were cooked a little longer than I normally like. The dressing was the perfect tangy amount of top. I chose the ribeye with sautéed vegetables on the server's suggestion. This is the main reason I gave this place 3 stars instead of 4. My steak came out thin and ragged where one of my friends who ordered the same thing got a nice thick juicy cut.  I understand the fat content can make the cut look like mine did but it's disappointing nonetheless when two steaks arrive at the same table with this extreme disparity.  I also ordered mine rare but it came out more medium instead.  This irritates me the most when ordering a steak. But I will say the sautéed vegetables were some of the best ever- perfectly cooked with great garlic seasoning.
I did give Luke a second try at brunch the next day since it was right around the corner from our hotel and again the gluten free knowledge. I got the crab omelet which was impressive with it's fresh large chunks of crab meat inside. But I also wanted the grits and was informed they weren't gluten free. Why add wheat to a wonderful product of corn is beyond me.  My partner did get to enjoy the jalapeño cheese grits which he found thick, rich, and very good.

After attempting to eat a burger at Port O' Call, but being told there was a 45 minute wait. My friend and I remembered Luke being written up on Yelp, so we headed over to the Business District for a late lunch. 

Upon entering, the space is a great mix of New Orleans and a french bistro. Beautiful wood floors, white table cloths, etc... 

The menu has a heavy German/Swiss/Alsatian influence.  So, they have an extensive offering of beers and interesting cocktails. I went traditional N.O. and the Bloody Mary with Okra and green beans was tangy and yummy. I added more black pepper. 

We ordered the flatbread with emmenthaler cheese, bacon, and caramelized onions to start. The bread was thin and crispy with all of the yummy toppings. It was delicious, but their were too many toppings. It could have done well with less cheese. 

For an entree, I ordered the Luke burger. The fresh ground meat of the patty was amazing! It was topped with lettuce, tomato, caramelized onions, bacon and emmenthaler cheese. Outstanding Burger and crispy frites... The only drawback was that the burger had such a similar taste to the flatbread appetizer! 

My friend had the fried oyster salad with avocado. Apparently some of the best fried oysters ever...there was nothing left in the bowl! 

All in all a great experience. I would recommend Luke for a late lunch or dinner.

I love this place! I had just landed in New Orleans for the first time and wanted to catch a meal before it got dark. I yelped and found this place to be conveniently a couple of blocks or so from the hotel I was staying at. Traveling alone on a budget, I wanted to catch their unbelievable happy hour, which I believe runs M-F from 3-6pm. Can't beat their $0.50 raw oysters and half-off drinks!

I arrived at the restaurant around 5pm on a Thursday and was immediately greeted by a hostess. No wait whatsoever! I decided to sit at the bar, which probably sits around 10 people. Sitting at the bar is great if you want to be immediately seated, watch sport games, or chat with the friendly shuckers.

The first thing I ordered were the raw oysters and they were amazing!! I never knew my love for raw oysters until I came to this place (I don't get to experience this kind of freshness back home in Los Angeles). I also ordered the Luke burger and French 75. The burger was huge and it also came with homemade fries. I ended up taking half my burger to go. Even as microwaved leftover, the burger still remained juicy and tender. I would rate it as #3 on my list of best burgers. The French 75 is a must-try! It's a nice blend of cognac, lemon juice, and champagne. Best cocktail drink I have ever tried!

I would definitely come back to this place next time I'm in New Orleans. Since it's located in the Business District, it beats the constantly overcrowded French Quarter restaurants if you just want a quick fix of oysters and drinks.
Not my favorite place.  It's waaay expensive for simple foods.   It's like Zea's except that they charge double!  My friends love the oysters and oyster prices, but I'm just not an oyster person.

I went for Happy Hour oysters over French Quarter fest weekend and definitely got my money's worth from the food. Four dozen oysters, a sandwich and drinks between two of us came out to be around $60.

 We called ahead and were assured that we had to get there early or they couldn't accommodate us, which might have been because it was FQF weekend, but the place was empty upon our arrival and had plenty of seats available when we left.  Being rushed in early and the attitude that accompanied that cost them a star in my review when added to the "lukewarm" service (sorry, couldn't resist). 

 I'd go back again when I can spare the time (shucking oysters takes a while) and when they can offer to accommodate me at an hour that doesn't make me feel like I'm too late for lunch and too early for dinner.

We ordered Boudin Louisianne and Crabmeat Masion for appetizers. Both were good. We ordered a few entree's and shared them. Love the shrimp and grits!!! We ordered the Luke burger. The burger was good. The fries were just okay. I think they were too greasy. We also had the crab and corn bisque which was very tasty.  We also had the court bouillon. (Definitely a small portion..) The portion sizes are small on most entrees so sharing was good for our group to taste a few things on the menu. The bread pudding was okay. Good food overall !!!

The service was great and the food even better. I had the 'pressed pig sandwich' and it was incredible. It is a toasted sandwich with the perfect fixins.  I could have gone across the street and down one block and had a toasted Quiznos sandwich for 1/3 the price, but it would have been a mistake!  If you like toasted sandwiches, you can't skip this one.

Came here for their awesome oyster happy hour. Great fresh, good sized oysters and half off all drinks - can't go wrong with both! The Crawfish Bisque is absolutely divine with a perfect consistency and chunks of crawfish. I wish I could've ordered a gallon to go, it was that good. Heard this place has the best shrimp and grits, so I'll be back.
Amazing food. Great service, the shrimp are amazing and fresh. The Gulf Fish are the best though. If you are around Canal Street the restaurant is one you cannot miss.

First meal in New Orleans. Easter Sunday at 9 PM meant plenty of tables. 

Loved the shrimp and grits ($25), crawfish bread ($16), crawfish bisque ($10), and blue crab gratin ($16). 

But definitely felt a pang of jealousy when I saw the rabbit and chicken liver pate ($11) hit the next table.

Tip: definitely order at least one shrimp and grits for the table

Had the opportunity to go to Luke's tonight with come great friends and had such a great meal and fantastic experience.  Not only was the food outstanding but the service was amazing.  We were lucky enough to have Richard (AKA Richie Rich) who was an absolute delight.  He "read" the vibe of our group and played right along with us.

We were a little concerned when looking at the menu on line as we had some "picky" eaters in the group but everyone was able to find something that fit their tastes and all raved about the food by the time the meal was over.

Will definitely be a place we return to on the next trip to the Big Easy!!
It was a busy Monday night. Service was spotty. Our fries were cold and limp, the steak underdone. Drinks and oysters were good though. If you like salty food, get the shrimp and grits.
Easily some of the best sushi I've ever had. The presentation of their food is 5 star, gorgeous. Friendly staff, great atmosphere. This just became my "go-to" sushi place. Amazing!

The food was amazing. We came in for a mid afternoon snack and drinks. We had the quail, rum cake, blue crab, and the brussel sprouts for the food. Everything was delicious! The drinks we ordered were good, but it took a long time to get a lemonade and a Riesling. A very long time as in they must have forgotten them. Maybe just an off day.
First time in new Orleans  and needed my nails done so came to first place we seen. The lady made me bleed not happy.

During our 4 day stay in New Orleans, we went Luke twice. The happy hour deals are a steal. On our first visit, our waiter had suggested the flamenkuche. It was mouth watering amazing. The service, the food, and the deals were so good, we had to go twice.

the shrimp n grits and grilled oysters were yummy. great service in the middle of mardi gras weekend .the burger looked ridic and most couples were sharing one with each having their own truffle fries. check it out! Great bar as well, enjoyed it very much

I totally forgot to review this place!

This was one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans!

$.50 cents oysters during happy hour. This is a deal that can not be beat!! For all you Californians, beware, these are not the typical small kumomodo oysters. These are some big guys, but still very good!

I had the Shrimp with Jalapeno Grits, He had the Special, Pork with grits, both were amazing and the portion after eating 2 dozen oysters and ordering 2 happy hour drinks each. His special came with a bowl of gumbo, and we were even given a free delicious bread pudding.

The total you ask? We paid $86 for 4 drinks, 24 oysters, 2 entrees with one gumbo and a complimentary dessert.

Wow LUKE! Way to go!! Thanks for making us feel totally at home and welcome at your restaurant. I am itching to go back just to eat here again.

They were very accommodating to our breakfast menu request even though it was 11:15 and they stopped serving breakfast at 11. It literally made our day. 

We started off with mimosas and bloody Mary's. I ordered the Crab omelet but it didn't live up to my expectations. The egg was a little runny for me and I didn't love the pesto sauce mixed in. 
My friend ordered the Southern breakfast and omg the grits were a fluffy cloud of heaven. The cheese and jalapeños mixed in made this the hottest dish of our dining experience.  My other friend got the Shrimp and grits which was our second favorite. Similar to the other grits but these had some sauce and jumbo shrimp tossed in.

They surprised us by giving us a few complimentary desserts which were mouthwatering. The bread pudding, crepe brûlée and pumpkin cheesecake were OMG Instagram worthy.

To go order: seafood gumbo, corn and crawfish bisque, bread pudding, and roasted brussel sprouts. 

4 stars with over 4k reviews, what could go wrong? Just about everything let's start with the worst dish, the seafood gumbo. The seafood gumbo can only be described as eating the leftover gravy from a smothered steak dinner. There was no seafood to be found in this dish only a few peices of sausage with a poor display of okra, DAMN Luke!!! Next up there was corn and crawfish bisque. This dish was more salty than I am right now it could have been a lot better, but there was crawfish so I guess that's a plus. The bread pudding is the only thing saving this place from 1 star, nice job Luke!!! The roasted brussel sprouts, a little too long on the roasted part. The first few layers of these tiny sprouts were complete ass...I mean ash. On the bright side someone told me they had the best burgers in N.O. don't think I want to find out.

Every single thing we ordered was amazing. Brussels sprouts are sweet with a bit of heat from finely sliced jalapeño. Crab omelette was big enough for two after the appetizer and came w crispy straw fries. We ordered a side of jalapeño grits which are normally such an after thought but stand alone as the best grits I have ever had. Pricey, yes... But you get what you pay for. I forgot to mention the service was great as well and Savannah was super sweet.

Ok Luke you and I will now remain in Holy matrimony.

I came back to LUKE because Chef John Besh was so disappointed from my bad experience that he wrote me personally on Yelp (Yes I died) and told me to contact his GM Mr. Mire to let him know what happened. I did just that and Mr. Mire invited me back to make up for the terrible experience. 

What was so awesome was not only does Chef John Besh keep an eye on what happens in his restaurants but his team is on top of quality control and never break a promise. I came in almost a year later and emailed Mr. Mire and he was very accommodating. I will never forget that, it was beyond hospitable.

My Co-worker and I came in and it was the best night ever because Chef John just so happened to be there that night filming a show about Oysters.

I stared at him filming like a little girl who is in love with a boy band, it was so cool I fanned out completely. 

Food
Beet salad with Butter lettuce-The freshest beets I have ever had, so sweet the ate like candy.

Crab dip-Creamy, light, with chunks of crab. Delicious and a nice start to the meal.

Shrimp and grits with crab-My go to favorite, the best I have ever had hands down. Lump crab, creamy grits, huge prawns, green onion, and a whole lot of love. This is a must have.

Rib eye steak-Perfectly cook, seasoned to perfection and the Frites that come with are so perfect. If you want a steak in NOLA this is the way to go.


Dessert-Bread pudding it is a solid dessert, I love the Steam chocolate cake better but they were giving these to every table complimentary because Chef. Besh was in the house.

Besides the incredible food, wonderful service and star sighting of the Great Chef Besh I appreciate them for going above and beyond to fix my terrible experience it is truly something that I will never forget and I will continue to come here every time I am in NOLA.

Thank you LUKE for being so fantastic.
Everything was delicious !!! Oysters , shrimp , and the Bread pudding was the best !!! The service was better thanks to Kris and Mike !!

We had lunch today at Luke's. First, the food was outstanding. We had oysters, crab dip (real crab by the way), shrimp and the Monday special. The oysters were meaty and sweet. The crab dip with crostini was the bomb. The boiled  shrimp was so flavorful that I could have eating 2 dozen! The lunch special was beans and rice with fried chicken. It was so good! The service was outstanding. Andrew, Jonathan and Calvin were great. Very attentive, engaging and fun! I would recommend Luke's highly.

Probably New Orleans' best restaurant. It's like a modern version of a classic New Orleans restaurant.

The crab gnocchi is something you must try. It's pricey, but real truffle isn't cheap. There aren't many people not considered foodies who have ever had truffle. So if you're curious, get this. The truffle shares the stage with the crabmeat and the gnocchi is just the delivery system. One of the best dishes I'ver had. I've been here about 4 times and have never been disappointed.

We ate at Luke on New Years Eve night. We had our own private room to accommodate all 15 of us. We started with some excellent appetizers that included pate foie gras and raw oysters. I had the mussels for my main course and they were cooked perfectly but needed just a little more flavor. My friends swordfish was incredibly savory. We finished the meal with a creme brule and some champagne which we later took to the roof to enjoy the fireworks. Service was good, however, the waitress incorrecly wrote down someones order but took no responsibilty for it when the wrong food came. She instead said my friend told her incorrectly what he wanted. Other than that small incident I was very impressed with everything else.

This was the best sushi I have had so far. I've been to ookah, JJ's, Noburo, and a bunch of others. 

The D&B roll was absolutely fantastic.
Very nice outpost. Friendly and attentive waitstaff. The raw oysters are great. An excellent fine dining choice.

My girlfriend and I loved this place. We hadn't originally planned to stop here on our trip but after walking by and checking out the dinner menu we added it to our list of things to do. The environment was great and our waitress was friendly and funny. The food was excellent. One of the highlights of our trip.

We had Crawfish Bisque, Seafood Gumbo a la Creole, Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte", and Fruge Farms Crawfish "Etouffée. We ended up sharing everything and couldn't decide who's dishes were better. I will definitely stop in again next time I'm in town.

Perfect!! After a weekend in New Orleans with mostly "off" service, our Easter brunch at Luke ended our trip on the highest note possible.
I was able to grab a last minute (literally 15 minutes in advance) reservation for a 1045 brunch.
Our server was fantastic. She started off with some drink specials- hubs got "the dude" which was a White Russian with a shot of espresso & I got a mimosa. While we waited on our drinks we perused the amazing brunch options. Literally everything sounded amazing. We narrowed things down to the newly added chicken & waffles & the crawfish etouffee.
The chicken & waffles was delicious- a full waffle & two large pieces of boneless chicken, topped with a pepper jelly & a sweet butter. The chicken was really crisp & the combination of the two toppings gave a nice balance.
But the star of the meal- the crawfish etouffee- OMG. Probably one of the best things I've ever eaten in my life. I am still dreaming of this dish & regret not being able to finish it. The crawfish were in season & were tasty, but the crispy rice- I'm obsessed. I have no idea how they do this, but I'm determined to find out. It was perfectly seasoned. I cannot stress how amazing this dish was (I luckily stopped halfway through to snap a pic), but order this!!

We asked the wait staff what  was the best pizza, our #1 mistake- I barely made it the 3 miles home before my insides came out of me . I will NEVER return to this place even if they offered FREE food and drink

I posed the question, and NO's Yelpers answered.
Having time for only one meal in NO, Besh or Emeril?  Overwhelming majority suggested John Besh.  Having been a fan since "the next iron chef"(which he was completely robbed), it was hard to turn down the opportunity to dine in his restaurant.
Service:  friendly and knowledgeable server Matt took good care of us with recommendations and prompt service.  
Ambiance:  clean, modern, casual
Food:  we ordered the following - Oyster Salad, stuffed crab ravioli, steam mussel, seafood gumbo, fresh local veg stir-fried, and the duck egg crème brule.  The fried oysters were lightly breaded and fried to perfection, the steam mussel is delicious with its herb/light cream sauce, the seafood gumbo was deep and rich in flavor, and the duck egg crème brule was absolutely velvet smooth.
Value:  priced reasonably, we had the entire meal above for about $120 with  1/2 bottle of wine.  
Verdict: Luke lived up to Besh's reputation and I would recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting the area looking for a casual but upscale dinning.
We love this place. The seafood was unbelievable, fresh and well prepared, especially the oysters! The hamburger was amazing. We will definitely return on our next stay in NOLA.

Tuesday night it was packed. I guess due to holiday season.. saw alot of family.. we normally dont like to sit at the bar but we both were pretty starving so just decided to sit at the bar. It took forever to get the food. Wait staff came to us and apologize that the kitchen is extremely busy.
