Appetizer shrimp shumai was served with two rolls we ordered ... appetizer was not .. hmm.. tasteless... should have ordered gyoja instead.... and the rolls were good but seafood udon was taking way too long so we ended up canceling the order and changed to two more rolls... we love their food , wait staff were kept apologizing. And at the end, served us dessert on the house for late service. I love the decoration of food.

My sister and I had a quick 4 day get away to NOLA. This restaurant was right around the corner from our hotel, Le Pavillion, and it was highly recommended by them.  WE AGREE!!!  The service was just wonderful and the brussel sprouts, out of this world.  The waiter even gave us the recipe.  Wine was wonderful and the establishment was just too cool.  We will certainly go again on our next trip.

I came to this place twice during my stay. One day was with my girls. We came in without reservations and begged the hostess for a table. She told us we had to go to the bar because they were booked for the night. We did, and then were told if we could eat quickly. So we sat down and ordered about 4 dozen fried oysters and a dozen and a half raw oysters alongside 2 French 75's. We made it in time for happy hour so we decided to splurge. And yes i ordered 2 at once. If i didnt have plans to go somewhere else i would have ordered more. The oysters were all spot on. Fried to perfection and displayed in a cute frying basket. We toasted and were able to finish in 45 minutes. The next day I returned for lunch. I ordered the seafood tower, le plateau de fruits de mer, with crispy brussel sprouts and stuffed p&j oysters.  The tower came with king crab legs, stone crab legs, oysters, mussels, clams, crab ceviche, and shrimp. The presentation was so beautiful.  I wasn't the biggest fan of the ceviche or the shrimp. Everything else was great. Mussels and clams were prepared with garlic, and the shrimp seasoned with Old Bay. All eaten with a glass of wine and another French 75. The brussel sprouts were good. They had an asian flare to it, sweet and salty with a crisp. The p&j oysters were very garlicky and buttery, baked with crab meat. Melanie, our waitress was great. She sat with us to explain the menu. She was extremely knowledgeable and witty and made a few food and wine recommendations. Would I return back? You have a fan if I'm in NOLA.

Based on my experiences at Luke's (and other restaurants in New Orleans), I've become a HUGE fan of John Besh. Luke's is a fantastic restaurant that is a must visit when you are in New Orleans. We frequent this restaurant because we stay at the Intercontinental on a regular basis. You'll love it!

Service was awful! Food was probably good but because the waiter served it cold we were unimpressed. Unfortunately the fella that served our table was training a new waiter so don't expect the service to improve. We had to ask who our waiter was after 15 minutes with no service. We weren't offered bread that other tables had. SIL asked for his beer to be served with his meal and it didn't come until he has finished his meal. 
On the positive side the crab bisque was nice and hot and delicious.
This restaurant located in New Britain Village Square. Actually, the chefs and waitresses are Chinese. It's not a real Japanese restaurant. The food is good, and the price is reasonable.

Yummy. I'll write more later. Fork in my face at the present moment....

Okay, it's been a while. Where does the time go?

I LOVE THIS RESTAURANT!!! This was my second visit and it didn't disappoint. Those jalapeño grits are so darned good! I didn't even want to share them with my hubby. Or my best friend. Stabbing with a fork is merited for anyone attempting to get between me and these grits!

And then, there's the stuffed french toast! Stuffed with what you ask? Well, nutella and strawberries! Need I say more?? Yep, that good.

Oh, and the coffee.... French press served with real, whole cream. Heaven! 

I can only imagine how good lunch and dinner are - gonna have to make it for one of those instead of just breakfast. 

Please, go and enjoy this restaurant. You won't be disappointed.

I wonder if the deliver to California...?

I plancd an order for pick up this morning for a department meeting 
Pick up service was great and convenient 
My disappointment was 
I got only four kinds of begles raisin , plain, sesame,
Asiago.
Only one kind of cream cheese plain all of them plain
I asked for a mixture of two dozen begals 
Mixture of cream cheeses 
I didn't know til I got to the meeting 
I did get the big carry out coffee for 12

Our party of 7 made it in time for our 11:30 Sunday brunch reservation, after a long night out on Bourbon street. We ordered a bunch of appetizers to share:

Stuffed P&J Oysters (gulf shrimp and blue crab) - I'm not sure why I kept reading this as PB&J, but I'm really glad it wasn't, even though it wasn't that good. It was mostly breadcrumb. I'm not even sure I can remember tasting any shrimp or crab in there.

Crispy Brussel Sprouts (toasted almonds, Espelette honey, Progress Milk Barn cheese) - sat this one out since I don't like brussel sprouts but everyone else who tried it said it was good

Pâté of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken Livers (perfumed with truffles, country bread croutons) - I enjoyed the crispy bread but this pâté was not for me. It was too buttery tasting and not enough liver flavor. I did like that they gave four different mustards and pepper jellies to try it with though.

Citrus Cured Gulf Tuna Tartar (crispy shrimp chips, chili garlic vinaigrette) - there was so little tuna in there, that none of us even realized that it was the tartar. We thought it was just another spread that came with the pâté.

On top of all of this, we each also got our own entree (although most of us were already getting full from all the appetizers by the time our entrees showed up). I had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte (roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausage) - this was pretty good. The grits were very flavorful but also very heavy. Might have been the wrong decision for a first meal after a night of drinking. Also not sure if it was really worth the $25 price tag.

If you want to splurge, it seems their entrees are pretty good. But skip the apps because they're all pretty mediocre. Except for the raw oysters. Oh yeah, we got those too.

Wonderful food and a great cocktail.  Great customer service. I was here on a work trip and needed a place to eat that I felt comfortable sitting by myself.   This not only fit what I was looking for but had the best NOLA version of a cuban and fries.

I will definitely be back..  Get over the fact that it is in a hotel.  It is worth it!

We spent Thanksgiving here enjoyed some Turducken, oyster stuffing, raw oysters, brussel sprouts and so much more! The price is reasonable. For 8 people our check came out to under $400 and that includes cocktails.  I dont think you can go wrong with anything on the menu.
The service was the best. Jessie and Savannah were our waiters. The day before that we had Gary and Kevin as our waiter.  Gary made it a point to co.e to our table to greet us. The manager (Byron) was also great. He fit us in at the last minute. Thanks for making our Thanksgiving (away from home) such a fun experience!!

At first the service was slow, my party and I were getting worried that our experience may go bad... but then once the wait staff got engaged with us it was awesome.  The crab and corn fritters were great and I'm not sure what the sauce is that accompanies the fritters but it's tasty.  My wife had a fried oysters, bacon, avocado salad. The bacon on that salad was no joke.  We're not talking 'bacon bits, this salad was topped with bacon cubes that had the best bacon/smoke flavor I've ever enjoyed.  I had the seafood gumbo which was fantastic.  The roux was dark and rich and it did not lack in seafood.  There were lots of shrimp and oysters.  I'd recommend this place to anyone looking a great meal outside the usual tourist spots.

Purchased a groupon for here atmosphere is great service was very good and the food was also great. More high end   Then realized, great for a date night. Pricing not horrible, but not great for little kids (no high chair) but all in all great experience!!!

I ate here awhile ago but I believe this restaurant hasn't really changed much. Which is a good thing. This isn't Besh's best place but it does what it does well. I would call it fusion bistro food, with an emphasis, of course on French/NOLA cooking. Everything I had was very good, and the wine list is excellent. I actually sent back my original wine as it was just too thin (of a pinot noir) and was very satisfied with the replacement. There were a lot of Burgandies to choose from! Suggestion: Ask to sit in the front room, it's much more desirable than the back. I would definitely eat here again!

Luke came highly recommended by my cousin who's a foodie local in New Orleans.  This place didn't disappoint at all.  Love it.  The corn bisque, oysters, gumbo and the sprouts are so awesome! Will be here again next time in town.
Huge fan of the foie gras dish. Great selection of wine. Great duck and chicken dishes. It's John Besh - there's nothing bad on the menu!

I've been coming here for a few months now and I am very satisfied with my membership. First of all, it's really hard to beat $20 a month. Although I was quite pissed when I signed up, because THE DAY AFTER I bought my membership, they began a sale where you could sign up for no registration fee. I have no idea why they couldn't have recommended I wait just one more day, but I guess I probably wouldn't give a damn if I were them, either.

I love everyone who works behind the desk. They smile at me and say "hi" when I come in, and they are always willing to answer a question. The gym area is always completely spotless, while the locker rooms are... well, they're locker rooms. They are gross. 

Their one major downfall is that their equipment is well-maintained, but they just don't have enough of it. You practically have to slit throats to use the squat rack. But they have abundant cardio equipment, and even at primetime it's not so crowded that you bump into people. 

Overall, RF is definitely worth the low price.
Brunch on a Saturday....... ughhhhhhhh no Redfish.....however the Chicken and waffles, were great. Crispy filet boneless breast, buttermilk waffle and the pepper jelly was very tasteful.

During my visit to New Orleans, this was by far my favorite restaurant. After many misses due to recommendations from our hotel concierge, we came upon Luke, and returned everyday for the remainder of our trip. Their burger is by far one of the best I have ever had, and their bartenders really know what they are doing, they serve wonderful drinks, specifically the French 75, we have been to many bars after this and nobody has been able to make this drink as well as Luke.  I will definately return the next time I am in town.

Came back during happy hour with a friend, and it was just FABULOUS!  We got two dozen oysters, and literally devoured it!  It was soooo good, especially after not having it for a while.  The oysters were a pretty good size, considering it is the off season.  We then ordered a cup of gumbo, the pate de campagne, and split an entree of shrimp and grits.  OMGOODNESS!  The shrimp and grits were absolutely scrumptious!  The sauce was just divine!  I loved everything about the dish.  The grits were at the perfect consistency and complemented the shrimp so well.  This dish was unanimously the best dish.  The gumbo was good and flavorful, and the pate was decent.  (Maybe I'm just not that big of a pate fan.)  We also got the bread pudding for dessert, which was good as always.  Can you believe two little Asian girls ate this much?!  Oh it's possible after a long week of school.  Hahah.

We also had a very friendly waitress. She paid the perfect amount of attention to us and also brought the plates out in good intervals.  Overall, a lovely meal and I can't wait to come back for more!
75 cent Happy Hour oysters plus great service = 5 STARS!

We had an amazing impromptu brunch at Lüke. Honestly, could not have been happier that we stopped in. We hesitated at first, as we were dressed casually and had two young kids in-tow, but the hostess was more than gracious and told us we were most definitely welcome for brunch, and that they even have a kids menu. 

The atmosphere is beautiful--old school, upscale feel and the kids had a blast watching someone behind the bar schuck oysters. Service was stellar and the manager even came out to make sure we were happy and give the kids her favorite, Mac n Cheese, on the house.

As for the other food---amazing. Uh-may-zing. My chicken biscuit was perfection. The fluffy biscuit with crispy chicken, egg, and tobasco honey was literally one of those dishes you dream about. My husband seemed equally impressed with his Lüke burger, which I also snuck a bite of. Cooked to perfection and full of flavor. Bacon and grilled onion with smoked cheese paired perfectly with the sweet bun. The kids burgers were even delicious. Overall, an awesome meal and we will most definitely be back.

Top to bottom this place was amazing!  The food quality, presentation and wait staff were spot on or as they say on flek!  The kids and i sat at the oyster bar initially and talked to the shucker.  Good man that gave one the kids an oyster pearl! Made his day!

We ordered dozen raw oysters which were really big, cold, and succulent with side of fresh horseradish and cocktail sauce.  The fried oysters were even better!! Had to order another dozen of fried oysters!  

We then got our entreess, shrimp and grits, gulf coast fresh fried fish, Thursday special, seafood gumbo,mattzaball soup,  softshell crab,  luke cheeseburger, grilled cheese,,chicken and waffles,and chicken tenders. Then they brought sides if gnochi and brussel sprouts in small cast iron plate. 

Shrimp and grits was hands down the best ever!  Seafood gumbo had a dark roux but i think it was from the tomato paste. Really rich and decadent gumbo. 

Overall,DeeDee, the manager at lukes does a great job.  She is to be commended with her genuine personality.  Lukes is a must stop if you are ever in New Orleans!

We were there for a girl's trip in May (sorry I didn't get this out sooner, but I like to travel!). This was just an overall great place. First, they accommodated my 87 yr old mom with a pillow for her back (where'd they find THAT?).
Then there's the food. We ordered appetizers: flammenkuchen and crabmeat au gratin. DEE. LISH. Oh, and the crab and corn bisque. Amazing flavors! Everyone who had oysters thought they were awesome. My daughter and I split the ribeye and the jalapeno grits. I'm getting hungry just thinking about it! The steak was cooked to perfection. Red wines were suggested and not over-the-top priced. 
We sought out the manager, Deidre Pryor, to let her know that our servers were terrific.Can't wait to visit their location in San Antonio!
Nice place, great food. The shrimp farci with blood orange hollandaise was excellent. The restaurant is a short walk across Canal Street from the French Quarter.
Great oysters and delightful staff.  Soft shell crab BLT was yummy.  We were there for happy hour, select drinks were half off and they have oysters on special also.

The Luke burger is divine!!!!!!!! It's made by magical hands that season this high grade beef to perfection!! It's so good that I just can't stop giggling and saying "mmm" (strong emphasis) with every bite! You have to have to have to try this burger. I'm addicted!!!

First of all Rich and Kenny are excellent waitersEach had great recommendations, kept our glasses full and clearly went above and beyond to make our visit great. My food was also exceptional, literally the best fried oysters I've ever tried ( raw oysters were just as good and very fresh) i also recommend you try the Brussel sprouts, I have never liked Brussels sprouts until I tried them at Luke's. . . Great food, friendly staff, good cocktails . If I ever make it back to N.O I would definitely go again

Was very excited to try Luke but was disappointed. Was with a group with a set menu with choices which all sounded great. Gumbo which was described as one of the city's best was average at best. Duck w/ crispy rice had all the right flavors but duck was medium well w/o any crispy skin. The bread pudding was all pecans and little bread to contrast. Service was good. Maybe individual dining would be better but in a city that lives for groups you have to get this right.
This our go to pizza place in our house. They are great. I recommend the cheese steak pizza.

We checked in to our hotel and decided to try to find a place to eat that was fairly close. A quick internet search led us to Luke. My husband got the matzo ball soup and I got the corn and crab bisque, which was exquisite. We both got the same entree, which was essentially shrimp and grits. It was so flavorful, and the grits were smooth and creamy. Although we were both stuffed, we couldn't leave without sampling their signature bread pudding. This was our first meal in New Orleans, and the bar has been set extremely high. If all the food here is as good as Luke's, I may never leave.

I had high expectations based on reviews for this place. The service (in my opinion) was NOT good although we were assigned 2 different people (Kevin and Chi). Every time we had a question or needed something we had to flag them down. Odd, it was a Tuesday and not overly crowded. The crab bisque was amazing. However, they served a cup when we asked for a bowl. Quickly rectified this though and served us a bowl.
The baked oysters were good, the pasta I absolutely would do without. I wouldn't revisit, it's not worth the money to deal with LESS THAN GREAT service and okay food.
The food and service was amazing. The raw oysters were fresh and the baked p&j oysters were the best we've ever had.  The shrimp and grits were amazing. You will not regret it.
Delish food and great service!  A nice escape from the French quarter for an amazing dinner! Make a reservation.... but if you don't, it's worth the wait.
Only came here for dessert and drinks. Banana bread was the best I've ever had. Oh and shot out to our bartender chris, he was great!

One of the best oysters I've had (both raw and fried) and they were only 75 cents each during happy hour! 

I've had this restaurant bookmarked for months even before I booked my trip to NOLA. This was our first stop after checking in our hotel. When we first walked in, the place looked so fancy that I was afraid it was out of our price range. But everything was very fairly priced. 

The staff here are very friendly. They recommended a cocktail for me that turned out to be delicious. We were a little too early for happy hour but they were nice enough to put our hh orders in after it started. 

I'd recommend this place for couples, friends, families, everyone!
Food was just okay. We had the schnitzel and it was tough and overlooked. Service was slow, didn't get our first drinks until after the appetizer was served. Overall felt rushed.
If for some reason I were ever sent to jail and was given the death penalty, my last meal would be the jumbo shrimp from here and Rich would be my server.

The only restaurant I went to twice in my 4 day trip. That's how awesome this place is. We came for brunch and then came back for happy hour. The brunch was amazing. The homemade jam wowed me. The grits were well seasoned and well textured. The oysters at happy hour were soooo fresh and sooo addictive. One of my best memories of NOLA was those oysters! Can't wait to revisit NOLA and come back here.

Came here for dinner and had very unfriendly service. Two people at our table's food was cold when served to us, so we asked for them to take it back and heat it up...They only took one person's ignoring the second person. When they returned the second person asked again for them to heat up their food. 

The tablecloths had paper on top, which was not classy at all and reminded me of a cheap family restaurant. 

Was not impressed with our visit.

The crab omelet was excellent, and I was surprised with the side of fries that came with it because  I didn't see that on the menu. I also had a mimosa for my early breakfast here.
Disappointed in the lack of friendliness from the hostess, and general ambiance of the restaurant. We were  the first in for the day on a Saturday morning. I thought it felt very quiet, but realized later they didn't turn on music until we had paid and were leaving. 
If it were not for the high quality of the food and preparation I would be have a lower rating.  Staff had a vibe of  ambivalence and annoyance of our presence.

We were recommended here by a server at Johnny Sanchez... since John Besh is also the owner we decided to give it a try and we left extremely happy! 

We went around 4:30 on a Wednesday and were seated right away. They had their happy hour menu which is amazing .75 raw oysters and 1/2 off drinks. We ordered raw oysters, fried oysters, and tuna tartare. For drinks we had the jalepaloma and the french [ not sure if i'm accurate on the name] either way we had no complaints! We will be back and try their famous burger which is what we originally recommended there for.

Terrible service, expensive, confusing order and payment layout, ok food.

I've come to this Cosi three times already, and each time, I question why I come here again for their terrible service.

The people that work there are highly unprofessional and rude. The hatred of patrons that the people that work at Cosi doesn't help with the confusing layout of the shop. 

You first need to line up (well, there's a sign to tell you where to line up to order) to talk to the sandwich makers. You have to almost yell since it's so loud, and they're often busy making sandwiches which adds to the confusion on who you should be talking to. 

After this, you awkwardly walk to the cashiers, whom each time I went, we're seemingly reluctant to take my order.

Also.. Why do I have to tell them my order twice, once to the chef, and once to the cashier? 

Also so confusing on where we should be to get our food. Do they go to us? Or do we stand somewhere near the line to pick it up?

The good thing is, the food is pretty good. Their chicken noodle soup is on point. 

But yeah.. This is probably the most confusing food place I've been to. Terrible service doesn't help it. Avoid. If you can.. Since they have a monopoly towards the University City students.

This was very mediocre in my opinion! The service was just okay, the courses were way too spread out, and the food was very okay. For what we spent, I can think of a hundred other restaurants I would have rather gone to.

First dining experience in New Orleans since the reopening of restaurants. We had an amazing experience & spectacular service from Rich. He was very attentive and patient with us while deciding on our orders. We ordered the Stuffed P&J Oysters as an appetizer and they were amazing! The main reason we decided to dine here for my birthday because they are so delicious & unlike any oysters I've had before. Rich was also able to accommodate my needs for not being able to decide between two entrees & giving me a half order of each which made it perfect. Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp & Grits & Louisiana Blue Crab Garganelli. Both full of flavor & the best of both worlds. My boyfriend ordered the Crispy Softshell Crab which paired so well with the watermelon, cucumber, & tomato. He almost licked the plate clean! It was so nice to be in a restaurant again and really appreciate the friendly staff that made our experience so wonderful.

This is a 5 star place in any town but New Orleans and it is one of my favorite places to eat in town, but I can't give it a 5 star rating due to the competition.  If I could do 4.5 I would do that.

I have nothing bad to say about it.  This was my 2nd dinner there.  Good stuff.  I had the Ravioli last time and it was superb.  This time, my wife got the shrimp and grits and I got the chicken.  I ordered wrong as mine was just OK.

The Shrimp and Grits were awesome.  

If you are looking for something that is moderately priced with a good New Orleans feel, I recommend this place.

Like I said, this would be 5 stars in any other town.
Great service...had to take my vehicle in after mangling the drain plug and they replaced it even though they extract the oil through the engine. Will go here again!

Restaurant linked to the Hilton on St. Charles.
Limited menu item selection. Excellent soups & salads.  
Happy Hour 3-6 with reasonable drink selection.  Lunch until 4.
Very pricey afterwards.
Excellent bar service.  Very good table service.  If female dining solo you may get missed by waiter numerous times while they seem to prefer guests dining with a male & missed for follow ups after receiving your meal, no matter how pleasant you are.
As a solo diner suggest you dine at the bar so you can get served quicker

Best steak ever! So tender and juicy! I wish they had a few more food options, but I'd probably still get the steak every time. The appetizers and everything were nice too, but the steak from the steak frites definitely stood out.

The staff was friendly and attentive, and we had a local acapella group come around the tables and sing for us. It was a wonderful experience.

Let me start by noting I'm not one who posts often.  I am pretty easy going, and so for me a 3-star kind of experience is not something I feel compelled to shout about.  Give me a five-star and I'll write; give me crap and I'll write.  Unfortunately this one hit the latter category.

Let's start with the people.  The service was horrible once we left the hostess' station (she was polite).  Our waiter wasn't remotely engaging ("what're you having?" was the longest sentence he uttered), and I had to dart out early and leave my wife with the bill because it took over 45 minutes to get our food, and I had a total of 55 before I had to be in a meeting.  Glad I did - it took nearly 30 minutes from the time we finished before we got the bill.  Thirty minutes to pay from forks turned on empty plates - seriously?

As far as the food, I had the special lamb and it honestly tasted more like pot roast than lamb.  Not sure if that was the way it was prepared or if someone accidentally fixed the wrong dish, but I was NOT impressed.  Portion-wise I get the whole "less is more" trend (sort of, anyway), but I still expect to feel remotely satisfied when I'm complete with the meal (cup of crab bisque and the lamb special).  Not here - I ended up making a snack run after my meeting because the portion was that weak.

I would definitely NOT recommend this restaurant.  The only saving grace (outside of the polite hostess) was the fact that my wife liked her salad.  For a world-renowned restaurant that's pretty bad.  I would recommend taking a stroll a block over to a more local restaurant than trying your luck here.
We had a great server and experience - thanks, Tre!!  Food was excellent. Drinks excellent. Price is high but worth a splurge.

This a thoughtful, delicious place to enjoy and have a great conversation. I was fortunate to stop by during happy hour. First the drinks were 50% off and oysters were 75cents fro raw and 1.25 for fried. At point I decided to try the fried oysters with a minimum 6 orders. This was my best decision. Crunchy, flavorful and not over fried but most important is you can taste the freshness of the oysters. I wanted to eat dinner like food so debating between the gumbo and ettoufee, I went with the crayfish ettoufee. It was creamy, yet the crunchy rice made it its own. I really love the twist and it was delicious. Totally new spin to a traditional dish.
Hidden gem in far bucks county. Clean and modern decor. The options are endless and everything has great flavor and was fresh. Great lunch specials.

Went for happy hour (3pm to 6pm everyday). 75 cents raw oyster and 1.25 for fried oysters.  Half price on cocktails, beers and wine.  Food came with bread and butter. Oysters came with saline crackers.  The raw oyster was really good.  The service was great.
Might be the BEST omelette ever (crab) - very light, fluffy and tasty!! The shrimp and grits was AMAZING! Great service! Highly recommend for breakfast. Can't wait to try dinner!

On my Sunday before leaving Nawlins, I decided to venture out on my own for early brunch (while everyone else was sleeping off Bourbon street) and study the (recipe) book of Luke! I was going to catch the trolley, but meh...decided to walk the entire way, which was 15 minutes. Near many of the hotels, this place has great location! Great southern charm with wood foundations and white linens...a bar is tucked away on the side as well to indulge in a few concoctions, mine being a simple mimosa to cheer on my Sunday indulgence. I wanted a traditional nawlins dish that was a little on the heavy side just because it was early! and why the heck not?! It New Orleans! I had perused the menu earlier and saw that this placed served shrimp n grits--my fav so I ventured out just to savor this dish. OMG!!! Great dish minus the eggs on top.I did try to let the dish remain as prepared, but when the eggs started running, I had to remove em! The texture of the white eggs were excellent-- not too hard and seasoned quite well, but it was the Shrimp nGrits that stole my heart! The first bite will leave you speechless! I had to savor that first bite for sure and just take it all in! I leave it there- I cant describe it enough to even make you comprehend tbe excellence at the Luke. Service was also excellent as well whereas the waiter checked on me frequenty and made me feel at home but not to pushy. Im glad I came early Sunday morning and not only had no wait but excellent service and food. I'm leaving Nawlins nice and full folks--its only right!

Came here for Lunch. We ordered the fried oyster salad with bacon, romaine, avocado, court bouillon,  and crab meat maison.
The court bouillon was the special of the day and came with a cup of soup. Decided to get the crab bisque... OMG i think it was heaven in a bowl..... OMG... sooooo GOOOD.
The salad was good, I've come to figure that Nola restaurants like to over dress their salads. It was good, but i like very light dressing.
The Court Bouillon was fanastic, really enjoyed the flavor and freshness of the seafood. 
The crab maison was also very good.
The meal was great, very happy with all the things we ordered.

We just had our puppy spayed at Seven Oaks.  Her follow up is this week but I can tell you, she has done extremely well since her surgery.  The care and direction by the staff was wonderful.  I know the follow up is only a formality since she has had no complications and barely had any redness at the surgical site.  They are very caring and knowledgeable here.

Visited this gem of a restaurant during my trip to NOLA and instantly feel in love with amazing decor, classical vibe of the place and of course with their seafood tower. I will definitely be back to Luke next time I visit

Definitely one of my favorite restaurants for happy hour. The drinks and appetizers are so good that it's hard to even save room for a main course. The French 75 (cognac, champagne and lemon juice) is fantastic!! And during HH it's half off! The fried oysters are $1.25 each and the sauce that comes with it will set it off perfectly. The crispy brussel sprouts as well as the crab and corn bisque are delicious as well. One thing that I love about Lüke is that the service is spectacular. There are always 2 people on each table so you'll never be lacking attention. HH is from 3-6pm and surprisingly never TOO crowded during the week (especially before 5pm).

We wandered in on an evening hungry and grumpy from a long road trip but were quickly blown away by the great food. We both ordered the ettouffee and agreed that it was delicious and hit the spot. Delicious food and a nice yet welcoming atmosphere.

The seafood gumbo was excellent.
I tasted the crawfish gumbo my friend ordered and it was really good too.
The flamencuchen was delicious.
The fried oyster salad was very good. Loved how the oysters used in this salad were fresh and warm.

My soft shell crab BLT was just alright.
My friend's shrimp étouffée was very flavorful and he loved it.

The seafood platter was great but it was unfortunate it came out after our entree arrived.

The server was not very attentive.

4.5 stars for the food, 4 for the service.
Loved my dinner at Luke! Beautiful venue. Excellent food. Enjoyed the oysters, table bread, fish, and salad. Server was a little slow, but I highly recommend this restaurant.

Unbelievable. I'm not sure I will ever eat at another sushi place again. We sat at the sushi bar (wait was about 30 mins so we went and grabbed some groceries at Giant)  and then sat down almost 30 mins to the minute, and watched the magic as they made the sushi in front of us. The other patrons were helpful is deciding what to get. Amazing and fresh and we will definitely be back soon!

I went for the steak Frits but they are only available for dinner =(..... so I went for my safe zone the burger! I have to say one of the best burgers I've ever had. Service was great, the wine selection was limited but worked, all in all a really pleasant experience btw try the pate appetizer it is amazing

Luke on St. Charles is THE place for fresh Oysters!  They have HH everyday 3-6p, and the best, largest, most succulent, tender oysters (for $.75 each) I had in town.  For HH, they have 1/2 off drafts, specialty drinks and glasses of wine. For the amazing Oysters, drinks plus excellent, friendly, witty and attentive service, a solid 5.0 for me!  Expect to spend $10-20pp for lunch or HH.

Was looking for a recommendation for the best oysters around town, and while many places in the area have 'em, this offer was the "deal of the day"! We started with 1/2 dz raw, but these were SO good, we ordered another dozen; and some of the larger ones were like "double" sized oysters.  These were served with fresh (strong) horseradish and cocktail sauce, mix it to your liking! 

To top it off, we ordered a dozen of their fresh fried oysters as well, served with a house remoulade.  These cost 6 for $10 or 12 for $18, and were the best fried oysters I've ever eaten, YUM!  And their fresh cut fries rocked as well!  Plus fresh warm rolls with your meal too.

Decor is traditional dark wood with tablecloths, but HH is the way to go, plus they also have a full menu of N'Orleans tasty foods like Gumbo, Po Boys sandwiches, and burgers for lunch.  But don't miss this treat if you LOVE oysters!  Enter Luke from the street or thru the Hilton. ENJOY!!!

The food is good. Really fresh. Good quality meat which is a nice change from other halal Chinese I have been to in NY or NJ. 
Only thing is check your order before you leave in case there's a mistake but otherwise I will definitely recommend anyone go. Portions are decent too. I'd say not too much or too little and the price I think is at par with the quality of food. 

Best item on the menu. Halal cheese steak rolls. Weirdly so good!

Probably best meal we had in NOLA which says a lot as we had many great meals.  Brussel sprouts gave me new found respect for fine cooking with hot sauce. Burger was perfect.  Friends' steak and shrimp and grits hit the mark.  Bread pudding was piece de la resistance!   Secretly wanted to go back every night!

I was excited to eat macaroni and cheese Saturday night! Unfortunately it was dry and not creamy as usual. They call it a large and just stick the same amount as a small in a large bowl. 
The bread was literally as hard as a rock and tasted burnt. 
I'm going to give you the benefit of the doubt that you were having a off night. I will eat there again and pray that the food is more up to par.

The cocktails are delicious, especially the French 75!  Our server was a little rough around the edges but nice enough and efficient.  

The boudin noir was AMAZING! Actually the potatoes, apples, onions and sausage were the stars, the boudin noir itself was pretty mild in flavor.  The pate of rabbit and duck liver was delicious too! I love the presentation with individually jarred pates and LOTS of it, 4 accompaniments and lovely buttered baguette toasts to spread everything on.  The crocque monsieur - OMG - I'm already in heaven and may very well die of clogged arteries!  It was also very delicious. The cheese sandwich was rich and decadent and the fries put this dish over the top.  Again, the presentation was rustic, simple and appealing.  A must try restaurant in New Orleans!

Went here for a late lunch on Friday a few weeks ago and had 

1) one of the best-done burgers I've ever had in New Orleans, 
2) some great oysters and 
3) Some great cocktails

My standard for a burger is high and they went way beyond it. Every element of the burger worked for me. The bacon was soft and crispy and the burger was actually medium rare like I requested! The tower of oysters given to my table could have had larger sizes but the taste made up for it. Great place to go for a way to wind down after the workweek and before a Friday night.

Came here for breakfast and I was very disappointed. I got the chicken as waffles and the chicken was so dry and the waffles were just ehh. I wanted to love this place because I heard so many great things! But I can't even finish it cause It was just okay. The taste of everything was good, just everything felt so dry.

The best thing I had there was probably the french fries. Maybe next time I come back, I'll have a better expereince.

Got food "to go" since I don't enjoy eating by myself.  Ordered the food over the phone and it was ready and neatly packed for me.  The staff who helped at the bar were very friendly and genuinely looked happy.  The food was really delicious so I plan actually dining inside later this week.

Rating only for happy hour.   Very affordable oysters during happy hour for only 75 cents each, fried ones are a bit extra.   Half off draft beers.  Server is personable and available for water fills.  

Fancy but not too pretentious ambiance.

I'm an avid golfer and I'm a strict grader when it comes to golf courses. Let me start by saying this certainly isn't a bad course and I would golf here again. 

This is a semi private golf course but tee times are always available. The area of the course is somewhat remote. They have locker rooms for both men and women and a restaurant on site. Also, they do have a person riding around selling food and beverages on the course. 

I really liked the course layout. A lot of the holes were different and it kept me guessing. It wasn't too easy but it wasn't hard either. The course had a lot of dog legs and hills. The reason for the 3* is they just don't take care of the course. The fairways aren't in good shape, the greens aren't in good shape and the rough is in even rougher shape, pun intended. If they were to really buckle down and take care of the course I think it would be a very good course you'd happily spend $80-$90 on.

Sorry, Lüke - this place just did not meet expectations.

It's a white tablecloth kind of place, with waiters dressed in crisp shirts and black vests and ties. The items on the menu are a little pricey, so I decided to go with the Tabasco and honey fried chicken biscuit, a smaller dish, with a side of grits.

Though the biscuit and chicken were good, I wasn't wowed. The food was lukewarm, which made the grits kind of hard to swallow. 

Don't get me wrong - I think it's good food, but compared to everything else in the area, it's just not /as/ good.
We went on valentines night and did not have a reservation. The food was amazing. We had the raw oysters  and bisque. I would recommend the Brussels sprouts  I would definately go again

Best service we had in N.O. the waitress knew the menu backwards and forwards and could make great suggestions.  We had the etouffe' and it was spot on.  She made great recommendations for happy hour. Overall it was the best experience even compared to some of the big name restaurants.  Mardi Gras parade right outside the door too!
Their flat bread pizza's are great especially if you're looking for a big lunch or dinner. I usually get take out.
Very tasty food and staff is always pleasant and polite. Their lunch special is a great deal with generous portions.

Amazing service!  I'm so glad we checked out this restaurant.  There is no signage indicating happy hour is taking place and it is pretty ritzy looking so I thought I was at the wrong place.  I came down to New Orleans for oysters and I had already tried Le Bayou and Royal House, but nothing beats the fifty cents oysters here!  Amazing value, good oysters and people are so pleasant without being overbearing or stuffy.  Also, wine and beer is half off.  It was only two blocks from where I was staying so I tried to go every day.  I ordered the Luke salad off of the regular menu: the buttermilk dressing was wonderful, the Bibb lettuce was fresh and paired so nicely with the root vegetable(?).  I ordered dressing on the side and I don't think the server remembered, but it didn't matter because the dressing was lightly tossed in. I'll definitely come back next year when I visit new Orleans again.

I went to Luke for my Husbands B-day.  The reservation was last minute and they were able to accommodate me, which I appreciated.  The drinks left a little to be desired but the waiter made up for it by comp-ing them since we were not satisfied.  The food was great though!  The waiter told us that the burgers were rated 5th in the country and man was he right!  The stuffed shrimp and the ravioli are really good and surprisingly very filling.  Our waiter named Rye was awesome and knew the menu like the back of his hand.  Overall really nice meal, even better staff!

This was our second oyster place during our trip because why not. Honestly, their menu looked like you couldn't really order anything wrong. Since we were here for dinner we also got mixed drinks. To be slightly healthy we added the sprouts to share. Overall I enjoyed my time here.

Oh my gosh. Three words: duck duck rice. If they ever take it off the menu, it'll be a crime. The flavors are phenomenal. The duck was cooked to perfection. And the rice is like fancy adult rice krispies, somehow double-cooked so that it's crispy/puffy and soaks up all that delicious sauce. We had a delicious bread pudding for dessert, but the entrée truly stole the show. This is a dish I'll never forget!
The food is ok. Service was good and fast. Price is a little on the higher side but expected.
The best service we've had in a long time! Delicious fresh oysters on the half shell. We went for Happy Hour and then took a few drinks to go.

It's a beautiful place with very good services, and it's cross street from our hotel (intercontinental). I picked it to have brunch based on the good reviews and it's so close. It took about 15 minutes to sit at our table with reservation. I saw people just couldn't wait any longer and just left. So if you decide to try it, MAKE RESERVATION. 
As for the food, it's okay. I had the shrimp grits (a little salty for my taste) and the rabbit/chicken liver. They are not bad, nothing special either. 
I did enjoy the clean table cloth and attentive service for a change (since most of the restaurants in New Orleans are situated in old-dirty buildings with minimum service).
When I was there, everyone around me ordered burger,fries,or po-boy. I would suggest you go else where for more authentic local cuicine.

To be fair, this is the first time I've visited this Chipotle, and certainly the gross smell we encountered is not always present. Right after we ordered our food we walked over to the soda fountain and were met with an unsavory odor coming from the bathrooms, which were closed off. The smell was bad enough that I can be confident whatever problem occurred in the bathroom had happened at least an hour earlier. I think a restaurant has a responsibility to handle issues like this right away. The smell filled around 50% of the place. For the record, the food was good, but we probably won't go back to this location.

Golden Pheasant is a beautiful and challenging course that is set back off of Rt. 70.  If you go I suggest getting there early and reserving a tee time.  There are lots of hills and if you hit you ball into the rough consider it gone.  The grass is very thick.  You will probably enjoy the 11th and the 17th holes.  On the weekends they have a girl who drives a snack cart and they have cold drinks.  Have fun playing.
Excellent food and service. Nice ambience, but has a casual feel. The Rabbit pate and brussel sprout appetizers were excellent, and the grits and shrimp was a big hit.

A lot of people have told me about this place so I finally decided to give it a try. I ordered the sesame shrimp and to my surprise, not as out of this world as I thought it would've been. Just regular Chinese food, but still fulfilling and served its purpose. Can't say I'll be in a hurry to come back, but certainly NOT on my list of things to never try again.

Had an opportunity to take the ladies out tonight to this restaurant popular with locals. Fortunately was able to make reservations on opentable and did not have to suffer the wait that the crowd by the entrance endured.

Did I mention that the place was popular? And loud. Not recommended for quiet conversation or a romantic night.

The service was congenial and attentive. Our server was quick to notice empty glasses needing refills.

We started with the crab and corn bisque. It was delicious, but arrived merely luke warm (not a pun). The brussel sprouts were enjoyed by the girls, but not my kind of fare. On the other hand, I savored the crab gratin on toast.

Through no fault of our server, who was constantly concerned about our wait, our entrees of oyster salad did not arrive for an hour.

Individually, the components of the oyster salad were delicious. The fried oysters were incredible. The lettuce, tomato and dressing were a delight. The bacon was a unique (to me) intense combination of Smokey flavor and salt curing that I liked immensely. However, the bacon was served in large chunks that tended to overpower the rest of the salad. I would have preferred smaller pieces to reduce the Smokey bacon influence over the salad. (I would love to have this bacon in a quiche).

In all, I like what the chef is saying to me, but the management of the kitchen has room for improvement. I've read other reviews where speed of service was a complaint. I don't see this as a dining room issue, but a kitchen management problem. The delay in serving dishes (a salad for heaven's sake) would not be tolerated by most and affects the turn over of tables. Improving kitchen management would certainly be appreciated by patrons and improve the profitability of the business.

I had a cup of gumbo and most amazing crab omelette with a mimosa for breakfast. Not to mention our waiter Matt was fantastic. The ambiance was very classy and inviting. I was with a group of 5 other girls and we had a great time.

Luke is a causal John Besh restaurant located in the CBD. It was one of the few good restaurants open for lunch on Saturday. 

We had the corn and crab bisque to start and it was very good. For entrees we ordered the burger and stuffed shrimp. 

The burger costs $16 which seems expensive for a burger (its the most expensive buyer i have ever had), but it was really good. The burger is huge and is topped by a wonderful cheese and smoked bacon. I am not a bacon fan, but apparently John Besh knows how to procure incredible bacon. The burger comes with some really good fries that are placed in a mint julep cup wrapped with paper. 

The stuffed shrimp was really good and came with vegetables. 

The wait staff was very attentive and friendly. I will definitely go here again. 

One word of caution. We at at Luke for lunch and La Provence for dinner. I would suggest only one Besh restaurant per day. There is no way to eat that much food in a day.

I'm giving two stars because they gave me an oil change and filled my tires with air. They did not however do a good job cleaning my car. Normally I wouldnt be annoyed because it's my junk so whatever but after I finished paying I walked outside to get into my car and there was a dirty pitbull standing inside of it. He made a total mess and left black paw prints all over my white interior. After giving a weak sorry  the woman working lightly brushed off a paw print or two. I left with an a car dirtier than I started with and played $50 for it. Wont return.

The GF and I had dinner reservations for Lüke on a Friday night.  However, we couldn't resist the happy hour 50 cent P&J oysters and half-priced cocktails and beer on Thursday.  Needless to say, we took advantage of the special price and had a dozen.  Although not included in the happy hour specials, we also had a half-dozen of the Blue Point and a half-dozen of the Kumamoto oysters.  All varieties were served properly chilled and were exceedingly fresh, juicy, and flavorful.  Although all three were pleasing, the Kumamoto's were my hands-down favorites with their clean, crisp brininess.  Pacific oysters are simply the best!  

As for cocktails, the sazerac was note perfect and a bargain at $4.50.  The GF had the French "75", a bright, refreshing cognac-based cocktail with  fresh-squeezed lemon juice and champagne...another bargain at $4.75.  Lüke offers a great happy hour experience which we thoroughly enjoyed.  Despite that fact, we cancelled our dinner reservation since we had filled in the John Besh restaurant block and decided instead to give another fine New Orleans restaurant a try.
My all time favorite place, happy hour included. Best appetizers, fresh seafood and amazing French 75's!
First time getting Hachi tonight and we truly enjoyed it. I had the crab croquettes as an appetizer and they were so delicious, the rolls also tasted fresh and yummy. Can't wait to go back!

I am smitten with Lüke.

During our whirlwind weekend in New Orleans, we tried to experience the whole gamut of N'awlins food. Everything was amazing, but Lüke was definitely my fave. A John Besh restaurant, Lüke pays homage to the grand old French and German brasseries that were once hugely popular in New Orleans. A mix of casual yet classy, modern yet vintage, with Southern hospitality ever present and food and drinks that delight the senses. I was floored.

While everything on the menu looked tantalizing, three out of four of us decided to get their daily changing 3-course Express Menu for $23. Best decision ever. I had crawfish bisque as my soup selection, and it was fantastic - a yummy little crawfish with its tiny head poking out of a delicious pool of flavorful bisque. The Friday dinner special was a Redfish "Court-Bouillon" with crab, shrimp, oysters and rice served in a skillet. The generous portions of seafood tasted so fresh, and the cajun sauce was so delicious that I polished off my entire plate with my bread. For dessert, we had Brendan's bread pudding with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce which was heaven in a bowl. Bread pudding is my favorite dessert, and Lüke surely blew away my tastebuds with it. And all this for ONLY $23!!

Lüke's classic New Orleans cocktails were also made to perfection. The French 75, St. Charles Streetcar and Sazerac were all wonderful.

Lüke really set the bar high for our dining experiences in New Orleans, but fortunately, we had many more wonderful ones to follow. A MUST VISIT. Your tastebuds will thank you for it.

Elm Cafe serves incredibly fresh coffee, salads, and sandwiches. The iced latte I had was smooth and refreshing. Although I was tempted by a muffin, I resisted - they looked freshly-baked. This cafe is very small with little seating (a couple of stools by the window), so it's really a take-out place. But definitely go for the coffee - the espresso drinks are incredible.
Great food, great champaign and lovely people. All this during Covid situation - thanks a lot for being so good to us!

Tried to walk in without a reservation and told to try the bar (which was full) and not offered a wait time. Considering we were dressed appropriately (dress for the lady, collared shirt for the gentleman), this felt unwelcoming. We went across the street to Trenasse and had an amazing dinner with no wait.

I'm from out of town and the hosts of the Airbnb I stayed at said Lüke was amazing. This place was just around average to me. 

Don't get me wrong, the food was good but I don't think it was worth the pricey amount it was. I ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp and it felt like it was missing something like a spicy kick. I feel like I could've got a better dish of shrimp and grits at another restaurant at a better price. Also, the shrimp was not all that jumbo in my opinion. They looked like regular sized shrimps to me. 

Service was not very good as well. Our server only came around three times to check up on us; the first to greet us, take our order, and drop off the check. Our waters were never refilled either. I don't want to say the server was rude, but it just felt like he was very stand offish and didn't care about us. The restaurant was not very busy so I'm not sure why this was a problem.

we had reservations for lunch but you didn't really need one because it wasn't packed. The restaurant is well lit and spacious.

We sat towards the open kitchen at the end of the restaurant. Our waiter was very eccentric and set a pretty good mood for the table. 

We ordered a dozen oysters to begin with. They were clean, juicy, briny, and meaty. I loved them. we contemplated ordering another dozen but decided against it, regretfully. 

my boyfriend got Cochon de Lait Pressed Sandwich and he's not even a big sandwich person but he really liked it. He couldn't finish it because it's soooo filling but he wanted to. 

I only got the mussels that are cooked in garlic chili sauce with your choice of ciabatta or fries. I prefer a white wine sauce with my mussels but these were really good took. not as big as i've had them but they were clean. They were all de-beareded and all opened.

So I came here for my sister's birthday, and OMG!!! It was amazing. I really enjoyed the vibe the restaurant gave off. It was a great dinner spot and I would most definitely go back. Also if want to get a good drink, you have to get the French 75. It was a huge hit with everyone at our table! So if you want some good food and hang out with good people you have to come here.

We came here on the suggestion of a friend and it worked since it was in the hotel we were staying at. 

The servers made the experience. We were sharing everything and the kitchen was kind enough to plate it four ways without us even asking! This is a first. They also brought out comped desserts since we shared that we were celebrating a special occasion and were visiting from Los Angeles. 

The food itself was ok.

It's been awhile since I made a visit to this teeny little cafe downtown. (I used to live right across the street). In the past I've always enjoyed their sandwiches, and to no fail, their early breakfast sandwiches. Today I ordered the breakfast sandwich with bacon, swiss chard, gruyere and fried egg. Although decent, it was nothing spectacular like I remember their sandwiches being. The fried egg tasted a bit rubbery. The swiss chard could've used more flavor and I found the ratio of bread to toppings too large. Service was okay... but I never expect great service from this place. 

They offer other sandwiches during lunch and a variety of baked goods including muffins, scones and cookies. For beverages, there is a variety of coffees, teas, and drinks available too.

Seating is limited to none depending on the crowd. With only 3 or 4 seats inside and a few tables outside.

Traveling through New Orleans and stopped at Luke.This is their "Monday Special". Tabasco Honey Fried Chicken with red beans and rice. This bowl of yummyness is $17 and so worth it. No one can ever say this dish lacks flavor but I did want just a tab more kick. Also at Luke in New Orleans is the JUMBO LOUISIANA SHRIMP "EN COCOTTE... aka Shrimp and grits. For $21 is dish will have you licking the  bottom of the bowl. For an additional $13 you can add crab on top. This place was great! Great Service and great food! This dish gets  out of 5 from me!

From the lack luster service to the horrifically under cooked burger, Luke was almost a complete and total disappointment. The only reason they are getting a second star is because of the fact that once the burger came back out, it was properly cooked and delicious. Every time we asked the waiter for something, we felt like we were putting him out. I am not saying that I was entitled to a certain speed of service, or even a certain level of excitement, I just don't like feeling like I am asking you to sweep my driveway when I need a refill on my iced tea. The soups and salads were seriously underwhelming and I am relatively sure the eggs had what resembled a live embryo in the yolk. Awful service, awful food and I will NOT be back, ever. There are many other, better choices all over New Orleans. Do not waste your time coming here, yelposphere.
This is a lively place with charm and atmosphere. Don't go for quiet conversation! Go for the delicious food, which is well-served by a friendly professional staff.

So valentine's day rolls around.  The girlfriend has been wanting to go here so I decided to surprise her with some reservations.  Got reservations for 4pm to avoid the big crowds and take advantage of happy hour.  Show up on time and as soon as I walk through the door it starts going down hill.  

The bar is packed (nothing wrong with that) and there are maybe 20% of the tables full.  None of the sections are busy.  Tell the hostess the name on the reservations and she looks around confused with a look on her face like where is she going to possibly sit us. It took 10 mins to sit us when almost all the tables were available but whatever, I ignored it.  Water came right away...took a little bit for the waiter to show who was obviously new...again, no big deal.  Ordered some drinks and oysters on the half shell.  Can't beat their happy hour prices.  In the mean time a 2 more couples came into the section we were in.  Drinks came with no oysters.  No big deal until both of the couples that sat after us got oysters along with several other orders coming out from the bar.  Let our server know, he apologized, came back with oysters and blamed it on them losing our ticket at the bar.

Still trying to manage a positive outlook...ordered some appetizers and main course.  Appetizers came, she had the bisque and I the escargot.  Mine was good, hers bland.  Not 3 mins after we got our appetizers the main course came.  Not acceptable especially since we had a table barely large enough to handle what was already on it.  The server who was not our waiter apologized without me having to say anything and took the food back.  Problem is when they brought the main course back out they may have well just left it on the table beside us.  It was cold.  I ordered a rib-eye which isn't wonderful cold but edible.  She had the hamburger everyone talks about.  Well, the problem with hamburgers is no matter how good they are made...they suck cold.  Fries cold too.  Horrible.  

So that's my Luke experience.  I'm sure without the errors of the staff it would've been a much better experience and if the food would've been presented at the right time the taste would have been better.  Unfortunately it wasn't therefore....2 stars.  Be happy it wasn't her writing this review!

Luke exemplifies craft NOLA cuisine. My first stop after my flight in from San Francisco was this restaurant and not one thing disappointed. The service was 5 star, the recommendations from the waiter were spot on and the price was on point. I will definitely return to Luke on my next visit to NOLA!

Came for coffee and bread pudding!  Did not disappoint

Delish!! Also appreciate Tim's kindness and friendliness!

Best meal I have ever eaten. Roasted chicken was flavored so well and some of the best potatoes I have tasted. Delicious grits as well. Staff was very friendly even on Christmas Eve. Waiters recommendations were right on. Very attentive staff. Clean restaurant.
Great happy hour with 75 cent oysters! Excellent beer selection and really wonderful Gumbo! We will be back next year!!!
Good food, especially the wings.  Great service and a nice spot to watch a game.  Price is right!!!

Wonderful good - rich, flavorful and the best food I had on my trip here. Have the gumbo - a great rue in this version. Skip the blue crab fritters. The Friday lunch special was amazing - highly recommend. I had several recommendations for this place; very happy with my experience there.

My fiancée and I ate here in August per a recommendation from our hotel and ever since we have been dying to get back to NOLA to eat at Luke. I think their etouffee was the single best dish I had in NOLA. Great atmosphere and definitely lived up to the "John Besh" hype.  Excited to try again this weekend for NYE. Try and ask for Richie as your server. He is the best!

Great, casual place with terrific food and service!  One of my favorite brunch spots.  The French press coffee is a notch above the rest.  The menu is not too extensive, so I always like to try something new and it never disappoints.  The French toast and breakfast sandwiches are my favorite.  Any of the lunch sandwiches and crab omelet are terrific for lunch.  I highly recommend Luke!

OMG...do delicious..I had the pasta and shrimp..so look delicious. Perfect...not to spicy..just delicious. Hubby had the potatoes chicken also so delicious. Can't go wrong..guy next to me ordered the burger OMG..looks devine..

WOW!!! I dug this!!!! Went there for lunch today & got their Thursday lunch special (veil roast, vege's & gumbo) EVERYTHING was VERY TASTY!!! dug dug DUG the GUMBO!!! So good!! & really really enjoyed the veil - so tasty & it was really just the perfect amount for a lunch!! the vege's were nice - green & yellow squash, grape tomatoes cooked perfect - not cooked to death & not seasoned to death either!! oh there was something underneath the veil ?? I don't know what it was ?fried potato pancake?? I don't know - don't care - it was YUMMY!! Service was fab! friendly!! I really enjoyed it!

Had my first mint julep here and I discovered  that I am not a fan. It was too sweet & strong for me. I tried the mussels and fries dish which came with a ton of mussels. They didn't skimp on quantity at all. Since I was visiting from Denver, a landlocked seafood less state, I was ready for any quantity of seafood. I also tried the croque madame (no egg = croque Monsieur) which was ginormous & presented on a cutting board. I tried the seafood gumbo which was really expensive but tasty. The potion could have been larger. Interior of this place is really nice with subway tiles and classic wood panels. The servers wear white coats & were very helpful and attentive. The majority of the patrons were business people. This place is walking distance from the French quarters.
Wonderful stuffed oysters, so good we came back the following day. Happy hour was also great. This is a NOLA treasure!

This place is amazing. I've been there for two days(dinner and happy hour)in a row. For dinner, you'd better make a reservation. I'm not sure they do validate parking but street parking is plentiful near here. The food is really tasty and the portions are quite large. During the happy hour (3-6 pm), the P&J Oyster is only 75cents each and drinks are half price. The staffs are very friendly and the atmosphere was great. I'd definitely go back!
Not what I expected.   Good food, great service but you have to have a reservation! No walking up to this place.
Not the most amazing food, service or atmosphere- there are so many more amazing places to eat and experience. Was solid but just not worth the high price tag overall.

Although this is an oyster house, we didn't actually have any. Instead we opted to try the Peruvian scallop. The flavor of the citrus and toppings went well together/was a good bite, but it overpowered the fish and I couldn't tasted it all. Makes for a great presentation though. 

We both got fish - swordfish with eggplant and trout almandine and we both were really happy with our selections. Custom cocktails were good too. Staff was pleasant and friendly. The table next to us got an extra/free order of the Brussels and they looked AMAZING. Very good portion size and stuff on top to justify the price. Would definitely try them next time. 

All in all a good experience, not a 5 star because of how crammed in the tables were. We were at a 2 top designed for us to sit across from each other, but I actually moved to the corner so that the waiter had space to get to the table behind us. If you're still wary due to COVID maybe sit at the bar or wait a bit longer.

If you go to this chipotle - take all your stuff in - we have been robbed twice - cars broken into, everything inside stolen. They have no cameras. Great food just sucks that they really don't care or watch observe the lot

I'm not a big one star type of guy, but in this case it's deserved. The level of chaos and poor manners from the hostess to waitstaff, servers to manager and even the servers to customers was so severe we left, after being seated and before ordering.

A server was loudly verbally trashing a patron to the manager, who obviously had no control, at the check in area, while the hostess rolled her eyes to us, clearly indicating this wasn't out of the ordinary. 

These behaviors continued until after we had been seated. After getting up and beginning to walk out, one of the servers yelled "What? How y'all going to leave?" across the restaurant, confirming our decision to escape.

Hopefully, someone will read this and do some much needed hospitality training.
The stuffed oysters were good. However our waiters were rude. I probably will not recommend to others due to the bad experience.

Had the gumbo, jumbo Louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" and steamed chocolate for dessert. This was the best shrimp and grits I've ever had and I've had a lot of shrimp and grits. Would definitely go back for their happy hour. Also, I'm a big advocate of John Besh restaurants and wasn't disappointed.

Don't let them sit you in the back room which is SO loud. 
Restrooms were clean, but smelled like sewage. There were no paper towels in the bathroom and one of the two soap dispensers was empty.
Food was just not good. Simple gem salad was drenched in beet juice, it took forever to get our first round of drinks, two people in my party of 12 added crab to their salads and both thought the amount of crab was way too little for the price, two people sent back the shrimp cocktail because it was mushy and tasted funny, flat bread was good, gumbo was good, I won't be back.

So I read all the reviews and decided to give this place a try to see what the hype was all about. I just got back from lunch and couldn't wait to write this review. 

I had lunch reservation for a later time but thought I'd try my luck and see if they could seat me sooner. I got there just in time before the lunch rush and was seated right away. My server was really nice and pleasant and I was quick to decide my lunch selection; I went with the Friday express lunch special the court bouillon which came with your choice of soup. My server recommended the crab bisque and that is what I ordered. I was seated in a corner seat with the view of the kitchen which was quite interesting. They were very good at getting the orders out quickly. I think the Friday special was a favorite as I practically saw one at every table. They brought out warm bread with butter first and then came the bisque. Needless to say, I quickly put my phone down and started savoring the soup as the aroma was very appetizing. This soup was divine. I didn't leave a drop of soup behind and the crab meat in it was perfectly sweet. Then, a few minutes later came out the "Court-bouillon" with redfish, crab, shrimp, oysters and Louisiana popcorn rice. I would say this was one of the best seafood dish I have ever tasted. I enjoyed my meal so much that I am contemplating going back there for dinner. If you are here, you must try this dish served only on Friday's. 

There was another table in front of me where a couple was seated and they received very special treatment by two men who were dressed in suits and looked like the managers of the establishment. Another table next to me with two men, were served a complimentary dessert on the house! Leads me to believe they are very serious about their regular customers unless of course they were family.

I had an incredible experience at Hachi. As a sushi lover, I'm happy to report everything we ordered was fresh, flavorful and filling! The portions are massive? I ordered 2 appetizers with my main and had to take the rest home because too much food. The service was quick, professional. My only complaint? They brought out the food too quickly. I felt a little rushed. Next time I'll ask for things to come out a bit slower.

I highly recommend this restaurant! A new favorite in the area.

On a business trip - great location. 

Had the small seafood platter (not small) it's amazing
Really great service - sat at the bar 

Wine and cocktail list great 
They have three options - glass/carafe/bottle 

Had a carafe and was able to sample an of world and new world wine selection 

For sure a nice spot to catch some fresh Louisiana bites

This restaurant has the best sushi i have had in a long time!!! Don't let the small restaurant or strip mall deceive you, the quality is amazing!!! Definitely my new go to for sushi. I went with 4 girlfriends. We all had a salad/soup app. We had kani salad, seaweed salad, kani seaweed salad and clam miso soup. All were perfect!! For rolls we had out of control, angry dragon, alligator, snow mountain and Manhattan monkey then ordered two California rolls after we DEVOURED the first order!!

Seeing Luke highly recommended on Yelp, I stopped in when I was in New Orleans recently. Even though the restaurant was crowded (Voodoo Fest weekend) and I didn't have a reservation, the host was able to find me a seat at the bar. The bartender also provided excellent service, and I ordered the Shrimp and Grits, which did not disappoint.

What did disappoint, however, was the rest of the staff. My seat at the bar was next to a wait station, and I heard a lot more than I needed to. The shouting and profanity that came out of the wait station was excessive, and I heard more than I needed to about how much the staff hated their managers, their coworkers, and the customers that night. Even though the shrimp and grits was pretty good, it's hard to speak highly of Luke when much of the staff seems to take no pride in being there.

Yum.  I travel more than anyone I know and have a rule against eating in a hotel. Break the rule and eat here..  The shrimp and grits with jalapeño were easily the best shrimp and grits I ever had and I am from NC. We had Brussels- excellent - and barbq shrimp.  If you havE had barbq shrimp in NOLA, it is not shrimp witH bbq sauce on a grill - it is soooooooo much better. Our only complaint wass that we were so full that couldn't eat dessert.

My experience mirrors that of Jon from MN. There are just too many outstanding restaurants in NOLA to waste a meal at a mediocre spot. In addition to the fair fare, our server was incredibly lame and he obviously had received zero training. We had to ask repeatedly for water, drinks, place settings and menus. When I asked who in the restaurant knew the wine list best I was initially encouraged when the bartender appeared. That changed quickly when I asked about a Cali red and he plugged it into his phone and proudly told me what town it came from. This was the full extent of his knowledge. Lastly, I tried to give management the opportunity to respond when I shared my email address on the bill in the section where they asked for comments. I wrote, Please email Me.That was three weeks ago. Zip. One and done.

We had a small holiday party during lunch at Luks. They put us in a small private room that was really nice for the occasion. Staff was exceptionally friendly and patient with our crew. The big winner of the meal was the Brussels sprouts. Everyone loved them; crispy and sweet. Burger was huge and those that had it said it was great. Court bouillon was very flavorful and hot....perfect for cold weather.  I would have given 5 stars but it was very very chilly in back of building, and we were told there was no way to control the temperature.

As a single business traveler I found this restaurant to be perfect.  It was within a nice walk of many hotels in the downtown/CBD area.  Wait staff was as gracious and attentive with me as they would have been with a party of four.  The recommendations they offered based on my likes and desires were right on.  It is a restaurant bar so there was noise.  However it was great for people watching and enjoying a delicious meal and great drinks.  I will recommend and return on my next visit to NOLA.

The Tabasco Honey Fried Chicken has to be one of the best things I have ever eaten!  I expected it to be a basic fried chicken with rice and beans, but the flavor combinations and depth of flavors were amazing!  It has been a couple of years, but I want to return to New Orleans just to eat there again!

Bottom line: Food was excellent, good ambiance, but small dining room. Food was expensive.

I had the shrimp and grits and it was on point. Succulent shrimp, not mushy, and the gravy was exceptional. 2 dozen raw oysters which were heavenly. Service was good and ambiance ebullient. The only negative was that I found the pricing to be a little high for a few things, but worthwhile as a treat.

Breakfast, Lunch, and Happy Hour -- Triple Crown

Spent 4 days in New Orleans on business and had breakfast, lunch, and one happy hour here and all were stellar.  Breakfast -- recommend the beignets with chocolate to dip them in and the pancakes with the yummy honey pecan butter.  Lunch -- huge sandwiches and great soups (especially the crab bisque).  If you're really hungry have the jumbo shrimp, andouille sausage and spicy cheese grits for lunch.  I had the fresh fish (Drum) prepared amandine with chunks of crab.  Happy Hour -- 75 cent oysters and half price beers, wines, and cocktails. I'm not an oyster fan, but was with two people who love them and they said they were fresh and flavorful.  Recommend making reservations, especially for Happy Hour.   Stop in -- you won't be disappointed.

What can I say that everyone else hasn't?! Lüke's is phenomenal. I consider myself a "foodie" and am eating my way around New Orleans this summer... And tonight I had the best shrimp and grits I've ever tasted. Each dish we ordered was honestly (no exaggeration) better than the last.

We started with the crab and born bisque... Incredibly flavorful and full of crab, which was cooked perfectly. For the main course I ordered the shrimp and grits (much fancier name on the menu) and my boyfriend tried the soft shell crab "sandwich" which is really an open faced sandwich. I really can't even describe how delicious my shrimp and grits were... Jalapeño grits baked with cheese, spicy sausage, and scrumptious shrimp. 

As two recent college grads, this place was definitely a splurge for date night - but it was worth every bite. Some seafood dishes can be heavy and extremely over-filling. But ours were just outstanding. 

Appetizers/soups/salads range in price; you won't find anything less than $7. The main courses are closer to the $25-30 range, but well worth it in our eyes.

Everything was so wonderful- I'd love to come back and try their breakfast or brunch menu! Will definitely be back, and I suggest you give them a try.

I woke up on a Sunday morning to a broken furnace and a home that was 49 degrees. I called Fahrenheit and Rob, the service manager arrived in less than 90 minutes.  He was very professional, honest and upfront about the issues and options we had.  Since our furnace was 28 years old (and the replacement parts may or may not have been available and probably would not provide a long term fix), he recommended purchasing a new unit.  The price he gave me was very fair and included a warranty and service plan above and beyond (even on our old A/C unit).  

His installation team was at my house within 90 minutes installing a new unit for me (did I mention this was a Sunday?!?).  Kyle and Pete were super nice guys and did a great job installing and cleaning up before they left.  

I would recommend Fahrenheit to anyone!

I think the Retro Fitness at North Wales is great.  If you plan your times correctly you never have to wait for a machine, they have pretty much everything you would need and just recently added some free classes that are an added value.  I belonged to LA Fitness and paid twice as much per month.. Retro is very clean and the machines are in great shape.

Cracked windshields, flat tires, wire clothing hangers and duct tape seem to be the norm at Pinellas Auto Brokers! Oh and I forgot the mulch! It looks more like a pick your part salvage yard!

I will admit that they clean the cars very well to stage in photos, but why even shine up flat tires with gaping dry rot cracks and punctures!  Look closely enough at the pictures and you will see the stereos are usually missing... Also you'll notice the mileage posted in ads is "N/A", umm' I think the odometers should work on at least a few vehicles... I swear some of the cars there were involved in a few sharknadoes, because the drivers seats looked to be bitten in half with springs exposed and stuffing all over the place...

I really hope life has treated people fair enough, that they will never have to find themselves on this ruin of a car lot... Just call Uber, ride the bus, or carpool so you can save enough money to shop elsewhere... Friends shouldn't let friends go to Pinellas Auto Brokers, unless you are curious about the existence of sharknadoes!
What can be said. Very upscale restaurant nice for special occasions. The food was some of the best we had in NOLA. Definitely a nice dining experience. Would recommend it for the great experience.

My second time to eat breakfast at Luke this morning, and each time it gets better!  The first time I went, I had the traditional Southern Breakfast...bacon, eggs, blah, blah.  It was good, but not something you couldn't get at your local Denny's.  This time, I opted for the local favorite, Grillades and Grits.  For those that don't know, Grillades are slow cooked pieces of meat with vegetables served over grits.  The meat can be beef, veal, or port--at Luke they use pork shoulder.  I accepted the upsell of two poached eggs for $5 added to the already hefty portion of grillades and grits I knew was coming.  The grillades were crisp on the outside and tender on the inside and perfectly seasoned.  The vegetables and sauce they were bathed in were reach and creamy, and balanced well with the thick grits they were piled on top of.
