The eggs didn't do anything for the dish in my opinion, except for that they looked nice on either side of the cast iron dish they were served on.

All in all, the dish was great.  I have had better grillades (try Coulis on Prytania) and for less money ($18 at Luke), but these definitely made my top 3 in taste.  The price is what I have the biggest problem with--traditionally in Louisiana, this is a hearty breakfast dish made with inexpensive, leftover cuts of tough meat, served over grits, which are also traditionally inexpensive.  By adding two poached eggs (which were quite overcooked), the dish before tax, tip, and beverage comes to $23.  I doubt any Cajuns had this price point in mind when they came up with this dish back in the day!

Luke's service has been consistently good over my last two visits.  The Franco-German look and feel to the restaurant was quite well done.  I will return to Luke in the near future to try their lunch and dinner dishes.  They were stocking the seafood bar as we left this morning, so I may have to check out their oysters and mussels on a future visit as well.
The food was hot and delicious. And the staff is probably the nicest restaurant staff I've ever came across.

Came here on a Sunday night and it was fairly crowded. We had a reservation and were seated promptly. The restaurant is not too large, but not too small on the inside. It is a foodie experience in a casual setting. A no frills kind of place.

We had the seafood gumbo and the Flemenkuche, which is a flat bread type dish. It was excellent! The combination of ingredients was just right and our whole table enjoyed this appetizer. I highly recommend trying this. For my entree, I had the Louisiana Jumbo Shrimp. The dish came out actually as a smaller portion thatn I had expected, but it was just right. The shrimp was huge and cooked to perfection, with the right amount of char.

The service was good and by the time we left around 10:30pm, we were one of the last. Great last meal in NOLA!

I love happy hour! I wish this is a thing in Boston but I intend on taking advantage of all the happy hour deals while I am in town in New Orleans! 
$0.75 oyster, $1.25 fried oysters and half off drinks 3-6pm everyday, are you kidding me?!?!
Me and my girlfriend came here for happy hour and had such a blast. The oysters are really big and delicious, the fried oysters are just heavenly, and the prices cannot be beat! 
What a great place to get drinks, their cocktails are superb and creative, I remember the French 75 to be especially good. We enjoyed so many regular and fried oysters and had several rounds of drinks at such a heavy discount and it just had our day! This will be the first time we are returning to next time we visit New Orleans :)

are you kidding me luke's knocks it out of the park best food ever drop ! this is where yelp makes me type more words in order to post a review so how about this ......... greatnesssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssssss !

Thoroughly enjoyed a respite of oysters, tuna tartare, rabbit & chicken liver pate and brussels sprouts and the service was exceptional.  In a city where there are more touristy venues than legit ones, this place rates a "we'll be back"!
Excellent. Second time here. Had 15pc sashimi.. very fresh, tasty. Great service and great  prices

So, the wife and I just checked in at the Jung Hotel and we are starving and I ask my man Delfo what's good around here ....he chuckles what do you like, try the seafood, he gives us a number of restaurants but writes down a couple more and Luke was one of them. The wife and I take the 15 min walk (which was nice ) and we walk in to the Luke and were seated , the place is fairly busy. Julian is our waiter and l ask what's this dish ( pointing to a picture on Yelp), he says it's shrimp and grits with crabmeat, so I order two, one for me the other for the Mrs., I'm not that greedy people.
  Our dishes come out and I think the wife died and went to heaven, after the first bite she says " Oh my God this is delicious" and after repeating that a few more times during the meal, I think she definitely enjoyed it, and by the way she doesn't like much. I have to say it was very delicious, didn't skimp on shrimp, and the grits were definitely not instant. There was a snafu on on my P&J oysters,but my main man Julian corrected the issue and all was well....This is a spot I will definitely return to when in the Big Easy, thanks for the great service.....P.S. try the oysters......I see you Julian.
Super dumb good!!!! Chicken wings are ok could be a seasoned a little better for my taste. However, i also had the curry chicken & broccoli SUPER FRESH TASTE!! Will definitely be back!

Guys let me tell you. I love this place and their Happy hour 75 Cent Oysters!!! My friends and I were on a hunt for Oysters but somewhere affordable and came across Luke. I read several of thier reviews which happen to be great so I suggested we check it out. HH is from 3pm-6pm and usually it seems that it would be wise to have a reservation because it can get crowded. The first night we went we were told it was an hour wait but we were lucky that we found space at the bar. We ordered two dozen oysters and let me tell you they were DELICIOUS. They were so big and we could never get those types of oysters where I am so I was very happy. We  shared two dozen oysters with 4 people and I felt like I could eat more but the Oysters are so BIG and FRESH! The next day we wanted more oysters and we looked around for somewhere new but we loved Luke so much we wanted to go back! We went back the next day around 3pm on a wednesday and I didnt need a reservation. We then again ordered our two dozen oysters and I also got a cocktail which was 50% off. I was very satisfied with the food, service and location.
Visiting New Orleans and took my husband to Lüke for his birthday.  The food was fantastic and atmosphere was lovely.  The wait staff were courteous and Johnny on the spot.

Ok. Let me start by saying how much we loved Sachi when they opened and how overjoyed  we were to have such a phenomenal sushi spot close by...no drive to philadelphia!  That being said, tonight was a mess.  They were short staffed on a Saturday night, and an hour and forty-five minutes into our time there, we still hadn't received our main course.  Things happen, I get that, but a response of, oh well everyone is waiting tonight, is totally inappropriate.  How about, I'm so sorry what can I do for you?  Ultimately we asked for our sushi "to go", we had children waiting to be picked up, and they took 20% off the bill, thank you.   Not the experience we had hoped for, but we will give it one more try.  Best "take out" I've ever had! Improve the service please so I can give you the five stars you deserve!

We went there for lunch on a Monday. We were seated right a way. I had the crawfish bisque and the rabbit and chicken pâté. My BF ordered the Chappapeela Pork Schnitzel. The bisque was yummy and the surprise was the stuffing in the crawfish head. The pate was rich and probably more than I can handle. The different relish were yummy and good palate cleanser. The schnitzel was good but not earth shattering. The mushroom sauce was a nice spin. The best part of the meal was finding out that they had a happy hour from 3-6pm. How can we pass up $0.75 oysters?!?! So we can't back. It would be nice if they have a happy hour menu with other small plates. The oysters were plump, with a hint of saltiness. We will definitely take advantage of this throughout the rest of the week.

Once you get there service they don't come out to help you. They installed a heater that was broken by the  manufacture and the manufacture wouldn't replace it.  Now it won't come on. $7,000!! Next step small claims court.

Shrimp & grits were AMAZING!

The service was great and fresh warm bread to start. Yum.

Jackson best server ever!!! I had the gulf drum and my bff has the soft crab blt.. I was amazing. I am a foodie and the food was the best hands now.. if you are visiting Nola please got to Luke.. I promise you it is worth the $$$.
Food is good for suburb sushi, however giving 3 stars because they will always ask to tip the chef for take out. Super awkward. I will usually tip but on my own accordance, I do not like to be asked.

Good one. Ate at the bar, food was good, staff friendly. They were busy. Oysters fresh. Shrimp and grits can to me a little in the cool side but they corrected that with a new plate promptly. I will return.

Although the food is good, it is quite expensive. The sandwiches are half the size of subway sandwiches and they charge more. It doesn't help that the chips they give are also puny. At $7 for a regular sandwich, I wouldn't buy it too often.

John Besh's restaurant is pretty good.  Its just unfortunate for Luke's that I had been eating way too many great meals in New Orleans and this gets lost in the shuffle.  For an appetizer we ate oysters and shrimp.  Both were really good but pretty standard appetizers in New Orleans.  For our main entree I had the jagershnitzel.  eh.  I wouldnt order it again.  The mix drinks werent as good as I had hoped.  Overall, I was really hoping for something better here.  Maybe it was the expectations.  This is really a 2 1/2 stars for me. Maybe the cooks that night were out partying at mardi gras.

Wow, what a pleasant surprise! I was expecting run of the mill strip mall Chinese. The decor is slightly upgraded from that, the service very efficient and friendly and the food was great! I could try to come up with something more clever to say but that really says it all.

They have good sandwiches, if only they were closer to my work.

The place lacks any seating, Especially in winter (in summer they set up some seats outside - really nice place to sit and relax). Its a pick up and go place, since its literally a hole on the side of a building.

They have good coffees and definitely good sandwiches (they change quite often and my random sampling of these every few months - i have not ran into a sandwich i did not like)

Great Coffee + Great Sandwiches = Perfect combo for a on the go meal.

I love this place! Went there today for dinner. I've heard of the famous chef John Besh and have been to Restaurant August, which is a high end restaurant also by John Besh. Luke is so much better! In terms of food and the whole experience, I was really impressed. To describe the food, I had their Tuesday special, which was soup, Cochon  De Lait with veggies and bread pudding for dessert. For apps, my date and I split a Flamenkuche, which is an onion tarte, with locally made bacon and caraway Emmethaner cheese. The Flamenkuche was so good. If you go to Luke's, you have to try it. I give it 10 out of 10.  My soup was corn and crab bisque, which was just ok, nothing special. My main course was good, the pork was tender and the veggies were very yummy. The bread pudding, after reading all the reviews, I had to try, but it was not as great as I hoped it would be. I will be back, just for the Flamenkuche. :)

My husband loves this place and I finally got to see why. We came here for our anniversary and despite the server being a little brusque preferring the couple next to us, she kindly gave us Prosecco and bread pudding to celebrate. Both of which were amazing. I ordered a burger and it was phenomenal. Normally I would get seafood but I was in the mood for a burger and it was great. My husband got his usual shrimp and grits and complained they were a little blander than usual, but I was quite happy.

The best shrimp etoufee I've ever had. 

I also ordered the fried oysters as well as the fresh.
The fried oysters were crunchy and met my expectations texturally but lacked flavor. 
You can't really mess up fresh oysters unless you don't shuck them right or serve ones that aren't fresh, but neither happened so I was satisfied with them.

They have happy hour specials every day so make sure you take advantage of the discounted price of 75 cents per oyster if you happen to want to eat oysters here during the 3-6PM timeframe.

The food was magnificent as well as the service. We order the jalapeño grits, crab and corn bisque, stuffed P&J oysters, blue crab gratin, and Brussels sprout. It was one of my best dining experience in New Orleans.
Our family celebrated my sister and mine's birthday here. It was amazing! Gary and Lillian were our servers, they were so sweet and accommodating!!!! Definitely recommend the Pate and French 75s!!!

Only suffering college kids could put up w this version of prison food.  Ugh.  Never again
LOCKED UP ABROAD - Philadelphia

Happy Hour Only ***

I came in on a Tuesday afternoon for their well known happy hour. They seem to be one of a few places near the French Quarter with oysters for happy hour. It was .75 per raw, $1.50 for fried. I opted for a half dozen raw and a glass of Cali Riesling. For HH food, it was only the oysters. Drinks were half off beers and domestic wines. I was hoping for half off some sides or something but there wasn't much else.

I sat by the bar since I was alone. I like that they have small TVs above the bar to view and you can watch the oysters being shucked. My bartender was nice and welcoming. I was provided the whole menu in case I wanted anything else. My table setting was made once I ordered. It was a white triangle napkin, small dish with saltine crackers and a napkin with utensils. My oysters arrived quickly after since it wasn't too busy. It came with cocktail sauce, horseradish and lemons. They were all pretty big and none were fishy. I didn't have any shells in mine but I noticed some sand grit in one.

I enjoyed the rest of my wine and another bartender  asked if I wanted anything else or more wine. I politely declined and he closed me out. I look forward to returning one day as it's hard to pass up those oyster prices!
I love their Duck Duck Rice!! And drink menu!!!

Great service nice ambience but noisy. Food was good, gumbo rue was fabulously light and tasty. Had the crab appetizer. Husband had the sausage trio, not our cup of tea. Nice choice of wine beer. Fun atmosphere.
The staff are very professional, pleasant and helpful. I've been in here quite a few times and have made some purchases and returns. I love coming here to browse around at the outdoor stuff.

Four stars for food taste, 3 star for prices, and 2 stars for hostess.  We came in at 8pm on a Tuesday night with a party of 3.  When I approached the hostess and told her how many in our group, she stated with an unfriendly tone, "With a party THAT big, you're looking at a 45 minute wait."  Since when was a party of 3 THAT big?! I was also a little in disbelief considering I saw a at least 4 open tables in plain view.  I thought to myself...ok maybe this place really IS that busy with reservations.   My group decided we'd still wait since we had already walked there and weren't familiar with the area.  Then literally 5 minutes later, we were called by a different host and ushered to a back room.  In that back room entitled "casual dining" there were probably another 4-5 open tables.  I really don't know what that hostess was talking about in the first place.  Whatever, we overlooked that and went straight in to looking at the dinner menu.  To my disappointment, the two "$$" was not really representative of the dinner menu.  Entrees were easily $21-$30+ and to me, that's not equivalent to $$.  It's more of $$$.  But since it was a John Besh restaurant...we wanted to go all out.  We ordered the PJ baked oysters, a dozen raw gulf oysters, shrimps and grits, and etoufee.  I have to admit, the raw gulf oysters were the most delicious oysters I've ever eaten.  Very sweet and did not taste like the sea.  The PJ baked oysters were equally to die for.  Very flavorful and came out piping hot.  Those were definitely the highlights of the meal.  I really enjoyed the etoufee too, especialy the sausage in them.  Service was great throughout our meal and our cups of water were never left empty.  Overall, the food and service during our meal was great and I liked how we could see the cooks preparing our food (could be a good and bad thing...since a few of them didn't look too happy and weren't entirely too refined while cooking).  I'm glad I got to try this place out and would recommend it if you are looking for a fancier but casual place to dine in LA.

My wife and I were SO looking forward to this dinner. We have all of John Besh's cookbooks. We have also had dinner a few times at the Luke in San Antonio and it was amazing. 

Luke in NOLA is NOT worth the trip. Our dinner was average at best.  First, the Hostess was HORRIBLE she was rude. She almost made us turn around and leave. Next it is LOUD and cramped. My wife was pregnant and uncomfortable. It was difficult to eat with the small table. 

The crawfish bisque was outstanding. My wife had shrimp and grits and thought they were good. My ribeye was due to come medium rare and it was overcooked. When the waiter asked about our food I told him it was overcooked. He didn't listen and said "excellent". Dessert was great. The white cake was excellent. 

Bottom line there are so many great food spots in NOLA. This one you can remove from the list.
Another lunch meeting; another great dish. I had the Tuesday special - slow roasted veal wrapped in crispy pasta in a creole tomato sauce. Cooked to perfection.

Wow, I loved this place. The comfort of the place and the comfort of the food. So, so good.

Happy hour is your friend. Get 75 cent raw P&J oysters, not just half off drinks.

Creole gumbo is a must. So is the gnocchi. Rabbit pate could've been better, but maybe it's a required taste. 

A lot of help from different servers. So you always seem to have somebody and that's good. 

Would go again, just for the oysters and brews.

Happy Hour 3-5
 .75 cent RAW Oysters
1/2 of Cocktails, Draft Beers, & Wines by the glass
Fried Oysters (6 or 12pc) *i forgot the price

You have not lived until you tried the Monday lunch special (tabasco honey chicken w/ red beans & rice). It comes with your choice of a soup or Luke salad (bibb lettuce, celery root, carrots, beets, & buttermilk dressing) for 17$. The chicken breast is fried to a tender crisp, the meat still juicy and succulent. The red beans and rice, cooked perfectly, seasoned perfectly, drool worthy!

The chicken & rabbit pate (11$) is a table pleaser too!

Definitely make a reservation on OpenTable so you don't have to stand around waiting! I am always able to score one for the time I need.

I love chipolte and was excitéd to try the queso...awful. Very watery like soup and granuley..like its a powdered cheese..I also got chips and queso and pico..never got the pico..and was stuck with grainy soupy queso and stale chips..not good.
The food here is beyond amazing! We were in NOLA for Mardi Gras 2016 and this restaurant came highly recommended. The severs here are equally awesome. I also highly recommend it!

Luke has become one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans after spending six months here. First of all, it's a John Besh restaurant, and I have grown to love his food in this city. I started off giving Luke four stars in my head, but knowing that I would be going back fairly regularly, I decided to hold off on the review and wait until I had more experiences to rate. I've been here at least 5 times, and I have 3 more weeks to add to that number. 

My favorite thing to do is go for their Happy Hour, which is a little known gem. Between the hours of 3p-6p daily, they have the best $.25 oysters. You just have to order them by 6pm, and you'll probably wait quite a while before they arrive on your table. It's worth the wait, because these are the best value you'll find in all of town. Share some oysters and the appetizers (rabbit and goose livers, the flamenkuche, foie gras terrine). As for the entrees, depending on your mood, I would recommend the cochon de lait or the croque monsieur if you want a sandwich or the shrimp grits if you want southern comfort food. One of the daily dinner specials is a pork dish over andoille cornbread stuffing. I don't know about the pork, but the cornbread can be ordered as a side (if it's the right day) and it's really, really good. The great thing about this place is how laid back and chill it is. The service is usually spot on too. 

Last tip, so you don't say I just repeated other reviews: My friends and I figured out how to make the sandwiches EVEN better. Ready? Take the pate and spread it in the cochon de lait. OMG it is sooo good. We told the waiter to recommend that to John Besh, but we're not sure if the message ever got there. If you're reading, Chef, try it!
Quick, healthy, and affordable... perfect lunch time stop! We both got the taste 2 special. (Half sandwich and soup) $8.49 each. Can't beat it!

I had the burger on my first trip and it accidentally went to someone else, so I had to wait a little longer- they were far more upset than I was and gave me the burger for free. The next day I went in and the manager personally waited on me- I had the etouffee, it was delicious!

Service was above and beyond! Very welcoming for a traveler and I highly recommend.
Amazing customer service! The guys here are great and super fast! I don't go to any other one. They are real and don't jerk you around. Thank you guys again for always being on point!

Very overrated  and It was underwhelming based on the great reviews. Service was good, but the food took a long time. We had the fried oyster salad and it was bland. The Brussels were ok, I think it was trying too hard with so many ingredients on it. The shrimp etoufee had nice flavor but wish it wasn't served as a pasta dish. Portions are quite large here.

The restaurant has a warm and inviting feel and the food was delicious.  Of course you must start off with some oysters...and the horseradish that goes with it will make you cry!  Yum!  After that, our group had the pate plate was divine just as Dieu N. says....

For dinner - our group had:
- Shrimp Farci - the stuffing in this was so good and the blood orange hollandaise - yum!
- Shrimp and grits - probably one of the best things at our table...if that is even possible.
- Crispy Pork Shank - it was huge - something that you need to definitely share
- Crabmeat ravioli - the meyer lemon with the crab is a perfect combo.

It's worth the walk for a dinner you will definitely remember!

Luke is a German themed restaurant with some seafood thrown in for good effect.  They have some good cold seafood "towers" of various types of shellfish.  They offer some changing daily specials with a core selection of consistent items on the menu.  It is a very pork heavy menu and there is a relatively small selection of main dishes.  They have a few beers that they have specially made for them and they offer some specialty cocktails. 

My favorite thing to do here is go for the Happy Hour raw oyster special.  The oysters used to be 25 cents each but the BP troubles (that caused us to release lots of fresh water into our wetlands and the fresh water, and not oil, killed off a lot of our oyster beds) caused an oyster shortage resulting in the price doubling to 50 cents an oyster but $6 for a dozen is still a great deal.  The happy hour goes from 3-6pm and it gets pretty crowded by around 4 so it can be a bit challenging to find a bar stool sometimes.  The entrees I've sampled here have been "ok" to good but often the portion size left me wanting more so usually I stick with the oysters and beer.

We came in at about 3pm having high expectations after seeing over 1000 reviews with 4 stars. 

They were 50 cents oysters so we snapped up a dozen between the wife and I. They were "meh". Large, dark, doesn't look all that fresh, not fruity or salty or anything. Pales in comparison to those I had back in Boston (island creek oyster bar). 

They were doing a express meal thing for $15 with a soup and entree. I chose the seafood gumbo which was amazing! Flavorful and rich，and not stingy with the ingredients although it was a mini cup size which left me wanting more. 

My main was a veal dish with crispy pasta. Which was great. I would go back again when I'm back at Nola

After a long day of sightseeing and experiencing New Orleans, we were looking for a convenient place to dine.  Since we were staying at the Intercontinental, we spotted Luke Restaurant at the Hilton right across St. Charles Street.

We enjoyed their daily price fixe, a fantastic lamb dish that was prepared perfectly.  The ambiance reminded me of a speakeasy or tavern from the 1930s.  Service was classy and all 3 of our courses were more delicious than the next.

The price was reasonable, the location couldn't have been better, and we left stuffed and satisfied with a wonderful taste of New Orleans.

Came here for the famous 50 cent oysters and other happy hour specials starting at 3pm, apparently every day tho I am not positive about that.  Selected drinks were half-price and certain appetizers reduced.  Didn't stay for dinner but would have had we not had other plans.  Did have dinner here a few yrs ago and don't remember any details but that it was good.

The food was good. We had the shrimp and grits with sausage and the roasted chicken. The cocktails were also tasty. The service, however, was not great. The waiters split our table (2 waiters). At one point, it took over 20 minutes for one of them to check on us, so long that we opted out of dessert due to the excessive wait. Wish I could have given five stars, but the service needs some work.

We decided to come here for Christmas Day dinner, which may have been the mistake. However, after research and looking at other yelp reviews, we thought it would be a good decision. We had a 945 PM reservation, there only one available, which was late but acceptable. We arrived at 935, and were not seated until close to 1015. We tried to be patient and understanding since it was a holiday. We did not receive our drinks until 1045. Some what disappointed by the long wait, we tried to rush and put in our order. Our server explained how tired he was to another table, which is understandable, however we placed in our apps and only received half of our order. I had put our reservation under a Birthday celebration, and reminded our waiter as well. As we closed out our meal, I waited for a special dessert or song, and nothing happened. I was very disappointed. I not only made the reservation with this in a note, but I asked front of the house, and our server! To say the least, our food was mediocre and service was less than fair. And, the menu posted online was not what was available. Which was also disappointing.

What a great little spot with an chill atmosphere, amazing food and outstanding service!!! 

I must say the waiter Eldwyn was one of the best I have had in a very long time.

Did not have good food experience. My grilled chicken sandwich was soooo rubbery and tiny bit of toppings including limp lettuce and tomato. Gave our dog some chicken strips and she has soft stools today. Service was very good and they wore gloves (hoping they are changing and washing hands frequently). Hamburger was so-so too. Not the Sonic I've had there previously. Has been a year or more.

W.T.F.

This place was a disaster from the first minute, when we walked in the door to be met by an apparent hostess with a spray bottle in her hand (getting a jump on closing duties, presumably, despite it being more than 90 minutes till closing...) and a grimace. We informed her that we had reservations and she allowed us to sit. Thanks!

We sat at the bar. Our corner thereof was covered with sticky dried oyster leavins, like, nasty. The bar guy took our order and we asked for maybe a wipe-down. He gave it a quick swipe with a DRY towel, explaining "This is where people eat a lot of oysters." Ah! Well, that explains it! If only people didn't eat here, it wouldn't be so nasty.

A little later another person came (maybe a floor manager or something?) and gave it another once-over with a DRY towel. Have these people been working in a bar more than a combined 4 minutes total? Anyway, the sticky oyster leavins were unaffected.

Unfazed, we ordered a dozen oysters. BOOM! Talk about quick service! Should be a plus, but what it means is that they took the thing out of a fridge. We saw it: a platter of already-shucked oysters, pulled out of the fridge. And the oysters were just what you'd expect under such circumstances: a bit dried out and rubbery (maybe the hostess could have spritzed them with her spray bottle?). Not what you're looking for in raw oysters.

We ate a couple, then asked for the bill. Total time elapsed: 10 minutes. Time to cut our losses and find something to eat.

To their credit, they noticed that we only ate a few of the oysters, so they took that off the bill. But seriously - for a fancy place with a great rep, what was going on this night?

What a disappointment.

We went on Christmas evening and ordered off of the shortened menu. Our oysters and cocktails came quickly and were fantastic. And then we went another 45 minutes without seeing our server again.

Eventually someone noticed we were sitting their hungry and unhappy. This was not our mysterious server. She comped up another round of drinks and sent over an appetizer neither of was interested in, and then our food finally arrived. I understand that the kitchen can get backed up, especially if you're short staffed due to a holiday, but you've got to keep the customer in the loop. Not just ignore them and hope for the best.

Now to our food. I actually enjoyed my shrimp and grits at the time, but with the hindsight of waking up the next morning with my mouth still tasting of salt I'm not sure I'd recommend it. Her pasta was over cooked and overtly sweet with tiny unappealing shrimp compared to the big tasty jumbos on my plate. She barely ate it.

If this were any other night, and every other restaurant in town wasn't either booked up or closed, we would have told them to bring us the bill instead of the mains, paid for our drinks and oysters, and left to find dinner elsewhere. Instead we were stuck. 

Even with the comped drinks and app, this was the most expensive meal we had in New Orleans. it was also the worst. And that's a shame.

I'm giving Luke 2 stars.  The food was just ok.  But the service was not what I expected at all.  Coming to my home town and seeing for myself how the staff here is Chy St crazy to me.  We had to be moved because the air condition was dripping water on my back. So not cool. I hope when I come back it will be much better.... Chow for now

Wonderful place!!  Great food, good atmosphere and weekend happy hour.  I had the stuffed P&J oysters, amazing!  The soft shell crab BLT was one of the best things I've ever had, finished every single bite!!!

Our came here on our first night in NOLA for dinner. The local oysters was fresh and yummy. It was more cheap than what we paid for in CA. We ordered small seafood platter and add half dozen of local oysters, shrimp etouffee, softshell crab, fried oysters salad and ribeye. Oysters were so fresh, the tuna poke with shrimp chip was really flavorful. Fried oysters salad was refreshing. The only dish I was happy with was the shrimp etouffee. The pasta is too doughy. Service was good and our server was attentive. Bread pudding was on the house as we were celebrating my friend's birthday.

I am writing this review on their breakfast/brunch. I've only been for dinner once, and I prefer the breakfast. Being a creature of habit, I order the pain perdu 99% of the time. It is out of this world. Gooey mascarpone cheese, thick and delicious bacon, sweet challah bread...what more could you want?! They have a load of great stuff, so try more than me! My husband switches it up a lot and hasn't been disappointed. He prefers the shrimp and grits, though. We always bring friends and family here when they're visiting. 
Prices are decent, but no bottomless drinks for brunch. 
Wait staff is slow, but friendly. 
The interior is beautiful and stretches all the way to the back, where you can then see the cooks doing their thing.

Sonic has really gone downhill in general, but this location disappointed me so much. I restarted my order three times because the idiot lady taking orders was not getting it right. Finally, it was repeated back to me correctly and I said okay an because they were busy had an above average wait time. I was then brought the wrong order. When I told the carhop I stated the order three times and it was still wrong he says oh I'm sorry here's your total.... no offer for fixing it, nothing. Just pay for your wrong order and eat it or don't. We ate as much as we could if the overcooked, nasty food. It was not worth the hassle of dealing with original idiot order taker or waiting another above average wait time for gross food so that was fifteen bucks thrown away and we ended up at Taco Bell's drive thru. I would avoid all Sonics but this location was especially subpar.
Platinum Best lunch experience and food heaven!  Very satisfied, so delicious, great wait staff, impeccable service and over the top delicious entrees!  Recommended 5 star!

Loved Luke. Problem is, you should make a reservation if you want to splurge on happy hour oysters! We went twice and in the end were able to secure a spot - we actually had to rush to the airport so the hubby and I slurped down 24 oysters within 5 minutes. Not great if you are an "on a whim" diner like me in a new city, but it was so worth it!

THE ABSOLUTE BEST!!!! I cannot say enough good things about this place!!! The service was out of this world!!!! I told our servers our sons name is Luke and they gave us a free cup and bag to take to him! The reisling wine I had was THE BEST glass of wine I have ever had!!!! The fried oysters are AMAZING!!!! Never have had better and never will!!! We got the salad but asked for the oysters to be kept separate. The salad was phenomenal. The bacon that was on that salad was unlike any I have ever had. We split the shrimp and andouille sausage dish. The creamy grits it came on were so tasty!!! Plenty of kick and seasoning but could still Tate what I was eating. The portions are huge...so splitting the meal was still so much food!!! I truly cannot say enough good things about this place!!!! I will come back every single time I am in NOLA!!!

We sat. And we sat. And continued to sit.....


 for our server who was for a lack of a better term, acting as if she was mentally challenged.  She wasn't seen serving any other tables, but I was willing to give the benefit of the doubt. Our story unfolds,   the wine I selected was unavailable, and the 2nd choice was warm.    The food-muscles were delightful, but the bread options were lacking.  I do not need a Susan Spicer artisian bread for muscle  gravy run-off.  I need a plain white french.  Co-author had the burger, and although enjoyed it- didn't warrant the 17 dollar price tag.  Fries were good.   We didn't stay for dessert.  Server was a wall flower who didn't "wow" us, didn't "sell" me,  and wouldn't care if we came back.   Too bad, I would have liked to.  I would have liked to come back and get served by someone who had passion for the food he/she was serving, and we would have gladly dropped more dime.


Props to the hostess for quick seating, and for standing in front of the flaccid and wilting floral arrangement at the door.  Sorry, I still noticed it.  Also, thank you for all the paper menus to go, I like to keep them.

Good food but service was bad. We had two servers - one was decent and the other not good - very casual attitude and didn't seem liked he had ever been trained. We were offered a dessert menu, accepted, but no menu ever came.

First visit to a Chipotle and I'm impressed. Everything was delicious and they're looking out for customers well. It wasn't all that busy but limited capacity due to covid precautions were present. Now, how do I get one of these located in Muncie?

Had a great happy hour here. Great, strong drinks and excellent bites. This was the first place I've been where I actually really liked the fried oysters--usually they have an odd, mealy texture for me. A little pricey but worth the quality. Would go again.

I've eaten at Luke in San Antonio several times and have been a fan since my first bite there. When I planned our trip to New Orleans, it seemed a no-brainer that we needed to try the NOLA Luke.. and I'm so glad we did. If it's possible, this location far surpasses the SA location in terms of atmosphere and quality. We were seated next to the kitchen which has windows to allow patrons to see all the action. It was a lot of fun watching the process of all the food being prepared and plated. We started with a River Bend cocktail (YUM!) and the Crispy Brussels Sprouts appetizer. Holy Hell. I have been scouring the internet trying to find a similar recipe and I can't find one.. the description doesn't mention that it's a spicy dish but don't let that scare you away. It might be one of the best things I've ever eaten. I got the shrimp and grits, because duh. New Orleans. My boyfriend got their Fresh Gulf Fish amandine style with the veggies. The first that night was drum and it was amazing. We opted against dessert because we had some sweets we'd picked up earlier in the day, but I have no doubts their desserts are as tasty as their entrees. If you've never been to Luke, I suggest you do it at least once in your life. You can thank me later.

I'm absolutely enamored by this place.  And how you can not with fifty cent oysters and half off drinks from 3-6 pm everyday?!  Everything about Luke, from the robust menu to the dark hardwood and tile throughout the restaurant feels right.  A little secret that I kind of don't want to share, is that they have several small TV's at the bar and when there is a Saints game scheduled during happy hour I'm there slurping down several dozen oysters and a French 75.

The oysters are always really clean with their muscle completely detached from their shells with almost no shell debris inside.  The flavors of the oysters definitely change with the seasons, but I've yet to have a dud of an oyster here.  Their French 75, a strong yet delicate cocktail made with cognac and champagne has a nice froth and mellow sweetness created by a booze soaked cherry.  Sometimes I will order small plates or a sandwich off the menu which have all been excellent.  Last time I ordered the pate it came with pickled watermelon rind and I'm still thinking about those sweet, crunchy pickles.  The Luke burger is one of the best in the city and comes with perfectly crispy fries.

Okay so I admit I used to always go here until the one off Myrtle opened since I live downtown. However we returned to this one today since we were going see a movie at Edwards on overland. 

It was busy during lunch time so we had expectations that our food might take longer and that's chill. Anyway we finally got our food and my girlfriends pasta she ordered wasn't warm and we asked the server if we could get it heated up and her response was "we have a microwave you can go use" and got all huffy when we were like we'll can you just do it? She ended up just making us a new one but she acted all put out which really rubbed us the wrong way. 

Honestly it left a bad impression and we won't be returning to this location. However at least we won't have to see her tacky poorly done tattoo sleeve? Lol

Super fancy place. Lol. Not exactly what I was expecting but they had happy hour oysters for 75 cents. Which is a steal. I'd never had raw oysters before so that was interesting. Very very salty and there's still sea water or something when you slurp it down lol. Awk.

I usually get the Luke Burger, but decided that it's time I tried something else AND wrote a review, so here we go!

Luke Burger (and Housemade Fries):  My wife disagrees, but I hold that this is the best burger in New Orleans.  I'm gonna qualify this by saying that for $5 less, I could get almost as much pleasure out of a Five Guys burger or a Dave's Single at Wendy's.  Take it for what it is.  The value here is in the distinctive flavors of the burger--Emmenthal cheese, SMOKED bacon, and carmelized onions.  If you can't imagine getting $5 more flavor from a burger than at Five Guys or Wendy's, then this isn't your item.  HOWEVER, it's still worth getting a side (or starter) of the Housemade Fries, cooked in duck fat and perfectly salted.  Just make sure you get to those fries sooner rather than later.  They don't sit around very well.

Fried Oysters:  OMG.  So good.  We were meeting friends at Luke for dinner this week.  We're usually on time or a few minutes early, but we arrived at 5:15 for our 5:30 reservation.  No problem.  The table was ready and waiting, so my wife and I were seated early and decided to get some discounted fried oysters since it was still happy hour.  They were delicious, and the dipping sauce was a perfect complement--creamy but light, not heavy or overly buttery, a complement of flavor that didn't override or obscure the taste and texture of the oysters.

Crispy Brussels Sprouts:  Our friends arrived and we got another starter of Crispy Sprouts.  Crispy is the correct adjective, and not burned--a wonderful texture that was rounded out with a fruity-sweet honey sauce and toasted sliced almonds.  This is happening again the next time we go.  (That's the theme of this review..."again...next time...")

Fried Oyster Salad:  This is where we lose a star.  Loved the oysters.  There wasn't a SINGLE leaf of wilted greens in the whole salad (yes, I'm that guy that rifles through his salad and tosses anything that even looks like it might have been crushed or wilted), but the bacon was too smokey for this use.  It's delicious on the burgers but not so much in the salad.  I read other reviews that said the same thing--too smokey or too much bacon (not possible)--but didn't believe them.  It's not too MUCH bacon, but there was definitely too much smoke (in total) in my salad.  That's such a devil's dilemma for me because I don't want to toss any of my blessed bacon, but there it is: too much smoke.  I (almost) ate it all, and regretted it when I was eating dessert 20 minutes later with smoke flavor still in my mouth.  I would say half the amount of bacon would be perfect, but my rule is, "if you have to ask for changes, you should probably order something else or go somewhere else."

Crawfish Bisque:  mmmmmmmm.  So good.  Smooth with kernels of corn for texture.  What I SHOULD have ordered was a whole bowl of this instead of only a cup on the side of the Oyster Salad.  Next time...

Dark Chocolate Torte:  I had a bad experience with chocolate cake as a child, so I tend to avoid it.  This was a happy exception to my rule, thanks to my wife.  It came on the plate with a ball of coconut sorbet, both of which were silky smooth on the palate, and garnished with tons of toasted sliced almonds.  The cake is small--the size of a hockey puck--so if you have "plenty of room for dessert," I recommend that you NOT share this one--you could end up like Gollum when there's two spoons going for the last bite:  "That's MY PRECIOUS!!"

Bon Appetit!
We had the BEST customer service today! I will come again just based on the kindness of the register person!

I was in the mood for some oysters after the Saints game Monday and this place hit the spot! The staff was friendly and the food was speedy. We got a dozen oysters, stuffed oysters, crab gratin and Brussels sprouts. They were all delicious and those oysters were amazingly satisfying when your kicker hits the game winning goal to win the home opener! Who DAT!

What a gem! Was here based on recommendations, even though it's like a 40 min drive form my house and could not agree with the reviews more.
When you drive up to this unassuming place tucked away in a suburban shopping plaza, you do not think that you will get some really high quality sushi. But it's legit! The decor is very modern and sleek. Lovely lighting and atmosphere. 
We were lucky enough to get a reservation for a Friday night and were seated at a nice round corner table. It's a BYOB so a huge plus. 
Ordered a verity of different appetizers and rolls. All a perfection! My favorite was the oyster shot from raw bar menu - fresh and delicious. 

The only real reason I give this place 4 stars is because we did not have a good service experience. I think the restaurant was just very busy and unfortunately about an hour passed before we got any food. Some of our appetizers came at the very end, after our meal has been served, at the point where we were no longer hungry. In fact I had to ask on a several occasions whether the food was coming out. We got our last dish about 1.5 hours after ordering it. 
I really do think it was just an off night and would gladly come here again to give Hachi another shot at redemption.

Best service!!! And as always, great food. We came with a large party for a friends birthday. Our waiter made sure everything was out at the same time and everyone's meal was nice and hot. Even shared their Brussel sprout recipe!!

This food is amazing! Eat here.  This ended our culinary journey of new Orleans royalty including: john besh, Emeril Lagasse, Paul Prudhomme, I've visited several before, but not in succession.   Straight up comparisons where possible were done.  
Here we had the following: 
Boudin balls
Pate
Crab bisque 
Pork schnitzel 
Shrimp etouffee 
Watermelon sorbet 
Lemon torte 
The pate and accoutrements were flawless and a major standout. I was soooooo happy I could have eaten it alone e for dinner.  My companion who "hates liver why should I taste it"  really liked it and ate an entire country crouton alone with a little brown mustard. 
I preferred the pepper jam with mine.  Adventure forth and try things here you've previously disliked John and his crew can make a shoe taste good with a bic lighter! 
Best etouffee I've ever had.
I personally prefer Emeril's boudin balls. See my review of Emeril's for specifics. 
I will never eat at K Paul's again. The management is suspect.  The food poorly prepared and served BLATANTLY untrained.  See my review of Paul's for details.   
The food and service from Emeril's and John's Luke are a close race and personal tastes come into play.  Both are worth your money and time from experience.   Follow me to enjoy my other reviews from around the country.

Good service and great food. We were seated promptly, even though we arrive :30 early. Food cake promptly and piping hot. Everything was to our liking and service delivered. Wouldn't hesitate to visit again.

Luke was a good choice for a fine dinner. The menu  was quintessentially New Orleans, and the ambiance was great. You can never go wrong with the local oysters, and our drinks were well-made. 

Our group had the duck duck rice (crispy rice in duck confit), shrimp and grits, and the shrimp/crawfish etouffee. Even the take-aways tasted good unmicrowaved (can't be too fussy after a night out on Bourbon). Anyway, overall a great experience, great service. It would have been a solid 5 -- but I got a tiny bit of hair in my etouffee. Didn't bother me as much as it did my friends. I would've still ate it.. but still, that was a little unexpected. 

Still would recommend!

Went with my gal pals for happy hour. It's a cool chill place. We enjoyed watching the hustle and bustle of the locals. Our server was great and very attentive. We stopped for libations and a lite snack but ended up getting coffee, dessert, and a cocktail. The cocktails were a bit strong for our taste but once the ice melted a bit they were good. Will definitely visit again before the end of our trip when we're not in a rush.

For me, some Besh restaurants have been hit or miss. This one however was one of the best. It is located inside a hotel so be sure to look for the banner out front with the name as the hotel facade is under construction. I opted for the Luke breakfast that came with house made andouille, a biscuit, eggs, and jalapeno cheese grits.  All were delicious. My crawfish bisque was great as well. Brunch cocktails included a French 75 and the coffee was French pressed. My server and  meal was perfect after a late night at Tipitina's.

Luke, a John Besh original and mainstay on St. Charles Street....333 St. Charles to be exact.  I am from San Antonio and used to frequent his Luke attached to the Embassy Suites on the corner of Houston Street downtown.  In its heyday, it was THE placed to go.  Happy hour was the bomb.  Tumultuous and trendy all in one setting.  Sadly, its management changed REGULARLY and the place just went to Hades in a hand-basket - it is now closed.  Oops...too much reminiscing of  place gone away...on to Luke, New Orleans.  Happy hour is 3-6 and they have $.75 oysters on the half-shell.  Yep, you heard me right..FRESH gulf oysters on the half-shell for a mere 3/4s of a dollar each.  So, my son and I ate 36 of those bad boys on November 21st upon arrival in the city.  I wanted to compare the "glory days" of Luke San Antonio with Luke New Orleans.  The oysters were scrumptious.  Literally.  They had ample bar specials and I drank two draft lagers - bartenders call - and he hit the mark.  Complimented the oysters spot-on.  My son had a Sazerac and tried the French 75 (a drink made of brandy, French champagne w/egg whites which give it a delightful froth on the top).  Some may call it a - at the expense of being called "inappropriate" - a girl's drink, but it is good stuff people.  Leave it for the last drink and call it dessert.  AND, if you still want to call it a drink for the fairer sex, then you can again realize why women rule the world and they just LET us think that we do.  Anyway, if in New Orleans and near Bourbon Street, go to the happy hour at Luke, suck down (or chew and swallow!!!) some oysters, have a drink or two or three at their full service bar and enjoy.  You will, I guarantee you that.  Oysters away.  Oh yeah, eat a meal there and you won't be sorry either...these folks can cook...try the shrimp and grits....a mainstay and worth the money spent.  Exceedingly New Orleans appropriate.  Off to the next spot....enjoy and God bless !

After a wonderful dinner at August the previous night, we wanted to try another restaurant in the BRG Hospitality portfolio. Luke seemed like a popular choice. 

When we arrived for our reservation, we saw that Luke was a popular choice...if you are a party of middle-aged men dressed in suits and ties.   What I'm trying to say is that Luke seems to be the place for a nice business lunch. We definitely stood out as tourists. 

My family decided to share the crawfish bisque, gumbo, stuffed P&J oysters, and hot buttered crawfish and burrata tartine. Everything was just alright. The crawfish gumbo was so thick it took on an almost sticky texture. The tartine had so much potential but fell short in flavor. The best item was probably the stuffed oysters, but I'd rather have the char-broiled oysters at Acme.

Overall, the food was mediocre and it was difficult to relax and enjoy our meal with all the hustle and bustle around us. After reading all the good reviews, I was disappointed by our experience.

Do not trust these people. We had a power surge in our neighborhood and our boiler blew. They came to our small city house and told us we needed an entirely new boiler system (even though ours is only about 10 years old) and quoted us over $8000!!!! Luckily, later that day we ran into our neighbors who told us they were having the same issue and that they were having the part (the transformer) replaced for around $300. Turns out all the boilers that were affected by the surge had the same problem which is a relatively simple part to replace. I thought it was shameful that Fahrenheit tried to take advantage of me and my family in a moment of need (no heat with a baby). Shame on you Fahrenheit.

Very bad customer service! The manager guy was very nasty he has a very bad attitude!!! My food was nasty like my chicken had be re cooked it was as dry an rubbery! I ask can he fix the problem change the order he said no! I'm bout to close I will credit u! I said we are hungry just give me my money back he said don't order here again!!!!! Watch out for this place.....

Their happy hour is bomb. $0.75 oysters and half off draft beer, cocktails and wine. We came here for a pre dinner snack and drinks and spent $150 for 42 oysters and loads of drinks for 6 people. The oysters were HUGE and very yummy. We came at 4:30, which was the perfect amount of time before happy hour ended at  6. Their first dinner seating was around 5/5:30, and at one point, we heard the waitress say there was a 1:45 min wait so make a reservation, even for happy hour.

Luke is pretty good.  Went here for lunch with my husband and his parents who were visiting for the weekend.  

I wasn't surprised to see that it was rather busy during lunchtime on a Friday since it's in the middle of the CBD.  Despite the crowd there was hardly a wait before we were seated.

Luke was definitely perfect for the in-laws.  Right up front they've got well-known newspapers for anyone to grab at their convenience in case you want to catch up on the news while enjoying your meal.  The newspapers were right up my father-in-law's alley.  

I really liked the decor as well but then it's just my taste in dark wood and I was impressed with the vintage pulley fan system.  I think if it was just my husband and I, I would have preferred to sit up at the massive bar.  

The service was swift and friendly.  My father-in-law thought his gumbo was too cold so they immediately brought him a new one at the correct temperature.

Personally, I got the express menu for the day which includes a cup of soup and an entree.  I ordered the crawfish bisque and the redfish "court-bouillon" with crab, shrimp, oysters, and rice.  Good deal, I'd say!  

The bisque was perfectly smooth and creamy.  It was a relatively cool day outside and it warmed me right up.  I might be biased though since I'm a fan of bisques in general.  I wasn't sure if I would like the redfish court-bouillon but it was excellent!  It came out in a small cast-iron dish and it was just a great mixture of seafood and rice.  The sauce had a kick to it without being too spicy.

I would definitely come back here again as I was rather envious seeing the Luke Burger being carried to other tables.  It just LOOKS good sitting on a wood plank alongside some fresh fries and you get these cute, teeny, personal condiments.  So yeah, next time!

This would be five stars except we were seated in the back room (probably because my daughter and son-in-law brought their baby) and boy did it smell strongly of mildew!  I was so looking forward to the cheese plate I had here several years ago, but was disappointed to find it's not carried any more.  The food and service were excellent, but be
 sure to ask to sit in the front room.

Had a great experience at Luke's on Friday night. The P&J oysters and shrimp prepared by Phil was amazing. I followed it up with the Louisiana Crawfish Étouffée which was delectable, especially the crunchy rice combination with the crawfish. Highly recommend!

Just returned from a 3 day weekend. I went here right after checking in because I just needed some fried oysters. It was too early for the oyster happy hour so the only way to get my fix was to get the fried oyster salad. What's not to like. Lettuce, ( the fancy kinds that make you look foolish while trying to find a small enough bite to shovel in), Benton bacon , avocado and ranch. Cadence was my lovely server and she was a delight. I was sitting near the glassed in kitchen so I could watch them work. Quite a well oiled machine. Well, I am a bacon lover and discovered that I could not stand Benton bacon. The hickory smoke was so strong it overwhelms the delicacy of the oysters and they were quite generous with it. I tried to pick it out but it was just too prevalent. So I just picked off the oysters which were fried so perfectly and ate the avocado. I never tried a bacon I didn't love until that day. The wine was nice but ridiculously pricy.

We did return for the oyster happy hour. They were just wonderful. The seafood gumbo was okay, all the veggies were cooked to death but I am unrealistically picky about gumbo. I had to take a star because while it wasn't busy, I think the bartenders were changing shifts and it took forever to get the check. Still love the oysters!
Hidden gem in New Orleans id say some of the best food i have had there! Staff is super friendly and professional! The Brussels are a must have!!

I stopped in here based off of the Yelp reviews and mention of awesome happy hour. I walked in and there were three young girls at the hostess stand. After asking for a table for one since there was no room at the bar I was questioned, "how many"? After explaining I was just stopping in for a drink and app I was ushered away from the main dining area which had plenty of seats. I asked if I could sit in the main dining area and was told "this will be fine for you". 

I was seated by the kitchen, this ended up being great, the kitchen staff was clean and working hard.

I waited a few minutes for my waiter, asked about the drinks and was given water. My drink was quite tasty, a speciality cocktail with champagne that. Y server recommended.

I decided on grits for my app as they sounded amazing. They came out fast, one bite and they were warm at best. I waited a few minutes for my server and asked if he could warm them up. I also requested more water as mine had been empty for a while. He was super nice about both requests.

My grits came out a few minutes later (fresh cast iron dish) and they were bubbling over, nice and hot. I wasn't given a new plate or utensils, one I got these I was able to DIG in! They did not disappoint! The chef came over to make sure they were hot enough and I assured him they were amazing. My only regret is I didn't try the tasty French bread I was offered and declined.

During my dining experience I noted my server standing in the back corner chatting with co-workers and laughing. He was very nice, not the most attentive but very nice.

The table next to me ordered a burger and it was so huge they so huge they spilt it. The presentation was beautiful and I could tell they greatly enjoyed it. 

Another table ordered the Brussels sprouts that looked to DIE for! Bowls of gumbo that they raved about, soft shell crab and etoufee. 

Would I come back again? Likely not, there are just too many other places to try while I am here.

Luke was a pleasant surprise. Our party was on the way out of New Orleans and had a few hours to kill so we decided to stop at Luke's for a meal. We were hesitant because we never heard anything about Luke and it is inside the Hilton in the French quarters. I tend to avoid restaurants inside hotels thinking that they are expensive and usually not that good. I'm glad I was wrong. 

To our delight, we discovered that Luke has 50 cent oysters during their happy hour. Their oysters were fresh and extremely delicious. We have had a lot of oysters during our 5 days stay, but none compared to Luke's. The fact that it was 50 cent each was just icing on the cake. 

The delicious oyster set us up for the main course. We were indecisive but all of us ultimately ended up ordering the ribeye. It was fantastic! My medium rare ribeye was sweet, juicy, tender. My friends all echoed the same about their ribeyes. It was just a perfect cap to our wonderful trip. Next time I'm in the Big Easy, I will definitely stop by Luke if only to take advantage of their oysters.

Lukes was actually a saviour of a place on Valentine's Day for dinner. The place I thought I had originally booked I made a mistake so we booked Luke's as a last minute what a great mistake to make!

From the moment we got there we love the place. The turnstile door was a perfect portal into an amazing restaurant.

Being that we had to book our Valentine's dinner last minute we were eating at 5:30 which worked out in our favour as it was still happy hour.

 Our server Gary gave us great recommendations on drinks and informed us that the P&J oysters were part of happy hour at a dollar each.  These were some of the freshest oysters we've ever had and you could taste the ocean in every bite.

Next we had the tuna tartare are. Great flavour amazing combination of tuna avocado cucumber and jalapenos. Just enough heat to add to the overall dish.

My sexy hot wife ordered the oxtail which came over a bed of homemade egg noodles, wild mushrooms and with crispy kale mixed in for texture. Season perfectly with amazing flavour.

I had the courtbullion which was a tremendous mixture of oysters, crab claws, shrimp and redfish over rice in a very flavorful sauce.

 This was a perfect mistake to make him reservations for Valentine's Day as we had an amazing meal and would definitely go back next time we visit New Orleans.

Love love love! Everyone who worked here was sooo friendly but also the food was delicious! I came here for an early birthday dinner and everything was lovely! We started with the spinach crab dip as an appetizer and ordered a bottle of champagne. The dip was so tasty! I ordered the crab pasta and my friends ordered shrimp and grits and the mussels and fries. I really enjoyed everything! (Of course I sampled off of everyone's plate!!) We went to order another bottle of champagne and our server said they were waiting on it to chill so they gave me a complimentary bottle of a different type. That was so shocking and so sweet! I also got a complimentary bread pudding and it was melt in your mouth delicious! 10/10 recommend! Also, the raw oysters were so big and didn't have that fishy after taste like you get from some other restaurants!

Oh my- we made a reservation for 6 and when we got there, they couldn't find the res. I almost panicked, as this was for a special occasion. No worries though, the hostess found my phone number in the computer and could see something went wrong in the initial res process, so she worked some magic to get us a table. We sat in the back room where we could see the kitchen exhibition style. The servers are classy and friendly- we ordered a bottle of champs and they brought us another on the house, since there were so many of us. They gave us a champs bottle opening presentation as well- which was a fun touch. We ordered oysters With crabmeat to start, hot and tasty served on a bed of salt presentation. Also the brussels sprout were uhhhhmayyyyyzing - they even shared the recipe with us. How gracious! Each of us selected our dishes, i got the grilled pompano fish on top of crispy kale and roasted parsnips- the kale was amazing. I tried my friends white wine and garlic muscles and couldn't stop eating them, also another friend got the lamb served with faro and beats- which i really liked! The staff was amazing, the food was great, the atmosphere was classy NOLA- we really had a special dinner!

Landed in New Orleans on Thanksgiving day and managed to get a spot here for Thanksgiving dinner. Since it was Thanksgiving, the other customers were mainly Asian tourists - it was pretty homey.

We ordered the turducken for the bragging rights. Honestly all the meat kinda tasted the same, but I was pleased with the juiciness. In addition to the turducken, we also got the gumbo (good) and the bread pudding (excellent!).

For two people who just got off a plane, this was a good amount of food. A pleasant first meal in NOLA.

I'm not a fan. It's a happening place though, I'll tell you that. I'm a fan of soup and salad but this place didn't do it for me and I really wanted it to be. When I walked in and the line was nearly out the door. Gotta be some good food! I noticed tablets on the wall where you can order your food and not wait in line. So I gave up human interaction and used technology. Free coffee signs illuminated the screen. I was disappointed on the menu selection. Limited number of soups and salads. They didn't even have clam chowder! We ordered and sat down. Was excited to get my soup in a bread bowl. The food came, the food went...It wasn't my order. Human error. Cool. 
My food came. The half a sandwich was more like 1/4 sandwich. Literally gone in two bites.  Rather disappointing. My friends soup had cheese that didn't melt and placed his finger in the soup and it was cold. I thought no way can't be cold. I took a spoonful. It wasn't luke warm- it...was...cold! 
Bread was okay... nothing special. 
Salad, Sandwich, and beverage $13. Could have spent the same money at a sit down restaurant and be satisfied.

A trip to New Orleans without trying a John Besh restaurant wouldn't be proper. He is a pride of the south in this industry and his food highlights why their cuisine is truly a gem, by adding his own twist and a touch of class.

Make reservations in advance. The restaurant is in the Hilton Hotel but with a separate entrance. Though the ambiance is upscale, the atmosphere was very relaxed and casual, buzzing with patrons ranging from families with kids, girls on a night out, couples on dates, etc. You get the picture - everyone's welcome.

This was our first meal on our trip where we actually felt hungry before eating. That said, we went crazy and ordered quite a few things between two people.

The bread that started us off was warm but we knew better than to get full from that. We however indulged ourselves more than we should with the vibrant and earthy PATE of Louisiana RABBIT & CHICKEN LIVERS ($11). I ate this with sweet peppers, blueberry preserve, table pickles, relish, and honey grain mustard atop a nicely crisp crostini. It was fabulous. I had fun with mixing and matching all the sides because everything seemed to work together. That jar of pate was begging to be licked clean, I tell you.

SEAFOOD GUMBO a LA CREOLE ($10/bowl) was served on a tin cup then poured over the rice on the bowl. This was mighty tasty for our first gumbo on this trip and hearty as should be. A cup might have been a more appropriate portion for us though.

We initially had no greens added to our order but our server raved about the BRUSSELS SPROUTS ($12), crispy and glazed with honey siracha. Now, how can we possibly say no to that? One bite was all it took for us to know we made a wise decision.

Our main dish was no other than the JUMBO LOUISIANA SHRIMP EN COCOTTE ($24). Wow, the shrimps were huge and succulent, the roasted jalapeno cheese grits were creamy and hearty, while the Andouille & green onion sausages were flavorful and added a kick - oh my palate was dancing and singing with joy! It was nice of them to serve this on split cast irons since we were sharing. The portion was just right, in fact, because the food was rich, you'll get easily stuffed. 

I don't know how we did it but trying BRENDAN's BREAD PUDDING ($8) was the very 2nd reason (next to the shrimp and grits) why we booked a table at Luke's. Our stomachs probably knew better and paved the way for its presence because man was it off the charts scrumptious in every way. The vanilla bean ice cream and the hot buttered pecan sauce were literally the icing on this cake. 

I have no complaints! Thanks to our server who was a sweetheart and for making our experience here more memorable.

I love Luke along with the other restaurants in the "John Besh" group. The location and atmosphere are both major pluses. I got the Rabbit Ragout and a dozen P&J oysters. The Ragout was AMAZING, such an interesting take on a typical pasta dish and it was so incredibly fresh. Same goes for the P&Js, they were huge and obviously fresh. My experience with Luke has always been great so it really does surprise me to see some negative reviews. Overall Luke is fresh and trendy, and I always have a great experience.

Came here on a whim looking for a good chicken biscuit. Wow! Was not disappointed. Best one I've had, it came with cheese grits that were also the best I've had. The design from the floor to the ceiling is amazing. Our server Matt was also fantastic, we informed him our son's name is Luke and he hooked us up with a bunch of restaurant items that have the name Luke on it. I'm bummed that this is our last day in NOLA, I would love to come back here and try out all they have to offer.

I've been to Lüke three times now and the food has always been fantastic but two of the three times the service was uncomfortable. Today I went for breakfast and the waiter seemed to hate his job. He didn't talk much, wasn't very friendly and was slow to fill our cups-- even when empty. Maybe he was tired from Mardi Gras. Who knows? At a place that is not cheap, I would expect better service.

Had res at 6 and got there a little early seated anyway and had the 50 cent oysters very good.  Shrimp and grits yummy as was my sons jaeger something(a veal dish with spaetzel). Veal good and smoky spaetzel excellent.  
Had the best wine ever here, a german Riesling from loose bros. vineyards, absolutely delicious!  And even better had 2 glasses while happy hour 4- per glass, would be happy to pay full price for this wine.
Bread pudding for dessert very good.
Wait staff good, could be a little more attentive.
Prices good.
Ate at NOLA the night after this and although more formal and quieter than Luke, the food was very disappointing, and had a snide douchy waiter.
Paid more at NOLA and didn't even have wine.
Gumbo was fantastic!! One of the best roux's I have ever tasted.

The food here is delicious! Originally came here for Happy Hour since they have oysters for $0.75/each! But we also ordered some food and it was sooo good! So good that we came back twice in our 5 day stay in NOLA, lol. On our first trip to Luke's, I made a reservation even though the restaurant was quite empty when we walked in, but the hostess asked if we had reservations anyway.. and they couldn't find my name, but were nice enough to seat our group of 6. They also don't write down our orders so food that we didn't order came out, but again, nice enough to give it to us on the house... or so we thought. They accidentally put it on the check and we had to make them take it off. Regardless, food is great, service is typical southern hospitality, and the drinks are yummy! 

During our second trip there, the same thing happened with the food, where they brought out food that we didn't order, except we didn't get to keep it this time. But we ordered everything new that we didn't eat the first time. All in all, def would recommend this restaurant.

Come for the happy hour and please get the fried oysters! I started with 1/2 dozen of fried and 1/2 dozen of raw oysters, and I kept ordering for more until I lost count (which I partially blame on the happy hour drinks). 

I'm not sure if I'll ever have the same awesome oyster experience ever again outside of NOLA, which kind of makes me sad, but definitely glad to know where to return next time I visit NOLA again! 

The waiter was phenomenal. He walked me, an oyster noob, thru each and every step and made me feel cared for from the moment I sat down until I left the restaurant. There was not one moment my glass (water as well as alcohol) was empty :)

According to me, a perfect meal always ends with creme brûlée, and so it was. When I visit this place again next time I want the night to go exactly as it did all over again. This place makes me look forward to visit NOLA again, whenever that is!

Came for happy hour- $9 for a dozen oysters, half price cocktails, beer and wine- how can you go wrong.

In our New Orleans weekend this was a happy hour stop before dinner that didn't disappoint!!!! In the future  it will be a dinner stop.
Clean and pleasant atmosphere, tasty food, attentive staff & cold beverages! Will definitely revisit!
Came here for dinner. Had the ​flammenkuchen and fresh gulf drum. Both were very delicious. Kevin and Gary were very good servers.

Had a birthday celebration for a good friend of mine. The staff was absolutely wonderful. I am so picky when it comes to sushi places but I must say this sushi was phenomenal! Loved that it's a BYOB also! We'll be back!
Had take out while traveling. The appetizers and soups were a little salty but very good. The shrimp and grits were salty and very average. We would go back.

I think the fact that we were able to walk in and be seen*on Sunday gets them 2 stars. * so being seen, we waited 60 minutes to get to waiting room, then get seen by vet over additional 45 minutes. Charged triple.  Almost 2 hrs for a simple problem. Avoid.

We stopped by w/o reservation and they said they had nothing available.  Hubby checked Opentable and there was one available. Booked it online, went back and they sat us immediately. Servers Gary and Kevin were great.  The small plates of gnocchi and brussel sprouts were fantastic. Amazing flavors creatively put together. Manager even gave us the recipe for the brussel sprouts. Hubby had prime rib w/creole spices topped w/ crab meat (at servers suggestion).  Fantastic combination.  Highly recommend for sit down or bar experience.  Crowd is more upscale late 30-40's crowd. Nice if you want to get away from the typical town scene.

Go for happy hour! 75c raw oysters, 6 fried oysters for $10 or 12 for $14. Half price wine, beer, well drinks and signature cocktails. It doesn't get much better. Also the place is beautiful and classy, the service was very attentive and the food plain delish. Other than oysters we also ordered the pate which comes out on a board with excellent condiments. It was smooth and rich just like it should be. It was a large portion so be prepared to share with a few people. The rest of the menu items also seemed reasonably priced. Definitely glad I walked the few blocks over from the French quarter.
My service was 5 star. Oil change took 10 minutes. They covered everything and went above and beyond to make the service seamless. Thanks Matthew and Jiffy Lube Team!

We got an appointment, which was the best idea ever. 10mins in the place was out of free tables and for good reason. The food was excellent. 

The roasted beet salad I got was perfect not overwhelmingly sweet, but the juices from the roasted beets made a great addition to the dressing.
The fresh gulf puppy drum was apparently great.

Although I wouldn't get the bread pudding unless you like very sweet deserts.

Had dinner at Luke for the first time over the weekend, and let me tell you it was well worth it! Not only is their happy hour great, but the food is amazing. Elegant and clean environment, with things on the menu ranging from soft shell crab BLTs to ribeye steaks and tuna tartare. What really floored me most was the service. Not only was our waiter attentive and upbeat (thanks Kenny!), but I watched as the manager went around to every table to make them feel welcome. When he made it over to us (Tim is his name by the way), he welcomed us to Luke and to New Orleans! He pointed out his favorites in the menu, and encouraged us to try a bit of everything. We took his recommendation and are glad we did! Best Brussels we had ever tasted! It was nice to see a manager that truly cared about his patrons and his staff. Thanks to Tim, Kenny, and the wonderful team at Luke for a great dinner and experience. We will be back!

Gary was the best, most attentive server i've ever had the pleasure of being served food from! Great suggestions from he and Savannah about what to get including freshly shucked oysters and savory crawfish bisque.

I came here solo on a Friday at 5pm. You can be seated anywhere in the restaurant to get the Happy Hour menu (ie you don't have to sit at the bar). Staff was really friendly and I had happy hour drinks (wine, cocktails and beer all half off) so I had them pour me the most expensive class of bubbly (the chardonnay champagne, $18) is REALLY good. I had a half dozen oysters (50 cents during happy hour!!) and half a dozen baked oysters. This was my first time eating baked oysters and they were SO delicious. The raw oysters were very fresh and absolutely delicious- and huge! It took courage to slurp them all down (although multiple glasses of champagne was helpful). Also, you can make a reso on open table.

New Orleans has excellent cuisines and Luke is no exception.  We don't usually like greens but we devoured their Brussels sprouts dish. The crabmeat remick was delicious. So were our main dishes of shrimp and steak.

This little fancy shmancy place is know for their seafood. It's cute and sweet inside the hotel of a Hilton? I don't remember honestly. Had a very urban feel but white table cloths look. I order some oysters on the half shell. They shucked them great! No prices of shell in my slurpy bites. I got a bunch of P&J and Southern Pearls. Yum yum for people who can really enjoy some fresh good seafood. They have bunches of seafood options. I also got the crispy potatoes. Very good and very crispy. Excellent. One thing I heard from my friends who joined me is that the gumbo is extremely salty. Maybe a little heavy handed with the salt. Or maybe just not our east coast taste. Either way I can't personally vouch since I didn't order or try it. Anyways this please is a bit posh but I have no other remarks!  For the oysters it's worth it!

My husband, son, daughter in law and I had dinner here last night and enjoyed the fine dinning experience. My daughter in law and I had the mussels and were seasoned so nicely that we soped up as much of the sauce we could. My husband had the shrimp and grits and said it was great flavor and balance. My son had the flammenkuchen and said it was really really good, the gravy he wants to learn how to make. Waitstaff was spot on with drinks and service.

Being a seafood lover, this place was very good!! We had the baked P&J oysters. Oysters were large and very flavorful in a herbsaint, persillade crust. We also had the Pâté Of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken Livers. Being a Pate lover, this wasn't the best. But the you can combine it with a variety of toppings to make it taste better. The crawfish bisque was very good. Creamy texture that comes with two crawfish heads stuffed. Remember to eat the stuffing in the crawfish! The Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en Cocotte" was good! I would recommend adding some lump crab in there as well! The Shrimp in the Jar was also good and flavorful! Service was very slowwwwwwwwwww. But he said he was new, so that is probably why.

Everything was amazing! Our first time going, and while it is on the more expensive side, I can't wait until we get the chance to go again. 

Their French 75 champagne drink was very delicious. We started with the spinach and artichoke dip which was filled with lumps of crab too! The toasted sourdough bread it was served with was the perfect compliment. 

My boyfriend ordered the Pecan Roasted Chicken and really enjoyed it. I got the Garganelli which was a bit spiced than expected but really great flavor rise and the noodles were cooked perfectly. We also ordered the crab ravigote which I would highly recommend! Perfect amount of horseradish and the crab was really fresh and delicious.

Oh John Besh how embarrassed you would have been on April 26, 2015 at 9:30am.
