I raved about this place as you can see in my previous reviews I have given it 5 stars each time. So I brought my cousin here for her first time to indulge in the goodness. Mind you we want to Emerial's the night before which was also her first time and the service as usual was bar none.

So I wanted to introduce her to my other favorite chef in Nola's cuisine. 

We walked in and I should have known something was off. The 2 hostess were not friendly especially the one with dark hair, large eyes,  drags her feet when she walks, and rolls her eyes at customers who is disturbing her morning (I asked for her name and was told he didn't know). It was so bad I just watched her even when we got seated and could not believe she was at the front of the house. The trash can behind the check in desk was overflowing and my cousin said that would never happen at Emerial's whom as soon as you take a sip of your water someone swoops in like dark Vader and fills your glass.

Anyway, we got seated after standing there for 18 min, no biggie. Our waiter Nicolas brought us a brunch menu and I said can we also see the breakfast menu since brunch technically starts at 10. It was 9:48 and he looked at his watch and said a unenthusiastic yep and brought the breakfast menu. Then I tell you know lie the first words out of his mouth when he sat the menus down was "So what do you want".. My reaction was like an old school episode of Punked. I said we need a minute.

We ordered a stack of pecan pancakes and shrimp and grits. 

When he brought us our food we being the yelpers we are we took our photos. He then says "Yea girl Instagram my shit". My biggest pet peeve Just because I am black don't assume I talk like a stereotype. I stated actually this is for yelp.

So he walked off, my cousin still mouth on the floor appalled. The pancakes came in a thin stack of seven with about a teaspoon of pecan butter on top. So we asked Nicolas for more butter. He says "You want that exact butter? We said yes and he said "I have to get it from the kitchen. Exactly 15 minutes later he sees that we haven't eaten the pancakes and says I don't know why they haven't brought you any butter I told them too. All this is while he fills the water glasses of the other tables and fills my glass with what's left in his pitcher and never comes back with more, see my pic.

So we then asked a nice guy who was cleaning tables if he could get us some butter and he was back within 5 min. However the pancakes were now cold and so was the butter so it was over. We told Nicolas and he said OK I will take it off the bill and then just brings us our check. He didn't offer to remake them, given us something different or even ask he wanted us gone. My cousin couldn't believe how mad I was and I told her this was more than a let me talk to the manager situation this was full blown Letter to the company situation. 

All in all we split the Shrimp and grits which were delicious and that's it and left hungry. We had to go somewhere else to eat after.

This day was beyond embarrassing to the John Besh name and with the mecca of food in Nola you can't slack on service. Now my new foodie cousin can care less who John Besh is and how amazing I say he is because all she remembers is being treated worse than a waffle House at 2am. 

I hope management reads this and addresses those staff member because this day was beyond any experience I have ever had in a restaurant on its worse day.

Second day in NOLA.  Lunch at Lukes.  I'm a little bias going into this review.  Big John Besh fan.  I have many of his books and use them often.  

We started with a dozen chilled Gulf Shrimp.  Awesome!  I also ordered a half dozen stuffed oysters.  Should have ordered a full dozen.  These were delicious!

I'm a Croque Madame aficionado.  I first fell in love with this sandwich when I went to Bouchon at the Venetian in Las Vegas.  When I saw it on the menu at Luke I knew I had to have one.  Sadly, I found it to be very heavy and doughy.  I ate all the ham which was good.  Sorry John but Thomas wins this round.

The Washington Parish Roasted Chicken was the best dish at the table.  I managed to snag a bite!  My GF the Queen of Reseda got the Crab & Corn Bisque.  I tried some, very good!  She also got the Tabasco Honey Fried Chicken, red beans & rice.  She didn't love it.  Said the chicken was dry.

I would go back in a heartbeat and try other dishes and most definitely get more of those tasty stuffed oysters and Gulf Shrimp!

Came here last night with my boyfriend after an open bar event a few blocks away. We stumbled our way through the CBD and luckily, Luke had a table ready for us (thank god for flash floods and rainstorms keeping the majority of people home). I'm a fan of the hotel/bank decor, but slippery stone floors and a tipsy rain-soaked me was not a good combination. 

We sat at a table and immediately ordered wine and appetizers: the rabbit and duck liver pate and a roast beet salad. My Bellini was great, with the fresh peach really resonating, but Daniel was unsatisfied with his wine (it came in a tumbler like Italian wine... weird). 

The pate was the hit of the night! So smooth and rich and buttery, accompanied with Creole mustard, tiny pickles, and 2 fruit relishes on buttery crisp toast. INCREDIBLE. We literally scraped the cute little glass container out. Restaurant August needs to take a tip on pate from Luke because this was seriously superior.

For an entree we shared the moules and frites. Amazing fries, fresh and hot, and a great creamy buttery garlic broth with the mussels (although a few were shriveled and overcooked). At this point we were happily satiated and thus declined dessert... and still, dinner was only $60! 

I've come before for the oysters and they are great and ESPECIALLY reasonable for happy hour. Their house microbrewed beers are delicious, although the cochon de lait sandwich I tried before was somewhat dry and bland. 

One of my favorite mid-priced spots for a chill delicious dinner. Can't wait to come back.

I admit it probably my fault, Decided at the last minute to play golf , So we decided not to travel far to play golf , Labor Day weekend ( Sunday) .. 
We go to Golden Pheasant- the course must have been under water all summer, the tee boxes are a hot mess , the fairways are a hot mess , the greens were a joke and worst of all they charged us $68 ( sorry first responders they don't give us a discount) At that price I would think the course would have been in a lot better shape .. I guess since they bought the Links they spend all there money on that course..  Avoid playing there it's not worth the money at all ( $30 course at best)
Great meal as always, but wanted to give a special shout out to Gary and Savannah, our servers, who were incredible. Great suggestions, extremely helpful, and very friendly.

I was looking at my Gucci it's about that time. - Big Tymers, Manny Fresh(NOLA rapper - obscure reference)

My stomach confirmed what my Gucci watch told me. It was past lunch and after scoring beads and coconuts at the Zulu parade I was hungry. Internal thought: "Looks like another hyped up John Besch restaurant is along the Rex parade route. You need to be there." For lunch I did all appetizers:

Charbroiled Parmesan Oysters. 5
I'm about to commit NOLA heresy. These oysters are better, than the already amazing oysters at ACME oyster house. Allow me to juxtapose. ACME charbroiled oysters: smokey, buttery, take 30m+ to make because of their popularity. Luke charbroiled oysters: large flavorful, covered in gooey parmesan, fall apart in your mouth, come out in 5 minutes. Ok, it was tough to juxtapose because your comparing a 30 year old whisky to a 45 year old whisky, both will amaze you but if drink enough you can pick up the nuances. 

Escargot. 4
You'll be taken; 0-60, swiftly (flavor wise).* No mistaking the flavor and chewiness when you have escargot and it was great here. It was made in a sort of bulinbaise soup, very unique and had some French bread that came with it.  

By the time I was done I'd pretty much missed the Rex parade on my inaugural NOLA mardi gras trip and although I kind of regret that I can never regret these oysters and escargot, yum. 

Verdict: Recommended but not NOLA requirement

*Paying homage to biggie smalls. No disrespect intended to Junior Mafia clique. No beef or bullets needed here.

All 3 of us had fantastic meals here. The chef made a delicious vegan entree for my wife as nothing on the menu was vegan. The bread pudding in the rear of the photo was good. The smores desert in the front was outstanding!  It was far better than the menu described it. We had excellent service as well and I would highly recommend this restaurant for a classy, yet still affordable night out.

The gentleman behind the bar shucking oysters (Tim and another man who is tall, skinny with a gold tooth) completely made my experience amazing. Knowing I didn't like seafood, Tim introduced my husband and and I to many different types of oysters. He wouldn't give up until He found an oyster I could handle. They both made for great conversation and a great time!  I would definitely recommend sitting at the bar and laughing with these to guys. You won't regret it!
We really just pigged out on the .75c happy hour oysters and 1/2 price drinks. Great value and if we had more time we wanted to try a 'real' meal there. This was our 2nd favorite spot on our visit.

Very expensive and we feel like my wife was taken advantage of at an emotional time. Spent $1100+ in 2 hours for blood work and xrays. They found nothing and our dog is fine. I called to give an opportunity to make things right and they held firm.  Not the customer service experience we wanted.

Overall good experience. The food and service were both pretty good. I loved the environment (causal yet classy), especially the bar's finish. My friend ordered the Croque-monsieur and I the Croque-madame, and both the rosemary potatoes and fries were delicious. From the looks of another table, I would've loved to try the buttermilk fried quail and oysters. The price didn't quite match the quality of the meal, in my opinion, but it was still a decent lunch.
I called yesterday with the measurements for 2 pieces of glass for my nightstands they were done the very next day. They look great! So pleased with the good service and reasonable prices.

Hachi is my favorite sushi restaurant in the area. The restaurant itself is small and intimate. Great place for a cozy romantic date. They have a wide variety of choices and they also do dinner combos. I highly recommend the rock shrimp tempura with spicy miso sauce for an appetizer - it's so good I didn't even have time to take a picture before they were gone. I can't wait to go back and try more.

We came here mainly for the 75 cent happy hour oysters! I made reservations before we arrived in NOLA specifically during the HH time. We found that we didn't really need them since we came on a Wednesday and it looked like they weren't too busy. 

Service was great - our waitress was extremely friendly and attentive. We ordered two dozen oysters and shared the jumbo louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" which had roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausage. The oysters were delicious - I had gone through about 6-7 until I saw what I thought was a red vein on my oyster... yikes, it wasn't that at all. I picked it up with my tiny fork and I couldn't believe what I was seeing... the little thing wrapped itself around my fork. It was a tiny little red worm. I found another one on another oyster. That was it for me, no more oysters for the rest of the night. I called over our waitress who then brought over the manager. He informed us that their oysters come fresh and that these worms are naturally found around the oyster shells, but not normally when they are plated at a restaurant. I asked if I could eat them since I could potentially have eaten one already without knowing and he said no. This worried me at the time. But I did some research online and it seems as though these worms are probably harmless. Nobody really wants to see a worm during their meal, c'mon... honestly, I just think the oysters weren't properly shucked and thoroughly cleaned before plating. 

I appreciated the offer for a new set of oysters. I declined, but my boyfriend agreed (not sure how or why) but was super careful eating them. They also gave us fried oysters on the house. The appetizer & two dozen oysters were taken off the bill so we only had to pay for the shrimp entree we had ordered. 

I guess that's the risk when eating anything raw.. lol. No more oysters for me, I'm sorry.

Nice place to pop into for "real" coffee. Love the cappuccino, espresso is very nice! Also had a few muffins from here, nice and fresh.

It's a small place so only really standing room and to tight to visit with someone. There are some little table outside during summer months.

Decided to stop in to have appetizers and drinks, little did we know we walked into a great happy hour. The service was great and everyone was very friendly.  Our servers were very informative and personable. The Ruston Smash cocktail was amazing. My husband really enjoyed the door#three cocktail. The best part was happy hour included half off cocktails, beers, wines and 75 cents raw oysters and 1.25 fried oysters. You can't beat that! The stuffed P&J oysters were so delicious. We didn't try the Brussels sprouts appetizer, but it seem to be very popular as most of the other tables were ordering it. We were sitting next to this gentleman that was from out of town and he stated "I waited two years to come back here to eat."  He couldn't stop talking about how much he loved it. The ambience and service over all was top notch. Would highly recommend and will definitely be going back.
Raw oysters during happy hour are a great deal and delicious. I've dined at the bar and at the table and both places have great service.

This is possibly my new most favorite restaurant in the world.  Our waiter was awesome!  He was very attentive but not overly, and very nice with good suggestions.  And I thought the food was delicious!  The beet salad with blue cheese was perfect.  I had the crab raviolis, and they were light and lovely and perfectly cooked.  But, I could go and just have the banana profiteroles.  And I don't even like bananas!  You have to try them!  Fabulous coffee too.  I like that this place has really good food and good service, but is casual and not at all stuffy.  I would go to New Orleans again today just to eat at Luke.  We had a fantastic dinner with never a bad note.

Luke was marvelous.  From the very friendly hostesses to the excellent severs, all service was impeccable.  The stuffed oysters and gumbo were both fantastic.  The wine list was substantial and well priced.  It was clear that manager Tanya was very present and ensuring that every guest had a marvelous experience.  Definitely recommend Luke for a memorable night out in New Orleans.

We had an amazing Christmas dinner here. The staff was attentive, warm and welcoming, and the food was delicious.  Our dinner was actually during the infamous happy hour, which they also continued on Christmas day. This happy hour does not disappoint - their oysters and fried oysters (that sauce!) were delicious, and half-off all drinks on the menu! We were there for about 3.5 hours, and at no point felt rushed during our dinner.  I had the Christmas menu and my husband had the gumbo and the shrimp and grits - think his dishes were a bit better.  Definitely save room for dessert - the bread pudding is sublime.

Best French 75 anywhere! Pretty good fried oysters too! Not a huge fan of the entree menu but they have amazing kids meals that are extra fresh and full of delicious veggies. My 4 year old approves. Always had great service as well except for once and they have happy hour 7 days a week!

This restaurant appeared linked to the hotel I was staying at.  The first night we went it was great.  Our server was attentive and the food was great.  I ordered the shrimp and grits and they were amazing grits!
The second time, however, could have used some work.  We were told that they were reservation only for the next two hours and that we needed to grab a seat at the clearly full bar.  We waiting for seating at the bar while eyeing all of the visibly open tables that were "reserved."  A couple walked in behind us and we could see them trying to find a spot at the bar also...but were eventually seated.  We ate our entire meal at the bar while some of the "reserved" tables never had anyone seated at them.
Now, maybe people were late to the "reservations" but if they were THAT late it would probably be in the financial interest of the restaurant to seat people who are there and paying..at what point is a reservation forfeited?
It just seemed like an excuse to not be seated and it wasn't warm or welcoming in any manner.

Highly recommend this restaurant! 

I went there for their happy hours 3-6 pm. 
Drink - 4/5 it was too sweet for me
Raw oysters - 5/5 their oysters and cocktails sauces are amazing. We got 2 dozens
Fried Oysters - 5/5 you must try this even if you are not a big fan of oysters. You can't really smell or taste the oysters which mostly turned people off
Services - our server is very attentive and fast

Totally will visit again next time I go back to New Orleans
Very nice atmosphere, the food was really good as well! We had the shrimp and grits which was great and I highly recommend and also the swordfish was good. All in all amazing place!

I have a love-hate relationship with Luke.  (Sorry, I don't know how to put umlau's in my reviews so you'll just have to suffer through my referring it Luke.)

The interior is gorgeous, with the high-ceilings and the classic tile floors.  I love those little tiles--early 20th century architecture is my favorite.  The place has very classic Arts and Crafts vibe to it.

They do a great job with lunch sandwiches.  The burger is perhaps the best in the city.  Basic bacon cheeseburger, thick but not too thick.  All the ingredients well balanced, juicy, done perfectly and presented on a cutting board.  The fries were nice and salty, shoestrings in a big conical cup.

The biggest problem with this place is that although the food is good, more often than not the entrees and appetizers come out completely different from how you would expect them to.  Maybe the menu is just very poorly descriptive, or it's the slipping in of subtle words (in French).  The waiters may be able to help, but seriously, why give me a written menu when you have to explain every dish?

I've literally ordered a salad and a chicken entree and had the salad come out with chicken/prosciutto in it (surprise!) and then the entree had a salad with ham sitting on top of it!  They could have sold me on the oyster appetizer instead and I would have been as happy as an oyster--er, clam.

Anyway, you know what you are getting with sandwiches and burgers here, so I stick to those.  4-stars there.

I personally have not had breakfast here, though a good friend was unimpressed--let's just say look at the menu (prices) before you commit to one.

We had a reservation, which I would recommend because it's quite the cozy inside, and we were seated right away.  The Brussels sprouts we ordered as an appetizer was the highlight of the meal.  They were sweet, spicy, crispy on the outside, and delicious! 

My fried oyster, avocado and bacon salad was served with a buttermilk dressing. The bacon was what I can only assume is Southern style, more like side meat than strips of bacon. Not really my style, don't get me wrong because this girl loves bacon, I just prefer it doesn't look like it could wedge itself into my coronaries.  The fried oysters were smooth, savory, and fulfilling. My husband's burger was delicious. It seemed to be a popular item on the menu. It's huge and really should be shared with another person.  

All in all the food was great, although the service was lackluster but that may be because our first night in NOLA we were spoiled at Emeril's.  I also felt like we waited a long time between meal courses. No free bread to start?  Lame.  Not the best experience I had in NOLA, the competition is fierce.

I used Seven Oaks for my 2 dogs.  I really liked it during my first visit; however, my following visits I had mixed experiences.  I could rarely see the same vet when I needed too and so often had to wait if I wanted to have proper continuity of care for my pup.  The one doctor that I truly felt comfortable with was Dr. Kho.  She was very nice and knowledgable.  She did take the time to talk to me about what was going on with my dog when he was going through problems with his liver.  

I do commend them for caring for my pup exceptionally when he had to have a liver ultrasound/biopsy.  When I went to pick him up I was expecting him to be a bit more scared.  But the vet tech had him happy and excited.  She was giving him treats and he seemed super excited.  

My biggest complaint was with the office staff.  They attempted to charge me for multiple items (food and medication) that my dog did not even need.  He was going though procedures to diagnose an issue; however, he was not diagnosed yet and the staff was checking me out and trying to charge me for medication and prescription food as if he had already been diagnosed with the condition.  When I had them ask the doctor if he needed it, she stated no.  And after the testing had been performed - he did not need it.  This type of situation happened on more than one occasion.  Additionally, it was just very impersonal.  The staff constantly seemed as though they were in a rush and stressed out.  

Ultimately I switched vets and am much happier with my current vet.

The oysters were so fresh almost like they caught them at the restaurant! We ordered matzo ball soup and it was just as good as my bubbe makes ;) me and my best friend addison got matching salads and im so deadass that was the sickest salad ever it was so fresh and delicious we actually ate it all! (addison has an eating disorder) i will dream about that salad for the rest of my life!
Definitely over rated. Waited well over an hour for dry duck.  Tried NoLa a couple days ago and their duck was several orders of magnitude better.

Everything on this menu was great. Even the cheeseburger! Fantastic service! 
The shrimp etouffe is best with both breaded and grilled shrimp as recommended by our server.

Wow! I went to Luke with two friends for dinner last Thursday and ate one of the best meals I've ever had. EV. . . ER. The service (thanks Richy Rich!) was amazing. And the food was spectacular. 

We started with the Brussels Sprout Salad. The brussels sprouts were cooked perfectly and tossed with little hot peppers in this sweet/spicy Asian type sauce. And some of the outer leaves had fallen off the sprouts and were slightly crispy. Every single one of us expressed an uncontrollable moan of pleasure at the first bite. There may or may not have been a fork fight immediately following that as we all tried to bogart as much of the salad as possible.

Then one of my friends and I were trying to decide between the same two dishes, so they brought each of us a half portion of the two dishes. The first was the shrimp etouffee a la Harry (shrimp etouffee with fried shrimp on top). If I could only have one dish for the rest of my life, this would be it. When you think fried shrimp, don't think butterflied and breaded, think flash fry. It added another element of taste and texture to an already perfect dish. Phenomenal.

The other dish was the fried catfish topped with crawfish. I will preface this with the admission that I'm not a catfish person. I don't typically enjoy it, so I don't get it. However, the description looked so good that I was tempted. And I'm glad I tried it. I'd order it again (if they were out of the shrimp etouffee :)). It was really tasty. So if you're not a catfish person, definitely try it, it might change your mind. 

Our other friend ordered a hamburger. Seriously. A hamburger. There's no accounting for taste, but he said that it was the best burger he'd ever eaten. So there you have it. If you want to go to a renowned restaurant and order a burger, know that at least it'll be a darn good one. But if I were you, I'd go with the shrimp. You won't know what hit you.

I really enjoyed Luke. This was right near our airBnB and thought it would be worth trying, and I am so glad we went. The oysters were fantastic (but that can be said about most oysters in NOLA) and the gumbo and crawfish bisque were also wonderful.

The atmosphere is very nice. We walked in when it was still quiet and within 15 minutes i it really picked up and was full by the time we left. I suggest reservations. 

Away from the French Quarter, but worth the 10 minute walk.

Listen: Luke is fantastic. If you want great oysters, cocktails, and service this is the place to go. It's never as crowded as Acme and is truly awesome. Check out daily happy hour from 3-6 for .75 oysters and half price cocktails! I love this place.
Out of the 100+ shrimp and grits I've tried, Luke's is best. It's the only one I crave.

We had to find a restaurant last secound because another restaurant we had reservations at was closed due to Covid. Luke's was the best food and service we had the entire weekend get-a-way! We drove in from houston and came right in for dinner our first night. We talked about the food the entire weekend because it was that good!

Amazing happy hour deals and the best oysters we had on our trip!  75 cent oysters during weekday happy hours 3-6 pm = to die for.

The bartenders were incredibly friendly and we had a great time chatting and having some happy hour drinks with our oysters.  It helped that our drinks were half off during happy hour as well!

I love oysters, and not the skrimpy mini ones that are "more sweet" and are "fuller flavor"...I like me some big ass oysters. You'd think a place like Luke, with its Parisian vibe would be trying to sell me on some babies, but they're not pushing the petites at all. 

You listen to mama Morgan and you go in during Happy Hour, 3-6, errday (last time I checked) and get you some big ass oysters. They don't call them that, cause that's how the businesses in the Quarter try to reel you in, but they are!...They're big and I love them AND they're 50 cents. Yes, 50 cents each, so splurge on a dozen or two. Of course, if you don't like oysters, just take me and I'll help you out. I have been to Luke a few times, and just recently discovered the humongoness of their oysters, only rivaled by Cooter Brown's, thought they may be a little cleaner here at Luke. Can you tell I like oysters?...

I love the vibe at Luke with a long bar that's great for dining at as a couple. If you are a people watcher, then request the front. If you enjoy your privacy, the back is perfect and intimate. I recently sat in the back here with my boyfriend's family. I must say I experienced some serious entree envy (which duh, don't order an appetizer then) when my boyfriend's dad ordered the HUGE burger and fries, and I went with the Crab Maison. I do have qualms with the price tag on this petite Crab Maison when comparing with similar restaurants, and it wasn't as flavorful as I had hoped though the temperature was perfect and the bread that it came with was a nice crunchy texture to go with the meat. Size-wise though this IS an appetizer so be forewarned this is not an entree substitute which of those who got entrees are rightfully sized.  To fill my belly, I ordered a side of their jalapeño grits though it wasn't specifically on the menu (thanks!), and they are damn good. Perfectly creamy with a spicy kick. I will definitely have to try their shrimp and grits some time that they cook with these grits. 

Our waitress was attentive without being overbearing, and handled a neighboring situation of ornery guests very well without missing a beat with us. 

I'll definitely be back for Happy Hour at the bar sometime very soon!

I dont understand what happened...

Ive been here three times since i found it less than a year ago.  First time i got the burger and it was amazing. fresh, perfectly cooked and still piping hot when i got home to eat it (less than 5 minutes away) i couldnt believe i had found a decent fast food place, especially a sonic which are usually terrible.

The last two times ive been it has tasted like the burger meat was sitting out for like 30 minutes. it is not hot at all and about to throw away most of it. all of the toppings are soggy and smashed in and clearly they made this like an hour before i ordered it. its absolutely disgusting.

i just dont understand how this could happen... i thought i had found a hidden gem fast food place in St louis but now it just tastes like the rest. luke warm and crappy.  the meat is burnt on the edges.  clearly there are two types of sonic workers. ones that care and ones that dgaf.

this is so sad to me. i just want a freshly made burger that is still hot and fresh when i eat it... i feel so badly for the terrible workers that made me dinner tonight because they deserve to be fired and probably/hopefully will soon.

my chicken sandwich is still hot. why is the burger not still hot.

side note: the chicken sandwich is disgusting. its exactly like a dollar menu item from mcdonalds... SMFH. not eating it bc im afraid ill get sick.

I was there on Aug. 20th.  What a crock.   I waited 18 minutes in the drive thru.  When I finally got there, the person said, " Were really busy.  People arent patient."  Ummm ok.  Why are you telling me this? 

Then I dipped the extremely hard bread into the COLD french onion soup.  I was so disappointed.  I called and talked to the manager on duty and he said, " Its always at pot temperature.  theres no way its cold"  I turned around in the parking lot and took it in.  He said, " I see some missing.  You ate it".   By that time, I had really had enough of his attitude.  I wont' be back  Someone else can enjoy your cold soup, crappy attitudes and long waits.

My wife made reservations at Luke's for my birthday evening.  It was Saturday evening and the place was full. 
Tip: always come here with reservations.  The place does get full very quickly.
We arrived on time and got our seat for 2. They greeted us with champagne glasses on the house for my birthday. What a great way to welcome. We ordered stuffed oysters and rabbit pate plate. Oysters were mind blowing. Best I have had ever. Pate just nailed it. The food presentation and quantity both hit the spot. We got full with just 2 apps. And decided to go directly to desserts. They had limited option so we decided to skip anything sweet to cut calories. But. To our surprise they got us bread pudding with ice cream and a small chocolate wishing "Happy Birthday ". Really neat gesture. Completely unexpected. 
Overall, we had a great time and enjoyed amazing food and service. Ambience of the place is classy so make sure to dress up.

Although the food was truly exceptional at Luke, I must say what made both our two evenings at this restaurant was our server David. Truly, should you come to this restaurant (and you really, really should!), get David as your server! He has the perfect recommendations on food to try (our first time in New Orleans, so we needed to narrow down all the tantalizing delicacies), and is quite possibly the kindest and sweetest person I have ever met! Not to mention the perfect service on top of all that! Should you wish to have some amazing food to accompany this superior service, I would highly recommend the boudin balls, the fresh oysters, the shrimp and jalapeño grits, the fresh fish...if your mouth isn't watering yet, it should be! All of the food at Luke was delicious. A must-go when visiting New Orleans!

Smalls Tea is your new favorite place to grab a piping-hot cup of herbal tea.  

Like Hao said, Smalls is not completely finished and is in a soft opening but still serves high quality tea. I stopped in because I had to see it and I am a mad man for a good cup of tea. 

The space is small(s) and narrow but super warm and inviting. You might get a cavity cause it's just about the sweetest little shop you will ever see. It used to be an ally way but back in the day (I have no idea when) they covered it to add another store-front. And thank goodness they did! It's all the room Smalls Tea and Coffee needs to spread the love on Cherokee Street! The design style is also really cute. The owner painted her walls the self and you can see the huge potential in the unique space. 

Lisa (the owner) herself will probably be the one helping you. This is a good thing because she is not only one of the most caring people you will meet, but she is also a wizard at making tea (witch sounds evil so I'm sticking with wizard). 

When I stopped by she was serving ginger and turmeric tea. At first I was a little hesitant because I'm not well versed in herbal tea and I've never had this kind before. Also, I'm naturally resistant towards ginger in food because I think it ruins it sometimes. I went for it anyways and so glad that I did. 

First off, she ground the fresh herbs for it in front of me. That's right, she pulled out the ginger root and turmeric and shaved it off! I could see the juices with my own eyes and smell how fresh it all was. She then boiled it in her magic cauldron and in to time it was done. At first sip I thought (this is different) but after a few more I was addicted. I'm not kidding you, I crave this tea. This is one of the best cups of tea I have ever had. It was the perfect amount of spicy and sweet (I added a little bit of honey). Like, I clutched that cup to the very last drop. I wish I had easier access to this tea. I want to drink it ALL. THE. TIME. 

I don't know if she had coffee set up yet but I know she plans on serving it. 

If you are on Cherokee Street, you must stop by and give this new and adorable tea shop a chance.

This was the fanciest place we've been to so far in NOLA. Prices were a little high but well worth it. For starters, we ordered the raw oysters & the stuffed oysters which were stuffed with shrimp & crabmeat. For entree we ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp to share. For dessert we ordered the bread pudding with pecans & vanilla ice cream. Everything was delicious & fresh. Would go again for oysters.
Excellent shrimp and grits.  The best crab omelet I've ever had!!!  Awesome service...can't wait to go back there again!

Excellent sushi and great staff. Unique rolls along with other delicious dishes. One of my favorites. 
Manhattan MonkeyPad Thai

Brussels sprouts and bread pudding ... Is how you stole my heart! 

Here's a few Luke tips to keep in mind before you arrive: 

1.  You need a reservation (at least on the weekends). The hostesses were not taking any walk ins. 

2.  The menu changes often, so do g come with your heart set on anything... Even their menu online is boy current. 

3. Try to get a table in the back room so you can watch the kitchen work their magic. 

What I ordered: 

1. Old fashioned: 4 stars because they use the good luxardo cherries. Beware they use Jim Beam if you don't ask for something else. 

2. Crispy Brussels sprouts with cheese and awesome sauce: 5 stars hands down best sprouts I've ever had 

3. Luke salad: 4 stars: tip you can order 1/2 sizes on the salads. Awesome house made buttermilk dressing and yummy yellow beets!

4. Squash crepes: 2 stars ... I sent it back it was not flavors I enjoyed.. Heavy sage and thanksgiving stuffing taste. 

5. Jalapeño cheesy grits: 5 stars ... Best grits ever! 

6. Pecan bread pudding: 5 stars. We were drooling over this in the window do the chef sent one out for us... It was as amazing as it looked. 

Despite sending my entree back, we had a great meal. The service and food was spot on. Thanks Luke!

Maybe it was the day of the week we went (Monday) or maybe the time of day (12ish), but the place wasn't anything special, just blah.  The waiters could smile a little more, but service was okay.  I got the croque madame, hubby got some ham? roast beef? sandwich, and wanted to get our little one mac & cheese - but they were out of cheddar???!...so a basic grilled cheese was out too...Is this a serious restaurant?  The ham was a bit salty so overwhelmed both our meals, and I'm not so sure the bread was fresh.  First impressions count, so won't be coming here again.

Weekday lunch, near the French Quarter. Outstanding food and service!  Don't miss this place when you come to NOLA.  Amazing brussel sprout recipe. Great oysters.  Shrimp and grits is heavy on the cheese, FYI. LOTS of great flavors here! Check it out.

FINALLY got a chance to try this Yelp icon! I can absolutely say it was worth the wait!! The dining room is split into two rooms separated by the Hilton Hotel Entryway. Even though there are a number of tables, make a reservation by calling or on Open Table. There is not a link on Yelp, so we were lucky to get worked in by the very friendly understanding host. 
The restaurant was beautifully decorated in New Orleans Coastal style decor and the ambiance was lively yet refined. 
The small details around the restaurant really add charm. Like the fresh seafood bar and the open kitchen views. 
So appearance was beautiful and service was too notch, but let's talk about food!
For an app we ordered the Blue Crab Gratin, a suggestion from our server. It was the perfect suggestion, we almost ate the whole thing!
Dinner didn't fall short of perfect! We ordered the Gulf Puppy Drum blackened w a side salad the Fried Oyster Salad with homemade fries. That side I will get the Drum next visit, I'm still dreaming about it lol. 
If you want a light meal, the Roasted Beet Salad was fine! 

I recommend everything we ordered!!!

Had one of the best meals I've ever had last night! Inventive and really tasty food, fantastic service! Kevin and Julian, our service staff, really made our night complete! Thank you for a wonderful dinner! We can't wait to return!
Clean, slightly upscale atmosphere w jazz softly playing in the background. Went for Saturday brunch and had the crab omelette, which was very good. Attentive, friendly staff. Would come again.

This company is horrible. DO NOT USE. They came out to look at my heater that wasn't working and after a few mins tried to tell me I needed a new system instead of working on it to fix the problem. When I gave push back on spending 4K on a new heater the man told me his boss would call me. His boss told me on a Saturday that he would send someone out Monday to look at the burners. Well Monday came and went no one showed up or even called to this day. Glad I was able to fix the problems without any money on my own and not have my 3 month on and 3 year old in a freezing house because  they don't operate an honest business. Stay away !!!

You need to change your policy.  I order and revived a t-shirt from your outlet.  Days later the outlet price was reduced, but you wouldn't give me a credit for the difference...stating we can give credits for outlet items.  So I order a new one and returned the old one (it was worn).  Thanks for the stupid hassle...NOT!  I hope you lost money by inconveniencing me!
Not sure what the hype is. QDOBA has better chicken, better chips, and better queso. The one.star earned is for.their.customer.service. its the only great thing about chipoltle.

This place was fantastic! Went with my husband and our 7 yr old son and we all enjoyed our meal. Service was great and food was delicious. The fried oysters were cooked to perfection. It says casual but you definitely want to dress up a bit to get the true feeling of dining at Luke's. A must try!

Luke is a gem and a must visit for Foodies traveling to Nola.   The Oysters are always plump and tasty.   If you're adventurous,  then you have to get the rabbit patté.  It's to die for. 

Author David Moon 
Books on Amazon 
Zomosapiens
Scales of Justice 
The Wife's Wicked Weekend
Service and food were both divine! Fresh oysters, blue crab au gratin and the tartare were a few of the choices we had for lunch. I will be back!

The best experience I've had while in New Orleans. Will be coming back for dinner and probably breakfast too before I leave. Ordered the Brussels sprouts and oysters . Asked for a champagne pairing and it was just wonderful .

Savannah was our server tonight. She was gracious, professional and knowledgeable. Gary gave us the excellent recommendation for the bread pudding. Best I've ever had!! We are in town for a conference and fell upon this restaurant. I had the fried oyster salad and it was AMAZING!! I highly recommend!

We stayed at the Hilton that is connected to Luke's and we stopped in to have a quick drink before our dinner reservation at another restaurant. Their Happy Hour is FANTASTIC!!! 1/2 select drinks and bottles of wine and 50 cent oysters and these oysters were HUGE!!! We ended up having a couple dozen raw oysters and their Baked Jalapeno Cheesy Grits. We enjoyed Luke's so much that we came here everyday on our trip for Happy Hour. Get the Jalapeno Cheesy Grits...you won't be disappointed!!

Members beware: my wife and I had memberships on autopay which was no problem until her card was compromised. So we gave Retro the new card number...except they didn't bother to update it. So now with two months of harassment by ABC Billing  (Retro's billing vendor), a company who refuse to identify themselves as such when asking for personally identifiable information, it's still not resolved, despite calls back to them and to this Retro franchise.  Retro, consider this the end of my membership.

Just finished and the course was in nice shape. It has a problem with drainage so you will run into free standing water on a few holes. Course is open in the being and tightens up in the back. If your hitting the driver straight you will be rewarded. Your 3 wood will be your freind on the back 9. The course does need to replace its cart paths to save the rough. Come the dog days of summer you will have a lot of burned up grass and difficult conditions.  For now, the course is in good shape and very playable. I enjoyed the round and give this place a solid 3.5

I came here with a group of 5 people for dinner on a Saturday night.  This is my favorite restaurant to get oysters in New Orleans.  They also have fresh and great tasting seafood in general.  They have a great happy hour (3pm-6pm) where they have 75 cent oysters and half off drinks.  We ordered the small seafood platter (shrimp, clams, mussels, oysters, tuna tartare), hot buttered crawfish bread, stuffed P & J oysters (stuffed with shrimp and crab), fried oyster and bacon salad, and brussel sprouts side.  All the dishes were delicious.  My favorite dish was the stuffed P&J oysters.  Their gulf oysters were enormous and very juicy.  Service was excellent, very attentive and fast.  Our waiter was so nice and gave us champagne and Brendan's bread pudding dessert on the house since it was my bachelorette weekend.  If I ever return to New Orleans, I'll definitely be back!

Had a three course meal here. The baked oysters were my favorite appetizer. I hate the steak cooked rare as an entree and the dark chocolate cake for dessert. I enjoyed the meal here, was not too loud and our waitress, Samantha, was very kind and helpful. Great place to go out on date or have dinner with friends.

I'm originally from the south - so my thoughts when I moved to Philly were 'what is this water ice business?' The name sounds unappetizing but far, far from it. 

Every flavor is amazing. Black cherry, banana, mango, peach, the list goes on. Rita's water ice is great on it's own, but getting it as a gelato was what turned me into a psychotic, obsessive water ice fiend. I'm sure a native who grew up with this - you lucky jerk! - will find this funny to read, but now I have a whole new reason to enjoy summer. I'm pissed every time I drive past this closed stand during the winter.

My oldest son Jack and I we're on our way to Texas from North Carolina and had an overnight stay in New Orleans. We needed someplace where he could find a burger because he's a basic eater and I could find some complexed tasty foods. This was a fantastic place. I have no complaints. But because of Covid the quarter is extremely barren and boring. 
I'm ready for things to get back to normal.

I am very upset. We agreed this morning to have a liver ultrasound done on our dog . The vet told us that if he found a mass he would do a FNA . I was under great duress all day but thought at least by the end of the day we would have answers. Well when we go in the vet told us he found several masses but did not do the FNA because he was afraid the dog would bleed internally. That was  never  even mentioned to us as a remote possibility. I cannot tolerate a professional  not telling all the possibilities before getting someone to get a test. All I know now is that he has several masses but what they are benign or malignent is still a mystery! Not happy all of this should have been told to us at the beginning. If he had run into an unforeseen complication during the ultrasound that made him change his mind about the FNA then he should have called us told us of his concern not make us wait until we went to pick the dog up and find out he found masses but no definitive answer!

Yes people, believe the hype! This place is legit delicious, fresh and for real. This was a bit of a drive to Chalfont, but well worth it. I went for lunch with my sister on a Friday. We both wanted sushi but not your typical suburban half price stuff, but the real goods you typically find at a higher end center city sushi place. Here the atmosphere is very chic, cool and modern. But it's the fish that's the real hands down winner. The service was quick and very attentive. We ordered several dishes to share. The stand out was the poke, and the sashimi lunch special. The raw fish was sublime! It was so fresh and tasty, almost like they just caught it for us. The poke sauce was spicy, and super flavorful. This place is a special little oasis in a suburban desert of half price sushi. I just wish it wasn't so far away!
I see why they call it Luke's..... everything was LUKE WARM. Waste of money and time. Food tasted like it was cooked 2 days ago. I could of made a better breakfast with 1 arm tied behind my back.

We had the coffee, grillade & grits ($15) and shrimp & grits ($24, plus I added crabmeat for $12). Matt J. was our server  for breakfast and he was outstanding! The food was simply amazing. So fresh, flavorful and richly seasoned. The best seafood in town!

The experience left such a great impression that... We returned at happy hour (3-6pm) that same afternoon. Wow! Great choice! We started with Ugni Blanc Champagne, French 75 and the St. Charles Streetcar. Their handcrafted cocktails were absolutely amazing and at half off (happy hour) they were even better! Also, their shucked oysters on the half shell were only $0.50 each. We literally ordered 48 oysters (4 dozen). We also enjoyed their flamenkuche (quite unique), which includes onion tartar, bacon and cheese on a cracker crust. 

The whole experience was outstanding because of the food, drinks and exceptional service by Richie Rich. We were pleasantly surprised that they honored happy hour prices restaurant-wide! We sat in the section with Richie Rich (Rich Whatley), who was so knowledgeable about their menu. He even recommended great combinations of food and drink to enhance our experience. Also, Richie had great recommendations for things to do in- and around the local area. Top level service, with a smile. When I return, I'll ALWAYS ask to be seated with Richie Rich. His high level of service sets the example for others to follow. Kudos to Lüke!
One of the best sushi restaurants around. We ordered the spicy tuna roll, tempura and california roll and were amazed how fresh everything tasted. We will be back!!

Cool looking place and good staff but the food was just okay. I went for lunch so I assume it was a smaller menu option. I got the burger and shared the brussel sprouts and both were presented well but like I said earlier it's was just okay.

I can't really recommend that you come here anymore.  I've eaten here 20 or more times over the past dozen years and they have no idea where they're going right now.  They're suffering from an identity crisis and now it's just corporate tourist food.  I would just move on.  I would give them 1 star after last nights meal if it were for all the good memories I've had.  The past few years have been hit and miss but last night I just wanted my money back.

We showed up for an overpriced and terribly executed Reveillon dinner.  The shrimp remoulade salad was way too spicy (not that it should even be a little spicy).  The weird turtle soup was vastly over seasoned.  The hangar steak was blue, raw.  I did love the demi-glace and the stuffing, although dry, was delicious.  The finish was an eggnog pot-de-creme that had gelatin!  OMG.  Really, you don't know how to make a creme?  The texture was like jello.  Awful.  It was a little too sweet with the figs and crumble too, by the way,

The service wasn't brilliant.  In fact was the worst I've had here.  The bread service is embarrassing.  It's Sysco par-baked garbage.  Inedible and beneath them.  It kinda shows how little they understand their own restaurant concept.  They've ruined the menu.  It's confused and without direction.  You can't even get the classic cocktails you used to get on the happy hour menu.  You can't have a Sazarac?  Really?  It's just Sazarac Rye!  I used to order one here.  It's New Orleans.  

I'm starting to really have my doubts about this restaurant group.

This was my first taste of New Orleans. I visited Luke on a Tuesday night with two others. We had a reservation at 7pm and when we arrived waited just a few minutes to be seated. Our servers were Kevin and Kyle. I was encouraged to order a mint julep by my dining companions, which was difficult to enjoy because it was an insanely heavy pour. We ordered a dozen raw oysters for the table to start. For my entree I enjoyed the Louisiana blue crab cavatelli, which was spectacular. I was starving and I could only wish there was more of it. My companions had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" and one of the fresh fish of the day, both were satisfied. Everything was very tasty and our servers were attentive.

Wow this food was amazing. I had never been before, but my friend works at Pizza Domenica and gets 50% off, so we decided to all go and indulge. They were very understanding when I got there on time and my friends showed up about half an hour late bc my friend was picking up her sister from the airport and the airport was a disaster. Thankfully the restaurant wasn't too packed and they were very understanding. I asked if they wanted to reseat us and our server said no worries and brought me bread and butter :) I'm not sure if her name was Kristin or Kristian but she was amazing. Both our servers, the other was David, were so thoughtful and helpful! Everyone was joking around as I waited for my friends and I got started on a drink. I got the Belle on the Bayou. It was very strong and spicy (tequila, jalapeño, blueberry, and basil) and delicious. Then we got the Wild Mushroom Flatbread (fried kale, charred onion, pesto, fontina cheese) which was absolutely amazing. We shared one and then I got a second one as my meal. I sometimes eat seafood, but I didn't really feel like it that day. I also got the delicious house made fries  with aioli. My friends got the muscles, bbq shrimp, stuffed oysters, pate, and corn and crab bisque. We had so much food and had to bring some home. Seems like the bbq shrimp was a favorite, as well as the flatbread. The flatbread had so much flavor and the leftovers were good cold the next day as well :) I would definitely love to eat that flatbread again!

We went here right at 3pm on a Thursday for happy hour. All drinks were half off and oysters were half off. I believe this lasts until 6pm. Sit at the oyster bar and you'll get to see just how many oysters they go thru. They said they'll go thru 30-40 dozen a day. The oysters were delicious but be careful with the horseradish...you'll feel like your head is on fire if you pile on too much. Save room for the bread pudding because it is unbelievable.

We had a lovely dinner here to celebrate my friend's brachelorette party. We all enjoyed the meal and were so very satisfied afterward. 

What I love:
1. Super friendly server who is very attentive
2. Pate of rabbit and chicken livers: yum yum yum...especially the watermelon pickles
3. Crawfish Bisque: very flavorful and rich
4. Rabbit stew with pasta: I loved it so much! 

What I didn't like so much:
1. Flamenküche: not so much to my taste but my other friends enjoyed it very much

Tips: 
1. Definitely make reservation in advance
2. Dinner express menu is such a good deal. It comes with a cup of soup and a dessert both of which you can select from their regular menu.

I had this restaurant scouted out before we even visited NOLA. We made reservations our last night in town, after a week of amazing eats. 

   The restaurant its self had a very classy modern euro modern feel, upscale. 

    The service was stellar. We had 2 servers, both men. There personalities were great. The one gentleman was such a character.

   Our food was good. The cocktails were very nice. I will say, there large raw platter was a bit overpriced and I'm not one to complain about price. I think it was 10'raw oysters, a baby food sized jar (literally) of ahi tartar and another of mixed crab, for the price of $52, for an appetizer. It was. It that impressive, just to be honest. I would skip it. 

    
 I also ordered the crab & corn bisque. It was great. The seafood gumbo was nothing to write home about. 

   Our 4 entrees were all very good. My dessert was okay. The pastry was a bit on the dry side and lackluster. The cream cheese ice that accompanied it, was so good.

On a business trip to New Orleans, a co-worker, native to the area, recommended this restaurant.
The service was exceptional; Brian and Chi offered prompt attention and quality menu suggestions. The food was terrific: matzo ball soup; mussels and French fries; crawfish étouffée; fresh bread. For dessert, the house bread pudding was to die for.
To enhance the experience, we sat right next to the glassed in kitchen area; we voyeuristically witnessed chefs preparing fantastic cuisine all throughout the evening. Very cool!!!

First off before this is like to say the vets were great. However, Watch out for the scam system they don't alert you about. Went in around 5pm and they close / switch over to pet urgent care at 6pm. Vet said they needed blood work and X-rays which was fine. We knew already what my animal came down with but they have a process I u det stand that. So at about 6:15pm they come back with results and like we knew my animal needed surgery. Money was tight so I asked how much EVERYTHING bottom line would be and was told all in all with everything it will be around $2,500. Final bill was almost $2,800. I paid it all off when I picked my animal up. Now 5 months later I have bill collectors calling for them wanting $800.... I called and come to find out they "change systems" at 6pm. So I have an outstanding balance of another $800 I never knew about because they never sent a bill. Same employees it seemed after 6pm... just an office name change to "Urgent Care" and nobody tells you you'll get 2 bills. One from Seven Oaks Pet hospital and one from Pet Urgent Care even tho it's at least the same people and building. Just be aware

Excellent experience! Had some bad customer service talking to other top restaurants in the quarter. Luckily got an opening at Luke's and the food and service was fantastic! Our waiter was great but another waiter "Richie rich" stopped by and was Awesome! Ask for Richie rich :) !!!

These guys make 1 good thing. A big honking burger with lots of meat and bacon. It's satisfying to say the least. They also have great parmesan fries here. 

Other then that a very small menu. If you're looking for a burger in the land of creole, go here!

Thanks to the Lyft driver who brought us from the airport to our hotel during our recent long weekend in New Orleans, we learned about Luke -- an oyster lover's paradise.

We checked into our hotel at about 3pm, then made the not-too-distant walk to Luke's.

Why so early in the afternoon? Happy hour.

But not just any happy hour. Of course, the usual beer, wine, and cocktails were available for half off from 3-6pm. But the star attraction is that they also sell their local P&J oysters on the half shell for just 75 cents each during happy hour.

So the 3 dozen oysters (yes, that's right -- 3 dozen, 36) my wife and I ordered to share that would have cost us more than $100 back home in San Diego, cost just $27 during happy hour. They were fresh and meaty. Being local, they weren't briny like the ones you would typically get from the Pacific Northwest or New England but they were tasty nonetheless.

My wife had a glass of Malbec to go along with the oysters and I had a local IPA. Both excellent. The server also brought us a warm baguette with soft butter. Perfect.

We liked the Luke happy hour so much we came back on our last full day in New Orleans. This time we scaled back to 2 dozen oysters and tried the cheesy grits (AMAZING) and fried potatoes (crispy and very good).

Very glad we followed the recommendation of our Lyft driver! Great food and great service -- what more could you ask for?

This time I came for dinner!!! 

Sooooo amazing on so many levels! They were fully committed for the evening so we were lucky enough to grab 2 stools at the bar. 

Our bartender Amalie(sp?) was so freaking amazing! We kept asking her about the drinks she was making and all the food on the menu and she explained everything with ease and honesty. My whole meal was based on her recommendations and I was in Heaven.

We ordered
Starters-cup of gumbo and Luke salad.

Gumbo had plenty of okra, sausage, muscles and more..Classically Devine!

My boss had the Luke Salad which was simplistic with balanced flavors. I kept stealing his yellow beets off his plate, they were so fresh, crisp and juicy.

Entrees:
I ordered the shrimp and grits with crab on top! Hot Damn my toes curled again!
The shrimp were cooked perfectly on top of Jalapeño cheese grits and a massive amount of lump crab on top. And the sauce was the best of New Orleans In your mouth.

My Boss had the Roasted chicken which had the best bacon I have ever had in my life in a sauce with Caramelized onions and more. My boss doesn't eat seafood which made me worry about eating in NOLA with him, but this chicken made me say seafood what???

And for the piece de resistance dessert..
 Steam Chocolate Cake with Salted Carmel ice cream and a crunchy decorative piece on top that added the perfect crunch to every bite! Mind you I'm not a chocolate lover and I could have licked the bowl..

Amalie also made us several mind blowing cocktails that were so balanced yet complex she is true mixology at its best.

Wonderful wonderful experience yet again!

service is amazing. during our 3 hours we had 3 different servers (rhonda savannah and gary) and all three knocked it our of the park. food was great. atmosphere is cool. and it waac time too pricy. love love love.

This place is a complete rip off.  They try to upsell you on things that you absolutely do not need.   We just moved to the area from Jacksonville and had a wonderful and affordable vet.   We brought our dog here for what ended up being a simple bacterial stomach bug that required one medication. They tried to sell us $900 worth of stuff as part of a "treatment plan" that he didn't need.   We will not be coming back, that is for sure.   If you just moved to the area and are looking for a decent vet for you furry family,  I would definitely not waste your time at this place.

Fast service! The guys were really polite! They explained all the procedures even though I didn't have a clue what they were taking about, they made it sound fancy. Lol. Only suggestion maybe put the bathroom somewhere that does not face the lobby. Feng shui the arrangement of items to agree with the natural function of the universe. Restroom time is kind a private, and if people hear you going, uh that can be embarrassing when you come out. They did got me in and out

This was the 1st time I came to cosi with my father and we were very disappointed with the service. The sandwich was ok but the service was very bad. We went to get a sandwich, soup and salad. Once I order the sandwich, my father started to order the salad from the same guy at the counter and was told to order from the person on his right and not him. Next we tried to order the soup and was told to order from the left side. As my father turn to the person on the left to order the soup, I heard him calling us stupid behind my father's back. From a person who never eaten at Cosi, this was something we didn't expect the service at the counter to have this type of comment. I expected better, even Mcdonald in many cases have better people working for them. What a disappointment...
Service was fast and the clerk was very nice. They did a very good job of informing me of what was being done to my car and what needed to be done in the near future.
Worst place to bring your puppy/dog. Horrible service and they overpriced for everything.

As soon as you walk through the door you are great with a smile and friendly staff. Everything was delicious! We had the amazing brussel sprouts, shrimp and grits, and burger.  Great start to my weekend! I will definitely be back. Our waiter Tirrione was the absolute best!!!!

Really good Croquet Madame!  Tip - only difference between a Croquet Madame and a Croquet Monsieur is the Madame has an egg on it!  

The Crab Maison is basically lump crab with some sauces/spices.  If you don't like horseradish, don't get this.  

We also got the seafood tower.  EVERYTHING was so fresh.  Pricey but worth it.  Goes really well with a nice bottle of champagne.  Good wine list and a lot of the bottles are reasonably priced.  

Service was really friendly and helpful!  I'll definitely come back for the Croquet Madame!

My favorite local place to get sushi. This place is always packed on weekends but rightfully so. The sushi is amazing and beautifully plated. Presentation is impeccable and everyone here is so nice. The spicy salmon and a spicy crabmeat are my favorite!

Although the prices are a bit steep, it is quite tasty.  I tried the squash soup today and it was delicious.  Most of the sandwiches I've had here are quite good.  One of the beat things for me is that they don't add chopped up raw onion to their mixes.  I'm allergic to raw onion so I'm always happy when I find a place that doesn't add them to the mix.  That way people who can eat raw onion can always have it added, whereas people who are allergic cannot pick out all the pieces safely.    I also really like the pastries here as well.

My only gripe is that the sandwich makers sometimes  put the fixings in the center of the bread leaving the sides completely dry and barren.  They don't all do that... some sandwich makers pay attention to the sides as well and I'm always delighted when they do!

I wanted to try this place after reading reviews and looking for some classy Louisiana fare.  I hadn't visited a John Besh restaurant before, and went with rather high expectations.  I started with the baked oysters, which were delicious.  For a main course, I ordered a steak, which was cooked right (medium) but was brought to the table at about room temperature.  My wife ordered a burger well done, it came out very red...however, they did correct that mistake with no hassle.  For the price, I'd expect better.

We had a lovely time at the tail of Mardi Gras @ Lüke!  Delicious crab appetizer, gumbo, burger & grits.  It is on the parade route so it offered some good people watching as well.  It was loud but had a nice old- bar atmosphere w/ helpful and efficient staff.

The stuffed P and J oysters were OMG!  The best way to eat them is to start by order a French 75 cocktail - as soon as its delivered, order a second one.  By the time the oysters come out your second cocktail should be finished (its now time for a third) and then you can chow down on the oysters.  You really can't go wrong with anything on the menu here in all seriousness.

Amazing place to sample some New Orleans seafood and hospitality. I had an amazing experience. 

Sat at the bar and watched a gentleman shuck oysters. He has got some talent. I ordered a 4doors vodka drink that was amazing. Has jalapeño cheese grits, converted me to a grits lover. I also had the chicken matzo ball soup which was perfect for a cool day. I really enjoyed myself. 

Atmosphere is comfortable and bartender was attentive. Got a sample raw oyster and omg what a shock! It was very kind of them since it was my first one. 

Definitely worth a try. Affordable too!!! Happy Hour!!!

I almost never go to a restaurant twice when traveling, but have been to Luke 3 times. The atmosphere is great, the service is prompt and friendly, and the food never disappoints. 
We came for happy hour and the $.75 raw oysters. We were very sad to see that they are not currently having $.75 oysters for happy hour. But, with all the struggles restaurants are having right now with COVID, we were ok with paying $1.50/oyster. We had three dozen and an order of the Brussels sprouts. Was an excellent way to spend happy hour!
We usually love sitting at the bar, but that too is a COVID casualty. We look forward to returning to Luke post pandemic!

Amazing oysters , during HH it is only .75 each.  
I also ordered crawfish bisque, basically no crawfish.. my bf ordered shrimp jumbo, portion is really small... Everything tasted ok, but since I had a really high expectation to this place, it turned out to be just ordinary.

by far the most amazing place in this county !  
we have had sushi and sashimi for 40 years all
over the world .
hachi blows everything away.

thank you hachi

Yesterday there was only one person working which was unfair to the employee because the amount of people who wanted food. He had to process food and the bill which caused a long line. The food was good but the service was okay, which is understandable when only one person is working. Today I went back and there were only 2 people working, and I'm pretty sure they just fed me raw chicken. The food was good which is why it's 3 stars but the service is quite disappointing.
Delicious! Had fried oysters and the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp En Cocotte. Spicy and hearty-you'll need an appetite to conquer this dish!! Staff were super helpful and polite and attentive.

I had two roaches in my food! I loved that place so im blown at fact that they know me and treated so poorly. They are not sanitary!!! I went to show them they told me to leave and never come back! They are rude and disgusting about complaints! Please be careful anyone who comes here. Take your own risk for a personable review.

This small place is at the base of a Hilton hotel.  Went here for brunch one day and I think one dish out of 4 was worth writing about.... the croque madam was really great!   Fries were soggy and a disappointment, other dishes were all cold.......
Not a great experience... BUT... someone told us this was not the norm and maybe there was an issue with the staff that day.... 
So we tried again this morning, we had a completely different experience.
I had one of the best chicken and waffle plates I ever had!!
The chicken was hot and juicy on the inside with great crunch on the outside.... perfect!  The waffle was crispy and perfect.  The jalapeño relish on top was perfect!!
Loved it and so so happy I went back!

BTW-  I went for the daily happy hour starts at 3:00 and if you want oysters and cocktails at about half price go here!!

Absolutely delicious! My girl and I tried the Pâté of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken Livers & Tuna Tartare! I am not a liver person but this dish was pair nicely and won me over. Kudos to the cooks in the kitchen!

I was a bit disappointed!  If someone said, pick one  word to you describe your experience here?  It would be INCONSISTENT.  
I ordered the ribeye steak medium well, but it came out to me with portions of the steak well done to medium rare.  My son ordered the chicken tenders and one of the chicken tender was cold.  The raw oysters were delicious and fresh, but some had broken shell pieces in them.  The french fries were unforgettably heavily salted. Didn't expect this at all with the positive reviews I read.
The positive is that my other son did enjoy his cheeseburger and my husband's shrimp and grits were really good!  So maybe it's just a different cook who dealt with theirs?  Who knows!  But if we ever do come back to NOLA, I don't think we'll be back here to eat again.

Egg white cups are fun! I get them often for breakfast but they're a bit unsatisfying and overly cheesy so I end up just wanting more food without feeling like I've eaten a good breakfast. I'm sad they stopped selling ancient grains oatmeal. 

I've gotten oatmeal from here a few times because it's right next to my first class of the day every day, but their toppings bar is rather limited and everything is sugared up and sweetened except the strawberries and almonds, and they often fill their oatmeal cups to the brim so it's hard to add a substantial amount of toppings. 

Cosi bread is THE BEST. My friend and I used to come here just because their multigrains are so yummy (and their plains have the same oniony? but not oniony? flavored awesomeness that goes with every meal you could get). If you get a warm slice it totally makes your day.

Their turkey avocado sandwich is *very* filling! Great for togo lunches when you're powering through your day, but it still just tastes like fast food. 

Service is consistently prompt, with on-and-off friendly cashiers. Some places you can walk into knowing you'll have really sweet service but here.

High music volume + the types of food is too fast-foody for me to say it's a fantastic place to go if you have your choice of time constraints, but it's healthy enough for a good, quick lunch.

Came for a light late dinner with my wife. We're from out of town, and Luke is a nice break from the chaos of the Bourbon street area.  Was not disappointed. Stuffed oysters were great, and the Luke salad was probably one of the best salads I've ever had. And the clincher, of course was the bread pudding! 

Great service too and ambience was terrific.  Would recommend this to anyone wanting a quiet evening with great food!
Loved the southern breakfast oysters and Benedict.  Little pricey but great food.  Service a little slow but who cares in nola.  Went twice would go back again

Attempted to visit this establishment 1/15/18... Granted, members of my group were not dressed in Business Casual but we had just arrived from Los Angeles... We got great recommendation from a friend that visits NOLA on a regular basis and regularly goes to LUKE. 

Unfortunately, the hostess at the front treated my party disrespectfully and lied straight to our face.  The second we walked into the establishment she rolled her eyes at us... We clearly saw several open tables and asked for a table for 7... She looked dead in our eyes and said, "we don't have any seats available," and promptly smirked.  My friend then asked if we could put our name on a list for the next available seat... She then smirked again and said, "ya maybe in an hour". Conveniently she gave us a time after happy hour would be over... 

Not a problem though... We gave her our phone number and she said she'll call us when a table is available.  An hour later and no phone call. We attempted calling from the phone number we gave them and we're unable to get through to the restaurant.  We then attempted calling from a different phone number and we're able to get through without a problem. It's as if they blocked our phone number!  

Our first stop in NOLA and such a negative experience.  Very upsetting.  We feel it would've been more professional just outright telling us, "we feel that you are underdressed for our exyablishment.". We would've gladly gone back to our airBNB to change our clothes but due to the negative experience certificate we just opted not to return to the establishment.

Amazing food and the staff is extremely friendly and well-knowledgeable. My husband asked if they had fried shrimp even though it wasn't on the menu and they said that they could make it for us. WOW! Just WOW! It was lightly breaded, butterfly shrimp that was so fresh; a dozen for the same price as their chilled shrimp that is on the menu. To top it off, being new to LA, the waitress so kindly drew up a list of must-try restaurants and sent us on our way :)

Absolute ripoff. My condensor unit stopped working so I had a service tech from Fahrenheit come out to take a look. He ran some tests and determined the compressor was broken. He then tried to sell me a $4600 Carrier unit without any attempt whatsoever to fix my unit. He also tried to sell me another $2400 worth of equipment that turned out to be completely unnecessary. Fortunately, I got a second opinion. Someone from another company came out and quickly diagnosed the problem as a broken capacitor within the compressor. He replaced the capacitor and now my a/c is working great. I absolutely did not need to replace the unit. The Fahrenheit guy recognized that I don't know much about HVAC and he tried to rip me off. Avoid this predatory company like the plague.
Delicious Fantastic happy hour drinks option even better dinners. I had the shrimp n grits and they were awesome the bread pudding was great probably don't need it A la mode.

They have a nice Oyster happy hour with 75 cent raw oysters and $1.25 fried oysters. YUM,  can't beat that.  Also, had their beet salad which is effing delicious. It's my favorite new salad.  I'd say their corn and crab bisque is just ok. A little thick and too salty. Crab gratin a nice starter.

First let me start off by saying I change my own oil. But I wanted to get my oil changed very quickly and without waiting. Plus I really didn't want to do it myself this time. Also, let me say that I feel Jiffy Lube in general is overpriced for oil changes. But if you use a coupon you will knock off up to $15 on your oil change. I went into get the oil change and thought that I would get an engine flush as well, because my engine has over 200,000 miles on it. After getting the Engine flush my vehicle was very jittery and was told that this was natural seeing that I had never had an engine flush before. They told me that all of the carbon and whatever buildup was removed. Well after a couple of days the jitteriness had not stopped, but had only subsided a little bit. Here's why they get my five stars. The manager was very polite and so was the staff for the next couple of days that I checked in with them. I really appreciate that. When I brought my vehicle in for them to look at because the jitteriness was only at an annoying level when I first started the vehicle and when I would go at low speeds like through across walk area. The technician there named Tosha (i'm not sure if I spelled that correctly) was very helpful and did feel what I felt. It felt good to have someone agree with you and concerned about the same issues. Normally add a mechanic place or some car place like that they play it off or make you feel sort of dumb. She and the rest of the staff quickly drained my oil and replace the filter for free. My truck is running so smooth again that it must've been all the extra build up from over the years. I highly recommend this place. Just remember to bring a competitors coupons that you get $15 off. I thoroughly enjoyed my experience there and will definitely bring my business and my jobs business to them from now on. Lastly, they are very military friendly and gave me a discount.

Made reservations at Luke tonight with some co-workers for a nice authentic Louisiana meal. Awesome vibe and great drinks while waiting to be seated. 
Ordered a variety of appetizers consisting of P&J oysters,  crispy brussel sprouts, and cheesy jalapeño grits. All I can say is "wow". Really fresh and delicious apps. The cheesy grits were by far the best I've ever had; creamy, cheesy, and delicious. 
The brussel sprouts were very good, though a bit on the sweet side and had a nice bbq type flavor.
The oysters were awesome. Big, fresh, and delicious with some really spicy horseradish! 
As we waited for our entrees, the manager came out and provided a complimentary appetizer of which I cannot remember the name, but was a thin crust type pizza with amazing blend of cheeses, artichoke, onion, pesto; UNBELIEVABLE! 
Meals arrived and were all truly outstanding. My crawfish ettoufee was really great, the rice was crispy, loaded with crawfish, TONS of flavor. Others got the ribeye and raves about it, redfish, and shrimp gumbo. 
Desserts were totally awesome. Bread pudding was rich and decadent with fresh vanilla ice cream and caramel sauce, pecans. Lemon meringue pie was great as well.
Overall just AWESOME food and service.

WOW!

Came back from vacation to find my place at 92°. Called Fahrenheit (who installed my Carrier system) at 7:30am. They were booked, but squeezed me in somehow. They called me at noon and said technicians were literally at my door.

They assessed quickly that a part was faulty. All parts suppliers closed at noon on Saturday's, so finding the part was a challenge.

They found one an hour's drive away.

They came back installed the part and my a/c is back in business.

They were professional, incredibly service oriented and great at communicating what was happening.

It's 3pm now and they just left. I rarely post reviews,  it I HIGHLY recommend Fahrenheit.

Zack and Jack rule. Thanks boys!

Had dinner on St Patties day evening.  We had a dozen P&J oysters which were incredible...buttery, slightly brunet and fresh.  I also had a cup of the gumbo, rich and full of seafood, very nice. For entrees my wife had the mussels and I had the smoked pork shank. she said the mussels were ok, she was surprised at the broth being creamy instead of a clear broth. The pork shank on the other hand was spectacular. Nice smoked skin with plenty of moist meat that was marbled. There was a small piece of pork belly that was unbelievable. Only complaint is there should have been a larger piece as I almost overlooked it. The bed of sauerkraut was sweet and tart at the same time. The dish also came with a nice link of veal sausage. I would recommend this dish to anyone who likes smoked meat and especially pork. Washed dinner down with a couple strong mint juleps. 

Service was impeccable. In fact we sat down 3 minutes to 6 with happy hour just about done. The waiter rushed in our drink and oyster order before 6 so we could get half price!

Worth the trip.
We loved it! Went to NOLA with 3 of my best friends and this was definitely a highlight of the trip! The food was delicious. Even the fries were notable.

Happy hour is the bomb 
75 cents raw oysters
Inside the Hilton hotel across from intercontinental
