My first time here I was unimpressed. Yes they had birria con consomme on the regular menu but the tacos I ordered were simply par. I asked the waitress about specialties to which she suggested the caldo de res (beef soup) and the godorniz frita (fried quail). I figured I had to revisit before I reviewed the place.

Both specials were extreme. The caldo de res was a slow cooked masterpiece. Big chunks of beef, half of a cob of corn, quartered potatoes and carrots.....mmmm. I can never emphasize enough how amazing almost any Mexican soup is. 

On to the quail. It was fried on a griddle with a weight atop it resulting in a juicy and tender bird resembling chicken but with more flavor. Plus it's small enough to dive right in, bones and all. 

We also ordered the mole which ended up being the highlight of the meal. This stuff wasn't even a distant relative to the canned variety. Spicy, sweet and bitter in just the right proportions. 

The staff also earned extra points. The owner knew better English than I've seen in most Mexican establishments that I frequent making it fun to talk about the dishes we ordered and other items I'm always hunting for in Indy. She said sometimes they have flor de calabaza (the flower of the pumpkin squash) for which I eagerly await trying here. 

The basic rundown of this place is as such... If you think of it as a Taqueria = 3 stars. When you branch out into their more intricate dishes = 5 stars.

Trivia night (Wednesday) is cool.  Weekend crowd is decent.  Bar seems pretty clean.  My last tab averaged out to about $7 /drink. Not bad.

The pizza is actually pretty good.  Better than I expected.  Ought to invest in various pan sizes and serve the pies on pans, instead of serving on a concave plate, which makes the pizza "slide."

One of the best restaurants in town - Luke is a can't miss.  The shrimp and grits are the best I have ever had. The stuffed oysters and bread pudding are perfection. I have had breakfast lunch and dinner here and I haven't had a bad meal yet. They get it right at Luke.
OK, the food tastes great and the service is good.  However the portion and price of the chicken soup were completely ridiculous.  The bowl was only dampened with the soup at the bottom.

Amazing customer service!
The gentleman with the beard and glasses who took my order was very nice and helpful when i couldn't decide what to order, he took the time to tell me what ingredients were in each of the most popular sandwiches and then gave me the option of the "pick 2" to add a cup of soup because i was getting a half sandwich, and then the option of a baked item for 99 cents more, which i normally wouldn't, but because the guy was SO nice i did.
AND THEN, when i was waiting for my to-go order, there was a gentleman (almost bald, a little on the heavier side) who was very nice to me and asked me my name so he could give me my order when it was ready and even asked if i needed extra napkins.
the whole experience was refreshing and i am SO glad they put one in by the mall - when i lived in California i used to eat a Panera Bread EVERY day and now i can again!!

So I ordered it to go order and they made me stand at the door for 10 minutes while the people behind the counter gave me dirty looks for standing there you're closing the doors three hours early and I'm waiting for a pick up order that is right there on the shelf. Almost started a fight. How am I supposed to get it to go order if you lock the doors? There were eight other orders on the shelf. Oh and I especially did not enjoy picking off the grill gristle from almost the entirety of my quesadilla.

We order from here a couple times per month. If that doesn't say enough, they serve exceptionally high quality sushi and other exquisite hot and cold dishes. Some of our faves include Hachi sashimi and grilled yellowtail collar (served with a sweet/tangy/citrusy yuzu pepper sauce). Such a fantastic find. Pricey but worth it.

This is by far the dirtiest of all the Chipotle restaurants that I have been in. Sure they get busy but apparently never clean the dining area. It is absolutely filthy. Something needs to be done. Imagine how the kitchen looks!!  One more thing. I have been here several times and it's always like this.

Tried this restaurant & it is amazing! The environment inside the restaurant is clean and contemporary. We ordered a few lunch specials, D&B Roll & Wasabi Lobster Roll. The special rolls are amazing with so many ingredients in each bite. Visually, the chefs craft the special rolls so beautifully that a picture can not even do justice. Overall, the experience including food & service was outstanding. Would highly recommend to any sushi lovers!

My new favorite sushi place in the burbs! Even my little sister who claims she doesn't like sushi wouldn't let us pick at her share of the rolls. We came here on a Friday night and sat at the bar. We ordered 3 rolls and chicken hibachi. After we placed our order we immediately were given a free appetizer! Being a sucker for free things, I would've loved anything they put in front of me...but this was actually really delicious. It was a fried white fish over finely sliced cucumbers with some sort of creamy drizzle sauce. So automatically we were off to a great start  

Our order came out quickly - We got 2 $6 rolls and one more expensive fancy one, but they all were so good. The chicken hibachi was amazing as well and was served with lots of vegetables and white rice on the side. Once we finished our meal the waitress brought out free orange slices and pineapple chunks. 

I'm definitely making this my new go-to for sushi in the suburbs.

Took my mom here for dinner, and our server Julian treated us so well! He was super attentive and we felt special the whole time we were there. The food was amazing. I enjoyed the French 75 cocktail and shrimp and grits. Our apps included gumbo and the boudin balls. Very satisfied! Take a peek at the desert menu, you won't be disappointed.

I like this spot, but the hostess was judgemental. I had a reservation,but she acted like I was a freeloader. I didn't have a mask, but there was a sign that they would hand out one if you're dining there. She looked at me and said I needed a mask. I said I saw the sign that they would give me one. She said it's only for customers dining here. Why would she assume that I was not dining at Luke's? I assured I had a reservation

One of our favorite spots out of the many, many places we went to during our visit. The chicken and waffles were so good I don't even know how to begin to praise them. The chicken was so juicy and crunchy- southern fried chicken perfection. The Tabasco pepper jelly was incredible not crazy spicy just amazing flavor. Went back for HH the next day and some of the best cocktails in the city especially when they are 1/2 off such a good deal. The cocktail with tequila, jalapeño, basil and blueberry was so unique and refreshing. MUST GO HERE!
Best happy hour in Nola! I love the oysters and French 75! 3 cocktails and a dozen oysters for $22! Can't beat that!

I ordered a Greek salad, half size. I paid over $5.00 for about 5 pieces of lettuce, a few tomatoes and olives and a piece of bread. Could it get any more pathetic? The great American rip off. And you want us to continue to support you during these times? Forget it!

Cosi is like the overpriced, overrated version of Panera. I have come here more than I would like as it is one of the few restaurants open after a 7pm movie screening, but I've never left without being annoyed.

First, you walk in and it's endlessly confusing where you're supposed to order and pay. I've been here in about 15 times and it's been different about 1/3 of the time, so it's definitely them, not me! Do not get the drinks here-I somehow paid close to $4 on a sweltering summer day for a 16oz lemonade that ended up being 500 calories. (Kicker? Not even good, it tasted like I was drinking pure syrup). 

I've had a lot of the menu items, and the only one that I really kind of like is the buffalo sandwich. If you're also forced into going here, the second floor is considerably nicer than the bottom floor.

Only one word can sum up Elm Cafe: Delicious. 

This little cafe, and I mean little - there's only 4 stools for seating!, offers a whole lot of taste. Their menu consists of 'earlies', which are breakfast sandwiches served all day. They also have an assortment of pastries and lunch sandwiches. When I stopped in, I got two of the lunch sandwiches and they were absolutely delicious. The bread was so fresh, the ingredients were perfectly in balance and had me in little paroxysms of happiness the entire time that I was eating. 

The lattes are also very, very good. Made fresh as you order, with cute little latte art on top. Pretty things always taste better, right?

The menu changes quite frequently, so it's always a surprise what is on the menu! If you want to know ahead of time, you can check out their Twitter or Facebook page. All of the sandwich names are incredibly punny, like Shia La Beef or Kim Jong-Yum. I can't recommend enough coming in for a bite to eat!

I was in the New Orleans area and was looking for an oyster spot. It was around 3 so I had a couple happy hour places that I was looking at. Initially, I heard good things about this place so I decided to check them out. When I first walked in, I was greeted by the front and was immediately sat down. There was a lot of seating and it was not too pack given it was a weekday and an odd time. Upon sitting, I see a waiter bring around some of the biggest and fattest oysters I have ever seen in my life. When he came to our table, he explained which oysters were on the happy hour menu and that they were only 75 cents! My mind was still in awe on the huge oysters so I asked him what types of oysters those were. He told me those were the on the happy hour menu and I knew right away I was going to like this place.

My party of four ordered 3 dozens and were patiently waiting as they were getting shucked. We were able to see the chefs shuck them from our table which made the food more appealing. They came out pretty quickly and they were finished just as quicked. My group devoured these oysters. They were amazing! The first oysters I have the area were amazing and set the standard very high. They were so juicy and creamy. Also for 75 cents is a price you cannot beat. The service was great and the place was very clean. Overall a 5-star experience. If you are in the area and love oysters, check Luke's out!

Stopped in by myself friday afternoon. Dawn introduced herself to me and asked me my name. Immediately felt comfortable after that. She showed me the menu and the food is righteous. Wings done right. Crispy but not burnt. Saucey but not soggy. Ow back to Dawn, she's great! Charming and personable related with me right away. I'm glad people like dawn exist. Makes my day off even better. She is a perfect bartender. (Hey boss give her a raise).

My wife and I were there in Feb. and we had to return to New Orleans for a wedding in July and our son was in the wedding. So we took him to Luke's   He is a fan of John and watches him on PBS TV. We enjoyed the food it was great.

Our food was awesome, my husband ordered a lg general tso's chicken. I ordered the chicken egg foo young. Hands down the best Chinese food ever!! For myself, I haven't ate Chinese food in over 15 yrs since before we found Chan's. The 1 and only Chinese food I will eat from now on, not to mention the fast delivery, our food was literally here 25 minutes after I ordered on a Saturday!! Thanks Chan's!!

This was my favorite place we ate during our visit to New Orleans, and it didn't hurt that it was across the street from our hotel! Huge oysters, delicious drinks (I had the Street Car), and great service. We showed up with a group of 5 on a Saturday without a reservation and they were nice enough to fit us. We were all very happy with our dinner, and I'll definitely be back to Luke's if I find myself in NOLA again.
I came here during their happy hour. Oysters were very delicious along with their delicious cocktails. Everything here was amazing and I would come back in a heartbeat. Highly recommend!

Quite possibly some of the best food I had in New Orleans. We picked this place originally because it was the only restaurant around that was still open after 11 but the food turned out to be outstanding!

Recommend: Fried Oyster, bacon and avocado salad and the crab stuffed shrimp with garlic green beans. So good!

I wouldn't know a celebrity chef if he bit me in the ass, so I really don't care about whoever Jon Besh is.  But this restaurant rocked!  Had the frisee salad with lardons and fried pig's ears, Dave had the express lunch of smoked beef brisket.  Both were outstanding.  Dave also had a Sazarac, mainly because he remembers Katharine Hepburn getting wasted on them at the end of "Man of the Year".  He's not a whiskey drinker at all, but really liked his drink.

Also, the service was almost too good.  This was just after Mardi Gras, and the waiter said he hadn't shifted out of high gear yet.

It took me a dozen or so trips to Lüke in Nola and SA before I ran into the Crawfish Homefries.  Everything at Lüke is excellent (though they could cut back on the bechamel for the Croque Madame) but the Crawfish home-fries sit alone atop a very specific category: hangover food.  Technically, I wasn't even hungover but my sobriety didn't impede my ability to appreciate the rejuvenative power of this dish.  Crispy home-fries smothered in crawfish tails, bits of fried okra, a creamy creole sauce with a fried egg on top (over medium please).  There's something salty and cheese I couldn't detect but the combination doused with Tabasco resurrected me completely.  Sweet baby J, I need to learn how to make this dish at home.

Luke restaurants' items are always tasty and you will never go wrong with any of the choices. I have tried their food like 4 years ago when we were living in NOLA and 4 years later I cane back for a conference. I ordered b sprouts and it was unique and super delicious. I also ordered crawfish bread and it was good. The managers are very professional and they will address your concerns (if any)immediately. I highly recommend it for brunch.

We had a pretty large take out order including the pescado frito which was against my better judgment but the boy child wanted it. We paid almost $50 after tip to our carhop/waitress and I really didn't like that they don't have pricing up outside. Maybe it's offered inside where we've never gone. We had 3 tacos de lengua which were average and 3 tacos de carnitas that went into the trash. Those carnitas were so dry it was like eating wood shavings. The sopes and gorditas were just ok. The plate the gorditas were on had a large whole burned through it so grease got in the bag and all over the other plates. We ordered one each of the tamales just to try them. The red was a big no. My son ate the green so it must have been okay. The rice and beans that came with the fish were inedible. Overall, most things lacked much flavor. Entire meal only came with the green salsa made from peppers and oil and it needed to be blended better. Had a very chalky taste. We've had better experiences from them before so I'm giving them 2 stars but we won't be back. Way too many other options up and down Nolensville.

We went to Luke for dinner. The room smelled subtly (and pleasantly) of sauerkraut when we walked in. The menu has German influences as well as local ingredients and dishes. We had the Wednesday special (Shrimp Creole) and the Moules  et Frites. Both were great. The mussels were some of the best I've had in a while - very fresh and flavorful. 

Service was just OK - attentive, but we felt like we were being rushed, and our server seemed impatient.

Used to be one of my favorite places to eat. Just went there and the waitress forgot to put my boudin order in. When I got it I didn't like it and wanted to order something else. I was told the kitchen was closed. I was seated at 10:15. Restaurant closes at 11. Got the Boudin at 11:10. I ate crackers and butter because I was hungry.

As I found common in NOLA, no veg options on the menu, but they were so happy to accommodate.  Luke had tons of different (and delicious sounding) sides, and our server asked if I'd like the chef to incorporate any of them into the dish.  Feeling adventurous, I asked to just be surprised.  I did the right thing, because I never would have come up with what I received by looking over the menu.  My entree - lightly roasted vegetables over perfectly seasoned spetzel(!).  Beets, turnips, green beans, asparagus, and tomatoes on top.  My meat eating dinner companions raved about their picks, though I was too awe struck by my own meal to remember what they ordered.  

Desert for me was the apple & currant tatin.  Best desert ever.  Please feed me this for desert with my last meal on this planet.  The strawberry shortcake (assumedly seasonal with local berries, and not on the menu) and chocolate-filled puff pastries also received much accolade.  

Service here was great.  No eyes batted at a split check request.  Very helpful servers with our special requests and any and all inquiries about the menu.
I LOVE THIS RESTAURANT!  They make their own mustard and a pate that comes in a mason jar. Like the bar and staff is great. Has a fresh feel. Yummy.

An establishment that cheats its customers. Customers who trusted them with their time and money. 

Hey Chan's Chinese halal restaurant if you charge $8.95 for a serving of vegetable lomein, then at least put vegetables in lomein. 
Hope you fix it because if you don't, one day you will lose all your customers.
FANTASTIC!!! Fresh oysters and the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp and Grits is AMAZING!!!  FUN atmosphere and the crew here is great!!!
Wonderful dining experience! Everyone was so friendly. Food was delicious and the dessert was to die for! One of the best meals I've had in my whole life.

2.5 stars for food and 3.5 stars for service. 

Let me start off by pretty sure I ordered the wrong thing or maybe I came on an off day. I forgot my friend recommended the raw oysters here and I did not order that. 

Service was very friendly! Arrived straight from the airport and the staff offered to store our luggage so we didn't have to roll it to our seats and take up space. They were also attentive and checked in frequently.


 Stuffed P&J oysters - very salty. Only finished 5 of the 6 oysters with the help of lots of water. Oysters were broiled over a seafood mix. Had it been less salty and the seafood flavor more enhanced, it would've been so delicious. 

Croque madame - average. Ham & cheese sandwich with egg. Paired w/ fries that were slightly over cooked. 


If I come back, I'm sticking to the raw bar

This is my go to sushi place in bucks county,   always good Asian  fusion good here. Great sushi, sashimi,  rotating menu it's always amazing. If you appericiate  good Asian food you want to  come here with friends or business clients . Leave the kids at home if you can and focus on the food and atmosphere. To make it better bring a bottle of wine or some beers, it's byob!

Love finding new hidden gems locally- this place is great. Been here a few times eating in and for take out. Hibachi dishes are a bit on the small size ( we were hungry) but food was all tasty. We had a mixture of rolls and hot food including teriyaki salmon, beef, chicken, tofu and other appetizers. Baby Bok Choy was a little salty for my liking but I don't usually like a lot of salt in my food. We had 3 orders of Gyoza- it was a big hit with all the family, big and small! 

Decor is new and modern. Nice atmosphere.! Look forward to trying more items on their menu!

Lüke was a nice find during my visit to New Orleans. 

The large dark wood bar takes up most of the restaurant. There are lower level tables off to the side. Every bit of usable space is maximized, so the tables are a little close together. The noise level can get loud, but the energy in the room adds to the vibe of the restaurant.

While there was no separate gluten free menu, there are several dishes that can be modified to be gluten free.The Washington Parish Roasted Chicken served during lunch is an extremely large portion and cooked well. It was juicy throughout and the potatoes added to the heartiness of the dish.

The service was friendly. I do have to commend the server for being extremely helpful and patient when I continued to question about the cooking practices, i.e. sauces, pan fried vs deep fried, etc. If he wasn't sure, he went back and verified with the kitchen rather than just making up an answer on the spot. This alone goes along way in my book.

Well, always a favorite so let's start there. The French 75 is always good and the oysters are always good. The food almost never disappoints. What did tonight was service. Fully staff, or don't open, or don't oversell when you don't have enough staff to cover. We love Luke, don't make us not want to come back.

Went here while in New Orleans for the first time ever. 

Did not have reservations but they had a table for us. The matzo ball soup was the best matzo ball soup I've had in my entire life and trust me I grew up on that! The Brussel spiritus were delicious and generous portion! 

Let's talk about the raw oysters!! This was the first time in my life I've ever tasted raw oysters so I can't say if it's better than other places or not, but it was good and interesting lol, my friend who loves raw oysters claims it was delicious! 

Will definitely be back next time I'm in town :)

Recently, I have been here several times for lunch.  The Luke burger is excellent, the shrimp and grits is very good and a bit different.  The crab, spinach and artichoke dip appetizer is excellent and needs someone to share it with.  The chocolate dessert was fantastic.  And the service is always excellent.  Highly recommended.

I have been staying at the business district Hilton all week. Being a diamond Hilton member I have experienced tons of Hilton branded restaurants.  Twice I have sat at the bar and all four bartenders I have interacted with have been totally fantastic. Bryan made me feel like we had been friends for years going as far as lending me his wine key for my certified somm exam. In my opinion thats the kind is customer service that makes a visit memorable.  His counterpart on Wednesday was hilarious and welcoming as well. Maddie was great Friday night despite being very busy. She really made me feel at home.  I had Malcolm's heirloom tomato salad. The food was great and the service was far better. As an industry veteran compliments like this don't come easily. LUKE deserves all five stars and more. If you are looking for a modern take on classic Southern Fare or some amazing gulf oysters as well as top of the industry service this is a killer spot.

Wonderful experience! A dozen of us  showed up for oysters and had a great time. Even though we pestered our server Savannah often, she was skilled, efficient and very pleasant! The fresh, sweet, local oysters were as good as Savanah's service! Great combination.

I came here for happy hour where it's a great deal (all drinks are half off and oysters are only .75/each!!!!!) The oysters were some of the biggest I've ever seen - very meaty and tasted simple and "clean" as in not much of a sea/salt water flavor but enjoyable enough. The sancerre went very well with the oysters.

Unfortunately, the service was lacking for such a popular "more upscale" place. I got a seat at the bar right away but it took the bartender at least 5 minutes before she came over to wipe down the counter and give menus. After taking my order, I had to wait almost another 10 minutes for my glass of wine. I noticed she served the drinks of a pair who sat afterward first. It wasn't that busy but she acted as if she did not want to be there. I expected more and better at a place like Luke. At least she went around letting everyone know she was taking last orders for HH right before it ended.

What a wonderful experience I had today at Jiffy Lube I needed my car's oil changed and the fluids topped off I also got my coolant fixed they were polite explained everything and I was very satisfied with the customer service as well as the clear explanation about the coolant and how I needed it flashed but it could wait I opted to have it done because I felt that they didn't push it on me they explained that it was going to need to be done rather than insisting you know a single woman alone I feel in many cases they in auto repairs try to push expensive repairs or products this was not the case thank you Jiffy Lube I will go back to you
Great place!!! Great wings!!! Ask for extra hot.

Always the best happy hour that I've been to in New Orleans.  Half priced beer, wine and specialty cocktails plus $0.75 raw oysters and $1.25 fried oysters.  Overall a fairly small dinner menu, but everything that I have had has been amazing.  Make sure to try the baked jalapeño cheesy grits and the crispy potatoes.  

The wait staff and bar staff are equally fun and attentive.  If you can get a seat st the bar, grab it, but during happy hour, you will more likely be standing at bar or sat at a table.

I want to preface this by saying I've only eaten here once, but it left enough of an impact that I felt like I had to post a review. The fried chicken sandwich here is a spiritual experience. Sweet, a tiny bit spicy, and cooked to perfection, this is truly the best chicken sandwich I've ever had and maybe ever will have. I might order one for breakfast tomorrow, and one for lunch too. Seriously dude, it's that good. If you're in town and nearby, this place is an absolute must.

Vets are informed and good about giving details and informing the patient. Some of the techs are excellent...

The three stars are due to the fact that they are expensive and some of the techs act like they are doing you a favor by speaking to you.  Staff needs to work in their customer service. If I am paying you money (more than I would in other places), spend money on food and medication in your establishment, then treat me with courtesy and respect... same as I gave you when I walked in.

Also, as I was waiting for my dog, whom they instructed me to pick after 245 and after waiting over 20 mins for him, I see the vet tech out front looking through and showing pics to the person in front desk. 

Took everything I had to remain patient. But in the end, bad reviews and loss of customer are more effective than yelling matches.

We got off the plane and had to wait for our hotel room so we needed a place to snack and have a cocktail. This is the PLACE!!

Really great happy hour. Delicious menu items at great prices and oysters at 1/2 price. What more do you need in New Orleans!! Cocktails were quite unique and fun. My husband ordered a bowl of the gumbo... twice!! And even the dessert menu was offered. Hospitable waiters and friendly menu suggestions make this a place we'll come to again for a NOLA happy hour!

Really awesome meal. The crispy Brussels sprouts were by far my favorite thing. The chili paste added the perfect kick. The fried oyster salad was yummy with the oysters just right. And the bread pudding was heavenly. Great rum sauce and the toasted nuts made it. Richie was a fantastic server and went the extra step to make the experience great.

Our hotel was just a couple of blocks from Luke, so after looking at their brunch menu online, and reading their reviews, we decided to go there for New Year's Day brunch. We were happy we took a chance, because the food was wonderful! I started with one of their signature cocktails. The name escapes me but the ingredients were: tequila, fresh blueberries, jalapeno and basil. It was delicious and I drank the whole thing, which is unusual for me. Other items ordered were the corn and crab bisque, shrimp and grits, and steak frittes. We weren't interested in partaking of their raw seafood bar, which looked great, btw.  The food we ordered was tasty, and satisfying, and the only things that could've been improved were if the shrimp and grits were hotter (was luke warm) and if my husband remembered to order bernaise sauce with his steak instead of butter. :) The service was stellar, too. Would definitely go here again, especially during happy hour (3-5pm) when some raw oysters are discounted and their signature cocktails are half off!

I am definitely a fan! We live right across the street but haven't had a chance to come and visit yet! However, I'm glad we did! It was delicious.

It's a tiny tiny little location, with only one staff member. But the food is great. They have only a few options overall, so being a vegetarian, I tried the Jackfruit Burrito. It was delicious and a good portion! I was definitely full after eating that. My partner had the pork burrito and thought it was great. They give you some Valentina to spice up your life, which I really like.

Today was a nice day and they have a cute little patio that looks out to 117ST. It's actually quite big, with ample seating! Bigger than the restaurant! 

The music was awesome as well. I had to pull out shazam to catch some of the great tunes playing.

They also have pretty cool merch for sale.
Currently under renovation. We arrived and their computers are down and won't be able to seat us for an hour...argh. and no other customers are waiting
fresh, delicious, fast & courteous service! happy hour rocks!  50 cent oysters and half price beer!!
Great atmosphere and great food. A little salty for me so if you're trying to limit your salt intake you may want to request less salt. Great bread pudding!!

This restaurant sits inside of the Hilton St. Charles hotel where we stayed while in New Orleans. You can enter right off of the main street. Located in the Central business area on the very outskirts of the French Quarter. Walking distance from the trolley and all of the Quarter's sites, this is a good area. (If you ever want to stay in The French Quarter but not too close to the craziness of Bourbon St, stay in this area.) This quaint little spot with it's intimate sitting area is crammed with tables and seems a bit congested however, is billowing over with old southern charm...the black and white tile floors screams old building. Elegant yet casual. The food is moderately priced and boy oh boy it is yummy!!! New Orleans fare. The jalapeño grits are to die for!! Get a side order just because!  You will not be disappointed!! You MUST try their Bloody Mary!! I think this is by far the best Bloody Mary that I've ever had; spicy, bold, and very flavorful. No, I didn't see the bill and thank goodness I didn't lol. 

The dress code seems to be business casual from the looks of the customers. The service was fast. The waiters were freaking awesome( ate here three times while there). They offered items that they enjoyed! Oh, and get the bread pudding!!! Oh goodness, you're in the South, bread pudding is a must!! The bread pudding was savory and sweet, moist and deliciously tasty. Go for breakfast!!!!!!

I tried this place twice prior to COVID. Management and hostesses were rude and unaccomodating. The oyster shuckers and bartenders were nice and friendly. I might give it another try soon to see if it has any redemptive value.

Showed up 5 minutes before opening and the manager came out and unlocked the door. It was cold out but she still didn't have to do it. I was in a hurry and her compassion helped get me moving along with my morning.
My service was good, grabbed my stuff to go, but the order was complete and correct. Coffee tastes great and my pastries were perfect. 
Definitely worth an early morning visit if your in need of a coffee fix.
5 star Shrimp and Grits. Worth every dime. Glad they were open when the rest of New Orleans was shut.

Loved this place! This is a John Besh restaurant (celebrity chef, and featured on Top Chef many times). We came here for lunch on a Tuesday and had no problem getting a parking spot in front, and we were seated right away. The bread they gave us first was crispy and warm and the inside was nice and soft... just the way I like my bread. We had a bowl of the Gumbo. The Gumbo appetizer was nice and earthy. It had sausage, meatballs, and oysters stuffed with pate'. It was tasty and also very rich, but very good. That alone could have been a filling meal. My entrée was the Louisiana Jumbo Shrimp with Mozarella and Jalapeño Grits. This was my first time having shrimp and grits and WOW! Tasted like HEAVEN! I didn't grow up eating grits, but eating this somehow gave me a feeling like I had been coming home to Louisiana all my life. It was that AWESOME! I highly recommend this dish to have. You will not regret it. My husband had the special of the day: Gulf White Shrimp and White Squash Etouffee. It was served with Jasmine white rice and was also very delicious. What a great dining experience! Staff was very pleasant, ambiance was classic, and bathrooms were very clean. I will definitely return the next time we are in town and recommend this place to all my friends.
Always a good experience here! Usually do takeout and everything is just as good. Love the edamame salad.

The food was JUST ok but I think it would have been much better if the service was better. I stood at the door waiting to be seated while what appeared to be three employees ignoring us as we patiently waited to be greeted or even acknowledged. Finally a manger noticed us waiting from the back and came and asked if we had been helped. I really wanted to leave by this point because the three gentlemen could at a minimum said "hi, hello, the Bruh man nod or something to welcome us." But my hunger superseded my patients this night. Don't think I'll be dining at this establishment again, if anyone is going to ignore me I'll let it be the under paid cashier at Burger King on her cell phone while at work. Matter of fact the service was better at BK then Lüke, The muffled distorted voice of a dive thru sign saying "Welcome May I take your order!" was more welcoming then being treated like you are invisible.

I just ordered a Green Goddess Cobb salad at the drive-through here in Boise on Franklin. The person who took my order was efficient and helpful when I asked multiple questions and for substitutions. I have had pickled onions but not on a Cobb before. It was delicious. Good job, Panera!
The shrimp and grits here were legit and the service was really good as well. Presentation of the food was on point. My Burger ws not seasoned.the bread pudding ws delicious.

Very nice and convenient.  We stayed at the Hilton next door, arrived late (after 10pm) and even in the Big Easy expected little late at night.  It was very good indeed, great, friendly service and the food (we chose simply - I chose the steak frites) hit the spot. Nice ambience, US version of a french bistro.  Wouldn't be my first choise to eat in NO - but if you are up late and want something GOOD - this is it.

We'd already just had dinner and were craving some raw oysters so we honestly just came here for the oysters happy hour. This review is strictly for their oysters. We didn't have dessert at the restaurant prior to coming here so this was pretty much our dessert. We ordered stuffed oysters, fried oysters and raw oysters (75 cents each!). We thought the fried oysters were okay. They were small and bready. The stuffed oysters were better. I thought it was pretty good. Then we ordered some raw oysters which you can't really go wrong with if you like raw oysters. Our server was wonderful and attentive. I may have to come back to try other items on the menu. We just couldn't because we were so stuffed from our dinner earlier.

This is a solid and adequate gym.  There's a good amount of cardio equipment with TV's, and I've never had a problem getting one.  It also has a decent selection of free weights and machines.  Also available is a  room for children, which could come in handy.  

The clientele is pretty normal, but not a place to go if you're hoping a meet market.  Chances are you will feel comfortable.

What's missing is a pool, and walking track.  I'd give it 3 stars, but for only 20 per month, that's a great value, and gets a bump up to 4. I'm glad I joined.

I had the most epic dinner at Luke's last night with my mom and a friend. We got in under the gun for discounted wine and 50 cent raw oysters. 

The wine we chose was a sparking rose that was very nice. Not too sweet at all. The oysters were perfect. They brought out a little sampler plate of all kinds of stuff like hog's head cheese, pate, a delicious relish, pickles, etc. Everything was amazing. 

For the main event, my mother and I split a beet salad and the shrimp and grits. Those golden beets were like candy.  The shrimp and grits were incredible. I could barely eat any more by that time, though (don't worry, I still managed)! My friend had the fried drum which she said was very good. She took some to go to eat the next day.

Long story short, no, I was not able to eat breakfast this morning and I'm not so sure about lunch!

My friend and i went to Lukes for a 4th of July dinner and had one of the best meals of our stay in NoLa.

Made reservations online so we were promptly seated when we arrived. Our server handed us menus, topped off our glasses with water and handed us some complimentary warm bread. Bread was delicious. Freshly baked, crunchy outside, soft and moist inside. :) 

For dinner we ordered a dozen P&J oysters, crispy brusselsprouts, jumbo louisiana shrimp en cocotte (aka shrimp & grits) and the french 75 for an alchy beverage. Everything was delicious. From the oyster to the drink. Oysters were fresh and large in size. I'm not a fan of brusselsprouts or veggies in general but i wouldn't mind eating this dish again. It's flavorful with a hint of spice from the jalapeño. The entree was the highlight for me. The server had the kitchen plate our shrimp and grits to share so we each had our own plate prepared. The shrimp was cooked just right. The sauce was light but flavorful and tasted lovely with the grits. 

Will love to eat at Lukes again when I am back in NoLa. :)

Tip: Make a reservation in their website so you dont have to wait!
This place made me an oyster convert. Happy hour is awesome, with 75 cent oysters and nice drinks. Def add it to your list!

Best food in New Orleans, hands down. We got in early and we're seated right by the kitchen. Those guys are having fun making your food! My hubby, two kids, and I enjoyed everything we ate including the grilled oysters, gumbo, and shrimp. We wish we went back because every place we ate in New Orleans was a disappointment compared to Luke. Unforgettable meal we will remember forever!
Luke has the best wait staff and oysters. Their happy hour is awesome and their French 75 is the best!

Always excellent food and service. I've always had a great meal here. Delicious entrees, tasty appetizers and tempting desserts always please, and servers are always outstanding. A favorite for takeout on the way home.

My husband and I went there for lunch. We ordered Cesar salad. My bowl was discussing, dirty.... it was brought to us with mine on top. I would think the server would see that and at least exchange for clean one.... nope! It's too bad because the food is really good....

Been here a few more times since my last review.  I think I'm gonna settle on 4 stars for now, because when it's good, it's pretty damn good, but with the risk that it might be bad.

Tonight I had the seafood gumbo and shrimp and grits.  The gumbo was good, it bowl wasn't big, but it's still a good amount.  The shrimp and grits was very tasty and highly recommended.

I have nothing but positive things to say about Elm Cafe and Elm Catering. My husband and I visited Elm Cafe for a quick lunch on a Saturday afternoon. They had 2 people working and there were about 6 customers in the small cafe. We were able to find a place to sit and our food was ready in approx. 10 minutes. Elm's menu is constantly changing, but we ordered a sandwich, a side salad with butternut squash and an Americano. Elm uses a lot of olives in their food. I'm not a big fan of olives but the the olives complimented the sandwich so well. For the first time in my life, I actually enjoyed olives. 

We had a great experience at Elm Cafe, so when we found out that our wedding reception venue (Little Brick) uses Elm Catering, we were more than happy. We had a cocktail style reception at Little Brick with h'ors d'oeuvres, tasting boards (meat & cheese board, dip & spread board) and  a variety of sandwiches for the late night snack. Our guests raved about the food. Everyone was happy with the variety of food and how Elm was able to cater to those with food sensitives (gluten-free, nut-free, and lactose-free). We couldn't be more happy with the quality and professionalism of Elm Cafe and Elm Catering.

A coworker told me I needed to have Oysters while in New Orleans, and Luke's popped up on the radar. First off the staff is really friendly. I arrived during happy hour (which I had no idea of) but the waitress kindly told me so. They don't have the full menu currently but it was still a great visit 
I ordered the oysters and they were great! I also had the Burger medium rare, it was good but nothing extraordinary. I had the jumbo shrimp and grits , it was phenomenal. I was stuffed but I tried my best to finish as it was great. I also had the Brussels sprouts but I wasn't a fan of those. Overall the experience and food was great! Definitely wanna go back again

This place is great and if you're looking for some oysters and drinks between 4 and 6 the happy hour makes it a relatively inexpensive treat.   The PJ raw oysters are very tasty and a great deal. The Brussel sprouts are five star delicious and a must order if you're into brussels!!  The tuna tar tar is wonderful as well.  Decent local beer selection as there were multiple pale ales/IPAs to choose from. Great food with great service. 
Win win for sure

Luke Restaurant was the most memorable thing about my 5-day trip to Nola. Boyfriend and I visited every single day during their weekday happy hour for delicious $0.75 raw oysters, $1.25 fried oysters, and amazing half priced cocktails. 

I recommend sitting at the bar for a good view of the gentlemen shucking the fresh oysters for you. During our first visit, one of the men gave us several complimentary oysters and just placed them onto our plates, he was very sweet. All of the oysters are fat and juicy and their fried oysters are too die for. The fried ones go well with the aioli dipping sauce that they come with (for happy hour, you have to order these by the half dozen). 

For cocktails, you can't go wrong with any of them. I think the most common drink that people order here is the French 75 which just tastes like a lemonade mimosa but it gets the job done. Depending on the bartender, they can make the drinks pretty damn strong which I love. 

Overall, if there was one place in Nola to go for happy hour oysters, I recommend choosing Luke because not only do you get amazing quality oysters for cheap but you also get fried oysters, great cocktails (compared to the sugary crap you get at other places), and your good ol' southern hospitality.

I was referred to this company after calling a 4.5 star company that I found on Yelp.

I scheduled an appointment for 3pm - 5pm on a Friday.  I was told they would call approximately 30 minutes before they arrived.  Well at 5pm on a Friday, before I leave the country on Monday for 3 weeks, no one had called or shown up.

A call to the company discovered they had entered all of my contact information incorrectly.

The were unable to accommodate my weekend schedule and refused to send anyone out today.

Now I'm forced to pay emergency rates to get this resolved before I leave Monday morning.  Will never call these guys again.

All bachelorette parties should include a boozy brunch... at Lüke, of course! All I can say is, I am so glad my MOH did her yelp research and picked this awesome restaurant (*special shout out to her*).

Food and drinks were very memorable. My faves were the stuffed oysters and crispy brussel sprouts - seriously must-get! I also really liked the stuffed french toast. Usually when the menu says stuffed french toast, it really means a french toast sandwich. At Lüke, it was INJECTED WITH NUTELLA! The soft shell crab BLT was also delightful and came with plenty of frites. For drinks, just one glass of the French 75 was enough to put this girl in an even happier mood ;)

Service was very professional - constant water refills, napkin folding, plate changing between courses, etc... although a smile from the server wouldn't hurt. Most of us grouped into pairs so we could share multiple dishes, and the kitchen split half portions for us! 

Since we were in a private room (another brownie point), I can't comment on the overall ambiance. From what I remember when first entering the space, it had a chic bistro vibe.

In the end, we walked out feeling full, tipsy, and fabulous!

Great HH from 3-6 where oysters are 50 cents and drinks are half off.
The oysters were a bit sandy, but how can you complain at this price?

Service was a bit slow and our waiter said it was because the shucking station was backed up.  Understandable.

I also had a delicious red beet salad.  Upon arrival, I only saw a bunch of greens only to find layers of the tangy beet underneath.  It was topped with gorgonzola and spicy pecans.  Quite delicious!

Husband had the fried oyster bacon salad.  
His advice:  Next time extra bacon and no oyster.  He didn't like the way they were fried.  The cube sized bacon bits were delicious tho!

I would definitely recommend this place for if you're in the mood for some oysters and a drink.  

Make sure you try the homemade potato chips while you're there!!
It was good, but for the amount of reviews and ratings I expected better. The Crawfish bisque is something I really recommend!

Driving by jerzee's you won't think It would be a place I'd like to go to, but then check out there beer selection.  AMAZING and well priced. Every time I go in there have something new that i haven't tried. The bar staff for the most part is awesome.  The food is fine for a place like that and they have an electric dart board. The only turn off is that sometimes things are hard to find, which makes since with all the new beers all the time, and sometimes the crowd sucks on poker night. The

Things started well but we were behind a large party so there was a very long delay between appetizers and entrees.  They made up for it with 3 exceptional comped desserts. (The bread pudding was the best I have ever had). 

Baked oysters were outstanding.  The fried oyster salad was also really good.  

Shrimp and grits were delicious.  

Service was attentive and would have been great if not for the delays.

We met the most amazing manager Tonya Alexander made sure that our experience at Luke was 10 stars out of five!

If you get the opportunity do you are the freshest oysters I have eaten in a very long time make sure you say hello to Tonya Alexander

The server put a $20 tip on my $45 meal, knowing that I was very upset with the service, and I put nothing on the gratitude line. Totally fraud! 
I got the worst service ever, the server ignored me for most of time, my food was late for almost half an hour while sitting there out of the kitchen, even when I wanted to have the check I got nobody came to me. I complained twice but nothing changed, and I put nothing on gratitude when signing my copy, then later my credit card was charged an additional $20. 
I wouldn't have noticed this if it was not for a business trip and I had to ask for a copy later to get it reimbursed.

ATTENTION: IS  important to read the REVIEWS   In a place where Everything seems to be the perfect place to bring you pet for care. The XRAY and MRI are the $$$ almost perfect scam to get money from you. If you refused any of this test then they misdiagnosed your pet give wrong medication all about money.  after spending almost 1500 dollars in 2 visits  this is the end results

I have to tell him my dog seems to have a UTI, wish it was positive after a Urinary test. My husband and I decided to have a late evening dinner at Luke's since it was right across from our hotel.  This visit turned out to be a horrible mistake.

The restaurant was fairly full for the late evening hour.  Our host attempted to seat us tightly between two other tables.  We asked and received better seating at a nearby table closer to the entrance.  

After perusing the menu, I settled on the chicken, broccoli and potatoes.  My husband ordered the shrimp and grits thinking that we haven't been any place in New Orleans where this dish wasn't a winner.  Both of these entrees were $26 each.

When our meals arrived, I had a nice size half chicken, potatoes with plenty of broccoli.  Everything was nicely seasoned and quite tasty.  However, my husband's shrimp and grits was a big embarrassment. It came in a side dish portion.  Basically,  it was about five teaspoons of grits with five tiny shrimp on top.  He said the taste was pretty good but the portion size was ridiculous for the price.  He had to request some bread to supplement the entree.  I even shared some of my meal so my dear husband wouldn't leave the restaurant hungry.

We had two servers for our table and no one was really checking to see if we were okay.  Just before receiving the bill, one of the servers came to refill our water glasses and my husband used this opportunity to complain about his meager meal for the price we were paying.  The server seemed quite disinterested and said that she doesn't set the prices.  At no time was she apologetic or offered to bring anything else.  She did say she could send the manager.  She did not follow through with relaying any of his concerns to anyone.  A good server should have taken some sort of responsibility for her table.  

By this time, my husband was totally annoyed and asked for the bill so that we could leave this sorry excuse for a restaurant.  DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME AT LUKES!  There are too many good restaurants in New Orleans to settle for this nonsense!

This is one of my parents' favorite restaurants in town so they asked that we go today for brunch, as they are visiting. I've been to Lüke several times for dinner and have had really great food and service.

After a five minute wait spent listening to a hostess literally whine about her inability to use OpenTable in front of several customers, we were sat in the back dining room, right up against the windowed kitchen. My boyfriend remarked that everyone in the back was dressed more casually/looked less like bobble-heads and lawyers than those seated in the front, but hey, it was crowded, whatever.

I got a Bloody Maria and the Bloody Mary mix was pretty much just tomato juice. No spice to it whatsoever. My boyfriend got some sort of River Boat fruit-y rhubarb concoction with gin instead of vodka and the flavors fell flat. I'm a cocktail snob, so maybe I'm being too picky, but whatever.

We got the charcuterie and it was decent. The chicken patê and housemade mustard were really excellent but nothing else was exceptional.

I ordered the fried soft-shell crabs, poached eggs and grits. When our entree came--and my mother's entree was dropped 2 minutes after the others--I attempted to cut into a poached egg with my fork only to find that the white was not cooked AT ALL. It was in a liquid state. I took a bite of the soft-shell crab before sending it back to be recooked because ew.

When my entree came back, it was all too evident that the kitchen was clearly like "well, goddammit, we'll cook it again if they're that demanding" and threw the whole dish into a pan so that when it came back, all the textures were disgusting. The hollandaise sauce had boiled over and was puffy and full of air bubbles, the grits were congealed together into hard little grit balls, and the second round of cooking resulted in a lot of the breading on the crab falling off. My eggs were cooked, but the dish was in such an lukewarm, unappealing state after the second cooking that it was inedible.

My parents and boyfriend forced their leftovers upon me and everything was thoroughly mediocre.

Our server did comp the single entree but the bill still came to $118 before tip for 3  mediocre entrees and an appetizer. Service in general was mediocre. Not very apologetic. Did not offer to get a manager.

I do think that the restaurant puts its D-Team in the kitchen for day service, but there is no excuse for such poor execution especially at the price point. Also, why even have a D-Team at your restaurant?
Elegant setting, awesome food , great service at a reasonable price. Will come again! Shrimp & grits was creamy deliciousness..Perfect balance to the crisp beet salad.

Got into town late. We were hungry. Consulted Yelp.  What a great experience. Went across the street from the hotel to Luke and found dining according to the gospel of Luke. You gotta have Gumbo when you visit New Orleans. Gotta have oysters in November in New Orleans. Saw the Luke burger at the next table so I gotta go back. They were crowded and we had no reservation but the wonderful host staff fit us in and the wait staff was awesome. It was noisy. But this New Orleans y'all.

We came to NOLA on our honeymoon and came to Lüke to celebrate. The local oysters are to die for! We had crawfish with handmade pasta and shrimp and grits...wonderful choices. Above all our server, Rich, went above and beyond with complimentary wine, champagne, and dessert to make the occasion extra special. Thank you for making our honeymoon unforgettable! Rich is amazing and if you can request him, I highly recommend you do! He made the experience that much better! :)

Fancy and upscale interior with great seafood, located in the CBD.

Luke bacon burger with fries was the best burger on the menu with what it was topped with, in my opinion. Shrimp and grits was delicious, as it was cheesy and creamy to the extreme. As a seafood critic, I am glad to have dined in here.

Chef here is wonderful bringing the elegance out of this restaurant. Decor is beautiful and service is just as spicy.
Everything we ordered was excellent. The server, busters and hostess were all first class. The burger didn't need any condiments and the gumbo was seasoned to perfection. I'll definitely come back!
A little pricey. Great sushi & you can't go wrong with the Gyoza! Nice atmosphere on the inside as well. Out Of Control Roll is one of our family favorites.

Nice server (think his name was Matt). We both got the chicken and waffles for brunch, my boyfriend gives the dish a 8.5/10 Id give it a 6.5/10 but that's just personal preference. It ended up being a lovely brunch! Would recommend!

I'm not sure I have adequate words to describe our experience.  

It started with drinks at the bar.  One of the shuckers gave me a sample of mussels, clams and shrimp that was incredible. 

When our table was ready, hubby ordered oysters and bisque.  His comment concerning the oysters was " if I smoked now would be the perfect time" as he finished them. 

I had the mussels.  Fantastic is too tame a word. I enjoyed them immensely. 

Finished it off with a to die for bread pudding.  

I highly recommend.

My wife and I celebrated our birthday's at Luke tonight. Have been reading a lot about this location here. I warned my wife about the service issues mentioned in some of the reviews. We arrived 15 minutes earlier than our reservation time. We were greeted with a smile at the hostess stand and seated immediately. We were sat in the rear of the restaurant where we could see the kitchen. Our waitress arrived quickly and took our drink orders. We had the French 75 and one the namesake dark draft beers. The beer was excellent, the French 75 was strong, but one of those drinks that you just wanted to drink one after another, after another...(the kind that can be "silent but deadly"!)

We ordered the rabbit and duck liver pate. A great choice. Not a fan of the pickled watermelon rind though. The stone ground mustard was a great condiment to add to the the bread. 

For entrees I ordered the ribeye steak and fries. The steak came out perfect. Med. rare, warm hot pink center and crunchy crust on the outside. It had a large pat of garlic butter on top. Steak sauce NOT needed. The fries were good. I had read somewhere that they were fried in "duck fat"? The waitress said, no. Where did I get that idea? I did not like the mini bottle of ketchup and mayo. Wanted a larger quantity I guess.

My wife ordered the shrimp and grits. A tasty dish, although not a large portion like I have seen at other restaurants. She enjoyed it and we shared our dishes with each other. 

For dessert we ordered the gateau basque cake and a chocolate mousse of which I cannot recall the name. The cake was fantastic. Very dense in the center and a nice crunchy crust on the outside. Strawberries that had been infused with grand marnier were the topping. We also had the coffee with the dessert. 

A great birthday meal. Our first visit to a John Besh restaurant.  Our waitress took great care of us.  Must try Domenica and Restaurant August soon. Luke was fantastic.  Gotta get back there for happy hour.

Went here on Christmas Day actually, and it is really great.  Wife had the Burger, which is just awesome, huge and delicious.  Even the fries are good.  It's right up my alley to have a nice restaurant with a gourmet burger.  

Cocktails are delicious as well.  Highly recommend it.

My favorite experience during my trip 11/6/20. We had the BEST TIME EVER! Went for happy hour the drinks were lovely, small plates delicious, the staff was so amazing, I cannot recall who served us but both people we so great. A guy with a very spunky personality, and a girl with an Afro. I even told the manager same night.

I've been twice. Once to dine in and once for takeout. Food and service were amazing. My first visit I had some briny oysters, crawfish etouffee and a great glass of wine. Service was super professional and warm. The next trip I grabbed the Fried Chicken Sandwich and the Crawfish Corn Bisque. Everything about the sandwich was spot on the bread, the cook toppings and fries. With seemingly every restaurant in in America having a Chicken Sandwich on the menu this was set apart. They did a great job with the to-go packaging as well. When I got back to my hotel everything was still hot and fresh.

Displeased that I was not told of 39.00 annual fee at time of signing.
Just showed up on my amex

Fabulous! Clean, great menu, authentic Japanese cuisine!
Highly recommend! Ordered comb platter with steak and chicken. Tender and just the right portion!

Due to construction outside you could easily walk right past this gem.  Inside it has a nice bar and it is loud because it's packed.  Make a reservation if you can.  The decor is so so.  The service staff are nice.  We tried the Brussels sprout dish that they are known for.  I don't like Brussels sprouts and must say they make them tasty.  PJ oysters were good.  Bery thin oysters.  The shell 8s 5 times b8gger than the oyster. Sneaky shell fish.  The puppydrum was good.  It's a fish by the way.  Yeah I didn't know that either.  The shrimp and grits is the best.  The French 75 is a good drink here and the draft beer is good.  Don't waste your time with the Dixie unless your a bud light guy.  Food is presented nicely and tasted great.  I was full.  Restrooms are large and clean.  I say check it out.

Had breakfast there and the Chicken and Waffles are awesome. The waffle is fluffy yet crisp ( I know it's an oxymoron) and the chicken with the whipped butter and sweet and spicy compote is a perfect combination. The staff was very attentive and professional.

Great Happy Hour from 3-6 serving freshly shucked Oysters or Fried every day of year. One the best French 75's you'll ever have is at Luke. 

The P&J Oysters, as well as the Mussels were such a hot during our happy hour visit we didn't get any pictures!

Found this gem of a place around the corner of our hotel and it has a very comfortable vibe and even business savvy for a professional lunch/dinner but still relaxed for a casual dinning experience. Loved the Oyster Salad and the table service we received was excellent. I travel a lot with my mom and she is a picky traveler when it comes to food, she loves her burger and fries so thankful LUKE's had that. I really appreciated it because I love the seafood and it had a burger for my mom also. It was a win win. Highly Recommend.

The soft shell crab "BLT" was good all around. The heaviness of the fried whole crab was nicely paired with fresh lettuce and tomatoes on a light mayo bread. There was some sort of green sauce, but it didn't seem to add much to the dish.

The fries definitely could have been better. They reminded me of McDonald's fries after you leave them in the bag too long - soft and limp.
The best Halal Chinese store on this side West side..... But please call in ur order cause the wait can be long....

The quality of cooking is uneven. I had good results with the hamburger, the rib steak, and the raw seafood. On my last visit I thought the chicken entree and fried fish entree was barely edible. Over cooked and dry. Just tasted a little and left it.

I'm so sad to say that I heard this retro fitness is closed.  Really depressed me because this was the best gym for the $$ in the area.  The trainers were great, especially the hit, cross training, kickboxing, etc. Very sad day for me.  No other gym this close/convenient with great motivating trainers.
Lisa at the register was so sweet, talkative and helpful! The garage sale and clearance options were worth every penny!

Amazing brunch! Was here for a conference, needed a quick lunch and stumbled across this place. Had the Lüke Breakfast and about died. 2 eggs over easy, heavenly grits, smokey bacon and sausage, and a biscuit and a rhubarb ham... To die for!!! 

This place rocks!

Grits and shrimp, boiled shrimp, hamburger and fries, etouffe, creme broulette, bread pudding were all good. Service was good, drinks kept full. We arrived without reservations and got seated in 15 minutes.

We have Cook's glass for 34 years, and they have done a great job taking care of us. We are really hard on doors and windows. Once in a big storm our front door was sucked off the hinges, and landed in the street. They got it fixed well enough, till we got new doors!

Great happy hour with 75 cent oysters! Excellent beer selection and really wonderful Gumbo! Get there early for happy hour as the place can fill up in a hurry!

We will be back next year!
Amazing!! We tried the bento box, hibachi dinner, several sushi dishes, and the ginger and seaweed salads. Everything was sublime -- I'm a pretty harsh critic and this place is a genuine 5 stars.

I've been to the Big Easy many times and have never wanted for a good dining experience. There are so many great restaurants in New Orleans that it's hard to go wrong. But even among such lofty company, Luke stands out as an example of everything that is great about dining in the Crescent City.  Not only is the food excellent and the seafood expertly prepared, the service is outstanding. Our waiters were so personable and attentive that we practically ask them to join us for dinner.  Classy, but not pretentious; traditional, but with a modern touch, Luke is a fresh catch in the NOLA dining scene.
Best happy hour ever! Raw oysters are 0.75/each and fried oysters are $1.25/each. Good price, delicious food and drinks and awesome waitor! Definitely will come back!

Went for happy hour and this was a solid find within walking distance of most commercial business district hotels. I'm a fan of John Besh since he was a loyal supporter of NOLA after the Katrina disaster so I enjoy trying his places whenever I can. I have never been disappointed and this was no exception. Since I was alone, I scored a great seat at the bar right in front of the guy shucking oysters. As others have described, fresh gulf oysters were 75 cents each and fried oysters were $1.25 while there were also drink specials going on. My cocktails were 50% off which I thought was a steal. I made friends with the shucker and got an education about the local bivalves. I appreciated his passion for his job and he was so proud of some of the local oysters that he shucked a few freebies from areas I asked about just so I could try them. I felt like I was a very welcome customer and his most important client while sitting there. I didn't get his name but tipped him well and I hope the restaurant knows that he represents them very well. I got out of there stuffed on oysters and bourbon for not a wallet-breaking amount. While you might be able to find oysters for cheaper elsewhere, it is hard for me to not love this place based on the experience I had.

Dined for Thanksgiving 2020.  My nephew and I were touring the city and made reservations at this delightful NOLA gem.  I was thrilled with their kindness with my sweet babe, age 9.  They spoke directly to him, took his order and made small talk with him.  I am grateful to Luke's staff for making this day so special for my little guy.  I adored that they had a burger on the menu for him even though it was Thanksgiving.  He was thrilled with that and the tiny ketchup bottle.  :) 
I had the turducken, creamed spinach and the most magical mashed potatoes that have ever graced my plate.  From staff, to food to the unique decor this has become my new fav NOLA spot.

I gave this place a shot based on other reviews and damn if they weren't absolutely accurate. I have had sushi all over the world including in Japan and this was at the top of the list of the best I've had. This place is in the middle of nowhere.

I love this place and they have done an amazing job adjusting during Covid. Payment over the phone, zero contact when you pick up. Just walk in and take your food off the numbered spot on the table in the vestibule. I adore their tempura green beans and my vegetarian child can't get enough of their vegetable fried rice. It's not overly greasy like fried rice tends to be in some places. Very polite staff!

3 WORDS. 

RABIT LIVER PATE.  GET IT.

Last night of NOLA, was brought here for happy hour, I believe it's 4-6pm.

Oysters - $.75 each, had some beers wine, DAT PATE, and some more the bill was less than $65 for 4 people. 

Great busy joint bit upscale but happy hour is good deal the pate so damn amazing, I ordered another one for TOGO brought it back to San Francisco with me and it was still good!

Super Busy!
A bit pricey!
Nice Waitstaff!

Ate there for dinner during the week. My girlfriend and I had the chilled shrimp from the raw bar and gumbo for our shared appetizers. The shrimp were good they had quite a meaty texture to them really hard to explain never had this before, I wonder if they were smoked or something? The gumbo was decent, definitely not the best I have ever had. I ordered the shrimp with grits for my entree and my girlfriend had a sauteed mussel dish served with frites. My meal was stellar the sauce/broth was very flavorful and I used one of her mussel shells to scoop out all the sauce from my dish. Her mussels were tasty but had them before at many other restaurants. We shared a bread pudding for dessert which was so yummy one the best I have had.

This is the best food I had while in New Orleans, and I was purposely hunting for the best food. The service was great and quick and they were super accommodating for my baby and I. They actually have a changing table in the bathroom and very few restaurants in New Orleans have anywhere to change a diaper. I got the shrimp Etouffee and DANG so good with the perfect seasonings. The beet salad had golden beets in it and they tasted like they came straight from the garden!!! The bread pudding was by far the best I've had in New Orleans and the ice cream was clearly homemade and so delicious.

Today was our first time that we went to Hachi. OMG that was so nice and tasty experience. The waiter that was serving us was a young Asian lady and she was very nice and gave us a suggestion what to order. The food was delicious. We definitely be back.
The seafood, the fried Brussels sprouts... it was truly epic. A beautiful brasserie, with fantastic, attentive wait staff!

I'm the type of person who dislikes the notion of celebrity chefs and the culture of hype, almost to a kind of chronic paranoia.

So I was a little skeptical of the great John Besh, whose book we seem to see everywhere around L.A.

I have to say, if this place is representative of the type of food he's serving up at all his places, his rep is well-deserved.

From the cultured butter, to the insanely good hog's head cheese (think a type of spiced foie gras, but somehow better: we ordered it on a whim), to the cochon de lait, this place was simply incredible.

FIRST PLACE, RESTAURANT TOUR 2009

Along with Dante's Kitchen, this places takes first-place for my "Back Home in New Orleans Restaurant Tour 2009."

Or something like that. Oh yes, we'll be back.

And apologies for all my puerile, predictable "Besh/Tesh" jokes. I know it's not clever, but I like it.
Normally I don't like Qdoba but this place didn't make me wear a mask just told them I was vaccinated and we cool. Thankful they didn't ask for my card as proof

I was turned to this place by CarGuru; and it was the best decision. David was the car sale associate who assisted me with my purchase. Very nice and accommodating when I had done my research on a car I was interested in. I recommend this place for your next vehicle purchase.

Visited on a busy Friday night and our waiter Richie Rich was very knowledgeable and attentive to our table of five.  Had the Pate, crispy Brussels sprouts, and shrimp and grits. Enjoyed every single bite.  Will be back!

You can't go wrong with Luke.  Fresh oysters and the famous Luke's Burger are must here.  The red beans and rice with fried chicken on Monday's are also a must.   I'm not sure if they still have Happy Hours during the pandemic, but if they do, it's great price for fresh shuck
Oysters.

Just had the Southern Breakfast here. Meal was everything you want in breakfast. I usually don't like grits but theirs were delicious. Not grainy or mealy, and just smooth and buttery. Silky texture. Really great. 

Good portions, great flavors. Clean place. Fast polite service. Curious to come back for dinner!

9 year member here. It's the perfect gym for the money and cardio equip is always available. It's conveniently located  and has helpful and friendly staff. Members are extremely respectful to each other.

If you love your dog, DO NOT bring them here. They are money hungry. I spent $3000 in two visits and they sedated my dog 3 times! After the third time my dog was sent home within an hour of sedation, suffered dehydration and was blind from sedation. He has since struggled with diarrhea since being sedated and they have no answers. Dr. Wishik does not care about your dog she cares about your money!!

Yes, please!  A group of my girlfriends and I enjoyed a delicious dinner at Luke's while visiting.  

First of all, do not skip the fries.  They were cooked to perfection and highly addictive. 

The pate board was a large portion and quite tasty. 

I ordered the ribeye and split it with my friend since we planned on having more bites after dinner.  They were gracious enough to pre split the meal.  The steak was prepared very well. 

Of course, you can't forget the oysters.  If you love oysters as much as I do, you'll appreciate the selection.  Honestly, you should have the Louisiana oysters along with the others simply because they are delicious and you can't pass on price compared to the other oysters. 

The only downfall was that we were seated in the back room which seemed to be with out heat.  It just so happened we were there during one of the coldest days of the year in NOLA.  We were all freezing, but the good food helped to over come the cold room temp!

DO NOT GO TO JIFFY LUBE
My wife took her 4Runner in for an oil change, the next day we found an oil puddle under the car. Turns out they cross-threaded the oil plug, damaging the oil pan, requiring it to be replaced ($350). They would not take responsibility for the damage and we had to pay for their mistake ourselves. Had they taken responsibility, we would have written a 5 star review about impressive honesty. We have been regular Jiffy Lube customers for almost 20 years, but will now never go back.

So I'm weird in the sense that I don't like fried food, because I feel like the oil just gets stuck in my throat after the first few bites and it feels weird. But omg, why is the fried oysters here so good? I mean, it's fried-food-good but it's not oily. What black magic is this?

My wife and I have been in New Orleans all of 4 days, but we both agree that Luke is one of the best restaurants we've ever eaten at, and for sure the best meal we've had on our first trip to Louisiana! We were taking a long walk and were deciding between Luke and Tressane (or however else it's spelled), and we're so glad the coin flip led us here.

We started off with the duck/rabbit pate and the fried boudin balls. To be honest, I still have absolutely zero idea what boudin is. Sometimes it'll be like pulled pork, other times a patty, and here it was like a fried hushpuppy or arancini, but regardless, it was still delicious! Not sure what the yellow sauce was that came with it (it was foamy and tasted like butter and mellowed out hollandaise sauce), but the sauce helped add another level to the boudin balls.

The pate was to die for. They brought out a giant jar of the stuff along with a full board of large-grain mustard, pickles, a pickled radish or some other vegetable, and two types of vegetable jams. When we ran out of crostinis (the jar is HUGE people) our waiter brought us some more bread. The pate is rich and has the lovely iron-like flavor you would find in liver dishes. Combined with the acidic and sweet flavors of the rest of the board, the pate was perfect. I would strongly recommend it, as long as you don't absolutely despise liver.

For our main course, we ordered the shrimp and grits to share, and the kitchen graciously divided the dish into two small skillets (thank god, otherwise I know my wife would have eaten more than her fair share of the plate). The shrimp were juicy, the sausages moist and full of flavor, and the grits cheesy and just bland enough balance out the strong vegetable stew/sauce that coated everything. It really was a well balanced dish and the portions were huge! I felt full even after eating just my half of the dish.

And holyyyyy cow, the bread pudding and ice cream was FANTASTIC. Probably the best part of the meal. The bread pudding is soaked in a whiskey caramel which, you'd think would be saccharine, but it was just the perfect level of sweet. If I wasn't in public, I would have licked that bowl clean.

Excellent meal and service. Great atmosphere. Really enjoyed ourselves and staff was attentive and very helpful. The only issue were the 2 hostesses that were rude, non-smiling and very unwelcoming. Treated us and other waiting guests as if we all were bothering them. And we all had reservations. Very disappointing way to be introduced to the restaurant and took a very good server to set the mood right.

12/3/19 - updated review: I went back to Luke due to late work meetings. Well this time is wasn't as great. The service was great but the food was not. I ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" which was amazing the the night before. This day, it was disappointing. The decor on the food wasn't the same. The dish came out cold. The waiter got
it reheated but the food didn't come out the same.
The grits were not as cheesy and delicious as the night before. It was watery and not as flavorful.
The highlight was the brusselsprouts. They were flavorful and had a hint of spice to it. Simply delicious! I was very disappointed with the grits, the dish was the only reason I came back. The plating was even different.

So so good. Glad we ended up here after the Ruby Slipper had an ungodly wait. 

Beautiful space and charismatic servers (thank you Jesse!) made the ambiance, despite being extremely hangry, very pleasant. 

The Brussels Sprouts were some of THE BEST we've ever had. Perfectly crispy, so flavorful and sweet and spicy, with a slightly creamy element in the barn cheese. They look crazy with the almonds, apple shreds, and jalapeño slices but the flavors are to-die-for. We soaked up the extra sauce with the complementary bread it was so good!  

The burrata salad was delicious as well - light and zesty with some surprising spice in the pecans (they're dusted in Cajun seasoning, not candied!). Being a cheese fiend, the burrata-to-salad ratio was on point. 

The boyfriend had the pork schnitzel sandwich to which he said, "I have never been humbled by a sandwich like this before". "It looked me in the eye and said, 'here's the door; you're not ready.'"Jesse accurately said the servings are "aggressively generous". Something to keep in mind so you don't end up lugging half a pork schnitzel and fries around for hours on parade day!

Fabulous food, fantastic service. 5/5 would recommend!

Visited NOLA during Valentine's Day weekend, and carnival.  We hopped an Uber to our hotel off of Canal St, dropped our bags and rushed to find a late dinner (after 9pm) within walking distance from the hotel.  I saw good things about Luke when I was searching Yelp so we heading over.  No reservation, but we were seated quickly at a table for 4.  The menu looked great and our server got us going quickly.  Sorry, no photos of the food because I was too busy stuffing my face and enjoying the moment.  started with a bowl of the corn &crawfish bisque.  so rich and delicious!  the french bread was a perfect compliment!  We had 2 entrees:  shrimp and grits, and the puppy drum.  The shrimp and grits were rich, creamy, and had a great flavor.  The puppy drum was amazing!  Our server (Shawn) was good, and helped to break down the menu.  Enjoyed cocktails with dinner from the full bar, and walked out with a go cup just because I could.  Good option if you are in downtown NOLA.

A group of 8 of us went Friday night.  OMG.  We were able to snag a private room which was great.  The food was absolutely outstanding...from the oysters, to the bread & butter, to the crabcake OMG to the shrimp & grits.  (Heaven)  I would reccomend this place to anyone who loves a great meal.

First time here. Coming back. Fresh is the word. Nice different options. The Japanese oysters were great - we ordered a second batch. The littleneck clam miso soup was excellent but a bit salty. 

Highly recommend.

Definitely a must eat location in NOLA!! I searched some breakfast locations and read some reviews and definitely was everything they described. 

Luke was packed! The Service was Amazing!! I'm a big stickler about how you treat your customers. Our waiter was awesome. He even gave me their Brussels sprouts recipe. The shrimp & grits was mouth-orgasmic! The boudin biscuits were different and delicious!! I was ranting about this restaurant to everyone. Must Visit!
