I'm still dreaming about the duck duck rice 2 months after having it here. 

The rice was soooo good. It was a bit crunchy and seasoned sooooo well. I usually don't like rice but I can eat the rich from this dish everyday. The dish comes with roasted duck which was very tender and juicy. But the highlight of the dish was definitely the rice. One of my friend ordered this dish as well and loves the rice as much as I did. 

My other friend ordered steak and fries. The steak was cooked to a perfect medium rare. 

My boyfriend ordered the pan seared stripped bass. If I remember correctly one side was pan fried very nicely. He also really enjoyed the summer beans that came with his dish. 

This was probably my favorite meal from my entire New Orleans trip.

I heard that Lisa of retrailer was doing a soft opening so I went out of my way to check it out. 

This is the TINIEST little space and too cute for words! This space used to be a walkway between buildings that got walled in and finished. It's super narrow but very welcoming. I love how Lisa put in rustic looking furniture and had clean black drawings painting onto the off white walls. She had a bunch of little teapots behind the counter and a neat set-up for making freshly grated herbal teas. 

Lisa was super friendly as I popped into the store. She had a cake from Whisk (dark chocolate and peppermint) which I immediately purchased a slice of (it was gone before she rang me up). She also had a lavender shortbread (I took it home and swooned at my first bite).

I also ordered a hot ginger and tumeric tea. I think this is my new tea craze. Freshly grated spices make this tea a brilliant yellow color with a nice fragrance and perky zing. A dollop of honey in the tea gave it just enough sweetness without being overpowering. I savored every sip!

I can't wait for this place to REALLY open (not 100% sure when, but she said sometime in January). Until then, I have my chinese-store purchased tumeric and ginger to tide me over.

Upon taking on a foster dog as a permanent member of my family I needed a vet that was closer to us here rather than close to the Rescue I was fostering her in in Orlando.

On my first visit the tech was amazing, and the doctor (Dr.Clifford) showed a lot of compassion and concern and knowledge for my sweet Lillian.  I brought her in for a UTI concern, but upon exam Dr. Clifford found a large hard mass on Lillians left shoulder and indicates that could be bone cancer.  

I brought her in for X-rays and additional tests if needed but upon seeing the films, we all agreed it appeared to be cancer.  Recommendations were to amputate - but being a disabled veteran with limited income, and concerned about quality of life for Lillian due to her breed and personality with such a procedure I went looking for a second opinion on the treatment options.  Lillian was still playing, and her normal self and not really in any pain.

It was going to be some time until I could get a second opinion with the veterinary surgeon and oncologist - and it became evident over the next 2 months she likely needed an amputation.  I called Seven Oaks Back and asked for a quote so I could plan financially - and was quoted over $2000.00.  I was gobsmacked.  Of course it's all needed up front.  I asked if they had any discounts for veterans etc - of course no.  But I scheduled the surgery anyway - for a month out so I could pay for it.  I expressed my concerns with the staff but all that was suggested was that I get CareCredit (which Inalready have and was maxed up due to other issues with another pet).

Someone did say MAYBE they would consider payments but it was going to need to be discussed. 

I didn't reply as I was trying to figure out how to help my dog.  I finally got a second opinion by the vet in Orlando and their advice was to not amputate as in their experience the cancer can spread and the dog only lives a few months more given the size of the mass and the age and temperament, and health of my dog.  

I decided on a pain managment option with Lillian, and when the Tramadol Seven Oaks insists on prescribing still showed no relief asked if they had another to see how that worked - they did give me some Gabapentin for Lillian - which did nothing for pain relief but made her totally stoned and dizzy. 

Trying everything - including Eddie's Wheels donating a cart for her so she could walk without weight on her front leg - Lillian still deteriorated literally overnight.  Today it has been 48 hours that all she does is cry and whine from pain and frustration and refuses to get up or even try to stand, so we made the difficult decision to have her put to sleep.  

I called Seven Oaks, and as Lillian is in pain and screams when I try to have her picked up I told them we need help letting her go - they are more than willing to come to the house to put her to sleep - $406!!! So I then asked if I could manage to get her there without her screaming in pain how much - $276!!!  First of all I live approximately 8 miles from Seven Oaks and for that awesome distance they charge $180.  They wanted to charge that to come check my cat to prescribe droncit for a tape worm - but droncit is(praziquantel) is an OTC med now.  You can get it at the same dose as the vet from the same company at PetSmart!  Seven Oaks wasn't going to prescribe it without examining the cat and I had assumed it was DEA regs - but That medication doesn't require a script And Seven Oaks is the vet that did the fecal to diagnose the tapeworm! 

I spent half the day trying to get my cats in the carrier to take them in and when that wasn't happening I had asked about a house visit as they advertise 

When we were still considering amputation upon scheduling the second opinions both of the Orlando vets said it would be just over $1000 if there were no complications and they would try to work with me.

When I asked their office gal at Seven Oaks to email
Me the estimate I didn't get an email
But she did go over the line items on the phone with me - and all of them - including the optional laser cauterisation procedure and optional medications came to under $800.  I asked her how it was $2023 when everything she listed was far less than that - she stumbled and stammered and said it was just the line items they had down here.

Bottom Line - while Dr. Clifford appears to be a genuinely caring provider at the Seven Oaks Veterinary Clinic - but the owner seems to be mostly about gouging patients for as much as they can get, with little care or compassion for the patient - the pet who is suffering.  Now I have to find another vet to put Lillian to sleep so she's no longer in all this pain and suffering.  Just because we live in Wesley Chapel doesn't mean we are wealthy retirees.
Entertaining wait staff (Elliott) and good food and drinks! The Brussels sprouts are amazing.

i'm only giving 4 stars because of the way the place is maintained. i'm here from Miami and my friend suggested this place. very authentic mexican joint. they have a food truck outside with like a curbside service and an inside where you can order and eat. we went in and grabbed a booth which was not that comfortable and the cushions were falling apart so I was skeptical at first. the menus are also worn out and torn up HOWEVER. they have large bottled sodas and different juices and amazing choices from tacos quesadillas burritos and gorditas. WOW all of us were amazed and didn't speak the entire meal of how good this food was. I am going back before heading back to miami I 100% recommend. pls pay this place a visit !!!!
I thought it was great.  Between the pate and the pork sandwich, I was in heaven.

While in New Orleans playing music for a convention, the music staff and I had dinner at Luke 's. We had about 36 people and the restaurant was very accommodating.  Even with that number of people the staff took the time to provide excellent customer service.  I will go back when I'm there again.
Amazing place. They really care for the animals . They saved my dog.  She was so sick and they cared for her with compassion and love

Shady Shady Shady. please buyer beware!!! They are sizing you up before they even get through the door. Technian never even showed. Never called and I even asked for a manager to call me back and...nothing. There's more to the story...I am familiar with HVAC and had a good idea what the issue was. Technician agreed, gave me a ridiculous quote over the phone and then never even showed up. I have not heard from them since. Just please find someone else because they are NOT HONEST PEOPLE!!!
Don't waste your time, you can fine better food in the tourist area if the quarter.  Service and food not worth the time you have to wait for your food.

This was probably the best food experience I had in New Orleans and we didn't plan on going. 

Food:
1. The Brussel sprouts are probably the most delicious I've ever had, cooked probably and seasoned so that there was some sweet, spicy, and salty. Must have!
2. Agnolotti was so tender and delicious. 
3. The grits were so good that someone who doesn't normally like grits liked them - they weren't watery but cheesy and with texture. 
4. The bread pudding was my favorite dessert compared to other cakes, pies, soufflés, etc. With ice cream and caramel used pecans!
5. The oysters were fantastic!
6. The beet salad was great and healthy given the heavy meal but nothing that stands out. 

Service was wonderful as well even though we were looking for a light late night meal.
Nice quick place to get dessert. Nice and sunny area. Nice customer service. No eat-in option because it's only a takeout area. Lots of open spaces to eat it though

Holy shucks. It looks like I've found my go-to place for happy hour. My boyfriend and I came on a Friday around 5 pm for happy hour (happy hour is from 3-6 everyday) and were seated immediately to our surprise. They don't have an official happy hour menu so you just got to ask what the specials are. 75 cents raw oysters, half price off their cocktails, drafts and wines. What an amazing deal. 

My boyfriend ordered the Ruston smash cocktail to drink and enjoyed it. I had the door three and thought it was refreshing with just the right amount of vodka. 

For apps, we had the brussel sprouts. MUST GET! You won't regret it. We also ordered a dozen raw oysters and half a dozen fried oysters. Oysters were fresh and soft. Best oysters I've had thus far in NOLA. Fried oysters were cooked to perfection.

In addition to the amazing food, the service here is outstanding. Our server's name was Richie Rich and he was very personable and attentive. Very nice guy. I'd definitely ask for him again when I come next week and the week after that. 
Honestly if I could give this place more than 5 stars I would.

My friend and I discovered that gem accidentally when visiting Nola during the Mardi Gras madness. Luke has the best oysters and desserts: Dark chocolate torte and Maple Crème Brûlée are  to die for! And we aren't even into sweets! 
But beyond food, the service was impeccable, the staff is very attentive, kind and genuine. It was our server's birthday the night we came, and staff sang him birthday song - it was so so touching. That gesture speaks volumes about the team and the management. Overall amazing atmosphere. I'll definitely be back and recommend to everyone. Skip all the touristy places that you need to reserve a few months in advance. Enjoy tres chic Luke

wow super super super overpriced, this place has nothing special , also their product not even fresh
order a blue crab dip, you'll see what i mean 
absolutely this place not recommended 
there's tons of places out side of downtown please look for them

YES YES YES YES YES YES YES!!

CRISPY BRUSSEL SPROUTS: I make amazing Brussel sprouts. People that hate Brussel sprouts, eat my Brussel sprouts. BFF took of a bite of these Brussel sprouts, looked at me dead in the eye and said, "Your Brussel sprouts are great. These are AMAZING."

Our server overheard him while attentively refilling our water glasses. He held his breath and tensed, ready to put out the fire that I would inevitably set on BFF. I took a bite.

Savory. Sweet. Tart. Spice. Remember how Pixar's Ratatouille visualized taste? Yep. Me with fireworks watercoloring through my brain. Our server looked at me and said they have a printed recipe card. So thoughtful. BFF was on point. And he did not catch on fire that night.

For dinner, we ordered the Luke Burger and Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte". Fabulous. Fantastic. The flavors made my head swirl in lush content. I could eat buckets of their shrimp en cocotte. Of course, BFF would need a wheel barrel to carry me out.

We ended up here for dinner because our aunt was craving for some proper shrimp and grits. Lüke came up on my search and basing from the pictures previously posted - this is the place for that.

We posted up the bar right away and ordered couple of beers. We got an order of dozen oysters (which were part of HH, $.75 pp), pate and split an order of shrimp and grits. Btw, from what I gather - you need a reservation for the main dining room. So snag a bar spot as soon as one opens.

Oysters were big and clean tasting. It's not the sweetest I've had (Kumamoto oysters fans anyone?!) but not bad. It's good for the money, that's for sure! The pate was good - it's not strong flavored but more well rounded. The condiments it came with was a nice touch as well. Now, for the star of dinner - Shrimp and Grits. They were kind enough to split the order into two plates and I was blown away by the portion! Their grits was light, fluffy, creamy and cheesy paired with the red eye gravy plus the big shrimps - it was just glorious!! Even with the half portion it made me full. Definitely a must try dish at Lüke's! 

All in all, I would give this place a 4 stars and a fun experience from one of Chef John Besh's restaurants :)

This place is very expensive and the quality of the food is horrible even a simple fried vegetable spring rolls they don't get it right... crispy from outside side but gooey inside... very disappointing!!! Definitely NOT coming back.

Hubba hubba those jalapeño grits!!!! No regrits.

Don't stop there, be sure to try the gumbo. Super rich and delicious. The Luke salad was divine. Very colorful and full of tangy deliciousness. 

My friend and sister ordered the burger but the smokey bacon flavor and strong cheese was a bit intense.

I sat at the bar on a Monday night. I was told there was going to be a 10 minute wait for a table for 1 (half the tables were empty), so I was like...ok.. you're either lying to me or there really is a long reservation list. The bartender was a sweetheart, and eventually people did start rolling in. If you plan to eat with 2 or more, plan to make a reservation (the place isn't big!). Maybe it's because Luke is Hilton's restaurant (adjacent but no direct access), or maybe it's because the food is great!

The Riverbend drink was light and refreshing. I was done after 2 :) I also ordered the shrimp and grits, which was FANTASTIC. The grits were so cheesey and jalapeno-y, and the shrimp was covered in delicious butter. I wouldn't say the shrimp was JUMBO like the description says it is, but they were medium large. There could be a little bit more shrimp and andouille, but it's a fancy place I guess. My side order of the salad Luke was also delicious. The beets were sweet and just crisp enough. I wouldn't mind ordering a full size for my meal next time. The gentleman sitting next to me loved his roast chicken dish, as well.

The guys shucking the oysters were really funny to talk to, also. I wouldn't mind sitting at the bar again. I was staying at the Intercontinental across the street, and I would totally do it all again!

Our hotel recommended this place and we are so glad they did! It will be on our list of places to go any time we visit NOLA again. Everything we ate from starter to dessert was amazing. I can't eat much spicy or acidic food comfortably and they adjusted the blue crab garganelli for me. My husband had the shrimp and grits, best grits he's ever had. We would definitely order the spinach artichoke crab dip again, but the best part was the bread pudding. It was perfect. The service was excellent from the minute we walked in until after we were leaving. Do yourself a favor and put this on your list of places to eat in New Orleans! The place is clean, friendly, delicious food, and a great environment, not much more you can ask for!

Nice French brasserie, with a nice take on seafood.  The 3 of us enjoyed 2 dozen oysters, P & J's and some Atlantic variety I can't recall.  The cold app assiete was awesome, especially the pate and the headcheese.  I went with the redfish with crab meat on the waiter's recommendation.  It was a bit disappointing...everything just tasted like butter and lemon.  One friend had the shrimp and grits, and it was definitely the highlight.  Delicious.  My other friend had the entrecôte grillée au frites.  Tasty, but nothing special, although the fries were just as good as everyone else has said.  Finished off with a dessert whose name I can't recall, but was kind of a beignet-bananas-foster dish.

Came here for convenience-sake and it was a disappointment: 1) wait for food was longer than anticipated; 2) gumbo roux tasted like flour- no touch of Creole seasoning whatsoever- I did not finish it. In addition, it was lukewarm3) and kid's meal fries were limp from being saturated in grease. 

I was not charged for the gumbo and I requested fresh french fries, which were delivered how they should have been initially. I will add I was given the opportunity to order another soup; but it was a tad late and I was over it.

The brussel sprouts were a winner. 

Not sure what happened to the gumbo though (insert sad face). Even though the roux was thicker than what I'm accustomed to, it was bland. First night in NOLA to eat good food, and was disappointed.

Great atmosphere, nice attention to many details. 

Seems more like a $$$ than $$ with $20+ brunch plates, but it was well worth it. 

A nice break from the sea of tourist traps and gimmicky locations.

The best part about Jerzees is the take out section called "The Dugout".  They have full array of food to go, as well as a large selection of 6 packs and individual cans for carry out up until 1am.  I am a "beer snob" and am very pleased with the large selection they offer.   This is one of the few places in the area you can go if you suddenly decide you need 2 slices and a 6 pack at midnight.
The bar itself is your typical neighborhood sports and hangout bar.  It gets  very crowded and rowdy on weekends and during Eagles games- good luck getting a seat.  The crowd is mostly under 30 but there are a few old heads here and there.   It seems to be the popular spot for all the local union (plumbers, carpenters etc) workers.  
Its probably best to check out for the first time on a weeknight as the weekend is crowded with what seems to be regulars.   They claim to be the best place around to watch the Eagles, but I've never gone in due to the wall to wall crowds on game day.
I haven't had enough of the food to fully review it, but its decent enough.  Its your typical pizza joint fare.

Best raw bar around.  Be sure to try the boiled shrimp; you'll never eat boiled shrimp anywhere else again, Tim is the master.  The staff, both bar (Lillian) and table service (Kevin and Rich) are amazing.  This place has its fair share of tourists but don't let that scare you off.  All food is top notch...when we're not eating the raw bar our go to items are stuffed oysters, gumbo, flatbread, Brussels sprouts and ribeye but you really can't go wrong with anything.  Check out happy hour for great deals.

We stopped by this little historic setting restaurant for a late night snack after checking in at our hotel. The ambience, atmosphere and the crowd just showered us with what we came to this creole city for. From the wood carving details at the bar where we sat because tables were not available on Sunday night without a reservation to the pulley driven row of fans with decorative ceiling as a backdrop, the gem of a find set us on the right mood for the Big Easy good times. We split the order of delicious shrimps with grits and sumptuous ginger bread á la mode on hot skillet dessert which were catered by the attentive servers at the bar while watching the oyster shucking show on the side. It's Mardi Gras time in our tummies!

Enjoyed a terrific business lunch at Luke where we dined on rabbit pate with chutney, marmalades and pickles. The pate was bursting with rich flavor and filled me up for what feels like a week! Similarly, the crawfish bisque was velvety with texture and overfilled with bite sized portions of crawfish meat in a creamy broth. Luke is a wonderful blend of casual and serious diners enjoying food in a category of its own.

Came here specifically to get the Le Grand Plateau de Fruits de Mer--- an amazing seafood tower with it came 1 whole Maine lobster, 16 oysters, 16 shrimp, 16 mussels, 10 clams, crab (with the king crab legs!) and ceviche. On top of that, we were there for the $.75 oysters during the happy hour from 3-6----- did I mention half off draft beers, glasses of wine and cocktails? We ended up ordering another 2 dozen oysters to go with our tower. 

Service here was outstanding- we had two servers who helped each other out, and were great. This place has the look and feel of a fine dining establishment without being pretentious--- perfect since you'll be in the middle of eating with your hands are you're cracking crab legs.

I didn't think it would be possible to be sick of seafood, but us three girls couldn't finish that massive tower and had to leave 5 shrimp behind. Not too shabby though considering the size of that thing! I would definitely recommend this place--- especially if you're in the Midwest and have few choices for decent seafood.

By far the smallest store of theirs I've been to & I've been to five.
Went to upgrade my hydration pack and was helped by a young lady that was very knowledgeable. Though their Camelbak selection is fairly limited in favor of Ospery.

I love chipotle. However the staff is rude. They get you through the line quickly but they aren't personable. Also this location is constantly out of something, bowls or rice or  plasticware, it's always something. I only come to this specific location because I its convenient for me. But if I can ever go to a different location I do.

Amazing service! Our bartender serves the drinks with fresh strawberry lemonade, made to order. I recommend the vodka strawberry lemonade or the spicy margarita of you like spicy. The crab au gratin and the duck & andouille gumbo were really delicious!
2 of my precious dogs passed away in the hands of seven oaks vet please second guess taking your animals there

Besh's casual spot was fine for brunch. 3.5 stars

Food: 4, service: 3, atmosphere: 3
Cost to worth it rating: 2.5 ($13 for ham and cheese sandwich, $22 for eggs in a jar)
Return worthiness: maybe 

Highlights:
- Eggs in a jar: literally just that but with large shrimp in a very thin breading hanging off the edges of a wide mouth glass jar
- Ham and cheese sandwich: cheesiest I've seen with the top of the thick slices of bread smothered in bubbly cheese. Impressive presentation coming out on a wooden cutting board
- Happy hour: one during the late afternoon with cheap oysters and drink specials while seated in the restaurant--not just at the bar

Midlights:
- Gumbo: nothing too tasty or special 

Lowlights:
- Waiter didn't see around too much so hard to get something when you needed it

Main food items were great, but something seemed to be missing from an atmosphere and service perspective to make it a complete experience for me. Still love Besh so will keep trying his spots.

Thanks to the Yelp reviews, I found about the happy hour special here! There is no happy hour menu on paper but they offer $0.75 raw oysters and $1.25 fried oysters during happy hour. Awesome offering and really enjoyed coming here! Very professional and efficient service in a nice setting. The oysters were very fresh. Cocktail sauce accompanies the raw oysters and a spicy ranch sauce comes with the fried oysters. They also serve complimentary bread which was hot and fresh. Highly recommend Luke!!

As a former PSC member (very fancy, lots of amenities) I have to say, I'm a born again Retro enthusiast.   

If you're looking for spinning, the spandex-set, the latest quasi- Martial art "fitness" classes, and swedish deep tissue massage, keep looking.

Retro offers a nice variety of cardio equipment either with its own TV or in the movie room.  I've never been out of luck with regard to machinery.   The weights set up seems adaquate (I'm not the most knowledgable) and the personal trainers are there if you want them but not pushy.    

Best of all, is the movie room.   Really,  I know it sounds cheesy; but in addition to new releases, they show great classic movies.   Running across Middle Earth or along with Indiana Jones is an awful lot of fun. 

This location is very family oriented.   You're just as likely to see boomers in T shirts and grandmoms doing kettle bells as you are fit 20 and 30 somethings.    It doesn't have the "pick up bar" ambiance that so many gyms suffer from.   People are just there to work out, which is SO refreshing.     The ladies locker room is spotlessley clean, I can't speak for the mens. 

Classes are offered to learn about the equipment on Saturday mornings.  (free with a sign up) 

I've only removed one star because they keep trying to sell me tanning packages.   Pasty of this calibur is a commitment.   Respect.

Second time, we went there. I dont know if its just me or what,  first time is always better than second. I loved their seafood udon, so i ordered it again, i think they put too much soy sauce in there. It was little too salty. Hibachi chicken dinner size was not worth of $19 at all.. (i will add pictures) plus we ordered two special rolls. They were ok. Overall, ok experience.

Review is based on Happy Hour Deals only!!!

Located right next to the Hilton on St. Charles. Dropped by for happy hour (3 PM-6 PM every day) on a Monday night. We arrived around 5:45 PM and were seated right away, the restaurant wasn't busy.

Happy Hour deals are raw oysters are 75 cents each, fried oysters are $1.25 cents each, and half off drinks! We got a dozen of the raw oysters, a dozen of the fried oysters, and two cocktails.

Oysters were mixed between big and small, but all fresh nonetheless. Fried oysters were a hit, especially the sauce, but I still prefer the raw over them. The restaurant is nice, great atmosphere, and plenty of indoor lighting.

4 stars because I would say there are better happy hour deals out there (Samuel's Blind Pelican), but still a great experience overall. Would come back here if I wanted to feel fancy!

I could not be happier with this company. Our 45-year-old heater finally died during the coldest week of the year. Rob came to our house within a matter of hours. He knew what he was talking about, as he was able to provide a temporary fix but we all knew it was time for a replacement. We were given an extremely competitive price and had a team at our house the next morning. The guys were all wearing masks, laid protective coverings, and offered us space heaters upon arrival. They were incredibly professional, communicated with is throughout the entire process, cleaned up beautifully, and we're actually finished a little earlier than anticipated. We will be using them from here on out, and I will happily recommend to friends. Thank you so much for your excellent service, professionalism, kindness, and wonderful work.

I had an issue with my online order the manager went above and beyond to help me and correct it. I can't say home nice it is to have great customer service. The online order was quickly fixed and my second order was perfect.
Good oysters. Good service. Outstanding selection of bourbons and rye whiskeys. Friendly fast service.  Corn and crab bisque excellent.

Review is purely for their happy hour.

$.75 oysters were out of this world delicious. I eat a lot of oysters in SF (when I can afford it) and having it at Lüke has changed my views on oysters forever. I did not know oyster meat can be so sweet and structured. Every one was super fresh and delicious. The complimentary bread was also really good! We tried a few of their cocktails and all were strong, not overly sweet, and made really well. Also, sometimes they have $5 Irish coffees (!!!) and it was one of the best irish coffees I've had. A must in NOLA.

PLEASE READ BEFORE EVER BUYING A CAR FROM HERE. I bought a Cadillac CTS from these guys 5 DAYS AGO to find out after 3 days of it sitting in the shop that it has a bad transmission. The worst part about it is that the salesman John knew!! I felt it during the test drive, I asked him about it and he told me "it was normal, that's just what cadillacs do!!" Then, after asking him, he only let me take the car for a block long test drive because HE KNEW as soon as the transmission heated up, I would feel it and therefore, NOT buy the car. What an absolute joke. Then, John sits there and tells us how happy he is that it is me buying the car, he wouldn't want it to go anywhere else, yadi yadi ya. I felt good about it. I felt like John was a genuine guy. Well, I was wrong. No morals, no respect, no integrity and not a care in the world what happens to you or that car when it leaves the lot. I was also told BY JOHN that the "owners don't give a sh*t, they don't even live in FL." I'd fire him if it was my car lot and one of my employees said that about me!! Especially after the customer just spent CASH money. All I wanted was for them to do right by me, as they should, seeing that I literally haven't even put 20 miles on the car before finding out it has a bad transmission. ESPECIALLY after he straight up and knowingly lied to me. This company would rather ruin someone's life than to just rip up the paperwork or put me in something else. Like they need the money more than us, yaknow? It's very sad and it's a shame. How could you work for people like that? Do not let these people get away with the same thing against you!!! This isn't the first time. And now that I read more and more stuff about this company... It's not the second, third, fourth, or fifth either!! This place does not value YOU as a paying customer whatsoever. I will NEVER EVER be back and Niether will anybody that I ever come in contact with. This is PINELLAS AUTO BROKERS. Not the "one across the street." Don't let them fool you!! Also, I highly encourage you to scroll past the few "good" comments that are below this review!'
Everyone was so friendly, and the food is insanely delicious. Definitely order the truffle baked chicken!

Came here while on a business trip -- it was fantastic.  I ordered the steak and it was one of the best steaks I've ever had and for only $35.  Well worth it. To be honest, the rest of the meal (apps and dessert) were not that memorable, but overall I would come back.

I wish I remembered to take pictures! The food, the staff and the ambiance were all great. 

1/2 of the tables were empty as they adhered to social distancing for all guests. They had signs advising that masks were required for entry & masks/gloves were required for staff. 

We ordered the spinach & crab artichoke dip w/grilled bread for the appetizer and it was so deliciously creamy. There were chunks of artichoke with a nice melted layer on top of the cast iron dish that it's served in. We also ordered fried oysters. They were piping hot & served in a mini deep fryer basket. Admittedly, I am not a huge oyster fan, but wanted to try new dishes on vacation. They were seasoned well and tasted like fried liver to me, so it you're into that, they will be great. My partner loved them. 

For dinner I ordered the Bacon Avocado salad w/grilled shrimp & it was oh so good. The bacon "bits" were huge and tasted great. They were a bit salty, so I opted not to eat as many when I reordered the salad (I ordered this 3x while we were in town). 

My partner ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp & Grits & it was great as well. He's typically a heavy eater and wasn't able to finish his dish. 

They had a nice Pinot Noir (I don't remember the brand) that was great. Sweet, but semi dry. We were told that happy hour was closing & ordered 2 glasses of bourbon to wrap up our meal. 

The only reason I gave them 4 stars is because the table near us found a bug on the wall during our meal. The staff addressed it immediately & appeared to be very attentive to the couple who was disturbed by their uninvited guest. However, even they said, "you're lucky the food was so damn good." It really appeared to be an isolated incident & the staff seemed to take every necessary precaution in the reopening since COVID. 

Because they are directly across from our hotel (The Intercontinental), Luke was our go to for the entirety of our stay. We came back to order the salad several times, the Luke Burger, Dark Chocolate Torte & Brenden's Bread Pudding. All were delicious & packed carefully to go. This will definitely remain a NO staple for us.

One of my favorite restaurants when visiting NOLA!!!

Came here for their happy hour - we ordered a dozen raw oysters, half dozen fried oysters, and a glass of wine each. It was sooo worth it. The raw oysters were cleaned very well (barely tasted a piece of sand whatsoever). My boyfriend was a huge fan of their fried oysters - they were so fat and juicy!! The texture was just so scrumptious. It was also my first time trying fried oysters, and it did not disappoint. 

Also of note, is their bread. Although it is compliment, it was SO GOOD. Warm, and soft, and chewy, I could have eaten the bread as a meal. But maybe I'm just a bread fanatic. 

Anyway, muuuuust give this place a try!!
Plenty of help but disorganized.  Out of white rice and napkins.  Lettuce was "bottom of the barrel".  Hopefully it's better if we come back.   My kids love this place.

Food was great. Service was rude and dismissive. From the dining room manager down to the host, everyone seemed to be bothered by our presence. The only nice person was the brand new busboy who was very nice and accommodating. Not sure if I will be back. There are other better food options in New Orleans with less surly staff.

Came here for lunch with the ladies and we were seated immediately since we had reservations .good service considering they were understaffed and super busy. The team of servers were responsive and incredibly gracious. Appetizers were delicious and my entree perfect.

We had dinner at Luke's last night. Loved the food: we started with Luke salad; the gumbo was excellent and the rabbit chicken liver pate pleased even my kids. The entrees are quite sizable: my teen kids split the burger and could barely finish it. My husband and I shared the shrimp and grits dish and took a doggie bag home. 

The only reason I gave 4 stars was that the service felt a little too rushed. Don't get me wrong: it is better than having to wait for a hour between  your appetizer and the main course. But we could barely enjoy our pate and I had to ask the waiter to slow down.

This was the first stop on our trip to NOLA - faaaan-effing-tastic way to get the first vacation of 2013 started ;) 

Initially, the plan was to head to Acme Oyster House, since it was just downstairs from where we were staying at the Astor Crowne Plaza, but the review of my good friend and fellow Korean foodie Vivian J. touting Luke's as the best raw oysters she had while she was in NOLA, changed my mind.  Not to mention that 50 cent price tag during happy hour - SAY NO MORE, I shall come and gladly slurp up as many of these incongruously delicious shellfish as my stomach can handle! (why do I say incongruous?  well, think about it. oysters, in appearance and texture, are not exactly the most appetizing thing ever... whichever brave soul decided to slurp down these shining gray booger-esque morsels of deliciousness.. I salute you and thank you.)

The oysters at Luke's? Huge. HUGE. The closest equivalent happy hour we have in LA are $1 at Enterprise and they are completely rink-a-dink compared to the one at Luke's. Not only that, but they were perfectly balanced and briny - so tasty, especially with a dash of minuet sauce, horseradish and Tabasco! I was planning on gorging myself but found that I was content after about a dozen or so.  (I was content.. But that didn't necessarily stop me)

We also ordered some of the main entrees to try, including the charcuterie plate, shrimp and grits and the fried oyster salad.  

The fried oyster salad was fantastic, with the oysters having jsut the right amount of breading and the avocado adding a nice creaminess to offset it.  The bacon was a nice addition but it made it just a bit too salty for my tastes.

I'm not very well-versed on charcuterie, so I don't think my opinion on that would be very helpful.  Shrimp and grits, though.. I had to basically ju-jitsu my friend Sophia to wrestle this dish from her, since she loved it so much.  Understandably so - some of the best grits I've ever had.  Buttery, creamy, salty, and perfectly complemented by the spicy, flavorful shrimp.

We also had some happy hour cocktails - I shared the New Orleans streetcar and the French 75 with another friend.. Both delectable!

Just a fantastic happy hour and a spectacular start to our NOLA trip!

Last "supper" in New Orleans  - Tuesday before heading to the airport, we grabbed 
Lunch at Lukes - John Bash' restaurant in the central business district. We glad we did. While I have the worst  time choosing dishes in NOLA that are meat -free and somewhat healthy, John's lunch menu was great. We started with fresh oysters, which were as fresh as they come and pretty huge in size. In fact, the fresh seafood bar is on display and its an impressive sight as you as you walk into the door. 
We loved the Louisiana shrimp with jasmine rice - just to make sure to get extra rice to soak up all that goodness. That's what soulful, southern cooking is all about to me - flavors and comforts, not grease and pork. 
Service was ahh, whatever, there seemed to be a general nonchalant attitude. Nothing terrible, no rudeness, just that sort of ahh, whatever, they didn't clear the oysters plate when the rest of the plates came. When I wanted more rice, I couldn't get the waiter's attention, even though there was only another table. Perhaps it's the high afternoon heat that generally puts everyone in a sleepy haze. The food was excellent and the lunch was the best value we have experienced in New Orleans.
Best happy hour in NOLA! Can't beat the half price cocktails, glasses of wine, and wells. 6 fried oysters for 10 dollars! A must stop anytime your in town.

Think of fancy meets good ol' southern comfort food! Wow this restaurant was nothing small. The have two dining rooms with great music and fresh oysters from multiple locations. We started with some oysters that were from two different locations. The service was great and it worthy of mentioning our service Ricky was super down to earth and very welcoming. He knew the menu items like the back of his hand. He recommended we try the crawfish soup so I had a cup of it... mouth watering! Side tip: get the fresh bread they provide... its perfectly warm and excellent for dipping with the soup. We ordered the prime rib steak. Note to those that are foodies: this is a 12oz steak and because of the marbling, it will be a little small to share with two people. We also ordered the Luke Burger. Perfectly cooked a medium rare. This was a monstrous burger and was full of flavor. The side of fries were crispy and Cajun seasoned. Now on to the top of the table, I personally ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte"... heaven in the South on a plate! The plate comes Jumbo shrimp with grits, melted cheese and roasted jalapeños (not spicy by the way) and green onion sausage. This is probably one of the best dishes I've tried in a very long long time! Check this place out.. I promise you won't be disappointed!
I am very understanding but poor customer service I understand the owner is a vet and loves his Marine vets sad to say his staff is far from respectful "I am a former Marine and would not come back

Good food. Mediocre service: ask about specials ( before 6 pm), they may not tell you, ask them to repeat your order, because they may forget about some of it. Ask them to repeat details ( if you want to make some changes to your meal), because they may not be able to remember. Produce is fresh. I can't tell you about my fish order, sorry, they just forgot about it.

W were here for Brunch on Daturday. Delicious Chicken and Waffles. My husband and I shared chicken and waffles and a Luke burger. The burger was good too,, but the Chicken and Waffles were delightful. I had a French 75 drink it was also very tasty. My husband had a Bloody Mary. It had a touch too much horseradish for him, If you like a lot of horseradish, you'll like the Bloody Mary

The staff was friendly and it was very close to our hotel. So all around a win, win.

My opinion of the Elm cafe is simple, it's delicious and original. The endless comments on the attitude of the baristas was shocking. I have been there a few times and they were nothing but helpful and polite. I'm going to continue to support the Elm cafe and assume the people who have problems with the service are either drama queens or have entitlement issues. Just keep up the great work!

My friend Reggie worked here as a personal trainer for a while and I stopped in here to visit him a few times. I was impressed with the design of the gym and he gave me a compelling pitch on all the details of the gym, so much that it convinced me to come here if I ever wanted to work out. I've also heard great things from a few friends that came here too. Unfortunately I do not have as much time as I want to get to the gym, but if I ever did this would be my first choice and one day I look forward to joining!

This place was okay, we were looking forward to the dinner here and really wanted to like this place. As other yelpers have suggested the food here is nothing to rave about. The decor is welcoming and the service was nice. We were checked on frequently throughout our dinner. Ordered the brussels sprouts for appetizer and I have to agree they were just too sweet and there was not enough green chili to balance it out. Also, orders the chicken the potatoes were delicious and chicken was soft but the seasoning was just okay. Also ordered the salad and the golden beets were again done very sweet and the balance is flavors were missing. The matzo ball soup had no flavor in it, and the dessert the yellow cake was so dense and hard that you would need a knife and a fork to get through it. I will go again to see if other things are good on the menu, but won't be my first choice.

First meal during our stay in NOLA and it did not disappoint. We came in on a Thursday evening and the place was somewhat busy, but we were able to be seated right away. Tables were spread apart. We lucked out in a corner so I felt comfortable dining indoors. 

Food was fantastic! We picked Luke's based on Yelp reviews and distance from our hotel so we are happy how it panned out. Oysters were large and fresh. I was surprised by the number of Mussels I got (felt never ending, but in a good way!) and the sauce was very flavorful. Our server did not hesitate on recommending the Shrimp and Grits and we thoroughly enjoyed that as well. Definitely recommend this restaurant to others!

Good but maybe a little over hyped. I got the Brussel sprouts and the shrimp and grits. The sauce on the sprouts is overwhelming. Too sweet and too spicy. And the shrimp and grits the same, too saucy. A little goes a long way.
Coolinary menu is awesome. Great place.  Frankly among the top two or three restaurants in New Orleans IMHO

Lüüüke!! I love this place so much. 50 cent oysters, 1/2 priced happy hour drinks for your liking, hand cut fries. Not the most expensive John Besh restaurant, but still a bit pricey. Worth every penny. Delicious food typical of any Besh restaurant. Parking is annoying. Staff is attentive and polite though and the burgers are so very good. Only the best ingredients used, and it tastes that way as well. My only complaint is that they shove a lot of tables in the restaurant and some are almost literally in the kitchen. The line of orders up are simply facing the other direction from the tables. I don't care though. I love it here! Classy burgers and fries, what's better than that?! Dress casual or dress it up, you're still dressed appropriately. (I should mention, it's more than burgers and fries. It's simply American food, presented in an upscale package, by a world famous chef, who hosts a comfortable yet fancy atmosphere. Love Lüke!)
Delicious, fresh, authentic sushi and sashimi, excellent service, and nice ambiance.  Very highly recommended.  (We have not tried the hibachi - yet!)

Thank you Lüke (and John Besh) for showing me what red beans & rice could and should be! We ordered a daily special of Tabasco Fried Chicken served with red beans & rice. The chicken was good but not the star of the dish. The red beans and rice packed so much flavor, superb seasoning & porky goodness that I will never think of them in quite the same way ever again!!! 

The oyster shuckers work very hard here & do a superb job! The $0.75 cent oysters during happy hour (3-6pm) are enormous, super sweet, tasty & served with a side of horseradish that will give you a head rush! We managed to eat a lot of those during our recent visit to New Orleans. And the Hopitoulas IPA on tap was also half off during happy hour. 

It's a great little spot to squeeze into for some delicious food, fresh oysters or a drink. It's not a large space and can get pretty packed.

Had lunch here on Christmas Day. It was absolutely and crazily busy. I'd give my experience there a 3 or even 2 stars; but considering they had to work on Christmas day to wait on a bunch of tourists or lazy people who didn't want to cook for themselves, i am willing to give it a break. 
That said, with so many wonderful and innovative restaurants in Nawlins, I don't see myself coming here again.

I'd give Luke a 3.5 stars overall, so opted to bump it up to 4.  Food was great, but I wasn't too crazy about the space and they were way understaffed when we went.

Went here my 2nd night in New Orleans when in town for business.  Our party of two was seated right at our reservation time, but then we had to wait quite a while for our waiter.  She finally came, and was super nice and sweet (and new we found out).  She took our drink order, and then left us to look over the menu.  We had plenty of time to decide, because the drinks took like what felt like forever.  I think it was at least 10-15 minutes.  That's much too long in my opinion.  She came over a few times to say they were coming, but I guess the bartenders were so backed up they weren't making the waiters drinks.  The place was rather busy, but didn't seem so full that they shouldn't be able to pour a few glasses of wine quicker than they did.  Even though she was new, she was very knowledge about the menu and was able to answer all our questions and give some pointers.  

We started out with a half dozen Jumbo Shrimp ($11).  They were served on an ice platter with cocktail sauce and lemons, and were very jumbo and sweet and good!  You do have to peel them, which is totally fine by me, but I know some people hate having to touch or do anything with their food.  I got the crabmeat maison salad with 
fresh herbs, local greens and country bread croutons.  This was delicious!  The country bread croutons were thinly sliced crostini pieces that came in a cute little container along side the salad plate.  The crabmeat was sweet and there was just the right amount of mayonnaise (not too much) for my liking.  My friend got the roasted beets salad with Bayou blue cheese and spiced pistachios.  She wasn't too impressed.  It was 95% lettuce, and a very few thinly sliced beets on the bottom.  It didn't have anything to make it interesting.  

We ordered a second drink, and it too took forever to come.  We also felt like we waited forever in between courses.  The bottom line was the kitchen and staff were just too busy to get things moving.  The manager was well aware, because she was circling the dining room trying to check in on everyone and make nice since quite a few people were looking around for their food and drinks.  I will say the waitress was super apologetic about it and at least acknowledged that the wait times were rather longer than they should be.

We finally got our main courses, and they were delicious!  On main courses, I'd give this place a 4 out of 5.  I got the shrimp and grits ($22) with delicious little bits of andouille thrown in for good measure.  It was served in a small cast-iron skillet and was piping hot and buttery and good!!!!  I could've eaten a whole giant cast-iron skillet of it!  The andouille was the perfect thing to contrast the buttery shrimp and grits. My friend got the smoked pork shank, Mangalitsa belly & bratwurst, with house-made sauerkraut ($23).  Both of our mouths dropped when this got delivered.  If you've ever been to Germany, this plate was exactly what you get in every bar.  A GIANT pork shank, with tons of other pork products.  It was so big she didn't even know how to start tackling eating it.  The sauerkraut was very interesting.  it was really quite sweet, but both of us liked it.  It was just different than normal sauerkraut.  The pork shank was perfectly smoked and had great flavor and tenderness.  The sausage was also delicious, and of course pork belly is always good.  Talk about a rich dish though.  My goodness!  And talk about seriously large portions...she didnt' even come close to finishing the meal.  I think a table of 3 could've shared this as one entree and been fine.  For reals.  it was big. 


We were so full we couldn't even look at the dessert menu.  We had also been there for so long we were tired and wanted to go home.  I think it was over 2 hours for dinner, which is totally fine when you're in that mood, but neither of us really were.  The timing was very off, but if you're there on a not busy night, I bet you'd love it!  

I also thought the pricing was very good for what you get.  The wines by the glass options were extensive too, and they do them all by the glass or 1/4 or 1/2 carafe.  That was a nice touch.

HAPPY HOUR! HAPPY HOUR! That's the absolute best time to visit LUKE... reason why? 75 CENT OYSTERS. No this is not a drill, delicous huge raw oysters sold for a tender 75 cents each which equal 9 dollars for a whole dozen for my math challenged friends. As soon as I found out about this I knew we had to check them out (we stayed at the adjacent hilton). anndddddd happy hr is from 3-7 every day can you really get better than that?

We actually visited twice in our short 4 day trip to NOLA. Both during HH. 1st visit it was just me and my boyfriend. we were able to snag two seats at the bar and we ordered a dozen oysters. I also got a glass of wine as it was half price during HH. The oysters came out so quick it was insane. Already plated with  the oysters were horseradish and cocktail sauce. They were perfectly shucked and we slurped them down with huge smiles on our face. I knew we had to come back, just to make sure it wasn't too good to be true.

Second visit was today. We had to head to the airport but had time to kill before our flight which was during HH so got 2 dozen oysters today. We were with my boyfriends sister. She does not like oysters, but under pressure tried one and even admitted "they are not that bad". she ordered matzo ball soup. Again- our oysters came out extremely quick (quicker than her soup actually) just as amazingly delicious as the first visit. She did not really like her soup, but really just get the oysters.

I cant say enough about this place and their amazing deals, if in NOLA make at least 1 trip to LUKE during happy hr, you will not regret it.

Best meal we had in New Orleans.  Started off with great bread and butter, and things only escalated from there.

Our server was an enthusiastic young man with a jaunty walk and ("Now if y'all are asking about the bread pudding, It wouldn't be right if I didn't tell you there was another dessert I preferred better. It's a steamed chocolate, we got a machine that steam-cooks things, topped with a scoop of salted caramel ice-cream, drizzled with caramel sauce").

Goat Cheese stuffed Squash Blossoms: 4 stars
This was recommended by our server.  Soft tempura-fried squash flowers served with aromatic garnishes and a Georgia peach chutney.

Jumbo Shrimp en Cocotte: 5 stars
It's a small portion served in a little iron dish and cost $24...  but is probably the best shrimp and grits in the country.

Bread Pudding:  4.5 stars
Heavenly spongy pudding topped with a fat scoop of vanilla bean ice cream, and butter pecan caramel sauce in the saucer.  It was so delicious, we ended up having this interaction:

[Only a drib of bread pudding remained in our ramekin]
Server:  Let me get that out of your way...
me:  No!!!
Server:  Oh, okay!  [backs away]
Partner:  Wow, you were really fierce.  I think he was afraid for his life.
me:  No, I wasn't!  I'm completely normal!
[Five minutes later the dish is licked clean]
Server: Can I take it away now? You're not gonna spoon-stab me or anything?
-- my partner's highlight of the trip

Just go eat here.  It's fantastic.

Loved the etouffee and the shrimp and grits.  Our party of 5 had a great business dinner together (with 2 bottles of wine among us), and the check was reasonable.  Lively and jovial, but not too loud to have a conversation.

Service was less than stellar (seldom refilled water, which was primary beverages) and food was ok. Not horrible, but expected a bit more considering the reviews. With limited time in town, not a restaurant we want to give another chance.

Fresh seafood, creative rolls, Szechuan Seafood soup is delicious. Small place in strip mall. Reservations recommended. It's a BYOB and conveniently there is a pub with a good beer selection and a State store for your wine and Sake in the same shopping center.

Luke's was recommended by some friends. We arrived and were seated in the busy dining room. Was thinking, great energy, boisterous noise level, bustling service staff. ...this could be good.
Server came over and said there would be he and another taking care of us,,,, Ordered a cocktail and perused the menu. A classic bistro menu, lots of choices,,

We ordered a gumbo and a flatbread,,,first spoonful of the gumbo, a mushy/soft shrimp in a broth that tasted like old seafood. The flatbread was ok, but nothing to write home about. 
We really wanted to order a bottle of wine, but couldn't get the attention of our server. We asked the food runner if he could send over the server for a wine order------10 minutes later we ordered a bottle of Gigondas, it was served when we were done with our apps. I also asked for some bread at this point, noticing that every other table around us had some.
Entree-  The duck breast came out medium rare, as I usually like it, but the breast itself was incredibly salty, as if had sat in a brine for hours.

We were never asked about our entrees, but I had earlier pointed out the bad shrimp in the gumbo, with very little to no response.

This experience was a complete departure from every other dining experience we had in New Orleans, very surprising. 

Well, it really shows what happens when a great restaurateur opens too many places. This place had been recommended several times by friends in the business.

Delicious tried three or four dishes from our large group - and they were all great! 

The French 75 I had was extra as well.

You land in a city that has a million happy hours. You land and you want great drinks and some oysters immediately. Would you always think of Lüke as the place to fit the bill? Maybe not but I am glad we did. 

We landed with just enough time to catch the last 30 minutes of happy hour. We aren't scruffy looking but I was a little worried since this place looks very nice. We walk in and notice no room at the bar but then discover that happy hour is for everyone no matter where you sit!  Hurray!

Kevin our amazing waiter come up to us and assures us he can get our order in before the end of happy hour (he was able to get us two rounds in)!  We did a dozen raw (75¢ each) and a dozen fried ($1.50 each I think). The most amazing thing happened. They were able to do gluten free fried oysters for my husband. He is sensitive not full celiac but he felt great after so either low or no gluten. Looks like they were fried with corn meal and they did mention they do a separate frier. They did mention if they are slammed it would be a long wait but we got our in minutes. Yay Lüke!

The oysters were amazing and the horseradish cleared out my sinuses like it should. 

We drank the Silver Saint (tequila, soda, lime, cucumber, Serrano pepper) and drank another immediately. They seem week but I promise they are not. 

We enjoyed it so much it was the only place we came back to on our 4 day trip and then we tried the Brussels sprouts. They are really amazing and I don't usually like them. I always try one but this batch had me fighting my husband for some. Maybe the honey in the sauce. 

We will be back Lüke and hopefully Kevin will still be able to help us!

Really welcome addition to the neighborhood. This is a really tiny little cute space--maybe just about 200 square feet--it's basically a long hallway with a storefront. Lisa, the owner and sole employee has made the most of it! I think I'm addicted. I go at least once a week now. I like the Chai (a house blend with fresh ginger added at brewing time). The "Cup of Sunshine" is great too (made with tumeric) and of course there are many other herbal options as well as traditional black teas. Did I mention she makes her own Earl Grey blend? Yes she does. Cupcakes made by Whisk are a bonus when in stock.

Cooks is a local, family owned and ran by family business since 1950 in the same location. They are wonderful to work with and they know their business as you'd expect after 63 years. If you need a mirror or glass for something check them out. I came to them with an idea for a wedding cake stand and they came through with flying colors. Today was no different. Just 2 minutes east of 465 & West Washington Street.

I was referred here for private lessons for my son. I called the front desk and spoke to two different people who were very unknowledgeable about pricing and services. I would not recommend this place, it's not worth the frustration. Many other country clubs in the area with better knowledgeable customer service !

Crawfish bisque was absolutely outstanding.  The Brussels Sprouts dish is in believable. The flavor is a tangy and sweet combined.  Can't believe it was a vegetable.  Next course was Shrimp and Grits.  Spicy but a great mix. Outstanding meal with great service.

Tried for the first time and found to be way over priced! Was charged twice as much as Qdoba charges me for the same thing. Qdoba has a lot more options as well. Maybe Chipotle is over charging trying to recover from all the law suits and the hundreds of cases of food poisoning caused by them in the last two years. Even a local mexican restaurant charged me $6 less than Chipotle did and the mexican restaurant gave gave free chips and salsa. NEVER AGAIN WILL CHIPOTLE RIP ME OFF!!! I highly advise to go elsewhere.
I've tried almost all the sushi places in bucks county and this is the best one I found.  Fresh, creative and beautifully presented.

So we came here twice, why?

Happy hour oysters.  $8 a dozen. Some
Of the biggest and juiciest I've ever had.  Service was great and a clean establishment.

I would come back in a heartbeat.  It's not touristy and off the beaten path so were good there.


Had the beet salad and corn/crab bisque and very good as well.

This is a MINT JULEP review, we didn't have food.

We got our Mint Juleps to go. 

In short, this is most likely the strongest drink you'll have in the French quarter. Every sip, felt weirdly good in the sense that you know you'll lost fine motor skills in your body but you can't NOT finish a Mint Julep. 

Come here when you're ready to be fancy drunk, as this is a fancy place.

Pro Tip: get your Mint Julep To Go! We went there on a Saturday afternoon and the place was PACKED! No sitting or standing room, simply go to the bar, get your drinks, enjoy a clean hotel bathroom and bounce!!!

When I made my 1st RETURN to New Orleans in OVER 20 years I searched and inquired from friends the best places to see, eat and drink... Lüke (like a few other places) had popped up in many searches and recommended by many fellow yelpers).... 

On our flight from Florida I locked in a reservation for a rather late night dinner (enough time to travel to our hotel, unpack and grab a pre-dinner drink... On the flight I also checked out the menu and pictures online and was impressed but was not expecting find more than one article rating Lüke as serving one of the best burgers in Louisiana... 

10 pm reservation on a weeknight and they were packed but our table was ready for us upon arrival.  The place is bright with impressive wood features like the eat-at bar and table partitions... the floors are should be for walking but they were drawing my eyes down to see the tile and wood inlay floors. The lighting fixtures and tin-ceiling tiles added to the charm. I also loved the way they displayed their seafood selection in a cold section at the bar.

I was very much in the mood to eat traditional New Orleans dishes like Shrimp 'N Grits or Étouffée, but I kept thinking of that burger so I went for it.... 

The Lüke Burger was legit.... bacon (glazed I believe), caramelized onions, tomatoes and emmenthaler cheese (I never heard of it either)... very pleased with my decision !

I also managed to steal a bite or two of their Shrimp 'N Grits (En Cocotte) which was absolutely spectacular !

Also enjoyed a Sazerac before dinner... they did New Orleans righteous with the city's signature drink
Went here right after they opened back up after COVID stay at home order. It was spectacular. Shoutout to Tanya who came by and made sure we were enjoying everything. We certainly were!
Great service! Gary/Larry/Steven was awesome. Pate was delicious, so was the pork schnitzel. Shrimp etouffee and shrimp and grits were reportedly good too! Casual and fun!

Richie Rich attended our table with lots of help and laughs for us Out of Town Folk. The food here is AMAZING! The Best dishes I think I've ever had!
Thank you to the staff for such Excellent service
We came here for happy hour, enjoyed some beautiful oysters and a huge Croque Monsieur.thankfully we split it!! Great service and friendly staff.
CAN WE SAY FRENCH 75!!!!??? That's about I have to offer for this review. Get the french 75 and I promise you won't be disappointed. PERIODT!!!!

Saturday night in Nola without a reservation. Tried Tranese across the street and was unsuccessful. We saw Luke across and thought we would give it a try.  Tried to make small talk with the hostess, without much luck.  She offered up a seat at the bar which my friend was not up for.  Said the wait would be an hour and a half for a table.  We were about to leave, and the manager called the hostess over, she said they could accommodate us, not sure what changed.  We were whisked away and seemed like we were heading for the kitchen.  The restaurant appears to be divided into two sections, we ended up in the rear section which overlooks the kitchen.  Which was o k as the restaurant really doesent have a view.  You could tell that the restaurant has been able to adjust for the throngs of people looking to dine post Covid.  But everyone there was hustling and commited to providing a good experience.  
We settled in and ordered a couple of cocktails.  And we're going to start with cooked oysters from the shared plates menu.  Until we learned it was $17 for 4 oysters.  We told the waitress that we needed a minute and she seemed irritated and said she would be back.  This may have been a mistake as we didn't see her for 20 minutes.  Once she got back we ordered we opted for half a dozen raw I think they called it PJ oysters, 2 cups of gumbo and as entrees my friend had the chicken and I opted for the pork cutlet.  
The food came quickly we got our oysters and soup at same time, I would have preferred a little bit of separation of time between oysters and soup.  The soup was good but Luke warm.  Oysters were fresh and tasty and $11 for a half dozen which I thought was reasonable. 
Entrees were large, could easily be split. My friend got a half chicken, nicely crisped potatoes, and some type of greens. Presentation could have been on larger plate, and chicken could have had a little more gravy but was tender and moist.  
My pork had two large breaded patties and a ton of perfectly cooked fries.  Both were on the well done side which I loved.  
Normally I would rate this a 3 to 3.5 star experience. However given the fact that manager got us a table, they were understaffed but everyone hustled, the food was tasty ,  with large portions and fairly priced I'm giving them 4 stars

10 stars!! Such an amazing meal. Have been here before but it has been a while. In town so I made reservations for 2 the same day. He had the shrimp and grits. I went with Luke salad, grits and we shared the sprouts. Everything came out so quickly and well cooked. There was bread for the short wait and received a second loaf with a smile. 
We got seating on the wall which I much prefer to the middle of the narrow restaurant where there is a tendency to get bumped a lot. 
Only suggestion is the same one I have for most restaurants. You have vegetarian options (pasta, rice) please put them on the menu/website. 
Well done - Can't wait to be back!
Had John Besh's signature Burger for lunch. I felt funny ordering a burger at a place this nice, but it's his award winner. Wonderful, best burger ever!!!!!
Came for happy hour 75 cent raw oysters. No wait to get seated, we were quickly in and out. Very satisfied with the oysters. Amazing meal for under $20 bucks.

I'm a huge fan of all things Chef Besh; he is a dynamo at menu creation and preserving the food heritage of the city. Having said that, I'm not above a fair critique of Luke. 

I can only get so many food opportunities in when we're in town so Luke has been on my bucket list for a while, waiting for the right time. On this stay, it was a short walk from where we were lodging and convenient for dinner after we got checked in. At 6:00 on a Wednesday evening the place was busy but not completely packed and we were seated promptly. The interior is beautifully comfortable, very French bistro-esque with charming black and white vintage tiles and gorgeous woodwork at the bar. Watching the staff was an exercise in fine dining perfection. The front-of-the-house manager and head waiter (I'm guessing) worked the floor with precision while also tending tables when needed as well as discretely guiding new staff on points of detail not to be overlooked. White-jacketed serving staff were welcoming, energetic, and polite and add to the posh old-school ambiance. 
In our particular experience this evening, there were just a few downsides. Despite amble wait staff, service to our table-for-two was fairly slow. It took a good 10 minutes or so to get our initial drinks after a bit of a wait for someone to bring water and take our drink order, explaining that So-and-so would be our server but he'd go ahead and get our drinks. Then another stretch of time before the (same) server came around so that we could place our smoked trout dip order, another stretch to place our entree order (same server), and another good wait before  my empty wine glass was noticed by the head waiter(?) and asked if I care for another. The trout dip was delish while just a tad over-salted, however to my hub it was perfectly fine. I usually ask him to weigh in to make sure as my tastes can be sensitive when it comes to saltiness; what is often very salty to me is well-balanced to others. It may due to back down on the salt to allow the diner to adjust at table, but I'm not going to be too critical here - overall, the dip rocked. The crackers served with were absolutely tasty all on their own and complimented the dip perfectly. 
For entrees, hubs ordered shrimp and grits and I went for the schnitzel. The S/G were very flavorful and decadent, however the amount of cheese used in the dish, while being a big selling point I'm sure, was absolute overkill imho and threw the balance off. Moderation on the cheese factor would make this dish outstanding. The gratin portion size is perfect for such a rich dish. My schnitzel leaned toward disappointment. While the flavor was very tasty, the pork juicy, and the breading substantial and nicely crisp, it was a bit over-browned and came sans a sauce/gravy of any kind giving it a dryness that a drizzle of a nice anything besides merely the juice of the grilled lemon half garnish would have improved. It comes served with a healthy portion of standard frozen thin-cut fries, another let down. Some good fresh cut side fries and a delectable sauce for the cutlets would make this dish shine. 
All-in-all I was almost in tears for finally getting to dine here and relished the fact that the slower service allowed me the time to take in the atmosphere and have a relaxing meal on our first night.

AMAZING. Food was delicious! Equality good was experience. Combination made it a true New Orleans evening. Stayed in the hotel and were to tired to walk around searching for something so popped in later in the evening without a reservation. Hostesses were so sweet about it  Had broiled fish and the most amazing dark chocolate dessert ever. Went back the second night after dinner at Galatoires to have the dessert again. Also had room service of fries one afternoon- so good. Manager so sweet and came and visited with us. Waiters Karl and Richy Rich were so absolutely amazing definitely ask for them.

Food was good overall, although some dishes were too salty.  

Very very loud, couldn't hear the person sitting across from me.  

Staff a bit overwhelmed by a conference crowd.  But made up for it by comping a 2nd round of drinks.

Hostess reading her phone as we exited, a thank-you would have been nice.

You should have seen the look on the bartender's face when I ordered 30 oysters all to myself. 

But perhaps I would have reacted the same way... These were pretty massive oysters and the platter on which they were laid out was practically larger than me. Why did I order so many oysters on an ordinary afternoon? If you saw their HH deals, you probably would too!

I don't think I had had such fresh and meaty oysters before. They were delicious, and paired really well with my half-priced glass of Austrian wine. This giant "appetizer" was so appetizing that I ended up staying for dinner, and I was not disappointed!

I had tried shrimp and grits at a few other nearby restaurants by that point, but I must say I liked Luke's version the best! 

At the other places, there was either too few shrimps, or the sauce was too salty, or it lacked flavor, or it was overcooked to an unappetizing mush. However, here, the shrimp and grits here were perfect in flavor, quality, balance, and texture. It's not a cheap dish, but tasted delicious and thoughtfully made, with roasted jalapeño cheese grits topped with andouille & green onion sausage and a good amount of jumbo shrimp in a flavorful sauce. 

Other delicious highlights were the rabbit and chicken pâté appetizer, as well as the bread pudding dessert topped with vanilla bean ice cream, hot buttered rum sauce, candied pecans (a.k.a. pure heaven in dessert form). Service was friendly and attentive. I definitely look forward to being back!

Recommended to us by a local. We came for the happy hour: 50 cent oysters and  half price drinks  made us quite happy. 

I asked for coffee and got a full carafe of terrific coffee. 

The service was great and the atmosphere was inviting. 

Attractively designed. 

One of my favorites on a recent trip.

The happy hour here is not to be missed!  The best deal in town from 3-6 pm!  Fantastic cocktails bursting with flavor, wines and beer all half price and fried or raw oysters that were the best in town for a dollar twenty-five a piece or less!  The restaurant is very classy with tablecloths and a beautiful tiled floor and it is my impression that they do everything well!  We will return!  Note to all: you can and should reserve a table for happy hour.

In a world of small plates to share, Luke is serving up big food.  There are starters to share (the Brussels sprouts are truly divine deep fried crispy goodness and they'll give you the recipe) but the main dishes don't mess around.  The schnitzel come with three large portions.  The drum is a huge filet.  The steak is enormous.  The chicken generous.  I'm assuming g the burger is even big enough to share.  All very good.  Come hungry and leave happy.

We had a group of about 20+ (all in town for a conference) and the service was UNBELIEVABLE - seriously, pay these people more, they were outstanding. We made it for happy hour (3-6pm) and ordered a barrage of food and drinks which included:

-Crispy Brussels sprouts
-BBQ shrimp toasts
-wild mushroom flatbreads
-pate and bread
-dozens and dozens and dozens of raw and grilled oysters at 75 cents each
-shrimp and grits
-other flatbreads
-I can't remember

I can't remember because drinks are half priced during happy hour, and that was an insane deal. Great cocktail selection.

A must for those stopping by New Orleans for the first time for both food and hospitality!
The best sushi in bucks.  Yummmmmmmmmmm. Fast n friendly service. Wish Covid was over so we could get something other then take out

This was my birthday celebration and another hotel guest said it was the best meal he had ever had. So we went. The menu is extremely limited. We were joking about how extensive it was. After reviewing the menu, my brother said he was going to order French fries(everything had French fries) and pudding! We asked our waiter if there were any specials to which he retorted, what you see is what you get. My husband ordered local oysters, which were billed as being large. Some were no bigger than a Nickel (okay less than a quarter but larger than a nickel) my sister in law ordered the PJ bbq oysters. There were four for $17. Pricey and you could not taste the oysters. I ordered the crispy Brussels sprouts. The saving grace was the honey drizzled on them. We all had drinks with our dinner. I ordered pork schnitzel ( menu had about five entrees and this was one)
Rather odd for a city known for Cajun food and seafood but nothing else looked interesting. The schnitzel was huge(two big pieces). Everything had French fries, which, I had no desire to have for dinner. I exchanged them for the cauliflower. This was barely warmed. The "mushroom gravey" came in a tiny container and was cold. My sister in law ordered the shrimp and grits. The sauce was thick, salty and obscured the taste of the shrimp.Our waiter filled water glasses but never asked how the meal was. He had words with (we assume), was the manager informing him he would not take any more tables to which the manager said that's fine because we are closed. Not something that helps digestion. We ordered another round of drinks. After a long enough period of time that the men in our group were going to cancel the order, a server(not ours) brought the men's drinks but not my wine. I asked if my wine was coming and the answer was no because they ran out of clean glasses! Now, most restaurants would have poured the wine into any acceptable container, brought it to the table and ask if I minded the same glass, explaining the situation. This young lady did not. I gave her my glass so they could "wash it" for future customers. She then asked if I wanted some wine in that glass. Too late not interested and done with the dismal dinner experience. Oh yeah, I forgot about boxing my meal. The manage boxed my meal. I asked to have the schnitzel and cauliflower boxed but not the gravy. He asked if I wanted new cauliflower. I said no just what I had. He boxed only my schnitzel and nothing else. I had to ask for cauliflower. For this wonderful meal, we paid 88 dollars before the  tip ( and yes, in spite of a bad experience, we still tipped the waiter)

My favorite place of ALL the restaurants we went to on our trip (and it was a lot)! What an amazing Happy Hour here:
 $0.75 Oysters! So fresh and large sized!
Chilled Shrimp that has been amazingly marinated. 
Chilled Mussels are a must have as well
CRAB & CORN BISQUE
SEAFOOD GUMBO Á LA CREOLE

It was also Friday and we're on vacation so we splurged on the Friday Special:
COURT-BOUILLON
REDFISH, CRAB, SHRIMP, OYSTERS, LOUISIANA POPCORN RICE

Just get it all. Everything was fantastic and we walked away with the smallest bill ever.

On my trip to New Orleans, I was on the search for good seafood and happy hour options because coming from Boston, happy hour doesn't exist! Lüke was the exact place I was looking for!

Lüke has happy hour from 3pm-6pm everyday. This includes 75cents P&J oysters, which are New Orleans local  and $7.50 for half a dozen of fried oysters and half off cocktails, beer and wine. 

New Orleans oysters are extremely fatty and delicious. Although I love New England oysters because of the super briny taste like I am tasting the ocean with every slurp, I still like the delicateness of New Orleans oysters. It comes with horseradish and cocktail sauce. I also tried the porchini and English peas agnolitti, which is like raviolis. It was so flavors and delicious. The pasta was aldente. The sauce was also super flavorful and tasty. I highly recommend this dish.

I also took advantage of the happy hour by getting a few drink. I got door#three and Pinot Grigio. Both drinks were amazing. 

Service here was over the top! Everyone was super polite, informative, and attentive. I would definitely come back!

Was very impressed with Lüke. The three of us shared a medium seafood starter, which had generous portions of oysters, crab legs, shirimp, etc. Very fresh and delicious. The main courses were excellent also (I had the minced boar). And the price /quality relationship was excellent. Good service, too.
This place stinks, small menu an slow service. Food is not worth the time.

One of my favourite spots for happy hour in the city, which runs from 3-6pm every day!! P&J Oysters are a $1 each and really fresh and sweet, although the fried oysters are my favourite. Their cocktails are also excellent (esp. door#3!!)
Great old style decor, the shrimp and grits was amazing, as was the bread pudding.  The wait staff is very attentive and goes above and beyond to make sure you're satisfied.

Excellent service, food was very good, menu is very limited, and way overpriced. If oysters is what you seek, this is their specialty.
