Fountain drinks come in bottles (Coke), so forget the free refills. The restaurant is located downtown, in the business district, so obviously they cater to business people who don't blink twice about paying $17 for a hamburger.

Happy to find this gem in my hood.  Elm is a nice tiny cafe you can easily miss with only 4 seats in the house.  I had the breakfast sandwich - something with zucchini, roasted peppers, spinach and a fried egg. Perhaps the reviews got me too excited,  I thought the sandwich was pretty good but nothing mind blowing.  I also had the latte, which was decent as well.  They have a promo going on where you get a free cup of coffee if you buy a bag of coffee beans on fridays.

Amazing surprise. 
The char-boiled version of their oyster is a must try ! We went in for a quick family dinner and didn't expect much but we were pleasantly surprised! Kids friendly and very welcoming staff. 
Good selection including a kids menu made it easy for us. The crawfish flatbread was excellent as well. 
Drink menu was below average but we will definitely head back here for dinner

Nothing posted on yelp is around. They change their menu very often apparently and that was a disappointment.

We ordered 2 dozen oysters and asked if we can try al 4 types, which are exactly the same price. He said no and wanted to charge us 4 halves.

I would have rated 3 stars but with the options around, it's not worth wasting the money here or time or stomach space.
Outstanding customer service. Jerry and Ryan were extremely helpful, friendly and fair. 2 thumbs up.
Stopped in here for a light, late dinner. I had the crab corn chowder and my husband had the gumbo. Both were really good, and hit the spot. We had the bread pudding for dessert and it was awesome!

My fave John Besh restaurant.  Doesn't hurt it's a stones throw from where I've worked for the past 5 years.  Besh came and totally revamped the space after Colbolt's didn't reopen.  He turned the space into the exact replica of a French bistro.  Their daily lunch special gives you an amazing lunch included with wither soup or salad for $15.00.  They also have a giant $16.00 burger before most other "fancy" places made the addition.  They have a great happy hour too.  I'm a little bias because I love French 75's.  They have nifty to-go cups with Besh branding of all his eateries.  Keep in mind it is connected to a hotel which can pose a problem during football season particualrly when it's a home game.  Regardless, I jump at the chance to eat here every chance I get.  On days I have to work on the weekend, I treat myself to breakfast here.  Why the hell not?!  I'm getting OT.

Being a franophile it makes sense that this is my fave Besh restaurant... but that aside, it's pretty freaking bad ass!

Best sushi I've had since I moved to PA and on the list for best ever. Highly recommend.  They cross hatched some of the pieces which leant them a texture I've never experienced before. The ambiance was stylish and relaxing and the manager Chris was great. They get fresh fish in every day and it shows. The fish in the display at the bar were glistening and the o-toro looks amazing. I'm going to go for that the next time I come. The prices are also amazingly reasonable for such high quality.
Food was amazing. Fresh and tasty. We were a big group like 7 and they were able to fit us in. Everybody ordered something different and nothing I had was less than stellar.

I went to Luke with a large group of friends during a very busy weekend in New Orleans.  We were all absolutely blown away by the food and the service

We started with the appetizer on special along with a Boudin and Oysters.  Everything came out in a reasonable amount of time and tasted phenomenal.  I had a gumbo before dinner that was also impressive, although a rather small portion.  As for entrees, every single one of us in our 8 person party got something different.  Many items were passed around and everyone was as into their own as they were the next.  

Next time I'm back in New Orleans and looking for a great dining experience, I'll be back!

I've been to Luke twice over the past couple of years, and I have never been disappointed. On this past trip, I brought my sister's bachelorette group, and we had the best experience. The waiter recommended the Brussel Sprouts, and we were in LOVE. We also got the crab dip which was delicious. I had the brandy milk punch, super aromatic and smooth,  and shrimp and grits, hearty savory, and delicious. The alcoholic frappe was strong but really yummy. Everyone was very happy with their food and the experience we had here.
We are so lucky Hachi is only 5 minutes away.  The very best Sushi and fried rice.  Try the Shrimp Tempura roll !

Full disclosure: I was hungover at brunch.

I know. How irresponsible of me, in New Orleans, on a bachelor party, to drink that much the night before. I say this not to sound cool because I party (still, I mean, guilty), but because my meal at Lüke (don't forget the umlaut!) was a truly amazing breakfast and I'd like to attribute that to the restaurant and not my then-state of malnutrition and dehydration.

Now, when you first see the menu, it's a bit overwhelming (again, let's assume this is not a side effect of drinking), and maybe even a bit expensive. But rest assured, it is money well spent - you will certainly taste the high-quality products they put in their dishes here.

I went with the seemingly straight-forward Southern Breakfast, soon realizing it was more of a Choose Your Own Adventure-type deal once the waiter started rattling off a series of this-or-that questions to me. Ultimately, I went with two (organic) sunny side-up eggs, some dude named Allan Benton's bacon (apparently, he's a big deal in the bacon world), a biscuit, and hash browns. That last item I honestly didn't see listed anywhere, not even as a side, but if I were you, I'd inquire about 'em, because they were the absolute highlight of my meal. The real surprise was that these taters came tossed with big chunks of super savory, tremendously tasty, thick-cut bacon. Of course, this kind of negated my Allan Benton's bacon pick. Therefore, fair warning, if you get the hash browns, choose the Chisesi ham (yes, Lüke likes to name-drop) or cane syrup sausage, if you want to try a different meat. Otherwise, hey, double bacon. Which is never a bad thing.

Either seeing how banged up our group of bros was on a Saturday morning and just figuring we were on a bachelor party weekend (correct, as we later confirmed with them), or Lüke has the most generous staff in New Orleans (could honestly be both of these things), we were brought over two bottles of champagne on the house to help us celebrate. We certainly weren't ordering extravagantly enough to deserve them, nor did our bodies particularly need 'em (please, we still drank up), but man, was that just a super nice gesture, much appreciated.

I will say though* that the strange layout of the restaurant was something I just couldn't get over during my meal. Typically I can ignore these things, especially when a meal is this good. But anyway, we were led to Lüke's back half, which was weirdly across a hotel hallway. It had the kitchen on display in what looked like a glass interrogation booth. And it also lacked the high ceilings and open feel of the front of the house, which came off as stately and very gastropub-y. This back room didn't come off as much of anything, and honestly just seemed like an afterthought, a place to put more patrons.

Still, strange second rooms won't deter me from making a repeat visit next time I'm in town. I'll just ask to be sat in the front half. And for more hash browns with bacon, please. And maybe some Aleve. Thanks.

*This means I'm about to sound like a dick right after the complimentary champagne comment, no matter how hard I try not to.

Centrally located right inside the Hilton - Luke's seems like a good idea. Its bustling, all the wait staff is nicely dressed and polite - but the food here is very average. 

Oysters had no flavor

Croque Madame - bread was stale, cheese was pungent and the ham taste like processed ham.

Don't get fooled by the crowd - the food is meager at best

Highly recommend to come just for oysters and cocktails. All my oyster were delicious! I've been here before years ago for them and I'm glad I tried again. This will be my go to spot for them.

Entree wise, roasted chicken was a waste. The chicken was very basic. I probably could get a better flavor one at Sams Club. The potatoes cubes just didn't make sense. As I tried to eat the dish I felt Unfulfilled. I should have trusted my gut and went with the hamburger.

Order an old fashion made with their well Bourbon and that was really food.
Stopped here for an oil change with a Groupon. Quick, no hassles, professional staff, and reasonably priced. Even clean restroom!
I absolutely love the FOODand the servers! it's a wonderful dining experience. Every tour should check out Luke's, you won't be disappointed

Really good place. Only been there once. One of the famous addresses in NOLA for visitors, but also locals. Pretty pricy with pretty high standards. Had the steak and fries but nothing else. Steak was really tasty and well cooked, buttery sauce was excellent. Only down point was the French fries which were not fresh, kinda disappointing for that price and a steak like this. But I will go back for sure next time I'm in town.

Great dinner at the bar since I was solo. Excellent Serbians food was great except my ribeye was a little too chill by the time it got to me. That's the only thing that kept me from giving 5 stars. Definitely will be back!

We arrived in New Orleans, Louisiana (NOLA) last Thursday afternoon the 23rd of May, 2019 for the Memorial Day long weekend. After a long road trip we were keen to get some food and try some local cuisine. We came across this restaurant Luke which was attached to our hotel. They have happy hour every day from 3-6pm on drinks and some of the seafood too. Bonus! We ordered a dozen of the P&J Raw Oysters at 75c each, 6 lightly fried Oysters and the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" with roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille and green onion sausage. All of these meals were shared between the two of us and the waiter was nice enough to have the Louisiana Shrimp dish plated into two individual servings as it's very filling. Overall we had a great dining experience at Luke, the atmosphere and service was fantastic also great value and very impressive food.

I had high expectations because Chef John Besh goes on Top Chef and gets to critique promising chefs, but I don't think his dishes at Luke would have succeeded on the show. 

For reference, we were a well dressed, party of 8 with reservations made two weeks in advance. 

Pro:
-Rabbit/Chicken Pate: It was a delicious pate that was served with mustard seeds, pickled watermelon, jalapeño/rasberry (i think) jam. Great flavors.
-Mint Julep cocktail has fresh and tasted nice

Cons:
-I ordered the second most expensive entree (Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en Cocotte" aka shrimp and grits) and was looking forward to a flavor explosion. It was served in a cast-ion casserole dish with a broken handle. I also noticed the portion looked small and like it was shoved to the right side of the dish (I compared it to the same entree that someone at my table was served. It looked like half the portion my friend received). There were also french fries in my entree, which didn't come with my dish, it just fell from other dish on the server's tray onto my dish. The server asked if everything looked good and I responded "No, my dish has a broken handle, my portion looks half of what someone else got, and I got french fries in my dish that don't belong in the entree". If this was a Chili's or some burger restaurant, no big deal, extra french fries, but I didn't know Chef John Besh was looking to create an upscale Popeye's. 
-Three of my friends ordered the grilled ribeye at different temperatures, but none were accurately served at the request temperature. The meats were not cooked consistently at the same temperature all the way through. Someone ordered medium, but the center of the ribeye was rare. 
-The service was really lackluster. The manager never came by to apologize about the shoddy plate they put in front of me.
-The bathroom was actually in the Hilton and it was messy. I don't know about y'all, but if I'm in a nice restaurant, the bathroom also has to be well-kept.
-It was my birthday dinner and my friends told the restaurant so they brought me out a dessert, but it said "Congratulations". I'm not sure what they meant by that. Congratulations you turned 30? It was just odd like they weren't paying attention and someone in the back was like "Oh, there's some occasion at that table. Write 'Congratulations' instead of asking what the occasion was". It just an example of lack of attention to detail from the famous Chef John Besh. 

The more I write this review, the more annoyed I am that our group dropped all that money at this "nice" restaurant which was basically a glorified Red Lobster.

OYSTER HAPPY HOUR AM I RIGHT?! I love eating raw oysters, but even more so when they're for a great price. We were seated in the back of the restaurant, which was probably one of the last available tables for our reservation time. As other Yelpers have noted, be sure to make a reservation during happy hour. 

Our server was fabulous and awesome and always seemed to be around and I wish I could remember his name because I loved him. There was another server who sometimes stopped by and took additional orders from us or refilled our waters periodically. 

Happy hour specials include 50% off glasses of wine,  beer and specialty cocktails, as well as $1.25 per fried oyster and $0.75 per raw P&J oyster. Our table was a graveyard of raw and fried oysters. My one complaint about the oysters is that the shells weren't cleaned very well, so when they stacked the oysters, some dirt got on the otherwise clean oyster meat. I rinsed it with my water.  The fried oysters were hot and crispy - do order at least half a dozen to try! I also ordered a French 75, which was not only 50% off but also a lot bigger than the French 75 from Arnaud's. 

We also ordered some apps to share, too. The hot buttered crawfish and burrata tartine was super rich but super tasty. Any dish with hot butter and burrata cheese in the title has my name on it! We also shared crispy sprouts, which were a tad undercooked. The flavor was on point but it definitely could have used a little more time in the heat. 

Overall, a tasty meal at a great price! Luke's is a must visit in NOLA during happy hour!!!

75 cents for oysters during happy hour? 

Well it's going to taste just like what it's charged for, 75 cents. I've eaten a lot of happy hour oysters in my life from varying cities.. DC, Boston, New York and this was by far the worst one but the cheapest one. 

I never thought you could screw up on food that's raw but clearly Luke has proven me wrong. 

There were broke shells in every slurp I took so my mouth was filled with raw oysters and shells each time I ate. 

The person who laid out the dish did a poor job, all the juices were gone. The oysters weren't laid properly so all the juice dripped out. One of the best things about raw oysters is the juice, it's what makes the crucial texture in raw oysters. 

I ended up having dried out oysters with bits of shell..

I decided to take a gamble with the fried oysters, not really that great either. It's just okay. 

I left wondering if it was fair for what I paid for, it was 75 cents a piece after all..

I love this little French bistro in the middle of the city. The french fries with truffle oil are worth the trip. It has a great atmosphere. If you sit in the back you can watch them cook. If you prefer to sit in the front it's very cozy and you feel like you are in France. The food is delicious!

Ambiance: attached to Hilton, relatively small dining area, very bright inside, full bar service

Service: half bad and half good, waiter was changed after the unpleasant experience from the first one, who stared at TV all the time and ignored our table, didn't serve us bread as other tables got, later another server helped, who was awesome from the very beginning before he was assigned. Since our original waiter was not in the mood to take care of us, I asked the second waiter questions about food on the menu and suggestions, he was very patient and friendly 

Food: overall good taste, not particularly extraordinary 
  Stuffed P&J Oysters - **** gulf shrimp and blue crab, very bold taste, recommend
  Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" - *** roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausage, the shrimp wasn't very fresh, but the grits was creamy and taste
  Tasso Rubbed Grilled Swordfish - *** fresh corn, fire roasted poblano peppers cilantro lime beurre blanc, very fresh fish, thick and chewy texture, the vegetables were very flavorful 
  Brendan's Bread Pudding - *** vanilla bean ice cream, hot buttered rum sauce, candied pecans, average taste

Price: medium portions and most items are on the pricey side, normally expect more than $30 per person

Luke's is always a joy.  Brought a couple of out of town guests in for dinner last Friday.  These guys are world traveled and always know the best places everywhere.  Growing up here, they had not eaten shrimp and grits.  Indulge me, I insisted.  Wellll, it was a home run.  From salad to desert, no complaints.  Hats off to the wait staff. My compliments to the chef.

Exceptional service, accommodating staff and delicious food. I ordered the goat cheese / beet salad and the honey tobasco chicken with red beans and rice. This is served as a Monday lunch special for $17 (the price includes a soup OR salad and entrée). Because I'm visiting from out of town, I missed the lunch slot and came here for a late dinner instead. The restaurant staff were nice enough to make the requested meal for me with the ingredients they had on hand. I have dined in many restaurants and have never experienced such friendly and attentive service - throughout the dinner, 4 staff members were tending to our table. Since I am pregnant and not drinking alcohol, the bartender created a fresh strawberry lemonade - ish drink, this tasted amazing and I reccomend you order it if lemonade is up your alley. Overall, a great experience at Luke.

Every time I come to New Orleans, I come here. If you can get in for the happy hour, that's the best bet but even if you miss it, it's worth coming here. The French 75 cocktail is the best I've ever had! We also love the oysters, they are always very fresh. My partner had the fried oyster salad which he loved. Everything we see that comes out of the kitchen looks appetizing.  Try it, you will not be disappointed!

Elm Cafe may be a small shop, but what it lacks in size it more than makes up for in quality and outstanding service.

Owner Nathan Box can be frequently seen behind the counter slinging coffee drinks -- make with 49th Parallel beans, which at the time of this writing, are exclusive to Elm in Edmonton. I frequently order a large latte from Elm, and am consistently impressed with how fantastic it is. Come to Elm and you'll experience one of the very best lattes in the city.

Beyond coffee drinks, Elm also has a frequently-changing menu of breakfast and lunch sandwiches. They change frequently because Box uses nothing by fresh ingredients from local food suppliers. But the food creations at Elm are to die for, and the ever-changing menu is refreshing.

If you'll looking for a quick drink or a great meal and you haven't checked out elm yet, you are truly missing out on one of this city's great cafes.

Enjoyed a wonderful afternoon at Luke on Saturday before Endymion. In case you didn't know, they have Happy Hour everyday from 3-6 with specialty drinks included. We tried several of the French 75 (Ha!), as well as a few others. The raw oysters and the fried oysters were fresh and delicious! We even convinced my picky 11 year old to try a fried oyster and she liked it. I ordered the crab gratin and thoroughly enjoyed it. I would definitely order it again. Everyone else ordered the burger because it came highly recommended and they all enjoyed it. We never felt rushed and our server was very friendly, while not over staying his time when checking on us. It was a great experience, especially since we needed a break from the crowds and the atmosphere was exactly what we were hoping for.
Really great spot, clean, great service and food quality! Decent value for the area, nice vibe.

Absolutely loved the food at Luke's! This was my second trip to New Orleans and the last time I was here, I didn't think much of the food in the city- and it was mostly places I was visiting in the busy French Quarter. This restaurant is on the other side of Canal Street, which definitely feels off the beaten path of the bustling Bourbon Street and the French Quarter. But it was such a pleasant surprise.
We got the corn and crab bisque with their crispy Brussel sprouts and Shrimps and Grits. All the dishes were great but the best of the evening were the Brussel Sprouts. Smoky and intense with flavor, it was such an indulgence. Even the shrimps and grits were incredible, especially the gravy. Mmm. Really good!
For dessert we got the Bread Pudding which is their signature dessert and it was one of the best desserts I have had! 
Such a great dining experience. Will definitely be back.

The food was incredible but the service was UNMATCHED. Richie Rich made our dinner unforgettable and was the sweetest, most thoughtful waiter we could have asked for. We'll never forget this experience, it made for the perfect night!
Great meal, had the duck, it was delicious. Also had the Pate appetizer. Highly recommended.

This is the only time I've ever walked out of a meal.
The service was insulting. The food was inedible.

We arrived on time for our dinner reservation. We were hungry and excited by the really great reviews we had seen on yelp.

The hostess (we later found out manager) was cold and inattentive in welcoming us, but it sounded like she was dealing with another unhappy table, so we didn't take it personally at first. We were told to wait while our table was prepared. She ignored us for a while but did greet other guests warmly. Finally another hostess asked what was going on with our table and was told that we were standing right there waiting.

We were seated brusquely, and did not receive bread which all the other tables had. At this point we were starting to feel a bit neglected. 
We ordered the Reveillon dinner. 5 minutes after taking our order, the waiter came back to asked us how we wanted the steak done.

At this point we figured that service was going to be bad and settled for hoping that the food would make up for it. For us, good food makes up for bad service.

The first course was a shrimp remoulade. The shrimp was fine, slightly overcooked. The main problem was that the dressing was overly spicy and incredibly sour. The dish was drenched in it. We literally couldn't eat any of the stuff at the bottom of the plate because the dressing was so strong. This was the first of a 4-course $60 meal. Presentation was a mess, like someone slapped it down with no care. And it looked like the garnish was canned mandarine orange pieces (soft and syrupy sweet). Neither of us finished the dish.

The waiter eventually came by and took away the half-eaten dish, but didn't ask if it was okay or if anything was wrong. At this point we really just didn't think that they gave a damn how we were doing.

Second course was turtle soup. It was completely overseasoned. The whole thing tasted like they dumped a bottle of italian seasoning in. We tried 2 spoonfuls and literally couldn't bring ourselves to continue eating it.

At this point I talked to the waiter, offered to pay for the meal so far, but made it clear that we did not want the rest of the meal. To their credit, the manager didn't charge us for it and apologized.

Maybe they don't know how to prepare their Reveillon menu properly? Maybe the staff was flustered with dealing with the other unhappy table?

It was a very disappointing experience for us since Luke had such a good reputation. We came back on yelp and saw that other people had recently had similarly bad experiences. I really don't know what's going on, maybe they had a change of management. I really just want to warn other people. I wouldn't want them to experience the kind of disappointment that we went through.

Finally found a good sushi spot in the suburbs! This place is a hidden neighborhood gem. 

The decor is very clean and modern. The staff  is super friendly from the hostess to the sushi chefs. We came in without a reservation on a weekend and the only availability was at the sushi bar- def not a problem. The sushi chef kindly prepared a complimentary amuse bouche to start. Delish!

Their menu has a variety of choices for both raw sushi lovers to the cooked seafood entrees. We ordered a couple of rolls: No. 7 Volcano, snow mountain  and tempura udon for dinner. Everything came out in a timely fashion and was super tasty! 

Whether you order take out or dine in you will not be disappointed!

Don't forget they are BYOB! Cheers!

Whatever they do here, I hope they keep it the way it is! This was the first meal I have ever had in NOLA.  We had an amazing customer service duo as well as delicious food.  The oysters are by far some of the best I have had and doesn't leave you with all of the salt that west coast oysters do.  Everything from the bread to the soups and the seafood dishes, were simply magnificent! The sauces and the dishes were all made so very well.  I could not believe how delicious all the dishes were.  The dessert was just okay though, but maybe it was what we ordered.  I hope to be back for sure!

Food 
MUST GET THE ETTOUFFIE! 
sooooo good. I had already finished my own dish I don't remember what I got but I only was trying to take a bite and sample some of my friendMs ettouffie and ended up finishing it all for her OOPS! It was just thaaaat good! 

Service 
Out waiters were great, he even cracked a pun regarding the wine bottle name

Atmosphere 
Don't remember the style of it but overall it was nice classy borderline fancy

I found out about 50 cents oysters happy hour and had to visit. The place was busy but I was seated at the table fairly quick and the waitress was very attentive. Mint julep was so strong but it was good & the gumbo was pretty good as well. The oysters took a while but I was expecting it and was happily sipping my drink - but a lady (I'm assuming a manager) was very nice and came to apologize.

I was really disappointed with Luke. The breakfast was simply just okay, nothing special at all. What really disappointed me was that the food was cold. The grits, which could have tasted fairly good, would have been better had they been hot. I asked the server for hot grits. He returned a few minutes later with a fresh serving  but they were barely warm. 
What I had hoped would be a great breakfast experience turned out to be a great big disappointment.

Ordered take out from this place and it was absolutely awful. The food did not taste good, everything was drowned in nasty sauce, and the shrimp was not cleaned well. There was also a lovely hair in my food... will not order again....

I decided to try Luke as my first restaurant in NOLA. However, we waited at front for around ten minutes and no server came serve us. Those two ladies were counting the menu and did not even talk to us, never explained about the wait. Thus we left. It was a horrible experience that made me feel so bad. Hope the waiters at least pretend they are welcoming customers.
Best breakfast I ever had. Great service also. The home made sausages were delicious!
Such a great place ... My new fav spot for lunch. Very good food, and incredibly  friendly staff. For me, this the perfect mix of traditional service, comfortable atmosphere and great food.

The food is pretty good but it doesn't match my image of what a John Besh joint should be like. Great local classics like gumbo, oysters and boudin noir (blood sausage)...you can also get a nice serving of mussels with fries or a good hamburger. 
They have a $ 0.50)/ea oyster happy hour from 3 to 6 pm. 
The service is mediocre to bad by any standards and he reason I rate this place three stars instead of four.

Total let down.  And I was looking forward to my meal here so much after some days of checking out the reviews and looking over the menu.  Had a Friday night dinner here for two.  We were a bit early so they had us wait for our table.  Fine.

I ordered the rabbit pate since many mentioned it.  I really did enjoy this dish.  They were VERY generous with the amount of pate served for this $11 dish.  The little picked sides with it was delicious.  My friend who does not like pate tried and did enjoy this.

My friend had the Poulet grand-mère (herb roasted local chicken, Allan Benton's bacon, farmers' market vegetables & whipped potatoes).  It was...good.  But not mind blowing.  Plate wasn't finished.

I had the Choucroute garnie maison (smoked pork shank, Mangalitsa belly & bratwurst, house-made sauerkraut).  Ok so for $23, you're getting A LOT of food.  I was getting the stares from the table next to me as I'm a 4'11" female served this MASSIVE pork dish.  But I gotta say, I was a bit let down.  The pork shank...which was HUGE was a bit dry.  And it tasted like a turkey leg at a fair.  You see it and oh man it looks juicy and it's so large but then you bit into it and it's...DRY.  I found myself eating more of the bratwurst only because it was less dry and tasted good with the sweet mustard.  Though I must say the bratswurst did not pack a good punch in the flavor department.  The pork belly was very delicious, however.  Melted in your mouth.

And finally, the two stars is mostly the result of the sub par service we received.  First, our server totally looked like an ice queen B the whole time serving us.  Then we get the cold shoulder and see her go all "is there anything else you need" Ms. Suckity Up to the older, more well-off looking couple sitting next to us.  When we got our check I wanted to tell her there's two cards but they won't be split evenly but she just grabbed the check without asking.  When I was trying to get her attention she put up her finger to pause me and then talked to another waitress for about two minutes.

So two minority, young looking females.  Cold shoulder.  A non-minority, well off looking couple a foot and a half next to us...let's make sure you're completely happy!  Swell...
It's been a few years...so glad to be back at Luke. Thank you all for taking care of us...Front of House all the way to the Back. Thank you Richie R. and Gary for taking such great care!

We were really underwhelmed by this restaurant. In a  city like New Orleans, known for culinary excellence this felt like a fancy tourist trap. Adjacent to a hotel, the decor gave me fancy, old American. The food was mostly watered down and mushy. My mom ordered the shrimp and grits as suggested by the waiter. It was like a cheesy, mushy soup. My crispy brussels sprouts were ok, but drowning in oil so I was only able to make it half way through. After it was all said and done we spent almost $100 for two people and left very disappointed.

Very good service, they were extremely helpful, courteous and easy to talk to about the services they recommended and the ones I wanted. The service was also completed in a timely manner, and would definitely come back here again!

I almost don't want to write this review, because this place was THAT good.

We have visited Hachi a few times now, sitting both at a table and at the sushi bar.  It is a BYOB which is a big plus when you're having sushi since the bill can add up. 

The place is small. The seating is limited. And on the night we were there, they ran out of wine glasses. We were offered chilled beer glasses, which worked just fine with our Sauvignon Blanc. The decor is very clean and modern Asian.  Perfect for a date night.  You don't feel like you're in a strip mall. The staff is friendly and attentive and will offer recommendations. Most importantly, the sushi is fantastic. We tried two new special rolls on the last visit that we LOVED. The Manhattan Monkey is to die for. And the Hachikaze was a close second. Sashimi was fresh and delicious.  The Hawaiian Poke is incredible and the Tuna Bites are also good as an appetizer. The Boston Monster is also good, but doesn't quite hit the level of the Lobster Dynamite at Ooka in Doylestown (although overall, I'd have to say Hachi is better!!)

I don't think you can go wrong here. Next time, I hope we still have room for dessert. Our server told us they are homemade.
Great brunch. I loved the atmosphere and I would recommend to newbies, visitors and residents. The food was so good and I was able to try new things and enjoy my staples.
Got oysters here for 75 cents a piece during happy hour. It was really good! Presentation and taste is 5/5. It's a classy place and tastes fresh. Only negative is that the restroom is out of order.

The food is awesome! The meat and vegetables are fresh and the sauce isn't heavy or greasy. I work at a local childcare center and ordered for lunch yesterday. My staff didn't know about the restaurant but my food smelled and tasted so good 4 of them ordered from there today! Delivery was quick on both days and we also picked up an order and it was ready soon as we got there. Customer service was great. Good job Chan's !

Love this place !!!! Food is absolutely amazing , great service except for Erin ( female server) . Hence minus one star. We know she is more senior than VUSI but she did not serve us at all except to pour our water , introduce herself and hand us the check.  Would you call that service.??? She was not even friendly to us at all but to the other table she was.  Was it because I'm Filipino??? The other table didn't even order as much as we did and she was joking around with them.  But VUSI was truly helpful and offered excellent, excellet service. We love Him!!!

Tips:
Order the foie gras and Mangalista pork, ask for fresh bread to go with your oysters and try the French 75 and their Riesling.

John Besh - if you are reading this, please take care of VUSI. In terms of Erin, you might want to reevaluate her performance and attitude towards her customers. Anyway, the food is outstanding and love, love, love the fresh oysters.  You might wanna get a different Malbec since the one you are offering by the glass doesn't taste like the Malbec I have had  in Argentina . It is lacking some spice.
Besides all the little mishaps, we came back here three days in a row. That is how much we loved this place.
Staff is very friendly and accommodating. Food is great from the appetizers to the entrees.  Love coming here.  Favorite place for sushi as well as their hibachi.
Great service and best prepared fast food I have had at a Sonic! Cherry limeades are awesome! Now I see why it's always busy here!

The place was amazing! We actually went on NYE without a reservation and they accommodated us. The food was fantastic...right from the drinks, through appetizers and dessert. Our server was great as well.
It was the worst Chinese food I ever had in my life I try 6 different items and the only thing good was the soda

I've never been disappointed in this restaurant! ORDER THE MOULES ET FRITES! You will not be disappointed! A huge serving of steamed mussels seasoned with chili, thyme and garlic and served with thin and crispy French fries! It's a must have! I also recommend ordering the crispy Brussel sprouts as an appetizer. They are topped with honey, almonds and a delicious cheese! The restaurant has such a great atmosphere and a wonderful bar serving delicious cocktails!

From my deep and extensive research on John Besh (basically watching one episode of Top Chef New Orleans), he seems like a nice guy. So I'll try to be delicate and say this the right way...

John, you need to spend less time in front of the camera and more time in your restaurant. 

Staying in the Hilton for a week netted me many opportunities to dine here. I experienced two brunches, a few happy hours and many just-before-closing cocktails. Each time was a different experience but the bad easily outweighed the good. 

Both of our breakfasts here were terribly disappointing. For breakfast one I sampled the "Eggs in a Jar" which, for $22, is not really that great. It consists of 5 shrimp stuffed into a jar with jalapeño cheese grits and eggs. Yup, eggs, shrimp, cheese and grits for $22. Oh, I forgot the jar. But you don't get to keep the jar. The dish was actually ordered by a table-mate and when it first came out, the eggs were not just undercooked, they were not cooked at all. My Korean friend who eats the snottiest eggs I've seen anyone eat had to send it back. My "Healthy Start", which was house-made granola and fruit on yogurt was sparse at best. The granola was sticky and chewy, not crunchy at all, and while the yogurt was delicious, it wasn't good enough to salvage my image of this $12 dish. I'll say this, the coffee was good. At $6 for a double espresso, it better be. Oh, and the beignets were proper, even though they sent out the wrong sauce with them. 

Our second breakfast here allowed me to sample one of the $14 biscuit sandwiches - the sausage, egg and cheese biscuit served with a cup of fruit. My North Carolina friends make better biscuits in Portland, and load them up with all sorts of meats, gravies, eggs and what-not for half the price. The biscuit here has decent flake and is fairly buttery, but it didn't stand up to the small sausage patty and cheese. One word comes to mind when I think about what I paid for this dish - ludicrous. One member of my table ordered the home fries and when they came with meat in them (no mention of meat on the menu), she sent them back and said "I actually am fine without these". Instead of just taking them off the bill, they sent back potatoes minus the meat. "But we don't want these" we said. "Oh you'll like them, trust me." she said as she walked off... and left them on the bill.  

Despite two food issues with each of our meals (not cheap meals mind you) no apologies, comps, or any other customer service was offered either time. How much balls does it take to not even verbally apologize for such an expensive dish sent out totally wrong? Especially since we're pretty nice in our response/request to have them re-done?

My bar experiences here were quite opposite to my meal experiences. Any time I could find a seat at the bar and order a drink, it was decent, and priced well. The whiskey list is short but there's some good stuff on there. The bartenders are friendly. The $.50 oysters and half-priced drinks at HHour are an insane deal. 

So it makes me wonder. Why go to lengths to offer such an amazing deal at HHour and good service at the bar, and then offer poor service and bad value for those wiling to sit down and spend more for a meal? Who knows. 

While I think this is a mighty fine hotel bar, as a restaurant it fails on value, on service, and frankly on quality of food. Had I been faced with half the prices, I might find this fare to be passable, but at the sky-high menu prices, I'd expect much, much more. 

I'm sure John Besh (if he ever reads these - probably not) doesn't expect his restaurant to be run this way. But c'mon. You send out completely see-through, uncooked eggs in a $22 egg dish and offer not even a verbal apology when the food is returned, let alone any other customer service on a $100 brunch for 4 people (no cocktails ordered)?! Yikes. 

We wouldn't have returned for an actual meal after the first visit for breakfast but had to grab grub on our last day on the way to the airport. Can't say I'd come back outside of happy hour. Maybe dinner is better? At least the bartenders are nice.

Really enjoyed dining here!! The server was very nice and patient and I feel like the food were all prepared by heart and so delicious!! The dining environment was elegant but relaxing. My favorite dish would be the oysters and the gnocchi.

Amazing priced lunch specials (3 rolls for $13) and and even more amazing atmosphere. it's so beautifully decorated it feels like you're in the middle of Manhattan, and the sushi chefs are so polite and usually give you a random little piece of something unusual before your meal as a little appetizer when you sit at the bar, so you get to try some new things. Wonderful place, fast service, all fresh food, you never leave unhappy.

This place is great! A bit small, and busy, but well worth it. Myself & the two people I was with, sat at the bar and the sushi chef offered the 3 of us some sashimi...on the house! And it wasn't the cheap stuff! It was Fatty Salmon. The employees were attentive and polite. The prices are a bit on the higher end, but the food we had was amazing. So much attention to detail. You can tell they take pride in there food.

I came here cause it's a convenient location to eat lunch here then go to the mall. I ordered a turkey avocado BLT with half a Mediterranean quinoa salad. I asked the gal for no kalamata olives.... and sure enough they were in there. Surely, I can eat around it but come on... my sandwich wasn't eatable; the bread just shredded as I bit into it. So I had to pick at it. And the tomatoes weren't ripe-I've worked in the kitchen to know what color they need to be for it to be flavorful. Plus I haven't been asked how my food is by the workers walking around. Overall I'm not impressed with my visit. I usually go to the downtown location-I'll continue to take my business there.

Visited here late night because we were looking for a place that was still serving food. Would highly recommend coming here , good selection beers and food came out hot and fresh. Was blown away by the size of their "small" calzones (which were packed with cheese & a variety of meat) and the cheesesteak was delish as well. Two thumbs up!

Friendly service , friendly patrons and good Philly bar eats. Can't go wrong. 

Cheers!

Good spot for fresh Chinese food, even the lunch portions are plenty for 2 people to share. Always fresh & hot with great sauces, their house made hot mustard is fantastic! All the food is good, but their apps are great. You can eat in, but togo is probably the better option.
Great food - great service - nice people - always fresh - my go to place for Chinese for lunch or dinner

The great reviews do not lie. The grilled brussel sprouts with honey & hot sauce are heaven.  And I'm not a  brussel sprout fan.  I could be after today. So here is another great restaurant we found in New Orleans: LUKE.  Tim, the Manager, and Deseree our wait person were terrific!  Ordered crispy brussel sprouts, fried chicken with red beans &  rice, Croque Madam w/ jalapeno grits and drinks...  Don't be fooled that it looks like it's part of Hilton.  It really isn't. Check it out.

My friends and I have decoy that this is must each time we come. Definitely take advantage of the happy hour on Friday. We initially stopped in for something and we're pleasantly surprised by the delicious French 75s. They were half off for happy hour. The bread pudding was really good. The ice cream comes directly on it. Which I feel was too much for me. Next time I'm definitely getting it on the side. Our waitress Savannah was great! She was so nice and attentive.

Came here for happy hours with a friend during our trip to New Orleans.  The oysters were super fresh and super sweet!!  We also order half a dozen of fried oysters, which were ok but i preferred the raw oysters.  We also ordered their fried brussel sprouts which were delicious!!  I have never had brussel sprouts prepared like this before.  They were fried, tossed in a honey hot sauce and covered with slice apples, almonds and cheese.  Very different very delicious.  We topped the meal with a bread pudding with a rum caramel sauce.  It was good but a little on the sweet side.  Great place to have oysters and some brussel sprouts.

Hachi is Center City quality sushi and Asian fusion, right here in Chalfont. Their special roll combinations are unique (especially compared to other local places) and their presentation is really nice. We've eaten at the sushi bar and at the tables. We absolutely love this little gem.

Sat at the bar.  Bartender was a machine. Enjoyed watching her pour involved drinks. She had a dry sense of service but friendly. She recommended the shrimp n cheesy grits and I was not disappointed, what a great meal. Not a large portion but very adequate. The drinks were 1/2 price and they were also great. I highly recommend. Would like to return to try their dinner menu.
Come here for happy hour. .75 cent oysters and half off drinks. The oysters and crab gratin were delicious. You get fresh bread and whipped butter. The staff were very attentive.
Definately worth a visit if your ever in the NOLA. We had oysters during happy hour which saves a lot of money. Drinks were great, and the server was awesome.
We came with a large group for a bachelorette party lunch. We got several appetizers, oysters, and entrees, all of which were delicious. The service was great and we would absolute recommend!
Great friendly service by hostess and waiter.  Welcoming.  Keto friendly.  Not too much seasoning (if you can't handle spices). Great wine! Will definitely return.

The girlfriend and I tried this place out this past Saturday (7/6/13) for a late birthday dinner for me.  That means she paid so I was even happier than usual to try a new place ;)

First off it's a John Besh place so you know right away that you will be getting locally grown, raised, or caught food of the freshest variety.  We had a 6:30 reservation and were seated immediately.  We were seated in the back by the kitchen which was completely open to see into.  Kind of nice scene.  

We started off with drinks.  Her a glass of malbec and me with one of their own craft brews; a Luke-Alt.  Luke-Alt is an amber style beer crafted by Heiner Brau out of Covington.  They also have a blonde lager called the Luke-Fru.  Both are good but the Alt was fantastic.  We drank a round while munching on their fresh cut fries.  PERFECTION!!!  Crisp, greaseless and hot.  

After this we order our entrees.  She had the shrimp and grits which from what I tasted were slightly spicy and really flavorfull.  I had a fried chicken special. It was a sweet and spicy chicken fried in tabasco and apricot flavors.  This was sitting on top of an okra and tomato etouffee.  So good!!!  

The portions were somewhat small for the price but perfect in the fact that I didn't want leftovers and I was full after.  The only drawback is that the legs of their chairs come down to a very small base.  If you lean back in them at all you are probably goign to fall.  I'm probably not suppose to talk about how my girlfriend fell over.  I'm definitely not suppose to talk about how I laughed so hard that I couldn't help her up.  She was fine other than slightly embarrassed.  Of course the embarrassment went away once a guy 3 tables over did the exact same thing. I think it was ok to laugh then.

So John invest in some new chairs my man.  Either that or release the blooper video of all the people falling who shouldn't lean over in their chairs.

Luke's has an amazing happy hour....which I did not make it to. But I really wanted to try their Shrimp and Grits based on the pictures, so my friends and I had dinner reservations here for our first real meal in New Orleans; reservations were easy to make via Opentable. 

Shrimp and Grits ($24.00) - On the menu, it's  Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte," and described as "roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausage." This was a touch too salty for our taste, but the flavors were good, grits were a nice consistency, and it had a good amount of plump shrimp on top. This dish was an explosion of flavors and textures, savory, meaty, perfectly cooked shrimp with some creamy grits. I really liked it. 

Shrimp & Crawfish "Étouffée" ($26.00) - Heirloom tomatoes, garlic, cavatelli. Please note that this comes on a bed of cavatelli (tiny shell pasta), NOT rice as you may be used to with this dish. This was still a solid dish and we were content with the amount of seafood in the dish too. This dish was good, but we all liked the shrimp and grits more.

Service was friendly, knowledgeable, and quick. For a group of 3, the 2 dishes filled us up because these items do tend to be a bit heavy. Prices are a bit on the higher end, but they do use quality ingredients and  give a fair amount (a little on the small side at first glance, but it's enough). 

THE SHORT: Get the shrimp and grits! Try to make it for happy hour if you can --- apparently it's $0.75 oysters and cheap drinks. Reservations can be made easily online, it gets packed. I'd definitely recommend sharing a few items so you're not too overwhelmed by all the rich flavors.

I really like the food here but the prices and disorganization routinely  keep them from getting my business.

Enter the store and enjoy your typical coffee shop atmosphere, complete with soft rock, coffee pastries, and free wifi. Now comes the GRE/MCAT/GMAT/LSAT ringer #1: where's the line to order? To assist you with figuring this out, the brains behind the operation has conveniently placed a sign on a column directly in front of the preparation counter indicating which side of the column you should stand on for salads (left) or sandwiches (right). Oh, but what's that you say? Where to stand if you want both or neither? Yeah, I've been trying to figure that out for the past two years. Apparently, this whole signage thing is pointless because either line will do. Particularly, since even when you do stand in the appropriate line, the next available server will call you over anyway. Talk about unnecessary confusion! 

Now, let's just assume you've figured out the ordering fiasco and would like to pay for your order so you can escape this unsolicited psychological experiment. Here comes the GRE/MCAT/GMAT/LSAT ringer #2: where's the check out line? If you came here during any of the multiple rush hours, the patrons randomly standing around the cash registers may dupe you into thinking that they are actually in line. Psych! They're not. They simply don't have any other place to put themselves. The disorganized multi-purpose space is supposed to accommodate ordering, paying, and waiting.  Unfortunately, without a proper traffic flow, you too may find yourself awkwardly waiting among the masses until a cashier hollers at you to ask if you are ready to pay. (Note to management: they make an app for that. Better yet, they also make signage for this very purpose, i.e. order here, pay here). 

Once, you've passed the test, it's mostly uphill from there. The food is quite good (disclaimer: this depends largely on the newness of your server) and I recommend a try, particularly their signature flatbread or any menu item made with it. Although the cost:value ratio ($9+ for a sandwich)  may leave you somewhat disappointed. For me, the hassle of just placing an order is disappointment enough.

Excellent food, in taste, creativity and presentation. The best Japanese restaurant I've been to in PA.  For appetizer, I ordered hot stone yellowtail. It was delicious and fun to eat. Sashimi were fresh, pistachio crusted salmon was melt in your mouth.  Lychee mochi was very fragrant and delicious for dessert. Will definitely come back.

This was a disappointing dinner experience especially since it had been recommended by a friend who is usually right on... 

First off it was excruciatingly loud. Uncomfortably so. We could not have a decent conversation and barely heard the explanations by the staff of various menu items. Service was quite good, though. It was the food that was just ok.

One item stood out as being very good and innovative  -- their rabbit and chicken liver pate. It was served in its own little jar topped with aspic. On the board were dollops of grainy mustard, pickled watermelon rind, apple chutney, and half sour pickles. Thin toasts came on the side. 

The cup of crab and corn chowder was just okay. They reheated it for me as the first time it was just barely warm. But I've had a better version at bonefish grill of all places. 

My entree was their drum fish. I ordered it almondine. It came fried with a light coating. But it was dry and topped with only 4 little almond slivers. I was hoping for the traditional brown butter sauce with almonds.... The fish was served over some root vegetables that had an off putting flavor. Not sure if it was the spice used or what,  but I didn't care for them at all. 

My husband ordered their featured pork schnitzel. The portion was large, but it too was overcooked and dry. Luckily there was some sauce on the side which he used to make it edible. The fries were cooked well done as requested. 

In a town where even a bad meal is usually good, we felt we'd waisted our evening. The seafood towers going by did look good though... as did the burger the kid next to us was served. Maybe we ordered all the wrong items? Now we know...

We ate here as our last lunch during our conference. 
Linda was our server she was Amazing!!! 
We had learned at our conference about peaks and valleys people experience during service at an establishment.  Linda absolutely gave us many peaks during our experience. The food was great but Linda made the experience Awesome!!!!

+ strong drinks
+ happy hour from 3-6pm; half off drinks and 75 cent oysters
+/- oysters were okay but I definitely had sweeter ones
+ new waiter made up for the former waiter's slow service

- slow service (waiter didn't put in our order until 20 minutes after he took our order!)

Seven Oaks Animal Hospital is our vet for our dog, Max. I took Max there on Wednesday because he wasn't eating and was lethargic. Max was found to have a high temperature so they did some lab work, which came back normal. The Dr recommended further diagnostics and so we had an X-ray and ultrasound done to hopefully determine the problem. As a result, we discovered he had a mass in his abdominal regional. We elected to do exploratory surgery to determine if the mass could be removed safely. Max was scheduled for surgery the following morning. Dr. Reddy worked miracles on Max and was able to remove the mass. Max had to have his spleen removed, as well as a bowel resection, but it was a successful AND miracle surgery. Dr. Reddy and his team are amazing. We received updates via phone calls and it was apparent they had Max's best interest at heart. All of the doctors and staff are truly fabulous. I can't think of enough positive adjectives to describe them but what comes to my immediate mind is PROFESSIONAL, COMPASSIONATE, HONEST (very important to me), extremely COMPETENT, SMART, and THOROUGH. They are everything that I look for in my own doctors. I trust them and I feel safe with them. Thank you thank you thank you Dr. Reddy, the other doctors, and staff for providing quality care and for saving my Max.

Great and taste.Love it!This place is a treasure - great food, fantastic service.Great menu that can satisfy either the savory or the sweet.
Highly recommend!

This place and their service has left me speechless and eagerly wanting to come back. We were a crew of 10 walking to Billie Jean who said 90 mins wait, minimum, at 11 AM. I frantically started calling surrounding eateries which either said no or a similar wait time. LIKE was my 4th call. I wasn't expecting a yes from them when I asked about our large party, but surely, they came back with a "come on over, we have seating." Took us 10 mins to get there and when we walked in, we were taken through several dining areas (the place is huge!) I didn't understand where they were taking us and when we finally arrived in our own fully private room, my jaw dropped. 

From there - our waiter, Corey blew us away even more. He was polite, attentive, friendly, and honesty. He went above and beyond what impeccable service is and truly gave us a remarkable experience at LUKE. 

And then then food came! From the oysters to gumbo to Benedict sandwich, everything was extremely delicious. We had quiet a few drinks and in the end, we paid $125 per couple (5 couples & generous tip included.)

Highly highly recommend LUKE and ask for COREY to be your waiter! He will not disappoint!

This is some of the best pizza I've had. Their speciality pizzas are amazing. Very pricy compared to other pizza places in the area but so worth it! My major complaint is their delivery service. While they always make it right with refunds, 2 out of the last 6 times I had to call to complain. First time, took over an hour and a half and I had no pizza... I call they say it's on its way... Half hour later I call and they realize they delivered it to my elderly neighbors instead bc the delivery driver wrote down the wrong house number. So they gave me my pizza for free and sent another one but it still took almost three hours for me to get pizza! Now tonight we order a simple cheese pizza. It comes and more than half the pizza has no cheese, it all slid off to the one end of the box. They did give me a full refund but I have no learned I can't order in from them, I can only have the pizza if I dine in. It's a shame because the pizza is so so good when they do it right, if is worth the extra money. Just don't get it delivered.
Very nice restaurant. The only reason I found this place was because I was staying at the Hilton. I skipped my free company lunches and ate here. Price was right and the food was great.

The best Sweet Potato Tempura Sushi I've ever had! The Asian Pear Salad is so flavorful and textured. It's something so simple that just lifts my flavor spirits every time I eat it. The food and presentation is of superior quality. Even though the food is made by different chefs each night you get a little artistic comment from each one of them. The one tip I'd give you as a customer is it gets booked up fast on the weekends so ordering out is a good option or call ahead for a reservation.

Great happy hour! The best French 75 I've had and cocktails are half price. The oysters are a great deal (.75 cents) and are big and delicious. We also enjoyed the pate, which was served charcuterie style with crostinis, picked veggies, and house made mustard. We'll definitely be back.

I am really disappointed that I missed the oyster happy hour. But we did stop in for Brunch which was very good.  I had the shrimp and grits. They were really cheesy and rich. I tried the French 75 after reading reviews on Yelp - it was good, but nothing to write home about. We also had oysters which were excellent.

Great spot. Staff was excellent too. We started with the flatbread. Although I was hesitant to order since it had anchovies and olives, the two with the cheese were amazing! For my main I had the shrimp and crab étouffée. I've never had étouffée with pasta, but it was delicious and on spot. If only I could take the pot of it home. Now my friend had the 1/2 baked chicken. Unfortunately it came out warm. The staff was quick to correct the situation and my friend truly enjoyed the chicken.

Highlight of my NOLA trip with my group of friends. Our party (14 people) got the private dining room in the back of the restaurant, but we easily could have sat in the regular dining space. The restaurant feels like an upscale diner - very family friendly, casual and warm - with wonderful staff who make you feel right at home. 

We ordered - 
APPETIZERS:
- Crispy brussel sprouts: GET THIS. This was my favorite dish of the night. Tossed with mouthwatering glaze and seasoning that adds a ton of kick, and topped with crumbled cheese. Heaven.
- Mushroom flatbread: I was a fan! Cheesy, savory, and easy to share
- Shrimp BBQ toast: good but not that memorable. If you're with large party, then go for it, but would not prioritize this
- Rabbit & Chicken pate: great to share and big portions, but I was not blown away, unfortunately. They give baked/thin crouton which I was not a fan of (would have preferred soft bread)

ENTREES:
- Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte": this is the most ordered item, and customer favorite, per our waitress. I got this as my entree (see picture) and was pretty happy. But the dish is 85% grits and 15% shrimp. Just FYI.
- Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp & Crab "Étouffée" : our waitress said this is her favorite dish. And I WISH I got this instead! My friends who got this loved it. I would say go for this if this is your first time.
- Luke Burger: one guy in my group ordered this. Your basic burger, nothing special, if that's what you're in the mood for.
- Washington Parish Roasted Chicken: huge pieces of chicken with country potatoes. My two girl friends could not finish even half of their dish.

Bon Appetit!

Excellent! Wine choices were great and everything we had was delicious. We ate dinner and ordered the Brussel sprouts and gumbo appetizers, and the risotto and shrimp & grits for entrees, with the bread pudding for desert. It was by far the best meal we had while in NOLA. 

Our entrees were $26 & $24 and our bill was $100 total with only 1 drink so I would say it is closer to $$$ than $$. 

Regardless, this place is very good and we would highly recommend it.

First and foremost, I want to say the service here was excellent.  With a group of 9 girls who may have had 1 drink too many, I know taking care of us was not the easiest task.  On top of that, we also had a show to catch.   Our server(s) were on top of it!  Quick, friendly, attentive, and overall we just had a very positive experience.

Coupled with excellent service, the food was also delicious.  We ordered:

Stuffed P&J Oysters (broiled) 
Raw Oysters
Hot Buttered Crawfish 
Crispy Brussels Sprouts
Fresh Gulf Puppy Drum (white fish)
Shrimp & Grits
Shrimp & Crawfish Etouffee with pasta

I think my favorite item might have been the etouffee with pasta.  There was a ton of crawfish and shrimp, and it was bursting with flavor.  Of course, needless to say the Shrimp & Grits are delicious too.  Oh, and so was the Hot Buttered Crawfish (if you can't tell, I LOVE shrimp and crawfish!).  I don't think you can go wrong with any items with shrimp and crawfish.  How many more times can Cecilia say shrimp and crawfish?!

Yes, I would highly recommend enjoying a dining experience at Luke!  Stellar service, delicious food, beautiful and classy space, it's a win all around!

Went thru the drive through yesterday and we decided to do one of their family feasts. Now they are a great deal however they were out of Mac and cheese so they gave us a choice of 3 kinds of soup. Ok so we picked broccoli cheddar soup. Get the the window and they are out of broccoli cheddar soup but now we can pick any soup. Nothing really sounded good but we already had been in line for a while and there's really no choice so we got chicken tortilla. They gave us an extra couple cookies. Get home we ended up with chips instead of a baguette and there wasn't even mustard or mayo on the kids sandwich it was lunchmeat and a slice of cheese and dry bread. Had I known that we wouldn't be getting anything we wanted. And I would need to add condiments that weren't included for $35 we would have just stayed home.

OK, this review might not suit everybody, but I only went there for the pizza and beer.  Here it is:  THE BEST GD PIZZA IN THE BURBS.  I dare you to find me one better.  And the afternoon bartender, Kevin, is one cool dude. Old-school bartender who keeps an eye on everyting.  Bartending as an art!!  I have not had any other food in this place, so I may have my head up my rear end.  But go for the pizza, you will be astounded that a sports bar frequented by a bunch of kids could have pizza this good.  I am not shi**ing you, it's really that good.  I lie awake at night trying to figure out ways to trick my wife into going to Glenside so we just happen to end up at Jerzees.  Maybe I should tell her that someone built a Bed Bath and Beyond next to it, then I'd have it made.
Stopped into this place during a work trip to New Orleans and was pleased. During happy hour, they have $0.75 oysters and definitely order the Brussel sprout dish as well!

Like a fine breakfast establishment from long ago landed in New Orleans today. And brought along lunch and dinner too. Including a great oyster bar.

The shrimp and grits were decadent, the coffee was fresh and kept full, the service was friendly and attentive (huge shout out to Devin, who was superlative), and we basically loved the whole experience.

My entree, the BLTAE, was tasty but served on the cool side. I was expecting it to arrive more warm, more hot and fresh, but I'm not sure what happened. Maybe it just sat a bit while waiting for my wife's entree to be done? In any event that was the only miss during an otherwise wonderful breakfast experience. We would happily go back. Hopefully the next time all entrees will be served equally hot.
Absolutely delicious.  We've been here several times and have always had a great meal and pretty good service. Highly recommend the Brussels!

Every time I come to this location they're out of something. The past two times it has been chips. At 7pm on a Wednesday they're out of chips?? I don't understand why they never make more of whatever they're out of when they're still open another 3 hours. Most of the time they're out of fajita veggies.

Two nights ago I had it delivered and received someone else's order. It had my name on it so it wasn't the delivery driver's fault, just whoever bagged it gave me someone else's order. Unfortunately, I'm lactose intolerant and the burrito bowl had cheese and sour cream all over. 

I love Chipotle, this just isn't a good location.

I came here pre-COVID and it was amazing. I can't speak to their entrees, but they offer HUGE $0.75 oysters for happy hour that insanely fresh. I would be satisfied with just these, but they also have fantastic fried oysters! During our 7 day trip, we stopped by here 4 times, that's how good the happy hour is. This is a must go for happy hour in NOLA!
The food was good but the waitress never followed up and I got sprayed with the disinfectant for the table next to me.

This was the highest rated restaurant near my hotel on Yelp and attached to John Besh so I figured it would be a no-brainer.  I sat at the bar and after waiting about 10 min, finally got service.  They ended up giving me the lunch menu and had to change my order once they realized my option wasn't available for dinner.  I ended up having the chicken dinner with bacon, veggies, and mashed potatoes.  It took a while to come out and when it finally came, it was served in a deceptively small cast iron skillet.  It was a large serving of chicken sitting on the mashed potatoes and veggies.  A little too salty for my taste.  I like to eat healthily and probably should've gotten the salad with fried seafood instead - satisfy my seafood craving, but the fried goodness would get cancelled out by the veggies. 

They have a $0.50 oyster happy hour from 3-6 pm weekdays, which I'm sad I missed.  Friendly bar patrons so you strike up conversation pretty easily.  Service was ok.

Sold me a lemon! The car didn't have a cap for the coolant at the bottom so it leaked out. It was filled with CLAY. Apparently it keeps it from leaking for a bit. Lights worked at the lot. Went out on the way home. I noticed it looked like the front end was submerged in water. Had to replace all electrical up front. Learned the gas gauge didn't work either when i went to school the next day. That was gonna be too expensive for me to fix right away so I had to worry about running out of gas. Tires started cracking and shredding. Had to get all new tires. Not to mention a huge oil leak. My starter and alternator blew out in less than a couple months. The first rain storm, I found out it had a leak somewhere underneath the hood and there would be a PUDDLE on the front passenger floor. Tried to resolve the situation but they basically said "screw off, too late now" I was 17 at the time. Very young and dumb. Never buy anything from them ever.

My first impression of Panera was great and every time I go back it doesn't live up to my expectations.  The food is always good but something always make me frown.  Last week it was the wrong order today it was a breakfast sandwich that left me wondering if they got the order right.  This is what you get for $8.

The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly.  here is the lowdown, on my wife and my experience.  Good:  made last minute reservations,at 8pm, on a whim and within 15 minutes of a phone call and short walk from our hotel, we sat at our table.  Bad:  It then took about 15 minutes for anyone to come offer drinks and or answer questions about the menu.  Once our waiter came, he was nice enough, but interestingly honest, when we asked him about the menu.  Very informative about the homemade, fresh, local food.  They raise there own pigs and veggies and whatnot. I was looking to do the brisket special, but was told that was a bad choice, as per my waiter that, and a few other items were subpar.  He recommended the burger(made with ground beef and brisket), due to its national acclaim.  So I went with the burger, my wife the crab ravioli, homemade pasta.  Ugly turned Good:  I ordered  a absinthe suisse, (once again the waiter warned against, stating that it was quite bad, but i figured i would give it a go anyway)... should have listened. two words, Nas-Ty.  He asked how I liked it, I was polite, but honest, and he said no worries, we will get you something else, no extra charge.  next drink much better.  Well now comes the finale, I wish it were grand but it was a mixture of G,B & U.  We did not get our food for about an hour and 15 minutes, keep in mind i we ordered pasta and a burger, not quite a time consuming ordeal.  Was it worth the wait, yes!.... and no.  When our waiter checked on our food that was just brought out, he asked if the fries were warm enough, prompting that he knew they were most likely not. (now he didnt straight out say sorry about the wait, food was done for a while and sitting under the heaters, but his comment and the LUKE warm fries and burger, surely did.)
I ordered my burger medium rare, but got medium, medium well. I would agree that it is one of the best burgers that I have eaten, and I am a burger fancier, but the interesting thing was my favorite part was the bacon, interestingly enough, when i commented on the bacons excellence to my waiter, he straight out told me that it was brought in, and not part of the pork they raise.  once again great honesty, great bacon, good job finding that amazing melt in your mouth flavor, but kinda funny since his main selling point was the interconnectedness with all the ingredients.  Ate a few fries, cold, so-so, let them be.  Now my wife's crab ravioli was pretty darn good, fresh, tasty, and a bit of spice, helping to tame down the sauciness.  perfect blend of yum.  the only thing that could have made this dish better would have been for it not to have mass quantities of crab shell in it.  I understand stuff happens, but would not expect to see it in a quality restaurant. Im not perfect, and i understand things like that happen, like i said I would have preferred it didnt and would have bumped up the star rating a notch had it not. but in one of the bites I had of my wifes plate, I had a shell the size of my fingernail.  Lame.  Had I swallowed that it probably would have hurt quite a bit going down. So there you have it, a mixture of good and bad service, good information and introduction, bad follow through on service and time management.  Good food, so close to Great that it is sad that the few Ugly shells from uncouth preparation destroyed what obvious potential this meal has.

Indeed a great restaurant option in the Central Business District of Nola!

Friends and I wanted a casual option that would have good food and would not have a line out the door on this particular evening during Essence Music Fest.  Like, we literall needed to go from day party to restaurant, to hotel to concert in not a lot of time.  Luckily not too many folks were up on John Besh's Luke Restaurant and I am glad I had this gem bookmarked on Yelp!

I had the Shrimp & Grits and literally scraped every last grit onto my fork - it was that good!  Started with the Salad Luke which was bright & lovely, bursting with flavors from the golden beets contrasting with the buttermilk dressing!  

My friends really enjoyed the Luke Burger and the Etouffee as well!  Would definitely come again and I know now that I have GOT to try out the other John Besh restaurants, SOON!!

Heads up this review isnt about the food. Its about the phenomenal service.

We made reservations at this restaurant. 

We were lost and the young lady who answered the phone helped us find the location.

When we arrived and reviewed the menu there was nothing my teenager daughter would eat. We had to leave. 

The waiter was pouring water for us when we told him. He invited us to drink the water while we found a more suitable place to eat. 

I have to give them 5 stars for not being pretentious or judgmental with us. When I come back to New Orleans without my kid you bet I will return.

I don't know how I missed all these terrible reviews before I purchased my heating and air-conditioning unit about seven months ago. I paid in full upon installation and after a week I realized that they had not even installed the condenser pump that I paid for. Here we are seven months later still waiting. We called them immediately upon discovering the oversight and were informed that they would call us back in one week to schedule.  No apology. We could deal with that if they actually ever called. We finally have an appointment today between 9 and 11 AM. It is now 2 o'clock and still no one here. I called and spoke to Matt on the phone to ask him the status he was completely unapologetic and rude he told us they would call one hour before they arrived.   I reminded him that they had told me the 9 to 11 timeframe and he said they always tell you that they will call an hour before and that is just a rough estimate. I'll say!   When I wanted to discuss this with him further he hung up on me. What an unprofessional, rude company. I'm not sure if Matt is an owner,  but he is definitely someone representing the company poorly. 
 I do not leave negative reviews eagerly. As a matter of fact, I will not post this until I cool down for 24 hours.  So if you're reading this, you know for sure they have done nothing to try to remedy the problem. I'm not accustomed to being hung up on by someone I am giving my hard-earned money to.   There were so many other companies out there I would not use this one again and I would recommend that you not use them too. 
**it's now 2 o'clock and I just call the company again. They told me that the driver coincidentally had a flat tire and will be here shortly. Once again if that was true, shouldn't they have called me to let me know? Having a hard time believing! Ok...so he finally arrived. He was scheduled to do an annual cleaning. Remember that is was only seven months old and we had called them to install the condenser pump that we had paid for. Fortunately, he did have one in the car and installed it. Finished up around 4:30 PM. Still waiting for a call back from the manager...
Bottom line... Don't is this company!
My favorite spot in the CBD for oysters, happy hour, French 75s made the correct way, and great service.  Geaux Luke!!
Great spot and classy place to eat. The chicken biscuit was the best I ever had and I've never seen grits like this. Must visit

Sushi was incredibly fresh and delicious! Each appetizer was better than the next. The Hachi employees could not have been nicer despite the craziness of a busy holiday weekend. Thank you for a great dinner and great service!

The place looks very fancy and well-kept. I was actually quite intimidated by the place and was afraid it would be beyond my budget.
We came here just in time for happy hour on a Thursday. There was no wait but you could tell that people were starting to trickle in.
We were immediately seated.

We ordered a bowl of Gumbo, some fried oysters, and some fresh oysters.
Everything we had was great and came at a reasonable time. 

For happy hour you get 75c oysters which is pretty good.
We also had a couple of cocktails (half off during happy hour) to start off the vacation.
The service was on point and our needs were addressed immediately.

Overall it was a good experience, I would say well worth the money you pay.
I would come back if I was in the area again.

I was recommended by my hotel to eat at this establishment. When I walked in I thought oh no this place is too pricey. They seated me and I looked at the menu. At my surprise it was very reasonably priced. I had the jalapeño grits and gumbo with a yummy drink, since it was happy hour. Sooooo yummy. I will be back again.
In response to your comment- I checked the price of the exact model thermostat on Amazon and it was $30. Not sure what you are implying

Possibly the best meal we had all trip. We called on a Sunday morning and were able to get our group of 7 in and got a private room! The ice tea cocktail was fantastic. Had the most amazing Brussel sprouts. The corn and crab bisque and jalapeño grits were a stand out. Wonderful service and a great end to our vacation!

A good place to come if you want good oysters for a decent price! They have a happy hour deal for oysters and drinks which is pretty good. The deal is 75cent oysters and 1/2 off house wines and draft beers from 3-6. Also they do accept reservations!

Connected within the Hilton Hotel it was pretty easy to navigate to in the Warehouse District.

We were date immediately and given great service from beginning to end.

I order the P&J Stuffed Oysters which were light yet tasty enough for my last day in Nola. My friends had the roasted chicken and the other the Shrimp and Grits. No complaints!

The decor was great, the bathroom was easy to find and the costpoint was comparable to locations attached a Hilton $$-$$$

I would come back during happy hour. The oysters were plump and yummy.

New favorite happy hour spot:
-Amazing oysters for $1 each
-1/2 off cocktails including their AMAZING French 75
-New favorite bartender (see pic!)
Come early (starts at 3) because bar seating is limited- 
Guy next to us ordered the most beautiful burger I've ever seen so we are going back for that (it's $18 and when you see it, you'd pay more!)
We ordered the tuna tartare with shrimp chips and 3 scallops app as well and they were both fantastic!
Bartender was hustlin- busier than anyone else in the room so we tipped accordingly and he was fabulous

Food was excellent. Ribeye was perfectly done and oysters were amazing. Nice atmosphere. Service was good. It got a little busy and there seemed to be not enough staff, but the food more than made up for it.
