Love this place!! My husband and I went during happy hour. We took a bike taxi from the French quarter area. Enjoyed a delicious Sazerac. The best seafood gumbo I had ever had. Made to perfection!! Also had fried oysters!!! Yum!! Service was excellent. Not to be missed if you are visiting NOLA.

Alright, so I saw this restaurant on a list of best restaurants in the kitchen and made it a point to have a meal here while on a recent trip. Not to mention, I'm a fan of John Besh. I chose to dine here for lunch during the middle of the week. It wasn't too difficult to get a last minute reservation and it seemed to be full of a lot of locals, which was a good sign.

I couldn't decide what I wanted because I was was past the point of hungry. It took what seemed like at least 10 minutes before anybody came to even fill my water glass and give me a menu, but when they finally did, I asked my server for suggestions. He seemed completely uninterested in talking to me and pushed for the Croque-madame. I should have gone with my gut, but listened to the server. While I was waiting- for what seemed like another 20 minutes before the meal even came, I asked for bread, which I saw on all the other tables. The server forgot about it, and by the time he came by to where I could ask him again, it finally came with my meal.

The sandwich itself was okay; I enjoyed the fries much more. Now it's been several years since I've had a Croque-madame, so maybe I didn't know what I was getting myself into. The sandwich was covered in what tasted like a thick bechamel sauce and broiled. In between two thick slices of bread were the ham and cheese. Oh, and let's not forget the fried egg on top. Honestly, it was so rich, I ate a quarter of it and boxed up the rest. 

The service was extremely slow, the server seemed like he could care less about serving me, and the best part of my meal was the fries. I was disappointed, and wished I would have come on Monday to get the honey tabasco chicken special. Coulda, shoulda, woulda....well I'm not sure I'll be back. Sorry, John.

Brought the wife and kids here for an early dinner. Had the oysters, shrimp and grits, fried chicken red beans and rice, and gumbo. The kids had the grilled cheese and Mac and cheese. Everything came out great. Also caught the end of happy hour, can never complain about half priced drinks. Highly recommended. Oh and the service was excellent!
Smallest portion ever. Taste awful and crazy expensive for trash. We wait so long for the food and it wasn't worth waiting and paying that much

My husband and I ate here last night for our anniversary! Our waiter was so awesome and the food was delicious!!! I had Shrimp and Grits and my husband had roasted chicken! Both were delicious as well as our cocktails! Great authentic NOLA food!!
Great spot to grab a bite. Excellent oysters and beer. The staff is very courteous and they even have a couple TVs if you're trying to catch a game

We had some lovely oysters here that were briny to perfection. The crab dip was also spectacular. The burger was good, however the portion size was quite massive and we wished they'd told us that when they saw the amount of food we were ordering. Other than that, we really enjoyed the food!

This place is everything you ask for on a good restaurant. Fast service, good customer service and awesome food. Highly recommended

Ahh and the owner is a Marines! Semper fi

Two stars for the lunch time bento box. While you get tons of decent food, it is not what I expected. When I order a bento box, I want a cute compartmentalized box. Instead, the food comes out on a large plate with a handful of items such as miso soup, salad, california roll, some vegetables, and some dumplings. I got the Chicken Katsu (fried) over rice for my bento box entree, and it wasn't even crispy.

First time here at Luke, absolutely delicious! The Brussel sprouts were a fantastic appetizer, definitely recommend. 

My boyfriend and I both split the crab pasta and burger meal- homemade noodles and sauce was to  die for.!!! Absolutely amazing!! The burger was delicious as well. 

The service definitely stood out, our waiter "richie rich" was hilarious, personable, and so attentive! I 10/10 will recommend to anyone, we will be back

We had high expectations going into Luke, and left mostly whelmed. Points for being open on Christmas Day, though. 

I ordered the fried oyster salad, which is essentially a cobb salad minus the egg with fried oysters. To be honest I mainly just wanted fried oysters, and Luke does them well. However, they definitely lacked that "omg amazing" factor. The salad itself was decent, but somehow they managed to put too much bacon in it. It sounds like sacrilege, but it's true.

My girlfriend got the roasted chicken, which in contrast was fantastic. The chicken is fantastically juicy and the potatoes were perfectly crisp. I would order this again in a heartbeat. 

Three stars for the oysters, five stars for the chicken, but three stars overall because we were really looking forward to oysters.

Shrimp and grits. Wow. We spent a week here and tried it several times and this was far and away the best version of it. Very clean restaurant and reasonably priced. The service was a little off but dang the shrimp and grits...make you want to slap your momma.

Good happy hour special! .75 cent raw oyster ( good and plum some of the shells should have be scrubbed a little more), 1.50 fried oysters (I think it was average), half price cocktails, selected wine and draft beers

Great little spot to grab a morning coffee and a snack whilst on your way to work. Handily located just off Jasper the Elm Cafe is easy to get to. The staff are always friendly and very helpful, if you have any questions about their feature coffees or menu they're most knowledgeable. 

I'm a big fan of the food offerings, everything is so fresh! Sandwiches are grand for lunch time but the breakfast offerings are my favourite. SPINACH. 

It is a little small and if there is a queue you'll be waiting a wee while - but it's totally worth it. Seat space is a little limited but in the summer they have seating outside. 

Grand place for a visit.

lucky luke is always good, at happy hours time... a miracle
better than the vatican

My husband and I came to this restaurant and decided to eat at the bar since there was a wait for a table. The bartenders were far from friendly and acted like we were bothering them to order a drink. My duck came out raw, almost like Sushi, I sent it back and asked if the dish could be cooked more. The bartender came back and said "the cook said that is how duck is cooked, you will have to order something else." Funny, because I have had duck at several restaurants and earlier that day  at Brennan's and never had it served like Sushi. I ordered Shrimp and Grits and that was OK. My husband's burger was an overpriced, piece of burnt meat on a stale bun. The manager came over and voided my first entrée and did not even apology for our experience with my dish. Sad, that they treated us like tourist because we are locals and would have gone back if our experience was different. In addition, we have told our friends and family our experience here. Please don't waste your time and money!!

Pretty good experience here. Went here to lunch on Friday with co workers around 2 pm. There was another table there when we arrived but then they left so place was quite empty. The food was good and they had a lot of great lunch specials. We really enjoyed the variety of food given that they provide you with Japanese and hibachi options. 

Something to know is that they are BYOB. So be sure to bring your alcohol with you! They have a variety of tea flavors available for those that want to ensure a warm beverage. 

Highly recommend the ginger dressing on the salad!

Seven oaks you ripped my family off to day for $400. Doctor was just like a automotive shop trying to sell, sell, sell. All my dog needed was a prescription refill, and was told oh it's been 12 months he needs an exam. Husband takes my dog bc I'm at work, and you did this, and that, blood work blah blah blah. Said if you don't have all this done, no prescription. My husband not knowing paid the $400. I would of taken my dog paid the office visit and left. I will never bring any of my pets back. Your business is known to price gauge, it's all over your reviews. There is way to many affordable pet care around, and I will make sure everyone knows where else they should go.

The menu has a good selection of tasty choices, and the chefs demonstrate proficiency in the canon of creole-style cuisine, and especially w/ seafood. Luke isn't visually interesting, or particularly comfortable, but the kitchen and staff deliver a good experience.

This place is a rip off they sell bad cars. I bought a car filled up the gas tank and went home got up the next day an all the gas had leaked out. Went back up there they gave me another car it would only start when it was cool outside. I live in FL its never cool here they refused to do anything about it.i was out of money and a car
Very good Japanese restaurant with excellent sushi and noodle dishes. Food is clean and fresh. Very friendly staff and excellent service. I cannot wait to eat their after Covid.

Luke was fantastic because every dish you get had a different flavor. 
I highly suggest ordering a bunch of entrees and sharing amongst the group. Every dish has great flavor of it's own.

My personal favorites were the brussels sprouts, the lousiana jumbo shrimp and grits and the roasted chicken!

I visited Luke after a conference in New Orleans and had the best experience you could ask for. The servers were attentive, friendly and quick. The food was absolutely magnificent - we shared three dishes, a salad, brussel sprouts and the shrimp and grits entree. The dishes all came pre-split between me and my colleague. The wine selection was great, and happy hour was a great value. Next time I'm in NOLA I'll be back!

Let's just start by how amazing the service is. My hands are clapping to that! The food doesn't stay behind though. We started with cups of soup I enjoyed the gumbo. We also ordered the Brussel sprouts to start and all I can say is WOW. I've had brussel sprouts almost everywhere I can get them and the honestly take the cake. By far some of the best Brussels I have ever had. Then my bf and I shared the shrimp and grits and once again blown away. The waiter was aware that we would be sharing so he had the kitchen serve us each our own portion, which just magnifies what I said about the Service. All in all amazing experience.
Food was less than par. Disappointed that we chose this place on New Years Eve. At least they didn't make us pay for it.

It's located a short distance from the French quarters. We unfortunately missed HH but luckily had already made reservations for dinner so we were seated in the dining area not too long after we arrived. Our waitress was so friendly and professional. She gave us a number of recommendations and checked on our table throughout the night. We ordered the raw oysters, seafood gumbo, shrimp & crab etoufee, and the Brandan's bread pudding (YOU CAN NOT LEAVE WITHOUT TRYING SOMETHING OFF THEIR DESSERT MENU! )

The raw oysters were delicious. The best I've had in a while. They were obnoxiously large; some were almost the size of my hand...so fresh and sweet...

My husband's gumbo was SO good. It was very flavorful, each bite had little piece of shrimp.

The shrimp & crab etoufee fell a little flat for me. I've had etoufee at other restaurants in New Orleans and they were so creamy and savory. But Luke makes it with this large pasta that's a little too dense and can fill you up really quickly.

Brandan's bread pudding was so fluffy and the ice cream just melts in your mouth!! A must try!
Great place with great service! They prepare the oysters right in front of you at the bar. Great staff and highly recommended! Best happy hour in town!

We went to Luke because it was super close to our hotel and was highly recommend. We ended up being a little disappointed though. Although their food was good it was pretty expensive. We also got sat so close to another table that the waitress had to ask me to move every time she wanted to get to the table next to us even though there were plenty of other tables available in the restaurant. Overall it was a little over priced for my taste and had an uncomfortable seating arrangement.

Came for breakfast and had the shrimp and grits which were good. The portion is a bit small for the price but it's a tasty dish. The other dishes at the table were bland (gumbo and the burger). The burger looked amazing but the meat had absolutely no flavor so that was disappointing. 

That same night I had a taste for bread pudding and heard that Luke was the place to go. It's probably the most beautiful bread pudding I've ever seen lol. And the flavors are unmatched! Omg so good, one of the best bread puddings I've had. You have to try it!

My heat went off on Saturday morning, and I had called Fahrenheit because we had a service agreement with them from when they installed my AC.  At first, they told me they'd be at my house at mid morning,then I got a call at 1 saying they'll send someone out and be at my house between 3-4.  Long story short- they weren't here until 7pm.  Now I understand it was a weekend call but they could have been a little more upfront on time instead of making me sit in a cold house all day.  So they told my husband that our 5 year old furnace was horrible condition and needed a new one.  The price was $9,000.  The guy then also blamed my chimney for the problem. My husband and I told them no.  We needed to discuss it further.  He was almost angry and put his boss on the phone to pressure my husband.  We still said no.  Today we had another company come out, the guy fixed my heater in an hour by replacing a part plus cleaning. He charged $249 and said overall my heater was in excellent condition.  The heater had nothing to do with the chimney.  I'd never recommend them.

Best happy hour deal ever! 75cent raw oysters and 1.25$ fried oysters with half price drinks.  My kid must have eaten two dozen by himself!  72 raw oysters and 12 fried with 3 drinks only 70 something $!!!  Make reservations since its a well known deal.

A must go to for happy hour and dinner! Some things on the menu are a hit, but there are many things on the menu that are a miss....choose wisely......

FOOD:
1) Shrimp and grits:
-On point!
-The grits were very creamy and the shrimp was plumped.
-The sauce was delicious, perfectly spiced!
-If you get fries, I suggest you dip it in the sauce.

2) Mussels:
-OMG DELICIOUS!! 
-The garlic has a great kick to it, you can tell it is fresh and not the jared garlic that had been sitting around for a while.
-They give you a lot and the herbs give it a perfect slaty garlic taste.
-I highly suggest you take the shells and scoop up the sauce while you slurp up the mussels. So bomb!

3) Gumbo:
-Eh, had better elsewhere.
-It wasn't as flavorful and taste bland. 
-Missing the southern spice.

RAW BAR:
4) Raw P&J oysters:
-0.75 each! definitely worth the wait and worth getting a dozen or 2 or 3 maybe even 4. 
-Down fall..the shells are very dirty so get your napkin ready!
-I didn't expect such a huge meaty piece for the price. I am not usually a fan of larger oysters because of the bottom feeder taste to it, but these were perfect. 

5) Fried oysters:
-Can't go wrong with anything fried!
-The batter was delicious, but a little on the thick side. Made the oysters look small, but still yummy.
-The tarter sauce was creamy with a hint of tart. Great match for its breaded shell.

6) Shrimp:
-Was't my favorite from the raw bar, but it was easy to peal and had a good crunch to its bite.
-They were kind of small though......

7) Thursday special: Jambalaya $17 with soup or salad
-Not a big fan of this dish. DO NOT ORDER THIS!
-I was so disappointed with this dish. I was expecting something grand since the day before I had an amazing lunch with their mussels and shrimp and grits. Was not a great way to spend my last meal in New Orleans....such a bummer.....
-It taste over cooked and the sausage was way to smoky and salty.
-There wasn't as much sauce as I would like and the corn bread taste a bit stale.

8) Crab Cake soup
-Creamy delicious!!
-LOVED the pieces of meat inside the soup. They definitely know how to deliver a cab soup with a mix of seafood worth the price!
-Although you can get this at anytime, it was included in the daily special.

SERVICE:
-The first day I went here, we had 2 brothers (forgot their names) and they were super nice and friendly, very attentive.
-The next day, we had this nasty waiter and ruined my experience that I had previously. He seemed very annoyed with us from the moment we sat down, not a great way to great your customers.

If you're feeling sexy, and you want lunch - come to Hachi for a sexy lunch with your BFF.

This place has Manhattan UES vibes, and can tell that this place must be POPPIN' at night for the dinner and cocktails crowd.  The atmosphere is modern, crisp, and classy.  Beautiful lighting and piped in music throughout.  The tables seems to cater more to larger groups, but I can see how reservations here are a MUST for a Saturday evening.  With these prices, they are VERY reasonable.

For lunch, my gal pal and I both got the Maki Set 2, which was for any three rolls, with soup and salad with ginger dressing.  I opted for an eel avocado, spicy kani, and a yellow tail roll.  I was the most impressed with the yellowtail roll because it wasn't mashed up into an unknown fish mess - it was an ACTUAL slice of yellowtail, dressed with paper thin scallions for a fresh taste.  GET THIS ROLL!  Absolutely caught this New Yorker off guard 100%.  Expectations are high, folks!

The miso soup wasn't your average packet soup either.  There's actually slices of shiitake mushroom and generous pieces of tofu in every spoon full; this place is a GEM.

I wouldn't tell people about here though; use this place as your secret Valentine's Day weapon!

One of my favorite places for ice cream. They are only open for the seasonal time but it is worth it. They have a mix of flavors and toppings. They have some of the most unique creations and flavors and is definitely worth giving a try.

Luke is my favorite spot in the city. It's away from the hustle but still close, and is 100% New Orleans. The menu is small, but somehow managed to have a great variety. Lastly, the service is always on point. For a good time and professional waiter experience, ask for Richard. He will be sure to make your evening dining memorable.

Great date night spot! I ordered the French 75 on their cocktail menu-- delicious! I ordered the shrimp and grits, super cheesy and loaded with shrimp and sausage. They followed all COVID guidelines and each table was spaced at least six feet or plexiglass installed between tables. 
Overall great food and atmosphere, the service wasn't bad but they weren't as attentive as they could be I felt.

Overall a good place to eat.  We had a carry out.  Probably a better experience eating in.  Food was above average .  Tuna tartare was great. Soups were exception. Grilled shrimp and grits was average.  I'd go back.

LUKE IS SO GOOOOD!!!! wowwwwowwowow. This is somewhere that has been on our list for a long time. We had to wait an hour and a half for a table but it was worth it. When we were seated we were greeted by our server savannah (literally an angel from above). She got us bread, water and took our drink orders. My boyfriend got a French 75 which is made with an egg white (he's a bartender on the weekends so he was super into it) he said it was the best one he's ever had. I got the belle on the bayou, which had tequila jalapeño and blueberry and basil. A little on the spicy side but very good. We started off with the buttered crawfish bread AND WOW, it was amazing, there is burrata cheese on it then bread is nice and crispy. 

For entree's we got the burger with fries and the softshell crab blt I opted for the cheesy jalapeño grits instead of the fries! My boyfriend said it's the best burger he's ever had. The softshell crab blt is awesomeeee tooo it's opened faced so it can get kinda messy but wow. So worth it. lastly savannah brought us out the smallest dessert to try no charge!! It was a dark chocolate cake made with steam and these great amarena cherries with amarena cherry ice cream!!! It was sooooo great, truly a great night !!! Thanks savannah!!!!

We enter this beautiful sushi restaurant, and right off the bat we knew we were going to love the ambiance. The waiters and waitresses were all very kind and polite and answered all of our questions even though we just kept asking what type of fish we were eating. The fish were incredibly fresh and very delicious my fiancé loves the albacore tuna here the most out of everywhere else in this county. I personally loved my sushi so much. My rolls had an incredible amount of filling to rice ratio. You can look at my pictures and see how much thin the rice is!! That means you're getting the most worth out of your dollar. Honestly I was just so excited how well-made the sushi was. We will definitely be coming back. The cheesecake bites were delicious

We truly enjoyed our Anniversary dinner at Luke's. The food was excellent, loved the crawfish corn bisque, the P & J oysters were okay not bad. I had the soft shell crab which was delicious, my wife had the ox tails which she enjoyed. We truly enjoyed our Dinner and look forward to returning on future trips.

Happy Hour: $6 for a dozen ginormous oysters. How can you beat that? Throw in some half price drinks. Heaven.

It gets better. The Louisiana Shrimp and Grits was AMAZING. Super creamy and cheesy, and tasted of saffron. I pretty much licked the entire bowl clean.

Also had the Charcuterie plate which was good as well.

Friends had the burger, which is apparently the #4 burger in the US. She wasn't that impressed though. Other friend had the gumbo which was good as well.

I am so hungry  now.

These people are TERRIBLE.  Here's why:

1) I scheduled a maintainance/consultation (consultation was re: moving the HVAC unit).  They came and gave me costs.

2) Ghosted me for a full year.  Really.  I texted multiple times, no response.  The only reason I stuck with them is my super said they were good.

3) A year later they finally responded.  Completed maintainance at high cost, but whatever.  They were SUPER late though.

4) This year I opened the indoor unit to replace the filter myself.  They had crammed a 24x24 filter in an 18x20 slot.  It was extremely difficult to get out--I thought it was going to tear and remain stuck inside. 

So if you want to pay a LOT of money to get treated poorly and have a shoddy job done...go for it.  But really, save yourself the trouble!
Amazingly  consistent excellence. Not a mediocre dish in three visits this week! The shrimp & grits are to die for as is the fried chicken and red beans.

Dear John,

You always welcome me with open arms, and this is no exception. My first visit to Luke Bob was more than a little grumpy because he was hungry and air travel is so damn annoying and let's face it...he is a little jealous of you, so maybe halfway there he was like "here's a place, let's just eat here" or "how much further?" I ignored him and just kept moving. And hot damn...we found it.

John - all of your restaurants are different, yet wonderful in their own special way. This one is more casual than others, kind of a Shrimp and Grits and Burger kind of place. It's also on the small side, so it can get crowded (and loud). Bob settles down when you put such a wonderful burger in front of him, and that makes me happy.  And the Bread Pudding...OMG the Bread Pudding is to die for. Even Bob loves you after the Bread Pudding.

This is also one of the best happy hours in NOLA. Drinks are delish, you can get me drunk for very little money except I fill my stomach with your half price apps. I met my first Yelper here - Rene D. suggested we meet for happy hour and raw oysters. Raw oysters just aren't my thing (flashback to a Friends episode where Joey stepped on one and said it was the biggest bugger he ever saw), but I've been told they're some of the best in town and she sure enjoyed them. I didn't mind sharing you with her when you walked up, cause that's what friends are for. You know, so many people make the mistake of thinking Yelp is "just a review site" but it's so much more than that. We are family, I got all my Yelpers and me. Don't get me going.

So just keep doing what you do best, and I'll look forward to seeing you in the Spring. You know I can't stay away.

Miss L.

Had to stop in for their happy hour oysters, $.75/raw $1.25/ fried and half price wine/beer/cocktails. A dozen and a half oysters later and a gin lace cocktail and I am honestly a happy customer. The price was on point and the fresh bread was an added bonus. 

Note: the service could definitely use some work. I saw one waiter working our section who was great friendly and talkative with customers and attentive. Unfortunately when seated we waited five minutes to be acknowledged by anyone despite many staff walking around. Our waiter finally came by, but then disappeared. We would have ordered a second round of drinks but he never asked - literally had to waive him down for the bill.

Holyyyyyyy shiet you guys, first time in NOLA & I'm in love with the food & Lüke's. It's a pescetarian's dreaaaaam come true. 

Service:
Absolutely excellent. Our waitress was so friendly & kind. They ran out of wild boar ragu that Josh G. wanted, so she gifted us bread pudding for freeeeee.

Prices:
Reasonable. Slightly on the expensive, but reasonable. Definitely worth every goddamn penny though because it was so good. 

Food:
I ordered a small cup of seafood gumbo & shrimp & grits, while Josh G. got the shrimp cavatelli. We inhaled everything; it was amazing. Best shrimp grits of my friggin' life. So cheesy & full bodied umami. Shrimp was large & juicy, while the gravy was to die for. The seafood gumbo was also a great dish. So earthy & flavorful with large hunks of oyster & shrimp. A little disappointed how small the cup is. It is literally the size of 1 cup, so if you expected it to be like a mug (2 cups), nope. Josh's shrimp cavatelli was also phenomenal. Full of umami - the tomato sauce was fantastic, I would straight up bathe in dat. It was savory, not too rich, creamy, perfect mount of sweetness, & very fresh. I need that tomato sauce recipe right meow.

Then came the bread pudding. Holy expletive, batman. You done good, Chef John Besh. That vanilla ice cream atop a sweet baked bread pudding with delicious pecans & caramel was "melt in your chair, swooning over the moon or seeing your celebrity crush" good. I would like a very large bowl of that right now. Can y'all deliver to Boston plzzzz?? 

Environment:
Large restaurant with pretty decent lighting. Perfect date night or a night out with friends. 10/10 would absolutely recommend. Left so full & happy.

edited: was drunk when I wrote this, so yeah.

This is my ALL time favorite go to place!!!!  It is absolutely delicious!  You will NEVER EVER eat take-out fried rice ever again after eating Haachi's fried rice!  It is so delicious!  Presentation of all the food is excellent.  My daughter LOVES the bento box.  She is the pickiest eater but she willingly eats at this place.  

So the vegetable wasabi fried rice is a definite MUST order!  And so is the mushroom roll!

My only request to the owners would be to have more vegetarian options available!  I would love to have them create beautiful & fancy vegetarian rolls with lots of variety.  The non-vegetarian sushi/rolls look so beautiful & colorful & creative...that's what I want...only difference is that I want vegetarian!

Because of their PJ Stuffed Oysters, we have been going to Luke for a few years now. On each visit to NOLA we have made a point to eat there once, and sometimes twice, per day. We have recommended Luke to countless random new friends we've met in the French Quarter.  My wife literally dreams about these damn oysters! 

Well....no more.  They changed the recipe on the PJ Stuffed Oysters and now we can't eat them. They aren't anything like before, totally different, and we will not be going back. Really sad...

These are the biggest, freshest, meatiest raw oysters you'll ever have. Best happy hour in the city, one dollar for these massive oysters, worth every buck. You'll also find one of the best burgers in the city here.

Tokyo Sushi is located inside the Riverfront Market.

I've gotten take out sushi from here quite a few times.

The one thing that sets their takeout sushi here from other places, is the thickness and the size of the cuts of fish they give you for your nigiri!

It's like eating a small sandwich! I absolutely love it!

The portion of the fish per piece of nigiri is pretty much what other sushi restaurants use for 2 pieces of nigiri!

The husband and wife that work here are very sweet, the chef is of a few words, but you can tell he enjoys what he is doing, and takes pride in it.

Can't wait until my next visit.

This review is for Happy Hour only.

While in NOLA, I wanted to go here - lucky for me they host a happy hour that made me extremely happy.  

Its day #1 in NOLA, I've gone and partaken at the Food Festival, but still feel the need for something.  I decided oysters would hit the spot (okay and maybe a drink too).  Luke has three types of oysters, the local P&J oysters (from 3:00 to 6:00, they are only $0.50 a piece), they also have Kumomoto and Blue point.  That day, I chose to get a half dozen of the P&J and a half dozen of the blue point.  I also ordered a sazerac (of which I promptly took a picture and sent to Gregg M so he could see what he had to look forward to when he got there).  The sazerac was good - they use Herbsaint rather than Pernoud like we get up here, but I really liked it.  I thought it was very well balanced with a hint of licorice.  My second drink was the St Charles Side Car - it was extremely peary, so not my favorite.  The oysters though were definitely the highlight.  They shucked them right in front of me, keeping up a good duologue and even let me try one Kumomoto that got shucked "accidentally".  I won't say that the P&J are my favorite as they don't necessarily have some of the depth that say the blue point or the Kumomoto's have, but they sure hit the spot.  

Since I enjoyed it so much, when Gregg M got in to town, this is where I took him for an oyster fix.  We got a dozen of the P&J and a half dozen of the blue point and Kumomoto.  I'll let him tell you about his impressions, but on this trip I did get different drinks:  The mint julep was only okay to me (I'm spoiled by the one at the Majestic in Old Town!), my other drink was the French 75.  It was good, but not necessarily my favorite.  I did like Gregg's version of the St. Charles Side Car tho' - different bartender.

I can easily say I would go here again for happy hour.  Honestly their menu didn't look too bad either - but that will be for another time.

One note - the individual shucking oysters on the second trip was not very good at letting the bartender know when an order was up.  As a result, some people (including us) were waiting a little while for our oysters.  Just goes to show you how important a little communication is - even if all you are saying is "order up"

We had a lovely dinner here! It was very busy when we arrived to our reservation, but were seated right away. Everything from the menu sounded delicious! We ordered oysters, brussels sprouts, calamari & chorizo pasta, jumbo shrimp & grits and flammenkuchen. 
The the drinks were great and the food so rich in flavor! Service was amazing, everyone was so friendly and attentive.
Highly recommend! We will definitely return on our next visit to NOLA.
Best happy hour in the city! Servers are amazing and those briny oysters are amazing. Solid cocktails, too!

My son bought a car from this dealership yesterday. His salesman, John, knowingly sold him a car with a cracked fuel pump. As soon as he drove it home, there was a puddle of fluid. It cost $800 to repair the car. The mechanic says he is lucky because a spark could have ignited a fire.  "Fuel leaks are the most common cause of automobile fires".  John refused to have the car fixed or to negotiate in any way.  There are plenty of other car dealerships in the area. Do not risk losing your money. Go elsewhere.

I was in New Orleans for three days for the labor day weekend 2011 and I had food at Luke on all three days. Best Etouffe I have ever had. Service was exceptional. The oysters are half price at happy hour and my wife and I had about 60 of them. The grits are simply awesome. John Besh really knows how to create recipes. I am a fan.

The staff at Luke's is beyond amazing! Especially Josie. She deserves a raise for making sure our sick family member got her Matzoh Ball Soup and Jalepeno grits tonight. I can't wait to stop in next time we're in New Orleans.

In a word; amazing!!!!! Order the crawfish bisque, because it's perfection, and then close your eyes and point to decide on an entree because you can't go wrong! I had the shrimp and grits at brunch, and it was a perfect balance of spice, creaminess, and juicy shrimp! My fiancé had the soft shell crab BLT and it was delicious as well. The service was attentive and friendly and the bloody Marys were perfectly spicy! Yum!

Really great, friendly service and excellent food. Tried the crawfish bisque and it was sweet with a little spice. Awesome. Oysters were gorgeous and delicious and the salads were generous. Great fare.

We were here for happy hour. Service was very quick. From 3pm to 6pm, drinks are half off and oysters are $.50. The oysters were nice, plump and yummy. Luke's spicy cheesy grits were my favorite in NOLA. Drinks are half off but would otherwise be a bit pricy. We also tried Blind Pelican who has $.25 oysters but I wish I stayed here because Blind Pelican was so slow. The oysters at Luke came out so quick. Luke is a bit noisy though.
We had Christmas Day brunch and it was delicious. French bistro feel, lots of delicious seafood. I had the fried oyster salad and the oysters were perfectly cooked.

The food and drinks were flavorful but the service and atmosphere negatively impacted the experience. The server didn't know how to describe the menu items to us and we had a lot off wait time during our dining experience as well.  The cleaner used on the tables also made it sticky. Ambiance is okay.

Probably my least favorite meal in Née Orleans. My mussels were overcooked, bland and fishy. Tried a couple other dishes at the table, the crawfish étouffée was delicious but everything else was middle of the road. Not particularly good or bad, just middle of the road at best.

A special meal. My wife and I went here for my birthday. The staff were very good hosts and the food was fantastic. First things first, there's no corkage fee, so bring a bottle and enjoy. We had the flamenkuche for an appetizer. It's a flat bread with caramelized onions, cheese, and the most flavorful, smoky bacon. The fennel seeds really cinch the dish. We then had crab and corn bisque, which had a nice kick of red pepper at the finish, and the beet salad, which is better than it sounds. It's beets, a mix of greens, blue cheese, and spicy pistachios. The only criticism I could offer is that the beets would be more appealing if julienned instead of sliced. For the main, we had the shrimp en cocotte, and that's definitely the dish to get your first time. [Side note: I've had a burger before, too, and it's one of the most under-rated in town. The price is high, but the meat mix is perfect and the result is great.] For sides, we added the roasted vegetables and, of course, the frites. You really can't go there and not have the frites. Dessert was steamed chocolate with salted caramel ice cream, which sounds a little strange but tastes great.

Our waiters were pros -- they anticipated needs/wants and met them. Besh, that old Marine, sets a high standard for his restaurants and Luke lives up to it.

This restaurant was recommended by a friend and so we decided to support the owner because he was a Marine. The food was great but the service was slow, in that it seems that we had to wait over 15 minutes just for orders to get taken. Overall they had a very good selection of beer and with a Pleasant atmosphere. The staff was very friendly, easy to get along with, and down-to-earth. The food was not too pricey and it was worth the price. I would have given this restaurant a five-star rating but its level of service was very poor, minus the pleasantness of the waiters. For my meal I had the chicken and red beans and rice.

best place on the other side of Canal st.. believe what you read !!!! Best oysters I have ever had fried,and I come from oyster capital of Texas. Luke burger is FINE !! daily specials are out of this world,I had Lamb meatballs on Wed. Comes with everything. Our waitress was Suzanne,PERFECT,I wish I had just one employee,as GOOD. Pat G. Corpus Christi,Tx.
Great farm fresh food! Waiter was amazing and made awesome recommendations. A bit noisy, but it's NOLA

Happiest of Hours!
Current hours are 4-6 pm (even Saturdays) half off drinks, raw and fried oysters. Oysters tasted very fresh. They were clean and huge. Service was extrememly attentive without being intrusive. Everything was perfect. 
A short walk from the French quarter, this spot may have a wait (what place doesn't in the city) during happy hour specials, especially until they open the lower backroom dining area for dinner. 
This place may look fancy, but I can assure you our entire group left very full on a fraction of the price we would pay anywhere else in New Orleans.

The happiest moment of my New Orleans visit may have been when the waiter informed me that french fries came with my omelette... I had been having a strange craving for french fries for days! 

Ok well maybe not the happiest moment... But I was pretty happy.    

Omelette was ok, french fries were amazing.  Everything we ordered was good, not great.  

Wait staff was very friendly and accommodating.  Was not compelled to return during the rest of my visit.

Food--the quality of the food was 5 stars but it was difficult to find something that I felt like ordering.  The menu felt disjointed.  I would recommend knowing what you want before going here.  Soft shelled crab open sandwich was excellent, Brussel sprouts excellent, bisque was excellent, and of course the oysters were solid.

Service--good

Ambiance--nice restaurant was nice, clean, sleek, but also cold and basic.  

Although the food was good and I would recommend this restaurant, it was not good enough to make me come back when visiting New Orleans in the future.
Gumbo was good. Burger was average. Dessert (cheesecake to go) was insulting. Service was pretty slow and got drink order wrong plus had to be reminded about our dessert order.

Please please please do yourself a huge favor and order their crawfish bisque! It was one of the best bisques I have EVER HAD in my entire life thus far!! Not too creamy, not too salty, crawfish flavor was not overpowering, and it was simply such a well balanced bowl of heaven. Please please order this!!! You can thank me later.

Oh, and our server was super helpful by telling us about happy hour that was coming up in 30 mins. And he was more than happy to accommodate our burnt roasted Brussels sprouts. Service and food were both excellent. I recommend if you're in NoLa but even if you don't have time to dine here, just order the crawfish bisque to-go at least! It's THAT GOOD!!!

First off, big shout out to our wonderful waitress Abby - everyone knows bad service can ruin the food, no matter how great it is,  and she literally helped elevate it to another level!  This place is amazing in a completely great way!!! Had the crispy brussel sprouts, mint julep, and shrimp and grits. This is by far the best meal we have had in New Orleans,  and dare I say it,  our travels in general (across Asia, Europe,  ama most of the U.S.)? I'm pretty  sure I made everyone uncomfortable with my constant moaning,  but it couldn't be helped.  Thanks for the recommendation Yelp family...now I'm off to my food coma induced nap :)

Food is simple yet very tasty.  We came here for lunch and left very happy.  We started with a dozen raw oysters, a staple of our meals in New Orleans.  Luke sources them from P&J, so they were on par with those at Deanie's and Acme's.

For our main course, we split a bowl of the seafood gumbo and the pressed sandwich of whole roast "cochon de lait" (pork).  The portion of gumbo wasn't very big, but it was filled with seafood, including a whole chunk of shell-on crab in the middle.  The sandwich was much bigger, and featured some of the best sandwich bread I've ever had - very crispy yet buttered thoroughly.  The meat was tender though a teeny bit dry - I got over this by slathering copious amounts of delicious cherry mustard onto it.  The sandwich came with cones of hot and crispy fries.

Service is very good.  When we told them we were splitting the food, they split the sandwich and fries for us in the kitchen so we got separate plates.  The french press coffee was so good that I had two pots.

Prices for lunch are reasonable.  They have a great $15 lunch prix fixe menu as well.

I'm so glad I did not try the BBQ shrimp anywhere else, but now sadly Luke's BBQ shrimp have ruined it for all other restaurants, as they won't measure up. Richard and the team went above and beyond, the food and service was great. This will definitely be my come back to place whenever I pay a visit to this city

Excellent service, food & ambiance. Our server Rick was the perfect accompaniment to our dinner service, a perfect blend of funny & knowledgeable, his recommendations were 100% on point. I had the p&j  oysters to start and had the crab & shrimp etouffe and it was delicious!!!!  I wish I lived here so I could go broke eating here. Even sang my girl a happy birthday tune. Would definitely return next time I'm in NOLA

Hands down the freshest oysters I have ever had! It was my first time visiting Nola so of course I had to yelp a few places. It was Luke's or Acme and a bunch of my friends said Luke's! They said Acme was super touristy and crowded. They did not let me down!

We came here for happy hour and WOWZERSSS it was fresh, delicious, and best of them all CHEAP! I would highly recommend coming here for their HH special. I ordered 2 dozen oysters and half fried oysters. They aimed to please!

Hice un pedido viendo que el lugar dice que este cierra a las 11 y que tenía disponibilidad de Grubhub por lo que decidí hacer una orden (8:34), una hora paso y no recibía la confirmación, dicido llamar y resultó que ya habían cerrado.
Aquí podría hablar dos situaciones, los empleados no les gusta trabajar y quieren ser pagados por solo decir que el restauran está cerrado o si no les gusta hacer pedidos para llevar pues que quiten la opción. 
De las dos formas el restaurante al igual que el dueño quedan con una mala imagen y ojalá sean los empleados y no la cabeza de el lugar por qué me hubiese encantado ir ya que todas las reviews son positivas.
Excellent meal and venue. We sat by the kitchen window and saw the magic unfold. The roasted chicken, mussels, and fried oyster salad were so delicious.

Fantastic!!! 

Me and my husband were in NOLA for 2 nights only and were trying to see and try everything in that short period of time. We went to LUKE for a happy hour and were pleasently surprised. The waiter was fenomenal, we ordered a few local brews, dozen raw oysters and a plate of steamed mussels and that all, let me tell you, was the freshest, tastiest seafood i had eaten in NOLA!!! Outstanding quality for half the price! The oysters were so gigantic you have to cut them in half! Fresh! 

Luke was one of the highlights of our stay in New Orleans, period!

This is the place to come for oysters!!! 95% of the tables dining here had massive displays of oysters!!! I believe that the tables that did not hadn't yet place their order!

Let me start by saying they have a phenomenal happy hour and what I mean by phenomenal is every glass of wine doesn't matter the price point from high to low is half off for happy hour in addition to $.75 oysters! You cannot beat that for an upscale restaurant! I had a fairly pricey glass(well two) of Pinot Grigio that was the cost of the house white glass and was thrilled lol 

Oyster - 4 STARS 
I got four of the $.75 happy hour oysters and two of the smaller size oysters from Alabama unfortunately I forgot their name but I recall the price point at $2. each! The happy hour oyster were large and a mix between salty and sweet, they were pretty good but I preferred the Alabama small and sweet oysters that day they paired perfectly with my wine!

Bowl of gumbo - 5 STARS
Divine! For my three day business trip I had gumbo everyday if not twice! I'm so serious! Why?! Umm, there's so many ways to try it! It was amazing here and highly recommend it!

Tuna tartare - 1 STAR
Blah... the cubes of fish were hardened together by what I'm assuming as sitting in the chiller pre-molded, not saying the fish wasn't Fresh it just wasn't freshly prepared and you can tell by how the pieces hard stuck together(I do sashimi weekly) and they weren't easy to break up with a little chips that they provided! My friend doesn't like spicy and they came in a spicy sauce however didn't state anything about it being spicy of the menu. They should consider adding that.
 
Burrata mozzarella salad - 5 STARS
Only tried a lil bite, was saddened my colleague didn't wish to share. Lol 

Oyster salad - 5 STARS
Doing a little dance right now as I reminisce on how delicious this salad was! Just something about it the thick cubes of bacon and the fried oysters mixed with fresh greens that really set my soul on fire! I've never had bacon served this way but let me tell you I am forever a fan! Gotta check out my photo! Top 10 salads I've ever had! Get ready to droll! 

Luke's I'm a big fan of your food and service! I'll for sure be back when in town!

Dinner at Luke was our favorite meal on our NOLA trip! We did not make reservations but managed to snag seats at the bar and the waitstaff was very friendly and attentive. We both had the Bayou Belle for drinks and tuna tartar and oyster salad as our entrees. Cannot recommend the tuna tartar and salad enough but everything that came out of the kitchen looked fantastic so I cannot wait to come back and try more! We ended the meal with the carrot cake sundae and bread pudding, both were great and we had a hard time choosing a favorite. I would say this is a must visit restaurant for NOLA!

I personally would not come here if you are paying with a card. They charged me 11 dollars for a 5 taco's a drink. But after wards fast forward a day I check my bank account and they charged me 14 dollars. So she pretty much gave her self a tip of 3 dollars. I would have personally gave her a tip. But I was sitting their for 20 minutes and by the time she came I didn't even want the food anymore. I personally wouldn't recommend paying with a card. Money isn't an issue but it's how I didn't agree to pay a 3 dollar tip and how she decides to take a 3 dollar tip for her self! Will follow up with this and keep in mind she took a 3 dollar tip from each of us and their was a total of 2 other guys with me so a total of 9 dollars in tips she took! SMH disappointed in the service and dishonesty of this restaurant!

Luke is a Creole-inspired Brasserie located in New Orleans' Business District (near the French Quarter neighborhood).

I tried the following:
- Raw Oysters
- Silver Queen Corn & Crab Bisque
- Crispy Brussels Sprouts - toasted almonds, Espelette honey, Progress Milk Barn cheese
- Jumbo Lousiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" - roasted jalapeno cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausage
- Entrecote Grillee et Frites - Painted Hills 14oz ribeye with maitre d'hotel butter
- Shrimp and Crab "Etoufee" - heirloom tomatoes, garlic, cavatelli
- Cocktail - door#three - St. Roch vodka, pomegranate, mint, lime  

Photo of Meal:
https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=KB7vu1tVw_ykTHqTFDSnJQ&userid=NvUeb5G_mSSxgKhEE_Hueg

Overall, food was pretty good, but the trend for all of the food that we tried in New Orleans was that it was too salty for our personal preferences.  The steak was pretty good, but since most of us were from New York City, our standards were higher (nitpicky, I suppose).  

Definitely worth a trip if you're in the New Orleans area.  Just be wary that food might be a little too salty for your preferences and depends on your standards for steak.  

ENJOY!!

Lüke is one of my go-to restaurants for a nice lunch or a casual (yet upscale) dinner. It is in the John Besh Restaurant Group, a French bistro with German influences (an homage to Kolb's, a long-standing German restaurant that was located in the CBD). Lüke is moderately priced and offers something for all tastes (as long as you are not a vegetarian, but it is pescetarian friendly). The prices for lunch and dinner are similar, so it is an even better value for dinner than lunch.

My favorite item on the menu is the Lüke burger- with Emmenthaler cheese, bacon, caramelized onions lettuce, tomato. This burger is HUGE- do not hesitate to split with another diner. The burger is accompanied with thin crispy fries served in a mint julep cup. If you split the burger, they will bring each diner his/her own cup! I used to work close to Lüke, so I have eaten this burger too many times to count. It is my favorite hamburger in New Orleans.

Another favorite item on the menu is the flamenküche- a thin tarte with caramelized onions, Emmenthaler cheese, and bacon. This Alsacien onion tarte satisfies all cravings- it is crispy, salty, sweet, creamy, and cheesy. It is a perfect appetizer to split among two people during happy hour, or between several people prior to a meal. Other starters of note are the paté of Louisiana rabbit and duck livers (brought in a small glass mason jar) and the slow poached yard egg salad.

I have enjoyed many other items on Lüke's menu, many of which are ideal for seafood lovers: the fresh gulf fish (my preference is served meunière), the crabmeat ravioli, and the moules et frites are all great choices. Lüke has great daily specials. The Friday special, a redfish "court-bouillon" (a seafood stew served with rice) is my favorite and an excellent rendition of this classic Louisiana dish. There is also an extensive "raw bar" selection if you enjoy cold, fresh seafood.

Lüke also has an interesting wine selection (served in juice glasses, reminiscent of how people once enjoyed wine in their homes) and fantastic cocktails. If you enjoy bellinis, don't miss Lüke's champagne au peche. Also, Lüke serves the best French 75 in New Orleans- a perfect combination of cognac, lemon juice, and champagne, garnished with a brandied cherry. Lüke's happy hour is a well-kept secret-  1/2 price drinks and .50 oysters from 3-6. Their oysters are always of exceptional quality- typically Louisiana oysters when available.

Whether you are visiting New Orleans or a local, Lüke is an excellent dining option.
Um.. it's ok if you like child sized servings.  This is what a bowl of gumbo looks like.  Including the rice it measured out to be 1.5 cups.  For $12 yet.

This is a review for its happy hour special of 50 cent oysters, which is an amazing deal! If you love oysters, this is the place to get them for cheap. A lot of the oysters are pretty huge too, which is a big plus! Beware though that it will take some waiting time for your order of oysters to get to the table, so make sure you order enough of them the first time around. I've also tried their crab bisque, which is delicious, but I thought the portion size for a bowl is pretty small relative to its cost ($8).

I don't know what's going on here. This place has a lot of hype, but it simply does not deliver. I had a flavorless soggy breakfast here and a disgusting Bloody Mary, but decided to try it again for lunch on a different day. I ordered the matzo ball soup and expected something savory and comforting. The meat was disgusting- debatably not chicken, the broth flavorless. For the price point and in a city with endless amazing dining options, I would say skip this one.

I have patronized this establishment several times. Tonight was one of my worst experiences here. First of all the young lady seem to be paying more attention to her friends and never greeting is. Second this restaurant is within walking distance of a major grocery store, but you have no lettuce. Management should have done a paid out and purchased lettuce from Kroger. Third DeTonyea has the nastiest attitude for customer service. This is a place of business if you don't like your job, find another job. There is no excuse to run out of lettuce and you are within walking distance of a major grocery store. Bad business and no one seems to care about anything.

Came here for brunch on a Thursday morning at 10:30; we had reservations, but there were plenty of tables.

Service was great, and the ambience of the place was old-school and cozy. I ordered the pain perdu, laughing at the irony that the dish has both challah and bacon, and excited for some sweet/savory goodness.

It. Was. Delicious. And HUGE. I mean, really massive. I couldn't finish it. The mascarpone sauce was really yummy, so much so that I hardly used any syrup. I enjoyed every bite.

I also tried some of my husband's fried chicken and tabasco honey biscuit sandwich (very yummy, only a little kick from the tabasco) and cheesy grits (yes).

Decided to stop by on Valentines Day after reading all the good reviews. Ordered the BBQ Oysters. Didn't really care for them. My boyfriend had the fried chicken sandwich that he said was just ok. The Brussels sprouts and Oxtail Pasta were amazing! Drinks were a little watered down but service overall was great

Happy hour oysters for only .75 cents sounded too good to pass up on.  The oysters were so muddy and earthy. I felt like it wasn't washed or even rinsed off because my entire plate was covered with mud. That alone was enough to turn me off. I'm not sure if it's a New Orleans thing. The oyster itself wasn't crunchy or sweet. It tasted bland and so I drowned the oysters in cocktail sauce and horse radish.  I also got tired of biting into fragments of the oyster shell. You really get what you pay for.  Hog Island still wins me over by far!

I'd like to start off by saying that I've never felt the need to leave a review but after my experience with this company I feel compelled to warn others to stay away from this company.

Everyone we spoke to was rude and unprofessional. We paid $99 for a diagnostic fee that was supposed to go towards the work we agreed to have done on our heater. The only issue is we never received a quote and each time we called to find out when the quote would be sent we are told "soon". It's been three days and when the technician who came to our house, Robert, said he'll email us my husband pointed out that Robert never took down his email address. 

After 72 hours with no response it has become clear that they were going to collect the $99 diagnostic fee and never follow through on the work.

Temperatures with the wind chill have been below zero and with a two year old child in the house, all we asked is for someone to give us a quote and date for when the service will be completed and they couldn't even give us that.

Came here for a fancy birthday dinner and was not disappointed! Our server was class, the place was beautiful (especially the building its' located in) and the food was amazing. We ordered so much and loved every single thing. Their menu is mostly creole/Cajun...and then they had a couple of german items on it, which were delicious! I remember having some flatbread and the shrimp and grits, which were both great. And the bread pudding was delicious!

I went in to have an oil change done and I believe it was done, which was great. I was offered all of these extra things and a majority of them I'll have done elsewhere due to upcharging. There was one thing I specifically asked for and that was for my wiper fluid to be topped up to which they assured me they had already done so. I even asked if they were certain it had been done because it was low and they were sure. When I was almost home,  about 20 miles from the store, I tried using the wipers and no fluid came out. I called and the guy said they filled it and I should check and when I did I found a dry and dusty tube where it was supposed have just had fluid go through it. They said I can come back and have it filled but why should I do that when I specifically asked and they reassured it would be done? It leads me to think that if they can't do that simple task and don't know if they did it or not but mark that it was done then what else are they cutting corners on? Im glad I didn't buy the things they were trying to upsell because who knows if it would get done.
There was a little bit of a mixup with my delivery but they got it sorted out and I got some free cookies and it more than made up for it!!! Great job guys! And thanks for the help!

This is our new date spot! 

Felt super underdressed walking in initially, plenty of people catching dinner there after work. We didn't have a reservation but were seated in under 10min (around 7pm, Friday). The service was great and fast. Decorations were gorgeous. Food came out really fast for how packed the restaurant was. 

Have been to three other Japanese restaurants recently and this was the absolute best. 

Total bill around 32$ for about 4 different rolls. 

The fish literally melted in your mouth. Should cost WAY more for the quality and presentation.
Good beer and wine selection, thoughtful cocktail suggestions. Happy Hour from 3-6 including fresh oysters
Solo dinner at Luke's. The oysters were delish. The shrimp and grits were to die for. I really wish my beautiful Catarina was with me so I could try hers. This was a great NOLA dining experience.

Everyone always talks about how New Orleans is such a great food town. So, it can be overwhelming to figure out where to go. I decided to try Luke based solely on Yelp reviews. 

Nothing overly distinctive about the decor. But there are wait staff in white coats. I felt like (and certainly looked like) an under-dressed tourist when I walked in and saw most tables occupied. I asked if I needed a reservation, and was promptly seated in the back part of the restaurant (which adjoins the lobby of the Hilton on St. Charles). It was happy hour, so I ordered Luke's signature French 45 -- champagne and fruit juice, it was quite delicious. A waitress brought over a small baguette wrapped in a towel -- warm -- with a metal bowl of soft whipped butter. So far, so amazeballs. 

Sadly, I am not too much of a seafood eater, so oysters are lost on me. My second waitress -- yes, I had two wait staff -- recommended shrimp and grits, with an addition of crawfish (currently in season). I also ordered a salad with buratta and grilled spring onions. The salad came with two slices of toasted bread, kale, onions and mushrooms tossed in a light vinagrette. The salad smelled heavenly and the cheese was meltingly soft and spreadable on the toasted bread. 

I really have no words to describe the shrimp and grits. I know that I will not have a dish like this anywhere else, ever again. Any other variation of shrimp and grits has to pale in comparison with what I ate at Luke. Smooth, cheesy, delectable grits. Huge, fresh, delicious shrimp. Butter. Chopped pieces of sausage. I didn't want it to end. There cannot be any greater compliment for a restaurant than for a patron to say they never wanted the food they served to end. The service was also top notch. 

Thoroughly enjoyable experience and highly recommended.

Great spot to grab food. We came here for breakfast, so i can't speak to dinner, but their breakfast was very good and worth going back for!

Will definitely come back for dinner when we are back in town

My husband couldn't decide what to get from the menu. The fried Crispy Brussels Sprouts were delicious and the Butternut Squash Bisque was to die for. The wine selection was great also, they also had some drinks that were very interesting but after so many oysters we kept with the wine.

i will cerrrrtainly do an update if i try to get here again and it actually turns out SUCCESFULLY, but it clearly did not because here i am writing this, lol.

so anyways we call and they pick up and a woman answers with an obviously loudly packed busy night as we can almost not hear her over the loudness, (don't care, it's a bar, makes perfect sense) but then she tells us to wait. so we wait. for like ten minutes while, i'm pretty sure her and about two or three other people are talking away. really didn't bug us at first, but at one point it's all employees talking about their night or something, discussing something about someone being too chatty or (insert any other thing that doesn't matter for this review) and so at that point i'm just laughing and we're on speaker questioning what's going on because it seems that the phone was put and left to be ignored instead of a hold. 
so we hang up thinking this will solve it assuming we might have been forgotten about because people were right in front of the phone and had seemed to even sound like they were laughing at us questioning into the phone. someone answers again, this time not saying anything, most likely assuming it's us because we were told to wait and never got an answer, and we wait. some more. (here comes a literal line out of spongebob) so much longer in fact that we have to call back a third time and someone replies "oh, shit, (customer service is D minus at this point, lol..) hold on a second." so we wait until it's nearly one and the place's kitchen freakin' CLOSES at one so we just hung up because we were left to wait until nearly 12:50.

couldn't even make a review for the food because it is nonexistently in front of me. ctfu.
Here for a happy hour before dinner.  Bar is tiny.  Was able to get a table. Oysters were a real disappointment...no flavor.  Steamed chocolate cake, on the other hand, was amazing

steak was extremely salty.  shrimp not fresh.  poor service. little portion. $100 for 1 appetizer and 2 entrees which is very expensive compared with others in the neighborhood.  very disappointed and will never come back again.

I have had to request service on my HVAC unit EVERY SINGLE summer since the installation to refill the coolant . Once again, I am without cool air and the company has continued to appear to service my unit... for free. Obviously there is a leak in my system and the company hasn't remedied the concern. Is Fahrenheit waiting for my warranty to be up to finally FIX the issue? I am not pleased, and I feel I was ripped off !

Coolness Alert!!!!   If you look up "dive" on Wikipedia, there is probably a photo of this place--but ooh what great food!  A classic hole in the wall, that serves really terrific "authentic" Mexican food.  This place is a step up from the ubiquitous Mexican restaurants around town that all offer the same boring stuff that all tastes exactly the same (like the chips they serve).  The food here is prepared more on the authentic side, with very good sauces and traditional elements.   Very friendly waitress and cook.   It is obvious true that the cook at Mexican In (I'm not sure if the name is a good or bad pun) not only knows the recipes, but is an amazing cook in general.   If you look past the register you can see into the kitchen and see her preparing the meals.  I have eaten here several times and have never been disappointed, in fact, I have been amazed at the quality and taste of the food each time.  The mole is sublime.   The carne asada perfect.   The place is family run, and ihey definitely saved money by not putting it into the decor which is a bit worn and and sun faded walls with old Naugahyde upholstered booths, but the food is what your looking for anyway right?  If more people knew about this place, I am sure it would have a  following such as El Sol, which is the closest restaurant I can compare it to in terms of how the food tastes.  But this place is far less pretentious or  expensive.  If you can get over the divey look of the place, and the location, and just appreciate the quality of the food, you'll will have found a great alternative to the clone like Mexican restaurants where you over eat and can't even remember how it tasted afterward.  In fact, this is likely where all the people that work at those restaurants go for breakfast, lunch or dinner out at a place like this.  I should mention that although the restaurant is a bit threadbare--I have observed a a very clean kitchen, with the cook wearing a spotless apron, so we know we have a cook who is serious about food and her kitchen.  All great finds like this one have their quirks and this one's quirk is it is easy to miss.  Although it is right on Michigan just west of the intersection with Rural on the near east side, and across from an old Hardware store, it kind of just blends in.   Do yourself a favor and take a chance like I did--you'll be back again and again.    Best of all it doesn't seem to do much advertising so it is never crowded, and often you can have the whole place to yourself--perfect for that long date where you just want to sit and talk with someone, but go with your boho adventurous spirit, and appreciate the place for what it is.  Oh, one more quirk--it is cash only, but that is exactly what you would expect.  :).

Ordered two Mini Blasts, less than $6.00. Swiped my card at the drive-in box, waited 10 minutes after the computer said I was approved. 

When all of a sudden a very distracted and upset girl roller-bladed to my car. Upon her arrival I greeted her politely and said "thanks"!

She read my total to me (keep in mind she was holding my completed receipt on her tray). I started to speak, to let her know that I had already paid, she interrupted and said: "You already paid didn't you...ok here is your copy" (she rolls her eyes). I smile at her to hopefully encourage her with my non-verbals.
 
She responds with "Ugh, anyway, I don't even care. Have a good day." She then roller-bladed into the path of a moving vehicle and she stopped. I'm assuming she wanted to be hit, because she sat there for a few moments. 


Her life was spared and she skated back onto the sidewalk into the safety of her burger making nightmare. 


In short-- this may have been the most emotionally draining and darkest Sonic experience I've ever had. 

Americas Drive In!

5 Star Breakfast - Small menu but don't let that persuade you not to try it.  I have to tell you I have probably had grist 3 times in my life, but if they were as good as Luke's were I would eat them everyday!!!  The service was on point - Jackson did a great job keep my wife's coffee cup full and our needs fulfilled.

The Fried Chkn Biscuit was delish, The "Southern" Breakfast was fantastic - the breakfast meats were top notch!!!  We enjoyed it and will try to squeeze it into our already stuffed list of breakfast spots we enjoy in NOLA each trip.   D.

I had come here before years ago and remembered loving it, so I made my friends try Luke when we came here to visit. I'm so glad we did because it was awesome! 

My group came here twice in 4 days, we loved it so much. The first time we made a reservation but the second time we didn't. It didn't matter though, they managed to fit us in with no wait. 

The first time we came for a late brunch. Two of my friends got the Luke burger and I split the local crab omelette with a friend. She and I both got a cup of crab bisque to start. The crab bisque was amazing, so creamy and hot and not at all fishy. It was one of the best crab bisques I've ever had, and I make it a point to try them all. My omelette was good but a tad bit greasy. The crab in it was very fresh and they put a generous amount of it. The salad that came with the omelette had a fresh, great tasting vinaigrette. We also got fries that were ridiculously delicious! I couldn't stop eating the fries, even after I was stuffed. The guys that got the burgers loved it. They said it was simple but well-done and very filling. 

The next day we went at 3pm for happy hour. The oysters were so good and so cheap! Ditto with drinks. I see why it gets so crowded during happy hour. The only negative part of the oysters was that they were a bit gritty and the shell part was muddier than usual. But that wasn't a big deal. They were fresh and big. My non-oyster-eating friends got the "cochon de lait" sandwiches and again, they loved it. 

As for the service: the waitstaff here is on point. They're obviously career servers. Luke has great service, even when it's busy. 

All I can say is, GO. The food was amazing and I can't wait to come back. I wish we had gotten a chance to try more food here!

This place is a nice restaurant; very upscale and classic decor. They do take reservations so be sure to reserve ahead of time.

Due to the reviews, I ordered the shrimp and grits and the stuff O&J oysters. Both dishes were delicious! You have to order both!  

I think this is the best shrimp and grits I ever had. I absolutely love the andouille & green onion sausages and the big plump shrimps in the dish. It was so flavorful! Since this is pretty heavy dish, I recommend sharing it with another person. 

The O&J oysters were amazing. I would say it is similar to the charbroiled oysters, but on a higher level. The O&J oysters are stuffed with shrimp and crab. Can you say seafood heaven? Give it a shot, you won't be disappointed.

I tried my friend's grilled ribeye and french fries. If you love thin cut crispy french fries like I do,  be sure to order some on the side. It won't disappoint.

I ate here at 3:30 pm. At 7pm I started getting soo sick. I didn't have anything else to eat or drink. I called manager saying i think i got sick at your establishment. She basically told me i didnt get sick from them. Its new years and im at my hotel puking my guts out. Its my first time in new orleans and im just sitting in my hotel puking and feeling awful. I spent like 70$ there and it ruined my vacation. I explained all this to the manager and she said they werent the reason im sick.

We ended up here for brunch after being told it would be a 2-hour wait at Willa Jean. There was no wait and our waiter Desmond was incredibly pleasant and helpful, so do look out for him. Out of the cocktails, the French75 was strong yet delicious (cognac, lime juice and champagne). PJ oysters were fresh and excellent. Ask to be seated by the open kitchen for the full experience!

This wasn't the top restaurants that was originally suggested to us ahead of time, but our hotel recommended it so we decided to give it a try. Unfortunately it was pretty booked out during prime dinner times, so we made a reservation for 5 pm. Thank goodness we did!! They have a fabulous happy hour! Half off drinks, $.75 raw oysters, $1.25 fried oysters, etc! Really good deals so I recommend coming for happy hour from 3-6 pm. 

Honestly, this was the best meal we had during our one week stay in New Orleans. Better than ACME, Nola, Oceana, etc. Everything was so good. We felt like the other restaurants had only one good meal, but with Luke's, everything was delicious!! The group felt the raw oysters were the best here over all the other restaurants we went to too. The Luke burger was really good and filling. The crispy Brussels sprouts were hands down the best- it was SO good... omg! I wish I had them in front of me right now. The Jumbo Louisiana Shimp "En Cocotte" was really really good too! The shrimp Étouffée was really good too but we liked the en cocotte dish better. They do have a vegetarian option- you have to ask for it though since it's not on the menu. When I asked my waiter what my vegetarian options were... he recommended mussels... so I think he might have been confused with what vegetarian meant. He asked the chef & told us that there was a vegetarian pasta that they can make. The vegetarian pasta was SO good!! Super flavorful & very filling. It was the best vegetarian option I ate compared to all the other restaurants we went to. The jalapeño grits was also really good! 

Service was fantastic as well! Everyone was super friendly, hard working, and attentive! I definitely recommend coming here! The best food, awesome happy hour, amazing staff made the entire dining experience fnatastic!

Came here for lunch one day while visiting NOLA. Best meal the whole trip. We all really loved our food! I had oysters and my partner had a croque madame sandwich. I wish I had this restaurant close to me because I would be a regular without a doubt!
Came back for the bread pudding! The blue crab garganelli in saffron cream was loaded with crab meat and excellent!

Very underwhelming. In their defense, of all meals, we had breakfast there. But honestly, this was my least favorite meal of the whole week (vacation). The Pain Perdue was dry and one-note in flavor. The additional bacon we ordered on the side was way over cooked. Coffee, orange juice, and 2 meals cost us $50. Not impressed.

The absolute best bartender works here ! Lillian  is fabulous- grace, art and talent in action.  We came in and sat at the bar.  Lillian immediately clued us in on the happy hour deals and the food was phenomenal!!! 
We are from Baltimore so seeing barbecue shrimp wAs a bit of a turn off ( I envisioned tons of barbecue sauce over shrimp). Luckily we were befriended by some lovely military folks who made food recommendations and reassured us.   
Get the BBQ shrimp -awesome! 

Best happy hour !!!!!

Luke's is my favorite restaurant in New Orleans. The everyday happy hour from 3-6 is amazing!They also take reservations on Open Table, which is extremely convenient. This place is awesome for solo diners since they have a bar that overlooks the shucking station.

My husband and I have been ordering from Chan's Halal for awhile , So with all that's been going on with the Corona Virus and racist crap about China not to mention I love Chinese food ! We are happy to report that the food is still delicious , There was a mistake with our order and they replaced it and corrected it with no problem. They even delivered at no extra cost to us . Great Food , Polite staff
Truly a great little place, connected to the Hilton, but very nice menu and drinks.  Would return!  Salad fresh, soups great, entrees not over sauced, can really taste the food.
Great atmosphere, great service, and even greater food. Don't miss out on this one (Go for the shrimp and grits).

Nice atmosphere, low key but also nice. Feels cozy. Food was excellent. The seafood tower is not to be missed. Great oyster selection. Moules et frites is a very generous portion. Was not disappointed with the menu. Cocktails were good, great breadth of wine too. Desserts also good. But the highlight was the service. Jesse W took awesome care of my party of 6!

Unfortunately, there was a bit of an initial mixup with my party's reservation and schedule. However, the waitstaff and manager at Luke did a phenomenal job to make sure our experience was outstanding. Plus the food & drinks were amazing! Everyone was so kind, personable, and brought a lot of joy to our evening. We wanted to give a HUGE shoutout to "Ritchy Ritch" (pictured), as he went above and beyond our expectations in taking care of us! Definitely recommend paying this spot a visit in NOLA.

I really wanted to like this place more. The ambiance and decor is nice, and the service is excellent. The only thing for me was that the food was average. I came for brunch and ate the burger (it was recommended- they claim it to be nationally ranked), although the meat was tasty, the cheese and bacon weren't that good. I also tried the Madam, which was average at best.
I came here for Father's Day and the food took over an hour to come out... I was very disappointed and the staff didn't even bother to apologize about it. Will not be coming back
The faux grois appetizer was excellent, the oysters on the half shell were yummy. They do a Sazerac right there too! Echo what everyone else says about the duck.

Disappointing online order. Overcooked schnitzel, missing Mushroom vinaigrette, burnt roasted vegetables. Grilled shrimp salad was very good, tasty bacon. Buttermilk dressing not substituted with balsamic per online order. Very little attention to detail.

The "Luke Burger" was one of the best burgers I've had in my many visits to New Orleans over the years. I ordered mine without bacon, and I'm glad I did -- the burger itself was so flavorful with a slight spicy kick. I could've eaten the patty by itself. The layer of caramelized onions added another delicious tang to the sandwich. I had never had Emmenthaler before, and I hate that it's taken me this long to discover it. It added such a unique taste to the burger. Lastly, the fluffy bun did a great job of holding everything together.

The house fries, on the other hand, were disappointing. Served in a tin cup, the fries were more soggy than they were crispy. They were incredibly short -- coupled with the sogginess, they were nearly impossible to dip in ketchup. 

The service was good, but I was surprised by how long it took our food to come out. Nonetheless, everyone seemed satisfied with what they ordered.

Being an oyster fiend[1], I was allured into giving Luke a try on a warm Sunday in early September.

Given the choice, I always prefer to seat at the bar, and the bar is absolutely gorgeous, with dark wood and wonderful decorative columns. Also, check out the beautiful tin pressed ceiling. Overall the atmosphere is that of a refined, yet casual (if a bit detached), brasserie. Mid-afternoon there seemed to be mainly business people here, but I wonder what the ambiance is like in the evening.

For drinks, I asked the bartender to pick one of the local beers on tap, and I was given a glass of Luke Fru blond lager ($6.5). I don't do lager[2], and I wish I was given Luke Amber Alt instead. The draft menu, albeit limited, includes two of my favorite beers: Maredsous tripel ale ($9.50) and Aventinus dopplebock ale ($8).

Having come here specifically for oyster happy hour (P&J oysters $0.50/ea 3-6pm), we started with a plate of 24 P&J's.  Getting two dozens for two people was, in hindsight, a bit overoptimistic: these oysters are about double the size of your average oyster! However, as it often happens with these mollusks, flavor is inversely proportional to size. Apart from a nice, mineral aftertaste, I found the oysters to be bland, and the meat too soft. This oyster probably gives its best when fried.

The entree of the day was fried Mangalitsa pork loin with Belgian waffle, pecan butter, and bacon-apple hash ($15). The dish was impeccably executed: the meat was perfectly fried on the outside, and nice and tender on the inside; the presentation in a skillet was quite pleasing. Overall, however, the dish was rather heavy[3], and skewed towards a dominance of sweet notes that I found, at times, overpowering.
