Nice, solid place. The food is a bit heavy, but portions are generous and prices decidedly reasonable.
-----------------------------------
[1] And being a cheap ass, you may add.

[2] My bad for not telling the bartender.

[3] This meat already has about double the marbling of average pork.

Food:
I'll be honest, we came for $0.50 oysters during happy hour 3-6 PM every day - nice medium to large oysters, fresh, meaty, not sweet, but not too salty either. I can eat 2, maybe 3 dozen, if I was really hungry. The shame was I didn't have much appetite in the heat when we visited in March. 

Our 2nd night, I did try the bread pudding with whiskey sauce ($8), and it was scrumptious. We also tried the Blue Point oysters from Connecticut, but these were so salty, I could barely eat 2. I do prefer sweet-tasting oysters with more delicate brine flavor.

Service:
We sat at the bar next to the oyster station because we like chatting with and watching the shuckers work, and it was great. The servers are friendly, chatty, and personable. :) 

Location:
Luke is located in the Hilton, on St. Charles, 3 blocks from Canal Street. Easy walking from the French Quarter, and so worth it, if you're looking to chow down on oysters. :)

What a surprise! We live nearby and it is easy to overlook the place. But it is the best take out Chinese food ever. We love it all, especially the shrimp dishes. The spare ribs on the bone are to die for. Real fresh veggies in the dishes. This place is so far ahead of the usual take-out. I just do not get the negative reviews that are mixed in here.
Every time when I back to New Orleans for Thanks giving and I will take dinner there. I enjoyed to have a dinner with my family here. The food is very and and the price is affordable.

I am not much of a Panera fan but the wife is. So on a somewhat cold day we stopped in for her favorite bowl of soup which is only available on certain days. Reluctantly I went it. I do like there self service kiosk just cause they give u a break down on what comes on all there sandwiches and salads which is nice. I have been surprised before with a weird dressing or toping u didn't see on the menu. I went with the turkey chili. After a couple mins are meals came out nice and hot and with a side of bread. The chili was very good even though I do prefer a more thicker meager chili with some kick I wasn't disappointed and the wife's baked potatoes soup was on point.. I would have liked to see adding some cheese as an option bit I am sure there gearing more towards the healthier lifestyle. All and all was a good meal for a decent price and in would hesitate going back. That being said we got there a little pre lunch so it was pretty dead but as we were leaving u could see the lunch crowd starting to fill up the place..

If I can give this place less than one star I would.  I recently purchased a car and when I went to trade it in I was told that the car prior had never been in an accident only to find out it had been into accidents and I got less value than I was expecting.  This place lied to me just to get me into a car I had many issues with my car which is why I want to trade it in.  I urge anyone to read this review and not go to this place.

I'm definitely a fan of their Happy Hour specials. I love the 50% off cocktails. The French 75 is a must! YUM! Their raw oyster happy hour price of .75/each is fantastic. I think you have to order them in sixes. I got 12 for a meal. The oysters come with horseradish, cocktail sauce and saltines on the side. Give me a bib and I'm ready to eat! One of my companions ordered a steak and frites. He did not share the steak and I don't blame him. It looked delicious! I snuck a taste of the frites and it was the bomb. They do have wine and beers on sale too during the happy hour that runs until 6pm. We called ahead and got a table reservation. You are able to get happy hour at the dining tables too (not just at the bar). If I'm in Nola again, I will be back to Lukes!

Nice food.  Uncomfortably racist.  Gay (I am gay) waiters dancing around
 making all the money while the black shuckers do all the work.  REALLY UNCOMFORTABLE

Luke has a nice atmosphere and my table of 4 received amazing service. We got the Pâté of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken Livers for my table to share and it was a great deal due to the abundance of pâté they gave us! It came with croutons which was in the shape of sliced French bread, but since we also got bread on the table we also used that to go with the   pâté as well. My friend got the burger, which she mentioned was decent but not life changing. Another friend got an appetizer of the brussels sprouts which I tried some of and was absolutely delicious. The other appetizers, the blue crab gratin and the stuffed gulf oysters, were great as well!I also got the bread pudding dessert, which was really rich topped with delicious vanilla bean ice cream and you can definitely taste the rum in the sauce. It was good, but for its size which I felt was quite generous, it needs to be shared as it is quite filling and sweet. I took off one star due to the table we were seated at not being big enough to accommodate the food we ordered. Overall though, my friends and I had a positive experience and our waiter Matthew was attentive and made us feel comfortable.

I'm sad to say that I was disappointed with this restaurant. It was just okay. I ordered the shrimp and grits and it just didn't really do it for me. I think that could be a hang-up of mine though, because the grits just didn't have the right texture due to the cheese that was mixed into them. I guess I'm picky that way. I probably wouldn't go back to this restaurant if I ever make my way to New Orleans again. There's too much other good stuff.

Hands down the most amazing service I've ever had at a restaurant. We celebrated our anniversary here tonight and the food and service was beyond our expectations. Richard I believe his name was, greeted us with complimentary champagne and if that wasn't enough, after a fabulous meal he brought out a dessert with a candle and happy anniversary chocolate. We were blown away by this recognition of our special dinner. Thank you so much. We will be back .

Went to this place due to it being across the hotel. Food was alright-not the best,not the worst. Would stray away from the Tuna Tartare. Service was not the best-had three different waiters and needed to ask a couple times to get a glass of water. I understand it's tough times, but still :/
The food was amazing, I tried their shrimp and grits and it was seasoned to perfection. Their brunch options are competitively priced with absolutely no wait times on a Sunday morning.

Fantastic service and great food, I'm glad I came here for my last meal in New Orleans. The salad was just a dinner salad but had fresh flavors from the cherry tomatoes and beets. I had the Jambalaya special and the spicy was just right, the sausage was perfect and the pork was a great surprise. I will definitely return next time I visit.

Came here last night for our first meal in NOLA and we are so glad we did..  We ordered a dozen of the P&J raw oysters that they had on happy hour.  They were so big and delish that we had to order another dozen right away.  Honestly we could of went for another dozen but ordered other dishes instead.  

We then had a bowl of seafood&sausage gumbo which was thick, rich bowl of goodness with a nice kick from the sausage.  The we split the shrimp and grits  which was freaking amazing!!!! Ton of flavor, big ol shrimp&sausage and the jalapeno cheesy grits were on point.  We finished the meal with the strawberry shortcake which was just alright but the pistachio ice cream on it was very good.

Service was good and we had no problem finding a seat at 4 pm  for happy hour on a wed night.

We would highly recommend this place and will definitely will be back here again before the end of this trip and whenever we visit new orleans.

I moved to New Orleans a few months ago and looking to go out to a nice dinner with my boyfriend and another couple.  After some yelp searching, we decided to check out Luke.  I will say, I would give more of a 3.5 stars than 3 but overall, we would most likely not go back but wouldn't be mad if we had to go back.  

Service - was hit and miss.  We didn't have one server, but anyone in a white coat could be our server.  Because of this it took a while for someone to take our order and check on as at moments.  We did have one server who I got the attention of that we were ready to order and then he didn't come back to check on us so we had to find another server to help.  The other servers were very friendly and attentive  but it was hard to tell who to go to when we needed something.  

Cocktails - were delicious!  and bartender was attentive

Food - the four of us split the grits and brussels sprouts - both very good!  Two of us got burgers, unfortunately very very salty.  One of us got the pasta oxtail ragu -  good, very heavy and filling.  One of us got the mussels - a big bowl of tons of smaller mussels - good.  We also started with a few raw oysters and they were yummmmy.  Overall the food was good but not outstanding or super unique.  

Atmosphere - a tad disappointing.  I thought it would be kind of a cool atmosphere for a little double date but the place was filled with tourists and families dressed very casually in t-shirts and shorts.  I felt like I expected too much coming into it.

Overall I would say a great place if you're a tourist staying downtown and want a solid place to eat without having to dress too fancy.  I would not suggest it as a "special" place if you're a local, but that's how I'm learning now that I moved here!
Just wear a mask and wear gloves. There's multiple staff inside; none wore masks or had on gloves.

Saw this place had great reviews and a happy hour oyster deal so we decided to come. Disclaimer - I'm only really reviewing this place based on their happy hour oysters, which is a shame because everyone else dining in who wasn't just doing the oysters was eating such yummy looking meals! Anyways, we got seated rather quickly, pretty much immediately, which was surprising given how full the place seemed. The interior was really nice inside, and I felt like we were dining somewhere a bit classier, but still with a chill relaxed atmosphere, if that even makes any sense.

Somehow I couldn't find info on their happy hour on yelp or their website, so if I remember correctly it runs from 3pm - 6pm, although I'm not sure what on which days specifically. You can get their P & J oysters for $.75 each, which is a lot better than their usual non-happy hour price of $2 each. And I think their fried oysters are $1.25 each during happy hour.

P & J gulf oysters - these were great! Very meaty, juicy, and fresh, and I especially loved the horseradish that came along with it. Somehow I don't think I've ever had horseradish with oysters before, and now it seems like such a natural sauce to add along with the customary splash of lemon. My only critique is the lack of selection of oyster type. I felt extremely limited because there was really only one type of oyster (unless you count the fried oyster) I could order during their happy hour (I think they had other oysters, but no happy hour deals on them), and indeed I only consumed the P & Js while here.

Roasted jalapeño grits - had to try some grits too. They were great! The layer of gooey cheese atop the dish was pretty mild in flavor, but awesome, as it provided that comforting melted cheese texture. The jalapeños, however, didn't add too much flavor to the dish in my opinion, and I would have liked it if there was a bit more of a kick to the dish.

Overall, a really nice restaurant! I feel bad giving this place a 4 because I'm almost sure I would have given this place a 5 had I come here and got other dishes besides happy hour oysters. Everyone else's food looked and smelled so delicious! But no, I was here on a mission and one mission only - happy hour oysters. And it was a pretty good deal, but just not enough variety. And for that I give this place a 4. Nonetheless, I think this place is still great, just don't come here for happy hour oysters if you seek variety in your oysters.

The food tastes so authentic, unlike most of the Japanese restaurants in the burbs that offer very generic choices like teriyaki and tempura. They also offer these dishes at Hachi but they also have other choices. We tried the Toban Yaki with salmon: very good. We also had the Alligator roll and No 7 Volcano roll. My dining partner liked the Alligator roll, I liked the Volcano roll though it seemed like they had cooked salmon inside. I think they should have used raw salmon instead. The jalapeno added a fresh flavor to the roll. We ended our entree with king yellowtail nigiri. The quality of this fish was very good. For dessert we had Yuzu-ginger Crème brûlée and Green Tea ice cream. Yuzu sorbet tasted as expected though it was a bit chunky. The crème brûlée had a hint of ginger. The ice cream had won ton strips along with fresh fruit which was a welcome addion to just ice cream as most places will do.  BYOB

best place for oysters, european style seafood platters and new york times reading bistro style crowds. felt like being in paris. in a good way, not the touristy part but the old world charm. 
house pates by mr. besh are amazing, this guy knows his meat. and doesn't beat it like mr. wagner :)

Love the atmosphere here! My table was in the back and i could see the chefs cooking, which I loved. Service is very attentive and just to my liking. 

Onto the food...

First of all, try their soups!!! The seafood gumbo and crawfish bisque were amazing ways to start the meal. The crawfish head in the Bisque is stuffed -- a delightful surprise. The gumbo was super tasty but it was a little sandy when I got to the bottom of the bowl. I found a tiny rock in one of my bites :( 

The quail was well fried and I liked that they added sweetness to balance out the gaminess of the bird. The shrimp and grits were perfect -- hot and cheesy and saucy. 

Lastly, definitely definitely get the steamed chocolate & caramel ice cream. You won't regret it! It's rich and melt in your mouth amazing.

Im gonna give this place 3 stars only because I think the overall quality of the food is good. It reminds me of a more expensive panera (yes thats right-MORE expensive). I had a turkey, bacon, cheddar sandwich and chips and a drink- $11. Yikes.

First of all, the ordering is pretty confusing. The "line" was all over the place. I wasnt even sure if it was my turn to order. I just stood there like an idiot until someone asked me if they could take my order. This was mainly because the people that were taking orders were also making the food. I thought..."hm how do they keep everything straight?"

They dont.....

I grabbed my number after verbally placing my order and waited in the crowd for my food. They announce the food order and number but its so gosh darn loud in there you cant hear. So I randomly went to the counter after a few minutes and saw a sandwich sitting on a 31 slip, which was my number. It was a tiny sandwich and I immediately knew it was wrong. I told them that it was wrong and that I got a whole not a half and she goes "thats what I was calling out"....uhhh what? 

The food was mediocre tasting. Good quality. But not so good that Id come back.

From all the staff on our first and our second, we received unparalleled service. Not only did your staff find a way to seat us on an incredibly busy day but, they remembered us the next day we came in for our last meal of the trip. I would like to specifically thank Richie Rich and Chi for sending some love to thank us for visiting 2 days in a row.

This was the first time one of my best friends and I have ever taken a trip together. Ya'll made it a memorable experience for the both of us.

I will continue to visit every time I'm in NOLA.

This was definitely a moment after which I wish I had left a bigger tip lol.

This is a cute little restaurant/bar within a hotel. We came here for the Saturday from (11am - 4pm). 

Service: 
- We were immediately greeted by a friendly hostess
- We didn't have to wait long to be seated 
- the service was a slow (perhaps they're understaffed?) 

Food: 
- Delicious seafood gumbo - it's a rich dish with a variety of seafood, the rue was not too thick but not too viscous, flavorful, but I would give it 4/5 stars because it was smaller than I expected it to be 

- Baked oysters - I usually don't eat oysters, but these were AMAZING! It was coated with a pesto coat and the "taste of the sea" was not overpowering 5/5 stars

- Jalapeno grits - it's a signature side in the south, but jalapenos?!?! Brilliant! The jalapenos added a nice kick to the cheesy grits and my taste buds were rather pleased 4/5 stars

- Croque Monsieur (without an egg) and Croque Madame (with an organic egg on top) - grilled chisesi ham & emmenthaler cheese sandwich with house-made fries - it was a little too heavy of a sandwich, so it's good for sharing, they're generous with the portions 3/5 stars

Ambiance: 
-casual setting
- there are tables as well as bar seating 
- it has a creole decor theme (especially at the bar)

Finally, a kick-a$$ sushi joint in the Doylestown area. It's in a strip mall but you'd never know it once you get inside. Wonderful ambiance and a very friendly staff started our first try off well. 

We started with the oysters in three different Japanese preparations. Well prepared. The live scallop was beautifully presented but lacked flavor, I've always enjoyed live scallop served on a Tahitian salt block to add flavor, this missed the mark. However, the fried oyster roll was insanely delicious, one of the best rolls I have ever enjoyed. Crispy and delicious, beats anything I've had in the Bucks Co area. The pink elephant roll (with beets) was very good, would have been great if it had been colder vs room temp. 

The individual sushi pieces were perfect, minimal rice and a perfect cut. Not like the golf ball sized rice portions and small cuts in other top-rated places in the area. 

Loved this place, we will be back!!
Don't come here unless you want creepy old men touching you. Tots were good though and cheap pricing
Minus the indoor smoking, free popcorn, cheap drinks, and Tuesday nights are poker nights, $5 dollar tournament and the players are bad.

The only reason that I did not give Luke a 5 was the service was slow even with 2 servers helping us.  The food was good, not amazing where you think about it for a week.  But decent where you do not leave thinking it was a waste of money.

My sis ordered the steak (Does not eat anything that swims.) and I had the pasta with shrimp and blue crab.  The pasta had a kick and was not a large portion where you have to run around the block a few times after to burn it off.

The bread pudding was yummy and had a good mix of flavors.

This company is unprofessional, incredibly offensive, and incompetent. 
I called them, requested a diagnosis for my nonworking heater. Their guy showed up at my house wearing sweatpants, took a cell phone picture of my heater, and texted someone. He then tells me that I simply have a bad aquastat. 
I bought a new, $75 aquastat only to find out that my heater doesn't even use an aquastat. Completely wrong diagnosis. I called Fahrenheit back, explained the situation, and the man I spoke to on the phone (Joe) became irate, called me an asshole, and told me he hopes my heater causes my house to blow up!
I called back and spoke to Matt. He was completely unapologetic about the entire situation, berated me, and ended with (surprise, surprise), calling me an asshole and hanging up.
Later Joe texted me, to call me an asshole again. I guess he wanted me to have written proof!

What a disappointing experience.   The food was good but the service was horrible.   After ordering a second dish to eat, I ordered a second glass of wine.  The second dish arrived, I ate it and still no wine.  The waiter finally brought the wine over after I had already finished my meal.  I told him I no longer wanted the wine because I would have liked to enjoy it with my meal and asked him to bring my check.  The check had the second glass of wine so I asked him to take off the glass that arrived late.  Here is the kicker, I watched him ask the female manager to remove the item, which she did.  I then watched her take the glass of wine from the bar (that I no longer wanted) and pour it into a to go cup and take it to the kitchen.  She made no attempt to swing by my table to acknowledge or apologize.   I told the hostess about my experience, she offered no apology but did say "thanks" for letting her know.  

Service can make a good meal amazing or a good meal disappointing.   Would not recommend.

I am highly disappointed with the service and overall attention to customers. I went there with my family, waited 20 minutes even if I had a reservation and then they give us a table in the hallway. Do not recommend. Very bad place

We came in as a table of 6 and ordered family style, which was great because the dishes are so good but so rich and a few bites of each was perfect.

Must get: crawfish étoufée, shrimp and grits, rabbit and chicken livers pate, blue crab gratin, crawfish bisque

Would skip: Brussels sprouts (too sweet), beet salad (way overdressed), seafood platter (meh underwhelming)

Reservations recommended!
Amazing food and atmosphere   Busy Valentines Day and we got right in!   Seated overlooking the busy kitchen. Staff friendly

My cousin and I dropped in here for the Happy Hour specials - oysters and fine wine? Yes please!  And these oysters...  So dang good!  And humongous!  And we had amazing service.    Our waiter explained the specials, fetched us samples when he could, gave us the history of chess pie...  now I judge a place first by it's service, second by the food.  This place passed with flying colors on both.  And the Happy Hour specials are a complete deal!  Go here!

We had a problem with our HVAC system and needed some quick help to avoid melting in the heat.  I called to get a few quotes and most places charged exorbitant service call fees that didn't apply towards the resolution.  After making a few calls, Fahrenheit seemed very reasonable and would apply any fees towards a fix.  They arrived the same day (less than 2 hours actually) and got the parts ordered.  Other quotes were much more, and based on my pre-research of the parts,  seemed way out of line - but not Fahrenheit.

When the parts arrived, they showed up the same day and got me back up and running.

Everyone we talked to and interacted with was very professional, courteous, and respectful of our property.

Reading the reviews had me worried, but honestly shocked at what I read versus what I experienced.  I couldn't have asked for better.

Was disappointed with our meal here but based on the majority of positive reviews, assuming it was just a off night for them. Service was lackluster and the food was not great. We ordered the shrimp appetizer and the crab Ravigote. Most of the shrimp weren't deveined properly and the crab dish, while super fresh, had WAY too much horseradish. We love spicy but this was just over the top. Entrees were tasty but the fries were just pitiful - soggy and not seasoned. This was our last dinner while in Nola so maybe we just expected more, especially after it came so highly recommended.

Luke Burger - One of the best burgers I've had ever.  Medium rare is the way to go.
Fries -  Good

Loud, casual...food is good.

Lunch!  Out of this world gumbo soup. I had a cup along with a bacon/avocado salad with the dressing on the side. 
Terrific service, I sat at the counter. This restaurant is connected to my Hilton Hotel and very convenient.

Another great place we went to for oysters. Ridiculously fresh and happy hour is a great deal. Honestly probably my favorite place that we went to on our trip for raw oysters and I would highly recommend anyone to try it if you're like us and came here to eat several dozens.

This is a family owned establishment and I have never had a bad experience. The food, prices and location are spot on. 
My husband is from NY, and he loves this place too. Our "go to" for fast and tasty Chinese food. 
Chicken egg foo young, is a must try
This place is elegant. The food is good. Great place for a fancy brunch. Great if your in the mood for seafood.
Was in town for business training and went here for proximity to hotel. Food and service was absolutely amazing. Had the shrimp and grits and bread pudding- delicious!

Memorably, today's was the first sit-down restaurant meal we've eaten since COVID-19 shut down our adopted hometown, and Luke (333 on the Avenue) certainly did not disappoint in any aspect of our dining experience. We made OpenTable reservations upon the recommendation of two friends who had recommended Luke for their burgers, as we continued our quest for the best in the city. 

Tanya warmly greeted us from behind her mask, promptly showed us to our table, and occasionally checked to make sure that their quality standards were being maintained. Jesse quickly filled our water glasses, answered our menu questions, took our orders, and kept the experience moving right along without making us feel rushed. Gary arrived with our entrées soon after we finished our boiled and chilled and succulent--as well as really jumbo--Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp, served with delightful remoulade and shrimp cocktail sauces. Our friends had not misled us.

My wife's medium-ordered Luke Burger was served with a nice outside char and pink inside. The Swiss had beautifully melted, and because of the thickly sliced bacon, caramelized onions, tomato slice and crisp lettuce, there was no need for mayo, ketchup (the cute little bottle of which we used for dipping the fries--which were crispy on the exterior, with a lovely, flavorful, inside chew), or mustard. The burger was juicy without being greasy. While in the restaurant, our exuberance resulted in declaring it the finest burger in New Orleans; however, on further (unemotional) reflection, we agree that it is at least in the top three of the twenty or so different hamburgers ordered from as many different restaurants and cafés, out of the 88 at which we've eaten in the last 3.5 years. Congratulations, Luke, and we will be sure to let you know where you stand after we have retested the current standings in the NOLA burger trinity!

Also consumed was the Louisiana Blue Crab Garganelli, with saffron cream, creole tomatoes, wild mushrooms, chili, and parmesan, and I *do* mean consumed, as in almost inhaled. Al dente was the pasta, and the entire dish was exquisite. Upon our future returns, if we both order burgers, I'll also have to get the Blue Crab Garganelli to go--it's that good.

We are closing in on the end of this review, so here are a few words about our shared dessert, Brendan's Bread Pudding with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce. The two of us were unanimous in declaring Luke's to be the best (densest and tastiest) bread pudding that we have so far eaten in our tour of the Crescent City's culinary establishments.

Thanks to everyone who makes Luke one of the very best in New Orleans.

If you are looking for a quick bite to grab, Cosi is the place. It's hard to find other healthy options around the 36th Street and Walnut area, with Federal donuts right around the corner and the Penn Bookstore cafe right next door. Service is very quick (depending on the time) although most of the menu is overpriced. Being a regular, most of the staff is friendly to me and always let me customize my orders. If you are looking for a light lunch, I would suggest ordering the bread and one spread. I highly recommend the sun-dried tomato spread since it is very tasty. With some basil, it makes for a healthy, delicious vegan lunch.

Came back here with the wife for dinner.

We shared a cup of the crawfish bisque and seafood gumbo.  Both are probably top one or two we had while in NOLA - probably the other contender is Acme's gumbo.  The bisque came with a stuffed crawfish head and the gumbo had chunks of oysters and shrimp with perfectly spicy-salty dark roux and fluffy white rice.

Next came the oyster-avocado-ham salad which had crispy greens, perfectly dressed.  The fried oysters weren't greasy at all- crispy outside and creamy inside.  So far so good!

The entrees were good but not great.  Wife had the grilled gulf fish with crawfish, artichokes, and mushrooms.  The portion looked a bit small, and the fish although cooked well tended to have a bit too much pepper in the seasoning.  I had the roast chicken which came in a nice cast iron pot with steamed veggies and garlic mash potatoes.  I gave the drumstick to my wife and she loved it- meat falling off the bone and crispy skin.  I felt the test of the chicken had good taste for the most part, and you do need to eat the meat with the skin.  The chicken was slightly overcooked around the breast unfortunately.  A pretty good dish, but still a notch below Thomas Keller's Bouchon chicken dish.  Veggies (carrots and cauliflower) were cooked well and tender.

For dessert we had the bittersweet chocolate mousse with dulce de leche ice cream topping.  Excellent choice - the sweet ice cream combined with the bitter dark chocolate mousse underneath is a winning combination.  My wife commented that when she scraped the bottom of the dessert glass things started to taste sweet again.  Interesting contrast of flavors.

Service was flawless with the server checking up on us frequently.

Can't say enough GREAT things about the food and service @ LUKE! If you are gonna be in NOLA, you have to hit this place up! And if possible, ask for Rich! He's the best server and will make sure you have everything you need!

This will sound like a fake review but it's the real deal. For the second time FAHRENHEIT has proven itself the class act in Philadelphia HVAC. I needed a new unit in a rental apartment. Despite few bumps at the start they got it done promptly, politely and at a fair and competitive price--during a heat wave!  Other companies treat you like you are lucky to be get a call back. Chet, Robb and their team treat you like a valued customer! I will always stick with these folks.  They actually answer the phone, text back and keep you posted as the job progresses. Rick P. says thanks for solid work!!

Like is a great option for breakfast, lunch or dinner and doesn't come with the wait time of other local options with similarly priced good. While it's not my favorite restaurant in the city, there's no denying that it does a darn good job of delivering refined good with a local flair.

For breakfast I can recommend the CRAWFISH OMLETTE, which is full of crawfish and had delicious flavor. The SOUTHERN BREAKFAST is filling and basic, but they do it well.

I recommend staying away from the PAIN PERDU unless you have a serious sweet tooth. It's covered in a huge amount of what amounts to slightly sour icing made out of moscarpone cheese. The bread itself is good, but no amount of scraping fully reduced the sweetness of the icing.

The coffee is made in a French press and is rich and delicious..I highly recommend it.

The SHRIMP AND GRITS was a great choice as well.

Overall there are enough dishes here to keep you happy and well fed.

So disappointed! I was so happy that we got last minute reservation but tge service was so bad. We could not find our waiter most of the time.  Luckily the appetizer and my entrée rescue the score. The oysters were good but the soft shell crab blt was so much better.

Luke never disappoints. I go crazy over their Brussels sprouts and get them literally every time I go there. I've always enjoyed my meals, service is consistently good and their deserts are amazing. I do like sitting in the upper area better, it's more quaint and not as noisy.

Finally got the opportunity to check out Luke. Modest brunch menu but what they do, it's well done. Enjoyed what was ordered. It's a bit pricey but is what you expect to pay for the area. Bill was even 100.00 that's including one starter, two entrees, my cocktail and  tip For two people to dine. The highlight definitely was the fried oyster salad. Oysters were cooked perfectly. Service was excellent and cocktail well made!

My wife and I went here for the first time for their happy hour.  We told our waiter that we were there for the happy hour and that we were not familiar with their specials.  He verbally explained the specials and I thought that I had ordered happy hour oysters but got the stuffed oysters instead.  They were good but I was surprised when we got a $19.00 charge for six oysters. I told our waiter, who had recommended the stuffed oysters, that I thought I had ordered happy hour priced oysters.  He pointed out that the stuffed oysters were not on the happy hour menu.  Guess it was my mistake but I specifically told him that were there for happy hour.

Fun time for happy hour though they raised the price to 75 cents for oysters. A little too busy for my taste. Waitress was pretty terrible. Never brought us bread, no oyster forks, would walk right by our table without refilling water or asking if we wanted more drinks. Got 4 dozen oysters total and wait was not bad. Oysters were fresh, tasty, and meaty. Ordered an extra spicy bloody Mary and it was not spicy but extra bitter so not really sure what they did
Everything was fabulous, but the one thing that stood out among the rest were the fried brussel sprouts.  Awesome wine list, great service, impeccable cuisine.

Atmosphere: The atmosphere here is very bright and trendy, although not very cozy. It's a good place to go with the girls for dinner but maybe not the most romantic location if that is what you're going for. It is also very loud so keep that in mind. 

Cocktails: DELICIOUS! I chose the Door#Three and my friends each got the Ruston Smash. These bad boys are dangerous since they are so tasty and easy to drink but still strong. Highly recommend getting a drink. 

Appetizer: We started dinner with the Flammenkuchen. Uh-mazing. The onion! The bacon! The cheese! All so good and so well put together on a very thin crust. The portion is also HUGE, even with three girls we couldn't finish it and it was very filling. If you're going with a friend or two for cocktails and an appetizer, I would recommend this one. 

Dinner: We had three entrees at our table... the Salad Luke, the Softshell Crab BLT and the Duck Duck Rice. I can only speak for my dish (the Duck Duck Rice) but it was so good. Keep in mind I was already very full from the Flammenkuchen but this crispy rice is seriously something I still think about a month later. It was so interesting and flavorful. The duck was cooked medium rare and very tender - to be honest I usually prefer my duck a little more cooked but it was still good. Everyone else was raving about their meals so I think all around it was a hit! 

Overall, I ended up being most impressed with the cocktails and appetizer and probably could have skipped an entree but everything was so tasty and unique that I was happy I got to try so much!

Here in NOLA for a conference and I heard great things about this place... so a few colleagues and I decided to give it a try... and I do have to say the food was delicious, the service was on point and the manager checked in with us. (Server Richard and manager Tanya) we had a variety between the five of us and it tasted great.

So your probably wondering why the four stars...originally I was going to give them 5, but we came here the next day and the food came out luke warm (no pun intended) we had to ask to wake it up again and it just didn't tasted the same. Service was still great.. and the manager was very apologetic. 

I understand things can't be perfect all the time... will I come here again, yes... do I recommend yes.. just a warning it depends on the day.

I called for pricing on the non anesthesia dental cleanings they offer and they refused to give me any kind of pricing, which I find incredibly odd. I even asked for the low-high range so I could get ballpark pricing and was told they only will give me pricing after I do (and pay) for an exam, which makes no sense. So I have to pay over $100 for both my dogs in order to be given pricing? What kind of business is run this way? All kinds of red flags. If you know the pricing, even the ballpark (which should be set prices) share that information with your customers so they don't waste their time or money. Transparency in business always wins.
Amazing. Sat at the bar and had a custom drink made for me and they cooked beignets just for me!

In my search for the perfect rolling backpack for an international trip I ordered two backpacks online and had them delivered to the store. At the encouragement of my husband I also paid for a membership. The backpacks were estimated to arrive a couple weeks after I placed the order. 

About a week into the wait I thought, "Hm. That's weird. I never received a welcome email for my membership or any notification that my order was received." I called the corporate number and they told me that I had entered my email incorrectly when I signed up. Okay, cool. I take responsibility for that. When they changed my email to the correct one I still did not receive a welcome email or any notifications in my regular inbox or junk folder about my order. 

The day the store was supposed to receive the backpacks came and went. No phone call. No email notification. I called the store. After lots of confusion on the sales associate's part (including comments like, "I'm not sure why it says they haven't shipped" and "Oh, it says this order was partially filled"), they located the bags and told me I could pick them up. Oh, great, I thought. I will stop by next week when the craziness of school and work has settled down. 

A little more than a week later I stop by the store and again there is massive confusion about where my backpacks are. The sales associate who finally looked up the order said, "Your order has been canceled." Turns out, the one email I got from PayPal (not REI) said that I didn't actually pay for them and that REI would collect payment when I came in to pick them up. Again, my fault for assuming that I had paid in full for the backpacks and they were just waiting for me to go get them.

Another sales associate (who at various times is also casually eating an energy bar or something while trying to help the first one) comes up to see if they are somewhere on the floor and finds just one of the backpacks I originally ordered plus the same bag in a different color. Resignedly I say that I will take the other color and when the sales associate rings it up, it is almost 190.00 MORE than the first bag, which is on clearance. 

From beginning to end the whole ordeal has been a disaster of miscommunication and on top of it they are asking me to pay 190.00 more than what I had intended to pay for a situation that is not my fault. I ask if they can honor the price of my original order and the associate radios Brad the "manager" (and I use this word loosely) to explain the situation and ask for the price adjustment. 

Brad simply says, "Nope." Or maybe he didn't say that. Maybe he said, "F off" or "Oh, hell naw" or "Pssshaaah!" I can only guess because Brad, in his role as "manager," never came to me to apologize for the mix up or try to make it right. In fact, as I was surrounded by three sales associates (the one who helped me, the masticating one who found the backpacks, and another who had to figure out how to refund the cost of my membership), Brad walked by, saw that I was unhappy by the look on my face (which, by the way, I am proud to say I did NOT take out on anyone in the store - although I totally understand why there is yelling, fit-throwing and general rage from other people in situations like this), LOOKED ME UP AND DOWN, gave me the side eye, then passed the whole situation by. 

This made me instantly realize that I was not being treated as your typical REI shopper. Maybe I should have thrown a fit. Maybe I needed to look like I just rappelled off a mountain to get stellar service. Maybe I should have insisted. But it's not my job as a consumer who was failed by a company to make it right. The sales associates were nice enough but Brad didn't stick around long enough to have that conversation. As I was waiting for the associates to figure out how to refund my membership payment, I told them, "This whole thing could have been avoided if I received a phone call or an email from the store to let me know 1. That my backpacks had come in, 2. That my order had been canceled and/or 3. That my backpacks were being put back on the shelf." The only response I received was, "Yyyeeeeeaaaaahhhh..... Sometimes we call people and sometimes we don't, so..... Sorry."

At no point while I was in the store did anyone try to convince me to keep my membership or offer a solution about how to make it right. I called the Corporate office to complain about Brad and the entire debacle and even they could not honor the price I originally paid for the backpack that went missing. At best, they said they would communicate with Boise about my treatment in the store and offer a 30% discount on any full price backpack I did buy - which doesn't even begin to the touch the cost I would have originally paid for the backpacks I found online.

This is the worst retail experience I have ever had. And I have been to Walmart in Florida! I will never shop at REI again and I will actively encourage my friends and family to never shop there.

This review is specifically based on our experience during their 3-6pm happy hour. 

.75 raw oyster
1/2 price house draft

We came in a little after 5pm and this place was packed! We managed to find a seat open at the bar and one of us grabbed it. Apparently, you can only order if you are sitting so we told him to tell the bar to keep the dozens coming. There's about 5 guys total in our group and we destroyed what they kept bringing. 

The oysters itself were huge, fresh, juicy, hint of saltiness so not too briny. 

The restaurant was an upscale and we came way under dressed however, we had a great experience with the little time we were there.

Needs a little improvement in the service department, though I can't be exactly sure whether this is just the situation for late lunch.

We've ordered an Omakase, which came magnificently serviced with an ice sculpture and fish that was delicious like I've not tasted in quite awhile.  Tuna, Salmon, Mackerel, Snapper, etc, etc, etc.  Presentation of the food other than an Omakase was also wonderful and the Spicy seafood soup was as they say "just what the doctor ordered"

Usually places like this you don't find the level of service and food presentation like this but this restaurant is a welcome exception.

The food here was really good and flavorful. I ordered the shrimp and grits and it was good. The reason I gave 4 stars is because the food was not as hot as it could be and the flavor could have been a little spicier. The bread pudding however was amazingly delicious!

A large group of Yelpers came here to eat. As such, we were able to sample quite a few items off the menu and share with each other. 

The tamales were the best I've had in Indy. Super flavorful, moist but not greasy, and the corn-to-meat ratio is great. The huitlacoche (corn smut) quesadilla blew my mind. It was one of those foods that I'd evidently eaten in the past without knowing what it was...upon the first bite, I thought, "Yes! THAT's what that was!" Smoky and savory, I can't wait to go back and order these again. Both of these were dipped into a sauce which I was told was "salsa verde". Between my janky Spanish and the worker's lack of English, I was able to deduce that it was some sort of puree of green tomatoes, avocados, cilantro, and lemon or lime...awesome. I crave it. I even took some home with me. For entrees, we had the quail, carnitas, and some sort of meat which was allegedly goat. We decided it might have been the head. The quail was delicious and tender, and my favorite of the 3. The carnitas (slow cooked seasoned pork) were very, very good also. The mystery goat was also very tender and flavorful, but had some weird membranes and tiny bones going on. I would recommend that only for the most adventurous. 

This is not a large restaurant and it is in a pretty crappy area of the city (a block from the Rural Inn). BUT if you can get past that, the potential language barriers, and the fact that they may be out of some things, there is some seriously good stuff to be found here. If not, I recommend La Parada on New York or La Escollera on E Washington. Both are very good and authentic without quite as many issues.
Etouffee of Blue Crab & Brown Shrimp for my guests and Canard Roti for me.   Yummy

I went here for lunch with a friend - we both ordered the crab blt and some raw oysters to start. The oysters - amazing. They were nice and fresh and plump. I could have eaten another dozen. The crab blt - sigh. My friend really enjoyed hers - I did not but that is because I hate soft shell crab which is what came on this sammich. I should have known better - I mean, I was in NOLA where soft shell crab is on every corner! Anyhow, I think that the manager could sense my disappointment and walked over to me and asked if everything was OK. I told him about my soft shell crab issue and he whisked it away and brought me a burger. The burger was delicious! Big juicy beefy burger cooked to perfection served on a cutter board with a lil bucket of fries - yum yum. It was probably one of the best I've had. The service cannot be beat at Luke's either. I know when I come back to NOLA that I'll be stopping at Luke's again...

Went to check out the hype... it was pretty good. We went for breakfast on a Monday. Found out the "Brunch" menu is served only on weekends  Disappointed. 

Food was tasty but had a limited menu for weekday breakfast. Had NO Sausage and Gravy  which is a southern staple! 

Service was excellent!!! Staff was fast, patient, courteous and accommodating! Would go back because of that.  

Overall ...would go back but for dinner or brunch on a weekend. 

4 stars because of menu items, limited space and priced higher than food served.

I stopped to the drive thru on my way to work and I order the pick 2 which is the sald and sandwich.  Well I wasn't very satisfied with my food. The sandwich was more bread than the chicken avocado. I had this sandwich before and it wasn't the great today.  The salad was good the passion fruit smoothie was good.  But the sandwich was a huge disappointment for 1$8.09 for that was not great.

You sent me the wrong order thru Door Dash. I called you to correct the order and deliver it. You agreed. After waiting an hour for the food, I called and was told you don't deliver and I have to pick it up. I paid to have my correct order delivered. If you sent the wrong food, you should deliver it to me. The girl who answered and told me that you don't deliver then HUNG UP ON ME. I WILL NEVER EVER ORDER FROM THIS RESTAURANT AGAIN. THE RUDENESS AND LYING MADE ME SICK. DON'T ORDER FROM HERE, THEY'LL DISAPPOINT YOU.

Luke is another John Besh restaurant combining Franco-German food and decor to create another masterpiece. I've been here several times and each time its completely full. On this occasion we went on Christmas night expecting it to either be closed or empty and were surprised to find it so full that we were offered seats at the bar.

Not that I mind... I enjoyed watching the oyster man hard at work cracking oyster shells and placing them neatly on ice trays. Who knew it was such hard work? 

We started off with turtle soup (our favorite)...but weren't too happy when it was served lukewarm. It was still tasty but less than what we expected at a John Besh restaurant. Next, for our main course we ordered the moules & frites and the Luke Burger. Both were very tasty. Having just arrived from Canada I was shocked at the large portion but was quick to adapt to the almost triple sized portions served in the States. The mussels were enough to feed a whole family!!! I highly recommend sharing...unless you got a really healthy appetite. Most people order their oysters...however not being a fan of raw oysters I am yet to try. 

The burger was good...served along with their house made fries...salty but good! And of course we never leave without dessert: dark chocolate mousse served with orange marmalade. 

See blog post for photos: 
http://hungrynomadeats.blogspot.com/2012/01/luke-new-orleans-usa.html

Happy Hour! The oysters are fresh and delicious. I mean, they're worth it even if you don't get them in the 'happy hour' window but if you do, that's just an extra perk :) Service was friendly and attentive, even when the floor was packed because many were seeking refuge from the storm! Great vibes all around

Hands down Luke is one of the best happy hours in the French Quarter, and busy! We found ourselves here after waiting to check in at the Hilton on St. Charles Avenue just in time. Luke quickly filled up and at one time was 3 deep behind our coveted bar spot with patrons trying to get drink and 75 cent oyster orders in. Happy Hour runs from 3-6pm ; all specialty cocktails , wines and beers ate half off! It's a great time to sample a drink you may have been wanting to try, like the Sazerac or French 75, both N'awlins 'native' 'must try once drinks'. I love the French 75 here; unlike some other establishments, Luke creates this special concoction with no gin, just enough lemonade, atop a small cherry, bitters and champagne.. the attentive bartenders even swirl a ' 75' or a pink heart atop the goodness. We made this our go to hh spot during our week in Nola. Can't find a place at the bar, no worries, you can enjoy the great hh prices from a table; another rarity. Great cappuccinos, which the bartender even suggested I try a smooth shot of a liquor called 43 / Cuarenta y Tres with: SOLD. We sampled bubbles including a nice Pinot Noir bubbly from France. We opted for dinner here one night , as well. I highly recommend reservations because the place gets packed and seemed to stay that way. For dinner I had the crab bisque , the best I've had in Nola , believe it or not. I say that , because I like the bisque to have pieces of crab throughout, and this one did. For my entree, I had the ribeye with maitre de butter and topped with crab. The ribeye was tender, but fatty. The waiter offered to take it back , but I did love the flavor and ribeye is not a filet! It was good, so no need to take it away! A wonderful warm bread comes with the meal and the ambience is old French bistro and lively. John Besh is known for his amazingness in his home of New Orleans. We had just missed his being here at Luke.. maybe someday again, we will have the opportunity.. because we will def return!
Keith and his crew were awesome! I was in and out in a jiffy. No bs, just straight talkin about my car. Got me all fixed up

It's been a while since I've been to Lüke so I thought I'd give it a try for Coolinary lunch; the tantalizing appeal of "Tabasco Honey Fried Chicken" with a choice of soup was more then enough. Combined with a "lüke" warm roll for $18, it's a pretty solid deal. I opted for the cup of seafood gumbo as my soup; it was delicious, perfectly cooked melding the plentiful array of oysters and shrimp with some lagniappe of andouille and okra. When the chicken came out I was surprised how large of a portion it was; not overwhelming, the perfect size in fact, I just figured they would cut corners for Coolinary. Not only that, the chicken sat on an abundant delectable mound of red beans & rice! They were about the best damn RB&R I have every tasted; they smoke pork butt then let it cook down into the red beans. Not exactly an energy booster, but, they are frankly, to die for. The chicken was also cooked perfectly; the meat fell right off the bone and the batter was perfectly fried in both flavor and crispness. While I ate all the chicken I had about 2/3rds of my RB&R left. I'll happily enjoy those at a later juncture. The ticket time was 4 minutes for the gumbo and 12 minutes for my chicken; perfect for those on the go or the working business class! 

Final Thoughts: It really was worth it if you want to venture into the CBD on a work day. If you are in or working in the surround CBD area and on your lunch break, this is a MUST DO.

I decided to come here with my husband after a good friend's recommendation. Unfortunately, I am very disappointed from my overall experience.

I ordered the Pâté of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken Livers, and it did not have all the truffles as seen on many photos on Yelp (I had four with mine, whereas most, if not all, had six truffles/assortments). In addition, I did NOT receive the bread either. I asked the waiter if any of the truffles and/or the bread was missing, and he rudely said, "Why would you trust any of the pictures or posts on Yelp? You definitely shouldn't. We change the menu all the time, you have to know that." However, he did get the bread for my husband and I after.

We also ordered "BBQ" P&J Oysters, Specialty Oysters and Citrus Cured Gulf Tuna Tartare. The food itself tasted great, but again, the service was lacking. 

For instance, the waitress would forget to get the refills of our drinks that we requested (water and Diet Coke) several times throughout the night, to the point where we had to keep reminding her and eventually another waiter. Overall, service could be better, and the waiter could have done without the rude comment.

I arranged a trip for 10 sorority sisters and booked on Open Table.  They provided us a GREAT room, so I'm upping the stars from 3.5 to 4 stars.   Our food was good, it wasn't bad, but didn't reckon a 5 star.  Debatable 3.5-4 star. 

 But for comparison's sake, we ARE from where French( and later German)  cuisine began....Mobile,AL (1702) and the Mississippi Gulf Coast (1699). We have standards, DAMMIT!  New Orleans didn't show her face until much later (google it why don't you?) 

Our server was a great one; my husband (the lone man but didn't mind) approved the drinks mightilly!
Our purpose was to gather together and catch up- Luke provided that.

Was let down by this place.  Our first NOLA experience 5/12/19 and chose Luke's. First off the fried oyster's were delicious!  Highly recommend them.  My entree of Jumbo Shrimp En Cocotte was good but lacking in portion size as well as the sausage.  The cheesy grits, shrimp and broth were very good.  My gf ordered the blue crab blt and i gotta say it was NOT GOOD.  It looked like a mess! Miniscule amount of crab except for the shell on top of the mess. The bacon was GREY and the whole entree was as if a kid made it.  Not sure why it show's two dollar signs for expense because it is fairly expensive.  Might give it another try..l but overall wasn't impressed for such an expensive place.
Luke, like all John Besh restaurants, is amazing.  Go for happy hour and stay for dinner.  Mussels and frites are highly recommended.  Great drink selection and cocktails!

Was expecting more here.  Perhaps my expectations were too high.  

Some of the entrees were really small (Fresh Gulf Fish) while others were filling (Choucroute Garnie Maison).  Good thing an order of the charcuterie sampler was ordered along with an order of the Burger.  

I will only comment on the burger, as I believe it was the best thing on the table.  Cooked medium rare *perfect*, juicy, crispy (bacon), rich (swiss cheese), tang (caramelized onions).  The bun that it came on was sublime.  Nice and buttery toasted.

Honestly, I'd only come back for the burger.

Review update time!

I went back here again now that they're officially open. The store is a lot more filled out with tiny tables, shelves, and a little bar area to rest your cup. It really brings the place together and makes it feel more homey. Event though it's small, the space still feels super welcoming and warm.  

I had the Chai tea which was amazing. It's nothing like that super sweet stuff that's often handed out at Starbucks. This stuff is legit. Smalls Tea has made me fall in love with ginger.  Fresh ginger makes tea so spicy and it's AMAZING. I highly recommend trying out anything that's served with fresh ginger if you like spice-y tea. 

I loved the Chai so much I bought some of it so I can make it at home. I've even been inspired to add my own ginger. 

I highly recommend checking out Smalls Tea and Coffee!
This is a very nice French and creole restaurant in New Orleans.  The ambiance has a fine dining feel and the menu is really pleasing to foodies.  It's all about flavor and taste.

My husband took me here for Valentine's day. The service was great,  but it was loud. I wouldn't suggest it for a romantic evening. I had an espresso martini that was just enough espresso to vodka ratio. We had the stuffed p&j oysters..... totally amazing! They were topped with a shrimp & crab stuffing that was so rich and delicious. If you like meat,  I suggest the duck duck rice. It was full of flavor and juicy. the rice was crunchy,  like rice crispy but it was savory. I had the tasso rubbed yellowfin tuna. This entree and the noise were the only reason I gave 4 stars. It just didn't work. It was  a bean stew that would've gone with a pork chop,  but not tuna. Everything else about the dinner was great!

Luke's was recommended to us and SO happy we went. Our server, Richie Rich (yes that's his name) was amazing. By far the best thing we ate was the Crispy Brussel Sprouts. They were so delicious that we actually went back the next day just to have the house special cocktails, Door#3 was awesome, and more Brussel sprouts! The only down side was the volume of the room where we sat. The back room echoes and they seat large parties there as well as 2 & 4 tops but at times we couldn't hear each other talk. Definitely going back the next time I'm in NOLA.
What can I say. Food, service all of it was perfect. We had the steak and étouffée. A little foie gras to begin with started us off nicely.
A very pleasant surprise of an awesome late lunch. Full disclosure - the Bloody Mary's are spicy.

We came here for happy hour for the oysters and it was lovely.  Drinks were tasty and the raw oysters were so divine, we had to get another dozen.  Too bad our waiter never came back with them.  Great food and drinks, not so great service.

House of China has the best Chinese food hands down. When we go, we get Hot Crispy Beef, Pepper Chicken, Crab Rangoon, and Fried Rice. I have a friend that just moved to the Lutz area and I got her hooked! I would totally recommend this place to anyone.

TL;DR this place may be good for happy hour oysters but don't expect anything extraordinary otherwise. Service is good. 

Okay, if you look at most of my other reviews from this week, you'll see why this was such a disappointment. Expectations were high and ultimately we felt like everything we had here ranged from mediocre to just okay.

To start, my wife asked for a recommendation on a dry wine but got a fairly sweet wine with a slightly dry finish (I tasted it and agreed even though I barely know wine). She felt bad about asking for a different glass but the waiter gladly replaced it... with the most watery, flavorless wine either of us have tasted. At least it wasn't sweet?

We started with the oysters, a half-dozen each of the Miyagi and Southern Belle. My wife liked the more briny Miyagis and I liked the more balanced Belles but neither of us felt like they were special in any way.

We then put in the rest of our order, asking how much food we should order. We asked for the Blue Crab Gratin, the famed Crispy Brussels Sprouts, and the Softshell Crab BLT. These were all recommended by the waiter and he didn't think it would be too much food.

The Brussels should be called Soggy rather than Crispy since they have so much balsamic glaze on them. I found them way too sweet and the cheese wasn't helping. I did have one nice bite with a fresh jalapeño but there weren't enough of those to save the dish. The Gratin was fine, nothing special.

Even with these starters half-eaten, we were full and probably should have canceled the Crab BLT but also figured it was already being made and would feel guilty canceling this late. It soon arrived, split for the two of us and it would have been more than enough food by itself for an entire meal (even before the oysters). 

Looking at the generous cup of fries that each of us got and the fairly large sandwich on each of our plates, we couldn't figure out how the waiter would have let us order all this food.

We did our best but the fries were mediocre and the sandwich was fine. We agreed that the oysters were probably the best part of the meal but nothing to write home about. Compared to most of the meals we've had here, the food lacked creativity and savory, unique flavors.
The seafood gumbo was okay. Prion was nice size. No crab shrimp were very tender but very small. I wish I would have tried something else. Ice tea was perfect.

I can't say enough positive things about this restaurant! The food is outstanding. I have dined here three times and will return anytime I come back to NOLA. The baked oysters and grits are a must. But the best park of my experience was the staff, Rich Whatley took care of us and made the entire night incredible! Thank you Rich.
Great wings and tacos basket. Frosted glasses for the beer. Great neighborhood bar. Great beer selection.  Great wait staff very friendly.

This little sushi spot is a gem!  The Tempura Shrimp Rolls were fresh and the portions generous! One roll we ate had crab on the top and it was a nice addition. The prices were unbelievably reasonable. I think we'll visit this place again while I'm in town.

Excellent breakfast. The grits were so creamy and good. We had the southern breakfast but after having the grits I wish I had the shrimp and grits breakfast.  Oh well next time!!!! The service was outstanding and friendly to boot!!!!

I hosted brunch at Luke the morning after my wedding. I had never been before, but the team who helped me with planning and booking was super professional and really accommodating. I picked the menu purely based off of my own preferences and I was shocked by how good the food was. The crispy Brussels sprouts were so incredibly good. We ordered appetizers for all the tables and I am pretty sure that I ate one entire order myself they were so incredibly good. The stuffed French toast was also to die for. I am not a sweets person but this dish was so incredibly unique and the perfect balance of fruity and sweet. I had the fried chicken and waffles and I think that is the best entree for brunch. Everyone was stuffed and absolutely loved the food. Great prices and ambiance compared to some of the other fancier restaurants in New Orleans. This place is fantastic for brunch.
My second time here, this time for my friends wedding reception! Menu was amazing!

Went there for a French 75. We were not impressed. It tasted like a whiskey sour. The food was very good. Flammenkuchen, Brussels sprouts and fresh oysters all excellent. Service very good. Serving the bread in a bag is a bit like a local diner. 

Overall we enjoyed
Mediocre at best. I really wanted to like this place but have been 3 times and it's just been ok all 3 times. Food is lackluster and serves is just ok

Horrible!!!! When I arrived I was told my order given to another customer and they were on the way back. I was reluctant to take the food that was given to the other customer but he came right back and it was still hot. Ok it gets worst SMH My shrimp rolls had no shrimp in them. I got 3 and not one of them had any. My Shrimp Lo Mein had not shrimp, but it did include hair. I called the store to let them know and I was put on hold so long that I just hung up. I was very disappointed because the food use to be good. I will never order from here again or recommend them. I really wanted to give them no stars but the person that took my order was very nice.

My husband and I ate at Luke last Saturday for our 29th anniversary.  The food and the service were excellent!  I would definitely recommend this restaurant to everyone for a very special dining experience!
Best sushi in the area, plus we love their noodle dishes and seafood pancake, even thru covid. DANG I miss their SUSHI BAR so much ! Help keep Hachi in town! Love love love this restaurant!

This restaurant services the Hilton St. Charles hotel.  We ordered in-room breakfast, food & coffee was cold when it was delivered.  I complained to the hotel & they said I would receive a credit.  Today I checked out & no credit was given.  Management ignored my complain today.

Came for lunch on a trip to New Orleans and I was very pleased with the food.  The restaurant had a comfortable atmosphere and was not the white-table clothed establishment that I was expecting.  A mellow-professional atmosphere.

For breakfast we shared the P&J oysters and the foie gras (it's delicious, I know, and we can't get it in California anymore so it was a must-have), and then proceeded to munch on the crab omelet and the eggs in a jar.  The crab omelet was light and the eggs must be how eggs taste in heaven -- I certainly haven't been able to replicate the lightness of the eggs at home.  If I were to come back for lunch, I would go for the eggs in a jar - beautifully crafted and delicious.

Service was little lackluster for a restaurant of this caliber.  It felt like I would have to wave someone down to get my water re-filled or to ask for something else.  Perhaps the quality of service is a bit different in the evenings.  But, the service wouldn't stop me from coming here again -- it's just an observation.

Good service! Nice people. Lots of options. Just didn't personally like the food enough. We ordered chicken/rabbit pate charcuterie plate, raw oysters, and something else but I can't remember.

I love raw oysters, but these were huge and kind of gross tasting. The best oysters are the smaller sweeter ones (an example is kumamoto). Obviously, they don't have that type of oyster in Nola, so not their fault. It's just hard to enjoy it after having raw oysters elevated in izakaya restaurants with ponzu sauce, chives, and tobiko. We both didn't like the oysters, so we had to leave them. I felt bad that they had to die for no reason, oh well :/

I usually LOVE pate, but I think the rabbit added a strange taste to the pate which made it less appealing. It was definitely worth the try though! I love trying new and unique foods.

First official meal in NOLA! A fine restaurant to dine in. The service is good and the speed to serve disjes is fast . We ordered 8 oyster for happy hour. We also ordered rabbit liver plate and seafood gumbo and shrimp with grit. Generally good but salty...Drink a lot of water...The oysters were great and very fresh.

I downgraded it by one star after the trip in NOLA. Really mediocre food and way too salty...

Went there for breakfast and had the best fried chicken and biscuit I've ever had. It had a jalapeño bacon marmalade that elevated what should have been a simple  breakfast sandwich, to another level. Oh so yummy!

The best shrimp and grits! I was surprised that I got delicious shrimp and grits at a hotel restaurant but they were so so good. We got another side of grits. If my memory serves me right, the grits are cheesy. We are at the bar as the restuarant was super crowded. Definitely worth stopping by if you are in New Orleans.

Amazing happy hour deal here but come early or have a reservation!! We arrived at exactly 3pm on a Thursday and it was already packed. The oysters are only 75 cents and cocktails are 1/2 off though! The oysters are decent sized and tasty and the cool dudes shucking the oysters even gave us a few extra for free! The French 75 cocktail was also really refreshing.

Excellent service and delicious food. We went here for happy hour upon arrival in New Orleans and it was amazing. The PJ Oysters were so large and fresh and delicious . I absolutely could have eaten all 12. The fried ones were delicious too (but since it trying to be good I only ate like 3). Let talk about the drinks! FIRE!!! The bartender hooked us up!! I was literally tipsy off of my first Ponchatoula porch punch. I felt like a pirate (ahoy). I can not express how amazing it was, definitely try that punch. The service was excellent!!! Shout out to Gary. If you get a chance, definitely go visit Luke's.
Wow !! Is an understatement. I was only in New Orleans a couple of hours !! This place is amazing the brunch is good big portions!! U have to have the fried chicken & red beans

Disappointed in the level of care. On my first visit I mentioned my cat was scratching his ears.  The Vet notated debris in them but did not examine further. I took him back today and they said he has ear mites. This should have been diagnosed in the previous visit. They seem to be more interested in up selling additional exams, medicine and Wellness Plans than actually taking care of the animal. Also, there was feces on their bench in the waiting area.

We have looking for a local sushi place that has a good selection and great quality at a reasonable price. Look no further, Hachi in Chalfont is the real deal!

Friendly and helpful staff and a menu that is quite extensive. They had an extensive amount of takeout orders but I really am happy to be back in a restaurant. The sushi was on point and we can't wait to go back.

Wife and I ate lunch here. I ordered the tomato/bacon/grilled cheese sandwich. The sandwich was trying too hard to be foo-foo. Instead of regular tomato, they use tomato confit (basically a grilled tomato with herbs, olive oil, etc). The tomato skins were chewy, so I pulled them out. The tomatoes themselves tasted terrible. The bacon was hard and tasteless. Regular ol' bacon would've been nice. The cheese had a somewhat bitter taste. Foo-foo again. How 'bout regular American cheese, like most grilled cheese sandwiches have? The bread was the only thing that tasted good.

Foo-Foo bacon with Foo-Foo tomatoes with Foo-Foo cheese made up a Poo-Poo sandwich. I was so disgusted, I bought a loaf of sourdough, some high-quality bacon, a REGULAR tomato, cheese, and made my own at home. Excellent sandwich.

WASTE OF MONEY AND TIME. 
Called for a heating issue, technician arrived and gave me an estimate over the phone of $5,800, he said the system needs to be replaced completely... I asked for a written diagnosis of his visit but never got that.
I brought two other technicians, both diagnosed it as a very minor issue and indeed the issue was actually fixed eventually for $200 by a different company, there was no need for a complete system replacement as Fahrenheit almost made me doing,
As I've seen in other reviews, many of the 5 stars are due to a discount offered for a good review. I'm definitely not going to use or recommend them again

We opted Luke for a fine dining spot in NOLA. We went for happy hour. It saddened me a bit though, because we came right before happy hour ended, and our server returned later, saying he could not grant us happy hour pricing. he did kind of meet us in the middle, with pricing though. Our trip to NOLA would not have been the same if we hadn't come here. It was a little ways off from bourbon street, but still very walkable.

The service was SO attentive, and knowledgeable.  We had the P &J oysters. BEST raw oysters in NOLA. They were clean, meaty, and just tasted so good. We inhaled these. ordered more and more, and these were easily the main component of our meal. We ordered salads and soups on the side.  if you can make it for happy hour, i'd definitely come back here. They also had half-priced glasses of wine, with a great variety offered. 

As a complimentary appetizer, we were given brussel sprouts. I'd NEVER had these in my life, but dang. These were great! nice sauce/dressing, some bacon, and a good crunch and texture to these. Makes me sad that I've been missing out on these all my life! I'm so glad i had something i never thought I would try before.

To finish, we had the bread pudding, which was great for a southern staple. Not overly sweet or rich.

We had breakfast here today. It was better than I expected. The shrimp and grits was the most flavorful I've ever had and served with two perfectly cooked sunny side up eggs on top. The bourbon punch is the southern brunch cocktail of my dreams. The coffee was strong. The service was exceptional. The place is intimate, but not so that you can hear conversations at other tables. I wish we could go back several times.

Fun time there.  Made a last minute dinner reservation for a party of ten.  They handled it with great service and humor.

The food was plentiful and yummy.  We tried a good cross section of their menu and everything was delicious and filling.

All in all a great evening

Its a John Besh restaurant so my expectations were elevated.  We started with the Oysters and they were good a fresh.  Got the shrimp and grits and it was average at best.  To be honest it tasted kinda burnt.  My son got sliders which were great.  But for this class of restaurant and expense it pretty sad to say order the sliders.  I would skip it and try one of Emeril's places on my next trip.

My friend and I went here for dinner tonight. We had a groupon that was given to me as a gift. We were excited to try it out since it is close by. Unfortunately it was pretty packed, probably due to the flyers game. We walked in with no idea of what to do. We wanted a table but there was no one to seat us. We went to the bar to ask what to do and no one acknowledged us. We ended up leaving because we couldn't get any service or attention. It seemed like a dive bar to me anyway which I don't usually like but since we got a free coupon I guess we have no choice but to return.

Had a late reservation and showed up there straight from our kayak tour. Felt a little weird because people were sort of nicely dressed. However, the staff was still very nice and friendly. It took about 10 mins for us to get attended to but once we did, the server was wonderful. He had lots of great suggestions too. We got the crawfish étouffée, cheesy jalapeño grits, shrimp, and for dessert the pecan maple butter bread pudding. The grits were so cheesy and good, the crawfish étouffée was very tasty, and the bread pudding was absolutely delicious. A must visit for when in New Orleans, but remember to dress nice.

Clean. Fairly quick service but was sat all the way in the very back which made us feel like only the fancy Caucasians got to sit up front. At first. 

But seriously, The service was great. The food was beautifully presented and extremely tasty.  The two of us shared four appetizers as our meal. We had more than enough to eat and our taste buds and bellies were very happy

We came here for Easter brunch and there were a lot of good things about it. The mains were very good- I had the shrimp and grits (grits w/cheddar and jalapeño), which was amazing. Great flavors. And I really appreciate that they worked with us to expand our reservation from 2 to 6 the night before what I am sure is a very busy time for them.

That being said, I was a little disappointed by the size of the menu; not a lot of options. And some of the side dishes weren't great.. the home fries were smothered in onions. Overall I thought it was a perfectly acceptable brunch spot, but a little pricey to not be wowed.

From the moment we walked in, the staff at Luke Restaurant treated me and my friend like royalty. From the beginning to the end, the service, atmosphere, and food was incredible. The servers are passionate about the food they serve, and they made everything on the menu sound so tummy! We loved "Richie Rich" and his fun personality; he checked on us several times, and we loved him so much, we wanted him to sit with us. Kevin was our waiter, and he is fantastic! This was my first time here, and I am definitely coming back for happy hour (great deals on oysters and cocktails), girl's nights, and I'll be treating my business clients here for marketing lunches. It was all amazing! Food recs: Brussels sprouts, any fish entree, and bread pudding.

Came here for New Year's Day brunch. Arrived 5 minutes before our 1215 reservation and were seated promptly. It is in an historic building that is currently a Hilton hotel. The decor is period and is beautifully preserved early 20th century. The waitstaff has very smart white jackets and ties. We started with a tasty Bloody Mary and a drink called w2 which is a combo of whiskey, wine and a syrup. I didn't try it but the husband said it was good. 
   We ordered a cup of crab and corn bisque and one of roasted chicken matzo ball soup. The soups were piping hot and both were excellent. They were both packed with their respective meats. The crab was fresh and sweet. We weren't terribly hungry so we decided to split the red beans and rice which the kitchen was kind enough to do for us. It came with a crispy chicken breast drizzled with tobasco honey. The chicken and the red beans and rice were both very good, with the rice being fragrant- possibly jasmine. Some of the best I have had. 
   Our daughter chose the shrimp and crab crepes though I'm not sure what the sauce was- she pronounced it excellent. It was a lovely meal and the service was exemplary. There is also a great deal of raw oyster selections of one chooses. This is a great place for a special brunch or dinner.

This was my first stop in New Orleans and I'll always remember it--sat at the bar and was well cared for by fun, enthusiastic, and just-the-right-amount if attentive service. 

Ordered half a dozen oysters (YUM!) but a dozen came...they still only charged me for the half. Got crab and crawfish etouffee--this was the star of the show. Silky and rich and lovely. The crispy rice is a beautiful touch of textural difference. Ugh. I wanna go back. 

Ruined my perfect meal with bread pudding as suggested by staff. I get that it's a specialty, I get that it's typically highly rated...I just discovered that I don't love bread pudding. And after such a delightful couple of bright seafood rounds, a heavy ass bread pudding just wasn't right.  It that's my fault, I should know better.

Elm Café has been on my list forever but I'm hardly ever downtown to eat. It's especially hard when it's one of those shops that close early. Well, I finally made it and met up with my boy G for lunch Thursday.

The inside is TINY (it's oddly similar in size and layout to Farrow Sandwiches). There's exactly four stools to sit at so most people were taking their sandwiches, pastries and coffees to go. 

They were already out of soup when we arrived but they do two types of sandwiches: earlies ($8.00) and lunch ($9.00). Check their Twitter feed (@elmcafe) to see what the daily specials.

- Banana walnut muffin ($3.00) - muffin was satisfyingly moist with a banana bread like consistency and walnuts mixed in for good measure.

- Risk it for the brisket ($9.00) - beef brisket, pulled pork, soy BBQ sauce, pineapple slaw, sesame mayo, lime and greens. Beware, this sandwich was one hot mess.
