Sauce was oozing out but it was worth getting your hands dirty for. Meat was tender and tasty, pineapple added a bit of sweetness and the spinach/coleslaw mixture gave it a healthy crunchy bite.

If you plan on coming often, grab one of their stamp cards. It's buy 12, get the 13th free (cue eye roll numero deux). Maybe if you could use it at their other locations (Burrow Cafe, Little Brick and District Cafe) but I doubt it. Anyways, cool lil' sandwich spot to grab a quick bite.

Out last night in New Orleans dined at Luke and glad we did. The shrimp and grits was delicious. Large shrimp was cooked just right and grits were very creamy.  We ordered the gumbo which was good. The pate was one of the best we've had.  The stuff oyster was basically like baked clams but with oyster...very good.  Skip the blue crab dip; not worth writing about. The special for October was pork schnitzel with mushroom sauce.  My husband's order had 3 good size cutlets which were tender but a little on the dry side.   Overall a good meal but our dishes were not cleared for 15 mins so we just skipped dessert and asked for the check.  The plus is that they took reservations on open table.

I have a self imposed rule to steer clear of restaurants in hotels because I theorize that they usually aren't great and wouldn't be able to survive on their own merit were it not for the hotel traffic.

This place is an exception and comes with a big name in the culinary world, John Besh. It doesn't feel like a hotel restaurant as it is separated and in an old and warm feeling space adjacent to the hotel lobby. The food is seafood and cajun influenced. I had some sort of shrimp etouffee on grits that was simple and wonderful. I coupled my meal with a great glass of wine and sadly stayed away from dessert to save myself a few calories.

The only negative thing that I would note is that it is loaded with tourist type folks. Not always bad but it can make for bigger and louder groups that at times intrude on converstation.

In all, it was really great. I will be back here soon.

My heater abruptly stopped working and it seemed pretty clear that the issue was a faulty thermocoupler, a relatively simple repair (though one I did not want to do myself, given the fire hazard).  I called up Fahrenheit who sent a technician, and explained to the tech what I believed the problem was.  He replied that it was not the thermocouple, but a faulty valve which would be $850 to repair.  I was suspicious, especially since the tech did not seems to really examine the furnace (which was only a few years old) all that much, and I got a second opinion.  Another company checked it out the following day, confirmed that it was in fact the thermocouple, and performed a repair on the spot for $140 total.  Heater is fine now.  The other company's rep also told me that, even if the problem truly was the gas valve, $850 was a ridiculous price. 

Stay away from this company.  They apparently tried to put one over on me even though I had identified the problem before they arrived and told them what it was.  I can only imagine what they would do to people who aren't familiar with heating/cooling systems.

Very friendly staff. We ordered a variety of items some were great and others were just ok. Pick up order also came with fried wontons and duck sauce so that was a nice surprise. I asked that the food be cooked in less oil and they listened. We will be back but next time we will skip the soup and tofu dish.

I've been to New Orleans twice.  I've been to Luke's 5 times.  4 of which is to their happy hour - M-F 3-6p.  $0.50 freshly shucked oysters.  Some people complained about the size of the oysters... hey, when it's the size of my handful I'm pretty stoked!  

The only thing is since it's cheap sometimes there's a lot of dirt on the meat.  Maybe because it's the high demand they had to shuck fast.  

Mixed cocktails are 50% off.  Normally around $10 each would be $5.  They don't skimp on liquor neither just because it's happy hour.  The French something is really delicious, it's cognac, champaign and lemon juice.  With a little syrup heart on top of the foam.  I also really like the other one with champaign and lemon peel in a champaign flute.  I forgot the name though....  I just keep thinking about that oysters...  so amazing.  Best deal in town for fresh oysters!

Had to make this one of my FAVS!  Don't miss this place.

Food:  Great oysters.  Fried or raw.

Atmosphere:  Cozy.  Get to happy hour early to get a seat at the bar 

Value:  Unbelievable value.

Service:  Outstanding from what we could tell.  Knowledgeable about other places in city for your next stop.

This is the best happy hour I have been to in NOLA - especially for the oysters. I have never been to an establishment that provide to you such big oysters. Seriously, you may think you're eating something from a different planet. Surprisingly, the flavor is fantastic which is not what I always experience with large oysters. The place gets crowded really quickly so be prepared to get there early or to wait in line. My wife and I have tried a number of the drinks there, and they are all good - with the Sazerac being quite delicious.

You can't get a better value and environment outside of Luke's which is why people rush to get there for the happy hour all days of the week.

Great all-around. We hadn't done much research and didn't make a reservation, but the hostess still got us a table for 3 at 6:00 (with the promise that we'd be done before 8)
The Poulet Grand-Mère was extremely flavorful and tender, the Étouffée was delicious, and the burger and fries were fantastic. Their beers were great too.

Service was great. The waiter was super friendly and made great suggestions.

You should make a reservation because I think we were really lucky to get in (plus it was a Monday)
We loved our meal, the ambiance and the excellent service by the wait staff and bar, who were unobtrusive but very attentive. Food was delicious, exceptional paté, our favorite.
Perfection! Great atmosphere, delicious food, friendly staff. Our first time here tonight and it won't be our last.
If you want to try authentic Cajun and Creole food this restaurant can give that experience. Loved their seafood and desert. And the service was excellent. Will definitely one back here.
Junk. Don't do it. They obviously have a very poor mechanic that rigs issues. Don't do it.

Amazing place! The food was out of this world fantastic. We knew what to expect there because of the great photos and reviews here on yelp. But the best part of our meal here was the servers and the service. We had a late lunch with my husband, mother in law and my LO 11 months old baby girl. The staff was so friendly and accommodating. Thank you!

My wife and I visited Panera. My wife ordered a salad and I ordered a ham and cheese sandwich. The salad was passé and the sandwich was dry, crumbly and tasteless. We both had decided to try them but were equally disappointed in the quality of the result. We usually give another try to an establishment, bur didn't think it was going to be any better. Very sad experience.

I honestly didn't know what the hype was for New Orleans food. It's just regular food right? No. New Orleans has some serious food and Lüke was my first experience of just knowing how delicious New Orleans food can really be. 

I came here for a cocktail hour so the whole back room was for our party. It's a great place if you want to rent out because theres an open kitchen concept there. I love the idea of open kitchen because deep down I want to see a Gordon Ramsay Hells Kitchen moment of someone cursing. Although, that didn't happen the food that came our was delicious and didn't stop. All the guest were completely satisfied. When you rent out the back they have a buffet style vibe with unlimited alcohol. My friends and I definitely took advantage of this open bar idea because hey, how often are we in New Orleans? and how often is a close friend getting married? 

Anyway, we got a great selection of their menu a little bit of everything. My friends were a little wary about eating oysters since they're raw but honestly oysters are the best! And especially being in New Orleans I had to take advantage of their seafood. The rest of the food was amazing and you can't make a bad decision.

The waiters were so attentive in making sure to give us another cocktail if he saw we were low and made sure to clean up anything on the tables. So happy my friends had a cocktail party here and will definitely be coming back here. There's no other place I can compare to New Orleans!

A solid 4-star Chinese restaurant. My sweet husband and I tried house of China tonight and found it to be quite good. We tried the house Mei fun, the orange chicken and the rangoons.  The Mei fun was a bit on the plain side for our taste but we added a little soy sauce and it helped a lot. The orange chicken was crisp and sweet, not spicy (which we miss) but it was very tasty. The rangoons were crunchy and full of cream cheese, very flavorful and not at all greasy. The service was great and they were super fast. Over all we were quite happy with our meal and will definitely be back.

We were there for dinner last night. Service was excellent, the place is very clean. Must try their raw oysters, they're super clean and fresh. One of our entree was a bit salty. If you're not from NOLA, it may not be a bad idea to order your food with light salt. Overall great restaurant and would come back.
Such a great experience! Great gluten free options available- service was excellent as well as the food! We had the Brussel sprouts, shared the grits and crab dip - enjoyed a great meal!

I'd looked forward to my first visit to Luke and my already high expectations were exceeded!   Simply the best meal I've had in a couple years.

The 1/2 seafood cold seafood tray was awesome-the tuna ceviche, oysters, clams and shrimp were so fresh and large, and the sauces were perfect.  The shrimp and grits entrée is the best version of this dish I've ever had-every aspect of it-the cheese, sauce, andouille and shrimp were cooked just right and it was a great mix of flavors, spice and heat.

My son had the ribeye and fries-again, cooked exactly as he ordered it and he loved it.   Bread pudding was terrific as well.

Good two-man servers and a small request I'd had as I hated to not get the crawfish etoufee was granted and for that and the entire experience, I'm recommending this place to everyone I know who is going to N.O. and will definitely return some day!

Yes. yes. yes. 

Breeze in through the revolving doors and take a load off. If you don't have reservations, you'll be lead into the back room, like pigs for slaughter. (No really, my sister and I were like, "Um, where are you taking us?") The service was still attentive and kind. No big deal. 

To start, we ordered the Brussels sprouts and fried quail. We practically gushed and got weak at the knees for the vegetable with a bad rap. Oh, it was sauteed to perfection with the perfect hint of honey. The breading on the quail was well-seasoned, not overdone, flawlessly fried and amazingly tender. This could have been my last dinner, and I'd have died happy.

We shared the mussels entree drowning in garlic butter sauce. Plenty of mollusks for everyone. Be sure to let your inner fat kid come out to play and dip-dunk the French bread in that magic sauce. 

I hope to God I can make it for the happy hour oysters next time, because $15 for a half dozen is ri-dic-ulous. I don't know who this Besh person is, but well done, sir.

-xoxo

This place deserves more than 5 stars! Definitely one if my favorite restaurants in the world! It never disappoints. Consistently blows me away every time. I had the Flamenkuche for appetizer. Was big enough to be my meal, but I reluctantly shared. It's a crunchy thin crust that has sauerkraut, cheese, and pork belly on top. Absolute gluttony! I ordered the Gulf Fish of the day. Unbelievable. Lightly breaded and perfect moist. Was drinking a blueberry and basil concoction. Not too sweet, not too strong. Don't overlook this place when visiting NOLA. The place is cute, too.

Love the old-school, modern yet vintage charm of this place, and the seafood-heavy menu!! 

Great food, great service...and the best Southern shrimp and grits we've ever had!!!  My mouth is watering just thinking about it!!

During this stage of COVID, there is no seating allowed at the bar. We were staying in the hotel that is attached and wanted to sit to watch some sports that the hotel television did not get. We were willing to sit in the restaurant to see tv while we eat, but the bartender was NOT HELPFUL. She didn't know what type of cable there was (DirectTV, etc) so we couldn't tell her what channel and she seemed increasingly confused. So we left the very loud restaurant and opted for room service. We ordered two desserts (couldn't decide between the 2) and a sandwich with drinks. They forgot ALL of our drinks. That was a bummer. But they corrected it (poor delivery guy). The food was really tasty and I recommend you try the Gateau Breton!!!!

First , I was in New Orleans over the memorial day week, so as always I asked the locals. I was told to go to happy hour at Luke since I was staying in the hilton hotel that was easy its attached to the hotel. Onto the food the oysters (pj) raw were so good and at 75 cents a piece made them even better. Also upon recommendation from my server I tried oysters stuffed with crab and shrimp and the were delicious also. The staff were very welcoming and attentive.
Exceptional sushi. Never disappoints!!!! Always fresh. Such a treat to eat there a couple times a month.

Best meal we had in New Orleans.  Staff was friendly and engaging.  Wait was long but the bar staff kept us entertained as we watched football. Drinks were well made.  If you like pate you are in for a treat.  Chicken on biscuit was excellent.  Really all 7 of us had fantastic meals. You can't go wrong here!

Beautiful interior and ambience! Good spot for seafood and local upscale food fare. We tried the crawfish bisque, shrimp grits, and bread pudding. Everything was fantastic! The bisque was flavorful and the crawfish melted in my mouth--unexpected and delightful. The shrimp and grits looked like a small portion for my husband but it was rich and filling. 

Don't miss dessert. Seriously, don't. It will be the best $8 you ever spend if you have a sweet tooth. We had bread pudding which had a nice crunchy crust, pralines, bourbon syrup (I think), and delicious local vanilla ice cream. It's small so it may not seem like enough to split but again it's rich and filling and super good. 

I focus on food but the staff was also fantastic! Definitely check this spot out if visiting NOLA. It's fabulous.

This place was wonderful. We stayed at the Hilton St. Charles. We came to breakfast. The architecture was amazing. The brunette server was prettier than Brittany Spears in 1997 and sweeter than sweet tea. The gentleman with the really short hair was gracious and also provided great service.
The crawfish omelette was amazing and my Dad let me try their grits. Coming from California, I am not very familiar with the grits. These grits were amazing and my Texan father agreed.
I usually don't write reviews but being in the industry I like to acknowledge wonderful service. Hope to come back soon!!!

Truffle Glazed Toasted Chicken was to die for! My friend and I shared it, they played it separate. So juicy, cooked to perfection and the potatoes were spot on. Another friend got shrimp and grits and the cheese pull was a sight to see, nice size shrimp. We plan to come back!

When I was planning my short trip to New Orleans, one of the restaurants my friends recommended to me was Luke. Apparently, Luke, a reputable establishment near downtown NOLA, is known for its 50 cent oysters during happy hour, its wonderful variety of drinks, and its excellent take on Southern cooking. I knew I had to make time to visit this restaurant.

For those of you who are visiting NOLA and are staying near the downtown area (e.g. Sheraton, Hilton, etc. on Canal Street), Luke is very accessible on foot. It's probably a five minute walk from Canal Street. Parking can be very bad, and so I don't recommend that unless you want to pay for parking or want to wait until the evening for free parking.

Unfortunately, I wasn't able to make it in time for happy hour (damn those oysters!). Luke has happy hour EVERY DAY from 3-6pm, and so if you want really cheap oysters (50 c for raw and a bit more for fried), come then. I arrived around 630 pm on a Friday night and this place was PACKED! If you are coming with a group, I recommend coming early or making a reservation. Since I was by myself, I was seated at the bar.

As mentioned, Luke is well-known for its assortment of alcoholic drinks. A lot of people come here just to party by the bar. If you are here just to drink, this is definitely the place. There's no real need to wait if you are willing to stand and the bartenders are very friendly. And if you are here to sit down and eat at a table, this is a great place for socializing. The atmosphere is wonderful and it's a fancy environment without a requirement for formal attire. Just a fair warning: it gets loud from the bar, and so this might not be the place if you want an intimate dinner. 

For dinner, there was only one page of entrees to choose from (rest of the menu was devoted to drinks). Coming in, a bunch of Yelpers recommended the Étouffée and the Gumbo and so I decided to get a cup of Gumbo and one order of the Crawfish Étouffée (so exciting!)

Gumbo (10/10). Not going to lie. This was absolutely the BEST GUMBO I have ever had. The soup was so savory, there was a hint of spice that wasn't overwhelming, and I could definitely taste that bit of seafood in my soup. In addition, the pieces of sausages were tender, and the rice blended well with the soup. It was $7 for a small cup, which I thought was reasonable given how tasty it was.

Crawfish Étouffée (9/10). For the first few bites (probably the first half), this crawfish étouffée was absolutely heaven. I've had and made my own before, but I have never tasted true southern étouffée until now. The crawfish pieces were big and plentiful, the sauce was so delicious, and there were also strips of cheese in there to give the dish texture. Furthermore, the rice was actually crunchy too. I've actually never had this kind of rice before, but it was an awesome experience. Unfortunately, after eating half of it, I started having an aftertaste in my mouth from the sauce. It was still delicious, but I ended up not enjoying it as much as the first half. This was probably also due to the crunchiness of the rice. It was awesome at first, but I would've preferred it soft. For the price (around $25), portion size is a bit small, but overall the étouffée was 100% worth ordering again.   

Overall, I was glad that I took the time to visit Luke. The food was good (omg that Gumbo) and the atmosphere was perfect for me. Even though I sat alone at the bar with no intention to drink, the bartenders were very welcoming and nice to me. The only downside was that if you don't speak up, they might ignore you and pay attention to people who are asking for more drinks. The price is a bit steep ($42 for one person), but that's what you get for such a premium experience. If I am in the area, I will definitely pay Luke another visit. I give this place an "omg, I'd travel 2 hours for this." 

Eat well and prosper,

For a $25 Softshell crab BLT you expect the crab not to taste fishy. Unfortunately, it was. I only did not send back because we were a party of 15 and on a time schedule. Our waitress did a great job, but drinks and food took an excessively long time even for a large party. French fries were decent as well as martinis well made,  and a friend enjoyed her Brussels sprouts, but for what we paid I expected better quality. I will not go back.

Came to New Orleans for my Birthday, and Luke was recommended by several locals. Only thing better than the amazing atmosphere,  was the food ( burger was out of this world!), and probably the best service we've ever experienced at a restaurant. Kenney and Rich were outstanding! They provided excellent service, a crazy sense of humor, and went out of their way to make sure we had an amazing experience. We highly recommend Luke, and we will be back!

Great New Orleans staple!  If you haven't been to Luke's and your in the mood for New Orleans food but in a more casual atmosphere, this is the place for you.   The gumbo, oyster salad, and buster crab sandwich are to die for delicious!

The service is excellent and Besh never disappoints. Great space to have business lunches or to catch up with friends.

Excellent Petit DeJeuner menu.  Our table had the Shrimp & Grits, Spiegeleier & the Southern Breakfast.  All of our food was amazing tasting and finished without hesitation.  The orange juice was fresh squeezed.  Would definitely return for breakfast again.

My husband and I were thoroughly satisfied with the food and service at Luke.  It was our first time in New Orleans and this was one of the few restaurants that we loved.  We loved it so much we came back the next day with our travel companions.  For lunch, my husband had the croque monsieur, basically ham and cheese sandwich with a fried egg on top, which was "amazing" and rich.  It was so good, that he "knew I should stop but I couldn't".  He's had many croque monsieurs in his lifetime but "this was the best!"  I had the veal cheeks with mushroom and pasta.  The meat was so tender but not fatty, and flavorful.  This place is a must if you're tired of the mediocre food of touristy restaurants off Bourbon street.

Incredibly fresh fish and well crafted sashimi dishes. My boyfriend and I went on a Saturday and got the sashimi lunch special for $13. (yay weekend lunch specials!) Every type of fish (salmon, fatty salmon, tuna, fatty tuna aka otoro, white tuna, even the unknown uncommon fish) in the dish was so fresh that it brought memories of Japan. The tuna sampler special was a great deal, the otoro tuna (fatty tuna) was to die for and the fried shito leaves with tuna was a nifty spin. The tuna tartar and pepper tuna weren't as good but still pretty impressive. 

The hot dishes were disappointing though. The 48hr pork belly appetizer was basically a slab of pork belly and some veggies on Chinese congee. For 48 hrs, it was not tender. On top of that, the congee was bland as expected but the flavors and sauce from the rest of the dish didn't compensate.

The eel lunch special was pretty average in terms of taste, if not a little on the dry side. The shiitake mushrooms were a unique add on though as it seems like they were marinated in some sort of sake. They did a cute job with presentation though so props to them.

They've got a large menu though, so I'll give them the benefit of doubt. Maybe, just maybe I got the wrong things. 

tldr; If you stick to the sashimi, be prepared to be blown away! On the other hand, the hot dishes are mediocre at best.

My husband and I were visiting from Los Angeles and had to try a John Besh restaurant in New Orleans. Luckily we were staying nearby in the CBD and found Luke on Yelp.

The food and service are both impeccable. 

The meal started with a complimentary warm baguette and whipped butter. I had the tomato salad, he had the Luke burger and we split the steamed chocolate for dessert. The tomato salad was a fresh delight in a city of deep fried everything; the tomatoes were flavorful and not overwhelmed by the dressing, burrata or ham. The burger was cooked perfectly medium rare upon request. The fries are shoestring and made fresh, but cool quickly so dive in right away. The steamed chocolate is their signature and most unique dessert, think of a cooked pudding served with salted caramel ice cream. 

Waitstaff are attentive without being overbearing. Individual sizes condiment bottles are a nice touch.

I'd make it a point to return here if we come back to New Orleans.

**JOHN BESH IS MY HERO**

Seriously. This man knows n'awlins food. 

Service was very good. Staff was nice, friendly, but not over the top. Ambiance was French-Bistro-ish, but with a touch of New Orleans flair. Can get loud; especially on the weekend.

I decided to take advantage of their *EXPRESS MENU* which is their prix fixe offerings of cup of soup, their specialty entree of that day, and dessert for $23.

Had the following:

(1) Seafood gumbo a la creole - Can I get a *WOW*, please. Incredible stuff. Flavors, balance, ingredients worked out perfectly inside my mouth.

(2) Redfish "court-bouillon" with crab, shrimp, oysters and rice - Tasted similar to the seafood gumbo, but has more OOOMPH. Generous seafood chunks and the amazing sauce had me soaking it all up with the leftover table French bread.

(3) Bread pudding - Tasted like a pecan pie disguised as a bread pudding.  Which was beyond amazing since I am a dessert freak.

One of the best meals for $23. Come on. I almost felt bad (that guilt only lasted maybe 2 seconds).

Cocktails are also fantastic. Try the French 75 ($9.25) or the St. Charles Streetcar ($9), both have champagne and tasted so lovely with the crazy humidity.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND the EXPRESS MENU and their refreshing cocktails.

Luke was decent and the service was super (waitress with the long ponytail and great attitude- thanks!).  One of the relatively few places open on Christmas night.   It's a traditional bistro, bright lights and noisy.   Good start to our first NOLa visit.

Great spot. Love the shrimp
And grits and the shrimp étouffée. Very tasty and fresh. This place is definitely worth a try. They also have happy hour from 4 to 6. The old fashioned is also a good choice. Service was good and friendly.

A friend told me prior from ordering here 'their food is disgusting'. I like to try things for myself a so on a quest to find the best General Tsos chicken in my area I decided to try Chan's via Doordash on a lazy Sunday afternoon. Unfortunately, my friend was right. I'm not really a fan. The dish was DRENCHED with a less than tasty sauce - usually General Tsos is a little sweet. This sauce was tart - not sure what was added. The chicken was very tough and cut in a variety of sizes which was strange. Must have been severely over cooked to be that tough. This dish instantly gave me heartburn - and General Tsos is my go-to meal and usually doesn't. I didn't even like the egg roll. Needless to say, this place puts a spin on traditional chinese flavors and you may or may not like it. It's a no for me.

This one won't be there long.  Oh my....no.  The evening started with bouncing between waiters and a very slow start to our dinner experience.  (We should have left then).  Finally, the waiter came to take our orders.  He was very friendly, which sorta helped with all the other shortcomings.  We got service only if we could flag someone down.  Our party of four was seated right by the kitchen.  The cook tasting the sauce with his finger really did not impress us.  When our food arrived, it was completely uneventful.  The quality we expect in New Orleans was not there.  Most of our entrees were not exciting.  No one at the table would order the same dish a second time.  ( I think that speaks volumes).  Apparently, there is a push to offer a mix of French and German fare.  You probably would do better ordering the hamburger.  Oh yea, we ordered their fries with one meal.  They never arrived.   We did not find the restaurant particularly clean.  This was confirmed when one patron fell on the slick dining room floor. 
A restaurant like this might survive in a small town, but it is not up to the standards of New Orleans.
Delicious Sushi!! Had dinner reservations at 5:00 and seated us right away. Service was great and food was fresh. Would definitely go back!

Wow. I am all the way late on this one. I told y'all I hadn't been to New Orleans in 10+ years. It seems as though I am the very last person to have heard of and eaten at Lüke. #fixed

My experience at Lüke reminded me of why, even after that damned storm, New Orleans is the center of American culinary awesomeness. It just can't be helped. When I lived here, no matter if I was at a shack or an upscale, coat-only establishment, I don't think I ever had a bad meal. Ever. I'm serious. Lüke keeps the streak going. 

I came here to meet and upon recommendation from my mentor. Yes, I have one. You should as well. This fellow set me on way wrt career choices, timing and strategy and it had been far too long since I'd seen him. Plus, he has fantastic taste in food/drink. We sat and were immediately greeted by that warm, chewy bread (with butter) I'd missed for so many years (yet instantly remembered once I smelled it). To my surprise, neither my mentor nor I wanted a drink. Where was I and who was I? No drink at lunch... in New Orleans? Something was amiss. I think I wanted to stay fully present in the conversation and meal. I stuck with my tonic and lime and availed myself of the $17 express lunch of the day. For less than $20, you get a cup of soup and the entree of the day. Being that it was Thursday, that meant my choice was the jambalaya. Done.

In no time, I was slurping on a bowl of hot, spicy, filling, decadent crab bisque. OMG. I'd missed eating like this. Eating is such a joy/(first world/privileged, I recognize) pleasure. To eat food that make your endorphins light up and mouth sing... it's a blessing. It is. The sweet crab meat was the star of the bowl. Not to be hidden amongst heavy cream, the shellfish was up front and present in every spoonful. I was feeling a wee bit full when my large plate of jambalaya arrived. The description said something about green onion sausage and andouille cracklin'. I dunno. All I know is as soon as the smell hit my noise, I couldn't get it in my mouth fast enough. Wait. I lie. I took a bite. Then took a bite of the corn bread. Then I crumbled the corn bread into the dish. Then I topped everything with a metric ton of hot sauce. THEN I put it in my mouth as fast as I could.

Our waiter was pleasant, accustomed to the lunch crowd and delivered the type of service that I remembered, service that helped make New Orleans restaurants famous. Bellies protruding and mouths achy from laughter, my mentor and I bid farewell to Lüke and got on with the business of the day. I was not even four hours into being back in The Big Easy and I didn't want to leave. A good meal and good conversation will do that to/for you.
Great happy hour!! Fresh and fried oysters along with great drinks. Make reservations!!
Very good brunch and service. Classic southern Louisiana ambience. Had the chicken and waffles and cast iron cinnamon roll and both were deliciou
I miss this restaurant being in San Antonio. Went very early and they accommodated our party. Great service! I love ordering the French 75 and the oysters are always great.
Hands down best place to eat in New Orleans!! Food was awesome. Service was the best we had all week. Bartenders went out of their way to treat you like family!! Loved the French 75 drink!!

Great, great meal.  Amazing portions and flavors.  

- Started with the gulf oysters.  Smooth, buttery, not a hint of fishiness.
- Also had the baked P&J oysters.  Pretty good.  Lots of flavor, but the oyster got lost.
- For my main, had the jumbo Louisiana shrimp with sausage and grits.  Just wow.  So many flavors.  I wanted to lick the skillet.
- My friend had the choucroute garnie maison, which is a fancy way of saying a casserole dish full of pork.  The two of us together couldn't eat it all.  The shank was ok.  The sausage and pork belly were very good.

Great service and attention to detail.  I'll be back.

I love Luke- have come here countless times over there years.  They also have great happy hours.  They also serve my favorite raw oysters in town.  I particularly love the atmosphere of the front room/bar- the back is fine.
Somehow I had never been here for brunch. I brough my sister & her husband who were visiting from out of town and our experience was top notch.  The service was exceptional and the food was delicious.  The fried chicken biscuit was out of this world.  The shrimp and grits were a favorite too- their grits are uniquely creamy!
I love that this place opens as early as 7am.  We wanted to entertain our family for breakfast- not a boozy brunch & this was perfect.
Thanks!

Lüke has great food. But they have such a bad attitude about everything, I just don't get it. The only reason I continue to eat here is that it is right next to the building I work in and near the hotel I stay in while in New Orleans so is super convenient. 

And know if you order food here to go that despite the 45 minute to an hour and a half quote for timing, your food will be ready in 20 minutes. So if you don't want cold food, either go pick it up after 20 minutes or make them call you when it's ready.
Phenomenal quality sushi. Best cuts I've had in a long while and I'm from nyc - I travel in from nyc specifically to eat here. They are such incredible quality !!!

A John Besh Restaurant...

Went there right before closing, and they still provided us with amazing service. 

Food: 
Choucroute garnie maison - smoked pork shank, Mangalitsa belly & bratwurst, house-made sauerkraut.  This dish is huuuuge.  For $23, this was amazing. I'm an AYCE kinda guy, and I could not finish this (a bit ashamed).  There was so much meat.   Tip:  get this to share with the group.
Etoufee - The flavors were just incredible.  They really know how to make a great sauce. 

Atmosphere:
Very classic feel to the restaurant, with a diverse clientele, including hipsters, daters, seniors, etc.  The servers treated all the same, so that was nice to see.  

The titles of all the dishes are all French, so it did take a while for us to navigate the menu.  Understandable, but just an FYI, you'll have to read, lol.  Ooops, forgot to mention they have an "Express Menu," so I guess this helps.

Short and sweet.

The service is fast, the food is hot.  It's good, but not great.  If I need a quick lunch in Nora, I'll stop, but never make a special trip here.

Not so impressed, and I am easily impressed.  Despite this being an outpost of local superstar chef John Besh, I found it pricey and non-exceptional for the price.  Service was perfunctory or less.  You might sample at happy hour for half price drinks and cheaper oysters, and see if you want to commit to a full meal sometime.  I didn't.  Oh, and there was a flea infested dog on the floor at the bar.
I've been coming here since I was a little kid. The food is unbeatable and you can't find anything even close to food this amazing. I highly recommended the house lo Meir and Crab Rangoon.

I give Luke 5 stars based on their service and oysters. I came here during happy hour and lunch and the service was superb! I wish I remembered my HH waiter because he made our experience special. I ordered a drink and he flat out told me it was horrible and recommended the Frenchman. (Try it, half off during happy hour!) The oysters are delicious! The stuffed P&J aren't on the HH menu and are a little pricy ($13 for 3) but they are perfect! The swordfish was the best I've ever had! Worth it!

As room service I was stunned, I got a bowl of gumbo and some shrimp and grits. Holy cajun heaven, wow I have had far worse food at restaurants with much more fanfare and history. I don't know what dinner is like here (I bet its great) but the food they sent up to me was fantastic.

The first time I came here was in December 2018, and my mom and I absolutely enjoyed our meal. We came here specifically for their 75 cent oyster happy hour. I'm not a fan of raw oysters myself, but my mom absolutely loved the oysters at Luke. Juicy, sweet, super clean, and big! The service was also impeccable as well. I came back to New Orleans in August 2019 and my mom and I decided to bring the rest of our family here since our first visit was so amazing. Big mistake! 

Now, I know August isn't the prime time to eat raw oysters, but we went ahead and ordered a half dozen anyway. Our waitress brought a platter of NINE oysters that were DARK BROWN and looked SHRIVELED. I wish I had taken a picture. It was super unappetizing to look at it. Now, there's two things here that I don't understand: 1) How did the guy shucking oysters behind the bar think it was okay to send that out? 2) How did the waitress think it was okay to serve that? Clearly, no one was paying any attention at all to their jobs... Never mind the fact that the oysters were terribly dark and dried out, but there were 9. You can't even order that amount (has to be in half-dozen increments only). 

Wanting to be polite, we immediately flagged down our waitress and pointed out that we had ordered 6 (we didn't mention the dark discoloration). She looked at it, and realized that indeed, there were 9 instead of 6 oysters, maybe to make up for the fact that "some of them were small." She then noted that hey, these oysters are sort of dark. (An understatement, but at least she addressed it.) She apologized and took the platter of oysters away, proceeding to consult with management about what to do. She ended up bringing out new oysters that were a little more decent. Now, we had also ordered a half-dozen of fried oysters... when these came out in a little fry basket, we realized that there were definitely more than 6. YUP, there were 9. Those 9 funky, gross oysters that were at our table earlier? Those just got fried and served right back to us. Not professional. You would think a nice restaurant like this wouldn't resort to cutting corners. 

That whole experience with the oysters soured our experience for the rest of the meal. Our Luke burger, which we ordered medium-rare, came out well-done. A waitress accidentally dropped a used fork on my brother's lap. On a positive note, the brussels sprouts were as good as I remembered it though. We also tried the fig flatbread & that was delicious as well.

Overall, a really disappointing experience, especially after looking forward to my return trip to Luke.

We were excited to have dinner at Luke and were met with disappointment. Our waitress (Shawn)was inattentive and kind of cold towards our group. Even though we were assigned two servers, only 1 came by and that was pretty rare. We spent 2 hours here- no appetizers and only 1 of us had wine. The food was okay but we had to send our frites back as they were cold. Our server did bring a new side out but it's just a little disappointing to have to send food back at a higher end restaurant.  The shrimp and crawfish étouffée was decent but the pasta in it was a little gummy. Another person in our party had the schnitzel and it was tough.  My husband ordered the roasted chicken and it was really good. I would not recommend this restaurant based on our first experience. Luke has lots of great reviews but we didn't have a great experience.

Lüke Restaurant is a John Besh Restaurant. In this restaurant, John Besh attempts to take our palates through a journey of Franco-German cuisine. At first glance, it is a cute little brasserie with a blend of old world charm and new world pace. You can hear chatters and clinking of glasses with crowds of business professionals clearly having a good time. I'd definitely recommend this place for after work happy hour and don't forget to check out their full raw bar.

Now on to the really good stuff. My meal. A trio of Canard.
Starter: Pâté of Louisiana Rabbit and Duck Livers perfumed with truffle and country bread croutons
Paired with Baron Herzog Gamay Beaujolais, 1998

Main Course: Choucroûte Garnie of housemade bratwurst, slow cooked Berkshire pork shin and creamer potatoes, add Confit of Duck Leg
Paired with Sausal Cabernet Sauvignon, 2005

Dessert: Duck Egg Crème Brûlée with fresh berry glaze
Paired with a Cappuccino

The Pâté was fantastically rich and smooth. It was accompanied by croutons that were unnecessarily salted. The shining star of the plate, though, were the sweet pickles of watermelon and cucumber. They were the perfect touch to cut through the bitterness and gaminess of the rabbit livers. I'm not sure what the current obsession is with gelée but at least this top layer of gelée melted when it touched my tongue.

Choucroûte for those of you who are not familiar can be best described as a cast iron pot of meats slowly and meticulously braised to a tender mound of goodness atop a thick layer of caramelized sauerkraut. I assure you, it's nothing pretty to look at. I imagine this would be what I'd eat if I was a man's man during medieval France. It was ALL meat. Meaty tender goodness. Slightly sweet meat from the caramelized potatoes and sauerkraut. Meat that fell apart from the scooping of my fork. The immensity of the meat taunted me and challenged me and I certainly would not have been a "man" unless I finished the whole thing...well I AT LEAST had to keep eating until I finished the wine. :)

I'd never tried duck egg crème brûlée. In fact, it never occurred to me to make crème brûlée with anything other than a (chicken) egg. Interestingly, it was not unlike crème brûlée, yet it was...different. Richer maybe. More... like it was made with an egg that could very well have just popped out of the ducky sitting in the back kitchen. Not too sweet, creamy, served room temperature as it should be. The berries were fresh and sweet and was the end to a very near perfect dinner. 

The service was attentive, the server was knowledgeable about the food and wine, and the atmosphere-fun. If you're ever in New Orleans, this one is not a "must have" but a "you definitely can't go wrong". Happy eating!
Good oysters and drum fish. Always a limited menu but generally everything is fresh and tasty.

I came in on a Sunday and was glad to see it was busy but not too busy to where I would have to wait.

Food: We had a dozen oysters and those were very fresh and just the right size! Not too big and not too small. They have some of the best shrimp n grits and I love their ribeye and fries! The price is great for the amount of food. They also offer happy hour oysters and fried pb&j oysters.

Great place for happy hour. Drinks are 1/2 price. Happy hour is on Saturday too. Happy hour is honored at dining tables and bar. Also discounted raw or fried oysters. We had both and were pleased with them. They have small TVs at the bar showing sports. The staff is friendly and efficient. They bring you small loaves of French bread and whipped butter. For happy hour is, it is definitely a great value!

This was my first real meal in New Orleans, and I'm so lucky I picked a good one! The service on both visits was impeccable, with my first server in particular recommending many great bars that I visited throughout my trip.

LUNCH - $15 EXPRESS MENU (Soup + Entree)
CORN AND CRAB BISQUE: Best ever, not that I've ever had it, but it was the best ever. 
BEEF BRISKET: Just danced in my mouth.
BREAD PUDDING: Because I was so happy with the first two courses, had to try dessert, and the bread pudding didn't disappoint in the least. I didn't try it at any other restaurant in New Orleans (because they all have bread pudding), lest my memory of this one be tainted. 

2ND VISIT - DINNER (last night in N.O.)
I really just wanted to have a full bowl of that corn and crab bisque, but when I got there I couldn't resist trying more.

First, I asked for a fancy pants bourbon and got a glass of Booker's, 126-proof, unfiltered. I had to take little tiny droplets of it on the tip of my tongue and swallow a bit at a time because, oh yeah, it burned. Burned so good, though, tasted like maple syrup lit on fire in your mouth.

Then, post corn and crab bisque, I was tempted into trying another dessert, the gateau basque, or vanilla cake, with blueberry compote and creme fraiche. Killerrrrrrr.

Highly recommend this classic bistro!

Amazing oysters! We have come twice during happy hour. Their happy hour is from 3-6 pm, and you can get local oysters for 75 cents. Also, I highly recommend the Brussels sprouts! This place is busy, so if you want a table, I recommend a reservation.  We sat at the bar both nights and it was fun to watch the bar tenders make all of the speciality cocktails.  The sazerac was a hit! 5 dollars a pop during HH. Make sure you wander over to Luke! It won't disappoint!

Luke was connected to my hotel, so after a travel day and working, I decided to eat here instead of going out. I was NOT impressed and wouldn't patronize again. The best thing about my visit was the glass of Malbec and the fact that they were abiding by social distancing protocols. I'm sensitive to slower business and lean staffs due to covid, but that shouldn't change service. As a lone diner, I was seated at a table for two. I sat for what seemed like longer than normal without anyone coming  to greet my table. I even started looking around for a server after putting down my menu (the signal that a patron is ready to order -- I was a server in high school and college). One server came to pour water only, gave a short greeting and that was it. But, I was surprised to hear him introduce himself to the table of three men sitting next to me. When the server finally came to take my order, again, no greeting or introduction, he started with "do you have any questions". I asked for a recommendation and he did a good job providing an explanation to help decide between my three choices. 

I ordered the shrimp and grits... it was ok, nothing exciting, not terrible, but I felt like it was missing some flavor. 

Finally, I asked for the bill and manager... I told him all of this above and he apologized. May seem like nothing, but again, being that I've been a server, I expect more. I'm a standard 20% tipper, this time, I left 15. I love NOLA and the food, but I'm rarely disappointed.

Pretty good food! So I searched for a new food spot after Superhouse tanked.  I read the yelp reviews here but they weren't good enough to make sway my decision either way. However, when I asked on FB it was nothing but positive reviews so I tried it out.  I had General Tsos chicken with just a bit of spice, and my husband had some wings and my kid has Shrimp Lo Mein. My daughter didn't like the noodles too much but she still enjoyed her food. My husband had the wings, he said they were good, but the wings were small.. baby wings.  I had the General Tsos and it was good! Beat superhouse hands down.  Right amount of sauce, chicken was good and spice was just right.  I will say the portions are a bit smaller than I am use to (they have large and small), but then again it could have just been put into a small container.  I called to order beforehand, they told me 15 minutes and the food was done in 15 minutes.  No long waiting, no attitudes, and fast, good service. I will return again.  Chan's will probably be my go-to spot! Plus it's halal, you can't beat that!

Stayed in town at the Hilton for work, was hesitant to try the restaurant downstairs but read great reviews. Was incredibly impressed. Every staff member was incredibly nice and helpful. The fried oysters were the best I've had and the shrimp and grits shouldn't be missed during a stay in the area. The meal was on the expensive side but absolutely worth it. Will recommend to friends and family for sure.

Even with a reservation and noting that dinner was for an anniversary, we were seated in the front area-the noisiest part of the retaurant.  Just a note, I had really talked this retaurant up to my wife before our 'experience'.

Conversation was almost impossible.  Service was erratic.  We received a round of drinks 'on the waiter' becasue they screwed up the drink order.  The food was ok but overpriced.  There are much. much better options withina 10 minute walk (such as the American Cafe Grill at the JW Marriott).This was my 3d visit to the restaurant.  First was good (I was seated in the back room which is much quieter) and the food quality was ok.  The second visit was awful.  Service was the worst I have encoutnered in NOLA in a year and the quality was not great that night either).  This was the tiebreaker and the tie went to another restaurant---any other restaurant.

First time here. 
Sushi was great! I had the sushi and sashimi combo, it was fresh and delicious. The presentation was great! Definitely coming back! Gotta go my dessert is here!... ...

Hip diverse crowd, TVs at the bar, very good draft beer selection. Small but creative menu. Good food, from what I gather even though I don't eat oysters it's one of the best raw bars around. To that point the atmosphere indicates that. So don't expect an elegant ambience.  I had matzoh ball soup (being from New York, it was a very good example), and a perfectly cooked steak, nicely seasoned.

My gf and I had some seriously good bar karma this weekend and it stuck with us when we walked in the door at Luke's. Two seats opened up just as we approached the bar, right in front of the oyster shucking station. The man with the knife asked if we were planning to order oysters and when I responded with a DEFINITELY YES, he slid a dozen in front of us, an extra due to another customer's order mix-up. Lucky us! They were huge and delish. While we sat there, in awe of the pace at which the staff was able to shuck, we sampled another kind of oyster from Alabama that was even better.

My gf also ordered a salad- big leaves of butter lettuce with slices of amazingly sweet beets and a dressing I wanted to drink.

Per the recommendation of my friend who suggested this place, I ordered a French 75- yum! I should drink more of these!

When the check came, I thought there must have been some mistake. The cocktail (which was delish) was half price for HH, I think $5. And the oysters, comped (thank you again, 5 star staff!!). Even if they hadn't been, these are a crazy good deal during happy hour. 

Definitely go to this place, sit at the bar, chat with the crew, and enjoy!
Back again.  Great oysters and service as usual.  We had two with birthdays and they brought us a great desert as well

One of our favorite meals in NOLA! Raw oysters were excellent as was the corn and crab bisque and etouffee. I don't enjoy bread pudding, but this was moist and we'll flavored - perhaps the best I've ever had. Service was slow, but it was a busy night. Would recommend to friends and/or return on a future trip.
Happy hour.  Great oysters and price. Also the baked oysters were awesome as was the foie gras !

Stumbled upon this on accident. Cool upscale gastro/bistro with bustling waiters and staff everywhere you turn. I sat at the bar solo to watch them shuck oysters and ordered lunch. Bartender was nice and pleasant but didn't really oversell or go into details about the food or make suggestions.

I ordered the matzo ball soup and the Luke Salad. 
Salad was so damn fresh that I even ate the little cherry tomatoes- and I HATE those!!!
I can just have a plate of the pickle beets and stuff myself on them alone for a meal!!! TO DIE FOR! 
I almost licked the bowl and still didn't feel "bogged down" or stuffed. 
I was very glad to see veggies added to the matzo soup. Almost like a chicken & veggies w matzo balls. Veggies were fresh and firm but disappointed in the blandness of the matzo ball. 

I wish I was in town long enough to try dinner...next time then.

Apparently, this gym doesn't want you to work on programs such as p90x. They will want to pay the trainers and do very similar exercises.
They recently posted a sign in the gym saying no p90x. If you cant do a workout program in the gym, where else would you go. Avoid this place at all cost.

Seriously, I really should not even be writing this review.  I went to a John Besh restaurant and ordered a burger.  TO MY DEFENSE (sorry I had to shout over all over your booos). To my defense it was 1) a work meeting and my expense account is slim so I had to pass on the $25 Grilled Mahi that I wanted and 2) the party I was meeting with actually recommended the burger and 3) it was DELICIOUS.  

Seriously huge bun and huge burger.  I ordered it well which is sometimes not a very good decision but it was still a good moist burger. High quality meat professionally cooked.  I actually ate the burger, (well half of it)  with no condiments.  Also a testament to the tastiness.  The shoestring fries were decent as well and over flowing from the little holder.  I personally prefer steak fries and less salt. but I still did manage to eat them all over the remainder of the work day.

Service, meh; ambiance, meh; parking, don't get me started.  However, I attribute all of those things to being in the CBD during lunch hour.  If any of those would have been above average, it probably would have been a 5 star for me.  Not my favorite Besh place but still decent.  Definitely a place I would take a visiting family member if they were staying in the quarter and treating.

Service was delightfully on point; the happy hour wine, cocktail, and oyster specials were so good, we went twice during our recent stay in NO. The place was crowded and we never wanted for anything. We ordered a few items off the regular menu and the quality was fantastic throughout. You won't be disappointed.
Good food, friendly service and an overall nice looking restaurant. I do think the dinner menu could use a few more items. But overall,nice restaurant which I would highly recommend.

4.5 Stars

I'm going to combine two reviews into one for Lüke. We had breakfast/brunch here and later in the day we came back for Happy Hour.

Breakfast first:

We sat in the front of the house and enjoyed the French Press coffee served with heavy cream in a pewter pitcher while waiting on our food. The ambiance is very nice with parquet wood floors, tin paneled ceiling and dark wood bar providing a cool vibe.

The Shrimp & Grits was spot on, served in a cast iron dish with SSU eggs on top. The sauce had just the right bite with an excellent concentration of flavors, the shrimp were fresh and large. The Omelette of Local Crab was crazy rich with nice local greens to help even out the flavors and textures, minor glitch was that we felt it was a bit oily. The frittes were really good as well but wow; how do you finish all that food?!

Service was fast and friendly, we wanted for nothing.

Happy Hour:

We sat in the back of the house which was quieter and gave us a view of the action taking place in the kitchen.

Oysters OTHS Special
Deep Fried Oyster Special
Half price beer!

Raw oysters were very fresh, very clean and very cold; this is what propelled Lüke to the top of the NOLA Oyster Odyssey List.

The deep fried oysters were good but nothing out of the ordinary. Lüke Fru, Covington, Kolsch was crisp and cold; a perfect match with the raw oysters. Our server was awesome, she made the whole experience light and fun.

Lüke is a little walk from the crazier parts of town but totally worth a visit; especially for their Happy Hour.

Cheers!
I had a cosi sandwich for the first time today. That was a good sandwich, it was turkey bacon, light mayo, lettuce and tomatoes. I will definitely go back tomorrow and get another one! delicious!

Had a good meal here with work colleagues.  We shared several appetizers including oysters, fried brussel sprouts, and crab and cheese dip.  The brussel sprouts were quite good unexpectedly.  The crab dip was good and I didn't taste the oysters.  The menu is interesting with burgers, fish, shrimp dishes, steak and pork schnitzel.  I had the shrimp etouffe which had the shrimp on top of pasta.  The taste was good and i enjoyed it.  The restaurant is in a Hilton hotel but better than many hotel restaurants.  I'd go again.

The downtown experience in suburbs. The food is always fresh and delicious. The presentation is taking it to the next level. It is our place to go for sushi. We recommended it to friends and family and now they are hooked too.

One of the most nicest restaurants I've been into! I'm not a fan of Asian food, but the kids I babysit wanted to go here. I do like sushi and they offer a variety of different kinds, the sushi is delicious. If you haven't tried it out yet, you really should!

Came for happy hour before strolling to Bourbon street! Had the fried oysters for 1.25 each. Sooooo good! We also got the shrimp and grits, equally tasty! 

Half off all alcohol beverages during happy hour, which starts at 3pm! And 1.25 oysters either fried or cold.  They are huge! 

Service was awesome! And the waiter sent us an extra drink, because ya know, why not! The place is a lil upscale and adjacent to the hotel.

Where do I begin? Everything at Lüke was simply spectacular!

I was in town for business, and after a long day of exhibiting at the Convention Center, we knew we would need a delicious place for dinner. My colleagues were discussing where they wanted to make reservations, and as they perused all the touristy French Quarter options taking online reservations, I decided to suggest this place I had bookmarked a few months back, after seeing some fellow Yelpers' vacation foodie photos. After a little convincing that they should save the touristy place for Monday in hopes of it being less busy, and that this would be closer to our hotel, they made us a reservation for four and our plan was set!

I was a little embarrassed because we arrived a few minutes after our reservation time, and one of our party had invited a fifth individual without updating the reservation. However, rather than making us wait until another large table opened up or splitting us as many restaurants would, they accommodated us within 5 minutes. I was incredibly impressed by that customer service -- wow!

Once we were seated, we ordered our beverages from a beautiful cocktail and wine list. I had a lovely St. Charles Summer: rum, pineapple, lime, toasted cardamom and Szechuan peppercorn. It was so smooth and flavorful from the cardamom, yet with a slight bite from the peppercorn. I wanted another, but decided to use some self control and savor the one I had. 

Although many of the items on the menu sounded amazing, I quickly decided on the fried quail, Brussels sprouts and a side of the jalapeño cheese grits (all small, but sharable potions, so everyone can have a taste). I was not disappointed by my decision at all! The crispy quail had a perfectly seasoned batter and then was drizzled with a sweet and spicy sauce and topped with cherry pepper rings. It was difficult for me to use proper manners among these new colleagues by using a fork and not just pick those bones clean and lick my fingers! 
The Brussels sprouts were fantastic as well, roasted to perfection, a little caramelized on the outside, but still crispy inside. Feta cheese accompanied them nicely, and the whole table sampled them eagerly, helping me quickly empty the serving dish! 

And of course, those jalapeño cheese grits... Just wow... Melt in your mouth creamy, with just a slight zest of the peppers, topped with melted cheese that had been bubbling under the broiler... I mean, I've met very few cheesy grits I didn't like, but these definitely rank up there as best around in my book. 

Our servers Christopher and Zane were extremely attentive. They regularly checked on us, answered allllll the questions my cohorts had (and there were a lot), gave us plenty of time to decide, kept the beverages full as needed and just did an all around amazing job of taking care of us. I'm so glad I had heard about this gem and it will definitely be on my itinerary on future visits to NOLA!!

So I have high(ish) grits standards. So many places offer grits that are too runny and/or completely lacking in flavor.

Luke, however, is not one of those places. I had the shrimp and jalapeno cheese grits for my meal. Now the shrimp were good enough, but the grits were excellent. The texture was perfect, and the flavoring was somehow even more perfect. Perhaps because of the good mood this dish put me in, I decided to indulge in a dessert. I ended up getting the bread pudding, which was an excellent choice. The various components of the dessert, such as the vanilla ice cream and the hot buttered rum sauce, all played really nicely together.

It was pretty busy here around dinner time, so keep that in mind if you plan to check it out.

Fantastic, had a business dinner here with 12, and the food was top notch!  I had Oysters, they were week made, and set up perfectly.

We had multiple apps, all were fantastic.

The service was better than the food, and the food was above 5stars.  I will take my wife here when we are back for vacation, and she will be blown away.

The desserts were crazy, huge and everything seemed to be cooked to order, like it was baked that minute, really unbelievable.  

Can't say enough about this place.
We were quite disappointed there. First waiter did not bring us any bread. And shrimps did not taste right for us.  Their fried oysters are good.

Just a recent update to my previous review.  Retro fitness north wales location added classes since I last wrote my review  I especially like their cross fit class, very inexpensive for the amount/ number of cross fit classes you can take.  Just when I think I'm  in shape these classes will prove you wrong.  However, I feel stronger and have more energy due to taking the cross fit class and the teachers/trainers for the class are excellent!!  They check on you to make sure you are doing the exercise correctly and to make sure you are okay.  Excellent idea to start this class- by the retro fitness north wales management!!
"Amazing!!! From the soups (tried both) to the oysters, to the bread pudding- perfection."

We came here for happy hour twice. They have fresh oysters for 75 cents a Piece. Have a great wine list and a decent beer list. The oysters fresh and yummy. My only complaint would be if you don't like oysters,  there is no other choices.

I came here during happy hour and found a seat at the bar. The bartender was attentive and friendly. Service was quick here. Oysters were 50 cents a piece during happy hour. I ended up eating a dozen. I also had a cup of seafood gumbo and their Sunday special veal as well as a few of the Tin Roof beers. They have a different special for every day of the week. The gumbo was decent. The veal was very delicious and the presentation was good as it came out in a metal dish. All in all, between the great food and service, I would definitely come here again and recommend others to come here for a delicious meal!
75 cent oysters are a steal.  They even gave my party of 8 a private room for happy hour.  I did enjoy the gumbo and wait staff.
bumping up the score 'cause james m. always loved the place. thanks for keeping it real rei

I was spending a few days in New Orleans with my mother, grandmother and sister. We decided to visit some restaurants by chefs we know from FoodNetwork. We picked Luke because of John Besh. When we got there, we were very excited about the food! Unfortunately, there was an incident where our food was served to another party. So, we waited almost an hour for our food. However, the House Manager was extremely polite and took care of our bill. The food was SO worth the wait though! We really enjoyed it and would most definitely come back!

Great food!  This was my first visit to Luke in New Orleans as I have been to Luke in San Antonio.  This location is just as fantastic as the location in San Antonio.  The shrimp and grits were amazing!   Everyone at my table enjoyed his/her selection.  The service was friendly... ambiance was average... nothing special.

I don't have any photos of my food because the food didn't last long enough for me to take any. We went at happy hour which has an awesome deal on both fried and raw oysters. They were prepared perfectly and paired nicely with the good local craft brew. There was a full bar if that's more to your liking too. 

The environment was nice with a fancier vibe than the shorts and flip flops I was sporting, but it's August and hot and I don't think anyone cared.   The service was excellent with a tag team approach to keep things moving. I certainly recommend it to anyone looking for great oysters and great service in with nice upscale feel.

Great restaurant and even better happy hour! $.75 oysters and half priced cocktails. Go early and stand at the end of the oyster bar and watch the guys shuck 'em! And if you're lucky, you'll get a little dance out of it too. Love this spot!

LA Gulf Oysters just okay. The ones we had were lifeless and not that salty. Nothing like Martha's Vineyard oysters.  The hot quail was just okay too. The ambiance is 4+! Chill music. Good service. The carb bisque--B. Not that thick on the sauce.

I must say the Shrimp and blue crab stuffed P&J Oysters were great!  Also, the French 75 cocktail which consist of cognac, lemons, and Champagne is my new favorite cocktail! This was my first visit to Luke's and they did not disappoint. While my husband was looking for shrimp and grits. I was looking for a good oyster bar and this was it!

This place is pretty decent. The daily deal is great, $23 for a soüp or salad, entree and dessert. You really can't beat that. The matzoh ball soup was so delicious with a flavorful chicken broth. The daily entree was stewed beef and vegetable provencale. Everything in that dish was good but I swear that the meat was lamb instead of beef. It had that distinct mütton smell. They probably made a mistake but I also like lamb too.

I also tried the fried oyster avocado salad. It was ünique but a little too rich for me.  A vinagrette dressing would be a better choice than a creamy dressing due to the avocado and the fried oysters already being rich.  The shrimp and grits were likewise  rich and a little salty for my taste. The grits though were fluffy and creamy. 

The dessert was fabülous. It was white chocolate semi fredo with elder flower sauce. It was light and tasty. 

The atmosphere was lively. Service was super quick and attentive. Would come back here if I had more days to spend in NOLA.

This is probably the worst Halal Chinese order I've ever had. I ordered some chicken wings and butterfly shrimp, I also ordered some egg drop soup. First of all it took the driver about an hour to get to me. Then when he got to me he wanted me to come downstairs outside to get my order! I informed him that the reason I ordered delivery was because I just got out of the hospital. He finally brought my order up reluctantly and again told me that he doesn't usually come to the door (?). I think he thought I was going to give him a tip, lol. When I open my food I was to say the least disgusted. The chicken wings were really pigeon wings and the shrimp was a large clump of batter with a shrimp inside. Neither one of these orders had any flavor. I tried salt pepper and sweet chili sauce to try and make it edible, but that didn't work. I called the restaurant and told them how I felt and they said to me that they do not come to the door and that maybe if I had ordered earlier the wings would be bigger! Then they asked me what do I want to do. It took everything I had not to scream at them, it was to say the least a stupid conversation. They offered to send me a replacement for the wings and never came. Now I'm sitting here $15 short and no edible food! I will never order from them ever again and I am going to call my bank and have their order cancelled from my account.  It's not about the money it's about the service and how the food taste and they failed on both counts.
Went here for my husband's birthday and it was wonderful. The service was amazing and so was the food!

For Chinese take out this place is great. Family run and everyone is so nice. They take all forms of payment. The food is great. Haven't had anything that doesn't taste good. A good option for Chinese take out in the area.

The shrimp and grits is one of the best dishes I've ever had. I crave it when I'm not in New Orleans and  always make Luke one of my first stops when I return. My husband says the Luke burger is the best burger he's ever eaten..and he's eaten a lot of burgers so that's saying something. Excellent service every time.

Super impressed with this place!  A group of 8 of us had just landed and gotten situated at the hotel and wanted to go and grab a few appetizers and some drinks on a Friday night around 8:30. Our hotel recommended Luke's, so we headed over. Got there and the place was packed!  We were already looking for other options to go when they said they could accommodate our large party.  We were sat in about 3 minutes after checking in!  We had a private room and some of the best service we've ever had!  Kudos to the manager for accommodating us last minute with no reservations for a large party on a Friday night and to the servers who got our table!  The food was phenomenal!  Brussel sprouts were some of the best we've ever had!  Highly recommend this place!
I really enjoyed my experience here.  i am always about the ambiance and I feel like Luke is the whole package.  A definite YES in my book!

Wow! the BEST oysters I've ever had in my life! I guess everyone has a different preference for oysters. I like it big, not salty, and chewier basically East Coast oysters. Even out of all the oysters I've tried from NOLA, this place had the best and the freshest. As you can see from the pics I've posted, first of all their oysters are HUGE. Shrimp and grits were amazingly delicious, so much taste in it with shrimps cooked very well and the grits were so smooth, yet solid and filing. I went to this place on my first day in NOLA and went back on my last day. Since this place is a bit out of bourbon street, not crowded much and didn't have to wait like other restaurants on bourbon street.

When I moved from Edison, NJ - I had to leave behind my favorite sushi spot, Sushi O.
It had swank decor, would never realize you're in a strip mall, the sushi was delicious, and the service was perfect.  I seriously mourned Sushi O when I left.

Until I found Hachi.

Hachi is better than my beloved Sushi O!
4.5 stars  (rounded to 5...see spicy tuna roll for the .5 off!)

I'm often in Chalfont/Doylestown now and upon craving chinese food one night, my bf and I went to the joint next to Hachi - that is when I first noticed Hachi and got very excited when I peeked inside....could it be just as good, or better? than Sushi O?  I yelped and googled Hachi hardcore, looked at all the pics and decided we must try Hachi!

Finally, this past weekend my bf and I dined here on a beautiful Sunday, early evening.
We were seated promptly, only one other couple seated not far away from our table.  Their food looked amazing - I got very excited.  

Here we go:
Environment - swanky cream neutral colors, very elegant but you don't have to be fancy pants to get through the door.  You would never believe you were in a strip mall next to a chain burger joint.  Seating was comfortable, table had good enough space for our food items, and a comfortable distance between each table.  While no one was sat next to us, if someone was - i wouldn't feel like I put my back side in their face to get out of my seat.  ha!
Service - our waitress was the sweetest, most helpful, attentive but not overly intrusive waitress I've had in a long time!  She was so pleasant, and offered suggestions when she had to unfortunately let me know they were out of otoro/didn't get any in yet for the season.  She kept our drinks filled, and table clean.  5 stars for service!
Food - 
Sakuro Steak:  seriously YUM.  Served on a scalding hot stone, teriyaki sauce poured over table side for a nice dramatic sizzle noise, this truly was a great starter.  4 bite sized pieces of steak dabbed with roasted garlic, nestled under grilled asparagus, and a grilled shishito hot pepper...I wish it was an entree..that's how much I wish there was more.
Tuna Bites:  Since they were out of otoro special, our waitress suggested the tuna bites (cause "sounds like you like tuna!")  girl i LOVE me some tuna and these tuna bites were bangin!  (yeah i said bangin!)  The mango salsa on top of the pistachio coated tuna chunks had just the right kick from jalapeno.  This was the one and only time I was thankful my bf doesn't eat seafood - cause I didn't want to share.
Crispy Ebi Roll:  at first I was like ehhh 11 bucks for a spiced up shrimp tempura roll...okay, I'll give it a go.  I'm glad I did, it was great and a good serving.  Two long shrimp tempura - crisp to perfection.  The sauce wasn't too sweet, just enough to elevate the taste.
Spicy tuna Roll:  I love me some spicy tuna - but I was let down by this roll unfortunately.  While it tasted good, I would not order it again.  It was cooked flake tuna cut with small chunks of plain maguro tuna.  It was disappointing to get basically a spicy tuna fish sandwich roll.  The consistency was just that, like tuna fish salad.  .5 stars off for this.  
Chicken & Steak Hibachi:  presented nicely in a shallow bowl - came with fried rice and veggies.  Ample serving of everything, the bf said it was real good - especially the fried rice being tasty.  I tried some of the veggies that he doesn't eat, and they were as he said "real good"!
No room for dessert - the waitress seemed disappointed cause all the desserts were "so good" - maybe next time!

I cannot wait to go back, I have fallen in love with Hachi and look forward to trying some of the other rolls and their tuna special when the otoro is finally stocked!

Great spot for a romantic date or a place to impress someone!  Hello Valentine's Day!  Price tag on the final bill wasn't too bad considering all we ate!  Under $80 before tax and tip!  Go to Hachi now, you will not regret it!

I was quite impressed with this place being one of the first places we went to in NOLA. The shrimp and grits are on point, even though I've never had it before, but I loved it and the whole experience was great. 

*Cooked and layer crusted Oyster - This was a smashing hit for me. It was hard to tell that these were even oyster because of what was on top of it. I believe it was scallop encrusted on top the oyster and it was delicious. They may have the happy hour oysters, but I think it's worth it to pay more for these cooked oysters. 

**Shrimp and Grits - MUST HAVE. This is what of the lick your plate moments where you wonder how have I not eaten this before. Shrimp and Grits is a common comfort food here and Luke knows how to mastermind it. The grits is covered in a great sauce and tons of large shrimp inside. Great from beginning to end. 

***Fried Pork Belly Thin Crust Pizza - If you want to have a headache from eating too much fat. This is the pizza that looks like it should be healthy at first glance, then you see the fried pork, and its not. The only thing thin is the layer, but the toppings are heavy.
Luke was amazing with great customer service! The food was great and so what the staff! Shrimp and grits are the best I've had and the bbq oysters are tender and well flavored..

It is the early evening and I got a tip that the restaurant in the nearby Hilton Hotel had great steaks and creative entrees. It didn't take much effort to convince Niki to give it a try since she was in the mood for a nice big juicy rib eye. So we got ready and out the door we went. It was a short walk from our hotel which was nice and once we arrived at the Hilton we noticed that the restaurant had its own separate entrance and over the door the sign welcomes you to LUKE. 

LUKE is a very nice restaurant, everyone in this place was dressed up and enjoying themselves which just added to the experience. Once seated we were promptly offered fresh baked bread and our drink order taken. Now the bread was fantastic but is it me or when dinning in a restaurant with a french chef, does the butter always taste better??? After spending some time reviewing the menu Niki chose the Rib Eye (what a surprise, lol) and I chose a cup of seafood gumbo to start and Rabbit Fricassee over pasta.

After a short wait my seafood gumbo arrived, it was great, no excellent, It was the best gumbo I had in a long while, French Chef, no surprise there. It was just how I like it hot, full of seafood, and just a spoonful of rice. Bravo! Our entrees showed up and Niki's steak looked sooo good and served on a wood cutting bored, how cool is that? The rabbit fricassee and pasta was to die for and a rare treat that I will have to enjoy again. I know alot of people cringe at the thought of eating rabbit but boy was this so so tasty.

For dessert I ordered the bread pudding. It was delicious and perfectly made. Alot of places just go way overboard with bread pudding and stuff it full of stuff. Here at LUKE simplicity is perfection and the just hit it every time.

I usually try to come up with some kind of catchy hook now to get you to go try a place but I think I will sum it all it in three words. GO TO LUKE!

First issues were fees that were not discussed. Read your bill carefully when talking to your vet and double check that it's the same bill before getting any work done. Even after discussing the changes between the two, they still called after surgery saying there was an additional fee because more pain meds were needed than planned. Next issue was my flea prescription. Chewy and pet meds said all they need is a phone call verification . Seven oaks refuses to give that over the phone or mail the prescription. I have to physically go back into that awful office and pick it up. Seven oaks hospital( not chewy) told them emails would not be accepted.

Luke's is one of my go-to restaurant in New Orleans! I always come here for the happy hour oysters and drinks. They also have amazing entree dishes. 

2018 
Crawfish étouffée - OMG. This dish was so good! It was my first crawfish étouffée ever and it did not disappoint. The dish was made with crispy rice instead of the regular white rice. I came back here in 2021 but this was no longer on their menu. 

Shrimp & Grits - Also really good. Super creamy and loaded with protein and flavor. 

2021
Shrimp & Grits - I'll always order this dish if I see it on a menu in NOLA. I love that they always include jumbo shrimps. 

Slow Cooked Oxtail Ragout - This dish has to be on my top 5 dishes in all of NOLA. It comes with homemade pasta so soft and chewy. Cooked just perfectly. The meat was so tender, and even included truffle shavings, and mushroom fried kale.

Pate of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken Livers - Such generous portions. Every side dish accompanied the pate very nicely. (Side dishes: mustard, pickled cucumbers/onions, & etc)

Luke has been on my go to try list for a very long time and I'm glad to finally have it crossed off my list because I probably won't be back LOL. I made it during happy hour which oysters are 75 cents a piece. Normally I would go to superior because it's 50 cents but I wanted to try out Luke's oysters and oh boy oh boy! I have never had an oyster that tasted like grass. It was nasty but I tried to drown it in Tabasco sauce but you could still taste the grass in the oysters. I ordered the crawfish bread, gumbo, stuffed oysters( server recommended it) and Brussels sprouts. Food came out really fast. Alrighty so the crawfish bread. Hmmmm it was tasteless and room temperature. I didn't know what to expect but I thought it would come out piping hot. I asked the server and she took it back to reheat the dish.
