Well instead of room temperature it was warm. At least they tried. The gumbo was thick. Thick like slime. One bite and I was done. The stuffed oysters were recommended so I was very excited to try. But man I was disappointed! It had so flavor whatsoever and what made it worse was the texture. Just a bunch of mush in my mouth. $14 for four oysters. I ate one and my bf ate one. The rest we didn't even touch. The only good thing were the Brussels sprouts. Server was nice though. She took off the crawfish bread even though she didn't have to. But overall my experience was mediocre.

I would have given Luke five stars but they made us wait 15 minutes before anyone came to our table to greet us. Also, to get drinks, apps, and bread it also took a long time. In general the service was spotty as the servers seldom came to the table - we wanted to drink!

Anyway the food is fantastic. I had the crispy redfish meuniere which i highly recommend. However, my friend had the pork shin and bratwurst. I think I ate more of the delicious shin than be did. Truly amazing. If you like thin and crispy fries then order a side of them.

My first time at a John Besh restaurant and it did not disappoint!  The crawfish bisque was recommended over the gumbo and I can see why! It was rich, delicious and very smooth, though I am sure the gumbo is amazing!  The crawfish ettoufe was my entrée and it exceeded my expectations.  It is spicer then most but very delicious. The service was excellent from start to finish! I can't wait to go back or try other restaurants of his.

Granted it was during lunch rush.  Pressed button and sat for about 3 minutes before someone said I'll be right with you. Then someone pulled right next to me and they took them I stead of me. Waited a few minutes and no one took my order so I left.  Could hear them taking others offers. Would give no stars for this visit if I could.

Well ... this is definitely a dive. Close to my office in Westport, and my coworkers and I were looking to try something new for happy hour. The pictures posted are a bit misleading. There are not nearly as many games as we thought (really just electronic dart boards) and also smoking is allowed inside, which none of us loved. The drinks were very reasonably priced and our server was friendly. Also, they don't serve food. You can order from the restaurant next door and they will bring it over. Probably has to do with the fact they do still allow smoking.
Great fried oyster & bacon salad. Everything worked well in this simple but delicious dish

I've been for the 50c oysters many times. Recently went back for dinner, and sat in the back dining room, which I didn't know existed. It hasn't quite got the atmosphere of the front, but it's nice enough and you can see the open kitchen. I like the casual brasserie vibe, the menu is mostly great - the french fries are a must, as is the charcuterie plate. If you can't quite afford August but still want to eat at a Besh restaurant, this is your go to. Impressive, affordable and relaxed.

Richie Rich crushed it!  We had a big group and he made the night amazing!  Marinaded crab claws were way too spicy, I couldn't even eat them.  But he more than made up for it with how much fun we had!  Shrimp n grits will blow your mind!  All great and he will make your visit memorable.   Thanks Richie!

I had an emergency with my dog Milo his normal vet is always so booked and 45 mins away we used that vet because of pricing . We had a medical emergency and I needed to get him in ASAP and seven oaks was the only vet in my area that would let us walk in. We were seen promptly and everyone was so incredibly nice to me and to Milo , they got him feeling better and the price wasn't outrageous for how nice the hospital was . The rooms were clean and I was even able to go back with my dog even in these covid times I just had to have a mask and take my temp . Which I was grateful as most vets make u wait in the car since pandemic , Milo is attached to me and needs me with him . Not only did they get him feeling better they also called next morning to check in on him . I'll be back with my other 4 for anything else needed . Amazing service .

Luke, is quintessential New Orleans food with extraordinary staff! It's a white coat type of restaurant but you don't have to be dressed up, and the food is just marvelous! I highly recommend the chicken liver board as a starter!

The happy hour lived up to the hype. Raw oysters were only 75 cents each. The fried oysters were like $1.25 each. Both delicious. The service was top notch too. Fine dining experience at the HH price.

We came here on Memorial Day for lunch around 12 PM but was told by the hostess that the next available seating would be at 2 PM. I could see the place was very packed so we decided to leave and come back later. I was able to make a reservation online for 2:30 PM so after walking around New Orleans, we came back to eat. I will say the food here is excellent! We enjoyed everything we ordered (oysters, pasta, jambalaya, and truffle glazed chicken - all delicious options!) 

The only thing that was a little disappointing was the service. You have one waiter that takes your order but we were told anyone wearing a white coat can help. Throughout our lunch, no one really comes consistently to ask if you need anything or to check on us. The staff were very kind, it just felt like we had to keep reaching out for things and didn't really have one waiter to go to. Aside from that, this is a nice place to eat in the downtown area, but I'd recommend making a reservation ahead of time just in case!

So... when I come to this Chipotle, I always feel like the staff would like to be elsewhere...maybe home, maybe school or heck maybe at the movies. But not here. The food is usually pretty good, It's healthy and most the time it's fresh. I mean, who doesn't like chipotle, right?  

I always order a salad but I order it with the shredded lettuce. The other lettuce just always seems like old lettuce to me, it's always wilted. we are also very fond of the Barbacoa on a quesadilla. You have to try this it taste like roast beef, it's delicious if you're a meat eater. 

But this chipotle is just a regular old chipotle. Nothing fancy. Nothing exciting. Just food. Good. Spicy. Fresh. Food.

So my sister loves Panera. One day, Indigo and I were out and I was hungry. I'm not really a sandwich person (strictly grilled cheese and pb&j) so I informed the gal working the drive through that this was my first time at Panera and then asked if they had a chicken wrap. Her response came off a touch condescending: No. We have what's on the menu. We can turn any sandwich into a salad wrap. 
Now, first of all, the menu is massive(the biggest drive through menu I've ever seen) and I didn't want to waste her time by reading every item. And her answer technically should have been yes, we can make any sandwich into a salad wrap, but not a tortilla wrap.
I said ok I'll have mac n cheese. And a large water please. She informs me of the complimentary side options, I choose an apple. 
So I get to the window and pay, she then hands me my Mac n cheese and apple and says "Have a good day" and begins to close the window. I ask for my water before she shuts it completely. 
If you're going to be somewhat condescending, please remember my water. The only reason I'm giving this 3 stars is because the Mac n Cheese was delicious. Service, needs work. I will be back to give them another chance. Maybe she had an off day. 
Indigo has no comment.
pâté and luke burger, 'nuff said.

We sat at the bar, Jamal shucked our incredible oysters, they were clean and cold and crisp! Perfectly shucked! He had great customer service and shucked the best damn oysters ever! Maddy the bartender was incredibly attentive and gave great recommendations on drinks and wine, she knows her stuff! All in all Luke was a great experience made even better by the excellent service! Oh and tip your oyster shucker! They deserve it!

Treatment plan provided was high pressure sales tactics and way over priced.   They have forever lost a customer...   I'm not even out of the office and posting this b/c it was so ridiculous.   On a previous visit my 18 y/o daughter was also pressured in same way but I just experienced it myself.  Run..

We are spoiled foodies from the city.  Our first visit to Hachi was just about perfect.  The depth and creativity will keep us coming back every chance we get.  In addition to top notch food, the service is wonderful and friendly.

This is a great spot.  I stayed in the Hilton St. Charles that is located in the same building and had room service and happy hour here through out our stay.  The happy Hour us 1 dozen oysters on a have shell for 1 dollar each or 1 dozen fried oysters for 15 dollars and 1/2 price speciality cocktails, wine, beer, and wells.  The service is prompt and very well staffed.  You will want to make a reservation to ensure a table.  The is a great southern vibe and well ran establishment.

Possibly my favorite restaurant in New Orleans, I absolutely love it! It's not very spacious so I could see that if you come at a peak time, the wait could be very long or the service could be lacking. Fortunately I have always lucked out with quick seating, great hospitality, and delicious food. I love the decor, Old New Orleans meets rustic. The wooden bar with the bull head (not real) adds a nice touch. John Besh is one of my favorite chefs and I love his menu here. Great for brunch, lunch, happy hour, and dinner. I love how you can come here casual or dressed to the nines and no one bats an eye. You could get something lighter like a nice salad or go all out with shrimp & grits (great choice.) The coffee is actually really good here too, and great gumbo. Try to reserve your table ahead of time by calling, OR checking open table and that might save you some time. A must try for a New Orleans!

Pertaining exclusively to the service at the course, as the course itself is in good shape. I booked a $70 6:52am tee time. At 6:52, there were THREE groups ahead of us waiting on tee 1. Is it the weekend? Yes, granted. But for the first tee times of the day, it's so clear they're just maxing out the tee slots with no regard to pace.

The fact these courses can jam tee times in all day and gouge you for 5-star course prices just makes you feel like a real chump who's just trying to get a round in.

Awful vets who tried to spay a Grand Champion show dog. They don't treat clients with respect and seem to actively discourage preservationist breeders in favor of puppy mills.

It's clearly going downhill - all of the reviews for the last year are 1 star.

DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY!! I have never dealt with a company like this in my life. First, their work is horrendous. They cut corners on installing an HVAC unit, wired our thermostat wrong, didn't remove old parts, emergency heat was running AT ALL TIMES (even with the AC), and then misdiagnosed the problem when trying to fix it. They stood by their terrible work by saying the things we asked for weren't in the contract. The customer service man and the manager both hung up the phone on me. They were offensive and repulsive. We had a different company come fix their problems - and they couldn't believe the sloppy wiring job that was done. They had never seen anything like it. Their work is of the POOREST QUALITY and their customer service is nothing short of REPULSIVE.

I went here with friend in from out of town. They had three dozen oysters for happy hour plus half dozen clams. These little girls could EAT!  I had the burger bc I couldn't decide what I should get. It was big and delicious. The oysters were also great. 

For dessert we had the bread pudding. OMG DELICIOUS. I was a little perturbed that I had to share with three others, but I wasn't really mad. 

The oysters are HUGE, hello! I was impressed with the setup, albeit a little crowded. The service was good, but it was busy. I would definitely come back here - during happy hour. Otherwise it could get a bit pricey. And I'm a lady with a budget. 

Well don john besh, well done.

Catherine was our server and had some great suggestions.  We took advantage of happy hour to do an unofficial wine tasting with 4 glasses of different dry reds.  Started with 2  dozen oysters, half raw half fried.  Wife thought fried were the best we've ever had and I'm not sure she is wrong.  Catherine convinced me to try the Shrimp and Grits.  Never really liked them before but these were REALLY good.  Other entree was Grilled Swordfish which was also quite good.  Finished with the best Bread Pudding ever.  We had table 81 which let us watch the kitchen at work.  Go to Luke's. You'll be glad you did.

One thing: the oysters are the best in the town (better than the popular ACME etc). Besides this, the environment is awesome and the waiters are so nice and try to give you the best service they could provide. I ordered my personalized shrimp  , which is fabulous! Would definitely recommend it!

Really wanted to like this restaurant....but was sort of disappointed. Mediocre experience. Appetizer (lobster bisque) was good but my fish was suuuuper fishy, ick. And I am a big fish lover. Bf was not particularly impressed with his meat order either. I am not sure if I'd go back although I feel it might deserve another chance to try other menu items. Also, didn't really love the atmosphere, wasn't much personality to it. Just didn't do it for me.

This place was delicious!

I was in town for a conference with my team and this place came highly recommended. It was easily walkable from our hotel, which was nice.

The inside is awesome but not too big, so I would recommend making reservation to ensure you get a table without waiting.

The food is amazing! We started with the Brussels sprouts as an appetizer. They were delicious and it was a large bowl of them, which explains why they are an app and not a side.

For an additional app, I ordered two scallops from the raw bar. They were fresh and delicious.

Most of us ordered the shrimp and grits for our entree, but one person ordered the étouffée. Everything was incredible! We all loved the grits. Very creamy and a lot of whole shrimp. I also ordered the broccoli as a side and it was excellent. My coworker who ordered the etouffee loved it, but said it wasn't enough food.

I would definitely recommend this place and go back there again.

was a lovely experience (saturday dinner, 8pm reservation).  ravioli and shrimp dishes were v good, as were the beet and luke salads.  our waitstaff were friendly and knowledgeable, and we were seated where you could see into the kitchen through glass - which made us feel good about hygeine :-) 

seems like they didn't overbook their reservations, so people didn't have to wait for their reserved table when they showed up - we noticed this because there were a smallish number of empty tables at various points which were then filled.  This is a bit of a pet peeve of ours (ie having to wait much after reservation time for the "reserved table", so this gets huge kudos in my book.

Wasn't a huge fan of the vanilla cake, but in the grand scheme of things was a small issue.

pricing quite reasonable, we thought.

We made a reservation at 5:30 on Sunday and found out they have happy hour til 6pm! Our initial drinks were half off! Pleasant surprise. We ordered a dozen raw oysters to start which were delicious. I started with the Luke Salad which has a variety of items that all paired perfectly. For our entrees we ordered the Jumbo Louisiana shrimp and Grits which I loved! We also had the moules et frites that had great flavor, you just have to love mussels. For dessert we had the apple cider sorbet which was amazing! If you love apple cider and sorbets get this! Service was perfect! There were multiple servers working together. The receipt says Team 1. They were awesome. Highly recommend this place for a nice dinner.

I honestly wish I had read these reviews before taking our precious girl to this vet. That said- prepare for a long post. We found this vet because they performed laparoscopic spays - better recovery for a hyper lab. The consult with the vet was fabulous...and that is the last positive thing I have to say. The day of the appt we dropped her off at 730. Was told the day before surgery would be performed at 830; was told day off 1030; and by 130 were anxiously calling. My husband was told they could not do the procedure timely as she was too anxious (she was a lab in a new place); I was told it was due to a shortage of lab techs. The procedure was finally done at 230 and we were sent home heavily sedated in surgical suit that was so large her back legs became entangled in it. Two days later i called as it seemed there were issues with the surgical opening and possible incontinence - was told to come in the following day (to see a different vet) but could not speak to anyone (and would have to pay additional charge for the visit). Made a call to our family vet who saw her and thought she was hemorrhaging due to the amount of infectious discharge coming from the surgical site. She immediately told us to remove the surgical suit (we were told to keep on her for two weeks) and started her on antibiotics. We just returned to our family vet for suture removal (that were falling out) only to be told that she had regular silk stitches subcutaneous that would never have dissolved and potentially were obstructing her healing. Our baby now needs wound cream and more antibiotics. We honestly thought we were doing what was best for an optimal experience and recovery and our $900 lap spay has cost us considerably more. I am absolutely disgusted with the experience we had and so upset that we did not take the time to research before choosing this clinic for our lap spay. I am happy to post pictures of the aftermath - absolutely awful. Sad part is that we aren't out of the woods yet- we may potentially need a debridement and re-suture if  things don't look better this week. I know it's cliche; but I seriously would give this zero stars if I could.

Two friends and I stopped in last Friday night while visiting for Jazz Fest (Anita Forever!), and Luke went ahead and delivered on the belief that there is only great food in New Orleans.

I ordered the Shrimp "En Cocotte," plus crab meat on top, with a side of Joe Fekete vegetables (roots like turnips, carrots, etc.)  We shared the crawfish and burrata tartine to start.

The shrimp and grits were just as you dream about: lots of flavor (if I had any critique it would be that they bordered on too salty, just a tad), a terrific portion size, and nice presentation in a little cast iron skillet.  The tartine was also terrific, a dish that we took turns trying to scrape the last bits of over and over again until the plate was spotless.  The vegetables were also tasty and in no way treated as an afterthought.

In terms of ambience, it's French bistro decor and full of happy eaters, but Like didn't necessarily carry the decadent mood that one would expect to feel her first night in NOLA.  So the bra stayed on, but the tummy was filled to the brim!

Talk about torn! In some ways Luke is 3 stars, service is just ok, the feeling is "we will get to you when were ready". One caveat, we dined at 3 pm, which apparently was shift change for servers, maybe for cooks as well. Took 25 minutes to get an order of 4 oysters on the half! They took the entree order 35 minutes after we were seated.  As far as food quality Luke is 5 stars plus. Gumbo, crawfish bisque, fresh oysters+++, fried oysters, mussels, jambalaya with pork belly and smoked sausage +++ , shrimp n grits- literally everything we tried was as good as ever tasted before. So between the who cares service and the beyond great flavors it's 4 stars.
Good is good! Setting nice! Reasonably priced! Fried oyster salad was amazing! Schnitzel was enough for two!

This place is top notch. Best oysters on this vacation. The service is Diamond level here. The entire staff works as one. Amazing service and some of the best fried and raw oysters in town. We also had thier trout which was perfection. Don't miss out on a true gem of a restaurant.

Just what I was looking for.. while traveling for work I stumbled across this little gem. Great drinks, cheers vibe (everyone knows your name) and friendly people. Kelly, Carol and Veronica offered outstanding service and made you feel welcome! Thanks for making my work week easier! Cheers!
Our absolute favorite place to eat in Nola. You will need reservations. Get the oysters, pate, and swordfish if they have it. People rave about this place, as they should.

Went to Luke's for breakfast / brunch while visiting New Orleans for the first time! Luke's is delicious. It was too crowded and we got sat immediately in a cute cozy booth. I ordered the croquet mossier it was delicious! We also ordered blueberry pancakes which were incredible. This place is a MUST!!

Alright guys. Because the oysters were so impressively large and fat, I came back my 2nd and 3rd day LOL. Oysters were a bit smaller, like average size on the other days, which was fine because we never know what kind of batch we are going to get. Regardless, they were fresh oysters every day! On my last night, I also tried their shrimp grits and bread pudding. Best shrimp grits EVER. I ordered similar food elsewhere in French Quarters but alot of restaurants make food so salty! This dish highly recommended by people who ate at Luke's and I just had to try it. The quality really lived up to these recommendations. Creamy and it felt like I was eating mash potato (haha). So good! Also the bread pudding was so CRAZY GOOD. I only had bread pudding at Mambo's and I had to go back to edit my review because Luke's really set high standard what bread pudding should be. The bread was so soft and puffy. There were.. walnut and they were powdered and roasted I think. It compliments the dish well. There were also vanilla icecream. If you grab some bread and icecream, it literally melts in your mouth with satisfaction. This is one of my top 2 recommendations to come back to!

I woke up on Sunday morning to a cold home and called Fahrenheit.  Someone was out in an hour to access the situation.  They made sure that we could be on emergency heat.  A part was needed and Vinny was back the next morning and fixed the complicated issue.  They are very responsive!  I will use them again!

Great food, fantastic service, lovely setting. Happy hour! Couldn't be happier! Yep this place hasn't disappointed. I don't normally really frequent the CBD, but when I do, this is a favorite spot. Great for meeting in a central location and I always suggest it. Great oysters. Great burger. Hats off to these guys.

I've not been that impressed with Luke.  Food is good, not great, and service is hit-and-miss.  If you love oysters, you'll probably like it more than I do.  Venturing beyond the oysters is not as rewarding.  You're paying for the John Besh name more than anything really great.
Food was so good! Service was great at lunch! Has a really good lunch menu! Dinner service wasn't greatest but food was good. Overall it wasn't too bad!

Always fresh and tasty. Fish is fresh, never skimpy.  Service is very friendly and accommodating. Lunch specials are a great deal. Avengers roll is amazing. Haven't found a sushi place better in a wide area.

Highly recommended. Very good value for the money. Chef was very accommodating. Three people in our party were celiac. Waiter knew what dishes were gluten free, what dishes could be modified to be made gluten free and chef whipped up variation of another dish to make it gluten free on request. Went during happy hour. Drinks and oysters discounted. Food was fantastic. One of best meals we have had here.

I happened in to Hachi tonight by accident.  I was unaware of its existence until now and I live locally.  I walked in to take a look at the menu and saw a couple of tempting items and decided to take a little something home.  The decor is nice.  Reminiscent of Ooka in some ways including the menu (actual physical menu...not contents).  
First...the positive and I mean, REALLY positive!  The food was spectacular!  I ordered an appetizer of Pork Belly and an Eel Dragon Roll.  The Pork Belly was, first of all, piping hot...even after the 10 minute drive home!  It was also really, really good....like Honey (Doylestown) good!  The Eel roll was great...perfect flavors/textures.  I will be going back soon and often, I'm sure.
Now...while I was waiting for my takeout, I had occasion to use the restroom.  Sigh....
I know it is a bathroom, and I know it is not the center of attention, but this is a stylish Japanese sushi restaurant with great food.  Why would the owners completely ignore the ambiance of the restroom?  First...only a one-person deal, so you have to wait outside the door if it is occupied....small place, so you can understand that.  However, what I cannot understand is that inside you find a pump container of Walmart-brand hand soap (the container at least) filled with the cheapest pink generic soap refill you could possibly find and metal (step-to-open) trash container that was obviously an inexpensive afterthought that hardly works and still has the manufacturer's stickers on it.  For me, these are the kinds of things that say management just isn't paying attention to the details...the WOW experience.
It may be "nit-picky" but it matters to me as a patron.

Review for happy hour only: while the rest of my bachelorette party crew decided to take a nap, I decided that I'd rather go to an oyster happy hour! The hostest let me know that the happy hour was 7 days a week and you can make reservations for it (!). When I showed up alone, initially there was no room but I reassured the waitress that I'm there alone so I should be quick. She made me feel welcome, gave me a table right away and even though it was reserved, she emphasized that I should not feel rushed. I ordered half a dozen of $1 oysters, a drink, and the fried oyster appetizer. The fried oysters were good, but if I had to do it all over again I would do a dozen (at least) raw.

The food is pretty good. I've been numerous times and the French 75 is my go to cocktail. The oysters are not your traditional chargrilled oysters, however, they are absolutely delicious.   The gumbo is amazing because they actually put duck in it. Lastly, I will say order a burger. It was perfectly cooked and super moist. Again, I have never had bad service.

I would have written a review with more stars, but the service wasn't good. The young worker was rude and unhelpful. 

The food was okay, though small portions for the price.

I am sorry I let Rob Harris inside of my home. I am 72 years old and he would have taken advantage of me. He stated my a/c compressor was seized and there was a serious problem with the coil atop my heater. He was like a used car sales man. He started with a price quote of $8,731.00. And  after a few minutes of me not taking the offer he tells me that if I would sign on the dotted line while he was standing in front of me there was a coupon offer of $1,200 off.  The sales pitch went on and on. Three levels of financing. When that did not work there was $500 off if I was a veteran. On and on. After he left he called back within an hour saying that because it was a holiday weekend coming up and they did not have too many installs at the moment he would further reduce my price by another $500 if he could come back and get my signature.  I would not trust Rob Harris, Joe or Matt Lynn (the 3 owners) in my house for any reason.

My review was quickly followed by a phone call from the owner Joseph Lynn. We went over what I experienced. My review is not a rant. I was not in the throes of angry temper. Neither did I embellish or misstated the facts. He was willing to lower the price further if I would retract my review. He claimed that a poor review for his company was almost unknown to him. However on Yep I found many 1 and 2 star reviews. That further convinces me that Mr. Lynn and Mr. Harris are disingenuous at best.  

Mr Lynn's  reply to my review should not mislead you. The condition of my equipment is a non issue. It is what he would charge to replace the equipment and his sales methods that are in question.


I have saved $4,119 and have  comparable equipment. I called Custom Aire Heating and A/C. The salesman did not know that I had a prior bid. He suggested two different units. The up front price without asking for a discount was $4,613. That price compared to the $8,713 offer from Fahrenheit was an easy decision to make.

Based on my experience with Fahrenheit and the poor reviews that I have found online I will suggest that the prudent shopper would do well to look elsewhere.

So much great food in NOLA, and unless you live there it's near impossible to try them all. I highly suggest you make Luke one of your priorities.

Best Shrimp and Grits I've ever had plain and simple. Large, fresh gulf shrimp with a wonderfully tangy sauce ( with slices of andouille sausage)  served over cheesy grits, it was rich, decadent , a joy to eat and a heartbreak to finish. I was completely enamored.

And this was after I had an excellent bowl of seafood gumbo. Featuring oyster and shrimp over rice it was a perfect gumbo, bringing back memories of visiting family in Texas. 

While a burger seemed like the last thing I'd want in NOLA my dining companion, who initially balked at the idea of a $16 burger, felt it was one of the best he ever had.

While not a disappointment , the vanilla cake didn't really thrill me. I had just a taste my friend finished it, so it could just be me. Also after reading Matteo's review I went for the Luke Amber instead of Luke Blond and that wasn't anything special either. I would suggest a different brand of beer or getting wine.

The staff was extremely nice, I was surprised to have  warm bread offered before my meal  (doesn't seem to happen much in NY any more) and while casual and busy it was never excessively loud. 

My biggest regret was not having time to return here to try more of the menu.

4.5 stars
The food is somewhat overpriced for what it is.  The atmosphere is nice.  There are much better restaurant options in the city.

Wow, oh, wow! I love this store. They literally have anything and everything you could think of for your outdoor adventures. Came here for a compact pillow that I could fit into a suitcase, a mosquito net, and headlamp. I am proud to say that I left with those items only - although I will say that while here I pondered purchasing a pair of Chocos, a new backpack, fancy herbal mosquito repellent bracelets, and a new set of camping towels. However, I exercised self control and only bought what I needed. Totally patting myself on the back right now as I type this. (Point: shoppers beware, all of the items in this store are enticing. It would be very easy to leave with a kayak when you came here for a snowboard. Totally exaggerating - but you get the idea. However - I'm sure that kayak/snowboard scenario has happened at some point in time.)

Anyways...

This place is a Co-op and offers a buy-in incentive for members. (I have yet to sign up for it, although I imagine I'll cave and do it sooner than later.) This costs only $20 and gives you perks like access to member specific deals, access to their garage sale (killer deals), and an annual 10% off dividend. 

Closing thoughts: A store like this just makes sense in a place like Boise. With the outdoors and all sorts of adventures in our backyard, it's really convenient to have a place like this around. Their employees are friendly, knowledgable and always willing to help steer you in the right direction. This store is a great resource for both avid outdoor enthusiasts and novice adventurers alike!

This was my first visit and my last. The service was slow and chaotic, it was like "who's on first". My order was incomplete, got all the way home to find I had no rice with my order. The receipt that tells you to check your order before leaving, was placed inside the bag, wo I didn't know I had to check my order. When I called back to the store, I was actually placed on hold for 13 minutes the first time, called back and was placed on hold for 8 minutes more before I actually got to talk with the cashier. The food was drowning in gravy as well. Would not recommend this establishment nor will I be returning.
Loved this place. Customer service was great. The Brussel sprouts were so yummy! Burgers and fries were also delicious. Dress code is business casual so dress accordingly. I recommend reservations.

Review for just happy hour oysters. At 75cents you can't beat that! I had 20 raw oysters and they were great along with 6 fried. Fried were good but a little small for fried (when fried I prefer the plump ones). I also ordered the jalapeno grits and that was good. I have only eaten diner grits and I just never got what's the deal with grits. So it was a surprise how much I enjoyed the grits. Service good as well. Very happy with my happy hour late lunch here.

How is this place not rated 5 stars!!! We came in for happy hour on Saturday at 5 and the place was packed. They were able to find us a table for3 in quick order and we ordered some happy hour oysters.  The gulf oysters are larger than pacific coast oysters but they were creamy and delicious . The drinks were so well made and perfectly balanced.  The service was much like service in the other restaurants we visited, generous and on point. Southern hospitality is real.  Come here for good food, great drinks and wonderful service.

Had dinner here tonight: 

Mussels were good, frites were too crispy and short - not much potato, a lot of crunch

Duck was ordered medium rare and the breast came that way, but the leg was well and dry, which was disappointing and a little baffling since dark meat should be harder to dry out, right?

Shrimp and grits - the best grits I may have ever had. Creamy and full of flavor. Very not-grit-like.

Etoufee - alright, here I have a bone to pick. There is "redefining a classic," and then there's calling something by the wrong name. If it has penne pasta instead of rice and is cream-based instead of roux-based, it's not etoufee! It's penne in cream sauce! 

"Oh yes, you'll really like our take on filet mignon. It's actually not a filet cut. It's a rump. And it's roasted. Like a rump roast. But we call it 'filet mignon' and charge you like that's what it is." Knock it off! 

/end rant

Someone else mentioned this already and I second it: the Benton's bacon is delightful but very thick cut, very smokey and salty, and if the menu says "with Benton's bacon" just be prepared to only taste the bacon part of the dish.

Tried getting ahold of events director for several days. Even went into store to get help. Finally got a call back and boy were they rude. We work for a local non profit and tried to find information on their programs and how we could work together to help enrich area youth. Apparently it's not in their job description or budget to be helpful.

I've eaten Chipotle for many years and always had a great experience, but with COVID today was my first time ordering from their app. They delivered my food stone cold AND completely wrong. They had the wrong meat and ingredients, didn't include the guac that I paid extra for, and added sour cream that I hate. When I called to complain, I was offered a 25% refund... I now have to "escalate" the complaint to have a chance to get a full refund.

TLDR: Chipotle messed up the order and still expect me to pay for 75% of it. That is bullshit

What an amazing lunch we had! Three of my best friends met up for our 10 year reunion and decided to meet at Luke's! Boy were we surprised by the great service from Gary & Savanna! Their entree recommendation was more than we could've expected! They recommended the shrimp and grits and by far the most amazing dish we had in New Orleans. And the drinks and the birthday dessert were pretty fabulous.

PARDON ME, CAN I BORROW YOUR GREY POUPON? My croque is without...
DENNY'S-ISH! Is it the flat decor, the weird sized tables, maybe it's the slacker staff?
MANIC PRICING is a crazy mix of extremes; yet a croque & frites for two is just $15.

What an oddly bipolar place Lüke is.  It's a casual hotel breakfast café that vends a bowl of yogurt & berries for a whopping $12!  The pretentious umlaut is offset by the "Golden Corral" ambiance.  The lunch menu swings from a $125 seafood "grand plateau" to the daily $15 two-course blue plate specials.  It celebrates classic French and German cuisine yet one of its most basic dishes, the croque madame, has no discernible dijon mustard flavor nor nutmeg in the bechamel. 

Maybe if I laid off the lithium I'd like it better...(hmmm?)

One of the best and most memorable meals I've had in New Orleans and in recent memory. We got the last reservation spot at 9 even though it says they close at 9 (their phone tree wasn't working when I called throughout the day). It's a mid sized place attached to a hotel, and it's fairly casual (people in tshirts and shorts) despite being a little more upscale. We started a half dozen with the P&J oysters which tasted very fresh and fishy but didn't blow me away - maybe I'm just not an oysters guy. We had had a pre-dinner beforehand and we weren't too hungry for a whole entree so decided to each get a gumbo bowl and then split the crawfish flatbread. The gumbo was very solid - very comforting and warm and satisfying. Great rich flavor. The flatbread was so good. The tomatoes had a fantastic flavor, sweet and savory and richer than any normal tomatoes. And the texture of the bread was perfectly crispy. Would definitely recommend getting this for an appetizer. We capped off with the bread pudding for desert which was phenomenal. The vanilla ice cream and the candied pecans were nice elevated touches but the real stand out is the buttered rum sauce. So damn good. An absolutely unreal desert and one I'll be thinking about for a long time. Overall an excellent meal and well worth the price. My only regret is that I couldn't eat more.

My second visit there, both times the service was prompt and courteous. This is one of the few places that properly known how to grill a bun. The food was very good, the prices fair, I'll be back here time and time again.
Food and service was great. Indulged in croque madam and it was delicious. The cheese was perfectly melted and the egg yolk was perfectly made. Would go again.
Loved the Brussels sprouts so much that I came back the next evening we had a great time here

I say ok because i really love the chicken bowl with double chicken. Except for to the point when the chicken is appearing burnt and when eaten it tastes bitter, and hard to chew up. I would hope that the cook wouldn't leave the meat on so long to char it and then serve it.  I don't think that too many people want to bite into their food and get this awful bitter taste. What a waste of my hard earned money. Chipotle needs to do a little bit better grilling the chicken just before the charring, burnt, and not enjoyable eating

The atmosphere is cool the service was attentive without hovering over you. The food is okay. I only had dozen oysters they were good but nothing to write home about...My buddy got a burger said it was over cooked and dry his exact words were what a boring burger...I have to tip my hat to acme they have fresher oysters and they are litter on the pockets.

Because of John Besh's popularity, I wanted to try Luke which was just down the street from my hotel. Walking into the restaurant, I immediately noticed that the clientele was just as varied as the menu. The ambiance was rather relaxed and the dark wood paneling created a homey feel in a semi-upscale setting.

I decided to try the express menu, which included a cup of soup and the entree of the day. On Saturday, it was slow cooked rabbit with grilled peppers, summer peas and tagliatelle. Although there was a lot going on in the dish including pesto that kinda appeared out of nowhere, it was simply delicious. The crab and corn bisque was a little salty, a little spicy and a little gritty, which was a little disappointing! Large pieces of sourdough bread accompanied the soup and entree. I finished the meal with the bread pudding but it was so sweet that it was nearly inedible. The hot buttered pecan sauce proved to be too much for even my serious sweet tooth. 

Overall, Luke was good but not as great as I'd anticipated. But, if you're looking for a great value, the express menu is definitely that.
Love this Panera location! Staff is super friendly. I would recommend trying one of their breakfast sandwiches. Probably one of my favorite things there
My favorite restaurant for many reasons...quality sashimi, amazing appetizers and delicious food ! Service is fantastic and very friendly!

Best sushi in central bucks area. Never a bad meal here. I've ordered almost all the rolls at some point or another. You wouldn't think much of it by walking buy since it's in a strip mall. However the food is phenomenal. I almost don't want to review it because it will make it even more busier than it is. Be prepared to wait longer than the estimated time they give you on a weekend night. Definitely worth the long wait.

There are plenty of restaurants where you can get a good meal, but there are very few where a great meal is the combination of exquisite food (i.e., crispy Brussel sprouts and oysters on the half shell) and the attention of a waiter (i.e. Richie Rich) that is beyond compare. This was one of those meals/events that make the trip. When you go, try to sit in Richie Rich's section. You won't regret it.

Lüke was one of my favorites in New Orleans. Their happy hour is SOLID!

- Half off cocktails (I recommend door#three if you like fruity, refreshing drinks)
- $1.25 fried oysters
- $0.75 raw oysters!!!

We had oysters at Felix's and Acme Oyster House, but Lüke's are by far our favorite. 

The food here is delicious. List of stuff I had the pleasure of trying: 
- Crawfish Bisque
- Crispy Brussel Sprouts
- Fruge Farms Crawfish "Etouffée"
- Moules et Frites (mussels)

List of stuff I had the pleasure of staring at:
- Entrecôte grillée et frites: a few from our group ordered the ribeye and it looked like it was cooked to perfection. I haven't eaten meat in over two years and looking at that steak really made my mouth water.. 

ANYWAY, solid happy hour, drinks, and food. Highly recommend!! If you're visiting New Orleans, DO NOT skip this one!

This past Sunday, on my last day in New Orleans, my friends and I decided to check out Lüke for out last dinner... for me it was an "okay" experience.

Location:
Lüke is located close enough to Bourbon St as to where you can actually walk to it from there without it being TOO LONG of a walk... but far enough as to where you're away from the chaos. Honestly, I enjoyed the walk, and am glad that we decided not to Uber. 

Menu:
The only reason why I am giving Lüke 4 stars instead of 5 is because of their menu. Now, don't get me wrong, their food is good, but I do feel as if there menu is very very very small and limited... to the point where my friends and I almost left before we met our waiter. The menu wasn't extensive, and I found it to be a bit pricey. 

Food:
Now, the part we're all interested in, THE FOOD! I'm not gonna lie, Lüke knows what's up... they probably don't have a huge menu because they'd rather master a few quality dishes instead. 3 out of 4 of us started off with a cup of the Crab & Corn Bisque ($7)... along with the complimentary bread and butter... my other friend had a cup of their Seafood Gumbo á la creole ($7) we all loved our soup, it was perfectly seasoned, and the bisque was so so creamy (however, it was basically room temperature, not hot enough, which turned us off). Next, we ordered two things to share 1) Fried Oysters (forgot the price)  2) Fried Oyster Salad ($17) THE FRIED OYSTERS ARE TO DIE FOR! Omg, best I've ever had... I wanted to drink the dipping sauce by itself lol. The salad was delicious, but the bacon it came with was very salty. 

Staff/Ambiance:
Lüke is what I would consider an "intimate" restaurant; perfect for a date. It's rather small, and the owner stands around and talks to the guests.. he was a sweetheart. I don't remember the name of our waiter, but he had blonde spiky hair and he was really amazing, he was quick and answered all of our questions. 

IF YOU GO, GET THE FRIED OYSTERS!!!!

Stopped by for lunch and was not disappointed. I had the shrimp and grits and my husband had the fried chicken sandwich. Both were cooked to perfection as was the bread pudding. Wait staff was awesome. Would both recommend and return to this restaurant in the future.
Best sushi in the area! Totally worth it the wait time and money! Quick pick on call ahead orders.

Was visiting New Orleans again, my daughter is considering Tulane University. 

Had lunch by myself. Very busy restaurant. Located in a hotel.

Wonderful service. Very loud and robust clientele. Fun atmosphere.

It was delicious. Had a pate which was amazing. Also had a salad. Rosé to boot. Very simple menu. I will definitely be back when I am in New Orleans again.

Unfortunately they don't have negative stars otherwise that's what this establishment would have received. I felt the need to balance out the other two 5 star ratings which must have been written by the owners. The food is absolutely disgusting. The worst rice I've had but the general tso chicken took the cake for the nastiest food ever. Pieces of multiple fried chicken smothered in a horrible sauce. My wife threw up after eating only a few bites and i had a bad stomache for hours.
The restaurant had 3 small children taking up 3 tables with their toys, books etc.
The only positive is the young girl taking the orders. She must be about 12 years old and handles the phones and in person orders like a pro. I've seen many grown adults that wouldn't hold a candle to her efficiency in this area.

Botton line is; save your money and eat anywhere else. Decent Chinese is tough to find in Tampa and this place should be at the bottom of that sad list.

Not sure what people see in this foid, but it was very bland and not seasoned well. The fried rice has weird strips of chicken oh, and it appears to have frozen peas and carrots. There was almost zero flavor in the fried rice. The sweet-and-sour chicken was also Bland, had no pieapple or peppers like most do, and the sweet and sour sauce wasn't even sour. It was only sweet.
Will we return? Nope. Overpriced blah food.

I had been wanting to try Luke for some time now and never got around to it. My best friend was visiting and we decided to go together. My absolute fav was the pâté & oyster (murder points). I had a Bloody Mary & extra dirty Martin (the dirty was my fav). Our waiter was awesome, he helped us choose the perfect oysters and suggested coming back for HH. I can see this place is going to become a fav for me.
Great menu, but our office favorite is a burger with Brussel sprouts - they do a great job with all seafood and Cajun food as well

I am very unhappy with this office. They charge 2-3 times what other offices in the area charge for all of their services and medications. I had a wellness plan for one of my dogs which they cancelled without telling me (it was supposed to be automatically renewed each year), so when I showed up today for my dogs checkup, they said my wellness plan was no longer active and I would have to pay for everything that was supposed to be covered by the wellness plan out of pocket. The practice manager, Amanda, would not even acknowledge that they cancelled my plan without my knowledge and that they should have told me it was going to be cancelled. When my other dog was a puppy and had a wellness plan, I had to submit a request in writing asking to cancel my wellness plan. Now they can just change their policy and cancel plans without even notifying people. Ridiculous. All they care about is getting people's money. I will say that I really like Dr Munoz, it's just unfortunate she works at this awful, unorganized place. I will not be going back.

This place is absolutely wonderful for breakfast! We made a reservation via Open Table for 9:45am on a Sunday. Our table was ready the moment we arrived and our server promptly took our order. Everyone from the hostess to the servers clearly cared about providing their customers with top service. For example, midway through our meal, our server replaced my hot tea with a fresh bag and water at no extra charge. The little things! And of course, our food was unreal good. My partner and I split the shrimp and grits with over medium eggs and the chicken biscuit sandwich (two courses for two people). Both are a must! Very fresh, very yummy. Many thanks to Luke for bringing us to life on a rough Sunday morning!

I have tried this store twice and each time the staff is rude and seems inconvenienced by having to help. Also, it makes zero sense to have to waite to try on shoes but I can go touch everything else in the store?! And God forbid your mask falls even slightly below your nose bc the staff will be sure to correct you or ask you to leave. Besides, anything REI sells at their ridiculously over-marked prices I can get online for way cheaper and I don't have to deal with rude staff. Being the only REI in town...maybe try harder.

I've eaten here several times before I was ever on Yelp and since I have been on Yelp I've never been back until the end of May 2017...that's about a 5 year absence...

Loved it before Yelp and enjoyed my brief lunch back in May...plus I recommended it for breakfast to my sisters and a group of their friends who were in NOLA for a birthday celebration just recently... So let's break down these 3 circumstances 

Pre-Yelp - ate here 2 or 3 times and enjoyed it immensely...never a bad meal..

Yelper - Always wanted to get back but something was always getting in the way and sidetracking me... until I attended a seminar in the Pan AM Tower across the street...was excited to do lunch but the people running the seminar were atrocious a time management so I was left with 30 minutes for lunch...not enough to truly enjoy this place but I went anyway and highly enjoyed my dozen on the half shell which is all I had time for...

Recommendation - the sisters and all their friends loved it for the breakfast the morning after the birthday festivities and if you think as a guy you can offer a dining recommendation that will please 7-8 women then you're an idiot...however this time I did and that's pretty much up there with seeing a freaking unicorn...

So take it from me, the see-er of unicorns, give ol' Lüke a try...

I guess I don't really get it. The food is fine, but it's basic sandwiches, salads, and soups. I ordered the pick 2 combo and a drink, and it was $15 before the tip. I'm cheap and kinda poor, but that's an expensive casual lunch, especially since it was a half sandwich, a small mac and cheese, AND I had to bus my own table. Basically, I'm still hungry. The place is poppin though. Every senior citizen in the greater metro area was dining in, so they're clearly doing something right.

The last couple of times I have been to this location, any car lane I went to, the card reader has not worked. It's a little frustrating considering the majority of people use debit/credit cards, you should make sure the paying source is working efficiently. Also, today I got their new 'Classic chicken sandwich' and it was not fresh at all and didn't have much flavor. It was very very bland. The workers have always been very nice and friendly though, which you don't see often enough anymore in fast food places, but they do rush sometimes and don't always remember to bring your condiments or extras that you ask for. But, even though the workers are very friendly the food that they serve at THIS location has been abysmal lately. I hope they step it up soon, because I love the food at other Sonic locations, but this one is the closest to me.

Luke is a great place for brunch. The newspapers on the walls as you come give it a bustling homey feeling and the ambience in general is down to earth and classic. 

My boyfriend had the shrimp and grits, while I enjoyed the eggs in a jar: creamy delicious grits, succulent fried soft shell crab, a subtle hollandaise and perfectly poached eggs. Everything in this dish is outstanding. I nearly couldn't finish it.

The dish of the day can run out though, so go earlier rather than later!

This particular Chipotle is my go to when I'm craving a burrito bowl. The staff is friendly, the meat delicious, the guacamole is fresh, and the service is fast. I normally get a steak burrito bowl or two [high metabolism and it's good, so I indulge] and I've never been let down yet. I have tried chicken in place of steak and that was also good! If ,and that's a big IF, they are in the process of cooking meat and you have to wait, they will accommodate you. That's awesome in my book!

One great thing they have going for them is on-line ordering. This allows the customer to just walk up to the cash register and pick up their food and bypass any line that happens to be there. I do this whenever I can and it's always ready to go. Since I order on-line to go, I've never really sat down at this particular Chipotle but it seems like it would be okay to do. The dining area is always clean, not overly loud, and not overly crowded [ I've been there at the peak and it's busy but not too busy. There's also a patio that people can eat at, also.

As for cons, a past incident would be about how my burrito was made a long time ago. The only issue was that my guacamole was at the bottom of the burrito  instead of mixed in. It's not a big deal as I found out I prefer burrito bowls anyway. I'm sure it was just me. Also, I wish the price was a bit cheaper [it's gone up a little within the year].

I'd recommend this place for anyone who wants a huge burrito, burrito bowl, in a trendy setting with plenty of room and friendly employees. I'd also recommend you try out their on-line ordering [ also can be done on your phone] for even faster service!

I knew I would love this restaurant. 
One of My Favorite Celebrity Chefs is Chef John Besh and I fell in love with New Orleans when I read his cookbook...before I even came to this city.
The restaurant is classic in decor but cozy and welcoming.
The staff here are amazing and gracious, especially the elderly  sweet woman who walks around, asking if all is well. She is adorable!!
I never had raw oysters before, but ended up having 3 dozen!! They were amazing and so fresh and so sweet, I couldn't stop eating them
Cocktail drinks were great and we had one of the best bread puddings EVER!! It was an amazing mix of indulgent and comfort food all in one dish
We are coming back in a few months and this will be my first stop

Went on Saturday just to check out. Band was great! Drinks were WEAK. They free pour like you are getting something, but I paid for soda all night. May give another try. Nice for neighborhood bar. They need to work on the drinks. Either give us what we pay for or use meters. We had a sampler, it was ok.. Chicken fingers were a bit over cooked. Again, may give another try.

I  am not a seafood person, I don't like fish or shrimp, and it has been that way since childhood. However, being in NOLA, I knew I had to try Oysters at some point. Luke's is a restaurant downtown in a hotel and they have an amazing happy hour deal with drinks and oysters. The service was amazing and the bartender really made me feel comfortable ordering the large oysters to give it a try. I shared it with a friend but I have to admit it was an interesting experience. I cannot speak to the volume if these are the best oysters in town because it was my first time trying them but from what I have heard it's great for the price that they offer. I think this is a must-visit location on your list if you are to ever visit New Orleans.

Don't take your pet here! This place is the most unorganized place I have ever been too. No one even knows how to answer your questions, the vets seem like new vets right out of school with little to no experience. The vets techs are not well trained. All they care about is getting money out of you. My poor pet suffered  with undiagnosed problems for 6 months. I spent close to $2000 So sad for the experience I had here. Hopefully the business owner realizes he needs to go back to basics and train his staff fully, treat pets and pet parents with respect and empathy.
This is a must if you are coming to New Orleans.  Their happy hour is so amazing and we have been coming back numerous times for amazing oysters.

I couldn't come to NOLA without going to John Besh's restaurant. 

We came here on a cold rainy day for happy hour and it was just perfect.

HAPPY HOUR

SAZERAC: rye, sugar, Peychaud's bitters & Herbsaint. To get me in the NOLA mood..
Actually hit the spot on a rainy day!

T. CHARLES STREETCAR: St. Germain, pear vodka & champagne. To get me in the NINA mood.. mmm..

50 CENT OYSTERS: Hello.. The cheapest oysters I have ever had in my life at John Besh's restaurant? $1 is as low as I have seen for happy hour. Not the best quality but hey, I'm not complaining.. love oysters.

**SHRIMP AND GRITS- roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausages. I Mean....

TERRINE OF SLOW COOKED FOIE GRAS - You better believe I ate Foie any chance I got once I left Cali. It is not cruel, it is delicious!This one was a little too pate-ish for me though.

*MOULES ET FRITES - Prince Edward Island mussels, steamed with garlic & thyme. Can't go wrong with that. Extra bread to soak, yes please and thank you!

**BREAD PUDDING - I mean whats not to love about bread pudding. This one was nothing short of fabulous. What a great way to end a great meal.

We stayed at the hotel across the street and wanted a quick breakfast so we popped in here and we were glad we did! We started out with the blue crab Au gratin and it was fantastic!! Hubby had the seafood gumbo...awesome as well. I had the jumbo Louisiana shrimp & grits and he had the slow cooked oxtail ragout...both were amazing! Hats off to Luke's!! A bit pricey but very tasty!
Egg rolls were kinda gross, the best part of our meal was the free sugar coated donuts. I don't think I'd make a return visit.

Went with my husband and another couple to celebrate my birthday and had the best night ever. The food was fantastic and the service was impeccable. The manager was beyond helpful in recommending our entree selections and even delighted the table with an off-the menu favorite of hers, french fries and crab/corn bisque. Now a favorite of ours as well. To top off the evening, the server brought us all glasses of champagne and toasted to my birthday. Atmosphere, food and service definitely made this a memorable birthday.

UNBELIEVABLE! We went for the happy hour $1.00 oysters and had to belly up to the bar due to not making a reservation. This ended up being a huge blessing and addition to our fun. The oysters were gigantic and DELICIOUS. The bartender "Lillian" was absolutely amazing!!!  watching  her wait on her folks at the bar in addition to making drink for every customer in a full restaurant was live entertainment that you can't pay for. She was delightful, and never frazzled. 
The Gumbo was the tastiest I have ever eaten and we have lived in the deep South for 45 years. 
To make a great time even better we pulled into a parking space right across the street.

The bread budding was so good!  I come here for the oysters, seafood, and dessert.   Luke has a great wait staff and the quality of the food was amazing.  Make reservations if it is on a game day.  We could not get in for dinner and the wait time was quite long for lunch was over an hour when Tampa Bay was playing the Saints.  We came back the following day to dine here for lunch.   Just as tasty as I remembered it from the last time we were in town!

This place was highly recommended to me by a friend and unfortunately I was very disappointed.  

We ordered the shrimp and grits, a pasta dish, the fish soup, and a burger. The shrimp and grits lacked that burst of flavor and tasted very bland to me. The macaroni dish looked unappetizing and tasted very bland as well.  Overall my table was not very happy with the food and i felt terrible for dragging them along with me to try it (why you gotta let me down like that Luke????) 

Anyway, I will not be returning nor recommending this place.

We came for happy hour and we ordered the raw oysters, the fried oysters, the fries (not on HH menu), and I got the French 75 cocktail. The raw oysters were quite large, and we enjoyed the fried oysters (the sauce carried a lot of it). The fries were also quite good. Overall it was a good experience but nothing really blew us away.

If you care about your pets, do NOT take them here.  There are plenty of others in the area that probably deserve your business over this one.  I brought one of my two doctors in due to blood in her stool and decided we would have the second one checked as well.  The Vet came in and spent less than 5 minutes looking at one of the dogs.  She spent most of the time trying to sell us an expensive membership, but when we told her we weren't interested right now, we never saw her again.  She sent a tech in to tell us our dog had hook work and it cause from soil.  Our dogs are puppy pad trained and NEVER go outside, but the tech didn't have any answers.  We were there for 2 hours and only 5 minutes or less with an actual vet.  When they realized I wanted my second dog checked, the tech came to get her and brought her to the back, but returned her minutes later.  I never got to see her checkup yet I was billed for a full checkup.  This could be a money laundering scheme as it is hardly conscionable that a real vet hospital would treat pets and owners like this!  Over priced is an understatement and wish I could bill them for the 2 hours of waster time I spent with an uninformed tech who looked dazed and confused the entire time!!!  All I can say is find someone with good reviews!  I won't make that mistake the next time.

They suck! Took my dog there with pancreatitis. They said they would give me a health plan but never did. I called them a couple of days later with a couple questions and they said they would call me back. Never did. I called again three days later because I had a couple of questions. I wanted to talk to the vet. Never happened.   
They got my $200 and that was the end of communications. I don't recommend them at all.

I gave them a 1 because they were prompt to respond to my call and scheduling - they came out to the house the next day. They initially asked if I wanted a new boiler at 8000 when they came to the house, I said no and asked how much to fix the existing Bryant heater. I have a tenant  and family in this home. They charged me 1100.00 to replace what was said to be an old burnt out 24v standing pilot gas valve , thermocouple , old tip pilot assembly , flame sensor and pilot tubing and to clean the boiler. Of course the heater experienced this problem the weekend off the snow 1/18/2020. I've been told they really took advantage of me. Upon review of the receipt there was no breakdown by itemization for cost of parts nor labor. I asked for this to be mailed to me but upon receipt I  received a computer print out that said residential repair and the total cost. I don't recommend them based on cost and not fully disclosing their prices. I had already called them to thank them for being prompt but will never use them again. Customer be warned

This place was really good and it was a lot bigger than I thought it was.  We had reservations and were seated in the back right next to the kitchen as we watched them cook all the food.  The restaurant was busy and crowded and the service was nice and attentive.  One thing that we didn't enjoy too much (nothing against the restaurant itself) was this party of women across the room from us, and I swear one of the women had a laugh similar to a witch's cackle.  It was hard to enjoy our dinner when she was going off every 5 minutes.  No hard feelings for people enjoying their own dinners and having a good time but I wish they were more mindful of being inside around others.

We had the crispy Brussels sprouts to begin and they were roasted to perfection.  We shared the slow cooked oxtail ragout with a side of the baked jalapeno cheesy grits.  All of the food was so good.  The oxtail was tender and the grits were also so tasty.  I would come here again to try other items off of the menu for sure.

Best around!! 
When we host out of town guests... we always do a sushi night at Hachi.  Even friends and family from out of town request it!!

I would give 5 stars because we LOVE this restaurant. We eat there every single day for each stay in NOLA. Yesterday we had brunch, it was delicious as usual but were so sad that our favorite dish, baked, crab and shrimp stuffed, P&J oysters was no longer on the menu. Understanding the shortages these days we know crab is expensive but maybe just use shrimp and still offer this awesome dish! We will still come but would so love to see this item added back by the two trips we have in February when we will be back (and already have reservations) for each day we are in the city!

My word!  On my third trip to New Orleans, I returned to Luke with a few friends.  We decided to try one of everything on the hors d'oeuvres menu except for the tuna.  Everything was so delicious, and surprisingly, a table of three women and two men did not finish everything we ordered, even though it was all super tasty.

The highlight for me was the charcuterie platter with the addition of rabbit liver pate and chicken liver pate.  Wow!  It was all so delicious!  The sausages looked and tasted super fresh; one of the pates, I forget which was which, was absolutely amazing!  The onion jam was a perfect accompaniment, as were the pickled watermelon bits-- who would have thought!  I could have stayed with that platter, for a long time.  No, seriously.  I still think about going some place comparable in NYC and ordering some wine and a platter.  No sharing, limited conversation, just a good drink and tasty eats.

We also enjoyed the crispy Brussel sprouts, jalepeno grits, crabmeat maison (super fresh and delicious!), baked oysters and a flatbread type pizza with the best bacon ever (a.k.a. Flamenkuchen).  

Again, everything was delicious with quality, thoughtful ingredients.  I get all the hype now after tasting an assortment from the menu and it all being absolutely, perfectly delicious.

To drink, I enjoyed the French 75.  It was well-made and tasty, but the highlight was the food.

I will be back next time I'm in NOLA.

I came here with a coworker during lunch and boy, the lines are pretty much out the door.  There are two lines, one for salads and one for sandwiches.  There's usually a person writing down your order before you get to the sandwich station though since that one is typically a longer wait.  

I tried the Prosciutto Olive Chicken melt.  It was okay, not great.  I mean, I wasn't expecting great prosciutto at Cosi so it wasn't bad.  The olives were bland and didn't add too much to the sandwich though.  But the flatbread is so yummy.

Forget Acme, Luke is where it's at! We came for the oysters and ordered them by the dozens. The fact that it was a John Besh restaurant was just a bonus. $1 oysters at happy hour, served daily!?!? YES, PLEASE! And the happy hour deals apply to all restaurant seating - not just at the bar.

We arrived around 4pm on a weekday and the restaurant wasn't busy at all. It seemed like the happy hour deal was a well-kept secret. My sister actually discovered Luke from a Facebook ad, so our visit was a bit spontaneous. Service was friendly and our first round of raw oysters came out quickly. I commend the hospitality from the manager - she greeted us during our meal and chatted with us. As more people rolled in during happy hour (who also ordered oysters by the dozens), the wait for more oysters did increase, but that's on us for underestimating the number of oysters that we wanted to eat when placing our initial order.

Having dined at Acme Oyster House the night before, I liked Luke's P&J oysters much better. We also enjoyed the tuna tartare which came with shrimp chips. Come hungry, leave happy. Luke was such a great find in NOLA!

The vehicle we purchased there was fine during test drive. I said I would purchase only if they would fix the A/C. I never received a phone call regarding that and they never fixed it. The transmission went out less than 2 weeks after I bought it. Now it's just sitting in my yard. We found out sawdust was put in the transmission, so it covered up the issues. I'd give this place a negative 5 star review if I could. I would not recommend buying a vehicle from this business.
Lame.   No lettuce.   Waited for 10 minutes while they did to-go orders instead of taking our order.

I visited this location this past weekend and I was welcomed with an enthusiastic "WELCOME TO CHIPOTLE!" I was so excited by my welcome that I struggled awkwardly through my order because I couldn't wait to dig into my burrito bowl smothered in guac. 

Being an experienced Chipotle eater, I have run into a number of Chipotle's that fail to have ingredients available and have workers who don't care about their jobs. There is no slacking at this location. The ingredients I want are always available and fresh and the employees are enthusiastic about their jobs. They offer you the best customer service, assuring that you come and leave satisfied. Can't wait to go back!

Chipotle expert tip #46: If you order a vegetarian burrito bowl, GUAC IS FREE. SAY WHAT?! (I hope your mind is as blown as my mind was when i found that out. That's nuckin' futs!)

This review makes me sad. Let's start with the good:  service was fantastic. The ribeye ($34) was cooked to medium rare perfection. The gumbo was amazing. 
The bad:  The ribeye had zero seasoning. zeroooo. It tasted like nothing. The burger had zero seasoning. It only tasted like the cheese that topped it. What use is cooking things correctly if they don't have any flavor? Why did I just pay a crazy amount for this 10oz ribeye and fries? Sadness and woe.
The veggie option burrito was overall a good experience. The actual wheat-based wrap was a tad chewey but nothing to complain about. Flavor was good.
Hands down one of my favorite sushi spots. Everything always comes perfect, the flavors and different varieties of sushi rolls are so good. I highly recommend this place and the grinch roll!

Best happy hour I have ever been to, hands down. The deals here are amazing - 75¢ raw oysters. $1.25 fried oysters, and half off basically all cocktails, beers, and wines. We ended up getting 36 raw oysters because they were so smooth and fresh, 6 fried oysters, and some drinks. The fried oysters are a must get item - the crispy and crunchy breading contrasts perfectly with the juiciness of the oyster on the inside. The ones we got were also huge so 6 of them ended up being very satisfying for 2 people. The cocktails were great as well, we tried the jalepaloma and the gintilly lace. Strong and flavorful, especially worth at half the price. Will definitely visit again when I am back in NOLA!

Good, then really bad, then ok. Our furnace kicked on a cold Sunday. Andy the technician came and he was great. Walked me through all my options and exactly what my issue was. Quoted me a great price and we signed an agreement and picked a date. I returned home from work on that date and no new furnace. I called and the office assured me that it was installed. I spoke with a second employee named Bruce who rudely insisted that they did install my furnace. It turned out they installed it... in the wrong house. My neighbor up the street. One owner named Rob called that night, was apologetic, and offered a night in a hotel and a 1 year extension on the warranty. They correctly installed the next day but I didn't know until I came home and inspected myself. No follow-up call. No return of my house key. No, "Hey, your unit is installed. Sorry again about the massive blunder yesterday." I never received paperwork indicating the warranty extension that was promised. Two weeks later, I get a generic survey encouraging me to share my experience online! Ok, if you insist. The paperwork also had two different addresses for my house, maybe part of the incorrect installation. I received a call from their office the same day and the woman who I spoke with was horrified. She was very apologetic and helpful. I got a quick return call from a different owner and a discount on the job, but he was condescending and just seemed to want to get me off the phone. Half my experience was great. Half was terrible. They have some great folks working there but there were just as many who were unprofessional.
You just cannot go wrong with Luke's. Covid safe and happy hour is still consistently fantastic. I'd be here every week if I lived here. Wonderful service and delicious.

Look everyone, businesses are short staffed. Please be patient with those who are serving you. 

I went to Chipotle on a Sunday evening and there were only 3 employees. I did an online order and waited about 20 minutes more than the time I had originally scheduled. I could tell people were being impatient waiting to order their food in line, but there were a ton of online orders as well. I finally got my food though! When I got home it was a little cold, but honestly when I took a bite, everything was seasoned well! A little heat from the microwave did the trick and I really enjoyed what I ordered! This was my first time visiting this location, so I'm not sure how the wait times are.

While in NOLA, you must try a John Besh restaurant. Maybe two. And I know most go for August. I promise you though, Luke has damn good grub and will not disappoint. Everything we dined on at Luke was just delicious.

We went for the lunch as it was right near our hotel so it worked out quite well for us. They do a daily rotating special and if you're smart, you'll go on a Monday for the Tabasco Honey Fried Chicken for $17. The chicken was crispy and the tabasco honey sauce it comes with? Divine! It also comes with a good size helping of red beans and rice. A more than filling midday meal.

I also was able to try the Croque Monsieur $16 - you can make this into a Croque Madame, as well, which is simply adding an egg on top. The amount of ham was inches thick on this beastly sandwich. Drenched in gooey cheese, it was anything but a basic ham & cheese sammich. 'Twas a monster.

Service was just lovely from start to finish and the dining room was a chill, business casual type vibe. 

For good eats, with non-jaw dropping prices from a signature John Besh restaurant slightly off the main drag, check out Luke.

One of the worse experiences of my life. Please do not call this company. There are not enough words to describe what I went through. They will turn things around and make it your fault for trusting them . I highly expect after seeing this review, they will claim they do not know me. That is their standard m/o when caught. My endless bank loan will tell you different.

BEWARE.....

Great all around!!! Has a great renovated store with good delivery time and great food.  The only bad thing I noticed is that the couple of times I have done carry out, the cash register is a little slow.  Other than that, it is a great experience that is quick and easy.

Great ambiance, great service, but more than those - really good food. 
The liver pate surprised with richness; brushless sprouts were a huge dish and tasty too; friend oysters were not as crispy as I waved, but fresh and tasty. 
The table next to us has the friend oysters salad and reported that it was a favorite as well.

Loved the happy hour! Can't go wrong with the $0.75 local P&J oysters on the half shell - they were luscious, fresh, sizeable. We also really enjoyed our cocktails, which were also a great deal during happy hour. Service was also friendly, attentive, and kept it fun with a good sense of humor. Overall, we really enjoyed our experience and would definitely consider returning for happy hour the next time I'm in New Orleans.

A white girls wet dream I assume just a high priced place to say you ate at this trendy chain. I felt I lost IQ points just spending money here... very starbucks uggs and yoga pants type of vibe. Much rather support a local small business then toss my money at a chain like this... upsell new tech trendy place guess I'm more of a quirky good food kinda girl that doesnt quite mesh in this type of establishment... it's a no for me.
One of my favorite spots when I visit NOLA. The crawfish hush puppies are ridiculous good and the drinks are superb.

If you care about your pet please take them anywhere else. This place should be shut down. My baby has been suffering for almost a month because we were told the medicine will help her get better. The veterinarian (old, thinning hair, I believe brown colored) lied about the prognosis and the time left I had. I am angry at myself but mostly this place for keeping my dog alive just to funnel over $1500 out of us. They will prey on you. My dog now has about 2 weeks to live and is doped up to ignore the fluid building up. I'm so glad I went to a different vet. 

This place also did not call back about blood work, if my dog was okay, etc. I do not want anyone to feel the kind of pain and misery we are in. Please never step foot in here.

This is complicated. I have had great food here, and I've been disappointed here. I keep coming back, as I'll have a great experience, as I did last Monday night watching the Saints at the bar and noshing on the exquisite pates and sausages. Doug had the duck and thought it was brilliant. The one low point that night were the raw oysters, which were small and not as juicy and plump as oysters we've had in the last few days at other restaurants. Last night we returned and tried the oysters again, which were so petite that we complained to the waitress; she brought us a few extras. Honestly, I've watched guys shucking oysters at Casamento's and Acme who toss aside the really little ones. They should do that here, put them in a stew or something. Doug had the chicken (poulet gran mere) and said it was the driest chicken he's ever eaten. I had the skate wing and it was delicious. So it's a mixed bag. If you order anything with bacon in it, the bacon is all you'll taste. It's a brilliant product, but overwhelms the other flavors in any dish it's in, as it's so heavily smoked. This is not my go to place for light food, as things lean toward the heavy side, but if you like Alsatian style charcuterie, it's quite good. Try to go and sit at the bar on a night when Tomas is working...he's a terrific bartender, and the Sazerac here is one of the best on the city.

Food is excellent, would have been 5 stars.
But the Chinese male waiter with the glasses is so rude, has no customer service voice or mannerism, Yelled at us when we asked a special request. There is a respectful way to speak to customers, even if can't the satisfy request. We are regular customers that go once a week, too.
