An amazing happy hour menu featuring New Orleans local P&J oysters for only 75 cents each! Super fresh and juicy. I tried fried oysters at Luke for the first time - really good! Um and can't forget this minor detail - half off draft beer, wine, and cocktails. RUN THERE NOW.

Delicious sushi and sashimi, this is our go-to place in the area. Everything we've had is fresh, high quality, and exquisitely prepared. This is not the sort of place that drowns beautiful, delicate fish in trendy, sweet sauces. Lunch and dinner are both excellent. Advice: if you want in-sort seating, make a reservation. The place is not that big, and the quality of their food and service is not a secret.

Luke is the hotel restaurant for Hilton St. Charles and is run by celebrity chef John Besch as the place a chef would want to hang out after work.  The bar is the center piece.  It's long and inviting.  There are no televisions.  Instead, it's all business with drinks being made, a fancy espresso machine, and the oyster shucker and seafood guy.  Notably, Luke has their own microbrew beers that are designed by the same guy who designed Abita Amber.  It's some of the best beer in town and it's on tap only at Luke.

The staff at Luke is phenomenal.  They are serious about their jobs, there are a lot of staff members, they are pretty responsive to your needs.  I think the managers being on site and very visible and engaged with the staff helps a lot.  

Next to ACME, Luke probably has the best raw oysters in the city.

But Luke is known for it's burgers and fries.  They are very good and have only the best quality ingredients.  Other dishes are extremely rich as well. I have had every item on the menu several times--none of it is healthy but all good.

But the overlooked meal by Luke is breakfast.  They have homemade yogurt, some of the best Anson grits you will ever have, and some of the best coffee (served in a french press) with cream in the city of New Orleans.  Hands down it is one of the best coffees.  I like to just swing in during a tough day at work and indulge in coffee and fries.  

This is truly an underrated New Orleans restaurant.  Sure it's just a hotel bar and eatery.  But the food has a soul.  The staff is very friendly and attentive.  The restaurant is upscale and yet relaxed.  I strongly recommend it as one of the better restaurants in the FQ area. 

One side note: people complain about the prices at Luke.  They are about $5 too high for everything (eg. cheeseburger is $16, but it's a phenomenal burger that you'd definitely pay $11 for.)  

The restaurant has ample seating up front near the bar area.  There are also tables in the back.  Large groups should call ahead to arrange for seating.

After several more successful dining experiences here, I have to up my stars from 3 to 4. I recently had some of the best Gulf oysters here, and I'm a big fan of their sausages and charcuterie. Go for happy hour and get 50 cent oysters, half price specialty drinks and $2 drafts (12 ounce pours). I also ordered the fried oyster salad, which I've had before, and it had a lot more lettuce last time. I told the server and he brought more greens expertly dressed. Great service.

I had high hopes but they were dashed. 
Ordered the southern breakfast- the eggs were supposed to be over-easy but they ended up nearly cooked through. My bacon was dry dry dry. Not a hint of grease kind of dry. Brittle bacon is not my thing. 
Husband had the fried chicken biscuit sandwich which he loved. 
Server was great. Coffee was delicious. They just need a cook who knows the basics.

Definitely a popular hit with locals because this placed was packed when we got there. I do recommend getting a reservation, especially during happy hour. The oysters were a good size and fresh. My favorite were the Peruvian Scallops, which I recommend any seafood lover to try. It was packed with flavor and a kick. I will definitely be back to Luke for HH again!!

Mussels were so good! We ended up running in because the restaurant was attached to the hotel we were staying at and we are so glad we did. I tried the pork schnitzel and my hubby had the mussels. I think this was my first time trying mussels and I was ready to trade dishes with him. It was so good. Everything was good and loved the door #3.

This Panera seems to be a mess. I give lots of room for "real life" right now because there is a nationwide shortage of restaurant employees so things are going to happen. 

Last time I went through (months ago) I ordered a sandwich that comes on a specific bread.  Never did they mention they were out of it, or I'd have  changed my order. Instead they made the sandwich on a totally different bread (called for Asiago and they did whole wheat so not remotely comparable) and I didn't notice til I'd left and got home to eat. I let that go...

However, today ticked me off. In the drive through we ordered Mac and cheese and a baguette. I also asked for a bagel bread sliced. The woman in the drive through said "so cut horizontally." I said "no, bread sliced." And then she said "ummm ok? So thick or thin?" I said "I've never ever in all the years I've been ordering bread sliced bagels been asked this. Can you just do it how people normally would get their bread sliced bagel?" Kid you not. Instead of asking someone around her, she replies and says "so would you like me to cut your bagel thin or thick?" I again said "I don't know how you normally cut bread sliced bagels. I've been going to Panera for 20 years and I just request this and it's always the same". She repeats ..."so thin or thick slices?"

I told her to just forget it. And she goes "ok!"

THEN we were served a bowl broccoli cheddar soup instead of the large Mac and cheese we ordered. I can't even.

UPDATED POST- please see the updated information below. 


UPDATE: Joseph the owner reached out to discuss my experience. I really appreciated his call and our conversation. We discussed the bill, the pricing, everything! I feel that he understood my concerns and said he tried to stay competitive in a very competitive business. I told him that the promptness of their response was excellent and the work was done quickly and without issue. Warranty and use of my Bryant heater parts was exactly what I was looking for in his or anyone's company. I only felt that I was not given more information about billing. He apologized and said I should have been given more information. 

To have him call tells me that there are still good people in this world that want the best for each of us. I have changed my rating to a 5. Joseph cares about his business and strives for excellence.
My go to weekly dinner. Amazing sushi, the best sushi restaurant in the area, hands down.

Came here pre covid with two of my friends and LOVED it. We came during happy hour for their drinks, apps and most of all.. OYSTERS! Service was amazing, food was amazing, just amazing all around. We came here twice within 5 days. Will be back here whenever I make my way back to Nola!

Came here for the happy hour oysters, but ended up being more satisfied with the breading pudding.

Like what over reviewers already said, you get what you pay for.  Just go elsewhere for oysters. 

We ordered a dozen raw oysters and a dozen fried oysters.  The raw oysters were tiny.  About half the size of the size to slightly smaller then the saltines that were provided.  There was no flavor, which is why you would have to drench them in the hot cocktail sauce.  The cocktail sauce by the way was deceivingly hot, with a 2 second delay, so you're shocked when your nose burns.  Back to the oysters.  There were shell pieces in them!  The fried oysters were the same.

Raw oysters happy hour - $0.75/pc
Fried oysters happy hour - $1.25/pc

The fried chicken entrée was good.  The chicken was perfectly fried with a light batter.  The beans were tasty, just a bit too salty for me.  The gumbo soup that came with it was good, but also salty.

Pecan bread pudding with ice cream was amazing.  It came out hot, and with a crunchy top layer.  The caramel sauce was so good, and I think there was a touch of alcohol in it.  Shared it with my bf, but I could have eaten it all by myself.  No need to count calories for desert! 

Service was great.  Our server was attentive and explained the happy hour prices to us. (All alcohol drinks are half off during happy hour.)

While researching places to go while in NOLA, I came across Luke and their famous happy hour. Yes, the place had great ratings and reviews for their food. However, I wanted oysters. This was probably one of my favorite meals in NOLA. 

Their happy hour special is just crazy with 50 cent oysters, 1 dollar/fried oyster and half off their beers.  It was like a light was shining down on me and I hit the jackpot. Needless to say, we had 2 and half dozen oysters and 4 fried oysters. The raw oysters were tasty and huuugee. Our waiter, bless his heart, didn't even bat an eye when we ordered that many. He was attentive and very polite. The fried oysters came with a ranch dipping sauce, seemed a little odd. However, ranch taste amazing with them! Who knew! Next time I am back in NOLA, I will for sure come back here and hopefully try their other dishes!
Loved it! Everything was good from service to food to ambience! A proposal happened to!!(to someone else lol)

I've been here plenty of times to know that this place is one of my faves for sashimi or rolls. Came here to indulge myself by selecting a new roll which is done at each visit. Ordered the out of control roll which had shrimp tempura and spicy kani on top. I typically like the rolls with raw tuna/salmon but for a cooked roll, I'd recommend it!

I started this review about 10 months ago and forgot to finish it. Since then, I have been back several times. Most of the time, the staff us efficient and friendly. There is almost always a long wait in the drive thru, because it us a pretty popular place. This isn't a shock. The sandwiches are so good and they have a broad menu. I have found the green goddess salad though,  and that is my go-to order every time. 

This place can be tricky to get the food you want. Because the menu is broad, it is easy to miss a topping or spread. Like, I ordered a cheddar and steak half sandwich with my salad one day, and I failed to notice that there was a spicy horse radish spread.  That would be ok... if I wasn't repulsed by horse radish. The food is expensive. You are paying for quality ingredients and I get that. But, when something is not right, the line is too long to deal with returning and I don't have 10 dollars to waste on a meal I won't eat. Every now and then, this happens. The food is too chic, looking great but either lacking flavor or over powered. This hasn't happened in a long while, now that I found what I like. Even still, it left enough bad taste in my mouth to drop me review from 5 to 4 stars.

I'm from st. Tammany parish staying at a hotel close to Luke.
I ordered takeout of their duck duck rice. Opened the box to see a very small portion of greens with 1 duck breast - no rice at all!! The duck was half fat and so tuff I had to sit out strings of meat after every bite.
I called Luke's to ask why I received something different from the menu? I was told a manager will be calling me to resolve the issue, no one has called. $30,00 for this, it is not right. I'll go to bed hungry tonight, but everyone I know will be warned to stay away.

We were group of 8 and got our reservations like a week ago. 
We got Brussel sprouts for starters, gumbo, shrimp and grits, oyster and pork schnitzel. Every single dish was delicious. The Brussel sprouts were so crispy, sweet and so well cooked. Gumbo & shrimp and grits were sumptuous. Tuna was fresh and had the right amount of tart. We were so happy with our selection. Door 3 for drinks was a great start and to end out feast, we got bread pudding for dessert which was fingerlicking good!

You would think that REI would be the most expensive sporting goods store but I just compared their thinsulate pads, camelback hydration systems, and katadyne water filters. Better selection and lower prices at REI. Better service. And you gotta love the dividend. It's a co-op.

Plus this is a historic store. Larry Craig was accused or cruising some guy in here.

My wife and I had dinner here on August the 10th. Our waiter was "Richie Rich". He was Excellent!!! It was "Coolinary" month with a nice selection of food. I had the pork schnitzel which was cooked perfectly. We started with brussel sprouts and the serving was HUGE. Overall an enjoyable experience and LUKE is definitely one of our "top tier" restaurants in NOLA. Signed....PappaGeorgio

Bennett, you are not alone, and in my opinion, from the experience I had with them, you have reason to think they were trying to take advantage of you. 

In my case, my hot water was sporadic. Fahrenheit came out and the technician put Joe on the phone to tell me the cost of the spark board repair. He said it would be 1400 dollars. I said "What, 1400 dollars?" and then he said he'd give it to me for the price he charged their customers under contract, 1000 dollars, more or less 1100 with the tax I think it was. I thought to myself, first it's 1400, now a moment later it's 1000, hmmm . . . 

I was able to get the brother of my usual heating repair technician to come out, since my usual technician was not available. He replaced the board with the actual identical part, rather than just one off of the truck that was not an exact match, and he charged me $350, tax included. It's been a week and the hot water's fine now. 

I, like you, Bennett, am out for the $99 service call money. I didn't think I should have paid that money, actually, b/c I think the service call fee is based on a good faith estimate. I called them to tell them that and after a heated conversation where Joe wanted to talk at me and not with me, I said I would call him to tell him what I ended up paying. Joe said he didn't give a f#@$%k what I would end up paying, so that was the end of that conversation--I hung up while he was still ranting.  

If you think it's good business practice trying to get 1400 for a job that my technician did in half an hour (Joe said it would take his guy a couple of hours), then call this company.  

Another thing that rang a bell with your review was the disparaging of the equipment. He said that my Crown equipment was junk. I've never heard that before from any technician. They all say it's a very good system (after all, it's the Honeywell spark board that went, which presumably could happen on any equipment). Funny thing was, his own technician that was at my house said that he had just put in a Crown for his mother, I think it was, so if it was junk, his own technician apparently disagreed . . .

If you like sushi this is the best place to go. They have variety and everything is fresh. Customer service is excellent. I went to this restaurant several times for occasions. Always happy with everything can't go wrong with Hachi.
Very exotic and a wide variety.  This was some of the best sushi I have ever had. Can't wait to return

Food 4/5: We ordered a dozen of oysters and Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp. The size of the oysters was smaller than I imaged, but it was still very good.  Both was very flavorful and the shrimp was tender. The oysters was fresh for sure, no doubts about that. 

Service 5/5: The waiter was top-notch, he was very attentive to our needs and explained the food in the menu very well. He was very nice and smiley. I hope the waiters there get pay more for their service. 

Ambience: This place is very bougie including their menu. If you need to find a place for a nice date, I'd recommend this place. I heard many companies would come to this restaurant for lunches. The interior design is very comfortable and high-class for sure.
Great cocktails and oysters. Went during happy hour so can't speak about the other food but loved that you can make reservations for HH.

I went to go get hiking boots, a sleeping bag, and a backpack. I waited at each of the designated "line starts here" signs by myself. The boots section is annoying (roped off, can't touch the boots), but at least I accomplished the task at hand. The only attention I got from staff at the other two stations was a dirty look and a "come back in 10 minutes". I left after an 1:15 with only my boots.
Great Chinese food and awesome service ! And I can't say that for a lot of other Chinese restaurants but I am very glad in finding this one. I haven't found one in town better.

On our recent short visit to New Orleans, my husband insisted we get grits for breakfast. I looked up the menu at Luke's to confirm our grits goal.

Couldn't have asked for a better visit. Loved the:
- Awesome service - waitress was originally from Hawaii but had the hospitality and charm of a New Orleans local.

- Food - I had the lump crab meat omelette with a tiny taste of cheese. Amazing!
(I always try to order what I can't get in my Denver home restaurants). And, the omelette came with a great green salad with a perfect vinaigrette and frites! My husband had the basic breakfast with eggs, bacon, and GRITS. The bacon was sublime.

- Atmosphere - very old school wood decor. I love a breakfast place with newspapers out. It encourages lingering. 

I'll be back on my next visit!

Horrible horrible place. The guy working lied about the wait time, said he'll start my pedicure asap, spent 3 hours in here total! No one here knows how to properly do or shape nails. Place is dirty. Attitude is horrible. Did not even gonna paint my toenails correctly. My 6 year old niece can paint better! Only went here as last resort after work and am unfamiliar with this area. Don't waste your time here!

Stopped by this place for a pre-dinner "snack" and the happy hour $.75 cents oysters...wow!! What a deal!! Started with door#three which was tasty on the sour end and their Tempranillo which was tasty!! Then had 16 of their raw oysters and then another 10 raw oysters after that!! Also got 12 of their fried oysters which was nicely fried as well!! Also got their gumbo which was tasty!! Added a side of delicious crawfish tails and it was a nice "snack!!!" The oysters were super fresh and clean tasting!! Really fun atmosphere and super nice and attentive bar tender!! Great happy hour!!!

The mussels were so good, I can't remember ever having eaten any this delicious before in my life - and I've had mussels all over the world. They were gooooood! The sauce was so perfect I asked them to pack it up - which they did, including extra bread - so I had it for breakfast the next morning. Incredible! Great meal!!!!

Amazing service and food. We had a party of 10.

#1 shrimp and grits
#2 Pork
#3 oysters
#4 ox tail

However, everything was incredible.

DID SOMEONE SAY 75 CENT OYSTERS?! Yes, 75 cent oysters everyday at Luke from 3-6PM!

It was my second day in New Orleans and although I had already eaten oysters at ACME the night before, I was eager for more - ESPECIALLY at such a steal. I walked over to Luke from my hotel and immediately got a seat at the bar. At around 4 PM, the restaurant was not too busy nor crowded. The atmosphere appeared classy yet casual at the same time. The bartender greeted me after a couple minutes and provided me with a menu. In addition to 75 cent oysters, the Happy Hour at Luke also included half-price wines by the glass, some cocktails, house brand liquors and draft beers!

I ordered a dozen raw oysters and a cocktail - all for just $16! The oysters were shucked right by the bar and presented with cocktail sauce, horseradish, lemons, and a red transparent sauce that I was unfamiliar with. The oysters tasted juicy and fresh, well-worth the HH price! 

While the bartender was not too engaging, the service was pretty prompt. I also got a chance to chat with some locals, which made my experience more memorable. PLUS, if locals were there, you KNOW it's a legitimate place! Luke, I will be back in the future!

Sadly, I got only one picture after my visit to Luke. But it was really cool experience. I am not a regular at fine dining restaurants, but this one is really great. Reasonable prices for seafood. Good selections on menu. We got oysters, salad and duck. Food was normal. But again, after a visiting of this fancy place, I did get really exited. Maybe I need to be more mature for such a places. 

Thats the photo of Old Fashioned by the way.

We've been ordering food from this restaurant for many years. Everything is always prepared fresh and the containers are packed tight. We have never had a bad meal from House of China. Plus their prices are so reasonable for the amount of food you get.

Holy Gluttony Batman!!!!

After a looong day of walking (and drinking), we popped in to The Emily Rose bar to try their almost world famous "Killer Po- Boys". They were open and were supposed to be serving the po boys but dude behind the counter informed me that they were getting ready for the 4th of July holiday and they had just shut down for the next week.

Bummer!  But I'm sure they earned their vaca so C'est La Vie.

Another dude at the bar (we stayed and drank more) heard me tell mama "no po boy" and started offering a multitude of dining options. After a long list he stated that Luke was his favorite place. I let him know that we chose Emeril's over Luke for lunch that day and Luke was on our list for next time. I was wearing shorts, a golf shirt, and flip flops and didn't think I was dressed appropriately for Luke anyway. His response cracked me up. "You are in New Orleans baby, so @#*^ing what." Off to LUKE.

We sat at the bar and watched the oyster shucker do his thing and even though July does not have an R in it we had a dozen sweet oysters on the half shell. They were delicious.

Mama ordered the burger. Good burger but my dish stole the show. Choucroute Garnie Maison smoked pork shank, Mangalitsa belly & bratwurst, house-made sauerkraut. Basically a beautifully roasted pork shank, a house made bratwurst sausage, a few pieces of pork belly, and some roasted potatoes over a bed of sauerkraut. An Iowa farm kids wet dream!!!!!! (see pics). The pork belly literally melted in your mouth and had a crazy good smoky bacon flavor to it, worth the $26 all by itself.

Two of the best meals of my life. I say two because no one could finish that dish. Stud waitress wrapped up the leftovers and put a French loaf and a mini jar of mustard in my go box. Breakfast the following morning was a pork shank sandwich with sauerkraut and mustard. WOW!

Emeril's and Luke on the same day, I'm a lucky guy!

I was worried when I found that this was located in a hotel, but the food does NOT taste like hotel food.  The ambiance was not what we were seeking, but then, we arrived during the extremely popular "happy hour" when oysters are 50 cents each.  After the end of the cheap oyster period, the place got much quieter.

The food was extremely good, and we walked out feeling we had eaten a great deal more than we hoped, but we could not have eaten less.   It was very good.  The service was excellent, and we would recommend Luke, even if you have to walk a little to get there.  Who can complain about walking in New Orleans?

I recently traveled New Orleans for the first time with a group of friends. One of witch has a sixth sense for finding the best restaurants around no matter where we go. Lüke was by far the best of many great food experiences we had during our stay. To keep this post brief enough to not be overlooked by most, I'll just say this. 

In a nutshell, good location. Extremely good food and drinks. With unexpectedly friendly service.  

It's far enough from Bourbon st. to get away from the drunks. But not too far that it's not within walking distance from it. The main dining room looks like the upscale intimate atmosphere you would expect. But the upper dining room by the kitchen is where we preferred to be. Still very nice, but with a little more breathing room. 

The drinks are simply amazing! We all sampled each others and the conversations that came after that alone was worth the visit. But then we ordered.... To our surprise, the evening got even better. Again we all shared a sample with each other. And again, we were all surprised with how great everything was. 

Now the part that it seems like most people have negative things to say here, the service. I'm my experience, that couldn't be further from the truth. Our server Kris was extremely knowledgeable about the menu, professional and attentive to just the right degree. He never gave me the feeling like he was standing over my shoulder. But every time I looked to find him, he was already walking towards our table. 

This place will be a staple to every trip I take New Orleans!
Awesome & polite service. Great food & beautiful atmosphere. Small drink selection, but lots of delicious eats

I was very happy with my experiencing using Fahrenheit to have my heater tuned up this past weekend. When I called the office they were very easy to talk to and I could tell I was talking to someone who was actually local.

Shortly after this their technician gave me a phone call to let me know he was on his way (very surprising since I didn't request same day service, maybe was a slow day?). After greeting him, he quickly went about checking all over my system.

He came back telling me there were no issues, I have a new system so I hoped so! When I do run into my first issue with this system I will give them a call back. Very nice all around.

This restaurant was a last minute decision- we wanted delicious food and a good happy hour but we needed a break from heavy Cajun style food. It's a beautiful restaurant, classy designs, lots of natural wood, it's lovely! Our server was extremely kind and helpful, we always love a waiter willing to chat and joke around a little. We initially went for happy hour, got some delicious oysters (the happy hour deal is amazing- 75cents for a raw oyster!!!). We were so impressed that we decided to get 12 more oysters and share the Flammekuchen for dinner. The oysters were all around impressive and I highly recommend this place for happy hour and snacks! The flammekuchen was slightly disappointing for us. It's originally a thin crust pizza from the Alsace region of France and that's where we first were introduced to it. We expected it to have lots of cheese and appropriate toppings. It came out mostly onion and bacon, with a very small portion of cheese sprinkled on top. The flavors were good but it was TOO much onion. We were pretty sad about it, and it definitely lost the restaurant a star. However, if you love caramelized onions and bacon, you will likely love this!

Overall this space is cute, convenient, and they have great happy hour deals! I hope that if we don't make it back by this trip, we will on a future trip because the entire menu was mouth-watering. Plus, it's hard to beat 75 cent oysters!

We tried shrimp and grits and softshell crab. Each dish was flavorful. One friend in our party was vegetarian and there was nothing on the menu. The staff was very thoughtful and offered to just whip up something off the menu. That dish was just as great as any others on the menu!

I drove here from Allentown (based on another reviewer who drove from Allentown as well) for my husbands birthday. When I pulled in the the shopping complex and saw the store front I got nervous! Why did I drive 45 minutes here for my husband's birthday to dine across from a Giant?! We walked in and it was a very nice atmosphere but MUCH smaller than I imagined.  I was happy to have made a reservation. All other fears were quickly banished as we saw other diners meals being brought out and they looked and smelled divine. We had an absolutely wonderful dinner here and out waitress provided excellent service. I would highly recommend this place. Just be sure to make a reservation on a weekend evening.

Yelp! YLMD!!!
My favorite place to go to when I don't want to cook was closed...so forced to look to yelp to help me out.
House of China, close by and good reviews.
Ok
Pork fried rice ...overcooked rice, how can this be?
Egg rolls, crisp outside but gooey inside and difficult to differentiate what was wrapper vs what was veggie filling
No sign of any ground meat product
Beef n broccoli....broccoli was amazing but the beef had a weird coating making me wonder if they floured it prior to stir fry?
So no HOC for us

last year i had a problem with the heat, these guys came and fixed the heat and got 1000$, which it wasn't fixed and he gave me 2 years warranty and a free service in spring, when we wanted to use the air condition it didn't work, he came and said it doesn't have any Freon, and he said there is no warranty you have to pay again. he said i can change the whole thing for 7500$, which the same thing costs 6500$ in some other place.
It was much too crowded to get a table. I did takeout instead. I ordered a variety to determine whether I would want to go back. It was very good.  I'm definitely going back.

The Happy hour 3-6pm daily is one of the best in the city! Happy hour includes half off oysters, signature cocktails, wines by the glass and beers. What more can you ask for? 

Get a couple dozens of the raw oysters and the fried ones too; they are both fresh and delicious!

The French 75 is what they are known for so try it. It's very yummy and a little on the sweeter side. If if you aren't keen on the sugar, get the blanc de blanc because it pairs so nicely with the fresh oysters and super refreshing.

Skip the gumbo. Order a juicy burger to soak up all that alcohol - you won't regret it! 

Overall, we had a wonderful experience Luke and cannot wait to come back!

I enjoyed this restaurant and recommend it 1000%! The food was delicious, The service was perfect, And they took us in on time for our reservation. My dad was familiar with the chef from the cooking network show that owns this restaurant. This was the last dinner we had while we were visiting in New Orleans and we were all very happy.

1st offical meal in New Orleans and it was amazing. I had the shrimp and grits and my daughter had the seafood gumbo. We finished with the bread pudding. Everything was amazing. We went on a Thursday afternoon and there was no wait.

All I an say is "Brussel sprouts" you have to try this unique preparation. Who would have thought this pairing of sprouts and jalapeños could be so delicious?  Tired of seafood in NOLA - get the burger, I promised you will be entirely satisfied!

I am extremely disappointed with a place I order from all the time. The person on the phone mumbled took long pauses when I ordered my wings. But then to not even check if my lids where on the container when you give me my wings. So when I go home everything flies out of the container and onto the floor. It'll be a long time before I order on Sunday!

Extremely, extremely, extremely small portions. Got the smallest dabble of queso on my tacos, minimal meat. They were also out of lettuce AND taco chips lol. Will never recommend this location to anyone. Even got red sauce to go and they only filled it up 1/4 of the way lol. Oh ya, and my steak was grossly overcooked. Terrible business practices. 2 thumbs down

Lucky enough to eat here twice in 2 weeks. Both times came in around 3, to partake of their awesome happy hour(HH) from 3-6. Each visit I started with a dozen raw oysters ($.75) @ HH.
First visit I also had the charcuterie platter, so many great and unusual things. The person seated next to me at the bar even mentioned how beautiful the plate was.  Recommend!. 
Next visit in addition to the raw oysters, I also had the fried oyster romaine salad.  it was very good, not sure if it was worth the price point ($17), but the oysters were awesome and the salad perfectly dressed.
*side note, I always base my reviews on the food...as service can sometimes, just be off, but both visits I sat at the bar, where I think you usually receive better service, I did not feel this was the case, either visit. 
1st visit, service was ok, second visit, was terrible, same bartender. She is not attentive,  even when not super busy at 4, on a Tuesday.
Fast delivery friendly staff that answered the phone and the delivery driver was very nice

Warranty company hooked us up with this company and they came out to fix our AC that would not turn on. It was a simple fix (switch inside unit) and they then suggested that we have the unit cleaned for $58.00. I agreed and made the appointment.  I was not at home when the service was performed, my husband was. When I got home, I noticed the bill was for 
$99.00 and I asked my husband what other service they had performed. Turns out, there was no additional services, that was the price of the cleaning.  I called the company to inquire why I was quoted one price and charged another and they told me that $99.00 is their minimum charge.  Still not sure why the tech quoted me the price of $58.00.  I paid $99.00. WILL NOT USE THEM AGAIN!

I'm at the post office near this restaurant quite often, but I had never seen or heard of this spot. After my first visit, I can understand why people speak highly of this establishment. The staff were quite friendly, and the food was some of the best Chinese I've had in Tampa/Lutz. We dined in and the food came out quick. Everything was steaming hot, and tasted fresh and delicious! I'll definitely be back, and would recommend to anyone looking for a solid meal. Support local business and check this place out!

I was sorely disappointed with my meal at Luke.  The service was absolutely terrible, and the food was just okay for the prices they charged.  Typically I do not write very negative reviews, especially when a restaurant is so well regarded (especially on Yelp).  

My wife was completely dissatisfied with the overall quality of the food and the lack of attention that we received.  I am sure if we had a different experience service wise, maybe I would have rated this restaurant differently.

Hands down the best sushi and Asian food in the area
Consistent.  Clean.   Innovative   And great service
Sensational oysters, drink sand the service is amazing!! This is a John Besh restaurant and it is stupendous!!

50 Cent oyster happy hour and half off drinks from 3-6PM at a John Besh restaurant.

50 Cent oyster happy hour and half off drinks from 3-6PM at a John Besh restaurant.

You need to know more than this? Fine.

This is a delightful spot with a nice atmosphere and unbeatable happy hour. I gorged myself on bivalves and experienced some dishes from a pretty awesome chef.

Jumbo Louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" - Excellent. This is shrimp and grits done very, very right. Yes, the portion is a little bit small but the flavor is rock and roll.

Crawfish bisque - very good.

The booze - at half price, awesome. I was a big fan of the St. Charles Streetcar and the Sazerac.

The only miss for me was the Duck and Rabbit pate. The best things about this item were the relish/pickles/pickled watermelon that it came with. The pate itself tasted like hanging out with old people who aren't family.
The best Japanese restaurant in the area.  Incredibly fresh food, great service.  We won't go anywhere else for Japanese!

I think this place has the best deal they have $20 meal one large pizza, cheese steak and wings all for $20. This is a great deal when you have friends over and you don't want to cook. My fiancé and I just moved to the area and love this place!! The pizza could have a little bit more cheese but other than that you cant beat the price. They also deliver beer I personally haven't used this service YET lol but I will try it soon. 

The young lady at the registered for take out is also really nice and offers to give me paper plates for the meal. This $20 meal last my fiance and I about 2 days we eat the left overs for lunch the next day. 

Overall this place is good I haven't dined in but there take out service is great.

When I first arrived in New Orleans, I consulted Yelp to find a Cajun restaurant where parking was not only safe, but wasn't a nightmare.  This is when  I found Lüke, located inside the Hilton on St. Charles Avenue.  John Besh, who is the chef behind Domenica and Soda Shop in New Orleans, is the culinary brainchild behind Lüke.

My first meal here was for dinner, where me and family started with the Boudin Louisianne (9.5), which was boudin served with cracklins and spicy cabbage.  I had never had boudin before in my life until then, so I have nothing to gauge its authenticity.  All I can say is, I enjoyed it!  The spicy cabbage lacked a bit of flavor except for the spiciness, but the it did compliment the boudin.  The boudin is definitely a dish to be split between several people, as it can get a bit heavy, but the cracklins really were a plus!

We also got the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "en cocotte" (22), which was roasted jalapeno cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausages all in a cast-iron skillet.  The jalapeno cheese grits ended up being my favorite part of any dish that night!  The jalapeno was just enough to flavor the melted, slightly burnt cheese on top of the grits.  And I didn't think I liked grits before this - but beware, it's oily!  The andouille sausage was also good, but unfortunately, the shrimp didn't taste very fresh.

We also had the Seafood Gumbo a la Creole (8), which was tasty, but in my opinion, not all that unforgettable for one reason or another.  It wasn't the spectacular gumbo I was hoping it would be, but it was still flavorful, though a little too salty for my taste.

edit//
I was told by one of the friendly staff that they have a happy hour with 50 cent oysters and half off drinks, so sure enough, I returned with a couple of friends.  The bar is quite the wait (reservations are recommended), but it's totally worth it!  The oysters are ginormous, they're fresh, and cleaned out well by the extremely friendly guys behind the counter.  I had the St. Charles Streetcar, which was nice and refreshing.  The Riverbend was also refreshing, but a bit sweeter and fruitier.  Needless to say, we had an awesome time, and completely recommend this to everyone (who eats seafood/oysters).

Overall an Amazing experience!!

The place was very well filled for a Thursday night. I came here with my family for some halal Chinese, and the experience exceeded my expectations. The service was outstanding and very friendly. We ordered the shrimp egg rolls for appetizer and it was very crispy and delicious. The entrees we had were amazing. It was a great visit and well worth the drive from Jersey. I will definitely be back for more!

So we went to Luke because it's around the corner from our apartment building. I'd heard the burgers are good so I was anxious to try one. Sadly, I didn't like it at all. It was undercooked and had very little flavor. I was happy with the Fried Oyster Salad, it was amazing. The hubby said the chicken sandwich was good. 
Great staff. Very attentive and polite. 
Very loud.

I'm a die-hard Panera fan, but Cosi has a good amount to offer. It's better than ABP in my book, at least! You just have to know what to get. And I've actually never had a problem with their customer service, and I've visited quite a few times... I mean, these places generally aren't known for their service anyway.

Come for lunch to get hot, fresh flatbreads with whatever you're ordering. They're amazing when fresh, but passable if not. I love their pesto chicken melt (not sandwich), steakhouse salad, and tomato basil soup to dip the flatbread in. The only pizza that's worth getting is the smoky BBQ chicken. Also, please don't get the squagels (hard as a rock!) or the lemonades (overpriced and so sour, in my experience)!

The prices are a little expensive for the quality, but at least they're consistent and convenient--and there are quite a few yummy options. It's also a great place to study or chat for a while; don't forget about the upstairs seating!
The pate appetizer is amazing, oysters super fresh, and service super good. Wish I had more time in New Orleans to try more dishes.

Happy hour 3-6pm for 50 cent oysters. And indeedy, it's a happy day for my boyfriend and I. We immediately ordered three dozen oysters plus cocktails without wreaking havoc on our wallets! This is the GO TO spot if you love oysters and cocktails for a steal. 

Lüke, we will be back!

This place was amazing for being gluten free! Our waitress knew the menu and was aware of how the chief could accommodate our gluten free needs! She had the cooks make us fried oysters in a GF coating and fried in separate fryer. Acacia's recommendations were out of this world. We had the mahi and the shrimp and both were so yummy!

What a great place. Very accommodating they gave us seating exactly where we asked for. Jessie our host was great! Very attentive and personable. Happy hour and the food top notch. Highly recommend, wish we found this earlier in our trip.
Bummer during covid. A limited menu, no flatbreads. I usually go for HH for the 50 cent oysters, now $1.50. Maybe again in the future they'll bring it back.

The first time I ordered take out from here, the food was pretty good (brussel sprouts and grilled shrimp). But the service was below average. The hostess seemed unsure of what to do with me when I arrived to pick up my order and I was kept waiting by the bar even though I could see my take out bag by the register. Despite this, I liked the food enough to try and order again via phone. I was only able to say "Hi, I'd like to place an order for pick up" before the woman who answered the phone (Ashley, I think she said) hung up on me (rather roughly too from the slam I had to endure in my left ear). Even if this weren't my last day in New Orleans, I would not consider trying for a third time due to the poor service.

Lunch was great (Maultaschen) and so was dinner.
The highlight was the seafood tower and the charcuterie plate.

The seafood was probably the freshest I've ever had and served with
a nice array of cocktail sauce, horseradish, mignonette. 

The charcuterie was THE BEST I've ever had.  Too many to describe including some wonderful house-made mustards and savory jams.

Deserts also quite good.

Wine list is like the food - Alsatian.  Had a cremant de jura which was excellent and an outstanding value. 

Pleasant and food savvy waitstaff.

I've been meaning to come here for years and didn't realize it was a Besh restaurant.  I made it for the 3-6 happy hour where oysters on the half shell are half price and speciality cocktails, wine and well are also half off. The host was friendly as was the bartender. I sat at the bar and got the fried oysters, (also a half hour deal i think i got 6 for $8) 
I loved the seasonal cocktail called "Barrely- making it through the holidays" which was a gin drink made with Prosecco and Licor 43 (which in never had before. She described it V as a vanilla flavor)
I ordered the fried oysters  and va the broccolini. As the oysters arrived at my table I could smell the aroma, they were gently fried and came with a white sauce. They were a little salty but V still amazing, likely  the natural sea salt.  The broccoli was perfectly charred with the right amount of crunch on the outside and not too chewy ok the inside.

Ordered here 2 of the 4 days I stayed in NOLA. The crispy Brussel sprouts & jump lump crab cakes & corn & crawfish bisque were my faves! My waiter was high energy and very pleasant & made our experience great. It's about a 15 min walk from the French quarter but so worth it!

My family and I (4 people) came to Luke for Easter brunch. After having looked at the menu, the waitress came to take our order. My son (12) who was ready to place his order for appetizer and main course, told her what he wanted. My husband and I were not quite ready and needed a few more minutes. The waitress felt the need to say (referring and looking at my son): "well, he will have to take a chill pill".
This set the tone for the entire visit, bc that was not only rude, but unnecessary. My son wasn't loud, he didn't misbehave ... he was just eager to order his entire meal. A response like "I'll be back in a few minutes" would have been sufficient.
It's never ok for a waiter/waitress to put someone's child in check. 

This was an unpleasant experience and should not have gone this way. We were there for a special day, and will not be returning. 
I hope that after reading my review, the manager can have a talk with this waitress.

I always have a wonderful experience here! I always walk into a smile and delicious smelling food! You get great service, never wait more than 10 minutes for hot and fresh food, and not to mention a full stomach! I usually will swing by for their lunch special, Mon-Sat from 11-3. The lunch special is a whopping $6.20!!! You get your entree, rice, an egg roll or soda, it doesn't get much better than this!! I'm also very picky with my sauces, being from NYC, we can get that way. But their sauces are delightful and always have the perfect amount of spice to them. My favorite is their garlic sauce....ummmm yessssss! Not too spicy but you can taste the red pepper a little, rich in flavor. Just, go get it yourself. Want a great experience and even greater grub, go to House of China.

Shell yeah! We came here for happy hour at the recommendation of my sister and her fiancé and the hype is real. We had our fill of raw and fried oysters and kept the drinks flowing. The oysters were so fresh and briny - honestly the best oysters I've ever had. The drinks were really tasty and strong. Their specialty drinks were half off - great deal for good drinks. The service was also impeccable - our waiters were very friendly and attentive. Special shout out to Chef Rich who came and checked on us throughout the night! Honestly shook that they have happy hour daily. Can't wait to come back! Luke, you are my father now.

Our furnace went on New Years Eve. My wife and I were really stressing since we have a newborn in the house.  I called a bunch of places and they were the only one that had a live person pick up.  He told me that a tech can be there that day around noon.  So I figured the tech would get there at noon or later. I was really shocked when the tech, Jason got there at 10am.  Unfortunately I needed a new furnace.  We also decided to get the A/C unit from them as well. (That went in Aug and was going to wait till spring to replace it).  He gave me a competitive price and it was ordered that day.  They installed the unit the following Monday.  The techs, Tony and Mike got there around 8am to start removing the old unit.  Jason got there later with the new one.  They were all very professional, courteous, and efficient.  I would recommend Fahrenheit to anyone.

In my humble opinion, New Orleans is one of the top 3 dining cities in the United States, and John Besh is arguably the best chef in town (granted, he has some strong competition in Donald Link and Susan Spicer). Whatever issues I may have once had with this restaurant have dissolved completely, and I joyfully and enthusiastically pronounce my love for this wonderful little bit of heaven on earth. When we arrived for our latest evening of indulgence, we discovered that the menu had been changed and some of our old favorites were missing. My husband's mood downshifted from expectant to irritated very quickly, but he need not have worried; the items we chose were sufficiently delicious to turn things around. We started with our usual 2 dozen P&J oysters, which were better than they usually are here. I usually get a French 75 and/or a bourbon old fashioned here, and they're still some of the best cocktails in town. We had a little glitch with my husband's drink, which at first had no vodka in it and then, after being doctored up by the bartender, had way too much vodka in it. He switched beverages and all was well. 
So one change in the menu was to add shrimp and grits (Shrimp En Cocotte), and, as this is one of my favorite dishes, I chose it. Good move. Their's may well be the best executed of this Southern standard that I've ever had; creamy and spicy roasted jalapeño cheese grits with smoky Andouille and green onion sausage, redolent of that full shrimp flavor that lets you know they've infused the dish with some stock, and sizable Gulf shrimp. Perfection. Really, if they never added another dish to this menu, I could be happy with this one forever. We didn't save room for dessert, but that didn't stop us from ordering one to share. If the Chocolate Bourbon Pecan Tart with Coconut Sorbet is still on the menu when you read this, get it. Coffee as always is great here too.

When we used to stay at the Continental we would eat at Luke's every once in a while and didn't think much of it.  After we bought our condo we didn't have a reason to sample them in our dinner rotation.  Once New Orleans opened back up after the End of the World and every restaurant was booked solid with out of town visitors we decided to give Luke another chance - and we are glad we did.  The Brussels Sprouts are the best we've ever had and the chargrilled oysters are amazing!

Okay guys, I have no idea why there's an umlaut in Luke, and this was a source of silliness for us the entire time we were in Nola. Our hotel was a block or so away, so we kept walking past this restaurant and pronouncing it with a very exaggerated umlaut. 

Imagine our surprise when all you yelpers suggested coming here for brunch. I was a little incredulous, given the umlaut, but it turns out, it's actually a legitimate brunch place.

We came on a Saturday at around 10am. There was no wait, we were seated immediately in the back, near the glass windows looking into the kitchen. This was probably one of the best seats in the house, because we got a chance to look at all of the good stuff coming out. So when the waitress mentioned that eggs in a jar were one of their most popular options, i believed her (I saw three of them come out while we were deciding what to get). 

Look, I understand it's one of the more important things on the menu, but if someone in your party gets this, and it's not you, you're going to be jealous. You are. So just order it. 

The shrimp is battered and then fried, and arranged around the rim of this jar. The jalapeno cheese grits and the egg are in the bottom of the jar, and all you really need to do is mix them all around and then throw the shrimp in there. This was by far one of the most interesting and tasty things I ate while I was in Nola. Save yourself the heartache, and just order it. You'll thank me later.

Came here for happy hour on a recommendation and was so glad I did.

Made a reservation for HH just in case (there's a bunch of open time slots ahead of time, but it was pretty packed when we arrived and fuller every minute.)

The raw and fried oysters were great! I felt like I ate an ocean's worth of oysters before dinner. We also got the Belle on the bayou which was on the stronger side but very good. I didn't taste the jalapeno too much, so if you're worried about it being "spicy," it's not. My partner got the French 75 which he loved and I also liked, despite neither of us being fans of lemon.

The service was good, we were served and checked up on in a timely manner. Although I noticed the table next to us waited a while for their order to be taken and a little longer to get their food, but again, it was pretty busy. I loved the pins our server was wearing, it adds a touch of personality in a small way.

I've already been recommending this spot for HH! Will definitely return!

Let me preface by saying that I hate "Southern food." All of it. Oysters, shrimps, grits, fried crap... I hate every bit of it. 
Was stuck in NOLA for a few months this year and had to endure. 
Came to Luke twice for breakfast with some friends. 
They LOVED it. LOVED it. Still talk about it... 
I had the Luke breakfast (had none of the Southern items I so hate) and it was EXCELLENT. Bacon, andouille sausage, massive biscuits, fresh 'taters ... top shelf food. Coffee was a French press w/ fresh cream. 
YES please. 
Had a Luke burger too. Solid burger for a joint that specializes in oysters and shrimps. 
Highly recommended.

As the restaurant for the Intercontinental in NOLA, Luke keeps up to the hotel's high standards. The restaurant decor matched historic NOLA and the food was great. We made reservations beforehand and it was a breeze from there getting seated. Our server was sweet and made sure to check up on us often. We went during happy hour but wasn't given an actual happy hour menu. I'm glad I studied the menu beforehand so we tried their boudin bites, crab bisque, dozen raw oysters, oyster platter, crawfish pot pie and brie burger. My wife and I enjoyed the crawfish pot pie the most. It was creamy and succulent while the crust was flaky and delicious. The bisque had great crab flavor throughout and the raw oysters were decently sized. The Oyster platter allowed to try all 6 broiled oysters but our favorites were the rockefeller and the one with bacon. The other 4 kinds were average and nothing to write home about. The brie burger was humongous and the meat patty was moist throughout. The sesame bun was toasted and the burger was everything you want in a gourmet burger. I would definitely come back to Luke next time I visit NOLA.

This was the one restaurant I had to try in NOLA because of their happy hour oysters - only $0.75 each! What's great is that they have happy hour EVERY DAY from 3-6pm! Unfortunately we didn't make a reservation for Saturday and the next available table would be after 10pm (we came in around 4:45pm) but the bar was open so our group decided to just eat there.

DELICIOUS OYSTERS! Not sandy and most oysters were quite large. I'm not sure why only half of us received crackers and vinegar sauce..

Drinks:
DRAFT BEER - Something called Provision or prohibition. Super easy to drink and kind of tangy. Even my friend who hates beer actually loved it!
FRENCH 75 - Wish I had ordered this for myself. cognac, fresh lemon juice & champagne - what could go wrong?!
SILVER SAINT - tequila, fresh lime juice, cucumber syrup, serrano pepper, & soda water. Really tasty and strong drink!

HIGHLY RECOMMEND LUKE!

We bring our Rhodesian/Rottie and our rescued mutt (a Pit plus Terrier of sorts?) here. They are attentive, staff friendly, etc. The prices seem fair and if they suggest creams or meds you don't want to give your dog, you can say "no" without being made to feel like an evil dog owner. We are in charge of our fur babies.

Greeted almost immediately upon seating by my friendly server - a young man who managed what appeared to be the entire front room without difficulty and maintained the demeanor of someone trained under the Thomas Keller Empire - the service would be perfect throughout.  Bread was timely, coffee and water refills spot on, plate descriptions accurate thorough, and all done with a friendly down-to-earth demeanor and a smile.  Going over the daily special with me I was left to decide while he went to get my coffee.

Listening to the room - lively but not loud despite the parade going by in the street - I labored over the menu for some time because everything sounded quite good - essentially bistro fare with a southern twist.  Returning with the coffee - a great thick blend with a bit of chicory but more prominently cocoa notes (I'm rather certain the same as that at August) I decided to go with the "express lunch" special - a $15 soup and main combo plus an added appetizer.  Smiling my server told me I'd made a great choice and slipped away to serve his other tables.

Arriving shortly after my order was placed - yet another crispy and golden French loaf, this time served with a delightful and grassy salted butter.  While the bread was not quite as delicious as that at Clancy's it was my second favorite of the trip and the butter put it over the top - thankfully I limited myself to just the one loaf because it turns out Luke's "deal" lunch is not for the faint of heart (or stomach.)

Arriving first, my soup - the daily special of crawfish bisque.  Clearly tomato and cream based with heavy spicing and ample crawfish the dish was unlike any bisque I've ever tasted, but certainly not a gumbo either.  Loaded with chunks of fresh crawfish and spicy without being "hot" I liked the bisque and as it would turn out (oddly) to be my only experience with crawfish on the trip I was glad I'd chosen it even though I likely would have preferred the daily gumbo.

My second dish, an addition to the prix fixe, was the Foie Gras - quite frankly, if a place is offering a terrine of Foie I'm probably going to order it.  Presented elegantly this terrine proved not only good, but exemplary.  Featuring a thick cut of slow cooked terrine painted on all sides with a Gewürztraminer reduction, topped with micro greens and a coarse sea salt, and drizzled with thick and sweet balsamic I can favorably compare this $16 preparation to the $30 supplemented version served at The French Laundry - though it wasn't quite as airy or delicate.   Served with toasted brioche (I was brought more on request) and beautifully textured I would strongly recommend any fan of cold foie to visit Luke for the experience.

Arriving next was the daily special - having looked at the menu I was surprised when it arrived because I expected a sandwich...but the surprise was the good kind...the really good kind.  In describing their cochon du lait prep my server told me how the slow roast pork is reduced down similar to pulled pork and then "rehydrated" with a dairy, onion, and garlic reduction (plus the chef's special spices) and then pan fried crispy on top.  If that description doesn't do it for you - try it...almost a sweet yet creamy pork meatloaf with a crispy and salty skin akin to pork belly.  Accompanying the pork on the plate were not only the advertised stewed greens and vinegar laden cherry mustard, but also a hefty helping of cornbread dressing.  Call it bistro food, call it soul food, call it comfort food - I call it one of the most unexpectedly delicious dishes I've had in some time.

Asking me if I was interested in dessert I told him I didn't even need the menu - just bring the bread pudding.

Arriving about 15 minutes later as I read a complimentary copy of the New York Times the bread pudding was an absolute masterpiece - the best traditional bread pudding I've ever tasted.  Described simply as cinnamon raisin bread pudding with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce the complexities of the dish were astounding for a bread pudding - piping hot with the smooth and creamy ice cream slowly melting the bread pudding itself was marvelous in custard/bread ratio and the sauce had minimal alcoholic kick while instead focusing on notes of caramel, pecan, cinnamon, and what may have even been honey.  Having had a whole lot of bread pudding in my time this was undoubtedly my favorite non-chocolate version to date.

Wow.  The power of good burger.  If you have a taste for a fantastic burger uniquely made this is the place. It's enough to share, comes cut in half with thick bacon, and is loaded with fries.  Located in the heart of downtown New Orleans Luke doesn't disappoint, even during the pandemic. Staff is wearing masks, tables are mostly socially distanced.  I also like the fact that several members of the Luke team waited on us, we never had to ask for anything... They were on point.
The menu is a bit limited but the items offered are some of their most popular!!
I love it here! The service is on point and the food is phenomenal! I am always ordering this food and will continue to! The workers are very nice. I will definitely be going back soon!

We dined here our last night in NOLA hoping to end our food adventures on a high. Sadly, we were disappointed.

The food was good, but not amazing, and the service questionable.

PROS:
1. Ambient. Not too loud. Not too crowded. Nice booths and tables.
2. Decent food, but nothing to go out of your way for. The dessert was better than the entrees. OMG, try the pot de creme (a chocolate mousse dessert) or the L'opera (huge ass layer cake with chocolate sauce on top).
3. Amazing coffee. Best coffee I drank in NOLA.

CONS:
1. Questionable service. I called to make a reservation for 5 around 8:30. The hostess said they were busy and it would be about 20 minutes. We walked in at 8:45, so a few minutes early. She said, "Your reservation is not till 9. Your table won't be ready until then or maybe even later. That's your table over there. They just need to clear it." 

WTF. First off, she didn't give me the time when I called. Second off, our table was empty. Just not bussed/cleaned yet. She sent us to the bar while our table sat unattended and unbused for 40 minutes! They weren't even terribly busy and I have no idea how this system makes sense. How long does it take to clear a table? Apparently a long time.

When we finally sat down, we were ready to order given the fact that we had 40 minutes to look at the menu. The waitress asked us, "Anything to drink?" I said, "Sure, but we're also ready to order our food." She said, "Oh, I can't take your order yet. Just drinks." I asked, "Why not?" She said, "I need to place this order I just took first. Then I'll be back." 

Again, random and weird excuses.

DO NOT GO HERE unless you want to experience potentially strange service protocols. DO GO HERE if you are okay with this fact and want some good coffee and dessert.

As for me, I won't be coming back.

amazing oysters but don't bother with the foie gras. it's not worth the price for what you get.  Also people who love darker rue gumbo should avoid the chef gumbo. it's much too light and doesn't have the rich deep flavor of darker rue gumbo though the seafood in it was great. I also loved the French 75, it's definitely better made with the cognac than with gin. beware of the crowds through. you should either come here early or make a reservation because it was packed by 6pm.
Very nice staff.  The staff is very friendly and always assist me with a smile when I visit this store.  I have never had a problem with my order.
The food was good. I specially enjoyed the gumbo soup and roasted Brussels sprouts. The service was OK.

Five stars because we actually could have eaten here 2 nights in a row and that's not too common for us.
I couldn't decide what my first taste of NOLA should be, toss up btwn the étouffée and the shrimp and grits. 
At the same time, upon entering, they had fresh king crab legs! And there was an amazing jagerschitzel which I knew my husband would be getting. I went with Shrimp & Grits because they are really the best grits, so I wanted to taste great grits.
I started with a Jambalaya too so as to know what theirs was like. Is was Ina "dirty broth" of everything crustacean- tasted like the ocean. Very delicious and warming in a spice kind a way.
Everyone raves about the burger too, saw it and it looked great. So many choices! But I came to eat what I can't get in California.
My kids had the most perfect chicken strips that tasted amazing and cheesy noodles that tasted amazing too,
My shrimp & grits were out of this world! I could eat those grits all day long! You'll eat them nodding your head with understanding how delicious they really are!
The schnitzel was "off the hook" crumbled bacon on top and sitting on the spaetzel that was cooked in smoked bacon, it was bacon overload but in a delicious OMG way. There were also some mushrooms..blanking on the kind, the brown stalky slender ones. So good!
Great great food.
Portions were good too that we could enjoy the desserts! We usually don't order but def. Don't miss the bread puddings/ vanilla ice-cream  and the vanilla cake w/ creme fraiche and blueberries!! 
Magnificent meal indeed!

My son and daughter in law brought a Sushi Platter after Thanksgiving, and Everything was Delicious, Fresh, Amazing!  The Salmon was very fresh, and melts in the mouth.  It came with sauces, and ginger, which were also so tasty and fresh.  Definitely Highly recommend!

Luke deserves every single star available lol!

We went there for dinner the very first night of my Bachelorette Party weekend in New Orleans. 7 of us girls and multiple people in our party said their food was "the best thing they've ever eaten".  

Our waiter was amazing! He was very enthusiastic and fun and any time we asked about a menu item he explained in great detail. His recommendations were on point and he even suggested some customizations to some of the menu items for us that turned out to be fantastic! 

Definitely no surprise this place comes highly recommended. If you're in New Orleans, its a must-do!

Stopped by today to grab some lunch for my grandson and me. I tried to order two quesadillas and was told I had to order thru the website. I said, you have all that I need right in front of me. Three different employees told me no you have to order thru the website. So got out of line and went to the corporate website and filled in all the blanks but on. My email address. They would not take my order without it. Having been a president of an ad agency for 33 years I knew exactly what they were doing. Getting my cell number and email to constantly bug me about their goofy stores. And I immediately received an email from them. Hey guess what I'm not coming back in this lifetime!! Chipotle in English is Horsepucky!

Five stars for their Brussel sprouts alone!  Service was amazing as well.  

We made a 9:30 pm Friday night thru Open Table.  We were a little surprised to find the restaurant only about half full when we arrived to be seated.  However, we were just glad we could quickly get seated and get something to eat!

I ordered the matzo ball soup and Brussel sprouts.  The soup was ok, nothing too amazing.  But the sprouts - they are deserving of a five star review all on their own!  Totally different than any order of Brussel sprouts I've had before.  I'm not usually a fan of vegetables with any kind of sweet glaze/flavor, but the combo with all the spice was really amazing.  My husband, who can't stand Brussel sprouts, even tried them and said they were good!

The wait staff was really attentive, kind and quick.  My only regret is I didn't try the beet salad.  I spoke to a friend the day after we dined at Luke and she said the beet salad is her favorite salad ever.

Came here for an anniversary dinner. The service and food was great. All staff had masks on. The sweet corn bisque was amazing. The Louisiana shrimp and grits was also really good. The French fries were also super delicious...but for $6 they had better be lol.
Best sushi around and so friendly! Love going to Hachi! Everything is crafted with such care. Great taste and beautiful presentation! Classy and yummy!

Thank you for the amazing food. Came in with no reservation around 4pm. Wait staff informed us of specials still available HAPPY HOUR which wasn't on the menu. So we were still able to get half off drinks. This is my moms first time in the city and she has been planning for 12 years. It's her birthday and they treated her with upbeat attitudes, great atmosphere and a surprise from the staff. Highly recommend this establishment!!!

If you are a raw oyster lover,  this is the place and still offering happy hour too.  Don't miss the fried oysters for a variety .  They do include some specialty cocktails and beer on the happy hour menu so make sure to order the French 75

We took our 3 dogs to get groomed there and when we arrived we were told they needed a fecal exam and a wellness exam, which, for each dog, would be about $100, in addition to the grooming. We were never told this when making the appointment. All we were told is to bring shot records. They said their policy was each dog must have a wellness exam and fecal exam within 6 months. So we left and the poor groomer was left with a 3 hour hole in her schedule.

The place is a ripoff don't go there.

Lüke Restaurant is consistent with their food: fresh, prepared as requested, the correct temperature, and served up in a eye-pleasing fashion. However, what is inconsistent is the service by the hostess. I visited with a party of three on July 8, 2021 at 1:30pm for lunch and the hostess was a complete disaster. We walked through the door right on time. The hostess never once greeted us. Instead, she glared at us while wrapping up a conversation about future reservations with a customer on the phone. It would have been understandable EXCEPT she stayed on the call for five full minutes (unacceptable). When I finally said, "excuse me, would you please call someone to get us seated" the hostess rudely retorted that she's the only one seating parties. I asked her to please put the call on hold and seat my party. She rolled her eyes, grabbed menus and quickly shuffled us to a table. No apology was extended. Unacceptable. Once seated, our party enjoyed both the burger and the chicken sandwiches, all accompanied by thin, crispy, and delicious French fries. The buns were toasted and the meat was seasoned well. The food experience was exceptional, as usual. The hostess situation left a lot to be desired.

I had such a fun time here!! The service was incredible. Our waiter was really fun and had a lot of character and personality. It was paced very well. We never felt rushed or like we were waiting too long on part of our meal. The only thing that felt like it was taking a while was the cocktail that my mom ordered and the waiter just gave it to us for free. The atmosphere was amazing, everyone sounded like they were having a great time and the decorations are very chic without being uncomfortably posh. We split the fried quail appetizer which was incredible! I highly recommend that because it was tender and beautifully seasoned. Then I had the ribeye as an entree which was very undercooked from what I asked (I asked for medium-well and got a steak that was closer to medium or medium-rare). But it was seasoned very well. For dessert I got the Creme Brûlée which was good but not great, but my mom got the bread pudding, which I tried a little bit of, and it was phenomenal!! I would absolutely recommend this place because it's reasonably priced and has an incredible atmosphere and good food!

The absolute worse. We're out $20k and we have to completely replace the system they installed only two years ago. The installation process was rocky -- crews repeatedly late, no apologies from office personnel -- and after installing the units they left large holes in the wall saying we had to call their guy to get it repaired.  (Their guy did come out once but was then unreachable.) A few months after installation, there was black mold in our bedroom and not all the units seemed to be working. More holes, more phone calls. We just gave up dealing with them and lived with the new holes and sketchy system until now as we renovate.  Contractors telling us now that we'll need to replace everything because of mold in the units. The Carrier warranty is not valid because the installation was done incorrectly. I would give 0 stars if i could.

Well that was pleasant! 
Needed to pick up a ship to store package from REI today. The parking lot was absolutely packed I thought to myself sarcastically, well this will be a treat! Turns out it was:)

They had a head counter at the door, along with masks in case you forgot yours and hand sanitizer. There was a sign with a large enough diagram to explain to people the correct way to wear a mask. Very refreshing.  While inside I didn't see one person that had forgot their nose has holes in it too. Refreshing!

So like I said very pleasant! A store with a lot of the outdoor goodies we all love that encouraged everyone to respect everyone By helping keep everyone safe!

Happy Hour from 3-6pm everydayyy!  $.75 raw oysters, $1.50 chargrilled oysters, half off wine and some drinks! :D

Sit at the bar because it's first come first serve and waiting for a table mayyyy take forever.  And service at the bar is way way faster, plus you get to see them shucking your oysters.  I was in a rush to catch a plane, and I was in and out of there in 30 min!

Loved the oyster shuckers, they were super nice, friendly, and funny! :) Tip them well!

Oysters are on the saltier/brinier side, compared to those of ACME or Felix's.

It's like people say on this review.  Great staff and Great food. Portions are large. You don't leave hungry.  My wife and I are from north of Toronto Canada. Next time we are visiting New Orleans we will definitely stop in.  Thanks again.

We spent a few days here in New Orleans trying the local food and ambiance. None of the places we have been to even compare!  The food is incredible, the ambiance is warm and friendly, but what stood out the most was the staff.  
Mandy is an absolute gem! Super friendly and makes your experience unforgettable! 

Habds down best place in New Orleans with the best staff!

I have yet to be disappointed by any of John Besh's offerings. Coming back five years after my last visit, the happy hour is still great as well as the food. It's one of my favorite happy hours in the city and one of the best ones I attended on this trip. $1 oysters are better quality than other places we went to and the craft cocktails are excellent. I enjoyed both the ABV and the French 75, both very good. Also their weekday lunch special is fantastic value --now that August no longer offers their Friday prix fixe lunch I'll have to manage with this one.

I ordered Fish Fillet Hunan Style. It was good with good veggie combo (broccoli, carrots, bell peppers, baby corn, and mushrooms were not mushy nor overcooked).  Chef said it was spicy but I thought it was mild. My hubby ordered some lobster dish and he enjoyed it too.  The price of everything was average. Not too many Chinese restaurants are good for takeout but this restaurant is.

Great happy hour and great service. The oysters were tasty, the beer delicious and the servers went out of their way to help each other and us.
Super classy place!!

A group of seven of us made a reservation after our city tour at 10pm. We read all of the good reviews and we were super excited to give Luke a try. When we got there, we were told that we had to order asap because the kitchen was about to close - understandable - but why allow reservations for 10 pm if the kitchen closes then? 
We ordered oysters (delish), tuna tartare (very good) and an assortment of different entrees. The swordfish was tasty, slightly over cooked, but the squash that it came with was nearly inedible salty. The burger was good - nothing to write home about, but it was a burger after all. The crawfish etouffee was just ok... I had much better from other spots in the city. The mussels were mediocre, not terrible though. 
We finished eating, and waited for an uncomfortable amount of time for the server to bring the check. Staff was closing the restaurant around us, and we were just ready to go. Finally after probably 20 minutes of waiting, the check was dropped. 
The servers were friendly but seemed agitated with our presence. Again, understandable as they were trying to close, but we made the reservation over 12 hours ahead. 
Unfortunately, Luke is not a place that I would recommend to family and friends visiting NOLA. We had much better meals, with better service, at a lower price at other restaurants during our stay. 
Overall very disappointing.

The food here was good: I ordered the gumbo (small portion) and split the bread pudding for dessert (delicious).

The service left something to be desired and had the potential to ruin our whole meal. Our main server abandoned us about 20 minutes in to give his attention to a bachelorette party and a loud argument about college football with some bar patrons but never found the time to put in our oyster and wine orders. Thankfully the second server took over, and he was great. I expected good service all around from a restaurant like this...

Very cool environment with great service!

Dropped by late at night as a second dinner. We ordered half-a-dozen PB&J oysters ($14) and a cup of silver queen corn and crab bisque ($9). Both were delicious! I loved how fresh the oysters were. They tasted refreshing and clean when paired with a squeeze of lemon juice and dab of mignonette sauce. 

I was also pleasantly surprised by the bisque. It was  a good creamy consistency and not too salty. It's definitely one of the better ones I've had.

Loved my experience at this restaurant overall. Would recommend if you are dropping by and want to taste delicious dishes in New Orleans!

Don't trust the seafood display.  The oysters are very small "seed" oysters.  Worse, when I placed my order, I mentioned that I preferred "nice sized" oysters and the waiter said that they were nice.  Then after the oysters were delivered he just smiled and said that the seafood display was fake, empty props.

Absolutely loved Luke !! The food was fantastic!!! Definitely will go back!! I chose a fried oyster salad to die for. Oysters were perfectly cooked in a light batter and fried to perfection and they love thick slices of fried bacon that was heavenly!!!!

Best sushi around. That statement comes from someone who lived in NYC for 13 years and has traveled al over. The quality of Hachi sushi rivals my favorite spot in Manhattan. All of their dishes are excellent.

After having a bad experience from the other location down the street I tried this one and this one is possibly worse. Customer service wasn't as bad or rude as the other one but the food quality is not up to par. First of all the whole ordering quesadillas online only is just dumb. But I played along despite the inconvenience. So now after waiting in line I take a few minutes and place the online order. It says it will take 12 min. But I think maybe quicker because it's pretty dead inside. Nope. Longer than 12 min. Now there's three of us waiting for online orders and the other 2 counter workers and the cooks start having some kind of Tik Tok dance party and the online order dude is getting slammed. And then another guy takes a cell call and walks into the dining area while nobody is helping to get our orders out faster. Still nobody at the counter either. So I finally get my order 6 minutes later. Get home and apparently I ordered the mini burrito not the usual hefty burrito one comes to expect from Chipotle. I take a few bites and man the rice is crunchy! Then they give us a moldy mandarin orange for the fruit in our kid's meal. C'mon!!! Striking out hard with these Indy locations. So weak.

Highly recommend an advance reservation. Visited during a Saints game and was looking to sit at the bar for a quick drink and appetizer. Upon arrival the bar was packed and the restaurant reservations were full and people were turning around. Long extensive drink menu and small plates, not many options for entrées. Ordered The French 75 and brussels sprouts. The brussels sprouts were good more soft than crispy. The sauce and overloaded almonds made it a good dish. French 75 was made with cognac instead of Gin which had a very settled taste instead of the tanginess which I appreciated.

I very rarely leave reviews but this place serves to be praised for every aspect of my meal.  I ordered online for pickup and the food was prepared, ready and waiting for me even before the pickup window that was provided. I arrived a few minutes early.
