Since moving to Bucks County 2 years ago my choices for good quality Sushi were minimal. The only excellent place I found prior to Hachi was Ooka. None of their 3 locations were ideal but I did the drive when I wasn't willing to settle for mediocre sushi.  Today I found Hachi I n Chalfont that is equal to and dare I see even exceeds Ooka.  Everything was excellent. The taste and quality of the food, the portion size, the attention to detail with the presentation of my meal was exceptional! This was a takeout order so I wasn't expecting beautiful presentation with a fresh cut flower in each container.  The Ikura was so French and full of flavor. The tuna was was delicious and clearly higher grade than what I am usually able to find at suburban sushi restaurants.  Even something simple like Kani salad was stepped up a notch with excellent ginger dressing.  Hachi could easily compete with the top notch Sushi offered in center city Phila. I am impressed by this place and excited to have a new go to spot for high quality Sushi close to home.
Best sushi restaurant in every way. They do a classy job. Thanx HACHI for giving us a great place to go in this ghost town of chalfont. I hope you never leave and everyone is so nice there

If I had to summarize their sushi in one sentence, I'd say their sushi is more like a salad with some meat than real sushi.

Phone person was rude. Fairly commonplace, but ok.

The sushi is beyond forgettable if not for the pricing. The sushi has the thinnest slices of the more expensive ingredients and otherwise is packed with cheap ingredients like vegetables. In fact, the rolls are so overpacked with "filler" ingredients they tend to fall apart when you attempt to pick them up. To make it even more obvious there is this painfully obvious attempt to deceive the customer, they stuff the sushi containers to the brim with useless kale leaves.

They're clearly cutting corners and trying to save a buck while charging a premium for a product they're skimping on. They don't deserve your business.

*My review is solely for happy hour* -- I came here for happy hour (3pm-6pm) based on the recommendations of my fellow yelpers and was not disappointed! Half off cocktails, beer and wine, plus $1.25/fried oyster and $0.75/oyster. You are required to get the fried oysters in increments of half a dozen. They were some of the better ones I've had in the area; crispy on the outside, meaty on the inside, and were decently sized. The raw oysters were amazing- they were massive and good quality, and you can't beat the price.  Definitely some of the best happy hour oysters I've had in my life! Service was very friendly, refilling our water glasses frequently and checking in with us just the right amount. Would come back here in a heartbeat during my next visit to New Orleans!

This was highly recommended to me by a friend and when I found out this was right across from the hotel we were staying in (intercontinental), I knew it was fate! 

We came here for happy hour and they certainly did not disappoint. We were seated immediately. I thought there would be a wait but it wasn't bad for a sunday afternoon. Of course, we came for the 75c oysters and they were every bit as delicious as I expected. We started off modest with only one dozen and then quickly realized this wasn't nearly enough for 2 people! We are fatties! We ended up consuming 2.5 dozen.

We also ordered the pate of louisiana rabbit/chicken livers. Sounds a little adventurous but don't shy away...pate is delicious. The portions were incredibly generous, the pate was placed in jar and served with crostini and a multitude of other toppings like a grainy mustard, chutney/jam?, pickled veggies, etc. Tasting each toppings individually was quite strange. However, once you put the pate on the crostini and pick your topping and eat it all together -- that's where the MAGIC happens. Wow, just incredible how well the flavors all somehow worked together. Don't be shy in asking for more crostinis because what it comes with isn't enough for the amount of pate they serve with. We shared this amongst 2 people but I feel it is more than enough for 6 people.  

Our server was just the right amount of attentive and our overall experience was very good. If you're in NOLA for a quick trip, this is worth it to add on your list.

The very few items on the menu are delicious. I would first recommend the bread pudding with extra pecans and the hamburger which tasted like smoked meat . The shrimp and grits had a twist that I never ate before which was added got sausage bites to it. It was really tasteful especially if you like spicy food. They can definitely add more selections to the menu but like mentioned before the very taste really good.

We stopped in for a quick lunch with our family on the way to the airport. It was a gorgeous space with easy parking. The staff were all so pleasant and the service was great. Food was very good. We had oysters for a starter and then lunch fare. The chicken sandwich was everyone's favorite along with the madame.

By far best oyster happy hour in the city.

Great service , killer drinks - and best happy hour.

The man we were transferred to when trying to have someone come out to fix our heat was rude and abrasive to my wife. We askd for someone to come out today if possible and they said yes but didn't give us a time. 2 hours passed and she called back. The same guy was once again rude, told her we had apparently cancelled our appointment, and when she said no she absolutely didn't he was short with her, told her to find someone else, and hung up on her. I don't know why companies seem to think this is an ok way to treat potential customers, but so far heating companies specifically are 0-for-2 with us today.
Great food and staff. Really, the service is what the gold standard should be. The chicken sandwich and burger were great, but the Brussels sprouts are where it's at!!

I have more issues with the Yelp reviews for this place than the actual place.
After reviewing everyone else's comments on the place, I'm not sure I went to the same place. It has a total hotel bar vibe (which, it technically, is). Kind of weirdly bright lighting and somewhat loud pop music.
A review below stated "very French and very upscale"??
I can't agree with either of those. "Upscale"? How is it? "French"? There are some french-themed paraphernalia on the wall. "Pretty dressy"? There was a family sitting near me all in shorts with kids covered in ketchup.

So. I don't get the other reviews on here.

This place is a casual restaurant that is attached to a hotel. As a sidenote, I left my hotel to eat dinner here and was kind of irked when I realized I was eating in another hotel restaurant. #FirstWorldBusinessTravelProblems

Solid raw bar with a seemingly ever changing selection of fruit of the sea. Pretty solid wine list as well - better than I expected, actually.
I also enjoyed the shrimp and crab etouffee - although I kind of thought the portion was a tad small (which is ironic because every other meal I've had in this town I thought the portions were a tad big).

So, go. It's good. You'll enjoy it.

As embarrassing as it is to order a hamburger in New Orleans, do yourself a favor and get down and dirty with a Luke burger.  It is unquestionably the finest hamburger I've ever tasted.  They use a slightly sweet bun, cook a huge hunk of high quality beef to an exquisite, dripping, true medium-rare, ladle on a pile of delicious carmelized onions, garnish with bacon and some Emmenthaler cheese, and kick in some thick-cut tomatoes and leafy lettuce for good measure.  It was huge.  It didn't need any condiments.  And it put me in a blessed state of food coma.
Do not use this company! unless you just want to give them all your money for replacing things that don't need replacing!
food was shit. Service was shit. Go to the grocery to get better food. Go somewhere else, save ur money!

If you honestly love your pet do not bring them here. My dog went in for a simple UTI and after all the medication they gave her, caused her whole body to shut down. She then died three weeks later. So bringing my dog here shortened her life span and cost me $3000. Please look for a vet that cares about your animal not money.

I was visiting the area from Chicago. My bunny started to show signs of GI stasis, a commonly known condition for rabbits, so I called around to see if vets accepted bunnies - they often do not since rabbits are considered exotics. Seven Oaks said they saw bunnies and I very specifically asked if they had the meds to treat her - it was confirmed over the phone that they did. It was New Years Eve so I understood that it would likely be busy so I made an appointment. I arrived a few minutes before my appointment to fill out the paperwork. And then I waited for 1.5 hours. 

I was finally moved into a room and waited another 30 minutes for the vet tech to come in. When he did, I told him her symptoms and he very seriously replied, "GI stasis? How do you spell that? I've never heard of it before." He then asked if she was vomiting, I told him that rabbits do not have the ability to vomit and he responded, "Wow! I'm learning so much from you. We don't normally see rabbits." I asked for a towel to put her on for the exam and they gave me a towel with a large stain but insisted it was clean.

I was then moved without explanation to a second room, which was filthy. They clearly had not cleaned in between patients. There was hair everywhere but the room also looked like it hadn't been deep cleaned in years with dead insects in the lights and dust blowing down from the vents - hardly the sanitary conditions you expect from a vet. 

The vet finally came in and saw my bunny. My vet in Chicago had faxed over all of her records; however, the vet at Seven Oaks informed me that they didn't have any of the meds that are typically given for GI stasis and she refused to write a prescription for me to find a pharmacy. She also confirmed they don't often see bunnies, which is why they didn't have any meds, but will see them if someone brings them in. Essentially, she confirmed they are just trying to get money from people. 

Generally speaking, vet appointments for my bunny are on the pricier side. However, this appointment was especially expensive with having accomplished nothing other than educating a vet tech and having the vet confirm my diagnosis. I ended up taking her to the emergency vet without an appointment and it only cost a little more - with the medicine. 

tl;dr: Said they could help, made an appointment, was at the vet for 2.5 hours, it was filthy, they told me they couldn't help my bunny, they charged me a lot of money (and confirmed they're basically only in it for the money).

I wish I could give this place zero stars. Do not send your animal here for treatment. I took my six month old sheepdog in for vaccines and a heartworm test. They came out and told me that they had to muzzle my puppy because he would not comply and that he needed obedience training. My puppy was visibly scared and also I could smell he sprayed from the stress. My family train dogs and obedience training may or may not aid in this type of situation . They mishandled my animal and were blaming me for the incident. Most veterinarian hospitals are trained in accommodating stressed animals.They do not know what they are doing at this hospital. Steer clear!

Response to Emily F. Review: if an animal is in distress, best practice is to get the owner especially if they are fearful. I am so sorry your staff had to restrain a vicious 6 month old puppy. Shame on you and your staff for this unauthentic apology and traumatic experience to my dog. There is no need to talk PRIVATELY, people need to know how you are treating animals.

I had a really good time at Luke. It was a special occasion. The service was excellent very friendly. The table was socially distancing so I felt safe. Gumbo was good. But the bread pudding was the best! I would definitely come back.

I loved it. The place reminded me on one of those long Brooklyn restaurant/bars with tile on the floor. The oysters were beautiful and my shrimp and grits were the best. I cannot remember what my wife ate but other than the oysters it probably did not have many calories. Felt very comfortable with the covid separation.

This was one of the first places that I wanted to try out, when I planned my trip to NOLA. Went to this place for brunch, and upon on arrival i was super excited to try out their chargrilled oysters. sadly, only their chargrilled oyster is offered at certain times. My girlfriend and I ordered the shrimp & grits, eggs in purgatory, and the p&j oyster(raw). The shrimp & grits was very flavorful and one of my favorite. Eggs in purgatory was okay, kind of reminded of shakshouka. But the OYSTERS was one of the best oysters I have ever had. Must try Luke when you're in NOLA. #JohnnyApproves

Best meal that we had in NOLA. Probably best meal that I have had all year.

Their version of gazpacho was heavenly-highlighted with fresh cherry tomatoes.

The shrimp ettouffe (sp) was a delight.

The Luke salad included super fresh and crispy chilled Bibb lettuce with delicious beets, cherry tomatoes, and cucumber. The sunflower seeds and soft creamy dressing were nice touches.

The grilled BBQ oysters were good. The gumbo was average. 

We enjoyed grilled broccolini and brussel sprouts, the later was dressed nicely and perfectly crisped. 

The staff was amazing.

The food here was spectacular! Delicious selection. Absolutely loved this place. We had the best service! Truly enjoyed my time here. I could not get enough of how cute this place was. Finished off dinner with a delicious cappuccino. Wouldn't have it any other way!

I'm a Canadian through and through, but today I felt like a real Southerner with Fried Chicken and Waffles glazed in Tabasco honey and creamy butter.  OMG it was superb.  Mint Julep to sip and I was loving it!  Wife had the Luke burger and was in heaven!  Service was impeccable and atmosphere was grand.

Today was my first time ordering take out. The food tastes good and was hot! The staff was nice also. I ordered the honey chicken meal/combo and the bourbon chicken combo. Both very good. Plenty of food to share or for the next day leftovers.

I went during daily happy hour (3-6pm) and waited for 20 minutes to sit at the bar on Christmas Day. They were completely booked and I can see why due to the quality of food there. I ordered a dozen of LA Gulf oysters ($1) and tried their fried oysters ($8/6). They were amazing! Like have you seen oysters this fat?! Worth my money. The fried oysters just melts in your mouth. I would say between these two, I prefer the raw on, given almost every food I ate in NOLA was fried . But also you can taste the natural sweetness in Raw oysters than fried. I also ordered myself 2 drinks (half off) and they were so good! I also had the best bartender, Lori (I think.. she has green hair). Would highly recommend this place.

This place is probably my favorite of the Besh restaurants. The reason for that is the because of the happy hour oysters (prices have changed over the years, by $0.25 each time). Currently the raw are $0.75 and friend $1.25 each. 

I love the raw oysters here, they are always high quality and very clean. When the peak season hits, they are the size of your palm

The fried oysters are also very good with a horseradish dipping sauce

The bar also has ample selection and probably has a few things you haven't tried before. 

Otherwise, the food is good, but the oysters are really the thing to come for

This place was absolutely delicious. We came for a work lunch and it was right around the corner. We were a group of about 8 and they were able to sit us easily. The menu is small and not overwhelming which I appreciate. I decided to go with the burger and they weren't lying when they said 10 oz! That thing was HUGE. I ended up deconstructing my burger because it was so big. The fries were also really great and crispy just how I like them. Everyone else was happy with their dishes. My director said the shrimp and grits was phenomenal. I will definitely come back! Yum!

I heard about this place a few times so I had to try. The food was not on the level I had expected but it was good. Our server kind of forgot about us in the end. Gave us our check and never came back. I'm know that businesses are suffering right now because they can't find help. I will try again when this crisis is over.

We went here after a work Christmas party and had a great experience. We ordered so much food. My favorites were the Flammenkuchen and the Louisiana raw oysters. I never would have ordered the flammenkuchen but the manager on duty, Peter, highly recommended it. It didn't disappoint! The oysters were so fresh and had a great salty taste. I was super impressed with the manager who was attentive to our table and noticed I wasn't drinking my cocktail. When asking me about it I said " it was a little too bitter for me but please don't worry about it" instead he took it and immediately doctored it up and then brought it back saying that he would be happy to get me a new one if this didn't help. Well whatever he did to it was delicious and it was so nice to have someone so attentive as fine dining should be. The food was delicious and the service was excellent... both which equally make the expertise of fine dining worth the money.

My first stop in New Orleans and my first time trying etouffe. I ordered the shrimp etoufee and the bisque. Both were good. There were chunks of crab shell in my bisque so I had to sort of watch out while I was eating. I also ordered the fried osyters, stuffed oysters and the raw oysters. The raw were good, but I probably would not order the fried (not very good) and the stuffed were okay. There were three hostesses at the stand cleaning menus and we stood there a good minute before we were acknowledged and when we left they didn't bother to say anything to us either. Our server was nice. I would eat here again.

First, shout out to Kayla (spelling?), you were awesome!!!

Came here during Happy Hour and decided to go light on the raw oysters because ACME Oyster Bar was scheduled for Wednesday. [ Good catholic boys can't eat meat on Ash Wednesday =) ] Well, in retrospect, I regret that decision. Lüke served better oysters. They were delicious, fresh, big, and not gritty at all. ACME's oysters had so much grit. However, this is about Lüke so...Be careful with the horseradish, it was really strong; you'll clear any nasal congestion by overdoing it. I also got a half-dozen order of their fried oysters which is served with some really good dipping sauce. (5 out of 5)

Crab Bisque: got a cup portion because my friend and I wanted to split multiple dishes to taste the menu but don't do it guys, ordering the cup portion that is. This was so good! This creamy soup loaded with tons of shredded crab meat was my favorite of the night. Don't pass on this! Must have! (5 out of 5)

Crispy Brussels Sprouts: I wouldn't call it crispy. UCHI in a Houston, Texas serves "crispy" BS and they're worth every penny. I really liked this nonetheless; they come second after UCHI's. The Marcona almonds gives a nice nutty tune throughout each bite and the Espelette honey gave it a sweetness that didn't make you feel like you were getting a sugar overload. (4 out of 5)

Shrimp & Grits: this has a little spicy kick to it from the jalapeños; somewhere between mild and medium on spice level. The Louisiana shrimps were meaty and tender and the grits very creamy in an andouille sauce with pieces of andouille sausages. I enjoyed it, it wasn't packing with flavor so I wouldn't say I'd order it again. (3 out of 5)

Brendan's Bread Pudding: I was told this is what their known for dessert wise. Though I liked it, I can't say it was the best bread pudding. I would suggest you ask for an extra side of their pecan sauce because that's mostly where the flavor will come from. (3 out of 5)

The noise level was HIGH. I don't know if it was because it was Mardi Gras week but don't bring your sleeping baby here.

The food is exxxxcellent! We got a whole array of things. Both gyoza were great, rock shrimp was my favorite, edamame was great, calamari was ok, miso soup was tasty, AC roll was good, grinch roll was pretty good. If I were local I'd return all the time. It's BYOB which we knew ahead of time so we came fully stocked lol

Amazing food! So good I had to go two days in a row on a two day trip to NOLA. The main thing I went back for was the Peruvian Scallop, my god, so yum. Bread pudding was also fantastic. The only issue I had, which doesn't take away from the rating is the second night I ordered coffee with my bread pudding and it never came. The waiter apologized and removed it from my bill (the coffee in the pic was from my first visit).

Luke
When it comes down to it, New Orleans has many different flavors of food to offer. We are most distinctively known for fresh seafood, soul food and of course Creole and Cajun cuisine. @lukeneworleans is a Creole inspired brassiere located right in the CBD. Now while it's known for happy hour every day and fresh seafood, I took a different approach and went for brunch and honey, they did not disappoint.

 The very first thing I enjoyed about their menu was the variety. The menu was well balanced w/ both breakfast and lunch items, but didn't overload the guest with too many options. My drink of choice was a French 75. The presentation was great. Cognac glass, lite fizzle and a highlighted 75 to finish it off. And yes, it tasted as good as it looked. 

 Now let's dig in! For starters, I ordered the "Crispy Brussels Sprouts" and the "Cast Iron Cinnamon Roll". I truly enjoyed both. The brussels sprouts were fried perfectly w/ toasted almonds, espelette honey and crumble cheese. Oh but the cinnamon roll was fantastic! The candied pecans were a perfect touch, the Creole cream cheese icing was irresistible. The entire cinnamon roll was just so soft, gooey, and warm. I had to stop myself from eating it all to make sure I had room for my meal.

 For my main course, I let my server choose for me. He surprised me with "Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp and Grits". Man he did not let me down. This order of shrimp  and grits  was a little different from what most restaurants offer. It had a tomato  base, roasted jalapeño  cheese  grits, andouille & green onion. The amount of heat from the sausage was perfect and the dish had all of your traditional creole flavors, topped off with flawlessly cooked shrimp . My date had  the "Croque Madame". It's very similar to a ham, egg, & cheese  sandwich, except the egg   is on top of the sandwich and sunny side up. I would suggest a knife and fork for this cheesy, yolky, goodness. 

 The server was attentive & knowledgeable. The vibe was nice and the location is fair. If you're not from NOLA, just a little hint, it's not spicy, it's only full of flavor! 
Overall 
Food, Service, & Atmosphere

Great atmosphere for lunch, casual or fancy. The service was fantastic and friendly. We ordered way too much food. The ONLY thing we didn't care for were the eggplant bites. But everything else was classy, elegant and tasty. If I can figure out how to attach the pics I took from my phone to this review on the computer I will shortly. It's definitely a food picture worthy place!

My favorite restaurant. I typically come here for friends birthdays with 10-12 of the guys. They're very accommodating and are a lot bigger inside the restaurant than what You can see. The food is unique and very professional too. So professional that I'm going on a first date here soon :).

Note: This is a long review, but with the cost of the work that you may be having done, I think it's worth the read.

Upon arriving home last Sunday from a weekend away, we walked in to a house that was 93 degrees with the central air conditioning blowing hot air out of the vents. I turned everything off and hoped that the evaporator coil was just frozen up from being overworked since it was 103° the day before in Philadelphia. We left it off overnight, but when we turned the unit back on in the morning, discovered that it still wasn't working.  I contacted JB Plumbing & Heating which was highly recommended on yelp in the Fishtown area and Mark told me that he didn't do AC work, but recommended Fahrenheit Climate Control to his customers.

I called Fahrenheit and they sent their service technician Jason out that afternoon, accompanied by a young apprentice I later learned was the owner's son.  I showed them to the deck where the outdoor unit is located and Jason instantly said that he knew that the compressor unit was shot. He told me that my Goodman condenser was a piece of crap and that they don't even make that unit anymore. He said that he thought that the unit wasn't under warranty because the serial number ended in 04, even though the builder that we bought the house from had only installed it the year before (2010).

He quoted me three options. 1) install a Hard Start Kit for $500 that could try to force the compressor to start up, but that was just a band-aid that could break again in a week; 2) Install a replacement compressor for $1800 but that he didn't trust Goodman products and there was no guarantee that it wouldn't break again in a year; and 3) to replace the outdoor compressor/condenser and the evaporator unit on the furnace for $3400 with a Carrier system with a 10 year warranty. At this point, I'll point out that he only took the side panel off of the outdoor unit and looked at the wires and listened to the sound of the machine.

I paid them $99 for the service call which would be applied to the final amount of work that we paid them to do. He left and I set to work doing some research online. After a number of calls, I discovered that my compressor unit was, in fact, under warranty, so I called back and left a message with Bonnie at their office to have Jason call me with a quote for the work without the cost of the compressor unit.

It turns out that he did call me back that evening and left a message on my voicemail which I didn't discover until later the next day. In the mean time, the next morning, I called the office and spoke with a man named Farrell. I explained the situation to him and said that I needed a quote for labor and replacing the refrigerant, etc. He said that he'd have Jason call me back. Having received no response, I called the office again at 1:30 that afternoon and Bonnie assured me that she'd have Jason call me.

When I got home from work late that afternoon, I found the voicemail Jason left the prior evening stating that the cost of the repair with the part under warranty was the $1800 that he quoted me the day before. I explained that he quoted me that price under the assumption that it was not, in fact, under warranty and that I thought the price should be much lower. He held firm and insisted that the cost of labor and flushing the lines and replacing the coolant added up to that sum.

We had a second opinion scheduled that same evening who immediately told me that the compressor would be under warranty and that the whole system didn't need to be replaced. He took the side panels and top off and tested everything with his meter to determine that the compressor was shot. He quoted us a price way below what Fahrenheit Climate Control insisted that the work should cost. He explained that he would get the part from the distributor and that the total for installation would be around $950 depending on the final credited cost of the part under warranty.

Jason, Bonnie, the apprentice & Farrell were all very courteous and took a lot of time to answer my questions.  The miscommunication with the missed voicemail led to a day's worth of back and forth, but that's my fault. My low rating is based purely on the fact that I was quoted a price for the part not being under warranty but that when I pushed back, they said that wasn't the case. I feel like I was being taken advantage of.

I learned a valuable lesson during this process: Ask a ton of questions and do as much research as possible. In doing so, I'm out the $99 that I paid for the service call, but I've saved almost $800.

My co-worker and I had breakfast here, and while it was solid, I didn't find anything particularly amazing or gourmet about it other than the prices and decor.  Don't get me wrong, the breakfast tasted great, but I'm guessing that lunch and dinner are the times to come here and get wowed.
Dr. Sree Reddy is the best veterinarian in Tampa Bay! My family has been taking our pets to Dr Reddy at Seven Oaks for many years, we all highly recommend.  Prices are good, service is excellent.

Rabbit and chicken liver pâté w/ grilled garlic bread. Then I was recommended the schnitzel by a local. Great food excellent service. However,as a solo diner,  I felt rushed.   Nonetheless, great place
Happy hour raw oyster $1/each, so fresh and big. The most valuable food. Crawfish Étouffée is tomato base with cream, high quality crawfish. Highly recommend.

Today I got someone that hardly put anything on my plate and I asked for just a little more and moved on with still hardly anything on my plate for a $15 meal... what really made me mad was while I was checking out the cook in the back said with a mad moody voice "if the customer asks for more don't give them a big scoop give them a little one" I'm paying $15 for this that's crazy.

Haven't been in a while, but I always enjoyed it.
Bro. Those oysters. Those oysters bro. Those oysters.
It's a little pricey but I do want to go back when oyster season comes back around. I believe they have oyster specials for happy hour, but I could be wrong about that. Either way, place is great and worth it.
Great burger and the Brussels spout appetizer is a don't miss.  I get the best service at the bar.

The Burger was super juicy and tasty.  It was good.  The Brussel sprouts were a little bitter.  Nice casual spot downtown with upscale service.  The only problem was that we had a few gnats flying around our table.

Walked in for Happy hour and the hostess was an absolute sweetheart! We were a party of 8 and our table was ready instantly. The $1 oysters on happy hour were delicious! Service was great. The Chicken noodle soup was the best I've had, ended up ordering 3. This is no chicken soup from a can. The drinks were delicious. A gentlemen who helped our table truly made our experience even more memorable. We were seated near the kitchen which is all glass and we can see into it. I would return to try dinner for sure !

Made a reservation with open table for lunch and we were seated right away. Seriously if you want to make sure you get a table and anticipate it might be busy make reservations!!! 
Everything was delicious and the service was great! This is located right next to the Hilton on st Charles. Inside is clean with classic designs. 

Everything was delicious from the drinks to the food. I can't say I ordered anything that didn't taste good. I was impressed with the food and the service and would definitely come back again. 
I ordered the shrimp and grits. It was probably the best dish I had!
Delicious!! Great food from apps to dessert!! The spinach artichoke blue crab dip was amazing and shrimp and grits were too. Beautiful restaurant as well.
Decent  Japanese food at  over price manu. Service could be much better.

Tonight was our third night getting take out and the food was amazing as usual. We have tried at least 12 different rolls and they all were great. I also had an order of fatty tuna sashimi and it was excellent as well. Although we have not eaten in the restaurant it is very nice inside and the staff is very friendly. Highly recommended!

Every year, 
John Besh brings out the best of himself whenever he throws his Marine Corps Birthday on every November 10th. 
I would go to his restaurant when not going to every annual Marine Corps Birthday Bash and id still love the way the restaurant Luke, conducts business.

If I could give this restaurant 10 stars I totally would...we ordered the most amazing Brussels appetizer, which came out in a fun cast iron skillet. It was like an explosion of flavors I would have never put together! The Brussels were coated in almost a Thai honey and chili sauce lightly and then topped with almond slivers, jalapeño and green apple straws! Amazing! I had chicken with a fried potato, which when rated together tasted like I was having friend chicken and mashed potatoes...amazing! We aren't from New Orleans but when we asked for recommended restaurants to try on our vacation many friend recommended Luke, and now I know why! Go!
A fav for gumbo. If you haven't had it you'll be WOWED! Over dinner had a nice visit with an actor in town to film a movie. It's that kinda place.

Come for the happy hour!!
The half off cocktails and 75 cent oysters ($1.25 fried oysters) are so worth it. Luke is a large restaurant with ample seating, and on a Saturday night at 5PM was already quite bumpin. I made a reservation for three, and were seated near the back of the quite large restaurant.

The cocktails were excellent, especially being half off! I started with a gin based drink that I thoroughly enjoyed. My friends and I started with a dozen raw oysters to start and a half dozen fried. The oysters were large and fresh, and was the first time I tried oysters with no brine (personal preference is with some brine). However, the cocktail sauce, horseradish, and lemon provided plenty of additional flavor. 
I enjoyed my fried oyster quite a bit as well. They don't skimp on the oysters and mine was large and meaty with an excellent crisp.

We didn't stay for a full meal, but had a great time at happy hour and would highly recommend the experience!
Fantastic oxtail pasta! Good helpful service. Split check on large table with no problems but my husband never received his side salad.

I really wanted to dine at one of John Besh's (James Beard Foundation Award for Best Chef- Southeast in 2006) restaurants and decided on Luke. It was mostly due to their happy hour- 75 cent raw oysters and $1.50 fried oysters. Great deal for great oysters. 

The pate of Louisiana rabbit & chicken livers came with country bread croutons and accompaniments. It didn't look like much, but there was a lot of pate in the jar. The seafood gumbo a la creole was also excellent. I'm glad I chose this place to end my trip in New Orleans.
Never use.  This place is a rip off.  They charged me $250 to come to my house and do nothing.  I was under the impression that the service was going to be $250.  NEVER USE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

AMAZING spot. It takes a lot for me to rate a spot five stars, so believe me on this one. The ambiance was impeccable and made it feel like I was in Europe. With the staff in their uniform, it was a great atmosphere and did not feel like New Orleans. Service was phenomenal and they were just the right amount of attentive. I came for lunch, which was great, but I can see this place being amazing for dinner as well. 

The A.B.V. was hands down one of the best cocktails I've ever had. I'm a whiskey sour kind of guy and this cocktail embodies that essence with a twist. The vanilla in it really brought it together too. The crab appetizer was amazing. The cheese was the perfect amount and the crab was good quality. The pork schnitzel was great too and was a hefty portion for what it was priced at. The mushroom sauce it came with made the dish, so definitely ask for more if you order it. Overall, an amazing restaurant and if I'm ever back in New Orleans, this will be the first spot I visit.

A good friend in the know recommended this spot and I actually ended up eating here twice during Jazz feast because if was walking distance from the French quarter and walk-ins actually were seated quickly. This spot is mix of local and tourist and offers daily specials as well as time-tested classics. In my instance, the court-bouillon is a mix of both, being available only on Fridays and being an original menu item. Definitely get it if you can; the seafood inside, including oysters, shrimp and fish are drenched perfectly and well balanced seafood broth with rice. Perfect. On the apps side, 100% get the buttermilk fried quail. I'd say this is better than the chicken biscuit main. The LA rabbit&chicken livers pate looks great too. And the flammenkuchen should cure just about any hangover when paired with a bloody Mary.
When I'm in New Orleans again, I'l definitely stop back.

Came here with a group of friends for a bachelor party, and this place did not disappoint. Our servers were friendly and upon hearing about our celebration, came back with shot glasses of Jameson to kick off the night. We started with the fresh oysters, and the pâté. Both Amazing starters. We followed it with the P&J oysters, etouffe and shrimp and grits. The Etouffe was such a unique dish that featured crispy rice and crawfish. Combined with the buttery and cheesy grits, it was the perfect entree to experience high end southern food. There wasn't a bad dish in the house and everyone absolutely loves their dinner. Everything is also priced very well. This is a must visit next time we are back in NoLa

Chan's fills a huge void in the Philly food scene: good, halal Chinese takeout. And that's why I gave them four stars. The food was delicious. I tried the General Tso's Chicken, Chicken Fried Rice and Shrimp Rolls. They all tasted freshly prepared. The shrimp rolls were crispy with a nice, peppery filling. The fried rice was also well seasoned and didn't need any additional soy sauce. The General Tso's had large chunks of white meat with a nice mildly spicy sauce. I'd order them all again. 

Now, the bad. Having recently opened, Chan's is going through some growing pains. I had to call four times to place my takeout order. Once, someone answered, told me to hold, then hung up. When I got through, placing a relatively simple order took minutes, lots of repetition, and there was still a mistake (I asked/paid for large, they gave me small). Also, the ETA to pick up my order was 45min on a weekday. 

Again, the food was great but the customer service needs some work. I'd recommend them as long as you're not in a hurry. I'm hoping I'll be able to update my review in a few months once they work out the issues.
Great food, excellent ambiance. Even better service. They are all taking this very seriously

This was an amazing place to go for a birthday dinner!!

Our server was amazing and the food was so good!!

We split a few things and went away satisfied and happy. 

The bread pudding was highly recommended so I tried it. Pretty good. 

But not nearly as good as the shrimp and grits!!!!


Our favorite item was the pâté!!! 
I'd eat that every day if I could. 


Would highly recommend and we are considering going again while we are here for only 2 days. 


The drinks were good as they need to be for NOLA. 

Everything was nice. 

There were even secondary waitstaff to make sure no one got left without anything they needed. 

Don't be dissuaded because it's at the Hilton. 

The place is charming and tasty and kind. 


Will go again for sure!

First, when you walk into the restaurant you immediately are welcomed with brasserie style environs, personable staff, seafood towers the likes you'd see in NYC and Paris bistros and brasseries.... Nice.  It's lively at Luke, the music for rhythm junkies.  I was at home.   I like the wood panels too.  It's a place i would want to have a few draft beers,  Kir Royale and seafood.  Walked in early around happy hour and we took advantage of the oysters special. At 1268 reviews and counting, this place is deelish. First,  I had a dozen. Sounds like a lot but there were mongers eating 2 dozen at a time.  The raw oysters were cold, the liquor crisp, clean tasting with a slight briny edge that confirmed they are fresh and shucked seconds ago.  

Then the shrimp and grits arrived. The description mentioned, jumbo shrimp and grits.  I wanted to try this dish here because it's been hailed as one of the best plates to try.  I sampled the grits, bold cheesy slightly rich yet simply put together, nice.  I got into the shrimp -- they were not jumbo, unless jumbo in gulf waters is medium sized in my book.  I found the shrimp to be fresh meaty good.  Then a powerful Cajun salty attack took over my palate.  I don't mind spice as I appreciate Cajun food but the salt was many dimensions above salty.  I sent it back.  I picked more oysters this time, since we seemed to have more luck with them.  There was a wait for fresh oysters at this time and we were treated to fried oysters on the house--  delicious,crunchy with a nice sauce for dipping.   That was very nice of them to do that.  In the meantime, my second course, the roasted beets salad with spinach and crunchy spiced/toasted pistachios came.  It was a bit oily, the golden beets were fresh and delicious, slightly to the tooth.   I  was OK with the dish until I crunched into one of the spiced pistachios and that too, was super salty. I couldn't help but think that the cooks at this restaurant smoke heavily as this is what I've experienced in cities like Paris or Rome, where smoking is common and chefs who smoke  are a bit heavy on the Na-CL.  Less 2 stars for the overwhelmingly salty food.

Was only able to take one foto too much fun drinking with friends over wine and cocktails. It was really fun here that I forgot about the food.  But, a reminder to Mr. Besh, please test your food.  

Tip:  As mentioned the oysters during happy hour at half price are freshly shucked scrummy.   I had 2 dozen at 50c a piece

Visits: 1
Great food! Our dinner was fresh and delicious. We had combination hot and sour soup, wanton soup, fried rice, Mongolian Beef, and hon y chicken. Everything very tasty.

I actually really love cosi. Ive tried their roasted veggie and hummus sandwich and was super surprised at the great taste! Their tomato basil soup is what brings me back every time. Its filling and only 5 dollars. As a college student with negative money this is super appealing to me. I think they get your food out super fast and its a cozy lil place.

So we have tried this place a few years back thru some friends ordering it for a party and no one was impressed with it at that time. We decided to give it another try this weekend and it wasn't too half bad. I don't think it would be the first place I would order again but it's the closest to the house. I ordered the Singapore mei fun and it was plain. No spices, no flavors, just mei fun noodles boiled in water the meats and veggies added with no seasoning or flavor. My beautiful wife had the orange chicken and it was tasty but it could have been sesame chicken or General tsos chicken or any other chicken served in a sweet brown sauce. Nothing set it apart as being an orange chicken. Crab rank goons that were just scallions and cream cheese. If there was crab in them they were invisible. Just nothing stood out from the rest of the Chinese take out joints in the area.

Happy hour is everyday from 3-6 and it's the BEST happy hour in town thus far.  You must get started with a couple dozens of the oysters because they are super fresh and delicious! The charcuterie/pate plate was divine and another must have. The foie gras on this plate was exceptional as well as the pork belly and the pate campagne.  

I ordered the shrimp and grits as my entree and it was really good, but I was told from an insider that next time I should add jumbo lump crabmeat and slow poached eggs. Mmm I can't wait until I come here again to try it! 

I'm definitely a huge fan of all Besh's restaurants!!

My girl friends & I came here for brunch & I must say: EVERYTHING IS ON POINT.
- The Nutella stuffed French toast was crispy, crunchy, lightly sweetened w/ Nutella & on a bed of fresh whipped cream.
- The brussel sprouts were lightly crisped, sweetened & delicious.
- The flambé was amazing w/ the melted cheese, large chunks of bacon & caramelized onions.
- Wow, the crab omelette had huge pieces of crab meat. It also had nice chunks of tomatoes & stalks of asparagus. And the vinaigrette on the salad was lightly sweet, adding a nice touch to the greens.
- I think I went to heaven when I ate the bread pudding... Vanilla ice cream on a bed of soft warm cup of bread pudding, yum yum yum. Soft, fluffy & lightly crunchy exterior topped w/ candied pecans. YES!

The service and food was so amazing, we ended up coming back for happy hour. Yes we did & boy, it was so worth it for those fat oysters & cheap drinks!

A must when you're in NoLa! Make reservations for brunch. So. Worth. It!

Ok, I know giving this place five stars is not shocking since it's the hottest restaurant in town. And I generally avoid the "hot spots" due to long waits even with a reservation, but our hotel concierge basically insisted on getting us a table there, so I caved.  And, wow, it really lived up to its billing! So great. 

We started with the baked oysters which are crazy delicious. Only six oysters and priced at $19, but trust me, it's worth it. I don't particularly even like oysters but these things will blow your mind. Sorry to be so dramatic but they are that good. 

I then moved on to the grilled chicken and you'd think "chicken is chicken" but not at this place. Seasoned and cooked to perfection. Very awesome. 

Great staff too, very attentive and personable. 

If in Nola, definitely go to Lukes! (Order the oysters..)

They are not as clean as I would like them to be. I had to ask the nail tech to rewash the metal nail scrubber because there was still dead skin from the previous client. She did, but then her hair was stuck in her gloves so I had to make her aware of that. Other than that, my experience here was okay. Her massages made up for the mistakes that were made. I shall return.

I enjoyed this restaurant. We came here during one of our many trips to New Orleans. We were recommended to visit this establishment by the staff at Hotel Monteleone, which is our favorite place to stay in the city. We tried a few dishes. I didn't take photos of all of them but the Brussels, oysters and cocktail shrimp were  delicious. My husband ordered some type of pasta that was very tasty as well. It is pricey to dine here but worth it. This is not your typical creole cuisine that you get in New Orleans either. Although they offer creole staples the menu has a spin on it. But it's  definitely worth the visit! Whoever the chef is here, is very creative! I will definitely come back. The staff was also very kind to us and accommodating to my infant .

Went in for a lunch. Good Bloody Mary (Tito and tony) - I was able to customize my burger and replace the patty with grilled chicken which was great. My son had a BLTAE - excellent- duck bacon, lettuce, tomato, avocado and egg. Looked beautiful and tasted great

We really enjoyed Luke. The food was fresh and very flavorful. The staff was friendly and helpful. We had a lovely dinner - it was really nice. I would go back and highly recommend. Make a reservation - you can via opentable which is helpful. 

One last note - I appreciate that the televisions were somewhat hidden so we talked and enjoyed each others company at dinner without television distraction. Well done.

We decided to have dinner here tonight due to convenience. Boy were we surprised! I had the Luke bacon burger and fries. Best burger I have ever had! The hubby had shrimp and grits, it was delicious! So creamy and cheesy! Our lil girl had chicken tenders with fries. Best dinner ever! Definitely recommend this place

This location is decent.  Not the most consistent with how they make things, sometimes I get tons of chicken in my salad or on my sandwich, sometimes it is less.  Sometimes I get the perfect amount of dressing on my salad or sauce on my sandwich, sometimes I don't. But all in all, the quality of food is good and they definitely hit the spot when I crave something that Cosi has on their menu.

All in all, the University City location is clean and does the trick.  The staff is always very friendly, and the food is always good (standard since it's a chain).

You can also do S'mores here where they provide a iron burner for roasting marshmallows, marshmallows, chocolate, and graham crackers.  Its fun and yummy!
  
Lines can be long, but if you time it right, you won't hit the lunch rush.  My favorite thing on their menu was their Chicken Cesar Sandwich.  No longer on the menu, but the staff here is always willing to make it for me anyway! They also have good coffee, the bread is always fresh and delicious. Lots of seating upstairs, some down in the main area, and a bunch of outside seating when it is nice enough out to eat outside. For a quick meal to grab when you are in the area, its a good place to come!
If you're in the CBD, I'd recommend going here for their oyster happy hour - otherwise, pass.

A great happy hour! 1/2 drinks, cheap oysters. The fried oysters were fantastic! I also enjoyed the Luke's salad. I will definitely come back on my next trip to NOLA. Service was very attentive. We also had lunch and  didn't have much time. We ordered the express lunch option and our server made sure we were out on time.

Guys, if you haven't been here, you don't know what your missing. No bragging, no flaking, I've been eating sushi around the globe...this place is no joke...one of the very best. We've enjoyed the daily specials, as well as some stables such as filet carpaccio, fresh oysters/scallops and even the sushi pizza. Go. Enjoy. Thank me later.
Slid in for a quick snack before dinner. Had the best oysters, soft shell crab sandwich, crawfish and gumbo.

My party was excited to try out Luke.  We had reservations and were seated immediately.  Luke had this older feel to it. White linen with wooden decor.

To start we had the BBQ P&J Oysters.  They were fine.  My plus one liked this dish because of the bread crumbs and parmesan, which is why we got fresh oysters too.   The fresh ones had a good salty flavor, but I've had fresher and sweeter.  

I did like the pate dish.  Spread that pate on long pieces of toasted bread with pickled cucumbers and watermelon rind.  Mustards as a condiments.   

We also got a bowl of gumbo a la Creole.  Gumbo was OK.  I wasn't my favorite dish.  Every part of the dish was not impressive.  Rice was fine and the included meat was not great.

My favorite was the bacon Luke uses.  We got a small side of it.  Delicious!
Higher end cost but you get what you pay for! If you're looking for a more formal dinning experience this is the place. Cuisine is the creole you're looking for and the quality is equally matched.

Spectacular! My husband and I had lunch at Luke for our honeymoon and the entire staff was amazing. They treated us with champagne AND dessert, which was completely unexpected. The pate appetizer was the best my husband and I have ever had (including in Paris and other parts of France!) Our waiter (I believe his name was Jesse) was phenomenal! There is not a single thing I would change about our experience at Luke. All of the food, drinks and staff were so wonderful. I highly recommend that you visit if you are in New Orleans.

I can't wait to come back here. They have an amazing happy hour, lovely service topped only by their amazing oysters (excellent raw and fried). We also loved the cocktails... The French 75 was strong and delicious, the Dr. Orders was an amazing Fanta-like boozy drink, and the ABV was excellent as well.

Absolutely loved our first trip up to Hachi! I wanted to try somewhere new for my birthday dinner and though it felt sacrilege to not go to our favorite sushi restaurant close to home, I'm surprised to say this place ties or potentially beats our old favorite!

Really nice atmosphere, music was a little loud... kind of like I was shopping in Express, but I stop noticing after a while. Decor is great too, you'd have no idea you were in a strip mall.

Menu is extensive and creative with lots of interesting flavor combinations. I wish I would of "prepped" and read the menu online before we went because I was a little over whelmed at first. We will have to come back again because there were way more things I wanted to try and my stomach is only so big.

We had some kind of lettuce wrap and a chicken meatball app which were both very good. The chicken meat balls were a little bit dry, but the flavor of the sauce was good enough to negate the dryness. The lettuce wrap appetizer was by far our favorite app. Just the right balance of spice and the freshness of the fish was so delicious.

We ordered the shiitake and fried shallot (?) roll, vegetable roll, No.07 Volcano, and Snow Mountain rolls. All were beautifully presented and wonderful flavors! We also ordered dessert, tempura bananas with ice cream... I think my fiancee would eat fried bananas everyday since having them. Very very good! The peanuts, mango, and honey on top were a really interesting and tasty combination.

I didn't anticipate writing this much, but if you made it to the end, congratulations. Hopefully my and other reviews will be persuasion enough to get yourself to Hachi. You won't regret it, unless you hate sushi.

Cosi isn't consistent. When I get a freshly made sandwich with bread just out of the oven and split, it tastes great, but once the bread cools completely, it can be cracker crisp, not pita soft. I don't understand what everyone's infatuation is with Cosi. Is it supposed to be healthy? Where you place your order is sometimes confusing. There are clearly signs that direct you to order from one of the sandwich makers, but sometimes they tell me to give my order to the cashier before I get my sandwich from them. When it gets busy during the day, it can be a madhouse in there.

I agree with wearing masks and limiting the number of people in the store - no problem. However we had a sales woman come over to us as my kids were trying on sandals and tell us that socks were required when trying on shoes and she needs to know which ones we touched so she could "quarantine them". I'm serious. In the adult section there were two women who were trying on sandals with no socks and had an employee helping them with sizes. If you are going to make up random Covid rules, like the virus spreads from your feet but we can touch all the clothes in the store with our hands - at least be consistent.

Is it a Yelp faux pas to give a restaurant five stars for one standout dish? I don't know, but the Shrimp and Jalapeno Cheese Grits at Luke are THAT good. Granted, we are from California and don't eat Shrimp and Grits often. But John Besh takes this dish to a whole new level. In fact, it's rendered me adjective-less. Heavenly? Blissful? Insane? Nothing does it justice. Just try it. Other dishes are also solid: Etouffee, Gumbo, Crab Bisque. Service is solid. Ambiance is a casual bistro style--no need to dress up. Tables are closely set together, but that's the charm of New Orleans. Everyone is so friendly--it's a perfect opportunity to strike up a conversation with someone you might not normally meet at home. :)

Ok, this really is the most pathetic REI in existence. Two weeks ago, I tried to buy a kayak from them. Nope, they don't carry kayaks (but you can order them on line). Pathetic, given all the kayaking possibilities in Idaho, but I got over it and bought one at Dick's. Today, I went back looking for kayaking accessories (bilge pump and sponge). Nope, they don't have any in store, only online. Also looked for travel clothing for a trip I have coming up. Nope, don't have any of that either (but you can order from REI online).  All they have is running and hiking stuff and a very limited selection of cycling accessories. Of course, this is the smallest REI I've ever seen. Smaller than any store in SoCal, Reno, SLC, Denver, Sacramento. Pathetic. They should close this store and point everyone online. In Boise, thank God for Sportsman's Warehouse, Dick's, Performance Bikes and Cabela's. This store sucks.

Just had a thoroughly enjoyable dinner with gf at Luke. We both had the wood smoked chicken and it was very good, not dry at all. And large half chicken portions. It came with potatoes and broccolini. All good. I substituted red beans and rice for the potatoes and could have made a meal of that. And we had a very pleasant bottle of Frech rose, reasonably priced. 

Service was excellent too. I can't recall the server's name but she moved to the city recently from Montana. We were too late for happy hour, so will need to return.
This is my go to! Happy hour is great here and the food and service is always great! Shoutout to Miguel the manager for always taking care of us!

If I could give zero stars I would. HVAC maintenance contract was a sham... parts were overpriced even after the so called contract "discount". Refused to honor last service after I questioned the overcharge. Kept on making appointments and then not turning up so I lost time from work. Finally one of the staff took pity and told me owner was playing with me!

Buyer Beware! Pinellas Auto Brokers sold me a lemon. I bought a vehicle a month ago from them for $5000. I've had the car for a month now and I have had to repair 3 tires, gaskets, oil leaks, coils, towing & more totaling over $2000. There is still more to be fixed but the last mechanic I took the vehicle to said that there was too much rust on the underneath that he was too scared to lift it in fear of the vehicle cracking in half. I called to see if there was anything they would do to rectify the situation, and was talked down to - told that I bought the car as is and there was nothing they would do about it. I feel I was treated poorly, and lied to by the information they failed to disclose. I would not recommend dealing with this company if you are looking for a vehicle. I took the vehicle to be appraised this week, one quote was for $695 and the other quote was for $900. Very dissatisfied with my overall experience for the money I've spent.
Love Love the food. Great service and always on time. Pork isn't allowed here. I try not to order every night, but it's hard !! Definitely A+.

The worst restaurant I have experienced in New Orleans. Made reservations for their Thanksgiving dinner (turducken is what they offered) but they ran out before 6:30. We ate salads and a couple of sides. Service was slow (like we were invisible) and rude. No second chances.

I love to shop at REI. They have things I want at generally reasonable prices, and great sale racks. But man, I can NOT get help in the bike shop at the one in Boise. I've been in there three times and hung around looking lost, to no avail. I've even stood at the service counter in that department and watched two employees have a conversation (in the back, but where they could see me) and was ignored for five minutes. I'll be heading to a real cycling store where they want to sell stuff to me.

Great sushi - questionable service. Overall i want to keep this review positive because this is phenomenal sushi to get in the suburbs, but multiple times ive had to wait 2+ hours for a pickup order that they quoted 45 mins for. A tip for management - use peoples names, not their phone numbers when they call in an order! A phone number is easy to mess up and takes a while to say, a name is simple! Come on! Thanks for staying open during COVID!

Absolutely the worst customer service ever. 4 paying customers come in at 10:20 and the woman at the hostess counter was rude and disrespectful. After asking if we have a reservation, she proceeded to tell us that it would be a 10 min wait for a table. SIDENOTE: There were several available tables in site.

A waiter and the hostess made contact and general glances in our direction at what which point he frowned and she rolled her eyes. 

We waited patiently as she stood at the podium a few more minutes before going and finding another woman to come back with her. They fiddled with the screen for a few minutes. Then we over hear them asking, "what time is it?", then looking over at us. 

Needless to say, we decided the best decision was the leave. Apparently Luke and John Besh do NOT need paying customers as it seems Leaving on time is the staff's top priority. 

Seems like a decent menu, too bad we were not allowed the opportunity to sample it. I will be sharing this experience with others.
Attached to the Hilton hotel and great food! The service was a little slower than expected but we were seated distanced from other parties and our waiter wore a mask.

I used to love Sonic Burgers. They were like the old fashion real beef grilled burgers. I probably won't have another one after tonight. I just got home and unwrapped the absolute worst burger I have ever eaten. The meat was hard, way over done, and very dry. I don't think they are even the same kind of burgers that Sonic used to sell. It definitely tasted like frozen meat substitute patties. The toppings were barely there and they were not fresh. I am really disappointed. There is so much on the menu that I guess it's quantity over quality. The service was fast and friendly. The restaurant area itself was clean.

Debating on 3 or 4 star review. I decided on 4 because the food was amazing! The crab dip and the mussels I got were FANTASTIC. I was very happy with my meal. The service, however, was lacking. Two things we ordered never never brought. The first was a soup we reminded them of before the entrees came out and didn't get until well after the entrees came out. The second was a mimosa that we ordered near the end of the meal. We never got the mimosa and no one checked on us so the next thing we got is our check, and we paid and left.

Again, the food was great. Maybe they were having an off night. I will try again in the future!

Open Monday thru Friday from 8 AM to 6 PM; Saturday from 9 AM till 2 PM; & Sunday from 11 AM to 5 PM, this veterinary office is LARGE! It has SEVEN DOCTORS on site & ITS SERVICES ARE EXTENSIVE. (I listed all offered services @ the bottom of this review.) On Google, Seven Oaks has 4 stars. 

I must have gone to a different place than the previous Yelpers because my three-yr-old cat has had nothing but EXCELLENT care. Dr. Pelletier (young female) was attentive and allowed me all the time I needed to ask questions before she explained everything thoroughly. PRICING WAS PROVIDED BEFORE ANY TREATMENT BEGAN. Dr. Pellerin phoned twice over the next few days to check on the status of my cat & later to provide the results of the blood panel-- so I'd finally learn why my Siberian Forest cat had been very sick w/ a virus for two months (a virus she picked up at another vet's office). A staffer phoned a third time to assure my feline was improving.

Each staff member I spoke w/ over the phone; at the sprawling front counter (see pic); and in the exam room (see pic) was very friendly & professional. Completed paperwork was handed to me after each visit. 

I did not award 5 stars ONLY due to pricing; prices are higher than what I am used to paying. This is a large veterinary hospital (by day) that offers EMERGENCY CARE AFTER 6 PM; its urgent care services are less expensive than Blue Pearl (a facility that I awarded one star). Seven Oaks operates the Hermoine Duncan Reddy nonprofit that ASSISTS CLIENTS w/ THE PAYMENT OF THEIR VET BILLS on a case-by-case basis. And due to Covid, Seven Oaks is currently offering free delivery of Rx's & Medical Food within a seven mile radius via its mobile service. (Also due to  Covid, virtual consultations are offered, but are not free.)

Attached to the hospital is a large pet store-- see Pet Depot. The entrance to the vet hospital is conveniently through the pet store:) It's a scaled down version of a PetSmart. 

The hospital was clean, modern, & offered multiple services. I spent approx $850 here before the cost of antibiotics ($32 × 2); however, my cat received fast & professional care when five other veterinary offices could not see her for two weeks unless I wanted to take a day off from my employment. (Those five include the office that introduced her to the Macroplasm virus). The extended hours this establishment offers are definitely a plus.

Don't forget to use the YELP CHECK-IN OFFER that offers a free trim-- I'm guessing one must have a dog. Perhaps $10 off an initial exam would be a more inclusive offer the owners might want to consider. 

Should you need to get your pet seen by a vet quickly, this is DEFINITELY the place to phone. My 'Mae' is close to being whole; I didn't have to take time off from my job for veterinary care; & ALL CONTACT w/ this business has been 100% PROFESSIONAL. I will likely return to see Dr. Pellerin or one of the six other doctors on staff here the next time one of my cats is ill. Missing work is not an option for me, so I am OK w/ paying more. Thank you, Dr. Pellerin & staff! 

THE SERVICES OFFERED (in alphabetical order): Acupuncture, Anti-Venom Service, Behavior Medicine, Boarding ($27 Cats, $22 Exotics, $30 to $46 Dogs) Cold Laser, Dental Care, Emergency & Critical Care, Exotics, Grooming, Holistic Medicine, Hospice & Euthanasia, Laparoscopic Procedures, Mobile Services, Pain Management, Parasite Prevention, Puppy & Kitten Care, Rabbits & Small Mammals, Radiology, Senior Care, Surgery, Ultrasound, Vaccines, & Wellness Exams.

I'm usually very skeptical about restaurants that are attached to hotels, so I was unsure about how I would like Luke, but I LOVED it. About a 10 minute walk from our hotel on Canal street, I found it to be in a relatively convenient location. My friend and I stepped in on a Wednesday evening and were able to get seated immediately. The restaurant was clean, and for being an oyster bar it thankfully did not smell very fishy! Additionally, the atmosphere is very intimate and the service was wonderful. Though the menu is small, my friend and I both found dishes we'd enjoy. We had the Pork Schnitzel and LOVED it. The pork was perfectly cooked, the jus that is served with it was excellent, and the French fries were delicious. Did not have room for dessert. I would definitely come back here if I find myself in NOLA again!

I loved the atmosphere of this restaurant. The staff were all very kind and helpful as well. Service was great and all were very attentive. I ordered the crawfish etouffee. It was my first time having it and I have to say I am hooked. It was so delicious. I will definitely return

Hands down one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans. My friends and I liked it so much we even went twice! Each time we went, I made sure to order the stuffed oysters, brussel sprouts and shrimp and grits. The stuffed oysters were perfectly cooked with a shrimp, crab and cheese topping. But my absolute favorite dish was the brussel sprouts - I don't even like brussel sprouts this much but I thought these were out of this world. 

I thought the menu had a good variety of food. We came around 10:30am so we were able to order off the breakfast and lunch menu. The service was also great and really accommodating of medium sized parties. If you're ever in the area, I would definitely recommend checking this place out!!

Yummy. Simple. Close to my hotel and beaming with fresh oysters and a solid bar menu. The space is big and is connected to the hotel - I mention this because after our table's order of oysters on the half shell, I went to wash my hands; unfortunately, there were no paper towels. I mentioned this to a member of the waitstaff - who apologized but told me, "...the bathrooms belong to the hotel, that's not us." I left it with that and didn't follow-up, fishy hands and all. 
Yeah, that disappointed me with what was otherwise, a good meal, moderate price point and convenient. #NOLA #Luke #NewOrleans

My friends and I decided to treat ourselves during a recent trip to NOLA.


I had the express meal which is basically prix fix.  I started with a yummy crawfish bisque, followed by a delicious out of this world seafood stew. My Jesus! So rich and meaty with little rice, hey! Great portions. I finished with delicious bread pudding.  I was amazed by the generous portion.  There was enough for me to have several bites, for my good friend to taste  and for my boyfriend to thoroughly enjoy. 

My boyfriend had the steak. My goodness!!!  It was served on a wooden chopping block with compound butter and a side of fries. The steak was huge and succulent. I had a bite and mmm! Right up my boyfriend's alley!  The fries were a tasty accompaniment.

My friend also had the express meal.  She was thoroughly pleased.  We both savored each bite of our express meal, especially the stew.  

Our one complaint: service simply was not what we are accustomed to. We weren't sure if we were being ignored or that's just how things were. We were not served any bread, though other tables were.  We were left wondering if it was because we didn't order alcohol?  I prefer to eat my money rather than drink it, unless I'm at a bar of course...

Either way, I do recommend Luke.  The food is delicious.

All in all, I left full ad satisfied. My meal lasted me all te way until mid day brunch the next day. Even through my morning wokoit. Nice. !

Front of the house was very polite but I was already hungry so I think I seemed rude to ignore the greeting in order to give them my reservation information.  We sat next to table that just kept growing with diners.

Great gumbo.  I preferred the plat lyonnaise over the etouffee.  I went here for dinner and loved having a paper to read.  The waiter was very helpful about recommendations.  I think you can do better than the vanilla cake with creme fraiche for dessert though.
Straight forward, great job.  In and out in 15 minutes with no up-sells.  Honest maintenance is in short supply but I feel these guys were refreshingly honest.  I recommend it!

best meal we had in New Orleans by far. everything was superb.

made reservation for a party of 6 and was seated promptly. restaurant shared the same building as Hilton Hotel. very clean and neat.

we did family style and ordered a bunch of stuff
- 1 dozen of P&J oysters
- half dozen of Jumbo Shrimp
- half dozen of Peruvian scallop
- crispy brussels sprouts
- fried oysters
- Oxtail ragout pasta
- Moules et Frites

oh boy, i don't know where to start, because everything was that great. service was excellent too. ordered a few drinks and we enjoyed the drinks as well.

will i come back? 6 yesses from our party.
5 STARS FOR HAPPY HOUR PRICED RAW OYSTERS!! This was my absolute favorite place with the best oyster happy hour in nola! Will be back next time I visit =)

It was our first time here (4 of us) our waitress was so rude and ignorant talking to us like we were stupid. I have to be honest the food was great. We all enjoyed our meals. If the service was as good as the meal I would have given 5 stars. Unfortunately we will not be returning.
I had to hit up another OYSTER happy hour deal in between meals.  The P&J oysters (normally $2/each) were $0.75 during HH.  A great snack if you're having a late dinner.

Hands down some of the best sushi I have had in a very long time. When it comes to Bucks County, there is no place that's even comparable or in the same class. I'm upset I didn't find this place until a friend of mine introduced me to Hachi recently. Thankfully it's right up the street from my place but I would have no problem driving far away to get my hands on their food. Thank you guys for being so awesome! If I could give you more than 5 stars, I would!

This place offered up the perfect bistro-style brunch.  I had the best Croque Madame I've ever had- thick cut bread, piles of delicious smoked ham, Swiss cheese, béchamel sauce and perfectly fried egg.  The side fries were hot, soft on the inside and crispy out.   My daughter got the southern breakfast and loved every bite.  Side of potato hash was delicious (very crispy!). 
The service was prompt, knowledgeable, and friendly.  I heard the waiter tell another table they were under-staffed, but I wouldn't have known.  I recommend this place!

Love this location and staff! We have pizza at least once every two weeks! It's always ready within 10 minutes and they always are sure to give us the specials. Typically to do accept military discount. They will adjust your order if your paying more so that you get the optimal use of coupons/specials. That matters to us! Parking is located in the back you can enter from the townhall side or the police side. The food is always hot even when we get home! As always we will be back!

I will say the service and oysters were excellent so that is why I did not give it one star; HOWEVER, it says ON THEIR WEBSITE and the staff member that we called ahead that day to make reservations with TOLD US that Luke's happy hour special $.75 an oyster still applied from 3-6pm daily. We made the effort to call ahead to double check since they opened back up after the quarantine before we came all the way out there to eat. I went with a group of 4 people and we ordered 7 dozen oysters to split with some drinks, and the waiter says NOTHING about them changing the happy hour from everyday to just Monday thru Friday... so we get the bill and our mouths dropped. The bill is $120 over what it would have been for happy hour!!!! The waiter gets his manager who ONLY takes off $60 from our bill which still is $60 more than what it should have been. Somebody should have told us this difference before we ordered 7 dozen oysters....

We went to Luke on a recommendation from friends, and I will no longer be asking those friends where to eat. They should call this place, "luke" warm, because it was an all around disappointment - from the service to the food. We went for brunch and it wasn't very busy when we arrived. Both hostesses asked if we had a reservation, which we didn't, but there were plenty of open seats. We were seated and waited at least 5 minutes to be greeted (mind you, there were a total of 4 parties, all less than 4 in the house). We were greeted by the busser, who later brought us water. We then waited another 5 minutes for our server. We ordered coffee and our meals, and waited another few minutes for our cold coffee to arrive. I ordered the buttermilk biscuits and the shrimp and grits, my hubs got 1/2 dozen oysters, and the croque madame. The biscuits were super disappointing. They arrived cold. (Insert shocked, sad, and disappointed face.) What good is pecan butter, if it doesn't melt when you put it on your biscuit?!?! I also asked for the strawberry preserves. Instead, lemon curd was brought to the table, it was not great all. It tasted like an ingredient, not a biscuit accoutrement. The server did eventually bring the strawberry preserves; they were good, but again, not really interested in any cold biscuit no matter what gets smeared on it. My husband said his oysters were decent. His sandwich came with fries, of course no ketchup was brought to the table. The sandwich was very average and warm but not hot. The sauce on top actually was very thick and seemed like more flour than anything else. The shrimp and grits had a lot of flavor, but again the meal was "luke" warm when it arrived at the table and it contained 4 medium-sized shrimp, and an extra tail with no shrimp attached, and a shit ton of sausage. It was flavorful, but the sauce to grits ratio was way off and again, why was it not hot?!? The meal was one of the more expensive we had for breakfast in the city, and I wish we had passed and will not recommend to others.

This was one of my top meals in NOLA. 

There is a daily happy hour from 3-6 with 75 cent oysters (warning they are large oysters if you prefer small ones)! They have a great French 75 as well! A group of us of 8 went for dinner so we tried a large variety of items. 

The seafood tower was spendy but was so much food. Honestly, we could have been happy with that and not order anything else.

Highlights of the meal were the duck duck rice with crispy rice - the crunch and flavors were spot on and jumbo Louisiana Shrimp en cocotte which was rich in flavor so best to get this and a something on the lighter side. The service was great - they were patient with us as we continued to order many drinks! This is the place to go for a nicer meal in NOLA!

By far my favorite meal in NOLA. Received a lot of recommendations to come here, so my group dashed here as soon as we arrived! 

Luckily we made reservations and caught happy hour. P&J oysters were going for $1 each and drinks were 50% off! The oysters are easily one of the top 3 oysters I've ever had in my life. They were huge and creamy and super fresh tasting. All the cocktails we ordered were really good and enjoyable! 

As for the entrees, we ordered the crawfish etouffee, shrimp and grits, soft shell crab and mussels. The crawfish etouffee is a must get. That was by far the best dish I've had in Nola. There was a generous amount of crawfish in every bite and the burst of flavor was absolutely delightful. Shrimp. + grits were good and cheesy! There was also an abundance of shrimp in it. Soft shell crab was also a solid choice. There was a hefty amount of crab. Could've done without the mussels though to be honest. 

Service was also good. They were quick and attentive! All in all, I highly recommend this spot. It's the one restaurant I definitely would've gone again in Nola.
Good option for those staying nearby. Apparently it also attracts locals too as our table neighbors were going on and on about the place. Oysters were fresh. Burger was good. Bread pudding was yummy.

The quality of the fish wasnt too good but the plating and ambiance was nice. This is byob and they do provide you with glasses and ice bucket. Sushi dinner was just okay but I really liked the ginger dressing on the salad that came with the entree. The seafood udon soup was disappointing because all the seafood looked old and bad. I didnt wanna risk getting sick. They also do charge you for side of sauces.

Be aware i had a broken heater so i call them to get it done ... The guy walk into my house dint even troubleshot my heater it dint even broad tools and the only thing he said was that i needed to buy a new heater and he gave me a quote for one and it was 7,000$ i end up paying 100$ for his trip .... Best way to lose 100$ .. I end up calling another guy from a smaller company and found out that it was a bad sensor ... Be aware of scammers like this people !!! Rob will rip u off !!

I'm so torn on this. 

First the food is very, very good.  The portions are kind of small for the price, but the food is very, very good. 

I went to get take out today, and they forgot part of my order.  So, I would normally let them know, but I wasn't treated well.  

The person up front asked me twice if I had a reservation, and I said "oh no, I have a to go order." There were two groups behind me.  The first group behind me looked more expensively dressed, and said "we don't have a reservation."  The person up front said "that's fine, we just ask it of certain people."  Anyways, I'm torn.  

Food is really good. 

Its overpriced for the portions on most items. 

The employees - not so kind.  I do get it - more people are out now, and I know restaurants are saying its hard to find people to hire, but I don't know.  I might delete this later.  

Thank you for listening.
