Went to Luke's with a large party and I understand that 10 people is a lot but I've had much better service with large groups at other places.  It was also a Sunday brunch so they were very busy. The hostess took 20 minutes to seat us when we had a reservation. They couldn't properly split the bill, we even split in to 3 separate groups to hopefully make it more manageable but everyone had each others orders on other bills. There were up-charges on substitutions with out being mentioned when ordering. The martinis were beyond overpriced. 
Overall, it was a very underwhelming experience for mediocre food at best. Very disappointed. Hopefully in smaller groups the experience may be better.

Came here around 9:30pm on a Tuesday night and got seated right away. We got the oysters, jambalaya, and swordfish entree. Being that the restaurant wasn't too busy at this hour, everything came out very quickly. The two servers for our table were extremely attentive and friendly; they seemed genuinely interested on how we enjoyed the dishes.

I'm not huge on raw oysters just due to the sliminess and texture, but I honestly really really liked the P&J oysters here. For those in the area during the day they have a happy hour for $.75 oysters from 3-6pm. 

Regarding the main swordfish dish - it was easily the best I've had. I've only had swordfish a handful of other times, but it was always too dry for me. The Tasso rubbed grilled swordfish here, however, was seriously cooked to perfection. It also sat on a puréed corn/ polenta kind of sauce, which was really bomb. The spicy peppers also complemented the dish very well. Personally I would've liked if the swordfish had more of a salt crust, but that's just nitpicking. Overall really enjoyed all of the food and experience at Luke's.

Had to make reservations 2-3 days ahead of time! 

It seems like this place is a well known, fancy spot. We showed up in leggings and hoodies.

Happy hour was half price wine/cocktails which was awesome! 

BRUSSELS SPROUTS!! GET THEM!! WE GOT THREE for our party of 4..lol 

I also got one of the salads and it was weird and not that good. Don't get it. 

Our service was really weird, he was just really casual with us and kinda grabbed plates in the middle of convos and stuff like that. Odd for a place that is fancy. 

You should go during happy hour (until 6pm) and get brussell sprouts + cocktails + wine :D

One of the John Besh top rated. Get there during happy hour and you will truly be happy. Huge fresh oysters 50 cents each. Yes I said 50 cents like in two dozen for $12. Nothing goes better with ice cold fresh oysters than half price cocktails. Beet salad was raised two levels with a healthy sprinkling of spiced pistachios. Duck breast for a main course is a "can't go wrong" choice. Not sure if you wouldn't rather have mussels? Order both and split the mussels and duck with your dinner mate. Better than I expected from a TV celebrity chef.

Don't order the chicken or Sunday veal. Everything is just thrown and mushed together in a skillet. You can't enjoy the dish's components, and the presentation was very sloppy. The foie gras was given with over buttered, over crisped toast. The wax paper was completely translucent, and you couldn't enjoy the richness of the foie gras. Very Disappointed.

I was staying at the hotel where this restaurant is located. I stopped in twice during my stay. The first night was for a quick sweet treat and nightcap. I ordered a glass of sparkling wine and order their modern take on a lemon meringue. Both were outstanding. The bartenders recommended this dessert, while I was leaning towards the bread pudding. They did not steer me wrong. My second visit was during happy hour. They have raw an fried oysters on special. I ordered a half dozen of each. Loved the mildness of the P&J raw oysters. The fried ones were outstanding. Different bartenders, but both times they were delightful. I did find out they are part of the same restaurant group as Borgne (which I love) and August (very upscale). The only downside is it can get very loud in there it's small, tight space. They do have seating across the hall, but the main space can get quite loud.

Amazing raw oysters!!! Happy hour is amazing! Not only the oysters are a dollar each, they are fresh and delicious! Fried oysters were just okay. Great service and atmosphere!  Also love the Brussels sprouts!

The wife and I enjoyed our meals very much.
I opted for theSpicy Tuna Roll and the Hachi sushi.
My better half ordered the shrimp pad Thai.
Both meals were perfect. You couldn't ask for fresher. This was our first visit, and I'm sure we will be returning many times.

I loved that crab dip so much! I can't even explain how amazing that fried chicken sandwich was. It was so juicy and crispy. This sandwich, crab dip, and oysters are definitely a must. The flavor of the sandwich was so delicious.. I'm missing my Luke lunch more and more typing this!

If you want to eat at one of John Besh's restaurants while visiting New Orleans I recommend Dominica over Luke. Luke was good, but Dominica was fabulous.  Luke isn't as fancy, but it's just as expensive and the portions are small. I mistakenly came here for my birthday dinner, should have done it the other way around. The restaurant has a really casual atmosphere and it wasn't all that busy on a weekend night.  I ordered the shrimp and grits and it was really tasty with thicker grits then usual, but at $20+ I felt that it was overpriced for the portion size. There were maybe a few big spoonfuls of grits and 4 or 5 shrimp. I'm a small person and easily finished the plate. For desert I got the pear tart and it was OK, nothing special. Our server was very friendly, but it seemed a little fake. Sorry John Besh I wasn't blown away.

Fried oyster salad was mediocre considering the hype; could barely taste the oysters once fried. Good value for the pâté, intriguing taste and paired well with provided toppings. Although the bread was burnt and had to be sent back; wait staff was professional and receptive.

Got takeout and we were all blown away. Never did I think the suburbs would have such amazing sushi. Ordering was easy and so was pick up. An amazing menu full of options for everyone but the fish is really where it's at. So fresh and silky wow. This is my go to sushi spot even though it's the furthest from me!
Amazing service from Keith this morning. I know nothing about cars but he walked me through each charge. Friendly, quick service and best service experience I've had thus far.

THE BEST in NOLA!! 

After our horrible experience with our server yesterday at Trenasse across the street, we did not have high expectations. However, we were pleasantly surprised. We showed up at 5pm (without making reservations) and were seated right away.

Our servers Eldwin and Jesse were both amazing in terms of providing service! They introduced themselves as soon as we were seated and drinks brought to the table within 3 minutes. There was never a time we had to look for either one of them to add on items to our order. They, along with other servers seemed to master the art of multitasking with smiles on their faces. Bravo!! Real pros deserve the biggest tips.

Skip the over-rated reviews for places in the French quarter, and come here. I promise you won't be disappointed! 

Wished we went here sooner... but glad we tried it before leaving for home tomorrow.

Great japanese cuisine. Our group has gotten a variety of items there (sushi, vegetarian sushi, hibachi dinner) all as take out, and it is always quite good. Many dinners have a tasty miso soup and salad with ginger dressing, so it's a good deal. We always get take out and their packaging is solid, even for very big orders. Definitely one of our favorite places for Asian cuisine nights.

Hands down my favorite and best sushi place in the area. You don't expect the suburbs to have a quality and place like this. 

Hachi SLAPS!!!! I will gladly drive 20 minutes to get this sushi every other week.
Best burger in New Orleans!!! The staff was amazing and the wait time wasn't as bad as other places.

Seriously, this place was so good we came twice during our 5 day trip to NOLA, yes it was THAT good!!! We were able to experience both breakfast and lunch and they were great.

The shrimp and cheesy grits here are AMAZING!!! They are suuuuuuuper cheesy, the sausage is tasty with a little kick - oh man it was so good I ordered it both times! We enjoyed the oysters, the crab claws, the crab omelette and I can't remember what else. But everything we ate was delicious and the service was on point.  

I highly recommend making this a stop on your stay.

Terrible customer service. They do not care about you or your pet. The first time I went there, I had a late afternoon appointment. I had to wait 40 minutes before the vet came in. No apologies from anyone. I had an early morning appointment today at 9:00 am. While booking the appointment, I had asked for the earliest available, after the bad experience the first time. The tech. took me back in the room, and 25 minutes later, I was still waiting. My dog was crying to get out of the room. The room was hot, and no one came to check on me and my dog. I finally couldn't take it anymore. There were a bunch of people, I guess techs, by the front desk, talking, and walking around. No one even noticed me, when I opened the door of the room they put us in. No one cared. I went over to the young woman at the front desk, and told her I had something to do. I had to leave. She didn't even look at me or make eye contact. All she said is that she would let them know. I will never come back here again. It's obvious they don't care about your pet, only your money.

I had a visit to Luke twice in 3 days for the oxtail ragú. Our friends flew in from Miami as we told them how awesome the meal was just to have it. It's a complete must have with the black truffle, chunks of oxtail and an earthy flavor. The BBQ Oysters my hubby had both times and he loved them. The service was excellent both visits. It will be

I was going to Quail Hollow for about ten years and one Saturday morning denied me because they were too busy with other appointments. Seven Oaks took us in and took care of her . I had another emergency and they took her in and I was out within the hour. It depends on your attitude and perspective from the get go. They deal with rude pet parents all day !

Went twice.  First for a late night drink and then a second night for dinner.  

I went back because the bartender the first night was a nice guy.  He took some time to recommend a *really* good bourbon and was not stingy on the pour.  

The dinner the second night was just some oysters on the half shell and a fried oyster salad.  The raw oysters were delicious and the salad was perfect.  Right amount of dressing, portion size was right on, and it tasted great.  

The next day I asked a local for a restaurant recommendation and without prompting they mentioned Luke.  So that says a lot.

I picked this restaurant for my friends and I to try, and I think I had the worst breakfast! I judge places on if they can do the basics best, so I ordered the Southern Breakfast. Nothing on my plate was crazy amazing, and the bacon was WAY too salty. I mean, I prefer salty over sweet 90 percent of the time, but this was inedible. Tragic. 

One pal ordered an omelette with a crabcake inside, and she said that was killer. My other friend had a ridiculous-looking croque monsieur and also commented on its deliciousness. Sigh. I messed up. But I really wanted eggs and a biscuit!

It was kind of pricey, and I left feeling like I could have found something better elsewhere. Plus, no Besh sighting. Oh well.

LOVE THIS PLACE. Every dish here is delectable and unique! My ultimate favorites are:

1) Raw Oysters - Great Gulf oysters! They're nice and plump, soft and meaty. A must get!
2) Crispy Brussels Sprouts (Toasted almonds, Espelette honey, Progress Milk Barn cheese) - So flavorful! I've never had brussels sprouts like these. The almonds, honey and cheese really compliment one another. Sort of reminds me of a salad!
3) Crawfish Bisque - So creamy and rich! Lots of chunky crawfish! Another must get!
4) Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" (Roasted jalapeno cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausage) - The cheese grits are fantastic! Shrimp tasted fresh!

Such wonderful customer service, everyone that helped us was so friendly and accommodating. We were a large group of girls too, so you can only imagine! The ambiance is very lively and fun. Would love to come back!

We go to NOLA once every year and try to do what the locals might do and eat where they recommend.  Someone FINALLY mentioned this restaurant to us so we decided to try it out for Happy Hour...we couldn't have more pleased!  
Raw and fried oysters were outstanding!
Beet salad was my absolute favorite new thing!
Richie Rich (our server) was incredible!  Funny, kind, knew his stuff and made great recommendations.  He also is from the Midwest so we had a lot to chat about!  He even had chef make char-grilled oysters for me even though they were not listed on menu.  That is a sign of a great restaurant when they listen to how you like the food...not just how they want to serve it to you.
Go there!  Try it out!  You'll go back!!!  We did...3 times!!!  It is fantastic!  And don't forget to try the dessert.  We got the chocolate cake that was decadent!  Very small but delicious and a great way to top off your meal!
Watch out Richie!!!  We'll see you again next January!

DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY!!!
Last winter my heater packed up. This was the only company who could come out the next day. Their serviceman said a switch was broken and it would cost $664 to replace. They also said I should sign up for their service maintenance which was another $400. He replaced the switch and serviced both my heaters and 15 minutes later I gave him $1064. It felt odd spending so much money for 15 minutes but it was the middle of December. 
I called them back to service my heaters 2 weeks ago. The serviceman Vinnie was extremely unprofessional, wanted to replace igniters  on both heaters because they were old (even though they were working) and said a part needed to be replaced. All in all the cost was going tone $2200. When I did not sign up, their office manager Joe said he would charge $1800 and he would order the part right away. Vinnie  said he would come out over the weekend and replace  it. I was getting pretty fed up with Vinnie and wanted him out of my house. I told him to finish the servicing and I would think about it. He then walked around my kitchen and talked about my kitchen appliances and would not leave.

I then called Bachmann HVAC in Jenkintown. They said the igniters did not have to be replaced and the part which Fahrenheit wanted to replace would only cost $500. When I showed him the bill from Fahrenheit from last year for the $664 switch he said that only cost $20. 

I am planning to report them to consumer protection services. If I was not so busy I would even take them to court. And I may just do that.

RG

Must admit, coming from Seattle, we're spoiled with the Flagship REI.  The Boise one isn't even the size of a Walmart and we managed to get parking IN THE SHADE on a 90-degree day, right across from the entrance on a Monday afternoon.  Frankly, I was skeptical I'd find anything at all.

However, things changed when I met Matt in the shoe department.  Last year I bought a pair of Scarpa hiking boots, and it took me more than 6 months, two sets of shoe inserts, countless sock combination experiments to figure out that the intense feet pain I experienced after every hike wasn't due to my Edward Scissorhands-like feet but the fact that my Scarpas were too narrow for me.

I'd done my research and found that Keen Targhees and Lowa Renegades were good for wide feet, and armed with this knowledge felt ready to do battle with REI's shoe department personnel.  Matt was right on his game, however, measuring my feet and determining that I'm a size 8 (not the 6.5 I usually am in regular shoes and in the Scarpas).  He also seconded the Keen choice, as it's a brand that runs wider.  Then, he proceeded to teach me how to *properly tie* my hiking boots in two different ways, so that I don't have to chaff my fingers pulling hard on the shoestrings every time I lace them up.  So, like a little puppy that'd been kicked once too many times to the curb, I slowly started to trust REI and its staff again.

The extra star is given for REI's over-the-top service.  I'd brought the hated Scarpas in for an exchange, thinking maybe REI would give me $50 off on this new purchase, or a voucher - but they actually gave me a full refund, no questions asked (the original inserts weren't even in the shoes anymore.  I probably had them made into dolls and burned them in effigy for the great pain the boots caused my feet).  

So, after walking into the store, expecting to butt heads with Customer Service and just wanting to try on hiking boots, so that I could buy them cheaper on Amazon, I ended up getting the boots (not on sale), a dorky hiking hat (not on sale), and a new backpack (on sale) at REI.  REI Boise's service more than makes up for the limited selection, and the company's philosophy of giving back to the customers in dividends is what keeps customers going back.

Went to their happy hour because I heard they had 75 cent oysters by the half shell. Although disappointed to learn they're actually a dollar each, they were still great quality and well priced. I did prefer the oysters at dragos a bit more in terms of size and taste but these were a steal. The beers and cocktails were half off as well. The waiters were very attentive. Overall a great place to have raw oysters.

I was recommended Fahrenheit Heating and Cooling for my furnace repair by JB Plumbing.  These guys are rip off artists!!  They came and cleaned my furnace and replaced parts worth ($200).  The whole job took 2 hours and they charged me $1200.  Don't use these guys unless you like to throw your money away!!

This place is by far one of the best restaurants in New Orleans! Our servers gee was amazing! The seafood is to die for ! 100% recommend and go for the seafood plateau! Oh and the bread pudding is out of this world amazing!

Make reservations ahead of time. Not your typical walk in restaurant, but more good for special occasions. It is super nice and the food is really good. The croque monsier was REALLY good. Brussel sprouts were good too, but crazy greasy. All in all would recommend.
I highly recommend the Shrimp and Grits! You won't be disappointed! It's full of flavor!

DELICIOUS! Their servings are big (and so good) so they're honestly worth the price. Our server was extremely friendly and it was a nice place, with good lighting and olympics on the bar TV, which we could see from our table. Only downside was that our table was a bit too small to fit everything we ordered! The brussel sprouts are amazing!! Raw oysters were delicious, as they often are in Louisiana. Tuna tartare is 10/10, as well as the peach & goat cheese flatbread.

This is an​ after-work​k/late night food if your tired of the usual​ cookout/McDonald's run.  OKAY?

....this place is not cute whatsoever, so don't get too boujie. 

There are two ways to go about this restaurant​:

1: Walk in and sit ​at any table or booths which are NOT comfortable​ and enjoy watching the news on one of the two TV's till someone comes to give you a menu or take your order if you are ready. 

2: Drive up to (usually a line) resturant, people come to your window and you order and they bring the food to your car and you can eat in the ambiance of your car or drive home and eat there.

The food process: 
It does take time so be patient, they are actively​ cooking the meat, and putting the tacos/sope/burritos/etc, together for you. 

Once your order comes, its time to enjoy. Trust me the wait is worth it.

This place is fabulous. They really do have $.50 oysters at Happy Hour. Service was fine, they didn't look down their noses at us trying to keep it on the cheap. We still ended up spending $100 on 3 people. Had to have the mussels and foie gras...
Ordered a bunch of food for the family of course the one thing I got for myself is ruined

menu was very simple and great choices for everyone. 
appetizers were also a good selection
atmosphere is simple and quasi farmhouse feel

service, was slow..it was crowded but very slow.
I ordered a burger and it took nearly 45 minutes.
Dinner for 5 took over 2 hours, way too long.

if service was more prompt it would be a 4 star rating.

15 minutes before store closed my family and I were reminded 4 times they were closing soon.  Maybe spend more time helping and less time trying to make us leave!   These people weren't knowledgeable on the products or friendly.  Would highly recommend shopping elsewhere. Business is earned my friends!!  Now it's time to return the $800 in product I just purchased!!!

I have to assume all the 5 star reviews ordered oysters, which freshness dominates.
My dish was Sunday special pork (not veal anymore?) it was not what you would expect from a famous restaurant. It tasted just ok, pork was hard. Coffee was watery. My gf had the shrimp and grit that many likes on yelp. Other than shrimps themselves, I found nothing tasty.
Bill totally for $50 with 2 dishes, two drinks, no alcohol. Walked out still hungry but didn't want to disappoint my tongue anymore.
Crab bisque that came with my dish was the only good thing I can think of.

Very disappointed here... 
Food and service was 1 Star. 
Really food came out cold and I asked them to heat up more... it was my New Year's Day dinner with my mother. Very poor service. There is better place to eat beside here.

Celebrated a birthday with brunch today. Great service, our water glass and drinks were never left empty. Food was amazing with huge portions and one of the best sazeracs we've ever had. Make sure to try to Brussels sprouts, they are addictive and if you're nice they will give you the recipe! We will definitely be back.
Went for the butter cake and ended up with a scone. I wasn't satisfied. The staff was pleasant
Great local food and drinks. We loved everything. Super cool they do happy hour on Saturdays too!

The worst return policy around.
Rude, mask wearing Sheep.
Can't wait until Sheel's, an America loving store, opens in Meridian.
Until then, my family and friends will never shop at REI again.

WEAR YOUR MA A ASK!

Look at my previous reviews for Lüke and you'll see my stars are all over the board. This is due to their inconsistency, not mine. I've had great meals here and serious fails. Dinner last night was good, as I like their brothy, tomatoey shrimp & grits with andouille sausage. I also like the Lüke salad, with its distinctive horseradish dressing, but wish they'd offer a smaller, pre-dinner portion. The menu in place when this restaurant first opened years ago was firmly rooted in Alsatian cuisine, and now I feel like they've lost their focus. Happy hour oysters here are affordable, but I've had better oysters at some real dives in this city; theirs are lacking the plump juiciness that I've come to associate with P&J oysters. Perhaps they're shucking them in advance and the briny liquor is spilling out? I don't know. Specially cocktail menus usually have me vacillating with indecision, but the happy hour offerings on the current menu were not compelling. I had my usual French 75, and found it unbalanced, with too much lemon and not enough cognac. I've had this drink here more times than I care to admit, and it's usually excellent. I keep looking for the wonderful Croque Monsieur to return to the menu, but haven't seen it appear. It's winter now, and a great time to offer this decadent delight. I had Revillion dinner here in December, and didn't have one course that I enjoyed. The long and short of it is that Lüke is sometimes good, sometimes not, and has less to do now with Alsatian food than it did when I opened. Great restaurants have focus and do one cuisine brilliantly. I wish Lüke would.

Luke, will you be my boyfriend? Because that's how much I love your assiette de charcuterie.

Anyone that knows me well knows my love for a good pate, so imagine my great delight when I saw a whole big plate of it offered at lunch. All house made too! There was a chunky pate de campagne covered in a lacy layer of caul fat, beautifully textured headcheese, a few thin slices of a boudin, creamy delicious pork rilettes and my favorite - truffled rabbit and chicken liver pate. It's all served with the usual accouterments (mustard, chutney and the like) which I skipped so not to miss any of my potted meats flavor. As a bonus, they aren't stingy on the baguette toasts.

My dining companion had a roasted chicken dish with garlic mash which he said was great. I'm pretty sure he was a little horrified at my excessive consumption of innards and nasty bits, but too bad - more for me!

Service was perfectly attentive and very friendly. The interior of Luke is lovely too - a little slice of Paris right off Canal St. If I lived in New Orleans, I'd be here on the regular for sure,

I give this place 4.75 stars. Why you ask? This place has great food, great decor, and reasonable prices for a quality restaurant. However, it does lose a quarter of a star because I saw some less than spectacular service/performance going on. 

This place is split up into two sections, a back area and a front area. The front area has the bar and a few tables, the back area has the open kitchen where you can watch the chefs cook and where you can have bigger parties sit.

I came here the first time for dinner; my friends were going to Restaurant August and I didn't have that kinda cash, so I settled for another of Besh's Restaurants, which is how I ended up here. At $22 plus or minus a plate, I would not call this place cheap, but it is a discount compared to the alternative. I ordered the Jumbo Shrimp En Coccotte. It was 5 or 6 shrimps served on top of creamy grits in a cast iron skillet. The flavors were absolutely amazing, very savory and complimented the grits. I also tried the creme brulee and the Galette aux fraise t for dessert, both were very tasty. The creme brulee had fresh fruit and was excellently done. The Galette was like a strawberry danish with a scoop of ice cream. Good but not amazing. Before we left, one of the busboys, who kinda reminds me of Kenneth from 30 rock, recommended that we try the pancakes for brunch. He told us they were delicious, but could not tell us why. We took his advice anyways and came back for brunch. We ordered a stack of Mimi's pancakes (comes with 6 pancakes) and a side of home fries. The pancakes were some of the best I have ever had, unfortunately I cannot explain why. They are just good. The home fries came with onions and Allan Benton's bacon. This was the first time I had ever had Benton's bacon, and it was just soo good that I had to order some to go. Both times I came here, the food was absolutely delicious.

The only down side to my experience was a couple of servers. Our server was Chris, and he seemed like he just did not care very much. He did the bare minimum to be our server including checking in on us, and refilling drinks. When asked about the shrimps, he just said they were good (which to his credit they were), but he did not describe them in any sense. You would think a waiter would know what they are serving. I also saw another server eating a handful of fries, from his hand, while working, and in sight of the customers. That just seems like something that would be frowned upon wherever you go. And that is where the half a star went. The other servers and staff members were very nice and helpful.

Overall, very good food, helpful staff and I will visit here again when I get a chance.

Went here a few weeks ago expecting something grand and that definitely wasn't the case... I had the corn & crab bisque (when ordering this I expect CRAB... There was none) & the Washington Parish Roasted Chicken... The chicken was seasoned well & the potatoes were too. I enjoyed it for sure BUT back to the bisque. To be quite honest, the bisque was tasty even though it lacked crabmeat so I won't just say it was horrible when it wasn't... I give the food an overall 3.5 because of taste BUT the service was not great. My waiter was very nonchalant and not attentive... I really like when waiters ask if you're enjoying your meal & ask about dessert amongst other things regarding your dining stay but this guy didn't. Seemed as though he wasn't happy to be at work. But all in all the food wasn't bad, and if you'd ask me if I'd go again... I'll just have to decline.
Great food, fresh oysters, and a helpful staff. I have only good things to say. Happy hour is great.

Went for dinner with my mom and two dear friends. Had a reservation for 6 pm and we were seated immediately. Our waiter was adorable (according to my mom, haha), attentive, personable, but not overbearing at all. He encouraged us to try new things, and was honest about his personal preferences. He was also very knowledgeable about the food (how it was prepared, where the ingredients came from, how much of it was in a portion, etc) and also about the various cocktails, wines, and beer offered. All in all, we had a great time and didn't feel bothered at all by our waiter, yet felt that he was attending to our needs perfectly. Clearly, he cares about his job.
Now onto the food! For an appetizer, my mother and a friend shared raw oysters. I'm personally not into them, but they could only describe them as "delicious" in between enthusiastically stuffing their faces. Everyone except for me got a burger, and I could tell they enjoyed themselves as the whole table fell silent upon arrival of our entrees since we were so busy eating. I had the roasted chicken with veggies in a bacon and mushroom sauce, with fries subbed for the usual mashed potatoes. It was excellent, perfectly cooked, and the sauce was, in a word, insane.
The cocktail my mother had, the French 75, was delicious and she said was pretty strong (in other words, worth the money). They have a good wine list, as well as many beers, both exotic and domestic. Again, the waiter was able to make great recommendations for both beer and wine to compliment our meals.
All in all, a great experience with great food. Definitely worth a visit if you're in the area.

Caught happy hour. Caramelized Brussels sprouts are fantastic, not your average Brussels sprouts. Shrimp ettouffe over cheese grits with a crab topper, the only way to eat grits. The hamburger was huge, you'll need to split it. Oysters... happy hour and wine.

Terrible dinner experience. Firstly, it took about 10 minutes for the server to arrive at our table. By that time, it was 6:03, and so happy hour prices were no longer available. Seriously. 
Drinks - GROSS. I ordered a French 75 and it came full of froth and terribly sweet. Obviously the champagne used was flat, or had been open for too long, which should have been obvious to the server and bartender based on the inch of froth in the glass. I was grossed out, but willing to overlook it initially.  
Next, they made a huge stink about us moving our drink orders from a small bar table to a dinner table once our entire party arrived. I have done this many times, in many restaurants, and never had such a huge deal made about it! In the meantime, a woman came by multiple times to remind us that this was a "VIP area" and we shouldn't take up room standing at different ends of the table and talking to each other (we had a large party to celebrate a birthday). 
The food was alright. Overpriced and unexceptional, but good, I guess. Nothing to write home about. 
When we divided up our check (we had a large party), it took 15 minutes for our server to return. When she did, she pointed out we had a discrepancy with our check - oops, sorry, here's how to fix it. Another 15 minutes, and she had run our cards. Half an hour to charge 6 cards? It was beyond awkward, and totally unnecessary. The woman there to apparently remind us how to behave had time to drop by during this time, just to ask us "how was everything," and yet our server couldn't be bothered to run the check for 30 minutes. 
In a city of exceptional food, please don't overpay here for decor and location, when service and quality is so severely lacking. 
Will NOT return, would not recommend!

The service and meal were superb! The shrimp and grits fall in the top three I've had in life. The sauce was sauce and paired perfectly with the creamy white grits. I'm sure I'll dream about devouring this dish until I can get back to New Orleans. The bread pudding was a decadent ending to a great brunch. I wish I could have bought a bag of those candied pecans. The vanilla bean ice cream gave the dish a perfect balance of sweet, creamy, moist goodness.

This is a 2 star review mostly because I am vegetarian and wasn't able to experience 99% of their food. People that eat meat have a different opinion for obvious reasons. 

But, alas, vegetarians beware. It's a pretty authentic mexican restaurant that sticks vegetarians with the same cheese enchilada they can get elsewhere, but without the fear of chicken broth rice or lard refried beans. I haven't verified either, but if i had to choose some place that the rice and beans were not vegetarian, i would probably choose this place. 

Meat eaters, give it a try.

Vegetarians, keep on truckin.

Visiting from out of town. Only 15 dollars for the entire week. They had new clean life fitness and hammer strength equipment. Had a turf area with CrossFit like set up. It was a great experience for the week.

I would say it's very fancy looking place for southern food but I was like I am gonna go in anyways. I ordered the Shrimp and Grits. It's Louisiana's shrimp, eggs, andouille sausage and jalapeno cheese grits. I hella loved it. It was cooked like a sauce and all mixed together perfectly on top of a very very very bomb jalapeno cheese grits. The grits I would say was the highlight. This girl loves grits and with jalapeno even more amazing. I would definitely come back again.

Came for brunch and the restaurant was empty. Realized quickly why. Menu blah and over priced, service blah, and bring a coat because it was FRIGID. Coffee was like warm and full of grinds. Maybe the reviews are from dinner??

Awesome lunch here while in for Jazzfest.  Kicked things off with the Seafood Gumbo and it was loaded with shrimp and oysters.  I also tasted the crab bisque and it was excellent.  Did their homemade pasta with shrimp for my main and it was a winner.  Solid service and hope to get back for dinner or their brunch.

I stopped here because I was in the neighbourhood, and I heard Elm was a pretty good coffee spot. I was a little surprised at how small the cafe is. There were a couple tables outside, and some seats at the window, but that was it. Elm Cafe doesn't really seem like the best option for me to sit down, have a coffee and "study" for school. It's a grab and go place, and that's okay. 

I grabbed a coffee to go, an Americano. They use 49th Parallel coffee, which I do enjoy. The service was friendly, and the coffee was good and strong. The lunch menu at Elm Cafe always sounds pretty good, but I was there well after lunch. One day I'll have to remember to come by a little earlier and try one of their sandwiches.

My boyfriend and I are sushi-obsessed. We went out of our way to check out a new place, and we agree that Hachi is awesome! We ordered the pork gyoza as an appetizer and it was incredible. We both enjoyed our sushi tremendously. Only con -- the service was a tad slow; however, it was quite busy and staff was incredibly polite!

I am a native New Orleanian and eat at this restaurant many times throughout the year.  Happy hour, birthdays, holidays, etc.  Today we sat at the bar and this was the worst service ever!  Bar staff had terrible attitudes.  Ordered a dozen of fried oysters and we received 8.  Informed the bartender and we thought she put in a new order or additional oysters.  She didn't.  We get the bill and it still reflected a dozen.  Brought it to the attention of the staff and they acted like it was a Problem to correct.  They did however correct it.  I refer all my out of town guests. Not anymore.  They are officially on time out.

The food is good, but it is very over priced.

Skip this and hit up something else, chances are it will cost you half and be just as good.

Please order their raw oyster during happy hour, it's fresh, big and yumm.

drinks are soso though.

Stopped in for a bite on a and enjoyed it thoroughly. The decor is nice, with a laid-back elegance that makes you feel warm and welcome. 

To eat, I cautiously followed a comrade's recommendation of the fried oyster salad. I'm not typically a salad guy (especially in the creole capital), but I have to tip my salad-discriminating cap to this one. A generous garnish of thick-cut-bacon-bits tossed in the fray with hearty and delicious fried Gulf oysters. Nom city, population: me. And you can tell people you got a salad. Take THAT, etouffee. 

Also, you'd be doing yourself a disservice if you didn't take a nibble of the bread pudding. After all, you had a salad for dinner.

Shrimp and grits: 3.5
I know this is there signature dish but I wasn't a fan of the pepper taste in the grits, and it didn't stand out to me

Brussel sprouts: 4 stars
I enjoyed the touch of sweetness from the honey but it had too much oil and I prefer mine crispier

Roast chicken and Matzo ball soup : 3 stars
The tomato was too prominent and made the soup acidic to me. Matzo ball was a tad flavorless and didn't have the right texture. 

Stuffed p&j oysters: 5 stars
Generous portion of crab, the Oysters meshed well and the overall dish was delicious 

Service: 5 stars
One of the only restaurants so far in NOLA who had no problem with the request for less salt and the staff were friendly. We decided to come back later for desserts and they were welcoming about it.

We were on a new oyster hunt at a place that was not Acme or one of the other New Orleans traditional restaurant. Luke was a great discovery for this venture. Upon reading some of the reviews on Yelp, and even though we read it has sometimes poor service, but great food, we decided to give it a whirl! Our whirl worked out well.  LUKE IS AWESOME!!!!!

The menu has a lot of German influences in it and that, we liked. We fired up the duck pate first, along with some Blue Point Oysters. DDDDDDDDDDDEEEEEEEEELISH. The pate was smooth, well blended, exquisite and fresh. It is served with a variety of freshly made relishes and some grain mustard to spread on some thin crispy toast. OUTSTANDING. We enjoyed it very slowly!

The Blue Points were the freshest, smoothest and best I have had in years. I was, at first, a lil underwhelmed with the dab of horseradish that came with the oysters and then quickly found out it was the most potent taste bud jarring spicy root. I love me some spice kick & this was fierce and very tasty! A dab will do ya' even if your a leather mouth.

My eating partner tried some bratwurst and I went for the beet salad. All outstanding. 

The service was excellent. They were very attentive and quick on all points. We loved our experience with Luke and then on top of all of that it was not outrageously priced. BONUS!!!!!!!!

Love to Luke!
Worst service ever. I wasn't even served. I stood there for 5 minutes looking like an idiot and they all saw me but nobody served me. I'm never going here again.

It was one of our better stops in NOLA.

Very casual and unpretentious yet very nice. The place was packed on a Saturday night. 

Our party of 8 got seated right away in a back room, with a full kitchen view. 

Our table had the pate, oysters, crawfish soup, Luke burger, croque madame et frites, and the etouffee. All good. Not outstanding, but good. 

The croque madame was mine and although it looked incredible (receiving ooohs and aaaahs from everyone). However, the bread was hard to cut through making me have to jam my knife into it with much more force and effort than I would like to use during a leisurely dinner (and why I took a star away). The burger was a good gourmet burger. The pate was one of the stars of the bunch. Presentation was great as was taste. 

What was outstanding was the FRIED OYSTER, BACON, ROMAINE
& AVOCADO SALAD!!!! We ordered two of those and everyone kept stealing from my plate! It was unexpected and beyond delicious. 

Service was friendly and overall good. I have to say that our waitress was quite patient and efficient with our large, rowdy group. 

I would definitely give it another go if ever in town, but only after I cross off other restaurants (like August) off my list.

After eating and enjoying Luke for many years, tonight has changed my opinion.  

After recently doing some Reveillon menu research on nomenu.com, I found Luke listed, visited their web site and was excited to explore their offering in person and in conjunction with a birthday/Christmas family celebration.  

Tonight, 18 December 2013, we made reservations and went to Luke. 

Let me begin with the service.  Upon arrival, it was paltry - at best - with the exception of one kind gentleman waiter who seemed to get it and really care.  

We started with 2 dozen raw oysters - that seemed to be shucked an hour earlier and left on a cooling rack.  Needless to say, it would have been nice to have freshly shucked and cocktail sauce of better quality than Sysco ketchup.

I chose the Reveillon.  The 1st course - I opted for the boudin.  It was not nearly as good as other local options like Cochon or Toup's Meatery, but sadly it was the best thing brought to the table in the four courses.  

For the 2nd Course, I ordered turtle soup.  Let me preface that I am a Cajun and eat just about anything; and rarely, if ever, send anything back.  Tonight, I sent the turtle soup back.  After being blown away two nights prior at R'evolution, this seemed like canned soup with three or four small pieces of turtle meat.  (quail, duck or deviled eggs or sherry were not involved or offered).

For the main course, the Flounder with crabmeat and spinach topped with what may as well been Velveeta was overdone, salty and quite small. In fairness, the spinach was nice. 

Although others had to wait longer for drinks than I did, the Tin Roof on tap was delightful.  

After having enough of the sub par food and long waits, we opted to take the desert home; but that took time too. 

I offer this to fellow locals and travelers visiting New Orleans.  I appreciate sharing and receiving good, objective information - especially about food; and I want others to have the best meals possible - regardless of the price point - while in New Orleans.  

Christmas festivities turned into a Last Supper for Luke.

Happy Holidays!
Great seafood, in a not so great location. We hit the happy hour for half priced seafood, just amazing!! Drinks were very expensive.
Great variety of unique options to choose from.  Went here twice.  Both times i wasn't disappointed.  You will be satisfied.
50 cent oysters and half priced cocktails makes a fantastic happy hour!  Love it!  I also had the étouffée which was good not the best I've ever had but decent.  Service was friendly.

I was on Penn's campus for a weekend class and got a steak bowl to go during my quick lunch break. The rice was hard and the cheese was bitter. I was surprised that highlight was the steak, which was cooked a beautiful medium rare but there wasn't enough of it.  The bowl was drizzled in plenty of sauce yet the flavor was still bland. All in all, I don't think it was a very well thought out combination of ingredients but Cosi will always get the job done for a fast, easy lunch.

Except for that horrific steakhouse that they have in the boring casino, John Besh is a talented chef and this is his best restaurant -according to me- especially when you consider the price and what you get (aka performance).

Luke has the best burger in town, maybe the state or the south. It is HUGE though (seriously, could be the biggest burger i have ever had) and it comes with delicious fries (thin and crispy).

Other entrees worth a try are the shrimp en cocotte which comes in a rather small dish and the pork schnitzel, which is good. Chicken liver with rabbit pate is the best appetizer (for someone who does not really like oysters)

Shrimp and grits are another favorite. That should be tried. For breakfast.

The bread pudding is the best i have ever had and i do not even have a liking for bread pudding (i actually find the idea behind this dessert appalling especially when you consider the conditions in which it transpired.) Though, this prone-to-be-dry pastry becomes a delicious treat here and is huge. Comes with ice cream on top. Try.

Steamed chocolate is another dessert worth trying, though it is rather small and this makes it just ok. 

Overall, a very good spot not to be missed. Especially if you are just dropping by to have couple appetizers.

While all our food and drinks were absolutely delicious (crab au gratin, étouffée, soft shell crab, Luke burger) some of us were left feeling like it wasn't completely worth the price. Mainly due to the portions. 

They got my friend's order wrong for both the appetizer and the entree. The entree she decided to just eat since we waited a while for it to come out. And the portion for the étouffée was definitely stingy especially when they make it so damn good, with the perfect amount of heat. 

Service was good. And despite the small portions (for some of our apps/entrees) and high prices I thoroughly enjoyed my meal.

We went for dinner on a Friday hoping to experience awesome food by John Besh during our trip to New Orleans.  Perhaps our hopes were too high but all the food seemed a bit plain.  Each dish was almost there, but fell flat.  Like everything needed more seasoning or spice.  We do not eat meat, and so that may have also played a part because there was not much of a fish selection.  The meat dishes around us, which is what everyone else was eating, looked amazing.  

The waitress didn't seem to care much about our experience, and seemed hurried, but we did have quick service.  

We did like the atmosphere and the quaintness of the smallish divining rooms.
Best, most authentic Chinese food I've found in the Tampa area. Portions are huge and owners are very nice.

Happy Hour is gr8, disappointed not even one domestic bottled beer. I ordered boiled king Crab Legs 38.00 & when the came they were barely warm. Shell was soft. Out of refrigerator pre-cooked then microwaved I believe, as my husband could see. The butter for dipping had to much lemon. I am sure this is a nice place but I don't have time to give it another shot

When I was an undergrad, I thought Cosi was really cool. I didn't know it was a chain, they had square bagels, and they would serve you s'more fixins with a fire. Pretty sweet.

Now I am not an undergrad and Cosi is everywhere and it is always crowded and I am full of rage standing behind the screeching law school students in line. And yet, when I can't figure out what to eat but I am starving and have no time, I go here. Because this is the function of a chain restaurant. And the food is pretty good.

Pros: Free wireless, nice seating area upstairs, chance to practice zen meditation while willing self not to strangle public at large. 
Cons: Lines, when it's crowded going from ordering your food to paying becomes a crazy mosh pit, pretty expensive for sandwiches. 

If you are going to go out of your mind if you eat another TBM or Signature Salad, you should order the Spinach Artichoke Dip. Just don't look at the nutritional information. Ever.

Had a lovely lunch here.  The hostess was friendly and full of energy as she showed be back to my table.  The server checked in on me regularly and made a good suggestion to help me with my order. The brussel sprouts were delicious.  Fries were not the best-they weren't hot, were soggy, needed salt.

Delicious - completely worth it and I would eat here again and highly recommend.
We had the buttermilk fried quail, flammekuchen, shrimp and grits and the bread pudding

All were great! Super creamy and tasty grits - top quality. You must get the bread pudding!!!
Best chicken and waffles I've ever had. Would have posted a picture but I was too hungry to take it lol
This is a late review (visited April 2014). Very good dinning experience, Hard to go beat at a John Besh restaurant. The gumbo and the octopus were the standouts, lots of bold flavors. I will return

The food was great the crawfish bisque was the best we had here in NOLA however our server didn't seem interested in serving us he seemed more preoccupied with rolling silver ware then checking on us or refilling our drinks
Glad to see Panera finally migrating to Boise. Love the food, the fast casual watiterless concept and clean, modern environment. Great soups, salads and baked goods.

This is what a gym should be like. 

First off, it's a good size. It has a variety of equipment. 

Every piece of cardio equipment has its own TV with 10-20 cable channels (including ESPN, MTV, and all the locals), and then theres 9 additional machines in their movie theater which plays a new movie every day. 

They have a good variety of free weights including: 2 smith machines, 1 free rack, 2 flat benches, an inclined and declined bench and then 3 dumbbell benches which can also be adjusted up or down, 2 full sets of curling bars (which are really convenient so that you don't have to keep switching weights. I haven't seen these at any other gym), one is an ez-bar and one is flat. 

They also have the normal resistance machines that other gyms have, however these machines are very new and have the most fluid range of motion of any machines I've used. They are also very adjustable and can be made to fit my short self easily.

All of these amenities come for only $20/month which is very comparable to other gyms in the area. The staff is also very personable and friendly. Sadly, I haven't been in the area for a while so I had to cancel my membership (which was easy to do), but if I am in the area again and need a gym, this Retrofitness will be my first choice.

I use to love Panera Bread a lot! Now a days it's just not the same... the food is way too over-priced for the portions you get. Me and my boyfriend paid nearly $30 for the get two, plus 2 drinks. That's just crazy! That's restaurant prices! I don't mind paying those prices if the portions were decent size, but they're not!
Really good gala food, fast service, Friendly staff and fair price. I'll recommend this place.

Cute spot for a lunch. Ordered three small plates for the two of us. We had the rabbit and chicken patê (beautiful selection of jellies, pickles, mustard), fried quail, and crawfish cheesy beignets. Everything came quickly and was presented nicely. Great portions when sharing between two people. 4 stars - maybe more variety for small plates would help to compliment already great dishes.

Presentation of all dishes is EXCELLENT and so is the decor!  Miso soup is great - this version has shiitake mushrooms which adds a slightly deeper flavor that is perfect for cold weather. Salad is good and complementary. The tacos are yummy and refreshing, and I will order them again. The negamaki and other steak dish come out sizzling on hot stones - it's beautiful, but the food is HOT and will not cool down even after 15 minutes on the stone so be careful!  Sashimi does taste really good - especially liked the King Salmon.  We were served by the owner who was very friendly. He said they have been open four months so far.  

Again, the presentation of the sashimi is especially excellent (I won't ruin the surprise by telling you what it is though).  If you are going on a date this dish is a good way to express your worldliness without getting stuffed full of food to the point of incapacitation.

The owner is Japanese but do not start trotting out Japanese at him or you will both end up looking 恥ずかしい (embarrassed) - trust me!   He was a very attentive and informative server. Apparently he pays extra to receive fish shipments daily instead of weekly like similar restaurants - maybe this is why other reviewers mentioned that the sashimi tastes especially good?

They do offer desserts but we were stuffed by the time they gave us dessert menus. A sensible future addition to the dessert menu would probably be a red bean (azuki) based dessert.

The place gets deservedly packed at "prime time" so you might want to try to make reservations.  Definitely recommended and will come again.

We enjoyed a very good meal with friendly people and a knowledgeable, helpful waiter. The bisque was good. Lana's ribeye steak was very good. My thick chunk of pork (cochon) was moist and falling apart, sitting atop a bed of spinach which sat, in turn, on a corn-bread base. The dish was smothered in a raspberry-dijon sauce. It was very good to excellent. The waiter suggested a Bourdeaux which was reasonably priced and complimented both entrees. The banana cream puffs were very good. In sum, the food was very good and very consistent. In addition, three other customers sitting apart from each other but near us engaged us in pleasant dinner conversations.

One note: I see that Luke is rated $$. That price range probably applies to lunch or perhaps to appetizers and a drink. Our dinner with tip was well over $100.00 and well worth it.

Can't go wrong here. Of course, the happy hour oysters and drinks are fantastic, but Luke is also a great place to go for a date or if you've got friends in from out of town. Awesome food and atmosphere. Not crazy expensive either.

Food was great.  The service was even better.  

I had the shrimp and grits.  The sauce was wonderful, very smooth and without a typically fishy taste.  The grits had a nice texture.  

My wife had the Croque Monsieur.  Very filling.  Full of cheese and well-seasoned fries.  

Staff felt they took too long bringing our dinner so one of the managers, John Knight! Brought us some boudin and also the crabmeat maison.  Very nice.  He even sent us off with a couple of truffles.  

I definitely recommend this restaurant.
Delicious! You've seen the reviews. It's totally true.

We had tried to eat here around 6pm without a reservation but they were booked for the whole night which seemed crazy. We decided to put in a reservation for tomorrow around 8:45 pm which was the only time slot for the night. 

We sit down and wait for about a good 10 min before someone came to take our order. Which was ok since we were talking to each other. We ordered the fried quail which was amazing. It was fried to perfection and it was glazed in a sweet maple syrup which added the perfect blend of flavors and spices. She got the crab bisque which also was made to perfection and I only got one spoon full since that was all my girlfriend would let me have. I had eaten so much gumbo, étouffée, crawfish and seafood yesterday I wanted a burger. I ordered the burger which was really good but there is one thing I didn't like so much. The fries that come with the burger were way too thin and crunchy and this is my opinion. 

Other than that the food was great and it all depends what you order. This place did not receive five stars from me because of the service. Our waiter was slow and if it wasn't for other waiters helping out we wouldn't have had refills as much as we did. The bill was around 75$.

Luke is a great place to go for lunch. I got the Poulet Grand-Mère, which was chicken with vegetables. The meat was soft, juicy and not overdone. The meat was high quality. I loved the way the vegetables were cooked, and the mashed potatoes was excellent. The portion was pretty big for me, so I gave the rest to my husband. It was perfect since he ate the shrimp and grits, and the portions for that was small. The waiter gave us a piece of bread. At first I was annoyed because I wished he would have gave us a bread basket, but it turned out it was enough to split the bread with my husband. I do wish that the bread was served on a plate. It was simply wrapped in a napkin and he laid it on the table. I'm sure they keep the tables clean, but it would have looked good for presentation purposes. 

I would definitely come back again to luke.

A little pricey. But you will feel and taste what you paid for. We ordered breakfast today the pancake, shrimp and grits and the fresh oysters, shrimp,muscles, and clams platter. Super good and even if we choose to share waiter not snobby.. (Like at Peche) Tip happy hour 3-6 fresh oysters 75c a piece great deal considering they sell it fir $32 a dozen regular price

I have eaten here a half a dozen times now and have had mostly terrific experiences.  I love their charcuterie, their boudin, and the oyster salad.  I have had great duck here as well.  I ordered the 1/2 chicken previously and it was murdered, dried out, overcooked and buried in so much bacon you couldn't taste anything else.  The dish was really heavy and heavy handed.  I ordered it again and it was succulent and beautiful, the veggies were a little crisp but this was a complete turn around for this dish.

We like to go for happy hour and usually enjoy the discounted oysters.  On one visit they were all so small as to be comical and it was hard to believe they would serve them and charge us for them.  Still, overall, I am a huge fan.  It's hard to judge a restaurant on a single visit and I try not to do it too harshly when I see that so many things are going well there and how obviously they know how to prepare and serve a quality product.  The bacon does not contain nitrates or sulfites and much of the product served is organic.  I really appreciate the effort to make sure that I am eating safe food John.  Thank you!

It's good for the price- nowhere near great. Service is phenomenal but too many of the items are 80% there flavor wise. Its tough to say because I enjoyed my two experiences there- but I was not a fan of the prices.

Didn't even get to sit. The place was half empty when we came with a party of 8 (bachelor's party). We were in sports gear for our bike tour after brunch.  Hostess proceeded to inform us they can't take a party of 8. When I asked if she can split us into parties of 4, she proceeded to let us know, politely, that she's actually all booked through Mardi Gras and can't take walk ins.  -.-"

This review is solely for Luke's Happy Hour and the pricing definitely plays a part in the rating.

75 cent for raw oysters (any amount) and $1.25 for fried oysters (6 or a dozen). Half off for cocktails and alcohol. 

We got 2 raw oysters, a dozen fried oysters, a cup of gumbo and a French 75. I love the fact that they didn't cheap out and give us bottom shelf cognac. The raw oysters were slightly sandy. Fried oysters were a little too over coated with batter, but slightly lovely. The gumbo was out of this world - smoky with a depth given by the roux, rich without being heavy and creamy. I could have eaten a whole bowl of it by myself. The other great thing was the complimentary fresh baguette with whipped butter. The John Besh restaurants really do well in the bread category. 

Total bill came up to $40, which is a bargain for food and drinks of this quality.

Absolutely agree with everything Jacquelin K. says. The staff here can get overwhelmed and unproductive when the line gets long. And yet, I've been in there when there was NO line, and it still took ten minutes to get someone's attention. One worker was rearranging potato chips behind the register while I waited patiently to order.

I give Cosi three stars because, unlike some other folks, I do think it's a cozy place to have coffee (or even a slightly overpriced sandwich.) The booths are a million times better than typical cafe seating.

I really love the Cosi flatbread when it's warm and fresh. But it loses it's kick when it sits around for a while---and that's what you're gonna get if you go in when the place is really busy. 

My favorite used to be the tandoori chicken sandwich. I hope they still have it.

Ate here for dinner with a few friends. We started with a cup of the gumbo which was on point. The shrimp was tender and not over cooked and the spiciness was perfect. For my main course I had the Poulet Grande-Mere, which was absolutely delicious. It was one of the best roasted chicken that I have had in a long time. It's cooked with pancetta in creamy sauce that was just divine. The service was what really made our experience from a good to a great one. He was a taller, young male, who was very attentive.  He was very informative and gave great beer suggestions. I will definitely be back when I visit New Orleans again.
Great P&J oysters - fresh and tasty. French 75 for a cocktail. Hope to visit here again - especially during HH!
Great sushi and super service! We have been here for both lunch and dinner several times and never been disappointed! My favorite is the Alligator Roll!

Had reservations for 2 & was seated immediately, in the back part of the restaurant (the front looked cooler).
Ordered a coffee, took 10 minutes to be served.
Overheard our waiter cuss at co-workers and snap at customers.
Left immediately. Did not stay to eat.
Had the swordfish and it was dry and over cooked.  Overall, a very good restaurant.  Just had a below average meal.

I came to Luke's for happy hour oysters with a friend-- she lives here, but it's my first time in the city. I've never had oysters before, but she told me she only gets them here, because they're always really clean and don't ever feel gritty. I don't have much to compare to in that respect, since this was my first experience, but they were definitely grit-free.

Far and away though, the best part about our meal here was the service. Our server, Rich, was attentive and pleasant without hovering, and really went above and beyond to ensure we had a good experience. He found out I was visiting NOLA, and that this was my first experience eating oysters, and really rolled out the proverbial red carpet. We asked for a sauce recommendation and were then given an incredible off-menu 8-sauce sampler (the duck sauce was to die for, but the béarnaise, 5-minute tomato, aioli, and signature Tabasco ranch were also wonderful. I wouldn't recommend the pepper jelly, but this may be more of a texture thing). 

My friend and I have both worked in commercial kitchens, and I appreciated the extra time and effort it took to pull that together for us--it was a little thing, but it elevated our whole evening. Our glasses were never empty, the food was always out quickly, and everything was delicious- but really, the service is what made this such a great way to kick off my trip to New Orleans. Would 12/10 recommend.

Stopped in with a friend on the way to catch a show at Tipitina's but too pressed for time for the modest wait.  It was the end of JazzFest & I really wanted a good meal rather than being on my feet at Tip's all night so I took a cab back & ate solo at the bar.

Sunday dining options are limited in this town I understand, luckily this place was just the ticket.  Friendly bar staff, recommended a good red.  One look to my left at the juicy steaks served up on butcher blocks & the menu was a formality (some very interesting offerings, though).  

Perfect ribeye, seasoned to let the natural flavors dominate, and the 'maitre d'hotel butter' on top was a decadent flourish.  The trend continued as the person beside me also ordered this but with the warm crabmeat on top...looked amazing!

I'd definitely make a point to return next time I'm in town.

AMAZING sandwiches and AMAZING service!! 

I don't think I've ever had better sammiches than I have at Elm. They are the sammich masters. Seriously, so delicious. Try the vegetarian sammich or the early sammiches for a nice egg breakfast creation. 

I can't wait to come back to Edmonton to get myself to Elm!
Great happy hour! I had a few French 75s which were amazing. I smacked on some brussel sprouts which were also great! Check this place out! I think happy hour is from 4-6pm.

I have long been a fan of Chef John Besh so I has to stop at at least one of his places on my trip. And Lüke did not disappoint. The meal was fantastic, well worth the cost, and with it being restaurant week they had down great specials as well. Best part of the meal though had to be the bread pudding which was hands down the best I have ever had. Also it was. Also sitting near the kitchen as you could watch them at work. And finally the exclusive beers made for The restaurant are also really good. And the servers can offer great paying suggestions.
I am the vehicle control officer for my job and bring all our vehicles here for fluid service. Super friendly staff, Frankie is awesome to work with too. She makes sure to take are of her customers!

Disappointed, went for breakfast. Greeted and seated promptly, then waited and waited, just as I was about to walk out a waiter recognized me and brought water, after further delay came to take my order and bring coffee. Food was good but there was no toast or bread with the omelette.  Had to ask for butter and coffee refill. Seemed like staff were B S-ing in the kitchen and not watching the store. For the price I expected better service.

I came to Luke specifically for their raw oyster Happy Hour special. Came in at 5pm on a weekday (with a reservation).

The raw oysters were super cheap (75 cents/each) and they came out pretty fast every time I reordered. I also tried the fried oysters and those were pretty darn tasty. Service was good, and the restaurant was lively and had a nice ambiance.

However, I went to Trenasse across the street the next day to also try their raw oyster Happy Hour, and Trenasse was better in my opinion. Both restaurants were great in terms of quality and price, but the oysters were larger/plump, had more variety, and more juicy at Trenasse compared to Luke.

The oyster selection, presentation & flavor were all outstanding. Larger than expected, we were seated in the back room - kinda missed some of the ambiance. Food was great - I had the ribeye and it was on par with a good steak house. Appetizers looked good, but opted for 24 oysters - lots of flavors - loved the Southern Belle's that we had not had before. Yum!
Good service. I really liked the Brussels sprouts; the mussels were good; jambalaya was salty. Going to try the shrimp and grits next time I visit!

A GOOD EXAMPLE OF A BAD SERVICE
Had a chance to visit this place on Monday and got seated pretty quickly - within 10 minutes as hostess promised. Our server, a middle aged man whose name I haven't memorized was exceptionally nice and professional at the beginning, he was very good about the food recommendations and even said my gin cocktail was going to be on house - "because it took too long", as he explained. We were absolutely enjoying our food and the outstanding customer service and couldn't foresee this ending badly at all.
After less than an hour when we were just done with our food and were continuing our conversation the waiter appeared out of nowhere with a bus boy. Without saying a single word or asking us whether we were in a mood for another drink or desert he demonstrably placed the check on our table, stretched his arm right under my chin, picked up my plate and placed it on the tray held by the bus boy. The same combination of actions in a complete silence happened to my friend's plates and utensils.   Strictly out of curiosity I started looking around in order to see whether we were really abusing this place's hospitality and it turned out there were FOUR vacant tables without a 'Reserved' sign on any of them and two people by hostess' desk waiting to be seated. 
The second wave of negativity and passive aggressive behavior was demonstrated when we requested our bill to be split between two of us -  we were frowned upon and were shown, so there are no any doubts, how annoying we were. 
The food was pretty good though, hence one star.

P.S. The tips I've left to my check were solely provided to pay for the complimentary cocktail and not the service or the level of professionalism of the above mentioned person. After what happened I don't feel comfortable accepting any on-house drink from this place.
I've never had Chinese food this good! The service is great and friendly and overall atmosphere is impeccable. Definitely a first choice among restaurants in the area. Yum!
Exceptional and exotic preparations.  Mine was skate wing, lightly breaded.  Tender, moist, succulent.

The Silo burger was pretty good. I'm not a big burger consumer but I don't mix dairy and meat so this was an appetizing option. Coffee is solid and the people are very nice. Prices are fair too. I'd go back again for sure.

My husband and I stopped in for lunch and enjoyed every bit of Luke's. There was not wait, we were seated immediately. The service was excellent, I had no complaints. The decor was upscale but you could still feel the New Orleans vibe. The food was phenomenal, I enjoyed everything. I ordered the  crab and corn bisque, shrimp En cocotte (shrimp and grits), and fried oysters. All 5/5! A bit pricey if you're on a budget but I believe in "you get what you pay for" and the food was well worth the price. I would definitely recommend.

Of you need anything for the outdoors this is a one stop place. They have just about everything an outdoors person could possibly dream of wanting. We needed a Lugaloo for actual tent camping. You can't go wrong with this place.
The best Oyster Happy Hour in town! The P&J Oysters are the best. Sat at the bar and enjoyed great conversation with Shucker and awesome staff.
Thoroughly enjoyed our dinner. Service was friendly, food fresh, creative and delicious.  I look forward to return visits and I highly recommend.

Stopped by for happy hour (3-6) and we were clearly underdressed but really what do you expect from a couple of tourists walking around NOLA during the hot and humid summers. We had to awkwardly hang around the bar area until some bar seats opened up but it's worth it for $0.75 oysters! At that price, you can easily just tell the bartender to just keep the oysters coming by the dozen. Most drinks are also half off. My favorite cocktail was the Door Three.

This place is AMAZING! The brussel sprouts are to die for (trust me, just order them - send me the bill if you don't like them)! The shrimp and grits were perfect ,and this is coming from someone typically who refuses to eat GRITS! You will not be disappointed. Also if there's a wait, just wait - your tastebuds won't regret it!
Absolutely a 5 star!   Creativity from the bar staff and superb wait team were fitting accents to the incredible food.

The food was great but the service was awful. It wasn't busy yet it took 20 minutes to get a drink from the time we sat down at the bar. 

We went to the bar waiting for a table 4 minutes there and no drink. Our table was ready so we were seated and continued to wait. I asked the waiter for a napkin, it never showed up. 

 Food was really good it's too bad the service will make me think twice before returning.
Go here if you want to get sick from old meat and expired sour cream and queso #TeamQdoba
Food presentations are amazing!! Jess, our server was fantastic!! Loved the fresh baked biscuits! Some of the food came out cold, so had to return. Overall, good experience.

Wonderful experience here! I took my 15yo pup here for laser therapy after an IVDD flare up. The entire staff is super friendly, and I was happy to meet Dr. Wishik who seems open to both holistic and conventional medicine. I am going to finish out my pups treatment, and then I plan on continuing to come here for her care. I would definitely recommend.
Excellent food. Great atmosphere. The shrimp and grits are excellent and a must try. Ask for Nicole, she is a very good waitress.

I stayed at the Hilton so Luke was easily accessible. Fantastic happy hour, as I had 30 oysters. 18 fresh gulf oyster, one that came with a pearl, and 12 fried. The fried oysters and sauce was fantastic! I went back another night and ordered gumbo, and crab claws. The gumbo was ok, the crab claws were good. The carrot cake dessert was not very good, although the ice cream with it was.

Oil change and maintenance performed on the Toyota, and given a $20 off another vehicle. Next day, Nissan oil change and maintenance performed anticipating Jiffy Lube honoring their $20 off, but ended up paying full price for 2 extra quarts of oil. No place on the flyer did it specify oil limitations. So instead, the cost was double the advertisement. Hmm, a classic example of false advertising.

"Fancy, aren't we?". This is a known high end restaurant. From the moment you walk in you get a, "I have to mind my manners in here". From what I observed, the customers were diverse. The host was very kind and friendly. Our seating was near the kitchen, with the glass view. Watching our food be prepared was clutch, it was cool to see the staff prepare our food. 

On to the food, I destroyed the Shrimp and Grits, it had a great mixture of flavors and crab and corn bisque was nothing short of amazing. The only take back from the bisque was that I ordered a bowl but the portion was more like a cup serving. Overall I'll give LUKE 4.6, nice place for a simple lunch date or just lunch period.

Had a reservation for 8:30, quickly seated. Only place that i will eat Brussel sprouts! Delicious!
Loved Jalapeño grits. Beet salad was incredible tasty! 
Bread pudding a must! Pomegranate mixed drink was delicious until server suggested we stir. He was wrong. Extremely biter. Moved to French 75 after.. much better.

I just came back to New Orleans for another Mardi Gras and this was my FAVORITE dinner. Despite the fact that it was Mardi Gras, they got us in relatively quickly and the bar was open for drinks. Our service was incredible from the moment we walked in the door. 

For dinner, I ordered BBQ shrimp and the Brussels sprouts. The shrimp wasn't the best bbq I've ever had but it was pretty good. The Brussels Sprouts has the entire table talking about them for days. It was incredible!

If you're in NOLA, stop by here for a more upscale dinner. You won't be disappointed.

I've been to New Orleans a hand full of times and feel like I've tried to tackle the best things to eat here scene so when I say I think Luke is one of, if not the best meals I've ever eaten in Nola that's pretty high praise. 

Booked a dinner rez here not really knowing if we'd keep it or not but more as a we are booked in somewhere for dinner instead of having to try to secure something last minute. 

We were staying super close which made walking over a non issue, even in dinner attire (I say this mainly for the women in heels ;) we did uber to/from our after dinner location since I wasn't in flats hahaha) back to dinner... pretty much blew my mind or shall I say palate. 

We started with a half dozen of p&j gulf raw oysters which I've never had in life so this was a game changer night from the jump. I actually really enjoyed these and would totally order them again here. I think having a "first" experience and it going this well always sets the right tone for a meal. 

We shared the most amazing bisque soup I think I've ever had which makes enjoying turtle soup and gumbo in this city nearly feel like they are only second best to Luke's bisque. 

Then it was onto the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" shrimp and grits dish and our incredible server brought the heartiest of samplers of their Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp & Crab "Étouffée" when we couldn't decide on which entree to share. 

After our dining experience the night prior and totally over ordering our server was the absolute best and understood we wanted to pace ourselves and be able to enjoy meal after meal during this trip without wasting things or having to bring meals back to our hotel fridge to sit in styrofoam. 

He steered us to the best dish to order being the shrimp and grits which is the absolute most correct answer. This dish is mind blowing with flavor in each and every single bite. The etouffee is also amazing, less flavor I'd say but the cripsy rice is one of those things you just need to experience, very yummy! 

We shared the Carrot Cake blondie sundae with cream cheese ice cream, butterscotch whiskey sauce and candied carrots, nice finishing touch to the meal. 

The service and atmosphere was perfection, really exactly what you'd want for a nice dinner out in New Orleans and even if you're a local I can see this being a great go-to option for the most yummy meal. I think what was most shocking in the very best way, was the bill... this meal was outstanding and other than us ordering a bottle of wine that cost nearly as much as our meal the price point is so reasonable for such amazing quality and service. 

Cannot wait to return and will surely recommend to anyone looking for one of the best meals in New Orleans. Luke is bar none, one of them!

I went in today and got very lucky. I immediately pulled into an empty stall, and three cars pulled up behind me. So right away, I was in a good mood.

I got greeted by Joshua and explained that I needed an oil change, and my battery checked.

Joshua and Leo looked at my Nissan Armada, and Joshua came back inside and explained what I needed (a new battery) and what he recommended. He also recommended a few things that I will need in about 10,000 miles.

About 30 minutes later, they finished the service, and the battery swapped out.

Because of the military discount that Jiffy Lube offers, I saved $50 off my total. Between that and Joshua's knowledge and professionalism, I will make this Jiffy Lube my go-to shop from now on.

I'll say it: I'd switch teams for John Besh. 

Restaurant August was already among my favorite restaurants in the nation, and Luke is a casual alternative that offers up an entirely different but equally tasty view into New Orleans food. 

For one thing -- and let's be serious: probably the most important thing -- they make an EXCELLENT burger. It is massive (and shareable according to some), covered in caramelized onions, Allan Benton's bacon, caramelized and Emmenthaler Swiss cheese. And although the brioche bun stands up well, it's unavoidably messy when cooked to a juicy medium rare. Our bartender friend informed us that this particular burger was chosen as 8th in the nation; I'm not sure by whom, but I'm not mad I got it, just mad I'm not on the committee. 

The shrimp and grits are also apparently a specialty of the house. We were told that they do them a bit differently than most places; as far as I can tell, they just cook the shrimp perfectly, and make the sauce good enough to drink. 

I was a bit disappointed that the fries were cooked past crispy into crunchy territory, but the lady on my left loved them all the same. For me though, the only downsides were said fries and the fact that their bloody mary is merely a mix (although I do like the Gator Blood), and they don't provide a spicy bean. Sacrilegious, I know, but give them a chance to make it up to you with the food.
