Came here for lunch with my family and it did not disappoint. Their lunch specials are super reasonable. I had a sushi & sashimi lunch which consisted of 3 pieces of nigiri, 7 pieces of sashimi and a salmon roll for only $14. Did I mention their lunch specials also come with soup & salad?

Despite the fact that it was busy, our food came out in a timely manner. I only knocked a star off because our waters were never refilled and nobody was to be found when my grandmother wanted more hot water for her tea. Other than that, it was a great dining experience. I wish sushi was this affordable in San Francisco.

First time in New Orleans and I got to say this is the best place to go! Mouth watering food/drinks and AMAZING service :) Our server Richie Rich made our dining experience even more enjoyable! Make sure to see if he's working #Nashville/CaliGurlz

HH 3-6 75cent oysters, half off drinks. 

I loved Luke's when I was visiting NOLA. Came with a group of 8 and they were extremely accommodating. No wait at 4 pm! Who can beat 75 cent oysters?! Given there are places who sell em for 50cents a piece, but are they as good?? Maybe next trip. These raw oysters were definitely better than Acme. 

Anyway, the pate was one of best pates I've ever had. I prefer to eat it with the table bread rather than the crispy bread given with it. The fried oysters were sooo mouth watering. It was perfectly crispy and evenly battered. The quail was delicious as well! The bread pudding was okay imo. Maybe I was too full to indulge.

I'm happy I got to stop by 3 of John Besh's restaurants while visiting.

Ok.  This is a tough one to write... I love this place, love the food, love the room.  I've partied a bunch with the kitchen team.  Awesome people.   But as one of the very first men to embrace the #metoo movement, I feel obliged to give the lowest ranking.

I was SUPER early to #metoo.  Probably one of the original people.  I remember liking a Twitter post from an actress I used to date (don't want to name names, but solid B-list celeb... used to be A list when she was younger).  Before long I saw the hashtag more and more, and I eventually even retweeted a few posts.  

So when I saw that the ownership of Luke was engulfed in the #metoo controversy, I felt I needed to replace my old 5 star review.

This is a good restaurant for french food & those who like seafood. 

Be forewarned, if you go to this place wanting items off the breakfast menu, they only serve breakfast Mon-Fri - not on the weekends. 

The service was great, the atmosphere was welcoming & the restaurant itself was clean.
Went for Happy Hour after work. Oysters and drinks great way to end the week! Bartenders weren't too friendly but the servers were. Definitely going back.

The starters & soups eehhhh you can do without. We weren't a fan of the BBQ P&J oysters at all. Not your "traditional" New Orleans Oysters at all. Shrimp & Grits -  by far the BEST shrimp & grits ever! The waffle was great also. The champagne in the mimosa is a better quality also. Doesn't give you that bloated feeling afterwards. Overall great experience.

Horrible service. I don't know if we did something to cross somebody but we scarcely saw our servers. We spent almost three hours there and most of it was spent waiting. Also -- this place is super noisy. It would benefit them to add something insulating. I don't know. Uninspired ambience. It really felt like we were eating in a bar. And that would maybe be okay if some other aspect of the meal had blown us away but the food was only just adequate. And at the end of the night, thread messed up our bill so we had to wait to flag down our sever and wait again for a new bill. This was my very first meal in NOLA and I'm disappointed. At minimum, I won't be back. Photos of food included because it wasn't bad, so there's that.

All the staff is super friendly and attentive. The oysters were good and the happy hour is a great deal. I was also surprised with birthday bread pudding on the house. Everything was great, but I docked off one star because the plates and glasses were stained from probably just being put in a dishwasher and not being properly washed.

Came for happy hour and it did not disappoint. Our server was great and the food/drinks were amazing! Best Oysters my sisters and I had in NOLA. Sad to see we were the only ones here. We definitely came at a quiet time during Covid and possible storms. Looking forward to come back and visit NOLA when life goes back to normal a little. Will def be coming back here!
It was so beautiful and delicious! Wandeful place and nice interior I had breakfast omelet with octopus and coffee, I was happy

My wife and I came across this restaurant by accident and I was happy that it happened. We were trying to get into a restaurant off of Bourbon Street in the French Quarters. All the restaurants had over a hour wait time and we were starving.
So we wondered around outside of the French Quarters until we came across Luke. 
They were able to seat us right away and their service was speedy. The food was fricking great and we've never had Cajun food before. We shared the Seafood Gumbo which was yummy with shrimp, sausage and oysters. My wife had the Shrimp and Grits and I had the Truffle Glazed Roasted Chicken. Must have the Pudding Bread for dessert.

THE SERVICE IS AWESOME! 


I came here on a Friday night to catch the end of happy hour and get some dinner. Our server was Richie Rich and let me tell you, he was the most considerate, kind, and funny server I have had in a while. While the food was good by itself (the brussel sprouts were delicious!!) the service made the evening!  Rich gave great food suggestions, served with efficiency and speed, and made us laugh the entire night! We will be coming back just to see him!!

I was a guest at Hilton and this restaurant was located onsite. First impressions: I was not asked what I wanted as I sat, not even water, just an empty glass at the table. I had to ask an employee cleaning a table to help me get the waiter. So not a great first impression. When I placed the order, it did arrive quick which was a plus. I had the crawfish etouffee. At first sight, I was disappointed at the quantity for the price. Was really small and I was done eating in like 2 minutes. Lol. However the taste was alright. I also had to ask about the dessert, waiter did not offer or ask if I was interested in dessert. However I loved the bread pudding. The cold Ice cream and warm pudding made for a nice melt in my mouth. If you like pecans, you'd love the crunch as well. I loved the ponchatoula punch. Well balanced and sweet. Rating 3 stars because I don't think I got a bang for my buck with the entree and the customer service was less than ideal.

Horrible !! My a true rating is zero stars.  How the tech mess up your real nail and then when she slops a crap load of acrylic on top - she then blame your nails  that she jacked up !!! Horrible customer service. Tech do not listen when you attempt to correct her. Please do not go here !

It's a little weird reviewing this John Besh restaurant after the sexual harassment allegations. We went before then so my how times have changed. We specifically came here to try Besh's food on a Sunday brunch.

The two of us shared the brussel sprouts appetizers, a cup of gumbo and the shrimp and grits. The waitress of course told us it was the best shrimp and grits in town. That's a pretty big statement in this town! Everything, including the shrimp and grits, were pretty good. What really surprised me was how tasty the brussel sprouts were! If you're not a sweet sauce fan, you might not like it as much but I loved the flavor and texture.

I was really looking forward to my burrito but was very disappointed. I found the pork very bland and tasteless.  There was an overwhelming tomato flavour, I don't know if it was the salsa, rice or beans but it was all I could taste - watery tomato. With a small tip and adding cheese and guacamole it came to $15.00 which I would have had no problem paying if the burrito was tasty rather than speedy. Unlike the other Black Box businesses this is not one I will be returning to.

Ate and licked everything Off the plate. This place was a Last minute find for my husband and I. Glad we found this place. My husband got a hamburger and finished the whole burger without offering me a bite..(he usually shares but that's how good it was) 

The service was top notch too. Everyone there was on top of the service and was very nice.

This is one of John Besh's more "casual" restaurants, so there's no formal dress code. I've come here many, many times over the years during their happy hour. I've eaten at plenty of other oyster happy hours but Luke's really does have the best raw oysters in town. It's every day (even Saturdays & Sundays!) from 3-6 PM. It's .75/oyster now I believe. Their oysters are always well-cleaned, fresh, with just the right amount of brine and REALLY good. I can easily finish off a couple dozen on my own with room for more. I've never had a gritty oyster from here before which I've had at other places and hate. Ask for the red vinegar sauce to go with the oysters! Their select cocktails are also half off during the happy hour.

Aside from the oysters, I've tried a few other dishes here and my other favorite is the Luke burger. It's served atop a cutting board with crispy shoestring fries in a metal pail. If you tell the server you're sharing it, they'll even split the portions for you which is super nice of them. I love the super cute condiments they bring out with the burger. I had a very rude server once a few years back but aside from that one incident, service is usually really good and consistent. I must make a return visit soon!

My favorite chipotle in town. Yeah I live downtown and there are like 4 chipotles closer to me. I enjoy biking the Monon and usually I stop by there if I'm heading to Carmel. 

I've always had good experiences and feel like they give bigger portions than the one in downtown. The food is hot and fast and never really have a long line.

Happy hour every day!!!!! Not that I care about the drinks, but the 75 cent oysters are what I'm coming for. Initially, I was extremely annoyed as the hostess made a joke at our expense to another set of diners. However as soon as we told her we were just there to sit at the bar she was much nicer *eye roll*

We were tended to by a great bartender who was helpful in recommending some appetizers. After we placed our order for 2 dz oysters (no shame here), we also decided to go for the pate of Louisiana rabbit and chicken livers. This. Was. Amazing!!!!!!!!!!! The oysters of course were excellent - nice and meaty! Not only did we get near 30 of them on our plate, the shuckers gave us a few extra after we were done! I noticed they did that to pretty much everyone at the bar. Extra points for them!

Overall a great experience and I would not hesitate to come back for happy hour!

I have been going to 7 oaks for 7 years. I've loved this facility, but in the past few years it seems just money driven. I have had a wellness plan for 7 yrs but today when I went in they wanted to charge me a fee. I told them I was on the wellness plan and they said it expired in January when I actually had renewed it. The staff member had failed to activate it but now they wanted to hold me responsible for a new sign up fee. I was so upset. Lady went out and came back and said they could reduce it by 15 dollars. I refused and said I would just rather leave. Well after an hour they eventually gave me a renewal for no fee. There was never an apology and when the vet came in it was rushed and no real interest in my pet. I'm really sad and don't think I would have signed up again had we not been in a middle of a pandemic and did not want to ride around looking for a new vet. It's a shame when businesses get too big to stay interested
Sushi is okay. You really don't get your moneys worth. They stuff it with vegetables and charge you a fortune for vegetables. You can get so much better for your money.

This review was solely based on our experience during their happy hour. 

We made reservations for Luke's happy hour before our dinner for more seafood nearby -- and boy did we have a good time. Our table of five ordered three rounds of raw oysters (.75/ea), a round of fried oysters (1.25/ea), brussel sprouts, and a couple orders of their stuffed oysters and plenty of drinks. All of their drink were half off (excluding bottled wine).

Raw oysters = to die for, Fried oysters = so good (not even a fan of fried oysters), brussel sprouts = stole the show -- perfect blend of crispy salty brussel sprouts with sweet honey surprises and crunchy slivered almond bites, and the stuffed oysters = ugh, so good. 

Drinks: Definitely get their Gintilly Dragon and the French 75. Also if you love tequila like me, get it! it was amazing! 

Great food and drinks and great atmosphere.

Definitely a mustEats! Best Shrimp & Grits & Crab Au Gratin I've ever had and I don't even like Shrimp or Grits! Delicious Brussels Sprouts, Corn/Crab Bisque & drinks had generous alcohol pour too. Atmosphere is nice, old southern, home some vibe. Ask for Chi Che to be your Server!‍ #hellohelloeats #eattheworld #foodporn #musteat #livetoeat #eatswithlovedones #withmybb#icjourneys #eatwithcin #flexitarian #ourchoice #NOLA

This review is for their donut! They specialize in brioche donuts. The guy taking my money said the dough takes 24 hours to prep. Well, I don't care how you make it, as long as it tastes good and you don't charge me an arm and a leg for a donut, I'm good. I tried the original and my husband tried the one with salt. Both were very good and substantial in size. I like that they were not overly sweet or covered in exuberant amount of icing. They are on the pricier side but not as expensive as some other places in town. I would definitely stop by once in a while for a donut if I'm craving one.

As soon as you pull into the parking lot you can smell the fresh bread! It was pretty empty inside and there was no line. I ordered the green eggs and ham sandwich while my boyfriend ordered the philly sandwich. my sandwich came on a perfectly flaky croissant and i couldn't stop talking about it. The philly came on an amazing pretzel bread. Home girl loves bread. 

I also ordered a cappuccino and it came on a cute wood board served with sparkling water and 2 chocolate beans! by the time we left there was a line out the door! i guess we came at just the right time! I loved the ambiance of the cafe and the food was so impeccable! next time i come back to st. louis this will be my first stop!!

Last summer I hit a bad pothole and blew my tire out. The next day I drove it to Meineke to get it checked out because it was the closest place to my apartment. They said the tire was ruined and I needed a replacement. Let it be known I had 4 brand new Goodyear tires put on in February last year. Not knowing much about cars, I thought I'd leave it in the hands of professionals, but that was a BIG MISTAKE. They put on a cheap-o brand tire that had lower treads and was completely different from my other tires. Left it on the front! I just got done having another tire replaced (from hitting yet another pot hole) at the original place I got the new tires (Sam's club). They said they had to replace the odd tire because it was dangerous to leave it on... when they took it off, it was plugged in the weakest spot. I was charged over $200 for this cheap USED tire from this scam of a business! Unless you know what you're talking about when it comes to cars, do NOT come here because they will take advantage of you and rip you off!!!

Ordered delivery, so that's why I'm giving the benefit of the doubt with three stars. 
Got the southwest chicken egg rolls and garlic buffalo wings. 

Egg rolls were good, but still so greasy. Like they had gone straight from the oil to the takeout container.

Wings were super weird. I think they use tempura rather than regular flour. The sauce was just buffalo, nothing garlic-y about it. 

Solid meh. Maybe I'll try again and actually eat in the restaurant.

Perfectly sized (i.e. Not enormous) coffee and delicious baked goods. Being surrounded by the smell of baking bread sure doesn't hurt either. I really like the space, the outdoor seating, and the service as well. Hooray Companion!

The donuts here are delicious - interesting flavors, not overly saccharine. But what is up with the hours? 9am for donuts and coffee? And I have to be honest, the experience here can be obnoxiously pretentious (it's donuts and hot dogs, not a three star Michelin dining experience - do we really need a meticulous verbal breakdown of every ingredient and the brioche process every time we come in? - this is particularly annoying when the line is long). Couldn't there just be signage with the donut contents???

As soon as you go up to the counter, you're greeted by awesome staff who are eager to explain the concept to anyone new. The donuts are brioche, which ties into the buns used for their hotdogs. 

They have some exciting options flavor-wise for both, though I only had a hotdog. The Mexican-food inspired hotdog was amazing, with corn and cotija cheese over a chorizo hot dog. The seasoned fries were super thing and crispy with just the right amount of spice.

This was my first visit, but NOT my last. I ordered the ZuZu's chicken sandwich. Superb! I managed to eat half. I'll finish later for a midnight snack. Difficult to park. Only a few seats for eating at the counter. I can't wait to try this place again.

The caramel pecan sticky buns are the best I've ever had, period. They are amazing. The only problem is that other people have figured this out and they sometimes sell out before I get there. Their brookies are phenomenal too - soft and moist all the way through with an impossibly thin and delicate crust that gives it just a little bit of crunch when you bite into it. I'm sure everything else they make is fantastic as well, but the caramel pecan rolls are so good I can't ever bring myself to get anything else.

This is not your ordinary buffet! At Iron Sheet you can find the typical Chinese foods found on a buffet line, but they also flirt with the more exotic. I was able to sample pigs ear's, a variety of delicious tofu dishes, chicken feet and pig's feet. While these are by no means extremely exotic foods, they are not commonly seen on buffets. If you want to eat at a "buffet" yet sample what could be considered specialty dishes of the house, this is the place for you.

Could use a makeover, a clean-up day, maybe another interior decorater but nonetheless the coffee is great. The pastries in the pastry case is often scarce but when it's not I always have to get a chocolate croissant which is amazing, it's almost like nutella in the inside when it's warmed.

Had another great experience at Sun Sushi last night, so I can confirm that there actually is good sushi in SB... finally. The box sushi was really good, we considered ordering a second order of it. The albacore was so fresh, we got it in sushi form as well as roll form. Good edamame too, which is always a good sign for a sushi restaurant (how can you make good sushi if you can't even make good edamame?).
The spicy tuna on crispy rice was 4/5 stars, I've had better but it was good and would order again.

I had really good sushi there with my friends. Everything was so fresh and delicious! Me and my friends loved so much. Especially their cheese cakes which import from Japan was so good!    Highly recommend this restaurant. I definitely will come back with my friends soon! Don't miss out if you love Japanese food.

We finally got out to try Sun Sushi - so glad we did! This place definitely lives up to its reviews. 

I had the salmon 6-steps, and in addition to the killer presentation, I found the fish itself to be just perfect. Really fresh, cut just right (I am so picky about that), with correctly prepared and sized rice ball. 

My husband ordered the box sushi roll and the Albacore Delight roll. He said the Albacore roll was good but the box sushi was completely out of this world amazing, and gave me a bite so I could agree with him. Yes, it was, and I'll order it next time! For those who have been to Sakana and are hooked on their box sushi - this is a great alternative.

My daughter got the chef's choice sushi - 10 pieces of whatever the chef thought was best. This was pretty incredible, and I'm sorry for not grabbing a photo. There was no skimping on it as some restaurants try to do - no, this had all the premium nigiri: toro, uni, jumbo shrimp, two kinds of premium yellowtail... The birthday girl was suitably impressed with her order and even more excited when the waitress surprised her with tempura green tea ice cream at the end of the meal.

One of the highlights of the service here is that the servers take the time, when they bring your order, to point out and tell you what each thing on your plate is. So if you aren't enough of a sushi expert to be able to tell what everything is at a glance, never fear!
I definitely recommend this place - a little pricier but totally worth the spend, and it comes with great service and a pleasant, traditional atmosphere.

I have to say that it is by far the cheapest way from downtown to the airport. That being said, it is understandable why it is so cheap. If I could rate my safety radar from 1 - 5, 1 being safe and 5 being on super high alert, I would rate the ride at a 4.5. The whole time I felt like someone was going to stick a gun in my face and ask for my belongings. 

When I got on the metrolink at the airport, a guy kept looking up and down the isle and walking in and out of the metrolink. He was not a security guard 4 sure also. Thank God he didn't stay on when it left.. Then a few stops down a bunch of shady people got on and it didn't stop there. Every stop after was even more. Mind you, there were some normal people that got one but I would say 75% is shady. 

Tip: When you go to the airport. Don't bring a lot of cash with you. Also if you have a cellphone or precious things, I advise you to make them hidden.

So I met my family at Argentos in Hudson for my fathers birthday this past Saturday night. The restaurant was packed we didnt have to wait to long for a table. The air conditioning wasnt working properly inside the restaurant we were very hot and uncomfortable throughout our dinner. The dinner rolls were great with the house marina, we also ordered the fried calamari appetizer it was AWESOME! Our server felt to us like she was just having a bad night, we had to continously ask for refills and get her attention. Our dinner salads were very large and the blue cheese dressing taste homemade. I was not thrilled with my chicken noodle soup, it tasted like it just came out of a can. I went ahead and followed the advise of the other YELP reviews of this restaurant and ordered the chicken parm. it was very tasty but I thought it was alittle bit over priced at $15 a plate, my fiance ordered the seafood zupree it was very good but again not to sound picky but it could of had just a little bit more seafood for the $18 dinner price. The pizza was great and tasted very close to the NY style pizza I am used to coming from the Northeast. Overall a great and fulling meal! I wish thea/c system was working properly, and I wished the pastry shop had fresher pastries and a more courteous staff member working the pastry counter, she wasnt friendly at all!!! I think I would go back once more if I was in the area to give the restaurant another shot.

Back for lunch. The sandwiches are ok, the cashier, possibly new, wasn't on top of things. I think I'll stick with the breakfast sandwiches. 4 stars for breakfast, 3 for lunch and pastries.

1 star for the stools, can't scoot in or scoot out of them. They look cool but don't function too well.

I visited Tucson and was so pleased to find an OTF right around the corner from where I was staying! The instructor was great and the gal at the front desk was helpful - my pod was not working and she made sure I was up and running before class started with a loaner pod while she tried to figure out what was up with mine.
Best atmosphere. Best hot dogs. Best beer. Best donuts. The donut + dog is our favorite spot in Nashville. Hands down.

I never expected St. Louis to have good transit. You'd think we're just too small a city for it. But I was wrong. St Louis has a very comprehensive bus service and a very high-quality light rail service, in the few places that it goes. Unfortunately, for reasons that are mostly out of Metro's hands, I feel very uncomfortable on public transit in St. Louis. MOST passengers keep quiet and are just trying to get where they need to go, but there are always some loud/obnoxious passengers, crazy people, beggars, and shady characters. This is most pronounced in Metrolink in the rear cars because the driver cannot see/hear there, and there is rarely a security guard.

As for the service, Metrolink has astoundingly good on-time performance. Now, it shouldn't be hard to be on time when each train is 10-20 minutes apart, but this is the US and you should not expect ANYTHING when it comes to transit. To avoid waiting too long in the Metrolink stations, be sure to reference the timetable, and trust it. I don't think I've ever had a Metrolink that arrived even a minute late.

Busses, on the other hand, are quite often late. This is much harder to control since they have to ride through traffic. If it's late at night, or any other time when traffic is smooth, you can trust the timetables, but otherwise, prepare for a 15-30 minute wait. 

I do own a car, so I don't use metro too often. I generally only use it to go to the airport (beats the heck out of Super Park) and maybe to go downtown or to the Delmar Loop where parking is atrocious. Since I'm an infrequent rider, I make use of the $3 2-hour pass. I always keep a few on hand. They will accept them on the bus (if you start on the bus, they will keep the ticket and trade you for a transfer slip). It's much better than needing to keep $3 exact cash on hand. Soon we will have smart cards and that's even better.

Summary: Trust the rail timetables, don't trust the bus timetables, and know your surroundings.

My friend lives directly across the street, so when we wanted to have a Girls Night In and eat a lot of food and watch a movie, Zuzu's seemed like the perfect option.  And it definitely was.  We walked across the street to order and waited for our food.  It didn't take long at all and while waiting there, we were able to really see how important this local business is to the neighborhood.  Neighborhood kids were bopping in and out, people were picking up orders, they seemed to be regulars, addressing Zu (the owner) by name.  I love the little quirks of this place; there is a beautifully decorated wall with a take one, leave one book system...I'll attach a pic!

I really love that small business feel and I love supporting local spots just like this one.  The food was great and the service was excellent.  I got a chicken cheesesteak and we split cheese fries.  It is also very affordable.  

This spot is located next to Lorraine's in Fairmount.  It's small with some seating inside, but would probably be best to take your food to go.  I recommend this spot and I will definitely be back!

I love this Cracker Barrel. When I go, I usually get the Meatloaf dinner or the country ham (which I must say is AHHHMAZING!) with green beans, mashed potatoes, and turnip greens. YUM! This is the typical country restaurant, but better. The food comes out fast and hot, but it tastes like it's been cooked slow, just like Grandma makes it. Everything on the menu is really good. As for the servers, I guess it just depends on the day you go, because some have been really short and ill-tempered, and some are really friendly and talkative. And I just HAVE to mention the manager. He makes me day everytime I go there. He walks around and asks everyone he can how they are and he says "Absolutely, absolutely!" He's one of those people that will instantly give you a good mood if you're down and out. The store side is VERY clean, and I love the old-timey decorations hanging all over the place. This Cracker Barrel location is my go-to for when I'm having a southern soul food craving :)
Of ALL the sushi restaurants I've been too this place to me has by far the greatest service, price, quality and preparation of food, environment, and people of all time. G.O.A.T.

The quality of the fresh fish here is worth 5 stars alone. It is rare to find fish this fresh in the area. I originally came here because I heard they have ocean trout, but the freshness of the tuna, salmon, etc. is going to keep me coming back. This was one of the best sushi dinners that I've had in awhile. I recommend the salmon sushi, ocean trout sushi, and avocado eel roll.

Terrrrrrrrible. Nothing was fresh. Food was soggy. They do have those single little ice cream cups which are neat because I haven't had one of those since summer camp. You know the ones I'm talking about, the little styrofoam single cup little guys?  Haha great. 1 star for you.
Campfire chicken was a great home cooked meal to eat with being away from home...the service was good also!

Arrived at 11:15am for lunch. A few other patrons seated waiting for there food. We were a table of 5 and once we ordered we found a table. After seated with our number it took them 20 min. to get are drinks out to us. After another 10 min. we noticed that the patrons that were before us hadn't received there food. After another 20min. They delivered 3 out of 5 sandwiches I looked at 1 of the 3 and asked which sandwich that was. He looked at me with no clue. The reason I asked was it was a piece of chicken with a bun. I had order The pit with no BBQ and added buffalo sauce. Sent it back for them to slap a piece of provel (not even melted)  poured BBQ sauce and I don't think the bacon even made it in the sandwich but they came back out with it. Sent it back again. Finally when they got it right it was cold , over cooked, , and found a bone in it. My sons chicken tenders were fried for so long you couldn't even taste the chicken. After another 20 min. the 4th sandwich came out and wasn't what she had ordered. Finally after the 4 of us were done my husband's sandwich came out. 

Plus they weren't even busy. There were only 4 other tables and us. Absolutely awful! They won't last long if they don't get there act together. Poor quality! Poor Service! I would rather eat at Chic A Fila!!!! By the way I walked out at 12:40pm. 1 hour and 25min. With a total of 5 tables !

Recently opened you're emerged into such a warm inviting place with a great back story. You'll have to visit to read about it (;

We were greeted right upon arrival and were given an overview of the menu. Did I mention they have donuts infused with alcohol!!!!

Unfortunately we just bought a bunch of fudge so skipped out on the donuts but they looked amazing.

We both went with the power lunch which is daily from 11-4. Any dog, fries and drink for $9.95. What a deal!

We got the Elote Loco and Flying Hawaiian. They were both fantastic, but I did take a few extra bites of my boyfriends Hawaiian. 

You order at a counter and the food is brought to you, but the person who took our order was courteous enough to come by and make sure everything is to our liking. Don't remember her name, but she's from California.

This is such a quaint delicious place I can see it being around for a long time.

Excellent food married to an excellent concept kitchen. It appears that the kitchen serves a few purposes: training for bakers, and providing food to other local places. There may be others. But I was blown away at the idea...eliminating waste by selling products in your store and through distribution. Not to mention the food was excellent. I had an egg and bacon sandwich on an everything bagel. It was very good. But, a tad pricey. I'll be returning however.

The best sushi in town. Hands down. Forget Arigato on State St. 

Best thing you can do is sit at the bar and have a conversation with the chef while directly ordering from him. 

Also try the cold sake. Just superb. This is now my go-to spot in Santa Barbara.

This is a jewel. You will LOVE sun sushi in Santa Barbara.  Strip center sushi place that flies sushi in from Japan.  Do not shy away from "today's tsukiji".  You will not be disappointed.  Enjoy it along with the Aji and an Asahi draft.
This restaurant seems to ALWAYS be busy. That's a good sign but I am too impatient to wait an hour to eat Cracker Barrel. Never had a bad meal though.

The name of this place drew me to it. It's a beautiful location, though its large size surprised me. The interior was also a surprise as a majority of the space is a glassed-in baking area with large-scale bread making happening.

In the common area, there are tables and a deli-style counter with lovely baked goods displayed from which you can select, or you can order a meal, soup, sandwich, coffee etc. The gentleman who served me was very helpful and kind and explained the story of his koi tattoo. He later stopped by and talked to me about my art and shared some of his. He circulated every so often and spoke to patrons.

I had a butter bar since I practically worship butter and couldn't pass up the opportunity to try this: crunchy on the bottom, buttery in the middle with a lovely caramel finish on top. My americano was perfect too.

I loved a gleaming metal wall along one side of the cafe but it took me a while to realize the gleaming metal was layers upon layers of baking sheets. The interior has an industrial/rustic look. A mash up.
Interest menu for 6 different salmons and tuna sushi! Friendly waiter and nice price!

What part of fast food don't they get? All I ordered was three drinks and we waited twenty minutes. By the time we did receive our order we had lost most of our appetite do to the very strong dumpster smell coming from the interior of the restaurant. To top it off I got attitude from the young lady that worked the drive thru just because I asked for napkins. to clean around the drinks that dripping on the side of the cups. I know it's just McDonald's but it's just my time and money.

Their lunch special is a good deal. Slightly on the pricier side but I think it was worth the money. For $9.95 you get a hot dog in a bun/toast they make in house, house chips or house fries and a drink. If you come at a certain time around lunch. Otherwise, each hot dog alone is $9.95 and it's an a la carte menu. I think they would be very wise to just make a permanent meal option and do away with the lunch special. Like, have the original style hot dogs as a meal to satisfy the masses and the gourmet ones sold at the full price to satisfy the boujie adventurers.. But hey, it's not my business. Just a happy customer with too much to say. 

I ordered their Bahn Mi dog and it was really good. I had actually ordered house chips to go with that but for some reason I got stuck with the fries. It's not a big deal but I really wanted to try the house chips. If I could take a half star I would but you can't. So 5 stars it is. 

It's a family run business. Wife & husband team, with a little one hanging around somewhere. I'm totally ok with that. The kid is going to grow up seeing their parents work hard and hopefully take from them and be a successful entrepreneur one day. So yeah, I like their customer service. They're very sweet. 

Would return again, but only during the lunch special hours. As I can't see myself paying $20 for two hotdogs. The Yankee inside me would just slap me across the face!
Awesome donuts and coffee doesn't begin to do this justice. You have to check it out to experience it. Can't wait to come back for the dogs...maybe in a few hours.

I love Cracker Barrel. I love it, love it, love it. I know, it's a chain and I'm supposed to be too cool for chains, but sometimes a good thing spreads and expands because it's good. Cracker Barrel have, amazingly, managed to keep it consistent and good. 

Things I adore about Cracker Barrel: 

1. Stuff to look at while you wait
2. You can buy Goo Goo Clusters
3. Hash brown casserole
4 Hash brown casserole
5. The biscuits and the best biscuit gravy anywhere
6. The coffee

I also love that you can make a platter out of four sides - the turnip greens are to die for, and the homestyle chicken meal (only available on Sundays) is amazing - plan to share it with someone or take some home because it is massive!

I'm kind of disappointed that they stopped giving you the slice of orange with breakfast - I always thought that was a nice touch, and yes Cracker Barrel, I did notice; however, I'll forgive you because everything else is just so amazingly delicious!

I love this place! I live a couple blocks from here, so I've been more than a couple times. The guy who is always there is so nice! The one thing I really like about this place is they cook over a grill, not a flat top griddle. Also, they really put love into their food... roasted peppers are roasted in house, not from a jar, burgers are hand made.... They have pizza as well, which is reallyyy good,  the crust is crisp and not soggy and over loaded  like a lot of other places on Fairmount and always different varieties available. I wouldn't  put this under the pizza place category,  they are doing so much more! Hummus and pita great! Grilled chicken with home made pesto over roasted peppers and fresh mozzarella- sooo good! Chicken cheesesteak  french fries  burger. And the place is simple and cute inside !  Thanks Zuzu's!!!!
I found the donut, to be better than a dog! Yes! It was very good! Busy this time of year but will be returning. Relatively inexpensive. Filling but keep in mind.... LOTS OF SUGAR

This little sushi spot is under new management or something. It is DEFINITELY worth trying! Super dank! So good! A MUST try! I had the Box Sushi, a salmon roll, and two pieces (1 order) of ikura sushi.  Love the traditional and authentic style.
I was visiting from NJ and decided to squeeze in a few classes. I'm so glad I did. Grant is an awesome trainer, and the staff is very pleasant. Thank you for being so welcoming.

It was my 1st time here at Meineke and it wasn't a bad experience at all. I went for a oil chance and they recommended I get breaks cause my pads were very low so I did so. The service was pretty quick too, I'm very much satisfied I'll be back.
A little pricy for a chicken salad sandwich on a crescent but tasty & fresh just the same. We plan to go back & try the sweets!

I drive past this place everyday but didn't discover this gem until very recently. I've been there a couple times now getting to try a lot of their lunch items, sandwiches, and soups and most have been very delicious. 

A lot of the standard sandwiches are pretty much exactly what they sound like. A standard roast beef, turkey, chicken sandwich etc, but everything is high quality and fresh. The items that stood out to me was the New Yawker, a salmon bagel, and the cornbread. The portions are decently sized so you will most likely be getting full from a full sandwich or soup / sandwich combo. 

They have different soups each day and the full sized salads are a ton of food as well.

Definitely will be back.

What a hidden gem! The place itself is small and a bit out of the way, but they are on Grubhub, so it was super easy for me to order delivery. The food was very tasty for the price point. 

Zuzu's Salad ($7.99) is like an oasis of leafy deliciousness. It consisted of spring mix topped with avocado, cherry tomatoes, chickpeas, artichoke, and sunflower seeds. Although $7.99 is not extremely cheap, it was HUGE, and was restaurant-quality, not just some iceberg lettuce bullsh*t from shady corner shops. 

I also got an order of boneless garlic parmesan wings ($8.49) which was clearly made from real chicken, with a very crispy crust. The one drawback about this item is that it was a bit oily (quite drippy), but other than that, it was delicious. 

I also ordered Zuzu's burger ($6.99!) which was ridiculous (-ly tasty!) I don't know why anyone would bother to go to Shake Shack and eat their fast-food quality burgers when they can get a restaurant-quality burger from here for the same price. Zuzu's burger comes with provolone cheese, chipotle truffle mayo, and is topped with both a fried egg and a crispy onion ring. 

All this might sound like a lot of food for one meal -- it is! But it made for great leftovers. I ended up spending only a bit over $20 for three meals-worth of great food. Not sure I can do this anywhere else in the neighborhood. Zuzu's Special Pizza sounds amazing. Definitely ordering that next time I crave pizza!

We had taco Tuesday here. Phil is the best the beef tacos are lit! The other tacos are brilliant! The boom boom sauce is good  I recommend light boom boom. Chx avocado is cheaper than whole food and comes with avocado! The nachos were finger licking good! Shout out to Phil it's lit!

Well, apparently my first update was premature. My credit report showed that I still owed Century Link $12 even after I talked with an agent on May 30, 2017 who claimed that he zeroed out my account. Instead, the amount decreased from $138 to $12 BUT I had cancelled within their 30 day grace period. So, again, 9 months after I cancelled service WITHIN THE 30 DAY PERIOD I'm still being plagued by accusations that I owe money. As on May 30, the agent today said that she zeroed out the amount owed so we'll see.
Best pastries I've had. Home cooked taste. Fresh and hot. Wonderful owners with great conversation. Quaint place to sit and drink some hot coffee and fill your belly with sweetness.

Very relaxing, quaint stop in the Hillsboro village area. The donut recipes are unique and innovative and very well executed. They have a menu full of high end coffee, tea, and even craft beer to serve alongside your donut. The environment is relaxed and warm, and it's a great place to stop by!
Yes-an awesome attached bakery serving Kaldi's coffee. Fantastic and fresh baked goods with great java. Will be back, and worth the drive if you are nearby.

Enjoyed my 2nd time at Sun Sushi as much as the first time. The wait staff is attentive and helpful in helping you order their delicacies. They get fresh fish from Japan on Tuesdays and Fridays. The salmon 6 step(6 different ways on an attractive wooden step structure) was especially tasty. 2 thumbs up for the replacement of Ahi. They're all veterans of other Sushi places in SB and have added their own touch and flourish to a Sushi establishment.
The Lamb Burger is hands down the best burger I've ever had! The French fries were delicious and were a large portion. Very friendly people behind the counter. Best bang for your buck!

Trainers are awesome and keep you motivated to do your best. I definitely would not push myself this hard when working out at a regular gym. Upbeat music and different workouts to keep you motivated. Awesome place to workout!

worst internet provider in tucson arizona. dont ever get this internet. they have 1.5 stars for a reason. unfortunately i have no choice but to have this provider due to my location but its almost tempting me to move elsewhere... i run my internet of my cell phones hotspot and its way better. ill be cancelling my internet soon

Had the lamb special pizza and the lamb burger.  Both were great. I have had their chicken fingers and wings too, but neither were as good as the lamb items. I can't wait to try more off their menu. It's a great addition to the neighborhood.

I'm giving this place 5 stars on a realistic comparison to other buffets in this price range. With a coupon, my lunch was under $6 before the tip (which they actually deserved). I don't write a lot of reviews, but there wasn't a lot of feedback on this place and I figured they deserved a little recognition for their effort.

My favorite part was definitely the Mongolian grill, which the manager gave us thorough instruction on which sauces to use. Whatever I made on that grill was definitely the most savory, spicy, and flavorful dish in the restaurant. The pho station is a similar concept with raw ingredients you choose and they cook for you. I'm not a pho expert, but it tasted great and was a welcomed lighter dish than the rest of the buffet offerings. I was also impressed by their chicken wings. I'm not sure what the sauce was and they were a little small, but the flavor definitely made up for that. Just try them. I was happy to find potstickers on the line, which is not always offered at similar restaurants. I am choosing not to comment on the sushi since we came around 2pm and it wasn't being made fresh at the time.

Every employee I encountered was courteous and helpful. The atmosphere is welcoming and definitely new. They've also got plenty of space with private party rooms. Again, for the price, this place takes the top spot in my mind for atmosphere, value, variety, and taste.
I honestly didn't feel very safe. Some people that were very loud,  another talking about his gang,  and some shady characters. I was counting down the stops!!

I love Cracker Barrel.  We go at least once a month, and we've never had a bad meal, never had bad service, and never left hungry.  I love being able to get breakfast any time of day, and I frequently do.  My favorite is the smokehouse breakfast with their down-home biscuits and gravy.  I also love their pancakes with real maple syrup.  

For lunch, they have a bunch of country salads which are all good, as well as a selection of sandwiches.  My favorites are the grilled cheese with bacon and the steak biscuits.  For dinner, I love the chicken and dumplings, my wife loves their meatloaf, and my daughter's favorite is the catfish.

Wayyy overpriced for it being so unimpressive. The sushi pieces are very expensive but the quality of the fish and preparation don't match up to that price. It doesn't hit any mark. There is better sushi. There is cheaper sushi. And there are other places with more thrills. I'm not sure where this one fits in
Gyoza was crispy, my wife loved it. Service was attentive. Six step salmon was a delight and all flavors and textures were on point. Will be coming back.

This was my first visit at Companion. I quite enjoyed the atmosphere, and the food was alright; nothing I can complain about. But I did have a negative encounter with an employee-I wish I knew his name-that I'm assuming is supposed to tidy up the lobby. Well, with this being my first visit at Companion, I began to clean off my table, throwing away the trash and as I am doing so he yanks the plates out of my hands and exclaimed "I'M SUPPOSED TO GET THAT!".Someone takes their job a little too seriously if I do say so myself. Shame on this lad for the way he treated me. I will not be coming back until he is gone, not only because of the way he treated me, but he was very uncomfortable to watch the entire time I was eating.

Great yelp find! We were staying at the Sheraton nearby and needed to find a quick breakfast, so I pulled up yelp and picked Companion without much research. So glad I did! The food was to die for. My husband and I had the eggs, pumpkin cranberry toast, and a donut. Everything was so good! The employees were super friendly too. It's in a bit of a weird location, around a bunch of office parks, but definitely worth the trip.

I have lived around the corner from Zuzus for the past 2 years. I absolutely love this place. The owner is such a great guy. He really worked hard to get Zuzus to the where it is today. The workers are awesome. 

Now to the food: if you want something that is delicious, quick (usually only takes 10-15 min or less from the time you ordered), and a menu that will keep you coming back time and time again; go to ZUZUS!!

My friend and I got advice from guy (who works at Camarillo premium outlets "Nike" store) to stop by at this sushi place.
We came from Los Angeles to try this place. The staff was very friendly, we got served by Lucy, very very nice and friendly lady. She gave us advices what to pick.

My sister and I waited an hour last night for our Togo food only for it to come out wrong and cold, it was two orders of broccoli cheddar chicken, soup, and a hamburger so it shouldn't have been that hard. When we asked for a manager, Eric, he had the worst attitude, mocked us, and talked down to us. He wasn't even going to comp our meal but instead asked us if we wanted desert. When my sister asked for our money back he looked at us like we had offended him. We then waited 30 more minutes for our food to be reheated (not in the microwave, because he assured us they don't do that, yeah right!) and when he went to the register to give us our money back, he then turned the entire situation around on us to make it look like it was our fault. We won't be back. We'll make the drive to Music Valley if we want Cracker Barrel.

I came here for lunch with my coworker and it was delicious!  She got the salmon and I got udon and we were both very happy. The owner was very attentive and let us know we can park at the hotel because parking in this complex can be difficult.  We will definitely be coming back!

I suppose if you do not value your safety, or you are living in a dreamworld, you can pretend not to notice the gangs of "urban youths" making everyone uneasy.  The St. Louis Metrolink is not unique in this regard.  Public transportation is this way in many cities in the US.  

Just do yourself a favor and GOOGLE St Louis Metrolink  safety, or some such other search.  There are bunches of stories of fights, attacks, intimidation and muggings, a few videos as well.  Let's not forget the beating of one lone 43 year old man, just a week ago, by 3 urban youths, all captured on video.  

In short, the St. Louis Metrolink is cheap and efficient.  Safe?........that's a roll of the dice.

Everything I've had at this place is freaking delicious. You literally cannot go wrong ordering anything here. I believe I've tried literally just about everything on their menu. And I really appreciate French style cafés because they're so rare and hard to come by and this place is a gem.
Workouts are always changing and they play great music!

Absolutely the best Italian food in the area. Seriously. The BEST food. My husband and I lived in the area for nine years and Argento's was the place we went to celebrate most of our anniversaries and birthdays. The bakery is dangerously good. If we ever visit Florida, we will go out of our way to eat here again.

SOOOOOO GOOOOOOD!

I was in town for a long weekend, and found St. Louis' public transportation system to be surprisingly good. Sure, vehicles could run more frequently, and they aren't 24 hours, but between the light rail and bus I got around easily, and nothing was crowded. Combined with what looks like easy biking terrain, it seems like you could live car-free here pretty easily.

I don't quite understand how the honor system/fare-checking staff system is simpler/more cost effective than just having turnstiles, though.
Pizza is crispy and tasty. Service was fast and friendly. Prices are great too. A small but efficient little restaurant, can't wait to try their milkshakes!

I stopped by here for lunch and to do some work on my laptop.  I arrived around 11:20, which there wasn't really a line or wait.  I stayed for about an hour and half, to which is saw the entire lunch rush come through.  The food was good, my sandwich was the best.  I had the beef barely soup and beef sandwich on pretzel bun with horseradish mayo.  My only complaint that it was very loud, but partially my fault for coming at such a busy time in a very corporate area. I would definitely come here again, did not disappoint!

Cracker Barrel. Ooo, this beast. I recently tried going in my hometown and was told there was over an hour wait. No thanks, small hometown. Before this location off of 65, I tried going to a closer one in town, only to be unable to find a spot in the lot. Insane. Found a spot right away at this one however, and someone immediately peddles us for money in the lot. Fine, fine, let's get this thing started. We walk in to the hostess, she looks at me without saying anything and I ask if this is where we put our name in. It is. Great. We put it in and 25-30 min turned into about 40-45 min of a wait. The store itself was filled with mostly people just waiting, so it was had to navigate around if you actually want to look like I do. As we were called we could barely even make it through to get seated, but we did, and it was well worth the wait as we got a seat close to the huge open fire! Ahhh. Ok. So our server was an older lady and she was sweet and funny, not to mention attentive. She got our food out fast, our drinks refilled, and everything else. The meal, despite its seeming setbacks, was going good up until this tiny moment where the waitress dropped off my food only to see her finger slide into my prized chicken and dumplins! Now she did not mean to do this, however, I usually always find myself watching for this when I'm out to eat. I ate around- and was cool with it mostly because she was so friendly. The biscuits are some of my favorites with the strawberry jam! Yum! Overall this was a good experience and I will be back- but Cracker Barrel's all over need to figure out bigger parking lots- more tables in the restaurant- better system for waiting and being called, it's kind of a hot mess right now. For as busy as they stay you think this would work itself out. But a plus side is you get good portion sizes for a good value because of the ever apparent crowds!

The cappuccino traditional is great. So is the food, the entertainment, the staff, and the manager(altho i feel like he gets a bit stressed at times, he runs a tight ship, hope he knows his staff and product are great, he should relax, its all good).

This place is such a treasured find!  Tasty, homemade baked goods made with love. Croissants are flaky yet tender, coffee is hot and fresh, and owners/staff are always happy to see you there.  Prices are very reasonable. 

Get here early because they are sure to sell out, that's how good this place is!  Closed Sundays and Mondays, too.

Love this place & owner is very friendly. 

Reasonably priced for the area. Everything is delicious but i usually purchase the buffalo chicken pizza, veggie pizza with boom boom sauce, chicken sandwich, or zuzu salad w/ chicken.

My girl was really excited about Companion after they catered one of the lunches for her company's board group and brought back a sandwich for me. I can't remember the name of the sandwich despite having ordered it numerous times since, but it was roast beef, cucumber, red onion, and a horseradish mayo on pretzel bread. Needless to say, from the bread to the ingredients within, it is delicious. The only problem I've run into is the consistency of the meat. Occasionally it is really chewy and doesn't bite easily, which could be a sign that the roast beef is slightly less cooked than it could be; this is not a safety or a taste concern, but a texture issue. 

In addition to this delicious sandwich, I have had the French dip and falalalala. The latter is like Thanksgiving in sandwich form with turkey and cranberry sauce, but, buyer beware, the bread is delicious and REALLY chewy. All in all, this is a great spot for a quick sandwich and baked goods.
Terrible service with a bad attitude.  Is this really a Wendy's?  Virtually everyone waiting for food has had to complain bout the wait.  Crazy...

The dishes are OK and the waitress is nice. We are glad to see another Chinese restaurant opening in Indy.
We went there with a 10% coupon on a newspaper. But when we checked out, I forgot to show the coupon. Yes, that's all my fault. The waitress kindly helped ask if we can get the money back. Actually I did not expect to get the money back. But what surprised me is the excuse we got from the cashier--the coupon expired. We took a look at the newspaper, it's from 2 days ago, and there's no expire date on the coupon. So we got another explain from the cashier, "You should show the coupon before checking out next time!". Yes, she was right this time!  Probability not, I mean, shall we go there next time?

So I didn't think I was going to be using public transportation, since I was visiting a friend with a car.  However, he had to run some errands and I wanted to explore the city, so I told him I would just check out what this city has to offer as far as mass transit.

I must admit, I like it, especially the metrolink.  Coming from Houston, we have awful mass transit.  Their metrolink resembles a mini version of chicago's rail system.  This one is only west and east.  There is a red and a blue line.  It even takes you across the river.

The pricing could be a bit better, they offer a one way, two way, a couple of hours, a day and a week rate.  I know chicago offers a 3? and 5? day pass?  It's good because especially if you're on vacation a whole week might be too much but 1 day is too little.  I went with the one day pass for $7.50.  

The people who rode the rail was very helpful to a tourist like myself.  It was on time and travels fast.
Staff couldn't have been more helpful and the service was incredible. In and out in 25 minutes. The food was very good and I was checked in on after every plate. Definitely going back.

Servers are great. Food is not that good. Chicken and dumplings were disappointing. Chicken was dry. Corn bread and biscuit are a bit dense for my taste. Mac and cheese is made with real cheese. Sweet tea is perfect. There was a long line at the cashiers. Not sure if thats normal. But I went on a Tuesday night. Prices are great. A hearty meal for less than $10.

This place is amazing! Where have these donuts been all my life? The flavors are so creative and delicious. The dough is light but with weight in the flavor...if that makes sense?!? We had the "Dirty O.G", "Southern Belle", pretzel bites, truffle fries, and Vanilla Orange Cream Ale (I know, weird combination, but it works!). Adorable place, great location, friendly, informative staff! A real gem for the local casual food scene.

Busy, a bit of a wait, but overall not terrible. The best part is playing checkers and that little peg thingy game on the tables. At least I'm not a *total* ignoramus. 

If you haven't been here you should go, and also who the hell has never been to cracker barrel?
This is a cool spot.  It's a neighborhood pizza spot but with a Mediterranean style.  You can get your usual pizza but also a house special lamb pizza or lamb wrap.  Good spot.

Century Link is scandalous. I even tried reporting them to the BBB. Such criminals. Do not use them. They will say one thing, charge another, and when your internet still doesn't work will cut a whole in your roof and call it fixed. I still get a bill from them. Ha. Good luck getting it. BBB backed them too. For shame. For shame.

All I can say is 2 thumbs way down. Staff and food both, piss poor at best. Sad. The waitress was one of the worst and most rude I've ever met. And I'm from Detroit. The food was terrible and thrown together. Lazy people. The owner of this establishment should recognize just because it's an airport, people are still people and should be treated as such. The 6 "Ps" of life: Proper planning prevents piss poor performance.

Great dogs and great service. Dog (canine) friendly. The power lunch is a great deal, any dog, a side and drink for $10. A little off the beaten path, but worth a little extra walk from Vandy or Hillsboro village.
We ate here last night. I had the chicken tenders. DO NOT EAT THE CHICKEN!  I was sick all night and still today. Food poisoning. Very disappointed and sick.

This place is great! I work around the corner and have taken to getting lunch here once or twice a week. So far, everything I've tried has been great. The cheese fries (with chicken, jalapenos, and a truffle sauce) are probably the best I've ever had. The Zuzu's chicken sandwich is also great. Really, everything I've tried here has been very good. The prices are also very reasonable and the owner and staff are all very friendly. If you're in the neighborhood, definitely stop in!

Trying to get any thing done with century link or direct tv is like pulling teeth. they continually raise the price without notice. the operators on the phone are not trained. They always say that was a promotional price. and that they can sign me up for another promotion, but its still more expensive.  The mafia is better than these thugs.  This has been the worst company that I've ever done business with. They will take your money in a flash but asking for a discount I was told it had to be approved and that would take 30 days. when I refused to wait the operator said well check back in 48 hours. One hand has know idea what the other is doing, confusion is no way to do business.  I also called and was passed around 3 times and landing in collections, called the next day and the same thing happened (3 different people) The first one just hung up.  
THE WORST...I'M DONE

Saw the Yelp reviews and decided to give it a shot. Happy we did! It'll probably be a quick fix neighborhood joint for us!

We ordered a cheeseburger, Zuzu's burger, a gyro, fries, and onion rings. The burgers and gyro were clean and tasty with very generous patty portions, which I don't love but I know others do. Fries and onion rings are nice and crispy how we like them!

We apparently ordered a cheesesteak instead of wanted cheeseburger, so the owner quickly adjusted the order for us very kindly with no complaints. 

We'll be back!

I travel a lot and this has to be one of the worst airport breakfasts I've ever had. Hot tasteless coffee was the best part. The egg sandwich and potatoes both served cold. I should have waited to eat and stopped at a good Jersey diner after landing.

Probably only deserves 2 stars but the decor is charming. We ordered chicken strips and fries....had to pay extra for dipping sauce.....bottled ranch. Overall those were fine. My husband had a chicken sandwich,  nothing special.  I ordered a 3 piece with coleslaw and that's were it gets bad. Way too salty, almost sent it back but it took so long to get it I just kept it.the breading had fallen off of most of the chicken so I had fried chicken with barely any crust. The coleslaw was bad. Tasted like mayo and cabbage and was not even fresh. I was so disappointed with this restaurant.  Obviously they put a lot of money into it and came up with a good menu. But did not deliver.

Whenever my family and I visit this neighborhood, we always eat at Zuzu's! It's a family-run, family-friendly business where literally everything is delicious. The owner, Adel, is kind and is always looking out for his customers' happiness. I'd highly recommend trying out this place when you're around.

I really enjoyed the Yelp Event visiting the bakery and touring. I will definitely try to get back here and take a class or two. The fact that you can see the processes taking place without a formal tour was also a plus for just eating here.

Our waitress was nice. The food was like other Cracker Barrel. The reason I'm giving only 2 * is because it is very dirty. I had my fork and spoon with crusty food on them changed 2 times and they where still dirty. I understand if they only had water marks, but food stuck to them? Not acceptable.
Really great selection of coffee, tea, beer, wine, pastries, soups and wraps. It's going to be a regular spot for us from now on.

Most beautiful buffet I've been in outside of Vegas. Best Asian buffet I've had in Indy. The all you can eat sushi was actually edible and the pho noodle soup is better than many pho restaurants around here. The owner, Daniel, is super nice and insisted that I try the Mongolian stir fry and noodle soup. I'm glad he did because normally I wouldn't. The beef here is fresh and the dishes for the most part, fresh.

What I'd like to see is better time management of the dishes on display. Some of them looked like they had been out for a long while. I did not try those.

You can thank The Most Interesting Woman in the World for convincing me to try this buffet. You normally wouldn't find me in one.

not sure if this is the right location i visited the one i believe on Simon near Sassafras Restaurant but here is the review  the chocolate chip cookie is good. the lemonade was ok  i had to docter mine up with ice and sugar but it was a little better with ice.  the coffe was good
I had the Elote Loco hot dog and my fiancé had the Banh Mi hot dog, we both loved them! The bread is so good, and the service is exceptional! I will definitely be back.
Amazing pizza, salads, and milkshakes. You get your moneys worth, a slice is literally 1/4 of a pizza. No seating inside, but fast for take out or pick up.

Pizza is great, service is not. I ordered twice on Grubhub and it was fine, but since I was starting to only get my pizza from there I ordered directly from their website, and after almost 2 hours, still no pizza. Called and they said they had lost my order. After a couple minutes on hold they told me they found it and said they will make it now, and asked if I would still like it. Um yes? I had already paid of course I still want it. And received no apology for the wait/loss of my order. Horrible customer service.
Best sushi in the area. People there is nice:) good service and new place. Love it. Recommend the fresh eel sushi. Best in town.

What a great find! While traveling in the Creve Couer area of St. Louis, we discovered this great place on Yelp! Very, very fresh and delicious! Portions where generous. Staff was friendly and helpful. You can watch them make all the dough for their products, very fun! Can eat outside too if you like. Highly recommend, and we will be back!
You can't beat the price to have your cars washed by hand. Also, I hate vacuuming the interior of my car and the fact that they do it for you is an added bonus. Love Swancy's!

Companion Cafe is just okay as a lunch spot.  This place is very expensive for a restaurant without table service.  A bowl of soup and small salad is $11.95.  If you have a drink you're basically paying $15 for lunch at essentially a fast-food place.  Many other places provide better value in the Westport area.

I went here on a whim and it was one of the most pleasant dinner experiences I've had. The place was poppin but we got seated immediately. Service was amazing and the sushi chefs was particularly amiable. Will come back!

The Metrolink is St. Louis' mass transportation system.  The fare is $2 for one ride, but you can get deals such as purchasing a month ticket for $60.  The Metrolink is reliable and safe, but there are some very strange people on here.  Usually when I use it, there is at least one semi-crazy person who is barking about this or that, although they never seem to do anything.  

It will be nice when the Link is expanded to even more places, but currently is great for the downtown and surrounding areas.  Try going on off hours if you can, because otherwise there will be lines.

I'm not a fan of Chinese buffet so that might have biased me.  This one is the worst I've been to.  About half of the dishes were identified.  Most of what I tried was luke warm at best.  The broccoli in the beef and broccoli was mushy and cold.  One pork dish was full of very small bones that made it inedible.  It looked like most of the chicken and vegetable dishes didn't have much chicken in them.

I stopped by tonight to get a hotdog - mind you it's only 7p - and I'm told that they "sold out" of hotdogs. How do you sell out of hotdogs?? I'm sorry but if your offerings are donuts and dogs and you don't have either, but particularly hotdogs at 7p on a Friday night, how do you expect to stay in business- let alone build customer loyalty.
The owner and the staff here are friendly and turnout great food. One of the cleanest pizza place I've seen.

We had the chili and queso dog. It was delicious. The dog was wrapped in bacon for an extra punch of awesomeness and the top split bun was fresh. We will return to try another dog soon. 
It's a super tiny restaurant. Maybe 5 or 6 small tables.

This location has been some kind of Chinese buffet for the past 10 years.  The latest iteration is pretty interesting.  They really embrace the Mongolian Grill concept and feature it.   For those of you unfamiliar with it, here it is in a nutshell:  Grab a bowl, put in your raw ingredients, vegetables, meats, noodles;  Mix up a sauce and hand everything to the guy working the giant circular flat top grill.   Watch him cook everything together using only a pair of gigantic wooden chopsticks.   Enjoy.

Iron Sheet Royal Grill also has a do-it-yourself noodle soup bar.   Think Mongolian Grill done with boiling water instead of a flat top.

Price is pretty reasonable (under $10).   You do have to pay extra for bubble teas and crab, but you should find plenty to eat from the grill, noodle  bar, and the standard Chinese buffet steam table options (sushi, soups, stir fries, hibachi grill, etc.).

I like this place, and loved it when I went to UNO and wanted somewhere a bit more comfortable than the library to study.  But for a coffeeshop in New Orleans, near TWO schools where people need to study at later hours in the evening, their hours are terribly short in my opinion.  And also, as someone said before, they're not exactly the most environmentally friendly coffeeshop, with their disposable cups and styrofoam plates.  I prefer Zotz, which stays open until 1 a.m. and gives you ceramic cups to drink use, or Fair Grinds Coffeehouse, which does the same -- but they're much further away from UNO and SUNO.

ZuZu's kitchen is a excellent addition to the neighborhood.  We ordered the fattoush salad and ZuZu's special pizza.  The portions were large and the food was delicious.  The best part was dessert.  ZuZu's had several desserts to choose from, and we picked the Tiramisu.  It was the perfect end to the meal.  We will definitely go back to try the other items on their menu!

On a recent holiday we cycled past Companion and were drawn by the fresh baking smells. Being closed, we peered into their windows and their GM, Price, kindly and unexpectedly invited us in. He gave us a private, impromptu tour and told us about the array of classes they lead in their teaching kitchen. We knew we must return for a meal, and soon. 

The physical space is reason enough to visit. You can watch bread making in action through big glass windows as you sip tea and nosh on a fresh bagel. Learn through a self guided tour about all that goes into making a loaf. Be surprised by the ways they've used everyday kitchen items (e.g. A room divider made of hanging rolling pins or a shiny silver wall of connected baking pans) to decorate the space. 

The food is quite good; we were pleased with the flavor and freshness. We brought home a nice metal branded drinking vessel and a loaf of pumpkin seed cranberry bread. 

We will certainly return for future breakfast and lunches. 

In a world of huge impersonal chains of mass food production, it's joyful to support this local company that cares about quality, local sourcing and takes pride and care in one's products.

I have tried to eat here a few times and have found the service to be lacking and indifferent. I even tried getting a drink at the bar. I prefer the bakery further south on 19 (Sorrento's). Not sure what's up with this place? I've met other people that like it. Decor seemed dated. One of those big pretty empty places where you're made to feel invisible. Sorry!!!

HUGE... can I repeat HUGE disappointment!  While I was happy to see pancakes and sausage on the menu, the food was worthy of the garbage can.  Typically overpriced and did I mention a HUGE disappointment.  Sadly, there are not that many restaurants to choose from when you are past security, so my suggestion it to hit the Cracker Barrel or grab a biscuit from Chick-fil-a before you arrive at the airport.  Your stomach and wallet will thank you.

In short: the salmon that we had was not of the great quality in terms of freshness and cut - one of the peaces had a bone in it and the meat get hard and a bit smelly. The price range at this place is the same as at Arigato but more than half lower in quality. Maybe it was just a bad day but it was what it was

I cannot comment on the quality of the service in terms of car repair, but this Meineke franchise is a pure rip-off.

I called the center about the cost for installation of new tires. Having priced out tires from other centers, I was curious about how much Meineke charged. Over the phone I was told I would receive a free estimate on new tires, but I could not be told the cost over the phone without looking at the car. I should have known to keep looking, but I figured it could not hurt since they were close to where I lived.

A few hours later, I received a call with an estimate and that I needed a new part (outer tie rod, which on the market is about $12) with an exorbitant fee of $725. Of course, I refused their service because I found other places charging far less (other places  were charging $400 or less, Meineke only offers one type of tire ~$100 each totalling $450 for basic installation). Tacking on the alignment ($75 or $100) and part replacement (it is not difficult to reach and can be replaced in 15 minutes), it would cost $275. That is ridiculous.

But that is not why I am giving them one star. I am giving them one star because when I went to pick up my car, they tacked on a $45 inspection fee. I did not ask them to inspect anything, I even said, I came in for a free estimate on new tires. "The tire estimate is free, looking at the car is $45." Never again will I take my car there, I do not care how conveniently located you are. Find a better mechanic.

This is Maryland Heights' best kept secret. The building is hidden in the warehouse district of Westport, but inside it is hip and open and clean (think Schlafly Bottleworks). Great bagel and egg sandwiches, gourmet toasts, pastries and breads. Good Kaldi's coffee. Everyone is friendly and you can watch what's going on with the dough while you eat. There are tables outside to enjoy nice weather too.

Y'all, this is the kind of hotdog that causes you to swear, it's so good. They packed so much goodness into the Elote Dog, and I will definitely come back for it. Also those fries are so crispy and so tasty. This was the perfect quick dinner on our way to the Belcourt!

Sadly I didn't get to try their donuts, as I guess they sell out quickly every day, but I hope to come back one morning and give them a try!

The people that work here are very kind and try to make sure we have everything we need. I like this Cracker Barrel but I wish they would warm up the syrup like the other Cracker Barrel's do. No one likes cold syrup.

The big knock on STL's mass transit (or at least the light rail portion) is that it's limited in the number of areas that it serves.  While that is true, if you're near one of the stops you should take advantage of it.  It's fast, clean, new and not that expensive.

During my last trip out of town, I choose to use MetroLink to get home from the Airport.  This significally saved on expense since I didn't have to pay for airport parking.  I live in the Webster area and MetroLink only goes as close as Maplewood.  But for the $4 ticket I was able to make a free transfer onto one of the Metro Buses to complete my ride.  It took about 45 minutes to get home, but I didn't have to deal with rush hour traffic, and my hands were free to catch up on email & social media.  

It's somewhat confusing to use the bus service.  Take time to plan your route ahead of time via their website.  They have a trip planner that will give you the best route option based on your starting and ending address.

I could not give this place enough stars!!! Both donuts that my friend and I got were perfect (sin-u-rita and stairway 2 heaven). The owners explained the ingredients and flavors to each item to help me get a better understanding of what to order. I got the elote hot dog, a spicy dog in thick Texas toast with cotija, corn and lime on it. With a side of fries, it was filling and full of flavor. If you haven't been here, YOU have to try it. We'll be back soon

Hot dog was delicious. Fries were delicious and super fresh. Coffee and donuts were also fantastic. The donuts had unique and distinct toppings, but they weren't too heavy or sweet. They were the nicest people, going above and beyond to answer questions and make sure we were enjoying things. Very cute inside and out. I can't wait to go back!

This place is delicious and the best Japanese food I've tried in Santa Barbara. I grew up in the bay and this place is comparable to Japanese restaurants there. I got the dragon roll which is a California roll with eel and avocado and it was sooooo good. My friend got the crunch roll and his was also very good, but we agreed that the dragon roll was better. Bathroom was also really clean. Definitely visiting this place again!

I've taken my car here several times and have never been disappointed. Matt and the rest of the guys here are great. I love that they remember me (and my car) when I come in no matter how long it's been since I've come in. I've had some really basic stuff done, like an oil change, to more extensive work and have never been disappointed. The price has quality of work has always been satisfactory. They do get busy though, and sometimes the turnaround here isn't the swiftest. Since I usually drop my car off and leave, I don't mind, but may be a factor for others.

This was my first attempt at a juice cleanse.  I bought the juice plus raw coupon from rue la la.  I figured having the dinner option would be easier for my first time.  I really didn't have a problem not eating during the day, and I appreciated not having to think about my meals, but this cleanse was a challenge due to the taste of the juice.  I had 2 greens, one lemonade, and one carrot to drink every day.  The green juice overwhelmingly tastes like celery, as does the carrot one.  I really enjoyed the lemon with cayenne.  I had a hard time scheduling my juice times due to my schedule, but I mostly wasn't hungry until the evenings, around 5/5:30.  I tried to eat the food around 6.  The food was all pretty good.  I loved the lasagna, pasta, kale salad, and the chocolate goji bars.  The texture of the burger was a little off-putting.  

For me this was a great exercise in will power, and I'm proud of myself for sticking though the 3 days.  I don't think I could do something like this much longer than that, because I work out too much, and need more protein.  Getting through my tennis match on the last day was definitely tough, and I didn't feel like I was at full strength which was frustrating.  I did get a lot of sleep so that I wasn't tempted to cheat at night.  Some positive physical benefits: super flat stomach, lost a few pounds, and didn't get tired in the late afternoon like I usually do.  I have another coupon so I will probably do this one more time.
