If you are trying to get food here before your flight, I personally suggest you make sure you have at least an hour before your flight boards. They have only 1 cashier and the service here is extremely slow. It took 50 minutes total to wait In Line, order and receive my order.

Total waste of time!

Awesome local place. This is our new favorite and hasn't been dethroned in over a year. We like to sit at the bar and try specials as well as their Delight roll which is incredible. The staff is super nice. It's not a fancy place until you taste the sushi- then it be like "fabulous."
Worst customer service ever, slow internet. They cannot communicate and this is a communication company!  Good by and hello to another company.
Out of chocolate frosty.  Can not provide a receipt.  Backed up and slow.  No organization.  Who owns this location as it makes me never want to go to another we day location again.
We love Zuzu's! My favorite menu item is the bacon avocado panini and my boyfriend really likes their cheesesteaks. Pizza is also on point and the lamb burger is divine! Highly recommend!

I had gone to the Clayton location when it was still opened. I wasn't too satisfied. However, this location has me coming back again and again. I've brought so many people to this place. The bread is, of course, fresh and delicious. The cornbread in particular is always amazing. The brownies and gooey butter bar are also must tries. My only reason for giving it four stars instead of five is the price. I would go here more often, but an average of $12 for lunch has me choosing other places instead. But that's just me--it hasn't really deterred the numerous other customers who line up every afternoon for their delicious salads, sandwiches, and desserts.

The Donut + Dog is now my favorite coffee shop in Nashville. Everyone is super friendly, but not in an obnoxious way. I've visited three times now and my coffee comes out consistent and pretty much perfect. I've had their truffle fries and a plain glazed donut and both were delicious. The donut rivaled 5 Daughters Bakery. They do have more decadent donuts I'd like to try at some point. The location is a house turned Business with charming, cool decor. There is outside seating too. Street parking with coin meters, but there are a lot of parking structures too within walking distance.
It's a crapshoot as to whether staff at the Metro will offer assistance or just stare at you blankly. We ended up not using it.

One star is too generous. I cancelled my service with CenturyLink within 30 days of establishing service and submitted the "30 day guarantee" form on November 4, 2016. I was assured by the CenturyLink agent that I did not owe anything since I was cancelling within 30 days. Great, so I thought. Today, May 27, 2017, I received a letter telling me that my "delinquent" account has been sent to a collection agency. I have not received ANY correspondence from CenturyLink since I cancelled 6 months ago and now my cancelled account is going to a collection agency?! If I really owed money, one would think that CenturyLink would have attempted to contact me during these past 6 months. I thought the speed of their internet was bad but apparently their record keeping is worse.

This restaurant has to be one of the best sushi restaurants you can find in Santa Barbara. The service, the fish, the prices, the atmosphere... Simply just wow. Please, do yourself a favor and dine at this restaurant. 

We loved every single dish we ordered. In particular, the Tsukiji market special. Yes, the famous fish market in Tokyo! They receive these fish from Japan, and you can taste the quality. Well worth the money. I don't remember all the names of the fish, but the servers were so knowledgeable, and explained each type.  

The dessert was so tasty, we ordered the ice cream tempura (yum!), and two slices of cheesecake. We chose the mango, and the matcha green tea.  

Compliments to the sushi chef, for what we gather from the server he has been doing sushi for a very long time, and was trained in Japan at a young age.

Thanks for such a great experience!
Update: My original comments are still valid but I did get the situation resolved. The Century Link agent zeroed out my account.
Went here for brunch and had a great time. Everything here was really good and great atmosphere as well. They had great salads, sandwiches and coffee!
Wonderful pastries.  I only wish they weren't so high priced.  Even the pastries in restaurants are less expensive than here.

I'm writing this review based on several different visits.  That's why they are getting a 2 from me instead of a 1.  On ALL visits (a total of 4 different times) the food has been either cold or lukewarm.  The orders have been wrong or we had to ask for something more than twice.  The servings have been small.  The service was horrible on 2 of those visits, however the manager did try to make it right when we complained on 1 of those visits (another reason it gets a 2 instead of a 1).   We were given excuses for the bad service every time.  Either they're being overworked or understaffed.  Maybe that's true, and if it is then management here is the problem!  I can say, in all honesty, this is the worst Cracker Barrel I've ever been to.  And, as a native Tennessean, that's a lot!  I believe if this Cracker Barrel were dependent upon the locals for customers, they would already be out of business.  But since they are directly off of Interstate 65, this saves them.  They get an unsuspecting crowd of tourists who think they are going to get another great Cracker Barrel meal.  My advice....move on to the next one down the road if you can.  I kept hoping I was just catching them on a bad day...over...and over.  But now I know it's pretty par for the course.  I know I won't be back to this one.
Seems to be the only coffee dig in a few mile radius. Nice little chill place. Not to much different than the other pj's around town

This pjs is my favorite in the city. The chai tea is to die for and the bagels are always super fresh. 

The owner is very nice and encourages her staff with positive feedback and casual conversation. It is very warm and inviting for college students and visitors.

One of my two favorite AYCE buffets in Indy. The other is The Journey on 96th.

Seafood: Sushi is really hit or miss here. Sometimes the rolls do not make any sense. Anyone want to try a strawberry roll? How about a california roll with just imitation crab and a boatload of rice? No thanks. Give me a simple salmon nigiri anyday... The Journey is better if you're craving seafood.

Chinese: Iron Sheet has some authentic Chinese dishes that I love including eggplant, greenbeans, sauteed mushrooms, meat and brocolli, and many more. The Journey's Chinese selection is limited to your typical egg rolls, chow mein, and fried rice. The mongolian grill is great. Their Pho bar used to be pretty good but today's soup was old and salty even though I was one of the first guests for lunch.

Ice Cream: Little premade cups. Nothing spectacular. I think vanilla is the best.

Fruits: Always a treat here.

Price: Iron Sheet definitely wins on price: $ for lunch and dinner. But seafood at The Journey even at lunch is hard to beat!

In a word, okay.  It was very okay.  I didn't come for a donut just a hot dog.  I probably came in with an unfair bias because I missed the Dog which had been at that location since I moved here 9 years ago, so I know my expectations were already set high.  

The service was fine. The guy at the counter was friendly and knowledgeable.  I ordered the lunch special which was just under $10. If you come at dinner time you are looking at spending about twenty bucks for a dog and a side and a drink so I appreciated the value meal at lunch.

I got my food to go and to be perfectly honest it was not an eat in your car or on the go meal.  The brioche bun was overkill. It tasted fine but was pretty greasy and frankly too big.  What's wrong with a normal hot dog bun? The sausage was cooked well and had good flavor.  Nothing to go crazy for. The fries were heavily seasoned. Almost too much.

Overall this is a nice place to visit. I'm sure there is an audience for whatever it is the donut and dog are trying to accomplish but if you are a fan of just a simple good thing like a hot dog, then there are better options out there.  At the end of the day it's a hot dog, you don't have to try and reinvent it.

As someone who has worked in every aspect of food service I find it hard to complain. I ask myself "do they seem like they are having a bad day?" "Does she seem like she's in training?" "Did someone in front of me just rip them apart?" As someone who has had a multitude of experience on the server side of things getting screamed at from the amount of ice cubes in the class to how things are priced on the menu, I try my best not to take it upon myself to ruin someone's day. That being said it's been over a week since I visited the Wendy's at the airport in Nashville and their horrible service is still on my mind. They had 6 employees working and 1 register open. The rest of the employees stood in front or in back talking to one another and cursing. I say this because there were children in line. I noticed one of them was the manager and thought there was about to be a change in attitude but she was just as bad as they were. The people in front of me were treated like crap because they ordered their "regular" a Jr bacon cheeseburger to be told "we don't have that outside shit here read the menu" the man ordered a combo and the woman a kids meal with a frosty. After they waited 10 minutes to receive their food the man had to come back to ask for his drink and then frosty along with getting the wrong size fries. He asked for napkins and ketchup and was ignored. He ended up reaching around me to grab them from behind the register for himself and they never got the frosty. I too waited 10 minutes along with multiple airport employees who missed half their lunch waiting for one girl to grab the food in the window that sat there half the time we waited. She handed the wrong orders to two people and they walked away and figured it out later and said "fuck it, my bad.. They ain't coming back whatever". When I finally received my order I too had to ask for my drink and they gave it to me half full. I asked for ketchup and was told "we don't have no ketchup try Popeyes". All in all a horrible experience, just glad my flight was delayed and wasn't worried about time. They seriously need to retrain or restaff SOON.
Tomato pie is 10/10. Super flavourful and filled with garlic and basil. Zuzus chicken sandwich and the boneless wings are amazing too. Best neighbourhood joint!

Went here for dinner with my in-laws. Gotta say that the food was pretty tasty. My husband got the chicken parm which was huge and really good. I got the stuffed shells which were filling and yummy. They served good bread before dinner with really good marinara sauce for dipping. They had a whole case of fresh pastries and cookies which we didn't try but they looked awesome. I had to take a star away for the ambiance, definitley lacking. All of my Italian in-laws love this place and they know their stuff so that says something.

First, the basics:

Poor seating - I wasn't aloud to move a little table to attach it to another so that me and my colleague could look at each other's screen while we worked on school-work. 

Poor coffee - I had a latte that tasted like burnt popcorn with mildly warm milk.

Poor environment - all you have to listen to is the obnoxious sounds from the coffee machines that might as well have been stolen from a dilapidated gas station somewhere well forgotten.


This, along with the rest of this chain of sub-par coffee joints, is the epitome of excessive wastefulness in the modern age:

Not only do they only have disposable cups, when I ordered cheesecake bites, each one was individually wrapped yet still  the girl working put on a new set of disposable gloves to grab them and put them on a styrofoam plate. Eww. 

I'm really turned off by this place but the cheesecake didn't taste bad.

My friends and I were intrigued and drawn into Donut + Dog by an Instagram post of a smoked latte. We spent the week looking forward to that latte but we were pleasantly surprised that this place is so much more than a creative and delicious latte. 

We ended up having coffee, donuts, and hot dogs. We were concerned about mixing so many flavors but the flavor profiles of everything has been created so meticulously that all of the food works wonderfully together. This menu was clearly put together with a lot of love and creativity. 

That same level of passion really shines through in the excellent and enthusiastic customer service. 

If you order the smoked latte, they bring the smoker to your table and you get to watch them literally smoke your latte right in front of you! The smoke infuses all of the flavors together creating a unique experience. 

I like to judge new donut places first based off of the basic donut. At Donut + Dog, that is the Dirty OG, which is your basic glazed donut but here they add pink Himalayan salt. I will say their basic donut is one of the best I've ever had. The sweet combined with a touch of salt is magnificent. My friends were equally impressed with their donut selections as well. 

They use as many local ingredients as possible and anything that isn't local is organic. We were expecting to feel gross and sluggish after donuts, coffee, fries, and hot dogs but we didn't! 

I highly recommend putting this place at the top of your list of places to try.
Everything I ordered was delicious! I ordered the chicken shawarma and it was seasoned and grilled perfectly. Their cheeseburger and wings were pretty great too.

Very poor service. I tried three times to get an inspection and oil change, and each time the guy behind the desk had a different excuse for why he could not do it yet. I decided not to go back for a fourth try. This was the least helpful service I've ever seen at an auto shop. They wasted a ton of my time over the course of two days. I will never be going back to this place.
What a great little place. The waitress was very. Not expensive. Fish was high quality and the appetizers were awesome!

This place defines "beyond expectations"!! Me and my husband decided to give it a try but not expecting a lot bc, you know, it's Santa Barbara (we came to SB from the Bay Area and have struggled a little bit adjusting to the "meh" food scene here). Walking in it was already a pleasant surprise: very beautifully decorated place: tradicional Japanese bamboo and curtains and super cool cement floors. From the moment we sat down we had AMAZING service: attentive, knowledgeable, sweet and polite. Not only was our server outstanding, but also everyone in the restaurant checked on us throughout the meal to see how we were doing and every single one of them bid us farewell on our way out. Honestly one of the best services I've ever had in SB. And then last but not least, the food!! OMG! So fresh and delicious. So delicate and with such well balanced flavors and the presentation was just out of this world. Honestly we were blown away by our experience. Thank you very much Sun Sushi team. We have found our new favorite restaurant in SB!!!

This place is terrific! 
My college-aged daughter's car broke down in University City and it was towed here. They were fast, fair and gave a complete explanation of the problem. The charges were broken down and easy for a person that isn't mechanically inclined (me!) to understand. 
I would recommend this business to anyone that is looking for an efficient, well priced repair shop.

Excellent place for really good coffee and a nice selection of freshly baked tasty breads and cakes. We came for breakfast early on a Sunday and it was pretty empty but still a lovely friendly atmosphere. The owners are very nice. Highly recommended!
This place is everything they say it is.  Tucked into the industrial area of Westport, it's easy to miss.  I'm glad I stopped in to try it out.  I'll definitely plan on returning.

If I could do a no star review I would. In the past month I have payed them $400 for a service I never used once. They have low life scam tactics, "verbal contacts" they don't tell you you've agreed to and a horribly unethical customer service. BE WARNED. Someone needs to shut this place down.

This is one of my favorite spots in Philadelphia. The food is amazing and high quality. I recommend the fish tacos and zuzu's chicken sandwich, but you really can't go wrong with anything. The prices are more than reasonable and the staff is excellent. 10/10 would recommend.

Went into the Cracker Barrel on Long Hollow Pike today for lunch for my boss any myself. I placed an order with a waitress at about 11:15am. Was told by the cheerful waitress it should be about 15 minutes. I ordered a fried chicken salad (No tomato or onion, with extra cheese and ranch dressing) and a low carb double meat breakfast (three eggs, and bacon with sliced tomatoes and toast). At 11:45 I was asked by a manager the name on my to-go order and she then promptly sent a waitress to check on my order. There was relatively no wait to be seated in the dining area so I wouldn't say they were slammed but steady busy.  The waitress comes to me and says "They are putting it together now." I said "It's been 30 minutes." Her response was "Oh, really?" Ten more minutes go by...still no food. So I went back and got the manager. The manager comes back out and tells me she's sorry and hands me a bag of food. The salad came out with tomatoes and no extra cheese, and I didn't notice until I got to work that my meal was the standard double breakfast so there was no tomatoes and extra items I did not want. But I didn't check it before I left, so that's on me.

I really hate complaining but it was a very simple order that should have only taken 15 minutes per the waitress that took my order. How do you take 40 minutes to do the order and still get it wrong? I caught the salad and they fixed it, only for me to get to work and there were still tomatoes in it (glad my boss isn't allergic to tomatoes), and my food be cold as if it had been sitting for a while.
Sun is the best sushi in Santa Barbara.  They serve the highest quality fish - its as simple as that.  Excellent service too.

ZuZu's is such a great little spot! The guys that work there are awesome and really friendly and helpful! One time, I was stick on the side of the road because TRUMP was coming through with all these cars and cops and the ZuZu employee literally walked my food to my car! They are always willing to work with you to ensure you enjoy your experience every time! Food wise, BE SURE TO GET THE SOUTHWEST SPRING ROLLS! They are soooooo good! 

If you want to have a chill experience and enjoy some really good food but don't want to pay an arm and a leg - ZUZUs is your jammmm!!
Since Zuzu's opened, they've consistently given great pizza and have a great atmosphere. 10/10 recommend.

I found this place on a Google search and had to visit after seeing the menu and pics online.  The customer service is phenomenal and the unique combination of gourmet donuts and delicious dogs makes this place a grand slam on my book!  Loved the atmosphere and can't wait to go back!
Food is great, service is friendly, delivery is fast- perfect combo! Love the burger, fries, and shawarma wrap. Heard people rave about the milkshakes but have yet to had enough room to order! 10/10

I'm so happy I finally got around to coming to companion. Had the Brie, tomato and cheese on brioche and died and went to heaven, so light and fluffy. I would compare it to a light, fluffy grilled cheese. My companion(tee hee) had the It's all Greek breakfast sandwich with spinach, artichoke and baked eggs on a bagel. Yummy as well. I enjoyed watching the bakers work while I enjoyed my breakfast. Will definitely return for breakfast and lunch soon. Closes at 2pm

best fucking everything forever. eat here or suffer disappointing pie. 
zuzus fries are pure heron, and so is the zuzu burger for that matter. 

back to the pie; it's perfect. order now.

Coming from Los Angeles, we were used to really good sushi and we're disappointed to find out that there really aren't very many good places in Santa Barbara. Once we saw this new place open up near us, we were super excited to try it out! 

The staff was very friendly and attentive as well as professional and respectful. *PRO TIP* sit at the bar! 

The food we ordered was very good. We ordered 4 rolls and enjoyed all of them! Only thing I would change is portion size. The rolls were very small, but tasted great! We will definitely be returning with family and friends!

Unfortunately I couldn't complete the 4-day cleanse I paid more than I could afford because they expired 1/2 way through.  I knew they tasted a little off, but all the bottles began to expand except cayenne/lemon and cashew milk.  

I drink vegetable juice often and these tasted way off by day two.  

Too bad.  Lemon/cayenne was fine though.

This place is a little on the pricier side, but it's 100% worth every penny. I ordered a Dirty Churro donut (which was DELISH), and then we split an Elote Loco and a Chili Queso. Both dogs were equally amazing, but if I had to pick a favorite, I'd go with the Chili Queso. I regret not ordering the Frito Pie because the chili was so delicious! Seriously can't wait to go back here next time we're in town!
Come here often before, in between,  and after classes.  Service is always courtesy and speedy. Coffee and cakes are fresh.
Wonderful pastries. The shortbread melts in your mouth. Not only are the goodies fantastic, but the owners are delightful to talk with and the place is decorated like my Nana's house. I love it.

We were in the neighborhood and decided to have some sushi, so I yelped this place and was very happy with my decision. The fish was so fresh, it just melted in your mouth. If you are ever in the neighborhood, stop by and give them a try. You will not be disappointed.
This is our favorite sushi restaurant. The food is so fresh & the staff is so attentive. The delight rolls are my favorite. Ignore the strip mall location- it's so good.

Big fan of Companion Breads but this was the first time I had ever been to the new Café or had one of their bagels. I ordered an everything bagel with plain cream cheese and an iced tea. The bagel was a bit more bready/doughy and less chewy than I like. The cream cheese was an off brand and tasted like it. The iced tea was good. The café is super cute I love the way the kitchen where the bread is being baked is exposed. I feel like I should have skipped the bagel and ordered some of their other pastries that looked really appealing. Next time!
Nasty cold breakfast here. Wished I read Yelp before wasting my money. At least it was cheap.

I will say the food is quite good. I have the French dip with a prom queen salad all of the time. That being said, their staff has a complete attitude. They are completely uppity and act like they are somehow better then the people they are selling bread and salads to. 

Customer service simply is not considered important at Companion Bread. This bye the way is coming from a long term client who eats at this location 1-4 times a week.

Great great place. Food, service, huge sake selection, seriously no complaints. My wife always has green tea but she loves it hot hot. She always has to ask, except here. They kept it full, fresh and hot. They are eager, friendly, will do any sashimi, nigiri or roll custom. Give it a try...

Nice patio for a beer. Looks-wise, it's cute. But preferred the previous, less fancy, hot dog place, with hot dog buns, good servings of mustard and ketchup, tater tots, etc... I don't think the combination hot dogs and doughnuts/coffee works for me.
I had the buffalo wrap- it was drenched in sauce. Practically inedible. The chicken was chopped up like a chicken cheese steak. Not good.
Who paid for these reviews? My pizza was peppery and the burger was ok but nothing to rave about also, the fries tasted stale.

You have to visit this place when you're in Nashville!! We stopped by on a weekday mid-afternoon, and the donuts from that morning were still to die for. Very unique flavor combos & the texture of the donuts is amazing- a lot thicker than most. The vibe is very cool- 90s music & mismatched seating in an old house. Probably the best part of the experience, though, was the owner, Will. He made certain to personally chat with every patron, and was eager to share his excitement over their products with us. It was easy to give him our business & we will definitely revisit if we're ever I'm Nashville again!

Underwhelmed at best.

The quantity of meat, cheese etc. on the Back in the Saddle sandwich was skimpy at best and lost in the "pretzel " bun which itself was uninspired.  The gooey butter wedge was rather dry and just not very good, and the granola wedge was merely so-so.  I had already purchased a full gooey butter cake to go and should have returned it, but hoped the piece I had with lunch wasn't representative.  Worse, the full one was badly overcooked and conspicuously burned all around the outside.  A steel knife required considerable force to break, more than cut, through the crust.  Talking about a gooey butter cake!!

I had also asked to buy a loaf of banana pecan nut bread and after a blank stare and asking again was told that I could buy it only by the slice.  Huh?  "Or you can order in advance." Oh well, lost sale.  Perhaps they can't predict demand and would rather lose some sales than have them go to waste (or sell at discounts).  Always a tough choice I'm sure, but another strike from me.

So overall not a good experience.  I can't imagine anyone rating the sandwich I had as good value, or as very good let alone "special" in any way.  (Reminds me a bit of McAlisters in that way and I've never understood why they are popular.)  But what really gets me is the obviously burned gooey butter cake.  Somebody took that from the oven.  Likely someone else wrapped it in plastic and put it in a box to sell.  Were they blind or just didn't care?  If you are trying to be an upscale trendy place and charging extra for it ($10 for a smallish gooey butter cake) then you can't let something like that get onto the shelf.  It speaks volumes and not in a good way.

The soups looked good so I may try again some day for them, but I'm not in a hurry.

Oh my gosh my young adult daughter and I love this place!  We were so sad when Companion in Clayton closed!  The whole wheat bread is moist and hearty goes well with the real butter it is served with!   We often order Tough Love salad that comes along with it ( not the other way around!!!!) with spinach, avocado, sunflower seed and other joys--- so tasty!!!! really makes you want to eat healthfully.  A menu full of salads, soups and Sam switches to explore:  so unique and creative that we used them to cater our daughter's Ladue High School grad party with a variety of sandwiches and cookies ( I bought drinks and fruits) and had many compliments!!!

If you like cold food please go & enjoy yourself.   Worse service & food.    They don't deserve a star at all.   Save your money & eat that two year old can of Campbell's tomato soup.   You will be better off trust me!

Better than any other donut I've ever had in Nashville.. maybe top 3 donuts I've ever had in my life. Super welcoming family vibe when you walk in, delicious coffee, and very comfortable to sit back on their couches. Also free parking in the back :) this place is awesome

I have never been so satisfied with a place before in my life!! The staff here is beyond incredible and are so helpful for literally anything. You can tell how proud they are of their ingredients and quality of food. They should be, everything was amazing. The donuts, the dog, the fries. Heaven. I'm a vegetarian and so is my sister so we just enjoyed donuts, fries, and pretzel bites but her boyfriend got the chili queso dog and said he was angry at how good it was. We had no complaints for anything. They also have a killer playlist which is always nice when eating somewhere. I absolutely love this place. We got there in late noon so donut options were a bit limited but still amazing. My sister got espresso and said it was amazing and her boyfriend also got coffee and enjoyed it. 5/5 place and people. Recommend for anyone in Nashville or passing through. I save my 5 star yelp reviews for the ultimate places and this is the second place in Nashville that is 100% 5 star worthy.

Friendly office. Casts a lot of stuff. Be prepared to share the waiting room with the resident casting dog. Parking can be tough. Not a bad walk from septa stop if you bus into 30th street or Chinatown.

Dr lee is the worst, i went to the dentist on monday had no cavities. I came here as an emergency  (re eval) and she found 11. There is no way! Then they have these little dividers that are supposed to be for privacy but I can clearly see and hear whats going on with the other paitents. The dr is very rude to paitents and her assistants. Never coming here again and im reporting this place!!!

The food is piping hot and fresh. My husband and i ordered the chicken schwarma and the meat lover's pizza. The staff is very friendly and the food was absolutely yummy. I can see why people love this place! I would definitely recommend to everyone and next time we visit Philly we'll be sure to go here again.
Worst service ever. They took forever just for a happy meal and a large fries and they give me my order wrong.

I was visiting philly from NYC. One of my friends suggested this place. I liked the ambience to start with. So we ordered a couple of things, zu zu chicken fries were so delicious I have not had such fries in NYC. Ordered a chicken sandwich that was sooooo tasty. Also ordered a lamb wrap, the wrap was good but not spicy probably I forgot to mention that I want it spicy. I would totally recommend this place if u r hungry n looking for quick bites. The guy at the register was too polite.

I love that Metrolink goes to and from the Airport and to major destination spots like Busch Stadium ect.  Other cities should take note. I was a visitor  and was pleased with the service Metrolink provided. Easily accessible, Convenient, quick travel from point A to B. No cab needed in this city. Its just like any other light rail service, smooth ride and fairly inexpensive from what I'm used to in California. I use public transportation everyday and I have traveled a lot. Metrolink is one of the better transportation systems.

I agree with other posters. If you go to DC which has an extensive great transit system, Metrolink doesn't compare. They need to find a way to put tickers on the train so that people with cards/tickets should go through the gate and not get hassled by security guards when they are on the train. Also in DC, they have this card which can be used on all forms of transportation and rather than having tickets you can use this card to go anywhere-- its like a debit card. All you gotta do it tap it on the payment thing on the bus or at the gate to the metro and youre in. Simple. I wish the metro  had it. 

Nevertheless, I love the Metro. I love what it has done for me personally and for the people of STL-- help us save money and gas! Outside of the problems I listed above and your occasional thief, beggar, masturbator, pisser, pothead, drinker, loud person (e.g., whether its a kid from East Saint who think he/she can have step practice on the metro or the rich businessman who expects the train to go faster when he curses and screams at it- -guess what asshole, the driver can't hear you) it is a wonderful system! I am appalled that more people don't rely on it like in other cities. It's not just for Cards games! 

Please note that chaning/expanding Metro is about money. Again, I am ashamed for this city that people do not use it more. In other cities everyone uses them. Here, I only see Illinois residents and-- I'll be frank about this-- underprivileged black people. This system won't make any money if certain people only use it. We're in freaking Missouri, a conservative state. The gov doesn't care if Metro is helping people; they wont vouch for it if it ain't paying out, it won't expand, just collapse. MAKE METRO WORK, PEOPLE!

If you are looking for fresh sushi, this is the place you should go. The sushi-6-step, that is 6 different favors of salmon is very tasty. The service is very attentive. I'll definitely be going back.

Bought the groupon for $49 and received the worst cleaning I've ever had in my life. The hygienist drenched my back with the water and the cleaning took 10 minutes...I made an appointment for 4:00 and was taken in to get X-rays around 4:30. I do not recommend unless you have state insurance. Then you really have no choice. This place is one of those dental offices that take state insurance, give minimal and crappy dental care, take 179930 patients a day. I was out of there by 4:53. The cleaning took maybe 7 minutes.
I've booked through Heery a few times- a great on camera office in the Philly area that knows their stuff!

This was my first time coming here and it was on a Saturday afternoon. The guy who took our order was very nice and patient with us as I changed my order twice and he didn't seem to mind at all. The food came out in about 5 minutes and was delicious!  The environment is really unique because you can see them making the breads all around you with each process labeled. We will definitely be back!

Taking only 1 star away because of the poor service, because I hope that's just a factor of the new restaurant. It wasn't very busy, but our drinks were never refilled and it took a long time to get anybody's attention for the check. I also noticed alot of customers coming in confused because nobody was on staff to welcome them or instruct them what to do.

On to the food.... the chicken was great. West county is in dire need of a sit down chicken joint and this place has the food and location to make it. If it doesn't make it, it will be because of the lack or service, but im pulling for it to be great!

Give the creamed corn and dark meat a try. Disclaimer: If i go back in a month and the service isn't improved, I'll have a hard time going back.
Always pleasant experience with friendly employees. The drinks are consistent and taste great.
Right in the middle of downtown!  Can't give it 5 stars because it always seems dirty and used.  Security is ALWAYS posted at this one so it's safe IMO.

We ordered 4 lattes, a quiche and an Ooh La La sandwich for breakfast. Enough for 4 people.  Delicious! 

We also got pumpkin-cranberry bread to go. They sliced it for us and it's really good.

This is a well established and great Cracker Barrel.  The food is always hot and fresh.  The servers are friendly and there are lots of cool items in the old country store.  Be sure to check out the clearance items in the back.  Great iced tea.

Not going back. The majority of the staff members I observed had horrid attitudes, talked down to several people while I was there, and gossiped about patients in front of everyone else the moment said patients left. I was treated nicely in a very insincere way while I was there. I suppose I should be grateful for that much considering the way other patients were being treated.

Expect to suddenly have a multitude of expensive problems with your teeth that need to be addressed even if you've never had so much as a cavity your entire life. They're only after your money and will fall over themselves with their contradictory statements in an effort to get more money out of you.

The only reason I give this place two stars instead of one is because of the dental hygienist who worked on my teeth. She was genuinely nice and never tried to push unnecessary and expensive procedures on me.

Edit: December 2015

I have now found a different dentist that I actually like going to. He did a very thorough check up when I came in due to pain. The advanced gum disease and serious infection of the wisdom teeth that Flawless Dental Group told me I had were nowhere to be found. In fact, many of the problems Flawless Dental said I needed to fix turned out to be non existent as I had suspected. These people really will make anything up to get more money out of you.

Ahi (the previous sushi restaurant in this location) was my regular "go-to" sushi place and it was very good.  Sun Sushi is even better.  Stopped in this evening and was pleased to see it was busy but had room or one more.
Ordered the steamed edamame  spicy tuna roll and California roll (I'm stuck in a 90's rut).  It was delicious fresh and worthy of 5 stars.
The wait staff were cordial and attentive but not overly so (as stated in other reviews). I have found a new "go-to" place.
I will try the 6-step salmon next time.  Saw it at the next table and it looked delicious.

I checked this place out for the first time this past Saturday March, 1 2014. The setting is beautiful, and much of the food....well OK. The soups were a hit, and there really was not a salad bar. Fruit, yes, but the "salad bar" consisted of a small bowl of dried out lettuce, NO toppings like eggs, mushrooms, bacon bits,etc...The small bowl of cheese for the salad was sitting on the counter top and was not being kept cool! There were plenty of meat offerings, and i was not sure how to order noodles. Some of the dishes displayed appeared that they had been"waiting for me" they were truly dried out and un edible  if not also unappetizing. As for hot veggies there were none except for ears of corn that people were not touching because the sign over it said "corn soup" and the lone vegetable on the steam table was green beans. No mashed potatoes/gravy, peas, spinach, greens-NOTHING! Also, you had to ask for silverware and the server acted like she did not understand us, and kept removing our plates before we were finished-wow! Comparing to the other area buffets if you want to really get a hardy meal at a cheaper price go to New China Buffet across the street. If you like sushi come here. The grills to order your own food is better, but in comparison to ones nearby it is also weak. A "thumbs up"for the individual ice cream cups-now those I really liked! Do not plan on returning but will never say never!

I went for a late lunch and the place was fairly empty, yet the hostess insisted on bundling everyone together. I guess so the waiter didnt have to look around to see who he was ignoring.  I neither found the place "elegant" or special, but it was fairly clean.

I was impressed by some of the offerings on the buffet,  spicy pork intestine, bbq pork foot those are things you normally dont see on a buffet.  Many of the dishes had been sitting too long, it was obvious. Their potstickers were pretty good, however my kung pao chicken lacked any punch. Nothing else was really memorable. 

The hostess asked me for my opinion on the way out, and I appreciated that. 

Will I go back? Maybe with a groupon and a friend,.

Great place!!!  Fresh bread, excellent sandwich, salad, bread and cookie choices!!!

This place is busy, but service is quick!!  Lots of matching options!!!

Honestly I think I've missed something here. I chose Sun Sushi based on the percentage of 5 star ratings on Yelp. I called at 7:00 p.m. to make last minute reservations for 7:30 that evening, Friday. I was told by a women I spoke to that they were all filled and there was a line out the door. With that said, My friend and I thought to just just drive by and see for ourselves and or find another place to dine. We arrived at 7:30 no line and there were open seats at the sushi bar along with 3 empty tables... 

When we entered the restaurant the gentleman asked if we had a reservation and I told I called and the women that answered would take one. Anyway, We were seated. Service was very OK. It took me to finally get the attention of a server to take out drink and food order.

We ordered the Soft Shell Crab Tempura Appetizer, Salmon Skin Roll, Yellow Tail, Uni, Salmon, Sweet Shrimp, Smelt Egg with Quail Eggs and Halibut Sushi along with a Salmon-6-Step.

All the fish was of OK quality not the best. the Yellow Tail smelt a little fishy. The Smelt Egg presentation was sloppy with eggs falling off and the Quail Eggs about to drip off. The Salmon-6-Steps was very OK too. The Uni was not the price listed on the menu in fact it was an outrages $15 (isn't Santa Barbara famous for their Uni?) The worse part of the meal was the Tempura Crab and Fried Shrimp Heads. I don't know where they get the recipe from but it certainly was not Tempura which should be served HOT in temperature and light in batter. The coating was a very heavy batter and all the fried food was barely room temperature.. so bad was the Crab that I had to pick off the batter to eat the crab. 

Food OK, Tempura horrible, Service OK.

I wasn't impressed.  I had the creme brûlée donut. The filling tasted like vanilla pudding and the topping was a bit too bitter so there wasn't a good balance of flavors to me. The chili queso dog was ok but I wouldn't order it again. The hotdog was kinda hard and spicy and the chili was too sweet for my taste.  Truffle fries were good. Visit at your own risk of spending nearly $20 for 1 person (Dog, fries, donut), but I would not recommend it.

First time we had a miscommunication with the reservation but we went back the next week and had an amazing meal.   The selection was traditional and also very unique.  We ate so much because we wanted to try everything.  Great service, good prices but make a reservation.  It is a small place and limited seating.  Can't wait to go back.

One of the best sushi restaurants in Santa Barbara - quite possibly my new favorite! The guys behind the bar were great, and the sushi was amazingly delicious - obviously fresh, high-quality fish skillfully and artfully prepared.  Wonderful service, wonderful sushi.  I will definitely be back soon and often!

I work at the airport, and have worked in customer service for 15+ years. The staff on Wednesday is terrible. They never say "Hi, how are you?" or anything of the sort. It's always, "Can I take your order?" 

Today, I ordered a grilled chicken wrap. Half of it was cold. I took it back up and explained my concern. The person at the counter went to the back, and the manager said, "It's cold?" in a tone of disbelief. The rep at the counter brought me another one and said, "It's the lettuce that's making it cold." 

I didn't argue, because you can't argue with apathy. Terrible service.

Hailing from Cincinnati, where light rail transit is merely a dream, I was ecstatic to discover St. Louis's MetroLink. I stayed at the Sheraton, which is conveniently located right across the street from the Civic Center Station. MetroLink was quick and efficient, and while being thoroughly used, it was never uncomfortably crowded. I opted for a day pass for $7.50, as I frequently hopped on and off exploring the city.

Unlike the traditional rapid transit system, MetroLink does not have a turnstyle to check tickets, like you may find in New York City. Instead, patrons hold onto their tickets, and security guards will get on at random stops to make sure no one is hopping a free ride. Out of the dozen rides I took on MetroLink, security only boarded once. However, I did see them arresting two teenagers who were free riding.

Compared to larger cities, MetroLink is a simple light rail system to use: it only has two lines. My only complaint is that I did get lost a few times because the maps at the stations were backwards: Illinois was left of Missouri. See:http://s3-media1.px.yelpcdn.com/bphoto/t2vBZtfq4keMIn5qEu-G2g/l.jpg

I have no idea why the map is printed this way in some locations, particularly since these were all at Missouri stations, not on the Illinois side.

Cincinnati desperately needs a light rail system, however residents are slow to get on board. St. Louis, being a city of comparable size to Cincinnati, is a wonderful example as how light rail can help both commuters and tourists travel with ease.

Notes for tourists:
 - Purchase a day pass for $7.50. It's good the entire date of purchase for infinite rides.
 - Pick up a map of the routes
 - Pay attention to the map at the stations, as some have Illinois on the left side of Missouri, not on the right.
 - If you need to transfer trains, pay attention to the color-coded destination signs located on the front and side of the train cars. This will help you know which line you are getting on.
 - There is also a MetroLink stop that will drop you off at Gateway Arch, and another near Citygarden. Most high-traveled areas Downtown are accessible through the Metro.

80's music greets you to this place cafe. A full coffee bar, bakery and cafe with bright, ample, well designed seating. There are both indoor and outdoor options, free wifi and fresh bread!! I ordered the the Clintonian breakfast sandwich ($7.25) : egg, cheese, bacon, lettuce, tomato. Refillable coffee ($2.65). The sandwich comes on a croissant but I substituted a poppy seed bagel. I don't see a lot of outlets that's a bummer. I work from home and sometimes need a change of scenery. After 11am they have fresh soups... I'm going to make a trip back to try. Today's choices are Clam Chowder, Manhattan Clam Chowder, Split Pea & Ham and Buffalo Chicken.

This is a teaching school and there is large, panoramic window that allows you to view the students learn how to bake commercially.

I went there with a friend and we had the Zuzu's burger, Zuzu's fries and pesto pizza. All of them were amazing! You could clearly see they didn't compromise on quality and I was more impressed when I found out they had just opened. The staff and the owner were very friendly as well. Definitely coming back soon and recommending it to all my friends.

Update: Went there a few more times and tried more of their selection, including the shawarma and a few other varieties of pizza, still in love with the place and their quality!

The juices are pretty good, so they have that, but that's about all they have. Get it together! You are a business, act like one! My experience dealing with the folks at Catalyst has been simply terrible, and from what I've heard I'm not alone. 

Correspondence is not timely, and sometimes totally non-existant. Emails were always answered at odd hours- 1:45am, midnight, etc. Are they being farmed out to another country or are they really that busy that they're answering emails so late at night? Perhaps hire some temps for post New Years craziness...it's not rocket science. 

I purchased a Living Social deal for $99, a three day cleanse plus a $25 gift card to Jar Bar. I had the intent of using it in a very specific way, unfortunately I could no longer do so because Jar Bar has since changed locations. After contacting the company regarding ordering a cleanse and to find out how I could still redeem my $25 gift certificate they replied:

"The specified $25 gift card is more of a credit, which you may use toward the purchase of another cleanse. I've attached our JAR BAR menu also, in case you'd like to order $25 worth of pre/post cleanse food items you'd might like to pick up along with your cleanse." 

The "more of a credit" part pissed me off. I know what a gift card is, just because they moved locations doesn't change the terms of their living social deal. I sent an email asking if I could order an additional four juices, any of them, from the Jar Bar menu. As I wasn't sure if I could use it for the Spring Garden location I asked if that was a possibility. I also requested at 1/10 pickup for juices. Days went by, no response. Finally I forwarded my email to another one of their email addresses late Wednesday night to see if I could instead do a 1/13 pickup since I hadn't heard from them. At 1:43am I received the below "oops we're sorry" email. 

"I'm so sorry Abigail....You are in fact scheduled for tomorrow, my records indicated you had been sent confirmation. You will receive a reminder tomorrow morning for any info needed such as pick up address and phone number. Thank you for your patience and understanding, it is indeed a very busy time;))"

Not only was the request for extra juices/question ignored, I am not confident that I would have ever received additional correspondence regarding my cleanse pick-up, which would have been forfeited. 

My assumption was that it was all a go, including the extra juices. I was also made to assume I was not going to be able to start a juice cleanse, and therefore did not prepare as thoroughly as I would have. 

Now on to the awful face to face interaction...
I arrived around 6pm at the Spring Garden location to pick up my juices. Imagine my surprise when the building was not marked with any Catalyst information, including on the multiple (five or six) doorbells. I called the number on the email, no answer, it went right to voicemail. I called the other number from the website, no answer. So...I had to press every single doorbell in order to receive my juices. At this point I was called "sweetie" by whomever was delivering my juice to me. Seriously? Is it 1955? Patronizing customers by calling them sweetie is absolutely disgusting and simply makes a company look ignorant. When I was met with my juices I was scolded that the email instructions say to call the number on the email (they do not) and when I explained that they don't actually say that, and that I did indeed call, showing the call on my phone, the girl was confused and shocked. Because I was so flustered from the pick up experience it didn't even occur to me to look for the extra juices. I got home and to my dismay there were none.  The entire experience from beginning to end felt like an awful experiment in bad customer service and business practices. I would never recommend Catalyst to anyone after the terrible experience I had.
Zuzu's is perfect. A local to-go place with wide variety of food. All of which does not disappoint. And to top it off they couldn't be more accommodating.

Great for visitors like myself coming from the airport and wanting to go to your downtown hotel. Cheap and efficient mode of transportation that can get you to places without having to put up with traffic. Compared to my normal light-rail experience, I like how the trains don't have to stop for street traffic since they are partially underground and away from the street traffic flow. I thought the method of validating the ticket after buying it was a little redundant, but hey, as long as it works, that's all that matters.

Great addition to the neighborhood! We liked it when it was Ahi but the service was slow and frustrating when hungry. The service tonight was impeccable, the fish fresh, the rice perfect and the rolls tight. The chicken teriyaki appetizer had enough for a meal. We are loving the new decor too! Come check it out, you won't be disappointed

this place has the HIGHEST quality fish, they must be paying big bucks to get fish that tastes this good. I haven't ever had the pleasure of eating fish that tastes this great. I do also really enjoy the service here because of how quickly they seat you and help you

Came here for a late dinner while we were in town for a conference and were staying at a nearby motel. Good ol' Cracker Barrel came through for us after a weary day of traveling. It was homey food and we all got what we wanted (including me, a vegetarian!) 

We were seated right away. Server was very polite and gave us time to peruse their huge menu. Breakfast available all day. 

I put together a Country Vegetable Plate with mac and cheese, country green beans, steamed broccoli, and a baked potato which also came which choice of biscuit or corn bread. So much food! 

They brought our drinks right away and our server was excellent and attentive to refills and clearing plates out of our way without being obtrusive to our conversations. 

Dependable and consistent. We had a great experience here and would definitely be back if we were in the area.

I've been here about twice/month for the past 3 months or so and it is the same woman working there by herself. Each time I'm there, it's never busy, but I've noticed that it is in desperate need of a cleaning and it gets worse with each subsequent visit. The restroom is particularly bad, which is a huge deal for me personally. If I had to guess, I'd say that the woman there is the franchisee and housekeeping is low on the list of priorities. It's a shame because even though the neighborhood leaves much to be desired (it is the East after all), it's still a nice, quiet spot. I have no problems with the service or anything I've ordered, it just really stands out as very unclean which is unlike any other PJ's I've patronized. On my last visit there was a help wanted sign in the window. So hopefully it gets resolved quickly.

Metrolink
There is so much potential for this train system but Metro does not take advantage of it. First there was the disaster that was the Blue line and then after passing Prop A, they haven't increased frequency across the board. A 20 minute wait is pretty bad when you are trying to catch a bus. Missing one train can set you back by an hour more. 

Often there is little to no open seats and when Cards fans get on board they often block the doorway and make it impossible to maneuver. Its irritating and makes it so obvious that most of those fans have no idea how to use public transportation.

My biggest complaint with Metrolink is that they are always under construction causing delays and even closures of stations, particularly the ones most important for me. This causes a great big inconvenience. 

MetroBus
Bus drivers tend to be rude, and do not enforce the not eating rules or no loud music rules making it an uncomfortable experience. The buses run about once every 40-60 minutes making them very inconvenient. Most do not run Sunday so getting to the nearest bus can take just as long itself. 

Buses rarely connect with trains or the train does not wait long enough for bus riders to get on board. Bus drivers do not allow riders to board the bus during the 20 minute wait time before they leave even when its scalding hot, freezing out, or rainy. You usually have to report the bus driver in order to get them to allow passenger boarding.

Bus stops are poorly placed. On some streets there are just too many such as on Rock Road which causes the bus to stop at nearly every stop and be late. While in other places there aren't enough. 

If you had no choice and had to take public transportation AVOID the bus at all cost!

Great breakfast spot! Had my first nitro brew which was sooooooo good and smooth. Donuts are out of this world. Owner is very passionate about his business and it definitely shows. Wouldn't hesitate to come back.

The sushi chefs were very attentive and customer service was excellent. This place is great to go when you want a casual date night spot but great sushi. The place is not loud so you will be able to talk with your date or party and you are in and out so no long wait times.

You get great quality and big rolls for the amount you pay. I got the 6 ways salmon which comes on an awesome display wooden plank. My favorite was the yellowtail delight roll because it was large and filling! The chefs really put their passion and creativity into creating great sushi.

I have had Century Link landline service for 3 months, I have had trouble with every time that it rained the line went dead, so I called the first time it happened and my friend fixed it, we then thought it was a problem with our inside equipment, i.e. landline phones,  so I called that first time and the repair would take place that same day within a couple of hours, then I cancelled because we thought we had fixed it, the second time it happened, two days ago, same thing they sent a repair person that day, I am very impressed with them and do not want to find out about how bad the DSL is, we still have Cox for internet/streaming, all I do know is that in this case I really like them and feel that if I have more trouble I will have help because of this company.

PJs is my favorite coffee in New Orleans probably my favorite coffee in the country. The coffee is exquisite it not to mention the southern flavors they offer for hot and iced coffee's. Granita's are their specialty and worth a try for sure. This PJs location in particular definitely needs a bit of a facelift. It's a great location near UNO and one of few coffee shops in the area. There is plenty of space to work inside. They offer free Wi-Fi for customers a great place to do some work or study. They definitely need to do a deep clean of the place it just looks a bit dirty. PJs is always five stars in my book but the actual atmosphere made me drop it down to a three.

Terrific new sushi spot for locals right next to Tee Off. Real Japanese chefs, fresh fish & great service. Complete meal, nice addition to the SB dining scene. Very fresh fish which is primordial for sushi. Great meal!

Ahi used to be my favorite sushi place in the city.  It was certainly the most authentic and cost less than Arigato.  Good food doesn't seem to guarantee success in this city.  The quality faded over the years, and finally it closed its door.  Sun sushi continues the tradition of offering choices that you can't get anywhere else in the city.  The salmon 6 steps was impeccably fresh.  My favorite was the buttery lightly seared nigiri.  Two of the pieces were a little too tart in my opinion.  I also loved the cubed salmon served in the spoon.  They were all delicately seasoned and should be eaten without any soy sauce that might muddle the flavor.  The Japanese scallop was silky and sweet.  The snow crab was topped with crab miso, a sauce made with crab liver.  Its one of those flavor that makes whole crab so much tastier than pasteurized crab meat.  The spicy tuna with crispy rice was similar to the version served at Nikka Ramen.  Sun Sushi's was less sweet and the crispy rice was more manageable in size.  The udon could use some change.  They went overboard with the seaweed and by the time all the seaweed were rehydrated, the soup became too salty.  The tempura side need to be reconfigured.  The broccoli and onion were cut too big, therefore, the middle of the broccoli had undercooked dough while the onion was still raw.  I was disappointed that I no longer see the 5 course omakase meal on the menu.

I wish all cities had a Metro. Take it from the airport. A cab from the airport to downtown for two people is $60-$70 for $3-$7 you can wait 20 minutes and take the Metro. The Metro will pretty much take you to any tourist stop, but you have to walk and wait awhile, in the end we saved a ton of cash. It was easy to understand the routes, and very affordable. I felt safe 99% of the time. 

The other 1%
However, be careful at UNION STATION stop. We saw some shit go down there, but you probably shouldn't stop at Union Station anyways, what a disappointment.

While the baked goods are fantastic, I've never really enjoyed their cafe items. Today I ordered the broccoli cheddar soup with a side of bread, but after eating it, I wish I had just gone to the Bread Co down the street instead. There were two enormous pieces of broccoli in my soup. They could have been cut down smaller. In addition, the broccoli stem was inedible anyway. The outside had separated from the inside and t was truly the weirdest broccoli I've attempted to eat. In the last, I've had subpar sandwiches here. The only reason I'm giving three stars is because I'm in love with their cheesecake brownies and fresh bread. Oh well, maybe I'll give the food another chance in the future.

Unfortunately I cannot give them less than one star. Walking in was confusing. You follow some chickens on the floor up to a counter and we asked the guy, do we order here and he says nah, just grab a table. We order here for lunch. We were not the only ones confused by this as we watched two other customers leave since there was no one to ask. 

Took us longer than you would expect to get our order going and then FOREVER for the food to come out. With the long wait and the fact that this place serves chicken, that's it, I was hoping for a spectacular piece of fried chicken. Was not to be. I ordered the 3 piece dark plate. Should have been two thighs and a leg. When the food finally came I had two legs and a breast. The fried chicken was bland. Unbelievably bland. The breast was dry and overlooked. My wife had a seared breast and she said it very bland. My mother-in-law had the fingers and hers were dry tasteless and over cooked. 

All around this was a poor showing for a "new" restaurant. If they continue like this it will spare the masses and will never become a staple.

My country fried steak and gravy was tasteless.
My seasonal veggies were cold.
My fries were cold and old.
Our cornbread was forgotten.
We were seated relatively fast.

was having major problems with my car..  other places nearby estimated almost double than what i was charged here.  they were able to fix my car for a great price and now i don't trust anyone else.  the prices that i were charged were broken down for me step by step and i don't feel like i was taken advantage of, which i felt like in other places. have had no issues since, all noises are now gone. great management and great place, definitely recommended.

It's not on the menu but they will make it for you if you ask....Spinach alfredo pizza... delicious. Their pizza is excellent and they have several different specialty ones. All very good. All of their food is very good. Argentos is one of my favorite places around.

It's CB people, a tradition in itself.   This is a great location that I have had the pleasure of frequenting and they have yet to fail me!  Pleasant workers and always great food and portions.  

If it's a friday or a weekend and prime time for dining, you may have a bit of a wait, but that shouldn't come as a surprise.  I noticed a review stating they had food poisoning all night and day after eating chicken here and NOT to eat their chicken! I will not be bossed by a mediocre review, especially when they aren't an avid yelper.

#1- I ALWAYS eat chicken at CB
#2- Only one or two forms of food poisoning have a fast onset of 1-4 hours, all the rest, most common, onset after 6+ hours after ingestion.
#3- Could you write more than a sentence maybe provide a time frame and some facts to back up your poorly diagnosed sickness.
And lastly #4- I do hope you called CB to let them know just what you ingested and when so they can take note if any other patrons become ill.  Otherwise don't bother leaving a negative review via one measly sentence.  

NOW- I had the chicken fried chicken plate with okra, mashed potatoes and hashbrown casserole and it was amazing.  It was my cheat night and I God forgive my gluttony.  I do intend to continue eating lots of poultry from the wonderful country grown establishment.  :)

This Dental Group was proffesional & caring.They are organized & excellent. Dr.Charles Wu was great & so kind.He knows what his doing & always ready &willing to answer your questions.Staff are nice& friendly.Price is reasonable.Clean environment.Xray&Cleaning was amazing!.Highly Recommended!!!

I'm a foodie and this place is paradise. Zuzu's kitchen is a hidden takeout spot in Fairmont that is an absolute gem. I've tried almost everything from their mouth watering Zuzu's burger to their delicious pizzas and their already famous Zuzu's Chicken sandwich. All I can say is..I have never once been disappointed. Whether you are picking up or getting delivery I highly recommend trying Zuzu's kitchen for its freshness, quality, balance and innovative twists to traditional quick eats.

i juice a lot at home and have ordered from 3 different companies. Blue Print Cleanse in my favorite. It has pineapple mint juice that is amazing. That being said Catalyst is very good and satisfyes me. Customer service is exceptional!!!! Thank you and if the price is right I would definitely do it again.

I love this cracker barrel.  Some of these reviews suprise me as I've been here so many times and not had any of these experiences.  Maybe I'm just lucky.  As for slow service, the only reason it would be slow is if it's busy.  And, btw, this is a CB in case to missed the first mention; they are generally always busy and for good reason.

If some of these reviews saying this place has slow service..  I would venture to say you should probably be at a McDonalds drive thru to be in and out.  Honestly.  Now there are some unacceptable instances I'm certain now and again, but with a little common sense, one can distinguish if something's not right or if it simply is because the capacity reached in the restaurant. 

Anyways. Visit for yourself, don't take my word for it and if you find something not up to par, give them a chance to fix it.  These guys and gals aim to please and will within their best resources.
POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE & HORRIBLE COFFEE!! Owner was very rude and had an attitude for no reason. When I told her I would not return because of the poor customer service she said that was fine.

Horrible customer service- worst I have ever seen. See they are being sued by multiple AG's for deceptive billing. No idea how this place stays in business. Spent 3 hours on the phone and received 6 different answers.

I'm so glad there's another donut shop in the area besides 5 Daughters. Tried their OG Donut and it was so good! Also tried their smoked caramel latte, which was just as good and fun to watch being made. I can't wait to go back and try their hotdogs/other donuts as well.

Customer service was top notch as well. The owners were very nice, as was the barista at the register. The space is great, and they have a (dog friendly) patio with picnic tables.

Update: hotdogs are fantastic, and you can't beat their $10 power lunch deal. Be sure to follow them on Instagram, as they'll often post exclusive specials in their stories!!

Awesomeness place for a great meal at $7.99
You can never go wrong thanks for the great meal 
A suggestion... remove the lobby items and place
More tables ...had to wait 30 minutes to be seated

If you like Quality pastries like me! We know that quality product makes quality pastries. Little Kitchen Pastries bring extra smile with delightful party in our mouth, every time we are here. This place takes their time, dedication and love of baking that is no where to be found in Treasure Valley. I believe pastries is art and this place has the best French Croissants, Danish, Caramel Pecan Buns. And more! Be here early and because they close at 2:30pm. Don't forget to request Lemon Almond  Braid - you will love every it.

Great fresh sandwiches, salads, bread ... and of course sweets. Get a good meal for $10-12. They always have a few good specials.

Pro Tip is to order ahead online. Lunch line is very long, then when you finally get to order you have to wait for them to make your fresh food.
Worst chicken sandwich I've ever had at Wendy's. Old cold and just plain nasty. I guess you get what you get at the airport.
This is one of my favorite local joints for a quick to go dinner. The owner is super nice and the food doesn't disappoint! My favorites are the zuzu salad with steak or the roasted veggie sandwich

My fave PJs in the city. The baristas are always super friendly, and although I try to limit my trips (lattes and cappuccinos add up!), I notice that they know who their regulars are and know their orders as soon as they walk through the door. 

The vibe is great; a lot of students from the local university come to this location to study and unwind. It's very homey, and I would love to go one day and just sit and people watch. 

I'm definitely not a coffee expert, so my knowledge on the quality should be ignored, but, in my HUMBLE opinion, I think the espresso drinks are way less bitter than other local coffee chains. My friend who lives in the area, too, disagrees, so again, take my opinion on that aspect with a grain of salt. However, if you're looking for a good atmosphere, patient and kind baristas, and am inexpensive cup of Joe...this should be your spot.

An amazing weekend spot! Outside smells like pretzels and inside is a spacious surprise. Inside or outside eating available. I got an espresso and gooey butter cake bite. Very moist and just enough as an afternoon snack. Menu looks flavorful and everyone seemed to enjoy the food! The workers were polite and helpful.

The good -
I've gone a couple times here for diagnosing problems, and also the routine oil check. Matt is really helpful and friendly ( I think he's the manager). The gentleman that helped me today is also very personable, friendly -- does all the right things (thanking you for your business today etc).

This would have been a higher rating except this morning's experience.. I scheduled an appointment online for 8:00am -- sat there for about 15 to 20 minutes, and no one opened the door, no voicemail, and no one answering the phone. If I were late to my job, I would be fired on the spot -- so I'm kind of a stickler for this. Posted hours on the door: 8:00 am to 6:00pm -- not a soul in sight

Other than that, I like the customer service overall.. except for the whole not being there on time today, and also not knowing the mail in rebate for oil change that was found on their website. Friendliness is there, personable /personality is there -- but professionalism may need a little bit of work.

Really enjoyed my early lunch at companions. Got a caramel macchiato, granola bite, tough love salad and corn bread. Really enjoyed it all separately but put together it was all interesting taste wise. Loved the tough love salad. Almost wish the lemon vinaigrette had a stronger lemon flavor. Pleased with the taste combo of the salad. Love their cornbread. Best cornbread I've ever had. It's very moist and you don't see a lot of moist cornbread. Their portions are huge. You get a lot of bang for your buck. Macchiato was good. Love kaldis espresso. Also love their granola bites. Just the right amount of sweetness.
The best Almond Crossiant I've ever tasted!  Delivery is accurate and on time.  Most definitely my go to bakery!

Hmmmmm....I don't really know how I am really feeling about the Metrolink....hence the three stars...I'm just...undecided....(but I am a loyal every day rider so I'm clearly not THAT disgruntled)

I mean....it's so much better than what we had here a few years ago (which was nothing) and it is probably the cleanest public transportation I have ever been on.  It is pretty on time...which is excellent.  You can always find a seat, also great.  I love that you can take your bike on it, and there's always room to prop it up somewhere near the front of the car, and honestly, the price isn't bad ($60 for a monthly pass that you can use on the bus and the light rail...I mean, that's standard American public transportation prices...so I'll take it)  Also, free parking at many of the stations....awesome....

However.....(and here comes my rant)

I just don't get what Metro is doing here?  I mean, there are two lines that go through, well, not the most logical parts of town.  It's great that they expanded to Shrewsbury, but seriously??  Where are they planning on expanding from there exactly??  Down River Des Peres...well THAT's logical...I mean so many people live next to the sewage river...great planning Metro!  I mean, while you are tearing up 40, why aren't you laying down tracks and making a line out to Chesterfield??  Wouldn't THAT eleviate that traffic problem you facing?      How about instead of planning more lines to North County you shoot something out to South County (down 55 or Gravois??) or out to West County who doesn't have the public transit??  (say 44 or Manchester???)

And sure, your trains run on time, but they only run every 20 MINUTES!!!  I mean, come on!!!!  20 minutes to wait for a train???  I lived on arguably the worst line in Boston and I'm telling you, it was NEVER that bad...(ok it was...but not on a regular basis...at least it was scheduled to come every 7 minutes)

And finally...WHAT is with your honor system???  You claim you are bankrupt...well...how about a train system that actually requires you to have a ticket instead of being the most easily snuck onto light rail in the country???  That might generate some more revenue.

Long story short....it's a great effort Metro.  I know you are trying and I know you are young.  You have made great strides in the short time since you expanded....but my checking account can't take $4/gallon gas.  Get cracking on more lines and more frequent trips, I'd even take better bus lines near parking....I think we can all see the benefit of a public transit system now...oh....and stay open past when the bars close....I beg you....

Was really confused first coming here. I was not sure if it was a store or a factory. I had not heard of it before but found it on yelp when I was in the area. I was pleasantly surprised, the food was really good!

CenturyLink has the very WORST customer service of any company I have ever done business with in my entire life.
They have outsourced some of the most vital customer problems to a foreign country that has awful reception and representatives that need to be offered better classes for them to learn English. I have spent over 3 hours since Monday (today is Wednesday) trying to get a serious issue resolved-to NO avail. Same thing over & over & over...nothing & nothing & nothing. I would not even have given them 1 star, but I had to do that so I could post this complaint for anybody to see & hopefully read. They are a travesty, a sham and a shame. I have already posted my experiences of the past 3 days on FaceBook, and whether or not anybody makes a comment to my post at least they know what a joke CenturyLink is-and likely always will be. I rate them an F- on their report card.
Hey folks, this is a taste like no other!!! Incredible donuts on steroids with flavor leaping onto your tongue. The hotdogs are an explosive aroma of international flavor. Thanks for the taste!!! S&P
Great food and fast service for lunch. Definitely get the gooey butter dessert, its fabulous. Lunch combo is more than enough food and comes with dessert.

Hubs and I have been going to Argento's forever.  It's one of the ONLY Italian food places in the area that my mother actually approves of...and by approve I mean, she didn't :

1) ask for it to be reheated.
2) request that it be made less spicy.
3) ask to have more added to the entree, as it was TOO small.
4) trade it for a different entree altogether.
5) ask to speak to the manager AT ONCE to complain about the first 4 things.

While Estelle insists that even Italy does not make Italian food as good as the Italian food in New York, she has never had an issue with Argento's and this, my friends, is a GOOD thing.  

The atmosphere in Argento's is warm and inviting.  It's kind of like sitting in someones dining room...a 70 year old Italian grandmother's dining room, but that too is a good thing.  The wait staff is always friendly.  Management is great, always taking the time to come visit the tables and make sure your meal is everything it should be.  

Their menu is a laid out as if you were going to your Italian grandmothers house.  It starts with insalatas (salads) and antipasto (appetizers).  Then, it is followed by the kids menu (because you have to feed the little buggers first so you can settle in with your meal, right?) and then, the normal pasta dishes, fish courses, followed by your chickens and veals.  Entrees run between $11.95 and $17.95 depending on whether you order a plain pasta dish or if you order something in the meat/poultry/fish area.  Most are served with soups (oh my god...their soups!) or salad with their amazing house dressing.   For lighter fare, they have stromboli's and gourmet pizzas.

There is a full bar with some pretty interesting cocktails like a blue mango martini or a "chocolate covered cherry".  Drinks run around $7.99.  There is a limited wine selection...a few reds, a few whites and a couple of blush wines.  There is also a limited amount of beer to select from, but a few imports included in that.

The highlight of Argento's is in the back.  They have tons of delicious pastries, cookies, cakes, etc in their bakery.  Desserts can be eaten in the restaurant or taken to go.  They make the BEST BUTTER COOKIES (with chocolate sprinkles! Ummm!) in the world.  You know the butter cookies I am talking about.  The green ones shaped like leaves.  The pink ones shaped like leaves.  The ones that are shaped like pretzels, all with that lovely dark fudgey center.  Or, the plain butter cookies with sprinkles or chocolate chips.  The ones with have cherries on top.  You know, the kind that you bring over to someones house for Christmas or baby showers...things like that.  They are drool worthy.  The have neopolitans, tiramisu, mousse, rice puddings. And, three words for you.  RAIN.  BOW.  COOKIES.  (Technically, that's two words, but I needed to draw it out for emphasis.  Creative license.)  All sorts of delicious baked goods.  Rarely do we ever leave Argento's without at least 3 of those glorious bakery boxes tied in that incredibly hard to cut through twine.  


The only thing I find incredibly annoying about Argento's is their website.  http://www.argentositalianbistro.com/  First of all, it's heavily laden with "flash" and things that move when you don't want them to.  Trying to look at the menu that flips on its own is a real pain in the a$$.  When you pause it for too long, it crashes.  Annoying.  But UBER annoying?  Every single page on the website has this REALLY loud Italian opera type music playing.  Not a problem.  Click "stop" and it stops.  Til you go to the next page. And it starts again.  And you click stop.  Til you go to the next page.  And it starts again.  And you click stop.

Aggravating.  Italian music on the front page?  Fine.  Not a problem.  But when you are trying to click around and take a look at the menu and various other things...to hear this man start howling like a sub par Andrea Boccelli is SO freaking annoying.  I wish I could think of another word than annoying...but its annoying.  

(Feel free to insert: vexatious - bothersome - troublesome - tiresome - pesky)

And under normal circumstances, it would be annoying enough to me to zap a star off their total score.  But the food.  THE FOOD!!!  That, and the fact that I am nom nom nomming on a chocolate chip butter cookie as I am writing this review so its very hard to take a star off when I have this blissful Italian goodness in my mouth.  

I strongly recommend the mussels marinara or the chicken alfredo.  Delish.

Argento's is a bright spot in Hudson...which is in dire need of bright spots.  

Trust me.  If Estelle loved it...you'll be entranced.

I think PJs is the bottom of the barrel in terms of New Orleans coffee shops. This location is the bottom of the bottom - the worst PJs around. From the weird lighting, half burned out at all times, to the awkward layout, to the cold case that seems to be constantly on the fritz. Come here only to prevent caffeine withdrawal.
