It is a shame that this is the closest coffee shop to UNO and SUNO. The students deserve better.

Sun Sushi is a local sushi restaurant with high quality fish.  They don't use much local fish except for uni.  Most comes from Japan and Korea.  Ask Max the owner or John the head sushi chef about the origin of everything.   They will gladly tell you. They have a very nice presentation of their Salmon tower, which includes Scottish and Atlantic salmon and ocean trout.  Very nice flavors.  I also recommend the amberjack--always very fresh.  John makes a very nice monkfish liver, and he will give you a taste to see if you like it before you buy.
Amazing sushi good prices, friendly staff, nice ambiance. Sit at the bar. Get the state street roll

I've always liked this PJ's, but I haven't been in a while. I guess they decided to get a little lazy with their iced latte skills. Just ordered an iced vanilla latte, and instead of taking the time to make the espresso, fresh, I see the girl pull out a pitcher of what?, premade freaking espresso or something? She then proceeds to pour that into a measuring cup to make my drink... No no no. This is not how you make a latte. Put the time and effort into making a delicious shot of espresso for my drink, and maybe I'll be back. Try making with some love. Thanks. 
P.s. it wasn't even busy in there, So why the rush?

I randomly found myself here about three weeks before leaving NOLA. Like most PJ's, pretty decent coffee. The granitas are their speciality thought, like a cooled frappaccino mixed with a slushie- absolutely refreshing on a 100 F 100% humidity day. Pricey, but not a big deal in comparison to Starbucks. Their pastries are crappy though, usually a day or two old and stale, don't get them.
Fast food at the airport. On the plus side, they did get my order right. On the minus side, they got at least one other customer's order wrong. And really, enough with the attitude sweetie.
I like Metro of St Louis. Cheap, efficient, and clean. Save the trouble to find taxi to the airport. The minor problem is that you could not buy one single trip fare with a credit card.

Service is horrendous in every way! Ate there yesterday about 3pm and the server was not friendly or efficient. Refused to answer my question whether they served Coke or Pepsi products.  Kept my credit card for what seemed like forever while she did tasks unrelated to my order. Service was very slow with 10 min wait time. No napkins with my order and not offered Ketchup both of which only available behind they counter.  Clearly better supervision and management is needed.  Wendy's should consider pulling franchise!

My wife n I are here to visit her family its a must that she eats at Cracker Barrel. I was not disappointed. The staff was very friendly. I had the Chicken Pot Pie and salad, it was great. Would I return?? Big yes.

This cafe is ALWAYS busy. But they manage to get people through the line efficiently, food was brought out quickly, and we were able to have a quick and delicious Work lunch on a Monday. I got the Companion lotto with the tough love salad and cinco de mayo sandwich. I went with the tough love salad because it's a healthier option thinking it might not be as tasty the other loaded salads... but it was SO good. I can't wait to go back and get it again. Prices are a little steep but the quality is worth it.

Wish I could rate it zero stars. I spend countless mornings and nights waiting for 20+ min in line here when there are hardly any cars. You need to learn to hire proper people. This is not fast food. This is a pathetic joke. I don't have this problem at any other McDonald's.
Meh. We've all experienced better. Here it sits. We'll come back as a convenience sometime.

I was disappointed for the most part. They have some kind of gross mayonnaise sauce and/or eel sauce on almost every cut roll. Tasted like miracle whip. I felt the menu was limited to many of the same things in different combos. 
On the bright side, the fish tasted fresh. The tempura veggies were pretty good. 
Not a nice strip mall, would not go back. Fairly expensive for what we got.

Food was great, service was great, this place is great. 

Ive been to Sun sushi twice and this most recent visit was really great. I was a little worried about going here since the last time I ate here over a year ago, the restaurant seemed to be going through some repairs and it was very hot in there. This time they have an updated decor with a bamboo wall (with signs that say don't touch) and overall the setup in there looks better. Any who, I went on a Friday night and I did not have a reservation--didn't think I needed one but I would suggest you make s reservation if you know you want to dine here. I had a relatively short 30 minute wait to get seated and while I was waiting the staff was friendly and attentive. 

We had three different special rolls and all were great. We started with the shrimp tempura roll, then the tiger roll, and finally with the sun roll. All were excellent but the one that really stood out was the tiger roll--you could taste the freshness. We ended up ordering a spicy tuna roll at the end because even with three rolls we were still a bit hungry.  

This is a bit of an expensive sushi restaurant but you pay for what you get, I'll definitely be going back for more delicious sushi.

It is good to like the restaurant that your mother works for xD The bakery is exquisite, the pastas are always made just the way I love it, even rivaling my mother's own cooking. The seafood is fresher than ever, and this is the place that caused me to like mussels finally. A great treat.

they are scamming customers. I went in for a state inspection, they told me it would 1 hour to do - 4 hours later they called and said my car did not pass inspection because i needed a new muffler, rear brake adjustment (not even possible on my car BTW), and new windshield wipers. I told them i did not want them to do the work and i would take it to my mechanic. After saying that they got really rude and refused to take the coupon i gave them for the oil change even though they took it before the work was done and said it was fine. The next week I took the car to my mechanic he did an inspection and passed it with no problem - nothing was wrong with the car.... Save yourself time and money and don't go here.

This has got to be one of the best Japanese restaurant in SB. I highly recommend it to everyone who is a Japanese foodie! 

They have  a good variety of food on their menu and they even have sushi omakase style. All the ones that me and my friends tried were really delicious and the fish is of high quality and fresh. Their salmon skin salad is outstanding and by far my personal favorite out of all the foods we tried. 

The ambiance made my dining experience much more enjoyable as it reminds me of Japanese restaurants I went to when I was in Tokyo. 

Service is of course excellent which is always the case with Japanese. Very friendly staff, accommodating and attentive as well.  

I would definitely go back to try their other stuff and I am excited to try their omakase too. This restaurant is a nice addition to the food scene in SB.

This is a great location. It's the only coffee shop servicing the Gentilly and New Orleans East at this time. It's small but very cozy. The workers are absolutely fabulous and  friendly. 

Expect yummy fresh baked  pastries at this location. Try the orange cranberry muffin.

Try out some of the teas at this location.
Top notch Italian food right in little old Hudson Florida. Professional service, and nice atmosphere. A good place to take company from out of town.

We ordered Toro, Amber Jack, Mada and Tamago, as well as shishito tempura and gyoza appetizers. All of it was very good, especially the tamago. Good atmosphere and the sushi chef at the bar was very friendly. Would recommend.

Always packet and service is soooo slow.
I don't even order eggs anyone because they always cold.
They bring you a plate for each item you order.
Really annoying.
Your table will be covered in dishes.
The waitresses won't pre bus tables either so you are always covered up in dishes.
I always have to ask them to get plates out of our way.
Plus, really overpriced for the type of food.
I only go here because of my inlaws!
Other than that I would pass this place right on by.
My inner fat kid has never been happier. The girl behind the counter is the sweetest thing ever. Go. Eat all the things.

The food was great and the kids meal at $7 is a good deal.   The pucker up salad is very good especially if you like grapefruit.    

The kids meal came with a full size cookie and bag of chips.  My kids loved watching the baking process through the window.   It's always busy around lunch M-F, so I suggest arriving early or late to beat the long  ordering line.   We visited 7/20/17.

The light rail trains were clean and saved me money getting from the airport to downtown. 

A few things they could work on to make it a much better and less cumbersome experience:

1. Use automated announcements. Other cities do it. Half the time you cannot hear the train driver make announcements because they are tired and rattle off their script. It's like going to an amusement park ride and hearing the safety briefing muddled into a muffled microphone. Not helpful and annoying. 

2. When you buy a ticket from a vending machine you must pick up the ticket and take it over to another machine to get it validated. Thankfully another passenger told me about it else I wouldn't have done it. Never have I had to do that in any other city on their public transportation. The ticket should have the time stamped on it when you originally buy the ticket. Cumbersome and not intuitive.

I'm surprised the Metrolink hadn't been added to the database. The overground subway system has been an excellent way to get from the Western part of Illinois to downtown STL and all through the city. It has been a cheap, safe way to travel through the city for many years. There are numerous locations to hop aboard the Metrolink. The lines can be pretty lengthy, though, especially after sporting events.

Good sushi and a great staff. The atmosphere was fun and relaxed and the sushi was great.  The Caterpillar Roll looked like it was shrunken (bonsai sushi?) and was adequate.  the fish/shrimp quality was good with the amaebi and albacore being deliicious.  I will have to go back... they ran out of the local uni.

Cute little space for either a meal, snack (donuts), or just coffee! Their donuts and dog buns are brioche-based, so extremely rich and delicious. They have a special donut of the day along with their classics with a good amount of variety in flavors. I would stick with the donuts here, tbh, and I gave minus one star for the just-okay dog I had (though the banh mi dog was quite creative). Really friendly service and staff, and I will come back when my sweet cravings arise.

I've traveled enough to believe perfect public transportation is a myth. I also know there is a significant difference in opinions of mass transit based on whether one uses it to commute or simply to get around during a vacation or brief stay. That said, I believe Metro is a great system for St. Louis.

I've used MetroLink as a visitor to St. Louis and, after moving to the city, as a commuter. In both instances, I've found it affordable, convenient, and effective. As in most cities, I prefer the Metro light rail to the bus system, and I do wish the light rail covered more of the metro area. However, those areas not covered by rail are well-served by buses, making the entire system quite accessible.

Pros:
Reliable schedule, even during rush hour
Reasonably priced
Easily navigable for out-of-towners
Stations are generally well-staffed with friendly folks

Cons:
Limited options for fare (a rechargeable card would be nice)
Limited rail service

I ordered the Fa la la la la sandwich, it had hearty, rustic bread and a delicious cranberry spread but the amount of turkey given was laughable. 7 inches of sandwhich bread with 1mm of turkey...come on. I also had ordered the chocolate cookie and it was incredibly hard and choco chips had a white coating- like why is my cookie fossilizing? Clearly not baked fresh daily. Couldn't even eat it and I also had the pain au chocolat-meh. I've had better at Panera, which is saying something. Wouldn't return
The Best sushi in town!!! Ask for Max, he will fill   all your sushi dreams !!!!!!!!!!

Great food, and great service despite it being Father's Day. Our server Christine was attentive and friendly. As usual the food was really satisfying, despite the portions getting smaller over the years as a price control.
Their sushi and salmon skin salad were very good. The place is nice and service was very good too.

I was very hesitant to try a new sushi place as I only go to Aragato and Sakana here in town.  I live here now but am from Los Angeles originally. LA does not have a lack of good sushi.  Unfortunately Santa Barbra has limited choices. This place had fresh sushi.  The uni was the perfect color.  I also had the Salmon 6 piece taster...perfect!  It was a little on the prices side, but what good sushi in Santa Barbra is it?!?! I would definitely come back and recommend this place to anyone that is a sushi connoisseur.

Michele E. Was our server and she was fantastic. Got in and out of there on a Friday night at 7PM. Food was fast and good! Very pleased since we had been traveling all day and were eager to get back on the road. Way to go team!

Conveniently located by UNO. I'm not a student but I find myself out this way quite frequently and this is the only coffee shop that supports this area.  

I got a almond croissant and a cup of coffee.  Wouldn't get the croissant again but coffee was OK.  Service was nice and quick.

This is one of our favorite lunch spots in Nashville. The donuts are to die for and their hotdogs are delicious. What makes this place even better is the friendly owner, Will. He is always welcoming to everyone that comes in. He introduces himself to new people and is easy to talk to. Extremely friendly and positive person. He's genuinely happy and grateful when you come in. I've never had a bad experience here. Support a local place!

It was busy but we were seated quickly. The place was very clean. We drove in from Texas on our way to Virginia. The hostess was very nice, but as she seated us the girl who was to be our waitress looked at her and said quite sternly, 'You Realize you've seated 3 tables in a row in my section!?' To which the hostess informed her that there was adequate time between the three. That seemed to upset the waitress. 

As a result we received very unfriendly service. When we ordered she wasn't even sure if they made Campfire Soup and had to ask. When my son took a couple of seconds making up his mind she sighed quietly but loud enough to be heard.  I get that things get busy and tempers rise when frustrations are high but it wasn't my fault that we were seated in that section and those conversations should be had away from the customer. 

Our waitress' name was Jessica. From our section we could see a young lady named Rylie. She was HUSTLING!  Wish we'd been in her section!

We stop at Cracker Barrel restaurants because they are generally dependable for service and quality of food. 

Waited 5-10 for refills. Had to ask twice. 
My daughter ordered Campfire Soup and after it being verified it was on the menu, our order came up and THEN the waitress came to say they were out of it. So all the rest of the food came out and my 10 year old had to sit and wait an additional 10 for her grilled cheese. 

I'm sad to say that while my food was good, my experience at this location was not... Disappointing.

We spoke to the manager and she was very kind.

I booked a job through Heery Casting back in May. I was given a call time and location for the job and everything was well organized. I'm not a union member, but was still able to be booked for the production they needed background extras for.

For background work/non-Sag/background work, I can vouch that they are good! I received my check promptly as well (within a month,I think it was). I've never been to their physical office; my only contact has been through email so I don't have any to add about their physical location.
Awesome place - great walk-in breakfast spot with full view of large scale production bakery activity. Check it out!

Would go occasionally to the former Companion in Clayton and also the one in Ladue. Thought these places were good for lunch meetings or when looking for a soup and salad or their amazing tuna. Also think their granola bar is fantastic. However, the new place surpasses with the clean open feel, getting to watch the Bakers, small size desserts and the new menu items, especially the kale salad with the lemony dressing. The new Companion really combines the best of the old with great new ideas.

I loved this place! Everyone I had lunch with enjoyed their sandwich. I got the petite sack lunch and it was more than enough! I had the spring chicken sandwich, side salad with balsamic and the gooey butter bite. All of which were excellent. I will be returning to try more on their menu. 

The inside was very bright and clean. You could see the bakery through large glass windows. Very nice experience!

If you like Quality pastries like me! We know that quality product makes quality pastries. Little Kitchen Pastries bring extra smile with delightful party in our mouth, every time we are here. This place takes their time, dedication and love of baking that is no where to be found in Treasure Valley. I believe pastries is art and this place has the best French Croissants, Danish and Caramel Pecan Buns. And more! Be here early and because they close at 2:30pm. Don't forget to request Lemon Almond  Braid - you will love every bite of it.

Best quality sushi and amazing service! Our server, Kelly, remembered everything we ordered off the top of his head! He was friendly and upbeat! Checked on us all the time even during a dinner rush! We felt spoiled. This place is a MUST TRY!
Amazing fort lunch- have had fantastic dinners here as well- the go-to sushi spot in Santa Barbara for foodies looking for the real deal!

Great prices, food and service.  Been very satisfied every time I've gotten food there.  The boom boom sauce is good.  Same goes for the Mahi Mahi tacos, the zuzus pizza, the zuzus chicken cheese fries, the lamb burger, and I'm sure all the other things I havent tried yet.

Okay, I'm writing from the perspective of someone who regularly frequents other "Metro" transportation, primarily Chicago and Washington D.C.  (I'm only reviewing the light rail.  I have never used the buses or shuttles).

By those standards, Metrolink is a sad and ailing relative.

I agree 100% with the comment about the "honor" system.  Why not put in turnstyles and guarantee 100% payment by all riders.  The first time I rode Metro trains I was not aware of the "validation" requirement.  WTF?  How ridiculous is this system that doesn't allow you to purchase a fare card and use it over a span of time or add value?

Additionally, the 1 line (with a spur) is a joke.  Metrolink would be truly useful if a train went up to Alton, down to South County Mall to Arnold, out to West County.  

With the ineptitude, graft and overall mismanagement by the City and Metro board, you can't expect much more than we have though, so I guess it is as good as it will ever be.  It will never make a profit, so it will never expand without massive Federal investment, which would be flushing more national treasure.

All you need is one visit to D.C. or the Bay Area or Boston or Chicago or even Philly and you'll see how very narrow the Metrolink has set up their routes to prohibit large-scale ridership.  It really does serve only a small fraction of St Louis City or County's residents and is almost simply a way to get airport folks to the downtown or out to Scott AFB.

To complete my rant, I'll add--lack of public restrooms, security bordering on stoogery and recently reduced service, causing even longer waits.

No thanks...I'll drive.

The customer service is not great during the afternoon and evening hours. Whenever I go, it is the same young lady working and she has a poor attitude. The tables are often dirty. In addition, the hours are not as advertised.

Total rip off artists. These guys are old school in their overcharging and scamming. My other half was out of town and our toilet was keeping me up all night running. Called these guys on a recommendation from a friend(thanks for nothing Steve). Guy came out and was immediately pretty rude. I thought ok he's a plumber it's fine. Show him the toilet, he replaces some little part and says your fixed. Wrote me out a bill. For over $200. For what turned out to be a $5 part and 2 minutes of labor. Now I get it, sometimes that's the price you pay for a service like that but here's the kicker. THE TOILET WASNT FIXED! I realized I'd been had. I realized his smug affect as he wrote out the bill was suppressed joy at taking someone. Needless to say I would be remiss as a human being if I didn't warn others of my experience. There's people in this world who feel it's ok to take advantage of others and I say SHAME. SHAME ON THOSE PEOPLE AND SHAME ON YOU A PERFECT PLUMBING.

Artisan egg sandwich - picture looked great, but was tasteless, felt nauseous for next few hours.  OJ ok, efficient enough service and a cheap quick fix, but really only went here because noshville line too long.

When I was visiting from Chicago a few weeks ago i decided to try out the MetroLink to see how it was compared to Chicago. As for On time, Clean, Safe and Friendly it definitely was more of all of those than Chicago combined. When it comes to the sheer sprawl of the system it is lacking and will come when they figure out how to make sure all users pay. I found it very easy to rub off the Validation and have it re validated. I paid for all my trips but tried to see if it could be done and it easily was. I enjoyed the ride to Forrest Park and to the Casino across the bridge in Illinois. If MetroLink can expand this would be a top class system.

Great Francisville restaurant. We had the chicken gyro and falafel. Both solid sandwiches. Good prices, excellent service. No culinary surprises here, but very good at sandwiches and pizza. The Zuzu fries were way more than we expected, but definitely worth the indulgence.

I've only had delivery from this place, but I'm a pretty huge fan. They deliver quickly and have pretty good prices and food.

I've had the lamb burger which is GREAT, the southwest chicken egg rolls which I always really like.

I've had the zuzu's burger and I am really not a fan. I think it may be the sauce? I'm not sure, it tasted really weird to me.

Haven't tried anything else yet, but planning on it!

Really enjoyed my early lunch at companions. Got a caramel macchiato, granola bite, tough love salad and corn bread. Really enjoyed it all separately but put together it was all interesting taste wise. Loved the tough love salad. Almost wish the lemon vinaigrette had a stronger lemon flavor. Pleased with the taste combo of the salad. Love their cornbread. Best cornbread I've ever had. It's very moist and you don't see a lot of moist cornbread. Their portions are huge. You get a lot of bang for your buck. Macchiato was good. Love kaldis espresso. Also love their granola bites. Just the right amount of sweetness
Got the Grilled Chicken Hoagie. Very good sandwich. Better than expected. Big and packed with meat.

I have been driving past the shop for the last few months and finally decided to stop in. This is definitely a mom and pop shop. I was told everything is made in house except for the scone filling. And it shows! Everything I ordered was delicious! The ham and cheese croissant was amazing! The croissants really are like a true French pastry not an out of the box mix. The sticky bun was rich and gooey and perfect. The shortbread cookie was like a fancier version of a Keebler "Pecan Sandies"cookie. The "morning roll" is a crescent roll dough rolled up with cinnamon, sugar, and orange zest. If you like orange rolls you will love this! Owners were very friendly and very helpful at describing every goody.

Dining at Sun Sushi is as close to dining in Japan as one can be while still being in Santa Barbara. The fish is exceptional, expertly prepared and always super delicious. I appreciate that the chefs bring in exotic fish because I feel that all too often, every sushi menu seems to mirror the next but there are often new things to try here. The sake menu changes often as well which is always appreciated. 

Try it out. You won't be disappointed!
Slowest service ever! Only waited because my grandma really wanted mcdonalds :(

Stopped here for breakfast. Cute country style restaurant. Busy, but very well staffed and we were seated right away. I had the French toast and my hubby had an egg and tomato breakfast sandwich... but we're very good. We will definitely be back again. Can't go wrong at Cracker Barrel.  Thanks for the good eats.!

These people have a lot of passion and rightfully so. Good hot dogs, and amazing donuts, and they have taps! *granted, the taps are limited selection... mostly IPAs to my great disappointment* Perhaps expand to provide bottles/cans? But that's an added bonus. Go there for the dogs, and finish with a donut or two

**Recommend having Ranch for the fries! It would make a great pairing.

Let me preface this by saying I was PUMPED to try this place for several reasons. First, I loved the Dog (and we even had our rehearsal dinner there...because what's not to love about hot dogs & beer the night before a wedding). Their Instagram also got me excited because it looked like they'd made cute updates to the decor. I also was excited to have a donut place closer to my house and near Dragon Park for a donut + playground excursion with my toddler. But at 11:30 on a random Thursday they were out of donuts which just seems like poor planning, especially when they've been open for a month & had time to work out the kinks. And the hot dog was pricey and left a lot to be desired. It wasn't bad, just expensive and had me missing a cheaper, less gourmet option. I also didn't love that you had to get a meal, you just couldn't get a normal hotdog, it had to come with a drink and fries/chips.

I would have never found this place if I wasn't in this area for a conference. My wife and I were staying at the Sheraton and knew the Bread Co. would be packed with it being in so close proximity to the hotel.

We decided to venture out a little bit (it's really not that far). When we got to the parking lot it was almost 8am, and I saw only one car parked in the parking lot. Either the place was closed or everyone was at the Bread Co. It was freezing, so instead of getting out of the car only to be met with a locked door, I decided to call. Matt answered and said that they were indeed open! Score!

The place was empty, so we were free to explore the café, reading all of the signs they had on the windows showcasing their baking area. There quite a few selection of sandwiches, bagels, and sweets. I ordered the New Yawker and my wife had the OOH LA LA! My bagel was fresh and very tasty. I especially appreciated the capers that were in the bagel. I've never had capers with a bagel before, but it was a great addition to the smoke salmon and cream cheese. I had a couple bites of my wife's sandwich, and I definitely appreciate how fluffy the eggs were, but I still preferred my sandwich. We ended breakfast with an Almond croissant, which was probably my favorite part of the meal. The croissant was covered in sliced almonds, and the almond filling...yummm.....I'm drooling just thinking about it right now. This was more food than we probably should've ate, but it was worth it.

Fast forward 4 hours later, and we are back! We were talking to our friends about this place, and they wanted to try it out for lunch. I normally don't like going to a place twice in one day, but I really enjoyed my breakfast earlier that day and wanted to hang out with my friends. This time I split a sack lunch with my wife. We had the FA LA LA LA LA sandwich with a side salad and a gooey butter cake bite. I would say I enjoyed the gooey butter cake the most, followed by the sandwich and then the salad. This gooey butter cake was probably one of the best I've had in the St. Louis area. My original favorite gooey butter cake is from Park Ave., but this one gives Park Ave a run for its money. My wife ended ordering another piece of the gooey butter cake, but instead of just getting a gooey butter cake bite, she got a bar. The bar felt like it weighed a pound. So dense, so delicious!

A feel like this is a little hidden gem in the area. Check it out as an alternative to Bread Co.
$8.50 is simply not a reasonable price for an egg and cheese. No matter where you are in the country or what the sandwich looks like. The staff was rude, to boot.
Very busy Cracker Barrel but we were seated quickly considering. Food was great as usual and staff was friendly

I absolutely love this place!  The food is always fresh; they almost always get my order right.  However, there are two things that could improve a bit outside of great service and great food.  Ordering online through my phone is hit or miss.  The second thing is that, today, I tried curbside pickup.  I was super excited about this since parking is a beast during their lunch rush.  Although, I wasn't sure how this was going to work since I did place my order on my phone, there was nothing that prompted me to let them know what kind of vehicle I drive or anything.  I got there for pickup, and unfortunately, there were several cars that were just parked in the curbside parking spots.  Rude people (not Companion's fault)!  Once I was finally able to park in a spot, I saw that there is a number that you text to let someone know that you are there.  Very cool!  Except that part of the service was down.  My food came out fairly quickly after I got there but I was a few minutes late because I couldn't find a place to park.  I'm sure that they are working out some kinks, but I wish there was a way to keep people from parking where they shouldn't so that the curbside customers could get their food and go!

I think I found the best pizza in town. The owner is so creative with his food. Extremely clean environment. The owner is so funny and friendly a great guy. And adding chick peas to the pizza is a really great idea. Huge variety of salads and the house dressing is amazing. I was concerned of the frying oil and the owner showed me what kind of oil they use and guess what!! It's 0 trans fat. The menu is to die for. Such a great experience. I ordered from there for a super bowl party and my friends were dying to know the address of the place I got the food from. I encourage such businesses when it comes to gourmet food and healthy at the same time! Way to go Adel "The owner"

I hate to pile on another negative review for Catalyst but based on the experience I just had I can't not share. Their customer service is too bad to let other people make the same mistakes as me. 

I've been a Catalyst and a Jar Bar customer for years. I've done 3 of their cleanses with positive experiences (although yeah, they take forever to answer emails and never, ever pick up the phone and no, the juices aren't nearly as good as BluePrint) but the juices are solid and Catalyst is a small, local business doing good, healthy work so I try to support that. 

I'd been to Jar Bar a few times before I bought a Ruelala deal for there. I'd had a few things that were good (and a few that we're bad - like the salad composed almost entirely of parsley. Just. No.) but I was trying to eat clean so I spent $75 for 3 5-meal punch cards. I went in and redeemed my Ruelala voucher for punch cards 

Unfortunately, I noticed almost immediately that Jar Bar never seemed to be stocked with the items I wanted to try. I'd hike across town to pick up a meal and all the better meals would be gone. 

Anyways, then the Center City location closes (!) and when I contact them (multiple calls and emails over weeks) to find out what I can do the owner and manager both finally tell me I can redeem my punch cards for food or put it towards a juice cleanse. Great! The food is just so-so but a juice cleanse would be awesome. I scheduled a date. 

And then I get another email that no, we were joking, you can't use your punch cards for a cleanse. Actually you can't use them at all. And their reasons kept changing : first it was because the location has closed, then it was because the original voucher had expired (but I redeemed my voucher! I got the punch cards that don't have an expiration date! No dice.), and then it was because I wanted juice not food (but the owner said it was okay!)

That final rationale was delivered by a shrill, screaming voice over my phone who played friendly for 0.5 seconds and then wouldn't let me get a word in edgewise. She spent 10 minutes berating me for being selfish in a condescending (and, yes, shrill) tone before I finally had enough. I gave up. I wished her a good day and hung up while she was STILL berating me. 

She could still be yelling at that phone for all I know.

Anyway, thus ends my 3 year relationship with Catalyst. It's just not worth the trouble. 

And PS - If you want good, clean food check out Lithe Methods amazing packaged foods or Pure Fare. Their prices are more reasonable, the favors are actually good, and the customer service is impeccable.
Goof cafe latte good banana nut muffin tea was ok

We arrived on a Saturday morning around 10. Thank goodness there wasn't a long wait; however, we did have to wait to for our waitress to get our orders. We waited about 15 minutes before she ever acknowledged that we were there. Once she came over to take our orders she didn't even say hello my name is.....sorry for your wait. She just came over and said can I get your order! I hate it when people do not introduce themselves! During our visit the food came out pretty quickly. Once again we had to ask for refills and anything extra we might need. Needless to say we will not be seating in her section again.

I've done 2 Catalyst Cleanses in the past and have really enjoyed each and would do it again. The first was by far the hardest - both because you're 1) getting used to not eating, and 2) getting used to some very strong juices. 

That said, the juices tasted much better the 2nd time around. (Maybe the recipe changed slightly? They were much less overwhelmingly celery-ish.) My favorites are always the lemonade and cashew milk, followed by the greenies, and then the beet and carrot, but the all grow on you by the 2nd day. Still, I would also love if they'd let you try some new flavors (the BP Cleanse flavors sound super tasty). 

Try doing your cleanse during a work week - the distractions definitely help you think less about the fact that you're not chewing. And also, try cutting down your caffeine intake at least 3 days before you start. Day 1's an adjustment, Day 2 can go either way, but Day 3 is always great. 

I would definitely do Catalyst again. I love supporting a local company, their customer service is really solid, the pick-up times and locations are good, and they run great deals on Ruelala and other deal sites from time to time - keep an eye out.

Not sure what's going on these days, but I've been getting super unlucky with food orders from my usual favorites, most recently this one. 

My 10-piece buffalo wings looked extremely sad. First of all, they looked and tasted old (as if reused from someone else's order), but they were also tiny and chewy, as if they came from unhappy scrawny underfed teenage chickens. I almost felt bad eating them, but was mostly annoyed that I did not get my money's worth ($8.50+). 

The greek salad was the same size as usual, but the level of freshness wasn't. The tomato and lettuce pieces had brown spots all over them. I also ordered a cheeseburger, and found that although the quality was roughly the same as usual, the beef patties were super greasy and the "cheddar" that came with it was more like waxy orange American cheese than cheddar. 

The lamb kefta wrap was probably the highlight of the lot, but it was a bit small and also super oily. It was hard to tell whether the filling was beef or lamb. For $5.99, it's not super expensive, but it's also not super substantial, with only ground meat, a few strands of red onions, and some parsley. 

The weirdest thing about this order wasn't even the food, though. The delivery guy parked outside of my building and called me, saying I needed to go outside to the car and get it from him. In the past, Zuzu's Kitchen has typically delivered to my apartment, which is why I've always included a generous tip on top of the existing delivery fee. But the delivery guy this time even made a fuss about dropping off my food at the security desk in my building, and the whole point of me ordering delivery was because I was experiencing some leg muscle aches, making going outside a bit tough for me. 

Needless to say, there are too many good places for food in the city to pay extra fees to get greasy food of declining quality not get delivered to one's home. It's sad because I used to really like this place.

Friday night is the night we wind down from a long week of work and going to school. Tonight, 2/5/16, we go to Cracker Barrel for dinner. The line is not long and we are seated in less than five minutes. The hostess is polite and the waitress comes to our table about 30 seconds after we are seated. This store had the fire going in the fireplace and this made the place nice and cozy on this cool evening. Once we were seated we noticed the overhead fan was on. We let the waitress know that this made it a little cool and she immediately had it turned off. She was very polite and made sure we got our food promptly. She got my husbands order wrong but promptly corrected that when it was pointed out to her. She apologized for the error. 
We had a great time and I would recommend this store at Long Hollow Pike in Goodlettsville for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

We have a CenturyLink Direct TV bundle.  We apparently got in a year ago, with promotional offers.  After the first year, the promotional offers dropped away and there was about a $60/month jump in our bill.  I called in December to find out why.  The person I talked to for both CenturyLink and DirectTV both told me that they were again running the promotions and they would drop us back to close to what we had been paying previously.  In January, my bill went up about $10/month from the December bill.  I called again and I was told that, because the move back to the promotion status happened in the mid billing cycle, the decrease would show up in the next bill (Feb).  In Feb, the bill went UP yet again.  I called and got a guy who said the promotions were in place but that CenturyLink/Direct TV had just renegotiated rates with the content providers and prices went up.   I cut some of my program providers to get the price back down.  He also said he would throw in a discount.  He told me that I needed to call them again in June to maintain the promotional status.  My March bill just arrived.  It is effectively $10 below February, but $40 above November 2016.  I'm afraid to call them again to find out why my bill is still this high for fear that they will give me another break that will turn into a rate hike.  We are on fixed income so random rate hikes won't work for us.  We are starting to look around.

Great customer service!  Great food!

Stayed open after closing to serve us. Friendly staff both at the counter and at the grill.

Nothing ever bad to say about a Cracker Barrel.  They seem to have a way of feeling like you're at the one that's by your house and you could be 3 states away.  The one thing I can say is different is the sweet tea is more sweet the further south you go.  Buy some old timey candy and eat some down home cooking.

This PJ's location is one of my regulars because of its proximity to my son's school.  It's busy in the morning, between folks working in the buildings across the street from UNO as well as students/faculty from the school itself.  Because of the morning traffic, they're always baking stuff, and the orange-cranberry muffins were right out of the oven.  Staff is cheerful, nice, and the coffee is always top-notch.

Careful of the glare in the morning! The shop has an eastern exposure.  While most of the morning customers are in-and-out, a few folks settle in to do some work.  A sunny day makes it tough to see a laptop at some tables.

NOTE: current address for the Gentilly PJ's is 6600 Franklin Ave, corner Leon C. Simon.  The address listed here went 12' under water in the Federal Flood of 2005.

I had the joy of living across the street from zuzus for a year. The only bad part about this is I just wanted to order zuzus every day because it is SO good. The food is so good and the people are so friendly. 

My go to order was normally pizza, because who doesn't love good pizza? I liked the plain, but would also mix it up with their variation of a Hawaiian pizza. The food is Mediterranean based so there's no bacon, but the ham they use on the Hawaiian pizza is better! 

They also have zuzus chicken cheese fries. They are delicious and also unique from regular cheese fries. They add jalepenos and truffle oil which gives it an extra burst of flavor. 

Finally, if you're looking for a healthier option zuzus still has you covered! They have some great salads and wraps. 

 And before I forget! Dessert! They do have dessert as an option, which certainly isn't what they are known for so I normally stick to the dinner options. But if I'm looking for something sweet their milkshakes are actually very good!
Stopped by for a quick late lunch and found "It's toasted cheese sandwich month!" The Farmers Market- half is a whole meal! Mmmmm

I stumbled on this lunch spot on accident. I was driving through the Westport Plaza business district and the cafe looked cool and out of place next to the other boring buildings. I decided to just get a salad from the cafe. My salad evolved into the Fiesta Chicken Sandwich and a bag of jalapeño chips. The sandwich was worth every Carb. As a matter of fact the bread was so good it made me happy. The bread was made of endorphin releasing carbs... The bread was made of therapeutic carbs.. The food was great/service was just OK. Maybe I came in after a massive rush and the staff was in recharge mode but that is why my experience was a 4 star and not a 5 star occasion.

Being in an airport they have a constant flow of patrons in spite of there lousy food. Cold, thrown together and far below the mediocre standard Wendy's sets for their stores out in the real world.

Yuk!

Ummm.... maybe b/c they are in an airport and you're in a hurry, they figure they can lack complete customer service?  The person taking the orders had no personality- she was also snippy to her co worker.  I asked for a different salad dressing w/ my salad than the one that comes w/ it and she quipped 'that's the one that it comes with'... she realized that she was wrong but didn't apologize and when we received our order, the wrong dressing was w/ it so a return trip was made to the counter and again for napkins b/c apparently they don't just provide those??...  

The tables hadn't been wiped in awhile as they were sticky and gross.  

I enjoy Wendy's Apple/Pecan Chicken Salads but I won't revisit this location the next time I'm at the Nashville airport.  The salad was scant w/ toppings but the chicken was warm so I guess there was one plus...

Wendy's was my absolute favorite place to get breakfast when traveling through BNA.  I have made comments to management in the past that Wendy's breakfast needs to be sold outside of the airport and suggested to friend that they should try one of the panini combo's. But today, Thanksgiving, they totally missed the mark. See my two pictures. Panini - bread was torn off one side and paper from the cheese (?) was left inside the sandwich. The manager was gracious and offered her apology and was clearly disappointed.  She offered to remake the sandwich but I declined and accepted a full refund. I then went next door to Popeye's for breakfast. While good, the hash browns can't beat the home style potatoes and panini.

I visited this (sort of) new location for the first time today for a late lunch. Turns out that it is only a 3 minute drive from my new office and I'll be adding Companion to my lunch rotation from here on out!

The space is huge and houses all of Companion's facilities (bakery, cooking classrooms, and of course, their cafe). The lunch crowd was just starting to clear out by the time I arrived at around 1:30 pm, so I can't attest to how busy it can get. Order at the counter, get your number sign, find a seat/table, and peruse the hardworking staff who are baking delicious breads through the looking glass. 

I ordered the whole "spring chicken" sandwich ($8.75), which was roasted chicken, onions, tomatoes, and creamy artichoke spread on a toasted and sublime ciabatta. I was taken aback when the sandwich arrived - it was huge! It was worth the money in both taste, quality, and value. I cannot wait to try their other sandwiches and salads. Overall, a very simple but promising first meal here. 

I also noticed that they have daily early bird (before 9am) breakfast specials. I'll have to make sure I'm not lazy enough and actually drive to work a little early so that I can give their breakfast menu a try.

Edit 6/20/16: I've been here several more times for lunch since my original review, and I just want to point out that the "sack lunch" deal is my go-to now. For $11 (about $2 more than the price of a whole sandwich), you get any whole sandwich, a side salad or fruit salad, and a full size cookie/brownie. The side salad is mixed greens with cheese with your choice of dressing and it comes in the size of a soup bowl, which is plentiful. the cookie is larger than my palm. The sack lunch is a great value. My favorite sandwich is still the spring chicken, though the falalalala is a close second.

Great food, great service, lovely decor. Just a nice place I happened to walk by.The lamb kefta wrap was spicy and delicious. I can't wait to come back and try more items! They also seem to have a number of delicious bakery items I can't wait to try.

I car share with my husband and wanted to be familiar with the routes and stops in the event I needed to use it. So I spent the day riding the Metro. For just $7.50, I was able to purchase an all day pass at my local Schnuck's. You can purchase anything from a day pass to a month pass and everything in between. 

Plan ahead and know when your route leaves/arrives, I spent more time waiting for the bus than I did actually riding the bus. I really like the Metro-Link, it's quick, doesn't make frequent stops and is generally on time unlike buses. The Metro-Link stops are also covered and have heat lamps in the winter (Milwaukee doesn't even have this)! Not all bus stops have a shelter in case of bad weather or a place to sit in the event of a long wait.

I like to use Google transit, it's the Google map feature for directions and then select the transit option (walking or bike are other options). You may also specify when you want to depart or arrive and it will tell you the route location and time to be there by.

Overall, I am very impressed with the routes and the condition of the St Louis transit system. Kudos St Louis!
Seriously what are you waiting for? GO get some Sushi! But..i do Highly reccomend coming in early for a nice quiet Vibe.
Least efficient Wendy's on the planet. Took around 25 minutes for my whole party to get served. I'd call it "slow food."

Stopped into this little pizza and sandwich shop for lunch and everything was delicious.

They have the usual stuff like pizza and burgers (which are good) but this place really shines with their special dishes (basically anything that is "Zuzu's" in the title).

Zuzu's burger is incredibly juicy. Zuzu's chicken sandwich is wonderfully spicy. However the must try item has to be Zuzu's pizza (Lamb, Chickpeas, Mozzarella & Feta Cheese, with Fresh Cilantro). I've never had lamb on a pizza before but since trying it I can't believe it took me this long. Absolutely fantastic! If you're in the area it is well worth your time to stop in for a slice.

Besides excellent food the staff were friendly and helpful. The whole place was also really clean. This is definitely a place where they really care about the quality of the food and making their customers happy.

They haven't been open that long but I really feel like this is going to become one of those neighborhood fixtures that everyone needs to visit.

I was here with my husband on a business trip. I tried to ride the train to the zoo. I walked from my hotel to the Union Station, where I was threatened by a very aggressive panhandler. He asked me if I would give him some money since he was homeless. When I handed him a dollar, he said loudly, "Did you hear me say I was homeless?" This scared me to death, and I parted with 10 more dollars before this guy took off after he grabbed the $10. I then got on the train. The ride itself was uneventful, but on the platform, I felt unsafe. I would ride again with my husband or if I were carrying mace.

After driving over 600 miles from Iowa, my boyfriend and was super hungry, so we stop to get food from here. We had been to several Cracker Barrels in North Carolina and were highly satisfied with their food and service. However, this particular Cracker Barrel was just the opposite of our previous experiences. I ordered French toast with apples, turkey sausage, and hash browns. My apples contained some kind of black substance, and my hash browns was barely warm. My boyfriend ordered pancakes, bacon, cheese grits, sausage, and eggs. His bacon came out raw when he requested it to be extra crispy. Also, his cheese grits contained some kind of sweet seasoning that was not listed in the menu description. After waiting for all the food to be corrected, all of our other food items were cold. Our server was kind but not really helpful at correcting the issue. We had to request to speak to the manager, whom offered us 50% off of our bill. I will never go back here again.

Called Friday. Was told anytime Saturday was available for an oil change and was recommended 8:00 AM. Said that was a bit ambitious, scheduled it for 10:00 AM. Dropped it off 10 min early. Came back at 12:36, and it was still in the parking lot. Walked it and asked what the appointment was for. Was told by a guy there were cars in front of me and mine was next. A few minutes later, was called up by the same guy and told sorry there was a delay caused by another repair. I know management can make shit up like this to appease customers, as I've worked in a service shop, so I'll just meet in the middle and give an even 3/5.

The food is excellent and we loved the atmosphere. We had three different dogs and each one was amazing and the flavors were great.  We chose the stairway to heaven and dirty churro donuts. They are amazing. This is one place you need to try. Once you do, you will be going back!

Decided to try this place since it got good reviews so far! I came in around 5pm on a Saturday night for takeout. I was happily greeted by the host and the sushi chefs behind the beautiful bamboo wall. 

I ordered the spicy yellowtail roll, soft shell crab appetizer, I love crab! And a cali hand roll. They can make handrolls of any of the menu items. Took only 15 minutes or less since they weren't very crowded maybe 8 customers. And happily on my way home to savor the sushi!

The host guy even offered me ice water while I wait since it was like 85 degrees today!

I would have given them a 5 star since the sushi and soft shell crab was outstanding but they forgot to give me wasabi and ginger. 

I'll definitely be back! Next time on a Tuesday or Thursday night when they have freshly flown in fish from Japan and have a special menu to reflect the freshness.

Thanks to some co-workers, I headed here while in town for work.  Everything made fresh and it was hard to choose what to have.  I was told if you don't get there early, they do run out of the daily specials.  The Black bean veggie soup was the best black bean soup I have ever had!  Flavorful and filling.  The place is very busy so expect a wait to order and to get your food - definitely worth the wait.
Love love love this place!!! It is worth going on Wednesday or Thursday for the breakfast deals. Kaldi's coffee is served here which is great! Definitely a weekly stop.

Our car was just inspected within the last couple weeks in NY and passed perfectly. We had to get it inspected in PA and they are saying there is $1300 in repairs due. I really doubt we damaged the car that much in 2 weeks, especially since it's basically been sitting in a parking spot all of this time.  The person we received the car from had a similar problem at a NY Meineke and took it elsewhere for a successful inspection. I would recommend staying away from larger companies and seek out reputable smaller businesses.

The best high intensity workout in town. I love that you can work out at any of the locations, even while traveling out of state. Awesome staff and coaches. They help you achieve whatever fitness goals you have.

Well, after passing by this little shop for the last 6 months, I decided to go check it out while I had a tire being fixed.  Wow!  Wonderful pastries!  Don't be fooled by the unassuming store front, there is a world of sweet love going on in there!  
     The sticky buns were the best I have ever tasted, and as I am a pretty decent cook myself, and have made them regularly.    John, the chef told me that he makes them out of Brioche dough.  Of course, I thought, as I bit into it's firm rich texture.  He also makes a caramel glaze for it, not some cheap, overly sweet concoction, I am talking about real caramel with the richness that only cream and butter can deliver.  Very impressive. 
      I decided to buy a few more things to take home and try.  I also ordered a couple of tarts, a beautiful apricot scone and a lemon-sugar cookie.   They make all their dough in house, and it shows.  The puff pastry used in the tarts has a rich buttery quality of a fine french pastry shop, and the cookie was so good it almost reminded me of a fine scottish shortbread with a wonderful lemon flavor that was not overpowering, but fresh and sweet in taste. 
      The apricot scone was an actual scone, not some crumbly  junk that most of the places try to pass off around here.  Kay, John's wife and partner, who are very pleasant by the way, explained to me that they used whipping cream in their scones.  Good deal, as it improves it texture tremendously and makes it moist but still firm, YUM.....
      So, this place has made a customer out of me, and I would hope that you would give it a try too.  Don't be fooled that it doesn't look very fancy on the outside, inside is a nice area to sit and enjoy your coffee or tea and a wonderful slice of heaven in pastry form.
     As far as customer service, you couldn't find nicer folks than the owners Kay and John, they seem like very nice people who really care about making their products great with good quality ingredients and a lot of love and pride.
      I spent over half my life in big cities, Chicago and San Francisco, and have a fairly picky pallet, and I guarantee that Little Kitchen Pastries could hold its own against any well-known Patisserie!

My friend and I had a really great dinner here. We order the salmon six step (which is my favorite), the shrimp and vegi udon, and the salmon skin salad. Everything is fresh and the flavor is great. The most important was all the staff were very friendly. We really enjoy it. Definitely will recommend my friend to have Japanese food here.
OMG!!! Best Sushi ever had HANDS DOWN!!!! Staff was really nice and food was AMAZING!!!!
Loved the tomato basil soup. Sandwich well-packed with meat and cheese. The open bakery is fun to watch. The bread, of course, is the star of the show!

What an experience! If the amazing sandwiches don't get you, or the house-made, constantly rotating all-star team of soups doesn't get you, or any one of the fresh and filling salads doesn't get you... THE BREAD WILL! I have eaten here three times in the last week (sorry, not sorry Jimmy Johns), each time getting something different, and the last time I bought some loaves of crusty bread to bring home with me (and a couple pastries... whoops). Needless to say, I might try for three times this week too! But seriously, it's such an eye-opening space with high-quality, well-portioned options, and you get to see them bake the bread. I've never seen a place like this, but I sure am happy I work right down the street.

Is it lunch time yet?

In the past 20 years, the concept of a Chinese buffet has drastically changed.  When these types of restaurants became popular, the food was a generic Chinese-American, rarely homemade, cheap, unhealthy, and rarely fresh.  More recently, owners of these buffets, wanting to compete with more traditional, sit-down Asian restaurants, have greatly improved their cuisine; they have become creative, greatly expanded their offerings, and are producing top-notch meals.  Moreover, they have drifted away from the Chinese-American food model, and are now considerably pan-Asian.  A new case-in-point has opened in Indianapolis: Iron Sheet Royal Grill.

Iron Sheet Royal Grill sits at the intersections 38th Street and Georgetown Road, and it occupies the space that formerly housed WTT Buffet.  WTT Buffet was huge; WTT Buffet was great; Iron Sheet Royal Grill is far better.  The new restaurant is massive, although in order to accommodate the large food selection area, the seating is more limited than I expected.  However, "more limited" certainly does not equate to "sparse."  The food selection area is conveniently divided into sections.  The first selection area is the largest, and features the sushi, salad, fresh fruit, and dessert bars.  Directly south of this are the main selections, where the diner will find fried foods, traditional Chinese favorites, American samplings, and Szechuan dishes.  Next, one will find the Mongolian grill, where fresh vegetables, pork, beef, chicken, and faux crab can be placed in a bowl, sauced, and grilled to perfection.  Traveling further east, lies one of the most unique aspects of the restaurant: the noodle station.  The Iron Sheet Royal Grill makes their own Vietnamese noodles, and the diner is able to create his own pho dishes.  Directly north of the noodle station, one will find two small kiosks filled with pot stickers and various soups.

Due to the large size of the Iron Sheet Grill, it would be difficult to fully experience it in just one visit.  Personally, I found everything to be wonderful, and thus, it is tough to narrow down a true favorite.  I was very pleased by the Kung Pao Chicken, overwhelmed by the sushi, and further wooed by the Mongolian grill.  I was also impressed that the restaurant featured some truly authentic Chinese dishes, including beef stomach.

The staff at Iron Sheet Royal Grill was amazing!  While the restaurant is a buffet, a server does take your drink order.  The manager was the most commendable, especially when it came time to visit the Mongolian grill or the noodle bar.  Since he is dressed in a suit, he is hard to miss. The manager was also quick to inform his guests on the varying selections his restaurant offered, as well as details on how the foods were prepared. With his assistance, and careful attention to my strict orders, my plate of Mongolian grilled vegetables and meat was perfect.

If you're in the mood for Asian food, have an appetite for destruction, and just can't decide what to order, head on over to the Iron Sheet Royal Buffet.  You'll thank me later.

We came in on a Friday at about 1:30pm.  I agree with the other reviews that it was slightly confusing on where to go at first.   You order at the counter in the room opposite the bar.   

Fried chicken is what it's about here.  I ordered the red, white, and blue sandwich with fries.  My companion got a 2 piece thigh and drumstick meal with a side of coleslaw.  

My sandwich a fried chicken breast on the small side came on a bun with coleslaw, blue cheese, and hot sauce.  For both meals,  the chicken was well prepared, crispy and savory. On the sandwich, the bun was kind of dried out, but it held together and was passable.   The sides were really good. The coleslaw was fresh and creamy and not overly sweet.  The fries were done perfectly and tasted great.  

Service was okay, not bad but not super fast or friendly. I hope they add a self service drink station as it seems strange to not have that option in a counter service fast casual restaurant.

This place is an excellent addition to Hillsboro Village. The Chili & Queso Dog was so delicious, we went back the next day for seconds. The freshly made chips were hot, crisp and tasted like a little bit of San Diego beach boardwalk in Nashville. Loved the punk pop playlist and friendly service. It felt like stopping by a friend's house for lunch!

Please don't go to this dentist office. My father went there for his dentures and the whole process took over three months. We were originally told that the process would take about a month, however there were so many delays. My father couldn't eat solid foods and was on a liquid diet for 3 months. He was miserable and he still haven't got his dentures. The office was apologetic but the service was horrible. We won't be going back!

I've heard Zuzu's has good food from friends, but their dessert it terrible! We ordered the oreo cake and a peanut butter milkshake. The milkshake had no peanut butter taste and instead tasted like mediocre vanilla ice cream. The "oreo" cakes were simply small round chocolate cakes with a little bland cream in the middle. There was a little bit of oreo crumbs sprinkled on top, but the cakes taste nothing like oreo. If disappointment had a taste, this would be it.

I really need a 3.5 rating on this one.  I'm torn in my star rating, just not quite a 4.  I think mostly because the consistency of the baked eggs still has me baffled.  The croissant sandwich all together was fine and good flavor, it's just that egg consistency...  I love the layout of the place and enjoy that you have a birds eye view of the bakery area.  I purchased some brownie bites for my work team, of which they absolutely loved them!

We stopped and got a sticky bun to go. There wasn't a lot of choice available at 10 when we stopped in but the sticky bun was very delicious. As others have noted, the grandparent type couple that runs the place are very congenial and warm, lending a very nice atmosphere to the place.

I was back and forth on where to land this review.  So pros and cons- 

Pros- the donuts are extremely good and the coffee is good as well.  I can't vouch for the rest of the food.  They are friendly and accommodating.  They did a great job renovating the building and it is cozy and comfortable.  The prices are actually really affordable as well compared to other coffee shops and donut places (ahem sisters) in the area.  

Cons- Looking at the menu it is a bit confusing as to what type of patron or meal they are aiming for.  It seems like "I'm kinda hungry at any point in the day, but don't want a full meal" food.  They also seem to be working out a few kinks with the streamlining the service process, but they just opened and they appear to be working on it so hopefully that is resolved soon.  They should also really open before 10 AM on the weekend.  As the only place with coffee and really good fancy donuts in a neighborhood of hungover bachelorette parties in airbnb rentals and local moms who need to get their kids out of the house they would probably make a killing.  I imagine they will figure that out pretty soon.

Cute little shop that reminds me of being at my Grandma's house! I ordered the Caramel Pecan Bum and it delivered on size and sweetness! Pair this with a good cup of coffee, and you have a delightful morning treat! This place has great service, great atmosphere and delicious pastries!
Really good, family friendly and clean place. Service was great, staff was so nice! I will come back when I'm in town again.

Excellent coffee latte here now. Friendly staff lady, a vegan, very interesting and helpful for living healthier. Oh, yes and the honey and Americano is great. Food options though I am going to another place for that. Modern store here in nice shopping stripmall area about 2 miles from Lakefront airport. Good choice here.

Ordered the new pretzel burger before my flight - was slightly disappointed and the bottom of the bun was very greasy.  

This review is more for the service than the food - it's a fast food joint in an airport, I didn't go into this expecting great food or anything.  But the service was AWFUL.  The cashier on my receipt says "Tigist" and she was the worst person I have encountered in a long time.  Was very rude, wouldn't give you any attention, people in line would ask her questions and she would look blankly at them and mumble something.  She would literally turn around and talk to people in the back while holding a customer's credit card while they were trying to pay.  Shut up and do your work, then go goof off.

I probably won't be back to Nashville, but if I did, I would avoid this place like the plague.

Always a good choice when you are in the mood for good old fashioned comfort food. Either go early or be prepared to wait. The gift shop is a great way to spend some time while waiting for your table. Or you can relax in the rocking chairs outside.

I've had friends pushing me to give OTF a try. As a runner, I am always a bit skeptical about treadmill workouts since I typically dread running on them. But, I am so glad I finally took my first class, and am now hoping to sneak in workouts a couple times a week!

I took a 3G class with Rene (didn't even realize it was different than the typical Orange 60) and really enjoyed the flow of the class. I've never used rowing machines seriously, and it was nice having the structured challenges (e.g., row 250m, do 10 jumping lunges, row 150m...). I also surprisingly really loved the treadmill portion of the class! It was nice jumping on the machine and feeling like it was constantly changing.

The best part, though, is the data. I loved having the heartrate monitor to see exactly how my workout was going. It is super motivating!

Also, beautiful, convenient location! First class is free, so give it a try.

Pretty good here. The service was good. We got 2 rolls and some udon soup and it was 48$ so a little pricy. I would definitely be back because it's close to home and very tasty. They are also open for lunch so that's a plus
Metro Link service should be boycotted (use a ride service) until ridership is controlled, and a visible security agent who is serious about their job, is on every train.

Cafe on steroids. Companion doubles as a full cafe & school for soon-to-be Baker's. Lovely location, super spacious for those dining in or outdoors with tables galore. But what's most extraordinary about the place is watching the team of students work from the open-view glasses teaching area. You can literally see individuals stirring, kneading, folding, tossing dough. Aprons filled with flour and your lunch literally being made with T.L.C. right before tour very eyes. 

Onward, I stopped in because I wanted to give the place a once over & grab a croissant to go. I've got a thing for comparing croissants all of a sudden. Well, the croissant was decent; I wanted it to be more flaky on the outside & dense on the inside...but this isn't about me.

Highly suggest Companion for those looking to host a lunch meeting, mid-day date or if time is limited; grab a pastry, coffee, t-shirt and roll out. 

There's plenty of Companion paraphernalia to choose from: apparel, Mugs, sauces, dressing, baguettes, granola, soup, soft drinks, YOU NAME IT. 

Service was fast & friendly. I got plenty of camera ready smiles as I snapped away. 

~Christy

Absolutely LOVE this place.  It's so nice to be able to see into the bakery, and the food is fresh delicious.  I miss the restaurant in Clayton, but love when I'm out west and can check out the cafe.  I also love the little St. Louis touches, like the Kaldi coffee :)

I ordered The Big Bucket for $34.99 which includes 12 mixed and 2 large sides. The chicken pieces were breast, thigh, leg, and wing. I called ahead to order carry out which I am not so sure is their specialty although it seems to be based on the "carry out" exit door sign and check-out counter I saw.  Instead of the counter, I was told to go to the bar.

With tax my total was $38+ for the chicken and 2 large sides.

The sides to choose from are slaw, 3 bean salad, fries, sauteed spinach,, creamed corn.
I ordered slaw and sauteed spinach.

The chicken was good. The drumsticks could be a little meatier.
The two large sides came in large 2-pound containers that were only HALF FULL.
The 12-piece chicken should feed 4-6 people, but the large sides were divided in three.

This is a new restaurant. I see good things to come.

During a walk following a movie at the Belcourt Theater, we meet a young man with a big donut box giving out samples ... but SO much more than "just" donuts! The box was filled with amazing hot dogs and fabulous brioche donuts, all in wildly fantastic flavor combinations! We were hooked! So we walked up the street to The Donut + Dog... a quaint, homey yet hip restaurant where friendly, passionate, knowledgeable owner, Will, explained the options.  We ordered the Flying Hawaiian and Elote Loco dogs with fries and the "Spring into Summer" organic raspberry & basil donut with bourbon glaze. Oh my! Every bite was a flavor explosion and a delight!  We WILL be back!! :)

Get the Sweet Baby Jesus! Not only is it named after one of my favorite Will Ferrel quotes...but seriously you have NEVER tasted a donut like this. It is so unique! First of all, you crunch into the brûlée topping (which is perfection) then the warm brioche  and ....lastly, the more than generous sweet vanilla custard filling that's soooo silky smooth. Not one bite tastes like "oh yeah, typical donut"! You will want to order a dozen of these. And when you meet the owner, Will, you too will agree he's one of the most genuine and personable dudes you've ever met. They even turned on the fireplace for us near closing time to truly make us happy and comfortable. With both the service (they even heat up your donut for you!) and the uniqueness, you can't go wrong. Try them!
VERY sub par. Not much sushi and it's okay at best. I love sushi and eat it all the time, I suggest to anyone who absolutely loves sushi to find somewhere else.

Not so much of fan. I went there to get lunch because I heard from many people that this place has great quality food. I got the broccoli cheese soup and it did not taste not any broccoli soup I ever had. The soup base was very running. The broccoli came in big chucks and you couldn't really taste any flavor. Not the best I had. 

I do enjoy the environment. It's bright on the inside and it gave you a sneak peak of the factory.

This place is awesome! They seriously have everything you could want. I was visiting from LA when my bachelorette party and I found The Donut + Dog. We sampled an amazing and delicious array of their donuts - they are some of the best I have ever had in my life. They are far better than Voodoo donuts and many of our west coast chains. 100% coming back to try more. Also, their place is super cute, and the decor is on point.
The fiesta chicken sandwich had just the right amount of heat and the bread was fresh!

Tomato pie is 10/10. Super flavourful and filled with garlic and basil. Zuzus chicken sandwich and the boneless wings are amazing too. Best neighbourhood joint!


UPDATE: Lamb burger is insanely good and the Boom Boom pizza is heavenly. Have yet to eat something I didn't like here!

Was in Tucson for a monthly visit, and stopped into this OTF Casa Adobes to get in a workout.  I was greeted by The manager Madi, and her crew.  They couldn't have been more friendly or professional.  I got one of the best workouts in that I can remember, and was able to get showered up and on my way for my dinner presentation.  I will absolutely go back every time I get the opportunity.  They are awesome!
I called about 15 minutes before arriving. The phone order process was extremely pleasant. Staff was pleasant upon arrival chicken Caesar salad is delicious!!

I can't agree more with the yelpers who gave this place a single star. This place is nothing but a rip-off. I went in to this place for an oil change and to get an estimate to get a faulty sensor fixed so that I can get the state inspection pass. The guy called me back and gave me an outrageous estimate which I refused and asked him to just change the oil in my car and a few faulty parking lights.

When I went back to pick my car, he gave me a bill for $138 which included a $70 charge for a  failed inspection which I never even asked him to do since I knew my check engine light was "on" because of the faulty sensor. When I objected, the guy took me into the garage so that his other customers couldn't hear me complaining about the charges and became extremely aggressive and rude.

The guy running the shop is a thug and a scam. I would never go back or recommend anyone to go to this garage.

Out grossing your average Wendy's in that you don't even get the bad food you ordered. Uncaring and lazy employees punch buttons, charge you twenty bucks for a couple of burgers, call out a number 10 minutes later which is a surprise bag of whatever they stuffed into it. Just swallowed two imodiums and glad I have an aisle seat on my flight out of this food horror land.

Sun Sushi is our favourite sushi place in Santa Barbara. I get the Volcano roll every time --a California roll with spicy mayo, eel sauce and bay scallops broiled on top. Delish. Hubby goes for the Rainbow roll and the Sun roll, with which I'm always happy to help him out. Sun's teriyaki salmon is great -- thick, perfectly done pieces of salmon and the right amount of teriyaki. Most places want to drown the fish in it, so I really appreciate the chef's touch. They use a tasty version of wasabi too, a slightly thicker grate to it, and a sweeter taste. I'm usually not a wasabi fan, but I love Sun's wasabi. I'm sharing this with y'all so you help keep this gem in business. Spread the word; I'm willing to wait for a seat.

I have been to Companion several times and everything I have tried has been wonderful!  The Frenchie is a must if you love Brie.  Love their pretzel bread.  Great Caesar salad.  My husband is a fan of their French dip.  Also take some of their granola home with you.  So delicious!

Some of the best sushi I've experienced. Great service but without great food, I don't think you can get 5 stars. I'm visiting Santa Barbara on business so decided to take the yelp stars to the test and Sun Sushi passed it with flying colors. Generous well prepared extremely fresh fish. I had the 6-step tuna, Salmon sushi, Kurodai Sushi and Yellow Tail sushi. All were excellent! I'll be back next time I'm in town!!!

This place has gone downhill. Service remains good, but there's no point in telling them how you want your food because you won't get it that way. For example, the eggs "over hard" were runny, but the "sunny side up" eggs were brown on the edges and not runny. The grits we didn't want came, the syrup had to be returned for the one we requested, etc. Given that not a single thing we specified was right, color me shocked that we received the dishes we ordered at all.

This place is absolutely amazing. The owner is so compassionate and sincere. Their hotdog and side  menu has a good variety of items! Even something coming soon for vegetarians. The brioche donuts are hand made twice a day with flavors that are always changing. So you'll never get bored if you like trying something new. My compliments to the chef who was gracious enough to deliver my food to me at the table and make sure everything looked and tasted amazing. 100% would recommend to everyone and anyone!

This would be zero stars, but unfortunately that isn't an option. I recently moved to the area from the suburbs, and figured a chain car place would be a good option. So, I brought my car in for an inspection, and they called and told me my car needed over $1500 of work done, saying that my shocks were "leaking fluid" and it was EXTREMELY dangerous for me to drive. Of course I was terrified, but I called my Dad (who is pretty knowledgeable about cars) and he told me to take my car to our usual guy in the suburbs to get a second opinion. Sure enough, NOTHING was leaking fluid- the parts in question were in good, 100% safe condition. My car only needed new wiper blades and a rear bulb. $90. 

Moral of the story: NEVER TRUST A CHAIN, especially this one. I feel unbelievably taken advantage of, especially considering I am a young woman, who I'm sure they assumed knew nothing about cars. Find someone local who you can trust, and isn't part of a big corporation whose only aim is to rip you off. I will certainly never make that mistake again!
Homemade brioche donuts & amazing flavors! Have not had a disappointing donut yet. Staff is completely friendly and helps make the experience!

Bought 2 groupons for my boyfriend and I for a xray, check up and teeth cleaning. Appointments were for 12 and we arrived at 11:45. We were not seen until 12:50!
First they gave me and Xray, then I went back into the room and the dentist came in, he looked at my teeth for a few minutes and then told me a list of things I needed done. He said I needed a $600 deep cleaning, not the one I bought with my groupon. He also tried to tell me I have 4 cavities when I have never had a cavity in my life. They printed out a bill for almost $1600 of work that I need done and asked what I wanted to start on. After I told them I just wanted the regular cleaning the dentist gave me the fastest teeth cleaning of my life! It was about 5 minutes. They did the same thing to my boyfriend but gave him a bill for $5700 worth of work! The only good thing about this place was that the staff at the front was extremely friendly

Stopped by at 11:15 to get some late night food. We got a slice of buffalo chicken pizza, chicken zuzu sandwich, lamb Kefta wrap, caprese sandwich and zuzu chicken fries. Everything was awesome but the lamb was my fav. They were closing so gave us 3 slices of the pizza instead of one. 
Someone also walked in as we were leaving and they just gave them few slices of pizza for free since they were closed. Amazing people n service.

Warning- Stale bread and pastries nice and early are sold here.  I would never go to a bakery that sold stale pastries in the morning and neither should you.
