Volcano roll was to die for 
Service was super quick. We got in and out within an hour. The presentation made each dish very unique!

Since COVID, we've been unable to get UNI sushi at our go too restaurants in Santa Clarita. This past weekend, we were in Santa Barbara for our anniverary and Sushi was decided as our special dinner, choosing a place that had it currently available and serving it. Local, Santa Barbara UNI is unparalleled.
Sun Sushi is off the beaten path of Santa Barbara, being 3 miles away from downtown--but this is a great thing! We were able to get a reservation on the day before at a time we wanted. Upon our arrival, the restaurant was busy but without a wait. By the time we left, every table and seat was taken at the sushi bar.
Max and his partner in business were our Sushi chefs. Both were personable as was their service staff and genuinely engaged in our experience. If there is one take away for someone reading my verbose review, let is be that THIS IS THE FRESHEST FISH WE'VE EVER HAD at a Sushi Restaurant, anywhere, including that famous chain in LA Live and in NYC.
The UNI was spectacular AND the freshest Spanish Mackerel and Red Snapper I've ever had.
We cannot say enough about an awesome experience other than that it was unfortunate that our son and sushi buddy was not there to enjoy it with us, however, a return visit is emminent so that we can enjoy it once again, with our son, too.
Tell Max Rob and Christine sent ya!

Whew! This review update is loooong overdue. Yet, they say late is better than never! (Plus now we can always blame the pandemic). 

Sun Sushi is my number one sushi spot in Santa Barbara. I don't care what anyone else says but it triumphs over the competition. While the exterior facade is unassuming--in a strip mall off Upper State Street next to the Tee-Off--the freshness, reasonable pricing and being family owned make it shine. You'll notice that the owner is almost always on site working, whether behind the sushi bar making maki or otherwise. Also notice how he goes out of his way to respond to each and every Yelp review.

The food is spectacular. The maki/rolls are made with care, not with an excessive amount of rice to fill you up quickly and cheaply, and are plated beautifully. For me, the appearance of food is instrumental and influences the taste. Everything from their basic California roll (made with real crab meat, not imitation) to more complicated sushi creations like the Box Sushi (fresh seared tuna and crab meat pressed into a bamboo box with sesame seeds and eel sauce) or the Salmon Six Steps (6 pieces of salmon each prepared differently and beautiful places on bamboo stairs). I have never had anything here I disliked or sent back! They also have freshly shipped fish from Japan on Friday's so that's the best time to visit. Check out the chalkboard for their specials. 

Have I said enough? Simply check it out for yourself!

Talk about delivering more than you promise -- that describes this place in spades! We were in search of food before a show, and we happened upon Zuzu's Kitchen. From the outside, I thought we were probably going to leave hungry -- not much curb appeal. But inside is well-decorated and spotless, and the staff is friendly.

But the food is the reason to come back. We ordered veggie burgers that were the freshest we've ever had. Fantastic food, and a place I'll come back to next time I'm in the area. Thank you, Zuzu's!

Not sure if the nigiri cuts are normally that thick but we tried the six step salmon and tuna and the cuts of fish were so thick that it wasn't enjoyable. The rice was too mushy and compact. We also had the uni shooter however the ponzu was quite heavily poured that it overpowered everything. Should really just be a dash of ponzu but the ponzu was half of the shot. The uni nigiri was probably the highlight as well as the toro sushi on the tuna six step however not memorable. The rolls on the tuna six step were quite messily cut. 
There was also part of a shrimp shell on one of the cuts of tuna between the rice and fish. 
Overall, not sure if this was an off day for them or if it was just hyped up but I was quite dissapointed. Sometimes less is more and in this case, I feel that the fish should be a bit more delicate and not a huge cut. Sushi should be enjoyable in one bite. Left feeling unpleasant in the stomach and displeased with the overall experience. Service was a bit lacking as I had to ask what each of the steps of fish were (what sauce, cut and preparation) and never got checked up on during our meal. Seeing all the raving reviews really made this place seem like the place to go to, however I was dissapointed.

Best Sushi in town! 
All the specials are "to die for".
The halibut carpaccio is the bomb and one of my favorites, and the Red Dragon... Tiger Roll... Mexican roll..Dang.. I guess they are all my favorites!

My son is a "sushi snob" and found this place while he was attending UCSB. He and his housemates would try to eat here once a week.  While we were visiting..my wife and Tried this place for the first time... and now we are hooked!  Reminds of of a small sushi bar in Tokyo that we visited in 2019.

We love to sit at the sushi bar, enjoy the  bottles of ORIÓN BEER and talk to the chefs... it's a blast... and if you toast a cold Orión or Sake... to the chefs...  the whole place lights up with smiles!

If you want the best sushi..go to Sun Sushi!
Buy some Orión Beer and bring on the laughter and smiles and great sushi. 

We love this place!
5 stars!!! Every time!
Arigato chefs!

I sometimes frequent to this PJ's location when I am "attending" church per my mother's request or studying here when I cannot concentrate at home. There are plenty of inside and outside seating. They recently changed their soft padded chairs to all wooden hard seats which I felt like was better since the padding on the older chairs were starting to wear away.

I usually order a hot/iced medium coffee with an extra shot of espresso to give me that kick starter I need in the mornings or before I begin study sessions. The nice thing about their espresso shots are that they're cold espresso shots so they don't melt all your ice down. I began drinking my coffee black a few years ago and found that you could really identify the true taste of different coffee grinds when it's not masked by cream and sugar. PJ's black coffee is my favorite because it's not too bitter and smokey like other places (Starbucks). Staff is usually friendly and nice!

Sun Sushi tastes great but it is expensive for small portions. We paid almost double what we normally order at most sushi places to feel like we were content.

However, the service is great and the food came out quick. All the sushi we ate was delicious.
If you want to eat quality sushi and are willing to spend a little more money for it, this is the place.

Lunch after church in my neighborhood led me to Companion Cafe. Most days I would opt for breakfast food over lunch, but today I ordered a lunch sandwich. Fowl weather is yummy. A good balance of sweet and savory between fresh multigrain slices of bread.
Order at counter and they give you a order marker to set at your table. Soft drinks and water are self serve. Stainless steel cups for water. Leave your trash and the staff will buss your table.
Staff is nice. Food is fresh and delicious. View of bakery while eating is different and interesting.

If you are looking for an accurate pick up time or if you need a punctual scheduled pick up time, do not go to zuzu's. Had a scheduled pick up.   Was not ready and provided zero explanation.  Left waiting a half hour after it was "ready".  I understand it happens but at least an honest explanation and owning it.   Came off as their regular process.
Thomas came out to do some fence repair and did a good job.  Would definitely use him again.

The experience I had with this company wall so unprofessional. I only called to inquire about services and to ask if they do a certain job, never booking an appointment for them to come to my home. First things first they call and text you extremely early in the morning and after no reply they just show up at your home unannounced bagging on the doors. And no mask in the middle of a pandemic. Save yourself the time and energy.

Sun Sushi is a great sushi restaurant! The workers are attentive and always provide great service. The food is always amazing & not too expensive for sushi! I always get a Crunch Roll (which always hits the spot) and this time I tried the Red Dragon Roll. The Red Dragon Roll was amazing! I would definitely recommend visiting Sun Sushi if you are in the area!

Really great customer service I enjoy it every time I go.... the people are nice and they customize anything that I need! Very attentive and fast. I don't care for the food that much but the coffees and Bubble Teas are great!

Horrible location!!! Same experience as another that left a review. I canceled my membership months ago, only to be called and texted begging to renew. Then two months later they charge my credit card. Had to report Aneissa to Oro Valley PD for theft and dispute with my bank with proof of phone calls and texts, can't even get cooperate to care enough to respond or protect their own employee for theft. STAY AWAY FROM THIS ONE AS YOUR HOME STUDIO FOR BILLING! F45 is a WAY better workout, cleanliness, and friendliness for the extra 5 minute drive. For members of OTF ask your self if you ever see people that go here for this workout ever change. Not many if any, it's a poor workout and way to much cardio and the same over and over again.

Alex is great. Unfortunately, management is not, especially the studio manager. Had to get a hold of, you'll get the runaround for months when you do, and in the end they'll still try to screw your over. It shouldn't be that difficult to get help. You'll have a better experience if you go to another Orangetheory nearby. Both the Grant St and Marana locations have been much better. Go there instead!

A lovely Japanese place that serves fresh fish from Japan. We went as a group of 4 last Thursday and got ourselves the fancy-looking and very fresh and melt-in-your-mouth 6-step salmon and tuna. Highly recommended, friendly and helpful staffs and great sushi chefs! I will be returning sooooonest :)

This review focuses mostly on Metrolink light rail system because a bus is a bus is a bus. The St. Louis metro area has had a light rail system for slightly over 2 decades.  If you are not from there, or are not familiar with the area, there is at least one thing that might cause you to take note - it crosses the Mississippi River!  Come to think of it, so do the Metro system trains in the Twin Cities in order to service both Minneapolis and St. Paul.

The representation of the layout encountered on brochures or on the trains is, in a way, inaccurate.  The routes appear to be very linear.  In reality, they are not.

The rail system has 2 lines, known as the Red and the Blue lines.  For a large extent of the route, they overlap and use the same right of way.  It is above ground, and visible, in virtually all instances and only functions as a subway in the downtown core. 
 
It's easier to discuss what the system does on the Illinois side of the river, which also has bedroom communities for St. Louis.  Both the Red and the Blue lines cross the Mississippi River into Illinois, with the only difference being that the Red line continues farther along the right of way than does the Blue line.  And, again, the trajectory is not linear and seems to sweep in a southeasterly direction toward Belleville, IL and towns in that area.

On the more populous Missouri side, both lines cover all the major stops in the city of St. Louis's downtown core so it doesn't matter if you use the Red or the Blue line ... but only as far inland from the river as Forest Park.  That station is actually named Forest Park - De Baliviere and the announcements really botch the French pronunciation of that surname to the tune of "Da-bah-luh-vehr" or something like that.  Just bad.  From there, the Red line goes northwesterly to the airport and to the UMSL campus.  However, from Forest Park, the Blue line continues due west toward Clayton, sort of a corporate edge city for St. Louis, and then makes a broad southwesterly sweep to the southwest suburbs.  Note that, to the west of Clayton is the Richmond Heights station, from which it is only a few easy blocks to the St. Louis Galleria, a fine commercial center.

For regular commuters, there are all sorts of pass combinations available and, needless to say, they work on the extensive bus network under the same purview.  For tourists, a day pass is $7.50 and a weekly pass is $27.  At 4 or more days, you come out ahead with the weekly pass. 
 
The rail system was really needed here because there are many area freeways with only 3 lanes in each direction, including cross-country I-70.  Not only that, every key area of downtown is covered by the train system - the main downtown area, the convention center, Laclede's Landing (think Gateway Arch), the stadium, the transportation hub (train and bus stations), and restored Union Station.

The ridership on the Metrolink is more animated and vocal than on the light rail trains in, say, more stoic and reserved Portland and Seattle.  Now, while I may not be a contributor to the decibel level, I certainly do enjoy observing the humorous banter.  And, for this, the Red line seems to be a better bet than is the Blue line.  Let's just get right to it ... characters gravitate toward public transit rail ridership more than they do to buses, taxis, or even their own cars.  So, take a deep breath, climb aboard, sit down, read something, listen to music, look out the window, do some people watching, and it'll all be good.  Or, it should be! Because the system thoughtfully goes to or within walking distance of all the major places a resident or a visitor would need to go, Metrolink gets 4 stars from me.
Absolutely delicious and great service. I ordered the dragon roll and I highly recommend it!!

I love Sun Sushi! One of the best places for sushi in Santa Barbara. We have done take out and dine in and each time it's phenomenal. Even with things being uncertain and ever changing with Covid their quality has stayed consistent and it's definitely one of our go to restaurants now.

This feels like a little hole in the wall, but I guess many of the best sushi joints give off that vibe.  We were spending a long weekend in the Santa Barbara area and stumbled up this place. We ordered the California, Dragon, and Crunch Roll, as well as the Salmon 6-steps.  

I've never seen the Salmon 6-steps before, so I was curious to see what that was all about.  I gotta say, that sh* was bomb!  I almost wish they had a Salmon 12-steps! Maybe I should have just ordered 2!  Each piece had a slightly different flavor.  Each piece was also quite fresh; no fishy smell or taste.  That was the highlight of my dinner.  ...and I wasn't even really hungry!

The rolls were primarily for my wife and kids.  They were your typical run of the mill sushi rolls.  Nothing fabulous, but very good nonetheless.

I don't live in the area, so it's unlikely I'll be back any time soon.  But if I should ever find myself in Santa Barbara again, it'll be worth dropping back here again for some steps!

This place is amazing. Incredible food, environment, and staff. I got the brioche breakfast sandwich and it was so good. The prices are really reasonable here too. It's a great place to go with people or alone to get some work done in a great environment.

I ordered food from their online website for pickup (lamb and beef gyro with Zuzu sauce) and went to the restaurant to pick up the food after about 30 minutes only to be told it wasn't made because the printer was broken. I told 'Dereket' (the employee) my order again in person and was told to wait 10 minutes for the food to be made which was fine to me since it would be fresher. After I got my order and went home which is about a 10 minute walk, I found out the sauce was missing. I needed the sauce since the gyro is dry without it so it was necessary to go back. Long story short, the service is terrible and the employees don't care about the customers time. Note to manager: train your employees to treat customers better and get the order right especially if they messed up and made the customer wait. However, the gyro was really good with zuzu sauce even though it was cold by the time I walked to get my sauce and come back.

Neighborhood gem! I live very close to zuzu's and it's so dangerous being so close because it's so good! Initially ordered because of proximity, but keep returning because of the high quality customer service and amazing food. My go to is the buffalo chicken wrap with fries. These are some of the best fries I've ever had - perfectly seasoned but not too seasoned. The guys who work here are so nice and have thrown in free garlic knots when picking up food. The menu can look limited at first glance, but I Recently called and asked for a Stromboli (not on the menu), and they whipped it up for me at a very cheap cost. And it was delicious. Must go here!

Discovering Zuzu's was a silver lining in our COVID-19 quarantine experience.  It's clearly always been a place that primarily serves takeout, so they're a well-oiled machine with long hours that we rely on now for easy online ordering and quick pickup or delivery.  The staff is friendly and the menu is huge.

I waited to review Zuzu's until we'd tried it a few different times for a few different meals, a la Craig Laban.  The best items are the sandwiches, especially the Zuzu's chicken sandwich, and milkshakes.  The pizza is decent and relatively cheap, but we plan to return to our usual pizza takeout spot now that we've given Zuzu's a try.  The wings aren't great; although there are lots of interesting sauce options, the wings themselves are tiny and not super flavorful.

We look forward to continuing our menu exploration and certainly will keep returning for sandwiches and milkshakes at minimum.  Highly recommended to those in the neighborhood and beyond.

This is a bad company.  They don't honor their pricing plans, always moving you to a higher priced plan, regardless of your contract.  Internet service is very slow, usually less than a quarter the speed they promise, and my phone goes out-of-service several times a year, sometimes for days, sometimes for more than a week, and they just don't care.

While I love their salads, I order online and pick up curbside and their online ordering process leaves much to be desired. And then only about half the time I get what I ordered.  Bread is usually missing that is on the receipt as ordered.  

My office is close by but just tired of their poor service.

My mother is in her 90s.  She has had her land line since the early 60s.

When the line went out I waited on hold with customer service for almost an hour and a quarter to speak to a human being.

I wonder how many people die each year due to the lackadaisical service offered by Centurylink. . . .
Great option for lunch. Fresh bread, good soups. Sandwiches taste good but are a little light on filling (meat and cheese).

I am SO impressed with this place. My friend suggested we check this place out. I blindly say yes and we make our way there. At first glance I thought we were at the wrong address as it is very residential. So we walked in with caution and were warmly greeted. The place is a house that has been turned into a cafe, which adds a degree of warmth. The young man who owns the establishment gave us a rundown of each of the donuts and how they are made. One can appreciate when someone takes pride in their work as he does. 
I ordered the raspberry basil donut and smoked latte. I was blown away by the donut. It was reminiscent of a raspberry vinaigrette. The play of salty and sweet worked excellently. The donut wasn't cakey like most donut shops, but was light and chewy. I was impressed at this moment, but then I was blown away. When I ordered the smoked latte I assumed it was made by caramelizing the sugar or maybe even adding some liquid smoke to the milk. The gentleman comes out with a glass apparatus and a burner, then actually smokes the latte table-side. My friend and I were both flabbergasted. 
I give this place 10/10 on ALL counts. Service, food, experience.

Ordered here for the first time last night and would rate the food a 7/10. My bf and I ordered a large Margherita pizza and tiramisu, which was from a different bakery. The price was on point and the service was great. Very friendly staff! The tomato sauce was rich and full of flavor. That was the best part about the pizza BUT it was not cooked long enough. Extremely floppy and needed to be in the oven for a few more minutes. You can tell from the pic that it could've used some additional time. It was still delicious and after putting the pizza back in my own oven for a few more minutes it was perfect...but I shouldn't have to do that. I read some reviews and seems like this place can be a bit inconsistent sometimes. I really did think the service was great and I would still happily come back to give this place another chance. Order pizza again and I would also love to try their Ethiopian food. The tiramisu I was not a fan of  and my bf agreed. It had a strong coffee flavor, which we liked but it just wasn't that great. I read reviews that their milkshakes are where it's at so maybe I will try that next time!

What a cute local stop to check out some delicious sweets!  The mango donut was outstanding! Service was friendly!  The donut batter was great but there was a lot of toppings that made it super sweet if you like that kinda thing!  Wish for just a glazed but maybe I'm too simple!  Would go back!

Went by the other day and it was closed down.  Not sure if they are planning on reopening or not.  They used to sell their pastries at the farmer's market in Boise and they were really good.  I hope they aren't closed for good.

So I yelped best sushi in Santa Barbara and this spot came in at #1. I decided to eat there last night and all I can say is I'm not sure how it garnered the top spot on Yelp. The rolls had the exact same sauces on them, which wasn't even good. We ordered the lobster roll, Mexican roll, and the salmon delight roll. The quality of the fish was below par. The salmon delight roll and the Mexican roll were too salty. I'm not from the Santa Barbara area, and if this is the best sushi Santa Barbara has to offer, all of you from Santa Barbara that frequent this place, I feel for you. You haven't had real quality sushi, and all these good reviews, make it that much obvious. Service was good and attentive.

What's not to love about Companion?!

I'm not the hugest fan of sandwich-ish places but I give Companion 5 stars for this type of eatery. 

The only sandwich I didn't love was the roast beef/French dip but hey, there's always something that doesn't fit your palate's preferences. 

The variety of soups, salads and sandwiches offer a great variety for pleasing a crowd and they're all great quality. 

The sweets are tasty too! My favorite is the brownie bite! 

Companion also offers cooking classes.
Really great quality sushi!! I love coming here whenever I'm in the area. The spicy tuna on crispy rice is amazing. And their tea mugs are really cute.

Smalls towns don't get the same service as big cities... Don't charge me the same if you cant deliver the product as paid for.... Not a fan. I cant run more than 2 devices off of the service I buy off them. I called asking why my rates went up and he stated it was a note sent in mail.  I never got it. Online it shows I can have internet for $49 for life... My price keeps going up. I was set up when I signed up over 3 years ago to have them send a modem...i never got it so I bought a new one. .. I wish I new of the lawsuit against them... I should be paying way less for this horrible service... Over 3 years.. Shouldn't my price drop the longer im with you... Every time I call in its to a person who can barely speak English so I cant understand.... Nothing but aggravation since signing up... Beware new customers your bill will change as well as your service.

Wow!!! The difference a day makes!!!

New owners!!! New attitudes!!! Fresh vibe in the place. The location is at 6600 Franklin Ave in front Rouses across from the UNO Lakefront Arena. 

I stopped in for a caramel granita after early voting this October 2020 and what a pleasant surprise it was to meet the new owner; she is beautiful inside and out, she was smiling and full of joy. Her joy spreads over into the whole atmosphere; the vibe when you enter is simply welcoming and amazing. 

The caramel granita was super tasty & refreshing. Although it has dairy in it and I'm not doing dairy, this is such a refreshing and welcoming treat, I just had to suck it up, literally and figuratively, and bear the discomfort. 

The cranberry muffin was fresh and I asked them to warm it up; it was oh so tasty, warm and melted like butter in my tummy. 

I look forward to many, many more interactions at this facility, I love it here.

I've never considered myself to be a hot dog fan but after the hot dog I had at The Donut + Dog I've converted to a full blown fanatic! I have seen pics of the Elote Loco Hot Dog on instagram so I finally gave in to the temptation and decided to give it a shot. We went on a cold Saturday night, we parked out back in their huge parking lot (don't pay for parking - there's so much room out back!) and walked in to a beautifully warm room with a fire going. The owner is one of the friendliest and most genuine person I've ever met! He walked us through the menu, explaining where they source their meat, how they make their coffee, donuts and chicharrones! I ordered the Elote Loco with fries and my husband got the Not So Basic - which is wrapped in bacon - and upgraded his side to the chicharrones with queso. We also weren't going to miss out on the donuts so we each got an OG to go for the next morning. The food came out quickly and oh.my.gosh. my food was all perfect. Did I mention that the hot dog is a chorizo dog on the Elote Loco? It's perfect. We ate in silence because we couldn't slow down long enough to make a sound except for a satisfied grunt now and then! haha! Seriously, Hillsboro Village got really lucky with The Donut + Dog moving in, it's a great addition! Also, I read the reviews about people being salty that they run out of food...I get that it's frustrating but I love that The Donut + Dog are sustainable minded. It doesn't make sense to have quality food that is wasted because they weren't as busy as expected. They are a new business, if they run out of food, congratulate them on a busy day and just decide to come back later - because it's worth it - and it's quality food!

This place is adorable. From the painted hot dogs and donuts on the concrete walkway to the fireplace and barn wood counters- perfect decor. Now- the donuts are 20 hr brioche dough. Makes for Perfectly light and fluffy doughnuts. I got the 99 problems donut and it was amazing light and full of fruit flavor. The honey bourbon pipet was perfectly paired. I also go the nitro coffee-- beautifully smooth and creamy taste. DELISH and everyone should try them out!

As a Kansas Citian who is uber jealous of any city with a light rail or effective public transportation let me just say Grrrr.  

Parking downtown at our hotel was outrageous so we opted to park by the Delmar Loop stop to grab the Metro back downtown.  First, what a great thing for baseball fans to have!  We used it mostly for exploring St. Louis' shopping on the cheap.  It was a nice way to get to know a city that we could have paid a lot to taxi's to get around in.  

It is very clean and  a nice comfortable ride.  The only part we were not prepared for was the very loud and unstoppable preaching of one of the guests on the train.  We were a little taken aback, it was a little much and made us feel awkward to talk to each other or even look toward the front because we thought we'd get called on for "audience participation."  But hey, it's good to know that freedom of speech is alive and well.  

Congrats on having some nice public transportation.  Here's hoping KC can follow your example.

Such an upbeat spot - staff have great energy with reliably good coffee & great pastries. Today I tried the pretzel croissant & it's as great an idea as it sounds -actually better! Will have to go back for more as well as holiday gifts for a variety of tastes.

DO NOT USE CENTURYLINK. I applied for install on 11/24 and was told it will be installed 11/30. 11/30 get called they ordered wrong parts and i found out they just canceled my order. 
I reordered on 11/30, that install was set for 12/7. 12/7 i get the same phone call, they ordered wrong parts and can't do it.
I reordered on 12/7 install was suppose to be this week.
I get called today the scheduling app was down and i needed to reschedule a date. Jay, the representative told me word for word my install would be Saturday 12/12 at 8am. 
Jay sends me a confirmation email saying install with be February 8th. 
While having to work from home, I'm approaching ONE MONTH of no wifi because centurylink isn't competent enough to do their job. 

Thank god centurylink is in contract with my complex to be the sole provider and then refuses to provide service.

I hope this company goes under, I would die a happy man if that happened

I have noticed a steady decline in quality of food and service in combination with longer wait times for a table and food at this location. We used to eat here probably a couple times a month, but frequent mistakes on orders, constantly being out of menu items, and way too long of wait times have definitely been a problem.  This evening takes the cake, though. Many times in the past we have made to go orders over the phone for my wife to pick up when she gets off work. I called to make the order at 3:40 pm. The first lady I talked to redirected me to the kitchen to make the order. From that point I was on hold on and off for 10 minutes. The lady at the front desk would pick up the phone every couple minutes and ask what I needed, and I would tell her "I need to make a to go order". She would reply, more exasperated each time, "They still haven't picked up?!" They finally picked up and I made my order,  which was only three items with only one special request, not a gigantic order or something. They said it would be ready in 20 minutes. My wife arrived at 3:10, and she paid for the order and was sent to the to go kiosk to wait. She was there until 3:50. They neglected to tell me when I ordered or her when she paid that they were out of some of the items on our order. They finally found our order after searching several times. The one special request I made was not granted. At this point I have written off this location completely. I'm not expecting gourmet food or spectacular service from any Cracker Barrel, but at least expect a consistent level of competence that seems to completely elude this particular store.

On another note, I have never experienced any rudeness from the servers or hostesses, but I don't know if this is possibly an issue with the kitchen staff or maybe just terrible communication between the two. 

Regardless, if you HAVE TO have Cracker Barrel, I suggest going down the road to the Hendersonville location.

Wow I'm blown away by this little gem !   I am kinda  sushi snob and I have to say best sushi I've had in Santa Barbara yet !!! Everything was amazing down to the salad !    And miso ! Yes I'll be back

Believe the reviews. 
A friend of ours actually recommended a different place, but after looking at their menu and reading reviews and then reading the reviews for Sun Sushi, we knew this was the place to go. 
No it's not fancy. Don't go for the atmosphere, go for the amazing food and great service. 
The blue fin tuna was like butter. 
Literally everything we had was delicious. 
Get there early as it's a small place and parking kind of sucks (like most places in SB), but you'll be glad you did, and so will your taste buds!

Yesterday was the most extraordinarily terrible food experience I have had in a really long time and it makes me sad and I want my money back. Why should I order from here again? 

I hadn't had Zuzu's wings in so long and I decided to treat myself. I had just gotten off work, had the house to myself, a good series on Netflix and no where to be... 

I call Zuzu's : $15 (after tax) for 10 wings? Ok -- pricey. 

I pickup the wings, get home, open the box....

Of the 10 wings, 2 were chicken drumstick lollipops and had no actual meat on the ends; just bone and cartilage. 4 wings were so gross and overly plump that I questioned if they were properly cooked. I actually couldn't bring myself to eat them. The 4 wings I COULD eat (for $15) weren't good! They were edible, not GOOD. 

The CELERY was hands down the most enjoyable portion of the meal. WTF Zuzu's? 

Why should I order from here again?

Trying to get anything resolved with this company is impossible. I was billed almost $300 for a service I never used for not 1 day. It was impossible to close the account and I was lied to and shuffled around from representative to the next all with different answers and promises on how to resolve this issue. 5 months later and there is still no resolve. I wish i could give a zero rating. Save yourself a huge headache from the worst customer service ever.

This is an AWFUL restaurant for delivery! The food is FROZEN and NOT FRESH! I had ordered from Hungry Panda, on the menu it has showed salmon(kama) with picture of salmon sashimi, and the restaurant give me tempura-like salmon! I had paid $15 dollars for toro, and the quality is very bad. The meat is very lose, taste like FROZEN toro that has been unfreezes and it's only 3 pieces. I don't mind if the toro is 3 pieces, I'm looking for quality, which this restaurant clearly doesn't have. I have visited this restaurant many times before COVID-19, their salmon 6 steps was fresh so does their sweet shrimp and tuna 6 steps. But this time I'm really disappointed!

Yes! This place lives up to the hype! If you are wondering what's the big deal about donuts and hot dogs, read on. 

If food can be paralleled with fashion, I'd say Donut+Dog is a fashionable designer presenting a haute couture take on a plain jane classic. D+D has elevated hotdogs to a fusion food; the brioche donuts are french and chic, look and taste-wise; and how many places will serve you fantastic tasting coffee drinks with a meal and a dessert? I actually sought D+D out because I badly wanted to have a delicious coffee drink, satisfying food and dessert under one roof- for some reason this trifecta is not as common as it seems.

D+D has a fair selection of coffee, donuts, hotdogs, sides, drinks and soft beverages. We ordered the lunch special for $9.95 - the banh mi dog, paired with loco fries and ice-tea. In addition, we got the hot campfire mocha and the dirty churro! All were solid flavors and absolutely delicious. While most of us would think "it's just hotdogs", the use of organic produce (and I think locally sourced) is the foundation of these above average dogs and donuts. 

The brioche donuts look beautiful, I almost wanted everyone of them. We decided on the dirty churro, which was sweet, light and airy. I love the crumble as it adds a crunch to the soft texture. Flavor was amazing and highly recommend it. 

So hotdogs are always problematic for non-sausage/pork consumers like me. But guess what? They had the option of a beef sausage so we went with a beef dog banh mi and we loved the flavor. It's a great twist on the banh mi! A little spice from the jalapeño, a little hint of pickle daikon, and beefy goodness...a very impressive fusion. 

The loco fries are what will make u truly loco! So delicious- tangy, a little kick and gorgeously crisp. I am loco about the loco fries! Also, the portion of dog+fries is decent.

The campfire mocha was playful and delightful. It's a s'more-y mochaccino; very well balanced and would definitely recommend it. 

And, what hospitality! So pleasant, friendly and upbeat. I could almost hear Mr.Rogers sing in my head, "won't you be my neighbor?". Quite literally though, the donut and dog is a transformed house in the hillsboro neighborhood- that explains the warm, welcoming and inviting feeling? 

I think it is  D*D (double dangerous), that I have finally tasted D+D (mathematical pun-intended). I can see D+D become my easy choice for hanging out over a quick fun delicious meal. 

P.S The one thing is it is a $1 to add a beef frankfurter.

Easily on my list of favorite places to go!! The size of these delectable treats was very surprising, the pics on the website had me fooled - these donuts are HUGE and worth every single calorie!! These carefully crafted donuts are almost too pretty to eat.... Oh, but eat you must. Kickstarter, Boss Hog, Southern Belle, and their seasonal donut;
Pumpkin Spice Latte, are my favorites. ESPECIALLY the Pumpkin Spice Latte - Pumpkin Filled, Cold Brew Glaze, toasted Cinnamon Meringue, Salted Caramel drizzle..... OMG!! I have yet to try the beef hotdogs, but I have had the Hot Chicken Sandwich, Truffle fries, and the Left Coast Burger.... man....the flavors of this burger, which is served on their O.G. donut...... YES PLEASE!!   

I found out about this little jem in April; four months after I arrived in Nashville, one month after the tornadoes, and one month after the early stages of this pandemic. Eater Nashville had listed The Donut + Dog as one of the businesses that was open for takeout orders (only). Thank goodness I extended my contract (healthcare traveler) or I would have completely missed this place. The courteous customer service and quality of food keeps you coming back for more.

Beer is available on tap and if you're a coffee drinker, I suggest the Horchata Cubano.
Weekends get pretty busy so, go early or pre-order and get your food to go.

This place has been good to us.  Have ordered from them multiple times.  Have had the margherita pizza, the regular pizza, the Zuzu chicken sandwich  (at the recommendation of the guy that answered the phone bc they were sold out of the lamb gyro... this sandwich was delicious).  

It's not the best pizza or sandwich you're ever gonna have.  But it's quality, it's consistent, and for the cost, I'm not sure there's a better value in Philadelphia.  

5 stars.

A shop that sells hot dogs and donuts under one roof? I will say that this is a first for me as I've never seen this combination. Another first for me is going into a place that sells donuts and not buying one! 

The Donut + Dog is located in Hillsboro Village and is in a cozy little house. Their porch and interior were both inviting and charming. I was greeted by an employee at the cashier once I walked in. He was very friendly and made a few recommendations once he learned I had never been in before. I wanted to try one of their great-looking hot dog lunch combinations which is your choice of a hot dog, a side and a drink for $9.95. I settled on the B.A.T.  which had bacon, avocado and tomato. I got the house chips as my side and an iced tea from their soda machine. I really enjoyed everything. The brioche bun was very fresh-tasting bread and the flavors on the hot dog all worked together. The chips were crispy and well-seasoned and even though I got my order to-go they did not get soggy. 

I was pleased with everything and certainly will be back. Hopefully next time to try a coffee-drink and a donut! 

Tip: Vanderbilt students and employees get 10% off your bill

Don't, don't, don't even think of getting this service. After numerous service calls, techs could not stop service from disconnecting every hour or more.  I tried to live with it for a year, but after 4 days with NO service I finally cancelled.
Now I'm being billed almost $200. for an early disconnect. Don't make the same mistake I did. Don't sign up or believe anything they tell you.
Worst internet service I have EVER had since the internet was invented.

2 months prior, in early February I ordered Fiber Gigabit internet from CenturyLink.  1st let me be clear, I have a RF engineering and IT background. I'm not the average idiot with home internet and have thousands of dollar of professional enterprise grade IT gear as my home network. I'm also well aware of the dubious reputation CenturyLink has in the industry for screwing this up and the utterly useless customer support for consumers or businesses.

I am still a Cox customer at 1gb at at nearly $149 per month and choose to move to Centurylink for the bi-directional fiber speeds of 1gband no data caps AND, most importantly the ability to obtain a 5x8 static PUBLIC IP address block.

3 months later, dozens phone calls, online chats, 2 service visits and still cannot get the correct account or my static IP addresses.

First of all, the customer support is provided by a bunch of south central or south east asians who only speak English as a second language.  As a US customer I expect those I'm talking to to comprehend and speak English. This alone is infuriating and causes language barrier difficulties only making communicating WORSE. I'm tired of talking to fake English names, or Ahmed every time.

Reps have little to minimal knowledge as to what they are talking about. Obviously script reading.

1.  Setting up fiber account online selects without your knowledge or input a pre-paid account called an Eshop or Web account.  This is useless type of account you can't do anything with. It's for lay people internet users and isn't eligible for static IP.  This wasn't known at time of order.  No where does Centurylink explain what the account is you're signing up for.

      Tech showed up and installed the Fiber ONT and left. Said call back to order static IP.

2.  Called to order static IP, said not available, must change account type to to a post-paid account and advised I could now order static.  Centurylink did a soft credit pull and assured me the account was changed to a post-paid CRIS account.

New service date set. Tech arrived, did nothing other than verify it was installed and left.   Cancelled the eshop account and got a new account number.

WRONG, you still can't order static even as a post paid account as it's still a web or eshop account.

3. More phone calls, more chats, going in endless circles.  Most reps don't bother and tell me I can't order static, static was never offered, isn't offered anymore since 2020 or the account isn't eligble. More frustration.

At this point I started a BBB complaint that has so far gone unanswered.

4. Still more phone calls. Still more online customer service chat still going in circles. Still non static IP order and each rep continues to tell me conflicting and useless information

Finally, after close to 30 chats and phone calls, i reach a technical support person who appears to be informed and verifies I am on a CRIS account an d can order static public IP.  He completes the order and says the static IP will be assigned by 715 on Friday 04/02/2021.

Now on Saturday, 04/03/2021 I contact customer / technical support to find out what the public static IP that's been assigned to be service is. I need to update the modem and update my own networking with this new IP address.

11 customer service reps bounce me around endlessly, same routing of yes you can, no you can't, I don't know, let me transfer you to yet another person.

The final rep states I am still not on the correct account time and static IP cannot be added.  He advised I must cancel this account yet again and call back on Monday to have sales "write up a new account" that can support static IP addressing on fiber.

CENTURYLINK HAS NOT RESPONDED TO THE BBB COMPLAINT

I STILL DO NOT HAVE MY STATIC IP ORDER COMPLETED NOR AM I ON THE CORRECT ACCOUNT.

THIS IS THE MUST INFURIATING CIRCLE JERK OF CUSTOMER SUPPORT I'VE EVER EXPERIENCED.

CENTURYLINK has one remaining opportunity to get this right.

Probably the most hit or miss place you could order from. We've maybe ordered from here 25 times since moving in a year ago?

The Chicken Boom Boom Pizza (chicken strips, boom boom sauce, ranch, parsley) has been our go-to, and we've turned a couple friends onto it. It's maybe the best tasting pie you could have. Sometimes, though, it'll have no substance in the middle of the pie and a slice tastes like cardboard for the first couple bites. Today the pizza came without the sauce it's supposed to come with. Had to sauce it up myself. Sometimes it's cold by the time we pick it up (on the timeline they gave us).

We've had other things that are good: Buffalo chicken calzone, onion rings, milkshakes. Some stuff not so good: their bone-in chicken wings, some of their other pizzas (steak boom boom was pretty weird). 

Service is spotty. Couple times had to wait a while past their estimation to get our food. When we order milkshakes, they usually don't start them up till we get to the restaurant.

It's cheap, and usually it's pretty quick, and most of the time it tastes good. I don't want to stop ordering from there. But I'd say one out of three times though something goes wrong.

Fresh and consistent food!
This has been one of my favorite places to eat for the last 3 years. The Zuzu fries are my absolute favorite! We ordered their pizza for the first time last night and it was very good. They will be my go-to place for pizza now too. I've had almost everything on the menu now, and I have yet to receive something I didn't like. You really can't beat the prices either. Highly recommend this hidden gem!!

I work in the West Port area and frequented the curbside delivery as it was convenient.  Too bad the online interface is inaccurate thus resulting in incorrect orders. Paul the manager, should be called, "the excuse maker" as that is only what he is good at doing.  Food used to be good, but now the salads have been reduced to 2/3 size of what they used to be.  No more to me. There are too many choices around the area and the service is so poor. Sad.

Wow, this isn't a regular sushi restaurant. I know my Japanese food--be prepared for some creative and delicious food! Atmosphere is nice, food is incredible.  I will return here whenever in the area.

I came here pre covid for some donuts. First, this is not the place to come for traditional donuts. This was a nice quaint place on the inside with specialty donuts. A person behind the counter explained the premise behind the offerings and helped with my selections. The price of each donut ranged somewhere between $3 to $4. After the purchase, I took them home for an evaluation. The donuts were good, but I would use the term donut lightly when referring to these treats. They were more like buttery sweet brioche bread treats shaped like donuts. They held up well over a day without the glaze breaking down. I did enjoy each one and hope you do as well if you decide to stop by.

This is my joint. I get the sushi lunch special once a week and replace the California roll with spicy tuna. The fish is fresh, especially Tuesday or Wednesday it's pretty much perfect. I know my fish, and have eaten at the best sushi restaurants in LA and Vegas lots of times. Ming is a great guy, great sushi chef. I feel at home, and happy to be a regular. Also, the rice is always perfect, Never a dry grain.

My wife, he cousin and I had dinner here on Friday night (08/28). We called in to ensure they had a open table if we came within 15 min. Luckily they did. We had the Yellowtail and Albacore Sashimi, Soft-shell Crab appetizer and some random nigiri. I also had the Spicy Toro Hand Roll and I gotta tell you, everything was fantastic. Every bite was great. The service was very attentive and things came out quickly. This might be my new go to Sushi spot.

I've come here several times over the years. The donuts are always amazing. The staff is super friendly. I happened to be there when someone  was injured in front of me. The staff was friendly, responsive, and professional handling that matter. The decor is cute. Would recommend the mimosa flight as well!

Ordered from the Foodsby ap. The CBLT is amazing and well made. The pretzels are good, as well. The tomato soup is not worth the money at all. No flavor and when I got it it was ice cold. I will never order the soup again.

I came here for dinner on Sunday night.
It wasn't crazy busy that night.
I saw omakase style with 5 courses meal on the menu.

Starter was mozuku-su with shoga and vinegar.
I loved it. 

2nd around was abalone, salmon saikyo, kaki fried.
It was very good presentation, pretty good portion.

Main was 10pices chef choice sushi and toro hand roll.
It was fantastic ! All the fish came from Japan and so fresh!

You can choose ice cream flavor for dessert.
The chefs and sever were super friendly.
If you order sushi, take a seat by sushi bar, they will tell you what you get for fresh sushi. 

I will definitely going back to sun sushi.

I was looking for an afternoon dessert in Meridian, yelped it, and happened upon this little place that I had never heard of.  What a darling little place!  I got there at about 1:45pm and they close at 2:30pm, so the owner lady explained what items she had left.  She was adorable.  I told her I found her on Yelp, and she gave me a cookie for my first-time visit - it was this yummy buttery sugar shortbread cookie ... made with potato chips.  

I'm not a super fan of cinnamon rolls or sticky buns, but the one in the case really wowed me.  She said if I was going to be eating it soon, she would heat it up for me, but I told her I would eat it in about a half an hour when I got home.  She said to make sure to microwave it for about 35 seconds.  

She gave me the tour of the place - there are a lot of old family photos of her family (parents and grandparents), curio cabinets and hutches with old time dishes and jewelry.  The cuteness even extends to the ladies' room that is clean, spacious, and decorated all frilly and nice too.  

When I got home to sit down and enjoy this sticky bun, I wasn't super impressed.  It tasted day-old but it made sense because it was what was left at the end of the day and she probably had made it at 5am and it was sitting in the case all day (much like the ones that you get on the clearance rack at Albertsons and Fred Meyer).  It was good, but not super good.  But then I remembered her telling me to heat it up.  So, I popped it in the microwave.  Oh.  My.  Land.  Heating it up melted all the gooey stickiness, warmed up the pecans, and made the dough all yeasty and soft and delicious again.  It was like night and day.  And it was such a delicious bite.  

The location is sort of odd, I feel like I have driven by there 900 times and never knew it was there.  It's right on Main Street, but it's in the same parking lot with another business (maybe it's even connected to it) so it's easy to miss it.  But don't miss it!

The pizza is really good here, but should probably be three stars.  STAY AWAY FROM THE WINGS.  Have had a few different pizzas here and they are great quality.  Calzones are also really good.  Now the wings,  I've tried them multiple times here.  The first time it was dried and crunchy with no meat.  It's good to support local so I tried them again and they were good.  Third time even worse than the first completely inedible.

WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE. I literally just got century Link (well, 2 weeks ago). Someone came to test the connection. They said it was good, but sure enough it doesn't work. Figuring this out, and trying to reach customer service has been a nightmare. After 45 minutes on the phone, we figured out that it would take an additional week to get someone here to figure out the issue. At this point she spends another 10 minutes confirming and repeating everything. Change your script centurylink. I still don't have that internet, but I'm honestly more pissed about the hours I've lost on the phone with these people

My first time here I took a chance on this place while at a friends in the area. This place went way beyond our expectations. The pizza was phenomenal. To me the pizza was the perfect mix between pizza from a sit down craft restaurant and pizza from a corner store. You can taste the quality and freshness in their food and for the price there's no beating this place. Adel the owner was very friendly every time I've been in there and actually remembered me from my first visit. Great food and exceptional customer service has made this place my new favorite pizza shop.
Get the Volcano Roll! Amazing! We love coming to this place because the service is great and the food is even better.

We used to live next door to this place and watched  it grow into a really good pizza shop.  Middle eastern influence with some great pizza, sandwiches, and wings. The guy who made the menu and started the shop sold it. Shortly after we  moved to a different part of the neighborhood and would order our favorites occasionally. This was our first time ordering in a couple of months. The large specialty pizzas cost 20 plus dollars , but don't taste or weigh like one. The attached picture was once one of their flagships, but weighs as much as an elios and was overcooked like a Saturday night forget me za. All in all. If I'm gonna pay 90$ for 2 pizzas and 30 wings, I'm gonna look somewhere else first. Wing prices might be high, and times are tough, but if you're making a light pie and are having a hard time, keep an eye on the oven.
My two sons 13/7 years old booked a extra job with Heery Casting. They had so much fun!!

Donut and dog has a pretty full-proof concept. I mean, what kind of sadist doesn't like hot dogs and donuts?

The good:

-great atmosphere. The workers were very friendly and there is nice outdoor seatings 

-the hot dogs and donuts were pretty good (7/10) rating

The bad:

Though this place will provide some solid instagram pics, the food is pricey. For two hot dogs, fries, and two donuts, it was about $30. That's not terrible, but it's a stretch for hot dogs and donuts. 

Verdict - food is fine, restaurant is fine, but definitely not a value play. If you're from out of town and are in the area, I recommend looking elsewhere. There are plenty of better food options for you. If you're local, i think it's worth a stop if you wanna try something new
Liars. False charges. Horrible customer service. They have the worst internet as well.

Stopped here for bfast on a Thursday morning.  Got there right at 7. We were the first ones there but there was a steady flow of people coming in every few minutes.  Luca was EXTREMELY attentive. My coffee was never empty.  The food was very good.  The restaurant and bathrooms were clean.  This was probably one of the beat experiences we've had at a Cracker Barrel in a few years.  I highly recommend stopping here.
I can't put into words how amazing this place is. It's probably the best sushi I have ever tasted. Anybody who has anything negative to say about this place is insane.

They continue to operate after the Governor's executive order to close for 30 days due to Arizona's spike in COVID-19 cases. This is very dangerous to the public health of the community and this disregard for the well-being of the public cannot be tolerated. Many businesses are dealing with the hardships of closing due to the unprecedented times we are in, so your lack of awareness is pure idiocy.

Recently moved neighborhoods within Philly and needed a new go-to pizza spot - it seems promising that Zuzu's will be filling the void.

I've ordered 3 times so far, usually pizza and wings and have yet to be disappointed.

The staff are friendly - I even got to sample the Zuzu milkshake because they made too much for another order.  Great marketing ploy because it was delicious and will now consider ordering one in the future, which is not something I usually think of doing.

Keep up the good work and I will keep coming back!

I am hoping these folks make it and I can upgrade their rating in the future. They are more than a 3, but not yet a 4 star. 

This a comfortable Mom And Pop kind of place. They serve Dawson And Taylor brewed coffee. But since it is served from a pump carafe, it wasn't as hot as we like it. I will ask them to zap it next time. They do have espresso drinks too.

Baked products ranged from cookies to pecan sticky buns. As first time customers, we were given a delicious butter cookie as a gift. Very good cookie and a nice gesture. In fact, their cookies are probably their best products. Try the chocolate quarter pounder cookie. 

They have croissants, including ham and cheese. But in all honesty, this item needs some work. Mine was under done and over-sized. Of course, I am comparing to Janjiu's croissants which are hard to compete with.

My wife had a apricot scone which she rated as good. It looked more like biscuit than a true scone. 

At 10 am they were out of cinamon rolls, so will have to try another day. I had a morning roll instead which I found to be very good. They also had pecan sticky buns available which called to me, but only so much sugar in one day.

We would come back for another try of more of their goods. We really want them to succeed.

Favorite restaurant in SB
Their short ribs and yellow tail collar is also really tasty
People here are very friendly

Yummy sashimi and good rolls!  Generally friendly service, but I definitely got the feeling that regulars were given favor over new patrons.     Calamari  and fried softshell crab was overcooked.  Freshest sushi I have had in town!

Brought in coworkers during the week, & family on weekends & whenever I'm there the place is busy &  the food is great. Sometimes it may look like there will be a wait but it's never taken more than 5 mins to order & the food arrives quickly. 
Love the coffee & baked goods of course. Seasonal variety of soups, sandwiches & salads are delightful. 
The other cool part is that you can look into the bakery so kids ( even the "old" ones) are fascinated by seeing the staff use huge mixing bowls & ovens actually baking the breads

I am from out of town, stopped here after a four hour drive through bugs in a Silverado. 
The outside of the wash looks rough but these three gentlemen but a great effort into making my truck look clean. Only $20 for a full size truck. 
I will come again for sure and recommend to anybody in the area.

I like Zuzu for what it is (see my prior review) - decent quality food at a fair price. 

However, today I ordered a cheese pizza with garlic spinach.  I assumed that meant fresh garlic. Instead, it was covered in garlic salt (not powder, salt). It was inedible. We had to toss it. Guess I'll boil some pasta?

I came during a snow storm on the way back to Illinois, a sign posted on the door saying they are understaffed and only have 1 server and 1 cook. We try our luck and are blessed with Donna as our server! She was working her butt off, we could tell and she gave us the best service we have ever experienced in the south so far. Such a sweetheart ! All the food came out together and pretty fast so kudos to the cook as well! 10/10 amazing service, very welcoming!

The pizza is good enough to kick my pizza cravings. There's a lot of different selections of pizza, and they've also never gave me an issue with customizing pizzas. My favorite part of Zuzu's are the french fries. They season them perfectly and they're usually crispy. Mozz sticks, onion rings, and sandwiches are pretty much run of the mill.

BEWARE!!!! If I could give ZERO stars, I would! He wrote a bid, promised to do the work in 3 days, requested a $1000 deposit, started work and did not complete 1 entire project. Then he messaged that his car broke down, next day same story, said he would come back the following week, and then sent a text saying he was sorry, that he could not return and hoped we could find someone else to complete the work. The trim work be completed in the master bath, had to be completely removed and redone because it looked straight out of Dr.
Seuss.

Yesterday I had the pleasure of attending the Wendy's in the Nashville airport and I'm still waiting for Ashton Kutcher to tell me I was on Punk'd.

After waiting in line for 10-15 minutes, a friend and I ordered our meals from the two cashiers. I ordered a Dave's single combo (no onions, no tomatoes) and a small chocolate frosty. What size combo? Medium. What would I like to drink? Coke. When the lady rang up my order, she stated my total was $16.something. I did the math in my head and knew the amount was too high so I asked her to read my order back. She couldn't and I still don't know why. The manager came over to void my order so I could start fresh and pay the correct total. I ordered the exact same items a second time and my total came to $18.something. If I stated my order was too much the first time, why wouldn't she realize it was incorrect the second time? The manager came back to void my order again, and for the third time I placed my order which totaled to $8.67. The receipt machine was out of paper and despite wanting confirmation my total was correct/probably needing it to dispute the charges to my bank, I told the cashier I didn't want to wait for my receipt.

I waited 5 minutes and was handed a bag and my coke. I wasn't surprised when I didn't receive my frosty and my burger had onions and tomatoes. I placed my frosty order a fourth time. What size? Small. Chocolate or Vanilla? Chocolate/how do they not have my order memorized at this point? 

My friend ordered a medium fry and a Fanta Orange Pop. The second cashier looked confused, so she repeated Fanta Orange Pop and pointed to the label on the soda machine. Naturally, she was given Hawaiian Punch. 
  
While we were waiting for our food, a man mentioned he'd been waiting 21 minutes for his chicken nuggets. My order number was 70 and his was 61. He walked up to the cashier and she didn't have his order in the queue and asked for his receipt. 

We had other friends that ordered after us and one was told "I meant to say order number 16 but I actually said 18" when handed the wrong bag.  

The icing on the cake was the small child running around in the kitchen. 

I would return to this Wendy's for the comic relief.

I selected Dr. Tomlinson as the office was in my network and was close to my house. I had no problem with the exam and found it very thorough. The issue came when I had to have a deep cleaning as I had not had one for 4 years (no dental insurance). This office will try to push unnecessary procedures and equipment on you without explanation, and they are aware most is not covered by insurance. I was told I had to schedule the cleaning in 2 appointments, which according to my insurance was not the case. I was also billed for a $100 toothbrush that was not covered. I will be completing the deep cleaning as right now I only have half my mouth done, but will not be going back for any other procedures.

Oh companion I love your breads and baked goods so much but man your cafe meals are a mess. 

I've come in a few times for lunch but the consistency at companions cafe is pretty sad. We grabbed a companion lotto which essentially is a you pick two. The turkey green chili was more of a veggie soup with turkey than a chili. I remember the south of the border salad was so yummy but the ingredients were subpar to say the least. Corn was mushy and tortilla chips were stale. Ugh. The Reuben while was pretzel bread sandwich it had 2 slices of slices is pastrami. For $12 I'll take my money elsewhere. 

I'll chalk it up to being in between the holidays but it was pretty sad. We will not be back any time soon for the cafe meals.

Extremely dissatisfied. I took my girls for breakfast today. Wait time wasn't bad. Sat down gave waitress our complete order as soon as she waited on us. It was a simple food order. Waitress came by one other time only because I flagged her down for a refill on my coffee. Two other people sat down at the same time as us. They received their food and were finished and us still no food and no one to ask where it was. Others sat after us and were eating and almost done. Still no food. An hour of waiting. Food finally comes after I complained and it was cold. Manager comes over and apologized. Her fix was to recook our meal. At this point my children are upset and I wasn't willing to roll the dice on how long it would take to recook the food, so we left.

Came to this restaurant for dinner. We to-go'd salmon "sushi," halibut "sushi," salmon delight roll, dragon roll, and Japanese fried chicken for two people. Overall, the fish was fresh and yummy. 

Salmon "sushi:"
We specifically asked them to do sashimi instead of sushi and the salmons wow'd us. It was pretty fresh that it melted in our mouth! Well $8 spent there.

Halibut "sushi:"
If you order this, you will see a thin slice of halibut on top of ball (oval shape) of rice. And you will get two pieces for $8. If I knew that, then I would've just ordered  2 thick slices of halibut itself to enjoy the sashimi only.

Salmon Delight roll:
If you cannot eat spicy food, ask them to either take out or set aside the jalepenos from top of the roll. It can get pretty spicy after eating 4-5 rolls. Otherwise this dish was good!

Dragon roll:
No comment. It was good. :)

Japanese fried chicken:
Well seasoned chicken. Just hope there was a special sauce on the side to enlighten the taste of the fried chicken. But it was worth getting it.

Would I come back to this restaurant? Yes! Just won't order halibut "sushi" but would order halibut sashimi!
I really like this place. It's a good place to go for reasonably priced and consistently good quality sushi. There are lots of options. I love the Mexican Roll and their yellowtail dishes.

This little unsuspecting spot is my new favorite! I was planning on bringing a box of treats to a friend and this gem was highly rated, so I thought I would try it out. 

The folks working were the sweetest!! I was given a rundown of all the items currently baked and ready to roll. Everything is large and definitely share size! But, that's honestly my favorite. So I sampled a bit of each of these. 

Everything is made from scratch and, boy can you tell!! The pastry for the danishes was AMAZING. I'll be dreaming of that for a while... 

And on your first trip in they give you a pecan shortbread cookie - made with potato chips! The owner's mother's recipe.

The staff is always friendly and they have a nice variety of deli type items for snacking. There are usually small and medium size cakes decorated in shapes of animals which are super cute. The majority of drinks are very good on the menu, I especially enjoy the chai latte. Unfortunately I have never had a decent cup of plain coffee here. Free city wifi.
Warning - hours on Yelp are incorrect - Used to be a favorite place, but appears to be permanently closed.

My daughter and myself are here Friday night and the food was awful. It was not home cooking. It was opening a can. Worse Cracker Barrel I have ever ate at
Your review  learn about great local businesses.

Please don't review this business if you received a freebie for writing this review, or if you're connected in any way to the owner or employees.

Great sushi bar with a local vibe.

My husband and I were visiting for the weekend and felt like having sushi, but nothing too fancy. Somewhere relaxed where we could sit at the bar and take our time. Sun Sushi came up, and I recognized it from dining at Tee Off next door, so we came in just before 7pm. 

It was quiet and we were seated at the bar right away. It feels like a classic sushi bar and they were ready to serve us as soon as we knew what we wanted. The place filled up pretty quickly with a dinner crowd. 

They have a good drinks list, with beers, wines, and lots of sakes. One of the sushi chefs answered our questions about the sakes and helped us choose one. He was attentive and ready to take our orders whenever we we decided on our next dish.

The miso was good, and a generous portion. We got a selection of nigiri - salmon, albacore, yellowtail, toro (fatty tuna), and scallop. Everything was beautifully presented, and most importantly all the fish was excellent. They also change things up a bit, for example the salmon had 2 pieces with ginger and 2 with a spicy concoction on top - not necessary when the fish is high quality, IMO, but it added a little variety. I would ask for the tunas without glaze next time, though. My only complaint is that the rice was a bit dry.

We also had a spicy tuna roll, the pieces were nice and small and they were well balanced, with a good amount of spice and not overloaded with sauce.

A great experience, and I'd definitely make a point to come back whenever I'm in town.

Absolutely the worst customer service experience I've ever encountered eating at restaurants. We get there 1 hour and 15 minutes before close to what I would call a not very busy night two days before Christmas. We were traveling through and just wanted a sit down dinner that would be somewhat quicker. Ordered quickly and that's where the wait began. 45 minutes after ordering waitress informed us the ticket was somehow lost and our food will be out shortly. We get our food 5 minutes before closing. Having a 1 year old and wanting to get back to traveling I started taking a trip of stuff to the car (had a 1 year old with us so lots of stuff to haul). Coming back in to help my wife get our daughter and the rest of the food (which we never ate because of how long it took to get) after starting the car. I get locked out of the building and I knocked on the window to see if I could be let back in to help my wife and daughter the hostess told me "it's not her problem". Called my wife who let me in and then a manager came over and acted like he's heard that his staff is useless one too many times and could care less. 

If I could give this place a 0 I would. Who knows how the food tastes when you have to wait over an hour for food (breakfast food nonetheless) only to be locked out while trying to get my wife and daughter back on the road.
Best croissants ever! Cool venue. Quick service. Had the Claytonian. Wish I could eat two or three of them.

I really love Zuzu's for their burgers which are some of the best in the city imo. The lamb burger and Zuzu's burger definitely carry it for me. However the sandwiches are disappointing. The Francisville flank sounded good but I was left with a small rubbery piece of beef with a horrible citrus taste that made it inedible. So much potential here.
Highly recommend this place. The food is exquisite and portioned well. Our server Luis was attentive and presentable making the overall experience very enjoyable.
Good quality and reasonably priced! Staff always polite and takeout sushi is nicely presented in large round trays.

I found Companion on Yelp while in St Louis. We needed a quick breakfast and a lunch to take with us. Our breakfast sandwiches were fabulous, mine, egg on croissant and my son's egg on bagel roll. Their sack lunches are very generous with huge sandwiches. Companion has a cool trendy industrial vibe, huge space to sit and enjoy with the ability to watch the production line. We'll definitely be back next time we're in St. Louis.

Woohoo! It only took me a year to go here! Man, why'd I wait so long! I could've eaten here multiple times! 

This sushi place took over the former Ahi Sushi, on upper State, I believe (which I used to frequent a lot.. for ramen.) they don't have ramen here and I remember not liking Ahi's sushi very much, but wow Sun blew my mind! Definitely the best sushi I've had in the last 7 years of being in SB. (Ok, I've been to Yoichi's, but that's not a spot you'll drop in last minute to spend less than your arm's worth.)

I trusted the reviews and went for the Box Roll and a salmon roll on the side. It was dinner and unfortunately I couldn't try their uni (my fav!) because they ran out. I usually don't go for super "saucy" rolls, but I really enjoyed the Box Roll! It's a bit sweet but it tastes really fresh. The salmon tasted really fresh too.

Service was amazing too! I came here with my dad and they were so nice to him! (He tends to avoid any new place on State St. because of bad service lol) That was such a plus. 

Definitely a spot to come back to! Good job!

I live at The Arboretum in Tucson. Since road construction started on Kolb my internet has slowed to a crawl. I can use my smart TV, but not my phone at the same time. My laptop takes 3 to 4 minutes to load a page. If I use my phone, the page takes longer to load.

According to the CenturyLink tech that came out  someone is here crossing wires and doesn't know what he's doing, so they spend their time coming out to fix his; meanwhile, getting through on CenturyLink's customer service or service line took me 15 calls. If you go off script, the customer service agent doesn't know how to proceed. It took 15 calls to get a tech out here. They asked me to reset my router ten times until I refused to do it again.  

CenturyLink is an abominable excuse for a company. With people working at home they need Internet. They need to be able to use their cell phone AND their laptop or use their cell phone ABD their television. That's not the case here at the Arboretum. Thank you CenturyLink for being incompetent.

Without a doubt the best sushi spot in Santa Barbara. Their fish is consistently super fresh every time I go making for delicious rolls. Location is a little random in a shopping center off state street but the quality of food makes up for outdoor dining in the parking lot.

My go to rolls are the salmon or yellow tail delight and the volcano. 

I usually just get takeout but last time i went I ate inside and the staff were incredible. Absolutely phenomenal sushi

I like this spot. My husband, 1 year old daughter & I had dinner on Saturday night a few weeks ago. The service was good, everyone was very kind & interactive with our girl. I don't remember what we ordered but it was all very good. We will definitely be back!

Went to Sun Sushi and had an assortment of dishes, all of which are excellent in quality and reasonable in price compared to the surrounding area. The sushi chefs at the bar and the waiters are considerate and accommodating, which makes for a great dining experience! One of the most cost-effective high quality sushi places in SB, highly recommend! Please see my individual dish ratings in detail:

Uni: First up was two pieces of delicious local santa barbara uni! They were fresh, slightly sweet, savory, and umami and gives a buttery melt in your mouth feel that is really extraordinary. I can't help but crave more uni :')

Salmon Six Step: Really lovely display of three different salmons (Scottish, Atlantic, Ocean Trout) prepared six ways. At a fair $22, this is not a cheap meal, but definitely high quality. The salmon was fresh, silky, and full of flavor. The seared salmon was particularly notable as it has a different texture than the rest, and tasted much thicker and firmer because of that. Each salmon was seasoned mildly different with soy, lemon, etc and added a nice hint, while not overpowering the star that is the salmon. Overall, really good way to sample different salmon!

Red Dragon Roll: This red dragon roll was amazing. It had a great combination of crunch from the tempura shrimp balanced with creamy avocado. The spicy tuna and mayo added extra flavor that really elevated the dish. All I can say is this dragon was slayed.

Yellowtail Delight Roll: Pleasantly surprised on how delightful this sushi roll was! The spicy yellowtail filling had a creamy texture that resembled salmon which was magical. Also, really love the spiceful elevation of a traditionally bland fish with sriracha, sriracha mayo, and jalapeno! Only thing I would change is instead of brining the jalapeno, maybe pickling it would've added some acidity.

Tempura Ice Cream: A gigantic scoop of red bean ice cream fried in tempura batter for only $7.95! The concept of tempura ice cream is particularly intriguing because you are frying ice cream in super hot oil, but the result is delicious! There is the outer crispy tempura layer that is warm which sharply contrasts the cold sweet ice cream inside. What I liked about this one in particular is that it didn't melt in two seconds because the ice cream was big enough. Tempura ice cream is definitely in the top echleon of desserts!

Chicken Kaarage: Wrapping up my Sun Sushi reviews with an appetizer of Chicken Kaarage, Japanese fried chicken! The chicken was very tender and crisp, and paired very nicely with a complimentary sriracha mayo I was able to acquire at the bar! Really love the excellent service and quality of food overall at Sun Sushi!

The staffs are friendly and helpful, but I have some suggestions for the sushi bar:
1. Please do not place a thawed shrimp head on your sushi plate, the liquid from that head will contaminate the sushi rice right next to it. It turns your appetite off when you see your sushi rice turned pink from the raw shrimp head juice.
2. Please learn the red snapper skin curing process properly, and the chef and the owner need to sample it before the serving. My first experience of the snapper sushi was not pleasant, the skin is as hard as a cowhide. I didn't say anything that time and tried to give the chef a break, nonetheless, the second time is worse, not only is the skin tough, but it has a fish bone in the skin! I gave the piece back to the waitress to show to the chef and hope the chef would be more careful when he preps the food.
3. Please do not place the uni on a soggy seaweed. 
I can see and appreciate the efforts from sushi chef in which it evidently showed up in the flavorful sushis that he assembles, and it's not a pricy place and you get your dollars worth, nevertheless, I just hope this place would thrive and make improvements along the way.
Waited for hour after they told us the wait was 30 minutes. Never got seated. Girl who was seating everyone had no experience and needs to work at Chick-fil-A learn then come back.

Best hour long workout ever. Takes the guesswork out of the gym. You can go at your own pace (or weight) and the coaches legitimately help with modifications. The staff is amazing, the variety of coaches all with different music playlists make the class fly by. Literally, the hardest part is showing up. Try it! You won't regret it!

I had a pleasant experience at Companion's, I went there just once to grab breakfast (to go) and everything was delicious. This time I went with few coworkers for lunch : I ordered their soup of the day as well a the combo for lunch, where you get half a sandwich with half a soup or salad, and a bakery treat ( $10.95 for the lunch combo). I didn't know what to expect portion wise, reason why I ordered this way. My total was $18.95 and it was plenty of food, I took half of it to go. You order the food and somebody comes to bring it to your table once ready. 

I tried the sandwich of the week, made with smoked ham, spicy mayo and ciabatta bread. It was ok, I think I would have enjoyed another one thought. I like that you can substitute the bread of your sandwich, one of my coworker ordered a salmon sandwich with a bagel  instead of ciabatta and it looked great. The soup was very tasty.
