For desert I had the chocolate chip cookie, which was good. Overall I think I prefered having their breakfast menu (love their almond croissants!) than the lunch menu, but will definitely go back. Note that it get busy for lunch, casual, and pretty noisy for me, but I had a good experience and recommend it !
I know my sushi and this place is absolutely outstanding! It's not the run-of-the-mill sushi either.

Been here about five times.  Parking is great. Nice large lot.  Plenty of seating. Nice it opens at 6am during the week. Plenty of time to stop by and not be late for work. 

There have been a few growing pains in terms of stopping here specifically for certain items and they don't have it, but it happens. 

Staff is friendly.  Service is typically very fast. One morning I had to wait maybe 15 minutes for the bagel/salmon but we'll assume that's growing pains. 

I had the claytonian and it was ok. The egg texture was off. Not smooth. The bacon and everything bagel was excellent. 

The pastries are amazing. My favorite are the donut, the pretzel croissant, and the blueberry muffin. The donut has a biscuit/croissant type dough that is not too sweet. Basically amazing. The pretzel croissant is a must try if you've never had one. 

I've had the Caesar salad for takeout. The first time it didn't have much but since then the portions were generous. It's tasty with bonus bacon. A little more dressing may make it better. It would be nice to also have croutons. 

At lunch starting at 11 they have various soups. You can get the salad and sandwiches pretty much anytime is what I was told.  They also have plenty of coffee options. 

The cafe is similar to the other restaurants but with a lot more parking and seats. The bakery is here so you have the opportunity to see the bakers at work. 

Bottom line. It's similar to a formerly local bread/soup/sandwich/coffee place but with much higher quality ingredients. Highly recommend a visit.

This dealership is over priced on there vehicles but the main thing I had go bad when I went here was that the will only give you half of the retail book value on your trade in vehicle. I mean if your trade in book value is $10,000 the will only give you $5,000. Not your cars retail value of like $15,000 not $10,000 so going here you will loss have the money you could have towards your new car if you go somewhere else that gives you full value of your trade in.
Just a warning for everyone in Idaho

Well, what can I say other than yum!! Where else can you get a grilled cheese sandwich with  donut "bread", and if that isn't enough, a so much better than traditional tomato soup.  Added a pineapple hard cider to drink for a lovely combo. My husband loved the Rueben dog & house made chips. Make sure you also save room for a donut "dessert". 
Perhaps not the most diet friendly place to eat, but worth the splurge.

Pleasantly surprising! Amazing, exquisite and out of worldly Sushi, perhaps one of the best I have tried so far. Stay away from the rolls and trust the Sushi master with the 10 piece special if you want the real deal. Otherwise, definitely try the Mexican roll (something different with a kick), the Box ( even though you have to have a PhD in chopstick handling to pick them up) and salmon Del roll. Try the Plum wine in the end if you have never had it before (remember it's quite sweet) but definitely start with Nigori or Senju if you are into them. The place is small and is in a modest neighborhood but definitely worth the drive to get to!
Donuts and coffee were delish! Everything else on the menu looked amazing, definitely going back to try more. Customer service was awesome to!

***** IF YOU'RE A LOCAL OR JUST VISITING YOU NEED TO TRY THIS BURGER*****

This is the best burger in the Vandy/Belmont area. let's start with how the top donut bun is delivered upside down so you don't have to worry about sticky fingers, innovative. The patty is seasoned and cooked PERFECTLY. The cheese is melted and the egg, either over easy or scrambled, sets the whole thing off. You can ride this horse on your own, but it would easily feed two people with a side. It was as if ever bite it was more and more enjoyable. The flavors blend together the longer it sits.

I came here on a Saturday evening with couple of friends, we all had a good time. The barista was friendly and helpful. I ordered a white hot chocolate and it was delicious. The layout is really nice, I love the big windows and the view.
If you are looking for a place were you can meet with friends, enjoy a cup of coffee and relax this is your place, but I'm talking about a day when the zoo is not in its max capacity, that I'm sure is another story.

My wife has been going to Orange Theory for a few years after hearing from our daughter who taught classes there what a great workout it is. She likes the workouts, however...she misplaced her heart rate monitor and purchased a new one for $125.  Before her next lesson she found her old monitor, but OTF would not let her return the new/unused one.  Find it hard to believe they could not reset a brand new watch, and not do a refund, or even charge a restocking fee.  Seems like such a money grab.

Great little sandwich café... the sandwiches are extremely tasty and the gooey butter dessert is a must try. Gets really busy at lunch time, so I recommend calling your order in or ordering online (especially if you're in a rush). Our group went here three times while visiting STL for training, every time we went, something in one of our orders was either messed up or forgotten... they were quick to remedy the situation... but I feel they get overwhelmed in the back and lose track of what orders they're working on.

After a phenomenal experience at Sun Sushi, definitely had to return after the first time! 

Volcano Roll - a classic California Roll baked with scallops, sriracha mayo, and eel sauce! Aside from the fact that it somehow came out of the oven cold, this is a roll I would highly recommend as it is one of the more experimental rolls out there that is really flavorful and pairs well with the silky scallops.

Yakiniku Ribs - this decently sized plate of short ribs grilled to tenderness with your traditional Japanese flavors. Not unusual for short ribs, but they were a bit hard to eat, but they tasted really good and was well seasoned and well cooked!

Salmon Skin Salad - interesting premise that I wanted to try but found it rather one dimensional with salmon skin + bonito flakes + a salad dressing that contributed similar flavors. I think some bold vibrancy in heat, acidity, or natural sweetness could help here.

Tempura Appetizer - also tried the tempura as well that I wanted to squeeze in. The tempura was battered just right and not overcooked, notably the broccoli which is the hardest to get right.

Spider Roll - As I've stated previously, soft shell crab tempura is an excellent combo to have. This roll combines this well with some Japanese pickles. The big thing I would change though is to add a generous drizzle of eel sauce and sriracha mayo as tempura is very dry by itself and needs something to sauce it up.

Overall, really good food, especially sushi, and phoenomenal service to go with the whole experience, I think Sun Sushi really provides a great value to our community, and would recommend everyone to try it if they haven't already.

You will definitely want to visit The Donut + Dog. This is an exceptional donut. Amazing cappuccino. And fantastic customer service. Wow. I'm impressed. 
Who I think was the owner explained all the donuts and let me know that they rotate flavors and offerings. They also sell out- so come early! Trust me when I say this is a donut worth having. It takes two days just to make the dough. 
The coffee- wow. Not only was the owner bragging on his barista but the barista delivered. I've never seen a cappuccino so beautiful, I didn't even know it existed. All the coffee is organic, fair trade, local, etc. 
The owner and the barista came and checked on me several times during my stay. There was quite a bit of foot traffic in here this morning and they still made it a point to check on me. I have no bad things to say! 
The music was on point and there was plenty of seating in the cozy house like atmosphere. The only thing is the menu is somewhat hard to understand/see. But who needs a menu when the owner can recommend and walk you through the options! 
Yes I definitely left with a sugar high but I look forward to coming back and trying more!
Amazing sushi! The rainbow roll was phenomenal, ended up ordering two. Also amazing service. All around great experience. Best sushi in SB

This place is a local secret :) Whenever the suhsi cravings kick in this is our first choice. This last time I've ordered the spicy tuna on crispy rice and six step salmon dinner. Overall great quality and delicious!

There is absolutely nothing better than treating yourself to great Chinese takeout after a long week, and their number is in my phone contacts! They even have a dandy way you can order online, so you can order takeout from your Smartphone from the East side, and by the time you drive there its ready. PERFECT! Their soups are classic and delicious, and I have never had a bad experience there. Sitting down dining is always a hoot, the older ladies there are sweet and funny and always attentive. I tip well every time, no matter whether its dine-in or take out. You may even luck out with the occasional free eggroll if they're in a great mood!

Brian just left my house.....I'm happy!  Thats good....lol

There arent many of these places around to do what they do but this place was the only place that had a good review.  I took the chance and I'm glad I did.  The lady that answered the phone was very nice and not too chatty...scheduled me in and was very pleasant in general.  They were scheduled today for 1:30.  They were an hour late BUT.....I can handle people being late as long as there is communication!  Not only did she call be BEFORE they were late to make sure I wouldn't need to reschedule but Brian (the tech) also call later on to verify that the timing was still good!  He was eager to answer all of my questions and they even came in UNDER the estimate.  I will definitely use these people again!  Thanks!

Chrissy made me look 10 years younger ,when she turned my short hair into a Barbie doll,chic, style to past my shoulder blades. Of course I got a lot of compliments, and my husband loves long hair.  I looked fab! She is a master at this stuff. She educated me, and I loved the feel of human hair. I kept extensions in for over a year,and at my wedding looked amazing.Thanks to a girl that knows whats she's doing, I would definitely recommend this girl to anyone .Her Salon is in a quiet area,no problem with parking.

Usually pretty slow but I would definitely be able to say that I have NEVER enjoyed their HASH BROWNS at this location... ok ok maybe once out of 100. 
All in all it's an average BK I guess but the HASH BROWNS need to be like every other BK on the planet...
Pretty good. The staff was good and friendly. They brought our food to us.  Plus, classical music was playing, giving the mood a much needed upgrade than mcdonalds or other fast food joints.

I've finally found my salon in st Louis after many failed attempts at other "top" salons..the minute I walked in the salon,it looked clean and beautiful and I was greeted at the front. Rachel was my stylist and did an amazing job fixing my previous cut and color, and left the salon feeling great ! She was professional,sweet and very attentive! Can't wait to go back !

Best Chinese restaurant in Nashville period!

My favorite is the spicy braised tofu and scallion pancakes for an appetizer. I have yet to have any meal here that was not amazingly good!

The portions are generally large enough that there is enough to take home for another meal later.

The staff is extremely helpful and attentive and the food usually arrives very quickly.

Highly recommended!

Update: I contacted John Mark after my conversation with Mary Elizabeth.  He let me know at that time that he had already sent the tile Next Day and apologized for not informing me beforehand.  However, the rude and unprofessional behavior exhibited by the owner is what turned me off and upset me- not the fact that the gentleman were unavailable, as she is trying to lead reviewers to believe in her response.

Extremely friendly staff! I placed an order to go, and they made me feel right at home, offering me complementary hot tea with pleasant smiles. The chicken lo mein was pretty good! This is my first time, but it will definitely not be my last!

It was alright. I ordered steamed dumplings, chicken fried rice, and egg rolls with a boba tea. I have nothing to really complain about, per se, but nothing to really rave about either. It was just... average.

Even though I didn't really order anything too adventurous, I was still surprised by how bland the fried rice and the dumplings were. I pretty much had to drown everything in sweet & sour and soy sauce. The bubble tea was delicious, but you can't really mess something like that up.

Overall, I probably won't go out of my way to go here again like I did this time around.

Very delicious and affordable white pizza, incredible cannoli, tiramisu, and baklava. The delivery driver had to wait like ten minutes before I opened my door but he was still very friendly, patient and kind about it. Very nice business, I also don't get why it only has two stars.

Having eaten here a few times, I am still undecided where Checkers falls in the world of fast food.  For chicken, no one can rival Chik-fil-a.  For burgers, on the east coast it is 5 guys and on the west coast it is in-n-out.  Checkers does a little bit of each.  All of their items are generally good, although few of their items have any healthy qualities.  Their menu variety and being open on Sunday makes it a great option if you have different preferences in your family.
Excellent service. Owner was very nice. Food was fresh. Similar to New York style pizza. The kitchen is impressively clean. Plus, Cold beer, you can't go wrong! Would definitely return.

5 star Chinese by Nashville standards. They have some hard to find items, like XLB (Xiaolongbao) soup dumplings! These cannot be found elsewhere in Nashville to my knowledge. I have chased soup dumplings in every major city from DC to NYC to the Bay Area. These were certainly not the best I have ever had, but they passed the test of not having an overly thick bun.

Sauteed pea leaves were really good, my favorite vegetable and well done here. Peking duck was good. Taiwanese braised pork (pork belly) was well cooked but a little under-seasoned for my liking. They have authentic dishes mixed in, like pork ear app. I liked how they served their spicy tofu dish in a boiling pot to keep it hot, and it was definitely good.

The owner sat down at our table after dinner and chatted us up. They were very friendly overall, service was prompt, and I really have no complaints. We will be back for sure, too bad this place is not closer to my office.

My Ground Zero joint. Owner Mike is very cool, often buying a round for everyone. I'm sure he counts heads first. They have a fairly dependable crew of regulars depending on who's working. Also having 4 8ft pool tables several pool leagues compete here. Another bonus is its location- 3 blocks from the airport which makes it a great option to the overpriced airport bars. They only have 8 beers on tap, but surprisingly each one represents its niche in the brew spectrum. Their food menu is very good, the burgers are truly stand-out. The bartenders, I can't forget the bartenders - Angela, Nikki, both are top-notch in looks and skill. Justin is new, and very attentive, AND is a hardcore movie dude.

Best florist in St. Louis. Chuck helped me pick out amazing flowers for my wedding. He was so kind and helpful and the prices are amazing. I highly recommend and will never go anywhere else for flowers!!
The hostess was very friendly but my dish wasn't impressive. For Nashville, it's not bad.

Sneakers #4 next to Denny's is the most awesome Bar to go through everyday the best bartender is Angela and the cook its named Brad he is awesome with  the most love and care for his food and it shows. But the bartender is Angela people come from miles around to try the Long Island iced tea or the best Bloody Mary all around

I was in town for work and this place was just slid under my door at the hotel so it was easy. I ordered a veggie calzone with a side of blue cheese. It came covered with olives which I hate and we're not on the menu description. It was also giant and the white sauce was leaking all over the place with a soggy bottom. No side of blue cheese. The mozzarella sticks had a funny taste to them as well. Would not recommend this

I've had better meals at your local "Chinese" food court spot. I won't go back Ever! Don't let these reviews about how good it is fool you. This was less than middle of the mall asian Americanized food at best. I give them two stars for great fast service. This is not even close to authentic Chinese cuisine. Corner Asian in Brentwood bears this spot hands down all day everyday.

In town for the night and ordered some delivery to the hotel. Food was delivered in less than 45 minutes. My wife had the stuffed shells which she said were very good. I had a Greek salad which was also very good but it had something in it that I couldn't figure out what it was. I told my wife it was almost like potato salad.   I finally had to look at the menu to find out what I was eating. I was right, it was potato salad. What a surprise. I have eaten a lot of Greek salads but have never had one with potato salad, however it was very good

With a generic name of Chinatown Restaurant, how could I not resist? Heck, even if they had named themselves Chinese Restaurant, I would still try it out.

Standard disclaimer: I love Americanized Chinese food, which I consider a separate cuisine than authentic Chinese.

And this place was delicious.

The decor was interesting. I think it was vinyl that covered the tables. Back home, my friends who were ABC (American-Born Chinese) told me the best Chinese food were always in hole-in-the-walls, where there was almost no decor. Places where the bus boys would pour hot tea on the glass tops covering the tables to loosen up any food stains. Here at Chinatown Restaurant, they actually decorated the place. Looked nice.

There were booths and tables.

I was given a free appetizer of fried wonton skins. I don't remember if that was plum sauce that accompanied that, but the yellow stuff was definitely hot Chinese mustard.

The oolong tea was soothing. And didn't taste strong by the end of my meal. It wasn't the type of tea where bits of leaves would fall into your cup. Perhaps it was tea from bags -- the bag didn't come with the pot.

Had my go-to standard of sweet and sour pork. They offered the sauce on the side, which was a nice touch. The sauce wasn't heavy on the sweet or the sour. Made me realize that I can cut back on both without sacrificing flavor. 

I loved the fact that they offer some dishes as sides: I had the green beans with black bean sauce, and it was a perfect amount. 

I came here early in the evening, and it was filling up with families with kids. I overheard a woman who was telling her young child that the [?] were as good as those from the Chinese restaurants back home in New York. 

The place was pricy for me, but given its location, I was willing to let that go.

Staff was so friendly. Even though I could tell she spoke Cantonese, I told her in my piddling Mandarin that I was not Chinese (because I get asked that a lot, and she asked me if I was).

A definite place to treat myself to good Chinese food.

Fireside Camp Supply is exactly that - a wonderful camping boutique that has the feeling of being fireside. The store is incredibly inviting, the staff is attentive to questions but isn't overly aggressive or annoying, and their products in stock are perfect for every type of camper - from the weekend warrior all the way to the experienced backpacker, they have everything you will need!

Highly recommended, stop by if you have a chance!

Have I done it?

Have I found good Chinese food in Nashville!? 

Well,  not completely but I'll take what I can get. 

I will say their bubble milk teas are SPOT ON. Limited in flavors but not taste. They even have a Quickly poster on the outside (which is a very well known franchised bubble tea shop). HIGHLY recommend the Royal milk bubble tea.  Tapioca was nice and soft.  Could use some pre-sweetening to make it ABSOLUTLEY perfect. Both the Peach Blossom and Passion Fruit teas are strong in tea flavor which I love. Definitely get it iced because they do make it very sweet here. 

Everything I've tried here has been A-OK.  The eggplant with pork entree is ABSOLUTLEY delicious. OMG. So savory and the eggplant is definitely the star here. I've also gotten the Szechuan chicken here for lunch expecting a spicy entree but it was not spicy at all with much milder flavors than expected.  Still good and tasted fresh.  A lunch entree was enough for 2 meals for me so portion size was great.  They also didn't charge more for fried rice,  which was actually dry but still edible. The eggroll wasn't your typical frozen variety and tasted like it was made in house. Definitely looked like something my grandma would make.

I've only ever ordered to-go here and the girls who work here have always been super friendly. Would really recommend trying this place out if you're in the mood for bubble tea and some decent Chinese food!

I wasn't impressed by the iceberg lettuce, as another reviewer commented on as well. The food was barely warm upon delivery and very stale, as if it had been left out for hours. Very odd. I'm giving one extra star for the delivery service but will not eat here again.

really enjoyed chinatown!  we've been searching for a good chinese place for years and we have found our new favorite.  the food was good and very reasonably priced...but the service was fantastic.  we will definitely be back...chinatown is highly recommended

Had some time to kill so my husband and I wanted to stop in for a bite, thinking it would be like Bullies. Nope.... Not the same. We got  2 feet in and couldn't get past the old booze and smoke smell. We don't smoke and thought there had to be a separate area for smoking around food these days? 
We left. Sorry, just couldn't get past how bad the smoke smell was and I couldn't fathom eating there or coming out of there smelling like smoke.
Joe is a fantastic agent! He's always helpful and a pleasure to work with. Keep up the great work!

3-16-18 time 2:00PM
Drive thru - whopper & small fries......It was EXCELLENT and lightly salted.  This is a winner 
Junior whopper & small fries.....Excellent 
Keep up the high quality......we love it

Former Steak n Shake customer. Good not as good as BurgerKing. 
McDonald has low quality in some of their product line.  Burger King is a winner hands down
Solid chinese food whenever needed.
This place is awesome. Free delivery, and overstuffed super fresh gyros. Their wings are good and filling as well, with a wide variety of favors.
GREAT SERVICE! Very friendly, quick and never had to ask for a refill. The orange chicken was great! The sweet sauce w the fried noodles was Awesome!

Good food WHEN IT'S CORRECT. I've been there a couple times within 6 months and they've NEVER gotten my food right. The first time I had a big order and they forgot someone's entire meal. The second I specifically asked for things not to be on my sandwich and they were on it, so I wasn't able to eat the food. Etc.
Mediocre food and terrible service. Really terrible. Do not waste your time or money.

This is definitely an interesting looking place with its duel drive thru and mini-dining area. It also has walk-up service as well.  It is a good fit for the location.

Ordered the Champ (no cheese), fries, and soda.  For a drive-thru the service was efficient,  prompt, and better than expected.  I guess it is nice when you get acknowledged and treated as a person not a cog in the process. They were definitely friendly. The food met expectations and was good. I enjoyed the spicy fries.
This place has good food and lots of pool tables. Down side they some how allow smoking while serving food. Not sure how they can do that legally, but oh well.

Mine was very much a 4 star dish as I had the crispy squid with beans. Very flavorful. My husband had the House Tofu. He was said it was OK to pretty good. He'll  try something else next time. The service was good to above average. Overall rating will be a 4 and we look forward to our next visit.

My family and I ordered the margarita pizza, mozzarella sticks, and fries. We were inclined to order in the first place because the menu was in between our door at the Sheridan suite. Well convienence was not our savior this time. The pizza took a little over an hour and it was cold, not warm what so ever. I'm a college student and honestly i was just trying to max on some greasy food with out much judgement and this was a huge dissapointment. I've never even bothered to write a review before, so ya the food was that embarrassing.. just don't do it

Would be unfair to compare them to Chinatown restaurants in New York or Boston, but I'm just happy they're here in Nashville. 

Their beef noodle soup does satisfy that occasional hankering for Taiwanese comfort food. (The xiao long bao however doesn't really do it)

The best Chinese food in Nashville! Granted, that's not saying very much, but here you can get both the Americanized Chinese (typically greasy) stuff as well as some more authentic dishes. In fact, this is probably one of the few places in middle Tennessee - Golden Coast buffet on West End on weekends is the other that comes to mind, and this place is superior in both food and decor.

In terms of vegetarian dishes, snow pea tips are tender and well-sauteed. A wonderful light yet flavorful green vegetable dish!  Sizzling tofu platter is also a good choice, as is the eggplant, and there is the usual vegetable lo mein, etc etc. They also offer bubble tea, but of course it's the powdered kind, and nowhere as close as good as the food.

The booths are well-upholstered and the place is nicely decorated, making it on par with quality mid-tier sit-down restaurants. On weekends, it can be quite busy! Parking is in the shopping center parking lot, or take the # 2, #7, or # 21 MTA bus.

I like the variety of the Pizza Famiglia menu. I like that they seem to double and triple check their delivery and to go orders. Getting home with the wrong food is so disappointing. They have long hours so they can hook you up with noms late into the night. They have sandwiches and options besides pizza, which is what I always get because I don't eat cheese. Portion sizes are great and prices are fair. Delivery is quick.


My hubby is not impressed with the pizza. He eats it, but he says it's typical stuff, nothing special. I've never had their pizza but it looks OK.

Nashville is seriously lacking quality Chinese take-out. Not that you really expect much in Chinese take-out, but you at least want to have some solid options. 

Chinatown in Green Hills is the closest I have found in town so far. Not only can you pick up for take-out, you can dine-in. I have done both and have had a good experience either way.

The service is....funny. The ladies working the tables are great. They always keep me laughing. 

So the service is good, but what about the food? The food is surprisingly great. I have had the sesame chicken, general tso's, beef + broccoli, etc and everything has been delicious. Plus, the portions are heaping! My girlfriend and I always have a ton of leftovers, but thats the point of Chinese food right?

less than average, chinese-american food.  ordered the veggie lo mein which barely had any vegetables...maybe 3 pieces of broccoli and 2 baby corn pieces.  a mess of a dish.  mu shu pork was forgettable...pancakes were dry causing them the break when you tried to fold them and the pork meat was extremely dry and hard.  the fried rice is a pathetic example of what fried rice should be.  the one shining light of the entire experience was the hot sour soup.  very hot and sour..perfect for a cold/rainy day.  

Is there any decent chinese food in Nashville?!
Service and environment is great here. But the food is better than anyone else in town except for the corner Asian cafe on nolensville rd and concord. Dish size is too small.

Winn Dixie took over the Sweet Bay operations at this site.  The changes were noticeable in a Winn Dixie way.  Buy one get one free, and more 10 for $10 items going on.  The Shell gas deal helps out.  I usually get one to two tankfuls a months.  One time I went, I had $1.20 off the Shell price.  Its good for up to 20 gallons, so I would wait until you're gas tank is almost empty.
Back to the store.  The aisles are clean.  The choices are plenty.  I like their produce area  over on the right.  Their pharmacy is over on the left with the dairy products right behind it.  Their specials on chicken are great.  The service at the counters have always been just right to accommodate the number of customers.  I usually get through the store with about $70 in purchases and about $15-$20 in savings.

Beautiful showroom and great selection. I needed tiles for a quick turnaround project, and Mission Stone & Tile made it happen; they got in a product in just five business days that other companies told me would take six weeks.

I also really loved all the girls who worked there (particularly Suzanne, who was the associate who helped me). They were very friendly and helpful and communicative until my order came in.

Also, while I admit that I didn't do a whole lot of cost research beforehand--I went to Mission after half a dozen friends on my Facebook page recommended them for our home restoration project--their prices seem really reasonable.

I love it in here, the location is great and the inside of the building is beautiful and always kept clean, the waiting room is nice and quiet and peaceful and the suites are all beautifully decorated inside

Got delivery through GrubHub and I think the food was pretty good. I got 20 wings and my girlfriend got eggplant parmigiana. She said hers was a little too mushy for her but the wings were good. Definitely a good go to order at almost midnight on a Saturday.

Service was top notch with Alan. Got all our questioned answered. We couldn't be happier with our i8. Won't go back to traditional mattresses because of the comfort and adjustability. Would have liked encasement option for husband's allergies. Never-the-less, the mattress cover they sell is fabulously sumptuous. Customers for life.

I have recently rediscovered the joys of camping. However I don't want to acquire all the equipment. These peeps have everything I need. They are extremely helpful, tips on what I might need, places to camp and the best spots in the campsite. Their equipment is really nice, clean, and at very reasonable rental prices. Ya gotta check them out. We need them in philly!
Thanks fireside.
So high tech and competent, with great ideas and caring staff, everything is first class and gorgeous. The experience and results are both great.

This isn't the tyical Americanized Chinese takeout food you usually find around here. Chinatown Restaurant is for people who are looking for- and appreciate- traditionally cooked Chinese food. Don't go here looking for Americanized dishes like general tso and orange chicken or else you'll miss out on a wonderful opportunity to try excellent Chinese dishes.

We went on a busy Saturday night, but I was impressed how helpful and polite the staff was! You didn't get that feeling that they were completely overwhelmed. The restaurant was run very smoothly. 

The food was absolutely delicious. I tried a little bit of everything my group got, and it was hard to pick a favorite because everything was so tasty! The roasted duck was delicous, and it seemed like everyone was really impressed with an eggplant dish we had. The tofu dishes were excellent. Even if you think you don't like tofu, try it here! Same with the duck! 

This is a place for trying new things and experiencing different food.Take a look at the menu and do some research before you come so you don't get so overwhelmed that you just order the same old Lo Mein, orange chicken, etc. Don't be afraid to try something authentic!

Also...BUBBLE TEA! I was so happy to have bubble tea again! If you have never tried it, definitely give it a try!

Mission Stone and Tile makes a claim on their website they cannot honor. They do not ship in 3 days or less. No way.
I've now placed two orders of tile with MS and T. These are not large orders - though they claim they are - for tile for two regular-sized bathrooms. The order has been held up 6 days so far because they said their warehouse was busy. Customer service is also dismissive when I question them about their claim. Though they charged my credit card immediately, I'm still waiting to get any kind of confirmation on the ship date for my order. By the way, I placed another order with a competitor - Glass Tile and Mosaic  - and this order came in 3 days. No delay, no excuses. And the tile arrived in good shape. Don't take the M S and T claim at face value - it ain't true.
Pretty good. The staff is always friendly and my order has always been right. Much friendlier and fresher than the nasty McDonalds up the road. I like the breakfast also.

I asked for a recommendation from the waitress: shrimp in lobster sauce.  I would never have picked it for myself, but it was SO GOOD!!! The menu was huge and seemed like it had a little bit for everyone. I also ordered the crystal shrimp dumplings - addicting but it did take 15 minutes...Still amazing flavors. My waitress had other tables but I honestly felt like she never left my table and was prompt with the order and refills on my drink. 

Whenever I am in town in Nashville I will always go back here. They were so good. Maybe I'll ask for a different recommendation! Yum yum!

My favorite local pizzeria hands down. Food always great and service is so reliable. All the employees are so kind and they really helped us out by delivering during hurricane Irma when no one else was. Would definitely recommend.
Just had Joe out to clean our chimney ...great job, very helpful and professional ...would definitely recommend
First rate equipment for rent and sale and on point advice for novice hikers like me. I cannot recommend this place enough!

I recently hired Jennifer to prepare a cooking party for my sister's low key bachelorette party. We made homemade gnocchi with pomodoro sauce and roasted chicken thighs. The food was excellent, and Jennifer was completely lovely, flexible, and sweet as could be. I also really appreciate her preference for organic, clean, fresh ingredients. In the end, it probably cost about the same as a nice meal out and was way more fun and intimate. 

I would absolutely do this again with Jennifer. So much fun!
Yes I know they are very busy on the holidays any other day you will get the sweetest waitresses and the yummiest food.

How does that saying go..."If you build it, they will come."  Why doesn't that apply to Chinese food?  Why does chinese food in Nashville have to be Amereicanized?  Is the Nashville palate that poor that they can't appreciate good, solid chinese food that is prepared with fresh vegetables (and plenty of it) and lots of flavor?
I really just don't get it.  Chinatown restaurant was disappointing.  More so in the fact that when we asked the owner what their best dish was, he seemed a bit bashful and replied apologetically, "Well, all the dishes are Americanized..." yes, sir.  Say no more.  What he's basically saying is, there is really nothing on this menu that will suit your palettes (because we are down home Chinese!)  That being said, I must say that this restaurant was mostly disappointing because their food was sub par.  When the fried rice was delivered, I was about to tell the waiter "Oh, I asked for fried rice, not brown rice" since that is what it looked like, but then she put the dish down and lo and behold there was ONE piece of egg I saw mixed in there.  I don't care what chinese restaurant you go to, the fried rice is usually made with white rice stir fried with scrambled eggs and usually a mixture of peas and carrots, sometimes green onions. Not here at Chinatown.  Just rice and the minimal amount of egg necessary to pass.  could't even really tell if it was real egg.
We then had the mu shu pork, some veggie lo mein and a chicken and broccoli.  Mediocre at best.  But the veggie lo mein - again.  Where are the vegetables?  This lo mein came with a couple pieces of broccoli (uncommon for lo mein which usually is served with a plethora of onions, cabbage, carrots, snow peas), two pieces of baby corn (always from a can) and a couple slivers of napa cabbage.  I mean, come ON folks. I know you are serving a mostly American clientele (and judging from the reviews below, with not very discerning palettes), but still.  Quality really counts and if Chinatown were to up their vegetables and their presentation, more people would come!  It really would not take that much effort.
So sad....

my  husband got a great haircut here and will definitely be back. i've been trying to convert him from sports clips, so he had a teensy bit of sticker shock but agreed the service, ambiance and products used were worth it. very glad we have one near by!

First reason this gets five stars is: bubble tea. Need I say more? But more than that is the fact this is the closest to authentic you will get around here, is fresh, and super delicious. I recommend the Taiwanese pork belly, calamari, and ma po tofu--I dream about this dish!

I'm not really a fan of Chinese food, but this is probably the most decent & authentic in town. They recently had a remodel and menu change. The previous dish I used to get, black bean chicken, is about 15 times hotter than it was before. The wonton soup and rice was all the same, but both dishes at the table were super super hot. Next time I will ask them to hold the spice. I do not care for the spring rolls. Super fried and greasy.
I have a love for the fries, but the staff gives terrible service every time. Fries are usually cold, and I usually end up going inside for new ones.

Thought I'd give Checkers a try since they were down the street from where I was working today.
Big mistake.
First off, even though their were only 4 people in front of me it took 20 mins to get to the front of the line so the lady could take my order! Then another 5 mins for my food to appear. No ketchup or napkins in the bag either. So I had to ask. If there is anything that burns me up is spending between 6 and 10 bucks for basically a burger and small fries and they can't even freakin bother to put ketchup in the bag or napkins like at this joint. Unreal. 
The food?
Totally bland. The burger was like a kid's size with some kind of combination of tartar sauce with orange color in it. Didn't taste tangy or spicy or anything just MEH and the bun was mushy with tasteless cheese. The fries were a well done almost burned take on Jack in the Box curly fries but without the kick and were just plain overcooked and stale. The drink was even weak tasting. Got Sprite and it tasted like water with some sugar in it. When a place even waters down their soft drinks it's time to call them what they are -- a ripoff. 

Won't go to a "Checkers" again. That's for sure!

One of the hostess was not friendly towards us when we wanted to order lunch socials. She tried to up-sale us the regular order when we clearly told her we don't want to order lobster. The food was not as good as used to be. We will not be back

We love a great Chinese restaurant and think we have finally discovered our Nashville favorite! It's a small place, hidden in Greenbriar Village directly across from Green Hills. We went for a late lunch, which worked perfectly for us. It was not too crowded so we got great, attentive service. All meals come with complimentary fried wontons and dipping sauces, which I loved! We got the General Tso's Chicken and Szechuan Pork, both super fresh and tasty- a far cry from yucky mall Chinese food. Since we went early, we got the lunch prices, and ended up with a very inexpensive meal with generous portions. So glad we found this little gem and can't wait to return! On a side note, we took our very loud, active baby boy and they were very accommodating, very family friendly!
Best grocery store around! Great prices, clean, friendly.

Wow! I ordered a "designer's choice" arrangement from the Walter Knoll website for my sister in celebration of her new baby boy.   Within 30 minutes of placing my order, the designer called me and asked me a few questions about the occasion.  When the flowers arrived at the hospital (on time and with no fuss) they were GORGEOUS.  The designer used very nice blue and yellow flowers to make a large arrangement, and even supplemented the flowers with fun (but sophisticated-looking) blue glitter accents.  My sister sent me photos and I couldn't believe how fantastic the arrangement was.  I could not be happier, and feel like I got much more than my money's worth.  This is the second time I used WKF to deliver flowers to my very-picky sister, and each time she's absolutely loved them.  Great florist, I definitely recommend them if you're in the STL area, or need a great go-to florist for deliveries to loved ones living in the STL area (like me).

Called in a take out order for sesame chicken, fried rice and an egg roll. Food was ready in less than 10 minutes, and the lady at the front & phone was very courteous and friendly. 

The fried rice was garbage. The pieces of chicken were really small and hard. Little to no sauce. Finally, the egg roll was like the size of a stick of gum! 

Now, I could easily deal with all of this for a cheapo price like $4.99 plus tax or something, but this meal was $10 and change! Ridiculous. 

I will not be back.

positively the worst fast food experience i've ever had.  

i ordered in the drive-thru. after handing the cashier $8, she tells me that i only gave her $7.  so i looked around a bit to see if $1 had possibly dropped on the ground.  no sign of any money.  i asked her to check inside the restaurant.  all i got was attitude.  so i dug out the change needed to pay the remainder of my order.  i pulled away after getting my food to realize i was missing a drink.  i went inside to get it, went back out to the car; wrong drink.  had to go back inside to get what i had ordered myself (followed by the manager who probably thought i was stealing a soda).

i filled out their phone survey and gave them a second chance a few days later.  not much better.  Burger King sucks.  their food is crap.  their employees are hooligans.  they won't get another dime of mine.

I live right around the corner from this place, decided to try it after recieving a flyer at my apapartment. The have a huge menu...pizza, pasta dishes, wings, burgers, and a lot more. I always get the #9 special, two pasta dishes, two side salds, breadsticks, and a two liter soda for 16.99....awesome deal, and the food is amazing. The only major downside is the delivery service which I doubt ill use from now on bc although we live close, it always takes way longer than they say it will. But ill keep giving them my buisness bc the food is great and so are the prices.

Ordered dinner via Uber Eats tonight because I couldn't leave the house and I just got back from vacation so I have no food. I have no complaints about my delivery person. He was friendly and here more quickly than I expected.

I asked for no peppers on the salad (it was even written on the tag attached to the bag) but my salad had peppers on it. I was also given absolutely no cheese for the spaghetti. Who eats pasta with no parm? With the $4 tip I paid $28 for a small bowl of spaghetti marinara and a Greek salad and I didn't even get cheese for my pasta? Disappointed.

I've been here lots of times but always ended up eating the food before remembering to take pictures!  Probably because I know how good it is. 

Went again today and it was the normal experience. Great food. Great service. 

Was in the mood for a potato dish that I used to eat in China so I asked the server and she spoke to the chef and he made it for me off menu. It's that type of place. If they can do it they will. 

Also got the chicken and tofu in peppers (can't remember the name in the menu). The sweet pea leafs which is my fav veggie. The scallion pancake and then the mapo tofu. They make my mapo with Sichuan peppercorns which is the only way to eat it as it really spices it up. 

Ate everything and will be in a food coma for the next day or so but it is really worth it. It might not be Chengdu but this is as close to authentic Sichuan cuisine that you will find in Nashville. Yummy yummy.

This is a run of the mill Chinese food restaurant. I will say the restaurant itself is very well kept and clean and the staff are extremely friendly but the food itself is average. I ordered the Orange Chicken with fried rice and my girlfriend ordered the General Tso's Chicken with Lo Mein. The Lo Mein was very good I must say but the fried rice was on the bland side. Both main meals were good but the funny thing was both the Orange Chicken as well as the General Tso's tasted and looked identical. Overall the food was ok but I wouldn't recommend going here if you're looking for GREAT Chinese food.

What a wonderful new small business! This lady has only been around for 4 months or so, but she shows promise and could become a staple in the neighborhood.  I wandered in looking for a gift for my outdoorsy fella, and found the perfect things! I got some great suggestions, and they have some fantastic items. This is not your standard big box REI experience. It's a lot of small purveyors and one-of-a-kind items, like the handmade flask I bought. Also, every First Friday they do a bonfire with s'mores and it's BYO in the backyard. Can you get better than that? Probably not.

Mission tile is your place as it is a pretty showroom and the sales people are great. The sweet sales lady even offered popsicles to my children as they were patiently waiting. Now if you calculated the wrong number of tiles or you need to make a return then you have a HUGE PROBLEM as the owner is not sympathetic and her attempts to apologize are weak. The owner condescendingly speaks in front of all her staff to the customer who has a reasonable request for a return. It now explains why her staff is afraid to cross her. I left unsatisfied and left with tile I cannot use. This is disheartening that this business owner treats her unsatisfied customers so badly. Good luck staying in business if this is how she continues to run her company.
I hope this was helpful.

I have not been to this location since it was Harry's a friend of mine suggested we stop there and I was apprehensive at first but walking in the atmosphere was good they had great drink specials for happy hour and the wings were awesome

So Nashville doesn't exactly have a plethora of good Chinese food. Having lived in Houston and New York City, I find the quality of Chinese food in Nashville pretty dismal. It says a lot that Chinatown is my go to Chinese good spot (for take-out) in Nashville. It's fine, and it's my go to. That's not ideal! 

But Chinatown really is A-OK. Big menu. So you're likely to find something you like. They've got EVERYTHING on the menu. From American favorites like Kung Pao, Mongolian Beef or Chicken, Orange Chicken, Sweet and Sour, etc. to more unusual, specialized cuisine (black bean sauce, dishes with bitter melon, Ma Po tofu...). So, yeah, it's not great Chinese food. But in Nashville, I'll pass about ten places to go to this one. WAY better than some of their competition.

Awful greasy food. Look at my pics and see how they served my fries. Fries were just thrown in bag, and were so greasy, it leaked through the bag, into my car seat, and through the wrapper of my sandwich. Disgusted. I would go back and curse the guy out, but he's not worth my time. First and last time at this location. Pure garbage to serve your customers food like that. That manager should be ashamed of him/herself. Those employees represent YOU!

I would give this Burger King a half star if I could but I can't. I went there twice in two months and both times they got my order wrong. On my last and final visit I specifically asked for my Whopper with no sauce (dry), and cheese. I even avoided the drive thru so there would be no confusion. I went inside and at the time I was the only customer in line. Ten minutes later (seriously) my order is ready and by then there's a large line. (One customer even came inside yelling they got his drive thru order wrong). I go to my car and proceed to eat the whopper in the car. Bad idea. Ketchup and mustard are oozing out of the burger and onto my pants. The burger itself -the one that I patiently waited 10 minutes for- is cold and lifeless- not to mention the slice of cheese thrown on top of the burger has absolutely no chance of melting. They even forget the only veggie I requested. Pickles. I immediately take the meal back in and have a nice talk with the manager. The manager assures me that he is working with the recently hired cook and to give him time - he's learning. The manager then proceeds to replace my burger with a fresh burger and upsize my fries for my inconvenience. I go back out to my car. This time the burger is piping hot and sauce less. However, the pickles are missing again. On top of that, the new fries the manager gave me are stone cold. I have all these remaining Burger King coupons. I'll just have to find a different Burger King to use them at.
The haircut was rushed and there was no real attention to detail. For $30 I'd expect a little more time and effort put in.

I gave them another try after i heard that changed chef, it been a couple of years. I got a order to go....

Egg Rolls - Greasy!!!! Inside was liquid grease!!!

Fried Dumplings - Definitely frozen and not good frozen. Did not put any sauce in my bag and did not put in the chilli oil that i requested. So that made them more inedible. 

General Tao Chicken - more breading then meat!!! and the breading was too greasy. 

Really no Fortune cookie!!!! 

If you can not get your to go business right!!!! Stay out of the to go business. 

Wont be back.... why can some one not open a decent Chinese Restaurant?????????
Even though we are not true connoisseurs of Asian cuisine, my family and I enjoy Chinatown and make it a point to go out of our way to eat here. Great food and great service!

Food was only okay, and the order took way too long to be delivered. I also got overcharged, which really bums me out.

I ordered chicken wings (butter garlic) and a sausage calzone. The wings were crispy, but didn't have a lot of flavor. I should've ordered something saucier or with more flavor because I couldn't even taste the garlic. The calzone was very mediocre, but it was sizeable and could feed two.

I got a flier under my hotel door, and it said fast delivery, but it took an hour to get to me. While the delivery guy Ryan was nice, I was overcharged for my order. Based on the menu prices, my order should have been $15, and even with tax it should've been only around $16. However, I was charged over $19. The delivery guy said he couldn't do anything about it and for me to call to complain. I tried calling 5 times that night but couldn't even connect, so I gave up. 

If someone from the restaurant reads this, I would love to have some followup.

For the negative reviews (I didn't read all of them) you have to understand the business, from my knowledge less than 5 people operate this place and so whenever they do delivers there is probably a maximum of two or three cars out at a time if that, with the remaining one or two people working at the shop.

The food I have received from this place has been awesome since my college days in 2011, I used to order with my roommate and he would never tip the delivery driver, I think they dodged his calls or didn't want to deliver anymore lol. However that is when my understanding of the place developed more, going to their shop and seeing that they really can't make a feasible living traveling all over Tampa area with their own personal vehicles.

The Wings are awesome, the hot garlic is my favorite, they are a decent size and I always have a ton of sauce almost too much. Today I'm thinking about trying the shrimp ever since the last time I came I have been thinking about them and so I want to give them a shot, the meal deals are excellent for college goers or thrifty shoppers in general. I don't think I've ever had the pizza, I eat enough pizza, but I bet it would be good. If you are thinking about eating in the ambiance is pretty cool, I never have been to New York but from Movies and TV shows it would seem like one of those chill-out diner/pubs however even smaller. 

Pizza famiglia now serves alcohol in store and from what I see they are moving on up and for such a small style shop I think it is awesome, give credit when credit is due.

It doesn't taste bad and it doesn't taste good. It actually taste like nothing. No love showed up in any of the dishes we ordered. The veg egg roll is half the size then the average and small the amount of filling had no flavor. The hot mustard packet was the best part. Beef and broccoli  zero flavor. Not beef not broccoli not delicious "brown" sauce. I just hope the cooks see this review and start tasting there food. Maybe go out to eat and see what others have to offer. Give it a try maybe it was a bad night.
One of the places open late in my area. And pretty damn good. Not sure why it only has two stars.

In Nashville for the weekend and found this little spot - my sister and I both lived in Asia (Taiwan and Singapore) for years, and found this a very acceptable walk down memory lane! Xiao long bao (small steamed buns) were good,  and Taiwanese Salted Crispy Chicken took me back to the streets of Kaohsiung. Service was solicitous and friendly; they were busy, but got our food quickly and hot. Prices are average ($8.95 for steamed buns, $11/plate for entrees) but portion sizes are generous. Rice was the only disappointment, a surprise at a Chinese restaurant, but we had so much food we didn't miss it. Orange slices for dessert were a treat!

I do not have high expectations from Chinese food in Nashville.  With absolutely no disrespect meant to the town which I visit frequently and like very much, there just not a large enough selection for me to expect excellence.  

I ate at Chinatown tonight, and found it very enjoyable.  My

We stopped here after shopping at the mall and Parnassus Books.  The atmosphere was very pleasant and comfortable.  The employees were all welcoming, warm, and helpful.  The food was amazing!  I had the pan fried dumplings and they were the best I had ever had.  I also had the General Tso's Chicken which was also great.  The portions were large and everything tasted fresh.  Finally the prices were slightly higher than normal Chinese restaurants but this was a much better experience in a nicer part of town so it was definitely worth it.
Updated to note that I did receive a refund a couple of weeks later for the missing samples.

I have been eating at Chinatown approximately once a week for at least the last 7 years. It is by far the best Chinese food in Nashville. The hot and sour soup is excellent- I get it as soon as I arrive home from a business trip as comfort food. The garlic sauce chicken, Kung pao and chicken in cilantro are also winners. Service is great and the owners are incredibly sweet.

A year ago I ordered from here and was blown away by the quality and service. Since then I've gone back three times, each time hoping for that same experience. I usually order either General Tso's or Sesame Chicken (basic americanized dishes, I know). A couple little things before I address the food- I always order to-go and haven't been given utensils or napkins since my first visit. It's not a big deal of course, but the little things go a long way.

The last three times I've ordered, the meat has either been such low quality that it's tough to eat or so deeply fried and such small pieces of chicken that there's almost no real food. 

I've gone out of my way to give this place more chances time and time again and I would love to have a reliable Chinese restaurant in Nashville, but I'm left feeling like this is not it. Unfortunately, I don't know of any great alternative. Their friendly staff and my first experience are the only thing salvaging a two star rating.

Fireside Camp Supply was recommended to me word-of-mouth as the go-to spot on South St. I heard it was a little camping goods store with a lot of local flare, but when I walked in I felt an intimate and immediate connection to what the place was all about.

The shop definitely exceeded all of my expectations. The design and decor is very reminiscent of all of the National Park visitor centers I stopped at while cross-country road-tripping. The entire store smells like firewood burning at a campfire; that smoldering, earthy scent that makes vagabonds seek solace and comfort in the mountains and valleys of our nation. The woman who owns and runs the store is this chilled-out, old soul who clearly has a strong passion for camping, hiking, and seeking out the more natural side of life, something that is greatly inspired throughout her shop. And the items she carries are unique, pragmatic, and can be your one-stop-shop for an upcoming camping trip.

Plus, it's totally important to represent and support your local shops and stores. You can obviously go to REI/etc. for your camping supplies, but what commercial retail place will invite you to a cookout and s'more night on their back patio? Fireside Camp Supply will. In fact, that's one thing her flier promotes. 

The owner wants you to feel welcome and wants you to be part of her awesome shop. Even though I just left with some Dr. Bronner's Castille Soap, I would absolutely go back to FCS to purchase cool flannels, better multi-purpose sleeping bags, and any smaller, camping-trip essentials.

Years ago this was the best Chinese restaurant in Nashville. They had authentic Chinese food. New ownership is horrible. Ordered wonton soup that was barely lukewarm. Egg rolls were of the quality you'd find in the freezer section at the grocery store. It seems that now they use poor quality cheap food. Don't recommend, you'll be disappointed.

Overall, a solid place for Chinese in Green Hills & very convenient if you work nearby.

Atmosphere: Clean, pretty quiet, & nicely decorated.

Service: Polite, friendly, attentive.

Food: Mixed. I've found a few great dishes that are my go-to (Mongolian beef is my favorite!) Some others have been very average (the lo mein is not that great). You get a lot for the price with the lunch specials & their egg flower soup and eggrolls are good.

Note: The last time I ordered online, it didn't work. The order went through successfully online, but when I arrived to pick up my food, the worker informed me that their online ordering wasn't working. I had to waste 10 min. of my lunch break while they made my food. **Always order by phone just to be safe!

Well, that was pretty ridiculous.  We are visiting Tampa from out of town and chose this pizza place because they are advertising in our hotel.  It is very close by - 7 mins away.  When we ordered, we were told that it would take 45 mins to arrive.  After we had waited for an hour, we called and were told that the driver was on his way.  30 mins after that (1.5 hrs after ordering), we called again.  They apologized and told us that they had actually made a mistake and the order was never put in.  Apparently, they only told us that the driver was "on his way" because they tell that to anyone that calls!  They promised that they would make the pizza and deliver it in 10 mins.  30 mins later (2 hrs after ordering) the pizza finally arrived.  It was missing one topping and it actually didn't taste that great. At least they had enough class to give it to us to free to make up for their mistake.

The first and only authentic Chinese restaurant I have encountered in Nashville so far.  I am Asian, raised and bred in Asian so I know what good authentic Chinese food is.  And they are it.

My husband ordered a whole fish, deep fried with their house sauce.  It is amazing.  So much so that I needed to steal a bite from his plate while he wasn't looking.  He is a generous guy who always shares his food with me but not this time.  That tells you how good that dish is.

I ordered a Tofu Clay pot good for this cold weather, also very delicious.

The thing that touched me the most about this restaurant is the hostess and the waiting staff.  They are nice, genuine, organized, attentive.  Makes me feel right at home.
This place is great!! It is clean and very good prices. The meat selection is always well stocked even during sales! Please keep this store open!!

Mission Stone and Tile has a beautiful selection of tile but their customer service is the absolute worst. All they care about is making money and could care less about the customer experience. Dealing with them has been one of the worst customer service experiences in my entire life. The other reviews are TRUE. *DO NOT* use them, you will regret it... I will NEVER go back there again after the experience we had. They are disorganized and when a problem comes up management is uncaring and extremely RUDE! Never again....
Mission tile has a beautiful showroom but has the worst customer service I've ever experienced in this industry.
You can't go wrong with the pizza here. It is by far some of the best in the area; and I have not had a bad slice yet. Only reason this place does not get five stars is the delivery time.
Ordered for delivery. Good food and hot. Flyer left under hotel door. Ordered steak calzone, fries, eggplant Parmesan and chocolate cake.

I love just walking around Mission Stone & Tile's showroom. If you are building a house, remodeling, or just sprucing up a bit a bathroom, kitchen, or really any room in your house, you have to check out the wonderful tiles here. In fact, it is more than just tile. There are beautiful collections of granites, limestone, glass, lovely slates perfect for an entry way, and even modern vanities and sinks. 

The super smart staff can help you design anything from a whole room to a simple counter top. Nothing is too big or too small for them. Everything in here is just elegant. There are understated muted colors for the conservative in decorating, to bold, modern materials for those wanting a contemporary look.

Make this your first stop on the list of things to do when renovating your home. You'll thank yourself!

Finally a company that does superior work, shows up as scheduled, cleans up after themselves and finishes on time!!  I cannot tell you how pleased my husband and I are with this company

We hired them to rebuild the chimney from the roof up.  Ron arrived at my home 3 days prior to the scheduled start of the job to MATCH the brick.  We have a multi colored brick home, in Avon, with colors of dusty rose, various shades of tan and brown.  After checking several brick chips we thought we found several close matches.   On Monday he arrives on time and began the tear down.  Once that was done he began to put a few bricks in place and realized that the color wasn't a good match.  He then began to search Indy for the correct color and texture.  4 hours later and a trip to Fishers he returned and with what we needed. Ron and his assistant began to work and returned the next day to finish.  Tuesday morning, as promised, they were back on the job and finished the brick work.  Keep in mind that the brick needs to sit for 30 days before a seal can be applied.
A couple days after the chimney was done, I get a call from their office for the balance of the payment.  I said that I once before I paid for a job in full---my wedding pictures---and the guy failed so show up at the wedding!  Therefore I was reluctant to pay the bill in full.  I was assured that they would be back as promised.

GUESS WHAT...THEY DID!!

So, if you need any type of chimney work done, call them and rest assured that they will do what they say and you wont be disappointed!

I had give up on Chinatown after it changed owners a few years ago. Recently, however, I've been back and very pleasantly surprised. Don't know if they got a new chef or what, but the flavor is back and I can't wait to go again. I've had the little steamed buns--more like dim sum dumplings, which were excellent. The pork with black bean sauce was fantastically spicy, and the lo mein was flavorful. The best review, though, is the number of Asian diners that now crowd the place.  You can't get a better recommendation than that. If you, too, thought the place was a washout  give it another try.

Great food! Great service! 

Especially for lunch. I always visit this place when I am in the mood for a delicious lunch and I am on that side of town. Soup, egg roll, the works! 

My absolute favorite is the chicken fried rice. I don't know what it is, but it is the best I've ever had! Ever!

I'd definitely suggest giving this a whirl if you are in Green Hills!

Growing up, my family ordered take-out... kind of a lot.  And one of our favorites (aside from the family-run pizza joint and KFC, of course), was the local Chinese restaurant that offered delicious thick lo mein, fluffy steamed rice, and the stuff plum sauce dreams are made of.

Chinatown Restaurant, thank you for bring it all back to me!  I love this hidden Green Hills treasure!  The staff is extremely pleasant and helpful, and the food was just as I remembered Chinese food used to be when I was a child - oh so good.

We got sesame chicken and general tso's, and a huge pot of green tea.  The portions were heaping, and they were equally generous with the steamed rice.  They even brought out their oobios tea for us to sample!  I was so full and happy by the time we got our check, but I was longing to try the moo shoo chicken with plum sauce, and the veggie lo mein!  That will definitely be next up on my list!

The owner came over to us and thanked us, which I thought was a really welcoming touch to the whole experience.  Another added touch was the extra fortune cookies they gave us for our to-go box, which by the way, were not the cheap-o brand - they were the original, real deal fortune cookies!  Yum!

O.K., let me start with: What Chinese food around here isn't at least somewhat Americanized? Americanized or not, Chinatown is a cut above the Chinese take-outs and buffets that litter our local landscape. 

Sit down Chinese restaurants (that aren't buffet) are a rarity around here, and it's nice to go out sometimes for a real Chinese meal. It does get crowded here, and when it does, there's a real atmosphere you don't expect from a tiny place in a strip mall. The food is also much better quality, and you can tell it's going to be as soon as you look at the menu. Chinatown offers steak and seafood dishes as well as brown rice. That's what impressed me: the brown rice. The only other Chinese place I know of with brown rice is P.F. Chang's. 

There's evidence of real cooking going on here, and I see more care going into their dishes than most of the other Chinese places I've eaten. My dish, which I asked for "spicy" came with a whole dried chili infused into it, which gave it a lovely, natural, not overdone flavor. The meat dishes have a healthy serving of vegetables, and not just the usual ones you associate with Chinese cooking. The broccoli was still green and fresh and my beef dish had fresh carrots, zucchini, and celery. 

I was truly impressed by everything I ate there, and I will be returning very soon with a troop of friends.

Formerly Harry's, a Chicagoesque reincarnation with deep dish pizza, formerly Harry's All-American, formerly Harry's Watering Hole (which had the freaky face masks of the Three Stooges on top of the big screen), this is now part of the Sneaker's local chain of smaller, working-class sports bars (as opposed to big Bully's and Sparky's).  Sneaker's in general has a more low-key ambiance without all the tables full of families and family things like arcade games and kid's meals and stuff.  I also find that bartenders at Sneaker's tend to be a lot friendlier than most any kind of bar.  Sneaker's brings their food menu thus eliminating all traces of the former Harry's.  For all you Chicago expats, if you missed Harry's you missed your last chance at Chicago food in Reno, except maybe that hotdog cart.  

Sneakers also finally eliminated all traces of the funky, oddball cartoon moose murals that used to decorate the old watering hole.  It is now painted in a somewhat aquatic theme of red and blue.  I don't know why I think red and blue is aquatic.  They also moved the entrance away from the bar which makes it fell somewhat more cozy.  They kept the four pool tables and will continue to host pool tournaments.  The Sneakers menu is pretty basic sports bar stuff with burgers, sandwiches, and wings.  Nothing special.  I'm not saying the basic sports bar menu is soporosely uninspired and oleaginously vapid, well, no, I am.  I'm not exactly asking for a hipsterification of the menu adding kale, quinoa, Korean tacos, and pork shoulder, but I don't know, I'm getting close to the age of the targeted demographic for sports bars and I'm just thinking, can we just try something new?  Do all middle-aged sports-loving dudes love chicken wings, onion rings, and burgers?  Really?  Really?  Ughhhhhhh.  But I really liked the bartender though.

I would love to give 5, as delivery was missing my salad and garlic bread. However, the manicotti with meatballs (added to order) was delicious!! Wings and cheese sticks were very good too!! I ordered from Alfonso's a couple months ago, what a disaster!! I have my new go to place now. Plus, their customer service was superb!!! Offered to bring my salad and breadsticks out asap :)) I will be back!!! Can't wait to try their pizza!!!

There are not enough words to describe how delicious this place is. I've never tasted a bad dish. And since the remodel, I feel like I'm getting fancy food in a fancy place at extremely reasonable prices. And the servers are the best!

Try the steam buns. Oh my! Never have I tasted something so delicious.

Their fried rice is AMAZING.  Hearty portions that are easy to make two meals.  This seems like the most authentic Chinese restaurant I've been to.  The service has always been fast and friendly.  Food comes out quickly and is always hot!  Highly recommend.
Very good.  Reasonably priced.  Everything you want when you want Chinese Food.  The owner Jack is awesome.

My husband and I ate here today. The food is always good, but the lunch special is no longer special - no soup and egg roll. The price is higher and the portion is smaller on a smaller plate.  There is more rice though!  $9.50 for Kung Pao and $10.95 for Mongolian Beef. Come on PF Changs.

It's Nashville, Nashville, Nashville....welcome!

Point is - context is key.  I think a lot of the reviewers on here are used to Americanized chinese food (it's what is mainly available here) and therefore graded accordingly.

Authentic  chinese food is not drowned in cheap stir-fry sweet/sour/salty sauce - the key lies in its balance of flavors without overwhelming the taste buds.  If one is used to eating salty food, the cuisine here will come across as bland.  So if Panda Express is your staple, I would not recommend this place to you.

Chinatown is a mix of both - authentic and americanized.  For the geographic area, they are about as authentic as it gets without scaring the majority of diners away who may or may not have tried authentic chinese food before. 

Now onto the food - good mix of meat vs. vegetarian dishes, generous portion sizes.

So for the Nashville area, it is pretty good.  But graded on my collective experience of Chinese dining - it is A-OK.    Every time the craving hits, this is my go to place. For now.

As a native San Franciscan/Californian, I've lived in Nashville for little over a year and the ONE ethnic food that was lacking authenticity was Chinese food. Yes, I know there are plenty of "Chinese" restaurants in Nashville, but those restaurants are catered to those who are not open to try the real authentic dishes of mainland China (Duck over rice, Peking Duck, Shanghai Dumplings, Steamed Sea Bass, Hot Clay Pots, Bean Curds(Tofu),etc). I was depressed that there wasn't at the very least a some-what authentic Chinese restaurant that would satisfy my cravings for good Chinese food until I found this place.  

If you're the type that loves the Americanized Chinese dishes such as General Tso's Chicken, Sweet and Sour Chicken/Pork, etc... you can still find it here. But let me warn you, ever since their reopening, their forte is NOT the Americanized Chinese dishes and instead their forte is their ability to cook authentic Asian dishes that range from Taiwanese, Shanghainese, Hong Kong, Central China, and Cantonese (tip: food in China varies by region so Chinese food is very broad). As a Chinese-American myself, I and grew up with home cooked savory Cantonese food, and great variations of Chinese food throughout California. In addition, I've lived in China and can confidently say this restaurant is the Holy Grail of authentic Chinese food that is comparible to that of the aforementioned. 

Before their reopening, the cooks at Chinatown traveled to all parts of China to learn the different techniques to the variouis types of cooking styles (contemporary and traditional) of Asia (mainly China and Taiwan); I know this because I asked the owners and the authenticity was explained after trying the dishes. You really can't get more authentic than that. I've spoken to other Chinese restaurant owners in Nashville, and many know the type of authentic Chinese food I'm talking about but ALL believe that Americans, especially Southern Americans, are not ready for REAL authentic Chinese food. So I applaud Chinatown for their bravery to make this move.

Tips to Yelpers: Don't be afraid to try the native Chinese dishes. Ask the waiters/waitresses how to eat certain dishes if you don't know how. It's very common in the Chinese culture to start off with soup (Taiwanese Won Ton soup is goood), then move on to appetizer, and share many plates of vegetables and meat dishes amongst your party. Dine in Chinese food is meant to be served family style.

I'm not affilated with Chinatown, nor have they asked me to post this review. I write this because this is definitely a gem of Nashville and want them to survive and keep serving me these great dishes (or else I may reconsider moving to the coasts for better variety of authentic food :) )
Just purchased the Beveled Arabesque Tile from #MissionStoneTile.  After seeing it in the showroom I just had to have it.  Can't wait to see it in my kitchen!
We have been looking for a good Chinese restaurant since moving to Nashville. We finally found it. This is our third visit and the food is consistently good! Service and staff are efficient and nice.

For Nashville, this is one of the better Chinese restaurants I have found. Sure beats Golden Coast off of West End. YUCK! I stumbled upon this restaurant after getting my nails done and sightseeing the other stores in the shopping plaza. It is a small, cozy family owned business. The owner is very nice. This restaurant has great lunch specials. Not the best Chinese I have had, in comparison to other Chinese restaurants, but if you are looking for the non-greasy Chinese staples, i.e. General Tso's Chicken, Beef and Broccoli, this is an excellent restaurant to try! If you are looking for a buffet, a pretty decent one is August Moon (in the same Hillsboro Pike/Green Hills area) or there is one in Antioch off the corner of Bell Road and I-24 (in the same parking lot as the Olive Garden but I forgot the name).

This place definitely has some of the most authentic Chinese food and it is reasonably priced as well. The crazy spicy chicken is excellent and the Mongolian beef has generous portions of beef and grilled onions. In addition, this place has many varieties of bubble tea for $2.99!!! You should definitely come to this place for fresh Chinese food and great prices!

I have been going to the Sneaker's in Sparks since it opened and love it.  We decided to stop into this location for a bite to eat before catching our flight since it is close to the airport.  The bartender (unknown name, dark haired lady) was very rude!   Before we even had a chance to sit down she said, "What can I get you??"  in a totally rude tone.  I asked for the breakfast menu and she said, "We don't have breakfast !" (In a tone like I should have know this....)  It was Sunday morning with NFL games on and no breakfast?  Ummm... Okay.  I said I would see the lunch menu then if they had that.  She said the cook was supposed to be there at 11.  It was  after 11 now and she went and checked and said there was no cook.   We walked out.  I did not feel welcome there at all.  Her attitude and no breakfast would help explain why the place was dead on NFL Sunday.    I would never again go back to this location.  It was also freezing cold in there too.
This place was a find. Great thin and crispy crust and nice fresh toppings. We had the 2 mediums special, a pitcher and a 2 liter soda for $30. We loved it! Thanks guys! Always great!!!

This place is great. The pizza is absolutely fresh and so delicious. I've been twice and both times sit down. Food comes out fast which is great. Place is clean inside which is my number one when it comes to eating out. Hands down my favorite pizza place in the area.
Small clean friendly pizzeria using fresh ingredients - I was there upon opening and witnessed the delivery of the raw materials - and simply the best pizza I have eaten in Tampa Bay bar none.

Really neat little shop for camping and hiking supplies, the employees are super nice and knowledgeable. If I ever need to get any more supplies I'll be coming back. They carry a good selection of Poler tents and bags.
This place is very close to my work. Foods are OK. It's your typical Americanized Chinese restaurant.
Best authentic Chinese I have had since moving here from bay area!

Great owners, but subpar Chinese food and even a bit overpriced, too.

When I first moved to Nashville, my parents and I ate at this restaurant hoping that we'd be eating great Chinese food.   We were greeted warmly by the owners, which was comforting.  But I wasn't expecting mediocre tasting Chinese food.  It's a huge disappointment if you're used to great Chinese food in Chicago, or if my family actually cooks better Chinese food that these Nashville restaurants.  

It's still in business, so I'm guessing some people out there must like it.  I wouldn't rule this one out, but if you have a palate for great-tasting Chinese food, I'm not sure if you'll find one here in Nashville.
