Been going to Jenna for a year now,so proud of how far she has come and definitely deserves it. Amazing customer servicing and reasonable prices for the results. Only person i've ever trusted with my hair

Let me start by saying that I am NOT a connoisseur of authentic Chinese food.  I usually choose the basics and don't get very adventurous with anything on the menu.  Now that we have that out of the way....I did enjoy my meal at Chinatown.  My husband and I went here for dinner on a midweek night and the restaurant was fairly empty.  The place was clean and the staff were friendly.

My husband and I shared the "small bun" which was really yummy!  My husband ordered something from that day's specials - I can't remember what he ordered but he enjoyed it.  I am really cautious about eating meat at certain restaurants, so I ordered the "Tofu with crispy bean blend" and it melted in my mouth.  It was fried tofu topped with these tiny little fried beans and onions and I swear it tasted like 'Bacon bits'.  Our server assured me it wasn't bacon and probably thought I was a weirdo.  I also ordered a Thai tea bubble tea -- it was great!

Even though it's a minor detail, my favorite thing about this place was that they served little Chinese crackers with duck sauce as an appetizer and orange wedges after your meal.  This was very nostalgic for me because it reminded me of the Chinese restaurant my family and I would frequently visit back home in West Virginia when I was a little girl.  It's the little things that matter!

Also, no delivery service.

Ordered dinner from her last night I'm not one to go off negative reviews till I try it for myself! Glad I tried this place I ordered a pizza, wings and cheesy garlic bread and Marinara sauce. The marinara was the best I ever had and everything was cooked to perfection! Pretty fast delivery and food was nice and hot. Well definitely be my pizza place for now on.

Great place with amazing coffee. Tucked away a little but easy to spot with the signage. 
We pass all the time and will be stopping by often!!

My friend got the worst nail job done at some nail store down the same block so it was about time she got a new place. This place is nothing you've seen before. It's huge, it's clean, and it's welcoming!! The workers take their time to make your nails look good! I highly recommend. Plus the price is pretty good too.

Tried here as I'm new to the area and needed a new barber.  Thankfully the Yelp community helped out and steered me to this highly-rated place that just opened in March.  They're on board with the new trend of having coffees and beers available while you wait at men's barbers, though I passed this time.  My stylist Philip was great and was fun and personable without crossing the line of being overly chatty.  Great experience overall and will definitely be back!

I usually go into each restaurant giving them 5 stars. I love food, I want them to be good, exceptional. Once I sit down there are various ways to start losing stars. This particular day the managed to get down to 1 star, 0 if we're being honest. So how did we get to 3 stars? Keep reading.

Our group decide on 11am for brunch. That good time when you can order breakfast and/or lunch and to not feel weird. We all smiled looking around the restaurant, they weren't busy. Phew. We were hungry too. 

Now, more people begin filling in, other parties of 4 or more. Now it's about 11:30, we still don't have our food. We're patient. But our eyes are like magnets to other people's food. They wonder in the plates of strangers, my mouth longing for a bite of something, anything. 

NOW.... it's 11:40 and the waitress, let's call her Jackie stops by the table. Wha wanted to inform us that 'the kitchen' needed to make another batch of pancake mix. Yes, pancakes.  But our food isn't rest yet.  pancake mix. Jackie offers gumbo for our wait. Now they're back up to 2 stars.

Food came eventually. It was good. Very good but, the. Service slow... make sure you have a lot time. Once the food came out, IT WAS GOOD! Normally I add pictures to my review but I was too hungry! Since the food was really good I moved them back up to 3 stars.

Servers are wearing no mask. And obviously they dont take orders from certain people who are wearing sleeveless shirts all of a sudden. Notice i said "certain people" if they dont know you. I had my U.S Marshal partner order my food instead and the chicken was pink and salty. They wont get another dollar from me

Went there yesterday... and never going back there. The food were of the cheapest quality you can receive from a Chinese restaurant. Ordered spicy garlic chicken, there was barely any chicken or any spice only tons of uncooked vegetables. The taste was so plain my water had more taste then it. Order beef belly in hot pot, also the same. The sauce was soo plain the only thing you are eating in there is the starch and beef broth. Literally one of the worst experience I ever have at a Chinese restaurant. The owner must have no tongue because clearly they have no real taste for Chinese food. I regretted ever stepping into this place from the moment I took my first bite. The portions were also outrageously small for a dinner price. 

Word of advice, if you are a real fan and you love Chinese food. Please do not disrespect your taste buds and go here. I recommend driving a little further to Corner Asian Cafe or Bistro. Either one will be 10X better then this place and it will cost the same or less.

First time visiting on Sunday and they had only a Brunch menu with limited menu.  Ordered a bowl of gumbo that came with a side of potato salad. The presentation of the food was great. But as soon as I dip my spoon I was disappointed. The temperature was not warm but not popping hot and the filling was absent to say the least. The taste was very good so I ate most of it.

After I was done one of the staff came and asked how was the meal. We expressed the disappointment of not having any filling and asked if there were any sausage and shrimp in there gumbo. She replied yes there was and that it seems the cook didn't dig down deep enough.  No other explanation or offer to change our impressions.

I guess it really didn't matter because I had already made up my mind I will not be returning!
Best authentic NOLA food. Everything is delicious and taste like someone grandma made everything from scratch. Best cornbread, read beans, and fried chicken.

Overjoyed!!! Sooooo everyone from New Orleans knows that Monday is Red Beans and Rice day, so upon looking for the perfect place for the New Orleans tradition I spotted Dunbar's...let me tell ya something! Real New Orleans cooked Camellia red beans baaaaaby not Blue Runners from the can( if you're from NOLA you know what I'm talking about)big plate full with smoked sausage(you can get fried chicken if you like), and the best sweet tea ever(when down south it's sweet tea or nothing). Now let me tell you about the customer service which I'm very big on...Cortez was awesome!!! Great smile, great personality, and absolutely an asset to the front of the house staff...He was pleasant and very courteous, he made the entire dining experience worthwhile so much so that I told him I was coming back for breakfast in the morning(yessssss they have $.99 cent breakfast)grit's, eggs, sausage and toast...and I love myself some grit's...well Cortez sold it and I bought it!! Can't wait until tomorrow....ANOTHER ONE YOU DON'T WANT TO SLEEP ON GUYS!!!!
I would recommend this restaurant if you have nothing but time on your hands! The food was good, but I would only return if I were on vacation.

Once great, now very disappointing.  New owners, food quality way down, prices way up.  Loved it for years, not going back. Fried rice without egg, peas, anything other than rice.  They said something about using a tiny egg!  I can do better with Uncle Ben's!
So good. Me and my daughter absolutely loved it was not greasy thin crust it wasn't salty it was perfect best pizza I've had in a while

Terrible experience. I went in to lighten my hair with foils and came out with dark hair and roots. The girl that "colored" my hair put a toner on  after she washed it which left my hair ashy and dull. The cut was fine. The salon was absolutely freezing and the music was blasting wIth techno music...will not be returning

We arrived at 9:43 and they refused to take our order or make our food. The employee was arguing with us and being extremely rude and disrespectful. They told us their boss "told them to start closing at 9:50," so they have to clean and cannot serve anyone. Taking into account we pulled in at 9:43, and it was not yet 9:50. If they are not going to be able to serve past a certain time due to cleaning, then they should close earlier. I will not be coming back.

Food was ok, but the service was really slow. Not to steal another review, but Dosh W. did a great write up and my experience was about the same. Even took forever to get a "to go" box and even longer to get the check.

Chinatown is a staple in Green Hills. It is always crowded even with a few other places next door. We came for lunch on a Saturday filled up pretty fast.  

Ordered the soup dumplings also called small buns on their menu. I did not get a sense of much soup, but they were tasty. About 8 of them. Normally we would devour them in a few minutes, but we had ordered a lot of food and were getting full. 
I had the beef soup. Saw a gentlemen worker on his break eating it and thought, hmmm that sounds good. It was appetising and filling. Good choice on me. Partner had the americanized sesame chicken. 

Before we left, we saw the specials. All LAMB. I don't eat a lot of Lamb, but I think it would be very good here. 

Service was amazing for being so full and so helpful and bonus was the yelp offer of 15 dollars for 10. Free 5 dollars with app. Would come more often if I worked nearby. Good Chinese food for Green Hills clientele.
Worst Landscaping service ever!  Still trying to recover from damages that they had done!  Please do research on this company before signing contract and compare other reviews!

Great chimney sweeps! After dealing with a pretty abysmal group of sweepers who never actually managed to sweep my chimney, I decided to give Your Chimney Sweep a try. First, I noticed how great they are with communication. You can request an appt. right through their website (yourchimneysweep.com) and they are quick to respond. When inclement weather was forecasted for the day of our sweep, someone from them called me and confirmed that they expected to still make the appt. despite the weather and would continue to stay in touch if that changed. I really appreciated that level of communication and commitment to getting my chimney cleaned.

The sweepers were friendly and happy to explain what they were doing as they went along. They not only swept the chimney but also pointed out potential trouble sources yet didn't pressure us to buy or do anything. We also got to see before and after pictures of inside our chimney. All the work was done inside the house using tools that went up the chimney rather than outside from the roof down. This was great as it meant less liability for both the sweeps and me with no one having to climb up on the precarious roof. Some of the cheaper chimney sweeps in the area don't offer this, I know for sure. So might be something to ask about if you go with someone else.

But don't go with someone else. These are the chimney sweeps you want to call if you want reliable service.

I rarely post such a positive response, but for this meal I have made an exception.  
Friendly, and courteous staff!  The food is outstanding and the prices are a great value for what you get.
I had the fried chicken plate with a side of red beans and rice.  Full of flavor and cooked to perfection, I chewed the chicken bones down to nothing,it was so good.

Very tasty food, but obviously, as most restaurants, extra slow with all the COVID-19 procedures, don't expect your food/service to be lightening fast. We sat inside and ate, but from what I saw, ordering to go before arriving seems to be the way to get your order faster.

Great breakfast! A lot of my classmates recommended this place so I decided to give it a try. I had the fried pork chop which was very flavorful. The biscuit was nice and soft and the plating of the food was very nice! The food is getting four stars cause it was a little pricey. I paid about 9 dollars and some change for a pork chop breakfast when there are plenty of other places in the city that charge about $4.99 + tax. Overall it was satisfying.

For a Chinese restaurant in Nashville, this is as good and authentic as it gets and would deserve 5 stars. However, since I am Chinese, and having been to real chinatowns in bigger cities (heck, even Memphis has quite a few authentic places), I can only give it 4 stars.

Now for the food review, the food is actually really good and authentic. A while back I even got a special Chinese menu, but last time I went I asked for the special menu and didn't get it (although they seem to have combined menus)... I haven't tried any "Americanized" Chinese dishes here, but all the dishes I've ordered have been spot on and delicious. Even my parents were impressed when they came to visit.

Some good chinese dishes:
Dou Miao
Mei Cai Kou Rou
Hui Guo Rou
any kind of "Bao"
This coffee truck is really cute and you can drive up to it! I got a plain hot latte and it was really good :)

I had no idea this hole in the wall existed... but now that I do I can't go a day without going! I've been there literally every day this week, and have loved every day more than the day prior! The staff is delightful and accommodating, they were so patient with me when I started coming through and had no clue how to navigate the menu (Which can seem intimidation because of how many fantastic options and combinations there are, but just start off by checking the specials board! Once you're more comfortable with the styles of drinks, the fun of customizing your own drink is a significantly more simple process) Do yourself a favor and skip the Shmarbucks line by stopping here instead!

I ordered samples of their Crema Firma marble.  The sample tiles were well packed and gorgeous quality tiles.  We placed an order for over $2200.  When it arrived we were shocked.  The packaging was flimsy.  An entire box was the wrong tile and another 10 tiles were damaged.  I sent pictures of the wrong tiles and the damaged.  I was told they would replace the wrong tile but my installer could cut around the damaged tile.  REALLY?  So I guess I paid for seconds.  I could have gone to our local discount tile store for that and paid a lot less.

Also I think its a rip-off how they charge you your credit card fee; a $25 loading fee and a $2 processing fee.

Never again!!  BUYER BEWARD!

Super friendly staff and great selection! I ordered Tiki Pink and Presto. Simple yet packed with flavor. Definitely a repeat soon! Going to try their iced coffee next. Located in a small lot along with few food trucks.

Christina White Salon has been an exciting day to myself where the experiences surpass any other salon I have been to. Walking into the Golden environment I feel like I in New York City or LA, but I am quickly reminded I am in Missouri with the sweet greeting from their front desk, their talented team remains humble.

As my pampering begins, I chat with friendly and interesting customers near me. Then we are surprised with a themed cocktail (crushed mint along the edge) and cheese cake bites and a side of raw almonds. 

Not only is the place gorgeous, food and conversation devine, the smells having you wanting to take a candle with their scent home.

I love going and asking my stylist and the owner about my hair idea, together we create a refreshing touch to my usual or play a little with soft pink highlights. I am always looking forward to my next cut, color, and other beauty options with Christina White Salon.
I was skeptical coming here because of some of the reviews but my experience was so good! The salon is CUTE! And my stylist was lovely and I LOVE my hair.

I frequented this restaurant when it was located on Freret and cant recall ever having an issue. Yesterday after seeing the announcement of their reopening my husband and I decided to give it a try for lunch later the same day. We were seated promptly as it was not crowded. Our waitress, a very pleasant little young lady with a beautiful smile. Husband ordered fried chicken and beans (he enjoyed it), I ordered "fried catfish" with fries and beans and "buttered french bread". Food came out in a reasonable amount of time HOWEVER, the fish that I received appeared to be "swai" or "basa" fish (often sold as catfish). It was a little fishier than I'd prefer but I decided to just not eat it, not say anything and continue eating the rest of the meal nonetheless. The BIGGER issue comes in when halfway into the remaining edibles, I noticed mold on the corner of the bread that I had already begun to eat. I informed the waitress when she returned to ask if everything was okay. She was very apologetic. She said she will need to inform her manager then took the plate, showed it to the owner who was sitting at a table near the counter before taking it to the back. When she came back she continued to apologize incessantly (as the owner sat and looked on yet said nothing), asked if I'd like anything else (to which I replied no) and informed me that she would just remove the charge from our bill. This is not the manner in which I would expect an owner to handle a situation like this. Needless to say I WILL NOT be returning to this establishment.

Service was great and the food is amazing! We were seated immediately with a smile. I had the ribs that came with two sides and my husband had the seafood platter. We could have chosen a better place, and we will definitely be returning!

I'm giving this place a star for the sake of the fact that I really did like my hair when I left there. I'm taking away four stars for what I feel is extremely non-transparent pricing practices. I saw good reviews on Yelp and decided to get an appt for a full foil hi-lite. I called to get an appt and was told that with the girl I'd be with, it would cost $147. Imagine how I feel when I go to pay and the receptionist says 'your total is $244'!! I was shocked as I expected it to be $100 less. Turns out, I was charged around $55 for toner and then $45 for a blowout. I was not even asked if
I wanted toner, so I assumed that was included in the price. Any other time I've been at a salon and toner was brought up, I was ASKED if I wanted it and TOLD how much extra it would be. I told the receptionist that the website with pricing did not list any of these extra charges. Usually a salon mentions in their pricing if a hairdry is not included with either cut or color. She just repeated 2-3 times 'all our services are a la carte'. Maybe to some people, paying that much to get a full foil and your hair dried is okay, but I feel those are Chicago prices, not Maplewood MO prices. I never would have made the appt if I knew it would be that much. The problem is not even so much the cost but the fact that these charges were not at all expected. Again, if I knew the full charge I would have said 'thank you for giving me that info' and moved on to another salon. Moral of this story is this---yes, the service itself was great and go for it of you are good with those prices, but I'd recommend asking at the time you make the appt for a line-by-line summary of the charges you'll be paying.

BEWARE if you choose to visit this salon. My experience was like none other. I booked my appointment online with Ari, as she came recommended. I called to see if I could add a cut to the appointment and was told I could, but would need to move the time from 9:15 to 9:00 because Ari was leaving at 3:00 to go on vacation. I got a text message on Monday to confirm my appointment. I arrived on Tuesday, was never told that my appointment would be with someone else, never offered to reschedule and never even introduced to the stylist. I did not realize that I had a different stylist until that evening,  when I noticed her business card had a different name. I called to see if this was common practice, was told it was an oversight on their part and received an apology. Was also told that the stylist was of the same "master" skill level as my requested stylist.

The next morning, I washed and dried my hair for the first time after receiving my services. My hair is severely damaged, dry and frizzy. My cut, which I believe was $75, is embarrassing. My "face framing layers" are puffs of dry, damaged hair. I have long pieces sticking out of the bottom in numerous places. I had to wear my hair up to cover the cut mistakes, and several people made comments about my "line" of highlights on the side. 

I am including pictures of my services. This would not fall under mastery skill level in my book, yet I was charged $330 for a level 4 stylist.   I've been to several different upscale salons and this one was by far, the most expensive. 

After corresponding with the salon, they offered to FaceTime me to show me how to trim the ends. If I wanted to cut my own hair and it was "a quick and easy fix" as they stated in their email, I would have skipped the trip all together. After seeing the pics, the did agree to  refund me $57 for the cut. It will take years to repair the damage of the highlight and cut. I have also had to have my hair toned to cover the bright orange roots.

Be careful, be very careful! My 86 year old father went into the Santa Barbara store to purchase a bed for himself and my mom.  He wanted a bed they could use for now together then later be split and they could use individually.... He spent $6,853.62 on a SPLIT Cal King bed.  Now, only 5 months later, my mom has to go into a memory care facility and they want to SPLIT the beds, one side go with her-one side with him.....Well, even after spending over $6,000... There is only one mattress pump and one bed frame control box.  He now is looking at having to spend an additional $2,000 to split the beds or just blow-off 1/2 the bed!  He could have purchased 2 separate beds for less than his initial purchase... Taking advantage of an old man???? You tell me!

Wow, the food here is absolutely delicious. The establishment was clean. The staff was friendly and efficient. I enjoyed every single morsel of food. The honey bourbon chicken and the ranch fries is the best combo. The flavors were just dancing on my tongue. I'll be back for sure.
Good coffee to get you going in the morning. Eggcellent customer service. Will be back!

I had asked for a plain burger, and they gave me one with everything on it. On the receipt it also said plain, so I don't how they fail to make the burger right.. They get my order wrong constantly, and I live a while a way. So waste of gas coming back. I shouldn't even need to look in the bag, it should be right when I get it.

I tried this place a few times with different stylists which obviously I can't judge the salon I have to judge the stylist but this last time I paid over 600$ for my hair to look the exact same when I wanted it to be a completely different color I wanted to go from my brown hair to a natural looking auburn-red color. I keep asking friends if they can see a difference but no one can. I'm super disappointed I'm just trying to find a good salon or stylist that will actually do what I want and has expertise but after that last time I don't think I'll ever be back nor will I suggest anyone go there again it's over priced for the work they do. They really only specialize in extensions not actually cutting and coloring I'm not trying to damage my hair with fake hair.

Good Chinese food . 
We have been so skeptical to try any Chinese food here in the south because all the Chinese restaurants look scary even from the outside.

But Chinatown is delicious and their dumplings are so warm and fresh. 
Definitely returning! 
There's parking right in front of the restaurant.

Note to all you southerners ; when you see Asians especially the race of that type of restaurant the food is going to be good and close to authentic .

And we saw Chinese eating at this restaurant.

Shoddy work. Hairstilists don't hear you. The professional who made my hair did what was easier for her instead of doing her best.
I complained, asked my money back, including the tip. I haven't received the tipping amount but I received my refund. A week later after moving my hair up, tapes started to fall and open. I showed some pictures of a extension which fallen from my hair and the professional asked where was it from. She did the job but she could not remember. Very disappointing. Today all the tapes opened and I had to look for a professional to fix this shoddy work. (It was a simple move up)I have it on my hair since February (other salon from other country). I know how to take care of extensions. The salon staff just want to sell products and new hair instead of providing basic expertise. I don't recommend this place for people who have ethnic hair. On the other hand, staff is very polite and friendly.

That cannoli changed me! The food (we ordered an extra large four cheese pizza, a chocolate cake and a cannoli) was so good we made a second order for more! Definitely a place to keep in mind for a reliable meal delivered in a timely manner!

I ordered two double cheeseburgers. I didn't get two double cheeseburgers. One piece of cheese on each, no condiments. One pick slice on each. Sad. I ordered cheesy tots for $1. I was given four overdone cheesy tots. They were dark brown and hard. They looked nothing like the poster.

The shop is drive up only which makes me feel safe that there is no one outside of their employees in the location. The coffee was amazing and service was quick. I will definitely frequent this location.

Careful here.  The kid at the window will say he can't give you change because because he doesn't have the coins.   Most likely, he's keeping it for himself.  A business with no coins in the drawer? It will be a long time before I return.
The prices and availability of groceries make the experience a very positive one. Shops here.

5 stars are a MUST for this company! Scott and I first found Your Chimney Sweep on Yelp and they were quick to respond to our questions and set up a date to come to the house. This time of year, the wait is a little longer (we waited a couple of weeks) but no big deal :)

They called the day before to confirm the appointment and then arrived right on time the following day! I was working but according to Scott, who was home, Joe was as professional as it gets. Not only does he have state of the art equipment, but he takes his profession seriously. Joe inspected the chimney in its entirety - including a trip to the roof of our house to make sure there were not breaches or damage that could lead to a fire. The camera he used to inspect the chimney provided very clear images - which then went into a nice PDF to be emailed to us.

It was really nice to see how the chimney was designed too! I like feeling involved in the process. Our neighbor apparently was in desperate need of a chimney sweep and came over while Joe was finishing up at our house. He was kind enough to go next door to take a look at their chimney too! Now that is 5-star service.

Joe left our home cleaner than he found it and I would absolutely recommend this service to anyone in town!
This place is short-staffed and packed and the manager remained calm and cool during the whole ordeal. the most professional man I've ever seen. I will be back.

This is a review for the carry-out food at Chinatown. Anyone who knows me knows I've long bemoaned the lack of great Chinese food in Nashville. Chinatown isn't necessarily an exception - I don't consider it to be exceptional. However, it's quite decent and serviceable, and in this town, that says a lot! 

Last night, we ordered carry-out on Chinatown's easy-peasy online system. A few clicks and a request to pick it up ASAP - we were set! The food was fresh and ready moments after we arrived to pick it up! Also, it was very reasonably priced - two entrees, a soup, a fried rice side and egg rolls - $30 with tax! 

Flavor-wise, the food is pretty good! I'm a big fan of mushu pork, and this was fine. It was a bit heavy on the cabbage, short on the onions, but okay. The shrimp and veggies with a simple sauce were great, and the egg fried rice was exactly as you'd want it to be. Wanton soup was satisfying and simple - same for the egg rolls. 

Is Chinatown going to win any big awards any time soon? No. I'd probably even rank it lower in a market with better options. But in a city that still has a huge gap between food court and fine dining Chinese, this is one of the spots to scratch the itch when a craving for basic Ameri-Chinese strikes.

We live close to this pizza shop and we've ordered many times. The pizza is delicious, fresh and comes hot! I will warn that it is a little greasy and it's definitely a thinner kind of bread. But I prefer it that way, so I don't mind. We are always pleased with the quality and quantity of the pizza. Also, the customer service is great!

Pizza was delicious, we got so many garlic rolls that were warm and tasty, and we got garlic parm wings that were our favorite so far in Tampa. They also have great deals and bundles for game day. We will definitely be back!

Found this little gem while driving around town. Very friendly employee and fast service. Ordered a double shot espresso and iced macchiato. Will definitely be back for some breakfast sandwiches  real soon! Love the options for keto and monthly flavored options.

We had the shrimp & grits and baked salmon w/ peas and spicy fried rice. I also had an Arnold Palmer and mom had a strawberry lemonade. Both drinks were great. The shrimp & grits were good, but I've had better. They could have benefited from more seasoning and spices, similar to what you would find in bbq shrimp. Mom said the salmon was cooked perfection, although her spicy fried rice--rice with onions and peppers--was kind of cold. 

Service was great, fast and attentive for the most part. The host was also very friendly and told us about the chargrilled oysters that were added to the menu. Will definitely try next time. 

Ambiance was fine. There were only a handful of customers in the restaurant, so it wasn't very loud. The place was clean, but I think it would look nicer if they went with white walls instead of the current mustard. The space, however, is huge with main dining in front and take out in rear. I'm told the restaurant can be rented after business hours for private events. 

The prices were reasonable and we'll be back. Will also have to try the $.99 breakfast.

I usually go here for some late night, after work, cravings. I never go in during the last hour, and tonight was no different. But man y'all could have just told me you didn't have chili dogs ready. Otherwise, the Bug Buford, fries and drink were all great. I appreciate what you guys put out, but this is whack man

Dunbar's is EXCEPTIONAL.

My dad first told me about Dunbar's because of their super cheap breakfast special they have that he likes to grab after weekday mass. 

We grabbed lunch on weekday afternoon and ordered the smothered okra with friend chicken, smothered okra with fried chicken, and the fried catfish platter. The smothered okra was rich and delicious and the fried chicken was hot, fresh, and super juicy! They also bring you this amazingly sweet and crumbly cornbread to eat while you're waiting. Our waitress was very friendly, made sure we had everything we needed, and even told us about the history of Dunbar's while we waited... such an excellent experience. Plus the servings are so big so we got to bring food home.

So tonight my husband and I were craving good, homestyle friend chicken, we got Dunbar's to go. Two 3-piece dark meat friend chicken dinners with choice of side (we both got Mac n' cheese), side salad, and garlic bread. Total was under $20. The chicken was hot, fresh, crispy on the outside but tender and juicy on the inside, and so utterly delicious! It's a great location that's super convenient to uptown with it's own free parking lot. To-go orders are super fast and staff is always super courteous... I can't say enough great things about it so just go!!!!

Allowed me to order my food and pay for my food, before rudely telling me they were out of my food. After I had paid. Thieves. My previous visit, they snatched a bag out of my hand in the drive through, telling me I had the wrong food, and gave me another bag. The bag they took from me had the correct order and they left me sitting at the drive through for minutes before they would talk to me again..

I was told this site would be good to get the traditional  on New Year's meal but that was not accurate.  The place is Okay it's clean.  The food was nothing great it was okay cornbread is Jiffy Mix didn't have the opportunity to have the greens because they didn't have any the catfish was not seasoned and I asked for it to be fried hard but it wasn't.   The black eyed peas were basic.  Not bad just basic nothing exceptional.

Worst service I've ever had. Waited 45 minutes for an onion ring. When asked for the money back caught an attitude and tried fighting. They didn't have their hAir up nor gloves while handling food. Half our food was cold when we got it. Would definitely not recommend going to this one

If your regular salon is not available this place is okay in a pinch. The staff is nice enough and the lady who gave me a manicure did a great job. It was a plain manicure with clear polish, the way she filed my nails and pushed my cuticles gave me a nice long nail bed. This is hard to do considering I have very short nails. 

The set up is satisfactory nothing special not extra clean just not noticeably dirty. For my pedicure I had to give her a look to ensure the liner for the tub was added. My pedicure looked good, I believed The technician who rubbed my toenails over and over again saying 'it's dry'. When I took my shoes off at home my big toe was a mess!

Again I will only return in a pinch this would not be a go to spot for me. There's an extra fee when using a debit or credit card, nowadays people are fearful of carrying cash.

I used to go to Chinatown a lot when I was a student at Vanderbilt. Chinatown is conveniently located near the mall at green hills; the service is fine. The food is OK, though I remember one time when I found the pork went bad. 

The same people have recently opened another restaurant on Charlotte Pike, next to K & S international market. The newer restaurant is called the lucky bamboo restaurant. It is bigger than the already crowded Chinatown and offers a wider variety of authentic Chinese food. I tried the new one recently and prefer this place over the old Chinatown.

As always, ask for the Chinese menu if you want to try real instead of Americanized Chinese food.

Do not recommend! Not happy with final product!  After a week, the top soil looks like sand with small branches and pine cones.  Also, my yard had turned into a pool of water, since the service.  My yard is ruined!   Best advice, do your research on the contractor, before you hire them!!

Jenna is TAMPA HAIR GOALS!!! 

When I went to Jenna I was extremely depressed because the last person chopped off my hair and thinned out my hair. My hair was so bad that I lost confidence. It took me 4 years to grow my hair out and someone ruined it in a matter of 40 mins. I also used to color my hair on my own. 

Jenna was completely understanding and saw my vision come alive. She is AMAAAZING with colors. I never did a baylage and was a little skeptical. I now ONLY let Jenna touch my hair. She has helped repair my damage hair, she respects length and has a keen understanding of hair color. She has helped restored confidence and is sooo knowledgeable regarding products she only uses the best products on your hair. I love how she is able to pick the best colors for my hair. She recently helped me find the best color to wear during the summer which a purple/red. I love going to her. She really takes her time with your hair. I also appreciate how well is precise she is. Her hands are magic!!! I love her! I recommend everyone to go see her. She changed my whole life! I no longer walk around with damaged hair

I have been to this location 3 times in 3 years.  Each time the service and cleanliness was terrible.  I am not sure if the employees here are mistreated or just enjoy being rude. Either way, the BK corporate brand is being run into the ground at this location.  I have enjoyed eating at BK for decades throughout the entire country and have never encountered one that was this poorly run.  The owner ought to drive 1 mile west on Olive and see what happened to the Steak and Shake location. Unless this places wakes up and decides it wants to be in the food business, the same needs to happen here.
The aquarium is in walking distance and it is very nice! The parakette house was too cute. It is not a big aquarium but still has wonderful fish.

We had fun here, they are very military friendly and offer great military discounts on pictures, tickets, and the gift shop. It wasn't as big as I expected though, but it was still super fun and interesting. Staff is amazingly friendly. We will be coming back on our next trip to NOLA.

This place was awesome!!!the waitress was really helpful! I had the brisit was cooked perfectly I also enjoyed the potato salad and baked beans the atmosphere was really cool to it was only a couple of other people and they are not too crowded for lunch time but shortly after I finished my meal I noticed the rash come in this place is located in downtown New Orleans but not like you think when you think ofBourbon streetmore of a Soho uptown district area:)

So came to Nashville with the wife , she likes country music I wanted hot chicken needless to say we both scored , 400 degrees hot chicken was great I had the 200 and it was perfectly Cooke , spiced  and served sides were awesome , get the citrus sweet tea , loved it with the chicken , perfect , perfect and perfect

I love aquariums but this one was fairly disappointing. It's normally $22.50 for adults but we had a $3 off coupon that we used. Still wouldn't pay the $19.50 to go back. It's two stories and very small and was quite dirty. Several of the interactive machines were broken, it had horrible upkeep, and overall just sucked. We went because we wanted to get out of the heat and do something away from bourbon street but I wouldn't recommend unless you're a parent looking to distract your kid for a little bit.

I like aquariums a lot, and usually try to visit the local one when I'm in a city.  I had heard this was an excellent one, but I was pretty disappointed.  They had a few cool things - a giant anaconda, a white alligator, penguins, and an otter - but nothing I haven't seen done better elsewhere.  All in all, the exhibits could have been much bigger, better, and more diverse.  I was disappointed.  Maybe this used to be better before Katrina - I know they had to send a lot of their animals away during that time.   Maybe they're still building it back up?  I don't know.  It was fun enough, and I don't regret going, but I wasn't really impressed compared to some other aquariums I've seen.
Talked briefly on the phone. No actual service. Thorough fair and reasonable estimates.

This is very unfortunate... Was in town for a meeting and wanted to try some Nashville Hot Chicken for the first time. Staying at a hotel close by; myself and 2 co-workers decided to walk up the street to 400 Degrees. We walked in at 6:35pm and we were told by the woman behind the counter that they were closed; the menu and sign clearly state they close at 7pm. Would have been nice to know that if you want Hot Chicken at 400 Degrees please show up at least an hour before they are supposed to close down.
This place was kind of cool. Nothing too crazy. Its fun for kids, but not the coolest aquarium I've been to.

Went there for lunch today and shared a combo of falafel and eggplant with sides of baba ganoush and humus. For drinks we had the hibiscus-rose water which was very nice and not so sweet. Very refreshing. The food was good and I'll definitely come back for dinner time.

200° their medium heat chicken is right on par. my nose didn't run like the menu said but equally tasty. beans where on the sugary side but it was a nice complement to the heat from the chicken. byob gotta love the combo. friendliest service that calls you out by name multiple times makes sure you don't need anything, I'll be back.

While 400 Degrees was miles better than Boltons to me, there's just not beating Hattie B's and Prince's. They both represent the two versions of Nashville hot chicken the best. I'd put 400 Degrees at a solid #3, and considering Aqui's humble beginnings that's pretty impressive. Aqui (owner) was cooking that day and was all too sweet, friendly, and welcoming in a way that only an old friend could be. That's something you will NOT get at any other hot chicken joint. 

Key here is to call ahead (if you can get through), and if not clear your afternoon because it's going to be 45m-1hr as its going to be made fresh just for you. Not getting that any where else either. 

400 degrees was a sloooooow burn. Ate a whole wing before I was writing my will. 200 degrees is the right amount of burn. Don't bother with 100 or 0. Why are you even going to get hot chicken??? Legend has it there's an 800...who are you that just got excited. You are not human. 

Go get some 400 Degrees next time you're near downtown, and bring some water to cut the sweet tea with :)

In general I always enjoy going to aquariums. Something about them is so peaceful, except for when dozens of kids are there screaming and being annoying, but other than that I really love them. I especially love going to them when I'm on vacation and the weather is less than desirable and that's what brought me here. 

The biggest tip I could give you is to buy your ticket in advance online. Initially we waited in a line that seemed to not be moving at all. They had two separate purchasing areas: one for season passes and one for non-members. Neither line seemed to be moving. Then I got the bright idea to ask if I bought the ticket online, where would I have to go. The woman replied as long as the ticket had a bar code (in my email) we could walk right in. And that's what we did.

Second (smaller) tip is that it's cold in here so dress appropriately.

You start your journey with this 30 ft tank that you walk through which was beautiful, slightly sparse, but still beautiful. These are creatures from the Great Mayan Reef. 

There is so much to explore here. I think my favorite part, which just because it was unexpected, was the Amazon Rain forest. You'd see hawks and owls which again, I don't anticipate seeing in an aquarium, but I did!

They also have, Parakeet Pointe, penguins, seahorses, sea otters, a touch pool- if you feel like waiting in line to pet sting rays, and so much more.

Plenty of restrooms along the way and a couple of snack options too.

There was plenty to see and a few interactive places that even us adults could enjoy too. So you're able to let your inner child out and have a good time for a good hour or two. Definitely worth the roughly $25 per ticket we spent and is an activity I think most people would really enjoy doing. It's a welcome change from the noise on Bourbon Street for sure.

It was EXTREMELY busy when we went that it was difficult with a stroller at some parts. But our daughter enjoyed all the fish and some interactive learning curves they had. There is a play structure upstairs near the stingray exhibit that I believe needs to be monitored due to very small children playing and kids above 10 aggressively running and climbing on the structure. We ended up needing to grab our daughter who is just over a year because there were way too many close encounters.

Hmm maybe I'm just not a fan of BBQ in general?

The upside: super friendly service! :D Our server Abby was one of the sweetest waitresses ever. She also paints, so you can buy her artwork to support her if you want.

The food: I felt it was pretty average :T they do provide 5 or 6 different sauces to drench your BBQ in; I recommend trying all of them to see which is your favorite (I  liked Southern Sweet with the pulled pork; the Fantasy Sauce kind of just tasted like something with Tabasco in it to me)

What we got:
-Pulled Pork Nachos: kinda dry, and the cheese hardened a lot before we dug in; I'm guessing we were supposed to add a lot of sauce to it? (which we did)
-Half Rack of Ribs: I guess BBQ and I just don't mix because I couldn't get all of the meat off the bone :/ The meat itself was tender though.
-Single Serving of Baked Macaroni [cup-size]: a little on the sour side for some reason?

To each his/her own though, cause my boyfriend highly approved? O.o

P.S. BYOB :)

Awesome spot for bbq I'm always there for my weekly dose of brisket. The variety of sauces is great. The ribs are very tender and a slab is more than enough for 3 people. The people that work here are very nice, Laid back and they have great owners that know what they r doing. Their brisket tops the list in new orleans. And the brisket melt really melts in ur mouth. Love it.

Not bad... you'll spend a lot of your time trying to find the aquatic life if they are small -  they are masters of hiding spaces.  

The seahorse, otter and penguin exhibits were my favorite. You get to pet Manta Rays and a baby shark.  Makes me nervous because kids aren't to be trusted with such delicate skinned creatures.  

It's very child oriented. They even have a play area for kids.  

Recommended for families with young children.  Just watch them to make sure they don't do any harm.

CLOSED ON MONDAYS

The chicken here is seriously hot but in my opinion it lacked flavor.  I mean I don't usually expect to beer wowed by chicken but after an hour wait I kinda wanted a flavor explosion. Several people in my party were just a little more unhappy but I try to be fair. I would say if you in town try it. It's the first and only I've tried to this date. And locals told me this was the best

Overall, a nice experience.  There were plenty of exhibits to see!! I loved that we were able to pet and feed the sting rays!  We really wanted to pet the penguin and watch the feeding but the morning feed started at 11 am, right when the doors practically open.  It was disappointing and we did not want to wait till 5 to see the feeding.  

I loved the tunnel we walked through! Sharks, turtles, and different fishes swam around us. It felt magical!   I loved the gianormous sea turtle! 

There were interactive learning tools for adults and children alike! 

Overall nice experience!

We were walking along Magazine Street when we smelled the heavenly aroma of smoked meats emanating from this establishment. A quick YELP search revealed favorable reviews from most diners. We had just toured Texas where we had some of the most outstanding BBQ in our lives. It was time to put New Orleans BBQ to the test, and Saucy's BBQ came through with flying colors!
 
We both ordered a 2 meat / 2 side combo for $14. We both chose Brisket and Pork Ribs, delightfully smoky, tender and succulent. The ribs were cooked just right (el dente, to the bite off the bone!) and flavorful. The BBQ dip sauce enhanced this flavor without overpowering the spices on the ribs. The brisket was easily the most juicy, tender and best that I have had so far. The horseradish dip for the brisket enhanced these beefy flavors perfectly. The sides we chose of Grilled Asparagus, Goat cheese mac-n-cheese, and Baked Beans were excellent! The biscuit made from sweet potato and cinnamon was a nice finishing touch. The service was fast and efficient. We would definitely eat here again!

Went to 400 Degrees when they first opened and just thought it was alright.  So this year I've decided to go back to all the places that I haven't been to in a while to give them another shot.
About a week ago I went to 400 Degrees. There was one person in line in front of me.  I get to the register to order and I'm told it will take 40 minutes.  Like most people on their lunch break from work, I don't have time for that.  Cashier told me to call ahead next time if I don't have the time for that wait.  
So I took his advice.  Today, I called and got an answering machine.  I kept calling for 30 minutes straight before giving up.  Sometimes that machine would pick up and sometimes it would just ring and ring.  I was never even able to make an order.  
I decided to go to another hot chicken joint in town and got in line.  I didn't have to call ahead.  There were 4 people in line in front of me.  I had fresh hot chicken and sides within 10 minutes.  
Not sure what they're doing at 400 Degrees, but I wouldn't waste my time if I were you.

This is an excellent natural history museum! Kids and adults will learn plenty from an afternoon here. The rooms dedicated to the rainforest and the natural habitat of the Bayou are well-planned, and the kids will love the large displays of peguins, sharks, and sea otters. It's similar in size to the new California Academy of Sciences. I wish the IMAX was included in the pricing, but c'est la vie...Hopefully, the Audubon organization will find a way to make the pricing more attractive to locals.

Seriously the best bbq I have ever had. The ribs were cooked perfectly, the asparagus was crisp and we'll seasoned, and the goat cheese Mac was incredible. If I'm ever back in New Orleans I'm definitely coming back!

Overall a disappointing experience. Very small aquarium with little organization. The entrance fee is about $24 per adult and we didn't feel it was worth nearly that much. The entire aquarium took under an hour to get through and that was with spending time to see each exhibit. It would be a great experience for kids, however I would avoid it as an adult. There are plenty of other things to do in NOLA such as the WWII museum.

I've been in here 2 since they have opened. Had a great time last time, and ended up with a dress and shirt. Completely spur of the moment shopping, and I walked away with items I love and can get a lot of use out of. They have good sizes so you can actually find things that fit. It was great considering I usually hate shopping and often walk out of places empty handed.

Everyone in my little family of three loves bbq.  It is quite possibly a fave of all three of us.  This place is our favorite bbq restaurant in New Orleans.  The menu is not too extensive, even a bit limited in some areas (like the appetizers) but what they do - they do well.  My son loves their ribs.  He gets the 4 rib/1 side item plate.  They ribs are huge and always well seasoned and cooked.  They're so big that he usually only eats two and brings the other two home.  My personal favorite is the chaurice sausage.  It's fresh, locally made,  and has an all around great flavor.  I've tried all of their side items.  The mac and cheese is by far the best.  The beans and potato salad are also very good.  The slaw - not so much - I'd steer clear of that one.  They also give you these delicious little sweet potato muffins.  I could eat tons of them.  Overal, on food alone, I'd give them 4 stars.  I gave them 5 because the owners are nice people, the servers always take good care of us when we go in, and the food is very consistent.  We have never had a bad meal here.  The food is always hot (unlike the joint) and its always cooked well (unlike squeal).  In my opinion, this place is one of the most under rated for bbq.  Squeal and the Joint always get the top 2 spots on the city's "best of" lists.  The people voting are either doing so out of name recognition, they ate there once and thought it was good, or they haven't eaten there at all and are just writing stuff in.  I say that bc we go to all three regularly - well we did until the joint served us ice cold food and said we had to eat it that way bc they couldn't warm it up.  Out of all three, Saucys has the best tasting and the most consistent food.  If you love bbq and your aren't eating here, then you are missing out.  New Orleans definitely isn't known for bbq but maybe Saucy's can change that.

We came to New Orleans for the first time in October, 2017 and decided to go to the aquarium since it was so close to everything else we were doing that day.  It was $60 to get in for 2 people, which to me was a lot.  The penguins were not there, it was kind of small and overall lackluster. The only reason I'm not too mad about it is because I saw the otters... that's it though.  Everything else just about put me to sleep.

First off - always order ahead of time regardless of the time you're going.

Atmosphere - it's within a food court shared with Nuvo Burrito, Quiznos, and J Gumbos.

Service - I've been here around the same time before and it was slower this time. I think it was the owner who was helping us but she was very nice. She seemed a bit irritated we had to ask for it to go but what do you expect when the "30 - 45mins" turns into 45mins - 1hr.

Food - The first time I had a chance to sample the chicken I was very unimpressed. The chicken was dry and just tasted like they handed me chicken that was just seasoned. HOWEVER this time around the chicken was worlds better. It wasn't over-seasoned like beforehand and the chicken was very juicy. I'm a sucker for crinkle fries and theirs are just as good as any - but they won't hold up well over time.

Overall - If you're into hot chicken then you should definitely try it out - order ahead - but try it out.

I called Frank and explained a problem with our kitchen range. He said he would be sure he had the parts and would repair it the following afternoon. Next day, shortly after noon, he called, confirmed the address and said he would arrive within the hour. He did and quickly confirmed the problem to be two defective burners and burned out wires leading to them. He made the repairs and explained as he worked what he was doing. He then noticed that the freezer door was not hanging right, even though we had not asked him to check it, and he quickly adjusted the nuts holding the door so that it closed properly. He did not charge extra for that service. The price was reasonable. I plan to call him again, if an appliance needs work, and I would recommend him to my neighbors. He kept up an amusing chatter salted with scatological terminology, which did not offend me. Much of the chatter was useful information about iPad apps, repairs, and the like.
If you have short hair and are looking for a new stylist, Melody is your girl! She being a artist and your hair the canvas you can't feel anything but beautiful when you leave the salon!

I used to love this place they have a awsome selection then they charged my debit card 2 times for the same thing and I called them and even though my bank said it was on them and nothing was pending they did not do a thing for me. Dawn they lady I was talking to was the most unapologetic person she could be not a sorry or anything. She was talking to me like I was wasting her time. And every time I went in there she was so unhappy and just seemed like she hated her life and her job. I am bummed out because I used to like shopping there every pay check but now I will have to order offline or almost anywhere where they mite be helpful and more enthusiastic about at least being alive and not a stick in the mud.

I havent been here in years. Im going off of what I recall. We had a great time looking at all the fish and even the bayou section with alligators and owls. During the Hurricane, all of the marine animals were killed. So, Im not sure if they are up and running again, and even if they are , how big of a selection they have. I hope that they are open and business is booming, its a great get away for the day. Its right next to the Riverwalk and Imax Theater and Parking is very close.

A cute aquarium and worth a visit, particularly if you're doing the Audubon experience pass (insectarium, aquarium, zoo). There's a lot to walk through and see although if you rushed you could do it in 1.5 hours.

The one major downside is that the signs describing the marine life are severely lacking and could really use an update.

This place has potential, and I'll try it again, but the sauces are bad. They need to either be more flavorful or have more options. Neither sauce really fit with my meal (ribs and brisket with Mac and cheese). Mac and cheese and muffin were good, and the quality of the meat was good, but what's the point of BBQ with poor sauce? 

Hopefully, this review doesn't invite another rant from the owners, like other reviews. You'd think maybe they'd offer some of the unhappy customers below the chance to try the place again and prove them wrong - I guess maturity isn't on the menu.

If I could give more than 5 stars rating I would!

Frank called me less than an hour after I placed the service call.  He arrived 45 minutes later and fixed my washer without any problem.  He is personable - we had a great conversation while he worked.  He also had no issue with one of my cats (Snickers) helping him work.  

He made a stressful situation fade away, the charges were more than reasonable and I made a great connection.  

If you need appliance or computer repairs, contact All Brands Service - you won't regret it!

Great place for the kiddos. Took my 18 month and 3 year old and they were able to be apart of everything. The place is clean and easy to navigate while giving space to run around a little.

Good job New Orleans, this was our second favorite spot next to the WWII museum, but the kids ranked it number 1!

Frank (owner) arrived within about a half hour of initial call. Spent a couple of hours, replaced a few parts, and fixed our clothes dryer.

Explained what he was doing along the way. Very pleasant. Reasonably priced. 

Would absolutely refer to family and friends.

This was such a FUN experience. I really appreciated the linear layout of the aquarium, as it made it easy to make sure we saw everything and it was easy to navigate. The parakeet enclosure was definitely my favorite. The birds are super friendly and it's just a delightful experience to turn around and have four cute little bird friends hanging out all over your body. I also really enjoyed the Gulf of Mexico exhibit.

I recently started having Tom do maintenance on my wife's Toyota SUV, he came recommended from a friend.

So far we've have two great experiences with the service that I can speak of:

1) About two months ago we got new brakes and tires, oil change and some other minor repairs. We paid what I thought was a reasonable amount for the service, and it was done fast.

2) This past week I took the car back for a new engine timing belt and 200K service, including new water pump and other belts. Also had a new battery and the annual PA inspection done too. Everything was done right the first time, no surprises. He even replaced an extra brake light bulb (something I hadn't asked about), at no extra charge. 

Overall very happy with the service, parts were NOT outrageously marked up, and the vehicle runs smooth.

Glad I found a good local shop I can trust to maintain our cars.

We had the ribs, brisket, mac and cheese, cole slaw, and baked beans. The ribs and brisket were cooked perfectly. Not too soft and not too chewy. The sauces are also tasty. The mac n cheese was great! I believe they had some goat cheese in it. I didnt eat the baked beans my wife did. She said they were amazing! Will definitely visit again.

I am from Mississippi...home of fat people who live and love to eat. Ive eaten ribs for a long time....

These ribs are some of the best my fat ass has ever had.

How? Half an inch of meat on each one. Cooked perfectly.

Sides are out of this world...bbq beans, potato salad, mac and cheese....

Stop reading and start eating....

This is about as good as an aquarium can get.   They have lots of different types of animals in every kind of exhibit you can imagine.  The big attractions are probably the shark tanks.  They are so big that they have stadium-style seating beside them so you can just sit there and watch these enormous sharks swim around their massive tank.

There are also some really fun interactive exhibits, like the Touch-A-Stingray exhibit. Bring the kids folks, this is a great place for them.

This aquarium is slightly smaller than, but definitely rivals, the Baltimore Aquarium. It is gorgeous and very well laid out. They have lots of neat things too! My inner (or maybe not so inner) child had a blast running around looking at all the different fish, turtles, frogs, birds, and other various sea creatures Audubon houses. My favorite exhibits are the penguins (obviously), the sea horses, and the otters.  Little (and big) kids alike should consider this a must visit when in NOLA, it's worth every penny!

God, I love this place. 

Thoughts:

1. The owners and staff are incredibly nice and fair when ordering for a large group. They always throw in a little something extra!!

2. The beans are a recipe that make me contemplate committing sins just to have one more bite. 

3. Most importantly, the meat cuts, portions, and sauces are INCREDIBLE!!!!

Go here. Get Sauced.

I have never had hot chicken before and didn't really know it was a "Nashville Tradition" so I thought I would start to make the journey around to try the different ones.  Thanks to the yelpers I tried 400 Degrees. 

To start off the review I knew it would be slow to get my food before I went and I would suggest to anyone that goes there to know it will be VERY VERY slow (even slower then you would imagine) blame it on making it to order.  Knowing that before hand I would only drop them down 1/2 a star.

First the chicken, good crisp with nice spiciness, inside was juicy and just the way good fried chicken should be.  The fries were crinkle cut and was prepared perfectly.  The cole slaw was OK (kind of standard)...  fries were better.

The chicken is hot  they have 4 flavors. 
0 -      which is pretty much sauce-less (didn't try).
100 - This is the flavor I ordered, I had quite a bite flavor.  A good amount of spice     
           without overkill.
200 - They were nice to let me try this on a fry... way WAY too hot for me.
400 - no thanks after the taste of 200 and the pain it put me through would have me     
          never try this. 

Good overall will have to try the other contenders but would come back again because this was good chicken... even with the wait.
Awesome! LOVE the pulled pork nachos! I get them every time. And the staff and owners are the best too!

400 Degrees is my favorite hot chicken joint, and I've had them all multiple times. The location is fantastic (right downtown), the space is nice (food court with quiznos and a couple other places) and the staff is super friendly. The owner, who is there every day, is a wonderful lady who remembers and cares about her customers. Their chicken is made exactly the same, all day, every day. At Prince's and Bolton's, sometimes you catch them on an off day, or their chicken isn't quite the same at some points in the day, but at 400 Degrees it's always consistent. And the chicken itself is delectable. 200 is a perfect level of spice and flavor, but super spicy fans will love the 400 (or even the off the menu 500 if you want a challenge). I live away from Nashville while I'm in college, but every time I come back this is the first place I go.
Depressing. Only one otter per cage, which is horrible for social creatures. Exhibit were dark and depressing. The large tank was over crowded. Only the entrance tunnel was cool when it came to fish.

For a $30 per adult entrance fee, I expected a to see a lot more! I enjoyed seeing what I could but the biggest issues were 1) individuals with massive "broods" (i.e. parents with five kids each and everyone running amok), and 2) Fat people; when the fat bellies block the fish exhibits you should be ashamed. (I'm overweight myself but I know to peek at the fish or penguins and move on; I'm not standing motionless with my fat stomach blocking the view for the rest of the patrons. I wish I could say these issues were minor but they got in the way of almost every exhibit. The bird area was okay and I got to use a feeding stick for an additional charge. I saw a sea otter for 30 seconds and it was cute. I pet a stingray which was cool. I also saw a 24 minute nature movie where small mammals (i.e. Chipmunks and mice) narrowly escaped predators like snakes and owls. It was 3D and pretty neat, I just wish you could see more than one movie per ticket!

SPICY chicken!!!...200 degree chicken is loads of cayenne pepper, 400 degree chicken is habanero.  

Sweet tea was syrupy strong.

This attraction absolutely lives up to its name: you're cast into different environments from around the Western hemisphere.  This is more than an aquarium -- it's a museum of habitats.

I was impressed with the breadth and depth of the exhibits -- they were entertaining, informative, and designed for all ages.  It wasn't just, let's look at the cute penguins (though there's a a nice tank for this), but focuses on learning about places like the Amazon and the local Bayou.

While admission is pricey (and tourism coupons are not accepted on Aquarium + IMAX bundles), it's worth the price for a long afternoon spent in a beautiful facility that deserves the support it receives from customers.

The IMAX is a must-see, particularly the Hurricane on the Bayou movie.  I'll write a separate review just for the IMAX, which is right next door.

This aquarium is not that great. It is small. If you are going to have an underwater tunnel, make it more than 15 ft long. It's so short it gets super crowded and is over in a second. Take a page from the book of the philly aquarium, please. Also- what kind of aquarium doesn't have an octopus?!?! And the final/real reason they get a 2 star rating is that they feature an entire exhibit sponsored by bp, shell and other oil companies that extols the virtues of offshore oil drilling and how the leftover platforms are just so wonderful for restoring the reef habitat and as great for fishing. When I saw that I did a combo eye roll and gag. Seriously?! What self respecting aquarium features this kind of nonsense and teaches it to the hundreds of children that visit daily. Call me old fashioned, but I like my nature conservatories/aquariums/zoos and the like to come with a big ol' helping of environmental/societal responsibility and a side of guilt for not recycling as much as i should and driving my low mpg vehicle there. And I expect  institutions that exist to educate the public about the natural world and promote conservation so future generations can enjoy these same wonders to be sincere.

Now for its more redeeming features- the penguins are awesome, and you can read their names on their wing bands. Shout out to my son's favorite penguin, Sticky! They have a very nice exhibit featuring fish and wildlife native to the Mississippi river and Louisiana.

Made for a nice excursion for the kiddos.  Lots of reviews complain about the price and I do think it's a little high but you're in NOLA- everything is high.  It's really a well done aquarium and my kids enjoyed their time there.  We took our time and didn't rush and were done in about 2 hours

I was in town for a conference and was dying to try some authentic hot chicken, Nashville-style. I read some reviews here and was delighted to see that this place was close to my hotel, about a 20 minute walk from Broadway.

It's located in an area with a lot of empty lots, inside a food court. Kind of nondescript and pedestrian. At first I wondered how good the chicken could be if it's in a food court with a bunch of chains. 

Was I wrong. I had to wait almost an hour, but it was worth it.  I had asked for a quarter leg, but my plate was huge, kind of equivalent to having three pieces fused together.  Being a bit of chicken myself, I asked for the 100 degree chicken. It was delicious, with just a hint of spiciness, well-seasoned and juicy.  The only disappointment were the generic, frozen food aisle fries. 

Hours later, I burped and was reminded of how rich all that seasoning was! It made feel a little queasy but it was worth it.  Now that I'm back in NYC, I'm looking for the same fix but sadly, it looks like we don't have much in the way of hot chicken. The best I could find was the spicy chicken at Popeye's, which was as mild as an old lady.

"GET THE BRISKET!!!!!!" It's  so good you don't need your teeth to chew it. Only need your tongue and the roof of your mouth to mash it into baby food Bar B Que paste. By far the best I've had in a long time. My wife and I will definitely be going back on our next visit to New Orleans.
Had a great time strolling around here. The sea horses exhibit was amazing. So many prego male sea horses with itty bitty pot bellies! The penguins were great too. Huge gift shop. Had fun.

I was fortunate enough to pop in during the Strawberry Festival and they were doing a wine tasting--their Sunset Blush is amazing!  And they were so knowledgable about the tastes and where the grapes came from and what they were called.  Bought a bottle immediately.  They also have all sorts of cute wine-related paraphernalia, like wine and cheese picnic bags and signs that say Cork the Whine.  Super pleasant experience, will definitely return when I'm back in the area.

This is a great activity on hot days. Exhibits change fairly regularly and there's always something fun to see. The new Parakeet Point exhibit is fun too. It's definitely worth a trip if you've never done it before.
Permanently closed, finito.  Trekked all the way from Broadway over here only to find out it ain't no more.   Grrrr.

Calling ahead was a smart choice, our chicken was ready within the time frame that they gave over the phone. And, it was great. I got the 200 degree breast/wing. I am a hot chicken novice, but it's hard for me to imagine how the taste of their chicken could be improved upon. In fact, on taste-of-chicken alone this joint would easily garner 4 stars. Holding it back is the ambiance, which is exactly like that of a food court in a small-town mall. Except, no mall. The chicken had a robust spicy crust - almost caramelized. Delicious, but damn near impossible to eat with the plastic knife and fork they gave us. Next time, take out. Steer clear of the wings, they are TINY, little more than skin, spice and grease - yeeech!

Disclaimer: I have not tried any other hot chicken places in Nashville.

But, I do love me some fried chicken and the fried chicken they serve up at 400 Degrees is pretty darn good.

Location: randomly placed in a food court right outside of downtown, the location was clean and basically empty when we went there on Saturday for lunch.

Service: the lady who served us was sweeter than the tea we ordered. She knowingly joked with me when I came in to verify my order, "Just a 100 and a 200 huh? No 400 today?" Seeing the stroller, she asked how our baby was doing. She asked how the chicken was and if we needed anything else. She said thank you as we left the restaurant. And, to top it all off, she threw in an extra wing for me! Who doesn't like free stuff!?

Chicken: the chicken itself was delicious. Moist, tender and flavorful. Their breading created, in my mind, the perfect "chicken-skin-crust." They cook it to order, so call ahead. We called about 15 minutes ahead and still had a good 10 minutes to wait before our food came. Since it was cooked to order, it was piping hot when it arrived at our tables (I think this added to the beads of sweat and runny nose we both experienced as we tore into our food.)

Hotness: my wife ordered the 100 degree thigh quarter and I ordered the 200 degree thigh quarter. My wife, who enjoys spicy food but can't handle it, said her chicken was the perfect level of spiciness. Just a tad bit past her comfort level. My chicken was also the perfect level of spiciness. Not so spicy that I couldn't finish it, but spicy enough that by the end of the meal I was sweating and my nose was running.

Overall, while the extras were forgettable (the fries were typical, frozen fries sprinkled with a bit of their hot seasoning and their sweet tea was way too sweet), the service and the chicken were excellent. I hope that someone takes up their franchising opportunities and opens a 400 degrees here in Louisville!

My daughter kept telling me this aquarium was boring and I kept  brushing off her opinion as that of a  teen that  is hard to impress. Well, she was right. It is kind of boring. They do have cute otters, stingrays to pet, a massive gift shop and some nice exhibits. But, you can easily see everything in under an hour. I still take visiting nieces and nephews there if I get good deals on tickets, but otherwise I don't feel it is a great bang for your buck on a full priced ticket. 

Maybe I am just spoiled by the aquariums of other cities I have lived in... Boston, Monterrey, Corpus Christi.

If you like fish and ocean animals, this is the place for you! If you time it right, you can catch the sting ray feeding in the Aztec tank which was pretty sweet (the workers have a sense of humor too). They also have a parakeet area nearby food court. You can feed the birds for $1.50 which makes for great photos if you're into that. You can also feed the stingrays for $2 if you time it right, but be warned you're going to be holding half a dead fish in your bare hand. Haha. 

Over all it's a cool experience, check it out if you have time. :)

This was my first time here. I ordered the 2 meat platter, 2 ribs = 1 meat and I got Alligator as my second choice. For my sides I got potato salad and baked beans. Ribs were good, I would prefer them to be a little more tender,(I like the meat to fall off the bone) but they were still pretty good. Out of the 3 sauces I like the chipotle the best, sweet coming in second. Both of those went well with the ribs. I liked the mayo based sauce for the alligator. Baked beans were pretty good, they had good flavor. The potato salad had too much mayo for my preference. Boudin was ok, IMO it's hard to find good Boudin in New Orleans, really anywhere east of hwy 49. lol  All in all I enjoyed the food and will be back.

Right off the back. Let me tell you. If you and your family plan on coming here over two or three times.  Please get the membership! The membership includes, the zoo, the aquarium,  and the insectarium.  Kids under 2 get in free. Me and my family went and my son got in free and we still spent over 50 bucks for two tickets. So definitely pricey! Is it worth it? Hmmmmmm???? Yeah. My son was scared of everything at first because this was his first trip but later on he loosened up and I started to see how excited he was becoming everytime we saw a new tank. Lol. It's not ad much stuff as I remembered when I went as a kid, but it was ok still. I was sad at the one alligator they had and small baby frogs that was on display.i think the boat who bit was a good idea, because my son absolutely loved the boat. He really thought he was  on water driving the boat. My son was happy and so was his father. Overall we had a blast! So check it out you guys!!

Nice place for the kiddos. Tons of different  exhibits. The Amazon Rainforest exhibit is really fascinating and makes you feel as if you're actually in the Amazon Rainforest. It can definitely get crowded between 12-3. There's also a stingray pool where you can actually gently touch them. The kiddos love it. The souvenir shop is nice and big, of course prices vary.

It's in a food court type of area, but don't let that fool you! Everyone working here is super friendly and they begin frying your chicken once you order...fresh! They periodically checked up on us to make sure we were still alive.

Pick your level of spice, from a wimpy 0 to a daredevil 400. I myself did not want to end up feeling the singe pass through body parts other than my tongue so I chose 200 degrees. Little did I know I'd be sitting here writing this review while my stomach emits a constant surge of heat to remind me that this might burn going out as much as it did going in.

The chicken sandwich is hot and huge, deep fried southern style and the spice comes from a dry seasoning as opposed to a wet sauce. Ordering the breast gives you a quarter chicken, with the breast and a wing attached, bone in. It sits on two pieces of bread that quickly soak up the spicy grease below.

My recommended weapons to become a victor in this battle: cole slaw, potato salad, and extra bread.
Was nice but was smaller than I expected. The pass that includes the insectarium, aquarium and zoo is worth it

My family and I walked a mile to eat here. We are on spring break. It says you close at 7 (which is early for Nashville anyways). We walked in at 6:15 and were rudely told that they weren't taking anymore orders. Terrible service. Times aren't even right on Yelp. Terrible.
Love it. I think it is better than the one in San Antonio. The hostess for the shark tank was very informative. Friendly staff.

We came in on a rainy Sunday afternoon for my mother in laws birthday and despite being the only people in the tasting room, had a lovely time! Our guide for the afternoon, Lindsay, was fantastic and really helped up make the afternoon really special for her. The Apple wine had us begging for fall to be here and we picked up some of the blush hoping that summer would be here sooner. They had us use plastic cups since their dishwasher was broken and didn't have any snacks but all good because we went out for a great dinner. Well be back!

Haven't been to the Aquarium of the Americas since before Katrina.. so I don't know how it is now. It was my favorite aquarium of all the aquariums in the US I'd seen so far, and I hope they can build up to what they previously had and more. 

I remembered that some of my favorite things about this aquarium included: the display of sea life by the body of water they came from, the water tunnel, the piranha tank right by the boa, the concave glass on the great white shark exhibit, and the albino alligator staring blankly as it sits around with a black alligator.

I hope to go back again someday, if I ever go back to New Orleans. I had great memories there.

While keeping in mind that this aquarium is in New Orleans and I have indeed been spoiled by aquariums in bigger coastal cities (e.g. Monterey Bay Aquarium in CA), I was still pretty disappointed by my experience at Audubon. 

Admission is steep though there is a student discount (I paid $21.95 for student admission). 

The animals here appear to be bored out of their minds. The fish and other sea life were not active at all in their enclosures and mostly seemed to be hiding and sleeping. The habitats were quite frankly depressing. For example, the penguin habitat was all concrete and a tiny swimming area. There were just too many penguins in that small of an enclosure and none of them were playing or swimming. There was a boa constrictor in a tank the size of a small car.
