I don't know about you, but if I were a boa constrictor, even if I weren't doing much besides digesting my big ass meal, I might want to uncoil once in awhile. 

The rainforest environment was pretty cool, but nothing particularly exciting. You just couldn't see the creatures very well. 

I get that aquariums might be magical places for small children as there are a number of interactive activities for them to engage in, e.g. the touch-the-sting-ray pool, but older children e.g. preteens+ would NOT be impressed by this aquarium. 

Bottom line: the enclosures/habitats are depressing, the animals look depressed, the entrance fee is expensive, the aquarium is not very big, and you could see everything within an hour or so. Unfortunately not worth it in my opinion.

It's true that this aquarium isn't as big as the ones in Chicago or San Francisco...it's in New Orleans, people. Chicago is the 3rd largest city in the US, and SF is the 13th. New Orleans is #50. Having said that, I was surprised at how good this aquarium was. Our toddler loved it. Price is a bit steep at $24 per adult, but if you have the time, the combination Audubon Experience package at $42 per adult is well worth it. It includes admission to the Zoo, Aquarium, IMAX, and Insectarium. These are must dos for kids in New Orleans!

This aquarium provides a great learning experience for both adults and kids, and it was definitely worth the price of admission. If you want to save a little money on admission, go find a brochure on the aquarium at one of the local hotels since they usually contain coupons or some sort of deal to purchase tickets at a discounted rate. The experience is really kid-friendly as the aquarium is set up so that you're able to view the different kinds of sea creatures up close. Things you'll be able to see there include the following:

-The white alligator which people mistakenly refer to as an albino alligator.
-The aquatic tunnel where you can observe different types of sea creatures.
-The Amazon Rainforest area where you can see piranhas, an anaconda, and etc.
-A penguin display where you watch them being fed.
-A pool where you can actually pet a sting ray.
-The Mississippi River exhibit that expounds on the surrounding habitat of the Mississippi.
-An informative section on the land acquired during the Louisiana Purchase.

I wasn't able to check out the Insectarium or the Audubon Zoo. Hopefully I'll be able to check out those two places during my next visit to New Orleans. Hit me!!!

While in New Orleans add on your to do list to snorkel in the Audubon AquariumIn. What a wonderful experience. Desiree and Dan were outstanding. They really informed us about everything we were about to encounter and made things comfortable. My wife wanted no part in this and ended up loving it. A lot of thought was put into this program. Its as easy as showing up with your bathing suit.

400 hundred degrees has that crunch you crave.  
I personally was not captivated by their flavor profile.  I liked the 200 degree flavor more than the 400 flavor.  The 400 heat didn't bother me, but the taste became a little toxic, IMO.
I also felt like the chicken was missing more extensive brining.
Still, this is clearly one of the best places out there, and I'm just nitpicking small details.  It's definitely the best crunch I've had at a hot chicken place, and I thought the flavor was still very good at the 200 level.
Fries were good. Potato salad was fine.  Service was great.
If anything, i wish a lot of money could be dumped into this gem so that they could have the capacity to cook more at one time, and so they could improve their signage, facilities and promotion.

I love the aquarium! (we're members). The exhibits are great. I love the fish, sea horses, penguins, otters, alligator, and discount iMax tickets with our membership. What I dislike are the sometimes hefty crowds, and the lack of dugongs. Seriously, the Sydney Aquarium has dugongs, so that's the 5-star standard.

Get the Audubon Experience combo ticket if you plan to go to more than one of the following (the aquarium, insectarium/butterfly garden, zoo).  It include all 3 and a free movie, to be used in a month.  Costs $45.  

Aquarium is fairly small, but has some nice features including a see-through tunnel, sting ray touch pool, jelly fish, seahorses.  You could probably finish going through in about 3hrs.

Excellent Ribs, Brisket Quesadilla and sweet potato bread! I had the ribs and the meat alone tasted great, it was seasoned well and fresh. Same for the brisket. Not to mention the service was excellent. I am a fan of the sauces as well. I will definitely return.

One of the best aquariums I've ever been too!  Try to go on an "off day" because it can get crowded with kids, ESPECIALLY at the otters and the stingrays. Also, if you do have kiddos, good luck making it out of the gift shop without buying anything, they have several and they are full of fun stuff animals and goodies.

After looking through many places on Yelp, I came across toms auto who were able to take me in as fast as possible. I walked in and was greeted very politely and generously. Tom was able to make a seat for me in the garage so I wouldn't be waiting outside in the cold. They were very accommodating and nice. They offered drinks and snacks several times. They thoroughly checked my car for any leaks or things that needed to be tuned up. I ended up getting an oil change and brakes change because they recommended it. Not only were they friendly about what I need, they didn't pressure me to get this and that to burn a hole in my wallet. They are amazing! Definitely would recommend this to everyone! They love Salus students! I would give them 10 stars if I would. Just give them a call and they will accommodate you as soon as possible!!

We drove from mobile to New Orleans to go to the zoo and aquarium.We loved going to the aquarium but it was extremely packed.
I was disappointed with the 2nd story gift shop when she said they sold the same items down stairs.(I only asked because they didn't carry many 'boyish' items up there.) So I leave the item I wanted for my daughter upstairs to go down stairs and buy it and something for my son instead of two transactions.I get there and find out they did not carry that item (not even in different colors) downstairs.  Of course I did end up buying something else. 
My kids enjoyed it and that is the MOST important thing to me. The staff helped us when we had questions. We will be back again. :)

Kinda small but still packs a punch in terms of diverse fauna. Really enjoyed the walk through, especially since it only takes around two hours to take it all in. The only downfall is the pro oil company rhetoric, completely ignoring the impacts of oil drilling on the gulf and claiming the importance of the habitats that are created on drilling rigs..... Didn't mention what they destroyed to put it there or what happens when things go wrong. Rigs to Reefs is a nice idea but so is duct tape for fixing things... Nice aquarium otherwise; will probably return whenever we get back down south.

What a great aquarium. But heed this tip:  You can wait in line for aquarium tickets, which can take an hour or more, or you can walk to the IMAX theater entrance 300 feet past aquarium entrance. Go inside and buy your aquarium tickets with little to no line, and in air conditioned comfort. Trust me: it's worth the 300 foot walk.
Love the displays...the beautiful fish...the sharks...rays.  Some displays could use a little more information or even maps showing where the fish are from.
Last minute trip for my husband and myself and we had a blast. We purchase the Audubon Experience and enjoyed all the parks. Perfect for true family time!

Excellent barbecue--especially the pulled pork. Great house sauce. Excellent mac n cheese. Prices are reasonable--our dinner for two was $20, which doesn't happen often in NOLA.

Service is prompt--not always the most friendly, but who cares?

I went in with moderate expectations; they did not even meet that. 

It is certainly meant to be for kids. The information, displays, interactive fixtures are all dumbed down to cater to the pediatric population. No display, information or exhibit in there evoked any excitement in me. 

I thought the $21 entry for such an unimpressive size and variety of an exhibit was appalling. Every free museum that I've ever been to in my life has been better than this. I'm sorry that I have to give such a review but they need to improve and end this highway robbery.

Je dois dire que j'ai été déçue par cet aquarium.
En payant 30$ l'entrée, je m'attendais à une expérience sympa, et au final, j'ai été déçue pour plusieurs raisons:
- pas très grand, 2 étages mais on fait vite le tour (j'ai fait le tour en 1h..)
- pas tellement d'espèces d'animaux (tous les poissons et autres présentés étaient plutôt communs selon moi, rien de rare ou d'impressionnant)
- certains animaux dans des petits enclos (ex. les requins et tortues qui tournent en rond dans leur petit aquarium)
- certains animaux en très petites quantités (ex. 1 seule otarie!)
- énormément d'enfants et de groupes scolaires, il y en a partout, ça crie ça court, bref, impossible de profiter du moment
Bref, je ne le recommande pas du tout, à moins que c'est la 1e fois que vous allez dans un aquarium ou que vous voulez faire plaisir à vos enfants!

This is definitely a solid place to get some BBQ in New Orleans.

Being from the south I naturally love me some good BBQ and this place is doing it right. I ordered the brisket sandwich with a side of their mac n' cheese. It wasn't crowded when I dropped in so my food came out pretty quickly. I guess I am just lucky because from what I hear this place is often packed.

I was surpassed how thick the brisket is cut, not saying that is a bad thing, just not something I've had before. They are generous with portion size and I love that they give you the choice of several different sauces, I believe there were 4 on the table and maybe another 1 or 2 hanging out by the beverage area. What's even better than sampling each one is the fact you can use as much as you want if you are like me and like a ton of sauce on your brisket. 

Something else I like was that they also give you the most amazing horseradish sauce in a cup to dip the sandwich in which was creamy and had just the right amount of spiciness. I enjoyed all the different sauces but I have to say the horseradish dipping sauce really stood out for me, granted I was dipping my sandwich that was sauced to the max, so I guess it was a collaborative effort on the part of the sauces.

All in all I enjoyed myself and want to go back here and try the pulled pork soon.

I went to the location in Florissant today. I saw the Marquis for one dozen roses for $12.99 which I thought was a deal. I went in and told Cindy (manager) that I was buying them for a friend that I was having lunch with who is a cancer survivor. She recommended that I choose Pink, which I did, that was an excellent idea I hadn't thought of. Cindy was friendly, cheerful and extremely helpful! I find it pleasurable to do business with businesses that have pleasant people. The roses were beautiful and I will definitely go there for my future floral needs. Thanks Cindy, keep on smiling!

I brought my grandkids ages two and three to the aquarium this past weekend.  I personally loved it, and wish I could've spent more time there, but the attention span of a two and three year old lent us to spending about an hour and a half there. 

The exhibits are wonderful, the volunteers are helpful, and everything is really clean.

We especially loved the parakeet area!  Even without the sticks of food, they were coming right up to us and sitting on our shoulders and climbing all over our clothes!

Here's where I have a couple of issues...

I find it to be ridiculously expensive.  It's just nuts that it's $18.95 for a two year old.  

For me, a two year old, and a three year old, and their mother, it cost $87.50.  I think kids should be broken up by age with 2-5 being $12.95, and 6-12 being $16.95.  I also think they should offer a discount to locals.

After doing some research online, I found that by paying just $65 more, I could've gotten a year long membership to ALL Audubon parks for me, my boyfriend, both of my grandkids.  I feel like this should've been said or upsold at the ticket counter...especially since it was 10 am, and no one was in line behind me.  So instead of upselling me a better deal, I came away disgusted with the prices.

Another issue that I had was that I didn't like how there were machines and opportunities EVERYWHERE that cost even more money.  $1.50 for a stick to feed the birds.  $2 for a photo booth.  $1 for the penny press.  The list goes on.  Thank God my grandkids were too young to ask for these things.

Went there expecting at least decent BBQ but the dry rub was a bit bland. The mac and cheese was cold and the meats had been microwaved. The manager was not apologetic and was even heard complaining in the kitchen. His defense was 'these are the best ribs in the city', yet the place was empty at 7:00pm and it didn't even smell like BBQ. The manager made no attempts to be accommodating.   

I do not recommend.

Come on said Pablo, this is the only one we have not tried,....1 breast medium hot = 200 degrees.  Savage it was or as they say in Heathers, .......'me gently with a chainsaw.  I managed to salvage some chicken without skin and it was still an inferno, Seems like it is the hottest chicken in Nashville - not sure if it is the best chicken but hey does it really matter when you are on fire.  $6 and super nice friendly lady who was the chicken mistress today.  Limited parking outside, It is shared space with Nuvo, Quizno and J Gumbo, so dining in is an option.  Super convenient for convention center attendees when it opens.  Call in 20 minutes ahead of time you need it as it is all cooked fresh to order.  Pablo has just run off to Boltons to get a piece to compare....trouble tonight methinks!

Damn good Hot Chicken.  I think there is some obvious comparisons between all the different hot chicken places in town.  I can say without a doubt I would go here first, before I'd go anywhere else. Why?  First, there is no absurd hour long wait for chicken like at Prince's. Secondly, The woman who owns the place is just a really nice person overall. I think the last time I was at Prince's I just got a surly woman bark at me to order faster.  Lastly, the restaurant is a really convenient drive from where I live ( I love convenience!).  Now, I do acknowledge that it is in a fairly shady part of town, but I really think if you let that stop you from going here that would be a shame.  Try a 400 Breast and see if you agree!

I've only been to the tasting room in Peddler's Village, which was okay. 
If you are in the area, stop in- it's free, after all. 
I am not crazy about the wine, but the store is nice, and it is fun to stop in while strolling around Peddler's Village.

Worth the money! If you're coming as part of a spring break group - call them ahead of time and they'll arrange you as a group and give you a HUGE discount! 

Also - don't miss the parakeet room. It's so adorable and you'll get a great photo opp there as the parakeets land on everyone, so you can have picks of them on your hands or shoulders.

Lastly, splurge $4 and get 4 fishies to feed the stingrays. The feeling is a once-in-a-lifetime experience and the photo lasts just as long. :)

NEVER AGAIN! 

Overpriced. 
Lacks CS skills. 
Been a customer for over 15 years.

NEVER AGAIN!   

Did I say NEVER AGAIN! Go anywhere else.

Ahh yes!! Finally a really good BBQ spot on Magazine, and it's in my neighborhood. I was so excited to see Saucy's move in where Ignatius used to be located, right across the street from one of my favorite restaurants Magasin. I had eaten at Saucy's  when it was located in Metairie because I had a Groupon, but I am not to fond of driving to Metairie for just for dining so I never made the effort to go back. I love BBQ food, and we so need this Uptown. So I got the pulled pork plate which came with two sides, I chose the mac-n-cheese and coleslaw. I had an empty plate when I was done and then I was picking at my son's smoked chicken. I don't know what was better the pork or the chicken. They also had five different sauces to try out, and I like how the labels on each one tells you which meat it goes well with. My favorite was the Southern Sweet. Can't wait to order takeout catering for my Saints parties! Everyone who likes BBQ needs to go to Saucy's and give it some business. I want this one to stay in my neighborhood!!! Oh yeah, and it's BYOB!!

I called All Brands based on excellent Yelp reviews to fix a refrigerator that was freezing all the food.  Frank was a pleasure to work with... nice guy, fair priced and knows his appliances!  I would highly recommend him.

The seahorses and photo booth made this very expensive visit worth it. It's not the best aquarium and not the worst, kinda placing itself into the tourist trap trap.

If you're an eclectic traveler, trying to find all the nifty things to see, do something else unless it's hot as hell or raining (my case). If you have kids or like to hang out at the expensive tourist locales (or just love the hell out of seahorses), hit up the aquarium.

Side note: they have boozey items at the concession, just in case your kids are driving you batty.
Delicious rich smoky pulled pork and great sauces. Yum !!!  Super friendly and helpful staff.

The aquarium itself is amazing, with more exhibits than some other aquariums in the southeast for the ticket price. We did the backstage penguin pass, and it was great; our 6 year old thought it was awesome. Tom, our host for for the backstage penguin pass, went so far above and beyond to make sure the kids had a great experience, and he was a fountain of penguin information.

Fun little BBQ joint in the middle of a variety of restaurants on that particular section of magazine. I would much rather go there then wait hours on end for Shaya. The place is small and cozy, you walk up to order, but all other aspects of the service are like a sit down place. The sweet waitress brought out food, took or plates and offered us to go containers. 

I ordered the pork and brisket sliders and asparagus, my BF ordered the brisket quesadilla, ribs (you can add to your plate for $2 each) and the goat cheese mac.

Hands down I've never experienced and quesadilla like that before. The brisket melted in your mouth, cheesy and toaster just right. It was hard to focus on my sliders after that!! I preferred the brisket slider over the cochon but once I added that sauce, it also hit the spot. The sides were also above average with the asparagus still a bit crisp and mac oh so creamy. I will definitely be back! 

For 2 people it was $30! Not a bad deal either.

We took the relatively short walk from Broadway.
We had to stop after reading all the great reviews.
WOW I'm so glad we did. If your on the fence about stopping get off and get some great chicken.
I got the 200 degree breast with a side of beans. I like medium hot nothing to crazy.
My first bite my eyes watered and my sinuses opened just like the sign said.
Now I'm thinking I'm in trouble. I told my self take it one bite at a time. 
Well I finished it all without a drink of any kind.
My wife got the 0 degree with a side of Cole slaw.
She loved it and typically will not eat fried chicken.
This place is a must stop!
Next time we are in town we will stop in.
A little secret they have a 500 and 800 degree not listed on the menu.

This is a Nice family oriented must go to aquarium in NOLA. The lines are long but move rather quickly. While standing in line for tickets a gentleman walked over to our family and gave us a free admission ticket (super thankful). There's a lot to see in such small space. The Natchez boat tour is right in front to catch and ride on the lake. Parking is easy and not far at all from the aquarium. My kiddo enjoyed the fish, the learning and overall. Experience I'm sure he'll never forget ;)! They even have a sting ray petting line ;)!

Nice aquarium with interesting exhibits. Very crowded and swarming with kids. It was filled with families and lots and lots of kids running around.  Makes it difficult to see the aquariums and take pictures. It was a Sunday afternoon.

Just the best game in town. The 200 degree is the perfect heat for fans of the genre. Haven't tried the 400 but will give it a go soon.  There is something so loving about the women who run this joint...they clearly put that extra love into each plate. While I wish they had a better location, there's something about the food court that makes it communal and less trendy. The food is what makes this place...period.

A good rainy day activity for travelers and locals alike. The aquarium offers the usual scene of wild children and frantic parents, especially for the screenings of special movie showings, which are an additional cost. Oh yeah, the animals are pretty cool, too. 

Be sure to check for coupons or get a membership if you're local, this will save you quite a bit.
Kind of a gloomy place to eat a meal in but the food was just fine.
Great BBQ. Had a bangin' brisket quesadilla. I've been to their food truck on 2 separate occasions and each time I left wanting more.

I love aquariums.  The New Orleans Aquarium is not as big or as flashy as some other aquariums that I've been to lately (Baltimore, Atlanta), but it does have some pretty solid exhibits.  

There are penguins.  There are sea otters (!!!! my favorite!!!!).  There are sting ray and shark petting pools.  There is an albino alligator (so spooky!).  And at the very end, there is a GIANT floor to ceiling tank with sharks and rays and fishes and even a giant turtle!

This aquarium is smaller than others, but also slightly cheaper.  (I think I paid $16 with a AAA discount?)  I spent about an hour and a half there.  It probably would have been longer but it was field trip day and I had my fill of the dozens of rambunctious kids excited to be out of school for the day (hey, I can't blame them).

If you like aquariums and realize this isn't the biggest, bestest aquarium in the world, I think you'll enjoy it.
I enjoyed my "home cooked" feel to the food I ate. It was great fried chicken and definatley worth the wait! Call ahead if you don't have the time to invest waiting.

Over the past two years I have made several purchases at Apex to outfit my home wood shop. Everything I have purchased has been fairly priced, sometimes well under internet pricing. On one large purchase they even delivered the items to my home for no additional charge!

Contrary to the reviewer who stated that she was not greeted when she walked into the establishment, I have found just the opposite. I sometimes feel like Norm walking into Cheers. I always get multiple staff personnel saying hello or asking if I needed assistance. 

Don't be sexist about the females working there. They know their stuff!

This is a great store with that "old time" feel.

We had high hopes for the aquarium...our 3 year old loves zoos and aquariums so we made the stop. 
We were a little unnerved immediately when there was a mass gaggle of people waiting to cross an active railroad....with a train on it....with no guard, bars, anything. As folks were waiting for the train to pass, the trolley appeared and it left folks stuck between the tracks for the trolley and the tracks for the train. For a location tailored to families this is dangerous and stupid. 

For the aquarium itself, admission was steep and the aquarium itself was average. Biggest issue was the complete overcrowding...some exhibits were just too packed to even get to. Whatever the capacity limit is, it needs to be reduced by a lot. People waiting to get in is better than people paying a lot of money and being unable to see all that they paid for. 

There were some good exhibits and the aquarium validates your parking ticket for $5 off. 

Unless it's a weekday in the dead of winter we probably won't be back. 

High hopes quashed....
Great food for good prices!!! I ate here two days in a row in NOLA where great food is everywhere so you know I liked it A LOT!!!

We enjoyed be aquarium and it was a nice way to get out of the heat. It's smaller than expected, but still enjoyable. I don't think it would be worth going to on it's own, but we did the tickets that also let you into the zoo and insectarium, so that was well worth it. I would definitely encourage you to get that pass and check out the aquarium during the heat of the day as a good escape. We only spent a few hours at the aquarium (compared to the entire day at the zoo). We took our time and saw everything. 

My son loved seeing the green anaconda. I enjoyed watching the penguin feeding.

If I could give no stars and still write a review then I would...I went to pick my flowers up for my wedding to find out they were the wrong color.  I asked for orange gerbera daisies and received mostly red gerbera daisies. My wedding colors were orange and purple.  My bouquet had the correct color of daisies and the groom's and groomsmen boutonnieres were correct.  However, all of the bridesmaid's bouquets were red.  I asked the girl working, Ashley, to call the manager, whom was at home, and she did.  While on the phone I asked why my flowers were not correct the manager stated "Amanda left us high and dry".  I then asked again why my flowers were not correct when the had my order form and everything said orange. She then stated "I have been sick and haven't been there to oversee anything"  I then asked what they were going to do to fix this huge mistake.  I was very upset at this point as my wedding was in two hours and not only were the bouquets the wrong colors, but the bouquets and the boutonnieres did not even match (and one of the 7  boutonnieres was already withering).  I then asked for a refund and was told I had two options: 1) I could have half of my money back and take the flowers as is or 2) I could take a whole refund and leave without any flowers.  I chose option 1 with it being 2 hours before my wedding and having no other options for flowers by then.  I was then told that since I had paid cash that they would have to cut me a check.  I refused a check and stated I wanted cash as I paid cash.  And due to how rude the managers/owners were being I was afraid to take a check from them or wait on a check from them.  I was then told I needed to wait an hour for the manager to drive there from home to bring cash.  I chose to wait.  While waiting 2 police cars came flying into the parking lot and 2 officers came into the store, because they had a call about a disturbance at that location.  When I and their employee explained what was going on they left laughing. I never threatened them, their employee, or their store.  I just wanted a huge problem fixed.  During all this time I was told "you are trying to take advantage of a mistake", "no one will notice, just take your flowers", and "I feel sorry for the person that is marrying you."  This all on my wedding day. Thanks Flowerama for making my day memorable.
My wife loves shopping here.  They have a great selection and very good customer service.  Haven't been open long but I hope they do well and are a great addition to the business community of Reno.
I love this place. The best hot chicken try it out you will love it my fav is the fries it's to die for

LOVED the hot chicken here, just wish I had ordered it hotter!!

We were a bit shaded out by the location but ever since we'd heard about how awesome it is we decided to come anyway.  The place is a serious hole-in-the-wall but so worth it.  We were greeted when we walked in by a really nice lady behind the counter.  She asked how we'd heard about the place & was genuinely happy we'd come in.  Great start!  We ordered a leg quarter and a breast, and after much persuasion from the people working there, we went with 100 degrees.  Not really that spicy at all but still very very good.  We doctored it up with some hot sauce, and we know next time to at least go for the 200.  They make it fresh when you walk in the door & order so if you call ahead it can be ready for you.  Us first-timers know that now for next time!  It was a very small eating area, maybe enough for 6 people, but we ended up eating there anyway.  We had the fries & slaw as our sides which were nothing crazy but still good.

Overall I'd have to say our experience was great.  We will certainly go back again when we get the hankerin' for some hot chicken (and we will call ahead too!).  By the way, THEY DO NOT TAKE CARDS.  You either need cash or check.

With the help of this extraordinary staff (especially Nina), I was able to pull off the perfect proposal to my now fiancee. They went above and beyond to meet my requests and never gave me any pushback. We will certainly be back to visit and we cannot thank them enough for their amazing service!
Easily the best barbecue in New Orleans.  Friendly, local owners, great service, and a very comfortable room.  The house sauce is my favorite - kinda tangy, not cloying.

I took my mother yesterday cause we didn't have anything better to do. I wish we had just stuck with our original destination [which we still visited, NOAAM]. This place is highly overpriced and NOT very big. I'm sure if I were 12 again it would've been the most awesome experience ever but alas that was NOT the case. The best part was the 10:30a dive show with the stingrays when you immediately enter on the right, other than that I wasn't to impressed but then again I am used to the Camden aquarium in NJ which is twice as big!

This is a very nice aquarium.  It is sectioned off into about six different exhibits concentrating on those regions of the world.  I think the most popular areas are the rain forest and the Louisiana Swamp area.  Well, those were at least my favorite.

The cost is about $18 for an adult.  It is best to get the IMAX combo for $23.  The aquarium is not really that big.  I think it is average in comparison to some of the others I have been to.  They do seem to have a lot of little gift shops and fast food areas.  maybe just a little too much?  

They also have an area for kids to play and touch the Sting Rays.  

If you come out to New Orleans, it is worth a little walk down by the river and take in a relaxing and informative tour of this place...and no, you can not bring in your beer!
people here are so friendly and helpful. beware of Kohl's online and customer service over the phone. but this store is great.

Great food. Friendly staff. It's so clean and you can see your food being prepared right before you. It's not necessary to bad mouth another Hot Chicken place to convey how great 400 Degrees is. Just go, ok?

Continuing on my trail of the best 25 sandwiches in Nashville per "TheCityPaper", I ordered the Hot Pork Chop Sandwich and it... well, it was.  It existed.  It wasn't bad, though it wasn't really that special either.  Of course, you have to deal with the nasty white bread since nobody in the city will toast it for you, but I suppose that is just part of the experience.  All in all, it was worth it to try it but nothing special and I won't be returning.

Staff was nice enough, but the restaurant is inside a building with a slew of other eateries kind of like a trucker stop or mall cafeteria -- very odd.

I absolutely love this aquarium. It was a unique treat to spend an afternoon watching seahorses otters and penguins. 

On a rainy day, I expected to see many people in front of each aquarium site. It is so well spread out that it wasn't overcrowded. 

Each and every area was well worked out. 

I want to go again and show my friends the highlights.

We chose Saucy's to cater an informal retirement function in May 2016.  Rich was very flexible with our order,  making it easy to accomodate various tastes.  He delivered and help set up the food.  Everyone thoroughly enjoyed the meal.  That Goat Cheese Mac was the big hit, but that does not take away from everything else.  Would recommend for functions or family dinner!  Thanks RICH, you were awesome.

Had a great time with my family, awesome atmosphere and our favorite parts were walking through the amazon rainforest and the giant shark tank. The sea otters are so playful and cute, they even responded to my wife and were reacting to her motions on the tank. She wants a sea otter now lol. The staff at the sting rays where you can feed and pet were very nice!

Only bad part was the food court closes way earlier than the actual aquarium so when we went to grab ice cream before having to leave everything was totally shut down, a bit early in our opinion there was still at least 45 min before the aquarium actually closed.

Still had a great time and saw amazing tanks with beautiful fish!
The parakeet enclosure was awesome once the birds got hungry; and I don't think anyone got "dropped" on :)

Got there and it was completely packed! But it didn't take long for us to be seated. Down to earth decor. It was pretty warm inside because the door kept opening from customers. The server was new but pretty good overall. I got the brisket sandwich with smoked beans. The brisket was delicious--they have about 5 sauces to choose from. The "Hot"  is what I thought went best with my sandwich. The beans on the other hand were not what I expected. I thought "smoked" beans and baked beans would be essentially the same thing but these beans looked and tasted completely different. I barely finished half. All in all, I liked the experience and I'll probably pay this place another visit!

I love the Aquarium! Now a Audubon member I decided to put my membership to use on a Sunday afternoon. Thank goodness I didn't have to wait in line, because it was super crowded. I feel like the Aquarium (and Zoo) are fun for children and adults alike!

Check out the school of clown fish, they are my favorite. The Seahorse exhibits are pretty cool too. They have a whole exhibit dedicated to Louisiana sea life. There is also an 16 year old anaconda in the Amazon exhibit. That snake is a beast.

Located on the riverfront of the Mighty Mississippi the Aquarium is easily accessible. Take the ferry from Algiers Point, the Canal St. streetcar, or there are many parking lots in walking distance

This is a fairly small aquarium, and although kind of interesting, very overpriced for an underwhelming experience. We arrived on a Thursday morning around 11am and thought we would be able to spend all afternoon there. Unfortunately, even after taking our time at each exhibit, reading just about every info plaque and staying for a presentation/feeding at the large fish area, it only took us about 2 hours - and that was with 2 kids in tow. Additionally, some of the exhibits were kind of sad with very few animals/fish. Not a bad experience, but I've been to much better aquariums.

this was good BBQ, but nothing incredible. we were in NOLA on vacation and this spot came extremely highly recommended by someone - we took a streetcar all the way here (40 minutes) and weren't over-the-moon impressed. just decently. good flavor, good quantity, just okay value though.

Wicked hot y'all! I really like certain dishes (like Thai or Vietnamese) to be spicy, but can't seem to handle this place's medium hotness of 200!?! I'm not worthy, I'm SO not worthy (bowing). LUV that everything's homemade there, and it's really worth the wait!

I'm a saltwater tank enthusiast and try to hit up aquariums in city's that have them. This one rates right up with the best of them. Plenty of things to see from fresh to saltwater. It's a little pricey at $21, but so are the rest of the aquariums.

For someone who loves aquariums. This was nothing special. For military discount it was a whole $3 per adult and $2 for kids. So a total of $45 for my and my 3 year old.... definitely not worth the money at all!! Made it through the whole thing in roughly an hour. Food was too over priced and if you can imagine so was the gift shop.

Really cool aquarium. I have been to many, and this is one of my new favorites. They have some really cool and different species from east-coast aquariums (ex: both salt and freshwater). Coolest stuff: shark tank, green anaconda, piranhas, otters, penguins, electric eels, tons of sea horses, the list goes on... Really great layout, so you don't need a map to do a complete walk through. Enthusiastic and friendly employees are all throughout with fossils, bones, and ready to answer any questions. The cost is high BUT typical for aquariums ($25 to $30 for adults). If you gradually walk through, read some signs, see some feedings, and enjoy yourself, it takes about 2 hours.
Always delicious better than the other local "hot" chicken. Staff and food make this place.

Drinking with our kids? Drinking while shopping? Umm, yea, go ahead and count us in! Although the actual winery has been on our list for quite sometime, we had never made it up there....yet. (Yoga in the vineyard sounds incredible and just my style! They also host other awesome events! Go on their site to check it out!) 

We were so happy to find out there's a tasting room right in the middle of Peddler's Village when we were visiting! Thanks Ma! Genius! 

The tasting room was a nice place duck away from the crowds and warm up for a bit when we first visited during The Village's Grand Illumination night. The store was decorated festively and there was much cheer in the air. It was a nice environment!

We were welcomed warmly upon entering and  the staff was every helpful when I was picking up a few bottles for my mother. They informed me their spring wine is made in season and once it sells out, it's gone. 

The tastings are priced a smidge higher than I'm used to on Senaca Wine trail, but lower than that of Napa and Sonoma. 

Traditional tastings are $8 and include one of the each varieties Chaddsford offers. There are also Sweet Flight ($8), Dry White Flight ($10), Dry Red Flight ($12) and the Reserve Flight ($14) which allows you to taste premium wines from the small-batch Artisan Series. 

All tastings can be done as walk ins, but I would call if you have a larger party. 

This winery is very well known and offers some of the area's most recognized and acclaimed wines.

I love that they offer deals the more bottle you purchase! I was able to stock up for the holidays and save! 

Doesn't miss Half-Price Wine Tastings (all day Thursdays) and Half-Price Wine by the Glass (all day Thursdays) which is only offered at the tasting room, not at the winery. 
 
Nice addition to the area and super smart too!  

Look forward to coming back on a warmer day when we could stroll the area more leisurely and even sit inside at one of their tables! Love that it's kid-friendly!

Bought our tickets on our mobile phones, and they didn't even look at them to let us in, just waved us through! Definitely skip the line and buy your ticket online.

The aquarium was very crowded, but we did go on a Sunday afternoon when it was raining outside. Defintely take your time walking through, give yourself an hour and a half to two hours to see everything.

The walk through tank was pretty cool. I also liked the jelly fish.

The penguin exhibit was nice, they are very engaged with the visitors and will follow you through the glass.

The very last attraction is the tank with the sharks, including a see-through section of the floor to look down on the tank.

Feel like I am cheating on my 1st aquarium love in Monterey, Ca. I liked this place better than Monterey...
To be fair- this place attempts to cover habitats for the Americas as a whole rather than the limited experience of the Monterey aquarium in which the Monterey bay itself is generally the sole star ( except when the animals themselves extend into a larger Pacific area)
Happily they had the sea otters I love - but so very much more. Great IMAX theater- mmm weekdays expect hordes of school kids. Torn on this- fun to watch them- but like 100 at a time? Can you say loud? Just saying- maybe Tuesday at 10 am was not the best time if that is a consideration for you. Otherwise- great place

Great aquarium.  It is expensive and gets really packed to the point of being difficult to walk around in.  That aside it has lots of great displays.   From jellyfish, seahorses, sharks, sea turtles, stingrays etc.  I found it amusing that so many displays there were sponsored by BP and the natural gas companies that are the ones threatening the very existence of the creatures they are pretending to be benign advocates of, and posting "information" (advertising) on the walls trying to have people believe that they do an important and necessary job that doesn't endanger wildlife despite their massive oil spills.  That happen much more often than media will inform you of.  Come visit!  Just don't believe the hype.

Not one of the most memorable aquariums that I have been to.  It's kind of expensive, considering how small it is.  Don't expect to spend more than 2 hours here.  When we got back to the entrance (place leads you in a circle), we were like, "that's it???"  It seriously took us only an hour to go through the place, and we're the type to actually stop, read the info, and enjoy the animals.  I won't undermine the good things they had to offer though.  The albino croc/alligator/whatever was fat and lazy, but that was hilarious in itself.  I loved him!  The jellyfish are worth a look- esp the upside down jellyfish.  Finally, the giant viewing tank at the end was awesome.  There was a nurse shark (I believe) that gave me the creeps.  It was pretty ferocious looking with those jagged teeth.  Overall, the aquarium is worth a visit, but don't plan your day around it.

Stopped in for a brisket sandwich when McClures was out and it was pretty good. The slaw I found to be just ok. I do like their slaw selection. Overall I still prefer McClures but this is a good backup.

Took my cousin from Kansas try 400 degree hot chicken today since it was featured on the travel channel.  I'll have to say the chicken was moist, full of flavor and hot! Haha  everything was made fresh from the time you order!!! Go check out 400 degrees hot chicken . You won't be disappointed!! Thanks so much for the hospitality Aqui ! I will definitely return when I'm in the neighborhood! So good!!

Ok here it goes...

I am NOT a huge fan of Fried Wings I like mine more traditional style, BUT I went to 400 Degrees and wanted the full experience so I got the 400 Degrees Leg Quarter (Yes Leg Quarter) Potato Salad and Bread for 7.50 (Great Price) 

Within the first Bite I KNOW I am a LIFELONG Customer. AWESOME customer service! 

VERY Spicy but not to salty and still flavorful. There is nothing worse then spicy food that is spicy just to be spicy and not favorable

Really good Chicken and the 400 is a REALLY good flavor for spicy eaters if you dont eat spicy 3-4 times a week stick with the 200 its delicious as well 

Only down side is its in a food court so its a little hard to find but once your in its pretty nice. Takes about 20 mins so call your order in to save time!

I really liked Saucy's. The joint probably ranks just a tiny bit higher but Saucy's is much closer to where I live and I absolutely loved their Carolina pulled pork. It's served with pickles and red onion which may be a little out of the ordinary but it works. Great mac and cheese too :)

For what you get, it's pricey.  Coming from the Pacific Northwest,  I have seen more than my fare share of aquariums, this was one of the smallest with the largest price tag. 
That being said it was a pleasant enough experience, I would totally recommend stopping by if you have the time. The exhibits were nice and the staff was friendly.

This is a nice aquarium but I found it to be really small. The little one liked it but we have been to much better ones. For the price you don't get what you pay for. 
Nice but not NOT great.
Another enjoyable trip to the aquarium. Some things haven't changed since I was a kid. Love the jellyfish and the huge 400,000 thousand gallon tank. I could sit there and watch it all day!

It was freezing cold outside. And this was a great option for the kids. The most unique and attractive part of this aquarium is the seahorse area. Truly worth seeing. Admission is a bit expensive (look for a coupon) but it does include admission to a 3D theater with several features to choose from. Also unique, it offers the opportunity to book feeding or snorkeling within some exhibits for extra cost. I had not seen that offered from other aquariums. 

The entrance is quite impressive, through a clear tunnel surrounded by, among others, rays that fly all over the place. A nice immersive experience. 

There is also a larger exhibit with larger species from the Gulf of Mexico. It includes some seating area for taking a long break and relaxing by looking at the large display.
Very nice aquarium. Gulf of Mexico tank is huge with lots of sharks. Pet the stingrays. Loved it all!

Our family drove through here while on vacation this summer and LOVED it! Being from the south were picky about out BBQ but this place was better than we hoped for! Found it on Yelp and so glad we came here. Family agrees this will have to be on the list of future stops! :)

This aquarium must really be seen as part of the package deal they try to sell you. It's expensive at $21. But if you add the "Audubon Experience" for only $14 more, you'll get access to the Audubon Zoo, Aquarium, IMAX Theater and Insectarium. Your still paying a good amount ($35), but you also have a days worth of activities. It's a bargain when you consider that your only paying under $9 per attraction when bought together. 

I would recommend you check it out only if buying the "Audubon Experience" pass or you desperately need to get out of the rain. Be warned though, if going on a rainy day, it WILL be packed with like minded folk also wanting to take cover from the rain. The aquarium has narroow halls as it is so visiting on a rainy day will  be crowded.

This is only for the Behind the scene Penguin experience. It was the best thing ever. Super cute and friendly!!! It was worth every penny. I forgot how much we paid, but I think it was $150 a person. 

You don't go in at the main entrance, but to the side where the movie theater is. A guide comes get you. I think they only allow 6 people max for the penguin, but we had 5 total in our group. 

You get to see how they prep the food, feed the penguins, and how they prep their medicine. Then you go into a room with one penguin roaming around freely. They tell you about how they live, eat, etc.....You get to pet it and only get to hold it IF they come to you. You can't force it. Only my friend got to hold the penguin cuz she jumped on her lap. We took many pictures and also you get to have a special painting afterwards. 

The best part was that you get to go into their home and feed all the penguins. It was a bit weird having everyone from the outside watch you. There are so many of them and they are all so cute. I wouldn't wear flip flops like I did because it does get very wet and there is a lot of poop. It was over 2 hours of great fun and you should do this soon. I heard they are remodeling the penguin tank soon, so not sure if they will still offer the behind the scenes. 

The guides were so friendly and informative. Great job!

The aquarium itself is small, but there is a lot to see for the size. Also it's super super packed. Can barley walk though.

My wife and myself had been here before. We went to peddlers village today to specifically go here. What a waste of time. We went for the flights. The woman at the bar was not the friendliest we've encountered. Last time we had really great flights. They had plastic glasses 2oz pour. Felt more like one. The flight felt more like a tasting. When asked she was very rude. The dish washer was broke. Oh well close or offer a discount. Who drinks wine from a plastic cup. What is this a picnic? Very sad. Was a go to for us.
Excellent ribs and sauce. Sweet and spicy vinegar slaw was good too. I will return next chance I get.

Ok - a dude from work suggested this place and simply told me: 'Get ready to get your taste buds burnt off.'  Wasn't too far from the truth.

For anyone who loves hot, fried chicken - this is the spot to go to in Nashville.  If you are in a hurry - call ahead with your order as nothing is pre-made.  Took us about 20 minutes to get our food - but worth the wait.  Oh yeah - it's cash only too.

The menu is quite simple - tell the people chicken or pork (may be more options I'm not sure) and hotness factor: 100, 200, or 400.  The portions are big, the fries are, well, fries, and the piece of bread they give you could cause a normal man to have a heart attack with the amount of hot goodness soaked into it.

Only negative thing about this place I could find is no A/C, but if you require A/C you are probably a wimp anyway and shouldn't eat here.
It seem overpriced, but the exhibits were nice. I wouldn't go back ,nothing unique. They did have a stingray petting pool. And a pare knee area. The penguins are also nice.

DONT WASTE YOUR MONEY. I have been to the aquarium in Atlanta, Baltimore and now here. It took about 20 mins to walk around the whole place. Waste of money and the main attraction which usually displays a ton of giant fish was limited to one small/medium shark and one sea turtle. Most exhibits have a dolphin show or two giant whales.

Excellent 
1st try at Hot Chicken 
This was GOOD!
Start off easy...mild def has flavor.
Medium was good for me, plenty of heat.
Hottt was lip-burning hot!

I'd forgotten how much fun these trails can be on a Mountain Bike!

Good rules of thumb:
1) Bring plenty of water!
2) Print out a map of the trail loops, understanding that they aren't to scale, but good use for reference.  
3) Bring a cheap comb and pliers for the inevitable invasion of cactus spines (in your tires and sometimes your face, ask me how I know)
4) Obey the one way only signs, please!  Some people think it's cool to ride it in reverse- not only can it be dangerous but it tears up the trails.

There are two spots to park and enter Fantasy Island.  The main trail head is at Harrison and Irvington- take Harrison south until it dead-ends at Irvington and there's a small paved lot for the riders.  Tip: try not to leave any valuables in your car- take your cell phone, etc with you.  There have been break-ins here, consider yourself warned!

The other entrance is off of Valencia, on the south side of the park.  The pullout is a dirt lot but the entrance is fairly easy to spot.  This will put you on the Bunny Loop and there isn't a map of the entire park at the trail head, so again, a map is a good idea.

This is officially State Trust land, so technically you need a permit (google AZ state trust land permit, you'll find instructions on how to obtain one).  While not strictly enforced, the money from the permits does go to upkeep of FI.

There are several large loops: Lone Cactus, Christmas Tree, Bo's, Burro, Bunny Loop, to name a few.  The trails are mainly flat single track with a few technical sections of steep washes, etc.  There are tons of Easter egg "garbifacts" out there too. 

There are about 26 miles of trails, most  loops are on the map that's located at the trail head, some aren't (Rez, Fire, Bunny, Snake Dance, Bunny's Revenge).  Basically, if you keep taking all of the right-hand options at the turnoffs you'll do all of them.  Some trail heads are well-marked, some aren't, another good reason to tuck a printed sheet of the map in your CamelBak.

A quick review of the loops with which I'm familiar:

Lone Cactus Loop: The Main Loop of Fantasy Island.  It's about 7 miles and has some steep sections right off the bat.  Windy and fast, it's a lot of fun if you can hold your line.  There's a really fun section toward the end called the Half-Pipe which is seriously a natural half-pipe in a small ravine.  Stay to the left and you'll follow it just fine!

Bunny Loop: Exactly as it sounds.  Flat and fast singletrack, but beware of the ever encroaching Cholla cacti on this loop.  

Snake Dance: This is a FUN loop if you're into really fast and tight corners.  

Bunny's Revenge: A combination of Bunny and Snake Dance.  This one has a lot of fun downhill sections that aren't technical.

Christmas Tree Loop: You'll know when you're on Christmas Tree Loop, trust me.      It's similar to Lone Cactus with fun decorations.  :)

Burro Pit Loop: Contains the smaller off-shoot loop of the Dead Cow Loop.  This, in my opinion, is the most technical of all the loops.  There are some features like The Shaft (it looks exactly like it sounds- steep and really fast!) and the Over-Under, a cool obstacle that you ride over, loop around, then ride under in a little tunnel.  You'll know when you enter the Dead Cow Loop- be sure to ring the bell for good luck!

Overall- plan on being out there for a few hours and if you're riding at dusk/dawn, bring a light.  A ton of tun and great exercise!

My husband and I stumbled upon 400 Degrees last Saturday afternoon after trying (and failing) to get a table at The Pharmacy. It can be a little confusing to find this place since it's in a food-court style building with a couple other restaurants. 

When we got there, there was no one in line. The lady at the counter was super nice and helpful, and explained the different levels of hotness to us. I got the 100 degree tenders with fries, and my husband got the 200 degree tenders with fries. We waited about 30 minutes for our food, but that's because they make it from scratch after you order. We thought the chicken was delicious, and you definitely get a lot for your money. The 3 tenders were served with 2 slices of bread and pickles. We easily could have shared an order of fries, instead of each getting our own.

We'll definitely be back if we're in the area!

A good way to spend an afternoon, especially if you have visitors in town.

Here's a tip that will save you 20 minutes if it's crowded: There are actually two entrances, the main one coming from the Uptown/Riverwalk shopping area side and a second smaller one by the Imax theater about 300 feet past the first (further toward the French quarter). However, even if you're not going to see a movie you can buy just a ticket for the aquarium at the IMAX entrance and walk back to the first, skipping the horrific lines that form by the main entrance. I don't know why there isn't a sign pointing this out.

Amazing hot chicken! Did have to wait around a half hour until it was ready, but well worth the wait! The staff was so friendly and seemed genuinely interested to make conversation. Next time I'm in Nashville, this is sure to be a stop!

We had the 200 & 400 degree chicken strips! Very tasty and piping hot right out of the grease!! The potato salad and Cole Slaw were over the top! Someone from our hotel recommended the place and glad she did!

My fiancée and I decided to visit the aquarium after hearing about it from a passenger on the airplane. 

We probably wouldn't normally have chosen to take one in but we were glad we did. They had some great exhibits, our favourites including: the shark tank with a giant turtle, also a white alligator exhibit and the stingray petting tank. It was a great thing to do to escape from the afternoon heat and was well worth the price of admission. The only thing I would have hoped for was more fish, reptiles and amphibians from the Louisiana area.

First time coming to NOLA this place showed up as no. 2 on the list for BBQ Chicken search. No reason to not give 5 stars considering I enjoyed the service provided and everything I ate except the Mac & Cheese.
Even though the smoked beans weren't traditional BBQ baked beans because they have four different types of beans versus one, they were still really good. I enjoyed both the chipotle BBQ sauce and the sweet BBQ sauce. 
The sweet tea wasn't bad but wasn't what I would consider traditional "southern" sweet tea. I'm not sure what sweetener they used and I'm not going to guess but it didn't taste like pure sugar cane. 

*Added Bonus* They offer a military discount to our service members. Thank you!

I've been pretty impressed with this place.

First things out of the way, I really don't care where a place is located or what it looks like unless it is clean and has delicious food.  This place does have delicious food and got a 95 on their health inspection rating.  So both criteria are met there.

Now to the good stuff, the chicken.  It is juicy and very flavorful.  It is clear that they either put it in a spicy brine or marinade prior to cooking, and it makes all the difference.  As for the style of the fried chicken, it comes out crisp with a spicy wet finish on the outside.  I got the 400 degrees level and it was hot, but not enough to make me sweat.  As a matter of fact, I didn't take the first sip of my soda until I was done.  Given that I am spicy freak, this should be plenty hot enough for mortals (for reference, I can eat the spiciest thing Prince's has without batting an eye, I frequently consider using pepper spray as a condiment).  But all in all, damn good fried chicken.

For sides, they have spicy crinkle fries (hit the spot), baked beans (the way they are supposed to be made), cole slaw and potato salad.  As well, they have a couple of random things like a burger(?) and they have fresh cookies for dessert.

Another nice perk about this joint is the people that run it are friendly - great customer service.  So there is another way they have Prince's beat.

Their hours are a little wonky,. 11AM-3PM M-F and 11AM-1AM Saturday.  As well, they only take cash, so make sure you come prepared or you'll be washing dishes.  My wait time was very reasonable, a little less than 20 minutes, and they recommend you call in your order in advance.

The penguins were nice and the rain forest was lush and pretty .  Liked seeing the white alligator .  The otters were cute and got to see them feed .  The facility is small and not very well lit . It only took us about 45 minutes to walk through the exhibits .  It needs more displays and better lighting

A very good attraction to take toddlers and kids to, the Aquarium has lots of good exhibits. Parakeet Pointe was quite interesting, as you can purchase a feed stick for $1.50 and feed the parakeets with it. They fly right to you and nibble off the stick.

The penguins are a lot of fun also. The exhibits are set up to where a toddler can stand on the floor and see the various fish swim around workout needing to be held by parents.

We didn't try the stingray touch pool (I still get nightmares of Steve Irwin).

The souvenir shop could stand to add more clothing options for toddlers, but that's nitpicking on my part.

The cost of admission is kinda high at $23.95, but we took advantage of $2 Tuesday for Louisiana residents. We may consider becoming Audubon members to get a better deal.

It's the aquarium. The reason my review is so low for this is because it's really disappointing. There is only one option when eating here and it's papa johns or Haagen daaz. And of course it's high priced because there are no competing other food places. The outside of the aquarium could be put to better use, picnic tables, maybe covered grassy shade area. But instead it's always cluttered with homeless people from the riverwalk and a wide open space. They should really consider building an outdoor pavilion for families to take a break or just have lunch there. Other than that it's a good place to take the kids for the afternoon on a hot day!
A very nice place . Staff is friendly and helpful. Located in a nice part of town. Only thing we didn't like was how small the food court is. We had to eat standing up. Other than that great time.

With the plethora of Greek, Lebonese, and now Egyptian cuisine in New Orleans you really have to stand out to survive. Torshi does that with charm and great taste. I've only been twice because it's on the other side of town and there are 52 restaurants in a 10-block radius of my house. But whenever I'm in the Saint Claude neighborhood I make it a point to visit Torshi. Not only are the dishes healthy and delicious (so much so that I forgot to take a picture before I enjoyed my meal), they are served with a smile. Plus, the fresh juices are amazing, and they have the largest baklava I have ever seen and I loved it!

When there is a sudden typhoon on the day you were planning all outdoor activities....what else can you do when you have no access to a car? Go to the aquarium next to your hotel!

Expensive, as expected. Not a good as some other aquariums I have been to (Newport near Cincinnati, Atlanta). But for an afternoon of torrential rain, it served it's purpose.

I just wasn't impressed. But then again, I'm comparing to the Baltimore Aquarium which seems to have much more. I didn't see one tank here that I didn't feel was adequate in size. In particular, I remember a tank with these metallic/robot-looking fish that just seemed crowded. They had no way to spread out. Same for many of the jellyfish tanks. Even the tanks with the larger animals such as turtles, sharks, etc weren't that great. And then the penguins...so small! It was a shame.

I now have a need hot chicken place that I truly love, now that I have quit patronizing Princes. The wait isn't dreadfully long. I was able to call in my order without the number being constantly busy. They quote that it will be ready in 20 minutes and when I arrived it was ready! Surprise, Surprise! The location is convenient and less scary. I didn't have to worry about parking or strange men coming on to me. :-) The workers were polite and nice. They even offered small talk.

I have been 3 times since finding out about this place. I have tried both 400 and 200. The 400 is great when you want the hotness. The 200 is more bare able for those who don't like the devil hot 400. I have tried the leg quarter, breast and wings. The only compliant there is the portion size of the wings. If the wings were bigger, that would be heaven. 

Between Pepperfire and 400 Degrees, I am at peace with my hot chicken cravings. 

Thanks 400 Degrees for treating your paying customers with kindness and respect for our time and money.

I will start by giving some overall advice (as I have on all the Audubon Nature Institutes). If you are planing on going to zoo, aquarium, and Insectarium you need to buy the experience pass!  The price for the three admissions separately would be $53 before tax. With the experience pass it brings it down to $35.. and if you are a student (or a graduate with an old college ID *wink*wink*) you get all three for $19.  Obviously this is what we did!  

We loved walking through the exhibits and seeing the different fish and sea life. The seahorses and jellyfish were cool!  You get to touch sting rays! The walk through hallway and HUGE viewing wall (above and below) to watch the fish and sharks were entertaining.

I did think it was kind of weird that there were birds.. lots of birds  - shouldn't they have been at the zoo?  I don't care about feeding the birds (and getting pooped on) at an aquarium.. I want to feed and touch more underwater creatures and fish!

Fun! Lots of charm and character. This trail has a good sense of humor. Trails are rocky and you are surrounded by cactus but they are easy to manage. Follow the signs! Lots of scary but manageable obstacles, including a crazy drop in wooden contraption. It looked intimidating but was really doable.

As we were leaving we ran into another couple from Huntington Beach who were also on a mt bike vacation. They asked if the trail was easy to figure out and we thought about it for a while and then said yes. 

If you love mountain biking you should check out the trails here. They are one of a kind and really fun!

When i want Hot Chicken and don't want to do it myself, I go to 400 Degrees. Her chicken is Hot, juicy and well worth the wait.  You must understand that every order is cooked when placed so that 15-20 min that you wait is normal.  If you'd never had get 100 but If you can handle heat go for the 400 or higher.  Enjoy

I really like Hattie B's. I haven't had Prince's. Birmingham has its own hot chicken food truck, Eugene's, and between that and the newly opened Hatties, I feel like I know what to expect from tasty hot chicken.

Went to Nash yesterday for a concert and 400 degrees was within walking distance of the hotel. We did not do any research ahead so were surprised about its food court location. Okay, no big deal. We were the only people in there and the owner/manager said it'd be a 30 minute wait! For 2 pieces of chicken? I think that's crazy. 

The staff was extremely pleasant/very nice women but at the same time discouraging us from eating the 200 level heat. I didn't really understand that. I'm here for your food. You should be selling it to me!

The crinkle fries are great. Can't go wrong with seasoned salt fries but the hot chicken was lacking. We couldn't really figure out what the problem was, but it is definitely lacking salt. Needs more flavor notes. You could only taste the heavy cayenne. I found the 200 heat to be very tolerable. Not at all unbearable as was suggested. I never even got tingly lips or hiccups! That's when I know I'm eating hot chicken! :P

With the long wait time and the lacking in flavor (and honestly, not that much heat), I would recommend Hattie's and other places over 400. 

I did see they had a 100 cleanliness/health dept score. That's a positive!

I loved the aquarium. We did the pass for 4 events (zoo, aquarium, insectarium, Entergy theater) and it's worth it. The aquarium was even better than Chicago's. We went on a Saturday and it wasn't packed like we were afraid it might be. I recommend the aquarium as a family event in an adult city like NOLA.

400 degrees has the best fried chicken in Nashville. I've tried just about every other location in Nashville & this is my favorite. The flavor & taste of the chicken is excellent. All you have to do is call ahead and pick it up when they say it'll be ready. I love the staff and the consistency every time I eat there. This place is the best!

Tried this chicken today and I wasn't crazy about it, I also had to wait well past the time they said it would be ready.... I had the 200.. The heat was nice but it tasted like Hot Flour with no seasoning Very Bland...Maybe next time in town I will try Prince's.

When you walk into the Audubon Aquarium, you're hit with some pretty cool exhibits.  My toddler had a lot of fun and there are a few interesting highlights like the White Alligator.  But, overall, the place is small and can be easily accomplished in under 2 hours.  

It's also pretty darn expensive - $22.50 per adult.  Compared to the zoo at $17.50, which I found way more enjoyable, it felt overpriced.  Children under 2 are free.

It's also in walking distance from the French Quarter and all indoors.  So, on a rainy day like the one we had, it's not a bad choice.  It's just not on the top of my list.

This is the Kohl's I grew up frequenting in Turnersville. I especially loved the store during the Christmas season.

Over the years, the set up has changed slightly (no more cards near customer service!), but there's still plenty of quality products to go around. Stop in for updates to your wardrobe or house, as well as a bunch of toys and small kitchen appliances.

It's a typical Kohl's store, and I'm glad it seems to be holding strong as a Black Horse Pike anchor.

Visited during a weekday afternoon, so there were loud packs of school kids romping through the place.  The large aquarium was an excellent spot to relax (when the kids weren't there) and the small tanks of jellyfish were wonderful to watch.

Beautiful aquarium that has always put an emphasis of the local costal eco system. The aquarium enclosures are stunning and you can even feed the parakeets if you'd like. They get a little crazy at times so you have to make sure they don't try to hitch a ride in your belongings. Little stowaways! Lol

The New Orleans Aquarium is small but all the exhibits are well constructed and thought really went into the design.   As you walk, ahead of you is a whole school of fish and then Mayan heads and a large tank, that you can walk under and see the fish.  They have lots of the same species of a fish.  If you went to see lionfish, there is a tank full of them and not just one or two.  I loved to see the seahorses and there were 2 tanks of them.  I've never seen so many and they were healthy and quite prehistoric looking to me.  There are piranhas, porgy, tiger sharks, flounder, shrimp, crawfish, blue crabs, lionfish, coral, blowfish, and many other fish species.  They also had an abundance of various jellyfish housed in different tanks.

There is also a white alligator that was hiding his head, so I only saw the body and tail.  Different regions specific to the South were also highlighted.  They had an otter exhibit and a gimmicky parakeet exhibit where if you pay $1.50 you get a stick with glued seeds on it.  The parakeets will walk on your stick and you can watch them eat. Too bad they are stingy on the seeds.  A couple of pecks from the parakeets and then no more millet.  Once the seeds are gone, you can kiss your parakeet goodbye.  Those little fair weather beasts, I should have smuggled in a giant seed bell and all the parakeets would have landed on me and I would have had lots of time with them. I had to minus one star for giving me a feeding stick that had less than a dozen millet on it.  Gimme a giant seed bell!

There's also a feeding tank for the small sea rays.  Lots of kids were lining up to feed the sea rays, but I was short on time and didn't want to wait.  There's an otter themed gift shop upstairs and a bigger gift shop downstairs.  You can pay to get your picture souvenir as well as paint your face activities for children. There is a cafeteria upstairs near the parakeet exhibit.  This is definitely a family friendly place and it's good to bring the kids here to teach them all about appreciating sea creatures,  fish and the wonderful animal life found in many of our rivers, swamps, lakes, seas and oceans.  If you are walking by the river and come near the aquarium you can hear the parakeets chirping and making lots of noises even in the evening hours.
Fantastic!!! Beautiful color, fantastic cut!! The friendly personality and impromptu comedy makes this more than a salon-- it is a destination!!

This aquarium was nice, but in my opinion, nothing special.  It is very small, but the exhibits were nice and kids would have a blast.  The aquarium is one of the few family oriented spots it seems in New Orleans, and definitely worth checking out.  

Look for Brandon who talks about "the largest aquarium exhibit in America..."

Absolutely love this place! Second time here and I felt compelled to write a review! The boyfriend and I ventured in on a Saturday night about an hour before they were closing. Staff was pleasant, very nice, attentive. I recently had their brisket quesadilla at a festival and had to get it this past weekend! Get it! You won't regret it! Regularly I would have gotten the pulled pork sandwich but I HAD to have the brisket quesadilla. it's so yummy and filling. They also have a few different sauces that you can pair your meats with. My boyfriend ended up getting the alligator sausage and then some marinated chicken which was amazing as well. The sauce for the alligator is on point! For sides we got the macaroni, beans and potato salad! My fav is the Mac and cheese. We will absolutely be back!
Pretty good sized aquarium. Some of the attractions are pretty cool. Parking sucks because your entry fee ends up being a lot from having to pay for parking.

Best bbq in Nola. They pushed together some tables to accommodate my group of 12. We did a family style meal and ordered as per the owner's suggestions. Everything was fantastic, especially the ribs and the potato salad. The food is excellent as are the people and location

My favorite hot chicken place in Nashville.

The chicken is the crispiest and juiciest, and it stays that way.  A lot of other places have chicken that gets soggy after ten minutes of sitting in its own grease.  Not 400 degrees... they have this shizz figured out.

Heat level is fairly high.  I would say 400 degrees is generally between "Damn hot" and "Shut the cluck up" at Hattie B's, and 200 degrees is a little less hot than their "Hot".  Sometimes when I'm not looking to challenge my small intestine, I wish they had a 300 degrees level, since there's a pretty big gap between 200 and 400.  Sometimes they've made it for me; sometimes they say "we don't do that".  They do have off-menu levels higher than 400 degrees, but I'm apprehensive...

Sides are fine, I'd say on par with Hattie's and better than Bolton's or Prince's.  You're there for the chicken anyway.

ONLY complaint are the hours.  I'm basically left with a five hour window on Saturday, since I can't really get there by 7:00pm on a weeknight, and getting it for lunch on a workday isn't really an option.  Why, you ask? Hmmm... just remember that their motto is "So hot it'll burn you twice!" Ha...

EDIT: Don't forget it's cash only, and also call ahead! They actually answer their phone unlike a lot of places.

The exhibits are nice, but for ~$30/adult & $22/child the aquarium is extremely overpriced. We were through the entire aquarium in an hour, even though it was crowded and we took our time at each area. When we bought our tickets the lady made it sound like we could watch all of the movies. That made the exorbitant ticket prices seem more reasonable. However, after watching one movie and trying to attend a second we were informed our tickets were only good for one show.

SAVE $$:  If you are planning your trip weeks (or months) in advance, make sure to look for ticket deals. The aquarium has a link to the Big Easy deal site (http://nolacc.neworleans-deals.com), and there are often half-price discount tickets available. The only caveat is that the tickets are mailed to you, so you have to order in advance.

The brisket is outstanding and I'm not a fan of brisket,actually ordered a pound to bring home, it was good!and goat cheese mac , amazing!!The sauces were great and great service even though it was counter service!!

I have no idea how this place is rated so highly. The only reason this place gets two stars is because of the sides. We had the Mac and cheese and beans, which were both decent enough.  The inside of the restaurant had no deep smoke smell and their was not smoke visible or to be smelt outside the establishment, a bad sign.  The meats we got were the ribs and the brisket. They didn't have any real smokey flavor and zero smoke ring, I fear they were boiled and then baked.  The meats had a grayish tint to them and tasted watery, further strengthening my opinion that their meat is boiled/baked.  Also their sauces were lacking in flavor which for a place named Saucy's just adds insult to injury. Anyone that knows good, real, slow smoked BBQ will be highly disappointed.

This place slays! 
We had the 100 & & 200 degrees. Food comes out fresh and totally blew my mind. Fries were great and crispy and the potato salad was the bomb. Portions are big too. 

They do tenders as well as the sandwich. They close early so make sure you check the times. We almost missed them. 

Staff was super sweet and man was that chicken delicious!!!

Great place to go to escape the New Orleans heat and see something educational and fun. Always loved the Aquarium and I'm glad that it's almost back to its former pre-K glory. Wish there were more sharks and sea lions. And more stuff in the touch pool besides sting rays. Gimme some turtles and starfish!! The sea horse and jellyfish exhibits are awesome and makes up for the rather lame touching areas now. And the petting area is really only for kids now. Boo!

Couldn't find the parakeet show then when I left, I heard it was in the cafeteria. Tricky, tricky! 

But overall, the Aquarium is something you don't want to miss when you're in New Orleans- either as a first-timer or a local being a tourist in your hometown.
It seem overpriced, 53.00 with a coupon .but the exhibits were nice. I wouldn't go back ,nothing unique. They did have a stingray petting pool. And a parakeet  area. The penguins are also nice.

To be perfectly honest I came here only because I found out they had a behind the scene penguin experience where you could actually pet a penguin so naturally I booked my flight to New Orleans and then booked this experience. The penguin experience is only a couple days a week and it is a very small group so you actually get time to interact with the penguin. Before meeting the penguin they give you information about the penguin exhibit and you get to go into the kitchen and see how their food is prepared. Then they bring one of the penguins out of the exhibit and place the penguin in a room with the people who signed up for the experience. The big thing is not to chase the penguin, let the penguin come to you and you can pet it. I was also able to feed the penguin up close, take a photo with it and received a little painting from the penguin. For a penguin lover like me this was a must because when else in my life would I be able to pet a penguin! Granted this experience was pretty pricey so good thing it included admission to the aquarium afterwards so I was also able to roam around.

Small but it has nice things for families with kids. The option to buy multi tickets for the attractions around the aquarium is one of the good options available to save you time and effort looking for the best price. They have Sheraton times to feed the animals and engage with the nature. They have fact labels all around the place for more fun and education. 
There is foodcourt available and gift shop.
They had a lot of different choices for the bbq sauces which was fun to try. The sausages was my favorite and a must try! Go go go! Stafff was super friendly too

I went here with a couple co-workers for lunch. It's interesting because it's located in what seems like a food court, so there is plenty of seating. The people here are nice, but not as friendly as the folks at Bolton's. 

I order the breast qtr at 200 degrees, which is there version of medium. It was spicy and awesome. The chicken is breaded and they use a sauce dry spice combo, which works well. 

Unless you call ahead, you will probably wait up to half an hour for your order.

Great things can't  be rushed so make sure you call at least 45mins before you pick up your order. I was introduced to 400 degrees a few years ago and haven't stopped going since. Unlike other places I've tried their chicken always juicy and spicy levels stay consistent. The only other place that gives them a run for their money is Princes.

I love that we have a BBW in a very easy to get to location on the northwest side.   This store has rescued me more than once when I have needed to pick up some last minute gifts.   

They have all the usual sales here, buy 3 get 2 free, plus endless coupons, and other sales, so no one ever actually pays full price as far as I can tell.
