They don't always have all products in all scents, but this might be more of a product line issue than a store issue.    It is a little random in terms of what scents have tester bottles out; it is definitely not all of them at this location, so I usually end up getting scents I'm already familiar with.   

Staff are typically friendly here and always offer to help and point out sales.   I do like that they will leave customers alone though if you say you don't need help.   

Other than at the holidays this location is usually not super busy so no line to check out!

Very clean eating facility that shares its space with a few other fast food joints.  The chicken is cooked fresh and hot, both in spice and temp.  I got the 200 degrees of heat level for my chicken, and tried a 400 pork chop.  The chicken was a big breast that was very juicy and flavorful, and spicy.  I'm someone that eats a lot of hot foods and have a high heat tolerance, and the 200 is perfect for someone that wants to open up the nasal passages a bit.  Honestly the 100 would be perfect to enjoy the chicken taste the best.  The pork chop is big, and 400 was pretty darn hot.  We liked their slaw and potato salad, as well as the seasoned fries.  Going to be a favorite when in Nashville.

After a particularly strong craving for ribs, I called in an order for a rack and a half. Easily some of the toughest and driest BBQ I have ever had the misfortune to gnaw on. I've had better ribs at Chili's. Top that with a sauce that is more salt and vinegar than flavor and I will never visit this BBQ joint again. Shame, because the mac and cheese was pretty good.
It's alright.  My child likes to watch the fish swim but I think they need more interactive activities for the younger kids

You know that feeling when you're shopping for a dress for a special occasion and you've been all over town, you've given up for the day,  you call home saying you're done torturing yourself today, you want a glass of wine and you'll go back to the trenches tomorrow, then just then you drive by and see that The Dress Barn has opened up.. hallelujah!  Could one hope?  
Reno has typically been a bit tough market for social event dress shopping, I know,  I have to buy one about twice a year.  Most department stores have just only a few choices, then I move on to a bridal shop...

  All my events are themed, the other dresses usually never work from one theme to another.  I've had some luck at David's Bridal but this season my event is during prom season so most of the dresses in stock currently there are for 15-18 year olds. (Other than the obvious wedding dresses)   I'm slightly past that and my event is not a prom or a wedding

When I walked in I was hopeful this would be the end of my journey. I have so many other things to do for this event as the co-coordinator, so shopping is a thorn in my side at this point, but a must do on my list. 
While they don't have a ton of special occasion dresses at least in April (only in relation to all that they have in stock)  they have soooo many dresses. They don't have prom dresses, if you're 15-18 you may want to go check David's Bridal or another bridal shop  

I grabbed a bunch of dresses and headed for the dressing room.  One of the gals working had already set me up in a room with my name written on it.  I didn't have to leave that room again. They helped me out, brought me dresses, gave opinions, zipped me up, it was like trying on dresses with girlfriends.  I told them my theme, my event purpose and had three ladies waiting on me.  Of course I left with a dress and a jacket to go with it. They set me up with a 20% discount for an item basically for being a newbie.  They bagged my dress up and sent me on my way. 

5 plus Stars for the excellent service I received. I wasn't in a great mood when I entered the store but I was ecstatic and completely relieved when I left. What a load off!!

Great addition to Reno shopping.  Much needed... I'll stop there first for my next event.

As soon as you walk in the door, the aroma hits you with love!! The Mac and Cheese was to die for.. I had the boudin with the slaw..awesome. My son had the grilled chicken with asparagus.. The spices on the chicken reminded me of a Caribbean dish, really good. My partner had the pulled pork with the smoked beans..another winner!!!

Diane Bertero is a wonderful nail tech.  She listens intently to your needs and delivers quality service.  She is the most kind and caring professional and your nails will will look spectacular.  I give her the highest ratings!

Although we got mixed reviews of this aquarium, I thought it was one of the best I've ever seen! 

I think the only reason people didn't rate this 5 stars is because they rushed through the place without really appreciating all that it had! Very well kept habitats and aquariums and lots to see! 

The parakeet aviary was a blast! And don't miss petting the sting rays!

AH-MAZING!!!! I was really doubtful that any aquarium would measure up to Monterey Bay but this place definitely did!!! I was beyond pleasantly surprised at how great this aquarium was. They had a ton of exhibits and my son (1 yr) absolutely had a blast! I liked that a lot of the tanks were at a level were he could easily view them without having to be boosted up. This was so much fun and I will miss it as we were just passing through. I highly recommend this aquarium!!

I coaxed my husband into taking part of the Backstage Penguin Pass with me on our honeymoon. I can honestly say it was one of the most special and awesome animal experiences EVER! Darwin, our guide, was so passionate about his penguins and it showed every step of the way. It was incredibly educational and even more fun. Our up-close and personal experience with Marina and Voodoo (our penguin ambassadors) was so wonderful-I never wanted to leave! Loved every minute of it and can't wait to go back.

Update: the owner of the store reached out to me and let me know that they were understaffed the day that I came in. I understand this happens, and it goes a long way when you reach out to your customers. That is certainly something you don't get from Amazon. I will keep supporting this business, as I am dedicated to shopping locally.
Never have had a bad meal, staff are very friendly.  The baked beans are amazing and definitely try the goat-cheese Mac & Cheese.
food was bomb but 35 min wait. Yes, it was made to order but damn it took a long time

Meh... Screaming babies and kind of small. The penguins were looking a little psychotic ramming their heads into the glass over and over. The jellyfish exhibit was the highlight of our visit. Kind of on the expensive side $74 for a family of 4.

This place is 10 stars.  I am new to Tucson and they make me feel like one of the family every time I go in.  Love my stylist Ayesha and my nail girl Diane.  They both go above and beyond to take care of my every need and keep me looking good.  My husband is even coming to Ayesha now for his haircuts.  Can't say enough good things about Mane Salon.

I love the Aquarium. If you are interested in seeing the zoo, aquarium and the insectarium, you can buy one package deal to use for all three places. You also get an IMAX movie included. Great deal. Any way back to the aquarium. It can be busy with school tours (like the day we were there) so it can be crowded sometimes. They have different areas based on Jungle, swamp, rivers and oceans. There is a great tank with many fish when you first enter. My favorite places to visit are the penguins, the seahorse and jellyfish and the white alligator. We were there when they were feeding the penguins which was quite cute. They all have names and different personalities. It is a great family place and if visiting New Orleans during the hot and humid months this is a good place to get out of the heat. After your visit check out the IMAX movies next door.
I have 2 complaints. First the meat is so tender and yummy that it's damn near impossible to eat with a fork. 2nd I am too full to try the rest of the menu in one sitting. Absolutely delicious.

Nice, family-friendly trail! I was a beginner rider when I first came here but I was able to build my confidence. First-timers should start on the Bunny trail(Valencia side) before transitioning to Lone Cactus(Irvington side). There is a map of the trails on the Irvington side which does not include the Bunny trails.

It is a well-marked trail with lots of random trinkets along the way. I never encountered a rider going the wrong way so it's safe to say everyone follows the rules - don't be that guy! 

Bring plenty of water, tubes and a comb in case you should encounter the stage-5 clinger known as the Cholla cactus!

I love bringing friends to this trail to get a good workout in before the traditional post-ride margarita.

We could spend all day here!

Great family spot and tons of aquatic wildlife to see. You also get a free pass to watch a movie in their theatres.

Definitely arrive earlier to avoid a long line. Once inside it doesn't get too bad as exhibits are quite large.

Also make sure to drop by to see the parakeets! We almost missed this when we skipped the food area, it's hidden next to the hagan Diaz.

Oh, and you also get to pet sting rays!

Let me start with the owner, Her name is Aqui. She make you feel right at home. I tried everything on the menu... But nothing to write home about... It just make you cry in eyes/bottom with the spiciness. 100 or 200 degrees you can enjoy the flavor

I've had Hattie B's and Prince's. 400 degrees is by far the best overall experience. I didn't call ahead and had a bit of a wait, but it was more than worth it! Flavor, spice, and excellent customer service made my day. The owner was highly interactive and called customers by name. That means loyalty. Thanks to the ladies behind the counter I will definitely be back!

I had tried Prince's, Pepperfire, Hattie B's, Knock Out Wings, Hot Stuff before finally getting to 400 Degrees this week.  We ordered the 200 variety and it was good.  Definitely plenty hot, I would not want to venture into 400 land!  As compared to the other hot chicken, we like Pepperfire better but it's on par with the others listed.  We ordered take out but the location was certainly cleaner than some others and Acqui, the owner was welcoming and friendly.  Depending where we are when the craving hits us for hot chicken, we'd go back.

Came here for the last wine slushy weekend of the summer and in love with their Hurricane slushy made with their Niagara wine. They had great tasting deals and the interior decor was cozy and they had the game on which was great. I would definitely come back for some wine tastings. They didn't have any food pairing deals which definitely should be added! The staff were nice and helpful.

I've been here several times, and every time I enjoy it. All of the sections are really well done, and I particularly like the high ceilings in several parts that make this seem more like a cross between a zoo and an aquarium than just a giant fish habitat. If you can make it to the Parakeet Point exhibit, definitely go and buy one of the little sugar sticks, it was a great experience to have dozens of little birds flying around and flocking to you in order to have a nibble.

Very much overpriced for what it is. Even with the $3 off coupon on the tourist map of the French Quarter, it was still $20 for an aquarium that took me less than an hour to go through. The only thing that made this worthwhile at all for me was to see that the albino gator was alive and well post-Katrina - I'd last seen him in 1997 in the Audubon Zoo. Now that I've done that, I will never waste my time or money on this aquarium again. It's poorly lit, poorly laid out, the signs are all geared toward little kids and don't have much information that an adult would find interesting, it has few species of sea life compared to other aquariums, and is just not worth the entrance fee.
The pulled pork here is average here but the ribs are just bad. They're dry and super salty.. Typical predominantly white run southern joint-- no flavor!

Little hole in the wall that had the best, most perfectly cooked meat and sides I've had in New Orleans for bbq. It was such a pleasant surprise. Goat cheese Mac was so good and I don't like Mac n cheese usually. The asparagus, I don't think , could of been better. Bring your own booze if you want to drink proper. Great job Saucy's.
Fun place for my 2 yo. Crowded weekend but he had a blast! Great area to spend a whole day in Nola!

I have gone here to my stylist Annie for a few years. She is amazing! She always listens to what I want, which is usually something different every time, and she delivers. I have never left disappointed. You rock, Annie!

This has always  been one of my favorite Aquariums. I was lucky enough to go on a Thursday morning when it wasn't too crowded.

Great exhibits and I love the white alligator. 

Just a really neat aquarium.
Had the 100 degree wings they were very tasty...my only surprise was that the location was in a food court. I did have to wait close to 30 minutes for my order to be ready.

The chicken here was ok. I've never had hot chicken before so I don't really know what to compare it to. This chicken had so much seasoning on it it tasted like the powder was caked on. It was also extremely greasy. I realize it's fried, but it was soaking with oil. We waited 45 minutes for this because they cool it fresh, which I appreciate the concept of, but it was pretty crappy chicken for a 45 min wait. The staff wasn't very friendly, except the shorter girl who was friendly. When I asked when they open the older lady said 12 and never even turned around and looked at me which is kinda rude. The medium heat chicken was melt your face off hot, but because the insane amount of grease and caked on powder seasoning it was hard to eat. The mild was good, still greasy. I will not be back here.

We loved this place. Whoever claimed it was too small must frequent some enormous aquariums. The otters were adorable, sharks and sea turtles were very impressive. Jellyfish exhibit was incredible. They had a great stingray exhibit where you can pet the rays. they also have a pretty nice selection of bird exhibits. My favorite though, was the white Alligator, be sure to check it out. After spending about 90 mins exploring the aquarium we watched a 3D movie about great white sharks at the attached IMAX theater. the 3D was great quality but the movie was only 40 mins long and left us wanting more. The total price for 2 adults for the aquarium and IMAX was about $55 which I found a little steep, but if your willing to pay, the experience is probably worth it.

Reasonable aquarium, albeit a bit on the expensive side. I guess we are a little spoiled, coming from Chattanooga, where we have been used to an incredible aquarium for many years.

Not that this is a bad aquarium, but it's just average. We certainly had some fun with the parakeets... in an aquarium! The fish exhibits were nice, and all of the exhibits looked well cared for. The highlight for us was the "Amazon" exhibit, which was nicely done. I think the focus on the Gulf of Mexico was nice as well.

Overall, I think this is a reasonable stop if you are planning to buy the Audubon package (Aquarium, Insectarium, and Zoo experience) but individually, it's not as great of a destination as you would want for the price.
And the Thunder rolls, while the Lightning strikes... #Tucson #TucsonAZ #Pima #520 #MonsoonSeason

LOVE this store.  Always friendly and helpful.  They know what they're talking about and have an awesome selection of tools and furniture making stuff.  They don't sell crappy brands, only good ones, but they service just about anything.  

I once spent 45 minutes in Home Depot at Summit Ridge with three employees trying to locate cross dowels.  Not only had nobody ever heard of them, but they didn't have them in stock except in a bag in one size under a different name (the wrong size of course).  That would never happen at Apex.  I know they have what I need and if they don't, they know what I'm talking about.

What made me rate 3 stars was the simple fact that I was in a aquarium in New Orleans, LA  and I forgot my location. This is by far one of the best you can get in Louisiana. 

I am a avid fan of Aquariums, conservation of our wetlands, marshes and seashore is priorty being from the West Coast one of my favorite aquariums is the Monterey Bay Aquarium. I wasn't disappointed, I didn't get the tourist trap feel normally associated with the location of this venue. The admission price for was overpriced however based on the tourist trap New Orleans represents. You have to see it to believe it, I didn't indulge in the full Zoo and Insect whatever experience due to the weather in season. 

 Downside: Location, location,  location!!!  New Orleans is not a place for children even in a off season time of December. Other than the aquarium you can't take your family to dining establishments serving alcohol...had a difficult time feeding my children.

 Oh but a miniature type mall next door to the aquarium which had a duty-free sense of feel "Way Over Priced" maybe due to the fact that cruise liners embark and disembark their passengers right on or next to the mall. I stayed at the Omni which is another review.

 Look if you can book a Hotel in Baton Rouge  and commute from there with your  children you will be okay. The drive alone would be cheaper than finding parking because if you stay in the area there is none and you would have to valet or park your car at least 1 mile or more. What is that 20 city blocks? No thank you, my valet parking was over 100 dollars for 2 days.

The Aquarium of the Americas is a wonderful place to be indoors on a warm day but here's a tip: do not take flash photos of fish; they do not have eyelids and can't close their eyes so when visitors take flash photos, the fish are blinded and stunned for several minutes.

It is debatable whether animals have fun but I think they do for example, otters seem to enjoy playing and it does seem like they do have fun and so I do enjoy watching them play. Visitors can also feed stingrays and touch their sandpaper-texture skin, watch penguins feed, and learn more about animals that live the aquatic life here.

I had heard about this place from some friends and decided to try it. My only issue is that I wish I had tried them sooner. Both the food and staff were fantastic. 

New Orleans isn't a city known for Barbecue  but this place does a great job with it. We tried a 2 meat plate (brisket and sausage) , a pulled pork sandwich, and a few different sides. Everything was great.

The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because you need to park on the street. Since there are quite a few restaurants in the same area parking is always a challenge.

400 Degrees shares an unmarked building with several other food stands south of Broadway at 4th and Peabody. There is limited free parking. The chicken is awesome, extra crispy and beautifully spiced. The heat levels are 100 degrees (mild), 200 degrees (medium) and 400 degrees (hot), but even the 100 degrees is mighty spicy! The sides are excellent as well. I did notice that most of the customers had called ahead, and it does take about 30 minutes to get your order. I'll be back, after calling first.

This is my go to BBQ.  Been to most of the other places around the city, but I always end up back at Saucy's.

If you're dining in there is usually only 1 waitress and on busy nights the owners sometimes hang around and help out. It's a no muss, no fuss kind of experience.  They get a lot of take out orders which keeps them busy, but it will be obvious why the waitress is taking so long when you see the line at the counter. 

BYOB

Sweet potato muffins - 5 stars, have ordered just these without any meat because they are that good
Boudin link - 5 stars, mustard is delicious
Pulled pork - 5 stars, get it with the bun
Ribs - 5 stars, like both the regular and sweet sauce

The only thing hit or miss are the sides.  Some days they are 5 stars and others I won't eat more than one bite.

I am a true lover of any aquatics so this was a great day for me and the kid. The huge viewing tank is awesome. never seemed to crowded and the creatures, animals and fish are all in well viewing area's for all to be able to see.. I have to say the albino allegator was very cool, we have never seen one before and didnt know there was such a thing!!! See we learned something new !!

Another New Orleans classic, I can remember when this place first opened.

I went to the Aquarium a few months ago for the 10 year anniversary celebration.  I hadn't been in a really long time, and I somehow remembered it being bigger.  No bother.  It was a lot of fun.  

I think my favorite was probably the HUGE tank full of sharks and the big school of fish swimming around and around.  There are a lot of fun attractions for kids and they have a really cute gift shop, if you want to buy yourself a memory.
Awesome aquarium - the penguins and otters were my favorite! Maybe it's just because I'm used to a fairly small aquarium, but I was definitely impressed with how many options there were here!

This place was great in the 1990s when I was hungover and with a bunch of rowdy college students. It was great a few years ago with the family and my children thoroughly enjoyed it. 

Especially the rainforest room. 

It's worth the money and gives the kids a chance to interact with animals. The penguins were a favorite.

It's been 10 years or more since I've been to the Aquarium, and unfortunately I was extremely disappointed this time.  It was not clean and is obviously not being maintained very well.  Most of all, I felt very sorry for the animals there...enclosures that are boring (for the animals), dirty, and far too small (penguins, otters, alligator).  Even the fish are over-crowded into the tank.  Not a very inspirational exhibit.

Of all the Audubon attractions, the aquarium is by far my favs.  Partly because it manages to instantly transport you to another world, an underwater magicland full of wonder and excitement.  Also, the Aquarium does a fantastic job of continually updating their exhibits, always bringing in something new and awe-inspiring.  Case in point: the new Mayan exhibit.  We recently traveled to that part of the world and I was surprised by how Audubon managed to capture the culture and spirit of the Mayan people while utilizing the existing space that they already had set up.  The Aquarium recently celebrated its 25th anniversary but I am more impressed by the progress they have made in the 10 years since Katrina.  When I was in school, I would come in here during a quiet weekday just to study and found I wasn't the only adult seeking a change of scenery there.  The little kid in me wants to give it 10 stars, just for the way it makes me feel inside.  Then the adult in me remembers that the $25/person entrance fee can be very expensive for those who don't hold a membership and this place can get crazy crowded during tourist seasons, especially if the weather is less than ideal.  Also, the food court offers a very limited, unimaginative and highly overpriced selection.  So plan your trip accordingly and enjoy the day.

As far as I can tell, the Audubon Aquarium is pretty standard as far as aquariums go.  They've got some great stuff--the penguins are adorable, the Mississippi River exhibit with the albino alligator (at least, I think that's where I saw him) is terrifying, the cuttlefish and blowfish and seahorses are adorable.  

It's definitely an awesome thing to do when it's eleventy billion degrees outside and/or pouring down rain, so this goes on the "beat the heat" activities list (that I have yet to create).  For me, though, the aquarium is also pretty expensive (as is the Zoo), so it's not something I do very often.  That said, I'm glad it's here.  

Side note: speaking of penguins, I remember being at the aquarium not long after the K word, and at that point they still had a board over the hole that had been cut in the ceiling of the penguin habitat in order to rescue them in the aftermath of the storm.  What happened at the aquarium after the K word is an incredibly sad story; thank you to the people who did everything they could to save the animals, and to the people who helped us pick up the pieces and put the aquarium back together after the storm.
What an awesome aquarium! Great exhibits. This is a gem. Way larger than you'd think and full of amazing species.
The Brisket! The Mac n' Cheese! Get them! Extremely delicious. Southern BBQ and hospitality at its finest.

Excellent hot chicken, the baked beans are the best I have EVER had. They're like candy  and I'm not much of a bean person. I recommend calling in an order ahead of time because the food is all cooked to order.

The hot chicken tour continues...there have been some casualties along the way (my wife literally missed a Southwest flight because of hot chicken, I won't go into details, but you will just have to trust me on this one), but the tour must go on!!

Like the other Yelpers, it's easy to miss this place if you're not looking for it.  Armed with a little prelim intel, I entered the food court with confidence, knowing my prey would be located within.  I found the smiling faces behind the counter to be just a little too friendly....I knew an ambush was in store, so I wasn't about to let my guard down.  Despite calling ahead and ordering, it appeared that my order wasn't ready yet.  I waited another 10 or so minutes, and there it was....2 orders of tenders of different heat levels....200 degrees for the sane and scared (me) and 400 degrees for the bold and beautiful (wifey).  The tenders were huge and served with the traditional white bread... and they were damn good!  As far as spice....the 200 degrees had a little burn, but nothing that would put you out of commission.  The 400 degrees....well, I'm not sure if saying that it was similar to calling in a napalm strike on a melting nuclear reactor core would be too dramatic, but it wasn't all that far off.  It was good...and for a few brief moments, I actually smirked at the ladies behind the counter and thought to myself "you'll have to find another sucker, because you didn't get me today", but then the harsh reality of the situation came into view.  The burn came...and then kept coming....in a delicious, 'I told you not to do it' kind of way.  Three glasses of water (and maybe a few tears) later, I was able to gather my senses and, for some reason, get back into the fight.  I wasn't going to let this awesomeness go to waste, not on my watch.

I ended up only having one 400 degree tender, the 200 degree was a little easier for me to handle.  Wifey took down the other 400 degree pieces in gallant and courageous fashion.  But I'll give you one guess on who missed their flight later that day.

This is a must stop for me when in Nashville. To say I love the chicken is an understatement. Its the best I have ever had. Great and easy spot for take out or nice place to stay and eat. 

Owner Aqui Simpson and her staff are friendly and always happy. Don't miss this treat of Nashville.

Apex is a great local store, with a huge variety of man toys. They sharpen all of my dull drill bits for a great price, and repair all of my broken power tools. Chad is such a great owner, and always takes time to make sure all of my needs are being taken care of. Way better selection than Home Depot, and competitive pricing all around. I will be coming here until I stop working!

Great way to spend a couple hours when you're looking for a family friendly air conditioned activity.  Plenty of exhibits and little extras like penguin feeding and stingray touch and feel tanks.  Plenty of clean restrooms and friendly staff.  Food court was pricey as expected but given its proximity to the quarter as well the mall right next door, no reason to eat in the aquarium itself.

It the best aquarium in the country but a nice one to visit. They have penguins, otters, sea horses, a white alligator and even a owl. Pretty sweet. Price is expensive so if you are planning on also doing the zoo then buy a combo pass.
Fair, fast, friendly. Really love tom's auto where you get prompt service and reasonable prices. Lower quote than another place nearby. With 2 old cars, feel lucky to have Tom's in my neighborhood.
Extremely well done.   We spent several hours there and throughly enjoyed it.   The exhibits are incredible.   This is definitely something we would do again!

Someone once said that you will never get a second chance to make a first impression. Ticket agents are the first ones to welcome you and represent the aquarium. Thank you SHEILA for your rudeness and attitude. Someone in the aquarium needs to re-evaluate the employees to ensure customer facing agent are trained to be respectful, friendly and welcoming of their guest. Keep in mind that New Orleans is a tourist city. People from all around the globe visit the city and needless to say places like this aquarium represent the city. 

What a shame that SHEILA lacks all the quality to be hospitable. Sorry that we interrupted your personal time as you watch something over your right side. Sorry that you weren't paying attention on how many tickets we're buying. We are not going to THANK YOU for the comp tickets because YOU made a mistake. We are not grateful getting a freebie from you because the aquarium was a rip off. 

We were there around 4pm - near closing and the place was like a ghost town. For a weekday sure it's expected but the whole aura was just MEH, I'VE EXPERIENCED BETTER. 

If given a second chance, I would have gone directly to the Riverwalk Outlet Collection and not set foot at this outrageous aquarium. The aquarium is not stroller and/or wheelchair accessible unless coming from the Riverwalk. Expect to cross the railroad tracks if you take the train.

This was an ok experience. Way overpriced for what we paid. They have some nice displays, but overall the place is tinier than it looks outside. I did enjoy that we got one free movie. The move about the oceans was really well done.

Located in downtown, small aquarium that can easily be seen within 1-2 hours. 

My husband and I decided to check out this aquarium last Monday afternoon. It wasn't too crowded when we arrived and seems to be less people in the later part of the day. 

My husband (not me) is a lover of the aquatic life, so we have been to so many aquariums across the US. 

This aquarium is two floors (we were never given a map after paying for our admission outside). I like the way some of the exhibits/ sections are laid out. For example, in the Amazon rain forest section, it was rather warm and humid in this area (just what you may expect in a rain forest like environment). The creatures found in this part of the aquarium are also what you would expect in the rain forest (which includes piranhas and different types of birds. There is also a large anaconda on display, behind a glass, for your viewing). 

In the Mississippi River section, you can see the white alligator. But the alligator just kind of stood on it's hind legs inside it's tank and never moved. It made me feel like it was fake... but I am sure it is real and just didn't want to move and expel any energy I suppose. 

I enjoyed seeing the cute penguins and this cute sleeping sea otter. 

It was also cool to see some of the animals being fed. It was also helpful to have an employee available to answer questions and explain the behavior of the animals. It was also really interesting to see the sting rays eating.

As mentioned earlier, this aquarium is kind of the small side. So don't expect to spend the entire day here because you will be able to get through it in about 1-2 hours. 

There is a food court on the 2nd floor and there is also a restaurant on site (you can order seafood at the restaurant if eating in an aquarium does not bother you). 

Admission prices are as follows:

$24.95 (plus sales tax): Adult 
$18.95 (plus sales tax): Child (2-12) 
$18.95 (plus sales tax): Senior (65+)

Triple A members can receive a $2 discount. Students can also receive a $2 discount (discounts cannot be combined). 

There is also free WiFi available here as well.

Right at the end of Canal street and along the water.. Next to a vast lawn area and water fountains for kids to play in.  The aquarium varies up things to do while in New Orleans- especially for chitlins.   We went for a quick Lookey loo - Facility is a tad tired, however Thoughtful and caring employees, wildlife exhibits along with  learning centers make it an experience that is enjoyed by all.  The facility is a nonprofit and guest funds support the cause and wildlife..nice.

Oh yes, this place is goooood. Yumm-o. Went tonight, they've been open in this location less than a week. 
I initially judge a BBQ places on their house-made sauce and Saucy's is delicious. Mom and I went. She had the 2 meat plate (chicken and pulled pork) with mac & cheese and cole slaw for sides. I had the pulled pork nachos. We ordered 5 of the sweet potato muffins too. The meats were tasty, juicy, smoky... top it off with their BBQ sauce and you're (literally) in hog heaven. The mac & cheese is clearly homemade which is exactly what you want. The coleslaw was a little meh so maybe we'll pass on that next time. We considered ordering a dozen sweet potato muffins to take with us, but we didn't --- they're really delicious. The only gripe I have were the nachos chips --- they were like those yellow movie theater-style nacho chips; however, the toppings were delicious of course. 
They do not have their liquor license yet, so BYOB of course, which is fine. I assume that will come later. In the tradition of BYOB they'll bring you a bucket of ice for your beverages.
I recommend you check it out. Mom said: "that chicken beast was THE BOMB"... and it really was :) check out Saucy's!!

Not being from Nashville I am a hot chicken novice, so no point of comparison with Princes, Bolton or Pepperfire.  But we are here to rate the food (not the building it sits in) and I have tried fried chicken here and there over a lifetime...and a stomach of steel ready to take on Nashville's best shot.

All I have to say is that Atlanta needs some hot chicken shacks quickly.  This shit is crack.  After reading the reviews, I called ahead and had no wait.  I went for the wings, pork chops and fries.

The chick was cooked perfect.  Crisp to the bite on the outside, but moist fall off the bone chik on the innards.  That's some fucking good chik let me tell you.   Colonel Sanders should have moved to TN.  

I'm a pork chop freak.  Give me the other white meat every day, or whatever they are calling it these days.  The other white meat was a home run.  My only complaint about each is the dry rub was pretty thick.  Feels a bit grainy in your mouth (and maybe this is the point, what do I know) so it's not something I'd eat every day.

The fries?  Sysco's finest crinkle cut fries.  I'll never get this.  You put a shit ton of effort into a quality chik product, cooked to order and all that shit...then you plop some standard crap fries on the plate?  Screw Sysco and their lousy substandard fries.  Even fast food joints like In and Out Burger are slamming a potato and cutting real fries in front of your face, places like this could do the same.

Overall though...bring the burn!

Had the pleasure of going here for lunch today and I was pleasantly surprised by everything from the staff to the food. Everybody couldn't of been nicer and now that I know where it is it is s sure thing that I will be back. I tried the 100 degree and the 200 degree. I thought the 200 was on the upper limit of my personal preference, but still good and should be fine if you eat hot things fairly often. 

The flavor was good on both and the 200 still had a good taste instead of going for pure heat like some places do. All in all glad I have a new place to show people from out of town some of Nashville's famous hot chicken. 

As a side note, the sweet fruit tea is pretty good.
Don't pass this place up, it's a quaint restaurant with a very casual feel and delicious meat! Don't skip on the goat mac n cheese!
Small aquarium that is showing its age; Think 90's saved by the bell. Was a nice way to spend an hour on a hot swampy day, but just a little pricy for its size and need of updating
This is an amazing aquarium! We almost passed it up, but it was definitely worth the cost! They have lots of really cool fish and exhibits! I really loved the rainforest area!

This is some serious Nashville Hot Chicken. I've had it several time. I like the 200°. The 400° is too painful for me. Very nice folks. Call ahead to order, takes about 30 minutes during lunch. It's as good as it gets. Get the pork chop sandwich. Try it for yourself. You'll thank me later.

Clean, fun and family friendly aquarium right off of the Mississippi River. River view from outside and short walk from the French Quarter. Huge seahorse exhibit, nice kids area. Only thing we weren't a fan of was the owl and eagle chained in one of the exhibit rooms.

I can't believe that no one has reviewed this place yet!  It is just incredible.  You enter through an enormous glass tunnel full of manta rays and scores of fish. Standing inside (underneath?)  the tunnel and looking up is the closest experience to scuba diving you can have while not, uh, actually scuba diving.  It is mind-blowing. And that's just the beginning.  They also have different sections: a rainforest area, a Mississippi River area. . .they have penguins, sea horses and sea dragons, two playful otters named Buck and Emma, and a white, blue-eyed alligator! (He's not an albino, it is a different type of mutation -- but he's beautiful!)  There's also an area where you can pet a baby shark and a whole pool full of rays.  (They apparently love to be touched, and they will come up and nuzzle you.  But be careful to pet their backs, and not their fins, because if you touch their fins they flip out, break the surface of the water and soak you in their gyrations.) I'm going back just so I can pet the rays; that's how great it was.  

They also have an IMAX theater and several gift shops of fun souveniers.

Great service! The waitress was really friendly and took our orders with a smile. I got the pulled pork sandwich and the portion was HUGE, especially for a 6-7 dollar sandwich. The sandwich itself was delicious with the slaw and would definitely recommend!

Plenty of variety of exhibits to see. The only problem was when I was looking at them, they made me feel sick, and this prevented me from fully enjoying it. The pictures were neat they took out front and reasonably priced.
Great collection of exotic large fish and other sea animals. There us penguin, seahorses, a white alligator and others. It was beautiful.

This place nails hot chicken.  I've had haddies (which I do really like), Pepperfire, and princes.  In my opinion- this is the best.  The ambiance is less than stellar (it's  located in a food court along w a Quiznos and nuvo burrito), and they don't serve beer (but you can bring your own!), but the amazingness of the food more than makes up for it.  The chicken packs in a fabulous flavor, great texture and perfect spice.  I got a medium and it's the absolute perfect heat level for those of us who love a good spicy dish but also are not interested in burning our insides out.   Crinkle fries are the bomb too (huge serving).  The staff/owners are awesome and so friendly and cool.  We WILL be back!

It is an amazing place.  None quite like it in the world.  It's not vast, but you can see the millions of dollars poured into this place.  Lost of learning going on.  Blah blah blah... worth the lotsa money to get in, just once.  

There is this poor penguin.  Blind with cataracts.  He is not with the others because the Law of Nature would banish him to death.  So he swims.  He swims, desperate, against the aquarium glass, swims, for hours, swims and swims and swims with his beak against the glass.  The announcer said, "He likes to swim."  But I don't know.  The dozens of penguins I was watching were not swimming for the sheer joy in it. Not endlessly, anyway.  

But he was, this poor, darling creature, being kept alive for what purpose?  I guess it's rather, he's not put to death because otherwise he is healthy.  The words, "He likes to swim" haunts me.  Anthropomorphism at its finest.  And, no doubt, I am guilty of the same thing.  

Besides, he's an amazing photo opportunity.  

In a few days he will fade from my memory, an example of my own problems, perhaps, my past, maybe even my present.  Why did I go to New Orleans from Oregon, if but to attempt to escape for a little while, only to find myself swimming against platen glass?  

Fortunately, or unfortunately, I had to face reality and return.  This little creature has a Doom so many of us can and do escape from, a Doom that some are trapped to live until the day we die:  He has no choice.  So he will ceaselessly, tirelessly, swim and will go absolutely nowhere.

The aquarium is nice , it is a bit overpriced, for what they have. I really like the one in Corpus Christi better. The best part was the ticket to the film. We saw the one about the hurricane in the swamp. It was brilliant. I highly recommend this film!

I might be a barbecue snob (Alabama is my home state and barbecue is a really serious thing there) but this place just isn't good. The sauce is really thin and didn't have much flavor, and the pulled pork was basically cooked down to mush. Seriously, it was gross. 

Everything is served in cheap plastic or styrofoam which is terrible for the environment (can't afford a dish washer? really?) and makes the food seem cheap. The baked beans aren't traditional--they have multiple types of beans in them, so be prepared for that surprise. The mac and cheese was dry. The sweet potato muffin was just weird. Why not cornbread?

While the girls at the register seem to try to make you feel unwelcome, the restaurant itself is cozy and charming. The atmosphere is really cool, very casual with an eclectic mix of vintage items to enjoy while you're waiting for your food to come. 

The hunt for decent barbecue in this city continues...

Note: We did not go to this restaurant during Mardi Gras and plenty of people eat at McDonalds but that doesn't make it good food. Downgrade to one star because of the owner's rant which appears consistent with the attitude of the staff and the lack of care given to the food.
Great place to visit lots of animals the penguin and sea turtle were my absolute favorite.

At first I felt like the price of admission was way too high. However, it's something really great to do! The variety of things to see and experience here are amazing. Animals are well tended to here and the ecosystems for those animals are huge! The aquarium has a solitary path one can walk through and see everything in about an hour. Check out the views on the additional floors. The huge tank with assorted animals at the end of the aquarium is great!

Staff was incredibly friendly. Hospitality second to none. 

 The brisket and bleu cheese slider was melt-in-your-mouth tender and with the ample sauce pairing options lead to a symphony of sweet and tangy I have never before encountered in my worldly travels. 

I will return to NOLA if for no other reason to fress at Saucy's BBQ

The Package including the theater worthed it. 
We spent a nice moment while it was raining a lit outside. 
A lot of different species interesting to see. Nice to do with kids.

Side are great! Had the mac and cheese, and the Asparagus.... yummy! Sauces are
good. Brisket was smoked perfectly.

What a waste of money....want to see the parakeet pay $1.50 extra...want to see the otter other than through thick glass...pay another $6...movie about the reefs..cough up another $6...
When my wife showed me the map I honestly thought there was a map missing ..took us less than an hour for the entire visit....shameful compared to other cities.
$29 just to get in the door, what a joke...

Wasn't impressed. It was rainy in NOLA so I thought I would check this place out. Admission cost is absurd (like $40) and the aquarium isn't even that big. Nothing special about this place. They have a cool food court area and gift shop but that's about it. Save your money.

So another hot chicken joint crossed off my list.  I had the 200° tenders and fries, with a bottle pepsi- $10.50

The heat was there, the flavor was there , the tenders were very moist.  It's not my favorite hot chicken,  but I see more return visits in my future.  I would rank it in top 5 so far.  

**alert**   it's a small operation, so unless you want to go, place your order, and wait 30 min. To 1 1/2 hours,  CALL AHEAD IS A MUST.

My family and I took the time to come here finally. It was a rainy day in NOLA and my pregnant sister-in-law thought it would be fun. There's a lot to see but for obvious reasons it's more on the expensive side. I would highly recommend if you have children or it's rainy day and you don't want to stay inside your hotel room. The staff is very polite, professional and engaging. My only suggestion would be for them to lower that picture price from $25. Lol

Great little spot on Magazine! You walk in, order at the register and someone brings your food. The brisket is fantastic! The best I've had in the city.  The brisket sandwich is huge and delicious. I also had their grilled asparagus and goat cheese macaroni and cheese---all of which were awesome! If you're looking for a casual dining spot with great food this is definitely for you!

Let me explain my 5 stars~ I don't care that the aquarium had empty tanks or displays that didnt make sense. I will even excuse (sigh) the fact I couldn't find staff to ask a few questions I had ( Isn't the point to educated?) Ok, I understand budget cuts I'm sure they are hanging on by a thread. Now the 5 stars come in because I fell in LOVE with a sea otter!! He was the biggest Ham you ever saw!! He was swimming and twirlling right in front of the glass for over 30 minutes! He loved the attention and I LOVED him right back! I swear he was posing and trying to give me enough time with my slow camera to get a good pic. I seriously could have stayed for a few hours watching him. His tank looked small for 2 sea otters (2 tanks connect)~ I was a lil sad that that was the case with many of the animals, snakes and fish had small tanks that you would see in a house, not a mega aquarium. Many empty tanks..did they die and not get replaced? Sigh...my imagination was overworking itself...20  bucks is alot but we did the 'expericence' for 39.99 and get 4 activiites 
(aquarium, imax,insectarium and zoo). So at 10 bux EXCELLENT deal!

Yeah....
I mean the aquarium was nice and all BUT it was literally just sad. If that makes sense.

This is based solely on taste, not atmosphere or wait times. I have given 400 degrees 4 chances and have been disappointed compared to other hot chicken joints in Nashville. I really can't ever get a flavor profile there, just tasted like chili powder... Heck, I didn't even taste the chicken. I ordered 200 and 400 and had the same result for both. If given a choice it would be Hattie B's for me. Nice staff BTW. Sorry guys, gotta be honest.

My family and I went to this store for the first time last week and we were truly blown away by how helpful the staff was. The owner clearly takes pride in his business and took the time to help us. The store is stocked with a wide array of tools and is kept maintained very well.

I must admit, when the suggestion was brought up to hit the New Orleans aquarium, I hesitated a little. I mean, I LOVE aquariums. A lot. I might be a bit of an aquarium snob. I love me those fishies and I don't mean just to eat. 
But New Orleans? What the heck is in the Gulf of Mexico? Will it be all alligators and crawfish? Are freshwater fish even pretty? 

Okay, obviously I need to get out more - mainly, away from the Pacific Ocean. 

When someone mentioned that Audubon had been compared to the Monterey aquarium in Cali (aka - the "Grand Poobah" of all things involving water and tanks) I figured this must be worth an investigation. Turns out Audubon can be described in many words, and one of them rhymes with "schmancy". 

From penguins to otters to alligators to even anacondas, this ain't your standard fish tank. Props to the numerous interactive exhibits that keep your eyes from glazing over after you've heard "fins" or "gills" for the 300th time. 

Okay I'll admit, I didn't really READ any of the signage cause I was too busy chasing down the penguins for a photo op...But considering there's an "insectarium" which could be potentially disgusting and terrifying, and potentially kick ass at the same time, I'll most likely be back.

Oh I love hot chicken. 

I got lost on my way in to find 400 degrees. I rounded the corner and backtracked to the random Quiznos and J Gumbo signage...in the food court? Could they? Yep!

I got two order of medium (200) to go. Fabulous news = you can mix heat levels! So that little voice in your head saying "Can you really handle 400 or are you going to be throwing away your dinner?" Now gets to say "Heck yeah do one of those, let's have an experiment on us!"

The staff cooks were su0er nice and we chatted about the hot chicken festival. I overheard the table of guys nearby dropping every hot chicken name place in town - yeah, it's kind of a beautiful cult thing and I love that they embrace it. 

Eleven minutes on the dot that they told me  - they know their business and I was out the door with my prize. Fifteen minutes later I got to dig in...and it was still piping hot (temp wise) for how fresh from the fryer it was, but oh so delightfully much better, that juicy chicken with a breading that actually maintained if not serious crispy then satisfying texture and that spice...all the hot kick and something just a little sweet when you really got down on the breading bits. The white bread was sodden with red of the secret spice - a real sign of my favorite thing (the flavor!) And the fries are just great and have that seasoning on them (because you need some fres, too to line your intestines with some recovery food). I love the sodden white bread I swear that's the best holding up those kind of gross looking red-infused glampy chunks like they're mana from heaven and stuffing them in. 

Fantastically cooked, great recipe, love the mix n match on the hot levels and my satisfying measures of perfection in the fries and bread.
This is a fun aquarium, though its a bit small. Even so I had a lot of fun and enjoyed feeding and petting the stingrays. It was also close to the hotel so it was an easy trip :)
It was so fun!!!!!! The gift shop was a little over priced but it was very worth it. The sting ray touching was cool but they are a little slimy.
A pretty unassuming neighborhood joint we popped into for lunch. The BBQ is GREAT. My favorite Carolina sauce was well represented, and everything we ate was incredibly delicious. I'd return.

This has indeed been the best hot chicken restaurant I've eaten in Nashville. Their clean and prepare their food as such. Even while I was pregnant I was craving spicy chicken. I ate some and my baby girl loved it in my tummy. (This was when nothing else would stay down), but 400 degrees chicken and fresh broccoli. I love this restaurant. The customer service is superb.

My husband and I, being from KY are always looking for good bbq. I got iced tea to drink and later found out it was out of a bottle. What bbq restaurant doesn't brew their own iced tea?!  We each got the 2 meat plate. I got the pork and smoked boudin and my husband got the brisket and pork. We each got extra sweet potato muffins and the baked beans and mac and cheese. The bbq sauces are on the side and I wish the waitress would have explained a little about the sauces, they have four different ones. The beans were really good and we liked the macaroni also. I hate mayo and am always glad when a place has more sides than cole slaw or potato salad. The sweet potato muffins were a little tough but the flavor was good. Maybe it was an off day for them. The flavor of the pork and boudin were good and so was the brisket, my husband claimed, though it looked a little dry to me. It's certainly not the best bbq I've had, but possibly the best I've had in New Orleans. I haven't tried McClure's and am looking forward to their opening. My husband and I both agreed we enjoyed our lunch and would return.

For a dank, miserable horribly cold and wet rainy day, this place was the perfect refuge.

It's a wee bit of a walk from the French Quarter to the Aquarium, down along the river.

You can get a pass for all 3 places that comes to cheaper than just individual passes, we got the 3 pass but never go to the other ones as we got distracted by Mardi Gras shenanigans on our way to the Insectarium.

Getting back to the Aquarium though, it was lots of fun. A bit of a maze because you never quite knew if you were going in the right direction. Now this might have had a bit to do with the fact that in Australia we always go left first... where as y'all go right. We went left. Got a bit lost. Entertained a few American's I'm sure while we were at it.

However the animals are cute. There's a huge huge fishy tank. With sharks and other big fish that could have easily taken a chunk out of the shark. Jelly fishies that change colour - I was mesmerised.

And who knew sea otters grew so big?! I want one. Not that I have a sea in my backyard or anything. But it's sooooooo cute! We don't have these back home so it was another thing that I might have totally behaved like a tourist over.

I was also stalked by a fish. It was huge. With a huge mouth. And it kept following me. Never been stalked by a fish before. 

All in all though, it's a great way to stay warm and enjoy the marine life.

I have been driving by this new BBQ location for a few weeks now and just finally had the chance to get a taste! Here are some things I love about this place: awesome location (close to my house); just the right size (not to small and not to big - close enough to talk to strangers and have a good time!); great food and awesome sweet tea! 

As a suggestion from Abby (very attentive waitress that was sincerely nice), I ordered the two meat plate with ribs and brisket with slaw and Mac and cheese. The ribs were great (dry ribs) and the brisket was very tender. Would I change a thing or two, maybe! I like to have a good rub on my brisket with a little char, but the meat was so tender that I didn't think about it - I just wanted more! The warmed Fantastic sauce was delicious, a nice tomato/vinegar/spicy mustard base.  They also served some other sauces that were quite good (besides the Fantastic -the Bold stood out to me the most). The coleslaw was a little thin on the dressing, but the Mac and cheese was amazing. 

I will go back often! They have great food and the management/staff make you feel at home! Enjoy!

The guys who run this place are simply amazing. Friendly,knowledgeable and serving up great food. In a sea of restaurant choices, you have to pick this place. The patters are large enough for two, the prices are right and the service quick.

I loved it. It was a great activity for a rainy day! The exhibits were beautiful and they had a ton of different fish. We especially enjoyed the Penguins, sting rays, jellyfish, otters, Gulf of Mexico exhibit, and the sting ray touch pool! I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a fun day in New Orleans, especially if you have kids with you!

This is a great way to beat the heat. We spent a couple of hours getting our $20 worth. My favorite exhibit by far was the 'Gulf of Mexico' with the sharks, fish and turtle swimming together in harmony. On a tangent, I like how this exhibit was sponsored by big oll companies (BP included). Oh, the irony.

They even have a sting ray feeding time at 2:30pm I think where you can buy food from the gift shop and feed rays in the shallow pool. The aquarium on the whole wasn't too crowded so you can really get around and see everything. They have a large collection of inhabitants from sea horses to tiny frogs so there's a lot to see here and most importantly beat the heat!

I've been a fan since they were in Metairie. I don't like beans; never have. Saucy's beans? I would sell you for a pint.   The owners are affable and always pleasant. As for the food, yeah...it is consistently delicious and delightful.

It took Frank all of 20 minutes from the time I first called him to verify that he had the necessary parts in his inventory, drive to my home and ring my door bell. Upon arrival Frank was very friendly and his abundant knowledge of all things drier related soon began to show itself.

All in all, from initial phone call to drier repair his departure it took only slightly less than 90 minutes. While he was here fixing my drier and telling amusing anecdotes he also provided several logic problems and other puzzles for my two very curious daughters.

Frank's level of service is nothing short of amazing. 

If you're even remotely near Havertown, PA and need an appliance repaired please do yourself a favor and call All Brands Appliance Service & Computer Repair.

We as a group got a little of everything. 

The spicy sausage was phenomenal, but remember when they say spicy, they mean spicy. As a Texan, I've had better brisket but that's not to say this wasn't a good piece of beef. Fat was melted and meat was wet. You'll be happy enough. Their best plate we came across was the pork ribs. They were some of the best ribs I've had around. 

Sauce lovers rejoice. They have a large array of sauces spanning from sweet to vinegar based to hot, hence the name. 

Best barbecue I'e had in New Orleans and will happily return if in need of some good pork while around Uptown.

It isn't the best aquarium I have ever been to and for the price if you have time for your trip I recommend going on their site, they are connected with the zoo and the butterfly garden and you can buy a bundle ticket for all three of them for half the price to go to all of them for regular price.

We came here to check out the new Mayan exhibit. As a member I am so annoyed with how members have to go to another line to get tickets. If they want to ensure members and not "bootleggers" are using their membership right add a photo to the member card or have them present an ID card at the entrance. Put turnstiles if you want a head count. We are members at the Steinhart aquarium and all we do is show them the card and ID and were are in..no lines. The new exhibit was pretty cool. If you've been to the Atlantis in Nassau its a smaller version of that. Still don't know where the shark tank (that was near the penguins) will go.

Nice little small spot. Decided to stop in. Good prices and a very friendly environment . It reminded me of someone's grandmas house. I ordered the 2combo Mac n cheese was delicious, very cheesy just the way I like it. The Briskets needed more seasoning and the ribs but the Bold sauce made it better. They have really good BBQ sauces. Not a bad place.
Tom's is my go-to place for auto repairs.  They're friendly, accommodating and fair.  They keep my cars running in top shape and I wouldn't go anywhere else for car repairs.

This is a must in the city of New Orleans. Great location down on the dock. We enjoyed the walk through but docking 2 stars because at $30/adult compared to other acquariums (boston) there was not as much as we would have liked to see. The tanks are interesting and penquin show cute, but movie not a great way to end the programming. It was 3D, but all about africa and its people fishing for sardines and we felt it a promo clip for something not really associated with an overall Acquarium and fish of new Orleans or tied to the city. 
Also, many tanks didn't clarify the exact fish in the tanks we were looking at. Some yes, but some were missing the descriptions to read about. 
Overall this aquarium is a nice visit while in the city and we recommend it, but try for alittle discount code to reduce its value to something we would have thought was fair at $21.95-23.95.

I ordered my food, a rib plate and Brisket.  On my trip to the bathroom the kitchen was full of bottles of Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce and microwaves so I thought, aw hell, this can't be a good sign.  Sure enough, it tasted like the meat was boiled and baked, there was no smoky flavor and I had to stop mid-rib cause I felt like I would get sick.  I wanted the sauce to at least be decent since the place was named Saucy's but even that was bad.  How did it win awards????!!!! Don't do it.

Always find something when I visit here. The selection is vast and if it's not in the store you can usually find it online. Returns are easy although it's all the way in the back of the store I feel weird when I walk through the store with my item. 

Always clean restrooms and holiday shopping is convenient. Get there early the lines can be very long especially at Christmas

I had to update my review and give the aquarium 5 stars because I recently visited and was able to experience Parakeet Pointe for the first time. It's a new outdoor exhibit with hundreds of beautiful parakeets and it might be my favorite thing about the aquarium now.

My daughter and I purchased bird seed sticks for a few dollars and headed into the exhibit. You just stand there, hold out your stick and one of the parakeets will come to you to eat off of it. It was awesome! I'm not kidding when I say I was just as excited as my little girl was when I had one of the beautifully colored birds land on my stick. So much fun!! The only thing that kind of took some getting used to was occasionally the birds will all "take flight" together at once and it's like that scary old movie "Birds" for a minute lol.  

You have to go and experience Parakeet Pointe! It is really special! I'm still a wannabe mermaid, but my daughter and I really loved it a lot.
Loved the exhibits and especially the penguins! Thought it was well laid out and very clean. Wish the sea otter exhibit was bigger but that's how it goes!

Tagged along with the wife on her business trip and spent about 5 nights in New Orleans.  
I don't know about most of you but one can only eat so many poboys, etoufee, etc.   Had enough of fried this and that we needed to try something different.  

Looked around for a bbq joint and ended up stopping at saucy's. Quick bus ride from Canal Street and the reviews were good. Also it being Sunday choices were limited since our main mode of getting around was public transportation. 

Really wanted to get the family platter but the wife talked me out of it as she thought it was going to be too much food so we ended up getting some ribs, pulled pork, brisket along with a side of some goat cheese Mac and baked beans. We also got an order of quesadillas 

Overall the food was tasty and the Mac and cheese was excellent. Smoked beans were also very good.  They had several different bbq sauces and they were all good.  The saucy's weren't  thick like the ones you see in a bottle (sweet baby rays) and I liked the fact that the sauces weren't overly sweet.  Another one of the sauce had a slight kick 

As far as service. I thought it was pretty good. The lady that was there was very attentive and kept my lemonade topped off.   She checked in several times.  Another gentleman from the back also checked in with us to make sure we were taken care of.  

I recommend a visit.  It's a short ride from bourbon/canal street. 

Tips: 
get a $3 day pass.  You can ride the bus or tram 24 hours.   

This place is BYOB so bring your fav alcohol. 

Make sure to check in on Yelp  ;) you save 20% off your bill.  (This place was my first Yelp checkin). 

Leave that 20% to the nice lady that's serving your food and topping off your drink.

We decided to come here since we were strolling around by the Mississippi River. The price was a little steep for just the aquarium but our kids loved it. Lots to see, lots of activities and even just an area for our kids to run around and climb on. 

We did the stingray petting, which was cute, there's a penguin feeding area, also fun, and many different kinds of jellyfish to keep our kids mesmerized. 

The gift shop isn't too bad compared to a few other aquarium shops, our girls walked out with mermaid dolls without us breaking the bank. All in all, a great time for the family.

Most Chain-like Hot Chicken in Nashville (It's located in a food court). Which might mean less character, but there's also more seating available. There's no signage on the outside, but just follow the directions to Quizno's and you'll get there. I went at 3 pm and found a spot in the smallish parking lot. No line either, but still a 20 minute wait for my mild chicken tenders with fries. Very friendly lady working the counter, and a good decent meal, although nothing made it stand out in particular. Great fries too. Would probably go with the 200 next time around.

While in New Orleans add snorkeling in the Audubon AquariumIn. What a wonderful experience. Desiree and Dan were outstanding. They really informed us about everything we were about to encounter and made things comfortable. My wife wanted no part in this and ended up loving it. A lot of thought was put into this program. Reservations are required and limited you only ned your bathing suit, everything else is provided.
Great BBQ- great prices and nothing was an afterthought- all the sides were top rate and meat was quality. Kids meals were a deal!

I came with a friend on a recommendation. It has a great little vibe. I got the alligator sausage amd a few different sides to test out. I really enjoyed them all. 

The place is small, so it can get packed really fast. Be prepared to wait. Other than that it was great.

"When's it my turn?
Wouldn't I love, love to explore that world up above?
Out of the sea
Wish I could be
Part of that world"- Ariel, Disney's Little Mermaid

You are WRONG Ariel, dead wrong!  Have you seen the global economy?  Have you noticed the Arab spring is turning to winter? If I were Trident* I'd make you go be part of that world and see how much you like it, you selfish, selfish mermaid.

Why do I mention Ariel, you ask?  It's because the sea (and other) life at the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas looked like they were enjoying things so much, I couldn't imagine them NOT wanting to live in the sea.    

This isn't a huge aquarium and it's not exhaustive, but for people with kids (or adults with short attention spans) it's just right.  Lots of fish, great information about the ecosystem in Louisiana and it's fairly interactive with exhibits as well as a great parakeet room.  I liked the sharks, penguins and otters a lot.

Some of the displays were a little worn and dated but I think this is a great way to kill a couple of hours and learn a little while you're at it.   

In closing, it's not all fireworks and Prince Eric, Ariel, but life out of the sea does have some good moments.

_________________________
*Trident is Ariel's dad, not the chewing gum. How weird would that be if gum could make you leave your oceanic home and live on land?

So I am from Tennessee and I have VERY high BBQ standards. 

We tried the pulled pork, alligator sausage, brisket and ribs. It was all sub par. The alligator sausage was actually awful and we couldn't finish it. Also the sweet potato roll thing was too sweet and dry. I tasted all their sauces and I appreciate the variety, but none of them were good. The one highlight is the mac and cheese is good and the beans are awesome. 

I hate to give this place two stars because my server and the manager/owner? was so nice to me, but the BBQ just wasn't good.

This is a great BBQ place!  Hands down the best Cajun Carolina Pulled Pork Sandwich on the planet!  Get it on the bun and add the southern sweet BBQ sauce!  Service was friendly and fast.  Thanks for a great meal!

I was very disappointed in this Aquarium.  I used to line live in New Orleans and went here a couple times with people who came to visit.  It is rather pricey to get into the aquarium and then it is not very big.  It is decorated well, but there is really not that much to see.  I have been to many other (Less well known) aquariums that were much nicer.  If you are in New Orleans on a trip, I wouldn't waste your time here unless you are an aquarium fanatic.

We came upon this winery over a year ago, and now it has become our favorite "tradition":  every few weeks, stroll through Peddler's Village on Saturday or Sunday morning, before the crowds swarm in, enjoy the charm of the seasons, browse the shops, and then sit down for a leisurely glass of wine on the winery's patio, sipping and "people watching".

In earlier times, the shop offered some cheese & crackers for purchase, but recently reduced their options to smoked salami [due to refrigeration concerns]. However, the owners do not mind if you bring something from outside, to enjoy with your wine.  So we take that into consideration before settling down on the patio. 

The patio is "pet friendly", and our twin mini-dachshunds enjoy sitting on our laps, watching the passers-by, and accepting compliments, along with bits of salami and cheese. Somehow, I can't see our 19 and 17 year-olds enjoying the same!  

The winery offers a wide variety of choices, and special tasting parties.  Haven't attended one of those yet, but will make a point.

This place has delicious bar b q. The meat is cooked to perfection, you don't need a knife, the meat dissolves in your mouth. My mouth is watering while writing this post. The brisket nachos are to die for. I have sampled everything on this menu, and have not been disappointed one time.

Fabulous swamp exhibit and the penguins are back.  The jelly fish & seahorse exhibits are way cool.  And they let you touch some stuff...although that's probably supposed to be mostly for kids.

I wish the IMax was bigger but you can't have everything.

I've done countless Aquariums with my kids. This place is a decent size and has a good variety of animals. It is set up well but it doesn't have a play area or anything to climb which breaks up the visit for the young ones. 

My kids really enjoyed the stingray touch pool and this was free. We arrived at the aquarium in the last hour but we probably didn't need any more time than that. I found it very pricey for something which entertains the kids for an hour. $29.95 for an adult and $21.95 for kids over 2 years.

I visit them all. Zoos, aquariums, botanical gardens. I am going to make it a life goal to attend them all! So when I came to New Orleans for just the weekend, the aquarium was one of the first places on the list that I wanted to attend. Everything is feels like it's within walking distance and the aquarium is no different. Probably less than half a mile from Jackson Square, you must come by and check it out.

There are many big aquariums in the US. The famous ones include the Georgia Aquarium, Long beach Aquarium of the Pacific, the Monterey Bay Aquarium and the New England Aquarium. I personally had not previously heard of the Aquarium of the Americas so it was a little bit of a surprise to me to find this here! There's generally an annoyingly long line in front. I wish they were more efficient. They didn't tell me that they had AAA discounts so be sure to ask for that. That being said, the fare is fairly standard for an aquarium of this size so it only made sense.

Skip the corny money making picture at the front and head inside. You're immediately greeted by a large group of look downs which is larger than any group I have seen elsewhere. It's like a maze here. If I remember correctly there is only 1 floor or if there is more, then no more than 2. They have a shark tunnel you walk through but I think one of the most interesting parts of the aquarium was at the end. There was a tank full of what I think are called paddlenose fish which was awesome. Never seen those before. I do wish however that their local fish section was larger. Would have loved to see a display on fish of the Mississippi or a larger section on the fisheries of New Orleans.

They did have neat alligators and tanks of blue crabs which was cool! I made it through it all in less than an hour and I did stop around to read the plaques although they are what you would think they would say. I probably learned the most in the local fish section even though it was on the smaller size.

Plenty of gifts to buy here... they should have more books available for the adults! Easy to walk to and a great place to visit in the early morning to avoid the crowds!

I highly recommend doing the VIP Backstage pass with the Penguins! You can register for it before hand and they do it 3 times a day. You pay $125 that covers your admission into the aquarium as well as at least an hour and a half of time spend hands on with the Penguins! You learn about them, prepare their food, go inside their exhibit to feed them and then play with some in a different room! At the end, the Penguins do art that you get to take home. It was definitely the highlight of my trip!! 

You can also pet stingrays which is very cool! The staff was very friendly and helpful! 

I throughly enjoyed my time!!

Memorial Day craving barbecue, my husband and I went to Saucy's. The brisket was tender, as well as ribs, meat falling off the bone! The mini sweet potato muffins are a scrumptious sweet to complement their signature vinegar sauce. The only reason I gave them 4/5 stars is that it was really hot to eat in there.

I was pleasantly surprised by my trip to the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas. I thought this was going to be something that catered only to kids and that I would be bored as hell, but I had a good time. It is a small place but I still managed to spend over 1.5 hours here. Besides seeing all the sea/wet animals, inside the aquarium you can also check out Parakeet Pointe, but since I was too lazy to use my map I never found or saw it, but it must be interesting, I suppose. 

At the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas there is definitely lots to see, experience and learn about if you are about that aquatic life or even if you're not.
Two great sauces, a sweet and a fairly hot. Great pulled pork sandwiches and Mac n goat cheese to die for

My wife and I recently relocated to New Orleans from NYC. This past week, my 12 year old daughter came down to visit, and we decided to go to the aquarium. Frankly, we weren't expecting much, but wow, were we surprised! It is a world class aquarium, and my family and I couldn't believe how well done everything was. The exhibits cover many, many marine subjects and are done in depth. It was truly amazing. We have been to aquariums in many states and this was by far the best. I am glad I purchased a family membership, because we are sure to return again. If the insectarium and Audubon Zoo are even close to the aquarium in quality, New Orleans is a very lucky city!

The service here is so friendly! Also, their sweet potato muffin is divine! Their ribs and pulled pork are excellent, but the brisket was a bit dry for my taste. The only downside is that the only 'greens' for their side coleslaw. I wish they had some collards!

When I think American wine, of course I conjure up images of sun-drenched Californian valleys.  I'm for competitive markets and all that, but really -- the East Coast north of the Mason-Dixon line is not exactly vineyard material, and it seems a little silly to me that people try so hard.  Still, the wine here is all right, and most bottles run about $12-15, which is not bad.  And for your first-time check-in on Yelp, there's currently a 20% discount.  I grabbed a bottle of apple cider wine, which seems like a distinct offering that you can't often find in retail.  Also provides something "adult" to do in this area.

I am a fan of fish, so last night I decided I was going to go see some fish.  So this afternoon I decided to run out to NOLA and and check out Audubon Aquarium.  Nestled up against the Mississippi river this small but very well stocked aquarium.  As soon as you begin the tour, you enter an aquatic tunnel with hundreds of fish swimming around you.  Much like the Long Beach Aquarium of the Pacific, AAA has regional fish as well as some great special attractions.  For me the pinnacle of the visit was the penguin exhibit.

A tour of AAA takes about A hours so it might be good to catch an Max movie while you are here.  If you are visiting on a Friday or Saturday, check the web site and you might be able to catch a great movie in Max. This week was dark night and had I known, it would have been a great Friday night.

If you have kids, this is a great place to go.
Nice exhibits but for the price to get in it is extremely small, less than an hour to go through the entire aquarium.
The food was really good, but Danielle the person that too my order over the phone was an idiot. She was very rude & very unprofessional. She should not be in customer service at all.
The best bbq ever!!!  Wonderful wait staff and relaxing atmosphere. S/B rated #1 in the City. Thank you Saucy's for a GREAT lunch before flying back to Cali.

This is the best BBQ place I have ever eaten at! The owners Gary and Rich go out of their way to make sure you have an amazing experience! The atmosphere is laid back and fun, very easy going. The location is perfectly centralized on Magazine street, with a lot of people watching, but not crowded. Great for hanging out with friends, food and booze! Everything on the menu is outstanding and you can really tell these guys put a lot of love into what they do!

The Best Hot Chicken in Nashville. 


I've had Prince's. 
I've had Bolton's. 
I've had Hattie B's.
I've had Pepperfire. 
I've had hot chicken all over this music infested town and Aquia's 400 Degrees is the hands down best! Consistent time after time. (This is a big deal because you never know who's behind the wheel at some of these joints)...400 Degrees is rock solid. The location is smack downtown near New convention center and hotels. It's shares a building with a Quiznos and burrito joint and  Parking is easy. 
To be honest I'd start out with the mildest temp(100degrees) because this chicken leaves a mark! 
Seriously it's hot with flavor as opposed to just being hot. Big difference!
There's a wait. Be prepared and be patient. This is not chicken in a hurry. It's a bad ass delicious,mouth watering and scorching taste treat! I wish I had some right now ! 
Here's a little advice.... Call your order in at least 35 to 45 minutes before you wanna get it. Trust me on this. Call it in!
You're welcome.

My kids love this magical place. You can view from sharks to alligators. When you're hungry and half way done, there's the food court. They have pizza, hamburgers, wraps, and fries. The price is reasonable. They also have 2 gift shops. Its hard not to go in and shop when you have kids.

I am not your typical hot chicken customer.  I can't handle spicy food.  It makes we want to die and I have no idea why people voluntarily torture themselves. 

That being said, I like 400 degrees.
