It's in a little food court area with an eclectic little mix of restaurants, so I suppose I have other options when my boyfriend's hot chicken cravings hit, but I don't think I'll ever try them. 

The chicken is classified in degrees - 0, 100, 200, 400.  
If you're a wimp like me, get the 0.  It's plain ol' fried chicken with a tiny touch of spice from the seasoning.  The chicken is juicy and delicious. 
On my second visit I decided to man up and try the 100... and I survived.  It's apparently nothing to most people, but my runny nose and watery eyes and fire breathing suggested otherwise.  The first few bites aren't bad, but the cumulative effect by the end had me cramming ketchup-covered fries down my throat for relief.  I still liked it, though, because while hot it still had flavor.  I don't see the point in burning your face off if your taste buds are burned off too.  

My wimpy body will never let me become a hot & spicy connoisseur, but every now and then I'll get my 100 and clear out my sinuses and feel proud of myself.  Maybe I'll get up to 200 one of these days.  Can you train yourself for heat?  I'll report back. 

PS: You will wait a long time for your food. Be warned.
I love aquariums, especially as a way to escape the NOLA humidity for a few hours. Well worth the price of admission and right next to the mighty Mississippi!

Pretty good size, price is a bit for me to make it a all the time spot to visit. Loved the ocean tank with the sharks and tuna fish. The food and drinks at the food court is way high, but good family place. Hope to see the zoo next time.

Taking over the spot that once held by EMPANOLA in St. Roch Market Torshi is a welcome and delicious addition to an eclectic lineup.

They are serving a lot of your Mediterranean favorites but with an Egyptian twist. Staff is friendly and attentive, serving portions hefty and well priced.

The hummus and baba ganoush are a most have as are the gyros and shawarmas. 

On a hot summer day make sure to get the mint tea slushy it is ideal drink for our hut humming days.

Take a break from drunken revelry and go look at fish. They have some very cool fish at this place. Big old snakes. Jack knife fish were cool. Lots of weird sea horses. The recovering owl was really cool. Big tropical fish including Dalmatian spotted rays and catfish bigger than a Toyota. I love aquariums and this place was a nice one. I'd go back!
I called on a Friday to inquire about a same day service for our washing machine, they had an answering machine pocking up their calls. No one even bothered to return my call.

I love Dr Oki and his staff, he is very intelligent and you can trust everything he says! I feel incredibly safe with him. He has a wonderful bedside manner and you can tell he truly cares about the health of both momma and baby!

Frank is great! Friendly, quick, and efficient. He explains what he's doing and gives you great info about your equipment. He fixed our dryer in less than 20 minutes and told me a few great stories too :-) Highly reccomended!!

Four words posted on the sign at the counter made me terrified, yet intrigued, by 400 Degrees' hottest offering, the 400-degree chicken:

"It'll burn you twice."

It did.

But despite the literal double-edged sword that pierced my body during and after my dive into delicious, deep-fried death, I am happy. I have found the best hot chicken in Nashville.

400 Degrees offers four flavors -- 0, 100, 200 and 400. The rise in degrees represents the corresponding level of heat. I tested the 100 -- pleasantly spicy with crispy, salty breading; the 200 -- a cornucopia of flavor covering the tongue with tantalizing, spicy complexity; and the 400 -- more than "heat for heat's sake," it features dynamite flavor and an angry-yet-likable kick.

Every variety of chicken featured the same degree of moistness, flakiness and grease-soaked goodness. That's what sets 400 Degrees apart -- its chicken is the freshest in town, with the best consistency I've experienced. 

Another reason 400 Degrees earns its fifth star: The experience. Aqui, the owner, mans the deep fryer herself, with personality and passion. She made uplifting, sassy smalltalk while she battered my bird. She also let my brother and I mix and match our flavors. Thank goodness, because I can't imagine a full meal of the 400 fireballs. Also, while Prince's may pride itself on quirky customer service and Hattie B's on its intimate dining quarters, 400 is spacious, clean and nice. It shares a food court with three other restaurants, which means there are plenty of napkins to go around.

All you need to know is this: I'm not a frequent reviewer. It usually takes me a couple months to recap my experience at a given restaurant. But I went to 400 Degrees yesterday, and I felt so compelled to share my praise that I hopped on the computer right when I got to work and went straight to Yelp.

It's that good. Even though it does, in fact, burn twice.
A great little barbeque place with great food and good service. The brisket is amazing. Be sure to get the baked beans! Not many tables and can get crowded so go early.

We live in Atlanta and have tried almost all of the Hot Fried Chicken places in Nashville. We were so excited to try this place and ended up being so disappointed. 

First, as soon as we walked in, the person at the register (maybe the owner) was rude. I nearly walked out immediately by my partner really wanted to try the food. 

We ordered wings (200 degrees), fries, and chicken tenders (100 degrees). The best thing on the plate was the fries and I still dipped those in ranch dressing. 

The wings had ZERO flavor other than being hot and tasted like they were caked in paprika. We had to add salt just to get through them. 

The tenders had a bit more flavor but we're still nothing to write home about. 

They get two starts because the food was actually made fresh and the health code rating is 100.  

We won't be coming back.
BBQ pork, brisket, and chicken plates are the best deals. Comes with 2 side and muffin. Get the macaroni with goat cheese. Great place to hang out with free wifi. Aloha. .

Went to Saucy's for lunch with my husband. My parents had said they didn't like it, but some friends of ours said that they loved it. So we went. Overall, it's ok. I got the brisket sandwhich and husband got the pulled pork sandwich. It was ok. Nothing spectacular about it. The sauces you could use tasted a lot like those you can buy at the store. The sweet sauce tasted oddly like Sweet Baby Ray's. 

The boudin was good, but we're pretty sure was Richard's, which also can be bought in the store.

Not able to get a dressed sandwich, only onions and pickles. No bueno. 

It was ok. So I would go again, but not go out of my way to get there.

While the aquarium itself is on the smaller side (it doesn't look like it from the outside but once you're in there you notice it's not THAT big), the penguin behind the scene program is worth every penny.

On our annual trip, my friends and I always try to do something animal-related.  This trip we decided on the penguin tour.  The director of the program explains the differences between types of penguins and such. Then you put together their fish "appetizer".  Then you are put in a room with two penguins!  They are some of the friendliest little guys you'll ever meet!  You are allowed to hold the penguins, ask questions, and interact with them.  Once everyone in the group has held one, the penguins paint a picture for you, which you later take home.  After all that fun, you go into the actual exhibit and get to wave at the school field trips on the other side of the glass, while also feeding all the penguins and interacting some more.  

Like I said before, it is worth every penny.

I'm really five years old.

I've been on a BBQ kick ever since I had the brisket at The Joint. I'm on a bit of a mission to taste all of the brisket that I can get my saucy little fingers on. Saucy's has some great brisket and they serve it with horseradish. I've never had it like that, and boy, I didn't know what I was missing out on.  It was a very nice and delicious touch. The brisket is tender and cooked perfectly with lots of flavor. For my sides I chose the potato salad and the baked beans. I liked both, but neither were anything to write home about. 

Service was good...no complaints there. The place is pretty small and a tad divey, but that adds to it's charm. On the table there were four different sauces to chose from and I sampled them all and they were pretty good.

Yay! Another great BBQ place in Nola!

As someone who has been to many of America's great zoos and aquariums I had high hopes for the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas - and while there were some hits, there were also quite a few misses.  Well kept but expensive, the space is very small and extensively children oriented compared to Monterey Bay, Tampa, Shedd, and others.  The discus display, the albino gator, and the Mississipi Delta area should not be missed.

Such delightful service!!! Genuinely cares about customers. BBQ is great but if you don't order the goat mac and cheese you're wasting everyone's time! Favorite quick lunch when I'm in a rush at work.
Saucy's is always wonderful. Great food, great owner and great atmosphere. Really fantastic ribs and pulled pork sandwiches.

We attended a party in Gladwyne, PA.  on June 3. We had arrived at approximately 7:00 pm. our car was valet parked using the services of EMPIRE VALET, LLC.  

When we tried to retrieve our vehicle close to 12 AM June 4,  we were told by the valet service, they could not find our key.  We waited for about 45 minutes and there was no sign of our vehicle or key. 

We live in Princeton, NJ.  I had plans to leave for a funeral in DC that morning at 4:00 AM. We found ourselves 80 miles from home, with no key to our vehicle or home. In fact when we asked the valet service where our car was, the gentleman could not even give us a specific location. He gave us an approximate location. 

That night we had to find a way home, call a locksmith to get into our house, and then drive back to pick up our car to drive down to DC. Given the fact that the valet service had not provided the precise location of the car, once we arrived in the general vicinity of the car, we had to drive around for 30 minutes until we finally found the car at 5 AM! Not counting the many inconveniences caused due to the irresponsible crew of Empire Valet. The expense incurred was $542 for locksmith and duplicate key! I would not recommend the services of Empire Valet in Wayne, PA.

Very rare to find authentic Egyptian. The gyro platter was moist and humus was smooth. The hibiscus rose water was out of this world, very exotic and well balanced. Everything was made from scratch with true passion for the craft. The owner is a delight.

Pretty small, especially for what they're charging. The rainforest part was fun and very well detailed. They have the walk under tunnel, and that was definitely fun. Made friends with a sting ray. There were a couple big exhibits, but other than that, mostly pretty small ones. It was an okay variety.

Loved this aquarium!!! The employees were so nice and interactive with the kids. It was well worth the money as there is so much to see and do! The walk to the aquarium was awesome and parking was easy! They literally have everything and had us as well as our kids on awwwwe the entire time! We had a great day and will be back for more! I'm sure we didn't even see everything they have to offer!

This is around 4.5 stars for me. I've hit all the major fried chicken places around Nashville multiple times over the past three and a half years. I like 400 Degrees more than most places because the chicken is both flavorful and spicy (two very different things). The chicken is less greasy than some places and the sides weren't bad at all.

Honestly everyone has different [and very personal] preferences when it comes to fried chicken in the south. Some will hop on Prince, others claim Bolton, some swear by Monell, and then there's the handful of restaurants that aren't specific for fried chicken but have it on their menu somewhere.

You can't really go wrong at any of these locations when it comes down to the fried chicken. Sure there are differences in flavor, greasiness, and spiciness, but they'll change the rating AT MOST 1 star (closer to 0.5 star). It boils down to personal preference and auxiliary stuff like wait times, customer service, cleanliness, etc when you see differences in reviews among those restaurants mentioned above.

Whatever. It's fried chicken and you're in the South. You can't find it better elsewhere. If you dislike all of them, then I'll be happy to examine you. ;-)

We've used Empire Valet on four different occasions now and they really are "the best in the business".  Jon is a pleasure to work with, his staff is polite and friendly, and they are a great value for the dollar.  Can't say enough good things about Empire Valet!  I would highly recommend them.

This is a good local attraction and for those who haven't visited an aquarium in a while.  They have a nice shark tank, some well themed exhibits (ie: a misty Amazon rainforest) and even a sting ray touch pool.  I felt the exhibits were not as informative as they could have been and serve more as an introductory experience for young children. You may be disappointed if you have been to any of the bigger aquariums like the Georgia Aquarium.

It was a very nice aquarium with many kinds of different aquatic animals to look at ranging from jellyfish to otters. Our only big complaint was just all the kids and how cramped and loud it was with them. Besides that it was great and would definitely recommend going there.

Went for a wine tasting. Wines were good,but the tasting in their little room was kind of weird. The original winery is in West Chester. Groupon offered a deal, which was worth it, but I wouldnt go back. Peddler's villiage is dying.

I enjoyed my visit here. There are amazing fish and penguins and jelly fish. If you've never seen the movie Birds, the Parakeet Pointe is a must-visit: it's a room full of yellow, blue, and green parakeets that will come and land on your finger, your shoulder, your head, etc. You can feed them but that's not necessary (be on the lookout for droppings). The parakeets and the jelly fish alone were worth the price of admission.

Speaking of the price of admission, it was not cheap. $22.50 seems a bit steep for one admission to one of the Audubon sites. For that amount, it would be nice to be able to visit both the Aquarium and the Insectarium (which is nearby), but, alas, the Insectarium is a separate charge. You see quite a bit at the Aquarium for the money, but you can get through it in an hour. It goes fast, even with crowds (which you will encounter on a Saturday, natch).
It is warm in the building, so dress appropriate in layers that you can remove as needed.

I didn't stop to read too many of the informational placards, but if you or your kids are into those, there are quite a few around the facility. On the day that I visited, they also had face-painting, which kids seemed to love. All of the kids there seemed to be having a good time, in general. They especially liked the Finding Nemo tank, the otters, and the jelly fish.

Overall, the Aquarium is expensive but mostly worth it. If I had to choose, though, I might put the money toward the Audubon Zoo, which is located in Uptown but well worth a visit.

Took my cousin from Kansas try 400 degree hot chicken today since it was featured on the travel channel.  I'll have to say the chicken was moist, full of flavor and hot! Haha  everything was made fresh from the time you order!!! Go check out 400 degrees hot chicken . You won't be disappointed!! Thanks so much for the hospitality Aqui ! I will definitely return when I'm in the neighborhood!

I haven't had the time to order anything other than a couple of sandwiches from Saucy's but my experience has been encouraging.  

The buns were fresh, the pulled pork was very good, very tender and moist.  I liked the cole slaw but they also serve a pulled pork sandwich with bleu cheese dressing on the slaw.  Nice combination but a little more bleu cheese, please.

Sandwiches are about $8 each and the menu includes brisket, chicken and smoked sausage.  

Attentive staff and a nice location on Magazine, with some outdoor tables available.  It's very good to have a bbq place in the neighborhood.

we really had a great time! its a fantastic place to take your kids. there was so much to see and a lot of information too! a penguin feeding, a very large tank that included several sharks and a tortuous, a white alligator, so many different fish and jellies to see, a gift shop and several places to take pictures.  everyone had a great time here.

I LOVE THIS AQUARIUM!

Seriously. I won't shut up about how awesome it is. I fell in love as soon as I walked in and saw their aquatic tunnel. You can walk through and view their Caribbean Reef. How cool! 

I really enjoyed the different sections they have. I couldn't believe they had an Amazon Rain Forest area. It was definitely interesting and had a sweet treehouse type thing that I loved playing in. I could have spent the entire day at this aquarium. 

At the end of our visit we sat and watched the animals in the big tank for quite a while. It was dark and peaceful in there and I totally wanted to take a nap.

I can't wait to go back to New Orleans and visit this aquarium again.

I'm a supporter of the Audubon Nature Institue and that includes the Aquarium of the Americas. I picked up a membership for myself and my girlfriend to attend the Audubon family which is worth every penny. The Aquarium may not be as big as others I've been too (the Georgia Aquarium is HUGE) but it's still filled with great exhibits. 

My two favorites are the penguins and the otters, Buck and Emma. I love the penguins and their dapper little tuxedo styled feathers. I can spend hours watching them play and swim. Plus one of the rock penguins is named Dennis! The otters are equally fun to watch. Catch them during feeding if you can. Buck and Emma are quite active most days and genuinely love their environment and their enrichment program.

Other great sights include the white alligator and the sharks, plus the touching tanks where you can pet a starfish or ray. Throw in an IMAX right next door and it's a fun afternoon in the air conditioning (a must during the brutal New Orleans summers).

Is the price too much for what you get? I don't think so but I can understand if others do. Best thing you can do is get a combo ticket for the Audubon Zoo and the Aquarium and save. Or get a membership like I did. Just three trips to the Zoo/Aquarium in a year and it pays for itself.
I loved the movie on The Coral Reef. That film was epic.

Came to visit New Orleans & wanted a change from the normal Creole food. Currently staying at a hotel on Royal street so wasn't down the block, took streetcar from canal & from there was about ten minutes! 
Now to the food, was very, very good. Portion is more on the small side, but very tasty. I had the brisket quesadilla with the baked beans. Both were delish. My friend had the ribs with the cole slaw and mac a cheese. I tried the everything but the ribs & it was deff all a must have. The ribs were good but a little greasy. Deff worth trying, but remember portions are small.
Awesome aquarium! Kind of expensive admission, but worth it.  The sea otters are soooo entertaining and feeding  the stingrays is a must do!

Pretty good aquarium. I think we may be a little biased as we've visited both Shedd Aquarium and Monterey Bay Aquarium in the last 6 months. Monterey is the best Aquarium in the states imho. I visited with my 3 1/2 year old and baby. Things didn't hold my toddler's attention as much as I thought they would so I'm glad they had the little play area, we visited that twice. The food options were meh. I think NOLA could step up their attractions' food. We fed the birds which was fun. We pet the sting rays which we've done in the past. They didn't require us to wash beforehand like we've done at other places when petting them so I thought that was a bit negligent. There are some beautiful exhibits and the categorization is nice and well done. The Amazon area is a nice departure from the typical tanks you see in aquariums. All in all it's a nice aquarium and the staff was very pleasant but it didn't take us all day as I'd hoped, we were there on a weekday from 10-2ish and we stretched to be there that long.

I spoke to the gentleman over the phone and explained the problem with my washer. He had me turn on the washer so he could hear the noise that it was making. He figured it was an easy enough fix that he could guide me thru it over the phone. It took just 15 minutes and the washer was back running fine. He even ignored a few incoming calls on his end while we were on the phone rather than put me on hold. I'd say this a pretty honest man who would come to your home and give you the best service possible at a fair price. How many other service people would do that for you rather than take you for a few hundred bucks. Not to mention it's 2 weeks before xmas.

I really love to go to this place on weekday afternoon when it's not busy and you can set your own pace without being shuffled or herded. It's got some wonderful exhibits for both children and adults, but as a local, I don't like to fight big crowds in order to do things, so I prefer to go when it isn't too busy.

 All in all it's an hour to an hour and a half worth of time and you'll enjoy it. Look for the owls in the ceiling near the end!
The brisket is tender and delicious! Horseradish dip and their sauces are awesome, too.

Decent aquarium. I am usually very picky about aquariums but I did have a chance to appreciate some of the attractions displayed for me. The penguins were a huge plus, as well as the sea otters. They had some diving suits on display which drew my attention (i am an active scuba diver) and I was glued to them for a while.  A lot of the marine displays showcase artificial corals which really pull away from the realism that they are trying to achieve with some of the tanks. I appreciated the shark tank, the otters and the penguins the most. The albino gator was awesome and I did not see any parakeet rooms or the such, or I would have gladly taken advantage of that as well. I also did not make it to the Zoo or Insectarium because of all the other stuff I had to get done while in NOLA.

I have not tried other hot chicken places either. The outside was crispy which is how I want it. i got the 400 degrees and it kicked my butt. They warned me but I wanted to do the macho thing. Next time, I'll opt for the 200. Ambiance is lacking but the food is sure tasty. The sweet tea was really good as well.

Very disappointed in this bbq. The meat had a nice flavor, but the sauce was definitely lacking! I ordered grilled asparagus, which weren't done at all. I've had much better baked beans, not sure what to suggest there. The Mac and cheese was pretty good.

Let me just first start by saying I really appreciate what they're doing here. As a barbecue aficionado, I can't help but bemoan the inexplicably desolate landscape that is the New Orleans BBQ scene (with the exception of a few new places that have popped up). We could use all the competition we can get in the BBQ category.

I'll also give them credit for the things they do right here:

1) the sweet potato muffins are pretty good, and are always a nice surprise to find in your to- go box.

2) they are never stingy about the amount of sauce they give you whether you dine in or eat out. They live up to that name pretty well.

3) the smoked beans have a decent smoky flavor, but could probably be improved with more spices and/or some meat in there like a lot of bbq joints do. 

Unfortunately, the quality of the bbq itself leaves a lot to be desired. I've gotten pretty much everything on the menu here, hoping that one thing will be better than the next. 

The sandwiches are fine, but the bread seems a little stale. 

The sausage is juicy, but at the cost of any real semblance of char on the outside.

The ribs--I get why some of the reviews have claims about microwaves. The bark on the ribs is just not there, and the rub mixture usually is just a semi-moist topping on them, reflecting none of that heat induced "sticks to the rib" trademark of many rib rubs. They do very much seem like ribs that have been microwaved. The meat on the ribs follows suit--it's tough and dry, with a bunch of chew. I've smoked ribs many times before, and these are exactly what microwaved  next day ribs come out like.

The pulled pork needs spices, or something to kick up the flavor. It's just kind of bland. I've never gotten a portion that has much bark mixed in, and maybe this could help, I don't really know. 

I would give them two stars, but the beans are decent and the muffins are not bad.

We're not a big BBQ market, but when others are doing melt in your mouth ribs with great bark and spiced pulled pork that is both juicy and flavorful, it becomes difficult to justify going to Saucy's, even if those other places are only open Weds-Saturday.
We loved this aquarium! Lots to do and learn for the kids. A bit pricey--bring a coupon. Ok food. Will definitely return.

This was my first time with Nashville Hot Chicken.  Went for the 200 degree version which was darn hot.   Suggest you do the same, unless you are experienced.  I had to wait 20 minutes, but the chicken was fresh and hot and outstanding.   The lady working the counter was a sweetheart, and I wouldn't think of going anywhere else.  Suggest you order ahead or be prepared to wait, since every order is fresh cooked.

Tom's Automotive is an Elkins Park treasure. We've been using Tom's for over fifteen years, bringing six different vehicles to the shop during that time. Have turned several neighbors on to this reliable, friendly, reasonable and competant auto service center over the years. The bottom line is that the customer gets prompt, honest, good work at a fair price. The bonus is that the place is run by a warm, smart guy with a witty style who happens to be quite an animal lover: witness the parrots and tropical fish adorning his little office space. You won't be disappointed.

I was very excited to order chicken from this establishment. My coworkers rave about it and it always smells great.  I'm sure the food is fantastic, BUT....I will never know.   I drove to 400 Degrees at around 6:25p Thursday night.  I checked Google for directions and the time to make sure they were still open.  Per Google, 400 Degrees closes at 7pm.   I got there at 6:35 and the cashier said "We're not taking any more orders."   Wow.  I just bowed out while privately vowing to myself never to return.  Who turns away a customer?  
Do better!

We've been Audubon members for three years and its such a good deal to join/get the annual membership. 

As far as the Aquarium goes, its very well done, flows fairly easily, and has some amazing exhibits. There's an IMAX theater and feeding of the various animals throughout the day. There's also an indoor play area near the sting ray tank. Around the Mississippi River exhibits, look up and around for the hawk, owl, and other live birds perched over head. 

Tickets for single visits can be a little high, but it is one of the best kid-friendly activities in the downtown along with the New Orleans Children's Museum.  Certainly worth the trip and has loads of photo ops for the family on vacation here.
Super fresh, delicious food. I got the falafel platter. The falafel was crispy and the sesame seeds were a great addition. The hummus & salad were equally good.

It took nearly 30 minutes to get our food. We had to be somewhere and I was clearly upset that it was taking so long. The gentleman behind the counter picked up on my dissatisfaction, and was very apologetic that it took longer than expected. I did not ask for any recompense, but he enthusiastically insisted. I probably should have passed on his baklava offer, since we were already running behind, but I am glad that I accepted because it was delicious. 

All of the food was delicious. The staff, there was a lady hustling behind the counter too, were really committed to doing the best they could in the limited space that they have, and they were committed to my satisfaction. 

I will probably eat there again, but next the visit will be when I have more time to wait for the scrumptious food.

A very nice facility with something for all ages. My favorite exhibits were the penguins and the sea otter. The penguins are much more interactive than at Sea World. Here they swim right up to the glass and interact with the guests. All of the exhibits were well maintained and signage was informative without being overwhelming.

We bought the Audubon Experience, so I have to go see this aquarium.  We are members of the Monterey Bay Aquarium, so when you compare them just by size, of course I have to deduct a star.  However, given that, this is still a very good aquarium.

Our highlight was the Stingray touch pool.  When we were at Monterey Aquarium, even though there is also a Stingray touch pool, we were never able to touch the Stingray.  1) b/c the water is way cold 2) the Stingrays didn't really like people touching them. Here, at this aquarium, the Stingrays are really friendly, they come up to you many times, and I and even my daughter who's only 9 can touch them.  My daughter who is usually frightened were so curious that day, and she touched them nonstop.  I think the Stingrays here are so friendly, b/c they were also fed by people/ visitors, unlike Monterey.  Just this is worth my money!

The food court is a bit lame.  They made the food when we ordered them (at 2 pm) I guess b/c lunch time was over, so the wait was a bit longer than usual. 

Other than that, you should visit this aquarium, it has the essential sea creatures that everyone looks for.

I came here on the fourth of July with a group of three friends. We were excited to walk around Peddlers Village and get to sample some wine. When we walked in to the nearly empty shop we weren't even greeted or noticed. My friends and I walked up to a gentlemen standing at the main room wine bar and asked him if they did wine tastings and he simply told us we had to go into the adjoining room where a woman was at another bar.  Upon entering that bar we were told we had to go back to the other room to pay the gentlemen we just left. So I suggested we pay after, which was fine. We sat at a table in a clean and quaint room for our tasting. Then we were informed that we could do a free tasting of sweet wines in the other room but we decided to pay the $12 for the dry wines. I had to ask for a wine list so I would even know what I was sampling. The lady gave us minimal information and it took on average 15 minutes between each sample for her to return to our table 5 feet from the bar.  At this time there was only 2 other people sampling wine so the fact we barely received any customer service was confusing. After tasting 5 wines, we paid and sampled some sweet wines (that were way to sweet for my likeing) and left. I was able to use the 20% off check in deal on a bottle. 
Over all, I wouldn't suggest this place if you are looking to learn about different wines in a timely manner with anything that resembles customer service. If the place was busy I would've understood the lack of attention but like I said, there were two people working and just my small group and one other couple.

400 degrees is my FAVORITE hot chicken spot in Nashville!!  Aqui, the owner, is always friendly and greets you when you walk in.  I usually order the 100(it's spicy, but won't have you begging for your mommy) and my son orders the 200 (hot and had me sweating).  The thing I love about 400 degrees is that it tastes great; you don't lose any flavor with the heat.  It is consistently good!!  If you're ever in Nashville you must try 400 degrees.  Oh, call ahead to place your order so you won't have to wait long when you pick up. (everything is cooked to order)

Saucy's pleasantly surprised me because 1.) I don't really like BBQ and 2.) I had a taste for oysters but landed here by default because I didn't get the summer vacation memo for Casamento's up the street.

Despite my hesitation, Saucy's wasn't such a bad second pick. My pulled pork sandwich was juicy, but the chipotle BBQ sauce really set it off. My smoked beans were also a great compliment to the sandwich. 

The service was great! This place is small but has tons of charm.

I love this place. The BBQ is better than The Joint in my opinion...and it's a muuuch shorter drive for me. My favorite thing on the menu is the nachos but the Brisket and Ribs are outta this world. I think they have 20 dollar racks on day a week (maybe Sunday?) Anyway it's a really cool atmosphere and they have huge tv's so I feel like it would be a good game day spot!

Really the best tasting chicken in the 'Ville'.  Smooth and favorable...try it you will like it...hummed princess is good but; the folks that work there Think that they are doing you a good deed for allowing you to eat their chicken..Not friendly at all...

Dick was amazing and was able to guide us in the right direction of what to get! We got the 2 meat with two sides. 
Husband got the alligator sausage and the pulled pork with the smoked beans and the goat cheese mac! And he got a side of rib.
I got the brisket and ribs with grilled asparagus and the goat cheese mac. I would have switched the brisket for the sausage personally but everything had such amazing flavors! 
That dick sauce was amazing too-it's like a creole mayo sauce! Super delish! Will definitely go back!

Pretty good. Nice layout. Good educational displays.

However, the otters did not have enough room to thrive. We visited there 10/10/2016 and I read that one of the otters died 12/8/2016; I'm not surprised. It was a little shocking.
Excellent hot, fresh and quick! The falafel were perfect combo of crunchy on outside and fluffy on the inside.

I use to eat here so much at its old location they should have gave me stock. So I visited the new location and it was cool to see the owner there. She is a super cool person. I ordered my food and YES it takes entirely to long. They take a ton of phone orders and place them all in order with standing patrons. I would find a better way to manage that. Luckily I was off that day so the hour wait only aggravated my hungry. Of course once I received the food I was back to being very happy I came. I eat hot chicken everywhere and I will say this place has always been a top places to go. Great representation of what Nashville is bringing nowadays.

5 stars for Dr Oki and 4 for the staff...

When I called to schedule the receptionist wasn't very friendly at all.  At the office the staff we interacted with was pleasant.

These screenings are unnerving, let's start there.  You want everything to be healthy and perfect and the wait to find out is hard.  It's normal to be on edge.

Dr Oki was all business to start, gathering our family histories and giving us a thorough lesson in genetics & screening options.  Was it warm and fuzzy, not really but he is extremely knowledgeable and clearly passionate about genetics and fetal development.  

We had a great 13 week ultrasound and learned even more as he showed us this and that about our baby.  We got a couple cute pics of baby and he was patient as baby was not cooperating to show us his/her nasal bone.  I felt completely comfortable with the doctor and am looking forward to our 20 week appointment.

I love aquarium's so was excited when my friend suggested we check it out. As other reviewers have pointed out, this place is pretty small considering the admission but if you purchase online and bundle with another attraction it's a bit better. Plus, they have penguins and otters! Try to get there in the early afternoon and you can catch the assorted feedings and lectures.

Side note: a new expanded shark/sting ray exhibit is scheduled to open next year!

I've had hot chicken once, so I don't have much to compare to.  And unfortunately, I still really don't, because staff at my hotel recommended the mild version, saying that it was still quite hot.  I did not find the mild version to have any amount of spice, whatsoever.  So, if you have any type of tolerance for heat, start with the hot (200 degrees).  

However, the chicken itself was super crisp outside and still tender inside.  And the leg quarter with crinkle fries was huge.  I could not stop eating it, and even though I wanted more, I was super full when I was done.  The chicken takes about twenty minutes to make, so do not go here completely famished, like I did.  

I cannot say enough about the friendliness of the staff.  I think I even got to chat with the owner briefly!  I'm just sad I didn't get back to try the spicier version.
One of my favorite places in NOLA!!! much better than the lame Houston aquarium. Jellyfish and shark exhibits are my favorites. Oh, and the penguins, which were very playful on this last trip!!

A must visit when in beautiful New Orleans. Take the Cotton Blossom riverboat and visit the New Orleans Zoo, too.

The Aquarium is beautiful. The Audubon Zoo is one of America's best!

Smack yo grandma! This is some spicy hot and deeeeelish chicken.
Friendly service.  The chicken is fresh, meaty and the breading is crunchy and packed with flavor.  The 400 was too spicy for me and tore the ass outta me. The 200 about the same.  The 100 was just right for me. A little kick.  Long live 400 degrees. A gem.
Everything so GOODDDDD.Boudin,ribs,brisket,grilled asparagus and potato salad.Its a very good location on Magazine Street

This is my first visit to an aquarium, so I can't compare, but what I experienced was impressive.

An enormous tank filled with sharks, sting rays, schools of fish, and a gigantic turtle. 

A walk-thru tank/tunnel so you can see the bellies of sting rays and varieties of fish.

Designated areas to actually touch sting rays and miniature sharks.

The entire building was clean and a happy environment overall. Great place to take friends, a date, and family.

I will let my photos do the rest of my talking and reasoning for my 5 star rating of this aquarium.

I came here today for lunch with a co worker. I ordered 2 meats the pork and brisket with side asparagus.  My friend same meat side was beans.  I really liked the pork. Nice portions as well.  The brisket for me was not as good.  I would have liked it thinner and more flavorful.  The asparagus were cooked to perfect.  Great service and clean.  Will try maybe something else next time maybe the chicken.  The sauces were a nice compliment.  My favorite was the sweet BBQ.  Great portions.  Will be back soon to try other menu items.

CUTENESS OVERLOAD!  If you're looking to go through your weekly quota of "awws" in one day, this aquarium is a good place to do it.  The sea otter feedings alone could be enough, but throw in penguin feedings too?  So so sugary sweet.

THE GOOD

Feedings:  The absolute best part of the Audubon Aquarium.  During my last visit we watched stingrays, penguins, and otters get fed and it was both enjoyable and informative.  Nothing is more fun than watching what animals will do for food.  To make things easy for all guests, the aquarium provides feedings times on all their maps so you know when you should start heading toward a particular tank.

Diversity:  Audubon has a good variety of non-fish animals in addition to their fishes, especially considering that they were pretty much starting from scratch post-Katrina, which is what I'm thinking happened based on other Yelp posts.  I never expected to see owls at an aquarium, and I heard that they're adding a parakeet exhibit soon as well.  Should be interesting.

Gulf of Mexico Tank:  Massive tank with a plethora of fish, sharks, and a giant sea turtle!  Plus there is an educational mini-lecture that they give everyday.  A nice place to relax and take a breather if you've had a long day of touring/exploring.

THE BAD

Cleanliness:  Specifically the bigger tanks, there was a lot of fog and mildew and dirt buildup along the glass, making it difficult to see several of the animals and fish.  For an aquarium, that's pretty unacceptable, considering it is more than possible to keep those tanks clean and crystal clear based on other aquariums I've been to.

Poor/Incorrect Signage:  I don't know how much control they have over this, since exhibits may change too quickly for them to change signs, but oftentimes the educational material and the labels on the tanks did not match up with what we were actually looking at.  There would be a cool fun fact about a particular fish, but that fish was not present in the tank.  It was frustrating at times too, when there were labels for a particular fish or animal but none to be found actually swimming around.

Food Court:  It's been mentioned before but it bears repeating: this food court is terrible.  Eat before you get here or wait until you leave.  

PURGATORY

Too Kid-Friendly?:  This is stupid, of course it has to be kid friendly to some degree.  I just wish there were some things geared toward an older sea-life lover, more akin to the sea-life wing of the Natural History Museum in DC.  I know, it's nitpicky...

Cost:  Not ridiculously overpriced, but still too expensive to be more than a once-every-blue-moon excursion for locals, which is too bad.

OVERALL

While there are some lowlights to the experience, hopefully with continued good business and patronage their funds will increase to the point where they can better address those issues.  Even so, the Aquarium is a great stop for a relaxing, educational, CUTE diversion from typical New Orleans life.

We visited this aquarium on my brother's twelfth birthday and he loved it.  As far as aquariums go, it wasn't the most impressive I've ever seen, but it was a lot of fun.  Clearer tanks would've been nice, but otherwise, no real complaints.  The displays all came with handy dandy notes and interesting facts, and the final Gulf of Mexico exhibit was pretty astonishing, complete with an enormous awesome wrinkly sea turtle.  Also, the otters and penguins were adorable.

Interactive attractions included hand-to-hide contact with stingrays and tiny sharks.  I embarrassed myself by shrieking when a VERY MALICIOUS STINGRAY tried to eat me when all I wanted to do was pet it, but my brothers were able to touch without issue, as were all of the other small children in line.

What a let down.  I've been hearing for years how great this aquarium is.  How it's so much better than the one in Dallas.  HA!  Ha, I tell you.

I was highly disappointed.  

1) It was super crowded--that was expected (it is a tourist attraction after all), however the layout is not conducive for effective traffic control.
2) A lot of the exhibits were dirty...filthy dirty with cloudy glass.  Come on.
3) It was a lot smaller than I expected.

The good: the huge tank at the end was very impressive; the Mississippi exhibit was awesome (white gators rule) and my kids loved the jellyfish.

This place is awesome, everytime I have gone here I loved it. I loved how they made the different setups like you would see in the gulf or the bayou.  Nice location too right on the Mississippi river. Highly recommended for any person interested in wildlife or for families.

Pretty darn good! A small dining area and BYOB are made up for by the super friendly staff and killer food. Ribs, and  pulled pork nachos were both excellent and came with several choices for sauces. Our kids loved their BBQ chicken and sweet potato muffins. Most places that do pulled pork drown it in sauce to cover up the fact that the meat has dried out, but this pulled pork was actually moist all the way through without any sauce. 
We will definitely be back!!

Came twice gave us attitude, needless to say the chicken is packed with flavor and heat, depending on the level of heat you choose. However, I do prefer Hattie's B based on the customer service alone as both chicken establishments produce great fried chicken.

*** Warning *** this location is now closed and has been replaced by a Quiznos :( tried to go for lunch and were disappointed that it is no longer there and the new location is not up and running yet - hopefully will have a chance to try on another trip!

My relationship with the New Orleans Barbecue scene would best be described as "It's Complicated".  I love the 'cue, and expect awesome with every bite.  NOLA is not a barbecue destination

That being said, I was glad to swing back by Saucy's last week to see if it went any better this time.  GetMyPerks.com hooked me up with a $20 certificate for $10, so the time was right for a second chance...

Some things - like the meat - were much improved.  Others (sides) still could use some work.  Off to the nitty-gritty:

The Meats:
The Ribs - They do a pretty decent St. Louis Rib at this joint.  The rub works well with the pork, and it has a good smoke ring.  The smoke flavor to all the meat is rather subtle, so a smokehead would be disappointed.  The first visit here, the ribs were a touch overdone (not that fall-off-the-bone is a bad thing), and they were a bit underdone this time.  They just had a bit too much "tug" for my tastes.  Average the two, and they are on point.

The Pulled Pork - Very tasty, light smoke flavor.  It was what one should expect from pulled pork - tender and moist.  It was quite good with the Vinegar Carolina Sauce.

The Sausage - They always have Boudin on the menu, and the special on this night was Chaurice, which is kind of a spicy creole chorizo-type sausage.  It was lightly smoked and quite juicy.  It was a pretty tasty hot link, and hopefully they will have it again on the next visit.

The Brisket - This one was a split decision.  I was not impressed by the Brisket, and felt it did not have any real flavor.  The bark/rub was completely underwhelming, and it tasted like roast beef.  On the flip side, the better half felt it was quite tasty, and the rub was good.  Then again, beef is usually pretty good in any form with a creamy horseradish sauce - which they provide with the order.  Still going to say some work needs to be done in this department.

The Sadness, er, Sides:
The Macaroni and Cheese - Our last visit provided us the opportunity to sample some mac with a broken cheese sauce.  They done fixed this issue.  The Mac N Cheese now has a velvetta-style base instead of cream, and is full of flavor.  Big upgrade here.

The Potato Salad - It was quite tasty - I guessed it was pre-made, and thus the second disagreement on this visit began.  The better half felt that it could be house-made.  No clue, just plain, simple, standard potato salad.

The Coleslaw - This was pretty bad.  It was a cup of cabbage with about three drops of liquid.  Very cabbage-y and very dry.  Needless to say, it is a draw as to which was worse, the old Purple Slaw or this stuff.

The Beans - No change here.  Look delicious.  Don't eat if you plan on being within ten feet of anyone for a few days.  Garlic.  Garlic, with a bit o' Garlic.  Seriously, these things are chock full o' Garlic.  Too, too, too much Garlic.  I love Garlic.  Other than the GARLIC, the beans were a bit garlicky.

THE VERDICT:
The 'Cue was much improved, with the only knock being on the Brisket (which was barbecued to a great tenderness) not having any flavor.  The ribs were a bit underdone, which was probably more of a random variance than anything else.  Two of the sides raised their game, the Mac and Cheese and the Potato Salad.  The Slaw hopefully hit rock bottom, and can only improve.  The Beans could use about five less bulbs of garlic per ounce.

The Meat was tasty, so we're bumping up one to Four Stars.  One of the better 'cue joints in NOLA.

A fun thing to do on a day when the weather is not cooperating. It is in doors. I would have to save the penguins and the others were my favorite.  I guess the ultimate question is would I do it again, no not so much.
Go in and try their apple cider wine... try it warm!

Have you heard of Fantasy Island?  Sometimes locals need to be introduced to Fantasy Island.  No, it's not a kinky place.  It's a place you can run or bike.  If you are a mountain bike rider, you probably have heard of the park.  But it is also good if you are a runner and need a long run!

There is parking on the corner of Harrison and Irvington on the south side of Irvington. Then, you start running.  It is like a normal wash and some technical areas.  Sure beats running on random canals.  You can also spot some random junk items on the trail occassionally.  I personally have not run more than a few miles so I just go out as far as I want and turn back around!  There are several loops.  Most of them are flat, but there are some steep hills.

The trails are located on a 355-acre piece of land that is part of the Arizona land state trust, so you are supposed to mail a form and $15 to Phoenix every year for permission.  I have not heard of anyone doing that - areas on Silverbell and Starr Pass are on state land trust areas also.

Bit of a BBQ snob due to living in Texas and near KC. This place absolutely met and then exceeded my expectations. Goat cheese Mac & cheese is an incredible side, and right now I'm eating the Cochon Bleu sandwich--pulled pork topped with melted pepper jack and crumbled bleu cheese. Incredible. So happy to find this place. Plus, free refills on soda, friendly service, and it's BYOB. What could be better? I hope this place sticks around.

LOVE THIS STORE!

Staff is SO helpful! They are knowledgeable they are eager to know  what project you are doing, so possibly they can give you hints and tips on a possible better solution.

I typically shop at the big box store for more wood and generic things, but when it comes to non wood products - I SO LOVE THIS STORE. 

It only took me one time there to realize what a difference this store makes in my life as a home do it yourselfer.

The first time I called about our frig not getting cold, Frank told us what to do to see if we could remedy the problem without paying for a service call. Though it worked, I still had him come out to check because it didn't seem quite cold enough. He gave me a lesson on how refrigerators work and the air temp/food temp in them. I gladly paid for the call, which was a minimal charge and it is guaranteed for 30 days. The point is that he gave me info over the phone the 1st time I called that completely fixed the problem.
This is an amazing aquarium.  Huge selection of sea life.  You can definitely spend a hot or rainy day in here. We want to do one of the penguin encounters when the kids are old enough.

my first time here was amazing! the workers were so nice and friendly and helpful.i love  how happy they greeted me and my east posse. then the food was delicious. i recommend the whole damn menu cause thats how me and my posse rolled that day.the pull pork was great. the grilled chicken quesidilllas was great. then the ribs were great. i am in love yall....with those damn sweet potatoe muffins....woooooooh.!!!!!.... now this place knows there bbq!!!

We were not planning on going to the aquarium on this trip to New Orleans but we were glad we did.  We have been to the National Aquarium in Baltimore, Georgia Aquarium in Atlanta, John Shedd in Chicago,  and the Tennessee Aquarium in Chattanooga.   The Audubon Aquarium ranks up high on the list.   Its not very big but the content was great.  The exhibits are neat and educational.  The layout is a bit confusing but good.  One great thing about the aquarium is the parakeet exhibit.  Weird that a bird exhibit stands out in an aquarium but the great thing is that you get to feed the parakeets for a small fee.  They just come to the feeding stick and just start eating.  They will land on your finger, arm, head or any part of you body to get a nibble.  My kids loved it and so did my wife and I.  The fish in the aquarium had a good mix but not to extensive where you feel like fish fish fish and only fish.  Also the great thing is that the location is right on the border of the French Quarter.  Great food and great attraction all within walking distance.  What can you ask for.  Good family fun.
For the price, it was bleh. A lot of money for VERY little return. The exhibits were short and bland. Not a whole lot to look at.

Okay....Wow! Loved this place. We tried the Smokey beans, slaw, pulled pork plate, blue cheese pork sandwich and the baked Mac n cheese. NOTHING was less than uniquely delicious! They have 3 sauces from Fantasy, to Sweet BBQ to Chipotle. They are all very good. The Mac n cheese has 5 cheeses and we ordered an additional pint before leaving because it is excellent! Very cheesy and rich, but, well balanced. The Smokey beans!? A mix of a variety of long cooked beans in a very special roux I can't describe any better than spot on. These are not over sweetened brown sugar beans. They are earthy, spiced, Smokey Beans. Yum! 
Saucey's got it goin ON! 5 BIG Stars!
Plus, the young person that greeted us and served us was charming, informative and cheerfully delightful.

This is a small, unassuming little shop with some pretty solid barbeque. I had the two meat platter with the pulled pork and brisket. The pulled pork was decent, the brisket was awesome. The potato salad is mustard based and excellent; the BBQ beans were made from mixed beans instead of the navy beans that are typically featured in the dish and quite good. So far it's one of the best BBQ places I've been to here in New Orleans. The prices are great; two big entrees with sides for about 25 dollars. You can get a sandwich and a side for under 10 bucks.

The restaurant itself is pretty cozy, maybe 8 tables in a seat-yourself arrangement with a couple tables outside for nicer weather. Beer isn't served but the restaurant is BYOB so feel free to pack in whatever. The service is very fast and friendly and takeout is available.

They have really good tender ribs..service was great..everyone was really nice..small Southern place with lots of charm..you have your choice of sauces..I will be returning Everytime I get to New Orleans..

One of the top 3 in the Country!! Did not know that this was here, and was pleasantly surprised that it was part of our package.
Very good displays. 
Don't miss the Sea Horses which were phenomenal! 
Great for Kids, but Adults will not be bored....
I am a scuba diver and have seen many of these in the wild, but this would be REALLY great for a non diver!!

Road a few loops today and love these trails. I felt safe riding by myself but always on the look out for wildlife. Today I saw a roadrunner. 
You def. need a map and to know where you are going or it's easy to get confused.

A must go if you're into the sea and having amazing photograph opportunities! 

What's funny is that my favorite part was Parakeet Pointe -- yes, there are birds in this aquarium. They perch on you and you can pet them! Gah! So adorable. 

You can also touch a stingray here.

We got the admission + IMAX movie and saw the penguin movie, which was super cute! Look up the times of the movie you want to see online before you get there so you can plan your time around that. They have multiple gift shops, the main one is in the lobby and you need a ticket to get in. SO MANY FLUFFY THINGS!

It was not as big as it seems from the outside. Not much special exhibits aside from the penguin's feeding. One of the more pricey aquariums I've been (i go to every single one i come across during my travels)

Fun!
My favorite are the cuttlefish, seahorse exhibit, and I loved the string ray petting pool. They can be hard to reach but once you do touch em it's such a bizarrely fun feeling. Lol!

It's not as big as I expected but that's ok. Also it's a little pricey. Parking is  $10+ and tickets $22.50 a piece for just the aquarium :/

Ordered through uber eats one rainy day. I wasn't expecting much but have to admit, I was pleasantly surprised! Meat was tender and well seasoned and the sides were great to boot. Ribs slid right off the bone, potato salad was spot on, mac and cheese was ooey gooey delicious and cheesecake finished off the meal fantastically! Will definitely order from them again!

An aquarium is an aquarium. This one is no better than any of the others you have been to. That being said, my children, 5 and 8, enjoyed it and it was a good way to beat the heat for an hour or two. Just an expensive hour, especially considering the adults were underwhelmed.

Chicken breasts the size of an actual HUMAN tit.  For like $5, I think.
GRILLED ASPARAGUS (I order by the truckload)
CHIPOTLE MAYO/MUSTARD I could DROWN IN
Excellent Chaurisse and brisket.  
Questions?

This is a great place to bring kids... and also for adults to enjoy. However, make sure you have money to cover your door charge. After you pay, there's a free cartoon movie for the kids to see. It's pretty pricey.  The aquariums are pretty awesome and stocked with your favorite sea animals otherwise that you wouldn't have an opportunity to see.

Really enjoyed Saucy's barbecue. The brisket was delicious. Also, the Cajun Carolina(pulled pork sandwich with cole slaw and Carolina sauce) was very good. I had a craving for good barbecue and this sure hit the spot!
While I can appreciate waiting 30 minutes for Hot Chicken, I'd prefer not too. It was an experience but can't say that we would go back unless we weren't starving and had plenty of time.

This location has special aspects going for it! First I have to give the first comment to the employees. They were so nice, funny, and knowledgeable. They didn't bombard me either. The employee on the floor let me have my space while I was shopping around, and if I did need her, she was at least in ear shot.

Every Bath & Body Works I have been to has been organized and clean. This is no exception; it was so organized even the items in tubs were easy to reach.

I love going to B&BW for the deals and coupons they always have, but my main purpose for this review is the quality of their products and how humble they are if a scent ends up not agreeing with you. Is it pricey, yeah maybe but how often can you find lotions, sprays, etc that can be that strong and actually last all day? I had a fall out with their products, but going back I'm glad I can find something under a deal, get help from polite employees, and feel satisfied while shopping.
Amazing food, fantastic service!  I got the brisket sandwich with chipotle sauce and it was great!! Will most definitely be coming back!

Our plan was not to go to Saucy's, but I'm glad we did. We originally wanted to go to Casamento's on Magazine, only to find out they're closed until SEPTEMBER; what a drag. Then we tried another place, that was closed for a private event! Ugh. 

So to get out of the Louisiana heat, we dove into Saucy's which far exceeded expectations! I got the brisket and alligator sausage. Which was great! The potato salad was good as well as the smoked beans. 

Overall, the meal was good, service was great, and helped us forget that we went on magazine for oysters!

There was a time when The Joint was the only good BBQ in the city. Now there are plenty to choose from, and I have to say I think Saucy's is the best of the bunch.

I judge a BBQ place based on their brisket & ribs, and I think theirs are the juiciest and tenderest around. I tried each of the sauces, and they were all delicious.

This place is underrated.

Edit: I've been back several times, and one thing I will say is that it's a little inconsistent. On a good day it's the best brisket in New Orleans, and on a bad day, it's very average and a little dry. Still highly recommend on the chance you get them on a good day.

Great aquarium. 
Nice layout, diverse fish. Staff are very friendly and informative. Could've been more fish to see. But over all it was a good time. I definitely recommend coming here if you enjoy learning while on your trip. 
 
Highlights: 
Otters 
Penguins 
Sharks 
Alligators

I treat my car like a Maserati....parking far away from other cars in parking lots just to avoid the door dings/scratches/dents that careless people cause when they open their car doors wide open. My car looks like new. I specifically mentioned to the Empire valet when attending a wedding to park my car far from others. At the end of the evening it was obviously dark; I could not see the dent and paint scratch which occurred that evening when I picked up the car. 7 hours later, early in the a.m. we saw it and nobody parked near that side of the car in the intervening time because we were in a hotel parking lot next to a median on that side of the car overnight.
Reached the owner, Jon, at Empire. Sent photos of the damage as he requested. For two months, he has given me the run around and told me to go to my insurance agent or lawyer....for a $400 auto body repair! (And I offered to meet him in the middle at $200) He would not answer the question of the distance between the cars when parked at this venue.....after numerous email and phone attempts. His last response was that I should have had video camera proof....really?? I was at my niece's wedding, not standing vigil at my car waiting for the perpetrator of my car's damage. Philander Chase Knox  Estate's (the venue -- Robert Ryan Catering) was also unwilling to resolve the matter and did not return phone calls/emails. Absolving themselves of guilt, as the National Park Service owns the Estate. Please, over $400-200, really???
They fried the chicken fresh for us and the sweet tea was really good. I guess it's more of a takeout place though. They still did a great job. The medium hot was perfect.

The grounds are beautiful, the wine is tasty, but there are children screaming in my ear. A nice day took a terrible turn today when 3 families showed up with at least 10 children under the age of 5. The ran all over the winery grounds, screaming. It was very distracting and made it incredibly difficult to have a nice date. The parents weren't even minding their children. It was downright worrysome. There are arking lots full of cars and children running free & unattended while their parents drink wine. It ruined our experience.

For $30 a person this aquarium is absolutely not worth the price. I get why it's so high they have to pay marine biologists and keepers and bills, I understand. But as a consumer it is not worth it. It took as about an hour to walk through the whole thing TWICE. We will not be back. The large tank they have at the end of the aquarium is the best exhibit they have, it's full of sharks and has a sea turtle it is very neat. The rest of it is a hard pass. Maybe if it's raining outside and you're in the area it's a good way to get out of the rain, other than that no.

Though situated in a "food court" just off downtown Nashville, the chicken at 400 Degrees is anything but pedestrian.

The breading is crunchy, the chicken is moist, and the sauce is not overbearing. Customers choose from a simple menu and a 4-tier heat scale, sides and extras notwithstanding. 

The food is cooked fresh, so expect a wait of 15-20 mins, but it is worth it. The chicken is moist, the breading well-seasoned, and the portions generous. 

And it is HOT. Even the basic 200 - their medium - was spicy enough to make my head sweat. I added a 400 wing for a nominal fee, and it was much hotter but not in a showy way. It is balanced to benefit the chicken flavor, rather than to test the diner's bravery.

I haven't eaten Prince's Hot Chicken, so I can't weigh in on the competition, but I thoroughly enjoyed the food and the people at 400 Degrees. Fried Chicken fans, don't hesitate.

Walked in randomly today with my mom and was met with very friendly and welcoming staff we ordered the pulled pork and chicken breast , baked beans coleslaw and baked Mac n cheese,everything was so delicious !! We will definitely be going back and I highly recommend saucys .

The aquarium is small only 2 large tanks and was expensive to get into with 4 kids.  I ordered their photos that they told me at the counter were around $20.  When I went to pick them up, they quoted me $40.  I asked why and there were taxes and frame prices and digital pass that they were not honest about when I said I wanted them.  Then they gave me a digital pass card and told me that all photos would be online.  Then I went to leave and the parking which said for aquarium right on it was another $40.  Oh ya, That digital pass card has never worked.  Trying to get help is impossible.  I sent a request online for help, no response.  They said if I didn't hear back from them, to contact feedback and let them know.  No response from them either.

I can't really give this place a rating because I didn't get to eat it. I love hot chicken and have tried Prince's and Bolton's so far but I heard that this place was great so I wanted to try it. I drove from Atlanta to meet up with someone and I made sure to make Nashville the meeting spot and made sure the time worked out in order for me to get there before closing. They closed at 5 pm that day so I got there at about 4:20 pm believing that it should be enough time for a small order. After arriving and looking over the menu, a lady said we aren't taking any more orders for the day. Only one person waiting, so it wasn't crowded which confused me. I didn't even ask why, I just left and went to Bolton's. I was really excited to try this place, but don't know when I will ever be back in the area.

Saucys BBQ is an amazing little spot on Magazine..the ribs are huge so order the smaller plate with just 2 or 3 ribs if just ordering for yourself.. Best BBQ  I had in Nola so far.. Super friendly staff as well..
Mac and Cheese is really cheesy too :)I

It's a walk up and order, we'll bring it to you kinda place with about 8 tables inside.
I came here with the girl who would be my gf and we were welcomed warmly, and had our pick of tables (no one else in there). 
I ordered a Cajun Carolina on French Bread. It's pulled pork with Cole slaw. Sides of potato salad and baked beans. 
My dining companion, girl who would be my gf ordered brisket plate with sides of Mac and cheese and Mac and goat cheese. 
There was music playing, and a laid back atmosphere, even as more people came in to eat. 
THE FOOD:  The Cajun Carolina had very little Cole slaw and, although the pulled pork was tender and moist, had little flavor . The French bread had good crunch. 
I tried the sweet bbq sauce and the sweet and Chipotle sauce on either side. The sauces here are flavorful, they also have Bold and a Mustardy bbq sauce. 
It comes with a hotter sauce in a cup that I added to give Flava. It needed it cuz the meat was mild. 
The baked beans were good, sweet, with brown sugar flavor, a bit of bacon, but not much bacon flavor. 
The potato salad was awesome.  Amazing. And, I really enjoyed it. Mayo and mustard and dilly. Creamy, and chucks of potatoes.  Loved it. 
My lady's brisket was incredible. Chunky. Meaty. Barky. Little fat. The fat that was on it had great taste and melted as it hit my palate. Soaked the sauce well. Highly recommended.  
The regular Mac and cheese was great. Cheesy flavor. Ziti noodles. Loved it. 
I liked the goat Mac and cheese. A little tangier, a little creamier. Mixed in some horseradish for added kick. 
The servers/people who worked there were sooo friendly, and helpful, it was a great afternoon. 
Magazine St is great for people watching outside. 
If it's not busy, go here, talk and watch and have a good time.
We did.
BYOB
Door attendants are very rude. One of them yelled at my family and I for exiting through the wrong door. We will never return.
If you don't know what you like...come here and you will know. The staff is so friendly and so knowledgeable. I recommend the sangria...but you are free to pick your own

Definitely worth a visit, but only if you already visited the Insectarium. If you have been to a bunch of aquariums around the world, lower your expectations as it will not be that impressive, but if you are a lover of all things aquatic, it's a time well spent. You can feed the penguins, rays, parakeets for an extra fee. I thought the aquarium was on a smaller scale than described, but ended up seeing it all in about 3 hours.

Had a great meal last night at Saucy's.  Hubby had ribs ("best ever"), and I had the delicious pork cheeks on a bun (not on the menu yet, but you can ask for them).  We both enjoyed the cole slaw; it was fresh and crunchy without too much dressing.  Brought my own $6 bottle of wine that was put on ice for us.  Excellent food.  Excellent waitress.  Excellent prices.  Hurray!

Kids EVERYWHERE, many with parents that were not paying attention. Many of the tanks were leaking from the top. Animal exhibits were small, and depressing with insufficient room for the animals to move around in. I will say, I was impressed with the Large fish tank at the end with sharks and other large fish. Serene to watch for a while. Also got transfixed with the frogs. DO NOT GO if you don't have kids. If you do, then this is your place!
Great prices! Great service! I love the employees there as well! Highly reccomend this place to get your nails done:)

I visit the aquarium 2-3 times per year, and look forward to every next visit. They do a great job of making sure they keep things interactive.  From feeding the stingrays to feeding the parakeets, you feel like you've made a connection with wildlife.  

I love to watch the otters play,  and the penguins waddle around in their exhibit.  And the sea horses are so cool!

There's so much to see - sharks, sea turtles, a white alligator - and soooooooo much more.

I think it's a must see and one of New Orleans' best indoor activities/attractions.

Had my appointment with Dr. Oki today and he was fantastic. I have complex health and have had my fair of doctors both good and bad and I could not have been more happy. I went into the appointment incredibly nervous and he made me feel at ease and had me laughing the whole time. Was very thorough and addressed any question we had, most of them before we even asked him. Thank you for such a wonderful experience on a very nerve wracking appointment!

If your an animal person of the water variety this might be your place. Kids loved the place, there is much to see and do. Really enjoyed the African penguin display, and stayed around for the 3pm feeding. They really go all out of this, however be aware it creates a bottleneck at the display get there early for it or past it if not your thing. Spent about 2 hours there after watching Hurricane in the Bayou at the included in the price giant screen.

During my trip to New Hope, I came down to Peddler's Village with a coupon for a free tasting for two here. It turns out it was unnecessary since they were already giving free tastings. I don't like particularly strong wines and really enjoyed theirs. I was a huge fan of their blush, sangria, and cider wines. I tried their cider cold and even more fantastically, warmed up. They had the cider in a coffee thermos for easy dispensing. I also really enjoyed their red table wine. Normally, I don't drink alot of reds but this was very good. 

The clerks were friendly and knowledgeable. Similar to another reviewer, I used my Yelp check-in offer for 20% a bottle of their blush wine. Their bottles were pretty reasonable at $12-$15. If I wasn't already close to my weight limit, I would have bought more, for sure.

Not worth the time or the money.......and I love aquariums! I was very disappointed with the entire experience. Even on a rainy day, I'm pretty sure we could have found something more educational, more entertaining and all together more fun.
The sweetheart working on Friday night sold me pops even though they were closed. Got 5 and have only tried one, but it was great!

This was the worst overpriced aquarium I've ever been to. Tickets were $25 and it was about $1 per minute spent in this aquarium. There wasnt even an attraction. No sharks, no dolpins. Nothing. Im sorry there was one shark in a tank with other fish and stuff. Definitely a waste. Would NOT recommend.

We came here, excited to learn of an aquarium since we're animal fans.  And what was particularly interesting for a tourist was seeing animals from the bayou area, like the crocodile.  We loved the penguins, as there are two different kinds here that are all in one exhibit, but my favorite exhibit was the sea otters.  There are four of them, which, most, if not all, were rescued around the Pacific Ocean and it was fun learning about them and watching feeding time.  They seem like a playful bunch.  Also, there's a gift shop right by the sea otter exhibit which carries mostly sea otter gifts.  There's an option to get a professional photo taken here, too.  It was a nice place to visit, especially since it's by the waterfront.

The fried chicken is amazing! its not better that Prince's but its definitely good. The 400 degrees is for their hottest fried chicken which is too hot to handle, be sure if you want to do it!  

Most importantly , please order for the food before going there because they take a very long time to get your food when you place the order when you walk in! They took almost 30mins to serve mine!

The aquarium sits on the banks of the Mississippi River which dumps out into the Gulf of Mexico (little geography lesson on the side there for ya) while wading through swamp land. So I was expecting a solid aquarium with lots of diversity and cool exhibits. What I got was an aquarium not to much different then the one I have down the street from me in ARIZONA! Come on NOLA you can do better than this! 

The price tag is a heft $18.50 and I was able to walk the entire aquarium in one hour and fifteen minutes before catching an IMAX. There are highlights to the place I guess, but not that warrant the price of admission. I like that the place had a flow and wasn't just free wandering. The kids 'Break" room was simple and their Moray Eel tank was pretty cool. If there was a 'WoW" exhibit for me it was the White Alligator in the picture who was as big as any gator I've seen, though I hear the gator at the zoo (and the Zoo for that matter is worth it, wish I had gone there) has a feeding time and is even better.

 I know there isn't much you can do with an aquarium that isn't the same as every other aquarium but one of the very best I've EVER been to is the one in Chattanooga, TN and who would have thought that!

Wonderful customer service every single time! I have never had an issue anytime I have ever been into the store. The lines were long but the cashier kept her cool and helped everyone without getting stressed.

Well the last time I was here was on my first visit to NOLA and I was about 7 so needless to say I don't remember much accept for a ride on the ferry boat and petting a shark... Now I am 23 and when I came back to town I just had to stop in and see if I could create some newer and better memories. The aquarium is nice and cold and it looks fully recovered as far as I can tell. There are no signs of a hurricane and all the tanks were full of marine life. My favorite experience was watching the otters play with toys like frisbies and just hamming it up for the cameras. The food court was not tested but something smelled pretty good over there... 
The one thing I looked forward to was petting a baby shark again but I had to settle for a sting ray instead which was cool and in the end I was glad that I got to  but bring wet wipes with you because hand sanitizer does not feel like enough! I liked the key chains from the insectarium much better than the ones they had here. The designs were tired and boring so I had to settle for a seahorse necklace, which makes me feel like I'm 7 again. Have fun!!!!

Penguins.  Otters.  Super cute.

I liked the experience in general, though I did feel bad for one little penguin in particular who was swimming at the glass hoping he'd make it out.

The "Gulf of Mexico" tank has a massive turtle in it that was beautiful to watch.

I've read a lot of Nashville hot chicken reviews and I've come to find that the majority of hot chicken eaters seem to rely solely on the level of heat for their opinions. This may be blasphemous and I'm sure I will receive backlash, but the data doesn't lie. You will usually read a review that describes how the chicken is "good" followed by a comparison of mild, medium, hot with other hot chicken restaurants in Nashville. I love hot chicken and all the varieties that Nashville has to offer, but many times the flavor of the spice or rub gets ignored. A great hot chicken should achieve a perfect balance between flavor, spice, and heat. 

With that, I finally made it to 400 Degrees after hearing good things about it. Is it good? Yes. Will I come back tomorrow? Only if someone wanted to go. For a cook to order operation, the flavor profile was not there. The spice dip was a two part taste of salt and light cayenne. I couldn't find any other flavors. I'm beginning to think that rubs bring about greater favors than dips (as I gravitate more to rubs). I got the 200 (medium) and found the heat level on par with a medium - I didn't sweat, my nose didn't run, and the heat didn't linger too long afterwards in my mouth. It was a solid medium that I personally felt was on the lighter side of the medium hot chicken spectrum. But as I mentioned earlier, heat is just one part of the hot chicken experience. 

Maybe I'm being snobby, or maybe I'm holding up too high a standard - but I can't deny my experience. The chicken meat itself (breast quarter) was tasty. The staff was friendly. The experience was fine. I've had a lot worse, and I've had a lot better. Take this review as you will - if you love 400 Degrees, then amen brother. Eat it and tell all your friends about it. For me, I just feel more and more that flavor is losing its importance with hot chicken. 400 Degrees didn't prove me wrong.

I rarely write reviews, but This place is great! The bar tender at our hotel gave us the recommendation for a good local place. I'm glad we took it! It is in a food court and an unlikely place, but super worth it! The pork chops were soooooooo good and my boyfriend loved the chicken. You get a lot of food for a great price! The lady, Aquia is extremely nice. You have to come here! It is a good deal. Mind you, it is not a place to go if you want healthy food or veggies. BUT, if you are looking for some really good, greasy, spicy porkchops or chicken, this IS THE place.

This is a decent aquarium, but a bit pricey and it was chock full of summer camp kids when we went. Sounds like this is very common. 

Best exhibits were the underwater tunnel (yes it is overcrowded), the Amazon rain forest and the open ocean tank. Parakeets were pretty cool, but we did not feed them and I was really paranoid about being pooped on so we left pretty quickly. The white alligator was really cool. 

I found it a bit disappointing really, but we went for the kids and it was a way to beat the heat.
A really fun place to go to if you have a couple hours to spare.  The scenery is very impressive and all the animals are lovely.
