Apparently "Nashville Hot Chicken" is going to be a popular thing now, so I gotta get in on this and try some straight from the source.  We happened to be passing through Nashville, and this place looked the most friendly for both me and my less spice-friendly wife.  

We were not disappointed.  

The young lady, who I assume owns the place based on how she was talking, explained to me that everything is made fresh to order.  As a result, our chicken took 40 minutes, but we had time, so we waited.  (CALL AHEAD to avoid this)

You can split the tender plates into different spice levels, so I decided to try both the 200 and 400 degree heat (tenders come with 3).  The 200 was very similar to "hot chicken" I've had here in Asheville, but the 400 was a step above, in both flavor and heat.  This town is serious when they say hot.  

There is a notable difference in flavor between the two levels I tried, and you can tell that the sauces are made with different peppers.  The 200 was tolerable.  I could eat lots of that and not die.  The 400...maybe less so.  It was pretty brutal. I was then informed that she actually has a 500 and 800, too, but I'm not that kind of cocky.
Delicious pulled pork, goat cheese mac n cheese and sweet potato muffins to die for!  Service from Danielle was awesome - trust her recommendations, you won't be sorry!

Good neighborhood BBQ joint in Uptown! 

I found the dishes to be reasonably portioned and priced, and helpful for my portion control; Yummy/fatty dishes are my greatest weakness haha.

Other pros - Bottled sauces come in six different varieties, and there are other sauces specially made for each dish.
The menu features alligator sausage option for those who want to try something uniquely NOLA.

I ordered the beef brisket plate with two sides, upon strong recommendation from the waiter. The beans were overladen with sugar, and the horseradish sauce he so raved about did not exactly complement the meat as he promised. But more importantly I suppose, the meat was tender, rubbed with a good mix of spices.

The ambiance is laid back, and it's BYOB! Grab a beer and head down over if you're uptown for a parade.

I have been to a lot of aquariums so that is why I rated this in the middle. It's a nice small aquarium, but it isn't impressive. It's the same ticket price as most other aquariums, but it's smaller. They only have one alligator, one otter, small jelly section. If it's raining then go, but don't go if you have other things to do.

BEST AQUARIUM EVER!  I have gone to the Monterey Bay Aquarium as well as the aquarium in Maui, but this one beats them all.  I came just because I had to see the albino alligator.  I was slightly disappointed that the alligator just lied there and didn't do much but the other animals made up for it.  The parrots were extremely playful and entertaining as they showed off on the branches.  And the sea otter was so cute doing laps in the water.   I enjoyed the other exhibits as well such as the frogs, sea horses and sting rays.
$$$$ for how small and little there is to see. I wouldn't pay for that again. A couple of nursing sharks, two otters and some penguins. Not the best aquarium for $30 a person.
lots of awesome sauces and brisket was amazing.  chicken was a little dry but the sauce it came with was good enough to make up for it.  Also its BYOB

Today, we visited both the insectarium and the aquarium. Both were phenomenal. This aquarium was bigger, and cooler than I could have imagined. Even if you aren't with kids in New Orleans, its something to see. My kids loved it. The sharks were my son's favorite, and my daughter loved the otters. I loved their priceless reactions from the whole experience.

I thought I had already reviewed this place years ago...

Well the aquarium is a nice quick trip for folks to take their kids on and is much faster than the zoo.  It is also interesting for adults who want to learn some more about water dwelling creatures of the Americas as in addition to a very large collection of fish they also have turtles, snakes, alligators, macaws, parakeets, penguins and sea otters (most kids seem to prefer the otter antics).  I've also been to several events here and it makes a decent place for a party.  The IMAX theater here is also pretty nice but it is really under used and they could have a better rotation of movies.

My main disappointment is after seeing all the delicious looking fish I get really hungry and they don't have a seafood restaurant in their food court.  For the steep price of admission you should get a fish dinner included in the cost.

I am only giving three stars because I am not a fan of the majority of their wines. Everyone has their own tastes when it comes to wine, so I didn't feel like I could use that as my only indicator when writing this review. To me, the majority of their wines are way too sweet. And, as a bubbly fan, they lose points for not producing one. However, the atmosphere is fabulous - relaxing and open. The staff is friendly and welcoming (even to larger groups), and they allow you to bring in your own food. I've been a couple of times with a large group of women, some who get glasses, some who get flights. They also don't rush you - you're welcome to stay as long as you'd like.

Overall, I'd definitely go back. But, I always get the same dry red because it's the only thing that works for me!

Excellent company call them first!!!!
frank came out in an hour from my call, taught me about my washer as he fixed in front of me, was washing in no time...one thing I cannot live without is a washing machine.  He let me know how everything worked and finished in 20 minutes... Then I was entertained by his stories while he billed me.  A pleasure to work with!!
Your in good hands

After living in Texas for last year I've been missing BBQ. Although I haven't found anything that compares to Lockhart, this is a fair substitute. Seasoning is spot on, sides & sauces are solid, only thing lacking was the quality of the brisket. I requested mine lean but the waitress haughtily explained that wasn't possible... Clearly she needs a bit more training. If I could've had a leaner cut I would've rated this 5*.

I am a BBQ snob who has eaten smoked meats with the local sauce across the country.  The quality of the BBQ at Saucy's blew me away!  The food here is top notch.  BBQ just doesn't get any better.

I had a two meat sampler with Carolina pulled pork and Boudin.  Each meat came with its own sauce which made it over the top special.  The sides, cole slaw and BBQ beans, were also perfect.  Wife had brisket sandwich and she was a happy camper.

Don't wait.  Go here and enjoy!

Came twice gave us attitude. Upon arriving at 6:15pm, the line cook instructed a worker to take the guests waiting in line their order. The owner then instructed the worker to tell those in line that they were no longer taking orders yet proceeded to take the order of the party behind me. Never have I experience such poor customer service and having race be a factor. Very disappointment and saddened that this occurred, now on to Hattie's B.

Cool Place, you can walk to it almost anywhere from the business district, The insect thing is only a few short blocks walk, and the Zoo is apparently ONE busline straight street route to get to it from a local street there so I was told.  I didn't get to the zoo, I saw the insectisarium building location (sp) later on Canal Street right near my hotel and I didn't know it.  I guess I will have to go back and do the whole "experience" ticket someday.

Probably the best pulled pork BBQ I've ever had, honestly. Perfectly sauced and the side of sauce it came with was kick-ass delicious. My girlfriend and I split a pulled pork BBQ plate and it came with two sides, we got the goat cheese mac n cheese (phenomenal!) and potato salad and we ate every bite of it. Didn't come with bread (you can order it as a sandwich/plate) yet there was enough pulled pork to fill both of us up--splitting it was the perfect portion for a super hot day and all for only about 15 bucks. I'd definitely come back and order this plate and eat it all myself, haha. The lady who took our ordered and took care of us was also really sweet, our entire experience was great. If we lived in the area I'm sure we'd come here again and again.

Went to 400 Degree on the recommendation of a friend. we were not disappointed. the service was great, chicken made to order and spicy. The owner Ahkee, was right in the middle of the operation which is probably why the restaurant produces such a high quality product. I can't think of a better method of quality control! 
Currently 400 Degree is operating out of a food truck in Bordeau, but is in the process of refurbishing a bldg. on site to house the restaurant. This will improve the customer experience and reduce their laundry, by eliminating the inevitable spills while eating in the car. 
Good food, good people and great customer service coupled with the authentic Nashville "hot chicken" experience.

It's been awhile since I have been to this aquarium, but other than it being a little small, compared to the aquarium in Atlanta, it was still a good time. It's a little on the expensive side to get in, but if you get there early in the day, you can see them feed the peguins and the white alligator which was pretty cool and avoid the crowds.

I personally think this is the best hot chicken in town, with Prince's coming in 2nd. 400 degrees was the 1st hot chicken joint around that sold chicken somewhat similar to Princes. All of these other places are just imitations trying to cash in on what's "hot". I love the way it's seasoned. Some of the hot chicken places fail in this area. The other chicken places seem to lack seasoning. It's truly hot chicken, and it's always juicy inside. With Prince's, although the skin is perfect, sometimes it's a bit dry inside. There's only a couple issues with 400 Degrees; everything is made to order--so if you are craving it, you can't just randomly stop by and pick up an order. They only have one deep fryer back there as well. The other issue is that the hours of operation are limited. They list that they close at 7 pm Tuesday through Friday. They list they close at 5 pm on Saturday--although there have been instances when I have called only to be told that they are closing early. Also, note, the last order will need to be placed about an hour before closing time. 

Which brings me to the final point. The good news is that you can call and place the order. The order is always ready within the time frame they give. They usually will tell you over the phone that it will be about 30 minutes to an hour on lunch rush during the week. If not for the wait, I would have given 5 stars (I just don't think you should have to wait for fast food in this day and age)

My family and I visited the aquarium this past weekend. For $39 each there wasn't a whole lot to see. We were done in an hour. The penguin habitat was small with a big crowd in front of the window so viewing was limited. Same for the otters. We did get to choose one of the three movies to see for free. The one we chose was about the oceans and it was in 3D and interesting. This is not my first time visiting the aquarium but I don't think there will be a need for me to return. I think they should focus more on making 3D movies which allowed me to view the animals in their natural environments and stop capturing additional animals.

Tried because one of my favorite restaurants across the street was closed. Good thing they were! My friend and I ordered some ribs, mac n cheese (traditional and with goat cheese), asparagus, and potatoe salad. I wasn't too crazy about the potatoe salad but that's not saying it wasn't delicious, just not what my palate is used to. The ribs were so amazing and the mac n cheese just fab! The staff was really nice and constantly checked on us which was nice! Sometimes after you've paid people forget about you, but they didn't! Now if I can only get the recipe to their muffins....

~3.5 stars. Went to this as part of the New Orleans Pass deal. I really don't think I would have come here if I had to pay the $30 cost without the pass. But since we already had the pass, it seemed like a nice place to just hang out and chill. I think we took about an hour and a half to finish this entire aquarium at a leisurely pace, and it was very relaxing.

The aquarium was actually relatively small compared to some other ones I've been to. However it was very nice and cute, and it was also pretty well organized. They have you snake through a predesigned path from start to finish, instead of having an open exhibition of everything. I actually really like it that way because the order was well chosen so that you felt like you were always getting experiencing a new variety of different aquatic climates and activities to do with the subsequent exhibit (the sting ray petting area was fun!), and I really liked that at the end it culminated in a vast fish bowl full of marine life just swimming about, where you could sit down after having completed the aquarium.

However, I did feel like overall they were a bit lacking in overall variety. Yes, they did have a little bit of everything from all major clades of aquatic organisms, but I recall feeling disappointed when I didn't see real leafy seadragons (they have videos of them however) in the seahorse exhibit - which I think should be a staple of every aquarium, or much variety in the jellies they have (they have like 3 or 4 exhibits in all). Especially for the $30 price tag, I don't think this aquarium is worth it. But it was pretty fun overall, well paced and well organized, and I guess a nice spot to just walk around and amuse yourself for an hour or two.

Looking for some BBQ and glad we came upon Saucy's. We got the family meal which included a rack of ribs, brisket  and choice of sausage with 8 single sides. Fed 4 of us plus plenty to take home for tomorrow's meal. Everything was soooo good! Ribs were tender, lean melt in your mouth brisket that came with a side of their horseradish. First time having alligator sausage which i dipped it in their mustard sauce. Definitely left the place satisfied.

This aquarium was average. I'm from Long Beach and our aquarium makes this place look really small in comparison. However, it did seem like a fun place for kids to hang out. they have a pretty big interactive section for kids to play in. The penguins were really cute and active when we were there. The price was okay for us because we got the Audubon experience that included the zoo, insectarium, and the theater. I wouldn't pay for the aquarium on its own though.

I love Saucy's! I am a picky, non-adventurous eater, so I always get the same thing: pulled pork sandwich and macaroni. Their pork is tender and delicious, and I always put the Southern Sweet sauce because it isn't too spicy. The macaroni is a little spicy, but so worth it! It is BYOB, and there is a little convenience store a block over. It is also order at the counter and get your own water/tea, but I'm okay with that. The staff and kitchen are very quick and friendly. All in all, a good neighborhood joint.

I love this place so much! I've been on a huge hot chicken kick over the last few months, and have eaten at almost all the hot chicken places in Nashville. (The only one not tried is Bolton's so far...but I'm on it soon.) One thing is for certain- I CRAVE this chicken!! The 200 degrees is a good heat; doesn't bring too much misery, but doesn't leave you disappointed. I haven't been brave enough to try the 400 just yet, but maybe one day. 

My advice to this little establishment- DO NOT change a thing!! It's so flavorful and addicting. 
Warning- it might burn you twice, but it's so worth it!!

If you need a quick BBQ fix this place will do, but don't expect the best tasting BBQ . For the price it's a good value, but if I want to pour some sweet baby ray's over some Luke warm meat , I can do that at home. Unless you need it, keep lookin' ya'll!

I ended up getting something at claudia clothing and I just happened to see this place so being so hungry I decided to put this food in my mouth I was ready to taste louisiana style bbq style a full rack the fantasy sauce was ok I liked the bold Southern and sweet southern sauce  good place to eat

All Brands is a one-man local business owned and operated by Frank (last name withheld--not sure what the Yelp policy on identifying individuals is), so I will simply refer to "Frank" in my review.

We've used Frank for all manner of appliance woes in the 10+ years we've lived in Havertown. I don't remember who recommended him, but we owe that person a debt of thanks: Frank/All Brands rocks! 

This week it was our microwave that just stopped, well, microwaving. We called Frank on Tuesday night and he was there at 8:00 Wednesday morning. This was also our experience when we had problems with other appliances--a couple of times, Frank arrived within an hour of our call! This time, the patient (the microwave) was too far gone, and Frank point blank told us that he'd repair it if we wanted, but that it would be more cost effective to just replace it. No gouging, no unnecessary work to turn a quick profit--just a frank (couldn't resist!) presentation of our options.

Frank's expertise in computers--which we only discovered fairly recently--has been a bonus. As someone with a home office filled with aging, long-obsolete equipment, I  appreciate Frank's practical, low-cost (and often no-cost) solutions to computer performance issues. He is an advance tester for new releases of Windows, so he has particularly useful insights on operating systems (for the record: he seems to be a fan of Windows 8). 

Frank himself is a bit of a character: an ex-Navy man who enjoys chatting about computers (but does not linger), who gets right to the task at hand, and who (in our experience) is VERY quick in identifying and fixing problems. For our money, having an excellent local go-to guy for appliance problems and computer issues has been a Godsend.

It's a little expensive and filled with too many children running around and screaming. Some of the fish things are cool.  If you don't have children  save your money and time. Again the lines are long. Be prepared  to spend 25 dollars a person just to walk around.
if i give it five stars ur gonna think im an employee. i love their BBQ, u will not be disappointed we do take out brisket and pulled pork and are very satisfied

Beautiful salon, great location and Phil Chavez is the best!  He uses his years of experience to guide his clients through the process of finding the most flattering style.  Great conversationalist too!

This really is a nice summer activity. If you haven't been, it is worth a visit. They don't have any WOW exhibits, but what they do have is nice and well maintained. I think they have a nice jellyfish exhibit. We enjoy the aquarium, but definitely prefer the zoo and Insectarium. Visitors to the city, get the pass for all three if you have time. I do recommend avoiding being there at meal times since it is typical expensive museum fare.

I've been going to Kohl's for years. 8/1/15 was the first time I came to this store. I was buying a Phillies shirt since I was going to the game the next day. Just like almost all the Kohl's stores, they pretty much got everything you need. I have no complaints about the service and the staff.
The chicken is good but sides options are disappointing. It says they are open until 7 but will not take an order after six. Much rather have Bolton's or Helen's.

My friend and I visited last weekend for a self-guided tour and wine tasting. They are open til 6pm, which was great! They had an outdoor deck and grounds, but it was too cold for us to explore much outside, so we mostly stuck to the gift shop and the tasting room :-). It wasn't too crowded, excepting a couple who brought their 2 kids with them to the tasting (????) and the kids kept running around and hitting my legs. Note to parents: it is not socially acceptable to bring your kids to a wine tasting. 

The self-guided tour was really short and quick, but they did provide a decent amount of information. It took us maybe 5-7 minutes to read everything and snap a few pictures. Then we headed to the tasting room! Tasting is only $8, and we got to sample 8 wines. They were small, tasting pours- but still a great price compared to other vineyards/wineries I've been to! The woman leading our tasting was really nice and interesting. I told her we didn't like sweet wines, so she gave us a few extra reds instead of their sweeter wines. We liked one of their two whites that we tasted, and most of the reds. We bought a few bottles to go (most were in the $12-14 range). I loved their spiced apple wine, which we tasted hot, and I bought a bottle home with me- instant hit, it was gone in a few hours! When we were leaving, there were a few couples enjoying snacks and bottled wine on the patio, which looked really cute. 

On a side note, my sister had her engagement party here. I missed it because I was studying abroad in Australia at the time, but both my mom and sister said it was fabulous, decently priced, and fun. So if you're planning a party in the area, you should definitely check this place out!

My gf and I got delivery from here one evening, and we enjoyed it thoroughly!  We split a 2 meat combo plate with brisket and pilled pork.  We also got boudin, baked macaroni, and smoked beans.  I thought it was all very good, and they give you a couple different style bbq sauces to try as well.  The little sweet potato muffins are pretty good too.  
I recommend for good, quick, inexpensive bbq.

Le plus bel aquarium que j'aie visité (et j'en ai vu pas mal).
Prevoyez le pull car la clim est surpuissante, mais ça si vous êtes déjà allés aux USA vous le savez déjà.

Tom is fantastic and incredibly honest! I have personally taken cars to this shop for the last 10 years and have always been impressed. All the guys here are super friendly, knowledgeable and Tom is super flexible with pick up and drop off. He absolutely tells it like it is and will not gouge pricing and always 'tells it like it is' for you to make the best decision possible.

I wanted to really enjoy this place but was disappointed during my visit. First the price was a little steep for 2 adults. Especially since during the visit some of the animals weren't even available to view due to habitat construction. This included the penguins. The rest of the face was clean but lots of open space. It felt as if some of the exhibits were only partially completed for viewing. With the exception of one staff person in the gift shop, every employee seemed like they didn't want to be there. Either on their phones or being short when asking for information. The admission did include a short movie. While I would have been OK without seeing it I felt they could have offered a ticket option that didn't include the 24 minute video. Overall I enjoyed it since I got to see a couple otters but felt let down based on cost.

Nothing is more romantic than sipping on deep reds and crisp whites with your significant other.  My husband and I shared a lovely afternoon of chocolate and wine tasting with another couple here the weekend prior to Valentine's day.  We were seated in a dim-lit dining room with round tables of other couples some young, some old but all there to enjoy an intimate and relaxing time together.  A selection of dry and sweet wines were laid out in front of each seat with a plate of Lindt's chocolates, one to pair with each wine.  I was happy it was Lindt's as they are one of my favorites but have to admit I was slightly surprised it wasn't more of a specialty brand or that of a local chocolatier, but I suppose they wanted to pair with more familiar kind. Nonetheless, they paired quite well with the wines. Our knowledgeable wine guide walked us through each wine and chocolate duo explaining why each were chosen but encouraged us to taste and sip different mixings of wine and chocolate to find the pairing that best fit our individual palates. The one that did it for me was the white chocolate truffle with a dry white - a perfect combo of sweet and dry. There was also a Pinot Noir that was a favorite among the batch that was a sure-take home, a $40 bottle, but worth the add to the collection. 

Our group and I had such a nice time tasting, that we decided to continue with a tasting of dry wines on the lower level of the winery.  The wine hostess was pleasant and friendly, but admittedly not as versed on the wines of the winery, stating that she was new, checking her cheat sheet, and having us read the descriptions ourselves to understand what we were tasting.  Despite that, the experience allowed us to determine our 2nd  wine purchase, a 'whimsical' Chardonnay.  Aside from a bit of the knowledge gap from the wine hostess which was forgiveable as she owned up to it, the beautiful premises, friendly staff, and delicious wines made for a wonderful winery experience.

Very cool little place and friendly staff, was impressed with the crispiness, and juiciness of the chicken, well cooked! My only complaint was the hot sauce mix seemed a little pasty and overpowering to other seasonings. The fries and potato salad were also very good, and the lady was so nice and helpful, even let me try a mix of 100 and 200 degree, I'll be back!

I have never left a nail salon before- until this place. There is a reason it wasn't on yelp as it doesn't deserve to be. 

They brought me in and put me into a spa pedicure chair that has been haphazardly painted (wtf). As I'm sitting and soaking I realize there are at least 7 people ahead of me for two women. They also take any waxing that walks in. Each had at least two people in nails going at once and then would get up and wax. Fine I think-this will take some time.  I asked to pick out a color and was handed a basket of poorly painted cards - if you can't paint a inanimate target with a steady hand, what are you going to do with my nails?!  While I was waiting patiently I began to look around - at the pumice stones and brushes laid out at each station that looked like a science experiment and realized this was no place for me. 

Needless to say I left, wet feet and all and didn't look back. I work in healthcare and have no doubt this place contributes to that angry, red, infected cuticle look of a dirty salon.

This was my first visit to the Aquarium since Hurricane Katrina. I was shocked at the transformation that has taken place. It's glory days are in the past. What has happened to the many outstanding exhibits that were here?  There are far fewer exhibits, less interesting exhibits and fewer fish. It is showing its age and needs better upkeep. The cost of admission is excessive for what is here.  I found it sad.
I get my hair cut and colored here by Carol.  She is not only terrific at cutting and coloring hair, but she is reasonably priced.  I like the salon staff too.  They are very friendly and helpful.

I loved this place! It came as a total shock that it was as great as it was. (I had just assumed it was over-hyped as a touristy type place) There was such a variety of exhibits to see and the array of animals and fish they have contains a handful that I (a person who loves seeing different aquariums) hadn't ever seen in person before. I especially loved the large tank that has a huge, adorable sea turtle and at least a dozen sharks of different types. There was a shark swimming repeatedly past the people opening and closing it's jaws looking fierce(very cool). If I have time on my next visit to NOLA I am making it a point to come here again. And to make sure it's at a good time to catch one of the Imax films too!
Ordered the brisket plate with smoked beans and grilled asparagus. All were delicious... Some of the best brisket I've had. No knife needed. Friendly waitstaff as well!

This place gets 4 for it's service alone.  The food is above average.  To their defense all BBQ I've tried in this city is average at best.  I don't get it but I'll keep looking.  That being said...uptown area this and squeal are the places to go if you are craving BBQ.

This place has some good brisket, great BBQ beans, and nice mac n' cheese.  Continuing the recent trend, that seems to be happening in the fast developing NOLA BBQ scene, they offer five distinctive types of BBQ sauce.  The brisket was very tender and flavorful but unfortunately lacked the hallmark of a distinctive smoke ring to really give the brisket maximum flavor.  The brisket was served with a side of horseradish sauce which was a welcome flavor addition.  The BBQ plates here are served with sweet potato muffins that are very tasty.  I was never fond of this location when Ignatius was here and I still think it is a bit small and cramped but it might add some unique charm to the place.  The BBQ options in NOLA continue to grow and improve and while this place certainly does offer some good BBQ and great sides the brisket at The Joint greatly outshines what is offered here.
Easily the best barbecue in New Orleans.  Friendly, local owners, great service, and a very comfortable room.  The house sauce is my favorite - kinda tangy, not cloying.
Chicken was real good and the service was to told me how long I had to wait and all didn't matter I'm a truck driver love to stand when I can
I had the ribs here, and they were done right! Many sauces to choose from (many on the sweeter side). Mac and cheese was great too. Will be back. Like this place more than The Joint.

If you like hot chicken but are grossed out by some of the not so great locations then 400 degrees on Peabody Street is for you.  It is hole in the wall food without the hole in the wall atmosphere.  Something almost feels wrong about eating hot chicken in a new clean urban spot but whatever it's good. Their new home is a semi food court so they share a larger area with a few other restaurants. 

The chicken here is good. I would rank it second on my hot chicken list above Prince's but below Bolton's. Prices are comparable. The breading was my favorite part. If they offered chicken on a stick I think I would probably give them 5 stars.

I ordered mine 400 degrees and it was probably the hottest chicken I've had... even more so than extra hot at other places.  I can usually handle heat no problem but 400 degrees stuck with me for a long while. 

They don't take cards so bring cash. Everything is made to order so it will take a while. You can call in your order ahead of time and I would recommend it especially around lunch.

Love love love it! Whenever my hubby and I take a trip we are always sure to visit the Zoo and Aquarium and NOLA is no exception.
The entire Audubon institute here is fantastic! As for the aquarium itself, very nicely set up and has lots of diversity! Nice and spacious for walking so even with large school groups it's easy to get around and see the exhibits.

I was very impressed with the aquarium in new orleans. I did not know it was so big with so many displays. I love aquariums and zoos and this one is by far one of my favorite. I would for sure return when im in new orleans again.

The staff is incredibly polite and helpful. Expect to wait 30 minutes for your order because the make everything from scratch. I ordered the 200 degree chicken and a side of baked beans.

First, I love Nashville Hot Chicken and am always looking for a new place to try. This is OK, it was coated with too many spices. It wasn't too hot, just a cake of spices. It wasn't my favorite hot chicken recipe, but it's definitely not the worst that I have had. The baked beans had too much sugar and were like syrup.

What are gourmet popsicles?  That is what I kept asking myself.  We were looking for a sweet snack and decided to give it a try.

I tried the blueberry cinnamon popsicle and it eas fantastic!  The flavor was very powerful and much better than its lab created counterpart.

They have an expansive selection of cool treats all of which can be dipped in milk chocolate if you wish.

A great place for a cool treat!

The Hyppo specializes in natural, gourmet popsicles which are made on site from fresh fruits and spices. The space is decorated nicely and is clean and trendy. The flavors range from Mexican hot chocolate to watermelon hibiscus to raspberry cheesecake. It literally took us like 5 minutes to decide which flavors we wanted, but we never felt rushed to order. The staff was pleasant and the popsicles are to die for. They even have a rewards card that gets you a free "pop" after a certain number of visits (8, I think). 

Yum! Must try.

Another staple in Nashville Food and a true must visit place. The owner cares insanely for the quality of her chicken and it shows across the board. If you ever travel through Nashville or Downtown Nashville just plan on going here. You will not regret it.

After spending the last 4 days at a nutrition conference surrounded by dietitians, I HAD TO stop being a role model for an hour and try some hot chicken while I was in town.  Saw the 4 star reviews on yelp and it was walking distance from the conference center, so we were sold.  Nashville hot chicken was our mission!

Can't speak highly enough of the staff.  It was a fast casual set up in a food court type building but the staff was attentive and wanted to ensure we enjoyed our meal.  I got the chicken tender meal with the white bread, pickles, and ranch and I opted for 200 degrees.  That was supposed to be medium heat but my friend and i were both in agreement it was WAY too spicy.  We were sweating it was so hot.  The chicken was crisp on the outside and moist on the inside but the heat was so overwhelming and it was hard to handle and I can do hot.  This was extreme.  The crazy thing is that they have hotter levels.  It was just so difficult to enjoy my fries or the chicken itself because my mouth was the most on fire it's ever been.

Our friend got the 100 degree and that was a very reasonable amount of heat and it was quite tasty.

A few tips- they make everything from scratch, to order so expect to wait.  Also, off the menu tip for someone looking for a challenge... You can order 800 degree chicken!

I have tried only the pulled pork and coleslaw here, so this is a very limited review.  That said, I liked it so much that it's the only thing on the menu I've tried for that exact reason.  Unlike a prior reviewer, I found the pork very moist and tender.  I also thought the coleslaw complimented it well.  It's not terribly spicy, but it does have jalapeño pepper shavings and coarse brown mustard in it, so it's far from bland.  The pork & slaw sandwich comes with the better of this place's sauces on it - it's thin, savory, and nicely spiced.  They do have a thicker sweet sauce too, but that's not my thing at all.  My six year old liked it better though.  The buns are nothing special - just regular egg buns - so the second time I ordered from there, I just ate my sandwich stuff sans bun.  Since there was coleslaw involved, I decided I was eating a pulled pork salad and even got to feign healthiness.  If Saucy's other offerings are as good as the pulled pork, it really could rival the Joint as yummiest BBQ in the city.  Yep.  A fan, I am.

When there for an after hours convention activity, and it was wonderful. The Aquarium was top notch alone, but the activities they combined with the event (three music stag in the building) and table seating was wonderful. Outside the Aquarium they had traditional food serving for the area, that was great for a buffet (I'm not a buffet fan, in general). The event planners for this Aquarium event did a great job.

This aquarium houses an exhibit, sponsored by several oil companies, that whitewashes the environmental effects of oil rigs on marine life in the Gulf of Mexico. An aquarium employee abjectly misleads an assembled group of children several times a day. (I got an employee to admit to me that the oil companies exercise editorial control over the content of the talk.) For this to be going on after the Deepwater Horizon oil spill, with absolutely no mention of environmental risk or harm, is unconscionable, and overshadows everything else. Don't let the easily bought, morally bankrupt operators of this aquarium propagandize your children. Certainly don't pay them for it. Go somewhere else until they shape up.

Also, since I'm writing something, the tanks are pretty poorly labeled. Many had no examples of the animals shown on attached signs, and many housed animals that weren't shown on any nearby signs.

Apex has a great selection, but I received very poor customer service. I went in to buy a tool for my husband, and the first person showed me to the Festool wall and left me there. I then went to the front desk and received very poor customer service from a second person. I was spending over $1,000 on a tool, and basically received no help. A nice man finally answered a few of my technical questions about the tool, but he was the third person. I try to support local businesses instead of Amazon, but bad customer service makes it really difficult to do so.

Place was cool. Wasn't crazy about how they break up different attractions and then charge for it-in my opinion they should've  be included into one price. Are the insects that much better than the Penguins and Fish that they merit their own exhibition and price point? Real talk, I'd pay to see a penguin and hold one (something they offer) over a spider. Neat place nonetheless daughter and  wife liked it. I did too!
Came here later on a Saturday night. Joe the bartender was so great and so friendly. Actually, every employee came over and talked to us. We had a great experience here and will definitely be back.

What a ripoff!!!!! Every vacation my family goes on we like to see the zoos, aquariums, etc. But this was not worth even half of what it cost. $21 per adult, $18 per child means for a family of 3 your looking at $60. I've been to Mystic Aquarium in CT and ought that was pricey, but worth it. I would not go back to the Aquarium of the Americas if it was free. Not worth it and half of the building is gift shops.

Maybe I am spoiled because I grew up with the Shedd in Chicago but this place was nothing special. 

Fish here and there, lots of empty space and OH, it was $$$$$. It only took us about an hour to walk through the entire place. This is not the place to go when you are trying to escape the heat of New Orleans for the day with your toddler. Also NONE of the food areas were opened. The one stand that was the worker was "talking with the manager" so you couldn't get anything.

The fish were pretty but this ship sank a little for me.

I was visiting from out of town and had problems with my car.  Tom not only got my car back on the road but kept informed about all that was happening while I was waiting.  He was even willing to stay after hours because the part he had ordered had not been delivered.  I don't come across this kind of customer service anymore.  I wish I had Toms in my hometown.  I would go there for all my car needs.

If you want to try Nashville's Famous Hot Chicken this is a good spot. This would be a 4 star if you are a fan of super hot stuff. Just a few blocks from the downtown honky tonk spots, but it closes early so go for lunch. This is in a shared food court with some other places. Clean and friendly, but not much on atmosphere. $10 got me a chicken breast on top of two slices of white bread, side of potato salad & a drink. Not bad, but I would not call it a great value. The Chicken was fried perfectly to order. I like that they cook to order and the chicken is never sitting around. You order your chick 100, 200,300 or 400 degrees. I went 200 and it was hot enough. Some good flavor, but mostly heat. If you you love the heat, I'd give this place a try.

Our Aquarium is excellent.  I think I actually like it better than the one in Atlanta.  It shows you creatures from all over the world and in interesting environments.  I haven't been since Katrina but I know they are trying their hardest to get it back to what it once was.  My only issue is that it is expensive, but it is a MUST for all out of towners or for parents and grandparents looking for something to do with their kids.

While it was good, I didn't think it was great.  The meat didnt have any distinct flavor.  Compared to McClure's, McClure's wins in my opinion.

Saucy's is slightly less expensive on some dishes but the $30 all meat all sides plate at McClure's is a steal (5 meats and 7 sides!).   
McClure's also wins with their sandwhiches coming topped with coleslaw.  Thats the only way to eat a pulled pork sandwich!
MacnCheese is better at McClure's. 
Better sauces at McClure's.
BBQ jambalaya is enough of a reason to go to McClure's. 
Smokier meats at McClure's although, the ribs weren't dry at Saucy's. 

I enjoyed my meal at Saucy's. If you're craving BBQ and in the area, this is a solid option.

I will admit that after going to the Atlanta aquarium, all other aquariums struggle to compare. However, I was not too impressed with this one. First, it is quite pricey. This is common for aquariums, but there just wasn't enough to do and see in my opinion. We were in and out in two hours.  Some of the exhibits were beautiful, like the tunnel in the beginning. We even saw some divers.  The otter exhibit was so so. We got lucky and one of them came out to play.  I enjoyed the parakeets and sea turtle (!!!!) but the big viewing window could've been more enjoyable if there was better seating (seats all the way in the back).  They do have penguins which was cool. There is a play area and touch pool. And, you get admission to a 30 min movie in the big screen theater, which was a nice addition. They have a food court and state no outside food or drinks (we did it anyway and no one stopped us, but c'mon!). Again, it is an enjoyable aquarium and it is in walking distance of the French Quarter. However, be prepared to spend $100 for a family of four.

I was on a quest to try all 4 fried chicken places before year-end. This one was by far the worst - but I'm willing to give it a 2nd try. I had the 200 degrees (medium) and the staff told me that it was similar to the medium at Prince's. WRONG! This medium left my mouth on fire. I was seriously sweating as I consumed this chicken.

The food itself - the chicken skin was so burnt. My friend and I described as follows: 1) You can cut through the skin and eat the white meat like a bread bowl. 2) It was like cutting steak. Heck, my fork snapped in half at 1 point.

Service: Well, we don't come here for that but these people didn't even look at you. There was no one in line and the 2 ladies were socializing. As I started to ask questions about hotness and comparable to the other chicken places, she simply replied, "You can see the menu. It explains it."
   Don't want soda? Better bring your own cup. This same lady looked so annoyed that we asked for a cup for water.

Willing to give this another try just so it gets a fair review on here - but with Bolton's and Prince's and even Pepperfire - why would you want to go here? Plus, they are the only ones that close at 7pm.

Hot chicken rookie here.  I found this place because it was close to my hotel.  Located in a corner food court with 3 other shops.  Service was prompt and courteous.  Prices were affordable and my food was cooked to order.  I got the 200 degree wings which were as much as I could do.  They have plain 100 and 400.  Maybe next time, but I do recommend this place.  Sides were fine so take a chance and visit.

We were done seeing everything in an hour. For the price, it's disappointing. The main reason of interest was to see the mermaids who were advertised as an attraction but upon arrival we found out the were only going to be there for two weekends in November (not when we were there). A few points of interest are the walkway with water above you, the Gulf of Mexico display and the croc (or alligator?). There's a gift shop and food court halfway through which strongly distracted our two year old. There were also multiple school field trips with kids playing too rough in the play space for our little one to enjoy it. 

Overall I wouldn't recommend it. Perhaps I'm spoiled by the two better aquariums we have in CT. Either way, if you have a younger kid opt to go to the children's museum which is more interactive, less expensive, and you can spend more time there.

This location is unique in that it's in a strip mall not a normal shopping mall. It was a bit awkward from the outside in a rundown strip in front of a bad Walmart. 

On the inside it definitely redeemed itself. Fully stocked with candles and lotions everywhere and looked the exact same as the mall locations. There was ample staff and they were knowledgeable as well. 

Some women were going crazy over the wall scents on sale too haha

Still gets pricey as it all adds up, went with a friend and she spent $100 on candles there after being brought in on the freebie mailers they send out. They definitely know what they are doing. 

Smells nice inside of course almost a bit overpowering, but still pleasant and the cozy decor really sets it apart from the area. 

In conclusion random awkward location, but the interior redeemed itself and the staff seemed on par.

We purchased a family membership from the Zoo, giving us free admission to the aquarium. Enjoyed the movie at the IMAX that was filmed before and after Katrina. And walking through the aquarium was great too. Good location, clean, great exhibits.

A small aquarium, lots of cool exhibits.

Getting there in a wheelchair is not easy, since you have to go over several railroad tracks and then uphill.

Once inside, everything gets easier. Plenty of room to maneuver and lots of cool exhibits.

This restaurant offers a range of excellent signature sauces. There are a number of excellent meats to choose from, including slow cooked brisket, pulled pork, and local sausages. The sides are excellent and aside from what's on the menu, they have seasonal specials too. Portion sizes are good for one meal and the price is right. Get the 25 cent sweet potato muffin!

The staff are super sweet, the service unrivaled.

My son loves the place what can I say. I've been countless times so it's a bit repetitive for me but I am excited to see what they do with the new shark exhibit that's supposedly being built. One thing I do recommend in the future if they can implement is please add some more food choices!

This is a great chicken place. They have great fire hot chicken that's real tasty. I had an awkward exchange with the person I was checking out with thus the lower rating. But the chicken was solid, and it's in a great lunch location downtown.
The aquarium is a great attraction in New Orleans! You must see it!

This place is our favorite! Always fresh and different flavors. My new husband and I actually love this place so much we had them cater our wedding for dessert instead of doing cake! It was so fun and different (and yummy!) and somehow their pops aren't drippy so they don't make a mess which is great! Love them!!

It seem overpriced, 53.00 for 3 adults with a coupon .but the exhibits were nice. I wouldn't go back ,nothing unique. They did have a stingray petting pool. And a parakeet  area. The penguins are also nice. Don't expect a lot and you won't be disappointed.

My husband and I went here in our quest to find hot chicken as good (or better) than Hattie Bs. We wanted to like this place because of the owner's background and positive attitude. But the taste and spice of this chicken doesn't measure up to Hattie Bs (where my husband craves hot tenders). The sides were OK; nothing to note. And the atmosphere, as others have noted, leaves a bit to be desired since it's a shared food court without prominent signage. Still, we hope the best for this young woman and her continued success in Nashville.

They have #1 THE HOTTEST Chicken in Nashville.  
The Best environment/atmosphere..
but not the best chicken....NO...not the best..maybe 4th best....check out my other reviews....I LOVE HOT CHICKEN.

But where do pain from extreme heat and flavor meat?  at the other Nashville hot chicken joints.  To be fair...I have not tried their mild...200 degrees and wish I had because 400 is just too hot for me.  I ate it...enjoyed it...but burped it up feeling hotness all day....it was too much...I wondered if I had harmed my body (and I eat hot stuff all the time).

The chicken is wet hot chicken as opposed to Bolton's which is dry (try Bolton;s fish...it is incredible).  Pepperfire has wet chicken and I think they are the best in Nashville....a better flavor (complexity)...heat and flavor maxed out just right. and of course Princes is a must...excellent chicken.

Atmosphere:  the best seating in Nashville...they are in a little food court type building place with a Quiznos and a couple other restaurants...with plenty of seating in a climate controlled atmosphere. which is nice....

I'm a judgmental person. We all have flaws... 

Allow me to judge Saucy's BBQ... Tasty. Tasty. TASTY! 

We went to Saucy's because we were in the area, hungry, and found a coupon on Yelp. The coupon brought us in, but the food will keep us coming back. The service was incredible, as was the food. We got a 1/2 rack of ribs (6) and several sides. The beans were amazing (sweet and savory). The coleslaw was not overpowered by mayonnaise. Delicious! We got the dry rub on the ribs. Slow cooked, fall of the bone goodness. O-M-G! It was especially nice to be able to try the assortment of sauces they have stacked on the table. 

I usually leave BBQ places regretting my decision to have BBQ in the first place. Few places have made me feel otherwise. Saucy's is at the top of that small list of BBQ exceptions.

Try it. NOW!

Juicy brisket. Fall off the bone ribs. Delicious boudin sausage. Creamy & cheesy Mac and Cheese. Crunchy slaw. Must I say more? I don't, but I will!

The 25¢ sweet potato muffins reminds you of Fall. Dunk it in the variety of BBQ sauces Saucy's offers & thank me later. 

Boyfriend opted for the brisket sandwich (boeuf french 9$) with blue cheese & a side of coleslaw. Stuff the coleslaw in the sandwich & get to eating. I love that they use the Vietnamese style French bread because it just adds that super light/ crunchy dynamic. Best freaking sandwich I've had at any BBQ place. I can truly imagine the French bread soaking up the juicy goodness from the pulled pork (which is what I'm choosing next time I visit). 

The brisket was thick cut & oh so juicy. It seriously just melted in your mouth. It didn't need any condiments because it stood so well on its own!

I loved the boudin sausage. It was seasoned so perfectly. & it wasn't mushy like other places. My only complaint is that the casing around the sausage made it really difficult to cut into. The horseradish sauce complemented the boudin like pb&j!

Also, hands down best Mac & Cheese I've had at a restaurant. It was super cheesy & so creamy. Which I know I said already. But some places are a little too dry. This was done perfect. 

Spicy slaw was Okay. Definitely enjoyed it more for the texture than the flavor. It wasn't spicy but maybe I just eat too spicy? Eh, wish I tried the bake beans instead. 

Seriously couldn't have had a better experience! 

Very inexpensive lunch. Especially if you check in & get your 20% off. Our meal was 24$

Nashville's hot chicken is my weakness and 400 degrees is a great place to get some. Their hours are a little weird but they do have a little parking lot. Hot chicken fanatics might be a little skeptical because it is so clean, but it is the real deal. I have had both the 200 and 400 degree versions. They aren't kidding when they tell the 400 degree is so hot it will burn you twice. Be sure to get their awesome sweet tea to wash it down.

We always visit the local aquariums when we travel. So much history about the marine life in the area. 
These compassionate people rescue the local animals during storms, injuries etc... 
They also offer a very important short film about the importance of the wetlands. Fun and educational for the whole family!

Very disappointed. We called to ensure they could accommodate children and they were very polite on the phone. Even asked us if we wanted to call our order in, and we explained that we had never been there and would need to see the menu. 

Upon arriving the area was very open sitting and I would say a nice atmosphere. No one was in line for 400 degrees. When we got to the register to order, we were asked if we had a call in. We said no, and she told us it would be an hour wait. 

We asked why when no one was there and it was explained that they had a lot of call in orders and they handle those first. We asked them "Don't you service your walk in customers first?" And they answered "No." We were totally floored! We left to find hot chicken somewhere else.

Very disappointed that they wouldn't service someone that walks into their restaurant first, especially after she explains that they don't cook the food until the person shows up to pay for it... Made no sense to us. We didn't even get to try the chicken due to the long wait. Doubt we'll go back.

Loved the laid back atmosphere of this place, clean and simple design. There were so many flavors to choose from! I ordered the Basil Honeydew Popsicle while my fiancé ordered the Blackberry Lemonade pop. We both enjoyed them. It's a tasty treat in the heat of Florida. I'm giving it 3-stars, because it was fine. I thought the prices were a bit high, but it probably costs a lot to keep up so many flavors. I suggest narrowing down the menu, and bringing prices down a couple cents.

We loved our experience, we actually bought a family membership, which includes unlimited access to the aquarium, insectarium and zoo for a year ($155). Our daughter loved Parakeet Point, where you buy a Popsicle stick for $1.50 and get to feed birds! Amazing memory for her. We also touched sting rays. The facility was very clean. We will be going several times this year, and I can't wait!

This is a great desert biking trail. When I was visiting my Arizona people I rented a cannondale F400 hardtail from Cycle Tucson and headed out. It's not like mountain biking. It's mostly a pleasure ride, with ups and downs on rocky little hills, a few challenging gravel covered areas, desert plants and cactus all around. There are places on the trail that twist through dense patches of prickly pear cactus. As I was flying through there at full peddle I just hoped I wouldn't hit some loose sand and dive into it. Saw a mad cow with cactus needles sticking out of his nose glaring at me. It's an easy ride with some cool little shrines people set up along the trail. I rode around on multiple routes for 3 hours but you could spend a whole day there. I saw maybe 3 people the whole time. After that I rode back to my grandmas place on Pantano Wash. It's a fun ride, especially for a lazy amateur. Wear sunscreen and bring a camelback full of water.

Based on yelp reviews, I was expecting something much more amazing.  Please note: We travel A LOT, and we've been to aquariums all over the world, so my standards could be unreasonable -- I don't know.
We went on a Monday around 2:30pm. I'm so grateful that it wasn't busy because it's pretty small.
This aquarium needs some TLC and an upgrade -- kind of disappointing. However, my tots thoroughly enjoyed themselves. We saw everything, my tots played to their hearts content, and we were still able to roll out of there in less than two hours.

Oregonians don't waste your precious vacation time here.  Go to the Oregon coast aquarium instead. Oregon coast is nicer and more affordable.  This aquarium was okay but it cost almost $20 a person and really wasn't worth that price.

I grew up in LA, at a time when there were two large sea parks (Sea World in San Diego and the now defunct Marineland of the Pacific in Palos Verdes) within driving distance. I have to say though, Audubon Aquarium did not disappoint. I have this thing about going to museums and aquariums because of my graduate work in biology, my husband has learned to indulge me.

To be perfectly honest I wasn't expecting much after seeing how much of the city still hadn't been rebuilt. But there was quite the variety of exhibits, the animals (otters, fish, frogs, penguins) seemed happy enough. I thought the penguin and otter tanks could stand to be cleaned as the glass was slightly foggy with minerals and debris. 

Yes it is small, but that isn't a bad thing. I really enjoyed the gulf coast tank - which is the largest tank. I could have sat in front of that for hours.

They had a lovely exhibit about Amazon fish - and the fish I had worked on were even in the tanks - that I thought was quite interesting.

All in all, I say if you have the time, if you're sober enough, it is definitely something to check out. Afterwards you can stroll along the Mississippi.

Great place to take the family in New Orleans! 

We had an awesome time here with our two year old and I'm sure older kids would love it too. It's quite large and has several different exhibits. Great place to spend 2 to 3 hours explore. 

In addition to the exhibits you also get to see one movie with your entrance fee. We chose the 24 minute 3D dinosaur movie and it was pretty cool. 

Another nice plus side to this museum is it's right by the Canal Street trolly stop so it's convenient to get to. We went in summer and there was also a little splash pad fountain area outside. If we had know that, we would have brought a towel and swim trunks to let the little one splash around.

Overall great experience and we would recommend visiting the Aquarium.

Loved this aquarium, they had a nice selection of sea creatures. My only complaint is that it was a bit small. I didn't want to leave :(

Touching the stingrays was pretty cool and slimy although I felt a little sad for them. Who would really want to get touched by strangers all day? 

Overall, it's a fun time for both kids & adults.

Read great reviews on this place.. but when we got here, the doors were locked.. They get zero stars from me today. It's only 4:15 PM and their doors are locked.  Lights are on, sign says open and is listed to close at 5pm... when they say close at 5, what does that really mean?

I had five trimming shears that became very dull after trimming  a certified, legal grower friend's outdoor-grown harvest in mid October, 2016.  I needed to find a professional sharpener who could rehabilitate trimming shears that I had made dull because I thought I knew how to sharpen them.  I did not!  I searched Yelp and discovered that although there are other professional sharpening services who may be just as excellent as APEX SAW WORKS in Reno, I nonetheless chose Apex because the other reviews gave Apex stellar reviews by other satisfied customers.
     I dropped my shears off at Apex on a Monday and was told they'd be sharpened by the next Monday, but I was pleasantly surprised they were ready several days earlier!
     These were expensive shears: carbon steel, titanium, and stainless steel, that must maintain a sharp edge and at a specific angle on the cutting edges and was very concerned that some ham-fisted Apex employee would not know how to sharpen these expensive, and unique trimming shears that are exclusively used by experienced, professional trimmers, (two with a curved tip- useful for removing fan leaves from the buds), and had a concern they may not have been sharpened correctly.  I was relieved that my concerns about proper sharpening were non existent.
     I was also relieved to find that not only were all shears expertly and professionally sharpened by Apex employee, BOB, (sorry-didn't get the man's last name), but the fee was very reasonable and fair.
     Perhaps there may be other sharpening services in the Reno, Nevada area that are as excellent, professional and with great pricing as APEX SAW WORKS.  However because I received such excellent, courteous, and professional sharpening of expensive and specialized trimming shears, I now can confidently and happily recommend the proven expertise of APEX SAW WORKS and their professional sharpener, BOB.
    I was additionally impressed by Apex employees I met there- two lovely women who were helpful, friendly and very congenial.
     I sincerely believe the emerging medical dispensaries, existing now, and others that will soon be open, should strongly consider submitting their trimmer's shears to APEX SAW WORKS to ensure their trimmers always have sharp tools to produce productive quantities of
trimmed product.
   Respectively submitted by grateful customer, David Tscheekar.

I very much miss one of the best hair stylists I've ever had, Aysha. She moved here to Mane Street a few years ago from Phoenix, and I was lucky enough to be one of her first clients in the Tucson area. I referred all of my friends to her, and now she's so busy she is booked weeks in advance. She listens to what you want- even telling you when you told her something different on the last visit- you know, for when you get those "wild hairs" and think about chopping off what you've been growing out for the last 5 years? She was like- uh, no, but if you tell me you still want to cut it next time I will cut it off. She was right, and I am so glad she listened to what I meant and not what I said.  Mane Street is a busy, friendly little place with an aesthetician, quite a few chairs, and a nice staff. Highly recommend.

I did have a bad extension job here once, but the guy that did it is long gone.

So yummy! I love the different flavors that Hyppo offers for unique popsicles. I always get the Vanana Banilla and it never disappoints! Tried the PB Pie, Pear Pie and Champagne Mango popsicles today too and we loved each one of them! Champagne Mango is my new favorite! Definitely stop in and try a popsicle, it's perfect for a hot summer day!

BEST HOT CHICKEN IN THE WORLD!!!

Hot chicken enthusiasts like to argue about who makes the best. The facts are, Prince's invented hot chicken, but 400 Degrees perfected it. I get the 200 which is a perfect balance of tasty buttermilk marinated chicken and cayenne heat. My husband goes for the 400 and does a dance when he eats it. I get a full body rush when I eat this stuff, it's like delicious delicious crack. The meat is tender and not greasy like other places and the crispy fries make a suitable companion. 

Call ahead and you won't have to wait. The owner takes the time to get to know her patrons and treats them like family. What more could you want?

I have always loved bbq, but I like it even more now.  I'm on the paleo diet and am constantly craving meat and fat, and boy does this place hit the spot.  The ribs are absolutely delectable, melt-in-your-mouth delicious.  The brisket and Chaurice sausage are great as well.  I went twice today.  The pulled pork is also good.  I'm from North Carolina, so I know.

We have been to a few aquariums that were really cool so for the price of this aquarium we had high expectations and were a tad disappointed. There wasn't a lot and we got through it in an hour and a half and that was with our 2 year old in a stroller slowing us down. It was very clean and has some cool things, it was just small. For a one time visit it was fine, but I wouldn't ever have a desire to go back.

My boss took me here today and I was extremely surprised about how good the food was! I'm talking spectacular! I had something call a grilled sourdough brisket sandwich. I didn't even know I liked sourdough lol

Frank is a skilled, kind, and helpful professional repairman. My refrigerator was on the fritz, and I thought I'd be burdened with an expensive applicable purchase just after the holidays. Frank worked to diagnose the issue over the phone, but scheduled an appointment to confirm the diagnostic issue. Not only did Frank figure out exactly what was going on, he brought the necessary part to complete the repair at the same time. Frank even gave a discount for paying cash. The refrigerator is now like new, my wallet is happy, and I found a local repair service to rely on. I strongly recommend contacting All Brands for your appliance repair needs.
Great for adults and kids.  Well worth the admission price.  Loved it, it was awesome!

The Hyppo is a gourmet popsicle shop with multiple locations in Florida, including Central Ave in St Pete.  They got their name because their original location is on Hypolita St in St Augustine (which was was discovered on the day of the Feast of Saint Augustine of Hippo).  

They have a crazy amount of exotic flavors so it's really difficult to decide. Now I wish I had realized earlier that if you look at the menu, you'll see a star next to the ones with dairy (maybe 7-8 of them). That may be a quick way to eliminate some flavors, if you want or don't want dairy. I wish I had gotten one with dairy because I like the creaminess. Instead, I got one without it, the guava hibiscus.  The flavors weren't really strong but it was good nonetheless. They're $3.50 each and on the small side. 

I'll give them 4 stars for having so many options and being creative with the flavors, as well as having friendly service. However, I wish they had more dairy options and were a little cheaper so  that it would be more affordable to try a couple flavors. I'd also recommend they chop one up so they could pass out samples. They do have a loyalty card where you'll get a free one after so many purchases.

Great Greek salad with gyro meat! Very fresh, the dressing was lemony-fresh and the gyro meat was delicious. Also, the staff is very friendly and welcoming.

While the food was fresh and tasty, prices did seem a bit on the steeper side. If I lived in the area by St. Roch Market, I would come by more frequently if it was a bit more budget friendly.

4/5 fun (but pricy!)

first review of 2014! this place was super fun - i always like aquariums more than zoos since i feel closer to the animals, albeit behind the plastic/glass. my biggest concern with this place is the price - a family of four would need to hand over $80 just to get in! i got in because of the free day for the parish - i think in the future they should consider spreading it out and doing it by zip code to ease congestion...

but once you're in, it's a pretty cool space. i had always thought it was just a tourist trap, but actually decent presentation. i like that they map a path for you, so you can clearly go through every section. i really like that the louisiana/southern-specific areas actually have strong showings, from the white alligator to the anaconda - yeah, was really surprised to see that one! they could throw a little more lighting on the educational boards and supervise a bit more on the folks sending their bright flashes into the tanks (poor nemo!) but i do appreciate the floor space. i didn't feel crowded even among the crowd. the cafe was also pretty affordable (about $10 for a sandwich/fries), but the haagen daz was not. the folks at the front are super helpful as you start out, and they may also be the same folks you'll see on the floor for the timed chats (though it is weird to feel otter pelt in front of their tank...). overall, it makes a cute date and i'd be back, but likely not unless i have a big discount or another free pass.

My husband and I visited the aquarium yesterday. We hadn't been in years. The Gulf of Mexico exhibit was our favorite. This exhibit houses sandtiger sharks, sandbar sharks, nurse sharks and some rays as well as a giant green sea turtle named King Midas. We got to see them being fed while we were there which was pretty cool. We really had a great time.

Great aquarium!  Perfect way to cool off after being out in the hot summer sun all day and learn about some really beautiful sea life.  The exhibits are divided into regions and the animals that are native to it.  The sharks, sea turtles, otters, and penguins were really cool.  Buy your ticket as a combo with the zoo.  I would say do the zoo first and then end your day with the aquarium to cool off.  If you can, go during the week to avoid large groups and crowds.  Definite must see!

The name is soooo right! They make you feel comfortable and at home like it's My spot. Great conversation and atmosphere while getting my nail services done. Prices are great, place is super clean and neat. Wont ever go to another place....this has been my nail home for 6 years!

My husband and I did a traditional wine tasting and chose 7 out of 12 wines on the menu for $8. The woman who did the tasting for us was amazing and was wonderful interacting with our 2 year old throughout the tasting. I would definitely recommend the stop at this little shop. Especially because you can take a wine slushie to go as you walk around the village shops in the area. 

Also, wine slushies are half price during happy hour making them $4 each!!!!!!

So pleased with this gem of a winery.

This aquarium is not the biggest or the fanciest I've been to, but the staff is super friendly and the prices are so reasonable! Lunch for my husband and I was only $13! The exhibits are beautiful and the animals are clearly well cared for. I was also impressed they don't use single-use lids or straws, and do use paper bags instead of plastic (way to "walk the walk" guys!).

What REALLY made this a five star experience though, was getting to meet Darwin and his pal Marina the penguin. We paid to do the penguin experience and were treated to a small group of only 6 getting the behind-the-scenes tour of the exhibit, the kitchen (and meal prep!), and small circle chit chat with Marina! She was the most amazing bird and I still can't believe she fell asleep in my lap  I learned SO much about the penguin exhibit at the aquarium, and her species in general, the crises being experienced by her population in the wild, and what we can do to help. We even got to go home with some art made by Marina! This was one of the coolest things I've ever done in my life. Definitely go and support them! Next time when we come back, we want to do this again, and the sea otter experience too!

The aquarium is a nice diversion and certainly worth a good 1.5-2 hours of your time. They have a cool jellies exhibit and they were showing off a baby alligator when I visited. My only real criticism was that a large amount of floor space was dedicated to animals not found in a fish tank.

I drive all the way from uptown to get some of their delicious hummus and baba ganoush. (Also the baklava was to die for) I was lucky to try their food their first week at St. Roch, and they were so gracious and excited. Their great service and food keeps me coming back! Try it and you won't be disappointed.

Full disclosure: I am no BBQ aficionado. I wouldn't even call myself a fan. It's something I'll have maybe once or twice a year. But the next time the mood strikes me, I'll definitely come back to Saucy's. It's a small place with a casual "bbq joint" vibe. They have a variety of sauces, all worth trying. I'm a fan of their smoked beans because they include a variety of beans instead of they typical one-note baked beans most bbq restaurants serve. And for the record, I came here with 2 BBQ lovers and they were just as pleased with their meal as I. If one restaurant can make all 3 of us happy, you've achieved quite an accomplishment.

Yummmmm. We went on a Friday evening and the service was fabulous! Tricia was super friendly and very knowledgeable. Service with a smile for sure! My fiancé got the watermelon hibiscus and I got the black goat which is blackberry and goat cheese. It was so good and creamy. I want another one! I can't wait to go back and try their other flavors

Rafik just served me the hands-down best Shakshouka of my life.  Perfect sauce, full of veg, but not too chunky. Eggs done right; soft, fresh pita, smooth creamy hummus, and the pickles were perfect contrast to keep you going back for more.  Gotta go, gotta go back.

I have been to lots of aquariums. This ranks 4/5 on my list. It is a small yet pretty cool aquarium! You can see lots like sting rays, owl, otters, penguins, sea horses, jelly fish etc. 

I had a nice time and will return again.

It was extremely crowded when we went, but not the reason we are giving it 1 star. The animals were amazing and the place was very nice, there were parts that were shut down, and we went through the whole place in about 30 minutes and it cost 90$ for my little family of 3 to go which I thought was a little ridiculously priced. I've been to much bigger, better aquariums for cheaper. I called the manager with a complaint I had & never got a call back so that is the reason for the low rating.

I love hot chicken, and have been loyal to Prince's Hot Chicken for over 20 years...BUT, I have become quite dissatisfied with Prince's.  I just can't deal with the wait and poor customer service anymore.  Today, my co-workers and I decided to give 400 Degrees a try.  THANK GOD we did.  It was great!!!!  They actually answered the phone when we called in our order, AND it was ready on time when we got there to pick it up!  Go figure!  The chicken was delicious.  Very tasteful and priced great.  Thank you GOD I don't ever have to go to Prince's again for Hot Chicken!

I like the structure of this aquarium -- the way the exhibits flow from one to another. $20 per person for a couple hours inside (mostly visiting the white alligator and viewing the various shark tanks) was money well spent. In addition to the fishes, there were also a lot of birds both in their own exhibits and sprinkled throughout the others. I was particularly excited to spot an owl but, honestly, I could have spent hours with the sharks. I'm a fan. The penguins were on vacation while we were there because their exhibit is undergoing refurbishment. 

There were a ton of children which is not my style but I certainly can't blame the aquarium for that. Luckily, we figured out that we didn't have to wait behind the large group of elementary school aged children and their adults (who were almost successfully blocking the main entrance) and got a good head start on them.

This place is incredible.  I know they have other BBQ places, but whenever I visit them they're closed.  The owner came out and talked to another table of Texans.  He is a transplant from Austin, which is the "hipster" part of Texas.
I got the opportunity to take some pics, and it was eccentric, clean, and authentic.  A good combo for a New Orleans restaurant.

I love most BBQ.  The Joint, Hwy. 23, and even Voodoo BBQ, (except the experimental "concept" store on Loyola)--that place is a disaster.  It's more like a "Terminus" in my opinion.  

I cooked some boneless, skinless, thighs using my "homeless chicken" recipe (it was taught to me by a homeless man I bought groceries for)--instead of the $10 cash we wanted.  (Wonder what that could have been utilized to buy?)
I used cherry wood and zuppardo's has the chicken.  It's perfect!  I love BBQ!  Can't get enough.  The owners of Bevi told me of some ultimate places I am still exploring.  I thank them eternally....  This is one they said was great, and they were "Johnny on the spot!!"

Maybe we're spoiled having Shedd Aquarium in Chicago but we were very unimpressed. It took us 50 minutes to walk through the place (Shedd in Chicago is 4-5 hours if you hurry!). The aquarium is very kid friendly but not very educational or entertaining for anyone over the age of 10. I understand they lost all the animals to hurricane Katrina and the subsequent flooding but that doesn't help the fact that it's a small, poor aquarium. Nothing special but if you have small kids, give it a shot.

I would not go again.  I was expecting way more exhibits than what I saw.  I was highly disappointed with the pricing of the tickets, the parking prices, and the time it closed.  I just thought it would stay open 'til atleast 6pm.  Yet it closes at 5pm.  Way too early, imo.  Yet who am I?  I would not recommend going to anyone with the pricing being high for tickets and parking.  Not worth it at all.

This gem is worth all the praise! The food is unbelievable, and the staff go above and beyond.  Everyone was so helpful with very outgoing personalities. This spot will for sure stay high on my list of favorites.
Nice but needs more reef aquariums and should have a flower banks exhibit.

Ein ganz tolles Aquarium mit unter anderem Seepferdchen, Quallen, die nicht viele Aquarien zu bieten haben.

Das Aquarium zeigt außerdem auch die Wasserwelt des Mississippi.

Alle Tiere werden auführlich auf Englisch erklärt.

Eins der schönsten Aquarien, die ich bis jetzt besucht habe.
It's a good way to beat the weather and spend an hour or so. But it's an ok aquarium at best. They're working on new exhibits so perhaps it'll get updated and be even better.

Tried Saucy's right after it opened and have been back since.  Such a cute location wafting such smoky smells onto the street.  Many different bbq sauces, many sandwiches on the menu in addition to the "normal" bbq additions.  Melty blue cheese over pulled chicken is delicious.  Sides are on point - every bbq staple.  Even with all the bbq joints around, Saucy's holds its own.  Very enjoyable and competitive.

Love the idea, and love the execution - props to The Hyppo. Gourmet ice pops definitely seem to be the new "cupcakes" but these are just so much better and you don't have to feel like crap for eating one. 

Hyppo has at least 40 different flavors of handmade ice pops, with combinations too intriguing to pick just one. I'm not sure how often the flavors get updated, but on a breezy March night the honey grapefruit was a personal favorite, as was the nectarine orange blossom and mango mojito. Each pop actually tastes like the ingredients it claims to be fabricated of, and best part is that each pop isn't overly sweet. Oh and at $3.50/pop this frozen treat is a no brainer. 

Much kudos to the staff as well, when I went there was a younger man and woman working there, both with great attitudes and happy to answer questions about the brand or specific pops. All in all this place was fantastic - please come to Baltimore!

Awesome aquarium! This coming from the man who thinks if you've seen one good aquarium you've seen them all. But I'd put it up there with the Georgia Aquarium in Atlanta and the Shedd Aquarium in Chicago. Maybe not quite on that level, but pretty close. They have a ton of tanks, a lot of exotic fish, and sculptures made out of trash reclaimed from the seas.

It is still very cool to go here, It was soo crowded and it was hard to stay and really enjoy anything because you are constantly jostled along and it is hard to hang out in any one spot and just enjoy it. It had been almost 10 years since my last visit, but it didn't really feel like they had made any changes or added anything. Still the staff is amazing and it is so cool to see all the amazing creatures.

Great store with great wine. They even allow you to taste it before purchase if you ask. I LOVE coming in here. The prices are very reasonable and the staff is super friendly. Every time I come here with my family we purchase between all of us about 10 bottles. We like to stock up on our wine from here so we don't end up buying inferior wine from elsewhere. Stop in and give them a whirl.
