Best hummus in the world!  Seriously, the hummus, baba ganoush and Labna are amazing (the baba ganoush had a delightful smokiness) and the pita fresh and hot.  If I could eat here every day I would (I actually did while I was in town).  In fact we got tubs of everything to go when we left town.

Yummy place to just grab a refreshing treat. Went there today with a friend to check it out and was quite surprised at how many different flavors they offer. This place is pretty new so everything smells like paint.
Okay.  What a delightful, fun spot downtown St Pete.  Flavored galore and flavor to savor.  Tasty, cool treats that are a healthier choice.  Fun.  Take the kids and enjoy it yourself.

Now this is an aquarium!

We had the entire place to ourselves and it was rented out for a corporate event. 

The aquarium is well maintained and clean. The exhibits are well thought out and orchestrated. 

The Penguins were my personal favorite and the albino alligator was something I've never seen before. 

This is an aquarium well done and puts others to shame.

Want to know what I think is super cool?  The ocean. A lake. The Gulf. Being near the water feels like home to me. It soothes and relaxes me and just feels right, ya know?

Want to know what's even cooler than that? Under the water. If you've ever scuba dived or gone snorkeling you know this, too. It is a entire different world down there. It is so tranquil. No car horns blaring, no police sirens...just blissfully quiet yet teeming with life. I love schools of fish, sea anemones, sting rays, sea otters (OMG so stinking cute!!) and just ocean life in general. That's my thing. 

Obviously I'm a fan of aquariums. Luckily I live near one of the best ones in the country. The Audubon Aquarium of the Americas is an excellent place to observe all of the wonderful creatures that live under the sea. My favorite time to visit is on one of the scorching hot days of summer, which are pretty often here in New Orleans. It's dim and cool inside and its easy to imagine that you really are under the sea.  There's also an IMAX theater here which is always showing something really neat and it's usually in 3D.  

You should go check it out. Who knows? You might even become a wannabe mermaid like me.

I was pleased to find that a barbecue restaurant had opened up in this area of uptown, as The Joint is fairly remote, Voodoo BBQ isn't very good, and Squeal is way up in the Riverbend area. Saucy's took over the space formerly occupied by Ignatius, right next to Miss Claudia's Costume Shop and right across from Magasin Vietnamese Cafe. Unfortunately, Saucy's BBQ isn't quite what the doctor ordered. The beef brisket was pretty good, but the pulled pork was dry and grainy. The house "bold" sauce that the server recommended was awful...tasted like someone had poured a fifth of cheap whiskey into a bottle of A1 sauce. The purple cabbage cole slaw had no flavor. The smoked beans were good but fairly unremarkable. The sweet potato muffin served with the BBQ platters was heavily sweetened, more like dessert than bread. This is a passable BBQ restaurant; certainly not terrible, but definitely not great either. The Joint is still the winner in metro New Orleans.

The best Mediterranean food I had in awhile. I didn't know what I wanted to try. I had a falafel platter and the falafel had an egg in it. So good! Never had that before and I'm so happy I tried it. I also got a Gyro to go, just couldn't pass that up. It was so much food! The manager was super nice and helpful. Will definitely be back!

I went to Dr. Oki bc of some off test results for the baby. I was stressed and really emotional with no answers. Dr. oki 's office not only got me in, they stayed late on a Friday night just to make sure we got the ultra sound we needed. He explained everything and was kind. And He didn't rush while we were in an almost two hour appointment when everyone else was gone home for the weekend. Thank you Dr. Oki for your optimism and kindness to my husband and I.

I was visiting some fam in St Pete and we decided to take an evening stroll after dinner. I was busting out of my jeans...literally! Practically rolling down the street because I was so full but decided to walk in and just "check the place out." I did a double-take on the flavors...there were LOTS of good ones so I knew I had to make space for a pop in my belly. Walked out of The Hyppo and briskly walked back and forth for ten minutes before I was back in and ready to order my pop. I went with the Chocolate Peppermint because it was a seasonal flavor and I loved it! I did not know craving pops was a thing but it is. I craved a chocolate peppermint everyday in St Pete and still am. This place is a definite if you're in the area.

Saying I have an obsession with zoos and aquariums is putting it lightly. I'm very happy to say, New Orleans, has two top notch Audubon institutes. 

I did an internship when I was 13 at the Aquarium, for fun, while others were fulfilling class hours. We would have educational hours, and then they would send us off into the exhibits to drop knowledge on the masses in our green uniform shirts and khaki shorts. I'd teach people how to pet a shark (with two fingers and not after munching on fries at the food court); I'd wrangle Macaws that jumped off their perches in the Amazon exhibit; and I'd explain that the white alligator was leucistic, not albino (you can tell because there eyes are normal color and not red) in the Swamp exhibit. 

Today I still feel that same sort of nerdy pride when visiting the aquarium, especially since they lost nearly all their stock when Hurricane Katrina knocked out the power and staff had to leave. They have since recovered wonderfully and added the Parakeet Pointe, a little cray if you have a fear of birds and noise. 

Check the schedule for feedings and special happenings before going so you can maximize your visit. This is an amazing place to go during the dead heat of the summer since most the exhibits, besides the Amazon, are kept at a pretty cool temperature. 

Once I get dive-certified and a few dives under my weight belt, I want to apply to dive in their entry tunnel tank to amuse guests!

I appreciate Frank responding so quickly and coming out to fix my oven, good to know there are still reliable people who know their stuff! I would use again if I had a problem with my appliances, better than calling the manufacturer for sure. My problem was the igniter went, all fixed in about 30 minutes. One less problem to worry about.
A little expensive, I thought, but what isn't anymore.
The aquarium was very beautiful. If you're not driving, I recommend taking the bus instead of the trolley. It's much quicker and easier to catch.

Coming to Hyppo is always a good time, employees are always kind and the atmosphere is great. An extremely diverse amount of flavors means you can always try something new! Definitely a jewel in Downtown St. Pete.

I love their chicken...I try to eat here once or twice a month this is the new hangout for me and my friends also try the tea, it's so good you might want to smack your momma. The chicken isn't to greasy or too hot...just the way I like it.

Definitely the odd one out here with 3 stars review but after reading the reviews on yelp we decided to visit Hyypo. 

We tried pineapple mango and sea salt chocolate (I'm a big fan of all these flavors in general) but it felt a bit disappointing. Popsicles are so easy to fall in love with generally. Pineapple- mango stood out among the flavours but both of them were a bit bland. 

Hopefully other flavours are much better.

For an aquarium, I have seen better. Since the Audobon Zoo is so amazing, I would expect nothing less from the aquarium, but it is simply subpar. That being said, my daughter enjoyed it. 

They do offer some nice and well thought out exhibits, but it is mostly aimed towards children and since it cost over $50 for a family of three to enter, I would expect more. They didn't have any fish or sea creatures that I haven't seen before and some that I would want to see were not there. The penguin exhibit was the most impressive, and that was because the penguins were super responsive to visitors. 

If you are in NOLA, I guess it is worth the visit, but expectations should not be set too high.

It was a beautiful day to go out so my family and I stopped by Peddler's Village in Bucks County. This is a good place to spend time with loved ones - you can shop , window shop, try food and even come across really interesting festivals/ events. I saw this winery on the map at Peddler's and wanted to see what it was about. 

The place is divided into two big rooms- one room has 8$ wine tasting where you are given a card and have the option of trying 7 different types of wine. I think the other room might have more selections but it costs more. I really liked the service because they walk you through the wines and explain everything to the detail. I felt very informed and it opened up my eyes to what type of wine I like the most. Because of their hospitality and great process I bought 2 wines home which tasted very delicious. 

I would definitely recommend this place if you're looking for good wine that's priced decently and if you just want to go wine tasting :)

Chadds Ford Winery was the first stop on our wine trail tour in Bucks County located in Peddlers Village in New Hope, PA. We already had the pleasure of having several glasses of their wines at a function the previous night and we're excited to try additional samples.

The location is beautiful, a small village of old world shops and eateries. The interior was spacious, rustic and had a nice size bar like area for tastings. We got to choose eight wines from dry reds and whites to sweets. All were lovely but the Sunset Blush with hints of peach and grapefruit was a true standout. 

Our host Danielle was awesome. She explained each wine exactly as it was when we tasted it. Bonus points for being able to sit down.
The chicken here is ok, the dry rub is so thick it's like a freaking cake of spice, I felt like I was eating straight dry rub spices half the time and couldn't find the chicken.
Was disappointed to find out the gyro meat comes from a box and the grape leaves are canned for 15$$. It tastes alright but I can't wrap my head around how it's supposed to be "homemade".

I love hot chicken and 400 Degrees serves up the best hot chicken available. I carry an undying love for Mr. Boo's that 400 Degrees can't replace, but Mr. Boo's is sadly long gone.

The hot chicken at 400 Degrees is caked in spice, and is always crispy and decidedly delicious. Good hot chicken starts with good fried chicken, and here 400 Degrees has Prince's clearly beat, specifically on the quality of the meat. The staff is great, especially compared to Prince's.

Call ahead, order a 400 Degree dark quarter, sweat, be happy.

Omgoodness if there's a hyppo In NY, would literally be broke and fat. That's how freaking good this place is!! There's over 500 different flavors (not all at the store), who thinks of that many different combinations!?!  Mango habanero (first one I tried, and I was hooked after that), avocado cream, pistachio coconut, pistachio rose water, kale apple... you get the idea. It's naturally delicious and made from fruit juices. And the BEST part is you can dip any popsicle in melted chocolate! How AMAZING is that. 

Oh and there's these point cards where you buy six and get one free.. my friend and I filled it up the same day. We couldn't stop. $3.75 a pop is so worth it!

I got the brisket platter and it was excellent. Also got the goat cheese Mac which was a winner as well. The real MVP is the brisket quesadilla with the chipotle sauce.... sooooooo good. Very nice owners and they gave us great service.  No bar but you can grab a drink next door or byob. Either way still five stars when it comes to the food and service if ya ask me.
Really nice selection of dresses and women's clothing.  Their having a great sale right now with up to 70% off.  The ladies working here were all friendly and very helpful.

fun museum, love the seal, the stingray petting and the jellyfish and seahorse exhibit. I wish the walk through tunnel was longer though. I wanted to walk More however i did learn a lot and it made it totally worth it with coupons.

Tip: you can walk to the imax entrance to pay for the  entrance fee if line gets too long. There is also a smaller gift shop there and an albino sea turtle.

Very awesome, check it out

My boyfriend and I stopped in the Chaddsford Winery a couple of days ago on our way to Longwood Gardens. We had looked this place up and thought it would be something fun to do while we were in the area. We also needed a bottle of wine to bring to the sushi restaurant in the area after our Longwood trip. The grounds are beautiful and the actual winery is in an old barn-style building with a lot of charm. When we arrived inside, we immediately looked around for some wine to buy. We chose the sangria and the apple wine. We then decided to do a tasting since we were curious about the wines that we purchased. Bowtie Matt was our wine expert and he was very informative and full of entertaining stories. I enjoyed the sweeter wines, especially the blush and the sangria. My boyfriend loved all of the reds. You get to keep the glasses that you use which is a nice touch, especially since the tasting is $10 each (not too bad of a price). We recommend it to everyone will definitely be back soon!

So typically me and my mother come here and it is absolutely delicious. One of the best bbq places around us. We've been craving their Mac and cheese lately so I went out and picked up some pork sandwiches and Mac and cheese. The sandwiches were absolutely delicious. But the Mac and cheese did not taste the same at all. It was fairly spicy and had long stringy onions in it which I hadn't noticed before. So my mother called the store and asked if they changed the recipe lately because it was extremely spicy and although the manager did offer to allow us to come back and switch the side for something we did like, I personally didn't feel like taking the drive back to Saucy's. She told us that the Mac and cheese is supposed to taste like that and I'm 98% sure the Mac and cheese is NOT supposed to be spicy. We were not satisfied.

LOVED the penguin experience!! Such a treat! And we were the only two for that session so it was like a private experience!

We met with Darwin and he explained everything you want to know about penguins and their exhibit. Then you go to their kitchen and get some fish for later. Then you get to go into a room for the penguin meet and greet! You can hold them, hug them, everything! It was so special to be able to do this because I know some other programs would let you be near the penguin but not touch them. But here, you can pick them up and touch them as much as you want!

Careful if they are feisty though. We had a young penguin named Sassy and we got scratched a bit, but that's ok. Hubig was much friendlier and both posed for our pictures. They also paint for you using their feet -- very cute.

Then they waddle through the hallway to lead you to the exhibit where you go in and feed the fish you got earlier to the penguins in the exhibit! Really an incredible experience.

The rest of the aquarium is ok. There's the sea otters., stingray touch tank, and rain forest environment. I also loved the parakeets. Make sure you get the feed stick so the birds will land on you and you can hand-feed them!

Yes, I love petting animals!!!!

Meh... Place is small for the $30 entrance fee.  We went in there late in the day we were worried that we went in late because we only had an hour 
 But... It takes a lot less than an hour to walk thru, if you skip the enormous gift shop that is... If you skip the gift shop it's a twenty minute walk thru.  If you have very small children of course it will take you longer but for two adults it just not worth it. 

The best part was the shark tank, and maybe because it was late in the day but I sort of felt that the glass was a little merky and hard to see thru. We also saw some very cute penguins.  That for sure was another highlight. 

The best thing is that the ticket includes a movie at the large 3d theater next door and that part was really cool. We saw the great white shark movie... Excellent!!!

Small aquarium. Has an albino alligator. 

There were a lot of large empty spaces due to the loss of marine animals during Katrina. It seems like the aquarium is trying to get back on track. They're in the process of installing a new seahorse exhibit. Price for one adult is $17. 
Also has combo tickets for the zoo but "the zoo is 7.5 miles away and you have to provide your own mode of transportation".

Love this shop! Prices are great and the staff is super friendly. I purchased some Equadorian roses for my mom which were absolutely beautiful. They lasted close to two weeks and were enormous when they bloomed. You can't beat the quality and price. Thank you Flowerama for keeping it affordable. I will be back!
What a deal, rose's for $12.99 a dozen. Short of the Soulard market where you can get a dozen real cheap, this place is a nice shop to get a dozen for that someone special.

God Save The Queen!

Nashville has had a Prince of hot chicken for quite a while but now it is time to respect the new royalty of hot. Aqui Simpson of 400 is cooking up perfectly cooked, tender, juicy chicken bathed in magical spiced that will amaze as well as burn. 

I started with the pleasant burn of the 200, and each bite was better than the last. Its safe to say I'm hooked. Next visit I'll take the jump to the 400 to get the full fix.

I've sampled quite a few of what Nashville has to offer in the way of blazing birds and she is with out a doubt the Queen.
I absolutely love the aquarium. My two year old has a blast every time we go. The staff is always friendly and helpful. The bathrooms are clean, even though they are usually very busy.

This is one of the premier aquariums in the country. It is located right next to scenic Mississippi River. Young and old alike will enjoy all that this place has to offer. You get sharks, penguins, alligators, and even some hands-on activities for the kids. 

Tip: you can have a snack here, but save your meal for some real New Orleans food that can be found in any direction outside of the aquarium.
Great appliance advice and so helpful! Saved me a ton of money by helping me out and giving me ideas over the phone. Definitely will use again :)

In St. Petersburg's hippest neighborhood, with a youthful, vibrant staff that really believe in what they're selling. They have about 100 flavors of the most amazing flavorful frozen Popsicles. A little expensive at 3.75 each but worth every penny

Peach bourbon & strawberry datil winners.
All juice & cane sugar. Datil is a hot pepper family. My first introduction- taste like cross btw chili/ habanero heat. 
Glad we stopped by to take a pic of the wall mural across the street. 
Flavors written on chalk board
They sell drinks as well. Good no frills setup.

The food is great, the owners are very nice and make an overall pleasant experience, the first time that I ate at the restaurant in the St. Roch market. Not so much for our return visit a few days later. Upon arrival, nary a soul was present at the booth, so we wondered to the attendants at the adjacent booth if the cookery was open for the day. The very attentive employee next door informed us that they were open for business, just that the sole person present was in the back reacquisitioning some necessary items. This was 5 minutes past 1, right in the middle of a lunch rush Tuesday, May 15.  Five minutes later, as we are sitting at nearby table awaiting our much anticipated meal, the employee returns, chomping gum noticeably from 20 feet away with a small serving bowl atote, clearly not anything substantial enough to leave an entire food booth unattended mid lunch rush. Next, we notice her donning sanitary gloves whilst manuevering her smart phone. Maybe the phone has been sanitized, maybe it was an extremely important call which could not wait...(sarcasm). At this point, it is clear that the initial experience that we had enjoyed at this foodery was not available at the current moment. Needless to say, we rerouted ourselves to one of the other 10 or so options serving the same food within a 2 mile radius. I understand that finding qualified and competent individuals to maintain the heart and soul of the intention of the passionate owner of a restaurant can be difficult, even moreso in a town with a pool of uneducated, lackadaisical people whose sole purpose for showing up at work is the paycheck. On the other hand, who you choose to represent your business reflects directly on the people in charge. Maybe we will retry and visit again next time we have a hankering, maybe not (Mona's fixed our craving), but if we do, it will be expecting much less, and with an expectation of being turned away before we even enter, ready to support another business.  This all makes me sad, because our first visit was fantastic! The food was great, the service was great!! It seemed like the owner was present..or at least someone who is capable of representing the goals the owner has set forth in their venture.
Soo many flavors and everything I've tried has been delicious! Can't wait to come back and try more!

I went here to indulge my inner (and outer) geek several years ago-- pre-Katrina. I don't know what it's like now, but once upon a time, this was a wonderful, awe-inspiring place.

This place humbles you.

There were sections of this aquarium where I was completely surrounded-- or practically engulfed-- by humongous tanks filled with amazing, gargantuan aquatic beasts, and I couldn't help but realize how tiny and insignificant I was as a human being.. in many ways. 

At this aquarium, you're offered a small peak into marine life.. and while only being the tip of the iceberg, the view is spectacular. As a child, I remembered reading stories about how huge manta rays could get, and I never could quite fathom what exactly was meant by the term "huge" until I saw one here that looked the size of a winnebago.

If this place hasn't changed much... or, rather, if this place has managed to evolve, grow, and become more amazing than it already was... then go! Go! GO! And if you have children, bring them there! It's a wonderful experience and opportunity that nobody in the area should ever pass up.

3.75 grapes. But in my opinion there is some good Pa wine to be found here. The winery knows it too, and it is priced accordingly. I come here once a year during Lahaska restaurant week. If you have a reservation at one of the restaurants( Caleb's or Barley sheaf should be your choice) your tasting is free. This is a sampling of their dry wines, some of which are in the $25 range. When you finish you can also sample some of their sweeter styles. On both visits the customer service has been very good, especially the most recent one. They also give you a great discount during R week, I've wondered if that is available anytime? Hard cider is a newer offering and it is nice and dry, I picture it going perfectly with pork. I usually buy the proprietors blends, they are in the $15 range, and with the discount even less. Come on people, we really need to support local wineries! Unless you'd rather see more condos, strip malls, and dollar stores.

Ordered ribs, coleslaw, and goat mac and cheese on Uber eats. They ran out of goat cheese mac, but they wrote a note apologizing and gave a bunch of other sides to make up for it. Everything was AMAZING. Especially the ribs--they were incredible. I can't wait to eat here again!
Ran in on New Year's Day. The service was great and the pops were delicious. The perfect treat for a warm afternoon.

Decided to stop here on a Saturday afternoon while shopping in Peddler's Village. We opted for the $8 tasting - you get to choose seven wines out of a list (list also breaks it down into categories so you can pick the kind of wine you like). The server that handled the tasting was attentive and asked us questions to learn what we liked. We definitely tried more then seven samples. Best part is afterwards you can purchase the wine - and they offer discounts if you purchase three or more bottles. Happy we stopped here!
The Gulf of Mexico exhibit is the coolest!  Get the pass to all the Audubon attractions...totally worth the extra money!

Always is nostalgic visiting here. Reminds me of my childhood, so anytime that I'm in the area, I try to visit. On the day we went there were some busted pipes and unusually cold weather so the theater was closed. We got a discount so we decided to go in anyway. There is lots to do and look at. I paid extra for the stingray feeding. My kids loved it. I didn't buy the ridiculously overpriced photos ($32 for one photo), though. I'll keep coming back.

My husband and I were in Peddler's Village for a wedding and on our way out when we noticed the Chaddsford Tasting Room. Quite some time ago when we still lived in Pennsylvania we had visited the actual winery, so we were pretty excited to see the tasting room and popped in for a quick tasting before heading out. 

We were quickly greeted by a staff member who kindly let us know what options were available, we were surprised to find quite a few. You can do a tasting, flights, or of course glasses or bottles. We opted for the tasting - 7 wines for $8.00. Our pourer was very friendly and knowledgeable and had actually worked under a local Virginia winemaker close to where we live now. We chose the dry tasting since we don't often drink sweet wines. She guided us through the wines and we chatted about what wines from 2018 may look like. It was just a quick in and out visit but it left a great impression again. 

We were quite happy to see that the winery that kicked off our wine journey was still doing well!

We were here for the Scales and Ales Annual event. 
This event was Awesome!! We arrived around 8pm. They had a nearby parking garage which they offered a huge discount. It went from $15.00 to $5.00 with a validated discount. 
They had all types of  food samples and drinks.
I was intrigued with what they called there version of  a Sangria. They gave it a shot of bourbon. Sounds crazy right. I actually liked it.
This ticket was $75.00. For general admission. 
I definitely think it was worth it with everything that was offered. They had DJs all over the place. They had a live band outdoors. We also had access to the inside of the aquarium. 
We saw all the fish and stingrays and then some. This event was for a very good cause. 
I am so glad that we were able to contribute to such a good cause and enjoy ourselves at the same time. My husband agreed that it was a very enjoyable event. I would not hesitate to attend this event again if we were in the New Orleans area.
Awesome concept, a huge variety of flavors, but as a first-timer, I wish the staff had told me about the chocolate dip!
3.5 stars.  Carolina-style BBQ with vinegar always makes me happy, but the food just didn't have any real oomph for me.  It was ok.

This place is located inside the St Roche market. Amazing food and amazing service. We got a free baklava on the house so that just made it extra special. Kudos to the chef. The food is fresh and healthy

So I walked by the other day and saw they had a Gouda burger, had to come the next day to try it and I wasn't disappointed. When it comes to a burger the bun is key and this one was perfect.  And the burger gouda combo was on point. My girlfriend ordered the brisket quesadilla, and as good as the burger was I was jealous as soon as she gave me a bite.  This is one of those places where I plan to try most things on the menu.  Best BBQ in nola I've had so far for sure.

Traditional Wine Tasting - 7 half ounce glasses for $10!

There were 12 options for you to choose from with a variety of white and red wine, some dry and some fruity. This was my very FIRST wine tasting experience and it was WONDERFUL! I would not consider myself as a wine person, but I think that is because I did not find MY kind of wine. 

The staff was very informative and patient when it came to recommendations. She was able to cater to my preferences very well. My personal favorite has to be the Sunset Blush!
no question about it... hands down best tool store in reno! great people, great products!

Visited the Audubon Aquarium of the America's on a Friday afternoon and ended up spending about two hours exploring the exhibits. 

There were quite a few exhibits and they were really well organized, I especially liked the Mississippi River exhibit which highlighted local wildlife, and was very informative.

While some of the exhibits were decent sized, there were quite a few that seemed small for the number of animals. This tends to be my problem with most aquariums, and I would have loved to see more information from the aquarium on where the animals came from (breeding programs, rescues, from the wild, etc.). And it'd be nice to see where the money goes or what kind of programs the aquarium has for protecting wildlife.

There was also quite a bit of construction on the exhibits.

The parakeet aviary was actually pretty neat. It was a large outdoor space with dozens of friendly little parakeets who aren't at all afraid of humans (at one point there were five parakeets on me).

This is nicer than many aquariums I've seen, just a few more things I would have liked to have seen, like larger habitats for the animals and more information around conservation efforts.

About 100 dollars for 3 adults and one child. What can I say? It was a waste of money. It was small, didn't have many exhibits, hundreds of unsupervised children running around (on some sort of field trips)... Will we go again ? No. This is definitely a one time experience. We were there an hour because my child stared at the sharks for 20 minutes. If she didn't like them so much, this would have been over in 40 minutes.

Was recommended to visit the Aquarium by a friend, and we got a coupon online for half off the admission price, which I'm glad I did because I don't feel like it was worth the full price. Overall, the aquarium was fun, the parakeet exhibit was cool, the penguin feeding, along with petting the stingrays. However, a part of it was under construction, and it was kind of small. So I felt it lacked something. You can complete the entire exhibit in 2.5 hours.

Wow!! So impressed with this hidden gem. Have had our knives for 15 yrs and they were in desperate need of sharpening. 
They are so reasonable and quick.

I had one bad experience in there other than that I do love the store. They have a great selection and every one else that works there is very nice. Chad handled everything on my end very well and was really nice about a negative review. I recommend the store to everyone that likes tools.

Love theses pops.  Unfortunate that they are far from me, otherwise I would probably be there everyday.  A bit disappointed that after driving 40 minutes they didn't  have any of my usual favorites in stock.  I didn't want it to be a wasted trip so I bought new flavors and as usual they were amazing.  But I'm a creature of habit and still missed the ones I normally get.

I have no doubt they have terrific food... But.. The service is POOR.  being told there is a 40 minute wait for 4 chicken wings or strips is super WEAK.  HIRE a couple of people, pick up the pace.  Disappointing.

There were at least 20 kinds of amazing flavored Popsicles here probably more like 30 or 40! Raspberry lemonade exceeded my expectations by a lot, and that is saying something. I wouldn't hesitate to take anyone here, heck, everyone. Let's go! It can be a snack, treat, dessert. There are vegan choices as well

As a family we spent a very wet afternoon here and it was fantastic. And what a stting just outside the French Quarter of this fantistic city right on the banks of the Mississippi river.


 Never realising about all the different types of fish and sealife. It was a really educational trip for all of the family, and if I ever get chance to go back to New Orleans it is somewhere that I will difinatley visit again.

Of all the Audubon attractions, the aquarium is by far my favs.  Partly because it manages to instantly transport you to another world, an underwater magicland full of wonder and excitement.  Also, the Aquarium does a fantastic job of continually updating their exhibits, always bringing in something new and awe-inspiring.  Case in point: the new Mayan exhibit.  We recently traveled to that part of the world and I was surprised by how Audubon managed to capture the culture and spirit of the Mayan people while utilizing the existing space that they already had set up.  The Aquarium recently celebrated its 25th anniversary but I am more impressed by the progress they have made in the 10 years since Katrina.  When I was in school, I would come in here during a quiet weekday just to study and found I wasn't the only adult seeking a change of scenery there.  The little kid in me wants to give it 10 stars, just for the way it makes me feel inside.  Then the adult in me remembers that the $25/person entrance fee can be very expensive for those who don't hold a membership and this place can get crazy crowded during tourist seasons, especially if the weather is less than ideal.  Also, the food court offers a very limited, unimaginative and highly overpriced selection.  So plan your trip accordingly and enjoy the day.
Walking by so we stopped in to try their food. Nice atmosphere and good service. Ordered a Rib plate to share with my sis, everything was tasty! Thanks Saucy's, I'll be back
This is a great place to eat, enjoy your time with friends and family!! Torshi is amazing, tasty and affordabl!

Love this place, they've always got a nice spread of flavors. You can get turned around just looking at all the popsicles, but they're not too expensive to stop you from grabbing two in one stop! You can also get them chocolate dipped for a dollar more and that just doubles the flavors possible. I'd really recommend this place and if you can't make it out to the St. Pete location give the Ybor or Hyde Park ones a try. You won't be disappointed and I'd give a Datil flavor too nice heat to go with your sweet. I also like that they have stamp cards cause they are easy to fill up and get a free pop.

When our washer stopped draining, I called Frank to come and take a look. He came the same day, took a look at it, found the issue and fixed it within an hour. He's a super friendly person and I enjoyed chatting with him while he was diagnosing the issue.
If you have any trouble with any appliance or computer issues, Frank will for sure be able to help you. Thank you, Frank!

Under new ownership. My husband stopped in to use the gift card I had received as a replacement for the above to review order. He was told it was no longer good since they were not the original owners and they don't have to except that gift card.

Delightfully painful chicken is here in Peabody Corner food court. Dare to test your limits and go the full monty. Just ask the cook for the maximum "400 degree" spiced heat which I promise will make you cry. If you're a wild one, but not that crazy, try the 300 degree. Initiates might be wise to start with the medium 200 degree choice. Sissy boys and girls can get the mild, and say they've been here and sampled the heat. Most choose breasts or the hot legs, but wings and fiery pork are also available. Pepperfire tastes better but this spot has nice spacious inside seating and wifi.
I really love the juices here. The green one especially is so refreshing and delicious, clearly made with fresh ingredients. Xoxoxo

Such an adorable store. They have great places to sit and helpful employees, but the only problem is the excessive use of plastic cups. As an environmentalist, it pains me to walk into such an amazing store and see trash cans filled with plastic cups. Great place and good wine, but I really wish they cared more about the environment.
Had very nice time at the aquarium. My favriot exhibit was parakeet point I like birds but any I like feeding the birds. The aquarium is beautiful.

I may be spoiled living in Baltimore, because I was pretty let down! We only did the Aquarium ticket, so we could have missed something, but I just felt like when we got done, there had to be something we missed, but we looked at the map again, and that was not the case! Didnt seem like there was a lot of information or identification of all the displays. 

I assume its good for kids, because they were EVERYWHERE!!!!!

It was just OK for me. I did enjoy seeing the large fish in the tanks, but the 3 birds that were there hard to see. The reptile section was open but closed because I don't know where the animals were. 

And not to mention, the lion looked over the whole thing. Unfortunately I only took video and not pictures to be able to show. 

I do believe kids will enjoy just seeing the animals, the kids there were full of energy, but for adults it might lack that excitement.

I love this place. The only reason I wouldn't give it five stars for my last visit was because they were out of coconut coconut which is my favorite flavor. The Popsicles are kind of expensive too. But I don't mind paying almost $4 for a delicious pop. Word of advice, eat the Popsicle inside. They melt extremely fast and mind ended up all over me when I was walking down the street in the 90 degree heat!

My friend and I got lunch from here on Sunday. It was excellent.

I was at first drawn in by the Egyptian cat statue on the counter. It was really cool. Then the friendly man at the counter, who we figured was the owner, gave us samples of his teas and juices. We looked over the menu as we tried his samples. (They were tasty. My favorite was the Lebanese Tea.)

We decided to split the Grape Leaves platter. It came with warm Pita Bread, Hummus and a choice of salad or rice. We chose the salad. It was all delicious. I am particular about Grape Leaves, and in general, I do not like most of them. These were warm and flavorful. The Hummus was outstanding. The platter portion was large and we were stuffed.

Next time we hope to try the Baklava.

Overall we had a good time. My wife and son especially loved the hands-on experience with the parakeets. Very well done and aesthetically pleasing displays. However, the staff definitely needs some training. I was with my 6 year old in the bathroom when two employees walked in. Their conversation was very colorful and full of expletives! VERY INAPPROPRIATE!!!!

I was really excited for this aquarium but it was disappointing.  There were a couple of nice exhibits that save it from a 2 star review, but it was certainly a bummer.

We arrived at the Aquarium around 3 on a Sunday.  The price to get in is no joke, we had a child, a senior, and an adult and it was around $80 to get in.  This Aquarium is small to begin with and several exhibits were empty, so that just meant we got through it even quicker.  

They have some nice eels and an albino alligator.  My son got to pet a Madagascar hissing cockroach which was great.  Not able to hold it unfortunately but that was cool.

The best exhibit was the penguins, but it was small and not well designed.  Most of the penguins congregated at the top of the exhibit, which was sort of walled off.  So, that meant if they were in certain parts of the enclosure you could not see them at all.

There was a food court which was convenient, although we did not partake.  There is the requisite gift shop as well, so if you have children let the bargaining begin.  I found the prices at the gift shop to be commensurate with other aquariums in large towns.  Definitely not cheap but not out of control or anything.

Overall, our time in the Aquarium was a little underwhelming.  I do not regret going, but I would not seek it out again.

This is a great place to visit, if you have an extra hour or two when visiting the Crescent City. If for no other reason, than to visit the Louisiana Swamp Exhibit. There you will find the famous Leucitic Alligator - white, but with blue eyes. A rare form of albinism. Also , a red tailed hawk and a barred owl. (I know, not fish, but still cool!)
There are sea dragons, seahorses, giant turtles and sea bass, to mention a few of the many exhibits. 
It is located at the end of Canal Street, right on the banks of the mighty Mississippi River.

The admission prices for a bit too high for my liking but it was so overcrowded with field trips we did not enjoy ourselves at all. It was so loud I could barely hear my children and we went through all the exhibits kind of fast to try to beat the large crowds but they were always right behind us because there were so many of them. So instead of getting to look at everything and talk about it we only stayed for a minute and moved on. The other issue we had was with the food. We had no idea there were other food options until we sat down at Papa John's and saw other people with different food once we ordered so we were stuck with their food. It would have been nice if there was a sign somewhere letting us know about the other place around the corner. It was also so loud we could barely hear each other. The gift shop was nice though. All and all when we left instead of being excited about all the things we saw we just felt like "meh" and went back home.

Website shows they are open til 7.  We walked in at 6:25 to be told they were closed.  I asked if they weren't open til 7.  The owner, in a condescending manner, said they were closed...almost implying I couldn't tell time.  We are big hot chicken fans and will eat at the many other (and better) places around town.  400' obviously has too much business as they are closing 35 minutes early and turning cash away.

Had a leaky ice maker hose and based on reviews called Frank. He came out and discussed the problem, we then moved the refrigerator (which wasn't an easy task), and Frank began his task. He is a magician. He tackled the work and in 20 minutes, he was finished and no more leaks! He is very good at his profession and will be my "go to guy" for any and all repairs! Loved his sense of humor by the way(ha-ha)... Thanks Frank for coming out and making my frig better.. He is a good guy to have in your repair arsenal...

First time visitor. I picked cucumber, lemon and mint; hubby picked pistachio with rose water. Mine is so freshing and flavorful; his is creamy and tasty.

And as many mentioned, the price is very fair. 

We are already planning to take our son to visit the place again. And we are planning to try different flavors. Maybe even just buy a bunch and put in the freezer since we are not in walking distance to the place.

Have to mention the young lady who is behind the counter is very nice and helpful. Highly recommend and will come back again and again,.

I've been here several times over the years and this place never fails to disappoint.  Most recently I tagged along on my son's school field trip. We didn't spend enough time before going to see the IMAX movie but we still had fun.  I always look forward to coming here.

UPDATE: 

During the week, and during lunch, it is essential to call the order in and then dine in or take out. I showed up on a Monday thinking I could just order and eat in. I was sorely disappointed. It seems the popularity has grown and they informed me it would be at least an hour. :( Sadly, I walked away, tail between my legs. :( 

So if you want this hot chicken, it is advised to call the order in first! I guess during my initial visit it was a fluke because it was mid afternoon and no one was around. Still 5 stars!
Excellent gourmet frozen treats!  Excellent selection and great on a warm Florida day!

I have been to a few Hyppo locations and always find them to be a delicious treat. They have a rotating assortment of pops so each time you visit there is a good chance that they will have something new for you to try.

Today I got a buckeye flavored one. It started with chocolate, then peanut butter and it ended with a layer of toasted coconut. I normally avoid all three of those but I love buckeyes so I had to give it a try and I was not disappointed! 

Just a heads up, if you plan on visiting this location, parking can be spotty and you will most likely have to pay for meter parking. Also, it's off of central so parking is just plain awkward.

Prolly din't have to see this attraction and could have skipped out on this one but still decided to check em out while I Was in town. They had many exhibits and all the animals were great. My top was prolly the sea horses and their habitats. They blend right in with the kelp! 

I must have went in at the wrong day as there were many gradeschool kids here running around and playing on their field trip here. but still got to see everything just took a bit longer than anticipated. Still something to see when your a first timer in the area.

Favorite aquarium I have ever visited. Love the up close and personal parakeet exhibit, penguins, and stingray pool.  Has a play area that small kids enjoy, too. Overall it takes about an hour and a half to fully enjoy.

Hands down the best non-dairy option for dessert in The Burg, and also there is still an option to dip any of the pops in chocolate for those that love that part of dessert. I'm a plain Jane so I always get a straight up strawberry and/or Champagne mango. BTW Champagne mango is just plain mango, there's no alcohol in it. Hella good! My boyfriends favorite is the cranberry apple. Honestly, this place never disappoints! Check it out :)

This is such an amazing shop for many reasons. 1) there popsicles are made with real fruits, tea leaves and vegetables. If you tell me (before I had tried the pops) that I was going to love a cucumber popsicle I would have looked at you like you were weird for thinking vegetables should be mixed with desert...but lo and behold I devoured that cucumber popsicle in minutes. These are definitely not your average Walmart popsicles. The word gourmet here is right on point! Everything tastes good so why not explore your senses with not average flavors like tea leaf green pop or black honey pop? The stuff your eating is also not junk food material. The ingredients are genuinely made out of mashed fruits and vegetables or tea leaves!

WE GOT TO PET A STINGRAY! And we saw a whole tunnel full of fish. I am in my happy place now! Well, this aquarium mostly reminds me of my hometown aquarium here in Denver. Though we didn't take advantage of the discounted offers on their website, we sure got the perks of getting $2 off for our little 3 year old trooper who was with us at the time. The Aquarium is very beautiful-- it's like being a mermaid and exploring the underground enchantment... Only without the Mermaid Tail. And the gills. Lol. This aquarium is small spaced and very hard to maneuver sometimes, but it's because it's targeted to children mostly. I went into small tunnels, hallways, paths.. full of the very amazing sea creatures!!!! The jellyfish were very intimidating because I thought I was gonna die from getting a shock through the display window. But that wasn't the case. My anxiety just thought it was hilarious to play mind games on me. 

The parking was not free when we got there. Very difficult and takes time to plan ahead for sure. Mostly the standard street parking, paid parking or bus?? Either way, I fell in love and think that every child should experience this wonderful aquarium sometimes in their life. Cheers from Denver.

4.5 stars because The Hyppo is not as good as Pop Craft Pops.

Yippie, finally got myself a Hyppo popsicle! So many flavors, which should I get? After studying the board for a while, I narrowed down to 2 flavors: Avocado Cream or Blood Orange Cream. Still facing with a decision I decided to ask the employee which he would get. He says he likes the Blood Orange, so Blood Orange it is. The cost for the popsicle is $3.75, tax included. For reference, these are smaller than Pop Craft Pops but also $0.75 cheaper.

If you like blood oranges, you've gotta get this. The taste of blood orange is very strong, unfortunately, the cream isn't. I like my popsicles creamier. Despite this, the popsicle is very tasty and refreshing.

The space is rather spacious for a popsicle spot. There lots of seating inside to hide from the Florida heat. I love the painted walls and how clean it is.

Definitely looking forward to trying other flavors.

What a gem this place is! I had the pulled pork (delicious) with mac & cheese, BBQ beans, and muffin (all also delicious), and my husband had the brisket, which he swears is the BEST he has ever had--EVER. (But note that the brisket portion is small, so he recommends getting the 2-meat combo and doubling up.) 

I spend a lot of time in New Orleans, and this place will be my new go-to for quick, inexpensive, and delicious food.

I try to support black business. But I was totally disrespected by the owner. I arrived at 6:29 and was told by the owner that they are closed and no longer serving food. She went on to tell me that it takes 25 min to cook the chicken, and she is trying to walk out at 7.  Well lady it isn't that hard to change your hours to 6:30. The disrespect came when my wife came in the place after I left and she was talking about another person like I was in the wrong. I am glad I didn't spend a dime. Go at your own risk.

I received these flowers today for my birthday from my kids in Florida. This has to be one of the most beautiful arrangements I have ever received. The flowers are so fresh and healthy and done so tastefully!! I worked in a florist for ma...ny years, several years ago, with a family owned company that took pride in what they sent out the door. This Flowerama location is the same way! Such a refreshing change to flowers in a box that never bloom!! Thank you for making my birthday so BRIGHT and BEAUTIFUL!!

I had seen this place a few times when I was out and about in downtown, but it wasn't open (I was out late). So when I was nearby in the afternoon I decided to give it a shot. I'm glad I did. 

The flavor selection was amazing, and you could tell the ingredients were fresh and not just some powder thrown into a mix. The store itself was clean and inviting, and the guy behind the register was helpful. Looking forward to coming back more, especially when it warms up a bit.

We were finishing our dinner at a nearby restaurant, and when we were considering whether to get dessert there, the waitress leaned in and whispered, go to Hyppo.  We looked at her in surprise.  Yes, they have the best ice pops, she said. Before they opened a store in St Pete, she and her boyfriend used to drive all the way to St Augustine with an ice chest to get the ice pops there. 

With such glowing endorsement, of course we have to give it a try.  And boy, it really is good.  I love that most of the flavors taste so natural and so rich in fruit, it's like biting into the fruit itself.  I also love that it doesn't fill me up like a rich ice cream may, so it makes for a perfect ending to a meal, a little something sweet and cold.

We ended up going there every single day we were up in the area, that's how good it is.  I look forward to continuing exploring there many flavors.  So far, my favorite ones are: cantaloupe mint and pear reisling.  I tried the datil plum, and it was so spicy my lips feel kind of swollen! Still love it though.

Window shopping on Central Avenue today and this place caught my eye. What could be better than a popsicle on a sundrenched Florida afternoon!

There's a big board with many MANY flavors to choose from, many unusual and exotic combinations. Everything is made there with all natural ingredients. The popsicles are frozen very hard, so you have to really bite down.

We tried straight up strawberry, strawberry sangria and espresso. 

The strawberry was tart/sweet and textured with bits of strawberry.  Excellent!  The strawberry sangria was similar, but with a little extra twist from a faint taste of sangria, also less sweet.  I didn't get a taste of the espresso because it was so good, our friend didn't want to share!

The pops are $3.75, not cheap. Quality is great, taste is outstanding and you can't beat the sensation of a popsicle on a warm and sunny afternoon.  Yes, mom, we had our ice cream BEFORE dinner.

This is the best aquarium I've ever been to! I've been to a few and this tops Boston's aquarium which is apparently supposed to be the best??? The parakeet house was my favorite part because they land on you and they're beautiful!! I also loved touching the sting rays and seeing the pregnant male sea horses! We also got to see a free 25 minute 3D movie after which was amazing and eye opening

There is a place down the street where the guy actually makes all the frozens in the shop! But this place isn't bad. Their pops are shipped in from somewhere not made in house. But everything made with natural stuff. Nothing goes wrong with that

I really want to say that I loved the aquarium! 


First, I'll say what I liked. They had really cool exhibits! There were tons of different varieties of fish and animals. It is really cool because there are not just fish, there are other species of animals. I feel like some aquariums are just fish, but here, they had many different things to see. 

Okay, now down to why it's only two stars. The main reason is because we saw some dead fish. I understand that this can not be avoided in some circumstances, and I'm not sure what they should do in these situations, but I just know that most people there do not want to see dead fish floating around. In the first tank you see when you enter the aquarium, there are a ton of fish swimming around in what looks to be like a small aquarium. There were two fish napping on the floor of the tank. I say napping because that is what the security guard told the kids who were near me. I swear he told them the fish were napping. It was awkward because the parents were like "oh" and shuffled their kids along. 

There was also a dead fish in the tunnel thing, that was kinda floating around upside down. I saw this when the scuba divers were in the tank, cleaning it. The other fish in the tank kept swimming by the fish and checking him out... Maybe they just wanted to make sure he got a proper burial. The scuba diver saw the fish, wiggled him around to make sure he was dead, and then swam up to the top of the tank to dispose of the fish, or reuse him for food to the sharks, probably the latter. He then "talked" to the other scuba diver with hand signals, in which she said "what happened" and he said "the fish was napping." Yes, I swear he used the international napping signal. 

Finally, there was a fish who was lazy or sick or stuck or God knows what in another tank. He was breathing like fish do, but not moving. I am posting a picture. 

The other reason I am not too impressed is because it was pretty expensive. Besides the dead (aka napping) fishies, it was a 5 star experience. But that is a big "besides"...

As far as aquariums go, this one is...pretty basic. Some beautiful things and some not so beautiful things. I took my girlfriend and our baby there today. Because my child is 1, she got in free. Nice. However, our tickets totaled to 65 dollars. That seems a little outrageous. It included a "free" movie. Tight. After seeing the entire aquarium (took about 45 minutes), we headed over to the movie theater. 
We made it in time for the 3:40 showtime. However, got to the screen 4 minutes after it started. No big deal to us and it didn't seem to matter to the six other people in the theater. Upon arrival, we realized that the movie is in 3D. No one informed us. So, I looked around for some glasses, but there were none. My girlfriend and baby had a seat and I went in search of help. The concession stand is just outside, so I went there. I asked the two ladies behind the counter if they could get us a few pairs, and they said the lady in the theater would give them to us. I told them there was no lady in the theater and they argued and said there absolutely was. So, I went back in, knowing there was no lady, and looked around again. After giving up again, I returned to the concession stand. 
I informed the two ladies that there is absolutely no other person with glasses and one of them decided to "show me where she was." We walked back in, she took a look around, and said, "oh. I guess she not here. Hold up," and retreated to a restricted area near the theater doors. About 30 seconds later, she returned with the glasses lady. 
This all took about 6 minutes. 
The lady, offered me a pair of glasses. I thanked her and said I needed two more pairs. To which she replied, "I only have one pair right now. I might be able to find some more but you're better off just skipping the movie and waiting until the next showtime." I asked, "you don't have any more glasses?" And she said, "nope." 
So we left. With no movie and no apology. 
What a poorly run operation. It seems like a place that's making 32ish dollars a person would have their act together just a tiny bit more.

The exhibits are nice and variety of animals are great. Unfortunately there's were too many screaming children and loud noise for us to really enjoy it. There were prints and streaks on many of the exhibits glass that made viewing difficult.  There was construction going on also. 
The location is nice.
The seahorses, jellyfish and penguins are a lot of fun. The white alligator is neat too. I'm not sure why they have a parakeet experience, it seems unrelated to aquaria. Although if you like birds it would be lots of fun! 
There were long lines at the touch pools. The piranha are interesting too.  The movie was really good!
The wait time was short and the ribs were off the chain good. Can't wait to go back !!!!!!!

This is probably one of my favorite places in down town Saint Petersburg to go to with my friends. They have soooo many flavors and all of them are so mind bogglingy delicous. It's vey inexpensive as well and they are all homemade and creamy!
Delicious meat, awesome sides, great staff! Oh, and like 5 varied sauces- all of which are yummy in their own way!

My dryer was running, but not heating. I called the company Tuesday, told them my issue, and gave him my model number. Frank came by the very next day. He was extremely pleasant and had a great attitude, in general. It took him about 30 minutes to fix my dryer. While he was writing up my bill, he noticed my computer and we began talking about it. He offered to help make it faster, and readjusted the format for me since I had just updated it to Windows 10. Frank was great to converse with, and I would definitely use their services again in the future. Highly recommended!

Nice place to grab a yummy ice pop on a hot day. I've been to one of these franchises in Gainesville before, and enjoyed it there too. It's a little on the higher end for the product you get, but since you can't get these flavors anywhere else, that's what you get. I just realize their margins are definitely set to keep their pockets full :-) I like that they sell Zoku ice pop makers in store too, so you can try to make your own at home. We already have one, so we might try to see if we can recreate some of the same flavors. The place was very clean, and had a nice light and airy feel. We'd have gladly sat in and hung out there enjoying our pop, but our 2 year old had other plans :-)

I went into the store seeking a Christmas gift for my husband. I have no knowledge on woodworking tools but the man that assisted me was very kind and I believe I have found a special gift for my husband! I highly recommend anyone to seek this store whether you have a wealth of knowledge of tools or not.

It's always a pleasure to visit here even in the cold season! I've been coming here since its open. This is located on Central Avenue in downtown St. Petersburg, Florida neighboring a line of boutiques.  It's right in the middle of everything I like in this part of town.

They have almost every combination of good flavors that you can think of and some you would've never guessed went well together. The different types include creamier dessert ones, holiday flavors, healthy light fruity, tea/fruit infused combos, etc. 

I have a soft spot for the lavender or ginger mixtures. They're all very good in general. The very friendly adorable cashier will help you make your decision.

If you're an open-minded human who likes frozen treats, this is a place for you!

I don't write many reviews (that's usually my better half), but we can't say enough about the impeccable service we received from Empire Valet! Our event ran perfectly from start to finish. All of their valets went above and beyond to treat our 300 guests with the upmost professionalism. Empire is truly the best in the business, and I would recommend them to my closest friends and family. We will definitely use them again in the future.

Thanks again guys!!

We loved this aquarium. It has so much more than tanks of fish. There was a Mississippi River section that included all wildlife found on the water, as well as a SUPER fun Parakeet exhibit where they fly freely around you. I would return!
I love this place!! Best flavor is the peanut butter pie. Not too expensive and yummy

I LOVE THE HYPPO! Whenever I have friends visiting from out of town, I make sure to take them here. As a vegan, it isn't always easy to find dessert options, but the Hyppo always delivers! The store itself is absolutely adorable, service is friendly, and the popsicles are delectable! My favorite is the Kale-Apple-Cucumber. Highly recommend this shop for the whole family!

Great aquarium! The traveling beach trash art show was cool (and sobering) to see, the food court was pretty good, and the behind-the-scenes otter meet and greet we payed extra for was worth every penny!

If you are in downtown St Pete and need a sweet healthy treat, you must go here. Their popsicles are amazing!!! And the variety of flavors are mind blowing! The creativity in their creations are impressive...blood orange, jalapeno, strawberry basil, key lime...it goes on and on. And you can dip any flavor in chocolate. So yummy!

Let me start out with why I only gave 4 stars. Parking is ridiculous! I went today for less then 2 hours and was charged $14 with having my ticket validated ! A lady was paying for parking the same time also paid the same amount with the same time in and out like mines also paid the same without having her parking ticket validated at the Aquariums. I felt cheated! We did enjoyed our visit to the Aquarium. We got to touch a live baby gator and saw a few people in wetsuit swimming with the fishes. Overall we enjoyed our time there minus the parking situation.

Amazing experience for Papaw & Granddaughter. Staff could not have been nicer, more helpful, or kinder. You get to snorkel in the Great Maya Reef habitat tank at the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas. Getting a peek behind the scenes is cool; getting IN the tank with fish & rays, waving at family and other folks watching from the Maya Reef exhibit glass tunnel is fantastic. A special thank you to Gabby and Andy whose knowledge and assistance made the experience educational, easy, and enjoyable--best Granddaughter birthday gift ever.

It's an aquarium, but not a particularly exciting one.  Maybe it was just the day we were there but it was PACKED with rude, pushy inconsiderate douche bags who clearly had no interest in being there.  Beyond that, the displays are ok but nothing spectacular.  Mostly I'd say this is a good way to escape the heat if it's hot and kill a few hours if you're tired of walking around the stupid French Quarter waiting for someone to puke on you.  Oh, and it's CRAZY expensive.

We did the Backstage Penguin Pass and it was worth every penny. 

When you arrive, go to the theater area (not the ticket area). They walk you through backstage areas to get to the penguin area. Along the way, you stop and get to see the highlights of the Aquarium without any other people there. We took pictures and our guide told us about the exhibits. It seems really decadent to get a private tour of the Aquarium. Our guide then took us to the penguin area where we got to watch the penguins in their exhibit for a bit. We were met there by Darwin, the resident penguin aficionado. 

Darwin told us about how the African penguin became endangered and the breeding program to try to save the penguins. Next, we went to the kitchen to learn about penguin diets and washed our hands really well to keep our penguin healthy. After each talk, Darwin encouraged questions and had answers for everything. 

Next, we went to meet our penguin, Marina. She was so wonderful. My heart melted. She felt so different from our chickens. Even watching her bend her "wing" is different than how chickens straighten their wings. She was friendly but tired and frequently went to Darwin to snuggle. She would "purr" to Darwin which was adorable. We spent so much time taking pictures and videos and asking questions. Darwin was very patient and answered everything. She painted us a picture with her feet and we got to bring the picture home with us. We also got to feed her fish. Once our time was up, she got brought back to the penguin area in a little cart like royalty. Darwin put her in the enclosure and we got to watch her go back to her friends. Darwin spent time with us after that answering our last minute questions. 

They have a snorkel adventure and sea otter adventure too. I will check out the others next time I am here. 

When you buy the Backstage Penguin Pass, you get to a ticket to the rest of the Aquarium and to see the movie. Your ticket does not include entrance to the Zoo or Insectarium and you can't upgrade to include those on your ticket (you get discounts for combo tickets). We were strapped for time, so we didn't get to see the movie but we did walk around the Aquarium. The exhibits were great. Definitely plan to spend most of the day there. We couldn't find the parakeet palace but we did enjoy the exhibit of shame, the sea horses, sea otters, the water tunnel, and the touch tank was fantastic (filled with "sea puppies" who want to be pet!). They have so many awesome exhibits. It was a real shame that we didn't get to spend the whole day there. The gift shop was very reasonable. I wish I had bought more gift souvenirs from there.
Very cute place and i love the free movie with my ticket. Will be back with my sea creature loving nephew.

I love this place so much! I came here for the first time a few months ago with my niece, mother in law, and husband.  I got a Mexican hot chocolate and it was refreshing and very flavorful.  It tastes exactly how it supposed to taste.  I came back and ordered the mocha cheesecake pop and ordered another spicy one for my husband.  It's $3.50 per pop which is inexpensive for a cold treat, and they are a lot better for you than eating regular ice cream or another dessert.  It satisfies my sweet tooth.  They also distribute the pops and sell them in certain high end grocery stores.  I know they are sold at the Publix Greenwise in Hyde Park.

This aquarium is cool, but it's not worth the price. 20 bucks to look at what seemed like the same exhibit over and over. This was mainly small fish and fish from the Mississippi River. If you're looking for large sharks, whales, dolphins, etc, you won't find those here. 

If you're planning a trip to New Orleans save the 20 dollar admission and walk across the street to the Casino... you'll have more fun.

We ended up here due to torrential downpours which ruined my plans to visit a brewery - so maybe I wasn't in the best spirits while in here. Seems like a good place to bring little ones, actually, this is probably the only place is NOLA where I would ever take a kid. The jellyfish were pretty cool and the otters were funny. We saw a movie at the IMAX also, which was nice. Once you've been to an aquarium you've been to them all.

First let me say that if you are visiting New Orleans with kids, this would be a must. But since there were just 3 adults in our group I have to give it 3 stars. It is cool and I especially liked the two resident otters, but its definitely not worth the price. $21 and we were in and out in less than 90 minutes. There are comparable aquariums in other cities, so I recommend checking out one of the other many activities in Nola before you fork out the cash for this one. 

As a side note, we also went to the zoo and I loved that, so save your money for the zoo, in my opinion.

Very good BBQ uptown.  They have a variety of different sauces.

My wife loves the pulled pork with spicy slaw.  I'm a big fan of the brisket.

Beans and Mac and Cheese sides are unrivaled anywhere but the Joint.

Great outdoor seating, which is available because this place is not packed yet. Owners are very friendly and always in the store chatting.

I liked them in Metairie when they were serving the same outstanding BBQ with the same sometimes struggles of drawing a huge crowd.  I'd love to see these guys get some marketing help, because once you try the BBQ, this place WILL be in your regular rotation. 

Give it a shot, it is good solid locally-owned BBQ Uptown!!!

Very disappointed. We called to ensure they could accommodate children and they were very polite on the phone. Even asked us if we wanted to call our order in, and we explained that we had never been there and would need to see the menu. 

Upon arriving the area was very open sitting and I would say a nice atmosphere. No one was in line for 400 degrees. When we got to the register to order, we were asked if we had a call in. We said no, and she told us it would be an hour wait. 

We asked why when no one was there and it was explained that they had a lot of call in orders and they handle those first. We asked them "Don't you service your walk in customers first?" And they answered "No." We were totally floored! We left to find hot chicken somewhere else.

Very disappointed that they wouldn't service someone that walks into their restaurant first, especially after she explains that they don't cook the food until the person shows up to pay for it... Made no sense to us.
I was taken there once by my brother and I have been hooked ever since! I live fairly close so it's hard not to just "swing by".

Aysha Martin has been taking care of our family's hair for over 6 yrs. My hair has never been healthier. With my medical issues of Diabetes & Thyroid Cancer, she knows when my system is off just by looking at my hair. Her attention to detail is definitely above & beyond. She takes care of the product & color she uses on my hair every visit.  
I can attest my husband will not let anyone else cut his hair. He loves the scalp massage when she shampoo's his head. 
People we have recommended her too come away saying that was the best haircut and  visit to a salon they've ever had.  
The salon staff is amazing, everyone is extremely friendly,  
Please go visit Aysha for the best hair experience you'll ever have. 
What can I say other than that she is AMAZING!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Enjoyed the ambiance and the peach Arnold palmer and grapefruit popsicle. I love this place and will return for more!

This is a good way to spend an afternoon for a $30 ticket.  The lines are long but they move quickly.

There is so much to see on 2 levels with a kid's play area and food court. There are feedings all afternoon and a touch pool for the stingrays. They have a rain forest area, frogs, seahorses, jelly fish, white alligator, owl, otters, penguins, sharks, and varied fish pools, etc.

Very nice variety of marine life with beautiful habitats and information panels at each display.

I cannot drive past St. Roch Market without stopping by to get something from Torshi's! I make everyone try this place!! 
My personal favorite is the rose hibiscus water - I just simply cannot live without it!! 
Baklava and the Gyro plate is also a very popular choice for my family. 
Nola is blessed with this food! I would give it a million stars if I could

After having looked forward to hitting this BBQ Joint for quite a while, we finally followed through and sampled their offerings, and the 'cue was pretty decent...

In order to get the full spectrum, we had the Ribs, Brisket, Pulled Pork, and Sausage (of the cajun variety).  For sides, the Baked Macaroni, Smoked Beans, and Purple Slaw were selected.

First, the meat...  Overall, the 'cue was good, but not very much smoke flavor on anything - it was very mild to say the least.  The Ribs were tender and good, with a mild dry rub.  Their tomato-vinegar sauce was suggested for them, and it worked well.  The Pulled Pork was good, standard pulled pork, again with a mild seasoning and smoke.  The Brisket was cooked very well, and served with a horseradish sauce.  They paired nicely together.  The Sausage was very tasty and firm, and came with a spicy chipotle mayo sauce.  We tried different combinations of the meats with their five sauces, and they all were decent, with their tomato-vinegar sauce winning.  The mustard sauce was a little plain for us, and the others came across as too sweet.  A quick disclaimer - we believe that good barbecue only needs a good rub and a tasty mop, so we are relatively anti-sauce.

Overall, the 'cue was pretty good, and among the better choices in the New Orleans area.

Next, the sides.  This is where the wheels fell off a little bit.  None of one we ordered were very good.  The Smoked Beans looked really good, but were (really, really) overpowering with roasted garlic.  Please note, we love garlic, and the beans were way over the top.  Once again, we did not get really anything as far as smoke flavor.  The Purple Slaw was definitely purple, but it seemed to be from beets as opposed to the cabbage.  It had a hefty vinegar twang to it, and an odd sweet flavor.  This one just wasn't our cup of tea.  The Baked Macaroni was not very good.  The cheese sauce had separated, and pasta was overdone to the  point of having a mushy texture.

As far as the sides - not so much this time around.

The restaurant itself is neat little space, and the server was excellent.  

Overall, it was a good experience - with a few small bumps.  We prefer a more robust, smokey, and flavorful 'cue, but we also appreciate properly made 'cue.  The sides were frankly a disappointment, but that could have been a fluke.

We will recommend this 'cue joint to others, and we will give it another try sometime soon.  If the sides were a fluke, this will bump it up to four stars.

So delicious! This is one of my favorite BBQ places uptown. Located in a great area to stroll off over eating - this restaurant offers a simple menu filled with every bbq option needed. Our table of five ordered nearly everything on the menu and nothing disappointed. The sweet potato muffins are completely magical. Definitely a must if you are in this area!!!

I had the pleasure of visiting all 3 Audobon animal places with my son on our recent trip to New Orleans. If you are intending to visit 2 or 3 of them, make sure to get an Audobon pass where you can visit all 3 within a month. If I remember correctly, i bought the pass for $40ish, but without it all 3 "parks" combined would have been at least $70.

I generally am not super into aquariums, but this one is pretty nice. The displays are nice, there is a lot to learn, everything looks kept up well (though one whole section near the sea horses was closed for...construction/renovation)?

It was not very crowded and was easy to navigate. I particularly liked th Aztec/Mayan area and the area that had the hawk, gaur, and albino alligator. If you like birds, the Parakeet Point area is pretty impressive as there are LOTS of them. My son is only 1 so we didn't participate, but you can feed them for a small fee.
