I generally am not super into aquariums, but this one is pretty nice. The displays are nice, there is a lot to learn, everything looks kept up well (though one whole section near the sea horses was closed for...construction/renovation)?

It was not very crowded and was easy to navigate. I particularly liked th Aztec/Mayan area and the area that had the hawk, gaur, and albino alligator. If you like birds, the Parakeet Point area is pretty impressive as there are LOTS of them. My son is only 1 so we didn't participate, but you can feed them for a small fee.

The Aquarium is nice and is located close to the Riverwalk Outlet Mall (if you don't want typical kid's attraction food). My son and I were there for about an hour and a half and saw all animals that were available that day.

THIS IS SO WORTH THE HYPE-OH MY GOD! They have so many flavors I couldn't decide but the service is so amazing and friendly and the place inside is so upbeat and friendly! I got the strawberry cheesecake and you could see the real fruit and my boyfriend got the banilla vanana and we could not be any more impressed
Awesome service!! Was really craving BBQ and haven't yet found a place in NOLA when I came across Saucy's. So glad they have convenient delivery and take out options.
Best selection of power tools in Reno. Staff is knowledgeable, courteous, and prompt. Great place to get anything you need to build a cabin in the woods

Excellent authentic Egyptian food. Sample their juices - the hibiscus reminds me of my time in Cairo!  The King Tut breakfast is a generous portion of excellent hummus with perfectly crispy falafel wrapped around a hard boiled egg. The accompanying salad was also solid. With friendly service as well! Highly recommend!

Our second visit here. My son's favorite is Watermelon! Mine is Pistachio Coconut!  We drove 40 minutes for a little piece of heaven  Small, clean, little shop with friendly staff to help with our indecisiveness. We arrived shortly after 9pm but they were kind enough to let us enjoy our pops inside.

First time going, showed up an hour before close (5pm -- bump that), got turned away, and was told to call in my order next time. 

One star for no food and bad service. I wouldn't consider my establishment "open" during a known, repeating timeframe in which I'm not accepting customers. That's the definition of closed.

What a fabulous little city aquarium! While it's small and limited in terms of sea creatures, the exhibits are all great, and best of all, the staff are super friendly, kind, and willing to answer any questions about the exhibits or just chat with you about the animals. That was really my favorite aspect of the experience. I absolutely loved interacting with them and learning about the penguins and stingrays in particular.

I went on a Thursday in the afternoon and stayed till closing at 5 pm. It was very uncrowded, which made seeing and enjoying all of the exhibits a breeze. I got to see the penguin feeding and feed the stingrays in just a couple of hours. The white gator was cool, all the fish were amazing, and the parakeet paradise area was super fun! I haven't tried the food court food, but the prices looked decent for what you get, unlike in some museums (*cough* NYC *cough*) where they OVERCHARGE you on everything.

I got a student discount so I didn't pay full price to get in. I recommend that if you go, you go in the off-season and on a week day.

We arrived on a Saturday night around 930 after an art show a block away.  It was crowded but only a few in line.  I had a hard time choosing my popcicle! We ended up with 8? Not on purpose! And they have insulated bags so the treats travel home.  The challenge we had when we got home was remembering what we ordered, and we didn't! So when we opened a cicle, we had to taste test it.  

I would mark them as they went into the bag next time! But a fun experience.  And we did get one with chocolate dipped.  I don't think they need it.

This place is amazing and we weren't even visiting with our kids. My husband and I considered going back a second time because we enjoyed it so much. Really well done. We fed the sting rays and the parakeets (adorable.) We watched the SCUBA divers clean the tube tunnel tank, we watched the keepers feed the penguins and enjoyed the entire place. A+. We purchased the Experience ticket because we also visited the Insectarium-which was also great, and the Zoo (which could have been a lot better.)

This place is amazing!  In case you don't know, NOLA is not just a party town - it's also a great place for family trips. This aquarium is proof of that. The exhibits are great and very educational. The kids loved it. It's a great size and doesn't take up an entire day to walk through. They also have package deals with the IMax and the Audobon Zoo. The location couldn't be better. It's right on the river, next to the mall. We've been a few times, and I'm sure we'll go back a few more.
Baba Ganoush is wonderful.  Friendly employees!! The only problem is choosing what to eat.

Expensive for what it is.  $30 for a ticket and I was done in 38 minutes. I went end of July 2020 so a few things were closed. I'm not sure if it was normal  Or things were shut down due to covid.  The rain forest part of the aquarium of was very nice but again it was very small. There honestly we're not and that many sea life creatures/mammals/ animals in the whole place.  The gift shop was probably the best part. It was very nice and had a lot of stuff in really liked.  The food area was closed so don't come hungry.  It's in a good location just outside of the french quarter in canal st. I would not recommend this aquarium to anybody though.

Let me start by saying this 400 degrees has the nicest staff you could ask for! Super friendly folks who are happy to make suggestions. I had the mild breast with coleslaw. I loved it! The only reason I didn't give them 5 stars is the chicken was a little greasier than I would have liked (but hey, it's fried chicken).

Flowers were delivered REEKING of smoke. I called your store to make you aware of what happened and when asked I told you what the driver looked like. I was told the smoke smell would eventually go away, and if it didn't to call back.  REALLY?!?! Then when a manager got on I was abruptly told how busy you were and asked if we could work it out tomorrow. With apparently no other option I said "I guess" and the manager hung up on me.  Don't think they will be calling me tomorrow to "work it out". Will never get flowers from your establishment again and am warning others of your horrible customer service, and flowers that don't smell fragrant, they smell like smoke. Would give NO stars if I could.
Best popsicle I've ever had in my life! I had the blueberry lavender lemonade. So good and full of blueberries.

My husband and I visited the Audubon Aquarium last week. It rained cats and dogs the entire time we were in New Orleans, so we did as much indoor activities as possible. The Moon Jellies, Penguins, Seahorses, Green Sea Turtle and the Sea Otters were my favorites. My husband put his index finger toward the glass and the otter tried to bite him through the glass. It was hilarious and the nearby children got a kick out of it. The otters were incredibly active and a pure delight to watch. The Amazon Rainforest was very loud and pretty awesome. There were many beautiful birds. The White Alligator was pretty interesting to watch. Employees were cleaning his area while we were there. We wondered if we were going to witness a "Gator Attack"! No luck there...We also saw three sharks just lying on the bottom of the tank. We watched for about 10 minutes. We assume they were just resting. We had never seen that before. I highly recommend visiting and I think it is appropriate for all ages. I found it to be very tranquil except for the Amazon Rainforest. I would have been disappointed, if it hadn't been loud and exciting! No kidding, put this on your bucket list!
The otters were adorable as well as the penguins! I really enjoyed the history of the Mississippi River! We had a lot of fun!

I must say this was an unexpected surprise!  The owner immediately offered me some tastings of his fresh drinks of mint lemonade and I believe a hibiscus one as well.  Yummy!
I am always looking for the best falafel, and here it is!  The were cooked fresh to perfection with toasted sesame seeds on top!  The crunchiness was just perfect, and the flavor was amazing!  I had a side of baba ganoush and hummus, and those were also packed with flavor!

I can't wait to go back!  I certainly recommend this place!
Picked up spicy cheesecake so good! Friendly service. Very spacious and Will come again

Hard choice between 60 flavors but not impossible. I had the Strawberry Lemonade and loved it. I met a girl in the park and she told me me I had to go there, so we all went on a popsicle adventure worth the 17 block walk.

I know, I know -- New Orleans isn't a BBQ town. Better tell that to Saucy's, though, because I don't think they got the memo.

Stopped by on a sunny Sunday afternoon with a friend to give it a try and I was not disappointed. When I try a new BBQ spot for the first time, I like to go with an old standard to see how it measures up. I'll then branch out from there if I like it.

At Saucy's, that meant starting with a simple pulled pork sandwich. I added to cole slaw on top, which I always like, and smothered it in their Southern Sweet sauce. While I didn't have my breath taken away, I can honestly say that I really enjoyed it. For my side I had the beans, which were adequate. Kind of strange that they don't have any fries -- or even potato chips. Would complement the sandwich nicely. No pickles either. And y'alll know how I feel about pickles! Finally, sweet potato muffins were delicious!!

Service was just fine: food came out fast, drinks stayed filled, and nobody was jerk-ish, so that was all good. And the prices were reasonable as well. When I need my BBQ fix, I know there's at least one good option in this non-BBQ town.
Who can resist adorable otters or playful penguins? Even the frogs are fascinating here! My only complaint is the $18 admission fee, rather high for 90 minutes' worth of entertainment and education.

It has a few nice things and a desirable central location, but as aquaria go, it really wasn't much. Highlights included sea otters big enough to be seals, a massive movie theater, a non-albino white alligator, and sea horses. That being said, it looked a lot bigger from the outside than it was inside, and whatever broader mission Audubon was, one didn't really get much of an experience here to justify the cost to enter.

This place is perfect for a hot afternoon or a date night. It's so unique and you will never get to try them all because the flavors are constantly changing. I LOVE the Elvis dipped in chocolate ( peanut butter and banana) and the creamy pistachio is a definite winner!

I have celiacs and am vegan. They went ABOVE AND BEYOND to ensure my food was safely prepared. They gave me all fresh ingredients + prepared my food on a separate cutting board. The food was DELICIOUS + FRESH. The hummus was the best hummus I've ever had!!!! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Saucy's is a solid BBQ spot on Magazine. 

For many years New Orleanian's have had to deal with a dearth of good BBQ restaurants. Back in the early 90's my parents took me to Tipton County Tennessee Pit BBQ which was located where Slice Pizzeria now resides. That experience blew my mind and made me a lifelong fan of BBQ. Unfortunately for me, it closed shortly after I visited, but I never forgot that experience and have sought out good BBQ ever since. Now that New Orleans is becoming a BBQ town, no longer will children have to wander the earth looking for high quality smoked meats. 

My trip to Saucy's was a result of my primary BBQ spot being closed on a Monday and my deep craving for brisket and pulled pork. Saucy's was not only open, but they served me some damn fine BBQ. 

Upon entering I noticed that Saucy's is a relatively small place. I would imagine it gets crowded, but I got there right at opening and only a few tables were taken. The cashier taking my order was friendly and professional. A man I believed to be the owner was also behind the counter and fully explained the sauces to me when I asked. I could tell that he was very involved and loved what he does. That was even more evident when I sat down back at my office and sampled the BBQ. 

When visiting a BBQ restaurant for the first time, I like to try a few meats. This trip I decided on a two meat platter with sliced brisket and pulled pork. The pork was very good, but that brisket. Oh my. That brisket was smoky, tender and delicious. It was so good that I wish I had eaten in so that I could have picked the owner's brain for tips on making my own brisket. To me, that brisket is amongst the best in the city. Even if you don't think you're a fan of brisket, I encourage you to try this version. It's that good. 

I look forward to many more visits to Saucy's. If you are a BBQ nut like me, I encourage you to give it a try.

Chicken was as advertised, and was definitely worth waiting for it. If you're in a hurry, call ahead, but don't let the wait deter you. Since its cooked to order, it comes out hot, both in temperature and spice. Have an ample supply of whatever beverage you prefer, and napkins. Definitely don't make the mistake I made and inhale before taking a bite. I breathed in pure spice.
Not the largest of aquariums but has some good exhibits and the staff is nice. Not cheap but when I went you could pay a bit more and add several other museums in town for a better deal overall.
I had the most amazing Shakshouka for breakfast! Some of the best food I've ever had.

New Orleans doesn't have Ikea, but they have THIS!!!


 You walk down this path off cool aquatic stuff stuff. A lot of it is hands on. I didn't do it because fish are gross but the kids had fun petting the baby shark!


 At the end of it all, the grand finale is this massive jellyfish collection and some of them glow in the dark!


 the only problem is their food selection is limited to JUNK! in the middle of this fish epicenter is a McDonalds. (people still eat that?) BLEAH!


 i want a seahorse!!!

When in New Orleans, we were mostly on foot so most of what we did needed to be within walking distance. Our hotel was on Royal so the aquarium was a sure visit. Although, it was a balmy 50-something degrees that day so a trolly ride might've been a tad nicer. 

The aquarium sits right on the Mississippi, next to the Riverside Mall and the Great, Big Theater. The actual entrance is on the side of the building facing the river, not the side facing the road/parking. 

When you buy the tickets, they'll push you to also buy discounted tickets to the zoo and the insectarium. We declined both; we knew the zoo was too far to walk (but the St Charles trolly takes you right there), and we didn't know what else we wanted to do. Tickets did seem a little pricey to me, but all aquariums are. But, regardless, you do get a free ticket for each person to the Big Theater next door.  Cool. And, we learned this by chance, if you decide later that you want to do the Insectarium, show them your aquarium tickets and receipt and you'll get a HUGE discount! Huge! Insectarium tickets went from over $80 down to less than $20, for all of us. 

The aquarium itself is a nice one; interactive, clean, lots of exhibits, easy to navigate. But there were a LOT of exhibits that were closed down when we were there, which was kind of a bummer. We still had fun, though. It was on a Tuesday afternoon and there were two other families in the entire building so it was perfect timing for those of us that hate crowds. You finish off like most aquariums, in the gift shop full of goodies. 

We did enjoy ourselves and are glad we went. Bring some change for the penny squashers, if you've got a collector on your hands!

I will preface my review by saying the review is based on my tastes. I will try to outline that in the review, as you might find 400 Degrees fits you perfectly. I schould also state that I like food that is really hot, as long as it is flavorful.

If you are familiar with Hot Chicken in Nashville, 400 Degrees is more on the side of Prince's or Bolton's, without marinating the chicken in hot sauce, as Prince's hottest is. But the breading is a bit thicker, which I find makes the chicken a bit tastier. Some other restaurants, like Hattie B's aim more for a really messy chicken heavily coated with sauce. 

400 Degrees is located in a building that houses a food court on the corner of Peabody and 4th Street. Inside the building you can also find Nuvo Burrito, Quiznos and a J Gumbos (Cajun franchise). 

My feeling about the food. The 100 degrees is too mild, almost to the point of bland. There is a hint of pepper, but not enough to rank it as anything different from most southern style fried chicken. The 200 degrees has a bit of a punch and there is really not much between 100 and 200. The 400 degrees is just ridiculous, shut your bowels down, hot. I can attest to the "shut your bowels down" aspect, as that it what my system did the next day. If you like hot, I would aim for 200 and consider whether you need to tone up or down from there.

For my experience, the pepper blend in 400 degrees is aimed more for heat than enjoyment. I can generally take really hot food without indigestion, but found myself having to stir some baking soda into water each time I tried 200 degrees or hotter. To me, this is similar to calling a really bitter beer and IPA because you added a lot of Indian hops. Technically correct, but the good beers in this style have a balance and have learned to mix good flavor with IBUs. To me, 400 degrees is about the heat of the pepper and not blending for taste. But, like peeps I know that like really bitter IPAs, I am sure someone will completely disagree with my assessment of the chicken here.

On the positive side, the chicken is very juicy. I have been to other hot chicken places that had really dry meat, which really ruins the experience, even if the spice flavor is awesome. On another positive note, they offer some items you won't find anywhere else, like pork chops. And the portions are nice. For a bit more than $6, you get a chicken quarter, with a huge breast or thigh portion. 

The only other item I tried was the potato salad, which was very nice. It is a mustard and mayo based potato salad, which is one of my favorite ways to do it, and the relish is added in almost perfect amounts, so the potato salad has a nice hint of sweetness that is not overpowering.

Would I go back? Certainly. The succulence of the breast meat was good enough to overcome the digestive burn of the specific peppers used. I would really enjoy something around 150 degrees in this establishment, however, and that is largely due to the way the pepper they use affects me (I will go hotter at Hattie B's, which does not affect me in the same way).

Such an amazing experience! Haven't been since i was a kid and really enjoyed it! All the workers are really nice and very helpful! My favorite was the bird section. Had little bit of construction going on so we didn't get to see a few things but the others made up for it! Make sure you check out the penguin feeding times! They were pretty cool!

One of my favorite shops on Central Avenue! The popsicles are absolutely delicious and very hard to resist. I've filled out MULTIPLE stamp cards during my time living in St. Pete. The only reason this place is getting 3 stars is the fact that it is overpriced and also they don't seem to let their employees sit? Please for the love of God give these kids some chairs !
Incredible doctor very knowledgeable and professional. He gave us all of the facts and the options. If you are in need of a perinatologist in the area he is a must!

This place is awe...some!!! I came here with my Mom. She loves fresh pops like these. She got one with coffee or cappuccino or something. I got mango as recommended by the staff. Both were great and the people who worked there were great! The only thing I would suggest to make it even better is more chocolate choices!!!!!

Highlights are:
Stingray touch pool:  they are very approachable.  I won't ruin it for those who want to touch them.  Apparently they've had a part of their barbed stinger removed so there's no chance of being stung.
Stingray feeding at the touch pool:  thank you Yelpers for the tip to get the feeding pass from the second floor gift store!  Even though you were only given a few strips of food, this is an experience you won't forget.

We could not get a backstage pass to pet and feed the penguins but watching them is fun.  They are so endearing. Make sure you lookout for the one isolated guy on the right hiding in the recessed area:  that seemed like a timeout :)
Otters:  there's a couple who seem inseparable.  There's Emma a separate otter who has her own Web cam.  It's a recording though.
Albino alligator:  he seems to be motionless most of the time but look below the water.  The lighting makes him look neon green.
Seahorses and jellyfish:  I could have watched them for ages.

There's a lot to see and displays are well done.

Before you enter, there's an opportunity to take a pictures.  Nice souvenir if you're willing to drop $35 or so.

Every time I visit Florida, I always go to the Hyppo. The popsicles are so amazing and there are always so many different flavors. I always go for the creamier flavors, but I've also tried a few of the refreshing options from my friends! Super big place- perfect for groups. Very friendly staff, too!
the Popsicles are great here and what drove us here is the original location we went to in st.augustine, definitely good
This location is closed and complete gone. There are no signs and the building is vacant with a for lease sign on the property.

My father, daughter, and I decided to take a field trip to the Great N.O., and while there we wanted to take my daughter to the one of the wonderful Aquariums of the United States. The Audubon aquarium offers amazing pricing, compared to aquariums in other regions and it was well worth the money! The aquarium only takes an hour and half to two hours to run through, so I would encourage families to buy a multi pass to the zoo, if you have a whole day to spend in New Orleans. There were a lot of neat exhibits and some very interesting sea animals that I have never seen before. The aquarium is well designed and you can easily flow through without worrying about missing anything. Our favorite parts were the Great Maya Reef area , the shark tank (also known as the Gulf of Mexico Exhibit), the otters, penguins, and the sting rays! We really did not have a dull moment and loved every inch of the aquarium. My only gripe is upon entering and when purchasing our tickets, no one told us to check for daily schedule of different features within the aquarium or that we could pay to feed the sting rays. My daughter was interested in seeing the sting rays being feed and I assumed as long as we made it in time she could watch this activity. It turned out visitors can feed the sting rays for an additional $4.50 but it is first come first serve and they only allow 15 people during each feeding time. So, be sure to stop by information if your kids are interested in participating in any exhibits. Other than that, we had a great time and I would surely go back!
By far my favorite nail place in the area...& I've tried like 10 of them. My nails look amazing! & they were super fast!

Hyppo Pops are pretty awesome. We were brought here by some friends of ours who are die hards. After a long day at the beach, these were awesome. I got the Cucumber, Mint, Lemon- so refreshing. My fiance tried one with datil pepper and (i think) coconut. He loved it, i thought it was weird. He also ordered another one, but ate it before I ever had a chance to ask what it was. The flavors change regularly and our die hard friends swear they're all good. You can also have them dipped in chocolate!

I knocked off a star because this place can get really, really pricey fast. I know they're using fresh ingredients and making a lot of pops, but we walked out of there having spent close to $15 on popsicles.
I really wished they cleaned their bathrooms more frequently and better.  EVERY SINGLE TIME I need to use the restroom or take my daughters to use it, it's filthy.

A very good aquarium if not the best.   Loved the penguin feeding session.   Thought the glass tunnel was great way to see the fish up close.   The smaller displays were very good as well.    All the people working there are helpful.    Digital photos are a nice keepsake.   You can do this aquarium in an hour if you want.  It is a short walk back to Quarter.   Worth doing.

Im a huge fan of marine life, so going here was such a joy. I felt like a little kid in a candy story. I love how realistic some of the rooms were, in particular the Mississippi river room was humid, but thats how the environment really was. And I was supposed to see how big the place actually was, just when I thought it was over there were more room. My favorite marine animal to see was the sea turtle, I was really excited they had one.

My kids love this Aquarium. I am kind of disappointed in their "new" mayan exhibit. It looks like all they did was change the decorations in the tanks.

Favorite parts: Penguins, Otters, Sea Horses and Stingrays. 

A bit pricey so If you're a local I recommend springing  for an Audubon Membership and seeing all of the Audubon facilities at least once.

This is a great place to cool off on a hot summer day. It compares with most big city aquariums. There are alligators here so that was fun to see. Also the large gar fish were nice. It is in the French Quarter near the free ferry. The free ferry across the Mississippi was a real delight.

I love this place...the chicken, pork chops...sides wow.  Bury me with a full belly of this stuff.  Aqui is the best...I love her.  She is a shining star.  Her location is perfect and the atmosphere is great...great for lunch with co-workers.  She doesn't load up so you wait a bit, so call it in....get used to the drill and we're good!  I would like to visit those who don't love this place with a flaming bag of poop on their front door step.

I came to St Roche Market surprised you see an Egyptian vendor. I'm glad I tried it because it was some of the best roasted eggplant and falafel that I've ever had. And I'm Egyptian so I'm experienced In this area lol. The owner is also super nice and had a long conversation with me about the business and his experience in NOLA. I'll def be coming back.

Excellent all day fun for the family at the Aquarium in New Orleans.  Price is expensive but worth it if you need a cool indoor activity to tire the little ones out.  Bonus break for mom and dad is the huge IMAX movie theater with great shows on ocean, wetlands, hurricanes, etc.  You can schedule the movie time around other presentations such as penguin feeding, sting ray feeding, reef talk and otter talk.  The exhibits are well planned and accommodate crowds nicely.  There is a cafe with drinks and snacks and a nice gift shop.  Highlights include the giant shark tank, the walk through tank tunnel, the rainforest tree climb, and the frog room.  It was fun for all and an easy walk from the hotel.  If we had more time we would've visited the nearby Insectarium and Butterfly Museum.

Florida is a very hot state. And what better thing to eat on a hot day than a popsicle! I would have to say this place is the best popsicle place ever! They have a variety of many different popsicles and for $1.00 more you can get your choice of popsicle covered in chocolate! The building itself is very nice. I love the wood and the paintings on the wall along the counter as well. Rustic but modern! I really hope you give them a try! Thanks for reading!

I was very excited to go to this aquarium and loved that it was an Audubon site. It was $30 something after taxes- the price is typical of a large city, impressive aquarium. This aquarium, however, is very small and the collection is equally as small. This is where you have to remember that it's part of the Audubon which is an organization dedicated to preserving wildlife- not like aquariums who purchase  lots of animals and support the animal farming market. They more so tailor to rescue animals and preservation, which is why the collection is small and why the price is so high. We loved the penguins and otters. They offer private hang out sessions with the penguins and otters for additional fees- we passed. The workers are informative and most likely studied marine biology or are interns who are studying. We planned on spending 2 hours there but we're shocked to finish it in under 1. I'd recommend this to families because it's important to educate and support these organizations and not places like sea world. There is a lot of interactive things to do. The children there looked like they were having lots of fun- especially in the parakeet peak area which is an open room where these birds dart around like crazy and fly onto you looking for food. They're harmless and it was hilarious watching my boyfriend scream and run out of the room flailing.

This is a pretty simple and cool - no pun intended - concept. Popsicles! A lot were dairy free (white dot on the label) and some were spicy (red dot). All can optionally be dipped in a dairy free chocolate. 

I tried the strawberry dipped in chocolate. I liked the strawberry, but found the chocolate to be bitter. I also tried a non-dipped strawberry lemonade which I liked better than the regular strawberry. 

Friendly staff that moved quickly and explained the concept since we were newcomers.

My go-to place for Q in the city, definitely the best brisket I've had so far. Also, the sides are awesome. Smoked beans are great and the goat cheese mac is really, really good. Take out service is super quick so you can take it home and eat it all weekend!!
Spectacular authentic Egyptian cuisine in a very nice public market setting. The owner made me a plate with fuul, falafel, baba ganoush and salad and it's positively crushing. Go here now.

My only complaint of this aquarium is that it was undergoing some construction at the time i visited. They do have a sting ray petting area, and they have an attached IMAX theatre. 

They have some interactive activities for the kids, but some of it seemed broken. The penguin area was pretty cool especially since I was around during feeding time. The penguins were probably the highlight of the aquarium. 

They do have a bunch of exhibits so it's better than say the Aquarium in DC, but it still pales in comparison to other aquariums.

We wanted to love this place because we are big fans of pleasant pops in dc. Service was great! I thought my pop (mango chia) was just okay - sort of freezer burned maybe? My husband got chocolate dipped raspberry cheesecake which was really good. I would rate my popsicle three stars and his four, so we are rating the place as a whole at four stars because of the sweet person manning the counter! I sort of wish I had gotten a cream based one. Next time.
Great little place to stop by and have a glass of wine before continuing your walk through the stores. Don't expect a fancy wine selection though.

Mango Habanero. Omg. Amazeballs. 

Just moved to St Petersburg from beautiful San Diego and I have to say, this place is where the kids and I have found our joy back...The Hyppo and Jesus, of course. 

Second time back in less than a week so bought a few to sustain us...

Purchase 20 or more and get this nice cooler to take home your popsicles. Yes, please! 

I haven't been this excited about anything in a very long time.

I just remembered that they sell four flavors at Publix. I just got happier.

The customer service was horrible tonight. 
I shop at dressbarn alot but the two women that helped me tonight lost business for the company!

Fantastic value when buying a combination ticket for the Audubon Zoo.
Children will absolutely love this place with it's informative and interactive displays. From penguins to jellyfish to sharks, there's a huge variety of aquatic wildlife to be seen here including an area where children can touch underwater creatures.
Great place and great location - right in the heart of the French quarter

Pricey for what you get. The aquarium itself is rather small, for a 32 buck adult ticket it seemed like there should have been more. The large and with the sharks and sea turtle and large fish is pretty cool, just make sure you take your time at all the smaller tanks so you don't spend 32 bucks for an hour!

So good!! Only downfall is the price.. kind of expensive but they do have a punch card rewards program. The chocolate peanut butter pie always sells out it's so good! And for those that can't eat dairy there's many pops that are dairy free as well. I love the Elvis since it's dairy free and still has a creamier texture than just plain fruit. You can't go wrong with any flavor.

Pretty disappointing. What an underwhelming experience this place is. There are few exhibits, and several areas are unavailable, in various stages of redo or prep. The Gulf of Mexico tank and the stingray touch tank are the two best exhibits, but still pretty blasé. Man does this place need a total renovation. Seems like a serious ripoff for the admission price.

RUDE, UNRELIABLE, WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE I HAVE EXPERIENCED IN A LONG TIME. 

My boyfriend ordered flowers over a month in advance to be delivered to my office on the Friday before Valentine's Day. They never arrived. I realized later that night that I had a voicemail on my work phone from 6:30pm - well after business hours- saying they were not going to make it. No apology, just excuses about being busy. 

I had my boyfriend call him back and the guy was a real jerk. -The tire gauge left on my passenger car seat hinted to me that the mechanic who worked on was a bit careless, which was verified in my next point.

- Right before I pulled into my driveway I noticed my car stuttered a little bit when accelerating. I thought maybe it was a hiccup, so I let it go. ::disclaimer::
I used a groupon for admission so I only paid $9.

This was a really nice aquarium. The tunnel of sharks was wonderful way to watch those critters scoot around. The variety of native and exotic fish was lovely, interesting and informative. I thoroughly enjoyed the penguins, and the sea otters were fun and engaging. The frozen treats they give the otters are worth sticking around for. It's amazing what how they get their goodies out. 

One of my favorite parts of the aquarium was the parakeet aviary they've set up. For $1 you buy a bird seed on a stick and the little buggers flock to you. It's really fun.

If I had paid full admission ($20) I may not have been as impressed, but for what I paid it was wonderful.

I'm so happy they have a rewards card (Not that I need a reason to go back every time! Hey, I'll take the incentive! ), only 3 more popsicles and can redeem a free one after 8th purchase! 

There are so many different flavors, I can't keep up with them all and it makes the decision even harder! I really love it that they carry unusual (Pistachio Rosewater, Prosecco Mango, Matcha Starfruit, Datil Plum, Sangria Starfruit, Peach Ginger, Pineapple Durian, Saison, Apple Honey Goat etc.) flavors and you get to expand your palette (Try something new every time 'cause life is too short! :D).

DOUBLE DOG ALMOND 4.5/5: The coconut milk paired with Double Dog espresso really came through, loved the richness of the dairy combined with cane sugar to add some creamy sweetness.

KALE, CUCUMBER APPLE 4/5 (No Sugar Added): It was really interesting tasting, not super sweet by any means and had a tart aftertaste. I like to think I got part of my fruit and veggie quota for the day, so I was happy! The flavors (cucumber, kale and apple) were all clearly present, refreshing for a hot day's stroll in DTSP.

I do find the popsicles to be expensive at $4 a piece, wish they weren't that much!  

I've also discovered I prefer the ones that are made with condensed milk for a creamier taste compared to natural ones that have no sugar added and/or no dairy. Visit their pop shops in Hyde Park, Ybor, and DTSP!
Amazing falafels and hummus. the gentleman is very sweet and the service is impeccable. hard to find better mediterranean food in this area

Audubon Aquarium of the Americas is an amazing multi level aquarium located on the Mississippi River. 

The highlights of our trip to the aquarium were the Amazon Rainforest and the Shark Discovery. The Amazon Rainforest is full of tropical plants and birds. A beautiful area to capture some photos. There is even a cool treehouse area that you can walk up and view the area from up high. 

Bow the Shark Discovery is phenomenal. There is a 13,000 gallon shark and ray touchpool. We spent so much time there trying to lure the rays to us so we could glide our fingers over their smooth skin. I could have spent hours there with my arm submerged in the tank. When the area opens there will be loads of people just wait and the crowd will disappearance you can have the tank to yourself and a few others. 

I love aquariums and the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas is a great aquarium to visit.

This store is, in my experience, is always disorganized and by all means not the cleanest of stores. The employees would rather stand around and gossip as opposed to doing their jobs, and the management is a toss up. If you're lucky they will show up and assist you. 

The store is understaffed or poorly schedule employees as more often than not there is 1 or 2 registers open causing long lines.

Surprised at the large variety of flavors. All fresh and cool combos. I had the coconut dipped in chocolate. It was light and very satisfying. Cannot wait to go back and try other flavors. Others in party had peanut butter, Mexican hot chocolate and dragon coconut lime. Everyone left happy. 
Have been thinking of this delectable dessert since my first venture. Returned and had the banana coconut!   
Did some research and LOVING this place even more.  Pops are all natural, no preservatives, fresh fruit, low calories and appear to be free of grains to which I am allergic. WIN WIN WIN

(Caveat: As a biologist who's worked in zoos as well as the commercial/retail fish trade, this review may be wayyyy more picky than you'd care to discover.  Read on at own risk.)

I visited this site on an off-season Friday afternoon, so crowds were minimal.

THE GOOD:

--Architecture: They must have the same architect as the Dallas World Aquarium, the layout is really nice.  You enter through an impressive arch underneath a Caribbean/Gulf Flower Mound faux reef tank, which swirls with the color and activity...then moves on to a several-stories tall atrium of Amazon exhibits.  From there it flows to a more standard aquarium layout utilizing multiple stories.  All in all, a reasonably large facility that can continue to grow in its current footprint.

--Interactive displays: A good balance of educational, hands-on displays aimed at children but interesting to adults as well (the  display on color spectrum shift due to water depth was clever, don't think I've seen it elsewhere) and the stingray touch tank was nice (and well-supervised, thank goodness...no children mauling the animals).  Other reviewers complain about the number of child-friendly displays; I think they could stand to even more.

--Cleanliness: Do you have any idea how difficult it is to keep glass smudge- and handprint-free when hordes of children (adults too) press their noses against the glass?  And yet the glass was remarkably clean, even at the end of the day--I'm impressed!  Tank sides and backs appeared recently scraped and algae-free.

--Live corals: They don't have them.  This is good; they know their limits.  Kudos to them for not attempting such and killing off already highly-threatened resources in the name of 'education'.

--Plants: Indoor and terrarium plants are thriving; a tiny orchid in a Dendrobatid paludarium was in bloom.  Very nice.

--Volunteer staff: Despite dealing with shrieking, overcaffeinated and undersupervised children all day (and adults who are not much better), the 3 volunteers I met were gracious and helpful.  Most are college students/bio majors; all were very open to questions.

THE BAD:

--Scope and design: What is the focus of this aquarium?!?  From its title, one might guess it was marine/freshwater flora/fauna of the Americas, but instead the aim seems scattered.  Pacific faux reef tanks are mixed beside Caribbean tanks, with no signage differentiating them...a room of marine tanks will have a fresh- or brackish tank mixed in (again, no signage).  I could reconcile myself to these peculiarities if there were some sort of story, narrative arc, flow to the facility (no pun intended), but try as I might none could be discerned; instead it often seemed a mixed jumble of displays.  And while I realize that the conservation message must be diluted in large doses of entertainment to be palatable, there are many MANY missed opportunities to promote such (labels of 'Endangered' and 'Threatened' were often the sole conservation notice).

--Signage?!?: many scientific names are misspelled, most tanks are un- or mislabeled.  An Alligator gar sign on the marine oil rig megatank display...really?!?  An arowana/arapaima tank with neither?  None--this means 0%--of the tanks listed all species inhabiting them, and my questions could not be answered because...

--Staffing: Where are they?  I've never seen a zoo/aquarium so invisibly staffed...saw only two official employees once past the ticket booth (both inaccessible in penguin exhibit).  Children (and adults, sigh) rapped on glass and tried to startle animals and there was no one supervising 98% of this facility...much less leading tours or otherwise interacting with the public.

--Amazon aviary zone: This was the defining point where my "ooohs" turned to "wha?"  This multi-story area could be stunning but seems underutilized and its tanks were disappointing; every species is commonly available in retail pet stores and not displayed at their best.  The mix of domestic discus need a blackwater tank, and don't even get me started on all the blood parrot cichlids...what the hell are man-made hybrids doing here?!?!  A volunteer confirmed that pre-Katrina, this area was a free-flight aviary but it's currently bird-free.

--Health of animals: All animals appeared well-fed, but why are so many marine fish blind or missing eyes?  Why do both barracuda in the hammerhead tank have raw beaks and skull deformities?  Why so many fish in the seahorse tanks? Illnesses, accidents, and deaths occur in the best of facilities but AAqA, you can do better.

--Noise: Pleeeeeeease turn it down.  Blaring 'soothing' music is NOT necessary.

CONCLUSION:

-I'm guessing this facility is highly understaffed, in which case they're doing the best they can...but with a more refined scope, more staff, IMPROVED SIGNAGE, and better use of a lovely facility this place could be world-class for even overly picky biogeeks like me.  In the meantime, for the average visitor, great place to spend a half-day.

We decided to visit to get out of the heat during our trip early August. It's a nice aquarium, but compared to others I have been too, on the smaller side and not as much to see. I wouldn't expect to spend more than 2 hours there at most. The hawk and owl was a nice touch though.

OMGosh is this place tasty. Had a nibble from a coworker from his take out and planned an outing for the weekend. 

1. Believe the yelpers when they say order ahead if in a hurry. She cooks to order. Scrumptious but if in a hurry, order ahead. You will wait the entire 11 minutes, and only if you the only order, so be prepared if in a hurry. But 10 to 20 minutes is def worth it. 
Again, made to order. YUM. 

2. 200 is sweating hot for the professionals. If you can't handle really really really hot, start with 100. 

3. She lets you mix it up. Therefore if you're feeling bold get the 100 and the 200. 

4. AMAZING taste, Everyone has their favs, this is mine. The heat and the taste do it for me. 

5. Fries, love fries, wish they were handcut but still very good.  Crinkle cut with seasoning. 

6. There is parking and seating.

7. There are 2-3 settings higher than 400. Ask about them. I am good at 100 and on a good day 200.  

8. You have to try this place. If you are a hot chicken fan, this place does it right and IMHO has the best flavor.
Its a great aquarium. Be sure to check out one of the IMAX shows. Inside, the exhibits are organized by habitat type. There is a really interesting area for local life.

Purchased Aquarium/ Insectarium tickets as part of a combo online. Drastically reduced the price of admission. Stand alone Aquarium tickets are more expensive than the zoo. 
This aquarium is nice and well spread out. It has 2 floors with several exhibits and a few areas for kids to touch feel and play.
The best area to us was the feed the birds area located next to Haagen Daz in the food court. Pay $1.50 for a popsicle stick with a little birdseed on it and you can feed the little parakeets. This was a great different experience for my 2. My daughter didn't want to leave this area of the aquarium. My son quite enjoyed it as well.
The aquarium is clean with a good flow and layout. It's smaller than most we've been to. Chattanooga's aquarium is tops. This one is pretty good. Not quite as big and not as many exhibits as Atlanta or Chattanooga.
In the rainforest a little macaw kept attacking people. It was pretty funny to see grown men run from a tiny bird. 
He bit the heel of my shoe. I didn't see him actually bite anyone. It seemed like a game to him and we watched him for a while. 
It's nice and cool in there. We expected rain today so we did the zoo yesterday and the aquarium/ insectarium today. While I don't think I would need to go back to this Aquarium if you're going to the zoo and you have kids buy the combo tickets online and it's well worth the modest difference in price to get tickets to all 3.

A fun place and the selection of popsicles is really quite amazing.  Stores like this are totally amusing and fun.  Of course we skipped the healthy fruits and went straight to the alcohol infused popsicles and were not disappointed.  Flavorful with a kick, kinda.  Not enough to prevent you from driving home, but tasty enough to put a smile on your face.

We came here for a wine tasting during our yelp road trip. It was pretty early probably like 10:30  in the morning so my husband and I were the only ones there.  The place is very spacious and decorated very nice. Our host was very friendly and knowledgeable about all the wines. We were given a sample of 8 different wines and she explained each wine in great detail as she poured it.

I liked that they divided their wines into different categories on the chart such as dry red, dry white, and sweet wine and included a description of each one. That way you have a better idea of what you're getting. I tried to pick at least a few different wines from my husband so that way we can maximize all the flavors, but there was a few that we both picked on both of our lists that looked too good to share.

I tend to like wines that are sweet, but there was one dry red wine called the red standard that had a Smokey black cherry flavor that we both really enjoyed. Every wine we tasted was very good and we ended up buying 4 bottles to take home. I got 2 bottles of Niagra which is a sweet white wine, one bottle of the red which was a sweet red grape tasting wine, and we got a bottle of the red standard. We received the in store offer for 10% off 3 bottles or more, but I didn't realize we had a yelp offer for 15% off until after we left, oh well. 

We enjoyed our time here and would like to get to the actual Chaddsford location one day maybe. I have friends that have been there and recommended it to us.

Always a good choice for the kids. Best part was the bird feeding (u have to pay $1.50 for a feeding stock). Stingray petting is fun too, and the big eels are interesting. The scheduled penguin show is informative altho a bit long for little ones. 

Parking nearby can be *very* expensive, might be good to do some research on this.

This is a review for Torshi's new location on Frenchman, where Mona's used to operate. Everything was so tasty! We had falafel, labneh, the roasted eggplant entree with hummus and salad, and khoshari. Each dish was super fresh and flavorful. The roasted eggplant was crazy good. I'll definitely be going back regularly.

The chef plans on opening the market space back up eventually as a fresh food market, with Middle Eastern goods and produce/juice.

A beautiful place-we wish had more time here!! We loved all the displays and got to enjoy a lesson during the otters training! We also got to interact with the rays in a touchable tank- with the guidance from the friendly staff!!

We also enjoyed the white alligator and the adorable penguins!! Make time to go here- you will be glad you did!
Didn't even make it in...the receptionist was so rude, I wouldn't dream of giving them one red cent of my money...

Saucy has the Magazine Street feel with some mighty good BBQ to serve up.  First of all, sweet tea is a must with BBQ and it was very sweet with fresh, brew flavor.  When I went in, my party was the only table and so our waitress was very serviceable.  There are four sauces and the pulled pork is served with its warm mustard sauce.  The sweet sauce was really good.  The mustard base and southwest Chipotle were pretty good.  The bold sauce was too bitter for my taste.  I had ribs, pork, mac and cheese, and potato salad.  Meat was really warm and tender and mixed well with the sweet sauce.  Potato salad was mustard base and creamy but the mac cheese was outstanding.  Mac and cheese had a little kick to it as well.  As far as value, I have been to other BBQ places and received more for what I've paid.  The two meat was $13 with 2 sides.  In summary, food was really good and prepared really well.  The sweet sauce is the best sauce they have.  The downsides are the bold BBQ sauce and I left feeling that I should have been given a little more meat for what I paid.
I have tasted every meat on there menu and they're all soooooo GOOD!! even the smoked burger yum! there saucy's are amazing. Melt in your mouth good. highly recommend Saucy's BBQ.
Best pops in town. So good. Fresh ingredients. Just wish they weren't $4 plus per pop. I know they have a reward card, but how about a multi-pop discount for all us regulars?

Though it was freezing out last night, I could resist buying a Popsicle after passing by this place. It looked like such a ute new hangout spot, very modern, the guy was super nice for letting us in last minute to look at the assortment of pops they had. I tried the persimmon Popsicle which was my favorite so far and also the peanut butter and chocolate banana. It was interesting! It had banana bits inside! This is definitely a place I would take out of towners and be coming often during the hot summer.

It's been a while since I visited, but the fact that I gained at least 20 lbs a few summers ago solely due to the fact that I was consuming their peanut butter pie pops is indicative of how addictive those bad boys are.  Yum!

What a beautiful expansive aquarium!  We had soooo much fun and would highly recommend a trip here.  They have many different areas to view even an area to see birds and to interact with them too.  An area to relax and have a bite to eat is also available.  A must if your in town visiting:)

This place is awesome! We go once a year (for the last 9 years) every time we go to New Orleans. So much to see.
The last time we were there a guy in a scuba suit was feeding the stingrays . Very cool. Very hands on for the kids. Employees are very knowledgeable and friendly. Line outside for tickets is long but moves quickly.

The one star is more for their corporate policies than the staff but I would rate the personnel
At the Reno store a 2. I have been a customer for over 10 years and purchased clothing in Connecticut and all through California.  Today was the last time I will walk in one of their stores. They lost $100 in sales today all because the $5 in Daisy Dollars I earned online but didn't have the receipt attached. Both sales clerks kept telling me it was their policy and pointing to fine print on back. I left them my Daisy Bucks and the clothes I was going to purchase and went to Macy's where folks are a bit more friendly. This was the first Dress Barn I ever entered where the sales clerk didn't ask me if they could start a dressing room for me...I had to ask.  Appears more training required.
Tastiest popsicles I've ever had! The Jackfruit was light and refreshing while the Mexican Hot Chocolate was rich and creamy with just the right kick of spice. Definitely anxious to try more flavors.

I'm not sure if she was the manager but this kind lady named Patricia helped us find dresses for an upcoming cruise. There's a formal night and an ice sculpture gala event onboard the ship. Make it extravagant but practical and for gosh sake make it affordable. 

We arrived 15 minutes before closing and not only did she encourage us to take our time, she also re-opened the dressing room. Then she helped us search for the perfect frock (of course we hurried out of respect for her and the store hours).  

A pretty decent selection and just all around great customer service. We're not ones to spend a lot of money on a dress that will be worn sparingly, this is the exception. If faced with this scenario in the future, this will be our first stop. You will also see us frequenting this Dressbarn again, for whatever reason. 7/19

The lady working was rude when I accidentally picked the wrong item for my free gift. She told me to, "Get out of line so the people in front of me could go first." However, I will say they have a decent selection of candles.
If you build it they will come..  nope just kidding.  No shark exhibit just a large portion of the aquarium forever displaying a giant pool of water.   Driving Audubon members to cancellation.

What a pleasure to work with Frank! Fixed my dryer and explained what went wrong. A reasonable price for same-day and beyond-pleasant service.  

Frank sure knows about making a lasting impression, as the rest of my review is about his customer service. 

He was generous with advice to improve safety and prevent future problems. Quite a charmer with my kids, giving them brainteasers and demonstrating to my daughter how to throw a ball with the full force of her arm (aka not throwing "like a girl" but of course he didn't say that). He was a wealth of cool information for a 10 year old about pennies, speed reading and a few other tidbits, all while he wrote up the bill.

He even shared the name of a legit free app for music downloads but Doh! I didn't write it down. 
Frank at All Brands will be the FIRST I contact for any other appliance.

I do like beer but I can only handle sitting in Cycle Brewery or Green Bench for so long before I have to tell the guys I'm going to walk around while they stay drinking.  Every time I leave and walk around the shops I end up walking by Hyppo.  It's so colorful and looks so yummy that I end up walking in and seeing what they have, and every time I look I have to buy one.

THey always have a big selection of their frozen fruit popsicles and what I love the most is that most of them are not just a plain fruit flavor like watermelon or strawberry. They usually are these really interesting mixes like Carrot Ginger, Blackberry Clove, Mango Habanero, Honeydew Basil, Bourbon Peach, Cantaloupe Mint. Pistachio Rosewater and so many more.

I've tried a bunch of them but I still don't have a favorite since I have loved them all.  I will say though you must pay the extra dollar to have your popsicle chocolate dipped, it's really worth it.

So much fun for the kiddos and the aquatic animal lovers alike. This aquarium was actually quite impressive. I am not really one for animals in enclosures, but I do admit that it does make a great way for us to learn about the many of them out there. My favorite part was trying to find the green anaconda that seemed to be in hiding or was quarantined for some reason. Just weeks before, I was at a zoo in Alabama (for my daughter's entertainment) and we got to interact with a yellow anaconda (yup, get in an enclosure with it), so I was really looking forward to the green anaconda. There was a lot of animals to see here and since my kiddo has seen a lot of animals in her almost 8 years of life, I think she was more entertained with running around with her friend. Anyway, the aquarium was easy to access from the interstate, really close to the riverwalk and the ticket lines went pretty quick. So many visual aesthetics that would keep kids engaged and entranced for a couple hours. Family-fun in New Orleans.

POPS!! Pop pop pop! Where has this been hiding for so long!!! Mmmm... The store was started in St. Augustine... And finally made it to St. Pete. Good location too... You just have to know it's there!! There's a frequent pop card... So get one....

Ok. So at any given time there are probably about 50 different pops you can choose from. Most are a serving of fruit... So you can feel good about eating this! Most are dairy free - those that have dairy are marked... And most a vegan and vegetarian friendly. AND you can have you pop dipped in chocolate!!! So what to choose... What to choose...

I went with the guava lavender pop. Very tasty and good flavor. Mostly guava flavor and subtle lavender taste.  Made from real fruit... Good to the last drop... 

There are so many others I want to taste. Of note is the Elvis, avocado coconut, horchata, mexican hot chocolate, dragon ginger, starfruit... I could go on and on... How I dream of pops!!

Used these guys about a month or so ago now. Frank came out right away to fix our stove as we couldn't get PECO to start gas service without proper repairs in our new apartment. He was even willing to look at my laptop for free while he was there with my fiance just casually mentioning it. I suspect the hard drive crashed during the Summer (confirmed by him). Time nor the proper funds to have it properly repaired yet (landlord was paying for aforementioned), but, it was nice of him to do.  

Def recommend All Brands for any problems that come up in your home.

Overall a pretty good place, but charging an "MCI charge" of just over $2 is low form. That's a charge for them calling you to tell you that your car is ready. It's a really insignificant amount for both sides, since it's a small percentage of the overall bill. Tom, you should get rid of that charge. MCI hasn't been around forever...

On March 29, 2016 I decided to take my lunch break and visit 400 Degrees. I went online to view the menu and hours of operation to save time since my lunch break is only 30 minutes. Been here on multiple occasions and I can't find one I don't like. 

The pistachio coconut is my new favorite!   Every Popsicle is made with fresh ingredients and the combinations do seem weird but I promise so worth it!!  

The employees know exactly how each one is made so always ask first.

Smaller aquarium and brief visit while a first time and out of town visiter ended with getting parking validation....????  We felt dup'd/screwed. Validation means you don't pay to park when having your ticket validated.  Advertised that parking is validated and come to find out it was a $3.00 discount off a $35.00 parking fee. NEVER AGAIN!  I will be posting my compliant everywhere!! BEWARE folks!!

I wanted to like this. (Especially for the cost of admission which was well over $100 for our family of 4.) However, our experience was spotty. 

We enjoyed some aspects; the highlight was the fantastic art pieces created from trash that was washed on shore in the "Washed Ashore: Art to Save the Sea" exhibit. The art was impactful and the kids were really fascinated at the types of items that the artist used, as well as disturbed at how serious of an issue this is. I love that Audubon chose to display this wonderful art-- if my kids were interested in this very serious issue after seeing the impressive art, then surely, so too would others. 

What we didn't enjoy was that on the day we visited, the aquarium was overrun by field trips. Of course, kiddos and schools should visit the aquarium but it seemed that there had to have been fire codes broken by the sheer number of screaming kids. I seriously wondered if the capacity of the building was exceeded. It also only took an hour or two to go through the exhibits, and after paying so much money, we would have expected to want to spend more time there.

This was my first time trying Egyptian food and that was exciting in itself. The food was incredible. The flavors were balanced perfectly and the gyro meat melted in our mouths.  We ordered the eggplant platter and a side of gyro meat. They also have fresh made drinks including mint lemonade and a hibiscus rose water. Next time I return I'll try the Egyptian peach iced tea. 

PROS: Gyro meat
            Roasted Eggplant 
            Rice
            Hummus
            Hibiscus Rose water
            Mint lemonade
            Prices
The young man Nick at the register was professional and   quick, I feel like I can never figure out how to use all the promo stuff but he helped me save some cash and was friendly in the process.

Great place to visit when in the Big Easy. The kids will love it. Grand displays of local saltwater fish. Lots of fascinating information. Also, go to the insectarium down the street for some buggy fun!

I became obsessed with The Hyppo pretty quickly, and if it weren't for the 1016 miles separating us, I would probably be picking out a popsicle from there right now.  Don't pass this place up or tell yourself that "you don't need one."  Life is too short to deprive yourself of the best popsicles on the planet!
There was a lot of construction near the entrance when I went that was a tad aggravating, but this was a fairly cool place. Be sure to time it so you can watch an IMAX movie during your visit.

Where do I start! 
First the young man who owns the place is super thoughtful, super kind. He prepares your food like he is eating it! 

The upside bowl is sooooooooo good! Like one of the best Greek meals I've ever had! I could eat this twice a week! The eggplant and curry cauliflower is amazing! The chicken is seasoned so good too. I definitely recommend this place.

Surprising family find in the French Quarter! Must see! similar to Boston Aquarium, large. well worth it. plan on half a day at least, there are also animal shows and films here. cafe inside. Appropriate for all ages, we took our college aged son when dropping him off for school at Tulane. Everyone loved it. I'm a teacher and biologist; outstanding exhibit quality. Bravo to the staff. also nearby: World War II museum, Riverboat ride and Audobon Zoo (take St Charles trolley connection) and Insectarium. Elevators etc fully acessible. Good also to get out of the sun for awhile when hot or storming. NOLA 97% humidity and storming when we were there! Great find!  Parking lot and garages nearby (Weston hotel garage or outside lot) or accessible by trolley (Riverfront), also easily walkable from Cafe du Monde. Shopping also nearby. nice location. ps SHARK TUNNEL! and dont miss the upstairs rainforest habitat w/birds as well!

Just as yummy and wonderful as the location in Ybor! 
After a long walk (I'm horrible with directions), we stumbled upon this well-lit shop. 
The man behind the counter was very helpful with us, and the couple that entered behind us.
Ultimately, I chose a Peachy Peach and my boyfriend selected a Guava Hibiscus. I liked his better, but mine was yummy too! 

We've now stamped 4 out of 8 spots on our card, and we'll probably finish out the other four in the next couple of weeks!
Great tasting clean food made really fast, what else could you want? Amazing pita and dipping options. Everything was presented beautifully and seasoned well. We felt great after eating there.

Went for lunch with a group of 5 and waited over 40 minutes for my food. I'm so confused because BBQ is precooked... I go to Blue Oak and the food is out in less than 10 minutes. 

Seating is limited so it's not good for big parties. You order at the counter, pay, and sit at any table.

Anyways, on to the food. I ordered the 2 meat plate with one side. I got 2 ribs and brisket with a side of grilled asparagus. My plate also came with some kind of pumpkin muffin. The bbq was good but nothing to rave about. There are sauces offered on the side. I generally like my meat without sauce so that I could taste the seasonings, so I didn't really add any extra condiments. 

Might come back, might not. No strong feelings towards the restaurant.

I've been to this aquarium 3 times since 1995. This was my 3rd time in about 10 years and it is definitely not the same. The whole place is not as clean as it used to be, the water not as clear. The variety of animals has decreased. This is a VERY expensive trip for a family of four and there is not enough value for your money especially after you pay for parking which, by the way, the aquarium can only validate for $3 off your total cost, not $8 like the first aquarium staff member said, and not $5 like the staff member who validated the ticket said, it's just $3. I really couldn't see spending more than 2 hours here. I would only recommend this if you have never seen any other aquarium before or if you just have no clue what to do with kids in New Orleans. Save your money for the zoo, it is amazing and parking is free.

Excellent food. So refreshing after having heavy creole food. We got a veggie plate with hummus, dolmas, labneh, tahziki, babaghanoush, tabouleh, and a King Tut falafel, which was gigantic and has a hard boiled egg in the middle. The food is fresh and full of different but delicious flavor.

You could just read my review of the original Hyppo in St Auggie, however, I am sure you are too lazy to do that, so I'll sum up here.  Craft Popsicles might be the most urban progressivey thing ever created, and as such I want to hate them,. but I cannot deny my roots or the power of the Hyppo.

Seriously, the popsicles are "lit, fam," as the kids say today.  made with super fresh fruit juice they literally explode with flavor.  there's a good mixture of standard, no-nonsense flavors, the tart pink grapefruit is my fave, and adventurous ones, especially, several made with hot peppers that pack a kick.

The space is great, with a beautiful mural of the Skyway filled with Popsicles on the wall, and it's a great addition to a booming several blocks in the Edge district.

All natural, homemade popsicles that taste pretty darn good. I've been in quite a few times and I always take people here. Everyone I have brought loves it and then I get more stamps on my rewards card (mwahaha!). You get a free pop after 8 purchases.

They have so many flavors. I think they had over 30 the last time I was in. For whatever kind of mood you are in: fruity, chocolatey, spicy. Lots of cool flavor combos. They mark the ones that contain dairy. For $1 you can have your pop dipped in chocolate.

Staff are so helpful and nice in explaining some of the flavors that are more unique as well as recommending a pop based on what you are in the mood for. Seating inside as well as out. So refreshing, especially in the Florida heat.

Great place to visit! 

I only had 2 (minor)issues:
1. On the website it gives you a list of discounts that are available, one of them includes a $2 discount for each ticket if you work for the state of LA. When I showed my id, the cashier told me the only discount they offer is for military. Not a huge deal but just change the website to reflect that policy.
2. I wish they would give out a map at the beginning of the tour. It would've been helpful to make sure we didn't miss any exhibits.

Overall I recommend, my husband and I don't have kids and we really enjoyed ourselves.
I had the falafel wrap.  It was absolutely amazing.  So much flavor.  And the guy that runs the place is super nice.  This is my new favorite spot at St Roch market.

Hyppo has been a staple in my life since I moved to the Tampa Bay area four years ago. Okay, maybe that was an exaggeration, but we've been to five Hyppo locations and have always been pleased with our popsicles. My personal favorite is the Blackberry Goat Cheese one, and I'm having a hard time moving on to another flavor. I've also had a seasonal flavor at some point a couple of years back, it was the Chocolate with orange I believe, that I wish would come back. Everyone behind the counter gives pretty good suggestions depending on what type of flavor appeals to you. I'm so glad that they now have a few flavors in Publix!
Best falafel I have ever had!  Not too dry or oily. And I love they're mint lemonade.

I've gone here a couple of times and overall find it to be a nice little salon that basically will meet your needs.  They do hair, nails, coloring etc.  It's in a good location right next to Trader Joe's & Starbucks-- get my hair done, my coffee fix, and my shopping done at the same time  :-)

However, I've never had an "amazing" experience here.  It's pretty average and the service I receive is mediocre/ average.  Usually I've found that at any salon I've gone to-- the salons and the hair dressers are fairly average and the service is usually pretty average too.  

(I've only had one person in my entire life at another salon I went to who gave me an "amazing" hair cut and made me feel like a million bucks but she's long gone so can't go back to her.)

The first time I went here I asked for a specific style and even had a picture but the stylist couldn't do it.  The next time I went in the lady didn't seem to know how to cut my hair-- so overall not a spectacular experience but not bad either.

Overall though this is a decent place to go in a convenient location.

I visited the aquarium in October 2019. It was an enjoyable time, but I can't say it was very memorable. 

Be sure to order your tickets online to save a few dollars. It will also save you time from having to wait in line. When you arrive be prepared to have a photo opp right away before even entering. I skipped this step and just went inside. The lobby is kind of cool with the gift shop immediately to your right upon entering. The service desk was also in the lobby and I noticed how they offer some audio sensory headphones for children if needed. This seems like a good perk if you or someone you know has a family member who might be sensitive to noise. They had a few audio-sensory rooms to visit as well, if I am not mistaken. 

It does not take too long to walk through the aquarium. We moved at a good pace throughout and made it through in just under 2 hours. My group and I were sad that the shark exhibit was undergoing construction so we could not actually see many sharks. The best part of the aquarium was the giant tank with all the sea life and animals! I can't remember how many gallons the tank was, but I can say that it was impressive. I also enjoyed the area within the aquarium where there was an owl! Seriously a real-life owl was so cool to see up close! My friend's son was with us, and he loved being able to touch the sting rays! This was a good exhibit for kiddos. 

Overall, the aquarium was just a-ok for me. I look forward to the shark exhibit being open so that I can visit it again!

Want to touch and play with the ray?
Want to meet the African penguins?
Those are some of the activities that this place offer.
They also have some birds (parrots, owls, hawk...) flying around in the room. The horse sea are also really nice to watch.
Of course, big fishes and sharks are also part of the shows. And not forgetting the couple of otters that just want to play, so cute and funny to watch. 
With your admission you can also enjoy a movie about animals. Some of them are in 3D. The movie theater is just huge and really nice.
This aquarium offers a lot of feeding, activities and shows. But be ready to pay the price... really expensive tickets.

An interesting aquarium - not quite on par with the Monterey Aquarium or the National Aquarium in Baltimore, but worthwhile nevertheless.  I was told that it remained closed for about 8 months after Katrina, but it is up and running now.  I was probably going to give it 4 stars, but I witnessed one "educational" talk in the "Gulf" area - the so-called educator pointed to an empty and sandy section of the aquarium and said that the Gulf of Mexico used to be like this - empty, boring and no place for fish.  She then went on to explain that thanks to mankind's magnanimous introduction of oil derricks to the Gulf, marine life now has something to cling to and that the Gulf is much more lively and interesting now (post-oil derricks).  She further outdid herself by explaining that the big nasty government didn't understand how great the oil derricks were for the environment and had foolishly passed a big mean law that required the poor suffering servants of humankind, the oil companies, to dismantle the rigs when the wells ran dry.  Well, she said, thanks to the oil giants re-education of the government about the manifold benefits of the rigs, the law was amended and the rigs are now allowed to stay and foster marine life.  Of course, the exhibit was sponsored by all the big oil companies.  Hmmmmm....... something smells a little fishy here, if you will pardon the pun.  I may not be a rocket scientist, but I didn't just fall off the turnip truck either.

The baba ganoush here is fantastic!! I'd recommend them having an option for those who are gluten free and do not eat pita. Maybe celery, carrots, or gluten free pita? I had to get a salad on the side to eat the baba ganoush with something. But regardless of the slight inconvenience, I still enjoyed it.

Slow cashiers ...have no idea about customer service
Too busy gossiping to do their job

After seeing the growing popularity of this shop on Instagram and Facebook, I was glad to stumble on this place while exploring St. Pete. When we stopped in it was busy and the line was long. There was only one employee working but the line moved quickly. All of the popsicles are made with fresh fruit and vegetables. There are so many interesting options that it was difficult to choose just one.   

I chose the Riesling Pear and my friend chose the Datil Strawberry. Any of the popsicles can be chocolate dipped but we kept ours simple. The Riesling Pear was sweet overall but it did not have a distinct flavor. I would probably not order it again. My friend, however, liked the Datil Strawberry. It was strawberry with a bit of spice in the background. We enjoyed our popsicles and I would be interested in trying some of the other flavors in the future.

Well, J.S. didn't leave me much to add!  Yep, same experience for me -- except that Frank has been fixing my appliances even longer (at least 15 years).  Today's bit of fun was a front-loading dryer that was a two-man job due to its poor design.  I supplied some extra muscle, and he supplied the brains.  

I am actually a computer expert, so I have no need of Frank's services there.  But, talking to him about computer-related topics leaves me with no doubt that he knows his stuff.  

Bad news if you have the same model dryer I do, though -- after today's experience, I'm pretty sure that he no longer services that style!  :-)

Enjoyed eating there last nite - it's mostly Mona's menu plus 5 Egyptian items' The 10 people in my party each ordered a different dish and 100% were happy. (Few know about Lebanon and they so can't compare - and it doesn't come up to Lebanon standards.) Chef came out to chat which was great - he is Egyptian. I had an Egyptian dish - pretty good - that's a sticky rice in the middle and the same items and sauce as Ethiopian. nothing is spicy. the eggplant appetizer is the phenomenal food item. Portions and platters are huge. about $25 a head with tip.
TORSHI! Amazing food and the people who work here and super lovely. Definitely grab one of their signature drinks! The mango ginger will rock your socks offfffff
Thats interesting the other post said poor bedside manner, because I had the opposite experience I even told Dr. Oki he had a great bedside manner before reading the yelp reviews.

Penguins!!!  Need I say more?!

For an extra fee, $125, you can interact with actual penguins!!!
First, you learn a lot about penguins from the very knowledgable trainers and then you get to actually pet 2 of the friendliest penguins in a small room.  They are adorable little creatures!!!  Then you and these 2 penguins waddle into the actual penguin habitat within the aquarium and be surrounded by 40 penguins and actually feed them. 

This was a very unique experience and worth the $$$.
Though I did get pecked once, penguins are still one of my favorite animals!

Oh and the group is very small, I believe it is a max of 6 people that can sign up each exhibit.   This is great so that each one of you can really interact with the penguins.  At the end, you can also tour and explore the aquarium, which is part of the fee.

Some fun facts that I learned: 
- They like shiny, dangly items, just like a cat.
- They make these unique, weird noise when they're happy, sort of like a donkey braying. 
- Penguins molt once a year, which is when they lose their feathers and regrow them.  Before this process, they overstock on food and gain weight since they cannot go into the waters while molting.

The 200 degree chicken breast was fairly spicy and came from the kitchen quite steamy. I had the baked beans as a side. The beans are sweet and not spicy and I found them to be pretty tasty. The bird was a bit lacking in the meat department. I wouldn't call it fast food since my order took 25 minutes to arrive. Not a bad experience, but I've had better and the atmosphere being an austere food court with Quizno's and another vendor left me longing for a local dive with funky wall hangings.
Don't bother. Go to Target. This store is disorganized and trying to return something is a hassle.
Best place in the Reno/Truckee area for woodworkers. They have all the major brands: festool, makita, etc. lots of bits, blades, etc.
We wanted something light for dessert and landed here. We both had tipsy pops. So refreshing! We'll be back to try all the flavors.

LOVE Dr Oki and his ultrasound tech June!! They've kept such a close eye on my high risk twins, and are always so helpful when it comes to my questions.. Dr Oki is very smart and definitely knows what he's doing

First off, they get a 5 for flavor.  These things are the bomb.  Their problem, and it truly IS a serious problem, is they don't know how to manage the availability of their more popular flavors, namely Orange Cream and Chocolate Sea Salt.  If I had a dollar for every time they're out of those, I could buy a franchise...which I wouldn't, because then people would be mad at me because corporate wouldn't get me enough Orange Cream and Chocolate Sea Salt.
