It truly is frustrating that they are CONSTANTLY out of those 2 flavors.  They need to realize that they need to make MORE of those than the Asphalt Fiberglass Kale or the Leather Kelp Acetaminophen.

Who doesn't love Popsicles? They have a wide variety of flavors from bourbon peach to banilla vanilla.  So yummy! We've been back a few times and always have something different.  They're right downtown so go in for a treat after lunch.  

And they were super sweet with my 1.5 year old and didn't mind him making the place his own.  Very cool staff!

My friends rave about this place so, I had to check it out. Its located in a small food court setup and I was confused for 15 seconds. LOL! However, I went to place my order. I ordered a breast with one side. They make your food fresh so you are going to be waiting. They give me two breasts because they didn't have their normal size that day. The 200 degrees level was perfect for me. Hot but not going to kill your spirit. LOL! The chicken was fried perfectly. Crispy. Crunchy. Perfect level of hot. Overall, great chicken and great service. The owner is a alumnus of Tennessee State just like myself. I salute her and her great business. I will always come back.

We usually come here once or twice a year, and actually made it during Harvest Festival this year for the Brandywine Valley Wine Trail tour.

I'm not much of a wine drinker, but I've found I like sweet wines like the Niagara.  Not a big fan of the Shangri-La Sangria, Spiced Apple, or the reds in general.

The place is pretty easy to get to with a lot of outdoor seating and acoustical music weather permitting.  The inside can get pretty cramped, but it's not too bad.  Tastings are fairly cheap; however, they're really stingy with the samples...  You get a glass though, so it's not all bad.  LOL

Man, I love The Hyppo. I wish I didn't only because I shouldn't be eating as many popsicles as I do!

Where to begin!? I didn't know anything about The Hyppo until I moved to Central Avenue. I walked inside and was already excited. So. Many. Popsicles. Where to begin? Well, for me I'm a strawberry guy, but they have more than just strawberry. In addition to standard strawberry there is strawberry lemonade, strawberry lemonade, strawberry cheesecake, and strawberry basil. I'm in heaven.

One of the perks of coming here; they have a frequent shopper card or a punch card system. If you buy 8 you get one free. Which for me won't take long. 

One thing I love is they have cooler totes which I got for $4 to carry your popsicles home without them melting. That being said, they wrap them normally in an insulated bag so that way they're double insulated.

The Hyppo has dairy and dairy free pops.

Some of my overall favorites are: blackberry limeade, straight up strawberry, and pineapple orange.

The staff here is so nice! Every one of them always so friendly. I just love it here. As soon as I walk in I'm happy and that's really all you can ask for, right? And really, who doesn't love a popsicle?

Food is soooo good! 9/10 times I eat at st Roch market I order from Torshi. And the employees are always super sweet about adding something a little extra if you request it (like extra seasoning). Today the owner, I presume, even came out and brought us some dessert on the house after our meal.
The aquarium was OK. But way overpriced for what it is. I was disappointed with the size of the exhibits for the price. But it is a great rainy day activity for the kids (just overpriced)

Just left Bath and Bodyworks empty-handed. Not one employee acknowledged me as I walked the entire store.......Left the store after the two employees who watched me walk in fell over themselves to greet people who came in behind me.

OTTERS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
I could sit there and watch them swim and play all day if I had the time. I remember going here as a kid and I hadn't been back in a while so I decided to check it out.  They have a lot of great exhibits and it is definitely worth a visit on hot day in New Orleans. Check out my tip to see on how to avoid those long lines out in the heat for tickets.

We ordered a variety of heat levels and meat types (dark, light, and tenders). Overall, the chicken is made to order, taste fresh, hot, and prompt service. However, there are better options for hot chicken in town that are better seasoned, and more juicy. The sides of beans and potato salad are standard fare.

This is a nice aquarium, but nothing really special.  It was very crowded on the recent Sunday afternoon when we visited.  My family of 6 lives in San Antonio, and we have been to the Texas State Aquarium in nearby Corpus Christi, which is probably slightly better than the Aquarium of the Americas.  An overall enjoyable experience (particularly the Rainforest exhibit and the oil platform area), but not as clean, unique and stimulating as the Insectarium.

This place is AWESOME! I placed a large to-go order (15 people) online and they were super accommodating every step of the way. When I came in to pick up the order, everything was ready, labeled, and neatly packed. The owner even helped me to my car. The food was delicious! I couldn't choose between the brisket and pulled pork, so I got the 2 Meat Plate. The  sauce was delicious with just the right amount of kick. Loved it, loved it, loved. Best BBQ I've had in New Orleans since I moved here from Texas ten years ago!
Maybe I'll just have to try it again another day to see what the hype is about... the brisket was very dry and the beans were flavorless

Great food and AMAZING tea!! Plus the service was OUTSTANDING! I went 2 days in a row and both employees were absolutly friendly, bubbly, and nice!!! Genuine people and food is soooo goood! Definatly vome back here if I'm ever in LA again!!!

I expected a little more out of the Aquarium, especially since it was sooooo expensive. I'm okay with paying the price if they have the exhibits to justify it. There wasn't much to the Aquarium, you could honestly finish it in about an hour (without any kids and if you care to read the signage about the animals). It's also extremely crowded there. A lot of kids were there because it was the weekend and it was a stroller nightmare. Parents bumping their strollers into each other, in the way of other people, it was just a mess. 

I would see the WWII museum first and if you have time left, come to see the Aquarium.

This place is brand new and it is fantastic. The hummus wrap is delicious and filling, the feta cheese is an amazing side, the drinks are fresh and cold. This is a nice change of pace in a city that is full of wonderful food places. 

The owner is amazingly friendly, and you can tell how happy he is to share his food with the world.

If you eat here, make sure that you are hungry. This food is filling and delicious. 

I will be back for sure.

Love, love, love!  Creative, delicious and refreshing! So many to choose from. I tried the watermelon hibiscus and it was surprisingly flavorful. Insulated freezer bags to keep them cold if you want to take some home.

Happened up on Saucy's today! Best treat ever! The brisket was melt in your mouth good!  I also had the baked mac & cheese and grilled asparagus...sooo good!  So check it out, you can actually buy a rib for $2.50 each!  The sauce..oh my goodness,   is called Fantasy Sauce and it lived up to it's name. My plate was served witb horseradish and Fantasy sauce. Great combination. Well I loved it so much, I purchased a 1/2 pound of brisket and am on the way to have my friends sample. The hospitality was super friendly. Way to Geaux Saucy's!!

Lets start with the price.  $30 a head.  Well lets see if it was worth it.

First, right before you enter they funnel you through a picture taking station that you stand in front of a green screen so they can get you to buy a picture of yourself before you even enter.  They should do away with that.  The guy took one look at me and said "you dont want a picture do you?"  I laughed and told me that he was correct.

You enter and the gift shop is directly to your right.  Did you catch that they already charged us 30 bucks and they seem to be really wanting more money.

The aquarium is actually really cool.  A ton of fish and other sea creatures,  They have an alligator on exhibit as well as a few sea otters.  The parakeet room felt like you were standing in a giant home bird cage.  Watching a guy try and feed them with the sick of food he purchased for 1.50 was entertaining.  The penguins were fun to watch as they ate breakfast.

They seem to be in the middle of an expansion or a remodel which should be pretty cool when they get done.  

It seems to be a very well organized place.  The volunteers were just kids that looked uncomfortable at the exhibits.  I didn't even bother trying to ask them any questions.  I thought it might scare them.  The surrounding area around the aquarium has its share of the homeless population.  We did not have to park a car but we did have to walk the general area and parking seems to be an issue in that area.

All in all its a three star place.  too expensive but a cool place to go.

This aquarium packs a punch. It is smaller but there is plenty to see and experience. Part of the museum is being renovated for a new exhibition with sharks but it was still fun for the kids. They do have the option to purchase a penguin or sea lion experience but they sell out fast and are very limited per day. We were able to pet stingrays and watch them get fed by a diver. We saw an albino alligator and some live parakeets, hawk, and owl. It was near for the kids and I'm sure will be even better when the shark exhibit opens.

Frank is a nice guy and knows his stuff, as he has been doing this for 50 years.   He also knows all of the angles, like a pool shark.  

My oven and broiler stopped working on my Whirlpool.  He immediately went to the igniter and replaced it.  But the Oven and broiler still did not work.   He said it may be the thermostat (dial).  It was.   

He and I looked online and found it for $60, and I ordered it.  He explained to me how to install it myself.  Then he charged me $223 for 40 minutes,  and to replace the wrong part.   He said if I want, he would come back to install it, and charge me more 

Thank you for nothing.

Smaller than other aquariums I've been to, this aquarium provides a nice change of pace from touring along the noisy, hot, and humid streets. There is a good assortment of creatures to view, and what I'll call "trash sculptures" are an interesting touch. 
The price for admission is quite steep (~$20-30), so I suggest going for the "Audubon Experience" for $45, which includes aquarium, insectarium, zoo, and one movie at their theatre.

The best part of discovering the St. Roch Market was discovering Torshi Egyptian. I spent some time in Egypt some years ago, and this is the closest I've come in the United States to eating an authentic Egyptian meal. It's clear that the owner puts his heart and soul into the food he prepares, and it was worth every cent. My wife and I will go out of our way to come back here.

Wow. Stumbled on this place while picking up some records up the street! Such a gem.

Their flavor selection seems infinite. Seriously. Selecting a flavor was so difficult with all the flavorful, creative options available. I went with Plum Mint, and let's just say, I'm writing this review with the taste in my mouth still.  It was delicious, with fruit pieces in it. My fiancé got the Peachy Peach and enjoyed as well.

Very clean atmosphere and great customer service. Hope to be back here soon again!

If you like your nails a certain way I wouldn't go here!!
 I visited this location after being referred by a girl that i work with. Turned out to be a bad idea . I wanted a full set and pedicure (the pedicure was ok but i couldn't enjoy it because the nail tech thought it was a good idea to do my nails at the same time. So i had to sit in a semi awkward position and hold the gel nail dryer in my lap. I specifically told the guy Mike i wanted French tip coffin shape and that i wanted my nails to be straight not curved. He basically did the opposite of what i asked and my nails turned out to be shitty. Would never go back here to get my nails done. The staff were nice tho ig smh

Extremely disappointed. We walked in at 1pm. At 145, while having a snack we were told that the whole aquarium is closing due to weather. Because we didn't just enter we were not able to get refunded. My daughter and I saw a total of 2 exhibits before heading upstairs to the food court. Can't say if it was amazing or not.. just know that the brash, rude security and poor policy for closing left a bad taste in our mouth.

Great place to try ribs! Awesome sides and better folks.
Note: They don't sell alcohol

Three couples visited for wine and beer. We were late but graciously served. I drank beer it was unexpectedly very good. Others all had a sweeter wine and no one complained. Special searing here with leather couches and armed chairs. We will return for a longer stay. Staff was extremely accommodating.

Such a fun place! The aquarium offers a nice break from the New Orleans heat. There are several hands on activities for both adults and children. We visit every time we are in New Orleans and enjoy watching the aquarium grow and add new and unique experiences.

I bought the Audubon Experience which allows you to visit the Audubon Zoo, Audubon Aquarium of the Americas and Audubon Butterfly Garden and Insectarium. Plus you get to see a short film at the Entergy Giant Screen Theater at the Aquarium. The Audubon Experience ticket was $44.95 (plus sales tax) for Adult which I think is a good price. Buying it individually is too expensive/ not worth it. I thought the aquarium was a cute fun place for kids. If you are a teenager or adult you will get bored pretty quickly. The aquarium is small and not much to see compare to other aquariums in the country. I feel they aren't utilizing their spaces correctly. For example next to the stingray section there was a huge empty space. They should add more chairs there or more bathrooms or more food vendors or even better... more animal displays. I'm surprised by how little animals they had. Alot of boring fish in boring tanks. One of the highlights of the visit was petting the stingrays (that was free) and feeding them 2 shrimps. That cost $2 extra. Tickets can be purchased at the gift shop near the stingrays. Also the Cuba short-film that they played at the theater was awesome. They should be promoting that film more. Wow. So good. Wish it was longer. I love it. The only thing that was a bit surprising was that the theater was outside of the aquarium so you had to walk few minutes. The parakeet feeding was nice, but because i went later in the afternoon their bellies were all full; so they didn't want to eat and were sleeping. The meal options for us were horrible only a cafe, papa johns, and a hot dog stand. Overall this aquarium is definitely not "a must see" but if you have kids or need to waste some hours then come here. Also i would love to see them use a more natural washable ink pad. My hand stamp has lasted for days. I have literally wash/scrubbed it with all types of things and it just won't come off. It's driving me nuts seeing this blue blob on my hand.

Let me begin by saying I have loved this store for a long time. 

I recently went in to buy supplies and was distressed by a lack of masks and social distancing in the store. I sent the owners an email telling them what I experienced and that, given that I am around immune compromised people that I would regretfully have to take my business online, though I much prefer shopping locally. 

The response I got from one of the owners goes so far beyond my expectations that I was stunned. He explained the difficulties based on the nature and layout of the store. He said they would continue to work on improving their systems. He also gave me alternative shopping options for the store that we so appreciated. 

This is the kind of local store and service that we need more of in this country. I'm not a big fan of huge chains and big box stores and always prefer to shop at small, local businesses. This one is at the top of my list now. 

If you need anything this store offers, don't hesitate to shop here. If you, like I, are concerned about exposure, call or email them. They will go above and beyond the call to help make shopping there work for you!!  

If I could give them 6 stars I would.

BEST ROASTED EGGPLANT EVERRRRRRR. The eggplant dip at @torshi_egyptian_food is my absolute favorite! If you're at @strochmarket you've gotta get this dish. I know what you're thinking... eggplant? Seriously? You can't be that excited about eggplant! Well, I am  -
Torshi strives to serve amazing Egyptian food and their food & staff are so so so great!

It's an adorable little hole in the wall on Magazine Street.  Really great BBQ, and an excellent friendly staff. 

I moved recently to New Orleans and wanted something yummy after wandering down Magazine Street.  A shopkeeper pointed me over to Saucy's, and thank god she did!  The interior is small, divey, and there is limited seating, but I was able to snag a table by the window.  I grabbed a menu, browsed it, and placed my order at the counter.  I ordered a pulled pork sandwich with the goat cheese Mac and grilled asparagus.  The sauce that came with the sandwich was spicy and sweet - a perfect compliment to my creamy Mac and cheese.  Get the goat cheese Mac - it's life changing!  The grilled asparagus is kind of a funky option for a BBQ joint, but it worked well with everything. 

Apparently, Saucy's is well-known around town and I'm glad I discovered this local secret.

Who doesn't love aquariums? Yes, my husband and I go to different aquariums and zoos in different cities whether we have our kids or not. I think they are fun and something nice to explore. After we walked around the Riverwalk Outlet, we explored the aquarium. It was nice and we seemed to walk through it fast. I'd say it took us about 1.5 hrs. We looked at all the exhibits, took pictures and just spent time together. This was a pretty good aquarium. The exhibits were nice and clean! It also was not to packed. That is the worse when at a aquarium or zoo is when it's overly packed. Overall, my husband and I had a good time and enjoyed our experience.

Beautiful! The workers are very friendly and love to teach which is wonderful. The exhibits are set up in a way that leads you through intuitively. Even on crowded days most of the views are unobstructed.  Don't miss penguin feeding time and be sure to see the otters!  There is a lovely room about halfway through where you have benches where you can sit and relax and watch the sharks and other large fish swim all around you in dim lighting which is very relaxing.  The facility was kept very clean.  We did not watch the movie and it took us about two hours to go through which was a good value for the price in my opinion.  If you buy your tickets online and show the code at the door you get a discount so make sure you do that.
The popsicles are delicious!!! Many wonderful and amazing flavors!! They even have "to-go" bags to get some for later!! Lol

I give Kohl's a 0 for online shopping. For the 2nd time ordering shoes I received them and they were already used by somebody else. Apparently they don't check the shoes before they send them out it's absolutely disgusting.
One of the smallest aquariums we've ever been in. We were in and out in just over an hour. The animal exhibits are beautiful, but not really worth it price-wise.

Amazing selection and quality of products! Very unique and refreshing concept. A bit pricey but worth it because everything is made from scratch and sourced from local fruit growers. 

Pablo was very welcoming and knowledgeable for our first visit and also gave us lots of tasty samples

After many recommendations, my husband and I ventured here with our kids and nephew. I have only been to one aquarium in the past, in Virginia and compared to that one, this one is a little small. My kids had fun! They especially loved the alligator exhibit and the sharks! I liked seeing the owl and walking through the tunnel. There are definitely a lot of things for kids including a pretty big gift shop. The aquarium itself is really clean but a bit crowded. The lines were also a bit long. The food in the restaurant part was pricey as expected but decent tasting. All in all, I think it's a good place to take your family for a day our. It's also really convenient to the river walk so if you're not in the area often i would definitely take advantage of both. We look forward to seeing the Audubon zoo next!

Feb 08 2018:  Datil cheesecake
Creamy but with a definite pepper flora flavor
Very good

Feb 08: watermelon jalapeño Rita
Very light flavor...great for a hot summer day
Not a flavor explosion nor much heat

Feb 10:  Blackberry clove...ohh yeah!   A hit!

Feb 13 Maple Mamey
Feb 17 Pine upside down....sinus congestion put a slight damper on my flavor nodes but still good!

April  29
Mex Hot Chocolate 
Ohhhhh yeah!!!  Spicy hot choc....frozen
There is no better

Do not go for the spicy dry rub sprinkled at the end.  Too gritty.  Chicken was overcooked... I understand going beyond done to insure food safety but my chicken was drier than a popcorn f*rt.

Only hot chicken joint on this side (downtown) of the river, a shame, now I am stuck driving to E. Nasty.

Selling jars of spice mix for $20.00... you must be crazy.

I thought it was okay; I've been to a lot of aquariums and Audubon was mediocre. It was smaller than most aquariums and the displays weren't that "wow." I really like seeing the penguins feeding time and there was a touchable sting ray pond. It took about a little over a hour to finish the aquarium because it was pretty small.

I'm giving him 3 stars because he is very knowledgeable, but also his bed side manner isn't the greatest. I got sent to him because of my age and almost every appt he seemed to find something wrong with my baby. He pushed the amnio almost every time which I declined. He even asked me if I was thinking of terminating if something was wrong with my baby. First appt he said my baby might have Down syndrome, I left crying, second appt he said my baby might have a disability, I left crying, at the last appt he said my baby might have a defect in her throat, I left crying. I am thankful that all these precautions were taken when my baby was born, but after running tests on her she is one healthy baby.

It's June in Louisiana and it's HOT!  This place has A/C, woohoo! I was able to experience this place for the first time through the eyes of my 12 year old daughter. Our favorites? The otters, penguins and jellyfish. 
Beat the heat and get to the aquarium. Just don't plan to eat there. High priced chicken fingers and Papa John's pizza slices. There's way too many places near by with excellent food and good prices to pay for below average here.

Made appointments for 9am for my mother-in-law and sister-in-law to get there hair done to attend a wedding. Arrived on time, one of the stylist was there he sat at the desk and took our name then sat there for ten minutes. We discussed the right time schedule we were on. 9:15 I asked if he couldn't fide our appointment. He answered that he sees the but was trying to figure out the system. Finally he took my sister in-law back to do her hair. I asked at 9:30 about the stylist for my mother-in-law. His answer, "yay that stylist called in sick, I tried to get another stylist in but couldn't. I think I'm just going to have to do both". Why didn't he tell us in the beginning? The website said it would take 25-30 minutes. He finished with my sister in-law at 9:50am. If he new the other stylist was unavailable and someone was waiting for a 9 am appointment that wasn't going to be seen until an hour later he should have said that in the beginning and let us make the choice to stay or go somewhere else. 

Aside from that he was kind and did a good job on both women's hair.
Love this place! Just wish they had Nutella Popsicles all the time, they are amazing!

Considering it costs $22.50 for general admission I expected alot more. The place was so small I thought I had gotten turned around and possibly skipped something but I hadn't. The only thing I really enjoyed was the huge shark tank. There was a barracuda and some really large fish in there as well. The penguins were out which was nice but I just can't get over having to fight people to see anything. There are $3 coupons you can print to get the price of admission down a bit. Overall it was something to do but I wouldn't be excited to go back.

I received a gel polish and it started peeling off the next day. 3 days after several of my nails have already chipped :(. The nail salon I usually go to my gel nails last at least 2 weeks and it's $10 cheaper. Do not recommend this place.

UPDATED - 9/28/2016
I'm so disappointed. It had been a while since I've been here and when we came, it wasn't the same at all. The tanks are nice and large, however, the parakeet exhibit has gone down hill. The netting is in front the plants - basically teasing the birds where they cannot get to them. The feeding stick prices went up to $1.50 from $1, which isn't bad except the food portion is drastically smaller. You used to get a full or half stick of food. You now get a speck of food at the tip of the stick. Literally the speck is about the size of my 2 year Olds thumb. On top of that, they have ads of various paid options plastered throughout the whole aquarium. Where the shark gulf tank is, for example, where they have the circle glass where you can look down and see the sharks, there were 2 other glass walls to view that tank on the 2nd floor. Those 2 glass walls are now covered with an advertisement. Like I said, the place is beautiful, it's clean, friendly staff, but these changes are very disappointing and a let down. Definitely won't be coming back any time soon though.


 original review 

Huge! Lots to see, fun & educational for the whole family. Prices are pretty high though unless you have a membership than it's free.

Great visit. Friendly staff. We must have hit it lucky wasn't that crowded. Cool exhibits. Friendly staff. Went early in the day. Bought pass to the zoo and insectarium too. Left at noon to see the movie included in our pass. Then walked down to get beignets and coffee and walk around the touristy areas. Came back and closed the places down to finish up the day. Nice break from the heat.

They have the freshest ingredients in their pops which add a bucket of flavor in your mouth. 

I firstly got the blueberry lavender lemonade pop and it was even better than I had imagined. As a lavender lover it can be a hit or miss on not getting the proportion right but it was just as tart as it was calming.  

The second pop I got ( because one just isn't enough) was a cranberry apple. The cranberry apple was texturally a bit like apple sauce which I didn't mind and actually loved. A woman I went with had the same pop and the flavor was great for her but the texture was a 6/10. 

They also have a rewards program for a free pop and I'm also thankful for the opportunity to get free food. This is my favorite place to get popsicles in downtown St.pete

I'm not a big fan of dress barn everything is so pretty and organize at each dress barn I've been too , this one doesn't have to long that it's been open but everyone seems really nice and it feels so happy and unique in the inside . Really excited to see how this location goes
Such a delicious gyro wrap I had today. Really hit the spot. Very fresh! And this place is located in the coolest food market. Will definitely be back!!

Popped in for a drink with my wife while waiting out one of the storms on Saturday and as always when we visit we had a very pleasant experience. Greeted with a hello and a smile from the woman behind the bar and she explained the tastings and the specials. My wife loved the sangria slushee as we walked around and checked out the wines available. If you're visiting the village you should definitely stop by and try a tasting.

I use to go get my nails done here, for years but they don't do coffin shape or glamorous nail looks. But they are a very clean salon, and did my Nails pretty! I'm thinking I should go back, because I'm over coffin nails now...I want my square shape back with pride and sophistication lolbvs
Came here with my mom post COVID lockdown and staff was super clean and helpful. Ask for the lady who is the owner. She gives amazing pedicures. Could be a little pricey, but worth it!

Located in the St. Roch Market. We didn't try any of the food here but we stopped to look at the juices and when we did the guy working there offered for us to try it. He went on to give us samples of each of the juices he offered such as the Mint Lemonade,   Egyptian Punch, Mango Ginger Lemonade, and Hibiscus Tea. All of them were very refreshing and really tasty. He also said that everything was made that morning and is made fresh daily. We got the Mango Ginger Lemonade in which has chunks of ginger in it, it was amazing other than the strings of the ginger.

I would definitely check this place out.

When I was in this store one of the workers (Mike) from what i saw on his name tag kept staring at me. I didn't notice until my boyfriend pointed it out. Even after making eye contact with him I kept catching him looking at me and it made me highly uncomfortable. I would not shop alone here when this guy is working.
I get a gel mani pedi done here monthly with Melissa! She is the best! My favorite thing is the cat eye gel nail polish.

When I've had a bad day and I need my fix like a crack addict needs theirs, I head to 400°. It's always a cathartic experience, quite therapeutic. I always get a 400° breast with fries and extra pickles. Sometimes she makes it a little bit hotter for me and that sends me into twitching, orgasmic convulsions where my toes will curl up and my eyes will roll to the back of my head. I'm here 1-2 times a week, on average.

Reno Maternity Care and Dr. Earle Oki put my life and my baby's life in danger.  If I could give zero stars as a review, I would. They did not listen to me as a patient. They bullied me into signing paperwork that didn't match my wishes. Dr. Oki did not do his job thoroughly and missed a 3.5x2x3 inch growth inside my uterus during his examination. I believe they broke HIPPA and the last straw was when I was verbally assaulted by the office staff. For the safety of you and your baby or babies, stay as far away from them as possible. If a provider of yours refers you to them, I would ask yourself if you want to be cared for by a physician who would support an office who abuses their patients.

This was a nice great if you bring kids. It took about an hour and a half to see everything with no children. If you have been to the Brooklyn aquarium this one is smaller more similar in size to the central park zoo.
Great aquarium. We had loads of fun only wished the shark exhibit was open. Loved the seal show and the staff were very friendly.

This aquarium is a good place to visit.
It is not too large but packs a large variety
of displays into an efficient space.

They mix a little history and bird watching
in with the aquatic displays which breaks up
the monotony and adds interest.

Terrible. I had an appointment today and I am driving all the way from Gardnerville Nevada. Due to Covid they're not allowing anybody in and my husband is gone for the moment for work. So I'm driving myself and I'm basically a one-man show, and certainly not feeling well at all! 
On my way up to my appointment that was at 11 AM today I got sick and had to pull over on the side of the road, rushing to a bathroom. I then started to make my way to the doctors office,in which I was already in Reno, and they called me asking if I was still coming in. I told them yes I'm in Reno right now I'll be there 5 to 10 minutes. The receptionist told me they were going to have to reschedule because my appointment was at 10:30. Now in hysterics crying also because I am hormonal I told her that's ridiculous I'm barely going to be late, you told me yesterday my appointment was at 11. The receptionist then argued back telling me no it was 10:30, no. 
Little does the receptionist know my husband who's gone on work, was on the phone with me overhearing the conversation with the reactions it's yesterday, therefore I had a witness that the receptionist told me my appointment was at 11. 
This is my first pregnancy I've been very very sick and I'm considered a high-risk pregnancy because I have an abnormality of my uterus. So after waiting three weeks for an appointment, being extremely hormonal, not feeling well, and a one-man show temporarily for my entire first trimester, I definitely did not respond in a polite way, which I do regret. However, I have never been so mistreated and the fact that I drove all the way from Gardnerville sick as hell, excuse my language, and was really looking forward to this appointment. I'm sure that the doctor knows what he's doing, but their patient care is absolutely horrid they will no longer be my doctor, in fact I have ever met them so I guess it doesn't matter. In order to reschedule  I was going to have to wait another two or three weeks to be seen, as a high-risk pregnancy patient. I absolutely do not recommend them unless you want to be treated absolutely terribly, when you're already feeling terrible in your first trimester.

Great aquarium, diverse sections representing a cross section of aquatic life and of course a gift shop. Not five star because the experence was a little short but you can stay as long as you like and could read the information on the sea life so really it last as long as you have interest. Large aquarium host a few sharks and other species unable to be contained in smaller facilities. This is in an area that is nice to explore with shopping and casino nearby also. I would advise to not park in this area and just get an Uber from wherever you are staying or park further into the business district.

Just left this place.  My boyfriend and I waited 45 minutes for food.  We ordered the Cochon bleu sandwich and the brisket with Mac n cheese and baked beans.  When we got the food it was cold.  We brought this to the attention of one of our servers, and were told we could leave.  So we're at Theo's down the street.  I'd rather have pizza on Labor Day than be disrespected for BBQ.  We won't be returning, ever!

Wonderful experience at the aquarium. Smaller than most but good exhibits.  The parakeet exhibit is something special and definitely with going there just to see them.  If you time your visit appropriately you can see some specialty movies and watch feeding times.   The museum is very noisy and crowded as it's a big attraction for children.  While they do have sensory packs and "quiet areas" these are limited and don't always have seating.  This is why I ranked it 4 stars. Overall with the time And price.

Was at the WWOZ Fund Drive event where Saucy's catered dinner and wow was it a treat. They gave us volunteers a great salad, jerk chicken breast, and the best beef brisket I have ever had and a mixed baked beans I have never had before. The salad was plentiful with a great Italian dressing, the jerk chicken was good and made a nice chicken salad if you wanted to. The stars of the show were the brisket and beans. The brisket was the most tender I had ever had, trimmed and pink. It was perfect in every way. One of the biggest problems I have with alot of BBQ places in New Orleans is the lack of great sides but the beans were excellent. Reds, and all kinds of whites and limas all mixed and baked together again they were excellent. This makes me want to go back and try the brisket again. Wow was I blown away.

This review is only for the movie theatre which is right adjacent to the aquarium with its own separate entry and exit doors. We had a rather alarming experience here of being locked inside the theatre while watching the movie which is huge security and safety risk considering there are little kids inside the theatre. Even bigger issue is that some of the staff admitted that the doors are locked after movie starts and supervisor Whitney who I asked to talk to after this incident completely denied they do this. 

This is what happened:

We went in for the 4 pm show and we were right on time. There were two guys standing outside the theatre who checked our tickets and handed out the 3 D glasses. After 10 mins or so of watching the movie we decided to leave since I needed to use the restroom and my toddler was getting really restless. We go to the exit and find the doors closed. We try to open it and realize its locked!!! 

We then started pounding on the door in the hope that somebody outside would hear us and let us out but looks like nobody was outside. After 5 mins of banging on the double doors, we decided to exit through the emergency exit doors right behind us while worrying all the while if we are going to set off any alarms. But no alarms went off thankfully and the doors led us out to the back of the building and we had to use an emergency exit gate to get out of the building( the alarm did sound then but did not look like anyone really noticed). 

We then had to walk all the way around the building to the main entry and when I went back into the theatre I noticed the doors were still locked and there was nobody outside. I then walked over to a staff lady standing near the food counters and asked her about the doors. She said " oh" and went inside an adjacent room to tell someone and then I turned around to see the theatre doors being opened from the inside by one of the guys who let us inside the theatre before the show. 

That guy admitted to locking the doors and said they do that so people just don't walk into the movie theatre without tickets etc and when I asked what if somebody needs to leave to use restroom the guy says ," Oh, I will let them out! " I told him that we were banging on the doors for so long and nobody let us out. The guy was not even standing outside the movie theatre where he needs to be especially if they lock the doors but seemed to be hanging out at the back/ restricted area of the building possibly taking a break since that is where he emerged from. 

I asked to talk to the supervisor about this incident and what a big security and safety risk it was!!! While she was nice enough to come over right away she completely denied they locked the doors!!!! 

Another staff member who my husband complained to about this incident actually said that the theater people have been locking doors lately so as to not allow walk outs/ in's and keep people inside for the entire movie!!!

I'm from Virginia and have been living in town while I go to school. I'm sad to be leaving this month, knowing that I don't have a place like Tom's back home! They've serviced my car several times over the last couple years and I'm more impressed with every visit. They always fit me in, even when it's last minute (which is usually is) and they never make me feel like a "dumb girl," which so many automotive places do. I found them based on a yelp review and haven't regretted it, so hopefully my review helps someone else!

GO EAT HERE! The chef is crazy talented (and a super fun guy to talk to). The babaganush and tzatziki are the best I've ever had. I'd also recommend the lamb thighs and the kibbie. They just moved to a new location on Frenchman Street. Fingers crossed they stay there, because it's walking distance to my house XD

We arrived late and the girl at the desk told us they were only open for another 90 minutes. We only needed 30. The building itself is beautiful as are a few of the exhibits, but most of them have no signage indicating what is in each tank, many tanks are empty, and there is no overall flow through the exhibits.  I was utterly disappointed. When we were ready to leave we couldn't find the exit. No wonder the place was so empty. Save your money and go to the Shedd Aquarium in Chicago instead.

Heartbroken and angry - I reported them to animal welfare. The penguin exhibit is SAD they can't move or swim, it's complete robbery - where is the ticket money going toward?
The shark exhibit is overcrowded with large fish that have to swim in order to breathe, these poor creatures, my heart breaks for them. Please don't support this, it's animal cruelty in disguise.

All I have to say is that Dr Oki is wonderful! He really takes the time to answer any questions you have during your ultrasound and also explains what he is doing and looking for. He has great bedside manner which is always a plus. 
There was an extra long wait but that's what happens when you're in a doctors office sometimes. When I went back he apologized for the wait which I found very nice of him considering I understand when emergencies occur or when an appointment may take longer than expected. I hope people can understand that this can be very scary if there is something wrong and considering his bedside manner, I see him taking extra time when necessary. 
The blood work can be done in office or at lab Corp and of course he gives you options based on your insurance. 
The staff is very pleasant and helpful when signing in and discussing billing. The phlebotomist was quick and thorough and also very pleasant. 
I would recommend him to anyone who needs to see a perinatologist!

Disappointing in comparison to the Chattanooga, TN Aquarium & the Atlanta, GA Aquarium. The displays seemed dated and had poor lighting and/or foggy glass. The jellyfish displays were very disappointing.

Insanely amazing popsicles! These need a better word since they are not mearly popsicles. They are in a league all of their own. So. Many. Flavors. Dare I say too many? It was so hard to decide. We each got one and then me and my 2 boys had to get a 2nd. Yes, 7 popsicles. My poor husband dropped $30 on popsicles and knows we can't wait to go again. We had Meyer lemon cream, key lime, orange cheesecake, strawberry cheesecake, coconut, espresso, and a mango/raspberry/banana called Phoenix. All great. Flavors of the fruit shine, perfect amount of sweetness, amazing silky icy texture, and high quality ingredients are identified immediately. I love ice cream but these I might have to say are better because at the end if the day ice cream is a bunch of some type of milk, lots of sugar, and a little fruit. That's a high quality ice cream even. Typically crappy ice cream would be minimal fruit, of any, and a bunch of artificial flavor. This is all real and it shows. Go get one. Just do it. No regrets.

So much fun! The aquarium is  divided into numerous parts all stocked with beautiful species of fish, rays and sharks. The rain forest part even has Macaws. With a two story tank with turtles, sharks, fish and rays is fun to stand for a good 20 minutes. I suggest visiting on an extremely hot day, or when a storm is passing through.

The food was good but the service was horrible.I went there on Sat.at around 3:45 pm so its not like it was crazy busy.Oh yeah that & the fact that there's only like 6 tables in the entire place & only 2 were occupied.So I'm not an expert on narcotics or anything but I'm pretty sure that our waitress was on some kind of pills/medication.She could barely keep her eyes open & our orders straight & then she kept disappearing. In fact we weren't the only one's in the restaurant that noticed it,the people  at the table next to ours were saying the exact same thing.If you can't hold your eyelids open ,don't go to work.We asked her for my order of Mac n Cheese 3 times! Then,she kept mixing up our order with the people right next to us.The food was really good but the fact that she was so messed up just ruined our entire lunch.The ribs were delicious & falling off the bone,the pulled pork was really good too.The ribs were definitely my favorite hands down.The brisket was good just not really good.The Mac n Cheese was really really good & they used Penne pasta so I thought that was pretty cool bc most places just use the same pasta.They definitely weren't skimpy with the cheese even though the portion was kind of small.On the table they also had 4 different sauces, the Southern Sweet was my favorite.Overall the food was good I just think the waitress totally ruined it & that's the only reason I'm giving them a 3 stars.

Came here last minute with only about an hour to see stuff. Honestly, I had a blast. The bird area was so cool. You can pay for a stick with seed on it and all the little birds flock to you. LOVED this part! Several birds hopped in my jacket, I couldn't stop laughing in here. The tanks had lots of sharks which are my fav water beasts. Beautiful and graceful. It was a quick trip but a def highlight.  Lots to learn and see.

Every year around Christmas we make a trek to New Hope and Peddler's Village.  This short review is for the Chaddsford Winery storefront in Peddler's Village and not the actual Winery.

Like I said, we make at least one trip down each year and we always stop in to sample the wines and we ALWAYS buy 5-6 bottles-mostly to have around the holidays or to drink during the summer.  While I am almost exclusively a red wine drinker, I actually prefer the white and rose wines from Chaddsford.  The Chaddsford wines aren't real bold flavored like I usually prefer, but they are tasty and I'm actually a big fan of their spiced wine...which is actually quite delicious when warmed a bit and muddled with some cider spices.  Very nice winter treat.  The storefront isn't huge, but they always seem to have wines available for tasting.  I recommend trying to sneak in at a time when they arent' too busy, especially if you aren't a big wine drinker.  The servers always seem to have a good handle on what they are serving that day, but when they are busy it's tough to spend time with everyone.

Overall, the visits here are nice, the employees are helpful, and the wines aren't bad.  a nice place to stop in and grab a taste before you continue shopping (though I recommend coming BACK for the wine so you don't have to carry it all day).  Not as nice as going to a real winery...so maybe we'll go to the actual Chaddsford winery some time this year.

Always heard good things about this place, but just recently tried it out. Fantastic variety of flavors: I tried the pear pie, but the variety had much more creative options like the pineapple cilantro I had on my next visit. Perfect for a Florida adventure, and I will be going back.

Perfect place to take baby on a hot & stormy summer day. Beautiful and interesting exhibits including a tunnel for viewing rays, sharks and fish from all different angles. Also a touch-pool with rays, various educational tables with knowledgeable staff to talk about items. Checkout the parakeets! No additional charge to enter this enclosed area, but you can purchase feeding sticks to feed them birdseed (it was 1.50 which is cheap compared to bird feeding sticks at our local zoo in FL). There's a small play area near the touch pool. My 1 1/2yo loved crawling and climbing. It really seems sized for preschoolers but watch out for rowdy big kids who want to climb and run. There's a VR experience for 7+ year olds. All that on top of beautifully designed and themed exhibits of aquatic animals. I'd gladly come more than once if we were staying in the area longer. There's a hawk in the Mississippi area, which a staff member was kind enough to point out. Also an impressive white gator and catfish bigger than my husband (that might be an exaggeration but they looked enormous). Loved seeing penguins and otters. Apparently you can do a behind the scenes experience with the penguins but only on certain days and there's an additional charge. Overall it's a beautiful and well designed aquarium. If we lived in the area we'd gladly become members. 

Tip: You can purchase tickets in the *air conditioned* theatre lobby to the right of aquarium main entrance (follow signage). If you arrive before opening, the theatre lobby is a good place for restrooms and a/c. 

 LUNCH: Pleasantly surprised by the quality of offerings at the "grill" upstairs. It's really just quick grab and go type food, but the wraps were a step up from what we've eaten at other aquariums or zoos around the country. I had a yummy chicken and goat cheese wrap made with chopped grilled chicken, lettuce, roasted red pepper and goat cheese. 
Chicken strips and PBJ for toddler (PBJ was one of those Smuckers prepackaged things. Perfect for tiny toddler hands, but might not be satisfying for big kids)
Husband had burger which he enjoyed.

For dessert or sweet snack there's a Haagen daz ice cream counter by the parakeets.

THEATRE: Theatre entrance is separate from the main entrance. If the building is on your right, then you'll actually hit theatre before regular admissions.  If walking with building on left then walk past admissions and main entrance. Unfortunately when we tried to checkout the theatre, our toddler wasn't into it. I will say it was a clean, cool spot to get out of summer heat. Nice concessions counter with candy & popcorn. Wish I could comment on the actual show/program but oh well.
Audubon Aquarium was GREAT!!! Bought tickets on line at a discount, had all kinds of different fish from different waters, and had quite a few activities for kids. A must do in NOLA!

2 hours of fun.  Right on the bank of the Mississippi river.  

It has themed sections in separate rooms spanning 2 floors; life in the Amazon; life on the Bayou; frogs; seahorses; etc.... Highlights were:
- Wide variety of fish from various areas of the world
- Going through a "fake" amazonian forest with associated life
- A variety of seahorses 
- A couple of sea otters
- A huge tank with sea turtles, sharks, and many fish
- Getting to feed and touch stingrays
- A kids play area (of sorts) near the stingrays
- Penguin feeding and education (I'll never eat an anchovy again?)
- Albino Alligator

There is a food court in the middle of the 2nd floor.  We were there late afternoon though... so don't know much about selection, sorry...

We didn't get a map when we came in (weren't offered one) so didn't know how much there was to see - just followed the flow - ended up taking 2 hours.  The place is clean, well-maintained, the volunteers are quite helpful and passionate about animals.  And... key for New Orleans - is air-conditioned!

Pros: Beautiful presentation. Great service - the staff member noticed that we were low on pita and heavy on the hummus left so he brought us extra pita bread at no cost. 

Cons: Very heavy on the tahini which gave our hummus a peanut buttery taste.

I went to this location after lunch one afternoon in downtown St. Petersburg and I can honestly say that I was pleasantly surprised. I didn't think much of a gourmet popsicle store but I can say that I will be heading out of my way to make another stop by. The employee that was there was extremely friendly and very helpful. Defiantly a must try if you are in the area!

Came back for the Cochon Bleu with a side of Mac and cheese! Have fallen in love with the food and atmosphere. 
If you'll order the Cochon Bleu, get it in a bun. The French bread tasted a bit dry last time I got it. Overall, delicious!

After visiting their Insectarium we were expecting more from this stop. My husband and son bought tickets just for the aquarium and they are definitely over priced for what you get. It is small, not a huge variety of fish. It is very kid-friendly- our youngest loved that she could pet the sting rays, and the displays were colorful and somewhat simple. The penguins were fun to watch. After recently visiting the Dallas World Aquarium this was a let down, and priced higher.
I've been to this aquarium over 30 times and I absolutely love this place!! By far one of the best aquariums I've ever been to!

The pops are good and natural which is a plus! There are almost too many flavor options it is hard to choose and I ended up panic ordering because they were busy. The papaya pineapple was by far my favorite. The ginger plum was too much ginger not enough sweet plum and the watermelon mint had no discernable mint flavor.

Novio and I were looking for a good BBQ place closer to home, The Joint is a bit of a drive from Uptown. On a casual stroll through Magazine St. we stumbled upon Saucy's BBQ, a quaint, homey, local that gave out a permeating aroma of smoked meat and spices. It's a seat yourself, order at the register kind of place, simple and straight to the point. The menu has various items, We both ordered the half rack of ribs, the sides are charged separately + water= a bill of $40.00. This seemed a bit pricey to us at the time, but then we got our plates. The ribs are HUGE, I ended up only eating three, Novio ate five of his. The baked beans are awesome, I have had better Mac n'Cheese.  We took four ribs home, part of our dinner for tonight. I recommend ordering The Rib Plate, comes with three ribs and two sides; its also more cost effective. Also we didn't order them, but the brisket and goat cheese sliders had my eye for only $4!  You can also call for pick-up and I believe they deliver if you use the Waiter app. Parking is on the Street. IMPORTANT: The place is BYOB( Bring your own Beer/Drink) !!!!

HOW IN THE HELL DO I GET TO THE EXITS?
Since recent terrorist attacks I have become much more aware of my public surroundings. Now I'm not paranoid but I do think it's prudent to know where emergency exits are. I work out at the Jewish Community Center and believe me, after a bogus bomb threat last summer I now know at least 4 escape routes to Leontine!

A TENEBRIOUS CROWDED STIFLING MAZE
Today as I crept in darkness between throngs of hyped up Lutheran teens on retreat and the indistinct teeming horde of 3' tall grade schoolers in the bottleneck near the Seahorses I got claustrophobic and then panicky: there was no clearly marked egress to get me the heck out.

BULT IN 1989 FOR THEATRICAL EFFECT
the dimly lit maundering Aquarium doesn't seem prepared for mass evacuation. I really didn't feel safe there.
1st time trying out this place and it was amazing! Crazy how they have over 500 different flavors. The staff was great and very helpful.

This place is kinda sad. The penguins are smooshed in and show signs of captivity anxiety. Hardly any of the tanks had clear labeling. It's not something I'll go do again. Heck even Seaworld is less depressing and that's saying a lot. Any flaunting of "sponsored by oil companies" is just gross and counterintuitive. It's a slap in the face. This place is just a bummer

Could of been better. Sparse exhibits. Very sad penguin exhibit. Lots of 'pardon our mess'. Seemed nearly empty like the aquarium was preparing to go out of business. The big tank was the best of all. Overpriced for what ya get. Have to say the staff there were very very friendly.

Took my elderly parents and it was so packed with kids and so loud, there was no way to enjoy the experience.  The tanks are not wheelchair friendly...you can't get up close and many of them are too high for viewing from a seated position.  We found the entire place to be small and poorly laid out.  The theater area is separate from the actual aquarium and the only way to get there is a very long walk outside.  For us, it was in the pouring rain.  Don't understand how the aquarium gets such great reviews, it doesn't have that many exhibits and I would recommend to skip it.  So many other better things to enjoy in NOLA.

Tucson got trails for fat tires! Yea! Fantasy Island is a blast! Fast furious fun on fat tires FFFFT! Not much elevation gain. Let them fatty's roll on tight curves through, up and down sandy washes onto packed DG! How fast can you roll? FFFFT!

Lots and lots of interconnecting trails. Ride it 1-WAY only--that's the rule! Avoid head on collision. Just follow the trail markers. I was a 1st timer here. Good that I had my Trailforks app to help make sure I scorched every trail. FFFFT!

Be vigilant, cacti wait to stick and prick you as you fry those knobby treads leaning into curves.  I was spinning and coasting as fast as I could on a 27.5 plus, 2.8 fat tire, Santa Cruz, Tallboy--Whew! FFFFT!

Park in dirt lot at corner of S. Harrison Rd. and E. Irvington Rd. Enter Harrison Greenway paved trail. Pedal a little bit and look left for a sign in dirt says "START" you're on your way to FFFFT!

Life is good at Fantasy Island--FFFFT!

While in St. Pete on a blazing hot Saturday I decided to stop by the Hyppo. There are tons of Popsicle options - mostly interesting combinations like Hibiscus Starfruit and Lavender Lemon Crème. Choosing a gourmet pop was definitely a challenge however, I decided to go with the Mango Champagne. 

The staff are extremely friendly and the space has tons of light with large glass windows with bar stools facing the street. I sat for a few minutes, ate my pop and watched folks stroll by. This is a great place for adults and children alike, I look forward to trying another favor on my next visit.

This place is sooo good! They always have new things to try. I'll come in with the intention of just buying one popsicle but end up walking out with 4-5 flavors I couldn't say no to and save them in my freezer for later.
Quality of ingredients is superior! Everyone that I've brought here to try ends up loving it too

I went in to Apex Saw today with every intention of buying a bench sander. The one I have at home is old and I need one for projects around the house. The store was recommended by a friend. When I walked in there were at least 3 employees and one customer looking around. My first impression was that it was very clean. That's the additional star. 

It went down hill from there. I was not greeted or acknowledged in any way. There was no howdy-doody or How-can-I-help-you's. The staff went on about their chattering, completely unconcerned with my arrival. I wandered around the store looking for the sanders and saw the one I liked, a Rikon for $239. (available on the internet for $144) 
I looked for a store associate to talk to. I stood in front of the counter for a few minutes thinking someone would finally approach me. I walked back over to the sanders a second time. There was still no assistance so I walked out the door. LOUSY customer service. I will never step foot in there again. I receive better service at a fast food restaurant.

When compared to the New England Aquarium or similar, Audubon shouldn't even be called an aquarium. When I went with my nephew last week, many of the exhibits did not even have fish or animals in them. Many of tanks / glass were dirty. There was only one sea otter in the "sea otters" exhibit and the viewing area was up too high for me to see much less my three year old nephew. The worst by far was the penguin exhibit - overcrowded, the penguins just stood around listless; there was hardly any room for them to swim. It was very sad. To top it all off, Audubon Aquarium is ridiculously expensive. Save your money and take the kids to City Park.
Called to place an order at 3 pm on a Saturday. Said they were on a 2 hour wait and weren't taking any orders. Kind of ridiculous. Guess I'll stick with Hatti B's

Can you please open a shop in Miami?!?!! If you build one, we ALL will come!!!
Holy @#$%! This is the BEST ice cream I've ever had in my life. I'm not kidding! 
The shop is cute, perfect location, street parking and all that exists here but lets talk about why this is the best gourmet ice cream possibly ever!
Flavor and all their concoctions of it!
I'm more of a salty girl but when I want ice cream I'm usually happy with just a vanilla or coconut, simple but delish. 
I wasnt ready for these flavors. I thought they'd have a good variety but not over 400 flavors!!! WHAT!!!!! And forget my vanilla they have eclectic flavors like pineapple cilantro (this was my 2nd favorite) dragon fruit, coconut avocado,  banana rum. beet pineapple giinger, and so much more but the holy.og.holys was the blueberry goat cheese . Listen, I know it sounds like it doesnt go...it freaking does and it is absolutely phenomenal. Guys there are so many flavors go on the website and please just go look. I was flabbergasted and appalled at first but after trying several I realized this was the best tasting gourmet, fancy AF ice creams ever! These should be in every freezer worldwide and the best thing is you can take them home. They have a little cooler thingy to keep them cold...just dont thinknthey make it to Miami...not unless you have some dry ice....lol..People the ice cream is that damm good...I want to try every damm flavor there is because everything I was allowed onto try tasted so great! Kudos to the creators of all the different flavors. I would have never put some of these ingredients together but they just qork!!!!

My kids and I love Audubon! The Aquarium is always neat. We expect crowds because it is touristy and centrally located but we usually go in the Fall when it is less busy. 

My daughter is 10 and even though we have been here several times, she still enjoys it. Her favorite exhibits are the Sting Ray touch pools and Parakeet Landing. The touch pool is neat and the wait is never long, she sometimes gets in line again and again. You can also buy a ticket to feed the Sting Rays. Speaking of feeding, you can buy a stick of birdseed to feed the parakeets!! It is a fun experience.

Staff is always nice and very knowledgeable. We have the family membership so we are able to pass up the ticket line, getting us to the fun faster. 

The only thing keeping it less thn 5 stars for me are two things. 
First, healthier food options would be nice although we don't expect it. 
Second, even though our parking ticket was "validated" per the front desk, the validation did not work. I asked the parking attendant about it and she said that the aquarium knows their machine is broke. She said it has been broke for weeks!! My daughter met me there and unknowing about it, we paid full price at the kiosk. It should have been $10 each but we were tricked into paying $30 total and once you pay at the kiosk, its too late.

First off, they get a 5 for flavor.  These things are the bomb.  Their problem, and it truly IS a serious problem, is they don't know how to manage the availability of their more popular flavors, namely Orange Cream and Chocolate Sea Salt.  If I had a dollar for every time they're out of those, I could buy a franchise...which I wouldn't, because then people would be mad at me because corporate wouldn't get me enough Orange Cream and Chocolate Sea Salt.  It truly is frustrating that they are CONSTANTLY out of those 2 flavors.  They need to realize that they need to make MORE of those than the Asphalt Fiberglass Kale or the Leather Kelp Acetaminophen.

A short walk from our hotel in the warehouse district is the Audubon Aquarium.  Very respectable in their exhibits, but nothing spectacular.  Lots of fresh water displays as well as marine.  The underwater tunnel through the coral reef is a good view, but gets too crowded with people just standing around.  Keep it moving People!

The open ocean tank has lots of reef, sand tiger and nurse sharks, sting rays and even a large green sea turtle.  The Amazon jungle exhibit is great with all the pacu, piranha and ariwana.  It's very humid in there, so it's not for you if you're having a bad hair day.  There's also a large penguin enclosure where the penguins hang out right up at the glass.  One of their prize animals is Spots the white alligator, you have to see to believe.

This aquarium is not large like the Georgia Aquarium or Sea World with their million gallon tanks, dolphins & whales, but is worth a visit when you're in NOLA.

Fish.
Reptiles.
Birds.
Escalators. 
Coral.
Plants. 
Funny Smells.
Shellfish.
Over priced tickets.

Thinking back to our trip here, what a great date place for a rainy afternoon! 

We parked in the open-air lot next to the Canal Shopping plaza parking lot (you can get validation for this lot from the aquarium) and walked over. We got combo tickets for both the zoo and aquarium. I think they that particular combo was in the $30 price range, which is a great deal. We didn't need to get the full monty package since we aren't all that interested in seeing an IMAX or the insectarium. Anyhow, we're looking forward to the zoo at a later date. 

It's not the largest or most exciting aquarium ever, but they do a really great job with the exhibits (favs include the otters, penguins, and giant tank sponsored hilariously by some big oil companies) and the parakeet part was a nice bonus. All in all, it took about 90 minutes of leisurely strolling to make it through the entire building. 

After visiting all the exhibits, we went for a nice river walk down to Cafe Du Monde to get some goodies and back. I think we paid a bit extra for the parking since we took longer than the validation was good for, but it was definitely worth it. 

Having seen it once, I don't feel a huge urge to go back again. However, having said that - we really enjoyed visiting and are happy we took the time to check it out.
If your from the upper east coast and have been to Philadelphia or Baltimore aquarium don't waste your time and money here. LAME

We love the aquarium! We actually bought a membership for here and the Audubon Zoo since we are always looking for fun things to do with the kids--and any excuse to hop on down to NOLA for the afternoon is usually welcome. I can remember visiting as a kid and loving it, so it is fun to share with my offspring now;) It can definitely get crowded some days, so maybe try to hit it up on a weekday, if possible, and check out some of the little "shows" like feeding the penguins--or even the IMAX, if you get a chance. Decent food/snacks upstairs and clean bathrooms, as well. I believe the variety of fish seemed a bit more expansive when I was little--more sharks, etc...but still plenty for the kids to see and spend an afternoon. Giant gift shop, of course, and pics you can purchase. Nice way to spend a hot day with the kids inside:)

Was in the area and wanted to try this place. to my delight it was open. Its in the building right at 4th and Peabody. Ample parking. The staff are very friendly referring to me by name. The nice lady did warn me plenty of times after I asked for the 200 degrees chicken. She even said, I would sweat, and it would clear my sinuses. She was telling the truth. I find it to be slightly hotter than Hattie B's "hot" and about on par with Prince's medium. There are disclaimers all over. So the person who rated this place bad was due to their own negligence.  They have a health rating of 100%.  The restaurant is set up in a food court type setting inside. She explained to me that since they make everything fresh to order it would be about 10 minutes. It probably wasn't even that long until it was ready. 

The chicken was good. Not as sweet as Hattie B's Seriously hot. Almost as much as I can handle. This is Nashville. Its supposed to be hot. I recommend the fries as a side. They are seasoned and go great with ranch. I ate the chicken plain and did not dip it in the ranch. 

All in all, delicious. The chicken was soft and tender, cooked to perfection. She asked me, mid meal, if I was ok, again referring to me by name. I gave her a thumbs up, and she smiled. She asked if I could take it hotter and I told her no I couldn't :) 

If you are in the area and craving hot chicken, I do recommend it. Particularly convenient for out of towners at the convention center / Country Music Hall of Fame / Downtown hotels.

Long lines to get in. Kids loved the sharks. Food court expensive. If u have the energy to stand around with tons of people and stare at fish and sealife behind the glass, it is okay. Not good to go since covid.
Absolutely amazing food and friendly staff. Chef/owner stoped by our table, what a treat to end our evening. Thank you

Wow!  Great concept - Popsicles with natural ingredients featuring a ton of unique flavors.  These are definitely not the food dyed, high fructose laced Pops I grew up eating.

Eleven shops in Florida and likely growing.  I visited their Saint Petersburg's shop in a revitalized section of the City.  The weather was perfect for a cold treat, especially following heated game of Shuffle Board with my brother-in-law.

At $2.25 -$4.50 they are worth every nibble, dribble, and lick.  After a long debate and a refusal of my request by the attendant to sample one of each Pop, I settled for a Pineapple Cilantro Pop.  Odd?  One would think, but the two flavors really blended and complimented themselves.

Check-out my photos of each freezer and the menu board drool inducing views.

First of all, the person at the counter was super friendly! There were several samples of the drinks for us to try and when we couldn't make a decision he also told us we could mix two drinks together. All the flavours they had to offer had a unique refreshing taste to it. Something you won't have commonly tried. The mango ginger lemonade was a very good mild drink to have but when mixed with the hibiscus rosewater and mint lemonade respectively it was even better. The minty-ness from the mint lemonade gives the overall drink a pop to it which made the drink so fun while the hibiscus blend moulded together in harmony

Nice aquarium that has a diverse selection of aquatic wildlife. In addition to saltwater, local, and Amazonian freshwater fish, they have penguins, otters, and a giant white alligator. They also have some unusual sharks such as the bonnethead shark, and a very large variety of seahorses.

Admission for adults is a little more than $22, but discounts and coupons can often be found on visitor maps and guides. You can either buy admission for the aquarium only, or buy a package deal for multiple attractions (Zoo, aquarium, insectarium) for a "bulk discount".

Great family outing in NOLA. Fun time in the bird cage, one got in my daughters purse, food available to feed them. Mealtime in the penguin area wand the narrative was very entertaining. Feed sting rays - all was educational and a nice break from parties.

One of the best aquariums I have ever visited. We went in 2004, before Katrina, and were so impressed. We were saddened to hear that so many fish were lost in the hurricane. Have not been there since, so maybe this review is outdated. But if they even restored 90% of what it was before, it is a great experience. Expect LOTS of people and kids, which may not suit some people.
I wasn't finished eating and I was already thinking about eating the left overs. Amazing house made saucys. Byob, no table service.

This was a decent experience. We came because my 4 year old really wanted to see the fish and penguins :)
Parking is not exactly close to the aquarium so be prepared for a little walk, about half a mile. ALSO they are doing construction in the area, when you get to the dead end go LEFT there IS parking there you don't want to miss out on. And yes while it's still half a mile walk; the other parking garage is even further away, but you can walk the river walk which is nice. 
You are also able to purchase tickets online which is nice to a voice the crowd. It was surprisingly crowded for a Sunday afternoon (or maybe its the norm) either way the line moved quick!
When you first walk in there are some extra experience items you can grab, I'm honestly not sure what they were since nobody was around to explain and it was awkward chaos. 
We walked in an theres a beautiful waterfall right in front before you start your experience.
I loved learning/reading about all the different jellyfish in the world. I will say the flow of the aquarium is chaotic OR we all just did not know the way the flow worked. There were multiple points where we were just stuck, only to find out each window was showing the same fish.
My girls loved the Rain Forrest area and felt they were up close with the macaws. We were disappointed in the penguin display as it was extremely small which was surprising because they were pictured on the advertisement.  The other disappointment was the otters. Most of the otter displays were empty OR they were just all on the end in this tiny area. 
The aquarium takes about an hour to get through and is great if you need to kill some time with the kids.

The reviews of this place are really good but I'm not sure how that's possible.  My husband and I came on a Saturday night and we were the only people there.  We got the spinach pie and hummus appetizer- the spinach pie was wrapped in something that was really bready and seemed microwaved- def not philo dough.  The hummus was pretty tasteless- not as good as grocery store hummus.  The hot sauce in the middle was good but that's about it.  Our falafel and gyro sandwiches were decent but not great.  Also the AC seemed to be broken and my husband may or may not have seen a rat.  The server was really nice and attentive though!

The Audubon Aquarium exceeded even the aquarium in my Hometown of Brooklyn.  Although the Brooklyn Aquarium is undergoing renovation, it still lacks a certain element -- The Crowd.  Everybody, from baby to adult, enjoyed the trip to the aquarium.  

The admission was steep, but once inside, its well worth it.  The place is so big you don't even know where you want to begin.  Perhaps, the camera guy or girl will lure you in for a family photo in front of one of the large tanks.  Of course, it's another fee, but you have the option of purchasing or not.  

The place is so big, and weekends are probably the worst time you can go, its bound to be packed with people.   If you can go on a weekday, it might save you the headache of dealing with a crowd, as well as save you a few bucks.

Just a note* The parking garage at Canal Place comps you a couple dollars or more off if you have your ticket stub.
Delicious fruit pops. The sheer variety of flavors was super impressive. We will definitely be back to try some more.
What a terrible experience. Some of the tanks were empty. Others only had one specimen. The carpets were in bad shape. The escalator didn't work. It was a sad sad excuse for an aquarium.
Great selection of Popsicles and great location.  Right on the 600 block with all the local shops, perfect snack while shopping.  They have so many flavors to choose from, more reason to come back!
Very nice place, although it can use more for the admission price. The food court is very limited and can use more food selection.

We spent much ore time there than we thought we would- it was just so wonderful.  Petting and feeding the stingrays was amazing and watching the penguins get fed was more fabulous than we thought it could be.  What a wonderful, interesting, fun place for all ages.

First the GOOD:

1. staff were polite and well spoken in the first instance. I got assurance my order was dairy free.
I chose a table right in front of their stall within 15 feet of where they took payment. It was clean, washroom tidy I washed hands and returned and picked up my 'sampler' dinner order.

2. Food was "edible".

Now the NOT so GOOD:

zero none 0 of the following tasted any good: baba, hummus, pita, salad, Here, Grape leaves. All sour acidy sameness, except for the pita bread which was bone dry / stale / taste free / bland.

No one inquired if my food was fine and dandy, including a *supervisor* who returned from break whilst I was dining, no one ever made eye contact, zero communication from the *Boss Lady* or the young gent who originally served and took pre payment. (Why is this when things are not so good? the modus operandi always seems to be the same innit? )

Finally the POOR:

value 17 plus $ couldn't eat much of, tried to like it, sampled everything.

Background:
My experience with this type of cuisine is wide. Travelled / spent nearly a year in the region where Torshi allegedly represents. Eaten Mediterranean type diet and prepared many of those dishes myself from scratch. The baba ganoush was particularly WEAK at Torshi, almost like it came from a premix? couldn't find evidence of eggplant. Hummus isn't a difficult FRESH prep. Theirs was characterless, bland, couldn't find any reason to eat it after tasting. Really disappointing. 'Grape leaves' they called it. I know it as Dolmai. Torshi's were mushy and sour inside = a weak effort.

I wanted this to be really good, hadn't tasted anything from the 'region' for a month or so, down Magazine Street (TAL's 4800 Block?). Talk about night and day! Big disappointment for me today, and feeling sorry as I write this.

Phenomenal aquarium!

-small, but packed with marine life, activities, birds, information, etc.
-plan to spend at least 3 hours, we stayed for about 3 hours and there were still things we did not do
-feeding the sting rays is a must! Only costs $2 and it is fun and educational (even for adults). Purchase tickets at the 2nd floor gift shop before they sell out
-affordable, adult tickets are about $29.95 for adults and $24.95 for children and seniors. They are $2 cheaper if you buy tickets online
-employees are helpful and friendly
-tanks are clean and clear and full of marine life
-around the tanks are ducks, parrots, and birds of prey
-highly recommend walking through parakeet pointe. You can walk through for free or buy food to feed the birds. The birds land on you whether you have food or not. Careful not to stand under the tree
-throughout the aquarium are easy to read, informative signs and screens (some even have audio and video)
-at some of the exhibits, employees bring out various creatures to pet and learn more about (ex. slipper lobsters, baby alligators)
-the new shark and ray touch pool was not ready during our visit, but it is coming soon!
-they have a theater, a gift shop, food service establishments, and an escape room
-convenient location adjacent to Riverwalk 

Definitely worth a visit, I have already encouraged several friends/family check it out!

The Aquarium is another wonderful attraction for kids and adults. 

Located on the riverfront next to the Canal Street Ferry and Woldenburg Park, there are several parking lots close by. 

There is an Imax theater attached to the Aquarium. There is a delegate charge for the theater. 

Once you enter the Aquarium you will see a grand waterfall fountain where kids can toss coins to make a wish. You will then proceed under an aquarium arch filled with colorful fish. This is a popular spot, and Aquarium employees will offer to take your photo (not free).

There are exhibits containing nearly every type of fish. My favorite areas are the Amazon (piranhas), the penguins (everyone's favorite) and the Gulf of Mexico exhibit. 

The gulf exhibit contains a simulated drilling platform and is a great example of the creatures off of our shores. Sharks, tuna, tarpon, etc. all live in this tank. It is huge and awe inspiring. 

There is an area where brave kids can pet sting rays and sharks. The jellyfish exhibit is also a big hit. 

Plan on spending several hours at The Aquarium. Even the gift shop is great. Thy also have the machine to crush pennies into souvenirs. 

The one criticism I have involves their food area. This is New Orleans. Our attractions should have world class food. The Aquarium has a food court that is no better than fast food. Come on Aquarium, bring in John Besh or the Brennans. J
