NYC does not have any good aquariums so I made it a point to come here and was not disappointed. The exhibits are absolutely beautiful, I especially loved climbing around the tree house area, and walking through the overhead tank. I saw sharks, penguins, seahorses, otters, a crocodile, jelly fish, and got to pet some slimy sting rays. The hurricane simulator is also neat. Everything is clean and the staff are friendly and knowledgeable.

They know their stuff! I went to buy paint for my cabinets and they helped me tremendously. They were the only store that carried the product that I was looking for out of the whole town. They also have a bunch of selections so if you're looking for something specific, try them out! you won't regret it :)

We got the Individual Plus One Audubon membership (kids under 2 are free anyway!)

It's such a great deal. The Aquarium can be especially expensive for individual admission, so the membership pays for itself. 

As for the Aquarium as a family outing, it's fantastic! They have a little bit of everything, and people of all ages can enjoy it. My daughter, at 10 months old, enjoyed strolling around and just looking at the bright colored fish... even though she likely had no idea what was going on. Now, a few months later, she gets a kick out of yelling "fish fish" and "biiiiiird" (penguin) and pointing at everything. Older kids/adults will enjoy the educational aspect of it too.

The gift shop has some adorable shirts, stuffed animals, and other various souveniers, at your typical gift shop prices. We'll definitely be back, multiple times. Typically we go to the Zoo during the spring/fall when the temperatures are reasonable, and then save the Aquarium for the winter/summer when we would rather be in a climate controlled environment.

Bonus points for being located right by the Algiers Ferry, so we can park for free in Algiers Point and walk to the Aquarium!

I had extremely high hopes for this place. It delivered nothing aside from an Albino Alligator. The grounds are drab. The lay out and flow is poor. They charge $25 for kids 2 and up. That's appalling. The layout and flow is poor. Save your money and take a pass on this place.

I used to stop in quite often, but haven't been here in over a year. The tea shop we wanted to go to today was closed, so my boyfriend's son requested for us to ride our bikes over to the Hyppo instead. The popsicles are a bit pricy, at $3-5 each. Today, I had the Honey honeydew, which was so sweet that I had to throw it away and usually I love sweets. My boyfriend chose the simply strawberry and his son chose a strawberry lemonade. Both of theirs were much better. It's worth stopping by on a hot day for a cool treat

Hubby and I made this one of our last stops before we headed to the airport. It's a bit on the smaller side but it's nice. Make sure you go feed the parakeets outside. I had two hand on my feeding stick and the weight caused it to fall but one of them was determined to eat and cane right on back to let me feed him. My husband caught it all on his phone which was great!

Love love the Egyptian eats here. Everything is fresh and the owner is so kind! The eggplant is my absolute favorite and I also love the Egyptian specials they offer. Plus, the wine prices at the attached bottle shop can't be beat.

Whenever I visit a city for the first time and it has an aquarium, it is highly probable that I will visit it. The Audubon Aquarium was no exception.

I walked in and the folks were so friendly. I paid for my ticket, got a map, and spent my time walking around. I was there for at least four hours.

I love penguins. They were energetic and cute. I also enjoyed seeing many varieties of fish, eels, frogs, seahorses, eagles, jellyfish, and more.

It is perfectly fine for you to take photos. I had both my iPhone and DLSR camera with me. It helps to not use your flash, if you can, so you don't annoy the animals and fish.

If you want to see what is playing at the 3D theatre, you need to shell out more for that. I didn't, as it does add up. For me, it's the gift shop that I'd rather hit.

I ended up getting a round, adorable stuffed penguin. If you love penguins, this gift shop will lure you in with all things penguin.

(49)

Okay I am officially mind blown by these pops. I usually don't eat ice pops for dessert but the Hyppo has changed my mind . The flavors of each pop are so fresh and natural tasting. The toasted coconut is easily one of the best coconut ice desserts I've had . The flavor is so clean and there are coconut flakes towards the bottom. I know for a fact these pops are made with real ingredients not any essence of flavor or concentrates 10/10. The jackfruit is pretty much self explanatory I would love to describe to flavors but if you had jackfruit this is literally jackfruit in popsicle form . The people who make these pops are experts and source high quality ingredients that taste just as they should 10/10. The service was amazing as well I cannot say enough nice things about Sara. She was attentive and made each guest feel loved. I will totally be back and would consider these pops if I want a healthier dessert . Psa I only intended to eat one on my first visit but got 2 due to temptation. They're that good guys

Best labna of my life, y'all. My GF Katie B laughed at me, as my enthusiastic reactions to the flavors brought her some kind of joy. I think I muttered, "eff yeah." 

Toshi Egyption Food is located inside the St Roch. And with so many delicious options to choose from inside the food hall, Torshi is by far the most aromatic, which creates a line. Food takes time, but it's well worth it. Even for a side plate of labna with warm pita.

I am an event coordinator and I have used Empire close to 20 times this past year, one event being attended by local politicians and state senators. For that specific event Chad actually came out a few days before our event to go over a game plan due to our event not being at a typical venue. Each time, they are quick to respond via phone or email and always provide excellent service. I usually have the same valet team working and they are wonderful with our guests (mostly senior citizens) and are always quick and efficient. Would highly recommend!!

Visiting a winery felt like a fun birthday activity, so we bought a groupon to visit Chaddsford.  Though we didn't initially realize the tasting room was actually IN Peddler's Village, it seemed like a fun Saturday trip. 

We didn't leave until later in the afternoon, and hit a massive wall of traffic - Peddler's Village does an insane business on a sunny Saturday, so beware.  I'd definitely recommend either coming early, or trying to hit it on a weekday. 

The tasting room was easy to find. It seems brand new, so everything is neat and clean.  We spent maybe a half hour tasting 5 wines each.  You could also purchase additional samples, or buy glasses of special wine concoctions.  We opted out of those, but went to the main room to sample a few more wines, which are free for anyone to try. 

The staff didn't seem particularly knowledgeable or engaging, though they were friendly enough.

I have been to a ton of aquariums. This one was nice but a little underwhelming. Still worth the price of admission--goes to a good cause anyway--but not as large or inclusive as I would have thought. That said, some of the larger tanks were truly awesome, and I didn't know turtles could get that big!

What kind of person would I be to not devote my 100th review to my new favorite dessert bar in town? I have the ultimate sweet tooth and visiting Hyppo pops satisfies all my cravings. Stopping in here is such a treat. 

I haven't been so adventurous over the past few visits since they offer everything I've ever wanted! I'm more into the creamier pops... They have Avocado variations, to Pistachio, to cheesecake- Plenty of ingredients catering to the most different taste buds. Next time, I'll be sure to get one of the fruitier flavors or dip my pop into dark chocolate to switch things up!

This aquarium is cool for the young and old (er!) 

There is your typical aquariums with big glass windows for you to view the fish but there are also huge Windows that extend from the roof to the floor and go around the corner. This particular section had huge sharks, stingrays and a variety of other huge fish swimming around inside. 

You can feed the stingrays but you need to pre book at the kiosk / shop just before the exhibit. It was only $2, so it filled up quickly and we missed out. 

There are two outdoor sections, one with Amazon wildlife and one with wildlife from the Mississippi. There was albino crocodile, fish, a few birds, snake and other animals. 

I particularly enjoyed watching the jellyfish and seahorses. 

There are several photo points where you can take your own photos with statues of sea life and also a small aquarium with a 'hole' in the middle. Kids can crawl under and put their heads in which looked cool.

My Nails has the best combination of price and quality out of all of the nail salons I have tried in Indianapolis. I've been coming to My Nails for the past 5 years, during which time the prices have not gone up like other places. I started here getting my nails done consistently once or twice a month, but have since moved further away and now only get them done for special occasions.

You definitely need to make an appointment if you want to get in. They used to have availability for walk-ins, but have been booked fairly solid the last few times I've gone. The nail techs, Gio and Quinn, are both very nice and remember you every visit, even if it's been many months since you've last visited. They have even kept the shop open late when I was delayed for my appointment because of traffic. They are very accommodating to their regulars. 

The only downsides are lack of a website and online scheduling capability. Appointments can be made only by calling. The nail techs frequently take calls during their appointments, which could be cut down quite a bit if they had an online appointment requesting system. 

Also, they have a small dog that is sometimes in the shop with them. The dog is old and just sits around, but just an fyi if you have an allergy to dogs. 

As far as payment, cash is preferred, but credit cards are accepted. They prefer cash so they don't have to pay the transaction fees on credit cards, so I take cash when I visit now. Personal checks are not generally accepted, unless you are a regular.

This was a really great aquarium. I had a really good time. The tanks were all clean and the staff was friendly. It only took about an hour to cruise through and see all the different aquariums. 

I loved the penguin exhibit. I just think they are so cute and I really enjoyed watching them interact.

Lots of cool fish in all sizes, shapes, and colors. I especially enjoyed all the varieties of seahorses. They are really fun to watch. And the stingrays were great too. 

I like how the aquarium is laid out by sections of the world. They had a huge anaconda. Lots of eels also. Even the electric eel. 

And you have to have an alligator, or it just wouldn't be Louisiana. 

The huge tank downstairs is amazing. Lots of sharks in that one too. 

Nice place to spend a little time!

I was visiting town for a conference and my friend suggested we try this place. I said "hot and spicy? I'm in." 

When we arrived, I got the usual shpeel about how "the owner is not responsible" and "it's really, really hot" and "are you sure you want to try the 400 degrees?" I asked what it's flavored with, and she replied "Habanero peppers." I informed the owner that I can eat habaneros like candies, to which she informed me that she had 500 degrees chicken (with Scorpion and Ghost Chilies) and 800 degrees chicken with the Carolina Reaper. Okay, now we're talking. I'd never even HEARD of the Reaper before, so, daring/stupid as I can be, I ordered the chicken fingers. She suggested one of each, 400, 500, and 800 and I accepted. 

Knowing how the heat in these things builds, and not being terribly hungry, I decided to start at the top and work my way down. It took me a few minutes, but I polished off the first strip in a few minutes. It was pretty darn hot, but I did not get the hiccups, tear up, or sweat. I did, however, start to turn a bit red, so that says something. I plowed through the 500 degrees strip as well, and eventually finished all three. The taste was average, but the heat was well above.

All the while, my friend, who had ordered the 200 degrees chicken, was commenting at how hot his was. 

We went for a walk around Nashville, and I could gradually feel my insides heating up. That night, for the first time in my entire life of eating hot and spicy foods, I experienced heartburn, so I guess that says something for the heat. 

If you want a hot challenge, check out 400 Degrees Hot Chicken!

Exceptional tool store in every way. Cram packed with quality wood working machines and accessories on display and in stock. The band saw I purchased there was $900, the best price I could find online was $1100 +shipping and Apex had it in stock. The staff could not be friendlier. A local small business that's a model for all. I will be a regular faithful customer for many years to come.

Best chicken shawarma in the city! Different than what you are used to- this is tender and juicy and full of flavor. Make sure you get their hot sauce on the side. Seriously considering asking if they will sell it to me by the jar next time I go. All the teas are delicious as well.

This is just a liiiiitlle bit better than what the ice cream man used to bring ;-)  A huge variety of gourmet popsicles that changes over time.  They have seasonal treats (like pumpkin pie), health food varieties (raspberry chia seed), and culinary trends (spicy/sweet popsicles).  I stopped in and had a datil pepper cheesecake pop.  The blend of creamy cheesecake and super spicy datil were a winner.  If I lived in St. Pete, I may go here every day.

In all fairness this should be 3.5 stars but yelp does not allow that.

First the not so great:
The server was not wearing a mask. I am still getting all my food to go but with someone handling my food I would still like them to be wearing a mask. Also I used their website to order my food. The website said 15 minutes. When I got there they had no knowledge of my order. The owner was super nice and asked what I had ordered and made it up fresh. They have only been opened since Friday so I know that's not entirely their fault.

The good:
The food is great! Probably the best Gyro I have ever had. Very thick slices. It was moist and crispy at the same time I loved it. I also got the lental soup and it was pretty good as well. I will definitely be coming back but will continue getting things to go.

The aquarium is kinda small and general admission is a little high. I would probably give it 4 stars for just normal admission? So why 5 stars?
BACKSTAGE PENGUIN PASSES! I did this as a surprise for my fiance that nearly cried when we went to the back and got to play with penguins! Worth every penny! Go online and reserve your tickets and times. Also included is a brief tour if the aquarium. We also saw a seahorse giving birth! 
Never knew how soft penguins' feathers are, like suede or velvet. Not rubbery. Fun tour!

I always go out of my way to make sure any of my guests visiting St. Pete get a chance to stop by here on their way down central! 

I absolutely LOVE the unique flavors, and the staff is always nice and attentive.
I love hippo!!!!!!!! It is so great and yummy! I've been going to hippo for about 4 years and I've loved it every day since than.

Note, you can only enter 15 minutes prior to your ticket time. They will not let you in even one minute early. The aquarium is easy to get to from the streetcar. The inside is clean and the staff wears masks. The aquarium itself is not very large and can be completed in about 45 minutes if you view most items. Really nice for kids.
i know it closed but i miss yalllllll. justice for saucy's. mac and cheese, pulled pork!!!

Excellent alligator links. 
Came here around 4pm so there was no crowd and I was pleasantly surprised by the food. 

Price: they have a coupon deal on yelp!  20% off which was pretty big since we wanted to try a bit of everything on the menu. The average sandwich was about 7$ and the plates were about 10$ so the meals were fair priced. 

Food: definitely recommend the alligator links it comes with creole mustard I believe. The sauce makes it superb. I got the two meat platter combo with the brisket and pulled pork because a lot of recommendations for it and I must say that was the only disappointing part. The meat was dry and even with the many sauces they had it wasn't better than just ok. 
The dessert is my favorite. Their cheesecake was beautifully designed. The attention to detail is what makes eating out a worthy experience. 

Service. Was good. Friendly and readily available and attentive.  She had some good recommendations too when we chatted with her. 

Ambience. Casual dine in restaurant. A bit small but that adds to the charm. They have live music once a week too so feels like a small town unique place to go. 

Recommendations. Get the alligator link and the cheesecake.

Fishes... sharkies... octopi... (yeah you're not gonna have me flagged)

Anywho, great addition to the city.  Great way to entertain the kiddies during the VACAY in the NOLA.  Also great for us locals to go and support Nemo & his buddies.

It appears larger than it is, can come off as massive... guess this is because of the IMAX theater just next door.  No matter, this is quite the circular adventure.  I saw that because it's but a BIG OLE circle inside.  I think this is great because this is a full-proof way to NOT lose the kiddies.  

Restaurant upstairs, near the Parakeet Point, serves up some goodies to tide you over until you leave. No eating of the Parakeeties... lol j/k.  Fun note, you can buy feed to feed the Parakeets, how cool, you can feed them from your hand.

I think my faves were the Penguins & the Otters, maybe because I'm a water baby... yeah I think that's it.  The penguins & otters are so graceful and sleek & fun loving.  

Love the effort put into the SWAMP exhibit, it's actually humid up there... and the Albino Gator... hello good thing "shootem Clint" didn't see him :)

Not only are you able to see the sights, but you're also able to get in a little Louisiana history in as well... read the walls, just do it.

i recall visiting on a field trip when this place first opened some time ago & I'm glad to say that coming full circle this place still amazes me.

WORD TO THE WISE:
I suggest you print an online discount coupon to reduce the admission price.

This aquarium is very small and parts of it are wholly empty. Compared to other aquariums (Boston, Chicago, Baltimore), it is a waste of time. It's also ridiculously overpriced for what it contains/offers. I wish we hadn't gone.

Very happy and surprised to see another Hyppo location outside of St. Augustine. Simply put, it's a popsicle shop - the larger location on the outskirts of St. Augustine offers food and coffee, but this is just a small outpost, perfect for sating that gourmet icy-pop craving. Yes, it is a craving I do frequently have - I am simultaneously praying for and hoping against the idea that a Hyppo ever opens up in Miami. It'd be dangerous, because I'd want to go quite a bit. 

What flavors do they have? What don't they have? Actually, I can tell you that - unfortunately, this location did not have the pistachio-rose flavor I came to love on Florida's NE coast. All the other flavors are excellent of course, but the pistachio-rose takes the modest popsicle to an entirely new level. Womp womp. Instead, I opted for a jackfruit pop. In case you don't know, a jackfruit is a giant, prehistoric-looking tropical fruit that could weigh up to 50 pounds. It has an odd but ridiculously tasty flavor, one that I can only describe as a cross between banana, bubble gum, and Vidalia onions. The popsicle carried all the unique flavors of the fruit without being overly sweet or syrupy. There was no doubt in my mind that I was getting more real fruit flavor than added sugar.

Nearly......nearly the perfect popsicle. I'll reserve that 5th star until the pistachio-rose comes back, though.

I liked the good variety of sea life exhibited, including penguins, sharks, jellyfish, seahorses, and sea otters. They also had exhibits focused on the Gulf of Mexico and the Mississippi River. Everything was well presented. Overall, very nice!

How did I forget to write my review about this place?!?  Oh well...let's rectify this situation right now.  In New Orleans, outside of eating yourself silly and sleepy, and watching different people do different form or debauchery, there are many family friendly activities in this city.  Audubon Aquarium of Americas is one good family friendly activity in the city.  This place, by no means, is wallet friendly!  Personally, I feel as though this place should come down on its pricing, but I have not been and the place has not been overrun by children.  Best option is to find someone with a year pass and then split the cost between the people that aren't covered by the year pass, if any.

Your children will love seeing the different types of fish and other aquatic entities in this place.  They grab your child's attention right away with an aquarium tunnel that they get to walk through.  The children love having fish on all sides of them, and above them.  There are plenty of factoids and explanations on habitats throughout the place.  There is also plenty of places to have your children strike a pose for cool photos to add to the memories they will certainly garner from this place.  There are also many hands on things for the children to do to ensure they keep themselves engrossed from floor to floor.

I was afraid to visit the food area of this place because if admission was pricey, I know they would have surely made the food expensive as well!  I didn't even let me kids see that part of the building!  Just remember that you can walk to Café Du Monde just up the street!  Beignets can make a child forget that he want pricey aquarium food!  

All in all, you have to do this place at least once.  Have your child, and yourself, touch a sting ray, feed a parakeet and gaze upon gigantic sharks, tarpons, rays and other aquatic species in a 400,000 gallon tank!  Use the website to find out the different things you can do at this place before you even step in this place.  Depending on the size of your group, see if purchasing a season pass would make more financial sense, then buying the one day pass.

I would give this a solid 3.5 stars, and we'll round up! This may be the smallest aquarium that I have ever been to, so if aquariums aren't really your thing already, you will not be very impressed. Additionally, there is a large area under renovation. It's some shark thing. Looks like it will be cool when they're done with it!
The exhibits that they do have are very nice. There's a tube tank that you can walk through. It's sort of short but pretty. There's also a large tank with some bigger sharks and mantas and other rays.
My favorite part though omg - I wasn't even expecting such a wonderful thing - the parakeet room!! You can buy little sugar sticks, but you don't really have to. You just walk in this aviary and the little cute parakeets just start flying all over you! It's so cute and fun - I was ecstatic!
Anyway, if you love aquariums, and you love little parakeets, you'll have a good time!

Extremely disappointed this year! They took out 75% of the Children's play area where they pet the stingrays and added yet another place to spend an additional $6 per person to see the reef?? The entire place needs attention. Looks like nobody doing daily clean up with all the dead leaves/plants, and they are way over grown in areas. Many of the fish tanks were so dirty you could not even see the fish. Then we make it down to the lower level of the huge aquarium to find they have removed the bleachers! Really?? This area is where families like to sit and educate their children as to what they are looking at. Shame on New Orleans for allowing this place to get so run down

I love aquariums ! This one was small yes, but overall it wasn't bad. The only thing I thought was pointless was the hurricane simulator, it was not worth the money. Being able to touch the sting rays was awesome. It was not bad. And they have military discount !

Delicious, all natural & so many flavors! Dairy, dairy-free, vegan - you name it, they have it. 

EXTREMELY dog- friendly. Yes, that means you and your dog can enjoy a popsicle on a hot Florida day. I would highly recommend "The Elvis." It's a peanut butter popsicle and dogs love it. 

I personally have tried the chocolate cheesecake, straight strawberry and a few others. They were all so good. Kind of pricey for a popsicle but hey, YOLO. There's actually a rewards system too if you happen to go often. After eight stamps, you get the next one free. You can also dip any popsicle in chocolate for an extra $1.

Indoor and outdoor seating and plenty of street parking.
Very friendly and helpful and offered samples. Hyppo pops are very reasonable priced and tasty if you like popsicles.
I love these delicious gourmet popsicles! Cute place with indoor OR outdoor seating! Highly recommend!

I've been to several other aquariums and was very under-impressed with this one. While they have quite a few unique fish they are missing some huge elements! And for the price I expected it to be more detailed and quite a bit larger. 
I did enjoy that they had a toddler play area (not huge, but was ample enough for my young grandbabies to expend some energy) and the sting ray petting area was a nice surprise! 
It is a little confusing to first time visitors as to which way to go though, maybe some more signs? I didn't see a stroller rental area, it's possible I missed it, but that would be a great option as this is a very touristy area and not everyone will have their stroller (like us). 
I think if the price had been lower I might could give it more stars. But for the price I will not be back. It was just over $100 for 3 adults, a 2yr old and a 1yr old......WITH a discount! $22 for a 
 2yr old is IMO excessive! YIKES! Plus parking! 
We had more fun outside feeding the pigeons along the river than we did at the aquarium...and that's FREE!

I feel bad awarding only four stars because the food is absolutely amazing... & deserves a solid five stars, plus!  

This is a new location for Torshi, and it's obvious they've got a few kinks to iron out, but trust me, the food isn't one of them.  The service was on point too, considering the fact that our server was new and in need of backup support.  The kitchen staff was new too, but had no trouble putting out the best chicken shawarma platter I've ever had, at a price that had me feeling a little guilty.  Everything on the platter was perfect!  They don't have a liquor license, so I ran home and grabbed a bottle of wine to enjoy with dinner.  I don't know of another place in NOLA where you can get a quality dinner for two for $25... including tip!  

Once they work out the staffing issues and can clean the place up a little, I'm confident that I'll be updating this review and awarding a full five stars!

This is a fun aquarium if you have small children.  The aquarium has an albino alligator along with a fun variety of fish.  There's also an area on the upper level where you can feed beautiful birds. 

Also, check out your family photo that the aquarium takes upon entering; ours turned out really cute. 

It'll take ~2 hours to visit the aquarium.

Note:  you can find coupons on the French Quarter maps provided by the hotels in the area.

STRANGE FLAVOR COMBINATIONS BUT THEY WORK = When you pass a sign announcing the Special as 'Avocado and Serrano Pepper' Popsicles... how could you not? I'll admit my mind was scared imagining I'd be licking frozen Guacamole but (thank goodness) it didn't taste like that at all. Mildly sweet, mildly creamy, gentle Avocado taste and then seconds later there was that spicy Pepper sting as opposed to the Pepper flavor.

NOT YO' MAMA'S POPSICLE = ...And Fiancé Shoes loved his Maple and Pecan version. There's many interesting combinations here--I totally dare you to get out your comfort zone and experiment. If anything your mind gets blown from the possibilities. All ingredients are natural, fresh with several non-dairy options for the lactose allergy crowd. Everything is well labeled. If you're overwhelmed go ahead and chat the staff; they'll help you figure out what you crave.

COOL PLACE TO CHILL ON CENTRAL AVE = Literally 'cool." Hehe. This tiny shop is located on a great section of the growing Central Ave area. Compared to commercial Popsicles, mine melted rather slowly however it is still difficult to wander far while eating a Popsicle. So grab yours and sit at the counter seating facing the road--great people watching. Although tiny, there's plenty of seating here because even with quirky murals the furniture is rather simplistic inside.

I am starting and ending this story on Yelp. I started here as a person who was unhappy with her previous mechanic and who had a car that was making a squeaking noise and occasionally not starting properly, that was also overdue for an inspection and had an expired registration. Sooooo I needed to take care of some business. I called because of the favorable reviews I read and because of the shop's proximity to where I live. Tom got me scheduled asap, allowed me to email in my documents (including my very recently renewed registration), which he later very kindly printed out and left for me. He gave me instructions on how to leave the car since my work schedule was going to make it impossible to drop off or pick up during normal business hours. He let me know what I needed fixed to pass the inspection, and approved the cost with me before starting the work. It was done in the time he said it would be and I was able to pay for it over the phone and pick it up exactly as I expected. The work was very well done and my car runs noticeably better, even sustaining a trip out of town later that same week that had me putting way more miles on her than I usually do. Side note: I've had a very obvious crack in my back bumper since I bought the car, and could never come up with a way to take care of it that didn't involve replacing the bumper, which I don't particularly have any interest in doing. Tom took it upon himself to mend the crack for me and it looks fantastic! I was so grateful, so pleased. Looks like I've found my new mechanic.

Tl;dr: Tom's is a fantastic shop. They do great work, go above and beyond, and have excellent customer service. Take your care there

New Orleans in the spring/summer is hot as hell. Anything that would get us out the heat was going to be a win. When we spot this place, it gave us a solid two hours of cool A/C educational fun. 

Purchasing Tickets was a little strange. While friends waited in line I decided to scope them out online. Purchasing a ticket online is suppose to save you about $4 per adult ticket. After the Convenience Fee and   
Sales Tax most of those savings have disappeared. But, it does allow you priority entry.

I'm a sucker for stingrays and the water teddy bears (otters.) But there was no way I was jumping in a tank to feed them. Luckily others were snorkeling through the Maya Reef habitat and provided great entertainment for us all as we passed through. The Stingray Touchpool was more of my speed.

Adorable children and their adults pressed up against the glass to watch the many animals swim pass. The placed filled with giggles when one of the littlest children started singing Baby Shark and of course the others joined along. Staff helped quiet them down a bit by pointing out animals and asking them questions. This wasn't a group session though. Awesome to see staff still engaging customers even as they pass through different areas. 

Checked how we measured up to the New Orleans Pelican's players in comparison to the Pelicans. See a white gator, old penguins, big snakes and plenty of people posing for their next facebook pics. Jelly Fish Exhibit has people (yes multiple) selling edibles. Yeah that was weird. But the rest of it was awesome, even the gift shop. Not the biggest aquarium around but still very enjoyable. Plastic displays were so insightful.

I just loved this aquarium. It's designed very well for a good walking flow. I felt like I saw everything in a natural path. The line to get in was very long but I didn't feel like it was crowded when I was inside. My favorite part was the bird room. You can purchase seed sticks to feed the birds. With your entrance ticket you can also see a 3D movie which was enjoyable. The penguins and otters were very entertaining too!

Love this place. Definitely a hipster ice cream joint. The freezer is lined with every flavor imaginable. I wish I could literally try all of them. I did have the Horchata popsicle dipped in chocolate. I recommend it any day of any week of any year because it was THAT good. I assume they'll be packed during the summer and spring because who doesn't want a fancy flavored popsicle on a hot day!

Fancy & delish! Coated in chocolate? Even BETTER! we can't get enough of The Hyppo! "The Elvis" is amazing! My husband can't get enough! PB, honey, & banana? Score!
I love all the flavors with Raspberry, most frequently I get the Raspberry Lemonade, freshly covered in Chocolate. I saw they have a Kale Apple Cucumber as a newer "no sugar added" pop, that's definitely on my list to try next!
They have punch cards for frequent poppers, we have gone thru a few cards now. You fill up one with I believe 8 pops and the next is free!
We love grabbing a delicious gourmet popsicle from here and strolling the lil shops of DTSP! It's nice that a lot of shops down by here say they are "Popsicle Friendly" so you can snack while you shop!
Definitely good on a hot or chilly day, honestly they're so tasty!!
Pop in and grab a treat!

Great place to come with families on a hot, humid, or rainy day. Well that's just about everyday then. We always try to be bring out of town visitors with young kids.  The parakeet  aviary is always a great hit and great photo op.

Let me start by saying the people that work here are incredible. So kind and passionate. Okay now the food! I've yet to have one disappointing meal here and I don't think it's coming. The eggplant is maybe my favorite entree. So flavorful and steamy. The salad is fire. Perfect, effervescent dressing on a simple, delicate bed of lettuce. The chicken and gyro are also delicious. I'm a falafel girl and this one hit the mark for me. Nice, large, juicy (not dry, Amen!) and packed with flavor. The hummus is awesome too. Smooth and lemony as it should be. I will say that the baba ganoush tastes like corn, not eggplant. Idk why that is but I still dig it. This is just a heads up, not an "ew". Grapes leaves are on point, get em! And I almost forgot about all the different teas this place has. They are ALL sooo good. Yum town, Louisiana. Go see these guys!

Visiting Peddlers Village for the 1st time. We were courteously greeted by a man at the register. When we asked for seating the gentlemen informed us that there's a room next to their wine tasting area opened. It was very SPACIOUS and wasn't too crowded so we got to rest our feet and enjoy our mulled wines there.

I LOVE MULLED WINE AND couldn't decide between their selection.....Spiced Apple or Holiday Spirit. The host at the wine tasting bar offered samples to assist with my decision. HOLIDAY SPIRIT was tasty and kept us very warm. It was FLAVORFUL and PERFECTLY spiced.  We had a wonderful experience from our greeting to grabbing our mulled wines to go! :) 

I would recommend making a stop here. Overall service and wine was very GOOOOD!!

It's a cool aquarium but I think it's insanely overpriced. If you plan on going more than once in a year, get the membership. If I recall correctly, this is one of the top things to do in New Orleans on TripAdvisor but I think that's a bit generous. You can go to an aquarium anywhere and this one isn't special. However, it is a nice thing to do with kids, especially at this time of year when the air conditioning is greatly appreciated.

Had to go here while in New Orleans because everyone told me to. Glad I went. $35 a ticket for adults. 

It's a nice medium sized acquarium with lots of exhibits. My favorites were the penguins and the shark tank. The shark tank is massive and includes many other big fish as well.

You could spend a couple hours here there is plenty to see and read.

Overall I'd recommend especially if you're staying at a hotel nearby, as it's an easy walk. It's also in a great place with many restaurants nearby.

Nice to have a new face in the St Roch market. Honestly, some of the best Middle Eastern food I've had the pleasure of eating in this city. Suck it, Mona's.
All ingredients are fresh and well prepared. The hummus is smoother than my wife's bum, the eggplant dish more heavenly than my wife's bum*, the shoarma... is well seasoned.
Good prices too.

* My wife has a really nice bum

I've literally NEVER been a popsicle person in my life until I had The Hyppo. The sheer variety of flavors (traditional and crazy) is impressive and the quality is fantastic. Personal favorites include: Chocolate Cheesecake, Avocado Serrano, Blackberry Ginger, Pineapple Hatch Chili, and Watermelon Basil.

Variety of Flavors: 5/5
Quality: 5/5
Service: 5/5
Price: 4/5 (a little pricy for a popsicle)
OVERALL: 5/5

Went 4/18 and I understand that there were weather issues that caused most of the cities business to close around 2, but when you sell people tickets at 12:30 with a message that you're closing at 2, you should at least do so at a discount.

Pleasantly surprised by our experience here! There was so much to see. Every time I thought we were near the end there was another room! I enjoyed walking under the tunnel and seeing the penguins and sea otters. We were able to watch them getting fed which was really fun. 

We went on the weekend during the afternoon which seemed like a very busy time. Lots of families. Social distancing wasn't really enforced and there were times I felt pretty cramped. I don't believe there's a time limit for your reservation. Just takes a little patience to see the exhibits social distanced but it's definitely possible :)

My first experience was great! My friends and I walked in during a busy time of the day (noonish) and there was 4 people in front of me in line. I only waited about 20-25 minutes before Mike took me in his chair. He did such a quick job with my nails, but it was not a bad job at all!! I got a full set done for $25 plus a tip. Mike was one of the best nail techs I've ever had! They treat their regulars very well here and prefer that you call to make an appointment but walk ins are welcome. The salon was very clean and well kept, but I would probably have more staff that were there to keep people from potentially waiting so long. Overall I would totally recommend this place to get your mani and pedis done!
Starfruit Habernero - Blueberry Clove - Ginger Dragonfruit - these are some of the exotic ice pops at this incredible place. Just try and only go once...

Severely lacking in information on the species, which in my opinion education is one of the main reasons for these institutions to exist. Some exhibits seemed too small for the size and number of fish present. Overall very underwhelming.
Love this place. Go every time I'm in DTSP. I really like the Coconut popsicle but every single flavor I've got has been delicious. Perfect dessert to end the night!

Every woodworker, machinists, and do it yourself home repair person should visit this store.  You can find everything you want when it comes to tools. And if they don't have it, they will help you get it. As a wife of a do it yourself fixer, they are the best at helping me find a gift for my husband.
I love their strawberry popsicles! Never been to the place before and I was pleasantly surprised but how much it tastes like actual strawberry.
The kids had a wonderful time today. They saw everything they wanted to see except whales. We will definitely be back to do this again.

(6/21/2014)  Place is inside the Peabody food court on 4th.  This was our first taste of Nashville Hot Chicken (did do a little research with the Saveur article); we were prepared to wait, each serving is cooked to order.   The chef/owner, Aqui Simpson came out to chat and check in on us (I guess we looked like tourists); service was very friendly, prices reasonable.  Chicken is moist and juicy, spices are in the breading/coating (light, crisp, flaky) and also mixed into the hot oil topping smeared/drizzled over the finished pieces.  Had the 200 degrees; I laughed, I cried, my nose ran, my tongue and lips went numb, and at some point, the heat of the chicken mixed with the heat of the spices made it painful to eat, it was just right for me.  My friend had the 400 degree wings, he looked like he was going to pass out.  I don't know if maybe it was my lack of experience with hot chicken, but flavor seemed kind of bland for all the spice.  I tasted predominantly cayenne, paprika and black pepper, but I could've used a little saltiness or savoriness (maybe some garlic?).  Cole slaw and potato salad were OK, ordinary, tangy (but you might want to get them anyway for their cooling effect on the tongue).The place was going to close at 5 pm the day we were there, but there was def a line for that last batch of chicken.  One local guy said he was there every single day for the 400 wings.  I imagine he has no colon left.  They weren't lying when they said "chicken so hot it'll burn you twice."

First off, I want to say how much I love this wine. We have visited the winery many times and the owners and staff are lovely and treat you like family. 

With that being said, I have never had good experiences coming to this location and last Saturday really drove me over the edge. My mother in law (who buys cases of this wine) and a few others from our family came into the store 13 minutes before closing. People were doing tastings and we wanted to look around and see if there were any new wines. Well, the two women running the store did not like the fact we walked in before closing. One said a rude comment to my mother in law when she asked about one of the wines and followed it with "don't expect a tasting we are closing". I walked to the far end with my 10 month old strapped to me to look at a wine. I literally heard the woman working say to a couple who was tasting "don't worry we will get them out of here, quick. We won't offer them a tasting". I literally stood there stunned, and the worker refused to make eye contact with me. I felt insulted, especially with my baby right there. 

We wanted to buy wine, but instead left upset and went to Free Will brewery and and had a great time. 

Unfortunately this is not the first time we have heard and encountered rude comments but this really is unacceptable.

I made it a most to see the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas when I came to visit new Orleans. it was a good experience, they have a cute little are for the penguins.  And being from the west coast I didn't know that there was a  giant white alligator or that they had one!!

the only real negative is a big one, that a lot of the other yelper said as well; "we saw everything in the aquarium in hour, and  For the price it's a bit disappointing.

The Hyppo is as hipster as you can possibly get, but no matter your feelings on hipsters, it doesn't matter because fancy popsicles are apparently delicious.

We went with a group of friends after lunch on a hot summer afternoon. Everyone enjoyed their order, but I can personally vouch for the champagne mango. They're $3.75 a pop (pun intended) which feels pricy for a popsicle, but really isn't for a gourmet dessert.

I wouldn't drive across Pinellas for a special trip here, but I would definitely stop by again when I'm in the neighborhood.

This is a nice aquarium but for me, the WOW factor was parakeet pointe. Sooooo cool! You can buy a stick of food to feed them, but we chose not to. Upon entering, the parakeets just flew on top of us. They are fearless birds that kept trying to sneak into my bag, our pockets, and hoods. I let them go into my bag from the back, they were adorable. The one that went from the front of my bag, I used my arm to block her after she landed on my bag and she was not having it. She nipped my arm. I got scared after that lol. But before that, it was amazing. They land on your head too. Before we left the area, turned out a parakeet actually snuck into my husband's hood and was chilling there. Before you leave, the workers will double-check to make sure if any birds have hidden away in your belongings. There's also a mirror for you to check yourself before leaving parakeet pointe. 

This aquarium is pleasant. Highly recommend to stop off here!

I felt cheated today at a cost of $85 for 2 adults & 1 child. Some of the exhibits at the rain forest were "under construction." The giant fish tank from what I remember in the past use to be a cool environment in air temperature, but I felt warm. There is way too many kids on field trips that are not being chaperone properly to where those kids are running freely throughout the property.

Let me first say that Hot Chicken is a way of life and when it comes to expectations, mine are very high.  

When you finally find this place (it is in a building that houses Quiznos and Nuvo Burrito) be ready or true Southern hospitality.  The owner and everyone helping are so personable and make you feel like you are about to sit down to eat at their own kitchen table.  

I ordered the breast quarter at 400 degrees (HAD TO) with crinkle fries and potato salad.  Be aware that the chicken is made to order and that you will have around a 30 minute wait from ordering to eating.  Do not fret, it is worth it.  You can walk a couple blocks to a Shell station and pick yourself up some milk if you want to be a veteran about it...

The chicken had an amazing flavor and just the right amount of kick.  My nose was running and my eyes had the slightest of tears, but I was never miserable.  Just a great heat level to accompany an expert breading and moist chicken.  The crinkle fries had a great seasoning to them and the potato salad was excellent.

Overall, the only reason this is not 5 stars is because I was left wanting more.  Not a bad thing in the least.  I would recommend going with the tenders for ease of eating and for overall amount of chicken to devour.

Happy 25th birthday Audubon Aquarium! I've been coming here since I was a kid and it remains one of my favorite things about NOLA. 

The aquarium is spread out across two floors with several different sections depending on the type of animals. Watch out for the rainforest section, yall! I thought Louisiana was humid...

My favorite part is watching the penguins and I hear that for a fee, you can get up close and personal with them. There is also a stingray tank where you can pet them (pretty slimy!). 

The facility is clean and very well kept up. There are also good food courts inside if you get hungry. 

Tip: I attended the Scales and Ales event this year and it was amazing! The ticket was $75 and you get free food and drinks from several local restaurants and free reign of the facility. Great way to support both the Audubon aquarium and zoo. If you can make it next year, you should definitely go!

Such a hot day ! I needed to cool down. Something healthy too! I came across this icy pop shop! So many frozen fruit treats to chose from! I chose the blueberry açaí. I am thrilled with my choice! Heavenly. 
Nice taste. Natural and so many health benefits. I ate my pop in the shop bc it was too hot to walk and eat. It's blueberry and I didn't want to make a mess. 
Stay inside and enjoy the charming pop art mural.  The fella working there was ultra nice , patient and helpful. 
FYI: They sell kid sizes if you need a smaller size.  Only 2 flavors available in kid sizes. 
Enjoy!!

Not as grand as I remember as a child. But it looks like they're putting some more work into different exhibits currently. Price is a bit steep, but the joint/package pricing is no terrible.

Staff are very friendly. I lost my stub, which I needed for the zoo later, and it was no problem getting a new one.

Love the jellyfish and seahorse exhibits.

We walked in right as the stingrays the other fish were being fed.  Then we petted stingrays with their stingers taken off.  They were amazing to touch.  It is funny but in the South and Midwest, there is a tendency to put fish in area that say things like "live bait."  Like the difference between California and the South is that CA helps save fish for the environment, while the South and Midwest show that if the fish are healthy, then we have more of them to eat!  Hey, I am a Midwest girl myself, I get it. :)  It has a good amount of sharks, the most lionfish I have seen anywhere, jellyfish, sea horses, tons of fish, frogs, penguins, otters and even a room where you can feed cute tiny birds and have them sit on your hand.  It's a little bit more than just ocean life.  I had a fun time and of course, the stingrays were my favorite.

Maybe it's because I'm not from Nashville, but I didn't see the big deal about 400 degrees. I ordered the chicken strips at 200 degree heat along with the baked beans as a side. The baked beans were pretty sugary, but they were fine. Not amazing, not so sweet that I was overwhelmed. They were also pretty nice to help out with the spice from the chicken, which did have some serious heat. I didn't enjoy the flavor at all though, so it made the whole experience pretty blah. In fact, I was dunking the chicken in ranch so I could get better taste.

Despite the subpar taste of the chicken, the worst part was the wait. It took upwards of 30 minutes just to get an order for two people. And mind you, this isn't a fancy sit down place. It's a food court. Luckily, we weren't in a huge rush, but it got to be a bit much for the wait. Service was polite, so I can't give this a 1 star, but between the wait and the taste, I wouldn't return here.

I have been visiting Tom's Automotive over the years for Subarus and an old Chevy truck.  Most of the time I leave feeling like I didnt pay enough.  In the past I've used different shops for each vehicle because places specialized in either new or old but not both.   They now have an expanded service center and off street parking which has greatly improved their ability to turn around work.

Walking around downtown St. Pete on a hot day and we just couldn't resist. We looked at their menu online and couldn't believe that all the flavors listed would actually be available. Boy, were we wrong! Our group had a hard time deciding but the staff is very helpful and had more patience than I! I selected the goat cheese blackberry. It was absolutely outstanding! The goat cheese was there but not overpowering. My boyfriend selected the Matcha peach which was a bit on the sweet side but still very fresh tasting. They do some strange flavor combinations but I'm looking forward to going back for more. Only bummer is, they don't do samples but luckily the popsicles aren't too expensive (I believe $3.75) so you can try a few without breaking the bank. The inside of this store is quaint and colorful and very inviting. I didn't mind spending some time in the AC on a hot day with a delicious popsicle.

Popsicles galore ! ! ! 

There are tons of adult magazines out there... some very skanky and dirty... and some that are more "soft"... some that show more than expected and some where people tend to read the articles too (or so they claim)... magazines such as Screw, Swank and High Society may all be adult magazines but at the end of the day no one holds a candle to Playboy.... That is THE HYPPO in a nutshell !

* * * DECOR * * * 

Colorful and pleasant with childish murals on the walls to make you feel that much more comfortable... community tables and of course the ordering counter which is actually the freezers with the huge assortment of flavors.  I love the use of todays style (white subway tile on the back wall with plank wood overlaid onto the freezers which beats the typical white freezers).

* * * CHOICES * * *

When it's time to pick a flavor, or better yet, when it's time to pick your favorite flavor combination, it's certainly a tough choice.  Without exaggeration, I do believe they offer plus/minus 50 popsicle flavors; yes, that was FIFTY FLAVORS !

I'd like to think that kids with their parents would have a simple time making a decision but once I read the list of flavors I kinda think kids would have some hesitations since I really see simple choices like chocolate or vanilla since most of flavor combinations. For example, many of the fruit choices are mixed with popular herbs such like "Blueberry Cinnamon", "Honeydew Basil", Cantaloupe Black Pepper", "Pineapple Cilantro", "Watermelon Mint" and "Ginger Plum".  

But then again they do offer combinations that may attract kids too such as "Banana Vanana" (which is banana vanilla), "Peanut Butter Pie", "Elvis" (which I believe is peanut butter, banana and honey), "Raspberry Lemonade" and "Pina Colada" (which of course is pineapple and coconut).

As for me, so far my favorites have been "Bourbon Peach" and "Mexican Hot Chocolate"

And don't forget for a small additional fee you can have your popsicle covered in a chocolate shell.  Personally I don't really care for it considering how flavorful most of these combinations are already; and I think the chocolate masks out the taste of the more subtle flavors. 

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * 

To make a long story short... the kind of place that let's adults feel like little kids again... Kids are welcome too but I like to think this place is here for me.

SUCH A COOL PLACE! The Hyppo is one of the neatest little places we have been since you don't typically see a popsicle store around! Popsicles are delicious and I personally felt that the prices were reasonable. 

Perfect place to stop for a sweet treat in Downtown St. Pete!

Oh. My. Gosh. I wanted to try alllll of them. My guanabana was amazing and took me back to Ecuador when I first tried the fruit - so authentic! My husband liked his key lime dipped in chocolate. Things we learned - they can dip any popsicle in chocolate for $1 (apparently free if you only want it half dipped), and unbeknownst to me the "datil" is a kind of spicy yet sweet local pepper that they use in some of their popsicles!

I first stumbled upon this place just this year to get a pedicure and was very impressed by the strong feeling of community here.  I had great conversation with the couple sitting next to me as well as all of the employees.  I've since been back in for pedicures, nails and a few massages by and am impressed by how friendly they all are.  They take pride in their work and I look forward to going.  So happy I found them and recommend them highly.  Thanks, Gio, Mike, Dee, Linsey and Willie, you a solid gold

Before our most recently visit I had not been to this aquarium in about 14 years. I was excited to come back and experience it again with my young nieces. There was a wide variety of fishes and other marine life including turtles, mana rays, sharks, and many more. Several of the tanks had a rock wall with foot holds and ledges to little ones could climb up and see. There were talks, touch pools, and a play area for the kids about half way through. We were pleased that they carried the same aluminum water bottles that the zoo does. They also were featuring several sculptures made from plastic waste to high light the impact of plastic in our oceans. The gift shop was reasonably priced and had several items, including several small stuffed animals that were copies of the fishes and animals. My nieces had a fantastic time, and I can't wait to come back with them again.

Great Popsicles!! I've read other reviews and am at a loss when people complain about the price. It's $4 a pop but they're sooooo good, and made with local produce. That kind of production is obviously going to be at a higher price. I go all the time though and have a bunch of punch cards saved up for a rainy day. Overall, I think it's always great to try new things and the popsicle selection they have always allows me to try something new. I'll admit that some flavors I don't like over others but that's just my preference.

Awesome food with great customer service! I really wanted to try the King Tut which is a falafel with a hard boiled egg in it. I went for dinner and typically they only serve it for breakfast. When I went to order I asked if they were still serving it, the cashier seemed unsure if they could but the chef cut in and said of course they could but it would be made to order and might take a little longer. I was so excited! Most places really stick to their menu especially when  something is labeled as breakfast  but I was excited that they were flexible and made exactly what I wanted. 

This dish is delicious! It has amazing flavor and comes on a bed of wonderful hummus and pita on the side. There is a side salad that was fresh and came with great dressing. The pita comes warm and is very thin which is great for dipping. I definitely recommend this food stand in St Roch and the King Tut dish!

Absolutely love the town and the Popsicles here were really good. Love all the weird flavors they have. My sister had honey honeydew which was really creamy and delicious. Definitely could taste the honey. I had guava hibiscus which was good, but the bar had tiny ice crystals formed on it like ice cream that has been in the freezer too long. Would definitely come back when in the area.

Although I've been to many aquariums over Europe and the US (my sister is a huge fan of all kinds of fish), this one has been special. The devision into different oceans and seas with their flora and fauna is implemented very well. This place seemed educative to me, as it points out the environmental problems we're facing. Make sure you also visit the IMAX theater.

This is my favorite hot chicken place in Nashville. Not only do they have hot chicken, but hot (and mild) fried pork chops (bone-in) too! What delicious pain they serve up-and with exceptional customer service too (unlike other similar establishments). 
Side note: the location was new and well kept, so this would be a good place to take out-of-towners or business clients for an honest taste of Nashville. 
The owner was super friendly (and generous) too!
It's a good thing 400 Degrees isn't near me (in terms of calories) because I would eat here everyday if I could!
Beautiful aquarium- the tanks are really well maintained and fish are healthy! I have visited several aquariums on trips and this was a very nice one. Great to see animals well fed and content!

Wow.  It's getting hot in here.

400 degrees hotter, to be exact.  A relatively new player to the Hot Chicken market here in Nashville (who knew there'd be such a niche?), 400 Degrees packs a lot of heat into a little joint.

Ok, so maybe the area of town isn't the greatest.  And maybe parking isn't fantastic.  Oh, and perhaps the sign isn't that visible so that you end up driving by a cemetery five times before you see it (talk about a buzz kill).

But oh, is this Chicken worth it.  Served in three levels of heat (100 to 400 degrees - get it?), this chicken is worth the drive and worth the wait.

Similar to one of the other major players in town (Prince's Hot Chicken), the secret of this chicken is in the rub and the marinade.  So expect your chicken, your bread, your bag and your car seat to be sopped in grease once you pick up your order.

However, unlike some of the other players, you don't have to wait an hour to get your meal.  Call it in, pick it up, and you are licking pure heat off your fingers within minutes.

And don't forget the sides.  The standard fares of French fries, Cole slaw and the likes are done with southern grace here, and slightly infused with a bit of the spice.

A word to the wise - no matter how much this chicken makes you cry, please make sure to wash your hands before you wipe your tears.  Trust me, however, this chicken is worth a little pain.
Wide range of popsicle flavors and wonderful staff. I recommend "Banilla Vanana," but all popsicles I have tried thus far have been delectable.

Something about the layout of this store always bothers me, but I'll deal with it for the Vera Wang jeans alone! 

They fit me like a glove - small waist and all - yay! 

I also bought my first Christmas gift - not intended, but I couldn't pass up either!  Perfect for my good friend! 

I got $10 KOHL's CASH too - I'll definitely be back to use it!

My husband and I were here on vacation and visited Monday July 8th in the afternoon. The aquarium was great and a nice break from the hot weather. We especially loved the birds. The only down side was we ordered an ice cream and sat down at the tables in front of the papa johns they have inside the aquarium. While waiting at the register another patron and her children spotted a rat behind the counter. The customer told three different staff members who shrugged their shoulders and continued to cook food for other customers. Disgusting! They should have shut down the entire kitchen right then and there . Aquarium and birds were wonderful just skip eating there.

I read it was supposed to be one of the top 5 Aquariums in the states. I did go on a cloudy day but the aquariums seemed dirty and there were several fish that appeared to be sick. The water was cloudy in the big tank.  On a positive note they were cleaning tanks and had some holiday spirit ( I went the week of Halloween) and the divers were dressed in costumes and actually carving pumpkins underwater.

It's smaller than I expected. Not much by was of interactive exhibits. I'm usually into these things, but quickly found myself uninterested- as was my six-year-old. Not worth the price alone. May have been a better experience had we purchased the package that included the Zoo and other activities. Many exhibits were closed which was also a disappointment.

I have a video I wanted to post about my experience, but sadly, Yelp doesn't allow videos. I went to The Hyppo when I went to visit my fiends in the Tampa Bay Area. They have a Hyppo where I went to school at in Jacksonville, so I figured I would try the store front. This place is just as I remembered it back in college. They have a WIDE variety of flavors and are extremely creative when it comes to the flavor combinations. 
I got the peanut butter and banana one (the Elvis). It was so good! If you want a refreshing treat, go to the Hyppo. It's worth the calories.

Have you been to Torshi yet? 
This Mediterranean spot has amazing food. I really enjoyed the brunch: Mezze Platter (baba ganoush, Labneh, grape leaves & eggplant ). The ROASTED EGGPLANT was incredible. 
Delicious  and worth a visit.
I love the relaxed atmosphere. My nails always look good when I leave My Nails. (pun) This is one of the better nail salons.

This aquarium was lovely! They had tons of different fish, from the local to the exotic. There was also a really cool hands on aspect with the sting rays (which were so friendly!). 

A good chunk of the place was under construction which kind of sucked but there was still so much to do and see. Would love to return to catch one of the films!

We visited the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas in New Orleans in January 2017.  I've been to countless aquariums over the years, many of which have been ranked in the top 10 of aquariums in the country.  We were excited to visit this aquarium as well, especially after we learned that it has been ranked as a top 10 aquarium.  There are plenty of animals and the aquarium has a good number of exhibits, but it wasn't as large as I'd hoped, especially given the admission price ($30 per person).  I did enjoy the jellyfish exhibit and seeing the rays and penguins, especially, but the number of exhibits and the size of the aquarium don't really justify the hefty admission price.  Still, I think it's a fun afternoon activity when you're visiting New Orleans, and the aquarium is located conveniently within walking distance of the French Quarter and connects to the French Quarter via Woldenberg Park, which affords great views of the Riverfront area of the Mississippi river.

I'm not even a big fan of "sweets," but this place is great. There are so many different flavors and mixtures and everything is extremely #fresh. #FloridaSummer is almost here, so I imagine #TheHyppo will be frozen-popping their brains out here soon enough. They have different #popflavors all the time and they're constantly adding new #creativeconcoctions. You can find everything from sweet to savory to spicy and combos of all. BONUS: The amazing mural by #MelodiousMonster. Good job all around.

Best place in Reno for power tools, woodworking machines and accessories. The guys and gals are always super helpful and know their stuff.  They have all the goods from DeWalt, Makita, Milwaukee, Hitachi, Porter Cable, Festool and a thousand others.

The aquarium itself was nice.  All of the exhibits seemed well maintained.
My only complaint is that when I went on line and purchased the tickets, it was stated that the admission price was good for the aquarium AND the Imax.  When we got there and inquired about show times--- we were told that they had closed the Imax indefinitely.  This would have been good info to know on the front end before purchasing the tickets.  The young lady at the door, sounded like she was readying for a script and only would say that "they have closed the Imax indefinietly".

This was a little disappointing.. some exhibits were under construction. Unfortunately we made it through the aquarium rather quickly. It was nice, clean, but very quick. A nice quick activity, but not sure if I'd go back.

This place is incredible. I normally wouldn't pay more than a dollar for a popsicle, but once I knew what goes into making these puppies I was hooked and never hesitated on the price. This isn't your normal popsicle place. With flavors like Rose pistachio, blueberry clove, peanut butter banana dipped in chocolate, and hibiscus, I've become addicted. You have to try it and you won't be disappointed. For foodies: try the Apple Honey Goat cheese pop.
Long Line Long Line.... Even if you bought the membership and made reservation, you still have to wait in regular ticket line.  What is the point of making reservations ... ridiculous policy.

Loved it and I am a grown behind woman 

Enjoyed the bird exhibit where you can feed and hold the birds

There is also an area where you can sign up to feed the sting rays. Did this, got wet, the sting ray didn't take the dead fish from me, and so I gave up and just petted him 

Come in just to enjoy yourself

Watch the feeding of the penguins and learn about how they live and survive, walk through the rainforest (remember don't touch anything), check out the albino alligator, brush up on your Mayan/Aztec history, and teach read up on various species

If that is not enough there are various movie showings in the other area of the aquarium (about 30 minutes a piece) that add to your knowledge 

Bring your kids, adults, friends, and family

This trail system was amazing!!  We rode our mountain bikes here after finding the trail system listed on MTB Project...and boy, are we glad we did.  We rode the Bunny Loop, Snake Dance, and Bunny's Revenge the first day, about a 7 mile set of loop trails that were very well marked, and obviously lots of care and maintenance on these desert trails.  We rode two weekdays and a Friday here, and the trails were only really busy on Friday mid-morning.  Plentiful and easily accessed parking was available.  What impressed us the most was the many cool trail signs, and desert knick nacks that were used as either memorials, or trail markers.  The trails were easy to find and route each time we rode.  The second day we entered the trail system from the north and rode Lone Cactus Loop, which was more of a blue trail with some fun ups and downs.  Definitely a better workout on that trail than the Bunny Loop, but the lower loops would be a great warm up to link with the northern trails.  Again, Lone Cactus Loop was very well marked and maintained.  There was one section that was especially challenging and it was aptly signed "Half Pipe."  I loved it, but my wife didn't enjoy some of the steeps as much.  We have ridden everywhere, from Moab to Sedona, and many places in California.  These trails we would highly recommend to visiting folks who may have never ridden in the desert or want to just get a good work out in.  They were a great introduction to the area, so much so that we didn't really seek out any other trails.  5 stars for sure, and just ride these great trails and have fun!!!

My husband and I love aquariums and we go to one on every trip possible. This aquarium is severely over priced. What they do have is nice, but they don't have much so why did I pay $30 per person? We had seen everything in about an hour, and it only took that long because we watched a presentation that took about 20 minutes. They need to drop the price by about 60% to make this even close to worth it.

We came here on Monday, the day of Lundi Gras.  On Yelp it, said it was closed on Mondays.  We were going to walk away but we noticed people buying tickets and walking in.  We lucked out and were able to buy tickets to the aquarium...it's $25 per person.

It brought out the kid in me to see all types of sea creatures.  They also had one section/room where they had parakeets flying around freely.  At one point, we saw a random owl just sitting on top of some rocks.   It was funny because one of us swore it was real, while two of us thought it was fake.  Our one friend said she saw it blink, so we're just standing there staring at it waiting for it to move.  We were standing there for about 10 mins when it finally moved..it is real.

I find it relaxing watching these sea amimals swimming in the water...

Just heard on the news that Hitler's alligator died at the age of 84 in the Moscow Zoo, where it had been since 1946.  Reminds me of the alligator that I saw in a zoo.

Rainy day in New Orleans, January 2020, so we walked a half mile to the river to the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas.  

Small aquarium compared to some others that I've seen, most recently the Honolulu Aquarium and the Maui Ocean Center in Wailuku.    Pricey $28 entry fee, and that's with advance purchase and senior discount.

Visitors enter the aquarium through a see-through tunnel, with fish, sharks, manta rays swimming above and around you on both sides.  

Always fun to watch the feeding of  sea otters, stingrays, and particularly the penguins, with their human like reactions to checking out the fish.
Big floor to ceiling glass exhibits of various fish swimming.  

They have a caged area called Parrott Pointe, where you can feed the parrots food sticks, with them getting all over and under your coats.  Unfortunately due to the rainy weather, this exhibit was closed.

They also have an Imax theater, with two shows coming with the ticket price.  Remember seeing the Katrina movie, where the hurricane came ashore and devastated the city.  

Anaconda snakes, macaws, man eating piranhas, and string rays in the Amazon exhibit.  Angelfish and tarpon in the Caribbean reef exhibit.  17 feet tall  400,000-gallon tank with moray eels, stingrays, sharks, and sea turtles in the Gulf of Mexico exhibit.  Catfish, owls, paddlefish, and pufferfish in the Mississippi River Gallery.   African penguins, sea otters, seahorses, and jelly fish in other exhibits.

Highlight of the 4 hour visit had to be the white alligator.  He just floated on the surface, but the glass partitions reflected the light so that he looked a lot larger than he was.  He had a dark gray spot on his snout, so I'm not sure he was an albino.     

Twenty years earlier with my ex, I had visited a white alligator in New Orleans, who was a true albino, completely white with eyes shining in the dark.  Likely this was the same alligator, who had outlived my first marriage, and well into my second marriage.   

And with this coronavirus going around unchecked, with no vaccine in sight, this alligator may outlive me, a senior male with underlying conditions!

They also have a companion Audubon Butterfly Garden and Insectarium.  Wife is big into butterflies, but I told her there's no need to pay to see the Insectarium, when we can see cockroaches in the local hotel for free!

My husband and I stopped in to check the place out. They do not offer a military discount for tickets but we were told they offer it in the cafe and gift shop. 

The place was two levels with a variety to include penguins, a variety of fish and a rainforest level. I was not a fan of the rainforest as it is already humid in New Orleans. 

We did get a chance to watch them feed the sting rays while there. 

Overall it was only okay. I've been to better aquariums and also worst. So on a rainy day while visiting I would come here but besides that I don't think I would have.

My laptop was completely hacked and Frank immediately came to the rescue! I don't know what I would have done without him and I definitely appreciated his explanation of te,hnical things that I had no clue about AND his reasonable price!

Specifically asked for corsage with red roses and got one with cheap red carnations. When tried to resolve problem, owner started yelling. Poor customer service. Corsage looked cheap. Should have gone to Dierbergs or Schnucks where we normally go.

Small aquarium but VERY CLEAN. It was kind of empty when we went on a Tuesday. I purchased the Audubon experience package and thought it was a great deal. You get to visit the aquarium, zoo, and Insectarium for 49.95 which is a steal compared to the individual prices for each. Can't expect too much from exhibits like this, most aquariums are small. The free movie was a little dry... but that is just my taste. I think it is a great place for a date or family outing. Smells better than Sea World too! 

Here is a small video recap of my experience: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RFsqyYUmKk8&list=PLyxP-Cz5LtfGKjvGj90p7V1PJ5cw7ATmQ&index=5

Only 5 stars because of Mary M. She is an excellent asset to the store and always goes out of her way to make people feel welcome. She also tracks down products when others (stores) don't.  She's fabulous and I'm very impressed with her work ethic. I live closer to another Kohls but find myself going out of my way to go here because of people like her.  (Not that others at this store aren't great but I go straight to her line! Lol)

The man working there was super knowledgeable about the flavors and very helpful! The flavors were so unique and they had such an array, it was difficult to pick just two. Mine was mango with habanero which was so delicious and subtle I was actually surprised. You can tell that the popsicle is 100% natural with nothing added. Definitely recommend!

This is kind of a lame aquarium.  You can blow through the whole thing in under an hour.  Even if you took your time you'd be hard pressed to spend more than 90 minutes here.  As others have mentioned, there were a lot of spelling errors on the signs, as well as fish that seemed kind of out of place for the habitat that the aquarium was claiming they belonged to (but don't in actuality).  I also found the corporate sponsorship more than a tad unsettling.  On the walls beside the large tank are plaques for Shell, Exxon, BP, etc.

There was also a film and audio loop near the entrance...not really loud enough to be an actual presentation...almost purposefully subliminal...that I didn't even pick up on until I overheard it saying something along the lines of offshore drilling being great for the environment because the coral and marine life flock to the base of the rigs "and it gives them a home in an otherwise barren deep sea environment".  Ninja, puh-leez!  Not only is this a scientifically unsound, factually inaccurate crock of industry-funded propaganda b.s., but given how much BP & Halliburton just essentially ruined the entire gulf region, I found it to be incredibly tasteless as well.

There are two locations in the Tampa Bay Area. One in St. Petersburg and the other is in Hyde Park. 

There are many popsicles to choose from. Some are only seasonal. 
There are some popsicles that are more fruity and some more creamy.
All the flavors I tried before were amazing. It's all natural and you can really taste the fruit. 
Today we chose blueberry cheesecake and apple cranberry. Both great but I think I prefer the blueberry more because it's slightly sweeter. 

Stuff is always friendly and helpful.

I highly recommend it.

One of the best aquariums I have visited - and I am from Florida, so that says a lot! This is a fairly decent sized two story aquarium and there's TONS of different sea creatures to look at. My favorite part was definitely Parakeet Pointe! I LOVED feeding all the cute little birdies! I also loved petting the sting rays!

The location is convenient to visitors staying in the French Quarter - it is directly across the street from Harrah's Casino which is surrounded by tons of restaurants and shopping. 

A word of advice: Pull out cash before entering the aquarium.
They have amazing customer service and really go above and beyond to make sure everyone is happy. Flowers are so beautiful. Will use again for sure.

Just like almost every other person who has been here, I love it! Endless choices but my favorite is the Coconut Coconut so I do have to say, I have been to every local location that Hyppo has in the Tampa Bay area and more often times than not, they are ALL out of this flavor. 

They are always polite and apologize and say it's one of their best sellers... so my thought process to that if this is the same outcome at every location... order MORE at one time or the company needs to boost up the production numbers for a sell out item. It does get kinda annoying when you can never get your favorite flavor and one of their staples so you leave empty handed more often than not. 

I will still walk in and check if I am in the area or any of their locations to check though... and have even called ahead.

Amazing hummus!  Perhaps the best I have ever had. Sampled the ginger mango tea and a mint one and both were absolutely excellent.  I am sure anything on the menu is excellent after trying the grape leaves, hummus and salad.  Loved the atmosphere of St Roch Market as well.
Very nice and lots to do! My kids didn't want to leave! Very friendly staff and good food too!

My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed our visit. The staff were friendly and helpful. The exhibits were nice and the whole aquarium was clean and well kept. We were able to catch the otter feeding and it was a great highlight to our visit. We paid the extra $1.50 for a stick to feed the birds. In my opinion that is a fair price.
