The price of the food was ridiculous, however. But, what are you to expect when you're eating in an aquarium. We bought the package Audubon experience deal and it was worth it!
Such a great addition to St Pete. Get yours dipped in chocolate for an extra treat. Love the strawberry basil & peppery cantaloupe.

I haven't been back to the Aquarium ever since I was a little girl growing up in NOLA and I was excited to come back with my baby to see all of the animals. First of all it was pretty pricey, $30 for adults and free for the baby. Fortunate for me, I was able to find some tickets online which was $60 for 4 tickets, but shipping of $5 because it as from Ohio. 

The exhibits seemed smaller from what I remember and there weren't as many animals as before. There use to be more fish in the big tank with the sharks. I wonder if Katrina might have wiped out some of the animals. I was somewhat disappointed. It was definitely not worth the price. It was nice, however that the IMAX movie was included in the ticket price. It used to be separate, but then maybe that's what makes the ticket more expensive. 

I think that it was a nice experience for the kids, but as an adult I expected more. It was just fun for the baby to get to come to the aquarium that his mom used to go to as a little girl.
Kids dream! Popsicles! Kellen enjoyed his banana split one. I tried few licks. Definitely tasted like banana. Unfortunately only popsicles but if that's what u are looking for...

The service is always friendly and helpful. The owner is almost always there and he's wonderful. 
The food is amazing! I love Middle Eastern food and have tried all the local places (Kebab, Stella Maris, Mona's, etc) and Torshi is my new favorite. Everything is seasoned perfectly and tastes FRESH. My favorite is the grape leaves platter but the eggplant is also fabulous. I don't eat meat but my boyfriend says the chicken is moist and delicious and the lamb is the best he has ever had and melts in his mouth. The drinks are great too; I like the Rose-Hibiscus ice tea best. Can't wait to come back! Thanks!!!

Love coming to the aquarium! My 7 year old is fascinated by seeing all the sea creatures!! Brought my 8 month old son for the first time today and he loved it as well!! On the downside I do hate that we have to pay SO MUCH $$ to park while we go here! $22 for 3 hour parking. When we were done with the aquarium and the Little movie thing after we had maybe 20 minutes to spare on the parking time. 
So do wish there was an aquarium parking lot for cheaper! Or even FREE! Bc we already have to pay so much to go in the aquarium! 
But overall my family loves coming to the aquarium! Everything was very friendly and it was kept very clean!

I like to come here and enjoy a healthy cold, refreshing treat! The staff is nice and friendly. I typically take my treat and keep walking but the inside area is nice and I see lots of folks enjoying the space. The Hyppo card that earns a free pop after several purchases offsets the price a bit:

I'll admit, I'm not usually fan of popsicles. I thought for sure that I had been entirely coopted by the frozen yogurt craze, and I still prefer it, but the range of flavors were so great here, and it was so delicious, that this place definitely changed my mind for the better on this frozen pop trend. And for that it definitely deserves 5 stars.

Stopped in here after dinner with the boyfriend to grab a quick dessert. The biggest problem with the place is that it almost always looks empty from the outside. It's really cutely decorated and definitely feels like a great local spot, but there's so few places to sit or stand while you eat that it's not really a place where you want to stay and enjoy your pop.

It's counter service, but while I was there it wasn't too busy so I didn't have to wait at all. The whole process was very quick once I figured out what flavor I wanted. I even got it dipped in chocolate and it only took a few seconds to order, get my bar, and pay.

But the real highlight are those bars. I obviously need to go back and try more. A lot more. There's just so many flavors, which such amazing combinations. I got a cinnamon cheesecake ice cream pop that was absolutely AMAZING. If the rest of the flavors are anything like that one, I'm all in at this place. Especially if they can get the fruit juice pops to be similarly impressive. Even the texture was awesome. It wasn't too hard and icy, but it also wasn't melting off all over my hand. They've seriously got this stuff figured out.

Plus the price is pretty good, AND they have buy 10 get 1 free cards. Who doesn't love collecting stamps on an easily-lost loyalty card? It's like a game. And I can't wait to play more of this delicious game in the future.

Amazing Egyptian food. We had the hummus and pita bread which was definitely fresh and delicious and cauliflower salad was very healthy and comforting. The owner was a sweetheart. St Roch Market felt nice and safe.

Great popcycles...natural flavors...excellent selection. 

A pleasant, healthy desert option in downtown St. Petersburg.

The establishment is tucked away in the shopping center by Trader Joes.  The business is owned by Kim and she is wonderful, funny and outgoing.  My stylist is Melody and she has been cutting my hair for the past three years.  I like that she is a perfectionist and takes painstaking time to do an incredible job.  I also like that she is so personable and we can chat and banter one another making the time in the chair just pass by unnoticed.   Cost is very reasonable (under $25).  Over the years I've seen some of the work on her female clientele and was impressed by the transformation she can create (cuts, color, style, etc.).  The location also does pedicures, manicures, and massages.  

If you're new to town or not happy with your current salon, stop by and give Mane Street a visit.  The entire staff is talented and fun!

This is a great place to visit. A bit on the pricy side, but definitely worth a visit. When you first go in, they have these tunnels you go through where you can view fish around you and above you. Sometimes you can watch them feeding the stingrays. Then there is the room where you can watch them feed the penguins. I love the rainforest type room, where you can climb up into the trees and look out over the fish. There is a white alligator to see. Plenty of jellyfish and seahorses. They have a room for children to play and to touch the stingrays. My favorite room has wall to ceiling glass. You can sit and watch fish, sharks, stingrays and turtles swim around.

I have to say I was a bit worried when I went in for my hair cut. I use Yelp often, since moving here,  but didn't for hair cuts. Let's just say I had some bad cuts. 
I asked for Melody since there was a positive review about her being great at cutting short hair. 
Not only did she have to cut my hair, she had to fix the previous bad cuts. I walked out feeling so much better. My hair is close to looking normal again and I don't feel covering my head any more. She knows what she is doing and is a true "hair artisan"!Thanks so much Melody!

Looking for a rainy day activity that's fun, head for the Aquarium! Having been many years ago we didn't hesitate to go back and enjoy all the aquarium has to offer. When I got to the window to pay I inquired about AARP discounts and they don't offer any. The price wasn't bad at $25 per adult. There's also an IMAX theatre there but didn't make the extra spend. 

Very clean, well maintained and well staffed facility. Friendly staff all along the way to answer questions and make your experience more pleasurable. Crowds weren't bad and the layout was easy to navigate. It took 2-3 hours to work our way through the entire facility. We saw colorful fish, star fish, turtles, otters, sharks, alligators, frogs, parakeets, pelicans, eels, stingrays, crawfish, lobster and tons of fresh and saltwater species. 

We stopped for a quick snack in the food court. Selections include Papa Johns pizza, Hagen Daaz ice cream and a burger and fry joint with a few sandwich options and sides. Prices seemed reasonable and the couple items we tried were as expected. 

Get off Bourbon Street, get out of the casinos, leave the jazz behind and come down for a little peace and tranquility at the aquarium....

500 Amazing flavors that rotate. I have been to a lot of the gourmet popsicle shops and hyppo pops have the most flavor. Something new everyday. Very friendly, dogs welcome. You also get a stamp card. When you buy 8 you get 1 free.

Just tried for the first time. Best ice cream pop EVER! I tried the seasonal Pumpkin Spice Cheesecake and it was perfection! I think I am in trouble since I live so close. Cannot wait to try more flavors!!!!

Nice exhibits but overall I feel the cost needs to be slightly lower.  The expense to manage the aquarium I'm sure is pretty high but if you drive here the parking is very expensive per hour for public parking nearby but they do validate.  Just an observation but there is a fair amount to see and you do get one free 3D theater showing.

Visiting New Orleans I took my daughter as a good inside outing due to the rain. You have to purchase your tickets online for a specific time, and the parking was very expensive, since they don't have their own parking lot. I parked in the parking lot closet to the Aquarium since we were already in for a day of walking. Mask are required while in the facility, and due to COVID a lot of the fun events were closed. There was a vast variety of aquatic animals and it was very fun. The guiding arrows were a little confusing and we often had to go back because we missed some animals. They have a great souvenir shop, and photo setup at the front entrance. They also have a food court upstairs so outside food is not allowed.

It was a hot November day, so we dodged inside the Hyppo to try some unique popsicles.  I ordered the Guava Cheesecake popsicle.  The flavors were powerful & a refreshing change from grocery store popsicles.  The only complaint I have is that the popsicle was so excellent that I wanted to try another one.  But the steep price of nearly $5 stopped me.  The Hyppo has an incredible menu board of popsicle flavors that all sound so amazing..  This place was a totally fun treat.

I was visiting New Orleans from Baltimore, Maryland.  The weather was a bit chilly for the zoo so my daughter and I went to the Audobon aquarium. Kinda disappointing.  It is small and nothing compared to the Baltimore aquarium. For example, the Baltimore aquarium has tanks of sharks while this aquarium had video footage of sharks playing. What was really disturbing is that they had a red hawk tied up with a sign saying that it was injured in the wild, could not fly, and would not survive in the wild. Surely there is a more humane way to keep the hawk other than tying it up. The bird was obviously in distress.  Would not recommend this place.

I love this chicken and I have been everywhere in Nashville for hot chicken. It is consistently good....not like other places where you may get good one time and re-fried the next. Aqui is a great lady and I wish her nothing but the best but the chicken speaks fo itself. I have had the fries and potato salad too which are both very good. This is my hot chicken spot. I always try new hot checken places, but I always come back to 400 Degrees!!

Great place for a light dessert after a heavy meal! They always have new flavors and I just love trying all the different flavors. I personally love all their pistachio flavor bars or any coconut flavor bars. Honestly you can't really go wrong with choosing the flavor. It all depends on how you are feeling that day. Fruity? Creamy? Adventurous? There are all different kinds of flavors to match your mood. You can always have your bar dipped in chocolate to satisfy your chocolate cravings as well.

I would come to New Orleans simply for this food alone! Hands down the absolute best food I've had in a while! I got the fattoush salad with feta and chicken shawarma for dinner, came back the next day for a late lunch and got the salad again along with his baba ganoush and fresh pita. It's so good I'm really going to miss this place when I go home. St. Roch market and Torshi is where it's at. 
(Pardon my half eaten salad, I was ready to dig in!!)

The popsicles here are so delicious and good. The have so many flavors to pick from I ended up trying the mango mojito. All flavors here are organic and taste like actual fruit in the form of a popsicle. These would be great to try on really hot days here in st Pete.

They are a little high priced but it is worth it in the end I'll definitely be back. They offer you a loyalty card where if you buy 8 popsicles you get one free. The staff is friendly and very helpful with advising you on what to get if your not really sure and it's your first time here. 

This place is also located on central ave in downtown st Pete and after grabbing a popsicle you can go for a stroll and enjoy it down the Ave and go shopping in other places as well. Definitely go try this place out

A huge thank you to Frank for diagnosing my problem over the phone! He not only diagnosed the problem he provided the part number we needed and suggested that, if we felt comfortable doing so, we could likely fix the problem ourselves. After ordering the $40 part and an hour spent on install, our refrigerator water dispenser is as good as new!! Thank you Frank! We appreciate your help and will absolutely call you each and every time we are in need of appliance repair!
Some of the exhibits still seem to be closed off. I only spent about an hour here looking at everything. They have a food area and gift shops.

Horrible! Ordered a flower birthday cake for my mom's birthday. It was not even close to what is pictured on their website. So unhappy I will be going to the store tomorrow when they open to get some answers! Don't offer an arrangement on your site if you can not arrange it the same way! Also ordered a ballon that was never delivered with the flowers! How can people stay in business if they do such a crappy job.
Like the low sugar carrot ginger pop! Thanks for offering a low sugar option. Sorry it is not always available!!!!

My family and I ate at St. Roch market for the first time today and it was just meh. I wanted to like it so badly but the atmosphere was not what I thought. Maybe it was just an off day so I am willing to give it another try. On a more positive note, I like this new food hall concept where you and your family can eat together even if you all want something quite different. The individual vendors seemed nice but overall this market felt cold. 

I ordered food from Torshi, I really wanted their roasted eggplant dish after seeing it on instagram . However, they ran out and I was offered moussaka in the place of it. Now, it may be similar as far as ingredients but it's different, right? Anyway, I ended up getting the chicken shawarma plate. It came with my choice of salad and hummus. Everything was fresh but I must say I wasn't expecting the chicken to taste like curry. I've never had shawarma to taste like that. Normally, it is more of a Mediterranean style spice blend. I don't know. It was not what I expected but it was still very good and fresh. I also thought they were expensive. My plate was almost $19 with tax I didn't get a drink.

If I go back to St. Roch Market I would eat from Torshi again, but I hope they have the roasted eggplant next time.

This place is great.
It's small so it will be about 2 hours of fun plus any shows you see. There is a water fountain outside of your want to dress in bathing suit or something that can get wet.
If you're a local check out the membership, by the 2nd visit it's break even.

Dive into the depths of the ocean and you'll see some amazing sea life.  If you prefer dry land, then Audubon Aquarium is for you! Located near the Mississippi, it's a great place that you won't want to m

I've been here several times over the years, and enjoy exploring the sea from dry land. 

The aquarium has a wonderful collection of sea creatures that will amaze and thrill any landlubber! 

My personal favorite spot is walking through the "tube", while sea animals swim about, enjoying their day. It's so cool to see various "rays", turtles, sharks, and sea plants from their perspective, all swimming about. 

There is a " petting" area for small and big kids alike. It's so fun to touch the starfish, sea anemones, and snails.  Remember to wash when done! 

If you're feeling famished, or just wanting a snack, there is a restaurant onsite that offers burgers, pizza, and other quick bites, so that you can get back to exploring the ocean life that you're surrounded by. There is even an ice cream spot if you're looking for something on the sweet side.  

There is a uber cool treehouse, and an owl perched high up, keeping his eyes pierced on everything that moves
The penguins will make you smile as you watch them dance, waddle, and splash about. 

When you've explored the depths of the sea, stop by the gift store, and check out some of the stuffed counterparts for sale. 

Remember... just keep swimming!

I love their wine - I have been ordering online all of covid. I was finally able to do in an person tasting. All of the wine was great to taste, the ladies were fabulous who gave us the tasting and of course I ended up buying 2 bottles of wine. The tasting was a great deal. Highly recommend coming for a tasting - only downside is you may end up buying a few bottles of wine!

The aquarium overall was very informative and it had nice displays, I just found them to be small for the animals. I saw there is a new display coming for sharks and the pool looks small and not very deep, not a big fan of that idea. There was volunteer giving a little tour/info by the gulf pool, he was very funny and with lots of facts and enjoyed what he had to say.

Terrible! I live in Texas and I was in town visiting. I went to the salon to get my nails done and it took them 25 minutes just to get the powder dip off my nails! 
The price was higher than I've ever paid and with my tip it was 54.00! If I had known it wasn't going to last I wouldn't have left a tip! The cost of the manicure was 45 then because I used a cc they charged me an additional 1.50! Don't go there unless you want to be overcharged and have a manicure that won't last! My only regret is that I am not there anymore to go and get a refund!

I stopped in to grab shirts for another event and had to get a popsicle while I was here! I got Nutella and it was delicious! They had so many more that I wanted but I didn't want them to melt on the way home. I'll definitely have to go back to try other flavors!

I grew up visiting the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas many times as a kid. Now that we are older we can bring my nephews here and they can be at awe of the fishes. The Aquarium is a great clean facility and fun for the whole family. It is very expensive though and to get the most out of your experience I definitely recommend you take your time and also watch one of the IMAX movies. The one based on Hurricane Katrina is quite interesting and the swamp scenes are cool.

The Aquarium is divided into a few sections. Honestly, I feel like it is quite small for what you pay for. There are the usually large fish tanks, the walk ways with sharks and sting rays above your head, as well as the popular white alligator. One of the funniest parts is if you decide to enter the bird room. You can purchase a stick with some bird food on it and feed the birds. It is cool when some land on your stick and you can get some awesome photographs taken. On the latest visit we missed the otters. The cute and energetic penguins made up for it though.  Overall it should be more of like 3.5, but I will up it for the fun I can tell children have when they are here. A highlight of any New Orleans trip as a break from the partying.

We had a city pass and needed to use one more activity before we left New Orleans so we decided to check out this Aquarium. Overall it is very average. There are things to see but nothing to write home about. If you have small kids I think they would have fun, but if they are older you might skip out and go to Marco gras world instead.

Good crowd
Variety of fish and activities 
Amazon rainforest themepark was excellent 
Shark area and penguin areas were a surprise

Lackluster at best. The otter feeding was cool. The rest of the aquatic life can be found at a pet store. Laughable that they charge an entry fee. If you want to see a legit aquarium Atlanta, Chattanooga, or Ripley's Aquarium of the Smokies are far superior. Also the Audubon Zoo is a much better time where you can see several of the same animals.

Fish are fish! My husband is a New Orleans native who always love coming to the Aquarium. This place is done very well, it's big and spacious and operates very much like an amusement park. There's a rain forest in the middle of the aquarium which is pretty cool. It has a tree house where children can run and play. The climate for the rain forest is exactly what is it supposed to be. It's muggy and the air is thick. Good experience here!

The layout of this aquarium was navigable and interactive. The wait was a little long in comparison to the Audubon Zoo, but I attribute that to it being so close to the French Quarter. 

Highly recommend!

I went for the first time after my sister recommended it and I wished I had visited them sooner. I got a gel mani and pedi early September and they both lasted longer than I expected. Let's just say my toes are still pink with gel and are just now due for a polish change. 
Side note: The staff at my nails is so personable. The massage chair is so comfy. I don't get my nails done faithfully but when I plan mani & pedi dates this is my go to location from here on out

Friendly customer service and tasty treat!  Stopped in after a day at school with my son and the employee explained to us the options.  She was patient and kind when we let others choose before us.  So many great flavors!

I love exploring aquariums in different cities... my husband and I were in New Orleans for the day (we literally had 17 hours between flights to wander around the city) and it was between the WWII museum and the aquarium. I, of course, advocated for the aquarium! 

It was about $65 for two tickets. They have you pick a time in advance. It was super confusing getting in because there was a long line, but it was to buy tickets. There was no clear signage for people who already had tickets. 

TBH, I was super disappointed with the aquarium! When we got done with the exhibits I was like "that's it?!" Maybe I've been spoiled by other aquariums I've gone to, idk. Also, COVID was still somewhat a concern being indoors with a lot of people and it was super crowded. It was hard to see a lot of the exhibits with the crowds. Definitely an overall "eh" experience.

Torshis is now located in the infamous Silk Road location on royal street. I've been dying to try this Egyptian cuisine and it didn't disappoint. Was able to buy good wine for decent price and enjoy at the table. Torshis fulfilled all my veggie dreams heart's desire. We got the deluxe hummus to start which was great. We ordered stuffed falafels but they were out :( my only complaint. I will return for those. We also got cauliflower eggplant grape leaves and spinach pies. Bread was a little lame and lifeless but everything else was to the T. The flavors were amazing and reasonably priced. My friend got the lamb entree which came with generous portion. Tables were spaced out by covid protocol and service was prompt. Just wish they would have brought out stuffed falafels not plain.

I went to Dr. Oki to have the first trimester testing done for my pregnancy. We came here on a Saturday morning and felt completely at ease considering the reason we were there. Our baby is healthy and developing wonderfully and Dr. Oki had us feeling comfortable and excited. In the room there is a big screen on the wall so you can see your baby and he took his time looking for measurements so we could watch our baby girl move around. The entire process was relaxing and we appreciate Dr. Oki and his soothing bedside manner. 

It was easy to get an appointment since my doctors office called for me.

Not really sure there is much else that can be said about the Hyppo. Enjoying Popsicles in the Florida heat and humidity is a win. 

You will be sure to find a popsicle that you will enjoy here. There are a myriad of flavors that customers can choose from. Did I mention that the popsicles were tasty? 

The staff is always pleasant and efficient here. The store is spotless because the employees are constantly cleaning. 

In addition to popsicles, the Hyppo also offers accessories that you can utilize to make your own! They also sell cute t-shirts, enamel pins, and other tchotchkes. 

My only gripe is that I wish there was seating outdoors. There isn't too much room outside of the storefront, so unfortunately this may never possible. So heads up, be prepared to take your popsicle to go.

I'm writing this review from a bit of a specialized view. I took my cousin to the Aquarium, and she is special needs and relies on a wheelchair to get around.

If you've walked the streets of New Orleans, you know that our sidewalks and roads are miserable. Add navigating a wheelchair to the mix and you can be a bit limited in where you can go.

I choose the Aquarium because it was July and we needed air conditioning.  The only challenge at all was actually getting to the Aquarium. I parked in the garage at Canal Place and headed over. Crossing over the area where the street cars run was a huge challenge. I don't know if anything could be done, but it is very difficult to navigate with a wheelchair.

Once inside, we had a great experience. I have always loved this place, but the ease of getting around with a wheelchair made me appreciate it a bit more.  

Make sure you pick up the list of activities at the front as those are some of the best things to watch. We managed to hit the otter training, the penguin feeding, and the sting ray feeding.

I highly recommend doing the sting ray feeding. For an additional $2, you get four semi-frozen small fish that you hold in your hand to feed the sting rays.  My cousin loved doing it.  

The staff throughout the facility are very helpful.  The exhibits are great. 

I had such a nice time that I upgraded to an Audubon membership on the way out the door.

Pretty expensive for such a small aquarium and many empty exhibits. Almost 100 dollars for a family of four. Took us 1.5 hours to walk through the entire thing and left us wanting more. Didn't seem to be memorable for our kids (9 and 5).

Wow! This is an easy 5 star review! The Hyppo has is going on. A beautiful storefront with a clear, crisp and fun brand image. The murals totally rock. The day we visited, they had over 40 flavors of popsicles. I have to admit it took a good 4-5 minutes to make some final decisions. What we tried: Blueberry Lavender Lemonade, Blackberry Jasmine and Raspberry. All of them were fantastic, but the Blueberry one stood out - not "perfumy" at all like you might imagine - just a perfect balance of flavors! Someone here has been doing their homework!

Though it was freezing out last night, I couldnt resist buying a Popsicle after passing by this place. It looked like such a ute new hangout spot, very modern, the guy was super nice for letting us in last minute to look at the assortment of pops they had. I tried the persimmon Popsicle which was my favorite so far and also the peanut butter and chocolate banana. It was interesting! It had banana bits inside! This is definitely a place I would take out of towners and be coming often during the hot summer.

Coming from Chicago, this Aquarium has nothing spectacular. I like the layout and the design, it's cool to wander through, but it really is just like every other sub-par aquarium. No meat-eating sharks or whales, I believe I only saw one alligator (although it was albino). The coolest part to me was the predatory birds that were free-roaming. You'd sneak a peak of them in the swamp area. Even caught an owl eating a rodent! Other than that, not worth it! :(

As a runner who bikes for cross-training purposes these are really pleasant trails. The north part is a bit too intense for me but bunny, bunny's revenge, and snake dance...all on the southern end...are all easily manageable by relatively novice bikers. Word of warning...bring a comb to help push stray chollas off of you. Also, while the trail is fairly well marked, the proper direction of travel isn't always, so make sure you ride counterclockwise, at least on the southern trails.
These pops are a delicious treat. Favorites have to be the mango with champagne and the guava cheesecake. They have kid size pops as well.
Very nice Aquarium. My kids enjoyed it. It was definitely worth the price. It took us about an hour to go through and gain some great knowledge of the fishes

Surprised at the large variety if flavors. All fresh and cool combos. I gad the coconut dipped in chocolate. It was light and very satisfying. Cannot wait to go back and try other flavors. Others in party had peanut butter, Mexican hot chocolate and dragon coconut lime. Everyone left happy
Absolutely love this place! So many unique and tasty flavors to choose from. My favorites are the Phoenix, Jackfruit, and Strawberry Cheesecake.

I've been to both Saucy's and McClure's and I think Saucy's is the clear winner, and definitely the best BBQ I've had in NOLA.  

The ribs were super tender, like fall off the bone tender.  This was in contrast to other places I've tried where the ribs were tough and difficult.  They were seasoned to perfection.  The brisket was equally tender, and wonderfully juicy as well.  Both meats were absolutely divine, and I love that they have a bunch of different sauces you can use.  Use their spicy sauce-it isn't kept on the table, but on a shelf above the tables.  

There are other BBQ places in the city with more side options.  However, no one, I repeat no one, has goat cheese mac and cheese.  Saucy's usually only has it on the weekends, and I usually call ahead to make sure they've got it.  It is the best mac and cheese I've had in the city, hands down.  And NOLA's got some pretty slammin' mac and cheese.  I also like the sweet potato muffins, and the spicy coleslaw is pretty good.  

The staff is super friendly and they have lemonade and iced tea so you can make an Arnold Palmer.  So happy to have Saucy's right down the street from me!

This is an amazing gourmet popsicle shop. They have easily over 20 flavors ranging from classics like orange creamsicle to datil blueberry and blackberry goat cheese. Their popsicles range from $3-$5 and they even have alcoholic popsicles for 21+! 

I got a a dark roast espresso popsicle (each popsicle with dairy is clearly marked) covered in chocolate (extra dollar!). The woman working the shop was very nice and knowledgeable. They have so many flavors it's a bit overwhelming but you can ask as many questions about flavors you don't recognize with no judgment. 

The shop is pretty spacious and the person working was wearing a mask! They also had adorable fruit and popsicle themed merch like t shirts, pennants, pint glasses, keychains, pins, etc. there's also a fair amount of room in there, and they have a table for 8 as well as a few other seats. 

As for parking, a public parking garage is your best bet as there's no private lot and limited street parking. I would highly recommend coming in and trying a lovely popsicle!

Believe the hype about Hyppo! I am usually a die hard for ice cream desserts but thought I'd give this place a chance. So glad I did! We tried the strawberry basil and blackberry limeade. Both were delicious. While some may complain about the price, I felt they were reasonable because we slowly savored our popsicles during a nice stroll through the downtown area. We enjoyed our experience so much that we returned the next night as well. I love the creativity of some of their flavor combinations. Check them out you won't be disappointed.

The food here is just incredible and additional perk: BYOB. We had a healthy dinner here and started drinking for our night out. 

We ordered a bunch of stuff off the menu to eat family style and every single dish was a hit - great flavor and perfect seasoning with fresh herbs. All the dishes were prepared with fresh ingredients and the portions for each were really healthy, too. I'm sad I don't live locally and can't go visit more often.

I don't think I've ever been treated so badly in a store. My husband asked the petite blond woman in the store if we could try the Chardonnay. Instead of suggesting a tasting, or a wine flight, she replied that she didn't have one open. Period. No suggestions of an alternative, no helpful information about other popular substitutes. It was very clear that she didn't think we were the "right" kind of people to assist. No smile. Nothing. It was extremely uncomfortable. We left and spent our money elsewhere at it was obviously unwelcome there. 

I should note that my husband and I are a pair of unassuming 50 somethings with ample income. I am truly at a loss at what we did to offend her.
Beautiful Aquarium, Parakeet Point was probably my favorite part, it was fun interacting with the budgies!
Very welcoming. The owner is very friendly. I love the vibe when I come here if my S/O. They always treat her well here and do great work!! 10/10 would recommend to anyone.

Why 5 stars? Because they have like 30 gourmet popsicles.

   ---   ---   ---

You guys. 30 gourmet popsicles.

This is going to be one of my shortest reviews, because - what else do you need to know?

You walk in. There's like a 142 square foot lobby and a counter. In the counter are 30 different types of gourmet popsicles. 

You agonize over which flavor, as if you're deciding something with life or death at stake. 

You pick a flavor (in my case - Guava Peach.)

You take the plastic wrapper off, and you thank your God that gourmet popsicles are a thing. 

What a time to be alive.

Last Saturday to my dismay my washer stopped working. I googled repairmen in Havertown and stumbled upon the reviews for Frank and decided to give him a shot. My husband called late Saturday afternoon and was able to get Frank on the first try. He explained the situation and Frank tried to talk my husband through fixing it himself. YES a repairman that actually tried to help us over the phone, this is the point where we knew this was a stand up guy. When it became evident that the washer would need parts Frank made us an appointment for Tuesday (Monday was a holiday). 

On Tuesday Frank came and fixed the washer within twenty minutes all the while explaining to my husband what to look for should it break again. On his way out he inquired about our computer and asked to look at he wound up fixing our computer that had been acting up in the last several months.

We had a great experience with Frank and highly recommend his services.
amazing popsicles!!!! so many cool, unique flavors to choose from. very nice environment and in a very cute area. can't wait to visit again!!! :)
Nice little aquarium! Better than the one we have in SLC,  but not as good as San Francisco or Vancouver. Other than that, we saw some pretty cute and pretty freaky animals. Penguins too!

Watch your receipts. Today, I purchased two packs of Gold Toe socks. There were electronic signs in the area specifying that Gold Toe socks were, "Buy One, Get One Half Price". I made my purchase using my Kohl's charge. The cashier offered me a scratch off for an additional discount, which ended up being 15%.
     The socks were tagged at $21 each. By my estimates, I should have been charged a total of $26.78. I was in fact charged $40.20. I did have a coupon valued at $30, but I did not see anywhere that this coupon would affect the discount. All I can say is, check your receipts before leaving the check out area. Unfortunately, I did not check mine until hours later and miles away.
     On another note, I was looking for dress shoes and shirts. The assortment of acceptable shoes in my size was almost nonexistent. There were plenty of shirts, but the department needed a total recovery as did much of the men's clothing areas.
     I won't go back to the store to complain. I did call them about the overcharge, but they were unwilling to pull the receipt up on their computer. So, I vote with my feet. I closed my charge account and will not shop there again. And I make my opinion know on the Internet.

Came here about 8 yrs ago.  I can't remember but I thought I liked it back then. But for some reason now it is not so great.  Not sure what changed.  

The aquarium is very small.  We saw just about everything in less than an hr.  And that's waiting in line to touch the sting rays (which none came up to us). 

I think maybe the tickets were $30-35 each person.  There wasn't much to enjoy.  Def there are way better aquariums out there.  No wonder my sister didn't want to come with us.

WHEN THE BBQ FLAVOR COMES FROM THE SAUCE..
and not the meats I'm never impressed. It's not that it is bad food, the quality of the chicken and brisket is high but the smokiness just isn't that perceptible. Also they don't serve smoked pork sausage just boudin or gator.

REGARDLESS THE SAUCES ARE REALLY GOOD
the sweet sauce is thick and actually not that cloying. But it's the unusual creamy mustard horsey sauce that goes very well with the chicken.

From alcoholic popsicles to unique flavors, Hypoo has anything for the partying adult or a family with kiddos. It is quite overwhelming with how many flavors they have but every one was great. I highly recommend this in the warm Florida weather!

As of right now , still early on in my pregnancy at almost 20 weeks, I was going to wait to do this review but at the same time I did want to review a little early to let you know my experience so far. 

I was referred from regular OB at OBGYN associates as soon as we found out that I was prediabetic at 11 weeks. I was told to make an appointment with him and a dietitian to start my meal plans and get in control. 

I did start with calling Dr.Oki's office and called to make my appointment first and then after my dietitian later that day. When I finally came into my appointment, the medical assistant and the staff at Dr.Oki's office were confused as to why I was there first if I have not had my appointment with the dietitian yet. I explained to them I was just told to make both appointments and was not told one had to be before the other.  

Keep in mind this is my first for EVERYTHING, so I kind of already had a bad impression at first because of the way they thought I should of handled my appointments. Either way I met with Laura Oki, the wife of Dr. Oki and she went over what she does, what they are going to do during my appointments, a little over what gestational diabetes is , and soon took my A1C1. With my numbers being so high , they put me on insulin right away. 

My first week goes by for the new changes and my next visit was for the first trimester screening. At this appointment I was excited and ready to see my baby.  But the first part of this appointment is where my experience so far became really iffy on how I feel about Dr. Oki . 

Keep in mind again, this is my first week with this new diet and insulin, as soon as Dr.Oki saw how my numbers were they were fluctuated with a range of high and low numbers and with that he automatically said "I personally think we need to bring the hospital in with the numbers that I am seeing". That part was understandable but he then goes on about the impact of me having a blood sugar crash with Insulin:

For the times I have described this situation, I stand by that I swear he said: "If you are driving, you might as well turn yourself in , surrender your license , and you can get a felony and go to jail." Yes I understand that he is just trying to tell me how serious have a blood sugar crash is when driving and that he just wants to make sure I follow what I'm supposed to do, but as a first time pregnancy and only at 23 years old, it was not what I expected at all and honestly caused me unnecessary stress that I shouldn't have. 

Besides the long lecture about going to jail and surrendering my license, I swear by when he talks about the hospital visit , he says how expensive it will be and that for me and my partner that "It is more than your income." Again another bad comment that was not needed and caused unnecessary stress. At this time, he did not explain any other options and when we said we wanted to wait to think about it, he says that : "you guys are obligated to do what you want, but you do not have my blessing".

To shorten this up, I ended up going to the hospital to be monitored because I was stressed out that I felt the only doctor that was important for my pregnancy was not going to help me unless I followed his suggestions. The hospital stay overall was not too bad and it actually led me to decide where I do want to give birth to my child when the time comes. 

But at the same time, the nurses were confused with Dr.Oki's orders during my stay and Dr.Oki also gave me mixed communication as far as if I should eat everything on the plate that the hospital gives me vs. what not to eat if I feel it is too much and will spike, which one day he said to eat everything and the next day told me not too if its too much. 

So overall as of right now as you can tell... my experience with Dr. Oki has been stressful since Day 1 that I started seeing him. 

BUT, he is the only High Risk OB here in Reno unless you go to the High Risk Pregnancy Center which is not recommended because they have a different doctor each time.

At the end of all this,  I realized that even though I agree with everyone else about Dr.Oki's bedside manners. He is a very intelligent doctor and knows what he is doing. His wife is the main reason why I continue to still go and have faith in my appointments moving forward, but I am also not someone to just give up even though one may not believe in me, which in this case is Dr.Oki this whole time.

I'm not saying everyone should give him a chance like I am and I know a lot of women would of changed doctors already,  but looking at a different perspective of things , especially with a doctor like Dr.Oki and being still early on , things may change in experiences. At least I hope it does. Which Is why I'm writing this review early on, things may change.

It's amazing to think that they basically had to restock this entire Aquarium after the tragedy of Katrina. 

Five stars hardly do it justice. It's one of my favorite aquariums. They start you off with a bang where you walk right through the fish and ray tank. You're part of the exhibit right out of the gate. Other highlights include the sea horses, the huuuuuuuuuge shark tank (why thank you) , the penguins and the Mississippi river exhibit. That last one has a white alligator, a place where the heal up birds of prey (red tailed hawk and horned owl currently) and has a big window overlooking Old Blue (You're my boy Blue!) It's a great place for kids and families too. 

Note: If you are going to visit the other Audubon attractions like the Zoo, Insectarium or IMAX, you should get the discounted tickets to all of them which are good for five days after your first entry.

The best part of the Audubon Aquarium is the local wildlife section that shows the fish and animals of the Mississippi river. The rest of the aquarium is pretty lackluster, although the sting-ray exhibit is another highlight.

This aquarium is definitely not the largest aquarium you will ever go to, not even in the south east. But there are a couple of really prominent highlights that elevate it a little bit.

The first is their local wildlife exhibit. It's really cool/interesting to be able to see the wildlife that inhabits the local area and I was shocked to see some of the freshwater fish that live in the river nearby. Very cool, and adds a "unique" and "local" feeling to this aquarium.

The sting-ray exhibit is also a highlight. It gives you the opportunity to actually touch some sting-rays. My three year old didn't want to leave this exhibit. She loved watching the sting-rays swim around, and loved putting her hands in the water waiting for one of them to brush past her.

Another highlight is the seahorses. This aquarium has quite a few sea horses and they are super interesting to watch. One of the seahorse tanks had a lot of male seahorses that were currently carrying babies and that was very cool to see.

The last thing I would mention is the sea otters. The exhibit itself is pretty small, but sea otters are always cool.

If you're looking for an afternoon to kill with kids (especially small kids), I would highly recommend the aquarium.

This place is in a little building with a few other places like Quiznos and J. Gumbo's in it too. It kind of reminds me of eating in a dining area at an indoor mall.

THIS WAS THE BEST HOT CHICKEN I HAD WHILE IN NASHVILLE, hands down! I seriously fell in love with Nashville after my first bite of my hot chicken strips here. I might have been able to handle the 200 degree chicken but I decided to go with the 100 degree, it was spicy but not overpowering, just right for me! The chicken was so juicy and tender, and the batter on the outside was just perfect! I could have eaten here every day!

They aren't open all day, I think they close kind of early on the weekdays, so double check if you're coming for dinner.

Also like some of the other reviewers have mentioned, you can call ahead for your order! It takes about 30 minutes for them to make it since it's made fresh to order. But again totally worth the wait!

I don't know what it is about this guy and his business, but I want to see him do well. With the food that he's serving, this shouldn't be difficult. 

I was in the mood for something that wouldn't make me feel like a fat lard afterwards, so I had the tabbouli salad and added chicken. I got a TON of tabbouli and some incredibly tasty chicken. Even the little bit of tahini that showed up on top of the chicken was delicious. 

Everything that was turned out of that little space looked amazing and I can't wait to try the rest of the menu, including the mint lemonade!

Really really neat place! 5 stars because there is no other place like this near Tampa! There are SO MANY flavors of popsicles and La Croix here.. my two favorite things!

Most of the flavors you will see here are unique and you will probably never find them at any grocery store. I've tried more than a handful and they were all very fresh and yummy. There's even a goat cheese one! 

If you love popsicles and fun flavors come here!

The Penguins were the highlight of the aquarium, they are very friendly and active. It was a great time watching them interact with each other. The over all experience was not worth the cost to me personally but I'm sure if you had children it would be worth it.

I have always wanted to come to a popsicle shop and here was an adorable one with TONS of flavors.  I had the pistacchio coconut (both flavors which I love) but I didn't like this at all.  It almost tasted like an egg nog flavor.  I took one bite and gave the rest to my husband.  He thought it tasted good, but didn't want it, so it went into the trash.  Waste of $3.75.

This museum is very tiny. There are nice exhibits of the otters and sting rays. I wish there was more to see. They had a few exhibits down but the staff was nice and the gift shop was $$ pricey as expected.
Had a very fun time in the H.A.R.T. Escape room, Robert was very kind and worked very well with children!

Not your typical breakfast from @torshi_egyptian_food in @st.rochmarket. The perfect falafel with a hard boiled egg inside, served on creamy hummus. This breakfast was incredibly filling, but didn't leave me feeling that 'I need to take a nap' type feeling after brunch. The fresh Greek salad  on the side with fig vinaigrette was also refreshing and delicious.

Loved treating myself to a Hyppo popsicle when I was in Gainesville and their St. Pete location is no different! They have countless flavors to choose from, ranging from fruity to creamy, and I'm not exaggerating when I say they're all delicious! You can taste the high quality ingredients in every bite. Honestly it's one of the most refreshing popsicles you'll ever have. My go-to is the pistachio but there's so many other choices it's a shame not to give the others a chance. You can also request your popsicle to be covered in chocolate if that strikes your fancy. 

The location itself is wonderful, a welcoming interior nestled in downtown St. Pete. And even more welcoming staff! Run, don't walk, and get your Hyppo fix asap!

Staff and Drs aren't very courteous.  Although they have high tech equipment and "CAN" do a lot of great imaging, they have only given us horrible images of our soon-to-be-born baby.  Plus, it seemed like Dr Oki was finding every little thing to get us to come back for another visit.  Dr Oki's bedside manner leaves a LOT to be desired.  It's almost like he has no idea or caring about what he says to his patients.  Needless to say, we will not be going back, and I definitely would not refer anyone to this office.  But, I think they are the only ones in Reno...and I would find someone else somewhere else to go.  I would have taken my wife to Sacramento if I knew the poor bedside manner and lack of caring on the part of Dr Oki.

In summary, this office is a thumbs down in my book.

We had my sisters bridal shower in the room next to the tasting room. It was absolutely perfect. The atmosphere of the room was awesome. Audrey helped us get everything in order and set up the room while Kathy served our guests wine and helped with everything!!! Everyone was available, helpful and very knowledgeable throughout the entire process of planning and during the shower. I highly recommend this room for parties!!!

My reasoning for a 4 star rating is simple. This place had awesome popsicles that are totally unique and made fresh and healthy. But for $4 a pop, I don't know, it doesn't seem too worth it for me. Definitely a cool place to try out however. Real ingredients, no additive or food coloring. It's really amazing how true too the flavor these popsicles are. Sadly I almost wanted to give this place a 3, because a bunch of popsicles is really all they have. There are a few overpriced things off to the side you can purchase, but really popsicles is it. There are lots of option for popsicles, but idk, just seemed like a whole storefront was a bit much just for popsicles. They are pretty amazing popsicles though, definitely something you should try.

So much more than just an aquarium. On a short vacation to New Orleans, this placed turned out to be my 11yo sons favorite place. So much that we went twice. 

Order your tickets online for aa discount. They also offer a veterans discount, even at the gift shop. 

Yes, there are fish, otters, and penguins. But our favorite was the parakeets. You can buy a seed stick, but you really don't need to. They were all over us. On our shoulders, heads, arms, pockets. We heard that they love darker colors. 

Definitely  recommend visiting if you have time.

I wish I could give All Brands a six star rating. Their service and prices were outstanding. Andrew the technician was very knowledgeable, on time and polite. He repaired out refrigerator ice maker, washing machine and dryer. And, we couldn't be more please with the results. We will recommend All Brands to everyone we know.

Love this place! Always so friendly let you try the wine before buying. My favorite vineyard. Just realized the Yelp coupon will need to use next time. I just wish they would bring back ChaddsFord red. I love that wine!

Tom's does great work and is very honest and reliable. I trust my car and my safety to them completely. So far I've had them install a toll bar, replace all the belts in the car and several other big jobs.

A few days ago, I discovered that my refrigerator wasn't refrigerating. The fan was running but that's about all that was happening.  My hunt for a good repairman took me to Yelp and I started reading all the positive reviews about All Brands Appliance Repair and Frank.  I gave him a call and left voicemail. He called back in about an hour and said he could come over in a few hours. What a great guy!  He got to work immediately and found the problem within 20 minutes!  Besides the coils being covered with about 2 inches of ice, there was a malfunctioning relay which was causing that to happen. After dealing with the ice with a hair dryer, he installed a new relay and, presto, it worked like new! I was highly impressed by how quickly he was able to troubleshoot the problem!
Afterwards, we sat around and talked for a while. He gave me all kinds of great advice for computers. His knowledge was astounding!  I wrote everything down he told me and will put it all to good use. 
I won't hesitate to call on him again if I need appliance repairs and will also recommend him to my friends.
Great and fast service! Food was delicious or even better!!! Loved the place! My salad was perfect and the cauliflower was awesome!! Try it you won't be sad!
Cold popsicles for hot days in St. Petersburg. We stop in every time we visit. Dozens of great flavors. Go there.

We ventured over to the Audubon Aquarium of the Americas because we were staying nearby. Little did I know, it was also free for locals that day and my bf had his ID so we were able to get comped admission. Score! We wandered about and saw an albino alligator, countless jellyfish, penguins, a sea turtle swimming with sharks, and countless fish. The aquarium is multi-level and while vaccination status is asked, masks weren't required. We were able to wander around and take our time with the various exhibits. 

I love visiting aquariums in various cities. One of my favorites is the Monterey Bay one but the Audubon Aquarium isn't as big, however the variety of fish is impressive. It was quite peaceful inside, so if you're looking for something to do that isn't super busy, checking out the aquarium is a nice respite from the hubbub of the city.

The sea otters, Buck & Emma, alone make this aquarium worth the price of admission.

One of the best aquariums in the world. You'll be amazed at the initial tank, the frog exhibit, the minute sea horses, the replica environments, the massive shark (and other large dudes) tank. And yes, you'll love the sea otters. Trust me.

Came in after having a hankering for something sweet. The place is a hipster popsicle joint peddling you guessed it, artisan popsicles in every fruit combination imaginable. The guy up front was friendly and helpful, he had suggestions for "desserty" or "refreshing" selections. My sons got chocolate cheesecake and watermelon flavors, and I got blueberry cheesecake and passion fruit pineapple. All were delicious! My favorite was definitely blueberry cheesecake. Definitely worth a snack on a balmy Florida day

If you compare this to the Shedd aquarium in Chicago you will not like it. Much different than the Shedd, smaller and less variety. Still a great aquarium! We saw so many beautiful creatures. I would have to say that my favorite thing was probably the seahorses, there were so many of them. We did not eat at the food court here but they had a nice variety. You have to pay to feed the string rays but you can touch them for free! The employees were all helpful and the youth volunteers were well trained and knowledgeable in the activity station type things where you got to touch different things (like sea otter fur) and ask questions.

Perfect! Perfect! Perfect!
I don't know why anyone thinks there is a better hot chicken in Nashville, the hot chicken capital of the world. This place has the crispiest outside, the juiciest inside, the best wings, the best fries and the best service!
Okay, I love spicy food but I'm a cautious girl when I go here. The 400 is too much so I order the 200. It's spicy enough! But the recipe is so perfect no matter what your taste. Even if you're a wimp, at least order 100 degrees to savor those secret spices. This is the best chicken anywhere!!! Too bad about the limited hours. Oh well, WORTH IT!!!

We were tired, starving, and had already walked out of one place. We argued up and down Magazine street and between the three of us, couldn't agree on anything. Or even disagree on anything. In the end, it was my wife, who generally doesn't pick BBQ, who said this was where we eating. It was a dangerous moment for anybody brave enough to take our order. We were verging on a family riot that would put the '68 Democratic convention to shame.

 Somehow, we managed to choose food and actually place our orders without interrupting each other. I ordered the Boudin plate, with smoked beans and potato salad. The kid (15) selected the goat cheese mac and a brisket quesadilla. My wife, the beouf gras sandwich and cole slaw. 

We waited.  Seconds ticked on the clock like hours. The atmosphere at our table was like that buzzing sound when you get close to a high voltage line. The food came. Our server walked away. My wife tensed up. Something was missing. I grabbed my phone and dialed 9, then 1, then.........our server came back with the rest of the order. That was close.

 We dug in. There was silence for a few minutes, then we all started talking. We shared food with each other. And everything was fantastic! And it wasn't just because we were hungry. This place is really good. We took an order of goat cheese mac to go and had that with the leftovers (well, theirs, I was in the clean plate club) for breakfast.

They're already planning a fall girls trip to NOLA and definitely will be eating at Saucy's again.

Skip the tourist traps with the $25 bowls of gumbo. Eat real food made by real people at real places like this.

Does not compare to our aquarium in Chicago or San Francisco

Small cramped and overpriced

Save your money and just watch national geographic

When I mention that I visited the aquarium while in NOLA, they will indubitably ask my thoughts. My answer has consistently been "Better than Boston, not as good as Toronto."

What I really enjoyed about this aquarium were the exhibits dedicated to local fish and wildlife. The Amazon rainforest exhibit was also pretty cool! Though, other than tanks with aquatic life, it seemed just a smidge out of place. 

Otherwise, you had a wide variety of fishes (with sharks, of course), and who could forget the ever adorable penguins! There is a jellyfish exhibit and some others dedicated to specific wildlife, like otters or seahorses. 

It takes an hour, maybe two, to see everything. I also wouldn't go as far as to say the aquarium was drab, but I did find the Toronto aquarium much brighter and more vibrant if that makes sense.
Torshi was awesome! We had grape leaves, Greek salad and gyros and all were excellent. We will be back.

Great Cafe Cubano and friendly conversation about Cuban politics and the island's future.

Felt like I was back in Miami.
Bakery awesome...Cant wait to try lunch...

Clean facility and friendly staff.   The staff interacts well with the children and creates a fun and safe atmosphere. They take the time to share your child progress and to explain the focus of their lessons.  There are showers and changing rooms available.  They utilize ribbons to reward the students progress and achievements.  The indoor facility allows for year round training.

A fabulous joint! The atmosphere isn't as bad as some of the reviews implied. It is actually rather comfortable and eclectic. Got the usual lecture about ordering in spanish (no problemo) and no cell phone use once your food is served. The owner is a cantankerous sort of curmudgeon, but that just adds to the atmosphere. We figured we were only going to have one shot at this as we were just travelling through so ordered a Cubano, a tacos de lechon (pork tacos), and a couple of empanadas de pollo (chicken empanadas). Everything was great with really good seasoning and great flavors. The empanadas were really tasty with a fine filling and delicious pastry, but perhaps a little dry. 

For a small place the food was really outstanding with authentic flavors. If our travels ever bring us to Nashville again we will be Back to Cuba!

It has been several years since we were last here, but I am happy to report that the food remains great. On a Thursday night they were reasonably busy, but there were enough seats so that as diners came in they were able to find seats.

Once again we enjoyed the empanadas (both beef and chicken). They are crispy and well stuffed with nicely seasoned meat. They are served with a really nice, slightly spicy chimichuri sauce. I preferred the beef, but I think that is mostly because the higher fat content in the beef gave it a more unctuous mouth feel. Both are delicious, however.

We also shared a cubano sandwich. These are really great. A perfect blending of meat flavors and textures. Yum! The cubano is a LARGE sandwich. Even though we were both hungry we still brought home almost half of the cubano. Blame it on the delicious empanadas!

We also had a side of tostones, fried plantains. This was the only part of our meal that we didn't find outstanding. They seemed a bit dry. When we had these in Ecuador they were usually served with a slightly spicy crema sauce. However I don't think this is the Cuban practice.

Fun funky atmosphere with art and photos from pre-Castro Cuba. Usually there are Cuban tunes on the sound system.

Went here a while back and was not impressed.  After some time passed I was feeling adventurous so I gave them another shot though and this time was much better!  Got a pizza steak and fries with American cheese on the side...delicious!  Steak chopped up well, roll was soft, nice amount of cheese and fried onions.  Only complaint is not enough sauce.  Five stars on the fries which were perfectly cooked and salted.  And melted American cheese is my crack.

great tasting food, but never anywhere to sit, i always feel rushed (especially if you are lucky enough to get a table) and I don't like the way you order. I want to ask questions, ask opinions, and take a moment to review the menu. 
BUT over all the food is great, so i keep returning and jockeying for position of getting a table.

Went for dinner and the food was very very good. Extremely flavorful. However the portions seemed a littttle bit small for the price. As far as service, it was fine except that some of the wait staff don't seem to know how to smile, and I'm pretty sure I overheard a manager yelling at one of the waitresses behind a thin curtain that separates the dining room from the kitchen. I would love to go back b/c the food was soooooooooo good but the staff needs to get their act together.

I've lived in the area for years and yet to have come to Back to Cuba until yesterday. I have no idea why I haven't gone here sooner but regardless I think it was meant to be. Why? Because what I ordered was everything I hoped it would be. Not only the food, but I spoke with the owner for a few minutes and he made the experience even better. He let me know the "do's and don'ts" of the place while cracking a few jokes along the way. He was charming and informative. 
On to the food: 
I ordered the grilled chicken and onions. It came with white rice, a huge helping of black beans, succulent plantains, and a huge bag of toasted bread. It all made sense to me while eating it. The seasoning was perfect. That for me does it when I don't have to have any condiments or even salt. I also ordered the chicken and beef empanadas. They are HUGE. I personally ate the chicken and gifted the beef to my boss (had to butter her up). It had enough spice to counter the richness of the fried empanada shell. I'll be back soon, especially for dinner. He invited me to come back with a few friends, bring a bottle of wine, and play dominoes. All while enjoying the Cuban fare and listening to records spin. What more could I ask for?

We are so excited to have shugga hi bakery open in Cleveland park!  Our food was delicious- christian got the breakfast burrito, I got "the Catherine"(eggs and bacon, and my mother-in-law got "the bomb" (a hot biscuit stuffed with eggs spinach etc) everything was fresh hot and delicious. We also had some rum and lemon cake which was equally good.  The staff was exceptionally friendly. I'm excited for them to become a staple breakfast nook in our community. They also have live music on Friday and Saturday nights! :)

Okay, so let me just say that this place is so good! This was my first time here and I actually enjoyed it. I was a bit skeptical because I hadn't heard many people talking about this place, but it did not disappoint! I went with a large group (10 people) at 11am on a Saturday and we had no trouble with seating. There was only one waitress working when we got there, so it took a while to get drinks and our food ordered. I had a Peach Sangria (wasn't on the menu) and it was SO good. Plus it was only $5, so you can't beat that. The food was great, too! There weren't any issues with what everyone ordered, which usually happens with large orders. I got the Dickerson Sunrise (added cheese to my grits) & was definitely satisfied. 

Overall, this was a great place. I definitely recommend it. The food was hot and delicious and the drinks were amazing. I will for sure be back!
Absolutely love it here! Started my daughter here at 2 yes old & she's learned so much! Thank you to everyone at DeMont for all you do!

We were only in Nashville for three days, but made it a point to come here twice for breakfast. The first time we chose from their regular menu. I had a veggie bomb that was mind-blowing! It's a homemade biscuit stuffed with vegetables, eggs, and cheese, baked, and then topped with honey butter. It takes about 15 min to get your bomb after ordering, but it's well worth the wait. They're huge! I could barely finish one, and an order comes with two. We also split the chocolate cake, which was to die for. 

On our second visit, we came for the blues brunch buffet. It's $20 a person with an option of $17 bottomless mimosas. The buffet wraps around the entire front of shop and offers about 20 breakfast and lunch specialties. If the berry french toast casserole is available, make sure to snag some of that. It's amazing!!
The service, food, music and atmosphere were all excellent. A great place for Sunday brunch.

Shugga Hi is adorable. There was jazz music playing, cool art on the walls and very kind and helpful folks working there. We went on a Sunday morning- there was no wait and an amazing buffet (only option on Sunday). It was $20 and bottomless drinks were around $17. Shrimp and grits, biscuits and potatoes were bomb.

I seriously rarely give out 5 stars unless it's worth like 100 stars to me.  

I have had exposure to managed health care, hospitals and so forth because I have had experiences with many relatives/families/friends including myself in various health circumstances.  this includes all over the country and I am not even in the medical field.  Therefore, I  only have the perception of a patron.  

Mercy Suburban is an EXTREMELY excellent hospital.  I do not know how they came around to be this way but I can confidently say (and highly recommend) that this model of service and professionalism be used by other institutions.. and it does not have be hospitals either.  

In general, I definitely understand how difficult patients can sometimes be and ESPECIALLY patient's families (because I can be that way too). So sometimes that means it's really not always easy on the other side either.    But this particular medical staff really puts all of this to a test (and pass!)   Further, I noticed that the nurses here are 'brighter' in that they can explain things better and in more detailed.  An example is that they cannot give diagnosis and all the info that a 'doctor' can do ... but they were able to at least explain some of the functions that they are involved in so those types of  info (no matter how minor) is really helpful (and sometimes even comforting).  it just shows that the health professionals are able to take the time out to explain and give you as much info as they can possibly provide.  NOW IMAGINE ASKING inner-CITY HOSPITALS TO DO THAT!  i dont think so. 

Great job and standing ovation for Mercy Suburban and i seriously hope that this hospital continues to remain this way for a VERYYYYYYYYY long time.

What's better than FREE?!  Babies two months to six months can take baby splash class for free.  That's four months of free lessons.  Classes meet every week for 20 minutes.  I got enrolled the first week I called.  There was daytime availability, weekend and one evening.  Even though my daughter is about 6 weeks old, she was allowed to enroll.

For your first visit you should get there about 15 minutes early to fill out a waiver and purchase a reusable swim diaper if you have not picked one up at Target, Little Bird Nesting Company or Green Baby Elephant.  All non-potty trained babes must don a reusable swim diaper-no disposables.  

There are plenty of changing rooms with benches or family bathrooms with changing tables.  There is a shower area and one hairdryer for use. 

While waiting for your class to begin there are about five rows of seating where you can view the pool area.  When everyone bum rushes the door, follow everyone in.  

There are two pools which are clearly numbered.  Each pool is 4 feet deep and kept at 90 degrees and uses UV to keep them clean and sanitary.  Only one parent is allowed  in the pool.  There are six infants in the class.  The other parent can come into the pool area and sit on a bench.

We sang songs, worked on floating, worked on tummy time, did "up and under" where you pour water on the baby head to toe through a cup with holes on the bottom of it, floated while holding mirrors in front of the baby, and went through a tunnel with toys dangling about.  Each class ends with the goodbye song and the baby was awarded a ribbon.  Our teacher is Miss Danielle and she was warm and nice.  I believe she is also a school teacher.

FYI- the school is in a strip mall.  Next up Little Froggy One, where she will be going under!  Yikes!

Water safety is really important and DeMont is a great asset.  They also host birthday parties.

After a long hungry 45 minutes or so of trying to decide what to eat, my boyfriend and I decided on Indian food. Our GPS led us here.

Initially, we were definitely turned off by the atmosphere (or lack thereof). With diamond plate covered beams placed throughout the interior, and cold, sterile, unforgiving fluorescent lighting glaring down on everything, we spent a good amount of our dinner discussing the million and ten different things we would do to make the place nicer.

But we were soon made comfortable by the overwhelmingly friendly staff, who supplied us with papadums and dipping sauce while we perused the menu.

The waitress did give me incorrect information when asked what sauce was served on the Chicken Kedai Curry, but she realized her error and came back to make sure it was okay with me.

While we were waiting, she brought us a complimentary Mango Lassi, which I had never had before, and never will again, because I thought I was going to throw up after I tried it. But my boyfriend thought it was delicious!

When the food finally came it was AMAZING and just what I had been craving. I was a little worried when they brought out the naan bread, because I've never seen naan bread that looked like that before, but it was super super yummy. I would definitely probably get medium spice instead of mild next time, as I really didn't taste any spice at all. My boyfriend ordered his hot, and he also said he would probably try medium next time (and this is coming from someone who would put hot sauce on everything, if he could). There was enough for both of us to take home an entire second-meal's worth in a doggie bag.

Of course, there were a lot of stinky farts and burps all night afterwards. But I'd happily pay that price again!

I've been here twice since I moved to town a bit ago. Its near my office which is nice and they are friendly and fast, which can make all the difference. I've had the ropa vieja and the grilled chicken dish. The ropa vieja was excellent--its one of my favorites and I really enjoyed this version. The chicken was good, with a squeeze of fresh lime that really made the dish. The black beans and rice were solid black beans and rice, and the plantains made a huge difference. A great option for a quick lunch and something a little different!

Im from florida and was excited to find an authentic cuban restaurant in driving distance from my house and I couldn't wait to try it. It was easy enough to find as it was directly off of the highway in a strip mall type plaza. the place is small but adequate and the music playing was not overly loud. I viewed the menu online and knew what i wanted walking into the place but there was a sign on the door that stated no cubans at this time (cuban sandwiches) so I was bummed because thats what I came to try. The lady that took my order was not very friendly and seemed rushed. I stood at the counter for about 5 minutes while she stood idle waiting for the other woman , who looked like she was on her lunch break, to come back. I ordered the chicken and carne empanadas and they were absolutely amazing. we were going to sit in and eat but were not sure if they could accommodate our two kids but they did have a high chair available. 

Side note: There is a $10.00 minimum to use a credit or debit card.

Being from Florida this place is the real deal.  Must go if you love Cuban food. Cuban sandwiches are huge and many other authentic Cuban dishes. I hear they are opening up in the borrow soon with dance floor.

I haven't had Indian food in a long time and had never been to India Grill before, so my friend and I stopped in for a late night dinner. We arrived around 8:45 and they were set to close at 9:30. We were seated right away and there were a few other occupied tables as well.

One of the hesitations that I usually have with Indian restaurants in general is that they tend to take forever to cook the food, but here this was not the case. We started off with the vegetable pakore (something like an indian version of cauliflower tempura) with accompanying sauce, which was excellent. I also had a bowl of daal (lentil) soup. It was not what I expected, but I was pleasantly surprised, it had some great spices and flavors to it. My friend got the mango lasse and lamb madras, both got a thumbs up from us. We also had an order of the garlic naan, but I wasn't very impressed with that as I thought it was too crunchy and prefer when the bread is softer.

The prices are a bit on the steep side here (i.e. $12.95 for butter chicken entree, most other entrees in the $13-15 range), but this is due to the fact that the portions are HUGE. It's literally enough for 2-3 meals to take home for leftovers, so it justifies the slightly higher price tag. 

Also, I was highly entertained by the indian music videos playing on the flat screen TV by our table, it really was a fun cultural touch. Since the service was good, the food was tasty and everything was an overall great experience, I will return again. Next time I'm getting some butter chicken. Nom, nom, nom.

I had brunch today, at Shugga Hi Bakery and Cafe and I thoroughly enjoyed it. They had both a breakfast and lunch buffet, together, for one reasonable price. I sampled just about everything. Got a waffle and omelet to order, which was included in the price of the Buffet. The waffle was so light and delicious and the omelet was very tasty.  Next time, I will try the Henley syrup. The syrup was very good, also. Had a good Mimosa.The coffee was excellent. I had decaf. Then, I sampled the buffet items. The biscuits were big, fluffy and delicious and the bacon was good. I like it crispy and they had a good assortment of bacon and ham, to please everyone. Both the breakfast and lunch buffets had a generous assortment of foods, from which to choose. Loved the Shrimp and Grits, Cajun Pasta, Collards and Pot Roast. So many different choices, didn't get to taste them all, but what I had, were all very tasty. And WOW!!!, the desserts are heavenly! The banana pudding, lemon blueberry sugar cookies and the chocolate chip cookies were delicious. They were busy and you may have a short wait, but totally worth it. I was not disappointed.  The vibe is good, very friendly, laid back atmosphere. I love the paintings on the wall and the decor. It is very inviting. I will most definitely be going back to Shugga Hi.

Ordered an extra large white pizza from here, one of the best white pies I ever had. Each slice was massive, cheesy, full of garlicky goodness and was soft as a blanket. Each slice was heaven in my mouth. Will be back ASAP.

If you're in Nashville this is a must! Holy cow, where do I begin?  We went for brunch on Sunday and omg, omg, omg, everything was delicious!!! Their strawberry French toast casserole (not sure if that's the proper name) was the absolute best. And the chicken... I've traveled all over the country and in my 35 years on this earth, I've never tasted a better bbq chicken.  So juicy, succulent, a gift to your taste buds.  As for the atmosphere, it felt like being home . One of the owners stopped by to greet us and she was just the absolute sweetest.  It really felt like stopping by the family reunion. Do yourself a favor and check this place out, you will not be disappointed!!!

This food is mediocre. If you think this is great Indian food, then you have not actually HAD great Indian food. I ordered the Tikka Masala chicken, and it was bright hot pink. It had some kind of food coloring in it; I have never had Tikka Masala that was that color before. It literally looked like it was out of a paint can from Home Depot. It tasted sort of artificial also, and was way too rich. It either had a lot of cream or a lot of ghee or both. The only other way I can describe it is that it was a very rich, oily sauce, that had very little taste.

The plain Basmati rice was good and the naan was no better than the frozen stuff at Publix.

If you really want great Indian food, I'm afraid a trip to the USF area of Tampa is in order. Or, even closer to St. Pete: India's Grill on Kennedy Blvd. in Tampa is very good.

It's really such a shame that the quality of restaurants in downtown St. Pete is so subpar.
I love BACK TO CUBA!   The ambiance is great, it is a cozy place.  I always get the black beans and rice, and flan. I don't know how they can beans and rice so good!

Just wonderful.

There's a lot of hustle and soul in the folks who work  at this little cafe.

Props to Simon K. for recommending the chicken empanada. Fried fresh to order, it was an amazing treat and a real bargain at $1.50 each. I'll be getting at least a couple of these on my next visit. 

Other highlights?

- The chimichurri sauce that came with the empanada and also was spread liberally on the churrasco steak.
