- The sweet, succulent plantains that came with my arroz con pollo (rice with chicken)

- The large portion and tender chicken in aforementioned arroz con pollo (although the dish overall was a little mild for my tastes).

- The delectable black beans that came with the churrasco.

- The dense, enormous, not-too-sweet flan.

- Strong and sweet Cubano coffee

- Fresh and refreshing mango juice


Drawbacks?

- Seating is tight

- No substitution policy with any of the sides (a little unusual for Nashville, but presumably meant to minimize confusion with the sole short order cook working furiously to churn out meals for the lunch crowd)

- A little pricey by Nashville standards for a counter service restaurant -- lunch for two ran us ~$40 for two entrees (with sides), an empanada, a juice, a dessert and a coffee, including tax and tip.

BUT this was for a huge amount of food (we took home leftovers) and more importantly, wonderful HIGH QUALITY food. 

Value-for-the-money is 5 STARS all the way.
Used to come here all the time when it first opened. The service now is awful and the food is not much better. The place was trashed and the workers were rude.  Will not be returning.

I have been trying to figure out where to take my child for swim lessons for awhile.
Places are so expensive!
Finally I decided on DeMont.  My friends were all telling me wonderful things.
So far it has been an amazing experience.  My daughter is in a group class (they only go up to 4 in a group) but it feels very individual!  They really pay attention to everything the kids are doing and are teaching them amazing skills to help them love the water!

Cupcakes! Who doesn't enjoy beautifully decorated, fresh baked, moist cupcakes? Well Smallcakes in Fairview Heights is open and I am excited Fairview has a sweet shop of its own on the main I-159 corridor. It's a little further down past Krispy Kreme if you are traveling south, but it is GREAT I can stop there for a sugar fix when I am doing shopping in the area. The place is beautiful and new, clean and pristine and you are greeted with a smile and cheerful hello upon entering! The staff is friendly and informative and I love patronizing places where people seem to love where they work and have a passion for talking about their products. 

I always have to get the basics- a yellow cupcake with buttercream. I find chocolate has a tendency to mask "eh" products, and people who love chocolate tend to focus on their love of chocolate over the actually taste of the product the chocolate is in. Also chocolate cake tends to be a more moist cake just because of the combo of ingredients and how they bake together. White or yellow cake can't be masked. If it is dry, flavorless and nasty you will know. That is NOT the case with Smallcakes! Now remember it is a franchise concept, and although each one is locally owned and operated, there is still a standard across all locations and this doesn't disappoint. 

Please patronize this place! I love Woods bakery in O'Fallon and I love The Cup in Edwardsville, but as much traffic that passes through Fairview Heights, let's keep this place going! Check this place out and support them! 

Please keep up the standards, Smallcakes Fairview Heights team! Don't make me regret my glowing review in 6 months!

I would give them 5 stars if they would find a place to put more tables!  We sat outside on what was a day almost too cold to do so.  I also saw at least 3-4 groups of diners leave due to lack of seating.  

I am a sucker for the Cuban sandwich.  My only gripe, and I don't know if mayo is standard on a Cuban, is that I don't want mayo on mine!  Not sure why everyone thinks mayo should be a standard condiment but it should not.  The ratio of all other ingredients though is perfect, the pork, pickles, mustard, swiss, and that oh so crispy bread.

My friend had the fish tacos and they looked great, 3 healthy sized tacos for $6.00.  We also shared the tostones (fried plantains), which I love but on this trip they lacked flavor.  Just needed to be kicked up with some seasoning.

I've definitely had better Cuban food down in Florida, but I don't live in Florida I live in Nashville, so this is going to keep doing just fine.

went here a lot before. started to taste like the meat was chewy and fatty in their steaks. other people I know noticed too. they could be using different steak to save money or something but this caused me to stop going here. Steve's and jims are much better.

I went to  Shugga Hi Bakery and Cafe on a Saturday for brunch. They were very accommodating as it was 10 of us. I started off with the peach sangria. I was very surprised by the large size sangria that I only paid $6 for. It was very tasty as well. They also had live music. The musician was soulful and played well. We also met one of the owners and she was so nice. She made sure my party was taken care of. The service did seem slow at sometimes. However, the live music and overall vibe was entertaining as we waited. My grits were so good!!! I didn't have to add any salt or pepper to them. This was a big plus for me. Please do me a favor and order the grits when you're there. I will definitely visit again when I'm in the area.

Shugga Hi staff welcomes you warmly and provides stellar service. We stopped for breakfast on our way out of Nashville and were very impressed! All the food and pastries we tried were top quality, absolutely divine! Our server was super sweet and offered us a free cupcake when she found out it was our first time in. Such an intimate, family feel. The decor and art is incredible and fun too!

Horrible customer service i ever had,  waited over two weeks to find out i was been purposely ignored and profiled due to my old car, i called over and over and no quote by anyone l.  I wish i never wasted my time going here and i will tell mbusa to revoked their license as well.  No idea how they do business!!!  Only high end cars and skin color matters!! Do not go here!

This was hands-down one of the best Brunch locations I have ever been too. The food was AMAZING!! And the sangria was to die for!!! Very affordable!! Absolutely beautiful atmosphere!!! I love this place so much I am going to book It out for my graduation brunch party!!

A good cheesesteak. Not the best, or you're a fool, but certainly delicious and decently filling. Having only been here once, I will have to return for a consistency check. I look forward to that day.

This is the perfect example of a NO STAR rating being needed for yelp. 

  This hospital is the worst. I was seen in the ER and told it was just a minor thing and take this and you will be okay. Two days later it didn't go away I went to my local ER and was admitted immediately for a life threatening issue. They told me if I hadn't gotten in when I did I could've required life changing surgery! To add insult to injury their billing department is just as bad as the doctor. They keep sending me bills saying my insurance has paid the claim! Stay away at all cost! They can cost you your life and credit score. Dr. Michael Fernades was uncaring, unknowledgeable, and dismissive!

 When I just tired to call in the number that's listed on here tells me that I have reached the after hours line and the office will be open from at 9:00 am. It's 10:41 am!!! I pushed 0 like the prompt says to and got an operator who informed me that the office is experiencing a staffing issue and to call back in 10 minutes! This place is a grade A Joke!

Stopped here really quick to pick up a Cubano after arriving back in Nashville from vacation. It was 3pm on a Saturday and they had three tables eating and then my ToGo order. The staff was pleasant and got right on my order. The sandwich was tasty and warm. I can count the number of Cubanos that I have eaten on one hand, so it's authenticity can not be guaranteed from my review. It was tasty, hand made, and they are a small locally owned establishment. I would eat here again.
the food is all right here but the pork here is really good here. The place is kind of small and the cuban food is not the best I've ever had but not much cuban in nashville
I heard great things about this place, I was disappointed , horrible food , all it tasted like was salt , I will never go here or any of their other locations again

Here in town for a few days visiting friends. Staying at an air bnb. Decided to hit this place up for a brunch. The bloody Mary's were amazing and da bomb on the menu, the biscuits made with it is absolutely life changing. Great place, great staff and amazing food. Will definitely be back and recommend to anyone visiting.
Best Cubano in Nashville. No one else even comes close. It's a meal and a half. I've tried several of the traditional Cuban dinners and they were tasty as well.
Slop and crap in disguise as Indian food. Place is filthy and stinks up the block. Get outta here already!!!

At first glance, India Grill seems to be just your ordinary 
"plain jane" type of Indian restaurant...  cheesy decorations abound and Bollywood videos on the TV.  But if you can get past all that you'll be in for a treat...
At lunch they offer us a wonderful lunch buffet for under $10. A great value and top-notch selections...
But at dinner is when India Grill comes alive with the smell of curry and some tasty food... flaky Veggie Samosas, Daal Soup and Butter Chicken is my favorite line up!!!
I have been there several times food is good, service is good for the most part, my only real complaint is the atmosphere... or lack of...

Cuban sandwiches and plates.  Saw pork dishes, chicken dishes, seafood options, beans and rice, plantains, yucca.  I had a bistec sandwich.  The bread was delicious.  It was soft on the inside and really flaky on the outside.  Yum.  The sandwich had potato stick snackies and grilled onions inside.  The meat was a wee tough.  The cafe con leche was so good and hit the spot.  Got me through the rest of my work day.  Inexpensive.  People working there are nice.  Cool lunch spot.

This is probably one of the better Indian Restaurants in all of Tampa Bay.  The lunch buffet is ok, although the selections are limited, IMO.  I would have liked a lamb dish as one of the buffet items.  10 dishes in all, if you include the naan.  The naan is probably average for an Indian restaurant.  Lunch buffet is good (though not as good as some I've had in other cities though, and their selections could be better).  Prices for non-buffet items are a bit steep for Indian food.  But good value on their mango lassi though.  

Their lamb vindaloo is pretty good.  Very close to Laziz, maybe a bit better.      

Although I'm giving it 4 stars, it's probably closer to 3.5-3.7 stars, because of the lack of selections on their lunch buffet, average naan, and no lamb dish.  

Service for lunch is good to above average (3-4 stars).

Went for the lunch and ordered the lunch buffet. It didn't have as many options as some others I've been to, but I liked the majority of the options, so that was a plus.

Prices were reasonable, no like some other lunch buffets. I didn't order anything else but the buffet, but I'm sure it all would have been good based on what I had. I would like to go back and try some other items in the very near future.

First Cuban restaurant that I've been to in Nashville. I left so full!  I had the churrasco skirt steak, plantains, rice and beans. I also had Cuban coffee. There was limited seating inside. Everything was delicious and it didn't take very long to make. They even bring you a basket of crunchy and buttered bread. I will definitely be back here again!
We got pastry to go, so I can't comment on the restaurant yet. But the people were very nice, the menu looked very good, and the pastry we got was excellent. We WILL be back.
Great service, sweet owners and the dessert/bakery is wonderful with a lot of variety! Da bomb is the best thing on the menu... You will not regret it! It is a must try!

We've been going here for years. We had our daughter in starting at a 6 month class and is now 3 years old. She gets lots of attention from the teachers and being indoors really helps. They also have large changing rooms. A little pricy and it's always difficult to reschedule classes with so many filled up

After not eating here in over a year, I decided to stop in and pick up some Cheesesteaks for my family. Good solid cheesesteak to be honest. Better than Pat's or Geno's tourist trap sandwiches or any pizza joint. Comparable to Steve's with way less grease, but they need more steak options. The fries are very good. Prices are not bad and free pickles and peppers is a nice touch. I'll be back.

Had the chicken kadai, it was pretty good... garlic naan was nothing special. Service was good. Atmosphere, meh.  The CL Bet of the Bay 2010 winner for Indian food lured me in.  How much do those things cost?  Ill be going back to Green Chili next time
Good collection. Friendly, helpful service. Stores like Boscov's are still needed. Hope it survives.

Of course this place is located in a random strip mall by the highway... conveniently located right next to a dry cleaner.. look out the window and enjoy the awesome gas-station views... 

Who cares.  The food here is fantastic.  I almost always get the lechon, but (as others have noted) the Cuban sandwiches are also fantastic.  The lechon (like the other entrees) comes with beans and rice and plantains and is seriously a LOT of food for the price.  You can easily get two or three meals out of one plate.  Also worth mentioning: the yuca with mojo.  I had never had yuca with mojo before but now I'm on a quest to have it wherever I go in a vain attempt to replicate the experience.

Don't ask me why I ventured into this joint looking for jerk chicken because obviously this isn't Back to Jamaica Cafe. However, I was pleasantly surprised with this place. Not being very familiar with Cuban cuisine, I don't have much to compare to. I can't even remember the names of what we ordered, but I had a shrimp dish and my husband a pork dish both cooked in a supposedly spicy cajun sauce. It wasn't spicy to my taste, but tasted great nonetheless. Both were served with rice, a salad with tomato, onion, and avocado (yummy), and fried plantains. I loved the plantains. We went for an early dinner after work and before our softball games later that evening (not sure if a great idea at the time because the portions are plentiful), and so it wasn't crowded which was nice. The menu is short and listed on colored pieces of paper mounted on a cork board, and there are no substitutions. Nothing to be impressed about on the inside for sure.

I'll definitely make my way back (not before a softball game in June however) and try the empanadas and sandwiches. The empanadas looked amazing, but we held back this visit!

I do have to add that we actually went to this place at 8:45 one evening after our games (they close at 9), and they offered to "make us a sandwich" but we couldn't order anything that had to be cooked in the kitchen. We said no thanks, but gave it a second chance. It was definitely worth it.

We saw the movie Chef and decided Cuban sandwiches were a good idea. The bread was good and the sandwich looked like it could appear in the movie so they did their job. They had some unique drink options; my only complaint was that there wasn't a paper menu. I like to read what I'm getting up close but whatever, I still enjoyed myself.

Not the best Indian restaurant but it wasn't the worst either. Somewhere in the middlin', I would say. Had the combo veggie platter with Pakora, Panak Paneer and Samosas. The samosas were extremely good. I had the Tandoori Beef and the chunks were moist, the onions well-caramelized. My friend had the chicken Madras curry..nice coconut flavor.
I loved the poppadoms with a spicy red curry dip. Service was okay..I was a bit disappointed that Chai refills were not free with as much as we ordered.
Bathrooms were just okay..not very pleasing and the Bollywood movie playing was perhaps a bit too much. I've heard the buffet is okay but I still like Curriez much better.

The cupcakes we got were delicious the girls were very very pleasant it will be much nicer once they get tables and chairs so you can sit and have coffee with your cupcakes we will definitely check back they're supposed to be getting them and we will go !!!!

When I got there, all the tables were taken. I was going to wait, but the guy behind the counter seemed pushy about getting me to order take-out. I told him I'd rather just wait for a table. He said that there was no empty table. I said that I knew that. He said that I couldn't wait inside the restaurant. I thanked him and said that I would be back. When I came back in five minutes, there was an empty table. And then, I had a feast. By accident. This "accident" was I grant you aided by the very real influence of a 20 oz. Heineken I BYO'd from a store in the same strip-mall (also had to help my date finish hers, of course). The palomilla was so good I had to eat it all, of course. And of course I had to eat all the plantains I ordered as a side dish. And, of course, dessert had to be followed by a caf cubano, a little dark coffee with sugar and hot milk. Well, the bill was bigger than I prophesied, but I felt so good I didn't care, at the time.
Absolutely disgusting flea market. The building and whole strip mall should be condemned
The cubano is really good.  The toasted roll is awesome. Also try the sweet plantanes.
Stopped on our way thru Nashville tonight and was not disappointed.  My wife had the shrimp and I tried the pork..... amazing!!  The staff was friendly and efficient.  We will definitely stop again.

The food is quite good, or the Cubans are quite good.

Of late, they are constantly out of Cubans later in the day.  This has to be their most popular sandwich (or certainly one of the more popular) and yet regularly out.  

And I don't mean out by around 5pm--I mean out at 1:40pm.  They have an alternative sandwich, but its much smaller and not hardly as appetizing and its simply not a Cubano.

There's also the occassional "On 15/20 minute" Break sign and locked door.  Its unfortunately not possible to know when the 20 minutes are up--which makes this challenging to deal with.  I saw this happen with roughly 3 people--presumably all employees on site.

I've been a reasonably loyal customer for quite some time.

This would otherwise be a 4.5+ review, but given the service and supply issue (ie not having key menu items on a semi-regular basis) I think it deserves a 3 out of 5.

PS.  Its also closed on Mondays as I recall.

I was riding down Red Lion Road and saw the sign that said Lunch Special $8.00 for a cheese steak, fries & soda.  Made a U-turn and went in.  Ordered a cheese steak with wiz.  When I bit it I new right away that it was not "Cheese Wiz" it had to be a cheap brand of cheedar cheese.  Several other people who order after me ask for cheese wiz also.  If you are not serving cheese wiz you should tell the customer that it is not the original cheese wiz but a cheap can of cheedar cheese.

I'll stick to Geno in South Philly.
Not sure if I got them on an off day, but I am not feeling the 4 star loving. Greasy and semi bland Cuban sandwich and poorly spiced black beans do not cut it for my idea of tasty Cuban fare.

Came here in '15 and this place was highly recommended.  My daughter and son love it. They provide showers for afterwards. Although, I don't bother bc some take longer showers than others. Not enough stalls for everyone to get changed you just gotta wait your turn.  Everyone is super nice!

Get ready for this review because it's not going to be pretty. We walked in on a Friday night. Few tables they have are all full. No waiting area. So we are just standing awkwardly by the register while the staff pass us numerous times but don't bother greeting us. A table clears up and we sit. She takes our drink order and decides to place my soda can inside my cup of ice. Really?? That's just gross. We were ready to order 
but the waitress never comes by again. She tells us you order at the counter. So we get up and order. Could she not tell us we order at the counter when delivering our drinks? The food comes but I guess she thought utensils weren't important. Had to get up and get that as well. How do you bring us the food with no utensils? 

Now I'm already feeling some type of way. This service is shitty as hell. And it's not super packed in here. So this food better be good. Considering I'm Dominican and can cook some good stuff. I order the palomilla steak. Dont waste your time ordering that. Steak is poor quality - very dry and chewy. The black beans were just okay. I make them better. The rice was an unusual texture not found in Caribbean restaurants. 
I'm already super upset. My boyfriend's steak was better than mine. He had the Churrasco. Which is skirt steak with sauce on top. Portions were decent. 

Bottom line. If you want Cuban Food from this place, call for pick up and bring it home where you have forks. Enjoy the okay food without shitty service. You are not missing anything. They had awards from way back. 2005-2006 on their walls. Seems like they need a new evaluation. They are hiring. Please help this place if you an experienced manager/server. 

Communication is everything. If we were simply greeted at the door and were told they were understaffed and the rules of the place like ordering at the counter we would have prepared ourselves. Instead of being let down. I take great pains to situations like this specially when it's your own people. Makes us look bad man.

On a recent trip I was not impressed, probably my worst experience there. I've never been a huge fan but it's convenient for a quick meal plus they have flat screens so you can watch the game or news of the day. First my soda was filled only 3/4th the way once settled. The roll was stale on the ends. The steak and fries were swimming in cheese. Can I get some steak and fries with my cheese please? The cheese is another thing... The melted American cheese taste funny. The Cheese Wiz tastes like nothing that I've had before. The staff are extremely friendly and helpful. The place is immaculate as far as cleanliness is concerned. They just need to pay a bit more attention to the products they are selling. I'll give them another try out of convenience for now. There are some other places I  prefer and would go to first if more convenient to me.
Love all of the different flavors!  The Peanut butter cup one is my favorite so far.  Must try!

My 4 star rating is based on several factors

restaurant is always clean
staff is friendly
cheesesteaks are better than average
cheese fries are great

Much better alternative to the other "philly cheesesteak place"  a couple miles down the road

Have only been for the lunch buffet, but it is always spot on.  They have the same items almost daily, but they are good and I don't go too often.  Splurge and get a King Fisher beer with your meal and enjoy.  

The butter chicken is one of my favorites and they have a lot of veg options too.  

I like that they leave an entire pitcher of water on your table. 

They always have Indian music or Bollywood movies playing on the tv.  It is not overly fancy, but has an Indian motif.  Lunch stays busy.  I dine in, but you can pay by the pound for to go.

Okay, the place redeemed itself, and now I feel compelled to give it a 5-stars to balance out the previous bland review, for an average of 4-stars, which is how I feel.  The pan con bistec sandwich was huge, crunchy, delicious in all the right ways, and rivals the ones you buy on Washington Avenue near South Beach in Miami.  Lechon asado was perfectly flavored this time with amazing rice and beans.  I suppose the last visit they had a stand-in chef?  But this place is respectable, with good food, and I am happier than ever I came back.  Hooray for second chances!

The best subway once you figure it out. The drive through is the superior factor in my decision to give 4 stars. The fact that it is subway prevents me from giving them 5 stars. Use the drive through and when your order is complete save your order under your phone number. You don't get texts or alerts, at least for now and not that i want them. When I go back though it makes it easy to retrieve my girlfriend and my last order... sparing me from a long list of ingredients. The inside is clean and nothing bad, but nothing extraordinary from the staff. But again the drive through is awsome.  Hopefully this subway does well and gets copied in the future.

 The ordering method is a touchscreen with toppings being listed as less, normal and more. I think this helps so you don't have any verbal communication issues. Now I have been here a dozen or more times with no mistakes to my order or excessive waits.
Their Buffalo Wings are AWESOME. Im still trying to figure out the ingredients in their sauce that makes it so addicting lol ...Feel free to share if the Owner see's this lol ;-)

I could never tire of eating here! it is, handsdown, the best Cuban I've had in Knoxville. They are always friendly, even when they're busy. Prepare to wait, if they're busy when you get there... But it's worth it.

The food here was not as overwhelming as other reviewers led me to believe. My dinner companion and I both had fish; one fish sandwich (which they said was deep fried) and fries, the other was the breaded fish with a chopped mango topping, salad, rice and plantains. We had a side order of plantains and mango juice.

The breaded fish had a pretty decent amount of breading on it, and, after swapping pieces of our plates we felt like we were eating the same type of fish. Which... Would've been nice to know that it was a deep fried fish with mango topping. For me, that wasn't terrible, except it wasn't spectacular. The best thing I had was the white rice which was seasoned very well. 

The mango juice tasted closer to mango flavored drink with chunks of mango added to it. The portion sizes were excellent for the price. 

While it's a small note, the cashier overcharged us and didn't notice. We had to go back inside to fix our total, but they were happy to do it. Definitely seemed like an honest mistake. 

Will we go back? Potentially to try the Cubano. I would highly recommend this spot for lunch. Eat up!

Just an ending note, absolutely NO substitutions are allowed, so, detailed eaters may want to know that going in!

Food was awesome !! Came on a Saturday at lunchtime and it was packed! Not a lot of seating but got lucky with a table outside. The Cuban sandwich was perfect and the plantains and rice and beans were just what I was looking for ! Will be back when I visit Nashville!

Nashville has gone...Back to Cuba!  Leave the southern meat and three behind and dig in to some of the best Cuban food north of Miami!  I've tried several items from the Cuban sandwich (I get mine "lightly" toasted), to the Vaca Frita, but my FAVORITE dish (that has yet to be replicated ANYWHERE...and I must come here to get my fix) is the Churrasco.  This is a simple, yet FLAVORFUL flat iron steak that is grilled and topped with the most amazing chimichurri sauce...YUM!  This dish is served with a side of black beans, tostones (double fried plantains) and white rice (this rice is sooooo good, I could make of meal of it alone!)
If my pic had smell-a-vision, you would be running Back to Cuba, not reading this review!  :) 

Enjoy!
Not bad on the prices, the food on the right size. I been eating here for over 15 years. I still go there have a great lunch lol

Great service. We were greeted by a lovely hostess and sat in s very sleek dining area. Great decorating in this modern looking, but inviting space. My daughter and I ordered Da Bomb. It was different, and we like it. My husband ordered the egg bowl and he really enjoyed it. My son got the omelette and declared his was the best! The server kept our drinks filled, and we left with full, happy bellies!

What a cute place. The service was wonderful and our meal was great. I enjoyed the chicken and waffles , sweet heat and great waffles. My husband enjoyed the waffle burger, so unique and tasty. The bloody Mary was also awesome. Their pastries are to die for, you must try the Apple fritter.

I'm a pretty huge fan of hole in the wall spots.  Back to Cuba felt like rolling the dice as we pulled into the gas station/strip mall parking lot.  Thankfully, it was the right gamble.  The staff is friendly but busy and a bit pre-occupied.  The true star of this show is the authentic Cuban food.  Everything I had was fresh and tasty.  When I go back to Nashville I hope to go Back to Cuba.
When it first opened it was great...since then...not so much...they serve hoagies now...roll was hard..when I got it home they didn't get the order right...it was ok...

Great place for authentic food! Not great for crowds. Only a few tables available. Steak sandwich soooo good and big. Desserts are the best and you can grab and few more to take home. 

Sometimes they run out of food, which is not cool!! I wish they would be open more.

In my quest for the best slice in NE Philly, we have a frontrunner. England pizza was the perfect slice that I was looking for. The crust wasn't too crisp, the slice wasn't greasy at all, and the price was damn good. The seasoning was good, so I didn't have to add anything to it, and if I did, I'm sure it would've only added to the slice. England is the one to beat so far....

I love real steak (non chopped ) I like Steves and old frusco's before they killed themselves. I like ginos and Lukes. I wasn't that impressed with this steak. I will say the combo price wasn't bad and here was more meat on this then most but the acual steak I tried a piece without anything on it and it was kind of minute steakish but slightly better. Fries were fries. Combo was 10.98+ tax i paid 13something with cheese for the fries. I'll up date if I try more items.

Delicious, but heavy. We had heard good things about this Cuban spot just up the street from our house and decided to finally try it out! The food was delicious! I got a guanabana juice and a special: pescado a la pina (grilled sea bass with pineapple, yellow rice, and salad). It was delicious, but very filling! I snacked off a few other plates as well - their sides are delicious! The yucca, plantains, and beans were particularly good! The only con? I don't think I'll be hungry again for days! Back to Cuba is charming - a very small restaurant with posters and pictures of Cuba on the wall. And it's popular! We walked in around one on a Saturday, and the time we left, there was a long line for food orders and a table! A great neighborhood restaurant that I'm sure we'll spend more meals at!

I have tried many an Indian place in my day, but this one is my favorite. I love the vegetarian options on the buffet and the fact that there is always pakora available. The servers there are very attentive, even during the buffet. They bring hot, fresh, naan to the table if it's not already on the buffet. The mango lassi is so delicious, the donut-type dessert is awesome, and I love all the vegetarian dishes. I can't even explain how much I love this place, but go for the buffet so you get a taste of all the best dishes!

Is a subway with a drive through! It's amazing! I didn't know all the options I could get. I've been here several times since it's opened and have never been disappointed. The drive through is also touch screen!!! It's a top subway for sure!

Having had Cuan food many times and mainly in Miami, Fort Lauderdale, and Orlando I can confidently tell you this place is legit.  They start you off with some toasted cuban bread, buttered to perfection-solid.  My buddy order the Cubano which was a super nice looking sammy, and needless to say he ate every bit. He also had a side of Plantains which were perfect and had a nice crunch.  I ordered the Shrimp in a spicy creole tomato sauce, it came with rice, tostones, beans, and salad.  The shrimp vere perfectly cooked, beans were awesome, tostones great!  This is a hidden gem. Make sure you also try the green hot sauce.

Cheers!

Love ShuggaHi! Could not say enough about this place. Staff is so sweet and accommodating, and the steak and eggs was the best I've had. They know what they're doing here! Also those alcohol infused desserts are dangerously good!
It's been a while since I was here but I agree with a previous review that the quality has really gone down. Not worth the trip.

Absolutely the messiest cheesesteak I've ever eaten... but delicious. Cheese oozing everywhere. I don't usually like the sliced steaks, but this was excellent. Also, other customers were really excited about the "long hots" - none for me, thanks!
Definitely clean and fast service. very pleasant staff also!

In a hurry so I'll keep this short.  Sandwich was made with bare hands. Are gloves not a requirement here? Tried to pay on two occasions and was not allowed to until we ate. Strange.  Got a Cubana and a Miami.  They were both just ok. Liked the flaky bread, but overall flavor was lacking. The unique soda in the goldish can was the best part. $24 w/tip for two people...  I would have enjoyed subway more. Love to support small business, so I wish I could say the experience was better.

Do not judge a book by its cover! The outside of the building is a bit odd looking, but once you step inside, you've entered heaven! Menu selections are southern, but unique and delicious, pastries are as pleasing to look at as they are to eat, and the staff is delightful. A must if you're in the neighborhood.... a must if you aren't!

Ordered a hoagie to pick up due to weather. I ordered hot peppers and didn't get any. The girl was very short with me (maybe she remembered my number from the last time) and the mayo was put on heavy. Will not be ordering from here anymore I'm really dissatisfied.

This is my favorite place to eat in Nashville. It's afforable and delicious. I always get the roast pork tacos with white rice and plantains. Tons of flavor in everything, including the rice. The blackberry juice is great too. The staff is always nice and I've never waited very long for my food.
Awesome school they take care of the kid really good my son been there for 3 month now and he love it, teachers are really good with the kids.

Took my kids to a party here. They had a great time.  The facility is very clean and well kept up.  The only downside is it gets wicked hot in the swim area.  And because of that the chemicals get pretty gnarly.  All that being said it seems like a great place to take the younger ones.

What an amazing breakfast...chicken and waffles was delicious! The sister owners were adorable, super friendly and I can't wait to go back again! Service was fast and friendly. Support local businesses, they deserve your money over the chains!
The best Cuban food! Amazing lechon and Pollo. Highly recommended this restaurant.................

My pizza was only warm in the middle, fries were cold and u know u can't reheat fries =\. I ordered a quesadilla and steak as well a salad. Salad was missing the dressing, the receipt didn't have the right dressing listed anyway. The food itself was ok, nothing to rave about

I was so excited to try a Cuban restaurant in TN. The prices are excellent but if you're looking for delicious food this is not the place. My mother, a Puerto Rican, could immediately tell that the tostones were frozen and heated up in a way that made them soggy (not unedible--just not very good). The empanadilla de pollo was good, but my mother could tell that it was not made at the restaurant. I had the Churrasco (a good size) and I enjoyed the tenderness of the steak. The steak and beans and rice were not flavorful, but I added salt and it was fine. My mom had the lechon asado (the easiest dish for Spanish people to make according to her) and it was mediocre. My dad had the vaca frita and it's usually shredded, marinated and dried so that it has a very satisfying chew to it. This was bland, carried very little citrus flavor and was soft, not chewy. It was nice to see a Cuban restaurant in TN, but it could/should be a lot better.

loved everything about this place. the fried plantains were out of this world and the Cuban was amazing. it is very small inside, max seating of 14 people, so grab a table if you see one before you order. My husband and I split a Cuban and plantains for $11. can't wait to go back!!
Good food, customer service was ok. Definitely seemed a lil overwhelmed. I was at my cousins and wasn't sure of any places to eat. Good food, long wait

It's against the law to charge a minimum purchase on a debit card, therefore that's why I reported this restaurant to MasterCard for not allowing me to purchase 2 empanadas that cost six dollars for dinner, I don't predict they will be in business for much longer

Wit or witout is definitely an up and comer in the northeast. 

Much cleaner and better looking than the traditional kings (princes?) of steaks. Not only that, they're actually cheaper. 

Wit or Witout has more flat screen TV's than half the bars in the neighborhood. Even their menu is displayed on a TV. The cashier is usually a cute girl--a nice change from the surly 300 pounders with sweaty bald heads i see at other places.

The cheesesteaks are meaty and delicious. Sliced not chopped. They have melted american (think Chickie's & Pete's crab fry dip) along with the classics: whiz and provolone. Trust me on this one, melted american is the way to go.

They also have a great condiment bar with pickles and peppers.

Jim's and Steve's are the big names in NE, but Wit or Witout is better, cheaper and nicer. Highly recommended.

Warm and welcoming staff, delicious breakfast (we had Da Bomb and the scrambled eggs, crispy bacon and grits with raw sugar and butter) plus cookies to go for later (salted caramel and chocolate chip), everything we tried was exceptional and we are so glad we stopped in while visiting Nashville based on the advice of other Yelp reviewers.

This is hands down my favorite restaurant. I originally started coming here like 5 years ago. I've tried the Cuban Sandwich (5 stars), the Miami sandwich (4 stars), Tres Leches (5 stars). The last year I've tried several things. The chicken empanadas which is hands down amazing. The pan con bistec not that great, it's really dry. Some other sandwich which was really dry as well. Then on Tuesday I tried the lunch special carne con papa, which was amazing. It's pretty much a beef stew (less stewy) with a creole sauce with a side of black beans and rice. It was sooooo great. I love this place. The ambiance is extremely great. When your inside hear you just forget about everything that's going on outside the cafe. The staff there are extremely nice and helpful, especially the girl that's always thanking orders, she's super nice.

I know nothing of Cuban food, but it's nearby so I've eaten here 3 or 4 times. I recently ordered the Ropa Vieja (shredded beef) special ($14) and it was good, but I've never been to Miami. I do know the black bean soup that came with it should not have been at room temperature, though the rice was perfect. The owner has a big personality, almost a Soup Nazi type, who does not allow smart phones to be used. But I'll buy in and say it's part of the place's charm. I've had other items such as the Cubano, and they all seem good enough, but there's an attitude of carelessness from the somewhat sullen staff, including, apparently, the kitchen.

The best Indian food in St. Pete that I've had.  And the lunch buffet is definitely the way to go.  An excellent value, and you get a variety of dishes to try.  I am really surprised to see some low reviews here, because this is our favorite.  It is also the favorite of our Indian friend from Bombay.  The butter chicken and the palak paneer are craveworthy.  Every time we go for the lunch buffet, the staff brings out fresh nan bread for us.  I think the service is great at lunchtime--we've never been for dinner so I can't say.  The food on the buffet is kept fresh and tastes great right up until the end, unlike some buffets. We've eaten at Green Chile Bistro, Curriez, Taste of Punjab, Ajanta, and Deeya, AND I've eaten my way across India.  This is my favorite Indian place in town, hands down, and we feel darn lucky to have it here.

If it weren't for my laughable ER experience, I'd give this place at least 4.5 stars! I was injured on the job, with a facial laceration and possible concussion when I came in. The doctor that saw me didn't check for a concussion though I was struck in the face/head and didn't bother to X-ray my nose which is where I had been struck right on the bone. Dermabond was applied to seal the wound, I was given a tetanus shot, and sent on my way until my recheck the following day. Thankfully I didn't have a concussion and made it home okay. 

Dr. Nicholson from the Business Health Center was the exact opposite. He was shocked that I hadn't been checked for a concussion when I told him I had been nauseous and lightheaded for at least 30 minutes after the incident occurred and that no X-ray was taken! He gave me medicine to help with the fact that it was already inflamed and needed antibiotics to not get infected. He also wrote me a script to get an X-ray for the root of my nose and thankfully there was no fracture! I feel like he definitely knows what he is doing and is a credit to this hospital!

I have recently returned from a trip from Cuba and was missing everything about it! I was so happy to find this place. The young lady wasn't as friendly as she could have been but thankfully the food was good. 

I had steak, black beans and rice with plantains. I washed it down with passion fruit. Since it's not in my area, I won't be back soon but I will return in the future.

The other reviewers are right: the food is spectacularly bland.

I went here for a weekday lunch buffet outing and although I don't care for Tampa as a city, as another reviewer on here said, when you've cut your teeth on USF Tampa-area Indian food, there is just no going back. 

For example: I go to Jai Ho in Tampa and the Tandoori chicken forces - forces - me to close my eyes in sheer ecstasy. Spicy, vibrant, alive with flavor. 

Here, it just...tastes like chicken. We get no reward for the (expected) dryness of the chicken...just dryish chicken with a hint of spice.

Every other dish suffered from similar lack of spice (or TLC?). I have literally had better Indian food from cans from the health food store. I guess one good thing I could say is that I could taste the butter in the butter chicken. That is how under-spiced it is. 

The naan was boring. Every dish was a bit...dire. Go ahead, convince yourself that the five-star reviewers are right and go there. Just don't say I didn't warn you. 

The restaurant was clean, but the servers dreary. 

Undercutting the experience further, as someone else long ago commented, there was a bleach or chemical-like smell in the air. It couldn't be fixed by now? It hurts the flavor experience...what flavor there was.

Ordinarily, an Indian restaurant is one of the few places where a glass of water is not only appreciated, but the perfect accompaniment to a meal. Here, all it did was wash away what faint memories of any flavor I may have had.

Dessert notes: 

OK, I am not claiming superior knowledge, but what they called some variant on Gulab Jamun involved no fried balls of anything, whatsoever. It was a pleasant, thin pudding. Good but not great.

And from the same cold bar, the "hottest" thing in the "extra hot mango chutney" was the standard flavor of raw onion. Bizarre. Mislabeled? I have no idea. 

Disappointing, and I will not be back. The search continues for good Indian in St Pete. I actually drove all the way to Pinellas Park today to check out the better-rated Clay Oven, but maddeningly enough, they were closed. I guess I didn't stare at my Yelp app hard enough. Have no interest in driving that far regularly, so I guess that leaves me Green Chili to try out for lunch buffet...will report back on that at some point here. 

p.s. not to lay it on any thicker, but I just had to share this: as I was walking out, a girl started to chat me, asking if I'd tipped. I said, sure, of course I did and she told me you shouldn't, as the owner keeps all the tips. She said she worked there, lasting all of one week before she quit. Her big moment of realization was one time she got a $20 tip and had to go into the bathroom to cry. 

p.p.s. I don't mean to utterly trash this place, the ingredients are certainly fresh and I feel well-fed right now, but it's just...uninspiring, to say the least.

Our daughter is in Miss Randi's Little Froggy 2 class and she absolutely loves it. We've also attended some makeup classes (due to illness) with some of the other teachers and I can say that every teacher we've had an experience with has been fantastic. They're kind, patient and allow each child to move at their own pace. The facility is always clean. And everyone there (staff, instructors, parents, and students) are typically in a cheery mood and are very kind and polite. I can't recommend this swim school enough!

I've come here a few times for the buffet and know very little about Indian food other than what naan is, so my review may have to taken with a grain of salt. 

The buffet was mostly fresh. Loved the rice and naan as well as the mango pudding. The fried vegetable concoction (not sure what it's called exactly) was also cooked well and fresh. Some of the items seemed to be sitting out for some time, though. The service was okay but I thought it could be better because there aren't many people there when I go. 

Overall, decent Indian buffet. I know there are more highly rated Indian places in the area, so I recommend coming here for the buffet if you've never tried Indian food before.
Very good Cuban food!  Reminds me of eating Cuban in Miami.  Tasty plantains, black beans and rice, as well as the chimichurri sauce.  Pastries and café con leche were excellent as well!

They did an extensive engine block repair on my 2003 Toyota Camry and saved me from having to get rid of the car.  In the interim, the radiator rusted out and 
Dash Automotive came to the rescue with outstanding service and an economical repair.

Very professional automotive repair company.  I will be using them for all my car repair needs.
Very charming and authentic food. The atmosphere isn't a chain restaraunt because it's not a chain! This place is the real deal and I look forward to trying more options soon
Wonderful cakes and baked goods, and a delicious brunch!

Wow this place. The aesthetic is wonderful. Nice, but not pretentious. Servers were really nice and attentive.  My friend and I ordered Chicken & Waffles and DA BOMB. DA BOMB is eggs, bacon, sausage, and cheese wrapped in biscuit dough and cooked, then drizzled with honey butter. Oh my goodness. It's delicious. The syrup for the waffles had Hennessy in it, and that was divine! The chicken was perfectly friend, tender on the inside and crispy on the  outside. Portions are large. Neither of us were able to finish our food. Will definitely be coming back here when we are in town!

Their lunch buffet (~$10) is pretty good especially the butter chicken. the incense got to me at first but I quickly got used to it; it's probably there to cover up the curry smell. Bollywood videos on the TV are fun to watch.

So far I'm not too impressed with this place, the cheesesteak sandwich itself is not as long as we're used to here in philly. The price was $9.27 for a sandwich that's shorter than a wawa hoagie or any other cheesesteak I've had. They also didn't add as much meat as I would've liked to see in a cheesesteak.. Not impressed at all.

Once again they took care of my 650i after it was sideswiped by a school but in NYC.  Made me not worry knowing that Ed was there to make sure that it was taken care of correctly.  Just makes me able to sleep at night knowing my care will get fixed the right way.

Loved this place from the moment we walked into the restaurant and was greeted warmly by the owner. The two sisters that own the restaurant and bakery were both so friendly, as was our very busy waiter. It took awhile for my Da Bomb and my husband's bacon and egg dish to arrive, but it was worth it. My dish was fabulous! The honey crusted homemade biscuit covered the bacon, sausage, veggie mixture. Yummy! We bought an apple fritter to take home for today's breakfast and that was equally good a day later.you can get beautiful cakes and cupcakes for special occasions. I highly recommend Shugga Hi.

I love how unpretentious this place is, and how authentic.  I used to live in Florida and would eat Cuban food often.  I haven't had good Cuban food in a while, and this is the real deal, it was like seeing a friend I haven't seen in years.  I'll definitely be going back.

This place is great if you are looking for authentic Cuban food. The environment was really clean and organized, and the staff was nice too! It definitely exceeded my expectations. Try the Cubano if you are looking for a hardy sandwich. Portions are pretty large. Would definitely recommend.

Service is horrible, but best Cuban sandwich ($7.50) I've ever had (including Cubanos from Miami and Puerto Rico) make it worth the wait.  Large portions on everything and great prices.  Not very many tables either so maybe don't go at peak time.  Great whole in the wall dive, I will definitely be back.

PS. As there are no signs explaining anything in the restaurant, what you need to do is (1) order from the open counter, (2) keep your ticket, sit, and wait for your food, (3) pay at the cashier counter.

This Subway is extremely convenient given its drive thru and interactive screen. However, I would like to note that the ladies that work here always seem pissed and less than thrilled to be serving you. Seriously... It's like they get pissed that they have to make your sandwich. I won't stop going due to its convenience but I feel bad every time I do.

I wanted to like this.  I need to accept the fact that Nashville is not a foodie town.  Good ethnic food here is hard to come by (although not impossible: see e.g. Nolensville Rd).  A lot of people on Yelp would find peace and loose a lot of bad attitude if they accepted this as well.

I appreciated the yerba mate soda.  But the plantains were not cooked right and the meat was really overcooked.  The empanadas were ok.  I have made better empanadas and I am not much of a cook.  Le sigh.

The only Cuban place in town and it's great! I lived in Miami for many years and i think this place is pretty authentic (there's even a domino table in the front).  Even the guava pastelitos tasted fresh.  The only bummer is poor ventilation in the kitchen so you'll smell like a fryer if you sit in the back.

I think this place is great. I've only been for the lunch buffet and am never disappointed. The service is great (we never run out of water, old plates are removed quickly, etc...) and the food is delicious. It never tastes old or dry. The decor is nice and traditional Indian. Basically, I have yet to find a downside to this place :)
My favorite restaurant in Nashville. Do yourself a favor and get the plantains and a Cubano. Great food at a great p

Not being a cuban food authority this place is OK
Using their rice and beans as a measurement I've had much better
More like a lunch counter then a sit down.
Service is quick and prices are reasonable

The staff here are among the nicest that I have encountered in an ER setting and because it is a small, Catholic hospital, it offers daily prayer services.  The hospital itself is extremely clean and well-organized and the triage wait time is usually well under an hour.  The doctors and nurses are kind and patient and really take the time to make sure that the patient understands all of the results and procedures, even when the patient speaks a different language.  Definitely A LOT better than the neighboring Montgomery.

Love this lil shop. The cupcakes are good and they have a great variety of flavors. The best part of this bakery is 1. The pupcakes-- little cupcakes for your dogs 2. Their rewards card-- get 10 punches on your card and get a free cupcake! Simply amazing! Some may complain about the cost, but this a speciality item a reasonable price point for such.

Really solid. I lived in the miami area for years and I have been to some amazing Cuban restaurants, so I cannot give this place 5 stars. That being said, Everything is really good - nothing excels, but I have eaten here many times and I have never been disappointed. They are the only Cuban place in town (as far as I am concerned), and if you have never had cuban food before, I highly recommend it.
This place is awesome! Great cuban sandwiches, milkshakes infused with topical fruit, braised and grilled meat of every variety, and the prices are really reasonable. What's not to like?

I spent most of my life as a Florida native so I have had my share of great Cuban food. Back to Cuba is OK but not great as many have mentioned. The Cuban sandwiches lack enough pork, enough fat on the pork, and the authentic hint of sour orange. The bread could be better as well. The other menu items are OK but again lack soul and authenticity. That being said the food is not bad just not great. This is the only Cuban place I know of in town and it is nice to go and be reminded of home. I think they have some room for improvement but overall it is a good place to get lunch.

I order delivery from this place ALL the TIME. 
Their food is good, and the value that you pay for is fair. They always have a killer lunch special, so you don't have to break the bank trying to get something from there. 
They have a very knowledgeable staff, excellent delivery guys, and your food is always on time if not early. They even text you when they are 3-5 minutes away, which works for me because I work at a school and I need to know when I need to leave the classroom to pick up food. Did I mention that delivery is free during lunch hours. Awesome place

I am writing this as I am stuffing a mouthful of their AMAZING strawberry cake in my face! I know, it's not on my diet, but it was a treat and I almost wished I had never tasted it. Now I know I am going to be craving it and the struggle will be real to try an avoid the temptation. So what can I say about this adorable place? Not enough! But let me try to explain my visit. Staff is super friendly. I got out of my car and and employee (he introduced himself as Michael) opened the door for me as I approached and welcomed me. After a brief discussion he put my food order in and got my desert ready. I had mentioned that the menu should be more descriptive on the breakfast burrito as it does not have egg in it. I explained that I had never had a breakfast burrito without egg. He agreed it should state that on the menu and asked if I wanted to talk to the owner. I declined as I was sure she was probably busy. Later as I was waiting for my food a woman came out and ask if I had been waited on. I said that I had, and I asked if she was the owner. She said "yes" and she introduced herself as Sandra. She was super sweet and we talked briefly. I told her about my experience at the restaurant, how friendly everyone was, how nice it was, etc and told her about suggestion about the breakfast burrito. She actually asked the cook why there was no egg in the breakfast burrito and he stated there has never been. I heard her say she needed to talk to someone about changing that. After a bit of conversation, it was time for me to go (I couldn't wait to eat my delicious smelling breakfast burrito). She thanked me for coming in and for my feedback and then.....she gave me a hug! It was so sweet and I welcomed her hug (this world needs more hugs!). There is great customer service in this new little gem for sure. That compiled with great food.......this place should be a hit. I told her about a monthly gathering that I attend with friends and that I was going to suggest her place for our next meet up. I took some photos which I will upload soon for you to see how inviting the cafe it. Oh, and don't let the name of the business fool you. It is not just a bakery and cafe. They have a nice set up. They can probably seat 35-50 people, they have a stage and live music on Sat and Sun. They have a great menu and all the food coming out of the kitchen looks amazing and is cooked to order. There is also an bar (damn, can't drink at lunch)! The ambiance is so inviting and the lighting is perfect! I love this place and I will be sure to visit on my cheat days. An added bonus is that it's only a mile from work and I can walk in, order, and get back to work within 20 mins! I highly recommend Shugga Hi Bakery and Cafe. I promise, you wont be disappointed!

I took ENTIRELY too long to write this review after eating there... so... I can't flipping remember exactly what we ordered.

First off, Back to Cuba is BYOB, winning them major cool points.

The Food: Cuba is surrounded by water, so I assumed that seafood of any sort would be a win. BINGO! I had a fish dish served with a tropical pinapple sauce that was so good! As an appetizer, I tried their fried yucca with the delectable sauce that comes with. The prices are reasonable enough that you can get an app, and entree, and a dessert without breaking the bank while drinking the Dos Equis you bought at the convenient store next door. Not a bad deal in my book :D

The Service: It's a family run place and absolutely everyone was super friendly aannndddd patient while I took ages to decide what to order. 

I can't wait to go back! Maybe, then, I'll update this review with actual detailed accounts of the awesome food.

AmaZing food. They've never let me down. From the cafe Cubano to the main dishes down to the empanadas- can't go wrong here! 
I highly recommend if this is your first time a must have is start with a cafe Cubano, have an appetizer or just skip straight to the ropa veja with rice, black beans and fried sweet plantains. If it is your first time, educate yourself with a google search or two before going so you know what you want to order. 
Let me address the service "issues". It's not American - there is a small language barrier - they aren't BK and they don't do it your way, get over it and enjoy the food.

Any one that eats here and thinks it's great has no idea what Indian food is suppose to be.  It really leaves me wondering who's in the kitchen and what of nationality. The food has a tremendous amount of oil and not well spiced. This is as Americanized as it gets, but not in a good way. 

I was really hoping this place would be better after its re-opening as driving to North Tampa/USF is a pain in order to get decent Indian food. But this is overall a disappointment. 

There is no competition for Indian food in St Pete, so hopefully someone will keep trying and finally get it right.

Awesome place! The palamilla was like my grandma use to make. The arroz con frijoles negros were awesome. 

The cuban sandwiches are the best this far north of Florida.

Definitely worth the drive.

I have been here multiple times to give this place a shot at turning out an amazing cheese steak, but to my disappointment that has not happened yet.  

Like other Yelpers I felt like the sandwiches weren't as full of meat as you would experience at another steak place in the area.  I really wanted to like them, because I like the name and its tie to the Philly Cheesesteak tradition, but for my taste... I can do Witout Wit or Witout.

Stay Away from this place at all cost. Not only do they struggle to take correct orders but then have the nerve to blame the customer. I've order from here 2x since management has changed and it's been a horrendous experience. My orders have been messed up both times. 
But on top of my order being messed up I found plastic inside of my pizza. 
I found the plastic when taking a bit of pizza. Picture attached. Then manager the had the nerve to tell me over the phone there's always a problem when I order. 
If I could give them zero stars I would.

Absolutely love their food! They have the best tri tip, brisket and oh my gosh their turkey legs!!! They definitely know how to smoke and prepare their meat and you can watch it happen! They are fast and their staff will make you laugh. Always a pleasant experience when i see them at an event!

Kind of surprised that these ratings are so low. They are obviously not on the same level as pats and genos, but price wise it beats Steve prince of steaks which is its closest competitor. You can get your meat chopped or flat, and they have stared to add additional items on their menu. One must try is their Italian pizza! Pretty cool decor inside and always bumping Philadelphia sports on the tv. Pretty chill spot low key low key

What a nice little restaurant. I had to check this place out after one of my friends reviewed this restaurant and I have to say all the hype is true.
I had the chicken and arroz plate. I also ordered a Cubano coffee. Everything was absolutely delicious. I really liked the plantains that came with my plate. They were really sweet. 
Lastly the Cubano was delicious. I'd rather get a cup of coffee here everyday as opposed to overpriced Starbucks coffee. Delicious food! I will be back!
We shared the Cubano sandwich, chicken empanadas, yuca frita, lechon asado, and a pastelito de coco. EVERYTHING was amazing. Seriously, you can't go wrong here.

I eat at the India Grill almost once a week and I always leave happy and satisfied!

I love their Chicken Tikka Masala! I haven't tried their buffet, but I've eaten there several times for dinner and never been disappointed. The garlic naan is delicious and all the portions are quite generous, I always have to get a box for my leftovers. Also good is the Butter Chicken and the Chicken Korma, I can recommend from personal experience.

The staff is pleasant and attentive, the only detractor is the decor, but they seem to have been working on that a bit. Some might not like it, but they have a giant tv on the wall that shows Indian music videos, I think it adds a fun flair to the meal!

My husband wanted to go here for his birthday lunch. It's a tiny place that seemed to stay busy the entire time we were there. I see why, it was delicious!! We are already talking about returning. YUM!

Been looking for years for a place to get my Caribbean food fix and I found it close to home. The pan con ajo was sift and tasty. The grilled chicken was very good and the rucw, black beans and maduros were heavenly. Generous meal portions and the place is very cozy. Will come back for more.

I am giving 1 star only because I cannot give zero. The most pathetic food I have ever paid for in my life, and I paid for it because I don't like to complain if food is free, and I just cannot let go of it. Papri Chat was bland, Samosa Chat was a pile of tomatoes, Mutter Paneer was uncooked, poori was oily, veg pakoras was salty and the worst was what the gave out as chicken biriyani....oily rice and uncooked chicken.....I can cook better food with my eyes closed and using only my left leg.....Advice to the owner, please eat the food you served today, and then review my review.

This place is awesome! Its got all the essentials and all the stuff you definitely never knew you needed or things that you definitely don't need but might buy out of nostalgia! They have everything from housewares to weapons or old school electronics. Prices are as reasonable as you'd expect and this place will definitely give you plenty of free entertainment!

Yummy Sammiches.  I still don't understand why they are constantly 'out' of the Cuban Sandwich.  

But, dang if it isn't convenient for take-out when you want something yummy that isn't pizza, mexican or chinese.

I have been living in the Northeast for years now....and I occasionally order from different pizza spots. Ever since I ordered from England Pizza...I didn't want to try any other place! My family and I agree that this is the best pizza spot in the Northeast.

 Their pizza are delicious and they are very generous with the toppings unlike most places. Sandwiches such as cheesesteaks, paninis, clubs, are above average. Other things like buffalo wings, jalapeño poppers, pierogies, salads are really good too. My favorite here are their chicken cheesesteaks. Actual chopped chicken breast...no frozen chicken steak here! Fries are OK...could be better.

Delivery guys are always friendly and on time..sometimes early which is even better!

One of the best breakfast I have had in awhile. Had the Tater Tot Waffles. It was amazing. Owner was cool as well as she saw the service was a tad slow she offered free desert while we were waiting. But let me tell you it was worth the wait. We will be going back for sure.
Not Bad steaks. Wouldn't say there the best around. Always get the wiz steak with fried onions and fries. The prices are not bad. Nice and clean on the inside to eat.

Pizzeria food is good, but the best is their Spanish menu! I had the tilapia platter with white rice. The rice is perfectly cooked and the tilapia is flavorful. The platter also includes a salad that is also great. It's got lettuce, tomato, cucumber, onion, avocado and cheese. So good!  And if that wasn't enough, there's a few fried plantains for good measure. Crispy and delicious.

I've had a better cheesesteak at a pizza shop. The cheesesteak is DRIPPING I mean DRIPPING with cheese and grease afterwards I felt like I have eaten a rock!! They also had a sign for a $7 dollar combo on each table and we were each charged $9 and we went back up with the sign and our receipts we were told "oh thats old ads, were sorry" Well throw them away don't leave them on the table then charge a different price! I don't think I will return to this location.
The service was awful, they said it would take 45 minutes but it ended up taking over an hour. My pizza and buffalo wings were both cold. Will never order from here again.

I went there Friday it was slow yet my shrimp was cold in the shrimp tacos I ordered. The shrimp wasn't seasoned yet it was "Grilled Shrimp Tacos"!!!!! No heat at all. The fries were ok.they gave me a can soda and I had to ask for ice! Hats nuts. This was my first time there and I won't go back.

Now, I'm not an expert on Cuban food, but it makes my taste buds happy.

This place can be hard to miss. It's located in a strip mall behind a gas station. There is limited seating. It maybe has 10 chairs? It is located right by the I-65.

There is also a table reserved for playing games. Dominoes, I believe, and they have dominoes at the table

For appetizer they serve bread. And let me tell you, it is so yummy. Always reminds me of that Pablo Neruda poem "Oda al pan (Ode to the Bread)" Yes, yes, I know he isn't cubano.

I've had the Cuban sandwich (pretty good), tilapia with mango sauce (excellent), lechon asado (pretty good). The sides that I usually get are black beans, yucca, and plantains. 

For me, the lechon asado needs more flavor so I have to add hot sauce. It's different than the Filipino version I'm used to eating.

Other things that are on their menu are smoothies and desserts. The mango smoothie is yummy. :] I've never tried their desserts. I know they have tres leches cake and flan. And maybe something else. It's a bit pricey. The tilapia tropical (mango chutney sauce on top) is about $13 --  one of the more expensive meals. The lechon asado is about $10? Something like that. When I go in, which is not too often, I look to pay about $12-15, which includes a tip.

It's yummy and it's filling.

Really good, authentic cuban food. The staff is very kind, and they remember you and what you like to eat everytime you walk in. I wish there were more spice in the black beans and rice but I let that slide because I realize not everyone eats food as spicy as I do. Friday and saturday nights there is usually some sort of cuban music around in the restaurant.

I've had the roasted pork with yuca and had the chicken with plantains on the second visit (both come with white rice and black beans). Both times the food was perfect. 

Plaintains have a mix of chewy and crispy texture that I think is distinct to Cuban cooking (as opposed to Jamaican plantains which are great also).

Atmosphere is welcoming and service is great. Thanks to the all of the staff!

This place deserves 6 stars and more. Drove from Chicago for my birthday and ended up in the neighborhood. The service is amazing and the entire staff made us feel at home. Juices are exceptional and the flavors are amazing and authentic. A must visit for anyone coming by or living in Nashville

I have had this place bookmarked for some time, so I was super stoked to finally get to try it!

It's a bit of a hole in the wall near Hundred Oaks. After my Cuban food experience at Havana Rumba experience in Louisville, KY (a previous review), I had high hopes. Though not as fancy, the food was tasty! 

To start off-- the coffee was fantastic! I also ordered the pollo platter with beans, rice, and plantains, and everything was cooked to perfection! The server forgot my plantains initially so when I told her, she brought me an entire plate full. I.heart.plantains so obviously that was a major score!

The platters are about $11 and up, which seemed reasonable. At the same time, when you throw in a coffee and a tip, it got a little spendy. I knock a star off only because a $20 lunch wasn't what I expected. However, it isn't enough to deter me from coming 'Back to Cuba'!
The food was super yummy, the service was great. When you order wine they FILL the glass!

Finally, after driving by everyday for about 2 years on-and-off from/to work, decided to try Back To Cuba. My first Cuban culinary experience was earlier this year in Miami, so I was hooked. Going in, I already knew not to compare to Miami, I kept an open-mind and this review is solely based on Back to Cuba. The place is small, 8 small tables, plus some bistro seating outdoors. Its in a small shopping strip attached to a gas station. Getting parking and going in-and-out can be challenging. We went in around 11:30, luckily not too busy. The menu is displayed on their wall, and can be a little confusing/overwhelming. We just asked what they recommended and we went with that. I had the pork roast plate and my husband has the cuban sandwich with fries. We also tried their chicken empanada. The roast pork could have used a bit more flavor, and maybe some spice/acidic. I really wished I could've substitute the yuca for plantains. The rice and beans were just average. The cubano was extra crispy. And the pork was chewy and dry, I couldn't even eat it. Also lacked some spice/acidic. Fries were good, and the empanada was as well. I definitely want to give it another try, perhaps try something different. Service was good, food came out fast.

Before celebrating a wedding in Nashville 23 June 18 ( white ave studios) are entire family ( 19 folks )had breakfast at this restaurant. We were seated promptly and are drink orders were taken right away. We had one server for 19 people so some delays and mistakes were expected and to tell you the truth I really didn't care because the food and service were excellent. I love  and appreciate this black owned establishment and the owner and employees went out of their way to accommodate are large party, including separating several checks which could be a headache. I had the chicken and waffles , which were pretty dam good. I also drink a red sangria ( delicious). This is a good spot in Nashville so don't pass it up. Ironically our server was our wedding photographer too , god is good always.

I've been seeing Dr Joyce for years. There's never a wait for my appointment, it's reasonably easy to get an appointment, and my relationship with Dr. Joyce is one of my most pleasant professional relationships! The equipment and facilities are state of the art, and the opticians, staff, and physicians are all great people.

The standard Indian menu plus some interesting and tasty recommendations freshly prepared and served with a touch of audacity by the gregarious proprietor. Try saying THAT three times fast! You won't be able to, you'll be too busy eating the Chicken Do Piaza. Go!

Roast pork was amazing!

Rice& beans and yucca were also very good.

Just a few tables in a strip mall, no atmosphere but the food is good!

I have been going to these guys since 2001 with my 540i and now my 650i.  Anytime I have a problem with an accident... All have been the other driver's fault... I go to see Ed and Anthony.  They always give me the car back better than it was before the accident.  I would highly recommend them.  They focus on BMWs and other European and German automobiles.

I stopped in on a whim and I am glad I did. The cupcake was so fresh and moist.  Good to share if you want to have less sugar. Really friendly ladies working.  I will know where to go for a great cupcake in the future.

Back to Cuba was one of my first meals in town when I moved to Nashville.  Upon arriving, I almost turned around before even leaving the car--thank goodness I didn't!  From the outside, it looks like a dingy hole in the wall found in a run-down strip mall.  But once I entered, I was impressed by the small but complete menu of meats, chicken, fish, and all the traditional cuban side dishes.  I ordered the fish special, which was an enormous piece of tilapia, simply prepared on the grill, with sides of rice, beans, and salad.  Plantains were also on the menu as an accompaniment, but weren't present--this was the only sad part of my meal.  Next time, I would also ask for the salad dressing to be on the side--the oil and vinegar-based dressing was heavily poured and left a pool around the entire plate.  I learned that this is often typical in Cuban food restaurants, and given that we're in Nashville, the land of butter, oil, and lard, they tend to be even more heavy-handed.  Regardless of all of this, the fish was delicious, and the rice and beans were enjoyable as well.  My favorite part of the meal was, hands down, the bread--it was buttery, crispy, and chewy all at the same time.  I'm salivating just thinking about it and can't wait to go Back to Cuba!

Don't let the sketchy strip this little gem is in scare you away.  Sandwiches and entrees have all been great and fresh each time Ive stopped in.  They can get pretty packed  during lunch, but a group of 10 from my office was able to get in and out in an hour.

I went with a coworker during lunch to India Grill.  I make sure to sample indian restaurants whenever I get the chance.  I was not impressed by their lunch buffet.  The food was mediocre at best.  I would not go back.
Good food! I grew up in Tampa and definitely miss the access to good Cuban food, especially a hot pressed Cuban sandwich.
So glad that Fairview finally got a cupcake place!!! Love this place and the awesome employees!!!

Absolutely love this place.  Don't go expecting a quick bite. The place is small and everything is cooked when ordered. I have never had anything not exceptional. The shrimp dish in a spicy sauce, the chicken fricassee and of course the Cuban sammich are all amazing and unique to this place. You won't find these flavors anywhere else in Nashville.  Ask if they have any 'pastelas', a homemade Cuban pastry. They are to die for!
Definition of a five star yelp.  Total gem.  Had the churrasco, and the roast pork sandwich.  Absolutely phenomenal.

After I ran the Rocky steps I came came here for my first cheese steak and I admit the cheese steak was good when I come back to Philly I would love to try Pat's or Geno's cheese steak I will definitely come back to here for more more cheese steak

Meh. I've been here twice, but I doubt I'll be making a third stop. The steak isn't BAD, it's just not that impressive, and this place is wild expensive. A side of fries is literally almost $6. Your sandwich is like $8. So if you throw in a drink, you're looking at a $20 lunch for a sandwich you can make better at home and some fries that I hope they sprinkle with gold leaf to justify that price. The sandwich is a good size, but that's pretty much the only positive. The sandwich I just had was VERY chewy and tough. You also have to ask for condiment cups if you want pickles and the like. Where the hell can you find an actual good Philly cheesesteak in this damn city?!

This place is a joke. The signage is explosive and so too will be your digestive system if you eat here.

Save your time and get a real steak at Steve's at Comly and the Boulevard. They've been local forever, they speak English and they don't use frozen meat.

The Cubano sandwich was very good. Perhaps a bit more $$ than you might expect for the amount of food, location, and atmosphere, but very close to fair. I can see more visits in my future!

Staff is genuinely friendly, seating is limited. Very small place with no sound dampening so it can get quite noisey during peak hours.

Best churasco y chimichurri I've ever had! Even after living in Miami for 4 years and frequenting Versailles! Good service. Very chill. Worth the drive out. They definitely have gringo-fied their menu with tacos etc, but I would expect no less in Nashville. Missed the ropa vieja y Elena ruz, pero they had the essentials! They do have quite a large selection of sandwiches. Everything was delicious. Rice was perfect. Black beans 9/10. Cuban bread 11/10- flaky and fresh. 

Unfortunately they did not have desserts when I was there, but they do have flan and tres leches on the menu at least. 

It was definitely enough to make me home sick for more!! Will absolutely be back soon!

The Back to Cuba Café is nothing fancy as a dining establishment but it's a great place to get Cuban take-out. Located in a non descript strip mall, I was more than excited the first time I visited. I'm not Cuban so I don't know how authentic it is, but I can tell you that as far as Cuban restaurants in the states go, it's a pretty great. If you have never tried Cuban food I suggest you go for the Lechón (pulled pork slowly cooked in delicious spices), and some good old black beans and rice. My #1 Latin Food obsession are fried plantains and in my many trips to the Back to Cuba Café I have had varied experienced - sometimes they are delicious, sometimes they are just ok. The previously mentioned Lechón, however, has always been absolutely fantastic. If food in Cuba is this good or better, it makes me want to steal a Coast Guard boat and break the embargo.

Hidden gem you wouldn't notice so thankful for yelp reviews that encouraged us to explore.  Staff treats you like family, exceptionally friendly.  They have savory food options.  I had chicken and waffles.  The chicken was seasoned to perfection.  My friend had dabomb breakfast Biscuit (pictured).  She said it was the best breakfast she has ever had. Perfect mixture of sweet and savory. The artsy feel of the room and the unique full bar give the cafe a unique feel.  Sad I do not live in the area as this would be a frequent breakfast stop.

I wish I can give them a zero star because they are not even worth a one star. Their steak is is no better than the ones you get at any pizzeria. They are fake imitations of Pats, Geno's, Jim's and Steve's. If I had a list of top 100 cheesesteak list it wouldn't even make #100.
