I've been twice, and it was pretty good both times. I like the plantains. I found a hair in my food last time, so that was a downer.

If you haven't been before, just know that you order at the counter, then sit down and they bring you your food. You pay at the front counter at the end.

They are the BEST of the VERY BEST! They have the newest state of the art equipment, technology and care! I highly recommend them. I have been under Dr Schwartz's care for 20 years. Glenn in the glass department fixed my glasses for me for no charge. The glasses were bought online from a company which told me that they could do nothing to help me! I love going there and feel so welcomed and comfortable in a perfect and lovely office setting with outstanding staff! No stress ever, just the ultimate in competence, skill and efficiency!

Best Cuban food in TN and probably the only Cuban food here lol-
Great prices and good food- but if u are looking for Cuban food like La Terisita in Tampa Florida it can't compete. 
Def try this place if you are craving Cuban:)

Cuban sandwich with a guava milk shake.  Awesome.  Cuban sandwich had the perfect amount of meat, the bread was perfectly crunchy.  The Bread really made the sandwich.  They make the fried plantains, I'm used to finding really good cheap cuban food from my previous trip to Miami.

This place has really good, moderately priced cuban food.

I don't often go travelling but when I do, I typically expect my friends to take me to wonderful and delicious places. My friend had been dying to try this spot and so we went for an early lunch, and I became a believer. The food here was actually pretty spot on, I had the fish and I really liked the flavor that was generated in the dish. The coffee was also off the hook, and it had me feeling good all day. At 11am on a Saturday it was actually perfect timing because it was empty when we got there so we could have an actual conversation and chill. 
This spot is very cute and wonderful, if I am ever back in town I look forward to coming back to eat here.

Today was my first time visiting Shugga Hi and I will definitely be back! 
Friendly staff , nice, relaxed ambiance. I had the chicken and waffles with Henny syrup and cheese grits! All I can say is AmazBallllssss!!! I also had the peach sangria, it was very refreshing and delicious ! 
My grandmother had the whiting fish and it was fried to perfection and plenty to share! 
Ms.Cathy came around and introduced herself as well as the head chef and music artist for the day! Definitely a place to try! 
Thanks Ms.Cathy, for your hospitality!

One of our favorite restaurants. Everything is cooked fresh. Pakoras are the best of any Indian restaurant I've tried. Lightly battered and fried. They have a nice delicate crunch. Service is great and staff is friendly. It's no wonder why they're packed every time we visit.
Nice clean place with friendly service.  The cheesesteaks are nothing spectacular but they are decent.  Could have had more meat to fill out the roll.

can't believe i didn't know about this place sooner and I used to live about 10 blocks away !!! 

I probably had more cheesesteaks in my lifetime than burger!!! Geno's, Pat's, Tony Luke's, Philip's, etc... Wit or Witout is definitely my #1 on the list for cheesesteaks.  

First thing is cleanness, they are definitely the cleanest cheesesteak joint i've ever been too; from the floor to the table to the condiments station. 

Second thing is the grease. Yes, people say it isn't authentic philly cheesesteak if you can't see through the paper bag or whatever. BUT i can live with a little grease and save my heart some work :) With that said, their cheesesteaks are nowhere close to being DRY. 

Third thing is the roll.  When i get my cheesesteak the roll isn't a piece of dough even when i order wiz. 

Last thing, the price.  If you're ordering just the cheesesteak then it's $7.29. They also have a combo for $10; cheesesteak, fries, and a soda.  Let see you get that much for $10 at Geno's or Pat's.  

They also have online order and they cater!!! 

my personal fav: Flat wiz witout

Might not look hopping from the outside but they do the best Indian I've had in the area.  Menu is extensive includes plenty of lamb options and their lamb is tender (not something you can always count on at other places).  Chicken dishes come out juicy too.  The sauces taste fresh and homemade, not too heavy or oily.  We've done the standard dishes, madras, chicken tikka masala, etc. if you need your curry fix you can get it here.
Local favorite of Nashvillians. Get there early or you'll be in the line out the door.

Finally got around to trying this because we were in the mood for pork beans and rice.  It was adequate and satisfied the craving.   Delicious starchy rice, yucca and pulled pork, salty but tasty - washed down with Tangerine Juice.  I think there were 6 tables and 1 reserved for games.  One portion was more than adequate to split with my husband.
Friendly service, reasonably priced.  Is it good?  I don't know.  My Colombian neighbor says it fills a gap.

Really great. Being Cuban Ive been spoiled by having some really good cuban sandwhiches in my life, so I can get a little snoody about them, and from the outside of this place and it being in Nashville, I was a little concerned. But once I walked in I knew the place was authentic. From the domino table to the staff to the menu, I could tell that it wasnt just a gimic. With that said I was hoping the food wouldnt disappoint, and it didnt. Woderful, wonderful, wonderful. Cuban sandwhich was a true cuban and all the food I saw looked great. It might be the only cuban place between chicago and miami, but totally worth stopping in if you get a chance.
Wow a great hole in the wall!  It would be very easy to miss this hidden gem.  The food is great.  A bit pricey but worth it.
Omg!!! my first time  here, and it is amazing.  I had the Vaca frita  ( grilled flap meat tossed with mojito  sauce , rice, beams and plantains ) I defiantly will be back

Moved here from Florida, this is the only place I know (that is still open) that has Cubans. 

Food:
Pros: Cubans are pretty tasty. Coffee is pretty good. (Neither are the best I've had, but beggars can't be choosers). I've sampled the rest of the menu, nothing blew me away, but nothing was inedible either.

Cons: They are not kidding about no substitutions, including when they are out of ingredients. Out of ham? Then you cannot order anything resembling a Cuban. I asked for alternatives, and they didn't even give me an idea. (I tried to order a pork sandwich and add pickles, order a turkey sandwich with onions...etc....absolutely no luck). I have no problem with the no substitutions, but when they are out of ingredients they should have some sort of idea for alternatives, especially since the essential sandwich is similar to others. 

Service:

Pros:.....?

Cons: Order ahead. It's small, cramped, and impossible to navigate during lunch. They have often been closed without warning, or cash only without notice. They are almost impossible to talk to on the phone (it isn't a language barrier at least in my case). I respect busy, but they are almost haughty in their rush. It isn't like they spit in my face or anything, but I always feel like I'm inconveniencing them by giving them my business. 

Overall:

Dying for a Cuban and coffee? Suck up the cons and you'll have a pretty good version of it for Tennessee.
Our server was Robin E. (absolutely precious) We had a wonderful breakfast ~ waffles with eggs and fruit were awesome!!! Loved the syrup with Hennessy!
Great cupcake variety & Military Monday is 20% off!! So good!! Highly recommend this place.

As a young Navy brat, I spent 3 years of my life in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, and quickly grew to love everything about Cuban food.  Back to Cuba is the real deal, folks.  

They are known for their pork, and I suggest you give it a try!  The Cubano sandwich is just delicious--melty and fabulous.  Today I had the arroz con pollo, which is equally tasty.  Shredded chicken, yellow rice, peppers and onions, and topped with sweet plantains.  Absolutely hit the spot!  You can also get plantain chips, which are crunchy and wonderful.  

They also have a variety of sweet "shakes", and authentic Cuban soft drinks.  Prices are moderate--my meal today ran me about $10, and that included a drink.  You'll pay around $7 for sandwiches, $12 and up for entrees.  The place isn't big and can get crowded right around lunchtime, but you can definitely get it to go!  

If you have never had Cuban food, give this a try--I guarantee you'll love it!  Best I've had in years by a long shot!

This is based on a lunch visit. Very austere surroundings. Service is ok but a bit dour - the owner could smile for a change. The selection of the buffet is rather limited and unfortunately the food is at best lukewarm. My wife liked the Tandoori chicken and the Mint chutney sauce but all of the other dishes are rather bland and the Naan is nothing to write home about. Our impression is that this is nothing special and the buffet is too expensive for the selection provided.  It is a pity that the Tampa Bay area does not have any good Indian Restaurants - there must be a demand.

Love this place! Everything's good. Pulled pork with black beans, rice, and plantain was yummy, tilapia with garlic butter? Was delicious. Good colada, too! It may look sketchy from outside, but don't let that discourage you. You won't be disappointed. Highly recommend!

Not sure what the point of having a drive-through is if you're only going to have one person working. Every time I come to the subway I have to wait a pretty decent amount of time before they complete my order because there's always someone who walks in that they have to wait on. I finally just drove off because the car in front of me and still hadn't received their order.

I was hoping to have a Tampa style Cuban when I found this little dive while visiting Nashville. While a little dissapointed when the sandwhich and the rice and beans were not exactly what I had expected, that dissapointment quickly dissipated after the first couple of bites. The sandwich was a great and I would definitely come back when in town. 

I had never had Cuban coffee, so I decided to order a cup. The waitress was kind enough to make sure I knew what I was getting. I knew it was a tiny a cup of coffee, but what I didn't know was just how much coffee heaven could fit into a little cup! I wish I could get this closer to home!

All in all, it was a great visit!

Being fortunate to have an amazing culture doesn't necessarily grant you culinary power. In this case, the cooks should go back to Cuba. I ordered the "Minuto". I should have thought a little longer than the name implies.  It's basically a chicken- fried piece of smelly fish. I was more enthralled by the flavor of the chunky green salsa verde which I used as a dipping sauce to cover the taste.  

The ambiance is loud and echoey.  The bathroom smells like rotten zapatos. 

It's only saving grace was the coffee. It's served in little espresso cups - very traditional and effective. While the coffee seemed to settle on my palate, I remembered Havana. I heard Buena Vista Social Club in my mind.  But when I came to- I realized there was no music playing in this "Cuban" Dive.   While on every street corner in Cuba is over flowing with music, this little cuban eatery lacked the very nature of it's name!!!!!! 

Ambiance - no stars
Food- two stars. 
The coffee was redeemable.

We went in when it was not busy, and got zero assistance from the two people on staff. We wanted to buy designer sunglasses, but they just pointed at the wall of frames and said "There" ... and that was it. After we made it clear we did not see what we were looking for, they did not say a word and just let us leave. They just looked at their computer screens.

I order from here on a weekly basis. I go at all hrs of the day and its always clean in there. Went there during lunch and I didn't even wait that long. I loved the sliced steak. Lets me know they use good beef. Alot of places chop it up to hide their crap steak

Paid $12 dollars for piece of crap.  
Dry steak. Unprofessional service. 
Disgusting. Never again.

I think that Jo F. pretty much nailed it in this review. 

The food is good, it's filling and it's just a little bit pricey by Nashville standards.

But I'll definitely go Back to Cuba, if for no other reason than to be able to order fresh guanabana juice.

Come on, admit it, "guanabana" is awfully fun to say. And the fresh squeezed (I presume) juice itself rocked my Norteamericano world. 

I garden and the one thing that burns my biscuits about gardening in Middle TN is that I can't raise tropical fruit like the guanabana. 

Incidentally, the English name for guanabana is 'Soursop'.

If you were trying to make a case for the aural superiority of Spanich over English, you'd be half way home if you introduced the guanabana-soursop comparison. 

Guanabana - sounds like a lovely cross between a guava and a banana, preferably something that I would eat in a hammock during a siesta with a senorita playing classical guitar nearby

Soursop - sounds like a guy who is really ticked off that he has to mop the floor

FYI, while my lechon asada lunch was in the ~$15 range that Jo F. mentioned, it is certainly possible to get out of here for less if you stick with a sandwich or one of the meat-filled savory pastry options.

FYI #2, this is a crowded little place. Coming with more than one friend at lunchtime seems risky, presuming you all want to sit together.
Awesome place with awesome people. Chicken and Waffles like they should be done. Loved the coffee too. Going back tomorrow for doughnuts.
Great Food!  Better tasting than places I've been to in Miami. The flavors are authentic.

Being from Miami, one of the first things I do when I move to a new city is look for Cuban spots. In true Miami fashion, I will also write this review like any Miami bro would. 

I'm an addict and when I need my fix please be sure to get the fuck out of my way. With that out of the way, this place is badass bro! I came for lunch on a weekday. Owner is sooo Miami. Got me the ropa vieja, tostones, arroz y frijoles, basically the whole damn menu. Can you say authentic AF? Cuz I sure can. Like for real though, that shit was fireeeeee. Irregardless, I dropped some Spanglish on the owner to build some street cred. It worked. After I finished ravaging my food the owner brought out some empanadas to go. Respect bro, respect. 

Oh and to those complaining about the service...welcome to your first Miami experience. Stop being soft and toughen up, you'll get the same service in Miami. You're right about the prices being expensive though but whatever its bomb Cuban in Nashville. I'll gladly hand over the plata.

Great food!  We had a group of six and ordered six different dishes that we shared.  The Cuban sandwich was a "hit", the skirt steak with chimichurri was very tasty as well as the spicy shrimp.  Four in our group had not tasted plantains and they loved them.  The music is to loud for the restaurant space and has very little seating.

Cuban food, done right.  I feel like I'm in a different world when I go here. The papaya juice is out of this world!  Fried plantains and black beans are heaven.  One of my favorite places to eat in Nashville.

They only take credit cards for orders over $10.

Love the flavor, it's real authentic Cuban food. Don't let the surroundings fool you. It's the perfect Cuban cafe. Food is good, fast and the service is awesome. 

 Will be back when I'm looking for my Cuban fix.

Disappointing. A Pauper, not a Prince.

I consider myself a "steak sandwich snob". I've eaten at every steak shop you can think of in the City of Philadelphia. I'm a LOYAL subject of the Prince, Steve's Steaks. With this in mind, I went to Wit on the grand recommendation of a really good friend who thought it was comparable to the Prince of Steaks.

I live about a mile from this location. I've eaten here twice. The lunch special is what got me in the door. I doubt I'll go back again.

It seems they're trying to rip off Steve's big time. The set up, the tiling and decor, all reminiscent of Steve's. Not very original. 

The meat is a la Steve's (Geno's), not chopped up low grade Steak'ums style "meat" like at most places (i.e., Pat's). Though, I do believe Steve's uses steer for their meat. The roll was decent. I think they even use the same bakery as Steve's.

I always order pizza steaks "prov, without" (I'm not from South Philly... I pronounce the "th"!). A Steve's "pizza, prov, without" melts in your mouth. Very little chewed necessary. Wit's, well, their meat is chewy -- but not tough. Their pizza sauce tasted old and stale. The actual sandwich wasn't very hot, either.

In a pinch, let's say you're starving, you're on Red Lion and don't want to eat at Wendy's next door and only have $8 on you at lunchtime, sure go here. But, if you want a delicious melt-in-your-mouth steak and have the extra cash for it then drive the mile and a half up the Blvd to Steve's!

I don't get what people love about this place. A friend brought me  cobbler from here -- well, that's what they
called it. Unlike any I've ever had and not in a good way. I'm from the south, so I know my cobblers
and this wasn't  even close to what it should be. Recommendation -- keep trying . 2 stars for effort.

I love this little place. Bought Cubanos today, plus yucca and plantains. I've had several dishes there that have all been good. You can eat in or take out, the menu is always written on a chalkboard and has some variability to it.

Ugh. Liked it on my first visit. Second visit a friend and I placed an order and then sat down. We waited a solid 40 minutes and asked about the food. It never came, so we walked out the door having wasted a lunch break. 

It gets worse from here.. The Owner ran out into the parking lot accusing us of not paying for our food. We explained the situation and she only said that the server must have done a bad job. No offer to get us food, no apology for the accusations. 

I'd like to have a good Cuban food option, but can't bring myself to go back and voluntarily give them my money after the experience with the owner.

I had body work done by them twice in the past 4 years (this was through my dealer though), each time they did a great job. So now with my warranty expired, and the dealer charging an arm and a leg every time for repairs and services, I decided to take my BMW to them for service and repair. Anthony did a great job at a great price. I made an 8 o'clock appointment and told them I would wait as I lived 20 miles away, they had the space in the shop ready for my car after I got there and started working on it immediately. I initially only requested for an oil change but after getting there realized that I was due for a full service he accommodated the request last minute, and including the time ordering and waiting for parts, I was in and out in 2 and half hours. He explained everything to me, and quoted a price before doing any work. I was very happy with their service. There is a glass window in the office where you can see the shop and them working on your car. So for those guys who like to make sure their cars are taken care can see it while it is being worked on, it is pretty cool. I am not a guy so I don't really care. But I was really impressed with how neat and clean the shop was, it looked neater than the shops at my 2 previous BMW dealers! I am planning to drive out 20 miles to have them service my car in the future. Fortunately I only need it once a year so I won't have to drive too much.

1. Bread is really good
2. Meat is chopped steak not sliced steak as depicted in pictures
3. Meat is very little and has no taste with a grayish color
4. Good seating area
5. Bathrooms are okay
6. Staff is ok. The kid on the grill appears to be unenthusiastic

I had lunch here one Saturday afternoon in August, and as I recall, there was no a/c, the place was hot, and I used my napkin to wipe the sweat off my face and arms.

I met a friend for lunch, and he knew the menu really well, I did not.  It's hard to order from a place like this because they don't allow substitutions and so many of us have food restrictions because of the GMO foods their selling us.

I ordered something that I could easily eat out of the shells, making sure not to Gluten myself.

The menu is varied, the prices are adequate, shame they don't think about their customers needs.
No, this is not a place I would return to.  I value my health, too damn much.

Y'all should know by now that I LOVE a good Cubano.

Back to Cuba served me a good Cubano!
Perhaps it deserves 5 stars, but I'm sort of a stickler on some things & the caption with 5 reads (Woohoo! As good as it gets!) & it would take a phenomenal effort to overcome the memory of what I have enjoyed in the Keys.

So, if you're in Nashville & don't plan on going to the Keys any time soon, you should safely assume this is an excellent place for a Cubano!

The bread was just right, double pressed & perfectly crispy. The pickles in it had character, all of the fillings were in good proportion & great tasting.
The only negative I'll offer on this sandwich is that it was a bit salty.
I watched them prepare it & am pretty sure that arose from the liberal amounts of butter that was brushed on to ensure the crispy bite to the bread. 
So the saltiness could likely be alleviated if the switched to an unsalted butter, or perhaps it's my wife's fault for making me cut back on salt so much that I find it so pronounced here :)

I am a fan of Back to Cuba.
I'm very thankful they're here (since I'm not in the Keys).
And I will most definitely be back.
Solid cheeseteak.  Good roll.  Finely chopped steak with melted cheese throughout.  It could use a little more meat in my opinion, but that wouldn't stop me from going back.

I've been here twice. Both times have been pretty bad experiences. First off, don't even attempt the Mango Lassi. They are sitting at room temperature all day and were poured from a pitcher into a glass. It tasted like pure corn syrup. The lunch buffet consist of over salted, bland Indian food. Service was non existent. Good Indian food has layers of spice that makes it unique from every other type of food. Here they use tons of salt and cream and it just doesn't come across well in their food.

This place is amazing! My eye was killing me from contacts and I looked around for a an eye specialist and they were able to look at my eye ASAP which was awesome.  Everyone there is extremely nice, friendly, and very pretty (kept me coming back)! Good work Dr. Schwartz! But I will continue to go there because of their service and expertise. Definitely go there!! They rock!

I just changed jobs from S.Philly and I have really been missing the food. One of my new co-workers ordered me a Cheese steak from here yesterday and I was blown away! Delicious food right around the corner! I found my new lunch time spot!

3 stars because it wasn't terrible but it also wasn't the best. 

Service was OK. People weren't super friendly but they also weren't bad. 

For the price, it wasn't worth it and I probably won't be back. We stopped because it was en route to where we were going. I think you could get far better food for the prices. 

We had the charraos - something like that - and the bistec palmilla. One was super bland and the other was super salty. Their beans and rice ARE good though. So are the plantains.
The food here is very delicious, the staff is very nice. The employees are very respectful to their customers.

I enjoy Cuban food and had not found a good source in Nashville, until now. Family run with recipes that must have come from grandma. I have enjoyed the pork, fish and beef. Yes, I sample everybody's plate.

The owner found out how much I have had eaten Cuban food and made sure I tried even more. I can safely recommend the entire menu. Do a dessert as well just to taste the local flavors.

It's been a while since I came here, but yum. I had the Cuban and it was delicious. I want to come back to try and actual plated meal. When I was in I was in a hurry; so sandwich seemed the quickest way out. 
Parking is a little tight and honestly so is the seating inside. 
Lots of great options to choose from. Great music and ambiance. I love Latin food; obviously and this is a hidden gem. Not really hidden, but I figure a lot of people overlook it. It's gets packed quick.

Still the best Cuban and media noche (Cuban on sweet bread which I prefer) in town but the meat was still cold in middle and cheese was cold.  Wish they would have been a little warmer.  The plantains have been better.  Still good flavor but didn't seem freshly cooked today.  Kinda tough and chewy.  Usually they are the best of anywhere I have ever had them.   Hopefully today was a fluke because this is usually one of nashvilles best kept secrets!

Excellent small very casual restaurant in a gas station strip center. At 3pm on a sat, most of the few tables were full, several families having roasted meat plates and tacos w sides. 
We got counter service and enjoyed the Cubano sandwich, tasty and grill pressed with super thin sliced meats and tangy pickles and mustard. 
And the Miami with its shattering crispy toasted bread and turkey. 
The roast pork platter was salted w crispy crust bits and excellent black beans and soft yucca all w sauteed onions. 
Not dirt cheap but excellent value, hope to come again.
Great cupcakes. Went here right after work cause I wanted something sweet and I was not disappointed. 5/5 and the red velvet is my favorite
Phenomenal food, very good service love this place. The Cubano sandwich is AWESOME. Also the Empanadas made fresh. There's not one bad dish here.

I'm from Miami and moving up here left a hole in my stomach for good Cuban food. This place, however, has filled it. Great place to get some good Cuban food and a cafecito for that pick me up. 

Recommend the Cuban Sandwhich or the ropa vieja if you are hungrier.

A very welcome addition to the metro east, because who wants to always drive to stl when they want to get a cupcake. I've been a regular customer every since they opened and I've always been very pleased. First of all- awesome, polite staff. Always warm and welcoming. The cupcakes are really good, some flavors better than others depending on your personal taste of course. They have a good monthly rotation of special flavors and great regular flavors. My favorite regular flavor is the wedding cake and the birthday cake. My favorite special flavor so far is the infamous pumpkin and strawberry banana. Yum.

Professional Painting and Auxiliary Work Done. On very short notice, Andy came out to our home to give us an estimate on the painting work for our home. The previous home owner had left some well-hidden damage that Andy pointed out. He also pointed out mistakes made by the previous owner's handyman that we had not asked him to evaluate. Throughout the work done by Andy and his assistant, they maintained great communication with us and were thorough in its execution. In addition to the damage to the wall, Andy also replaced trim at the bottom of the wall for an additional fee, and that work was also well done. I highly recommend Andy Funez for any painting and general wall work you may need done.

The food was incredible, the atmosphere of the restaurant was a bit lacking.  We also heard the manager yelling at the staff (as did Jessica), which definitely puts a damper on the over all experience.  Also the TV playing Bollywood was a little distracting and pushing it for an Indian vibe.  It's definitely worth a try though not something that is a must in St. Pete.

I ate here while visiting my sister in law at Eckerd College. She wanted to get off campus so we checked yelp for Indian food. This restaurant did not have great reviews, but we decided to chance it. Turns out, the other reviewers were right. My curry was not well flavored. I asked for extra spicy an it taste like the chef just added way too much dry red chile powder. It was pasty and bland and still not very spicy. My sis in law did enjoy her mild butter chicken and the garlic naan was tasty. Certainly not the best Indian food, but probably not the worst.

Wit or without is a nice steak sandwich shop
I prefer my steak flat not chopped
Very flavorful excellent rolls

Service and cleanliness above average
5 stars on my last visit.

The immature teenagers that work at this place take your order then proceed to talk about condom size and how weed they smoked right in front of my 3 year old. I will NEVER return to this place again. If I wanted that kind of atmosphere, I'd take my kids to Genos following an Eagles loss. Do not go here.

Next time, let me park where I want you arrogant punk

I don't know what is up with this Subway, but I have never seen people make sandwiches so slow in all my life. They have a drive-thru, which sounds awesome and convenient, but it is the slowest drive-thru I have ever been in, anywhere, for any chain. You can see most of the restaurant from your car, and I have often seen three employees and zero customers at the counter and it still takes ten minutes to get a sandwich when I am the only one in the drive-thru. 

Skip it.

Service is great. The food...oh the food! This was our first visit, it will not be our last. We had yellow rice, tostones, croquetas, empanadas and yuka. The chicken in the empanadas was tender and flavorful. We didn't care for the croquetas but that's just a personal thing, I am sure they are delicious if you are into them. Lots of food, great prices.
This place is absolutely delightful. The cakes are moist and the icing is delicious. The staff is also really pleasant. My girlfriend loves these
Fast repairs, fair pricing and excellent customer service! Never had a problem they couldn't fix. They do all of my fleet and personal vehicles. Wouldn't go any other place!

I am not a born and bred Philadelphian and have not found a cheesesteak I love until today. My husband brought me a Wit or Witout cheesesteak to me for dinner while I am in Doylestown hospital and even after sitting in the fridge for hours and reheated, it was fantastic! Can't wait until I am able to get one freshly made. Thanks, Trevor!!!
It's a lie. Open to 10:00 my but. Cleaning up at 9pm with door locked and light on. Stop going to Subway.

Another great example of Yelp exposing me to good food that I otherwise would not have tried.  I went here for lunch today with a co-worker.  

I tried the arroz con pollo, which came with a side salad, and fried plantains. It was wonderful.  The plantains were just slightly crispy on the edges which gave them some nice texture. The chicken and rice had a subtle flavor that I really enjoyed.  

My co-worker got the Cubano sandwich at the suggestion of another patron.  He said it was a great sandwich and brought half of it back with him.  

The man behind the counter was rather gruff, but we all have bad days, so no worries there. I'd recommend this place to others, and encourage them not to be put off by the location or surroundings.

If I could give it less stars, I would. Waited 30 minutes in the drive thru for a 6'. For my sandwich and hurried back to work where I found a complete mess. It was supposed to be toasted, but instead my steak and cheese is cold, not a single veggie made it on the sandwich. Instead it's all just thrown on top. There's mayo everywhere- and that's all I can taste. There's almost no meat on the sandwich. To top it all off, I paid for extra cheese and didn't get a single slice. Called the store to complain and the lady said my only option was to bring the sandwich back for them to remake. But that's not possible since it took 30 minutes and I have a job to be at. Terrible customer service and terrible food.

I went here this past Saturday and had the most wonderful dining experience! Caught the tail end of the brunch jazz, and enjoyed an amazing waffle and grits (brought to my table by Kathy, one of the owners!). The food was delicious, the location was spacious, and the room was full of light despite the thunderstorm outside. Kathy was a delight and the food was great, I'll definitely be back next time I'm in Nashville.

My first love, honestly, truly. Literally, before Salsa, this was the only place my dad and I could go to get true, authentic Caribbean food. I always, ALWAYS, get the pechuga de pollo... the plantains are exquisite, the chicken breast is always seasoned perfectly and I love how they top it with onions. The white rice and black beans are so filling. I always get a Malta to compliment my meal, too. I know my dad and brother really like the smoothies (specifically the mango one). The bread they give your before your food comes out is so good too. EVERYTHING IS GOOD. Cannot go wrong. Craving it rn actually.
Wow the veggie bomb was delicious! My two friends and I had veggie bombs and coffee and the total with tip was $20.
Consistently slow service. Inconsistent hours. I once arrived an hour before closing time and was told they had just closed. Will drive 10 minutes to the location in the CWE for better service.

They have a good lunch buffet weekdays and Saturday.  Parking is problematic but then so is all of downtown.  The service for drinks is slow but the buffet more than makes up for it.  The butter chicken is to die for.  Our friend from Bombay says it is his favorite Indian restuarant in town.  I wish they would vary the dessert option more, it always seems to be rice pudding.

My friend and I stopped in for Easter Brunch today and the food was amazing! The buffet had lots of options to choose from at a very reasonable price being that we are college students. The live music was great as well. 
However, we had to literally flag down our waitress for more water on the table. She did come back to check on us, but didn't refill our cups until we asked.
This was our first time here and we asked the owner the price of a to-go box at the end of our meal. Instead of answering the question, she said "uhhh" and walked away! We both thought that was extremely disrespectful. We simply didn't know, and didn't get an answer until we had to ask our server. 
Also, as we were finishing up as they were closing she went to every table and talked to each person still eating except for us. Probably because everyone else was visibly much older than we were and she must not have thought it was important to do so. 
I would definitely come back here, but I definitely hope that next time things are a little better as far as service goes. I understand it was Easter and busy, but it definitely did not go unnoticed.

In a restaurant experience straight from Calle Ocho, Back to Cuba did nothing but impress. Seriously, no joke, not even a little bit. This was every bit as good as the fabled Versailles in Miami, sans the hour long wait with tourists fresh off the boat. 

Don't overthink your choices, go for the same thing you would at any walk-up counter, Cubano sandwich, beans & rice, & a cafe cubano. As much as people call a Cubano the most un-Cuban thing you can order - who cares - a delightful blend of meat, cheese, bread & butter. If it's not Cuban, it's definitely got some American flair!

Don't short yourself - go for the cafe cubano as well to round out your experience.

Forget any reviews talking about inattentive service or expensive menus - it's worth every minute and every dollar.

According to Science, 70-75% of what we perceive as taste is really smell, which is why food is never as good when you have a head cold. The relationship inverted means that, if there's an overpowering, distracting smell while, the quality of your gastronomic experience will suffer for it. 

India Grill punched me right in the nose when I walked in there for lunch. Cloying incense, vaguely chemical, swept out onto the sidewalk like walking by the candle store at the mall. Normally, I would've yielded to the crashing wave of scent, letting it carry me back out onto the street and on my way, but I was determined to try this place. The former 1st Ave N location had served some pretty good (though monopolized) buffet and, though Green Chili Bistro was great, I wanted to explore options. 

Both Green Chili and India Grill suffer from the need to cater to bland palates - I guess the average Floridian can't handle the heat - but India Grill was missing out on the flavor, too. Butter chicken, Tandoori, vegetable curry, and everything else we tried elicited the idea of Indian food, but not the deep expeditionary feel of exotic spices trooping across your tongue. 

Gulab Jamun, a dessert cake ball soaked in sweet syrup, tasted vaguely plastic.

There are two reasons that I will go back: one is that I heard the dinner menu is significantly better than the buffet offerings - this makes sense and I will give them the benefit of the doubt. The second is that my visit was within a week of them opening. A guy wheeled in their beverage mini fridge while we were eating. I'll hope that they can get into a little better groove and dish up some exciting flavor. 

Surfing the smell back out onto the street after the meal, I looked across the way at Green Chili Bistro, and its savory welcoming smells of food, and knew what I'd choose for lunch next time.

I think their steaks have greatly improved from when they first opened, because I did not care for them. However, they are probably one of my fav steaks now. I try to eat more on the healthy side but I do enjoy indulging every once in awhile, and I love their "wiz wit" steak, with long hots. They also now offer salads, wraps & hoagies. They have a hot pepper/pickle bar also to add to your sandwich. 

Everyone here is always so pleasant and welcoming. If you have never been here, you must try their steaks in 2017! Or, if you weren't impressed before, like me, go back, I promise you won't be sorry. 

You can always look around for coupons.
Awesome food hospitality and music.  I'd recommend this place to friends and family time and time again.

I order from here just about every Friday night for pizza parties. The food is always great, staff is courteous and always gets my order ready  very quickly and 100% correct. Easily the best value in Northeast Philly for pizza, wings and sandwiches.

Just had the scariest experience there.  Got accosted by several kids panhandling for cigarettes and other things.  They were using the foulest language imaginable.  The fifteen minute wait for my order saw these kids going in and out of the store, calling me names, and trying to dump ashes from a blunt on my shoes.  I don't know why management didn't throw the kids out.  I like this place, but I am hesitant to go back.

If I could give negative stars, I would. I don't know if anything will be done or anyone at this location will read this but here goes. So I pull up to a drive thru (the only one in my area that has a veggie patty). One person at the counter and two cars in the parking lot. I'm the only one in the DT at 4:23pm. I order (touch screen) and pull up to the window. The employee is at the counter making sandwiches for the woman I saw at the counter. Fine. I wait. And wait. 15mins go by with NO acknowledgement that I was sitting there other than side eye. No coming to take my money, no wait a minute finger, no nothing. Someone walks in the door and the employee glances at me and then takes this customer's order. I drive off. I come home and email corporate what happened and I call the store and ask to speak to the manager. Someone gets him. I explain what happened. He replies "yeah." I said "really? This is all you have to say? You're supposedly the manager." He says "I was making your sandwich when you drove off." I said "IF that was true, you could've acknowledged me by taking my money, coming to the window and telling me it'll be a minute, go to hell....anything but yet you chose to glance at me and start someone's order." He said "no, it was yours." I said "no that was wheat. Mine was on flatbread." He was just breathing into the phone so I said thank you and hung up and emailed corporate with his response. Don't patronize me by lying to cover your rudeness/lack of respect/laziness. If it's too much to run the counter and drive thru with 3 people in the whole restaurant, shut it down. What happened to customer service?! I've been there before when a couple of EXTREMELY nice women were working but not this guy. Won't be going back.
An excellent department store with great bargains and sales.  There is a department for everyone. The staff is helpful & knowledgeable. They are mainly in the PA area.

This is definitely the best place to get authentic Cuban food in Nashville. I had the papa rellena, pescado con ajillo, and empanadas-- all of which were FANTASTIC. I loved it so much that after discovering this place with my friend, I came back the next day with my mom (she loved it too).

This place is great. We recently enrolled our 4 year old into their intro to swim classes. Classes are 30 minutes, once per week, year round. They offer 3 to 1 student to teacher ratios. You can tell they know what they are doing as they really take their time to make sure the kids are improving. They do offer make up classes if you miss. 

Nice indoor facility with a good waiting area (with windows) for the parents. 

Little more expensive then I would have liked but it's a good value for what you get. I've heard from others the progress is slow but that makes sense at 30 minutes per week. 

I would recommend for others.

I enjoyed the chocoholic cupcake, but it was rather crumbly and didn't stick together too well. I love my cupcakes moist and dense, and this one was rather crumbly, dry, and airy. However, the icing was incredible! Friendly service and a clean store- is definitely come back and try another one.

I love this place! Found it about a year ago and it always consistent always good. After living in Florida for seventeen-years I thought good Cuban food was a thing of the past.  It is a hidden gem. It is worth the drive from anywhere in Metro Nashville. Their Cubano will make you think you are in South Florida.

I highly recommend Back to Cuba!!!

Got a cheesesteak American wit, it was average at best. Very bland and the guys at work now call me crimson chin after how long it takes to chew the meat. For the price of the cheesesteak just go somewhere else.

I never knew how good a Cuban sandwich was until I got to experience the real thing. This place is a little hole in the wall cafe that makes trying new things an adventure! My only wish is that there was room for more tables and chairs so that meals could be enjoyed with large groups.

Ok I give this place 2 stars because 1 there food is good it's not bad but the service sucks ass man they are all like miserable i hate walking into business like that and 2 I went in the other day to get a cheesteak and I said toast the roll young girl at the counter had it rite on the slip I asked her to ask the cook witch by the way she is the owner and she said it to her with a attitude like yes it's toasted it's on the paper I did it the young girl turns around and looks at me like you heard her so I stay quite wait for my food she don't bother to hand it to me knowing it's mine she goes and puts it on top of the over  so young girl grabs it and comes around to give to me I walk up grab it and I open it in there face and show her how SHE DIDNT TOAST MY Roll soggy ass cheesteak I watch you make it if I said something is obviously because I didn't see you put it in the dam oven... I didn't say anything because it isn't the first time I'm just not taking my money there any more really sucks bc they have pretty good food just the owner is a b*****

This family owned place is delightful!  Service was great and Cathy, the owner, came out to introduce herself. A wonderful jazz musician was playing throughout breakfast.  Nice touch!  Waffles were so fluffy and potatoes were cooked perfectly.  A diamond on  Dickerson Pike
All women painting did a fantastic job painting many rooms in our house. She is great to work with on picking out colors. Very neat, creative and trustworthy. Def recommend her to all.

We came here for a Fathers Day brunch and it was great. Fortuately we were a little early as the place filled up.The service is attentive and everyone makes you feel right at home.

The self-serve food line is long with lots of different items to try. I did the breakfast first, but had a few white beans which were delicious. I went back for catfish and got more beans. I think they are the best I have ever had.

They have a full-service bar as well. Restrooms are clean. There was a good electronic piano guy playing which set a festive atmosphere.

I recommend Shugga Hi's brunch and plan to try a weekday lunch one day before too long.

I'm so glad I enrolled my daughter in swim lessons. I wish I had done so earlier! We've been to 5 lessons so far and she's become much more comfortable in the water. She's even gone under!

We take the 18m-3y class. We sing songs, work on body positioning, learning to climb out of the pool, jumping into the pool, and going under. 

Our teacher, Megan, is wonderful. She's been very patient as my daughter has been very fussy. Fortunately, the more lessons we've gone to, the less fussing she's done. 

You pay a monthly tuition for swimming lessons once a week. If there's 5 in a month, you're not charged more. If there's less than 4, the amount is prorated. I like that they list pricing on their website too. 

They offer a free swimming program for babies aged 2-5 months. I plan to sign my next baby up!

Sooo good! I think the hours are a little funny, but I think it's because the owner has an Italian restaurant to run also. I usually get the grilled chicken with a side of shrimp. Native Cubans say it's just ok, (I've asked) but I think it's amazing!

After hearing many recommendations for this spot, especially the Cuban sandwich, we decided to give it a go. Arrived about 10 minutes after opening on a Saturday and placed a carry out order. We got empanadas and the Cuban sandwich. Waited appx 35 minutes for the order and once we finally got it the smell was incredible. Got home and dug in. The empanadas were good not great. The pastry was nice and flaky but the beef inside was average. I was expecting a little more flavor. The Cuban was extremely underwhelming. Had very little flavor and in my opinion was way over done. I've had better Cuban sandwiches at sports bars. No kidding. Way over toasted and I cannot begin to explain how disappointed I was in the lack of flavor. It was essentially a toasted ham sandwich. I'd like to tray some other dishes but the two we got were disappointing. Especially for the wait time.

I hate giving this place a two star review. 

It's a small, locally owned business. The food is pretty good. The server was excellent. I just didn't feel particularly welcome. 

While my wife and I were enjoying our food, I received a text message from work. We normally have a no phones at the dinner table policy, but a glance at a message is okay at our table. While I was checking the message, a man, who I could only presume to be the owner, hollered at me from behind the counter, "No texting, put your phone away at the table!"

My wife and I looked at each other, incredulous. I realize that it is his restaurant and he can run it as he sees fit, however, there was no sign notifying patrons of this policy. Also, if he wanted to make an issue of it, he could've visited the table and discreetly asked us to comply with his wishes. We DID comply, as I didn't want to be asked to leave while finishing my meal, but I will never dine in this restaurant again. 

It's a damn shame, too. The Lechon Asado was absolutely delicious. The rice served with it was also good, the beans just okay. If you go, be warned, the food is good, but keep your phone in your pocket, lest the Cuban Nazi make an appearance and bellow at you too.

OMG the food was delicious and taste fresh don't change anything best in northeast Philly.the young lady that answer the phone was very nice and helpful.i will be coming back here i am a customer now.
Just amazing food , have to love the BBQ. The walking taco is very good.. The award winning chili is great when you fire it up. Be prepared for the heat .

After the lunch rush hour, friend and I hit Back To Cuba for a late lunch.  
She got the shredded pork plate (no substitutions, on any plate) and I got the grilled pork steak with fried yuca, moros and avocado on lettuce...
They have a hot green sauce in a squeeze bottle that is definitely worth going there to have!
My pork was tough, overcooked and dry, but.... the fried yuca was really good!
Friend said her shredded pork was dry..  (maybe if they would shred it, and then refry it in lard, it would be more juicy)...

$13 for my plate.
$11 for her plate
$2.50 for a side of plantains.
(**** notice all the other reviews are on the Cuban sandwich.)

I've had superb, cheap Cuban food in So Florida...
This place does not compare.  But it is what it is.
Not cheap, that's for sure.

I will probably return in another 3 yrs..
Best Indian in downtown St. Pete for sure. The lunch buffet is the greatest! The staff are all very nice and friendly. The place is clean and has beautifully decorated. Love it!

THIS PLACE THO! The food is amazing. I put down my cell phone so I could concentrate on the flavors hah. It tastes like it was made with so much care. The place is just a little hole in the wall but it's delicious but healthy comfort food. The plantains are sweet and flavorful and not too chewy or too soft. The beef is incredible. They even gave me a free mango milkshake
Very good food! It's a place that has a lot of history and worth a try. When I went, I didn't try any of the desserts but they all looked so delicious!
Great lunch!  The Camaronea al Ajillo was fantastic!  Food was made fresh and had good spice to it.  I noted they also did take out for to-go folks.

I am new to the DeMont Swim family. My young son is in baby swim. I absolutely love that they encourage baby swim by providing the classes free for the community. I used to be a competitive swimmer and taught swim lessons myself, so I am very excited to see my son enjoy the water. If you want to get your baby started right away at three months, I recommend looking into classes well before they turn three months. There are limited spots. I called when my son was 2.5 months and he has started baby swim at 3.5 months. The staff is friendly and the set up of the pools and facilities are nice. It is not state of the art, but it does the trick. I don't have access to a pool and while having a young child in Tucson, I want an indoor facility. I will most likely continue on paying for swim lessons after baby swim for that reason. I do find the lessons a bit on the expensive side, but I hope that means they will be top notch!

Here in Nashville on a vacation and found this place. Nice atmosphere and the food is delicious!  We had the Dickerson breakfast and the waffles with tots. Service was top notch. Can't leave without getting a few donuts. Which were delicious. On vacation calories don't count, LOL!!

This is my bite of heaven! I was born in Cuba and grew up in south Fl. I now live in Memphis and come to Nashville on business once a month. I take every opportunity to come here. Food is authentic and spot on. Cuban sandwich is a huge value and the taste is great!!

What a huge disappointment. I have been to other shops in this chain and this one wasn't worth the money. Icing is the true call of Smallcakes. The icing here was skimpy and dried out. Instead of smooth luxurious creamy frosting there was a blob of crusted over mess. I bought a cookie sandwich and a cupcake. The cookie sandwich wasn't any better. So sad...I wasted my time and calories here. Don't however give up on Smallcakes...just visit the store in Springfield or Champaign.
Truly the worst "BBQ" sandwich I had ever had.  One bite and I tossed it.  Nothing like a mouthful of canned nacho cheese sauce as a condiment.  That was a first for me.

Get here early because it fills up quickly. It's very laid back atmosphere. Live jazz music which is a great break from the usual honky tonk that Nashville has to offer. Service is slower than I would prefer, but the food makes up for it.

The people are kind and tend to your need as you wait. They have an option for Sunday brunch(came on a Saturday) where you get a buffet style brunch. They also have bottomless mimosas that are a tad bit cheaper than the majority of the city.

I ordered the breakfast sandwich with turkey sausage and a fried egg;although you can have the bacon option and the egg prepared anyway you like. I also had a cranberry mimosa that hit the spot. 

Overall, the food was cooked great and not greasy like most restaurants. 4:5 stars only because of the extended wait.... but again... well worth it. I'll be back!
Amazing food and incredibly kind staff! The pork was amazing and I loved the yuca and the plantains. I will definitely be back!

I'm not from Philly, so you can take this review with a grain of salt if you must...but from my experience this is the best cheesesteak I have had since I've been in Philadelphia area the last four years. The prices are a little high I think, but that seems to be the trend with cheesesteaks throughout the entire city. I have had Pat's, Tony Luke's, the one in Reading Terminal, and Prince of Steaks...and this is by far the best cheesesteak I have had yet! They chop the meat if you want, which I prefer; and they have different options for cheese. I would definitely recommend Wit or Witout!

I've driven by Back to Cuba multiple times and have wanted to try it, but a recent episode of Parts Unknown brought my BF and I here after craving a Cubano sandwich. 

The restaurant is nice inside with a casual atmosphere where you order at the counter. The menu is handwritten on what seems to be cardboard paper and is a bit difficult to read. I appreciate the craftiness but wish it was a bit larger. We ordered the Cubano sandwich (of course) and the roasted pork with rice, beans, and yuca. The sandwich was huge and plenty for two people. It was very good! The roasted pork was also very flavorful and delicious, and the yuca was unreal good. I loved it so much!! I wasn't a big fan of the beans and rice; the beans didn't taste fresh, and I was disappointed because the pork dish was more expensive, and I expected higher quality from the rice and beans. 

Overall, I liked the food a lot (especially the yuca) and would like to give them a try at dinner. It's a pretty heavy meal for lunch (although delicious) so I am curious to come back and get some more dishes to sample!
Hidden gem in Nashville. Lovely staff and delicious food

I am between 3 and 4 stars for Saturday brunch. 4-5 stars for food, 4-5 stars for ambience, and 4-5 stars for staff attitude but the service was still so bad! :(  They gave us one glass of water then came back for another. One cup of coffee then had to come back for another. One set of silverware--same story. Had to ask twice for milk and sugar and refills on coffee (never came).  The food took so long to come out. The staff apologized but we were hungry and here for a loooong time with periods in which no one seated had food. Music was also good, so clearly I'm feeling conflicted. I may try again for Sunday brunch (bc with the buffet, maybe the service won't be such a problem).
Go try it. Me describing it will not do this place justice. Delicious, positively  food coma inducing I can't wait to go back!!!

This place is great - in a strip center with basic surroundings but incredible tasty food.  Service awesome, thy brought me a pastry with my coffee and super friendly staff.  

I'm committed to eating everything on the menu in the next 12 months.
Oh. My. Word. The German chocolate cake is AMAZING. The slice was huge. My son had a glazed donut and he loved it also.
Schwartz eye care provided excellent eye care in a timely and professional manor.  Dr Schwartz was fabulous!  See him if you want a thorough  professional eye exam.

They had some good collectible things. A lot of Star Wars, Lord of the Rings, some Harry Potter and Pez. There's also a lot of junk though and it's a bit untidy and dirty in there. The people in there are a little creepy too. It's got some good stuff for cheap but if you are wary of 'hoods then stay away. I think this place would be really nice if they just took the "flea" out of their "market", if you know what I mean.
So delicious! Satisfied my hunger. I got a turkey hoagie onion rings with chipotle dressing so bomb
Yum!!! So good. We tried the wedding cake, vanilla with chocolate, and Oreo cakes. We scarfed them and wished we had more. Can't wait to go back and try other flavors.
Excellent hospital ER is great and Hospital also I had two of my birth at this hospital always come here. They treat you nice and take good care of you.

With a couple of highly skilled docs, much investment into the latest diagnostic technologies and a charmingly efficient staff you are certain to enjoy this visit to the doctor. I am always impressed with how modernization keeps improving the patient experience. This place is investing in me and my time by ensuring I get the best care with as little fuss and bother as necessary. 
And the frames collection is expansive. Don't forget to check out the sunglasses. You know you want them.
This place is such a find! The instructors are magic, I wish I could give ten stars!!

Way better than it used to be. They use different meat and rolls now. It's a completely new sandwich. I believe they have new owners as of recently. Would highly recommend. One of the best cheesesteaks around.

The service was soooooooooooooooooo AWFUL. The set up of this place is weird to begin with. You walk in the door and pretty much stand around. It reminds me of a Southern Baptist church kitchen (at least in the front). We waited about 20 minutes to be seated on a Saturday around 11. It wouldn't of been so bad but everything seem so disorganized and chaotic. Once we were seated we ordered drinks. My brother had to order his bloody Mary twice and still never got it but somehow it ended up on the check. The food took about 45 minutes to come out. I ordered the breakfast bowl. I really really enjoyed it and I especially liked the special sauce which had a surachi  base. It should also be noted that they just have turkey sausage not pork. And all meat is cooked medium well unless otherwise mentioned. I got a slice of Keylime cake to go - it was just okay. I wouldn't get it again. I have definitely had better. Overall, they need to seriously work on training their staff how to handle large crowds, turning tables, listening, and improve efficiency. 
I will eat here again but it would probably be more of phone order type of thing. 
They have a lot to improve. Oh and parking is trash.
Great food and live entertainment on a Sunday morning what love can you ask for? Everything tastes like it was made from home! Very excited to come back soon!

The single star is for this program only. I am a talk radio fan. Listen to talk all day long while I work. This station deteriorates mightily starting at 3 in the afternoon. Phyllis Valentine and his Ed McMahan wannabe sidekick are two of the most boring people in media. Valentine snorts and grunts and giggles and laughs and chuckles constantly, and his partner, Jonnie Bee, has a cackle that will slay you. He laughs hysterically at the drop of a hat. Thing is, there is usually NOTHING funny being said, yet the constant guffaws. I can't remember Limbaugh laughing very often. Then, there is the constant inside crap between the two about something the audience has no clue about. They will crank up about some remote singer nobody has ever heard of and stay with the conversation for endless ages. How this lowly program ever got a national audience is beyond me. Hannity is on at the same time, so there is an alternative. Not a great alternative, but an alternative.

I'm surprised that they're still in business.  I had to return steaks a couple of times on different orders because there was literally one piece of steak on each sandwich!  It was loaded with globs of liquid cheese. I gave up on them after multiple attempts to get a decent cheesesteak.
 Overpriced, way too salty, and not worth the trip.

I was very excited to try out Back to Cuba when it was picked for the most recent UYE. I love trying small authentic places like this and while I'm not an expert on Cuban food, I'm always up for trying new things! I was happy to be going with someone that new their way around the menu. Back to Cuba is located off of a busy street and next to a gas station. Parking can get crowded but I had no problem finding a spot on a Thursday night. The inside is small and there are just a few tables but it's cozy enough and we were able to get a table, no problem. The menu is handcrafted with paper and marker, but is clear enough. Everything had a small description to help clueless people like me. My friend and I decided to split a meal so we could get something larger. We ordered the Churrasco (skirt steak, chimichurri sauce, rice, beans, tostones). At $18 it's one of the pricier things on the menu but it's steak so that can be expected. We also ordered a side of sweet plantains and mango milkshakes. The system seems to be order at the counter, grab a seat, and then pay at the end at the counter. The milkshakes and plantains were out in no time. The mango milkshake...holy YUM! So freakin good. I want one every day. It was huge and was an appetizer in itself. I've never had plantains so I don't have anything to base them off of, but they were also quite delicious. Sweet and full of flavor. The Churrasco was out just as we finished the plantains. The steak was thin but large. It was the perfect size to split. The chimichurri sauce added a nice salty flavor. The steak was tender. The rice also blew me away for just being white rice. I can't describe the flavor. Salty? But not really. I don't know. It's good. That's all you need to know. I would definitely recommend this dish to anyone. But I'm sure everything on the menu is just as good! While the cafe itself isn't the fanciest, you can tell the focus is on the food. They know what they are doing and they do it well. I can't wait to come back and try more!
This is the best Cuban food in Nashville. I absolutely adore this place and it reminds of back home in Miami and keeps me comforted when I'm home sick. Friendly people and amazing food. 10/10!!!!

This place is GREAT!! I was going to another place that, although very friendly, would make me wait for 1-2 hours after each scheduled appointment before I could even be seen.

I was seen right away here, didn't need to take dilation drops (there's a choice between that or a $49 picture to see the back of your eyes), didn't have to do any of the old-school tests (they have all the newest technology!), and things were REALLY fast.

Dr. Joyce was very friendly and Glenn at the glass department was awesome.

The place I used to go to was a family favorite but this one beats it tenfold. LOVE IT and I won't put off making appointments anymore! :)

Absolutely stellar!!! I made reservations a year ago for 8 friends and they loved it so upon visiting Nashville again this weekend I had to check it out for myself. Catherine greeted us at the door with the kindest smile and made us feel instantly welcome. My 2 year old devoured his waffle, my burrito was fabulous and the rest of our party enjoyed their meal. We all got sweet treats to go and they were just yummy! The best part? LIVE MUSIC AT BREAKFAST!!! Great blues and a cute bakery to boot! You can't beat it. It's a new must eat for our Nashville trips!

Also I thought I lost my wallet while there and the waitresses came outside to help me find it. Great customer service!

Stopped here for a quick meal in route to a wedding. Most notably the staff was very kind and helpful. They definitely created a welcoming, small town atmosphere. I ordered a small milkshake and a chopped steak, with onions, and whiz. Overall I think this was a great classic cheesesteak (I recognize that I say this completely as an outsider). The bread was the perfect combo of soft, crisp, and a little chewy. It came with a generous portion of steak, cheese and onions. The milkshake was less sweet than most, something I liked, but others might not. They had a self serve pickle accouterments bar featuring some spicy hot peppers. Don't expect to find any "healthy" options if you come here, but if you're in for a steak, check it out.

This was a cool little place! The vibe was low key and jazzy. Loved the live music and the family owned feel. Also, it's a black owned business. The only down side was that the food was just ok. But overall it was great service and food atmosphere

I took a quick trip for this good reviewed place, will start best to worst 
 
Service 5/5
Ambience 5/5
Location and parking 4/5
Food 3/5
Wait time 2/5 

Here is why: 
I visited on a Thursday afternoon 3ish where I was the only customer. I received a good welcoming and some suggestions, but didn't expect to wait 35 minute for being the only customer at the time for a burger and fries. The idea of waffle burger was good, the taste was good, but it was barely warm and fries were luke warm - cold. They couldn't  make it medium rare burger so ordered it medium and it came well done, and the sandwich fell apart, the waffle too soft. Good idea poor execution. 

Had a desert cupcake prior to leaving the store it was decent 4/5. 

Will I come out of my way to come here? No

Bon appetite

Slow, no health standards, meat ball sub, meat room temp, lady picked up each meatball with her hand, u think she could feel they were not hot nor warm, during the making of footlong, the lady caughed many timrs ,pulled out her phone 2 timrd, texting, then back to footlong. I returned it, was told to eait 5 minutes for changw, only to be told hold on while they find more change, caughed 4 times on my money in their hand. Before giveing it to me. Most subways serve good food, not here, they are never busy, no customers most the time, they get poor service & crap food, and never come back.
Lo mejor de Tennessee buena calidad buena  atención me encanto es segunda ves que vengo y me quedo encantado lo recomiendo

I'm rarely a negative restaurant reviewer, but in all my time here in Nashville, this was the worst experience I've had. I created this Yelp account specifically to write about this restaurant. My fish was undercooked and completely covered in lemon butter, which also smothered my salad since it was served on the same plate. They even burnt the rice! It was rock hard. We could taste the frost bite on the bread they served. My date's meal was equally as disappointing. A terrible meal for 2 for $35 was all I got. I hope they change their ways.

I love subway and my food was great, but I also wanted to give credit to an awesome employee. I came in this evening around 5:20pm. I dont remember  her name, but the employee on duty was in the dining area cleaning and sweeping. She came to take my order (after washing her hands and putting on gloves). It appeared that she was the only one taking orders at the time and at least 7 people showed up while I was ordering. The whole time, she was patient, polite, and didn't rush me. I ordered 2 sandwiches, and I always get a lot of toppings on my sandwich - despite this my sandwich was very neat and clean looking when she was done. It's just the small gestures like this that make you want to come back to a place. I appreciated the great service and food from her. Good job!!

I love to visit places where the people who work there see to enjoy their jobs. We came for lunch after visiting the St. Louis science museum (check review) the food was good of course! It was clean, neatly organized and fresh! 
Only complaint is there is no changing table in the restrooms. 
When I told them we were from Kansas City and asked about some restaurants they were eager to suggest places to dine while we were in town. I typically do not like to eat at places where we can eat at home but I'm glad we did this time. They made it an amazing lunch!
They painted our  entire interior prior to sale and  they did such a fantastic job, we are having them paint the entire new house. Neat, clean, professional, good paper work and a wonderful person.

For several years, a non-profit that I supported had a rather large booth inside Peddlers Mall, an Eastside flea market that has seen better days and the most dominant business that still happens to be open inside a retail strip that has also seen massively better days. 

A year or two ago, the non-profit closed their booth and actually closed as an organization. As a result, I've not been back to Peddlers Mall before my rather random visit today that occurred precisely because I was in the area and remembered an incense vendor here who had really great prices and I wondered if they were still around. 

They were! So, I picked up a few packs of incense at $1 each and left Peddlers Mall a fairly happy camper. 

If you don't know this strip center, it's the same one that also includes the free-standing Blueberry Hill, a rather blue-collar but beloved breakfast joint that is probably the nicest place in this corner. 

That's not saying much.

It appears that real estate developer CBRE may have become involved with this corner - this could potentially be a good sign as it may mean some long-needed renovations may be in order. We'll have to wait and see, though I did notice a couple smaller retailers in the area seemed to have opened up shop along with one storefront ministry. 

Peddlers Mall has been in this location for years. As has been noted, though I personally think overstated, it's a run-down flea market and, yes, it currently does have more vacancies than usual. I've seen very few flea markets in Indy that I would consider "clean" and I don't think that Peddlers Mall is that far out of the ordinary. That said, it certainly is run down and it sure seems like even in the time that my friend's booth has been gone it has gone somewhat downhill. 

There's semi-formal accessible parking, though it's not particularly well marked. It's certainly not ADA compliant. The curb cut at the entrance is in disrepair to the point that anyone with some upper body issues will struggle a bit. Again, there's a curb cut there but it sure doesn't qualify as accessible. 

There's a double doorway entry, both glass doors, and even the entryways are in some disrepair. For the most part, the aisles inside are relatively accessible - or at least wide enough for a wheelchair. However, there are certainly exceptions within booths. When my friend's booth was open, it was stellar but that was because he was very aware of accessibility and made sure of it. 

The biggest reasons for the 3 star rating rather than low? The people here have always been friendly and helpful. From all that I've heard from my friend, they were good as landlords as well. While there are quite a few booths vacant right now, there's still quite the selection ranging from mattress booths (all wrapped in plastic), books/music, incense, housewares, tattoo supplies, and pretty much all the other stuff you expect from a flea market. Prices, for the most part, are reasonable. 

Peddlers Mall is certainly not a destination flea market. It would be absurd to drive out of your way to visit it. The parking lot is, indeed, filled with pot holes, though you can certainly make your way through the parking lot without hitting them. This particular retail center has been neglected for years and pretty much the entire strip center looks in distress and even the buffet that used to be located across the strip center closed primarily due to rougher clientele. 

However, I love my incense and for 5 bucks I got enough to last me quite a while. So, since I was in the area anyway it was worth a stop. Besides, I've had my tetanus shot. I'm good.

The menu offers plenty of choice (but not so much that each item can't be perfectly prepared). I went for a Cubano, black beans and tres leches. All were fantastic--the black beans were a revelation and the Cuban bread had an incredible crunch--but what wowed me just as much as the flavor was the portion size. I got what I paid for and more. I took half my sandwich home and left some beans and cake on the plate because there was so much. I also tried the Malta (soda) at my friend's recommendation. I thought it was great, but it's definitely sweet, so I was glad I had ice water to go with it. 

The location nothing to look at, but you don't go here for to decor. The service was quick and very friendly, and the food was fantastic.
Incredible food, quick service, friendly staff. We loved the chicken soup (special of the day) and the grilled chicken plate, but everything was great.
This place was awesome!  We had Sunday brunch buffet and everything was delicious!  Totally was not expecting the incredible live jazz!!! Keep up the good work Shugga Hi!!!

Don't go here unless you like being yelled at and harassed.  I was sitting looking at my phone waiting for my to go order when the owner yelled at me "no texting". Then he stalked by me and out the door. He came back in and yelled at me again before disappearing into the bathroom. I told the two girls at the counter I would not be back unless this was stopped and further that I would post the incident on yelp. Nothing happened so here it is. I won't be back and I would advise no one else to go either!
Awesome place. Great Churrasco and flan
Great addition to the Cleveland park neighborhood. Breakfast all day, fantastic baked goods and super friendly owners! #BreakfastBurritoandCoconutCake

My daughter wanted to come here for a while but haven't had a chance.  Lucky for me today is the day. Loved everything about this place.  The owner greeted us upon entering and seated us. The musician at the piano was playing lots of oldies and  her music was noticeable but not loud ( kind of important because I hate go to a place the music is so loud so everyone has to be loud to communicate) the owner (Kathy) checked on us few times during our lunch and refill our water. 
The food was soooooo good. Home made food served hot and fresh.  Love the Kale Salad , donut casserole, and the sauerkraut and neck bone are my favorite.  We will be back.  This is great find.

There's not much for vegetarians... you can order off of the sides menu.  And those sides are good.  I had rice, beans, and fried plantains, and it was pretty good.

Seating is a bit limited, and I have the feeling things happen there at other times as there are game tables and some music instruments laying about, but nothing was happening while I was there.

I can't speak to authenticity as the only Cuban I've had before was in San Fran at a veggie Cuban place, but for Nashville it was some place I could eat at without feeling completely alien.
Great place to take your kids to learn to swim in a comfortable setting. They take great pride I teaching the kids an important skill!

This was my first visit and I was pleased with the menu, the waffle and baked chicken were extremely tasty.  The eggs were piping hot as was the food on the lunch Buffet.  The owner was super personable and was attentive to make sure everything was to our liking. The live music was totally amazing and a perfect compliment to our brunch experience.

I was excited to find a Cuban Restaurant located in Nashville after relocating from the Miami area of South Florida and was looking forward to finally finding a place to stop for a Colada. 

I visited around lunch on a Tuesday since they are closed on Mondays. They are located in a small strip mall with a gas station and several other businesses so the lot was crowded and their was a line inside. Once I got up to the counter I ordered a double shot Colada and a Cubano Sandwich off the menu. 

The service was adequate and the staff was friendly. The inside area of the restaurant was small but typical for a Cuban Lunch place. They also have several bistro style tables with chairs outside on the walkway. Most the other patrons were ordering to go so getting a table was not difficult. Despite the crowd my order arrived to me quickly. 

The Colada was a generous size for a double shot and had a nice espumita and was correctly sweetened. It arrived at my table relatively quickly but I was surprised to find it not hot but rather almost barely lukewarm and left me disappointed. I am hoping this was a one-off and that maybe it was delayed in reaching me or the espresso maker was not working correctly on the day of my visit. 

The Cubano arrived and looked great. I was disappointed to find that the bread seemed to be stale as it was very hard and crumbled apart as I tried to eat. I had read other reviews stating that the bread was hard but thought the reviewers were not accustomed to a sandwich being pressed. This was not the case though as the bread was dry and falling apart. The sandwich was dry and I did not find any mayonnaise and a very small amount of yellow mustard. While the portion size was decent I was unable to eat the entire sandwich due to how dry it was. 

I will try the Colada again when I am in the area but will probably leave the food alone and await our next trip back home.

I love this restaurant.  The owners are extremely not very and the food is AMAZING!  The only set-back is sometime service can be a little slow...BUT you kinda forget that when your food arrives...lol

Brunch is the best in the city!

My sister and I went yesterday, clean ,great waitress with a wonderful personality, everyone was ,friendly and helpful,the food was wonderful, we really enjoyed it also the dessert is awesome, can't  wait to go back again. I highly recommen going.
Excellent authentic Cuban food & the owners are so welcoming you'll feel like part of the family ! All the great dishes are available & cooked to order !

I loved their coffee...I'll begin with that. We ordered a Cuban sandwich with yucca and a plate of pork and plantains. It was not as flavorful as I'd hope. The pork was dry...my sandwich was dry. I'm just not used to that with Cuban sandwiches. The waitress was blah...like really blah. I felt as if I was bothering her by just asking for water. Maybe she was having an off day? Who knows, but I really enjoyed their coffee.

New staff every time I go in, but I can see that they're trying to make changes. Some of the booths are excellent! Others need to clean up. Found some really great bargains that were cheaper than what I'd find at a yard sale, and stuff that I need for my house.

If I could have given a minus star I would have! This place is so gross! From the horrible driveway full of massive potholes to the rank incense smell permeating the building! I've been to many Peddlers and Vendors malls but never any this disgusting! Half the booths are empty the others filled with random crap probably from dumpster dives! Heed my advice for pickers and people who enjoy treasure hunts...DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME! And if you do dare to venture in, don't forget your hand sanitizer!!
