Let me start by saying I'm from the east coast NJ to be exact so I grew up eating pizza in NJ and Ny. I will say the crust of the pizza was similar to my pizza but I was disappointed because the menu had Stromboli's on it but I asked our server why there wasn't any calzones on the menu and she said it's the same thing!!! Anyone who grew up near Ny or on the east coast knows they are not the same. So I ordered a few slices of "NY style pizza" like I said crust was similar but not much sauce, not much cheese. Which brings me to my shock, I asked for extra cheese put on my slices and the server said we don't do that, and then the pizza chef came over and said they don't add toppings, that is against their policy!!! No good pizza place in NJ or NY would have such a ridiculous policy or charge you $3.50 for a slice. Will not recommend to anybody looking for East Coast Pizza

5 stars for atmosphere
5 stars for taste
5 stars for location
1 star for drink selection
1 star for no gluten-free options

hubs and I rry local pizza everywhere we go and this is top notch- described as New York pizza its thin crust but substantial corn meal dusted crusty and chewy but not tough - fresh toppings and mushrooms. the sauce is rich tomato not bitter or overly sweet - #legit

YUMMMMMMM! I love their pizza! For an appetizer we ordered pesto chips, which were out of this world delish! When you read the words chips... you really think chips will come out, however the chips only means that it is a flat  pizza crust cut into small pieces layered with deliciousness. The pesto is not overwhelming, really the perfect amount. For our boys were ordered the  cheese super slice to share. This was great because it was just the right size and a better deal than ordering a smaller pizza. We ordered a medium BBQ chicken pizza and for three of us to share was perfect (pesto chips helped!). The pizza was sprinkled with a sweet BBQ sauce, chicken breast, mozzarella, red onions and fresh herbs. Oh my goodness it was soooo awesome! I love how they also have honey right on the table. There crust is so thick and chewy perfect for the right amount of honey and ranch combination! The Waiters were beyond friendly and prompt. They even had one waiter that was practicing tossing pizza doe with a towel and our boys thought it was so incredible. He came over and did it right next to the table to show them! Both boys were laughing and have a great time. I appreciate the little extra kindness that was shown to our family. It just adds to overall wonderful atmosphere and makes us more likely to come back and recommend to everyone!

One friend and I stopped by here on our first weekend in Nashville and were pleasantly surprised to be seated right away thanks to an amazing hostess even though they were already packed on a Saturday evening at 8pm. We had had a few beers before hand so went a little heavy handed by ordering the large portion of (8) garlic knots which were HUGE but very yummy. Next we ordered the small Dave's pie which arrived very quickly, super hot & tasted amazing. Shoutout to our server Carrie who kept our drinks full despite the rush & had great energy the whole time. We will definitely be regulars here! Highly recommend.

Fabulous addition to the neighborhood.  Love!

Okay so here's the rundown.  I will preface, this is a Jersey Girl's rundown.

NY pizza you are not, sorry, it hurts to type that. The sauce is close but the crust is too thick and the pie isn't greasy enough.  Let me elaborate.  The crust is a little too doughy but the size of the slices are close allowing me to fold that bad boy.  Now with the grease, I know, you probably say gross, but really, it comes with the NY slice.  There are three ways of eating a NY slice, you shove that puppy in your mouth, you fold and let the grease drip off onto the plate or if you aren't into the grease you dab it with napkins, plural.  This my friends is the reasoning for the doubling, tripling up of paper plates.  

Now to the garlic knots, where is the garlic??  Where are the pieces of garlic on top?  Again Nashville, I want garlic in my garlic bread.

The antipasto was satisfying and I would definitely get it again, especially the mozzarella.  I need to come back anyway, they ran out of prosciutto.

Now to the good.  The pizza is satisfying despite it's lack of NY-ness.  The location is perfect, the beer selection great, quick service and the atmosphere is a family friendly joint.  Seriously, I've never seen so many families out, it was wonderful!  (I should note I'm a single gal as well.)  

I will absolutely be back, probably quite frequently, most likely all the time.  Job well done 5 Points Pizza!

This is the best Pizza in Nashville. Its the only place that counts. I love this place and support it completely. If you want New York Style pizza its the best. Wait times and seating may vary. Plan accordingly. With a new expanded seating area and Late night window! You cannot go wrong.

Last time I ate there, which was about 10 years ago, the Red Rooster was a destination. What happened? the atmosphere is lovely. the bar is lovely, the music is good. everything was feeling good. until the food came.
grilled caesar: yuk. soggy lettuce with gross and too much vinaigrette and what? an entire can of chickpeas dumped on it?
my husbands burger, ordered medium came out less than rare. eeewwww. my trout: just meh. too bad. we won't be back

Recently moved to the area and this is my 3rd time here.....definitely will return. Pizza is very good, atmosphere cozy and staff very friendly! I feel that they appreciate the business I bring to the establishment.

I'll try and be brief and to the point. My wife and I and one of our daughters visited for the first time last night. We thought we'd keep it simple. We ordered salads which were fresh and plentiful. As for pizza, our daughter ordered a slice of cheese and we ordered an 18" Old World. Pretty simple. What we got seemed more like the idea of a pizza. The pizza itself was lighter than air, not a good sign and the crust was stiff and dry. I want that slice to droop! I want to have to fold that crust in my hand. I concur with some of the other reviewers. Gimme some grease! Give me my guilty pleasure! If this pizza hadn't been cut into slices I could have used it for a frizbee. The toppings were barely there. Yes I know , the Old World is basically a Margerita pizza with just mozzarella, tomatoes and/or sucace and basil. In this case there were NO tomato slices as the menu advertised. Just little splotches of sauce, which was tasty but few and far between, along with razor thin slices of mozz along and basil. Again, it just seemed like the idea of a pizza. Call it 'essence of pizza'. Sorry to report but, our daughter's slice of cheese pizza wasn't much better. We're no pizza snobs but, we know a lame pizza when we try one. I never write reviews like this so that ought to tell you something.
So, for three salads, one 18" pizza and three sodas we paid, with tip $61.00. Coulda gone to Pizza Perfect, paid about half the price and gotten the real deal.
We are totally glad Five Points Pizza has arrived. But, with what we got and what had to pay, I have to say it'll probably will be a while before we return. Make a REAL pizza and we'll run back and keep our money in the neighborhood.
This place is great. The Garlic knots are a must. Dont you dare come in and eat some pizza without ordering some garlic knots. The sweet tea is AMAZE-Balls.

This is how NY pizza is done in NY. You can buy slices or pies to eat there or to go. The slices are a bit bigger than the traditional NY Italian pizzeria, but I'm not complaining. Great atmosphere, the pizza is great for NY pizza outside of New York City and Long Island. Much better than other Midwestern places that try to emulate a New York pizzeria. Felt like I was back home on Long Island already. Try the garlic knots, they are amazing and generously sized with a bowl of dipping marinara sauce that is equally as delicious. Good beer selection too. The location did feel a bit out of place and the parking in the back sucks. Otherwise, it was worth the drive from Murfreesboro to start a night in Nashville. I found the fact that it's a NY style pizzeria that is named Five Points in an area of Nashville called Five Points, quite funny. I'll have to find a pizzeria in Five Points Brooklyn with the same name now when I visit home.

This is my son's favorite special pizza place when we are in East Nashville. It is totally amazing. We have never gotten a bad slice and we try to mix it up a little when we go. The atmosphere is great. We like to sit at the window and people watch as we eat.

Visiting Nashville from Austin, this place felt like home! 

There was a short wait, so we grabbed a seat at the bar. The bartender was very knowledgable about all the beers and gave lots of samples! 

The service was friendly and fast. The pizza was wonderful! I had a slice of the vodka sauce pizza minus the meat- it was so good. 

I would go back for sure- friendly staff, awesome pizza and beer- how can you go wrong?

the service is really good here and the inside is really clean.  
I would come here late nights with some people from my church and the employees were always courteous and friendly.   
i know sometimes you can get cranky mickie d employees, but it is not the case here :)

the only annoying thing about this place is turning a left out of the restaurant -_- stupid ridge pike.

Best pizza I've had and I'm from the Chicago area.. that has to say something. Lol got the meatball pizza and everything tasted super fresh. I went around 12am so it was only a 15 minute wait. Great prices too! I'll definitely be back if I'm in the area again.
Worth the wait. The vodka pizza was fantastic. The crust is perfect. Great service. Nice beer selection. The T-Rex was great. The capicola on it was so tasty.

I love finding more great places for a great meal in Nashville. One thing I love about my family is that we're generally all game for exploring and giving a new place a try. Last night was no different.

First we started off with ice-cream at Pied Piper Creamery before dinner (because you know that just can't be done #notarule @EscapeAdulthood) but ended up staying around in East Nashville looking for a new place to try.

We saw a few different people walking by us with pizza boxes and pizza started to sound better and better. We quickly pulled up Yelp on my phone and found Five Points Pizza was just around the corner.

Based on the 45 minute expected wait it looked like this was going to be a pretty good place for picking up some pie! Expectations not disappointed!

Sometimes pizza for my family can be a challenge. You see I'm adventurous and like to get some pretty interesting combinations, my wife can be a little adventurous and my kids usually prefer just a plain slice of cheese or pepperoni pizza. Five Points didn't disappoint because they offer NY style pizza by the slice or you can order some great specialty pizzas in a 14" or 18" size.

My wife decided on the South Brooklyn (The Old World with an olive oil base, a full layer of pizza sauce, and basil baked in (no shredded mozzarella), my daughter got a single cheese slice (but wanted a 2nd before we left!), my son got a single pepperoni slice and I went with a slice of Meatball Pie (Fresh and shredded mozzarella, thinly sliced meatballs, red onions, garlic) and I believe a slice of Caprese (Sliced heirloom tomatoes, chopped basil, sweet house-made balsamic reduction, olive oil, fresh and shredded mozzarella (no tomato sauce) - but I think it also had some arugula and gargonzola cheese as well).

You see in addition to the cheese and pepperoni by-the-slice, they seem to also have a couple of different daily options available. I started with the Meatball and it was delicious, not sure why I'd never really thought about thin-slicing some meatballs and adding them to a pizza but it was fantastic. I was actually a little surprised when I tried my 2nd slice and decided I liked it even more.

We'll be adding this to our list of places to take friends and family when they visit and of course we'll be back again ourselves soon. I've definitely got to go back and try the Habanero Cream Sauce Pie! (House-made habanero cream sauce, bacon, oven-roasted grape tomatoes, red onions, roasted garlic, fresh basil, fresh and shredded mozzarella (no tomato sauce))

A quick word on price, the individual slices of cheese and pepperoni were less than $4 each and were huge slices of pizza. My two specialty slices were both less than $5 each. So, overall some really tasty pizza for a great price.

Note: ingredient descriptions in parenthesis taken directly from their website

Lion's Choice is a fast food chain exclusive to St. Louis, and is always worth a visit whenever you happen to be in town. Their roast beef sandwiches are to die for, same with their cheap dip cones (like 30 cents for a small cone) and their fries. The interiors aren't really any different from most fast food restaurants, and the service is the same as well. It is still my favorite fast food chains in existence. I could eat here all day.


Interior- 2.5/5
Food- 4.5/5
Service- 3.5/5
OVERALL- 4/5

This was my first experience to Nashville food. I arrived at 11pm to my brother's house and we were hungry, he explained that Nashville is not like Miami and that most restaurants close early around 10. I told him it did not matter what was available so he brought us to Five Points Pizza. I must say that this is really good NY style pizza. One of the better one's that I have had. I have my go to NY pizza place in Miami but this one is kn par to it and might have a slight edge because the dough is cooked better here.

I can't believe I've lived in Nashville for 26 years and have never tried the magic that is Five Points Pizza. Talk about hitting the spot after having a few drinks at a nearby brewery! We got a slice each, which is all you need to have a savory pizza experience. Clearly the joint is popular, as the main restaurant was pack to the brim. We walked over next door and discovered a 'to-go' area where you can also buy by slice. This place brought back lots of delicious New York-pie style memories -- authentic and flavorful. Thank goodness we only stuck with a slice, not that I would have been ashamed to walk the streets of East Nashville donning a major food baby. So good. So tasty. Get thee to Five Points.

Possibly the best pizza we've ever had. they serve beer here too. If you don't get an order of garlic knots you should dump your drink down your pants. There are only 4 different pies to choose from which was nice. Plain, pepperoni and 2 specials they chafe up daily.
Really enjoyed the pizza. Just note If you want to check this place out, you'll probably have to wait. It's always packed! Def a good place if you're visiting Nashville and staying in the east side.

Here visiting from Texas. Rented a VRBO in east Nashville. Every time we passed this place it was packed. We tried the pizza last night for dinner. It was one of the best pizzas I have ever had. My husband (who doesn't eat pizza) loves it as well. If you are in Nashville you should give it a try.

Pizza is not very good or special. The atmosphere and service are good, however the pizza is extremely overpriced for what it is; a standard ny slice. Don't come in expecting anything out of the ordinary.

Food was great! Great prices! Caesar salad tasted fresh. Pizza was very crisp yet doughy. The toppings tasted clean and fresh. The bear selection was good. Customer service was good. Would I eat here again? Fuck ya! 
Just between us I would recommend this place to anyone who loves pizza and beer and I plan on going back again. 

Now that I have been here three times in one week, I would like to say that each time I have not been disappointed. I am in love with the Cesar salad. I crave that shit. I am stuck on the General's pizza. It is so good! I swear that this has got to be one of the best pizza places I love. 

I just want to say that service can be a little slow but that is due to how busy it can get. So can't hate on them for being so popular. Also if you are looking for cheap pizza then go to little Caesar's with their cardboard crust. You get what you pay for and with the blind onion you get damn good food.
Quick lunch place, so yummy. Hubby loves pizza, so we always like to check out good local pizza joints in different cities. I am so hungry just by looking at my pictures again.
Two words: Vodka pizza. It's so flippin' good! Also, their late night pizza window is perfect for a later night snack. Also, get the garlic knots... You won't be disappointed. Delicious!

My girlfriend and I go here about once every two weeks and get "The Generals" pizza. 

It's very good, and I do enjoy it.  I will also buy it again. 

But the wait is long, and last time we went, we ordered a pizza to go.  After we waited about 40 minutes, I asked them if it was ready.  Our pizza ended up sitting on top of the oven for over 20 minutes while we were just waiting on it.  The individual who took our order must have just passed it off like someone else would have taken care of it.

Sorry, but only 3 stars because the service aspect ruins the operations.

I burst through the doors with two active preschoolers in tow.  My son makes a break for it, charges toward the shelves, and grazes a bottle of Scalptherapie Anti-dandruff Shampoo.  I readjust the display, look up, and am met with dead-eyed stares.  I get it.  We're a customer service nightmare.  But seriously...for a four-year-old girl, getting a haircut is just a notch below Disneyland.  A little faux enthusiasm would be appreciated.

I immediately reassure the staff that my son's styling needs would be taken care of at home via a two-man operation involving a Flowbee, and that my daughter - who follows directions well - is thrilled to be having her bangs trimmed.  Someone draws the short straw, and leads my little angel to a chair.

We don't have to wait, which is awesome, and the process itself is efficient and uneventful.  The male stylist doesn't say two words to my daughter, but she doesn't seem to care.  She's grinning from ear to ear.  In her mind, she's a choppy-banged version of Princess Elsa.

"Lollipops for the kids?"  "Sure, I'll take one for my daughter."  "What about your son?"  "He's on a special diet."  "That doesn't seem fair.  He looks sad!!!" I glance dubiously at my son, who's still obliviously eyeing the Biolage rack, wondering when he can make his next move. "No...really...he can't...he has allergies."  And with that, I herd my brood through the door. 

Sure our experience was underwhelming...but for the price?  $6 (plus tip) can't be beat.  We'll be back!

What isn't there to love about Five Points? Local Neighborhood restaurant with very tasty pizza! What makes it for me is those garlic knots. If I crave something and my mouth waters any time I think of them, you know they are doing something majorly right. 

I also love that it's family friendly too. We have a daughter and enjoy that there are more and more places in East Nashville that we can take her. 

In the words of Tina Fey, "go to here." :)

I'll start by saying we love five points pizza and they have usually been good to us, but tonight we experienced horrible custom service . When my husband went to pick up our pizza he went a little early and checked in and they told him to wait. He ended up waiting 30 minutes past when they said it would be ready only to check in on it and our pizza had been sitting there for 20 minutes without anyone letting him know. He was obviously miffed but they made no effort to apologize or make it right in any way. So disappointing.

If for any reason you are in Nashville you HAVE to eat here.  This place is amazing!!  We tried the cheese slice, a pepperoni slice with basil and a veggie stromboli.  This place is legit.  Service is fast, every employee works with a purpose.  It's a joy to see an establishment put such a high priority on service.

It was so good we went back the next day.  We contemplated going back the 3rd day.

The pizza was amazing. We ordered the garlic knots and they are great, a house salad which was very fresh and plenty for my husband and me, and a 14" TRex the crust, sauce, cheese and meat were perfect. This is not really an eat in restaurant and parking is limited in the area so call your order in and go get it, the staff was great.
Great pizza!! Ran in really quick to grab a slice. Grabbed pepperoni slices. Had great flavor. Very close to NY style! Definitely will be back for another late night slice.

Great place to grab a couple of slices over in East Nashville. Have been coming here since they opened and have yet to have a slice I didn't like. The main part of the restaurant can get busy, so there can be a little bit of a wait. But they have solved that issue with the new addition, making it really easy to pop in for a quick bite, or to take it to go. Great spot in 5 Points!

I just moved to Nashville and was excited to try this place and I was not disappointed! The garlic knots were delicious and it's a great hangout place too (sat at the bar while I waited for my to-go order and service was fast and friendly). The pizza (I had the Brooklyn pie) was some of the best I've tasted (and very New York authentic) - can't wait to take friends and family there because I've been raving about it ever since my first visit!

I ordered my own individual "super slice" and I wasn't that impressed. I've been to Blind Onion a few times before and their pizza has always been excellent. This time, the crust in the middle was thin and acted like a cracker when bitten into. For awhile, I didn't even know what to do when I came in. The two girls working the counter never told me that I had to sit somewhere and wait for a server (the couple of times before you ordered at the front and the pizza was brought to you). However, it was fairly priced and relatively quick.

We love pizza and we love The Blind Onion, but the service we had today just doesn't make the price worth it. It took 45 minutes for our server to get our drinks and take our order. She was rushed (even though it was a slow lunchtime hour) and she wasn't friendly. I watched as the other server picked up the slack at her other tables.

Wonderful Garlic Knots, their signature item!!!  Worth returning to just for that.  Their pizza's a 4-star quality, nice selection, fresh ingrediants.  It's their Garlic Knots quality that pushes them up to a five-star selection.  

Have gone 3 times in the past 5 weeks, and the knots are just as great as ever.

Was recommended by a very valuable source. Very good pizza. Went in around 4 pm on a Monday and everything was super quick and very yummy. There were a lot of people inside, but still very quick. Had the pepperoni pizza and the garlic knots. Worth stoping by!

Super huge slices of yummy pizza! After a long, 14ish hour day of work, I was hungry, but it was around 11pm and I knew I might be limited on choices for food at that hour. I Yelped places that were open and pizza by the slice sounded perfect - quick, cheap, and satisfying. This place is open late, has a walk up window after a certain hour. I ordered a slice of veggie pizza "on a plate" to eat right away and a slice of cheese to go (which was just pizza "on a plate", in a paper bag). The crust was thin and crispy; perfectly toasted for the perfect amount of crunch. I ate the slice of cheese cold the next day and it was still delicious. I would definitely go back here!

This is one of the top three pizza places in Nashville and the BEST pizzeria in East Nashville. They have a vegetarian and non-vegetarian special everyday. You can either enjoy a whole pie in the restaurant, where they also have a decent tap selection, or you can order by the slice next door. Also, they are open late which comes in handy if you are pub crawling through 5 points.

We go there when we want that "special pizza". 
Quality is really good. People are friendly.
Sometimes the wait is a bit longer than the "pizza chains", but that's OK. Worth the wait!
And try the honey when you get the pizza. It's great on their thick crust!

My friend and I were headed to Bridgestone Arena for a concert and rather than pay the over-priced cost of under-whelming food within the Arena or fight for a spot in a restaurant in the tourist trap that is lower Broadway we decided to stop at a top-rated spot we've yet to try in Nashville which led us to Five Points Pizza which has the reputation of being the best pizza place in Nashville. I double-checked to ensure they have their own parking available so that we wouldn't be paying twice for parking in one night and saw that they (allegedly) did.

We got here pretty early for a dinner crowd (5pm) so getting a seat inside was absolutely no problem. However, the available parking is very, very limited and our server quickly let us know the neighboring businesses are tow-happy so my friend ran out to move his truck to another spot only to find none, but he found a neighborhood street to park in and was back relatively quickly. Anyway, long story short don't count on parking on-site no matter how early you get here but you'll find free parking within walking distance--now what's more important, let's move on to how good the food is, shall we?

I hadn't planned on ordering a beer but (a) I wasn't driving and (b) the beers on tap list here is pretty irresistible for any beer drinker. There was a nice mixture of IPA, stout, cider, ale, pilsner, etc. from the area and around the country. No prices listed so I just went with what I felt but the brews were ultimately fairly priced (not sure about any happy hour options). I started with a Left Hand Nitro Milk Stout which was creamy and delicious. We opted for a half order of garlic knots for the ridiculously low price of $4 and they were on our table in under 10 minutes--5 rather large knots dripping with delicious butter, oil and garlic with fresh marinara dipping sauce. I liked these almost more than I liked the forthcoming pizza.

For pizza--some interesting options but ultimately we opted for the "Zeus" for it's feta, pork, olives and oil. Thin, airy crust with a splash of sauce, an adequate serving of cheese, and plenty of toppings. Fold it over and chow down. And...it was pretty, pretty, pretty good. I was hyped for the "best ever" pizza and I can't say it was quite that though I hold out hope that one of these pies may fit that bill but it was certainly the best pizza I've eaten in some time since most has been from chain franchise joints.

Service was friendly, fast, and prices were economical.

Awesome Pizza! We were driving by after a concert and flipped around when we saw a line of people at the take out window...I ordered the Prosciutto  and Basil slice, my friend ordered the Pepperoni slice. We ate it while asking for directions back to our hotel. We did make it back to Five Points on Sat afternoon  and sat inside..it's small but I tell you it's worth it. Order the Garlic Knots...delicious!

WHAT DO YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT THIS PLACE:

1.  It's 50/50. First time my roomie brought it home on a Friday night (30+ min. drive home BTW) and it was INCREDIBLE. I was OBSESSED and had to go back the NEXT WEEKEND MYSELF.  However, I went on a Saturday laaaaate afternoon to take home for dinner with the hubs, NOT NEAR AS GOOD. WHYYYYYY. WHY IS THIS PLACE HIT OR MISS???!

2.  YOU NEED TO KNOW that you'll likely pay for parking just to walk across the street to pick up your pie. Add $5 (minimum) to the cost of the pizza, b/c that's going to be pretty standard.
The traffic flow is super obnoxious so be prepared and plan accordingly.

3.  YOU DEF NEED TO KNOW their garlic knots are RIDICULOUSLY AH-MAZING. There are literal chunks of garlic on them. MY DREAM, to die in a bathtub full of them while being the perfect amount of full in a gluten comma drifting away dreaming about them. Pretty great, right?

4.  Pepperoni, it's good. I'm pretty picky about pizza meat. It's yummy here. 

5.  Overall make sure you drink water... all the salt is enough to have you begging for cold fresh water, overnight and through the next day, especially when you eat the leftovers.

6.  Leftovers. The pizza is amazing leftover, the garlic knots, not near as good as the pizza... you know what that means?  Eat all the garlic knots and you can finish off the pizza the NEXT DAY.

7.  YOU DEF NEED TO KNOW if you go on a Saturday and go in for pick up etc. It's slamming busy, probably all the seats are taken, and you'll likely have a long wait in line just to pick up and pay for your to-go pizza.  Insanity.

Overall, I'm not SOLD on this place. I'm a girl that likes consistency ya'know?
Please me every time I eat your food, and I'm forever yours.
Jury is still out on Five Points Pizza.

My boyfriend and I love pizza.  Its not something we take lightly.  Having said that, this place has the potential to be the best in town. 

We LOVE their pizza.  You want fresh pizza made with care and an eye for ingredients?  You really cant do better in Reno/Sparks.  The dough is fluffy and perfect.  The sauces are amazing.  The veggies are fresh and crisp, and all of the ingredients, married up with their sauces, work perfectly.

That being said, this place needs......tweaking.  Three words:  UNIFORMS, SERVICE, PROFESSIONALISM. Most employees are walking around like they just left class from the high school down the street.  There is no differenciating who an employee is or who a customer is.  Uniformity would really add to the cohesiveness.  This place isn't a small joint on Victorian anymore.  Its a chain, and recognized as one.  Start showing the professionalism...

Next:  SERVICE, SERVICE, SERVICE.  We've never been okay with sitting at a bar and waiting 20 minutes with an empty couple of glasses in front of us.  If you are in the area, scope out your bar.  Notice.  Its not that hard on a Monday when its totally dead. Be PROFESSIONAL.   If you work here, let the other employees serve you.  Don't show up, off shift, looking like a gang banger and walk behind the bar and fill your own drinks.  It looks VERY tacky and incredibly unrefined.   We like dive bars in this city, but we don't expect this place to be one of them. 

This place has MOUNDS of potential.  The food is literally incredible.  Imagine how amazing the PLACE would be if it compared....

Really enjoyed the food here. My parents and I got the Zues pizza and the garlic knots and can I just say OMG. Delicious.  I love the garlic knots so much I wanted to eat them all right then and there. The pizza was huge and the slices where big I love that and the pizza itself tasted great. We took the left overs home for dinner. Just great food. Loved the inside of the place too. I wish it was a Tad bigger felt a little close and crowded but I loved it it was my first time ever being there and I left happy.
Last time we ate here we had the meatball pizza which was amazing. Going to try the meatball Stromboli this time and the garlic knots. Heard they where delish!!
Oh my damn!  The pizza is great..... I'm hooked

Great pizza and def my favorite place to go in Nashville! We usually go to the To Go area for a slice. My only complaint is the people that work on that side tend to be rude and pretentious, like we're inconveniencing them. Hopefully the owners can take note and have them go through some customer service training.

Awesome pizza! Freshly made dough, fresh ingredients and cooked in a brick oven. 

I had the vodka sauce pizza, which was amazing. The crust is thin so it's not super filling and you can eat more slices.

Seating inside is limited, but you can also go to the carryout side and order a pizza to go.  They also have a few pizzas pre-made to try by the slice and grab a seat at the counter.

Some of the best pizza I have ever had, and East Nashville neighborhood is an added bonus. Easy five star rating!

For Nashville, this pizza is very good. I wasn't expecting anything special especially because I'm from the New York area, but this impressed me. Very cool atmosphere and the service and staff were more than exceptional. Definitely the best slice Nashville can offer.

Lives up to the hype! Great pizza, even better garlic knots. The waiter was super friendly and fast to greet us and take our order.  I loved that we were able to wait at the bar down the street and have a beer and then the hostess called me when the table was ready.  Just a great experience all around.

Always great food but awful and I mean awful service. This staff doesn't care how long you have waited or if they forgot to make something. I would've asked for the manager but based on these reviews I didn't bother. It is very apparent that the staff who runs this location has no food/customer service experience. I recommend going to one of the other Blind Onion locations. I will continue to go to the others even though I live close to the Los Altos location. (By the way don't bother asking the young man with the grey flat bill hat about the service because he has less experience than a wal mart greeter and made a joke about the fact my pizza was burnt and forgot to make my salad) 

Please go to a different location!

When I arrived on a Friday night the place was completely packed; there were absolutely no tables!  Luckily I spotted a space at the bar and quickly filled the only available spot.  The menus are in the front of the restaurant and when I was ready to order I ordered with the bartender.  If I had been at a table I would have had to order at the register.

I settled on a side salad with Italian dressing for $4.00, their pesto chips for $6.75, and their medium chicken Parmesan pizza which consists of Fred's red sauce, mozzarella, chicken breast, Parmesan, and fresh herbs for $16.75.  I also asked to add Spinach onto it but never ended up getting it.  Good news is they comped two beers and a wine to make up for the mishap.

The only problem that occurred happened at the end of the meal.  I had requested a wine which the bartender said he was going to get but then I never received one until I had to ask another bartender; the first guy had completely disappeared! The place had started to clear out by the time I'd finished eating and it still took forever to get my check.  The 2nd bartender spent most of her time talking to another employee sitting at the bar drinking; I assume at this point the employee was off duty.  Then when I got my check not all the drinks that were supposed to be comped were off the bill and it took a good 10 to 15 minutes to get the bartenders attention in order to have the check changed.  It took another 10 minutes to get my card back.

All in all I would say Blind Onion on Los Altos has terrific food but it is obvious they have some major kinks to work out with their timing and follow up.  I recommend waiting to go here until they work those kinks out and even then give yourself a lot of time to eat there as it takes a while.

If you want to read more about this or other restaurant in Reno/Sparks visit my blog at: http://jparkhurst07.wordpress.com/

Today I went outside of the. Box and rocked a Stromboli for the very first time. I will say that it is a challenge to complete the action of eating it all alone, however I pulled it off barely. The service was great as I sat at the bar and enjoyed some wine on tap as well as  the welcoming atmosphere. I have always enjoyed this spot and feel very fortunate to live just .8 miles from this  awesome spot.....love it all!!

Shitload rooms, lie about bed size, bait and switch fees, Windows are thin so the highway noise is nonstop.  Only mold and a smell is missing from here to make this the worst place I have ever stayed at.

Food: 4
Service / Hospitality: 5
Atmosphere: 4

I first came here when the place first opened (which was super exciting because I'm a long time fan of Blackfish). While the food then was amazing, I had a less than perfect experience. The restaurant was exceedingly gracious and called to say the next meal would be on them. 

I came back for restaurant week, certainly not expecting them to remember something that happened 9 months ago. After sitting down, they said the meal was on them. I am incredibly impressed. A restaurant that cares that much about a single review written 9 months ago, and follows through on their word is one I respect and will develop loyalty to.

The food is pretty good - I had the ricotta gnudi and braised short rib. Certainly no complaints, although I admit not particularly memorable (and why I give them a 4). Actually, last time I was here, I enjoyed the food more. 
Overall it was a great experience, and I'm sure I will be back!
This place is great! Wish they'd kick the customer service up a bit though.

Eat here once a week! Pizza is practically a food group for me, and I have pretty high standards for my favorite pies. This place is the best!! I wish they delivered, but we usually use the favor app and just pay $5. Hot Hawaiian and South Brooklyn are my favorite pies. Garlic knots are a must, obviously.  Service is always decent. Great atmosphere and love that it is around the corner from my house.  Great NY style pizzas!
Hands down the best pizza place in Nashville. Best pizza, salads, stromboli ect..  The garlic knots are amazing! This is the only place that I've gone off my low carb diet for!

I do not get it, perhaps too old, very noisy, pizza nothing special, garlic knots are yummy.  A quick slice of pizza and a beer at the bar with some knots was $13 - good vfm but as I said too noisy and crowded - the 5 points mob just not for us.

Looking for excellent pizza and stromboli?  Look no longer.  This place is fantastic.   The Zeus stromboli is not to be missed.  The vegan pizaa was perfect.   Ask for Jake for service as good as the food!

Moving from NY, pizza means a lot to me. So I was suspect when we came across this place because so far the other pizza places in this state have been horrible. BUT here I must say the pizza is pretty good. We ordered a pie which wasn't bad but I would recommend ordering by the slice. Huge difference. By the slice is much better than ordering a pie. We sat at the bar so the server Cain, he was pretty cool told us some cool places to check out. Will be back here.

Nice place with an industrial feel.  The pizza was really good.  Not the best I've had (pizzalleys in St. Augustine, fl) but much better than most.  It was on the expensive side, $20 for a pepperoni an mushroom 18" pizza, but my husband and I had leftovers.  The crust is thin.  The cheese was very good.  It had a unique flavor to it.  The service was great!  Parking is limited but we found a parrell spot out front.

Cody was amazing to watch at the bar which was quite busy while we were there at lunch time on Friday.  He took care of all of his customers and was very personable.  He gave us a taste of draft that he thought we would like and was spot on.  The pizza special of the day was great and the house salad was filling.
Thanks for a great first experience in Nashville.

When I got into Nashville my Uber driver told me to try this place and I'm happy I did. If you like pizza then you have to try this place out. Everything about it was good from the crust to the cheese and sauce. I highly recommend it!

I think I got lucky in that this was my first slice in Nashville, wow.  It was better than I could have imagined.  I'm from the east coast originally and have a bias to pizza, it usually takes me awhile to find anything worthy when I move to a new city, this was found in my first week here.  Lucky me, I will be here often I'm sure.

Hey there yelpers!

So here's the thing about Five Points Pizza, the food is absolutely great and the service wasn't even that bad either, however... the wait time and claustrophobia-inducing atmosphere could most certainly use some work. The staff quoted us about 30 mins to wait but the pizza was ready in closer to 10 mins, so I must give them Kudos for that. However it's a very small place and it's almost always extremely busy due to its immense local popularity, understandable, but I feel they could do more to branch out and grow the building some.

So, when someone visits a restaurant they want to know (or should want to know) about all aspects of your visit and not just how the food is, hence. The wait staff was quite nice and rather attentive to us (we were a larger party of about 7 or 8 people) so it couldn't have been easy, but they certainly managed well. The pizza was massive and the slices were large, tasty, and greasy, all of which are traits a pizza should have.

I would definitely recommend this place to anyone who loves pizza as much as I do but not so much to someone who has issues with large crowds or small spaces. Patience is a plus, too.

Thanks and happy yelping!

Fast service, decent pizza (I'm a Chicago native so my standards are quite high!) and they gave the kids dough balls to play with, which was an unexpected treat. 

Our waitress was around a lot and helped quite a bit. She gave us a great dessert recommendation and told us about a local park for the kids too. 

Very nice place and more family friendly than expected!

My friends and I came here for restaurant week.  I ordered the Ricotta Gnudi, Amish Chicken, and Sour Cream Pannacotta. 
The Gnudi was DELICIOUS.  I was debating over this and the chick pea fritters, and while the chick pea fritters were good, I'm so glad I chose the gnudi.   The chicken dish was good as well but nothing "special".  The chicken was cooked well.  The added pumpernickel was good.  But just felt like an average chicken dish.  The sour cream pannacotta was good.  My friend did rave about the chocolate cake option. 
Overall, not bad. not great.

Great pizza!
Great garlic knots!
The staff? Slow and slower.
Oh well.... call ahead and get take out the pizza is yummy!
My absolute Favorit epizza place in town thus far. Beer list is solid as well and environment and location are great! Their garlic knots are ones you HAVE to order!

Five Points Pizza, I love you. We stopped in for a late night snack while staying in East Nashville. A guy had just gotten shot in the restaurant across the street, so police had the entire area taped off but our Uber driver dropped us off in the back alley - TOTALLY worth it. The pizza was awesome, huge thin-crust slices. I think it was $10 for 2 slices and they were both so big we had leftovers for breakfast. Super greasy, in a paper bag on paper plates kind of take out. Unfortunately we didn't make it back a second time during our visit but I will absolutely seek it out if I'm ever back in town! They have specialty slices (1 or 2 per day) as well as cheese and pepperoni. You can also dine in or order full pizzas for takeout, but their walkup window/takeout side was awesome!

We ate here Wednesday evening and had a one hour wait to be seated. We chose to dine in, but there is faster service if you want carry out. But believe it or not the one hour wait was worth it. The pizza was outstanding. We ordered the Super Bianco, see attached picture of our pizza.  The crust is outstanding and the ricotta cheese was a great touch. The price is certainly reasonable and the service was great.We also ordered some garlic knots, which came with marinara sauce and those were wonderful, be careful not to fill up on them before the main pizza.  we did not order any beer, but it looks like everybody had a beer.
Classic pizza restaurant. Cheap but very good, and fast! The atmosphere is also really cool if you wanna sit down instead of take out
We absolutely love the new Blind Onion out in Sparks at the Galleria. Great sandwiches, good house wine, and awesome beers on tap. Everyone is friendly and it is always busy. What a great place!

Super fresh and delicious pizza. I love that I can get it by the slice here. Their garlic knots are to die for. It's always extremely busy if you dine-in so we typically use the pickup window. If you do eat in, they have local craft beer to pair with your pizza as well!

Got take out from here our first night in Nashville after a long flight. The pizzas were huge and delicious. I got a plain cheese and it was on the money. The rest of he family got the a variety and no complaints.

Truly a deserving name. Our air bnb was only a couple of minutes away from here and we came after a late night of hiking and walking through the beauties of Chattanooga, TN. This pizza hit EVERY spot. We got the Southern Brooklyn, the vodka pie and the Spinach Gorgonzola which was by far my favorite. The salty Gorgonzola balanced with the spinach and mushroom was absolutely mouth watering. The crust is cooked to perfection, the mix of toppings and flavors was incredible. Lots of vegetarian friendly options and a lot of variety for picky eaters. Also a plus, for any pizza that is topped with fresh basil, they give you chopped basil on the side for freshness! I mean...I'm trying to go again before I leave Nashville! (andddd I'm here on a bachelorett party)
Went there and had a couple slices. They were fantastic. Some of the best pizza slices I've ever had and I'm from Chicago

We ordered a double bacon smoke house burger. There were absolutely NO fried onions and a small SINGLE piece of bacon on it. In addition, we tried to obtain bbq sauce at the window while picking up the food. We were informed it would be an additional 27 cents per packet for condiments. This is an outrage. No other fast food establishment charges for condiments. This is a major turnoff McDonalds. Needless to say, we were very disappointed in our experience today.
Super good! Happy hour is from 3-5, so a large 1 topping pizza is like 12 bucks! Great deal and awesome pizza.
This is a cool pizza joint with a good vibe.  Pizza was good and the cheese bread was awsome!  This was our first time there and when when we comeback to Reno, we will be back here!
Almost NY style but not quite.  Still, very good pizza with great beers and good service.  We all were very happy.
Took 20 minutes to take our order, sat there for amother hour before just leaving after waiter said "i dont know whats going on" definitly wont be back. Pizza isnt hard to make...
Holy yum! Best pizza I've had in Nashville so far and the garlic knots are top notch. I will definitely be visiting again even for a higher than I'd like to pay price.

I love this place. Service can sometimes be a bit "hit or miss" but honestly the superior taste and quality of food makes this place a huge hit. Being from New York, pizza is in my soul and this place knows how it's done. I also am a huge fan of their support of the local Nashville beers they have in stock and on draft. I sometimes wish they would make other New York pizzeria classics but then I realize that it would take the focus of what is so great about these guys, the pizza. Very chill and great place. Five Points Pizza is certainly a staple to all those trying to experience the Nashville food scene.

I really love that this place is open late because I till late at night and sometimes a pizza just sounds really good! I also love the portions when buying here because it is really big. I personally just like a plain cheese pizza, but my boyfriend will try other topping combinations and I have yet to find one to complain about. Last week, we tried the garlic knots and I have to say those are really good too!!!

I agree with the other reviewer, get a room that doesn't face the highway.

I come to NJ 3-4x a year to visit grandchildren. We used to stay here but their prices have gone up quite a bit in the recent year or two. But anyway, they have decent room accommodations and a nice hot breakfast. If you have kids, they have an indoor pool.

I lived here about 5 years ago. Maybe it was six. Idk. But I actually lived in the pizza parlor. Got my haircut as well. I'd say they have food and beers. It's not really a place for food but a great place to walk and dog the dog out before the rains hits. I wouldn't bank on having a good time either. They don't really serve you but judge you because well, it's Five Points Puzza. So I'd say skip it. You're welcome. Buh bye
This place has been decent but it has taken a turn for the worse, save your money and eat at Little Cesars at least their pizza isn't cold on the top.
Great pizza! Every dish is very flavorful. Fast service and the waitors are super nice and attentive. Reasonable prices and big portion sizes!

I'm not a big fan of pizza, but I am a fan of Five Points Pizza, especially their meatball pizza.  There are a lot of good beers on tap.  Their quarters are a little tight, but the servers are friendly.  The only thing I don't like about them is that 3 slices of pizza pretty much cost the same as a whole pizza.  They are expensive.  If you like thin crust pizza and fresh ingredients then it's definitely worth it!
You want classic NY style pizza in Nashville, here you go. Nice local beer selection.

We have been waiting patiently for the restaurant to open after we found out that it was going to be another one of Chip Roman's restaurants. We finally had a chance to go in for a quick bite last night and it was as delicious as expected. We had the gnocchi and beef short ribs. For dessert, we had the rhubarb & strawberry with coconut mousse. Everything was cooked to perfection and service was amicable. The restaurant had a very nice ambience. Would have stayed longer for a few more drinks but was exhausted after a long week. Will definitely return. Highly recommended and you will not be disappointed!

The Treemont is Chef Chip Roman's 4th fine dining restaurant in the Philly area (preceded by Blackfish, Mica, and Ela, all of which are standouts, and not to forget Tradestone Cafe)...

We went to the Friends & Family* opening on Sunday April 13th, but it was identical to what will be the opening menu for the public tomorrow on Monday April 14th.  I'll write up more details (see photos), but sufficed to say it was fantastic.  Particularly like the Foie Gras, and the melt-in-your-mouth veal tenderloin.

It is also one of the most attractive restaurants in Philly.

An interesting crowd was in attendance: Kevin Sbraga and his wife & kids, Drew Lazor, Jessie from Sbraga, Shola Olunloyo, Chip's wife and her girlfriend had the window seat, some regulars like Jeremy and Shelley that I recognized from Blackfish/Mica...

Note, in addition to the dining hours listed on this page, the bar is open 4:30PM-1:00AM, 7 days a week.  Small bar, but the cocktails were excellent.  They should do a good business being so close to the Academy of Music/Kimmel Center.

More background information:

http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/the-insider/Blackfishs-Chip-Roman-opening-The-Treemont-in-Center-City.html

*This was a "Friends & Family" event, so everything was complementary, except the tip.

I absolutely hate pizza...I mean I hate everything about it.  I always tell my fiancee that I have had pizza that actually tasted good twice, once in Chicago and once in Italy.  Yes, Italy.  But, at Five Points Pizza I have been awakened to the joy of pizza.  Five Points is a delicious, crisp, dripping slice of wonderment that I try to frequent every time I'm in the area.  You can't get a better deal than a $5.00 slice at the window.  You walk up, order your a REAL hot slice of pizza and sit down on the curb to enjoy each cheesy, veggie bite.  This place is in a great location and emits an atmosphere of unique, creative spirit married with good food.  I have definitely become a regular of Five Points Pizza and would recommend it as the essential pizza place in Nashville.

The pizza I got was the  carnivore pizza and is great but the service was ridiculous. i was the only customer in there and stood waiting while some guy stood there talking on the phone talking to his friend. I mean is hard to hold the phone call real quick, don't you want my business? thought it was good pizza.  I won't be back to eat in the restaurant I'll go for carryout.  2 stars cause bad service. Pizza gets a 4!

The pizza here is yummy. Large thin slices.. I got a pepperoni slice.. my love got the prosciutto (however you spell it lol) and basil.. we both loved it. Very greasy but that's too be expected.. I saw the guys making the dough fresh, which was cool.

I was nervous because I heard that they had terrible service here, but I did not have such an experience.  It was lunch and it wasn't too busy, but not dead either.  We were thinking of splitting a small pizza but couldn't totally agree on toppings and the nice guy at the counter said why don't you do the lunch special.  Two pieces of a large pizza and a drink.  SOLD!!  I went with the General and my lunch buddy went with pepperoni.  I also should admit pizza is not my favorite thing to eat.  Sometimes it can actually make me feel sick to my stomach if it is too doughy.  I mean doughy as in raw texture of the dough.  I am weird what can I say.  I will eat it if I must and it was my buddy's turn to pick.  I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of food they make at The Blind Onion.  The crust was cooked very well and on it's own had good flavor.  The pizza had a good balance of ingredients.  I really enjoyed all the toppings and I actually ate both pieces (gym here I come).  The sauce didn't have that tomato paste flavor some places have and it wasn't too spicy.  I had just enough flavor and I think it helped make the pizza sing.  It sang That's Amore if you must know.  The decor is fun and I like how they have all the extras you can add in old 6 pack containers.  They staff actually showed us those so we wouldn't forget and the girl brought the gigantic thing of honey and a side plate to pour some out on to.  I will most definitely add this to pizza joints that I actually like the pizza from.

I'd probably go with a 2.5 star, but I'll give the benefit of the doubt. Pretty standard location and what you'd expect. I think it's had it's hits and misses, but nothing out of the ordinary. I'll typically make a quick stop after heading home from a game and need a quick bite. Sometimes the food is hot and fresh, occasionally a not-as-fresh item. Usually the drive thru is ok, but I've had the occasional long wait (10-15 min) with only one or two cars ahead of me.
Great thin crust pizza. Hot and crisp, sauce is perfect. Best value in town. Two large slices and a drink for $8.

Best Nashville pizza! What's also awesome about this place is that they have a walk up window to order from outside.  Even though there is a line the wait is worth it, and the line moves pretty quickly.  I made the mistake of sharing a slice of pizza with a friend, so even if your not that hungry get your own slice or whole pizza, its worth every bite!
Great new addition to center city. Very nice winds list. Creative menu. Loved the skate wing, char grilled calamari and escargot. Definitely will return!

We hired Acoma Roofing to repair a leak in our upstairs bedroom two years ago. We received a free estimate for the repair. They do the repairs on a time and material basis. They gave us a cost range. The two men who came out to repair the roof were very courteous and professional. They knocked on the door before starting and again when they were done. The clean up was awesome. Our bill came out under the estimated cost. We used them again this year for a leak in our garage. The estimate came in right in the range quoted. We are very happy with service we received and have recommended them many times to our friends and neighbors.

Delicious New York style pizza and good salads with friendly and accommodating staff who treat their guests with respect! The server delivered us the wrong size pizza and more than made up for it by giving us a second small pizza to go on the house :)

This place seriously knows how to do pizza. Personally, I'm not a huge pizza fan. So un-American, I know. But I could seriously eat here more than frequently. We did get here around 7:30 on a Friday for a group of 4. We're pretty patient people and prepared to wait. By that, I mean we went across the street and had drinks until our table was ready. I like that they call you when the table is ready. We still had drinks and asked if 5 more minutes was acceptable, and they were totally fine with it. I mean, they're already starting off awesome simply by being cool. 

We started off with beer, I had the Yazoo pale ale. Typical choice. My boyfriend had something I can't pronounce. Delicious choice. We started off with garlic knots. I don't even know how to describe the level of yum! I mean, there's dough... Amd it's covered in garlic, fresh basil, Annnnd of guess olive oil. I didn't even need the marinara offered. Pizza... I have a deep love for fresh mozzarella and most places don't do it, but FIVE POINTS DOES! I was extremely stoked about it! The crust, perfect. The sauce, perfect. Overall, an amazing blend of perfection.

Seriously the best pizza I have ever tasted in my entire life!!! The crust is thin with just a slight crunch and you can taste the freshness in every ingredient they use. Not much selection but when you pick out a slice they warm it up for you. Wish they had more seating.

A rude young African American girl gave me tude bc I had to ask her to remake a child size ice cream cone. Her corny dude conworker laughed at me for making the request. I don't understand how they don't understand what a child size ice cream cone is compared to a huge adult sized one. Behavior was rude from both.

Got a Stromboli and it was delicious. It was big enough for 2 people unless you're very hungry.
The crust is soft and chewy. The filing (Zeus Stromboli) was plentiful of spicy capicola, bananas peppers, feta, olives,and pepperoni.
The side of marinara sauce is also good.
Looking forward to going back and having the pizza before we leave Nashville. 
The restaurant is on one side the other side a separate area for take out orders. A great set up to handle the crowds. One can order ahead for pickup or order on site for take out. Will definitely come back.

Heavenly Deliciousness. 

That is Lions Choice all summed up into two words. 

Roast Beef Sandwich. 

In my refrigerator. 

In the cafeteria. 

Not so special 

Do I love it?

Not so much. 

Roast Beef Sandwich. 

Lions Choice. 

Heavenly. 

Deliciousness. 

Do I love it?

Oh Yes. 

I am not sure how they did it...or what is in the seasoning....or how I could possible love a sandwich that is void of cheese and mayo.

And the best part you ask?

When you skip the butter, this little slice of heaven rakes in at only 284 Calories. 

Good for my skinny jeans and my taste buds. 

Heavenly Deliciousness indeed!!!!

Not sure whats causing the lower reviews.  Every trip here for me has been great.  Good service at a table or bar.  
Pizza has been great Every.Single.Visit.  
Employees have been friendly and accommodating each  time.  
The beer selection is quite good and its nice to have a comfortable bar atmosphere in this part of town.  

Spanish Springs is a better place having Blind Onion in the neighborhood.
Sue is a treasure. Have been using her service for about 15 years. I can go on vacation with total confidence knowing that my pets and home will be secure and healthy when I get home. Thank you sue.

Fast friendly service, packed at 6:45. The garlic knots are huge, that is half order in my pic.  I'm had the zues Stromboli. Nice dough, fresh flavorful fillings.  The marinara sauce is not to sweet. Great beer selection.

So let me preface this by saying that while I live in Nashville, I'm originally from NY and thus and super snooty/picky about my pizza. I was really worried about moving to the south and still being able to find a good slice, and have definitely had a disappointing experience or two since moving here.

That being said, five points pizza is the BEST pizza I've had since moving to Nashville. It was super exciting for me to know I'll still be able to get good pizza here. Tried a variety of different toppings and they have pretty unique pies in terms of toppings offered. If you're looking for a good slice or are very picky about your pizza like me, I'd definitely give them a try.

I recently attended a Nashville Food Bloggers event here. The owners were nice enough to close off the right hand side of the building and bring out pizza upon pizza for us to try. I tried the cheese (amazing), pepperoni (amazing) and a pepperoni, black olive, red onion and I think feta pizza (amazing and my fav). 

The staff was SUPER friendly and gave kitchen tours and even let us try to spin the dough with a rubber one they practice with. 

I love the decor and finishing of the restaurant. The left side has chairs and a bar and the right has some stools and counters. They even have a neat little walk up window if you want to get a slice on the go. I didn't look at the prices of the pizza, but I'd expect them to be reasonable. 

My only grips are about parking and price of the keg wine. I know parking in East Nashville is always a pain, but the night we went we had to park a few blocks away and walk. On the way back to the car I was thing it was all for the best because of the amount of pizza I ate. 

Secondly, the keg wine. As you're aware, I was at a special event and we were offered free pizza and half off beer on draft and keg wine. They have a butternut (white) and a troublemaker (red). I got the troublemaker and it came in a cute (small) little carafe with a glass on top. It was nice. It cost me $4.37, so full price would be $8.75. That seems a little pricey for a keg wine in a small glass.

Fresh and always good. Never had bad pizza from here. My absolute favorite is the South Brooklyn  (their version of a Margarita pizza, it's pictured.) I always order pick up, take it home and drizzle olive oil and sprinkle some fresh ground sea salt on it. Literally. The. Best.

This is the best pizza in town and the have a great selection of draft beers, many local.  The basil and prosciutto pizza is incredible.  If you go for lunch, definitely go for the 2 slice special with the drink. Quick, friendly service at the bar if you are in a hurry.

We tried this location after hearing several recommendations of The Blind Onion from friends. Maybe it's just this location at fault, but we had a pretty horrible experience. First of all, we ordered the bread stick appetizer to start since we here very hungry, but they didn't even bring it out until literally about 1 minute before our pizza. Second, I ordered a greek pizza which was supposed to come with Kalamata olives, artichoke hearts, red onions, and sun dried tomatoes, but what I received was a pizza with about 3 slivers of sun dried tomatoes, about 3 pieces of red onion, a decent amount of artichoke hearts (no complaints there), and absolutely no olives. It pretty much looked like a white-sauce cheese pizza, which is very disappointing when you pay the money for a specialty pizza. The pizza tasted "ok," crust is very pretty but on the plain side in terms of flavor. In terms of staff, our waitress was very pleasant and friendly, but 2 other girls who assisted with bringing our food were not very knowledgeable. Overall we were not very happy with our experience and won't be going back.
The basil prosciutto pizza is AMAZING! Takeout window is a life saver after a night out.

Sooooo good!!
The server didn't seem super personable, but he did bring dough for the kids to play with, so that was cool. His was nice though standoffish. Would 1000% recommend this place. 
Pro tip, just pay for the parking instead of parking in be convenient store lot, they WILL tow!
just tried the pizza at the sparks blind onion, it is great !!
Good pizza. Good Service. Good prices.  Did have a half Zeus and half Dave's.... very good. Had a beer flight and the City Wine... all good.  Small, quaint, in the neighborhood.

So, I'm one of the few people on the earth who really isn't a big fan of pizza.....UNTIL NOW.

I had no idea pizza could taste this amazing. It is absolutely unbelievable.  The four of us got a few random slices and shared them and I have never experienced anything quite like it. Aside from the overall taste, you will not find a more perfect thing crust in the world. 

If NY style pizza is your style, then this is your joint. Anytime in the future that I find myself in East Nashville, I will definitely be stopping by.

An inexpensive appetizer that is sooo delicious is the garlic knots.  They're happy to give extra dipping marinara sauce too.   I love that they have slices of the days- always 2 options-a vegetarian choice and a meat choice.  Great late night hours at the slice window!

This place has consistently good pizza and friendly staff. The TRex is my favorite (all the spicy Italian meats!). The garlic knots are pretty awesome, too. They keep a selection of draft beers and a couple of wines, which is nice, too. There's also a daily special menu that has inventive and tasty options. It's a small place, so don't go at the busiest times of day expecting to walk in with your party of eight and sit right down (I mention this only because I saw it happen and then heard the group complaining outside because they had to wait...). It's also super popular, so always ask how long it'll take for any carry out order you place. In general, this place is great and I highly recommend it.

I'm in town visiting some friends and we hopped over to Five Points Pizza after we wrapped trivia next door at Three Crow. The beers and pizza came out quite quick. Both categories have awesome selections. The pizza reminded me of NYC pizza. You can buy full pies or you can get one of their "daily" slices. I did the latter and ordered the veggie pizza and it was so yummy. Paired it with one of my favorite beers, Good People IPA. The server was super nice and efficient. My only note would be on the hostess- she looked annoyed that we wanted a table and barely made eye contact. Pretty much a cold shoulder. Everything else was so great though so five stars for Five Points Pizza!

We walked up to this place right at opening and were greeted with a big smile. The beer was cold and the pizza was delicious. I'm a simple man so I ordered pepperoni and cheese but I tell you that pizza was perfect in my eyes. Crunchy, cheesy and ohhhhh soooo tasty. Wash it all down with a cold Yazoo beer and this was a great stop.

Well, normally this place is a 4 or 5 star buuuut the last few times (3 to be exact) have been less than enjoyable. Two weeks ago we came and had very prompt service and got our order in. After that all hell broke loose, wrong order, kitchen messed up, kitchen forgot etc etc. Then comes tonight, we arrived and sat down to the left of the entrance in a booth/table, after about 15 minutes of no one acknowledging us we moved to another table and waiting yet another 15 minutes without so much as a we will be right there or anything so we decided to take our business somewhere else and left. We love the pizza and the atmosphere here but it seems like the service is on the decline.
Simple, straight forward menu. Good sized New York style slices for $3 bucks, fast and friendly service, great hours. Can't think of a better pizza place. I'm in love

Heard a lot of great thing about this place and it really lived up to everything! 

We called ahead to get our pie for pick up. I would recommend this if you're just looking to experience the pizza! It only took about 20 minutes! For to go orders you go to a small shop where you can order slices or whole pies. There is parking in the back but you have to pay (another reason why pick up is great, one person can stay in the car and another go in!) 

It was pretty packed in the shop when we picked up on a Saturday evening. The service was quick and really friendly as well! 

As for the pizza...I can barely explain it, it's just SO good! When I try to isolate the parts...the crust is pretty mediocre and the toppings aren't anything special the pizza is soooo above average! It maybe is the sauce?!? Really not sure but it's working!!! 

It's also pretty fairly priced about the average price for pizza!

Came here on a Saturday for dinner with some friends and it was amazing!  We only had to wait about 15 min which wasn't bad at all. We ordered the Old World and the Bianca pizzas and both were incredible! Would definitely return next time I'm in Nashville.
Absolute pleasure doing business with company! The owner is very honest with everything, he doesn't give you the run around!

Five Points Pizza is one of my absolute favorite stops. I will eat all pizza, but I will only truly enjoy certain pizza. This place is fun, casual, and DELICIOUS.

My girlfriend and I often stop in the grab and go side to get a couple slices and enjoy. The slices are the size of my face, so, at $3-5 a pop, it's still cheaper than going to dinner out. She almost always gets one of the specials and the basil-prosciutto pizza. I am a purist with my cheese pizza. The crust is thin, so you don't get bogged down with bread. It's not too greasy, either, and oh my gosh is it good.

The garlic knots are good, but SUPER garlicky. Be prepared to have garlic breath for the foreseeable future.

The real star here is the basil lemonade. "Basil... lemonade?," you say? Yes. Basil. Lemonade. It's amazing and refreshing; tart and sweet at the same time. I will drive to East Nashville just for the basil lemonade, it's that good. 

The service is always great. The line can get a bit long, but I've never waiting an outrageous amount of time for my pizza. The grab and go is connected to the main dining restaurant, so you can get over to the bar to get some basil lemonade to sip on in line. 

The only downfall is the limited seating in the grab and go side (hence the "go" part), but it makes you feel all the more accomplished when you grab some stools on a busy night.

I was encouraged to go to this pizza place by a hairdresser...and a book store employee...and a tour guide. Coming so highly recommended I had to go. It was pizza heaven. If I may, I'd quite like to adopt the pizza maker and bring him back to Florida with me. The pizza is fantastic. Pizza lovers!!!...flock my loves...flock to the perfect slice!

Yes! Come here if you're looking for a good NY style inspired thin crust pizza. Just the right amount of sauce and cheese. The salads are good too. Get a salad and add slice of cheese pizza can make a really good meal at around $10 budget. Friendly staff and quick turn around time. The togo order window us open till 3am, so another perfect place to pick up food for that late night munchie.

Thin slice goodness! 

Restaurant opens till 11PM/12PM! And they have window service till 1AM/3AM on the weekdays and weekend respectively! Perfect for those late bar hopping nights in East Nashville. The slices are large enough to satisfy those late night munchies or just to soak up the alcohol. Will cost you about $3-$5 per slice. My personal favorite is the Prosciutto and Basil. So good! The  guys who work behind the counter also have some of the manliest beards I've seen this side of East Nashville. 

Definitely check them out if you're looking for some late night pizza/snack!

Pretty good pizza. Glad to have a joint that serves pie by the slice. They have some very interesting daily combos. Today I tried spinach, mushroom, Gorgonzola...  Definitely worth your time. 

Sauce isn't that great but a decent slice. (Maybe a little biased with my NY ties)
Great food! The Bianca is my favorite! Staff is meh.
They have that "New York Style" pizza!!! HANDS DOWN!!! Some of the best pizza I ever tasted!!!

Lemme just say this: at the height of the busiest hour on a recent Friday night, my kids and I were unusually high maintenance (lemonade fell, asked for something to munch on while waiting etc) the staff didn't bat an eye lash. They smiled, hooked us up and then served us (as always) the best pizza we've ever had. 
5 Points is more than pizza. I wish it was its own country. We'd move there.

This was my first trip to East Nashville and I am glad this place was recommended to me.  I'm a pizza snob and this place did not disappoint. It was delicious pizza and a fun neighborhood experience. I would go back for sure.

They have a huge selection of "juices" and pricing is fair. I am fairly new to "vaping" and this was my first visit to this shop. I rated 2 stars because I was turned off by their credit card policy.  I purchased 6 bottles of juice and 2 tanks. My total was over $70. I paid, and realized I had forgotten to buy a lanyard for my vape pen, The gentleman handed me the lanyard and the total was around $7.50.  I began to swipe my card and he said " Oh sorry, we have a $10 minimum".  I literally JUST spent over $70 not even 2 minutes ago. The juice tastes great, but I doubt I will be going back.
So delicious. Hot cheese, fresh toppings, creative flavors, crispy crust--it's just EVERYTHING I want in a slice of pizza. It's probably a good thing I live 12 hours away!
OMG this place is a MUST when in Nashville. Have the garlic knots too. The rocket and the Gorgonzola spinach were great together!

The Blind Onion had a really nice atmosphere with a few eco-friendly touches. Their crust had a pretzel edge to be dipped in honey, ranch dressing or marinara. I tried bbq chicken. The sauce was full bodied leaning more towards sweet than smoky. The cheese was scant but the chicken was very well seasoned and tender. There were crunchy red onions and a generous sprinkling of fresh basil. The Hawaiian slice had chicken instead of ham by special request and cheese that was noticeable this time. The marinara was well balanced not too tart not too sweet. The third slice was chicken Alfredo.  The Alfredo sauce was creamy and garlicky and the chicken was consistently good.  The service was pleasant and efficient.  The atmosphere was good for families despite the bar. My favorite slice was the bbq chicken.

My husband and I came here for a late lunch, and were under a time constraint as we had tickets to a show. Without even being asked about timing, the server warned us that the Stromboli I ordered would take 20 minutes to cook. I really appreciated the thoughtfulness, and changed my order to a slice of the prosciutto basil pizza, which was insanely good. We also ordered the garlic knots, which you can order a half or whole order of. The server thoughtfully showed us what a half order looked like by pointing to another table's order, so we knew that a half order would be plenty for the two of us. it was all delicious and quick, not to mention very reasonably priced. One small warning: as I am writing this review hours after having gone there, I can attest to the terrible breathe that will follow the garlic knots, so if you eat them, make sure whoever is with you does too!

I am one of those weird Americans who doesn't want to eat pizza for every meal. I was the crazy kid who ordered spaghetti at Pizza Hut growing up. Now, married to a pizzaholic, I eat my fair share of pizza, and I have to say that Five Points Pizza is the best pizza joint in Nashville right now -- and that's a big honor coming from me, who usually doesn't like it if a pizza place doesn't offer a pasta counterpart.

I am a fan of New York-style pizza, and this is the closest thing we've got here in Music City. Being able to be seated immediately the handful of times I've been is a huge point (ahem, Mafiaoza's), and offering up pizza by the slice for those of us who are pretty much done after one or two pieces -- yes, please. Especially when you are also serving up cheap $5 garlic knots, basically greasy, carb-y, delicious hunks of bread to dunk in a sweet-salty marinara sauce. (And I do judge my pizza joints based on the sauce -- RIP, Da Vinci's.)  The pizza itself is big slices, on crust that's the perfect balance between thick and thin, served on paper plates, the kind you have to fold in half to eat. I usually get it by the slice -- once we got a whole pie, and the topping options are much better, but it gets a little pricey. The beer isn't cheap either, but they do have a good selection.

Go after 10 on a weeknight (not sure about happy hour on weekends) to get $5 for a slice and a beer. That's a better deal than you get from most food trucks around here.

So I didn't really understand the hype behind Five Points Pizza as I don't really think of Nashville as a 'pizza' town. My friends & I decided to check it out anyways and boy, were we pleasantly surprised by how fabulous the pizza was here! Crispy thin style with fresh & delicious toppings!

We tried the prosciutto basil that everyone was raving about... and NOW I see why. Seriously delicious - you need to order it if you come here, assuming you like basil of course! We also tried the Italian sausage which some of my friend's actually liked more than the prosciutto & basil but I thought they were both equally tasty and unique form each other. 

Prices were totally reasonable too especially considering how delicious and well done the pizza is! Definitely would come by again next time I'm in Nashville.

I have not had any sort of bad experience there before. Their pizza is phenomenal and the servers seem to really care about the food. We had one server recently at our table who described a pizza so intensely that we ended up ordering it when we wouldn't have ordered it to begin with and you could tell he genuinely cared. We were checked on regularly, drinks always full, great experience.

I highly recommend!

Lion's Choice is one of my favorite "Fast Food" spots.  I love this location, maybe because I remember coming here as a little girl.  

The roast beef sandwich is so good.  I dip my sandwich into BBQ sauce. The meat is thinly sliced and seasoned.  The roast beef is rare, if you want it well done just ask.  If you do not want the seasoning, just ask.  They accommodate all special requests (like extra seasoning for me).  One of the best parts of the sandwich is the butter steamed bun.  They steam the bun with butter for a few seconds before assembling the sandwich.  Fries are great.  Veggie sticks are also good.  

A favorite for locals in STL.

I wonder what would happen if you ate pizza everyday?  I mean everyone knows that it contains 4 of the major food groups and if I get to eat pizza everyday then I would absolutely pick Five Points for Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.  I really enjoyed the flavors and the onions on my pizza were amazing like onion candy.  It is important to note that we ate here during Tomato Fest. The hostess told me that Tomato Fest is the busiest day of the year for Five Points yet their pizza and their service remained on point.  

They offer some unusual toppings as well as all the old favorites.  We ordered the Zeus and subbed the capicola for some sausage and it was delicious!   The table next to us had the Garlic Knots and they looked tempting.  I will definitely try those next time we are in the area along with on of their Chocolate Chip Cannolis. mmmmm

I have heard so much about blind onion being a great place. I must've caught them on a bad day. Order taker was indifferent and seem to care less if she took my order or not. My wife went to find a table and couldn't find a clean one and when told the order taker she basically shrugged it off  Waited what seemed like an eternity for our food.
