the food, however, was AWESOME!! can't say enough about it...the mac n cheese was VERY good (almost better than my homemade mac n cheese :)...the helpings were so large that i was able to get 2 meals out of it (i paid about $14)...the banana pudding - let's just say that i only got about 2 bites, because my daughter inhaled it!  but from the 'taste' that i had, it was VERY good as well.

i will definitely be going back!  next weekend, as a matter of fact :)
Delicious, delicious, delicious!  Fried pork chop was the best! We even met nephew Charlie and talked about the filming going on for the new reality show. Very fun!

This Chipotle is the best Chipotle. The team they have working the assembly line is friendly, fast, and motivated. The burrito I get is always spot on and none of the ingredients are undercooked.

The Chipotle in Abington (see my review) should come and observe this Chipotle to learn how the operation is supposed to run.

5 stars to the GOAT

Awesome St. Louis soul food!!!!!

I love soul food!  I effin' love it!  I've eaten it all over the country and this place is as good as any I've had.

First of all, the location was in a cool part of town.  I'm not familiar with it (The Grove) but it seems urban, historical, had some nice murals painted on buildings, etc.  I might have to return with a camera.  Street parking (some metered) for S-Pie's is in a residential neighborhood.

For people complaining about the line, I went on a Thursday when it opened (11:30am) and was greeted by a massive line of ten people so, plan accordingly.  You don't go to the most popular soul food restaurant in a city on a Sunday after church and complain about the crowd.  And I'll parlay a suggestion I've made on other reviews:  it's crowded for a reason.  I'm sure there are much less desirable restaurants around town with no lines that'll be happy to seat you right away.

As far as the serving line, I wasn't met with poor, unfriendly service.  Then again, I usually take ownership of the way others treat me.  If you're friendly, smile, and get them laughing, they'll usually be nice to you (and give you larger servings).

As for the food, here's the breakdown from what I ordered:

Meatloaf:  4 stars.  I'm not big on pepper or tomatoes and it was inundated with both but, still, it worked.  A nice flavor.

Mac n Cheese:  3.5 stars.  I'm big on mac n chz and have had much better at BBQ joints throughout the South so I'll give this a "good, not great."

Mashed Potatoes n Gravy:  3.5 stars.  Again, lots of black pepper in the gravy.  Still, good taste.  

Corn:  5 stars.  This was some of the sweetest corn I've ever tasted.  It could have been labeled as a dessert.

Cornbread:  1 star.  Dry and tasteless.  Boston Market has better corn bread.  TIP:  Avoid the dry, tasteless cornbread.  Eating the heavy, starchy brick of cornbread will fill you up faster and prevent you from enjoying more of the great food.  

Peach Cobbler:  5 stars.  To die for.  Unbelievable.  I'm more of a banana pudding guy (and it looked great) but tend to lean towards a restaurant's more popular dish and I'm glad I did.

Not since eating at Nashville's Loveless Cafe have I sat so long at a table, completely full, but unwilling to leave until I finished my plate because -- food that tastes this good shouldn't be wasted.

I'll be back.

Brett, Chad and the rest of the Indy Tire team are terrific!  Great work, fairly priced and friendly.  I drive an older model European car and have brought it here for everything from oil changes,tire rotations, new rims, brakes, wheel bearing replacements and electrical sensor work.  If they can do the work they will and they'll do a great job.  When they can't... they've directed me to other good mechanics/specialty shops - like custom muffler work (Mufflers and More in Westfield).  Very glad to have someone I trust take care of all 4 of our family's autos!
I don't consider this Soul food, I consider that stuff homestyle. I can do just as good if not better at home. This place is way overrated.

Hit this place up last summer after it was on TripleD. Figured there'd be a Saturday lunch crowd, so we went in the later part of the lunch "hour."

Went straight to the cafeteria line . . . no wait! Actually, we wandered around a little before getting in line to see what this joint was all about. The bar area looks grand with huge old (vintage) lucious wood armoires/fireplace mantles for the backside of the bar . . . beautifully presented and looked like they came out of some turn-of-the century mansions on Lindell or in Parkview.

Happy, happy people work here. Portions are more than generous.

We both got basically the same thing. Fried chicken is WINGS. Where do they get these chickens?? Three wings was the portion, and it was a huge amount of food!

We did not get the person who carries your tray to your table. We ported ourselves. No biggie.

But they bus your table, so are bringing your beverage . . . refilling . . . including extra napkins and your to-go vessel. We both got unsweetened tea, which was fabulous, with numerous and plentiful refills.

Mac and cheese was great, green beans were fabulously cooked with some meat, maybe bacon or corned beef. Collard greens were ridiculously flavorful. Cornbread was fine, but sat so far down on the list, I probably don't give it justice.

While we were dining, a family came in who were unfamiliar. Trying to go down the wrong way of the cafeteria line and running dead-end into a potted palm. We just got up and showed them how to go through the line, even though the staff was trying to show them, and they didn't get it. But they were grateful for the assistance. I hope they enjoyed their meals.

The Hubbster and I decided to take a 100% random trip to Saint Louis for memorial day. First of all, never again. Secondly, Sweetie Pie's a redeaming light for STL in an otherwise pretty dismal place. We didn't even get a chance to put our hand on the front door before someone was there to greet us like old friend. The customer service is not to be matched. I've been to quite a few meat and threes in my day, but the customer service really makes this place what it is. 

Location: 
It is what you would expect for a meat and 3...a semi sketchy place with parking across the street. It's not to scary or too off the beaten path so that was good. 

The decor inside is very pretty. Clean with a restored feeling of your well to do gradmother's house. Booths and lots of window seats. pretty spacious. 

Food/serving:
Its a buffet line as usually that moves pretty quickly. The have a wide variety of soul food. All that you would expect out of any honest to God soul food place. The prices are ok. meat and 3 - $9 but varies on which meat you get which I thought was strange. 11 -12 if you get 4. 

Dessert is fine, but honestly not the icing on the cake. I hate to be that one, but it is good food, but its not great food. It is definately a plate that you could make at home with a few tries. That is my honest opinion. I love sould food and it was just not as off the charts as expected. I'm in TN. I 'm in the true South, and I'm telling you that might fly up north but my mom has cooked better meals. 

Customer Service and ambience really gave this place an extra star. AND the fact the they have been picked up by Oprah's network for a reality show. So there is camera crew everywhere which was kinda neat. 

My fellow yelpers, I have to be honest. Don't beat it up. If you are in STL, sure go visit. If I lived there, I would not be a regular. 

Arnold's Country Kitchen in Nashville, would put this place out of buisness.

Hype.  Fam loves fried chicken, but we hate to clean up from frying at home.  So, we went to SP and got chicken, mac-n-cheese, green beans, okra, yams, corn bread to go.  Chicken was mediocre; flavor profile we wanted was absent.  We wanted to be wowed.  Everything else tasted like it was from a box, can or had been left over from the previous day.  Daughter wouldn't even taste it because it didn't look "fresh" to her.  She's 8.

I just moved from Los Angeles and was sold bad tires before I left. The manager and staff at this establishment really pulled through. I had to buy 3 new tires and the price was cheaper than the bad tires I received in LA. They were so fast and so nice. I will defiantly be making this my go to car repair shop. Thank you!

came here for the fried chicken and it wasn't that good, it was pretty average.

got the cabbage and the mac and cheese for the sides and they were friggin' awesome.

The Carne Asada is fantastic, the homemade corn tortillas I could eat by themselves.  In the summer, I love to get the shrimp cocktails to go, it's the perfect light refreshing lunch. A ton of shrimp in the delicious cold tomato-y liquid with onions and cilantro and avacado- it really is amazing.  

Plus, the waitresses are totally hot and dress like hoochies, which I like in a mexican joint.  It's pretty authentic Mexican food, but white people come through too. I almost dont want to tell anyone about it, because then it will get busier and more expensive.
Hands down, the best gourmet sandwich joint in Delaware county!

How anyone gives this place more than one star is beyond me. This is the worst soul food I've ever had! I keep seeing people give this place 3 & 4 stars. Either they have to be from St.Louis or they don't know real soul food. I'm from Chicago and we'll cook these people under the bus. First off everything is sweet! The Mac & cheese was sweet, The green beans was sweet, The cabbage was sweet hell everything. The chicken wings was tough! The spaghetti was gross. The Carmel cake taste like a box cake. The Service was horrible! This place is all hype! Mrs.Robbie is actually rich from serving this garbage to people. Oprah needs to be shamed for pumping up this less than sub-par food up. The only good thing I tasted was the fried fish (which was a bit too salty). I think these people are star struck by stating this is some good soul food. I took my family (3 of total) and spent $49!! I feel Mrs.Robbie owes me a refund for this garbage. That's what it is GARBAGE! ALL HYPE BECAUSE THEY'RE  ON TV. Oprah would'nt know good soul food  if it bit her in the ass. Heed my advice go else where for soul food. Real Talk.

I may have a slight obsession fried chicken. Sweetie Pie's may have cured that obsession, because there really isn't any better fried chicken in the St. Louis area. Their chicken wings are probably from pterydactyls, because I've certainly never seen a chicken capable of generating wings that large. The meat is moist and well-seasoned, and the crust is perfectly crispy. Oh, the sides are excellent, too, but really, if you're coming to Sweetie Pie's, you need to eat the chicken.

Wow! Reading some of the comments about the food making people sick had me going for a minute. I visited the Mangrove location during the time Ms. Robbie was working on the Upper Crust.  We traveled from Indianapolis as this was something on my bucket list, and it was my birthday weekend. Not sure why the experience was so terrible for many, but I was PLEASED with everything. The food was "off the chain" as my young nieces and nephews would say. We sampled everything, and what we could not eat, we were able to take it back to the hotel for cravings in the late midnight hours. Since it was my birthday, and I knew all of the main characters on the show, they were than accommodating to take photos with me. Tim allowed me to see pictures of the baby, Charles was hilarious, and Big D made sure our table was stocked with all the condiments one would need for greens, cornbread, chicken, fish, chops, mac and cheese, ribs, cabbage, spaghetti, corn, green beans, sweet potatoes, cobbler and carmel cake. Yes, our crew was HUGE and we did not miss out on anything! 

Moreover, I do wonder if the shows notoriety has caused the taste of the food to diminish? I plan on returning in October, but I'm skeptical due to the fact that I will have the best soul food cook accompanying me; my beloved Granny. She can be critical, and I want to chose the best location. Given the fact that Ms. Robbie knows how she wants her food to taste, one would assume that going to the Upper Crust would be ideal, but after reading reviews on all three locations, I am perplexed. I will do an "eenie meenie minie moe process:)"

The catfish was good but a bit salty, the cornbread and cabbage was good, however  the green beans, macaroni n cheese were way too sweet, the spaghetti was absolutely AWFUL! the peach cobbler, YUCK. Our server was very unattentive.Sad,  this place is overated, will NEVER be back.
if i die of a chipotle overdose i will die happy.   General chipotle praise aside, I have always found the staff here excellent.   They're always in a good mood.

Trusting connections is an awesome service to take the guesswork out of finding someone to take care of your child.  They do an excellent job of finding awesome and reliable nannies and we have loved  every nanny we have been provided with.  I have always felt my child is safe with the nanny they send and they do a great job of using the same two nannies for our ever changing schedule. My child is always happy and I feel the nanny is a continuation of care my child adjusts to without issue.  I highly recommend trusting connections if this is the type of childcare you want for your child.

I feel like my review would be pointless to write now after reading Angela S.'s review. 

Here is the bottom line: clear your night out after eating here because you are going to be stuck in the bathroom for the rest of the evening. Give it 2 hours after you ate here. 

When you walk in here, it seems like a fantastic idea. Sweetie Pie's is on tv! Cool. The owner used to sing with Tina Turner! Cool. She grew up in Mississippi. Alright! A fellow Southerner. I get it. Yet the hype around it just doesn't seem that original to me or worth paying $18 for only one person. Overpriced, heavy on the stomach, and quite overdone. 

I respect the business and what they're going for, but it reminds of a Piccadilly's Cafeteria and the quality of it too. Very similar and more expensive. I don't think I would make a point to return, but if you are into this sort of thing then by all means come see it for yourself.
Had lunch here today and my rice and beens were cold. My chili calirodo was strips of thin steak and a tomato chili sauce. Had a taste and paid for the meal even after telling them my food was cold.
Great friendly people to deal with and my order was about half the price of lifestyles around the corner. If I have any more events I will be coming back, thanks for the great service!

Lives up to the hype! Those greens are amazing. Definitely worth the visit and the wait in the long line. Once you get to the food the service is lovely as they take your tray to an available table to help you find your seat.

Incline location. Nice and cozy. Nice people. Ordered lunch to go. Quick service.
Enchilada - bland and little chicken. Tostada - chewy and fatty "beef". They have so much potential......
I won't go back. I threw the tostada away. YUK!

My family has been trusting the Nannies from Trusting Connections for over 3 years. We have been so blessed to have such a fantastic service for our 3 boys. The nannies that care for our children are kind, respectful, and responsible. My favorite part of the service, though, is the staff at Trusting Connections. From time to time, I need to speak with someone. Usually something as simple as I need to adjust the starts by time for the nanny since plans changed. They are always so gracious and offer me the help I need. As a busy Mom, it is so nice to know I can rely on them to help me get through my day. Thank you so much for taking care of my family!!
-- Jennifer M
Every time I come to rocco's  I feel like family. The food is amazing and the staff is incredible. Some of the best pizza in the area.

Came here for a vegan veggie bowl. They messed up my first bowl by putting chicken in it. When they made me a new one, they put sour cream on it. When i said i didnt want sour cream, they tried to scoop it off with a plastic ramekin. I ended up just saying nevermind and leaving. 
I wasnt a fan of being rushed through line anyway.
Now im just frustrated and hungry. 
I dont usually waste my time at fast food places, but i thought the non GMO ingredients sounded like a good lunch choice on my break. I guess i will possibly try another location sometime?
One star because they are gmo free.. 
One star because i do feel bad that i left.

Im not saying not to come here, but i reccomend to be very specific and clear to the employees so they dont mess yours up like mine!
Yum!  Great fried chicken and peach cobbler.  Have to go back again to try some of the other foods like mom made.  Cheerful staff.

Man oh man, I too was one of the "Viking" (what's in your wallet) contingent to ravage Sweetie Pies on Saturday and I'm still full.

It was c-c-cold or much colder afternoon than we're used to and the southern comfort food provided a perfect stick-to-your-ribs meal. My more than generous plate consisted of 2 pork steaks smothered in good brown gravy with sides of  fried chicken wings, spaghetti,  cabbage, stewed okra and a hunk of cornbread .

Like Mark said, knives were totally useless for the chops as they were fall off the bone tender. The cabbage and okra were a nice one-two kicker for the meal and the spaghetti had that rustic home made goodness to it. All that was needed was a couple of splashes of hot sauce and the feasting was under way. Definitely a repeat go to place...

So, all of my friends rant and rave about Sweetie Pie's and against my mother's advice I tried it for myself. My word of advice, never ever go against your mother! The food was mediocre at best and the presentation was not up to my standards. I don't want my food to be presented in a sloppy way. The baked chicken looked extra wet and the fried chicken still had feathers in it. If i'm not mistaken feathers in the chicken need to be removed at cleaning hmmmm...I'd rather stick to my own soul food or hound my mother.
The service is always good, the prices are inexpensive,  The salsa that comes with the chips is tasty.  I love their chicken mole.

Against my better judgment, i tried the collards again  I WISH somebody would tell these "soul food" cooks that it isn't necessary to drench your dishes with sugar:-(. On the up side, the mac n cheese is whats up!!!

The best meat loaf ever...could it even be better than mine?  YES!  Sweet potatoes were yummy and the mac n cheese was to die for.  Tried the collard greens for the first time in my life...very good.  Huge servings.  Cornbread not sweet but tasty.  Staff was very pleasant and helpful. We will be going back in the near future.  Good job Robbie!

Sweetie pies was my favorite spot in st louis until today i cant understand why they did me dirty today first the ran out of pork steak so i had to wait so the food server gave me a post it to give to the cashier which i did second the ran put of cornbread so i had to wait on that also third when i gave the post it to cashier she told us to go sit down and someone would bring us the food so i listened because they haven't steered me wrong before i waited for 15 mins like they said we then went up to the register and the food sure enough was sitting by the register the cashier said she was calling our name but she clearly didn't but it is 2014 so she might have done it telekinetically lls so i got my food and the food was good like always the cornbread was the worst of all though it was so dry and thick and unsweetened like a big piece of yellow drywall. Then i looked at my receipt and nothing that i ordered was on their so i asked the server to get someone to explain this to me because it seemed like i paid for another meal that i didn't receive so a manager came over and tried to explain and her excuse for the receipt was (they just punch anything but thats the same as what u got it all adds up to the same thing you get it) i really didn't understand  anything that was said during her explanation but whatever i didn't have an understanding of why 2 chicken wings cost $10 but its ok thats the sweetie pie way i don't think i will be back unless i bring my own chicken to save me $10 oh and another thing i also brought some cologne from a guy selling it in the back of the restaurant I'm not complaining because i got a hell of a deal but wow thats crazy ole sweetie pie herself mig need to do a pop up visit.

I love Countryside. It's definitely a regular stop of mine for sandwiches. The menu is diverse and interesting with sandwiches named after various schools of higher education. Sitting outside when the weather is nice is wonderful. The decor inside is kitschy country deli and the staff is not always the most friendly, but the food is worth it.

It was good until I found out that the buyer for Chipotle gets half his stuff third world countries. The pork products come from Vietnam all the beef products come from Honduras, lettuce tomatoes  from Guatemala. The Wonder everybody's getting sick

We have always purchased our tire at other tire centers. This was my 1st visit and the service, customer service and the tires were awesome. I also had the oil changed, alignment and tail light replaced. Very convenient.. one stop shopping for a good price.  

The assistant manager Mike Grimpe was outstanding. He was the difference. Thank you Mike.

This was my second time visiting this location and I am equally unimpressed. The foods was cold, everything was cold except the collard greens. And there seemed to be sugar in everything. Sugar in the collard greens, mac and cheese black eye peas, etc.  Why anyone would put sugar in the greens is beyond me, but I was completely unimpressed.  I won't give it three times,

I told myself I wouldn't go here again after waiting for over an hour for some average fried chicken. But when I got to the Gateway city I decided to give them a second chance and I wasn't disappointed. 
This time the chicken was something to brag about with the perfect blend of spices and herbs. Not dry but not too greasy. I had green beans and mac & cheese as my sides. The veggies were good not great but the mac & cheese was nasty to me. It had a sweet taste to it similar to macaroni salad. So just imagine warm macaroni salad with cheese... yeah not so appealing. 
Once again I was so impressed with the amazing peach cobbler (the only reason I gave them a second chance). Perfect amount of crust, peaches, and syrup filling. 
I would definitely go again but instead of mac and cheese I'll try the yams.

Tried it a couple of times and was disappointed during each visit. Lines are long, service is slow but more importantly, the chicken is below average. During every visit I found the chicken either overcooked and dry or so greasy that it wasn't edible. 

Similarly, the sides taste canned, not fresh. The mashed potatoes were underwhelming and the corn and green beans clearly tasted like something from a #10 can. Food temps were also an issue with them coming off the service line from warm to chilled, never hot. 

For all the lines and waiting, it is substandard food isn't worth the wait or price.

I was new to the area and picked this place for a gel manicure mostly because of the name and the website. The front desk staff were very friendly and welcoming.  I was given an appointment for an hour or so later which was fine.  When I returned the staff remembered me by name and I was offered a beverage.  I already had gel on my nails and she had great difficulty getting it off.  While this was occurring, I inquired about color choices of gel.  The choices were extremely limited and there were no chips to pick from.  I settled on a color and she proceded. I discovered a place she missed and she just painted over the spot.  Later, I looked at the manicure carefully and the polish was not near any cuticle, but only in the nail center.  Further, there was uneven application and by 12 hours post manicure, the Polish was peeling off like a skin!  Needless to say, I am very disappointed!  This salon might be excellent at other things, but I will not go back for a manicure!

Savory, delicious, great value, and fast (usually).

This Chipotle has a convenient location in Center City if you live in the area, but I imagine it's a real pain to find parking.  Delicious food, however the setup of space (can get very crowded) and noise level (usually on the louder range) make it not the ideal place to dine in.  I usually just grab and go.

Rundown:
Burrito bowl to go with tortilla on side
Mix brown and white rice
Extra rice instead of beans
1/2 steak and 1/2 chicken
2 scoops pico
2 scoops corn
Lettuce on top
Cheese in a cup

Outcome:
Slide that 1lb bad boy into a bag, grab some napkins and 2 forks, I'm usually good for two meals.

This meal was the single most item I craved when I was in Africa for 3 weeks.  Either very sad...or just very awesome food...maybe a little of both.

Cool looking place. I definitely feel like I went here on a bad day.

Everyone tells me that Chipotle is the best mexican fast food chain (I can't believe this is even a category, it used to be just Taco Bell..) I can find.

I gave them an easy one my first time here, I usually go with the complex burritos, etc. But decided to go for a chicken quesadilla for my first experience at Chipotle. I think they forgot to grill it.

It was pretty expensive for chicken, cheese and a tortilla and fell apart as soon as I lifted it up. I'll definitely give this place another try because of the good things people say about it, but for my first visit, I was extremely disappointed.
I just found out today that they put a tip on my credit card.  I disputed it and my credit card company is handling it.  WOW!  The nerve of these people!

I'm not sure I get all the Chipotle hype.  Especially this location.  It is extremely narrow and near impossible to find seating at lunchtime.  
The staff seem to be almost robotic...don't dare ask a question about rice when they shout "chicken, beef or pork."  It will completely throw off their groove, and you will be on the receiving end of a nasty little look.  I speak from experience.  
The ingredients are fresh, I guess.  But when they all mix up in your little bowl or burrito, they are indistinguishable from one another.  Nothing special here my friends.

Holy smokes! I came here with a friend and ordered the fish which was two giant fillets that were perfect! We also each got two huge sides and corn bread. The service was very friendly and the price was reasonable. I definitely plan to go back.

Amy Poehler once said, "This is Oprah! She farts on a book and it magically sells a million copies." I don't know how applicable this is to a review about a restaurant... but it's certainly a true statement. If Oprah endorses you, you're set for life.

Sweetie Pie's, in The Grove, is set for life.

Yes, Sweetie Pie's will be featured in the line-up of new reality shows to hit the Oprah Winfrey Network in the coming months.I think that means that, despite what I say in this review [don't worry, it won't be bad], Sweetie Pie's can be sure that their doors will remain open.

And thank heavens, because the soul food serving establishment is absolutely blissful. Apparently, Oprah knows what she is talking about.

My girlfriends and I decided to go to Sweetie Pie's as a part of our eating out group. It may not be ethnic (which is what we usually prefer), but the Mississippi style eatery was definitely the most unique establishment we've been to!

First of all, when they say that soul food is "down-home cookin'" the emphasis is on the word "home." Not only was the food straight up homey, greasy, comfort food... but the décor was simple and totally unpretentious--just a few photos and some fake flowers on the family sized tables. Basically, the place felt the way dinner at home feels.

So, other than the great food and great service--what made Sweetie Pie's unique? Well, when you walk in you will find a cafeteria-style set up. Just grab your tray, pick your meat, pick your sides, pay and then prepare to demolish some good eats.

Options include fried and baked chicken, pork steaks, cabbage, okra, mac and cheese, corn, beans, mashed potatoes, green beans, and cornbread--aka all the best things in life.

Because the line was moving pretty quick, I felt a little overwhelmed and pressured to order fast... luckily, I work extraordinarily well under pressure and made some amazing choices. I choose to get fried chicken, mac and cheese, beans, and cornbread. (Hello calories!)

And do you know what? I would recommend every single portion of that meal. I suppose if you twisted my arm and threatened to beat me up, and I had to pick ONE thing to recommend, I would say that you should definitely not skip the fried chicken. It's probably the most fattening choice, but heck, it's not very often that you can get fried chicken that is as good as your momma's, so be sure to take this opportunity.

It was just so good and greasy... I can't stop thinking about it...

Seriously, I better wrap this up before I start salivating all over my computer...

If food and service don't impress you, then cheapness will! For only $12, I got a heaping huge plate of food. Seriously, the meal was legitimately enough for two servings (they gave us FOUR chicken wings)--and boy oh boy, I cannot wait for lunch tomorrow. Leftovers are the best.

All in all, the whole meal and experience was lovely. We were stuffed and happy, the waitress was attentive but not annoying, and the cameras were even there preparing to film!

Unfortunately, I will not be appearing on Oprah's network any time soon. BUT, I'm not giving up hope of someday becoming a famous extra on the OWN network. I definitely plan to return to Sweetie Pie's someday soon. Well, maybe not too soon... for fear of my cholesterol spiking severely.

To finish this long-winded, gushing review, I have only four words to say to you: GO TO SWEETIE PIE'S. Well... Let me add one more word. Go to Sweetie Pie's... NOW.

Let's see where do I start..... the wait to get inside & seated was almost 2hours. Now considering the "hype-ness" of the restaurant I get that they have a massive amount of people waiting to get in to see what the hype is about especially on the weekend . HOWEVER if you are going to have people wait out in the sun in a line wrapped around the building for hours to get in I would think you could offer small bottles of water or cups of ice as a appreciation gesture. I mean really how much is bottles of water in bulk from a dollar store?  Alternatively, I am sure if you solicited interest from local businesses, they would donate the water as a nice gesture.  It's the little things you do that sets you apart & generates loyalty from the public but I digress. 

Now let's move on to the food itself...if you have never had any authentic soul food or a fabulous granny to throw down in the kitchen then I can understand how someone would go crazy about Sweeties Pies.  The food here is NOT bad HOWEVER I have had and can cook better.  The food is mildly seasoned and extremely bland, did I mention the mac & cheese has sugar in it yuck, and I won't discuss the basic recipe of hard  cornbread. The best thing there was the desert, now that was delish! One thing I will give credit for is proportions, you really do get your money's worth, you get a huge heaping of everything! I'll stop there let's move on to the workers. 

Everyone EXCEPT for the individuals who fixed your plate was a joy and really pleasant to engage with. However, those ingrates back there fixing your plate should GO! They were grumpy, didn't smile, and flat out rude.  It's apparent they do NOT like their work station. With all of that said I probably would go again on a weekday to try something different but I would have to be there soon as the doors opened lol it is not worth an hour wait. P.S Gladys Knights in Atlanta is wayyy better in my opinion!

Definitely opened. Ate there today. Food was awesome. Place is a lot nicer now that they've remodeled. They have some new menu items and are offering fresh seafood. The fried chicken and Mac and cheese were off the chain!!

I understand the the draw that Chipotle holds for poor college students and young adults... its a ton of food for not a lot of money, but that's all it is, and it doesn't even keep you full very long.  Everything is luke warm and nothing tastes fresh or even good.  The only reason I got dinner here was because the boyfriend had a BOGO coupon and I figured it'd be a cheap way to do dinner.  I got the bowl, not the burrito (I have some crazy thing against burritos, don't ask...), and didn't eat more than half before thinking "why the heck am I eating this..."  

Never again.

I've got a little tradition going that has one more iteration before it ends - go to wood turning class on Saturday morning then stop in the Grove and eat somewhere new.  I usually take Corondolet westbound and pull over just past the Grove sign then check Yelp for what's nearby.  This was week 3 of 4.  It's kinda fun...

Apparently I'm the only dumbass in town.  I came to Sweetie Pies for lunch on my way home without having the slightest idea that this place has been on TV multiple times or that there was a reality show based here - the wife told me when I called her to let her know that I now have a favorite fried chicken in STL.  Naturally, I got ridiculed but I didn't really care after the meal I had just consumed.

I use the term "consumed" rather loosely.  I ordered the half chicken special with 2 sides for about $10.  I ate half of everything and had the rest packed up to feed to kid 2 when I got home.  I probably could have eaten more but didn't want to wind up face-down on the couch all afternoon - we had things to do, dammit!

With the number of reviews already posted for this place there isn't much I can add but here are the highlights:

Fried chicken was incredibly moist, flavorful and crispy.  My preference is the bottom half of the chicken but I ate the top half because I knew the kid prefers the leg and thigh.  I'm usually less than please with chicken breast in this country because we don't seem to raise chickens for flavor as much as for size.  With this in mind, I didn't have very high expectations...boy was I wrong!  Juicy, plump and just plain delicious - also huge.  That piece, the wing and the square of cornbread filled me up!  I poked at the sides (yams a& green beans) but the majority of them went into containers to go home to the kid as well.  Crying shame as they were delicious and I wished I had room for more.

Great service, very friendly and delicious food all adds up to a place I will try again!

I was disappointed the restaurant opens at 11:30 but they didn't open their doors until 1146am. The line was long and moved slower than my great grandma. The food was overrated. Fried Chicken was bland,  the mac and cheese had too much extra "stuff" in it. Ridiculous to have people out in the heat waiting with so many empty tables inside. I almost forgot they did not have sweet tea available. The one item she markets the most isn't available? Did they not know they would have customers today? I was actually at the Delmar location because Mangrove was closed.

Chipotle, overall, I enjoy.

This location can get the job done (chicken burrito bowl typically for me). However, as I compare this location to several others in CA, they could go a bit faster. Through observation, they should pay more attention the the patrons' ahead of me's orders as they tend to mess up which causes a delay in the process.

But I still enjoy Chipotle!

I wonder how many people in the city got a buy one get one free coupon from Chipotle like I have, the place was packed. Luckily I got a table in the former lofty Susanna Foo space and while I had to order lunch, my companion kept watch on the table. 

The space is pretty nice, clean and brand spanking new with great lighting. I've never been to a Chipotle since most of them are in the burbs and I don't drive. So I've ordered two burritos, one barbacoa and one steak. Frankly I didn't know what barbacoa was as it didn't state it on the menu, I know it means barbecue but I don't know whether it was beef or pork, turns out, it's beef. 

At the assembly bar, the server steamed the tortilla slightly and put the  sauce, meat and rice and beans on top, then it's passed on to another person to put on sour cream, cheese, salsa and lettuce. You can pay extra for some guacamole. The end product is huge. I can hardly finish one and I'm a big guy.

I have to say though that the sour cream mellow out a lot of flavor, so the various available Tobasco sauces were welcomed. I love the steak cubes even though there's not much of it, it provided a chewy bite that provides variety to the other textures. The corn salsa also added some sweetness. I would like the whole thing to be grilled to a crisp and I would also have welcomed a steak sauce but it'd be quite unauthentic. 

With a drink, it'll be about $10 a person which is reasonable. Again, the whole burrito is quite filling, so it's possible that you'd share one of this with a friend. They also have bowls, taco (x3), salad and chips and salsa available. If they could salt the meat a little bit more to add some flavor, it might be better but I surely don't mind it, especially with a free coupon. Nothing wins my heart over faster than free food. 

Is anybody else appalled that a tortilla is 200-300 calories? That's the downsize of listing the calorie values of each ingredient isn't it?

I highly recommend all foodies to fill their empty bellies with some soul at Sweetie Pie's. Sweetie Pie's is definitely the best soul food in St. Louis. It seems to be hopping with a great staff and loyal customers. 

The place is set up as a cafeteria-serving style. You pick what you want at the line (meat and sides) and you pay at the end of the line. Then you take your tray at a table. The menu has too many deliciousness to choose from. They have a list of daily specials and they also have the every day menu that consist of baked chicken, pork steak, wings, meatloaf, and pork chops. On top of that, they have a list of great side items that leaves you lost in the abyss of your decision-making. YIKES! Plus you can't forget their amazing corn bread that always comes with your meal. 

I got the baked chicken with okra and mac and cheese on the side. The portion on the plate, I must say, is a generous amount. The baked chicken was so juicy and so tender that the meat just slid off the bone. The skin had some great flavor as well. Also the okra seems perfect and it was my first time trying okra. I couldn't resist getting mac and cheese. The mac and cheese was rich and creamy, and I couldn't let go of my fork even though I was so full at the end. Also I recommend ordering the Arnold Palmer (1/2 tea and 1/2 lemonade). After this delightful meal, I hope to come here in the future to try everything else on the menu, especially those crunchy wings that are flying inside my head now... I'm getting hungry!

I would say Sweetie Pie's is definitely a place you want to take visitors when you're at the "Show Me" State.

Have been there many times.  It has been hit and miss. One time the pizza was good, next time, not so much.  The wait staff is either good or bad.  They keep the restaurant so cold, you sit and freeze trying to eat your pizza, and of course the pizza gets cold.  I'm from NY and have had better pizza here in Florida.  We usually go with friends, but went one night by ourselves.  We ordered a cheese pie and it appeared to been sitting in the kitchen and reheated for us.  Was not happy with that visit.  Need to find another place.

Totally a Hole in the Wall serving cheap cantonese dishes for the locals. What's interesting about this place is you can order fresh dim sum dishes (no carts), most being around $1.80 per dish.  Although, the quality isn't as good as the more popular dim sum places in Philly, such as Ocean Harbor or Joy Tsin Lau. Service is nice but decor is rather lackluster and depressing.

I loved Lupita's when it opened. in fact, i ate there so many times the owner asked me about it.
The quality dropped, though. I've held off giving it a so-so review, because I really want them to succeed. It's been years since i had a good meal there. So just three stars from me.
I got a margarita, a taco and a beef burrito. Because I got the margarita they gave me a free ceviche tosada and it was nice. The margarita was bad. Tasted watery. Not much flavor.
The taco was the best part ot the meal. I don't remember which meat I got. The burrito was forgettable. For either value or quality, there are many restaurants out there better than Lupita's.
Always my go-to spot for a quick, fresh Mexican meal. Dependable, reliable, delish! Guac is definitely worth the extra $

Gross hotel! Musty smell throughout, dirty rooms, halls and elevator. Plus, you have the added luxury of seeing swarms of drunk VLT addicts as you go in and out of the building. Not worth the $190 a night!!!

This place is ok in terms of food I went because of the atmosphere and the name it had carried.. I had the meat loaf and some chicken but chicken wasn't as good as the one I had from hodaks or even from uncle bills

So we finally at at Sweetie Pies!  I was excited to finally be here and see for myself.  We waited in line for about 45 min, but that was ok with us.  I am sure it could have been faster if they were more organized.  It seems like just when the line would progress, they would have to stop to address running out of pans of food, change at the cash register, waiting for the waiters to help people to their table, take out and numerous other issues.  Anyway we finally get our food and sit down!  By this time we are starving and can hardly wait to eat.  We are from the south, so we have grown up eating this type of food.  The sweet tea was delicious, the catfish had a very thick cornmeal crust and was over cooked in our opinion, green beans were average, corn bread was average and the macaroni and cheese was very average.  I was so disappointed in the fish and macaroni and cheese!  After watching the show many times, it was on my place to try.  Now that I have been I don't feel the need to return.  I really wanted it to be better, but it is what it is.
Contractors were remodeling today. They said Sweetie Pie's is reopening August 29th!

As usual, enjoy chipotle as much as everyone else. Fast service. 
Once I went and the rice was really undercooked which ruined it as I always get it to go so I was at work and disappointed but that only happened once. Otherwise very happy with chipotle. I always get a sofritas bowl, yum

My family of 4 went to Sweetie Pies for lunch sat 12/03/11 at 12.30 pm and the line was clear across the restaurant to the door but it only took 15 min or so to get up to the food line and I needed it to deside which dishes to order. They all looked soooo good I loved the food and 4 chicken wings ( which looked like the chicken farm must have been near a nuclear power plant or something they were soooo big) sweet potatos and mac&cheese with fresh squeesed limonade and peach cobler everything was as good as it gets esspecally the peach cobler ; I have been serveer coblers with pasty crusts and peaches hard and tasteless but this desert was perfict in every way   kudos to everyone at sweetie pies. The place was packed but they got us in and out in an hour. WE LOVE SWEETIE PIES ps there is a lot across the street w free parking

Chipotle is my go-to hangover food on a Saturday/Sunday morning. I will wait anxiously like a little kid on Christmas for it to be 11am so I can go get my burrito to start easing my whiskey-induced pain courtesy of the night before. 

Rarely do I eat at this location. It's not just because 1)I look like a hot mess when I roll in there or 2) because, let's face it, it is impossible to look attractive while burrito is falling every which way on your hands and face. Rather, the restaurant can be pretty crowded and it's difficult to find a seat depending on what time of day you go. 

I have never had bad service here so I am happy about that. Though, I can't help but get a tad peeved when they tell me that "guac is extra". Yes, I know, what does this look like amateur hour? Just heap on the goodness, I'm not concerned about the cost. 

My review is now just about as big as chipotle's burrito which, for those of you who don't know, are huge. I can't speak to the delayed effects of Chipotle (which some people can unfortunately experience) but I can personally attest to its ability to please my taste buds and stomach.

Traveling through from Idaho and staying nearby. Of two Mexican restaurants in the strip mall, this one was open. My order was "to go" so can't speak to sit-down service or any chips etc they might offer diners. I gave my usual to-go order: 'burrito al pastor' and also got side of guac and flan when they said it was homemade. While the guac and flan were indeed homemade and quite good, the burrito was barely worth finishing. It lacked flavor and was simultaneously dry (rice, meat, tortilla) and greasy (beans). Moreover, the fillings were not well-integrated, so a bite on one side was mostly dry rice and on the other, mostly meat/beans. (fyi I live in Fruitvale district of Oakland and my expectations are based on the 'al pastor' burritos I find there). The flan was definitely flavorful and a lovely texture, but the sauce was something other than the caramelized sugar syrup I expected and love. My next trip thru I'll try somewhere else.

My brother swears by Chipotle's quality and flavors.  I've experienced much better.

I tried the Sofritas bowl yesterday, as I didn't see any veggies in the bin, and as I needed something with protein.  My first disappointment was with the proportions.  A decent amount of rice, about four black beans, a TON of Sofritas, a bit of pico de gallo, and a bit of cheese.  Understandably, when I started eating, I noticed how overpowering the Sofritas were in the dish.  It tasted like a bowl of salt.  I kept trying to get more and more rice on the fork to ease the salty taste.  

Perhaps the new American palate is all about salt, but as much as I love it, I think it needs to be toned down.

Out of all the pizza places I've been to in my 20 years down here, Rocco's is the best, no competition! Pizza is always done very well and exactly as ordered. Crust, sauce and toppings are all first class quality. You can't pass this restaurant without stopping in for a real treat. You feel like you're back in NY at one of your favorite pizzerias. Keep up the great work!

Decent food with casual authentic atmosphere. Rice and beans were cold although nicely seasoned. Chips and salsa tasty, crispy, and fresh. Salsa was very spicy. Main course was decent.

I had the Camerones a la Diabla. Very tasty chipotle twist on a classic tomato sauce shimp dish. Thick sauce which was great in their home made corn tortillas. Small rice and bean portion that was cold, did not even melt the cheese on top. Bar slash restraunt so be prepared for a lively crowd on a friday night. Large menu with many choices. Veggie options for people with food restrictions. My girfriend enjoyed the veggie enchaladas, good assortment of veggies. I would return if it was convienent for me to do so. Would not make a special trip across town.

I usually go to the food court one at the mall, but decided to take a walk during lunch today. I made it to this chipotle at around 12:30PM and there was literally no line at all! I'm not sure if it's because it's the week after Presidents' Day weekend, and many people simply decided not to work this week or what, but I was very excited about the lack of line !!

They are not very generous with the portions here! So If you're someone who loves chipotle for the portions, this specific store might not be the move.

All in all, solid clean chipotle. No complains. Lots of seating as well.

Sweetie Pie's exceeded all of our expectations. It was Friday, so 1/2 fried chicken was the special ($10.99), which we all got, and it was fantastic. It came with two sides--Rondi & I got the Mac & Cheese and corn, and my sister got the cabbage with the Mac & Cheese. It also came with a large slice of corn bread. I'm a big eater, but took half of my food home. The corn was so good my tongue was slapping my face trying to get to it, and my sister kept raving about the cabbage. We got there at about 5 pm, which must be the perfect time, since the line was short. Very soon after, the line was pretty long, but moved quickly. Everything was fresh and hot, and the man who made sure our drinks were full was not only attentive, but incredibly friendly. I guess my only complaint was that the cobbler was undercooked, so it was more like peaches and dumplings. We will definitely be back!

Ok....  Food presentation isn't their thing, but Ms. Robbie does her Soul Food right & tasty. Would have loved a picture w/ her, but I assume she was busy running her empire.  We made quick work of the fried chicken - this chicken was seasoned & crispy on the outside & most certainly seasoned prior to battering & frying. No collard greens today :-( Sundays only. We also had macaroni n cheese - done to perfection w/ a little over-cooked goodness on the edges & real cheese used, not that powdered or liquid gunk. Also had the cabbage - seasoned & appropriately firm. Cornbread was expertly baked w/ enough sugar & butter to ruin a waistline. Candied yams were not overly firm & didn't have that overwhelming cinnamon flavor that you often get when folks try to doctor up canned yams. Mash n gravy didn't disappoint. Unfortunately, the black eyed peas were my least favorite, could have used more salt or seasoning. 
 
Desert - we ordered both the peach & pear cobbler. Assumed I would prefer the peach, but the pear was on slam-oh-lah!!!!!  OMG!  Not super overwhelming or sweet, just gooooood. Unfortunately, they do not serve icecream, even though their website says they do. My suggestion is to take the cobbler home & slap a little Hagen Daas or Breyers vanilla on top & go to work. Would have been even better.

Portions size is great & there was plenty of street parking. Although, I would be careful about parking there after dark. Now on to the reason 4 stars, instead of 5 were earned. As I mentioned previously the presentation just isn't there. Food served in styrofoam containers whether or not you are eating in or out - kinda strange for the customer to take to a table & terrible for the environment. Customer service is exactly what you would expect - Unfortunately!!!  Dining area was pretty raggedy looking in this location, not sure about the others. Didn't use the restrooms, so I am unable to rate. Entrance both outside & inside are unwelcoming. All that said, I would definitely return in the daytime & order double portions of the Fried Chicken, Mac n Cheese, Cabbage & Pear Cobbler.
We were very pleased with the food. The oxtails melt in your mouth, so succulent and mouth-watering. We will be stopping back on our next trip down there.

No question the sandwiches are very good...however the owner is a rude arrogant @#$tard.  I ate there many times and thought it was just me but when talking to friends it turns out we all had similar experiences, many times over.  A good restaurant is more than just being able to make good food, agreed it may be the most important part but how the staff and especially how the owner treats you must figure into the equation. No thanks, I'll spend my lunch dollars elsewhere!

My first time at Sweetie Pie's was a lunch visit to interview someone for an article I had to write.  The interviewee suggested the spot and I have been hooked since I walked through the door.  

I'm gonna digress to let you know why:   I was very fortunate to work for the Home Depot when I was pregnant with my only child.  The ladies in the call center made sure that momma and child were well fed - with more soul food than this British girl knew what to do with.  I had catfish, okra, sweet potatoes  and more every time that baby kicked.  I became a fan for life (as soon as the baby was born I added hot sauce to everything).

Walking into Sweetie Pie's made me smile as I thought of those Home Depot gals, making sure my baby was fed right.  I ordered the fried chicken, green beans, mashed potatoes and corn bread and had a Peach Vess - you gotta have a Peach or Strawberry Vess if you're gonna eat at Sweetie Pies (it's a personal rule but I highly recommend you follow it).
The other memory the restaurant induced was the amount of food you receive when eating soul food.  I could have fed four children with the chicken piled on my plate not to mention the mound of sides overflowing onto the table.  My Peach Vess couldn't wash it all down.

If you want to experience the BEST of St. Louis cooking, head on down to Sweetie Pie's - you too will become a patron for life (or for as long as your in da' Lou).

They give you so much food. You will need a take home box for sure. The servers make you feel at home. Very welcoming and polite. Everyone is having a good time. I thought it was a nice touch that they had live music.

Okay, so we went to this place just to check it out since is was shown on TV. We took a cab there from downtown and we were greeted by a police officer as soon as we walked in. The place is cafeteria style, you pick up your food and find a seat. The menu is different every day but they have the fried chicken wings as staple. I originally wanted oxtail or fried cat fish, those are on Thursday and Friday unfortunately. I ordered the chicken wings with two side ( cabbage and mac&cheese) and corn bread for $10. The price was good and the food was okay. The seasoning from the wings was good, and the sides were decent.

We went around 5pm because we wanted to skip the long dinner lines. But 5pm was still not early enough. Our total wait from the time we walked in the door to the time we stood at the counter to place our order was about 45 minutes, and this is with the line backed up all the way back around the bar, so even though the wait was long, the line moved at fairly good speed. The fried chicken and macaroni and cheese was delicious, definitely worth the wait. I didn't like the black eyed peas because they were sweetened and I normally don't like sweetened veggies. The collard greens were pretty good - these were sweetened also but not overly sweet so it didn't overpower the flavor of the greens. If you enjoy soul food, then this is definitely a must-stop, just be prepared for a long line.

I am not sure whether it is Chipotle in general or just this particular location, but WOW this place has gone downhill fast. Their ingredients used to be great quality, but now it's all nasty.  I ordered a salad and got more leaves of cilantro than actual lettuce.  Or at least I think I did.  I couldn't actually tell if there was lettuce in the bowl under the 65 pounds of salsa they slopped on.  What a hot mess of a place.  Also, there is literally nothing left that isn't encrusted in cilantro.  It's been real, but see ya never, Chipotle.

Les doy dos estrellas por que consideró qué aunque la comida no fue de lo mejor (arroz de mala calidad, muy pocos frijoles) con los precios razonables que tienen, uno consideraría volver... Mi esposo y yo nos dimos una segunda oportunidad de regresar, pero solo para comprobar qué el servicio, aunque fue con dos diferentes meseras, fue fatal! 
La primera, nunca ofreció más bebida aunque estaban vacíos los vasos y aunque no fue grosera, traía una cara de amargura todo el tiempo 
En la segunda ocasión llevábamos dos bebes y jamás se ofreció a llevar unas sillas para infantes. ( mi esposo se paró a traerlas) 
A la hora de tomar la orden ni por cortesía ofreció traer nada para los niños 
Su rostro también siempre fue perdido y jamás se le miro una sonrisa 
Me tome el tiempo de escribir esto por qué es muy importante que tengan meseras amigables y preocupadas por sus clientes 
Yo tomó mucho en cuenta esto por qué consideró qué cuándo tienen buena actitud, aparte de las propinas, uno puede ignorar la mala calidad de la comida, la limpieza del lugar y muchos detalles más 
El servicio es para mí lo más importante

I've had a lot of chicken in my life. But I have honestly never tasted anything like this. Crispy, meaty, perfectly seasoned. Worth the line, just hang in there! The sides are all fantastic. I've never had well prepared black eyed peas... I know this because these were amazing and anything  else is now considered poorly prepared. The Mac and cheese was perfect mix of creamy, savory and a hint of sweet. Complemented the chicken perfectly. I really want to go back for the ox tails!!! I'm simply blown away. I can't believe it took me so long to come here. It won't be another 20+ years before I get my hands on some sweetie pies again that's for sure!!!

Sweetie Pie's is the most famous soul food restaurant in a city with dozens of options. This was my first visit, and I was quite pleased with the food, the decor, and the prices. It is located in an old, restored building on Manchester Ave.-- which is mostly commercial-- but is surrounded by residential neighborhoods. So street parking was the only option.

The four of us arrived on a Wednesday at 4:45pm.  There were four people ahead of us. I expected to be seated, but we were directed to a serving line. It is cafeteria style. The options are all on a chalkboard behind the serving line. They fill your plate with whatever it is you ask for, and you pay at the end of the line. A very attentive waiter seated us and brought us our drinks.

The serving line is fast and efficient. Pleasant servers, all women on my visit, put your order on your plate and pass it to the next server for additions. I had the liver, sweet corn, okra, and cabbage. My wife had the smothered pork, sweet potatoes, okra, mashed potatoes, and a pear cobbler. My daughter had the chicken that Sweetie Pie's is famous for. And my son had an assortment of sides as he is a vegetarian.

All of the entrees were delicious.  The liver was smothered in liver gravy and were done to a T. Not overdone; still tender and could be cut with a fork. The server gave me three pieces of liver-- an enormous serving; no wonder so many diners were getting "doggie bags." The smothered pork was a breaded pork steak that is smothered in a brown gravy. They were fork tender and my wife said it was the best pork steak she had had.  The half chicken was a hit, as my daughter finished it completely and raved about it in the car on the way back to our hotel.

The sides were all good.  The cabbage, boiled in seasoned broth until very tender, was a nice, lighter accompaniment. The okra was good, but it was falling apart, and I like mine still looking like okra. It was, however, very tasty.  The cornbread was wonderful. Moist, hot, and flaky.  It was not at all sweet, so you should be prepared for that. I know some people who only like cornbread if it is quite sweet. 

The restaurant is tastefully furnished with a mix of antiques and posters. Dark wooden tables with wooden or tile tops fill the place, but their placement is not very orderly.  That, however, adds to the visual appeal in my mind. Our waiter was very attentive and kept our drinks filled and checked to see if everything tasted good. The entire staff was very professional.  I would call it an up-scale soul food restaurant except that the neighborhood is not upscale and it is, after all, soul food; plus, the prices are far from upscale. 

All in all we found everything nearly perfect-- the food, the service, even the traffic.  If I had one complaint it would be that the music was quite loud. While I liked the music,. we were there visiting our kids and we all found it tough to be heard over the music. 

The diners were a mix of well dressed men and women, mostly black, and people wearing shorts and t-shirts, mostly white. Often all at the same table. I know that doesn't have any bearing on the food or the restaurant, but I thought it was an interesting difference in the cultures of the diners.

After dinner we took a short walk around this part of town. It is a mix of buildings that are in terrible disrepair-- abandoned, some even burned-- and others that are being nicely renovated. The bones of the neighborhood are beautiful, and I suspect it may soon be gentrified. i doubt that will hurt Sweetie Pie's at all, but it might change the character of the neighborhood.

From reading these reviews I was expecting this place to be much better.  I had the fried chicken with mac and cheese and sweet potatoes and my husband had the meatloaf.  His portion was not that big but the meatloaf was tasty.  My chicken was VERY disappointing and I have had much better fried chicken than the one served here.  The sides were great but I have to say that I think Popeye's fried chicken is considerably better and they are a chain restaurant.  The breading was too thick and it was unfortunately a big letdown for us.

A good restaurant will have food quality consistency. The sides were small and most of the food was salty. The fish was excellent but the chicken was not so great. The food did not warrant the high price.

Soon as my flight landed. I knew I had to go try Sweetie Pies to see what everybody is talking about. 
I arrived and there was no line no wait. The set up reminded me of a buffet style place. I wasn't a fan of that (Piccadilly). 
Well my $ 15.00 dollar plate consisted on fried chicken wings, okra, mac n cheese and peach cobbler.
Fried chicken wings- were pretty good. Reminds me of something a Mississippi  grandmother would cook LOL

Okra- had a really good taste but was totally over cooked and slimy. It should have been called okra soup.

MacNcheese- delicious!!

The food and pizza here are consistantly good.  Tonight I had the eggplant parm and it was delicious.  My only complaint was too that too much sauce was used.  The eggplant was well cooked and the pasta was good.  The salad was just a salad, nothing special.  The bread was a big disappointment though not crispy like good italian bread, tasted like white bread shaped like a loaf.  Overall a good experience and Ill be back.

I work at the nearby hospital and kept meaning to get over to Sweetie Pies, even before the reality show hit the air because I'm a huge mac and cheese lover and a cobbler craver. Otherwise, the menu doesn't offer the kind of fare that generally appeals to me as I'm not much of a fried foods fan.  Fortunately, Sweetie Pies was full of surprises.

My friend and I split everything we ordered---portions are absolutely gigantic.  I really, really liked the flavorful, juicy meat loaf.  And I never, ever make meat loaf nor do I order it.  I liked it so much, I'd get it again :).  The rich and corny cornbread was INSANE---alone, it's worth the trip. The tender green beans offered an added bonus of potato chunks---don't let the drab olive color fool you.  Strangely, I  didn't go gaga for the mac and cheese---it was more buttery and less cheesy than I like it.  And, the peach cobbler was just ho hum---its syrupy sweetness out drowned the peachiness.

The people watching was fantastic---everything from a dapper group of smarty dressed older gentleman to a herd of red hat society ladies, resplendent in purple and red.  Our waitress was quite friendly and efficient and we even got a smile from Sweetie Pie herself.

Loved the building and the crazy, rude/sassy signs around.  A hoot!

We had a good lunch and a good time.  I'll keep Sweetie Pies in the rotation, just for the novelty.

I love the Grove atmosphere.  But Sweetie Pie's left a bad taste of the neighborhood.   My social work class did a field trip to Rise because of its connection with the community, welcoming and helpful.  A bunch of us went to discuss projects we were working on and decided on Sweetie Pie's. My intention was to try their food as i had never been there.   As part of the group went to get food some sat down.   They told us if we weren't eating we couldn't take up their table space.  There were MANY tables open otherwise.   We had to leave part of our crowd in and left.  Terrible customer service!!!  I don't care if they had the best food I will never be back or recommend!

OK, I am about to commit heresy.  I doubt that it is PC to not blindly love a DDD that has been anointed by Oprah.  However, it is important that we be honest with ourselves when reviewing restaurants.  While I can only review the items that I sampled, Sweetie Pie's was not worthy of the hype.  I went with serious expectations of some knee buckling soul food, dripping with love and character.  What I experienced ranged from just OK to completely mundane.

We have had Sweetie Pie's on our list for some time and finally scheduled to meet the D's for dinner.  We went on a Saturday evening and made sure we did not go late.  We had an hour and a half wait.  What is deceiving is that once you get inside you still have a block long serpentine line.  The wait is not the issue, good food is worth it.

Contrary to some recent reviews, the process worked pretty well and we found the people to be friendly, providing good service for their approach.  As you probably know this is a cafeteria line where you order your main selection and then the sides.  There is absolutely nothing wrong with this.  It is truly appropriate for a place like this.  My only slight problem was that the line was so dense that I really did not get a good chance to look at the offerings before they asked me what I wanted for my main selection.  No fear, I selected the Fried Chicken Wings.  Ms T selected the Barbecue.  The T's selected Fried Fish and Chicken Wings.  For sides Ms T and I had Black Eyed Peas, Okra, Mac 'n Cheese and Green Beans.  Unfortunately I did not see that they had what looked like "Fried" Cabbage until too late.  It was not listed on the board.  So here we go.

The best thing we had was the Fried Chicken Wings.  It is a large serving of four whole wings.  The coating was nice and crisp and the wings were hot, fresh (they were selling a lot of them).  I found the wings to be "just fried chicken".  Nothing special.  I have not yet been to Hodak's, but I'm guessing the chicken is at least as good and you would not wait 90 minutes to get it.  I know King Edward's is better and that's not saying much.  Sweetie Pie's wings were OK, but they had no salt, no black pepper, no seasoning of any kind and yet they were the best thing.

Ms T's Barbecue was what appeared to be the trimmings produced when whole spare ribs are turned into St Louis Style ribs.  They were in a sauce that was very sweet and a little tangy.  The meat was well smoked and while it tasted good, it was almost inedibly chewy.  This is something you really want to love, but you feel like you are eating a hunk o' jerky with each bite.  We did not finish it because we just got tired of chewing.  I'm pretty sure this was over done in the smoker.

Sides were also a mixed result.  The best by far was the Mac 'n Cheese.  I liked the style.  It was not pasta in a Velveeta sauce.  It was dryer with good cheddary flavor.  It was downhill from there.  The okra was simply whole boiled okra.  It was unsalted and unseasoned.  Fortunately I like the flavor of okra, but it can be prepared so much better.  If soul means dumping some water on okra pods and boiling it, I guess anyone can have soul.  The okra is advertised as having tomato, but that was scratched off the menu when we were there and it was not included with the pods.  The Blackeyed Peas were a surprise and a disappointment.  The surprise was that they were sweetened.  I expect Black Eyed Peas to be savory, but that is a matter of style I guess.  The disappointment was that they were otherwise completely unseasoned.  I was expecting some ham hock or smoked jowl or side meat or fat back or something.  Again, apparently soul here is either cooking some dry peas and adding sugar or dumping out a can of peas and adding sugar.  I wish I could have you taste the ones I make and I clearly have no soul.  Finally the green beans.  Again, nothing was added when they dumped the can into the pan to warm them.  There was no onion, no bits of slab bacon, nothing.  

I suspect something has happened to Sweetie Pie's since they were discovered.  Perhaps fame and a TV program have diverted focus from cooking real home-style soul food.  Perhaps St Louis soul food is just stuff dumped out of cans and warmed up (I doubt it).  I lived and worked in North Carolina for a number of years.  I do have a basis for making this judgment.  I still return to NC at least annually and we get better food at average places there, without exception.  None of them will ever be sponsored by Oprah.

I did not express my thoughts to my dining partners.  They voiced the same opinion, completely unsolicited.  It is hard to imagine people going back for the things we sampled.  My only explanation is that people are uncritical and DDD and Oprah have anointed it.  And "look, there is a big line, it must be good".   It gives me no pleasure to make this review but someone has to point out the Emperor has no clothes.

I enjoyed this chipotle as I do any other.  This one did not particularly stick out in my mind as far as the food goes because they offered the same choices for food as the others.  The place itself was very cramped and a little uncomfortable standing in line because the tables were right next to you so you almost felt like you were hovering over their food which I did not like feeling like that and I am more then sure they did not appreciate it as well.  The line was long when I got here but, they were on the faster side of some chiopotles they were really churning and burning to get the line moving which is always a plus.  The staff was friendly and efficient because not only were they going very quick they were getting everyone's orders right.   Which I think is actually the most important part.  Parking was nearly impossible I did not bring a car as I ran here from school but, it did not look like there was anything but street parking and that was so few and far between that if you have to drive here you might want to choose another chipotle.  They are also doing roadwork in that area around this time so that also cuts out a lot of parking and really backs up traffic.

While in St. Louis I stopped here with friends for lunch. The food was great home style cooking. The potions were more than we could eat. The service was friendly. Although the food is served cafeteria style your tray is carried to your table. Once you sit down you don't have to get up until you are ready to leave. The guy that carries your tray to the table comes by often to check if you need anything else. I definitely will stop here again when I am in St. Louis.

Food was delicious!! Yes, I am aware literally everything my friends and I ordered had loads of sugar added to it but whatever!! It was amazing!

I had the fried chicken wings (which were huge), mac n cheese, okra, and a slice of white cake with chocolate icing. All of it was yum... Most especially the cornbread. I love love loved it, it was a basic southern style cornbread but was better than any cornbread that I've ever had in life.

Negatives - Line moves really slow and the banana pudding is not well done. The wafers were still on the crunchy side which is no bueno. 

Besides the line, the service was great though! The people assisting at the food counter and our waiter was amazing! I was so excited because I recognized our waiter from TV and I asked him if he knew Charles (my favorite person on the Sweetie Pie's reality show on OWN) and he said yes, which made my day :)

Reality show on Oprah's Network? Yes! Appearance on DDD? Yes! Qualify for a mandatory food stop on the road trip? ABSOLUTELY!!

Sweetie Pies is a cafeteria style restaurant. You walk down the line, point at what you want and the ladies behind the counter serve it up to you! Only problem: we had to wait an hour in line to get to the beginning of the line. But it is worth the wait.

I ordered the fried chicken with the mac n cheese and green beans. Also got a side of the fried fish. First thing you notice is the colossal portion size! 4 big chicken wings with 2 sides...everything is done bigger in St. Louis! Best of luck finishing it all! The fish was perfect! The fish was so moist itself, but the crust added the  contrast of texture with a great crunch! The green beans were good, nothing special. The mac n cheese was ooey gooey cheesy goodness! Best part is definitely the crispy burnt ends. You'll have cheese all over the place, but probably the second best mac n cheese I've had (Chicken Lady still wins). As for the main entree, sorry KFC, but this fried chicken is the real deal and is fingerlickin' good! The chicken was moist and flavorful and the skin was beautifully crispy! Could just eat a plate of the crispy chicken skin by itself. 

For me, the highlight was the hospitality! The entire staff was so nice! Acted like we were friends from back in the day!

You want some soul food love, make your way down to Sweetie Pies! 

Warning: You may be disgustingly full after this meal and not want to eat fried food for a week!

We travelled from Chicago to St. Louis just to eat at Sweetie Pies.  

The food and service were all outstanding! We had the chicken wings with black eyed peas and macaroni and cheese as well as the pork steak with macaroni and cheese and yams.   The portions and presentation were all excellent!

Our taxi driver recommended this location as there were a variety of bars to visit after dinner.

We visited Sweetie Pie's in October 2010. WOW! Folks were lined up to the door, it moved quickly and it was like watching the traders in the stock market on Wall Street as ladies behind the line beckoned for your order choices, if you weren't paying attention, you were down the line without food! It was great! A sign on the walls and the food line said "We won't take your order if you're on your cell phone!" Perfect!
This place was down home and old school, full of traditions many have forgotten, good manners, excellent food and Robbie Montgomery there overseein' it all. This is a top notch spot!! The food? Down home southern cooked perfection!! Sweet Potato Pie; Homemade Meatloaf and baked chicken to die for!! Greens, sweet potatoes, home made mashed potatoes, stuffing, cornbread .... different foods are on the line on different days. We were there on Sunday and it was like a holiday meal. Go get ya some and learn about this former Ikette turned culinary godsend. :)  So, worth it!

At Sweetie Pies....and let me tell ya!! SO GOOD!!!!!  The yams, the Mac n cheese and the chicken are the best I ever had!!!  The cabbage too!!! ALL the SIDES WERE DELICIOUS!!!

Let me warn you.....the original tea (I'm bottle ) is super gross!!!!
Was just ok! Rice was cold. Fish wasn't fully cooked! Something to do while in the Lou. Probably won't go back. But I did it. Wait staff was very nice!
this used to be bachmann's in the 50s 60s....lolz....I ate alot of ringdings and yodels there

This place seriously has the best Pastor and Adobada Tacos I have had in America. I've been going here for six or seven years now and have experienced a (very) few off nights, but the vast majority of the time has been a fantastic experience. If you're the type of person who tries every hole in the wall searching for the best taco, do yourself a favor and come here. The search is over. I've loved everything else I've had here too, but honestly it's the tacos that keep me hooked on this place.

This place is definitely something you should try out if only for the experience. The food was pretty good; I got the bbq ribs, they were ok but I really wish I had gotten fried chicken instead! Mashed potatoes/Mac and cheese/cornbread was pretty amazing. The service while getting your food/paying was pretty lackluster. Be warned: it is cafeteria style! I wasn't prepared for that. Once you are seated there are waiters to get your drinks and bus the tables and those guys were the best. Get there early! We went in at 530 on a Sunday and got through the line fairly quickly but as we left the line was out the door, I wouldn't be surprised if it was a full hour.
 Overall, I probably wouldn't go back but it was cool to experience once.

This was my first time using Basket of Flowers. "Lois" was very efficient, friendly and helpful with the telephone order I called in for my daughter that was delivering a new grandson at Summit Medical Center. I will remember this place of business and use them again when the need arises and will surely recommend them when given the opportunity.

Good Mississippi cooking as this place says. Our merry band of "vikings" took the metrolink and walked a few very cold blocks here. It was worth it. We were greeted at the door. The place has the kind of wood floor that creaks and it's a very large clean restaurant. The food is served to you buffet style. It's the meat and two or three side kind of joint. 
I went with smother pork steaks, black-eyed peas, mac-n-cheese and sweet tea. Block of corn bread comes with it. The drinks are delivered to you. My pork was fork tender. The Mac was OK very basic. The B-E peas were OK. The portions were large. Word was the friend chicken wings, catfish were good. The had whole breaded fish also. Other sides were okra, green beans, yams, spaghetti (sweet sauce), mashed potatoes and deep fried pies (apple, peach). I think this place will be a stop when in St Louis.

Soul food with soul. Too often soul food is another word for overcooked and greasy. Not here. You'll get big helpings for sure, but the food is fresh and tasty. Sometimes you'll even have to wait for that fried fish or chicken to come out because they're making a new batch. Great macaroni and cornbread to die for. Just the way mom made it.

Upon arrival , almost walked out because it looks like a buffet (I hate buffets. HATE them) . But decided to try it. We were already there. 
     Glad we didn't leave. Got fried chicken, green beans and Mac and cheese. Wife got fried chicken, corn and mashed potatoes and gravy. I was so impressed with all the sides! Home-made, full of flavor and delicious! Beans had chunks of pork belly( fantastic). Corn was creamy, butter, and wonderful. Fried chicken was crispy on the outside, and oh so juicy on the inside. 
    So don't let the cafeteria style entrance fool you. This food is top notch. Only down side was its a little pricy, and the corn bread was dry.. Everything else was great and I highly recommend it.

I was visiting Saint Charles, MO, the week of August 1st.   Friends from Chicago had recently moved there and we thought we'd check out Sweetie Pie's.  Our mouths were watering with anticipation.  Coming from a tradition of Soul Food Sunday's in both of our families, we knew that we were in for a treat.  

We arrived at the same time as a bus load of folks, so we jockeyed for a position in line.  I had loved the fact that there were staff outside of the restaurant greeting the bus load of folks.  The prices were reasonably and the staff was hurried but helpful.
