Amongst our table we ordered; fried chicken, fried catfish, spaghetti, green beans, corn, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes and something with okra in it (which my niece loved).  The Children, 4 & 6 loved the catfish, the adults were not impressed, the catfish was fried extremely hard without much flavor, but the serving sizes were very impressive.  The mac and cheese was tasty, but nothing you couldn't find in at any ordinary soul food restaurant.  I must say that everyone loved the chicken.  The spaghetti, well.. I'll just say, it must have just been an off day or a bad batch.  The corn.. now, growing up eating some tasty corn, I was geeked.  The corn tasted as though it was right out of the can with not additional flavorings.  Do not get the corn.

Our service was good, our server Calvin, was fun, engaging and very attentive.

Not sure that I'd ever visit the place again.  If you're going for great food, pass this one up, if you're going for entertainment purposes and to just say "I've visited Sweetie Pie's" go for it and have fun.

Thhis place is amazing. Yams, Mac n Cheese, peach cobbler, black eyed peas, fried fish. Nothing was bad. We got there a little before they opened at 11am, waited until opening and went through the huge line that was forming all the while. It was well worth it, but be sure you schedule yourself a nap afterwards.
Amazing fried chicken! A great southern food experience.  A must-try if you're in St. Louis.
Always my favorite.  I received a healthy amount of everything I asked for.  Staff was friendly and kind.

I finally found my favorite place for pizza in the area. The pizza is made with the freshest ingredients and cooked to perfection. The dough almost has a sour dough taste which just gives it that extra zip. We got the cheese sticks for an appetizer and it was a large portion and wonderful taste. I will be back for sure!!

We finally visited Sweetie Pie's after much hype on this beautiful snowy Sunday.  We are new to St. Louis/Dogtown area and have read/watched/heard that this is a must if you are in the area.  We are so happy we did!  The food was absolutely wonderful!  

My boyfriend and I both got the fried chicken, mac n cheese, greens, and I got sweet potatoes and he got the stuffing.  The chicken was moist with the right amount of spices.  All the sides were delicious.  The mac n cheese was probably the best I've ever had.  Greens were so flavorful.  The sweet potatoes, wow is all I can really say.  I'm usually not a huge stuffing fan, but this also hit the spot.  We finished our meal with banana pudding and pecan pie, bot were divine.  

On top of the food being spot on, the service and staff were extremely welcoming and friendly.  I'm so happy we tried it and it lived up to the hype for us.  Looking forward to going back.  But now after all of that I think I need a nap!  :)

Can't go wrong with this place. They have a great list of sandwiches and a really great atmosphere. My favorite thing is the roast beef roast pork combo. The cheese is sharp, roll is crusty and meet is tender. Once of the best sandwich places I have ever been to.

Chipotle is a staple in my diet.  I hit the Cherry Hill location literally 4 times a week.

I'm just trying to spread the Chipotle stoke.  I'm re-copying some of my Chipotle "lessons learned" from my Cherry Hill review here.  

1.  Don't fear the salad
--It's essentially a bowl with some lettuce on the bottom.  I throw a little white rice on.

2.  Skip the dressing
--It's unnecessary (and it's made from crappy oils) -- just get all three salsas and you are golden.

3.  Barbacoa is really dependable
--It's also the only meat on the menu that is not cooked with soybean oil (soybean oil = not desirable).  I get the steak when it looks fresh off the grill.

4.  Guac rules

5.  Get shredded lettuce on top of the guac -- keeps it from sticking to the lid.

6.  Skip the soda, pimp the lemons
--I ask for a cup for water -- squeeze three lemons in and fill with water.  Lemon aid, for free.

Honestly, the Cherry Hill location gives this one a run for its money.  This location doesn't quite hold up in terms of service and quality.  But, by all means, it's still an extremely solid Paleo / gluten free option for under 10 bucks.  Rip it.

I like Chipotle. This is one of the better ones. 
I don't like Center city though. Fuck that place. 
All these people breathing up all the air. Crowding into places. Can't park anywhere!

My family and I were treated to a meal at Sweetie Pie's on Sunday afternoon by a family member that was here from Chicago.  We hadn't been there in years (definitely not since the reality show era).  Unfortunately, we weren't very pleased.  

I had the half fried chicken special with mashed potatoes and okra.  The chicken was overcooked.  The gravy on the mashed potatoes was horrible.  The okra was OK.  I liked the dinner roll.  The best part about my meal was the service (EXCELLENT!) and the fruit punch.  Other than that, we probably won't be back.

Sorry, Ms. Robbie!  You are missing some beats.  My husband (who works in the restaurant industry) was very disappointed in the way the space was not being utilized at the front of the store.  One of the workers was wrapping up plates of cakes.  He feels like that space could be better used for serving something or something - rather than someone wrapping cakes at the front of the restaurant for everyone to see!

Word on the street is they are planning to set-up shop in Houston.  Good luck with that!  Everything is big in Texas, and they don't play!  I hope y'all don't bite off more than you can chew.  The Breakfast Klub in Houston is on and poppin', along with plenty of other wonderful restaurants.  As my grandmother would say...I hope y'all know what you're doin'.  Sigh...

Hmmm were do I start 
Saturday afternoon - wait was about 20 minutes they had A young lady singing I would guess R&B 
Fried chicken was Fried to hard , The customers raved about the pork steak but it was only OK ,,to the macaroni and cheese was awesome The peach cobbler and banana pudding was to die for the only real complaint that I have Is 
My food was cold !!!!!!
It's overrated and overpriced for what they got. None of the food looked appealing at all and it didn't taste any better either. Just because it's famous doesn't necessarily mean that it's good.

Best soul food I ever had. This place has a great reputation. I'm mad almost everybody in my family ordered Fried Chicken because I wanted to try different things. Fortunately my mother ordered ribs and That was something different so luckily I got a taste of it and it was delicious. The fried chicken was moist and crispy. The service was excellent. Not one rude employee. They are all pleasant.

Decided to stop here on the way home from Texas after mixed reviews from my FB friends and I have to say that the "nay" people were pretty much right. Opening almost 15 minutes late didn't help either but here's my review. 

Service: good. The waitstaff was great.

Food: ended up here on Catfish Friday so I tried it and although it was fried harder than expected, it was delicious. Two large pieces of catfish and two (kinda small) sides, $13. My daughters BBQ wings were undercooked. The mac and cheese and sweet potatoes were pretty good. 

Cost: for two meals, one dessert and water I spent over $30 which in my opinion was a bit pricey. 

Glad for the experience but I can't say that it was the best I've ever had or that I would return.

If I were to rate Chipotle for being Chipotle, it would for sure get an easy five stars! However, given the assumption that most readers have already frequented a Chipotle and knows the goodness that it is (with its standard ingredients that pervades across this nation), my two-star rating applies solely to this particular location. 

For one thing, my friend found a short frizzy piece of hair in her food that was NOT characteristic of anyone at our table. Um yeah, ew. 

For another thing, why would they meld ALL the hightop chairs into the floor so that they can't ever be moved? So basically if you ever go with more than four people, either you're going to have to a) split into two tables, which is never quite as fun, b) have the extra person stand as they eat, or c) eye whoever is at the ONE booth table that's basically always taken until they leave and quickly snatch it up and squeeezeeee (which is what our party of 6 did). #poorarchitecturaldesign

And finally, the servers here can be pretty stingy about their veggie portions, even when you ask for just a little more and it's closing time anyways... (sad face).

I've been here several times.  Good filling portions of soul food.  I like the beef on the bone entree.  Also the mash potatoes are excellent.  I think they add something that makes it very rich tasting.  This place has a great location which is fun to walk around after lunch.  If you want to save some money, go to other good soul food spots such as the place on Compton ave. near SLU medical.  But if you want more ambience, then go to Sweetie Pie's.

Came to STL on business with some coworkers and had to stop by Sweetie Pies. LOVED IT! I don't eat soul food from restaurants but I would definitely come back any time I'm in town. Staff was amazing, the waiter Calvin was super friendly, I would recommend this place to everybody!

Here's what I like about the place.  The vegetarian options.  I eat here at least once a week. Every time I get the same thing: a vegetarian burrito or vegetarian bowl with white rice, black beans, fajita vegetables, and guacamole. It's somewhat   Healthy. Sort of. For fast food that is. And it tastes pretty good too.  The meat looks terrible to me, so I never go near it.  In any event, i prefer it to the other Mexican place up the block.

The food was good but not awesome as I expected. I think the hype had my expectations way too high. The greens beans tasted like the can. And I think $18 was a bit much for 3 chicken wings, 2 sides desert and a drink. I did taste my friends smothered pork steaks and it was awesome. The gravy had some teeth to it and the catfish was really good. They didn't have any greens so I was bummed out, but the cabbage was pretty good as were the sweet potatoes. I gave 4 stars but would wish I could give 3.5 and 3 is too low, because my expectations really weren't met, the can tasting green beans and the price. 

The staff was super friendly and nice and didn't mind taking pics with us.

It is Chipotle. It is better than the place you go to. It is better than Qdoba (and always has been and always will be).

There's nothing specific about this Chipotle that's different than the rest so in other words, you can rest assured that their recipe for success is still working.

Occasionally it gets very busy. It does not however, occasionally get less tasty. In fact, it gets more, and MOARE tasty!!

Also, if you don't like chipotle, you're probably just not ordering enough of it. You need to spend at least 20 bucks. Get guac on everything man, like seriously everything, even your soda. And you can't not get chips, unless you're like made out of freakin chips, in which case BRAVO sir. You basically HAVE to get chips and guac. Also, if you don't eat here at least once a day then you are probably some type of inhumane ungodly looking creature and we shouldn't be friends.
Best Mac n cheese ever. Lots o food for cheap.

3.5 star food.  1 star service 1 star location.  
First off, this place is pretty ghetto.  I saw it was on diners drive ins and dives and was going thru  st.l on a roadtrip with my brother so we stopped.  The sides/desert were really good, but the fried chicken was just meh.  My brother got something else was which even more meh.  Baked chicken maybe?  The ordering was very scary considering we were the only white people in the place and we were pretty much getting yelled at by 5 workers taking our order.  Just had no idea what we were doing but ended up with a pretty decent meal for like $12.   Very uncomfortable but solid food.

Soul food at it's best. It gets four stars because there is a lot of hype and not any wow factor. That being said, the fried chicken is the best I've had in the city. The half chicken is always a food deal.  It comes with cornbread and 2 sides. I always get macaroni mashed potatoes and or black eyed peas.  They are the best sides.

good sandwiches, yup. delicious sweet potato fries, mhm. 
the handful of times i've been the service wasn't awful, but wasn't fantastic. just kind of blah. however, i do understand the reviewers that are pretty frustrated with the place; the food isn't so good as to excuse bad service.

Visited this restaurant while in St. Louis for the weekend. I've heard the hype and even seen the OWN TV series in the past so I was excited to go here. The place was full with out of towners. Its cafeteria style with a daily menu selection and a select weekly menu.  I got the baked chicken-dark,  mac and cheese,  cream corn,  corn bread,  and pear cobbler. The mac and cheese was unique and pretty good along with the pear cobbler. The cobbler was extremely sweet. So sweet you can't eat it in one sitting. My chicken and cream corn was basic and can get anywhere. I wasn't disappointed with my food,  I was just expecting more due to the hype everyone has over this place. I enjoyed my food and even picked up a few sweet teas at the local Schnuck's grocery store. The tea is so sweet as well and taste artificial. I ended up giving them away because I couldn't drink them. The server was nice and entertaining. He joked with my table and promptly removed items we were done with. If you are visiting the area I would recommend stopping here just to say you've had it. Also,  there's a big sign by the entrance/exit of Ms. Robbie for people to snap photos with.

Miss Robbie,  You have got to stop your "out of control" son!  He is ruining everything you worked so hard for because of greed.  He is doing you no favors spending your money as fast as you make it...........Tim needs to be yanked up by the short hairs and learn that he does not own these businesses, you do and he is not spending his money, he is spending you right into the poor house.

So on the way home from Mizzou we decided to have dinner at Sweetie Pie's and spend the afternoon in St. Louis. After a 45 min. wait, we got our food and sat down. We ordered fried chicken, meatloaf, mac n cheese, greens, candied sweets, potatoes n gravy, cornbread and corn. I have to give extra props to the wings and meatloaf. Both were very good. We actually bought ribs, Mac n cheese and greens to take home for dinner the next day. 

So... Skip the mashed potatoes( I really expected freshly mashed) the ribs were dried out( skip) and skip the green beans. Im still not sure the vegetables were made from fresh produce but the greens were ok. I'm not a fan of the desserts. 

The place was clean and portions decent.

Took a trip to St Louis this past memorial day weekend & we were on a mission to try Sweetie Pies. We were not disappointed! Got there early on Sunday & beat the rush. The food was hot, fresh & delicious! My highlights were the chicken wings(amazing!) and the banana pudding(a piece of heaven!). Everyone in the group greatly enjoyed all the food. All the staff we encountered were very nice, another plus. Overall well worth the trip & I hope to return.

Awesome pizza place. Been there a few times and have always been impressed. Tried about everything on the menu. Always go with a pizza supreme or just cheese. The calzone is great and the rolls too. 

The guys there are always easy going and the place is really well run. Recommend highly for pizza in this area for take out.

Well, damn. 

Just had a unexpected surprise with a more recent client being from Swarthmore (where no one in Los Angeles would recognize such an area) and I was only too excited to catch up with an old 'local'. I mentioned this amazing deli that a couple of friends and I would go to after-or between-classes to study and just shoot the ****. I had forgotten the name, but right away, the man mentioned Countryside Deli, so I made a point to look it up. Sadly, I guess he hasn't been there in quite some time either since it no longer exists. 

My default sandwich would be the 'Haverford': chicken breast, lettuce, tomato, pickle and honey dijon mustard on a roll. Sounds so simple, but they did it so well. I recall this came with chips (or fries, I forget) and a always a cookie on the side. For under $8, this was a bargain where out here, you get just the sandwich for that same price at a majority of places. 

Little surprised with all the comments about terrible service. One of the girls from college worked here part time, and although she complained about her bosses, think about it, who doesn't? I realized later on she was rather shady herself, but besides the point, I never had an issue. But this was over 15 years ago, so what do I know.

I read that Countryside may be built once again, so if so, hopefully it will retain the same menu, quaint design, and possibly better service to welcome back those who are willing to return.

Sweetie Pie's is an experience.  It is not your typical restaurant and it is not run by your boring run of the mill staff.  The portions of food are large and delicious and everything is served by smiling and energetic individuals.  The buffet line can be a bit chaotic and choosing what to order was probably the hardest decision to make. Ultimately, I went with the fried catfish, greenbeans, and mac-n-cheese. Mmm, mmm, good.

Fried chicken - good (not enough meat on the bones)
Mashed potatoes and gravy - good
Green beans - okay
Cornbread - bad
Banana pudding - great
Service - good (but I could use more than one napkin when I'm eating greasy fried chicken!)

I went when it first opened and used my debit card to pay.  Next thing I know, I got a BOGO coupon in the mail!  I wonder if they just sent it to everyone or if they got my information from my card, however it happened, I'm not complaining because I'm going to go back to this very pretty space for a chicken burrito that has tortilla that doesn't stick to my teeth (as compared to Qdoba) and perfectly prepared rice (as compared to Qdoba's) for double the yum!

I cannot BELIEVE I am the first to review this fantastic restaurant!  Attention, Reno Yelpers:  You NEED to go try out Lupita's!

Husband has been bugging me to go with him to Lupita's for a while...turns out he and his work buddies frequent the place.  We finally made the trip all the way out to Sparks (it's, like, MILES!)  on Friday night, and boy, am I glad we splurged on the gallon of gas!

Now, we all know that there are a LOT of Mexican places to choose from in Reno/Sparks, and many of them are good.  So it gets hard to say what makes one Mexican place stand out above the others.  In Lupita's case I can tell you two of those things...beef tongue and raw octopus.  Husband ordered the Lengua in Salsa Verde and it was heaven on a plate.  For $10.  Yes, you read right, $10.  And that included rice and beans and tortillas.  I had a sopa and two tacos, one lengua and one carnitas.  The carnitas were so flavorful and tender.  Combo plate total: $8.  Along with our ridiculously cheap meals we were given complimentary ceviche that was so good I was ready to order another GALLON of it!  This was seriously the most satisfying meal I have had in a long time.

Lunch specials are even more reasonable than dinner...starting at around $5.  This is just a great, casual, sit down place with great atmosphere and wonderful food.  If you don't feel like waiting in line at Beto's or spending a lot of money at Bertha Miranda's, give Lupita's a try next time you're craving Mexican.
The fried chicken and side macaroni were perfect. The sweet potatoes were too sweet though. Must try before you die.

Everytime I visit Sweetie Pie's they treat my mother and I like family. Recently my mother had undergone a transmetatorsal amputation on her right foot and uses a wheelchair at times. The staff go above and beyond to make sure my mother is well taken care of and comfortable. Bruce, Curtis, D, Lil' Charles and even Miss Robbie herself have been the best people you could ever ask for. I recommend the Meatloaf, Mashed Potatoes, Mac-n-Cheese, Green Beans and Banana Pudding.
Pizza is tasty, garlic knots to die for and exceptionally friendly staff and service.  We are from out of town and ended up eating here two days in a row.

Bad experience with the line staff being rude for no reason at all. Does not represent all staff, but no guarantee if you will be yelled at or welcomed with a smile. My advice, don't risk it and skip the trip- won't miss much.

Just an all in all letdown. Waited longer than the line would lead you to believe. Place is dirty and lacking any ambiance. Service is generic - except old dude with the gold grill running around taking selfies with customers. That was cool, I guess. 

Main issue: It's $15 for two pieces (they won't let you order a half chicken) of boring, dry and flavorless fried chicken w/ two sides and a drink!!! For seriously?!? Criminal. Don't waste your time, it's an extremely disappointing experience.

Reading through all the good reviews, I have to wonder if I am crazy for thinking this place is just eh...... 

I have heard great things about it, so me and the hubby stopped by on a Friday evening. It was pretty slow so we didn't have to wait in line. The ordering process was very confusing and for being so slow I would have thought they would be a little more patient with me. I didn't really know what everything was or how it worked. I got the baked chicken, mac n cheese and green beans. My husband got the fried chicken, mac 'n cheese and something I don't know? 

The baked chicken was extremely dry, but I know, what was I thinking ordering baked chicken anyways......I had a piece of the fried chicken and just found it ok, there was barely any meat, I felt like I was gnawing on a bone. The mac n cheese, ok, nothing spectacular. The cornbread was way to greasy. 

I am sure this place is great if you like soul food, but I guess I just don't. It is very bad for you and I felt gross after eating it.
Great find for pizza in Hernando County; as good as most Jersey joints I remember (the benchmark state for pizza iMO) My son loves the Chicken Roll.  Nice owners trying to do it the right way!

I'm a Mississippi transplant to StL.  Sweetie Pies is like being home.  I've been twice and it's great.  The fried chicken and the fried catfish were excellent.  The cornbread even has a little sweetness to it.  Speaking of which, SP is one of the few places in town to get real sweet tea.  Portions are super-generous, although I think they could cut the portions down a little and drop the price a few dollars.  I'm not complaining though.  There's even a kids plate that has smaller servings of fried chicken, etc.
Brett, Mike and the rest of the staff are great! I didn't even need to check around....they gave me the best price and unbelievable service. I wouldn't go anywhere else!!

I'm rating this place three stars because of the length of time it took to get served. Nice waitress but I stopped looking at my watch waiting for the food. It's clean, has a bar and the food is very reasonable and decent.

I've only eaten here once, and I'm still full. I'm guessing we easily topped the 5,000 calorie mark with classics like chicken-fried steak, mac n cheese, mashed potatoes, peach cobbler, and cornbread. 

A co-worker would never stop talking about it until we all finally went. Most of us enjoyed the classic soul food, but most of us were unable to walk after that excessive display of love for soul food.

Will I go back? Yes. 
Will I feel guilty? Absolutely. 
Will I get over it? Duh.

I stopped by this location to have them check out a slow leak on a tire. The staffer offered to patch it pointing out that since it was close to the sidewall, it wasn't the preferred fix. He also pointed out that the manufacturer recommends replacing all tires at the same time because of differential functions. I appreciated being given options and having reasons explained to me. I was out in just 2 hours during the lunch rush without an appointment.

Out of all the pizza places I've been to in my 20 years down here, Rocco's is the best, no competition! Pizza is always done very well and exactly as ordered. Crust, sauce and toppings are all first class quality. You can't pass this restaurant without stopping in for a real treat. You feel like you're back in NY at one of your favorite pizzerias. Keep up the great work! 
Add to your must try list, meatball parm hero and calzone. Excellent!

The food was delicious. I had the fried chicken, collard greens, macaroni and cheese, yams, and cornbread. The desserts were splendid as well. The price is reasonable for the amount of food you get. I had peach cobbler and banana pudding for dessert.

Its got the hype, its got the long line of people waiting to be served their meat and the sides, alas if only the food would have been hot, it deserved the 5star rating. The wings were very tasty even at the luke warm temperature. The spicy corn was fabulous. The mac n cheese was disappointing as it was cold and the crust super hard. No i didnt pack the food, i sat at the table. Well i don't know how could i time my arrival at the counter when the fresh batch of meat and sides arrive to get them piping hot especially the meat as anything deep fried need to be hot to melt away the conscience of eating a high calorie diet!
They should change the names to Shittypies. Salty yet completely flavorless. Don't fall for the hype. This place is not good.

Ok. Some of the best fried chicken I've ever had but the Mac and cheese was kind of mediocre and the cornbread a bit dry. Sister cities' was much better. But, they give you tons of food for the price. I may be a it biased on the food as we were a bit annoyed having to wait 10 mins for clean silverware. All in all an ok meal but a bit over-hyped.

After a wait through a very long line that snaked throughout the restaurant, we got 1 meat loaf dinner w rice and sweet potatoes, 1 chicken wing dinner w mashed potatoes and mac & cheese, and lemonade. This was way more than enough for the 3 in our party as we had lots of leftovers. I think this place is over-hyped as it seems to be the only good eats opportunity in this area of the city. The service and basic logistics needs to be improved. The food is served cafeteria-style and I wish the selections were labeled as I wasn't sure what was what as the chalkboard menu didn't match what I saw on the steam table. The server couldn't see my 4'10" mother and skipped her. We had to yell our orders over the sneeze guards and watched as our food was tossed onto plates. Maybe it was because is was a busy Sunday lunchtime, but still. Only the mac and cheese was remarkable and just barely. The lemonade was too sweet, everything else was just ok. Pricey, to boot.

We drove a little further to get lunch the other day and I am glad we did. It was my first visit to Sweetie Pie's and for the life of me I can figure out why it took me so long to get here.
Let me first comment on the "ladies" of Sweetie Pie's, they are amazing, so friendly and down home. They make you feel as if you are dining at your favorite Aunt or grandma's house.
I had the fried chicken wings and two sides. Don't know where they get their chickens , but I think they are on steroids. The wings were huge, biggest wings I've ever seen. My sides were Mac-n-Cheese, which reminded  me of my favorite Aunt's and Green Beans that were equal to my Grandma's.  The servings were so down-home plentiful, I had lunch for the next day. 
I'm going back and on my next visit, I'm dining in so I can experience the true experience of Sweetie Pie's.

Never got a bad burrito here!
Awesome place.
You can customize your order, order ahead, and pick it up.
Fast and Good Food.

Just had lunch at Lupitas yesterday and left SO happy.  Just wanted to update to say that this is such a fantastic lunch spot...their lunch specials are so cheap!  (But they only last until 2pm.)  Mom, Toddler, and I had three huge plates of food, two horchatas, and two beers for only $30.  Plus, we walked out with leftovers.  Such a bargain, such good food!

Good food, especially the wings, mac and cheese, peach cobbler. I think it's a little over hyped though, from the tv show. It was good food but some of my friends complained that they could taste sugar in everything, which they didn't like. Service was slow. They ran out of chicken so we had to wait. It took them forever to ring people up so they could get out of the line and sit down. And they acted like it was no big deal. I think they were trying to find people seats before they rang you, but I already had a seat with a group that had come in earlier than me. By the time I sat down some of them were ready to leave!! I felt like the food wasn't that good that we should have wait in line so long letting our food get cold. But it was still good. Had to since I was in St. Louis.

I waited four years and had to work my way for years for probably one of the most depressing experiences of my life. Sweetie Pies is not worth the hype at least when I was there. The Mac and Cheese was cold and the Meatloaf was dry. I could have asked for more sauce but I doubt that would have helped. One meal with a desert was $20 bucks. OVERPRICED. Sweetie pies is not Graceland. Its not an attraction. 

Long story short if you are coming because you've seen the show on OWN then try it out at your own RISK. It will probably ruin the show and at the very least make you question the trip.

My son and I decided to try it today after reading all the great reviews. We walked in and had no idea what to do. You see all the dining room tables, but no hostess. I had to ask a patron who was leaving if we should seat ourselves or what. He pointed to the back of the restaurant to what looks like a buffett type setting. The line employees were not friendly at all especially the cashier. The food was so-so. The one good thing was our waitress. She was super sweet..

My husband and I traveled from Indy this past weekend just so we could share the Sweetie Pie experience! We didn't mind the hour wait outside as well as the 30 minute wait inside, but what we did mind was the unprofessional staff! We were in line and before we could see the food, we were being yelled at as to what we wanted!  We felt like we were in a mass human assembly line! Don't get me wrong the food was good(not great) and the serving sizes were adequate, but to travel hours to get there to be treated like a kid in the school lunch line is TOTALLY NOT WORTH IT!

Fast food with a more upscale feel. Food quality is always very good and the portions are big. The choices for what type of food is more limited so if you're looking for a large variety, I would say look somewhere else. It really depends on what mood you're in, if I'm looking for more variety, I almost always go to Qdoba; however if I'm looking for a solid burrito and that's it, Chipotle all the way!

I was a bit skeptical at first.  The reviews caused me great concern re: my overall health and well being.  I was concerned about the sodium levels and my girlish (read: grandma) figure.  But we were here for a conference and my colleague wanted to go, so...what the heck.

A short cab ride (I think the driver took the long route tho) and we were standing in Sweetie Pies original spot.  Nothing special to look at and the layout was a bit different than I expected but hey, it's a soul food joint and the environment is NOT the star of the show.

Walked in and it was bustling, but not a crazy crowd.  There were seats (and LOTS of rules - don't hold a table, don't point, no REAL flatware) and a few pretty funny signs ("Anyone looking for a husband has never had one").

The buffet line was full and fresh ("coming around hot") as the tins of chicken, mac 'n cheese, neck bones and other specialties were refilled every few minutes.

The food was pricey but not outrageous ($8 for fried chicken/$4 for baked - what's up with that?) + $3.35 for sides.  The lady in front of me said to the line staff (you betta not THINK about touching the food yourself until they give it to you) "I have a vegetable plate" to which the server replied, "no you don't, it's $3.35 for each side."  She and I just look at each other kept it moving.

I had the Fried Chicken, yams, black eyed peas and white rice.  The chicken was VERY good and the yams were as expected, not too sweet.  The peas had a subtle sweet taste that was surprising but okay.  The rice was...rice.  I didn't eat the cornbread because I was really out of bounds for having the chicken in the first place (sometimes being GF - not by choice - you have to make a decision to just deal with the consequences) so didn't want to push it.

I spent ~ $15 for a good lunch +  $5 tip for the line staff (you can pay with credit but must tip in cash).  The service was fine, not over the top friendly but certainly courteous and fast.  The buffet line can get REALLY long (we just beat the rush) and moves slowly ( think the pay station is the bottleneck) but I had a good experience and was glad I went.  I've never seen the TV show (doubt I will) but the food is worth a visit.

BTW - the 4th star is for the fried chicken (I'm a fan) and even though I'm paying the price today, I have no regrets.

I went on a Saturday at around 4:30PM and am surprised to see there's a line for it. The waiting wasn't too bad, I was able to get my food within 10min. However after I tasted my food I've no idea why this diner is so famous that it even got itself a show it appears. 
1. Fried chicken- the trade off for not having to wait forever in line is the food is cold and old. Fried chicken is so bad and bland I think raising cane's is so much better than theirs at half the price 
2. Cabbage is fine but nothing special 
3. Baked Mac n cheese is cold. I could see its potential if it's fresh out of the pan, unfortunately the slice I got was cold and reminded me cafeteria food from middle school. The flavor isn't there either 
4. Mashed potato is fine but nothing special 
5. Service is next to none, even though there were a lot of staff. A server came to my table after I'm seated and said he'll bring my water. The water never came and he was just standing there, chatting with people.
6 the verdict? For $14 the meal is not pricey, but the experience left much to be desired, and I don't think I'll be bringing friends over as I'm sure St. Louis has better soul food to offer. I'm just glad I didn't came at a rush hour and wait for hours to get food here.

Well.... We got to Sweetie Pies at 4:30p and didn't get our food until 6:45p. Well I can safely say that I will NEVER go there and get the Fried Chicken AGAIN! If you are disabled like myself, DO NOT EAT HERE! Also you would think that the food would be at least GOOD after standing for THAT LONG, BUT DRY OVERCOOKED CHICKEN DOESN'T taste good and a HUGE HUNK OF EVEN DRIER CORNBREAD (NOT SWEET) WITH NOTHING to put on it makes this trip a waste of GAS MONEY, TRAVEL TIME, PATIENCE AND TIME OUT OF MY precious life! I'm sorry I think I'll leave these kinds of places to the people who are just desperate for the QUANTITY of Food and I focus on spending my money to get a QUALITY MEAL THAT FOCUSES ON TASTING GREAT!

Loved their service!  They handled a special request that included three different arrangements for family friends who lost a member of their family.  As it being a sensitive time, they handled my detailed instructions  on delivery to a T as I wanted my friends not to be disturbed.  From the arrangements to the delivery, they executed everything perfectly.  My friends were extremely grateful.  I was a bit nervous since I am in California and wasn't able to be there in person to place my order, but I wouldn't hesitate in using Basket of Flowers again.  I can't thank you enough!!!

I was in St. Louis for a business trip and had my first taste of soul food at Sweetie Pie's. This place had the BEST fried chicken I have ever had in my whole life! Most of my experiences involving chicken have not been pleasant. I'm more used to chicken from KFC/Popeye's/Church's, where dry and unflavored meat is coated in inch-thick breading. But the fried chicken here was so juicy and flavorful that I actually called back home to rave about it. I also got baked chicken, stuffing, mac n cheese, and yams. Yum! I will definitely come back here the next time I'm in St. Louis.

I often find it difficult to find a quick meal in Center City that is somewhat healthy and fast, with great taste and quality products.  Chipotle Mexican Grill in Rittenhouse Square comes to the rescue!

The food is always piping hot and fresh.  I have been to the location four times, and during each visit I found the line fully stocked with food that was fresh, hot and recently stirred.  The store has many healthy options that fit into a 500-750 lunch diet.  My recommendation is the Burrito Bowl with the Barbacoa.  According to their website, the shredded beef Barbacoa is actually lower in fat than several of their other meat dishes.  This location now served brown rice - which combines the cilantro flair of the white rice, with a light nutty flavor.  Other lower fat and lower calories options include the tacos, the burrito and the salad.  (The meals fit so well into my calorie plan that I can even get some full fat shredded cheese.)  

While this store gets very busy (up to 15 people in line during my peak lunch hour visit), the lines move super fast.  The staff hardly has a second to think as they are so focused on getting you in and out the door to get you back to your office.  Service is important to me -- and I have found the crew members here are always on their toes and extra efficient.

The only downside to this newer Chipotle location is the lack of seating.  During almost all of my visits the dining tables have been full.  However, there is something to be said about being popular! 

My recommendation for healthy lunch:  Barbacoa Bowl with Brown Rice, Pinto Beans, Extra Salsa

For a treat (not on the diet plan), don't skip the tortilla chips!  They by far are the best in Philadelphia with a hint of salt and lime.  Better yet, get a bag to go!
Good location. Fast service and short line at 9:30PM on a Monday. Plenty of seating and super clean bathrooms.

I'm usually one of those people, shooting 3-10 photographs of my plate before I take a single bite, but not this day. I did consider giving them 4 stars just for making me wait outside for I don't know, like 30 minutes, on a hot and humid day, however that meal was just two damn, satisfying for me to actually hold them back based on it. Hell, the line is long because it's worth the wait. 

If I lived hear I'd comeback at a less busy hour, or during nicer weather. However, if you are vacationing I suggest sticking it out. (Unless you can't handle it, then you don't deserve to eat here.)

I had fried wings, mashed potatoes with gravy, cornbread, mac & cheese and a taste of my huband's entree: ribs. Everything was totally tasty and on it's own a standout southern dish. 

We went with 7 people total and everyone was satisfied from head to toe, after you wait for 45 minutes they give you a massage with butter and gravy. 

When I go again I'm eating: fried wings, mac & cheese, cabbage, cornbread and trying to eat some peach cobbler if I have room

Side Note: They have a show on Oprah's Network OWN, which I didn't know, but I'm now tempted to watch in hopes of putting that mac & cheese together at home.
Awesome experience! I came in close to closing and instead of turning me away the manager, Brett, helped me find the problem with my tire and fix it. He was also very friendly and personable!

OMG. This is hands down the best soul food restaurant I've ever been to, and yes I would make the trip again just to eat this food. I ordered the chicken wings with mac n cheese and string beans, and a piece of cornbread. Everything was awesome. The cornbread wasn't the best, but everything else was cleaned off my plate. The only things I didn't too much like was that my chicken wasn't hot, it was very tasty but not hot, and neither was my cornbread. Overall, I still want to come back, but next time I'll skip the cornbread and ask for fresh wings.
Authentic and delicious Mexican food!! The sopes are the best I have had, street tacos were flavorful and the chili Colorado is to die for! Friendly, fun and fast service. A must try!

They give you so much food. You will need a take home box for sure. The servers make you feel at home. Very welcoming and polite. Everyone is having a good time. I thought it was a nice touch that they had live music.
Solid great tasting pizza. You can taste NY in their pizza!! Antipasto is huge!!!! We had pizza and flatbread and meatballs! All were happy. Will come back here!!!!

From best to worst...
- sweet potatoes: like eating a crust-less sweet potato pie.  Like, a really, really good such pie.
- okra: I was put off by the slimy appearance, but gosh, I just love okra.  Our garden/farmers market won't have okra for another few months, but this got me excited.
- banana pudding: it's not my favorite dessert in general, but I enjoyed this one.
- mac & cheese: good, rich
- line server: there was some miscommunication b/w servers (relaying my order), but they acknowledged it and ended up giving me extra mac & cheese for it (of their own volition, not because I asked for it).  But, I also ended up sans tartar b/c the first person I asked told me to ask somebody else instead, and I forgot...but, mostly my fault there.
- cornbread: moist...corn-y...
- fried fish: the "fried" was alright (standard cornmeal), but the "fish" was mushy, like that of frozen fish sticks (which I had the next night at home, and enjoyed just as much as Sweetie Pie's)
- black eyed peas: flavorful, but inedibly salty =(
- while we stood in line, one of the workers came by and grabbed my baby's foot, which startled her and made her immediately start crying loudly.  We tried (in vain) to calm her down, and then he did the same thing(!) a few minutes later.  I'm sure it wasn't his intent, but the result was a baby who did not stop crying, so we had to switch to get our order to go.
- to-go containers: styrofoam =(

Slow service, cold food. The only thing that was good was the $1 margarita!!

Ordered a chimichanga, it had tomato in it. It should state that on the menu. I told them no bells because it said it had them.

You walk into this place and you are smacked with happiness. It could brighten Scrooge's day with the excited friendliness of the cashiers and politeness of the servers.
We had moved into town for 10 days and we made the trip twice during that time. My husband and I are absolutely obsessed with the Banana Pudding. We even took an extra home and stuck a candle in it as my birthday "cake"!
I LOVE their Mac N Cheese!!! I have had the meatloaf and the fried chicken and both were very good. I also had the cabbage both times. The first time it was way too salty, but then second time it was perfect.
The food is great and the ambiance is freaking fantastic! Love this place!!

Let's keep this short and sweet (see what I did there?); the place is clean, has really good food, and a great atmosphere, too. It's a buffet, and the meal choices consist of combinations of items from the buffet (though you can add items a la carte). The prices were a disappointment, but not nearly high enough to make me regret coming - in fact, I'll go again the next time I'm in town!

Sweetie Pies offers a humble cafeteria style setting but with a nice atmosphere and really great comfort foods.  My favorite things here were all the side dishes.  Aftering having had Gus's Fried Chicken in Memphis, I can't get excited about any other fried chicken.  So, I concentrated on my delicious sides and gave my fried chicken to others.  The mac and cheese was some of the best I've ever had.  The crispy cheesy crust and the soft gooey cheese within the mac was a perfect combo.  The mashed potatoes and gravy were also very special.  Some of the best green cabbage I've ever had, and I heard from others that the green beans and sweet potatoes were outstanding.  Definitely a solid place to go if you're in the mood for some down home cookin'.

Ok, so I've never seen this place on their show, but I've heard of it.  And now I know why there's a show about this place.  This was some of the best soul food I've ever had in a restaurant setting. Hands down. We shared our meals and I sampled the meatloaf, greens, cornbread, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, peach cobbler and banana pudding. ALLLLLL OF IT WAS AMAZING! It's rare to find a soul food restaurant that does all of that well, but they nailed it. The employees were hilarious and kept us laughing about being from out of town. I ate myself into a food coma and still had food leftover for another meal. Fabulous!
Best fried chicken on the planet. Enough said!  Yelp want more words...  Great fried chicken. Great fried chicken!  Ok Yelp?
Get the pear cobbler.  Everything was fantastic and the portions were huge, but get the pear cobbler. I'm only giving 4 stars cause I waited a while to get seated and ended up doing take-out instead.

This is possibly one of the most flavorful meals I've had in a very long time.  Simple but good.  I had the baked chicken, macaroni and cheese, green beans and for desert......banana pudding. From start to finish every bite was full of flavor.  I loved every minute.  A must eat in St Louis.

I really really wanted to love Sweetie Pie's. Cool place in the neighborhood. Not trendy or hip and I love Southern food and really like Soul food. 
Unfortunately, I didn't. All of the sides I had were sweetened to excess. Now I wasn't looking for Healthy Soul Food as I know that's basically a contradiction. And I expect most everything to be overcooked cuz that's the style. But I did want a break from the cloying sweetness between bites and it was nowhere to be found. The beans, the cabbage, the cornbread, all much sweeter than the other places I've eaten soul food in town, eg Delmonico Diner, Crown Kitchen.
I'm going to give it another try though.

Loved the food!  I don't eat soul food regularly so I ordered 2 meals.  My favorite was the fried chicken wings and fried fish.  You don't need any added seasoning to the meat.  I usually sprinkle a little hot sauce on my fried chicken and fish, not at Sweetie Pies!  I was disappointed when I learned that they were not serving greens on the day that I went but they made up for it with the pear cobbler.  Never had or heard of pear cobbler.  The pear cobbler is a must have desert.  I can't wait to get back.  I had an overall great experience.  The cast came out and were very friendly.  Also the people in line were very friendly.  Too bad they don't have a Sweetie Pie's in Chicago.  Thank you Oprah for introducing us to Sweetie Pie's.

I highly recommend Sweetie Pies!!!  The fried catfish was amazing, the sides and dessert too.  You will defiantly get your money worth, if not more.  I can't say anything about waiting in line,  because we went after the lunch crowd and before dinner.  If you visit St. Louis you have to eat @ Sweetie Pies !!!   Guarantee you will not be disappointed.

Great cafeteria style soul food. We drove by and it looked closed at 4pm, but we spotted some staff outside and they let us know it was open. So, don't be deterred if it looks a little dark inside. If you watch the show then you know the lines can be RIDICULOUS, but at 4, we were the only ones in the line. The inside was not super packed, and there were tables available. 

But, the important thing, the food. For $22, we got 2 half chicken specials w 2 sides each, and cornbread. I literally had 3 meals worth of food - just from my 1 order. 4 pieces of chicken, sweet potatoes and mac n cheese. The chicken was amazing, crispy, and fresh, especially they just made another pan. And, it wasn't greasy, just delicious, not really spicy (in case that's a concern for anyone). The sweet potatoes are exactly like (or better than) the one's your gramma makes. You know how some people's mac n cheese is literally just macaroni and a crap-load of cheese? Not here. There's definitely some red pepper and black pepper, some butter and some other awesome stuff, AND a crap load of cheese. 

Then the 2 girls at cash register were the hilarious contrast of a really sleepy cashier and the friendliest person you could every meet. The one swiped the card and didn't really say much other than lean on the register. The other girl made conversation with us, thanked us for coming in and was so ridiculously bubbly that you couldn't help but be a little happier.

If you love fried southern food, you should definitely go here.  But bring two more people, or tell them you want a to go box for half of it up front, because only a superhuman could eat an entire dinner as they serve it.  This is definitely a sometimes food but when it's that time, it's worth it.

I think Chipotle has finally lost a loyal customer. I have been trying to hang on, but they've become so stingy. No wonder their business is hurting. I always have to ask multiple multiple times for more veggies...otherwise I end up with a sad empty bowl of lettuce and beans for $9. There are plenty of other options in the neighborhood. Chipotle, step up your game!

Good fried chicken wings,  very crispy outside and tender inside, not as flavorful as Goody Goody's fried chicken. Mac n cheese so so, the velvetta cheese a fit fake taste. love the mash potato n corn bread. still a good dining experience.

OMG. 

I live in the north and was visiting St Louis for work. A friend picked me up and drove me immediately to Sweetie Pies. I had the fried chicken, Mac and cheese, green beans and the banana pudding. It was HEAVEN ON EARTH! This please should not be missed.

After reading all of the negative reviews I almost did not go but decided to just because it's something Worth seeing.  My Auntie and I went on Tuesday around 330 found easy parking and had no trouble with the restaurant. We quickly figured out it was cafeteria service and read the menu items to figure out that the options were chicken, chicken wings, short ribs and a few others. We went with the chicken and the chicken wings and the chicken wings were amazing!  We both had macaroni cheese and cornbread and also realized we were supposed to choose a second side dish and I chose the cabbage with the pork and she chose the green beans. All was very good. Very very charming waiter offered to carry our trays to the table, asked what we wanted for drinks and brought back the sugar-free iced teas we ordered, he, bantered with us and that was a good part of the fun being there.  As the service got more slow and there was no one in line , 3 of the serving girls started singing Working at the Car  Wash and it was just so priceless.

Regarding the price, it was $26 for the two of us.  A meal and a half if not two meals each. I don't know what people are complaining about.  This is not a chain cafeteria, and it is also not Goody Goody quality nor service.  Crown candy is in a league of ther own as I soon expect Sweetie Pies will also be.

I will definitely be back with my foodie friends.  Plus, neat to see the old neighborhood blossoming again.

Michael

I asked for balayage/ombré color in my hair. I have medium brown hair and wanted a honey/champagne color towards the bottom. The stylist said she did that all the time. After about 3 hours in the salon, my entire head (except my roots) was beach blonde. I was speechless. I told her I wanted to darker and she said that I just wasn't used to it. I called later that day and asked to come in so they could fix it. They were SO rude about it. I felt so uncomfortable coming in again and they still didn't do what I asked. Ended up having to go to a completely different salon. So disappointing. Never going back there again.

I don't know what they hype is about this place. Is it because it has it's own television show? The food tasted like it was all from a can or a box and was microwaved. The service was horrible. No smiles and eye Rolls. What a waist of my money and time.

I went to this Sweetie Pie's location two weeks ago and had the chicken,  mashed potatoes and corn.  The first piece of chicken was good but the second piece wasn't cooked well enough or it wasn't fresh.  I tore off a piece and the inside smelled like raw fish.  The server gave me a refund for my order and asked me if I wanted anything else.  I said no and left afterwards.  This is the location that's shown on the OWN network.
The absolute  best banana pudding I've ever had.  Outstanding food amd great service.  Definitely THE place to go for soul food in St. Louis.

A real experience... I'm glad we went. That being said, I won't bear that line another time. 

Pros:
- The experience! (Especially when they're filming. It's fun to see the show from the inside).
- The food! So good.... SUPER rich. You'll have trouble walking to your car.

Cons:
- The line. We waited hours.
- The service. They're grouchy and will shout at you. (I know, I know, it's part of the experience...)

Decent fast-casual food. Better than Qdoba. Salad bowls and guacamole are pretty good.

The space for sitting and eating is comfortable and well lit.

I've TRIED to go to Sweetie Pie's two times and both times it has been closed, although I went during the hours listed on the website.  The second time was yesterday at 1:30 pm.  The website states that it opens at 8:00 am.  Yelp says that it is not opened Monday.  I wish I had checked the yelp hours before going.   The first time I went was Saturday at 9:00 pm.  The website says that the restaurant closes at 10:00 pm on Saturday (although I now see that yelp states that it closes at 8:00 pm on Saturday).  I'm just disappointed because I would really love to taste this food that everyone is raving about.  I just wish they would update the hours on their website.  Once I finally taste the food, I will update this review.

The best nanny service I have ever used! They have an amazing ability to attract the best nannies out there! If you have not tired Trusting Connections, you are seriously missing out. I have tried to find care for my daughter in a few different places...until I found Trusting Connections.  I have called a week in advance, and an hour in advance, to book a nanny and have not been able to trip them up yet! They always find a way to get me the help I need for my family. They are a local company are are amazing to deal with.  Life is too hectic, let trusting connections make your life easier!!

Short version: I was their first customer of the day. Had to wait for the workers to finish their personal conversation prior to ordering. I ordered a salad, only to find out there was no lettuce and "there wouldn't be for awhile". I ended up being charged $15 for a bowl of a half scoop of rice, chicken, corn, and some brown guac that had definitely been left out overnight, and a fountain drink. The worker then proceeded to argue with me for another 10 minutes while ringing me up and my food was cold. Best part? I go to get my soda and there is a cockroach on the counter by the forks/drinks/condiments. A COCKROACH!!! They had just opened so clearly nothing was sanitized or wiped down upon opening. I would hate to know what goes on back in the kitchen....

#TEAMQDOBA4LIFE

Oprah, I knew you wouldn't steer me wrong! This fried chicken does not disappoint! 

Got the fried chicken wings and they were so tender and crispy. Got the corn and sweet potatoes for sides. The sweet potatoes were so cinnamon-y and delicious and the corn...well the corn was the best part of the whole meal! There were fresh peppers diced in the corn and the broth was so delicious. The corn is a MUST!

Will def return next time in in STL. I would also recommend going on a weekday. Heard Sunday afternoons were packed so we opted for a Monday lunch and didn't have to wait at all.
ok once and a while. a little better than qdoba. their guac is really good.

I thought this place would not live up to the hype of the reality show. I was WRONG!!! Everything was so very good. Everything. I especially enjoy the touch of having a waiter find a table for you and bring your food/drinks out to you. It's very efficient. 

I'm from the south and have grown up eating soul food almost everyday of my formative years and I have to say tasting the macaroni and cheese brought me back to being in the kitchen with my grandmother. I had such a wonderful nostalgic experience eating here. I will come back anytime I am in St Louis. I really really want her to bring one to New York. The Soul Food places there are horrible.

This is absolutely our go to spot for cheap eats. If you can't decide on which meat you want, they let you do half/half. I usually do half chicken and steak and they're both awesome. Just simple and good fast food.
The food is good, no question! However, it wasn't worth a two hour wait.  I found the Mac and Cheese to be too salty.  The staff were really friendly and entertaining.

My parents and I were in town for a hospital visit and decided to try Sweetie Pie's for an early dinner before we headed back home to KC. We must have gotten there at the perfect time (around 4pm) because it was almost empty. We were able to walk right up and order immediately.

The selection of entrees was a bit too small for my liking. That day they offered fried chicken, baked chicken, pork chops, neck bones, and beef liver.

Ordering was a bit confusing, as there is no true menu. I asked the guy behind the counter for a leg and a thigh of the fried chicken, he pointed to a piece of paper above the fried chicken trays that said "fried chicken dinner - breast, thigh, leg, wing, and 2 or 3 sides" and told me I had to get all four. No big deal, but I didn't really want all of that because I knew I wanted the sides. My dad and I ended up splitting it and my mom tried the baked chicken.

Since we split the meal, we got 3 sides: Mac and cheese, green beans, and mashed potatoes. My mom got Mac and cheese and cabbage. We all got peach cobbler as well. 

When we got to the register we were pretty shocked by the price, that's why they didn't get more stars from me. $38.00 for two meals and three desserts, and we all had water! It's pretty steep in my opinion. And if you compare the prices of some of the meals, you'll notice that some things are crazy expensive. The baked chicken meal, which consists of either a leg and thigh or a breast and wing and two sides, costs around $11.25. The fried chicken dinner which is a leg, thigh, breast, wing and three sides goes for $12.50. So for $1.25 more you get double the chicken.

But, the food was great! The fried chicken was seasoned extremely well. We loved every single side we got and the cobbler was amazing also. It's extremely rare for all of us to be completely satisfied with everything we ordered, we were shocked.

We all left completely stuffed and still took home a full to-go box. We will definitely return, we'll just order smarter next time.

The Fried chicken, Mac N Cheese, green beans, and cabbage were delicious a few women behind the counter weren't the best customer service providers for a place that's on TV that seemed odd but overall ok with me my waiter guy was awesome forgot his name!

I came for the mac & cheese, which is almost worth the hype.

Just so you know, this is a cafeteria-style restaurant, so walk in, go to the rear left corner, grab a tray and get in line. The table will be selected for you. Skip the beverages at the start of the line. Go for the sweet tea, which is just right- I've had it elsewhere where it's TOO sweet. I had the honey glazed wings which were meaty and spicy- very good. The mac & cheese was great, but not the best I've ever had. What really blew my mind was the dessert. I saw peach cobbler and what I thought was apple cobbler. I asked for the apple and was told it is Pear Cobbler. Never heard of it before, so what the heck? All I can say is WOW, it was phenomenal! I will try to make it on my own, but I don't expect it to compare.

Go for the pear cobbler!

This past October (2010) was the first time I have ever been to Sweetie Pies.  A co-worker from Kentucky was in town for the weekend and he decided he wanted us to try it out since the owner of the company and his wife had highly recommended it.
We went on a Saturday afternoon for lunch and it was quite busy. Both the outside of the building and the interior decor were quite charming.
Rather than ordering your food from a server... They have it setup where you walk through a cafeteria type line. We waited for 5-10 minutes before picking up our trays and deciding what we wanted to eat. The women serving the food were very nice. I decided to have fried chicken, sweet potatoes, and Mac n' Cheese. The portions were HUGE. I believe they gave me 3-4 BIG pieces of chicken and enough sweet potatoes/Mac to feed 2. 
It ends up being about $10 per person, maybe a little more. But WELL worth every dollar. We sat at a nice little table next to the window and chowed down. We both were very pleased with the food. Our server was very attentive and quick to refill our drinks.
I have been back several times within the last couple of months and my experience has been the same... GREAT. I've shared my love for Sweetie Pies with friends, family, and co-workers and have been surprised at how many of them had not been there or even heard of it! 

MmMm I just got hungry.

My wife had the catfish with cabbage and yams, and I had the half fried chicken with Mac 'n cheese and string beans. We shared our meals, but we had to get a doggie bag! Topped of the meal with Sweet tea and Carmel cake. Awesome food! Definitely worth a visit. Miss Robbie, Tim and Charles weren't there but the OWN camera crew was filming!

I was really hungry.......So 5 stars......My experience was magically good.

I finished my whole plate in a NY minute.

I ordered Smothered Pork Steak, Mac & Cheese, Beans, Okra, Rice, Corn Bread and Sweet Tea....I also tried Fried Chicken, Fried Fish and Spaghetti, courtesy of some very generous regulars, who felt I needed to try everything....Everything was wonderful.  The Service was prompt and courteous, It was clean, including the bathrooms (something you notice when driving across the country.)  The other Patrons were fun and obviously very nice.  

I'm driving across across the country from LA to NYC.  I hadn't had a delicious meal since Sophia's in Albuquerque NM.  This meal hit the spot.  If you are nearby, this is a place to visit.

I had planned since this morning to visit.  I had eaten very little breakfast to make ready the appetite.  A gorgeous, crisp Thursday morning, I walked in around noon and the line was past the door.  I was glad to see the place so crowed with such a large demographic.  At the end of the line was a jazzy, well groomed lady my age who easily engaged me in talk.  She had an appointment in west county and throughout our wait assessed if she had time.  

Before us was one of the many large circular tables enpeopled family style, they looked like healthy escapees from some high end nursing home.  Eventually my line mate had to abandon and I got to the head of the line.  Beverages were bottles of soda, this cozy place serves cafeteria style.  The daily specials were neatly chalked high on the wall.  Everyday has wings, but Thursday's offer was appealing meatloaf or oxtails.  I chose the wings, it came with two sides.  The line folk called out for you selections.  Most, come to find out, order for take out and get served in take out containers; unlike myself I enjoyed tasteful ceramic plates.  The serving sizes adequate for my $11.50, and tasteful to boot.  

Eventually Chloe, showed up and made it clear she was my server.  I saw her later, too much so for my liking, with a to-go box like most everyone else, who couldn't consume their food had forsightedly requested.  Overall the ambiance very exciting, decor very "Grovey".  I'm wondering how much has its appeal been enhanced by its feature on Oprah's TV network.  I've been her several times and have never been disappointed

Every time we eat here, the food is incredibly fresh!  My wife and I have made Lupita's a frequent lunch destination, and have never been dissapointed.  The chips are made fresh as is the salsa, and these are offered complementary while you wait.  Fast food prices, but 4star quaility, very recommended!

Really enjoyed the whole experience!

We went at lunch and we were seated immediately.  I was expecting a wait, but we were pleasantly surprised.  

The ladies that served us were friendly & fun.  Calvin was our waiter and he was exceptional! The food was great...  Fried Chicken fresh & hot...  Mac & cheese was beyond yummy!

A return trip is already in the planning stage!
The cornbread was the bomb!! We loved it!  Hubby had fried chicken. I had fried fish... It was hot & delicious. Our server & the staff were very courteous.  The lines are long tho.... Great place!
Food was very rich, heavy, and delicious. Heavily seasoned and flavored, just how i like my southern food! I definitely needed a nap afterward, the itis is too real though.
I love chipotle! The staff here is generally really friendly and helpful. Food is always great. Love the burrito bowls. Usually the line is not too long. You can also pre order online and pick up.

Food was great. Very southern, lots of soul. The fried catfish was by far the best I've ever had. Side dishes: cut corn from the cob was mixed with green peppers and had the perfect blend of sweet and savory. The macaroni and cheese looked amazing, but it was too sweet for my taste. It had the perfect amount of cheese on top and baked a bit crispy, but again it was on the sweet side. The mashed potatoes was creamy and standard. Cornbread was just ok. 

The line to order seemed a bit awkward and  not very smooth. It seemed more chaotic than it needed to be.

Umm, I went to Sweetie Pie's twice in one week.  I'm pretty sure that's not good for my heart or my arteries, but it does make one thing certain: I LOVE their mac n cheese.  I guess because the cheese just tastes so real and so hearty instead of those powdered cheese you sometimes get.  

Other than that, I liked the yams, although they were really sweet and the fried catfish and jack fish was pretty good too.  It was fried really crisp and was really tasty, but it ended up causing this huge food coma that took over the better part of the afternoon.

The service here is awesome, everyone is really nice and attentive and even helps bring your tray to your table.

Without having seen the TV show, this is what I expected. Southern food served up with hospitality. A must stop for anyone who loves the Food Network, home cooking, or supporting a local business. Can't go wrong here!

UNPROFESSIONAL - Sooooo I flew to St Louis to try Sweetie Pie's yesterday. While I realize it's the holiday season, the sign on the door said hours for several days this week, were closing early at 6pm, which included December 29th. Imagine my shock when I arrived at 1pm to and empty restaurant and no sign or voicemail message indicating anything different. My sister checked hours before I came to make sure we would be good and NOPE. So disappointed. Ms Robbie this is not what I would have expected at all

Stop by there on a weekend trip to St Louis.  Stayed at the Hyatt Regency at the Arch and couldn't resist to go to Sweetie Pies at Mangrove.  I was pleased with the meatloaf, mac n cheese, corn bread and greens.  Didn't like the peach cobler.

I highly recommend this place for your tire, oil change, alignment, air filter, wiper blade needs.

Brett is the manager.  I have dealt with him and his crew.  Everyone here cares about their company and about providing great customer service so you want to come back.  

I am here now - working (and writing yelp reviews :) ) in the reception area.  I have listened to Brett work with his customers.  He communicates very well, explains the issues, giving options and listening very well to what people are saying.  They not only listen, they have been going out to the cars (when needed) to check them out before doing any work to make sure they understand the issues being requested (important when someone says they ran over something and need a tire repaired.)

My wife and I were customers here back in the early 2000s and we liked it then.  We left Indiana and after coming back, we found ourselves coming back for great service and products.

They will take walk-ins, but I would suggest calling ahead.  They'll let you know when you can get in.

SIDE NOTE: There is free coffee and water in the waiting area.

OMG.  This place is awesome.  It's one of those places that I take all out-of-town visitors to eat at least one meal.  You can't go wrong with HUGE portions and cheap prices - it's cafeteria style, so get in line, grab a tray, and take a good look at all your food options.  I haven't had anything that I didn't like - fried chicken is always a safe bet, but the fried catfish and smothered pork chops were also delish.  The sides - yumm!  Hands down, some of the best mac & cheese I've ever had (the only one that MIGHT be better is the bf's, but I think it's bc he makes it extra fatty for me to get addicted to it).  I am also not really a fan of cornbread, but this place has converted me - I realized I just had never had really good cornbread!  Top off the meal with a lemonade (order it at the cashier) - it's so yumm!

This place has super long lines on Sundays, so try to time your visit to avoid "peak" hrs.

tried sweetie pies for the first time last night.  we got there at 6:45 on friday night and didn't have to wait at all.  all the line servers were very friendly and kept everyone moving along.  our server, calvin, made our visit even more enjoyable.  the food was very good.  i had fried fish fillets with black eyed peas and green beans.  the fish was excellent and the portion was hugh.  the black eyed peas were good but the green beans were bland.  my husband had the jack salmon with okra and sweet potatoes.  he enjoyed all of his.

The FOOD was great.  Maybe some of the best fried chicken I've had.  The sweet potatoes were perfect and the cabbage was as well. The Mac and cheese, which I give a B-, and the "service" is why I gave it 4 stars. 

The Iced Tea/Lemonade mix can send you into sugar shock....just like I like it! Just ask for extra ice and let it melt down while you take baby sips....no dessert needed! 

Although the service sucked and I can get better Mac and cheese from many places, I still can't wait to go back! Defiantly a must try.

mmmm. carbohydrate heaven.
Husband saw this on Food Network. So when we in St Louis last week, this was the first place we came after checking into our hotel. 
Had the fried chicken with mac & cheese, mashed taters and gravy, and cornbread. 
husband had the fried chicken with mac&cheese, taters and gravy, stuffing, cranberry sauce, and cornbread. 
The food was gut filling, rib sticking, carb and calorie laden deliciousness.
The service was excellent, from Mama working the register to our awesome and hilarious server Dee, well worth the trip. 
We went back with the rest of our group on our last day, and again, it was fantastic. A must go any time we make it back to St Louis.

Figured I had to visit Sweetie Pie's since I was in St. Louis so my coworker and I went our first night here. We walked in and in around 7 pm and there were only 2 other tables. We walked in and a host explained that we had to go choose what we wanted from the line and we could sit down or get take out. I figured it would be a sit down restaurant. I ordered the half chicken special and the woman who got my chicken was friendly. I then moved down the line to get my sides and the woman serving there was unfriendly and kept saying "What two sides?"; not giving me time to look at what was available. I decided on cabbage and yams. Our server, Aaron, then came up to me and my friend at the register to let us know that the tip jar was not for him. (Inappropriate). He then took our trays to the table and said he would bring us back water. 10 minutes later, no water, so we asked another server, who brought it. 

The fried chicken was ok, only the skin was seasoned and I took most of that off. The yams tasted like they came from a can. The cabbage, which I am usually not a fan of, was delicious! The cornbread was cold, and when I asked for butter, the waiter brought back a little packet that felt like it had been in the freezer. I couldn't even get through half the meal. Our waiter came to check on us very early during our meal and we didn't see him again. My friend I wanted boxes for our food and tried to get the attention of one of the 8 people standing around on the line and no one ever came over. I then went to the line, where there is a large stack of takeout cartons, and asked for 2. I was asked where my waiter was, when I told her we hadn't seen him in a while, she said they weren't allowed to give the takeout containers to customers (WTF?) Another waiter finally came over and gave us containers. Another waiter, Dee, helped us with the containers and gave us bags.

I really wanted to like Sweetie Pie's but the experience and food was just disappointing.

Wow!  If you happen to be in St. Louis and crave good soul food, make SURE you find time to go to Sweetie Pie's.  The only reason this restaurant doesn't get stars for me  is the lack of seating for a single diner--no stools at the bar, etc.  I ended up eating my amazing meal in my car...which was a little awkward.  Not the end of the world, but a little weird.  I'm pretty sure this place is crowded no matter what time of day, so be prepared to wait in line for your food--no saving tables.  The atmosphere is hectic with people trying to find tables and waiters delivering food/drinks, but honestly it just adds to the fun.

Some entrees stay on the menu each day, while others rotate.  I went with fried catfish, and added mac n' cheese, black eyed peas, and (of course!!) cornbread.  I think I paid about $11 for my HUGE portions of food.  As I dined on my fabulous meal in my car, I noticed the spices in the catfish breading--awesome!  It was light and crunchy, with just a kick of subtle heat.  The mac 'n cheese was creamy and cheesy, and the black eyed peas were tasty.  The cornbread was a nice say to sop up some of the juices from the peas.  I drove off happy after my meal from Sweetie Pie's.  If I visit St. Louis again, I will definitely return here!

Pizza is adequately priced, place is large, garlic knots were great, pizza was thin but cooked well. Didn't flip over when folded. Cheese was nice and salty and the sauce was the right amount of acidic, not sweet at all. 

Highly recommend this place
Sweetie Pie's. So good. Large portions. I love the cobbler. I always try to go on Mondays, but need to remember they are closed! One of my favorites. Wings are the best and the cobbler!

We use their nannies at Unity Spiritual Center of Peace for the nursery kids during our Sunday services. Our nannies are always on time, professional, and caring. We are very appreciative of the care given to our little ones!

Shatangi almost forgot to review this place.  I was reminded about it from a feature on Food Network last night.  This was one of the most memorable meals I enjoyed in St Louis.  Finally a restaurant that was just trying to be itself.  We went on a slower, freezing cold weeknight and the warm service made up fro the trek.  Soul food tastes much the same throughout the Midwest but when made right, the simplest dish can evoke memories of childhood  and summer that make the not-so-healthy combo of salt and grease a delight to the senses.  Mos def on my list of places to go to celebrate.

Shatangi told you...

This place really lived up to the hype. I had chicken, sweet potatoes, Mac n cheese, green beans, corn bread, and banana pudding. ALL was amazing! Staff was great the ATM was out of order and I had no cash on me couldn't tip I felt horrible ....oh well excuse to go back he deserved the tip!

Maybe it was the time of day we went (5ish on a Wednesday), but all the reviews that talk about the line was, that didn't apply to us at all. We walked right up to the counter, there were maybe 3 people in front of us.

One thing I will say, for a cafeteria style buffet layout, the staff is very helpful. I can't say enough about how helpful both the floor staff and the staff behind the counter was. We had never been here before, so we weren't sure how the process worked, but they helped us out.

Best fried chicken I've had at a restaurant Bar none
Great fresh food. It s filling and a healthier version of fast food. Organic but still flavorful.

Wait time? 
about 30 minutes on a Friday afternoon

What did I eat? 
Baked chicken - very good!
Mashed Potatoes with Gravy - Excellent!!
Macaroni and Cheese - Scrumptious - especially the crispy ends with the crusty cheese - OMG the best part!!
Corn bread - a little dry - probably my least favorite part of the meal.

I did NOT have dessert as I was too full.

Did it live up to the hype?  Well, first of all, I thought everything was fairly priced considering 1 - portion sizes were good and 2 - that I liked almost everything I ate, to me that makes it worth it.  I would like to go to the other location, but would not wait more than the 30 minutes we waited - especially if we were starving.  But then again, I wouldn't wait longer than 30 minutes for ANY restaurant - too many options out there.

I have to say, I was a big fan of this restaurant before their TV show was created. I was actually there in the Mangrove location one day for lunch while there were camera crews there before the show first aired. My date and I thought they were just filming a commercial. Boy were we wrong?! The food here is great soul food. I highly recommend the fried chicken (which is huge), meatloaf, macaroni and cheese, greens, and sweet potatoes. I've eaten at every restaurant location in St. Louis at least twice, and these items have all been consistently good at all of the locations! You won't be disappointed. The prices are kind of higher than what you'd expect for a soul food restaurant (around $13 a person), and it is cafeteria style. I wish they had a better system of seating people because the long lines and waits are a bit much. However, I will say that the food is worth the wait.

I have eaten at Sweetie pies so many times,  what can I say "wonderful". When I know I'm going there it makes my day. usually when I go somewhere to eat I have a taste in my mouth for food I order when I bit into it, at Sweetie pies it wake my taste buds up, really it is awesome. Every time I go there the food is great. 

Everyone there have the nicest personality, I mean everyone. When you first walk in you see a smile. My family in LA have what we call our Bucket List for foods that aren't in our state (foods we have to try). They have Sweetie pies on the list.  Those that haven't tried it want to know why we didn' t take them there.

If I could I would eat at sweety pies everyday, really mean everyday. Awesome.

Arissie
