The food was excellent, the staff was very nice and pleasant. There was also live music which also highlighted our experience. The deserts were fantastic. The pear cobbler is a must have!

My wife and I coordinated our vacation to ensure that we made a stop at Sweetie Pie's.  I kept my fingers crossed in hopes that the restaurant was not all hype.  Trust me when I say, they lived up to the hype.  Not only was the food outstanding, but the service was as well.  The food was so good that we decided to visit again on our second day there, and the experience remained consistent.

I never experienced Chipotle before I moved into Philly, and I'm not sure how I survived without it.  I've had several things off the menu and have been impressed with each and every item.  At this point, I'm hooked and am constantly craving burritos.

But, I must admit, that I tried Qdoba again for the first time in years, and they have really stepped up their game.  Chipotle needs to get it together and get queso and a rewards program like you can find at Qdoba.

Fried chicken fried chicken..... Yes please with the "to die for" Mac & cheese. Oh yes I am going to have the corn bread with it and I don't need butta on my corn bread! Mash potatoes w/ gravy. I was in town for Convention and this was on my way out of town. The VIP treatment and decadent food - this was way worth the minor detour to get home. So much food so tasty. Get your soul food on at Sweetie Pies. Thank you for a truly at home experience!

I feel a bit silly writing a review for a chain fast food restaurant, but everyone's doing it so why not! Most of you probably know how good the food is, so I won't go too much into that. However, just be aware that this location is THE prime Chipotle in the city. There is one on 12th/Walnut, but this one attracts basically everyone in the Rittenhouse/Financial District area so definitely expect it to be packed from 11:30am to 2:30pm any given weekday. Even on the weekends, it can get somewhat packed around these times. The line does however go faster than one may initially think. The service is pretty standard. You do get the stereotypical employees every now and then that are pretty stingy on the ingredients (which definitely doesn't work for a vegetarian like myself!). However, on the contrast, sometimes they hook you up with extra stuff, especially when they're closing up for the night or when they're closing early like on NYE.

I wish there was more seating in here, but I guess I've mostly taken it to go and eaten at work so I guess I can't complain much. Last but certainly not least, FYI they just raised prices so a veggie entree is about $7.50 now :(.

I really can't add to all the praise this place receives other than praise them.  We arrived around 5:30pm which is early and we had no line.  As we walked in we were greeted by a gentleman who directed us to the serving line and how things worked.  I guess my daughter in law and I had deer in the headlight look going on.

This is a soul food restaurant or really what is known now as comfort food.  Never did like the word comfort food as my pants get too tight when I eat comfort food.  Fried chicken, macaroni and cheese with side of green beans.  And they gave us huge slice of corn bread.  I am not a cornbread guy but I did like the taste of it.

The interior is very funky with pictures of The Beatles, BB King, Tina Turner, Steve Martin and Gregory Peck from To Kill a Mocking Bird.  Cool.

As this is cafeteria style you eat and go.  We had such a nice young man serving our table and chatting us up I just had to give something extra for his being so darn nice and wearing a tie!!!

What an experience. Went there to use a deal chicken last night. The waitress inform us it was expired all though the expire dated is 2/15. Another server told us the same thing. After 1/2 hour of being ignore the server told us she would call the owner. 
After 15 mins she said ok to use. She took our order for dinner and a pitcher of margaritas after 20 min we got the margaritas. Food came out 15 mins later. Food was good.  Margaritas ok.  What a terrible 2 hour experience.  
I hate using a deal chicken or groupon or such when servers think we are trying to get something for free. The fact is we purchase these vouchers with money so it's not like they are giving us something for free.

My coworkers picked up food from Sweetie Pies for an event at work - we ordered the fried chicken wings, corn, and macaroni and cheese.  The chicken was still crunchy and the corn and mac and cheese were bubbling hot so I was pleased.  I hate ordering food and having it come stone cold because the restaurant made it earlier in the day. 

The corn was probably my favorite part of the meal, followed by the chicken and the mac and cheese.  The chicken was crunchy but really greasy and it wasn't that tender.  And while the mac and cheese was good it was just loaded with grease.  There was litterally a pool of what appeared to be butter or grease just floating on the top.  

All in all it was A-OK.  However if I lived here permanently I doubt I would wait in the long lines just to eat here.
Always satisfying experience to come here. You get value for the money and even more. Great spot for a quick meal on the go!

I waited about 2 hours for this and I wasn't impressed. There was a line which was fine. I get the place is busy, but a few of the employees came off as yelling. At the same time there were plenty of employees who were very nice. I don't eat things with bones, so this could be why I wasn't impressed. I had the spaghetti, Mac n cheese and mashed potatoes. The spaghetti was good, the Mac b cheese was just ok and the mashed potatoes were your standard industry kind. My husband had the fried chicken and he did say it was good. The sweet tea and lemonade were also super sweet. This isn't my favorite genre of food, so this could also be why I wasn't impressed. Functionally, the place has a lot of room for improvement, especially with the bottleneck at the cash register.

It makes me sad that this place only has a 3-star average because the food is definitely 4-star-worthy, but the service can leave something to be desired. Notice I said "CAN." I think the secret is to go on a weekday for lunch, as opposed to a weekend for breakfast. They get so crowded on weekends that things just get a little crazy. I've been here an equal number of weekdays vs. weekends and without fail the weekday experiences have been better. So that's my tip.

Like I said, the food is great. I've had a number of their sandwiches, all of which were excellent, and I love the cookie they put on top. Note that the "Lang Hall," while listed in the sandwich section, is most definitely NOT a sandwich. It's a huge bread bowl stuffed with turkey, stuffing, and gravy and surrounded by sweet potato fries. It's good, don't get me wrong - a little TOO good. I just think anyone who orders it should be warned. (My first clue that all was not as it seemed was when my waiter brought me a steak knife.)

Breakfast is really, really good too - all of the diners around here bum me out with their nondescript, non-tasty breakfasts, and that is NOT the case at Countryside. Everything I've tried has been yummy, and I even like their eggs (I'm picky about eggs).

Hi. My name is Alicia and I'm a guacamole addict. There. I said it. These things can't be helped. Or can they? Chipotle certainly gave it a go! 

I like the burrito bowl. Picture it: last week. Cold, tired, and hungry. I passed by a Chipotle and stopped. Is this real? I thought it was Qdoba or nothing. Alas! I get in line and decide to order my usual from home. Rice, fajita onions no beans! Chicken, lettuce, cheese, sour cream, and a heaping spoon of guac. NOM. I can hardly stand to talk about it because I miss it so. 

Point of this is I'm dramatic and I love Chipotle. I thought it'd be salty like sometimes back home but no! No salt overload, good quality, and delicious. Plus the service was good, they came and checked on us like a real place. I did notice my friend's burrito was on the small side so 4 stars it is, though I'm pained to say it.

Pretty good Mexican food at good prices. They also let me order chilaquiles off the menu and I'm glad I did as they were pretty good. My lime margarita had too much ice. It was hard to drink. My kahula and cream was good though. Nice ambiance and good service. 

A little tricky too find and not as clean as I would want it to be, but a good find.

We were in town for a Bears vs. Rams game and a fellow Chicagoan recommended Sweetie Pies to us. The food was great!!!! Fried Chicken was crispy and juicy, mashed potatoes were fluffy and tasty, and mac & cheese was amazing!!! Banana pudding was the best we ever had. Our Bears embarrassed us so THIS place was the highlight of driving to STL from Chicago. Service was great with fellas handling tables in timely fashion. Worth the wait. Very good place...highly recommended.

Me and my family went to Sweetie Pie's on 06/11/2010 during our family vacation road trip. What sparked our interest was their being featured on Food Network's "Diner, Drive-Ins, and Dives". 

The food was excellent. I ordered Smothered Pork Chops, Mac & Cheese, Okra, and cornbread. Dessert was banana pudding and peach cobbler. My husband ordered catfish, mac & cheese, cabbage, and cornbread. Both of my boys had spaghetti. We came hungry and left very full.

Not impressed by the food at all. The collards were spicy and sweet (like they added sugar), the cornbread tasted like buttery pound cake and the fried chicken taste like Chinese restaurant chicken. The service was decent considering this is cafeteria style. I'll stick to my NYC southern style restaurants.
Headed to North Dakota. Had to stop by. Food was delicious. Staff was amazing. You must eat here if you in town!!

The food is excellent but the wait to get your food is atrocious. You might be standing for 2-3 hours before you are seated. Make sure your calendar is clear for the day before you go.  Also their credit card machine is broke so your forced to use their atm machine and pay a fee. Otherwise the food is as advertised.  The live band was also amazing but I'm not sure I would come back.  I could have saw a movie and come and eat for the time it took me just to get seated.

Seriously...best Soul Food I've had north of the Mason Dixon Line, and considering how similar my mother's cooking is to Paula Dean's, that's saying something.

If you don't believe me, just order their mac and cheese.  It's nothing short of amazing.  The atmosphere is wonderful and it's never hard to find parking outside the restaurant.  If you are looking for home cooking and you're too lazy to do it yourself, just go to Sweetie Pies.

I can't believe I did not review this restaurant earlier.  It is my favorite soul food place.  I pass by two other soul food restaurants that are much closer to my house.  Everything is usually great.  GET THE PEACH COBBLER!!!!  Recently, the inside of the catfish was under cooked.  They will work to make it right, but disappointing if you get carry-out, then get home ready to throw down.  This is a must visit, monthly.
Classic soul food.  Great Mac and Cheese.  Friendly staff.  Wish I lived closer.  Will be back every time I am in the area.
Second time here, pizza is excellent (former nyc)....today was seafood bisque....OMG!....I will be back....probably one of the best I have had.

Had to eat at Sweetie Pie's while hubby and I visited St. Louis this weekend.  It was Friday afternoon and the place was packed.  The gentlemen greeting us at the door were super friendly and inviting.  The cafeteria ladies serving the food, not so much.  My high school cafeteria ladies were friendlier.  However, the most important attraction, the food, was outstanding.  My hubby ordered the fried fish, green beans, corn, mashed potatoes and gravy and banana pudding.  I ordered the baked chicken, cabbage, sweet potatoes and peach cobbler.  With the exception of the mashed potatoes and gravy  that was cold (how does that happen?) everything we had was delicious.  The flavor is definitely authentic and delicious.  The portions were good too, we carried out doggie bags.  The prices are reasonable too for home-cooked food.  A bill of $37 purchased  2 meats, 5 sides, 2 drinks and 2 desserts and enough for a carry out.  I think this is reasonable.  If I'm in the St. Louis area, I would definitely go back.   I think Sweetie Pies should open in my neighborhood.

this was our stop in St. Louis last Fall on a week-long cross-country road trip (LA to NYC) and I still remember the deliciousness!

Generous portions; mouth-watering food.  Really friendy staff: they convinced us to take a few minutes and see the Arch, which was so much more beautiful and interesting than I had imagined.

If I ever end up in St. Louis again, I'd definitely go back

I wouldn't normally express myself via this particular medium, however, this establishment did not live up to its reputation. Underwhelmed is an adjective that perfectly depicts the level of disappointment that I encountered while dining at sweetie pies. From the servers to the food, this experience, as well as, the bland chicken left a bad taste in my mouth. I guess it is partly my own fault that I set the bar particularly high and had unrealistic expectations, but having your patrons wait in a line for 30 minutes to dine at an establishment that is slightly shabby with servers and waiters that are somewhat rude validates this review and my disappointment. While I didn't drive from Chicago only to visit sweetie pies it was certainly supposed to be a highlight of the trip. Sadly, it only confirmed for my family and I that we'll never dine here again.
The fried chicken was delicious and the cabbage was good too. I liked the candid yams and mac&cheese. I can see why it lives up to the hype. Great soul food
Long,long line. Food was good, but nothing too special, I make better soul food at home.
Very good soul food! It took us a while to get a seat but besides that it was banging! They were out of the sweet tea that was sad. I was so full I could barely walk!

This place is newly renovated and looks a lot better. The food was awesome.  Great fried catfish. Huge selection. Absolutely not closed,  just better than before. Wasn't as busy as it normally was which was nice. They're doing live music on Friday, Saturday,  and Sunday. Love it!

I've used Basket of Flowers in the past with extremely good service and beautiful flowers. Unfortunately, I have to admit it's been a while since I'd sent flowers to my wife. A couple of days ago I called. The lady answering was extremely friendly and helpful. Only about two hours later, my wife called. The dozen red roses (with extra Baby's Breath, just like I asked) had already arrived! And she said they were beautiful! And now, two days later, she still is complimenting how lovely they are on her office desk. I couldn't have asked for a better experience. I'll always use Basket of Flowers!

I don't "do" lines.  Patience is a virtue I admittedly lack when it comes to meal time.

HOWEVER--I will wait in line for Sweetie Pie's cafeteria-style lunches any freakin' day of the week.  

Fried chicken wings with succulent meat, home-style meatloaf with a slightly sweet tomato sauce, mashed potatoes with tasty gravy, greens adorned with all kinds of yummy meaty bits, yams that taste like Christmas and mac n' cheese that just might oust Chicago's Smoque from my #1 favorite spot...  I haven't tried the dressing yet, but the woman in line ahead of me ordered THREE sides of it to go.  For herself.  She told me she could eat just that every day and be happy.  Note to self: get the damn dressing next time, already!

Seating is available at tables and booths, and it's fun to play I-Spy with the St. Louis-themed mural on the wall, but it seems lots of folks just take their food to go.  I'll keep that in mind the next time I'm crazy full but absolutely NEED one of their desserts (today's banana pudding looked very, very tempting).  Although knowing me, the dessert-to-go probably wouldn't even last the car ride home.  It's that whole patience thing again... ;)

Sweetie Pie's is a special place, filling your belly with some fine soul food.  If you visit on a Sunday, get there by their 11:30am opening time to beat the church crowd and be first in line.  Just be sure to leave some for me!

If I could honestly leave no stars I would. Food is cold, stuffing is gritty, food is to sweet. I will not come here ever again. I wasted my $25. I'm really upset. I'm asking for my money back. 

And there are nets everywhere in this place. All over my food. I came all the way from Virginia to St Louis for no sense. Not feeling this at all. The value for the money is good but quality is not. 

I've never before asked for my money back from any place until today. I could have just went to Golden Corral and would have been satisfied honestly. 

Maybe Sweetie Pies was just having an off day. I would give them the benefit of doubt.

I drive by Sweetie Pies every single day and for the past 4 years I've been super curious about it. I know Oprah loves it and there is a tv show, but is it really good enough to justify the insane lines and bus loads of people? YES. I don't watch the show so I have no idea which reality celebrity was there, but the food was so good. 

Walking in though is much like arriving at Disneyland. There are signs posted everywhere as to what you can and can not do (pull up your pants, don't point at the food, no flash photography, etc), so don't get distracted or you will get passed by. The fried chicken was exceptionally delicious, enough so that I'm pretty sure my cardiologist should just leave his business card on the counter. Mac and cheese, holy mother of mary, creamy and cheesy perfection. The cornbread was also out of this world. The sweet potatoes, not so much, and the okra was soggy and mushy. And the lemonade was sweet, like call your dentist to address your new cavity sweet. But I will return when I see there is no line and get more chicken, mac cheese and cornbread. Just forget those darn veggies.

I wish I could give more stars. We were so excited to try Sweetie Pie's. The staff was all very nice and helpful. The restaurant was cool looking and had a nice ambiance. They succeed at most of their side dishes. The macaroni & cheese and cabbage were very good. I hear the yams are great. I had to take away 3 stars for these reasons: Although the breading on my fried chicken was very tastey, the meat inside was dry and tasted like it had been sitting under a heat lamp for a long time. The cornbread was way way dry. I did not care for the mashed potatoes, honestly, tasted like a mix, very disappointing. All of the Sweetie Pie teas are absolutely disgustingly sweet like cough medicine, not refreshing. Although my husband's smothered pork chop tasted good, he payed for it later. Actually, we both paid for eating there later. Consuming this food messed us up baaaad! 'Worst digestive experience in quite a while. We can't, in good conscience eat this food again. We're just not that into self torture. I was born in NOLA and have had waaaaay better, actually authentic southern food. Sweetie Pie's food is a bad forgery.

I didn't want to do such a negative review but I felt the need to. A friend had told me about an agency she went to and loved it so I googled nanny agency and found Trusting Connections. It went well but as soon as I hadn't heard back from the company in 5 days I decided to see if there was another company who could promptly assist me. I did and the other company is great. TC emailed back and forth with me about how unsatisfied I was and not once was any sort of empathy shown. I understand there is a no refund policy but when there is a time crunch and you didn't live up to your end of the bargain, some sort of refund should be given. It was a cold no so I just moved on. I did try to talk another girl with the agency but I have so many other things to do and she could have easily emailed back. She did call me and I did speak to her briefly. It didn't make sense for me to give this company any extra minute of my time since  all our communication was done through email and I felt there weren't willing to do anything to make the situation better. It would have been nice to get an I'm sorry at least from the original girl. Oh well. Choice Options is great and they helped me find the perfect nanny for my family's crazy schedule!

Evan is the man! Great cuts and high attention to detail. Gets busy on the weekends - just call ahead to check. 

He cuts exactly to your liking if you bring in a photo. Great at making conversation as well. 

The other guy, Leo, gives great cuts too. Have been coming here for months ever since my buddy introduced me.

I have not been here in almost a year. The last time I was here I watched the Saints game on the tv in the dining room. My BFF and I hit Sweetie Pies up after seeing it on Food Network. It's a tab pricey considering soul food is an inexpensive way to stretch the basic ingredients. 

Overall it was a nice experience, most def heavy, calorie packing grub. So don't go if you're on a diet! 

the peach cobbler is seriously the best I've ever had. Love the greens, mac & cheese and corn bread!

We were passing by Reno and decided to grab a bite. I was craving tacos we found Lupita's Mexican Restaurant. The service is great, the food is delicious and their prices are really good. To bad I live in AZ otherwise I would make this my go to spot. It's a restaurant bar but again the food is delishhh
I was having a soul food kinda day and then I found Sweetie Pies. It was quite a find. The ambiance was exactly what I needed. Lifts the spirit and definitely feeds the soul. Highly recommended!

O.M.DELISH.

My Hubs knows soul food...so when all these places claim to have really good soul food he gets nervous.  Sweetie Pie's definitely lived up to all the hype.

Everything we had was SO good. EVERYTHING.  The Hubs had the catfish, mac and cheese and candied yams.  I had the roasted chicken, mac and cheese and mashed with gravy.  We topped off the meal with one of the best peach cobblers in the world.  Can you say soul food heaven?  As if that weren't enough, their staff is friendly and on top of their game!!! If they had a Sweetie Pie's in Chicago, I would want to go all the time, it was that good.

Okay I have seen the show's episodes and l love soul food!!! So when I came to St. Louis for training from California. I had to check this place out! It was Friday and there was fish but I opted for the fried wings with 2 sides but got an extra side. The chicken was so good and crispy. The candy yams were so tasty and sweet. The black eyed peas were cooked perfectly and tasteful. And the mac and cheese was cheesy, warm and good. Corn bread was sweet and not dry. I had a Sprite with it to wash it all down. And the dessert....was so good. I was already full but had to have Peach Cobbler was nice warm and sweet. Probably the best I have had. I was impressed with the staff being exceptional friendly,  nice and polite. Always came to see if we were doing okay if we needed anything. 

Overall experience was very good, especially from being from out of town. When I come back this way, I will definitely be back in.

First time here in The 'Lou so I decided to pay homage.  The restaurant is in a good location but it's on street parking.  The set up is cafeteria-style so you choose and move. I had ribs, cabbage, and okra.  Everything was tasty.  The ribs are cut small but you get a lot.  The bbq sauce was an original and greatly enhanced the ribs.  The okra was okay,  not too much you can do to it.  The cabbage was delicious!!  Simmered with bacon it needed no enhancements.  For dessert I had some delicious peach cobbler.  Sweetie Pie's does soul food right.

Trusting Connections is an amazing nanny agency. We have used several of their nannies and have been very pleased with all of them. Each nanny was extremely professional and wonderful with both of our small children. They went above and beyond the call of duty. The attention to detail was great. All the nannies were very approachable and complied with all of my requests. I can be quite picky with certain aspects in my home, but each nanny was more than willing to complete requests my way.

If I had any questions the owners returned my phone calls almost immediately. The customer service is stellar when compared to any other agency. They were even great when I had an emergency and needed someone to watch my children ASAP. I will never use another agency again. I have recommended Trusting Connections to several of my friends and they all love it as well. I am always thanked for my recommendation to use Trusting Connections. If you're looking for a nanny agency in Tucson this is the only one that is truly incredible!

i really really like sweetie pie's. i'd eat there a lot more often, but it's quite spendy for what it is, so i had to mark it down one star.

the restaurant is cafeteria style...except you dont serve yourself. you walk down the line pointing out to the serving ladies what you want, and they pile it on high for you. then you pay at the counter and a nice gentleman will walk your tray to a table for you while you're busy paying. once you're seated, he asks what you want to drink and he goes and gets it for you. i was a little thrown off by this; the way the food was served was so informal and then i seem to have this young man very attentively waiting on me? i wasnt sure if i was supposed to tip him or not...

anyway, besides the awkward setup, the food is AMAZING. the fried chicken is EXCELLENT, and the mac and cheese is awesome. i always get the mashed potatoes as well as a glass of lemonade. if im feeling particularly gluttonous, i might get some of the pear cobbler too (although truth be told, i really shouldnt because after the huge helpings of food i dont have any room left!)

last i was there they were shooting some type of reality-type series for oprah's new network. dont worry though, they will ask you to sign a waiver if they want you to appear in anything (i saw this happen to a table of people near me). if you really dont want to be filmed, take the food to go. sweetie pie's is too good to pass up!
Pizza was fantastic! And staff amazing... Place was packed but that's a great sign of good food.

There is a sad person attacking a wonderful person. To claim racism when none exist is worse than being an actual racist. There is 1 person attacking this business for their own actions so please know this is a wonderful business that does great charitable work in our community and is appreciated by many. Do not believe any orchestrated post from people who do not even live in this state.

Well-run, efficient, tasty, dependable, quick. 

I order the burrito bowl every time, changing up the protein, and am never disappointed. Very consistent as far as quality and taste, and love that the beans no longer are cooked with bacon grease. Well done Chipotle!

What more can you ask for?

This is one of my all time favorite restaurants in St. Louis!

The setting is comfortable, nice, yet not extravagant. The staff are very pleasant and the food is freakishly delicious.

I HIGHLY recommend the meatloaf and mac and cheese. I've tried to replicate both at home to no avail. I guess i just need more soul.

We went to Sweetie Pie's on an early Saturday evening for dinner after seeing a matinee show at the Fox.  Wow!  The food here reminds me of my childhood and eating a special dinner at grandma's house.  I had the fried fish and sides of sweet potatoes and mac n cheese.  Everything was fabulous.  Yes, I said fabulous.  The food is served cafeteria style so you have to stand in line to select what you want to eat.  They offer soda in bottles and fresh lemonade.  I had the lemonade and it was excellent.  For dessert I had the rum cake.  OMG!  It was awesome.  We took enough food home with us for a couple more meals.  We will definitely be back!

I went with my mom and her church for a day trip. We had a great experience. The Upper Crust was exactly what we expected. Everyone was extremely nice and helpful. Our bus arrived early so we waited and were allowed in a little early which was appreciated since we had older members in our group. We all loved the food. The only complaint any of us had was about the green beans which no one enjoyed. They were greasy. The fried chicken, smothered pork chops, and fried fish were all divine. We all loved the corn bread and black eyed peas. The spaghetti was good as well. Well last but not least, the peach cobbler was to die for- it was extremely sweet but hey its dessert and it was made very well. The food was rich and not great for the figure but getting there every now and then will be a well deserved treat. We were also pleased to see Charles. My aunt adores him and he was very polite indulging all the questions coming at him all at once and allowing people to take pics with him. forgive me but I forgot Ms. Robbie's sisters name but she was so sweet and delightful. She was a joy to be around.  

Gotta support the black owned businesses. 
Congrats on the success and may they have continued success.

It's been a while since I have eaten here but that's because I will never go back. I had the fish, sweet potatoes and beans. Sweet potatoes were so good but everything else was not so good. I was not a fan of how they served the food, felt like I was being forced to choose immediately and wasn't given time to really look and decide what I wanted but just pushed through the line.  The waiter who brought our drinks out was fun, he was entertaining and keep our glasses full.

In town for business, so I had to check out Sweetie Pies.  The line was wrapped around the bar because a couple tour buses beat me there.  The wait was ridiculous and the setup of the cafeteria counter did not facilitate speedy service.  They had far too many waiters wandering around and not enough people scooping out food.  The decor was a bit all over the place, and I wasn't a big fan of my sides.  The macaroni was a bit overcooked and the noodles were soft in my opinion and the sweet potatoes were too mushy and far too sweet.  However, all that being said, I ordered the fried chicken and for $12 you get half a chicken and 2 sides, which is enough to feed a small family.  Now for the meat.  The fried chicken was absolute perfection.  I was lucky in my timing and they brought out a freshly fried batch right as I got to order.  The skin was perfectly seasoned and fried.  Finger licking good.  I will be back, but I won't order sides next time.  It's definitely a staple in STL and a place you should check out for the history, and the chicken!  Also, if you're on a diet, take a day off...who wants to eat baked chicken at a fried chicken joint?

I could eat a whole pie alone it's that addicting!!! In search of NY style pizza while in Florida and stumbled upon Rocco' s while leaving Target. 

Rocco ' s is a take out or dine out Italian pizzeria.  Ample dining seating and very courteous wait staff. Our waitress was from Staten Island and shared that several others were from up north. There are paintings and photos of the New York City skyline.  

We ordered a half pepperoni half sausage pie. When it came out we were amazed by the perfection. The cheese and sauce were just right, the dough and crust were thin and not chewy like much of what you will find in other states. The MEATS!!!! The sausage was fine cut and just. ...damn good! I usually hate sausage. This pizza was flavorful! I'm unsure what they used but...if you dine anywhere else for pizza, you're a fool. The prices here are on the money. I've never had a pie in NYC for $17.99 with quality ingredients and taste.

It's kind of ridiculous the amount of food you get for the price.  Very good soul-food in the St. Louis Area.  On this outing I had the fried wings, mac & cheese and cabbage and collards.  Best fried chicken I've had to date.  Too awesome really!  Don't tell my wife - but the mac & cheese was on par w/ hers.  I'd give them more stars if I could have had a cold beer or glass of wine w/ dinner.

This Chipotle's burrito building efficiencies are paragon. They must have gotten A+'s at burrito school. You know how sometimes they just throw the beans on there with all their bean juice, and the tortilla is sog city? Not here. The cashier was in swipe zone and wasn't gonna quit until all the cards were swiped. She was like "can't stop, won't stop" and just kept swipin and swipin her way through the lunch onslaught, only taking a break to wipe the sweat from her brow, and high five herself. On. Her Gaaaame.

I needed to get an annoying, slow leak fixed on a tire. Bret is at the helm of Indy Tire & he treated me like an old friend when I walked in the doors for the 1st time. It only cost $18 for the repair. He is very personable, professional, respectful of my time. I worked in customer service at the phone company for 12+ years and I know great service when I get it. I have been a Firestone girl many years, now I am an Indy Tire girl. Just walking in the door - the vibe here is good! 
 I dropped off my car & had a tennis match down the road. He passionately high fived me for the win when I came back for my car! My new place for oil changes, brakes, tires, all things auto.
This place is a sensory sensation! The sights, sounds, and smells heighten your being. You're guaranteed to leave nourished, body and soul.

First place we stopped on our tour of the South East 2011.  And so far it has been hands down the BEST!  I love me some Soul Food and Sweetie Pies brought it.

The food was outrageously delicious and they just keep piling on the sides. I had the Meatloaf with a side of corn, macaroni and cheese, and mashed potatoes.  The meatloaf was better than my own and I like my cooking.  The corn had something in it like peppers and it was cooked in something.  Love probably because I loved eating it.  The Mashed potatoes were light and fluffy and delicious.  But oh the Macaroni.  That Mac and Cheese was to die for.  Seriously some of the best food I have had in a long time.

The service is not to be dismissed either.  The workers there were very friendly and we happy to explain how everything worked to a couple of rookies, and they never left us in want for anything.  They were masters at leaving you alone yet stopping by to offer things like refills and to go containers. They were unfailing polite.  Ever heard of how southerns are really just the most polite people, these guys and gals epitomize this.

Without equivocation or mental reservation I would highly recommend this place and I put it on my top 5 restaurants in the last year.

My 1st time here, got tired of dealing with Firestone and Meineke for auto repairs.  This has a family feel, they scheduled my appt for my 1974 MGB, and were able to deal with tube tires (others will not). Paid very reasonable price. Highly recommend these guys.

I was a bit taken back by the price $$$$ to eat at Sweetie Pies. For a 3 piece wing meal that comes with 2 sides and cornbread the price is $12.75, to add an additional side was $3.60, to further add a side of dessert was another $3.60, plus my daughters food was $8.25. I'm leaving drink prices out but I paid 37 dollars to eat at a semi buffet style. I've never seen a buffet that you can't serve yourself at. What I don't understand is, we have to sit down in order to get our drinks. And refills are dollar, everywhere else has free refills on sweet tea. After complaining about the price, the food was very good!!!!!!

Other parents encouraged me to write this review so that I could save people some $ and possible frustration.

The owners bill this company as "Tucson's premier nanny service", and charge prices in line. The Flex service ($16/h after a $180/6 mo membership was purchased) was a hassle and generally ranked well below the quality of sitters I have hired from other online services or through friends' recommendations ($10/h on average). 

The first nanny that TC sent (for two children less than 2 years old) didn't change diapers (both children were wet and one soiled for hours) and she disregarded our written instructions for no screen time. Another nanny requested physical intimacy in exchange for a child's request for food (I work from home and overheard this), and also disregarded our written instructions for no screen time.  When I contacted the agency, I received emails back from the owners that were condescending, attacked my character, and dismissive of my concerns -- the nanny was just "being playful" holding food over my child; personal photos on a cell phone did not count as screen time; if only I had given more feedback their nannies could have done better. 
This last comment was in stark contrast to the "Laminated Family Profile Sheet" that the owner does a home interview with you about, that I thoroughly filled out with our family's wishes and then explicitly showed to each sitter.  TC says this sheet is meant "to keep in your home so you don't have to spend time communicating care instructions...and other pertinent information with each nanny..." 
Sounds great, like so much of what TC offers, but if your wishes (or basic respect or sanitation!) are not minded, and the owners justify or excuse these behaviors, why pay such a premium for this service?

Awesome!

I love soul food!  I effin' love it!  I've eaten it all over the country and this place is as good as any I've had.

First of all, the location was in a cool part of town.  I'm not familiar with it (The Grove) but it seems urban, historical, had some nice murals painted on buildings, etc.  I might have to return with a camera.  Street parking (some metered) for S-Pie's is in a residential neighborhood.

For people complaining about the line, I went on a Thursday when it opened (11:30am) and was greeted by a massive line of ten people so, plan accordingly.  You don't go to the most popular soul food restaurant in a city on a Sunday after church and complain about the crowd.  And I'll parlay a suggestion I've made on other reviews:  it's crowded for a reason.  I'm sure there are much less desirable restaurants around town with no lines that'll be happy to seat you right away.

As far as the serving line, I wasn't met with poor, unfriendly service.  Then again, I usually take ownership of the way others treat me.  If you're friendly, smile, and get them laughing, they'll usually be nice to you (and give you larger servings).

As for the food, here's the breakdown from what I ordered:

Meatloaf:  4 stars.  I'm not big on pepper or tomatoes and it was inundated with both but, still, it worked.  A nice flavor.

Mac n Cheese:  3.5 stars.  I'm big on mac n chz and have had much better at BBQ joints throughout the South so I'll give this a "good, not great."

Mashed Potatoes n Gravy:  3.5 stars.  Again, lots of black pepper in the gravy.  Still, good taste.  

Corn:  5 stars.  This was some of the sweetest corn I've ever tasted.  It could have been labeled as a dessert.

Cornbread:  1 star.  Dry and tasteless.  Boston Market has better corn bread.  TIP:  Avoid the dry, tasteless cornbread.  Eating the heavy, starchy brick of cornbread will fill you up faster and prevent you from enjoying more of the great food.  

Peach Cobbler:  5 stars.  To die for.  Unbelievable.  I'm more of a banana pudding guy (and it looked great) but tend to lean towards a restaurant's more popular dish and I'm glad I did.

Not since eating at Nashville's Loveless Cafe have I sat so long at a table, completely full, but unwilling to leave until I finished my plate because -- food that tastes this good shouldn't be wasted.

I'll be back.

some of the sandwiches at this place are truly phenomenal. try the turkey with sweet potato fries. the lemonade is good too. this is as genuine as place as you will get. if you're ever in the swarthmore, pa, area, be sure to stop by.

This place was close to work so I decided to check it out.  I called the same day and they were able to fit me in.  Got one of the best hair cuts that I have ever had by Jenny.   She was really nice and listened to what I wanted.  I left some of the decisions up to her and I couldn't be happier with the result.  So happy to have found my new salon!  Side note.. The salon was really clean and they also offer massages, facials, mani/pedis, etc.  it's seemed to be full service.   They also offer you a drink right when you walk in which I thought was nice.  The haircut was $33 ( I don't know if all the stylist charge the same), which I thought was well worth it.

I had the misfortune of having to spend about 2 weeks at the Howard Johnson Clearwater when I first moved to the area. It was AWFUL. 

I could list dozens of reasons to avoid this hotel, but I will just go over a few: 

First, staying in the rooms will make you sick. I am unsure if the problem is that they do not clean the rooms properly or if it is that they do not change the air filters in the air conditioning units or if there is some other, unknown, problem, but I had SEVERE allegery problems from the minute that I arrived at the hotel. And it was not just me, as EVERY person I encountered at the hotel had the same symptoms: heavy sniffling, constant coughing and frequent sneezing. The symptoms would ease when I left the room, and I recovered quickly once I checked out of the hotel.

Second, the hotel seems to be a central party location for local townies on Friday and Saturday night. On each of the two weekends during which I stayed in the hotel, the loud music (along with the constant talking/yelling on the balcony) made it impossible to sleep. Complaining to the front desk had absolutely no effect.

Which brings me to my final point, that the staff is unhelpful and rude. When I checked into the hotel, and told the clerk that I was a professional, in the process of relocating to the area, I was treated with a lecture as to how there are "too many rich professionals" in Florida, and how the state "needs lawyers and bankers to leave". And things got worse from there.

There are a few good things about the hotel (the location is decent, the free breakfast is good, the wi-fi is fast), but none of those traits are remotely unique. Further, none add enough value to make it worth staying at the Clearwater HoJo. Avoid it at all costs.

It has taken me four years to take my family here, but finally it happened. My mother and grandmother have been raving about this place for years (they are fans of the TV show). Thankfully there was no one at this particular restaurant this past Friday for dinner. I will say that everyone we encountered was really polite and courteous. Security met us at the front entrance and introduced us to our server. We then proceeded to the buffet style line. I had the fish, mac and cheese, and sweet potato while my family members had different combinations of the following: Chicken, mash potatoes, okra, cabbage, and corn. 

The Good:
The chicken was crispy and had the perfect amount of flavor. The same goes for the fish. I was given two pieces of catfish. Large pieces (thank you). The mac and cheese was good but not great. I have had it before at this location and it was much better. I like that they put a little sugar in the mac and cheese to give it some sweetness but that was lacking this day.  It could have used more flavor. The mac and cheese used to be one of my favor things on the menu and convinced me to try to use sugar in my home made mac and cheese.  I hope that today's blunder was a temporary one. THE YAMS.. THE YAMS.. THE YAMS. They had the perfect amount of brown sugar. There is no need for dessert if you get the yams.  I really wish I had their recipe. This was my first time having the cabbage and I am really happy I was able to try it. It was perfectly seasoned. It taste just like my mother would make.

The cornbread was really good. My only negative about the cornbread was that it wasn't sweet. I am from the south and when I eat cornbread I am expecting it to have a little sugar.

On to the bad: 
The okra had no seasoning. None. I am not a fan of putting salt in my food after it has already been prepared but the okra needed something. The corn was not that great either. It was pretty average. It wasn't bad, but I expected for it to be seasoned better. The mash potatoes were meh. Cooking the mash with more butter may have done the trick. I also think the brown gravy on the mash could have been seasoned better. This would have given the mash a bit more of a pop! 

Overall I enjoyed my experience and my family enjoyed theirs too. I think that the food here is B+ when it comes to soul food but the service is top notch. I am leaving St. Louis soon and I am happy that I had the chance to eat here again.

If you're down for some home-styled comfort food this is the place to go!

I've ate here several times after seeing it on Diners Drive-Ins and Dives. On the episode they claimed it was the best mac'n'cheese in St. Louis so I had to try it. My verdict? They were right.

 The mac'n'cheese is what keeps me coming back.The reason for the three rating is because the other entrees baked chicken and smothered pork steak didn't appeal to me. The baked chicken is soggy and the smothered pork steak was not very flavorful. However, my favorite items and the friendly staff (everyone seems genuinely friendly and happy to be there! keeps me coming back. The meal I always order is mac'n'cheese, mashed potatoes, and fried chicken. If these three dishes are picked I doubt anyone can be disappointed.

Great home style food and friendly service will definitely go back when I'm in town! I had the baked chicken but couldn't help to steal a few pieces of fried chicken from my family they definitely have the best breading on their fried chicken. Sides were all great especially the corn. I had the peach cobbler as my desert it was great I had to force it down though since I was so full from the huge portions. Lastly if you don't have the lemonade... You are doing yourself an injustice!

The food is 4.5 stars. I like the catfish better than the ribs or fried chicken. Actually the chicken is kinda bland. Good sides includes corn, mac n cheese. The cobbler is only ok. 

The wait is 1 star. Their system is no system and is designed for maximum inefficiency and is infuriating. I have yet to go without a wait of 1.25-1.5 hours. And because they have no separate takeout line, there is no way to avoid the wait.

How many times have I been told that I have to go to Sweetie Pies as a right of passage as new St. Louis resident? Many. Finally went on a Sunday night, despite there being no line it took what seemed like decades to get our food. Not only were the workers utterly disgruntled and slower than mollasses but there were people just standing there when they could have expedited service. 

The saving grace was our waiter Calvin. Utterly personable and prompt with service he greatly contrasted the Siberian gulag-esque service we received at the buffet line. The food, was above mediocre but barely decent. Their way of conveying deliciousness is to over season everything with salt, fat, and black pepper. The fried chicken was slightly dry, having been sitting out on the warmers for hours. 

Again another instance of just because it is famous or on TV doesn't mean it merits the accolades of "best southern food in St. Louis"

It's as if Jesus came down and laid his hands on that mac n' cheese, y'all. We used to go to a little soul food place when we lived in New Orleans called Dunbar's Creole Cooking on Freret Street, and Sweetie Pie's has the same food and the same wonderfully nice folks. The yams were tooth-achingly good, and the smothered pork steak was delicious.  And that mac and cheese? Hoo boy.
I brought home some peach cobbler 'cause I couldn't stuff myself there any further. Oh man, with a cold glass of milk...put me to bed now.

This is a truly delicious place to eat. Don't worry about fancy spices and expensive items that are hard to pronounce. This is food, real food. The kind of food that made America what it is, overweight and cocky. 
All of America's bloated ethnocentrism aside, I decided to stop by here after watching "Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives" on the Food Network. I have been back twice and will continue to go back. 

I thoroughly enjoy the smothered pork and the mac-n-cheese. I also suggest the Fried Chicken (don't expect KFC, this is the real stuff!).
I went to sweeties pies today the food was good and staff was nice,took a lot of pictures and it topped off my vacation to st louis

This was my first time here (on a Saturday night) and mostly likely my last.
The food was very average. The atmosphere was pretty undesirable (the customers influenced this heavily), but the prices were very reasonable.
When the chips and salsa we're brought to our table I immediately knew I would not be a fan of their salsa...and I was right. The salsa (chile verde) brought with our food was also subpar. For me, salsa is usually a make or break with Mexican food because I eat it with every bit which means it  has to be as good or better than the food.
The wait staff was very nice and work very hard at this establishment.

It breaks my heart to leave. ;( The young waiters are very nice. The good was great! mac and cheese, roast beef, dessert, so good! can't wait to come back to St. Louis to visit again! I know it'll be wrong if I asked for a "healthy" version =P

I am thrilled when a local person hits a home run with a restaurant, it is a rare occurance.

Let me be clear, if it were not for the Oprah Channel, and the publicity it generates in the black community, Sweetie Pies would have closed long ago.

I love soul food.  I love fried anything.  I love greens.  I hate canned veggies, and that is the speiciality of Sweetie Pies.

Sad to say that the quality is totally inconsistent.  It seems to be a function of whether anyone is watching the kitchen staff, for the food to be properly seasoned.

I love fried chicken, and the only way to get it at Sweetie Pies is an order of 3 fried chicken wings.  Sorry that just will not cut it, I want thighs and breasts and not greasy bones.

The fried catfish was way overcooked and so bony as to be unpleasent.

Sylvia's of Harlem, this ain't!

I am not a fan of long tables where you get to sit with people you don't know.

If a Soul Food restaurant serves pork, it better be smoked, no such thing at Sweetie Pies.

A neat gimmick, and as long as Oprah supports them, the restaurant will remain open, regardless of the unseasoned schlock they serve.

Basically you wait in line for mediocre food that is served Mess Hall style by employees who emulate zombies, then Sweetie pies is your choice.

Tremedously over rated.

She may have been an Ikette, but never found a salt shaker!

First and last time here! Unfortunately our food was extremely salty! I ordered a ceviche de camaron tostada, my husband ordered 2 ceviche pescado tostadas and lastly my son had a carne asada burrito.  I'll admit my ceviche de camaron was the only dish with a decent flavor, However my poor child didn't say anything about his burrito til he was half way done. He described it as sour , so I got concern and tasted the meat! WOW it was extremely salty! I can't believe he even ate half of the burrito like that! My husband also complained about his food being salty. After asking for the check I decided to mention to our waitress that our food was extremely salty. She thanked us for the feedback but stated she couldn't do anything regarding our check. (I never asked her to deduct or suggested I wasn't going to pay my bill ) I was very disappointed not only in the food, but the customer service.

This place was the highlight of my visit to St Louis.  I was in town with family for the Bears vs Rams game and I must say I am so glad we stopped in.  The food and ambient was very good.  Best cat fish I've ever had and the Mac and Cheese was excellent. Services was great. Banana pudding was the best thing i've ever had.   Highly recommend Sweetie Pie's.

Sweetie Pies was o-k. I had high expectations but my fellow yelpers had already told me to expect minimal. It was kind of dirty , but at least our food was warm, which was my concern since many people had reviewed that theirs was not. The ambiance is home-y, but the restaurant is kind of off, when you walk in the right side offers absolutely nothing and kind of brings the place down a bit. Not really much to say, but would not return.

Went to Sweetie Pie's last night with a frat brother. Omg the food was so good. The porksteak was tender and flavorful. The server drowned it in gravy before i could stop her. I had the cabbage which was seasoned and cooked to perfection. Not mushy at all! Also has the mac and cheese.  It was excellent almost as good as mine. I had to take my peach cobbler back to my room. It was delicious. I also had a chicken wing that was crispy and well seasoned.

It's been a while since my last visit, so I couldn't NOT stop in for food while driving by.  Once again, never disappointing.  This time I had the fried pork chop...O M G.  It may be my new favorite.  And of course I couldn't resist the mac & cheese, the best stuff in town!  And lucky for me, a fresh batch of cornbread was coming out as my tray was coming down the line...mmm.

The staff is incredibly nice, and one of the ladies took one look at my pork chop and threw in one of their delicious fried chicken wings (still jointed, so really 2 wings!) - she must've known what a secret fat a** I am bc she simply said, "Honey, this pork chop is way too small.  I'm throwing in some chicken for you!"  How can you not fall in love with that?!?!?!  Esp since normally it'll cost you an extra $1.25 for that wing...LOL.

Oh yea, I know I already said it, but get that lemonade.  Mm mm mm....

Sweetie Pie's, I HEART YOU.

I love Chipotle I wish they had one closer to my place.  This is probably the closet one but its downtown in a not so easy area to park so unless I wan to walk 25 minutes or a burrito I only hit it up once and a while.

Line move fast they were extra generous on the gacu which is a super plus I hate when people are stingy, especially if you are paying extra for it.  I tend to get the veggie burrito it comes with gacu but occasionally I get something else and usually add it.

Wait time was 1 1/2 hrs on a Saturday afternoon.  A little much I thought.  I had the fried catfish, cabbage and mac n cheese.  Catfish was VERY greasy and almost overcooked.  The mac n cheese was great.  Cabbage-ok.  Even though you receive huge portions of food for your money I don't think it is worth the wait in line.

Sweetie Pies is so greasy and not really my style. I thought the food had okay flavor, but nothing really special. Go for the experience, because it's fun and take a few Tums before you go---you'll be happy you did. Nothing here knocked my socks off. The chicken is okay. The sides are fine. But honestly, not sure what all the hype is about. Probably won't be back unless an out of town guest really wants to go.

I love Chipotle! It's the best place for fast mexican food. However, this one isn't the best of them. Don't get me wrong, I come here often bc I love the food, but the lines are RIDICULOUS!!! And sometimes, I felt a if they were rushing so bad putting things together that it sometimes spills out of the bowl. And if you have never ordered from chiptole before, I feel as if they rush you. I felt so overwhelmed the first time I ever went here. It's a what do you want and they just scoop away. I felt like there was no time to look at the items they have.

So, I then resorted to ordering online. It makes the whole experience so much better! You walk in, skip the lines and watch all the stares of people standing in line thinking in their heads like..wtf!! HAHAHA. I have waited a few times, but not as long as if I ordered there.

My fav - Burrito bowl w/ brown rice, tomato salsa, hot salsa, corn salsa (yes, I know...it's tons of salsa, but sooo good), black beans, lettuce, cheese, and barbacoa. I skip the sour cream and guac (gotta watch my girlish figure...lol. JK)

I really wish there was a chipotle near where I lived. I would probably go everyday. Hmm, maybe it's a good thing I don't live near one. I'd prob have a heart attack.

So tasty!! Went here after a softball game and it just hit the spot. I had the baked chicken, green beans, sweet potatoes, cornbread and apple cobbler. Plenty of leftovers... they were all delicious, too.

The only reason that I give it four stars is that going in as a first timer was confusing as to the flow of things. We stood around for a couple minutes just trying to figure out what we were supposed to do, until someone finally recognized our perplexed expressions and walked us through it.

I want to say the service was really good . The workers helped make the experience a very good one .  They were the deciding factor for the four stars instead of three . 

I really liked the atmosphere of the building. It reminded me of a few placed back home in Charleston, SC. I thought it was fun , and comfortable. 

The food . 
Everyone in my party got the fried chicken . It was very good . Very juicy and seasoned very well . It reminded me of my grandmother's fried chicken. That is the highest compliment it can give it . 
The baked macaroni and cheese was good, very traditional. It was better than some but not as good as others . 
The greens were excellent . They had a slightly sweet taste that set them apart from the pack . 
I got rice with gravy with mine . The gravy was to thin to stay on the rice . I couldn't taste it . My friend got the mashed potatoes. It did stay on them , but it was still watery . The cornbread was very good . I could eat the entire batch if you would let me . 
I got the banana pudding . Yummy . Very tasty. 

In all the some of the food was okay, others was really good . I am willing to give it another go another time .

We heard about Lupita's on the radio, so my hubby and I decided to go since it was a mexican restaurant which specializes in seafood from Nayarit. The food was amazing, we fell in love with the place. Too bad we live in SF, CA and can't go there often.

I can't believe how fat I feel after that lunch.  All I had was a pork steak, mac and cheese, mashed potatoes and gravy, green beans, cornbread, and pear cobbler...  Oh, I guess that does make sense.  I actually felt relief when unbuckling my seat belt after the drive home.  The portions are incredibly large, the food is ridiculously good, and the staff is fun-loving and grateful.  I'm about to fall asleep on my laptop.  Note to self:  Get a box next time, dummy.  I couldn't stop eating.  My favorites were the mac and cheese, cornbread, and pear cobbler, but everything was great.  This might be the worst place restaurant in town if you're counting calories (my coworker gaged his meal at about 1,400), but it's a great place to go if you want to fall into a Thanksgiving-like food coma.  Don't let a huge line (of perhaps the most diverse group of people in the city) deter you either.  It's cafeteria-style and it moves quickly.  The staff will be sure to find you a table.  And it's cheap!  $10 will get you a giant entree, 3 sides, and a big piece of the best cornbread you've ever had.  Be sure to plan accordingly though, as you will likely not want to do anything active for hours after waddling out of here.

By far the best haircut place in South Philadelphia. By far, the way you want your hair done is the way your hair will be done. It's not like when you have to go to some place like sports clips or Hair Cuttery, this place knows how to trim and cut every single hair on your face and head to perfection. I can't speak highly enough

Very homey feeling. The food is amazing good. The fried chicken is one of the best i've tasted, and the mac and cheese,.....i didnt know mac and cheese can taste that good. I also got the ox tails. Very tender and delicous. Everything here definitely taste like it was cook with soul. I wish i can go back and try more, but unfortunately this was a one time visit to St. Louis.

There are much better places to try than this.  We went because of the history of the place and because of how well its known.  However it did not live up to expectations.  The fried chicken is JUST ok and sides are all just ok.  It is set up as cafeteria style so you move through the line letting the server know what you want, its efficient and quick.  The friend chicken depending on how busy it is sits in a tray, my particular piece was cold when I let the server know she took it to the back and 'refried' it.  The mac and cheese was good but two 'meals' with three sides each was over $30.00 and I wouldn't particularly say it was that much better than KFC.  Go to Gus's.

Walked right in, no wait. Stood there for a moment confused, manager on phone pointed us in right direction then staff behind line told us to, "come on over!". Server was an elderly man, attentive & adorable. Food was beyond fantastic. Banana pudding; exceptional. Corn & mashed potatoes are full of sweet flavor & the chicken was better than expected. Will be returning soon!
I like chipotle. Good for vegetarians like myself. This location is ok kind of noisy and the staff unpleasant. I like the one at the City ave location much better.

Had to fly a hour away from Atl to get some good southern food. Just kidding I was visiting & happened to pass by here. 
The staff was just as great as the food.
I liked that they don't put actual corn in the cornbread but it wasn't amazing but good.
Only had two options for dessert, I was tempted but held off.
Not sure if they had a dedicated parking area but we lucked out and got one right on the street that takes change or you can download that parking app and pay that way.

I love Chipotle! Not just this location, but just about every location I've been to. Chipotle is by far the best "fast-food" style mexican place out there, miles above places like Qdoba or Moe's, and light years past Taco Bell.

Chipotle not only offers delicious items (their spicy salsa is the best), but they are fast, efficient, and in no way skimpy. Obviously, prices are a little high for fast food, but the extra couple bucks are well worth it. So glad they opened one up in Center City, and looking forward to many more of these opening up all over the city!

Our family has been using Trusting Connections for the past two years.  Having used services similar to this before, I can tell you that it this is, hands down, the best nanny service I have ever used.  As with any quality business, especially that concerned with customer service, you really see their worth over time.  Every single nanny we've used, whether it be for an evening out or for a weekend, has been wonderful.  Every single one!   Our kids love to play outdoors and are very energetic.  Trusting Connections matches their energy every single time.  

The nannies they choose are both smart and responsible.  They take their job very seriously and will follow directions to a "T."  I know that our kids are having a great time with the nanny when they say they are having too much fun to talk right now.  That seems to be the norm with this truly wonderful business. 

When it comes to watching over one's children, you want nothing less than the best.  I trust Trusting Connections with watching over our children, giving my wife and I complete peace of mind while we are away.

At Chipotle, I had the Sofritas Burrito, which was warm, comforting, good clean food. It's a fair sized portion. 

Solid food that's reasonably priced. 

3.5 stars

I know it's just a Chipotle but...
ITS A CHIPOTLE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! FINALLY!!!!!!!!!!!!1111!!!!


it feels so spacious (I wasn't there during a busy time but even so, the ceiling is really high and makes it feel more open). i love the seating, stools at tables all the way back the narrow restuarant (but not narrow in a bad way). 

It's so nice and clean and new. The employees are happy and nice (they haven't had time to hate their jobs yet probably). There's this really cool Aztec-looking art on the wall. 

Chipotle itself has really awesome fast food that I definitely prefer to Qdoba. They use a lot of fresh, organic, and local produce and though I don't eat meat, I'm pretty sure they're behind fair and humane practices.

Good job, Chipotle, for placing yourself one block from my work.

Great service. Good portion sizes and affordable. Mac and cheese and cornbread pleases well. If you want to indulge and have a diet free day, this is the place to enjoy it!Good for family, friends large groups even.
Do not come on Friday, Saturday, or Sunday: the lines are ridiculously long. The food is good but pricey, and so are the drinks.

Looking for an authentic soul food in St.Louis? 

This is it!

So I checked the restaurant's website and apparently Oprah and Gayle visited this place! Throughout the meal, we got to enjoy various soul music as well as lively dining environment. 

Ordering Food: We were really confused when we initially walked into the restaurant, but one of the staff pointed toward to where cafeteria trays are located and told us to grab a tray for each order. As we moved progressively through the line, staff asked us about what types of meat, side dishes, and desserts that we want. So I got baked chicken, mac & cheese, cornbread, and sweet potato (no dessert) - all for less than $11!  

Baked chicken - I can't say it's the most flavorful chicken I had, but chicken tastes very decent.

Mac & cheese - You know what, this IS probably the best mac & cheese I ever had. Not only the flavor is spot on, but there that crusty texture to it. 

Sweet potato (yam) - I really like this side dish! Yams are really soft!

Cornbread - It totally depends on whether you got it on the edge of cornbread tray or on the center of cornbread tray. The one on the edge happens to be a bit dry and the one in the center tastes not as dry. 

Overall, it was a pretty good dining experience. My tummy was very satisfy after the meal.
Amazing soul food and pie. The line and the wait are worth it. Best part of St Louis. Will be back!!

4.5!   
Totally worth all the hype!   It has become a family tradition to go down to STL for Sweetie Pies when im in the midwest.  They have live singing. I love their fried catfish, the macaroni and cheese, the greens, the potatoes.  Im absolutely love their Pear Cobbler.  I got that because of Gayle King and that is now my favorite dessert.   It pains me to say this but I was disappointed with the sweet tea during our last visit.  They use to make an in house fresh brew sweet tea that was on point, but the last time we went (September 2014) they had pre- packaged mass marketed sweet tea that tasted terrible.  Very synthetic tasting.  We sent it back and got Sprite.  We plan to go again when im back in the midwest and I truly hope that they got rid of the packaged sweet tea and back to brewing it fresh. Aside from that sweet tea issue, I absolutely love this place!
When two lonely women lock eyes in Chipotle, a bond is made. A connection, an understanding between two fake-Mexican-loving overeaters.

I was pretty impressed with the food, and most of the staff.
We waiting in line about 30 min, the line had not entered out the doorway yet.
When we finally go up to where they dish your food out, there were NUMEROUS signs "DO NOT POINT AT FOOD"  and "DO NOT TOUCH FOOD", I can understand the touch but not the point.  I told my kids, keep your hands in your pockets!

then gentlemen that brought our food to our table, were kind and helpful
The food tasted great!  I had the "Smothered Pork Chops", tender, seasoned well and hot, "Mac and Cheese, was great, Yams were tasty and Peach Cobbler was wonderful, no complaints on the food!  

I think we got in there at a good time, 4:30pm....not to crowded but full, and I loved all the Hats the women had on , there was a convention going on in town.

The owners Rosalind and Caroline have been amazing to work with. TCNA is a natural referral for me for the families I work with who need some additional coverage or an in-home nanny when they return to work. My families have been very satisfied with their nannies and love all the flex benefits as well. As an after baby consultant and home safety professional, I was asked to come do a talk for their nannies on the importance of home safety.  They were incredibly appreciative and a lot of great questions for me. Not only do they provide nannies for day to day  and night support but nannies to help at events, birthday parties, weddings and Christmas parties too. Their flex program offers sick care or emergency coverage and date night support as well.  I highly recommend Trusting Connections for all your nanny needs:)

Today was my first time at this Indy Tire location! I've been to another location as a repeat customer. My experience at the Carmel location was just as great! The staff is personable and so kind! They go above and beyond to help you understand the issue and the solution! I love giving them my business! I always leave happy! Kudos to the great staff and the great work they do!

A fantastic dim sum 'hole in the wall'!!!

My boyfriend and I Had been coming here on a weekly basis for years before we moved to California. It's extremely well priced and the food is delicious. We've tried many other dim sum places in the city and none of them were as fresh as Lakeside...

Their congee (rice porridge) is fantastic as is their crispy taro triangle. Personally, I cut up my taro and put it into the congee and devour a couple bowls in minutes. Also, their steamed vegetable dumpling (which has shrimp in it - beware) is VERY tasty...I highly recommend their congee as it's the best I've ever tasted and definitely think every dim sum fan should give this place a try!

There's no way this dude has a barber license. It's not clean, the clippers weren't sharp (he dragged them across my face and made them awfully red, cut my neck) and his fade was completely trash. He didn't even attempt to blend it.

Don't be surprised if you get a fungal infection from this place.
Not safe, my estranged husband went to the desk and talked them in to giving him keys to my room. He wasn't on the registry. Only my name was listed as a guest. They game him keys. NOT SAFE. ILLEGAL.

The agency helped very quickly in getting us help when we needed it most in finding late night help. TC also was able to find us two very qualified candidates for a nanny position requiring the care of two infants. We have become close with both placements and they have helped our family through the challenges of our first child. Expensive but worth the cost.

When I heard Chipotle was opening up in Center City I almost was in disbelief!!

I love me some Chipotle and this place is swanky. Yes I used the word swanky. 

Only two reasons 4 and not 5 stars is:
Place is really dirty after 7pm-ish
I don't like having to ask for more beans or rice!

I was out of town and I had ordered tires for my wife's X5 which came in while I was gone.  She has the sport package with the 20" wheels so we took it to two other places that said they couldn't get them mounted.  Well, Indy tire installed them in 2 hours with no troubles at all.  I can't say enough about Ron at the W 86th St. location.  Not sure why one of the posters above called them a chain store.  They are simply a locally owned business with a few locations around Indy.  Took a huge load off of my shoulders after having my wife and kids sit a two other places for 4-5 hours each time.

OK, this is my first Yelp review, and feel obliged to reminisce on my all time favorite restaurant ever, Lakeside.

I had eaten here since the early 90s, and brought my now wife, and all three kids, eventually only to learn of it's abrubt closing.  Shear heartache.

Lakeside had the most incredible Noodle Soups, Curry Chicken, Vegetable Dumplings among any of their Dim Sum items.  

The food, the unassuming decor, and the gracious owners service just made this place feel like home every time.  

So many memories, I'm at a loss for real words.
My chicken wasn't hot and the waiters were changing shifts so I felt neglected the parking wasn't good but the food was delicious especially the peach cobbler.

I was so pleasantly surprised by Sweetie Pie's.  I tried to go there before but unfortunately they were closed.  They do everything right here!  From the moment we walked in the door to the moment we waddled out the door.  We were greeted by "D", whom I recognized right away from the TV show.  He pointed the way to the cafeteria style layout.  I explained we had never been before so he explained how Sweetie Pie's works.  The only negative comment I have and it is but a small one is I felt a little rushed to order my food and since there wasn't anyone behind us, I think it was a little unnecessary.  The food all looked fantastic, the prices are presented in full view and easy to understand.  My friend ordered the fried chicken which was half a fried chicken (which was a big one) and two sides...he chose the spaghetti (for me) and mac and cheese (10.50).  I ordered the fried catfish alacarte (4.00) and the banana pudding (3.50).  The staff was so efficient in serving us, taking our payment and seating us. 
At the end of the line, there was "D" again waiting for us, he took our tray and asked that we follow him to our table.  

Back to the food...we had enough food on our table to feed a family of four.  The chicken was crispy, juicy and oh so flavor-able and I say the same for the monster piece of catfish breaded in corn meal which I am still dreaming about.  The side of spaghetti (if you want to call it a side) was very meaty, perhaps a little too sweet, but I like sweet sauce.  The side of mac and cheese is just like mama makes.  Last, but certainly not least was the best banana pudding I have ever had!!!!  I was over full but could not stop eating.  While we ate I enjoyed observing the restaurant, seeing pictures of Miss Robbie, watching the camaraderie among the staff.  We had a woman stop at our table to ask us where we were from, when we told her we lived locally she told us her and her group of friends were there from Baltimore and they were so excited to be there, definitely fans of the show.  "D" was so super nice and patient answering the patrons questions and posing for pictures.  As we were finishing over eating, "D" was right there again with a to-go box.  We never had to ask for anything he was a step ahead of us taking care of anything we needed.  

GREAT JOB Sweety Pie's, can't wait to go back!!!

A nice quiet place to get some good Mexican food in Sparks.  We had the taco salad which was loaded with avocado, lettuce, shredded beef, bell peppers, beans, and rice.  They can do a little better by offering something other than the typical overcooked Mexican rice, and refried beans, and changing the oil that they cook the shells in a little more often; but other than that a very satisfying plate for under $10!  The ambiance is a little dark - there is a full bar, so I'm guessing the place can get rowdy late at night sometimes; but I bet that's how the owners like it.  There is a patio, so I'll check that out the next time I go.  Thanks again for the good food!
Great food (as with most Chipotle restaurants) and usually isn't too crowded, even at peak dinner times the line doesn't take more than 5-10 minutes to move through.

After reading all of the shining reviews for Lupita's, I was excited to try it out.

For me and my friends, it was just adequate. My shrimp a la diabla was fine. The sauce was reminiscent of BBQ sauce almost and it tasted like it was made with condensed OJ. It was a nice flavor, just threw me off a bit.

The carne asada was overcooked and far too gristley. I realize that it isnt supposed to be a fine piece of meat, but Ive had better versions almost everywhere else.

The service was also adequate but all in all a very forgettable experience and not one worth driving across town for, for sure.

Soul food served fresh and hot.  We hit this while on the road on a Sunday.  It was the after church spot for many.  The wait was a bit long otherwise no complaints.  Also, not all of the food is served on every day, just select items.  Oprah is filming a reality show there to air on the O Network, so there were camermen and producers all around the place.

We came to town to visit some friends and we facades it was a day for pool and
Pizza. They recommended this place and wee look it up on yelp,it was no disappointment the pizza was very good, ingredients in it tasted fresh and good quality, huge portions. We also had the wings and they were delicious too! Price was right too! If you're in the area or pass by get you a good New York style Pie.

I expected so much more from Sweetie Pie's. My overall experience was okay. First I was caught off guard by the dated decor and the cafeteria style dining. The line was long but I was so anxious to taste this food that because of it's popularity that I remained patient. When I finally got up to order I looked at the food, some items looked more appetizing than others, my excitement lessened a bit.  Then I looked at the wall mounted menu and noticed that the dinners were served based on the day of the week, i.e. pork ribs served on Sunday. My excitement lessened even more because the menu options were limited and to top it off they restricted the options even more by breaking the dinners down to be served on specific days. I say may I have the beef ribs, we don't have that. Okay, may I have the okra with tomatoes, we just have okra. Mind you the okra looked like a watery slop. So did the black eyed peas. I wanted to order the Catfish but because I couldn't handle anymore disappointments I ordered the BBQ pork ribs...how could they go wrong with that right? My dinner came with two sides thus I ordered mac n cheese and sweet potato, corn bread, and peach cobbler. My aunt ordered catfish, fried chicken, cabbage, black eyed peas, cornbread, and 7up pound cake. I had a few bites of her  food as well. My ribs were good a little tough but taste good, I've had better though. The Catfish was surprisingly good, it was breaded with cornmeal. The fried chicken lacked flavor. The mac n cheese were sweet, threw me off a bit. It taste like they added cream and sugar to it...cream is cool but sugar, no. It wasn't nasty though. The cabbage taste okay. I skipped the black eyed peas because it didn't look appetizing but my aunt who LOVES black eyed peas said it didn't taste good at all. The peach cobbler was bad, the best thing about it was the little bit of crust and few pieces of peaches that were surrounded by this glob of very sweet and weird tasting cobbler. The texture was weird too. I have no complaints for the 7up cake, it was good. The WORST cornbread I ever taste in my life! It was very salty. I hope the cook accidentally used the salt instead of the sugar, because if not, they need to change the recipe ASAP. I didn't taste a bit of sugar in my cornbread, as a matter of fact some of the sugar that was in the mac n cheese should have been in the cornbread mix.
