The highlight of my dinner believe it or not was the SWEET POTATO....absolutely delicious. The taste, texture, everything was on point. It was spiced just right. Overall my experience was okay. I traveled all the way from NYC with high hopes but was sadly disappointed.

Sooooooooo this restaurant was not what I expected it to be. I initial saw this restaurant on diners, drive thrus and dives, and thought it was going to be great! Well it was average at best. They give you ample of food but it wasn't that flavorful and the meat wasn't tender, the 45 minutes wait in line wasn't worth it, the decor wasn't well put together and staff was loud and there was this one waiter who kept on rubbing his nose and handling drinks .

I only gave a conservative 4 stars since my experience with Indy Tires @ Carmel was limited; it was a very good one. I had a flat tire overnight with a big ol' nail stuck to it. I didn't have too much time to take it in for repair that day, so I tried one of those fix-a-flat sealants. It didn't completely seal the puncture, so drove wife's car to work instead.  I called around for repair appointment, both Tire Plus and Midas refused me  because the sealant was used. One told me it would ruin their machine, and the other said they would have to clean the entire tire "inch by inch" and that would end up costing me more than buying a new tire. Both of their solutions: buy a new tire. Sure.  So I called Indy Tire randomly and reached Chris.  He said it would take them a little extra work but would take care of it without any additional charge. No problem, that was their job, he said. Next day, the job was done promptly and the service was great. I gave Chris 5 stars for his friendly and professional attitude.  Now I know where to go for tire repair and new tires next time.
Great place, grabbing lunch before heading to the Apple Store, very delicious steak bowl
Had the chicken wings and mac and cheese. Tons of food for the price.

As a former New Yorker I've had the best pizza in the country. When I tasted the pizza at Rocco's those food memories came flooding back. 

This is some of the best pizza I've had around here. The crust has the perfect texture and taste - a bit crispy at the edges. The sauce is not sweet but has a tomato and Italian spices combination. Fresh toppings add to the flavor. Try the vegetable pizza with broccoli - to die for!

While visiting St Louis I was looking for a place that served southern food and Sweetie Pie's was suggested. The black eyed peas were to sweet, the greens were bitter and the mashed potatoes were like glue. The fried chicken wings were good, but I would have liked another part of the chicken. And there are other places to go to get good fried chicken. With that said it was not worth the 2 hour wait. 
There has to be a better way to speed up their service.
The posting on their front door states that they are open for breakfast but when I asked a server they stated that they do not serve breakfast.

I ate here last year, summer of 2014 while visiting St Louis and attending a Cardinals game. The line wasn't extremely long and we got through probably within 30 minutes. But the thing is, people are constantly coming! It's like her lines never end, so she consistently has business here. I ordered the fried chicken with corn, cornbread, cabbage greens and her sweet tea. My guy had the same and we had cake for dessert. The only thing I didn't like was the cake. It was dry and not too tasty to me. But everything else was to die for! Her chicken was so juicy and flavorful. I wish someone would fix some of the photos on the wall that are crooked! I have a slight case of OCD and it nearly killed me to contain myself from not fixing the pictures myself!! I came back a month later to go to her Uppercrust location. You should definitely take a trip out to visit her restaurants! It's a shame they haven't opened in Houston first before they ever went to Los Angeles.

We were in St. Louis getting my nephew set  up for college when we were lucky enough to be told about Sweetie Pies!  We planned on going Wednesday evening but didn't make it.  So on Thursday our last day and with little time to spare we ventured over to the Groves to see what all the hype was about.  From the moment we arrived we felt at home.  Having lived in Savannah, Ga for nearly 8 years I'm no stranger to soul food, that's exactly what we had, even more so the best soul food I have ever had in my life!  My mom and I actually split the $10.50 special for 1/2 a chicken with two sides(plenty of deliciousness to go around).  The chicken perfectly seasoned and juicy, green beans best ever, cabbage (omg) delish, the winner the Mac and cheese, cheesy, gooey scrumptiosness....finished off with the best peach cobbler on the planet.  Out server Eric was polite and professional!!  To sum it up the whole experience was epic and one that we will not forget.  We all agreed we may have one more reason to visit St. Louis often!!  We were "soul fool" haha

My girlfriend and I decided to give sweetie pies a shot after a long drive from Milwaukee to STL. 

I have to admit we would never had heard of it if not for Oprah. 

We stopped in on Friday afternoon around 2pm or so. There were no issues with parking and we waited in line approx 2 min. 

I had the gravy smothered pork, mashed potatoes and gravy and candied yams. I have to admit, it was far better than what I had expected. Quite possibly one of the best pork dishes I have ever had. 

As we were eating Tim walked by and struck up a little convoy with us. After giving him some crap about the cardinals being a game away from the World Series and me being a brewers fan, Tim asked if I had tried the Mac and cheese. I embarrassingly answered no. He gave me a look and ran off. He came back with a bowl of it for me. It was simply amazing. 

The food was amazing and the wait was little to none. I am not sure I would wait in a line if 100 people an for two hours. But again I doubt there is any food on the planet I would wait that long for. This guy needs to eat!

Awesome food, insanely awesome staff. 

Try it!

I tried both the Mangrove and the Upper Crust location. At both places the food was good but the Mangrove location seemed to be a bit better. The food was more flavorful, the pear cobbler was the best I ever had, and the host/service staff was very friendly and made the spot lively and welcoming.

I finally got to taste the food and, for the price, it was good.   I will say that some of the food was too sweet for my liking - for example, the macaroni and cheese and the peach cobbler.  BUT for what you pay for the amount of food you receive, it's worth it.

Really good food! I've been here a few times and never got a bad meal. Love the chicken wings and mac and cheese! Wonderful. This last time I went the crowd waiting was lined up throughout the restaurant, so plan for that if you go. You may have a bit of a wait..............but.......it is worth it!!!

The place looks nice from the outside but inside was not clean. The tables and floor need to be wiped down and swept. Ok for fast food but not pleased with the appearance. Prefer Qdoba over Chipotle now that I tried it.

Had a slow leak fixed very quickly.

The tire was one that I had under warranty with them and they honored the warranty with no questions asked, very easy process.

Thanks Indy Tire!
This is a nice location- never much of a line, if any, when I come in, and the crew is very friendly!  Glad I live so close to here!

The company I work for decided to try out Chipotle's catering as an option for one of our quarterly office events for my department. I will say the food itself was oK, it came with everything that we needed (The ONLY reason I gave 2 stars as opposed to 1), however the process to get the food was extremely stressful, exhausting, and a huge inconvenience. We tried multiple times to place the order for delivery online as well as on the phone with different credit cards that worked fine with all the other orders that we made. Do to Chipotle's system issues it would not allow us to make the payment so we had no choice but to place the order for delivery which took away time we didn't have to spare. I called the morning of the event to confirm everything was in order and I was informed that the order was canceled. I had a whole department waiting and they cancelled my order without a call or at the very least an email to inform me. One of the customer service representatives looked into it and said it was a store manager that cancelled because they can't accommodate our order. They said they will place another order for a later time and I still had to pick it up. What really befuddled me is that they placed the order at the very same place that it was canceled after they claimed they couldn't accommodate. I had to go with it because at this point I was in a bind and had a department full of people to feed. Thank God we eventually got what we needed but that shaved an hour off of our time that we have to get pre-approve for these events as well as took us away from work that needed to be done that day. When I called to discuss the matter I was told that they would like to keep our business and they will have someone call me back. It's been a week and I have yet to receive a phone call. Very unfortunate. I couldn't convince my company to go with this business again if I wanted to do to the lack of professionalism.

Returned with my family on Easter & it was a hit. My mother won't stop talking about it. She doesn't understand we can't eat here every family function! The staff is still very attentive as well as attractive. My dear lord; talk about eye candy. I could rave about the food all day long. I know this has nothing to so with the restaurant itself but the fellow customers have always been very friendly as well.

Glad to see a Chipotle make its way outside of freaking University City and City Line Avenue.

As a transplant from Maryland, an area that thrives off Chipotle, it's good to have one in the city I now live in.

Cannot go wrong with almost any item here as they are all DELICIOUS. Especially the vegetarian burrito and chicken burrito.

Their guac is phenomenal for a chain, so I definitely recommend that as well.

All in all, I will be visiting this location more often when I'm on that side of Walnut Street.

I ended up getting the three piece fried chicken meal. The chicken was pretty good but I felt like there was too much breading.  The breading was packed full of flavor but a little bit on the salty side.  There wasn't anything exciting about the sides.  I stuck with the mac & cheese and mashed potatoes to be honest I prefer the mashed potatoes and spicy chicken from Popeyes.  Although the food was mediocre the service was outstanding.  They were kind from the moment we walked in the door until the very moment we walked out.  Overall this was a very pleasant dining experience.

My friend, originally from Georgia, was craving for soul food.   Back in Los Angeles, we don't have many options for authentic soul food as you'd get down south.  Illinois and Missouri aren't the "south", but we hoped that we'd find a place with awesome soul food.   We got it here.

The line was out the door and everyone was ordering the same thing: fried chicken.  For side dishes I tried their mac and cheese, okra, sweet potatoes, and cornbread.  I also had a bite of their roast beef.

The line was pretty long and we had to wait an additional 20 minutes because they ran out of their famous fried chicken wings.  I thought their macaroni and cheese ranks up there with the best I've had.  The fried chicken wings were ridiculously huge - I'd be scared to see the chickens they came from.  We loved their okra.  My friends at the table didn't quite love their roast beef or turkey much.  Stick to what they do well.

Overall, we were really happy with what we got here.  Most importantly, my friend was happy to satiate that craving he's had for so many years.
The sweet tea, candied yams, and banana pudding were very good. Ms. Robbie & her sisters were very nice.

If you don't like Sweetie Pies food then you must be a picky eater and/or a hater.  I live in St. Louis, but just visited Sweetie Pies for the first time a few weeks ago and now my coworker and I are addicted!  

It's not the type of food that is good for everyday consumption, but just think, there was a time when black/southern/country people ate this kind of food everyday!  Yeah the place is hectic, but what would you expect from a place where a 2nd season reality show is being shot and a place that is also vastly popular?!  Also, it is hectic because the food is hella good and everybody wants it.  

The mac n cheese, cabbage and cornbread are all the BOMB!  Definitely better than I make at home and I think I do a pretty darn good job on these fares at home.  I've also had the fried chicken and smothered pork chop.  The chicken was good, but since I've been making fried chicken at home for years, chicken has just become chicken to me.  The smothered pork chop was very good and tender and big enough for me to save some to eat at home later.  

Sweetie Pies is THE St. Louis staple and I can't wait until her new place opens in Grand Center.  I wish this establishment all the best and more!

So the food was decent.. but i got a vibe of attitude from this restaraunt.. tried to small talk with the person at the register but i was met with what felt like a superiority complex... your foood might be awesome, but if your customers don't feel important your success will be short lived.. i might try again in the future.... might...

We went to this location in Mangrove.  It was nice, and clean; lots of seating, no line. We went in at about 2p. It was a bright, clean, atmosphere.  They had plenty of windows. You could see the food prep and cafeteria set up in one glance. The wait staff was exceptional for this type of eatery. The variety of choices was outstanding.  We had the fried chicken,  oxtails, pork steak, corn, okra, green beans, mac-n-cheese, and peach cobbler! Whew! We couldn't move. They had to roll us out of there and we still had doggie bags! The best to me was fried chicken and okra. Even my grandma don't make those like that.

Really wanted to try this since it came highly recommend by friends and all the hype from the tv show on OWN. I was a little disappointed. Staff was very friendly and the line moved fast. The fried chicken and mac 'n cheese were excellent. The chicken has a little spice and not greasy at all. The mac 'n cheese was creamy and super cheesy but it had a great crunchy top from being baked. The meatloaf was ok; moist and great texture but it was too sweet. The green beans were too sweet as well but it did have big hunks of ham. The cornbread could have been more moist and it actually wasn't sweet enough.

I was going to give it a three star based on ambiance and food, but our server,  Calvin, boosted it to a four! My son made the "mistake" of representing his team, the Kansas City Chiefs, and instead of letting it go, Calvin harrassed him like family and singled him out in a friendly way the whole night. Calvin's demeanor made us feel like we were family,  making our experience something we won't forget.  We highly recommend the SUPER decadent and cheesy macaroni and the juicy meatloaf. For dessert, our favorite was the banana nilla wafer bread pudding.  Great vibe and would return if we can through Ram country again.  :)

Massive sandwiches, cute area, wonderful spot. Only draw back is management is snippy and the service varies depending on which group of new high school students have the job that week. But the food is delicious, massive, and a great deal for the money. I like the Haverford, and the giant chocolate peanut butter cups.

i didn't want to spend a lot; so i ordered a 16" pie w/sausage for 13.00. wow! was great. i have no complaints. even thogh it was 9.20pm; and they close at 10- they had no problem about working right until the end. staff was friendly and professional. there was still a family seated at a table eating. nobody was being rushed. not all places will serve you a half hour before closing. there are a lot of pizza places in spring hill. i thought this was the best i've had in a long time.

It's good eats. Been there twice. Enjoyed the Short Ribs. Fried Chicken is good. Mac n cheese is the best. Service is good. There is one lady who bends over backwards to make you comfortable. But wait a min, i couldnt get a refill to go? Interesting.

Hubs and I have gotten pizza here at Rocco's several times and it has always been great. I do like it better when we eat the pizza there in house because it has a great crispy crust...but when we do a "pick-up" by the time we get home the crust is soft. But it even still it is very delicious!

I also didn't have such an enjoyable experience here. After a raving review from my friend, I decided to try this place out this afternoon. We made it right before lunch hour, so we didn't have to wait in line.

Appearance (3-4 stars) - Nothing looked better than a row of food lined up in front of you complimented by interesting decor around you. The place felt very retro; it felt like one of those dusty abandoned stores you see in vintage flicks.

Food (3 stars) - I got the baked chicken with green beans and corn. The baked chicken showed signs of having been cooked a couple hours ago, with the meat dried and lukewarm. The green beans were pretty decently done, having been cooked in chicken broth. The corn was just some creamed corn with some peppers in it, nothing too special. The saving grace of the plate was the cornbread. I loved it, and stole my friend's since he said he was full. The cornbread is super buttery but a little dry, but it goes down just right. I heard that the Mac&Cheese was the bread and butter of this establishment, but I didn't try it because I heard that after I had ordered. I guess someone can enlighten us on that if you decide to go.

So what made me give this establishment 2 stars instead of 3-4 based on my review thus far? The price. One piece of (small) chicken and two sides will run you close to $10, not including a drink. For that much I could have gotten food just as good at Lee's Chicken or an All-You-Can-Eat southern style buffet.

I was expecting more for less, and unfortunately Sweetie Pie's did not deliver for me.

If I could give Ms Robbie and company 100 stars, I would. The food here is amazing! From the chicken and mac n cheese to those delicious desserts. The staff is really nice especially the wait staff. If you get a chance to eat here come hungry and have plenty of time cause there's always a line!

Overall, I LOVE Sweetie Pie's food.  The service is sometimes questionable (IE: a while back, a group of us were seated in in the dining room eating near closing time, and the wait staff began to clear our table WHILE WE WERE EATING.  Not cool, people, not cool at ALL!); the dining room is always very clean and the tables are bussed right away.

But my issue today is SUGAR!  Soul food cooks: it is NOT necessary to saturate the dishes with the sweet stuff!  Today I am enjoying smothered pork steak and gravy (very flavorful and tender), mac n cheese (they never fail with this one), and cabbage.  

Now here's the problem, the cabbage (as usual) has so much sugar in it, it borders on being a dessert.  I keep trying this, and the greens, when they are offered on the off-chance that the cooks will have run out of sugar! So far, I've been disappointed EVERY TIME.  I'm just going to start bypassing these two items when I visit the restaurant.

I cook greens and cabbage regularly for my family and NEVER EVER use sugar.  To date, I have not had one complaint, and as a matter of fact, my greens are requested for every event where food is involved - so I must be doing something right.  

I wish someone would school these cooks and ask them to ease off!

Meh - I don't know what I was expecting, but I suppose for a vegetarian whose choices here are limited to one thing, I should have realized I was just going to get something pretty basic. Good? Yes. Fresh? Oh, very. In fact, that THAT's probably the big draw here - everything is super fresh and that shines through. Cheap? Yes! Win! But I can make seasoned veggies at home. I wish I had more to say - I wanted to LOVE Chipotle, but I was impressed with everything BUT the taste. 
           Employees were so nice I wanted to take them all home. Place was clean, even the restroom. I may be back, if only because I feel confident of product quality, price point and staff, but I can't say it'll be my go-to. This makes me sad, but....I know for a fact that there ARE locations of Chipotle that carry faux meat for their burritos and tacos. GET WITH IT, center city Chipotle! I need some seitan in the mix, here! THEN you get your 5 stars, I promise.
Best mac n cheese.  Friendly service.  Definitely recommend. Extremely generous portions.  Really wishing I lived in St. Louis because I would eat at Sweetie Pie's A LOT.

I'm going to be real. This is my go-to fast food minus chick fil la- not open on Sundays so I can't be totally devoted to that. 

I come here 3-4x a week on average. I don't like cooking very much so this is the place I go to for lunch and dinner.

I get the half chicken/half steak...I think this is the best way to maximize the amount of meat you get. You get charged for the steak but I think it's worth it. 

This is first on my top ranked fast food place. Close tie to chick fil la but like I said..chick fil la ain't open Sunday so I give it to Chipotle. The line goes by pretty quick which is also why I ranked it above popeyes because who doesn't like fried chicken? #amiright

Soooo was on a girl's weekend trip to STL and my girlfriends were raving about this restaurant Sweetie Pies and how it was on the Oprah Network and how we had to go try it. OK...I'm game. When in St. Louis do as the St. Louisan's do.

My take on Sweetie Pies??? SUPER over-rated. 

I wanted to try the meatloaf, but they only have it on Thursdays. I had the catfish with green beans and spaghetti. The spaghetti was just ok and it kinda tasted canned to me. Green Beans were decent and the catfish was seasoned well. But not the best I ever had. I am from Chicago and I feel like MacArthur's has better soul food than this place. Caramel Cake was good.

The line was almost out of the door when we got there, but the line went pretty fast and everyone was very friendly and helpful. Customer Service was A plus plus plus.

If you are visiting I would say try it just to say you ate there, but it is nothing I would make a special trip for.

Sorry Oprah!!!!

Stopped at this place after seeing it on Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives while on a road trip. I was pretty excited after seeing this on the food network and was ready for some delicious food. However, it didn't turn out quite as I thought it would. First, we walked into a completely empty restaurant which I thought was pretty weird considering it was lunch time. Then, we walked over to the cafeteria-style line to pick out our meals (which I also found pretty weird AND gross). Nonetheless, I was still excited to eat some tasty food. After getting our meals from the not-so-fresh cafeteria line, we sat down and ordered some lemonades. Minutes later, the waiter came out with sweet teas only. After much confusing conversation between us and the waiter, we decided to just stick with the sweet teas, even though we don't like sweet tea. I took a few bites of my meal, which consisted of fried chicken, mac and cheese, and mashed potatoes - all of which was nothing special.Then, my boyfriend discovered a huge feather in his fried chicken. At that point, we were already feeling pretty uncomfortable considering we were the only people in the place and we were being hawked by the wait staff, that we decided it was about time to leave. We felt rude leaving the food behind, so we asked to take it to go which the wait staff also made very awkward and uncomfortable. We later threw out the remaining feather-ed fried chicken and continued on our road trip. Needless to say, I was really disappointed by Sweetie Pie's for the service and the food and probably won't trust that show again!
Unfortunatly closed in January 2008 due to retierment of the owners. We will remember this place with gratitude for wonderful quality of the food and warm attitude to the customers.

Been hearing so much about Sweetie Pie's and  the great food  that they have. So my family planned a vacation to Branson, Missouri and decided to stop by Sweetie Pie's on the way. Everyone was so excited and hyped! Area of the restaurant is in a very nice location. We arrived about an half an hour before opening time so, we were just out snapping photos in front of the restaurant killing some time. Line started forming fast, so you need to get there early because they are super busy! The staff is oh so friendly and ready to greet upon entering the building. Everyone in our group  got their food, which you have a lot to choose from. The waiters were there to seat you to a table after you have gotten your food. They were very courteous and funny! Okay, on to the food. Is Sweetie Pie's the name of the restaurant because sugar is in everything they cooked!! The cabbage had sugar in them, the green beans, all you could taste was the sugar and garlic in them! Who on God's earth put sugar in green beans? Guess that must be an acquired taste if you like sugar green beans! Everything I ate had sugar  in it, all except the baked chicken that was just plain. It had very little flavor to it. My meal consisted of baked chicken, cabbage, corn and corn bread. My hubby had oxtails (which were loaded with fat), cabbage and sweet potatoes (those were good). I think the food was prepared the day before because it did not taste fresh and it definitely was not hot....it was like lukewarm. I think Sweetie Pie's is more hyped than what it really is. I would like to meet Robbie myself to let her know how disappointed my family was with Sweetie Pie's. If you are making a special trip just to eat there, I say, don't waste your time.....big disappointment for us! Now I can say I've had Sweetie Pie's and what? Won't go back there!! Good luck to all that do!!!!

As "real" authentic Mexican food places go, ie: one where actual Mexicans eat, this one is pretty good.

I had the Sin Nombre which was ceviche and quite good, though I couldn't finish it (very generous portion). We got a pitcher of margaritas. Kids had tacos, quesadillas and fried ice cream for dessert.

Looks like a whole lot of nothing, it's in a strip mall on the corner, but we enjoyed it and will likely return. The seafood seems to be their specialty.

Great food and really friendly service. I got the fried pork chop and its made to order so its a ten minute wait. very good. I also had the fish, bbq ribs, mac & cheese and pasta all great. skip the mash potatoes just okay. get the roll over the cornbread. be sure to check their website out before going b/c they have items they have everyday and some items only on certain days. I found out the hard way when I came back the next day and they didn' t have what I wanted because it was only on saturdays.

I was in town on business and decided to stop in....I have also seen the show on TV.
It was a Friday afternoon, a line but due to a large order of take-outs. They need a separate line for take outs. I ordered wings, Mac n cheese, black eye peas and sweet potatoes. The sides were awesome!!!!! The wings just needed some extra seasonsing or something, they were hot and fresh. The staff was nice and friendly. I will be back!!!!

Do not go here unless you are prepared for a long wait due to a very inefficient operation. Also the restaurant is VERY loud.  The food is good but not good enough to wait 1 1/2 hours in total confusion.
Best guacamole and chips hands down. BOOM! Best burritos and burrito bowls too. Now it just needs beer to wash all that deliciousness down.

To be honest I had never heard of Sweetie Pies and all the hype surrounding it until a month ago when my friend decided to plan a trip to Saint Louis so we could taste the food and visit the restaurant that was on the Oprah Network.

Sweetie Pies was our first stop on our weekend fun and food adventure so straight from a 5 hour drive from Chicago to Saint Louis my friend and I were so excited to go to Sweetie Pies but the excitement didn't last long.

When we first stepped into the restaurant we really didn't know where to order and eventually a man with a great smile told us to grab a tray and place our order cafeteria style, so we did just that.

When we looked at the sea of Soul Food in the line of metal trays surrounded by glass, I have to say my mouth was watering it all looked good and if I could I would have ordered a little of everything.

The aroma that filled the air was heavenly!  It made me get more excited to chomp down on the food that was eventually on my plate.

My friend ordered the Catfish fillet which was good, I got the fried chicken which was sorta bland(I was surprised because it looked so good) my friend got the fried corn(which we later found out was canned Del Monte,really) I got the cabbage(it was sweet) we both got the mac n' cheese which was good at first bite but as it cooled it began to taste like sugar, yams(pretty tasty), and banana pudding (my granny's is so much better) their was thick and just so/so.

The running theme in Sweetie Pies is the SUGAR!!! Ugh!!

When we get to the cash register a young lady says would you like "Sweet Tea or Soda?"  the way she asked my friend and I thought it was included in the price so we both ordered our drinks just to get the receipt and find out we were charged 4.60 for both our beverages.

Now, it wouldn't have been a problem if the young lady would have said "Would you like to add a drink to your order?" being that we had never been to this place it was a little deceiving in my opinion.

My friend asked for a glass of water and it took about 15 minutes before she got a cool glass of water with no ice...really?

While we were sitting and eating we saw these big cans of Del Monte Corn and Green Beans...lol, CRAZY ME! I thought the veggies were fresh! That took away from the experience of real Southern Soul Food Cooking!

I had to use the restroom and the floor was so slippery I have no idea if someone had come in before me and dropped something but I know I was holding on for my life...lol, I just knew I was going to fall on my bum.

Bottom line is I truly don't see what all the hub bub is about and I can't say that I would go back to Sweetie Pies or even recommend my friends to go.

It truly didn't get a happy dance from me! 
 
I think the people who think that this is the best Soul Food around haven't had the opportunity to taste some real Soul Food like my Granny use to make!
One of the best fried chickens, green beans and banana puddings I've ever had.  Just make sure to come early if you want their daily specials.

Best fried catfish!! The yams and black eyes peas are also top of the list! I must stop here every time I am in St Louis.  Worth all the hype.  The only knock is the wait,  this day there was little to no line however the orders were stopped because it took 3 people to change out 1 pan of sides.  What should have taken 5 min took 15,  seemed like the boss was not on site as the team seemed to be taking it easy while we waited.

Happy and extended one night. This is a 2 star hotel (by traditional ratings) but I give it a 4 for that category. Clean, which is #1 requirement. Nice front staff and appears to be family run.  Breakfast was really minimal and below expectations. Coffee, bagels, some cereal.

Went on a gorgeous Sunday afternoon and waited about an hour to get food, but well worth it! Had the fried chicken wings with sweet potatoes, mac and cheese, and peach cobbler for what I like to call #CarbFest2015. Definitely eat here on a cheat day so you don't have to miss out on any of this Southern goodness!

CORNBREAD. Ain't nothin' wrong wi' that!

I was pleasantly surprised by how nice this place is. And very clean!

I had fried chicken, mac 'n' cheese, green beans, cornbread, sweet tea. All great. The fried chicken was delicious - juicy without being greasy. And they give you three huge pieces. Sweeeet.

My only complaint was that the food wasn't very hot by the time we got it to the table - but that's the nature of the cafeteria style food, and there was a huge to-go order in front of us that kind of held up the line, so I think that had something to do with it. Our waiter was more than happy to heat it up for us.

Everyone was super friendly, from the women that dished up our food, to the young girls that rang in our order, to the busser that carried our trays to the table, to our waiter Tony who was incredibly sweet and really wanted to make sure we were happy with our experience. If you haven't picked up on my reviews yet, good customer service is supremely important to me, and can a lot of times make up for less than stellar food. The staff at Sweetie Pie's was wonderful. And considering this place was HOPPIN' on a Sunday night when I expected it to be dead, you can tell they really build a rapport with a dedicated clientele. Everyone, the staff and the customers, seemed happy to be there. Really made for a pleasant experience.

I know where I'm going when I'm craving down home cooking and Southern hospitality.

not much to say but:

FINALLY!! A CHIPOTLE IN THE CITY!!

also, the exterior design is stunning. reminds me of a luscious apartment building in downtown new york. already made me happy walking up to it and i wasn't even inside yet!

interior is also wonderful as well. very clean, spacious looking (mostly white interior). and the best part? stools!

staff is friendly and quick with orders.

well priced and you get your money's worth.

will be coming back many times more!

I eat here often.  why I keep trying the greens, though, is beyond me.  The cook/chef still thinks that greens need to be sugary....NOT!  My daughter said the green beans were sugary, too.  i guess all the salt was in the smothered pork steak gravy, which I had.  The mac 'n' cheese and peach cobbler is what's up!!

Now..the real reason for this review:
I had received an RFT Food Promo on November 8, 2012 that stated: student special Tue-Thur $6.50 with ID.  No expiration date, no other stipulations.  Not surprisingly, Sweetie Pie's staff claimed this deal was no longer offered because it was only for the chicken thighs and they didn't have those any more.  Huh?  When I showed the cashier the text and asked for a manager, she claimed there wasn't one in the building.  Really?  Robbie just lets y'all run things by yourselves?  I'm sure that is NOT the case!  Anyway, the cashier took my cell phone number and is going to have someone call to discuss the issue.  I'm sure I'll never hear from anyone,  No biggie...I know of a couple other soul food eateries nearby that have great food..and a bit cheaper too.

I spent five years in North Carolina and during that time I became more than a little obsessed with southern cuisine and that divine nectar, sweet tea.  After my sojourn in the south I spent a few years in Seattle where they've never seen a good biscuit and sweet tea is lipton with granulated sugar dumped in it at the table.

I was a little sad when I moved to St. Louis and didn't find the sweet stuff to be as ubiquitous as it was in Carolina.  Thank God I was tipped off about Sweetie Pies.  I just went there today and as I type this I am drifting into a food coma the likes of which I not experienced in some time.  

As noted by the other reviewers, Sweetie Pies operates on a cafeteria system.  You pick your entree and either two or three sides.  The entrees are gigantic and the side portions proportionally so.  I had pork smothered in gravy and onions, black-eyed peas, greens, and mac and cheese.  All meals also come with corn bread.  Everything was delicious, flavored by that perfect seasoning agent, smoked meat.  

At $10-13 for a meal, things may seem pricey but this will be two meals for me so it all works out.   The real key here is that the available entrees vary depending on the day of the week.  All the more reason to go back again and again!  I know I will!

WHERE IS THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT?....The first thing I picked up several forks and spoons trying to find ones that weren't caked with dried food. GROSS! All my food was more room temperature than hot. Steam tables are to be at a certain temperature to keep bacteria from growing. 

The food was mediocre, Fried Chicken was crispy yet dry, cabbage and macaroni would have been delicious if they were hot. Service was attentive.

This is the first review I have ever written. I just couldn't let such a huge concern go by.

If you need vehicle service GO FIND ANOTHER DEALERSHIP. As part of GO AUTO this dealership I am still today fighting with and they do not care to find solutions for their customers. My vehicle is in for " extended warranty work" at just 4 k over manufacturer warranty and it's been a nightmare not only do they charge labour costs to look at the various issues on my Escape but then they don't fix a damn thing and say none of it is covered and charge me an inflated cost they are OVERINFLATED LAZY AND INCAPABLE.   I brought in my own battery from NAPA AT over 150 less than this dealership was trying to scam me for the service manager is an ASS and clearly doesn't like strong willed women. This service department thrives on the rip off tactic!  I'm still fighting the fight since last week and am having to involve AMVIC!
Best pizza in spring hill hands down great food and staff also a great Italian atmosphere i would recommend Roccos to anyone

We had a great time at Sweetie Pies. We had been stuck in suburbia for three weeks on business. We were excited to try Sweetie  Pies as some of us watch the show. We immediately saw Tim, who although busy was very friendly. They were not really busy so we flowed through the line and flowed through quickly. I was craving veggies so I had a side plate with okra, black eyed peas, cabbage and banana pudding. My coworkers loved the fried chicken! The service was awesome. Great experience!

One of the best country style delis I've ever been to!  I had the Haverford sandwich (Lightly breaded oven baked chicken breast, leaf lettuce, tomato slices, pickle chips and honey dijon mustard on rustic bread) and it was absolutely delish!  With a menu of 40+ customizable sandwhiches, you'll want to keep coming back for more to taste the Bowdoin, Lafayette, University, Book Store, Post Office and Bryn Mawr sandwiches!!

Prices for lunch are $7-8 for a bite.  Not too shabby.  Loved it.  I'd go back in a heartbeat - service could have picked up the pace a little bit thought.  Attracts the nearby Swarthmore College crowd and the resident geriatrics ;)

This is an amazing southern/comfort food establishment.  I've only went once and that's all I need to say the food was AMAZING.  Both my wife and I were very impressed with the food.  The place was nice enough and the staff was friendly.  A must see place.

I wish I could give negative stars.  We first went to the Upper Crust but Robbie had the restuarant closed for her annual party.  We got to see her outside walking around getting her party together so that was nice.  However, the place was closed until 8pm and we decided to go to the other location.  I was able to see people who were on the tv show.  I saw Neicy Nash and Kita from the T.O. show fame but the food - oh my GOD!  I didn't like anything but the mashed potatoes and that was salty.  We had a huge group and we were on a family trip but only one person in our group was satisfied.  We are not sure what type of fish we were served but the menu just said FISH....it was fried very hard.  The chicken was huge but so full of hormones that I thought it was Hacksaw Jim Duggan in my plate.  The place is a hole in the wall which is ok and I understood it would be a long line but it wasn't moving fast enough when I think it could have.  One of the girls in the line was rude - my mother told her she wanted mashed potatoes and she gave her sweet potatoes then when my mother tries to correct her she says "I heard you" my mother who is not a "confronter" just took the sweet potatoes.  After being seated it took the guy (very nice guy) 30 minutes to get us water.  Would  have been easier just to get a beverage machine so we can get it ourselves.  The food was poor.  The peach cobbler was HORRIBLE- no sugar - not cooked all the way through and the prices are high for the cheaply made food.  No one in our party of almost 20 left satisfied.  The only thing I got out of this was to say that I visited Sweetie Pies.  I love the show but the food is not good.  I hope they don't get so busy with the show that they give sub par food out.  I am from the south and know good food - this is not it!  Sorry  - but if you want to see C-list celebrities drop on by!

My husband and I are visiting St Louis from Georgia. I am a really big fan of Sweetie Pies Reality Show. I love Mrs Robbie! We stopped in to have lunch today and the food was delicious! I had the fried chicken, Mac n cheese, cabbage, corn bread and peach cobbler. My husband had the fried catfish. That was the best catfish ever. The staff was friendly and the wait in line wasn't bad at all. They had a live band and the band was great! I will defiantly visit Sweetie Pie the next time in in St Louis.

I finally made it to Sweetie Pies!!!!!  This was a first time visit and I was with my family Sunday evening for dinner. We got there just in time because soon after the line was close to out the door. It's cafeteria style which is the reason for the long lines. I think if people were seated and served at the table service would go quicker. Once you go through the line and get your food, you have to wait at the register to be taken to a table. They could just seat people who are dining in and let the people making to go orders go through the line. Anyway, on to the FOOD! I had the chicken wings with mac n cheese and candied yams. I got banana pudding for dessert.  The mac n cheese let me down! They scraped the edges of the pan for us and it was cold and hard. I wish they would have just given us some from a fresh pan. The yams had a good flavor, but my pieces of yam were really hard. The only edible parts were the small crumbs that had been soaking in the juice. The chicken was good. It had a nice crust and it was juicy.  I think the best thing I had was the banana pudding. I really liked it. I could tell it was home made and it was perfect.  My sister had the turkey wing and she liked it ok, but it was disappointing that turkey wings were being served and they weren't serving dressing. My brother said the green beans were some of the best he has ever had.  I don't remember our servers name but he was great. He made sure we had everything we needed and he was friendly. I will be back to Sweetie Pie's because there are some other things I would like to try. I'm looking forward to having a better experience on my next visit.

Dinner for two $40 the decor is lacking not much more then a hole in the wall. The service was great for a nice people enjoyed talking with them treated us well great attitudes. The food however was beyond lackluster I had the barbecue it was tough chewy dry as if it had been there for a week. I spoke with the manager she kindly offered to change it for something else which I took her up on, I requested the fried chicken wings. The fried chicken wings tasted like cardboard in that they had no taste whatsoever I would rather eat Kentucky Fried Chicken then eat the chicken they brought out to me. Did i mention that the black eye peas had sugar in it and it want a good thing it's a great landmark great for sightseeing I would never spend money there again.

I walked in the door to a nice clean and inviting environment.  I was greeted by a friendly employee, Danielle.  She personally took me to the sales department which is what I was looking for.  I guess I walked in the wrong door as there wasn't parking where I should've been able to park.  Either way.  No wrong doors there.  Everyone was polite and professional and I was still able to start the process of buying a car.  I dealt with Stuart McKay.  I'm now purchasing my first car!! The finance department are super helpful and informative.  Stuart is helping me find a car that's right for me and Danielle in service has been superb!


I recommend Kentwood Ford to all of my friends!

The best. I went there on a Thursday specifically to have their special that day--ox tails. So good. If you've never had them, you don't know what you've been missing. If you have had them, have them again. And again. And again! Truly great.
As is the pie. The extra spices really kick it in. 
And the ladies behind the counter.

The girlfriend and I decided to hit this place up a few weeks ago and try the fried chicken after hearing so much about it. 

The staff are extremely friendly and helpful, and just has a very friendly atmosphere to the place. The proportions are huge and the friend chicken was absolutely awesome along with the mac and cheese amongst everything else. We were induced into food comas afterwards. I will definitely be back, this place is pretty sweet.

I heard of this place from friends at work when they heard I was heading to st louis.  Sweetie pies lived up to the raves and beyond.  I had the meatloaf with cornbread dressing and collared greens. Very good one person had the fried chicken  it was like 1/2 s chicken.  I didn't tty it but my sister said it was very good, not dry   you get to St Louis look up sweetie pies.  You won't be disappointed.
I was unimpressed with this place, all of my food was cold and at 24 bucks for a kids meal and 1 adult meal it was some pricey cold food.

Broooo I've only been to three chipotles; one in Bensalem, one in University City and now this one. It's been a year since the last time I've had chipotle so I was like why not. But they are NOT generous with their portions here. The bowls I always gets are always overflowing---the best thing about chipotle! But man here they do not give you the right portions. The guy literally put one scoop of rice and one scoop beans and THREE SCOOPS OF SOUR CREAM in which my rice and beans were swimming in. Honestly though at least give enough rice and beans???? That the whole core of the bowl!!!!! Idk I was super disappointed in this location and honestly it wasn't very clean in there and I got a side of guacamole and it was sort of brownish. Chipotle has disappointed me for once. Sad.

This is a pretty cool place with good fried chicken and better sides.

The candied yams were amazing, pretty sweet but also with some spice that made it so much better than most sweet potatoes I've ever had.  The mac n cheese was also really really great, I'd highly recommended getting some of it too.

The fried chicken was pretty good, but not that exceptional compared to some other places I've been.  While the chicken itself was good, the batter didn't have that much flavor.  The fried catfish was pretty delicious, the woman at the counter said it was her favorite.

You get your food cafeteria-style, but it is set up a lot nicer than it sounds.  The food was surprisingly expensive for soul food, my 2 sides + fried chicken and a drink cost around $13 after tip.  They clear your table for you and everyone working there was very nice to us.

This place is awesome! We stumbled upon it when my son was craving pizza. The chef heard us say we had never been before and treated us to knots and a sample of creamy french onion soup. I have never had it before and it was so yummy. All the flavor of french onion but with more bite and richer flavor. The wait staff, Katlyn, was attentive and on point with every need; even the special needs of my picky eating daughter. I had the meatball sub and the rest of my part had different pizzas. Even the cheese slice was legit. I will make a point to stop by again when I'm in this neck of the woods!

For a sub $100 hotel in edmonton, its my choice....got kingbed, 42" flatpanel, clean room, climate control with tstat on wall, not on the ac/heat unit...so it keeps the room the correct temp....lotsa hot water, toilet paper is a lil cheap, but I carry baby wipes,  internet isnt gonna be able to netflix stream on , but I got 95% of what I wanted done, done. Hallways have some stains and are that warm kinda stale smell, room was perfect, didnt has to use the airfreshner that I always has packed....theres no views except that of a parking lot and a freeway, but its not a resort, its a place to sleep. And its non smoking.

Food is great but last time I showed up to get take out I had to wait a half hour for them to unlock the door because when they get busy that is what they do. All I can say is if you feel like a great meal and being fed by (The food Naz%) do it

I love that the food is locally sourced and fresh, and you can really taste it. The burrito bowl is hands down my favorite item to get here with brown rice, a ton of veggies, chicken, black beans, salsa, tomatoes and cheese. I have loved the service I have gotten here.

About what I expected. Yes, I saw this on Food Network and that's why I had to check it out, okay? ;)

The atmosphere was pretty chill.  A lot of old wood bench-style seating with great details. You order cafeteria-style. It is NOT A BUFFET! just don't expect to get an all-you-can eat meal here.  Although the portions are RE-DICULOUS!  :)

You pretty much get to choose 1 meat selection, 2 sides (veggies) & you get cornbread. Drinks are extra. All that is usually around $10-$15.  

I had fried chicken (which was very good...not a ton of spices though), candied yams (to die for!) & mac-n-cheese (which my 3 year old said was pretty good since I didn't get any).  My wife had fried chicken, ribs (which were smokey & delicious), & other sides that I can't remember.  The cornbread seemed excessively dry.  And the sweet tea was just that...sweet.  WHEW boy.

The staff was the best part.  They really seemed to welcome anyone & everyone who came in.  They were very friendly & conversed with everyone.  The wait staff was excellent!!  Those guys & gals deserve BIG tips because they take your tray to your table, get your drinks & are all over any requests you have.

A visit to this place is a great experience.  If you love down home cooking with a side of soul, this is the place to try.  I'll be back.

Good experience! Love my truck. Big red F-150. They let me drive it out of the show room! My salesman went over the vehicle with me after I purchased it to make sure I understood how it worked and they're always asking for feedback. When I get it serviced the team is always super nice and try to get me out as quick as possible. They treat me with respect and although I over paid for my truck, that was my own fault for being young and coming by myself haha.

I ate here with a friend from out of town last week and we had a nice experience.  I had the half fried chicken with mac n cheese and corn and she had the meatloaf special with mac n cheese and black eyed peas.  Our meals also came with corn bread.  The portions are huge so bring your appetite.  The fried chicken was decent but the mac n cheese was my favorite part of the meal.  My friend's meatloaf was excellent, but neither of us were fans of the black eyed peas.  I felt like we were being transported back in time.  This place gives off a good vibe.  It's something different from so many of the current trendy "foodie" places that all seem to offer the same menu.  Be prepared to wait in line, as they serve things cafeteria style.  Everyone was friendly and seemed to enjoy working there.  Be sure to bring some cash since you can't leave credit card tips.

This was my fourth trip to STL and I finally decided to go and see what all the hype was about.  The bad thing about expectations is that when you have them and they are not met you get two stars. The wait was almost two hours.  I wasn't super hungry so that wasn't too bad. I had read the previous reviews and expected the wait so that is not the reason for the low score. After looping through the line and finally getting to the food there was no fried chicken. Actually it was cooking but there was a bunch of people waiting in an additional side line for it to come out. Really??? Okay so you adjust when you're hitting the 2 hour mark. Moving right along, I had the fried catfish,  macaroni and cheese,  and corn. Add peach cobbler and sweet tea. My companion had smothered pork chops, black eyed peas,  and cabbage. Add lemon pound cake and the sweetest punch ever. The food was just aw-ight. The catfish was super salty and fried extra hard. The macaroni and cheese was under seasoned,  and the corn was just okay.  The pork chops were very tender but room temperature,  the black eyed peas were sweet which was very confusing to me,  and the cabbage was super soft and soggy. And the cornbread that accompanies each meal was dry and hard. The best part about the meal was the desserts and the drinks. The peach cobbler was the bomb.com. I had it hours later,  heated up.  I asked the server for extra crust and that paid off. The cake was also delicious, very moist. I had that the next day at the airport. Now you do get a whole bunch of food but what good is that if its mediocre at best?  
So go just to say you went to Sweetie Pies but please don't have any expectations that way you're feelings won't be hurt.
2 stars - 1 for the desserts and 1 for the drinks

Okay enough telling and writing excellent reviews. My plan is to find some kind of public transportation. Departing S.F. inbound to St.Louis. resources is limited. But I must find a way to get to Sweetie Pies. Ellen Degenerous where are you?

Lunch on a weekday. Reminded me of my favorite place in chi-town in the South Loop, the one Barack Obama used to frequent, with all the politicoes, cops, lawyers, homeless people, and various nutjobs all squashed together. 

Sweetie Pie's in fact has fewer rough edges, but also fewer surprises on its menus. 

It was just solid, decent food. I had the baked chicken with gravy - cooked just right. Okra was perfect. Excellent mashed potatotes. Didn't have room for the pie but it looked good. These guys could be on the Wikepedia entry for "comfort food."

Absolutely superb. We arrived just as the chicken had come out of the frier, and it was the best I've ever had -- and I've had it all over the country. Crispy, spicy, juicy, and huge pieces.

The mac and cheese was very, very good -- though mac and cheese anywhere is never as good as I think it's going to be. The green beans made up for any disappointment, though. Mashed potatoes and gravy were not good -- tasted right out of the package, rather than fresh or home-made.

All in all, though, just a great experience, if daunting in the huge portions and deliciousness of that chicken. Makes me regret living so far from St. Louis.

After buying 2 vehicles here previously from Scotty "the Bulldog" Olsen, Kentwood Management decided to welch on a deal that was signed. They wrote the odometer on my trade in wrong and a week after I had my new truck at home, told me I had to come in to renegotiate. They would not pay my trade in off, so I told them to shove the truck. They wanted 10K more and the slimy "Jeff" tried to hide the amount after we agreed I would give them 5k more, he tried to screw me out of the other 5K!!!
Scotty Olsen is good, but his bosses are terrible, terrible people. Buyer beware here more than usual!!!

Pear Cobbler, Pear Cobbler, Pear Cobbler...get it!  It's oh so good.  Love their fried catfish, fried chicken, black eyed peas, cabbage, green beans and mac n cheese.  I always get Pear Cobbler.
I would give them 4 stars but the Mangrove location is very cumbersome when waiting and someone needs to re-design their layout asap!  1st off, why oh why someone has to wait in that long line for a to go order, makes no sense.  They have a bar area that is not in use and in my mind, that would be great for to go order placement.  The way the line is routed through the interior and the decor is also silly.   It's probably just as well that the don't have a to go order line because I'd have Pear Cobbler once per week.  ha

Every time I visit, everyone is so friendly and the food is excellent. I love visiting Sweetie Pies and make sure when family is in town we stop by.  Meatloaf, Mac and cheese, cobbler -- you can't go wrong! So delicious. Thank you to everyone at Sweetie Pies for being so awesome and providing exceptional service!  You all are the best!

I thought. I would never find a good tamale in this town. Most every tamale I have ordered has a ton of mass and very little filling. My grandmother spoiled me with homemade tamales.
The tamales you get at lupitas are darn close to my grandmother's.
I ordered a chicken enchilada and pork tamale.
Both were fantastic, chock full of flavor.
The restaurant itself is nothing special, but looks can deceive
Give this little Mexican restaurant a try for some fabulous food..

I happened to be in Sparks for a tournament and saw Lupitas out of the corner of my eye. Could it be the same beloved Lupitas as in Incline? YES, it is! After the tournament, I stopped by for 3 small tacos (lengua, pastor, and asada) at $1/ea and it tasted just like Incline. I would have ordered the ceviche, but I wasn't that hungry after a hot day in the sun. At the Incline location, the servers are definitely friendlier, but all was good in the end.

I'm not a fan of Mexican food so I had never heard of Chipotle, but the guy I was on a date with said he wanted a burrito and it had to be Chipotle. So, we drove into center city (it took about 40 minutes) and found Chipotle. The guy behind the counter did a great job helping me decide what to put in my bowl. It was really good, I was pleasantly surprised. Another employee came by while cleaning up and asked how we were doing. she chatted for a few minutes - very nice.
 I highly recommend the stop

I had the chicken wings mashed potatoes and Mac and cheese with cornbread. I had a turkey wing to go. The line was very long expected from a show on tv. I happened to be in the area for work. I live in the south Texas. So I was red to try so called soul food in the Midwest the chicken wings were awesome. Mashed potatoes not so much they were instant with box gravy pass the Mac and cheese was ok.. Nothing to rave about... The turkey leg was the same kind they sell at six flags frozen and put in the oven. Cornbread wasn't sweet.. The sweet potatoes were good though I had with my turkey leg.. I will say not worth the wait inline. This is a place that's hyped because of tv or for people who just can't cook or don't know what soul food is... For this part of the country with very few black people in the surrounding states what I expected.

I know that some folks just love this place but I am not certain why!  We went on a Thursday at about 1:30.  After waiting in line for 45 minutes we finally had some food.  I guess you could say that the Good News is that there is plenty to read while standing in line!  I have never seen so many "this is how you get in trouble" signs in my life!  Everything from count your change before you walk away to don't point at what you want.  The staff has definitely been in trouble many times as they had lots of signs directed just at them posted around the unused bar area.  I imagine this may be why they were all so crabby!  

The food was mediocre at best.  The chicken was lukewarm, the yams oversweetened, the cobbler undercooked.  I had been looking forward to okra and greens but when I saw both of them swimming in vats of brownish water my decision to choose something else was quick.  I love good southern food and maybe at one time this was good but it appears that being in the spotlight may have lessened their need for quality.   A bit sad, I think.

Their food is good, Camarones a la Diabla are the best though, love them. The service is good, a little bit of room for improvement. The spaces between tables is tight though, I don't suggest this place for large groups of people.

We were in St Louis for my sisters graduation * The very 1st Lawyer in our family* I'm so proud of her. Along with our sight seeing and whatnot we decided to go to this famous restaurant Sweetie Pies ( as seen on Ophra network. Sweetie pie who's best friends with Tina Turner and was her back up dancer back in the day) I Loved this restaurant. The food was great and generous proportions. Your served cafeteria style. The lines are long so go early to get ahead of the crowd and to find close parking. The area is sort of ??? So lock your doors and hide your belongings in the truck that are of value. 
The waiters were great the diversity in clientele was great. The food was Sooooooooooooooo good. They had a good verity of items to choose from. If your ever in St Louis looking for a great down southern meal try Sweetie pies
I hope this review was helpful enjoy your day.

Upon arriving in Reno, the first task I undertook was to begin interviewing the hotel employees about their favorite restaurants.   I was looking for good Mexican because of the rather sizeable Hispanic population in the area.   Most recommendations named Bertha Miranda's....so I looked on Yelp and found mostly favorable reviews except for a few that sounded like a negative review that I would give.  Going on my gourmand instincts, I kept looking around and found this solitary review of a place they thought better than Bertha's.    I took the bait.

At first, this is a little hard to find if you are not a local.  It is at the end of a rather long strip mall (1/4 mile) and faces a corner street, so Lupita's has an address but the store faces the other corner street.  At the time I went in (7 pm ish) the restaurant was half full with local patrons, most all of them speaking Spanish. GOOD SIGN

Walking in reminded me of the many local, one store, one owner Mexican restaurants in East LA .   The decor is festive and is in a perpetual Cinco de Mayo state of readiness.   Clearly they are not catering to the tourists, but you can feel the culture deeply embedded in the interior decorations.   Although most would immediately think the objects hanging on the walls and from the ceilings gave it a cluttered look, upon closer inspection, it became obvious every item had a particular meaning to owner.  I love just going into places like this.

So how was the food?
1.  Pork tamale:   For $2 a la carte, a smallish tamale the size of two king sized Snickers bars was actually very tasty.   Very modest amount of meat however.   I would have preferred to have a $4 tamale with more meat in it.   Overall, still very tasty.   4 stars given the price,
2,  Pork taco:   Served just like the vendors in the streets of Mexico.   Two small tortillas (4'"in diameter)  covered completely with a mound of cubed, seasoned, and skillet fried pork with onions and cilantro.   Sauce on the side.   This was just great and it was only $1 per taco.  5 stars.
3.  Sin Nobre (assorted cerviche seafood).   I wanted something different than the standard, taco, enchilada, rice, beans, fajitas fare....so scanning the menu I noticed cerviche.   For those not familar with it, it is raw seafood marinated at least overnight in lime juice and spices.   The citric acids literally cook the seafood when it sits for long periods of time.   The translucence of seafood turn an opaque white when it is "cooked."   In this version they had octopus, oysters, mullosks, shrimp, crab, some kind of white fish, squid.  The portion was generous and the result was fabulous.   At $13, this was a real bargain.   An upscale DC restaurant could easily charge $30-$50 for an entree like this.  5 stars for this dish.

If you are ever in Reno and want to have Mexican food, take the time to drive 10 minutes east to Sparks and give Lupitas a try.  You will not be disappointed.

And thanks Tracy for the Yelp posting......

I am so offended at the fact that be
Burger King has the nerve to shut down their ice cream machine at 11:45 at night yet they are open 24 hours. This is ridiculous! I feel triggered.

This is tried and true soul food. You'll die happy eating the smothered pork steak.  The mac and cheese goes fast for a reason.  The sweet tea is good in that it's not overly sugary.  The cornbread definitely doesn't need butter.  Fried chicken wings... I could have eaten 30 of them.  Service was terrific, made me feel right at home.  The decor is pretty cool too. 

Bear in mind that there's a process.  First, it's cafeteria style, so just saddle up to the counter.  But also, they handle the plating so you don't get your grubby little fingers into everyone else's food.  You know who you are.  If you want it for there, grab a tray and silverware, and they'll hand you the plate.  If you want it to go, they'll handle the box for you.

I loved Sweetie Pie's!!! I went here March 27th for my birthday. Much to my surprise (I am a picky eater) I loved EVERYTHING I tried. I read reviews before I went, so I was familiar with the cafeteria style line. Some of the workers were very nice, and some of them had poor attitudes (but that could be at any restaurant), but I enjoyed my visit. My son even got to take a picture with Tim.

My family and I had an amazing trip to Sweetie Pie's on a busy Saturday afternoon.  Because of their new TV show, the restaurant is continuing to get more and more business, but they didn't let that slow them down!  

We got there about 12:30 on Saturday afternoon and the line was about 40 people deep.  Many of the "stars" from the show were working but obviously haven't let their stardom get to their heads.   The restaurant is set up in cafeteria style with several different amazing choices.  Saturday's specials were fish and BBQ.  I had the Fish, hubby had the pork steak and our son, the BBQ ribs.  The line went very quickly and while the restaurant was packed, the staff very quickly cleaned off a table for us so we could dig into our amazing food!

Within the first few bites, we were in heaven.  The fish didn't need hot sauce, or tartar sauce, or onions and pickles.  The cornmeal breading was very flavorful and the fish fried just right.  The pork steak was smothered in brown gravy and tender to cut.  Hubby enjoyed it so much he didn't let me taste it!  The BBQ ribs were so good, they quited a 17 year old who had been talking all day for over 20 minutes.  All that was left were a few bones.  We tried several sides, the macaroni and cheese, green beans, corn, sweet potatoes, cabbage and black eyed peas between the three of us.  All were very flavorful, just as we would expect from an amazing soul food restaurant.  Towards the end of our meal, we slowly took bite after bite trying to savor each amazing bite.  I really wanted to take a plate of chicken wings home with me, I was so full and knew I wouldn't be able to eat them when I wanted to.  

Everyone in the restaurant was amazingly wonderful.  They provided great customer service with amazing food.  It's a restaurant I would HIGHLY suggest to anyone and can't wait to go back!!

I'm a believer! Saw this restaurant on the OWN Network "Welcome to Sweetie Pies."
We got there at 11:00 (they open at 11:30) and by the time the doors opened, we had 40 people in line.
The food was incredible - comfort food! Paula Dean would've loved this place before her diet. Everything was incredibly tasty! And big portions, too. Loved the Mac n Cheese, the Peach Cobbler, Rice, and corn bread. Smothered pork steak was fall-off-the-bone tender. Servers were pleasent and helpful. The owner, Ms. Robbie, is genuine and came out and greeted us and posed for pictures. I'll be back!

I work equidistant from two Chipotles and had originally only gone to the other one, which always had a mammoth line. I tried this Chipotle on a whim one day and was promptly swept into a whirlwind of efficiency.

I walked in to a half-full seating area and a line of about five people (the prep counter is all the way at the back of the narrow space). I mentally prepared for a wait, but I was immediately engaged by an exuberant employee, who cheerfully asked what I wanted. I uttered a response, and no sooner were the words out of my mouth was the next station's employee asking me for the rest of the particulars. This service continued down the line so fast that I almost couldn't keep up, and I think it only took me a cool 45 seconds to order, receive my food, and pay. My head was spinning as I grabbed some napkins and left.

The food is typical Chipotle quality--yummy, environmentally-conscious meats, three choices of salsa, and delicious guacamole. No complaints there!

Further trips by me and others confirm that this is indeed the fastest Chipotle on Earth.
The pizza was good but it wasn't anything spectacular. The crust was nice and crispy.

I was introduced to Sweetie Pies at a work event where I received a "sample" of Sweetie's (2 pieces of chicken and their amazing greens). I fell in love with the food immediately and made it my mission to make my way back the very next day. I had friend chicken, mac n cheese, sweet yams and peach cobbler. It was magnificent. Being a California girl I don't know if I've had food that good before. I will definitely go back.

This place is solid, but not really worth a drive across town for.

The fried chicken and catfish were really good, though the catfish was a bit dry.  The mac'n cheese, mashed potatoes, and sweet potato were only ok.  The cornbread... meh.   They probably started charging more because they've become more popular recently, but the food here is definitely not worth more than 10 bucks a person.  

I'm pretty certain there are plenty of other soul food places in the area that are just as worth visiting in the St. Louis area.

This was my first time trying Sweetie  Pie's. I've driven by it dozens of times, but always end up going somewhere else nearby. I've heard nothing but rave reviews and was looking forward to trying it. We went on a Sunday, right when the church crowd heads to lunch. I think it took us about 45 minutes from the time we entered to the time we sat down to eat. 
I was impressed with their selection of food and efficiency with serving everyone cafeteria style. 
My husband and I both had fried chicken (breast and wing). I had green beans and sweet potatoes for my sides and he had mac'n'cheese and mashed potatoes. And they give you cornbread to top it all off. Very generous portions!! Definitely don't eat breakfast if you plan on going for lunch. 
My favorite side was the sweet potatoes. They were so sweet and lovingly spiced and tasted like Thanksgiving in a small cup. Also, the fried chicken was super crispy, a pinch spicy, and juicy. Very delicious!
So why not 5 stars? The food was great, but it's not somewhere I would frequent. The food is so heavy that you really need to allow yourself enough time to digest or nap before going on with your day. Try it once, you'll like it!

The food was good I'm glad that I got to taste it. I was very underwhelmed with how my food was plated. I shouldn't have to ask for a separate plate or bowl for each item. It's just your typical grandmothers cooking though. I will say the mac and cheese is enough to slap someone over if they ask for a bite. You should definitely stop by if you are in the area. You won't regret it. I promise.

I love coming to Sweetie Pie's! The staff is always so friendly. You can always expect to get a great home style meal from them. Their candied yams are always tender & oh so sweet! The fried chicken wings are seasoned well. The macaroni and cheese has a little bit too much liquid for my liking. I always have to get a to-go box because the portions are too big. Great vibes, amazing food, good people

I can't believe I was stupid enough to buy vehicles here. My husband put a deposit down on a used focus. He went back the next day to find out it had been sold to someone else. Ok, mistakes happen but the salesman and manager could have cared less. Basically told my husband to buzz off. A week later the sales man finally called back to try and make things right. They offered him another car at a decent price. When we took deliever of the car, kentwood didn't detail the car (owned by a pig and previous smoker) or fix the windshield that had a gigantic chip.

Same thing happened with  my brand  new edge. They sold us the edge in the color and package we wanted. Only to find out they could not deliver that combination. So, they said to be fair they would upgrade us to something with a few more gadgets. Yay, right? Except they gave us less for our trade in to make up the difference.

SItuations like this go on and on...


The service dept is run by a gang of ignorant thugs. Not a friendly or intelligent person among the group. 

FMC can thank Kentwood for my next vehicle purchase being anything BUT a Ford.

i cant remember what life was like before i knew the downright delicious drops of heaven commonly known as chipotle burritos.

sometimes i order ahead via iphone chipotle app. sometimes i dont. it just hits the spot after a long day at work when i dont want to cook and pizza isnt on my tummy's radar. so thanks for never judging me when i come here too often.

Tried Sweetie Pie's today and cannot say enough great things about this place. It opened at 11:30 AM and we arrived about ten minutes early. There was already a line but it was not too bad.

As soon as they opened the doors they made every effort to get everyone waiting outside in the restaurant. Once inside the line moved very quickly and I would say we waited no more than 10-15 minutes to order our food and be seated. The service at Sweetie Pie's really is truly impeccable. The helpful servers choose a table for you based on how many diners are in your group, carry your tray to the table, and get your drink and make sure it is filled throughout the meal. I've never had a counter type experience with such excellent service! 

Now, onto the food, the most amazing part of the Sweetie Pie's experience, it was to die for! My friend and I both got the daily special (1/2 chicken with two sides and cornbread). They really are not kidding with the half chicken, I got two enormous breasts, a thigh, and a wing. It was way more food than I could ever eat in one sitting, especially with the huge helpings of macaroni and cheese and collard greens as well as the cornbread. In addition to giving you a ton of food, the food is also delicious! I truly loved all of it. The batter on the chicken was incredibly well seasoned and it really came through in the meat as well. The mac and cheese was to die for and they made sure to give everyone they served a little of the crispy cheese on top.

All in all the Sweet Pie's service combined with the food makes this a cannot miss stop if you're ever in St. Louis!

I have been having issues with the front wheels on my jeep.  The manager Brett helped me from the start and he and his entire staff were absolutely great to deal with!  They were quick, informative and fair. Couldn't not recommend them enough. I almost wish I had another problem so I could go back!
Chose this restaurant after getting off the plane and making to Spring Hill. It was fantastic! Pizza, mozzarella sticks, and salad were great!

So normally with a place as popular as Sweetie Pies, you would expect a bit of a disappointment with the food or service. 

But wow, I was glad to be wrong. The food - fried chicken, catfish, pork chop - were excellent and the desserts were great too. And the mac & cheese, just get it. It's as good as they say it is.

Sadly, overrated.  The establishment has potential but misses the mark.  The server behind the counter was not very friendly or welcoming. As a first time visitor I didn't know how to order and was confused. The server could've offered assistance.  Furthermore,  our table server took a while to come to our table with drinks and rarely came around to check on us.  When the soda came it tasted like filtered sugar water.  The food was average.  The only thing I would try again is the mac n cheese.  Food presentation is not very appealing.  An overhaul of both customer service and the restaurant are needed to encourage returning customers.

I have never waited so long in a line to eat a casual dinner before, but it was COMPLETELY WORTH IT. I'm from Chicago, so it's difficult to find really good down home cooking back home. My friend brought me here when I went down to St.Louis to visit and it is the best fried chicken I have ever had in my life. The macaroni was delicious, the sweet tea was mouth watering, the staff was helpful and friendly, and my stomach and taste buds were very happy campers when I left. I will definitely be back next time I'm in town. For anyone who hates lines as much as I do, I promise- it's worth it if you stick it out.
Had the meatloaf and macaroni and cheese, both items were very sweet. I was pissed, I paid $12 for it. I am a diabetic, beware, probably won't be eating here again.
The service was fantastic and the food was even better! It was a little pricey at 50 dollars for three of us but you get what you pay for here, we took boxes to go!

Don't believe the hype. I drove here from GA and this place was on "to do" list. I wish it was not. The customer service was so BAD. It's cafeteria style and one server complains about how sick she is while serving us/ plating our food. GROSS! Soul Food, I think not. The food was sugary and salty. I felt my blood pressure rising with every bite. The bathrooms we so unkept. I thought I was using a bathroom at a gas station. The neighborhood is sketchy too. Don't waste your time.

I have been using TC for about a year now and am very impressed with the services. Having been a nanny for TC myself when I was in college I couldn't imagine anyone else taking care of my own child. I am happy to report that TC treats their employees as well as clients with the upmost respect and kindness. I cannot say enough good things about TC!

I love me some Chipotle....but I'm done with this location.  And it's all customer service related.  It was not crowded - there was one person in front of me and two behind me.  The counter guy talkedsofreakinfast about what I wanted on my burrito that I had to say "Uh, sorry - can you repeat that?" several times.  For the 2nd time in a row, I came back with a broken burrito.  I should have watched him more closely.  That's just sloppy service, especially when it wasn't peak time.  If you are so eager to rush me out the door, maybe it's not worth it to step through the door in the first place.  No thanks!

We have been wanting to come here for almost a year!  We came out to St. Louis last year and the line was too long for my partner to wait so sadly, I had to settle for eating somewhere else and only dream about eating at Sweetie Pie's.  So, we planned this outing to St. Louie again, specifically to eat at Sweetie Pie's.  We arrive only to find that they are not accepting debit or credit cards and the ATM inside is down.
