That pretty much ticked me off right off the bat.  I was not about to go trapsing up and down the street in a town I don't know, looking for a money machine.  So, I gathered my wits and quickly found a gas station and downloaded some cash and went back to SP's.  It's located in a cool building.  There was not line yet and we were inside and going through the serving line in no time.  There were many items to choose from but I chose the fried half chicken, dressing with gravy, collard greens, corn bread and peach cobbler.  My partner took meatloaf and mashed potatoes and gravy.  Now, the portions are quite generous.  Our server Calvin, was affable and bright and pleasant.  He seated us promptly and took our drink orders.  He also helped me get a tee-shirt later to take home.  The dining experience was quite pleasant and quite filling.  The chicken was flavorful.  The coating was a corn meal base and was pretty good but could be a bit hard and overly stiff when it cooled.  So, don't let your chicken get cold.  The dressing was nice and moist and nicely seasoned with a ladle of gravy over it.  I found it to be delightful!  The collard greens were perfect!  Not overly bitter but still that greeny "bite" and simmered in a wonderfully pot likkah.  Cornbread was moist and fluffy, not too cakey or dry.  The meatloaf serving was quite generous, very well seasoned, cooked perfectly.  It held together nicely without being to soggy or too dry.  Wasn't thrilled about the topping on it but that's no biggie just a different way of preparing it...Didn't obsess on that.  Mashed potatoes and gravy did not taste from scratch but were not unpleasant.  The peach cobler was out-freaquing-standing!  A great combination of peach flavor, sweetness and yet the cobbler had a nice body to it and wasn't soggy or overly stiff and chewy.  Perfect!  Wish I could have had a scoop of ice cream or just cream with it but that's not a criticism.  I think the chicken could be a little better.  Maybe I should try the neck bones or the barbecue. next time.  It was a great experience.  The mac and cheese looked fabulous and I wish I would have tried it!

I knew that Sweetie Pie's was a great restaurant when I first entered the doors but I was not prepared for how delicious it would be. 

I went in and ordered the friend chicken with Mac n Cheese and mashed potatoes. The first thing I noticed was how great the ambiance was; It made me feel very comfortable. The next thing was the presentation: all the food looked absolutely delicious. The best part however was when I sat down with my plate. 

The food was absolutely delicious. The mashed potatoes were smooth and creamy. While I will say that my mom makes excellent Mac n Cheese, I think even she would agree that this was something special. But I think the best part was biting into the large piece of friend chicken with its crunchy and flavorful exterior and it's delicious interior. This meal was beautiful and I will definitely be coming back for seconds sometime soon!

The first time I tried sweetie Pies I was in awe, The food is that good. That was approx. 5 years ago. Always crowded, food always taste delish. The more popular it became, the less food you received and  the more they charged. Bottom line the food is so good, but your not getting enough of it. :((Very Skimpy!!!!!

It's Chipotle, the food and atmosphere is the same as every one I've ever been to. It's clean like most Chipotles. I only come here when I have a random craving for Chipotle, or when my friends convince me we should all get together here because it's cheap. 

One time they gave me a hard time about my "homemade" Halloween costume for a cheaper burrito, but they still gave me the deal, so that's neat.

There's nothing great or bad about it. As per usual, I just love the chips from here for some reason. It's just a Chipotle. Guac is still extra.

I went here about a month ago. Hence this review is long overdue, but I remember it all pretty clearly. My actual rating is 4.5 stars. I really wish yelp would make half stars an option.  

Atmosphere is decent. Seemed clean. Cafeteria style, but maintains a homey feel. The waitress was very friendly, but a little pushy, as waitresses that work in cafeteria style establishments often are. Prices are a little on the high side for counter and tray service, HOWEVER.......

The food here is FANTASTIC. Truly. I loved it. My entrée was the duck. So flavorful, so moist, so good. For sides I went with the renowned mac and cheese, the string beans, and the okra and tomato. The mac and cheese was actually quite amazing though it sadly did fall short of the hype. When the hype is the best mac and cheese in existence though, falling short of the hype ain't too shabby. The string beans were phenomenal. Perfect flavor and moisture content. Melt in your mouth type beans. The okra and tomato was actually my least favorite and I'm a huge okra fan. I guess I found it just to be a little heavy on the brown sugar. My girlfriend got some candied yams which were fantastic and the baked chicken which was actually a little dry. I went back at the end of my meal and got a piece of fried chicken, dark meat. It was great as well. Excellent skin and salinity which complimented my hot sauce perfectly. 

Definitely a must stop if you are in the area and enjoy soul food. I WILL be returning and trying the other entrées, which rotate throughout the week.
One of the nicest chipotle restaurants I have ever went to . Everything was clean and good portions .

I didn't even get a chance to go to my room before I was kicked out... let me explain; my husband had went into the lobby to get our keys for our online reservation... we have a service dog which we explained that we left our original card in Ohio by accident (I did have a photo copy to show). She then was VERY rude and unprofessional and told me the photo copy meant nothing to her. My husband asked if there was a problem and then she threw his ID and credit card at him and told us to GET OUT in a rude tone. I asked if my card was going to be charged and she shouted NO! I then looked at my statement and my card was indeed charged.  I don't know what the rooms look like but I do know that the staff is horrible..

Went here last year while i was in town and the place did not disappoint!!;  Go for the  history; go for the friendliness; go for the atmosphere but man oh man go for the FOOD; I'm a southern boy and i love fried chicken and theirs was excellent;   plenty of food also and great service for us out of towners; can't wait to go back

Went on a Sunday with the girlfriend and her mother and was disappointed. We waited nearly two hours to eat and it wasn't worth it. The meatloaf was bland the fried chicken was dry as dirt without much flavor and the wings weren't anything special. As far as sides everything was ok at best. We had black eyed peas, sweet potatoes, cabbage, dressing, okra, mac n cheese, and mashed potatoes. The cabbage, okra, and sweet potatoes were ok everything else was mediocre. I gave two stars because the staff was great and the third because the banana pudding was good.

Came in to enjoy some food. Our waiter Karla was AMAZING! However there was another waiter there older lady with blonde hair. The whole bar area referred to her as "Guera" was yelling and being hostile to the other staff making the experience less enjoyable. But again Karla was great, the food was delicious. But that waiter could use a chill pill.

So I came to Sweetie Pie's because my mom watches her reality show on tv and reminded me multiple times leading up to my trip that I just HAD to go. I'm glad I was the obedient child because the food was ridiculous!
It absolutely reminded me if my grandma's good old southern cooking. I shared the fried wings, catfish, black eye peas, and green beans. We each got our own mac & cheese cuz let's face it, we both knew we weren't sharing it lol. 
Everything was excellent. Although the catfish was a little too salty for my taste buds, I was pleasantly relieved that it didn't have that Mississippi River taste that catfish usually has. I'm usually not the one for black eye peas but I was this time : )
My dining experience was perfectly fine until we got ready to leave. The party of seven that was near us, that reminded me of understudies for the Klumps movie, were taking pics of my friend's butt. We were both ready to attack but decided to leave with dignity and huff and puff in private. 
With that being said, as a girl who was raised by a southern mama, SP's gets five stars for food but 3 stars for the experience (which fortunately had nothing to do with SP or their service).

I went to Sweetie Pie's on Sunday, 9/3.  The servers were rude, the rest rooms were dirty, and the food was so salty I have been sick for three days. 

In addition they didn't have three of the main entrees listed.  It was a salty disappointment.
After much prodding I decided to visit Sweetie Pie's looking for some down home southern food. The food was good, but not the best I have ever had. Maybe I should have tried it when thy first opened.

Wilson's shoe repair is the best.  L O N G  term family business.  George does fantastic work and often can do repair while you wait.  I have had heel caps and a purse strap repaired on the spot.  AND they clean & shine your shoes so upon pick up they are ready to wear.  Wilson's also repairs luggage, bags, etc.  Try to hang on to your ticket & don't wait too long for pick up. Good people & great work.

AWFUL!!!!!! Came in today with my bf we just came from the Phillies game, 13$ for a burrito and drink (it's a fast food place) the food was terrible and my bf was vomiting shortly after. The cashier/girl with the tattoos on her arm was beyond pushy I said I wasnt hungry and was watching calories, she then went on to describe in detail what I should order. No thanks I'll stick to Qdoba if I want cheap (mexican) fast food or El fuego.

Great food... Great atmosphere... Very pricey!!

It was our first time and surprisingly it wasn't too crowded. We were prepared for the cafeteria style lunch line, which mares selecting a bit rushed compared to having time to sit and review a menu.

The selection is based off what is available for the day, I was hoping for peach cobbler, but they didn't have it that day.

The food was really delicious! But make sure to bring ur wallet...

Awesome, awesome food. We went to celebrate my mother-in-law's birthday, and it was a huge hit. However, it's important to be aware of what you're getting into, especially if you're going on a Saturday like we were. 

1. Get there 45 minutes early. I am not kidding. We did (by accident, as we thought it opened half an hour earlier), and so we were near the front of the line. By the time the doors opened, that line went around the block. People were waiting a long, long time in the heat.

2. Be prepared to deal with a lot of people all around you. The staff kept order very well, but if you don't like crowds, brace yourself or don't go on a Saturday afternoon.

3. The staff are all very nice, and the male waiters will carry the women's trays. (I was a little confused at first when this happened, but it was nice!)

4. They carry your tray because your tray is HEAVY. A LOT of food. Don't worry, you can get a box. 

5. I had fried chicken (special), yams and macaroni and cheese. All very, very good. 

Enjoy!

I had a moving service unload my stuff. One of the guys was from New York. So I had to ask, where do you go for pizza? Rocco's! He goes at least twice a week. Boy was he right! This is now my Friday routine! Handmade dough, homemade sauce, lots of toppings makes for an amazing pie. Can't wait to try the rest of their menu! Anyways ready when they say it will be and very friendly staff (despite always being busy).
I love this store!   Great Prices and so many great wines to choose from.   The people who work her are awesome, I am older and they always ask me if they can help me to the car with my purchase.

As a former Maryland resident I was excited to see a Chipotle appear near my office, and the staff at this location is phenomenal.  Service is always fast and friendly, and if you're a once-a-week-or-more regular with the web orders, as I am, quite quickly they recognize you and have your bag ready to hand over when you get to the counter.  Qdoba is closer to my work, but I've not darkened their door since this Chipotle opened.

Only pizza place I'll go . I have never had bad service or food when I have gone here . They have a great selection with great variety. The Chicken Knot is pure heaven , and so is the Chicken Parm Sandwich. The Stromboli is massive and at a great price . And finally the pizza . I love the pizza the supreme is fantastic not to greasy like other pizza joints, and a plus they have a nice gluten free pizza for those who have a gluten  intolerance. This is one restaurant on my list

Where do I begin with working with Tara? To say she was amazing would be an understatement. Her attention to detail and kindness throughout the whole process made me feel like we were friends from the beginning. The entire process from beginning to end and all of it in between was flawless and Tara was a joy to work with. She helped me to feel like a princess on my wedding day without overdoing the make up as someone who does not wear too much makeup on a daily basis.

I will be recommending Tara and her team to all of my friends who will be getting married in the future.

I freakin LOVE this place! And I am not saying that on a biased opinion, or because others rave about it also.

When I went back home for my yearly trip, I knew this time I HAD to try this place, last time the place was closed, and I had to catch my flight. I went with my grandparents, and boyfriend. We drove there and it was pretty full, a bit of a struggle to find parking but that was OKAY for me this one time knowing that it is a famous place.
We found parking got in and got in line to get food. It is very simple, and to be quite honest a great way of doing things in order. The wait was about 30 minutes or so the line went fairly fast. I got up there with my grandparents, and I pretty much ordered the moon. My and my granddaddy both got catfish while my grandma got barbeque and my boyfriend got catfish. I got extra sides than the two that you can get with the meal strictly because I was there for the experience and price was not a object. I had so much in my hand the waiter came and helped me first. His name is Calvin, he was extremely nice and my grandparents loved him. He made jokes, and kept the whole table laughing. He was very attentive to all his tables. Sweetie Pies has great customer service. I have been to soul food joints and to be quite frank the customer service is bad. NOT here! Ms. Robbie is not going to play with you treating her customers and kinda way. :) 
My boyfriend loves the TV show personally I don't. My boyfriend and I both agree that Sweetie Pies is the best soul food we have ever had. We can't wait to go again next year. The place is awesome and I will be going for years to come.
Very good food.   Service standard for this type restaurant.   Beware - a small is huge!!!

Its been almost 3 months now, since I purchased my Fusion and the crap you read about their service depatment is starting to reveal its ugly head.

I have put on 6,000km and during that time, 2 things are starting to happen with the car. 1) from time to time, I have a problem downshifting into first, when I'm stopped at a stop sign or traffic lights. Slamming my foot to the floor on the clutch or "double clutching" doesn't always work.  I did bring the car back to them and asked for a mechanic to take a look - in short, I was told that the mechanic found nothing wrong, and maybe I wasn't shifting properly. EXCUSE ME?! I learned to drive standard in the Army - I think I know how to drive a standard vehicle both AGRESSIVELY and city-wise!! 2) About 2 weeks ago, I had to make a sharp right turn before smashing into a huge owl on the Edmonton Garrison, and now I am having issues with my power sterring. You know that winding sound it makes, when its low on fluid? Yup - and since then, I have put almost 2 bottles of power steerring into it!

Now when I bought the vehicle, I paid almost $3,000 to have the warrenty extended to 100,000km. When I took the car in - NO ONE mentioned that I had to pay $150 upfront as the deductable on that warrenty. The tech who was asking about the issues, showed me a peice of paper outlining the possible problems and its costs and then asked if I wanted to pay the deductable now ....... or after the repairs?! 

So the car is not being repaired at this time, till I can budget the deductable .......... and I pray nothing else goes till then !!  I can see why people are happy about buying cars from Kentwood but not so much on the repairs! And like Gary C. from here in Yelp ........ the slaesman I bought my car from AND the young woman who set up the paperwork - are no longer employed there. Makes a person think about what the hell this dealership is doing!

All I can say is it's a long long wait, really really really good home made food from scratch. The chicken hot and fresh as well as the other side dishes too. It was like eating a Sunday dinner at home, all except we were lazy and didn't feel like cooking. So we piled up the kids and went there.

Fried chicken wings. Mac and cheese. Black eyed peas. Cornbread. Peach cobbler. Banana pudding. Sweet tea. OMG. Worth the line wait. And the staff!!!!! Amazing. Seriously amazing. I want to eat here every Sunday.

Four tacos, warm chips and the best salsa I've tasted for $7.00 and change. Unbeatable! Grilled Serrano peppers add the needed heat. Warm friendly atmosphere. The carne asada is missing that authentic taste but overall a very decent place.

This place is good and the staff is very nice. There had to be a 2 hour wait to get food. Lucky we got there at 11:15 am so we didn't wait long. I had the chicken with corn and Mac and cheese. My boy had the catfish and both were good, I was hoping to have greens but they didn't have any so that's why I have it a 4 instead of a 5 but I am going back home (Bay Area) a happy man. 

Thank you STL it's been a great trip
Overall. Some if the nicest people I have ever meet. Sorry my 49ers spanked you but we do own the NFC West!!! Until next time

Probably the best Chipotle I've been to in my area. For being the only chain that has a place in my heart, I haven't found a chipotle that doesn't have some sort of issue. This location is great. The staff is prompt and courteous, they listen to exactly what you want, and they're organized! Food is always stocked and warm. Gasp! I know it seems ridiculous to hear, but I have had some horrible experiences at other Chipotles. Other locations I've reviewed could really use some pointers from these guys! 

Only flaw is how tight of a space it is. I never sit down to eat there. Weird seating plan.

This place is right off the Yellowhead & easy to find. There is a ton of parking & Kathie at the front desk was awesome. She's always friendly & really puts the service in customer service. She really went the extra mile to make our stay comfortable. She has an incredible knowledge of the city & surrounding area & knows which way to point you for whatever you're looking for.
The rooms are clean & tidy. I had everything I needed & getting extra towels & pillows weren't an issue. The internet was slow but it did the trick.
Some of the clientele are a little shady but it is a truck stop so a transient nature is to be expected. 
It isn't the hilton but for a motel 8 it's worth the price. I would for sure stay here again next time I'm in Edmonton.

Great juicy fried chicken, the yams are so sweet and delicious, corn bread was fresh, Mac and cheese was cheesy and savory. The best part is the banana pudding pie!!!! We went while they were filming a new season of their reality show and unfortunately were waiting for our drinks, napkins, refills, boxes, etc, not a good time to ask for service. It put us off and we won't be going back for awhile. There's still a million more places to try is saint Louis!!!

I wanted the catfish, but they were out. Got the fried chicken... glad I did.  It was juicy and well seasoned.  No complaints.  Also had candied yams.  Delish!  Perfect, actually.

Oh... yeah... and THE FRIGGING MAC AND CHEESE.

Sweetie Pies is famous for this like... for a reason.  

I'm something like a mac and cheese expert.  I've had the fancy smancy stuff with the guyere and pancetta and things...meh.  I've had small time diner stuff... hit or miss. 

But this right here... this mac right here... is kind of  the best I've had (right under moms).  Like I ordered an extra to go because I'm greedy and never mind a diet.  

My mouth is watering...

The quality of service provided combined with the outstanding customer service makes this the only place I take my automobile for service! 
Visit Brett & his team of professionals- I promise you won't be disappointed!

First of all the food was good! The chicken wings and corn bread was on the greasy side though, could benefit from some drainage. Moreover, the service was TERRIBLE, my mother was not greeted when she came inside. Also, there were not any souvenirs stocked. They should get a course on hospitality and friendliness. I would have given Sweetie Pie's a 4 star but the service knocked it down to 2 star!

Enjoyed the banana pudding very much.   Had the special of the day, 'ribs' ... excellent.  A bit of a wait to get food though but worth it in the end.  Baked beans were good as was the mac & cheese.  Would go again for the banana pudding alone.  When you are there I would recommend looking at the chalkboard above the buffet line to see the specials and order one of those.  Price was good.

I have been off and on coming to Countryside ever since it opened in the mid-1990's. There is no question the food is fantastic, from the generous breakfasts to the gourmet Ivy-league school-named sandwiches. The food deserves 5 stars, however, I have 2 issues with Countryside that take away a star each. 1. The service is pretty lame. I don't remember ever having someone truly pleasant. The staff look like they don't want to be there. 2. Every place everywhere else gives you free refills of common drinks such as sodas and coffee. Not Countryside. You pay for every refill. Big no-no. Coffee should be bottomless, especially for me who tends to take a lot of it. This is a major factor when picking a breakfast place, I'm sure for a lot of folks. So in summary I will suggest that Countryside's food is well worth it, but just do takeout instead...
The BEST fried chicken in America! The sides were crazy good, too. I can't believe how nice the service is. Next time I'm in Saint Louis I will return.

Love this place! I often stop by for lunch when I visit a doctor in the area during the week. The place is quaint, the food delicious, and the staff is very friendly. I see others have complained but perhaps it's a weekend crowd issue or even that they've hit during rush hour noon. I am there usually between 1 and 2 and get a great seat, fantastic service, and refills of my tea without asking. No complaints here except that they aren't closer to Rox/Manayunk where I live.

Brought in two pairs of Allen Edmonds shoes to Mr. Wilson for new heels. One pair had a missing tassel.  When I got them back I could not have been more pleased with the quality of the work. They looked like new and the new tassel looked just like the original. Very pleased and I highly recommend Mr. Wilson. He is a real professional!

Came through on vacation..... Excited to have some REAL soul food.... Fried chicken had real flavor but was dry :( , corn was great, BEST MAC N CHEESE EVER!!!!!!! , so much food took home leftover and ate Mac n cheese cold and was still good!!! , yams were delicious, waiter was funny and attentive!! Probably just an off night for the chicken :(

For a cafeteria style soul food spot, it doesn't get much better than this. Probably the best mac and cheese I've ever had in my life. Two sides? Double order of mac then.  The smothered pork steaks are worth a call before visiting, as they do not have them everyday.  So tender you could eat them with a dull spoon. 

The staff is incredible and the prices are very affordable, although so much of it looks good the add-ons add up quick! lol  

P.S. I also recommend the cobbler.

Delicious. Everyone was friendly. Food was fantastic! Fried chicken portions were large but seasoned great and not dry. Neck bones were tasty and not fatty. Mac and Cheese was cheesy and creamy. String beans, cabbage, banana pudding and peach cobbler were all good! The only thing I didn't care for were the black eyed peas, I've only started eating black eyed peas in the last few years (as a child I couldn't get over the "eye" thing) but the times that I've had it the base was creamier; these were watery and had a strange sweetness to them but heck, Robbie can't get it ALL right. LOL

Will I be back? Definitely...if only I didn't live 1500 miles away. :)
It made both me and my fiance sick last night.  I got the vegetarian sofritos bowl and he got the chicken bowl.

my friend & her kids wanted to come here since they saw it on oprah & of course im always down to eat! I had fried chicken, okra, corn, mac n cheese, cornbread & peach cobbler. The peach cobbler was my fave part of the whole meal and it wasn't even that great. Ive had better back home in Chicago but we had to at least try it. my friend agreed & we both were disappointed with the food we all tried.

Ok, so ive never had dim sum or been to chinatown for that matter, but when you date an asian girl you get to do these kind of cool things..
----------

FOOD: You can get some other things, but my girl wanted to get me some dim sum, so thats what we got. The vegetarian choices are kind of sporadic, but you can find them. We had to ask a bunch of times for meatless stuff and still got some meat.
Otherwise it was pretty tasty. mmm.

DECOR: Its a chinese restaurant style. Pretty nice.

SERVICE: Well you really dont have one person, you have a bunch with carts with food on them, but they were friendly. One drawback however is that they mark the slip entirely in chinese. So if youre a bean counter and dont know chinese, youre going to be out of luck.

----------

WOULD I GO BACK? Sure would, but not without my girl. She knows what to get and what not. I just know good food when I eat it..
Excellent store. They have absolutely everything under the sun. Great owner and employees!  Will definitely recommend this store to everyone. Thanks for carrying Guidance Whiskey
Love the selection and service here. This is a wonderful owner who dos so much for the community.

Yo, when they say like a cafeteria, they mean it. And when they say it's soul food, they mean it!

Decor: It's actually a pretty big place. Once you enter and you turn around the corner, you'll see that nice familiar cafeteria booth with all the metal trays with the poles designating how/where to line up. It was a bit stuffy/warm for my preference, so much so that the windows were all foggy from the temp difference.

Service: First off, the man who fills up my Sweet Tea and who welcomed me in was ABSOLUTELY WONDERFUL. He joked with us and always had a smile as he persuaded us to get more Sweet Tea refills (Free!!). The workers serving the food are very generous with the portions and they're super funny.

Food: Going down the cafeteria line, I decided on the following foods (pictures posted)
- Fried Chicken: uh, no duh I'll try that. They were GINORMOUS, juicy and greasy. yessss.
- Mac&Cheese: I do not generally eat mac & cheese. This? I gobbled it up in a jiffy. 
- Candied Yams: Tasted sugary like a pie and sooo delicious. 
- Cornbread: This was about average, not to say it wasn't good.
- Sweet Tea: pretty decent, pretty good. I went to the South once and well.. this wasn't like the South's but it was good.
- I tried my friend's fried catfish which was pretty good.

It was all comes up to about $10+ which isn't too bad, I thought, for the portion you get. The food+decor also explains why this is so popular among college student. :]

Bottom Line: Yeah, you'll feel a little greasy and you'll feel some indigestion, but you need your fill of soul food every now and then and this is the place to get it. :]
Bret helped me get the correct size and style tires for some classic cars I'm working on. Everything fit and worked perfectly. Thanks!

Pretty darn tasty!!! I have been wanting to try Sweetie Pie's for a while and today was the day! I ordered the fried fish with sweet potatoes and collard greens. The fish was hot out of the fryer, the potatoes were sweet and full of flavor and the collard greens were off the chain!! So delicious. Also tried the fried chicken, green beans, and mac and cheese! The fried chicken wasn't listed on the menu but it was very inexpensive!

This place will charge you 100 dollars just to pull codes.  They are a business first and a service second.  They are good for tires.  Overcharge for oil changes. Manager is nice (Brett) but obviously a company man.  This is based on years but f experiences but this last one really rubbed me wrong. 
Update now that I am less angry: I went in to have a sensor replaced.  They wouldn't do it without diagnostic work.  Once they did the diagnostic (all they did was pull codes, the same common codes I already pulled.) and came up with the same problem I did.  Then they want the charge me even if I have them do the repair.  The truth is they operate just like plenty of other chain mechanics and I am sure the owner has made plenty of hundreds of dollars off of plugging in a machine and pressing a button.  Hopefully someone will revolutionize the auto repair industry and make these types of shops be more honest and transparent or go out of business.  I am fine with either. These guys have the experience to quickly diagnose (that is a compliment) but they treat every situation the same and that is BAD customer service!!!!  The "owner" commented that they would like to talk more, but left no contact info.  Just trying to save face on a bad review it would seem.

When you sit down with your plate of food at Sweetie Pie's, it's pretty much a five-star experience. Everything looks so awesome and you're all excited to destroy everything in front of you. But things quickly turn two-star when you realize how heavy and rich everything is and you spend the rest of the night in physical pain from what you've done to yourself. I'm talking just from eating half of what they give you. Clear your plans. You're not going for that jog. You're not running by the store to pick up a few things. Just forget it. Your night is over.  

Insider tip for those who share my anxiety about eating chicken wings in public: there's a camera crew running around that will catch every embarrassing bite as you gorge yourself. If you don't want that making it to prime time on the Oprah Winfrey Network, I suggest you order the fish. 

Don't get me wrong. The food is great. The people are super friendly. I would sell my own mother for their pear cobbler and if she tasted it she probably wouldn't even blame me.

But it all comes at a price...

My wife and I stopped by today based on recommendations from other yelpers. The Fall leaves and Halloween costume decorations in front of the restaurant accentuated the name of the place. Place was pretty full for a rainy Monday noon. We found the service was attentive and food was brought out promptly. I liked the Widener Way sandwich (corned beef and pastrami with swiss cheese, sauerkraut and russian dressing grilled on rye bread) per the recommendation by the waiter. My wife had the half (ham salad) sandwich and (vegetable and chicken) soup combination. She found both a little on the salty side. Overall an enjoyable experience.

Visiting from New York Roccos was recommended by family who live here we stopped in on a busy Friday night and had a great meal. Service was very adequate my wife accidentally spilled her drink and they moved us to another table immediately.Had pasta with clams mussels shrimp.very reasonably priced. My wife and fettuccine Alfredo and it was cooked just right had leftovers brought him home and we ate them again the next day very good everything was excellent I recommended very highly the prices are really very very good and this is coming from a person who owns a restaurant in New York. I have not tried the pizza but I have heard that it's pretty good
When I'm in need of soul food, there's no other option for me.

To me it was the worst experience ever. Its says Mexican restaurant but what kind of Mexican restaurant doesnt has red Chile enchiladas?  So I got the child relleno and it was disgusting.  The restaurant is very messy. Their servers suck they take forever to help you. I believe for us to get our order on drink it took about 20 - 30 minutes, and it wasn't even that busy. Just a very bad experience. Would never go back.

I don't know what some people talking about that this hotel is a 1 star? I got a non smoking room and it's big and smells normal. Internet is fast. Free breakfast. For $115 a night with 2 queen bed is average in the city. Maybe not he best deal but it's acceptable.

Upon the urging of daughter, we went to Chipotle this evening.  While I love their burritos,  this was the first time that I had the displeasure of eating a steak burrito that I did not like.  Five pieces of steak were mostly fat. I understand that the fat gives the steak most flavor,  but I'm sure that my burrito would have tasted better if the pieces of steak had been leaner. I still like Chipotle,  but I'll probably consider having something other than a steak burrito.

Honestly one of the most tedious and slimy car buying experiences of my life.  I like the car and some of the staff were nice, but customer service was terrible.  Lots of waiting around and feeling like a cog in a wheel.

We came on a Monday around 10:30 and the drive through was really busy but the man on the other side was collected and polite as could be. Our service was fast and Pete(?) (older bald gentleman) was very polite and smiling. It's nice to have good complimentary service like that!

The trick to eating at Sweetie Pie's is to go when there's not a 100 person deep line snaking down Tower Grove Ave. Do what I did and go on a Sunday night, where you can get in and get out with no wait.

Everyone got the fried chicken. It comes with a 1/2 fried chicken, roll/cornbread, and two sides. The chicken was marvelous, crispy and juicy and just perfect. The okra was a miss for me, the texture was pretty gross. But the mac and cheese was sublime. 

Service was friendly and quick.

This place is awesome. Good food, casual, friendly atmosphere. As others mention, its cafeteria style, and they have extensive daily specials.

Chicken wings are great, but I've recently tried their boneless catfish fillet and it is the SHIZNIT. Great flavor, slightly spicey, meaty and tender and flakey, and a large portion of it. The sides are fantastic as well. My favorite are the corn, mashed potatoes, and of course, the mac and cheese.

The food is heavy no doubt, and i'm fairly certain that it accounts for a lot of the morbid obesity and high mortality rates in the area, but its WORTH it.

So went  on a thursday for lunch  had a 1/2 chicken breast   2 sides-  Cabbage and okra -  Grease  above all  limits  okra was so overcooked I wouldnt have known  what it was ,cabbage was tasty only  but  because it had a huge hunk of salt pork  in it.  and so greasy I asked to just have one side    no I had ro take 2   This meal cost me almost $12  . That's a lot of money  for that kind  of meal
I left most of it 
Never again

My boyfriend ate here over the weekend right before his night shift and had to leave early (i.e., lost wages) as he had explosive diarrhea and vomiting. He vomited all night and had chills, dizzyness, headache, and body aches. He's still recovering. I called the manager but he said that "no one else reported anything", and clearly didn't care.  Don't risk it, eat someplace that doesn't have a long history of poisoning people!
Very good, but the music sux. No great atmosphere and music other than rock would have earned a extra star.

The car has been repaired and still there nothing found with the shifting problem.

I had a chance to chat with the General Manager of Kentwood and he himself, test drove the vehicle and still found nothing. He appoligized for how everything was dealt with and how we were treated from the Service Tech.

Overall experience with this dealership - not impressive.

I'm truly disappointed.. It's cool to have said I've been here now but I wouldn't recommend anyone come here. The male waiters were probably the highlight of my day. They were so nice and respectful and truly were the best part. The food was awful, the strict rules on what you can get and not being able to customize is stupid and clearly so old they need to change it. Not to mention the women that plop your food on to your tray are extremely rude. They look like they simply don't want to be there. I had ribs, mashed potatoes, and corn. The ribs were average they had been sitting there a long time. The potatoes tasted weird I can't even explain it. The corn was so different it was ok though. Oh and the cornbread I was so looking forward to it and it was just dry and bland. I was going to get dessert but the cobbler looked runny and like it had been sitting there awhile. I paid like 16$ to eat shit. Not to mention I had bought a bottled original sweet tea.. OH MY GOD! Do they even taste that? It's the worst tea I have ever had in my life.. I almost threw up! I can't believe they're allowed to sell it! I had to ask for a sprite instead cause I couldn't drink that. I was expecting since it's the 2nd location that it would be done up all nice.. Nope! I'm pretty sure the building was an old Chinese restaurant because that's what the decor was! It's was hideous! Save your money and go elsewhere the experience is sooo not worth it.

Co-worker took me here for lunch and bless my soul.....
Authentic, tasty, love it!
I had the Chile Verde and it was great. No, hold that, it was smack my ass and call me Guera Loca good.
My co-worker had the Tamale combination and it smelled and looked great and he said it is his favorite and he comes here a couple times a month.
I will definitely be coming back and bringing my husband.

Now, let's keep in mind I'm comparing the Chipotles here in Philly to my  fair, fun and beloved state of California. 

Pros: 
-consistently great taste of the food. Steak or chicken, the meats are delicious. The veggies and dressings are fresh too. 
-the tables are clean and even though this place is always busy, you can always snag a table. 
-another thing, the packaging of the product is cute! Aesthetics are important too you know! A nice, decorated recycled brown bag for the food is cute :)

Rocco's is the best  for many reasons, Pizza is the best , Rice Balls just like my family makes, Unbelievable! The portions are large, and delicious. Never had a bad Anything here, Place is spotless.

Everyone treats me like family, waitresses are great, very willing to go out of their way for you.

Thanks Rob for your kindness as well!

Can't get any simpler.

1.You go in and stand in line  
2.Choose burrito or bowl add to it whatever you feel like it (type of rice, meat, dressing etc)
3.Pay  
4.Bon apetit.

Few things to be aware of: guac is extra so are chips and drink. In all decent lunch that is going to fill you up.

The service here is awesome! The server really made us feel like we were at home. The food was also great! The fish and fried chicken are really yummy! The mac n cheese is also really good! Everything we had was really good. The only thing that keeps it from being a 5 star review is the fact that the food is served off a buffet line, and not made to order. Everything was good, but if it had been hot and fresh, it would've been even better!

Great! I make sure to visit here whenever I go to St. Louis. If you love soul food this is the best place to go. I love it! I recommend the chicken wing meal with mac & cheese with greens or sweet potatoes. I don't think you can pick a bad combination.

This place was pretty neat, you walk in and walk through like a cafeteria line getting your meal along the way from some very friendly people and its all right, but the food just didn't "WOW" me, they do serve different food throughout the week so you might want to find that menu if your expecting to get something someone recommended.

Some of the sides were really good especially the mac and cheese, it was pretty fantastic, but the rest of the food wasn't all that.  i would have to say i would have to have a hard time taking someone new to st Louis here, it wouldn't be a "must go" place and that's sad because its local.  they have big tables so you could go in big groups and there was fairly a descent amount of them so not a long wait at all. it wasn't packed on the day i went so i feel lucky from what Ive heard.  

The server/host/seater guy rocked!  he was very friendly and funny always making some sort of joke to keep us entertained.  Him and the mac and cheese get all three stars!  Not probably going to be back here for a while but ill give it another chance for sure

The only reason this place received two stars is because of a few of the servers who were really nice. The food was under seasoned and too sweet. I bought fried chicken wings, Mac n cheese, green beans, and peach cobbler. Everything including the mac n cheese was way too sweet...horrible!!! Some of the money being used to open up new restaurants around  the country should be spent on remodeling, and cleaning up this disgusting place. I was so disappointed and will never visit any of her "cafeterias" again!

I and my family visited Sweetie Pie's Mangrove this Pass Sunday, and absolutely  enjoyed the food, atmosphere and friendliness of the Wait staff! We're coming back to visit the Sweetie Pie's upper Crust!

I visit yesterday with two of my friends and I had a great experience overall. The place was packed, we waited an hour and half in line before we got to the actual buffet line to order, but it was worth it! Food was delicious and the customer service was fast and courteous. Overall the place was clean and had a convenient parking area across the street from the restaurant. Definitely a place to go!
I've been here a few times and it's always busy. The line goes quickly and I love their food.

I herd this place was good, wow is that an understatement, It was GREAT! Great service from our server joe and his coworkers. The chicken knot was delicious, as well as all our food. Had the pleasure of meeting one of the owners, Stephanie, she was awesome, made us feel like she was welcoming us into her home. The pasta carbanara was sooo good. Cant wait to go back! Save room fir the mississippi mud cake YUMM!! Thanks again Stephanie.

We have been here several times over the years. Mostly because of the location, close to work and other local businesses. The service is always fast and friendly, good chips and salsa. The food is OK but nothing to rave about. Everything we have tried from tacos to tamales seems to be made fresh. I would assume they make most of their profits from the large bar area. We would return.

This place should really get 6 stars for being up in the spring hill/brookesville area.  I would imagine the line would be out the door 24/7 if Roccos was down here in Tampa.

The portions are huge, the prices are right, and the quality is really there.  Just typing this I feel like words are not enough to praise this family Italian spot.

Order some pick up or pop in for some dine in, you wont be disappointed.  All of their pizza looks amazing, but we've been stuck re-ordering the Stromboli and calzones.

You will not be disappointed..

All of my friends who had sweetie pie's say it's not all that. I don't know if they are just saying that because of pride/bias because people always feel that their mother makes chicken the best  or if they are really mean it, but the chicken hear was off the chain! All the sides were good- collard greens, macaroni, peach cobbler you name it. The only downside was the location and the long line. The location was a little sketchy and I guess a long line means great food but damn, an hour and a half is just to dang long for some fried chicken haha. It's a good experience to go at least once to this place but I refuse to wait that long for some fried chicken again.

Stay away!  I went looking to purchase that day. I knew exactly what I wanted and had cash with me. Frenchy, is his real name, insulted me over and over. So I went straight to city ford and bought an Escape that day.

Curiousity beheld the cat...

Sweetie's was virtually my prime reason for traveling to this neck of the woods.  Perhaps I expected too much-- I am a born southerner who loves southern food and on top of that, Sweetie's is on TV. That being said...

This location, for some reason, was recommended over the Upper Crust one.  It was located in a part of town you'd want to steer clear by sundown. Cute exterior, but the interior was somewhat dingy and cluttered with signs that say off-putting things like "We are used to stupid questions." Okaaaaaay, so much for any hospitality.

The staff was efficient, but lacked warmth. I kinda felt like I was imposing on their down-time. Well, perhaps the food would make up for any perceived shortcomings, I opined.

Ha! Not by much, Ms.Robbie. 3 cold wings + 1 gross-tasting, lukewarm cabbage + 1 what-the-heck is in my green beans (cold, tasteless, odd-shaped potato pieces)+ peach cobbler (this GA peach gives it an A+)+ tap water= $15.69.

Add in the cab fare to get there and it was a $35 excursion. (Thankfully, I didn't have to pay for a round trip.) So, doing the math, you can say that I spent $35 for a small peach cobbler-- even more if you add in airfare and hotel. The cobbler was good, but not THAT good, LOL!

I recommend that if you're a newbie going to venture to Sweetie's, try the Upper Crust location. I was subsequently told that this is where filming takes place. Certainly, you'll get more for your money than a small serving of cobbler!

We just left out and it was TASTY!!! 3 of us had the catfish dinner, although it was fried a bit too hard for my liking it was still delish... I had the Mac n cheese and yams which comes with cornbread. I also had the black eyed peas over white rice and it was BLAND! So NO to that. And the 4th person had pork steak and they liked it. The only bad thing is the line was REALLY long. That could be due to the Hawks playing tonight and the Bears playing tomorrow. Chicago is DEF in the Lou today.

Soooooo slow.  I thought this was fast food?!?  I never eat here.  This reminded me as to why I don't.  The people working seemed annoyed with one another.  One kid was trying to fill the Coke Freestyle machine with ice while another one snapped at him to help with the growing line.  It was just kind of chaotic.  Our fries were hot and fresh, but salty and poor quality.  They don't hold a candle to Wendy's or McDonald's.  My nuggets were too bready (if that's even a word).  Burger King just isn't my cup of tea.

If you have never had soul food then this is the best place to become acquinted.

Atmosphere:
Comfortable is a good way to describe this place. If you're not quite sure how do get around people are always willing to help out point you the right direction. It's usually kinda loud but never overwhelming. Friendly and welcomed are great ways to describe Sweetie Pie's.

And it's non smoking in there from what I've seen. 

Food/Drink:
Yams, Mac and Cheese, Greens, Fried Chicken, black eyed peas. I could go on and on about the food. My fellow Yelp'ers have gone into deeper detail on the menu. I would say if you're on a diet then don't go here!! 

Drinks are your standard fare of sodas, juice and water.

Cost:
For the amount of food you'll get here it's a pretty good deal. The portions are huge. I don't think I've finished a plate during any of my visits.

Overall:
One of the best restaurants in St. Louis easily. There are few places in St. Louis that cause my mouth to water when mentioned. If you've never gone then make it a point to go.
The food was really well-seasoned. The staff was friendly and courteous. The cobbler was the best!!!!!

Sandwiches have always been delicious, and the sweet potato fries are great. The shakes and smoothies leave a little to be desired, but prices are reasonable for the quality. To address the other reviewers, I haven't experienced the snippy waitstaff or management, and have always had adequate service in the dozen or so times I have been (at least as good as any other local lunch spot).

Being a southern California native I love Mexican food!

Lupita's menu is in Spanish first with English translations- everything here is amazing and the prices are unheard of- $6 for a 2 item combination plate with beans and rice! The portions are perfect- not so much you that you overeat. Their salsa is great and all the food is so flavorful, salsa is really not needed.

Although they are closed on Tuesday's (and I always seem to crave them on Tuesday's)

My partner is half Mexican, and I'm usually the only gringa in the place- a great sign for great food!

Hands down the most real Mexican food in Reno!

Disclaimer: we visited two days in row as we were from out of town. 

Now that's outta the way, I will say that my first meal was delish. It consisted of the three wings, yams and Mac & Cheese. Wasn't too fond of the cornbread, guess I'm just a Jiffy cornbread lover. Other friend had the smothered pork steak but it was cold but her sides (black eye peas, yams and mac & cheese). Other friend had the same meal as me except she had other chicken pieces. Two of us had peach cobbler and one banana pudding. 

Sunday: it must have been good cuz we came back for some more to take home, four hours away. Meals included meatloaf, baked chicken(good) and of course, wings again...Mac & Cheese(better than Saturday), greens(ON POINT), yams...all good. Peach cobbler was good but that banana pudding was right on the money!!!

Downside: on Saturday, while in line, the line staff is a bit rough in tone. We had picked up their brand tea and from outta nowhere we hear someone yelling, "CAN YALL LAY YALL TEAS DOWN ON THE TRAY FOR ME?" We were like what the hell just happen. We were feeling like Seinfeld's soup nazi episode, like obey the rules or get out. 

Side note: bottled tea was not good at all

Sunday: back in line, since we were traveling, I asked could my yams and greens be put in the side containers. Out of nowhere, some lady comes with a EXTRA bad attitude, yelling that any side the line lady put in those containers would be $3.69 a piece. SAY WHAT!!! I'm traveling, I don't want soggy chicken when I get home. The issue is that she was extra rude to my friend and I and it was completely unnecessary and it could have been handled much better. Even when we asked the staff her name, they even shrugged and rolled their eyes like, "huh, she's one of the managers"

Good food..bad customer service tendencies...need some retraining!!!

Very happy with the quick service (and knowledgeable staff) that was provided for my 2006 Honda Pilot when an irreparable hole from a roofing nail was found in one of the tires. I was able to get the car in on a Saturday morning and get two tires replaced, after it was explained to me why this was necessary. I appreciated the quick service because I needed to drive it out of town the next day. I will definitely recommend this business to others!
Lots of food and a consistent line that flows quickly. We had to get to go boxes because of the large plates of food.

I have always been real happy with Indy Tire. The staff is very helpful and attentive. I have never used them for anything other than buying/ repairing tires, but they have always been good to me. Comparable prices to the wholesale clubs, but more personalized sales and service. The only way they could do better would be to spray those new 215/55 R16s with some ArmorAll before giving the car back.

Give them a try and support local businesses!

Well I'm still new to this whole Yelp thing but here it goes...

Chipotle has always been a mainstay on my commute to and from my job. I usually like to get a big old burrito before I clock in at the lab. TeckQuarp has a very strict policy regarding employees smelling like food upon entering the building and I'm happy to report that I just smell like fresh chicken when I arrive now. 

When I visited Chipotle this morning, I ordered my usual: Fresh chicken and salsa verde... and welp, they delivered. And even with a smile. As I type this, I get excited to stop by tomorrow (or even tonight because I getting hungy as I type this!!!)

Service with a nice smile and free tap water in a to go cup. 

Yes. I'll be back tonight!

4 stars for the cool wall mural & dcor + 1 star for the luke warm fried food = 2 stars experience at Sweetie Pie

The thoughts of retro cafeteria style soul food was mouth watering.  Sadly, the reality at Sweet Pie's fell short of my expectation.

Though there was a respectable flow of patrons during the late lunch hour...the food was obviously cooked very much earlier in the day and it showed...the fried catfish and chicken wings particularly suffered from a cold chewy crust, rather than being hot and crispy...okra was also cold & mushy...the best thing on my plate was the macaroni and cheese mainly due to the fact that it was warmer than room temperature.

There are Qdoba people, Chipotle people, El Fuego People and none of the above.

I am more a Qdoba (sans tortilla, sans cheese, try to get the calorie count down).

Meanwhile, Chipotle (which is now corporate fast food owned) is an inexpensive and FILLING (even the salad or bowl options are HUGE) lunch or quick dinner.

Their meats (Chicken & Beef are the only ones i have tried) are spicier (more peppers??) than Qdoba.  Also they use white meat - Qdoba uses thighs.

It's OK by me.  A-OK - in the true yelp 3 star way.

This location is new and relatively clean (crowded at lunch time on weekdays - deserted at dinner.).

Was so excited when Smyrna finally got their own liquor stores. Was even more excited when Smyrna Divine opened up. The owner,  Shirley has always been most helpful in my ignorance of wine and they have the best prices in Rutherford County. Looking over some of the other reviews, I'm wondering what the motivation is in some of these folks. Although I do not know any of the workers personally, I have always seen nothing but professionalism towards their customers When shopping there and I'll go a lot.

Family run restaurant with super fresh a la carte dimsum and a more Chinese than non-Chinese clientele. I like the Cantonese fried chow fun noodles with beef, most of the dim sum, and the baby bok choy w/ garlic. Great value, zero ambience. Rather, the ambience is functional rather than decorative. Bustling during lunchtime and often at dinner. Like most Asian restaurants, they welcome kids. Take a date who appreciates great food, not fancy lighting.

They'll also do takeout orders. And I think they're closed on Thursdays. Or it might be Tuesdays.

Horrible Horrible Restaurant!  The owner needs to stand in line for an hour and let someone slap food on her plate.  She should be embarrassed.  I have worked in food service, therefore I have knowledge and this was a nightmare.  Food was COLD!  The mashed potatoes were from a box, gravy was cold, the chicken was mediocre, the fish had been soaked in egg so long that it tasted like eggs & fish, the green beans were from a can and cooked to death and greasy, black eyed peas were like black eyed rocks, the peach cobbler was basically sugar soup with a few peaches in it.  I felt like I was at school with those poor ladies spooning food onto plates.  You can't hear anything, and did I mention the flies circling the pans of food and the restaurant is DIRTY.  Lets not talk about the "old bar" area and all the junk, employees personal belongings, mop buckets, punch clock, etc - this is what you have to look at while you wait for 40 minutes in line #1.  How about cleaning up?  The entire set up of this restaurant is a _ _  backwards.  You stand in line #1 for 30-40 minutes only to stand another 30-40 minutes in line #2 near the food. This place could be run so much more efficiently and customers wouldn't be writing BAD reviews (Oh, and there are many) about Sweetie Pies.  Then at the end of the line, after you have paid for the cold food on a plate - a waiter shows up and takes your food to some mystery table - then you have to spend time trying to figure out where he went because there are so many people.  If Oprah went there today, she would be terribly disappointed.  This place needs a make-over - it's a disaster.  They have the nerve to videotape a reality TV show there?  It's more about drama at the restaurant - don't we already have a multitude of crappy TV shows about the same topic?  Here's some reality - this place is horrible, gives soul food a bad name.  And they opened up a second restaurant?  How about cleaning up the first restaurant?  Perhaps the camera should focus on the mess instead of the drama and confrontations within this so-called restaurant.

This food is so dang good. Like. There's nothing else to say. I had the fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes and the peach cobbler. The chicken as cooked perfectly and had the crispiest skin. The mac and cheese was cheesy gooey, and savory. The sweet potatoes were exactly how my grandmothers cook them sweet and soft! And I truly could've died over the peach cobbler (so much I went back and bought some more). The line was long when we first got there considering it was a Saturday evening but it moved quickly and we even got to take a picture with TJ. (is that his name?) Overall food was great, staff was great, my experience was...well Great!

Use to eat there 2-3 times a week. Not anymore, they can't seem to get an order right & @ 6:00am the end of the catsup dispenser looks like it wasn't cleaned the night before & that's just the out sid

While chipotle isn't the best burrito out there it can still be pretty good in a pinch. That being said the employees at this location are rude and the meat is often cold. The last time I went I asked for beef on my burrito and the grumpy woman ladling the lukewarm meat into my burrito gave me four chunks of beef. When I asked if that was all the meat she was going to put on it she said "yeah you got a problem with that?" And I said yes I do that's hardly any meat and she said well that's all that were supposed to give you but with a whole lot of attitude. I then asked for guac and said I wouldn't mind paying extra and instead of putting it on my burrito like I asked she put it in a to go cup. I asked her if I could have the guac on my burrito and she pretended like I didn't hear. The service here really sucks don't waste your money.

let me tell you... i absolutely loathe chain mexican food. BUT, this is actually some good stuff. fresh and simple ingredients, clean place, and not too expensive. This is quickly becoming one of my favorite quickie food stops in center city. oh and p.s. their guacamole is actually really good, dont be afraid if your an avocado snob like me :}

Let me add review #390...just in case you weren't convinced by the previous reviews!

Even though it was busy with a line to the door, they did a great job of keeping things moving.  It was a Saturday and it was dinner time, but y'all ran out of the fried chicken, no biggie..you quickly brought it to the table!  Thank you!  It was awesome!

No doubt I'll be a return customer a few more times, but I don't know how you put up with the rude demands of some customers...you handled them great!  

4 star service, 4 star food!

I travel the country and taste food. Thats what I do. I know soul food and I'm not from deep south. First off, when examining a review, one  must take into consideration, WHO is giving the review. Someone that breaths soul food or someone that trys it every now and then. With that said you must trust me on this review. 

This food is served cafeteria style. Any time food is served in this manor there is so much room for error. Either food will sit in grease too long or temperatures will go up and down. Some foods don't taste good after the original heat has left it and taste quite different when reheated. The guards covering the food were kind of high up which means with just a slight bend, hundreds of people can now be breathing on all the food.( People with colds, flu, etc..) 

The food : It appears and taste like sugar is one of the main ingredients in all of the dishes, including mac and cheese. Putting sugar in mac and cheese is not needed to bring out great flavor. Just tasting it threw my taste buds off big-time. I had a serving of short ribs with potatoes. I gave up looking for meat as most of it was fat mixed in with shreds of meat. The candie yams were loaded with sugar with a heavy taste of molasses. I had a cup of it and I had maybe 2 or 3 pieces of yam and the rest was mashed up sugar and potato. I could not take more than two bites before I gave up. I wanted fish but they only do fish on Fridays. ( anybody can fry fish or chicken without any great skill )  The chicken was the only solid tasting thing I got. I held on to that piece like it was the last piece on earth. Not because it was that damn good, but because I was trying to stall on eating the rest of this crap that they piled on my plate. (enough for 3) Plus, I had to figure out a fast exit strategy because this location is surrounded by empty and boarded up 2 and 3 story buildings...First time I've ever seen a neighborhood in this kind of shape..If you do go anyway, please make that trip in the day time. You will thank me later....
AMAZING is the only way to describe their food! Smothered pork chops, fried chicken, mac n cheese, green beans and banana pudding to die for!!!

This is the best auto servicing place I've ever been!  They were fast, accommodating, and didn't try to up-sell me.  Had a slow leak I just knew everybody I'd go to would say I needed a new tire or four.  They cleaned the chrome rim corrosion and sent me on my way for a reasonable price.  Thanks Guys!

(To the tune of The Chainsmokers' hit, Kanye)

I was feeling hunger pangs
Didn't seem to fade away
Despite gum I was chewing
Tried to get 'za from Bufad
Service was just really bad
What were they all doing?

Took BSL to the Walnut Street Stop
Looked around... Looked around....
Then I just knew, that the food I would chew would be foundddd....

I wanna eat CHIPOTLEEEEE
It keeps me oh so fullll-yay!
Barbocoa in my belllayyy
All day... Chipoootttleee, yeah, yeah.

That said, this Chipotle in particular, while delicious as per usual, has some issues with design. Namely, there's no real funnel for folks trying to wait in line for their food ordering process to begin. This results in a kind of splotchy "line jumble" that isn't really a line at all, mostly just a jumble. Not a problem in the middle of a late afternoon, but around lunch time.... trouble.

Not a buncha seats. This WOULD be a problem... if not for the other Chipotle about 3 blocks away.

I went here about 15 minutes before closing. Instead of telling me that they had run out of most things the guy started making my order. He put literally 5 pieces of chicken on my order, no beans, no vegetables and when I asked him what was going on one of the other women comes in and claims this is the usual portion size of chicken. When I complained and told her I'd been here enough times to know that was not the case the guy making my order agreed to add in sofritas. If I hadn't complained all I was going to get was rice and 5 pieces of chicken. I am disappointed that there was no apology, they charged me full price for a sub standard product. Another guy came in after me and made the right choice by going to qdoba. I'm going to do that in the future and you should too.

Went to another place and they quoted me 4 hours to look at my tire and then told me to go to gas station to air a low tire. Best One told me to come right in and got it fixed in an hour on a busy Sat. Very quick, courteous and professional. Thank you!

Minimal indigestion.

Fast line.

Cheap.

Huge portions. 

Always get the barbacoa, get a burrito bowl with extra black beans and skip the rice and enjoy your low carb meal.

We were on a trip in St. Louis and we decided to go to Sweetie Pies.   The line was long, but it moved pretty fast.  I had the catfish, mac and cheese,  and green beans.  The catfish was too salty and fries too hard.  The green beans were sweet and the mac and cheese were alright.   My husband had the pork chops, green beans, and the black eyed peas.  He said the only thing that was good was the pork chops.  Everything else on his plate was sweet.   He was even disappointed with the bottled sweet tea.  If we visit St. Louis again, this restaurant will not be on the itinerary.

I went there for dinner at 8:30 p.m. (1.5 hours before closing). They were out of (at least) mild salsa, corn, and chips. A few people left because of this. Not sure why these couldn't be replenished since 1.5 hours were left. The guacamole was brown. The stations were a mess (cheese and corn spilled everywhere). The cashier was very inefficient and rude. He was not attentive to the customers checking out. After I paid, he shoved my uncovered bowl towards me, after which I told him it was "to go." He then yelled "can I get a lid?" Someone placed a lid on the bowl. The cashier never came back to bag my order so I bagged it myself. With all the setbacks Chipotle has faced and the increased competition in the city, and generally, I would expect better, especially since this location is already easily accessed from a sketchy side street/alley so it is not uncommon to see people under the influence inside or to be aggressively harassed for money while dining in (which should not happen). Do better!

REALLY REALLY GOOD. This food reminded me of my grandma's cooking. In a really good way. 

Ordered the fried chicken, macaroni and cheese, and sweet potatoes. It came with cornbread. 

Everything was SUPER tasty. It could have stood to be a little hotter, but the flavors were there. And the portions are HUGE. I couldn't believe how much food was on my plate! They are not stingy here at all. 

Another huge plus was the friendliness. Everyone, EVERYONE here was super friendly. From the sweet guy who directed my confused boyfriend and I to where the line started, to the woman who plated our food, to the cashier, to the busboy who brought us our drinks and cleared the table. EVERYONE was super nice. I felt right at home. 

I ordered some peach cobbler to go. I really wanted to try it right then and there, but my stomach felt as though it would explode if I forced any more food into it, so I passed. 

If the food was a tiny bit hotter, this would easily be a 5-star place. Next time, I'll come RIGHT when it opens to get the perfect experience. 

Thank you, Sweetie Pies!

Tara did a great job on every girl that was in my wedding, she is reliable and extremely professional. I would definitely recommend her to anybody looking for great makeup for whatever special occasion you need, especially weddings. There is no other person out there who will make you look more beautiful on your special day. She also does awesome Halloween makeup when it comes time to impress at parties. I have seen her do some of the most realistic scary faces/masks around. She is definitely a professional at what she does, look no further and call her for your makeup needs.

We will most likely not be back. We came because my husband loves fresh made tortillas, well they don't make them anymore. When I ordered I had to ask for three different things since they were out of what I asked for. This was at 10:30 am so you would think they would be ready for the day. It also smells like smoke inside. Overall it was not a good experience. The food I ordered,mole, was ok. My son couldn't eat his carnitas though. Our food also took almost 45 minutes to come out and we were the only ones in there.
Had to get new tires so I went here.  The staff is awesome.   They were friendly and took the time to explain everything to me.   Very helpful. I had a great experience and will be back.

Macaroni was too sweet....staff was obnoxious....not a friendly enviroment... they don't want you to point at the food but they can't hear you behind the food and will get attitudes.  The chicken was Ok. ...
somebody call the dea. they put some sort of drug in the mac n cheese. addictive as hell.

Definitely a "hidden gem." Everyone I know who has eaten here considers Lupita's one of the best Mexican places in Reno/Sparks.    

As other reviewers have said, I usually find myself the only gringo patron, which is definitely a good sign.  If you think Super Burrito or Q-Doba is authentic Mexican food, you might want to stay far away from a "real" place like Lupita's.  Or treat yourself and try something new, but you probably won't ever want to go to the fake Mexican places again.  

Lupita's seems to have an abundance of seafood items on their menu.  Everything's divided into combo plates that include beans and rice, or a la carte items.  One half of the restaurant is a bar area, with non-functioning poker machines set into the bar, and TV's that play soccer games and Mexican music videos, for the most part.  

If you order tequila at the bar, you get a free ceviche tostada with each round.  I'm not sure if this is only at night.  The one time we did this, it was pretty late and they were getting ready to close.  That didn't stop the bartender and servers, who were all extremely friendly and didn't try to rush us through our drinks and food.  At $5-7 per tequila shot, things got expensive quickly, but if you consider the tostada piled sky-high with sliced fresh octopus ceviche, that $5 round isn't too pricey (the tostada alone costs $3.50 if you order it a la carte).

For those who haven't tried ceviche, if you enjoy octopus and squid at the sushi bar, you owe it to yourself to give the Lupita's ceviche a try.  As Clint U. pointed out, ceviche is fish marinated in lime juice and spices.  The lime juice starts to "break down" the seafood to make it more tender, less rubbery and to soak in those all important spices.  The tostada itself (a deep fried tortilla) is the size of a large saucer, and they pile it 2 1/2-3" high with the seafood of your choice.  You can get it with shrimp or octopus by itself, but I like the ceviche combination which features squid, octopus, and shrimp, tossed together with cucumber, tomatoes, and onion.  I think last time they might have thrown in a few scallops as well.  Two tostadas ($7) is more than enough for a full meal.  If I remember correctly, the bar served the octopus only with the cucumber, tomato and onion mixture.  These are extremely authentic, fresh items that I can only compare to the food I ate when  in Mexico, as far as a reference point.

A word of warning about the bar: it was deserted the night we went, but on the weekend (even early in the afternoon) the bar can be quite busy and EXTREMELY LOUD.  There are no walls separating the bar from the dining area, so your ears get pretty well blasted by the Mexican music cranked up to top volume.  Apparently they have karaoke here as well, probably just in Spanish but I'm not sure.   The fact that it was clearly not karaoke hour didn't stop two hearty-voiced gentlemen from singing/screaming along with the music videos.  It was pretty disorienting at 1 p.m. to have my meal accompanied by raucous drunken singing, so if you're sensitive to noise you may want to consider a more formal "sit down" type place.  The server was very considerate though, and asked me if the noise bothered me, I'm sure she would have tried to quiet the drunks down if I had insisted.  The bar scene at Lupita's could also be intimidating to someone who wasn't Latino possibly...it seemed like a fairly close-knit group of friends/"associates" who were hanging out if you catch my drift.  So if you're used to the soccer mom-style bar scene like Chili's or Applebee's, you might be in for a good dose of local flavor.

If you're not going to drink, just order off the a la carte menu, unless you're hell-bent on getting the beans and rice for an extra $2-3 a plate.  Tacos are $1.50, the meat is good but they're very small.  I tried the "adobada" last time which is beef marinated in a spicy sauce.  Carne asada, carnitas and al pastor also hit the spot.
The best value, though, is the burrito which is only about $4.  I get mine "banado" which is similar to the "mojado" (wet) burrito that a lot of places serve: dipped in the sauce of your choice: red, green, or mole.  I've only tried the red so far, but next time I'm all about the mole mole moley!!  Along with the sauce, a small amount of sour cream is drizzled on top, also a handful of "queso fresco" which is Mexican crumbly white cheese (kinda like a cross between bleu and feta cheese, but not as strong-tasting).  My only complaint about the burrito was that I ordered it with avocado--if there was any avocado in there, it was too small to detect.  Hopefully I didn't get charged for it.  There is a big variety of items to choose from that I plan to try, including soups, fried fish plates, and seafood cocktails.  The iced tea tasted like a weird carbonated verison of Lipton's, so other than beer, I'd recommend the "fresa" (not listed on the menu) which is strawberry juice--VERY sweet and refreshing.

Perhaps it is because I've gotten all the soul food I could ever eat from some of my relatives or maybe we caught them on a too busy day...but Sweetie Pie's is good - just not more than 3 stars good to me.  It is a cafeteria line you stand in (and depending on when you hit it, you will be standing for a bit) and based upon how much you want to spend you get that much food.

Hubby did love the chicken wings, the candied yams were a bit too sweet for me, greens weren't too bad, and the mac and cheese was yum!  But the peach cobbler let me down.  Was not feeling it, tasted too artificial to me.  The staff is friendly and even as busy as it was, our server kept bringing back the tea for us (good tea!) 

It's a good place to go for an experience in good down home cooking type of food.  We won't be going back because it didn't impress us that much and as I've said above - I have relatives who cook this way. And they're free  ;)
A must for your bucket list!  I'm up at 3AM back in the ATL & wanting some Mac and cheese and some peach cobbler!  My dad is a chef so I KNOW I'm a foodie aficionado!

If you're going, get there early before rush hour starts and even then there's a line. I ordered the chicken wings. I received 3 and shared with a friend who ordered fish which is only served on Fridays. I also ordered 3 sides, pinto beans. Mac n cheese, and okra. My Mac & pinto beans were loaded with sugar. The fish was really tasty. I would definitely go back for the fish, maybe the wings. Some in my party had green beans that were sweet. The pear and peach cobbler were raved about as well as the sweet potatoes.

If you ask someone the definition of soul food, they'll give you some spiel about soul food coming from the heart, and stuff about family. Really, soul food comes from an amalgamation of African, Southern, and Mexican cooking using the garbage parts of the animals that were given to the slaves by their owners. You can see how collard greens might have come from this, and dirty rice and cracklins make plenty of sense. Some foods, I'm not so sure: macaroni and cheese? Sweet potatoes? Red velvet cake? They're all homely enough and make sense, but until my visit to Sweetie Pie's, I didn't really believe that the hospitality had much to do with it.

Everyone who works here is extraordinarily nice. Not that creepy sort of "Stepford Wives," type of nice, either - a genuinely warm and inviting atmosphere that was infectious. I felt happier just being here, and that was before the food.

I wanted some fried chicken, and I said as much to the young man working behind the cafeteria line. I stopped him after I watched him put four large thigh pieces into my takeout container. Surely he thought I was eating with another person, because that was way too much food. He told me that this is an order, and suggested I have some for leftovers. I accepted this and moved on to some greens and mac and cheese, both of which were served as heaping servings, severely weighing down my flimsy styrofoam container. As he was closing the container, he wrote "8.50" on the top. At the time, I thought there was no way that all of this food could be mine for only eight and a half bucks, but the register confirmed it.

Soul food is not the trickiest cuisine to make, but fried chicken is probably the most difficult. You either have a crispy, dry exterior with a juicy interior, or you don't. Sweetie Pies' passed muster very well, and I ate more than I was expecting. The mac and cheese was done right, too, with indulgent amounts of cheese in a baked casserole with a crusty brown top. The greens were slightly bitter and with a reminiscence of pork, as the good ones usually are. 

As I left with over half of my meal remaining and a genuine happiness in my heart, a lady behind the counted asked me how everything tasted. I said it tasted very good, but if I could have articulated more at that point, I would have elaborated much further.

If your goal is to gain a couple hundred pounds, clog your arteries and have a good time doing it, this is the place for you! 

Don't be thrown by the name, this is soul food at its best. Friendly workers, enormous portions and too many great choices. 

This cafeteria style eatery has a few guidelines. You get in line and always, I repeat always keep your tray on the counter! Meal choices are laid out. You get to choose one meat. I chose the fried chicken wings. You get four and they are the biggest chicken wings I have ever seen. Really tasty too. Then you can pick either two or three sides. The macaroni and cheese deserves a parade and the fried corn was pretty great too. To top off your heaping plate that already weighs about 12 pounds they add an enormous piece of flavorful cornbread! 

While checking out I asked about the desserts. The nice lady explained that they had apple cobbler and fried apple or peach pies. Fried pie? I had to try this for myself, so I got one to go. Who knew that McDonald's or Hostess didn't invent this idea of the little pie pocket deep fried? 

After sufficiently stuffing myself and vowing to make this a regular destination, I took home 3 of my 4 chicken legs and my fried pie. Which later on that evening I found to be completely amazing!

When you wait in line for food for over 2 hours, ANYTHING taste good. With that being said, I've had better food than sweetie pies. They were filming the reality show when we were standing in line and they recorded us for the show. So that was cool. The food isn't the best.
