Went there for the Gumbo the day after Christmas. Service was not good. Waitress was always in a rush. Rush to take order, to explain dishes. Had to hunt her down for water refill and bill. Food quality was very average. Prominent location near the market seemed to be attracting customers off the street.

Service was horrible. Food was overpriced. When I go out to eat I want the restaurant to make food that I cant make. The Cajun Creole sampler was something I could make with some rice and pre-made sauce mix. No refills on soda. Disappointed that I wouldn't give 1 star but had to for yelp.

This place sucks. Looks good on the outside cause it's right by the river but when you walk inside it is far from that. It's half in a strip mall and you can see people walking by doing shopping it's just really odd. The food tastes like garbage. Service was really shitty and the place was kind of run down. I asked the server what jambalaya was and she replied "it's rice with shrimp." "You don't know what jumbalaya is?!!" In a very bitchy manner. I am not from the south or New Orleans. How am I supposed to know? You're the sever it's your job to tell me what the native food is. Stay away from this place, I will never come here again. I should have gone to another place!

Great service! Staff are nice, room is great! Shuttle bus is a bonus to have which I believe lead you to the Hard Rock Cafe. The hotel is close to Ascend Amphitheater and Nissan Stadium! (Like 10 mins away) I recommend coming here again!
The food was generally good. We also had a great server that night. The red fish, fried oysters and fried catfish was delicious. The gumbo though, not so good.

As a chef I admit that yes, I do have a slightly higher standard of food...but this place was bad...everything was fried and the oil used was clearly old and should have been changed about 2days ago. Then to top it all off, after we got our main courses our waitress (Rebecca) came over and says that there system went down and that we had to pay in cash! I had to get up from the table and walk a block to the nearest ATM.... by the time I returned my food was luke warm at best... needless to say I did not finsh even half to plate....dosent matter where you are at, this way of running a business is simply unacceptable.

Service was horrible, waitress disappeared several times, had to ask other servers around for refills!  Then she added 18% for tip, we were waiting on change and host asked us to get up so he could seat someone else!!  We ate at other restaurants where quality was much better!  Worst dining out experience in NOLA!

Sheffield's Diamonds is the perfect place to get an engagement ring. I was only 23 at the time, just about to graduate school, and I had no clue about what kind of ring to get, all I knew is I wanted to ask my girlfriend to marry me!

When I came in, the staff was super nice and very welcoming. I was helped my Mr Sheffield himself! He asked me what my girlfriends taste were and if I had any pictures of what she likes. I showed him one in particular and he knew exactly what to get me. 

I feel it's more trendy now to get a more simple ring design and the ring I picked out was absolutely beautiful!!!! I had to choose between two diamonds and couldn't make a decision, that's when Mr. Sheffield weighed out the pros and cons for both and pretty much picked the right one for me. 

The staff was never pushy on anything and they treated me as if I was a long time customer! The engagement ring ended up being the most beautiful ring, in my opinion, I could ever give my now wife! Whenever we are down in Tucson, I come to say hi, and we come to get the ring shined! I would highly recommend someone going here compared to a place like Tiffany's or those other joints! There is a huge difference in customer service and the Sheffield staff are all great at making you feel like
you're the most important customer!

wThe blackened redfish is fantastic. Was in New Orleans 3 + 1/2 years ago and had this dish twice. Came back now, went out of our way to return, and just as great! You have to try. Melissa was a fantastic server as well! Will be back.
Have been coming to Redstone since they opened.  Consistently good service, food and management.
Amazing place. Visit joe bacon at the art table. This place is full of art and good art at good prices.

Wow. So good. The best pizza I've had in Florida hands down. 
So I'm from Chicagoland, and have lived in NYC-so I know my pies. This place is legit. 
The crust perfectly charred with that amazing combo of crunchy and chewy. 
The toppings are fresh, delicious, and aside from maybe a bit too much garlic on one the pies (whole cloves-tasty but Wowza) I can find no faults. 
Service was ridiculously friendly, knowledgeable and quite frankly I can't wait to return. 
Now as soon as my tummy settles I'll get to work on the cannoli I brought home. 
This is must do for any foodie in Tampa Bay

Surprisingly enough - this was the best gumbo in NOLA that I tried.  

Very touristy.  We only went for the gumbo on a recommendation from a local.

Well... I have a lot to say about this place. After being turned away from 3 other places on a Saturday night because of a "backed up kitchen" we were lucky to find refuge at the Gumbo Pot. The host was friendly so we had high hopes. Unfortunately we were ignored until we had to flag down a waitress who told us she would find out who our waiter is and get them "in trouble." Things were looking up finally. She came back shortly and said she would take care of us because the other waiter didn't want to work anymore... She made some other comments that made us smile. Definitely looking up. We ordered the BBQ Shrimp appetizer, the gumbo, and the Creole Sampler dinner. After having the BBQ Shrimp at Deanie's this was definitely nowhere near as good... In fact it almost shouldn't be called BBQ shrimp. It wasn't terrible, just... meh! The gumbo was good. As for the creole sampler, the jambalaya was the best part. The crawfish étouffée was ok and the shrimp creole I could've done without (too tomatoey & not enough seasoning.) I have an overall mixed review but I don't think I would return. There are much better choices in the French Quarter.
The blackened redfish was better than last night's Redfish Grill and the chicken andouille gumbo was fantastic. Terrific place for dinner before a paddle wheel cruise.

I very much enjoy stores like these - but under certain conditions: I make a plan and stick to it (because you could spend all day here), or I have something very particular I'm looking for. This Homegoods is a good bet - I found exactly what I was looking for the other day, I just had to zero in on it! They also have a lot of clothes, home goods (duh!), and other random shit you probably don't need - but shopping is fun, and so is looking at everything all under one roof! Like in my review for nearby Marshall's - if you don't find what you're looking for here, there is a Stein Mart and Marshall's nearby.

Very good American fare, pricey but worth every cent. 

Their burgers are amazing and pretty affordable when you compare it to the heart attack on a plate that is served by the five guys who work for the coronary stent manufacturing industry.

The burger is actually an all beef burger that  stays securely in place on the bun.

Treat your self and a friend to what a burger should be !

ok folks, this place is about as touristy as tourist gets, so know that when before you even go. its definitely not there for the locals! but with that being said, as a die hard local, i gotta say i was impressed with the gumbo, which is really good, and with their version of bbq shrimp. prices are reasonable (for those who think it too expensive, get a clue!), the location is great, and the service is pretty good, plus they open for breakfast, and serve a fairly good breakfast. for the idiots that complained about the fries being bland....come on, they're french fries, if you think they are bland there are more than enough condiments provided for you to make them whatever you want them to be! great place to grab a bowl of good gumbo and some seafood. don't come here expecting gourmet fare and you should be pretty pleased, and it's easy on the wallet

I've been using this establishment as a quick-lunch place for quite a while now.

To me the pizza is standard, and there is nothing special about the place itself. Has a fixed menu, with slight alterations, and they don't have the "you must try it here" item.

The place will not wow you, it doesn't aim to. But it will never disappoint. always good, warm, fresh food.

 Which is good, because this is one of my go-to lunch places, and I would be annoyed if they erratically changed something about them, or revamped their menu, or focused on making a few "more popular" items.

It is very wallet friendly. Serves freshly made pizza slices (among other things), and the staff is nice as well.

easy parking in the lot outside.

me and hubby came here for dinner, the gumbo is salty and extremely salty. When we order the "catfish salad", my hubby told the waitress that he want his CATFISH well fried. Ok. So after almost 35 minute waiting (unacceptable), they delivered CRAWFISH salad, when we tried to tell them we order catfish not crawfish, one of the black waiter told me" you sure? you sure it not your delusion mind? He think it funny, i think it mean and racist. Just because we are Asian, does not mean we cant pronounce CATFISH right, and hey, he is not the one who took my order at first. The food is terrible, the service is awful, when we tried to ask for to-go box, another waiter asked me " You sure you want these to-go back to your hotel??" Sure, jack-ass, Sure if you have to pay over price for 30 $ red fish, 8$ for a small cup of gumbo and 25 $ for a salad, yes, no kidding right?. Not recommeded. Please, do not come here.

Went there at 5:00 pm on a Saturday so we could get a table in the bar area.  Seems like we got lucky and were seated immediately.  They have a nice diverse menu with good surf and turf options.  We started w/ the Tuna seared w/ pepper and salt along the edges.  It was awesome!  I had the cajun ribeye w/ a side baked potato and corn bread.  The ribeye was one of the better steaks I've had in a long while.  It was good quality, seasoned perfectly, and cooked to my liking - medium.  Our waiter was friendly and knew the menu well.  No complaints.

Went here today for a light lunch with mom. It was very trendy (too much for me) but very friendly and prompt service. They get an A+ on service. Food was good. I had the flatbread and caesar sald combo for 15 bucks. The flatbread had mushrooms (cremini) and truffle oil. It was good. not fifteen dollars good but edible and satisfying. The flatbreads at Cork in Haddon Twp. are 3 dollars less and are way better taste wise. They brought out the wrong food but appologized  3 or 4 times and brought back the right meal in 2 seconds! The salad was excellent and they didn't charge us for sharing. We din't see a drink menu with all these yummy drinks everyone else was talking about. We didn't see a "noshing" menu either. i guess me and mom are not hip enough. Nice atmosphere, okay food just not my kind of place. I definately wouldn't trek all the way up to Marlton in traffic to go eat here.

Had breakfast here,. Creole Breakfast and Lost Toast.  Not all that bad.  I am a grits fan so the grits were pretty good.  Lost toast is their version of French Toast.  A po-boy bun made into French Toast.  Pretty good.  Service was so so.  Food was decent.  Outdoor Dining with a nice patio.

Great Sunday Brunch! We celebrated our anniversary here a few weeks back and I can't wait to go again. The wait was minimal for a table. The waiter brought us free breakfast bread that was to die for (blueberry lemon) and complimentary mimosas. I had crab cake eggs Benedict and my husband had steak and eggs. I'm not sure of the cut but they looked like 2 petite filet minions and I wanted to lick my dish. I think we spent about $50 for the meal plus tip which was way less than I was expecting, you could easily spend that in some of the diners around here. Service was impeccable.

I LOVE THIS PLACE!!!  I can't seem to stop going there!!  I've loved everything I've eaten there and they always provide great service.  The spinach artichoke dip and the barbeque pulled pork sandwich are to DIE for.  SOOOO GOOD!!!  I'm never disappointed when I go there.  There can be a 2 hour wait on the weekends but it's obvious why.

Was excited to eat here, given the name of the place i thought the gumbo would be good if not delicious-was so disappointed! i ordered the creole combo which consisted of the crawfish etouffee, jambalaya and shrimp creole and the seafood gumbo. the chicken in the jambalaya was so dry i could have chocked on it, the etouffee was decent and the shrimp creole tasted like shrimp cocktail but on a plate, the seafood gumbo was something you would get at a chain restaurant like Pappadeaux's. the price was not worth the food it was overprice for mediocre food. wont come back, to top it off the waitress gave me the bill while i was still eating and i wasn't even half way done with my meal, then i waited 15 mins for her to come back and run the card, i had to wave down another waiter who spoke with the host who finally got the waitress so we could pay our bill. 2 stars because the food wasn't bad but it wasn't good the waitress was decent at first and very lacking at the end.

if you want good gumbo at a good price go to The Original Coffee Pot - Gumbo on St. Peter St.
Soooo good! Loved the pizza pop it was amazing, affordable, and a lot of food! Have been there 3x so far and have loved everything I've gotten.

I had the farm girl pie roasted duck,mushrooms, cheese,tender fave beans and white sauce all topped with arugula, it was very good, light on the sauce, flaky thin crust, fresh ingredients, fast and friendly service.

If no one greets you upon arrival and you awkwardly sit there for more than 5 mins, feel free to walk yourself up to the counter and ask to place your order up there. Worked for me! I'm gonna chalk it up to new business growing pains as to why I had to walk up to the lady at the counter several times to 1) ask for a menu 2) order my food 3) pay my bill. Granted it was busy for a Sunday brunch, but only for a good couple hours before the rush died down and we were still having to wait around for someone to come and close out our bill in the end. To their credit, when I did speak out and walked up to the counter to let them know we hadn't had anyone come around our table, they were profusely apologetic. However, I would like to wait a little longer before I decide to go back for brunch or anything that requires me to stay and eat as opposed to picking up a treat to go. I think it comes with time and experience to be able to manage rush traffic smoothly. The only reason why this place deserves four stars versus three is because their crepe was one of the best I've had! Your order comes with two crepes and you have the option to choose between savory and sweet or one of each! You also get to customize your crepe with ingredients made to order. Same thing goes with the egg omelette but you only get one omelette. Both dishes came with a side of roasted fingerling potatoes. I can't wait to come back and dine here again when they get a better handle of managing tables or perhaps I will just have to come by during off peak times.

Food was good. Customer service was horrible! I have never gone to a restaurant where the waitress treated you like she was giving you charity food. Everyone else with other servers got a french bread and butter and a flag for the 4th of July fireworks and we did not. Didn't think it was for everyone until we encountered the other customers. Horrible!

I met a friend here for tea and dessert, and love it. The decor is very cool and sophisticated  and the pastries are top notch. We tried a couple of different things (opera cake and chocolate pillow) and they were both delicious. I bought a box of a dozen macarons to take to my sister and they wrapped it up nicely, so that was a nice touch. The layout is open so you can see the bakers making things, which was fun. The only thing that was a little strange to me was that the different-flavored macarons were the same color. Probably just a pet peeve, but it wasn't intuitive that both the pistachio and lemon were pink, that sort of thing. I love that they offer classes - my husband and I have made macarons at home twice now (first time was perfect, second time not so much), so we could use a professional's help.
The gentleman made it right today. Very thankful for managers who can correct their staffs attitude and train them with more affective and approachable customer service techniques.

The food here is good, but I'm not sure if it's worth the wait or the price. Especially considering that so many great restaurants are less than 2 minutes away.

On a Tuesday night it was totally packed. There were people everywhere, you couldn't get a drink at the bar and the inside was a mob scene. It's not where you want to go on an intimate night out, that's for sure. 

We ordered the buffalo shrimp because pretty much everyone said they were amazing. And they really were. I didn't expect the combo to work, but they are pretty addicting. 

The cheese fondue was pretty great, but the chicken wasn't really necessary. It would make a great vegetarian option.

Besides that we got sea bass- which was crazy good and cooked well, but a very small portion and the sides weren't very good- and a strip steak- which was well cooked but had way too much butter. 

Dessert was really unimaginative, don't waste your time. Overall, I'm not sure if I'd go back. I don't know if it's worth the insane crowds and the even crazier prices.

Digusting food.. I got the seafood gumbo and it was far worse then mediocre. Barely any seafood and the flavor was so bad.. Tasted like something from a can. It was my first time in NOLA and this place looked like it was good.. I wished I Yelp'd it first. Never going back

This hotel was inexpensive and it's for a reason. It's something out of the late 80s and it is in desperate need of paint and new rugs and a new lobby. That's just my shortlist. However, for $215 in Nashville, it wasn't that bad. We were flying out the next morning anyway and wanted to hit Broadway one more time. We didn't know until we got there that they had a shuttle service to Broadway. This was a big plus. It has to be a nightmare to park on Broadway or anywhere near it. We were happy with the shuttle service except for the fact that it ends at 9 o'clock. Broadway isn't exactly 9 o'clock kind of place unless you decide to start getting ready to go there at 9 o'clock. Regardless we were flying out in the morning and it was fine with us. The bathrooms really needed a full redo. The doors were chipped, there was a really cheap psychedelic curtain as the closet door, and the cheesy crushed velvet bed runners were so disgusting I threw it on the ground the minute I got there. That aside, the service was friendly, the room really was clean, and the beds were comfortable. Would I stay here for more than one night? No way. But for an airport hotel, which it really isn't an airport hotel but for us it was, it was fine.

My wife and I stopped in to look for an end table.  They didn't have what we came in for but we ended up looking all over the place and buying a few other things. 

The store is clean, the staff friendly, and selection varied.  What is nice is the selection isn't stale.  Just wait a week or so and check out the new stuff.  Oh, and check out the clearance isles as well.  Clearance here doesn't mean damaged, just looking to move it.

Great place to find some unique stuff and always a stop for us when we are in the area.

My first trip to Nashville and most downtown hotels were sold out. I booked at the Clarion for 3 nights  for reasonable rates and pictures looked nice. It is clear they are understaffed-it took 30 min just to check in. The bed is comfortable. We definitely did our late nights on Broadway coming in at 1AM. The first night non stop yelling from persons outside to someone in the hotel; partiers are coming in loud at all hours through morning. The second night was pounding on a door next to us and more partying. Each morning/;late evening the front of the hotel is littered with cigarette butts, empty beer cans outside and in the elevators and on each floor. The last morning there were people passed out on the lobby couches. Not recommended for families at all or anyone wanting sleep.

A lot of the museums in Indianapolis are free, for this place to charge admission is ridiculous. Even if it were free it is not worth your time.  
       I suppose if you have kids, they might enjoy it more because there's a few interactive games. Other than that, there's just posters of some athletes that I have never heard of.

The food was okay and the prices were pretty high for what you got. The shrimp in the gumbo was cooked well but the rice was a bit undercooked and the sauce was average. The red beans and rice was pretty good. The kids got shrimp poboys that were tasty. It wasn't that busy but our waiter seemed overwhelmed. I think he was acting as bartender also.

First of all they deserve only 2.5 stars but i'll throw a bone and round up.  It's just too easy to come to and fro Jax and the pier and stop at this place.  I've been several times and they are all over the food road.  It's truly one of those hit or miss joints and I really think their location is what keeps the doors open.  The servers have always been good, though.  As routine would have it, I order bread.....they have no bread, but at this point I think that's more my truman show luck than anything else...(see my review on buttermilk drop and the one about elotes for a helluva laugh).
Food was okay, service mediocre, and prices are crazy high.

Well this is just as about idealistic as it gets in Indy! For that reason, Gallery is my new go to spot in the city to crank out work. The plush chairs, ample table space, natural light, and top notch coffee makes this spot ideal. 

My favorite day to come is a sunny Wednesday when the macrons are $1 each and they open the front garage door to let fresh air in. Although I've not yet had the opportunity to check it out, they recently opened an outdoor patio space as well!

I highly recommend working with Christine! Christine is not only interested in getting you the best bang for your buck, but shows genuine interest in finding exactly what you're looking for. My now fiancé and I went in a couple weeks before we needed the ring and Christine did what she needed to in order to get the ring to him in time. Christine is patient and best of all, not pushy. She has been working with diamonds for many many years and does a great job of educating diamond newbs like me. Go to Sheffield's and see Christine!
Friendly staff and they do a pretty good job with our 3 dogs.also a really clean workplace.we always bring my dogs here.

Forgot what had..... it was a sampler of everything around like $20. The Tartar Sauce was Kicking though! The Gumbo was Good you can get your rice on the side. Wouldn't  come back..... only because  I want to try other places around it. Food was  Great and Service was Kinda Fast..... I times it. Food came out Hella Fast.

Okay, we must have passed this place like 100 times in all of our trips to New Orleans.  Either going to the Mississippi river, JAX, public parking, or just walking up the street to café du monde... and every time it was just a passing "hmm, wonder if they are any good?".  

Was it so amazing that I stripped off all my clothes and went running into the French Quarter, screaming that people must have this prior to the rapture?  No.  But was it good enough for a table of 9 to sit and have a meal that not only were there zero complaints, but food was actually being passed around for tastings??  You bet!!

We had a large group, but decided to skip the appetizer.  I think people we more curious about cocktails and possibly dessert anyway.  So we went straight from drinks to meal orders.  For this occasion, and it being a lunch, I decided to keep it simple with a shrimp po-boy.  The shrimp were small, but at least plentiful (falling off), and it was served with the expected lettuce and tomato.  All was very good, bread soft, thick, perfect for a po-boy.  And the shrimp not only provided the right texture, but had a good flavor too.

Everyone definitely enjoyed their food and plenty of it was passed around with "oh taste this" or "wow, yeah, you gotta try this" comments being made.  So I'd say we made a good choice, and if you're looking for a simple and tasty option, then I'd definitely recommend you make the same choice.  :)

This was the first spot that my group and I visited to eat when we landed in New Orleans. It was a little before noon, so some of us ordered breakfast while the rest of the group had gumbo/lunch. 

I ordered the Creole Breakfast which included eggs with creole sauce, biscuits, and gritz. Wasn't too happy with my order since the creole sauce (that was supposedly spicy) was not spicy! Major disappointment as the whole dish itself was just very bland and not at all filling.

The biscuits were tasty, though. 

Service wasn't so bad, but the people who work there should be more knowledgeable because when food was brought to our table, they didn't even know  what dish it was when we asked. (Really?) -___-

Just stopped in to have them take a look at my Cartier tank watch that i purchased in the early 80s which was showing discoloration on the casing. I had tried cleaning with the cloths I had to no avail.  The jeweler cleaned it for me and it looks brand new.  Highly recommend. Exceptional service.

I had a kale salad and tortilla soup, others had spinach salad and salmon sandwich. We all found our meals very delicious. I personally had every intention to eat half my soup (cutting down). That didn't happen. Big pieces of chicken, great texture, very good.  Kale wasn't tough, not overdressed and ate every bit. Will definitely return.

The food was great the service not so much. We were a group of 5 when the bill was delivered the waitress had put everything on one ticket and had added herself an 18% gratuity. It clearly states on the menu that tables of 6 or more will be automatically assessed an 18% gratuity. We called her out on the one ticket and made her split our tickets amongst us...we never, we repeat never asked for everything on one bill.  I also had water with my sandwich (free I am assuming) when she brought me out a refill she had brought me a sprite (3.75 on the menu).....old trick..

None of us were trying to be cheap our table of five ( not six )  spent 160.00 (with 18% gratuity added) I'm not sure what it came out to after she  stumbled about bringing us our seperate checks (still wrong).

Great food.....Shady service.

I was in the service industry myself when I was younger and I find her actions deplorable.

Enjoy the food, but check your receipt carefully.

I absolutely LOVE this place. It's definitely a hidden gem!

On Saturday, my husband and I, celebrated our one year anniversary. My husband got very sick at our wedding reception with the stomach flu. We spent most of the night at the emergency room and I ended up there two days later and we missed our honeymoon(best weekend of our lives right?). This means that we never got to cut our cake, let alone taste it! Tonight we got to do both(finally) and we're able to stay out of the hospital! 

The Gallery Pastry Shop let us celebrate with an amazing anniversary cake. I will forever recommend them to anyone! Thanks so much!
Extremely slow service and terrible food. The shrimp Po Boy I had gave me food poisoning. Stay away from this place.

Soo much potential this place has . Maybe it was a bad day. I feel like it starts with management , very unorganized it seems , we the consumer suffered. I would share the servers name but I believe since he saw a 6 top full of early 20s adults he was under the impression he wasn't gonna b tipped. Our bill was written as if we were at a waffle house and the total was rounded to the nearest dollar. After unclean silverware & a meal that tasted spoil the manager attempted to make our day better but failed . 

When dealing with tourists or first time guest im a firm believer of " great service can make up for a bad meal but bad service cant make up for a good meal " 

I would like to say when I return to New Orleans id come back but i dont hold the desire to & at the moment i wouldn't recommend it to friends back home .

This was the worst meal I had in new orleans. Shrimp was cold not de veined rice was not cooked I would stay away. Wow it was not even just bad it was gross! I am not a picky eater either. Stay away...
They did not accept the yelp checkin coupon for a free wine with an entree. Food was really mediocre. Highly recommend Felix instead. Rude staff . Will never go again.

Dropped in to have my wedding ring checked, after getting a recommendation from my nail tech.  I was shown that one of the prongs on a small side diamond was missing.  It was repaired beautifully, with additional small caps on each mount, blending nicely with the original design and making the ring more secure. The estimate was reasonable and the work nicely done.  My only complaint was that I had asked that it be ready before we left on an extended vacation.  With two days to go, I called and was told someone would call back with a status update.  Next day, no call, I called again with the same promise and the same result.  The last possible day, the ring was ready and they did call me.  The ring looked great.  I will go back.

Got the crepes,  picked a few filling items,  and devoured the perfect yummy mildly sweet goodness! For dessert we had a chocolate pillow thing! Soooooooo amazing and divine! When I die,  I request to go to whatever heaven that dessert came from!

Hello ,we had a birthday celebration 1st time here the hostess were very rude ,we felt like we should not be there but our waitress was very nice n food was good but we wont go back there sorry, give the young ladies a training on how to treat your customers not make them feel unwelcome .ty

A hidden gem. You have to know where you are going to find it, but definitely worth the exploration. Omelettes and crepes made to order (delicious!)  and superb coffee. The one disappointment (oddly enough given that this is a pastry shop) is the pastry. Have tried the chocolate croissants twice and both times disappointed. Both times it tasted at least a day old and soggy - made worse by the server's  insistence that it "had" to be served warm - normally I would agree, but both times it was overheated which left the croissant flat and greasy.

Great service, comfortable beds, welcoming staff, tidy rooms and yummy breakfast. Chris and Joe were so kind and accommodating. Jacque cleaned our room perfectly. Major made an amazing breakfast. All around good experience.

I love Mexican- in Smyrna this is my go to place! Ask for Abelle or Ashton; they are the best! It's hard to make a bad decision here when it comes to the menu. Restaurant is clean, ticket times are speedy.

Much work needed.  A rowdy crowd (teenagers/early 20 something's dressed like it was prom - not football fans...that would have been much better) forced us to sleep with the TV on.  No toilet paper, 1/2 light bulbs missing, disassembled smoke detector, water damaged ceiling in the bathroom.  That rowdy crowd left the halls, lobby, and elevators littered and smelling funky the following morning.  Breakfast left much to be desired.

This place is called the gumbo pot so you'd think it'd be something worthwhile. Instead it was quite subpar. I ordered a bowl of seafood gumbo and crab cakes, both of which were not really that good. 

The service was good though.
Very pleased with tech and his results.  He listened to my problems and worked till he resolved the issue.  Would definitely call again and recommending to friends.

Had dinner there.  Nice atomphere.  our waitress was great, very friendly and helpful.   I had their special pineapple with voka drink there, was told is dangerous; didn't know what it mean because it tasted so light.  that's when they said its dangous because one can drink many and not feel it until later.

for appetizer, we had the flat bread pizza....very good.

For main course we had the bone on ribeye, and sirlon.  big portion, cooked just right.

Enjoyed the dinner, and will go back.

$1 macaroons on Wednesday! Brunch 10-3, it's fun with loud music! Their own Bellinis. The GM is amazing. There is a patio outside. You can come in and hang out, do your work here. I feel this will be my new office!  Ben, the GM gave us the history of the business and we watched the Chef create a delicious chocolate treat. The macaroons come in 6 flavors.

This particular experience came on a weekday lunch with my parents although I have been here on several other occasions for business lunches, drinks and brunch.

First I will say the best item on the menu is the Jumbo Buffalo Shrimp. I'm an avid foodie and a seafood and hot sauce connoisseur and have never had anything quite like these before.

However I would not recommend Redstone as a lunch destination unless you are prepared to spend at least $50. 

My Dad and I both ordered the Simple Grilled Fish (market price, I got the Halibut and he got the Seasonal Salmon). Our mistake not to ask what the "market price" of these fish were but it would have been helpful for the waitress to alert us too.

When our meals came to the table both seemed like a reasonable lunch portion (5 to 6 oz of fish plus rice and the vegetable of the day) and we both liked our meal very much.

However when the bill came the Halibut was $32 and Salmon was $28 which seemed ridiculously overpriced for the size and quality of the meal.

I'm sure I will be back at Redstone for drinks and appetizers but never again for a lunch where the price is the same as dinner with a portion half the size!

For those in the area PF Chang's and Brio (both right next door) offer significantly better value/quality for lunch.

I went for my first time last night to celebrate a friend's birthday.  It was fantastic!  They offer foods of any price range for you so it can be affordable for you. But, they also offer expensive plates that look amazing if you want it!!  There were 4 girls total, and we all got appetizers, an entree, and dessert. I cannot wait to go back, I was very pleased.
Great waitstaff. And great stuffed crap!  Awesome bread pudding with chocolate and whipped! Best part because it was free with a check in coupon from YELP!!!

Tonight my mom and I had requested to sit out on the patio. One of the hostesses told us we were first on the wait list and would be sat next. We noticed another party that came in after us sitting near us waiting for the patio as well. We overheard one of the other hostesses reassuring them that a patio table would be available shortly. A short while later, we saw them get seated outside and we were immediately then offered to sit inside if we "got tired of waiting". We asked the hostesses why they gave our table away as we had been waiting over an hour at this point and were "next up for the first patio table available", one of the hostesses lied directly to us stating the other party had been there first. We told them that couldn't have been true because we saw them walk in after us, and the one hostess tried blaming one of the other hostesses by saying they were on a different list on the computer which was different than the list we were on and she just had come in so she didn't know. It was just one excuse after another. They couldn't just be honest with us and admit they gave our table away right in front of us. After waiting well over an hour with not an apology or offering to have us speak with a manager, we left very upset and hungry so went somewhere else. We were just very disappointed how unprofessional the hostesses were and how they thought we wouldn't notice what they did and even lied about it.
Good food , can be expensive but nice atmosphere .extensive cocktails. Staff is friendly.

Server was GREAT! Gumbo was mediocre. Had brunch for 4 people and bloody Mary's. Ticket was 192.00 tip not included. Bloody Marys had to cost 12.50 each. Wayyyy overpriced. I had a 23$ shrimp and oyster platter. There were 6 small - medium shrimp and 6 small oysters and like a lb of fries. Won't go back.
Sitting at the bar realizing an ordinary glass of wine is $16!  Really?  Maybe in Manhattan!

Been here 3 or 4 times before, received good service. Tonight we show up 35 minutes before closing and they tell us we are closed. They seated their last table. WTF! Its 9:25. No apologies, no recommendations. This used to be a must when we came to New Orleans but not anymore.

I've finally built up the courage and came back.  Had their delicious wild mushroom soup cooked fresh that day.  Was in the mood for appetizers so had some great crispy calamari, crab cake full of crab meat, and seared ahi tuna.  For dessert we tried the warm chocolate chip cookie sundae with candied pecans, whipped cream and fudge sauce... rich but tasted like heaven!

Service is excellent here... even the manager, i believe, came over and asked if we wanted more sauce with our crab cake, noticing we ate it all up!

Everything was delicious again, but this time I didn't get sick!  Woohoo!
Try the Tamal and a side of Plantains with extra green sauce and you will cry tears of joy.

Not my favorite.  I'm a publix girl. However Winn Dixie has been adding more and more Buy one get one free deals each week. I find myself here every other week or so to purchase a few items. Then I head to Publix to get everything else I need.

Given the price, it is okay.  More effort resources could be put into the interactive stations upstairs.  They give equal attention to all sports as you would hope the NCAA would.  Do not expect to see too much on the history of the sports.  You do have to pay for parking, but this is still very fairly priced.  Be sure to wander around in the "park" outside.  The space is beautifully done.

This place was awesome!  Our service was excellent. I'm always so excited when I get great service because I'm very particular about customer service. The Bacon Bloody Mary was fantastic! The Mint Julep was devine!  We had Gumbo Ya Ya - its the best on town. I did not much like my crawfish etoufee and the happily exchanged it for red beans and rice. Wow, the red beans and rice was wonderful. I would highly recommend this place to anyone visiting like us. Kudos to the staff!!!

We really wanted this to be good. Nope. Came for dinner. We were told there would be a 20 min wait, we asked  if we could eat it the bar. The host seemed confused, and said "Yeah, but there is a 20 min wait". We saw coming around the restaurant that bar was empty. After walking all day I asked if we could just go sit in the bar. He said, "Oh yeah, that you can do." Ok? So we sit in the bar. As we come in we are yelled at by the bar tender, "Excuse me, can I help you?!?" Like we are not allowed in. Told him we were told we could sit at the bar. "Oh, ok." I counted two wait staff and two occupied tables. No problem, maybe there is a problem with the kitchen. He proceeds to yell at every party that comes in the exact same way. We ordered, food was mediocre. As I was about to ask for our bill, the bartender left to go outside for about 20 min. So we just sat and patiently watched a roach climb around the liquor bottles until he returned. I could tell this guy is having a bad night, but wow. This place clearly is struggling with some issues. If you're on vacation, don't waste a meal in NOLA here. Every other meal in this city has been incredible.

If your hours on your website are till 12am and you come in at 10:30pm you don't tell your guests you stop serving dinners. Just inform people on your website that after a certain hour you can only get appetizers and salads.
I've only been here twice and both experience were good! The prime rib is huge and really good! :) def worth ur $29!! :) and yeah, the warm chocolate chip cookie sundae was great!!

I was a bit skeptical based on some reviews but this place was great! The staff is super friendly!!! The shuttle service downtown saves on taxi/Uber use. The free breakfast is amazing!!!! I would definitely stay here again! Never paid more than $15 on an Uber anywhere so it's a great location.  Bartenders and front desk people were all great! Thanks for a great stay!
Love this place, always try to get here for a special .. Service is great and always get a booth when I book with opentable.
The desserts are beautiful and tasty and the drink specials are great on first Friday. Plus the staff is incredibly friendly.

Two of my friends and I came in on a Saturday night with a 9 pm Open Table reservation. The place was pretty busy and there were still plenty of people just sitting down for dinner even as we were leaving. 

I ordered the half rack of ribs, which was the perfect amount of food for me. It came with a side of fries (perfectly fried) and some cole slaw, which had this weird cumin (?) seasoning it it. The ribs itself were flavorful and tasted good, but was a tad on the dry side. 

For a chain restaurant, everything overall was actually better than I expected. 

Tip - if you need to use the restroom, avoid the "open kitchen" area. It looks like you can walk through it, but you will get yelled at for no reason.

Went for lunch and our party got a few flatbreads and various salads.  Everyone loved their food!  Service was fast and efficient.  They were very accommodating and we were seated even though we were missing one person.  We did have a switch in servers in the beginning but both were nice and professional.  We never felt rushed and enjoyed a great lunch!

The Gallery Pastry Shop sets up very high standards for any restaurant offering brunch in the SoBro area! Here are the many reasons that just made me fall in love with this place.

Menu
- Fresh & local ingredients 
- $5 Mimosa (with fresh orange or grapefruit juice)
- Authentic crepe!!! 
- The concept "make your own" crepes ($15 for 2) or omelette ($10) with fixed price
- Complementary pastry, when ordering brunch

Place & Service
- Little to no time wait (which is incredible considering the area and the quality of the place)
- Friendly and helpful staff
- Charming and well decorated place

I definitely recommend this little gem to anyone who appreciate fine and high quality food. It is the best for a friends brunch or just to treat yourself during the weekend!
Food is consistently good.  They have outdoor bar and seating which is lovely in nice weather, and heaters for colder weather.  Big bar crowd.  A little pricy.

Wait time to order was a little long, but it is Saturday night. We didn't have to wait for a table for 4. 
Halibut is AMAZING, Lobster bisque is delicious!

Very lovely pastries in a comfy retro environment. Can see the pastries (or brunch) being made right before your eyes. You can smell the food right as you come in. A very great foundation from which to build a solid network of businesses in the SoBro area
This is not a quite place, but food  and service is good as well.  Deserts are good, but the place is expensive.  If you are a few vegetarian entrees and not many if any vegan ones I noticed.

Gallery Pastry Shop is a city favorite. Their desserts are amazing and well priced - the shop itself has beer and wine and even offers a boozy brunch on the weekends. The decor and vibe is to die for - mix matched furniture with a jaw dropping chandelier. There is limited outdoor seating as well. Gallery Pastry Shop is tucked away so its easy to miss if you're driving for the first time!

I stumbled by this place because it has a nice open seating area and I was with my pooch.  The service was very good and after sitting down I decided to see what folks had to say/what to order.  Needless to say the reviews didn't have me excited but frankly I thought they missed.  Everything was very good.  Especially enjoyed the grits.  And overall a good open spot for breakfast.

great service, excellent food.  Yes I was in New Orleans and ordered a salad,but oh what a salad!  Wanted gumbo, but it had okra so i had to pass.  Salad jayne sounded good and it was worth it.  big salad with shredded crab and  about 10-12 HUGE  shrimp.  I loved it.  Will order it again next time i'm there.

Good food, Good service to your face.  I went there today to have a dinner with my family.  What I noticed was the staff making faces and rolling their eyes after talking to customers.  It must be a regular thing with their staff, because I saw 3 different staffers do it - all hostesses.  I saw it once at the front desk when I was waiting to be seated, once while being seated as people held up the hostess while walking out, and once while seated watching another table stop a hostess to ask a quick question.  They were doing it out of view of the people they were interacting with, but that doesn't stop others from see it.  This is typical behavior by workers that don't appreciate their jobs, and if it happens as often as I saw it today, it's an unfortuanant culture at this restaraunt.

We went here on a Saturday morning after a long night on on Bourbon street. Needless to say we needed some good stick to your ribs breakfast, a beignet just wasn't going to do it.  My husband and I both got the eggs, bacon, and grits breakfast.  We both agreed that the grits were the absolute best grits ever.  The bacon was excellent as well. I had never had deep fried bacon, I am a fan.  Overall, this was a good stop. We will definitely go back, they were starting their gumbo as we were leaving, my husband wants to go back for that. The smell of it throughout the restaurant was delicious.

The decor is also a great treat.

I booked this hotel with Priceline.com.  Initially, based on reviews I saw, I thought it might be a pretty good place to stay.  I was initially pretty impressed by how close to the interstate this property was, but the surrounding area seems very old and ghettoish.  Clearly, this is an older building with come Choice Hotel "charm" slapped on it.  The exterior is in need of sprucing up and a generally appearance upgrade.  I did not take advantage of the shuttle to downtown that is offered.  There are plenty of Uber options available that worked great and were probably a lot cheaper.  The lobby was clean and actually somewhat inviting.  The bar area was ok, and the breakfast area was basic.  The elevator bay was in pretty dire need of some touching up as far as appearance goes.  The corridor area on my floor was ok, but again, need some appearance upgrades and general sprucing up.  The cardboard recycling bin and trashbag near the elevator was an extremely cheap touch.  The housekeeping ladies that were taking care of the rooms when I arrived were pretty nice, however, the conversations that they were very clearly having on their cell phones didn't sound very professional.  The room was, again, OK, even marginal at best.  Now, this isn't necessarily a fault of Choice Hotels, but I didn't particularly care for the two queen beds.  I called a couple days ahead to see if I could potentially be guaranteed a king bed, but was told they were already sold out.  Again, appearance issues.  Tattered and worn wallpaper and paint, and carpet that was torn.  Dust and dirt on the AC vent in both the main area and bathroom.  Also, what appeared to be an electrical wire hanging out from the side of the bathroom vent.  The room was clean, yes, but appeared very dated and worn.  The bed was fairly comfortable and clean so that helped.  AC worked fine and was comfortable.  The shower was nice and worked well.  TV was adequate.  Wifi was free, but slow, however it wasn't a huge problem for me.  Probably could use more than one bar of soap to start with, but it was quickly gotten at the front desk with no issue.  

Honestly, for the price I ended up paying via Priceline, I could have had a much better room paying directly with another company and for slightly more.  I hate to say it, but I'm not impressed with this property.  This was my second time using a Choice Hotel property in Nashville.  Unless there are significant changes, I think I'll stick with a different brand.

Typical hotel. Was probably beautiful when built. But, has had little to no maintenance since. 
Our room has a window that leaks rain. Now, around the HVAC, the wall needs some major work. 
Pool area needs lots of work. Lights out or blinking. Water so cold it's unbelievable. And cloudy. Makes one wonder if there's any chlorine in it.
Way too overpriced for my tastes. Foods and drinks are not that spectacular for the price.  But because it's in the Sagemore plaza and attracts a higher end crowd they get away with it.
Food is good, not great but good.  Clean relax environment.  If you cant find some ranked higher or they are full, this place will do.

This place exceeded my expectations by far.  I searched YELP for several hours looking for a good location for a date and I settled on Red Stone.  The ambience is a unique mix of casual but intimate, which made it ideal for the situation. As you walk into the center area it instantly reminded me of the inside of an old ship.  

The menu was just the right size, enough items to give you a choice but not too many that you end up just staring at the menu for a long period of time and ending up choosing something safe. 

I got the blackened mahi mahi. It was actually blackened, which is quite a compliment because most places think blackened means burnt. It came with a chilled mixture of orzo type rice with sliced grape tomatoes and black beans and guacamole (can't remember if it was homemade or not). The blackened spice and chilled sides was a little strange but very nice (in fact the waitress warned me of this when I ordered it).  Also got the peanut butter desert. It was good, strange, but good. It also came with a gravy boat full of amazing chocolate sauce. 

The only complaint I could say about this place was that the kitchen initially mixed up my sides. However the waitress was so on point that she grabbed the plate and took it back before I could even say something to her. The manager came over immediately, apologized, and offered to treat us to appetizers or desert. The manager made sure to touch(come over) the table several times after personally bringing  my food back over to me. As such, even my only complaint the restaurant was able to turn into a bonus. I would highly highly recommend this place, but probably should make a reservation if planning on going at a peak time.

After tearing up a 5k race, 3 of us racers went over for the Sunday brunch.  During this brunch, with each meal you get a free mimosa.  Not too bad.  While pricey, the food is really good and the service is excellent.   The highlight of the meal; however, was the giant sticky bun they gave us at the conclusion.  Incredible!  I could actually feel body fat increasing with every bite.

My man and I stopped in here spontaneously one day because we were hungry and it was the first thing I seen. I honestly didn't think any place was bad in the quarter. However, I was wrong! We ordered a simple catfish dinner and shrimp dinner and it was alll so bland. I didn't think it was something you could mess up on.. the place was empty when we arrived which should've been a sign..
Best Jerk Chicken and soups. Great ambiance. Nice sit out and bar. Love to go there in late Spring, summer and early fall.

If there was an option for zero stars, I would have rated it zero. This restaurant was a horrible experience. In fact I have never completed a rating on yelp before but I felt that I should warn others to stay away. Our ticket was over $40 for lunch and the only part I could eat was the frozen french fries. The only thing this place had going for it was the hardest working bus boy I've ever seen.
Some of the slowest service I have ever received. Waitress was inattentive and mia majority of the time. Food order was wrong on multiple dishes.

Six of us arrived on an early Sunday evening. First thing we noticed is how damn dark it was where our table was. Most of my party absolutely could not read their menu without a flashlight or cell. Second, they have an open kitchen arrangement which unnecessarily adds to the din with pots and pans and other noises throughout dinner. What were the designers thinking! Wall it off with glass. Dont get stuck in that left side corridor. The bar area looks very nice and is quieter. 
They actually have a selection of draft beers, including one IPA. Our server was very good in taking care of us. I started with an awful pear martini special which was sickeningly sweet and contained little alcohol for $12, so I switched to a beer. The calamari contained many fried slices of lemon, otherwise it was very good. They mentioned that their specialty was rotisserie "chicken" with mashed garlic potatoes and a veggie. It was misleading as it was more like pieces of a cornish game hen for $18. I mentioned this and she quickly brought out another piece. You envision, but don't get, a whole "chicken." It was good nonetheless. For the high price we paid, we won't be back.
The worst dinning experience here. The food was under  season and a very pricey menu. I would stay Away. There are better choices at the same prices

We've only eaten in the patio area, which is one of the best as far as the ambience goes.  The food is just ok, with some standouts such as the salads, the flatbreads and the corn bread.  A little pricey for what it is.  The bar area is usually crowded, which brings me to my big complaint.  Evidently, cigar smoking is permitted on the patio.  This presents a problem when people are eating, not just drinking.  When seated next to someone with a cigar, and the available seating is limited or nonexistent, what do you do?  Ask the person to put out their cigar?  Or just leave?  It would be greatly appreciated if cigars were not permitted.  Cigarettes are difficult enough to deal with but cigars are awful when eating.  I understand the restaurant is trying to accommodate their smoking clientele but those of us who don't smoke would like to enjoy being outside also!

This place is great for lunch and dinner.
service is always excellent and the food is consistently great
Not good, but not horrible. The food was mediocre at best, but the worst part was, a few of the waiters were bickering over tables in front of the customers.

I love everything about the Gallery Pastry Shop. I've never had a bad meal whether it's been for an extended weekend brunch or a quick lunch meeting. Their food and desserts always impress me. The lunch menu during the week is limited, but even if limited the food is great - fantastic quiches or meat/cheese sandwiches. The weekend brunches are always packed, so get there early as you won't want to leave. I do not go nearly enough!

I've been to Redstone before and it was OK in the past, but this last time there I felt the hostess was quite snooty and very rude.  I was meeting a friend there and I arrived earlier than she did-I asked to be seated so I could order something as I had not eaten anything all day, and they told me I couldn't be seated till all of the party was there.   I explained to her that I wanted to order something to eat and she rolled her eyes and slammed down the menus on the podium.   I dine out for work multiple times a week, and this was the first time I have experienced the attitude-I expect better.  Once seated, our server was quite nice but food was just "meh".

Meh!  Should have read the reviews first.  Service was so so.   We ordered the po boy burger and a cup of gumbo ya ya.   The burger was huge and luke warm just like the gumbo.  The shrimp sat on top of the gumbo so i do think it was cooked with the roux.  Probably so it can be made to order.  My bf needed mustard for his burger.  I waved at a waitress who I know saw me.  She ignored me.  A busboy asked if she saw me.  I told him I'm pretty sure she did.  He went to tell her again, and she ignored him.  She never came to see what I wanted.  She was an Older lady with glasses.  Wish I had gotten her name.   Just straight ignored me.   Anyways,  i'll never be back.   Once again, the yelpers got it right.   

Ps.... The hurricane was on point.   Thats the only reason they got a 2 star review.   What a waste.

Went to Redstone American Grill for brunch on a Sunday morning. They are one of the best when it comes to crab cake Eggs Benedict. Good sized, lump crab meat crab cakes, perfectly cooked eggs, a great Hollandaise sauce, and perfect English muffins. Service here was good and there was a nice atmosphere. Also, their breakfast bread is really good. What's nice is all the brunches include a mimosa, too.

Literally the best thing about this hotel isn't the room or the location, it's Jordan, one of the bartenders. On a Monday night, his bar is wrapped, and he's KILLING it. He's full of info on the city, super courteous, full of info for people who have never visited Nashville, and awesome and keeping drinks coming when the time is right! 10/10 recommend Jordan! He's AWESOME!

There is no reason to shop here. The store is dingy and set up as a cross between a grocery store and dollar store but there are no real deals that I can see. Across the street is a cLean and well-stocked sweet bays

Absolutely one of the best spots in Indianapolis. I've been coming here somewhat regularly since they've opened and only now getting around to leaving a review.

Fabulous breakfast items and some of the best croissants I've ever had (including France ). Staff is super friendly and accommodating to everyone. Lots of fun sitting at the counter and watching the kitchen do its thing as well.

Behind breakfast the 2nd best thing they do is holiday desert orders, the bread pudding and gallery pies are holiday traditions in our house now.

If you're not interested in dealing with a crowd (it can get pretty busy by noonish) be there right at 10 and you can get right in.

By far the best pastries I've had in the Indy area, and I've sampled a lot! The pastries are meticulously prepared by an award winning pastry chef and his staff. The kitchen is open to the restaurant, which I love and the interior of the restaurant is adorable. The staff was very attentive, friendly and passionate about the restaurant. The location itself is hard to find, it tucked a ways off of 54th Street.
 
We tried to the almond pear tart and the chocolate pillow. They were as much a work of art, as they were flavorful. However, at $8 a pastry they are a bit pricey, but worth it for a special treat. 

I can't wait to go back on Sunday mornings for their breakfast and $5 mimosas.

A+ + service from Stephen
A+ food taste and quality 
A+ waiting time for food
A+ waiting time for seat

Great place to have lunch

We hosted a reception here and the service was exceptional. They are willing to work with you and help you out in any way. There are many interactive exhibits, tennis ball speed, football throwing speed, hoe high you can jump, downhill skiing, basketball court, and many, many other things. The best was probably the basketball court, where we held a three point shooting contest. For anyone that is into college sports, it is a great place.  For the average person, it could be a little boring.

First, let me say the food here is not good.  I ordered the chicken and andouille sausage gumbo.  There was one slither of chicken and zero sausage.  When I asked the waitress if what I had was the correct gumbo she said yes but would take it back to get sausage in it.  She brought my original gumbo back with 4 circles of sausage on top of it.  So I had bland roux, slither of chicken, and 4 sausage circles.  No flavor to it whatsoever either.  I also ordered the jambalaya.  Rice wasn't cooked thoroughly, lacked flavor or anything resembling creole/Cajun food.  My daughter ordered the crawfish étouffée.  Same story on the rice, crawfish was definitely frozen, étouffée was very watered down.  It also was very bland.  Now, if that wasn't enough, our waitress attempted to scam me!  I was in such a hurry to leave due to my extreme disappointment of the food that I gave her my card before she brought the check...something I've done many times before at other places.  I knew my total should be around $50.  She came back and said the machine was down and she couldn't run my card.  She then asked me to go to the ATM machine outside and get cash to which I refused because of the fees I'd be charged to use it.  I asked her the total and she said $62.60.  I asked her if she said $62.69 and she said yes.  She immediately said let me talk to my manager.  She comes back and asks me if I'm ok without a receipt because it won't print one.  I said absolutely not.  She comes back in a couple of minutes with my receipt and the printed itemized copy of my bill.  I said how nice it started working and she didn't seem happy.  They weren't alerting other customers paying with cards of this issue either so I know she was doing this to me.  Btw, my bill was $52.50.  I will NEVER go back there nor do I recommend this place to anyone.  There are far better places to eat in NOLA than this and I'm confident they won't try to scam you.

We stopped by after my friend sent me a picture she found. I tried the Provence and she ordered macarons. The location is nestled back off the street but is a cute little shop.  Well worth our efforts to find. The lavender sweeteness of the Provence was a light yet filling dessert. I can't wait to try the creoes; which I'm told right now are only available on Sunday but they hope to expand to other days soon. We will definitely return to check out the expanded menu.
Not sure where the good reviews are coming from. Our food was awful and our server basically ignored us. It wasn't crazy busy or anything.

Terrible shrimp and grits and service was poor. We were unhappy with a salad and sent the salad back, but were still charged. Overpriced and terrible seafood. I do not recommend coming here. Overrated.

Taormina's is a nicer pizzeria which also offers a wider menu of Italian food.

The restaurant itself is an upscale pizza place: Cozy, but nothing fancy (4.5 stars).

We tried the pizza, calzone, a cheesesteak, a chicken/pasta dish and a few sides and very much enjoyed them all (5 stars).

During our visit, we found the service mixed: Servers were friendly, but they could have been more attentive and time from seating to ordering was a bit long, and the time from ordering to the arrival of our food was far too long (3 stars).

Prices were reasonable, and I'm willing to give Taormina's the benefit of the doubt that the long delays during our one experience here were an unfortunate fluke, hence the 4 stars overall.

Ohhhh my, the gumbo ya ya was fantastic. After spending a week in New Orleans, this was the best gumbo I had all week, and I had a lot of gumbo. My wife really liked her shrimp po boy, and the service was good, although it was not very crowded. 

At first, we thought the place looked like a chain, but it has a personal touch, and the prices are fine, my bowl of gumbo was under $10.
Decent service and drinks...but could have made better Mexican at home. Burrito came out in what seemed like marinara sauce and covered in mozzarella....Mexican?

I have been here for breakfast which was OK Id say a 6.5. 
Dinner was about a 8. 
What made me fall in love with this bar is the Strawberry Balsalmic Martini. 
Please please please Redstone bring it back!!

Have been here a few times and my favorite day is macaroon Wednesday. 

Didn't have too many issues until the last time I visited. One of the dishes was missing meat but it was addressed and taken care of which I appreciated. 

The food and dessert here are worth some of the parking issues you may have on a busy day. It's a great spot for groups and $5 mimosas make it pretty affordable for anyone. 

It's also in an area (on the Monon) where you can walk and visit other businesses.

Walter had the best customer service!  We loved the Creole Combo, ya ya gumbo and catfish and oyster platter between our party. Sharing was easy too. Everyone loved it all!  Oysters were my favorite!!!!

So I was called a "cheap ass weirdo"...and  furthermore telling me to ask wait person for seperate checks...okay...lol

We did ask for seperate checks.  She was sheisty end of story.   The table behind us was also carefully scanning their bill as well as it was obviously  inflated as well. 

You weren't there, you don't know.

None of us is, was,  or has ever been "cheap"

My review was honest.

I stand by my statement. 

Decent food,  sheisty service.

So go look for some more scathing responses under your bridge troll. 

"Cheap ass"...lol

Get a life

Merry Christmas.
Great customer service, knowledgable sales and in gold and diamonds. Carry many designer brands owner manager

This is a restaurant that goes strictly on their formula of how they prepare their food and their process to deliver it.  Don't expect them to deviate!
The food is okay.  They bank on tourists and having a very convenient location.  They would not accommodate a request for a combo shrimp and oyster po boy because " they never deviate from the menu" and the menu only has a one seafood po boy!
Service was slow but the waitress was nice.  The seafood gumbo was just okay- I've had much better.  The bread pudding was sub par!
The manager would not make any accommodations when we spoke with him- he just claimed that " that is how it's been" since he joined the company- no special orders.

I had the bacon Bloody Mary. It was AWESOME. Ordered the seafood gumbo. It was really good. They would have gotten more stars but charges $2 for bread to dunk into the gumbo. REALLY????  I have never been charged for bread before. The hostess was not friendly and welcoming. Felt like we were bothering her. Our server was nice I think his name is Jamel. Bartender was very friendly and helpful. Over all would have liked a better experience for our first place we visited on our vacation.

I was going to bring my dog here but I realized the night before that I misplaced his shot records so assumed I wouldn't be able to bring him in (understandable). I left a message just in case as he is registered so he obviously has his rabies shots. They called me back in the morning and said that I wouldn't be able to bring him in (which I completely understand) not only due to their policy BUT because of the "nature of his breed". First off, he's a mixed breed but looks like he is part chow which is what they were referring to. Second, my Yorkie is more aggressive than him so I'm not sure why any "dog lover" would have the nerve to say that/judge any breed of dog. I now have his records but am not going to make another appointment due to that comment.
This taco bell is fast and never has messed up my order. The drive thru line moves quickly. So don't be too overwhelmed if you arrive and see it super long. They are super fast.

This place is world famous from how horrible it is. I've worked in restaurants for years and you just don't treat other human beings the way we were treated. Kitchen was solid for being a tourist trap but the "world famous" hurricane was post hurricane bad, we told the hostess to move us because of bad weather (told her twice to sit us inside).  After sitting for an hour, watching tables larger than us get food, and a server chase down a couple for a lack of tip we were moved indoors. Food ended up getting in at the 1:30 minute mark.  Like I said it was decent for a tourist trap. If you're desperate IHOP serves all day. Do not eat here until management changes!!!

I have never had anything but an outstanding experience at Sheffield's Diamonds.  The staff are very friendly and knowledgeable.  I bought a watch from them and have had rings resized and appraised.  Everything was done professionally and at a good price.  I highly recommend them.

By far the worst place I hav been...service sucked. I tried to return a dish that I took 2 bites ( the jambalaya )I told the manager that the taste of bay leaves was over whelming. She replied "I'm sorry u ate more than half".. I replied ma'am I didn't even eat the shrimp. ..thas where ya money at not the rice".. she walked off said sorry but if u didn't like it u should not have played with it and walked off...so yes this place gets a big fat 0
Descent hotel. Friendly staff, clean rooms, and convenient parking. Hotel was a tad bit run down, bad grout work in bathroom, paint and wallpaper was peeling.

I brought my truck in fully working with no smoke, noise, or running issues for a recall. After spending over $1000.00 in repairs, my truck is now sitting in my driveway with yet another issue that will now cost over $800 to repair. Your service department is fully aware of the issues that have happened.
I would never recommend your service department to anyone! I would never consider making a purchase at your dealership.
This was the worst and most expensive  customer service I've ever received! I am beside myself that anyone could be treated like this!
Delicious as always and the service top notch. Go with the buffalo shrimp appetizer and cookie dessert you will be in heaven.

Went to dinner last Tuesday night to celebrate my anniversary. My fiance and I have been to this restaurant many times. We have not had a bad meal yet. The food is delicious, the drinks are great, the ambience is cozy. The only negative is that they don't have one in Ocean or Monmouth counties. I love this place!!

Never EVER!!!! EVER AGAIN! DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY OR YOUR TIME! I show more hospitality in my own home... And the manager is black with almost all black waiters. Unless you are white and/or older white person don't you dare!!! sooo upset

I have to tell you about Lynette. We were walking to our car from the french quarter and my mother started to over heat. Lynette let us sit down and served us some water even though she knew we had no intention of eating. She also chatted with us for a minute. Very sweet lady. I will be eating here next time I'm in the quarter.
One of my favs again. The shrimp, the jerk chicken fondue, the flat bread Pizza with figs. Everything is delicious on the menu, the corn bread is outstanding,  and the signature drinks are a must.
Stopped in for lunch with coworkers and service was soooooo slooooow. Food was great once we got it. I'd go back when I had more time to linger.

Stayed at The Clarion Hotel Downtown Nashville Stadium for 4 nights with a group of 124 Miami Dolphins Fans. We all had a GREAT time. Everyone in the city was great and the crew at The Clarion were amazing. The Bar crew were friendly and Justin was a comedian that kept us laughing and drinks flowing. His family had a reunion that weekend so he only worked our first night but fear not Toni, Kelly and Lindsey were just as great the following nights. We closed the bar down each night and we all had a great time. The front desk was helpful and polite. Albert, De Andre and Jessica greeted us every time we came in and were helpful when our group had questions about the area. The shuttle busses to downtown made it easy to get around without renting a car and the drivers were great. I would recommend my friends and family staying here if they visit Nashville for any reason. THANK YOU!!!! 
Marc Angelo

Loud 80s pop, extremely eclectic furnishings from mid century to 70s, 8o. Mixed with traditional, to industrial to log cabin chique. The explosion of items on the walls and ceilings bring to mind estate sale, especially with the garage door open. None of this does a thing to elevate very pretty dainty pastries that actually are very good. The Opera Cake reminded me of a Tiramisu. The Chocolate Pillow was very soft and creamy. I think for dining-in they should remove the item from the little gold cake boards and add a drizzle, flower or piece of fruit. I don't like clutter and the open kitchen coupled with the garage sale dining area really is not very comfortable for an anti hoarder personality. Maybe next time items to go instead of dining in.

Very delicious food and friendly customer service. Jasmine was the best and made sure we were happy with our meal! The gumbo was a little cold and we asked her to microwave it and she offered to give us a brand new dish. Very happy with my experience here!

If I could give Sheffield's 6 stars I would.
First of all, if you're looking for quality diamonds, jewelry, watches, etc. this is THE (only) place to go in Tucson. They carry Tacori, Hearts in Fire, Tag and many other high end brands. Christine is great to work with and the owner Eric is very friendly and helpful. We got both our wedding bands here, both Tacori, both ah-mazing. Love these guys, we will be back!

I'm giving it 4 stars because its somewhere in between 3 and 4 from my experience.  Great menu, but I felt a bit underwhelmed.  Could have been very impressed by my crab & corn salad, but instead it was just decent.  

Service was good.  People seemed friendly enough.  Food seems of good quality.  Overall nothing that wows me and I don't have enough disposable income to make this a place I would go back to without a weird reason.
Best macarons in the city. The croissant are worth cheating on your diet plan, and the pastry case is truly edible art.

dined here this evening (monday night)

homemade soup special every monday is french onion = a great reason to make the reservations!

redstone's salads with the rotisserie chicken can't be beat.  two in our party had the spinach salad and thoroughly enjoyed it.  from the sliced apple, to the grapes, eggs, walnuts, mixed with bacon and manchego cheese slices along with a fair amount (but not drenching it) walnut-bacon dressing.

seating tonight was a breeze especially when making a reservation (which i highly recommend).

our server (RON G.) was by far a real professional.  from the way he took our order to the way our "special needs" were met.  (one of our diners liked her bacon cooked a certain way.)  he was pleasant, courteous and very attentive.  we can't say how lucky we were to have him as a server at this establishment.

tonight was a "winner" across the board.

I was so surprised to find such a great place tucked away off of 54th street. The menu isn't extensive, but the desserts that they do offer are excellent. The back patio is amazing for enjoying Sunday brunch or a glass of wine on a nice day. I would highly recommend checking this place out.

The NCAA Hall of Champions is such a cool place to visit. I absolutely love sports, and college sports are an amazing thing as it is, with many different sports available across the nation. It was cool to read up on all the different sports offered all around the country and personal accounts of student-athlete's experience in playing in those sports. I thought that was so cool as it was, but I thought it was even cooler when I went upstairs and saw all the interactive things that could be done. I went during a really good time when nobody was there, so I had the entire upstairs to myself. I was able to shoot hoops around by myself in their little makeshift gym, I was able to play on the interactive video games uninterrupted, and I was also able to walk around and see the last part of museum. Hands down, the funnest part was being able to shoot hoops and playing the video games of the different sports. I could only imagine what it is like during the busy season, and I'm glad I didn't come during that time. I had a blast and appreciated everything for what it was. I'm glad a place like this exists for everyone to experience.

This is one of my favorite places! The brunch is phenomenal. It comes with mimosa and caramel roll. The only thing I haven't liked from the brunch menu is their take on eggs Benedict. You must have their hash brown dish. For dinner, the buffalo shrimp are an excellent appetizer. You have to try the banana custard dessert - it's amazing! Also try the stoli doli with strawberry puree. It's a pineapple infused vodka drink and it's excellent. It can get pretty packed but it's worth the wait!

I'll try to keep it short on this one. 

When I was in NOLA back in April I visited that restaurant. I love it-from the atmosphere-the food to the people. 
Now the food Omg was so good. I ordered the shrimp PO' Boy and the gumbo. 
(if you don't know what a Po' Boy/gumbo is then I suggest you google it-sorry)

The people were very friendly (of course I was in the south)-the ambiance was nice and welcoming. 
The price for the foods was very reasonable. 
The only regret I had was the fact that I didn't go there my first day when I first got there. 

I will definitely go back again.

I was so disappointed with the food. I'm from Louisiana, so I know how crawfish etoufee and boudin balls are supposed to taste. The crawfish were small and tasteless and looked like they had come from a frozen package. The sauce was a dark roux which tasted like a thick flour paste. The boudin balls tasted like they were made with minced meat. The bread pudding was dense and dry. Way too high of a price. Quality really bad. Probably the worst I have had in New Orleans in years.

Not a Taco Bell fan, haven't been for years, but I was curious about the fries! After waiting in line for almost 20 minutes I finally got my food: a Baja blast and fries. Almost 6 hours later and I'm throwing up, having the worst stomach pains I've ever had. Pretty positive their food got me sick, so be careful.

Some people would rate this hotel low because of silly things like the rough edges. Well the beds are good service is there when you need them and the price is right. Why pay twice as much to be on 2nd Ave downtown Nashville when you can stay in a nice hotel across the river that has a courtesy shuttle that runs till 9:00 every night. And the breakfast. Well let's just say it's a full spread. Anything you want. They prob have it for breakfast.

Had dinner there last night and will never go back. Meat was tough. One of our friends got the wrong meal and the server was snotty. It took forever to get our food. I won't recommend this place to anyone.

i was quite disappointed with brunch here... 

the start was good! the blueberry muffin/bread thingie was super delicious and appetizing!  it had the nicest aroma and really puts you in the sunday-brunch-lazy-day feel.

i had slightly higher expectations for this place especially after i tasted the morning bread.  also, b/c this isn't a cheap breakfast/lunch place either... but then the entree completely dropped the ball with the underwhelming quality.   i ordered steak and eggs.. and the first thing i noticed was that my food was kind of dry and it looked like it was under the heating lamps a little too long... the steak was close to unbearable! i ordered medium rare and it came out well done... you think since it's a steakhouse, they would do a better job on "steak and eggs"... boy was i wrong.
