I had the house drink, the Redstone Doli ($10) - which is made with aged pineapples and New Amsterdam Vodka. It's a simple tasty cocktail with a lot of kick. The aged pineapples are visible in big jars right on the bar top. 

The Mrs. enjoyed a Bellini ($10) - which is made with champagne, white peach, and Peach Schnapps. It was very nice, with just the right bit of sweetness. 

For a starter we elected to have the Jerk Chicken Fondue ($15) - which is made with spicy grilled jerk marinated chicken, sourdough croutons, apples, red grapes and of course smoked gouda fondue. This was absolutely delicious and I kept the fondue for my main course to dip with, because it was absolutely delicious. The chicken was made with a caring hand and burst with flavor. The croutons were the perfect texture. Not too hard and crunchy, not too soft. A very nice consistency. 

As an entree I went with the Pan Seared Swordfish ($33) - which is made with a brandy-garlic crust, stir fried vegetables,  with Asian sesame vinaigrette and ginger cashew couscous. The swordfish was absolutely divine, thick and juicy and nearly made me divorce salmon as my favorite fish. I had a side of Garlic Mashed Potatoes ($6) which fit nicely with my meal. The veggies were nice and the couscous was nearly addicting. 

The lady in my life went for the Signature Fillet Mignon ($42) - which was served with garlic mashed potatoes and vegetables. You couldn't ask for a better 10oz cut of meat. It was juicy and tender, cooked to a perfect medium rare with no blood trail whatsoever. Just an amazing piece of meat that I was nearly jealous that I didn't order. 

We paired our meal with a bottle of Benvolio Pinot Grigio ($35), which worked nicely with our meal, though a red would have really brought out the flavor of that fillet and is even said to pair quite nicely with swordfish since it is such a meaty kind of fish. 

With all said and done, my belly was happy and carefree about the final tabulation and we left a nice 18% tip for our excellent server Moira who was absolutely attentive, knowledgeable and pleasant. She gave us just the right amount of attention and made us feel at home without smothering us. I gander that we'll be back at Redstone.

Our dinner was amazing! We had a party of 5 and no reservation... They got us in within 10 minutes. We ordered the corn bread for appetizer and OMG SO GOOD. Service was fantastic. I had the meatloaf for my entree and took left overs for lunch next day! Will definitely be back!!!

Worst customer service and management ever! I have a medical condition OCD and I have to have my food a certain way. I order my food Togo 2-4 times a week here and never had a problem before last week I called and places a Togo order like I always do and the person I placed it with didn't speak good English or couldn't understand me. Either way I specified that I wanted no cheese on it all on the side (4 small 2oz containers is what they always do) I called back up there and the man who took my order argued with me about how I get my food all the time I explained my condition to him and he stated next time I ordered that it would be taken care of because it was their mistake. So I called yesterday to order my meal and they couldn't do it because the manager wasn't there. So I called back again today and he still wasn't there I asked if there was any supervisor or acting manager that I could speak with and the lady who answered the phone was extremely rude and kept insisting that no one could speak to me. She placed me on hold and came back to the phone stating that I could get the vegetables that Coke with the 10.00 meal I order and that was it. No chicken no rice JUST VEGETABLES! So I ask for the lady who approved that to come on the phone and the lady whom answered the phone yet again argued with me that I couldn't speak to her. Finally she came on the phone and stated that there would be no manager at the establishment for over a week because he was going out of town. Needless to say I'm very disappointed that someone whom eats there so often gets treated like dirt! I will not be going back and I will be contacting the owner of the establishment.
Great open kitchen serving up pasteurized, breakfast , and every other goodies your heard and tummy desire

The food was terribly OVERPRICED! You will pay $20+ for a mediocre bowl of gumbo. You're pretty much paying money just to be near the French quarter. The waiter was okay, the service we received was up to par and the food came quick. The food was good but not worth the price.

The restrooms were DISGUSTING!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! The staff doesn't keep up with cleaning at all. 

Will not return.

Food was just okay they are way over priced and to top it all off they overcharged us I would not go back there again watch out because they want to overcharge their customers. We went there today for lunch

Don't let first impressions fool you, Taormina's is a lot better than you would expect.  Sure, it's in a dated looking strip mall and the inside could stand for a total makeover by Chef Robert, but the food is surprisingly good.  

My go-to are the paninis.  They are excellent.  Great bread.  Good size.  Lots of filling.  Surprisingly decent fries.   I haven't tried the pizza in a long time, but I remember it being pretty decent as well.

Price wise it's also pretty reasonable for the panini and fries.  About $9 depending on the type you get.

THIS PLACE IS AWFUL! I came to Nashville with my family and we stayed there, it was very nice inside. We went out and came back to the hotel and our whole bathroom was flooded!!! The dry wall had came down and leaked water everywhere! We had a suitcase in the bathroom that got completely soaked and ruined with drywall all over it! My brother went and told them and they didn't care at all. The police that was working there even agreed with us and he came and looked at it. He was on our side! We didn't get a new room...we stayed in the hotel with a flooded bathroom all night! We didn't get the room paid for or even any discount! They were extremely rude and obviously didn't care! Not one of the clarion staff members even came and looked at the room!  One of the staff members even suggested that we were all lying when we had pictures and a police offer for proof!! HORRIBLE customer service!!! When we were even letting the manger know, all the staff was so nosey they just stood there and listened but did nothing about the matter! They clearly don't care about their customers. It's nice inside but just remember it may fall apart on you and ruin your things..but don't expect them to care or even do anything to accommodate the situation! My family and I will never be back!
Wow, everything we tried was amazing! It was easily the best brunchy food I can remember.

Glad we didn't read the views first!

Shrimp poboy - GOOD! lots of shrimp! And the shrimp seasoning is divine!

Red beans and rice - good! Flavorful but I won't say they are the best because I don't have anything to compare them too!

Seafood gumbo - NICE SPICY KICK! not too hot at all but just surprised me! I would say it's pretty damn good!

A great stop for any sports fans, especially those with kids.  The museum is a great testament to achievement and the importance of collegiate sports to the development of hundreds of thousands of students across the country.  The interactive stuff on the second floor is fun, (though it could really use an ice hockey stop hint hint).
Expensive but ok when you have a broken iPad screen that needs to be fixed quickly.

My friend told me about $1 macaroon Wednesday's and after reading everyone's reviews I had to check this place out immediately. What an adorable set up! The display counter for the desserts is stunning. Unfortunately there was a private event taking place so we didn't have access to sit out on the patio. However, the staff was happy to get our macaroons and they were exceptionally friendly. My friend and I were able to sit at a picnic table at the store next to the pastry shop. 

I got white chocolate, salted caramel, mixed berry, and chocolate ganache macaroons. I've had the mixed berry and white chocolate so far. Both delicious. I'll definitely be back to try their brunch and check the place out more. 

Everyone's reviews lived up to the hype. A hidden gem in SoBro.

I was so impressed with The Gallery. The French press coffee, croissant, omelette and sides were all winners. I love the shared sides concept for brunch. The portions are decent-sized but not too much.

The atmosphere is also fantastic and the staff was super helpful and friendly. I loved the open air feel, beautiful wood tables, integrated kitchen, and lovely outdoor dining area. I definitely want to go back and try more of the menu. 

Big thumbs up!

I have been to the Redstone a few times now and my initial complaint was that it was overpriced. I do believe it is on the high side but I think that you get good quality for your money. Order the cornbread as an appetizer, it is absolutely delicious. While the menu is not extensive, there is an adequate choice from seafood, meat and even some pasta dishes. My son had the meatloaf which was excellent and I had the Parmesan encrusted codfish which was very good. My wife believes that the ribs were some of the best that she ever has had.
Can I give Redstone more than 5 stars? Great restaurant! I had the Kids Chicken and Fries and it was marvelous. Our server Daryle was a super server.

omg....the service and the food are amazing.We started with Boudan balls than had the Pepper Jelly Oysters , Chicken Gumbo and Bourbon Bread pudding. No words can describe. Dwayne our server was terrific...thank you .  Will be back if we come back to New Orleans !!

I still can't get over how great the Gallery Pastry Shop is.  We went recently for my birthday (which happened to fall on Dollar Mac night, swoon!) and I had a wonderful time.  We got a plateful of macarons, which were delicious and maybe one was berry flavored and they were gone before we could make good heads or tails of what flavor the rest were.  But they were fantastic.  We also shared a little chocolate-chocolate-chocolate pastry thing that was unspeakably good.  They were super kind and put a candle in it for me!  I cannot wait to go back, especially during bike ride weather.  Especially for brunch!
Worst place I've ever eaten In NOLA. Gumbo & Red beans and rice was watery and not seasoned whatsoever. *gag*

Nice place. Great for drinks and apps. Dinner is limited menu but everything on it is great. Love the seared ahi tuna. Nice selection for the cocktail drinker. Outside is beautiful with stone and fire pits and a huge bar with flat screens. Plenty of seating and a great view of promenade shopping center as well as a nice pond with fountain.

We've eaten here about a half dozen times in the last few years. Basically, the place is inconsistent. I can say, do not order the prime rib. The price is $30 for 14oz which makes you expect something better. In the last 4 times, I have problems with 3. Despite a good deal of fat, they rarely have any flavor other than too much salt. They are thinly cut and easily over or under cooked. My last two have been tough/chewy for prime rib. The same applies to the ribs. These things do not appear to be really cooked on-site and are probably vacuum packed and just finished to order. On the plus side, the bar and atmosphere are great.

This is a nice sized smaller homegoods and clean and organized.  It was a little less busy than the other one in Kirkwood.  I spoke to one employee on the floor and she was nice and helpful but she told me I could find more information on other locations up at the service desk.  The two woman up there didn't know their head from a hole in the ground nor did they seem willing to go out of their way to get me the address to two more home good stores...all I was told is that they are currently out of those sheets of paper that has this information printed on it.  Oh-well---cut my shopping trip short today...

I am an admitted restaurant chain snob, and will do almost anything in my power to avoid chains.  When an out-of-town friend came to visit and we were hanging out in Voorhees, NJ, we had no choice but to go to a chain.  We decided on Redstone for brunch and it wasn't too shabby.  No specific dish to write home about, but I did appreciate the complimentary mimosas and pecan caramel monkey bread thingy.

Touristy... but I am one so.. :-)
I liked the food!  I had the Jambalaya (my first on this trip) and it was very filling with large chunks of sausage, chicken, and shrimp.  I really wanted to try other dishes but I don't have 5 stomachs... usually!

However, the ambiance was VERY laid back so you have to be open to that.  My waiter was very nice and even gave me a to-go cup of iced tea (didn't even ask for it!).  So great tourist stop! :-)

Superb!! Always a wonderful time. Chef Ben is amazing and he's staff is very talented and kind. The macaroons are the best I've ever had and the opera cake is TO DIE FOR! They have a great coffee selection. The ambience and decor is great for a relaxing afternoon. Def a must try

Redstone is very close to my home - I have been here 3 or 4 times with my wife. I feel that I have more complaints than praises, but the place isn't BAD. I have a hard time finding a dish that I want, but everything I've ever ordered has been good... I just feel limited by the menu (but you may find 10 dishes you like). Parking near the restaurant can be tough because it's so busy - which leads to my biggest complaint... the NOISE! It is often very hard to hear everyone at your dinner. My other complaint would be that it's often very dark in the dining areas. If you have poor eye sight or a hearing problem this place would be a nightmare for you.

We were craving pizza and didn't want the typical Papa John's, Dominos, etc. or wait for a table at one of our fave places nearby, so why not try something NEW?! Love the idea of farm to table anything so this stood out immediately. We ordered a bon bon and pizza to share. The bon bon was delicious and the pizza wasn't bad but could be even better if it were cooked in a coal oven. The coal oven thing is probably not their thing so you can't blame them. The place itself felt a little lost in identity. I think it just needs more personality, like changing up the decor and dimming the lights, play some hip music too. Other than that, it wasn't bad for a newer place. Worth a try- support a local business!
I had brunch here last weekend. Amazing!! Food was great, and service was fantastic.  I will definitely be back. The set up is adorable.

Taormina's is a great new restaurant that just opened in June. It replaced the old Portofinos. From  appearance of the restaurant from outside, it can easily be viewed as a standard plaza pizza shop, but don't be deceived! It is so much more! The meals here obviously made with great ingredients! The sauce is what makes or breaks an Italian restaurant in my opinion, and Taormina's certainly makes the cut in my opinion At the moment, the place is still relatively new and not heavily advertised, so its not packed day to day. Lansdale is slowly catching on and the weekends are getting busier and busier as schools are now in session and vacations are spent.  The best items on the menu in my opinion are under the "Chicken and Veal" section, but the seafood is phenomenal too! My favorites are the Sorentino, the Taormina, and the Farfalle Dolce Vita. Be sure to have some of the cassics too like Chicken or Veal parm. The most important thing to mention here is the PRICE! This food just isn't available ANYWHERE else for this price!  The average entree is about  $12.00!! I dont think theres anything on the menu for more than $13.99. Dinners come with a salad and garlic bread, and they also have fresh brushetta on the table as soon as they greet you. Its BYOB with a Wine and Spirits just down the road,  but if you don't need a whole bottle of something they offer a glass of complimentary wine with entrees. This place gets 2 thumbs up from me!

This was our first meal in NOLA ad it was ok.  The server seemed cool at first but then got distracted and actually almost walked away without taking my teenage sons order...it was just kinda weird.  I had the BBQ shrimp which was tasty and I liked that it was served with rice that wasn't just plain white rice.  It was seasoned with maybe turmeric and saffron?  My husband had a sampler and the best thing was the Etouffe, it had a nice flavor.  The creole shrimp was kind of lame, tasted like canned sauce and the Jambalaya was pretty ok.  We got a cup of gumbo yaya that was just ok.  My son had fried shrimp and liked it, although the cheap frozen fries weren't very good....if you are just going to use frozen fries, ok, but don't buy the cheapest crappiest ones!!  I hate that.  Anyway, it, like nearly all of our food experiences in the Quarter, was just ok...nothing special and very expensive.  It's that whole tourist thing, they don't care about customer loyalty or repeat business.  Shame.

While we were sad to see the original market operation had moved, we are thrilled there is still a market for local art and flair. 

My wife lovestalking to the artists, as she herself is bohemian... There is a little something for most every taste.   The original photography from the area can be a great inspiration for places you need to see.  

The prices are great compared to other items in the Quarter and you leave with a story too!

We miss the gazebo but they are making it their own now!
The service was great and the food was pretty good. My companion and I had the cornbread,  calamari which tasted very fresh and braised short ribs which was very tender plus the ambiance was nice.

Tony Vincent is my service tech and he and Adi, the inspector are both wonderful. They are very knowledgeable, professional, courteous and respectful.  They are very respectful of our property and treat it carefully. They are sure to educate us about the do's and don'ts of how to make the most of their service.
Tony is very friendly and personable and never makes you feel a stigma attached to having 'pests'. He said it is all part of living in Tucson!! As we are rather new to Tucson, that was good to hear. I would recommend Tony  and Truly Nolen Pest Control!!
Also Truly Nolen uses pet safe 'green' chemicals. So no need to worry about our doggies!!

This is one of my favorite places for brunch! You get a complimentary glass of mimosa and a free breakfast bread. Delicious food at an affordable price! 

Quick tip: Make sure you make a reservation during brunch time since it get can packed quickly and the wait can be long (sometimes over an hour).
The Gumbo was quite good, as was the Jambalaya, but I was disappointed in the Po'Boy. Glad we went, but I don't know if I would recommend it over any other Gumbo shop.

Always an amazing meal. Tend to think the prices are a few dollars high but it is still worth it. Nice outdoor bar and tables with fire pit. Tend to go there more in the summer but inside is upscale too.

We live in La Vergne, just a couple miles from La Siesta, so we chose to try it for its proximity, in spite of the mix of positive and negative reviews. Our experience was nothing but great, both in terms of service and quality of the food. 

I can't speak to the Mexican side of the menu. We ordered from the Peruvian section. It was outstanding! I had a Pisco, wonderful! Wife had a peach daiquiri, also very good. The missus ordered pollo a la braza (rotisserie chicken) with sweet potato fries and fried yuca (mandioca), which had a very nice flavor. I took the ceviche mixto, a combination of shrimp, mussels, calamari, and a white fish marinated in lemon and seasonings. It was fantastic! And a side of plantain, nicely sweetened. One thing, the pollo a la braza is only available Fri thru Sun. 

For dessert, the wifey had the sopapilla, which comes with a really big ball of fried ice cream rolled in corn flakes and drizzled with chocolate and honey and sprinkled with cinnamon. Excellent! I had what may be the best flan I have ever tasted, and believe me, I've tasted a lot of flan in my time. Creamy, and perfect flavor. 

Our server was Ashley, and she did a great job taking care of us. They were fairly busy, we went on a Friday evening around 6:30, but we didn't have to wait to be seated. We will definitely be regular customers here. There are at least three other offerings from the Peruvian side of the menu that I want to try. Prices quite reasonable--with each of us having a cocktail, plus main entrees and dessert, we were at $46 before tip.

I had been meaning to go to this restaurant for some time as it had always been highly recommended to me by friends. I went last night to meet up with an old friend for dinner.

From the very start, I was very underwhelmed. The music playing outside was awful. The hostesses were disorganized and not very personable. When we finally got seated after the half hour wait(not too bad for dinner time), I ordered a glass of Malbec. The wine was decent.

We decided to skip the appetizer and go straight for dinner. As this was our first time dining at the restaurant, our server let us know that they have a scratch kitchen and that everything is prepared fresh daily. We both got the classic rotisserie chicken which came with mashed potatoes and grilled asparagus. My friend who doesn't care for asparagus opted for broccoli instead.

We were very surprised that our meals came out so quickly. As we began to eat, my hopes were let down again. The rotisserie chicken was soggy, our vegetables were both cold and undercooked, and our mashed potatoes were bland at best. I would compare it best to Boston Market. The only differences are that everything at Boston Market is typically piping hot and well flavored, one third the price, and double the portion size.

After we picked at our dinners, I ordered coffee and a hot cookie sundae. The coffee tasted sour. The sundae came out in a skillet. My friend reached over to grab the plate and was burned. The skillet had obviously come right out of the oven. Typically when you drop something served in a piping hot dish with a handle, you warn your patrons that the dish is hot..

Needless to say, we will not be returning to Redstone. With so many amazing restaurants in the Marlton/Cherry Hill area, why would we? To be frank, as I was half we through my meal I thought to myself, "We should have gone to Panera. I'd be enjoying myself so much more."

BEDBUGS!!!!! DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!!! 

We went out of our way to stay here because of a previous good experience. However, I now have over 100 bites covering my body and we found bedbugs all over the bed and crawling on me. We packed up immediately and called the manager. They comped our room but that still doesn't account for the fact that I'm miserable with all these bites, it ruined our vacation, and we had to throw a lot of our stuff away that couldn't be heat treated. Let alone all the stress and anxiety it has caused. 

A previous reviewer from 2 months ago also got them there so clearly they aren't doing what they need to do to get rid of the issue.

Before going here, all I heard was that this place was great for 40+ year old singles.

Well I am 25 and just wanted lunch.  I have been here a few times.  One time I did sit by the bar and noticed older day drinking men and woman flirting across the bar to each other. 

The waiters/waitresses here are pretty laid back which I like.  They give you recommendations on how they like certain meals and even let you try out different dressings on the salads so you can decide which one you want.

The food is average and for some reason, I never leave wanting to come back.  The bar outside looks cool. It would be cooler if I was older I guess..

This place is very good for NOLA staple food.  The "Ya Ya", Red Beans n Rice, bread pudding were all very good and true to taste.  They have a great Bacon flavored Bloody Mary.  The mint julep was tasty.  The service is really what made the meal though.
Best Omelette ever.  For realz.   Beer momisa with sun king cream ale...the best hangover cure ever.  I'm in love with this little gem!

The location is perfect (next to public parking) and the amount of food you get is HUGE!  Our particular visit this week yielded a rather frustrating experience.  The waiter was slow to return with items and SELDOM got the items correct! That may have been overlooked, except we were 1 of 2 tables in the whole place!  Also, the policy states that "checks cannot be separated".  7 of us were there, due to a conference, so you can imagine the nightmare attempting to figure out how much we each owed!  They would only accept 2 credit cards to pay, so we had to go find an ATM.  The food tasted good, but was Luke warm.  Our bill also had items on it we did not order and was given the excuse that it was left there to replace an item we hadn't been charged for because it was cheaper.  I'm no expert, but I have a hard time believing a fuzzy navel costs more than a Vodka on the rocks, yet that's what I was charged for and billed for--VODKA THAT I NEVER HAD!  I gave two stars ONLY because of the taste of the cold food still being good, and the convenient parking.  The service absolutely SUCKED!  Almost forgot...one of our party ordered a medium steak and it came out rare.  They took it back and brought it out well done, but it was the exact same steak he'd just bit off.  They put his steak off his plate with his germs BACK on the griddle!  Unreal!  Can you say HEALTH CODE VIOLATION???

I went here for lunch with a friend last weekend. I ordered the lobster bisque and the steak cobb salad. The salad was delicious with the perfect amount of dressing, not too much but enough for taste. It did not come with the usual roll like a typical salad which worked in my favor. The service was great. I would go back.

Probably still the hottest table in Marlton. It's one of those places where if you live in the burbs, this is the place to be seen on a Friday or Sat night. As a result, expect a long wait when you go. 

I do like it here. The outdoor patio provides some ambiance.  My only complaint is the price. The slider appetizer with beef tenderloin, angus burger, and barbeque pulled pork sliders is $58.00. No, that's not a typo-and yes that's crazy!  For dinner, we had the scallops and steak, both of which were delicious. Cooked to perfection. I also think when compared to the rest of the menu, they're the most appropriately priced items on the menu.

We stopped by here for a weekday lunch and that seemed to be the happy medium. Late fall day, sat outside, heaters on and sunshiny. We requested to be seated outside as the inside was pretty crowded and there seemed to be a wait. It was breezy but a beautiful day.

I went with a soup (French Onion) and salad. The SO had the grilled meatloaf with mushroom marsala sauce. Both were very good. I did not see that the prices on the menu were overly high for the meal we were served.

I'm cutting the wait staff some slack as there were not many people outside (but there were a few) and it was a little on the cool side for the slow service. We weren't in a hurry and that really did not bother us at all. 

I learned from experience that going to the "hot, hip, etc" restaurants for dinner (and on the weekend) will just add to my impatience and frustration. Going at lunch during the week makes it pleasant and enjoyable and also affordable.
Small chain with a big feel.  Friendly staff are welcoming and the food and drink rank high against area competition.  If you have not been go, it will be worth your time.

When I first moved to the area, this is the first restaurant I went to.  I absolutely LOVE IT!!!!!  It has the best burgers.  Also, the chicken and ribs meal is excellent.  The service is always on point.  I have to say that is what impressed me the most.  From the moment you walk in to you walk out the door, you get first class treatment.  The store is very clean.  I will definitely become a regular here!

Good spot for group gatherings and going out with family and friends.  Always packed, and has consistently decent food. That said, so busy that the waitstaff never make it back to your table to refill drinks, but are very friendly when taking your order.  So DO order your refills at the time they drop off your entree.  Make reservations or plan on a 25-40 min wait and being sat in a less than desirable location.  Outdoor patio seems to be a favorite of the 20-30 crowd, while interior seating accomodates the 40-60 crowd.

I have been going to Redstone in Marlton since they opened. Lately it has been less than good. The servers are always excellent but the food is not. I was there yesterday for lunch with my husband. I was excited to order the salmon tacos. When they arrived they looked beautiful but upon eating them the only salmon that was in them was what you would throw away. It was the slimy skin something. Just terrible. Our server was wonderful and brought it to the attention of the manager who didn't even have the courtesy to come see us. Surely won't be going back.

My husband and I purchased my Tacori wedding ring set and his wedding band here. Christine and the rest of the Sheffield team was great to work with. She patiently assisted us as we looked through their entire collection of rings to be sure we were happy with our decision. My husband and I each had to drop off our rings at one point, his to be resized, and mine for the diamonds on my engagement ring to be aligned with my wedding band. Sheffield's took great care of our rings, and though the month plus long wait was difficult, we were happy with the results. Everyone was always friendly, professional and helpful.

This place is an adorable, tucked away gem in broad ripple. Very cute atmosphere, but a little loud. I went there for brunch and ordered the grape mimosa (delicious), 2 eggs hash (good but not amazing - it was mostly potatoes, I would have liked more chorizo and veggies), and lemon merengue (also delicious). I took off one star for how pricey it is and the service, while good, was VERY slow.

Shoulda looked this place up before we went. How a place like this stays open in a town with so many options of really good food is beyond me...maybe the tourists coming from the Natches.  We tried it because we were hungry and wanted a quick bite to eat. Ordered a couple of shrimp cocktails and beans and rice...price for this and 3 drinks was about 50 dollars!!!!!!! The shrimp was off, the beans an rice bland and the sausage was burnt to a crisp...just the worst food I have had in this town and SO over priced I felt ripped off (I was really). Service was lack luster at best. Someone could really do well in this location IMO with good food and service...Shame.

My obsession with this place is undeniable. Although I've never had an actual meal here, the $1 macaroons on Wednesdays have been amazing enough to earn my loyalty. Trust me, you'll feel like you're biting into a light, sugary cloud. The service here has always been good, and I've never had a complaint. This is a great place to meet up with a friend for brunch or after work. They serve Bee coffee, and I'm a big fan of this spot. Also, they have a lot of outdoor seating!

The buffalo shrimp and corn bread skillet are a must! The Caesar salad was bleh. I had the short rib which was delish and hubby had the Wellington which he said was pretty good but wouldn't order again.

As I currently sit at my table, sweating my ass off so badly that my legs are wet against the wood chairs (it's not even hot outside today. It's gorgeous out and it's cooler outside than in here), I also have a wonderful view of no less than 5 flies on the window next to me. Waiting for the check, that our server with the nastiest attitude, advised us she couldn't split after the fact, I can't help but wish I had chosen a different restaurant. Blandest food I've ever had. Worst service I've ever encountered. Terrible all around. I can't wait to get back outside where there is air flow.

This place is right near JAX. Run for your life!!!  We came for breakfast - everyone was rude - from seating to servers.   Waited literally 45 minutes for $15 eggs only to receive our orders cold and not as ordered.   Not a little cold - not hot.     Our toast was served after we ate our full bfst.  Terrible.   Did I mention the awful service?!
Most gumbo in NOLA is good.  This not so much.  Service was perfunctory at best.  Music was good.  Price too high for quality

I was pretty happy with the whole process.  I dropped my ipad off on a Monday and it was ready for me the next afternoon.  It was barely missed.  They should put on their web site that they will charge less if they are doing more than one repair, because it almost scared me away that I was going to have to pay $100+ for a screen repair and another $100+ for a button repair.  But when I called them, they told me that it would only be $30 for the button repair since they would already be in there.  The lady I dealt with when I picked up the iPad was super nice and friendly.  I was overall very happy.

I've been here twice, once in the summer on the patio for Sunday brunch and once indoors for lunch. The first time (brunch) I showed up hungover with my three sisters and 9-month old niece. You would have thought pushing a carriage with a sleeping baby inside was a cardinal sin to the fake-breasted / fake tanned snobs cock-eying us as we walked through the patio to find a table. To you snooty Marlton   / Medford BridalPlasty wannabes: seriously? Eat something on your plate. No, like really. I dare you. 

We finally sat down and ordered the cornbread appetizer which comes out in a cast-iron skillet with a huge side of maple butter - holy crap, it might have been one of the tastiest things I ever ate, i didn't even know you could MAKE cornbread that good. Of course that was before I found out that one slice of said cornbread hosts 855 calories and 62 grams of fat (I've linked that info below - and it is, literally, per slice).

Ew!

The coffee was also really good and I heard they will serve free mimosas as well, but you have to be cheap enough to ask for them because they certainly were not offered to us. Although maybe that's because we had a sleeping spawn of Satan with us (aka quiet and adorable baby). On second thought, perhaps those nasty b's  thought she was a sausage or something else that would make their plastic lips melt off, I don't know. 

Anyway, the rest of the food was WAY overpriced for what you got; we all ordered breakfast things off the brunch menu; for some reason the egg platters come with three eggs so I asked for two (I was so full from the bread I'd never eat three, nor would I take it to go) but three arrived on my plate to be wasted, anyway. The potatoes were actually AMAZING and the toast and sausage just OK. Definitely not better than you get at a diner for 1/8 of the price. At brunch you can also ASK for the complementary cinnamon buns but again, it's like they force you to feel like a cheap bastard in the process. We only even found out it was complementary when I asked her where that amazing thing was on the menu. She kindly sensed my awkward response when she told us it was free and spared me the humiliation by packing us one to go. So cornbread + potatoes + free cinnamon roll thing: check.

So for lunch the other day I had a small garden salad with some vinaigrette that had ZERO flavor, like when the server poured it only the oil came out or something. The salad was a nice size, but not worth the price by any means; it didn't come with any bread which annoyed me after I saw the table next to us get two huge baskets from another server after I had long finished. My husband had the cream of wild mushroom soup which tasted like, well, cream of mushrooms. The coffee at lunch HAD to have been a different brand from the last time or had been sitting on the burner for hours because it tasted like a low-grade Folgers. The cornbread was again the best item purchased, save for my husband's $4.50 mocha that came with it's own side of whipped cream and a stick of rock candy for stirring.  Cornbread + Mocha: check check.

In short, the restaurant is unnecessarily pretentious and expensive for what you get, and the clientele it attracts leaves much to be desired. Also, if you are going to offer complementary items like mimosa's and cinnamon rolls, don't force your customers to feel like they need to know the speakeasy password to get the hookup. Lame.

The cornbread recipe:
http://www.food.com/recipe/redstone-restaurant-famous-cornbread-with-maple-butter-194584

I was soooo disappointed.
The server was quite pleasant and suggested an appetizer of shrimp and peppers - the shrimp and sauce was good, bread seemed a bit stale and old.
I ordered shrimp creole ( and have had this dish many times as I was born and raised in the city) when my food arrived it was a few grilled shrimp in what seemed to be tomato soup. There were no seasonings or veggies cooked/simmered into the mix - just tomato soup and some grilled shrimp which did not seem to be seasoned either. We also ordered fried oysters and catfish which was decent. Our server brought the bill but did not let us see the itemized receipt. We had a 25$ for 50$ restaurant.com gift certificate... Our bill for 1 beer, an appetizer and 2 main dishes after our gift cert. was 68$ 
This seemed a bit excessive if you ask me for not a good experience.
To add  on top the 68$ food bill we parked in the lot attached to the shops and restaurant which charged 15$ for parking, no validation or discount offered either for going to the eatery.

83$ for a beer, appetizer and 2 main dishes not impressing at all - 
needless to say we will not be going back, I find it a bit fishy as well that our server didnt present us with an itemized receipt.

Very nice place. Good music and perfect for a nice dinner. They don't do any subs for foods you don't like but they do have great choices. The food looks great and taste awesome. I would recommend the grilled cheese that is my favorite. Also the French fries are awesome and they are warm and crispy.  They are always nice but the front desk people are not very nice or very good. They don't great and they don't even smile.

I went and ate there for lunch. The food and service is excellent, prices very reasonable. This is a nice place to go to lunch or dinner.

Joe

This is a locally owned family business. They always do a great job and never complain about my dog not liking to be groomed. They are pretty busy and you often have to wait a week or so for an appointment but it's worth it.

This place had such potential. Located between the Wharf and the Quarter, it is close enough to be convenient but tucked away just enough to not be insanely busy. I should've know there was another reason they weren't busy. 

We waited forever for our drinks. I had Abita Amber (can't go wrong) and my family had Hurricanes.  Again, should've known - but $11 each for ice and juice is too much! 

We had seafood gumbo and shrimp po-boys. All decent enough to eat, but nothing to rave about.  We also waited forever for our food. Not to mention, we asked for waters 3 times and never received them. 

The waitress did apologize that she was very behind and trying hard to catch up, but it just wasn't enough to save the day.  If the food had been outstanding or the drinks had been off the wall, I would've understood.  But nothing was stellar, and I wouldn't bother going back.

My wife and I dined here for New Year's Event, and it's definitely nothing to write home about. I thought it was mediocre at best, and for being mediocre it was definitely over priced. For a steakhouse the selection of steaks is small. The restaurant was very loud and you could barely here the person next to you. Definitely won't be back. Really just an overall disappointment, but it's my fault for waiting until the last minute to book a restaurant for New Year's

Stephanie took care of our little Maltese. Very, very good job. He looks like a Maltese again. 

Very personal service. Highly recommend...

ordered the jambalaya not good at all...the TWO  shrimp tasted old...and i got ONE a half  piece of a piece of a sausage ( if that makes sense) ...the rice had a lot of OLD stale chicken...
BARF!!!!!! oh and to it off when i checked in on YELP it gave me a coupon for 1 free bread pudding and they told me i couldn't use it...and were RUDE about it...SMH
What a gem. Love the Peruvian part of the menu! Not greasy/oily, just wonderful flavorful food. Great value on top shelf drinks too. I'll be back!

POOR, POOR, POOR SERVICE! We didn't even eat here because we were initially told by the host the wait would be 5-10 minutes for a table inside and that we could wait outside. Well, after waiting 20 minutes OUTSIDE in the heat then chatting with folks at the table next to us that said they'd been waiting 45 minutes (after also being told 5-10 mins), the waitress came over to us and said, "I'm sorry, you should probably order because I don't see any tables opening up inside." Then, we see the manager yelling at this group of people because they were blocking entrance. After that, we grabbed our things and walked out. Wouldn't attempt this place again when I'm in NOLA...

This place was very deceiving, the place is nice with good music , but the food was not good at all , we were a party of 6 and no one enjoyed their food, too plain and the flavor sucked. I would not come back.

Stopped in to get a drink and use the restroom, I usually like sheets and wawas because they are convenient and clean. This location is neither. Nor do they have public restrooms. Rude girl at counter sent me across the street to the restroom... the gas station across the street appears to have closed. I will shy away from wawa and look for sheetz. 

Maybe their food is better than their service??

Great food! Great atmosphere! I had the crab cakes- mostly crab, very little filler. Drinks were amazing also! Friendly and prompt service. A little pricey but very well worth it! We met with two other couples and everyone enjoyed their food. I would definitely recommend and plan on going again soon

I've never had creole food before, and my friend insisted on us coming to try it. I was hesitant about coming, but really glad she convinced me!
We walked in and was greeted by the nicest host (Matthew) ever! He always came by our table just to talk to my friend and I- very funny/cool guy. He gave us GREAT recommendations: cup gumbo yaya, cup seafood gumbo, and shared a catfish po boy sandwich. 

Everything tasted fantastic! The gumbo yaya was my favorite. The po boy sandwich is huge! The waiter service for Mardi Gras Saturday was whatever, but the other staffers (busers & host) totally made it up for it.

DAY 2: Came in again before we left Mardi Gras weekend on Sunday. We were surprised the host remembered us, and gave us the very same table we sat at yesterday. This time the service was excellent- she was so nice and sweet, and checked on us frequently. I ordered the the sampler that came with shrimp etouffee, jambalya, shrimp (something)- it was really good but I when I come back next year, I'll just get the gumbo and jambalya!

So this was my first visit and it was a good one. Hidden away is this cute little pastry shop. We went for brunch and it was delicious. The prices are a little higher than your normal breakfast place, but they use high quality ingredients and it's delicious. You're started off with a complimentary cinnamon role and then several menus . I was obviously confused how to order regarding 3 Menus and given Pens to fill out our order. Luckily the waiter was kind enough to explain it to me. This is a very cozy and nice place for a delicious breakfast and some coffee. I can't wait to bring others to this lovely spot and enjoy some more food and mimosas!!!

Located in the old Jackson Brewery.  Nice decor with friendly staff.  Absolutely the richest most flavorful chicken and andouille gumbo I have ever tasted.  I thought I had created an authentic recipe, I am after all, a Cajun, but it was nothing compared to this.  The Jambalaya was good, it tasted like my fast gumbo recipe.  Dos Equis served with a wedge of lime.

So full right now can't think! We went for a late lunch and ordered grill chix wing w ranch sauce so good ! Margarita pizza had better but this isn't an Italian Restuarant so it's fine the best is probably the dessert omg so so good warm chocolate chip w vanilla ice cream I shared it w my sister and my moms  and there was more than enough! The cookie was perfect and the amt of ice cream perfect usually places do not give enough ice cream w the warm cookie or brownie bc it all melts but this was heavenly I am so so full! Now excuse me as I go take a nap

We've marked La Siesta as a go to place for large group meals in Smyrna. So far they are the only restaurant that always gets the orders and tabs correct, and gets us in and out in a very reasonable amount of time. There's always an order for the queso fundido, which is delicious and well portioned to share amongst a group of four as an appetizer. The guacamole is tasty and not too bland. I recently had the shrimp quesadilla and a side of rice for lunch. The quesadilla was a a flaky yet soft tortilla well stuffed with lots of big shrimp, chunky veggies and generous cheese. There was no skimping on the fillings, which was great as it made a filling meal with the rice. Their enchiladas are a pretty safe bet, flavorful but mild. The tacos are also pretty standard but good. The vegetarian menu is full of meals that are well priced and satisfying. I always appreciate when restaurants use the big chunky veggies, not the small diced stuff you can tell was meant for a meat dish. Dinner time can get pretty crowded and noisy here, but for lunch it's usually quiet. They occasionally have bands play on weekends. Lunch meals are less than $10 a person and two people can have meals and adult drinks for under $30. All round good place to stop in.

There were three of us and this review is unanimous. The gumbo was pathetic: a thin, tasteless gravy. The po boy was pathetic: no sauce or salad, nothing but small fried oysters that were mostly crust. The catfish po boy was equally disappointing. The service was indifferent. I guess this is just a tourist trap that does not expect any repeat business. And what is with the fake stuffed swordfish???
Excellent, friendly service and good knowledge of fine watches. Nice to know the owner is on-site and cares a lot about his customers' satisfaction. I will definitely return to this jeweler.

Had dinner here last night, the restaurant smelled amazing and Dwayne was awesome and so polite.  Mardi Gras music playing in the background helped to get us in the spirit.  Dad and I split the seafood platter, lots of food, we couldn't finish the fries!!! Mom had the eggplant Parmesan and the flavors were amazing, the eggplant was cooked to perfection and the sauce had perfect flavor.  Great beer selection too
service and outdoor space is great. husband was disappointed with bbq meatloaf - too much filler.  the BBQ salmon was just ok - the sweet potatoes side was great.

I have always heard you can never go back.  The last time we were here, the food was delicious and service wonderful. They must have the pre Mardi Gras, you can serve any crap and get away with it menu out today.  The salad with blackened chicken was more like bland, pale, white, boiled chicken cut up in the yellow portion of iceburg  lettuce.  The Gumbo Ya Ya was thin, flavorless and room temp.  The utensil given my husband was a fork, it all ran between the tynes.  Disappointed beyond words after looking forward to an excellent meal.

Second morning in NOLA and strongly in need a hearty brunch to get the day started; nice warm weather and seeing patio populated, right after the car was parked we decided to give Gumbo Pot a visit, since it was but a short walk.

I am uncertain where all the hate come from; from stepping in under the patio shade until I paid for the check and left, I got thumbs up services and food quality. There were two tables available, and hostess let us chose where we wanted to sit. The Bloody Mary arrived as we finally settling into our seats, and were exactly what we  were looking for to go with the brunch.

Spotted Lost Breads on the menu, which was definitely unique, as I personally would have never think to use FRENCH bread to make FRENCH toast! Dusted with powdered sugar and drizzled a little syrup, the crunchy yet toasty bread worked with Bloody Mary while waiting for the next two dishes. This blintzes stuff has gotta to be creole specific because I have never seen it before; topped with freshly sliced strawberries and whipped sour cream, it was a good balance from the breakfast potato plate.

We got here right before they closed, so restaurant was practically empty.  Got great service and were not rushed.  The blackened red fish was off the hook!  Especially loved the smothered cabbage.  Husband had bread pudding and said it was great.

I had a Chargrilled salad when i came here.. I was on Fried food/ carb overload and needed some greens re-introduced to my diet! The Food was ehhh ok, nothing to write home about. I did try my friends Gumbo and thought it was extra Yummy but this place is farely expensive for what it is... you go further down Decatur towards the French Market and you'll find the same eats for half the price.

Ur Gadget Doctors is a perfect name for this business. As with actual doctors, not all diagnosis are initially correct and not all surgeries have the outcome expected. 
That being said - I have found the "Doctors" to be most knowledgeable about their products and electronics in general. They have never been anything but honest in every conversation I have had with them either in person or on the phone. Their support staff is knowledgeable as well as being quite service oriented.
I purchased an android TV "box" from them a year ago. As with any electronic device - this one I had some problems with. I took it back over the course of the last year several times because it was acting up. Each time one of their techs looked at it and fixed the problem I came in with, at no charge because I purchased it from them. 2 days ago I found the need to return once again to the "doctors" as it again was not working properly. Upon entering the store, one of their techs - Mike - recognized me and said - Oh no, whats going on this time. I explained the problem and he hooked it up to his TV to check it out for himself. After waiting a few minutes he decided that enough was enough and swapped out my "box" for a new one as I have had enough problems already.
I brought the new device home, hooked it up and it seems to be working properly. This was the second time in a row that Mike was the tech that helped me and he couldn't have been more professional. Knowing that sitting around a "tech store" can be frustrating, Mike kept up a conversation about movies, TV or anything else to make the wait more satisfying. KUDOS TO MIKE! All the time setting up the new device so that when I returned home everything would be working as expected, and it did.
I would recommend Ur Gadget Doctors with one caveat, nothing is ever concrete when dealing with electronics and computers, very much the same way that nothing is ever "concrete" when given a diagnosis from a medical doctor. There is always a possibility of an error, it's how the error is handles that makes the difference and these "Doctors" and their support staff do a great job, in my opinion.

This restaurant is near our home and always convenient.  My boyfriend is Mexican so I always value his opinion when it comes to Mexican food.  While not so much authentic, it's a good Americanized version.  Service in general has always been fair, nothing special.  Prices are reasonable.
We went for a pop-up dinner, so that is out of the ordinary, but man...good stuff!!

I have ordered take out from Joli about 3 or 4 times. I always get the "Pizza Pop". Its kind of like a Stromboli.  They usually only have 2 or 3 of the 5 types listed on the menu. The service is usually great although I have mostly dealt with one of the owners. They have a canoli bar where you get to choose what goes on it. I had a classic canoli and it was delicious. My low rating comes from trying to order lunch from them today. There were signs outside saying they were having a grand opening so when I got to work, I attempted to call in a take out order. Without any explanation or apology they just said they don't deliver anymore, which is fine, I work close by so I was going to pick it up. Still needing to order some lunch I walked over and they doors were locked and an employee  was inside talking on the phone. I wasn't even acknowledged. Meanwhile, as I mentioned, there was a 'Grand Opening" banner over the door and flags strung up around the outside eating area. I want to love Joli but today's experience was so strange that Im not sure I will be eating there again.

Stayed at the Clarion for 5 nights.  Overall excellent experience.   
Very close to Titan Stadium and they have a shuttle that runs every 30 minutes to Downtown.   Drops you off literally on Broadway.  On more than one day, the shuttle drivers, Victor and his brother Raul even dropped us off closer to the actual place we were going!  They were great!!!!!  Make sure to tip these guys.  Coming home we usually took an Uber and it was about $4.50.  
The hotel was very clean both inside and out.   Looks like the rooms have been updated within the last few years.   Bed was very comfortable but the boyfriend hated the small pillows.   The bathroom looked updated as well however, it looks like a few shortcuts were taken in that remodel.   Shower faucet looked like it was coming apart from the wall and there was actually a gap in he ceiling.  Water pressure wasn't the greatest either!
The Clarion did have a morning breakfast buffet.  Don't expect anything too fabulous here but hey, it's ok and it's free!   Make your own waffles, oatmeal, scrambled eggs, sausage, biscuits and gravy (imagine that down South), and some diced potatoes.  They so had bagels, cereal, toast, yogurts, fruit and muffins as well as juice and coffee.  
There was no problem parking and they even have a security guard after 10 PM.    We had no problem leaving the Harley there. 
The lobby was nicely decorated and a small bar with a grill with your basic burgers, quesadillas, sandwiches, etc with everything under $10 was also a bonus.   
Free wifi and a free safe in the room.   Also had a fridge and microwave.   Big bonus for me were the amount of electrical plugs in the room including on each side of the bed.  Typically, I have a hard time finding enough to plug in all of our items. 
Only about 4 hangers in the closet so bring your own if you need more.  
The gym was also very clean.   2 TVs, an elliptical, a couple of treadmills, a bike, weights, and a universal weight machine.  Towels and cold water were also in the room.   I loved that there were wipes in the fitness room as well for wiping down the equipment after use.  It does get very hot in there though and they really should a couple fans in there.  
Staff were all very friendly.   If you don't mind being off the strip and saving money, this is the place!!

Just like every other review here m, bad bad bad 

So on my last day in NOLA we decided to go by the water (Mississippi River) and have lunch before our flight. We walked down a bit didn't see any restaurant but this one and a food court on top, which I didn't want to eat at. Without checking my Yelp We walked into this place, we got sat down right away. 
As I was looking at the menu nothing looked appetizing, we order drinks (lemonade and coke) which we were later informed that refills are not free. Food: since I've never had a poboy I decided to order one, the Hamburger poboy to be exact
Poboy: nothing special just a burger on a different type of bread and I had to add my lettuce, tomato, and mayo.  
My Bf didn't take that chance he order the spaghetti and meatballs he said it was good 

The serve was mediocre the waiter was nice but busy talking to his coworkers or other friends at the restaurant 
It was until half way through our meal that I decided to check Yelp and saw the reviews 
My Bf got mad cuz he knows I'm always yelping and the one time I don't, we get a bad place 
The only good thing out of this was my free glass of wine I checked in for and I took it to go!!! 
I would have rather eaten at the food court

It was fun, especially the interactive stuff, but I was a little disappointed. I was a college athlete, come from a family of college athletes and am a big college sports fan, so I guess I expected a little more. $5 is a good deal though for a museum.

I've had a chance to go through the Hall of Champions free of charge a few times now.  It's a fun experience.  Probably really good for kids.

You can learn about all of the collegiate sports.  There are a number of interactive displays where you can gain an appreciation of how fast a tennis ball is coming at you, play some hoops, see how long a long jump is, and other fun stuff.

If you have some free time, check it out!

"UR" Gadget Doctors is nothing more than kids in scrubs playing doctor on our electronics. Their claim for quick 24 hour repairs is a sad lie and the employees are extremely lazy. 

A diagnostic for a console should be more than a teenager playing a low quality game for thirty minutes (if that) and saying nothing is wrong. Besides completely ignoring the issues discussed and not even ATTEMPTING to find the root of the issue, the kid just dusted the console and sent it back with us. Such a waste of time and money. 

And I mean, come on, how can you take anyone seriously who dresses up as medical personnel and not actually do any true repairs? Not to mention I never got a phone call when they were done "testing" my console; I had to call at the 24 hour mark and ASK if they even looked at my device yet.

Of course as soon as I brought my console home and plugged it in it crashed, with the SAME EXACT issues it was brought there for. So what exactly did they do to my console besides dust it and charge me? I'm not too sure. But all the employees sure looked like they were having fun in the workspace riding around on mini skateboards.

If you actually want a proper repair done for your electronic devise DO NOT come to this place.

I've been going here for awhile, even though this place is way out of the way for me I've made it a point to come here because they don't keep my dogs for hours at a time and the groomer does a good job.

Absolutely a must if you are in need of a brunch! Not only is the food delicious, but included with brunch is a complimentary mimosa, as well as an orange/coconut muffin with icing and coconut shavings (muffins change weekly I believe)! As in free! As in, the waiter asks if you want the massive muffin as dessert or to take home! Did I forget to mention the to die for Eggs Benedict? Go here for brunch!

Not even installed yet and I'm livid. First scheduled day and they were a no call/no show. It was raining so I didn't expect an install, but to not call at all and force us to call multiple times until someone picked up is inexcusable. Now today I was told an install team would be out at 10am and another no call/no show. After multiple calls/voicemail and an email to the owner, the owner finally called back. His response? They put on his calendar the install was today (which was what was communicated to us), but put tomorrow on the installers calendar. Needless to say, i expect tomorrow to happen and you better believe that I will do a walkthrough to verify the fence is to my expectation of quality or it will be redone. I have no faith in this company's accountability or customer service and to still pay full price for because it's a "service" is a joke. So far the service isn't worth it. Avoid them.

- Great patio space with plenty of seating
- Great ambiance inside as well with the bar and booth and table seating
- Nice Happy Hour selection and great wine list
- The turkey burger is delicious, slightly spicy
- The coleslaw is also very good - not overly saucy
- The buffalo shrimp are what everyone gets when they come here!

Can't recommend this hotel enough- friendly staff, helpful room service and the best customer service! Dorothy- I just can't say enough about this extremely welcoming and accommodating woman. Especially after having the worst experience at the scummy hotel next door- the Knights Inn. This place is so nice and worth every dollar! Will definitely come back here!

Best Rotisserie Chicken I've ever had. Juicy, moist, and loaded with great flavor. You need the Spinach Salad or R. Chicken Chopped Salad. A nice size salad, perfect for a meal. Great flavors. Do not order as a salad app. because 1) the price and 2) you will be too full.

They have a soup of the day - different soup each day. Lobster Bisque is very good. Not the best I've ever had, but maybe the 2nd best. Only served on Saturday nights.

Service is good.

Atmosphere is nice. Great for a date, night out with friends or family, etc.

Prices: Can be somewhat on the higher end for some dishes, but overall not bad.

We ate breakfast here because it was close to where the Natchez departs. 

Service was slow - though our server was nice.  She just didn't seem to be in any hurry to get to our table.

The food was ok - but hard to goof up scrambled eggs. One odd occurrence - our server brought our toast out about 2 minutes before our eggs. Their idea of toast was warm bread..not a shade different from white bread.

Their biggest problems for me are consistency and price.  Sometimes I get food that's great, sometimes I get food that's not great at all.  In my opinion they're a little over priced, even when the food is good.  Seems like a pretty hip spot as far as nightlife goes but it's not really my type of crowd.

So the bar was great that food was good. To be honest I expected more out of my steak for the price. I've had a better beef selection at a cheaper price. Don't get me wrong the steak was delicious and very well cooked..... but it didn't melt as much as I would have liked.

This place does not care much about the customer. The service was okay BUT do not make any special orders because they will not homer them. I talked to the manager and he told me this is how we have always served things and we will not change. Save your money and go else where.

Check your credit card statement after eating here. I spent $40 and left a 20% tip on the card. When I checked my statement the waiter had lest himself a $20 tip. Really?! They take advantage of tourists. I contested the charge and got my money back. I read some more reviews and this has happened multiple times.

We went for lunch on a Saturday after reading the glowing reviews on Yelp. We both ordered a side salad with the homemade Italian dressing and 2 slices of cheese pizza. For the price - $4 salad, $2 per cheese slice - the meal was fine. We weren't blown away. The pizza crust was plain and the tomato sauce was lacking. It's ok for a quick, inexpensive bite. Maybe the other menu options are better? Or maybe it was just an off day?

Driving through Nashville and were only there for one night. Didn't want to spend $200 on a hotel downtown. This hotel was about 5 minutes drive to downtown tourist area. Clean and great customer service. Free breakfast. Use to be a days inn which got confusing when we were first looking for it on a map, but it is now remodeled and currently still under construction on some parts of the hotel. Would stay again.
Clean, Nice, Affordable, Comfortable beds... Not much this place doesn't do, would come back.

Second trip here was much better than the first. Didnt think I would go back but everything deserves a second chance! I had a delicious salad and my daughter had a awesome prime rib sandwich. Drinks were good and food was great this time.

I absolutely love this place!  The omeletes that are served are scrumptious and the choices for fillings are many. It is a flat price for whatever ingredients you want in your omelete - you can choose just one filling or every option listed.  They also serve crepes both savory and sweet.  The ambience & service is great as well, but the most delicious croissant I've ever had ( I've been to Paris twice) is their almond croissant.  The croissant is flaky & has an almond filling similar to marzipan and is topped with toasted almonds. They are to die for! 
The only negative is that the omeletes & crepes are only served Sat & Sun.  I also find their website menu to be a bit confusing. Have to really study it to figure out what is served when, but this is a small complaint.  It is my new favorite spot especially on the weekends!

I would leave a 0 star review if it was possible. This has been the worst restaurant I've ever been to. We started with our very rude server called JENNIFER who came to the table and ask "what do y'all want?" Didn't even give us her name (we took a pic of the bill to make sure we had her information). When we asked her for more time to look at the menu she rolled her eyes and walked away without saying anything. We proceeded to order and after 10 minutes or so she came back to the table with our side dishes, 5 minutes after she comes back with my friend's food but ours (4 ppl total) was nowhere to be seen. I finally see our po-boy sitting on the pass under the lamp (which was already turned off so our food was getting colder by the second). Minutes go by and Jennifer is nowhere to be found, then she comes around to the table behind us and starts throwing silverware around and then proceeds to walk to the back without even checking on us.... she CLEARLY didn't care at all about her table. We're able to see her a few minutes after (at this point we already decided we didn't want out cold food) and she stands in front of our po-boy and continues to clean the station spraying some sort of chemical all around and wiping down RIGHT NEXT TO OUR FOOD!!! All this time she still hasn't check on us and she goes and sits down at a table where other servers are sitting down gossiping. After a good 20 minutes of our sandwich being prepared then she comes with it to the table and she didn't even remember who it was for as everyone else was done with their meals already. I tell her we don't want it and she's like "oh.... you don't want it anymore?" And I said no, it's been sitting there for 20 minutes right in front of you, I'm not paying $15 for a cold/soggy po-boy. 
She went to get the manager to remove the item from the bill and after another 10 minutes she finally came with it. She said they didn't split checks so we did the math for her and handed her 4 cards so she could split the payment (HA! That clearly made her angrier which we enjoyed btw) Needless to say her tip was a big fat $0. We were eager to talk to management but he/she never came around. Clearly no one cares in this place, don't let them take your money. I wouldn't be back even if it was the last place on earth.

4 of us went for lunch and no one really enjoyed their meal. We were told they were out of tomatoes so that eliminated a few menu choices. Two chose the ham and cheese sandwich but only one liked it. One of us couldn't find an entree she liked so chose a croissant and creme brûlée which she said was very good. I had the vegetarian quiche which was savory but not remarkable. The background music was very loud for such a small space. Their pastries looked wonderful but we weren't wanting more Christmas calories. If you like charcuterie and smoking goose meats, you'll probably like this place. I don't and would not recommend this place for a ladies who lunch spot.

When I saw the reviews I was excited to try this place with my foodie friend!  We loved the decor and the fact that it wasn't too crowded.  However, the pastry selection was slim (unexpected given the name) and while the pastries were fine they weren't anything special.
Buyer beware stay away from this fence company the biggest rip off out there taking advantage of every body gets deposit never does the work!!!!!!

Had a flatbread and the Sea Bass with my father.  Food was great and further enhanced by the atmosphere.  Quiet and waitress actually listened when we said, 'Come back in 15'.

Only detraction is that lighting was a touch too dim.  Bit hard to see the menus.  No big deal - but a potential issue for some. Worth the visit!

Ka-POW!!!

Very Good with decent value

Ahi Tuna Appetizer was the least of the meal. I don't feel the tuna is prepared at the restaurant and was on the dry side. Tasted Frozen.

Wild Mushroom Soup was excellent.

Turkey Burger according to my friend was very good.
Appetizer of Chinese Ribs was very succulent and meaty.

No entrees were ordered.

60 dollars for two. I enjoyed the experience and will be back.
This place is a solid choice for getting electronics, especially cracked iPhone screens repaired. Quick and courteous...and in my case they've given me a discount after multiple cracked screens.

This restaurant was not a favorite on our trip. The meal was over priced, the service was lacking, and we left thinking we just wasted a lot of money. Please do not confuse this restaurant with Gumbo Shop which I might add was superb.

I love seafood gumbo and every time I am in New Orleans, I try to find the best seafood gumbo. I have tried many highly rated restaurants offering seafood gumbo but nothing has really satisfied my expectations. We tried this place hoping to taste a great seafood gumbo but only to burn my gums and lips with too much spice. There was not any seafood in it. I counted three bits of shrimp and a half shell of a tiny crab (if you happen to be there and order this, don't even try to open the crab since there is no meat in it). If you are looking for simply hot thick rice soup, then this is the place to be but be aware that there is no seafood flavor in it.

First time visiting Redstone and I was highly impressed.  The fig/goat cheese flatbread appie was awesome as was the cheese fondue and cornbread (don't get me started on that honey butter!!).  Pricey, yes.  But well worth the price.  Right about $300 for 6 of us, but there were several appies, plus some drinks and entrees all around.  So--decent, if not your weekly choice, a great place for an occasion.  My entree of parm crusted Walleye was superb with grilled asparagus.  Heaven!!  And service was really great.  Wish I could give it five stars, but I'd go with 4.5, for sure!!  Really excellent place.  I look forward to going again soon!!  Oh--and when I go back I plan to arrive extra early so we can enjoy a drink at the outside bar by the firepit!!!  Ok--I guess it is a 5 star place!!  Lol.

Very disappointed! Dined on Saturday with a girl group. Service was slow and they refused to give me my points because the host didn't get my name right for the booking. Food was just ok nothing special.

Came in for breakfast before a city tour. The prices are high (starting at 9.95) for breakfast. I ordered two eggs with bacon and home fries. The fries had good flavor although they were cold. The bacon was also cold. The coffee was great as was the server. Overall.. What a let down. I honestly would have preferred a fast food meal.

I went in there extremely hungry and ordered a soul food omelet. Not only was it really tasty, but it was also really huge! The grits were good, and I could tell that the biscuits were made from scratch because they weren't perfectly round. Our server was very attentive and hospitable, so I tipped accordingly.

I was there this past monday night and I have to say I was very happy.  I sat at the bar and had a fresh new jersey craft draft. awsome.  Bob, my bartender, could not have been more helpful.  My hamburger came out just as I ordered and after another craft beer, I left.  I found out that it is a small, but growing, chain that appears to be doing alot of things right.  Congratulations.

After dealing with 2 particularly rude gun dealers yesterday I found these guys on google, I went in and they had the gun I was looking for at a great price, I left with my gun, ammunition, and a holster. I will only do business with these guys from here on out! Impact and Boise Gun should take some lessons from these guys!

This is one of the coolest cozy spots in broadripple. It's a garage turned into a cool resturant. Here's a few reasons why I like this place. There's plenty of seating, you can bring your pouch with you and sit out side and have lunch, they raise the garage door open on really nice days, they grow alot of the veggies that they use and the decor is just darn relaxing! I love the chandeliers so classy! The employees make you feel like you've been friends for ever! You have to check this place out. The only small (and I do mean small) drawback is that it's a little hard to find but there's nothing wrong with hidden gems! It's kinda hidden behind other shops but it's worth looking for. And lastly  it's just a hair off the monon. So you can eat then take a walk.. or walk then have lunch. Hope you take time to check out this cool place. They also have Saturday and Sunday brunch. There a different menu on the weekends.
Haven't been there in a year. When they stopped making the dip by like I went back a couple of times and found that the other dishes didn't excite me

Just went to Red stone today and it was great! We sat outside by the water fountain and our waitress was very nice. The main menu had a great selection but I chose from the specials menu.  I had the breakfast flat bread and it was delicious. I will definitely be back soon.

I am a very picky person where I eat & stay and if I find something good or bad I must let everyone know. I am in NOLA for spring break with my family & the service was horrible. We didn't even know what our servers name was. He did not tell us or anything. We waited yet another 20 mins to ask for bread but apparently you have to ASK for bread. Now when I go restaurants I normally get bread WITHOUT having to ask for it. I had the chicken Parmesan which did not come with a side so I got a side order of French fries that looked liked they came straight out of the freezer and were in the oven for 15 minutes just enough to get them warm. We did not have an silverware so we asked for some and a different server came back and gave it to us and mumbled a rude expression towards us. I am very disappointed in this restaurant, as it looked popping with energy on the outside as we walked by it which in reality it was filled with awful awful service & okay food.
Terrible service, food was low quality and not worth the $20 dish I ordered. Would not go back and never recommend.

The hostess was absolutely rude! We didnt get seated for twenty minutes after our reservation. They did not explain or apologize. Every time i would try to say something, they would cut me off. The manager and the hostess all suck. Never going back here again.

We visited our last night in town. Was a little nervous considering the reviews. I wanted something other than seafood and a po boy.  I tried the chicken parmesan, it's not your regular chicken parmesan you get from an Italian restaurant. The chicken is great, nicely breaded and fried. I wish the cheese on top was browned, but that was fine. The sauce was very flavorful (spicy) with peppers and cajun seasoning. My husband got the gumbo, he enjoyed it.

My coworkers brought me here in hopes of finding me an eligible bachelor. There were zero eligible bachelors here. However, the food and drinks made up for that.

We ordered the Gouda cheese fondue for the three of us to pick at while we downed our drinks of choice - mine, the seasonal citrusy margarita. The drink was delicious, but not terribly strong considering the $11 price tag. The fondue easily fed the three of us. It was served with bread, apples, grapes, chicken, and veggies. We also opted in for the $8 up charge for steak - which was a huge rip off. Our steak came in the form of about 20 teeny, tiny chunks. So small I cannot fathom the effort it must have taken to cut it. Not worth an additional $8 by any stretch of the imagination.

Our server was kind and accommodating, until the restaurant began filling up. We went a couple of stretches of about 20 minutes without seeing her, and when we paid our bill, she was clearly flustered. (Not that I really blame her) Perhaps it was a lack of staffing. Who knows.

The crowd with a mix, but mostly 35+. There were no advertised happy hour specials (see $11 margarita), and our server did not mention any. It was a super classy vibe, and entrees run $25 and up. Not really my type of joint, but I'll be sure to give it another shot in the spring/ summer because they have a nice outdoor patio area.

Nice little spot; good vibe, good service, good food.  It can get a huge line quickly over the weekend.

Had the "Sis' Soul Food" omelet, quite tasty.

Took a star off because orange juice refill wasn't free; little surprised when I saw my bill.

Came for the gumbo. Disappointing no flavor and lukewarm. Tasted like a buffet. Asked them to heat it up and it came back colder. Then waitress said she had to microwave it. Must be famous for the worst gumbo.

check out THE SIGN on the lobby of the restaurant, 18% tips charged in advance fot tables over 7 people! we were 3 and anyway someone add us 18% TIP...the food was NASTY chimichangas wth very cheap ground beef...the server with no manners at all ask me...whats you drink men!??? terrible experience in a very dark unclean place.. WILL NOT COME BACK FOR SURE! one more thing...to the owner, never charge the tip in advance...its not our obligations you have to earn it!

Buffalo Shrimp, Cornbread with maple butter, Rotisserie chicken with mash and asparagus Excellent! The smoky flavor of the chicken with t he garlic in the mash was perfect. Their cornbread comes in a skillet and is to die for. We visited the National Harbor location. Perfect ambiance by the water with great food

Especially love coming here for happy hours, during fall or early spring, since they have such an amazing outdoor heating system and cool fire pits. Of course, stoli doli's are amazing, but can be dangerous. Always have friendly wait staff and food is good, and not terribly overpriced for being in the Promenade. Good times!
Service and wait staff were very slow and unorganized for a 12 o'clock lunch rush.  But once we got seated and served,  the food was very good.

Could be more vegetarian friendly, but still a great place.  Their brunch is one of the best around.  You get a free caramel roll and a free mimosa or bloody mary.  You can't beat that. Also has a great patio that is good for eating or just to meet some friends for drinks.

Been to this place many times.  A few weeks ago I had the meatloaf and mash potatoes and had very bad stomach cramps and had to rush to the bathroom as soon as I got home.. please for the love of god do not serve food past its expiration date.
