I know better than to visit most tourist places in the FQ but I was with a friend and her two kids and they picked this place for convenience. I won't be back. Get a to-go cup and keep walking. Food was not a representation of good Nola food.

I went here for a holiday dinner with my girlfriends and had a blast.  The restaurant is gorgeous.  Over and over we said that it looked like a restaurant in a Christmas movie with the beautiful fireplace, huge bar, dark wood, and the appropriate lighting.  

We immediately ordered their fondue which they brought out promptly.  We shared it between the four of us and each got a good amount of delectable hot cheese.  I couldn't tell what cheese was in it but it had a nice bold flavor.  It went well with the grapes, bread, apples and jerk chicken.  However the chicken wasn't very spicy despite it being "jerk" chicken and was slightly dry - good excuse to dip it into more cheese. 

I ordered the mushroom/roast chicken flatbread which had TRUFFLE OIL - YUM.  The waiter oddly asked me if having truffle oil on it was okay with me - CERTAINLY MY GOOD FELLOW!  (yes i said those exact words to him).  Who doesn't like truffle oil? Probably tiny children.  Anyways, the flatbread was truly a FLAT bread.  The crust is so thin and crunchy - loved it. Just the right amount of mushrooms, truffle oil, chicken and sun dried tomatoes.  Oh and to my delight, there were a ton of cut up, fresh basil all over it - z o m g.

My friends ordered the meatloaf, roast pork and italian flatbread.  Portions were huge and the roast pork - highly suggested.  It's probably the most tender pork I ever had.  

Overall, restaurant was beautiful, food was very good, service was decent - he forgot the wine but remembered to refill my club soda immediately..thus making me drink 3 club sodas in one sitting. Will definitely bring my parents here for a nice birthday/anniversary/something special dinner.  **p.s.  make reservations.  it gets really crowded in there**

Love coming here for appetizers and can usually make it a full meal. The Jerk Chicken Fondue is both tasty and fun when dining with a group of two or more. We tried the Philly Cheesesteak Flatbread (on special that night) and it was very good. My dining partner had the Ahi Tuna and loved it.  I highly recommend this place as the food is great and the  ambience is a mix of trendy hip and romantic.

@mike there wasn't a lot going on behind the scenes. I have a picture of the hostess and our server I do not. But we sat there for 30 min the server gave us rude and evil looks the 3 times she looked at us. Not once stopped by to ask us for drinks. 20 min into us waiting a couple sat down across from us the hosted came by minutes after asking if they had anyone come by for drinks. While we still wait waiting you can hear she had a attitude told the server "you have guest ummm waiting at table 17" as she rolled her eyes. Still another 10 min go by no one check in on us. Then the server helps the guest whom sat down after us we just walked out. This all took place 29 Feb 2016 around 1230. This is not the first time service was slightly slow but the first time our server apologize to us and gave a honest explanation which we noticed this time was totally different and highly disappointed.
Great friendly service and the remodel looks great, I think they forgot to paint all of the doors to the guest rooms? The shuttle service was great and very convenient, Victor was the best driver!!
Ate breakfast here on a Sunday morning.  Quality breakfast joint in the Quarter.  Will have to try this place for dinner next time.  One of my fav meals while in Nola.
Food was excellent. Staff was very friendly and courteous. Only reason I didn't give it 5 starts is the price. Very pricey.

I have had this place bookmarked for months, I am so sad this is my first visit to The Gallery.  I finally made my way from bookmarks to check-ins and I'm so glad I did.  I had an hour before my next appointment and really wanted a GOOD cup of coffee.  I decided now was my chance, so I stopped into The Gallery.  
I will say, parking was a nightmare at 11am so I can only imagine how bad it may be at a really busy time.  So I parked down the street and took a little walk to the shop.  I was greeted by the staff, who gave me the rundown of the dessert case.  I've never seen such beautiful pastries! I decided on the chocolate pillow. But wait, I came for coffee! They recommended the lavender pear latte. Both were amazing! 
I sat with this hazelnut, chocolate ganache deliciousness, and a slightly sweetened latte, with the sun coming in through this huge window, over the rustic decor and watched the kitchen staff make even more beautiful creations.  This is my happy place!
I'd like to know where to find the information about these cooking classes everyone keeps talking about, and I will definitely be back for brunch, or a celebration, or to make myself feel better after a rough day, or on a random Tuesday... You know, whenever the spirit moves me!
Food was great and waitress was nice... cock roaches were good company. Ew! Saw them in the hallway next to the kitchen as we were leaving.
A bit on the expensive side but repairs done were solid!

Love this little space--the long live-edge wood tables and benches, interspersed with bright butterfly covered upholstered chairs and an infinitely instagramable setting in general. That's for a start. Then you look at the lovely displays of unique desserts and sweeties. I'd seen pix of the macaroons. And while there weren't a ton of different flavors on offer--just three actually--they were REALLY good. Raspberry rose was so flavorful, and lovely. The staff is super friendly. I did have a little trouble finding it. I had pulled into the parking lot across the street where the donut place is, and happened to notice the tiny little sign pointing to the other side of the street, and it was in the back of a bunch of businesses facing each other--very cute little enclave. Parking was a bit challenging.

First time here and everything we had was outstanding. Definitely want to come back and eat outside it looked beautiful but there was a wait for outdoor seating so we went inside. The open concept kitchen is really neat and our waitress was awesome.

Well, I wish there was something good to say about our experience, but there's not. Miserable experience. Definitely understand it's Mardi Gras time, but the food was comparable to "slop". Extremely greasy, almost inedible all the way around from those in our group of 3. There could be absolutely nothing world famous to eat at this place. Also restrooms were backed up, with standing water in the sinks almost to the top. Top it all off with auto added gratuity. Will not return. Ever.

How should I begin .... I found a rather large roach in my first room . The second problem was the shuttle . I was attending a conference at the Omni ( should have stayed there ) . I spent hours waiting for the shuttle from clarion even though it's supposed to run on the 1/2 hour  . I called at one point 4 times and was told he was on his way . He in fact never showed . I was late for several events during my stay because of this . Third , the breakfast was nothing short of terrible . pLEASE don't stay here you will be very disappointed !!!!!!

There are so many good things to say about Gallery, I don't even know where to begin. I have the fortune of living five minutes away and it takes serious will-power not to stop on my drive home every day.

I've been on multiple occasions for brunch, afternoon macs and late night desserts and coffee. Everything -- and I mean everything -- is top notch.  There is not a bad option. The pastries are incredible, both in taste and presentation. The staff is friendly. We enjoy sitting at the bar and watching as the chefs perfect their next creation. The space is gorgeous, though it is very noisy when packed (which is often -- they are so good!) but worth dealing with the bustle. The patio is lovely when it's warm. I haven't even touched on the insane $1 Mac day they run every.single.Wednesday! The Gallery is easily one of my favorite locations in Indy.
Gumbo was only so-so. (If you're going to name a restaurant after a specific food, least make that dish well!) the only thing that made the meal enjoyable was the patio seating.

I'd give this place a full 4 stars but because of my work associates amusing reaction to the fact that the wine list doesn't include a single Italian wine I had to knock it down a notch. 

A solid (food) menu complete with several cuts of steak, buffalo shrimp, Australian sea bass, and... grilled meatloaf? While I thoroughly enjoyed my 12 oz prime rib (with blue cheese), another work friend ordered, that's right, the grilled meatloaf. 

Everyones meal was delivered on obscenely large plates but the taste fit the bill. I'd highly recommend the buffalo shrimp as an appetizer. The calamari was too soft, but the jalapeno peppers were a nice touch.

Redstones food is always consistent. I like going here in the summer so that I can sit outside... the inside is a little dark and closed in... which is great if that's the mood you are in for! Their bartenders are friendly, personable and male great drinks! Definitely a local staple.

Cute and trendy pastry shop. I got the opera cake, the chocolate pillow and the creme brulee. I took one star off because they don't have to-go dishes. You can buy the creme brulee ($8) and the dish ($6), but I didn't want to spend $14 on one dessert. They boxed up my creme brulee in parchment paper so I had a slightly tough time eating it. But everything I got was absolutely delicious!!! I would definitely come back....but will eat the creme brulee in the shop!

My new favorite brunch spot in Indy! I really appreciate the crepe combo, where they let you order two crepes any style, so you can get one hearty savory crepe and one light, sweet crepe to satisfy every brunch craving you came with. I also really enjoyed their latte, top notch espresso. Aaannnd, being a PASTRY shop, you better believe their baked stuff is incredible. Those flat cinnamon danish things?! Mmmmmmz.

Half price wine bottles on Sundays! Can't beat it. Just like the Terminator, I'll be back.
Awesome ambiance - came here for 'brunch' but Saturday has limited breakfast.  Ended up with lobster bisque; fig and prosciutto flatbread; french toast- all top marks!  Highly recommend
We stopped by this morning but they were really rude so we left. Turns out our tour guide told us not to even go there. So looks like turning around was a good thing.

Always enjoyed our visits and the great service since they opened. Went for a relaxing meal, sat right down and as the server brought our water I ended up soaked from the waist down. Couple of towels and I'm very sorry for your trouble was the way they handled the event. Fortunately this has not happened to us over many years but in the few instances I have to say no one has been as casual and nonchalant in addressing as we experienced this evening. We can walk to the location but doubt we'll be doing so again anytime soon. Sincerely- still drying out

My wife and I just got back from this restaurant - It earned itself a review. Not a negative or positive.....just different.

So here it goes -
When we entered, the decor was nice albeit dated. We we promptly seated by the young man at the front. The aroma smells like almost any Mexican restaurant - nothing offensive. After we sat, and our server had come to take our drink order then delivered it, I had to get my own silverware set from an adjacent table. Shortly after that, our first order - guacamole - arrived.

Now, I don't pretend to be a foodie or anything close to a connoisseur, but I must say the guacamole missed the mark. It was about 4oz, in a ramekin. It consisted of an avocado, and a very small amount of cilantro and onions. There flavor from the cilantro was nil and I think I found two pieces of the onion - also flavorless. Overall, the guacamole leaves much to be desired. There was no seasoning, lime, tomatoes, or even a traditional dish.  

The salsa was a disaster. Pace Picante tastes better. It was very similar to ketchup. It was a tomato paste with a little bit of onion and a smaller amount of cilantro. The reconstituted tomato paste flavor overtook all the other meager ingredients. Luckily there was dirty hot sauce bottles on the table so we could try to make it acceptable to our not so refined pallets. There was also no spice to it. I'm very serious when I say it was tomato paste. 

Then our meals were served! We were hoping against hope that our entrees would be good. My wife had a puzzled look on her face when she looked at her entree. The chicken enchilada of the combo A was a corn tortilla burrito about 1" wide and 5" long. While this is an acceptable size for somethings, it is unacceptable for a enchilada. The flour hard shell of the shrimp taco was decent - once some of the mound of cheese was removed. The flavor of both were described as "meh, it wasn't like, delicious or anything". The beans and rice on the side were mostly cheese. Speaking of which there was a lot of cheese on the plate. It glues everything on the plate down. While I love cheese, and I mean love, this wasn't the good cheese. It was "Cheese Food". Similar to what I used to eat in the military and wouldn't melt in the sun or microwave.  

My dinner was in the same ball park. My Burrito California (I've eaten A LOT of burritos in CA when I was stationed there) was not what they make there. In the picture on the menu, it had trimmings and cilantro on the top. The burrito I got was a long burrito with the steak falling out of both ends and just a pile of white sauce filling the plate - very boring. I was at least hoping the burrito would be packed with meat and tasty. The flavor was OK. I've had better on deployments. But what was a shocker was the amount of meat! There were 6 strips!!! Each of which was .5" x 2". While this might seem decent, the three strips coming out of the front and the back was all of the meat! The middle of the entire burrito was completely empty of meat! The lettuce was old and tasted like freezer burn and the vegetarian middle was just OK. Surprisingly, the prices were still on the average highish side of a Mexican restaurant - $8.50 for my blah burrito, $7.75 for my wife's tiny meal, and  the tiny baby guac was $4 - all before tax.

Overall, this place hit the mark, but it wasn't the mark they were hoping for I'm sure. Instead it was the mark on the list of DO NOT GO BACK TO. So, my wife and I will be off in search of a better Mexican restaurant. 

Do not go to this place unless you're expecting less then you were hoping for.

- on the plus side, the waitress was friendly and a good waitress.

WOW! hands down the worst restaurant experience I have encountered in many years. My culinary experience ranges from White Castle Hamburgers to The French Laundry in Napa, Ca. - Belagio's PICASSO in Las Vegas to Per Se in NYC. I was at a graduation party for my nephew (Thur 6/22/17 7:45 PM) with 22 other guest's. Well, I think they tried to bring out the food all at once and only had "1-2" cooks in the kitchen. The food delivered to the table was cold and only about 2-3 orders were luke warm at best. I don't think parties of 8 and above is their cup of tea. Of the three server's only one smiled, and I don't know who the blonde haired tall male server was but you think he was serving "lepers". We where never asked to refill or order more drinks, we weren't even asked to refill our water glasses. Even the Manager who came to the table to discuss the HOST's problem with receiving a "COLD COOKED STEAK" looked apathetic at best. I will email the GM and Corp office but I'm afraid I'll just get a "SORRY YOU HAD A BAD EXPERIENCE" reply. Any way, good luck at this place.

Servers very professional 
Food was good 
Creative dish ware 
Good flavors 
Portions are decent 
Drinks were good
Great food, fabulous atmosphere, professional service. Always busy, so reservations recommended.

My sisters and I were stopped by a host telling us how great this place was. His reason was that the lady in the kitchen had been cooking there for forty plus years. Well she must not have been working that night. I'm not a fan of spicy food but I really like well seasoned food. I ordered a shrimp Poboy and it was beyond bland and I paid extra for fries that were lukewarm at best. I'm not a big ketchup lover but to add flavor to a bland meal I found myself reaching for the bottle. My sisters had kinda like a sampler of traditional New Orleans classics. They tasted spice not seasoning. When the bill came the gratuity was added automatically. The service was OK and I would have tipped and no we were not a huge party but rather 3 people. So service was OK but food was bland and not worth price.

The desserts here are sooo goood! Never too sweet and they always switch it up. Service is always really good and the outside patio is really cute. Weds are dollar macarons. I love it here. I always come back and highly recommend it.

This was a great find for us! We had a big van so the free parking was great. They provided a free shuttle to downtown which was really easy! It took about 5 minutes to drive in. The rooms were spacious & clean. Breakfast was great too... Waffles, eggs, sausage, cereal, pastries!! Good value. We would stay here again.

The food here is pretty consistent - the drinks are expensive - but all-in-all, it's an ok dining experience.  I must comment that OUTSIDE, it is SO dark, the crossing the street to get to the parking is very dangerous, to say the least.  It is very hard to see the curb and traffic bumps in the road.  The other night I ordered the Kale/Brussels Sprout salad with chicken - the salad was fine - the chicken dry as dust.  I would have sent it back, but I was a guest of someone else and didn't want to create a scene.

I wish I had Yelp'ed this before we went here.... #1 - DO NOT order any salad from here.  #2 - If you expect any type of decent waitress/waiter service, turn around.  Our waitress forgot our bread, utensils, my salad dressing, etc.  And then when we informed her, she forgot to come back and I had to tell another waitress just to get decent service.  #3- The special with gumbo, jambalaya, shrimp, etc was not good... my boyfriend had it and it was a watered down mess.  #4 - Mimosas are not worth it.  They are just orange juice...  #5 - They tack on an 18% gratuity for all parties.  Two entrees with crappy service and two mimosas came out to $80 total for us.  Money NOT well spent - not sure why there was such a line to get in - I would never recommend this place to anyone!

Def a tourist trap, had the gumbo and shrimp po boy.  The gumbo was ok/average and needed more spice/heat.  The shrimp on the po boy was tasteless, they didn't even use salt in the batter.

Service was pretty good, but overall I wouldn't  recommend this restaurant.

Major in the breakfast area is helpful and adds a hint of fun to start the day. Both mornings he made us smile while we were at breakfast, The folks at the front desk were very helpful and nice as well.

What an awesome dinner out. Of course, it could be the company I was with, but regardless, the food and drinks were awesome. 

The wait was longer than estimated by the host stand, but we were so caught up with some red wine and the fireplace that the time flew by. When we were finally seated, we ordered some appetizers -- corn bread wedge and grilled wings. Oh man, both were so delish. I could have eaten a big plate of the corn bread with the butter for my meal. 

For dinner, I opted for the RedStone burger; my friend had the rigatoni bolognese. Both were so good and so perfect. The burger was exactly the way I like it cooked and the bacon was probably the best I've ever had. I sampled the rigatoni -- it had sausage in it, which gave it a nice flavor. 

For dessert, we shared the banana cream pie. To be honest, it was so big, I took most of it home. I should have known when they brought out a serving spoon with the plates that it was going to be big. It was so creamy and tasty with some caramel drizzled over it. It will be a great snack later tonight. 

Our server was excellent and attentive. He kept our drinks full and was able to make recommendations.

We stopped here more or less by accident and when I saw the Peruvian menu, I had to order from that.  I had the Arroz chaufa with beef.  The best fried rice ever.  And yes, it's very authentic to Peru - they had huge communities of Asians there dating all the way back to the early 1700s and there are over 9,000 Asian restaurants in Lima, Peru alone.  The portion was large and the amount of steak in this so much more than you would ever get in a Chinese restaurant plus it wasn't paper thin or tough. It was so good that withing about a week I drove down to Smyrna by myself to eat.  This time I got Lomo Saltado and then got an order of each - chicken and beef arroz chaufa.

Fantastic place for breakfast/brunch/lunch and I assume dinner. Have been here multiple times since opening and have always left very satisfied. Their tea and coffees are a nice selection. Typically I drink Americano but the pear lavender latte is a nice change. 

On our most recent visit we started with a charcuterie platter which had some fantastic meats. I had the smoked salmon which was fresh and the mixed green salad was tasty and seemed like a "I bet if we just throw this stuff together it will taste good." The eggs with bacon looked amazing at the table as well. 

Always happy to visit the GPS.

Tourist trap. VERY SLOW service. Poor food quality.

Made the mistake of coming here for brunch during Mardi Gras. The service is terrible and slow, I would recommend skipping just based on that. To add insult to injury, the food wasn't very good either - under seasoned, cold, cheap. 

Skip it.

Great Location! Free shuttles to and from downtown broadway st every half hour! Free parking lot.. big enough to park our truck and covered trailer! Free breakfast! This hotel has everything! Justin at the hotel bar mixed a pretty good drink and had some great suggestions for things to do "off the strip.. where the locals go!" And Raul the shuttle bus driver couldn't have been anymore friendly!!

Great place.  Upscale inside and out.  Cougar-haven.   Not an extensive menu, but the offerings are good, not pub-grub.  I had the sliced turkey on multi-grain and side of beans, both were awesome.  Was there Friday night, 9p-2a, and it was absolutely mobbed, so don't expect to sit right down if you go during the rush.

We went for breakfast.  The eggs creole was very good and the biscuits baked to perfection.  The lost bread is fantastic.   The restaurant is clean.  The hostess did an excellent job and quickly explained where the restrooms were!  My only complaint is the wait staff seemed a bit preoccupied.  It was not at all busy and he had to come back to the table because he forgot our order.  I waited forever for a water refill. The service was the slowest I had experienced in the quarter
Did a very good job fixing my iPhone broken screen.  You never would know it cracked!
Best place in Smyrna for cuisine costumer service they make you feel like family. Plus the very best Margaritas!!!!!
We came and had breakfast which was ok but nothing special.  The prices for what you get are ridiculous and not worth it.  If you have no other option it's fine but be ready to over pay.

Cameron (McCary?) was our waiter tonight, and he was fantastic! From recommendations to overall service, he made our first time at Redstone an experience to be repeated! Be sure to order the strawberry stoli doli!

This place is a joke. We live very close so the only pro is the convenience. They have officially screwed up our order THREE times and each time when we went back to have the order corrected they could not care less. Save yourselves the time and order from another restaurant. Anything with steak is extremely watery, the sauce is bland, the pizza is never fully cooked, and the people are the worst part.

Definitely a gun store. They do one thing and do it well. They have all sorts of guns and ammo. Good prices on the ammo too. Also if you add them on Facebook the owner Scott adds all his cool new deals. Highly recommend to any gun enthusiast.

I enjoyed stopping by the Palace Market which is near Frenchmen St with all the cool jazz clubs. The market vendors are very talented local individuals from Nola that sell custom jewelry, art, shirts, clothing, scents, and custom home items.  The items are unique and one of a kind. I also enjoyed the surrounding seating area of the market and its unique decor and music.  The palace market is free (no charge) to visit.  I would definitely recommend the Palace Market to others to browse and purchase Nola made items or  just unwind in the seating area of the market and people watch.
Just left from breakfast and I should have knew better when the restaurant was empty.  Please do not waste your time.  Not worth it.  Nice staff but horrible food.

I LOVE this place! The food is amazing. Buffalo Jumbo Shrimp... half or full order, you won't regret it. Talk about BIG shrimp! Lodge Cornbread with maple butter... just order the full skillet - leftovers are even better the next day for breakfast! Can't go wrong with the flatbreads (less the fig jam for moi). Sea Bass. Crab cakes. Braised short ribs. BBQ rotisserie chicken. Meatloaf. Sides - all delicious! Need to save room for dessert for sure!

Amazing seafood and good customer service.

I had the seafood platter for two, and it was more than enough to fill up two people. The stuffed crab was delicious and fried to perfection.

Thank you  Gumbo Pot for the free wine!!
 Fir the first time inhad the chance to eat the authentic Gumbo !!

The service is fast and they are per friendly;))

Wow. Just wow. Simply said, I am mad at myself for not getting here sooner. Went in on Sunday for brunch. Tried to make reservations in the AM, however, they were fully booked. So we took the gamble and went in and tried to get a table around 10:15am. They told us it would take 45mins, which we decided to wait for. They take your number adn there is a link that they send out that shows you where your spot is in the waitlist line. However, the 45 minutes was only 20 for us! So we got lucky. 

They did tell us while getting sat that our table had a reservation in 90minutes, but that would be plenty for us. 

I ordered the crepe entree - comes with two crepes, I did one savory and one sweet. Perfect combination and amount of food! The lemon curd was SO heavenly. 

They gave us cinnamon twist for the table that were amazing.

We also got a half price bottle of cava w/ OJ. It was a great experience and very tasty. I'll be back!

This is such a cute and relaxing place to have a pastry or a coffee.  I have a friend from Europe who ate here and said it was one of her favorite places due to the quality of the desserts, so I had to check it out. I hope they have a their fall outing again this year where all the shops open up and for an evening of fun. Great location in an old building right off the Monon

we came here for lunch and... 

I liked:
-fast (but bear in mind we did order gumbo), friendly and very attentive service
-the gumbo and smothered cabbage were delicious. 
-great location for those in the jackson square/french market area. 

i didn't particularly like:
-we ate out on the patio and a few times during the meal some bus boys shuffled past us with bags of garbage. maybe the back door was broken?? yes, it was trash. i watched them walk it to a near by dumpster.
-the shrimp in my gumbo wasn't deveined. i'm not talkin little poop veins... HUGE poop veins... ew. so, i sat there and deveined this suckers myself.

overall, i had a good experience and would go back!

I came here on Friday night with a friend and the place was jam-packed.  Lucky they take reservations because we were seated close to our reserved time.  While waiting, we went outside to have a seat at the bar.  Though the night was cold and rainy, Redstone's patio provided ample heating and a big awning so it was impossible to get wet. We ordered martinis and they packed a punch.  The only disturbing part of being outside were the cigar smokers we had to move away from.

Once seated, we were greeted immediately.
We chatted for a good half an hour before ordering and the server was so nice about it.  She didn't rush us or make us feel unwelcome.  
When we finally ordered I had the buffalo shrimp appetizer (OMG,TDF) followed by their signature house salad.  The food was excellent and I can't wait to go back.

Patched up, covered up flip hotel. It is old and not well updated. Strange substances everywhere on walls, floors, etc.. Bare minimum cleaning, lousy location.  I will choose a better chain next time. For $200/night I expect much better. Might as well have been an extended stay. Ghetto.

We've been customers since the place opened.  Love the outdoor patio & sometimes the food.  That's the problem with the place; INCONSISTENCY.   I always felt the prices were steep for the food and drink, but now either the food or the service or both can fail at one time or another.  My last meal was lunch.  I ordered the special, which was a pulled pork sandwich, but without the bun because I avoid wheat.  It came without the bun, but covered with french fried onions.  Sent it back, my husband finished his lunch while I waited and waited.  Huge plate came with a plop of pulled pork on it.  That's all.  No presentation, no fries, no cole slaw as promised.  The waiter said, "I don't know what's wrong with them."  I know what's wrong; they don't want my business.

We went to Redstone on a random Wednesday around 6 and were seated right away, but soon after the place filled up. The service could have been better and friendlier. We only got our waters refilled once....during dessert. It is also pretty pricy. 

We started by sharing a flatbread, and it was plenty for a shared plate. It was cut into 12 pieces and was very visually appealing. We got the fig and prosciutto one, and it was loaded with toppings and yummy goat cheese. We really enjoyed it. 

My boyfriend and I decided to split a few apps for our meal. We got the calamari & shrimp and it was delicious. Lightly breaded with a creamy sauce. It was a large portion, plenty to share. We also got the roasted Brussels sprouts and they were delicious. Slightly sweet, with a creamy aioli on top. It doesn't even feel like you're eating a vegetable! Lastly we had the jerk chicken fondue. We weren't sure what to expect, but the cheese came in a small pot with a candle under it, and it was surrounded by a good amount of yummy bread cubes, ripe grapes, sliced apples, and of course the jerk chicken. One of the best things about the dish was the unexpected hot peppers that came on the chicken. They were super spicy and were a great fresh way to cut the richness of the cheese. I would highly recommend all of these. The other members of our party got the fish special of the day and the pork chop. They were also both very happy with their meals. 

Before dessert, they brought out hot towels to clean your hands which was a nice touch. For dessert, we ordered the special dessert of the day (which was an Oreo cheese cake) and the chocolate chip cookie, which was humongous. You could easily share it between 4-6 people. Delicious!

Good hotel for bachelor/bachelorette parties. Bad for everything else, especially kids. Bad neighborhood at night. This is where all the party goers stay and are loud, creepy and disrespectful when they arrive from their Broadway adventures. One positive: they have a shuttle. Bad: Breakfast, housekeeping, interior(don't be fooled by their lobby look), pool is dirty, business center, security guard. We were taking to the security because of some curfew breakers and he proceeded to tell us he needed to do some cocain to wake up
Best French macaroons ever!!! This place is amazing! Great service and even better pastries!

Ate here recently. Amazing food. We had the chicken based on the recommendation from the waitress and we were not disappointed. She offered two different sauces, a house bbq and some thing else. The bbq was ok, the other one was great. Wish I remember what it was. I've also heard there salad with grilled chicken is good. Haven't tried that yet. 

We will definitely be back.

good food and atmosphere
I ordered grilled chicken on a salad and they added it no problem

Arrived at the restaurant around noon and we promptly seated to a table that might as well had been in Siberia. We had to hunt down a waiter to take our order after we had been setting for 10 minutes. The manager was away of this issue and never once made a trip to our table to apologize. 

The food was ok but because of the poor customer we will not be going back.
Great place to eat. Staff was friendly and very accommodating. We had a party of 11 and they made us all feel very welcome. We will return.
I didn't eat here but I stopped by before every tour for a drink  (Tour meeting place is right outside) and Kobe bartender behind the bar was VERY pleasant every time and makes great hurricanes.

Our second time here and quite a disappointment. Although our server was delightful, the experience left a lot to be desired. Taste wise the plates were acceptable, but nothing to write home about. Portion wise, the plates were less than expected. I ordered a filet with a baked potato, served with grilled summer veggies. My dinner date, a halibut special touted by the waiter as a must have. My plate was ok, with the steak prepared as requested, but the potato tasted as though it had been under a heat lamp for a few hours. My date's halibut however, was a total disappointment. It was, at best, 5 oz. and not what was expected at both the price point or the waiter's acclaim. When I brought this issue to the waiter'a attention, I did have a what I believe to have been a manager ask, "how did your meal taste," but no one addressed the portion question posed, and given that she didn't identify herself, I am not sure who she was. Red Stone is not an inexpensive meal and so I didn't expect a portion befitting a tapas restaurant. The waiter obviously felt bad, as he verbalized he felt as though our issue had not been resolved. He comped us a glass of wine, but he was right, we left
With a bad taste in out mouths feeling our +$100 meal was not a good buy. Spend your money at Flemings or Bone Fish, right down the road.

Food is ok, but don't sit outside to eat. I've been here five times,  and the flies are ridiculous!!! You would think for $16.00 an appetizer they would spend something on mitigating the fly problem on a the deck. Overpriced and mediocre service. (Waited until my 5th visit to comment)..
P.S. tipped 40%, twice, and bartender didn't remember me! Not worth the trip.

A great little BYOB Italian restaurant. The food comes in large portions with very reasonable prices. 

The staff is very friendly.

Definitely have the cannoli for dessert.

I was reluctant to go with a larger national name exterminator as I've had negative results in the past with quality and customer service from such companies.  However, I did some research and polled the neighborhood for recommendations for Tucson's lower east side.  Truly Nolen kept coming up.  Now I see why.  It's personal caring and customer service from reps like Adi, who follow up and check in to ensure the comfort and quality is ensured.   Who take the time to answer questions and explain all process.  These days, that is very hard to find.  Field techs like Tony who are thorough and professional.   

I am very satisfied with TN.
Another great spot near the 54th and College corner. For both brunch and just pastries/coffee, you feel like you're eating in a European Cafe!

I would give this hotel 3 1/2 stars but the customer service blew me away. Shout out to the lovely Terri (Front Desk Wonder Woman)! I had a horrible experience at another hotel the day before and checked in here. They changed my opinion of Nashville and I'm glad I have another night.

Visited this restaurant this evening for my birthday. Enjoyed the fried calamari and shrimp appetizer and the rack of ribs. The food was delicious and the peanut butter dessert was awesome. I will visit this restaurant again. Service was great!!

I was so excited to hear that sobro brought in a new pastry cafe! This space is perfect for get togethers or if you just want to come in and relax over a cup of coffee and a pastry. The owner was friendly (even when I had to call her twice for directions) and took the time to explain the different items on their menu. I had to resist buying everything off the page, everything sounds so scrumptious! I ordered six French macarons and had to resist the urge not to eat all six by myself and save some for my husband. I can't wait to come back and try some more pastries! Apparently they offer French macaron making classes as well.

If I could give them 10 stars, I would. We've been looking for a good groomer to take our dog to and each time it was a swing and a miss. But our search has finally come to an end! These guys are hands down the best groomer! They really know their products and what they're doing. We will only go to poochinis from now on. Thank you guys for taking care of our dog.

My first visit to this place was for brunch last week. Let.me.tell.you.something. This is one of my new favorite spots. I went with friends and we sat at the bar area right in front of the kitchen. The kitchen system is a well oiled machine. Each person was excellent mixing, cooking and prepping the food. All the food was made fresh and when it touched my tongue, I damn near fell off my chair! I don't remember what I ordered but you can see the pics. The mimosas were great and bottle prices were even better. I'll def be back next Sunday for another round of good food, good atmosphere, good cooking and good convo. 

I didn't have room for dessert but will be sure to leave from this week. And let me mention, the location is in the cut, which I like.

Great first visit! Everything was pretty grand starting from the staff to the appetizer and entrees. We started off with the cast iron skillet corn bread which was soooo scrumptious that had a golden brown crust on top and the edges. I had to stop myself to save room for my beef wellington. It was my first and this one was sure to please. If you like medium rare to medium doneness, it's worth a try. Our server was congenial and attentive. He was awesome which made our experience top notch. My hubby had the filet with grilled mushrooms which were good but for a side that was priced $7, the portion was a bit skimpy. The filet quality was above average, some parts chewy, some parts tender. In all, it was a charming visit and we'll be going back soon. P.S. their garlic mash is on the dense side if you're into that kind of stuff.

All their food is amazing, just one thing i want to pick on, that us the moose crape. It is very sweet but if they add a little salt it would be better because it would balance out the sweetness with salty. Over all every this was amazing. 10/10.
The bbq shrimp, smothered cabbage with red beans and rice was awesome!!! #halfsweethalflemonade  #fullandhappy
it is the worst restaurant i never ever have in life time. the plates are dirty and the food is suck.

Wednesday $1 macaron Day is a great way to get acclimated to this charming, rustic bakery and restaurant. The macarons are fresh and amazing! The rotating flavors are worth a try every time! 

The staff is always friendly, even when they're busy. If you're sitting down, make sure you get their attention. I've gone unnoticed a couple of times. The food was worth the wait.

Macarons! Macarons! Macarons! Vive la macarons!

Also vive la for...

1. funky interior. love the mismatched tables and chairs.
2. outdoor seating
3. tucked away location makes for a quiet place for conversation
4. all pastries and sweets are to die for! Opera cake well executed.
5. the macarons are up to par. I am very, very picky about these and have eaten them all over the world.
6. delightful tea selection
7. also serves booze. I don't really drink like mimosas so this is a good spot to venture to if someone else feels the need to imbibe.
8. yummy savory eats too, mostly meats/sandwiches from Smoking Goose.

Basically this is my favorite coffee/pastry shop to work remotely from. I can spread out at a table order a few small tasty items and work in peace. 

One note: sitting in front of the large window can get kind of toasty with the sun shining down.

We had a 7:30 reservation and were seated promptly. Waitress was friendly. Drinks came very slowly. Caesar salad had sooo much dressing in it we could hardly eat it. They offered a shrimp scampi special and it had hot pepper flakes in it. I ordered it but without the hot pepper flakes. The waitress said the sauce is pre-made so it can't be made without the pepper flakes. I've never heard of pre-making a scampi sauce so I ordered something else. We ordered baked potatoes and all our dinners came out with mashed potatoes. We told the waitress and she took them back. The manager came over and told us they were out of baked potatoes which is why we were given mashed. Food was way overpriced and it was just ok. We won't go back.
The food is great!!! The atmosphere is great!!! My only problem with this place is that the food and drinks are way overpriced. But other than that it was a great dinner.
Food was OK.  Good Gumbo.  BUT very pricey and service wasn't anything amazing.   Weak drinks.  Next time I will be willing to brave lines in other places  as this was definitely a disappointment.

This place is one of our favorites and worth our 45 minute drive to go there.
Everything from the food to the service is done right and top notch...The do charge you for this experience vs other chains,but I consider the expense worth the experience.We never had a dish we didn`t like (ahi appetizer is OMG terrific).
The wait staff always friendly & helpful and quick with a refill. This is a real deal experience from food to comfort and my only complaint is that there isn`t one closer to me.
Note-the banana cream pie,isn`t really. It`s more of a banana pudding with some crumbles..It`s ok,not $9ok and not a pie.

Had an awesome brunch at The Gumbo Pot. We sat on the patio and it catches an amazing breeze off the water. I had the Eggs Sardou and it was so delicious! The skillet potatoes and biscuit were great too. I would have given 5 stars but I do feel that it's a tad over priced. I guess location has a lot to do with pricing but I definitely enjoyed it!

We stopped in here for lunch today because it was near the steamboat we were going to take after lunch.  We both had gumbo - me seafood and hubby duck and andouille.  His was too salty and mine was a-ok with a bit of a kick.  It certainly wasn't the best I had in New Orleans, but I did finish the bowl.  The service was friendly and the location convenient.

As a venue for event like Indy Gourmet's Cheese War it was great. But as for the macarons we're less than happy. The last batch we got some were stale/hard. Others are soft. What is the consistency supposed to be? Can box at least have a date of manufacture so we can see if it is simply older stock that goes rock hard and inedible?

The brunch menu on the weekends doesn't really give a whole lot of selection. You have your crepes, your omelets, and you can order the pastries. Which is fine. A few items that are really good is better than dozens of items that are average.

I was feeling basic so I went with a bacon and cheese omelet. I probably should've gone with the crepe because the omelet was good and hot, but nothing really stood it out from an omelet I could have gotten in dozens of breakfast places around town.

The plain croissant was hot, warm, and on point. This ranks up there with my other favorite croissant from Illinois Street Food Emporium. As close to France as you'll get in Indiana.

There was also a dark chocolate pastry cake-like item that I had that I greatly enjoyed but the name escapes me.

Now, about the service:

I was asked several times if I was ready to have my plate picked up when it clearly still had food on it and I was still eating. This happened at least twice. I don't know if they were running out of plates or they were trying to rush us out the door, but this seemed odd.

Also, the music. It is loud! Really loud! Admittedly, this is essentially one big room so this isn't meant for a quiet meal. But the music was really loud and it never really got turned down and really ruins the experience if you aren't into loud music during a weekend afternoon meal.

I'd love to come back here for some pastries to go as that is where they excel at. But I don't know if I'll be dining in anytime soon.

My favorite spot for a Friday night happy hour = Redstone's fondue appetizer and glasses of Riesling. With that said, all those days of stressing at work are meaningless. 

*Outdoor seating is high in demand but the inside seating is just as fun

I've been trying to figure out why I absolutely ADORE The Gallery Pastry Shop.  l had the hardest time pinpointing why.  Was it the eclectic decor?  The open kitchen where Chef Ben and his team create flawless pastries that have the magical power to transport me back to the pristine places I visited in Paris?  The variety of picture-perfect confectionery you don't see at any other sweets shop in Indy?  The almost too-pretty-to-eat macarons?  The recent schedule of pastry classes that's up on Facebook, so I can learn the secrets of the sugar master?

All of these things are contributing factors, no doubt, but with a little reflection, I think it all boils down to the fact that The Gallery is elegant but not pretentious.  It's a place that welcomes my palate as well as my curiosity as to how beautiful foods are made.  It's a space that feels approachable, and better yet, impresses the hell out of me.

I look forward to continue being wowed by the jaw-dropping confections coming out of The Gallery's kitchen, and hopefully I'll acquire some newfound pastry skills by the end of the year!

Phenomenal. This place is one of those types of places that makes me feel like I am in some cosmopolitan metropolis on vacation eating gourmet desserts. Then I remind myself that I am in Indianapolis, IN, and it's enough to make me smile right then and there. The concept is cool. Patrons can take a long hard look at the dessert options on display, order, and take a seat for full table service. They have wine, beer, cocktails, tea, and coffee for any upper, downer, or inbetweener one's heart desires to complement their dessert. The atmosphere is great. It has a somewhat rustic feeling to it, and the chefs are hard at work making their craft in an open concept kitchen. The desserts themselves are some of my favorites in the city. They have something for everyone. They have many unique offerings that are served nowhere else in the city. If you like sweets at all, come experience gallery pastry shop!

Horrible experience. In town visiting friends and family.  Waitress was terrible from the start. Tried to explain the specials and kept saying "um", every other word. Highly recommended the short ribs, saying they were fantastic! Group of 8 of us for dinner. Two guests ordered short ribs and two filet mignon steaks, medium. Other 4 ordered fish, including myself. When food served, first steak was so bloody, it looked like seared ahi tuna. Second steak served was comparable to beef jerky. Both steaks were sent back. Waitress was rude and asked what we wanted to do. Then waitress came back after other food was delivered and said sorry to the two guests that ordered short ribs. She said they were now sold out!! So, half of our party had food, the other half did not. My wasabi crusted tuna was terrible. Taste free and the rice was undercooked. However the vegetables were over cooked. The 2 new steaks were still not cooked correctly and weren't brought out until everyone else was finished. After empty plates scattered the table 20 minutes after we were done, my wife had to request the waitress to clear off the plates!!  Then the manager comes over and apologizes for one of the steaks not being correct. I brought up that two steaks were messed up, and the manager just said, oh sorry. Nothing was ever said about the "sold out" short ribs that were never delivered. Overall, it was a horrible experience including over priced food, horrible service, and a bland, terribly cooked meal all around. I would never recommend this place to anyone!  I could understand if one aspect of dinner wasn't up to par, but 50% of the food was terrible and 100% of the service was horrible. Steer clear!

Don't waste your time or money here. One star is very generous here.

Boudin balls were good.
Calamari was ok.
Gumbo was terrible.
Po-Boy was average.

We mentioned to the server the quality of the food and asked for something else. They would not remove a simple pot of gumbo from the bill. Hindsight, probably should have been more persistent, but not in the mood to battle.

I give them a 
C+ for appetizers 
D- for gumbo and poboy
F for service. They didn't even care.

Too bad, location is great. But buyer beware, you order it, you own it.

3 stars in generous....I wasn't impress with the service nor the food...their weren't 10 people in the place at the time we visited and service was bad....so I cant imagine how it is when they are busy....

I'll pass

Sheffield's has a great product line and excellent customer service.  I recently purchased an engagement ring for my fiancé.  Christine was very helpful and took the time to show me a variety of ring styles and cuts.  When everything was picked out I gave her the date when I needed it by.  A week later my time table changed and I needed the ring sooner than expected.  I called in and spoke with Eric Sheffield, explaining to him my dilemma.  He said he would see what he could do.  Not more than an hour later he called back and assured me the ring would arrive in time.  I went down and picked it up 2 days later and it was even more spectacular than I had imagined.  She loves the ring btw, and is already looking at a Ritani wedding band to compliment it.

Thanks to Eric and Christine for coming through in a pinch.  We will be back when it's time for the next big purchase!

Easter brunch was fantastic! Great selection of buffet dishes for breakfast and lunch. Awesome coffee and deserts. Delicious cocktails rounded the meal out. The food and drinks were only outdone by the excellent service and friendly staff. Thank you for making Easter Sunday special!  I think we may have started a family tradition for Easter morning after church.

This place falls well short of the price tag and the service is deplorable. Multiple times guests from my party were reminded to "get out of the way" of servers including myself (caught behind other folks trying to transit the restaurant). My party of 4 was brought 3 of 4 requested waters and drink orders took excessively long but we were more than welcome to the $95+ tab for 3 gumbo bowls and an order of the breaded eggplant.
This place was simply not worth the effort and cost, do yourself a favor and walk across the street for a muffuletta.

I'm so late posting a review of this place, but here it goes.  Indy you are so lucky to have this charming and delicious shop in your city.  I visited this shop a couple of times this past summer when I was visiting and I was thoroughly impressed.  Chef knows what he's doing.   Wow.  His pastries were as delicious as anything I had in Paris.  My fingers are crossed that all y'all support this business so that it's still there next time I'm in town.  Selfish?  Sure. But Indy needs to embrace and support these kinds of businesses if it ever wants to be considered a city worth visiting and get to the next level.

Brunch was OK.  Nice Environment, but really food didn't match it.

Perhaps their business plan involved a nice environment with little quality in food.  

The brunch was still a decent deal, and I wasn't really disappointed, just expected more as I grew up in Mtown before the expansion of shopping.

Nothing beat Olga's or Chammps.  (Olga's doesn't exist anymore i'm told :( )

I stopped in a little while ago to check it out as a potential birthday brunch location. I talked to a few staff members, and they were extremely helpful with providing menu options, seating, rain plan, etc. Chef Ben caught me eyeballing him from across the room, and invited me and my bro & sis to come watch him. Don't mind if I do! We all had a lengthy chat while we watched him work and then he asked what we ordered. We told him we were gonna get macarons, but they were sold out. He stopped what he was doing and made macarons for us! Perfect!

Birthday brunch day was lovely! We sat outside and the service was wonderful. We ordered from the menu, and soon the table was filled with custom made omelets and crepes. They brought them out as they were ready, and I didn't hear any complaints from anyone. I wanted mimosas for the table, and our server suggested we make them since bottles of champagne (and wine) are 1/2 price on Sundays. Everything was delicious including the vanilla cake! 

The only downside was the heat! I love outdoor seating, but a few table umbrellas wouldn't hurt out there. 

Such a lovely place with several options. Stop in for wine or coffee, pick up sweet treats to go, weekend brunch, and much more.
Very disappointed flavor wise. The service was good but the food was very bland and mediocre. Cannot believe a place in downtown New Orleans had a flavor proboe

Love love love this place!  There is so much I like that it's hard to choose.  Definately flatbread for an appetiser but need to make sure to save room for the Banana Cream Pie.  Best cornbread on earth!

It was okay. Many angry people when we arrived. Not a good sign. We had to wait for our room...arrived hour past posted check in. No hair dryer in room. It appeared clean but cheap. Location was convenient when driving but you wouldn't want to walk off the site. Pretty sketchy urban area.

Ambiance. Fantastic. I wouldn't say any of the chairs look like you would want to stay awhile but the place is beautiful. Great staff. Food-I got the lavender and the chocolate pillow and a chocolate croissant-all three met expectations but I wouldn't necessarily rush back or recommend. However because it was **TIP** Wednesday macrons were a dollar so I took some to go.  Here's the thing. I am a lover of food but I have never enjoyed a macron. I keep trying out of pure curiosity. These were exquisite!  Take me back. Every Wednesday!!

These guys are smart and fast and reasonably priced! Had a minor problem after installing new hard drive on my laptop. They fixed it in minutes without a charge and were even pleasant! I have told everyone there IS a great place for tech repairs and support.

The atmosphere was dark and very cramped.  The wife and I went with another couple and got stuck in a booth.  Each side of the booth was barely big enough for 2 people, felt like I was crammed in there (and we are average size people).  The white queso was pretty good and the beer was priced well... That was about all it had going for it..

The wife had the fajitas, which were just ok.  I had the enchiladas and wasn't impressed, the chicken wasn't all that great and the rest was nothing to write home about.  We will try a couple other mexican places before returning here..

This was my first trip to Nashville and I want betty happy to find out that almost every hotel wad already full so we wouldn't be ankle to stay on the main strip. I was then pleasantly surprised by the clarion. They have shuttles running downtown every hour and when we did take a cab it was only 5 0r 6 dollars to each main spot. Our rooms are nice and clean and the front desk people were very helpful. Is worth it to pay for the cheap can rides instead of paying a few hundred extra to stay on the strip.
Ehh....  Good location.  Ordinary fare and service.
Everything was great! Food, service all 5 star, one of the better establishments for brunch.

Not what it used to be. We've been dining here for about 6 years. I would've given it a 5 star rating at one point. The last few times I've gone (maybe 3 times in the past 7 months), the food has been pretty mediocre (not hot enough, burnt crap cakes, salad drowning in dressing), which is unacceptable for the price point. Service is still friendly. I hope they get it together again.

Yesterday we went for brunch.  It was delicious.  One of the best brunches I've had in awhile.  Smoked salmon omelet was fantastic.  Husband loved the Breakfast Sliders.  The hash browns were amazing...could die happy having had them.  Only disappointment was the mimosa, really weak.  Didn't even seem to have any champagne at all.  Next time I'm going out for brunch, this is the only place I want to go.

My husband and I both love sports and so since we were in Indy I know we'd go there. Admission to the museum is $5/adult which isn't bad. 

The museum is small and really focused on male sports which is annoying but aligns with how the NCAA operates (Title IX works in theory but not in practice). 

Anyway, on the first floor there have interactive screens where you can take quizzes on each of the sports. As well, there is information, memorabilia and a small theater where you can watch a 5 minute film. 

On the second floor they have more hands on things. Such as a basketball court, simulation, etc. My husband had a blast on the second floor. He would have stayed a lot longer had he been alone! 

Given how big the NCAA is, I just expected it to be bigger and have more information. However, but for only $5 it's a nice way to spend an hour!

Service is very good. We arrived early in the morning after driving overnight from Chicago. 
Front desk was very courteous and check us in and let us sleep. 5 stars for her.

Hotel is not too far from downtown but not walkable. Just park your car and uber to town and walk around to save the ridiculous downtown parking fees. 

If you don't care about aesthetic of the surrounding, this hotel sitting between industrial zones will do just fine. Or else pay more money in downtown. 

Room is clean, water pressure not too strong, beds are big and comfy, the building is definitely old but just recently updated the decor, walls are per thin, can hear everything next door and down the hallway. But we were so tired and didn't care. Breakfast is mediocre. But all the staff are very good and courteous.  

Great staff all around!
Had the chance to visit this place during our night and thought it was okay. It's kind of a smaller night market with a lot of art.

One word.  Don't!   Never again, Gumbo Pot.  We were dragged into this place by friends because it was handy.  Let me say this first.  The waiter spouted off the menu so fast we couldn't understand him, and I'm from the south.  He was rude, didn't have time for a question, and acted like he was doing us a favor just being there.  He was too busy to refill our drinks, but had plenty of time to chat with fellow wait staff and the bartender.  He was a large guy, and I guess he thought he would be intimidating, because when he brought the bill, he had written at the bottom, as he tapped it with his pen to draw my attention "suggested tip $25"   He actually hovered over my shoulder and I wrote $15 on the tip line he actually said "$15" out loud.  This was actually 15% percent of the tab, which including drinks came to right at $100.  I came unglued and told him it was $15 dollars more than what he deserved.  RUDE, INTIMIDATING, THUG!!!

Now on to the food.  I expected as much from a "mall restaurant"  But honestly, how do you operate a restaurant in NOLA, call it the Gumbo Pot, and do such a bad job on the gumbo?  You would think something would have at least rubbed off on your taste and cooking ability as a chef, but sadly this isn't so.  The Gumbo Ya Ya was thin, watery, and hastily thrown together. And, just as my wife's Jambalaya, served over Minute Rice!  SACRILEGE!  Come on...take the time to cook some good rice.  You are charging top dollar for this stuff.  My wife is from Louisiana and know's her way around the kitchen.  We eat Cajun cooking at least 3 times a month.  This ain't Cajun cooking!

I was buying our friends lunch and they each had a drink and seafood salad.  Our bill came to just over $100.  Looking back at the menu..I'm still not sure how it came to that.  For what we had, and how bad it was, the price was exorbitant.  "

Lastly, let me add my rant against separate checks.  As with most restaurants in NOLA, they don't like to do them.  They don't do them here either.  If you are paying this much for a meal, there is no excuse for not providing separate checks for you customers. If you wish to add a gratuity for a large party, so be it.  But separate checks in this day and age is inexcusable.
Great food, especially chicken and steak dishes. Drinks are healthy. But can be very busy especially on weekends.

Great food. Great service. Rather pricey. 

We arrived at the end of a busy lunch period. We both ordered the Open Face Turkey Sandwich. Wood fired rotisserie cooked turkey with homemade cornbread dressing, mashed potatoes and homemade cranberry sauce. Excellent. The chocolate cake came with vanilla ice cream and a delicious homemade whipped cream. The portion was large enough for THREE people, and very good. 

My only complaint would be that they charge extra for coffee with dessert even though we had cold drinks with our meal. Many restaurants allow coffee to be viewed as a refill. Their loss...I didn't order a dessert since I would have had to pay another $2 for coffee. Turns out the cake was more than enough for the both of us.
This place has a cool decor, is very unique, and the food was great.  They stay packed until late in the evening as it is a very popular spot.
Good upscale bar & grill. Some damn good flat breads.

Had the jambalaya.  It was delicious.  It had good heat and the jumbo shrimp was huge.  Our waiter was very friendly and did a great job explaining the menu.  He even gave us a serving of bread pudding on the house.

Be very careful!! Poor customer service..Two computers came out with some sort of issue that was not there in the first place. They wouldn't make good on the second one because "they weren't making money on it and had to run a business"  YUP that was the response.. Do Not Suggest These People.!

We had a late breakfast so it was 2pm before we were hungry and wanted something small.  My plan was to get a bowl of gumbo, but my very smart wife suggested we get an appetizer and a cup of soup.  Great Idea!!!

We had an order of crab cake remoulaude with their ya ya gumbo.  The 2 crab cakes were pretty large with a spicy remoulaude sauce - very good.  Then a sizable cup of gumbo that was full of shrimp, fish and sausage.  Can't beet eating like this.

The place just keeps  going down the hill. The service is unbelievably slow. It took 30 minutes to get just appetizers. After we were done with appetizers, it took 20 more minutes to get main dishes. The place was busy and packed but that's not an excuse for bad and slow service. The food was not bad. But I did find hair in my buffalo wings.  It's a real shame because the restaurant looks nice and it used to be a great place.

Carlos Serrato arrived from Truly Nolan to service my home. He did a great job as all those who have done work for me from this company have always done. I addition he suggested a fix for a problem that I have had in the past with a ceiling heater which will take total care of the problem. I appreciated his service and his kindness. Thanks Carlos and also Paul Grijalva - both have provided excellent service.

Let me thank Kelly for providing us with excellent customer service!! You rock!! 
The food is normally better tasting, the mac & cheese was undercooked and had to be returned and the ribs whole tender weren't appetizing. The cornbread was yummmny !! 
The atmosphere is romantic low lighting but slightly loud. The prices are mild expensive.  Would recommend this location only!!

The menu here is great. The dishes are unique, presentation is very nice and everything is delicious. The ambiance is nice too. The tables have an intimate feel and the inside is usually dimly lit. The patio out back is a great spot to hang out and socialize during warmer weather and there's a nice sized bar in the middle of the restaurant. The staff are very friendly although the customers that dine here are often pretty pretentious, creating a somewhat snobby environment. Prices are a bit high even though Redstone aims to be more upscale but they aren't outrageous for what you get. I highly recommend coming here for their Sunday brunches, which are excellent and make up for this. Brunches include a free coffee or mimosa (provided you're of legal drinking age), a free desert equivalent to a giant cinnamon roll and fantastic meal options to choose from. All of this will only cost you about $15 a plate on average.

There should be a negative sign in front of the one star I'm given this place. The service was crappy as hell. There is plenty of good places to eat around here so please skip this one. Boooooooooooooo!

The food is very mediocre. You could taste the tomato sauce in the gumbo and jambalaya. Zatarans is sooooooooooo much better. Very disappointed in the quality.  And then the bathrooms were absolutely horrible.  Doesn't close,  seat was broken,  just filthy.  Never coming here again!  Just like the others said,  NEVER EAT HERE.  DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME OR YOUR MONEY.

A truly horrible business, I called and was told if I arrived and dropped it off Friday it would be done Saturday. I drove there and had them look at the Ipad. They Examined it and I specifically asked if it would be done on Saturday, Their answer yes, they would call/ On Saturday afternoon I called to ask. I recognized the repair agent was lying and he said he overextended himself. I sent him an email requesting when it would be done. He called later and said tocome pick it up as he refused to fix it. I told him Fine I would see him in court, he could argue in my territory. he made a contract and decided to screw me. I went back up to pick up my ipad/ Will be filing this week, take your chances but based on other persons experiences dont trust them. I could not have been more ecplicit/ This is a ripoff agency and they don't care. This is what is known as Consumer frqud in New Jersey. Glad to sue them. Arrogant and insolent.

We really like the place, my wife ended up there one cold Friday evening, after our fiasco at the other "Gumbo Shop" on 630 Saint Peter St (see my review)  around the corner. Here at Gumbo pot, the dining room was large and spacious, nicely decorated with ample space to stretch your legs or open a menu, which was extensive and rich in various local dishes.  The staff nice and friendly and our server a tall African american  man who was  very attentive to our requests. We ordered the Creole Seafood Combo (creole shrimp, Crawfish Etouffe, Jambalaya), Gumbo and other stuff, all very tasty and filling. By the way we noticed we were the only white customers in this restaurant  tasting creole food, that says something. It takes one to know which place is worth the trip. Definitely we  will come back next time we are in town.
Way overpriced! $5.25 for one little scoop? I could go to shoprite and buy a whole bag of cookie dough for under $4.00.  I don't see this location lasting long.

Stopped in here while we waited for our steamboat trip, as it's by the dock. Had a bowl of gumbo, since, well, that's supposedly what they're famous for. It was mediocre at best. I've had better at most places. And prices were just right for a tourist zone, way too expensive. Definitely not worth it.

Dinner on a Monday night.  Inside was a bit stuffy and dark, patio was available and comfortable with a breeze from the north.

Made my own selections from the menu, a bowl of Chicken Andouille gumbo and a side of jambalaya.  In a word, disappointing.  The flavors in the gumbo base were just off, there were a few chunks of flesh floating around that didn't seem to belong in the dish, I didn't finish the bowl.  The jambalaya was a bit better, but pretty bland.  The Louisiana hot sauce from the bottle didn't help, do they water it down?  And minus one-half star for serving a domestic draft from a tap that imparts a dirty-socks flavor to beer that is supposed to have almost no taste at all.

As I was finishing, the couple next to me sat down, looked at the menu, complained about the prices and got up and left.  Good for them.  Rounding this one down to 2 stars, won't make my regular rotation.  Go across the street to Cafe Maspero for better and cheaper food.

Not even installed yet and I'm livid. First scheduled day and they were a no call/no show. It was raining so I didn't expect an install, but to not call at all and force us to call multiple times until someone picked up is inexcusable. Now today I was told an install team would be out at 10am and another no call/no show. After multiple calls/voicemail and an email to the owner, the owner finally called back. His response? They put on his calendar the install was today (which was what was communicated to us), but put tomorrow on the installers calendar. Needless to say, i expect tomorrow to happen and you better believe that I will do a walkthrough to verify the fence is to my expectation of quality or it will be redone. I have no faith in this company's accountability or customer service and to still pay full price for because it's a "service" is a joke. So far the service isn't worth it.

*update* installers were late, but their work was incredible. Solid fence. The customer service level could be overhauled, but their installers are quality, even with the language barrier. Doesn't completely fix the experience, but the two guys that came out helped improve it.

HORRIBLE!!!! Do not do it! We went in without checking reviews first and regret it BIG time. We spent $90 for NOTHING. I took one bite of my almost $18 jambalaya and could tell it was old and there was something wrong with it. I made my kids stop eating ($10 each plate) paid and left. Service SUCKS as well. Avoid a very bad experience and feeling robbed and just DON'T go here.

At first I was hesitant.... 

The 30 something suburban crowd was intimidating compared to the adolescent faces of my five other friends. However the waitresses were nice about our age ( a true rarity ). After a 25 minute wait, she asked if we wanted to sit on the patio. What a mistake! Not only did we sit by the bar and stared down by tipsy soccer moms, our waiter was rude, and an obnoxious band was playing so loud we could barely hear ourselves. 

We then asked we could move and the waiter seemed more than pleased. He told us it would take another 25 mins but we were too lazy to leave and go somewhere else. So when we arrived back to the  main dining room, we were immediately seated.

At that moment my dining experience completely changed. Our waitress, although she said she was new, was comfortable, cheery, and pleasing to talk to. She told us her favorites and even some items that were not on the menu. She even convinced us all to get the raspberry lemonade when we all ordered water at our last table. 

Unfortunately, none of us ordered the steak, but a pizza type dish served on a platform. The pizza was ultimately delicious, but since 3 of us had ordered it, the table was awkwardly crowded.

OVERALL food was great and service depended on who you had. Don't sit on the patio because they might play the theme song to jeopardy as entertainment and just remember to ask for items off the menu.

The food was typical Italian - good and affordable. Had dinner there one weekday night and service was fine. Took co-workers there for lunch on a Friday afternoon and waited 45 minutes for our food. Had to gobble it and run to keep the boss happy. Our waitress was bonkers over too many people in the place. They need more help there. The owner had cooks from the back out front in the restaurant to clean up tables, etc. Not a very polished operation. They do a good business because of location and BYOB. They wouldn't make it in S. Philly.

Terrible. Got the Creole combo and nothing was seasoned. Shrimp creole and crawfish etouffee were absolutely inedible and jambalaya was barely tolerable. Wife got the gumbo and ate maybe half just because she was hungry. Try anywhere else in the quarter and you'll be better off...

This place was horrible. First, the service was terrible. Our first waitress took drink orders after we sat for 10 minutes waiting, and then forgot about us, so someone else took over. The food was tasteless and overpriced. The gumbo was soupy with very little meat. The jambalaya, supposedly a specialty, was a complete joke, I took two bites and pushed it aside.....two big lumps of bland rice over tomato sauce, sprinkled with 4 small chunks of andouille sausage, a few pieces of stringy chicken, and 3 small shrimp. My wife had a salad that clearly looked like the bottom of the bowl lettuce.

Used to come here once per week. Unfortunately that will stop now. While eating with my family tonight a big cockroach/Waterbug jumped on my shoulder. That is hands down the easiest way to ruin your dinner.

Where should I start? First waiter was rude and inattentive, asked if there are refills on soft drinks and he said no with an attitude, then we asked for ice water and he never did come back to check on us.  Someone else brought the water, so we decided to leave because we could see this was not going to be a great experience.  Looked at the menu and they are over priced so if you are thinking of going here please don't, try Deanie's and get a great meal for the money.  Wish I could rate them 0 star.

Not sure what everyone else's issue is but..... This food is pretty darn good if I must say so myself.  The seafood gumbo is on point and filled with shrimp. The catfish is AMAZING.  It is clean, fresh and tasty to add. My reasoning for 4 stars is of course pricing,  but I know the prices are based on location. The waitress, Linda was extremely friendly and was very attentive. Overall great experience....
They came same day and stayed as long as it took to get the job done.  Professional and polite.

Where do I begin. I will start with the good stuff. The staff is super friendly and the bartenders are very tentative, thank you Justin and Jordan.

The shuttle service is great, if you have Raul! He makes sure everyone gets to where they are going when they need to be there. Other than that, the shuttle service is terrible. And it's about a 2 mile/30 minute walk to downtown.

Housekeeping is friendly but does not do a great job. The first night they came in and took our towels and did not replace. Daily they would come in and kind of straighten up the room. The vacuums that are used are very out dated, not even sure what it is picking up. The sheets were never changed (we stayed 5 nights). And we specifically left trash on the floor to see if it was picked up and it was not. 

The room itself is very outdated. The one curtain did not open. The door to get in was loose and would make noise every time someone else opened or closed their doors. We had a leak near the window dripping into the room. I am sure that the room has mold. The bathroom door was peeling yellow paint. It is very dusty and dirty. Dead flies and bugs behind the chairs and curtains. When you took a shower your water would go from hot to cold to hot to cold. 

You can hear everything! You can hear your neighbors conversations. 

The continental breakfast the first morning we were here (Monday) was terrible. The food was severely picked over and not replaced. The tables for sitting was a hot mess. The coffee ran out. Staff was not tentative to make sure everything was readily still available. We got to breakfast at 8:45 so there was still and hour and 15 minutes left. I will say as the week went on the breakfast got better. The eggs looked sketchy though. 

The ice machines are only on even floors and we were lucky if they worked.   

Overall we were super disappointed in this hotel. I do not recommend staying here especially for the price you pay.

First time using them. We bought a new 40" TV and needed it installed. We already had the mount from the last unit and needed the new one to get hung. I found HelloTech from Google search and booked an appointment online. Very easy. Was able to book a time the next day. The tech was on time very friendly and knowledgeable. We were quoted 79.00 and that is what we payed. No games or extra charges. Highly recommend them from our experience.

The hotel was in a good location and a mile from downtown.   We had a family reunion and 29 of us stayed at this hotel.  The hotel was very clean.  They have one shuttle that holds 11 people at a time and that gets booked up very quickly.   Plan ahead if you have dinner plans and want to use their free shuttle service.   If you use Uber downtown it's only $4.00 so nothing to complain about.   Considering the hotel price with the free breakfast, free parking, swimming pool, free internet and free shuttle service you can't beat this location or hotel.    I would definitely stay here again!

Finally made it to The Gallery for $1 macaron day. Absolutely amazing! Lemon macarons were adorable and perfectly flavored. Can't wait to go back and enjoy more treats as soon as possible! They also offer brunch and half priced bottles on Sunday's! More reason to run over!

This place always delivers and I had another outstanding meal with an old friend last night. The braised short rib entree was nothing short of incredible. The meat was so tender it easily pulled apart effortlessly with a fork. There was almost no fat to be found and the broth and vegetables were a perfect compliment. When I return, I'll order this dish again without hesitation. Kudos to our waitress for recommending it because it was worth every penny.  May even dream about it I'm not exaggerating. The people with me enjoyed their entrees as well. The auju served with the French dip had an onion based flavor that complimented the sandwich well. Outstanding service, quality, presentation and atmosphere. After about 830 the lights get dimmed and the older crowd at the bar starts looking for their one night only soul mate- very entertaining to watch. Make a reservation, this place gets packed for good reason.

Red stone, I can honestly say that I have never had a bad experience. The last visit I had with Red Stone American Grill was for my anniversary and needless to say, everything went to absolutely perfect! Our server just started working there, he joked around, and conversed, lightened the mood and the timing with our drinks, appetizer, dinner and dessert were precise! We loved it so much we talked to the GM to brag about our wonderful night! I would definitely recommend this great place to dine, for ANY occasion!

There's a reason I've been coming here for ten years.
