NCAA makes billions of dollars a year off of student Athletes. So I had high expectations of a quality museum. I was expecting to see a lot of old jerseys/equipment and history of significant events in college athletics.

What did I find? A bunch of plain facts that anyone can Google about every sport with a boring sporting equipment next to the fact. They had displays of each sport and a lack worthy touch screen display that was a bit flunky to use.

The admission to the museum is cheap at $5.

The museum itself is extremely small and feel unfinished to me. For the size of the building, I was expecting something similar to Indiana State Museum across the street. Instead I found a partitioned off museum that was 1/8th of the actual size of the building in comparison to the rest of it.

Upstairs of the museum was more interactive if you want to call it that. The only part that was a full sized video game setup where you get to throw a football, soccer, baseball, etc.. against a cloth wall with the game projected on it. That was probably the only entertaining part.

There was a basketball court to play on, but it was used by many young youths. Most of the things displayed were mounted and really weren't interactive. They have a tennis ball machine that hits the window constantly to let you know how hard of a hit of a tennis ball is. Great... I'm entertained.

Save your 5 dollars and spend it elsewhere. This place isn't worth your time. I was hoping to see a bunch of different schools with information about them and jerseys of famous well accomplished athletes. Instead you get information about the sport which you already know. 

I mean if you're going to have a museum about college sports you should be displaying known famous college athletes that make the sport popular. Instead I got a bunch of googled facts.

I really tried to stretch my time there, but you can walk through and read everything in about 20 minutes. 20 minutes??? I saw people that left before I did and there were only about 2-3 other groups at the time.

Pathetic NCAA. You should be really ashamed. If it's called Hall of Champions.... display the Champions... You didn't. What a misleading name.

John and Matt were both great! They took their time and explained everything in terms I could understand. Matt also sat in my Yukon with me and hooked up my phone, went over all of the many systems and never seemed in a rush. Just a great couple of guys to deal with and I am very happy with my new Yukon.

If I could I would give you a ZERO on service alone! The food was good but the service is absolutely horrible. I will never be back at this establishment! I would rather go to Camino Real or Margarita house, at least when I go there I know the service will be good or at least decent. The girl was rude, never greeted us. Nor did she take or drink order. Thirty minutes after being sat we had to approach her.. I would also not let someone with her attitude run my customers off.

Being from the area I sometimes like to try the touristy places. Usually always a mistake and this was one. We sat outside and the service was mediocre. But I'm all about the food anyways so let's get to that... I had the crabmeat remaloude appetizer. The dish came out with two crab cakes and the sauce on the side. The sauce was pretty much straight horseradish. The taste was unbearably strong. Not sure where they got their recipe but even google could provide a better sauce than that. I don't care what they called it that was not remoulade sauce. Then I ordered a shrimp poyboy which isn't too hard to screw up but the shrimp was so bland.

Basically I recommend you walk across the street to Johnnys Poyboys. Over half the price and much much more tasty!
Worst place I've ever eaten In NOLA. Gumbo & Red beans and rice was watery and not seasoned whatsoever. *gag*

This is my favorite chain taco place! I used to go here all the time when I lived in Metairie. 

The service tends to vary given the fact it has a high turnover rate among the employees. Overall I have been satisfied with the service though, Its usually quick and friendly. 

The food at this Taco Bell is pretty good. I love Dorito's Locos Tacos! The tacos,burritos,Nachos are good too. I still haven't tried the pizza here yet.

The best feature to this taco bell is that it has a Pizza Hut attached. My favorite taco and pizza chain rolled into one, Pure Heaven!

In short great tex mex classic and they sell pizza!

Confused by the low ratings here. I went alone and had a phenomenal time, which to me is the tell of a great experience. The exhibits were very easy to navigate and the content was very interesting. There were two short films, one on the history of the NCAA and college athletics which was extremely well done. The other was a comical one about the importance of being both a student and an athlete. The interactive exhibits were also enjoyable both trivia and the displays. I am sure some people will say the interactive displays are "interactive light" , I would agree somewhat ... the rifle, the diving and the fencing exhibit don't even allow for motion. The snow boarding and basketball were plenty for me though. The hall of fame display was also designed to allow you to search by school. Being able to find the University of Pittsburgh without reading through every year was great! The staff helped me take pics of myself since I was alone and I got a long sleeve t shirt and key chain deal for $20! I'm not sure how far people expect $5 to go nowadays but this was the most bang I've ever gotten for my buck at a museum! Plan to return with friends if back in the area.

Water leak in room which made carpet wet and room smell of mildew, electric outlet not working, bath drain not draining   causing standing water in shower. We advised the front desk and they offered to move us but never noted accounted or returned call, maintenance was call and he confirmed our issues and did nothing about it. Maintenance advised he would come back but did not return. We had a concert so we could not wait around for the issue to be fixed. When we retured our issues were never addressed after talking to the front desk they offered to comp 1 night of our stay and but didn't note our account about that either. Now on my last day I am having to wait for a manager to resolve this issue. I can not recommend the property if you are visiting Nashville.
The BEST brunch place in Indianapolis, best service, best food. It doesn't get much better than gallery

I live in Baton Rouge so I go to NOLA pretty often. I should have known better than to get caught in a tourist trap!! Food was way over priced and it wasn't any good. Chef Boyardee could put together better Louisiana style food. Save yourself a bad experience and walk into the Quarter to eat. Every place I've eaten in the Quarter is better than this place!

I was lucky enough to find out about the Gallery Pastry Shop at a Goose the Market Meat sale.  I purchased some Banana Nut bread and Macaroons and we were extremity impressed. My wife is a a Banana nut Bread Nut and said it was the best she ever had. 
Based on my first impressions of the Gallery pastry shop we decided to go there for brunch with my daughter and her hubby.  We did call ahead seating (recommended) and the wait was less than expected. 
This is not just a pastry shop, the a great for Brunch.  We started out with Mimosas (Half priced bottles of wine on Sunday and served with Blood Orange juice.  
We were all extremely pleased with our choices 
'merica | two eggs your style, smoking goose jowl bacon, hash browns $10; 2 crepes | choose your fillings $15; brioche toast | mixed berry compote $4.
The stars of the meal were the hash browns; smoking goose jowl bacon - Oh my that was good; and the make your own crepes- Banana fosters!  I french Canadian went there upon my recommendation and said the crepes were fixed perfectly as crepes should be fixed (not the American version)
We will go back soon and are very happy we found this place.  The service was good, but when my friend went they did not have great service

Unorganized. Unprepared. Overpriced. We made reservation for 8 people, and called & left message 4 hours before reservation to ensure we were sat together. When we got there, we waited over an hour to be seated, and we had to be split across 2 tables. There were 2 tables next to each other, but they refused to allow us to sit there without explanation so we were nowhere near each other. Decorations were not much of an experience. There was a 60 second long haunted house that was ok. They were out of most food items. Our server didn't enter our order correctly. Food was mediocre and kinda strange. The cheese quesadilla was 80% tomato with about 8 small beans. The blood bad drink was good, but thats about it.

My family and I went to the restaurant to celebrate my daughter's birthday. Before we went, we called the restaurant to see what time was their last seating, and no one told us we needed reservations. Upon arrival, they were not very accommodating because they said we didn't have reservations and it was hard to seat a party of five without a reservation due to COVID. Understood! We waited around, got seated on their covered patio. The waitress was very rude to us. When we got our dinners, everything was burnt. From the quinoa to the burger. Our waitress never even came back to see how we were doing. We asked for the check,  paid our bill and left. We didn't complain because we didn't want to create a scene. We have eaten at Redstone many times and never had an issue. We will not visit this location anymore!!! It's important to train your wait staff because they could create a bad impression for a great restaurant.

The Buffalo Shrimp appetizer was absolutely the most amazing thing - definitely get it.  Giant shrimp, with blue cheese sauce and chunks of blue cheese.  They were not too spicy but had a ton of flavor. I got the smoked chicken pasta which was probably one of the best pastas I have ever had.  Lovely atmosphere and delish!

I had never heard of this place until my friends decided on brunching there. Brunch is super popular, so I recommend reservations. Parking is limited and tight. Service was great!

The whole place was comfy and cute with mismatched tables/chairs as well as bar seating, where you could watch the magic happen as they prepared your food.

What I ordered:
Blood orange mimosa - $5 on Saturdays, blood orange was recommended by our server and I was so pleased
Plain Croissant - buttery, flaky perfection
2 crepes (bacon/gouda and chorizo/cheddar) - both were so great, chorizo wasn't greasy or too spicy, bacon was meaty and savory
I had a taste of my friend's almond creme croissant, and it was beyond delicious

The sweet treats at the pastry bar looked too good to eat. I wanted to order one of each edible piece of art and some macaroons, but I resisted temptation. I'm regretting that decision, but I'll be back for those babies!

We had the most incredible engagement ring and diamond shopping experience. The staff were all kind, helpful, fun, patient, and applied absolutely no pressure. I will shop there from here on out. Best jewelry buying experience I have ever had. And the best part? The prices! Wow! Thank you all so much for making us laugh and cry!

This was a bit of a surprising disappointment. Located in the midst of White River State Park, the NCAA has some large and elegant buildings that house their National Headquarters and Museum. Inside the museum, or "Hall of Champions" there is very little to see. There is a circular room with some fine plaques.  The first floor has a small screen video to watch about each NCAA sport. The second floor has some interactive sports games, but they are a bit dated and mostly for one person at a time. There is a basketball half court to take a few three pointers. That's about it. Too understated in memorabilia or anything that I found truly engaging, I would not go again nor recommend.

I honestly don't get this place- Seriously what is this??
I know what a Bakery is- Donuts, Cupcakes, Breads, everything that makes the world worth living. I know what a Coffee Shop is- Lattes, Coffee, teas- Also essential for life. I know great Brunch places- share some bacon and I will be yours forever. But the Gallery Pastry Shop fits in no where! The decor is drop dead gorgeous: Patios, Chandeliers, Rustic mixed with modern. I would live there in a second. However when I look at the menu I see drinks, desserts, and 3 food options- a charcuterie board, croissant sandwich or quiche, I was very disappointed because looking through trust yelp I saw great looking crepes and omelets. Well now I realize where we went wrong- Brunch is served on the WEEKENDS ONLY! After coming to terms with my limited options, I went for a Croissant Charcuterie sandwhich and after ordering I learned that they were out of Croissants and it would be 30 minutes before the fresh ones where ready. While I did have limited time, it was the only thing on the menu that was real food, so I waited excited to experience a fresh warm flaky croissant. I'm not quite sure what was happening in the kitchen but when the food came out it was anything but warm- major let down.
I won't be back for food- but if I ever have an odd sweet tooth I would consider swing in for a drink and Chocolate pillow.

Went in for lunch and loved it! The vegetarian quiche was incredible and my friend ordered a ham and beer cheese croissant and loved it as well! The chocolate pillow is a must try, alongside the lemon tart and classic eclair for dessert. The macarons are very tasty as well and one of the cheaper places to buy them in Indy.

Loved this spot! No idea they offered a full menu of brunch and lunch options! 

Sit indoor at cute tables or outside next to the life size chess game. They are taking precautions during COVID and had excellent service. 

I ordered the 2 egg hash - over easy eggs with vegetables and hashbrowns - very hearty and Delish. Friend ordered the vegetable quiche and she enjoyed as well. Husband got the croissant and gravy and absolutely loved it. 

Will definitely be back!

The only late night market for artists we have ever seems. They open until 1 am on weekends. Isn't it insane. Vendors started coming as it goes night and night. Small area only but between the most famous atmosphere on historic Frenchmen street. Art lovers gonna love this late night show of art.
Taylor the Tech was great!  He called to arrange a time, was pleasant, polite, knowledgeable, thorough, and most importantly, fixed the network problem I was having.

First and foremost, this restaurant does not sell alcohol. The host informed us of this as soon as we arrived so if that's a deal breaker this is not the place for you.
The service was quick and friendly. My son had chicken and sausage gumbo with French bread which he loved. I had the ya ya Gumbo and it was flavorful with plenty of shrimp. My husband had the red beans and rice with sausage and he enjoyed it also. I have read some poor reviews but personally had a good meal. The restaurant was quiet and clean and the prices were high but all in all about the average for the area.

These guys are rocking it! They have pivoted their entire business model during the pandemic to not only accommodate their (well deserved) fan following, but also to support as much of their amazing staff as they can (hey and they are taking some burden off the system). 

It's sad to see the poor reviews of an amazing place because some people were inconvenienced to wait outside for a pick up on Mother's Day, during a pandemic... meanwhile their staff was serving guests as best they could on a holiday during a pandemic - certainly their first day of this volume with a totally new system in place, all while trying to keep guests and staff safe during this time. A little grace and patience are due. 

Keep up the great work! We can't wait for an in person brunch, soon. Love you guys!

As a cookie dough lover I've been searching for a spot like this on yelp but was disappointed that most were located in Nyc which is a hike but I was happy when I saw this spot one day while walking through the mall. They have a large selection of flavors ranging from sugar cookie, red velvet, caramel, regular choc chip cookie dough to even brownie batter. They stopped me after 3 samples. Hey I'm not trying to freeload I am just a new customer trying to see what I'm about to get myself into. The samples are about the size of a penny so cmon. Be a little more friendly. For the small size, you can only get one flavor which I didn't like. You have to get medium or large if you want to combine flavors which is way too big. After eating about half of my small sized cup of cookie dough I got tired of it and have not craved more since. Thank god I did not take that spontaneous drive all the way to NYC for this

I love Gallery. It's such a fun little experience. The brunch is amazing. I get so excited to come here with people who haven't been before! If you can, I also recommend checking out their baking classes. They are pricey but who cares. You get booze while you learn some tips and tricks!! They also send you a recipe home. Support small business!

We were referred to this place by a friend when looking for a spot for a sendoff brunch for our daughter who we were dropping off at Butler.  It's 9 minutes from campus.  Wow.  I don't write too many Yelp reviews but WOW.  It was perfect.  Has a gorgeous outdoor seating area.  Really felt safe.  They took our temp as we walked in.  But the story here is the food.  Everything that everyone ordered was amazing.  I got the eggs over hash and I will never get anything else.  My wife (and daughter) got the breakfast at Tiffany's omelette that neither would share and they always share.  Our son got the croissant breakfast sandwich that he loved.  Really special place that we will surely go to every time we go back to visit.

This place was recommended by one of the local for that "real" New Orleans dining experience. We went in for breakfast, and were intrigued by the menu. Maybe it was just a bad day for them... but the service wasn't very welcoming. Can't say it was bad, but t wasn't good either. The food was tasty, but we had to send it back because the shrimp weren't clean. If 'm going to spend 14 bucks on a plate...at least clean the shrimp! Right? We decided on meatless dishes that were kinda tasty.But can't say I would go back..not to mention our waitress who decided to add her gratuity on the heck for her lackluster service. Wasn't a good impression at all for me. I see other people had better experiences...

This is my favorite places in SoBro. my friend and myself only frequent the gallery together. It's located near Good Morning Mama's. We try to go on Wednesday's as that's when they run their french macaroon special. They serve delicious brunch and offer cooking classes. The cooking classes fill up almost as soon as they release the dates online. I love the calm atmosphere of this small pastry shop. You can sit inside or out. the outside has a life size chess board for you to play. The staff is generally friendly and helpful. their french macaroons are perfect .  They have an open concept kitchen so you can watch them prepare everything from breakfast to their wonderful desserts.

Highly recommended this company !! 
From beginning to end everything went as planned and was on schedule . Communication was the best I have had dealing with any company in a very long time and our fence turned out beautiful. Thanks guys for a job very well done .

The Gallery Pastry Shop is my absolute favorite place in all of Indy. The environment is so aesthetically pleasing, I love to just sit and watch them make beautiful food in the kitchen. The macarons are to die for! Lemon and raspberry are my favorites. The employees are so kind and fun. I highly recommend visiting on the reg.

Fun place to go get delicious pastries. Everyone was very nice. Small space and was busy so be okay with close quarters. Love that they serve drinks along with food and pastries. It's cool that you can see them working in the kitchen as well.

$1 macarons on Wednesdays.   That's all you need to know.   It seems like every pastry chef worth their finishing salt is making macarons these days and I'm a fan of the trend.    At the Gallery Pastry Shop they have turned the process into something Henry Ford would be proud of.   The young apprentices here put them out by the hundred and customers can't get enough.   Have a seat at the counter to watch them work (and if you're lucky, they might toss you a couple of the imperfect ones). 

There's also an extensive beer list and a limited non-pastry menu so you can have a full meal here.   The breakfast menu looks amazing so I'll have to come back some morning to try that....but still remember to leave room for dessert.
My all time favorite place in Indy! The desserts are absolutely delicious!!! Their croissants with their raspberry compote is the best!!!

Really enjoyed the coffee, pastries and ambience. The staff were super nice and attentive. My husband really liked the home potatoes mixed with grilled onions. 

My chi coffee was on point. It was made with coconut almond milk, cinnamon and nutmeg. Simply delish

Had brunch here today...and it was AH-mazing. From the mimosa spread to the 2-egg hash to the amazing pasteries - you literally can't go wrong. Not to mention awesome ambiance and great wait staff. All around a good time. Experience it for yourself.

I recently had the pleasure of working with Eric Sheffield to create an incredible custom ring. Erick took the time to listen to me about how special this piece would be to me (we would be resetting an heirloom family treasure). He listened again when I described the style of ring I wanted to have designed. Together we envisioned exactly the ring of my dreams!! Then Covid happened! Once Eric was able to reopen, he contacted me right away to continue with my project. My ring was delivered today and seeing it literally brought tears to my eyes! It is perfect, original & spectacular! We are already planning our next custom project! Thank you Eric for working with me to create a once in a lifetime extraordinary ring!

Metro Fence did a great job, fence looks dead level and straight. They finished in one day and I expected it to take longer because of the length and corners they had to do, so I am a happy customer and will use them again soon for another project!

Been coming here for years! I've always loved this restaurant, especially for weekend brunch. I am a little sad that they changed up their ingredients in jerk chicken fondue dish, as well as a few other items on their menu, but overall, great food, service and environment. It is family friendly, however it is also a great place for a date night, or to even just hangout at the bar for happy hour or weekends.

Love, love, love this place. The croissants are so light and flaky, They melt in your mouth.  The macarons are delicate with full flavor. All of the pastries have been wonderful. The staff has always been very nice.

Nice location just across the river from downtown, formerly King of the Road. Nice breakfast buffet and free shuttle to and from downtown so you do not have to pay the outrageous parking rates. Best shower I have had in a while with lots of water pressure. Room was clean and comfortable.

My go to place at least once a week. I have NEVER had a bad experience. Food is always great and fast. On the weekends they serve Peruvian food as well and it is amazing. Friendliest staff out of all the restaurants in Smyrna.

Great food and service is the best. Love the Peruvian cuisine never tasted it before but had a recommendation from the waiter and it was amazing now it all I get.  Please continue to support this fine restaurant during this time

Gallery Pastry Shop is my number one brunch spot in Indy. They have a small, but well curated menu that anyone could find something they like on. Always get the hashbrowns!! Service is always great, and I have been back way too many times to count.

New Orleans has so many great souvenirs that just seem to find their way to you, so I don't usually go shopping on purpose but my friend wanted to poke around so I followed. That's when I found my Tina Butts. 

Tina, from Bob's Burgers. Just a little portrait but it really speaks to me, me and Tina have a lot in common and I'd like to think that when she's older we'd be good friends. 

Joe Badon is the artist and he only asked a very reasonable $15 for this beauty. The shading on the butts is really nice!

This place is a 10/10. My family and I have been coming here for years and it beats any place in town. The service is great and fast. The food is always bomb and never let us down! They have trivia nights as well as live music sometimes. At the end of every night we choose to go, they always have York Peppermint patties, or little Mexican treats you can perchase for a super low price. Love this place and will continue to come here anytime I'm craving Mexican!

We have been Eric's clients for many years. He always makes it a pleasure
to "part with your money". Kidding.  Makes visiting Sheffield's an enjoyable experience.

Had a reservation and upon arrival, they took us to sit in an old toy factory that they rented out to expand their seating. The first seating area was well decorated, had a the pastry bar, and smelled wonderful like fresh omelettes. They made little effort to do anything to their extra seating area: blank random colored walls, smelled like a moldy mattress, cold, and random chairs/tables. On top of that, they had plastic bins on the floor right next to our table where servers would place all the dirty dishes from the room. Never offered to refill my coffee. Served "roasted" and "sauteed" vegetables cold. Mixed up the drinks/food on our separate checks. Food wasn't bad but our first impression mostly ruined our meal. Recommend asking for specific seating if you make a reservation. I'm sure it would have been better in the other space.
This place blows. The waitress couldn't even understand what we ordered and brought us eggs. Also friend had a hair in his food, gross. On top of all that you can't even split checks boooooo

We've been taking our small, mixed-breed dog to Poochini's for almost two years and have been very pleased. No matter which of the groomers works on her, she always looks great. She's never been a fan of being bathed and groomed, but everyone at Poochini's is always kind and patient with her. During snowbird season they do tend to be quite busy, so it's best to book an appointment well in advance.

Out of all the restaurants available in the Promenade, Redstone is definitely the best. While I did come in with low expectations, I was pleasantly surprised and then some at the food and the offerings here. I like that they use OpenTable, and me and a friend were able to get a 7pm reservation just a couple days beforehand. We were seated right away, even though I noticed that the restaurant was super crowded. 

Redstone offers your typical American fare, but they do a better job than your average chain restaurant. The menu items are slightly more unique, but still familiar for the less adventurous eaters. I ordered the rotisserie chicken pizza with truffle oil and my friend had the burger, both of which were delicious and executed very well. We also ordered the cornbread, which was a huge portion, even though it was just a "side." I also definitely want to try that buffalo shrimp in the future, which seems to be a specialty. Overall, it's a little pricier than most the other restaurants in the area, but can easily be forgiven, since the quality is also a little higher. Waiter was pretty attentive and refilled our drinks fairly promptly. 

Given that I'm an OpenTable junkie, next time I'm looking for an American restaurant in the area, Redstone will definitely be at the top of my list for a reservation. Even though there's a lot of stigma with chain restaurants, Redstone definitely bucks that trend, and I'll definitely be back.

When I brought in my firearms for resale, they treated my business, top-notch.

They did a quick assessment, filed all the neccessary paperwork and provided me with great resale value on the items that I brought in.

Wait, not only was the offer top-notch, but the customer service was great, as well. 

If I was ever looking to purchase firearms resale, they have won my business, by conduct and merit.

Highly recommend.

This spot is a must go! I'be been here about 4 times and I like it more and more every time I go. The food is delicious and the pastries are even better. The environment is chill and also mesmerizing to watch the open kitchen. The specials are real and worth every cent! It's a staple in my brunch cycle of restaurants!

Needed to find a place with good chips and salsa. Saw the reviews and figured I would give it a try. The salsa is the best I've had since moving to Tennessee. I ordered the fajita nachos. They were very good. A little too much lettuce for my liking but I picked around. The server was great and attentive. I think I may have found my new go to restaurant for Mexican food!
Great food! Great outdoor space! Friendly bar tenders! The outdoor space and fire pit make it possible to enjoy on cool fall nights. My kids love their menu too!

Macarons.... delicious, melt in your mouth macarons.... and I never even thought I'd be a macaron fan. We've bought the macarons twice now and were here for Cheese Wars, so I can't comment on the food at this point, other than those amazing macarons. The owners are really nice and clearly extremely talented. It's a really sweet spot (if you pardon the pun) with a lovely patio. Can't wait to do brunch here!

We booked the Gallery for our wedding desserts. The desserts were pretty good, however, communication and follow-through with the event coordinator, Casey, were poor. Response times are very long, which leads to more stress. Additionally, after emails discussing set up, the GM of my venue just found the desserts left in the delivery packages on our dessert table on our wedding day. Would absolutely not recommend this vendor for events, but the cafe is pretty nice!

He was on-time, knowledgeable, courteous and said we could ask for him if we want to use service in the future. Jose was great and a great representative for Hellotech. Took care of our needs quickly. Got same day appointment and paid 1/3 of what I had previously paid using the Geek Squad. Could not be happier.
Redstone Rip-off: Place charges you about twice or three times what's its worth. Foods not terrible, but nothing to rave about.

Every pastry at gallery is a work of art. I see your hesitation; we've all been there- you see a beautifully decorated cookie some place and give it a nibble only to find you were tricked! It tastes like chalk. This will NOT happen to you at Gallery Pastry Shop. I have yet to find anything that tastes below the rating of "unconsciously groan inducing". 

Also, their brunch food is just as good as their macarons! 

Gallery has lovely outdoor seating with umbrellas. They were very strict on Covid precautions and mask policies (hooray!).

Pre-covid, my favorite spot was inside watching the pastry chefs work!

Service excellent, food presentation great. The food was very bland and weak with flavor. I have had omelets at many restaurants for different prices that were waaaay better. The taste should reflect the cost.  My Chorizo omelet with a teaspoon of protein and a ton of onions was horrible. Looked good tasted like eggs and onions

Perfect spot for brunch, such a great vibe!! Loved sitting at the pastry bar and watching them work so diligently making all the goodies for the day! The staff was extremely friendly and helpful and the food was 10/10! I got the breakfast at Tiffany's and milk and honey crepe. Can't wait to go back!

What a gem!!

I stepped inside this extremely hip, cool market last night and was blown away by how creative some of the merchandise was. So many beautiful handmade creations - from jewelry to artwork to these cool art lamps made of vintage or antique musical instruments and NOLA reclaimed bargeboard - I loved everything!  And every vendor that I met was so personable.  I was encouraged to pick up items for a closer look. Where else do you get that?'

And it was so clean! 

I'm impressed and can't wait to stop by again.

I definitely think this is an essential Indianapolis museum, and a must-visit if you've never been. Like other people have said in other reviews, the NCAA Hall of Champions is not as big as some of the other surrounding museums, but it packs a lot into a small space. 

We visited on one of the free days they offer throughout the year. (It's free on MLK Day with a donation of a canned good, on Presidents Day and on Smithsonian Museum Day.) I'm not sure if they always schedule an activity on their free days, but when we visited on Presidents Day, we were greeted with an activity card and told that if we visited all five activity stations, we would earn a medal. I was totally just going to take my kids around and see what we could see, but having this fun activity to do (with a prize at the end!) really made us pay closer attention to all of the different exhibits in the museum. 

There is a room where you can shoot baskets, a digital soccer goal where you can kick a ball and try to get it past a goalie, a station where you can check to see how high you can jump, and much more. There are all kinds of little exhibits everywhere showing you the different college sports that are available. My kids were introduced to a few sports that they didn't know existed, like fencing and precision rifle competitions. I love that many different sports are represented here, not just the usuals.

So happy I didn't find what I wanted at other shops, and when I called, Matt told me what he could get for me online and at what price. I drove over near closing time and stayed for 1-1/2 hours visiting with Matt and Martin. They are without a doubt the most enjoyable guys I have dealt with at a gun shop and they engaged in our conversation about my firearms collection with interest. I felt very much at home as we discussed what I was looking for and handled a few pistols. Finally I took a surplus pistol that I had been checking out online, and they gave it to me at a lower price, especially letting me select from several to get what I was happy with. I have found great people now without the attitudes you find with know-it-all dealers around the country. I will be going back for sure.
Everything is amazing: short ribs, crab cakes, fried calamari, mashed potatoes, french fries, rack of ribs, cookie skillet, and chocolate cake are all a must.

I love Gallery Pastry Shop! The gelato and pastries are always so good!! If you go for brunch, it's so much fun sitting at the bar seating where you can watch everything being made! It's just the cutest place!!

Crispy calamari was tender and had a delicious spicy sauce.  The wild mushroom and the shrimp and sweet corn chowder are both amazing, rich and velvety soups.  Crusted chilean sea bass was just ok and needed sauce, but the scallop special was so yummy.  Waitress was very nice and even brought out a sampe of the wild mushroom soup from the day before when I mentioned I would've like to try it.  Overall, a great dining experience.

The reason it only gets 2 stars is because of the horrible food poisoning I got afterwards.  I kind of want to give this place another try because the food was good but I'm scared of getting poisoned again.

They're the victim of a scam and don't even know it!! At least I hope that's the case.

  I bought two tactical knives from them on August 14th. On the box it was labeled "Wilcox Tactical".   The knife my wife got did not work. I contacted them directly and they say they don't make knives. Someone is counterfeiting items and attributing it to Wilcox Tactical!

I see if I can ferret out what's really going on.
Only been there once. My husband and I came here for our wedding anniversary. Beautiful inside and out and the food is yum especially the macaroons
10/10 would recommend on Saturdays for brunch... bottomless mimosas, need I say more?

Great food and Drink but just a little pricey.  We call it the C note place as you can drop $100 on just apps and drinks.  The food and service were fine. The only thing, we ordered the meatballs on shared plate menu came with 4 small meatballs for $14.  Sorry you can't share that.

First time here and glad it's mostly on a gift card from my wife's boss. Ordered the special shrimp fra diablo and my wife got a prime rib. Never saw a prime rib that looked like that. No bone??? 5 over-cooked shrimp on a small bed of pasta served luke warm. Prime rib was 50% fat and gristle and my wife still tasted it the next day. Baked potato rolled in salt and barely edible. Very disappointing and extremely overpriced. Gee maybe they were having a bad day but at my expense...  I think not.  Can't figure out all the great reviews. Maybe they didn't like my jeans.

I have a long hair kitty named Handsome. This is my first long haired tabby, and I was surprised at the amount of hair he would leave behind. So, I called Poochini's Pet Grooming, and made an appointment. I had never done this before, so I had no idea what to expect. The gentleman on the phone was nice. And, when I showed up for Handsome's appointment, I was surprised to have a pleasant conversation with him. Then I met Handsome's groomer, Andria, who asked me numerous questions about Handsome. Then, she took him into the back. Fifty minutes later, I picked Handsome up and he looked like a new kitty!
   Our second visit to Poochinis was just as pleasant. If you have a kitty, and you need to get him groomed, you need to make an appointment with Andria. She was professional, friendly, and she does fantastic work! I highly recommend her!
   Thanks to everyone at Poochini's Pet Grooming, and especially to Andria!!!
UPDATED

My sister-in-law booked us for brunch here and I'm falling in love with this place. A complimentary mimosa with brunch? Yes please! And their delicious cornbread? That's how to start brunch off. This particular one was blueberry lemon, yum!

We started off with the fondue because it's seriously just that awesome. With the sweetness I had gotten from the cornbread, I went savory for my main dish. My mom got my second choice, french toast and that was so light and fluffy. Delicious. I got a hearty ham & Gruyere omelet mixed with potatoes & caramelized onions. It was huge!! I would have liked more Gruyere in it. Along with that was rye bread and hash browns. The hash browns weren't crispy as I would have preferred, but wet. I know that's a odd way to describe them, but it's true. 

Full to the point I would have to be rolled out, I couldn't even think about dessert. 

Brunch did get busy so prepare for a wait on food & drinks. But when the weather is perfect out, sitting outside is the best choice.

Had a reservation, and they were packed for brunch. Waited about 10 minutes before we could order anything, and this continued throughout our time there. Drinks consistently empty, difficulty getting anyone to come to the table to order:food, drinks, refills,etc., other than that, the food was good. Cute place. Wish we could've tried dessert, but out breakfast took about 2 hours and we didn't have any more time to try to track someone down to place our dessert order.

This place is an awesome hidden gem tucked away from the bustle of the busy Broad Ripple area. Pastries look stunning. The food is extraordinary. I almost don't want to review this place so it will not get busier than it already is. You will not want to leave.

You want European, mainly French, pastries? Here you go... as authentic as it can be on American soil. Chef Ben has it going on. 
I was introduced to the pastry during a Yelp Meet the maker Event. The macaroons were so good, I just had to check out other goodies, so I brought my meet-up group here for brunch. 
We were not disappointed. I love that you can get awesome coffee creations as well as some delicious adult beverages. I fully support the mimosa movement. 
For brunch you could choose, among other things, an omelet for $10 or a pair of crepes for $15. You are given an order form on which you mark what you would like in your omelet or in  your crepes. With the crepes you can choose different filings for each crepe, and choose whether you want to go with the savory or the sweet or one of each (my choice). you get to pick as many or as few items for your dish as you like. 
Also we received complimentary cinnamon rolls for our table... omg, I had to buy a couple of those. They were just soooo delicious. Just a tiny crunch on the outside and a buttery soft on the inside, perfect texture followed by a buttery sugary taste explosion in your mouth. Uhmm, did I mention I'm a fan of those things? 
Anyways, another dish that got my undivided attention was the citrus Brule... who came up with that? I love it. Slices of various citrus fruit, warm with a crust of caramelized sugar. How can you not love that stuff? 
Besides the food, I must say the interior is very welcoming, the atmosphere relaxed and warm, the staff very friendly and helpful. A bit pricey, but well worth it in quality and service.

I've eaten here many times. One time several years ago I had the tomato basil bisque and it was life changing. I wanted to marry anyone in the kitchen who could get me that recipe. Sadly it came off the menu. 

I went for lunch this week. Had the kale and salmon salad on special. It was just ok which was surprising since most of the specials are noteworthy. But here's the thing that ruined my lunch: going to the men's room mid-meal, I was forced to watch Fox News playing on the monitors over both urinals. Why can't they play something neutral like HGTV, like my dentist does?

When I half jokingly mentioned it to our server, she said it's a corporate decision to indoctrinate us with bullshit while peeing (my words, not hers). But honestly if that's true, I don't need to support that establishment no matter how good the soup is. Will it hurt them? No. But I always feel better knowing I'm not contributing to companies that support mind numbing propaganda (oh and blatant lies).

Palace market is an outdoor nighttime arts and craft market that allows you to roam around and check out fantastic local artists. Surrounded by all the great clubs on Frenchmen Street in the Marigny, Palace Market is a fun escape from the noise and sounds of the street and an oasis of creative beauty. I spoke with many of the artists, admired their work, ultimately buying some beautiful art pieces to bring some NOLA back home with me.
We dined in the lovely outdoor patio yesterday. Our server was Sam. We had a great meal, and Sam was the absolute best! We will surely ask to be seated in her section each time. Thanks Sam!

While I've never been into GPS to dine in, I have been inside for an event and to watch the chefs baking away for a variety of pride-related events. 

You'll find GPS at a variety of locations around the city and at special events. Their macarons are amazing, especially when they're only $1 on Wednesdays! Their crepes are also delicious that I've tried when they partnered with Foundry Provisions earlier this summer. 

Their pastries are always delicious and the staff are always friendly. Double win in my book. Prices are a bit much, so it's only a special treat for me when I purchase their goodies, but they're worth it when you learn about the expertise and work that goes into each dessert. 

Looking forward to trying brunch at their storefront soon!

I've never left a review on Yelp but this place was so enjoyable I felt obligated to share. Every staff member was considerate, accommodating, and extremely pleasant to be around. It was my first time visiting The Gallery and our server, Mikaela, was helpful in recommending some incredible dishes for our table. The owner, Ben, was present at the restaurant greeting guests and ensuring everyone's satisfaction. 10/10

I popped in with my 6 year old after school one afternoon when I had a little work left to do from my day (b/c HOW do working parents navigate a 3:45pm school pick up and have a full time job? But I digress...). I knew The Gallery Pastry Shop would feel special and also give him something to enjoy watching while I typed away for a few minutes.

We were greeted at the entrance and spent a few moments admiring the beauty within the pastry case. For the end of the day there was still a good selection of macarons. 

The tables were set at this point for dinner and I mentioned we were only there for a treat but they still invited us to sit anywhere. We opted for a table at the pastry bar so we could watch the three pastry chefs at work. We were soon offered a menu &  some waters. My son ordered a chocolate croissant (I know! Mom of the year here!) and I requested a decaf coffee. At that late hour (4:30 PM) they did not have decaf coffee but offered a decaf Americano or any of the other specialty drinks. I stuck with coffee and was glad I had - as it was delicious. Our order was presented within a minute along with napkins and some gorgeous gold tone silverware.

I used the wifi to wrap up my work, my son devoured his warm chocolate croissant and we chatted about all of the cool stuff happening before our eyes. It was an all-around treat for the senses, and when our bill was presented for a total of $6 I left feeling like the experience was worth a whole lot more. Also worth noting, the staff nicely balanced checking in and taking care of us with leaving us to enjoy our time. That's an art, and The Gallery got it right.

This place is such a gem. We'll be back. Maybe on a Wednesday for $1 macarons, or maybe for brunch or dinner with grown ups (though I bet the kids could hang), or maybe just to relive the sweetness of today's visit with my kiddo!

Let me start with I am visiting from
Colorado and my friend bragged on this place. Great omelet. However it took 75 min to receive. One waitress for the entire outdoor seating. I realize restaurants just opened but if there's not enough staff to accommodate tables and provide exceptional service what's the point? We had to ask for more tea and water and the hostess when I initially walked in was standoffish. The fruit plate we ordered for my niece had a yellow pudding which for an adult is great but should have been exposed as it was clearly ordered for a child. Children are picky. 


After this above review, Ariel personally reached out to me and my family. She has gone above and beyond to make things right regarding our experience today. Not only did she send my family a gift card for the amount in which we spent today but she sent me w box of macaroons to Colorado. This is exactly what the world needs to see in their small businesses. I'm
Beyond impressed that she took my constructive criticism and made it right. If ever in Indy I will be back. Again the food was never the original issue as it was beyond yummy. In today's world we need more small businesses and personal touches. I've never been treated so promptly and kindly by a small business. This is exactly what we need more of. Thanks so much
Excellent tasting brunch with a variety of menu options to choose from. Covid precautions in place, prices are reasonable

I started the engagement ring shopping process with no idea how to shop for a ring. Sheffield's Diamonds was extremely helpful in explaining everything to me and helping me get the perfect ring. There were weather related issues (out of anyone's control) during shipping that delayed the arrival of the ring and Eric (the owner) ended up meeting me on a day their store was closed to get me the ring in time for me to propose while my mom was still in town. I highly recommend working with them on any jewelry endeavor!

A hidden gem! First, do not be misled by their webpage, they were told they can no longer do bottomless mimosas by the powers that be. 

We arrived without a reservation and were seated within 15 minutes. The build your own omelette and crepe menu have ingredients that you normally don't find at other brunch places, which was a welcome surprise. Another member of my group could not stop raving about the hash browns.  

Food prepared in an open (and very clean) kitchen. Because they cook to order, food for parties can come out separately, but not with much delay. 

Located in a strip mall, but don't let the location steer you away. 

Check this place out!
Get way to crowded . Search for service , i recommend sitting at the bar , more personal attention

Had two iPhone screen replacements here because my screen shattered. The first made my screen turn gray and it cracked within 3 weeks. They made me pay for the second and now the screen is so sensitive, lightly touching it  makes random apps open. Bad quality products.

Came here because most of the restaurants were packed and I completely regret it. I should have just waited in line or either gone to mcdonalds. Terrible service and terrible food. I dont know how this place stays open. 

I ordered the catfish and oyster platter with 2 cokes. The catfish was just coated in batter. Fries were undercooked. Service was terrible. The server couldnt remember our order yet she wouldnt get a pad to write it down. She instead write it down on the paper on our table. She kept coming back to see what she had written down. As we were paying for our bill, we had split the check and paid oneperson with the cash and used their credit card. We each put down some cash for the tip. The manager told us that it was inconvenient for them to accept the cash tip. I've never heard of that before. 

Overall, I wouldnt come back and wouldnt recommend others to eat here.

Our experience with Gadget Doctors brings to mind the classic Dadism, "Fool me once, shame on you.  Fool me twice, shame on me."  I don't know what I was thinking when I went back to them a second time.  Twice now, GD has failed to correct problems with our computers.  Twice now, they sat on our computers for 2+ weeks and wasted our money buying replacement components to experiment with solutions.  Twice now, someone else was able to diagnose and correct the problems quickly and inexpensively.  

GD's business model appears to be fixing simple problems and collecting bench fees + component markups on things they cannot handle.  Their diagnostic procedures appear to be quite bizarre, searching for zebras and unicorns when the horse is staring them square in the face.  And when they finally give up, after wasting 2+ weeks of your time, they blame it on the motherboard.  

Bottom line, if you need a new screen for your phone or a new battery for your laptop, GD is probably capable of handling that.  Anything else, go somewhere else.  DO NOT allow them to start ordering parts for "experiments."  And, if they take longer than a day to return your phone call, they are out of their depth.  Save yourself weeks of lost time, pick your device up, and take it someplace else.

Met an old friend for dinner. He is on Atkins and they had no problem w a substitution on his sides for his ribeye. I had the Chilean sea bass and it was delicious. We began w buffalo shrimp. Different & tasty. Very large shrimp & not over cooked. The waiter was personable but a tad intrusive. Service was a little too fast for me. I'd certainly go back.

My husband and I love going to this cute little place for breakfast/brunch.  Everything is delicious and employees are all friendly.  We enjoy sitting at one of their tables or at the counter where you can watch and chat with those preparing the food.  The pastries and desserts are amazing.  They have a great selection of macrons, and we are particularly fond of their almond croissants.  Parking can be a challenge, but it's well worth it.

Wandered by this place in the mall and stopped in. Tried a sample of the Americano (espresso and hazelnut) and ended up ordering a small cup with chocolate chips. Should have just stuck to the sample by the end the flavor was just too sweet and too much, can't imagine ordering anything larger than a small....a kiddie size probably would have been better. Dough was at least soft, have tried others and it was hard an unappetizing. Kinda expensive for what it is, I think I am over the edible dough trend.

If I could give 0 stars I would. My best friend and I went here for lunch and it was the worst customer service and food experience ever!!! I ordered the YaYa gumbo and my shrimp had scales on it! The flavor of the gumbo considering it's called the Gumbo Pot was mediocre. My best friend ordered the hamburger po'boy which was two frozen patties on bread with lettuce and tomato on the side. It was disgusting! We asked our waiter if she could get something else and he said he would ask. 20 minutes later a man came up and I explained to him the sandwich was not good. His response was "Well she ordered it!" I explained to him that we were not from New Orleans and had never eaten here before. He went on to say he couldn't take it back because it was made fresh...OBVIOUS LIE since it was clearly a frozen patty. He said if it was Gumbo or Jambalaya he could take it back because those are pre made. After he said that I was disgusted and over the situation.  After another 10 minuets I finally was able to get the waiter to bring the check. I asked him to split it since we were paying separately and he said no.  TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE!!!! We didn't want to not pay for the food just wanted an alternative that was somewhat edible. Will never eat here again when I visit New Orleans!

This might be my favorite dessert place in town. The case in front has a constantly changing arrangement of desserts that look and taste amazing. It is clear a lot of hard work and love go into what is made here. I have not had something I didn't enjoy. 

Aside from the excellent quality of food I really appreciate the atmosphere. I have been to a lot of nice dessert places and many of them come off as pretentious. GPS is far from that with a warm, welcoming setting and friendly staff while still delivering top tier food. 

There are also so many special events going on to enjoy. They host events such as the dessert series and also get involved with other local  businesses for pop-ups and special outings. I love to support local businesses especially when those businesses continue to support local. 

In summary: great food, great environment, great local involvement.

Wow, this was a very busy place on a Saturday afternoon.  The weather was turning but people just kept placing their names on the list and waited for their table.

I got lucky and was inside near the kitchen and watched the chefs in action.  The food was very good and service was good.  She kept a watch on me, but let me sit and eat while reading my book.

Had to try the dessert (of course!) and was not disappointed here either.  Great eclair!  Good job everyone!

I visited Redstone for the first time today and was completely shocked by how good it was! Their menu is the perfect size--not too overwhelming, but still has lots of fun options. We got the brussel sprouts and cornbread to share for the table. The sprouts were very flavorful--somehow they were drenched in sauce and still retained their crispness!! The cornbread was awesome as well. It's a huge skillet and it comes with maple butter. It could easily be shared between 8 people. 

For the main course, I opted for the fish tacos. They were very fresh but lacking in flavor. I wish there had been a bit more seasoning on them! I ended up pouring the sauce that it came with on them and that did help. They also came with fries which is always a bonus for me. We then shared the cookie skillet for dessert. THIS WAS SO GOOD!!!! I'm not super big on desserts but this was incredible. A gooey cookie with ice cream....and drizzled in chocolate. Unreal!

After finishing our entrees, I was surprised when they brought out hot towels for us to wipe our hands with. Nice touch! The employees here were extremely helpful and very pleasant which added to the already great atmosphere at Redstone!

We arrived to Nightmare before Tinsel during Happy Hour time and had to wait a few minutes to get in.  Once we did, it was pretty packed.  Photos were a must before we lost our ability to move without spilling a drink.  They go all out on their decorations and I'm glad we made it there.  

The drinks were just okay, nothing special, but the blood bags were interesting.  I'm just happy we didn't go the weekend night we were trying to.  Stick to the weeknights to be able to get in sooner.  I think we'll take this advice when we try to get to Tinsel later in the year.

Theses guys are great, I have purchased several guns from them, they have a great layaway program. They are open late on weekdays, and the only gun shop open on Sunday. Huge selection new and used firearms, tons of holsters and magazines. You can tell they like what they do!

This place is a mess. Disorganized,  short-staffed,  and extremely rude servers. 

We will never go back.

Pretty close to downtown, but the price is decent. You can tell the near by area is nit that good, but don't need to drive everywhere because they have shuttles to downtown till 9pm..free parking, breakfast, and the lady work at the front desk was super super nice. Shower was nice and hot with great water pressure.

Downsides..
The Wi-Fi is not real stable.

I found two bugs.  One close to the bed the other one in the bathroom, not a cockroach or bedbug, but they were big enough to creep you out if you are scared of bugs.

The Gallery Pastry Shop is chicken noodle soup for the soul, from the food to the baked goods, down to the staff and the ambiance. When you walk up it is absolutely lush, the outdoor seating is filled with flowers and greenery (seasonal allergy warriors, you've been warned). If you choose to come inside, it is the rustic chic vibe that warms your heart. Every table has a different theme and I think it's adorable. 
I chose the Rose Macchiato iced, and I did the hash with chorizo added. The flavors in both the drink and the food are exceptionally balanced, the eggs were cooked to perfection, and the vegetables were perfectly sautéed. The rose in the macchiato is not overpowering, but it is very much present on your palate. Amazing.
The baked goods here are exquisite. You can tell that whoever is in charge here truly knows what they are doing. Not only delicious, but everything in the case is a work of art. 
This is an amazing place for brunch, and overall a really amazing place to bring people together and enjoy each other. Definitely impressed!

I really wanted to like this place. The ambiance and decor is very cute and seems like the perfect place to have a girl's lunch/brunch or to have a dessert date night. I came in for dessert after dinner, and the lady behind the counter seemed annoyed when I said I just wanted to check out their desserts (I assume she was annoyed that I wasn't sitting down to eat?). She was very rude when I inquired about different desserts and I felt as if I was inconveniencing her by ordering macarons. I have worked customer service jobs before, and I will never understand why people in those jobs act inconvenienced by having to help a customer. I will not be back because the worker I interacted with made me feel very unwelcome and it was honestly an uncomfortable experience.

First night in town and we were hungry. We originally had other dinner plans but ended up stopping here because it was closer. I don't think I've ever said this before but I am SO glad I didn't check Yelp first! We  might not have stopped. Instead, blissfully ignorant of any negative reviews, we had a great experience.

Awesome seafood gumbo, just the right amount of spicy. My friend loved the chicken andouille gumbo. Servers were very nice and the food arrived FAST - just what we wanted! Clean restrooms. My only complaint is that they don't serve hushpuppies :(

This is one of the worst TB I have ever been to. Our food came overcooked. My daughter had a steak quesadilla it was burnt and flat like a sheet a paper. You know how its cut into 4 slices? The 4th slice was just tortilla..no meat no cheese..just flat burnt quesadilla.
I had a mexican pizza and it tasted off. I realized that the tostada had been over cooked and affected the taste.
So dissapointed.
Go elsewhere..

The waitress showed us a table and asked us to sit, unfortunately, there was food all over the chairs.  The wait staff uses their hands to put straws in the drink, right at the tip where you are supposed to drink from.  The floor was disgusting; the place could use a good cleaning.  I would talk about the food but no one came to our table after sitting there for 20 minutes so we left.  Worst service ever......the wait staff could use an upgrade.
Always a good meal, cool delicious drink and a nice atmosphere. Can't really go wrong! Recommend the Bang Bang cauliflower and a Doli pineapple.

We visited the gallery for the first time after my friend had just said "yes to the dress" at a dress shop near by. We knew it was supposed to be a great experience, but I think everything was even better than our expectations! The wait staff asked if we had done anything fun and of course we showed them pictures of Brittanys beautiful wedding dress. They were kind enough to celebrate with complimentary champagne! We also had yummy meals. The veggie crepe, to die for. Jowl bacon, such a treat. And the chocolate mousse dessert was like a piece of heaven. Thank you!!!!
Overrated super crowded I try to order a different thing every time hoping that maybe something will be good and I would say the food is OK but way too much money

They are sleeping not cooking at this restaurant! Food was like canned beans and boxed rice. Server held the face and warmth of an icicle. Don't order a chili relleno unless you like to be disappointed! Save your money and send it to starving children - this place over charges. I bet you could make a better Mexican meal going to the dollar store.
A roach ran across the bar. I alerted the bartender who said cavalierly, "this is New Orleans."

I met a friend for lunch at The Gallery on a rainy, chilly Saturday. The place was crowded and loud but with an extremely appreciative vibe because the food is delicious. My friend had just spent a week in Paris where she savored the amazing array of great food and wines. But we both agreed that the "side" we ordered and shared was on a par. Red and golden beets paired with grapefruit, a little soft cheese and micro-greens drizzled with sweetened olive oil. It was like nothing I've ever had and hope the same "side" is available when I next return.

We're fans of Tinsel, the holiday pop-up bar that looks like Christmas on steroids, so naturally when we heard they did a 'Nightmare Before...' version for Halloween, we knew we definitely wanted to check it out! We're so glad we snuck a visit into the the craziest that is our October. The decorations and experience did not disappoint! 

The place is jammed packed with creepiness....the blue body bags over the bar were an excellent touch! The moving one was awesome! I loved the baby doll feet hanging on the back room too. I mean, what's more disturbing than that! I just sat and wondered how they got them up there. The classic horror masks and room for photos were great ideas too!

Sure, You're going to overpay for your themed cocktail, but this is once a year ana it's so fun! The blood bags were awesome, and of course make for that amazing insta photo! 

In case you didn't know, children ARE allowed into these pop-ups.  We bring ours to Tinsel for Shirley Temples every year. This however may be a bit scary for the real little ones. My kiddos who are now 8&10 had no issue. They may have stayed a bit closer to us than normal though hahah Kiddos are cool to enter from 2-7pm with a guardian. 

A spooky time was had by all! I really hope they bring it back next year! Its such a fun was to celebrate Halloween in the city! I appreciate not having to leave the city to get in on the horror fun! 

We had no line on mischief night and combined with a great meal in the city afterwards! Makes for a really rad night! I knew what to expect from the crowd and ability to move around, but others may find it a bit claustrophobic. You will be squished next to others, but I didn't find it to be annoying. Some may.
I am a Bloody Mary lover but usually have to add at least pepper or hot sauce. Not here! It came out perfect. We had the gumbo. Got a cup and it was enough for two of us. Definitely at stop in Nola.

I have visited this establishment numerous times and never had any issues ordering beverages. I came tonight with my mother and my daughter, and saw my ID was lost. Very upsetting that my other forms of identification were not valid. I am a New Jersey resident as well as a medicinal mmj patient which has my legal age. As well as a copy of my ID in my pictures. No alcohol service, needless to say I will not be back to spend funds here. I come here at least twice a month..

So many may over look this hotel but it was perfect for us!  While this is an older hotel, it has been very nicely updated.  The free breakfast Buffett was plentiful, our room was very nice and the free shuttle to downtown was great!  But the best thing here is the staff.  Everyone from Tiffany at the front desk to the great breakfast staff were friendly and helpful.  Great accommodations for the price ...and free parking!

The bouncer denied us access due to someone in our party walking with a limp. The bouncer said the person had to sober up before entering. After I explained that the  person had a physical disability that caused the limp, they said that they couldn't prove that and still did not allow for us to enter. This is entirely discriminatory and I really hope that something is done about this.

While I love this place, my five year old adores it more.  He has a wonderful appreciation for macaroons.  Our favorite is $1 Wednesday.  

It's worth heading into the shop and dining in.  The decor is amazing, the staff is friendly, and you can watch them making their next creations.  My favorite is to sit at the bar and watch.  

They offer a variety of beverages, cocktails, pastries, and food.  I have popped in for a croissant to enjoy the next morning.
This place was amazing, there service was amazing and you get your food really quick I would recommend the Steak filet with a side of Mac and cheese! 5 star!!!

I somehow found Computer Housecalls (actually their other site http://electronicgadgetrepair.com/) when searching for a place to get the cracked screen on my daughter's ipod touch 4 fixed and they were the only alternative I found that was not in Philadelphia or NYC, and since I work just off of I295 they were easy to get to.  Having already had to fix a couple of digitizers on my wife's iPhone 3GS and one of my Blackberrys, I understood the process and have experience with the repair shops in NYC.  Computer Housecalls was a pleasant change.  They do the repairs out in the open (so no chance they are messing with your device) and they went well above and beyond the call of duty when some issues arrived during the repair.  I actually took my Ipod to them to get the battery repaired two days later.  

Brad (the owner) and Joe (the guy who did my repair) were very nice and pleasant and provided great customer service (which is hard to find these days).

They repair gaming systems and smart phones, while also doing any computer repair you could get from Geek Squad (at a cheaper price with faster turn-around) in their store or at your location (hence the name). 

I highly recommend them, I plan on recommending them to our internal IT team (we have standardized on iPhones) and will use them again the next time we have the need for a screen repair or computer problem.
Very nice place to stay close to everything downtown. Clean rooms and good breakfast. Only downside was the staff at check in. The worst front desk staff I've ever encountered

Philadelphia is great for most things, but in years recent the cute Pop-Up bar culture that you see in LA and NY has been missed here in the city of Brotherly Love. That being said, I'm extremely impressed with Tinsel's efforts to encompass the market for Halloween Lover's interests for their newest venture "Nightmare Before Tinsel."

Because there are a lack of options when it comes to theme bars in the city, I would highly suggest you leave this one off your list for a weekend spot. The space is tiny (however, wonderfully decorated) and can become extremely uncomfortable during high volume hours on the weekends. My friend and I decided to visit on a Monday night around 7:30, and Nightmare wasn't eerily empty, but was at a comfortable level to enjoy the space without feeling claustrophobic. 

Now onto all the decorations (what we're really here for, right?):
You enter the bar through a wall of spiders and their thick web to open up to the bar on your right with a custom bar top painted by local artists. 
Walk through to the back and to a wall of faceless figures and severed doll bodies hanging from the ceiling. Creepy, but effective. There is a small "room?" in the back left hand corner filled with creepy doll heads that had this Halloween fanatic thoroughly creeped out. 

They offered a pretty entensive menu of themed cocktails that were rather expensive, but these type of bars have to make back their money spent of decorations somehow so it's understandable. We opted for the "Blood Bags" with Faber Orange Vodka, red bull, and grenadine served in a cute blood pouch for extra spooky vibes. 

Overall not the best Pop-Up Bar I've ever been to, but the best one I've been to in Philly. The owners really did a good job on the decorations, and the drinks albeit expensive, are awesome in playing off the Halloween theme. If you're someone who starts Spoopy season as soon as it drops below 70 degrees, this place is for you.

Oh my goodness...what has happened to my old time favorite? I am so disappointed. We could always count on the buffalo shrimp. I was so disappointed tonight. The shrimp were a bit tough. Barely sauced. Huh? The prices have gone up. I ordered the steak Cobb salad. Steak medium well. The steak was pink in the middle yet dry-Which I thought was a feat in itself lol! But yeah. Guess I've got to let them go
Brian, the tech assigned was thorough and methodical. He got my reasonably complex home network back in operation in a reasonable amount of time, and identified a faulty router. Thanks Brian!!

Excited to go back to try more items on the menu!!
This is the cutest place I've ever dined. We opted to sit at the counter which surrounds the open kitchen, best decision ever. We chatted with Jeremiah as he prepared food. I greatly appreciated him answering our random culinary questions, he's fantastic.
I ordered the Gallery Club, best sandwich I've ever had. The house made aioli has me rethinking ever putting mayo on a sandwich again. The chicken velvet soup had a unique flavor profile, it wasn't bad just not what I expected. I still ate most of it.
Lastly, the pastries were magical. I had my chocolate croissant warmed; buttery flaky chocolaty goodness. I practically inhaled it. I also had a couple of macaroons; no complaints here they all made my taste buds perk up in delight. 
Overall this place is worth repeat visits. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, the staff are all amazing, and the food is utterly delicious.

This is my 5th time frequenting gallery pastry shop since moving here in July. I am now 8 months pregnant and the croissant & gravy has been one of my cravings ever since ordering it at the restaurant several months ago. I can't recommend it enough. Unfortunately, the past two times, my experience ordering it has been under par.

The item is not listed on their online menu for pickup. I called to order it in and unfortunately my name was not taken and the staff was very out of touch with how their online menu presents. I took this with a grain of salt recognizing the hectic times we're in. I showed up to the restaurant and basically re-ordered and paid. Now expecting a fresh order of croissant & gravy. I sat waiting for close to ten min before another hostess asked me about my order and guided me to the outdoor hostess stand handing me my to-go order. I have no idea how long it was sitting out there and was quite disappointed to see less gravy on the order than the past times. :/

I appreciate the chefs and quality of food at this establishment! However, due to the disappointing service and lack of communication- I am probably better off learning to make my own gravy from now on.

Though less than 1/2 a mile from LP field and about a mile from downtown, the Clarion is in really industrial section so there is not much to see just walking around the hotel. Also if there is a game trying to get to the hotel is a nightmare, for some reason the Nashville police block about 80% of the roads in the area and hand direct all street light traffic, the worst! 

We loved the updated lobby and rooms. We had two queen beds with nice white cotton bedding. The only thing I didn't like about our room was that the bathroom light was connected to the fan, so if you wanted to see you had to have the super loud fan on. Though the fan is obnoxiously loud it sadly did little to take away the steam from the shower.

They server a complementary hot breakfast which was ok, as expected. Make your own Belgian waffles, eggs, sausage, eggs, mini bagels and muffins, cereal, yogurt, coffee juice. Oh and terrible diced potatoes!

There is a small bar, but its not open until later in the afternoon. The bartender said wine was like $12 which seemed a bit high for the atmosphere.

They offer a shuttle until 8pm to downtown but be forewarned you have to sign up for it at the front desk. Raul the driver was nice enough to make a double trip when there were too many people.  

Prices change based on demand, but at $440 for two nights it was a great deal for us.

To start off...when I 1st visited GUMBO POT i was greeted by a guy smoking a cigarette a few steps away & who pointed at the sign and said "we specialize in 2 things  *points to the 1st word in the sign* & says GUMBO *then points to the 2nd word* and says "POT" then laughs to pretend he is kidding. 
anyways.... The 1st time I went with a group of friends visiting from out of state. We had brunch and I ordered the eggs benedict with artichoke hearts...there was hair in my food of which clearly did not come from me. I had already eaten half of it and therefore didnt feel the need to make a scene. 
The 2nd time I went back (yes i gave it another try) I ordered the seafood gumbo which contained no crab like the menu said, and the shrimp had no taste. the gumbo was spicy and thats about all the flavor it had...didnt taste like seafood, file, okra, etc...and my friend & husband who got the Chicken & sausage gumbo werent pleased either...tasted like the sausage was in it, but didnt have an authenic GUMBO taste. bleh again. My husband and I also shared the catfish and shrimp plater, the shrimp and catfish lacked flavor...the breading was just that...and no seasoning. I was not pleased and doubt seriously I will visit again. The New Olreans Hamburger & Seafood Co directly across the street has AMAZING food and i have always been pleased there, their Catfish is thin fried and in huge portions!

Remains one of my favorite spots in broad ripple. The staff is warm and welcoming. The atmosphere is quiet and unique in that you get to watch the pasty chefs. 

Their baked items have not disappointed yet. Everything is so fresh, and you can truly taste the difference. They offer a limited menu, but they do their menu well above just par. 

Update: place is still dynamite. Very few places can offer this level of consistency in the quality of their offerings.

Raul (Row-ul) the shuttle driver for the night time on Thursday May 30th, was extremely disrespectful to two men who had been waiting for his shuttle back to the hotel. We arrived to the pickup/drop off spot and two men were sitting there and had been sitting there since about 8:00pm (it was 8:35 at the time we arrived) and the shuttle is suppose to run every 30 mins. The shuttle arrives with a large group of people so once they got off we all started to load up, and at that point more people had shown up to take the shuttle back (like us). Those two men were gentlemen and let people get on the shuttle first and by the time we were all sat down with a full bus we looked out and realized those two men were still outside. Me and the four other people I were with yelled to the bus driver from the back and said "Sir those two men have been waiting since 8 for you we can squeeze and there's no one in the front seat can you let them on, if not we will get off for them." And he replies "I've got 10 minutes" and speeds away nearly knocking me off of my feet. We got back and notified the front desk about Raul's disappointing behavior. We felt so bad we waited for the two men to get back and made sure they knew we tried to vouch for them to get them onto the bus. 

On a happier note, our stay otherwise has been outstanding. The bartender Justin has been funny, outgoing and a great laugh to come back too. Dee and Reeza have been incredible shuttle drivers (actually going above and beyond for their guests, unlike Raul). The front desk and that team has also been more than accommodating for us! They are whom deserve the three stars I am giving for this stay. We still have two more days and are definitely looking forward to it!

The Gallery Pastry Shop is a great place for brunch! It is tucked away behind some businesses in SoBro and there is a downtown location as well. The space is beautiful decorated with vintage detail and offers outdoor seating. While the breakfast was good, the pastries were phenomenal. Definitely recommend for a fun girls brunch and treating yourself to some dessert. They also offer classes for macaroons and other baked goods which sounds awesome!!

I cannot believe it's taken me so long to come to this gem. It was adorable with the outdoor seating and string lights. The atmosphere is great for date night or girls night! I was a little off put with the ordering/payment situation. You have to walk past the register to an unmarked location by the display case to order and then go back to the register to pay. The flow of the process was a little stressful because it wasn't marked and people around us were getting frustrated since they weren't sure if the service was slow or if they were also standing in the wrong place to order. After the ordering confusion, things went smoothly. I got the white chocolate cheesecake and two macaroons -mixed berry and salted caramel. It was all very good but the cheesecake was a little dry. I also got a berry Bellini to drink and would rate it a 12/10. SO good! I can't wait to go back now that I understand the ordering flow.
