I went out in the evening with friends. We found a table easily and the service was efficient and quick. There's a corner around a campfire that was lovely and we really enjoyed ourselves. A little noisy outside but still worth it!

Very pleased with their service! I handed them an older, lagging gaming computer with many issues, and they refurbished it like new! About 2 weeks later, I went back because my computer fan seemed to be making a loud noise. They fixed the "noise", FREE of charge. Was very pleased with their work, and how fast they fixed my computer. Highly recommend!
Everything looks beautiful and is absolutely delicious. The coffee is great as well. The staff is very friendly. The price is a little hight but it's obviously pretty sweet spot for sweets.
You get what you're going for! It's a super themed bar. Decorated to the T. Drinks are expensive but they're also themed and very on-brand for the bar. You go for the experience.
Exquisite desserts and the personnel is very friendly. We tried their savory crepes and the banana foster crepes all delicious. Not cheap but worth it, if you value the experience.

Had used these guys to fix a Dell PC desktop back in 2013 and was very satisfied with their support and repair services. Now, 3 years later, our second desktop, a 2-year old ASUS started making loud noises like it was a race car at the Daytona 500. So off to these "doctors" again and they took great care of my computer....again! 

They are the real deal, no b-s you and they do repairs on smartphones and tablets as well as computers. They also sell used equipment, if you want to save lots of money.

This is a little late but I needed everyone to know how great Nightmare Before Tinsel was!

My roommates and I tried but failed to go to a Halloween silent disco this past Halloween and after that mess (not to be dramatic) but we didn't know if we could save our Halloween. We had heard about Nightmare before Tinsel via visit Philly or something like that and we definitely wanted to check it out.

Our night was saved! We had to wait a little bit in line but that's to be expected, so once we were in it was lit. Literally. There were lights everywhere and creepy/dope Halloween decorations all on the walls and ceilings. It was so cool!

It's definitely a small bar so don't expect to have much room to walk on a busy holiday, but honestly it didn't seem that chaotic. I got a rum and Diet because I was being basic and cheap that night, but my roommates got the specialty drink that was in a blood bag so that added to the fun Halloween-ness of it all. The drinks weren't cheap so keep that in mind but it was worth it for the experience.

Can't wait to go back for Tinsel (the Christmas version!)
Lunch was awesome - not crowded, so everything was served really fast. The food was really good and the service was great. Definitely a recommended stop.

Everything about this place is 5 stars. Their service to the ambiance to the quality of the food... I would give this place 6 if possible. Meatballs app excellent, breaking bread comes with the best dipping sauces. Prime rib very good, cedar plank salmon excellent. Our third visit and not one aspect of any visit has disappointed. Can't wait to come back.

WARNING - this is a TOURIST TRAP - NOT recommended at all. We went there for lunch and were greeted - such as it was - at the door, seated and the sever started pushing beer suggestions at us. As we were thirsty, we asked for glass of water so we were each given a bottle of water - at $4 EACH. Hmmm.  When we placed our (very rushed) order (server was in a hurry for some reason as the place was barely at 50% capacity) we were asked if we wanted bread or crackers and we asked for bread. I had the seafood gumbo and my wife had the chicken / sausage gumbo and there was no difference in taste except that I had a few small shrimp. Oh and the bread was an extra $2.  We had better service and much tastier food from a Bourbon Street hotdog cart vendor later that night. 

Yelp really needs to consider implementing a zero or minus star rating selection.

I almost never review hotels on Yelp but I am doing so for this hotel as a public service. This is an infested Pig with Lipstick. Our rooms were dirty as in makeup smeared on walls, bugs on the bed, other people's socks and ponytail holders on the floor. Housekeeping is lacking and they are really loud banging around in the morning. Our key cards had to be rekeyed the third night because they screwed them up.  The whole place was basically new stuff shoddily installed and the whole place was just a disappointment. The breakfast was not good and I had low expectations going on since I often eat at the breakfast bars at their competitor's properties. Would not return here. Way over priced for the level of service and amenities provided. Above all a hotel should be clean. They failed.
Best brunch experience in Indy!!! The back of the house is just as amazing as the front. This team has it figured out when it comes to creating a true culinary experience. Second to none.

If you want great prices, knowledgeable staff and a great enviroment, then you need to head to Idaho Gun and Outdoor.  If they don't have what you need, they will be happy to order it for you.  They treat you like family!!!

Eclectic and definitely a gallery. You can sit at the bar and watch them cook your food. Dinner and a show sounds like a great first date. There are cool chairs at every table. It's a tight space but can still hold a group of 8. Looks like there is a lot of space for outside seating in the summer so I'm sure this hidden gem is a great spot. 
I got the egg hash. Delicious! The hash was very fresh with seasonal vegetables of mushroom, asparagus, spinach, onion, and tomato. The service was good. I would definitely come back to take photos and sit at the bar.

I have to admit, The Gallery Pastry Shop was great. Definitely coming back here again. Such a fabulous menu, it was simply hard to choose, but I am really happy that I had Opera. The lovely people working there are extremely attentive and helpful. Do you need another reason to stop in The Gallery Pastry Shop?

This is my favorite not so hidden gem in Indy. I am so glad their business and popularity seems to have exploded. Lunch, brunch, coffee, or a treat this is a great spot. And, just steps from the monon. The best part--- they made my gorgeous wedding cake (their carrot cake is amazing). It tasted delicious even a whole year later

Dr. Angeles has cared for me and my family for many years ! She always goes the extra mile . She listens and listens . Just like we are taught in nursing school . She cares for the " whole " patient !

There is something really magical about shopping for handmade crafts at night.  

Maybe it hit me extra hard because I'm from Boston, a cold city where smiling at strangers is uncommon, but this little night market, tucked away within a short stumble of the raucous nightlife on Bourbon street, absolutely captivated me. It's been a few months since my visit to New Orleans and I can still vividly conjure up the sense of magic I felt when I came upon Palace Market on Frenchmen street one sweltering September night. If this gem weren't so easy to miss, I would almost hesitate to write about it and rob others of the joy of discovering it themselves. It's right next to the Spotted Cat music club, so the area should already be on your radar as worth a visit.

You won't find any of the same old souvenir items found on every corner here. Instead you can have real conversations with friendly artisans about their work and inspirations, browse art prints, jewelry and other unique items, or just sit down under the lights and take it all in for a while. It's really the perfect spot for visitors to find gifts for people at home (because really, who wants a magnet from the airport gift shop?) -or to treat yourself to something wonderful.

I've never been anywhere quite like Palace Market and would recommend it just for the sparkle it shone onto my trip, but on top of that I can now attest to their wonderful customer service; I reached out to the market via email this week, 4 months after being in the city, to ask for help tracking down a vendor. I bought a pair of earrings with cash during my visit, lost one almost immediately, gave up hope of finding the jeweler and only recently realized there was a possibility I could ask the market organizers about it. They got back to me quickly & identified the piece's creator as soon as I sent them a photo (even though she isn't currently a vendor, according to their website). Fingers crossed I'll get a replacement - either way, I can't say enough good things about this place & I will be back.

Decent atmosphere but ridiculously overpriced in my opinion. I had a stuffed meatball appetizer, it came with 4 small meatballs, $14.  My gf had the mahi mahi, came with a small piece of fish and veggies, astronomically priced at $31.  My lasagna was $22. I have no problem paying up for good food,  but the food was average at best. Service was on point. Our waitress was great and the only reason I'm giving 3 stars..

Gumbo is amoung the best in New Orleans, good roux, fresh ingredients.  Situated I center or tourist district, though view of parking lot and train tracks requires on open mind if you dine on patio.  Interior provides a noise and climate refuge that is welcome.  Service is prompt and attentive, though needs some cultural sensitivity.  Being in the tourist central area requires more awareness than I observed. Np oration sizes are gargantuan.  Only
Americans, and New Orleanians consider a portion size 5 times greater than needed as normal.  As a weight-conscious diner, I find the appetizer size and cups of gumbo or other selection as satisfying.  From my exposure to Japanese and European portions, the entire sizes  could feed whole families.  Please recommend to foreign tourists accordingly.  I saw serving staff teasing a Japanese tourist about his wife eating more than him.  Japanese are discreet eaters, and hypersensitive to saving face, and this teasing would be seen as highly offensive.  Europeans see Americans as morbidly obese, and portion sizes as extreme, and would see this teasing as immoderate.  Being in the central tourist area, you can't afford to alienate these populations.  Your food is fresh and well prepared, so start with recommending something small, with other tasty follow ups if they are interested and hungry.  Give them tastes from a variety, rather than bury them.  This maybe more profitable as well. This Japanese tourist had you throw out most of his entree, and that is wasteful and embarrassing.  
Don't for the big cash haul, pull 'em in slowly, and charm them with your engaging and welcoming personalities.  You've got the rest of the act together.  See yourselves as fishermen, not hunters of big game.

Only our go to place for after dinner sweets. Their pastries are top notch not only in taste but also in presentation. Our all time favorite being the Provence (the purple one), a white choco mousse with lavender, just light and not too sweet with the nice hint of lavender. Portion is just right as well not too big but still enough to satisfy any sweet tooth. The wife have taken a few of their cooking/baking classes and she enjoyed all of them. We've also been to one of their pop up dinner (Butcher Babe) and it was awesome and worth every penny.

One of my favorite little gems here in Indy. I love their roasted Brussels. I think I order them every time go to Gallery Pastry Shop. Some of my other faves that you must try are the Almond Croissant (this has to be the biggest croissant I've ever seen, filled with a delicious sweet but kinda creamy filling), two egg vegetable hash (very filling), and the house sparkling lemonade (the berry basil is refreshing)! And the staff is always welcoming and friendly, and gives great suggestions to try. There is indoor and outdoor seating, and with the kitchen being open, I love to sit and watch the chef's prepare the food.

Awesome customer service throughout the stay. Front desk super friendly and an accident on my part booking incorrectly for wrong date was easily resolved by manager (something that could have taken me 30-45 minutes normally). Breakfast crew just as friendly. Great location & free parking and breakfast.
I love this spot. Food is consistently great. Service is always spot on as well. Love a place that is always on target...never miss!

I brought my I phone 5C in for a new charging port.    It appeared to be loose or worn.   The tech looked it over and found a very small piece of plastic that had gotten in to the port - likely from a chip off the protective case.  He carefully removed it with tweezers, checked it over, tested it and handed it back - no charge.He could have easily charged me for a new port and I would have been happy and never would have known.   Great service and an honest business deserve to be recognized.    Bring them all your electronic repairs..... I know I will.

Gallery Pastry Shop was such a fun brunch spot for a Saturday! We had to wait about 15 mins, but they do take reservations i learned so will try to do that next time. The food was great, but it is a limited menu. They give you sheets to fill out with what you want to order, and the prefer limited to no substitutions it felt like. Part of why we came was bottomless mimosas, however, they don't do that anymore (per the website) but do have 1/2 priced bottles. It was our first time and our server seemed very annoyed when we asked questions or didn't know you paid upfront. Can't wait to go back when it's nice out and sit outside!

While I absolutely love the desserts, brunch, and overall ambience of the Gallery, the service level is more comparable to that of a half ass coffee shop or fast food. 3 out of the last 4 times we have been we have had multiple items we ordered just not come out and at least once having to remind them more than once. None of those times has it been overwhelmingly busy, the staff just seems more interested in anything outside of their task at hand. I would just love to see this place with a staff that had urgency, passion, and prided themselves on delivering an experience to match the level of artistry put on the plate. On multiple of these occasions we have brought out of town friends or family and have been let down and felt embarrassed ourselves. It sucks to have to think twice about going and lowering our expectations.
Was charged the wrong amount and didn't even apologize. Food was cold just as service was!

[this applies only to their BRUNCH]

So it makes me sad to give this place such a poor review, as it had so much potential. I'm sure their desserts are fabulous, and when they're more fully staffed, it is a fantastic place to be. But today I was not impressed.

A friend and I arrived at noon on a weekday, ordered within 10 minutes of being seated, but did not get our lunch for an additional 45 minutes. We both ordered the croissant sandwiches, neither of which required any cooking, other than the sunny side up egg on mine. We were told the wait was due to fresh croissants baking in the oven, but our croissants were not warm and did not taste like they had been made that recently.

When I ordered, I asked the waitress for one egg and a croissant. She told me that would have to be a croissant sandwich ($12...mind you, the croissants are only $3). So fine, I added some ham. It turned out being ok, except they cooked the egg wrong! The whites were still runny, but the yolk was wayyy overdone. The side salad was good, and the san pellegrino was tasty, but I don't understand why I had to wait nearly an hour and pay $20 for a meal with an overcooked egg on a croissant. 

My friend enjoyed her sandwich and her matcha latte. As an ex-barista, I tend to judge a place by the quality of their steamed milk. This one needed some work. Still a tasty drink, but their espresso machine is not up to par with the type of drinks they're serving. 

On the bright side, their decor is fabulous both inside and out. Staff seemed knowledgeable, but probably a bit stretched thin. If I come back, it will not be for brunch, but rather to pick up desserts and go.

We bought a very expensive ring by Tacomi here in 2009.  A year later we needed it re-sized.  The sale included two free re-sizings.  The ring is a band with very delicate and intricate details.  The craftsmanship on the resizing was so perfect you could not tell where it was cut and re-banded together at all.  The ring has held up to some rough treatment.  We are still happy with the purchase today.  Sales is friendly, straightforward and un-pressured.  Service was quick and accurate.

For me this is slightly above average highlight was the buffalo shrimp those are 5 star but my under cooked jumbo grilled chicken wings was a deal breaker. My entree was blan and rice was dry. The atmosphere was great service was poor. If I'm in the neighbored I will pop in for the buffalo shrimp but not make a special trip.

Would love a good patisserie in the neighborhood. This is not it. Purchased a croissant and when I got home I threw it out because it was so awful. I love croissants but not these. My hubby brings me ones back from Montreal that are all squished and they are 100% better.  Wait staff is rather inattentive.

Love the ambiance & the outdoor fire with bar. The problem is that they have a very limited menu. I'll go to have a drink & appetizers but not excited about the menu. Great place to hang with friends & just have a night out.  Wish they'd have more to choose from when I'm hungry!

This review is for breakfast only.  We have never had lunch or dinner. We has Creole Eggs and grits.  I enjoyed it.  

Also had eggs, potatoes with corned beef hash.  Very fair but not spectacular. 

We had a very sweet old lady helping us.  Not particularly fast but very nice.

I enjoyed my breakfast.

Horrible, I wouldn't recommend this dealership to my worst enemy. This was back at the end of April and it was the first time I would be purchasing a new vehicle. I went to look at a gmc sierra and the sales associate was rude. His name was ray and he kept continually saying I don't like to waste my time to me before, during and after the test drive. We started negotiations and he continued to be rude. We also talked to the manager (RJ) and he was extremely rude. I left there disgusted, they made me feel like crap and thank you ray for wasting my time because in the end I went to pointe gmc and bought a 50,000 dollar truck from them. I just have no idea how they are open if they treat any of their customers the way they treated me.
Food was OK if you are dying for cajun food and no other options exist but the food was so so and the service was not that good...Go to the ACME Oyster house instead....MUCH MUCH BETTER!
Always consistently delicious . We miss the management and staff who were always so welcoming and hope everyone is doing well!

Had two of their savory crapes - wow! Amazing!  It was so tasty and perfectly seasoned.  I took a friend there to catch up.  We had a wonderful time and felt safe with their Covid precautions they practiced.  I would love to go back and try more of their menu items.

I have been to redstone twice now last time was more then 5 years ago food was pretty good from what I remember and second time was last night a few buddies and I went there for dinner and we sat at the bar the bartenders were really nice drinks were good but the food wasn't ..we ordered naked grilled wings with the sauce on the side and they were nothing special they weren't that hot and the meat was kinda chewy as a matter of fact we didn't even finish them and then I ordered a redstone burger asked for it medium and it came out kinda mushy again not super hot not much flavor at all the fries were cold and overall it wasn't that great of a meal and for a almost 20 dollar burger I was deff not impressed at all I won't be going back save urself some money and go to five guys if u want a decent burger cuz redstone is not that great

The hotel was clean and relatively affordable; however, this is NOT a 4 star hotel. I paid over $100 the second night (Weekend rate) BUT that was on me for not catching it when I booked through Expedia.  Good breakfast everyday until 10 AM. Free shuttle bus to the downtown hub (STOPS PICKING UP AT 9 PM). The title of Downtown is misleading because you do need a car or uber to get to the downtown area. I think the shuttle should run a little later than 9 PM to justify the price and title of "downtown".  Staff is super friendly.

Seriously disappointed. We've been waiting for the day when we could afford to try out The Gallery, and today was the day! We wanted bottomless mimosas and great pastry. 

When we sat down, we were never given menus or silverware- we had to ask for both. Then, I ordered the bottomless mimosas, and by the time the server, Ariel H came back to take our order, 20 minutes had passed, and I still didn't have my first mimosa. I didn't even remind her about it because I knew I wouldn't get it for another 20 minutes, and by then, what was the point of "bottomless"? 

We got a couple of entremets, and while they were gorgeous, they didn't actually taste that great, and definitely weren't worth $8 each. After we finished eating our (quite good) omelette, it took Ariel another 10 minutes to notice that we needed our check. We sat at the bar and felt totally ignored. 

I would love a coupon for bottomless mimosas on a day that isn't Saturday, because I imagine that on any other day we would have had better service and we'd like to give the pastry another chance. And maybe I could try the mimosas finally.

Jealously struck as I viewed pic after delicious pic of Yelpers trips to The Gallery Pastry Shop. One Sunday morning, I packed up my bookbag to head off to the shop for a working brunch (yes, that's a real thing). It took me a few laps around the 54th street to figure out where the heck the place was at, but it was worth the trouble. 

Immediately loved the atmosphere. Bright, airy, with plenty of natural light because the garage door was open. Nice touch! I was dining solo and it wasn't too packed so I was able to snag a table instead of sitting at the bar area near the kitchen. The menu was limited, but pretty fascinating. I already knew I wanted the crepes. I started off with the glass slippers tea, which was just ok. Then I ordered a sweet and a savory crepe. I loved how you had the option unlimited add on's to your crepe. Sweeeeettt!! Mushrooms, cheese, asparagus, sausage. I wanted it all! For the sweet crepe, I had to have the banana foster. It didn't take long for my crepes to arrive. Mmmmmm, so incredibly delicious! Well worth the 15 bucks for two. My only complaint is that they should have placed my crepes on different plates or one with a divider. I had mushrooms in the whipped cream. That was a bit annoying. The potatoes were a bit overcooked. I ordered in the infamous eclair with the blueberry sauce to go. Silly me, I left the  $5 eclair in the car for a few hours so by the time I remembered it was a dry mess. Sigh... FYI - although some crepes are gluten free, the ones are the Pastry Shop are not. Sorry gf peeps.

This place is definitely worth a visit. Nice atmosphere, service, and delicious crepes!!

Brunch with kids and hubby @ Redstone was a hit. Started with their famous Bloody Mary with bacon cheese cubes and olives filled with cheese and Jumbo buffalo shrimp . The Omelet , the Margherita flat bread and the egg Benedict were all very delicious with the servers all so professional and courteous . Will
Visit soon and bring more friends and family . The host even sent a complimentary pastry to make up for the wait .

I don't even know what the inside of this place looks like. Is that crazy? Well when you have an amazing outdoor patio and bar like Redstone does, then I don't see any reason to go inside! 

Redstone is in our rotation of great local restaurants with friendly bartenders, great wine/cocktail lists, and creative cuisine. We find ourselves here often, especially when the weather is agreeable. And the outdoor patio/bar is covered, so no need to run for the hills if a rain shower rears its ugly head.

We've been here for everything from Saturday afternoon cocktails, to dinner with our parents. Their menu is inspired and plentiful without being fatiguing. Patrons and staff alike are truly friendly. Striking up a conversation with other people at the bar is welcomed and we love that. Who needs stuffiness in such a nice atmosphere? 

Parking is a-plenty, but it's also an easy place to Uber in and out of. 

Cheers to mild weather and outdoor dining. May winter forget to show up this year!

This pop up has a goal in mind and they execute it well. 
It is the perfect mix of campy and creepy. 
Drink prices were a little high especially compared to the adjacent bars but they made them pretty strong.
Not terrible, but you can probably walk through this thing in 10 minutes. But for $5, not bad value

Called to place an order was told to go online advised I was driving the host placed me on hold for 15 mins and never got back on the phone. HORRIBLE SERVICE FOOD NOT CORRECT WAITED 15 mins for someone to come out curbside and everyone that I interacted with today was horrible including the manager , Britney and Justin. Will NEVER COME TO THIS LOCATION AGAIN!!!!!

My wife and I dined there last night for the first time.  The waitress informed us that everything was cooked on-site.  We ordered the Buffalo Shrimp and within five minutes it was brought out.  Fast I thought for shrimp.  It was fully cooked but the termperature was cool.  For the main course I had the BBQ Ribs and Chicken while my wife had the Crab Cakes.  Again the food came quickly and again, while it had been obviously cooked, it was cool as if it had sat around the kitchen.  They do cook everything on-site, but apparently they cook it up in advance and just wait for someone to order it.  It was the worst $78.00 I ever spent on dinner.  There are far too many great restaurants in the Marlton area to waste money on food that sat around waiting for a customer.  The least they could do if theyre going to serve old food is invest in a heat lamp.

What a great place! You have to get a chocolate pillow (w/ hazelnuts). Incredible! Just stopped in for a cappuccino and the chocolate pillow so we didn't get to try any of the crepés. The cappuccino was decent but nothing to wow over. We sat at the counter. The employees working there seemed humorless and unfriendly. The hostess and our server were kind and friendly.

I have always heard of the Gallery Pastry Shop but have never visited, but I am happy that I finally did!! The best way to describe the atmosphere is a combination of modern and hipster,which is very fitting with Indy vibe. The food is amazing! You can create your own crepes and omelettes, so I did the crepe option. You can choose two crepes, which is perfect to satisfy your sweet and savory cravings. Loved this place and can't wait to go back!

Very friendly staff and free shuttle rides to downtown.  This location needs a few updates but the room was very clean!   Our room was nice and quiet too, I barely heard anything at all outside our door.  I do wish the room & bathroom had better lighting though.  Free breakfast had a great assortment, but the hot food was a bit soggy due to the accumulation of steam in the warming dishes.  Honestly though, I don't think this can be avoided unless they were to waste a lot of food and change out the pans more often.  And, the cooking staff were all pleasant as well.  The hotel shuttle runs downtown about every 30 minutes, and, you can catch the city bus right across the street from the hotel.  Overall everything was fine.  It may not be my first choice for a return stay, but no major issues.

Overrated, overpriced. Too dark to see the flippin' menu. The calamari was okay. The drink was eh. The waitress was forgetable, though I won't hold that against her--though the fact that I couldn't hear her, I will. 

Had the grilled steak sandwich. Arugula and crispy onion rings on a sandwich with steak. How could this be bad? But it kinda was. 

If I want to drink myself to sleep in an underwhelming but costly booth, I'll stop by Redstone again some time.

My friend and I came here for Brunch on a Saturday. We started w the mimosas that was $25 for a bottle of champagne and choice of juice. 

I cannot have dairy so my options were limited. I did go w the Vegan Hash. It was made w basic ingredients but was so delicious. I also had the brioche toast w berry compote. 

The service was amazing. 

We went inside and got some pastries to go. This place is reasonably priced and deliver amazing products.

The service was good, the prices for meals are high.  The services size for the appetizer and meal are small portions. This was the first time I went to a restaurant and no one had any left overs. We were celebrating a birthday and the waiter said happy birthday and you can buy a slice of cake from the desert menu. The food was just okay. For the price it was not worth it.

Now I love The Gallery Pastry Shop BUT what I do not love is taking the time to call and make a reservation only to find out upon arrival there is no record of my reservation. I have learned after several visits a reservation is important and it has been told to avoid any issues is to make a reservation. I wasn't the only person to experience a lost reservation the day another person was complaining about their reservation being lost as well. The only thing that saved the situation is that we got there early enough it wasn't a problem.  Now let me get to the brass tax the food on the other hand is ALWAYS on point. By the time I got to Gallery I was starving and wanted all of my favorites so I got a build your own omelette, berry trillium on a croissant, and has browns. I must have say they stepped up the presentation of the trillium it was so pretty I didn't want to eat but as I said I was hungry so I did lol. I love the options that you can get with the omelette and it always seem so fresh. My omelette had chorizo, feta cheese, red peppers, and mushrooms. The hash browns always tasty and crisp but on this visit they were a bit on the harder side. Overall, another tasty visit to Gallery. I just hope they get their reservation situation together soon.

Love the buffalo shrimp here they are delicious. I'm giving this place 4 stars instead of 5 because I wish they had more options on their menu. It can feel a bit limited and it also changes so you may not be able to get the something you enjoyed if you come back a few months later. Despite this, the food is delicious and the service is good. However the lighting is abnormally dark in the restaurant but great place overall

With the NCAA HQ next door, and the title "Hall of Champions," you would believe that this would be an enticing exhibit of great materials, such as news headlines, videotapes, great speeches by motivating coaches.  It's nothing of the sort.  It's not worth the small price of admission.
Stayed here on 6/21 with some friends. Easy access to the highway, shuttles to downtown Nashville, very clean hotel, friendly staff. Great breakfast variety! A tad pricey but worth it

Easy review! 

Near perfect restaurant - excellent food, beautiful atmosphere & great service. 

The downside - pricing is a bit high. 

With dinner plans later on, we opted for appetizers for our lunch. 

The chicken salad stuffed avocados were so, so, good and were a generous portion - 3 big halves of whole avocados (if that makes sense?). 

The flat bread pizza was good, especially the crust it was on - not crisp at all. 

Lastly - the absolutelydelicious crab dip!  My Lord - this is the "ringer!" 

We're looking forward to our next trip already!!!!

Let me start w/dessert. That chocolate cake was really good and moist.  After it arrived at the table, it didn't look like it'd be good but it actually was. That banana cream pie was also good with fresh bananas inside. Not mushy at all. 

Came here off a recommendation and wasn't too impressed. The drinks were very good and strong. 

The ribs were tender and had some flavor, just needed some more cause on top. The meat was just falling off the bones with a slight tug at it.  The Buffalo shrimp were huge and good. They weren't spicy, kinda wish it had a slight kick to it. One of our orders came with fries and they were nice and salty, had a crunch to them and were nice and hot. The garlic mashed potatoes were good also. Not too much garlic, just enough and they were nice and creamy. 

Overall, it was ok. The food was wasn't too impressive to me. I felt like the inside was too dark. We had one light over our table and the other lights were very dim.

I needed a WiFi thermostat installed and Hello Tech sent an IT person who didn't know the product well enough to know it needed a specific connection - a C-Wire. Please note- this tech was punctual and personable and knows computers very well and was able to set up my home alarm system - but not thermostats. 

This caused my house to heat up to 92 degrees one day while I was at work - when you selected "cool", heat would come on. 

The most upsetting part of this experience is that I begged them to send someone else and they refused and sent the same tech. 

After spending two hours on the phone with India, he was unable to get this new thermostat to work and thankfully he was at least able to connect my old thermostat until I figured out my next move. 

I called an AC guy who showed up within a few hours and got everything working perfectly in no time.

What's really upsetting is when I asked for my money back, Hello Tech instead reimbursed me for the AC guy's work which was $20 less than their charge. How does this make any sense? You sent someone who couldn't complete the work, shouldn't you not charge at all? I will never use Hello Tech again nor will I recommend them.

Food used to be good from here. But now every single time I order takeout from here there's either something in the food that shouldn't be (like grill brushes, hairs, pieces of napkin) or the food is just inedible because it was made wrong. I got a soup once that was so salty it was like pickle juice. I don't complain though because one of the guys that works the phone or something just gets really rude and confrontational. I miss when the food used to be good from here it was my favorite restaurant. RIP

Oh man! I LOVE this place. Cookie dough???!!!! You can't go wrong. They allow you to taste test before you make a selection. The dough taste fresh and delicious. The cookie dough is good for 4 days so if you get a nice helping, you don't have to consume it all in one sitting. Nevertheless, great service and great dessert.

Beware!!!!  Extremely disappointed how the owner Kathryn has decided to treat her long term customers so disrespectfully and allow her groomers to make decisions on what your pet needs.  Our gorgeous golden doodle was completely shaved without our approval and was washed with an oatmeal shampoo (that he is highly allergic too) as well!  His sanitary trim was cut so closely (the area blistered and we had to spend $200+ at the vet (and had to have our doodle do sit spats in the tub for a week)!

We've been clients of Poochinis for over a year and have referred countless others. We trusted our wishes would be adhered to and now feel betrayed.  When we discussed this situation with Kathryn, she argued with us for over 30 minutes (talking over us/defending the groomers actions/no apology/no refund or discount/no resolution) and actually blamed us!  Also Kathryn apparently video records all  happenings inside the salon (customers should be made of aware of this).  I wish we were aware of Kathryn's business practices, this is why I decided to write this review, to warn others.  The saddest part is how devastated our sensitive golden doodle has reacted, he literally has been acting as if this event has traumatized him
ADORABLE place. Lovely outside seating, great brunch menu, delicious desserts and good service! I will be back for sure. Would highly recommend.

Loved this small location tucked away in SoBro (Southern Broadripple) with a myriad of choices the pleasant staff didn't have any issue explaining all of our choices. My daughter had come before to attend a cake decorating class which is one of their many cooking class offerings.  So upon their request to come for an after school snack I was more than happy to oblige. 

The interior give a nice homey feel without the forced look to be too much and while maintaining a professional ambiance. The open kitchen becomes the focal point and I'm a sucker for kitchen sitting. The chefs were seemingly unaffected by our eyes following them as they completed their daily task work. 

Finally, the food. We ended up with about one of everything. And it was amazing. Buttery crisp and flaky bread, creamy and wonderfully textured and sweet fillings! Even the ice cream was great!

I'd highly recommend just stopping in just because, maybe grab and expresso and a croissant and enjoy!
Fun experience, great server, drinks were not bad. Had the vampire kiss, con azucar and a watermelon margarita.

Amazing brunch and pastries! This place is definitely a place to go for a "boujee" or special brunch with the significant other or the girls! Been here a few times and the first time we sat inside by the window where we could watch them prepare our brunch and watch them construct the pastries they were working on..so cool! The outdoor patio area is shaded and felt great on the sunny hot day we were there. I've had the hash a couple of times as well as the fruit plate with the delicious lemon curd, along with their omelettes, also delicious! Let's not forget about the macaroons this place offers! The day I went I had one each of the white chocolate and the pistachio. Both so light and airy yet crispy, and melt in your mouth. On Wednesday's they offer $1 macs and have a good selection of variety and flavors to choose from. Oh and I also had this Bavarian cream with banana, and coconut pastry that was pretty much summer on a plate for a pastry! Friends had the cheesecake-so smooth and velvety, and the PB & J pastry..also noteworthy and equally as delicious! We were lucky enough to go on their bottomless mimosa day, and besides your typical champagne and OJ mix, they also offer grapefruit and blood orange juice as mixers. Also the outdoor patio is dog friendly!

My first time here was for their weekend brunch.  Our large group was very well taken care of with fast friendly service.  The omelets and crepes were liked by all and the drinks were delicious.  It was a nice morning and  lots of people were sitting outside in the sunny weather.  It was easy to order and easy to pay with our large group.  I like the weekend brunch idea with lots of options for things to put in the omelets and crepes.  It's a little pricey, but the food in fresh and made to order.  Their desserts looked amazing, I will have to try one next time I go.  Their caramelized fruit dish was very good, I recommend it!
Whether you're in the mood for brunch, beautiful pastries & desserts or champagne, Gallery Pastry Shop has you covered! I loved the ambiance and decorative space!
Work was completed correctly and in short time.  I love the idea that they contact you by email.
Great staff, very helpful . Kept me from getting the wrong ammo.......long story but great help. Highly recommended these guys to anyone
The food is always top notch and the environment is super welcoming! Our server was super helpful and personable! Such an enjoyable experience

This place slaps. The end. Seriously though, their breakfast is always delicious, fresh, and perfectly seasoned. I've tried many items now and they are all fantastic but some top favorites are the hash, crepes, JTL, and croissant and gravy. Lattes could use a little work. But overall great atmosphere, staff, and food.

This spot is decent, but the service is questionable at best. I called ahead to secure a reservation for 7:15 last week. The man on the phone was very courteous but I could tell he must have been busy. When I arrived the black host sat me, he was polite and charming, but I was surprised by how young he looked. When I sat down I was waited on by Alicia. She was okay, she seemed stressed but remained helpful and kind. The entre came out close to an hour later and our substitutions were incorrect, but I have to admit the food was still pretty good. The manager, I believe his name was Garrett, stopped by and inquired about our dining experience. Although the dinner was a little rough in the middle, the few people made our overall experience welcoming. I wholly intend on going back there!

This is one of those places that a local wouldn't be caught dead in. I tried to duck in here for drinks during a festival but the line was a mile long.  The food is good but their cool factor is in the toilet.

We were told a wait of sixty minutes give or take 10 minutes.  After an hour I wanted to check where we were and told next table was ours.  Given away.  Waited hour and half told them we were leaving and another hour after that I got a text my table was ready.  Was chaotic and not in a good way.  Was treated very rudely.

I just can't keep away from this SoBro gem. I have one word for you. Provence. It's this wonderful lavender mousse pastry that I'm pretty sure is also made with angel kisses and Tinkerbell's fairy dust. It will make you that happy. It is so incredibly light and melts in your mouth. If you're looking to go the opposite route and want something chocolatey and rich, you can't go wrong with the chocolate pillow. It's chocolate heaven. The macarons are divine, and I haven't met one that I don't like yet. But my favorites are the lemon and the Earl Grey. Go on Wednesday's to try them out. On Wednesday's you gets Macs for $1!!!!! Best day ever. I've also had the Creme Brûlée and almond croissant. Both are amazing. You can add European butter to accompany your croissant and I would go for the upcharge. It's worth it, I promise. 
Onto the space. I love, Love, the open space, and the fact that you can see everything that is going on in the kitchen. I could sit there for hours and watch them create pastry masterpieces. Find them on Instagram. Follow them. You won't be disappointed. But most importantly, you have to stop by and try this place.

This is my closest wawa to my house and It sucks because it's also the worst one in the area. First of all it's super old and tiny and the parking situation is annoying there's no clear arrows direct people which way to go.  To top it off it's in the middle of a crazy intersection and they have no bathroom. The cashiers are usually nice as other reviews mentioned but the people that make the food have been getting progressively ruder. I always thank them when they call my number because I do generally appreciate someone making me food and I work in customer service so I get how much it can suck. But lately, they are really slow and don't even acknowledge me when I address them which i find a little  weird. Like I get it's not a dream job but like damn

Very nice place.  
The quick menu for covid outside dining has a very nice array of choices. 
The coconut shrimp and Bang bang cauliflower for starters was very good.  Cooked perfectly and good portion given. 

The chicken copied salad was a winner to my test buds. The freshness was very taste able.  The portion was enough to fill me but not make me feel stuffed. 

The Banana Cream Pie.  A must try. Again a generous portion to share or eat alone.  Each bite you taste the flavor.  

The outside seating by the water is very good. Nice breeze from the water was felt. Even in the 96 degree weather.

The waitress was very tentative and had no problem answering all my questions.  

A very good ex experience and will be back for sure.
Terrible service,  very rude staff. We made reservations and they "lost them." I would never go back here. It was supposed to be a surprise party and it was a terrible experience.
I went in to have a ring prong repaired, and Eric was able to fix it on the spot.  He also didn't charge me and we had a stimulating conversation. I highly recommend!

Only come here if you're ready to be blown away at every bite!! Seriously, everything we tried was amazing. I was in Indy for a wedding and saw this place on a list of must go's. It was the perfect afternoon hangout for a quick caffeine and sugar hit! A friend and I split the espresso layer cake and pumpkin croissant and each got a latte. Mine was a Graham Cracker latte with oat milk and hers was the Pear Lavender latte. While the lattes did take a little while to come out, we barely noticed because we were fighting over the pumpkin croissant! 
Everything was so fresh and flavorful and we were both very impressed with their local sourcing! Ambience was also super cozy and Instagram-able! 

We were so impressed with our whole experience that we came back before our flight a few days later and they did not disappoint!

This is probably my new favorite pastry shop. It's super cute and quaint. The decor is very vintage and Rustic at the same time. The staff was super sweet and helpful even getting my puppy a bowl of water. The pastries are to die for. And it's even more awesome that they have an open kitchen where you can watch them work. Super perk $1 macaroons on Wednesday's.

Redstone, where have you been? Like, why am I just meeting you?

Beautiful establishment. Excellent Service. Love a server that will steer me in the right direction as well. 

So after a day of retail therapy it was time to dine. Gary the Manager was so pleasant along with the staff. 

We ordered Buffalo Cauliflower, Calamari and Brussel Sprouts as appetizers - delicious. 

For dinner I had the Prime Rib which came with a mashed potato. Someone else ordered a steak and the fish. Presentation alone was amazing. Did I mention we had the cornbread. They brought baked beans and they were good. Redstone, you just may be my favorite stone. 

Following dinner your are given warm towels. I just loved this place. I'll be back.

If there's a place like this in CT, someone please tell me because this was a total gem. Eclectic atmosphere, delicious food, and they even offer classes! I had a raspberry white mocha and a chocolate pillow, others enjoyed an amazing almond croissant, open faced grilled cheese and of course, macarons! Very much enjoyed this place!

TGPS,
Thanks for hosting me on my "Treat Yo Self" forced PTO day. Lol. You never disappoint! The JLT was bomb!!! It had been far too long, and I promise not be a stranger.

I can't actually review any of the food, drinks, or desserts at Gallery Pastry Shop. I couldn't get any of the hipsters working there to even acknowledge me. No one said "we'll be with you in a minute" or asked if we'd been helped. I stood there, with my mother, right by the sign that says "Please wait to be seated." If you're looking for amazing desserts AND good service, I highly recommend the Cake Bake shop in Broadripple.

You are about to read a review of the worst dealership I visited during my search for a new car. I visited about 7 dealership last August/September.

This dealership played phone tag with me for two weeks regarding the purchase of a new buick. They even managed to make me the best offer on a new lease beating every other offer by $30/month. So how could they possibly be getting 1 star? 

Here is how:

1. I went for a test drive, liked the car, sales associate ran some numbers. I left dealership saying I will think about it.

2. Sales associate calls just about everyday for the next week. Offering better and better deals. 

3. I say the deal sounds great, can you please clean the car and I will come purchase. Associate says we need to run your credit first. My credit is run for the first time.

4. With a fresh credit inquiry and an autographed check I visit the dealership and behold the vehicle is not clean or ready (odd). I leave dealership, and get a call the next day about the mishap.

5. I say I will comeback tomorrow but have the vehicle clean and ready. Upon my return the vehicle is clean, but has small chips all over it( AND IT IS BRAND NEW). I ask what the chips are all over the hood. The salesman asks the detailer in front of me if the detailer went over the chips. He says yes but I could not get those out!! 

And there it is, weeks and weeks of phone tag, three visits to the location 2 inquiries on my credit report, and they tried to sell me a vehicle 2013 model year that was STATIONED AT THE SHORE DURING HURRICANE SANDY! Ah, no wonder the car was never cleaned. They don't want those little chips glistening in the sun!

I asked if they would offer me the same deal on a similiar car in the lot. The answer was a defiant no. HA caught red handed, wasted two weeks of my time, and a few hours, 10 voicemails and another hour in talk time. They still had the audacity to call me the next day and offer me the other vehicle at a higher price.

Guess what Barlow Buick?

Barlow even managed to ruin the fact that I originally wanted a Buick. I went all the way to another dealership spent $60/month more and own a Cadillac now. Oh, they clean the cars there everyday too, they were doing it when I arrived. They treated me like the prince of friggen' Egypt, I think they are building a shrine to me there now. I still get calls asking about my purchase , if I am happy and if there is anything they can show me or help me with. I only have ONE credit inquiry from them(and I actually bought the car there). They service it for free, were polite when I bought it and installed aftermarket options for me as part of the deal. I get cookies when I show up and a handshake after my oil change.

BUT I didn't need and don't need any of that! I needed a little integrity and customer service AND they had that, needless to say your place did not, does not, and probably will never.

DO NOT EVEN THINK ABOUT BUYING A CAR HERE!

Take your business anywhere else, I wanted to ride a bike around town after this experience.

Allllll I know is that I can't wait to go back.

I was in a daydream the entire time I was here. Yes, I had just woken up, but this dream was related to the beauty that is Gallery Pastry Shop: Wood-paneled outside, mismatched vintage chairs, velvet sofa, sexy lighting, friendly staff, a lit-up display of gorgeous desserts. 

I've heard that macaroons are only $1 in Wednesday's, but I believe that brunch is where it's at. There's a fun brunch menu that allows you to create your own crepes: one savory, one sweet. The beermosa also looked delicious- even better than a mimosa. 

I was in a hurry, so I opted for something fast and ordered the croissant with Tulip Tree cheese. Sounds simple right?! 

I don't know what I expected, but this was OUT OF THIS WORLD. It came on a large plate with a beautiful presentation. The cheese in the croissant had been caramelizad and the cheese was already melting from the inside out. There was fresh, chunky jam, and honey drizzled over the whole thing. Amazing. Instead of being handed a simple piece of bread, I was handed this wonderful slice of heaven. 

I can't even imagine what it'll be like next time when I can stick around for a full brunch but I can't WAIT.

I feel badly giving a subpar rating but I was very unimpressed by what we got for $22 per ticket. The actual "haunted house" was well done enough. Great example of making the best of their COVID situation. We felt safe yet spooked. Then you return outside to grab a drink and sit at the halloween decorated benches. Unfortunately when you walk up to get the free drinks there's no signage for what is included so we just picked something off of what looked to be a separate halloween menu to find those drinks were not part of our ticket. Then the bartender had no idea what we were actually allowed to get with our tickets and it was just an uncomfortable situation where I had to pay $12 for a drink that I thought was included in my ticket.

I stopped in on a weeknight with some co-workers for a few cocktails. The restaurant itself is large and has a nice atmosphere. The bartenders were attentive and refilled my water without me having to ask. The cocktails I tried were delicious and not watered down. I asked the bartender whether I should go with the white or red sangria and he suggested the red. His suggestion was spot on as the red was not as sweet as the white. The crab dip was pretty decent and a perfect choice to share over cocktails. Taking a look at the menu, it is a little pricey but from my experience with each of my choices in cocktails and appetizer the quality is definitely present so I didnt really mind it. The outside dining area was beautiful and a perfect setting for summer cocktails.

This isn't the first time I come to this place, I've always love to have brunch here with my friends; I've decided to make a reservation and celebrate my birthday, and when I arrived; the host was really rude with me, a bad rushing aptitude towards me and my friends, and service were rushed up since they have a wedding event at 12 noon; and my reservation was made at 11am.
I can't believe that one of my favorite places to have brunch, became such a bad experience and the worst thing, on my special day, my birthday and with my friends present.
This was a terrible experience. I can't express with words how mad I am for this situation.

So, I love everything about this place!!! The breakfast omelets (unlimited toppings), crepes, and of course the desserts! It is so classy here and the ambiance is so perfect for a friends catch up session or even a birthday brunch!

It is so clean and so classy! I truly can't stop coming back to this place. One thing I LOVE is that every Wednesday the macaroons are $1 each vs. the $2.50 normal cost. So, someway, somehow I make my way out here every Wednesday for $1 macaroons! This really makes the place stand out!

Also, there are books everywhere: in the restaurant and even in the bathroom! It's like a mini library! The back outside patio is so friggin adorable... it's a little hidden but totally adorable! 

My only concern with this place is that the desserts are pretty expensive and the portions are a bit small. Will I be back? Duh!... next Wednesday :)

This place is amazing! I'm here almost every weekend and the food is always wonderful! The service is wonderful as well! Be sure to check out the pastries and start with a fruit brûlée. You will not be disappointed!

Went for a special Sunday brunch with girlfriends. Had an extremely strange server who kept checking in on us to see when our last guest was arriving. When she arrived, the server was nowhere to be found and we had to track her down to place our order. One guest asked for NO PEPPERS in her dish, as she is allergic. When our plates arrived, they were garnished with a topping. My allergic friend... you guessed it... hers was topped with red peppers. We flagged the server down, and she immediately went into a rant, expressing that it wasn't her fault.  Before our food arrived, the server was clearing the table of debris such as paper from sugar packets. She snapped up my bag that was in front of my glass, which contained my important medication that I needed to take after I had eaten some food. I pulled it out of her hand and told her not to touch my medicine. She left in a teary state, exclaiming that she didn't know, over and over. The oddness continued.

The brunch items are extremely overpriced. An average size omelet with a teeny portion of soggy home fries and 1 slice of bread. $15. No thank you. You can get much better food at your local diner!

The gallery pastry shop reminds me of the old saying if everyone was jumping over a bridge. The service is horrible.  After we placed our drink order it took them 20 minutes to bring a nuke warm dirty chai latte, which was not even what I ordered.  At which point I sent it back and didn't order anything to drink in fear that it would take another 20 minutes for it to get to me. I orsder the omelet in a side a hash Browns. However  the server must have decided that I didn't need the hash Browns. So, I never got them. The environment was awful, over crowded, loud and noisy.  In truth the whole experience ruined our entire day.
Eaten there several times and the food is good but really go for the  outside bar with firepits.....lots of people on weekends which makes it a party like scene !!

Fell in love with the gallery pastry shop the minute I opened the door and nearly fainted from happiness when told it was one dollar macaron night! BEST MACARONS EVER-not because they were one dollar, because they are the BEST EVER. Perfectly "snappy" wafer (not sure if that's the correct term) and the inside was moist and rich with flavor.
Sat down with some friends for a bit of a "pre-meeting, meeting" so we were not able to stay as long as I wish we could, but I will definitely be back soon! The lights were dim and it was already dark outside (they have a garage door type wall which I assume provides a beautiful natural light during the day) and my phone was not taking pictures that did the space justice. My friends and I could not get over the decor. I want to bring everyone here because it is the perfect pastry shop and every single item on the menu sounds delicious and needs to be tried!
The location weirded me about at first, I questioned whether the shop existed after accidentally driving past the turn in...twice. Just keep driving back into that cove--you're not lost and it's obviously worth it!

For as long as I've had The Gallery Pastry Shop bookmarked, I thought it was just a pastry shop; however, I recently learned they also serve brunch, so I made plans with a friend at 10:30 a.m. on a Sunday. I had a little trouble finding it because it's set back off the road a bit, in a sort of business cul-de-sac. We had no trouble finding parking and were immediately seated at the bar, where we had a bird's eye view of the kitchen staff, busy at work. 

I believe everything is locally sourced, so the menu options are pretty limited. We both ordered cheese and bacon omelettes with hash browns and both were pretty bland. They don't have ketchup. The star of the meal was the croissant with brulee trillium and berry compote. It was presented well and full of flavor. That's why I gave them four stars versus three. 

I'm a sucker for french macarons, so we also took home a dozen, but they were disappointing compared to other bakeries in the area. With the exception of the Earl Gray Tea and sea salt caramel, the rest lacked flavor and were kind of ugly. Nevertheless, I've signed up for a french macaron class here to learn how to make them. I plan to try something else from the pastry counter during my return trip.

Food was decent, but nothing to write home about. Service was subpar. Server brought out wrong meal to my wife and forgot my cocktail sauce. On top of that, my wife's shrimp and grits was only warm when it was brought out to her and half way through it it had cooled down to being too cold to eat. 
Fountain drinks are $2.75 and do NOT come with refills. 

Only shimmer of hope was the FREE glass of wine we received by checking into Yelp.

Today I visited The Gallery for a neighborhood meeting. The large dining tables and benches are really neat for groups. There's an amazing light fixture above the table where I sat. 

I overheard someone say "grapefruit mimosa" and my eyes darted straight to the menu  I ordered one for myself and warm bread pudding to go with it. 

The mimosa was just $5 and the bread pudding was very very tasty. Someone said they made the bread pudding with croissants. Thy had me at the caramel drizzle.

Okay...we've been here three times, twice because other people invited us, once because I was soooo hungover and thought I was getting the brunch.  

We had dinner there, and it was okay, expensive but okay.  We had brunch there and I nearly died from the excitement over eggs benny w/crab and FREE CHAMPAGNE.  The bloody mary's, while $13/pop, had meat in the them.  That was really cool.

I had a four day bachelorette party in AC over Labor Day (yeah...) so drove home early Monday morning, and thought we were going to have brunch not realizing it was MONDAY and not SUNDAY...
So we ended up having lunch, and it was okay...expensive again...$15 for a roast beef sandwich?  But it was a tasty sandwich.  
The service is very good.

So dinner gets 3 stars.
Lunch gets 3 stars.
Brunch gets 18,000 stars.

Took my 15yo son here. To my surprise he sat through the entire 12 minute video presentation when you first walk in. The video is very inspiring! Makes me wish I had done sports in college. 
The first floor of the museum has exhibits on the various sports in the NCAA. There are touchscreen monitors with videos to watch. The exhibits are bigger than life but not very engaging. The upstairs had a bball court you can shoot on, an interactive football and soccer exhibit (a bit dated) and  a few other things.
Overall I was expecting more to be honest of the NCAA Hall of Champions. I'm glad we went and check this off the list but unfortunately it's not an engaging enough place to return to.

Okay, first of all I went to Poochinis because of the reviews, the grooming itself was pretty good, but the terrible customer "service"  from Jim (owner's husband?) has left me aghast.  I had been warned about his attitude from somebody in the "pet" industry after the first time, but I didn't have to deal with him the first time, so I didn't understand.  The first appointment I had they told me to come back in two hours, I don't live close by so I went shopping, and ran some errands and came back in two hours.  The groomer told me she needed more time and asked if I could come back in an hour.  I went over to Saffron Indian Bistro(excellent food by the way, but I digress)  and placed an order to go, then went back to Poochinis.  There was nobody at the desk, but there was a pile of dog poop on the floor and a roll of paper towels and a spray bottle, and I went and picked up the dog pile, and cleaned it up because it appeared as if someone came out to clean it up but got called away.  No big deal, the place is clean, I was just helping out.  I waited for about 30 more minutes.  Jim came out and sat at the desk, and didn't say anything about the fact that the poop pile had been cleaned up, and frankly maybe he forgot it was there.  My dog was ready after 3 and and 45 minutes.  I went and picked up my food at Saffron (which had been sitting for an hour at that time) and left.  The grooming was good, the price was right, and I made another appointment.  

This place is close to my office so I booked for a day when we have our sales meeting 9am.  I brought him in at 8am and got a call that my dog was ready at  11am.  I said I would come at 1pm so as not to miss the rest of our meeting. Nope, there is no space you need to come now.  I left work, drove my dog home (nicely groomed) and missed the second half of my meeting.

Time number three,  I made an appointment for a Saturday, dropped him off at 8am, went to the farmer's market,, and then went to breakfast.  I heard my phone ringing after I ordered, I picked up and I got the incredibly rude Jim.  "Hello?" "This is Jim from Poochinis"....silence.    You have already received a call to pick up your dog.  (Which I didn't realize as it had only been an hour and a half at this time).  I said, 'oh I'm sorry, the last times it took three and four hours I didn't expect him to be done so early.  I just ordered breakfast I'll be there right afterwards:.  Rude Jim says, "it has never taken us three or four hours, you need to come pick up your dog right now."  Zing!  Um hello, I sat and waited for over an hour the first time (while cleaning up dog poop that wasn't my eight pound Maltese's poop, but a much larger breed.  Just sayin') Last time it was three hours.  He argued with me!  He said it never takes that long.  I was so ticked off that he was so nasty.  I went in to pick up my dog, and he launched right in about how they need to dogs to be picked up right away.  I informed him that he needed to learn customer service skills, and that some people don't belong in the front of the house.  He said that's fine.  We went into the whole how long it took before business and he said.....(here  comes the final straw)  "maybe you just didn't' pick up your dog for four hours, we never take that long.  Yeah, the customer is always right huh.  What a jerk.  I immediately called the vets office to tell them they were right about what they heard about this place.  Its a shame, but if this business plans to survive, Jim needs to find another job, if he is a part owner in this business then he needs to let his wife run it.  It is utterly ridiculous that he deals with the public.

Installed a 6 foot fence when I was to get a 8 foot fence. The expected dayof arrival was a no show no call. And the fence that is installed looks nice but is 18 inches short and does not touch my other fencing, so I have a 18 inch gap. I have to go out and purchace boards to fix myself.

We stayed here 2 nights.  Very friendly workers.   Lots of sitting areas to gather and talk in lobby and an area outside as well.  Room are decorated nice and roomy. 
The have a pool which we didn't use and a workout room. 

Breakfast was very good with plenty of options and included with room.  They open at 7 am but wish we could have gotten coffee earlier.  They do have coffee makers in the room but I don't ever like to use those.  

Shuttle service is very convenient.  It takes about 15 for shuttle to get you to downtown Nashville.   They drop you off at a designated spot.  So shuttle is approximately ever 1/2 hour depending on traffic.  I believe it holds 12 people so make sure to get out there early enough to get on.  We never had a problem.  Someone told me to tuber back was $8 one time when she checked and $18 another time.  (I'm sure due to demand)  You can actually walk over the pedestrian bridge and get to downtown Nashville.  I think about a mile.  

Hotel price  was inflated as I think to being on a weekend but being a AAA member saved us some $$. I did put in dates online and saw prices are much lower during the week. 

Not really any restaurants to walk to around hotel.  Really couldn't find any fast food nearby either.  I did hear flatbread pizza pretty good at bar.... Oh yea did I tell you they have a bar? 

Free parking 

We would possibly stay here again if we ever come back to Nashville
Always great meal and excellent service. I've never had a bad experience here. Their rotisserie chicken is great!

Metro fence did a fantastic job despite the negative reviews. Their prices far beat the competitors. Fence was perfectly done and couldn't be happier. Would recommend to anyone looking for a white vinyl fence.

Saying that this is my favorite South Jersey would be an understatement! I LOVE LOVE Redstone. It is the only Restaurant that has been consistent over the years!!! I hope they stay that way. When I am too lazy to dress up, I even get take out from here. The Cornbread is the best cornbread that I have ever had (Dont tell my mom lol) Its sooo amazing!!  The Meatloaf is my favoriteeeee. Like its so tender and filled with flavor. The Jerk Chicken Fondue is great also.!  If you want a solid American meal no surprises go here!

A very pleasant surprise. We went to Joli because we had a Valupak coupon.  I expected your run of the mill neighborhood pizza joint.  Joli is everything but that.  The food is fresh, well conceived and flavorful.  Our "Veggie Bon Bon" featured a house made mozarella, prosciutto di parma and a splendid supporting cast of flavors. Our Cir. 1897 pizza was delicious.  Unfortunately, it was a Saturday night and only 5 people were there.  If you live in the neighborhood, you owe it to yourself to discover this place. You won't be sorry.

After not having been to Redstone in a few years, I decided to check it out again with a friend a few nights ago. Luckily, the food was just as amazing as I remember it to be years ago. 

We went on a Thursday night around 7pm and it was completely packed. Many people were on the patio outside enjoying cocktails and meals, but the inside was just as busy. Upon arrival, we checked in the hostess stand, which had about 4 or 5 different hostess standing there. None of them were friendly or polite, but for some reason I wasn't surprised (and shows the reason I'm not giving 5 stars). 

After waiting around 30-40mins for our table, we were finally seated. Our waitress, on the other hand, was such a sweetheart and took time to carefully explain the menu and show us some favorites as well as the specials for the day. I ended up ordering the Rotisserie Chicken and my friend ordered the Chicken and Ribs. When our food arrived, I was surprised at how large the portions were and was actually unable to finish my whole meal. Nevertheless, the food was delicious. It was cooked well and had tremendous flavor. 

Other than the encounter with the hostess', I would definitely say we had a nice experience here and I would most likely come back again.

I've been there twice to have things fixed. Once a cell phone and once a MacBook. Both times they tried and were unsuccessful.  The people were nice, but could help me. Payed $26 once and $65 the other time.

Pros:
-EXCELLENT staff. Every single person was so friendly, sweet, and helpful to us. An extra shout out to  Tony (continental breakfast), Victor (shuttle driver), and Dorothy (front desk) for exceptional service.
-free shuttle downtown. It runs every half hour, and it's very prompt. 
-comfortable beds
-great selection for continental breakfast
-clean rooms
-reasonably priced

Cons:
-Not in a great neighborhood
-could not adjust temperature in the room, and it was way too hot
-they didn't have simple things such as band-aids at the front desk
-rooms look a bit outdated

Overall, a pleasant experience. I would stay here again.

Ordered a birthday cake last weekend and was blown away by how beautiful and delicious it turned out! We requested white cake with a little gold embellishment. It was perfect - even the chef who attended the party asked where I got it and repeatedly complimented it! Great shop to work with, excellent communication, and I am looking forward to visiting to dine in sometime very soon after seeing the shop and menu.

An awesome, eclectic atmosphere that has incredible food! Brunch is delicious and the pastries are a great addition to a meal. Would highly recommend the breakfast sammie with bacon. Great spot for date day or just a nice breakfast out!

Love this place For the ambience in the service and the food. I was a regular before the pandemic and since they've opened after the pandemic I've been there three times already and will be there again in the next week. I've never had a bad meal the food is excellent the desert is wonderful and the service is the best. I will continue to support them through the pandemic and after the pandemic

Awesome lil neighbor gem...Sunday Brunch Style...it's not just pastries uts great food

Food is fresh and creative.

Service with smiles and vibes

Atmosphere shabby chic yet comfy and groovy.

I don't want rave cause I wanna save this place just for me, but it is a must try in SoBro let alone the city!

Eat Local, Shop Local, Live Local JC

Bought a Treverse Saturday - my brother told me i had to check the place out. the entire staff was friendly and cared about my family's needs. Thank you Jim, I appreciate your professionalism and honesty. My wife & kids love the car - thank you!!
Social distance seating was followed, excellent holiday cocktails.  Great spot for a snack and drinks while shopping at The Prominade

Employees were rude and wouldn't help me with anything. 
Head to another place if you get the chance. Or take your chances. Was a wasted trip for me. Maybe you'll have better luck. Not a fan
Really great selection, and everything I've had here has been delicious. Probably the best pizza I've had in Pinellas county so far. Sad to see it gone.

Wow where do I start...first off I have to say Eric Sheffield is an amazing person! Down to earth, humble and relatable! I had the honor to help Eric and his lovely wife capture a wonderful moment during their wedding! Their day was perfect as a disney love story! 

About a few years later, it was my turn to open the chapter of love and go down the romantic and lovely journey. Love was no longer just a job for me but now it's time for it to become my life. Eric gave me the best experience ever.

The shop was beautifully displayed and the varieties of jewelry was endless. It was very clean, staffs were welcoming and they even offer complimentary coffee and water.

I was nervous! I didn't know where to start or how to begin. This is when Eric shined! He took me through the whole process from one end to the other explaining the history, story behind each brand, jewelry and company. I kid you not! This guy lives and breathes jewelry! He was very patient, knowledgeable and answered numerous of my questions professionally and willingly.

After hours of back and forth Eric finally laid out a perfect scenario and route for me to take which I totally loved and helped me decide when I was stuck at the fork on the road! This is top knock customer service and I did not feel like I was talking with a salemens but a consultant, yet more family! Eric never once judged what I was willing to spend, do or pick.

In closing, I had a lovely and amazing experience here and I would strongly recommend anyone to come check out Sheffields Diamonds! I will be returning to finish the other half of my scenario, which myself and my fiancé are ready to experience!

Thank you Eric and Sheffields Diamond for all you do! See you soon!

There was 6 of us there Friday night and it was disappointing!  I've been there multiple times and it's really gone down hill.  A few of us had dinner salads, $18 and it was the size of a side salad.  The brussel sprouts weren't nearly as good as they used to be and other meals ordered were sub par.  They included gratuity and our waitress never came around.

We have been using Poochini's for a number of years. However, I found it necessary to cancel all of our future appointments. Here is why:

The last two times I was expecting to get a call, as usual, that my dog's grooming was complete, I did not receive a call long after I expected to receive that call. On both occasions I decided, since I was in the area, to drop by and wait. On both occasions my dog was already done and was being warehoused in a cage. No telling how long. Either the organizational capabilities are no longer there or they just didn't care to place a phone call to let me know my dog was done.

The last time I picked up my dog, she was dirty. I have never before picked her up where it seemed like she didn't get a bath, but was only made wet.

Another reason I no longer want to use this company, is because they are very expensive and although they do a pretty good job cutting the dog, this client wants to feel appreciated; like something other than a number. Mr. Personality at the front desk does absolutely NOTHING to make me feel like I'm either valued as a client or wanted. Okay, I can take a hint, if you don't want my money I will be happy to give it to someone else for my grooming needs.

The other reviews are completely accurate. I'm so upset that I failed to check yelp before I picked this restaurant. 

I feel swindled out of a dinning experience. 

For starters, the customer service is non existent. Our waitress was so bad it almost felt like she personally hated us. She slammed down every plate and cup. She would disappear for long length of times, and she never did a two bite check (I used to be a waiter. The two bite check is where your waitress comes back and asks how is everything tasting/ if you need any anything before you really get into your meal).

Her entire demeanor was sour as if we were bothering her for ordering and being hungry. She never introduced herself. I only know her name because of the receipt (Lakeisha).

I know it's not fair to let one waiter destroy a restaurants reputation, and I am also a forgiving and gracious person. I would have overlooked the poor service had no other issues popped up. 

Gumbo Pot's food was edible but completely underwhelming. The food lacked seasoning, flavor, and all shreds of uniqueness. I have no idea why the sign outside says "Famous" because this food tasted like a microwave dinner. Also, for the blandness, lack of presentation, atmosphere, air conditioning, refills, and split checks, the prices have no right to be priced  that high.  The entrees were averaging around $20 but legitimately should have cost $10 for the low quality of food. 

Final take: Avoid the Famous Gumbo Pot unless nowhere else is available to eat and you are tired of walking in the Nola humidity.

This place is a hidden gem, literally! It's tucked away in South Broad Ripple in a strip of businesses. You won't be able to see The Gallery from the road, so be prepared to turn into the parking lot (or to do a quick turn around down the road like I had to) 

I visited The Gallery a Tuesday afternoon with a couple friends for brunch! We didn't make a reservation, but thankfully we didn't have to wait too long for a table. I would definitely suggest making a reservation prior to going just in case! The hostess/waitress was so friendly and provided helpful suggestions on the menu. I got the breakfast sammie and it was *perfect*! I will be day dreaming about that croissant sandwich until I get to eat it again. My friends got the crepes and were very happy with their choices as well. 

The ambiance was great and I can't wait to visit again!

Everyone we encountered were friendly and helpful.  Russ made the buying processes a very enjoyable one.  He was honest and truthful and should be commended.  If this type of service continues through the life of our vehicle you will have made us customers for life.

First problem, appetizer came out cold in the middle. Second, gumbo was fair at best, but my wife was served seafood gumbo when she ordered a sausage and chicken. Service was on the low side of average. The biggest disappointment came when I approached the manager to discuss my concerns. His attitude was indifferent and told me "it was not my fault". Obviously... I was their to enjoy new orleans at its best. Did't happen tonight. For the record, would have rated at a "2", but manager's lack of concern drops my rating to a 1. Find somewhere else yo spend your $.

Get your wedding cake from Gallery Pastry Shop!! I'm not kidding it was the best cake I have ever had. We originally went with them because we didn't want a huge cake and liked the idea of macaroons better. But when we tried their cake during our virtual tasting we knew we had to have it! They were easy to work with and accommodated our ever changing guest count (thanks covid ).

We got a two tier smaller cake for our wedding and I could not be happier. Also they told us on our first year anniversary they will give us a complimentary small cake so we don't have to eat frozen cakes!
