My partner and I decided to take a spontaneous trip to Nashville just for fun. We looked at lots of hotels downtown where the added parking cost was insane. We chose the Clarion because it was affordable and looked nice. Parking is included and there's even a constant free shuttle to get you downtown (which is at most 15 minutes). 
Upon arriving staff was so cheerful and friendly. The pair we checked in with around 4 on Sunday were great hosts! We did pay a bit extra for a room with a city view. It was so worth it! We were on the 4th floor so we worried we weren't high up enough but the view was great. The hotel lobby is very large and there's tons of places to hangout. The pool is nice but I wished it opened before 10AM! Their free breakfast is expansive- biscuits and gravy, eggs, sausage, potatoes, waffles, yogurt, cereal etc. I wake up early and usually leave the hotel room so others can keep sleeping. The staff in the early Monday morning was so cheerful, friendly and just fun to be around. Throughout our stay I was so impressed by the attitude of the workers. I have worked several hotels and resorts (multiple positions) and everyone here just seemed like a nice person ready to accommodate your requests or answer questions. It's difficult to staff a hotel so well- my hats off to the manager. 
The room itself was nice. There were a few marks on the walls and a lampshade was a bit ripped but none of that bothered us. The shower pressure was amazing- Id never comment on a shower but the one in 421 felt like a massage. The room was clean, beds were comfortable, sheets were soft and the view was great. We had a very loud fridge in our room and the very nice maintenance man found us a new quieter one in 15 minutes. He's great! 
Overall we loved our stay. We felt well taken care of and felt like we made a budget friendly choice without sacrificing quality.

This past weekend a group of friends and I made a reservation at the Gallery Pastry Shop for her birthday! There were quite a few of us, about 9 girls, so they made room for us at a large table outside. First off, when you visit the Gallery, you are immediately faced with the beautiful decor and scenery of this cute little brunch and pastry spot. The hippy and earthy feel of the atmosphere makes it both comfortable and aesthetically pleasing for any photoshoot that may or may not take place. 

After being greeted by the hostess, we were placed at our table soon after arriving. Since there were many of us and it was a busy Saturday afternoon, we had no issue waiting for a bit for our table. We started off with waters at the beginning but quickly ordered bottomless mimosas (tip: this is a great deal if you're having more than 3 glasses, which why wouldn't you). Although I could have easily indulged in their appetizers, such as the fruit plate with lemon curd which is always amazing, our group ordered our breakfast options after settling in with our champagne and juices. 

When it comes to the cuisine, this is no iHop-type breakfast place. (nothing against iHop, it's there when you need it.) The best thing about the Gallery is that everything on the menu has its own creative spin. I consider myself a very picky eater, so if you identify as the same you will still absolutely find a delicious meal for you! My favorite that I've had so far is the croissant and gravy with eggs on top. I always opt for my egg option to be scrambled instead of over easy as well as adding a little cheese on top. Despite their brunch, the macaroons and pastries are to die for if you prefer to have a quick snack. 

Overall, the service, atmosphere, and cleanliness amount to a wonderful experience at the Gallery. This is definitely a local's spot as I saw many returning guests hugging and greeting the servers (clearly, the staff is chosen with care). I have also visited their newer downtown location which deserves the same amount of hype and praise. Eating out during the time of a pandemic can be a risk, and if this is an issue for you I have found this restaurant to be extremely clean and safe, especially with their outside seating. 

Go visit and get a mimosa and pastry!!!!!

STOP! STOP! Please avoid this place even if there is no where else to eat. First off the service is absolutely horrible. If you do take the chance and go, avoid server by the name of Dwayne M. He poured us water and did not even ask if we wanted anything else to drink. We had to ask him can we get something else to drink besides water.  They will not split up a check. They say it's on the menu but unless it was an oversight on my part I didn't see. Second of all the food came to us just warm. It wasn't like it was freshly cooked out of hot grease. Third management sits in the back and don't even won't to take the time the see what a guest wants. I REPEAT DO NOT EAT AT THIS PLACE EVEN IF THERE IS NO WHERE ELSE TO EAT.

Finally.... it only took me a few years to finally get to go to the Gallery Pastry Shop. After hearing so many people rave about it, I finally was able to experience it for myself. So here are my thoughts, the croissant and sausage gravy is absolute fire. The croissant is beautifully crisp, the sausage gravy is well spiced, with clear evidence that the sausage used is a good quality sausage. I also ordered the tiramisu, and let me tell you, the best I have had in Indy by far.... the cream was smooth, the cake portion light and moist. While the environment can be a little bit of a hipster overkill, the food and service made it an incredibly amazing experience!

Incredibly impressed with the staff, Ashely at the front desk gets credit for the friendliest check-in I've ever had...in any hotel ever!  She took time to notice we from a LONG ways away and asked me about our drive. She was a breathe of fresh air after a 13 hour drive. Jordan at the bar was incredible.  Rooms are clean and comfortable and I'd stay here in a heartbeat based on the friendly people working here on its own merit!

I can't say enough nice things about this adorable pastry shop! The owners are wonderful, the desserts are delicious, and the decor of the shop is beautiful. I came here last week with a friend to buy their $1 macarons (special deal evert Wednesday). We got a lemon flavor and a dark chocolate flavor... Both were super good! 

The setup of the shop is perfect, too. You can sit along the bar and actually watch the pastry chefs make the macarons and other desserts! If the weather is nice, you can sit outside on the picnic benches (makes for great Instagram photos). 

I know they also offer baking classes, so this could be a fun activity with your gal pals or mom! If you haven't been here yet, go go GO!

Such a great brunch spot! The broadripple location is adorable. Their croissants are so delicious! And their desserts are even better! They also offer baking classes at their downtown location. It was SO much fun!!

I had been wanting to try this amazing place for a while, and I am SO GLAD we did last Sunday!! I would definitely recommend making a reservation, as they seem to get very busy around 11AM (when we tried to stop in a few weeks ago, but left that time due to the 45-50 minute wait).

My husband and I sat at the bar which was a very neat experience. The kitchen seemed to run so smoothly, and the food creations were so beautiful!

We had the bottomless coffee and two macaroons to share to start our brunch off right. Then, we each ordered the crepes. I ordered one savory and one sweet. I LOVE how you can add as many ingredients as you want and it's no extra charge! I loved the fresh veggies, meat, and cheese in the savory crepe. For my sweet crepe, I ordered the lemon zest, mixed berry, and whipped cream. SO GOOD!

For dessert, we shared the tiramasu. You will definitely want to save room for dessert here. From start to finish, we had a fantastic brunch and cannot wait to go back together soon. We loved every bite! I look forward to trying the mimosas next time!

We were walking at the mall and we saw some folks holding a different type of cup. So we wandered around and we found this place! This was the old tea-vana spot, they just opened! "Edible Cookie Dough" I've never had one in my life to be honest so why not try it ? They were giving us free samples and decided to get the 2 flavor medium size, it was pricey. The serving ? This is where it gets interesting.. I got a totally different serving than the other medium we ordered, yes folks it was at least a scoop difference, so I told myself they just opened maybe they will get better. Our experience was okay, nothing to brag yet. Will try again very soon

This was a filthy hotel that had bugs. Our rooms had dirty socks and other people's nasty belongings on the floors. The walls were filthy and we did not have a wall mirror in our room. The breakfast is one of the worst things I have ever tasted. Do not stay at this hotel.

As promised, we returned today after really enjoying the preview last evening. Guess what? The place was even better today than it was yesterday! Seriously, check out the picture and tell me different :) 

Today we decided to eat outside. It was a gorgeous morning. One of those mornings you read about in a novel. The host was great and inviting. She told us all things macaroons...because it $1 macaroon Wednesday. 

Once we got the menu, I had no idea what to get because it all sounded great. I settled for a ham and cheese croissant. Sounds basic huh...it wasn't. It was a really good infused cheese with mint and stuff. The ham must have been carved from heavens supply. Then it was aided by a fresh salad. 

I wish I could insert a heart eyes emoji, because that's how I still feel. This is the best kept secret in Indy. So serious. The food was great and the people are amazing!! If I didn't have to catch a flight, I would've eaten more and more and more. 

This gem is hidden next to Mass Ave Toys. Great indoor and outdoor seating. Bring your family and friends. They also have free WiFi.
I want to like Redstone more, but find the food and menu mediocre. The service is always good and they have a pretty good brunch.

Pretty decent location and appears to be fairly clean. I grew up in Florida and I was never much of a Winn-Dixie customer because of a couple negative experiences, but this location isn't bad at all. I wasn't there at a busy time, so I was checked out at the register immediately and she was pretty friendly.

I spent far less money than I usually do at Publix, and almost everything I bought was either marked down or less money if you bought two. Using my grandmothers member number helped to save a bunch lol. 

I was hungry so I grabbed some wings from the hot bar where they charge by weight. I mixed and matched and got buffalo, lemon pepper and teriyaki, two of each kind. It came out to about $5 and the wings were really good. 

All in all, I wouldn't be against coming back to this location.

Really disappointed for Mother's Day. They were out for quite a few things- the al a carte pastries were questionable. There was no line for the breakfast/lunch - we didn't hear positive things from those waiting and ended up at the cake bake shop
Never had a bad meal here. Get the ribs. They fall off the bone the fries are great and the slice of chocolate cake can feed a family.

I'm not sure how they can't keep the drive through line moving on a Friday night but I have been stuck on the line for at least 30 minutes at this point. I also had already tried to order pick up from inside but the doors were already locked so obviously that must not be an option even though the app and website show it to be available

Service was horrible last Saturday.  There are many spots that serve great food in this area...Why spend your money at a place who has horrible service and the food is not even that great.  Our waiter had an extreme attitude and prided himself with letting us know that there was no free refills on drinks.  He left our table never to return.  There menu is overpriced for example a shrimp po-boy is $16.  The same po-boy but bigger and better tasting is served at Deanie's for $9 and refills are plentiful.  The service at Deanie's is hands down way better and the food is AMAZING!!!! There was no wait to be seated at the Gumbo Pot and a major line at Deanie's (that went very quickly) and I see why....Customer Service and Food Quality..thumbs down for the Gumbo Pot....Save your time and money!

I've written a lot of five star reviews, but this place is truly five stars. We came for brunch yesterday morning, tempted by their simple menu and bottomless mimosas (not all the time, only sometimes) for $10! We seated ourselves at the diner/bar, because their setup allows you to watch them prepare and cook your meals. I really, really enjoyed this. They had a lot of people in the kitchen, and initially looked like chaos, however may have been one of the most organized kitchens I've ever seen. Every single person had a purpose and knew exactly what they were supposed to do. I could've sat there all day watching them. 

Now onto the brunch. The mimosas were great, my wife and I each having multiple throughout the morning. For meals, I went with the 'Merica hash, which included two over easy eggs, hash browns, and bacon. The bacon was incredible, and watching them serve it almost looked like they bake it. I really, really enjoyed it. On the hashbrowns, they seasoned it with a little bit of herb to give it a little extra something. Once I noticed that, all was lost, I was in heaven. The eggs were cooked perfectly as well.

My wife went with an omelette full of multiple vegetables and chorizo. She says it was the best omelette she's ever had, and I may have to agree. I don't usually order omelettes because I think it's too much egg, however this one was perfectly done. 

To top it off, we finished with a chocolate croissant. You have to get a pastry at the French Pastry shop, right?! It was perfect. Buttery, chocolatey, perfect for the two of us to split. They have multiple delicious looking pastries that I would love to try, and on Wednesdays offer $1 macarons, many of which I have tried and loved. This is a perfect gem hidden in the heart of SoBro.

Girls brunch. Boys brunch. Summer. Spring. Fall. 

Whatever you have to do, whoever you are with--come here. The food is wonderful beyond words and the aura of the place and people are simply the best. I've not had a bad experience here and I cannot envision I ever will. 

Go and enjoy yourself.
Love the hotel, loved the updates, right by LP field, Free shuttle and taxi ride with tip under $10! Great place to stay and great breakfest. We will stay there again.

Perfect pop up Halloween treat! The decor is spooktacular! Really, they did a fangtastic job decorating the place. There's something to see in each corner. 

We got here mid afternoon on a Saturday and walked right in. There were maybe 35 other people there, but plenty of space. 

I opted for a pumpkin beer, and I've seen higher drink prices, as I know others are complaining about them. 

It's a really cool place to check out and enjoy a drink or two. Saw others with the blood bag iv drinks- looked like a fun drink.
Definitely worth the hype! The bar was decked out with skeletons and served Halloween themed cocktails and there were plenty of photo opportunities! Can't wait for the Christmas set up!

My review is based on one thing and one thing only ... the buffalo shrimp. When I am fortunate enough to see New Jersey in my rear view mirror for the last time, I will miss three things. One of them is Redstone's buffalo shrimp. They're a hole in one. Everything else is par.

I may be the only person in Indy who didn't know this place existed but I'm glad I found it! It's tucked away down a strip of businesses right off of 54th in SoBro. It's not visible from the street so it's definitely a hidden gem! 

I found this searching to pick up a cake for a birthday. I browsed the pasty counter and asked for descriptions of what each item was. The service I got here was awesome. They described each type of cake/dessert and asked what I was looking for. Then packaged my choices up really taking delicate care. 
They were out of cakes but I was able to get 4 different personal sides cakes so all worked out! I also grabbed 2 original croissants and they are DELISH! 

The inside is also adorable, it opens to a decent sized patio and is decorated to feel like the perfect brunch spot. Plenty of people were outside enjoying this warmer weather even though it's October! 

I will definitely be back to crush some really great smelling food!
The owner is extremely honest and a genuinely nice guy. This is the only place I've taken my jewelry for appraisals and repairs for years, and can't recommend it highly enough.

I love Red Stone. Their food is amazing. Although, when my cousin ordered the Mac and cheese, she received a very small dish. We had to order 3 of them just for her to be full. I do especially love the Brussels sprouts!
Love this wawa, ok I love every wawa but the staff here is always helpful and friendly. Even if they are a bit short handed some days and get a rush they are polite and efficient.

Cannot do this place justice with my review. We have been back to this place 3 times in the last 2 months.
1st visit- drank amazing cold brew coffees while waiting for a table (at noon on a Saturday). Once at the table enjoyed balanced mimosas and a macaroon. For our main we ordered the 'Merica and regular breakfast plate; and had to get to a to go box. Everything was seasoned perfectly and the bacon was crispy. 
2nd visit- delicious drip coffee, build your own mimosas, split an omelet and sides of bacon. Staff was helpful and prompt. Omelette was stupid delicious.  
3rd/today's visit- drip coffee, blood orange mimosas, split crepes and bacon. Crepes were just enough filled to be satisfying without sloppy. 

TLDR- amazing food, seasoning on point, great staff that will give you coffee while waiting (if you ask)

I love taking girls on first dates here. It's always a classy upscale atmosphere with great service and great food without breaking the bank. It's also kind of hidden away so it's very cool that it's tucked away on BR the way it is. Coffee is a little too light for me but they have some great pastries that look as good as they taste. Waiters are always friendly.

Friendly, knowledgeable, and respectful, even after they found out I was from California. They have excellent inventory at reasonable prices. The attached photo is what we saw crossing the border from Oregon.
This place is the best!  They not only resuscitate dead iPhones, but they make recommendations for future protection and improvement.  Friendly and very fast.  Highly recommended!

Avoid this place. 
I wanted to go to gumbo shop and thought this was the same place. 
Take a look at the pic. There's 2 bay leaves that they left in me bowl and half a hard shell crab that you can't get into. 
Flavor does not represent Louisiana.

Update. They used frozen shrimp for our seafood gumbo.

Gallery Pastry Shop not only has beautiful but delicious treats. Don't forgot to look beyond just their bakery selections and be sure to check their brunch. Pre-COVID it was my favorite to watch the chefs create delicious masterpieces while sipping on a mimosa (see photo for exact scene). Be sure to also visit in warmer months and they offer a great outdoor seating scene accompanied by outdoor games. A favorite unique place in Indy!

Nightmare before Tinsel probably is the best themed pop up bar in Philly as of 2019. Many probably thinks I'm over exaggerating, but you will understand where I'm coming from once you were inside Tinsel. 

For me, Haunt was a huge disappointment. Lightly decorated, short menu offerings, etc.... I caught a glimpse of how Tinsel was gonna look on PhillyMag, not much but very impressive. Word of advice, AVOID SATURDAYS NIGHTS!!! Man, that line extend all the way down and around the other street‍. 

Me and hubby decided to go after work on Saturday. We arrived at Tinsel around 10:15pm, lines were long but not as bad. Let's just say, half an hour pass, that line looks so freaking scary. We were glad we made it at the time when we arrived. We probably got inside by 11:30(there is $5 cover charge, CASH ONLY). 

The moment we stepped inside, instant WOW factor. Decorations everywhere, from the walls, restroom, bars, to the ceilings etc...... Is really hard pushing my way to the bar, boocoo amount of ppl. I made it to the sticky(maybe to represent bloody??)bar after 20 minutes of pushing lol. We purchased Elvira $12 plus $5 to put in a Tinsel souvenir skull mug and Blood Bag $16. I didn't like Elvira but we love Blood Bag.

The desserts and pastries are fantastic. Brunch, not so much. Pro tip: courses should come out at the same time not 15 minutes apart. Still not certain if the cinnamon pastry was an an unspoken apology for that or what. Also, if you have and open kitchen make sure the girl with the long blonde hair wears a hairnet or a hat because everyone can see her continually brushing her hair back wth her bare and and then touching the food.
Ginger was great to deal with.  She answered all our questions and was up front with all the details. We will definitely seek her out for our next automobile purchase.

I chose Redstone for lunch with a friend thinking it would be pretty quiet during the week. Oh how wrong I was! I walked through the doors and the area in front of the host stand was packed with people. Despite this, the hostesses were hustling and each group was seated shortly after arrival. 

Everyone we encountered was very, very nice, and wait times for drinks and food were not long. They really have their lunch service down. Our server was so sweet and accommodating, especially with regards to my friend's one year old son. 

I think I could have liked Redstone a bit more if I had ordered differently. The Caesar salad was on the small side, with just lettuce, croutons and a teeny tiny Parmesan crisp. But I will say that the dressing was delicious and the rotisserie chicken I opted to add on was tender and flavorful. I could have used another handful of lettuce and a piece of bread or something. My friend's flatbread looked pretty great. 

Redstone's pricey but you wouldn't know it based on the crowds. Ladies lunching and business people filled the place. I love the patio and will probably return for drinks during the summer months.

I LOVED this place!!! I had the blood bag drink which was a little too sweet but super adorable. I also got a drink in a skull cup which was actually just a vodka soda bc I couldn't do another fancy cocktail. 

They also had a great craft beer selection, I introduced my bf to zombie dust. 

Definitely a fun spot!!!

First of all, I have been to 'Gallery Pastry Shop', a couple of years ago, when it first opened.  This was way before their 'Gallery Pastry Bar' and 'Gallery at 16th' had even opened.  I remember the first time I visited 'Gallery Pastry Shop', a couple of years ago, it was mostly empty.  After I had my meal, I asked for the bill and the waitress calculated the bill in her head, no physical check was presented.
After visiting 'Gallery Pastry Bar', a couple of times in downtown.  I decided to stop by 'Gallery Pastry Shop', in Broad Ripple.  It was around 2:00 p.m., on a Tuesday.  I didn't expect there to be so many guests, at the time and place!  The shop was packed with guests, almost every single table was full!  They also have a clear window, so you can see into the kitchen.  I even spotted their pastry chef, Ben Hardy (@chefboyhardy) behind the counter, making brunch!  He was wearing a black apron, with a black button down shirt with his sleeves rolled up to his elbows.  It was a real treat to see all of them, especially Ben Hardy, behind the counter making brunch!
The display case was filled with pastries, croissants and macarons!  'Katy' took the time to tell me about the almost dozen pastries in the case.  She even told me what was in them.  
I went with 

3 'French Macarons' (Almond Praline, Cinnamon Pear & Pumpkin)
2 'Misc. Pastries'
1 'Almond Croissant'

It was such a nice experience!  Next time, I'll have to dine in!

I have been to Redstone numerous times and I can't believe I haven't reviewed it before now!  It is one of my favorite places for breakfast/brunch, lunch and dinner - as well as cocktails and appetizers on the patio in Spring, Summer and Fall.  The food is great, service is usually spot-on (ask for Ian, if you get a chance) and we have never had a bad experience or meal there.  When my parents visit every year from Japan, Redstone is a 'must-go' destination several times during their usual month plus visits.  It is one of their dining highlights in the US and they LOVE it, truly!  The steaks  and ribs are awesome as is their rotisserie chicken.  The breakfast bread that comes with breakfast/brunch is always yummy and the signature pineapple stoli doli cocktail, as well as their bloody mary is awesome.  For dessert, the deconstructed banana cream pie is dee-luscious.  A great place for friends, family and even for business dinners.  You won't be disappointed!

7/21/13

Slight summer breeze blowing in the outdoor seating area w/ contemporary R&B tunes playing. The mood is set for an  early afternoon brunch.

Red stone buttermilk pancakes w/ chicken sausage patties & hashbrowns. The pancake was sweet without the syrup and filling. I was not a fan of the chicken sausage... Can't quite put my finger on the displeasure of the taste but I did not like the sausage. The hash-browns were undercooked with the middle portions needing a few more minutes in the skillet.

The best part of the meal was the morning bread w/ blueberries which came out before the meal. Buttery, sweet and filling. You eat more than 2 slices of this bread and you have no room for your meal.

This was my first brunch here which was just alright. I have been here for lunch a few times and have been vey pleased with my meal selections. I will give brunch another try some other time. Every place has a time when they are just off kilter a little and I'm hoping this was the case on this day.

I absolutely loveeeeeeee this place! I am huge on customer service and let's just say the entire staff goes above and beyond!! My favorites are the breakfast sammie and the breakfast with Tiffany! I'm a hugeeee Brunch fanatic and this is my all time fave. The vibes and music are superb!!! Tommy and his team are great!!! :)

Never going back to this place I wouldn't be surprised if they are out of business in a year... their customer service is a JOKE! Went in a few months back and they were rude and unprofessional then, figured okay maybe they had a bad day.. tried again today ready to purchase an AK and RIP bullets and yep ~ rude again! Telling me "oh you like those cuz they're cute huh?! " wtf are you serious?! Must of been the Raider gear! 
They are over priced, white nazis, rude as f***!  Your loss BRO - had 3k to blow.. I will take my money and my business to Overland Armament who are extremely friendly, PROFESSIONAL, and prices are very good and always putting together deals for you. If you want the best customer service experience and top quality and a great price visit overland armament.
Worst car service ever. What was supposed to be a one day job turned into a week and cost twice as much as orginally quoted.

Alicia our server was friendly and attentive. Juan the bar tender made a delicious margarita!! My son enjoyed himself for his birthday, the male manager walked around the introduce himself, the ambiance was nice, food was delicious and fresh we ordered, 2 roasted chickens, buffalo grilled wings, bday dessert, chicken noodle soup, chicken sandwich with bacon added  and skillet of cornbread ...everything was tasty! Thanks again!

We travel a lot and concluded this is one of the best hotels we have stayed at for out road trips. Easy access from I-24. Family of four, including mom, dad and two adult daughters found the double queen room exceptionally spacious, bathroom was roomy too. We were right across from the elevator but the room was quiet. They have a great lounge and bar area and a free buffet breakfast that added to the value. A shuttle runs every half hour from the hotel to Broadway Street so you don't have to drive to the bars. All in all, great value, clean and comfortable.
Service ok, but the Creole breakfast far from our traditional breakfast back home we took a chance and it did pay off. Very tasteful & full of flavor :)

My cousin and I were in your shop Tuesday for lunch . The decor and service was fine. I got the club sandwich and a glass of water. The aoli was almost non existent and the jowel bacon was tough. What's with the trend of serving room temperature water as if it were a delicacy ?.....it's not. I purchased a classic eclairs to take home. Not only was it absent of cream filling for almost 2 inches, it was one of the worst eclairs I have ever had. 
I wanted to like your shop, but with your overpriced mediocre food, I won't be back. Maybe my expectations were too high.

It's all about the lemon blueberry eclair. That delicate fluffy cream tucked between fresh pastry with a serving of blueberry compote on the side -need I say more? It was so refreshing, I'd swear it was healthy.... ;)

I've been dying to check out The Gallery Pastry Shop after all of the great photos and reviews I've seen pop up over the last few weeks. I was even lucky enough to have a macaroon hand delivered to my house from my dear Allison F. I'm not one to flock to macaroons but I know this one was exceptionally delicious (and the color palette they offer is stunning boxed as a gift). In addition to eclairs ($5), croissants, macaroons, and desserts like tiramisu, they offer mimosas made with Simplicity Juice, cold brew from Bee Coffee Roasters, wine and beer. I also noticed that they have offer charcuterie and cheese board selections from Smoking Goose, Tulip Tree Creamery, etc. 

Beyond the food and drink is the great atmosphere they've created with indoor and outdoor seating, overhead garage door (open when the weather is right), bar seating facing into the open kitchen concept, two stunning communal wooden tables and generous natural lighting. 

I look forward to trying their other seasonal eclair flavors (hazelnut, chocolate, etc.) and hopefully popping in for one of their baking classes (ranging from cookies and pies to everything chocolate).

I went to try to chicken wings. I know I know. But I had to. I also ordered cinnabites while there. The server taking my order was VERY nice. She was just so pleasant. I wish I knew her name. The wings were passable enough I guess. Imagine frozen chicken wings. These aren't good wings by a long shot. She shoulda leaned way harder into Taco Bell flavors. They played it way safe. The cinnabites were very tasty. They only come in 2 or 12. Such odd options

I have been here a couple times now and each time has been such a great experience. The staff is lovely and attentive and the atmosphere is great!

Highly recommend making a reservation or joining the waitlist ahead of time. Luckily, the one time we walked in, we were sat immediately.

As far as food, they have so many delicious options and I always say I am going to try new things each time I've come but I always end up getting the same thing.

Can't recommend the savory crepes enough. I have tried the breakfast with tiffany and the greenie, both delicious. I also got a chocolate croissant both times but definitely want to try the hazelnut next time I'm in. You also can't go wrong with the breakfast sammie.

I love vanilla chai lattes and I tried theirs....TOO PEPPERY! It tasted like so much pepper I couldn't even finish half of it. If you end up ordering, ask them to add more syrup and that will balance it out but dang....not my fave.

Overall, really cute place and I will def come back to try other things!

I want to thank La Siesta for being so kind and letting I and my friends husband use the patio for his wife's surprise 50th Birthday party! They don't take reservations but said that if we called ahead ahead would see what they could do! They did! The service was excellent, the fajitas and tacos were great and our wait person she is a jewel! She knew we at 16 persons who needed a lot of TLC were great!  We love this place and thank Juan the Mgr for being accommodating and the cooks and staff who kept us plentiful in margaritas, chips, guacamole and salsa.  Thank you again!
Somehow they clipped my dogs tongue and acted like nothing or apologized. They charged like nothing was wrong.

We like to come here for brunch on Sunday. It's always crowded but we bypass the lobby nonsense and eat at the bar or outside when the weather's nice (you wouldn't think a stormwater basin could be a focal point). Creatures of habit, we usually get the same thing: spa breakfast (granola, yogurt, fresh fruit) and the morning flatbread (like a giant triangular cracker with eggs and sun-dried tomato). Coffee is usually good. Free mimosas a nice touch. Love the Sinatra.

Summary:
Not a fan of the gumbo, but the jambalaya was very good.

Details:
It was my first time in New Orleans and wanted to try Gumbo. I ordered the Gumbo and Jambalaya to split with my girlfriend since we weren't too hungry. The server, while probably making a joke, seemed a little stand off ish that we were only getting appetizers 

I'm not sure if I'm a fan of gumbo, but I didn't particularly like it here. Don't think I will be coming back.

The atmosphere is everything at Gallery Pastry shop. This was my first visit and certainly not my last! I tried the pear lavender latte- delicious!!! The perfect pair of sweet/floral notes complemented the espresso. For brunch I tried the Fromage crepe, and the bananas foster crepe. Both were to die for! Every plate the passed by looked divine. I cannot wait to come back!! I even brought home a little pastry desert for later- have not tried it but I already know I will not be disappointed. Would highly recommend a visit!
Bill was professional, virtuous, knowledgeable and patient with all my questions!  He showed that he truly does care about my family's protection!  Thank you!

Not very impressed but luckily it was only $5 per person.  

Limited info on the 1st floor about the NCAA sports.   

2nd floor had interactive area but tennis simulation didn't work, basketballs in basketball court were flat or worn out, & the 2 interactive video areas only had 1 ball for each sport so people wanting to try the same sport at the same time had to share the ball.  You would think they could afford to purchase sports equipment for both video areas to have its own balls.  

We ended up playing a little basketball with the worn out basketballs just to feel like we got our money's worth.

This place could be so much better if more effort was put into it.

I didn't think there was anything better than macaroons until I discovered $1 Macaroons on Wednesdays. They taste better when I can get a few extra and take some home for later! I also tried the Pear LavenderLatte last time we were in. I was presently surprised. I was hesitant at first, fearing it would be to sweet. The flavors weren't overbearing though and it was a balanced delicious drink. We'll be back soon!
this taco bell always serves hot, fresh, and delicious food..the staff is always professional and courteous..

This is my second time [during the pandemic] at Gallery Pastry Shop, and it did not disappoint! The first was during the summer when there was plenty of outdoor seating. This time it was January and a bit chilly, so no outdoor seating. The main space is cozy but they had some windows vented which brought a slight breeze, if you're wearing a sweater you will be fine but if you are a cold person then they have portable heaters they can sit by your table. They also seem to have seating across from the main space, but I wasn't able to check that out.

You have to try the jowl bacon - let's get that out of the way. Order a side of it. Or two.

I got the pick two crepes, they offer a few preset crepes and you can make your own. The breakfast at tiffany crepes is a little sweet with the corn and whipped nettle, but it will still satisfy any savory craving- and then the west fork whiskey banana foster crepes has a healthy amount of whip cream to pair with the soft caramelized bananas!

My boyfriend got the biscuits and gravy croissant breakfast and I think he may be sold on croissants as a replacement to biscuits now. The sausage in the gravy is spiced but not overwhelmingly so.

FYI: Gallery Pastry Bar is the downtown location, and Gallery Pastry Shop is the SoBro location. Easy to get these mixed up but they do have slightly different menus.

The food here is consistently good. Don't love the lunch menu options and prices are high but at least you can count on a quality meal. Wish they'd change up the menu and offer new and different salad and sandwich options. Cocktails were perfect.

All time family favorite of ours. We go for birthdays, holidays and even just to gtab a burger. Ahi tuna is the best. We usually eat here for Father's day as this is one of the most comfortable and casually intimate places my husband chooses. Love this place but I recommend reservations on open table website.

Still no reimbursement from Hellotech for the damage they caused in my home about six months ago.  Please avoid this company.

See my review from a month ago.
Hellotech damaged my front door when installing a SimplySafe system at my home.  I had to pay to have it fixed. I was promised that hellotech would reimburse me. They have never sent the check they promised to reimburse me for the damage I had repaired two mo ths ago.  Also the technician they sent to install my system totally messed up the installation breaking 3 pieces of the SimplySafe equipment. Beware of this company.
I've been coming to this place for years and have always enjoyed their brunch, desserts, and most importantly mimosas. I always get the 2 egg hash and never been disappointed.

It was a little over priced and the service wasn't anything special.  The food we ordered was ok and may have even been good other places but there are just so many better places within a couple of blocks of here.  

Also, this place was only accepting cash when we went.  Our bill was around $55(which included a grutiuity that was automatically added in) and we gave them $70 and asked for change.  The server insisted repeatedly that he couldn't provide change.  We finally got him to give us the change but it was still an odd experience for a place that was only accepting cash to not be able to provide change.

This restaurant is one of my favorites in all of Indy - they have amazing brunch and can you say HOMEMADE CROISSANT? It's delicious - get the breakfast sandwich! Check out their Instagram page for rotating specials - they always look delicious. Parking can be difficult at the restaurant, but if you're willing to walk there are adjacent parking lots.

I recently moved to Milwaukee after living in Indianapolis for 21 years. I meant this with my whole heart: I came back to Indy this weekend just to have Saturday brunch at Gallery. This place is truly the most incredible pastry shop I've ever found. I've had croissants/macarons/coffee in multiple countries and from the most well-known names, but this place takes the cake. I've had the privilege of having two birthday cakes done by the amazing folks at Gallery. You will truly not find a place with more amazing food, delightful service, or enchanting atmosphere. You are missing out if you haven't treated yourself to a day at Gallery.

This place is a gem!!! Highly recommend! I didn't know what to expect when I went and thought they just had more pastries and coffee but they have a full menu and so many options. We split a cheese board and our waitress recommended 2 amazing cheeses. She was very attentive but let us have tome to chat and enjoy the food:) I had the pear lavender latte which was delicious! They use smoking goose meats () and their croissants are to die for! I will definitely be returning very soon! 
Also, they have a really cute patio to enjoy when the weather warms up!

I did not try the gumbo.....probably should have. However, I wanted to try a Po boy. Allergic to shrimp, so I had to settle for the fish. OMG, that fish is great....life altering even. I'm no big fan of catfish or anything, but I could honestly eat that fish everyday. This table next to us ordered the catfish platter and this lunch room tray sized plate of fish was brought to the table. So, basically I'm saying I have my next meal ordered already. Our waitress was extremely friendly and pleasant, so she's like the icing on the cake or better yet the hot sauce  on the Po boy.

Gotta love Redstone. It's nice to have a more upscale restaurant in the midst of the suburbia that is Marlton. It's a beautiful looking restaurant with one of the best outdoor seating areas in south jersey. We happened to be sitting outside last night and it was perfect. Although it was starting to get chilly at night, the outdoor heaters they have above the tables really makes the area warm and cozy. We were seating immediately on a Saturday night because we opted for outdoor seating. 

Service was prompt and to the point. We started with some drinks and the jerk chicken fondue. I love redstone because it is one of the few places that can make a killer dirty martini AND they have blue cheese olives!! My favorite. The jerk chicken fondue is life changing. It puts melting pot to shame. I probably could have gotten 2 orders of it and a flatbread and called it a night. For entrees we ordered the Short Rib entree and General Tsos turkey burger. The short rib was phenomenal- melt in your mouth tenderness and covered in Au jus. I wasn't really a fan of my fiance's burger... It wasn't prepared badly it was just a bizzare mix of ingredients. We ended with the cookie sundae which left us completely stuffed and satisfied. Service was fast all night. Can't wait to come back.

I have a Dell desktop PC that's very old (in PC terms). I bought it from Dell direct when Vista first came out. I have since upgraded it myself to Win 7 and finally started to get dreaded BSOD after about 7 years of daily use. Needless to say, I thought it was the hard drive or video card. I did back up everything luckily to an external hard drive I had (from my days as a PC Geek) while running Win 7 in Safe Mode.

Anyway, I had searched for alternatives to BB Geek Squad (rip-off artists) and found these guys on Yelp. I saw the other reviews and figured, why not, give these guys a try too. Well, I am glad they are local to where I work and live.

I dropped the PC off on a Wednesday (my day off) and picked it up that Saturday. This was all last week. I am writing my review a week later, as I wanted to make sure the PC still worked. :-) It is running faster and better now (thanks to a tune up and no more extra crap I had added to the computer. 

These guys were very professional and courteous. I told you readers some background information because I used to fix computers and worked in the IT field for years so I knew what these guys were talking about, I just didn't have the diagnostic tools to figure out if it was hardware (anyone can reload windows but that doesn't solve hardware problems).  They reloaded my Win 7 and MS Office and installed new  antivirus software that is faster than the Constant Guard from Comcast. 

I highly recommend the UR Gadget Doctors for computer service. They also fix Macs, smartphones, and game consoles (so says their website). I don't have a smart phone (go figure) or game console so I can't rate them on that. For PC service, these guys are highly recommended. Much cheaper than Geek Squad and cheaper than a new PC, even if I'd rather replace my desktop with a new one but not this year.

Seemed like a decent selection of guns, ammo and accessories packed into a smaller location.

Reasonable prices in ammo and magazines.

The customer service is iffy. I asked a few questions to one guy behind the counter, and basically blew me off and walked away. The ither fuu who rang me up was very friendly and polite.

My only ding on this gun shop was the lack of customer service at the counter

This is a review based on being a consumer attending a conference in the NCAA Hall of Champions conference facilities.  I took a pass on the Hall of Champions because it was not "included" in the facilities' rental agreement to gain admission (like $5 admission is going to kill them????).

Conference rooms with break-apart walls are standard fare.  NCAA Hall of Champions facilities are no different.  Our group used three rooms for presentation all day and they were routinely serviced after each break.  Very little set-up was required by the provider.

The real rub for me was coffee and water.  The provider ran out of coffee before the morning sessions started and was in no hurry to make more.  In fact, they didn't.  The conference coordinator actually decided to go to the staff offices to pull two cups of coffee out for two of us who were asking for more.  I guess they figured time vs time wasted.   The water in the conference rooms were provided in plastic "globes" with very small plastic cups and 4-foot high soft drink thermos-coolers (aka - dip your own ice; make noise during presentation).  Not very functional but extremely cost-effective for the provider.

Stated earlier, it seemed to me like if/when a group rents the entire conference room facility out for a day.... all in attendance would be given a $5 voucher to go next door to the Hall of Champions.  Nope... not the case.  Too bad.  

Not impressed.  Especially since the NCAA is recognized for rolling in the dough through it being the governing body of college athletics.   Too too too bad.
The outside seating is very nice. The food and drinks are good; however, it's on the pricey side even for Marlton. It's a solid 3.5 stars--when is Yelp going to allow half star ratings?

One of the best customer service experiences I've ever had and they didn't even service my home!! I called because I found termite tunnels. Reuben showed up and immediately let me know there was a warranty on my termite control from a different company. He gave me the information I needed to reach said company about getting them out to my house. The company told me I did not have a warranty, I called Reuben and he told me there is at least a year warranty and gave me advice on how to handle the situation. He asked me to keep him posted on the situation and stated if I needed any additional help to call him. As a first time home buyer I am super grateful for the honesty and helpfulness Reuben provided. Thank you so much!!

Right before writing this, I glanced and saw the opening line to someone else's review that read; "What's not to like about Redstone?!" Well, allow me to tell you: $18 for 3 shrimp.

Redstone is opportunistic. It's located in the swanky little Marlton Promenade, so it ratchets up its prices to take advantage of the waspy, upper middle class clientele. I was there last week with the Misses, and I kinda feel like I got robbed to a degree. 

First, it's a nice place; inside is a little dark, but we decided to dine outside. Our server was almost suspiciously pleasant. We sat down, perused the menu, and settled on the mahi mahi ($32), the vine ripened tomato "spaghettini," (a special $18) and the mozzarella stuffed meatballs to start. The appetizer came out and was pretty tasty actually. The marinara was delicious, and the meatballs were seasoned well, and piping hot. 

We took a step back with the entrees though. The first thing out of the Misses mouth, before I even took a bite of my food was, "this Mahi Mahi is SUPER bland." SO, I took a bite of my "spaghettini," and yup, absolutely lacking ANY seasoning. (By the way, my entree came with no protein, so I added shrimp, and it came with THREE shrimp, for an additional $13. The MEAL was $18. Adding THREE shrimp was almost as much as the meal.....THREE shrimp. THREE.) The food tasted fresh, but nothing was actually SEASONED. I shouldn't have to season my own $31 entree.

The two entrees, one app, an Arnold Palmer and a glass of wine was almost $100. And it's one thing if the food is bomb, but to drop a Benjamin and be disappointed is another. 

Redstone has been coasting on its Buffalo Shrimp for years now. Yes, they're good. Yes, they're MASSIVE. But the rest of Redstone doesn't live up to the expectation their prices sets down. 

It'll be another few years before I go back. *shoulder shrug emoji*

I am vegetarian. I ordered from Taco Bell yesterday. I'll post a picture of my order. Everything was correct except I was given a burrito with MEAT in it. Not black beans like I had ordered. I didn't find out about this until after I bit down, ingested, and noticed something was off. I looked at the burrito which was filled with meat. Totally unacceptable. Disgusting. I haven't eaten meat for 2 years. Included picture of meat burrito.

Found this little restaurant while traveling.  My husband and I shared a fantastic plate of nachos and a drink.  He had a draft beer, and I had the best Sangria I have ever had.  I'm quite sure is was made by the bartender and not a generic bottle sangria.  The food, drinks and staff were exceptional!  We will definitely visit again when we're in the area!

Several folks and I visited the Gallery Pastry shop the Tuesday before Christmas for brunch at 10:30 a.m.  Much to my surprise there were only two or three other tables of patrons.  On the weekends if you don't arrive before opening you won't get a table without a long wait.  Having checked out the online menu before arriving I knew that I was going to get the appetizer sized portion of bruleed fruit (oh so good-a must have) and the create your own two crepes.  However the menu in the restaurant was different than the online version and no longer offered the build your own crepes and the bruleed fruit plate had increased in price and size.  The waitress was apologetic about the build your own crepes option only being offered on Thursdays as she said it slowed things down in the kitchen.  Thought that was kind of strange since the place was practically empty...but I just ordered the breakfast Sammy instead.  Although I had planned to purchase some pastries to take home the pastry case was virtually empty so this visit was a let down for me.  The highlight was the bruleed fruit as always, however, I just checked the menu again and during the week crepes and bruleed fruit are no longer served.  Guess the only way to get my "fruit fix" in the future is to fight the weekend crowds.

This place has great ambience and nice seating options both inside and outside. I stopped by for breakfast and I was underwhelmed. Eggs Creole and bacon seemed reheated. The grits were good though. I had a YELP coupon for bread pudding and it was pretty good. All in all, my visit was just OK. I've been super impressed by other restaurants in the French Quarter and I was looking for more flavor.

During my latest visit to Gallery Pastry Shop, I ordered the Croissant with Bruleed Tulip Tree Trillium, honey, pecan, mixed berry compote, scrambled eggs, Smoking Goose jowl bacon and hash browns. The croissant itself could have been a meal, and eggs, bacon & hash browns together could have been a separate meal -- I ended up taking half home.

And, of course, I couldn't leave without grabbing a few goodies from the pastry case. There were a lot of tempting options in the case, but after already over-indulging, I limited myself the mandarin mousse and opera cake to take home.

I can't recommend Gallery Pastry Shop highly enough for brunch, lunch or even just to grab some coffee or dessert!

Checked out Nightmare Before Tinsel on Halloween and it was cool. All of the creepy decor was fun to see at the pop-up bar!

Since it was Halloween night when I stopped by, I believe this is why they had a $5 cash cover to get into the bar (I stopped by previously on the weekend and there was no cover). Before entering, the staff asked for id (that they scanned), proof of vaccination card or wear your mask while in the bar (if you did not have the vaccination card).

The space is not that big (even smaller with a lot of people in there...yikes). I decided to keep my mask on for the most part of my time there, looked around at all of the cool decor, places to take pictures/selfies, music playing, there was a guy dressed up as a grandma that was in full character (funny lol), also grabbed a pouch drink (the drink was good: Red Bull, tequila, and I forgot what else lol). 

I enjoy stopping by Tinsel when they're open! Will be back for their Christmas pop-up!

Obviously their pastries are amazing, but the food here is also to die for. I absolutely love the breakfast w Tiffany crepes!  We have lived everything we've tried so far. Instantly became our favorite place for brekky or brunch.

Surprised this has a three star average rating... Had to read other review to understand why. As a current NCAA athlete and general sports fan, it was super cool to see the history of the NCAA and what it is currently. It's hard to tell a story of so many athletes and sports, but I felt like it was well done and good for many ages who can appreciate it!

The Hall of Champions provides numerous photo opportunities from the flying wedge, the basketball court, and the interactive sporting areas. Downstairs you can explore more of the history of each sport by seeing uniforms from various institutions as well as detailed information on previous championship winners, individuals, etc. Going upstairs, you see the interactive elements. You can stand behind a think plastic/glass window and see the tennis ball coming at you between 80-90 miles an hour to simulate a college tennis player's serve. Shoot on the basketball court, do a simulator for football/soccer/tennis/baseball and more.

Even in the national headquarters is incredibly open, great lighting, and lots of photo opportunities. Really tall ceilings and it is super clean which makes it pleasant.

Tucked away right off 54th street is this gem of a place. Saturday morning brunch it is busy so plan accordingly. If you have to wait, its worth it. We ordered take out and everything was packaged well and ready when I arrived. It was packed just as gorgeous as it would have been if we had ate there. 

The boxed goodies are 4 random flavored macarons and the chocolate pillow (which I had to have) everything was delicious. 

Brunch included the 'Merica and a sammy. The sammy was the best breakfast sammy anyone could ask for. Flaky croissant with a perfectly cooked egg and cheese spread from tulip tree  

This place is a must try! We already have plans to go back for an anniversary brunch. P.s. they have bottomless mimosas on the weekends

Late night, yes. 

Goods and services, well yeah!  

Drinks, well it wouldn't be Norleans without it! 

And so we land ourselves at the Palace Market across from the music/bar area of Frenchman Street in Norleans! This place is just truly a gem. How many markets do you know of where you have art, food, drink and just about anything you could imagine available for purchase? And best of all they run it during prime time staying open till at 1 am if not later! I was floored and amazed with the entire concept. They have it down pat.  

We wound up buying some local memorabilia from a vendor there. He was so kind as to hold our goods till we finished at the bar. Southern hospitality at its finest, again! I'd come back to this market in a flash. It really was all that. 

Not much else to say but just get here if your ever in the area. It;'s about as unique as they come.

Multiple trips to different Redstones and this one is just as disappointing. I ordered a club soda, it was flat the bartender tried again it was still flat, he was kind of, oh well. So I asked the female bartender to take it off the bill and give me water, which she did. They were out of many things because the menu is changing the next day. 
Wanted a salad w romaine she said everything is a mix. So I odered ceasar, she said that's a mix too. I ended up ordering 3 buffalo shrimp which are always great. I did notice that they used to have 'Maytag' blue cheese, now its just plain old blue cheese. There is a big difference. 

Maybe because it was after nine, but I ordered a baked potato and I definitely got an old microwaved potato, and I think micro waved asparagus as well. 

I was just very underwelmed. High priced place like this, I expect fresh food.

CALLING ALL HALLOWEEN LOVERS!!! IT'S HAPPENING!!! My absolute favorite Halloween Party Scene is open!!! Seriously- I have yet to find a Halloween themed bar that tops Nightmare Before Tinsel. 

Nightmare Before Tinsel (NBT) is an old jewelry store turned into a holiday themed pop-up bar (In December NBT turns into 'Tinsel', which is a Christmas lover's dream come true). 
 
The space is small and in previous years (especially on weekends) the line can be very long. That being said, the spooky, brilliantly designed bar is well worth the wait. The decorations are impressively detailed-- providing plenty of picture opportunities for you and your crew! The cocktails are crafty (though a touch sweet and a tad pricey) and super fun. Costumes are not mandatory but obviously encouraged (especially closer to Halloween). 

Pre-COVID, I would plan Halloween themed nights- a quick dinner in Old City (The Bourse Food Court, Buk Chon BYOB, Lucha Cartel are all good places to start), a trip to the Ghost Ship (@ Race Street Pier underneath the Ben Franklin Bridge) and a quick stop at Independence Beer Garden before heading to our final destination, NBT. 

I am SO HAPPY that Nightmare Before Tinsel is open this year and looking forward to visiting Philly next weekend!

Dang.. I wish this review could be positive but I was really disappointed in my experience today. I was so excited to go back to Gallery Pastry but my dessert, which had no name, and my friends chocolate eclair were both very dry and did not taste fresh at all. My dessert was a chocolate cake filled with carmel and peanuts. The cake portion was so dry it just crumbled to bits when I tried to cut it with a fork. My friend couldn't cut her eclair because it was so dry. She had to pick it up and bite into it like an apple. Extremely disappointing compared to our previous experience. I'm not sure if they were preoccupied with the private event that was about to start, or making a cake for the Hedge Row event tonight, but the pastries were definitely subpar. The person behind the counter was nice but not helpful and rather slow. He didn't know anything about the pastries or taste, did not know how to run the coffee machine, and couldn't find silverware. Overall, I'll likely be back but I may try other places first.

This was a pretty cool event that I have been wanting to come to for years now. With the admission, there was also a haunted house to walk through which was pretty awesome! I got a good scare and screamed cause I am a big baby! 
I ended up buying a blood bag for 16 bucks, just cause i thought it looked cool, but as far as taste, it was eh... not great... more like juice again, but after I had a buzz... so guess there was some alcohol in it. 
I was hungry too and ended u ordering dinner, i got a fish and chips platter that came with potato wedges and peas, and wow it was delish! I forget where they said they get there food made from, but it was really yummy and worth the 16 dollars I was spending on it. 
I look forward to coming back next year, and enjoyed the time out with my sister and niece.

Great experience! Maguire was our server and he was excellent!! Food was very good. We had buffalo shrimp, red snapper, lobster shrimp cakes and bacon wrapped scallops. We weren't crazy about the drinks; Redstone Manhattan and Tito Lemon-Aid.  The noise level is very high so if you're looking for a quiet place, this isn't it. Will still go back.

You won't find a better store in all of Arizona! I searched over 3 years and several different states for a wedding band and found perfection at Sheffield's. I walked in to a warm and welcoming staff, where Christine worked her magic. Her experience gave great value when her first choice to match my very custom ring, was beyond a perfect match. They were not pushy or forceful in anyway and I actually left the store to think about the decision. When I came back (the next day) to purchase the rings, Eric the owner and Christine made the entire process truly enjoyable. They stayed an hour past their closing time so that we could order the rings and we all celebrated by toasting to the occasion. This store is unlike any other and I cannot say enough how wonderful the atmosphere and staff is. We will be life-long customers! Thank you so much!

I would say that Redstone is a nice place to catch a drink or two and even have a decent meal. The prices are a little bit on the higher side, but the quality of food is top notch. I have had the pleasure of dining in on two occasions. The only negative, but positive thing would be the monthly rotations of beer on tap. Negative as one of your new favorites could be gone, but positive because it opens you up to new and local beers!

I was impressed with the prime rib. The size was massive at 14oz and the seasoning truly popped. The meat was juicy and melted in my mouth. Mashed potatoes and vegetables came with the meal. Both were very good and cooked to perfection. The potatoes were the perfect consistency. We ordered the chocolate chip sundae as a treat afterwards and we were not disappointed AT ALL! The warm cookie is baked in the pan with vanilla ice cream and whipped cream on the top. The portion was mind blowing and might be one of the best desserts I have had in quite awhile!

The restaurant has plenty of seating with a mixture of tables, booths, and bar seating. Everything was clean and the service was exceptional!

I met Ben, the owner of the shop, several weeks ago from a mutual friend. I told him that night I'd be contacting him to order a petite carrot cake for my sister's upcoming 50th birthday celebration. He was given full creative license to create, and he did not disappoint! The cake was just beautiful ... and then it got even better once we sliced it and each had a piece. My sister is a food snob (and a chef and baker at heart in her own kitchen), so her palette is quite sophisticated. She said, "This blows (another local cake shop) out of the water", and proceeded to rave about how dense the cake was and how she appreciate the freshly grated carrots and other goodness packed inside. Thank you, Ben, for making her evening so special! Also, I had never been to Gallery before and when I approached the structure to pick up the cake, I heard heart-warning chatter and laughter from the very diverse patrons that filled the outdoor and indoor areas. The atmosphere was whimsical, and I plan to visit for breakfast/brunch so I can soak up all this magic as well! The fact that Gallery is a locally-owned small business is the cherry on top.

I love it here. I have followed them for years. I have been wanting to go. I was able to try out the bar downtown. And I loved it so much, but I still wanted to go to the original. So I had a little girls day with one of my friends, when they were doing bottomless Mamosa's around the holidays. And the vibes of the shop are definitely different than the bar. This was more like hang out with your girlfriends and sit and talk for hours. And the bar was more cute and fun and hip, like to go there on a first date!! But I love them both for different reasons. And I will definitely be back to each location!

I've been going to Poochinis since 2016. Most times, the clips have been good. Their customer service aspect needs improvement. This last time, I got there a little late to pick up my girls. I still made it in time before they closed. Jim made the comment to me saying that if I was any later they would have been locked in for the weekend. No.1: That would have never happened as I would have gotten the authorities involved. No.2: You don't talk that way to your paying customers. They are not cheap whatsoever. I've been paying $146 ( includes a tip for each groomer) every 8 weeks for many years. His comment made me so mad, that I called them and cancelled the next appointment I had. I am taking my business elsewhere where they value my business and are much less in cost. Suggestion for Poochinis: Value your customers, Treat your customers with respect, have good customer service.  People have many other places to choose from to take their business to. Time for a change.

I had a really good experience as far as car shopping goes. Jeff Lato and the rest of the staff were easy to talk to and I felt completely comfortable. I had an idea of what I wanted going in and Jeff didn't try to sway me or push me into something I didn't want.  I got out of a pretty bad car loan and into something much better considering my credit. The process was smooth and hassle free.

Incompetent or dishonest?  

When working with car dealerships it's tough to tell.  This morning I was online, saw an inventory of several GMC Denali pickups advertised at 20% off MSRP.  I filled out an inquiry form regarding one of several Blue trucks and received a call around Noon.  I made an appointment for 6pm and was emphatically told to call ahead if plans changed.  A few minutes later I receive an email confirmation, noting that I would be meeting with John Barlow and the truck I wanted would be out front ready for a test drive.

I arrive before 6, walk through the showroom that's completely empty of staff.  I then walked the entire lot looking for the Blue GMC Denali finding only a 2017 version that's 15k more in a back corner of the lot.  Finally back to the showroom where I find John Barlow.  He knows nothing about the appointment and says the 2016 Blue Denali trucks were all sold in the morning.

At that time I noticed a white truck out front, not that I'd ever buy a white one.  Apparently instead of admitting they sold the vehicles when I spoke about making an appointment, they tried a bait and switch.  Also apparent they have no regard for wasting my time even though they went out of their way to make sure I showed up on time or called ahead.

Note if you check online now, they still list the blue trucks as available and in stock.

Lesson learned.  Don't waste your time dealing with these guys!
We love Eric and his staff, we've been loyal customers for many years. From our wedding rings to watches and all my wife's jewellery, we wouldn't trust anyone else.

Oddly enough, Red Stone has locations where I live in Minnesota and here in New Jersey where my parents live. So I have dined with Red Stone in two states, and I'm happy to report consistently high marks. I am borrowing liberally from my other Red Stone review since it is essentially the same... It is called a GRILL and I generally find that things that are grilled are the best -- primarily steak. This is one of my go-to places when I want a really good filet. Here are my highlights:

-Buffalo shrimp appetizer. This is one of the few food items I actually CRAVE on a regular basis. By far the best Buffalo-flavored thing ever. Giant shrimp coated in crispy batter, fried and then coated in delicious Buffalo sauce, then drizzled with some kind of cream/crema and bleu cheese crumbles on top.. the half order comes with three, full order with five. Just get the full. Also makes for a great lunch with a bowl of soup. I was apparently so busy eating these that I forgot to take a picture of them, but check out Louise M's review for her photo!
-Petite filet. My go-to. Always cooked perfectly with a lovely crust and juicy inside, cooked exactly med-rare the way I asked for it. With a loaded baked potato on the side, it's pretty much heaven if you like a good steak every now and then.
-Chocolate cake. As someone mentioned, this is like seriously the size of your head and delicious. The most sinful part about it is that they bring it to the table with a little silver pitcher of chocolate sauce and ask you so slyly if you would like any EXTRA chocolate sauce on your cake. Seriously.Seriously?!?!? No, please take the chocolate sauce away, since I obviously have oodles of self control since I ordered this gigantic piece of chocolate cake on top of my huge meal.
-My husband ordered the coconut halibut, which he reported to be good. My mom likes to get the salmon. This is all I  know about the seafood that is not Buffalo Shrimp.
-Service is always good to great.

Oddly enough the only thing I don't like about Redstone is their booths. There's something about them that makes it hard for me to fully relax, but I think it's just the table height. I'm 5'2" so the table is too high or too far away or something. But if you can get a normal table, problem solved.

I spent 4 days in New Orleans and passed the Gumbo Pot several times and was curious about the place, but none of my friends seemed interested in trying it out.  On my last day there I was alone for the whole day and before my flight decide to walk around to kill some time. I was approached by a gentleman handing out fliers for the place so I decided to try it out and get a small bit to eat for lunch before my flight.

The man who approached me in the street was the same man who seated me and brought me my glass of water that I requested.  However the server took a long time to come take my order. She wasn't friendly at all. I was all smiles and said "I'm not too hungry so I'd just like something small before I head back to NY and wanted to try this place out" She looks at me like "yeah OK so what" in my mind I'm like "OK so this is where she is supposed to make some suggestions.. She didn't. I decided on the craw fish salad. I wanted the house creole vinaigrette, she says "No I don't have that!" i ask " OK well what do you have?" she says 'it's there on the menu
 so i finally decide to get the remoulade and asked for.  My salad came out pretty fast, but I was very disappointed. It was just huge chunks of iceberg lettuce with three big slices of tomatoes and a bunch of small pieces of fried craw fish that had no taste.  It also had the onions on it when I asked for no onions. The server never came back to me to check how I was doing or if I needed anything. When I got the bill is when the server tried to be a little friendly, but at this point it was too late in my book. I only left a $4 tip on a $15 bill. I normally leave servers more because I know they work for it. But I was not happy with her service, also as I was walking out of the restaurant I hear the server saying "this little girl left me a $4 tip" I don't know if she was complaining or what, but I would not go here again because of the service and my salad was not up to par at all.

We should've just stuck with our first instincts to go for burgers and tater tots, but we decided to try The Gumbo Pot instead. BIG MISTAKE!
First, we waited for the maitre'd, but there was no one around, so we made our way towards the interior of the restaurant only to be flagged back outside by the maitre'd. After we were seated at our table, I had to go to the ladies room. It was disgusting! The last stall was NOT clean and I almost threw up!
I came back to the table where there were five of us dining. We started off with water while we decided what drinks to order. One friend ordered a SoCo Hurricane and another one ordered a Malibu Rum Punch. They each took one sip of their drinks and said they tasted wrong and were disgusting. When our waiter, Jeremy, came by to ask how things were, my friends had told him about the drinks, that they weren't any good and were thinking about ordering something else. Instead of insisting on taking those drinks away, he tried to defend the drinks and the bartender by saying that "that's how those drinks are supposed to taste. They're stronger than regular drinks." Just before he walked away, he just left the drinks sitting there.
The seafood gumbo arrived and my friend and I were excited because it looked so good. Actually, it was the worst gumbo I've ever had. I was so disappointed, that I didn't finish mine. I ordered crab cakes as my entree and they were so bad too!! They were BURNT, not crispy! They were the saltiest crab cakes ever. 
Overall, the whole entire experience was just terrible. The ambiance was terrible. The service was awful, awful, awful!! The food was so bad!! My friends and I were just so upset that for a restaurant which charges so much $$ for their meals, they should've been more accommodating.
Although other Yelp! reviewers may have been pleased with this restaurant, we left with such a bad taste in our mouths. We've eaten at plenty of restaurants in the area and were so thrilled with them. It's a shame that we hit this sore spot.

We were visiting Mass Ave Toys and noticed The Gallery Shop as we were leaving. This strip of businesses sits back off the road and easy to pass if you're not reading signs or searching for a specific address. As I walked in I found myself saying I how cute! I was expecting a sterile bakery atmosphere but instead found a warm and inviting cafe. So much I wanted to tell the hostess yes, we'd sit at one of the many tables but no time today. But Soon!

The dessert and pastry counter was filled with gorgeous delicacies. Perfect for an event when presentation and flavor is important. The open kitchen is a nice feature in the room with seating so you can admire their creativity. They also offer various classes so you can perfect your treats.

I ordered Pistacho Macaroons and Chocolate Crossiants to go. The Macaroons were delicate, so fresh and not overly sweet. The Chocolate Crossiants were my favorite. I warmed it for just a few seconds and it was so buttery, flaky with rich, dark chocolate inside. Every bite was Delightful!

I can't wait to come back for brunch! Plus this summer I have to visit the patio area.
All goes smoothly from making an appointment to the service completed in a timely Manor. Very happy with my 7 years of using Barlow Buicks service department.
Such delicious macaroons. I was gifted a small box with assorted flavors. Hands down the best I've ever had!!! So soft and flavorful. The pink ones were my favorite. I highly recommend this shop.

I usually love Redstone and have always went to the location in Plymouth Meeting with great experiences each time. After COVID hit, I tried the location in Marlton expecting the same experience. Unfortunately that was not the case. 

I ordered one of my favorite dishes the Cedar Plank Salmon which came out burnt on the outside with burnt lemon wedges as garnish. So bad I had to flip the lemons over to salvage the pic. Before I ordered I asked for it to be cooked medium medium rare like it usually is at Plymouth Meeting, and it seemed almost purposely the server brought out this burnt salmon. Why be so malicious towards customers? 

I love the garlic aioli that used to come with it but its not available right now with the new post COVID menu. This is something I feel the server could have mentioned to me while ordering as I mentioned I come  here often so I didn't read in detail the description. I usually dip my salmon and asparagus in the aioli and it's my favorite part of the dish. 

The Cornbread still taste good but for some reason I don't remember it having actual Corn  pieces in it...? Maybe I forgot, but I could do without the corn inside. 

I also ordered my usual buffalo shrimp which was $17.50 and I only received 4 pieces instead of the usual full order of 6. There is also no option for a half order of 3 neither anymore. The new limited COVID menu is frustrating to any long time goers because the menu isn't huge to begin with and there also no weekly specials. I think I'll just go back once their menu is back to normal. Biggest plus is my Redstone Manhattan  still taste pretty good just a little stronger than usual and it's already a strong drink. 


The server was very indifferent throughout the entire meal, and did not act like he cared about us enjoying ourselves at all. He actually brought down the mood it was so bad. I didn't even want anything else to eat. We left without dessert. I don't want to feel I have to fight to be treated right at any restaurant. Will never return to this location.
Poor customer service! owner displayed no accountability and follow through.  I preferred to give the small local based company my business but now I understand the reason to buy from Cabela's.

Julianna was a great server, super friendly! super attentive.  she really made our dining experience excellent. Highly recommend the spicy guac burger. The mocktails were awesome. Great experience all around.

This is a dreamy place. This is the place where you go when you're on a good date, or the place you take your child to for a special treat, or the place you visit by yourself to just get away, breathe, and treat yourself to something nice. 

One time, one rainy day, I just planted myself here and ate three croissants. Because ... they have great croissants. It was also $1 croissant day, so I only spent $3 (plus whatever it cost for a cup of black coffee)!

I was here once with my husband and we only ordered desserts and tea. It was perfect, because their desserts are wonderful and the tea is sublime. 

They have an outdoor seating area that is great for just sitting and relaxing. 

The parking is kind of atrocious, though. The parking is very limited, so you might have to park a little ways away and walk, but it's totally worth it to dine here.

I LOVE Redstone.

I have been here twice now in the last year, and just can't wait to keep coming back. I'm sad I've been missing out on such quality food and service over the years (been living in the area for 20+ years). The first time I came was late last year with my brother and SIL for a quick drink and snack. The drinks were delicious even though I can't remember what we got. We also ordered Baked Brie for the first time and fell in love. That was on their limited weekly menu though, so when I came back 2 weeks ago, it was no longer available. Sad times 

However, when I visited most recently, it was for a Sunday brunch. We opted to sit outside in the patio at the bar which was a great decision. It wasn't extremely hot outside yet, but the fans were all on just in case. My bf ordered breakfast (2 eggs any style, toast, potatoes, and bacon), and I ordered the Margherita flatbread minus pesto. We shared a basket of fries, and I also ordered the Morning Sangria (I forgot what it's actually called) which was insanely delicious. All of our food was fantastic. Our service was impeccable as the bartenders were also our waitresses. I definitely recommend & can't wait to be back!

Delicious brunch! I thought they were just a really good pastry shop, but they also do a daily brunch menu. I went for a Saturday brunch and had the crepes. You get to choose two crepes and fill them with whatever they have listed on the menu. I chose a savory crepe with spinach, mushroom, bacon and feta, along with a sweet chocolate mousse crepe.
