Every bite was perfect. The vibe is farmhouse chic, casual, sunny, friendly. I can't wait to come back.

When you visit NOLA there's two things you need to try: Gumbo and Jambalaya! Well of course I tried the gumbo from here. It was really good. You can taste all of the various spices and flavors they use for your creation. I ordered the seafood gumbo. Wasn't to spicy but pretty good for lunch. You get a lot of food and the price is just right. Not much of a drink menu. The waitress we had was soooooo bad. Plain and simple. But our hostess was exquisite and overall had a great experience. Gets pretty hot during the day so eating inside is mandatory. 
Good luck!

A brunch spot where you can make reservations?! Need I say more?! The service is always top notch and I can't say enough about their beverages and food! I suggest to make sure you start with their caramelized fruit. It rotates depending on what fruit is the most fresh and it's always so delicious! I always tend to lean towards their make your own omelets. I wish I could make an omelette as delicious as they can....but I can't...so thank goodness this place is in my neighborhood and j can go all the time! Oh and be sure to try their lavender latte if that's your thing.

I have lived here for years and had never made it here.  That all changed today. The Hall of Champions is a well organized interactive museum located next to White River Park. Total disclosure, I went on a day that they were giving free admission. But, it is normally only $5 for adults and $3 for kids anyway, so it does not break the bank anyway and is well worth that.  

They validate parking to a discounted $5 if you park in the White River Park underground parking garage. The entire staff there is very helpful and friendly. The museum is very very clean and they have hand sanitizer all over the museum to try to keep the RONA down.

When you walk in, you are faced with a display of football linemen statues, with masks, looking right at you. The ground floor has an interactive display for all the major NCAA sports, Hall of Honor, and a small gift shop. There is also a replica of the NCAA trophy down there too.

The second floor has a mini-basketball court, but the rim is regulation, where you and your group can "make it rain". There is a sports simulator where you can pitch baseballs, or kick soccer balls past an alien goalie. There is also sprinter and swimmer starting blocks that you can get on.  My kids enjoyed seeing a 75 MPH ball coming flying at them. And by enjoyed, I mean scared their pants off.

Some notable exhibits in the museum include the impact of HBCUs, and contributions/impact of women athletes.

The place is not very big. I spent a little over an hour there, but it was still entertaining and impactful.  Surprisingly, my 1 and 5 year olds actually had a lot of fun. FYI, this museum is located by many other museums, as well as the zoo (all within walking distance) and could be part of a larger itinerary to maximize your day. I really enjoyed my visit and am glad that I came here.

"My.02 ~ So far, these are some of the best chips and salsa in Smyrna!"

We have been here multiple times and I do not remember the chips being this good. "Come on man - it's just a chip!" These are different - same shape - same basket lined with paper, but they were not one bit greasy! Not grease spots on the paper either - almost as if they were baked. The salsa was a perfect heat level - not real hot, but you knew it wasn't mild by any means. We only got one basket, but they were packed in there so good and piled so high - it took three bowls of salsa for us to finish them - and finish them we did! My nose sometimes itches from eating greasy chips - not that problem here. They were just thick enough that you didn't have to worry about cutting your gums or the roof of your mouth.

Yesterday's special was 2 enchiladas with red sauce and melted cheese, rice and beans. It was just enough (after I ate what my wife left of one of hers). I would have been fine without her leftovers, but I am not sending it back! House margaritas were $3.99 as well. Honestly - I have never had a margarita at a Mexican restaurant where you could even taste the tequila. If you are looking for a buzz, better get a pitcher and a designated driver - maybe - they seem that weak. It's like drinking a fruit drink. 

The two dinners and one margarita for my wife was around $15 and that included tax. Not bad for an evening meal. Service was excellent and the waiter was very nice and obliging. I asked for some sour cream, so instead of charging me for a larger bowl - he brought me just enough in a small plastic container.

When I saw this place at the Cherry Hill Mall, I knew I had to go. The thought of edible cookie dough was very intriguing, and although I'm glad I gave this place a try, I can't say I'd return. 

The establishment is super cute and trendy. It is bright and colorful with cool wall art with funny quotes and puns. The gentleman working behind the counter was very nice and encouraged me and my fiancé to try as many flavors as we wanted. 

After sampling a few different ones, we ended up sharing a medium cup with a scoop of two different flavors: mint dynasty and cinnamon bun. It came out to roughly $8.50. Probably more than what you would spend on an ice cream, but when you think of the price you would pay for fresh cookies, I guess the cost makes sense. 

The flavors were great and tasted exactly like how you would imagine. Although we both really enjoyed our first few spoonfuls, it wasn't long before we were rethinking having gotten a medium. It is so extremely sweet and heavy. Although it didn't make me physically ill, I was crashing in just a few minutes. We were told that it can be refrigerated, but honestly, the thought of taking it back and having it later wasn't appealing. 

Since this is a fairly new trend in the area, I'm happy I gave it a try but when it comes down to it, bowls of edible cookie dough just isn't for me. I thought the medium was too big (even when split between two people), a small would maybe be reasonable, but what I really think they should do is create a kids size. Maybe then I'd go back!

O.M.G. My precious babies, Pookey and Angel, look so handsome and beautiful right now! I had them deluxe groomed and used the limo service today. Jim was so kind. He picked them up at 3:13, about two minutes before they were scheduled to be picked up, asked if there were any special instructions which I told him, and promptly returned my two HAPPY HAPPY dogs home at 5:00ish. They had Halloween scarves on! LOL! I am pleased beyond words! I'm telling EVERYONE I KNOW about this wonderful pet salon. I knew about it because I get my nails done next door, Sprouts is across the way, and Cheng's Chinese restaurant is two doors away. When I overheard a conversation between two women who were standing in line at Safeway speaking so highly of Poochini's, I knew it was the place to go. I can't find the words to express how pleased I am with all aspects of my Poochini's experience today!! Yaaaaaay!!

Great selection of rifles and shotguns not to mention there handguns and Hospitality. If you're looking for some great outdoor fun, this is the place to go! Prices seemed really good too, I should mention.

Loved the ambiance of this place. Super friendly bartenders. Had a reservation for 5 and we were able to get a table outside, perfect weather for it.

Hands down, the fondue was my favorite thing here. I would go back for cocktails and just the fondue. Buffalo shrimp were tasty, but not exciting.

I was on my beef kick, so I dove into prime rib. It was good..but I wish I had tried something else after a couple of bites. It needed more flavor. Obiviously the loaded baked potato was a meal in itself. The veg of the night was too basic. 

Key lime pie, huge slice and was delicious. 

We all had some wine, but the pumpkin martini stole the show.
BEST vegan hash I've ever had! Wonderful service, the Gallery is filled with kind staff! I've been in many times and have never had a bad experience.

I had an amazing experience here for brunch on a Sunday. I wish I'd known about this place earlier. They serve amazing fresh made crepes. You can order as many toppings as you want either sweet or savory for a reasonable price. I tried a chorizo bacon crepe and also had a sweet banana crepe with whipped cream and meringue. Overall very delicious and came out quickly. 
They provided complementary cinnamon rolls for our group which was a plus.
I had also tried their warm kale salad which was a side item. I was quite impressed since I normally dislike kale.

In my previous review I gave Redstone American Grill 5 stars. If you read my reviews you will notice that I do not give out five star ratings. When it comes to the food, ambiance, and the service of the wait staff; this place is one of the best. I have enjoyed dining at Redstone from the very first time I set foot in the place years  ago. However due to an unfriendly incident that took place Friday night, I will no longer dine at this establishment. 

I was dining at Redstone Grille Friday night night (11/30/2012) with another couple. Once again, the meal was awesome! The Service was awesome! So why am I downgrading the star level after latest visit? Because the young ladies at the hostess stand and the manager are not the friendliness, and lack just some basic common people skills and the ability to think on their feet.  

I left my phone at the restaurant. When I realized I didn't have it, I used my iPad and tracked the phone back to the restaurant. My wife called and asked if someone could quickly check the table to see if the phone was there and the hostess refused. She stated that someone was sitting in the booth and that she would not disturb the party. (After speaking with the GM today 12/1/12, that was not true) I have been in Redstone dozens of times and on a few occasions a diner would call or return to retrieve an item. On two occasions I was that customer in the booth  and without hesitation, granted the employees and the customer the opportunity to look for their belongings. She  instructed us to leave our number, and said someone would contact us that night or the next morning when workers turn in any lost items at the end of the night. So if you forget your wallet, or credit cart, you have to wait till the end of the night to find out if someone turned it in? 

My wife drove back to Redstone Grille to look for herself. She arrived at the restaurant ten minutes later and the table was empty contradicting the hostess statement.  Our server came over to the table to assist my wife. When they were unable to find the phone, our server asked, the manager on duty, Tessa, to assist. The manager pretty much didn't want anything to do with the situation. When my wife returned home, she spoke with the Manager Tessa again by phone. When she informed the manager that we were filing a police report her response was "fine, file a report." She also declined to do anything to assist us with any information to help find the phone. 

Prior to speaking with the General Manager this afternoon I believed another customer seated after us, or an employee took my phone. Following that conversation, I was more convinced that my phone was in the possession of and removed from the premises by an employee of Redstone Grill. When he informed us that there was no party seated in that booth after we left, contradicting earlier statements, it pretty much casted a shadow of suspicion over the employees working the front of the house, especially whomever were responsible for clearing the table. Even the hostess actions are a little suspect. 

I was the one that forgot my phone in the restaurant. Redstone is not responsible but they could have been more helpful or at least pretend to give a damn about the situation. Ten minutes after my wife left the apartment the phone started to move. I firmly believe an individual or a group of individuals employed by Redstone participated in the effort to remove my phone from the premises Not saying she would have found it, but the phone could have been still on the premises. Good thing I had a really good meal last night, because it is my last. I will not set foot in this place again. The food here is awesome, but Redstone needs to hire individuals with people skills, and don't participate in theft.

Jim & Katherine have been wonderful to us and our little Baxter. We have been coming to Poochini's Grooming since moving to Tucson 7 years ago. I will hate to see them leave, but we wish them a very happy retirement.

LOVE IT HERE!!! By far, one of my favorite restaurants! It's a huge fan favorite and my family and I dine here often...especially on birthdays! 

This place is always packed so I would go at an odd time or make a reservation. They are Open Table participants! If not, be prepared to wait...a lonnnnnng time!

It is pretty pricey so I would take a look at the menu ahead of time if you are concerned about the total cost of your meal. 

My most recent visit was last week and they had an avocado salad as an appetizer which was absolutely delicious! It was cucumber and super fresh avocado served with a lime vinegarette and a roasted lime was served on the plate that I squeeze over the whole salad. There was also fresh cilantro. I don't even like cilantro but it was so fresh tasting and the whole salad just tasted so fresh and yummy. It was so, so good. I wish it was always on the menu!

In the past I've had the flatbread, buffalo shrimp and calamari appetizers...all delicious!

Their crabcakes are super good! I always get my starch switched to mashed potatoes which are creamy and delicious. 

I've had desserts which are yummy. Their fish is always fresh, my brothers love their burgers and ribs and my Dad always orders a special which he ultimately loves every time. 

I've only had one entree that I didn't really love and I only ordered it because it was recommended to me by a friend. From now on, I'll stick to my own choices because I've never been unhappy with anything else. It probably just wasn't my taste. 

I love the atmosphere. The booths are comfortable. It is kind of loud but most restaurants tend to be, these days. The bar scene is always hopping. They have outdoor seating available in the front and on the side. I don't love the front only because it seems like you are out in the parking lot. It seems like it would be fun for a group, though. There are fire pits. I think they may have live music sometimes as well. The outdoor seating along the side of the restaurant looks nice. It reminded me of being on vacation somewhere. I'd be willing to try it on another visit. 

I've never had a complaint about the service. They are always attentive and professional. Some I like more than others but that's just a matter of taste. The bathrooms are clean and I love the sinks!

I hear they have an amazing brunch. I've never been here for it but it's definitely something I would love to try!

I was super disappointed with this pop-up. I have visited Tinsel and had a good time, but the Halloween version felt a little flat. The decorations were very elaborate, but felt a little boring - like walking through a Halloween store. The drinks were very overpriced for the quality. And most people were doing it for the Instagram photo ops, which was expected yes but made it feel like a sham. I went a few doors down to Haunt and had a much better time.

This is still my favorite (and in my assessment, the best) casual American restaurant in NJ. 
The apple pie eggrolls are amazing.

Redstone used to be our favorite go-to restaurant for a casual, but enjoyable meal.  However, last night's visit was a total disappointment after not having been there for awhile because of Covid.  The food has certainly gone down hill.  Small portions, higher prices and much lower quality.  Soggy chopped chicken salad, the fondue was very watery and thin, jerk chicken (extra charge) which we ordered, never came.  When we asked the waitress about it, she brought us a small plate of chicken that looked nothing like the jerk chicken that once was included on the plate.  Very small portions.  Hopefully, the Redstone will go back to the way it was.  
Could be part of the reason why it was less crowded than we have ever seen.

We haven't yet stayed at the Clarion but our recent interaction with one of the hotel staff left us feeling very optimistic about a great trip. We had some mixup with our reservation and Andre helped me out and in the process was super courteous, fun to deal with and highly competent. We are very much looking forward to our stay.

Returned for a second time with friends. Made a reservation (which is the key to getting seating). Same stellar experience with service and the food. They've now started a $2 mimosa deal on the weekends, which is in or with other deals around town.

Nope, not worth it. Sure, it's only $5 to get in but if I knew what I know now, I wouldn't even waste that much. My friend and I found ourselves making last minute plans and decided we'd try this spot. We got there kind of early to avoid the long line, wait, and crowd - maybe showed up around 7:30/8pm? 

The line wasn't too bad when we got there but by the time we left, probably half an hour later, it had tripled. Inside is decorated with cool spooky stuff but is super tiny, one bar, and it was already nuts in there. Front door didn't even check for vaccine cards and masks are optional. If there was a time that I would get COVID, it was from this place. 

It's also way pricey for what it is - $23 for 2 HOUSE gin and tonics that were mostly all ice and in tiny plastic cups. My friend and I finished them in about 15 min. and ran towards the door to leave.

Idk, maybe I'm too old now but this was just not worth it. As I mentioned before, our entire experience was about 30 min. haha safe to say, won't be going back.

What a lovely hidden gem! The shop just opened this week. It's off 54th St right across from Posh Petals. Go toward the back of the parking and there they are! The shop opens up to the outdoors and then have two lovely patios for outdoor eating. Service was welcoming and friendly and you could watch Chef Ben in action. We loved the macarons, which were almost as good as the ones we get at Ladurée in NYC! We also tried one sweet and one savory crêpe. The texture and flavor of the crêpes were perfect. We had one with bacon, feta and chive. Another was bananas foster - I liked how the bananas were petit diced and you could taste bits of brûléed sugar in it. They also offer omelettes (as part of the Sunday brunch menu). We will definitely be back for more macarons and to try other crêpes and some of their pastries.

Go to place for wine, flatbread pizza, and Ahi Tuna.  Nice atmosphere if you don't mind a middle-aged pick up bar in the middle of the restaurant.  Flatbread pizzas are amazing. The fire and outdoor seating area create a nice oasis in the middle of what is just a huge parking lot.  Plenty of trees shield you from the sounds and lights of the traffic on 73.  Seems upscale with well trained and friendly staff.  Our special occasion occasional place. :)

We had a great experience staying here. The rooms were comfortable and clean, as was the rest of the hotel. The breakfast was more than we could ask for, everything from pancakes to waffles to oatmeal to eggs to yogurt and plenty more!

The pool was great with an 8 feet deep end so you can really get in a good swim. It was also a salt water pool which was nice! I wish it had longer hours- I think it was 10am to 9pm. The small fitness center was also a plus and it was open 24 hours. 

They have a nice shuttle that goes downtown, too! We had a car but this option was great because we didn't have to find parking. The driver was very friendly. And the hotel wasn't necessarily in a super hip location, but it was very close to a lot of the things!

The staff overall at the Clarion were very helpful, friendly, and professional. I'd stay here again!

This place is a gem!!! Highly recommend! I didn't know what to expect when I went and thought they just had more pastries and coffee but they have a full menu and so many options. We split a cheese board and our waitress recommended 2 amazing cheeses. She was very attentive but let us have tome to chat and enjoy the food:) I had the pear lavender latte which was delicious! They use smoking goose meats () and their croissants are to die for! I will definitely be returning very soon! 
Also, they have a really cute patio to enjoy when the weather warms up.

What a gem! Definitely check out this place. They have awesome specials: $1 macaroons on Wednesday, bottomless mimosas on Saturday, half off wine on Sunday's...come on. It doesn't get any better! Their atmosphere is so beautiful and welcoming. The owner and staff are so fun and kind. We make a point to bring all friends here when they visit from out of town. They've also recently added impossible meat to their options, so as a vegetarian, I definitely love that! They opened a location downtown that I'm looking forward to visiting as well!
No good. Service including waitress and manager was unacceptable at the Plymouth Meeting location.   Will not go back to this location again.   Very disappointed .

I am shocked by how we were treated tonight. Not only do we live an hour away, but it was to celebrate my daughters 14th birthday. 

I had high hopes as the restaurant even called me this morning to confirm my reservation. 

We arrived on time and were seated. We sat in an area with several tables. My family and I sat there for 20 minutes, as servers and waiters passed us. I cannot believe we were not spoken to or even gotten our drink order. Insane! We decided to leave as I don't feel comfortable spending towards $200 for dinner and not to be valued. 

If you don't want to be valued as a customer, come here!

Our server this 4th visit was amazing her name was Cynthia. She was extremely accommodating and full of smiles and energy. We fell in love with this place years ago while in NJ with our then middle school age girls in which one was turning 13 and we searched for somewhere near our hotel to have dinner and stumbled upon this place. Fast forward to the past couple of years we've made it our business to stop here when on the road driving from NYC to the DMV and beyond down to the Carolinas (in the rare chance we decide to drive as we prefer the flight life).

Our go to is BRUNCH as the morning reads are amazing and we've had different flavors at various locations however we've had two type at this location one being the Orange Cranberry and Lemon BlueBerry. Today's visit we experienced the Lemon Blueberry which was amazing and I wanted more and more LOL. Another perk of brunch is complimentary mimosas as long as you are of age and would like some = SCORE as long as you are not driving (Glad my husband is driving and doesn't drink).
Our youngest girl LOVE the Buffalo Shrimp small plate with a side of fries, our baby boy enjoys the grill cheese however you MUST specify Cheddar cheese otherwise it's made with American which I believe is something people like (not my family), my husband orders the rotisserie flatbread mostly or the steak and egg whites with potatoes, I usually end up with a Salmon burger or margarita flatbread to go with my mimosas :-)

The ladies up front could take some pointers from the servers when it comes to how to speak to someone or how to greet paying customers which is why I can't make this a 5 star review...

Here is what I think.
For $200+ a night, it isn't worth it for a business trip.  If I'm here to party it may be, but it's all work and no real play.
Pros-
The staff is on point, they are  great! 
The rooms are spacious. 
They have a shuttle that runs every 30 minutes.
Cons-
Walls are thin, I can hear the man snoring in the room next to me.  I had to run the AC all night to drown them out because they were loud at night and then turn it lower when he woke me up with his snoring. 
Which leads me to needing extra blankets in the room, this thin blanket isn't enough.  
Or add ear plugs to the bathroom, which isn't unusual, as you can also hear the street traffic very well. 
I most likely won't be returning here, if I did it would be for your staff, they really are that great!

The Gallery Pastry Shop has been on my must-visit list for about a year now (if not longer). Sure, the crepes were a draw, but the menu, concise and inviting, was more alluring, as well as all the photos that seemed to be, well, everywhere I looked! 

After a few cursory visits to the patisserie, I finally made it out for brunch. I haven't been to too many brunches here in Indiana, largely because I spent almost none of my adult life here- the kicker is that I LOVE brunch. I love the ambience, the atmosphere, the idea of getting a relaxed start to the day and celebrating that start with good food and drink (because who needs hurried, pre-office breakfasts anyways), and of course, the bubbles.

My friends settled on mimosas while I can't turn down anything berry-flavored, so I settled on a sparkling lemonade (that I later shamelessly added some of their extra champagne to, of course). It was refreshing, spritely, and surprisingly, almost not sweet at all! 

While my croissant was a little too indulgent for my taste, the hashbrowns were absolutely divine, as were my others' friends orders of: Goose chorizo hash, bananas foster crepes, and a make-your-own omelet. 

The menu has so, so many things I'm left wanting to try and with a new Downtown location adorned with some fabulous artwork of Bourdain, there's absolutely no doubt I'll be one of the first customers.

I had my wedding reception brunch here and everything was just as we'd hoped. The manager Jonny is so helpful and friendly and the owners Ben and Alison are awesome too. Aside from the wonderful customer service experience the food and desserts are absolutely delicious! Since our wedding, we've continued to visit, and are never disappointed. I recently ordered my husband's birthday cake from here, and it's was absolutely delicious!

This is a place of dreams!  I only tried two macaroons and espresso but based on that and all my eyes could see, I confidently give this place 5 stars!  I cannot wait to go back!  All of the pastries looked delicious (and unique), beautiful cakes, and the made to order omelettes looked like a great selection of ingredients to choose from.  Open kitchen to watch the chefs work while you eat.

"You can't eat a bad meal in New Orleans"
That's what so many friends tell me and that has been my experience in all the times I've visited New Orleans. 
That's why I didn't check Yelp reviews before walking into this place. 
Big mistake. 
This place is a tourist trap. We ordered our drinks before I decided to look around the room and spot the signs. Everyone eating here was obviously from out of town. Visors, fanny packs, and "family reunion" t-shirts at every table. 

I hoped that maybe I would get lucky and have a decent experience. 
Here's how that played out for me:

Our drink orders were too complicated for the waitress. One diet coke, five waters, three beers. But one of my friends called her after and told her instead of one beer he wanted another. I was ready to bet my first born that both beers would arrive at our table. Would've had twins if I did. 
Next, the food. It took a very long time and our food came out in episodes, with two of my friends getting their food first, then the third, then a long time after that my other friend and I got our side dishes (without our main course). So I sat there watching everyone eat while nibbling on some frozen food section fries. Eventually our food came out. 
The food was passable. I guess that's the only upside to our trip here. Passable. I was able to finish my shrimp po-boy. That's a difficult dish to mess up. My friends ordered breakfast items, which are also difficult to prepare incorrectly. 
The bathroom was absolutely disgusting and there were no paper towels. 

Hilariously, After we were all done eating, the biscuits and toast were brought out, like some kind of punch line.

I'd say the bill was the last straw, but I can't. You know why? Because I'm still waiting for it to arrive.
